You CAN'T get: coverage outside the Atlantic Forest biome, or enforcement — the system feeds IBAMA, state environmental secretariats and police, and the state Ministérios Públicos. For activists: this is how you reach a prosecutor with a dated, geolocated, property-linked clearing already documented.

trackers.name: COICA — Coordinadora de las Organizaciones Indígenas de la Cuenca Amazónica
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the basin-wide confederation of Amazonian Indigenous organisations, founded to act for 511 Indigenous peoples across the nine Amazon countries, around 66 of them in voluntary isolation or initial contact. It works through one national member organisation per country — in this country that is COIAB, Coordenação das Organizações Indígenas da Amazônia Brasileira — and its governing Council brings those presidents together. Its standing work areas are territorial rights and natural resources, human and sociocultural rights, and international law, and it has issued a formal declaration on the defence of Amazonian Indigenous defenders. USE IT: go to COIAB first — COICA is the regional weight behind a national organisation, not a direct service. It is the route to carry a territorial case or a threat against leaders from your community into regional and international forums.

trackers.name: Brazilian Election Justice
trackers.desc: Brazilian Election Justice — tribunal (Brazil).

trackers.name: Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU)
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Brazil, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Tribunal de Justiça do Estado da Bahia
trackers.desc: Tribunal de Justiça do Estado da Bahia — appellate court (Brazil).

trackers.name: Agência Pública
trackers.desc: Brazil's pioneering nonprofit investigative-journalism agency, reporting on public money, land, corruption and abuses of power.

trackers.name: dados.gov.br
trackers.desc: National — official government open data / budget portal. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this is the broad budget/open-data hub for how money is allocated overall — for the specific firms winning tenders use the procurement portal, and for findings of misspending use the supreme audit institution. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Brazil.

trackers.name: INESC (Institute of Socioeconomic Studies)
trackers.desc: Brazilian non-profit (est. 1979) analysing the federal public budget through a human-rights and equity lens and advocating fiscal transparency. Here you can trace how Brazil's federal budget allocates money, analysed through a human-rights and equity lens.

trackers.name: STF – Jurisprudência
trackers.desc: Official jurisprudence search of the Supremo Tribunal Federal. · Find here: the case-law (jurisprudência) of Brazil's Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF).

trackers.name: Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU)
trackers.desc: Federal Court of Accounts auditing public spending. Here you can trace public-audit findings on waste, irregularity and misspending in Brazil.

trackers.name: Portal da Transparência (Brasil)
trackers.desc: Brazil's federal transparency portal: detailed spending, suppliers, contracts, tax expenditures and open data/APIs. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Brazil.

trackers.name: Portal da Transparência
trackers.desc: Brazil's federal transparency portal of revenues, spending and transfers. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Brazil.

trackers.name: Central das Emendas
trackers.desc: Independent Brazilian organisation dedicated to transparency of parliamentary budget amendments (emendas parlamentares), with a searchable tool for the low-oversight 'Emendas PIX' (special transfers), data panels and research.

trackers.name: Financial Activities Control Board
trackers.desc: the national Financial Intelligence Unit of Brazil linked to the Central Bank of Brazil

trackers.name: Defensoria Pública da União (Federal Public Defender) of Brazil
trackers.desc: National institution of Brazil that provides free legal representation and defends access to justice, fair-trial and due-process rights for people who cannot afford counsel.

trackers.name: Compras.gov.br
trackers.desc: Brazil's federal procurement portal (formerly ComprasNet) for tenders and contracts. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Brazil, and for how much.

trackers.name: Empresas – gov.br (Juntas Comerciais)
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: companies in Brazil — find access to the state commercial-registry (Juntas Comerciais) network of entities and filings.

trackers.name: National Register of Legal Persons (CNPJ)
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Access restricted to authorities/obliged entities.

trackers.name: Brazilian Institute of Geography & Statistics (IBGE)
trackers.desc: Brazil's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Brazil.

trackers.name: Jusbrasil
trackers.desc: Brazil's largest structured legal database — jurisprudence, case tracking and doctrine across all courts. · Find here: a large aggregator of Brazilian case-law, legislation and legal news (JusBrasil; some content gated).

trackers.name: JusBrasil
trackers.desc: Large aggregator of Brazilian case law and legal documents. · Find here: a large aggregator of Brazilian case-law, legislation and legal news (JusBrasil; some content gated).

trackers.name: Observatório Social do Brasil (Sistema OSB)
trackers.desc: National non-profit network (since 2008) coordinating 70+ local Social Observatories across 100+ municipalities. Volunteers monitor municipal public spending, procurement (licitações) and contracts in real time, publishing findings and a Public Transparency & Governance Index of city and state governments.

trackers.name: FNMA — editais e termos de referência (national calls)
trackers.desc: WHERE THE NATIONAL CALLS APPEAR: the Fundo Nacional do Meio Ambiente was created by Lei nº 7.797 of 10 July 1989 and is the oldest environmental fund in Latin America, a unit of the environment ministry financing the national environment policy through social participation. This is its editais and terms of reference page — the live calls. Scale, from a recorded round: two calls totalling nearly R$ 8 million, including R$ 5.44 million split between FNMA (R$ 1.97m) and the Fundo Nacional sobre Mudança do Clima (R$ 3.47m) for socio-environmental projects reducing climate vulnerability in urban and rural areas. TWO WARNINGS. Those calls were approved at meetings resuming the funds after 4 years of paralysis — this fund has stopped before, so check for live calls rather than assuming continuity. And check who the edital is addressed to: some are directed at municipalities rather than civil society, with annexes listing the eligible municipalities, so a community group may need its city hall to be the applicant.

trackers.name: Defensoria Pública — free lawyer who can file an ação civil pública
trackers.desc: THE FREE LAWYER WHO CAN SUE FOR THE WHOLE COMMUNITY. Lei nº 7.347 of 1985 governs the ação civil pública for damage caused to the environment, consumers, and goods of artistic, historic, tourist and landscape value — and Lei nº 11.448 of 2007 amended article 5 to give the Defensoria Pública standing to bring it. The Supreme Federal Court upheld that standing as constitutional, and EC 80/2014 rewrote article 134 of the Constitution to state expressly that the Defensoria defends individual and collective rights; later STF case law extended it to diffuse rights — the category the right to an ecologically balanced environment belongs to. WHY THIS BEATS A PRIVATE LAWYER FOR A LAND FIGHT: an ação civil pública protects transindividual interests — indivisible rights held by indeterminate people linked by circumstances of fact — which is exactly a community facing a development, where no single resident holds a right they could vindicate alone. The Defensoria can act for the group, free, in every state. AND REMEMBER WHO ELSE HAS STANDING: article 5 also lists the Ministério Público, the Union, states and municipalities — so a sympathetic city hall can file the action itself, which matters when the permission came from a higher tier of government.

trackers.name: INECE — not where you report, but how you find who enforces
trackers.desc: READ THIS BEFORE YOU WRITE TO THEM: INECE IS NOT A COMPLAINT ROUTE. Its members are inspectors, prosecutors, regulators, parliamentarians and judges — a community cannot report a violation to INECE. It is worth an entry for three other reasons. FIRST, THE REGIONAL NETWORKS ARE A ROUTING DEVICE: INECE names AECEN (Asian Environmental Compliance and Enforcement Network), AELERT (Australasian Environmental Law Enforcement and Regulators network) and RedLaFiCA (Red Latinoamericana de Fiscalización y Cumplimiento Ambiental) as part of the network — if you do not know which body enforces in your country, the regional network is a shorter list to search than the world. SECOND, ITS CITIZEN-SCIENCE POSITION IS LEVERAGE: INECE runs an ongoing webinar series on ‘how can citizen and community science contribute to environmental compliance and enforcement?’ — that the global network of enforcers is itself asking that question is citable when an agency dismisses community-gathered evidence. THIRD, IT SHOWS WHAT KIND OF BODY TO LOOK FOR: its named members include a superintendency, a protection agency, a ministry and a supreme court — which is why searching for ‘EPA’ by name fails outside the US. The Secretariat is the Environmental Law Institute, not a government; it keeps an online library of compliance and enforcement resources and runs training — a recent series on environmental and social impact assessment drew 161 people from 31 countries. Founded 1989, covering administrative, civil, criminal and judicial enforcement, with support from UNEP, the World Bank, the European Commission and the OECD. BE AWARE OF THE MEMBERSHIP WALL: members have exclusive access to INECE materials and capacity-building programmes. IN THIS COUNTRY: The Brazil Supreme Court co-chairs the Executive Planning Committee — a court, not an agency, which is unusual and tells you where environmental enforcement authority sits here.

trackers.name: FEMA — Fundo Especial de Meio Ambiente (Município de São Paulo)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY, CITY LEVEL: São Paulo's municipal environment fund, created by Lei nº 13.155 of 29/06/2001, redisciplined by Lei nº 14.887 of 15/01/2009 and regulated by Decretos 52.153 and 52.388 of 2011. READ THE PURPOSE CLAUSE: it funds projects for the sustainable use of natural resources, maintenance and recovery of environmental quality, research, and activities of control, inspection and defesa do meio ambiente — defence of the environment. A city fund that will pay for environmental defence work is unusual; most cover planting and education only. WHO CAN APPLY: Brazilian non-profit OSCIPs and NGOs, legally constituted, and public bodies — one edital required a minimum of 3 years' existence. You apply through editais de chamamento and must register in CENTS; the Comissão Técnica de Avaliação issues an opinion, and CONFEMA decides. Scale: Edital 11 put R$ 1.710 million behind 10 proposals. READ THIS FIRST: priorities are set annually by CADES, the municipal environment council, so write to this year's directives. SVMA, CADES and FEMA together form the local organ of SISNAMA inside the municipality, which is why a São Paulo fight is fought here and not only federally. Contact svmafema@prefeitura.sp.gov.br, Rua do Paraíso 387, 1º andar, tel (11) 5187-0301; awards are published in the Diário Oficial da Cidade.

trackers.name: Instituto Guaicuy — Assessoria Técnica Independente
trackers.desc: The lever to know in Minas Gerais: since early 2021 an Assessoria Técnica Independente is a RIGHT of dam-affected people under the state Política Estadual de Pessoas Atingidas por Barragens, and the adviser is chosen democratically by the affected communities themselves, not by the company. Guaicuy serves in that role for communities hit by the 2019 Vale dam collapse across Pompéu, Curvelo, Felixlândia, Três Marias, São Gonçalo do Abaeté, Martinho Campos, Morada Nova de Minas, Biquinhas, Paineiras and Abaeté, and for the Doutor dam decommissioning at Antônio Pereira, Ouro Preto. WHO IT SUITS: communities facing a mining company across a table with far better technical and legal resources — the ATI exists precisely to close that asymmetry, covering damage assessment, compensation matrices and monitoring of the reparation agreement.

trackers.name: NACAB — Núcleo de Assessoria às Comunidades Atingidas por Barragens
trackers.desc: A second Independent Technical Assistance body operating in Minas Gerais, working with communities affected by the Brumadinho collapse and, under licensing Condicionante 39, with thirteen communities across Alvorada de Minas, Dom Joaquim and Conceição do Mato Dentro. That condicionante is the point worth knowing: a mining licence can itself require the company to fund an independent adviser that the affected communities choose. WHO IT SUITS: dam- and mine-affected communities entering a reparation process — NACAB does the loss-and-damage survey, the valuation of what should be indemnified, and monitors delivery of what was agreed. Choose between the accredited ATIs rather than approaching one at random; the selection is run by the public prosecutors and defensoría.

trackers.name: FMDA — Fundo Municipal de Defesa Ambiental (Belo Horizonte)
trackers.desc: A CITY FUND AN INDIVIDUAL CAN APPLY TO. Created by Lei 4.253/85, the FMDA funds projects improving environmental quality in the municipality, proposed by organised civil society and/or by duly qualified individuals. Eligible: non-profit legal persons and natural persons domiciled in Belo Horizonte, NGOs, and direct and indirect administration bodies — a resident can apply in their own name, which is rarer than anything in the wealthy-country funds where the barrier is membership numbers or a half-million-euro project floor. Recorded round: R$ 240,000 through an edital published in the Diário Oficial do Município, with proposals delivered in person to the Secretaria Municipal de Meio Ambiente by the stated hour on the closing day. It funds recovery, maintenance or improvement of environmental quality. Questions to smma@pbh.gov.br.

trackers.name: Fundo de Conservação Ambiental (FCA) — Município do Rio de Janeiro
trackers.desc: CITY MONEY FOR CONSERVATION: the FCA is provided for in the sole paragraph of Art. 129 of Rio's Lei Orgânica, created by Lei Municipal nº 2.138 of 11 May 1994 and now regulated by Decreto nº 41.248 of 19 February 2016, which replaced the original 1994 decree. Attached to the city environment secretariat (SMAC), it finances environmental recovery and restoration, prevention of environmental damage, and environmental education. READ THIS BEFORE APPLYING — IT IS NOT AN OPEN GRANT: under Art. 4 of the regulating decree the resources go to projects developed by SMAC or agreed with it (conveniados), to payment for services executing specific projects, to management and planning instruments, and to running conservation units. A community group therefore needs a convênio with the secretariat rather than simply submitting a proposal — a materially different route from São Paulo's FEMA, which runs open editais. Approach SMAC about a convênio first.

trackers.name: SPVS (Paraná) — RPPNs e reservas próprias
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a Curitiba conservation organisation founded in 1984, an OSCIP since 2001, which owns and manages 19,000 hectares of its own reserves on the northern Paraná coast — Águas and Guaricica in Antonina, Papagaio-de-Cara-Roxa in Guaraqueçaba — and works with private owners to turn land into RPPNs, the only private protected-area category in the national SNUC system. USE IT: to get Atlantic Forest land in Paraná protected as an RPPN or acquired outright. The argument that lands with owners and mayors: Paraná's ICMS Ecológico redistributes a share of state tax to municipalities holding conservation units, so an RPPN pays the municipality real money every year — Antonina and Guaraqueçaba have drawn millions of reais on the back of SPVS reserves alone.

trackers.name: RPPNM Curitiba — Secretaria Municipal do Meio Ambiente
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: Curitiba's municipal environment secretariat runs the Reserva Particular do Patrimônio Natural Municipal, the city-level private reserve Brazil's first municipality created for URBAN green land. You apply to the SMMA through the PROCEC electronic portal with a management and conservation plan; if approved the reserve is created by municipal decree, in perpetuity and irrevocably, recorded against your title at the property register. Live and current — reserves were still being created by decree in 2026. USE IT: the incentives are the point, and they are financial. Full exemption from IPTU urban property tax on the wooded land, and transfer of 100% of the building rights you give up to unrestricted parts of the city — which you may sell on the construction market. Land stays yours; the reserve may be used for visitation, ecotourism, education and research. For an owner of a wooded urban lot under development pressure, this converts the threat into an asset.

trackers.name: Conselho Municipal do Meio Ambiente — the seat that controls the fund
trackers.desc: GET ONTO THE COUNCIL — IT DECIDES WHAT THE CITY FUND PAYS FOR. Under Curitiba's Lei nº 15.852 of 01/07/2021, the Conselho Municipal do Meio Ambiente is consultative, normative and deliberative: it analyses and approves the plan for applying the resources of the Fundo Municipal do Meio Ambiente and deliberates on its programmes, projects and money. It also decides at second administrative instance, on appeal, on fines and on gaps in environmental legislation — an appeal route inside the city, before any court. AND YOU CAN SIT ON IT: the council and its Technical Chambers are composed of representatives of the public authority, organised civil society and academia in equal numbers (de forma paritária). THE PATTERN IS NATIONAL: the model municipal environment fund statute has the fund administered by the environment secretariat in articulation with the municipal environment council, which defines the criteria and priorities for applying the money. In a Brazilian city, the council seat is worth more than any single grant application.

trackers.name: Idesam — Instituto de Conservação e Desenvolvimento Sustentável da Amazônia
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a Manaus-based institute working across the interior of Amazonas state, whose concrete offer to a community is technical assistance to get a Plano de Manejo Florestal written, certified and selling. Through the Cidades Florestais project, backed by the Fundo Amazônia and BNDES, it works with residents, settlers and extractivists in fourteen Amazonas municipalities; the Uatumã reserve association it supported won FSC certification and saw its oil price rise from R$1 to R$8 a kilo, with average income for 370 extractivists reaching close to R$3,000. USE IT: where community forest management is the realistic alternative to illegal logging on your territory, and you need the plan, the equipment and the buyer, not a lawyer.

trackers.name: Movimento Xingu Vivo Para Sempre
trackers.desc: Based in Altamira and formed in 2008 at the second Encontro dos Povos do Xingu, which brought together more than two thousand indigenous people, ribeirinhos, small farmers and fishers against Belo Monte. It is the movement of the affected themselves, working with territorial organisations, traditional communities, fishers, women's movements and periphery residents, and it has supported legal actions nationally and internationally alongside partner NGOs and the Federal Public Prosecutors' Office. It is now the main opposition to Belo Sun, which would be Brazil's largest open-pit gold mine with a tailings dam nearly three times the size of Brumadinho's. WHO IT SUITS: communities of the Middle Xingu and Volta Grande facing the dam's aftermath or the mine — including on where Belo Monte's royalties actually go, which it campaigns to put under community oversight.

trackers.name: Federal District
trackers.desc: Sub-national government portal (Brazil) — entry point to this unit's budget, procurement and finance information.

trackers.name: SEMARNAT Gaceta Ecológica + SINAT
trackers.desc: Mexico's weekly federal gazette of every project entering environmental impact evaluation (PEIA), with the SINAT system holding the underlying files. You CAN get: which projects entered evaluation this week and where, the MIA (impact statement) itself, resolutions approving or rejecting, and the legal trigger for demanding a consulta pública — you have 10 days from Gaceta publication to request one. You CAN'T get: state-level projects evaluated by state authorities. For activists: this is the early-warning system — read the Gaceta for your state weekly, and the 10-day consulta clock plus the MIA's own weaknesses are the two levers Mexican communities have used to stop everything from marinas to mines.

trackers.name: Centro Prodh (Miguel Agustín Pro Juárez)
trackers.desc: Jesuit-founded Mexican human-rights organization (est. 1988) based in Mexico City — defends victims of arbitrary detention, torture, enforced disappearance and extrajudicial execution through a multidisciplinary “integral defense” methodology combining strategic litigation, psychological and social accompaniment and advocacy; it has taken emblematic cases (including Ayotzinapa, Atenco and Tlatlaya) to the Inter-American Court and generated jurisprudence on due process, torture and the rights of indigenous prisoners.

trackers.name: Centro de Derechos Humanos Fray Bartolomé de Las Casas (FrayBa)
trackers.desc: The Centro de Derechos Humanos Fray Bartolmé de las Casa is a non-profit organisation that works to defend and promote the human rights of Indigenous peoples in the state of Chiapas, Mexico, through the promotion of peaceful and civil proposals.

trackers.name: Transparencia para el Pueblo
trackers.desc: National right-to-information authority; Transparencia para el Pueblo is the federal access-to-information body created in 2025 — a deconcentrated unit under the Secretaría Anticorrupción y Buen Gobierno that absorbed most functions of the abolished autonomous INAI, handling federal transparency appeals and the National Transparency Platform, Mexico.

trackers.name: CEMDA — Centro Mexicano de Derecho Ambiental
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Mexico's principal environmental-law organisation and a founding member of AIDA. Litigates environmental cases and supports communities against harmful projects. WHO IT SUITS: Mexican communities challenging permits or impact assessments. NOTE: canonical domain not yet verified; named as an AIDA founder on aida-americas.org. SOURCING UPGRADED, NOT CLOSED: the domain remains unverified, but the organisation is now confirmed from the Inter-American Court of Human Rights' own published participant list for Advisory Opinion OC-32/2025 — filing alongside Healthy Reefs for Healthy People and AIDA, and separately with NuestroFuturo A.C., Iniciativa Climática de México, the Comité Campesino del Altiplano and the Unión Verapacense de Organizaciones Campesinas. That is stronger evidence of capability than a website would be — it demonstrates international litigation capacity, and OC-32/2025 is the proceeding this map's other Inter-American entries should be read against. CEMDA's own account: 33 years of work on the conviction that a healthy environment is not a privilege but a right, currently including the Maya communities of Hopelchén before the Supreme Court on their right to a healthy environment, water free of toxics and protection of their territory from pesticides.

trackers.name: AIDA — Interamerican Association for Environmental Defense
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a regional organisation of Latin American environmental legal experts providing FREE legal and scientific support to communities and local groups, using international and inter-American human-rights law. Track record includes stopping a large dam in Mexico, halting clear-cutting of native forest in Chile, and the La Oroya smelter ruling in Peru. WHO IT SUITS: communities whose national system has already failed them and whose fight needs to go to an international body. AIDA works across Latin America, so it may be able to act in your country even if it has no office there — ask.

trackers.name: Fondo Mexicano para la Conservación de la Naturaleza (FMCN)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: Mexico's national environmental fund since 1994, channelling endowment income and international money through periodic convocatorias — open calls for non-reimbursable grants, including Fomafur (fire management and restoration) and Conserva Aves. WHO IT SUITS: legally constituted local civil-society organisations — FMCN's own term is Organizaciones Locales Legalmente Constituidas — not individuals or unincorporated collectives. HOW IT DIFFERS: an endowed fund, not a campaign donor; frame the ask as long-term protection and management of a defined area.

trackers.name: Pronatura Noroeste — private land-protection instruments
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the northwest arm of Mexico's oldest conservation NGO, working across nine states and reporting 266,000 hectares protected with private legal instruments — outright land purchase and servidumbres ecológicas, the ecological easement under which one owner permanently restricts development on their parcel in favour of another. USE IT: to get a threatened parcel bought or permanently encumbered instead of fought permit by permit, especially coastal wetland and estuary in Baja California, BCS, Sonora and Sinaloa.

trackers.name: FASOL — Fondo Acción Solidaria
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a Mexican fund constituted in 2007 that moves flexible money straight to grassroots groups, collectives and communities defending their territory — small seed contributions rather than big project grants, with a capacity-building programme and mentoring network attached. WHO IT SUITS: unincorporated collectives and communities, not only registered A.C.s — this is the door that stays open when the big national funds demand legal personality. It explicitly funds responses to threats against territory and collective rights. HOW IT DIFFERS from FMCN: grassroots-facing philanthropy built to reach groups nobody else will bank. NOTE the canonical domain is fasol-ac.org, not fasol.org.mx.

trackers.name: Centro Mexicano Pro Bono
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a clearinghouse that brokers free legal accompaniment from commercial law firms to communities and civil-society organisations, with a stated environmental-defence line covering constitutional, administrative, environmental and regulatory litigation — amparo proceedings, filings and appeals before authorities, and legal opinions. For a small organisation it can also cover the unglamorous work: reviewing a contract clause, fixing your legal structure, meeting your compliance obligations. WHO IT SUITS: community groups and CSOs with no budget for counsel. DISCLOSE: the lawyers come from commercial firms donating time, so conflicts with a specific company are a real possibility — name the developer you are up against when you first make contact and ask them to run a conflicts check before you share anything.

trackers.name: IDEA — Instituto de Derecho Ambiental A.C.
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a public-interest environmental law office constituted in Guadalajara in 1997, founded expressly because western Mexico had no public-interest environmental lawyers. Its stated work is supporting indigenous communities defending their natural resources and promoting the environmental and territorial rights of communities in situations of vulnerability. Its founders ran the first environmental law workshops in Mexico with the Environmental Law Alliance Worldwide, alongside the newly formed CEMDA. WHO IT SUITS: indigenous and rural communities in the occidente — Jalisco and neighbouring states — where CEMDA and AIDA are Mexico City-centred. NOTE: its canonical domain could not be verified live this session; it is listed by the Mexican Committee of the IUCN at comitemexicanouicn.org, which is the route to reach it. A public-interest law practice founded in 1997 in Guadalajara, created because western Mexico had no public-interest environmental lawyers. Its stated mission is accompanying and educating communities that cannot afford a competent legal defence, with a specific focus on indigenous communities defending their natural resources and on territorial rights. USE ITS PRECEDENT: after the 1996 LGEEPA amendments made Mexico's citizen complaint non-binding, IDEA exhausted domestic remedies and took the Lake Chapala case to the CEC — the North American Commission for Environmental Cooperation (submission SEM-97-007, later Chapala II) — a documented escalation route when a domestic complaint has no force. It works with ELAW and with Universidad de Guadalajara researchers who build and document the cases, and is a member of the Mexican Committee of the IUCN; address Isla Española 2859, López de Legaspi, 44950 Guadalajara, Jalisco. NOTE: not CEMDA, and not the Paraguayan Instituto de Derecho y Economía Ambiental, which shares the acronym.

trackers.name: CompraNet
trackers.desc: Mexico's federal public-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Mexico, and for how much.

trackers.name: Mexicanos Contra la Corrupción y la Impunidad (MCCI)
trackers.desc: Major Mexican anti-corruption civil-society organisation (since 2015) combining investigative journalism, strategic litigation and research. Exposes ghost companies, procurement fraud and gaps in officials' asset declarations, and pushes for a robust public-integrity system.

trackers.name: datos.gob.mx
trackers.desc: National — Mexican federal open data portal. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Mexico.

trackers.name: DeclaraNet (Declaraciones Patrimoniales)
trackers.desc: National — federal asset & interest declarations of public officials.

trackers.name: Fundar, Centro de Análisis e Investigación
trackers.desc: Independent Mexican civil-society research organisation (est. 1999) whose core work is budget analysis — monitoring public expenditure and whether budget priorities are realised. Here you can trace how Mexico's public budget is allocated and whether spending matches stated priorities.

trackers.name: IMCO (Mexican Institute for Competitiveness)
trackers.desc: Non-partisan Mexican think-tank producing evidence-based public-finance, competitiveness and anti-corruption analysis and policy proposals. Here you can trace Mexico's public-finance, competitiveness and anti-corruption analysis from IMCO.

trackers.name: MAR Fund — Small Grants Program (Mesoamerican Reef)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: an ecoregional fund created in 2004 by the national conservation funds of Belize, Guatemala, Honduras and Mexico, running a Small Grants Program by competitive Call for Proposals — now past its 17th call — with two windows, the Traditional Window and the Reef Rescue Initiative. WHO IT SUITS: civil-society groups working on coastal and marine protected areas anywhere in the Mesoamerican Reef System. HOW IT DIFFERS: transnational by design, so a project spanning the reef across two countries is a fit here where a national funder would balk.

trackers.name: Quinto Elemento Lab
trackers.desc: Mexican investigative journalism lab probing corruption and abuse of public resources.

trackers.name: Registro Público de Comercio (SIGER)
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: companies in Mexico — find the Registro Público de Comercio of entities, directors and filings.

trackers.name: SCJN – Semanario Judicial
trackers.desc: Official jurisprudence (Semanario Judicial de la Federación) of the Supreme Court. · Find here: Mexico's Semanario Judicial de la Federación — Supreme Court theses and judgments.

trackers.name: Auditoría Superior de la Federación
trackers.desc: Mexico's supreme audit institution. Here you can trace public-audit findings on waste, irregularity and misspending in Mexico.

trackers.name: Cámara de Diputados de México
trackers.desc: Official Mexican Chamber of Deputies site with legislative information, voting records, and parliamentary proceedings. — Holds to account: lobbyists & influence-seekers — find who is lobbying whom, and meetings held.

trackers.name: INEGI
trackers.desc: Mexico's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Mexico.

trackers.name: Tribunal Superior de Justicia de la Ciudad de México
trackers.desc: Tribunal Superior de Justicia de la Ciudad de México — tribunal (Mexico).

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Justice of the Nation
trackers.desc: Supreme Court of Justice of the Nation — supreme court (Mexico).

trackers.name: Transparencia Presupuestaria
trackers.desc: Mexico's open budget and public-spending portal. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Mexico.

trackers.name: PAOT — denuncia ciudadana por uso de suelo (Ciudad de México)
trackers.desc: HOW TO FILE, CITY LEVEL: the Procuraduría Ambiental y del Ordenamiento Territorial exists to defend the rights of Mexico City residents in environmental and territorial-ordering matters, and anyone may denounce acts or omissions that breach those rules — with violations of land use among its most-denounced categories, alongside damage to green areas. A development operating outside what the alcaldía's urban development programme permits is precisely what it takes. THE TRAP THAT LOSES CASES: an online submission is only a pre-denuncia, and you have 3 working days to ratify it — if you do not, it is treated as never filed. Scale: 4,326 citizen complaints received January–June 2025. It issues numbered written resolutions, publishes them, and notifies both the complainant and the environment secretariat's inspection directorate, so there is a public record and a named recipient. Routes: the form at paot.org.mx, open 24 hours, or 55 5265 0780 (option *), Monday–Thursday 9–18, Friday 9–15, extensions 15410, 15430, 15440, 15450; offices at Medellín 202, Col. Roma Sur, Alcaldía Cuauhtémoc, CP 06700.

trackers.name: SEDEMA — which body takes which complaint (Ciudad de México)
trackers.desc: FILE IT WITH THE RIGHT BODY OR LOSE THE TIME: Mexico City's environment secretariat publishes which authority handles what, and the distinctions matter when a build is already underway. For a change of land use — activities on a plot not permitted by the alcaldía's urban development programme — the competent body is the Instituto de Verificación Administrativa, and the complaint may also be filed with PAOT. For commercialisation, possession or harm to wildlife it goes to the federal PROFEPA, not to the city. For domestic animal cruelty, PAOT, the Secretaría de Seguridad Ciudadana's Brigada Animal, or the alcaldía. USE IT: check this page before filing — a complaint lodged with the wrong authority costs weeks a construction schedule will not give back.

trackers.name: Sociedad de Historia Natural Niparajá
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: founded in La Paz in 1990, and one of the few Mexican organisations that buys land outright for conservation — from 2001 it purchased property on the open market to create the Reserva Natural El Portezuelo, now over 7,300 hectares certified with CONANP as an Área Destinada Voluntariamente a la Conservación. Its land programme covers 350,000 hectares of priority terrestrial and coastal habitat, with a stated goal of a million toward a Sierras Giganta y Guadalupe biosphere reserve. It also built Mexico's first network of Zonas de Refugio Pesquero, in the San Cosme–Punta Coyote corridor, with community surveillance backed by CONAPESCA and PROFEPA. USE IT: to get a Baja California Sur property bought or certified as an ADVC, and for the water-quality monitoring it uses to argue the Sierra watershed against open-pit mining.

trackers.name: Cooperativa AMBIO — programa Scolel'te
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a cooperative based in San Cristóbal de las Casas running Scolel'te — Tseltal for 'the tree that grows' — started in 1997 with campesino communities of the Selva Lacandona, ECOSUR and the University of Edinburgh, and the longest-running programme of its kind in the voluntary carbon market anywhere. It pays landholders directly for reforesting and sustainably managing their own land under the Plan Vivo standard, a methodology that originated in Chiapas. WHO IT SUITS: ejidatarios, communities and smallholders in Chiapas who hold their land — over 1,500 participate and more than 2,500 families receive payments through some 100 organised working groups, including Tojolabal, Tsotsil, Tseltal, Lacandón and Chol communities. You need tenure and a working group, not a legal case. HOW IT DIFFERS: recurring payments to the landholder, not a project grant to an NGO.

trackers.name: EDUCA — Servicios para una Educación Alternativa
trackers.desc: Thirty years old and fifteen of them accompanying community defence against mining in Oaxaca, where its own research counts 294 live mining concessions as of 2020, some 5% of the state under concession, and at least 66 projects labelled 'small' hydroelectric — in one case nine on a single river. It accompanied the eleven Valles Centrales communities that took amparos against concessions granted without their consent and won a suspensión de plano. WHO IT SUITS: agrarian and municipal authorities and community assemblies, not individuals — the amparos are brought by the assembly. It convenes through the Colectivo Oaxaqueño en Defensa de los Territorios and REDECOM, the state community defenders network, so it is also the way into a wider bloc.

trackers.name: Pronatura Veracruz
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the Veracruz arm of Pronatura, working the windward slope of the Cofre de Perote on cloud-forest protection with Rainforest Trust funding, and building protection around ejido common lands and local owners rather than around them — the areas it protects include the Reserva Ecológica La Cortadura, the Reserva Campesina Parcela 23 and the Reserva Privada de Conservación Ejido Las Carabinas. USE IT: if you hold or share ejido land in Veracruz and want it recognised as a campesino or private conservation reserve, and for help standing up a community patrol brigade to watch it afterwards.

trackers.name: Coahuila
trackers.desc: Sub-national government portal (Mexico) — entry point to this unit's budget, procurement and finance information.

trackers.name: Veracruz
trackers.desc: Sub-national government portal (Mexico) — entry point to this unit's budget, procurement and finance information.

trackers.name: Mexico City
trackers.desc: Sub-national government portal (Mexico) — entry point to this unit's budget, procurement and finance information.

trackers.name: Procuraduría de los Derechos Humanos (PDH)
trackers.desc: Procuraduría de los Derechos Humanos (PDH) — Guatemala’s Human Rights Ombudsman — the authority overseeing the Law on Access to Public Information, monitoring compliance and receiving complaints. — Holds to account: Guatemala’s public bodies on disclosure — find access-to-information compliance reports and complaints handling.

trackers.name: Centro para la Acción Legal en Derechos Humanos (CALDH)
trackers.desc: Guatemalan human-rights legal center — strategic litigation for indigenous peoples and victims of the armed conflict (including the Ixil genocide and enforced-disappearance cases), defense of criminalized human-rights defenders, and Inter-American system casework. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: CALDH IS NOT AN ENVIRONMENTAL ORGANISATION. Its core work is transitional justice — representing victims of violations committed during Guatemala's 36-year armed conflict. ITS RELEVANCE HERE IS PRECISE: it provides legal advice and representation to current human rights defenders, and states that facing the grave situation of defenders in Guatemala it will be alerting at national and international level about the attacks and acts of criminalisation and the risks they face in the legitimate exercise of the defence of human rights. ‘Actos de criminalización’ is the operative phrase — where a land defender is facing charges rather than bringing a claim, that is the framing under which CALDH works, and the international alerting is itself protective, not merely advocacy. It also strengthens local organisations and victims' groups, particularly women survivors. ITS INTER-AMERICAN CAPACITY IS PROVEN, NOT CLAIMED: CALDH constituted itself as petitioner on 24 August 1993 in Case 10.686 v Guatemala, on the forced disappearance of María Tiu Tojín and her daughter Josefa, where the State was found responsible including under article 19 (rights of the child) read with article 1(1). This map records the Inter-American route repeatedly — Suriname, Paraguay, Nicaragua — and the practical barrier is almost always finding a petitioner organisation with that experience. AN ARGUMENT WORTH BORROWING from its filing: the judgment is a measure of reparation, but so is the opportunity to be heard, to recount what happened without being accused of being resentful communists, to speak when fear has often silenced them — of particular value where the victims belong to indigenous peoples who have been denied that. The process has reparative value independent of the outcome, which is a reason to pursue an international route even where enforcement is doubtful. Founded 1983, official after the 1996 Peace Accords; address 6a. Avenida 1-73, zona 1, Centro Histórico, Guatemala City. It runs the Casa de la Memoria ‘Kaji Tulam’, a public space exhibiting the impositions and resistances of those who inhabited these territories — a venue as well as a record.

trackers.name: UDEFEGUA — Unidad de Protección a Defensoras y Defensores de Derechos Humanos
trackers.desc: Guatemala’s human-rights-defenders protection organisation, operating since 2000 and independent since 2009. It registers, verifies and accompanies attacks on defenders — including Indigenous authorities, journalists and land and justice activists — provides an integrated protection system and, increasingly, direct legal defence against criminalisation (for example taking on the technical defence of prosecuted journalists), and publishes the country’s emblematic annual report on the situation of defenders. It also supports defenders across Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua and southern Mexico.

trackers.name: Fundación Defensores de la Naturaleza
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: in 1990 became the first NGO in Latin America legally entrusted with managing a state protected area; now co-manages four covering about 5% of Guatemala, and separately creates and runs private and municipal reserves, mainly in the dry Motagua valley. USE IT: to get a threatened property declared and managed as a private or municipal reserve, and for a partner with standing inside the protected-areas system.

trackers.name: CALAS — Centro de Acción Legal-Ambiental y Social de Guatemala
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Guatemalan environmental-law organisation that has repeatedly stopped mines in court. It filed the constitutional amparo against the Progreso VII Derivada mining licence at La Puya on the ground that indigenous communities were never consulted as ILO Convention 169 requires, and was the amparo petitioner in the Escobal / San Rafael case — both recorded on the Ministry of Energy and Mines' own case pages, and in both the courts suspended the operation. WHO IT SUITS: indigenous and campesino communities facing a licence granted without consultation, and defenders being criminalised. It works on collective rights rather than individual claims, and it also joins criminal proceedings as a plaintiff where officials or companies have broken the environmental framework. NOTE: its canonical domain could not be verified live this session — reach it through the case records on the Ministry of Energy and Mines site, mem.gob.gt. CALAS has no website of its own that could be verified across three rounds of searching, so the link is its Front Line Defenders profile, which carries the case history and urgent appeals — a guessed domain was deliberately avoided for an organisation whose people are targets. Founded by the human rights defender Yuri Melini and based in Guatemala City, it works through incidencia política on environmental governance, community participation and the collective rights of indigenous communities in relation to the environment, and has run a documentation centre since 2006. UNDERSTAND THE RISK BEFORE MAKING CONTACT: CALAS has actively denounced abuses by mining companies, in particular the transnational Tahoe Resources and its Guatemalan subsidiary Minera San Rafael, and its director Rafael Maldonado has received death threats over that conflict; Front Line Defenders records harassment and threats against Guatemalan defenders rising from 2012. USE IT: for a mining or indigenous-territory case this is the organisation with the litigation record — approach it through Front Line Defenders rather than through an unverified address.

trackers.name: Plaza Pública
trackers.desc: Guatemalan investigative outlet examining power, corruption and public money.

trackers.name: Datos Abiertos Guatemala
trackers.desc: National — official government open data / budget portal. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this is the broad budget/open-data hub for how money is allocated overall — for the specific firms winning tenders use the procurement portal, and for findings of misspending use the supreme audit institution. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Guatemala.

trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: an ecoregional fund created in 2004 by the national conservation funds of Belize, Guatemala, Honduras and Mexico, running a Small Grants Program by competitive Call for Proposals — now past its 17th call — with two windows, the Traditional Window and the Reef Rescue Initiative. WHO IT SUITS: civil-society groups working on coastal and marine protected areas anywhere in the Mesoamerican Reef System. HOW IT DIFFERS: transnational by design, so a project spanning the reef across two countries is a fit here where a national funder would balk.

Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Guatemala.

trackers.name: Organismo Judicial de Guatemala
trackers.desc: Official judiciary portal with jurisprudence and court services. · Find here: the portal and case information of Guatemala's Judiciary (Organismo Judicial).

trackers.name: Registro Mercantil
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: companies in Guatemala — find the mercantile registry of entities, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Defensoría del Pueblo del Ecuador
trackers.desc: Defensoría del Pueblo del Ecuador — Ecuador’s Ombudsman — the guarantor body for the Organic Law on Transparency and Access to Public Information (LOTAIP), monitoring compliance and handling complaints. — Holds to account: Ecuador’s public bodies on disclosure — find LOTAIP compliance reports, complaints handling and guidance.

trackers.name: Fundación Regional de Asesoría en Derechos Humanos (INREDH)
trackers.desc: Ecuadorian human-rights foundation (est. 1993) — provides legal assistance and accompaniment to victims of grave rights violations and their families, litigates cases of enforced disappearance, torture and criminalized protest, and defends indigenous-peoples’ and nature rights.

trackers.name: ECOLEX — Corporación de Gestión y Derecho Ambiental
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an Ecuadorian environmental-law NGO founded in 1998 with a standing Litigio Ambiental practice and two tools most groups never hear about — Línea Verde, a free national phone and email line for reporting environmental damage and getting advice on your rights and the rights of nature, and a community paralegal programme that trains a recognised local leader in environmental, agrarian and organisational law inside their own community. WHO IT SUITS: rural, indigenous and peri-urban communities facing damage or a land conflict who need a first legal read at no cost, and groups that want their own trained paralegal rather than a lawyer flown in. The site has not been refreshed since 2016, so confirm current staffing by phone.

trackers.name: Fondo del Biocorredor Amazónico (Fondo BCA)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the vehicle channelling Ecuador's December 2024 debt-for-nature conversion, which refinanced roughly USD 1,530 million of sovereign debt and secured hundreds of millions for conservation. It launched its first grant convocatoria in April 2026, funding conservation, restoration and bioeconomy projects, with targets of 4.6 million hectares of protected areas better managed, 1.8 million hectares of additional forest and wetland protected, 18,000 km of rivers safeguarded and 40,000 hectares restored. WHO IT SUITS: organisations working in the Ecuadorian Amazon. Selection weights technical viability and management of social and environmental risk, so a community proposal will need a technical partner. HOW IT DIFFERS: new money on a fixed programme timetable — the early calls are the accessible ones.

trackers.name: Ministerio de Ambiente y Energía — Convocatorias (Ecuador)
trackers.desc: Ecuador's national environmental authority, which publishes its open calls on a standing Convocatorias page. You CAN get: grant and selection calls aimed at civil society — recent ones include support for Indigenous peoples' initiatives in the Putumayo-Içá basin under a GEF-financed, World Bank-implemented project, and the executing-entity selection for the Amazon Biocorridor Fund — alongside the ministry's public notices to affected residents about environmental registrations for specific operations. You CAN'T get: any assurance a call is still open; dates pass quickly and the page is not archived. For activists: the same page carries the citizen-notification notices, so it is worth watching for the first public sign that something is being permitted near you.

trackers.name: COICA — Coordinadora de las Organizaciones Indígenas de la Cuenca Amazónica
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the basin-wide confederation of Amazonian Indigenous organisations, founded to act for 511 Indigenous peoples across the nine Amazon countries, around 66 of them in voluntary isolation or initial contact. It works through one national member organisation per country — in this country that is CONFENIAE, Confederación de las Nacionalidades Indígenas de la Amazonía Ecuatoriana — and its governing Council brings those presidents together. Its standing work areas are territorial rights and natural resources, human and sociocultural rights, and international law, and it has issued a formal declaration on the defence of Amazonian Indigenous defenders. USE IT: go to CONFENIAE first — COICA is the regional weight behind a national organisation, not a direct service. It is the route to carry a territorial case or a threat against leaders from your community into regional and international forums.

trackers.name: SERCOP – Compras Públicas
trackers.desc: Ecuador's national public-procurement service. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Ecuador, and for how much.

trackers.name: Contraloría General del Estado

trackers.name: Senace — EVA environmental certification registry
trackers.desc: Peru's national reviewer of the biggest projects' environmental studies (EIA-d) in mining, energy, hydrocarbons, transport, agriculture and waste, with the EVA single-window where every study is filed. You CAN get: the full EIA, its resolutions, the company and consultant behind a project, its current stage, and a formal channel to submit citizen observations during participación ciudadana. You CAN'T get: projects below the detailed-EIA threshold (those sit with sector ministries or regions). For activists: when a mine or pipeline is announced near your community, pull its EIA here before it's approved — the comment window is your legal opening, and the study's own baseline data becomes your evidence.

trackers.name: OEFA — environmental enforcement + SINADA complaints
trackers.desc: Peru's environmental enforcement agency for mining, energy, fisheries and industry, with public enforcement reporting (PIFA portal) and SINADA, where any citizen can file an environmental complaint. You CAN get: supervision and sanction records against named companies, administrative measures, and a formal complaint channel that obliges a response. You CAN'T get: criminal prosecution (that's the Fiscalía Ambiental) or enforcement in sectors held by regional EFAs. For activists: a contaminated river or illegal discharge becomes actionable the moment it's a SINADA case number — and a company's OEFA sanction history is ammunition in any campaign against its next project.

trackers.name: Autoridad Nacional de Transparencia y Acceso a la Información Pública (ANTAIP)
trackers.desc: Autoridad Nacional de Transparencia y Acceso a la Información Pública (ANTAIP) — Peru’s national authority for transparency and access to public information (within the Ministry of Justice and Human Rights). — Holds to account: Peru’s public bodies on disclosure — find access-to-information guidance, supervision and reports.

trackers.name: Manolo (manolo.rocks)
trackers.desc: Civic tool scraping Peru's official visitor/interest-management logs to expose who meets public officials. — Holds to account: those who meet Peruvian officials — find a civic tool scraping official visitor logs to expose who met whom.

trackers.name: Tribunal de Transparencia y Acceso a la Informacion Publica (Peru)
trackers.desc: Peru's Transparency and Access to Information Tribunal, the last administrative instance when a public body refuses a request. You CAN get: a free appeal, filed online through the gob.pe mesa de partes, which the Tribunal must resolve within 10 working days; the Ministry of Justice publishes a model appeal form you can adapt. The deadline is 15 working days from an EXPRESS refusal — but where the body simply stayed silent, a tacit denial, there is NO time limit, so an old unanswered request is still live. The Tribunal applies the exceptions in articles 15 to 17 restrictively: an agency stamping a document reservado without justifying it has no effect. You CAN'T get: enforcement beyond the administrative route. For activists: use it for withheld permit files, inspection reports or concession records. WHEN NOT TO USE IT — the useful part: you do NOT have to exhaust this route. A habeas data action goes straight to a civil judge within 60 working days of the refusal, so if the matter is urgent, go to court instead of appealing here.

trackers.name: Comision de Derechos Humanos (COMISEDH)
trackers.desc: Peru Comision de Derechos Humanos is a non-profit association that is dedicated to the protection and promotion of human rights in Peru. It mainly works on combatting torture and sexual violence against women and girls. It also supports transitional justice and Indigenous people’s rights.

trackers.name: AIDA — Interamerican Association for Environmental Defense
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a regional organisation of Latin American environmental legal experts providing FREE legal and scientific support to communities and local groups, using international and inter-American human-rights law. Track record includes stopping a large dam in Mexico, halting clear-cutting of native forest in Chile, and the La Oroya smelter ruling in Peru. WHO IT SUITS: communities whose national system has already failed them and whose fight needs to go to an international body. AIDA works across Latin America, so it may be able to act in your country even if it has no office there — ask.

trackers.name: Profonanpe — fondo ambiental del Perú
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: Peru's national environmental fund, running Bosques Tropicales — built from the Peru–US debt swap, awarding non-repayable grants — and Conserva Aves calls aimed squarely at creating new subnational protected areas: regional, municipal, communal, indigenous, public or private. WHO IT SUITS: indigenous organisations, native communities and local or regional groups with a recognised record of work with indigenous and local people, plus holders of the various conservation titles; universities qualify only with community participation. HOW IT DIFFERS: it also sub-grants climate finance directly to indigenous organisations, so a federation can hold the money itself.

trackers.name: DAR — Derecho, Ambiente y Recursos Naturales
trackers.desc: A Peruvian non-profit working since 2004 on Amazon governance — hydrocarbons, roads, the Hidrovía Amazónica, energy projects and the finance behind them. WHO TO ENLIST for technical and policy backup on consulta previa, environmental impact assessment, the Escazú Agreement and defender protection; it has backed successful court actions brought by indigenous federations, though partner lawyers usually run the litigation. You CAN: use its free guides and consulta-previa protocols, including autonomous protocols written by federations themselves. For activists: strongest while a project is still at the permitting or financing stage, where the leverage is procedure.

trackers.name: COICA — Coordinadora de las Organizaciones Indígenas de la Cuenca Amazónica
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the basin-wide confederation of Amazonian Indigenous organisations, founded to act for 511 Indigenous peoples across the nine Amazon countries, around 66 of them in voluntary isolation or initial contact. It works through one national member organisation per country — in this country that is AIDESEP, Asociación Interétnica de Desarrollo de la Selva Peruana — and its governing Council brings those presidents together. Its standing work areas are territorial rights and natural resources, human and sociocultural rights, and international law, and it has issued a formal declaration on the defence of Amazonian Indigenous defenders. USE IT: go to AIDESEP first — COICA is the regional weight behind a national organisation, not a direct service. It is the route to carry a territorial case or a threat against leaders from your community into regional and international forums.

trackers.name: Defensa Pública — 34 district directorates and the ALEGRA centres
trackers.desc: A FREE LAWYER THROUGH 34 DISTRICT DIRECTORATES nationwide, grounded in Article 139, numeral 16 of the Constitution guaranteeing effective access to justice, particularly for people in situations of vulnerability. HOW IT WORKS: go to a Centro de Asistencia Legal Gratuita (ALEGRA) with your DNI and any evidence; a public defender opens a carpeta de defensoría setting out what to do, and the case is tracked through it. The lawyer will accompany you to the relevant institution. You sign a declaración jurada of your economic situation. THE PART THAT MATTERS UNDER DEADLINE: they verify your situation within 20 days and the defence continues meanwhile — only if you are found able to pay does a Resolución de No Gratuidad follow. Representation starts before means are proven. CHECK SCOPE FIRST: the named specialities are criminal defence and assistance to victims of family and sexual violence, abandonment and offences against life, body and health, plus matters listed in the regulations to Ley 29360 as amended by Decreto Legislativo 1407 — a land or environmental matter is not a named speciality, so confirm it falls within the regulation. It also runs extrajudicial conciliation and popular arbitration.

trackers.name: Defensoría del Pueblo — what it can and cannot do for you
trackers.desc: USE IT FOR PRESSURE, NOT FOR A REMEDY. A constitutionally autonomous body created by the 1993 Constitution, with offices throughout the territory and a free line 0-800-15-170, handling complaints, queries and requests from citizens whose rights have been violated. It has an Adjuntía de Medio Ambiente, Servicios Públicos y Pueblos Indígenas and publishes guidance for human rights defenders, and it warns publicly about the risk of social conflict in communities — which is worth triggering early. BUT KNOW ITS LIMITS BEFORE YOU RELY ON IT: it does not act as judge or prosecutor, does not substitute any authority, does not issue judgments, and does not impose fines or sanctions. It produces reports with recommendations or exhortations whose force rests on persuasion and the strength of technical, ethical and legal argument. Governed by Ley Orgánica 26520, amended by Leyes 29882 and 32028.

trackers.name: Profonanpe — competitive funds, including money to create protected areas
trackers.desc: PERU'S ENVIRONMENTAL FUND, AND SOME OF IT PAYS COMMUNITIES DIRECTLY. Bosques Tropicales gives non-repayable grants funded by the Peru–United States debt swap, and its eligible applicants are exactly the right ones here: local organisations that directly use the natural resources of their own territory; indigenous, local and regional organisations with recognised experience working with indigenous peoples; holders of the various conservation and sustainable-management modalities; and universities with the participation of indigenous communities. CONSERVA AVES IS THE ONE TO NOTE IF YOU WANT LAND PROTECTED: it finances initiatives promoting the creation and/or expansion of subnational protected areas for threatened, endemic and declining migratory birds — it pays for making protection happen, not just for studying it. Other competitions fund bionegocios in Loreto, Amazonas, San Martín, Madre de Dios, Puno and Cusco, and ventures around ANP, ACP and ACR areas.

trackers.name: Fondo Concursable Puna — check which window you are in
trackers.desc: CLIMATE ADAPTATION MONEY IN 58 DISTRICTS of Arequipa, Apurímac, Cusco, Puno and Lima (Yauyos). THE WARNING FIRST — NOT ALL WINDOWS ARE GRANTS: in the second call, of 40 preselected initiatives 36 were in ventana 1, which is repayable funds, and only 4 in ventana 2, non-repayable. Ventana 2 targets micro and small enterprises, communal enterprises, producer associations and cooperatives with clear commercial objectives; ventana 3 requires a business plan approved and an agreement signed with Agroideas. Know which window you are applying to before treating the money as a grant. INCOMPLETE LEGAL STATUS IS NOT FATAL: campesino communities, producer associations and cooperatives in the process of formalisation may apply with the support of civil society organisations. ELIGIBLE MEASURES: conservation and restoration of bofedales and qochas, agroforestry, restoration of native forests and of andenes and terraces, integrated soil fertility management, infiltration ditches, contour and conservation agriculture, sustainable pasture management. EXPECT TWO STAGES: preselected initiatives go through diagnosis and planning with accompanying organisations before final selection.

trackers.name: FENAMAD — Federación Nativa del Río Madre de Dios y Afluentes
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the indigenous federation of Madre de Dios, running since the mid-1980s and defending the collective rights of Harakbut, Yine, Matsigenka, Ese Eja, Awajún, Kichwa Runa, Amahuaca and Shipibo communities, plus peoples in isolation and initial contact (PIACI), which it has worked on since the mid-1990s. Its practical work is legal security of territory: demarcation, georeferencing and legal recognition of communal land, run with the regional government's land titling directorate, and resizing Bosques de Producción Permanente that overlap communal territory. USE IT: where illegal gold mining or logging is entering titled communal land. It receives confidential satellite monitoring reports from Conservación Amazónica's MAAP project identifying which communities are being invaded. NOTE the domain is fenamad.com.pe, not .org.pe.

trackers.name: Grufides (Cajamarca)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Cajamarca organisation that advises, trains in rights and provides legal defence to communities whose eco-territorial rights are being violated — the region concentrating Peru's largest mining investment and, per the Defensoría del Pueblo, a long-running cluster of socio-environmental conflicts. It brought the amparo in the Conga case and took it to the Latin American Water Tribunal. WHO IT SUITS: campesino communities, rondas and water committees facing a mine, a hydroelectric project or informal mining. It also runs an Observatorio de Conflictos with case files, mining-concession maps and reports naming operators — useful before you have a lawyer at all — and tracks criminalisation of protest, which matters if leaders are already being prosecuted.

trackers.name: PRODHAB — Agencia de Protección de Datos de los Habitantes
trackers.desc: PRODHAB — Agencia de Protección de Datos de los Habitantes — Costa Rica’s national data-protection / information authority, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: CEDARENA — Centro de Derecho Ambiental y de los Recursos Naturales
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Costa Rica's environmental and natural-resources law centre, a founding member of AIDA, working on environmental law and land and resource rights. WHO IT SUITS: Costa Rican environmental permitting and land-rights disputes. NOTE: canonical domain not yet verified; named as an AIDA founder on aida-americas.org. SOURCING UPGRADED, NOT CLOSED: the domain remains unverified, but the organisation is confirmed from the Inter-American Court of Human Rights' own published participant list for Advisory Opinion OC-32/2025, appearing as Asociación Centro de Derecho Ambiental y los Recursos Naturales. A body on the participant list of the Court's climate advisory opinion has demonstrated international litigation capacity — which is what you would have wanted the website to tell you.

trackers.name: AIDA — Interamerican Association for Environmental Defense
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a regional organisation of Latin American environmental legal experts providing FREE legal and scientific support to communities and local groups, using international and inter-American human-rights law. Track record includes stopping a large dam in Mexico, halting clear-cutting of native forest in Chile, and the La Oroya smelter ruling in Peru. WHO IT SUITS: communities whose national system has already failed them and whose fight needs to go to an international body. AIDA works across Latin America, so it may be able to act in your country even if it has no office there — ask.

trackers.name: Asociación Costa Rica por Siempre
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: administrator of several standing Costa Rican conservation funds — the Fideicomiso Costa Rica por Siempre, SAVIA from the first US debt-for-nature swap, the second swap, and the Fondo Azul — supporting around 45 priority protected areas a year through open convocatorias. WHO IT SUITS: SAVIA calls target social organisations across six regions; the marine window has been open to natural and legal persons, national and foreign, which is unusually wide. HOW IT DIFFERS: an endowment tied to national protected-area commitments, so proposals strengthening a declared área silvestre protegida land best.

HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM A PLAIN COMPANY REGISTRY: this names the real HUMAN owners behind a company; a company registry names only the legal entity, its directors and filings. Use the registry first to find the entity, then this to pierce the shell to the people who profit. — Holds to account: the hidden owners behind firms dealing with Costa Rica’s government — find beneficial-owner filings.

trackers.name: Servidumbre ecológica — protects part of a farm without freezing the rest
trackers.desc: THE INSTRUMENT THAT ANSWERS THE OWNER'S OBJECTION. A servidumbre ecológica (Ley de Biodiversidad 7788 art. 123, with art. 37 LOA) lets an owner permanently dedicate part of a farm to conservation, inscribed in the Registro Nacional — registration is what makes it durable rather than a promise. Crucially it does not limit permitted development on the rest of the property: only the dedicated portion must stay natural. That is precisely the objection that defeats designations elsewhere in this map. THE ALTERNATIVE: a Refugio Nacional de Vida Silvestre Privado (Ley 7317 arts. 82–87, Decreto 32633) is officially recognised protected status, requiring presidential decree published in La Gaceta and an application to SINAC with preliminary physiographic, biological and socioeconomic studies; it lasts 10 years, renewable indefinitely, and its main financial benefit is exemption from land tax plus authorised ecotourism income negotiated with MINAE. SO: the easement is perpetual but private; the refuge is renewable but carries tax relief. BE REALISTIC — legal analysis describes only a small line of judicial decisions actually enforcing easement conservation content, and the question of survival on transfer to a later buyer is the one to settle before signing.

trackers.name: Nosara — a biological corridor built entirely from voluntary agreements
trackers.desc: A MODEL A COMMUNITY CAN ACTUALLY RUN. Nosara is building Guanacaste's first biological corridor entirely through voluntary conservation agreements between private owners, using servidumbres ecológicas inscribed in perpetuity in the Registro Nacional — led by the Asociación Cívica de Nosara with SINAC under the regional biological corridors programme. The corridor links the uplands to the Ostional wildlife refuge on the coast, and Nosara still holds about 80 percent forest cover, exceptional for a coastal zone. THE ARGUMENT THEY USED IS THE REUSABLE PART: continuity protects fauna, regulates temperature, reduces erosion, prevents landslides and guarantees aquifer recharge supplying the district — framed as local self-interest, not abstract conservation. AND THE THREAT IT ANSWERS: the Informe del Estado de la Nación 2025 records that coastal development there has been marked by the segregation of former cattle properties into multiple parcels. Fragmentation by subdivision is the mechanism to watch — the same trap this map records for community land in Kenya. NOTE SINAC'S OWN DEFINITION: a corredor biológico is a territorial extension generally of private property whose function is to interconnect protected areas — so corridors are expected to be built on private land.

trackers.name: Contracorriente
trackers.desc: Contracorriente — Honduran in-depth investigative outlet (born of the 2015 anti-corruption protests) reporting on graft, mining, organized crime and power in one of the world’s deadliest countries for journalists. — Independent watchdog of officials and public power.

trackers.name: Instituto de Acceso a la Información Pública (IAIP)
trackers.desc: National right-to-information authority; Honduras’ IAIP is the deconcentrated guarantor body under the LTAIP (2006) — it reviews recursos de revisión and runs the SINAIP/SIELHO transparency portals, Honduras.

trackers.name: ASJ — Asociación para una Sociedad más Justa (Transparency International Honduras)
trackers.desc: Honduras' national chapter of Transparency International, founded 1998, and one of the few national bodies documenting violence against environmental defenders: with CONADEH it published the 2026 report finding at least 111 environmentalists killed between 2015 and 2025, 92% of those crimes unpunished, and over 30% concentrated in Colón. It runs ALAC Honduras, an Advocacy and Legal Advice Centre that takes citizen corruption complaints - relevant where a concession was granted without the consultation the law required. WHO IT SUITS: communities needing their case documented and escalated rather than litigated; ASJ is a watchdog and advice centre, not a litigator. NOTE: its canonical domain could not be verified this session - reach it through Transparency International's national contacts directory at transparency.org. It runs ALAC Honduras (Centro de Asistencia Legal Anticorrupción), opened with technical support from Transparency International, which receives corruption complaints rather than only studying them: it advises victims and witnesses on filing with the competent authorities, explains the legal options, and accompanies and follows up cases until they are resolved. Report on 2213-1439, at diloaqui@asjhonduras.com, through diloaqui.asjhonduras.com, or via the Dilo Aquí Honduras app for iOS and Android. Between 2012 and 2016 ALAC filed 156 corruption complaints, of which 53 reached the courts. USE ITS RESEARCH TOO: ASJ counted 3,471 complaints to the Ministerio Público between 2008 and 2015 producing only 283 prosecutions — about 1 in 12 — which is the figure to cite when arguing that filing alone is not enough. NOTE: ASJ-US (asj-us.org) is a separate sister organisation; this entry is the Honduran chapter.

trackers.name: Bufete Jurídico Justicia para los Pueblos
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Honduran human-rights law office founded in 2000 by Kenia Oliva and Edy Tabora, combining litigation with investigation and documentation, and working in coordination with social, territorial and trade organisations rather than taking walk-in clients. It defended the Guapinol river defenders of Tocoa against criminalisation, and the Inter-American Commission's Precautionary Measure 137-23 covers the firm itself alongside the Comité Municipal para la Defensa de los Bienes Comunes y Públicos de Tocoa — its lawyers are under threat for this work. WHO IT SUITS: communities and campesino and indigenous leaders facing criminal prosecution brought to clear the way for a mine, dam or plantation. It works through organised movements, so approach with your committee or federation behind you.

trackers.name: MAR Fund — Small Grants Program (Mesoamerican Reef)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: an ecoregional fund created in 2004 by the national conservation funds of Belize, Guatemala, Honduras and Mexico, running a Small Grants Program by competitive Call for Proposals — now past its 17th call — with two windows, the Traditional Window and the Reef Rescue Initiative. WHO IT SUITS: civil-society groups working on coastal and marine protected areas anywhere in the Mesoamerican Reef System. HOW IT DIFFERS: transnational by design, so a project spanning the reef across two countries is a fit here where a national funder would balk.

trackers.desc: National corporate registry; the Instituto de la Propiedad (IP) administers Honduras’s property & mercantile registries — company & trade-name registration under the Registro Mercantil — alongside intellectual property, Honduras. — Holds to account: companies in Honduras — find the Instituto de la Propiedad's mercantile registry of entities and trade names.
