A WORKED EXAMPLE FROM ITS OWN ANONYMISED CASE LIST: a 600 square metre parcel in a protected zone, industrial extension project, recours brought by the neighbourhood AND AN ENVIRONMENTAL ASSOCIATION — the pairing this file keeps recommending.

trackers.name: BBBD & Associés — it acts for riverains and GROUPS OF RIVERAINS, and files the suspension
trackers.desc: WHO IT ACTS FOR, in its own words: the cabinet assists, accompanies and advises PARTICULIERS, RIVERAINS OR GROUPS OF RIVERAINS who decide or are considering bringing a recours gracieux or a recours contentieux against urbanism authorisations, with a view to obtaining their WITHDRAWAL OR ANNULMENT. AND THE PART THAT STOPS A SITE: the cabinet can file a RÉFÉRÉ-SUSPENSION bringing the immediate suspension of urbanism authorisations and consequently A HALT TO THE WORKS, OR THEIR NOT STARTING AT ALL. Filing before the machines arrive is cheaper and more effective than filing after — practitioners note that lodging a recours does NOT automatically suspend the permit, that construction may continue unless a judge orders suspension, and that examination of the main case averages 18 months. A CAUTION RECORDED PLAINLY: the same cabinet states that promoters, national and regional, and local authorities entrust the DEFENCE of their urbanism authorisations to its lawyers. Check conflicts. AND WHO HAS STANDING, from practitioner guidance: any third party justifying an intérêt à agir — a RIVERAIN, an APPROVED ASSOCIATION, or the COMMUNE; a lawyer is obligatory for the main claim but not for a référé-suspension, though strongly recommended.

trackers.name: Fondation de France — 982 sheltered foundations, and it funds COLLECTIFS DE CITOYENS
trackers.desc: THE SCALE, AND THE STRUCTURE BEHIND IT: each year the foundation and the foundations it SHELTERS support more than 12,000 PROJECTS through grants or bursaries, making it the first actor of philanthropy in France; it houses 982 SHELTERED FOUNDATIONS. France had 39 filed entries and only two funders. AND WHO MAY APPLY, which is the line that matters: its programmes work by appels à projets, open to an ASSOCIATION, A COLLECTIF DE CITOYENS, a public establishment, a research team. A citizens' collective can apply directly to France's largest philanthropic body — no incorporation required, and its remit expressly covers associations in the social, educational, cultural OR ENVIRONMENTAL field. AND THE PRACTICAL POINT ABOUT SHELTERED FOUNDATIONS: a hundred of the 982 deliver around 2,000 bursaries or honour loans each year, and others award prizes — so a community looking for money should search the sheltered foundations by theme rather than only the parent. Its own summary of the appeal is worth borrowing: the fact that the Foundation is the one 'of all causes', its NEUTRALITY and its seriousness convinced me.

trackers.name: The French environmental funding map — regions, communes, ADEME, and 36 corporate foundations
trackers.desc: WHERE THE MONEY ACTUALLY IS, laid out by tier: communes, départements and régions offer specific financing schemes — the REGIONS generally have dedicated funds for ecological transition and BIODIVERSITY, and the COMMUNES offer aid for projects of local scale: SHARED GARDENS, GREEN SPACES, awareness work. Above them sit the national agencies and ministry programmes with direct subsidies for structuring projects. Your own commune is a funder, and most groups never ask it — and a search platform is named that queries more than 150 PUBLIC SCHEMES AND 36 CORPORATE FOUNDATIONS against your organisation's number, territory and project type, with a free account for a first look. AND THE FUNDRAISING ADVICE, which is the most transferable thing in the entry: rarely can an association live on a single subsidy. BUILD A BOUQUET OF FUNDERS — a basic public subsidy, completed by a private foundation, with SKILLS PATRONAGE in reinforcement. That also shows funders your project is validated by several sources. AND HOW TO WRITE IT: consult the local programming documents — Agenda 21, climate action plans, REGIONAL BIODIVERSITY STRATEGIES — and show how your project ALIGNS WITH THESE PRIORITIES. Funders value projects that pool efforts and resources with other associations, local authorities and businesses.

trackers.name: Buying wild reserves — 30 EURO buys 200 square metres, and 500 hectares was bought off an ESTATE AGENT
trackers.desc: THE SHARE PRICE THAT LETS ANYONE JOIN A PURCHASE: A SHARE OF WILD LIFE IS 30 EUROS, WHICH MAKES IT POSSIBLE TO PRESERVE 200 SQUARE METRES OF NATURE, and the association says this MAKES IT POSSIBLE TO PRESERVE ENVIRONMENTS OVER THE LONG TERM AND IN A SHARED AND DEMOCRATIC WAY. France had five acquisition entries against 41 total. AND THE PURCHASE ITSELF: THE MAD PROJECT WE RECENTLY MANAGED TO CARRY OUT WAS TO BUY 500 HECTARES OF LAND IN THE VERCORS AND GIVE THAT SPACE BACK TO THE ANIMALS AND TO NATURE. AND THE DETAIL A COMMUNITY SHOULD TAKE MOST SERIOUSLY, from the companion report: IF THE LAND COULD BE BOUGHT, IT IS QUITE SIMPLY BECAUSE IT WAS FOR SALE AT AN ESTATE AGENCY. The land that gets saved is often just land that was on the open market, and watching estate agents' listings is a task any volunteer can do — no negotiation, no persuasion, only noticing in time. AND WHAT THE PURCHASE BUYS IN PRACTICE: in these reserves ALL ACTIVITIES THAT HAVE A HARMFUL IMPACT ON THE NATURAL ENVIRONMENTS ARE FORBIDDEN: CUTTING TREES, FISHING, HUNTING, MOTORISED VEHICLES, PASTORALISM, TAKING AND GATHERING, while human presence is LIMITED TO CONTEMPLATIVE AND IMMERSIVE WALKING. The association owns FIVE WILD RESERVES across three departments, having acquired ABOUT 1,200 HECTARES IN 10 YEARS, starting in 2010.

trackers.name: The LPO's land policy — owning 2,200 hectares, and MANAGING land it does not own
trackers.desc: WHY A CONSERVATION BODY BUYS RATHER THAN CAMPAIGNS, in its own words: LAND OWNERSHIP ALLOWS THE ASSOCIATION TO PROTECT SPACES DURABLY AND TO CONTROL THEIR MANAGEMENT — a policy it began in 1989, IN ORDER TO FIGHT AGAINST THE DESTRUCTION OF THE GREAT MARSHES OF WESTERN FRANCE. A land-acquisition policy begun explicitly to stop a wave of destruction is the precedent for any community facing one, and it has run for over thirty years. AND THE HOLDING, which shows that small parcels count: AT PRESENT THE ASSOCIATION IS THE OWNER OF NEARLY 2,200 HECTARES, SPREAD OVER 89 SITES. WHILE SOME ARE LESS THAN 1 HECTARE, 4 OF THEM EXCEED 200 HECTARES. Eighty-nine sites, some under a hectare, is what a real portfolio looks like — a community should not assume its parcel is too small to interest a national body. AND THE SECOND ROUTE, for land it will never own: IT ALSO MANAGES LAND ON BEHALF OF ITS PRIVATE OR PUBLIC OWNER, FOR THE PURPOSES OF PRESERVING BIODIVERSITY. THE ASSOCIATION THEN CONCLUDES A MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT WITH THESE OWNERS. An owner who will not sell can still hand over the management — and the association publishes A MAP OF THE LAND IT OWNS AND THE LAND UNDER MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT, which shows a community who already holds ground nearby.

trackers.name: Openpolis
trackers.desc: Independent Italian foundation liberating and curating public data on politicians, spending and power. — Holds to account: officials handling public money & power — find open data on officials, votes and public money.

trackers.name: Camera – Register of Interest Representatives
trackers.desc: Italy's Chamber of Deputies register of lobbyists and interest representatives. — Holds to account: interest representatives at the Chamber of Deputies — find the register of lobbyists and their declared activity.

trackers.name: Italgiure (Corte di Cassazione)
trackers.desc: Official case-law database of the Italian Court of Cassation. · Find here: the Italian Court of Cassation's case-law system (ItalgiureWeb).

trackers.name: Corte di Cassazione – SentenzeWeb
trackers.desc: Free public archive of the last five years of civil & criminal Court of Cassation judgments — no registration. · Find here: the free public archive of recent Italian Court of Cassation judgments (SentenzeWeb).

trackers.name: Giustizia Amministrativa (Consiglio di Stato / TAR)
trackers.desc: Freely searchable decisions and opinions of the Council of State and Regional Administrative Tribunals. · Find here: the decisions of Italy's Council of State and Regional Administrative Tribunals.

trackers.name: Corte Costituzionale – Giurisprudenza
trackers.desc: Constitutional Court judgments from 1956 to present, freely searchable. · Find here: the judgments of Italy's Constitutional Court (1956–present).

trackers.name: Autorità Nazionale Anticorruzione (ANAC)
trackers.desc: National anti-corruption / integrity authority.

trackers.name: Transparency International Italia
trackers.desc: Transparency International's Italy chapter (30+ years). Anti-corruption research, education and advocacy; runs an Advocacy and Legal Advice Centre (ALAC) for victims and witnesses of corruption; and helps citizens and organisations obtain public data.

trackers.name: FAI — Fondo per l'Ambiente Italiano (donate land or property)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: Italy's national trust, founded 1975 on the British National Trust model, which takes ownership or long-term concession of buildings, gardens and fragile natural habitats and protects them permanently, opening them to the public. It accepts land and property by donation in life, by bequest, or by concession, and runs its own conservation department. USE IT: if you own or can direct a threatened parcel — gifts and inheritances to FAI are exempt from succession and donation tax and from the imposta ipotecaria and catastale, so the whole value reaches the protection. Property that FAI cannot itself hold can be donated and sold to fund work elsewhere, so a non-scenic parcel is still worth offering. THE ARGUMENT THAT PERSUADES A LANDOWNER: FAI's first-ever property, in 1977, was just over 1,000 square metres of coastal land at Cala Junco on Panarea, given by the lawyer Piero Di Blasi expressly to avert a subdivision plan that would have irreparably disfigured the landscape — the very first gift FAI received was land donated to defeat a development, and at a thousand square metres, size is not the qualifying test. AND FOR AN OWNER WHO WILL NEITHER SELL NOR GIVE: 9 of FAI's 75 institutional properties (as at 31 December 2025) are held by concessione or comodato d'uso — a free loan-for-use where the owner keeps title and FAI takes on the care. IT HAS ALSO PUBLISHED WHAT IT WANTS: to increase the number and variety of its historic and natural properties in every region, particularly in the SOUTH and in major cities beginning with ROME — a published appetite for more property in a named region is an invitation.

trackers.name: Legambiente — Osservatorio Ambiente e Legalità / Ecomafia
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Italy's largest environmental association, which says plainly on its own legality page how it fights — by constituting itself parte civile in criminal trials, and by appealing to the regional administrative courts (TAR) and the Consiglio di Stato against unlawful and damaging administrative measures. It coined the term ecomafia in 1994 and publishes the annual Ecomafia report through its Osservatorio Ambiente e Legalità, which tracks the ciclo del cemento — abusivismo edilizio, illegal quarries, rigged public-works contracts — region by region and names the cases. WHO IT SUITS: a community facing illegal or corrupt construction, quarrying or waste dumping, where the route is a criminal prosecution you can attach to rather than a permit challenge you must bring alone.

trackers.name: Corte dei conti
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Italy, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Investigative Reporting Project Italy (IRPI)
trackers.desc: Italian investigative outfit tracing organized crime, corruption and illicit finance.

trackers.name: MASE VAS-VIA-AIA portal — national environmental assessment
trackers.desc: Italy's national VAS-VIA-AIA portal for state-competence environmental assessment and authorisation under Part Two of Legislative Decree 152/2006 (run by the environment ministry, now MASE; a platform migration is under way). You CAN get: technical documents for projects under national evaluation and the concluding acts issued since 1989, plus the 45-day public-comment windows. You CAN'T get: regional-competence procedures handled by the Regions. For activists: track a national project's file and file observations during the consultation window.

trackers.name: Acquisti in Rete PA (MEPA)
trackers.desc: Italy's central public-procurement marketplace. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Italy, and for how much.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Cassation
trackers.desc: Supreme Court of Cassation — supreme court (Italy).

trackers.name: dati.gov.it
trackers.desc: National — official government open data / budget portal. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this is the broad budget/open-data hub for how money is allocated overall — for the specific firms winning tenders use the procurement portal, and for findings of misspending use the supreme audit institution. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Italy.

trackers.name: Italian Council of State
trackers.desc: Italian Council of State — administrative court (Italy).

trackers.name: ISTAT
trackers.desc: Italy's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Italy.

trackers.name: Registro Imprese
trackers.desc: Italy's official business register of companies and filings. — Holds to account: companies in Italy — find the business register of entities, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Register of Beneficial Ownership of Companies
trackers.desc: Register of Beneficial Ownership of Companies — Italy’s beneficial-ownership register, disclosing the real individuals who ultimately own or control companies. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM A PLAIN COMPANY REGISTRY: this names the real HUMAN owners behind a company; a company registry names only the legal entity, its directors and filings. Use the registry first to find the entity, then this to pierce the shell to the people who profit. — Holds to account: the hidden owners behind firms dealing with Italy’s government — find beneficial-owner filings.

trackers.name: Art. 13 L. 349/1986 — recognition that carries standing to annul
trackers.desc: GET ON THE MINISTERIAL LIST AND STANDING COMES WITH IT. Associations recognised under article 13 of Law 349/1986 may, under article 18(5), intervene in environmental damage proceedings and appeal to the administrative courts for annulment of unlawful acts — standing conferred by law, not argued case by case. TO BE RECOGNISED: exist for at least 3 years, work in environmental protection, and be national in character or present in at least 5 regions — presence meaning member nuclei, a regional office and substantial activity across the region. The ministry assesses aims, democratic internal ordering under the statute, continuity of action and external relevance, and the criteria are cumulative, not alternative: fail one and recognition is refused. CHECK YOUR OWN POSITION: recognition covers the association and all branches governed by the same statute, but not affiliated or federated bodies with their own legal representative or a different statute.

trackers.name: How far that standing reaches — and the planning-law limit
trackers.desc: THE COURTS READ IT WIDELY. Standing under articles 13 and 18 covers environmental interests in the narrow sense and in the broad sense — conservation and enhancement of cultural property, the environment widely understood, urban, rural and natural landscape, monuments, historic centres and quality of life — grounded by the Council of State in the horizontal subsidiarity principle of article 118 of the Constitution. THE LIMIT, AND PLAN FOR IT: the legitimate interest in compliance with urban-planning and building rules belongs to specific, differentiated and qualified individuals, and recognised associations cannot assert it in their place — their special standing covers environmental interests, which are diffuse by nature. So run the association's environmental grounds alongside an affected neighbour's planning grounds. AND IF YOU ARE NOT ON THE LIST: the prevailing case law holds that listing creates no rigid automatism — a judge may admit an unlisted association after verifying its concrete representativeness, the so-called doppio binario. Committees, though, have been held to fall outside the article 13 category.

trackers.name: MASE sustainable development call — join the Forum as you apply
trackers.desc: THE NATIONAL ENVIRONMENT MINISTRY'S OWN CALL, open to non-profits based in Italy — associations, foundations, universities and research bodies whose activities are dedicated as a priority to sustainable development, under the Avviso pubblico for the National Sustainable Development Strategy. THE PREFERENCE THAT DECIDES WHO GETS THE MONEY: priority goes to proposals from organisations adhering to the Forum nazionale per lo Sviluppo Sostenibile — or that have applied to join by the date the proposal is sent. So joining is step one and can be done in parallel with the application, not years ahead. Submission is by certified email (PEC) to the address in the notice, by a fixed date and hour. REGISTER FIRST, THOUGH: most Italian third-sector funding runs through the RUNTS register — covering volunteering organisations, associazioni di promozione sociale, foundations with civic or social-utility purposes, philanthropic bodies and associative networks — and many regional calls admit only partnerships composed exclusively of ETS.

trackers.name: Where Italian environmental money actually comes from
trackers.desc: THE STANDING SOURCES. Fondazione Cariplo gives non-repayable contributions to third-sector organisations for cultural, social, environmental and research projects. Fondazione CON IL SUD runs environment calls for third-sector and volunteering organisations in Basilicata, Calabria, Campania, Puglia, Sardinia and Sicily — one Taranto call put EUR 970,000 into integrated environment-led development, requiring partnership with productive, institutional, university and research bodies. 5 per mille routes an annual contribution through taxpayers' income tax returns and is recurring, largely unrestricted income — rare enough to be worth registering for on its own; alongside it sit 8x1000, the Social Bonus and ordinary fundraising. If you have no grant experience, start at your local CSV (Centro di Servizio per il Volontariato), funded by the Fondo Unico Nazionale, which provides services and sometimes small local calls. TWO WARNINGS FROM ITALIAN SECTOR GUIDANCE: many bandi require co-financing — one large call sets a minimum 10 percent in cash — and money often arrives late, so you need a donations base to bridge the gap; and larger calls expect consolidated design experience with a budget, cronoprogramma and named territorial partners.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: SNPA — your regional agency, and the segnalazione that outperforms its programme
trackers.desc: CITIZEN REPORTS DROVE MORE THAN TWICE AS MANY INSPECTIONS AS THE AGENCY'S OWN PROGRAMME — and that comes from the agency's own published account. Arpa Toscana received 1,216 segnalazioni in 2019 from citizens acting individually or as organised groups, and in the reported period 346 accertamenti were carried out following a segnalazione against 160 programmed controls. That is the strongest argument in this map for making a formal report rather than assuming it will be ignored. WHERE TO SEND IT: every Italian region has its own agency — 19 regional ARPA plus the two provincial APPA of Trento and Bolzano, with ISPRA, forming SNPA under Legge 132/2016, operative since 14 January 2017. This link is SNPA's own directory of all 21 agency websites — find your region there. Each has an URP (public relations office) listed in the SNPA SI-URP section, and publishes both an ordinary email and a PEC address — in Italy a PEC is legally certified delivery, so use it where the report must be provable. KNOW THE FOUR OUTCOMES, BECAUSE ONE IS NOTHING: an inspection or notice of a programmed one; a request for support to your Comune to carry out preventive checks; a written reply based on the rules and existing knowledge; or archiviazione d'ufficio — filed without action. Controls are also triggered by an AIA permit's own terms, by local authorities, and on delegation from the Magistratura. THE SYSTEM-LEVEL POWER WORTH CITING: through the Consiglio SNPA the network gives a parere vincolante — a binding opinion — on Government measures of a technical nature, and may formally signal the opportunity for interventions, including legislative ones, for the reduction of consumo di suolo. Land take is named in its founding purpose. The agencies exist because the 1993 abrogative referendums stripped environmental control from the health service, moving it to ARPA/APPA under Legge 61/1994.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Italia Nostra — takes property by donation, comodato or bequest (Italy)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: Italy's oldest heritage and landscape association, founded 29 October 1955 and recognised by presidential decree of 22 August 1958 no. 1111, now an APS registered in the third-sector register under d.lgs. 117/2017. Its statute has it acquire property of historic or environmental value by donation, comodato, bequest or any other form in order to secure its protection, managing it in the public interest. Its published list of beni runs from the Centrale Idrodinamica of Trieste's Porto Vecchio to a regional nature reserve on the western Matese, land at Valle Banca in Civitanova del Sannio, and a stretch of the Imera meridionale between Monte Capodarso and Monte Sabucina. USE IT: this is the second Italian route, for a parcel FAI will not take. The same list mixes outright ownership with management on someone else's land and with agreements that do no more than guarantee opening and access, so a site can be placed with the association at whatever depth its owner will actually accept — which is a lower bar than a transfer of title. The Milan case is the one to put in front of a council: Boscoincittà, about 120 hectares of woods, meadows, watercourses and wetland with roughly two hundred allotments worked by residents, was built by the association from 1974 on municipal ground through its Centro Forestazione Urbana, and in October 2017 the city handed it a second derelict site at Porto di Mare to repeat it. It is currently in the Coalizione Art. 9 pressing regions and the state to designate suitable areas and stop ground-mounted photovoltaic consuming farmland, so a solar scheme on agricultural soil is a fight it is already inside.

trackers.name: Fondazione CON IL SUD — funds the southern regions Cariplo does not reach
trackers.desc: WHO IT COVERS: third sector organisations in Basilicata, Calabria, Campania, Puglia, Sardinia and Sicily. Together with the Lombardy foundation already in this file, that puts the two ends of Italy in the file and leaves the centre and north-east to the regional banking foundations. Via del Corso 267, 00187 Rome. THE SCALE, FROM ITS OWN ACCOUNT: in seventeen years it supported over 1,800 initiatives, involving more than 7,000 different organisations — non-profits, public and private bodies — and disbursed close to €300 million. It also seeded the first seven southern community foundations, in the historic centre and Rione Sanità in Naples, Salerno, Benevento, Messina, the Val di Noto, Agrigento and Trapani — which is the same funder-creating-funders pattern recorded for Serbia in batch 113, and those seven are nearer to a village than Rome is. WHAT IT FUNDS THAT BEARS ON LAND: a standing Bando Ambiente, now in its fourth edition, inviting southern third sector organisations to propose exemplary projects for preventing and reducing environmental risks. A local development call, Riabitare il Sud, with €8 million for at least four territories, expressly covering the valorisation of common goods — disused schools, urban spaces — and of environmental resources including natural parks; each project must cover an area of at least three neighbouring municipalities with a population no greater than 20,000. A €1.5 million call that produced nine new energy and social communities in the south. And a circular economy call whose partnerships may include municipalities, regions, municipal companies, schools, universities and local firms alongside third sector bodies. THE ELIGIBILITY PATTERN TO EXPECT: its calls require an Ente del Terzo Settore with a registered office in the candidate area, constituted before a stated date and registered with the national third sector register or the previous ONLUS register, and some require documented experience in project design. Registration and a date of constitution are the gates — as in Moldova, and unlike the Balkan funders that take informal groups. ONE UNUSUAL OFFER: a volunteering call of €4 million where support is not tied to submitting a project proposal but to consolidating and developing an organisation's ordinary volunteering activity, aimed at depopulation in small inland municipalities. Money for existing work rather than for a new scheme is rare anywhere in this file.

trackers.name: Domini collettivi — and the national Consulta that federates them (Italy)
trackers.desc: WHAT THE LAW NOW SAYS, and it is the most important sentence in this entry: under law no. 168 of 20 November 2017, the bodies managing collective land — Università Agrarie, Comunanze, Partecipanze, Consorterie, Regole, ASBUC and ASUC, however named — are recognised as Domini Collettivi with legal personality under private law and statutory autonomy, an expression of the primary legal order of their communities. The collective domain partakes of private property in that the owner enjoys the asset exclusively, and of public property in that it cannot be used so as to deprive individual members of the community of their enjoyment — and is distinguished from both by absolute unavailability. IF NO MANAGING BODY EXISTS, ONE CAN BE CONSTITUTED: where collective assets are being managed by the Comune itself, the law provides for the prefect, after ascertaining which municipalities are in that position, to convene the electors pending constitution of the Dominio Collettivo. A community whose collective land is administered by the council can ask to administer it itself. THE NAMES TO LOOK FOR, because a community may not know what it has: comunioni familiari montane, comunalie, consorzi di utenti, università agrarie, beni sociali, vicinie, regole, comunelle, partecipanze agrarie, società di antichi originari, ius, consorterie, ademprivi, ASUC, ASBUC, frazioni. Working examples include the Regole ampezzane, owners of four fifths of the territory of the Comune of Cortina d'Ampezzo and managers of the Belluno Dolomites national park, the Trentino ASUCs, the Parma comunalie, the Magnifica Comunità di Fiemme, the Partecipanza di Trino Vercellese, the università agrarie of Lazio and the Emilian partecipanze agrarie. WHO TO CONTACT: the Consulta nazionale della proprietà collettiva, a non-profit association founded in Rome at the Senate on 7 March 2006, now based in Trento, with a federative structure organised in regional coordinations, bringing together communities of usi civici, demani civici, università agrarie and collective properties to defend and develop them. Alongside it, APRODUC publishes material on applying the 2017 law and directs enquirers to the regional administrative offices and the regional usi civici commissariats. ONE LIMIT ON THE INALIENABILITY: the Constitutional Court, judgment no. 119 of 15 June 2023, declared article 3 paragraph 3 of law 168/2017 unconstitutional in the part where it fails to exclude from the inalienability regime privately owned assets subject to usi civici.

trackers.name: WWF Italia — 200 local sections, an affiliation route for private land, and it goes to the TAR
trackers.desc: WHY THIS FILLS A REAL HOLE: Italy's bucket had acquirers (FAI, Italia Nostra), funders and the collective-domain bodies, but nothing that combines a local presence with litigation. THE NETWORK: around 200 regional and local sections plus aggregated organisations that can take the form of committees or associations with their own legal personality, each bound to WWF Italia by a contract setting out mutual rights and duties. There are also volunteer guards working, unarmed and entirely voluntarily, in surveillance. Find your nearest local section first — it is the door, and in Italy the local section is a legally distinct body that can act in its own name. THE LAND: over 100 Oasi covering roughly 27,000 to 31,000 hectares across every Italian region, of which around 6,500 hectares are owned directly by WWF. AND THE ROUTE FOR PRIVATELY OWNED GROUND, which is the part most communities need: since 2005 some Oasi are not managed by WWF local groups but by other private parties, affiliated to WWF Italia through the Programme of Affiliated Areas — an affiliation agreement that allows protection of areas of environmental interest that lie on private land. An owner keeps the land and gains the designation and the network. That is the Italian version of the private land conservation route already filed at European level. IT LITIGATES, AND IT INTERVENES ALONGSIDE OTHERS: the Abruzzo regional administrative court upheld a WWF Italia appeal that unblocked the establishment of a national park; and in Sardinia, WWF Italia and LIPU, both represented by the same lawyer, intervened in a case brought before the regional administrative court to protect a coastal area of outstanding natural and landscape value next to a marine protected area from a tourism development. Intervening alongside an existing claimant is cheaper than bringing your own case. AND IT ACTS IN COALITION: it has joined ENPA, LAC, LAV, Legambiente and LIPU in calling on citizens and political groups over hunting legislation — that list is Italy's environmental bloc, named. Around 80 staff nationally, and it manages four nature reserves of the Sicilian Region.

trackers.name: Lipu — volunteers monitored 359,218 hectares, and it reports to the judicial authorities
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: the Lega Italiana Protezione Uccelli, founded 1965, headquartered in Parma, BirdLife and IUCN affiliate, with roughly 26,500 members, 77 staff and 1,441 volunteers, funded by membership fees, Italy's 5x1000 tax designation, bequests and individual donations. THE NUMBER THAT MAKES IT A WATCHDOG, from its own social report: 359,218 hectares of territory monitored by volunteers in one year, an 11 per cent increase, described as surveillance so that the major threats to sites and habitats can be caught. Volunteers put in around 312,000 hours in total and gave almost 127,000 consultations to the public. And it states that it relates to the judicial authorities, for reports and complaints. If something is happening to a site, there is a national body that both watches ground at that scale and takes what it finds to prosecutors. THE LAND: Oasi and Riserve across Italy protecting 5,000 to 7,000 hectares, holding over 5,000 animal and plant species and more than 300 bird species; established under national and regional law and carrying international recognitions including Natura 2000 and Important Bird Area status; managed in cooperation with public bodies and sometimes private parties. Twenty-six are open for birdwatching and guided visits. Its recovery centres treat around 20,000 to 30,000 animals a year. TWO PRECEDENTS WORTH CITING: a site was taken from criminal hands in 2005 through the joint action of Lipu, the magistracy and others, and later entered the Natura 2000 network; and it has acquired sites outright, one such operation made possible by a large private donation, allowing more direct management. Land can be recovered, not only bought. HOW TO REACH IT: the 'Italia della Lipu' page maps its presence region by region — delegations, oases and reserves, recovery centres and offices, with addresses. The delegato is the official territorial representative, a volunteer appointed by the executive to carry out the mission locally. That is the named person to contact in your region.

trackers.name: The ministry's list of associazioni riconosciute — being on it is itself standing to sue
trackers.desc: WHY THE LIST IS THE RESOURCE: Italian case law holds that the standing of national environmental associations to challenge administrative acts in environmental matters derives directly from articles 13 and 18(5) of law 349/1986, which of itself attributes it to those entered in the ministerial list. Being on the list is standing. A community that finds a listed association willing to lend its name does not have to argue about legitimacy at all — and the list, with addresses and PEC addresses, is published by the environment ministry. AND THE LISTED BODIES ARE MORE VARIED THAN EXPECTED: the register carries the familiar conservation names alongside anglers' and hunting-adjacent federations, rural-environment associations, park and forest guard bodies, and a wind energy association. Read it before assuming who your ally is — and note that at least one entry is marked with its recognition SUSPENDED by ministerial decree, so check the current status of any association you rely on. HOW AN ASSOCIATION GETS ON IT: an association constituted at least three years, operating in the field of environmental protection, may apply to the environment ministry. Recognition is by ministerial decree on the basis of the programmatic aims and the democratic internal order provided by its statute, and of the continuity of its action and its external relevance, after an opinion of the national council for the environment — and if that opinion is not given within ninety days, the minister decides anyway. THE SCALE TEST, WHICH IS THE REAL BARRIER FOR A LOCAL GROUP: recognition is for associations of national character or present in at least five regions — and presence must be shown by groups of members, a regional office, and a substantial distribution of activity across that region's territory. A single-site residents' association will not qualify. That is a sharper threshold than France's or Spain's, and it means the Italian route is to work with a listed body rather than to become one. PRACTICAL: recognised associations may state the wording and decree number on their own website, so you can verify a claim; and one reported use of the status was challenging a public body's silence on a request for environmental information.

trackers.name: Legambiente — 1,000 local groups, 20 regional committees, 60+ areas managed
trackers.desc: WHY THIS AND NOT THE MINISTRY: Italy's environment ministry publishes the list of recognised environmental associations — already filed here as the standing route — but its own grant-making to those associations has been criticised in Parliament as discretionary, with criteria often unclear, no verification of the quality of services delivered and a total absence of controls on the use of the sums paid out. Recorded because a community should not plan a campaign around Italian ministerial contributions. The reliable Italian resource is the associations themselves, and this is the largest. THE NETWORK: recognised by the environment ministry as an association of environmental interest and described as the most widespread environmental association in Italy, with more than 1,000 local groups, 20 regional committees, 115,000 members and supporters, around 30,000 school classes in its education programmes and 3,000 participants in volunteer camps. A thousand local groups is the densest coverage recorded in this file — more than Sweden's 270 kretsar or Finland's 150 local associations. AND IT MANAGES GROUND: over 60 natural areas managed directly or in collaboration. It is a member of Federparchi, IUCN, FSC and the European Environmental Bureau. WHAT IT RUNS THAT A COMMUNITY CAN USE: Goletta Verde, which photographs the health of the Italian sea every summer, and Treno Verde, which measures smog and noise in cities — two recurring national monitoring campaigns that produce published measurements of a named place. Its volunteering lines are Puliamo il Mondo, Spiagge e fondali puliti, and volunteer camps for environmental restoration. AND THE NATIONAL TARGET TO CITE: Italy's Strategia Nazionale per la Biodiversità al 2030 commits to legally protecting at least 30 per cent of land and 30 per cent of sea, with at least a third of protected areas strictly protected including all primary and old-growth forests, and to ensuring the ecological connection of protected areas at local, national and supranational scale.

trackers.name: Iustlab — a searchable Italian directory of environmental and planning lawyers, by city
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: an interactive directory of Italian law practices filterable by field and by city, with parallel lists for diritto ambientale, EDILIZIA ED URBANISTICA, and ricorso al TAR — each lawyer describing their own practice in their own words, with their city and distance shown. Italy's bucket had land trusts, funders and campaigning bodies but no way to find a lawyer. WHAT THE ENTRIES SHOW YOU BEFORE YOU CALL, which is the value: one names a Master in Environmental Law and membership of the editorial committee of the environmental law review; another lists waste, building and planning, and environmental pollution proceedings; another handles authorisations — AIA, VIA, VAS — waste management, environmental liability and greenwashing, assisting COMPANIES, PUBLIC BODIES AND ASSOCIATIONS. AND ONE ENTRY DESCRIBES THE PROBLEM IN A COMMUNITY'S OWN TERMS: master plans, environmental constraints, the consolidated building and environmental acts, environmental crimes, AND MUNICIPALITIES THAT APPLY THE RULES TO THEIR OWN ADVANTAGE AND TO THE DETRIMENT OF CITIZENS AND ASSOCIATIONS — this is the thicket every single citizen runs into. Read what the lawyer says they do before you pay for the first hour; some list challenges to illegitimate measures — SCIA, silences, refused amnesties, landscape and environmental constraints.

trackers.name: Who can actually challenge a building permit in Italy — vicinitas, comitati, and what it costs
trackers.desc: WHO HAS STANDING, from a practitioners' guide, and it is better news than it sounds: the most frequently entitled parties are OWNERS OF PROPERTY BORDERING OR NEAR the building work, on the criterion of VICINITAS — physical proximity — the main test administrative case law uses, because whoever lives or owns near the contested work directly suffers its consequences: LOSS OF VIEW, REDUCTION OF LIGHT, INCREASED TRAFFIC, DEPRECIATION OF THE PROPERTY. AND CRUCIALLY: recognised environmental associations and COMITATI DI CITTADINI — citizens' committees — can have standing to bring the appeal. A residents' committee is a recognised litigant in Italy, which is what this file has been looking for in every country. WHAT IT COSTS, stated plainly so a group can budget: the overall cost of a TAR appeal in building matters — including the interim relief phase, the investigation and the merits hearing — runs indicatively between 3,000 and 10,000 euro, plus the court filing fee. AND THE STRONGEST GROUND IT NAMES: breaches of the 1968 ministerial decree on building distances are easily demonstrable with planimetric measurements, and settled case law holds that the decree has force of law and PREVAILS over any more permissive local planning instruments — annulment having led in several cases to an order to demolish.

trackers.name: Infobandi CSVnet — a search engine for every open funding call for the third sector
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: THE SEARCH ENGINE FOR FUNDING OPPORTUNITIES FOR VOLUNTEERING AND THE THIRD SECTOR, with an environment tag listing open calls as they appear. Italy had 30 filed entries and only two funders; this is the standing index rather than one grant. WHAT ITS ENVIRONMENT LISTINGS ACTUALLY CARRY, from one snapshot: a multi-year EU facility to revitalise European neighbourhoods with design geared to sustainability and inclusion, supporting projects of SUSTAINABLE TRANSFORMATION OF THE BUILT ENVIRONMENT; a foundation supporting the resilience of communities to natural disasters; a fund for SMALL TARGETED INTERVENTIONS of modest economic commitment — A MAXIMUM OF 5,000 EURO — but effective in favouring gradual self-development; contributions for innovative communication projects able to influence public opinion and increase political support; and an award for projects by women engaged in concrete actions to DEFEND AND PRESERVE TREES, from urban to rural areas, working in close collaboration with the local community. A 5,000 euro ceiling and a tree-defence prize sit in the same index as an EU facility — which is why an index beats knowing one funder. Alongside it, a national municipalities association runs a call supporting COMUNI to assign UNUSED OR PARTLY USED MUNICIPAL PROPERTY into the management of people aged 18 to 35.

trackers.name: Fondazione CON IL SUD — and its offer to help a community BUILD its own foundation
trackers.desc: THE OFFER THAT MATTERS MOST, and nothing else in this file makes it: the foundation intends to play a propulsive role, FLANKING AND ACCOMPANYING LOCAL COMMUNITIES THAT INTEND TO CREATE A COMMUNITY FOUNDATION, becoming their strategic partner, and is interested in learning about proposals to constitute community foundations and assessing whether they meet the requirements for support. A national funder that will help you set up your own local funder is the longest-lasting resource a region can acquire — because community foundations, in its own words, are an important instrument of SOCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE for the territory, based on the aggregation and collaboration of bodies EXPRESSING THE LOCAL REALITY, able to ATTRACT RESOURCES, value them through careful asset management, AND INVEST THEM LOCALLY. AND WHAT ITS OWN ENVIRONMENTAL CALLS FUND: a fourth-edition environment bando inviting third sector organisations in six named southern regions to present exemplary projects for prevention and reduction; a local development bando putting 8 MILLION EURO behind small comuni and third sector organisations, whose eligible actions include valorisation of environmental resources — creation of SOCIAL ENERGY COMMUNITIES, RECOVERY AND USE OF ABANDONED LAND, of natural parks — requiring a territory of at least three neighbouring comuni with a population no greater than 20,000; and one putting 300,000 euro of private resources behind bringing a 13-hectare holding back into cultivation.

trackers.name: The Programma per le Aree affiliate — a PRIVATE owner can have their own land made an oasi
trackers.desc: THE ROUTE FOR AN OWNER WHO KEEPS THEIR LAND, and it is the one this file has been looking for in Italy: since 2005, alongside the directly managed oases, there are oases NOT managed by the association's local groups BUT MANAGED BY OTHER PRIVATE PARTIES, and for that reason AFFILIATED through the PROGRAMME OF AFFILIATED AREAS — an affiliation agreement that makes it possible to protect ALSO THOSE AREAS OF ENVIRONMENTAL INTEREST WHICH FALL WITHIN PRIVATE LAND. An owner who will not sell can still put their land inside a national network of protected oases by agreement, keeping title and management. THE SCALE BEHIND IT: 106 oases across all Italian regions, totalling 31,000 HECTARES of protected territory — of which 6,500 HECTARES BELONG DIRECTLY to the association; management is in most cases entrusted to the LOCAL associations. AND WHO ELSE HOLDS OASES, each a separate door: pioneer associations including the bird protection league, a Pro Natura body and Legambiente. The bird league has protected and managed since 1973 areas important for the reproduction of migratory birds or the conservation of particular bird species, such as Important Bird Areas, with about 50,000 faunal and floral species censused and preserved in its oases, including some 250 bird species, and named oases among them.

trackers.name: Bosco Rocconi — how one oasi was actually paid for, purchase by purchase
trackers.desc: THE FUNDING HISTORY OF A SINGLE SITE, which is the most useful thing a community can read before starting its own: in 1995, with a named forests campaign, came THE FIRST PURCHASE OF 130 HECTARES, thanks in part to the contribution of a named member from Siena who gave ABOUT TWENTY MILLION LIRE towards the purchase, and to whom he devoted many years of his life. One named individual's donation started a 130-hectare reserve — the whole thing did not need an institution first. AND HOW IT GREW: subsequently A SUBSCRIPTION BY LONG-STANDING MEMBERS allowed the area to be enlarged by a further 4 HECTARES of woodland at a named locality. Finally, at the beginning of 2009, THANKS TO THE GENEROUS DONATION OF A MARRIED COUPLE, it was possible to acquire a further portion of land (5 HECTARES) in one of the wildest zones. A hundred and thirty hectares, then four, then five — a reserve assembled in pieces as money appeared, which is how a community should expect its own to grow. AND WHAT THE PURCHASES BOUGHT IN STATUS: since 1998 the oasi has been part of a PROVINCIAL NATURE RESERVE, included within a Special Conservation Zone and a Special Protection Zone — private purchase first, public designation after.

trackers.name: How to buy a wood in Italy — 26 owned, 28 AFFILIATED, and a live 4-hectare appeal
trackers.desc: A NATIONAL FOREST BUYER AND, MORE USEFULLY, THE OPTION FOR OWNERS WHO WILL NOT SELL: IT IS ALSO POSSIBLE TO AFFILIATE TO THE NETWORK OF FREE WOODS; IN THIS CASE THE OWNER WILL KEEP OWNERSHIP OF THE WOOD, RECEIVING FREE OF CHARGE THE NECESSARY SCIENTIFIC ADVICE TO MAKE IT AN OASIS OF BIODIVERSITY. Italy had six acquisition entries against 34 total. Free scientific advice in exchange for keeping the trees is the lightest possible ask of an owner, and the numbers show it works: TODAY THE FOUNDATION COUNTS 26 WOODS OF ITS OWN PROPERTY FOR 200 HECTARES IN ALL, PLUS ANOTHER 28 AFFILIATED PROPERTIES FOR 274 HECTARES. The affiliated land is larger than the owned land — more ground was protected by advice than by purchase. AND THE STATUTORY LOCK ON WHAT IT OWNS: BY STATUTORY OBLIGATION THE FOUNDATION'S WOODS ARE LEFT TO THEIR FREE EVOLUTION, WITHOUT CUTTING FOR ECONOMIC PURPOSES, though felling remains possible for legal, phytosanitary or common-sense reasons, BUT NEVER TO PRODUCE INCOME. AND A LIVE CASE ANY READER CAN JOIN: an ongoing project concerns THE ACQUISITION OF A WOOD OF 4 HECTARES IN TUSCANY, WHICH THE CURRENT OWNERS HAVE PUT ON THE TIMBER-SUPPLY MARKET; A LARGE POPULAR COLLECTION IS UNDER WAY AND ANYONE CAN CONTRIBUTE. Nearby, a father and son planting since 2000 reached OVER 15,000 PLANTS and used a European rural fund to RESIST THE PRESSURE OF NUMEROUS PURCHASE OFFERS FROM BUILDING FIRMS.

trackers.name: When the seller changes their mind — a failed purchase, and what the money did instead
trackers.desc: A COLLAPSED PURCHASE, RECORDED BY THE BUYER ITSELF, because a community should know this happens: IMPORTANT NOTICE: UNFORTUNATELY THE EXPANSION OF THE OASIS IS NO LONGER POSSIBLE, BECAUSE THE SELLING PARTY HAS CHANGED ITS MIND AND, EVEN THOUGH IT HAD SIGNED A REGULAR PRELIMINARY CONTRACT OF SALE, IS NO LONGER SELLING. A signed preliminary contract did not hold the land — the single most important warning in this file for anyone raising money against a promise. AND WHAT WAS DONE WITH THE MONEY, which is the part worth copying: ALL THE DONORS WERE INFORMED AND WERE ASKED WHETHER THEY WANTED THEIR MONEY BACK, BUT NOBODY ASKED FOR IT, SO THE PROCEEDS OF THIS FUNDRAISING WILL SERVE TO PAY THE NOTARIAL COSTS OF SOME LAND THAT HAS BEEN OFFERED IN DONATION TO the foundation, SO SAVING FROM FELLING A LARGER AREA, EVEN IF FRAGMENTED. Telling every donor and offering refunds is what let the fund be redirected, and the redirected money bought more ground than the failed purchase would have. AND THE ORIGINAL NUMBERS, useful as a price benchmark: THE PART TO BE BOUGHT IS ABOUT 5 HECTARES FOR A COST OF 16,500 EURO. WE ARE LOOKING FOR 20,000 EURO BECAUSE WE WILL ALSO HAVE TO PAY NOTARIAL AND ANCILLARY EXPENSES. The appeal budgeted the legal costs on top of the price — the item most community appeals forget.

trackers.name: Sir[a]
trackers.desc: Sir[a] originated from the Community Action Group, a grassroots organisation working on mental health and human rights. It is a centre for holistic medical, psychological, and legal care for people affected by situations of violence, mistreatment, or torture. Its headquarters are in Madrid, with a presence in Barcelona, the Basque Country and Valencia. Staff members are professionals in psychiatry, psychology, medicine, law, and journalism, including with high-level expertise on the Istanbul Protocol. Sir[a] works to support processes of justice and reparation, including rehabilitation through a human rights, psychosocial and cross-cultural approach. Around 80% of the referrals it receives are of people who suffered ill-treatment and torture. Its work includes lawsuits for ill-treatment and torture in Spain but also for other courts, such as the European Court of Human Rights or the International Criminal Court. In addition to individual cases, Sir[a] carries out expert reports on collective cases of human rights violations and torture at the international level. It also has a research area dedicated to the implementation of innovative tools for the documentation of torture, the credibility of allegations and impact assessment.

trackers.name: Maldita.es (investigative outlet)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (investigative newsroom); Maldita.es (investigative outlet) — Spanish fact-checking and data-journalism newsroom holding power to account, exposing disinformation and using FOI to force transparency.

trackers.name: IIDMA — Instituto Internacional de Derecho y Medio Ambiente
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Spain's nonprofit environmental law centre, founded 1996 and declared of public utility, which puts law at the service of the environment through litigation before public administrations and the courts — most Spanish environmental cases run through the contencioso-administrativo or criminal jurisdictions, and IIDMA works in both. Accredited to the UN Environment Assembly since 1998 and a member of the Justice and Environment network, so it also pursues EU-level routes. WHO IT SUITS: a group with a case that can move Spanish or EU environmental law, rather than a routine neighbour dispute — this is a strategic-litigation and policy centre, not a walk-in advice desk.

trackers.name: Plataforma de Custodia del Territorio (Fundación Biodiversidad)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the state-level meeting point for Spain's custodia del territorio movement, run by the Fundación Biodiversidad under the environment ministry. Custodia is a statutory mechanism: article 76 of the Ley de Patrimonio Natural y de la Biodiversidad obliges public administrations to promote voluntary agreements between accredited custodia entities and owners of private OR public land whose main object is conserving natural heritage, and lets the State cede management of its own land in natural spaces to those entities. Publishes the national inventory of custodia agreements and entities. USE IT: to find the custodia entity that can take on a threatened finca near you, or to push a municipality to sign as an owner or as an entity itself — hundreds of agreements already sit on public land.

trackers.name: Justice and Environment — European green-law network
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the European network of environmental-law NGOs, whose national member here is IIDMA. Its fifteen members act as the environmental-law service point in their own countries, taking cases and intervening in legislative processes, while the network defends communities and nature in court and lodges infringement complaints against member-state governments. Its standing themes are access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, environmental assessment and pollution control. WHO IT SUITS: anyone who does not yet know which lawyer to call — knock on IIDMA's door first, and use the network only if your problem crosses a border. The network itself does not take individual cases; its members do. YOUR NATIONAL MEMBER IS International Institute for Law and Environment (IIDMA) (iidma.org) — go to them, not to the network. J&E members serve as environmental law ‘service points’ in their countries, handling cases, participating in legislative processes and sometimes providing legal analyses and consultations for national governments. The network has 11 full and 4 associate members, and can launch infringement proceedings against faulty governments — a route a national body alone does not have. CURRENT SCOPE: access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, climate, environmental assessments, and the Environmental Liability Directive. It previously worked on waste, transport, health and Natura 2000, so an older document may overstate what it covers today.

trackers.name: Fundación Biodiversidad — convocatorias de ayudas
trackers.desc: SPAIN'S MAIN PUBLIC ENVIRONMENTAL GRANT-MAKER, attached to the environment ministry and awarding competitively. WHO QUALIFIES: non-profit entities of state or EU scope, or of regional or local scope provided they take part in networks or programmes of state or EU character — with seat in Spain, legally constituted and registered. Some calls also admit public research bodies, universities, professional bodies, local administration entities, and agrupaciones of up to 4 entities. CHECK THE MINIMUM PROJECT SIZE BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — the floor excludes small groups. The bioeconomy call held EUR 39.62 million but required each project to budget between EUR 500,000 and EUR 2,000,000, with co-financing up to 85 percent in less developed regions, 60 in transition regions and 40 in more developed ones. The DANA recovery call held up to EUR 5 million: Eje 1 EUR 350,000–1,000,000 per project, Eje 2 EUR 100,000–500,000. A group with a small project cannot apply alone — join an agrupación or a state/EU network, which is also how you meet the eligibility test. AND READ THE TERRITORIAL CLAUSE: the DANA call's Eje 2 was open only to third-sector non-profits with registered office in Comunidad Valenciana, Castilla-La Mancha or Andalucía. Regulatory bases: Orden TED/818/2021 and Orden TED/1060/2024; calls are published in the BOE and on the foundation's site. More than 1,100 entities have been supported over the programme's history.

trackers.name: Custodia del territorio — a neighbours' association can hold land in custody
trackers.desc: A VOLUNTARY AGREEMENT BETWEEN A LANDOWNER AND A CUSTODY ENTITY on how to conserve and manage land — and the entry barrier is remarkably low. An entidad de custodia can be any non-profit, public or private: the named range includes a neighbours' association, a conservation body, a foundation, an ayuntamiento, a consortium. In practice 63 percent are associations, 17 foundations, 13 public entities. THE AGREEMENT MAY BE VERBAL OR WRITTEN — of the agreements inventoried, 2,385 were written, 734 territorial conventions and 498 verbal. Forms run from managing a finca on sustainable criteria in exchange for technical advice, through agreements limiting exploitation, to outright sale of the parcel to the custody entity. YOUR COUNCIL CAN BE EITHER PARTY: 466 agreements sit on public patrimonial land and 23 municipalities have signed as custody entities, covering 151 agreements over more than 2,000 hectares. FIND YOUR REGIONAL NETWORK — Xarxa de Custòdia (Catalonia), Avinença (Valencia), ICTIB (Balearics), Castilla y León, Madrid/Castilla-La Mancha, Transcantábrica, Aragonesa, Ínsulas (Andalucía), Rede Galega — coordinated by FRECT since late 2011.

trackers.name: Modelo de acuerdo de custodia — do not draft from scratch
trackers.desc: A PUBLISHED MODEL CONTRACT, so you are not starting from a blank page. It is structured around identifying the parcels exactly as they appear in the Registro de la Propiedad and the cadastre, and then describing the natural values — ecosystems, habitats, species, landscapes — that justify the agreement, stating whether that value is European, state, regional or local. Getting that second section right is what makes an agreement defensible later. SCALE, from the 7th Inventory (2020–2023): 4,632 custody agreements, up 49 percent on the previous count. Predominant use is forestry (35 percent of agreements) then agrarian (32). Ownership is 79 percent private, 17 public and 4 percent communal — so this is primarily a tool for reaching private owners, and every autonomous community has agreements in place.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Fundación Global Nature and the custodia del territorio agreement (Spain)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: custodia del territorio is Spain's dominant conservation instrument for private land — a voluntary agreement between the owner of a finca, public or private, and a non-profit custodia entity, setting conservation objectives for that specific holding. Fundación Global Nature is one of the largest operators: it reports work with almost 200 owners under 179 agreements covering about 23,700 hectares across six autonomous communities. Nationally the inventory kept by Fundación Biodiversidad counts more than 225 custodia entities, some 3,100 agreements and close to 600,000 hectares. USE IT: two facts change what a Spanish community does. A municipality can itself be the custodia entity, not merely the owner — the national inventory records 23 municipalities signed up as entities across 151 agreements on more than 2,000 hectares, and 466 agreements struck on public patrimonial land. And the agreement may be verbal or written, which lowers the threshold for a first conversation with an owner considerably. THE TRAP, AND READ THE CAVEAT WITH IT: custodia agreements are also being used as the vehicle for the compensation packages attached to renewable-energy consents.
