An organisation that led the creation of the country's national parks is the one to ask how a new designation is won.

trackers.name: A volunteer network of ACADEMICS AND SPECIALIST SCIENTISTS, and what it does with a breach
trackers.desc: WHERE THE EXPERTISE COMES FROM, which is the resource a Greek community most lacks: to carry out its mission the organisation relies, besides its staff, ON AN EXTENSIVE NETWORK OF VOLUNTEERS, MANY OF WHOM ARE UNIVERSITY ACADEMICS AND SPECIALIST SCIENTISTS. Greece is among the least-worked buckets in this file. Academics volunteering their expertise is the free version of the expert report that decides most cases — the same gap Austria fills with a statutory office (batch579) and Australia with a volunteer register (batch506). AND THE LADDER OF ACTION IT USES, set out from lightest to heaviest: THE ORGANISATION INTERVENES, ALONE OR IN COOPERATION WITH OTHER ENVIRONMENTAL NGOs, TOWARDS THE PUBLIC SERVICES AND OTHER COMPETENT BODIES WHEN IT ESTABLISHES VIOLATIONS OF NATIONAL OR EUROPEAN ENVIRONMENTAL REGULATIONS AND LAWS, OR THREATS TO OUR NATURAL ENVIRONMENT. THIS IS DONE BY DIRECT COMMUNICATION, LETTERS OR PRESS RELEASES OR, FURTHER, BY APPEALS TO THE COUNCIL OF STATE IN CASES OF IMPORTANT MATTERS. A telephone call, a letter, a press release, then the supreme administrative court — and the same body does all four, so a community does not have to change partner as the dispute escalates. Its interventions have also ended in OFFICIAL COMPLAINTS TO THE EUROPEAN COMMISSION.

trackers.name: A technical guide written FOR JUDGES AND PROSECUTORS on environmental liability
trackers.desc: A DOCUMENT AIMED AT THE PEOPLE WHO DECIDE THE CASE, not at campaigners: a named TECHNICAL GUIDE: THE ENVIRONMENTAL LIABILITY DIRECTIVE AND WILDLIFE — GUIDE FOR JUDGES, PROSECUTORS, COURT AND PROSECUTION OFFICIALS, published by the country's oldest nature organisation with a ministry, running to 96 PAGES, and TWO FURTHER TECHNICAL GUIDES WERE ISSUED under the same action. A guide for judges is a resource a community can cite in its own filing, because the bench is the audience it was written for — the counterpart to the Slovenian handbook for civil society in batch573, aimed at the other side of the courtroom. AND WHAT IT COVERS, which tells a group what arguments it supports: EUROPEAN AND NATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL LEGISLATION, WITH EMPHASIS ON THE NATURA 2000 NETWORK AND THE DIRECTIVES ON WILD BIRDS AND HABITATS, ON THE BASIS OF WHICH IT WAS CREATED AND PLACED UNDER MANAGEMENT IN THE MEMBER STATES OF THE EUROPEAN UNION, together with OTHER PARTICULAR FIELDS OF ENVIRONMENTAL LAW, WITH CURRENT MATERIAL. Natura 2000 and the birds and habitats directives are named as the emphasis, which is where a Greek site's strongest protection is likely to lie.

trackers.name: Register of Lobbyists (Ministry of Justice)
trackers.desc: Register of Lobbyists (Ministry of Justice) — Czechia’s official register of those paid to lobby ministers and government agencies. — Holds to account: who influences Czechia’s executive — find lobbyist registrations and activity.

trackers.name: Office for Personal Data Protection (ÚOOÚ)
trackers.desc: Office for Personal Data Protection (ÚOOÚ) — Czechia’s independent data-protection / information commissioner, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Constitutional Court (NALUS)
trackers.desc: Official database of decisions of the Czech Constitutional Court. · Find here: the decisions of the Czech Constitutional Court (NALUS database).

trackers.name: Info Pro Všechny — FOI requests (CZE)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (FOI request platform); Info Pro Všechny — civic Freedom-of-Information request platform (Alaveteli/mySociety network) — lets citizens file public-records requests and publishes the requests and the authorities’ responses in a public archive.

trackers.name: Frank Bold Society — citizens' and municipalities' legal counselling
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Czech public-interest law NGO whose counselling centre answers over 500 queries a year, free, with an emphasis on environmental protection, maladministration and clientelism — and which publishes model legal submissions, FAQs and manuals online so you can file yourself. Works on both Czech and Polish cases from offices in Brno, Ostrava, Prague, Kraków and Brussels; long record on coal, air quality and permit proceedings. WHO IT SUITS: an individual or a local initiative being shut out of an administrative proceeding or refused information by an authority. Note the separately branded commercial law firm is a different entity that also acts for businesses — the NGO is the public-interest side.

trackers.name: Justice and Environment — European green-law network
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the European network of environmental-law NGOs, whose national member here is Frank Bold Society. Its fifteen members act as the environmental-law service point in their own countries, taking cases and intervening in legislative processes, while the network defends communities and nature in court and lodges infringement complaints against member-state governments. Its standing themes are access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, environmental assessment and pollution control. WHO IT SUITS: anyone who does not yet know which lawyer to call — knock on Frank Bold Society's door first, and use the network only if your problem crosses a border. The network itself does not take individual cases; its members do. YOUR NATIONAL MEMBER IS Frank Bold Society (en.frankbold.org) — go to them, not to the network. J&E members serve as environmental law ‘service points’ in their countries, handling cases, participating in legislative processes and sometimes providing legal analyses and consultations for national governments. The network has 11 full and 4 associate members, and can launch infringement proceedings against faulty governments — a route a national body alone does not have. CURRENT SCOPE: access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, climate, environmental assessments, and the Environmental Liability Directive. It previously worked on waste, transport, health and Natura 2000, so an older document may overstate what it covers today.

trackers.name: ČSOP — Místo pro přírodu (land-purchase collection & pozemkové spolky)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: buys land to stop it being destroyed, using a registered public collection rather than an endowment. Místo pro přírodu has run since 2003 and has purchased 218 hectares at 61 sites — near-natural woodland, wetlands, steppe, flower-rich meadows, and ground along watercourses earmarked for restoration. Bought land becomes ČSOP's own property and is then handed to a local pozemkový spolek, a land trust, to care for permanently. USE IT three ways. Donate and CHOOSE THE SITE — the collection lets a giver pick which of dozens of locations their money buys, so a community can point outside support at its own parcel. Bring it a site: recent purchases include a hectare added to the Sedmihorské mokřady wetland and three hectares of floodplain forest near Karviná, both prompted locally. Or start your own land trust — ČSOP publishes the founding stories of existing pozemkové spolky as a how-to, and ownership is often the only durable way to protect ground that designation alone has failed to save.

trackers.name: Pozemkové spolky — Czech land trust network and purchase procedure
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the network of Czech land trusts, which take on care of natural and historic sites by agreement with the owner and, where agreement is not enough, by purchase — and unusually, it publishes the actual procedure instead of an invitation to get in touch. USE IT: the sequence is the point. You can apply to have a locality accepted into the purchase campaign BEFORE any negotiation, so the National Land Trust Council rules on whether the site qualifies before you approach the owner, and a Council member or central-office officer visits it before the application is decided. A second application follows once a specific parcel is agreed with the owner. The local land trust does the negotiating; the central office drafts the contract. Two things worth taking from their own guidance: gather everything you can about the site and, where you do not have a fact, say so rather than write an unverified assumption. And if no land trust covers your area, the site sets out how to found one.

trackers.name: OPŽP — the main environmental fund, and spolky can apply
trackers.desc: THE BIG MONEY, AND ASSOCIATIONS ARE ELIGIBLE. The Operační program Životní prostředí draws more than CZK 60 billion over 2021–2027 from the European Regional Development Fund and the Cohesion Fund — and its listed applicants expressly include foundations, endowment funds, institutes, spolky and public benefit companies, not only municipalities. Calls cover slowing runoff and retaining rainwater; flood protection and strengthening the landscape's natural retention capacity with nature-friendly measures preferred; creating and restoring nature-close water and vegetation features including anti-erosion measures; remediating the most seriously contaminated sites; and stabilising extreme slope instabilities. Apply and manage through IS KP21+, and subscribe to the email alerts rather than checking for calls by hand. Administered with the Státní fond životního prostředí, which co-finances through grants, loans and financial instruments across water and air quality, waste, nature and landscape protection and environmental education.

trackers.name: Nadace Partnerství — up to CZK 100,000, and money for aftercare
trackers.desc: THE SMALL, FAST ROUTE. A Czech environmental foundation running since 1992 and part of the Environmental Partnership Association, giving grants plus advisory and educational services. Up to CZK 100,000 for tree planting, water retention in the landscape and other adaptation measures — and, separately, up to CZK 100,000 for the care of newly planted trees, which matters because planting without maintenance money fails. The Sázíme budoucnost call targets measures mainly in the open landscape (non-forest, unbuilt) that even out temperature extremes, improve air quality, raise the soil's capacity to hold water and increase biodiversity. CHECK YOUR LEGAL FORM FIRST: eligible applicants are legal persons only — spolky, institutes, public benefit companies, church legal persons, contributory organisations, unit owners' associations, cooperatives, foundations and endowment funds, school legal persons, municipalities and their associations, and public research institutions. An unincorporated group of neighbours cannot apply, so constitute first.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Frank Bold Society — free legal advice line for active citizens (Czechia)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Czech association founded in 1995 that runs what it describes as the largest free legal advice service for the public in the fields of public law, the environment and anti-corruption, from offices in Prague, Brno and Ostrava. Its advice line is restricted, deliberately, to active citizens whose case is not merely their own private matter — it says so on the intake page. Threats to the environment, the impact of construction on quality of life, corruption, poor administration, public participation: those are its subjects, and a purely private neighbour dispute is not. WHAT YOU GET WITHOUT ASKING ANYONE: a published database of more than 420 legal manuals, answered questions and templates, free to use, covering how to found an association, how to make an information request, and how to keep track of significant building proposals near you. For many groups that is enough to take the first three steps without spending anyone's time. UNDERSTAND THE STRUCTURE BEFORE YOU WRITE: Frank Bold is a group. The association runs the free advice line, funded by foundations, grants and donors; Frank Bold Advokati is a separate paid law firm specialising in renewable energy, public and construction law, which donates to the association and lets it use its premises. The finances are stated to be separate. If you are opposing a renewable energy scheme, say so at the outset and ask which part of the group is answering you. The Polish foundation in the same group is a sister organisation, not a branch.

trackers.name: Nadace Partnerství — Czech Environmental Partnership Foundation
trackers.desc: WHAT THE CONSORTIUM IS: the Environmental Partnership Association, headquartered in Brno, is a consortium of six independent national foundations in central and eastern Europe that give grants to community projects protecting the environment. It grew out of a programme begun in 1990 by the C.S. Mott Foundation, the German Marshall Fund and the Rockefeller Brothers Fund, and the national foundations were established as independent bodies in the early 1990s. Alongside grants they run education programmes, provide professional services and build the capacity of civic initiatives — which is the part a new local group needs most. THE CZECH MEMBER: founded 1991 and the largest of the six, it distributes grants and works on environmental protection, climate adaptation, sustainable transport and tourism, tree and water protection and the quality of public spaces. Over its first 23 years it distributed more than 238 million crowns across 2,722 projects in the Czech Republic alone; a later figure puts the total above 396 million crowns. It also runs the Czech Tree of the Year competition, going since 2002, which became the European Tree of the Year in 2011 — a cheap and effective way to put a specific threatened tree in front of a national audience. SOURCING: the consortium and its six national foundations are documented on the Environmental Partnership Association's own site; the national figures and founding dates come from consortium and partner material rather than each foundation's own pages. Confirm current grant rounds with the national foundation directly.

trackers.name: Hnutí DUHA — local groups that watch development, and teach citizens how to win
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the largest Czech nature protection organisation, founded 1989, Friends of the Earth's Czech member and a founding member of the CEE Bankwatch Network, with offices at Údolí 33, Brno and in Prague, pratele@hnutiduha.cz. The instruction on its own volunteering page is the entry: the Brno and Prague offices handle national issues only, so if you want to protect nature where you live, contact the branch in your region. Its local groups do what their region needs — and the list of what they do includes actively watching the development of towns and the countryside, working directly and successfully with local councils. WHAT THE BRNO GROUP ACTUALLY DID, as a worked example of what a local group is for: alongside other initiatives it forced a second referendum on the location of the city's railway station, and its stated long-term aim is to build a platform of civic initiatives that can be a constructive partner to the city administration on measures affecting quality of life. That is a community taking a seat rather than sending a letter. AND IT TRAINS PEOPLE: it states that it teaches active citizens how to achieve change. For a group that has just formed, that is the offer to ask for first. ITS RECORD: it has beaten off proposals that would have opened the most valuable zones of Czech national parks to developers and to logging; it pushed through strict limits on mercury emissions that brought forward the end of the largest polluting coal plants; it stopped the official culling of lynx by appealing to the ministry and then ran field projects against poaching. Around fifty staff. WHAT IT IS NOT: not a land buyer and not a law firm — Czechia's other entries in this file are a free legal advice line and a grant-making foundation, and this is the campaigning and local organising leg. Note also that it actively supports wind and community energy, so a community opposing a renewable scheme should expect a different view here.

trackers.name: Zelený kruh — 28 members, a platform of 70 more, and a published member catalogue
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: an association of Czech non-governmental ecological organisations, founded in November 1989 and one of the oldest umbrella NGOs in the country, with 28 full members — and since 2002 it provides the organisational base for a sector platform of environmental NGOs that includes around 70 further organisations beyond its own membership. Lublaňská 18, Prague 2; member of the European Environmental Bureau. Named members include Arnika — already in this file — Ateliér pro životní prostředí, Auto*Mat, Beleco, Calla, the Czech Ornithological Society and Čisté nebe. AND IT PUBLISHES A CATALOGUE OF ITS MEMBERS with a short description of what each organisation does and named contact people with email addresses. That is the fastest route in this file from 'I need help in Czechia' to a named person at the right organisation. WHAT THE OFFICE ACTUALLY DOES FOR MEMBERS: it monitors proposals for changes to legislation and policy, coordinates the preparation of joint thematic positions, and has long worked specifically on the question of public participation in decision-making about projects and plans with an impact on the environment. It also coordinates the selection of experts from ecological organisations into interdisciplinary working groups and government advisory bodies and commissions, and analyses how MPs vote on key laws. WHAT MEMBERSHIP COSTS AND GIVES: full members take part in joint decision-making, help formulate the association's positions, and receive legislative monitoring and support in advocacy activities; there is an annual membership fee set individually, with an information pack for prospective members and a named staff contact. Associated membership exists as a lighter form. It notes its members differ in size, focus and regional coverage. AND THE RECORD IT CLAIMS: joint campaigns by member organisations secured protection of valuable territories in national parks, and members have jointly called on the prime minister and party leaders to support existing national park protection and the declaration of a new one at Křivoklátsko.

trackers.name: SFŽP and the Národní program Životní prostředí — spolky are named eligible applicants
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the State Environmental Fund of the Czech Republic, established by law 388/1991 and administered by the environment ministry, which says it has invested more than 231 billion CZK to protect and improve the environment, nature and landscape since 1992. Its Národní program Životní prostředí is financed from the charges collected under the component environmental laws and is designed as a complement for projects not supported by the Operational Programme Environment or other schemes — so it is the route for work that falls between the big programmes. AND NON-STATE NON-PROFITS ARE NAMED: in a published call for improving the environment in national parks and the quality of life in the municipalities inside them, one activity strand is open to national park administrations and non-state non-profit organisations whose main activity is environmental education, upbringing and awareness — especially registered spolky and public-benefit companies — at 85 per cent of total eligible expenditure. Another strand is open to all legal persons except commercial corporations with under 50 per cent municipal ownership, and political parties and movements. Read each výzva: eligibility is set activity by activity. HOW TO APPLY: electronically through the SFŽP agenda information system at zadosti.sfzp.cz; you can apply only within a numbered, published výzva aimed at one of the priority areas, and the conditions — who may apply and how much — are set out in the text of that call. The programme is divided into ten priority axes. SCALE AND OBLIGATION: the NPŽP framework for 2024–2026 was approved at 3.3 billion CZK, within a fund budget running to tens of billions a year. Note one duty attached: the recipient is responsible for informing the public that the project was carried out with the financial participation of the Fund, following a binding publicity manual. AND THE SISTER PROGRAMME TO CHECK: the Operational Programme Environment lists nature and biodiversity, and blue-green infrastructure among its priority areas; general enquiries info@mzp.cz, +420 267 121 111.

trackers.name: Informační systém EIA and SEA — and the SEA side holds the municipal land-use plans
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the national information system run by CENIA, the Czech environmental information agency, keeping the record of assessed projects and publishing the documents produced during the assessment process on the internet. Every záměr appears with its current stage. AND THE SEA SIDE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES NEED: the parallel SEA system holds the record of assessed koncepce at national level, zásady územního rozvoje at regional level, and ÚZEMNÍ PLÁNY OBCÍ — municipal land-use plans — at local level, publishing the documents acquired during their assessment as the law requires. The plan that decides what may be built in your village is assessed, and the assessment is published. WHO MAY COMMENT, AND WHEN: not only the affected administrative authorities but the wide public can take part in the EIA and SEA processes with their comments. Anyone can comment on projects published on the official notice board or on the internet throughout the whole assessment process, up to the date always stated on the published document. At the end the competent authority issues a binding statement, agreeing or disagreeing, on the basis of all comments received, the notification, the documentation, the expert review and the public hearing. WHAT ELSE THE SYSTEM CARRIES, which is unusual: a list of sub-threshold projects; projects outside Czech territory; the register of holders of authorisation to prepare documentation and expert reviews, and of holders of authorisation to assess impacts on the Natura 2000 network; the legislation with the environment ministry's methodological guidance; and the list of affected sites of Community importance and bird areas. A published register of who is authorised to write the assessment lets you check the developer's consultant — and the methodological guidance is what to cite when an assessment skips a step.

trackers.name: Místo pro přírodu — a licensed public collection that buys land, 220 hectares so far
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a long-running national campaign and veřejná sbírka — a LICENSED PUBLIC COLLECTION, authorised by decision of the Prague City Hall — whose purpose is saving valuable places in nature from destruction THROUGH THE PURCHASE OF LAND. Czechia had 69 filed entries and one acquirer; this is the buying machinery. A publicly licensed collection with a permit number is a fundraising form a community can copy, and the permit is what lets strangers give with confidence. THE NUMBERS, AND THE RATE: over six dozen Místa pro přírodu across the country, 220 hectares; roughly 10 hectares of valuable land saved per year over more than a decade; and almost 3 million korun spent on land purchases in a single year. Purchases are fully dependent on public support — a gift of any size is welcome. WHAT IT BUYS, which is a scope worth copying: naturally and scenically valuable land — near-natural forests, wetlands, steppe sites, flowery meadows; land forming part of the proposed territorial system of ecological stability, to be gradually returned to a natural state; and land around watercourses suitable for revitalisation. AND WHO LOOKS AFTER IT AFTERWARDS: the land becomes the property of the national union, and local POZEMKOVÉ SPOLKY — land trusts — take the sites into their care under an agreed plan, because most need mowing, grazing or pool restoration. National body owns, local trust manages.

trackers.name: Místo pro přírodu — 213 hectares bought on 59 sites, and LOCAL GROUPS PROPOSE THE PURCHASES
trackers.desc: THE ROUTE IN, and it is the answer to 'who decides what gets bought': if the LAND SOCIETIES know of parcels that would be suitable to buy and do not themselves have enough means, THEY CAN PROPOSE THE PURCHASES within the Place for Nature campaign — and the localities for purchase are mostly proposed BY THE LAND SOCIETIES themselves. A national purchase fund whose acquisitions are nominated by local groups is one a village society can put its own threatened parcel to. Czechia's bucket had the fragmentation problem recorded; this is the machinery that works around it. WHAT IT HAS DONE: the public collection was declared in 2003 as THE VERY FIRST COLLECTION IN OUR COUNTRY WHOSE AIM IS THE PURCHASE OF LAND FOR THE BENEFIT OF NATURE; since then about 27 MILLION CROWNS has been raised, with THOUSANDS OF INDIVIDUAL DONORS and a corporate foundation fund giving regularly. WHAT IT BUYS: either land naturally valuable for the sake of its protection, or land suitable for CREATING NEW OR RESTORED NATURAL HABITATS. The union owns the purchased land; the local land societies take it into their care. AND WHY THE MODEL WORKS, in their own words: land societies do not approach owners FROM A POSITION OF POWER, BUT AS PARTNERS. They set an example themselves; they are not the ones who merely instruct or order, but concrete work in the landscape can be seen behind them. Often they are LOCAL PEOPLE WHO ARE PART OF THE COMMUNITY. All of that opens doors even to people who otherwise view nature protection sceptically.

trackers.name: The collection account and the land-society directory — a bank number and a national address list
trackers.desc: WHAT THIS PAGE GIVES: the union's street address in the capital, TWO TELEPHONE NUMBERS, an email, and THE PUBLIC COLLECTION'S BANK ACCOUNT NUMBER, with the collection itself permitted by a numbered decision of the city authority — so a donor can see the permission behind it. A named bank account with the permitting decision printed beside it is what lets a community raise money into an existing legal collection instead of starting its own. AND THE DIRECTORY IT POINTS TO: closer information about the LAND SOCIETIES, THEIR COMPLETE ADDRESS DIRECTORY and a range of interesting documents are published on a separate national site. A complete national address list of local land-holding societies is the sheet that tells a village which body already works its own district. THE RUNNING TOTAL, as published here: since 2003, when the campaign began, 213 HECTARES have already been bought on 59 LOCALITIES across the country. A companion page records the next step being funded: two new localities and the extension of two already cared for, adding 4.2 hectares, at a cost of 990,000 CROWNS — and elsewhere, ownership of more than 220 hectares and eight wetland sites in a single region, the largest built up gradually, to 10.7 hectares.

trackers.name: Arnika's Občanův průvodce — a citizen's guide to planning and building proceedings
trackers.desc: WHAT THE GUIDE IS FOR: getting your bearings in planning and building proceedings is not simple, but it can be significantly useful if construction is being prepared near you. PARTICIPATION IN ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS IS THE BASIC TOOL FOR DEFENDING YOURSELF AGAINST HARMFUL PROJECTS. It sets out WHO CAN TAKE PART, AT WHAT MOMENT, WHAT THE DEADLINES ARE AND WHAT RIGHTS PARTIES HAVE. Czechia had 72 filed entries but only three on legal help. AND THE HONEST WARNING IT GIVES, which a Czech community must know before planning a campaign: after the amendment to the building act, PUBLIC PARTICIPATION HAS BECOME SIGNIFICANTLY MORE COMPLICATED; the standing of associations in building proceedings and spatial planning has been RESTRICTED, and in practice a society now takes part only in proceedings on FELLING TREES, and even then only where the felling does not precede construction. AND WHAT IT SAYS TO DO ANYWAY: it is still worth founding an association — it can act as A SOURCE OF INFORMATION FOR CITIZENS IN THE MUNICIPALITY, and it is certain that associations CAN take part in projects for which an EIA OPINION has been issued under a named act. Nobody took away their right to ASK TO BE INFORMED OF PROCEEDINGS BEING OPENED, even where they may not easily join them. A standing request to be told when proceedings open survives even where the right to join them does not.

trackers.name: Arnika — 20 years watching one city's development cases, with a live advice clinic
trackers.desc: WHAT IT RUNS: a LIVE ADVICE CLINIC on a city's forthcoming master plan — a practical meeting where we show you HOW TO READ THE PLAN and where to look for information — staffed by a named LAWYER SPECIALISING IN ENVIRONMENTAL LAW, BUILDING LAW, LOCAL SELF-GOVERNMENT AND THE PROTECTION OF THE PUBLIC IN PROCEDURAL SITUATIONS, and a named ecologist and elected councillor with long experience of DEVELOPER PROJECTS. A free session teaching residents to read the plan document itself is the cheapest legal training a community can get, and the event is OPEN TO EVERYONE, REGARDLESS OF PRIOR KNOWLEDGE, with questions invited on the registration form in advance. AND WHY IT MATTERS: the master plan will, once approved, be BINDING FOR ALL CONSTRUCTION in the city FOR DECADES, and comments could be submitted only until a stated date. AND THE TRACK RECORD BEHIND IT: Arnika has been watching the city's development cases FOR 20 YEARS and is an opposition voice representing citizens' interests AGAINST BIG DEVELOPERS, with 13,000 people joined to it. It supports active citizens, provides expert advice, and organises public events, and works to have the council treat citizens as EQUAL PARTNERS IN DISCUSSION. The clinic was run jointly with a second national organisation.

trackers.name: Místo pro přírodu — a standing PUBLIC COLLECTION with one bank account, 218 hectares bought
trackers.desc: A NATIONAL LAND-PURCHASE FUND ANYONE CAN PAY INTO, running continuously: the conservation union IS SEEKING THE PURCHASE OF TWO MORE VALUABLE WETLAND SITES, and IS LOOKING FOR SUPPORT FROM THE PUBLIC THROUGH ITS LONG-RUNNING COLLECTION 'A PLACE FOR NATURE'. IT THUS OWNS, AND THEREBY PROTECTS, MORE THAN 220 HECTARES OF LAND THROUGHOUT THE REPUBLIC. Czechia had four acquisition entries against 74 total — one of the thinnest ratios in this file. A permanent collection account, not a campaign that opens and closes, means a threatened parcel can be funded the week it comes up for sale — and the account number is published in every appeal. AND THE REASON GIVEN FOR BUYING RATHER THAN RELYING ON DESIGNATION, which is the sharpest statement of it in this file: one named site DOES HAVE LEGAL PROTECTION TOO, BUT FROM OTHER PLACES WE KNOW HOW AN UNCOOPERATIVE OWNER CAN COMPLICATE OR EVEN MAKE IMPOSSIBLE THE PROTECTION OF A SITE EVEN IN SUCH A CASE. OWNERSHIP OF THE LAND IS SIMPLY CERTAINTY. Legal protection plus a hostile owner can still fail; ownership cannot — which is the argument for buying even ground that is already designated. AND THE LOCAL STRUCTURE THAT MAKES IT WORK: sites are cared for by LOCAL LAND ASSOCIATIONS, one of which has looked after a named meadow FOR MORE THAN 15 YEARS; the purchase is described as AN INSURANCE FOR THE FUTURE THAT THIS LONG-TERM WORK WILL NOT COME TO NOTHING. In one region alone there are EIGHT such places, the largest built up to 10.7 HECTARES by successive purchases.

trackers.name: What a Czech purchase costs — 990,000 CROWNS for 4.2 hectares, published before the appeal
trackers.desc: A COMPLETED PURCHASE, WITH THE ROUTE IT CAME BY: IN THE CZECH REPUBLIC THERE ARE ALREADY MORE THAN 60 SO-CALLED PLACES FOR NATURE — NATURALLY VALUABLE SITES WHICH THE CONSERVATION UNION HAS BOUGHT FOR THEIR PROTECTION, and the newest, a former ski slope of 1.8 HECTARES, is described by local naturalists as ONE OF THE BOTANICALLY MOST VALUABLE MEADOWS OF THE RANGE OUTSIDE PROTECTED AREAS. AND HOW IT CAME TO BE OFFERED, which is the sentence a community should try to bring about: THE OWNERS DECIDED TO SELL THE MEADOW AND OFFERED IT AS A MATTER OF PREFERENCE PRECISELY TO THE CONSERVATION UNION. An owner who already knows who the conservation buyer is will offer to them first — so making that introduction long before a sale is the cheapest thing a local group can do. AND THE VOLUNTEER SIDE, which is what the purchase secures: volunteers had worked the slope for years, and when they return THEY WILL ALREADY BE WORKING, SO TO SPEAK, ON THEIR OWN. AND THE RUNNING TOTAL: WITHIN THE 'PLACE FOR NATURE' CAMPAIGN THE CONSERVATION UNION HAS ALREADY BOUGHT 218 HECTARES OF NATURALLY VALUABLE LAND AT 61 PLACES IN DIFFERENT CORNERS OF THE CZECH REPUBLIC. A separate appeal put the price of four new parcels totalling 4.2 hectares at 990,000 CROWNS.

trackers.name: Register of Lobbying
trackers.desc: Ireland's mandatory register under the 2015 Lobbying Act — quarterly returns of who lobbied which officials; among the strictest in the EU. — Holds to account: anyone lobbying Irish officials — find quarterly returns of who lobbied which officials on what, among the EU's strictest regimes.

trackers.name: Office of the Information Commissioner (Ireland)
trackers.desc: Independent regulator reviewing decisions under Ireland's Freedom of Information Act. — Holds to account: Irish public bodies — find the Information Commissioner's reviews and decisions on FOI refusals.

trackers.name: Legal Aid Board (Ireland)
trackers.desc: Statutory provider of civil legal aid and advice in Ireland. · Find here: civil (and some criminal) legal aid in Ireland (Legal Aid Board). FIVE OF THE EIGHT EXCLUSIONS BITE DIRECTLY ON LAND DEFENCE — read them before you apply. Section 28(9) of the Civil Legal Aid Act 1995 excludes: defamation; Small Claims Court cases; licensing; election petitions; class actions to establish a precedent on a point of law (test cases); any matter where the applicant is a member of a group having the same interest in the proceedings; representation for actions in tribunals (the Board does take Refugee Appeals Tribunal cases); and some disputes concerning rights or interests in property. Licensing covers the permits most developments need; a test case is excluded as such; and being one of a group with the same interest is what a community campaign IS. Section 28(9)(a)(vii)–(viii) adds that aid may not be granted where the application is made in a representative, fiduciary or official capacity — so applying as an officer of a group is itself a bar. BUT THE SAVING IS THE REASON TO STILL CALL THEM: the Board's own fact sheet states that ‘legal advice can be given in most areas — even the excluded areas’. The exclusions bite on legal aid (representation, s.27); legal advice (s.25) is any oral or written advice from a solicitor or barrister and includes writing a solicitor's letter and negotiations on your behalf. So a solicitor's letter and negotiation remain available in an excluded area — for many land disputes that is the intervention that matters. ASK FOR ADVICE EXPLICITLY: it is recorded that there is little focus in practice on the provision of legal advice, with no data in the Board's 2021 Annual Report on advice cases. THE MONEY: disposable income must be under €18,000, minimum contribution €10, and disposable capital over €100,000 makes you ineligible — though the value of a house is generally excluded, and disposable capital is counted for legal aid but NOT for legal advice. ASK ABOUT THE HARDSHIP DISCRETION: exceptionally the Board may grant aid without reference to means and waive the contribution where there would otherwise be undue hardship. Services run through Law Centres nationwide.

trackers.name: Office of the Information Commissioner (OIC)
trackers.desc: National right-to-information authority; Ireland’s Office of the Information Commissioner is the independent appeals body under the Freedom of Information Act 2014 — reviewing public-body FOI decisions (affirm, vary or annul) and publishing binding decisions, Ireland.

trackers.name: Community Law & Mediation — Centre for Environmental Justice
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an independent community law centre and charity (working since 1975) providing FREE legal advice, representation and mediation, which opened a dedicated Centre for Environmental Justice in 2021 — launched by Mary Robinson — staffed with an environmental justice lawyer. Runs a free legal advice clinic, publishes a guide to the Aarhus Convention, and produces template consultation responses communities can adapt. WHO IT SUITS: Irish communities impacted by social exclusion or disadvantage where an environmental harm falls hardest — that equality framing is the centre's explicit remit, so lead with who is being affected, not only with what is being built.

trackers.name: An Taisce — The National Trust for Ireland
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Ireland's oldest environmental NGO (provisional 1946, incorporated 1948), a statutory consultee in the Irish planning system that also brings judicial review against An Bord Pleanála — including the Edenderry Peat case (An Taisce v Bord na Móna [2020] IESC 39), which established that an EIA had to consider the impacts of extracting the plant's peat feedstock, and the Kilkenny Cheese challenge. Currently challenging, with Friends of the Irish Environment, the Planning and Development (Costs of Part 9 Judicial Review Proceedings) Regulations 2026 as breaching the Aarhus Convention and EU law. WHO IT SUITS: Irish planning and habitats challenges with national significance. NOTE: canonical domain not verified this session.

trackers.name: Friends of the Irish Environment (FIE)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an Irish environmental NGO that litigates in the superior courts — it brought Friends of the Irish Environment v Ireland [2020] IESC 49, 'Climate Case Ireland', in which the Supreme Court quashed the Government's national mitigation plan, and it litigates jointly with An Taisce on planning and access-to-justice matters. WHO IT SUITS: strategic challenges to State plans and policies rather than a single local application. USEFUL TO KNOW: under s.50A(3) of the Planning and Development Act 2000 as amended, an environmental organisation does NOT need to be incorporated or registered to bring a planning judicial review in Ireland, and after the Heather Hill judgment environmental litigants are generally liable only for their OWN costs — an unusually open door, though the 2026 costs regulations are narrowing it. NOTE: canonical domain not verified this session. An activist network founded to ensure European environmental law is properly implemented in Ireland — useful where a national body has approved something that EU law would not.

trackers.name: NPWS — about the National Parks and Wildlife Service
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the State agency for nature conservation, within the Heritage Division of the Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage. Its remit covers designation of Natural Heritage Areas, Special Areas of Conservation and Special Protection Areas under the Habitats and Birds Directives; licensing under the Wildlife Acts; peatland policy, turf compensation and relocation; land designation and land restoration; and management of State-owned National Parks and Nature Reserves. USE IT: to work out which designation, if any, already applies to a threatened site and who inside the Department holds that file — designation status changes what a developer must prove.

trackers.name: NPWS — useful links directory for Irish nature bodies
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the State conservation agency's own list of the organisations that matter for Irish nature — An Taisce (the National Trust for Ireland), Coillte (the State forestry company), BirdWatch Ireland, the Heritage Council, Bat Conservation Ireland, the Irish Whale and Dolphin Group, the National Biodiversity Data Centre and the Irish Ramsar Wetlands Committee. USE IT: a government-maintained starting point for finding the specialist body for your habitat or species, and a way to confirm an organisation is the real one rather than a soundalike.

trackers.name: Coillte Nature Trust — funded native woodland creation
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the Nature Trust raised over EUR 7 million from external funders to create 650 hectares of new native woodland in Ireland, and has transferred the established woodlands to An Taisce to hold and manage long term. WHO IT SUITS: restoration and native-woodland creation projects rather than defensive campaigns. HOW IT DIFFERS: it is a worked model of the corporate-funded creation plus NGO long-term stewardship split — useful as a template for structuring a similar deal, and as evidence that Coillte land can move into conservation hands.

trackers.name: Irish Wildlife Trust — find your county branch
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Ireland's nature conservation charity and lobbyist (since 1979), with branches that organise conservation activity IN THEIR COUNTY — Dublin, Cork, Galway, Kerry, Waterford, Cavan, Laois/Offaly and Longford/Westmeath among them. WHO IT SUITS: a community facing development who wants people locally rather than a Dublin office. BE REALISTIC: branch coverage is partial, and the IWT describes itself as a single nationwide organisation rather than a federation of independent county bodies — so a branch is a route to the national organisation, not a separate local charity with its own resources. It has a campaigning record on habitat protection, including opposing the 2017 Heritage Bill provisions extending hedge-cutting and scrub-burning into the bird breeding season.

trackers.name: BirdWatch Ireland — local branches
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Ireland's largest independent conservation organisation (est. 1968, over 15,000 members) with a network of more than 30 branches nationwide — the widest local conservation coverage in the country. It also manages nature reserves and works with the National Biodiversity Data Centre on wildlife monitoring. WHO IT SUITS: any Irish site where birds or their habitats are affected. THE PRACTICAL VALUE IS EVIDENCE: a branch with local recording history can supply documented species records for a threatened site, which carries far more weight in a planning objection than an assertion that birds use the land.

trackers.name: Irish Environmental Network — member directory
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the umbrella body for 34 of Ireland's national environmental NGOs, with a directory describing what each one does — An Taisce, BirdWatch Ireland, the Irish Wildlife Trust, Bat Conservation Ireland, CELT and others. USE IT: Ireland has no county-level conservation trusts, so finding the right national specialist is the equivalent step. Work down this list to find the organisation whose specific remit matches your site — bats, birds, water, woodland — because a specialist body carries more weight on its own subject than a general one.

trackers.name: The Rivers Trust — member trusts in Ireland
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the same 65-member network extends to the Republic of Ireland and Northern Ireland, and its Irish members are INDEPENDENT LOCAL CHARITIES, not branches of a national body — the Maigue Rivers Trust in County Limerick, for example, runs its own catchment programmes with National Biodiversity Action Plan and LAWPRO Community Water Development Fund money. USE IT: this is the exception to the general Irish pattern. Ireland has no county conservation trusts, but it does have catchment-based river trusts with their own funding and their own staff — so if your site is in a river catchment, there may be a genuinely local organisation after all. Check the member map before assuming there is nothing nearby.

trackers.name: Special Criminal Court
trackers.desc: Special Criminal Court — tribunal in Ireland.

trackers.name: data.gov.ie
trackers.desc: National — official government open data / budget portal. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this is the broad budget/open-data hub for how money is allocated overall — for the specific firms winning tenders use the procurement portal, and for findings of misspending use the supreme audit institution. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Ireland.

trackers.name: Register of Beneficial Owners (RBO)
trackers.desc: Register of Beneficial Owners (RBO) — Ireland’s beneficial-ownership register, disclosing the real individuals who ultimately own or control companies. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM A PLAIN COMPANY REGISTRY: this names the real HUMAN owners behind a company; a company registry names only the legal entity, its directors and filings. Use the registry first to find the entity, then this to pierce the shell to the people who profit. — Holds to account: the hidden owners behind firms dealing with Ireland’s government — find beneficial-owner filings.

trackers.name: Transparency International Ireland
trackers.desc: Ireland's chapter of Transparency International — leads the movement for public integrity in Ireland, runs the Transparency Legal Advice Centre providing free legal support to whistleblowers, and advocates on lobbying transparency, political finance and anti-corruption.

trackers.name: Office of the Comptroller and Auditor General
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Ireland, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Courts Service of Ireland
trackers.desc: Official portal for written judgments of the Irish superior courts. · Find here: written judgments of the Irish superior courts (Courts Service of Ireland).

trackers.name: Companies Registration Office
trackers.desc: Ireland's statutory company register and filings. — Holds to account: companies in Ireland — find the statutory company register of entities, directors and annual returns.

trackers.name: Central Statistics Office
trackers.desc: Ireland's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Ireland.

trackers.name: eTenders
trackers.desc: National public-procurement / budget-transparency portal. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this shows the specific firms winning specific tenders and contracts — for aggregate budget totals use the open-data/statistics portal, and for findings of waste use the audit body. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Ireland, and for how much.

trackers.name: Bréagchúirt Uí Dhálaigh
trackers.desc: Bréagchúirt Uí Dhálaigh — tribunal (Ireland).

trackers.name: Labour Court
trackers.desc: Labour Court — tribunal (Ireland).

trackers.name: Oireachtas Register of Members’ Interests
trackers.desc: Legislator / public-official financial interest & asset declarations.

trackers.name: SIPO – Standards in Public Office
trackers.desc: Ireland's body overseeing political donations, election spending and officials' interests.

trackers.name: Community Water Development Fund — pays for the surveys you need
trackers.desc: IT FUNDS EVIDENCE, WHICH IS THE SCARCE THING. Administered by LAWPRO for all 31 local authorities, this fund is open to all community and voluntary groups — and the guidelines expressly contemplate applications from unregistered voluntary groups, so lacking formal registration does not shut you out as it does with most funds. Grants ran EUR 1,000–25,000 per project in 2024. Fundable work includes feasibility studies, ecological surveys, habitat management plans and biodiversity action plans, as well as riparian planting, invasive species control and wetland enhancement. VOLUNTEER TIME COUNTS AS MATCH FUNDING at up to EUR 14 per hour on the Voluntary Labour Schedule — a group with people but no money can still meet a contribution requirement. A separate Small Grants and Events Scheme runs all year round for initiatives under EUR 5,000. SCALE AND COMPETITION: the scheme grew from EUR 180,000 in 2018 to EUR 1,047,000 in 2025, but LAWPRO records that applications exceed the budget and the standard is high.

trackers.name: CWDF guidelines — what sinks an application
trackers.desc: READ THIS BEFORE DRAFTING. ALL REQUIRED PERMISSIONS MUST BE SUBMITTED WITH THE APPLICATION — planning permission, Appropriate Assessments, Strategic Environmental Assessments, landowner consent and lease arrangements. LAWPRO requires evidence of consents and environmental assessments, such as appropriate assessment screening, before projects start, and Method Statements may be needed to scope consents from national bodies such as NPWS. You also need a Tax Reference Number and evidence of Tax Clearance or a Tax Clearance Access Number. PARTNERSHIP IS SCORED: projects with strong partnership arrangements and local involvement are rated higher, evidenced by letters of consent — so gather them early and show how you engage the wider community. Proposals must clearly define aims, objectives and actions, with physical works specified in detail. AND AFTERWARDS: a close working relationship with your local Community Water Officer is mandatory for physical-works projects, and any change of scope after approval must be notified to them in writing in advance.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: Costs protection in planning JR — after Heather Hill, all grounds are covered
trackers.desc: IN A COMMON-LAW JURISDICTION, COSTS EXPOSURE DECIDES WHETHER A CHALLENGE HAPPENS AT ALL — and this map's Legal Aid Board entry records that Irish civil legal aid excludes licensing, test cases, tribunal representation, and matters where you are one of a group with the same interest. So the costs rule is the operative protection here, not a supplement to legal aid. Two instruments implement Aarhus article 9(4)'s ‘not prohibitively expensive’ requirement: section 50B of the Planning and Development Act 2000 (as amended 2011), and Part 2 of the Environment (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2011, whose section 7 expressly provides for pre-emptive costs orders. FIRST ESTABLISH WHICH DIRECTIVE THE CONSENT IMPLEMENTS, because it decides whether protection exists at all: the public-participation provisions of the EIA Directive, the Strategic Environmental Assessment Directive, the Industrial Emissions Directive, or articles 6(3) and 6(4) of the Habitats Directive. HEATHER HILL IS WHY THIS ENTRY EXISTS: in Heather Hill Management Company CLG v An Bord Pleanála, the Court of Appeal ([2021] IECA 259) had narrowed protection to environmental grounds only — but on 10 November 2022 a five-judge Supreme Court allowed the appeal and held that ALL grounds in proceedings challenging such consents benefit from costs protection, finding no justification for dividing the costs where some grounds engage the directives and others do not. THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE IS LARGE: you do not have to strip out your non-environmental grounds to keep costs protection. Under the earlier approach, mixing a habitats point with an ordinary ultra vires point risked losing protection on the latter. Plead the case you actually have. The Court also recorded that section 50B goes further than EU law requires under Case C-470/16 North East Pylon. ASK FOR IT BY NAME: a protective costs order, claimed in the statement of grounds — an order obtained in advance of trial that you cannot be liable for the respondent's or notice party's costs if you lose. An order before trial is the whole value: certainty at the moment you decide whether to litigate. AND MIND THE NOTICE PARTY — in planning JR the developer is usually joined as one, and their costs are the larger exposure. Ordinary costs run under Order 99 and section 169 of the Legal Services Regulation Act 2015.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status. AND IRELAND IS THE PROOF THAT ORDINARY PEOPLE USE IT: since Ireland became subject to the mechanism in December 2013, nine non-compliance cases were accepted (two ruled inadmissible) and ALL were initiated by communications from the public. Findings in three were endorsed at the seventh Meeting of the Parties in October 2021 under Decision VII/8i — the first time Ireland had non-compliance findings at a MOP. Nine cases, every one started by a member of the public, three ending in findings endorsed by the Parties.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Native Woodland Trust, Hometree and IWT — three ways to get Irish land held
trackers.desc: AN ORGANISATION THAT BOUGHT TWO SITES IN ONE YEAR IS AN ACTIVE BUYER, NOT AN ASPIRATIONAL ONE — and that is the difference between a body worth approaching and one that will thank you politely. The Native Woodland Trust publishes dated acquisitions: Coill Sheanadh Gharráin in the Connemara Gaeltacht, April 2025, and an as-yet unnamed site in the Slieve Aughty region of South Galway, December 2025. It has grown from a single small woodland reserve to over a dozen woodlands, four nurseries and a permanent HQ, run by a voluntary board of trustees with a small core staff and volunteers in local areas. IT IS REGISTERED AS ‘IRISH WOODLAND TRUST’ AND TRADES AS ‘NATIVE WOODLAND TRUST’ — worth knowing when you search a register or draft a conveyance. AND IF THE FEAR IS THAT PROTECTION MEANS LOSING ACCESS, ITS OWN PRINCIPLES SAY OTHERWISE: ‘all woodlands shall be open to the public and shall be held for the enjoyment of the general public, subject to issues of safety and conservation’. SECOND BUYER — HOMETREE, AND IT HOLDS IN PERPETUITY: working with expert ecologists, it purchases and rehabilitates strategically significant pieces of land, expressly including degraded peatland for rewetting, monoculture commercial woodland for conversion, and abandoned sites — exactly the land a developer treats as low-value is an acquisition priority for someone else. Its terms: the sites will be owned by the trust which governs the charity and held IN PERPETUITY for the benefit of all in society. It runs a conservation subscription — a recurring revenue model, which is what lets a small trust commit to a purchase. THIRD — AND THIS ONE SUITS AN OWNER WHO WILL NOT SELL: the Irish Wildlife Trust's reserves are ‘a mixture of privately owned land managed for wildlife in conjunction with the IWT as well as land owned by the IWT itself’ — the owner keeps the title and the IWT manages for wildlife. Where a sympathetic owner cannot or will not sell, that is the arrangement to propose.

trackers.name: Irish Peatland Conservation Council — buys bogs (Ireland)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a registered Irish charity (CHY6829) and NGO that buys peatland and holds it. Six reserves — Lodge Bog and Lullymore West Bog in Kildare, Scragh Bog in Westmeath, Girley Bog in Meath, Ketts Lough in Clare and Fenor Bog in Waterford — run from the Bog of Allen Nature Centre, which is where to write: Lullymore, Rathangan, Co. Kildare R51 V293, bogs@ipcc.ie, +353-45-860133. USE IT: three purchase routes it has actually used, not three it offers. Fenor Bog was bought by selling symbolic share certificates — no single donor, a whole constituency holding a certificate each. Girley Bog, 8.5 hectares, was bought in 2014 on the back of two years of appeals, with Meath County Council, the National Parks and Wildlife Service, the Native Woodland Trust and Coillte among the bodies around the table; IPCC describes it as community-led conservation and means it. And the standing sponsor-an-acre scheme sells an acre or part of one with a commemorative certificate, which keeps a campaign alive between purchases. THE ROUTE NOBODY THINKS OF: since 1983 IPCC has bought Irish peatland together with Dutch conservationists, and Dutch individuals started buying Irish bogs in 1987 — because the Netherlands had already cut away every one of its own. A country that has destroyed the habitat you still have is a funding constituency, and it does not need a government to act first. THE SCALE TO EXPECT: about a hundred volunteers at any one time and two thousand supporting friends, with core funding channelled through the Irish Environmental Network. Purchases are measured in single-figure hectares. Bring it a bog, not a landscape.

trackers.name: National Biodiversity Data Centre — Biodiversity Maps, and it will help you identify a species
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Centre exists to make biodiversity data and information more freely available in order to better understand and assist the protection of Ireland's biodiversity. Beechfield House, Carriganore, SETU West Campus, Waterford; +353 51 306240; info@biodiversityireland.ie. Ireland's bucket held An Taisce, FIE, a legal aid board and branch directories, but nothing holding the record. WHAT TO SEARCH: Biodiversity Maps at maps.biodiversityireland.ie, Ireland's biodiversity data and mapping portal, integrating terrestrial and marine data as a portal for the geographic presentation of observational data. Alongside it: national biodiversity indicators, invasive species tracking, the National Vegetation Database and the all-Ireland Biodiversity Monitoring Programme. AND THE DIVISION OF LABOUR TO UNDERSTAND, because it decides who to ask: the Centre's emphasis is tracking change in the wider countryside, to complement the work of the National Parks and Wildlife Service on tracking change in Ireland's protected species. So for a rare or protected species the record may sit with NPWS, which primarily collects records of species on the Checklist of protected and threatened species in Ireland — and some of that data is treated as sensitive, obtainable only by submitting a data request form. Two custodians, two routes. THE HELP OFFERED TO A BEGINNER, which is unusually explicit: it says if you are not sure or have no idea what species you are looking at, you can always ask for assistance with the identification; its Citizen Science Portal has dedicated recording forms for the major taxonomic groups plus an 'Other Species' form for anything else; and the Biodiversity Data Capture App or the web portal will give you the spatial reference from a map or your phone's GPS. It also sells identification swatches and guides. Its own instruction is to be certain of identification before entry, and to seek help rather than guess.
