HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Poland.

trackers.name: Najwyższa Izba Kontroli (NIK)
trackers.desc: Poland's supreme audit office — independent audit of the government's economy, public spending and administration. — Holds to account: the Polish government — find audits of state spending and the annual analysis of budget execution.

trackers.name: Sejm Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej
trackers.desc: Official Polish Sejm (lower house) website with legislative documentation, voting records, and comprehensive parliamentary archives. — Holds to account: top officials & cabinet — find their assets, interests and integrity declarations.

trackers.name: WFOŚiGW — your statute wording is the eligibility gate
trackers.desc: APPLY REGIONALLY, NOT NATIONALLY. NFOŚiGW is central and has no regional branches; the 16 voivodeship funds (WFOŚiGW) are where a local association realistically applies. THE CLAUSE THAT DECIDES ELIGIBILITY: the offer is addressed to bodies with a provision in their statute and/or KRS entry stating that the organisation's purpose is environmental protection and/or ecological education. Your constitution is the gate — amend it before there is a dispute, as in Finland and Italy. TERMS: grants and loans with preferential interest, the possibility of partial write-off of loan capital, and no fees or commissions; a dotacjo-pożyczka can top a grant up to 100 percent of net eligible costs. A recorded window ran grants 1 February to 29 March, loans to 31 December or until funds ran out. FUNDABLE WORK includes preparing protection plans for areas protected under the 2004 Nature Conservation Act, and removal of invasive alien species.

trackers.name: Gdańsk WFOŚiGW rules — continuous intake, and two exclusions
trackers.desc: BETTER TERMS THAN MOST OF THIS MAP, IF YOU AVOID TWO TRAPS. The Gdańsk fund receives applications continuously and considers them at least once a quarter — no single annual window — and funding may reach 100 percent of eligible costs for ecological education and nature protection tasks, and in special cases for public finance bodies and NGOs. THE TWO EXCLUSIONS: it does not finance completed tasks, so do not start the work first; and it does not fund tasks that have already received foreign funding, including EU funds, so do not plan to stack it on an EU grant. NATIONAL CALLS ADMIT NGOs TOO: an Eastern Poland biodiversity call ran 13 November to 29 February with a budget of PLN 12.5 million, open to NGOs, local government, forest and water managers and education bodies — while a PLN 110 million call for national park education infrastructure was non-competitive because only 9 parks could apply. Some support is aimed explicitly at social dialogue and resolving conflicts over nature protection.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Justice & Environment — a public-interest environmental lawyer in your country
trackers.desc: A LAWYER YOU CAN ACTUALLY GET, IN YOUR COUNTRY, WHO ALREADY DOES THIS WORK. J&E members ‘often serve as environmental law service points in their countries, handling cases’, and its lawyers are seasoned environmental law experts, experienced within their national legal systems, familiar with the challenges faced by their communities and well aware of the EU legal framework — the combination that lets a local case be argued on EU grounds. ITS THREE PRIORITY ISSUES ARE EXACTLY WHAT A LAND CASE TURNS ON: the Aarhus Convention, environmental impact assessment, and Natura 2000. THE THING TO ASK FOR BY NAME: the ATOJ-EARL project, led by ClientEarth and coordinated by J&E with EU LIFE support, produced a public-interest lawyer database regrouping lawyers active in environmental law — precisely what a community searching for an attorney needs — covering Austria, Estonia, France, Germany, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia and Spain. AND GIVE YOUR LAWYER THIS GUIDE: ClientEarth's ‘Access to Justice in European Union Law’ is, in its own description, the only document that captures both the case law of the EU courts and the findings of the Aarhus Convention Compliance Committee — which this map records separately. ClientEarth litigates itself too: Spanish authorities lost an appeal against its landmark case on industrial livestock harm. Poor implementation of EU environmental law is estimated to cost €55 billion a year. ON MEMBERSHIP: J&E publishes its member countries — Austria, Bulgaria, Czechia, Croatia, Estonia, Germany, Greece, Hungary, North Macedonia, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain and Ukraine — though one published list gives 14 members including Belgium and omitting Ukraine, and another gives 15 including Ukraine. Check the current membership.

trackers.name: Fundacja Frank Bold — takes your case to its legal team (Poland)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a public-interest legal foundation in Kraków, ul. Skłodowskiej-Curie 4/3, which asks you to submit a specific case to its legal team through a form on its site. Its published record is about stopping mines, and the numbers are concrete. Its arguments helped persuade the General Directorate for Environmental Protection to refuse the environmental decision for the planned Złoczów lignite mine, which it records as sparing 33 villages and 3,000 residents from displacement. Working with residents and councillors of the Gubin and Brody communes it helped bring the investor to abandon a lignite mine there. It supported local farmers facing an opencast lignite mine, and residents of Imielin. It was among the organisations that challenged the environmental decision for the Turów mine, where the court suspended that decision pending a full hearing. IT ALSO RUNS AN ADVICE LINE: it opened a free legal advice service aimed specifically at informal local groups, activists and NGOs facing harmful industrial air pollution, with a short verification form as the way in. If your fight is with an existing plant rather than a proposed one, that is the door. WHAT TO BRING: it works at the scale of environmental decisions, concessions and industrial permits. A single house extension is not its case; a mine, a plant or a road is.

trackers.name: Kancelaria Radców Prawnych Frank Bold — the fee-charging firm, and its conflict (Poland)
trackers.desc: WHO TO CALL: the associated law firm, a team of legal advisers specialising in environmental protection and corporate responsibility. Its own list of services is unusually precise about what it will do for a resident: represent people exposed to the harmful effects of neighbouring investments, in administrative proceedings and in civil claims for nuisance; help local communities take part in environmental proceedings for schemes planned next to them; help NGOs join administrative proceedings; prepare legal analyses and opinions; and in criminal matters draft notifications of an offence, draft indictments, and represent private, subsidiary and auxiliary prosecutors. It states plainly that it does not act as defence counsel. READ THIS BEFORE YOU WRITE: the same firm advises individuals, companies and local authorities on planning and delivering renewable energy investments — checking a scheme against the local spatial plan, supporting investors in administrative proceedings, and drafting the lease agreements, transmission easements and connection contracts behind them. That is on its own services page. If you are fighting a wind or solar scheme, name the developer, the site and the consenting authority in your first email and ask directly whether the firm is free to act for you. WHICH ONE DO YOU NEED: the foundation takes public-interest cases; this is the commercial practice. Ask the foundation first, and let it tell you which of the two your case belongs to.

trackers.name: Fundusz Partnerstwa — Polish Environmental Partnership Foundation
trackers.desc: WHAT THE CONSORTIUM IS: the Environmental Partnership Association, headquartered in Brno, is a consortium of six independent national foundations in central and eastern Europe that give grants to community projects protecting the environment. It grew out of a programme begun in 1990 by the C.S. Mott Foundation, the German Marshall Fund and the Rockefeller Brothers Fund, and the national foundations were established as independent bodies in the early 1990s. Alongside grants they run education programmes, provide professional services and build the capacity of civic initiatives — which is the part a new local group needs most. THE POLISH MEMBER: Fundusz Partnerstwa, the Polish foundation of the consortium, founded 2004 and the youngest of the six, at ffp.org.pl. Poland already has a land buyer and a legal ally in this file; this is the missing funder. SOURCING: the consortium and its six national foundations are documented on the Environmental Partnership Association's own site; the national figures and founding dates come from consortium and partner material rather than each foundation's own pages. Confirm current grant rounds with the national foundation directly.

trackers.name: OTOP — buys and leases land, and fights the road (Poland)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the Polish Society for the Protection of Birds, founded 1991, a public-benefit association and BirdLife's Polish partner, now past 2,500 members. Its own statement of method is the point: to protect birds and their habitats it buys and leases land and runs reserve management on it. It manages seven reserves — Karsiborska Kępa in the Świna delta, Beka on the Puck Bay, the Krajnik and Bolesławice aquatic warbler sites, and Mścichy, Ławki-Szorce and Laskowiec-Zajki in the buffer zone of Biebrza National Park. Karsiborska Kępa was its first and is an active-management social reserve rather than a closed strict one. WHAT IT BRINGS TO A CASE. It coordinates the Monitoring of Polish Birds programme commissioned by the Chief Inspectorate of Environmental Protection — so the national bird dataset runs through it. Its stated objectives include collecting data documenting the state of and threats to the national avifauna, drawing up and implementing conservation action plans, any legal action favourable to the protection of birds and their habitats, lobbying for protective legal provisions and for the enforcement of provisions that already exist, and encouraging local action by establishing and supporting local groups. That last one is the offer to a new committee. ITS RECORD ON INFRASTRUCTURE: one of its activists co-organised the campaign defending the Rospuda valley against the Via Baltica expressway and won the Goldman Environmental Prize in 2010. Its current campaign tags include opposition to the E40 waterway and river protection work. This is an organisation with a proven record of stopping a road through a wetland. HOW TO WORK WITH IT: it recruits volunteers whose tasks it describes as requiring specialist knowledge of ornithology, law or ecology as well as general help, and it runs monitoring training. Bring it a site, ask what the monitoring data shows, and ask about forming a local group.

trackers.name: Article 44 UOOŚ — 12 months of statutory activity, and you join as a party
trackers.desc: THE SHORTEST QUALIFYING PERIOD IN THIS FILE: under article 44 of the 2008 law on access to environmental information, ecological organisations which, invoking their statutory aims, notify their wish to participate in a given procedure requiring public participation, take part in it ON THE RIGHTS OF A PARTY, if they have conducted statutory activity in environmental or nature protection for a minimum of 12 months before the day the procedure was initiated. Article 31 para 4 of the administrative procedure code does not apply. Spain requires two years, France three, Italy five regions. Poland requires twelve months. AND THE ADMISSION IS AUTOMATIC: courts have held that admitting an ecological organisation to participate on the rights of a party in an environmental-conditions decision does not require a ruling — it is enough for the organisation to invoke its statutory aims, and the authority has no obligation to examine whether it has a legal interest. A ruling is issued only to REFUSE admission, and only the ecological organisation may appeal that refusal — the applicant and other parties cannot challenge your admission. YOU CAN ALSO ARRIVE LATE: an ecological organisation has the right to appeal a decision issued in a procedure requiring public participation, where justified by its statutory aims, EVEN IF IT DID NOT TAKE PART in the first-instance procedure — and lodging the appeal counts as notifying the wish to participate. It then participates in the appeal on the rights of a party, and the same applies to a complaint to the administrative court. Missing the first round is not fatal in Poland, which is the opposite of most jurisdictions in this file. THE ONE THING TO GET RIGHT, from Polish practitioner guidance: the statutory aims must be defined as precisely as possible, so that it can be established that they are closely connected with the subject matter of the case. If there is no connection between the statutory aims and the subject, the organisation will not be admitted. Write the statute to name the things you will actually be defending.

trackers.name: WFOŚiGW — a provincial environmental fund in every voivodeship, taking NGO applications
trackers.desc: THE STRUCTURE: Poland has the Narodowy Fundusz Ochrony Środowiska i Gospodarki Wodnej (NFOŚiGW), ul. Pańska 97, 00-834 Warszawa — and beneath it a wojewódzki fundusz in every voivodeship, each with its own board, its own calls and its own beneficiary portal. The page above lists them so you can pick the one for your territory. This is money administered close to home rather than from the capital. AND NGOs ARE NAMED AS ELIGIBLE: one fund's rules state that grants may also be given for purposes beyond its standard list where the task is co-financed under competitions or calls, or is carried out by public finance sector bodies or by NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS. THE PROGRAMMES THAT FIT A LAND CASE, from actual published calls: 'Zadania z zakresu ochrony przyrody' — tasks in the field of nature protection, as grants, with applications taken until the allocation is exhausted; and 'Ochrona różnorodności biologicznej i funkcji ekosystemów' — protection of biological diversity and ecosystem functions, one regional round of which carried 1,200,000 zł, made up of 100,000 zł from the provincial fund and 1,100,000 zł from the national fund. Each fund publishes a Lista przedsięwzięć priorytetowych — a list of priority undertakings — and applications must match it. TWO PRACTICAL POINTS: at least one fund takes applications on a continuous basis, considered as they arrive and at least once a quarter, rather than in a single annual window — so there may be no deadline to miss. And applications are submitted through the fund's beneficiary portal or the ePUAP platform, not on paper. SCALE, FOR CONTEXT: the national fund planned to spend over 15.8 billion zł on environmental projects in one year, of which more than 11.7 billion in grants, and it separately finances Poland's national parks to extend the areas over which they protect local ecosystems.

trackers.name: PDWD and bazaoos — every authority from minister to wójt must publish its environmental documents
trackers.desc: THE OBLIGATION, AND IT REACHES YOUR OWN VILLAGE: under the Prawo ochrony środowiska and the 2008 access-to-information act, public authorities must keep a publicznie dostępny wykaz danych (PDWD) — a publicly available register of documents containing information on the environment — in electronic form, made available to the public over the internet. The duty runs from the Minister, through Voivodes and Marshals of Voivodeships and Starosts of Poviats, down to Wójts, Burmistrzs and City Presidents: at every level of public administration where decisions concerning the environment are taken, a register must be kept. Since December 2006 the register must be published on the authority's own BIP page. WHERE TO LOOK, AND A LIVE CHANGE TO NOTE: registers are available at ekoportal.gov.pl and at the General Director for Environmental Protection's bazaoos.gdos.gov.pl. At the end of June 2025 the climate and environment ministry withdrew its central 'Wykaz' application, and municipalities have moved to their own systems — one has switched to a commercial module, another to its own BIP page. If the national portal has nothing for your commune, go to the commune's own BIP. WHAT THE CARDS COVER: karty informacyjne describe concessions, permits and administrative decisions, alongside reports implementing environmental law, analyses, plans, programmes and agreements affecting the environment, emissions and pollution affecting or capable of affecting the environment, and the state of health, safety and living conditions of people connected with the state of the environment. WHAT A RESIDENT ACTUALLY DOES WITH IT: search the karty informacyjne for decyzje środowiskowe — environmental decisions — to find out whether installations that may affect the environment are planned near you, before they are built. A Polish guide puts it plainly: quick social intervention can block or halt a harmful investment. AND FOR THE OFFICIALS' SIDE: the ministry has published guidance on preparing the cards, with a descriptive part and a table naming each document type and the authority responsible for publishing it — useful if an authority claims a document need not be listed.

trackers.name: Obszary chronione prywatnie — four organisations, one brand's money, 148 hectares
trackers.desc: THE MODEL, AND WHY IT EXISTS: Poland's highest forms of nature protection are national parks — 1 per cent of the country — and reserves, 0.5 per cent. There is far more land of significant natural value that needs protection, but the existing law does not favour creating new protected areas, so following the international example NGOs, private individuals and even private firms are taking matters into their own hands and BUYING LAND ON WHICH THEY CREATE PRIVATE RESERVES. Such areas complement the network of official state protected areas, provide ecological connectivity, and are staging posts between habitats for many species. WHO IS DOING IT AND WITH WHOSE MONEY: WWF Polska with nature partners from Klub Przyrodników, Alauda and OTOP, funded by a consumer brand — together they have already brought more than 148 hectares under protection, the first parcel bought in one river valley and the next in another. A consumer brand paying for private reserves, with four conservation organisations doing the work, is a funding route most campaigns never consider. AND HOW THE POLISH BUYERS ACTUALLY OPERATE, from the partner that has done it longest: it has bought xerothermic grasslands and peatlands scattered across the whole country, held just over 130 hectares by 2020, and reports that previously purchased areas were, ON ITS OWN APPLICATION, placed under reserve protection. Buy first, then apply for the reserve. Its own fundraiser raised about 62,000 złoty in three years, and one purchase required the consent of the state agricultural land agency.

trackers.name: Wieczne Lasy — 40 złoty buys 11 square metres, and the forest plants itself
trackers.desc: THE PITCH, WHICH IS THE CLEAREST SMALL-DONATION MODEL IN THIS FILE: you do not need to plant trees or a forest. It is enough to give back to nature scraps of meadow, field and wetland. The forest will arrange itself — provided you help us buy the land where the Eternal Forest will grow. The foundation undertakes to care for that forest and not allow tree felling on such ground, so that the trees live out their years, giving life to the next generations of forest. Your 40 złoty creates 11 square metres of Eternal Forest. WHY IT WORKS AS AN ARGUMENT: only 1 per cent of Poland's area is national park, and in the Carpathians forest the size of five football pitches is destroyed every hour. WHO THEY ARE: an expert organisation bringing together naturalists and foresters working for the natural heritage of Poland and the Polish-Ukrainian-Slovak borderland, whose successes include finding thousands of localities of protected and old-growth indicator species, and several dozen species new to the country or considered extinct there. AND ITS OWN STATEMENT OF METHOD, worth quoting to any funder: a huge role is played today not only by creating protection zones but by GIVING SPACE BACK TO NATURE. The latter we can provide by buying land which we return to nature. We do not intend to plant trees, but let natural processes arrange the forest.

trackers.name: Polish odwołanie practitioners — 14 days, and the ecological organisation needs 12 months' standing
trackers.desc: WHO CAN APPEAL AN ENVIRONMENTAL DECISION, from a practitioners' account, and it is the first thing a Polish community needs to know: the right belongs to PARTIES to the proceedings — usually the investor and OWNERS OF PROPERTIES WITHIN THE RANGE OF THE INVESTMENT'S IMPACT. A conventional boundary of 100 METRES from the plot is often assumed, but in reality the range is frequently greater; it all depends on the scale of the undertaking. AND THE ROUTE FOR EVERYONE ELSE: ECOLOGICAL ORGANISATIONS play a special role — they may lodge an appeal IF THEY HAVE BEEN ACTING FOR ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION FOR AT LEAST 12 MONTHS. Twelve months of existence is the price of standing in Poland, which is an argument for founding the association before the fight rather than during it. THE CLOCK: you have 14 DAYS from delivery of the decision; where it was announced by public notice, the period runs from the day 14 days after the public announcement — so in practice 28 days from posting, BUT IT IS BETTER TO ACT SOONER. AND WHAT AN APPEAL MUST ACTUALLY CONTAIN, which is less than people fear: at the very start you do not have to cite specific paragraphs. It is enough that you indicate your LEGAL INTEREST and describe why the decision is defective or unfavourable to you. Its closing advice: the key to success is not emotion but cold calculation, hard evidence and timeliness — and it notes the practical trap that improving a road for cars can paradoxically worsen the situation for all residents.

trackers.name: Polish environmental-law kancelarie — and the one that handles flooded plots and smog damages
trackers.desc: WHAT THESE PRACTICES LIST, and the range is wider than a community expects: environmental protection law, NATURE PROTECTION LAW and water law; water permits; DECYZJA ŚRODOWISKOWA; illegal waste storage; international waste transport and importing waste from abroad; REMEDIATION; COMPENSATION FOR SMOG; and FLOODING OF A PLOT. Compensation for smog and for a flooded plot are named services in Poland — two harms that neighbours of a development commonly suffer and rarely think to claim for. Poland had 23 filed entries and no lawyer at all. AND WHAT ANOTHER WARSAW PRACTICE CONFIRMS ABOUT THE ROUTE: an appeal lies from an environmental decision to the higher-instance body, and thereafter A COMPLAINT TO THE ADMINISTRATIVE COURT — it is essential to keep the statutory deadlines; the documents that matter in such a case are applications, ENVIRONMENTAL REPORTS, administrative decisions, technical documentation AND EXPERT OPINIONS; and an advocate can help with analysis of environmental obligations, representation before administrative bodies, and court proceedings. A CAUTION RECORDED PLAINLY: most Polish environmental practices advertise to companies and institutions — several state it outright, offering environmental audits and ongoing retainers to businesses. Ask directly whether they will act against an investor before instructing.

trackers.name: The Polish private-reserve list — SIX named organisations that already own or lease refuges
trackers.desc: THE LIST, AND IT IS THE MOST USEFUL SINGLE ARTEFACT FOR A POLISH LANDOWNER: the model of protecting valuable areas BY BUYING AND LEASING THEM through nature organisations, which then carry out the necessary protective actions, has taken hold in Poland too. At present, after several years of activity, refuges protected precisely BY THE RIGHT OF OWNERSHIP OR BY THE PROVISIONS OF A LAND LEASE AGREEMENT are held by: a north-Podlasie bird protection society, a nature protection society, a regional naturalists' club, a friends-of-nature society, THE NATIONWIDE BIRD PROTECTION SOCIETY, AND A EUROPEAN UNION FOR COAST PROTECTION. Poland had 25 filed entries. Six organisations that already hold land by ownership or lease is six bodies a threatened owner can offer a parcel to — and lease matters as much as purchase, because an owner who will not sell can still put the land beyond reach. AND THE ASSESSMENT THAT COMES WITH IT: nature protection carried out almost exclusively by social organisations, among other things through the creation of private reserves, IS ALSO A METHOD — and in most cases, as it turns out, THE MOST EFFECTIVE. The guide also records that the areas most valuable for birds on a national scale are covered by INFORMAL PROTECTION, with the involvement of the society's members — and it asks directly whether a refuge can be entirely private, mine and mine alone.

trackers.name: The Polish bird-organisation address list — five national bodies, with streets and towns
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a published list of the most important nationwide protection organisations dealing with birds, each with a STREET ADDRESS, POSTAL CODE, TOWN AND WEBSITE — the nationwide bird society in Warsaw, a nature protection society in a named city, the naturalists' club in a named town, a friends-of-nature society in a fourth city, and a further nature society. Five national organisations with street addresses on one page is the contact sheet behind the private-reserve list, and it notes that the addresses of some REGIONAL organisations can also be found in the chapter on regional ornithological centres. AND ITS OWN APPEAL, which is the reason it exists: we warmly encourage everyone to make contact with one of them. It describes joining a social organisation as an extremely useful form, ACCESSIBLE TO EVERYONE, and states the case plainly: economic development, modernisation of the country, new investments and so on, although on the one hand undoubtedly making our lives easier, on the other often — IF CARRIED OUT IN AN UNCONSIDERED WAY — produce dramatic consequences for wild species of plants and animals. The harms it names are the ones this file keeps meeting: excessive felling and the liquidation of OLD STANDS, the regulation of rivers and streams, THE DRAINING OF WETLANDS, or the conversion of marshes into reservoirs.

trackers.name: Klub Przyrodników's land holdings — nearly 300 ha, and the SPOŁECZNE REZERWATY it creates
trackers.desc: WHAT IT HAS ASSEMBLED, and how: thanks to funds from projects AND FROM OUR OWN COMMERCIAL ACTIVITY, we have managed to gather ALMOST 300 HECTARES of land, OWNED OR LEASED. Among them PEATLANDS, dry grasslands, SEMI-NATURAL FRESH MEADOWS, purple moor-grass meadows and extensive meadows. A conservation body funding land purchase out of its own trading income is a model a local association can copy — the same shape recorded in Portugal, where a fixed share of sales feeds a purchase fund. WHAT IT DOES WITH THE LAND: all these areas are intended EXCLUSIVELY for nature conservation purposes, and WITHOUT OUR INTERVENTION THEY WOULD MOST PROBABLY HAVE LOST THEIR VALUABLE CHARACTER LONG AGO. It works across the whole of Poland, carrying out inventories, drawing up protection plans for reserves, landscape parks and Natura 2000 areas, AND CREATING SOCIAL RESERVES (społeczne rezerwaty). A 'social reserve' is a reserve a civil organisation declares on ground it holds itself, without waiting for the state. AND THE STANDARD IT SETS ITSELF: every day on which we fail to protect another hectare of naturally valuable land we consider lost.

trackers.name: The NFOŚiGW land-buyout programme — national parks paid to buy PRIVATE land inside their borders
trackers.desc: THE MONEY AND WHAT IT BUYS: the national environmental fund's priority programme PROTECTION AND RESTORATION OF BIOLOGICAL AND LANDSCAPE DIVERSITY, PART 1: PROTECTION OF AREAS AND SPECIES OF NATURAL VALUE, funds national parks TO BUY OUT PRIVATE LAND WITHIN THEIR OWN BOUNDARIES. One park received over 640,000 złOTY to buy parcels inside two named Natura 2000 sites, on land holding 17 VALUABLE BIRD SPECIES and named peatland and bog-forest habitats with habitat codes. AND WHY THE PARK WANTED IT, in the director's own words — which is the plainest statement of anti-sprawl purpose in this file: the surrounding built-up area is BUDDING, and we want to SLOW OR LIMIT THAT PROCESS in places of natural importance. Of course, not everywhere. We are aware that villages must exist and people must function normally in them, BUT THERE ARE ZONES IN WHICH BUILDING WOULD BE INADVISABLE, because it could harm nature or the landscape. The park has 2,500 HECTARES OF PRIVATE LAND within its boundaries, and the grant lets it increase what it directly controls. AND THE REASSURANCE THE FUND ITSELF PRINTS, which matters when neighbours hear about it: the land buy-outs DO NOT HAVE THE CHARACTER OF EXPROPRIATION — they will take place AT MARKET PRICES.

trackers.name: Poland's PRIVATE RESERVES — the bodies that buy land and protect it without waiting for the state
trackers.desc: WHY POLISH COMMUNITIES BUY RATHER THAN PETITION, and the arithmetic behind it: the fullest forms of nature protection in Poland are NATIONAL PARKS (1 PER CENT of the country's area) and RESERVES (0.5 PER CENT). BUT THERE IS FAR MORE LAND OF NATURAL VALUE THAT NEEDS PROTECTION. That is why, more and more often, NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS, PRIVATE PERSONS AND EVEN PRIVATE FIRMS ARE TAKING MATTERS INTO THEIR OWN HANDS. THEY GATHER FUNDS AND BUY UP LAND, ON WHICH THEY CREATE PRIVATE RESERVES. One and a half per cent of the country has the strongest protection, so buying the ground is the route for everything else — and the article names the bodies that have already done it. AND THE WORKED EXAMPLES A COMMUNITY CAN CITE: the POLISH SOCIETY FOR NATURE PROTECTION SALAMANDRA BOUGHT, BACK IN THE 1990s, ONE OF THE POZNAN FORTS, which is an important WINTERING SITE FOR BATS; reserves were created ON THE INITIATIVE OF THE OWNERS THEMSELVES, including two named ones established in 2004 and 2011; and the SOCIAL RESERVE KARSIBORSKA KEPA was placed under protection in 1993 BY THE POLISH SOCIETY FOR THE PROTECTION OF BIRDS, on an island together with the adjoining islets. A disused fort, a fish-pond complex and an island have all been protected this way — the category of site is wider than most groups assume.

trackers.name: The micro-reserve programme — a protected zone around a nest for ABOUT 1,000 ZLOTY
trackers.desc: THE CHEAPEST PROTECTION RECORDED ANYWHERE IN THIS FILE: a Polish foundation IS RUNNING A COLLECTION TO CREATE SMALL RESERVES AROUND THE NESTS OF RARE BIRDS. EACH SUCH ZONE PROTECTS NOT ONLY THE HABITAT, BUT ALSO THE TREES AROUND IT — and THE COST OF EACH OF THEM IS ABOUT 1,000 ZLOTY. Poland is the smallest bucket in this file. A thousand zloty buys a legally protected zone around a nest, and the trees with it — which puts protection inside the reach of a village collection, not a foundation budget. AND THE SCALE ALREADY ACHIEVED, which shows it is a working route rather than a pilot: UNTIL NOW IT HAS BEEN POSSIBLE TO CREATE 144 SUCH PLACES, and THE FOUNDATION PLANS ANOTHER 30. AND HOW THE SITES ARE FOUND, which is the part a community can supply: OUR FIELD WORKERS AND THE EXPERTS WITH WHOM WE COOPERATE SEARCH OUT ZONE SPECIES IN THE WILDEST CORNER OF POLAND, a named forest. The protection follows the species record, so finding and reporting the nest is what starts it — local knowledge is the input, and the foundation supplies the rest.

trackers.name: Fundacja Dzika Polska — the road was built, but ON A VARIANT AVOIDING the peatlands
trackers.desc: A DOCUMENTED OUTCOME OF THE KIND A COMMUNITY IS ACTUALLY FIGHTING FOR — not cancellation, but relocation: the foundation joined THE CAMPAIGN FOR THE PROTECTION OF THE MARSHES OF A NAMED VALLEY AGAINST A PLANNED EXPRESS ROAD. THE CASE BECAME THE LOUDEST NATURE-PROTECTION CAMPAIGN OF RECENT DECADES, and FINALLY THE CAMPAIGN ENDED IN SUCCESS — THE EXPRESS ROAD WAS BUILT, BUT IN A VARIANT AVOIDING THE VALUABLE PEATLANDS. Moving the route is a win, and it is the one most reachable — a community that cannot stop a road entirely can still shift it off the ground that matters. AND WHAT THE FOUNDATION PUT IN, which tells a local group what to ask a national body for: it SUPPLIED SIGNIFICANT FINANCIAL, EQUIPMENT AND PERSONNEL SUPPORT DURING THE ORGANISED PROTEST OF ACTIVISTS. AND ITS STANDING WORK, which is available before any protest is needed: PASSING ON COMMENTS ABOUT COMPLIANCE WITH THE FSC STANDARD DURING AUDITS; CONSULTATION ON FOREST MANAGEMENT PLANS AND ON NATURA 2000 PROTECTION-TASK PLANS; INVENTORIES OF PROTECTED SPECIES CONNECTED WITH NATURAL FORESTS; MOBILISING SOCIETY AND INSTRUCTION FOR PEOPLE WISHING TO ACT IN FOREST PROTECTION; and PUBLICISING EXCESSIVE AND UNLAWFUL CASES OF FELLING. Commenting into a certification audit reaches a company's customers, not its regulator — a separate lever from the permit.

trackers.name: RUTI – Unique Register of Interest Transparency
trackers.desc: Romania's public register listing decision-makers' meetings with interest representatives. — Holds to account: lobbyists & influence-seekers — find who is lobbying whom, and meetings held.

trackers.name: ROLII
trackers.desc: Romanian Legal Information Institute: free access to Romanian court decisions. · Find here: free Romanian case-law and legislation (ROLII).

trackers.name: Ia Statul la Întrebări — FOI requests (ROU)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (FOI request platform); Ia Statul la Întrebări — civic Freedom-of-Information request platform (Alaveteli/mySociety network) — lets citizens file public-records requests and publishes the requests and the authorities’ responses in a public archive.

trackers.name: Justice and Environment — European green-law network
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the European network of environmental-law NGOs, whose national member here is the Bankwatch Association. Its fifteen members act as the environmental-law service point in their own countries, taking cases and intervening in legislative processes, while the network defends communities and nature in court and lodges infringement complaints against member-state governments. Its standing themes are access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, environmental assessment and pollution control. WHO IT SUITS: anyone who does not yet know which lawyer to call — knock on the Bankwatch Association's door first, and use the network only if your problem crosses a border. The network itself does not take individual cases; its members do. YOUR NATIONAL MEMBER IS Bankwatch Association Romania (bankwatch.ro) — go to them, not to the network. J&E members serve as environmental law ‘service points’ in their countries, handling cases, participating in legislative processes and sometimes providing legal analyses and consultations for national governments. The network has 11 full and 4 associate members, and can launch infringement proceedings against faulty governments — a route a national body alone does not have. CURRENT SCOPE: access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, climate, environmental assessments, and the Environmental Liability Directive. It previously worked on waste, transport, health and Natura 2000, so an older document may overstate what it covers today.

trackers.name: Bankwatch Association (Asociaţia Bankwatch România)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Romania's member organisation in the Justice and Environment network of European environmental-law NGOs, and the Romanian arm of the CEE Bankwatch tradition of scrutinising internationally financed projects. WHO IT SUITS: communities affected by a project with public or development-bank money behind it, where the financing itself is the pressure point; the network does not state what casework it takes, so ask. Domain unverified this session — reach them through the member list on justiceandenvironment.org. Founded by the CEE Bankwatch Network (15 member organisations across 13 countries in Central and Eastern Europe). It runs named campaign desks — energy transition, mining and fossil gas, just transition, hydropower — so write to the relevant coordinator rather than a general address.

trackers.name: Romanian Court of Accounts
trackers.desc: Romania supreme audit institution

trackers.name: RISE Project
trackers.desc: Romanian investigative group probing organized crime, corruption and money networks.

trackers.name: Átlátszó Erdély
trackers.desc: Transylvania-based nonprofit (sister of Hungary's Átlátszó) using FOI and investigations to expose corruption and public-money abuse.

trackers.name: Context.ro
trackers.desc: Romanian investigative startup covering corruption, fraud and organized crime.

trackers.name: data.gov.ro
trackers.desc: National — Romanian government open data portal. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Romania.

trackers.name: Romania — ANI asset & interest declarations portal
trackers.desc: Accountability source (official asset-declaration register); Romania — ANI asset & interest declarations portal — the National Integrity Agency (ANI) searchable portal of Romanian public officials’ asset and interest declarations.

trackers.name: National Institute of Statistics
trackers.desc: Romania's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Romania.

trackers.name: SICAP / SEAP
trackers.desc: Romania's electronic public-procurement system. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Romania, and for how much.

trackers.name: ANI – National Integrity Agency
trackers.desc: Romania's integrity agency — asset and interest declarations of public officials, plus conflict-of-interest checks.

trackers.name: ONRC (Trade Register)
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Beneficial Ownership Register (RBR)
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Publicly searchable.

trackers.name: Constitutional Court of Romania
trackers.desc: Constitutional Court of Romania — supreme court in Romania (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: Bucharest Court of Appeal
trackers.desc: Bucharest Court of Appeal — appellate court in Romania (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: High Court of Cassation and Justice
trackers.desc: High Court of Cassation and Justice — supreme court in Romania (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: AFM Biodiversitate — funding, but you must be a custodian first
trackers.desc: THE NATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL FUND, AND NGOs ARE NAMED BENEFICIARIES. AFM is Romania's main source of financial support for environmental projects, built on the polluter pays and producer responsibility principles and financed entirely from its own revenues. Its Biodiversitate programme lists non-governmental organisations among beneficiaries, alongside administrative-territorial units, public institutions, museums, public research institutes, accredited universities and economic operators — where they hold the status of custode-administrator. SO THE ORDER MATTERS: get the custody contract first, and the funding follows. County environmental protection agencies may apply instead for protected areas that need no administration structure and are not assigned in custody, as may administrators of wildlife rehabilitation centres.

trackers.name: Custodie of a protected area — and who now issues the aviz
trackers.desc: AN NGO CAN BECOME THE CUSTODIAN OF A PROTECTED AREA. Under OUG 57/2007 on the regime of protected natural areas, with the methodology for assigning areas in administration and custody approved by Ordin 1052/2014, protected areas are administered directly or through partnership and administration contracts — the door for a civil society organisation. A quarter of Romania's territory is protected natural area; the Danube Delta has its own separate administration. CUSTODY IS REVIEWED, NOT PERMANENT: there is a formal commission for evaluation, transfer and takeover of areas assigned in custody, and periodic monitoring and evaluation of administrators. CHECK WHO ISSUES THE AVIZ BEFORE OBJECTING TO A PROJECT: ANANP, created in 2016, issued the opinion required for works interfering with protected areas as part of the environmental agreement documentation — but the government decided by emergency ordinance to merge ANANP into ANPM, and the environment ministry acknowledged that approving projects will be easier while saying legal rigour would hold. Critics argue reforming ANANP would have been preferable, since investments touching protected areas previously required a separate special opinion.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Foundation Conservation Carpathia — buys forest to stop it being logged (Romania)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a foundation established in 2009 by Christoph and Barbara Promberger which buys forest and alpine meadow in the Făgăraș Mountains and takes hunting rights out of circulation, funded with private and public money. It has bought and restored more than 1,991 hectares of clear-cuts, alpine pasture and spruce monoculture, planted over 4.1 million saplings, built nine tree nurseries, and done erosion control on more than 30 kilometres of old tractor tracks. Over 8,000 hectares of what it holds are now non-intervention zones in the Făgăraș Natura 2000 management plan or core areas of Piatra Craiului National Park. USE IT: it keeps buying forest that comes onto the market specifically to stop it being logged, so a Romanian community that knows a block is about to be sold has somewhere to send that information before the sale rather than after the felling. It publishes what the work costs, which almost nobody does: €2.10 to plant a sapling including one to four years of care, and €60 per hectare to protect forest and wildlife. Those are the numbers to put in a local appeal, because they turn an abstract cause into an amount. Its restoration work employs an average of 200 seasonal workers hired from the surrounding communities. KNOW THE POLITICS BEFORE YOU ALIGN WITH IT: the foundation is contested in the Făgăraș region. It is largely financed by foreign philanthropists, its stated goal is a national park, and Romanian landowners' representatives and local press have run sustained criticism of a foreign-funded body accumulating Carpathian land. The foundation's own answer is that the holdings are meant to return to the Romanian public domain as a national park rather than stay with it. A community in that region should expect the association to be used against it, and decide with that in view.

trackers.name: Fundația pentru Parteneriat — Romanian Environmental Partnership Foundation
trackers.desc: WHAT THE CONSORTIUM IS: the Environmental Partnership Association, headquartered in Brno, is a consortium of six independent national foundations in central and eastern Europe that give grants to community projects protecting the environment. It grew out of a programme begun in 1990 by the C.S. Mott Foundation, the German Marshall Fund and the Rockefeller Brothers Fund, and the national foundations were established as independent bodies in the early 1990s. Alongside grants they run education programmes, provide professional services and build the capacity of civic initiatives — which is the part a new local group needs most. THE ROMANIAN MEMBER: Fundația pentru Parteneriat, founded 1998, at repf.ro. Romania has a substantial forest buyer in this file and no funder; this fills that. Note the practical pairing — a Romanian community that has found a block of forest coming up for sale needs both the buyer and the money to do the survey and the campaign around it. SOURCING: the consortium and its six national foundations are documented on the Environmental Partnership Association's own site; the national figures and founding dates come from consortium and partner material rather than each foundation's own pages. Confirm current grant rounds with the national foundation directly.

trackers.name: Fundația ADEPT Transilvania — makes the grassland pay so it stays grassland
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a biodiversity conservation and rural development NGO founded 2004 at Str. Principală 166, Saschiz, Mureș, +40 265 711 635, office@fundatia-adept.org, working the Târnava Mare region of southern Transylvania in the triangle between Sibiu, Sighișoara and Brașov — one of the most important High Nature Value farmland landscapes in continental Europe. Its own framing is that it protects those landscapes by working with and supporting the small-scale farming communities that created them and maintain them, giving them an economic future rather than a restriction. WHAT IT HAS ACTUALLY DELIVERED, WHICH IS WHY IT IS HERE: its field surveys of habitats and species led to the area being included in the EU's Natura 2000 network. In 2011 it designed new national measures protecting grazed orchards and damp grasslands that had no protection until then, with the result that farmers managing 400,000 hectares of those two habitats became eligible for payment for good management. It has advised the Romanian ministry on agri-environment scheme design and worked with the European Commission's agriculture and environment directorates-general. An organisation that got a habitat type into the national payment system is an organisation that can tell you whether your grassland already qualifies for something. WHAT IT CAN BRING TO A THREATENED SITE: habitat, species and land-use mapping including landscape features; identification of High Nature Value grassland and of indicator species for judging condition; local management plans co-designed with small-scale land managers; and concrete restoration on the ground, with baseline and annual species monitoring. It is also developing a biodiversity-credit results-based payment scheme in Târnava Mare intended to pay farmers for nature-friendly management and reduce the pressure to expand agriculture. WHAT IT IS NOT: not a land buyer and not a law firm. It works through cooperation with farmers and ministries rather than opposition, so bring it a grassland that needs an economic case and a management plan, not a confrontation. Romania's file entries now cover the forest buyer, the funder and this — the farmed landscape. ONE DISCREPANCY: its own pages give the founding year as 2004; a major funder's grantee page says 2014. Take 2004, which appears throughout its own site and history.

trackers.name: Agent Green — over 50 forest cases against the Romanian state, and two EC complaints
trackers.desc: WHAT THEY DO, IN THEIR OWN WORDS: investigate environmental crimes, expose them strategically, propose legislative initiatives, act in court, run education and civic engagement campaigns and use national and international media. Romania's bucket had a forest buyer, a grassland foundation and two legal networks — and no investigator. THE CASELOAD, WHICH IS THE ENTRY: over 50 forest cases against the Romanian state, and two complaints lodged with the European Commission. Its own description of method: after field investigations it takes the best of Romanian and European legislation and goes to court — and most of the time it succeeds. After the first Commission complaint the Romanian authorities received a warning that infringement proceedings would open and an obligation to intervene in the destruction of protected areas; infringements opened in February 2020 for illegal logging and degradation of Natura 2000 sites remained open, and during them Agent Green obtained a prohibition on illegal logging in Natura 2000 sites. AND THE CAMPAIGN RESULT WORTH QUOTING TO ANY COMMUNITY: in the campaign to protect Romania's 13 national parks, strictly protected areas rose from around 30 per cent in 2011, when the organisation began, to over 67 per cent in most parks. That is a measurable, published shift achieved by an NGO over fifteen years. WHO WORKS THERE NOW: it has hired a former senior officer of the Mountain Gendarmerie, who will run training courses for authorities and contribute to developing a new law on penalties for forestry offences; he is not the first representative of the authorities to join. It also reports contributing to record fines for illegal logging. AN HONEST NOTE ON ITS CAPACITY: in its own 2025 retrospective it says it invested more in actions for nature than it took in, exhausting part of its emergency reserves, and cites limited media visibility and a lack of political support. Expect a stretched organisation. It works alongside Greenpeace România, Declic and WWF-România on forest monitoring demands.

trackers.name: Romania's 30 and 60 day clocks — miss them and you lose the right to contest at all
trackers.desc: THE DEADLINE, AND IT IS THE HARDEST IN THIS FILE: a Romanian urbanism practice records that Law 102/2023 imposed strict terms — 30 days for suspension and 60 days for the action in annulment — and that exceeding them entails LOSS OF THE RIGHT TO CONTEST the building authorisation. Its advice: contact a lawyer specialised in urbanism immediately on becoming aware of a harmful administrative act. Romania is the only country in this file where missing the window extinguishes the right outright, and the two clocks run at different speeds — suspension is the short one. WHAT THIS MEANS IN PRACTICE: the suspension application is what stops work while the annulment case runs, and it must be filed inside 30 days. Romania's bucket already holds Agent Green with over 50 forest cases, Bankwatch, Conservation Carpathia and the AFM biodiversity fund — what was missing was the clock. AND THE PRELIMINARY STEP THAT APPLIES TO ALL ADMINISTRATIVE ACTS: Romanian practices describe the procedura prealabilă — the mandatory prior complaint to the issuing authority — before going to the contencios administrativ court, available to a person who considers themselves injured in a right or a LEGITIMATE INTEREST by an administrative act. Building authorisations are named among the contestable acts.

trackers.name: Romanian urbanism practices — annulment of PUZ and PUD, and demolition of unlawful buildings
trackers.desc: WHAT THEY DO, from Romanian practices' own service lists: annulments of PUZ, PUD and certificates of urbanism, of avize, and of expropriations; demolition of constructions raised in breach of the legal provisions; and assistance and representation in litigation concerning the contestation of urban plans and documentation and of authority acts issued in the field. Another lists assistance and representation in the procedures for ADOPTING urban plans — public consultation, and submission for approval by the Local or General Council — and the formulation of petitions against abuses or negligence of public authorities. Being represented during the public consultation on a PUZ, not only when contesting it afterwards, is a named service in Romania. AND THE THREE PLANNING INSTRUMENTS TO KNOW BY NAME, since they are what actually decides land use: PUG (general urban plan), PUZ (zonal urban plan) and PUD (detail urban plan) — with practitioners noting the PUZ regulates how land in a given area may be used and developed. CAUTION, recorded plainly: these firms act for developers too — the same lists cover obtaining authorisations and defending investors' interests. Check for conflicts before instructing.

trackers.name: How Romanian conservation land is actually secured — three locks, and the state's first refusal
trackers.desc: THE PURCHASE RULE, WHICH DECIDES WHO CAN BUY: forest can be bought only from natural persons or companies, and only after the Romanian State, which has FIRST REFUSAL, declines to acquire. Romania's bucket had one land acquirer; this is how buying there actually works, and the state pre-emption is the sixth recorded in this file. THE THREE LOCKS PUT ON THE LAND ONCE BOUGHT, which is the part to copy: the terrain is protected by the foundation's own statute; by REGISTRATION AT THE CADASTRAL OFFICE AS CONSERVATION ZONES; and, where possible, by over-protection — more than 9,000 hectares placed in the non-intervention zone of a Natura 2000 site, in the strict protection core of a national park, or in the NATIONAL CATALOGUE OF VIRGIN AND QUASI-VIRGIN FORESTS. Statute, cadastre entry, and then the strongest public designation available — three locks rather than one, and the catalogue entry protects for an unlimited term. THE SCALE AND THE STAFFING: 26,900 hectares of forest and alpine pasture under the foundation's protection, patrolled by a team of RANGERS to combat illegal felling; 27,027 hectares purchased in total; almost 2,000 hectares reforested with over four million young trees; five nurseries created; and a LIFE project that added 1,100 hectares to the virgin forest catalogue while protecting 5,000 hectares of forest and alpine pasture. The stated aim is a model nature reserve benefiting biodiversity AND people, who are to have alternative, environmentally friendly sources of living.

trackers.name: The Romanian objection to conservation land-buying — recorded because a community will meet it
trackers.desc: WHY THIS IS FILED: every other acquisition entry in this file describes buying land as the solution. In Romania it is contested, loudly, by forest owners and by a national forest owners' organisation — and a community proposing to bring in a land-buying foundation will meet these arguments. Recorded so they are not a surprise. WHAT THE OPPONENTS SAY: that the foundation buys through commercial subsidiaries (SRLs) in an aggressive campaign of forest land acquisition across named communes; that its own objectives include acquiring the right to extract minerals and transferring properties to the Romanian State only when its board decides the conditions are met; that its companies hold over 16,000 hectares in one county alone; and — the banner — the Făgăraș Mountains are not for sale. A forest owners' organisation adds that the environment ministry hid the scale of the projects, and names the private foundation and the farming company behind the money, with 7,261 hectares of forest and 12,155 hectares of agricultural land bought in Romania by the latter. AND THE FOUNDER'S OWN ACCOUNT OF WHY HE BUYS, which is the answer to the objection and worth carrying: a new conservation project has to be based on buying land, because if you work with the town hall or other authorities and convince someone, then elections come, the people change, and you start from zero. He also records that locals suspected he knew about gold reserves or wanted a ski slope; nobody believed we wanted to make a protected area.

trackers.name: Platforma de mediu pentru București — 18+ named organisations, and a coordinator with an email
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: an initiative launched by a community foundation to FACILITATE COLLABORATION BETWEEN CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, AUTHORITIES, COMPANIES AND CITIZENS in order to solve the capital's environmental problems — with a named coordinator and a published email address. Romania's bucket had litigators, a land trust and funders but no convening platform. A platform with one contact address, that already convenes NGOs, councils and companies, is where a Romanian group starts rather than writing eighteen separate letters.
