A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Ukrainian Nature Conservation Group — writes the scientific case for protection
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an expert group that does the thing a community genuinely cannot do for itself — survey a site, write the scientific justification for protecting it, and petition the oblast council. On its petition the Mykolaiv oblast council created the Kovalivski Plavni hydrological reserve of over 394 hectares inside the Olshanska territorial community, and it has taken further proposals to completed-justification stage, including a roughly 300-hectare steppe system holding eleven Red Book plant species, twelve Red Book animal species and four Green Book communities. Ukraine's other allies are three legal bodies; none of them can write the botany. IT ARGUES TO THE VILLAGE, NOT ONLY THE COUNCIL: approval decisions are taken by the hromadas themselves, and it produced a booklet for residents of the Butska hromada setting out why the Voloshkovyi reserve should be created, as well as inventorying the biodiversity of a single hromada as a worked example. A community that has to vote on protecting its own ground needs something to read first, and almost nothing else here produces that. WHAT IT SAYS ABOUT ENFORCEMENT, WHICH YOU SHOULD READ BEFORE RELYING ON AN INSPECTORATE: it found clear-felling in a habitat of spring snowflake in the Drohobych forestry district and reported it to the eco-inspectors with photographs of the stumps and the plant; its published account of the response is that it exceeded the worst expectations. It publishes more broadly on how the eco-inspection covers illegal felling rather than fighting it, with worked examples from Zakarpattia.

trackers.name: Rewilding Ukraine — restores wetlands and helped a community get a national park proposed
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: a Ukrainian team working in the Danube Delta since 2017, part of the Rewilding Europe network, operating alongside the Danube Biosphere Reserve, the Izmail water authority, Izmail Forestry, local fishermen, landowners and communities. Since 2019 it has restored seven wetlands covering more than 18,000 hectares and reconnected 20 kilometres of river networks; it reports improving water quality for more than 50,000 people. Its work has continued through the war. WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES THAT A COMMUNITY CAN USE: physical restoration — removing sections of dyke on Ermakiv and Tataru Islands to restore natural current, reconnecting Kartal, Katlabuh and Kugurlui lakes to the Danube, reflooding 500 hectares of marshland, removing ten dams on the Kogilnik River, and restoring more than 500 hectares of Tarutino Steppe that had been illegally ploughed eight years earlier. If land near you has been drained, dyked or ploughed unlawfully, this is an organisation that has reversed exactly that, at scale. AND THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST HERE: it worked with the Borodino community to get the Budzhak Steppes National Nature Park proposed, running the public consultation with the Centre for Regional Studies, assembling a team of scientists to prepare the scientific rationale, and contributing both expertise and financial support to the community's own initiative. A Ukrainian community that wants its ground formally protected has a body that has taken another community through precisely that process, and paid towards it. WHAT TO EXPECT: it is a restoration and reintroduction organisation, not a land buyer and not a law firm, and it is working in a country at war — its own account records staff mobilised into volunteering and civil defence. Approach it about a delta, steppe or wetland site in the Odesa region and about getting a protection case scientifically documented.

trackers.name: National Ecological Centre of Ukraine (NECU) — 24 territorial branches, and it watches the banks
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: one of the first national-level environmental non-profits registered in independent Ukraine, founded 30 August 1991, working on the protection of natural territories, biodiversity, climate and the negative consequences of the energy sector. It has 24 territorial branches across Ukraine, plus a youth branch revived in 2003 — which is the single most useful fact here, because it means there is very likely a branch in your oblast rather than only an office in Kyiv. WHAT IT DOES WITH A CASE: it pushes officials and politicians to take decisions with environmental protection and public safety in view, prepares its own assessments and studies, and proposes alternative solutions. That last part matters: an alternative on the table is consistently stronger than an objection alone, as the Italian and British entries in this file also found. It is a member of IUCN and of the CEE Bankwatch Network, and it states that its staff pay particular attention to the projects of development banks. THE SPECIALISMS ITS OWN PEOPLE DECLARE, which tell you what to ask for: work with local communities; the state of water resources; biological and landscape diversity; the nature reserve fund and the development of the ecological network; green zones in settlements; organising public conservation campaigns; and countering corruption in the environmental sphere. One of its council members directs a regional landscape park and the southern branch of its ecology institute, so protected-area creation is inside its experience. IT RUNS NAMED CAMPAIGNS: including one to save the Buzkyi Hard, which is the kind of long single-site defence a community can ask to be added to. USE IT WITH THE OTHER UKRAINIAN ENTRIES: this file already holds a group that writes the scientific justification for protection and petitions oblast councils, a team that restores wetlands and steered a community through a national park proposal, and an environmental law organisation. NECU adds national reach, 24 local branches and the development-bank angle. WHAT IT IS NOT: not a land buyer and not a funder, and it is operating in wartime.

trackers.name: ТОП — Ukrainian Society for the Protection of Birds, and the IBA programme
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Ukraine's first non-governmental bird conservation organisation, founded 1994, BirdLife partner since 1995 and full partner from 2006, with a membership network of around 2,000 individual members. PO box 143, Kyiv 03150, uspb@birdlife.org.ua, +380 44 339-99-81. Membership is open to anyone — conservationists, bird enthusiasts, scientists and amateurs alike — and the organisation is run by a democratically elected council between congresses of its members. For a Ukrainian community with people rather than money, that is the way in. WHAT TO ASK IT FOR: it runs Ukraine's Important Bird Areas programme, and its species work spans the aquatic warbler, greater spotted eagle, red-breasted goose, great bustard, white-tailed eagle and saker falcon across the Carpathians, ancient forests, peatlands, steppe grassland and coastal habitats. If a threatened Ukrainian site is an Important Bird Area, or holds any of those species, this is the organisation that can say so with standing — and it has spent thirty years mapping exactly that. ITS RECORD ON GETTING GROUND PROTECTED: with the wider BirdLife partnership it has played a key role in expanding Ukraine's network of protected areas, and in 2017 the Ukrainian government passed legislation protecting the country's remaining primeval Carpathian forests — an initiative it helped design and champion. A community seeking designation for its own ground is asking an organisation that has done it at national scale. IT ALSO RESTORES: it has worked on restoring wetland and peatland ecosystems, including freshwater lakes in the Dnipro delta, and takes part in international programmes for the aquatic warbler including translocation between countries. WHAT IT IS NOT, CHECKED SPECIFICALLY: not a land buyer — I found no evidence it purchases land. Ukraine's other entries here are the group that writes scientific justifications and petitions oblast councils, the Danube delta restoration team, an environmental law organisation, and the national centre with 24 branches. This adds the bird record and the IBA network.

trackers.name: ІСАР Єднання (ISAR Ednannia) — one of Ukraine's largest domestic grant-makers
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a Ukrainian civil society organisation that has spent about 25 years developing civil society and strategic philanthropy in Ukraine. It is described as one of the largest genuinely Ukrainian grant-makers, providing upwards of 500 grants a year for public-benefit initiatives across the whole territory of Ukraine. Ukraine had no funder in this file, despite having four other allies. THE SIZES AND SHAPES TO PLAN AROUND, from its published calls: a competition for local civic organisations with most supported projects budgeted up to 294,000 hryvnia, around 55 organisations supported, projects of about six months, open to bodies implementing local initiatives anywhere in Ukraine with priority to five oblasts — Chernihiv, Sumy, Kharkiv, Mykolaiv and Zaporizhzhia. A project grants competition for initiatives driving systemic change, democratic transformation and recovery of processes damaged by the war, expressly including advocacy campaigns. Grants for strategic partners strengthening the expert capacity of local civil society organisations, networking and sector development. And a fund for organisations working in communities that have suffered critical disruption. THE RARE ONE, AND IT IS THE MOST VALUABLE FORMAT IN THIS FILE: an institutional support competition of up to 2,500,000 hryvnia for the upkeep and development of the organisation itself — salaries, office rent, equipment and organisational development, with no tie to a specific project. Most grants pay for activities; this pays for the organisation to exist. Only PONT's operating costs, the EEA institutional grants and the southern Italian volunteering call compare anywhere in these 166 candidates. HOW TO USE IT FOR LAND WORK: it is not an environmental funder. Its themes are democratic governance, human rights, recovery and local initiative — so a Ukrainian community should frame a case as residents organising to solve a local problem or to advocate on a decision, which is what the calls describe. The Ukrainian entries already in this file supply the science, the restoration, the law and the branch network; this is the money.

trackers.name: UNCG's zapovidna sprava desk — it writes the case for protecting your site, and has ~100 wins
trackers.desc: WHAT THEY DO, IN ONE LINE: they prepare the obgruntuvannya — the scientific justification — for creating new protected areas in places genuinely worth saving first. On their justifications around 100 protected-area objects have already been created, in Kyiv, Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson, Lviv and other oblasts; across all its work the organisation has contributed to creating more than 150 objects of the nature reserve fund, and describes itself as the leader by area of protected objects created in Ukraine. THE FRAME A COMMUNITY SHOULD UNDERSTAND: their own statement is that the greatest achievement in nature protection is granting protective status to a valuable natural territory. Ukraine has over 8,400 objects of the nature reserve fund covering 6.8 per cent of the country. Where Turkey's route turned out to run through designation rather than purchase, so does Ukraine's — and here is the body that writes the paperwork. AND THE STEP THAT DECIDES IT IS LOCAL: for a proposed zakaznyk in the Chortalka valley between two named villages, the account is explicit — after the petition came long negotiations with the hromada, which had to agree to the creation of the zakaznyk, and on 15 June the deputies of the Mostivska hromada supported the initiative and agreed it. The community council's vote is the gate. A residents' group that wants its ground protected should be working on its own council while the scientists write the justification. WHO THEY ARE: formed in 2014 as a common name for scientists already creating protected areas separately — botanists, a lichenologist, a steppe protection specialist, a national park director — and registered as a civic organisation only in spring 2018. More than 50 members, most of them working scientists elsewhere, with only a few full-time. Expect expert capacity, not an office. PRACTICAL NOTE ON WHO PAYS FOR LAND: under Ukrainian law, buying out private and communal land for nature reserve fund territories is done from the state budget for objects of national importance and from local budgets for objects of local importance. The money for acquisition is public, and follows the designation.

trackers.name: WOWnature — the Ukrainian route to putting land under protection without expropriating it
trackers.desc: WHY THIS MATTERS FOR UKRAINE SPECIFICALLY: Ukraine's bucket held 31 entries and nobody who takes or holds ground. It is also a country where buying land for conservation is often not the realistic move. The pryrodno-zapovidnyi fond — the nature reserve fund — supplies the alternative, and this platform is the public-facing route into it. THE KEY FACT, AND IT CHANGES WHAT A COMMUNITY NEEDS TO RAISE: declaration of a pam'iatka pryrody — a nature monument — is carried out WITHOUT WITHDRAWING the land, water or other natural objects from their owners or users. Protection can be organised either with prior allocation of land and registration in the cadastre, OR WITHOUT ALLOCATION, by concluding a PROTECTION OBLIGATION (okhoronne zoboviazannia) with the existing owner. You do not have to own the land to have it protected, and where an owner is willing, the obligation is the cheapest route in this file. AND THE REGIME THAT FOLLOWS: on a nature monument any activity that threatens its preservation or leads to degradation or change of its original state is prohibited; and on change of the landowner or land user, including a tenant, within these territories they are obliged to maintain the protection regime. The obligation runs with the land. WHAT A LOCAL GROUP HAS TO ASSEMBLE, from a published step plan: a map-scheme with the boundaries of the proposed plot; survey reports, expert conclusions and natural resource inventory materials; cadastral data (land, forest and so on); agreement of the petition with owners or users where they exist; and arrangements for the conservation project to be drawn up by specialist institutions before the authorised body decides.

trackers.name: Hromadskyi Prostir — the Ukrainian noticeboard where environmental grants are announced
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the long-running Ukrainian civil society portal that publishes grant announcements as they open, including environmental ones. Ukraine's bucket had one funder filed; this is the place a group watches so it does not miss the next call. A WORKED EXAMPLE FROM IT, showing what these calls look like: a UNDP grant to support the implementation of initiatives aimed at protecting the environment, delivered in government-controlled hromadas where the security situation allows, across eight named oblasts — Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, Luhansk, Mykolaiv, Sumy, Kharkiv and Chernihiv. Eligibility was assessed against the CACHE capacity assessment checklist, and proposals from organisations not meeting the requirements were not considered at all. Where a donor names a capacity checklist, read it before writing anything — the assessment is a gate, not a scoring factor. AND A SECOND SOURCE WORTH THE SAME ATTENTION: the International Renaissance Foundation has run a small grants competition to support environmental civic initiatives from the south-eastern oblasts of Ukraine during the war. Small-grant windows aimed at a named region are the easiest entry point for a group with no grant history.

trackers.name: ІSAR Єdnannia grant tiers — from 294,000 UAH local projects to 6,000,000 UAH systemic ones
trackers.desc: WHY THE TIERS MATTER: ІSAR Єdnannia is one of the largest genuinely Ukrainian grant-makers, giving more than 500 grants a year across the country. Its front page is already filed here; what was missing is the shape of the money, which runs from small local grants to systemic ones. THE LOCAL TIER: a competition for local initiatives from anywhere in Ukraine, most supported projects budgeted up to 294,000 UAH, around 55 organisations supported, projects about six months long, with priority to five named oblasts. Selected organisations also get development support from an organisational mentor. THE SYSTEMIC TIER: grants up to 6,000,000 UAH for systemic solutions, whose named thematic areas include green transformation — resource efficiency, environmental innovation, adaptation to climate change — alongside anti-corruption integrity, openness, accountability and public oversight. THE ELIGIBILITY GATE, RECORDED EXACTLY BECAUSE IT DISQUALIFIES PEOPLE: applicants must be officially registered under the laws on public associations, on charitable activity and charitable organisations, or on associations of local self-government bodies, AND included in the Register of Non-Profit Organisations with the appropriate non-profit code (0032, 0036, 0038, 0039, 0048). Check your non-profit code before you check the deadline.

trackers.name: Ukrainian Nature Conservation Group — 75 per cent of all new protected area in a decade
trackers.desc: THE RECORD, AND IT IS THE STRONGEST DESIGNATION CLAIM IN THIS FILE: we are the leaders by area of protected-fund objects created in Ukraine — 75 PER CENT OF THE PROTECTED AREAS CREATED IN UKRAINE OVER THE LAST TEN YEARS CAME ABOUT THANKS TO OUR GROUP. Ukraine had one land acquirer filed. If three quarters of a country's new protected land was created by one organisation, that is the organisation a community brings its site to. WHO THEY ARE AND WHAT THEY DO: formed in 2014 when Ukrainian biologists united to protect Ukraine's wild nature, they CREATE PROTECTED TERRITORIES, work on improving legislation, and DETECT CASES OF ILLEGAL DESTRUCTION OF NATURE, combining the efforts of experts and scientists for the protection of biological diversity and the development of the nature reserve fund. Their listed work includes PARTICIPATION IN THE ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT PROCESS and MONITORING OF PROJECTS HARMFUL TO NATURE. AND WHAT DONATIONS HAVE ACTUALLY PAID FOR: when a biosphere reserve fell under occupation from the first hours of the full-scale invasion, thousands of people in Ukraine and abroad decided otherwise — and thanks to charitable contributions the reserve's team could continue autonomous work under occupation FOR 13 MONTHS.

trackers.name: Ukrainian Society for the Protection of Birds — it runs the IBA programme that names your site
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a national public organisation founded in 1994, one of the largest and most active in the country, and the BirdLife International partner, working to protect rare and endangered bird species and to support species diversity by conserving the ecosystems key to their existence. AND THE PROGRAMME THAT GIVES A SITE A NAME: it runs the IBA Programme — a unique international initiative launched by BirdLife International to IDENTIFY, MONITOR AND PROTECT the worldwide network of Important Bird Areas, promoting the conservation of both global avifauna and biodiversity generally, with species receiving protective status according to NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL CRITERIA. This file recorded in Cyprus that IBAs have been accepted by the European Court of Justice as a scientifically sound basis for protected-area boundaries — and this is the organisation that designates them in Ukraine. Bring it your records. AND ALSO ON THE MAP FOR LAND QUESTIONS: an all-Ukrainian section for the protection and rational use of land within the national nature protection society, alongside a surveyors' union and a farmers' and private landowners' association — named bodies with published addresses for anyone dealing with a land-use dispute rather than a species one.

trackers.name: The zakaznyk route — protection WITHOUT taking the land off its owner
trackers.desc: THE POINT THAT UNLOCKS A RELUCTANT OWNER: the creation of ZAKAZNYKY takes place WITHOUT THE WITHDRAWAL of land plots, water or other territories FROM THEIR OWNERS OR USERS, and people's access to these territories remains free. Ukraine had one land-acquisition entry filed; this is the route that needs no purchase at all. A designation that neither takes the land nor closes it is one a farmer and a village can both be persuaded to accept — which is the objection this file meets in almost every country. AND WHAT THE FUND IS FOR, in the statutory words: the nature reserve fund comprises areas of land and water space whose natural complexes and objects have SPECIAL CONSERVATION, SCIENTIFIC, AESTHETIC, RECREATIONAL AND OTHER VALUE, and are set apart for the purpose of PRESERVING THE NATURAL DIVERSITY OF LANDSCAPES, THE GENE POOL of animal and plant life, maintaining the general ecological balance and ensuring background monitoring of the natural environment. Aesthetic and recreational value are named in the statute alongside science, so a community whose case is beauty and use, not rare species, is arguing on listed grounds. The categories run from nature reserves and biosphere reserves through national nature parks, REGIONAL LANDSCAPE PARKS, zakaznyky, NATURE MONUMENTS and protected tracts.

trackers.name: The klopotannya procedure — how a citizen's petition becomes a protected area
trackers.desc: WHAT THE PETITION MUST CONTAIN, published on the state free-legal-aid wiki: the KLOPOTANNYA must contain A JUSTIFICATION OF THE NECESSITY of creating or declaring a territory or object of the nature reserve fund OF A PARTICULAR CATEGORY, and a characterisation of its CONSERVATION, SCIENTIFIC, AESTHETIC AND OTHER VALUE. A community writing the justification itself decides which category is asked for — and this file has recorded a Ukrainian organisation that has had about a hundred such justifications accepted. AND WHAT HAPPENS NEXT, step by step: if the petitions are approved, the ministry and its local bodies CARRY OUT THEIR AGREEMENT WITH THE OWNERS AND PRIMARY USERS of natural resources within the territories recommended for protection. On the basis of the results of that agreement, the ministry ensures the development, BY SPECIALISED DESIGN AND SCIENTIFIC INSTITUTIONS, of the projects for creating the reserves, parks and zakaznyky. The owners are formally consulted before the project is drawn up, not after — so a community that has already spoken to the landowners arrives at that stage with the hardest part done. Free legal aid publishing the procedure means the whole route is documented on a state site a citizen can cite.

trackers.name: ISAR Yednannya — 500+ grants a year, and NEWLY FORMED groups are SPECIALLY INVITED
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a Ukrainian civic organisation which for 25 YEARS has developed civil society and a culture of strategic philanthropy, described as ONE OF THE LARGEST NATIVELY UKRAINIAN GRANTMAKERS, giving FROM 500 GRANTS EACH YEAR for socially useful initiatives ACROSS THE WHOLE TERRITORY OF UKRAINE. Ukraine had three funding entries filed. AND THE ELIGIBILITY LINE THAT MATTERS MOST TO A NEW GROUP: one of its calls, worth up to 294,000 HRYVNIA for LOCAL civic organisations, is open to bodies registered under the named acts on civic associations, charitable activity or local self-government associations and entered in the register of non-profit organisations — and it states that NEWLY CREATED ORGANISATIONS (created no earlier than 2024), WHICH HAVE NO EXPERIENCE OF IMPLEMENTING PROJECTS OR ONLY SLIGHT EXPERIENCE, ARE ESPECIALLY INVITED. A funder that specially invites groups with no track record is the opposite of the two-year and one-year bars recorded in Slovenia and Croatia — and it is what a committee formed last month actually needs. AND THE OTHER SIZES ON OFFER: a training-and-grant programme up to 400,000 HRYVNIA for newly created organisations with up to 4 years of activity and a team of at least two people; organisational development grants up to 45,000 HRYVNIA; and emergency-response capacity grants up to 1,000,000 HRYVNIA, sized according to the organisation's justified needs and the submitted budget.

trackers.name: The self-assessment route — the grant is awarded on YOUR OWN development plan
trackers.desc: HOW THIS GRANT IS ACTUALLY WON, step by step, and it is unlike any funding route filed so far: the applicant organisation must first carry out a SELF-ASSESSMENT OF ITS ORGANISATIONAL CAPACITY using the SELF-ASSESSMENT TOOL in its working account on the funder's site, which can also be downloaded. AND WHO SHOULD DO IT: involve the team and the members of the board in the assessment, in order to identify PRIORITY AREAS FOR DEVELOPMENT — and for the application choose A MAXIMUM OF ONE AREA of high priority. The results show which areas of organisational development most need change, and THE DEVELOPMENT PLAN THAT COMES OUT OF IT IS THE BASIS FOR RECEIVING THE GRANT. A funder that pays for whatever the group itself identifies as its weakest point is money a community can spend on the thing it actually lacks — bookkeeping, a website, legal capacity — rather than on a project designed to fit a call. AND THE REST OF THE SEQUENCE: after the selection commission approves, the applicant is notified in its working account on the site; a contract is concluded between funder and organisation; funds are transferred to the organisation's account ON THE BASIS OF THAT CONTRACT; and the organisation later submits programme and financial reports.

trackers.name: Vykup for public needs — a NATURE RESERVE ADMINISTRATION can initiate the buy-out itself
trackers.desc: WHO MAY START A COMPULSORY PURCHASE IN UKRAINE, and the third name on the list is the one that matters here: the initiator of a buy-out of a land plot for public needs may be an EXECUTIVE AUTHORITY, a body of LOCAL SELF-GOVERNMENT, or A SPECIAL ADMINISTRATION FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF TERRITORIES AND OBJECTS OF THE NATURE RESERVE FUND. Ukraine had one land-acquisition entry filed. The body that runs a protected area can itself initiate the purchase of private land — so a community with a reserve nearby has a public buyer already empowered to act, and asking it costs nothing. AND WHERE THE POWER SITS: a named article of the Land Code determines the bodies of state power and local self-government WHICH HAVE THE RIGHT TO TAKE A DECISION ON THE BUY-OUT of land plots held in private ownership, contains THE LIST OF PUBLIC NEEDS, and establishes the general legal principles of the buy-out procedure. A statutory list of what counts as a public need is a document to read before assuming a purchase is impossible — and the same list governs takings a community may want to resist. The page also covers the disposal of land plots BY AMALGAMATED TERRITORIAL COMMUNITIES, which is where local decisions about land now sit.

trackers.name: The forced-alienation algorithm — and the case where the state SUED TOO EARLY and lost
trackers.desc: THE PROCEDURAL DEFECT THAT DEFEATED A TAKING, from a reported case: the court found that the required decision HAD NOT BEEN TAKEN BY THE BODY that decided on the buy-out of the disputed land plots from the respondents, and therefore concluded that the regional administration's application to the court WAS MADE IN BREACH OF THE PROCEDURE ESTABLISHED BY LAW AND WAS PREMATURE. A taking that skips a step in its own procedure can be defeated on that alone, without arguing the merits — and the ruling is cited with its court, date and case number, so it can be produced. AND THE LIMIT ON WHEN FORCED ALIENATION IS AVAILABLE AT ALL: the forced alienation of land plots and other immovable objects located on them, on grounds of PUBLIC NECESSITY, MAY BE CARRIED OUT ONLY WHEN the executive body has met the conditions the law sets. Public necessity is a higher bar than public need, and it is available only in the circumstances the statute allows. The piece sets the whole sequence out as a step-by-step algorithm, which is what a landowner or a community lawyer needs to check a taking against.

trackers.name: Hromady.org — the land-questions desk for amalgamated communities, answered by the cadastre
trackers.desc: WHAT THIS IS: the all-Ukrainian association of amalgamated communities publishing THE STATE LAND CADASTRE'S ANSWERS TO QUESTIONS FROM THE COMMUNITIES — the practical land questions a village council actually asks, answered on the record by the agency that decides them. Ukraine had two land-acquisition entries filed. AND THE ANSWER THAT REMOVES THE USUAL OBSTACLE: asked WITH WHOSE MONEY the land-management documentation can be produced, the reply is that naturally, if there is a person interested in obtaining the land plots for use, THEY ORDER AND PAY for the land-management works — but THE COUNCIL MAY ALSO FINANCE THE PERFORMANCE OF LAND-MANAGEMENT WORKS FROM ITS OWN BUDGET. A village council can pay for the survey out of its own budget rather than waiting for a developer to fund it, which decides who controls the resulting document. AND THE PROTECTION IT RECORDS FOR SHELTER BELTS: the tenant of FIELD-PROTECTIVE FOREST BELTS situated on agricultural land MUST ENSURE the conditions and measures set out in named Cabinet-approved rules on the maintenance and preservation of field-protective forest belts. Shelter belts come with binding maintenance duties on whoever leases them — the same category Moldova counts separately, and a duty a community can ask to see enforced. It also notes that land transferred into COLLECTIVE ownership REMAINS collectively owned, and ITS FURTHER FATE IS NOT REGULATED BY LEGISLATION.

trackers.name: Átlátszó (atlatszo.hu)
trackers.desc: Hungarian investigative and FOI newsroom exposing corruption and misuse of public funds. — Holds to account: officials handling public money & power — find investigations and public-interest data requests.

trackers.name: Courts of Hungary
trackers.desc: Official judiciary portal with the collection of anonymized court decisions (BHGY). · Find here: information, case search and selected decisions of the courts of Hungary.

trackers.name: Hungarian National Authority for Data Protection and Freedom of Information (NAIH)
trackers.desc: Hungarian National Authority for Data Protection and Freedom of Information (NAIH) — independent body overseeing the right of access to public information.

trackers.name: Ki Mit Tud — FOI requests (HUN)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (FOI request platform); Ki Mit Tud — civic Freedom-of-Information request platform (Alaveteli/mySociety network) — lets citizens file public-records requests and publishes the requests and the authorities’ responses in a public archive.

trackers.name: Hungarian Helsinki Committee
trackers.desc: Leading Hungarian rule-of-law and human-rights NGO and a key election-integrity watchdog — publishes electoral-integrity assessments and the joint Citizen Election Report, litigates freedom-of-information cases, and tracks legislative changes to the electoral framework.

trackers.name: EMLA — Környezeti Management és Jog Egyesület
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Hungary's public-interest environmental law association, founded 1992, whose core activities are environmental legal advice AND legal representation of citizens and NGOs before authorities and courts, alongside research and training. Publishes free practical guides and document templates for people who want to take the legal route, plus a decision-tree tool on remedies. Also advises municipalities on their statutory environmental duties. WHO IT SUITS: a resident or civil organisation confronting a polluting or destructive project who needs an actual lawyer, not just information. Capacity is limited and cases are selected.

trackers.name: Justice and Environment — European green-law network
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the European network of environmental-law NGOs, whose national member here is EMLA. Its fifteen members act as the environmental-law service point in their own countries, taking cases and intervening in legislative processes, while the network defends communities and nature in court and lodges infringement complaints against member-state governments. Its standing themes are access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, environmental assessment and pollution control. WHO IT SUITS: anyone who does not yet know which lawyer to call — knock on EMLA's door first, and use the network only if your problem crosses a border. The network itself does not take individual cases; its members do. YOUR NATIONAL MEMBER IS Environmental Management and Law Association (EMLA) (emla.hu) — go to them, not to the network. J&E members serve as environmental law ‘service points’ in their countries, handling cases, participating in legislative processes and sometimes providing legal analyses and consultations for national governments. The network has 11 full and 4 associate members, and can launch infringement proceedings against faulty governments — a route a national body alone does not have. CURRENT SCOPE: access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, climate, environmental assessments, and the Environmental Liability Directive. It previously worked on waste, transport, health and Natura 2000, so an older document may overstate what it covers today.

trackers.name: Registry of civil society organisations
trackers.desc: registration authority in Hungary

trackers.name: State Audit Office (ÁSZ)
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Hungary, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: EKR
trackers.desc: Hungary's electronic public-procurement system. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Hungary, and for how much.

trackers.name: K-Monitor
trackers.desc: Hungarian anti-corruption watchdog that monitors parliamentary activity, public spending, and political integrity. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Hungary, and for how much.

trackers.name: Direkt36
trackers.desc: Hungarian investigative center exposing corruption and the misuse of public money and power.

trackers.name: e-Cégjegyzék
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Hungarian Central Statistical Office (KSH)
trackers.desc: Hungary's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Hungary.

trackers.name: Természetvédelmi pályázat — 100 percent funded, paid in advance, no own funds
trackers.desc: THE MOST GENEROUS TERMS RECORDED ANYWHERE IN THIS MAP. The agriculture ministry's annual nature protection call gives a one-off non-repayable grant of up to 100 percent of all eligible costs, transferred in a single sum as an advance to your bank account — and providing own resources or co-funding is not a condition. Against Italy's 10 percent cash requirement, Serbia's co-financing framing and GEF's 50 percent expectation, Hungary asks for none and pays up front rather than in arrears. ELIGIBILITY TURNS ON YOUR STATUTE: you must qualify as a civil organisation under the Civil tv. and have environmental and/or nature protection purpose recorded in your alapító okirat or alapszabály — the fifth country in this map, with Finland, Italy, Poland and Greece, where your own constitution is the gate. FUNDABLE: habitat protection and management, habitat rehabilitation and reconstruction, operation of the Natura 2000 network, geological natural values, caves, landscape protection research, ecosystem mapping and valuation, publications, films and environmental education. Work must fit the Nemzeti Természetvédelmi Alapterv.

trackers.name: Which Hungarian call to enter — and read the exclusions first
trackers.desc: THERE ARE TWO NATIONAL CALLS AND THEY FUND DIFFERENT THINGS. The NKP környezetvédelmi call is the larger — a frame of HUF 400,000,000 with up to HUF 10,000,000 per application, again one-off, non-repayable and up to 100 percent of eligible costs — but its categories are awareness and consumption: air quality, environmentally conscious consumer behaviour, communication on greenwashing and on credible ISO Type I ecolabels. So this is the money for public-facing campaigning; the agriculture ministry's call is the one for habitat work. ELIGIBLE here are Hungarian-registered associations and foundations under Act CLXXV of 2011, expressly excluding parties, trade unions, mutual insurance associations, public foundations and party foundations. READ THE EXCLUSION LIST BEFORE DRAFTING: the nature call names topics for which support cannot be requested — some outside the portfolio's remit, others funded under a different framework — so a proposal aimed at an excluded topic is wasted work. In one round 22 organisations were funded, with the decision published as a table showing funded, reserve-list and unfunded applicants — so a near miss is visible and worth following up. The ministry also runs a workshop to help submit adequate applications; attend it.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: MME's nine county land-holding foundations (Hungary) — who actually buys the land
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: BirdLife Hungary's land arm is not the national association but nine separate foundations it established, and MME states on this page that conservation land purchase and conservation land management were among the purposes they were created for. They are Baranya Természeti Értékeikért, Bihar Természetvédelmi és Kulturális Értékőrző, Cserhát Természeti és Kulturális Értékeikért, Dunatáj Természet- és Környezetvédelmi, Pro Vértes Természetvédelmi, Tiszatáj Környezet- és Természetvédelmi, Tolna Megyei Természetvédelmi, „Göcsej” Természetvédelmi, and „Tolna megye természeti értékeiért”. Four of them are public foundations (közalapítvány) rather than private ones. USE IT: approach the foundation covering your county, not MME in Budapest — MME says the foundations operate independently of the association, and they are the bodies that hold ground. The detail worth carrying into a council meeting is the next sentence on the same page: municipal and county governments were frequently co-founders alongside other civil-society organisations, and MME's presidency delegates board members in whole or in part. In several counties a local authority is therefore already inside this structure and can be asked to act as a party rather than lobbied as an opponent.

trackers.name: Ökotárs Alapítvány — Hungarian Environmental Partnership Foundation
trackers.desc: WHAT THE CONSORTIUM IS: the Environmental Partnership Association, headquartered in Brno, is a consortium of six independent national foundations in central and eastern Europe that give grants to community projects protecting the environment. It grew out of a programme begun in 1990 by the C.S. Mott Foundation, the German Marshall Fund and the Rockefeller Brothers Fund, and the national foundations were established as independent bodies in the early 1990s. Alongside grants they run education programmes, provide professional services and build the capacity of civic initiatives — which is the part a new local group needs most. THE HUNGARIAN MEMBER: Ökotárs Alapítvány, founded 1992, at okotars.hu. It has also led a multi-country consortium on protecting civic space, working with partners in Bulgaria, Czechia, Poland, Romania, Serbia and Slovakia and delivering training to local and national civil society organisations and activist groups — so it is a plausible first call for a Hungarian group that is being obstructed rather than merely outspent. SOURCING: the consortium and its six national foundations are documented on the Environmental Partnership Association's own site; the national figures and founding dates come from consortium and partner material rather than each foundation's own pages. Confirm current grant rounds with the national foundation directly.

trackers.name: MME Monitoring Központ — 154 published trend graphs, and regional coordinators to call
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: the Magyar Madártani és Természetvédelmi Egyesület, over fifty years old, a founding participant in BirdLife International in 1993 and its Hungarian partner. Its members are organised in thirty territorial organisations, covering the whole country through a network of volunteer groups, with eight specialist sections built up over the decades and a youth section. It aims to run at least one active group per county, and where possible per significant landscape unit. Hungary already had MME's nine county land-holding foundations filed as acquirers; this is the research and organising side. THE DATA, WHICH IS THE POINT: the Ringing Centre and the Monitoring Centre databases are outstanding by international standards, holding tens of millions of data records. Several hundred volunteers a year take part in fieldwork and data submission, directed by territorial coordinators and the Monitoring Centre. Calls, guides, recording forms and field notebooks for most programmes are downloadable, results and summaries are published regularly, and internet upload and information portals have existed since 2005. Its stated aim is that all habitat and species data end in a single central database that every surveyor can query. Its summary publication is the Magyarország madáratlasza. WHAT YOU CAN CITE WITHOUT FIELDWORK: 154 trend graphs are available from the MMM online database — five biodiversity indicators (agricultural habitats, forest habitats, long-distance migrants, partial and short-distance migrants, resident species), 98 breeding-season species and 51 wintering species. Of 30 species showing significant decline, 70 per cent are dominant users of agricultural habitats and 53 per cent are long-distance migrants. If your ground is farmland, that indicator is the argument, already computed. PRACTICAL: joining a survey means committing to the same area or species group for several years, which the organisation states plainly. Local programmes are explained by the local groups. MME is a kiemelten közhasznú — prominently public-benefit — organisation, and can receive the 1% tax designation.

trackers.name: MTVSZ tagszervezetek — over 100 member groups, in every county of Hungary
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Hungarian Friends of Nature Association, founded in 1989 by 32 rural nature protection groups to represent conservation interests at national level, now a community of more than 100 environmental and nature protection associations and groups whose activity extends to every county of Hungary and, through partners, the whole Carpathian Basin. Individual members of those organisations exceed 28,000. It is Friends of the Earth Hungary. Hungary's bucket had a legal association, county land foundations, the bird monitoring centre and a funder — and no route to the local group. WHY THE MEMBER LIST IS THE RESOURCE: eleven countries into this file, a published membership list has been the most useful artefact each time, and this one is explicitly county-by-county. A Hungarian community can find the environmental organisation nearest it from one page. WHAT THE FEDERATION ITSELF WORKS ON, and it names development directly: mitigating climate change effects, integrating sustainability into sectoral policy, supporting GMO-free and nature-friendly agriculture, action against harmful infrastructure and industrial investments, and exposing greenwashing by environmentally destructive giant companies and banks. It describes itself as radical in its principles, working through community actions, professional events, well-founded studies and targeted lobbying. TWO CURRENT FIGHTS THAT SHOW THE SHAPE: it backs a Stop palagáz! initiative seeking a national shale gas moratorium, noting that new concessions would affect protected areas and waters in the Homokhátság, Hortobágy and Zala while the affected local population receives no substantive information. And with other organisations it went to a felling site in the middle of the Bükk National Park to show that protected forest habitats are being destroyed. IT ALSO WORKS THE FUNDING MONITORING SIDE: with member organisations it has pressed the case of local communities, civil organisations and small businesses in three named counties as beneficiaries of the Just Transition Fund, and works inside operational programme monitoring committees where civil participation is a statutory obligation.

trackers.name: Hungarian környezetvédelmi jog practices — they sue for lost view and lost intimacy
trackers.desc: WHAT THEY DO, from a Hungarian firm's own environmental-law page: legal representation in environmental litigation including proceedings before the authority AND the court, representation in permitting procedures, and drafting environment-related contracts. Hungary's bucket held EMLA and the European green-law network but no private practice; this is one. AND THE HEAD OF DAMAGE THAT MOST COMMUNITIES NEVER THINK TO CLAIM: the firm names damages actions for environmental harm connected with the construction and operation of mobile phone masts, motorways and roads — NOISE, AIR POLLUTION, LOSS OF INTIMACY AND LOSS OF VIEW. Loss of view and loss of privacy are pleaded as compensable harms in Hungary, not merely as objections at the permit stage. ANOTHER ROUTE ON THE SAME PAGE-SET: Hungarian administrative practices list construction authority matters, KISAJÁTÍTÁS (expropriation) matters, environmental, water-law and road-law authority matters, land registry matters, and birtokvédelem — possession protection proceedings and possession actions. They note that the remedies are the fellebbezés and the közigazgatási per, and that in those stages professional legal representation is in any case necessary. A CAUTION: environment-law practices in Hungary also advise operators on compliance and risk. Check for conflicts.

trackers.name: Kúria summary opinion on building-authority practice — and the case where NGOs were parties
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Kúria — Hungary's supreme court — publishes a summary opinion on the practice of building-authority procedures, listing the whole governing instrument set in one place: the code of administrative court procedure, the territorial planning act, the OTÉK national settlement-planning and building requirements, and the government decrees on building-authority procedures and inspections, on construction activity, and on the settlement development concept and integrated settlement development strategy. A supreme court's own summary of how these cases actually run is free and authoritative — the third such digest recorded in this file after Latvia and Slovakia. AND THE WORKED EXAMPLE FROM HUNGARIAN CASE LAW: in a reported case társadalmi szervezetek — civil society organisations — took part in the proceedings AS PARTIES (ügyfélként), lodged appeals against the first-instance building permit, and then brought court proceedings seeking annulment of the decision INCLUDING the environmental permits it covered, and asking the court to order a fresh procedure. Their ground: the decisions contained no economic and social impact assessment and weighing in relation to the planned construction, and the authority had not assessed how the affected residents would be impacted. A local district council appealed alongside them.

trackers.name: The 106-organisation letter on national park land — Hungary's roster, and the transfer it opposed
trackers.desc: WHAT HAPPENED, and it is the clearest recorded case of protected land changing hands: the three largest Hungarian nature conservation organisations wrote to the government over a decision process under which the ASSET MANAGEMENT OF 50,000 HECTARES OF PROTECTED AREA could pass from the national park directorates to the National Land Fund Management Organisation. THEIR ARGUMENT, which transfers anywhere a conservation body is stripped of land: they saw no guarantee that the land fund would be able to carry out the tasks tied to protection, since it possesses NEITHER THE INFORMATION NEEDED TO PROTECT THE NATURAL VALUES NOR THE EXPERTS, and held that the decision would result in a deterioration of the natural state. They also feared the parks would lose significant rental income, upsetting their budgets and further weakening the conservation infrastructure. AND THE ROSTER: 106 organisations supported the letter, published as a named list running from small county nature protection associations and civil societies to national bodies. A published list of 106 signatories is the largest single roster recorded in this file — and the three initiators went on to launch a new movement to strengthen the position of nature conservation in Hungary. A LEGAL POINT RECORDED WITH IT: transferring the managed lands to the land fund was, according to the position of the deputy commissioner for fundamental rights, unconstitutional — and the same reform gave the land fund the tasks in expropriation and PRE-EMPTION procedures that conservation bodies had performed until then.

trackers.name: NFK vételi ajánlatok — who may buy state land, and the minister who must consent
trackers.desc: THE CONSENT THAT PROTECTS A SITE, and it is the useful part: the consent of the minister responsible for nature conservation is required for the TRANSFER OF OWNERSHIP of a parcel qualifying as a PROTECTED NATURAL AREA or a NATURA 2000 AREA; likewise the water minister for a water protection area, the construction minister for a declared archaeological site or protective zone, and the forestry minister for land under the Forest Act. A protected or Natura 2000 parcel in state hands cannot change owner without the nature conservation minister agreeing — a named signature that a community can ask about, and object to. AND THE LIMITS ON WHO CAN BUY AT ALL, which decide whether your group could: a domestic natural person who is not a registered farmer may apply to acquire state-owned land only if the land they already hold, together with the land sought, does not exceed ONE HECTARE; a foreign natural person may not acquire ownership of land; and a LEGAL PERSON MAY NOT ACQUIRE OWNERSHIP OF LAND at all, so an association can apply only for land withdrawn from cultivation. In Hungary an association generally cannot own farmland — which is why the land-buying foundations recorded here matter, and why the parcel's cultivation category decides everything. A FURTHER STEP: where a parcel is under an asset management right, ownership can be transferred only if the asset management contract is terminated first, and the applicant must obtain the manager's prior consent.

trackers.name: Levegő Munkacsoport — a staffed advice service for citizens, twenty hours a week
trackers.desc: WHAT IT OFFERS, and the honest limit is stated in the same breath: in 2010, thanks to grant support, THREE COLLEAGUES received those seeking help FULL TIME — but because of cutbacks, today only ONE colleague does this work, and only TWENTY HOURS A WEEK. With citizens' support we could continue the advice at the earlier level. A staffed advice desk for members of the public is rare in this file, and this one publishes exactly how much of it is left — so a Hungarian community knows to book early and to come prepared. WHY ITS OPINION CARRIES: those working in state administration and decision-makers pay attention in numerous cases to the Levegő Munkacsoport's proposals, and its international memberships bring information that helps approach problems from many sides. AND THE ACCOUNTABILITY RECORD IT PUBLISHES, which matters when a group is choosing whom to give money to or be represented by: the tax authority and other state bodies have carried out on-site inspections at our office on numerous occasions, and found all our accounts in order. According to the State Audit Office, our management and records CAN SERVE AS A MODEL FOR OTHER CIVIL ORGANISATIONS.

trackers.name: ZöldCivil.hu and the Zöld Civil Együttműködés — a browsable list of Hungary's green groups
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a browsable directory of Hungarian green civil organisations, each with its own description and a central email address. Hungary's bucket held MME's foundations, litigators and the 106-signatory roster; this is the standing list rather than a one-off letter. WHAT THE ENTRIES SHOW, and why they are worth reading before writing to anyone: one describes itself as a team that grew from a circle of friends into an environmental association, held together by long acquaintance and similar thinking — WE GOT FED UP THAT THE DESTRUCTION OF NATURE WAS HAPPENING RIGHT UNDER OUR NOSES, AND WE ARE NOT SLOW TO ACT AGAINST IT, working through awareness-raising tours, sport and artistic works, and organising litter harvests in other towns. Another is a regional network whose mission is the conservation of biological diversity through the promotion of sustainable development, carrying out lobbying and awareness campaigns at European, regional and national level, holding trainings, and implementing LOCAL NATURE CONSERVATION PROJECTS THROUGH ITS MEMBER ORGANISATIONS. AND THE UMBRELLA BEHIND IT: a community formed of more than 100 Hungarian environmental and nature protection organisations since its founding in 1989, PRESENT IN EVERY COUNTY OF HUNGARY. An umbrella with a member in every county is how a rural Hungarian group finds someone within driving distance.

trackers.name: Ökotárs Alapítvány — a rolling ACTION GRANT with no deadline, plus mentoring
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: it helps civic initiatives with grants, CAPACITY BUILDING, MENTORING AND ADVICE, so that strong and cohesive communities are born across the country, awarding support in an OPEN COMPETITION SYSTEM based on expert review, and managing domestic corporate, European Union and other international and philanthropic foundation funds. Hungary had two funders across 25 filed entries. AND THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST TO A GROUP IN A HURRY: send in an ACTION GRANT idea — THE CALL IS CONTINUOUS, to bring social change and environmental benefit to your community with your idea. A rolling call with no closing date is the rarest funding shape in this file, and it means a community does not have to wait for a round to open. WHAT IT RUNS FOR SMALL RURAL GROUPS: a community organising programme has since 2016 supported around 50 local citizens' groups and community organisers, PRIMARILY IN SMALLER RURAL SETTLEMENTS, through training, mentoring and network-building; and a mapping programme has since 2018 helped local and regional civic networks form with SMALL-SUM DONATIONS, workshops and mentoring. AND THE PRECEDENT FOR GREEN SPACE: a long-running corporate-funded programme let local civil organisations AND CONDOMINIUM ASSOCIATIONS apply to create or renew COMMUNITY GREEN SURFACES, supporting 25–30 such projects a year. Its stated conviction: environment and community are inseparable from one another.

trackers.name: The ministry's environmental call for civil organisations — 100 per cent of eligible costs
trackers.desc: WHAT IS ON OFFER: an open ministry competition for the professional programmes and activities of CIVIL ORGANISATIONS, with 400,000,000 forint available, awards of up to 10 million forint, and — unusually — the maximum rate of support is 100 PER CENT OF ALL ELIGIBLE COSTS, as a one-off non-repayable grant. A grant needing no co-financing at all removes the barrier that stops most small associations applying — compare Croatia, where 80 per cent is the ceiling. WHO CAN APPLY: associations registered in Hungary (excluding parties, trade unions and mutual insurance associations) and foundations (excluding public and party foundations). AND THE ELIGIBLE ACTIVITIES, which are more physical than most awareness funds: alongside attitude-shaping on green waste and community composting, it names INCREASING GREEN SURFACES, converting them for environmentally friendly purposes, and RENEWING NEGLECTED GREEN AREAS by creating BIODIVERSE green surfaces to reduce the heat-island effect and improve air quality — for example PLANTING LOCAL NATIVE PLANTS IN PUBLIC SPACES, creating demonstration green roofs and green walls, and CREATING, DEVELOPING AND MAINTAINING POLLINATOR-FRIENDLY ECOSYSTEMS. Programmes to cut air pollution from local transport are also covered.

trackers.name: NFK vételi ajánlatok — the ministerial CONSENTS needed before protected state land can be sold
trackers.desc: THE CONSENT LIST, published by the land fund itself, and each line is a separate official a community can write to: the consent of THE MINISTER RESPONSIBLE FOR NATURE CONSERVATION is required for the transfer of ownership of a parcel qualifying as a PROTECTED NATURAL AREA OR A NATURA 2000 AREA; the consent of the minister responsible for water management bodies is required for the sale of a WATER PROTECTION AREA; the consent of the minister responsible for cultural heritage is required for the sale of a parcel covering a PROTECTED ARCHAEOLOGICAL SITE or its buffer zone, or qualifying as a MONUMENT; the consent of the minister responsible for forestry is required for the sale of land defined in a named section of the Forest Act. Four different ministers can each block the sale of state land, depending on what the ground holds — so establishing that a parcel is a Natura site, a water protection area, an archaeological site or forest under that section names the office with a veto. AND A FURTHER GATE: the ownership of a parcel under asset-management right can only be transferred IF THE ASSET-MANAGEMENT CONTRACT IS TERMINATED BEFORE the sale contract is concluded, so THE APPLICANT MUST OBTAIN THE ASSET MANAGER'S PRIOR CONSENT and attach it to the purchase offer. The page also states that a foreign natural person may not acquire ownership of land, and that a domestic person who is not a registered farmer may apply only if their holding, together with the land sought, does not exceed 1 HECTARE.

trackers.name: Termeszetvedelem.hu — state protected land can leave state hands ONLY BY EQUAL-VALUE EXCHANGE
trackers.desc: THE RULE THAT PROTECTS HUNGARIAN PUBLIC LAND FROM DISPOSAL, published on the state nature conservation site: a protected natural area in STATE OWNERSHIP may leave state ownership ONLY BY EXCHANGE, IN THE INTEREST OF NATURE CONSERVATION, WITH THE SIMULTANEOUS TRANSFER INTO STATE OWNERSHIP OF AN EXCHANGE PROPERTY OF AT LEAST EQUAL NATURE-CONSERVATION VALUE. Hungary is joint-smallest bucket in this file. Protected state land cannot simply be sold to a developer — something of equal conservation value must come back in exchange, and that equivalence is a thing a community can contest. AND THE MINISTERIAL GATE ON TOP: the exchange requires THE PRIOR CONSENTING DECLARATION OF THE MINISTER RESPONSIBLE FOR NATURE CONSERVATION, and the request must identify the properties affected BY LAND REGISTRY NUMBER and, WHERE POSSIBLE, REFER TO THE NATURE-CONSERVATION VALUE EQUIVALENCE between them. A named minister must sign, and the parcels must be listed by registry number — both checkable on the public record. AND THE ROUTE FOR A SYMPATHETIC COUNCIL: a MUNICIPALITY may acquire ownership of a state-owned protected natural area of LOCAL OR NATIONAL importance ONLY WITH THE CONSENT OF THE CURRENT ASSET MANAGER — so the council can take title, but the existing manager holds a veto worth knowing about before the ask is made.

trackers.name: The 106-organisation defence of national park land — when 50,000 hectares were to be moved
trackers.desc: WHAT A HUNGARIAN COALITION LOOKED LIKE WHEN IT MATTERED: ONE HUNDRED AND SIX CIVIL ORGANISATIONS joined the initiative of the national nature-conservation organisations, asking for a favourable government decision to forestall the further weakening of the position of nature conservation. AND WHAT WAS AT STAKE: a government decision process under which THE ASSET MANAGEMENT OF 50,000 HECTARES OF PROTECTED AREA could pass FROM THE NATIONAL PARK DIRECTORATES TO THE NATIONAL LAND FUND MANAGEMENT ORGANISATION. AND THE ARGUMENT THE THREE LARGEST BODIES MADE, in a dated letter to the government: they saw NO GUARANTEE WHATEVER that the land fund would be able to carry out the tasks tied to protection on protected areas, SINCE IT POSSESSES NEITHER THE INFORMATION NOR THE EXPERTS necessary for protecting natural values, and held that the decision WILL RESULT IN THE DETERIORATION OF THE NATURAL STATE. Whether the body taking over has the experts and the data is the argument to make when land is moved between agencies — and the piece names all 106 signatories, which is a ready-made list of Hungarian organisations willing to sign onto someone else's fight.

trackers.name: TASZ on fighting PRIORITY INVESTMENTS — who to ring when the rules have been overridden
trackers.desc: THE SITUATION THIS ADDRESSES, which is the hardest version of a development fight: THE GOVERNMENT DECREE DESCRIBING INVESTMENTS OF PRIORITY IMPORTANCE FROM A NATIONAL-ECONOMY POINT OF VIEW OVERRIDES NATIONAL AND LOCAL RULES IN THE INTEREST OF THE INVESTMENT BEING REALISED, AND SHORTENS THE TIME OF THE PERMITTING PROCEDURES. NATURE-DAMAGING PROJECTS ARE OFTEN CLASSIFIED AS PRIORITY INVESTMENTS SO THAT THEY CAN BE BUILT FASTER AND MORE EASILY — BUT EVEN THEN YOU CAN ACT AGAINST THEM. Hungary is joint-smallest bucket in this file. Being designated a priority investment is not the end of a case — and this is a rights organisation saying so in a public how-to. AND WHO TO APPROACH, with the division of labour set out: LOCAL ENVIRONMENTAL ORGANISATIONS KNOW THE MOST ABOUT THE LOCAL NATURE THEY PROTECT, AND HAVE EXPERIENCE IN HOW THE LOCAL COUNCIL AND THE GOVERNMENT OFFICE CAN EFFECTIVELY BE REACHED. THE NATIONAL GREEN ORGANISATIONS HAVE GREAT EXPERIENCE, TAKE PART IN THE WORK OF INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATIONS AND POSSESS SERIOUS LEGAL EXPERTISE. One national body is named as DEALING EXPRESSLY WITH ENVIRONMENTAL LEGAL ASSISTANCE, and the advice is blunt: IT IS WORTH TURNING TO BOTH THE LOCAL AND THE NATIONAL-LEVEL ORGANISATIONS. Local groups know the ground and the officials; national ones bring the lawyers — and the guide says to use both rather than choose. It also carries a worked case: a coastal association whose mission is MAKING THE LAKE SHORE A COMMON TREASURE, where locals have fought FOR SEVERAL DECADES to recover a shoreline expropriated as a party resort.

trackers.name: The KÖTHÁLÓ advice network — 14 members covering the whole country, offering REPRESENTATION
trackers.desc: A NATIONAL NETWORK BUILT FOR EXACTLY THIS, and the coverage is the point: since 1997 it has linked TOGETHER THOSE GREEN CIVIL ORGANISATIONS THAT DEAL PARTICULARLY WITH ENVIRONMENTAL ADVICE. THE NETWORK'S 14 DOMESTIC MEMBERS COVER THE WHOLE TERRITORY OF HUNGARY. Fourteen advice centres between them covering every part of the country means no Hungarian village is out of reach of one — the same test Kosovo's fourteen mobile offices passed in batch516. AND WHAT IT ACTUALLY PROVIDES, which is more than most advice lines: TO SUPPORT LOCAL RESIDENTS, WITH THE HELP OF THEIR ADVISERS, IN GETTING TO INFORMATION AS SOON AS POSSIBLE, and ALONGSIDE LEGAL ADVICE, TO PROVIDE LEGAL REPRESENTATION FOR ENVIRONMENTAL LAW ENFORCEMENT. Representation, not merely advice, is the line that separates a service that explains your problem from one that carries it. AND THE RANGE OF EXPERTISE THE PAGE CLAIMS FOR THEM: THEIR PROFESSIONAL COMPETENCE IS AMONG THEIR OUTSTANDING VALUES; AN ORGANIC PART OF THEIR WORK IS THEIR ECONOMIC, LEGAL, SETTLEMENT-DEVELOPMENT, ARCHITECTURAL, TRANSPORT, AGRICULTURAL-ENGINEERING, BIOLOGICAL, CHEMICAL AND OTHER KNOWLEDGE. Settlement-development and architecture sit in the same list as law — which is the combination a planning objection needs and rarely gets from one source.

trackers.name: Hungary's largest conservation membership body — 10,000 members, and who it works with
trackers.desc: THE BIGGEST CIVIL CONSERVATION BODY IN THE COUNTRY, and the list of who it deals with is what makes it useful to a village: founded in 1974, it is OUR COUNTRY'S LARGEST NATURE CONSERVATION CIVIL ORGANISATION, NUMBERING APPROXIMATELY 10,000 MEMBERS, and TO THIS END IT COOPERATES WITH THE POPULATION, WITH THE LOCAL AUTHORITIES, WITH FARMERS AND WITH STATE NATURE CONSERVATION.
