Hungary is among the least-worked buckets in this file. Farmers and local councils are named as partners alongside residents and the state — which matters because a development fight usually needs the farmer next door more than it needs a ministry. AND WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES ON THE GROUND, done by members rather than staff: WITH THEIR VOLUNTEERS THEY CARRY OUT RESEARCH AND PROTECTION ACTIONS, HOLD EDUCATIONAL LECTURES, ORGANISE CAMPS AND PUBLISH MATERIALS. Research carried out by volunteers is the survey evidence a small group cannot otherwise afford, which is the same answer recorded for Greece in batch607 and Australia in batch506. It also supports NATURE CONSERVATION BY RESIDENTS AROUND THE HOUSE with published guides and equipment.

trackers.name: The 1% tax designation — and what a Hungarian group publishes so you can give it
trackers.desc: THE FUNDING ROUTE EVERY HUNGARIAN TAXPAYER ALREADY HAS, published in the form needed to use it: the organisation lists its TAX NUMBER and offers THE PRINTABLE 1% DECLARATION FOR DOWNLOAD, alongside its street address. Hungary is among the least-worked buckets in this file. One per cent of income tax, redirected by a form, costs the giver nothing they would otherwise keep — the cheapest funding any local group can ask a village for, and the same mechanism the Moldovan beneficiary list in batch546 exists to serve. AND WHAT THE MONEY BUYS, from the published activity list: SPECIES-PROTECTION AND AREA-PROTECTION PROGRAMMES; AREA, HABITAT, SPECIES AND BIRD PROTECTION PROGRAMMES LED BY THE LOCAL GROUPS; and EXPERT ADVICE — ASSISTANCE TO THE NATURE-PROTECTION ACTIVITY OF STATE AND MUNICIPAL BODIES, AS WELL AS OF FARMING AND SOCIAL ORGANISATIONS. Area protection is run by the local groups, not from the centre — so a community approaches the county branch, and OUR LOCAL GROUPS MAINTAIN SEVERAL HUNDRED NEST BOXES AND HABITATS NATIONWIDE. Its centrally organised programmes TOUCH THE WHOLE TERRITORY OF THE COUNTRY.

trackers.name: Office for Personal Data Protection (SR)
trackers.desc: Office for Personal Data Protection (SR) — Slovakia’s independent data-protection / information commissioner, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Otvorené súdy (Open Courts)
trackers.desc: Civic project publishing Slovak court decisions, judge profiles and court performance data. · Find here: a civil-society database profiling Slovak judges and their decisions (Otvorené súdy).

trackers.name: VIA IURIS — Občan (public participation & environmental litigation)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Slovak public-interest law association behind the Pezinok landfill case that won a Goldman Environmental Prize, with a long litigation record for communities and conservation NGOs — small hydro plants on the Hron struck down, an unlawfully sited quarry expansion at Ludrová reopened, the Detva cyanide gold mine defeated, Banská Bystrica's zoning plan challenged, the Triblavina junction changes stopped. Publishes free manuals on participating in siting and building permit proceedings, EIA, and access to information. WHO IT SUITS: residents or a civic association trying to become a party to a permit or zoning proceeding, or facing intimidation for defending the public interest.

trackers.name: Justice and Environment — European green-law network
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the European network of environmental-law NGOs, whose national member here is VIA IURIS. Its fifteen members act as the environmental-law service point in their own countries, taking cases and intervening in legislative processes, while the network defends communities and nature in court and lodges infringement complaints against member-state governments. Its standing themes are access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, environmental assessment and pollution control. WHO IT SUITS: anyone who does not yet know which lawyer to call — knock on VIA IURIS's door first, and use the network only if your problem crosses a border. The network itself does not take individual cases; its members do. YOUR NATIONAL MEMBER IS VIA IURIS (viaiuris.sk) — go to them, not to the network. J&E members serve as environmental law ‘service points’ in their countries, handling cases, participating in legislative processes and sometimes providing legal analyses and consultations for national governments. The network has 11 full and 4 associate members, and can launch infringement proceedings against faulty governments — a route a national body alone does not have. CURRENT SCOPE: access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, climate, environmental assessments, and the Environmental Liability Directive. It previously worked on waste, transport, health and Natura 2000, so an older document may overstate what it covers today.

trackers.name: Slovakia Business Register (company register)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (official company register); Slovakia Business Register (company register) — the official register of companies and legal entities in Slovakia — the primary public record of corporate existence, ownership, directors and filings. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM A BENEFICIAL-OWNERSHIP REGISTER: this shows the registered entity, its directors and filings; where a separate beneficial-ownership register exists, use that to reach the real humans behind a shell company.

trackers.name: data.gov.sk
trackers.desc: National — Slovak Republic open data portal. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Slovakia.

trackers.name: Register of legal entities (RPO)
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Publicly searchable.

trackers.name: Register of Public Sector Partners (RPVS)
trackers.desc: Slovakia's public register of the beneficial owners of any company doing business with the state. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their conflicts of interest with the state; who really owns and controls them.

trackers.name: Register of Public Sector Partners (RPVS)
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Publicly searchable.

trackers.name: Statistical Office of the Slovak Republic
trackers.desc: Slovakia's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Slovakia.

trackers.name: Investigative Center of Ján Kuciak (ICJK)
trackers.desc: Slovak investigative center probing money laundering, organized crime and abuse of public funds.

trackers.name: National Council – Asset Declarations
trackers.desc: Legislator / public-official financial interest & asset declarations.

trackers.name: Business Register on Internet
trackers.desc: Company / business register of Slovakia — official registry of legal entities.

trackers.name: UVO / EVO
trackers.desc: Slovakia's public-procurement office and electronic platform. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Slovakia, and for how much.

trackers.name: Environmentálny fond — grants up to EUR 200,000, and the procurement trap
trackers.desc: SLOVAKIA'S STATE ENVIRONMENTAL FUND, created by Act 587/2004 Z. z. and administered by the environment ministry, gives grants and loans. Oblasť D funds nature, biodiversity and landscape protection — natural species composition of ecosystems, management of invasive non-native species, measures for favourable status of protected species, wetland restoration, monitoring of species and habitats, breeding and rehabilitation stations, and prevention of brown bear damage. ELIGIBLE: municipalities, self-governing regions, občianske združenia, interest associations, foundations and non-profits, with support up to EUR 200,000 and about EUR 1.16 million allocated. THE TRAP TO PLAN FOR: public procurement is not required when you apply — but if the grant is approved, the support contract cannot be concluded without documents proving procurement was carried out, with the deadline and scope set out in the notice sent with the minister's decision. A small group can therefore apply without having run a procurement, but must be able to run one quickly afterwards. Prepare for it before the award, not after.

trackers.name: Program ochrany prírody — open to individuals, for hands-on work
trackers.desc: A SMALL-GRANT ROUTE OPEN TO NATURAL PERSONS, not only organisations — run by the Environmentálny fond with ŠOP SR. Funded work is deliberately hands-on: mowing, removal of successional woody growth, removal of invasive plants, treatment of protected trees, making and placing nesting platforms and bird boxes, creating amphibian breeding sites, and green infrastructure elements — alongside strands for nature-protection infrastructure, sustainable tourism and environmental education. CHECK THIS CONDITION FIRST: these activities may be carried out on land where no economic activity is performed. CEILINGS: EUR 5,000 for natural persons, municipalities, civic associations, foundations and non-profits; EUR 8,000 for micro-regional associations of municipalities. Worked examples include rebuilding an educational trail in a bird protection area, improving roosting and nesting for bats and birds, and tree care in a protected area. AND KNOW WHO HOLDS THE GROUND: ŠOP SR is only marginally an owner or lessee in Natura 2000 areas — management is done by Lesy SR, Vojenské lesy, the Slovenský pozemkový fond, Slovenský vodohospodársky podnik and NGOs. The body designating protection is usually not the body holding the land.

trackers.name: Unknown-owner parcels — how a municipality can secure them
trackers.desc: A REAL ROUTE FOR ABANDONED OR UNTRACEABLE LAND. Where a parcel has an unknown owner, administration by the Slovenský pozemkový fond can be recorded on the application of the municipality — supported by a residence confirmation from the Interior Ministry and a confirmation from the municipality that it holds no registered residence for that person. ONCE SPF ADMINISTRATION IS ENTERED ON THE TITLE DEED, the land may be leased to the municipality to create a green or rest zone, or ownership transferred for consideration — but only if its public-benefit use appears in the municipal land use plan (územný plán). So get the intended use into the územný plán first: without it the transfer route is closed, and with it an ownerless parcel can be brought into public green use rather than sitting available for development.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Lesoochranárske zoskupenie VLK — buys forest with small donations (Slovakia)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a Slovak forest-protection association which buys threatened forest outright using small public donations, through a standing campaign called Kúp si svoj strom — buy your own tree. It began in 1997 with an effort to save fir and beech forest in the Čergov range in eastern Slovakia. The first block, 21.24 hectares, was bought from its owner with 1,822 separate contributions from donors in nineteen countries, and it is now the association's own property. Across Čergov it has since bought close to 138 hectares. WHAT HAPPENS TO THE LAND AFTERWARDS, WHICH IS THE PART TO UNDERSTAND: in 2004 the whole of that first block was declared the private nature reserve Vlčia, carrying the fifth and highest degree of protection under Slovak law. A community here does not need the state to own the ground to get the strongest protection on it — a private association holding the title can reach the same level. AND IT PUBLISHES THE TITLE: the parcels making up Vlčia are listed on deed number 510, cadastral area Olejníkov, district Sabinov. Very few organisations anywhere in this file give the land-registry reference for what they hold. It means a donor, a journalist or a sceptical neighbour can verify the ownership in the cadastre rather than take the claim on trust, and it is the answer to the accusation that a conservation body is not really buying anything. USE IT: bring it a specific block with a willing seller in the Slovak forest belt, and expect the money to be raised from many small donors rather than found in a fund. That is how every purchase here has worked.

trackers.name: Nadácia Ekopolis — Slovak Environmental Partnership Foundation
trackers.desc: WHAT THE CONSORTIUM IS: the Environmental Partnership Association, headquartered in Brno, is a consortium of six independent national foundations in central and eastern Europe that give grants to community projects protecting the environment. It grew out of a programme begun in 1990 by the C.S. Mott Foundation, the German Marshall Fund and the Rockefeller Brothers Fund, and the national foundations were established as independent bodies in the early 1990s. Alongside grants they run education programmes, provide professional services and build the capacity of civic initiatives — which is the part a new local group needs most. THE SLOVAK MEMBER: Nadácia Ekopolis, founded 1991, at ekopolis.sk. Slovakia already has a forest buyer and two legal allies in this file but no funder; this is the gap it fills. Approach it for the money to do the survey, the campaign or the site work that a case needs, and ask specifically about capacity building if your group has just formed. SOURCING: the consortium and its six national foundations are documented on the Environmental Partnership Association's own site; the national figures and founding dates come from consortium and partner material rather than each foundation's own pages. Confirm current grant rounds with the national foundation directly.

trackers.name: SOS/BirdLife Slovensko — buys and leases land, runs the bird database, and guards sites
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: Slovakia's main bird conservation organisation, a civic association whose mission is the protection and research of nature, especially wild birds and their habitats. It continues the Czechoslovak Ornithological Society founded 1926, took its present form in 2006, and has more than 1,000 members and over 4,000 sympathisers with a staff of around ten. Slovakia's bucket held two legal bodies, a forest-buying group and a funder — and nothing holding the species record. IT BUYS AND LEASES: its stated mission includes helping birds through the purchase and protection of land, wetland restoration, care for territories, planting and guarding sites (stráženie území). Concretely it has bought more than 80 hectares of wetland in the Senné IBA/SPA — the most important breeding site for some waterbirds in Slovakia and the most important stopover for migrating waders — and leased more than 150 hectares of taiga forest in the Horná Orava IBA/SPA, an important black stork breeding site. Leasing is the cheaper instrument and it is being used at scale. THE DATA: Aves symfony is its unified online database system, through which it collects and assembles data on bird distribution across the whole of Slovakia. It runs the Common Bird Census, the Waterbird Census, voluntary IBA monitoring and other schemes, and campaigns for all Slovak Important Bird Areas to be given EU Special Protection Area status — the record-then-designate chain again. It shares databases with Czech colleagues. WHERE TO FIND IT ON THE GROUND: its field base is the Avescentrum at Senné, where members meet and it runs volunteer camps, excursions and bird monitoring; it has also built observation towers, information boards and trails at Senianske rybníky, Medzibodrožie, Žitavský luh, Zúgov near Nové Zámky and Záhorie. FUNDING NOTE FOR SLOVAK READERS: it is eligible for the 2% tax designation, which is a way to direct money to it at no cost to yourself.

trackers.name: Slovakia's four platforms — and the 50 organisations that signed the Slatinka declaration
trackers.desc: THE STRUCTURE, BECAUSE SLOVAKIA HAS FOUR PLATFORMS RATHER THAN ONE: Ekofórum, a network of environmental NGOs bound by an agreement defining a shared value and communication space — described variously as 20, 22, 23 and 24 organisations, and holding representation on the government council for non-governmental organisations; Špirála, the nationwide network for environmental education whose members include CEA, ŽIVICA, DAPHNE and SOSNA; the Klimatická koalícia; and the Slovenský ochranársky snem, formed in 2015 as a grouping of activists, scientists, experts, politicians and figures from media and the arts. THE MOMENT THAT SHOWS THEM ACTING TOGETHER: on Earth Day 2024 at Slatinka pod Poľanou, 50 environmental non-governmental organisations jointly published the Slatinka declaration of nature protectors, supported by more than 130 public figures, issued in the name of Ekofórum, the Klimatická koalícia, Špirála and the ochranársky snem together. Its message: they will protect Slovak nature, landscape, people's health and their own community from the destruction and disintegration threatening them, and will stand firmly side by side. A separate gathering brought over 500 representatives of Slovak civil society representing 411 of the largest organisations. WHY THAT MATTERS TO A COMMUNITY: a joint declaration is a signature list, and a 50-name one issued by four platforms is the closest thing Slovakia has to a single directory of its environmental sector. Read the signatories and match one to your ground. AND THE HONEST ASSESSMENT, from a state-commissioned study of the sector: the joint activities of the Ekofórum network have in recent years been subdued, and the organisations cooperate more on individual cases. The same study records that in supporting environmental organisations through public finance the state has, throughout the existence of the Slovak Republic, failed. Expect case-by-case cooperation rather than a standing coalition, and expect the money to be thin.

trackers.name: Judikáty.info — the Slovak case-law search, and the test for who is a party
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a searchable Slovak case-law database indexed by subject term — 'účastník stavebného konania' (party to building proceedings), 'stavebné povolenie', 'zrušenie stavebného povolenia' — returning Supreme Court and Constitutional Court decisions with their právna veta, the legal holding, and the statutes in force. Slovakia had two legal networks filed and no way to check what has actually been decided. THE HOLDING THAT DECIDES WHETHER YOU CAN ACT: to assess whether a natural or legal person should have been a party to building proceedings, one must examine whether carrying out the construction under the building permit CREATES THE POSSIBILITY of affecting ownership or other rights to land and buildings — and it is NOT necessary to examine a real, factual interference with those rights. The possibility of effect is enough; you do not have to prove harm has already happened. AND TWO MORE ROUTES RECORDED THERE: review of a decision outside the appeal procedure under the administrative code is a supervisory remedy that can extend to all kinds of decisions issued in administrative proceedings; and where authorities are inactive without serious reason, the code gives natural and legal persons a route to seek judicial protection of the right to have a matter dealt with without unnecessary delay. PRACTICAL: appeals against a decision run within 15 days of its delivery; and where appeals are lodged, the building office must notify the other parties and invite them to comment — in one published case within 15 days.

trackers.name: Slovak stavebné právo practices — the same firms that draft objections also file them
trackers.desc: WHAT THEY DO, from a Slovak construction-law practice's own service list: EIA — assessment of environmental impacts; withdrawal of land from the agricultural land fund and other administrative proceedings connected with preparing construction; submissions to the building office including applications for building permits, territorial decisions and binding opinions; and — the part that matters to a neighbour — drafting and lodging OBJECTIONS AND APPEALS against decisions of the building office, plus attendance at hearings. AND ONE SERVICE THAT CUTS BOTH WAYS: proposals for agreements between parties to the proceedings — for example investor and neighbour. A negotiated agreement is a named service here, not an admission of defeat; where a community cannot stop a scheme outright, the same practice will paper the conditions it can extract. A CAUTION, RECORDED PLAINLY: these firms act for developers as well — the same list covers contracts with designers and suppliers, easements and access rights, and defending an investor's interests before the building office. Check for conflicts before instructing.

trackers.name: Súkromné chránené územie — an owner can have their own land declared a private reserve
trackers.desc: THE ROUTE, AND IT IS THE OWNER'S TO TAKE: the owner of land which meets the conditions laid down by the nature protection act for a protected area, nature reserve or natural monument, and which has NOT YET been declared protected, may — ON THE BASIS OF A SUBMITTED PROTECTION PROJECT — ask the district office at the seat of the region to declare a PRIVATE protected area, private nature reserve or private natural monument. Slovakia's bucket had two land-buying organisations, funders and lawyers but no designation route; this is it. WHO DECIDES AND WHAT IT COSTS: the declaring authority is the district office at the seat of the region, NOT the government; the applicant submits a protection project drawn up under the decree, which should be done by a professionally competent person; the area is given a degree of protection according to what the site requires AND WHAT THE OWNER CHOOSES; and, in the words of the state conservation body's director of the nature protection section, there should be nothing to pay for the declaration. THE OWNER'S TWO OBLIGATIONS, stated plainly: the owner marks the territory at their own cost, and must do so within six months of the declaration. And because the declaration is on the owner's own land, no chapters on compensation for restriction of ordinary management are drawn up. HOW RARE IT STILL IS — which is the opening: by 2020 only three private nature reserves had been declared, and the first private protected area followed in 2021. A buffer zone can also be declared, but only if the applicant owns it too or the affected owners consent, and the applicant must obtain that consent.

trackers.name: Obecné chránené územie and the zones — what a Slovak municipality can declare, and what the letters mean
trackers.desc: THE MUNICIPAL POWER: an amendment introduced the possibility for a MUNICIPALITY to declare a municipal protected area in its own cadastral territory, or — by agreement between municipalities — across several cadastral territories. Two councils can protect a site that straddles their boundary without going to the ministry, which is the shortest route recorded for Slovakia. AND THE ZONING SYSTEM, because it decides what may happen where: zones are delimited as whole parts of a protected area according to the nature of the values in them, the originality of the ecosystems, the degree of human intervention and the use of the territory, so that the FIFTH degree of protection is in zone A, the fourth in zone B, the third in zone C and the second in zone D — and zones may be divided into sub-zones. Ask which zone your ground falls in; the letter is the protection level. PROGRESS AND THE OBSTACLE, RECORDED PLAINLY: by the end of 2025 zonation had been declared for six large protected areas — named — and for 40 small ones. But zonation of protected areas is complicated by ownership relations to forest land, and small protected areas that become part of declared zones of a landscape area or national park are always abolished. A SEPARATE ROUTE NAMED IN THE SAME REFORM: the state may EXCHANGE private land inside protected areas for its own land.

trackers.name: Združenie domových samospráv — it makes residents PARTIES to the permitting process
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES, in its own words, and it is the most precisely useful offer in the Slovak bucket: we try to help the inhabitants of towns and villages across the whole of Slovakia to become EQUAL PARTNERS to the local and public administration, and so to become — DIRECTLY OR THROUGH OUR ASSOCIATION — PARTICIPANTS IN PROCEEDINGS in environmental impact assessment and in PERMITTING PROCESSES. An association that will carry your standing for you, where you cannot get it yourself, is what this file has been looking for in every country — and it operates nationwide. AND THE THREE KINDS OF HELP IT NAMES, in order: we help them regain the confidence and respect that was often not shown to them; we help them with THE EXPERT SIDE, so that their submissions are QUALIFIED; and finally we help them with THE LEGAL FRAMEWORK by means of which they can achieve their aims far more effectively. ITS STATED POSITION, worth quoting in a Slovak submission: we maintain that the interest in a quality living environment is paramount, and that other interests — personal, economic, political and commercial — must be subordinated to it. It fights alongside residents for their right to comment on prepared projects and pushes solutions in the public interest of the inhabitants of the affected municipalities.

trackers.name: The Slovak občianske združenia catalogue — find the group already fighting near you
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a browsable national catalogue of Slovak civic associations — nearly 2,800 listed under this heading alone — each with its own website, STREET ADDRESS and contact details, filterable by category and locality. Slovakia had funders, litigators and land buyers filed but no way to find the neighbouring group. WHAT IS ACTUALLY IN IT, from the entries themselves: an association for support of nature protection in the surroundings of a named town, carrying ARTICLES, POSITIONS, PHOTOGRAPHS, A PETITION AND OFFICIAL DOCUMENTS — a fully worked local campaign, published; a non-political organisation for the protection of nature and landscape, above all the environment in a named town, and the PROTECTION AND CREATION OF GREENERY, SUBMITTING COMMENTS; and others for protection and creation of the living environment and projects for environmental protection. A local association that has already published its petition and its official documents is a template and an ally at once — and the catalogue is how a Slovak community finds the one nearest to it, or the one that fought the same developer last year. ALSO ON THE MAP: a donations platform carries an association composed of specialists devoted to the protection of GROUNDWATER AND DRINKING WATER, whose aim includes commenting on legislation and verifying water quality at as many water sources across Slovakia as possible.

trackers.name: Zelené oázy — twenty years of corporate money for looking after a valuable place
trackers.desc: WHAT IT FUNDS: a grant programme that supports the CREATION OF AND CARE FOR ENVIRONMENTALLY VALUABLE LOCALITIES WHICH SERVE THE WIDE PUBLIC, ACTIVE AND EFFECTIVE NATURE PROTECTION, and the concept of permanent sustainability. Its twentieth annual round carried 62,000 euro from a named oil company, divided among the best projects, with a published deadline and a webinar for applicants whose presentation is posted afterwards. Slovakia had two funders. Twenty consecutive years of corporate money channelled through a foundation, with an applicant webinar you can watch before writing, is about as reliable as small-grant funding gets. AND THE FRAMING OF ONE ROUND, which tells a community how to pitch: the theme 'we look after the family silver' offered support for RESCUING, RESTORING OR CARING FOR our natural, cultural and community heritage — places WITH THE POTENTIAL TO CONNECT PEOPLE, CREATE NEW RELATIONSHIPS AND STRENGTHEN LOCAL COOPERATION, restore traditions and build community spirit. WHO RUNS IT: a foundation with 25 years of experience managing grant programmes aimed at the democratisation of civil society and environmental sustainability, which supports the projects and activity of hundreds of non-governmental non-profit organisations ACCORDING TO THEIR CURRENT NEEDS — WITHOUT UNNECESSARY BUREAUCRACY. Its other programmes include People for Trees, a water competition, and a Good Neighbour grant programme supporting communities AND ACTIVE INDIVIDUALS in named city districts.

trackers.name: The Slovak corporate community grants — open to associations, SCHOOLS, towns and villages
trackers.desc: WHO CAN APPLY, and the breadth is the point: civic associations, SCHOOLS, TOWNS AND MUNICIPALITIES, and also other non-profit bodies can take part. The condition is that the project has a PUBLIC-BENEFIT CHARACTER AND A POSITIVE IMPACT ON THE ENVIRONMENT IN THE GIVEN REGION. A grant a village council and a residents' association can apply to on the same terms is worth knowing about before either of them tries alone — and the aim is to support projects that actively contribute to the protection and improvement of the state of the environment in the individual regions of Slovakia. AND WHAT ANOTHER BANK FOUNDATION'S COMMUNITY PROGRAMME LISTS AS ELIGIBLE, which reads like a menu for a local group: volunteer activities aimed at cleaning and protecting WATERCOURSES, TREES AND FORESTS; green oases; COMMUNITY ECO-GARDENS; viewpoints — restoration and creation; educational activities for children and young people; PROTECTED AREAS; observation and protection of game and birds; and beekeeping. Its stated purposes include supporting activists and volunteers with an active approach to protecting and cleaning nature, and supporting civic initiatives and active involvement in solving problems AT THE LOCAL LEVEL.

trackers.name: Lesoochranárske zoskupenie VLK — it owns and manages several reserves, and refuses all felling
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS AND WHAT IT HOLDS: a Slovak civic association registered on 22 June 1993, whose best-known project is THE FIRST PRIVATE NATURE RESERVE IN CENTRAL EUROPE, and which OWNS OR MANAGES SEVERAL NATURE RESERVES IN SLOVAKIA. It is composed of a headquarters and branches — TRIBES — named after their home area, with a named chief and a seat in a named village. AND THE STANCE THAT MAKES IT USEFUL WHERE FELLING IS THE THREAT: in one national nature reserve, logging was permitted despite the high value of the natural stand, with the knowledge of the park administration. VLK LEASED THE FORESTS FOR 40 YEARS AND, AS THE HOLDER, REFUSES ANY FELLING. A forty-year lease taken specifically to refuse the felling the state had allowed is the clearest single act in this file — and it works where purchase is impossible. AND WHAT IT HAS ENLARGED: it secured the expansion of one nature reserve FROM 52.09 TO 391.98 HECTARES; one of its branches was involved in enlarging a national nature reserve which was re-created with roughly EIGHT TIMES the area; and in 2005 it submitted a proposal for the protection of a named forest, where a nature reserve came into being. It cooperates with a foundation that owns further smaller forest parcels.

trackers.name: Environmentálny fond — the state fund, and its published list of WHO GOT THE MONEY
trackers.desc: WHAT THE FUND IS: a STATE FUND established to support the protection and creation of the environment on the principles of sustainable development, whose main task is to provide funds IN THE FORM OF GRANTS OR LOANS for projects at national, regional OR LOCAL level. Slovakia had four funding entries, all corporate or NGO. AND WHAT THIS PARTICULAR PAGE GIVES A COMMUNITY: the fund publishes AN OVERVIEW OF APPLICANTS for funds in the form of a grant, ON WHOSE SUPPORT THE MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT DECIDED, listed by area of support with, for each one, the DECISION NUMBER and date, THE APPLICANT'S NAME, THE PROJECT NAME, THE NUMBER OF POINTS AWARDED, THE SUM REQUESTED IN EURO and THE APPROVED GRANT IN EURO. A published score and the gap between what was asked for and what was granted is the clearest guide any applicant can read — it shows what scores well, and how much of a request typically survives. AND WHAT IT PAYS FOR NOW: the fund has published its specification for the year's grants under AREA D: PROTECTION OF NATURE, BIODIVERSITY AND THE LANDSCAPE, with support oriented to THE BUILDING, RENEWAL AND REVITALISATION OF GREEN INFRASTRUCTURE ELEMENTS and mitigating the negative impacts of climate change IN THE TERRITORY OF THE MUNICIPALITY. Approved projects are administered with AN ASSIGNED PROJECT MANAGER whose name and contact are given in the award letter.

trackers.name: The Program ochrany prírody — grants an INDIVIDUAL can hold, up to 8,000 EURO
trackers.desc: WHO CAN APPLY, and it is the widest eligibility recorded in this file: the nature protection programme is available to MUNICIPALITIES, ASSOCIATIONS AND INDIVIDUALS WHO CARRY OUT NON-COMMERCIAL ACTIVITY in the field of nature and landscape protection. An individual can hold this grant — no association, no registration, no waiting years, which puts it alongside the Australian auspicing rule as one of the two lowest bars in this file. AND THE AMOUNTS: the maximum grant for NATURAL PERSONS is 8,000 EURO; legal persons — municipalities, associations of municipalities or of legal persons, CIVIC ASSOCIATIONS, foundations and non-profit organisations, as well as NATIONAL PARK ADMINISTRATIONS — may apply for up to 10,000 EURO, from a call total of 200,000 EURO. AND WHAT THE MONEY BUYS, from the fund's own examples: applicants have built NEW INFORMATION PANELS on territorial and species protection of nature, supported the infrastructure of educational tourism, and built A FLIGHT AVIARY FOR INJURED BIRDS OF PREY. The programme covers three activities — PRACTICAL CARE AND MANAGEMENT of specially protected parts of nature; infrastructure and sustainable tourism in protected areas; and INFORMING AND EDUCATION about nature protection — and across four forms of support the fund allocated more than 3.5 MILLION EURO for local governments, CIVIC ASSOCIATIONS and schools.

trackers.name: The state buy-out of land in national parks — THE OWNER SETS THE PRICE, and there is 68 million euro
trackers.desc: A PUBLIC BUYER WITH REAL MONEY BEHIND IT, announced by a national park administration itself: the environment ministry LAUNCHED THE BUY-OUT OF LAND IN NATIONAL PARKS through a WEB APPLICATION, WHERE OWNERS MAY NON-BINDINGLY OFFER THEIR LAND IN A PROTECTED AREA. ALMOST 68 MILLION EURO IS SET ASIDE for the purchase of suitable land. AND THE TERM THAT MATTERS MOST TO AN OWNER: THE SELLERS DETERMINE THE PRICE THEMSELVES; a commission decides on the final purchase from the non-binding offers submitted. An owner naming their own price, without committing to sell, is the lowest-risk approach a community can put to a wavering neighbour — and the application COMMUNICATES WITH PUBLICLY AVAILABLE INFORMATION FROM THE CADASTRE, so no forms need filling. AND THE ELIGIBILITY, stated plainly so nobody wastes an application: in the first round the state buys ONLY FROM NATURAL PERSONS who are SOLE OR CO-OWNERS of land in national parks WHERE THE 3RD TO 5TH DEGREE OF NATURE PROTECTION APPLIES; and SHARES OF LAND THAT ARE COMMON IMMOVABLE PROPERTY under the named land-associations act WILL NOT BE BOUGHT. A named park officer's email and mobile number are published for enquiries.

trackers.name: Združenie domových samospráv — it makes residents PARTIES to the EIA and permitting procedures
trackers.desc: AN ASSOCIATION WHOSE STATED SERVICE IS CARRYING THE PAPERWORK FOR YOU: WE HELP YOU TO DEFINE AND ACHIEVE YOUR AIMS BEFORE THE AUTHORITIES, SO THAT YOU DO NOT HAVE TO BURDEN YOURSELVES WITH THE BUREAUCRACY ALONE. Slovakia is joint-smallest bucket in this file. Bureaucracy carried by someone else is the specific help a working household cannot supply for itself — and it is what most objections fail on. AND WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES, from its own account of its role: it extended its work of PUBLIC CONTROL AND ASSERTING THE PUBLIC INTEREST IN ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION FROM ONE CITY DISTRICT TO THE WHOLE OF SLOVAKIA, holding that THE LAW MUST APPLY TO EVERYONE AND THE INHABITANTS OF SLOVAKIA HAVE THE SAME RIGHT TO ITS OBSERVANCE in the capital or in any other named city. AND THE SENTENCE THAT DEFINES THE OFFER: WE THEREFORE TRY TO HELP THE INHABITANTS OF TOWNS AND VILLAGES THROUGHOUT SLOVAKIA TO BECOME EQUAL PARTNERS TO LOCAL AND PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION, AND SO TO BECOME, DIRECTLY OR THROUGH OUR ASSOCIATION, PARTICIPANTS IN PROCEEDINGS IN THE PROCESSES OF ASSESSING IMPACTS ON THE ENVIRONMENT AND IN PERMITTING PROCESSES. Becoming a party THROUGH an existing association, rather than founding your own, is the shortcut where a country's standing rules are strict — the reverse of Slovenia's 200-signature route in batch573. It says openly that INVESTORS, DEVELOPERS, DESIGNERS, URBANISTS AND OFFICIALS OFTEN IGNORED these needs, which is why it exists.

trackers.name: Priatelia Zeme — SPZ — help for CITIZENS AND COUNCILS facing a polluting scheme, since 1996
trackers.desc: WHAT IT LISTS AS ITS OWN WORK, and the first line is the one a threatened village needs: HELP TO CITIZENS AND LOCAL AUTHORITIES AFFECTED BY SCHEMES THAT COULD POLLUTE THEIR ENVIRONMENT, DEFENDING THEIR RIGHT TO A HEALTHY ENVIRONMENT; RESEARCH, MONITORING, THE PREPARATION OF EXPERT ANALYSES; and THE CARRYING OUT OF PRACTICAL ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIONS. Naming councils alongside citizens matters — a small municipality that wants to resist a scheme is as short of expert analysis as its residents are. AND WHAT IT IS: operating SINCE 1996 as a NON-PROFIT CIVIC ASSOCIATION protecting the environment and nature in Slovakia and in the European context, working ON STOPPING ACTIVITIES HARMFUL TO PEOPLE AND NATURE, and INDEPENDENT OF ANY GOVERNMENT, PARTY, POLITICAL OR GROUP INTERESTS. AND THE ALLIANCE BEHIND IT, which tells a community how much weight one call reaches: the national Friends of the Earth body is AN ASSOCIATION COMPOSED OF THREE CIVIC ORGANISATIONS FOR ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION, with the forest-protection group recorded in batch564 as AN ASSOCIATED MEMBER. Three national organisations and the forest-buyers in one alliance is a single introduction to most of the Slovak movement. Funding comes FROM INDIVIDUAL SUPPORTERS — PEOPLE LIKE YOU — from INDEPENDENT FOUNDATIONS and SMALL BUSINESSES.

trackers.name: Commission Nationale pour la Protection des Données (CNPD)
trackers.desc: Commission Nationale pour la Protection des Données (CNPD) — Luxembourg’s independent data-protection / information commissioner, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Justice.lu
trackers.desc: Official Luxembourg justice portal with court information and selected case law. · Find here: Luxembourg's official justice portal — courts, procedures and selected case-law.

trackers.name: Fondation Hëllef fir d'Natur (natur&ëmwelt)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: buys land. Created in 1982 as a public-utility body within natur&ëmwelt, its two stated core activities are the acquisition and the management of nature reserves — specifically the purchase of ground of high ecological value — and its reserves now cover roughly 1,650 hectares spread across the whole country, with the explicit aim of acquiring more. In a country this small that is a substantial share of the protected network. USE IT: if a wetland, orchard or grassland near you is coming up for sale, this is the body that can hold it permanently, and it takes donations and partnerships earmarked to specific acquisitions — so a community can fund a purchase it could not make itself. The wider natur&ëmwelt association alongside it runs a nature advisory service and carries the political and campaigning side, so approach the foundation for the land and the association for the fight.

trackers.name: Cour des comptes
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Luxembourg, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Superior Court of Justice of the Grand-Duchy of Luxembourg
trackers.desc: Superior Court of Justice of the Grand-Duchy of Luxembourg — supreme court (Luxembourg).

trackers.name: Marchés Publics
trackers.desc: National public-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Luxembourg, and for how much.

trackers.name: STATEC
trackers.desc: Luxembourg's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Luxembourg.

trackers.name: Cour des comptes
trackers.desc: National — Court of Audit of Luxembourg. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Luxembourg.

trackers.name: RCS (Registre de Commerce)
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Beneficial Ownership Register (RBE)
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Access restricted to authorities/obliged entities.

trackers.name: European Union Civil Service Tribunal
trackers.desc: European Union Civil Service Tribunal — tribunal in Luxembourg (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: Agrément article 72 — one status unlocks both money and the courtroom
trackers.desc: GET APPROVED FIRST; EVERYTHING ELSE FOLLOWS. Article 72 of the loi modifiée du 18 juillet 2018 on protection of nature governs the agrément of environmental associations — and that one status appears on both sides of this map's needs. FUNDING: the appel à projets for the 3rd Plan national concernant la Protection de la Nature lists eligible beneficiaries as syndicats de communes for nature protection, syndicats de parcs naturels, public establishments with environmental attributions, and ‘les associations et les organisations agréées conformément à l'article 72’, with selected projects funded from the Fonds pour la protection de l'environnement. COURT ACCESS: the reform package guarantees the right of access to a judge for approved environmental associations, in conformity with international and European law. A PROCEDURAL UPGRADE WORTH KNOWING: the recours en annulation is replaced by a recours en réformation, aligning with the ‘eau’ and ‘commodo’ laws — annulment lets a court quash and send back; reformation lets the court substitute its own decision, so the administration cannot simply re-take the same decision with better reasoning. THE COUNTERWEIGHT, STATED HONESTLY: the same package enlarges the list of construction types needing no authorisation — access improves and the permitting net loosens together. Avant-projet 8308, approved 28 July 2023.

trackers.name: Pacte Nature — 84 of 102 communes already signed, and the catalogue is public
trackers.desc: YOUR COMMUNE HAS PROBABLY ALREADY COMMITTED. Voted 14 July 2021 and running to 31 December 2030, the Pacte Nature gives communes a legislative, financial, technical and advisory framework — and more than 80 percent have signed, 84 of 102. That changes the conversation from persuading your commune to care into holding it to a commitment it has already made. HOW IT WORKS: a public catalogue of 79 concrete measures in six categories covering urban, open, aquatic and forest environments plus communication and cooperation. Certification comes at 4 levels — 40, 50, 60 and 70 percent of catalogue points — the subsidy depends on the level, and communes must improve by a set number of points each year. THE STATE PAYS FOR THE ADVISERS: communes receive funds covering the cost of Pacte Nature conseillers who help plan and implement, as well as for measures on the ground. THE LEVER FOR A RESIDENT: the catalogue is public and the scoring is transparent, so identify which of the 79 measures your commune has not taken and press for the ones that protect your site — with the state already funding the adviser to deliver them. RELATED TOOLS: the cadastre des biotopes, environmental incidence evaluation of communal PAG plans, arbres remarquables, and the zone verte / Bauperimeter distinction.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Fondation Hëllef fir d'Natur — acquisition is named first in what it does
trackers.desc: ‘The principal areas of activity of the Fondation Hëllef fir d'Natur are the ACQUISITION and management of nature reserves’ — acquisition is named first in its own description of itself. Its reserves cover about 1,400 hectares in Luxembourg and keep growing, with the stated objective of strengthening the national and European network of protected areas. Working for 30 years, it describes itself as the largest Luxembourgish environmental organisation, with specialists, geographers, biologists and engineers who draw up the management plan for each reserve — which is the technical capacity a community needs and cannot hire. APPROACH THE RIGHT DEPARTMENT: there are three — the a.s.b.l. (the association), the Foundation, which is the one that holds the land, and a wildlife care centre that takes in sick, injured and orphaned animals and animals seized or confiscated. For an acquisition, go to the Foundation, not the association. AND THERE IS A FUNDED BUYER ACTIVELY LOOKING RIGHT NOW: LIFE ArdennEislek (January 2025 to 2031), led by Natagora with the Fondation Hëllef fir d'Natur and natur&ëmwelt, will restore over 450 hectares in the Belgian and Luxembourg Ardenne — including 110 hectares of NEW ACQUISITIONS. If your site is in that area and is meadow, heath or biodiversity-rich forest, there is an EU-funded budget running now with land still to buy. A second project, LIFE ToadAlly, coordinated by Natuurpunt Beheer, covers Limburg and Liège.

trackers.name: Mouvement Écologique — the Grénge Telefon, and seven regional sections (Luxembourg)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Luxembourg's main independent environmental association, an asbl at 6 rue Vauban, L-2663 Luxembourg, +352 439030-1, meco@oeko.lu. It runs the Grénge Telefon — a green telephone line where a member of the public can ask what the law says about an environmental question and get an answer. Its own examples are exactly the everyday kind: what ecological rules must a business follow, how do I make a natural pond, what does the law say. For a country with almost nothing else in this file, that is a free first call. AND THE REGIONAL SECTIONS ARE THE POINT: it has seven — Miersch an Emgéigend, Echternach-Mullerthal, Luxembourg-Ville, Sud, Nordstad, Syrdall, Uelzechtdall — each with its own committee and named contacts, and it says that where no regional section covers your area you should write to the national office. Its stated view is that many of its goals are achieved by citizens working in the local and regional sections. WHAT IT DOES ON DEVELOPMENT: spatial planning and urbanism is one of its standing subjects, and it has published detailed case-by-case criticism of specific schemes — a filling station in open green belt beside a motorway, a housing development at Huncherange that would take a village of about 800 people to some 2,500, major residential projects at Leudelange, a shopping centre at Livange and a mixed project at Wickrange, an activity zone at Differdange/Niederkorn, and a bypass and oil reserve at Bascharage/Sanem cutting through a European-level protected area. Its argument in each case is that the scheme contradicts the government's own spatial planning guidelines. That is the frame to bring it: not that a project is undesirable, but that it departs from the state's own stated policy. IT ESCALATES TO BRUSSELS: with natur&ëmwelt — already in this file as Luxembourg's land-owning foundation — it has jointly filed complaints against the Luxembourg government with the European Commission over loss of protected habitats and species. The two organisations work together, and a Luxembourg community should treat them as a pair. WHAT IT IS NOT: not a law firm and not a land buyer. Advice, positions, complaints and local sections.

trackers.name: Œuvre Nationale — lottery-funded, with Environment as a standing field (Luxembourg)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a public establishment under the tutelage of the Ministry of State, financed almost entirely by the Loterie Nationale, created at Christmas 1944 by Grande-Duchess Charlotte to help victims of the Second World War and now the central philanthropic actor in Luxembourg. It organises and finances projects of general interest in five standing fields: Social, Culture, Environnement, Sport & Santé, and Mémoire & Patrimoine. Luxembourg had no funder in this file. THE ROUTE THAT FITS A LAND CASE: the demande d'aide ponctuelle — a one-off support request, addressed to any organisation wishing to finance or co-finance a concrete project limited in time. Any asbl, foundation or société d'impact sociétal operating at national level can request financing for a concrete, time-limited project with social impact in those five fields. Legal form is required — an unincorporated residents' group must incorporate or find a partner. THE EVIDENCE THAT IT PAYS FOR LAND, which is why it is filed here rather than as a general charity funder: it supported the Koulbich valley work of Luxembourg's land-buying foundation, where 2024 saw 18.5 additional hectares acquired, including a large tract of deciduous forest and several ponds for restoration, toward a target of 30 hectares to complete the reserve. A Luxembourgish community that has found a willing seller has, in this body, a funder with a demonstrated record of paying for the parcels. HOW IT WORKS BESIDES GIVING MONEY: it describes itself as a facilitator and intermediary, launching appels à projets and supporting initiatives coming directly from the ground, and it convenes the sector through exchanges, conferences, thematic days and training. Its impartial position lets it coordinate between stakeholders, and the guidelines for its initiatives come out of those exchanges. Telling it what is missing is part of how its calls get written. SCALE, FOR CALIBRATION: its themed calls have carried envelopes such as €250,000 for one programme and €2,000,000 for another, with individual funds capped at figures like €25,000. Watch the appels à projets page for an Environment-facing call.

trackers.name: Méco's sections régionales — they intervene in your commune's land-use plan
trackers.desc: THE LINE THAT MAKES THIS AN ENTRY: the Mouvement Écologique is represented on the ground in different regions of the country, and among the activities on its regional and local sections' agenda are interventions in the framework of the establishment of the plans d'occupation du sol — the land-use plans — and suggestions for the development of the region. Intervening in the commune's land-use plan is precisely the moment a land-loss fight is won or lost, and there is a section that does it. WHERE THEY ARE: seven named regional sections — Miersch an Emgéigend, Echternach-Mullerthal, Luxembourg-Ville, Sud, Nordstad, Syrdall and Uelzechtdall — each with its own comité and published activities, plus eight local sections. The site says the sections welcome any collaboration and invites you to contact the people responsible for your region; and if there is no section where you are, to write to the national office: 6 rue Vauban, L-2663 Luxembourg, meco@oeko.lu, +352 439030-1. ONE SECTION'S SCOPE, AS AN EXAMPLE OF HOW LOCAL THIS GETS: the Stad Lëtzebuerg section focuses exclusively on the commune of Luxembourg city and its individual quarters, working on the tram and on concrete development projects in the quarters, with a named contact. TWO STRUCTURAL FACTS WORTH KNOWING: members may group themselves into local and regional sections and working groups, and a conseil consultatif of section and working-group heads must be convened within a month at the request of a single regional section or national working group, with the board obliged to rule on its proposals within fifteen days — so a local section can force a national decision. And no office-holder of a political party may sit on the board or on a regional, local or working-group committee. AND THE OTHER LUXEMBOURG NETWORK: natur&ëmwelt a.s.b.l. — already in this file — has more than 9,000 members distributed across local or thematic sections which autonomously organise excursions and nature protection work in their own region.

trackers.name: Portail national des enquêtes publiques — and the warning printed on it
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: Luxembourg's national portal listing public inquiries on établissements classés — the commodo/incommodo permits — with the file number, the object of the authorisation request, the authority organising the inquiry and the one following the dossier, and the legal articles engaged. Real entries include a fuel depot with transformer stations and refrigeration installations, and a multipurpose hall. THE WARNING PRINTED ON THE PORTAL, WHICH IS WHY THIS ENTRY MATTERS: the posting on the national portal is for information only. The legally operative publication is the notice displayed in the commune in the usual way by the communal authority, and from the day of that display the complete file is deposited at the maison communale and may be consulted there by all interested parties during the display period. Watch the commune's own noticeboard, not the national site. HOW TO OBJECT, IN TWO FORMS: any written observation against the project must be addressed to the collège des bourgmestre et échevins of the commune where the installation is sited. Any oral observation is made to that commune at the enquête de commodo et incommodo, whose date is given on the publication notice. After 15 days the mayor collects the written observations and holds the inquiry, at which all interested persons who present themselves are heard. The inquiry must be closed and the decision taken no later than 30 days after the display period expires. TWO THINGS THAT FOLLOW, AND BOTH ARE USEFUL: people who submitted observations are informed of the decision by registered letter with acknowledgement of receipt from the commune. And throughout the operating life of an establishment, a copy of the authorisations issued is kept at the commune and may be freely consulted there — so you can check an existing operator against its own conditions. PRACTICAL DETAIL: applications must include a cadastral extract less than 12 months old showing neighbouring plots within 200 metres, generated from geoportail.lu; neighbouring communes within that 200-metre radius each receive a copy. Publication in at least four Luxembourg daily papers is at the applicant's expense.

trackers.name: KRIEGER Associates — a Luxembourg practice given over entirely to construction, urbanisme and environment
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: a Luxembourg firm with offices in Luxembourg and Diekirch, entirely devoted to real property, public and civil law, with reference expertise in construction law, urbanisme, ENVIRONMENT and energy, tenancy and co-ownership. Luxembourg's bucket had Méco's regional sections, the state fund route and the commodo/incommodo portal, but no practitioner. This is one, and the whole firm is in the field rather than a department of it. WHAT THAT COVERS FOR A COMMUNITY: real property law here governs relations between purchasers and sellers, and between all of those and PUBLIC ADMINISTRATIONS, promoters, contractors and architects — which is the map of who a community ends up arguing with. AND IT FOLLOWS THE COURTS PUBLICLY: the firm publishes notes on administrative rulings, including one where the Cour administrative declared itself WITHOUT JURISDICTION to hear an appeal brought against an order of the President of the Tribunal administratif. Which court can hear which appeal is itself contested in Luxembourg, and a practice that tracks it is worth more than one that does not. PRACTICAL NOTE ON FINDING OTHERS: Luxembourg's small bar is covered by regional listings of housing, construction and development lawyers by commune, and the questions those listings say a lawyer answers include receiving an administrative decision on urbanisme or environment and wanting to bring a recours, and disputes with a neighbour over a servitude or land use in a lotissement.

trackers.name: Luxembourg's ONG co-financing line and the forest aid schemes
trackers.desc: THE ENVIRONMENT MINISTRY'S NGO LINE: the state operates a system of co-financing for NGO projects, a dedicated budget article whose general objective is to encourage the activities of NGOs and public-utility FOUNDATIONS working in environmental protection at national level, through their contribution to national and Community environmental policy. Public-utility foundations are named alongside NGOs — which matters where the land-buying body is a foundation. AND THE FOREST SCHEMES, which are the practical money for wooded ground: the government runs a set of aid schemes for the forest sector grouped into four regimes, aimed at improving and strengthening forest ecosystems, including aid for the preservation of them. A CAUTION WORTH RECORDING, from the state's own investment-aid rules: the purchase of land and preparatory steps such as obtaining authorisations and carrying out feasibility studies are NOT considered the start of works — which is what lets you buy and survey before an aid decision without forfeiting eligibility. Aid there runs from 10 to 100 per cent of eligible costs depending on the scheme, is paid after completion, though one or more instalments may be released as the investments proceed.
