AND FOR ANY GROUP SEEKING STATE CO-FINANCING: Luxembourg's development-cooperation model shows the standard shape — subsidy requests must be submitted by an ORGANISATION APPROVED (agréée) by the ministry, with two calls a year. Get the agrément first.

trackers.name: SICONA — 44 member communes, machines and staff, and it will build the habitat for free
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: two inter-communal nature conservation syndicates — SICONA Sud-Ouest, an association of 21 communes for more than 30 years, and SICONA Centre with another 22 — which together encompass almost a third of the country's surface area and form the largest nature conservation organisation of its kind in Luxembourg. Luxembourg was the thinnest bucket in the file; this is the body that does the physical work. THE OFFER A RESIDENT CAN TAKE UP DIRECTLY: SICONA will lay out for you FREE OF CHARGE, with the financial help of your commune and the environment ministry, a flowering meadow, a natural pond or an orchard in the green zone. A public body that will build the habitat on your land at no cost is the most concrete offer recorded in this file, and the contact is a single email and phone number. WHAT IT HAS BEHIND IT: a regional biodiversity centre and a machine hall, from which a joint team runs planning and scientific monitoring of projects and the practical implementation of nature protection measures with a specialised machine fleet. Its aims are to protect biodiversity and landscapes and to create, maintain and manage natural habitats in the member communes, plus support and advice to communes. AND THE ROUTE IN FOR A COMMUNE THAT IS NOT A MEMBER: the long-term objective is to see them join, and SICONA also supports national nature protection through a convention with the environment ministry. Ask your commune to join — that is a council decision, not a ministerial one.

trackers.name: The Natura 2000 COPIL — the steering committee your association already sits on
trackers.desc: WHO SITS ON A LUXEMBOURG NATURA 2000 STEERING COMMITTEE, named in full: representatives of the ministries and regional services (nature and forests, water, agriculture), the 17 communes concerned — each listed by name — the inter-communal nature protection syndicate, farmers and agricultural advisers from the Chamber of Agriculture, an organic agriculture institute, the foresters' grouping, THE REGIONAL SECTIONS of natur&ëmwelt AND of the Mouvement écologique, and the regional tourism office. The regional sections of the two national environmental organisations sit on the committee for your site — so a community reaching its own regional section is reaching the table where the site is managed. AND THE OWNERSHIP FACT THAT SHAPES EVERYTHING THERE: in that Natura 2000 area private land represents more than 90 per cent of the surface and the communes 9 per cent. Designation in Luxembourg is mostly designation of other people's land, which is why the free habitat works above matter more than any purchase fund. ALSO NAMED: the Observatoire de l'environnement naturel, whose role is to help the minister and the communal syndicates define the orientations of nature protection policy and assess the state of conservation, to propose a programme of concrete actions, to evaluate measures carried out by the State and the syndicates, and to write a detailed report every two years. Its members include the foundation, the syndicate, the Mouvement écologique, the nature administration, a natural park and the natural history museum.

trackers.name: The PAG procedure — two 30-day windows, and you lose the right if you miss the first
trackers.desc: THE PLAN THAT DECIDES EVERYTHING, AND ITS CLOCKS: a modification or recasting of the plan d'aménagement général is published at the maison communale, where the public may consult it for 30 DAYS; the deposit is also published in AT LEAST FOUR NATIONAL DAILIES and on the commune's website; and any interested person then has 30 days to send written observations to the collège échevinal. AFTER THAT DEADLINE, INTERESTED PERSONS LOSE THEIR RIGHT OF CLAIM. Luxembourg joins Romania as a country where missing the window extinguishes the right, and this file has recorded the Luxembourgish permit portal's own warning that the national site is informational only. WHAT YOU GET FOR OBJECTING IN TIME: those who lodged observations will be CONVOKED FOR A HEARING, and a report is written. The communes also organise at least one INFORMATION MEETING for the population. And those who claimed during the publication period and do not obtain satisfaction from the minister may bring an annulment appeal against his decision THROUGH A LAWYER AT THE COURT. Only those who objected in time can appeal later. AND THE ENVIRONMENTAL LOCK WORTH KNOWING: where the recasting or modification of a PAG CHANGES THE DELIMITATION OF THE GREEN ZONE, the Minister of the Environment must also approve it. A green-zone boundary change needs two ministers, not one.

trackers.name: L'Œuvre Nationale — lottery money for any asbl, in five fields including Environnement
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS AND WHO CAN ASK: a public establishment financed by the National Lottery, which IDENTIFIES AND FILLS THE NEEDS NOT COVERED within our society, helping associations carry out public-interest projects in five fields — Social, ENVIRONNEMENT, Culture, Sport & Health, Memory. Luxembourg had two funders across 20 filed entries. ANY non-profit association, foundation or societal impact company working at national level can request financing for a CONCRETE, TIME-LIMITED project — and applications go through an online submission platform where an account lets you SAVE FORMS IN PROGRESS and consult requests already submitted. AND THE TWO-STAGE FORM, worth knowing before you start: the ponctual aid request has a pre-form and then the full form — so a group can test whether its idea qualifies before writing the whole application. AND WHAT IT DOES BESIDES FUNDING: it brings the actors of the field together around exchanges, conferences, THEMATIC DAYS AND TRAINING, and launches its own calls for projects. It states plainly that it responds to needs NOT COVERED BY PUBLIC FUNDS OR PRIVATE INITIATIVES — which is the gap most community campaigns fall into.

trackers.name: The Luxembourg dons-legs guide — every environmental body that can take a gift or a legacy
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a published directory whose stated purpose is to make better known the institutions, small and large, which work in many fields, giving a broad overview of their indispensable role — listed by theme, with environment as its own category. A national directory of bodies that accept donations and LEGACIES is where a community finds who can receive a gift of land or money, and Luxembourg's is public. WHAT ITS ENVIRONMENT SECTION NAMES, and the first is the one that matters: the land-holding foundation born in 1982, under the High Patronage of the Grand Duke since 2008, whose principal fields are THE ACQUISITION OF LAND OF HIGH ECOLOGICAL VALUE, the management of its nature reserves, public information, THE PUBLICATION OF SCIENTIFIC STUDIES on Luxembourg's fauna and flora, and national and international biodiversity projects — alongside the national and international bodies working in the country. AND A ROUTE RECORDED FROM A PROJECT REVIEW: besides state purchase and purchase by that foundation, BIODIVERSITY CONTRACTS are concluded through the BIOLOGICAL STATIONS, with subsidies paid for better management of sensitive areas — a limited and LATE MOWING in meadows, FENCING ALONG RIVERS AND STREAMS TO CREATE A BUFFER ZONE, the installation of grazing infrastructure. The range of action is very wide, and the communes commit through a national nature pact.

trackers.name: Fondation Hëllef fir d'Natur — 1,650 hectares owned, and the stated aim is TO ACQUIRE MORE
trackers.desc: THE HOLDING AND THE INTENTION, which together make this the land resource for Luxembourg: the foundation's reserves today cover an area of about 1,650 HECTARES, spread across the whole country. THE AIM IS TO ACQUIRE FURTHER LAND AND PROTECT IT so as to preserve nature for our generation and for future generations. A foundation that says openly it wants to buy more land is one a community can offer a threatened parcel to — and its reserves are described elsewhere as constantly growing, with the objective of STRENGTHENING THE NATIONAL AND EUROPEAN NETWORK OF PROTECTED ZONES. AND WHAT MEMBERSHIP BUYS, in its own words: as a member you contribute to the association engaging successfully for the protection of biodiversity through awareness actions, A NATURE ADVICE SERVICE, and by taking practical, scientific and political measures at local, national and international level. Its two-sided description of the work is worth borrowing: as a nature protection organisation it is a matter, on the one hand, of working concretely ON THE GROUND, and on the other of MAKING OUR VOICE HEARD AMONG POLITICAL DECISION-MAKERS. A free nature advice service attached to a landowning foundation is the cheapest expert help in the country. It employs specialists, geographers, biologists and engineers who draw up the management plan best suited to each reserve.

trackers.name: Juricaf — the free archive of Luxembourg administrative-court rulings on PAG and permits
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a free, searchable archive of Luxembourg ADMINISTRATIVE TRIBUNAL judgments, published in full text with case numbers and dates — so a resident or a lawyer can read what has already succeeded before drafting anything. A free judgment archive is the cheapest way to check whether your argument has ever won, and this file recorded the same use in Iceland, where a practitioner can be checked against decided cases. WHAT ITS RULINGS SHOW A LUXEMBOURG OBJECTOR: in one judgment the tribunal records the Ministry, faced with the great gap between the land potential provided by the draft PAG and the authorised maximum threshold, recommending that the commune develop a clear and coherent strategy to structure the phasing of territorial development, giving PRIORITY TO SURFACES WITH LOW ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT, classifying environmentally delicate land as a ZONE OF DEFERRED DEVELOPMENT, or RECLASSIFYING AS GREEN ZONE that whose impact will be difficult to mitigate or compensate — and the tribunal finds the objection well founded on this point. An objection that a commune has zoned more land than the threshold allows has already succeeded here. Another ruling shows the opposite lesson: claimants failed to specify which point of the PAG article had concretely been violated, and lost.

trackers.name: The public-private leverage — EVERY EURO spent on land can be matched by the state fund
trackers.desc: THE MECHANISM THAT DOUBLES THE MONEY, and it is the reason to give to a land fund rather than buy alone: the foundation runs a hybrid model founded on A PUBLIC-PRIVATE LEVERAGE EFFECT. EVERY EURO INVESTED IN THE ACQUISITION OF LAND CAN BE TOPPED UP BY THE FUND FOR THE PROTECTION OF THE ENVIRONMENT, which multiplies the impact of the funds collected and secures the long-term strategy. Where the state will match private money spent on buying nature, a community raising 10,000 euro is putting 20,000 into the ground. THE NUMBERS, published in its annual report: 1.167 MILLION EURO collected in one year, up almost 14 per cent — 631,000 in PRIVATE DONATIONS, 511,000 in SPONSORSHIP, against 1.026 million the year before (501,000 donations, 140,000 sponsorship, 385,000 DONATIONS AND LEGACIES). An earlier year records over 540,000 euro in donations and 305,000 IN LEGACIES from private donors, plus 400,000 in sponsorship from companies. AND WHAT IT BOUGHT WITH IT: 117.09 ADDITIONAL HECTARES acquired in one year, mainly in two named regions, taking it past 2,050 HECTARES PROTECTED in Luxembourg. In a country where land is rare and expensive, that combination makes it a central actor in long-term environmental investment.

trackers.name: Why the foundation exists — TO FILL THE GAP where nobody was buying the parcels
trackers.desc: THE FOUNDING PURPOSE, stated in one sentence, and it is the clearest statement of why a private land buyer is needed at all: the foundation was created, among others BY THE BIRD PROTECTION LEAGUE, more than 40 years ago. ITS PRINCIPAL AIM: TO MAKE UP FOR THE LACK OF INITIATIVES TO BUY AND MANAGE PARCELS, IN ORDER TO PROTECT NATURE. An existing membership organisation founding a separate body whose only job is buying land is a step any national association can take — and this file has recorded the same split in Hungary and the Netherlands. AND THE STRATEGY IT FOLLOWED, which tells a community where to point it: since the beginning of the 1980s there has been a list of SENSITIVE ZONES, progressively classified as protection zones of national interest. FROM THE OUTSET THE FOUNDATION TRIED TO BE PRESENT IN EACH OF THESE RESERVES BY BUYING CERTAIN LAND FROM PRIVATE OWNERS. Buying a foothold inside every listed sensitive zone, rather than concentrating in one, is a deliberate strategy a national body can be asked to extend to your area. It also names the ministry's own Natura 2000 coordinator and a national Natura 2000 site, and stresses that the management of the different natural environments matters both for the quality of the landscapes and FOR THE FIGHT AGAINST CLIMATE WARMING.

trackers.name: A Luxembourg ruling — a CITIZENS' INITIATIVE, a nature a.s.b.l. and the commune sued TOGETHER
trackers.desc: WHAT THE CASE SHOWS, and it is the configuration this file has recorded winning elsewhere: before the administrative tribunal, actions were brought against ministerial orders by a COMMUNAL ADMINISTRATION on one side, and on the other by A CITIZENS' INITIATIVE FOR THE COMMUNE (BIERGERINITIATIV) constituted as an a.s.b.l., a NATURE a.s.b.l., AND THE MOUVEMENT ÉCOLOGIQUE, together with others. A village initiative, a nature association, a national environmental movement and the commune itself, all in the same case — the same four-part configuration recorded as decisive in Malta. AND WHAT THEY BROUGHT: a RECOURS EN RÉFORMATION against ministerial orders issued by the Ministers of the Environment and of Labour and Employment under a named 1999 law on CLASSIFIED ESTABLISHMENTS. Because both actions were directed against the same ministerial decisions and related to the same establishment, the tribunal JOINED THEM to be decided by one and the same judgment. Separate challenges to the same permit get joined into a single case, so parallel groups need not coordinate before filing. Each side is recorded with its named advocate and the bar roll they are enrolled on — a working list of who takes this work.

trackers.name: The Luxembourg appeal rules — 40 DAYS, and THE LOSER PAYS THE COSTS
trackers.desc: THE TWO FACTS THAT SET THE RISK, published on the EU justice portal: an appeal against a decision of an administrative tribunal MUST BE LODGED WITHIN 40 DAYS, and THE LOSER WILL BE ORDERED TO PAY THE COSTS OF THE PROCEEDINGS. Loser pays is the single most important sentence a Luxembourg community can read before filing — and it is the opposite of the Finnish rule recorded two rounds ago, where winning removes the fee and legal aid removes it entirely. Where the loser pays, a group must budget for the other side's costs, not only its own. AND WHY 40 DAYS MATTERS: it is long by the standards of this file — against two months in Slovakia for a first-instance action, 15 working days in New Zealand and 30 days in Croatia's noticeboard window — but it runs from the tribunal's decision, so a group that has already lost at first instance has under six weeks to find the money and the advocate for an appeal it now knows it may have to pay for. Check who pays the costs before deciding whether to appeal, not after.

trackers.name: The convention with the ministry — nearly 440 hectares bought in four years under one agreement
trackers.desc: WHAT ONE AGREEMENT WITH A MINISTRY DELIVERED: between 2022 and 2025 ALMOST 440 HECTARES were acquired THANKS TO THE CONVENTION WITH THE MINISTRY, including 117 HECTARES IN 2025 ALONE, taking the foundation past 2,050 HECTARES PROTECTED at the start of 2026. Luxembourg is joint-smallest bucket in this file. A standing convention between a conservation foundation and the environment ministry is what turns occasional purchases into a hundred hectares a year — the agreement, not the appeal, is what a community should ask its national body about. AND HOW THE PARCELS ARE CHOSEN: the foundation states that EVERY LAND ACQUISITION IS THE SUBJECT OF CAREFUL CONSIDERATION, placing BIODIVERSITY AND ECOLOGICAL COHERENCE at the heart of each decision, with the bought land REINFORCING EXISTING RESERVES. Buying to reinforce and connect what is already protected, rather than buying isolated parcels, is the stated strategy — which tells a local group how to make its own site attractive to a national buyer. AND THE FOREST WORK THAT FOLLOWED: bark-beetle damage required SANITARY CUTS, THINNING AND SECURING MEASURES, followed by REPLANTING WITH MORE RESILIENT SPECIES, and MORE THAN 30,000 TREES were planted in a single year.

trackers.name: What 2,050 hectares actually consists of — forest, wetland, open water and ploughland
trackers.desc: THE BREAKDOWN OF A NATIONAL CONSERVATION LANDHOLDING, which is the useful part for a community wondering whether its own ground qualifies: of the total, the foundation manages 996 HECTARES OF FORESTS AND SCRUB, 641 HECTARES OF WETLANDS, 272 HECTARES OF BODIES OF WATER, and 205 OF PLOUGHLAND AND MEADOWS. Ploughland and scrub are in the portfolio alongside wetland and forest — so ordinary farmed and rough ground is bought too, not only pristine habitat. AND WHERE THE MONEY CAME FROM, in one year: more than 1.1 MILLION EUROS of PRIVATE DONATIONS AND COMPANY DONATIONS, plus ENDOWMENTS FROM THE FUND FOR THE PROTECTION OF THE ENVIRONMENT. Private giving and a public environment fund together, in roughly equal measure, is the funding model behind the purchases — and the public half is a fund a community can ask about directly. AND THE REACH: the foundation manages nature reserves THROUGHOUT THE WHOLE COUNTRY, so there is no region where a landowner is outside its scope.

trackers.name: Stëftung Hëllef fir d'Natur — its MAIN AIM is buying land, and four bodies founded it
trackers.desc: THE PURPOSE, STATED WITHOUT HEDGING: THE MAIN AIM OF THE FOUNDATION IS THE PURCHASE OF LAND, WHICH IS THEN LAID OUT AND MANAGED AS NATURE RESERVES. Luxembourg is joint-smallest bucket in this file, and this is the body behind the 2,050 hectares recorded in batch553. A foundation whose stated main aim is buying land is the first call for anyone with a parcel to save — not a body that buys occasionally when funds allow. AND HOW IT IS PAID FOR, which confirms the model: activities are FINANCED BY DONATIONS FROM PRIVATE PEOPLE, BY SPONSORS FROM THE PRIVATE ECONOMY, AND THROUGH A CONVENTION WITH THE ENVIRONMENT MINISTRY, with individual projects CO-FINANCED BY THE EUROPEAN COMMISSION under named EU programmes. The first such CONVENTION WITH THE ENVIRONMENT MINISTRY, TO REGULATE THE FINANCIAL HELP OF THE STATE, WAS SIGNED IN 1989. The state funding agreement is nearly forty years old, which is why the purchases are steady rather than occasional. AND WHO STANDS BEHIND IT: founded in 1982 and recognised as AN ORGANISATION OF PUBLIC UTILITY, it was carried until 2012 by FOUR ORGANISATIONS — a nature association, a bird-protection league, a naturalists' society and a garden-and-pond association — and in 1986 it founded, TOGETHER WITH SEVEN OTHER ASSOCIATIONS, a house-of-nature ASBL running an information centre with the capital city.

trackers.name: A Biergerinitiativ that took SEATS — two councillors and a place on every commission
trackers.desc: THE ESCALATION MOST RESIDENTS' GROUPS NEVER CONSIDER: IN 2017 THE BIERGERINITIATIV WAS FOUNDED BY SEVERAL CITIZENS FROM THE COMMUNE. THE BIERGERINITIATIV IS NOT A POLITICAL PARTY, BUT AN ASBL WHICH STANDS UP FOR THE CONCERNS OF THE INHABITANTS. AND WHAT IT DID ABOUT A PROBLEM NOBODY WOULD FIX: one of the main problems in the commune is THE TRAFFIC SITUATION, WHICH GETS WORSE FROM DAY TO DAY. FOR DECADES THE TRADITIONAL POLITICAL PARTIES HAVE PROMISED AN IMPROVEMENT, BUT IN ALL THOSE YEARS HAVE IMPLEMENTED NOTHING. THIS WAS ONE REASON WHY THE BIERGERINITIATIV STOOD AT THE LAST COMMUNAL ELECTIONS, with the aim of OFFERING THE VOTER AN ALTERNATIVE. AND THE RESULT, which is the reason this is filed as a resource rather than a story: THE BIERGERINITIATIV IS TODAY REPRESENTED BY TWO COMMUNAL COUNCILLORS ON THE COMMUNAL COUNCIL AND ALSO HAS A SEAT ON EVERY COMMUNAL COMMISSION. A residents' association that stands for election can end up inside the body that grants the permits, and on every committee that advises it — the furthest escalation available to a local group, and it took one electoral cycle. AND HOW IT KEEPS ITS MANDATE: AS A POLITICALLY INDEPENDENT VOICE, CITIZENS' ASSEMBLIES ARE ORGANISED REGULARLY TO WORK OUT PROPOSALS, WHICH ARE THEN PUT TO THE COMMUNAL COUNCIL.

trackers.name: Commissioner for Right to Information & Data Protection (IDP)
trackers.desc: Commissioner for Right to Information & Data Protection (IDP) — Albania’s national data-protection / information authority, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Albania
trackers.desc: Official site of Albania's highest court with published decisions. · Find here: information and judgments of the Supreme Court of Albania.

trackers.name: Commissioner for the Right to Information & Data Protection (IDP)
trackers.desc: National right-to-information authority (dual-mandate); Albania’s IDP Commissioner enforces the Law 119/2014 on the Right to Information — examining complaints, investigating and imposing administrative measures, Albania.

trackers.name: EcoAlbania (Qendra EcoAlbania)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Tirana organisation that brought the first environmental lawsuit ever heard in Albania's Administrative Court — and won it twice. In December 2016 it went to court against the Poçem hydropower plant on the Vjosa together with RiverWatch, EuroNatur and 38 affected residents as co-plaintiffs, arguing the environmental impact assessment was inadequate and the affected community had not been consulted, in breach of Albanian law and international conventions. The court struck the project down in 2017 and recognised the residents' standing; the Administrative Court of Appeal confirmed the annulment in 2024. Its own account calls that the case that opened the door for every environmental claim brought since. WHO IT SUITS: communities facing hydropower, and anyone whose project's paperwork is thin — the winning grounds were procedural. Worth copying its other habit too: when the government announced Vjosa protection in 2020, EcoAlbania read the actual public documents and found the designation was a protected landscape, not a national park. Always check which status was really granted.

trackers.name: Public Procurement Agency
trackers.desc: Albania's electronic public-procurement platform. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Albania, and for how much.

trackers.name: Albania Register of Beneficiary Owners (RBO)
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Publicly searchable.

trackers.name: HIDAACI
trackers.desc: Albania's High Inspectorate for the Declaration and Audit of Assets and Conflicts of Interest.

trackers.name: INSTAT
trackers.desc: Albania's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Albania.

trackers.name: Supreme State Audit (KLSH)
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Albania, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: National Business Center (QKB)
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Park natyror bashkiak and Kurora e gjelbër — the municipal routes
trackers.desc: TWO ROUTES THAT DO NOT REQUIRE A COUNCIL OF MINISTERS DECISION. Under Ligj 81/2017, a park natyror bashkiak is declared by decision of the municipal council — an environmental protected area equated with category IV — within one or more municipalities, after preliminary approval by the responsible minister; its purpose is activities suited to the area and related exclusively to the needs of the community, management plans are approved by ministerial order and sent to municipalities for implementation immediately, and such parks join the national network. AND THE SECOND ROUTE IS AN OBLIGATION, NOT A REQUEST: a Kurorë e gjelbër (green crown) is declared by the Këshilli Kombëtar i Territorit as a forest protected area inside a municipality — and the law states it is an obligation for every municipality. If your municipality has not declared its green crown it is in default of a statutory duty, which is a stronger argument than asking a favour. FOR NATIONAL DECLARATIONS, the opinion of academic institutions, the municipality, civil society, field experts and the community of the area must be obtained first, and the declaring decision must fix permitted and prohibited activities per sub-zone and the use of revenues generated.

trackers.name: The Vjosa precedent — unsigned contracts do not survive a declaration
trackers.desc: WHAT A DECLARATION CAN DO TO A PROJECT ALREADY IN THE PIPELINE. VKM No. 155 of 13.03.2023 declared the Vjosa river ecosystem a National Park (category II), 12,727 hectares of water, bank, forest and pasture, upgrading it from Park Natyror to Park Kombëtar, with the boundary map and coordinate table forming part of the decision. THE OPERATIVE CLAUSE: activities for which the relevant contract had not been signed — regardless of procedures under way — and contracts which on the day the decision entered into force had not fulfilled their relevant conditions, are not permitted inside the Park where they come openly into conflict with article 16 of law 81/2017. So an unsigned concession, or a signed one whose conditions were unmet on the day of declaration, does not survive it — if a project is mid-procedure, the declaration is the race. A management plan was to follow within 2 years. TWO THINGS FROM THE 2024 AMENDMENTS: a proposal to change the area of a protected zone must be consulted in advance with the local community, with owners whose properties are included or removed, with scientific institutions and local government, and must argue the need — so boundary reduction has a consultation trigger to hold them to. But watch the carve-outs: activities in 5-star and agrotourism accommodation structures and their supporting infrastructure are listed as permitted regardless of whether the declaring VKM says so.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: Energy Community — private bodies may complain, and refusal is appealable
trackers.desc: A COMPLAINT MECHANISM WHERE REFUSAL BY THE GATEKEEPER CAN BE TAKEN OVER ITS HEAD — which is rare, and is the reason to know about this. Under Article 90 of the Energy Community Treaty, private bodies may approach the Secretariat with complaints about a Party's non-compliance, and under Article 12.2 of the Consolidated Rules the Secretariat initiates procedures in response to a complaint by a private body as well as on its own initiative. AND IF THE SECRETARIAT DECLINES: the revised Rules give the complainant the right to approach the Permanent High Level Group directly, which may hear the complaint directly or initiate a preliminary procedure — in most systems recorded in this map, a secretariat declining to act ends the matter. The PHLG can also take interim measures in matters of urgency under Article 47(c) — that is what matters when works are already under way, so ask for it expressly. THE ENVIRONMENTAL ACQUIS IS IN SCOPE, including the EIA Directive as amended by 2014/52, which was to be transposed by 1 January 2019. CHECK THE TRANSPOSITION DEADLINE FOR THE DIRECTIVE YOU RELY ON — failure to transpose by the stated date is itself the non-compliance, and is a far simpler case than arguing about how a rule was applied. THE REALISTIC WIN CONDITION: a case opens with an Opening Letter, escalates to a Reasoned Opinion giving two months to rectify, then to the Ministerial Council — but a case closes whenever the Party complies, and many are recorded as complied with before any decision was adopted. The opening of proceedings is the lever, not the final decision. YOU CAN ALSO JOIN AN EXISTING CASE: interested third parties may access the case file and submit written observations, provided they substantiate their legitimate interest. Case law from Opening Letters is published with dates and numbers, so precedent is visible. Write to the Energy Community Secretariat, Am Hof 4, 1010 Vienna. ONE MORE ROUTE: the amended Rules provide for cooperation with national authorities and courts, giving concrete assistance to national courts on the interpretation of Energy Community law — a domestic judge unsure how an EU-derived rule applies can be pointed at it.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: ELAW — free attorneys and scientists who will critique the developer's EIA
trackers.desc: IT WILL READ THE DEVELOPER'S EIA AND TELL YOU WHAT IS WRONG WITH IT — which is the thing a community cannot produce alone and usually cannot afford. ELAW is a global alliance of attorneys, scientists and other advocates, founded 1989 in Eugene, Oregon by public interest lawyers from ten countries, that provides legal and scientific support to grassroots advocates to challenge destructive projects. FOUR CONCRETE FORMS OF HELP: legal support to local public interest lawyers; scientific support, including critiquing environmental assessments; economic insights on projects; and security expertise — ‘ELAW helps environmental lawyers improve their security so they can work without fear. When our partners are targeted, we act quickly to help defend and protect them.’ That last one is a named function, not an aspiration, and ELAW co-founded the Alliance for Land, Indigenous and Environmental Defenders. HOW TO USE IT — THROUGH A LAWYER, NOT AS A CLIENT: ELAW works through more than 300 public interest advocates in its network, and its stated strategy is ‘locating strong lawyers who are committed to protecting the environment in their home countries’. You can approach ELAW directly, but the leverage is greatest when a local advocate is the conduit — that is how the network is built. It has hosted nearly 300 advocates from more than 65 countries as Fellows and provided support on thousands of cases; several partners have won the Goldman Environmental Prize. Focus areas include biodiversity, fossil fuels — expressly assisting advocates in contesting fossil fuel development projects — plastic pollution, and work with coastal communities. It publishes guidebooks, including one to give communities sufficient understanding to challenge oil and gas projects, and clause-level summaries of national EIA law — so its site is also a route to learning exactly what your own EIA law requires. ASK WHETHER ELAW HAS A PARTNER IN YOUR COUNTRY: the network is described as spanning 70 to 80 countries but the member list is not published country by country, so this entry does not assert a presence in yours.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: EcoAlbania — goes to court alongside the village, not instead of it (Albania)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an Albanian environmental organisation created in December 2014 by biology professors from the University of Tirana together with the Save the Blue Heart of Europe team. Its method is to bring the case jointly with the affected residents as named co-plaintiffs, not on their behalf. Poçem: with 38 residents of Kutë village, plus EuroNatur and Riverwatch. Kalivac: with 39 members of the affected local community. Shushica: with 28 residents of Brataj. That is the offer — the villagers stay parties to their own case and the organisation brings the lawyers, the science and the international partners. WHAT IT HAS ACTUALLY WON: the Poçem concession was struck down in 2017 because the company had held no public hearing with the affected Mallakastër communities, having consulted 50 residents of Fier instead, and the Court of Appeal confirmed the annulment. The Tirana Administrative Court dismissed the Kalivac developer's challenge to the ministry's negative environmental declaration. In December 2024 the same court annulled the acts behind four hydropower plants on the Shushica. THE TIMELINE, WHICH IS THE THING TO BE HONEST ABOUT: the Poçem action began in December 2016 and the appeal was confirmed in 2024. Shushica took close to three years. A village considering this route should plan in years, not seasons, and should note that the organisation and its partners carried the cost across that span rather than the residents. THE ARGUMENT THAT KEEPS WORKING: in the Poçem case the fatal defect was the consultation — the wrong people were consulted, in the wrong place. Whatever else a community gathers, gather who was invited to the hearing, who attended, and where they lived.

trackers.name: PPNEA — Albania's oldest environmental organisation, and its science
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the first environmental organisation in Albania, established 5 June 1991 by decree of the Albanian Academy of Sciences, based in Tirana, with somewhere between eleven and fifty staff and the national BirdLife partner. It works across effectively all of Albania's protected areas and in the transboundary areas with Kosovo, North Macedonia, Montenegro and Greece. Its stated method is rigorous scientific research, community involvement, strategic partnerships and continuous interaction with decision-making institutions — which is the combination a community needs when it has to prove a site matters. WHAT IT CAN ACTUALLY SUPPLY: monitoring schemes run jointly with government agencies, training delivered to law enforcement bodies, and long-running species programmes — Balkan lynx since 2006, brown bear, Dalmatian pelican, Egyptian vulture, Mediterranean monk seal. If your site holds any of those, there is an existing monitoring record and an organisation with standing to speak about it. It also states a deep working relationship with investigative media, which is a different and sometimes faster route than a consultation response. AND IT SUPPORTS OTHER GROUPS: institutional development of environmental civil society organisations is one of its stated strands, so a new Albanian committee can ask for help becoming an organisation rather than only for help with its case. USE IT WITH THE OTHER TWO ALBANIAN ROUTES: EcoAlbania, already in this file, litigates alongside named village residents as co-plaintiffs; PONT, also in this file, funds environmental actors in exactly this region including operating costs. Science from PPNEA, the case from EcoAlbania, the money from PONT. Albania now has all three. WHAT IT IS NOT: not a land buyer and not a law firm. On its own account it works with government agencies rather than against them, which makes it strong on evidence and weaker as a confrontation partner — ask it for the record, not for the fight.

trackers.name: GreenAL — grants to environmental organisations across Albania, and a roster of them
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a grants programme to strengthen environmental organisations across Albania, administered through Co-PLAN, the Institute for Habitat Development. Albania had no funder of its own in this file — only the regional Balkan trust. THE MOST USEFUL THING HERE IS THE GRANTEE LIST, because it is effectively a directory of Albania's working environmental sector. Its second call funded, among others, the Albanian Ornithological Society (AOS), the Institute for Environment and Territory Management (ETMI), Qendra Res Publica, the association ILIRIA on environmental and social protection and development, PPNEA — already filed here — and Shtëpia e Gjelbër. Its smaller initiative grants went to a long list of local bodies including ADAD Malore, North Green Association, Agro-Eko Dibra, the EPER Center, DARC, SEEP, the Albanian Regional Environmental Board, Qendresa Qytetare, and the Cukali association of users of natural, forest and pasture resources. WHY THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE MONEY: an Albanian community looking for an ally near its own valley now has around twenty named organisations to choose from, several of them explicitly regional — Dibra, the mountains, the north — and one of them an association of people who actually use forest and pasture. Nothing else in the Albanian bucket lists the sector. TWO OTHER ALBANIAN ROUTES SURFACED ALONGSIDE, both worth knowing: LëvizAlbania, a Swiss Development Cooperation project run by a consortium of the Open Society Foundation for Albania, Partners Albania and Co-PLAN, which supports civil society actors, informal groups and individuals on local democracy — across two phases it ran nine calls, backed 362 individuals, informal groups and organisations, and reached more than 75,000 citizens, and one of its supported cases was an environmental organisation working on municipal noise. Its journey was described as concluding, so check its status. And the European Commission has run calls for Albanian civil society with a dedicated lot on environment, climate change and nature protection. WHAT IT IS NOT: a grants programme, not a permanent institution. Confirm whether a call is open before planning around it.

trackers.name: AMSHC — the Albanian state agency that funds NGOs, and spreads grants across the country
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Agjencia për Mbështetjen e Shoqërisë Civile, Albania's state agency for supporting civil society, which runs numbered public calls (thirrje) inviting non-profit organisations to submit project proposals. GreenAL is already in this file as Albania's sector funder; this is the state's own money, on a separate track. THE FIELDS IT NAMES, and two of them fit a land case directly: environmental initiatives for the protection of the environment and sustainable development; encouraging local and regional development through improved cooperation and participation and the activation of development and community actors; encouraging community development and strengthening volunteering and local and regional cooperation; and developing civil society through better institutional instruments and mechanisms. Another call lists protection of the environment and raising citizens' environmental awareness among its objects. THE DETAIL THAT FAVOURS A VILLAGE OVER TIRANA: the agency states that a distribution of winning projects as wide as possible across the whole territory is part of its philosophy and mission, and it has published the territorial distribution of winning projects by administrative region for its calls. That is a funder that reports where its money landed, by region — so a group outside the capital can see whether its own qarku has been served, and say so. Fourth funder in this file to prefer the periphery, after Montenegro, Serbia and Cyprus. HOW TO WATCH IT: calls are numbered and published on the agency's own site with the fields listed each time; the fields change between calls, so read the current thirrje rather than assuming. A SECOND ALBANIAN TRACK, for context: LëvizAlbania has run Grante Strategjike supporting formal and informal civil society actors and citizen engagement for accountability and participatory governance at local level — and its calls have explicitly invited networking and thematic coalitions between actors.

trackers.name: TOKA — five years of litigation, a bailiff at the powerhouse, and a SLAPP survived
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: The Organization to Conserve the Albanian Alps, founded June 2016 in Tirana and Valbona Valley National Park, with founding members from the local community, biologists, tourism experts and other supporters. That composition is the Kruščica checklist again — residents plus the expert disciplines — assembled at the start rather than recruited under pressure. It is one of the leading groups opposing plans for fourteen hydropower projects along the Valbona river inside the national park. WHAT THEY WON, AND HOW LONG IT TOOK: a group of residents together with the association filed suit, and roughly five years later, in July 2021, Albania's High Court ruled that the work and operations of two plants must stop immediately pending the outcome of the administrative case, with reports that the court also suspended the concession contracts. The plants kept running anyway. Enforcement came separately: a bailiff visited the powerhouses and confirmed they had ceased operation, with TOKA's founder present. Its own warning afterwards was that if the company switched the plants on again, even for five minutes, it becomes a criminal offence they will prosecute. Winning the judgment and enforcing it were two separate fights. THE GROUNDS THEY RAN: lack of proper impact assessments; threats against those opposing construction; and that such construction should not take place in a national park. Residents also claimed in court that the names of dead relatives, and names used without permission, appeared on documents purporting to show local support — so check the consent signatures. AND THE COST, WHICH IS THE WARNING: the developer brought an indemnity claim against TOKA and against its director personally for approximately 150,000 euros over alleged denigration and reputational damage. The Tirana District Court dismissed it; the company appealed. Members and others reported constant pressure over their opposition. Expect the personal suit. CONTEXT WORTH KNOWING: Tropoja is one of Europe's poorest regions, remaining residents depend on agriculture and the promise of tourism, and Valbona is one of Albania's top outdoor and mountain tourism destinations — the tourism argument carried real weight here.

trackers.name: AKZM and the AdZM in your qark — a protected-areas office in every county
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: the Agjencia Kombëtare e Zonave të Mbrojtura, the central state institution responsible for protected areas, created in 2015 under the environment ministry and taking over much of the abolished Forest Police. Protected areas now make up around 21.3 per cent of Albania's territory. THE PART THAT MATTERS LOCALLY: below AKZM sit the Administratat Rajonale të Zonave të Mbrojtura — regional protected-area administrations with a seat in every qark, forming the specialised local institutional network responsible for protecting and developing protected areas in that county — and the bashkia cooperates with the AdZM in exercising its own functions. A community does not have to reach Tirana; there is an office in its county, and its municipality is already required to work with it. HOW A NEW AREA GETS DESIGNATED, and where a community can push: environmental protected areas are declared by decision of the Council of Ministers on the proposal of the responsible minister, under law 81/2017. For Special Areas of Conservation the ministry coordinates identification with AKZM, the National Environment Agency, research and university institutions and local government units, a study is done, a preliminary list is drawn up and further assessed — and then the ministry organises discussions and consultation with interest groups, civil society representatives and academic institutions to present proposals and take opinions for improving the proposed list. That consultation is a named, scheduled entry point. AND THE EVIDENCE THAT PARTICIPATION HAS CHANGED BOUNDARIES BEFORE: the national assessment of Albania's protected-area system involved 44 meetings and consultations across all 12 qarks, with particular attention to consulting civil society groups and academic representatives, at which a large number of important proposals were gathered for revising, changing or expanding protected-area boundaries. PRACTICAL NOTE: AKZM also publishes calls for experts in named protected landscapes, some supported by PONT, already filed here as the Balkan long-term funder.

trackers.name: The 26-organisation joint letter — a current, named roster of Albanian groups that will co-sign
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a joint letter to the government from 26 Albanian environmental organisations over damage to a river during construction of a national corridor, demanding immediate intervention — published with the full signatory list. This file has recorded that the most useful free artefact in a country is usually a membership or signatory list; Albania had no federation, and this is the equivalent. THE NAMES, because that is the resource: Shoqata AlbNatyra; Qendra NORMA; Reinforce Sustainability (RESU Albania); GO2Albania; Qendra LUMI — Lëvizja për Ujërat, Mjedisin dhe Integrimin; PPNEA; Rrjedha; Qendra Balancë; EcoAlbania; Unë Gruaja; INCA Albania; PSEDA-ILIRIA; Eko mjedisi Durrës; AGRIEN; REC Albania; All-Green Centre; Milieukontakt Albania; Shoqata Ornitologjike e Shqiperise (AOS); Shoqata Ekspertet e Rinj Mjedisor (SHERM Albania); Shtëpia e Gjelbër; Instituti për Menaxhimin e Mjedisit dhe Territorit, among others. Three of these are already filed here individually; the rest are doors a community has not yet knocked on. WHY A CO-SIGNED LETTER IS ITSELF A RESOURCE: a village objecting alone is one objection. A letter carrying 26 organisations is a different document to receive, and the list tells you exactly who to approach and that they have signed together recently. AND THE CONTEXT THAT MAKES IT URGENT, recorded plainly: reporting on the Vjosë-Nartë protected landscape describes the government lowering the protection status of an ecosystem and reducing it by more than 5,000 hectares in 2021, and residents and activists protesting at barbed wire erected across a beach inside a protected landscape by a company holding a government permit. Protected status in Albania has been reduced by law before; designation is not the end of the work.

trackers.name: akzm.net — the protected-areas portal, and the state target of 25 per cent by 2030
trackers.desc: WHY THIS AND NOT A LAND TRUST: Albania has no private conservation landholder — I looked twice. As in Moldova and North Macedonia, the holder is the state: protected areas in Albania are declared national wealth under Law 81/2017, and this portal is the public face of the body that manages them. THE THREE LEVELS, so you approach the right one: AKZM, the central public institution directing and administering conservation and management of all environmental protected areas; the AdZM, the LOCAL body responsible AT QARK LEVEL for the protected areas in that qark; and the AZM, the local body responsible for a single protected area. AKZM has the status of a General Directorate centrally and is organised on a qark basis below that. Founded in 2015 with 224 staff, it took over many functions of the abolished Forestry Police. THE TARGET TO QUOTE BACK: the current programme aims to conserve and protect at least 25 per cent of Albania's territory by 2030, including NATURA 2000 areas and other area-based conservation measures, and to improve management through integrated and budgeted plans, with active involvement of local actors. Protected areas already stand at about 21.3 per cent of the territory. A community offering a site is helping the state meet a published target. WHAT ELSE THE PORTAL CARRIES: it is maintained under an EU- and Sida-funded project implemented by UNDP, with an e-learning platform for protected-area staff and a modernised online database for METT — the management effectiveness tracking tool — enabling standardised, comparable assessment. METT scores are how you show an area is being managed badly. AND THE DECLARATION ROUTE: a protected area is declared in accordance with the national plan, after obtaining the opinion of academic and scientific institutions and of the municipalities.

trackers.name: Albania's protected-area categories and the declaration decisions — with the boundary changes in them
trackers.desc: WHAT THE INSTRUMENT SHOWS: the Council of Ministers decisions declaring managed nature reserves and natural parks under Law 81/2017 set out, area by area, the approval of changes of status AND OF SURFACE AREA of existing protected areas, each with a map annex and a table of coordinates. Albania's bucket held litigators, funders and the state agency — but nothing showing how a site is actually declared, or how its boundaries move. THE CHANGES RUN BOTH WAYS, and that is the point: one ecosystem was upgraded from natural monument to natural park, its area rising from 1,740 to 4,927.67 hectares; another rose from 2,000 to 17,490.7 hectares; a third from 430 to 1,410. A protected area's surface can be enlarged by a single government decision, and the decisions naming the hectares are public. WHO MUST BE CONSULTED ON THE MANAGEMENT PLAN — and this is the opening: the responsible ministry approves the management plan and conservation objectives in cooperation with line ministries, WITH THE MUNICIPALITIES, WITH THE INTERESTED PUBLIC, WITH CIVIL SOCIETY AND WITH THE PRIVATE OWNERS whose properties lie within the territory of the protected area, drafted by specialists with the national agency within two years of the decision entering force. AND THE CATEGORY THAT FITS A LOCAL SITE: managed nature reserve or natural park (category IV) covers areas of LOCAL AND REGIONAL importance, maintained through active human management to conserve species and habitats. Albania has 11 national parks, 718 natural monuments, 23 managed nature reserves and 11 protected landscapes.

trackers.name: PPNEA and AOS on the boundary redraw — the map with the airport patch cut out of it
trackers.desc: WHAT THEY DOCUMENTED, and it is the clearest worked example in this file of a boundary being redrawn around a project: 44 territories in Albania holding protection categories from national park to protected landscape were subjected to a revision of their boundaries. An ornithological society named the scale; an institute for nature conservation named the mechanism: if you look at the maps, the patch where the international airport is planned inside the Vjosë-Nartë Protected Landscape has been removed completely from the map — and, in its words, nature does not stop at the patch they have made; nature is one and continuous, and this practically destroys the whole area. Compare the old boundary map with the new one and look for the hole — that is the check, and two named Albanian organisations have done it before. Activists' stated fear is that fragmenting protected areas will open the way to construction. AND THE EUROPEAN LEVER RECORDED ALONGSIDE: the European Commission stated it was closely monitoring developments in a named protected landscape and repeated that, to close Chapter 27 on environment and climate, Albania must demonstrate the ability to manage future Natura 2000 areas and to prevent their degradation. Environmental organisations argue amendments permitting luxury construction in protected areas conflict with EU nature protection standards and the spirit of the Natura 2000 framework.

trackers.name: The 25-organisation defence of Albanian environmental protesters — and the three attack patterns it names
trackers.desc: WHY THIS IS FILED AS A RESOURCE: twenty-five organisations put their names to a letter defending environmental protesters and demanding an investigation — so a community under attack in Albania has a named body of allies that has already stood up for people in its position, and a published template for doing so. THE THREE ATTACK PATTERNS THEY IDENTIFY, which a group should expect and prepare for: first, civil society representatives and activists accused WITHOUT EVIDENCE of misusing donor or EU funds, personal enrichment or foreign influence, in order to discredit their work and reduce public trust; second, activists defending a named protected area PRESENTED AS FINANCIALLY OR POLITICALLY MOTIVATED, shifting attention from the environmental concerns to personal attacks; third, the public exposure of citizens taking part in protests — PHOTOGRAPHED, IDENTIFIED BY NAME AND LABELLED as politically infiltrated, which may violate their privacy, expose them to intimidation and discourage participation. AND THE LEVER THEY USE, which this file has recorded working across the Western Balkans: they tie the situation to Albania's European integration process, stressing that respect for the rule of law, fundamental freedoms, media freedom and GUARANTEEING A SAFE ENVIRONMENT FOR CIVIL SOCIETY are key elements of the EU accession process. The letter notes that in several cases activists, organisers and citizens were named by public officials and made objects of mockery instead of being answered.

trackers.name: Citizens.al — the Albanian outlet that covers the residents' side, case by case
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: an Albanian news platform whose coverage centres on citizens, civil society and environmental disputes — this file has already used it for the Vjosë-Nartë boundary redraw and for the 25-organisation letter above. Albania's bucket held litigators, funders and the state agency but no outlet that reliably reports the residents' side. A community's first job is to be findable and its second is to be reported, and knowing which outlet covers these disputes is how a local fight becomes a national one. WHAT ITS COVERAGE HAS DOCUMENTED, from the pieces already used here: the revision of boundaries across 44 Albanian protected territories, with a named institute demonstrating that the patch where an international airport was planned had been REMOVED COMPLETELY FROM THE MAP; the European Commission stating it was closely monitoring that landscape; and the organised defence of protesters against online attacks and police violence. AND THE SCALE OF WHAT IT REPORTED IN 2026: protests beginning over a luxury project inside a protected coastal area grew into a movement named after one of the many bird species that inhabit it, described by an investigative outlet as the largest civic mobilisation since the fall of communism — having started as a typical environmental and territorial protest over the lagoon, biodiversity, the impact on protected areas, the transparency of administrative procedures, and PUBLIC CONSULTATION WITH LOCAL COMMUNITIES.

trackers.name: LevǐzAlbania — it funds INDIVIDUALS and INFORMAL GROUPS, not just registered NGOs
trackers.desc: WHO CAN APPLY, and this is the rare part: the project invites civil society actors, INDIVIDUALS, INFORMAL GROUPINGS and citizens to apply for support, encouraging civil society organisations working in the community, NEW ORGANISATIONS, individuals and their groupings to apply ONLINE, with concrete ideas and initiatives aimed at improving local governance, transparency, accountability and inclusion in decision-making. Albania had two funders and no land-holding body. A funder that names individuals and informal groups on its own FAQ is the one an unincorporated village committee can actually approach — the same shape recorded in Serbia and Lithuania, and the answer to the registration barriers found in Ukraine and Hungary. AND THE INSTRUMENT FOR AN URGENT CASE: RAPID REACTION is another important instrument, through which initiatives of civil society and individuals are financed, linked to CAUSES OR EMERGENCY ISSUES THAT RISK BEING ASSIMILATED BY THE TIME FACTOR. Emergency funding for things that will be lost while a normal grant round runs is exactly what a community facing bulldozers needs — compare Bulgaria's Speshen fond. THE SCALE, AND THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST: across two phases it ran 9 calls for applications, 12 strategic projects, 23 RAPID REACTION projects supported, 362 INDIVIDUALS, INFORMAL GROUPS AND CSOs, involving more than 75,000 citizens — and about 40 per cent of the civic stakeholders CONTINUE TO WORK on projects benefiting their communities, demonstrating a sustainable and long-term impact. It runs through a consortium of three named Albanian organisations and encourages the mobilisation of communities in URBAN AND RURAL areas.

trackers.name: Milieukontakt Albania — 22 years in the country, and it fixed the missing noise maps
trackers.desc: WHAT IT FOUND AND FIXED, and it is a gap most communities never think to look for: the ABSENCE of an action plan, a MAP, or defined measures on noise levels by the municipalities had created a void in providing information to communities and local organisations. So Milieukontakt Albania, with grant support, decided to work in this direction and find the most appropriate solution. The organisation has 22 years in Albania. If your council has never made the map or the measurements a law requires, that absence is itself the case — and here an organisation was funded to build what was missing rather than only to complain about it. AND THE FUNDING ROUTE IT USED, which is the model: it worked with the support of the LevizAlbania grant mechanism, whose case studies are published as success stories from the grant mechanism — so a community can read what has already been funded before writing its own application. The wider project it sits in is committed to strengthening local democracy by giving actors in the civic space the power to be AGENTS OF CHANGE who exert the necessary pressure to ensure that LOCAL GOVERNMENTS FUNCTION IN THE BEST INTEREST OF CITIZENS.

trackers.name: PPNEA — Albania's first environmental organisation, and it SUPPORTS other groups
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: an Albanian environmental NGO based in Tirana, established on 5 June 1991 by a special decree of the Academy of Sciences, and described by itself and by international conservation organisations as THE FIRST ENVIRONMENTAL ORGANIZATION IN ALBANIA. Albania had 25 filed entries and three funders. WHAT IT DOES, and the last item is why a local group should call it: it works on the conservation of threatened species and habitats, WILDLIFE AND HABITAT RESEARCH, environmental education, ADVOCACY FOR NATURE CONSERVATION, and SUPPORT FOR ENVIRONMENTAL CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS IN ALBANIA. A national organisation whose stated work includes supporting other environmental groups is the one a village committee approaches first — and it does its own habitat research, so it can supply the survey a submission needs. AND THE STANDING BEHIND IT: it is the Albanian partner of BirdLife International and a member of the International Union for Conservation of Nature, and describes its early role as providing AN INDEPENDENT CIVIL-SOCIETY VOICE for environmental protection in Albania. It publishes an annual report. Its campaign work is run with an international political foundation's Tirana office and international partners, and covers species down to a lynx with FEWER THAN 10 INDIVIDUALS LEFT in Albania.

trackers.name: Green-AL — a Swedish-funded programme to STRENGTHEN Albanian environmental civil society
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a project titled 'STRENGTHENING CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS FOR ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION IN ALBANIA', financed by the Swedish international development agency with funds of the Swedish government, which commissions and publishes regional thematic studies on environmental issues written by named university academics. A donor-funded programme whose whole purpose is strengthening environmental groups is a funder and a partner at once, and its regional studies give a community the documented baseline for its own area — written by someone else, at no cost. AND THE SUPPORT SUCH PROGRAMMES OFFER, recorded from a parallel Albanian capacity programme: CAPACITY-BUILDING ACTIVITIES CONCEIVED SPECIFICALLY FOR SMALL ORGANISATIONS — a youth skills programme, a guide to ORGANISATIONAL SUSTAINABILITY — and, for consolidated organisations, ADVANCED TRAINING ON EU FUNDS, alongside environmental advocacy and lobbying support and the exchange of experience and promotion of organisations. Its stated aim is the further strengthening and specialisation of civil society in the environmental field in Albania, so that it is able TO PRESENT THE COMMUNITY'S NEEDS, provide services and support, DEVELOP PARTNERSHIPS AND JOINT NETWORKS.

trackers.name: EuroNatur — the foundation that got Europe's first wild river national park signed
trackers.desc: WHAT IT ACHIEVED, and it is the largest designation win recorded in this file: after ten years of dedicated action by LOCAL COMMUNITIES, environmentalists, scientists and artists, the Albanian government signed a commitment to establish a Wild River National Park protecting the entire network of the river from the Greek border to the Adriatic Sea, INCLUDING THE FREE-FLOWING TRIBUTARIES. Albania had 27 filed entries and still no land-buying body. A foundation that carried a ten-year local campaign to a signed national park is the partner an Albanian community brings a river to — and it says of itself that EuroNatur played a key role; it is the decisive step towards the declaration of the national park. HOW IT WAS DONE, which is the copyable part: several nature conservation organisations SUBMITTED A DETAILED PROPOSAL for the creation of the national park to the Albanian Ministry of the Environment; a memorandum of understanding was signed between the minister and the managing director of an outdoor clothing company; and a working group was to be established WITHIN 30 DAYS to start planning. The park will bring visitor centres, rangers, and scientific and educational programmes, and NEW ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES FOR THE LOCAL COMMUNITIES, and is intended as a role model for many other rivers in the region. It also runs public campaigns projecting demands onto landmarks in Paris, Berlin, Brussels and Tirana.

trackers.name: EU4Nature — money and staff for protected-area management, aiming at 25 per cent of Albania
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS AND WHAT IT PAYS FOR: an action funded by the European Union and Sweden and co-implemented by UNDP Albania and the Italian development agency, whose objective is to contribute to the protection and conservation of AT LEAST 25 PER CENT OF THE ALBANIAN TERRITORY, at land and at sea, by 2030, through a system of protected areas including NATURA 2000 sites and other effective area-based conservation measures. Protected areas already cover 21.5 per cent of the country. AND WHO IT IS FOR: it provides ENHANCED CAPACITIES OF RELEVANT AUTHORITIES, CSO, ACADEMIA AND PRIVATE SECTOR, and the necessary resources for new AND EXISTING protected areas' effective management. A programme that funds civil society organisations alongside the authorities is one a local group can ask to be included in, and its stated core is partnership: government agencies, civil society organizations, academia, and the private sector are all working together. WHAT IT HAS ALREADY DELIVERED THAT A COMMUNITY CAN USE: with the protected areas agency it brought together experts and academic researchers to identify SIX KEY INDICATOR SPECIES IN 10 PILOT PROTECTED AREAS, and all Regional Administrations of Protected Areas have received tailored training to enhance BIODIVERSITY MONITORING and improve CONSERVATION ENFORCEMENT.

trackers.name: Albania's Protected Areas Act — ANY person can ask for their OWN land to be declared protected
trackers.desc: THE PROVISION THAT ANSWERS ALBANIA'S MISSING LAND ROUTE: batch492 recorded that no Albanian land-buying body exists, so the route had to be designation. This is the statutory text: EVERY NATURAL OR LEGAL PERSON HAS THE RIGHT TO REQUEST THE MINISTRY THAT THEIR OWN PRIVATE TERRITORY, OR PART OF THE TERRITORY IN THEIR OWNERSHIP, BE DECLARED A PROTECTED ENVIRONMENTAL AREA or be included in one of the categories of protected areas. An owner who cannot be bought out can put their own land under protection by asking — which turns a sympathetic landowner into the whole solution, at no cost. AND THE INTERIM PROTECTION WHILE THE REQUEST IS BEING CONSIDERED, which is what stops a project in the meantime: the MUNICIPALITY within whose administrative territory the area lies, AND THE OWNERS (WHEN THE PROPERTY IS PRIVATE), TAKE TEMPORARY MEASURES FOR THE PROTECTION AND ADMINISTRATION OF THE AREA DURING THE TIME THE PROPOSAL FOR ITS APPROVAL IS BEING EXAMINED. Protection begins when the proposal is filed, not when it is approved, and the municipality is named alongside the owner as the body that must act. AND WHAT THE FILE MUST CONTAIN: among the required elements are THE TRANSFER OF OWNERSHIP AND OF THE RIGHTS TO USE ELEMENTS OF BIOLOGICAL DIVERSITY, the area being part of the planning document, and approval by the NATIONAL TERRITORIAL COUNCIL of the boundary and its INTERNAL ZONING.

trackers.name: Albania's communal forests — 244,000 hectares transferred, and VILLAGE USER ASSOCIATIONS hold the rights
trackers.desc: WHAT WAS TRANSFERRED, and it is the largest community landholding recorded in this file: 40 PER CENT forest and 244,000 HECTARES (60 PER CENT) OF PASTURES under the control of the COMMUNES. Albania had ZERO land-acquisition entries filed. AND HOW IT WORKS AT VILLAGE LEVEL, which is the part a community can use: the size and boundaries of the areas assigned to each commune AND DEPENDENT VILLAGE were completed, and A 10-YEAR USE CONTRACT WAS SIGNED; forestry directorate staff prepare a management plan WITH THE INVOLVEMENT OF THE COMMUNES; and AT VILLAGE LEVEL, CITIZENS ARE IN USER ASSOCIATIONS THAT TAKE UP RIGHTS TO USE THE AREAS FOR PASTURE, HARVESTING FIREWOOD OR MEDICINAL PLANTS, AND OTHER ACTIVITIES. A village user association already holding contractual rights over communal forest is a body with standing over that ground before any project appears — and it exists in villages across the country. AND THE MONEY BEHIND IT: a state forests project spent 3.72 MILLION US DOLLARS on small investments in 126 named units. A separate directorate has jurisdiction over the parks and reserves, while a forest service police carries out inspections and enforces the laws AND THE CONTRACTS WITH THEIR CONDITIONS OF USE.

trackers.name: The PARK NATYROR BASHKIAK — a MUNICIPAL nature park category, with a list of unapproved ones
trackers.desc: THE CATEGORY MOST USEFUL TO AN ALBANIAN COMMUNITY, named in the national protected-areas assessment: alongside the state categories there is PARK NATYROR BASHKIAK — MUNICIPAL NATURE PARK — IUCN CATEGORY IV, and the assessment publishes A LIST OF UNAPPROVED MUNICIPAL PROTECTED AREAS. A published list of municipal parks that were proposed but never approved is a list of places already assessed as worth protecting, waiting on a council decision — and it pairs with the Kosovar municipal decision filed in batch530. AND WHY THE SYSTEM IS UNDER STRAIN, in the assessment's own terms: Albania has seen a series of large and complex changes as a result of intensive economic, social and tourist development, CHANGES OF OWNERSHIP OVER THE TERRITORY, PROPERTY COMPENSATION, and UNCONTROLLED DEVELOPMENTS (OCCUPATIONS AND BUILDINGS WITHOUT PERMIT) which, IN MANY CASES, HAVE NOT TAKEN INTO CONSIDERATION THE BOUNDARIES AND STATUS OF THE PROTECTED AREAS. Ownership change and compensation are named by the state's own analysts as drivers of protected-area loss, which is the argument to put in a submission. The document also tabulates the protected-area network BY COUNTY and lists the RAMSAR ZONES, so a community can check what its own area already carries.

trackers.name: The Federata Kombëtare e Pyjeve dhe Kullotave — it REPRESENTS THE FOREST USERS' INTERESTS
trackers.desc: THE NATIONAL BODY BEHIND ALBANIA'S VILLAGE USER ASSOCIATIONS, and it is the one to call: the associations are organised at REGIONAL level, forming REGIONAL FEDERATIONS OF FORESTS AND PASTURES, and those regional federations are a constituent part of the NATIONAL FEDERATION OF FORESTS AND PASTURES, which is A NON-PROFIT, NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATION THAT DEFENDS AND REPRESENTS THE INTERESTS OF THE FOREST USERS. A village user association is not alone — it sits inside a regional federation and a national one whose stated job is defending its interests, which completes the route filed in batch533. AND THE OTHER NAMED ACTORS a community can draw on: the FACULTY OF FOREST SCIENCES, THE ONLY UNIVERSITY INSTITUTION in the field of forests, which PROVIDES TRAINING for municipal forestry staff, DISSEMINATES INFORMATION, DRAFTS MANUALS for management-plan activities and ASSISTANCE FOR DRAFTING THE PLAN GUIDELINES. AND WHO MUST BE CONSULTED IN A MANAGEMENT PLAN: the process names as key actors THE COMMUNITY, FOREST USERS, FOREST USERS' ASSOCIATIONS AND NGOs, and the responsible structure TRANSMITS THE ANNUAL MONITORING DATA on interventions and events to a named national information system. Community, users and NGOs are named parties to the plan, so a submission is expected, not tolerated.

trackers.name: Albania's Forest Law — PUBLIC FORESTS TRANSFERRED INTO MUNICIPAL OWNERSHIP, and the fee to take them out
trackers.desc: THE DEFINITION THAT DECIDES WHO A COMMUNITY MUST PERSUADE: a COMMUNAL FOREST is the forest IN THE OWNERSHIP OR IN THE USE OF THE ORGANS OF LOCAL GOVERNANCE — and a numbered government decision provided FOR THE TRANSFER INTO THE OWNERSHIP OF THE MUNICIPALITIES OF PUBLIC FORESTS AND PASTURES, ACCORDING TO THE INVENTORY LISTS, from the ministry and the former communes. Albania transferred its public forests into municipal ownership by inventory list, so the council owns the wood and the list says which parcels — a document to request by name. AND THE PRICE OF TAKING LAND OUT, which is the number that shapes a project's economics: a further numbered decision sets THE TARIFFS FOR THE REMOVAL FROM THE FOREST AND PASTURE FUND OF AREAS THAT ARE USED FOR THE CONSTRUCTION OF INDUSTRIAL WORKS, and another sets the rules for submitting the request, keeping and completing the TECHNICAL DOCUMENTATION, and the CRITERIA AND PROCEDURES FOR REDUCING THE AREA AND VOLUME OF THE FOREST FUND. Every removal of forest for an industrial work has a published tariff and a documented procedure — both checkable, and both a place where a project can be shown to have cut corners. The law's stated purpose is protection as obligations IN THE INTEREST OF PRESENT AND FUTURE GENERATIONS.

trackers.name: Free legal aid in Albania — a FREE LAWYER, a green line, and centres listed by address
trackers.desc: STATE-FUNDED LEGAL HELP WITH THE COST QUESTION ANSWERED OUTRIGHT: NO, YOU PAY NOTHING FOR THE SERVICE YOU RECEIVE AT THE CENTRES, ORGANISATIONS OR LAW CLINICS. ALSO WITH THE BENEFIT OF SECONDARY LEGAL AID / A FREE LAWYER YOU PAY NOTHING. EVERYTHING IS COVERED BY THE STATE BUDGET. Albania is among the least-worked buckets in this file. A free lawyer, not merely free advice, is what secondary legal aid means here — the distinction that decides whether a community can be represented rather than only informed. AND HOW TO GET IT, which is the practical part: TO COMPLETE THE DOCUMENTS NEEDED FOR THE FREE LAWYER YOU CAN GO TO THE CENTRES FOR THE PROVISION OF PRIMARY LEGAL AID, WHERE OUR LAWYERS WILL ASSIST YOU IN FILLING IN THE FORMS NEEDED TO OBTAIN SECONDARY LEGAL AID. The primary centres exist partly to fill in the application for the free lawyer, so a person who cannot draft the request is not shut out by it. There is also a GREEN (FREE-OF-CHARGE) TELEPHONE NUMBER 0800 10 10 and an online platform. AND THE CENTRES THEMSELVES ARE PUBLISHED WITH THEIR STREET ADDRESSES, most of them NEXT TO OR INSIDE THE PREMISES OF THE LOCAL COURT, in named towns from the capital to the north and south. HONEST LIMIT: YOU CANNOT CHOOSE THE LAWYER.

trackers.name: What the free legal aid system does NOT cover — the gaps, reported by its own sector
