trackers.desc: THE LIMITS OF THE FREE SERVICE, reported from inside the sector, which a community must know before it relies on the previous entry: the identified problems are SERVICES THAT ARE NOT ACCESSIBLE BECAUSE THEY ARE FAR FROM THEIR AREAS, OR ARE ABSENT IN SOME ZONES AND MUNICIPALITIES OF THE COUNTRY, and THE CURRENT FREE LEGAL AID OFFICES WORK WITH REDUCED STAFF — ONE PERSON ON THE STAFF FOR AN OFFICE THAT COVERS A WIDE TERRITORY. AND THE GAP THAT MATTERS MOST TO A COMMUNITY FACING A DEVELOPER: THE ABSENCE OF SERVICES THAT ARE MAINLY PRIMARY — THAT IS, INFORMATION AND PREPARATION OF DOCUMENTS, AND NOT REPRESENTATION IN COURT, WHICH IS VERY NECESSARY FOR VULNERABLE CATEGORIES. In practice the service delivers information rather than representation, and in some areas free representation is simply not found — one worker reports that IN SOME AREAS WE DO NOT FIND FREE LEGAL REPRESENTATION FOR THE CASES. AND WHAT PARTLY FILLS IT: the centre COOPERATES WITH SEVERAL OF THE ORGANISATIONS LICENSED BY THE MINISTRY OF JUSTICE FOR THE PROVISION OF FREE LEGAL AID. A licensed-organisation list exists alongside the state centres, and is where a group should look when the state office is one overworked person.

trackers.name: Personal Data Protection Service of Georgia
trackers.desc: Personal Data Protection Service of Georgia — Georgia’s national data-protection / information authority, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Georgia
trackers.desc: Official site of Georgia's highest (cassation) court with judgments and case information. · Find here: information and judgments of the Supreme Court of Georgia.

trackers.name: Ask Gov — FOI requests (GEO)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (FOI request platform); Ask Gov — civic Freedom-of-Information request platform (Alaveteli/mySociety network) — lets citizens file public-records requests and publishes the requests and the authorities’ responses in a public archive.

trackers.name: GYLA (Georgian Young Lawyers' Association)
trackers.desc: Georgian legal-watchdog NGO (since 1994) that monitors government activities and elections (15+ years of election observation), advocates legislative and institutional reform, and runs accountability projects on budget spending and freedom of information.

trackers.name: Green Alternative (Association Green Alternative)
trackers.desc: Georgia's leading environmental and social-justice organisation, formed out of the campaigners of Friends of the Earth Georgia and a member of the CEE Bankwatch Network. It targets large projects with severe environmental or social impacts — hydropower above all, plus transport schemes and privatisation deals — and its published case files are unusually detailed, documenting for instance a hydropower plant approved inside Kazbegi National Park despite an explicit statutory prohibition. WHO TO ENLIST when a dam, road or concession lands on your valley. You CAN: use its alternative report on Aarhus Convention implementation in Georgia to argue access to information and public participation, and reach the wider Georgian Green Network and the independent forest monitoring network, both of which it founded. For activists: it explicitly pairs campaign work with capacity building of local groups and getting them directly into the campaign, so approach it as a partner rather than a service — with around ten staff, it cannot take everything.

trackers.name: State Audit Office
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Georgia, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Anti-Corruption Bureau — Asset Declarations
trackers.desc: National asset-declaration registry; Georgia’s Anti-Corruption Bureau publishes ~60,000 searchable officials’ asset declarations online (monitoring moved here from the Civil Service Bureau; two-month review before publication), Georgia.

trackers.name: Georgia — public officials’ asset declarations
trackers.desc: Accountability source (official asset-declaration register); Georgia — public officials’ asset declarations — the Civil Service Bureau’s public database and monitoring system for Georgian officials’ asset declarations.

trackers.name: IDFI (Institute for Development of Freedom of Information)
trackers.desc: Georgian watchdog/think-tank (since 2009) promoting freedom of information, open governance and anti-corruption. Monitors public procurement, the state and municipal budgets, and proactive disclosure by public bodies; advances citizen participation in decision-making, budgeting and lawmaking at central and local levels; and publishes officials' asset-declaration data (including after access to the official portal was restricted).

trackers.name: NAPR
trackers.desc: Georgia's National Agency of Public Registry (company registry). — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Public Defender of Georgia — National Preventive Mechanism
trackers.desc: Public Defender of Georgia — National Preventive Mechanism — Georgia’s OPCAT National Preventive Mechanism — the Public Defender’s Special Preventive

trackers.name: State Procurement (Ge)
trackers.desc: Georgia's unified electronic state-procurement system. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Georgia, and for how much.

trackers.name: National Statistics Office of Georgia (GeoStat)
trackers.desc: Georgia's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Georgia.

trackers.name: დაცული ლანდშაფტი — the category for a place where people live
trackers.desc: GEORGIA'S PROTECTED AREA LAW, adopted 1996, provides 5 categories — state reserve, national park, natural monument, managed reserve and protected landscape. THE LAST IS THE ONE THAT FITS AN INHABITED PLACE: დაცული ლანდშაფტი is created expressly for the harmonious coexistence of nature and people, development of recreation and tourism, and support for the region's economic potential and the population's living conditions — and different zones may be arranged within it. That zoning flexibility is what makes it usable where people live and work, and it is the same category Skopje used for Vodno. It may sit inside a biosphere reserve or World Heritage site, or itself contain a natural monument. For sustainable resource use, zones with different permissible ratios of conservation and multiple use may be delineated. The first official reserve on Georgian territory dates to 1912.

trackers.name: Caucasus Nature Fund — it matches your government, so lobby your government
trackers.desc: A FUNDING MODEL WITH A LEVERAGE ARGUMENT BUILT IN. CNF is a conservation trust fund founded in 2007 by Conservation International, Germany's development ministry and WWF, with offices in Tbilisi and Yerevan, supporting 18 protected areas across Armenia, Azerbaijan and Georgia. Its mission is long-term funding for operating costs — the hardest money to raise anywhere in this map — plus improved management. THE MECHANISM: it works through partnerships with the three governments by matching, but not exceeding, the state budgets. So CNF money rises and falls with what your own government commits, which means lobbying your government to raise its protected-area budget also raises the matched international money. Use that argument directly. WHAT ASSEMBLES AT SCALE: a five-year initiative for 12 Georgian protected areas totalled USD 10 million — USD 1.8m GEF, USD 4.8m from the environment ministry, USD 3.1m CNF and USD 200,000 from the Bank of Georgia. AND KNOW WHO MANAGES YOUR SITE: protected areas total 600,597 ha, about 8 percent of the country, but only 387,800 ha — 64 percent of them — is managed by the Agency of Protected Areas. More than a third sits elsewhere, so identify the manager before directing a complaint.

trackers.name: Caucasus Nature Fund — matches the state park budget, so cutting the park costs the state euros
trackers.desc: THE LEVER HERE IS THE MATCHING RULE, NOT THE GRANT. CNF publishes an “up to 50 percent principle”: it matches, but never exceeds, what the state itself budgets for a protected area. Read that backwards and it is an argument you can put in writing to the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture or the Agency of Protected Areas — every lari stripped from a park's operating budget, and every hectare degazetted out of it, strips matching European money with it. Georgia is the bulk of CNF's programme: 16 of its 21 parks, among them Borjomi-Kharagauli, Vashlovani, Tusheti, Lagodekhi, Kolkheti, Kobuleti, Mtirala, Machakhela, Kintrishi, Kazbegi, Algeti, Javakheti, Batsara-Babaneuri, Pshav-Khevsureti and the newer Racha National Park, Aragvi and Truso Protected Landscapes. WHO TO CONTACT: the Tbilisi programme office, via the contact page and named executive director at caucasus-naturefund.org/about_us/contact/. WHAT YOU CANNOT GET: a grant. The money goes to protected-area administrations under agreement with the government, not to community groups, and there is no community application window. Two practical uses instead: CNF funds SMART patrolling and a ten-year biodiversity monitoring plan in Georgia, so ask the park administration what CNF-funded monitoring already covers your area before you pay for your own survey; and CNF states that the management plans it funds are made with a participatory approach involving local communities and farmers, which is a documented commitment you can hold a park administration to when a plan is written without you. EXCLUSION: CNF's mandate names Azerbaijan but its published park list contains no Azerbaijani site.

trackers.name: Legal Aid Service — the free consultation has no means test; only representation does
trackers.desc: THE INVERSION: THE CONSULTATION IS OPEN TO EVERYONE, AND YOU NEED BRING NOTHING. The Service states that its free consultation may be used by any person and that no document is required to obtain one, though bringing the papers about your problem makes it a better one. The means test bites only at the next stage — a state-paid advocate to actually run your case requires registration as a low-income person or another reason you cannot pay. So the sequence for a community facing a permit or a land decision is: take the free consultation first, on the facts, before spending anything on establishing eligibility. WHERE: the Service works through a network of bureaux, consultation centres and a register of invited public advocates; ka.wikipedia lists 13 bureaux and 39 consultation centres, a figure this entry does not treat as established — use the office list on legalaid.ge. Contact info@legalaid.ge, +995 32 292 00 55. HONEST GAP, AND IT IS THE IMPORTANT ONE: this entry does not establish that administrative disputes over land, planning permissions or environmental decisions fall within the case categories eligible for a state-paid advocate. Ask that question on the first call and get the answer before building a plan around it. A second claim seen only on a third-party legal directory, not on legalaid.ge, is that the Service is subordinate to no state body and reports only to the Parliament of Georgia; if true it matters a great deal when your opponent is a ministry, so ask them to confirm it rather than relying on it. SEARCH TRAP: querying this body in English returns the United States state of Georgia almost exclusively, and adding “legalaid.ge” to the query does not fix it — search the Georgian name.

trackers.name: Agency of Protected Areas — its mandate covers landslide, erosion and water-recharge ground, not only wildlife
trackers.desc: READ ITS OBJECTIVES BEFORE YOU DECIDE WHAT YOUR SITE IS, BECAUSE ONE OF THEM IS NOT ABOUT WILDLIFE AT ALL: the Agency lists among its aims the protection of territories actively affected by erosion, mudslides, floods, avalanches and landslides, and of areas of surface and underground water formation together with their flow and discharge areas, from anthropogenic impact. Most Georgian development fights are about slopes and water rather than species, and this is the clause that lets a community put such a site forward on its own terms instead of straining to find a rare animal. A second, separately useful aim is the conservation and restoration of historical-cultural landscapes and landscapes characteristic of architectural and archaeological complexes — the heritage-landscape route. THE DOOR: the Agency's stated objective includes planning, creating and developing NEW protected areas, so there is a body whose job is to take ground into protection, not merely to run what already exists. It is doing so — a national park of roughly 15,000 hectares in Guria has been announced by the minister. It administers strict nature reserves, national parks, natural monuments, managed reserves, protected landscapes, biosphere reserves, world heritage sites and wetlands of international importance, and has been a legal entity of public law since 1 February 2008. TWO ENTRY POINTS THAT ARE PUBLIC AND EASY TO MISS. Management plans get public discussion sessions held at the Agency — the Batsara-Babaneuri protected areas plan was aired that way — so the plan governing your area is amendable at a meeting you can attend rather than a document handed down. And the Agency runs grant projects: it launched one for Ajameti with financial support from BP Georgia. That funding source is worth knowing before you rely on it: an oil company underwriting a protected-area grant programme is a real tension, not a detail. WHO: chaired by David Iosebashvili with Tamar Khakhishvili as deputy chair; Tbilisi. THE LIMIT, AND THIS FILE HAS NOW SEEN IT TWICE: the body that holds the land can be the body developing it. The Agency also runs ecotourism and visitor-centre infrastructure inside protected areas, and it sits under the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture, so do not expect it to front a fight against a scheme the government backs. Where that is the situation, Green Alternative is already in this file with a record of taking such projects to international lenders' accountability mechanisms. Cross-reference the Caucasus Nature Fund entry too: CNF matches state budgets for many of the parks this Agency administers, which is why cutting or shrinking one of them costs the state matched money.

trackers.name: NACRES — it drafts the management plan, and the management plan is what decides what is allowed inside a protected area
trackers.desc: THE POINT OF INTERVENTION MOST PEOPLE MISS IS THE PLAN, NOT THE PERMIT. A Georgian government analysis of protected areas records the Tusheti National Park management plan being revised by NACRES, and management plans determine what activity is permitted inside a protected area — grazing, infrastructure, tourism development, extraction. Read alongside the Agency of Protected Areas entry in this file, which holds public discussion sessions on draft management plans, that gives two nameable points at which a community can act on the document that will govern its area for years: the organisation drafting it, and the meeting where it is aired. Both come long before anyone applies for anything. WHAT MAKES IT USABLE RATHER THAN MERELY EMINENT: NACRES runs a Community Ranger programme that trains community members to take part in biodiversity monitoring of Georgia's protected areas, and its grassland work is built around exactly the conflict a rural community faces — it notes that local people have used grasslands now inside protected areas as grazing land for hundreds of years, and its Kazbegi assessment produces a grassland habitat distribution map and a database of pasture biodiversity, fodder quantity and ecological status feeding into a pasture management plan. If your dispute is about grazing or access inside a protected area, that baseline already exists or can be commissioned. It also works on human-wildlife conflict around protected areas and with the single settlement inside Borjomi-Kharagauli National Park. TRACK RECORD AND STANDING: founded as a group in 1989 and registered in 1991 as Noah's Ark Centre for the Recovery of Endangered Species, later renamed while keeping the acronym; more than seventy conservation projects, more than twenty-five donors, and per the Aarhus Clearinghouse some 130 scientific articles and nine books by its staff. It implemented Georgia's Biodiversity Country Study for the government with UNEP, and a named staff member coordinated the finalisation of the national biodiversity strategy — so its work is inside national policy, not outside it. Current field analysis of key species distribution across Georgia's protected areas, funded by the Caucasus Nature Fund and WWF, identifies pressures on populations and produces recommendations to the protected areas. THE LIMIT, AND IT IS THE SAME ONE THIS FILE HAS NOW RECORDED FOR RSCN, THE AGENCY OF PROTECTED AREAS AND OTHERS: NACRES is commissioned by the Caucasus Nature Fund, WWF, GEF/UNDP and the government itself. It is embedded with the institutions that manage the land rather than opposed to them, and should not be expected to front a fight against a scheme the state backs — Green Alternative, already in this file, is the body with that record. Use NACRES for the plan, the baseline and the evidence. Note also that the Tusheti plan-revision record comes from a 2012 government document; that NACRES still holds a plan-writing role today was not established this round.

trackers.name: SABUKO — it wrote the stocking rates meant to become the terms of the state's own grazing lease
trackers.desc: THE LEVER IS THE LEASE, AND SABUKO IS WRITING ITS TECHNICAL BASIS. Its published pasture management recommendations for the Chachuna Managed Reserve set estimated stocking rates and a provisional rotational grazing scheme, and state their purpose directly: the plan should serve as the basis for a future leasing contract that meets the requirements of a protected area. Where land is grazed under state lease, the terms of that lease decide what actually happens on the ground, and this is the organisation putting numbers into them. If your dispute concerns grazing pressure inside or beside a protected area, the stocking rate is the argument. UNDERSTAND THE SUBLEASE CHAIN FIRST, BECAUSE IT EXPLAINS THE OVERGRAZING AND MOST OUTSIDERS MISS IT: a large part of pasture is leased by the state to individuals, who then sub-let it to farmers at a considerably higher price. Farmers economise by leasing less land than they need and grazing more animals on it than permitted. The person degrading the land is often not the person holding the lease, and an intervention aimed at shepherds rather than at the rent structure will fail. Georgian sheep numbers fell roughly forty per cent after the Soviet period while pasture pressure rose, because the flocks were concentrated into small areas. WHAT IT HAS ACTUALLY DONE: since January 2019 it has led a gallery forest and grassland restoration project in the Iori river valley under the Endangered Landscapes Programme with the Cambridge Conservation Initiative and BirdLife International, assessing land cover across 748.1 hectares of Chachuna's 5,032, and it works in partnership with the local shepherds rather than over them. A SECOND CASE WORTH KNOWING IF YOUR SITE SITS BELOW AN UNFINISHED SCHEME: the Dali reservoir, begun in the 1980s and never completed as intended, is now sealed and limited to fishing and irrigation — but it drove desertification downstream, replacing floodplain forest species with arid ones. SABUKO's position is that state policy on the reservoir should serve conservation and not irrigation alone, with staged water release to restore natural flooding. Infrastructure that was never finished can still be the thing destroying your valley, and its operating rules can be reopened. The reserve holds over twenty-five raptor species, ten of Georgia's seventeen imperial eagle pairs, and a count of ten thousand little bustard on the grasslands. Successor to the Georgian Centre for the Conservation of Wildlife; BirdLife's Georgian partner. ONE THING TO WEIGH: SABUKO also builds ecotourism infrastructure inside the reserve, and reporting on the opening acknowledged that many Georgian protected-area tourism projects have damaged biodiversity through noise, light and habitat pressure. Its own stated safeguard is a management plan per site with income returned to conservation. Pair with NACRES, already in this file, which drafts the management plans themselves.

trackers.name: Social Justice Center — it argues mining benefit-sharing, not just whether the mine happens, and it works with environmental activists
trackers.desc: THE MOST USEFUL THING THIS ORGANISATION HAS DONE FOR A MINING COMMUNITY IS TO TREAT THE QUESTION AS THREE-SIDED RATHER THAN TWO. Its work on the Georgian mining sector examines the taxation and benefit-sharing arrangements around extraction, analyses the models in use, proposes a more equitable framework, and is deliberately published to local communities through articles, videos and infographics so that they can take it to government and to the companies themselves. Most communities are handed a binary — the project goes ahead or it does not — and lose it. What the community gets from a project that proceeds is a separate argument, and this is a body that has already built the case. IT ALSO ATTACKS LARGE DEVELOPMENTS ON THE GROUNDS A COMMUNITY CAN ACTUALLY USE: its published analysis of a major real-estate development project addresses the opacity of the underlying agreement, restricted access to environmental information, and disregard for public participation. Those three are procedural failures with remedies, unlike an argument about whether a scheme is desirable. WHAT IT PROVIDES DIRECTLY: legal assistance to individuals in human rights cases within its areas of expertise, and it names environmental activists among the groups it works with, alongside workers, minorities and others. On the manganese mining crisis at Chiatura it set out publicly that a reorganisation and mass dismissal affecting thousands of miners was being conducted unlawfully — identifying the exclusion of miners from the government's crisis working group, template consent forms circulated without informing workers of the new structures or terms, and the absence of the consultation with trade unions required before mass layoffs. That is the kind of specific procedural documentation that turns a grievance into a case. Founded in 2012 and based in Tbilisi; it describes its own politics openly, which a community should weigh in deciding whether it is the right partner for a particular fight. BEFORE YOU RELY ON IT, KNOW THIS: the organisation is under legal and financial pressure of its own. The European Court of Human Rights has begun examining the merits of its application concerning Georgia's foreign agents legislation and its law on grants, and a defenders network reports that the prosecutor's office has frozen the bank accounts of several Georgian human rights and civil society organisations. Its capacity may be constrained for reasons unrelated to your case. NAME CHECK: searching this name returns a large number of unrelated organisations in the American state of Georgia. Match on the .ge domain.

trackers.name: Bankwatch — if the project is financed with international public money, the money has a complaints desk and this is who helps you use it
trackers.desc: FIND OUT WHO IS PAYING BEFORE YOU DECIDE HOW TO FIGHT. If a scheme is financed by a development bank rather than purely by private money, there is a second route entirely separate from your national courts: the lender's own accountability mechanism, which can investigate and can hold up disbursement. The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development established an independent project accountability mechanism in 2020; the European Investment Bank and the World Bank have their own. THIS NETWORK EXISTS TO HELP COMMUNITIES USE THAT ROUTE. In its own words it investigates the impacts of public finance, works with affected communities and local organisations, helps them protect their rights and livelihoods, and makes sure their stories are told in Europe's power centres — it meets the institutions it monitors and keeps staff in Brussels. Its stated purpose is working with local communities on campaigns to stop or change harmful investment projects funded by international public finance. IT HAS DONE THIS IN GEORGIA SPECIFICALLY, MAINTAINING PROJECT PAGES ON NAMED GEORGIAN HYDROPOWER SCHEMES, and it reports supporting civil society across the Caucasus and Central Asia since 2000 in influencing internationally financed projects. USE IT ALONGSIDE THE GEORGIAN ORGANISATION THAT IS ITS MEMBER HERE, NOT INSTEAD OF IT — the member knows the valley and the ministry; the network is in the room when the lender's board meets. Those are different jobs and a community needs both. It has seventeen member groups across fourteen countries in central and eastern Europe and the Caucasus, with a secretariat in Prague and staff spread across the region, and it publishes an anti-corruption reporting procedure with named contacts and protection for those who report. THE LIMIT DECIDES WHETHER IT IS YOUR ROUTE AND IT IS SHARP: it works on projects financed with international public money. If your quarry, road or dam is funded domestically or by a private company with no development bank behind it, this is not the door — check the financing first, because the answer determines which of the routes in this file applies. It is also a network rather than a local service: it works through its member organisations, and in Georgia that means approaching the member.

trackers.name: Inclusive Development International — it traces who is actually financing a project, on request from the community
trackers.desc: THIS IS THE BODY THAT ANSWERS THE QUESTION THE OTHER FINANCE ENTRIES IN THIS FILE TELL YOU TO ASK FIRST. Since 2016 it has taken requests from community advocates to research and map the investment and supply chains behind harmful projects, identifying the banks, investors, insurers, development finance institutions and major brands that make them possible. Its researchers work from financial databases, company reports, import data and shipping manifests — so ownership can be traced even where a developer discloses nothing locally and the national registry shows only a shell. WHAT COMES BACK IS NOT RAW DATA BUT A SUMMARY WITH AN ANALYSIS OF PRESSURE POINTS AND POSSIBLE ADVOCACY STRATEGIES. In cases it judges to have high potential it will, on request, help execute legal, advocacy and negotiation strategies — and where it cannot take a case itself it refers it to partners with the capacity to help, so an approach that fails may still produce a referral. IT ALSO PUBLISHES FREE TOOLS THAT AUTOMATE THIS WORK — a shareholder tracker and a development bank investment tracker — built expressly because the financial databases it relies on are unaffordable for the communities that need them. Start there before asking anyone for anything. It trains advocates around the actual projects they are fighting, having trained more than fifteen hundred people in selected methods, and continues supporting them afterwards. USE IT WITH THE TWO OTHER FINANCE ENTRIES RECORDED FOR GEORGIA: this body finds the financier, the network carries the case to the lender's board in Brussels, and the Georgian member organisation knows the valley and the ministry. THE HONEST LIMIT: its documented casework and requests are from Southeast Asia, Africa and the Americas, and no work in Georgia or anywhere in this region could be established. The service is described as open to requests from community advocates without a stated geographic restriction, so the route is untested here rather than closed — approach it knowing that.

trackers.name: Front Line Defenders — a 24-hour line answered in Russian, and grants that pay the legal fees when you are the one being sued
trackers.desc: THE GRANT COVERS THE SITUATION THIS FILE HAS RECORDED IN GEORGIA: protection grants of up to €7,500 can pay LEGAL FEES FOR DEFENDERS WHO ARE BEING JUDICIALLY HARASSED, improve the physical security of an individual or an organisation, cover digital and communications security, pay medical fees for defenders attacked or made ill by their work, and provide family assistance where a defender is imprisoned or their family is at risk. This payload already records a Georgian organisation operating while a prosecutor froze the bank accounts of several rights bodies and its own legal status was contested at the European Court — which is precisely the circumstance this grant exists for. AND THERE IS A 24-HOUR EMERGENCY LINE, WITH THE OPTION TO BE FORWARDED TO SOMEONE SPEAKING RUSSIAN, alongside a secure encrypted email channel for urgent assistance. The person who answers can mobilise rapid international support. Note the language list before a crisis rather than during one. IT ALSO OFFERS TEMPORARY RELOCATION, training on holistic and digital security, and a rest and respite programme for defenders under extreme stress — the last of which matters in a country where campaigns run for years. READ THE EXCLUSIONS CAREFULLY, BECAUSE THEY DEFINE WHAT THIS IS NOT: it will not fund projects addressing broader human rights issues rather than the specific situation of defenders, will not cover defenders already in exile, and will not pay ongoing office costs such as salaries and rent. This is protection money, not programme money. Based in Dublin. THE LIMIT: no case of its own in Georgia could be established from what was reached, and the organisation publishes no country eligibility list; its service is described as open to defenders at risk without a stated geographic restriction. Treat it as available and untested rather than confirmed.

trackers.name: Legal assistance centres — free lawyers on private property cases, in four cities, who will file in court
trackers.desc: THE TWO THINGS THAT MATTER ARE THE CASE TYPE AND THE FACT THAT THEY FILE. Its lawyers provide free legal consultations, help prepare legal documents, AND SUBMIT THEM TO COURT IF NECESSARY — and the case types it names first are those relating to PRIVATE PROPERTY. A free consultation that stops at advice leaves a community where it started; this is a service that will put a document in front of a judge. AND IT IS NOT ONLY IN THE CAPITAL: centres operate in Tbilisi, Kutaisi, Batumi and Zugdidi — which puts a free property lawyer within reach of western Georgia, the Black Sea coast and Samegrelo, in a country where this file has recorded that almost everything else it lists is Tbilisi-based. Published street addresses and telephone numbers exist for the regional offices. WHAT IT IS NOT: a specialist environmental or planning practice. The other case type it names is labour rights in public service, and nothing found shows it litigating a development scheme or an environmental permit. Approach it as a property lawyer — which, for a community whose land is being taken, expropriated, devalued or encroached on, is frequently the more precise framing anyway, and this file has recorded elsewhere in the region that the property route often succeeds where the environmental one does not. IT SITS INSIDE THE GEORGIAN CHAPTER OF AN INTERNATIONAL ANTI-CORRUPTION NETWORK, so a matter that involves a permit obtained irregularly, a discretionary exception, or an undisclosed beneficiary falls squarely within its parent organisation's core work — this file recorded in R131 that a Tbilisi park permit rested on a discretionary exception granted in haste, and in R119 that identifying who benefits is a distinct and harder exercise than identifying who breached. USE IT ALONGSIDE THE OTHER GEORGIAN ROUTES RECORDED HERE: the state legal aid service for representation where you qualify, the rights litigator for strategic cases and benefit-sharing arguments, and the international financial complaint routes where a lender is involved.

trackers.name: Georgian National Platform — a published member list, and an environment working group with named members
trackers.desc: THIS IS THE DIRECTORY OF GEORGIAN CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS THAT THIS FILE PREVIOUSLY RECORDED AS NOT EXISTING. It publishes a list of member organisations, each tagged with the working groups it belongs to — and WORKING GROUP 3 IS ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION, CLIMATE CHANGE AND ENERGY SECURITY, with its own group members page, its own subgroups and published minutes. A community that cannot find who works on its issue in Georgia should read that group's membership before searching anything else; this map has failed three separate times to reach the Georgian organisational layer by searching, and here it is listed. IT ALSO HAS REGIONAL REPRESENTATIVES, which matters in a country where nearly everything else in this file operates from Tbilisi. MEMBERSHIP BRINGS TWO THINGS A COMMUNITY ORGANISATION CAN USE DIRECTLY: access to a REGRANTING SCHEME, and participation in consultations organised by the Council of Europe, the World Bank and the EUROPEAN INVESTMENT BANK. That last one is the sharpest: where an international lender finances the scheme you are contesting, a seat in its consultations is a route this file has otherwise only reached through foreign accountability organisations. Members also get advocacy training and access to European networks. IT IS PROPERLY CONSTITUTED RATHER THAN INFORMAL: an elected coordination council of nine, chosen at a general meeting, with a charter, a code of ethics, a compliance committee, a secretariat operating since 2013, and a published route to join. It exists to represent Georgian civil society in the European Union's eastern partnership structures and to work with government on association agreement implementation. AND IT DEFENDS ITS MEMBERS PUBLICLY: it has issued statements on a draft transparency law of the kind this file has recorded shutting down civil society in Kyrgyzstan, and on a smear campaign against civil society experts in Georgia. A body that will put its name to a defence of organisations under attack is worth knowing before the attack comes. THE LIMITS: it is a general civil society and European integration platform, not an environmental organisation — it will not object to a scheme, assess one, or litigate. Its membership is organisational, so an unregistered village group is unlikely to qualify directly; use it as a directory and a route to members who can act.

trackers.name: IUCN NL Land Acquisition Fund — it pays for long-term rights over land, not only for buying it
trackers.desc: IT FUNDS THE ACQUISITION OF LONG-TERM MANAGEMENT RIGHTS WITHOUT ANY TRANSFER OF OWNERSHIP — long-term leases and conservation agreements — as well as outright purchase, with grants of up to around a hundred thousand euros to locally registered non-profit organisations. Read that against what this file has recorded in this country: a wildlife corridor declared by municipal decree without anyone's land being taken, pasture user unions legally authorised to hold and manage grazing land, and passports documenting who uses which pasture. THE MECHANISM THIS FUND PAYS FOR IS THE MECHANISM ALREADY IN USE HERE. ITS STRONGEST PRIORITY FOR A COMMUNITY FACING A SCHEME IS CONNECTIVITY: land that links fragmented habitat as a corridor or stepping stone, alongside sites holding critically endangered, endangered or vulnerable red list species and areas of recognised biodiversity value such as important bird areas. A scheme that severs a corridor creates exactly the case this fund exists to fund. THE LOCAL ORGANISATION HOLDS THE LAND AND THE RESPONSIBILITY, not the funder — the model is explicitly that the reserve belongs to the local body, which is familiar with the context and works with the community. ELIGIBILITY: locally registered as a non-profit, non-governmental or civil society organisation; directly responsible for the project; and holding A BANK ACCOUNT IN THE ORGANISATION'S OWN NAME in the country of establishment or of the project. An unregistered residents' group cannot apply alone and should work through one of the registered conservation bodies recorded elsewhere in this file. Annual call with a published spring deadline. Running since 2001 across more than forty countries. THE LIMITS, STATED PLAINLY: no project in this country was found in its published record, its examples run heavily to tropical habitats, and it funds acquisition rather than objection or litigation. Confirm eligibility with the fund before building an application around it.

trackers.name: Guardians of the Rioni Valley — the residents' movement that forced a government retreat on a dam
trackers.desc: THIS IS WHAT A COMMUNITY THAT WON LOOKS LIKE IN THIS COUNTRY, AND IT IS THE ONLY RESIDENTS' MOVEMENT THIS FILE HAS BEEN ABLE TO REACH HERE AFTER FOUR FAILED ATTEMPTS. Local residents along a river valley north of the country's third city organised against an eight-hundred-million-dollar hydropower cascade, and after months of protest the prime minister announced a SUSPENSION OF DAM CONSTRUCTION FOR NINE TO TWELVE MONTHS, a re-examination of environmental impact by foreign AND local experts, and a five-million-lari fund for the valley's development. WHAT MOVED PUBLIC OPINION WAS NOT THE ECOLOGY — IT WAS THE CONTRACT. Two facts became public and changed everything: that the state had transferred LAND TO THE COMPANY AT A SYMBOLIC PRICE, and that the CONFIDENTIAL AGREEMENT signed for the project contained onerous terms. This file has recorded elsewhere that following the money reaches places an environmental objection cannot; here is the clearest case in the payload. Ask what the land was sold for and what the agreement says before you argue about fish. THEIR CAMP EXISTED BECAUSE ONE OF THEM OWNED THE GROUND: the permanent protest camp at the construction area was pitched ON LAND BELONGING TO ONE OF THE ACTIVISTS. That is the practical precondition for a camp that cannot simply be cleared as trespass — and note that police removed it anyway, on the stated ground that the nearby river might flood it. THEIR DEMANDS WERE SPECIFIC AND WENT BEYOND THEIR OWN VALLEY: halt construction, ANNUL THE CONTRACT, impose a MORATORIUM ON ALL SUCH PROJECTS nationally, and open criminal proceedings over the approval. A demand list that names the contract and the sector is harder to buy off than one that names only the site. EXPECT WHAT THEY GOT: villages placed under police checkpoints, camps dismantled, and a campaign portraying them as enemies of energy independence, as backward, and as foreign agents — with an electricity price rise publicly blamed on them, and slander directed at a named leader. AND EXPECT ISOLATION: reporting records that the movement had only moderate support, or silence, from the capital's civil society organisations — which is the failure this file identified in Georgian campaigns generally. Two things broke that: a mass rally in the regional city rather than the capital, and support from a small number of named rights and environmental organisations recorded elsewhere in this file. TWO PIECES OF EVIDENCE THAT WORKED: an institute's computer simulation showing that a dam failure in an earthquake would send a thirty-four-metre wave into a city of that size — though the institute itself cautioned the modelling used incomplete data — and the fact that the SAME COMPANY'S EARLIER HYDROPOWER PLANT IN THIS COUNTRY COLLAPSED WITHIN TWO MONTHS of a four-hundred-million-euro investment. Check what the developer has already built and what happened to it. THE LIMITS: this is a movement, not a registered organisation, reachable through its public page; the project's later status is not established here; and a movement is a source of experience and solidarity rather than a service that will act for you.

trackers.name: ELAW — free scientific and legal backing for whichever lawyer takes your case
trackers.desc: IT DOES NOT TAKE YOUR CASE — IT ARMS THE LAWYER WHO DOES. A global alliance of attorneys and scientists supplying legal, scientific, SECURITY and organisational expertise to public interest lawyers, with more than three hundred advocates across over eighty countries and upwards of four hundred projects calling on it each year. ITS SCIENCE TEAM DOES EXACTLY WHAT THIS FILE HAS FOUND DECIDES CASES IN THIS COUNTRY: it CRITIQUES ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT ASSESSMENTS, SUBMITS EXPERT TESTIMONY TO COURTS, helps advocates explain technical matters to communities, builds systems to MONITOR environmental conditions, and RECOMMENDS CLEANER ALTERNATIVES to proposed projects. This payload recorded that Georgian campaigns turn on who wrote the assessment and on whether a project was wrongly held outside assessment scope, and that a court sent such a question back for an expert report; an independent critique of an assessment is the document that argument needs. AND IT DOES THE ONE THING THIS FILE IDENTIFIED AS MISSING HERE AND COULD NOT SUPPLY: IT FACILITATES ENGAGEMENT BETWEEN LOCAL SCIENTISTS AND LOCAL LAWYERS. A university with the data and an advocate with the case rarely find each other unaided; this exists to introduce them. ITS LAW TEAM HELPS PARTNERS BRING ENFORCEMENT ACTIONS, critique proposed statutes and REPLICATE MODEL LAWS FROM OTHER COUNTRIES — which matters where a community is told no law covers its situation, and where this file has recorded that a body elsewhere responded by drafting the legal framework it lacked. It also works explicitly on DEFENDING DEFENDERS, improving the safety of advocates under attack, and publishes guidebooks for challenging particular kinds of project. HOW TO USE IT: it works through PARTNERS — public interest lawyers in their own countries — rather than directly with communities. Find or instruct a local advocate first, then ask them to approach the alliance for scientific and legal support; the support is provided at no cost to the partner and the alliance describes its model as high impact at low cost. THE LIMITS: it will not represent you, fund your litigation or lobby your government. It is a support network for lawyers, and its reach in this region was not established here — ask whether it has partners in this country before relying on it. DO NOT CONFUSE IT WITH THE SIMILARLY NAMED ENVIRONMENTAL DEFENDER LAW CENTER recorded elsewhere in this file, which is a different organisation that finds pro bono lawyers.

trackers.name: ELKANA — a farmers' union of more than two thousand members that helped write the national biodiversity plan
trackers.desc: IT IS A UNION OF FARMERS AND ITS MEMBERSHIP IS OPEN TO ANY CITIZEN INTERESTED IN ORGANIC FARMING AND ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION — which means a rural household defending its land can join the body that already speaks for two thousand others. Founded in 1994, working with more than two thousand farmers across different regions, with a head office in the capital and TWO DEMONSTRATION AND CONSERVATION FARMS IN NAMED VILLAGES, one running since 1995 and one since 2004. This file failed four separate times to reach Georgia's community layer; this is a membership organisation rooted in it. ITS POLICY STANDING IS THE PART TO USE AGAINST A SCHEME: its experts were involved in drawing up THE AGRICULTURAL BIODIVERSITY COMPONENT OF THE COUNTRY'S FIRST AND SECOND NATIONAL BIODIVERSITY STRATEGY AND ACTION PLANS. A body that helped write the national plan is a body that can say authoritatively whether a project conflicts with it — and this file has recorded across the region that an objection framed against the state's own commitments travels further than one framed against a company. IT ALSO GIVES A COMMUNITY SOMETHING SPECIFIC TO PROTECT: it reintroduces INDIGENOUS WHEAT VARIETIES that were wiped out under the Soviet planned economy in the 1960s, putting them back into fields for local and commercial use, networked with mills, shops and restaurants. Land carrying rare local varieties is not interchangeable with land elsewhere, and a seed programme that documents which varieties grow where turns that from sentiment into a record. Its work also covers organic farming extension, training and advisory services, agro-ecological practice, and diversifying rural economic activity. ITS INTERNATIONAL MEMBERSHIPS MATTER MORE THAN THEY LOOK: it belongs to the European coordination of the global peasant movement, alongside seed and breed conservation, agricultural biodiversity and food sovereignty networks. The peasant movement in particular exists to defend land and seed rights, which gives a Georgian farming community a route to international solidarity that no other entry in this country's listing provides. THE LIMITS: it is an organic farming and rural development association, not an objector or a law practice — nothing found shows it opposing a mine, a dam or a road, and its subject is farming rather than planning. Use it for membership, for the varieties argument, for the national plan, and for the networks; take the objection to the litigators and the free lawyers recorded elsewhere in this file.

trackers.name: CASE — referral to lawyers, campaign help and emergency funding when a lawsuit is used to silence you
trackers.desc: WHEN A COMPANY OR AN OFFICIAL SUES A CAMPAIGNER TO SHUT THEM UP, THIS IS THE BODY THAT FINDS THEM HELP. It is a coalition of more than a hundred and twenty organisations across Europe and beyond, and it CONNECTS TARGETS OF ABUSIVE LAWSUITS TO THOSE WHO CAN ASSIST, drawing on a network of lawyers, NGOs and advocacy organisations for LEGAL EXPERTISE, CAMPAIGN ASSISTANCE AND EMERGENCY FUNDING where circumstances permit, plus published guidance on protecting yourself in advance. This file recorded that a residents' movement here faced a campaign portraying it as an enemy of energy independence and as foreign agents, with slander directed at a named leader, and that a national civil society platform issued a statement on a smear campaign against civil society experts. PREPARE FOR THE FORM THE ATTACK TAKES: its analysis finds such suits are COMMONLY BROUGHT AGAINST INDIVIDUALS rather than organisations, usually rely on DEFAMATION PROVISIONS, and claim a median of around fifteen thousand euros — an amount designed to ruin a person rather than an institution. Decide before a campaign starts who is named on statements and what support that person has. ITS DATABASE IS ALSO EVIDENCE IN ITSELF: more than thirteen hundred documented cases across dozens of countries, with the silenced subjects identified as corruption, government action, business practices and ENVIRONMENTAL CONCERNS. A court or a journalist shown that a claim fits a documented international pattern hears it differently from one shown a single aggrieved defendant. AND IF THE OTHER SIDE'S LAWYERS ARE THE WEAPON, IT PUBLISHES A LEGAL ETHICS REPORT ON HOW THE PROFESSION AND THE COURTS SHOULD PREVENT LAWYERS ENABLING SUCH ABUSE — the document to hand a bar association with a complaint. THE LIMITS: a coalition and a referral network rather than a law firm; it will not represent anyone; its emergency funding is conditional; and although this country sits within the wider European human rights system, the European Union's anti-SLAPP directive does not apply here. Pair it with the free legal centres and the rights litigator recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Aarhus Centre Georgia — it monitors public participation in impact assessments, and counsels citizens on the law
trackers.desc: IT DOES THE TWO THINGS THIS COUNTRY'S DISPUTES KEEP TURNING ON. It MONITORS PUBLIC PARTICIPATION DURING THE ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT PROCESS, and it PROVIDES LEGAL COUNSELLING TO CITIZENS ON ENVIRONMENTAL MATTERS — alongside facilitating access to environmental information and training people on the convention that underpins all three. This file has recorded here a valley movement that forced a construction moratorium and a development fund, a scheme declared to fall OUTSIDE ASSESSMENT SCOPE until a court overturned that determination, and campaigns that turned on who wrote the assessment. EVERY ONE OF THOSE IS A QUESTION ABOUT WHETHER THE PUBLIC WAS PROPERLY LET INTO THE ASSESSMENT — AND THIS IS AN INSTITUTION WHOSE PUBLISHED JOB IS TO WATCH EXACTLY THAT. If a hearing was not advertised, if comments were taken after a decision, if a scoping stage was skipped, that is the body to tell. THE LEGAL COUNSELLING MATTERS BECAUSE IT IS FREE AND EARLY. This map records litigators and free legal centres for this country, but a community usually needs an answer before it needs a lawyer — what the procedure requires, when the window opens, what documents must be published. KNOW THE NAME CHANGE OR YOU WILL THINK IT HAS CLOSED: established in 2005, it has SINCE 2013 BEEN TRANSFORMED INTO AN ENVIRONMENTAL INFORMATION AND EDUCATION CENTRE, which provides access to environmental education and to comprehensive information on the environment. Search both names. THE NETWORK BEHIND IT IS LARGE AND ITS REACH INTO THE COURTS IS REAL: sixty such centres operate across fourteen countries, and judges and representatives of national judicial training centres from this country and its neighbours have been trained specifically on the ACCESS TO JUSTICE pillar of the convention, alongside the chair of that convention's own task force on the subject. A judge who has been trained on those procedural requirements is a different audience for an argument about participation than one who has not. THE LIMITS: it is supported by an intergovernmental organisation and has been folded into a government-facing information and education function — IT IS NOT AN INDEPENDENT ADVOCATE, and it will not represent you or oppose a project. Counselling is advice, not representation. Use it to establish what the process owes you and to have a failure of participation recorded by an institution; take the case itself to the litigators, the free legal centres and the rights organisations recorded separately here.

trackers.name: Public Defender — it can file an amicus brief in your case, in the ordinary courts
trackers.desc: IT IS AUTHORISED TO EXERCISE THE AMICUS CURIAE FUNCTION AT THE COMMON COURTS AS WELL AS THE CONSTITUTIONAL COURT. THE COMMON COURTS ARE WHERE A LAND DISPUTE ACTUALLY SITS — which makes this the most directly usable court power found anywhere in this file's survey of complaints institutions. A community already in litigation over a permit, a valuation or an assessment can ask the Public Defender to submit a legal opinion in that case. An opinion from the constitutional watchdog, filed in your proceedings, is a weight no community can generate for itself. IT ALSO ANALYSES THE STATE'S LAWS, POLICIES AND PRACTICES AGAINST INTERNATIONAL STANDARDS AND ISSUES RECOMMENDATIONS. This file has recorded here a scheme declared outside assessment scope until a court overturned that determination, and a payload-wide finding that strategic environmental assessment is missing; a permitting regime, not only a permit, can be put to this office. ITS INDEPENDENCE IS PROTECTED BY STATUTE RATHER THAN BY CUSTOM: it exercises its functions independently, bound only by the Constitution, international treaties and law — and ANY INFLUENCE OR INTERFERENCE WITH ITS ACTIVITIES IS PROHIBITED AND PUNISHED BY LAW. Its powers sit in an organic law of 1996, and it also serves as the national preventive mechanism under the torture convention's optional protocol and as the body for the disability convention. THE LIMITS: an amicus brief is an OPINION, NOT REPRESENTATION — it does not become your lawyer, and this file records litigating organisations and free legal centres for this country that do. It advises and recommends; it does not decide. And it is a state office, so what you send it is disclosed to a public institution. Use it to add weight to a case already running, to have a permitting practice measured against international standards, and alongside the impact-assessment participation monitoring recorded separately here.

trackers.name: The cadastral map — see every registered plot, and who is buying around you
trackers.desc: AN OFFICIAL INTERACTIVE CADASTRAL MAP, WITH AN ENGLISH INTERFACE. It shows the geographic data uploaded to the public registry and lets you VIEW LAND PLOTS BY CADASTRAL CODE. Every parcel in this country carries a unique cadastral code in a fixed four-part format; it appears on the title deed, and it can also be found by looking up an address on the registry portal. USE IT TO CHECK THE PARCELS AROUND YOURS, NOT ONLY YOUR OWN. Schemes are assembled quietly, plot by plot, and a single buyer accumulating neighbouring parcels is the earliest warning a community gets — this file has recorded here a site sold at a symbolic price and agreements kept confidential, both of which show first in who owns what. AND THE REGISTRY IS NOT ONLY IN THE CAPITAL: it delivers its services through PUBLIC SERVICE HALLS, COMMUNITY CENTRES AND TERRITORIAL OFFICES as well as authorised users — so there is a physical counter to walk into outside the city, which matters when a lookup needs to become a certified extract. THE LIMITS: the map shows what has been REGISTERED, so unregistered, customary or disputed holdings may not appear as their occupants would describe them; and viewing a plot on a map is not the same as obtaining an extract naming its owner, which is a separate service and may carry a fee. NOTE THE RELATIONSHIP: the agency that maintains this map is ALREADY IN THE LIVE MAP as a separate entry. This is its cadastral map service rather than the agency itself — a different address doing a different job, and both are worth holding.

trackers.name: Small Grants Programme — a country strategy written jointly with civil society
trackers.desc: THE FEATURE WORTH ACTING ON IS HOW ITS STRATEGY IS MADE: THE COUNTRY PROGRAMME STRATEGY IS DESIGNED JOINTLY BY DONORS, GOVERNMENT, CIVIL SOCIETY AND ACADEMIA. That means the document deciding which landscapes and which themes get funded in this country is not handed down — civil society sits in its drafting. A community organisation that wants its valley, forest or wetland to be a funding priority should be asking who represents civil society in that process and when the strategy is next revised. THIS PAYLOAD HAS RECORDED MANY FUNDERS AND HAS NEVER BEFORE FOUND ONE WHOSE PRIORITIES A COMMUNITY CAN HELP WRITE. THE PROGRAMME WAS LAUNCHED HERE IN 2012 and is tailored to the specific needs of the country. It covers biodiversity conservation, climate change, INTERNATIONAL WATERS, LAND DEGRADATION, and chemicals and wastes, and alongside environmental benefits it is directed at poverty reduction, livelihood improvement, GENDER EQUALITY AND WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT. AND THE MONEY GOES STRAIGHT TO THE COMMUNITY'S OWN ORGANISATION. Grants are made directly to community-based organisations and non-governmental organisations rather than through an intermediary, which distinguishes this from almost every other funder in this file. WHAT TO DO FIRST: obtain the country programme strategy, read which landscapes it names, and establish whether your ground lies inside one — strategies commonly commit most of the funding to a few priority areas. Then find the national coordinator, and ask when the strategy will next be reviewed. THE LIMITS: the applicant must be a constituted organisation; co-financing of roughly half is normally expected THOUGH IT MAY BE IN KIND, meaning volunteer labour, land use and materials can be counted; and proposals must be framed as environmental work rather than as opposition to a particular scheme. Decisions are made by a national steering committee. Use it with the land acquisition fund and the cadastral map recorded separately for this country: the strategy sets the priorities, the fund can buy or lease, and the map shows what is where.

trackers.name: Registering land you already occupy — the free window closed, and what replaced it
trackers.desc: IF YOUR FAMILY USES LAND IT HAS NEVER REGISTERED, THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT THING IN THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING — AND THE EASY VERSION OF IT HAS JUST ENDED. Under the systemic registration reform, in areas fixed by ministerial order, THE AGENCY MEASURED PLOTS ON ITS OWN INITIATIVE, SEARCHED OUT THE DOCUMENTATION AND REGISTERED OWNERSHIP, across 59 MUNICIPALITIES — the whole country apart from the self-governing cities. THE PROGRAMME ENDED ON 1 JANUARY 2026. THE SUCCESSOR ROUTE IS NAMED AND MOST PEOPLE WILL NOT KNOW IT: THOSE WHO FOR OBJECTIVE REASONS COULD NOT USE THE REFORM BETWEEN 2022 AND 2025 MAY, FROM 1 JANUARY 2026, APPLY TO THE PUBLIC REGISTRY UNDER THE SPORADIC PROCEDURE. The door did not close; it changed shape and price. WHAT CHANGED, PRECISELY. REGISTERING A SELF-OCCUPIED PLOT IS NO LONGER FREE. The service and registration fee for the sporadic route — reported at six hundred lari — is to be reset by government decision, so CHECK THE CURRENT FIGURE BEFORE BUDGETING. AND THE MUNICIPAL LAND-RECOGNITION COMMISSIONS HAVE HAD THEIR POWERS SUSPENDED FOR A YEAR, which removes the local body that used to recognise possession. WHAT THE FREE PERIOD ACTUALLY COVERED IS WORTH KNOWING, BECAUSE IT SHOWS WHAT THESE STEPS NORMALLY COST: document search and systematisation, certification of the parties' signatures on a transaction, NOTARIAL MEDIATION, recognition of the ownership right, and constatation of facts were performed without charge, and registration itself carried no agency service fee. Under the paid route each of those is a cost line. TWO WARNINGS THAT DECIDE WHETHER AN APPLICATION SUCCEEDS. FIRST, AFTER YOU APPLY THE REGISTRY ALLOWS TEN DAYS FOR BOUNDARIES TO BE CLARIFIED — and where documents do not prove where the plot is and a municipal representative's testimony is not accepted, THE APPLICANT MUST GO TO THE NATIONAL BUREAU OF ENFORCEMENT TO HAVE THE FACTS ESTABLISHED. Have your evidence of location ready before you file: old photographs, utility connections, witnesses, anything dated. SECOND, AND IT CAUSES REAL DISPUTES: NEIGHBOURING PLOTS ARE NOT MEASURED AS PART OF THE PROCESS, WHICH CREATES A RISK OF OVERLAPPING REGISTRATIONS. Talk to your neighbours before filing, and if you can, agree boundaries between you first — a registered overlap is far harder to undo than an unregistered disagreement. THE LIMITS: this is legislation, not an organisation, and it has been amended repeatedly — most recently in December 2025 — so confirm the current text and fees. The agency that operates the registry appears elsewhere in this map for a different purpose entirely, as a COMPANY registry for finding firms and their directors; its land function is what matters here.

trackers.name: National heritage committee — the people who can answer a structural condemnation, and the resources centre behind them
trackers.desc: OLD BUILDINGS ARE RARELY DEMOLISHED BECAUSE SOMEONE ARGUES THEY ARE WORTHLESS. THEY ARE DEMOLISHED BECAUSE SOMEONE PRODUCES A REPORT SAYING THEY ARE STRUCTURALLY UNSOUND AND BEYOND SAVING. THIS IS THE NATIONAL COMMITTEE OF THE INTERNATIONAL BODY THAT ADVISES ON WORLD HERITAGE, AND IT RUNS TRAINING IN THE STRUCTURAL ANALYSIS AND CONSERVATION OF HISTORIC BUILDINGS — which makes it the one organisation in this country's listing equipped to meet that report on its own ground. ITS TECHNICAL DEPTH IS DOCUMENTED RATHER THAN CLAIMED. It has run an intensive week-long course on structural analysis and conservation of historic structures built on the methodology of the international scientific committee for structural analysis and restoration of architectural heritage; and A WOOD CONSERVATION COURSE DEVELOPED AND DELIVERED WITH NORWAY'S DIRECTORATE FOR CULTURAL HERITAGE IN NOVEMBER 2024, using the curriculum and methodology of the intergovernmental conservation centre's international wood conservation course. IN A COUNTRY WHOSE HISTORIC HOUSING IS LARGELY TIMBER, A BODY THAT TEACHES WOOD CONSERVATION TO INTERNATIONAL CURRICULUM IS THE ADDRESS FOR ANY ARGUMENT ABOUT WHETHER A WOODEN BUILDING CAN BE SAVED. IT ALSO OPERATES A HERITAGE RESOURCES CENTRE, which is where its courses are held — so there is a physical place, a library of practice and a body of trained people, not merely a committee name. WHAT TO ASK FOR, AND BE SPECIFIC: whether it will review the structural report relied on to condemn your building; whether any of its trained conservation specialists will inspect; and whether it will state, in writing and in its own name, what conservation of the structure would require and cost. THE LAST ONE MATTERS MOST — an owner or authority claiming a building cannot be saved is answered by a costed conservation method, not by objection. ITS INTERNATIONAL AFFILIATION IS ITSELF USEFUL. A national committee of the body that advises on world heritage speaks a language that ministries and international funders recognise, and its opinion travels further than a local petition. Where a site has any claim to national or international significance, an assessment from this quarter is the document to obtain first. THE LIMITS: it is a professional and scientific body, not a campaign group or a law firm. It will assess, train and advise; it will not litigate, buy land, or run your campaign, and nothing found shows it opposing developments as such. Its work is buildings and monuments rather than landscape or ecology. Use it with the free registration route, the cadastral map and the environmental legal resources recorded separately for this country — and note that this file has also logged a second heritage organisation here, an arts and culture centre recognised by a European heritage prize jury, which works with communities on traditional knowledge and crafts.

trackers.name: Treaty compliance committee — a member of the public can file against the state, and forest licensing has been challenged this way
trackers.desc: A COMMUNICATION TO THIS COMMITTEE MAY BE BROUGHT BY ONE OR MORE MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC ABOUT ANY STATE PARTY'S COMPLIANCE WITH THE TREATY ON ACCESS TO ENVIRONMENTAL INFORMATION, PUBLIC PARTICIPATION AND ACCESS TO JUSTICE. You do not need an organisation, a lawyer, or a domestic court victory to file. AND THIS COUNTRY HAS BEEN THERE BEFORE ON EXACTLY THE ISSUE THAT DECIDES LAND FIGHTS: a communication concerning it dealt with PUBLIC PARTICIPATION IN DECISION-MAKING ON THE ISSUANCE OF LICENCES FOR LONG-TERM FOREST USE. If your problem is that a long-term licence over land was granted without the public being properly involved, THAT IS A PATH ALREADY WALKED HERE. THE DATES ARE PUBLISHED AND CURRENT: SUBMISSIONS REACHING THE SECRETARIAT BY 28 SEPTEMBER 2026 ARE CONSIDERED FOR PRELIMINARY ADMISSIBILITY AT THE MEETING IN THE WEEK OF 9 TO 13 NOVEMBER 2026, if complete, in the REQUIRED FORMAT and needing no translation. English, French or Russian are accepted and the secretariat translates the latter two — BUT TRANSLATION COSTS YOU THE DEADLINE. ITS FINDINGS ALSO DEFINE WHAT THE STATE MUST DISCLOSE, WHICH IS USEFUL BEFORE YOU EVER FILE: government decrees on LAND USE AND PLANNING, feasibility studies, financial agreements, RENTAL CONTRACTS FOR LAND HELD BY A STATE FORESTRY FUND, and raw monitoring data have all been treated as environmental information. QUOTE THAT WHEN YOU ARE REFUSED — the refusal itself then becomes the evidence for a communication. WHAT SINKS SUBMISSIONS: anonymity; duplicating a pending case; trying to re-argue litigation lost at home; being brought by a state body; and above all INSUFFICIENT SUPPORTING INFORMATION. Build the file as you go — every request, refusal, notice period and hearing date — because the committee judges what you attach, not what you assert. THE LIMIT: this improves a state's compliance; IT IS NOT A REDRESS PROCEDURE FOR INDIVIDUAL RIGHTS and will not cancel a licence. It produces findings and recommendations, monitored over years. Pair it with the national information centre, the free registration route and the heritage committee recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Vreau Info (Moldova)
trackers.desc: Moldova's civic freedom-of-information request platform, built on the Alaveteli/mySociety software: you file an access-to-information request to a public authority through the site, and both the request and the authority's response — or its silence — are published in a public archive. USE IT: the archive shows which authorities answer and which do not, which is evidence in itself.

trackers.name: Portal of the Courts of Moldova
trackers.desc: Official national portal publishing decisions and case files of the Moldovan courts. · Find here: the unified portal of the courts of Moldova — case search and decisions.

trackers.name: State Chancellery — Access to Information
trackers.desc: National right-to-information implementation body; Moldova’s State Chancellery implements the 2023 Access to Information of Public Interest Law (Tromsø-aligned), with Ombudsman oversight, Moldova.

trackers.name: Eco-TIRAS — Asociaţia Internaţională a Păstrătorilor Râului
trackers.desc: The association of more than fifty environmental organisations across Moldova, including Transnistria, and Ukraine, built around the transboundary Dniester basin and registered under Moldovan law. WHO TO ENLIST: use it as the switchboard — if there is a local group anywhere in the basin, it is probably a member, and reaching the network is faster than finding one cold. You CAN: draw on its compilation of Moldovan environmental legislation, published in volumes on its own site, and on its scientific capacity, which is unusual for an NGO here — it developed a methodology for assessing hydropower impacts on river ecosystems and has surveyed riverbank erosion. It sits on the Dniester river commission it helped create, so it has a seat where basin decisions are taken. For activists: it has form on access to information, having pursued a case internationally under the Aarhus Convention after a state service demanded a very large fee for environmental data — worth citing if you are quoted a price for records.

trackers.name: EcoContact — Centrul Aarhus Chișinău / free environmental legal aid
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the association that has hosted Moldova's Aarhus environmental consultancy and information centre since 2013, and whose stated strategic aim is increasing public access to justice on environmental interests. It gives free legal assistance on environmental matters and has supported court actions on access to information, public participation and the protection of natural resources — reportedly more than fifty consultations across 2024-2025 — and it does not wait to be visited: in 2024 its teams reached 182 of the 187 localities in its target districts to offer free legal help on the spot. WHO IT SUITS: rural communities above all, and local councils, since it also drafts local environmental regulations covering grazing, mowing, recording of offences and transparency in decision-making. Two things that improve your odds: it runs the environmental-cases programme for judges and prosecutors at the National Institute of Justice, so the bench has been trained on exactly these questions, and it moderates a platform of over 230 environmental organisations and experts if the expertise you need is not in-house.

trackers.name: Court of Accounts
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Moldova, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: RISE Moldova
trackers.desc: Moldovan investigative group (OCCRP sister) tracking cross-border corruption and illicit money.

trackers.name: data.gov.md
trackers.desc: National — official government open data / budget portal. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this is the broad budget/open-data hub for how money is allocated overall — for the specific firms winning tenders use the procurement portal, and for findings of misspending use the supreme audit institution. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Moldova.

trackers.name: MTender
trackers.desc: Moldova's open public-procurement system built on the Open Contracting Data Standard. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Moldova, and for how much.

trackers.name: MTender (Public e-Procurement System)
trackers.desc: Moldova's official digital public-procurement service (Ministry of Finance), publishing all public tenders and procurement decisions online in real time via a government portal and open-data database, so citizens can watch how state and local budgets are spent.

trackers.name: National Integrity Authority (ANI)
trackers.desc: Legislator / public-official financial interest & asset declarations.

trackers.name: Public Services Agency (ASP)
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Constitutional Court of Moldova
trackers.desc: Constitutional Court of Moldova — supreme court (Moldova).

trackers.name: National Bureau of Statistics
trackers.desc: Moldova's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Moldova.

trackers.name: Ziarul de Gardă
trackers.desc: Moldovan investigative newspaper exposing corruption and abuse of public office.

trackers.name: Fondul Național pentru Mediu — the fund that replaced the one you will find first
trackers.desc: CHECK THE NAME BEFORE YOU APPLY. Searching for Moldovan environmental funding surfaces the Fondul Ecologic Național across many government pages — created by Government Decision 988 of 26.09.98 under Law 1515/1993 — but it has been superseded. Law 54/2022 and Government Decision 711/2022 established the Fondul Național pentru Mediu within the state budget, exclusively for projects in environmental protection, climate change and sustainable management of natural resources. Its size is set by the annual state budget law and its money runs through the single treasury account. It is administered by the supervisory committee of ONIPM, the National Office for Implementation of Environmental Projects, which now issues the calls. AN EXISTING COMMITMENT DID NOT LAPSE: programmes the old fund's administrative council had already decided to finance — including drinking water and sanitation projects — transferred to the new Fund's administrator. The stated reason for reform was that the old arrangement limited environmental activity, and that better management would bring more transparency, equality and equity.

trackers.name: ONIPM — where the calls are actually announced
trackers.desc: WATCH THIS, NOT A STANDING WINDOW. ONIPM announces numbered calls approved by its supervisory committee — for example Apel nr. 04/2025, aimed at selecting investment projects to develop, modernise and extend recycling infrastructure for plastic, paper and packaging waste. Each call targets a defined theme, so the question is not whether the fund is open but whether a call matching your work is live. ELIGIBILITY SHAPE, from the predecessor fund: local public administration bodies, institutions, enterprises and civil society organisations of Moldova could apply, with restrictions on organisations already holding a grant — check the current regulation for the equivalent rule before assuming a second application is possible. ANOTHER ROUTE: a UNDP-GEF project on conservation and sustainable management of wetlands, focused on high nature value areas in the Prut basin and working with the Prutul de Jos Biosphere Reserve — the kind of programme a local group partners with rather than applies to.

trackers.name: Energy Community — private bodies may complain, and refusal is appealable
trackers.desc: A COMPLAINT MECHANISM WHERE REFUSAL BY THE GATEKEEPER CAN BE TAKEN OVER ITS HEAD — which is rare, and is the reason to know about this. Under Article 90 of the Energy Community Treaty, private bodies may approach the Secretariat with complaints about a Party's non-compliance, and under Article 12.2 of the Consolidated Rules the Secretariat initiates procedures in response to a complaint by a private body as well as on its own initiative. AND IF THE SECRETARIAT DECLINES: the revised Rules give the complainant the right to approach the Permanent High Level Group directly, which may hear the complaint directly or initiate a preliminary procedure — in most systems recorded in this map, a secretariat declining to act ends the matter. The PHLG can also take interim measures in matters of urgency under Article 47(c) — that is what matters when works are already under way, so ask for it expressly. THE ENVIRONMENTAL ACQUIS IS IN SCOPE, including the EIA Directive as amended by 2014/52, which was to be transposed by 1 January 2019. CHECK THE TRANSPOSITION DEADLINE FOR THE DIRECTIVE YOU RELY ON — failure to transpose by the stated date is itself the non-compliance, and is a far simpler case than arguing about how a rule was applied. THE REALISTIC WIN CONDITION: a case opens with an Opening Letter, escalates to a Reasoned Opinion giving two months to rectify, then to the Ministerial Council — but a case closes whenever the Party complies, and many are recorded as complied with before any decision was adopted. The opening of proceedings is the lever, not the final decision. YOU CAN ALSO JOIN AN EXISTING CASE: interested third parties may access the case file and submit written observations, provided they substantiate their legitimate interest. Case law from Opening Letters is published with dates and numbers, so precedent is visible. Write to the Energy Community Secretariat, Am Hof 4, 1010 Vienna. ONE MORE ROUTE: the amended Rules provide for cooperation with national authorities and courts, giving concrete assistance to national courts on the interpretation of Energy Community law — a domestic judge unsure how an EU-derived rule applies can be pointed at it.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: ELAW — free attorneys and scientists who will critique the developer's EIA
trackers.desc: IT WILL READ THE DEVELOPER'S EIA AND TELL YOU WHAT IS WRONG WITH IT — which is the thing a community cannot produce alone and usually cannot afford. ELAW is a global alliance of attorneys, scientists and other advocates, founded 1989 in Eugene, Oregon by public interest lawyers from ten countries, that provides legal and scientific support to grassroots advocates to challenge destructive projects. FOUR CONCRETE FORMS OF HELP: legal support to local public interest lawyers; scientific support, including critiquing environmental assessments; economic insights on projects; and security expertise — ‘ELAW helps environmental lawyers improve their security so they can work without fear. When our partners are targeted, we act quickly to help defend and protect them.’ That last one is a named function, not an aspiration, and ELAW co-founded the Alliance for Land, Indigenous and Environmental Defenders. HOW TO USE IT — THROUGH A LAWYER, NOT AS A CLIENT: ELAW works through more than 300 public interest advocates in its network, and its stated strategy is ‘locating strong lawyers who are committed to protecting the environment in their home countries’. You can approach ELAW directly, but the leverage is greatest when a local advocate is the conduit — that is how the network is built. It has hosted nearly 300 advocates from more than 65 countries as Fellows and provided support on thousands of cases; several partners have won the Goldman Environmental Prize. Focus areas include biodiversity, fossil fuels — expressly assisting advocates in contesting fossil fuel development projects — plastic pollution, and work with coastal communities.
