AND A WARNING FROM THE CASE LAW IT CITES: where claimants FAILED TO SEEK ENFORCEMENT OF THE AGREEMENT ON COMPENSATION for expropriated properties, THERE IS NO LEGAL BASIS ON WHICH THEY COULD CLAIM PAYMENT in civil proceedings. A compensation agreement that is never enforced can be lost entirely.

trackers.name: Bosnian expropriation case law — the right to compensation for a road built on your land DOES NOT EXPIRE
trackers.desc: THE HOLDING THAT MATTERS MOST TO ANYONE WHOSE LAND WAS SIMPLY TAKEN: part of the courts hold that THE CONSTRUCTION OF A PUBLIC ROAD WITHOUT A DECISION ON THE TAKING OF POSSESSION of a natural person's property CONSTITUTES FACTUAL DISPOSSESSION, which is the basis for exercising the right to compensation under the Expropriation Act — AND THAT THE RIGHT TO THIS COMPENSATION DOES NOT BECOME TIME-BARRED. No limitation period on a claim for land taken without procedure means an old, unremedied taking is still actionable — which is the opposite of what most owners assume. AND WHY: the right to peaceful enjoyment of property, and the prohibition on its taking except in the public interest, is guaranteed by PROTOCOL NUMBER 1 TO THE EUROPEAN CONVENTION ON HUMAN RIGHTS, so THE RULES ON LIMITATION OF CLAIMS FROM THE LAW ON OBLIGATIONS DO NOT APPLY to the protection of that right. AND THE POINT THAT STOPS A DEVELOPER'S DEFENCE: such a dispute CANNOT BE RESOLVED by applying the provisions on ACQUIRING OWNERSHIP BY BUILDING ON ANOTHER'S LAND, because the structure has become A PUBLIC GOOD IN GENERAL USE. The page also records that the investor who undertook by contract to deposit the funds needed to pay compensation was held liable JOINTLY AND SEVERALLY with the public body.

trackers.name: Koalicija za zaštitu rijeka BiH — it turns up for villages, and it got them a lawyer
trackers.desc: WHAT THE COALITION ACTUALLY DID FOR ONE VILLAGE, told by the villagers: residents had been resisting FOR MORE THAN A MONTH BY PEACEFUL GATHERING against the construction of small hydroelectric plants on the river of the same name, and the coalition came to them. Bosnia is joint-smallest bucket in this file. AND THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST TO ANY COMMUNITY STANDING ON A BRIDGE, from a named villager: THE HYDROELECTRIC PLANTS WILL NOT BE BUILT ON THIS RIVER. BY ENGAGING A LAWYER WE GAVE OUR STRUGGLE A SERIOUS DIMENSION. THE LAWYER NOTICED, FROM THE EXISTING DOCUMENTATION, A SERIES OF IRREGULARITIES IN THE PROCEDURES THAT HAD BEEN CARRIED OUT, AND THAT IS WHAT WE ARE RELYING ON. The irregularities were already in the papers the developer itself had filed — a lawyer reading the existing file, not new evidence, is what changed the case. AND WHAT THE COALITION BROUGHT BESIDES BODIES, in its own representative's words: WE PROMISED TO HELP YOU AND WE DID. ABOUT THE EVENTS IN this village WE INFORMED THE OSCE, THE UNDP AND THE DELEGATION OF THE EUROPEAN UNION. WE ASKED FOR SUPPORT FROM ALL OVER THE WORLD FROM OUR PARTNER ORGANISATIONS AND WE RECEIVED IT. A national coalition can put a local dispute in front of the OSCE, the UN and the EU delegation in a week — access a village committee does not have on its own.

trackers.name: The Doljanka open letter — TWENTY named Bosnian organisations that co-sign for a village
trackers.desc: A READY-MADE DIRECTORY OF ALLIES, because the letter prints every signatory with its town: WOMEN OF KRUSCICA; an ECOLOGICAL-HUMANITARIAN ASSOCIATION in Fojnica; GREENS-NERETVA in Konjic; an ECO ASSOCIATION in Buna; a village group for the Doljanka in Jablanica; the CENTRE FOR THE ENVIRONMENT in Banja Luka; a CENTRE in Olovo; ECO ELEMENT in Bugojno; the AARHUS CENTRE IN BiH in Sarajevo; LABORATORIUM in Tuzla; the CENTRE FOR KARST AND SPELEOLOGY in Sarajevo; ARBOR MAGNA in Banja Luka; GREEN TEAM in Novi Grad; ECO FORUM in Zenica; a group in Kruscica; a town association in Vares; a MYCOLOGICAL ASSOCIATION in Sarajevo; SANUS in Prijedor; EKUS in Bihac; the COALITION FOR THE PROTECTION OF RIVERS OF BiH; ECO ACTION in Sarajevo; and ONE CITY ONE STRUGGLE in Sarajevo. Twenty organisations across both entities, each with a named town, is the contact list a Bosnian village would otherwise spend a year assembling — and they co-sign for communities they have no local stake in. AND THE ARITHMETIC THE LETTER PUTS TO A COUNCIL, which transfers to any small scheme: such plants NEED TWO OR THREE JOBS FOR THEIR DAILY FUNCTIONING, IF THAT, BECAUSE EVERYTHING IS AUTOMATED, and the promised municipal revenue amounts to ABOUT AS MUCH AS THE ANNUAL RENT OF A MEDIOCRE BUSINESS PREMISES IN SARAJEVO. Comparing the promised revenue to an ordinary commercial rent is the cheapest way to deflate a jobs-and-income case.

trackers.name: The state free-legal-aid centre — who it is for, and the honest test of whether you qualify
trackers.desc: THE PUBLIC LEGAL-AID BODY A BOSNIAN RESIDENT CAN BE SENT TO, named with its founding statute: IF YOU NEED EXPERT LEGAL HELP, YOU CAN APPROACH THE CENTRE FOR THE PROVISION OF FREE LEGAL AID in a named city. Bosnia is among the least-worked buckets in this file. AND WHAT IT IS: under the law on free legal aid, THE CENTRE FOR FREE LEGAL AID IS A REPUBLICAN ADMINISTRATIVE ORGANISATION WITHIN THE MINISTRY OF JUSTICE, FOUNDED BY THE GOVERNMENT, with the aim of providing legal aid TO NATURAL PERSONS, CITIZENS... AND OTHER PERSONS WHO ARE ON THE TERRITORY. AND THE ELIGIBILITY TEST, stated plainly: it is for those IDENTIFIED AS SOCIALLY VULNERABLE CATEGORIES, WHO ARE NOT IN A POSITION TO MEET THE COSTS OF REPRESENTATION IN PROCEEDINGS FOR THE REALISATION OF THEIR RIGHTS AND LEGALLY BASED INTERESTS BEFORE THE COURTS. The test is whether you can afford representation, not what your case is about — so a planning or environmental dispute is inside the scheme if the person is, which is the same gateway recorded for Montenegro in batch614. HONEST LIMIT WORTH STATING: this centre is an organ of ONE of the country's two entities and serves people on that entity's territory, so a resident elsewhere in Bosnia should expect to be directed to a different body; and the page frames it as the fallback IF YOU NEVERTHELESS NEED EXPERT LEGAL HELP, after self-help routes.

trackers.name: Agency for Information and Privacy (AIP)
trackers.desc: Agency for Information and Privacy (AIP) — Kosovo’s Agency for Information and Privacy overseeing the Law on Access to Public Documents (No. 06/L-081) and adjudicating access-to-information appeals. — Holds to account: Kosovo’s public bodies on disclosure — find access-to-information appeal decisions, guidance and annual reports.

trackers.name: Information and Privacy Agency (Kosovo)
trackers.desc: Information and Privacy Agency (Kosovo) — Kosovo’s national data-protection / information authority, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Constitutional Court of Kosovo
trackers.desc: Final authority on constitutional interpretation and judicial review in Kosovo, publishing its judgments. · Find here: the decisions of the Constitutional Court of Kosovo.

trackers.name: dumeditë — FOI requests (XKX)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (FOI request platform); dumeditë — civic Freedom-of-Information request platform (Alaveteli/mySociety network) — lets citizens file public-records requests and publishes the requests and the authorities’ responses in a public archive.

trackers.name: ARBK – Kosovo Business Registration Agency
trackers.desc: National — central commercial register of Kosovo (fully electronic, searchable). — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: e-Procurement Kosovo
trackers.desc: National public-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Kosovo, and for how much.

trackers.name: National Audit Office (ZKA)
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Kosovo, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) of Kosovo
trackers.desc: Financial intelligence unit of XKS — receives and analyses suspicious-transaction reports to counter money laundering.

trackers.name: Neni 24 mbrojtja paraprake — protection before designation
trackers.desc: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO WAIT FOR DESIGNATION TO GET PROTECTIVE EFFECT. Under neni 24 of Ligji nr. 03/L-233 për Mbrojtjen e Natyrës, an area is placed under preliminary protection by decision where the Institute determines on professional justification that it has the characteristics of a protected area and/or where the procedure for taking it under protection has begun. The trigger is disjunctive — either limb suffices — so getting the Institute to state that an area has the characteristics is itself the intervention. This is the second such instrument in this map, alongside Bosnia's privremena zaštita. NENI 23 — WHO CAN UNDO PROTECTION: where a municipality-declared area loses the values for which it was protected, the body that protected it may terminate protection only after prior consent of the Ministry — but that consent is not required where termination comes by law or by a sub-legal act of the Government. So a municipality cannot unilaterally de-protect what it protected, while the Government can; the route by which de-protection is attempted tells you which safeguard applies. Municipalities do hold a nature-protection role — the law names the organi kompetent i komunës. DEFINITIONS THAT DO WORK: peizazh expressly includes elements of civilisation; përbërësit e natyrës names fossils and rocks among the components of nature; and përtëritja e natyrës defines restoration as returning damaged diversity to a state approximating the original.

trackers.name: Kosovo Institute for Nature Protection — approach it first
trackers.desc: THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT BODY TO APPROACH FIRST, because it is the Institute whose professional justification triggers preliminary protection under neni 24. It is the central institution for nature conservation and for monitoring the state of protected natural values in Kosovo, sitting within AMMK, with a lineage from a nature-protection unit formed in 1968 inside the body for protection of cultural monuments, later separated into its own Enti and given statutory footing by the 1988 law on protection and development of natural values (article 78.2). SCALE, from the Ministry's Raport për Gjendjen e Natyrës 2010–2014: 116 protected areas covering 118,913.95 ha, or 10.9 percent of Kosovo — 11 strict nature reserves, 2 national parks (Sharri and Bjeshkët e Nemuna) and 99 nature monuments, among them the source of the White Drin with the Radavc Cave, the Gadime Cave, the Mirusha Waterfalls and the Rugova Gorge. NOTE THE DISTRIBUTION: 99 of 116 protected areas are nature monuments. That is the working category here, and it covers caves, waterfalls, gorges, springs and individual trees — so for a single feature, the monument is the realistic ask. Sources differ on whether the law sets six or seven categories; this entry does not resolve that — read the current text.

trackers.name: KCSF — it funds unregistered initiatives and individual activists
trackers.desc: NO INCORPORATION REQUIRED — which removes the commonest barrier in this entire map. The Kosovar Civil Society Foundation, mobilising resources since 1998, states that it provides grant instruments for civil society initiatives — NGOs, unregistered initiatives and individual activists — through a people-centred approach. That puts Kosovo alongside Bhutan, Andorra and the Pacific Development and Conservation Trust as places where a community group need not register first. DISTINGUISH THE INSTRUMENTS: Engagement for Joint Action (EJA Kosovo) gives grants plus capacity building, with an annual Democracy Award; Organisational Development Grants (ODGs) fund the development of the organisation itself rather than a project — where the problem is that your group cannot sustain the work, that is the instrument, and few funders anywhere in this map offer it; and small project grants are for concrete results within a set timeframe. It also runs a Resource Centre, and the Kosovo Resource Centre with Community Building Mitrovica. ALIGN WITH ITS STATED DIRECTION: KCSF has added resource diversification to increase local ownership and sustainability, including support from the private sector, diaspora, citizens and public funds — a proposal showing domestic co-support now matches where it says it is going.

trackers.name: EU Civil Society Facility — the Green Agenda is the named object
trackers.desc: AN ENVIRONMENTAL PROPOSAL IS NOT SQUEEZING INTO A DEMOCRACY PROGRAMME HERE — it is the programme's stated purpose. The EU Office in Kosovo's Civil Society Facility & Media Programme 2024–25 allocation (EuropeAid/183890/DD/ACT/XK) sought proposals to strengthen participatory democracy and EU integration ‘through an enhanced contribution by civil society to the implementation of the Green Agenda in the Western Balkans’. HOW IT RUNS: a concept note stage first — the 2024 allocation set 19 May 2025 at 15:00 — with guidelines and annexes as a single ZIP, calls published on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal. A RULE THAT SHAPES YOUR CONSORTIUM: a lead applicant may not be awarded more than one grant under a call and nor may a co-applicant, so one organisation can appear in at most two submitted applications — once as lead, once as co-applicant, under two different lots. Grantees must collaborate with the EU-funded TACSO project. GET IN BEFORE THE CALL OPENS: EU TACSO runs online consultations with potential beneficiaries on the priority sectors and themes of planned calls, and webinars on applying in English with interpretation into Albanian and Serbian — attending the consultation is how a theme gets into a call. AND LOOK FOR THE SUB-GRANT LAYER, NOT BRUSSELS: under Green Horizons, the EU and CARE Deutschland allocated EUR 80,000 in sub-grants to 8 local organisations for 8–10 month projects in urban gardening, waste recycling and renewable energy. Eight grants averaging EUR 10,000 is the realistic community-end scale.

trackers.name: Energy Community — private bodies may complain, and refusal is appealable
trackers.desc: A COMPLAINT MECHANISM WHERE REFUSAL BY THE GATEKEEPER CAN BE TAKEN OVER ITS HEAD — which is rare, and is the reason to know about this. Under Article 90 of the Energy Community Treaty, private bodies may approach the Secretariat with complaints about a Party's non-compliance, and under Article 12.2 of the Consolidated Rules the Secretariat initiates procedures in response to a complaint by a private body as well as on its own initiative. AND IF THE SECRETARIAT DECLINES: the revised Rules give the complainant the right to approach the Permanent High Level Group directly, which may hear the complaint directly or initiate a preliminary procedure — in most systems recorded in this map, a secretariat declining to act ends the matter. The PHLG can also take interim measures in matters of urgency under Article 47(c) — that is what matters when works are already under way, so ask for it expressly. THE ENVIRONMENTAL ACQUIS IS IN SCOPE, including the EIA Directive as amended by 2014/52, which was to be transposed by 1 January 2019. CHECK THE TRANSPOSITION DEADLINE FOR THE DIRECTIVE YOU RELY ON — failure to transpose by the stated date is itself the non-compliance, and is a far simpler case than arguing about how a rule was applied. THE REALISTIC WIN CONDITION: a case opens with an Opening Letter, escalates to a Reasoned Opinion giving two months to rectify, then to the Ministerial Council — but a case closes whenever the Party complies, and many are recorded as complied with before any decision was adopted. The opening of proceedings is the lever, not the final decision. YOU CAN ALSO JOIN AN EXISTING CASE: interested third parties may access the case file and submit written observations, provided they substantiate their legitimate interest. Case law from Opening Letters is published with dates and numbers, so precedent is visible. Write to the Energy Community Secretariat, Am Hof 4, 1010 Vienna. ONE MORE ROUTE: the amended Rules provide for cooperation with national authorities and courts, giving concrete assistance to national courts on the interpretation of Energy Community law — a domestic judge unsure how an EU-derived rule applies can be pointed at it.

trackers.name: ELAW — free attorneys and scientists who will critique the developer's EIA
trackers.desc: IT WILL READ THE DEVELOPER'S EIA AND TELL YOU WHAT IS WRONG WITH IT — which is the thing a community cannot produce alone and usually cannot afford. ELAW is a global alliance of attorneys, scientists and other advocates, founded 1989 in Eugene, Oregon by public interest lawyers from ten countries, that provides legal and scientific support to grassroots advocates to challenge destructive projects. FOUR CONCRETE FORMS OF HELP: legal support to local public interest lawyers; scientific support, including critiquing environmental assessments; economic insights on projects; and security expertise — ‘ELAW helps environmental lawyers improve their security so they can work without fear. When our partners are targeted, we act quickly to help defend and protect them.’ That last one is a named function, not an aspiration, and ELAW co-founded the Alliance for Land, Indigenous and Environmental Defenders. HOW TO USE IT — THROUGH A LAWYER, NOT AS A CLIENT: ELAW works through more than 300 public interest advocates in its network, and its stated strategy is ‘locating strong lawyers who are committed to protecting the environment in their home countries’. You can approach ELAW directly, but the leverage is greatest when a local advocate is the conduit — that is how the network is built. It has hosted nearly 300 advocates from more than 65 countries as Fellows and provided support on thousands of cases; several partners have won the Goldman Environmental Prize. Focus areas include biodiversity, fossil fuels — expressly assisting advocates in contesting fossil fuel development projects — plastic pollution, and work with coastal communities. It publishes guidebooks, including one to give communities sufficient understanding to challenge oil and gas projects, and clause-level summaries of national EIA law — so its site is also a route to learning exactly what your own EIA law requires. ASK WHETHER ELAW HAS A PARTNER IN YOUR COUNTRY: the network is described as spanning 70 to 80 countries but the member list is not published country by country, so this entry does not assert a presence in yours.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: EC Ma Ndryshe — builds the neighbourhood group and watches the permits (Kosovo)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Kosovo organisation working on local governance, urban structure and cultural heritage, with offices at Fehmi Lladrovci 94 in Prizren and in Prishtina. Its stated method is community mobilisation and oversight of public decision-making. It has built local community groups at neighbourhood and village level across Prizren municipality and has been extending that practice to other Kosovo municipalities since 2018 — so the offer is not only advice on your case but help constituting the group that will carry it. WHAT IT DOES ON A LIVE CASE: it takes concerns from residents, obtains the official file from the competent institutions, and compares what was consented with what is being built. In one Prizren Historic Centre case both the Regional Centre for Cultural Heritage and the municipal Inspectorate confirmed the works did not match the approved project, and the Inspectorate imposed stop measures. It sends information requests to other institutions and publishes what comes back, including where a building inside the Historic Centre was demolished without heritage consent, and where works began on premises part-owned by the mayor's son. IT ALSO PUBLISHES THE GROUNDWORK: it has produced its own analysis of spatial planning in Kosovo municipalities covering unpermitted construction with Prizren as the case study, and it records that in the first half of 2012 alone 62 consents were issued for building or intervention inside Prizren's Historic Centre, with a considerable number of those works departing from the approved project. That is the context a Kosovar community needs before it assumes its case is unusual. WHAT IT IS NOT: not a land buyer and not a law firm. It works on urban space, heritage and municipal governance, it names the shortage of reliable data and its own financial sustainability as standing challenges, and its reach outside those themes is limited.

trackers.name: Balkan Green Foundation — sub-grants to local groups, and the SLAPP warning (Kosovo)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES FOR A LOCAL GROUP: with the Institute for Development Policy it has run sub-granting schemes putting money directly into small Kosovar organisations — one project supported 59 local NGO project ideas across Kosovo with a total of €355,000, funded through the EU Office in Kosovo, in environmental protection, green energy and circular economy. Its current work includes empowering environmental civil society organisations in Kosovo with partners including Emancipimi Civil Ma Ndryshe, which is already in this file, and Let's Do It Peja and 7 Arte. Kosovo had no funder at all before this. WHAT IT SUPPLIES BESIDES MONEY: independent data and analysis, tracking of public and international funds, and convening of regional coalitions, working with municipalities across the Western Balkans. If your case turns on whether a scheme was properly financed or permitted, this is the organisation that follows those numbers in this region. READ THIS BEFORE YOU PUT YOUR NAME ON ANYTHING IN KOSOVO. The Deçan hydropower case shows both what is possible and what it costs. Civil society organisations and a local political coordinator filed suit in the Basic Court over environmental and operating permits; the Supreme Court ultimately held that three of the company's small hydropower plants must be shut down and confirmed the permits had not been handled by the book. But the company sued an environmental activist for €100,000 for defamation after she documented the damage, and sued a Deçan activist for €10,000 — lawsuits Amnesty International classified as SLAPPs intended to intimidate and silence them. The suits were later announced as withdrawn unconditionally. A Kosovar community should assume that naming a developer publicly may draw a personal lawsuit, and should line up organisational backing before an individual signs anything. WHAT IT IS NOT: a foundation, an analyst and a re-granter — not a law firm, not a land buyer.

trackers.name: FIQ — Forumi për Iniciativa Qytetare: grants and mentoring for informal groups (Kosovo)
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: a Kosovar foundation founded around 2000–2001 by young community activists after the war, whose stated mission is to mobilise citizens and empower them to claim their rights and hold authorities to account. It has promoted local philanthropy since 2009. Note the address change: its site has moved to fiqorg.com from the older fiq-fci.org. WHAT ITS GRANT PROGRAMME OFFERS, AND THE ELIGIBILITY IS THE POINT: financial assistance and mentoring to local CSOs, informal groups, networks and innovative initiatives, to help them carry out meaningful community actions. Grants have ranged from €1,000 to €63,000, with sub-granting to over 42 local organisations and more than €280,000 given since the programme began in 2009. A group with no legal registration is explicitly inside the scope, and the range means both a small survey and a substantial piece of work are fundable. HOW IT DECIDES, WHICH TELLS YOU HOW TO APPROACH IT: it describes a triangular approach — involving community members of different target groups directly in community discussions, alongside representatives of local community-based organisations, local government and the private sector. Come with the community in the room, not with a paper application from outside it. IT ALSO WORKS ON ENVIRONMENT DIRECTLY: its sustainable development programme addresses economy, energy and environment, and its own framing is that local communities are the best place to develop civic activism and improve the environment for citizens. ONE CAVEAT ON ITS LARGER CALLS: some of its EU-funded schemes, including matching grants for coalitions of local organisations, have required applicants to be legally registered for at least a year with full tax and registration documents, and to co-fund. The small-grant route takes informal groups; the coalition route does not. Ask which call you are looking at. KOSOVO NOW HAS TWO FUNDERS in this file, this and the foundation filed in batch 108, plus the community-organising body from batch 32.

trackers.name: ERA Group, Peja — works across the Kosovo, Montenegro and Albania borders on rivers and lynx
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Environmentally Responsible Action, established 2003 in Peja, working on nature protection alongside tourism promotion, alpinism, cycling and ski touring. Kosovo's bucket held funders and a neighbourhood organiser but no body doing nature protection and species work. WHAT IT HAS ACTUALLY WORKED ON: many areas of wildlife conservation, most notably the study and protection of the endangered Balkan lynx, and the protection of rivers and their ecosystems in Kosovo and beyond. If a Kosovar river or mountain site is threatened, this is the organisation with the field record on both. THE CROSS-BORDER PART, which matters because these mountains are shared: it is a member of international associations and works with Mountain club Hajla and PSKH Hrid in Montenegro and the Valbona NGO in Albania, all operating in the bordering areas. It coordinated a trek across three countries promoting the Balkan Peace Park project, and hosted the meeting at which participating NGOs established a Coalition of NGOs for the Balkan Peace Park. A threat on one side of these borders has organised counterparts on the other two. IT ALSO RAN A COMMUNITY PROCESS: with Milieukontakt of the Netherlands and two other local organisations it implemented the Green Agenda — a community-driven initiative working towards sustainable development — in three communities: Istog, Rugova (Peja) and Prizren. That is a named participatory method already run in Kosovar villages. PRACTICAL: based at the Haxhi Zeka Mill cultural heritage site, V. Gërvalla street, Peja; info@eradirect.org; +383 49 204 421; contact person Fatos Lajçi, who is also credited as a naturalist and film-maker and helped gather residents' questionnaires in the Bjeshkët e Nemuna settlements ahead of the area's declaration as a national park. Its members speak English, German, Italian and Serbian. HONEST NOTE: it has described itself as volunteer-based with projects completed on a volunteer basis, so expect capacity limits.

trackers.name: Free Legal Aid in Kosovo — the state agency, six accredited NGOs, and a phone line
trackers.desc: THE STRUCTURE, WHICH IS THE USEFUL PART: the Constitution of Kosovo defines free legal aid as a basic human right, and the law guarantees it in civil cases, administrative cases, minor offences and criminal procedures, to individuals meeting certain legal and financial criteria. The government's Free Legal Aid Agency partners with NGOs across Kosovo, of which six are accredited to provide free legal aid. Administrative cases are named — that is the category a permit challenge falls into. Kosovo's bucket held funders, registries and two organising bodies, and no legal ally. ONE OF THE SIX, IN DETAIL: the Kosovo Law Institute's Legal Aid Center, operating since March 2019 under an Access to Justice programme, offering legal aid in criminal, civil and administrative matters, with special attention to sensitive groups. It is the only one of the six providing online free legal aid, runs a free phone line, and serves in Albanian, Serbian and, where needed, English. Around 20 staff; beneficiaries rose from about 564 in 2022 to 698 in 2023, with case engagements up roughly 30 per cent after the online expansion. It also runs the media outlet Betimi për Drejtësi. THE HONEST LIMIT, AND WHAT TO DO ABOUT IT: eligibility runs on legal and financial criteria — this is aid for people who cannot afford representation, so an individual resident may qualify where a well-resourced association would not. In Kosovo, unlike Cyprus, the route may be through named residents rather than through the group. Ask the Agency which of the six accredited NGOs covers your municipality and your subject. AND A SECOND BODY WORTH KNOWING: the Group for Legal and Political Studies in Prishtina, an independent, non-partisan, non-profit public policy organisation conducting research in politics, law and economics, which systematically publishes rule-of-law assessment reports. Not a representation service, but the place to get a legal question in Kosovo researched properly.

trackers.name: Oda e Avokatëve të Kosovës — the searchable roll of Kosovo advocates
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Kosovo Bar Association's public list of advocates, giving each advocate's name, office address and details. Kosovo's bucket had one legal route and no way to find a practitioner; this is the roll a community starts from, and the place to verify that whoever it instructs is actually admitted. AND THE STATE BODY TO USE ALONGSIDE IT: the Institucioni i Avokatit të Popullit — the Ombudsperson — at Rr. Migjeni 21, Prishtinë, with REGIONAL OFFICES listed across the country in municipal and administrative buildings, including one in north Mitrovica. A free complaints route against a public authority, with an office in the regions rather than only the capital.

trackers.name: MMPHI permit registers — every environmental consent and every unlicensed building, by municipality
trackers.desc: WHAT THE MINISTRY PUBLISHES, and it is an unusually complete set: the register of environmental consents, the register of environmental permits, the register of integrated permits, the register of water permits, and — the one to open first — the register of buildings WITHOUT PERMIT in the municipalities of Kosovo. If the thing being built near you has no permit, there is a national register that says so. AND THE NOTICES THAT GIVE YOU A DATE: the same site carries njoftime për debate publike dhe Raporte të VNM-së — notices of public debates and environmental impact assessment reports, which is where a community learns a hearing is coming. TWO LISTS FOR CHECKING THE OTHER SIDE'S EXPERTS: the ministry publishes the list of legal persons licensed to draw up EIA reports, and the list of natural and legal persons licensed for compensation of damage, alongside the register of architects and engineers and the licensing board. You can check whether the consultant who wrote the developer's assessment is licensed to have written it — the second country in this file, after Czechia, that publishes its assessors.

trackers.name: Kosovo's protected-area directorates — and the categories a MUNICIPALITY can establish itself
trackers.desc: WHO HOLDS AND RUNS PROTECTED LAND IN KOSOVO, which the bucket did not yet name: under the Law on Nature Protection, protected natural areas are governed by DIREKTORITE — directorates. Those for national parks, nature parks and natural monuments of special importance are established by the MINISTRY, while THE OTHER CATEGORIES OF PROTECTED AREA ARE RUN BY AUTHORITIES ESTABLISHED BY THE MUNICIPALITY. A municipality can establish the managing authority for a protected area itself — which is the shortest route in a country with no conservation land trust, and it puts the decision in a building a community can walk into. THE NAMED BODIES, all under the environment agency: the Drejtoria Parku Kombëtar Bjeshët e Nemuna, the Drejtoria Parku Kombëtar Sharr, and the Drejtorati për Administrimin e Monumenteve Natyrore me Rëndësi të Veçantë — the directorate administering natural monuments of special importance — alongside the nature protection institute already filed here and the hydrometeorological institute. WHO AUTHORISES WORKS, AND WHERE TO COMPLAIN: authorisation for interventions in strictly protected areas, special areas, national parks, nature parks and natural monuments is issued BY THE MINISTRY; authorisation for works and interventions in landscape and protected monuments of park architecture is issued by the administrative authority or the competent MUNICIPAL authority — and appeals against the decision of an administrative organ or of the competent municipal authority may be submitted to the Ministry. THE CATEGORIES TO ASK FOR: the law classifies protected areas in six categories following IUCN, with the strict nature reserve carrying first-degree protection and declared by the Government. Nature reserves cover 847 hectares, and Kosovo has three kinds — including seven botanical reserves. The agency's own reports record that investment in the protection and advancement of protected areas is lacking.

trackers.name: Kosovo's 115 protected areas — 99 of them natural monuments, and the institute that lists them
trackers.desc: WHAT IS ALREADY PROTECTED, AND IN WHAT PROPORTIONS: Kosovo has 2 national parks, 11 nature reserves, 99 NATURAL MONUMENTS and 3 protected landscapes — 118,913 hectares in total, with the list maintained by the Kosovo Institute for Nature Protection and national park policy overseen by the environment and spatial planning ministry. Ninety-nine of Kosovo's 115 protected areas are natural monuments — the smallest category, the one that covers a spring, a tree, a cave or an outcrop. For a community with one feature worth saving, that is the category the country actually uses, and this file has recorded the same pattern in Bulgaria's mini-reserves and Portugal's small-site body. AND THE PRECEDENT FOR A NEW ONE: a published account of the Bjeshët e Nemuna national park campaign records the legal progress of the initiative to declare it, thanks its interviewees — intellectuals, scientists, institutional officials, members of civil society and of the community — and names a jurist consulted on the draft laws and two named environmental activists from two named NGOs in two towns who, using their own mountain huts, helped distribute, complete and collect the QUESTIONNAIRES in the settlements of the massif. A door-to-door questionnaire run from a local hut, feeding a national park declaration, is a community's own contribution to a designation file. The same account urges that the proposed initiative for a new national park be implemented as soon as possible.

trackers.name: Balkan Green Foundation — cross-border municipal money and the Green Talk platform
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a Western Balkans foundation working on sustainable development, which has run a 40-month cross-border project in one Albanian and one Kosovar municipality under the Cross Border Cooperation Programme for Environment between Albania and Kosovo, aiming to enable the transition of municipalities into the sustainable green economy through integrated policy, SMART PUBLIC INVESTMENTS, and capacity development — with each stakeholder in the two municipalities a direct beneficiary and part of the implementation. A cross-border programme that pays two municipalities to change how they invest is a route into the council that no campaign letter opens, and Kosovo's bucket had no such funder. AND THE STANDING FORUM IT RUNS: Green Talk, a platform dedicated to fostering discussion on energy and environmental issues, PROMOTING ACTIVISM, addressing challenges and exploring opportunities in Kosovo's green sector. IT ALSO PUBLISHES THE SCORECARD: a periodic review of where Kosovo stands on the Green Agenda, with a section on BIODIVERSITY PROTECTION, setting out planned actions, current implementation status and forecast deadlines — naming the environmental protection agency, the Scientific Advisory Council and the National Council. A published implementation scorecard tells a community which government promise is already overdue.

trackers.name: The Kosovo expropriation defence — villages that gave one lawyer a joint power of attorney
trackers.desc: WHAT THE RESIDENTS ACTUALLY DID, and it is the organising step this file keeps looking for: the citizens, IN COOPERATION WITH THE MUNICIPALITY, gave a power of attorney to a named advocate, who filed a claim in the Supreme Court. One lawyer, many owners, and the council alongside them. THE SCALE OF WHAT WAS TAKEN: by government decisions 83 hectares were confiscated in one municipality and around 50 hectares in another, with the advocate representing owners in both. His assessment: the court has every condition to accept the claim, because the citizens' demands are well founded. AND THE ARGUMENT AGAINST 'PUBLIC INTEREST', which transfers to any expropriation anywhere: the law defines clearly what public interest is. It does not necessarily mean that what is in the interest of the CENTRAL level of government is also the interest of the LOCAL COMMUNITY, of the people who live in the territory of this municipality. AND THE PROCEDURAL COMPLAINT WORTH CHECKING IN YOUR OWN CASE: the ministry called a PUBLIC HEARING on the expropriation and set dates for it — but the MUNICIPALITIES WERE NOT NOTIFIED, and owners say they learned only days beforehand what the government intended to build. Construction machinery entered the land while the dispute was live.

trackers.name: MMPHI's registers — the licensed VNM authors, the damage assessors, and the unpermitted buildings
trackers.desc: WHAT THE MINISTRY PUBLISHES, and each of these is a working tool rather than a document: the register of environmental consents; the register of environmental permits; of integrated permits; of WATER permits; the register of case tables completed by municipality from the LEGAL OFFICE; and the REGISTER OF BUILDINGS WITHOUT PERMIT IN KOSOVO'S MUNICIPALITIES. AND THE THREE LISTS OF PEOPLE YOU MIGHT NEED TO HIRE OR CHECK: the register of architects and engineers; the list of natural and legal persons LICENSED BY THE MINISTRY FOR COMPENSATION OF DAMAGE; and the list of legal persons LICENSED TO PREPARE VNM — environmental impact assessment — REPORTS. If the assessment behind a permit was written by someone not on that list, that is checkable in an afternoon; and if you need your own damage valued, the ministry names who may do it. This file recorded the unpermitted-buildings register in batch 302; these are the rest. ALSO PUBLISHED: notices for PUBLIC DEBATES and VNM reports, the licensing board, and lists of waste intermediaries, registered waste traders and licensed municipal waste operators — so an operator's licence status can be verified before a complaint is made.

trackers.name: ERA — the Kosovo organisation that leads the residents' hydropower fight, and measures the flow
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: along one river four hydropower projects sprang up, provoking the reaction and protests of residents, LED BY THE ENVIRONMENTAL ORGANISATION ERA. Kosovo's bucket held the bar roll, the free legal aid agency, the registers and an expropriation case — this is the organisation that runs the campaigns. AND THE TECHNICAL CHECK IT MAKES ON SITE, which is the single most copyable act in this entry: under the laws of our state, the company is obliged to respect the 30 per cent known as the BIOLOGICAL MINIMUM — that is, 30 per cent of the river must be flowing from this dam — and at this moment we see that it is not flowing at all. A number in the permit, checked at the dam with your own eyes, is evidence anyone can gather. Its representative's account is equally usable: what worries us is the death of a river — behind me we see a concreted dam where the river dies; from here upward there is no more aquatic life. AND THE LONGER ARGUMENT IT PUTS: the irreparable consequences of such interventions in Kosovo's rivers will appear after many years, with the Balkans set to be the red point attacked by drought in the years to come. Officials confirmed on the record that for operators who do not finish on time and do not return the environment to its previous state, they do not exclude WITHDRAWING THE WATER CONSENT, WATER PERMIT AND ENVIRONMENTAL CONSENT.

trackers.name: Çohu! and Preportr — the investigative pair that documented the hydropower permits
trackers.desc: WHAT THEY ARE: an anti-corruption organisation and the Kosovar Centre for Investigative Journalism, working as a pair. Their published finding is the context a Kosovo community needs before it starts: the construction and operation of hydropower plants has caused numerous environmental damages. They have caused dissatisfaction and protests. On the other hand, THERE HAVE BEEN ATTEMPTS TO SILENCE AND INTIMIDATE THE ACTIVISTS AND CITIZENS WHO OPPOSED THEM. An investigative outlet that has already documented the intimidation is one a threatened campaigner can go to — and it also tracks the permits: some hydropower plants are currently in the process of obtaining environmental permits, some awaiting court decisions. AND ITS EXPERT FINDING, which a community can cite rather than having to prove: experts say that Kosovo's rivers are not a suitable alternative for hydropower, because THE DAMAGES ARE FAR GREATER THAN THE BENEFIT. WHAT THE STATE ITSELF FOUND, reported alongside: a government commission's voluminous report covering ALL THE HYDROPOWER PLANTS OF KOSOVO recorded many violations — in water acts, in environmental acts, in the inspectorate, WHICH HAD NOT MADE SUFFICIENT FIELD VISITS, and violations of TRANSPARENCY, compiled after the ministry met residents, operators and non-governmental organisations.

trackers.name: Kosovo Green Action — three named organisations, each with a contact, and a complaints panel
trackers.desc: WHAT IT GIVES A KOSOVO COMMUNITY: a single page listing THREE IMPLEMENTING ORGANISATIONS, EACH WITH A NAMED CONTACT PERSON, EMAIL ADDRESS AND WEBSITE — a green foundation with its programmes manager and phone number, a transparency movement with its project manager, and an open data organisation with both a project coordinator and an executive director. Three organisations, six named people, and every address published is a contact list a community can work through in an afternoon. WHAT THEY DO TOGETHER: the project engages diverse stakeholders in collaborative SOCIAL ACCOUNTABILITY on climate and energy-related priorities, through activities that improve stakeholders' ACCESS TO INFORMATION, good governance, accountability and transparency of government institutions. It is financially supported by the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development through a Global Partnership for Social Accountability grant. AND THE ROUTE THE SAME PAGE NAMES, which exists in every country with a development-bank-funded project: the World Bank Inspection Panel is the INDEPENDENT COMPLAINT MECHANISM AND FACT-FINDING BODY FOR PEOPLE WHO BELIEVE THEY ARE LIKELY TO BE, OR HAVE BEEN, ADVERSELY AFFECTED BY A WORLD BANK-FINANCED PROJECT, with an information-request form published alongside.

trackers.name: Drejtoria e Parkut Kombëtar — the park directorate that can FINE and CONFISCATE on the spot
trackers.desc: WHAT THIS BODY CAN ACTUALLY DO, which is more than most conservation agencies in this file: it applies MANDATORY FINES AND THE CONFISCATION OF THE VARIOUS MEANS WITH WHICH ILLEGAL ACTIONS ARE CARRIED OUT IN THE NATIONAL PARK. Kosovo had 23 filed entries and no land-holding body; this is the state directorate that holds and polices the ground. AND ITS OTHER DUTIES, each one a thing a resident can report to it: it implements measures to protect nature from FIRES, damaging insects, plant diseases and various polluters; CONTROLS THE TRANSPORT OF TIMBER within the park's territory and takes legal measures against irregularities; CONTROLS AND MAINTAINS THE SIGNS OF THE PARK'S EXTERNAL AND INTERNAL BOUNDARIES; and controls movement and transport in the territory. A body that maintains the boundary markers is the body to tell when a boundary has been moved — and this file recorded in Albania that a protected-area map had a patch quietly removed. AND THE CHAIN OF COMMAND, published: the head of the directorate for the administration of the national park REPORTS TO THE DIRECTOR GENERAL, and the park has its own law with a numbered citation. Kosovo has two national parks declared by the Assembly, together covering 115,957 hectares.

trackers.name: Instituti i Kosovës për Mbrojtjen e Natyrës — the central body, and it MARKED the strict reserves
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the central institution for the conservation of nature and THE MONITORING OF THE STATE OF PROTECTED NATURAL VALUES in Kosovo, sitting inside the environmental protection agency alongside the hydrometeorological institute, the two national park directorates, and a DIRECTORATE FOR THE ADMINISTRATION OF NATURAL MONUMENTS OF SPECIAL IMPORTANCE. A single agency page listing every nature directorate, each with its published duties, is the map of who to write to — and it also carries reports, studies and publications and an annual state-of-the-environment report. AND WHAT IT HAS PHYSICALLY DONE, which a community can ask it to repeat: under a project for THE MARKING OF PROTECTED AREAS it marked the STRICT NATURE RESERVES that form part of the protected areas list — work carried out in both national parks and in other parts of Kosovo's territory, INCLUDING THE NORTHERN PART OF THE COUNTRY — with the aim of raising awareness through the placing of OFFICIAL NOTICES in these zones for the wider public and for visitors and tourists. Official signs on the ground are the cheapest defence a protected area has, and here is the institution that installs them. Its teams have also visited most of the localities of endemic species and published a national biodiversity volume.

trackers.name: Agjencia Pyjore e Kosovës — it will HELP SMALL OWNERS FORM A MANAGEMENT ASSOCIATION
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the executive agency responsible for the regulation of forests and forest lands, the administration and management of PUBLIC forest lands AND OF THE FORESTS IN THE NATIONAL PARKS of Kosovo. Kosovo had 25 filed entries and no private land-buying body; this is the state body that holds the forest. AND THE PROVISION THAT MATTERS MOST TO NEIGHBOURING SMALLHOLDERS: the forest agency WILL ENCOURAGE THE OWNERS OF SMALL PARCELS TO JOIN TOGETHER IN FOREST MANAGEMENT ASSOCIATIONS and, with the agreement of such owners, MAY TREAT THE PARCELS OF SUCH ASSOCIATIONS AS A SINGLE PARCEL. A state agency that will help fragmented smallholders combine into one managed block is the answer to the fragmentation problem this file recorded in Czechia, where hundreds of co-owners made a restoration impossible. AND THE PROTECTION IT PUTS ON PRIVATE FOREST: in private forests and forest lands, NO PERSON MAY CUT AND NO PARCEL OWNER MAY BE PERMITTED TO CUT TIMBER UNLESS AN AUTHORISED OFFICIAL OF THE FOREST AGENCY MARKS THE TRUNKS BEFORE FELLING, and officials may only mark them where the cutting is consistent with the law and the plans. It can also restrict, prohibit or decide on ZONES OF LIMITED USE. It appeals publicly to municipalities, its own municipal units, the fire service and the police for coordination, and asks forest guards to identify the wrongdoers and give timely information to the authorities.

trackers.name: Kosovo's forest law — the agency can go to COURT for people whose water or rights are threatened
trackers.desc: THE ROUTE THAT MAKES THIS A RESOURCE RATHER THAN A RULE: where people feel endangered in their HEALTH, in the QUALITY OF WATER, and in the violation of the rights to use forests or forest lands, THE KOSOVO FOREST AGENCY MAY APPLY TO THE COURT. A state agency empowered to litigate on behalf of villagers whose water is at risk is a plaintiff a community does not have to pay for — and this file has spent forty rounds looking for bodies that will carry a case. AND THE SECOND ROUTE, for the person already wronged: a person who loses the right to use forest resources because the procedure laid down in this law was not followed by a government organ, or because a government employee acted contrary to this law, MAY REQUEST FROM THE COURT a remedy — with compensation reckoned on the market value of the lost forest products. AND WHERE THE MONEY GOES, worth knowing before a community argues about local benefit: charges on non-timber forest products go to the FOREST REGENERATION FUND, and 20 PER CENT of the value of standing timber licences is dedicated to MUNICIPAL BUDGETS, in proportion to the charges realised there. Kosovo has around 41 per cent of its territory covered by forest.

trackers.name: ANJF — 7 regional offices, 14 MOBILE offices, and a FREE PHONE line
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Agency for Free Legal Aid, established by a named 2011 law, an INDEPENDENT PUBLIC INSTITUTION providing free legal aid in CIVIL, CRIMINAL, ADMINISTRATIVE AND MINOR-OFFENCE procedure for all citizens who meet the criteria. Kosovo's legal entries were courts and registers; this is the service itself. Administrative procedure is named in its remit, which is where a permit challenge sits. AND HOW FAR IT REACHES: provision extends across THE WHOLE TERRITORY of Kosovo, through 7 REGIONAL OFFICES FOR FREE LEGAL AID AND 14 MOBILE OFFICES for free legal aid; the site publishes the central office's street address and telephone, THE STREET ADDRESS AND TELEPHONE OF EACH NAMED REGIONAL OFFICE, an email address, AND A FREE PHONE NUMBER. Fourteen mobile offices and a freephone line mean no Kosovar village is out of reach of a lawyer — the second mobile legal service recorded in this file after Bosnia's. It was created in May 2006 and describes itself as THE FIRST AND ONLY OF ITS KIND IN THE SOUTH-EAST EUROPE REGION, institutionalising legal aid to provide and ensure EQUAL ACCESS TO JUSTICE. Some mobile offices in named municipalities were opened with the support of a named foreign donor.

trackers.name: How to claim it — the nearest office decides WITHIN 5 DAYS, and can assign you a free advocate
trackers.desc: WHAT THE AID ACTUALLY IS: free legal aid is given in the form of INFORMATION AND LEGAL ADVICE on legal procedures, THE DRAFTING OF DOCUMENTS, and all other technical assistance relating to COMPLETING THE CASE FILE and REPRESENTATION in civil, criminal, administrative and minor-offence procedure. Drafting the documents and completing the file is the work a community cannot do itself, and it is explicitly included. AND HOW TO START, with the clock: the procedure is initiated by SUBMITTING THE REQUEST together with the required documents AT THE NEAREST OFFICE for free legal aid. After application, the agency's officials assess WITHIN 5 DAYS whether the criteria for benefiting from free legal services have been met. Five days to a yes or no is fast enough to be worth trying before a deadline runs — the same five-day standard recorded in Lithuania. AND WHO CAN DELIVER IT: the regional offices, THE MOBILE OFFICES, ADVOCATES, and NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS in cases where they enter into partnership with the agency. A companion page adds that the official assesses whether you are a beneficiary and what legal actions should be taken, and depending on the case DECIDES ON ENGAGING A LEGAL REPRESENTATIVE OR FREE ADVOCATE.

trackers.name: KCSF's donor directory — who funds Kosovar civil society, and how much each gives
trackers.desc: WHAT THIS PAGE IS: the Kosovar civil society foundation's published roundup of THE FOREIGN DONORS FOR CIVIL SOCIETY IN KOSOVO, naming each programme, what it funds, its ceiling and where to apply. Kosovo had three funding entries filed. A directory of who funds what, written by the body that administers much of it, saves a community the months of asking around that usually comes first. AND THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST TO A VILLAGE FIGHTING A PROJECT: the EU office in Kosovo runs A GRANT SCHEME FOR ADVOCACY INITIATIVES BY COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS, whose general purpose is SUPPORT FOR ADVOCACY INITIATIVES OF COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS WHICH CONTRIBUTE TO CHANGES IN SOCIETY AT THE LOCAL LEVEL, with total support of around 500,000 EURO. A scheme that pays community-based organisations specifically to do ADVOCACY at LOCAL level is the closest thing in this file to money for opposing a project — not for planting trees, and not for a study. AND THE SMALLER, FASTER ROUTES ALSO NAMED: an embassy's DEMOCRACY COMMISSION SMALL GRANTS PROGRAMME supporting civil society organisations AND INDEPENDENT LOCAL MEDIA, where the largest grant is 24,000 USD; and a further embassy small-grants programme supporting activism. Another programme aims to encourage positive and constructive inter-ethnic communication by focusing on COMMON PROBLEMS, NEEDS AND SOLUTIONS.

trackers.name: Prishtina's municipal park decision — a MUNICIPAL ASSEMBLY protected 1,126 hectares itself
trackers.desc: WHAT A KOSOVAR MUNICIPALITY DID WITHOUT WAITING FOR THE STATE: the Municipal Assembly of the capital DECIDED TO TAKE A NAMED PARK UNDER PROTECTION AS A NATURAL PARK, and by that decision PROTECTS AN AREA OF 1,126.01 HECTARES. Kosovo had one land-acquisition entry filed. A municipal assembly can protect eleven square kilometres by its own decision — which is the cheapest and fastest route recorded in this file for a community whose council is sympathetic. AND THE GROUNDS IT USED, which are broader than a species list: the area was given legal care because of its NATURAL BEAUTIES, its source values AND NATURAL AESTHETIC VALUES which are of CULTURAL-EDUCATIONAL, SCIENTIFIC AND TOURIST-RECREATIONAL IMPORTANCE. AND THE PRECEDENT BEHIND IT, which is the part worth copying: as far back as a numbered decision of 31 MAY 1966, the territory was designated as A ZONE WITH SPECIAL PURPOSE, 'FORESTS AND PICNIC', in order to create favourable conditions for REST AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF TOURISM, covering named cadastral zones. An old special-purpose designation still on the books is a ready-made argument for protecting the same ground today. The park is managed by a named MUNICIPAL PUBLIC ENTERPRISE, with professional monitoring by the Kosovo Institute for Nature Protection.

trackers.name: Property rights in Kosovo — what expropriation must prove, and the trick councils try
trackers.desc: WHAT A COMMUNITY FACING EXPROPRIATION SHOULD KNOW, set out in a documented review: property may be expropriated when it is necessary for the construction of economic housing, public health facilities and other facilities that are OF COMMON INTEREST. If a project is deemed to be of common interest, the proposal for expropriation is submitted to the competent MUNICIPAL authorities, and must be submitted WITHIN TWO YEARS of the taking of the 'decision on common interest'. AND THE REQUIREMENT THAT IS OFTEN THE WEAK POINT: a MUNICIPAL VALUATION COMMISSION decides what compensation must be paid and by whom — and the proposal for expropriation MUST DEMONSTRATE THAT THE MEANS FOR COMPENSATION EXIST. A taking that cannot show the money to pay for it is not ready to proceed, and the two-year clock on the common-interest decision is a second thing to check. AND THE PRACTICE THE REVIEW DOCUMENTS AND NAMES: some municipal authorities try to BYPASS THE EXPROPRIATION PROCEDURES by 'persuading' property holders to give their properties to the municipality WITHOUT ANY COMPENSATION, or for an arbitrarily determined compensation amount WHICH IS OFTEN MUCH LOWER than it should be — with numerous examples named in SEVEN NAMED MUNICIPALITIES and corroborated in an international mission's own report. Compensation can also be given as property rights over other land rather than money.

trackers.name: Kosovo's Forest Law — SMALL OWNERS ARE ENCOURAGED TO COMBINE INTO MANAGEMENT ASSOCIATIONS
trackers.desc: THE PROVISION THAT TURNS SCATTERED SMALLHOLDERS INTO ONE BODY: the Forest Agency SHALL ENCOURAGE THE OWNERS OF SMALL PARCELS TO JOIN TOGETHER INTO FOREST MANAGEMENT ASSOCIATIONS and, WITH THE AGREEMENT OF SUCH OWNERS, MAY TREAT THE PARCELS OF SUCH ASSOCIATIONS AS A SINGLE PARCEL. Kosovo had two land-acquisition entries filed. A statute that instructs the state agency to help small owners form an association, and then treats their scattered plots as one holding, is the cheapest route to a block of protected ground — no purchase, no consolidation of title. AND THE CONTROL THAT COMES WITH PRIVATE FOREST: NO PERSON MAY CUT AND NO PARCEL OWNER MAY BE PERMITTED TO CUT TIMBER UNLESS AN AUTHORISED OFFICIAL OF THE FOREST AGENCY MARKS THE TRUNKS BEFORE FELLING, and officials may mark them only if the cutting is consistent with the requirements of this law and any regulation and plans made under this chapter. Every tree felled in a private Kosovar forest must be individually marked by a state official first — which makes unmarked felling reportable, and the marking decision challengeable. AND WHOSE NEEDS THE FOREST PLANS MUST SERVE, named in order: (a) THE MUNICIPAL NEEDS for forest resources; (b) Kosovo's needs in general; and (c) in the case of private forests, THE NEEDS OF THE LANDOWNER. Plans must favour NATIVE SPECIES OVER FOREIGN (EXOTIC) ONES.

trackers.name: A 51-page legal analysis published FOR COMMUNITIES to use in court
trackers.desc: A FINISHED LEGAL ANALYSIS HANDED TO RESIDENTS, which is the scarcest kind of resource in this file: a 51-PAGE LEGAL ANALYSIS, worked on OVER THE LAST 5 MONTHS, addressing THE LEGAL VIOLATIONS THAT HAVE BEEN COMMITTED IN THE CONSTRUCTION OF HYDROPOWER PLANTS IN two named national parks. Kosovo has the smallest base of any bucket in this file. AND THE STATED PURPOSE, written for use rather than for the record: THIS RESEARCH AIMS TO BE IN THE SERVICE OF THE COMMUNITY AND OF INTERESTED PARTIES WHO CAN USE THE FINDINGS OF THIS REPORT TO PREVENT THE MISUSE OF WATER RESOURCES... TO EQUIP THE ADVOCACY GROUPS AND THE RESIDENTS IN THEIR FIGHT IN DEFENCE OF THEIR INTEREST THROUGH THE RESPONSIBLE INSTITUTIONS, THE ORGANS OF JUSTICE AND THE COURTS IN KOSOVO. A report written so residents can carry it into court removes the single largest cost of a case — and it names its targets: the analysis CONFIRMS THE RESPONSIBILITY OF THE INSTITUTIONS OF KOSOVO, the energy regulator AND THE MINISTRY, AS WELL AS TWO NAMED COMPANIES. AND THE FINDING MOST USEFUL TO A LANDOWNER: those companies INTERVENED WITH WORKS ON THE PRIVATE PROPERTIES OF THE RESIDENTS OF THOSE AREAS WITHOUT THEIR PERMISSION AND OUTSIDE THE NORMS AND CRITERIA PERMITTED BY LAW. The body also acts as A CONNECTING BRIDGE BETWEEN THE COMMUNITY AND THE INSTITUTIONS OF KOSOVO.

trackers.name: How a protected zone gets REZONED — the inter-ministerial council to watch for
trackers.desc: THE MOVE A KOSOVAR COMMUNITY SHOULD WATCH FOR, because it defeats a designation without ever attacking it: WORRYING ARE CERTAIN CASES WHERE, IN ORDER TO FAVOUR SPECIFIC PROJECTS, AN INTER-MINISTERIAL COUNCIL IS FORMED WHICH HAS THE EXECUTIVE POWER TO CHANGE CERTAIN ZONES FROM ZONE 1 TO ZONE 3. IN ZONE 3 THE CONSTRUCTION OF HYDROPOWER PLANTS IS PERMITTED, WHILE IN ZONE 1 AND ZONE 2 THIS IS NOT POSSIBLE. Kosovo has the smallest base of any bucket in this file. The project does not have to beat the protection; the protection gets reclassified around the project — so a community should watch for the formation of a council as closely as for a permit application. AND THE REMEDY THE ANALYSIS PROPOSES, which a group can adopt as its own ask: SUCH A POSSIBILITY OF CHANGE IS UNJUST AND MUST BE REGULATED IN A LEGAL MANNER. SUCH COMPETENCE FOR DETERMINING ZONES AND ZONING MAPS SHOULD BELONG EXCLUSIVELY TO EXPERTS AND THERE SHOULD BE NO POLITICISATION OR POLITICAL INFLUENCE IN IT, AND STILL LESS SHOULD THE CONSTRUCTION OF HYDROPOWER PLANTS IN NATIONAL PARKS BE PERMITTED AT ALL. Demanding that zoning maps be set by experts rather than by ministers is a concrete, borrowable demand, and the analysis warns of the risk that these areas will be DAMAGED FOREVER.

trackers.name: Personal Data Protection Agency (DZLP)
trackers.desc: Personal Data Protection Agency (DZLP) — North Macedonia’s national data-protection / information authority, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: State Commission for Prevention of Corruption
trackers.desc: North Macedonia's anti-corruption commission. — Holds to account: lobbyists & influence-seekers, top officials & cabinet, officials handling public money & power — find who is lobbying whom, and meetings held; their assets, interests and integrity declarations; corruption cases, sanctions and integrity data.

trackers.name: Constitutional Court of North Macedonia
trackers.desc: Official site publishing the decisions of North Macedonia's Constitutional Court. · Find here: the decisions of the Constitutional Court of North Macedonia.

trackers.name: Agency for Protection of the Right to Free Access to Public Information (North Macedonia)
trackers.desc: Agency for Protection of the Right to Free Access to Public Information (North Macedonia) — independent body overseeing the right of access to public information.

trackers.name: Agency for Free Access to Public Information (KOMSPI)
trackers.desc: National right-to-information authority; North Macedonia’s KOMSPI decides appeals and monitors implementation of the Law on Free Access to Public Information, reporting to Parliament, North Macedonia.

trackers.name: Justice and Environment — European green-law network
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the European network of environmental-law NGOs, whose national member here is FRONT 21/42. Its fifteen members act as the environmental-law service point in their own countries, taking cases and intervening in legislative processes, while the network defends communities and nature in court and lodges infringement complaints against member-state governments. Its standing themes are access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, environmental assessment and pollution control. WHO IT SUITS: anyone who does not yet know which lawyer to call — knock on FRONT 21/42's door first, and use the network only if your problem crosses a border. The network itself does not take individual cases; its members do. YOUR NATIONAL MEMBER IS FRONT 21/42 (front.org.mk) — go to them, not to the network. J&E members serve as environmental law ‘service points’ in their countries, handling cases, participating in legislative processes and sometimes providing legal analyses and consultations for national governments. The network has 11 full and 4 associate members, and can launch infringement proceedings against faulty governments — a route a national body alone does not have. CURRENT SCOPE: access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, climate, environmental assessments, and the Environmental Liability Directive. It previously worked on waste, transport, health and Natura 2000, so an older document may overstate what it covers today.

trackers.name: FRONT 21/42
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: North Macedonia's member organisation in the Justice and Environment network of European environmental-law NGOs. It is the only green-law contact point the network names for the country. WHO IT SUITS: anyone in North Macedonia with an environmental permit or access-to-justice problem and nowhere else to start; the scope of work it accepts is not stated on the network's page, so ask first. Domain unverified this session — reach them through the member list on justiceandenvironment.org. No website or directory listing could be verified for FRONT 21/42 across two rounds of searching, so none is given rather than guessing a plausible domain. Do not substitute the Regional Environmental Center country office in Skopje (mk.rec.org) — that is a different organisation. A targeted search in Macedonian is the next step. DOMAIN NOW CONFIRMED: front.org.mk, taken from Justice and Environment's own members page, which lists each national member organisation with its own website. The fallback route this entry originally gave — go to the network's member list — is what produced it. Recorded for provenance: two earlier search rounds found no primary domain for this organisation and deliberately declined to guess the obvious .mk address; the domain here is the one J&E publishes beside its member's name, not an inference.

trackers.name: State Audit Office (DZR)
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of North Macedonia, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Center for Investigative Journalism SCOOP-Macedonia
trackers.desc: North Macedonian investigative-journalism center reporting on corruption and abuse of public office.

trackers.name: E-nabavki
trackers.desc: North Macedonia's electronic public-procurement system. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in North Macedonia, and for how much.

trackers.name: Investigative Reporting Lab
trackers.desc: North Macedonian nonprofit newsroom focused on corruption, crime and governance.

trackers.name: Central Registry
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Open Data Macedonia
trackers.desc: National — official government open data / budget portal. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this is the broad budget/open-data hub for how money is allocated overall — for the specific firms winning tenders use the procurement portal, and for findings of misspending use the supreme audit institution. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in North Macedonia.

trackers.name: State Statistical Office
trackers.desc: North Macedonia's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in North Macedonia.

trackers.name: Студија за валоризација — no study, no protection: fund that first
trackers.desc: THE GATE, AND THE THING TO ASK FOR. Under the Закон за заштита на природата, only with a completed valorisation study can an initiative to declare or re-declare a protected area be submitted. These studies need field research, expert data processing and multiple expert profiles, so the cost of professionally preparing the documentation is part of the real financial framework of protection. AND THAT COST IS WHERE CAMPAIGNS DIE: the Jablanica citizens' initiative reached the Government in 2019 and received support at a working session — but funds for the valorisation study were not allocated, so legal protection could not proceed. Political support was not enough. Unlike Montenegro and Turkey, where the state funds the study by statute, here the money is discretionary — so make funding for the valorisation study the explicit ask, not protection in the abstract. WHAT THE STUDY CONTAINS, from Šar Planina: published data plus 2 years of field research on geodiversity, climate and pedology, flora, fungi and fauna, ecosystems and landscapes, valorisation of natural heritage and socio-economic values, and an analysis of threats — which is where a specific development belongs.

trackers.name: The Vodno precedent — a city council initiated the protection
trackers.desc: A SEQUENCE WORTH COPYING EXACTLY. The proposal to declare Vodno a protected area in category V — protected landscape was submitted to the ministry by the City of Skopje (letter of 29 April 2020), based on a decision adopted by the Council of the City of Skopje. That decision was itself preceded by preparation of the Study, communication by the expert team with affected parties, and analysis of development and natural-resource-use plans, the area's size, its population, the needs of the population and traditional values — on which basis category V was judged best to reflect the specific interaction of people and nature there, consistent with IUCN standards. SO: study → engagement with affected parties and the population's needs → council decision → the city submits to the ministry. AND WHERE THE STUDY MONEY CAME FROM: the Vodno study was prepared inside an EU-financed IPA 2 project implemented by UNDP, while Šar Planina's was authored by UNEP with the ministry — so the practical move is finding a project to attach to rather than a grant to win.

trackers.name: Energy Community — private bodies may complain, and refusal is appealable
trackers.desc: A COMPLAINT MECHANISM WHERE REFUSAL BY THE GATEKEEPER CAN BE TAKEN OVER ITS HEAD — which is rare, and is the reason to know about this. Under Article 90 of the Energy Community Treaty, private bodies may approach the Secretariat with complaints about a Party's non-compliance, and under Article 12.2 of the Consolidated Rules the Secretariat initiates procedures in response to a complaint by a private body as well as on its own initiative. AND IF THE SECRETARIAT DECLINES: the revised Rules give the complainant the right to approach the Permanent High Level Group directly, which may hear the complaint directly or initiate a preliminary procedure — in most systems recorded in this map, a secretariat declining to act ends the matter. The PHLG can also take interim measures in matters of urgency under Article 47(c) — that is what matters when works are already under way, so ask for it expressly. THE ENVIRONMENTAL ACQUIS IS IN SCOPE, including the EIA Directive as amended by 2014/52, which was to be transposed by 1 January 2019. CHECK THE TRANSPOSITION DEADLINE FOR THE DIRECTIVE YOU RELY ON — failure to transpose by the stated date is itself the non-compliance, and is a far simpler case than arguing about how a rule was applied. THE REALISTIC WIN CONDITION: a case opens with an Opening Letter, escalates to a Reasoned Opinion giving two months to rectify, then to the Ministerial Council — but a case closes whenever the Party complies, and many are recorded as complied with before any decision was adopted. The opening of proceedings is the lever, not the final decision. YOU CAN ALSO JOIN AN EXISTING CASE: interested third parties may access the case file and submit written observations, provided they substantiate their legitimate interest. Case law from Opening Letters is published with dates and numbers, so precedent is visible. Write to the Energy Community Secretariat, Am Hof 4, 1010 Vienna. ONE MORE ROUTE: the amended Rules provide for cooperation with national authorities and courts, giving concrete assistance to national courts on the interpretation of Energy Community law — a domestic judge unsure how an EU-derived rule applies can be pointed at it.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: ELAW — free attorneys and scientists who will critique the developer's EIA
trackers.desc: IT WILL READ THE DEVELOPER'S EIA AND TELL YOU WHAT IS WRONG WITH IT — which is the thing a community cannot produce alone and usually cannot afford. ELAW is a global alliance of attorneys, scientists and other advocates, founded 1989 in Eugene, Oregon by public interest lawyers from ten countries, that provides legal and scientific support to grassroots advocates to challenge destructive projects. FOUR CONCRETE FORMS OF HELP: legal support to local public interest lawyers; scientific support, including critiquing environmental assessments; economic insights on projects; and security expertise — ‘ELAW helps environmental lawyers improve their security so they can work without fear. When our partners are targeted, we act quickly to help defend and protect them.’ That last one is a named function, not an aspiration, and ELAW co-founded the Alliance for Land, Indigenous and Environmental Defenders. HOW TO USE IT — THROUGH A LAWYER, NOT AS A CLIENT: ELAW works through more than 300 public interest advocates in its network, and its stated strategy is ‘locating strong lawyers who are committed to protecting the environment in their home countries’. You can approach ELAW directly, but the leverage is greatest when a local advocate is the conduit — that is how the network is built. It has hosted nearly 300 advocates from more than 65 countries as Fellows and provided support on thousands of cases; several partners have won the Goldman Environmental Prize. Focus areas include biodiversity, fossil fuels — expressly assisting advocates in contesting fossil fuel development projects — plastic pollution, and work with coastal communities. It publishes guidebooks, including one to give communities sufficient understanding to challenge oil and gas projects, and clause-level summaries of national EIA law — so its site is also a route to learning exactly what your own EIA law requires. ASK WHETHER ELAW HAS A PARTNER IN YOUR COUNTRY: the network is described as spanning 70 to 80 countries but the member list is not published country by country, so this entry does not assert a presence in yours.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen.
