One case removed the need for anyone to ask again. That is a far larger prize than a single file and it costs the same litigation. WHAT IT EXISTS FOR: the country's freedom of information law dates from 1998 and is described by the organisation's own director as formally progressive, but it was set up specifically to promote the law's IMPLEMENTATION — on the view that a culture of secrecy and bureaucratic exhaustion is where requests actually die. The gap between a good statute and an answered request is the problem it works on, which is the same gap this file has recorded in Lebanon, Turkiye and Central Asia. ITS METHOD IS SIMPLE AND REPEATABLE: submit the request, and when refused, take the authority to court. Its published examples include winning disclosure against a prisons authority after a refusal on privacy grounds, and winning twice against a religious authority over a list of practitioners found negligent — refusals dressed as privacy protection are its ordinary business. THE LIMITS: it is a transparency organisation, not an environmental or planning one. It will not object to your scheme, assess it, or represent you at a committee — for those this file records planners, a legal centre and a planning-rights body in Israel. Use it for the documents, and use the documents with them. Nothing found shows it acting on a land or development matter specifically, so approach it as a freedom-of-information question rather than as an environmental one — which is how the request should be framed anyway.

trackers.name: Keren Sheli — it funds a fight, not just a project, and unregistered groups can apply
trackers.desc: ITS OWN TERMS SAY AN APPLICATION MAY BE OF THE NATURE OF A STRUGGLE, or of positive initiated activity. Most funders in this file pay for surveys, restoration or capacity; this one will pay for the campaign itself — and it says so in writing, which is what a group needs when explaining to a funder that it intends to oppose something. UNREGISTERED GROUPS MAY APPLY. Both registered non-profit associations AND non-profit organisings or groups that are NOT registered as associations can approach it — which removes the barrier this file has documented repeatedly across the region, where registration is the gate that stops a village group before it starts. AND IT DELIBERATELY EXCLUDES THE WELL-RESOURCED: it does not support organisations with a significant budget, and gives priority to GROUPS AT THE START OF THEIR PATH and to the social and geographic periphery, as well as to groups that cooperate with environmental organisations. A new committee of neighbours is the intended applicant, not an established body. THERE IS AN EMERGENCY WINDOW, AND IT IS DEFINED IN THE TERMS THAT ACTUALLY MATTER: in exceptional cases the fund will consider emergency requests of up to 20,000 shekels where an emergency organising faces an environmental threat that is IMMEDIATE, IRREVERSIBLE, ON A SHORT TIMELINE AND OF SIGNIFICANT SCOPE. That is the machinery-arrives-next-week case, and almost nothing else in this payload has a route for it. Ordinary grants run to 25,000 shekels, and come with professional accompaniment and individually tailored consulting hours rather than money alone. TWO ROUNDS A YEAR, IN WINTER AND SUMMER — check the current dates rather than assuming, and note that calls are published in Hebrew and in Arabic. The fund is a partnership of environmental funds operating through the New Israel Fund and administered through its empowerment and training centre, which has worked with grassroots organisations since 1982 and describes its own mandate as reaching constituencies on the economic and geographic periphery and building coalitions among them — so the consulting hours come from people who do that work. ONE THING TO WEIGH FOR YOURSELF: the fund operates through a foundation that is itself a subject of public political contention in Israel. This file records that as a fact for an applicant to consider in their own circumstances, not as a judgement either way — the same treatment given to the politically framed bodies recorded elsewhere in this payload.

trackers.name: Negev Coexistence Forum — it trains residents to document demolitions, and works to the residents' own committees
trackers.desc: ITS FIRST PROGRAMME IS A DOCUMENTATION NETWORK BUILT OUT OF THE AFFECTED POPULATION ITSELF: residents — women, children, teenagers and men — are trained to record home demolitions, arrests, demonstrations and daily conditions, through photography and video projects, and everyone who takes part joins a standing human rights defenders network. This file has repeatedly found that campaigns lose because nothing was recorded at the time. Training the people who are present to document what happens, and making that training a route into an organised network rather than a one-off workshop, is the most transferable thing here. AND IT WORKS TO A STATED PRINCIPLE THAT DECIDES WHO IS IN CHARGE: it operates on a do-no-harm basis in close coordination with RESIDENTS' GROUPS, whom it describes as its strongest partners and allies — alongside the legal centre, the planning body and the capacity-building centre recorded separately in this file, which makes it a hub connecting a community to all three. THE CONSTITUENCY BODY BEHIND IT IS WHERE THE STRUCTURAL LESSON SITS, AND IT IS WORTH COPYING ANYWHERE A POPULATION HAS NO AUTHORITY OF ITS OWN: a regional council for the unrecognised villages, established in 1997, is a democratically elected body representing forty-five villages whose residents belong to no municipality and so cannot elect representatives. Each village elects a local committee; the committees form the general assembly; the assembly elects a chairperson and executive committee every four years. That ladder turns a dispersed population into a body with which a ministry, a court or a funder can deal. It has no verified address of its own and is reached through the organisations that work with it, including this one. WHAT IT PUBLISHES IS THE EVIDENCE BASE: annual counts of demolitions — 2,586 structures recorded in one year, a rise of thirteen per cent on the year before — alongside accounts of land-ploughing operations across thousands of dunams reaching named villages, and of police conduct during them. Year-on-year counts turn individual events into a documented trend, which is what an advocacy case needs. Its second programme is campaigning and advocacy aimed at changing state policy; a third strand trains women in digital skills so they can help others in their villages access rights administered online. ITS RECORD ALSO SHOWS THE SMALLER WINS THAT KEEP A COMMUNITY IN PLACE: one village obtained approval for temporary portable structures to house essential services, in that case schooling. THE SCOPE LIMIT: it works in the Negev and on the rights of the Bedouin population there. It is not a general environmental or planning body, and a reader outside that context should use the planning and legal bodies recorded elsewhere in this file.

trackers.name: RCUV — an elected council of forty-five villages, and it warns what recognition can cost
trackers.desc: WHEN A COMMUNITY IS OFFERED RECOGNITION, ASK WHAT THE BOUNDARY EXCLUDES AND WHAT IS SIGNED AWAY TO GET IT. This council argued of one partial-recognition scheme that the recognition it offered came at the price of RENOUNCING CONSIDERABLE VILLAGE LAND CLAIMS, and that drawing boundaries around the area of habitation alone — zoning out most of the grazing ground — would leave settlements unable to grow or support themselves, without business districts or the services that make recognition real. Its counter-position was to seek recognition of all the villages together with their land claims, framed with a ratio worth borrowing: the land in dispute amounts to no more than two per cent of the region, while the population concerned is more than a quarter of it. A SMALL SHARE OF LAND SET AGAINST A LARGE SHARE OF PEOPLE IS AN ARGUMENT ANY DISPERSED COMMUNITY CAN MAKE, AND IT IS HARDER TO REFUSE THAN A PLEA. WHAT IT IS, AND WHY THE STRUCTURE IS THE MODEL: established in 1997, it is a grassroots organisation AND A DEMOCRATICALLY ELECTED BODY representing forty-five villages and, on one account, close to a hundred thousand people who belong to no municipality and therefore cannot elect representatives in the ordinary way. The residents of each village elect a local committee; those committees form the general assembly; the assembly elects a chairperson and executive committee every four years. Any dispersed population that no single authority represents can build that ladder, and it produces a body that courts, ministries and funders can deal with. IT LITIGATES AS A CO-PETITIONER RATHER THAN ALONE, WHICH IS HOW A COMMUNITY BODY REACHES A SUPREME COURT: it has joined petitions with the legal centre, the planning-rights body and other organisations recorded separately in this file — including proceedings over services in named villages and over discrimination in remote learning provision. The pairing this map has recorded repeatedly — a constituency body supplying standing and facts, a legal centre supplying the argument — is visible here in its most complete form. AND IT BUILT ITS OWN MEDIA DEPARTMENT IN LATE 2023 BECAUSE OF A GAP IT IDENTIFIED IN ITS OWN COVERAGE: it reports reaching millions through social media and initiating hundreds of stories in Israeli and international outlets, while noting that MOST OF THAT COVERAGE DID NOT ADDRESS LAND ISSUES. Getting attention and getting attention for the land question are different problems, and a campaign should measure the second. It takes donations directly and publishes its projects. THE SCOPE: it represents the unrecognised villages of the Negev and nothing else. A reader outside that context should take the structure and the two arguments, and use the planning and legal bodies recorded elsewhere in this file.

trackers.name: MedPAN — a Mediterranean fund this country is actually eligible for
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY IS NAMED ON ITS PUBLISHED ELIGIBLE LIST, WHICH MATTERS BECAUSE MOST CONSERVATION FUNDING EXCLUDES IT. This file has recorded two international funds that bar high-income economies outright and a third whose reach effectively does the same; a marine trust fund recorded in the previous round does not list this country among its priority countries either. This one does. WHAT IT OFFERS: calls for small projects of up to around twenty-five thousand euros for a single marine protected area, or up to around forty-five thousand where three or more areas cooperate — open both to the organisations managing an area AND to other bodies, including scientific institutions and NGOs, working with the responsible management authority. Given the strength of this country's marine research institutions, the cooperation category and the science route are the realistic openings. IT IS ALSO A NETWORK OF AROUND EIGHTY TO A HUNDRED MEMBER ORGANISATIONS THAT MANAGE OR ARE CREATING MEDITERRANEAN PROTECTED AREAS, WITH MEMBERSHIP OPEN TO BODIES CONTRIBUTING TO THE CREATION OF ONE — so a group campaigning for a coastal designation can join before it has obtained anything, and can reach practitioners in neighbouring countries facing the same coast and the same pressures. IT RUNS TRAINING FOR PROTECTED-AREA MANAGERS, HOLDS LARGE REGIONAL WORKSHOPS, MANAGES A MEDITERRANEAN PROTECTED-AREAS DATABASE AND PUBLISHES A STATUS REPORT EVERY FOUR YEARS. THE LIMITS: marine and coastal only, so an inland dispute is outside it; past calls have required the applicant to match around a quarter of the cost; and it funds management and protection rather than objection, litigation or campaigning against a scheme.

trackers.name: Farmers' Federation of Israel — the umbrella body of farmers, and why nobody can buy the land here
trackers.desc: BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE, KNOW THAT BUYING THE LAND IS NOT AN OPTION IN THIS COUNTRY. A Basic Law provides that the ownership of Israel lands SHALL NOT BE TRANSFERRED EITHER BY SALE OR IN ANY OTHER MANNER — long-term leasing is permitted, selling is not. No conservation purchaser, no land trust and no community buy-out can acquire such land. The routes that remain are the ones this file has recorded elsewhere in the region: leasehold, designation, use rights and agreement. Establish the tenure of the ground you are defending first, because it decides which half of this map applies to you. NOW THE BODY: an umbrella organisation of the country's farmers, grown out of an association of agricultural villages founded in 1920 and among the oldest agricultural organisations here. ITS FUNCTION IS THE ONE THIS CATEGORY EXISTS FOR: it is concerned with the professional, economic and social problems of its members and REPRESENTS THEM BEFORE GOVERNMENT AGENCIES. Its structure reaches the ground — local branches in the form of AGRICULTURAL COMMITTEES OR COOPERATIVES across dozens of villages, thousands of member families, and separate associations for particular branches of farming, alongside affiliated supply, marketing and mutual funds. THAT MATTERS FOR A LAND DISPUTE BECAUSE THE VILLAGE-LEVEL AGRICULTURAL COMMITTEE IS THE BODY THAT ALREADY SPEAKS FOR THE GROWERS OF ONE PLACE, and a national federation behind it is what turns a local objection into a sectoral one. Its secretary-general appears at national agricultural conferences on reforms affecting the sector, so it is active and audible. THE LIMITS, AND THEY ARE REAL. It is a sectoral representative body that works with government on marketing, taxation and transport rather than an environmental objector, and nothing found shows it opposing a development scheme. Its membership is private farmers, so tenants and labourers may not be covered as they are under the Turkish chambers recorded elsewhere in this file. AND NO WEBSITE COULD BE REACHED — this entry points at its own public page; much of the published description of its structure is decades old and should be verified. ONE HISTORICAL NOTE WITH PRACTICAL FORCE: the cooperative village model here — community ownership of land, individual ownership of homes, cooperative enterprise — was studied by a visiting delegation who went home and founded the first COMMUNITY LAND TRUST. The vehicle communities elsewhere use to hold land collectively was exported from this country, even though this country's own law forbids the sale that such a trust would need.

trackers.name: Planning information site — file your objection here, and read the committee's minutes first
trackers.desc: THIS IS NOT A MAP. IT IS WHERE OBJECTIONS ARE ACTUALLY FILED. The site allows SUBMITTING OBJECTIONS ONLINE FOR PLANS THAT HAVE BEEN DEPOSITED, and it was built by the planning administration's own digital division FOR TRANSPARENCY AND TO MAKE INFORMATION ACCESSIBLE TO THE GENERAL PUBLIC as well as to professional bodies. Every other entry recorded for this country tells a community who might help; this one is the door itself. BEFORE YOU OBJECT, KNOW THE TWO REQUIREMENTS AND THE EXCEPTION THAT MATTERS MOST. You must prepare a file setting out THE REASON for the objection, and you must hold A LAWYER'S AFFIDAVIT — EXCEPT FOR NATIONAL INFRASTRUCTURE PLANS, WHERE NO AFFIDAVIT IS REQUIRED. That exception is the single most useful fact in this entry: the largest schemes, the ones a village is least able to fund a fight against, are the ones it can object to without paying a lawyer to swear an affidavit. You then verify your identity through the government identification system, and the objection form is presented with guidance. READ THE COMMITTEE BEFORE YOU WRITE TO IT. The site publishes THE CONTACT DETAILS OF THE PLANNING COMMITTEES and information about their deliberations — INCLUDING AGENDAS, MINUTES AND DECISIONS. An objection written after reading the minutes of how similar plans were handled, and addressed to the committee that will hear it, is a different document from one written blind. YOU CAN ALSO SEARCH PLANS, APPLICATIONS AND APPEALS. Appeals matter: seeing whether anyone has already appealed a similar decision tells you whether the ground has been tested and on what argument. NOW THE WARNING, AND IT CAN COST YOU EVERYTHING. DATA ON PLANS UNDER LOCAL COMMITTEE AUTHORITY WERE RECEIVED FROM THOSE COMMITTEES AS THEY SUPPLIED THEM, DO NOT CONSTITUTE AN OFFICIAL OR LEGALLY BINDING PUBLICATION, AND ARE UPDATED ONLY SO FAR AS THE LOCAL COMMITTEE PASSED THE INFORMATION ON. The information is provided as it stands and the state accepts no responsibility for errors. AN OBJECTION PERIOD MISSED BECAUSE THE PORTAL WAS STALE IS NOT RECOVERABLE — so confirm the deposit date and the closing date directly with the local committee, using the contact details the site itself publishes, and do it early. USE IT WITH THE LEGAL AND PLANNING ORGANISATIONS RECORDED SEPARATELY FOR THIS COUNTRY, which are the bodies that can draft the objection and supply the affidavit where one is needed.

trackers.name: National hydrological committee chair — a named route into the water authority
trackers.desc: THE CHAIRPERSON OF THE NATIONAL HYDROLOGICAL COMMITTEE SITS IN BOTH THE NATIONAL COMMISSION AND THE WATER AUTHORITY, with a published address and with correspondence copied to a secretariat that publishes TWO TELEPHONE NUMBERS. THAT MATTERS BECAUSE THE WATER AUTHORITY IS THE BODY THAT DECIDES ALLOCATION. This is a named route into it through a scientific committee rather than through a complaints desk — and a technical enquiry addressed to a committee chairperson is answered by a different part of an institution than a grievance addressed to its public counter. WHAT TO ASK: which body holds the abstraction and allocation records for a named stream, spring or aquifer; whether monitoring data exists for a site; and what the committee has published on the basin in question. THE ANSWER TO THE FIRST QUESTION IS OFTEN THE WHOLE PROBLEM — communities lose water arguments because they do not know which office holds the numbers. AND THE COMMITTEE ITSELF IS A MAP. The programme recommends that national committees be MULTI-STAKEHOLDER IN MEMBERSHIP — scientists, water managers, government bodies, professional associations and CIVIL SOCIETY — so asking who the members are identifies every institution in the country working on water, and asking whether civil society is represented is asking for what the programme says should be there. THE LIMITS, AND THEY ARE PLAIN. THE CHAIRPERSON IS AN OFFICIAL OF THE WATER AUTHORITY, WHICH IS FREQUENTLY THE COUNTERPARTY IN A WATER DISPUTE — this is a route to data and to people, not to sympathy. The committee runs under government authority. Frame everything as a request for records and for the identity of the record-holder, and take the dispute itself to the planning objection route, the legal organisations and the environmental groups recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Cooperative societies register — the body that actually holds the land lease, and the model rules you can adopt
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY WAS THE LAST IN THIS MAP WITH ONLY ONE ROUTE TO HOLDING LAND, AND THE GAP WAS REAL RATHER THAN A TAGGING ERROR — ITS LISTING HOLDS CAMPAIGNERS, PLANNERS, LAWYERS AND A FARMERS' UMBRELLA, BUT NOTHING THAT HOLDS GROUND. HERE IS THE VEHICLE ITS OWN COUNTRYSIDE RUNS ON: THE ALLOCATION AGREEMENT IS A LEASE SIGNED BETWEEN A COOPERATIVE SOCIETY AND THE STATE LAND AUTHORITY, and the allocation is the TOTAL UNIT OF LAND ASSIGNED TO THAT SOCIETY — for agriculture, industry, employment, commerce, leisure and other designations, with an individual holding inside it being the land designated to a member for residence and livelihood. IN THE RURAL SECTOR HERE, THE COOPERATIVE SOCIETY IS THE ENTITY THAT HOLDS THE LAND. A group of people cannot lease state land as a crowd; a registered society can. THE TYPES ARE FIXED BY REGULATION AND CHOOSING THE RIGHT ONE IS THE FIRST DECISION. AN AGRICULTURAL COOPERATIVE SOCIETY covers bodies engaged in settlement or agriculture, or whose members wholly or partly are — and it is expressly SUITABLE FOR SOCIAL, SETTLEMENT AND BUSINESS AIMS ALIKE, which is unusually wide. A COMMUNITY SETTLEMENT SOCIETY organises members' settlement as a community and runs community life as its own statute provides. AND THERE IS A WATER SUPPLY SOCIETY WHOSE WHOLE PURPOSE IS REGULATING THE SUPPLY OF WATER TO ITS MEMBERS — which is the form to examine wherever a community's fight is about a spring, a well or an irrigation source. REGISTRATION IS SIMPLER THAN COMMUNITIES EXPECT, AND ONE PROVISION SAVES MONTHS: A SOCIETY MAY ADOPT THE MODEL RULES THE REGISTRAR HAS APPROVED FOR SOCIETIES OF ITS TYPE INSTEAD OF DRAFTING ITS OWN. This file has warned repeatedly that a statute drafted badly closes doors for years; here the state supplies a tested one free. Founders submit two signed copies of the statute and appoint one person to negotiate the registration. KNOW ALSO THAT THE REGISTRAR DETERMINES THE SOCIETY'S TYPE AND NOTIFIES IT IN WRITING — AND MAY LATER CHANGE IT, amending the register and issuing a corrected certificate. THE TYPE IS NOT PURELY YOUR CHOICE, so match your stated objects to the type you want before filing, and keep the notification, because the classification governs what the society may do with its land. THERE IS A PUBLIC DATABASE FOR FINDING ANY REGISTERED SOCIETY. USE IT BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE: find out which society already holds the allocation covering the ground you care about, because the lease-holder is the party a developer must deal with, and its members are the people whose votes decide. ONE MORE STRUCTURE WORTH KNOWING: AN AUDIT UNION IS A REGISTERED ASSOCIATION OF SOCIETIES WHOSE MAIN PURPOSE IS AUDITING THE ACCOUNTS OF ITS MEMBER SOCIETIES, alongside supervision and education in cooperation — a route to independent scrutiny of how a society is being run, which matters when a society's leadership is the one agreeing to a development. THE LIMITS: this is a legal form and a registry, not an organisation that will help you — nobody here advises or funds. Most land is state land leased through this system rather than owned, so a society holds a lease and its terms govern everything. And the same form is used by settlements of every political description; recording it here is a statement about a legal vehicle, not about any of them.

trackers.name: Open spaces fund — one per cent of state land revenue, spent on protecting open land
trackers.desc: THE FUNDING MODEL IS THE REASON TO RECORD THIS AND THE REASON TO LOOK FOR IT ELSEWHERE: THE FUND IS FINANCED BY ONE PER CENT OF THE STATE LAND AUTHORITY'S REVENUES, FIXED IN REGULATIONS. A SET SHARE OF WHAT THE STATE EARNS FROM LAND IS SPENT ON PROTECTING OPEN LAND — so the money grows as development proceeds, which makes it the rare fund that is not exhausted by the pressure it exists to answer. It was established in 2009 and is operated and financed by the land authority itself, under regulations made in 2011, and governed by a NINE-MEMBER BOARD representing institutions named in those regulations. WHAT IT PAYS FOR IS BROAD AND EXPLICIT: THE PRESERVATION, ENVIRONMENTAL DEVELOPMENT AND CULTIVATION OF OPEN SPACES OUTSIDE BUILT-UP URBAN AREAS — INCLUDING OPEN SPACES IMPORTANT FOR BIODIVERSITY AND ECOLOGICAL SYSTEMS, parks and recreation areas — AND ASSISTANCE TO BODIES WORKING TOWARDS THOSE AIMS. It also funds THE REHABILITATION OF QUARRIES AND ABANDONED SITES, which is the answer for a community living beside a worked-out pit nobody will restore. IT BUDGETS SURVEYS AS WELL AS WORKS. That is the line to ask about first: a funded survey of what an open area actually contains is cheaper than a project, far easier to approve, and produces the documentation that every later argument depends on. THE SCALE IS REAL — IN ONE YEAR A HUNDRED MILLION SHEKELS WENT TO NINETY-THREE ENVIRONMENTAL PROJECTS — AND IT DISTRIBUTES THROUGH PUBLISHED CALLS FOR PROPOSALS, three of them in a single year in one instance, one specifically for PRACTICAL ACTIONS IN OPEN SPACES. BUT READ THE ELIGIBILITY BEFORE PLANNING ANYTHING: THE APPLICANTS NAMED IN THAT CALL WERE LOCAL AUTHORITIES, GOVERNMENT MINISTRIES, GOVERNMENT COMPANIES AND STATUTORY BODIES. A COMMUNITY DOES NOT APPLY — ITS LOCAL AUTHORITY DOES. So the work is to arrive at the council with a specific, costed proposal for a named open area and ask it to submit, exactly as this file recorded for a municipal heritage fund in another country. A regional council with open land in its area and no cost to itself has little reason to refuse. AND USE THE PUBLISHED DECISIONS, WHICH INCLUDE PROJECTS REJECTED FOR FAILING THRESHOLD CONDITIONS. READING WHY OTHERS WERE REFUSED IS THE FASTEST WAY TO LEARN WHAT A COMPLIANT APPLICATION LOOKS LIKE, and it costs nothing. THE LIMITS: it is operated by the authority that manages state land and sells development rights, so it funds preservation within the state's own planning framework and will not fund opposition to a plan. Its money follows government priorities and its board is institutional. AND IT PAYS FOR WORKS AND SURVEYS ON OPEN LAND — IT DOES NOT BUY LAND OR PAY LEGAL COSTS. Read it with the planning objection routes and the cooperative land vehicle recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: State legal aid — free representation on an income test, and the significance test a land case should aim at
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING HELD PLANNERS, A LEGAL CENTRE, A FREEDOM-OF-INFORMATION LITIGATOR AND OBJECTION ROUTES — AND NO ANSWER FOR SOMEONE WHO CANNOT PAY A LAWYER. UNDER THE LEGAL AID LAW, PEOPLE OF LOW INCOME ARE ENTITLED TO FREE OR SUBSIDISED REPRESENTATION, ON AN INCOME AND PROPERTY TEST. BUT THERE IS A SECOND TEST, AND IT IS THE ONE A COMMUNITY SHOULD AIM AT: THE MATTER MUST BE A CASE OF SUBSTANTIAL LEGAL AND SOCIAL SIGNIFICANCE. A DISPUTE THAT AFFECTS A WHOLE VILLAGE, A SHARED WATER SOURCE OR AN AREA OF OPEN LAND IS EXACTLY THE KIND OF CLAIM THAT ARGUMENT FITS — so an application should set out the public significance as carefully as the poverty. HOW TO APPLY, PRECISELY: a detailed form to the legal aid department, with personal details, FINANCIAL DOCUMENTS, and a full explanation of the legal proceeding required. Attach income confirmations, payslips and an affidavit of financial position. THERE IS A TELEPHONE LINE FOR THE LEGAL AID DIVISION for questions before you file. NOW THE PART ALMOST NOBODY IS TOLD, AND IT DECIDES THE QUALITY OF WHAT YOU GET. APPOINTED LAWYERS COME FROM A POOL OF EXTERNAL LAWYERS THAT EACH BUREAU RECRUITS AND MANAGES, AND MEMBERSHIP OF THAT POOL IS A THRESHOLD CONDITION FOR BEING APPOINTED. The bureaus keep CLOSE AND CONTINUOUS SUPERVISION over the pool and deliberately keep it SMALL AND HIGH-QUALITY so that supervision can be effective — which means the lawyer you are assigned is being watched by the body that appointed them. AND A RULE WORTH KNOWING IF YOUR CASE IS QUIETLY HANDED ON: A LAWYER IN THE POOL MAY NOT TRANSFER A LEGAL AID CASE TO A LAWYER WHO IS NOT IN THE POOL — NOT EVEN A PARTNER OR AN EMPLOYEE IN THE SAME FIRM. If a different person turns up to handle your matter, ask whether they are in the pool. Replacement of an assigned lawyer may also be examined depending on circumstances, though it may not be granted, AND THERE IS AN ONLINE PUBLIC ENQUIRIES FORM FOR RAISING IT. IF YOU ARE REFUSED, THE ROUTE DOES NOT END. Those found ineligible are directed to free or nominal-fee assistance from other organisations — including the bar association's PRO BONO PROGRAMME and UNIVERSITY LEGAL CLINICS, and this file records a planning-focused body and a legal centre with a land and planning practice separately for this country. THE LIMITS: eligibility turns first on personal poverty, so a community that is not individually poor will not qualify however important its case — in that situation the significance argument belongs to the pro bono programme and the clinics instead. Legal aid also covers defined categories of proceeding, and planning objections may not be among them; ASK THE HOTLINE WHETHER YOUR TYPE OF PROCEEDING IS COVERED BEFORE ASSEMBLING THE PAPERWORK.

trackers.name: EcoPeace Middle East
trackers.desc: Founded in 1994 as Friends of the Earth Middle East and still a member of Friends of the Earth International, EcoPeace is staffed and directed jointly by Jordanians, Palestinians and Israelis, with its own offices in Amman, Ramallah and Tel Aviv and a national director in each. WHO TO ENLIST: the office in your own country. Its Good Water Neighbors programme works with communities on either side of a shared water problem, pairing them across the border rather than treating each in isolation. You CAN get community-level organising support and technical and advocacy weight on water, sewage and Jordan Valley development. You CAN'T get a litigator — EcoPeace works by cross-border cooperation, research and advocacy, not by suing proponents, so a community that needs a permit or an approval challenged in court should look elsewhere. For activists: in Jordan and Palestine this was the only substantial environmental organisation with an office and a named national director that could be verified on its own domain.

trackers.name: Audit Bureau
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Jordan, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Companies Control Department
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Department of Statistics
trackers.desc: Jordan's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Jordan.

trackers.name: JONEPS e-Procurement
trackers.desc: National public-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Jordan, and for how much.

trackers.name: Financial Disclosure Department (Ministry of Justice)
trackers.desc: National asset-declaration body; Jordan’s Financial Disclosure Department collects officials’ sealed declarations, opened only on complaint, Jordan.

trackers.name: Jordanian Constitutional Court
trackers.desc: Jordanian Constitutional Court — supreme court in Jordan (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: Article 23 delegation — a voluntary society can hold ministerial powers
trackers.desc: THE ROUTE JORDAN ACTUALLY USES. Article 23 lets the Ministry, with Cabinet approval, delegate any of its tasks or powers to ministries, institutions and relevant voluntary societies in environmental protection — provided the delegation is in writing and specific. That is how the Royal Society for the Conservation of Nature enforces wildlife law by delegation from the Ministry of Agriculture, works with the environmental police, and has issued hunting licences since 1973. SO THE QUESTION IS WHO HOLDS THE WRITTEN DELEGATION for your subject and area — ask for it by name, because the law requires it to be written and specific. BUT ARTICLE 24 IS A REAL GATE ON ORGANISING: licensing and renewal of licensing of non-governmental societies working in environmental protection happens only after prior approval of the Ministry. The renewal limb is the one groups forget — diary the date and start ministry approval early. A DEFINITION WORTH USING: degradation means reducing the environment's value, distorting its nature, depleting its resources or harming living organisms or antiquities — antiquities sit inside the environmental definition of harm.

trackers.name: Special protection area — the category for a threatened species, not a view
trackers.desc: PICK THE RIGHT CATEGORY BEFORE YOU ARGUE. The nature reserves and national parks regulation defines: national park — land, water, shores, oases, forests or heritage areas that the Council of Ministers decides is one, so a site need not be wilderness; protected land — deliberately broad, any land the Council decides is protected; and special protection area — an area hosting a distinctive ecosystem or wildlife threatened with extinction. That last is the category to seek when your argument is a specific threatened species or a distinctive ecosystem rather than scenic value. WHO DECIDES: the Council of Ministers, on the Minister's recommendation — so the recommendation is the step to influence. The competent body that establishes or manages a reserve is appointed the same way, which is how a non-state body can run one. Article 21 requires the specifications and conditions for any reserve to be set by regulation, so the standards are written and checkable. CONTEXT: RSCN founded 1966, first reserve Shaumari 1975, Dibbeen sixth in 2004 at around 1,200 km²; Fifa 2011; Burqu, Dhuheikeh and Dumaitha 2018. RSCN has an elected 11-member board, elected every 4 years — a membership you can join and a board you can stand for.

trackers.name: Environment Protection Fund — currently disbursing, chaired by the Minister
trackers.desc: AN ACTIVE GRANT WINDOW, NOT A DORMANT ONE. The Board of the Environment Protection Fund meets at the Ministry of Environment and is chaired by the Minister of Environment, and has approved financing for a package of environmental and development projects covering sustainable agriculture and green economy work — aimed at protecting the environment, ensuring sustainability of natural resources, and enhancing the participation of local communities in achieving sustainable environmental development. TWO THINGS FOLLOW: approvals are being reported currently, so the fund is disbursing; and local community participation is an express objective of what the board has just funded, so a community-participation framing matches its stated priorities rather than arguing against them. The board being chaired by the Minister tells you the level at which decisions are made — ministry relationships matter alongside a paper application. Approvals are announced through Petra, the Jordan News Agency, which is a way to track what has actually been funded before you draft. DO NOT CONFUSE IT with the Saudi صندوق البيئة (Environment Fund), a different country's body covering ‘environment and meteorology’ that surfaces on the same search terms.

trackers.name: GEF endorsement runs through Planning, not Environment
trackers.desc: APPROACHING THE WRONG MINISTRY LOSES TIME. Jordan's GEF Operational Focal Point sits in the Ministry of Planning and International Cooperation, not the environment ministry — the Secretary General, focal point since 17 March 2021 — and a working contact is published: Head of Division, World Bank Division, International Cooperation Department, Amman; tel +962 6 4644466 ext 644; email maher.abdelrahim@mop.gov.jo. A GEF project needs that focal point's endorsement. Jordan sits in a constituency with Afghanistan, Iraq, Lebanon, Pakistan, Syria and Yemen, and financing for national and regional projects is inclusive of all participating countries. UNDER GEF-8 STAR FULL FLEXIBILITY, funds may be drawn across biodiversity, climate change and land degradation, with the source focal area endorsed by the Operational Focal Point — so which envelope your project is charged to is that person's decision, and worth discussing before submission. Jordan is also a Green Climate Fund country with a National Designated Authority. OTHER BODIES: JOHUD (created by royal decree 1977) is the largest development NGO, with a network of 51 community centres and, since 1979, special legal status with administrative and financial independence — its mandate is poverty, women, youth and water scarcity, not primarily environmental, so approach it on a livelihood or water framing. EcoPeace Middle East works across Amman, Bethlehem and Tel Aviv.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: RSCN — an NGO you can approach that carries state enforcement power and proposes new reserves
trackers.desc: THE INVERSION: THIS IS A NON-GOVERNMENTAL BODY THAT ENFORCES THE LAW. The Royal Society for the Conservation of Nature enforces the Wildlife Protection Act under a special mandate from the Ministry of Agriculture and works alongside the environmental police unit, the Rangers — so a report to RSCN behaves more like a report to a regulator than a letter to a charity, and it is one of very few organisations in the Middle East holding that kind of public mandate. WHAT IT HOLDS: ten protected areas — Shaumari, Azraq, Wadi Mujib, Ajloun, Dana, Dibeen, Yarmouk, Fifa, Burqu and Dahek — covering 4,656 square kilometres. THE DOOR FOR A COMMUNITY IS THE PIPELINE: RSCN states that additional sites are proposed as locations for new reserves in coming years. Land that enters that pipeline is being assessed by the body that will manage it, which is a far stronger position than objecting to a plan after it is filed — approach RSCN about the site itself, early, rather than about the project. CHECK YOUR FIGURES AGAINST RSCN'S OWN PAGES: several widely-copied third-party profiles still describe seven reserves covering about 1,200 square kilometres, which is badly out of date; RSCN's own What We Do page gives ten and 4,656. Quoting the stale figure at a hearing hands the other side an easy correction. THE LIMIT, AND IT MATTERS: RSCN holds its mandate from the government. It is at its strongest against hunting, overgrazing, encroachment and unlicensed works, and a community should not assume it will front a fight against a development the state itself is backing. Founded 1966, based in Amman.

trackers.name: BirdLife Hima Fund — grants for Important Bird Areas, but you apply through RSCN, not directly
trackers.desc: THIS IS ONE OF VERY FEW DOCUMENTED GRANT WINDOWS FOR LAND PROTECTION ANYWHERE IN THIS REGION, AND JORDAN IS ONE OF ONLY FOUR COUNTRIES BIRDLIFE NAMES AS HAVING RECEIVED ONE. BirdLife records that the Hima Fund launched in 2011 with four approved grants to Partners in Jordan, Lebanon, Qatar and Oman, to reinforce or revitalise Himas at four sites. The fund was established in Qatar in 2008 and endowed by a one million dollar donation from Sheikha Jawaher Bint Hamad Bin Suhaim Al-Thani, with the stated purpose of conserving Important Bird Areas and their threatened species in the Middle East. THE ROUTE IS INDIRECT AND THIS IS THE PART PEOPLE GET WRONG: the grants went to BirdLife Partners, not to communities. In Jordan the BirdLife Partner is the Royal Society for the Conservation of Nature, already recorded in this file — so a community with a threatened bird habitat approaches RSCN and asks it to carry the application, rather than applying to Doha. WHAT THE FUND BUYS IS THE HIMA MODEL, NOT A PURCHASE: the Hima is a traditional land designation under which a defined community controls access and use, and may forbid hunting, wood cutting and destruction of trees and shrubs within it — so frame the site as a community-managed protected area, not as a piece of land to be bought. THE CAVEAT THAT MATTERS MOST AND WEAKENS THIS ENTRY: no evidence of grant-making after the early 2010s was found during verification. The founding donation, the establishment and the first four grants are documented; a current, open application window is not. Establish that the fund is still disbursing before building a timetable around it, and ask RSCN, which would know. DO NOT ASSUME A WIDER REMIT MEANS A WIDER FUND: press reporting from 2010 lists twelve countries the fund was geared toward; BirdLife's own page names four that received grants. This entry exists in those four only.

trackers.name: Justice Center for Legal Aid — because Jordan's statutory right to a free lawyer stops at ten years' imprisonment
trackers.desc: START FROM THE FACT JCLA ITSELF PUBLISHES: JORDANIAN LAW GRANTS THE RIGHT TO FREE LEGAL ASSISTANCE ONLY TO THOSE FACING A SENTENCE OF TEN OR MORE YEARS' IMPRISONMENT. For anyone fighting a development, a quarry, an expropriation or a permit, that means there is no statutory route to a lawyer whatsoever, and the courts being formally open to all is not the same as being usable. JCLA is the body that fills the gap: founded 2008, the first legal aid organisation in the country, now operating clinics across all twelve governorates, and by one account defending more clients than Jordan's other twelve legal aid organisations combined. Roughly 375 consultations a month and representation for about 150 people across 200 cases. THE CONSULTATION AND THE REPRESENTATION ARE TWO DIFFERENT DOORS. Any poor or vulnerable person may visit a clinic for advice; representation requires passing three checks, revised annually — a means check on whether you could afford a private lawyer, a check that the case falls within JCLA's areas, and for civil and family matters a check on whether the case has reasonable prospects of success and whether representation is actually necessary to a good outcome. The assessment is applied regardless of nationality, gender or legal status, and neither the centre nor the assigned attorney charges the beneficiary. THE TRAP, AND READ IT BEFORE YOU BUILD A PLAN: JCLA's published areas of representation are civil, criminal and family or sharia law. Administrative law — which is the category a challenge to a planning decision or an environmental permit falls into — is not among them. A civil claim framed around damage, nuisance or compensation may fit where an administrative challenge does not, so ask how your matter would be classified at the first consultation rather than after. One encouraging sign not confirmed on JCLA's own pages: the InforMEA environmental legal protection directory lists JCLA, which suggests environmental matters are within reach — treat that as a question to put, not a fact. Contact info@jcla-org.com; use the clinic locator on the site rather than a published count, since sources give both 21 and 24 clinics.

trackers.name: Ministry of Awqaf and the Awqaf Council — waqf land carries an expropriation consent gate ordinary land does not
trackers.desc: THE LEVER: JORDANIAN WAQF LAND CANNOT BE EXPROPRIATED IN THE ORDINARY WAY. Article 24 of the Awqaf, Islamic Affairs and Holy Places Law provides that, notwithstanding anything in any other legislation, no waqf land may be expropriated except for fair compensation and with the approval of the Awqaf Council — and that where waqf land is expropriated, no part of its area may be deducted free of charge. Two consequences a land defence should act on. First, there is a body whose consent is required, which means there is a body that can be petitioned to withhold it — that is a door ordinary private landowners facing a road, a dam or a zone simply do not have. Second, the free-of-charge deduction that public-purpose takings normally rely on does not apply, so the arithmetic of a scheme crossing waqf land is worse for the developer than across neighbouring plots. ESTABLISH FIRST WHETHER THE LAND IS ACTUALLY WAQF, BECAUSE THE REGISTRATION LEAVES A TRACE: on a valid charitable waqf the Department of Lands and Survey registers the property and issues the title deed in the name of the General Custodian of Islamic Awqaf; on a family or shared waqf a waqf annotation is entered on the reverse of the register sheet recording that the whole parcel is dedicated as family or shared waqf, in the terms of the waqf deed. Check the register sheet before assuming, and check it for neighbouring parcels too. THE ROUTE THAT PUTS LAND BEYOND ORDINARY DEALING: dedicating land as charitable waqf, with charitable Islamic awqaf and the transactions relating to them exempted from taxes, fees and stamp duties. THE COUNTERWEIGHT, AND IT MUST BE READ: the Ministry's own investment arm buys and sells non-waqf real estate with waqf funds, and the Ministry may take financing or issue Sharia-compliant funding instruments — this is an institution with a development portfolio, not a conservation body, and on another site it may be the developer. VERIFY THE CURRENT TEXT BEFORE RELYING ON ARTICLE 24: Law 32 of 2001 was amended in 2025, and a legal database rendering of the provision carries the free-of-charge protection without the Awqaf Council approval requirement, which may reflect the amended wording. Take the article as it now stands from the Ministry's own legislation pages rather than from this entry. Founded 1968; Jordanian waqf administration ran under the Ottoman Awqaf Administration Regulation of 1280 AH until 1946.

trackers.name: JREDS — got the Aqaba master plan amended and the change gazetted, so it is permanent
trackers.desc: THE TACTIC THAT WORKED WAS AMENDING THE PLAN, NOT FIGHTING A PROJECT — AND GETTING THE AMENDMENT GAZETTED SO IT COULD NOT BE QUIETLY UNDONE. Jordan's entire coastline is 27 kilometres. Since the Aqaba Special Economic Zone Authority was established in 2001 the country lost around 10 kilometres of shore to investment, leaving roughly 5 kilometres of public-access beachfront. JREDS built a coalition of more than seventy organisations and some 2,300 people — including 1,441 young people aged 18 to 25 and 871 school students — running awareness workshops on beach access and on the zone authority's development plans, and taking people on field visits to see the state of the public beaches for themselves. The result: the authority's Board of Commissioners accepted the proposed amendments to the master plan, and the changes were issued in the Official Gazette by the cabinet, making them permanent. A plan amendment published in the gazette outlives the campaign that won it, in a way that a promise from a board does not. The campaign also brought the seven largest environmental organisations in Jordan into one coalition, and its next stage was legislative advocacy to write public beach access into national law. WHO THEY ARE: founded in 1993 by Jordanian diving enthusiasts and registered in 1995 under the Ministry of Interior as the first specialised Jordanian organisation for marine conservation; IUCN member; three programmes covering marine conservation, outreach and advocacy, and sustainable development. Offices in Aqaba. NOW THE PART YOU MUST WEIGH BEFORE ENLISTING THEM, AND IT IS UNCOMFORTABLE: their published partner and funder list includes the Aqaba Development Corporation, the Aqaba Container Terminal, a large potash company and a named coastal resort project — that is, coastal developers and a port operator in the very zone whose master plan they campaigned to amend, alongside international agencies. Reported income also includes fees from hotels and beaches. That does not erase the gazetted amendment, which happened; it means you should establish where they stand on your specific site before assuming alignment, and expect their advocacy to aim at regulating development rather than stopping it. SCOPE LIMIT: this is a marine and coastal body. For inland Jordan the file carries RSCN for protected areas and the Justice Center for Legal Aid for counsel. SOURCING NOTE: the coalition figures and the gazette outcome come from a human rights practice platform's case study rather than from jreds.org, and the funder list from a network member profile — confirm both with JREDS before quoting them.

trackers.name: CEPF Mediterranean Basin — live calls with published deadlines, and Jordan is named eligible in both
trackers.desc: THIS IS THE ONLY FUND IN THIS FILE WITH DATED, OPEN CALLS RATHER THAN A DOCUMENTED PAST, AND JORDAN IS NAMED ELIGIBLE IN BOTH OF THEM. A large-grants call for letters of inquiry opened on 1 July 2026 and closes on 18 September 2026 at midnight Washington time, with grants from fifty thousand to a hundred and eighty thousand US dollars, restricted to two strategic directions: traditional land use practices, and preservation of threatened plant species. A separate small-grants call ran from 9 February to 15 March 2026 with grants of twenty to fifty thousand dollars from a total pot of five hundred and forty thousand, restricted to conservation of threatened freshwater biodiversity, with projects to start on 1 August 2026 and finish by 30 September 2027. Read those strategic directions carefully before framing anything: a Jordanian project about grazing, terracing or other traditional land use fits the large-grants window, one about a spring or a wadi fits the freshwater window, and one that fits neither will not be funded however good it is. THE ELIGIBILITY BAR IS ORGANISATIONAL AND IT IS STRICT: applicants must be legally registered entities with their own bank accounts and authorisation under national law to receive charitable funding. Individuals cannot apply and must work through such an organisation. LOCAL AND NATIONAL NGOS ARE EXPLICITLY PRIORITISED in the small-grants call, which is unusual and favours exactly the kind of body this map exists to connect people to. Letters of inquiry go through the ConservationGrants portal in English or French; the regional implementation team is BirdLife International with the Slovenian bird society DOPPS, reachable on a published team address, and the team ran language webinars with session times given for Amman. WATCH THE CALLS PAGE RATHER THAN THE FUND: windows open for roughly five to ten weeks and then shut, and applications after the deadline are refused whatever the reason. CEPF is a joint initiative of the French Development Agency, Conservation International, the European Union, the Global Environment Facility, the Government of Japan and the World Bank; the global fund belongs elsewhere in this map and only the Mediterranean window is recorded here.

trackers.name: GEF Small Grants Programme Jordan — grants direct to community organisations, running here since 1992, with a national coordinator you can approach
trackers.desc: THIS FUND GOES DIRECTLY TO COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS RATHER THAN THROUGH A NATIONAL INTERMEDIARY, AND IT HAS BEEN IN JORDAN SINCE NOVEMBER 1992 — more than two hundred projects funded in its first two decades alone. It supports local community members, community-based organisations and civil society organisations, working across the environmental focal areas of biodiversity, climate change mitigation and adaptation, land degradation and sustainable forest management, international waters and chemicals. Land degradation and sustainable land management is the direction most likely to fit a land-defence project. THE STRUCTURE IS THE ACCESS POINT AND IT IS UNUSUALLY REACHABLE: the programme runs in a decentralised, country-driven way through a National Coordinator and a National Steering Committee, so decisions are made in Amman by people you can meet rather than in a foreign capital, and proposals must align with the Jordan Country Programme Strategy — read that document before drafting, because alignment with it is an explicit assessment criterion alongside meeting the programme's own criteria and being proposed by a national community or non-governmental organisation. GRANT SIZES ARE OFTEN MISQUOTED, SO TAKE THEM FROM THE GEF ITSELF: the core global programme funds grants up to seventy-five thousand US dollars, with up to a hundred and fifty thousand for strategic projects intended to scale a proven approach across a landscape. The widely repeated figure of fifty thousand is the older ceiling and still appears on many UNDP pages; the practical average has historically run well below either, around twenty to twenty-five thousand. A separate CSO Challenge Programme launched in June 2026, led by IUCN with ten million dollars available and grants up to three hundred thousand, but its eligible-country list could not be verified on a canonical source this round and must be checked on thegef.org before anyone relies on it. ONE FIGURE WORTH KNOWING IF YOUR GROUP IS WOMEN-LED: UNDP reports that 55 per cent of the community organisations benefiting from Jordan's programme are led by women. CURRENCY CAVEAT: the Jordan page's published project count runs to June 2014, so confirm the programme is currently accepting proposals and identify the current National Coordinator before preparing anything. The global programme belongs elsewhere in this map; only the Jordan country programme is recorded here.

trackers.name: Royal Botanic Garden — 180 hectares held and restored, and the herders who opposed it ended up with more pasture
trackers.desc: THE EVIDENCE HERE ANSWERS THE OBJECTION EVERY PROPOSED RESERVE MEETS. When this garden was established the local sheep and goat herders feared it would take their grazing and their livelihoods. Grazing was stopped on the site in 2008 for three years, agreed with those communities, so that the recovery of the vegetation could be measured and a sustainable grazing level calculated from what was actually observed. A herder from a neighbouring village is on record saying that once the site was fenced and protected the plant cover grew, that in summer they began finding good pasture there, and that they could graze for longer. If you are told a protected area will cost the village its pasture, this is the case to cite: a measured three-year exclosure that ended with more grazing, not less, and a number attached to how much the land can carry. WHAT IT HOLDS: 180 hectares — 1,800 dunums — at Tal Ar-Rumman about 25 kilometres north of Amman above the King Talal dam, with more than 300 metres of elevation change across the site, which is why it can represent a large share of Jordan's flora. The site was declared an environmentally important site by the Ministry of Environment in 2014, so the land carries a designation as well as an owner. Five Jordanian habitats are being re-created on it — deciduous oak, pine, juniper, Jordan Valley and freshwater. WHAT IT CAN GIVE A CAMPAIGN: a seed bank holding over 1,200 accessions of more than 400 species, representing over sixteen per cent of Jordan's native plant species, built with training from the Millennium Seed Bank and intended for habitat re-establishment and restoration; and a herbarium whose specimens have been scanned at high resolution to form the region's first online herbarium. If you need to establish what grew on a site before it was cleared, or to restore it afterwards, that is where the material and the records are. Its community rangeland rehabilitation work is reported to have raised and diversified incomes for local livestock owners, and it welcomes volunteers. A non-governmental non-profit founded in the mid-2000s on the initiative of a member of the royal family who also founded the Jordanian marine conservation society recorded elsewhere in this file — worth knowing, since the two are the country's strongest non-state conservation bodies and share a founder. THE LIMITS: it is one site and a research and restoration institution, not a litigator, a funder or a national campaigner, and its royal patronage places it firmly within the establishment. It will supply seed, records, restoration expertise and the grazing precedent; it will not object to your scheme. Founding year is given as both 2005 and 2008 across sources; the garden's own material and the earlier listings favour 2005.

trackers.name: Rasheed — Jordan's transparency chapter, whose own strategy is helping communities act on specific grievances
trackers.desc: ITS OWN PUBLISHED STRATEGY IS THE REASON TO RECORD IT: it commits to helping individuals, communities, civil society organisations and social movements ACT ON SPECIFIC CORRUPTION PROBLEMS IDENTIFIED IN THEIR COMMUNITIES, and to take action on specific grievances — not only to publish indices. That matters because this file has established that Jordan's conservation bodies are royally chartered and do not object to schemes, and that organised opposition runs through unions and parties rather than through organisations a village can approach. This is the first Jordanian entry here whose stated purpose includes acting on a community's own grievance. It is a non-profit founded at the end of 2013 by anti-corruption activists, and has served as the Transparency International chapter in Jordan since April 2014, based in Amman. It also states an aim of establishing and leading a watchdog coalition. ASK IT ONE SPECIFIC QUESTION, BECAUSE THE ANSWER WOULD CHANGE WHAT IT IS WORTH TO YOU: does it run an Advocacy and Legal Advice Centre? The Transparency International network operates these in more than fifty countries — free, confidential advice for victims and witnesses of corruption, expressly including help to ACCESS PUBLIC INFORMATION, to identify the documents that would strengthen a case and how to obtain them, and to draft, submit and follow up official complaint letters. NO SUCH CENTRE IN JORDAN COULD BE CONFIRMED, and that is the single most useful thing to establish before relying on this entry. NOW THE WARNING, AND IT IS THE FOURTH OF ITS KIND IN THIS FILE AND THE SECOND IN THE SAME PLACE: in 2025 it launched a complaints platform IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE AQABA SPECIAL ECONOMIC ZONE AUTHORITY — the same authority that signs the land leases for development in that zone. This payload already records a Jordanian marine society that campaigned against coastal development while listing the zone's development corporation, its container terminal and a coastal resort among its partners. A complaint about a project inside that zone, routed through a platform co-run with the zone's own authority, is a complaint travelling through the body being complained about. Establish where a complaint goes and who reads it before using it, and consider whether an external route recorded elsewhere in this file is safer for that particular grievance. THE OTHER LIMIT: its subject is corruption and governance, not land, planning or environment. Frame the matter as a procurement, permit or integrity question rather than an environmental one — which, on the evidence in this file about Jordan, is likely to be the more productive framing anyway.

trackers.name: Jordan Environment Society — fifteen branches outside the capital, and it teaches impact assessment
trackers.desc: IT HAS FIFTEEN BRANCHES AROUND THE COUNTRY AND ITS STATED PURPOSE INCLUDES PROMOTING COMMUNITY ACTION AT THE LOCAL LEVEL. That matters because every other Jordanian body in this file operates from the capital or the Aqaba zone — a community in a governorate has had nowhere in this map to walk into, and now has fifteen possibilities. Ask which branch covers your area and what it has done there. AND IT RUNS TRAINING COURSES IN ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT, as a series rather than a one-off. This file has recorded four times over that the way a scheme is actually beaten is by attacking its impact assessment — a Turkish association forcing a court audit of one, a Kazakh group counting the developer's own emission figures, a Turkish movement counting felled trees against the number the report declared, a Georgian body checking which consultancy wrote it. ALL OF THAT REQUIRES SOMEONE WHO CAN READ THE DOCUMENT, AND THIS IS THE ONLY BODY IN THIS PAYLOAD'S JORDANIAN ENTRIES THAT TEACHES IT. Ask when the next course runs and whether a community member can attend. Established 1988, based in Amman, described as the largest non-governmental organisation in its field in the country and a member of the international conservation union, with a published postal address, telephone and email. Its project record spans water and environmental awareness, waste and hazardous waste management, recycling, biogas, integrated pest control, environmental media and a student network. NOW THE PART THAT DECIDES HOW YOU USE IT, AND IT IS NOT SMALL: IN 2003 IT SIGNED A MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING WITH THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT FOR COOPERATION IN ALL ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES, and the Jordanian government sits among its supporters alongside foreign development agencies. It frames its aim as a balance between economic growth and the environment. THIS IS NOT A BODY THAT WILL OBJECT TO A GOVERNMENT-BACKED SCHEME ON YOUR BEHALF, and nothing found shows it having done so. This file has established across three rounds that Jordan has no such body: its conservation organisations are royally chartered, and opposition to large projects runs through unions, parties and parliamentarians rather than environmental organisations. Use this one for the training, for the local branch, and for technical understanding — and take the objection itself to the legal aid service, the access-to-information route and the international finance mechanisms recorded elsewhere in this file. Verify currency before relying on it: the most detailed accounts of its training programme reached are some years old.

trackers.name: Tashbeek — a Jordanian platform listing which grant calls are open now, and to whom
trackers.desc: IT LISTS THE FUNDING CALLS OPEN TO JORDANIAN ORGANISATIONS RIGHT NOW, IN ARABIC, IN ONE PLACE. Each listing shows THE FUNDER, THE SECTOR — environment and green innovation among them — the project start and end dates, WHETHER APPLICATIONS ARE OPEN OR CLOSED, and a direct link to apply. Every other funding route recorded for this country is a single foreign funder that a group has to already know about; this is a domestic list that tells you what exists and whether the window is still open. THE CALLS IT CARRIES ARE THE KIND SMALL GROUPS CAN ACTUALLY WIN. One listed programme states that it supports initiatives DESIGNED BY LOCAL COMMUNITIES, backing limited and clearly defined activities that can realistically be carried out BY COMMUNITIES WITH LIMITED RESOURCES over a short period, and requires proposals to demonstrate LOCAL LEADERSHIP and community contribution. That is an explicit invitation to exactly the village associations this file has failed four times to reach in this country. Another aims at practical local and regional solutions improving environmental quality and human wellbeing while building more resilient communities. READ IT AS AN INDEX OF FUNDERS AS WELL AS OF CALLS: it names the funding body behind each opportunity, which tells a Jordanian group which institutions fund work in this country at all — a question this file has otherwise answered only with foreign hotspot funds and small-grants windows. HOW TO USE IT PROPERLY: check it before designing a project rather than after, because the sector, the eligibility and the closing date shape what is worth writing; and note that closed calls stay listed, which is useful — A CLOSED CALL TELLS YOU WHO FUNDED WHAT LAST YEAR AND IS LIKELY TO FUND IT AGAIN. THE LIMITS: it is a listing platform, not a funder, an adviser or an advocate — nobody there will help write the application or take up a land dispute. Its listings span education, peace, women's programmes and innovation as well as environment, so filter by sector. And a listing is only as current as its last update; confirm any deadline with the funder before relying on it.

trackers.name: Naua — a Jordanian donation platform where a registered association can raise money from the public
trackers.desc: THIS IS THE FIRST ROUTE IN THIS ENTIRE MAP BY WHICH ORDINARY PEOPLE CAN GIVE MONEY DIRECTLY TO A LOCAL ASSOCIATION'S PROJECT. It hosts the charitable and development projects of associations, non-profit companies and charitable foundations, and lets donors contribute to them. Every other funding entry recorded for this region is an institutional grant window with a call, a deadline and a competitive process; this is a platform where a Jordanian association publishes its own project and asks the public to fund it. FOR A COMMUNITY TRYING TO RAISE MONEY — to buy land, to fund a survey, to pay for a study — THAT IS A DIFFERENT KIND OF INSTRUMENT: it has no theme, no funder's priorities to satisfy and no closing date, only whether people will give. HOW TO JOIN, AND THE CONDITION THAT DECIDES IT: you apply through an online subscription request and a representative of the platform then contacts you for further information. YOU MUST BE REGISTERED WITH THE MINISTRY OF SOCIAL DEVELOPMENT OR THE RELEVANT MINISTRY AND HOLD THE LICENCES AND APPROVALS NEEDED FOR YOUR ACTIVITIES, and you must meet the platform's transparency standards. An unregistered village committee cannot use it directly and must work through a registered association — which is the same constraint this file has recorded on the international land acquisition fund and on most grant windows, and is the strongest practical argument for a community registering a body early rather than late. WHAT TO PREPARE: a defined project rather than a general appeal. The platform hosts projects, so the ask has to be a specific, costed thing donors can picture — a parcel, a survey, a legal fee, a nursery — not a campaign. THE LIMITS: it is a fundraising channel, not a funder, an adviser or an advocate; nobody there will help design the project or take up a land dispute. Its stated framing is charitable and developmental, so an openly adversarial campaign against a named scheme may not fit its terms, and this file has recorded across the region that framing land defence as conservation, livelihood or development is usually what makes it fundable.

trackers.name: Global Forest Watch — free satellite monitoring of your own patch, with alerts by email
trackers.desc: YOU CAN DRAW YOUR OWN AREA ON A MAP AND HAVE THE SATELLITES WATCH IT FOR YOU. The platform lets anyone define a custom area of interest — by drawing it, uploading a boundary file, or selecting a region — and SUBSCRIBE TO AUTOMATED EMAIL ALERTS when tree cover loss or fire is detected there. It is free: all data, tools and reports, with no subscription or licence fee. This file recorded that this country has lost roughly a third of its natural forest in thirty years, that woodland covers under one per cent of its territory, and that forest rangers have been threatened and assaulted by illegal cutters. A resident with a phone can now watch a specific hillside without asking anyone's permission. WHAT IS ACTUALLY AVAILABLE HERE, STATED HONESTLY: the ANNUAL TREE COVER LOSS RECORD FROM 2001 ONWARDS is global, and so are the DAILY FIRE ALERTS. The weekly near-real-time deforestation alerts are described as covering the tropics, and this country lies outside them. That still leaves two decades of comparable loss data for any patch of ground and a daily fire feed — which in a country where cutting and burning are the documented threats is the relevant pair. ITS FIELD APP TURNS AN ALERT INTO EVIDENCE: designate areas to monitor, store the satellite change data ON THE DEVICE, overlay protected area and concession boundaries, NAVIGATE TO THE EXACT POINT WITHOUT A PHONE SIGNAL, and record photographs and structured forms on site, uploading when back in range. That sequence — alert, visit, photograph, form — is how a claim becomes something an authority or a court can act on, and this file recorded a Turkish group that beat a developer's figures by counting trees itself. USE ALERTS AS A STARTING POINT, NOT A CONCLUSION: the platform states plainly that an alert shows where loss MAY be occurring and requires follow-up — checking recent imagery, testing overlaps with concession and protected area boundaries, and visiting the site — before action is taken. An overstated claim hands the other side its rebuttal. THE LIMITS: the main platform needs an internet connection, some datasets update only annually, and the range of layers takes time to learn. IT IS ALSO APPARENTLY BEING REBRANDED UNDER A NEW NAME COVERING NATURE RATHER THAN FORESTS — check the current address before relying on a bookmark.

trackers.name: General Union of Jordanian Farmers — the body whose stated job is representing farmers and defending their interests
trackers.desc: THIS FILE SEARCHED THIS COUNTRY SIX TIMES FOR AN ORGANISATION THAT OPPOSES PROJECTS AND FOUND NONE. IT NEVER LOOKED FOR THE BODY THAT REPRESENTS THE PEOPLE WHO LOSE THE LAND. A general union of Jordanian farmers exists, with a board of directors and a director general, and its stated role is REPRESENTING FARMERS AND DEFENDING THEIR INTERESTS while building their capacities and improving the agricultural production environment. ITS ACCESS IS UNUSUALLY HIGH FOR A MEMBERSHIP BODY: its board was received by the DIRECTOR OF THE ROYAL COURT, who described it as an important link between official bodies and farmers, said it plays a pivotal role in conveying the voice of the agricultural sector, and undertook that the matters raised would be followed up with the competent authorities. In this country that is the channel that moves things, and a union that reaches it is worth more to a farmer than a campaign group would be. WHAT IT ALREADY CARRIES UP THAT CHANNEL SHOWS WHAT IT WILL TAKE ON: production costs and solar power for wells, communications in the badia, MAINTENANCE OF AGRICULTURAL ROADS, and the infrastructure supporting agricultural production. Those are land and infrastructure questions, which means a road, a pipeline or a scheme cutting through farmland is within the range of things it already raises. IT IS ALSO ACTIVE AND VISIBLE: its director general issues public guidance to farmers and livestock keepers across the kingdom, which is how to confirm it is functioning before approaching it. ONE THING TO ESTABLISH BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE IF YOUR LAND IS IN THE JORDAN VALLEY: a law dating from 1977 is recorded as having established that ALL DEVELOPED AGRICULTURAL LAND THERE COULD ONLY BE SOLD TO THE STATE VALLEY AUTHORITY. If that still holds, no conservation body can buy your land and no trust can hold it — the only lawful purchaser is the authority, and the routes available are the lease, agreement and designation ones recorded elsewhere in this file rather than purchase. Verify the current position with a lawyer before spending effort on a buyer. THE LIMITS, STATED PLAINLY. It is a sectoral representative body working with government rather than against it, and nothing found shows it objecting to a development scheme. NO WEBSITE FOR IT COULD BE FOUND — this entry points at the published report of its meeting with the royal court; reach it through the agriculture ministry, a governorate agricultural directorate, or a local agricultural cooperative.

trackers.name: Jordan Bar Association Legal Aid Unit — a lawyer paid for by statute if you cannot afford one
trackers.desc: THE BAR ITSELF RUNS A LEGAL AID UNIT, AND IT DOES SO UNDER ITS OWN STATUTE. It provides LEGAL ASSISTANCE AND JUDICIAL AID to anyone whose POVERTY AND INABILITY TO PAY A LAWYER'S FEES IS ESTABLISHED, pursuant to an article of the Bar Association Law. That is a different and stronger thing than a charitable scheme: it is an obligation the profession's own governing law places on it, which means it does not depend on a project, a donor or aministry's goodwill. THE ROUTE IN IS SIMPLE AND WORTH KNOWING EXACTLY: A PETITION FROM THE PERSON SEEKING AID, SETTING OUT THE CIRCUMSTANCES. Not a form, not an intermediary — a written account of the situation and why the fees cannot be paid. Prepare it as you would any application that must persuade: what the dispute is, what is at stake, what the other side is doing, and what your household income is. THIS FILE PREVIOUSLY RECORDED THAT JORDAN'S PROFESSIONAL BODIES HAD NO PUBLIC FUNCTION, AND THAT WAS WRONG. Across six professional legal bodies examined in this region, only two serve the public at all — a Gulf bar with an aid office in every court, and this one. USE IT ALONGSIDE THE COUNTRY'S LEGAL AID ORGANISATION RECORDED SEPARATELY IN THIS FILE: two independent routes to a free lawyer are better than one, they apply different tests, and a refusal by one is not a refusal by the other. The bar also publishes its council decisions, circulars, statements, research, journal, library and standard forms, which is where to find how the profession has ruled on questions like conflicts of interest — useful if you suspect the lawyers in your district are acting for the developer. THE LIMITS: aid is means-tested and poverty must be ESTABLISHED, so a household with land but no cash should expect to have to prove the position. It is general legal aid rather than environmental or planning specialism, so frame a land dispute as a property, compensation or administrative matter — this file has recorded that reframing working in Georgia, Kuwait and the Emirates. And the association is otherwise member-facing, running a pension fund, health insurance and training for its own lawyers.

trackers.name: ILC EMENA — there is a national land coalition in this country, and this is how to reach it
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY HAS A NATIONAL LAND COALITION, AND THIS FILE SEARCHED FOR SIX ROUNDS WITHOUT FINDING IT. It is one of only two national land coalitions across the whole Europe, Middle East and North Africa region — the other is in Palestine — and it sits within a global alliance of nearly three hundred organisations in eighty-one countries working on land rights. A national coalition is a standing multi-organisation platform on land governance: exactly the federation this map found in Georgia and Lebanon and repeatedly failed to find here. THE MEMBERS PAGE IS TAGGED BY WHAT ORGANISATIONS ACTUALLY DO, and the categories are this map's subject: LEGAL ASSISTANCE, LEGAL EMPOWERMENT AND ACCESS TO JUSTICE; LAND MONITORING, INDICATORS AND ALTERNATIVE REPORTING; MAPPING AND LAND REGISTRATION; LAND CONFLICT RESOLUTION; and EFFECTIVE ACTIONS AGAINST LAND GRABBING. You can therefore find a member by the thing you need rather than by guessing an organisation's name — which is how this file has failed in this country again and again. AND IT ANSWERS RATHER THAN RETURNING NOTHING: the site states membership status country by country, saying plainly where a country has no active members. That is more useful than an empty search, because it tells you to stop looking. EVERY MEMBER HAS SIGNED A PLEDGE THAT MATTERS IF YOUR PEOPLE COME UNDER PRESSURE: to uphold gender justice by supporting women's participation and leadership, AND TO DEFEND LAND AND ENVIRONMENTAL DEFENDERS WHO ARE CRIMINALISED, INTIMIDATED AND MARGINALISED FOR ADVOCATING CHANGE. This payload has documented defenders prosecuted, sued and smeared across five countries; a signed, published commitment to defend them is something you can hold a member organisation to. THE COALITION'S BROADER COMMITMENTS INCLUDE TRANSPARENCY: unhindered and timely PUBLIC ACCESS TO ALL INFORMATION that may contribute to informed public debate and decision-making on land issues AT ALL STAGES, and decentralisation to the lowest effective level. That is a principle to quote when a plan, contract or valuation is withheld. PRACTICAL DETAIL: the regional platform was established in 2017 and publishes a postal address, telephone number and email at the coalition's secretariat abroad; a named regional coordinator represents it publicly. THE LIMITS: it is a coalition and a platform, not an objector, a funder or a law practice — it will not take up your case. Its membership is organisations rather than individuals, so a village committee reaches it through a member. And the regional office sits outside the region, so the national coalition here is the closer door.

trackers.name: Dana and Qadisiyah Local Community Cooperative — the village that built its own body to keep its land
trackers.desc: THE PEOPLE OF TWO VILLAGES SET THIS UP IN 1994 AFTER THE GOVERNMENT AUTHORISED THAT THEIR CUSTOMARY LAND BE TURNED INTO A NATURE RESERVE. It is a community body created because its land was taken — and taken for conservation, which is a warning this map should carry: a designation can dispossess as surely as a mine. It has a general assembly of MORE THAN A HUNDRED FAMILIES and a SEVEN-MEMBER ELECTED VOLUNTEER BOARD, and it works to claim back the community's customary land by building the local population's political role and by explaining that loss of land rights to an international audience. ITS METHOD FOR KEEPING THE LAND THAT REMAINS IS THE MOST DIRECTLY COPYABLE THING IN THIS ENTIRE MAP: it protects local ownership of the village's INDIVIDUALLY OWNED land by ENCOURAGING LANDOWNERS TO JOIN THE COOPERATIVE AND TO SELL TO THE COOPERATIVE ONLY. That is a community right of first refusal built by private agreement between neighbours. It needs no new law, no outside purchaser and no trust deed — only enough households to agree that when land is sold it is sold inward. Anywhere in this region where land is quietly bought up parcel by parcel, that is the cheapest defence there is. IT PAYS FOR ITSELF IN PART: it set up and operates COMMUNITY-OWNED TOURISM VENTURES — a lodge and a hotel — alongside donations from community members and outside bodies. A community body with its own revenue is not at the mercy of a grant cycle, which this file has recorded as the weakness of almost every other organisation here. IT ALSO PRESERVES AND TEACHES HIMA, the traditional land management the tribe used for centuries, restores the historic village, and runs distinct YOUTH AND WOMEN'S PROGRAMMES.
