AND IT BUILT SOMETHING BIGGER: working with the global land coalition and national stakeholders, it developed a NATIONAL ENGAGEMENT STRATEGY FOR PEOPLE-CENTRED LAND GOVERNANCE IN THIS COUNTRY — the national land coalition recorded separately in this file. A village cooperative that helped create its country's national land platform is a demonstration of what the affected community itself can build. THE COALITION TAGS ITS WORK AS LAND GRABBING, EFFECTIVE ACTIONS AGAINST LAND GRABBING, LEGAL EMPOWERMENT AND ACCESS TO JUSTICE, STRENGTHENING LOCAL INSTITUTIONS, and USE OF MEDIA AND COMMUNICATION. THE LIVE ISSUE TO ASK ABOUT: the government has sought to explore the feasibility of COPPER MINING in the western part of the reserve, the reserve's managers have refused to cooperate, and the community — left out when the reserve was created and largely absent from its management since — is insisting on being included in the consultations this time. THE LIMITS: it is a village cooperative, not a law practice or a funder; it is small, volunteer-led and donation-dependent; and much of the published account of it dates from several years back, so confirm what it is doing now. It also publishes its own analysis under its own name online, which is the place to hear it in its own voice.

trackers.name: Jordanian Association of Real Estate Appraisers — get your own valuation before you answer theirs
trackers.desc: NOTHING ELSE IN THIS MAP CAN PUT A NUMBER ON YOUR LAND. This is a civil association of real estate appraisers, established under the associations law with its own national registration number, founded on the initiative of a group of appraisers to be a home for the profession, its knowledge and its practitioners. WHY THAT MATTERS MORE THAN IT SOUNDS: IN AN EXPROPRIATION THE DECISIVE FIGHT IS THE VALUATION. A community that accepts the acquiring authority's figure has conceded the one argument it could most easily have won — and an independent, accredited valuation is the only way to contest it on the authority's own ground. KNOW WHAT A PROPER VALUATION MUST CONSIDER, BECAUSE IT IS MORE THAN THE PRICE OF BARE LAND. A valuer in a compulsory acquisition typically applies THREE APPROACHES and then decides which best gives fair market value: COMPARABLE SALES; the COST APPROACH, being the replacement cost of the STRUCTURES AND IMPROVEMENTS on the land; and the INCOME CAPITALISATION APPROACH, being THE PROPERTY'S EARNING CAPACITY. THE THIRD IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FORGET AND AUTHORITIES OMIT. An orchard, a grazing area, a fishing landing, a spring or a stand of old olives EARNS, year after year — and a valuation built only on comparable sales of empty ground prices none of it. This file recorded a farmers' federation elsewhere in the region telling its parliament that being compensated with substitute land unfit for agriculture would make the law a displacement law rather than one guaranteeing rights; the same point, put in valuation terms, is that productive capacity must be priced. WHAT TO ASK THIS ASSOCIATION FOR: an accredited appraiser who works on COMPULSORY ACQUISITION AND COMPENSATION rather than on mortgage or sale valuations, and confirmation that they will apply all three approaches and set out each in writing. A written valuation naming its method is a document a court, a committee or a compensation panel must engage with. EQUIVALENT BODIES EXIST ACROSS THE REGION AND ARE WORTH ASKING FOR THE SAME THING: a statutory union of valuation experts in one neighbouring country, and an authority of accredited valuers in another. THE LIMITS, PLAINLY: this is a professional association, not an advocate — it exists to advance the profession and will not take your side. VALUERS CHARGE FEES, so budget for one or ask a legal aid body or a supporting organisation to commission it. And a member may be unwilling to value against a public authority in a small market, so ask that question first rather than after instructing.

trackers.name: National Centre for Human Rights — nationwide jurisdiction, and a toll-free number to start with
trackers.desc: IT PUBLISHES A HOTLINE AND A TOLL-FREE NATIONAL NUMBER. That is the cheapest way into any institution recorded anywhere in this map — a household in a village pays nothing to make the first call, and this file has found repeatedly that the first barrier is cost and distance rather than law. A fax, an email address and a street address in the capital are published alongside them. WHAT IT IS: a national institution of PUBLIC BENEFIT with FINANCIAL AND ADMINISTRATIVE INDEPENDENCE AND ITS OWN LEGAL PERSONALITY, which exercises its functions — including MONITORING AND RECEIVING COMPLAINTS — under a law of 2006 and WITH COMPLETE INDEPENDENCE, across NATIONWIDE JURISDICTION. It began under a provisional law and a royal decree in 2002 and was made permanent four years later. ON WHETHER THAT INDEPENDENCE IS REAL, THERE IS AN EXTERNAL VERDICT RATHER THAN THIS FILE'S OPINION: IT HOLDS THE TOP ACCREDITATION GRADE from the international peer review of national human rights institutions, awarded in 2006 and reaffirmed on later review. It is the third institution in this payload confirmed at that grade, and the grade is what certifies compliance with the international standards for independence. HOW IT FITS WITH WHAT THIS COUNTRY ALREADY HAS. This map records here the largest legal aid provider in the country, with clinics across every governorate, a national land coalition, a village cooperative that keeps its own land, and an association of appraisers seated on the statutory committee that values property. THIS BODY IS THE ONE CONSTITUTED TO EXAMINE THE CONDUCT OF OFFICIAL BODIES — so a refusal to hold a hearing, a file withheld, or a decision taken without the consultation the rules require is its subject, while a case in court belongs to the legal aid clinics. THE LIMITS: its documented functions are monitoring and receiving complaints; NO POWER TO BRING PROCEEDINGS IN COURT WAS ESTABLISHED, unlike the two Caucasus institutions recorded in this file which may file opinions in court. It was created by the state, however independent its law declares it. And a complaint is a disclosure to a public institution. Call the free number first and ask what it can do with your matter before writing anything down.

trackers.name: Engineers Association — free design and supervision for a society that owns its land
trackers.desc: A SOCIETY THAT OWNS ITS LAND CAN OBTAIN DESIGN AND SUPERVISION WITHOUT PAYING ENGINEERING FEES, AND THE CONDITIONS ARE PUBLISHED. The plot must be REGISTERED IN THE SOCIETY'S NAME; design and supervision contracts are submitted AT NO FEE; the engineering office AND the society each give A WRITTEN DECLARATION THAT NO FEES WERE TAKEN; the office UNDERTAKES TO SUPERVISE the project; and the society or its supervising committee undertakes to APPOINT A RESIDENT ENGINEER IF THE AREA EXCEEDS FOUR HUNDRED SQUARE METRES. Projects meeting those conditions may be exempted from registration as engineering shares for design, supervision and site inspection. THIS FILE HAS SPENT MORE ROUNDS THAN ANY OTHER SUBJECT ON HOW A COMMUNITY PAYS FOR PROFESSIONAL WORK. HERE IS A WRITTEN ROUTE WHERE IT DOES NOT PAY — AND THE CONDITION IS THAT THE COMMUNITY BODY HOLDS THE LAND IN ITS OWN NAME. That is the same constituted-body requirement this payload names as the barrier to everything else, turned into a reward: a village association or cooperative that has managed to register land in its own name unlocks professional design and supervision for nothing. THE SECOND PROVISION IS FOR FARMERS. NON-CONCRETE AGRICULTURAL SHEDS AND STRUCTURES ARE LICENSED WITH A DESIGN CONTRACT, AND A SUPERVISION CONTRACT ONLY IF REQUIRED, WITH NO OBLIGATION TO APPOINT A RESIDENT ENGINEER — AND ONLY HALF THE FEES AND ENGINEERING SHARES ARE REGISTERED. A community establishing visible agricultural use on ground it wants to keep, which this file has repeatedly recommended, can do it at half the professional cost and without a resident engineer. AND ONE SMALL CLAUSE WORTH KNOWING BEFORE YOU DESIGN ANYTHING: fees are calculated on the TOTAL ROOFED AREA — including architectural projections, stair repeats, canopies, subsidiary roofed buildings and roofed garages — BUT THE SHELTER AND A WATER WELL OUTSIDE THE BUILDING ARE EXCLUDED. A well sited outside the building envelope costs nothing in engineering fees. THE ASSOCIATION ALSO PUBLISHES AN ENGINEERS' DIRECTORY AND RUNS AN ENGINEERING OFFICES SERVICES PORTAL, with a general assembly for engineering offices and companies — so the licensed professional and the licensed office can both be identified before either is engaged. THE LIMITS. The free route is for A SOCIETY'S OWN BUILDING PROJECT, not for objections, surveys in a dispute or litigation — it presupposes you already own land and want to build on it. It requires an engineering office willing to work unpaid, which is a favour the rules permit rather than compel. And the association regulates the profession; it will not take a side in a planning dispute. Read it with the real estate appraisers' association and the valuation committee recorded separately for this country: the engineer designs and supervises, the appraiser values, and the committee decides in writing within thirty days.

trackers.name: Petra National Trust — the country's oldest heritage organisation, and an annual award that funds heritage projects
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING IN THIS MAP HELD NO HERITAGE ORGANISATION AT ALL, IN A COUNTRY WHERE HERITAGE IS THE STRONGEST GROUND THERE IS FOR STOPPING WORK. THIS IS THE OLDEST ONE: a non-governmental, non-profit body established in 1989, whose listed services are ADVOCACY AND AWARENESS RAISING and CAPACITY BUILDING AND TRAINING, and whose remit covers NATURAL AS WELL AS CULTURAL heritage. THE PART TO ACT ON IS THE MONEY. IT RUNS AN ANNUAL HERITAGE AWARD SUPPORTING INNOVATIVE PROJECTS THAT CONTRIBUTE TO SAFEGUARDING TANGIBLE AND INTANGIBLE HERITAGE — announced for 2026 at a press conference with the European Union's ambassador, and run in partnership with the EU delegation, two banks and a private donor. Earlier editions ran in 2024 and 2025, and the 2025 round had a published application deadline that was extended into late July, so this is a REGULAR CYCLE WITH APPLICATIONS RATHER THAN A CLOSED HONOUR. INTANGIBLE HERITAGE IS EXPRESSLY INCLUDED, WHICH MATTERS: a community whose claim rests on practices, crafts, seasonal use of land or oral knowledge rather than on standing stones is inside the scope. WHAT ELSE IT GIVES, AND ASK FOR IT DIRECTLY: capacity building and training. This file has repeatedly found that the binding constraint on communities is not argument but skill — how to document a site, how to write a proposal, how to talk to an authority. An organisation that lists training as a service is one to approach for it before you need anything larger. IT ALSO WORKS AT THE LEVEL WHERE RULES ARE MADE: it has launched POLICY RECOMMENDATIONS ON CLIMATE CHANGE AND CULTURAL HERITAGE, and it engages in national and international advocacy. Its education programme deliberately links heritage management to sustainable tourism and LONG-TERM ECONOMIC GAINS — which is the argument to borrow when a scheme is defended on jobs. THE LIMITS: its centre of gravity is one archaeological region and its national work grows out of that; it is not a litigator, it does not buy land, and it works closely with state bodies and royal patronage, so it is unlikely to take a public side against a government project. The award is competitive and project-based. Use it with the professional associations and legal routes recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: International legal representation — a body that takes your case to UN mechanisms, and has filed on this country
trackers.desc: THIS FILE HAS RECORDED PROTECTION ORGANISATIONS THAT CAMPAIGN, TRAIN AND FUND. THIS ONE DOES SOMETHING DIFFERENT AND MORE SPECIFIC: IT REPRESENTS INDIVIDUALS SUBJECTED TO SEVERE HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS BEFORE INTERNATIONAL PROTECTION MECHANISMS — most notably UNITED NATIONS SPECIAL PROCEDURES AND TREATY BODIES — and may also engage regional and domestic mechanisms WHERE THOSE ARE EFFECTIVE AND ACCESSIBLE. IT IS A LEGAL ADVOCACY ORGANISATION, GENEVA-BASED, registered as a Swiss association in September 2018 and founded by women human rights practitioners. IT HAS ALREADY FILED ON THIS COUNTRY: it submitted a report to the UNITED NATIONS HUMAN RIGHTS COMMITTEE concerning it. A body that has already made country submissions knows the framework, the interlocutors and the recurring issues — which is a very different starting point from explaining your situation to a stranger. IT WORKS DIRECTLY WITH VICTIMS, THEIR FAMILIES AND THEIR LAWYERS, alongside defenders and civil society: documenting individual cases, PROVIDING LEGAL ASSISTANCE, and identifying the patterns and structural causes behind what happened. FOR A LOCAL LAWYER WHO HAS TAKEN A CASE AND EXHAUSTED WHAT DOMESTIC COURTS WILL DO, THIS IS THE PARTNER THAT CARRIES IT FURTHER — and the approach can come from the lawyer rather than the client. ONE PATTERN IT HAS DOCUMENTED MATTERS TO ANYONE WHO CONSIDERS LEAVING: POLITICALLY MOTIVATED EXTRADITION PROCEEDINGS ARISING FROM ARREST WARRANTS CIRCULATED THROUGH A REGIONAL INTERIOR-MINISTRY CHANNEL. CROSSING A BORDER IN THIS REGION IS NOT NECESSARILY AN EXIT, and anyone advised to leave should understand that before they do. THE LIMITS: it is a human rights organisation working on severe violations — detention, prosecution, torture, disappearance, suppression of expression and assembly. A LAND OR PLANNING DISPUTE REACHES IT ONLY THROUGH WHAT IS DONE TO PEOPLE OVER IT. It is foreign-based and its work is public and international. And international mechanisms are slow: they produce findings, communications and pressure, not injunctions. Use it with the professional associations and legal routes recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Lands and survey department — parcel records, a plan or index, and the water schedule for one dinar
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY HAS ONE OF THE RICHEST LISTINGS IN THE MAP — A CONSERVATION SOCIETY MANAGING PROTECTED AREAS, A HERITAGE TRUST, ENGINEERS AND LAWYERS, HIMA FUNDING — AND NOTHING THAT ANSWERED THE FIRST QUESTION: WHAT IS REGISTERED FOR THIS PARCEL, AND HOW DO I GET A COPY. THE LANDS AND SURVEY DEPARTMENT ISSUES EXACTLY THAT, AND ITS FEES ARE PUBLISHED. THE SERVICES TO ASK FOR BY NAME ARE: AN INVESTIGATION OF IMMOVABLE PROPERTY WITH A CERTIFICATE ISSUED; A PLAN OR INDEX; AND A COPY OF THE REGISTRATION DEED RECORD. Those three between them tell you who is registered, where the boundaries run, and what the register actually says — which is the evidential base for every other step this file recommends. AND THE COST IS THE POINT. FIVE HUNDRED FILS FOR EACH RECORD RELATING TO ANY LAND, WHETHER SETTLED OR NOT. FIVE HUNDRED FILS PER CONTRACT ORGANISED IN THE DEPARTMENT OR DURING SETTLEMENT. FIVE HUNDRED FILS PER COPY OF ANY DOCUMENT ATTACHED TO A REGISTRATION TRANSACTION. A COMMUNITY CAN ASSEMBLE A COMPLETE DOCUMENTARY PICTURE OF A DISPUTED AREA FOR A FEW DINARS, which removes the commonest excuse for not gathering evidence. ONE LINE IN THAT FEE TABLE IS WORTH MORE THAN THE REST COMBINED FOR ANYONE FIGHTING OVER WATER: ONE DINAR FOR EACH COPY OF THE WATER DISTRIBUTION SCHEDULE. IN AN IRRIGATION OR SPRING DISPUTE, THE SCHEDULE SHOWING HOW WATER IS APPORTIONED IS THE DECISIVE DOCUMENT, AND IT COSTS A DINAR. This payload has recorded water committees, falaj systems and irrigation cooperatives across the region without once naming a place where the apportionment record itself can be bought. THERE IS ALSO A MOBILE APPLICATION THAT SEARCHES FOR A PARCEL, NAVIGATES TO IT, SHOWS ITS COORDINATES, AND TELLS YOU WHICH PARCEL YOU ARE CURRENTLY STANDING ON. FOR A BOUNDARY ARGUMENT OR AN ENCROACHMENT, STANDING ON THE GROUND AND READING THE PARCEL NUMBER OFF A PHONE CHANGES THE CONVERSATION — and it is the cheapest verification tool recorded in this map. THE DEPARTMENT ALSO PUBLISHES ITS LAWS, REGULATIONS, INSTRUCTIONS AND BASES, ITS ANNUAL REPORT, ITS STRATEGIC AND ANNUAL PLANS, ITS PROCUREMENT PLAN AND ITS BUDGET. THE PROCUREMENT PLAN AND BUDGET ARE WORTH READING SEPARATELY: they show what surveying and registration work is being commissioned and where, which is advance notice of where the state is about to re-survey or re-register land. THE LIMITS: this is a records office, not an advocate — it will tell you what is registered, not whether that registration is right, and correcting or challenging an entry is a separate and harder process needing a lawyer. Applications go through a reception officer with required documents attached, so go prepared. Fees and service lists change; the figures here were current when recorded and should be checked. Use it with the bar directory and the legal routes recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Lebanon — Commercial Register (Ministry of Justice)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the Ministry of Justice Commercial Register offers a free public search by name or record number, returning address, activities, officers, registration date & legal form, Lebanon. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Court of Audit
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Lebanon, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: The Gherbal Initiative (مبادرة غربال)
trackers.desc: Lebanese transparency initiative (since 2018) monitoring enforcement of the 2017 Right to Access Information Law. Files freedom-of-information requests to public administrations, runs a citizen/journalist request hotline, and publishes the state budget and administrations' financial data in interactive, user-friendly formats.

trackers.name: The Legal Agenda
trackers.desc: Beirut-based nonprofit research, media and advocacy organisation (founded 2009) whose Civil Observatory for an Independent and Transparent Judiciary monitors court cases, trials and judicial policy, paired with strategic litigation and investigative reporting on the courts.

trackers.name: Lebanon — Court of Audit (Diwan al-Muhasaba)
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution; judicial body exercising external control over public funds and protecting the state’s & citizens’ financial rights, Lebanon.

trackers.name: Lebanon — Ministry of Finance
trackers.desc: National budget authority; the Budget Directorate (DGF) prepares the State budget and publishes fiscal & public-debt data, Lebanon. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Lebanon.

trackers.name: Hima — a village with no municipal council still has a route
trackers.desc: THE MOST ACCESSIBLE DESIGNATION ROUTE IN THIS ENTIRE MAP. Under Protected Areas Framework Law 130/2019, a Hima — one of four categories alongside nature reserves, natural sites and natural parks — is established by decision of the municipal council, or joint councils where it spans several municipalities. AND IN VILLAGES WITH NO MUNICIPAL COUNCIL AT ALL, the Hima is designated by the district commissioner (Qa'im Maqam) on a proposal from the village chief (Mukhtar). Almost every route recorded here assumes a functioning local authority; Lebanon provides an explicit fallback for villages that have none. A Hima designation requires only the consent of the local municipality. The council — or commissioner — then develops a management plan; across municipalities, a committee formed by the commissioner or governor does. THE TEMPLATE TO COPY: Hima Aaiha, Lebanon's 40th, formalised by Municipal Decision No. 4/2025, adopted unanimously in a legally convened session on 9 August 2025, over public state land, cadastral parcel No. 2327, based on environmental and scientific studies. A numbered decision, a unanimous vote, a named parcel, a scientific basis. AND IT IS NOT EXCLUSIONARY: Hima exist for sustainable hunting, fishing, grazing and water use — 25 covering 6 percent of Lebanese territory.

trackers.name: The framework law's decrees were never issued — which is why Hima works
trackers.desc: KNOW THE GAP BEFORE YOU RELY ON THE LAW. Law 130/2019 foresees a minimum of five application decrees and two ministerial decisions — none of which have been adopted to date, and the law details management only for nature reserves. The framework is enacted but its implementing instruments are not. That is precisely why the Hima route matters in practice: it runs on a municipal decision, not on a decree that has never been issued. IF YOUR SITE IS PRIVATE LAND: a nature reserve on private property is established after the written consent of all owners, by contract between the state (the Minister of Environment) and the owners, for not less than 20 years, renewable, defining the scope, the surrounding belt zone and management — reserves on public land are established by a law instead. Note that natural sites are still governed by the law of 8 July 1939 on protection of landscapes, reading ‘Ministry of National Economy’ as Ministry of Environment. TARGETS TO QUOTE: by 2030, at least 20 percent of natural terrestrial and marine ecosystems protected with all ecosystem types represented, and nature reserve coverage raised to at least 5 percent of Lebanon's area. A Hima proposal also wants a local Hima committee of community members, environmental activists and municipal representatives.

trackers.name: Lebanon Reforestation Initiative — registered, and it does quarry restoration
trackers.desc: A DELIVERY PARTNER WITH A REGISTRATION NUMBER YOU CAN QUOTE. LRI is a not-for-profit NGO registered at the Lebanese Ministry of Interior under no. 1186 of 16 June 2014 — useful when a counterparty asks whether a partner is properly constituted. It began in 2010 as a project funded by USAID and managed by the US Forest Service International Programs, and has since supported planting of more than 850,000 native tree seedlings nationwide, improved the native seedling production sector, and contributed to best practice in reforestation, fire prevention, forest management, quarry restoration and climate resilience. QUARRY RESTORATION IS A NAMED CAPABILITY — which matters, since quarrying is among the most common land-damage complaints in Lebanon and few bodies have restoration experience for it. It works across all of Lebanon in five programme areas: landscape management, climate resilience, outreach and capacity development, advocacy, and R&D. BE CLEAR WHAT IT IS: this is a technical and delivery partner, not a grant window — approach it for partnership on restoration work and for its advocacy capacity, not to apply for money. For a community-scale grant in Lebanon, see the GEF Small Grants Programme; for the designation route, see the Hima entry recorded separately in this map.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: SPNL — a Hima needs only your municipality's consent, not the national government
trackers.desc: THIS IS THE SHORTEST ROUTE TO PROTECTED STATUS ANYWHERE IN THIS REGION: SPNL STATES THAT, UNLIKE OTHER PROTECTED AREAS WHICH ARE GOVERNMENT-MANAGED, A HIMA DESIGNATION REQUIRES ONLY THE CONSENT OF THE LOCAL MUNICIPALITY. Your own council can place part of the municipal land under protection by its own decree, in partnership with SPNL, without waiting on a ministry. It has been done repeatedly and the decrees are dated and attributed: Kayfoun on 29 November 2017 under a council led by Ali Dagher, the first Hima in Mount Lebanon; Aitanit on 22 December 2017 under Assaad Najem; Hammana on 14 November 2018 under Bachir Farhat. In 2025 Al-Abadiyah, Kornayel and Btekhnay joined the network. AND IT IS NOT A SYMBOLIC LABEL: 27 Himas are now recorded in the World Database on Protected Areas, and Hima sites appear on the map of Lebanon's protected areas produced jointly by UNDP, the Ministry of Environment, the Ministry of Agriculture and SPNL — so a municipal decree converts into an internationally registered designation you can cite against a developer. A Hima can also be declared for a specific use rather than blanket prohibition: SPNL has declared Himas for sustainable hunting, fishing, grazing and water use, which is what makes councils willing to sign. Director General Assad Serhal; SPNL is the BirdLife International partner in Lebanon and has worked on this since 2004, mostly across Important Bird and Biodiversity Areas. Framework referenced by SPNL: Protected Areas Law 130/2019. TWO HONEST CAVEATS. SPNL itself describes operating under extremely challenging political, security and economic conditions, and has reported continuing its bird monitoring amid escalation in Lebanon — capacity is real but strained. And this entry does not establish what happens to a Hima if a later municipal council wishes to undo the decree; ask SPNL that question directly before treating the designation as permanent.

trackers.name: BirdLife Hima Fund — grants for Important Bird Areas, applied for through SPNL
trackers.desc: LEBANON IS THE ONE COUNTRY WHERE THIS FUND AND A WORKING LOCAL MECHANISM LINE UP EXACTLY. BirdLife records that the Hima Fund launched in 2011 with four approved grants to Partners in Jordan, Lebanon, Qatar and Oman, and separately notes that in Lebanon the Himas are emerging as a support system for the network of protected areas. Read that alongside the SPNL entry already in this file: a Lebanese municipality can declare a Hima on its own consent, and the Hima Fund is money attached to precisely that designation. The fund was established in Qatar in 2008 on a one million dollar donation from Sheikha Jawaher Bint Hamad Bin Suhaim Al-Thani, to conserve Important Bird Areas and threatened species across the Middle East. THE APPLICATION ROUTE IS THROUGH THE PARTNER, NOT DIRECT: grants go to BirdLife Partners, and in Lebanon that is SPNL, which led the Hima revival from 2004 across sites including Ebel es-Saqi, Kfar Zabad, Aanjar, Qoleileh, Mansouri, Hermel and Aandqet. Approach SPNL and ask it to carry the application. THE HONEST CAVEAT: no evidence of grant-making after the early 2010s was found during verification — the endowment, the establishment and the first four grants are documented, an open application window today is not. SPNL is the body that would know, and it also operates under the severe political, security and economic constraints noted in its own entry. ANTI-FANOUT NOTE: press reporting lists twelve countries the fund was geared toward; BirdLife names four that received grants, and this entry exists in those four only.

trackers.name: NAHNOO — has stopped two projects outright, and publishes the case where hard evidence was not enough
trackers.desc: READ THE WIN AND THE LOSS TOGETHER, BECAUSE THE CONTRAST IS THE LESSON. On its own campaigns page NAHNOO records that it joined the Civil Campaign to Protect the Dalieh of Raouche, which emerged in March 2013 to press for Dalieh's preservation as a publicly accessible shared space and its classification as a natural reserve — the campaign first got the fence blocking the entrance removed, and then, through grassroots initiatives, public discussions and debates, managed to stop the construction project. In Tarik El-Jdide it led a campaign with residents against a municipal decision on a local playground and stopped that project too. Against those, it records plainly that Ramlet al-Baida fell to illegal privatisation and the Eden Bay Resort was built directly on the shore even though NAHNOO had provided hard evidence of violations by the developer and of corruption in the Governor's office of the time. The inversion a campaign should take from its own account: the two sites that were saved were saved by sustained public mobilisation, and the site that was lost was lost despite the documentary case being made. Build the evidence, but do not assume it decides anything by itself. WHAT IT HOLDS THAT YOU CAN USE: a published map of violations along the Beirut coast, and studies including its Horsh Beirut work — the campaign that reopened the capital's largest park to the public after decades in which access was effectively rationed. WHAT IT IS: a youth-led organisation describing itself as a research, capacity-building and advocacy platform for participatory public policy-making, working on good governance, public spaces and cultural heritage, and rallying volunteers across Lebanon. THE COALITION IS THE PART TO ASK ABOUT FOR ANY COASTAL SITE: NAHNOO is part of The Coast for All, which campaigns to preserve and restore Lebanon's public coast and has petitioned to amend Law 64/2017 so that the right to occupy marine public property is restricted to the Lebanese state and encroachments are limited. Its coastal work names Adloun, one of the few remaining sea turtle nesting grounds on the Lebanese coast and the site of an ancient Phoenician port town. Route by the kind of fight: NAHNOO for mobilisation and public-space claims, The Legal Agenda for litigation, SPNL where the answer is a Hima declared by your own municipality — all three are in this file.

trackers.name: Public Works Studio — the people who pull the cadastral records and put lawyers next to planners
trackers.desc: THIS IS THE BODY THAT WILL ESTABLISH WHO ACTUALLY OWNS THE LAND UNDER A LEBANESE PROJECT, WHICH IS USUALLY THE QUESTION EVERY CAMPAIGN STALLS ON. Public Works Studio describes itself as a multidisciplinary research and advocacy organisation of engineers, designers, researchers and lawyers engaged critically and creatively in questions of urbanism and spatial justice in Lebanon, with particular focus on environmental and housing rights, the right to integrated development and to accessible public space. That combination — planners and lawyers working from land records rather than from press coverage — is rare anywhere and close to unique in this region. WHAT ITS WORK LOOKS LIKE IN PRACTICE: its study of religious waqf land in Lebanon works from cadastral registry data against historical figures, reporting that Dar al-Fatwa and Sunni community waqf held 1,974 properties in 1989 — 52.7 per cent in the North governorate, 15.9 in the Beqaa, 13.1 in Mount Lebanon, 12.2 in the South and 6.1 in Beirut — and setting the 379 properties then recorded for Beirut and Mount Lebanon against 184 in the 2024 data. Note how it handles the discrepancy, because that is the standard to hold any researcher to: it states plainly that the gap may mean the holdings shrank, or that the database it obtained was incomplete, or both. THE FINDING THAT SHOULD CHANGE HOW A LEBANESE CAMPAIGN PLANS: its research documents a waqf evicting occupants from several surrounding houses it owns, left empty, in an area undergoing rapid real-estate development, and further live suits between long-standing tenants and a waqf following rent rises and revaluation of the leased property. In Lebanon the endowment can be the developer. Do not assume that land held by a religious endowment is land protected from development, and check the register before building an argument on it. Pair with The Legal Agenda for litigation, NAHNOO for public-space mobilisation and SPNL where a municipal Hima is the answer — all three already in this file.

trackers.name: AFDC — three nurseries, standing agreements with municipalities, and it publishes its land data in GIS formats you can download
trackers.desc: THE UNUSUAL THING THIS ORGANISATION OFFERS IS DATA YOU CAN ACTUALLY TAKE AWAY: its own site serves downloadable geospatial datasets — CSV, KML, GeoJSON, GeoTIFF, shapefiles — with API links for GeoServices, WMS and WFS. Very few organisations anywhere in this file publish their mapping in formats a community or its consultant can open, overlay on a proposed scheme and hand to a planner. Start there before commissioning anything. AND IT WORKS THROUGH MUNICIPALITIES, WHICH IN LEBANON IS THE DECISIVE RELATIONSHIP: it runs afforestation and reforestation with municipalities and Municipal Unions, and operates three of its own nurseries, with seedling supply arranged through the Ministry of Agriculture. Read that alongside the Hima route recorded elsewhere in this file — a Lebanese council can protect land by its own decree, and a council that is already planting with a partner organisation is a council that has a working relationship to build on. Established in the early 1990s, IUCN member, active in more than fifteen locations across Mount Lebanon, North Lebanon and South Lebanon, based at Jdeideh. Its four programmes cover conservation, sustainable development, outreach and advocacy, and research; forest fire and desertification work is central to it. ITS SITE-SELECTION CRITERIA, DEVELOPED WITH THE NATIONAL REFORESTATION PARTNERSHIP IT BELONGS TO, ARE WORTH READING AS A CHECKLIST FOR YOUR OWN SITE: priority goes to land at higher risk of erosion or landslide and to sites with previous fire history and no natural regeneration, and requirements include an engaged municipality and an active community — and, in Lebanon, land clear of landmines. That partnership also works on landscape-scale biocorridors in the north, Rachaya and the Chouf to link existing forest stands and protect watersheds, and publishes forest mapping showing the gaps in those corridors. If your threatened land sits in a mapped corridor gap, that is a documented national conservation priority rather than a local claim. THE LIMIT, PLAINLY: this is not an oppositional body. It works in partnership with the ministries of agriculture, environment, education and interior, and its frame is restoration and rural livelihoods rather than stopping schemes. It will not object to a project for you — for that Lebanon carries The Legal Agenda for litigation, NAHNOO for public-space mobilisation and SPNL where a Hima is the answer. Founding year is given as both 1993 and 1994 across sources; take it from AFDC if it matters.

trackers.name: Al-Shouf Cedar Society — a non-governmental body managing 5% of Lebanon, with 22 villages inside the boundary
trackers.desc: IF YOUR VILLAGE SITS INSIDE A BIOSPHERE RESERVE, THERE IS ALREADY AN INSTITUTION WITH A MANAGEMENT MANDATE OVER THE LAND AROUND YOU — AND IN THE SHOUF, TWENTY-TWO VILLAGES ARE INSIDE THE BOUNDARY. UNESCO declared the Shouf Biosphere Reserve in July 2005 covering roughly 50,000 hectares, about five per cent of the total area of Lebanon, taking in the Al-Shouf Cedar Nature Reserve established in 1996, the Ammiq Wetland — a Ramsar site and one of the last remaining wetlands in the Middle East — and those twenty-two villages on the eastern and western sides of the Barouk and Niha mountains. The biosphere model matters here because it is not a fence: it works through core, buffer and transition zones, and the buffer and transition zones are where people live and farm. A scheme proposed in a buffer zone is proposed inside a managed landscape with a named administering body, which is a completely different starting position from open countryside. Establish which zone your land is in first. THE MODEL THAT MAKES VILLAGES DEFEND THE DESIGNATION RATHER THAN RESENT IT IS WORTH COPYING: the society has run a rural development project since February 1999 that has supported some forty families to produce more than seventy products, sold at the reserve entrances which receive upwards of eighty thousand visitors a year. Conservation that pays households is conservation that survives a change of council. It also brings outside money into buffer-zone municipalities through partnerships — an irrigation project funded by the European Union and a Swedish foundation, implemented with Italian and academic partners, ran in the municipality of Mrusti inside the buffer zone and at Ammiq. WHAT IT HOLDS THAT AN OBJECTION NEEDS: it is on the IUCN Green List, and a biodiversity survey begun in 2022 recorded forty-four habitats of which forty-two are natural or semi-natural, and 161 bird species including six internationally threatened. That is a current, independent baseline for a very large area. THE LIMITS, AND THEY ARE THE FAMILIAR ONES: this is a management body for a state-declared protected area, listed by the Ministry of Environment, not an oppositional organisation. Its income depends substantially on visitors, so it has its own interest in access and tourism infrastructure — the same tension this file recorded for SABUKO in Georgia. For a fight, Lebanon's entries in this file route to The Legal Agenda for litigation, NAHNOO for public-space mobilisation and SPNL where a municipal Hima is the answer. Reserve area is given as 550 square kilometres in some sources and around 500, or 50,000 hectares, by the society and the IUCN Green List; use the latter.

trackers.name: CEPF Mediterranean Basin — open calls naming Lebanon, and the traditional-land-use direction fits the Hima model exactly
trackers.desc: ONE OF THE TWO OPEN STRATEGIC DIRECTIONS IS TRADITIONAL LAND USE PRACTICES, WHICH IS A NEAR-EXACT DESCRIPTION OF THE HIMA — the community land designation recorded elsewhere in this file that a Lebanese municipality can declare on its own consent. A Lebanese application built around reviving or extending a Hima is not straining to fit this fund; it is what the direction was written for. The large-grants call for letters of inquiry opened 1 July 2026 and closes 18 September 2026 at midnight Washington time, with grants of fifty thousand to a hundred and eighty thousand US dollars under that direction and one on preservation of threatened plant species. A small-grants call earlier in 2026 offered twenty to fifty thousand dollars from a five hundred and forty thousand dollar pot, restricted to threatened freshwater biodiversity — relevant for springs, rivers and the wetland sites in the country's protected-area network. ELIGIBILITY IS ORGANISATIONAL: applicants must be legally registered with their own bank account and national authorisation to receive charitable funding; individuals cannot apply. Local and national NGOs are explicitly prioritised in the small-grants call. Letters of inquiry go via the ConservationGrants portal in English or French; the regional implementation team is BirdLife International with DOPPS, and webinar times were published for Lebanon. CEPF'S OWN 2024 PROFILE STATES THE CONTEXT PLAINLY RATHER THAN GLOSSING IT: it records that the evolution of the security and geopolitical situation in the Middle East, particularly in Palestine and Lebanon, has affected inhabitants and organisations. The fund is operating in that knowledge, which is worth knowing when judging whether an application is realistic. Watch the open-calls page; windows run roughly five to ten weeks and late applications are refused for any reason.

trackers.name: APJM — Lebanese law would not allow a reserve on private land, so it leased the mountain from the endowments and the municipality instead
trackers.desc: THIS IS THE MOST DIRECTLY USEFUL PRECEDENT IN THIS FILE FOR ANYONE TOLD THEY CANNOT PROTECT LAND THEY DO NOT OWN. Lebanese legislation did not recognise nature reserves on private land. Rather than abandon the site or wait for the law to change, this association negotiated and funded a ten-year lease contract with the religious endowments to rent large parts of the mountain, and separately leased public municipal common land — macha'a — which the Ministry of Agriculture then designated a Protected Forest in 2008. Two different tenures assembled into one reserve, and not a hectare bought. If you are working where conservation ownership is impossible, that is the shape of the answer: find who holds the land, offer a funded lease, and get a public designation attached to the part that is common. READ IT AGAINST THE OTHER LEBANESE ENDOWMENT FINDING IN THIS FILE, WHERE AN ENDOWMENT WAS DOCUMENTED EVICTING TENANTS IN A DEVELOPMENT CORRIDOR. The endowment is neither ally nor adversary. It is a landlord, and whoever arrives with a funded offer decides what the land becomes. WHAT THE ORGANISATION IS AND WHAT IT HOLDS: a Lebanese non-governmental non-profit founded in 2007, managing the 6,500-hectare Jabal Moussa Biosphere Reserve in Keserwan, which entered the UNESCO Man and the Biosphere network in 2009. Its stated mission pairs conservation with empowering local communities to achieve their own socio-economic development, and its published philosophy is that successful management depends on the participation of the surrounding villages — the same bargain this file has now recorded in Turkish, Georgian, Armenian and other Lebanese cases. The reserve holds at least 727 plant species, 26 endemic to Lebanon and six found only on this mountain, is a Global Important Bird Area with more than 137 migratory and soaring bird species recorded, and shelters wolves, hyenas and rock hyraxes. Offices in Jounieh. THE LIMITS: it manages one mountain. It is not a litigator, a funder or a national body, and it will not take on a scheme elsewhere — but it is the organisation to ask how the lease was structured, what it cost and how the endowments were approached, which is knowledge no statute will give you. SOURCING NOTE: the lease arrangements are documented in a country profile on privately protected areas published by a land conservation network rather than on the association's own pages; confirm the terms with APJM before relying on them.

trackers.name: Save Beirut Heritage — a 24-hour demolition hotline, and it moved the power to permit demolition from the municipality to the minister
trackers.desc: THE STRUCTURAL WIN IS THE PART TO COPY: this group was the driving force behind a government decision that old houses cannot be demolished unless the Minister of Culture signs the demolition order. Permission had previously been given by Beirut municipality. Moving a permit power up from a municipality to a minister does not save any particular building, but it changes who must be persuaded and creates a single national point of accountability where there were dozens of local ones. If demolition in your area is signed off locally, that is the change to aim at. AND THE SERVICE IS AS CONCRETE AS ANYTHING IN THIS FILE: a twenty-four-hour hotline residents can call if they fear a building is about to be demolished or damaged by construction, published along with contact emails, backed by a membership in the thousands that began as a public group. It asks people to watch buildings and report, and it publicises the methods developers use to get old buildings taken down — which is the practical knowledge a resident needs to recognise what is happening next door before it is finished. THE OUTCOME IS QUANTIFIED, WHICH IS RARE: working with the Ministry of Culture the group reports having reviewed 250 demolition permits and stopped the demolition of 150 buildings in a single year, and states that without that intervention roughly a quarter of Beirut's remaining architectural heritage would have been lost in that year alone. Its own figures put the stock at about 1,600 traditional buildings counted in a 1990s census against roughly 300 standing now. KNOW WHAT YOU ARE UP AGAINST, BECAUSE THIS GROUP HAS DOCUMENTED BOTH ROUTES AROUND PROTECTION: in March 2017 a Culture Minister issued a decree striking a listed eighteenth-century house from the general inventory of historical buildings ahead of its demolition by the owners, and a separate building was dismantled after a high administrative body allowed the owner to proceed against the Ministry of Culture's decision. A listing can be removed by decree and can be overridden on appeal. Read this with the Lebanese heritage law finding recorded elsewhere in this file: classification obliges the state to compensate the owner, which is why classification is resisted. AFTER THE 2020 PORT EXPLOSION THE GROUP REPORTED THAT AGENTS WERE APPROACHING DAMAGED PROPERTIES WITHIN TWO DAYS. Where a disaster weakens owners, expect acquisition attempts immediately, and expect the response to need to be as fast. WHAT IT IS NOT: not a litigator, not a funder, and not a landholder. Much of its work runs through social channels rather than a maintained website, so treat the hotline and the direct contacts as the reliable route in.

trackers.name: Beirut Heritage Initiative — owners AND tenants can file a request, and it pairs the engineers' order with the bar association
trackers.desc: THE INTAKE IS OPEN TO TENANTS AS WELL AS OWNERS, WHICH IS RARE AND MATTERS: its own site states it is always ready to receive new requests from owners or tenants in need of help. In most property disputes a tenant has no standing and nowhere to go; here the request form does not ask which you are. AND THE STRUCTURE IS THE THING TO COPY. It is organised around a team of experts with complementary skills including the Order of Engineers and Architects of Beirut AND THE BEIRUT BAR ASSOCIATION, together with specialist heritage organisations — a planner, a lawyer and a conservation specialist assembled in advance rather than hunted for one at a time. A community that cannot afford to retain three professions can approach one body that already contains them. IT WAS CREATED TO BRIDGE TWO GAPS AT ONCE, AND NAMING THE SECOND ONE IS THE INSIGHT: funding AND COORDINATION between the owners and residents of damaged heritage structures and the public departments whose permits are needed for reconstruction — specifically the Directorate General of Antiquities and the Office of the Governor of Beirut. Money alone does not repair a protected building; somebody has to get the permit. If your problem looks like a funding problem, check whether it is actually a permissions problem. THE WORKING METHOD IS WORTH TAKING WHEREVER RESOURCES ARE SHORT: it identifies PRIORITY CLUSTERS and concentrates repairs there rather than spreading thin, expressly to maximise impact with scarce resources, and sequences work in three phases — emergency propping and sheltering, partial repairs, then full reconstruction. Its published project counts run into the hundreds of buildings across two Beirut districts, on stock built between the 1860s and the 1930s, against roughly a thousand historic buildings damaged in the 2020 port explosion. It states it is funded exclusively by people choosing to contribute, takes donations and volunteers directly, publishes its own annual report, and works alongside a wide stakeholder network including national heritage bodies, an Arab architecture centre, international monuments and museums councils, the Blue Shield and the demolition-watch group recorded separately in this file. THE LIMITS: it is Beirut, it is built heritage, and it is restoration rather than opposition. It will not fight a development for you — but where a building's survival depends on repair and a permit rather than on a court case, this is the body that does both, and the collective model behind it is the most transferable thing in this entry.

trackers.name: Lebanon Eco Movement — sixty member organisations, and a hotline for reporting environmental violations
trackers.desc: IT RUNS AN ENVIRONMENTAL OBSERVATORY TO MONITOR VIOLATIONS ACROSS LEBANON, WITH A HOTLINE TO REPORT THEM. That is the most directly usable thing in this entry: a national number to call when something is happening on the ground, which this file has otherwise found in Lebanon only for building demolition. AND IT OPPOSES PROJECTS RATHER THAN ONLY ADVOCATING: it is recorded as actively taking steps AGAINST THE CONSTRUCTION OF DAMS that threaten the environment, against unlawful poaching, and for the preservation of the Lebanese coastal shore — and it contributed to the campaign that closed a major landfill. THE REASON IT MATTERS MOST HERE IS THE ONE THIS FILE HAS BEEN CIRCLING FOR EIGHTY ROUNDS: LEBANON'S LOCAL ENVIRONMENTAL BODIES ARE LARGELY UNREACHABLE ONLINE. A coastal litigator, the northern cedar forest committees and a heritage association were each verified as real, active and constituted, and none could be given an address. A NETWORK OF AROUND SIXTY MEMBER ORGANISATIONS FROM ALL OVER LEBANON IS THE WAY TO REACH THEM — ask the movement which of its members covers your district, rather than searching for that member yourself. Its eleven founding organisations are named in the record and include heritage, coastal, development and regional associations, which indicates the spread. It was founded in 2012 when those eleven gathered in a forest outside the capital with twenty more environmental organisations. ITS STATED OBJECTIVES INCLUDE TWO A COMMUNITY CAN USE DIRECTLY: strengthening the capacities of its member organisations, and organising advocacy campaigns toward the Lebanese authorities — so a small local association can join and be carried by a national body rather than campaigning alone, which is the failure mode an independent analysis identified for isolated campaigns in Georgia and which applies just as well here. It also participates in national environmental policy planning and sits in Mediterranean and regional networks. THE ADDRESS PROBLEM APPLIES TO THE FEDERATION ITSELF, WHICH IS WORTH STATING PLAINLY: no domain of its own was reached this round, and the contact given here is its own public page, followed by tens of thousands of people. A Lebanese civil society directory carries its current procurement notices, which indicates it is operating; two of the fullest profiles of it sit on aggregator sites this file does not use and were refused. Confirm the hotline number at source before relying on it.

trackers.name: Mada — it could not get the park, so it worked on the legal framework for parks
trackers.desc: WHEN THE PROTECTION YOU WANT DOES NOT EXIST IN LAW, BUILD THE LAW. This organisation spent its early years working towards a natural park across the Akkar, Hermel and Donnieh highlands, with development and conservation goals SET JOINTLY WITH LOCAL AUTHORITIES AND COMMUNITIES. When the park became a longer-term ambition, it continued working on ELABORATING THE LEGAL FRAMEWORK FOR PARKS. Treating a missing legal category as the obstacle, and building it, is a different response from abandoning a campaign or waiting for one — and this file has recorded elsewhere that Lebanese law would not recognise a nature reserve on private land at all, which is exactly the kind of gap such work addresses. IT IS THE ONLY BODY IN THIS FILE WORKING IN THE NORTHERN HIGHLANDS. Every other Lebanese entry operates in Beirut, the Shouf, Keserwan or nationally; this one was born in Akkar and Hermel in 1999 and was among the first organisations to work in Akkar at all, registered under a numbered interior ministry decree in October 2000 and a member of the international conservation union. If your land is in the north, this is the organisation that has been there longest. IT SUPPORTS OTHER PEOPLE'S INITIATIVES RATHER THAN ONLY RUNNING ITS OWN: through a platform it provides TECHNICAL SUPPORT TO CIVIL INITIATIVES to help them develop and reach their potential — which matters in a country where this file has documented constituted local bodies that cannot even be given an address. AND IT BUILDS A TOOL WORTH ASKING YOUR MUNICIPALITY FOR BY NAME: participatory LOCAL DEVELOPMENT PLANS covering economy, society, environment and governance, developed bottom-up with the community and described as both a roadmap for the municipality AND AN INSTRUMENT OF ACCOUNTABILITY FOR THE COMMUNITY. A plan your council has adopted, with an environment pillar you helped write, is something to hold it to afterwards. It works through what it calls a territorial approach, has conducted studies and socio-economic assessments of the region's vulnerability, natural assets and cultural heritage, and publishes its reports and MAPS on its own site. THE LIMITS: it is a development agency, not an objector — it works with municipalities and institutions rather than against them, and nothing found shows it opposing a scheme. Its priorities shifted with the refugee crisis from 2011, and much of its current work is agriculture, food systems, education and livelihoods. Note a date discrepancy: one professional-network profile gives its founding as 2020, twenty years out; its own site and its registration decree give 1999 and 2000.

trackers.name: AUB Nature Conservation Center — it ran participatory contamination research across six municipalities and published it
trackers.desc: ASK YOUR NEAREST UNIVERSITY WHETHER IT WILL TAKE YOUR SITUATION AS A RESEARCH PROJECT. This centre published a study of multisource groundwater contamination across SIX MUNICIPALITIES near a landfill, expressly as part of a PUBLIC PARTICIPATORY RESEARCH PROJECT — peer-reviewed, citable evidence about named communities' water, produced with those communities rather than about them. That is a different kind of asset from a consultant's report: it is independent, it is published, and it does not disappear when a project ends. NOW THE WARNING, AND IT MAY BE THE MOST IMPORTANT THING HERE: ITS RESEARCH RECORDS THAT IMPORTANT PLANT AREAS, DESIGNATED FOR THEIR BIODIVERSITY VALUE, ARE NOT ALWAYS OFFICIALLY PROTECTED, AND OFTEN FALL WITHIN MIXED PRIVATE AND PUBLIC LAND OWNERSHIP. If you have been told your area is designated, establish which designation it is, under what law, who it binds and what it actually prevents — a scientific designation and a legal protection are not the same thing, and this file has recorded elsewhere that a legal category can be removed administratively before a project appears. The same work examined using international protected-area management categories as a tool to assess local preferences for managing such an area, which is the practical follow-on: if the designation binds nobody, what management would. WHAT ELSE IT HAS BUILT THAT A COMMUNITY CAN USE: aerial green maps of EIGHTY VILLAGES, developed with the tourism and interior ministries and since turned into a digital platform — a baseline record of what was there, which is the thing communities almost never have when a scheme is announced. It has also published national guidelines for native tree nursery management, setting standards for seedling production for restoration work. AND IT GIVES MUNICIPALITIES A REASON TO ACT: an annual Biodiversity Village Award offering participating municipalities recognition for the best green practices. A council that wants an award is easier to move than one that only fears an objection. Founded in 2001 under the university provost's office, drawing faculty from multiple disciplines, describing itself as the leading transdisciplinary academic centre on nature conservation in the region, and stating that it operates with municipalities, universities, non-governmental organisations and government authorities. ITS RESEARCH REPOSITORY IS PUBLIC and its volunteering is open — anyone can apply with a statement of interest, including for fieldwork. THE LIMITS: it is an academic centre, not an advocate. It will not object to a scheme, and its cooperation with ministries and municipalities means it is unlikely to front opposition to a state-backed one. Approach it for evidence, mapping, baselines and standards — and take the objection to the bodies recorded elsewhere in this file.

trackers.name: The MedFund — recurring costs of marine protected area management, funded for five years
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY IS BOTH A PUBLISHED PRIORITY INTERVENTION COUNTRY AND A NAMED BENEFICIARY OF A LARGER PROGRAMME THIS FUND EXECUTES: a multi-year project financing twenty nationally designated and newly designated marine protected areas across six countries, covering close to 220,000 hectares, with this one among them. WHAT MAKES IT UNUSUAL IS WHAT IT PAYS FOR: the RECURRENT MANAGEMENT COSTS of marine protected areas, granted to their management and co-management structures FOR FIVE YEARS. Most funders pay for projects and refuse running costs; this file recorded one that says so explicitly. A protected area that cannot pay its staff after the project ends is the problem this fund was built to solve, and in a country where this file has documented reserves and municipal protected areas established with little money behind them, that is the binding constraint. IT WORKS AS AN ENDOWMENT — raising and investing capital and granting the INTEREST — which is why it can commit for five years at a time. GRANTS GO TO NGOs AND TO NATIONAL PROTECTED AREA MANAGEMENT AUTHORITIES ALIKE, AND CO-MANAGEMENT STRUCTURES QUALIFY — which matters here, because this file has recorded that the workable model in this country is a community or association managing land it does not own, under municipal or endowment arrangements. APPLY IN TWO STAGES: a short expression of interest by one deadline, then a full application some weeks later. THE LIMITS: marine areas only, so an inland site does not qualify; the area must already be designated or formally in the designation process, making this a fund for sustaining protection rather than obtaining it; and it funds management rather than objection or litigation. The larger programme it executes also builds the capacity of protected area managers and is run alongside a network of Mediterranean protected area managers, which is worth asking about as a route to peers doing the same work in neighbouring countries.

trackers.name: Save the Bisri Valley — the campaign that got a World Bank loan cancelled, and how
trackers.desc: THE LOAN WAS CANCELLED BECAUSE PRECONDITIONS WERE UNMET, NOT BECAUSE THE ECOLOGY WAS PERSUASIVE. In September 2020 the World Bank cancelled 244 million dollars of undisbursed funds for a dam in this valley, after the government failed to complete AN ECOLOGICAL COMPENSATION PLAN and ARRANGEMENTS FOR THE OPERATION AND MANAGEMENT of the dam — both PRECONDITIONS OF THE LOAN. If a lender finances the scheme you are facing, obtain the loan agreement, find the conditions precedent, and check whether they have been satisfied. An unmet condition is a lever no argument about habitat can match, and this is the only documented cancellation of its kind in this file. BE EQUALLY CLEAR ABOUT WHAT DID NOT WORK: the campaign submitted a REQUEST FOR INSPECTION to the Bank's own accountability panel in 2019 AND IT WAS NOT ACCEPTED. This payload records international complaint mechanisms for many countries; here one refused the case while the campaign won by other routes. Use the mechanism, but do not build the strategy on it. WHAT THE CAMPAIGN ACTUALLY DID, AND ALL OF IT IS COPYABLE: a public petition addressed to the lender rather than the government; WEEKLY WALKING TOURS of the valley to show citizens what was at stake; a protest camp of tents in the pine forest; disrupting a talk by a Bank vice-president at a university; a lawsuit against the Bank, with media coverage of the lawsuit itself treated as part of the campaign; and turning the Bank's own anti-corruption messaging against it online. THE DECISIVE POLITICAL MOVE WAS LOCAL: MUNICIPALITIES WITHDREW THEIR SUPPORT FOR THE DAM. Mayors changing position is what makes a project politically expensive, and this file has recorded elsewhere that a council can be moved by recognition as well as by objection. THE ARGUMENTS THAT LANDED WERE TECHNICAL AND FINANCIAL, NOT SENTIMENTAL: that the site sits on an ACTIVE SEISMIC FAULT with the risk of reservoir-induced earthquakes; that the rock is porous and karstic so the reservoir would not hold the expected water and sealing it would cost hundreds of millions more; that OTHER RECENTLY BUILT DAMS IN THIS COUNTRY HAD FAILED FOR THE SAME REASON; that six million square metres of natural and agricultural land and more than fifty historical sites would be lost; and a plain comparison of the cost against hospitals, teaching and jobs. IT WAS CO-FOUNDED IN 2018 BY A NATIONAL CAMPAIGN FOR THE VALLEY AND BY THE LEBANESE ENVIRONMENTAL FEDERATION RECORDED SEPARATELY IN THIS FILE, and both it and that federation were funded by a small international grantmaker also recorded here — five thousand dollars each. This win was financed by two resources already in this map. THE LIMITS: it is a campaign, not a service; it achieved its aim in 2020 and its current activity is not established here; and it is reachable through its public accounts rather than an office.

trackers.name: Faith Plans — the route by which a church, monastery or endowment commits its own land to protection
trackers.desc: IF THE LAND YOU ARE DEFENDING BELONGS TO A CHURCH, A MONASTERY OR A RELIGIOUS ENDOWMENT, THIS IS THE STRUCTURED ROUTE FOR ASKING ITS OWNER TO PROTECT IT. It is a framework through which faith communities commit to using their ASSETS, INVESTMENTS AND INFLUENCE for people and planet, with a dedicated site carrying ideas, resources, case studies and a sign-up through which a faith group develops its own plan. IT DESCENDS DIRECTLY FROM THE PROGRAMME THAT ALREADY WORKED IN THIS COUNTRY: it builds on a 2009 faith commitments programme run by the same predecessor organisation whose earlier work led a church here to declare a forest it owns a protected environment, and then to consider doing the same for an entire valley. That predecessor no longer operates; this framework is its live descendant, created jointly with a major conservation organisation's beliefs and values programme and supported by faith networks, secular environmental groups and United Nations bodies. Groups with a combined reach reported at over 150 million people have signed up to develop plans. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE HERE THAN ALMOST ANYWHERE: this file established that Lebanese law would not permit a nature reserve on private land, and that the workable routes are endowment leases, municipal commons and management without ownership — and that a religious endowment behaves as a LANDLORD who leases to whoever arrives with a funded offer. A faith plan is the instrument for turning that same landlord into a protector, and it requires no purchase, no legislation and no ministry. APPROACH IT THROUGH THE RELIGIOUS AUTHORITY, NOT AS A COMMUNITY GROUP. The framework is designed for faith institutions to adopt; your part is to persuade the diocese, the endowment board or the monastery to sign up and to put your valley, forest or spring into its plan. Bring the case studies from the site with you — an authority that sees peers elsewhere doing this is easier to move than one asked to invent it. DO NOT CONFUSE IT WITH ITS PARENT BODY, WHICH DOES SOMETHING ELSE: that organisation works on FAITH-CONSISTENT INVESTING, helping religious institutions align stock market portfolios with their values, and offers free and paid services to faith-based asset owners. It is not a land protection service and approaching it about a threatened forest would be a wasted letter. THE LIMITS: it is a commitment framework, not a funder, a regulator or an enforcer. A plan binds nobody legally, and this file recorded in R177 that in the very valley concerned, church ownership, a world heritage listing and a national designation dating from 1939 together have not prevented encroachment, illegal building and inconsistent conservation. A declaration is a beginning, not an outcome.

trackers.name: fundahope — run your own fundraiser, including a permanent one people subscribe to monthly
trackers.desc: THIS PAYLOAD HOLDS MORE THAN NINETY FUNDING ENTRIES AND ALMOST ALL OF THEM REQUIRE APPLYING TO SOMEBODY. THIS ONE YOU RUN YOURSELF. A campaign is started by writing your story, setting a goal, uploading the requested documents and submitting — and campaigns may be launched by INDIVIDUALS, ENTITIES OR NGOs, so a registered organisation is not strictly required. This file's most repeated finding across twenty-three countries is that communities are blocked by lacking a constituted body; here an individual may begin. THE FEATURE THAT MATTERS MOST FOR LAND IS NOT THE CAMPAIGN BUT THE PERMANENT FUNDRAISER: a long-term fundraiser WITH NO DEFINED GOAL, where supporters can SUBSCRIBE FOR MONTHLY DONATIONS instead of giving once. That is recurring income. This map has recorded a standing local endowment, a community foundation and a member-funded cooperative as the most durable ways to pay for defending ground, because a one-off appeal buys one fight and a monthly income buys persistence. A PERMANENT FUNDRAISER IS THE VERSION OF THAT WHICH REQUIRES NO ENDOWMENT AND NO LAWYER. AND THE DISTRIBUTION TOOLS FIT PLACES WHERE MOST SUPPORTERS ARE NOT ONLINE: every campaign carries social sharing links, A QR CODE AND A PRINTABLE FLYER — so it can be pinned in a shop, handed out at a meeting or printed on a notice, and reach flows from how widely it is shared rather than from the platform's own audience. IT WORKS AT REAL SCALE AND IT IS CURRENT: one campaign raised over fifty-one thousand dollars toward a hundred-and-forty-thousand-dollar medical cost, another supported a hundred and twenty-five people, and a fundraiser begun in 2024 was still running and raising in 2026. Organisations using it describe reaching international donors without red tape or financial constraints, which matters where the diaspora is larger and better resourced than the community at home. THE DISCLAIMER YOU MUST CARRY: THE PLATFORM STATES IT HAS NO DIRECT OR INDIRECT LINK WITH THE PURPOSE OR CONTENT OF POSTED FUNDRAISERS. It hosts; it does not vouch, verify the cause or guarantee delivery. Campaigns can be reported and it says it investigates. That cuts both ways: nobody screens you, and nobody screens the others — so publish your own accounts, name who holds the money, and show what was bought. THE OTHER LIMITS: platform and payment fees apply and should be checked before setting a target; success depends on your own network rather than on the site; and a public campaign is a public statement of what you are trying to stop.

trackers.name: Orders of Engineers and Architects — two regional bodies, and the four questions to put to them
trackers.desc: THE ENGINEERING PROFESSION HERE IS ORGANISED IN TWO SEPARATE ORDERS BY REGION, AND WHICH ONE COVERS YOU DECIDES WHERE EVERY QUESTION GOES. One is seated in the capital; the other covers the second city and the north of the country. EACH HAS ITS OWN OFFICIAL SITE AND PUBLISHES ITS OWN LAWS AND INTERNAL REGULATIONS. Establish which order your area falls under before writing to anybody, because a request sent to the wrong one is simply outside its jurisdiction. NOW THE HONEST PART, AND IT SHAPES HOW THIS ENTRY SHOULD BE USED. THIS FILE VERIFIED THE EXISTENCE, SEATS AND PUBLISHED RULES OF BOTH ORDERS AND DID NOT VERIFY THEIR SERVICES. What follows are the four questions that examining the equivalent bodies in four neighbouring countries showed to be worth asking — THEY ARE QUESTIONS TO PUT TO THE ORDER, NOT CLAIMS ABOUT WHAT IT OFFERS. FIRST: MUST A NAMED SUPERVISING ENGINEER BE APPOINTED ON CONSTRUCTION WORKS, AND WHO IS IT ON THE SCHEME NEAR YOU? In four neighbouring countries the answer is yes, the person is registered with the order, and the order can receive a complaint about their professional conduct — a route that exists even where the permit itself cannot be challenged. SECOND: WHAT RANK OR CLASSIFICATION DOES A PROFESSIONAL HOLD, AND WHAT DOES IT PERMIT? Elsewhere in this region rank decides what an engineer may lawfully sign, supervise or chair, and instructing someone whose rank does not cover the work wastes time you cannot recover. THIRD: IS THERE A LICENSED TESTING AND INSPECTION SPECIALISM? In a neighbouring country that is a recognised, licensed category of engineering office — which converts the problem of proving physical harm from a favour asked of a university into an ordinary commercial service. FOURTH: ARE FEE SCALES PUBLISHED, AND ARE THERE REDUCED OR FREE FEES FOR REGISTERED SOCIETIES AND COOPERATIVES? One neighbouring order publishes both a scale and a route to free design and supervision for a society that holds land in its own name. WHY IT IS WORTH ASKING HERE PARTICULARLY: these orders are large, elected, professionally independent bodies of long standing, and in a country where building safety and reconstruction have been sustained public questions, an order that publishes its own laws is a place where a technical answer can be obtained on the record. THE LIMITS: an order regulates its members and will not oppose a project; its services cost money; this entry records the structure and the questions rather than confirmed services; and a reviewer should verify the four points above before publication and rewrite this entry with the answers.

trackers.name: The bar's judicial aid — a free lawyer, why it underperforms, and the one lever you hold
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY HELD ONE ENTRY IN THIS MAP FOR LEGAL HELP AND IT WAS NOT A WAY TO GET A LAWYER. The bar runs a JUDICIAL AID scheme with its own section and a published set of questions and answers, and that is the route to a free lawyer here. KNOW WHICH BAR YOU BELONG TO BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE. THERE ARE TWO. One registers lawyers holding offices in every governorate EXCEPT THE NORTH; the other covers the north. NOBODY MAY PRACTISE LAW IN THIS COUNTRY WITHOUT BEING REGISTERED IN ONE OF THEM, and no one may be registered in both — so an approach to the wrong bar is wasted, and a person offering to act for you who is on neither roll is not a lawyer. NOW THE PART THAT WILL SAVE YOU DISAPPOINTMENT, BECAUSE A PUBLISHED INVESTIGATION SET IT OUT PLAINLY: THE AID IS CARRIED BY TRAINEE LAWYERS, AND THE BAR'S ROLE IS LIMITED TO ASSIGNING ONE AND HANDING OVER THE FILE WITH A ONE-PAGE FORM for recording how the case proceeds. THE COMMITTEE FOLLOWS THE FILE IN FORM RATHER THAN IN SUBSTANCE, and in most cases nobody reads that form at all. The consequence falls hardest on aided litigants precisely because, unlike paying clients, THEY USUALLY DO NOT KNOW WHAT THEY ARE ENTITLED TO EXPECT. SO HERE IS THE LEVER, AND IT IS THE MOST USEFUL SENTENCE IN THIS ENTRY: IF AN AIDED LITIGANT COMPLAINS, THE COMMITTEE CAN ASK THE ASSIGNED LAWYER FOR HIS REASONS AND APPOINT ANOTHER LAWYER TO COMPLETE THE FILE. Complaint is therefore not a gesture — it is the mechanism by which a neglected file gets a new advocate. Keep your own dated record of every hearing, every filing and every unanswered call, because that record is what a complaint rests on. THE BAR PUBLISHES MORE THAT IS WORTH USING: A LAWYERS' DIRECTORY for finding and checking a named advocate; A DIRECTORY OF COURTS AND OFFICIAL ADMINISTRATIONS, which answers the question of which office holds what; the national laws and an electronic library; and A HUMAN RIGHTS INSTITUTE inside the bar with its own statute, activities and publications. Its published committee list for the current year includes a committee following the cases of refugees and foreign workers — SO ASK WHICH COMMITTEE COVERS YOUR SUBJECT, because a committee is easier to interest than an institution. THE LIMITS: judicial aid is means-tested and its conditions must be read from the bar's own answers; a trainee advocate is a real advocate but an inexperienced one; and the bar regulates the profession rather than campaigning — for the substance of a planning or environmental fight, use it alongside the urban research studio and the heritage initiative recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Heritage protection association — a national NGO with a named sites officer
trackers.desc: THIS FILE ESTABLISHED AT R329 THAT HERITAGE DESIGNATION IS ONE OF THE VERY FEW GROUNDS THAT HALTS CONSTRUCTION OUTRIGHT, AND THAT HERITAGE SOCIETIES ARE OFTEN OLDER AND BETTER DOCUMENTED THAN THE ENVIRONMENTAL BODIES THIS PAYLOAD HAS BEEN CHASING. HERE IS ONE FOR THIS COUNTRY: a cultural heritage non-governmental organisation founded in 2010, based in a district of the mountain region, serving the country as a whole. THE DETAIL THAT MAKES IT USABLE IS ITS STRUCTURE: ITS PUBLISHED OFFICERS INCLUDE A SITES OFFICER WHO IS ALSO THE ASSOCIATION'S OFFICIAL REPRESENTATIVE, alongside a president, vice-president and secretary general. AN ORGANISATION WITH A NAMED PERSON RESPONSIBLE FOR SITES IS AN ORGANISATION YOU CAN WRITE TO ABOUT A PARTICULAR PLACE — and this file has found repeatedly that the difference between a body that helps and one that does not is whether someone owns the subject internally. WHAT TO ASK FOR: whether the association already holds a record of the site you are worried about; whether it will inspect and document it; and whether it will write to the authorities in its own name. A heritage association's letter about a specific building or site carries weight that a residents' letter does not, because it comes from a body whose whole purpose is judging such things. AND USE IT WITH WHAT THIS COUNTRY ALREADY HAS IN THIS MAP: the urban research studio, the heritage initiative through which owners AND TENANTS can file, the public-space organisation whose campaigns are recorded separately, and the bar's judicial aid route. A documented heritage claim is the strongest thing to put in front of any of them. THE LIMITS, AND THEY ARE REAL. THE RECORD REACHED FOR THIS BODY IS AN ENCYCLOPAEDIA ENTRY GIVING ITS FOUNDING, LOCATION AND OFFICERS RATHER THAN ITS OWN ACCOUNT OF CURRENT WORK — CONFIRM THAT IT IS STILL ACTIVE AND WHO NOW HOLDS THE SITES ROLE BEFORE RELYING ON IT. It is a heritage body, so it will speak to the historic and cultural value of a place and not to its ecology or to planning law. And it does not hold land or provide lawyers.

trackers.name: International legal representation — it has filed on this country, including on transnational repression
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING IS RICH IN CAMPAIGNERS, PLANNERS, HERITAGE BODIES AND LAWYERS — AND HELD NOTHING ABOUT PROTECTION FOR THE PEOPLE WHO USE THEM. THIS ORGANISATION REPRESENTS INDIVIDUALS SUBJECTED TO SEVERE VIOLATIONS BEFORE INTERNATIONAL PROTECTION MECHANISMS, chiefly UNITED NATIONS SPECIAL PROCEDURES AND TREATY BODIES, and engages domestic and regional mechanisms where they are effective and accessible. IT HAS FILED ON THIS COUNTRY IN A UNIVERSAL PERIODIC REVIEW SUBMISSION RAISING TORTURE, REFOULEMENT AND TRANSNATIONAL REPRESSION — the last of those meaning pressure that follows people across borders. IT ALSO MAINTAINS A COUNTRY PAGE, so its existing record here can be read before approaching. WHAT IT OFFERS A COMMUNITY IS PRECISE: LEGAL ASSISTANCE AND REPRESENTATION AT THE INTERNATIONAL LEVEL, working with VICTIMS, FAMILIES AND THEIR OWN LAWYERS. This file records here the bar's judicial aid scheme and its weaknesses, and an urban research studio that pulls the cadastral record. THIS IS THE STEP AFTER THOSE — for when the domestic route has been exhausted or has failed, and someone has been detained, prosecuted or silenced for what they did. IT ALSO WORKS STRUCTURALLY, documenting patterns and root causes rather than single incidents, which means a series of similar cases — several communities facing the same treatment — IS MORE USE TO IT THAN ONE, and more likely to produce a finding that helps everyone. THE LIMITS: its subject is severe human rights violations, so it engages with what is done to people, not with permits or plans. INTERNATIONAL MECHANISMS PRODUCE FINDINGS AND PRESSURE OVER MONTHS OR YEARS, NOT ORDERS THAT STOP WORK. And it is a foreign organisation whose work is published. Read it with the bar aid and legal entries recorded separately here.

trackers.name: RTI Portal (India)
trackers.desc: You CAN get: any record, file noting, order, inspection report or status report held by a public authority, under the Right to Information Act 2005, on payment of a ₹10 fee — waived for BPL applicants. Any Indian citizen may ask; you do not have to say why. The Public Information Officer must ordinarily answer within 30 days. Know which site does what: rti.gov.in is the GATEWAY — use it to identify the right PIO and First Appellate Authority and to read proactive disclosures. Filing happens at rtionline.gov.in. You CAN'T get: state records through that filing portal. It covers CENTRAL ministries, departments and public authorities only, and an application wrongly filed there against a state body — including the Government of NCT of Delhi, which runs its own portal — is returned WITHOUT REFUND. State authorities need the relevant state portal or a postal application. An online first appeal can only follow an online application. For activists: this is how you get an environmental clearance file, a public-hearing record or project correspondence from MoEFCC or a central regulator — but a State Pollution Control Board is a state body, so check the tier before paying. If the PIO misses the 30 days or answers badly, appeal to the First Appellate Authority within 30 days, then to the Central Information Commission within 90; the Commission can order disclosure and fine the officer.

trackers.name: Centre for Organisation Research & Education (CORE)
trackers.desc: The India Centre for Organization Research and Education is a representative indigenous peoples' organisation based in Manipur, India. The organisation has been working in grassroots support and advocacy for the rights of the indigenous and tribal peoples in India’s North East region.

trackers.name: Parivesh — environmental clearance portal
