trackers.desc: The Philippines' independent constitutional supreme audit institution — audits all accounts and expenditures of government funds and properties. — Holds to account: officials handling public money & power — find audit findings and how public money was spent or lost.

trackers.name: Department of Budget and Management (DBM)
trackers.desc: The Philippine executive agency overseeing the national budget — allocation, release and management of public funds. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in the Philippines.

trackers.name: Office of the Ombudsman (Philippines)
trackers.desc: Philippine constitutional body investigating and prosecuting graft and corruption by public officials.

trackers.name: Philippine Statistics Authority
trackers.desc: Philippines's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in the Philippines.

trackers.name: SEC Philippines
trackers.desc: The Philippines' Securities and Exchange Commission corporate registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Writ of Kalikasan — how to file, and who qualifies
trackers.desc: THE REMEDY, NOT AN ORGANISATION. Founded on Section 16, Article II of the Constitution and operationalised by A.M. No. 09-6-8-SC, Rule 7. THERE ARE NO DOCKET FEES — the rules waive them so public-interest litigants can reach the court. File directly with the Supreme Court or the Court of Appeals; it is not filed in the Regional Trial Courts, and a petition lodged in an RTC is in the wrong forum. The petition must be verified (sworn), naming the law violated, your circumstances and the respondents, or stating that their identities are unknown. Procedure is summary: petition, writ, the respondent's Return, a summary hearing, a possible TEPO, then judgment — with liberal admission of evidence and site inspections. Reliefs include injunction, environmental protection orders, rehabilitation and continuing mandamus. TEST THE THRESHOLD FIRST: the harm must transcend personal or property rights and threaten the life, health or property of inhabitants in 2 or more cities or provinces — a single-site development inside one municipality does not qualify however severe, and that disqualifies most local fights. AND WINNING THE WRIT IS NOT WINNING A HALT: in the Sibuyan Island case the Court issued the writ against the miner, DENR and the MGB, gave 10 days to comment and referred the case onward — but denied the temporary environmental protection order; and reporting on the writ's record notes that granted petitions have not always been implemented by local governments.

trackers.name: Public Attorney's Office — district offices nationwide
trackers.desc: THE GOVERNMENT'S OWN LAW OFFICE FOR PEOPLE WHO CANNOT PAY, under Republic Act 9406, with district and field offices nationwide — many inside Halls of Justice, court buildings or local government complexes, so this is a local service rather than a capital-city one. Go to the office covering either your residence or where the case will be filed. TWO TESTS, BOTH MUST BE PASSED. Indigency: published limits are ₱24,000 net monthly income in NCR, ₱22,000 in other cities outside NCR, ₱20,000 in municipalities outside NCR — and owning a modest family home does not by itself disqualify you. Merit: the case must have a genuine legal basis and not be frivolous or harassing. BRING: an Affidavit of Indigency plus an income tax return, payslip, or a Certificate of Indigency from the DSWD, the Municipal Social Welfare Office, or your Barangay Chairman. Filing fees are 90 percent discounted for indigents and fully waived with a PAO certificate. THREE LIMITS. PAO can act for one side only — if your opponent is also indigent, one of you is referred to the Integrated Bar of the Philippines. Caseloads are extreme: a PAO lawyer averaged 458 cases in one recorded year against about 40 for a private lawyer, so expect little time per client and turnover of the lawyer on your case. And for a public-interest environmental matter, also try the IBP provincial and city chapters under Rule 139-A, law school clinics — some of which waive means tests where the case involves environmental protection — and groups such as FLAG and SALIGAN, which take landmark land-rights cases at their discretion.

trackers.name: CBFMA — 25-year tenure, and a consent right over permits
trackers.desc: HOW A COMMUNITY GETS SECURE TENURE OVER FOREST LAND IT DOES NOT OWN. Under EO 263 and DENR AO 96-29, a Community-Based Forest Management Agreement runs between the DENR and a people's organisation for 25 years, renewable for another 25, under the community's own Community Resource Management Framework. It is also the instrument issued to POs in allowable zones within protected areas. THE RIGHT THAT STOPS THINGS: a PO must be informed of and consulted on all government projects in the area — and the PO's consent must be secured by DENR before granting or renewing contracts, leases and permits for extraction and utilisation of natural resources inside it, with an equitable sharing agreement reached first where the grantee is not from the affected community. A consent right inside your own tenure area is far stronger than objecting to someone else's permit from outside. You also receive all income from sustainable use within the area (subject to NIPAS), and exemption from forest charges on plantation products under RA 7161. THE PROCESS TRAP: your LGU must endorse the application before DENR can act — and PENRO/CENRO are mandated to orient local executives about CBFM, so ask DENR field staff to run that orientation rather than lobbying the LGU alone. KNOW WHAT IT IS: CBFM is a production sharing arrangement and communities under it have been oriented toward timber plantation harvesting — it secures tenure, it does not by itself mean preservation. For indigenous peoples the stronger route is ancestral domain recognition under RA 8371 (IPRA).

trackers.name: Datalex
trackers.desc: Official Armenian judicial information system: case search, schedules and court decisions. · Find here: free Armenian legislation and court decisions (Datalex).

trackers.name: EcoLur Informational NGO
trackers.desc: Armenia's environmental information organisation, built around a repeatable model rather than a single campaign: it runs named S.O.S. campaigns site by site — Amulsar, Teghout, Akhtala, Qajaran, Kapan, Agarak, Sotq, Ararat and others — acting as the information coordinator for residents living beside a mine or a polluter. WHO TO ENLIST when what you need is the evidence and the timetable rather than a lawyer. You CAN: use its independent-experts library, which collects geologists' and geomorphologists' opinions, social-impact surveys of affected communities and reports on new circumstances in an ESIA — the material that turns an objection into an argument. It also publishes notices of scheduled public hearings on exploration and mining permits and reports the council votes on them, which is the single hardest thing for a rural community to learn in time. For activists: it works with CEE Bankwatch and other Armenian groups on complaints to development-bank accountability mechanisms, so it is a route to the financing side as well as the permit.

trackers.name: FPWC — Caucasus Wildlife Refuge (Foundation for the Preservation of Wildlife and Cultural Assets)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: gives a community an alternative buyer for its own land. FPWC built the Caucasus Wildlife Refuge from 2011 by taking on land from more than a dozen communities across Ararat and Vayots Dzor — mostly by lease, with the payments going back to the villages for their own improvements — and it now covers around 30,000 hectares buffering the Khosrov Forest State Reserve, the first privately protected area in the South Caucasus. It employs local rangers and funds part of the work through ecotourism rather than donations alone. USE IT: this is the counterparty when someone else wants your community's land. Gnishik gave its land to the refuge under pressure to lease it as a hunting ground instead; another community turned down a company's cash offer and ceded the land for conservation. If a concession, a hunting lease or a mine is being dangled at your council, FPWC is the competing offer that keeps the ground intact and still pays. Note it is lease-based, so the community keeps title.

trackers.name: ARMEPS
trackers.desc: Armenia's electronic procurement system. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Armenia, and for how much.

trackers.name: Audit Chamber
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Armenia, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Statistical Committee of Armenia (ArmStat)
trackers.desc: Armenia's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Armenia.

trackers.name: Corruption Prevention Commission
trackers.desc: Armenia's independent commission overseeing asset declarations and integrity.

trackers.name: Hetq
trackers.desc: Armenian investigative outlet reporting on corruption and abuse of public office.

trackers.name: Union of Informed Citizens (UIC)
trackers.desc: Armenian NGO (since 2014) working to consolidate democracy through multi-component election observation, state-procurement monitoring, and advocacy for electoral, constitutional and anti-corruption reform. Runs the Fact Investigation Platform (FIP.am) fact-checking outlet and the Reforms.am tracker.

trackers.name: State Register of Legal Entities
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Armenia Multi-Sector Register
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Publicly searchable.

trackers.name: Court of Cassation of Armenia
trackers.desc: Court of Cassation of Armenia — appellate court in Armenia (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: SLAPP suits against Armenian defenders — take advice before you post
trackers.desc: READ THIS BEFORE CAMPAIGNING PUBLICLY. International groups issued a solidarity statement over Armenian environmental and human rights defenders facing defamation and criminalization. Around one mining project the recorded pattern was: dozens of activists sued for social media posts or for comments made during meetings; 2 media outlets sued for publishing news stories about the project; and 2 members of parliament sued for their speeches during parliamentary meetings. That last fact is the measure of the exposure — if parliamentary speech draws a suit, an ordinary resident's comment certainly can. Anyone campaigning on an Armenian extractive project should assume defamation exposure for ordinary public comment, keep records of the factual basis for every claim made, and take legal advice before posting rather than after being served. This is recorded plainly because listing funding opportunities alone would understate what this work costs here.

trackers.name: Caucasus Nature Fund — it matches the state budget, so that is the lever
trackers.desc: RECURRING CORE FUNDING, WHICH IS THE SCARCEST KIND. CNF was founded in 2007 by Conservation International, Germany's development ministry and WWF, and has a programme office in Yerevan supporting protected areas across Armenia, Azerbaijan and Georgia. Its purpose is long-term funding for operating costs, improved management and sustainable development — not one-off projects. THE MECHANISM IS THE ARGUMENT: it works through partnership with the three governments by matching, but not exceeding, the state budgets, so each side commits long-term. For an Armenian campaign that means arguing for a larger state protected-area budget is also arguing for more international money — the two move together, and the domestic budget line is the lever. ALSO PRESENT: UNEP and REC Caucasus run capacity development jointly with the Ministry of Environment, including on biodiversity strategies — programmes to attach to rather than apply to. HONEST GAP: no standing Armenian domestic grant programme with published eligibility for local community groups could be verified; what exists is a regional trust fund, international agency programmes, and organisations to partner with.

trackers.name: Leasing, not buying — how private conservation works in Armenia
trackers.desc: THE MECHANISM THAT HAS ACTUALLY WORKED HERE. Private conservation in Armenia has proceeded by leasing community-owned and state land for conservation rather than by purchase, with rangers employed from the local communities — the model behind the Caucasus Wildlife Refuge. Where buying is impossible, or politically impossible, a long lease plus local employment is the route to look at: it gives the community income and a role rather than presenting conservation as land being taken away. The same shape appears in Austria's Pachtvertrag fallback and China's entrusted management, so it is a transferable pattern. TO FIND PARTNERS: CANEECCA, the Eastern Europe, Caucasus and Central Asia network, lists Armenian organisations working on afforestation and reforestation, public participation and civic activism, advocacy and lobbying, organic farming and ecological education — useful both for co-applicants and for the letters of support that several funds in this map require.

trackers.name: Caucasus Nature Fund — matches the state park budget, so cutting the park costs the state euros
trackers.desc: THE LEVER HERE IS THE MATCHING RULE, NOT THE GRANT. CNF publishes an “up to 50 percent principle”: it matches, but never exceeds, what the state itself budgets for a protected area. Read that backwards and it is an argument you can put in writing to a ministry — every dram stripped from a park's operating budget, and every hectare degazetted out of it, strips matching European money with it. In Armenia CNF names five sites: Arpa Protected Landscape (formerly Gnishik), Dilijan National Park, Khosrov Forest State Reserve, Lake Arpi National Park and Zangezur Biosphere Complex. Region-wide it reports 21 parks, 850 park employees in 2023 and 850,707.1 hectares supported, against 70 rangers and 107,000 hectares in 2009. WHO TO CONTACT: CNF runs programme offices in Yerevan and Tbilisi with its head office in Frankfurt, and publishes a contact page and a named executive director at caucasus-naturefund.org/about_us/contact/. WHAT YOU CANNOT GET: a grant. CNF money goes to protected-area administrations under agreements with the national government, not to community groups, and there is no community application window — approach it as a funder of the rangers and monitoring that already police your area, and as a party with a financial interest in the park not shrinking. Its funding also pays for the biodiversity monitoring an objection needs, so ask the park administration what CNF-funded monitoring exists for your valley before commissioning your own. EXCLUSION WORTH KNOWING: CNF's mandate names Azerbaijan, but its published park list contains no Azerbaijani site and its own parks filter offers only Armenia and Georgia — do not assume an Azerbaijani community has this route.

trackers.name: Public Defender's Office — free representation DOES cover administrative cases, but only if you apply for it
trackers.desc: THIS IS THE INVERSION THAT MATTERS ACROSS THIS WHOLE REGION: ARMENIA'S FREE-LAWYER SYSTEM EXPRESSLY EXTENDS TO ADMINISTRATIVE AND CONSTITUTIONAL CASES, NOT JUST CRIMINAL ONES. A challenge to a permit, a designation or a state decision is an administrative case, so unlike Jordan — where the statutory right to free assistance reaches only defendants facing ten years or more — an Armenian community fighting a project is inside the system rather than outside it. BUT THE TRIGGER IS COMPLETELY DIFFERENT FROM THE CRIMINAL ONE AND THIS IS WHERE PEOPLE LOSE THE ROUTE: on criminal matters a public defender is assigned by decision of the body conducting the proceedings, whereas on civil, administrative and constitutional matters free legal aid is provided on the citizen's own application to the Head of the Public Defender's Office. Nobody will appoint you one. You apply, in the cases and under the procedure the law prescribes. THE GATE IS THE PERSON, NOT THE CASE: the Office states that on application, free legal aid goes to sixteen specified groups of people, leaving aside suspects and the accused who are covered on the proceeding body's demand. So the first question is not whether your case is strong but whether you fall inside one of those sixteen categories — establish that before drafting anything, because a strong case brought by an ineligible applicant goes nowhere. WHAT YOU CAN GET EVEN SHORT OF FULL REPRESENTATION: consultation, and the writing of claims, applications, complaints and other procedural documents of a legal nature. For a community that can argue its own case but cannot draft a filing, that is often the whole problem solved. The Office publishes its public defenders individually by name, so you can see who you would be dealing with, and complaints about the service go to the Head or the Deputy Heads with supervision by the Chairman of the Chamber of Advocates. Public defenders are advocates employed by the Office through competitive selection and paid from the state budget; the Chamber of Advocates describes itself on its own pages as an independent, professional, self-governed non-profit body. A stronger claim — that the Office answers to no state body at all — appears on a third-party directory rather than on the Chamber's own site, and it matters a great deal when your opponent is a ministry, so ask them to confirm it rather than relying on it. Pair this with EcoLur, already in this file, for the documentary record on Armenian mining and land conflicts.

trackers.name: TIAC — frame the mine as a public-resources and corruption case, not an ecology case, and its mandate reaches you
trackers.desc: THIS IS THE FRAMING DECISION THAT DETERMINES WHETHER ARMENIA'S BEST-RESOURCED LITIGATOR CAN TAKE YOUR FIGHT AT ALL. The Transparency International Anti-Corruption Center is not an environmental organisation, and an approach that leads with habitat or landscape may fall outside what it does. Its published aims are to promote the rule of law by pursuing proper law enforcement and the protection of human rights, and to protect public resources through responsible management of public property and finances — so a mine, quarry or development that involves state land, a licence granted irregularly, or public money is squarely inside its mandate when it is put that way. Its listed activities include strategic litigation of public interest issues and assistance to stakeholders in combatting corruption, alongside research, monitoring and evaluation of public policies. It also states that it maintains a principled opposition to government decisions or actions that threaten good governance, which is a written commitment worth quoting back when the decision-maker is a ministry. WHO TO CONTACT: 53 Aygedzor Street, Yerevan 0019; +374 10 569589, +374 10 569689, +374 96 000388. Founded in 2000 by Amalya Kostanyan as the Center for Regional Development, accredited as Transparency International's Armenian national chapter in October 2001, and reregistered under its present name in 2008. ONE CLAIM THIS ENTRY DOES NOT TREAT AS ESTABLISHED: that TIAC advocates specifically for improving Armenian mining policy and practice to meet high social and environmental standards. That appears on a development-coalition member profile rather than on transparency.am, so ask directly whether mining is a current programme before assuming it. WHAT IT IS NOT: a source of a free lawyer on demand. Strategic litigation means the organisation selects cases for their public-interest value, so expect to make the case that yours sets a precedent. For an appointed advocate under the state scheme use the Public Defender's Office, already in this file; for the documentary record on Armenian mining and land conflicts use EcoLur, also already here.

trackers.name: Armenian Environmental Front — before you join anything, know that the mining company filed fifteen suits against its critics
trackers.desc: READ THE LEGAL RISK FIRST, BECAUSE IT IS THE DEFINING FEATURE OF ARMENIAN MINING DISPUTES: Lydian International filed no fewer than fifteen lawsuits against dissenting voices over the Amulsar gold mine, in what monitors characterise as strategic litigation against public participation — suits brought to intimidate and exhaust critics rather than to win. Separately, police contacted a member of this initiative's coordinating board after the company complained that he and colleagues had threatened it. Armenian environmental defenders have also faced defamation and smear campaigns in local media. Assume the counter-suit is part of the plan, and get counsel lined up before you are visible, not after. WHAT THE ORGANISATION IS: a civil initiative rather than a registered service body, based at Spendiaryan 5, apartment 24, Yerevan, with a published join page. Its own framing is direct — it describes fast eco-colonisation of Armenia through foreign capital and local oligarchy, irrevocable loss of nature, and the resulting eco-migration from villages. WHAT IT HAS ACTUALLY DONE, WHICH IS WHY IT IS HERE: residents of Vayots Dzor blockaded the road to the Amulsar site continuously from May 2018, keeping construction vehicles off the mountain for roughly two years, with this initiative organising the national rallies that kept it politically alive. The blockade ended in August 2020 when the mine's newly hired security detail removed the defenders' trailers by force, with injuries and arrests. The EBRD later terminated funding and exited the project. THE OPENING THAT MOST CAMPAIGNS MISS, AND IT IS SPECIFIC TO THIS SITE: part of the mine lies inside an Emerald site designated under the Bern Convention, and a complaint was taken to the Bern Convention by EcoLur together with an international network. If your Armenian site carries an Emerald designation, that is a forum outside the domestic courts. Amulsar sits at the headwaters of the Arpa and Vorotan, beside reservoirs one of which feeds Lake Sevan, with confirmed uranium deposits in the project area. WHAT IT IS NOT: a law firm, a fund or a landholder. Pair it with EcoLur, already in this file, for the documentary record, and with the anti-corruption litigator recorded here for Armenia if the case can be framed as public property or irregular licensing. NAMING NOTE: it appears in international reporting both as Armenian Environmental Front and as Pan-Armenian Environmental Front; the Armenian name is the same body.

trackers.name: HCA Vanadzor — where to go when the company sues you or the police call, and it litigates as far as Strasbourg
trackers.desc: THIS IS THE ENTRY TO READ BEFORE YOU BECOME VISIBLE, NOT AFTER. Elsewhere in this file Armenia carries the record of a mining company filing fifteen lawsuits against critics of a single project, and of police contacting a campaigner after that company complained. This organisation publishes a Get Free Legal Advice page and runs a strategic litigation practice, and it is the standing answer to that situation. IT TAKES CASES TO THE EUROPEAN COURT OF HUMAN RIGHTS: it provides free legal assistance to victims of human rights violations and has extensive experience in strategic litigation including before the Strasbourg court, having assisted citizens to lodge applications there. Armenia is a Council of Europe member, so that route is real, and it is the escalation available when the domestic courts have been exhausted — which for a land defence facing an aggressive claimant may matter more than any domestic remedy. THE FRAMING POINT IS THE SAME ONE THIS FILE MADE FOR ARMENIA'S ANTI-CORRUPTION LITIGATOR, AND IT DECIDES WHETHER YOU GET HELP: this is a human rights organisation, not an environmental one. Its free legal assistance is directed at victims of rights violations and at socially vulnerable citizens, and its declared fields are legal support, monitoring, legal analysis and initiatives, and capacity building. A case presented as harm to a landscape may fall outside it; the same case presented as persecution of the people defending that landscape — the suits, the summons, the pressure — is squarely inside. Present the human facts. WHO AND WHERE: founded in March 1998 as a branch of the Helsinki Citizens' Assembly Armenian Committee, registered as an independent organisation in 2001; described as non-political, non-religious, non-commercial and independent, with a named long-serving president. Offices at 59 Tigran Mets Street in Vanadzor and on Komitas Avenue in Yerevan; hcav@hcav.am; telephones published on its own site. It also drafts legal acts, participates in amending legislation and maintains a hotline, and it reports to the Armenian Human Rights Defender and to international bodies. THE LIMITS: it is not an environmental expert, a funder or a landholder, and its capacity is finite — a figure of roughly four hundred people receiving legal aid annually appears in third-party sources rather than on its own site, so treat volume as a reason to approach early rather than late. Pair it with EcoLur for the documentary record on Armenian mining, the anti-corruption litigator here if the case can be framed as public property or irregular licensing, and the Public Defender's Office for an appointed advocate in an administrative matter.

trackers.name: World Land Trust — it exists to fund the purchase of land, and Armenia is its one named country in this region
trackers.desc: THIS IS THE ONLY ORGANISATION THIS FILE HAS FOUND ACROSS TWENTY-THREE COUNTRIES WHOSE STATED PURPOSE IS PROVIDING FUNDS FOR PARTNER ORGANISATIONS TO PURCHASE LAND AND ESTABLISH PERMANENT WILDLIFE RESERVES. It does not buy land itself and it does not work directly with communities — it funds a local partner organisation that does. In Armenia that partner is the foundation already recorded in this file, and the arrangement it funds is the answer to the question this whole region poses: how do you protect land when nobody can buy it. THE MODEL, IN WLT'S OWN WORDS ACROSS SEVERAL OF ITS PAGES: the communities CEDE LAND to the refuge under lease and are PAID, and those lease payments give them an income for village improvements. More than a dozen communities across Ararat and Vayots Dzor have been enlisted on that basis, safeguarding over 26,000 hectares within a refuge of some 30,000 — described by WLT as the only privately protected area in the South Caucasus, buffering a state reserve. AND THE JOBS ARE PART OF THE BARGAIN, NOT AN AFTERTHOUGHT: the rangers who patrol the refuge are employed from the local villages, doing daily patrols against poaching and fighting wildfires; a reforestation programme of 700,000 trees across 300 hectares is monitored over ten years by trained local staff, women from local communities among them. This is the same bargain this file has recorded in Lebanese Hima villages, Georgian biosphere buffer zones and a Turkish Ramsar lake — protection that pays the people living beside it is protection that lasts. WHAT A COMMUNITY OR ORGANISATION ELSEWHERE SHOULD TAKE FROM THIS: the money for land protection in this region does not come from domestic land trusts, because there are none. It comes from an international funder working through one local partner. The route is therefore to become or reach such a partner, not to look for a national equivalent. WLT also runs schemes letting individuals and companies fund acres directly and a carbon-balanced programme pairing offsets with habitat protection, which is how the money is raised. THE LIMITS ARE REAL: this is one country and one partner in this region, the refuge is in Ararat and Vayots Dzor, and nothing found shows WLT funding anywhere else in the Middle East, the Caucasus or Central Asia. Its global operation belongs elsewhere in this map. And note that WLT publishes the lease-and-pay model clearly while neither it nor the partner publishes the payment amounts — a community negotiating such a lease should treat the terms as something to establish, not assume.

trackers.name: My Forest Armenia — it secures land by community agreement rather than purchase, and it publishes why planting alone cannot work
trackers.desc: THE LAND ROUTE IS THE PART TO STUDY, BECAUSE IT INVOLVES NO PURCHASE. Its own account of preparing to plant is: drafting and signing agreements with the communities, preparing Environmental Impact Assessment documents, and obtaining final approval from the Ministry of Environment. Two parcels secured in Lori that way are described as 86 hectares and more than 300 hectares, and the land is then fenced. A community that wants land taken out of degradation and put under trees does not need anyone to buy it — it needs an agreement, an assessment and a ministry signature. AND THE SELECTION CRITERIA PUT THE COMMUNITY'S WISH ON THE LIST WITH THE SOIL: rainfall and its distribution through the year, soil quality, sun exposure, altitude, and — in its own words — the wish of the local community to have a new forest and to take care of it. If your village wants the forest, that is a stated criterion, not a courtesy. NOW THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST, AND THE ORGANISATION PUBLISHES IT AGAINST ITS OWN INTEREST: one per cent of Armenia is 30,000 hectares; planting runs at roughly 3,300 trees to the hectare; and at its own rate it would take 250 YEARS to raise Armenia's forest cover by one per cent. Read that before deciding where to put your effort. Planting cannot outrun clearance. Stopping the loss is the fast half of the work and restoration is the slow half, and an organisation honest enough to publish that arithmetic is one worth listening to on everything else. WHAT IT ACTUALLY RUNS: nurseries at several altitudes and locations — Debet, Gugark, and a 2.1 hectare site at Haghartsin in Tavush — plus a greenhouse built with the national agrarian university, growing many tree and shrub species from seed the team collects in local forests because large-scale quality seedlings were not otherwise available. It reports 16 permanent staff in Yerevan and Vanadzor, 31 in the nurseries and greenhouse, and up to 240 people hired locally each spring and autumn for planting and maintenance, training and employing rural communities as part of the method. Planting reached 426,000 trees in its second season and is reported at 910,000 in 2023, against a long-term aim of 5,000 hectares restored, concentrated in Lori where the loss is worst — that province is reported to have lost more than 1,000 hectares of tree cover between 2001 and 2018. Companies can fund a named forest through a named deputy director; individuals can give monthly. THE LIMIT: it restores, it does not object. It works with the environment ministry rather than against it and nothing shows it opposing a project. It also works alongside the older Armenian tree organisation recorded in this file.

trackers.name: Environmental Defender Law Center — pro bono lawyers, case funding, and defence for defenders facing retaliatory suits
trackers.desc: THIS FILE RECORDS A WARNING THAT ARMENIAN ENVIRONMENTAL CAMPAIGNERS FACE RETALIATORY LITIGATION, AND THIS ORGANISATION EXISTS FOR EXACTLY THAT SITUATION: alongside its casework it acts for individuals charged or imprisoned in politically motivated criminal prosecutions, and defends speech and protest critical of environmental harm. WHAT IT PROVIDES, WITHOUT CHARGE: lawyers, resources and grants. It enlists law firms around the world to work pro bono, screening cases from a lawyer's perspective before accepting them and then helping shape strategy. It runs a fund, created in 2010 and described as the only one of its type spanning the developing world, for the EXPENSES of public interest litigation against those responsible for resource development projects harming communities — the small sums that decide whether a case is brought at all and that foundations will not give on a one-case basis. AND IT WRITES THE INTERNATIONAL HALF OF THE ARGUMENT: it prepares and files briefs on international human rights law, including in cases seeking recognition of indigenous land rights, addressing pollution from resource projects, and asserting the participatory rights of communities affected by MINES AND DAMS — designed to dovetail with local lawyers arguing domestic law. It also has access to expert networks and has obtained scientific assistance for communities on numerous occasions. READ IT WITH THE ARMENIAN LEGAL BODIES ALREADY RECORDED HERE, which provide domestic representation and strategic litigation to the European Court; this adds funding, international briefing and expert access rather than duplicating them. THE LIMITS: developing countries only, cases of international significance where a strategy can be replicated, and no case of its own in Armenia or this region could be established. Founded 2003; funded entirely by foundation grants and individual donations.

trackers.name: Front Line Defenders — protection grants that pay for the defence when a company sues the campaigners
trackers.desc: THIS FILE CARRIES A WARNING THAT ARMENIAN ENVIRONMENTAL CAMPAIGNERS FACE RETALIATORY LITIGATION. THIS IS THE FUND THAT PAYS FOR THE DEFENCE: protection grants of up to €7,500 explicitly cover LEGAL FEES FOR DEFENDERS BEING JUDICIALLY HARASSED — alongside physical security for an individual or organisation, digital and communications security, medical fees for those attacked or made ill through their work, and family assistance where a defender is imprisoned or their family is at risk. A campaign that can absorb a retaliatory suit financially is far harder to silence with one. THERE IS A 24-HOUR EMERGENCY LINE WITH A RUSSIAN-SPEAKING OPTION and a secure encrypted email route, staffed to mobilise rapid international support — worth noting in advance of any confrontation rather than looking for it afterwards. It also runs temporary relocation, holistic and digital security training, and a rest and respite programme for defenders under sustained stress. WHAT IT WILL NOT DO: fund broader human rights work as opposed to the specific situation of a defender at risk; support defenders already in exile; or pay salaries, rent or other running costs. USE IT ALONGSIDE THE ARMENIAN LEGAL BODIES ALREADY RECORDED HERE, which provide representation and strategic litigation — this pays the bill and protects the person, which is a different function from arguing the case. Based in Dublin. THE LIMIT: nothing found records a case of its own in Armenia, and it publishes no country eligibility list; its service is described as open to defenders at risk with no stated geographic restriction.

trackers.name: Arnika — it samples your soil, water and your own body, has it analysed abroad, and comes back to tell you what it found
trackers.desc: THE REASON THIS MATTERS MORE THAN ANY REPORT: THE SAMPLES ARE ANALYSED OUTSIDE THE COUNTRY. Soil, dust, sediment, water and human biological samples are collected in the mining-affected villages and sent to the Czech Republic for laboratory analysis, which gives residents data that does not depend on a domestic laboratory, a domestic regulator or the company's own monitoring. That independence is the whole value. IT SAMPLES PEOPLE, NOT ONLY PLACES. One programme collected 55 soil and river sediment samples together with 83 BIOLOGICAL SAMPLES FROM LOCAL RESIDENTS across four regions, mapping how heavy metals travel from named gold mines, a processing plant and cyanide and tailings dams into the people living beside them. A later field mission collected 108 samples of soil, dust, sediment and human urine in the southern mining communities. Biomonitoring evidence of metals in residents' bodies is a different order of proof from a soil reading, and almost nothing else in this file produces it. AND THE RESULTS COME BACK TO THE VILLAGE. Public presentations are held in the affected communities, residents are given clear recommendations on reducing their own exposure in daily life — using local water sources, growing food, keeping livestock — and the partner organisations then support communities in USING THE DATA IN NEGOTIATIONS with local authorities, mining companies and national institutions, AND IN ENGAGING IN ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES. Data produced for the assessment process rather than for a journal is what a community actually needs. IT WORKS THROUGH TWO NAMED ARMENIAN PARTNERS, one of them the environmental news service already recorded in this map, the other a community mobilisation centre — so the route in is through Armenian organisations rather than a foreign address. It has worked in Lori since 2018 and in Syunik for years, and has convened discussion in Yerevan of international tools for pursuing polluters. IT ALSO NAMES THE STRUCTURAL POINT A MINING COMMUNITY SHOULD PUT IN WRITING: the profits from extraction flow abroad to investors while the environmental burden and the health risks stay with local people. THE LIMITS: it is a Czech organisation working on projects with external funding, so its presence depends on those projects continuing; it concentrates on mining-affected areas of Lori and Syunik and named northern and central regions rather than the whole country; and sampling happens on field missions rather than on demand. Ask when the next mission is and whether your community can be added, rather than expecting a laboratory service.

trackers.name: CCMS — founded by activists from ten villages, and it made a mining company admit its impact for the first time
trackers.desc: THE WIN IS THE MODEL, AND IT IS TWO STEPS. A family living beside an operating tailing dump took part in independent pollution research. This organisation then ran a PUBLIC DEMAND CAMPAIGN in their village in support of them — and the mining company ADMITTED FOR THE FIRST TIME THAT ITS ACTIVITIES IMPACT THE ENVIRONMENT and offered to help the family relocate. Evidence alone had not moved the company; evidence plus a public campaign naming a specific family did. This file records the sampling programme separately — the pairing is the point: get the data, then make a public demand for one identifiable household rather than a general complaint. The householder's own account is worth carrying too: he had no idea when he bought the house of the health risks of living near a tailing dump, or that the dump would resume operation. WHAT IT IS: a grassroots organisation established in 2009 in the Lori mining region and based in Alaverdi, FOUNDED BY ACTIVISTS FROM TEN DIFFERENT VILLAGES to promote civic participation in decision-making and in infrastructure development. It works on environmental protection, public health, human rights, youth and local development, through formal and informal education, civic engagement and support for civic projects, and it is explicit that its work includes OPPOSING THE OPENING OF NEW MINES. It has established active groups in communities and plans a school of activism for local community leaders. IT IS ALSO A ROUTE TO MONEY AND SUPPORT FOR YOUR OWN CAMPAIGN: it is the Armenian partner in a support programme run with a Czech organisation offering backing for civic campaigns and initiatives — ask what is currently open. And with its partners it escalated beyond the country, addressing United Nations special rapporteurs on human rights and the environment and on toxics on behalf of residents affected by mining and smelting. KNOW WHAT IT COSTS THEM, BECAUSE IT TELLS YOU WHAT IT MAY COST YOU: this organisation has been the subject of defamation campaigns in the media and of STRATEGIC LAWSUITS AGAINST PUBLIC PARTICIPATION BROUGHT BY MINING COMPANIES, which it regards as attempts to silence it. That is the exact circumstance the defender protection fund recorded elsewhere in this file exists for — its grants expressly cover legal fees for defenders facing judicial harassment. Read the two entries together before you begin, not after. THE LIMITS: it is regional rather than national, centred on Lori, and it is a mobilisation and education organisation rather than a litigator or a landholder. For the laboratory evidence, the sampling programme recorded here; for the documentary record on mining, the environmental news service; for a lawyer, the Armenian legal bodies already in this file.

trackers.name: Green Armenia — it publishes the mine case record and sued over the state loan guarantee
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SETTLEMENT IS ON THE AFFECTED-COMMUNITY LIST BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE, BECAUSE IT DECIDES WHETHER YOU MAY OBJECT AT ALL. In the case record this organisation publishes, residents of one village recognised as an affected community were able to appeal the mining permits — while THE LARGEST COMMUNITY NEARBY HAD NOT BEEN RECOGNISED AS AFFECTED BY THE STATE, so nobody living there could lawfully challenge those permits, whatever the impact on them. If your settlement is not on that list, getting it added is the first fight and everything else waits behind it. AND KNOW THAT AN ORGANISATION'S RIGHT TO BRING AN ENVIRONMENTAL CASE HAD TO BE WON: a court had refused to recognise organisations as plaintiffs in an earlier mine case; the law was amended; a judge excluded them from this one in 2016; and only FOUR YEARS LATER did the Court of Appeal restore the right of organisations to appeal on environmental issues and send the case back. Budget for that kind of delay, and note that the point may be contested again. ITS OWN CURRENT CASE ATTACKS THE MONEY RATHER THAN THE PERMIT: with an anti-corruption centre, a community support organisation and a group of citizens, it petitioned the Administrative Court to invalidate the government's decision to GUARANTEE A HUNDRED AND FIFTY MILLION DOLLAR LOAN to the mining company — arguing that if the company failed to repay, public funds would cover the debt. Challenging the financing decision rather than the environmental permit is a distinct route, and this file has recorded elsewhere that following the money reaches places an environmental objection cannot. IT ALSO PUBLISHES THE CASE HISTORY IN DETAIL — including that public hearings in the affected village were held with multiple violations and that those documents nonetheless became the basis for the project, and that the Administrative Court has already invalidated administrative acts concerning the expansion of the mining plot and changes to the permit period. A published, dated case record is what lets a new community see what was tried and what worked. NAME WARNING, AND IT IS SERIOUS: this file has documented a six-way collision on the name Green Armenia, including a dormant body whose founder died. Match on this domain, not on the name. THE LIMITS: it is an environmental organisation that litigates, not a law firm — it does not represent individuals, and the cases described are brought jointly with other organisations and citizens. Use it with the litigation-cost fund and the defender protection routes recorded here, because this file has also documented that the company in these proceedings filed at least fourteen actions against critics, including communities, lawyers and journalists.

trackers.name: Armenian Forests — led by an environmental lawyer, and it convened a public environmental court
trackers.desc: ITS DIRECTOR ESTABLISHED A PUBLIC ENVIRONMENTAL COURT IN WHICH ENVIRONMENTAL CASES HAVE BEEN HEARD, AND THE DECISIONS OF THAT COURT ARE SENT TO THE GOVERNMENT, THE MINISTRIES, THE PROSECUTOR'S OFFICE, THE INVESTIGATION COMMITTEE AND THE POLICE. This file recorded one round earlier that Armenian organisations were shut out of environmental proceedings for four years until an appeal court restored the right, and that a community the state has not designated as affected cannot lawfully challenge a permit at all. A CITIZENS' TRIBUNAL IS WHAT YOU CONVENE WHEN THE COURT IS CLOSED TO YOU: it produces a reasoned, public, dated decision that named officials must receive, even if nothing compels them to act. Nothing else in this payload records the tactic, and it is available to any community that can assemble credible people to hear evidence. IT IS LED BY A PRACTISING ENVIRONMENTAL LAWYER HOLDING A DOCTORATE IN ENVIRONMENTAL LAW — which is what Armenia's coverage in this file was missing, alongside twelve entries for mobilisation, protection, funding and contamination data. The organisation's stated work covers afforestation and reforestation, nature protection, ENGAGEMENT OF COMMUNITY MEMBERS IN DECISION-MAKING PROCESSES, protection of human rights, DRAFTING ENVIRONMENTAL LEGISLATION and ecological education — the drafting element being the same move this file recorded in northern Lebanon, where a body that could not obtain a protected area worked instead on the legal framework that would allow one. ITS COMPLAINTS HAVE BEEN FILED TOGETHER WITH IMPACTED LOCAL COMMUNITIES to challenge the authorities' decision authorising a gold mining operation, which is the pairing this map keeps finding: a community supplies the standing and the facts, a lawyer supplies the argument. KNOW WHAT IT HAS COST HER, BECAUSE IT TELLS YOU WHAT THIS WORK ATTRACTS: the mining company filed a defamation complaint against her personally in a Yerevan court for criticising the project and alleging undisclosed relations with authorities, one of a series of actions that international observers have described as judicial harassment of defenders, journalists and lawyers. Read this entry with the litigation-cost fund and the two defender protection routes recorded here before making contact. TWO PRACTICAL WARNINGS. It has no website; this entry points at its own public page, and its director's professional email appears in her published academic writing. AND DO NOT CONFUSE IT WITH A SIMILARLY NAMED YEREVAN REFORESTATION ORGANISATION RECORDED SEPARATELY IN THIS FILE — both work on Armenian forests, both are in the capital, and they are different bodies doing different things: the other plants and secures land, this one litigates and drafts.

trackers.name: reArmenia — public and diaspora fundraising, where the community you are defending is the asset
trackers.desc: THIS IS A ROUTE BY WHICH PEOPLE GIVE MONEY DIRECTLY TO A PROJECT, AND THIS MAP HAD NONE FOR THIS COUNTRY. It is a collaboration and fundraising platform used by local and pan-Armenian civil society organisations, and its reach extends to Armenian communities abroad — organisations from Javakhk and from France took part in a session it ran on how to raise money. A diaspora is a fundraising base that most communities in this region do not have, and it is reachable from a village. ITS DIRECTOR'S OWN ADVICE IS THE MOST USEFUL THING HERE, AND IT INVERTS HOW EVERY OTHER FUNDING ENTRY IN THIS FILE WORKS: public fundraising succeeds by BUILDING A COMMUNITY AND TREATING THAT COMMUNITY AS AN ASSET, because WITHOUT AN ACTIVE COMMUNITY IT IS IMPOSSIBLE TO SUCCEED IN PUBLIC FUNDRAISING. Grant applications require a community to fit a funder's priorities; public fundraising requires only that a community exists and can be mobilised — which a group defending its own land already has. Build the supporter list before you need the money. IT WORKS WITH THE KIND OF BODIES THIS FILE STRUGGLES TO FIND: the session it ran was attended by more than fifty people from local and pan-Armenian organisations, and the examples discussed included a VILLAGE DEVELOPMENT FUND raising money for a specific local facility. A named village fund with a concrete project is exactly the profile of a community body defending land, and it is the profile this platform is built for. PREPARE A SPECIFIC, COSTED PROJECT rather than a cause: platforms host projects, and donors give to a parcel of land, a survey, a legal fee or a nursery far more readily than to a campaign. TWO FURTHER ARMENIAN ROUTES EXIST AND ARE WORTH COMPARING BEFORE CHOOSING: one is the fundraising platform of an established relief foundation which states that A SUPPORTER COVERS ALL ITS ADMINISTRATIVE COSTS SO THE WHOLE OF EACH DONATION REACHES THE CAUSE, and invites people to send in project ideas; the other is a general Armenian crowdfunding site carrying individual campaigns, which offers to help turn a written appeal into a platform campaign. Check what each deducts and what each requires before committing. THE LIMITS: a platform is a channel, not a funder — nobody there raises the money for you, and a campaign that attracts no donors raises nothing. Its framing is development and collaboration, so an openly adversarial campaign against a named company may sit awkwardly; this file has recorded across the region that framing land defence as livelihood, heritage or restoration is usually what makes it fundable.

trackers.name: CASE — the coalition against abusive lawsuits, and the first place to go when critics start getting sued
trackers.desc: IT CONNECTS PEOPLE WHO HAVE BEEN SUED FOR SPEAKING OUT TO THOSE WHO CAN HELP THEM. A coalition of more than a hundred and twenty organisations across Europe and beyond, it provides resources on how to avoid being targeted and what to do if you are, and it DRAWS ON A WIDE NETWORK OF LAWYERS, NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS AND ADVOCACY BODIES TO SUPPLY LEGAL EXPERTISE, CAMPAIGN ASSISTANCE AND EMERGENCY FUNDING where circumstances permit. This file recorded for this country a mining company filing AT LEAST FOURTEEN ACTIONS against its critics — communities, lawyers and journalists among them — and the director of an environmental legal organisation sued personally for defamation over the same project. Until now this map offered those people nothing. KNOW THE SHAPE OF THE ATTACK BEFORE IT ARRIVES. Its analysis records that such suits are COMMONLY BROUGHT AGAINST INDIVIDUALS rather than organisations, that they typically rely on DEFAMATION LAWS, and that the MEDIAN AMOUNT CLAIMED IS AROUND FIFTEEN THOUSAND EUROS. That figure is the point: it is calibrated to ruin a named person, not to bankrupt an institution. A community should decide in advance who signs the letters, who speaks to journalists, and what happens to that person's household if a claim lands. AND KNOW WHAT SUCH SUITS ARE FOR: its own findings identify the subjects they silence as corruption, government actions, business practices AND ENVIRONMENTAL CONCERNS. A defamation claim over a mine is not an aberration; it is the standard instrument, documented more than thirteen hundred times in its database across dozens of countries. IT ALSO PUBLISHES SOMETHING USEFUL IF THE DEVELOPER'S OWN LAWYERS ARE THE INSTRUMENT: a report examining how the legal profession and court systems should PREVENT LAWYERS FROM ENABLING SUCH ABUSE and how institutions should respond when it occurs. That is the document to put in front of a bar association when complaining about the conduct of the other side's counsel. THE LIMITS: it is a coalition and a referral network, NOT A LAW FIRM — it will not represent you, and its emergency funding is explicitly conditional. Its focus is Europe, and while this country falls within the wider European human rights system, the European Union's anti-SLAPP directive does not apply here — so the protections its advocacy has won elsewhere are not automatically available. Use it alongside the litigation-cost fund and the two defender protection routes recorded separately in this file, which between them cover legal fees, relocation and physical safety.

trackers.name: Human Rights Defender — reaches private organisations, files to the Constitutional Court, and intervenes at Strasbourg
trackers.desc: ITS REMIT REACHES BEYOND THE STATE, WHICH ALMOST NONE OF ITS COUNTERPARTS IN THIS REGION DO. Under the Constitution it is an INDEPENDENT OFFICIAL who observes the maintenance of human rights and freedoms by STATE AND LOCAL SELF-GOVERNMENT BODIES AND OFFICIALS — AND, IN CASES PRESCRIBED BY LAW, BY ORGANISATIONS. Where a company rather than a ministry is the problem, that clause is worth establishing precisely: ask which cases the law prescribes. IT GOES TO COURT, IN TWO DIRECTIONS. It submits SPECIAL POSITIONS — amicus curiae — TO THE CONSTITUTIONAL COURT, a practice running since 2016, publishing summaries in Armenian and English; the issues examined have included THE STATE DUTY CHARGED DURING ADMINISTRATIVE TRIALS AND EXEMPTION FROM IT. Court fees are among the commonest reasons a community abandons a case, and an institution that has already litigated that question is one to approach about it. AND WHERE NECESSARY IT DRAWS UP THIRD-PARTY INTERVENTIONS IN COMPLAINTS AGAINST THIS COUNTRY AT THE EUROPEAN COURT OF HUMAN RIGHTS, and submissions to the Council of Europe's Committee of Ministers. That is a route out of the domestic system entirely, and this file has recorded international accountability bodies for many countries here without being able to name a domestic institution that will help you reach one. IT CAN ALSO REQUIRE AND OBTAIN FROM STATE AND LOCAL SELF-GOVERNMENT BODIES AND OFFICIALS THE INFORMATION NECESSARY FOR ITS WORK — the disclosure power a community lacks. AND ON THE QUESTION OF WHETHER A STATE-LINKED BODY IS REALLY INDEPENDENT, THERE IS AN EXTERNAL VERDICT RATHER THAN THIS FILE'S OPINION: IT HOLDS A STATUS FROM THE GLOBAL ALLIANCE OF NATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS INSTITUTIONS, THE TOP ACCREDITATION GRADE, and it belongs to the European network of such institutions and the international ombudsman institute. It is elected by parliament for a six-year term and has operated since 2004. THE LIMITS: it contributes to the restoration of violated rights and improves legal acts — it does not represent parties, and an amicus position is an opinion rather than advocacy. Its reach over organisations is limited to cases the law prescribes, which must be checked rather than assumed.

trackers.name: e-draft — read why proposals like yours were refused, before you write one
trackers.desc: IT PUBLISHES THE REASONS PROPOSALS WERE REJECTED, WHICH NOTHING ELSE IN THIS FILE'S SURVEY OF CONSULTATION SYSTEMS DOES. On any draft you can view the posted text, the PROPOSALS THAT WERE SUBMITTED, THE SUMMARY SHEET OF THOSE PROPOSALS, WHICH WERE ACCEPTED, AND THE JUSTIFICATIONS FOR NOT ACCEPTING THE REST. Read those refusals before writing anything. They tell you which arguments this system absorbs and which it discards, and on what stated grounds — which is the difference between guessing and aiming. THE SITE IS THE SINGLE PLACE WHERE DRAFT NORMATIVE LEGAL ACTS DEVELOPED BY GOVERNMENT AGENCIES ARE POSTED, and it exists to let agencies present drafts publicly, run public discussions online, and bring civil society into law-making. You can search drafts, FOLLOW A DRAFT'S SUBSEQUENT PROGRESS, and — once registered — SUBMIT PROPOSALS OF YOUR OWN. There is an English interface alongside the Armenian one. ONE HARD RULE TO DIARISE: PUBLIC DISCUSSIONS RUN FOR AT LEAST FIFTEEN DAYS. That is a floor, not a promise of more, so check the closing date on the draft itself the day you find it. AND THERE IS A BODY ALREADY IN THIS MAP THAT INTERVENES HERE. The human rights defender recorded separately for this country has objected to a draft posted on this platform on the grounds that NO ASSESSMENT OF POSSIBLE IMPACTS AND RISKS HAD BEEN PRESENTED AND THAT PROPER PUBLIC AWARENESS WORK AND DISCUSSIONS WITH STAKEHOLDERS HAD NOT BEEN CARRIED OUT. Those are exactly the failures a community meets, and they can be put to that institution about a draft rather than only about a decision — which is earlier and cheaper. NOW THE HONEST LIMIT, TAKEN FROM THE SAME REPORTING: IN THAT CASE THE DRAFTERS DID NOT RETREAT, even though the justice ministry had also given a negative opinion. A member of a civic initiative that uses the platform regularly describes it as worth having and says proposals can be written, while holding that the system could be better. PUBLISHING A REASON FOR REFUSING AN ARGUMENT IS NOT THE SAME AS ACCEPTING IT — treat the platform as the place to create a documented record that an objection was made and answered, which is what later challenges are built on. PRACTICAL NOTE: an updated version of the site was launched in October, with a report-a-problem tool and a ministry hotline for technical faults; older links to the platform may not behave as expected.

trackers.name: Chamber of Advocates offices directory — find the firm that does this work, and learn who the other side will use
trackers.desc: THE BAR PUBLISHES A DIRECTORY OF LAW OFFICES WITH THEIR PRACTICE AREAS, AND THAT IS THE LITERAL ANSWER TO THE QUESTION OF WHERE TO FIND AN ATTORNEY. Firms are described by what they actually do — including REGULATORY MATTERS IN MINING, ENERGY, UTILITIES AND REAL ESTATE, and litigation practices presented as among the leading ones in the country for LANDMARK LITIGATION AND ARBITRATION. This payload records bar associations, legal clinics, assignment duties and legal aid across the region; what it has rarely recorded is a way to identify A PARTICULAR FIRM THAT HANDLES THE SUBJECT OF YOUR DISPUTE. NOW THE HONEST PART, BECAUSE IT DECIDES HOW YOU USE THIS. FIRMS DESCRIBED THAT WAY MOSTLY ACT FOR COMPANIES — the mining and energy regulatory work is done for the developers, not against them. That makes the directory useful in two ways rather than one. FIRST, IT TELLS YOU WHO THE OTHER SIDE IS LIKELY TO HIRE, which is worth knowing before a meeting rather than after. SECOND, AND MORE USEFUL: THIS FILE RECORDED IN ANOTHER COUNTRY'S ADVOCACY LAW THAT A LAWYER WHO HAS BEEN CONSULTED ON A DISPUTE — EVEN INFORMALLY, EVEN BY WAY OF OPINION — IS BARRED, TOGETHER WITH EVERYONE IN THEIR OFFICE, FROM LATER ACTING AGAINST THE PERSON WHO CONSULTED THEM. Whether the same rule applies here must be CHECKED WITH THE CHAMBER RATHER THAN ASSUMED, but if it does, an early conversation with the leading mining-regulatory firm is not only a way to get advice — it may remove them from the other side. KEEP A RECORD OF WHO YOU SPOKE TO, WHEN, AND WHAT YOU SHOWED THEM. SEVERAL OF THE FIRMS LISTED BELONG TO INTERNATIONAL LAW FIRM NETWORKS AND COOPERATE WITH FIRMS IN OTHER JURISDICTIONS — which matters for the routes recorded separately in this file that are pursued in a company's home country rather than here. THE LIMITS. These are private firms and they charge; the directory lists no environmental specialism as such, so you are matching on mining, energy, land and administrative litigation instead. The chamber is a professional body that regulates advocates, not an advocate for anyone. Use it with the free legal channels already recorded for this country — the human rights defender who files court positions, the anti-SLAPP coalition, and the legal empowerment funding — and note that this country has documented judicial harassment and a defamation campaign brought against environmental defenders by a mining company, so choosing counsel who has faced that before matters more than usual.

trackers.name: Center for Ecological-Noosphere Studies — the academy centre that measured the contamination
trackers.desc: THIS IS THE CENTRE WHOSE MEASUREMENTS ENTERED THE PUBLIC ARGUMENT ABOUT MINING IN THIS COUNTRY. This file recorded that a National Academy of Sciences centre produced figures showing SURFACE RADIOACTIVITY EXCEEDING THE PERMISSIBLE LEVEL BY MORE THAN THREE AND A HALF TIMES in a mining region, and that campaigners cited them publicly — but the centre could not then be named. IT IS THE CENTER FOR ECOLOGICAL-NOOSPHERE STUDIES OF THE NATIONAL ACADEMY OF SCIENCES, AND IT HAS HELD A UNESCO CHAIR ON EDUCATION FOR SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT SINCE 2011. THAT COMBINATION IS RARE AND IT IS THE WHOLE VALUE: A NATIONAL ACADEMY INSTITUTE, WITH INTERNATIONAL STANDING THROUGH A UNESCO CHAIR, WHICH HAS ALREADY PRODUCED CONTAMINATION MEASUREMENTS THAT WERE USED AGAINST A DEVELOPMENT PROPOSAL. This payload has said in almost every country that communities can describe harm and cannot afford to prove it. Here is an institution in this country that has done the proving, and whose figures were credible enough to be quoted in a national argument. WHAT TO ASK FOR: whether the centre holds existing measurements for your area, what its published work says about soils, water or radioactivity near a proposed or operating site, and what a baseline survey would involve. EXISTING DATA IS THE FIRST ASK — a measurement already taken and published costs nothing to obtain and cannot be dismissed as commissioned by objectors. AND ITS CHAIR SUBJECT IS THE OPENING. A chair in education for sustainable development is mandated to teach and to reach beyond the academy; the chairs programme describes such posts as BRIDGEBUILDERS BETWEEN ACADEMIA, CIVIL SOCIETY AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES, so an approach by residents falls inside its stated purpose. THE LIMITS. It is a state academy institute, funded accordingly, and its outputs are research and teaching rather than advocacy — it will not campaign, and it will not appear for you. And the source used here is a UNESCO listing of chairs rather than the centre's own site, so CONFIRM ITS CURRENT ADDRESS AND WHETHER THE CHAIR IS STILL HELD BEFORE WRITING. Use it with the chamber of advocates' offices directory and the anti-SLAPP coalition recorded separately for this country: the centre measures, the firm argues, and the coalition covers you if the measuring makes you a target.

trackers.name: Civil society map — find the organisation working on heritage or community development in your own district
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING IN THIS MAP RUNS TO TWENTY ENTRIES — LAWYERS, ANTI-CORRUPTION WATCHDOGS, TREE-PLANTING BODIES, LAND FUNDS, POLLUTION TESTING, PROTECTION GRANTS — AND NOT ONE ROUTE TO GETTING A PLACE RECOGNISED OR DESIGNATED. That is the largest single gap in an otherwise strong listing, and two searches failed to reach a working heritage organisation here. THIS IS THE TOOL THAT LETS YOU FIND ONE YOURSELF. IT IS A MAP OF CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, SEARCHABLE BY FIELD OF WORK, WITH EACH ENTRY GIVING THE ORGANISATION'S MISSION AND USUALLY ITS FOUNDING YEAR. AMONG THE FIELDS IT USES ARE CULTURE, CULTURAL EDUCATION, INTANGIBLE CULTURAL HERITAGE AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT — so the category this file has been arguing for since R376, heritage that lives in practices rather than monuments, IS A FILTER YOU CAN ACTUALLY APPLY HERE. HOW TO USE IT PROPERLY: FILTER BY FIELD AND BY YOUR OWN REGION, NOT BY THE CAPITAL. An organisation already working in your district has the standing, the contacts and the local knowledge that a larger body in the capital will lack, and it is far likelier to answer. Read the mission statements before writing — this file has found repeatedly that a body will help with what its own stated objects cover and refuse what they do not. WHAT TO ASK FOR ONCE YOU HAVE FOUND ONE: whether it will document what you are trying to protect; whether it will apply jointly with you for funding, since almost every window recorded in this file requires a registered applicant; and whether it will put your subject before an authority in its own name. THOSE ARE THE THREE THINGS AN ESTABLISHED ORGANISATION CAN GIVE THAT AN UNREGISTERED GROUP CANNOT GET ALONE. ON THE DESIGNATION QUESTION ITSELF, WHICH THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING STILL LACKS: the culture ministry operates an agency for the protection of monuments of history and culture, and maintains an intangible cultural heritage section. THAT IS THE DESIGNATING SIDE, AND A COMMUNITY SEEKING PROTECTED STATUS WILL END UP THERE — but this file has not yet verified how a citizen initiates such a request here, and says so rather than guessing. THE LIMITS, PLAINLY. A DIRECTORY IS ONLY AS CURRENT AS ITS LAST UPDATE AND THE PAGE REACHED CARRIES AN OLDER DATE — verify that any organisation you find still operates before relying on it. It lists bodies by mission, not by track record, so it cannot tell you which of them has ever fought a development. And it is a finding aid, not an ally: it will not act, fund or advise.

trackers.name: Treaty compliance committee — an ordinary person can file against the state, and its findings already cover land-use decrees
trackers.desc: THIS MAP RECORDS THIS TREATY'S NATIONAL INFORMATION CENTRES IN FIVE COUNTRIES. IT HAS NEVER RECORDED THE BODY THAT HEARS COMPLAINTS AGAINST THE STATES THEMSELVES — AND THE RULE IS THAT COMMUNICATIONS MAY BE BROUGHT BY ONE OR MORE MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC. NO ORGANISATION, NO LAWYER AND NO STANDING REQUIREMENT: a person may file. THERE IS A LIVE DEADLINE: COMMUNICATIONS RECEIVED BY THE SECRETARIAT BY 28 SEPTEMBER 2026 GO TO THE COMMITTEE MEETING IN THE WEEK OF 9 TO 13 NOVEMBER 2026 — provided they are complete, in the REQUIRED FORMAT, and need no translation. Submissions may be in English, French or Russian, and the secretariat will translate the latter two — BUT A SUBMISSION NEEDING TRANSLATION WILL MISS THAT CUT-OFF, so filing in English buys months. WHY THIS MATTERS PARTICULARLY HERE: A FINDING IN A CASE AGAINST THIS COUNTRY ESTABLISHED THAT STAND-ALONE GOVERNMENTAL DECREES RELATING TO LAND USE AND PLANNING ARE ENVIRONMENTAL INFORMATION that must be disclosed. That is the exact document a community is refused when it asks what has been decided about its ground — and there is a ruling saying it must be handed over. Its findings have also treated feasibility studies, financial agreements, RENTAL CONTRACTS FOR LAND ADMINISTERED BY A STATE FORESTRY FUND, and raw uncalibrated monitoring data as environmental information. WHAT GETS A SUBMISSION THROWN OUT, FROM ITS OWN DECISIONS: BEING ANONYMOUS; abuse of the right to complain; being manifestly unreasonable; USING THE PROCEDURE TO RE-RUN LITIGATION YOU LOST AT HOME; duplicating a communication already before it; being brought by an organ of the state; AND — the commonest and most avoidable — BEING ACCOMPANIED BY INSUFFICIENT INFORMATION TO CORROBORATE THE CLAIM. Attach the refusal letters, the dates, the notices and what you asked for. A thin file fails at admissibility, not on the merits. THE HARD LIMIT, STATED BY THE COMMITTEE ITSELF: THE PROCEDURE EXISTS TO IMPROVE A STATE'S COMPLIANCE AND IS NOT A REDRESS PROCEDURE FOR VIOLATIONS OF INDIVIDUAL RIGHTS. It will not quash a permit or compensate you. What it produces is findings and recommendations against the state, monitored over years — which is slow, public, and useful precisely because a government that has been found non-compliant on public participation is easier to hold in the next case. USE IT WITH the national information centre and the environmental lawyers recorded separately for this country, and note that this file records here the coalition against abusive lawsuits — which matters, because filing internationally is one of the few steps that is hard to sue you for.

trackers.name: EPBC Act Public Portal — federal referrals
trackers.desc: Australia's public list of every project referred for federal environmental approval under the EPBC Act (administered by the new National EPA from mid-2026), with each referral's documents and a public comment window. You CAN get: every proposed action touching nationally protected matters — the proponent, location, documents, decisions, and 10 business days to comment on whether it's a 'controlled action'. You CAN'T get: projects with only state-level impacts — those sit with state EPAs. For activists: the comment window opens the moment a referral is published, so watching this portal for your region is how campaigns get ahead of a mine or development while the federal decision is still open.

trackers.name: Australian Government Register of Lobbyists
trackers.desc: Federal register of third-party lobbyists under the Lobbying Code of Conduct. — Holds to account: lobbyists & influence-seekers — find who is lobbying whom, and meetings held.

trackers.name: Australian Government Register of Lobbyists
trackers.desc: Public register of third-party lobbyists and clients who contact Australian Government ministers and officials. — Holds to account: lobbyists & influence-seekers — find who is lobbying whom, and meetings held.

trackers.name: Foreign Influence Transparency Scheme
trackers.desc: Register giving the public visibility of activities undertaken on behalf of foreign principals to influence government and politics. — Holds to account: lobbyists & influence-seekers — find foreign influence, funding and agents.

trackers.name: National Legal Aid (Australia)
trackers.desc: Peak body representing the eight state and territory Legal Aid Commissions, with national access-to-justice data. · Find here: the network of Australia's state and territory legal-aid commissions. IT DOES NOT TAKE APPLICATIONS — go to your state or territory commission. National Legal Aid represents the eight independent Legal Aid Commissions and their directors; the commissions are independent statutory bodies and NLA is a peak body for policy, advocacy and national projects. The national name is the most findable and the least useful — the same pattern recorded here for Canada's 13 provincial plans. THE FINDING THAT MATTERS FOR LAND WORK: NLA's own budget submission records that disaster response legal assistance has become a specialised area and an expansive area of law, expressly including insurance, housing and tenancy, grants, environmental and planning issues and income support. That is a named, separately funded stream in which planning and environmental matters are an express component — where general civil legal aid would not reach an environmental question, a post-disaster framing may. New South Wales, Victoria and Western Australia have received funding to deliver disaster response legal services, each state delivering differently on a place-based approach. BUT THE FUNDING IS DESCRIBED AS TEMPORARY and only three states are named — ask whether a service is currently operating. FOR NON-DISASTER ENVIRONMENTAL WORK, ASK ABOUT COMMUNITY LEGAL CENTRES: some CLCs specialise in particular areas of law, including environmental law, and the commissions administer the Community Legal Services Program funding — Victoria Legal Aid alone funds 42 CLCs. Ask your commission which CLC in your state specialises in environmental law; it administers the funding and will know — a more productive question than asking it to take the case. WHO WILL DO THE WORK: over 70 percent of approved legal aid cases are assigned to external practitioners under a mixed delivery model — but there are falling rates of private practitioners willing to take legal aid work due to disproportionately low remuneration, especially in regional and remote communities, which is where most land disputes are. The Justice on the Brink report found $484 million more per year is needed and the commissions critically under-resourced for over a decade.

trackers.name: Bush Heritage Australia — buying land for conservation
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a national not-for-profit that BUYS bushland outright to protect it permanently — 44 reserves covering over 1.4 million hectares, bought, gifted or bequeathed, each locked down with a conservation covenant that binds every future owner in perpetuity (no subdivision, no clearing, no building). USE IT: if land you are trying to save has outstanding conservation value, pitch it to them as an acquisition target, or partner with them on a purchase.

trackers.name: Australian Government (DCCEEW) — conservation organisations directory
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the federal environment department's own list of the conservation organisations that buy and manage land for the National Reserve System — Bush Heritage, Australian Wildlife Conservancy, Tasmanian Land Conservancy, Trust for Nature and others. USE IT: the official starting point for finding which body might acquire or covenant the land you are defending.

trackers.name: Environmental Defenders Office (EDO) — public-interest environmental law
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the largest environmental legal centre in the Australia-Pacific and an accredited Community Legal Centre — runs litigation for community groups defending their area from destructive development, and gives free expert legal advice. Its lawyers have fought some of Australia's biggest environmental battles, from the Adani mine to drilling in the Great Australian Bight. WHO IT SUITS: community groups, farmers, Traditional Owners and residents anywhere in Australia or the Pacific — never proponents. If you are not yet at the litigation stage, their online Legal Help Gateway carries free fact sheets.

trackers.name: Australian Wildlife Conservancy (AWC)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: acquires land and partners with other landholders to establish sanctuaries for threatened wildlife — the largest private owner and manager of land for conservation in Australia, covering 31 sanctuaries and partnership sites across more than 6.5 million hectares. USE IT: pitch a threatened parcel with high wildlife value as an acquisition or partnership target.

trackers.name: National Native Title Tribunal — future acts and Indigenous land use agreements
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Tribunal mediates and arbitrates the FUTURE ACT process — the statutory procedure triggered when a government proposes to grant a mining tenement, exploration licence or other interest over land where native title exists or is claimed. Native title parties get procedural rights: notification, a right to be consulted, and in defined cases a right to negotiate, with s. 31 agreements recorded. WHO IT SUITS: this is a right to be AT THE TABLE and to negotiate, not a general veto — be precise about which it is in a given case. The Tribunal also publishes dedicated guidance for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, mining and exploration, cultural heritage and land acquisitions.

trackers.name: GrantConnect via DCCEEW — how to catch every Commonwealth environment grant
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: individual Australian environment grant rounds open and close constantly — the Environment Restoration Fund ran 2019-2023, the Communities Environment Program closed in 2019 — so chasing a named programme is the wrong strategy. ALL Australian Government grant opportunities are published on GRANTCONNECT, the Commonwealth's grants information system, where you can register free and set a self-defined notification profile covering both live and FORECAST opportunities. WHO IT SUITS: any Australian community or environment group. HOW IT DIFFERS: the forecast feed is the real advantage — it tells you a round is coming before it opens, which is the only way to have a proposal ready in time. Funding continues through the Natural Heritage Trust, a $1.1 billion commitment running to the end of 2027-28.

trackers.name: National Landcare Program — Environment Small Grants
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: grants of $5,000 to $50,000 for projects improving the local environment through natural resource management, COVERING UP TO 100% OF PROJECT COSTS — no matching contribution required, which is unusual and makes this reachable for groups with no reserves. Eligible activities include weed treatment, pest and disease management, fencing, erosion management, revegetation, access management, community education, Indigenous land and sea country planning, and recording Indigenous ecological knowledge. WHO IT SUITS: community and environment groups. HOW IT DIFFERS: the 100% cost coverage and the explicit inclusion of Indigenous knowledge and country planning set it apart from co-funded programmes. Check the current guidelines — rounds and amounts change.

trackers.name: Landcare Australia — grants
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a national body that works with governments, corporate partners, philanthropic organisations and donors to build grants programmes for hands-on environmental projects — habitat restoration, sustainable land management, biodiversity. WHO IT SUITS: landcare and community groups doing on-ground work rather than campaign or legal work. HOW IT DIFFERS: rounds are intermittent and the site states plainly when nothing is open, so subscribe to the newsletter rather than checking hopefully; the money is raised from partners, so timing follows their cycles, not a government calendar.

trackers.name: DCCEEW — revolving funds by state and territory
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the federal environment department's own directory of the state-based revolving funds — the bodies that buy conservation land, covenant it and sell it on so the capital can be reused. Lists the responsible organisation and contact details for New South Wales, Queensland, South Australia, Tasmania and Victoria. USE IT: the fastest way to find the acquiring body for your state, and the route to South Australia's Nature Foundation, which is named here. ONE CAUTION: the directory carries at least one transposed web address for a listed fund, so use the phone numbers and email addresses to confirm, or search the organisation's name directly, rather than typing a URL straight off the page.

trackers.name: Bush Heritage — what a conservation covenant actually prohibits
trackers.desc: READ THIS BEFORE SIGNING OR PROPOSING A COVENANT: a conservation covenant prohibits subdivision, building (except in very limited locations), removal of native vegetation, interference with native animals and their habitats, disposal of non-degradable waste, and interference with natural watercourses and wetlands. It also compels the owner to protect ecological integrity, control feral animals and weeds, manage fire and erosion, carry out ongoing monitoring, and use local seed stock for any revegetation — so it is an obligation as well as a shield. Where land is held on a long-term Crown lease the covenant holds for the life of the lease and is easily renewed, which makes it substantial protection rather than a gesture. USE IT: the prohibition on subdivision and building is what stops a future owner developing the land, and it binds them, not just the person who signs.

trackers.name: Tasmanian Land Conservancy Revolving Fund — buy, covenant, resell
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a science-based non-government organisation running a revolving fund. It buys property with significant natural values on the open market, registers a Conservation Covenant on the title under the Tasmanian Nature Conservation Act 2002 in perpetuity, then puts the property back up for sale, with the proceeds returning to the fund to buy the next one.
