ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Snowchange Cooperative — buys damaged land on the open market and rewilds it (Finland)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a Finnish cooperative that buys peatlands and forests damaged by peat production and intensive forestry, on the open market, and restores them. Its Landscape Rewilding Programme began in 2018 and its own account by 2025 is 8,500 hectares owned outright and land concessions offered over more than 60,000 hectares, across five main catchment areas — with a later figure of 10,000 hectares owned. Over 178 sites, including Sámi sites. THE CASE THAT SHOWS THE WHOLE ROUTE, AND IT IS THE MOST USEFUL SINGLE EXAMPLE IN THIS FILE: Linnunsuo was a former peat production site responsible for fish kills in the Jukajoki river in 2010 and 2011. Snowchange bought the 110 hectares from Vapo, Finland's largest peat industry company, in April 2017 after a year of negotiation, funded by a €75,000 loan from Rewilding Europe Capital. It became a strict IUCN protected area that November. A second loan of €200,000 in late 2018 paid for a further 72 hectares next door, taking the site to 182. A community bought a damaged site from the company that damaged it, with borrowed money, and had it protected within seven months. WHY IT WORKS WITHOUT DISPLACING PEOPLE: Linnunsuo is co-managed so that a limited harvest of water birds by Selkie hunters continues, and the hunters help control invasive mink and raccoon dog. Its sites are registered as Indigenous and Community Conserved Areas, its stated method is that communities guide the work through collaborative management, that Indigenous women lead decision-making on their own territory, and that no decision is made without the consent of the affected community. Where it does not own, it negotiates land use agreements with private owners on what restoration will happen. WHAT TO BRING IT: drained peatland, a ditched forest, a river catchment damaged by peat extraction or forestry — and ideally one where the damage is documented, because that is what made the Vapo purchase possible. Finland has over five million hectares of drained peatland; this is the organisation that treats that as a supply of buyable sites rather than a loss.

trackers.name: Laji.fi — anyone can request the hidden data, and you can attach a map of the planning area
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Suomen Lajitietokeskus (FinBIF), which assembles observations from many Finnish species databases — from individual enthusiasts, citizen science projects, authorities and collections — and publishes them openly. Records can be entered through Vihko and Mobiilivihko, which take single observations with photographs and fetch place and time automatically. Finland's bucket held a funder, an acquirer and a legal service, and nothing on the record. THE TWO-TIER STRUCTURE, and it is the part that decides whether you find anything: sensitive records are karkeistettu — blurred — according to a list compiled by an authority working group, covering some but not all threatened species, chosen by assessing how much threat disturbance or collecting poses. For blurred records the public portal does not show the exact place, the date, the observer's name or several other fields; in some cases both place and time are coarsened, to 10 km and one year. A closed data store holds the exact, unblurred detail of every observation, browsable by Finnish authorities that have signed an agreement for the authority portal. AND HERE IS THE ROUTE MOST COMMUNITIES WILL NOT KNOW ABOUT: anyone can make a data request (aineistopyyntö) for sensitive data, from the public portal, giving a justified reason — and the owner of each dataset decides case by case. The request system asks the applicant to state the justification, and an applicant can be asked to complete the application by attaching, for example, a map of the planning area (kaavoitusalue). Land-use planning is written into the process as a reason people ask. You can choose to receive the data as a table or via an API for three months or one year. THE LEGAL BASIS TO CITE OR EXPECT: the blurring rests on the Finnish Act on the Openness of Government Activities, section 24, which makes secret documents containing information on threatened animal or plant species or on the protection of valuable natural areas if disclosure would endanger the protection of that species or area. That is the test — endangering protection — so a request aimed at protecting the site is arguing with the grain of the exemption, not against it.

trackers.name: Kunta- ja Järjestö-Helmi — 95 per cent if volunteers do the work (paused, read on)
trackers.desc: STATUS FIRST, BECAUSE IT MATTERS: there was no application round in 2025 and one is probably not being held in 2026–2027 either. The scheme is filed anyway because the Helmi programme runs to 2030, rounds are opened by ministry decision as need arises, and the terms below are the clearest statement of what a Finnish volunteer group can be paid for. THE CLAUSE THAT IS UNIQUE IN THIS SWEEP: the standard grant share can be raised — for special reasons up to 95 per cent — and the guidance names as a justification the project's measures being carried out to a significant extent by voluntary work, such as talkoot organised by associations. Significant natural values requiring urgent management also count. Volunteer labour raises the grant rate rather than reducing it. No other fund in twenty-eight says so. WHO MAY APPLY: municipalities, joint municipal authorities and other municipally owned actors, associations and foundations, water cooperatives, and joint water area shareholders' collectives. Joint projects are allowed, the grant going to a lead applicant who administers on everyone's behalf — though all participants must meet the requirements. WHAT IT PAYS FOR, INCLUDING THE PAPERWORK: concrete restoration, repair and nature management — and projects may include inventories, plans and permit processes that firmly support the management measures, where those measures are also carried out in the project or have other demonstrable funding and timetable. Purchased services, equipment and supplies are eligible. THE LIMITS, RECORDED PLAINLY: the grant is directed primarily at land owned by municipalities; sites on other owners' land are possible but need arrangements securing the management and its continuation. In forested habitats the grant is given only on protected areas. Built stormwater wetlands are excluded, as is overlap with agri-environment contract obligations. AND THE PROGRAMME BEHIND IT: Helmi 2021–2030 protects and restores mires, birdwaters, traditional biotopes, forest habitats and small waters, and its measures rest on landowners' voluntariness. One round drew 70 applications; 42 were funded with 2.35 million euro.

trackers.name: ymparistolaki.fi — a Finnish firm specialised in environmental and property law since 1994
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: a specialised Finnish asianajotoimisto with experience in environmental and real property law at national and EU level, acting for companies, public bodies and private property owners, providing legal services since 1994. THE SERVICE LIST, WHICH READS LIKE A COMMUNITY'S PROBLEM SET: kaavakonsultointi (plan consultancy), KAAVAVALITUKSET (appeals against plans), rakennusluvat, poikkeusluvat (exemption permits), and the legal problems of shoreline building; permit applications and valitusasiat — appeal matters — and compensation questions relating to permits and damage situations; plus compensation for environmental damage, and soil and groundwater remediation liabilities. Finland had a Vilnius-style legal clinic route and the Laji.fi data body but no named practitioner; this is one, and appeals against plans is its second listed service. WHY THAT MATTERS IN FINLAND SPECIFICALLY: the plan — maakunta-, yleis- or asemakaava — is where land use is settled, and this firm sells consultancy on the plan as well as litigation against it.

trackers.name: Finnish planning-appeal reality — only 6–10 per cent of appeals change anything
trackers.desc: THE NUMBER A COMMUNITY SHOULD KNOW BEFORE SPENDING MONEY: a Finnish firm publishes that, on statistical evidence, appeals to the administrative court succeed poorly — generally only about 6 to 10 per cent of hallinto-oikeus appeals lead to changes, with wide case-by-case variation. AND THE CONCLUSION IT DRAWS, WHICH IS THE ADVICE: because of both the real possibility of influence and the risks inherent in the chances of an appeal succeeding, it is especially important to take part in the planning process at its EARLY STAGE, when the possibilities of influence are better. Where a maakunta-, yleis- or asemakaava is being drawn up over your land, follow its preparation closely and try to affect its content at the earliest possible preparation phase. This file has recorded Iceland's scoping-stage comment window and Czechia's published assessment of municipal plans. Finland supplies the arithmetic for why they matter: the appeal at the end fails nine times in ten. PRACTICAL, from other Finnish firms: building permit matters often cause conflicting views with neighbours and are frequently appealed to the administrative court; environment and land-use appeals are heard in the maaoikeus and hallinto-oikeus; and one firm's plain advice is that if the matter is complex or the other side has hired a lawyer, you should get one too.

trackers.name: METSO — the owner offers, keeps the deed, and the compensation is tax free
trackers.desc: WHAT TO PUT IN FRONT OF A FINNISH LANDOWNER: under the METSO programme the forest owner may apply to have their forest protected, receives a TAX-FREE COMPENSATION, and chooses the option that suits them. Permanent protection can be done by establishing a PRIVATE protected area, in which case the area REMAINS IN THE OWNER'S OWNERSHIP; the alternative is to sell the area to the State. Temporary protection runs as a protection agreement of up to 20 years, or a 10-year environmental support agreement. AND THE STEPS, which a community can walk an owner through: anyone interested can contact their own regional centre, the forest centre or other forestry actors, who pass applications on; an expert establishes the site's natural values and its suitability for the programme; and if accepted, the centre makes an offer of protection to the owner. THE SCALE AND THE HONEST PROPORTION: the target is 96,000 hectares offered voluntarily by landowners, plus 82,000 hectares of commercial forest nature sites secured through environmental support and nature management projects — but Finland has 22.8 million hectares of forest, so that is only a little over 0.4 per cent. A WORKED COMPENSATION EXAMPLE: for permanent protection where the owner keeps the land, the compensation in one calculation was a rauhoituskorvaus of about 40,600 euro — and when a private protected area is established the value of the ground itself is not compensated, only the loss. On METSO sites the timber value is set as an average over three years, to level out fluctuations in stumpage prices.

trackers.name: Establishing a Finnish protected area — and the entry in the property register that makes it permanent
trackers.desc: WHO CAN START IT: a protected area can be established either on the LANDOWNER'S INITIATIVE OR ON THE AUTHORITY'S, and the decision is taken by the regional centre. The owner may apply for a protected area on land they own, or give consent to a proposal made by the authority. Almost 7,800 nature protection areas already exist on private land. THE GROUNDS ON WHICH ONE CAN BE ESTABLISHED — which is the checklist for a site: an endangered, rare or declining species, community, habitat type or ecosystem; a breeding or resting place of a species requiring strict protection; the need to maintain or achieve favourable conservation status; special significance for the ability of habitat types or species TO ADAPT TO THE EFFECTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE; or being otherwise so representative or typical as to warrant it. AND THE TWO FACTS THAT MAKE IT STICK: the decision establishing a nature protection area is PERMANENT, and an entry is made in the PROPERTY REGISTER — so it binds the land, not the owner. In protection by agreement land ownership does not change. The State may alternatively buy land areas at market price, and in both cases possibilities for recreational use of the area generally remain unchanged. ONE LIMIT, RECORDED PLAINLY: the decision may not be issued unless the owner and the centre have agreed the protection rules and the compensation — except where the area is already inside a government-approved protection programme, in which case the centre may act without the owner's application or consent.

trackers.name: Luonnonperintösäätiö — it publishes its PURCHASE CRITERIA, and most offers come from owners
trackers.desc: WHAT IT BUYS, in its own published criteria, so you can judge your site before writing: it seeks forest areas that are NOT actively managed commercial forest but have significance for diversity protection in one way or another; areas should preferably be AT LEAST 4–5 HECTARES; the regional emphasis is the southern half of the country but proposals are worth making from the whole of Finland — THE FURTHER NORTH, THE MORE NATURAL THE AREA MUST BE. Besides forests it has acquired mires, wetlands, small waters, islands, rock outcrops and traditional environments. AND THE LINE THAT MATTERS MOST TO AN OWNER: a large part of the forest areas bought now come to our knowledge THROUGH CONTACTS MADE BY THE FOREST OWNERS THEMSELVES. The owner writes to them, not the other way round. IT BUYS THE LAND OUTRIGHT AND LOCKS IT: founded in 1995 with a fisherman-writer's donated savings, it acquires areas of significant natural value into its OWNERSHIP with donated funds and secures for them PERMANENT protection under the nature conservation act, buying forests together with their ground — by purchase, BY EXCHANGE, or through donations. It holds over 200 conservation areas totalling more than 7,000 hectares. AND WHAT IT WILL TAKE THAT OTHERS WON'T: partly commercial-forest areas are acceptable if there are natural values there — we have also bought old commercial forests; they return to old-growth fairly quickly — including forests left with little management by estates of deceased owners.

trackers.name: The regional and specialist Finnish land foundations — PLUPS, the wildlife fund, and the volunteers
trackers.desc: WHY A REGIONAL ONE MATTERS: PLUPS is a lake-region nature heritage foundation that ACCEPTS DONATIONS FROM PRIVATE INDIVIDUALS AND COMPANIES and has assembled holdings piece by piece — two parcels bringing its area at one mire to about 150 hectares, a 73-hectare forest bought in one December, and a 3.5-hectare forest and farm DONATED in another village. AND THE DETAIL WORTH COPYING ANYWHERE: a local branch of the national conservation association DONATED a small island property to the foundation for conservation purposes. One organisation giving land to another that can hold it permanently is a move a local group with a parcel should know about. Its donation account is published openly. TWO MORE FINNISH BODIES ON THE SAME PAGE OF THE PICTURE: a national conservation foundation that owns protected areas acquired IN ACCORDANCE WITH DONORS' WISHES — including some 420 hectares of valuable mire and forest across two municipalities and a 21-hectare area of mostly old forest — and which runs a PREDATOR PROTECTION FUND supporting the protection of predators and their habitats by research, surveys, training, communication, POLITICS AND LAW. AND THE VOLUNTEER ARM: a friends-of-old-growth association concentrates on VOLUNTEER HELP and organising activity such as work parties and excursions on the foundation's protected areas, with joint campaigns run since 2008 with a regional ornithological society and a conservation district.

trackers.name: Luonnonperintösäätiö — over 200 reserves and 7,000 hectares, bought with donations
trackers.desc: WHAT IT HOLDS AND HOW IT GOT IT: a foundation established in 1995 which ACQUIRES INTO ITS OWNERSHIP, WITH DONATED FUNDS, AREAS OF SIGNIFICANT NATURAL VALUE, AND SECURES FOR THEM PERMANENT PROTECTION UNDER THE NATURE CONSERVATION ACT. It has acquired MORE THAN 200 NATURE PROTECTION AREAS, TOTALLING OVER 7,000 HECTARES. Two hundred separate reserves assembled by donation is the largest privately built protected network in this file. AND THE THREE ROUTES BY WHICH IT TAKES LAND: the foundation acquires forests BY BUYING, BY EXCHANGING, OR THROUGH DONATIONS — and it protects forests as untouched as possible from different parts of Finland, with most areas in the south but, in recent years, acquisitions in the north as well. AND THE DOUBLE LOCK, which is the detail worth carrying: in the foundation the forests are IN DOUBLE SAFETY, since they are protected BY THE NATURE CONSERVATION ACT AND BY THE FOUNDATIONS ACT. Land held by a foundation is protected twice over — by conservation law and by the law governing what a foundation may do with its assets — which is why a foundation is a safer holder than an association. Named older and newer reserves are listed individually, some as small as 7 hectares, one later expanded from 13 to 17.5 hectares.

trackers.name: Suomi.fi on appealing a decision — the court fee is WAIVED if you win, and legal aid removes it
trackers.desc: THE COST RULE THAT DECIDES WHETHER A FINNISH COMMUNITY CAN AFFORD TO APPEAL: a court fee is charged on most administrative court decisions, and its size is set annually. IF THE ADMINISTRATIVE COURT CHANGES THE DECISION IN THE APPELLANT'S FAVOUR, THE COURT FEE IS NOT CHARGED. And separately: if a person has received public legal aid, they do not have to pay the administrative court's handling fee. Winning costs nothing, and being poor costs nothing — which removes the fee objection from most Finnish planning appeals. AND WHERE TO GET HELP: if you need more detailed help you can buy it from private advocates or law firms. IF YOU HAVE LITTLE MEANS, YOU MAY HAVE THE RIGHT TO HELP FROM A LEGAL AID OFFICE. AND THE WARNING ABOUT WHAT CANNOT BE APPEALED, which saves a wasted filing: preparatory or implementing decisions cannot be appealed — for example PREPARATORY DECISIONS CONCERNING THE PLANNING OF A MUNICIPALITY'S AREA. The preparatory stage of a plan is not appealable, so a community must object within the process rather than wait to litigate it. The page adds that the decision document usually states at its end HOW AND TO WHOM the decision may be appealed, and that almost all decisions of municipal, wellbeing-region and state authorities can be appealed.

trackers.name: The Finnish hallintopakko demand — ENVIRONMENTAL ORGANISATIONS can force an inspection
trackers.desc: THE ROUTE WHEN A COMPANY IS BREAKING THE RULES: when a private person wants to make another private operator comply with its environmental obligations, IT IS USUALLY EASIEST TO CONTACT THE COMPETENT MUNICIPAL OR STATE AUTHORITY TO MAKE A DEMAND FOR ADMINISTRATIVE ENFORCEMENT (hallintopakko). AND WHY THAT IS THE ROUTE RATHER THAN A CHOICE: private supervision and enforcement of public-law obligations IS NOT POSSIBLE — private persons cannot directly demand in court that another private operator answer for breaches of public-law environmental obligations. In Finland a community cannot sue the polluter directly; it must make the regulator act — which changes where the effort goes. AND WHO MAY START ONE: the right to initiate an enforcement matter depends on the substantive law, but under the Environmental Protection Act it belongs to the parties concerned, ENVIRONMENTAL ORGANISATIONS, certain municipal and state authorities, AND THE SÁMI PARLIAMENT. An environmental organisation has standing to demand enforcement even where an individual might not, which is a reason to route a complaint through one. And the teeth: the supervisory authority can generally reinforce its order with A CONDITIONAL FINE, or with the threat that the omitted measure WILL BE CARRIED OUT AT THE DEFAULTER'S EXPENSE. Anyone at all may contact the authority and report possible breaches.

trackers.name: What the Finnish forest foundation will accept — INCLUDING former commercial forest
trackers.desc: THE SENTENCE THAT WIDENS WHAT A COMMUNITY CAN OFFER, from the foundation's protection manager: AN AREA THAT HAS BEEN PARTLY IN COMMERCIAL FOREST USE IS ALSO ACCEPTABLE TO US, IF THERE ARE NATURAL VALUES THERE, and WE HAVE ALSO BOUGHT OLD COMMERCIAL FORESTS. THEY RETURN FAIRLY QUICKLY TO OLD-GROWTH FOREST. Finland had seven acquisition entries against 34 total. Ground that has been logged before is still worth offering — the commonest reason a community assumes its wood is not good enough, answered directly by a buyer. AND WHERE SUCH LAND IS FOUND, which tells a local group where to look: IN SOUTHERN FINLAND PRIVATE FORESTS ARE CONTINUALLY FOUND — FOR INSTANCE FORESTS LEFT WITH LITTLE MANAGEMENT BY ESTATES OF THE DECEASED — WHICH ARE ALREADY RETURNING TO A NATURAL STATE. Neglected inherited woodland is the most available category of all, and an estate with several heirs is often looking for a buyer. AND THE SCALE AND THE CONSTRAINT: the foundation HAS SUCCEEDED IN ACQUIRING 5,752 HECTARES OF NATURAL AREAS FOR PROTECTION, FORMING 227 AREAS, and its officer notes that AT PRESENT ONLY A LITTLE FOREST GETS INTO PROTECTION, BECAUSE THE STATE FUNDS ALLOCATED TO IT ARE SCARCE. A national panel calculated 404,000 HECTARES of unprotected old forest in the south and 407,000 in the north.

trackers.name: 'A felled forest does not answer' — a national appeal, and the TWO LOCKS on what it buys
trackers.desc: A DIRECT PUBLIC CHANNEL INTO FOREST PROTECTION: the foundation OFFERS, AS A NATIONWIDE ACTOR, A DIRECT CHANNEL TO THE PROTECTION OF FORESTS, and WITH THE PROCEEDS OF THE APPEAL ACQUIRES THREATENED FORESTS INTO ITS OWNERSHIP AND GUARANTEES THEM PERMANENT PROTECTION. Finland had seven acquisition entries against 34 total. AND THE DETAIL WORTH CARRYING ANYWHERE, because it answers the question every donor and community asks about permanence: THE PROTECTED AREAS ARE BEHIND TWO LOCKS — THEIR SURVIVAL IS SECURED BOTH BY THE NATURE CONSERVATION ACT AND BY THE FOUNDATIONS ACT. Two separate statutes holding the same land is a stronger guarantee than either alone — the conservation law protects the site, the foundations law stops the owner disposing of it. And: THE PROTECTION DECISIONS ON THEM ARE NEVER DISMANTLED. AND WHAT THE PUBLIC KEEPS, which is what makes such a purchase locally popular: AFTER PROTECTION ONE CAN STILL WALK, PICK MUSHROOMS AND PICK BERRIES IN THESE FORESTS. Protection that keeps the picking rights is protection a village will support. The body has been at this FOR 26 YEARS and lists a bank account, a reference number and a text-message donation code.

trackers.name: CADA — Comissão de Acesso aos Documentos Administrativos
trackers.desc: Portugal's independent authority on access to administrative documents — the right-to-know regulator. — Holds to account: public bodies that hold records — find information-commissioner decisions and appeals.

trackers.name: DGSI
trackers.desc: Official databases of Portuguese higher-court jurisprudence. · Find here: the official databases of Portuguese higher-court case-law (DGSI).

trackers.name: Quercus — ONGA nacional / ação popular ambiental
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: read the standing rule first, because Portugal's is the most open in Europe. Article 52(3) of the Constitution gives everyone — personally or through an association — the right of ação popular, naming preservation of the environment expressly, and Lei 83/95 regulates it. It is not a special procedure but a species of active standing: you can bring ANY action, in ANY court, including interim measures, to defend diffuse interests, WITHOUT having to show a personal and direct interest or any connection to the matter. A citizen can act alone. WHO IT SUITS: everyone, which is the point — but an association carries weight and evidence a citizen cannot, and Quercus is the national environmental NGO of public utility, founded 1985. Note the screen for associations under article 3: legal personality, the interest in your statutes, and no professional activity competing with firms or liberal professionals.

trackers.name: Portugal IRN (company register)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (official company register); Portugal IRN (company register) — the official register of companies and legal entities in Portugal — the primary public record of corporate existence, ownership, directors and filings. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM A BENEFICIAL-OWNERSHIP REGISTER: this shows the registered entity, its directors and filings; where a separate beneficial-ownership register exists, use that to reach the real humans behind a shell company.

trackers.name: Portal Justiça – Registo Comercial
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Central Register of Effective Beneficiaries (RCBE)
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Publicly searchable.

trackers.name: BASE – Contratos Públicos
trackers.desc: Portugal's public-contracts portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Portugal, and for how much.

trackers.name: dados.gov.pt
trackers.desc: National — official government open data / budget portal. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this is the broad budget/open-data hub for how money is allocated overall — for the specific firms winning tenders use the procurement portal, and for findings of misspending use the supreme audit institution. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Portugal.

trackers.name: Statistics Portugal (INE)
trackers.desc: Portugal's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Portugal.

trackers.name: Portuguese Court of Audits
trackers.desc: high-court in Portugal

trackers.name: Entidade das Contas e Financiamentos Políticos
trackers.desc: National campaign / political-finance disclosure body — party and candidate financial reports.

trackers.name: ONGA status — 100 members buys you a seat at the table
trackers.desc: THE REGISTRATION THAT TURNS AN ASSOCIATION INTO A STATUTORY CONSULTEE. Under Lei n.º 35/98 of 18 July, registering in the RNOE gives an association the right of consultation and information on administrative documents or decisions with environmental incidence; representation in the consultative bodies of local, regional and central administration according to the territorial incidence of its activity; status as a social partner in the scope recognised; and eligibility to apply for financial support. THE GATE IS A NUMBER: the application must include a declaration signed by the President of the Direção stating the number of members, and the mandatory minimum is 100 associados — above Iceland's 30, far below Norway's 5,000. Also required: the geographic area of activity, minutes of the general assembly electing the governing bodies, Cartão de Cidadão copies for the Direção, and the IRC declaration filed with the tax authority. The entity must be an association, legally constituted, non-profit, aiming exclusively at defence and valorisation of the environment — and registration is voluntary but not automatic: all the rights depend on it.

trackers.name: What registration unlocks — and why local scope is the norm
trackers.desc: TWO FINANCIAL CONSEQUENCES AND ONE REASSURANCE. MECENATO: ONGA and equiparadas registered in the RNOE — and other associations pursuing environmental defence — may receive donations in money or in kind from patrons under the Estatuto dos Benefícios Fiscais, so registration unlocks tax-advantaged private giving as well as public grants. UTILIDADE PÚBLICA: after 5 years of activity and registration an association may request the estatuto de utilidade pública under Lei n.º 36/2021. AND THE REASSURANCE — LOCAL IS THE NORM: of 116 actively registered ONGA at the end of 2024, up 8.4 percent on the previous year, 36 (31 percent) hold local scope against just 17 national and 13 regional, plus 27 equiparadas. A neighbourhood association defending one place is the typical ONGA, not the exception. ADMINISTRATION: the register is run by the Agência Portuguesa do Ambiente and published annually in the Diário da República, recording inscriptions, modifications, suspensions and annulments — registration can be suspended and later lifted, so check an organisation's current status rather than a historic list.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: MONTIS — land-purchase fund and land-donation route (central Portugal)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a Portuguese land-conservation association, founded March 2014 and based at Vouzela in Viseu district, that acquires abandoned and marginal ground and manages it for biodiversity. At the end of August 2025 it had 345 members and 34 properties in central Portugal plus four more near Lisbon. Some parcels it bought with public subscription, some it received as donations, and others are baldio commons or company ground it manages under protocol without owning — Baldio de Carvalhais and Baldio da Granja are both on its managed list. USE IT: it runs a standing land-purchase fund and posts the running balance in public, and that balance is the fact to act on. It stood at €12,073.94 on 31 August 2025 and €12,098.94 on 31 July 2026 — a gain of twenty-five euros in eleven months. MONTIS will not outbid a developer. What it will take is a parcel offered by donation, or ground it can manage under protocol while the owner keeps the title, which is the route for an owner who will not sell. Two figures for its area appear side by side on its own pages, about 300 ha and about 313 ha, depending on which one you read. For cash gifts to the fund it states the tax position: an individual deducts 25% of the amount given against tax due, capped at 15% of that tax, and a company books the donation as a cost at 120% of its value, under articles 62 and 63 of the Estatuto dos Benefícios Fiscais.

trackers.name: LPN — Liga para a Protecção da Natureza (Portugal)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the oldest environmental association in the Iberian Peninsula, founded in 1948, a national ONGA with Utilidade Pública status, headquartered at Estrada do Calhariz de Benfica 187, 1500-124 Lisbon. It holds its own reserves in the Castro Verde cereal steppe and runs long-running territorial programmes there and elsewhere — Castro Verde Sustentável, the lynx programme, and a forests programme — describing its method as concrete measures worked in close partnership with local communities. WHY IT IS DIFFERENT FROM A LAND TRUST: since Castro Verde was made a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve on 14 June 2017, LPN has sat on its Management Council and is responsible for its governance — alongside the municipality and the Associação de Agricultores do Campo Branco, the local farmers' association. A Portuguese community told that protection means taking land away from farming can point at a designation where the conservation body, the câmara and the farmers govern the same ground together, and has done for years. WHO IT SUITS: a case in the Alentejo steppe or anywhere its species programmes reach, and any group that needs an established national association rather than a new committee to carry the argument. It complements MONTIS, which works in central Portugal on abandoned and marginal ground; LPN's holdings are working estates in the south. ON THE FIGURES: a Portuguese wildlife directory reports LPN as holding six estates of about 1,800 hectares at Castro Verde plus a further estate at Vila Nova de Poiares. I could not confirm those numbers on LPN's own site, which refers to its reserves without totalling them. Treat the holdings as real and the hectares as unverified.

trackers.name: ZERO — takes Portuguese cases to the European Commission (Portugal)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an environmental association founded at the end of 2015 by around a hundred people, working on climate, pollution, waste, ecosystems and public participation. It files complaints against the Portuguese state with the European Commission — one recent example alleged that Portugal was allowing 28 municipal waste landfills to operate outside the law, in breach of European rules in force since 2014 requiring pre-treatment before landfill, with the cases also reported to the national environment and spatial planning inspectorate. That is the route above the ministry, and this is the Portuguese organisation that uses it. THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST FOR A COMMUNITY, AND IT IS UNUSUALLY WELL DOCUMENTED: it publishes what happens when you ask public bodies for environmental information. Of eight requests it made to the Portuguese Environment Agency, it had to resort to the formal complaint mechanism in five, and two were still unanswered months later. It also points out that the access-to-information commission publishes an annual list of the public bodies that receive the most complaints for failing to answer. A Portuguese community that is being stonewalled is not unlucky, and there is a documented pattern and a named list to cite. IT ALSO WATCHES THE FARM MONEY: with the European Environmental Bureau it has issued joint statements on how Portugal plans to spend Common Agricultural Policy funds, arguing public money is going to those causing environmental and social harm and that Commission supervision is weak. If the threat to your land is subsidised farming rather than construction, that is the file. WHAT IT IS NOT: not a land buyer and not a law firm. Portugal's other entries here are a small land-buying foundation and a body holding estates in the Alentejo; this is the complaints and public-participation leg.

trackers.name: Programa Cidadãos Ativ@s — Gulbenkian as fund operator, and named project managers
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Portuguese Active Citizens Fund, the EEA Grants component built specifically to support non-governmental organisations, run by the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation in consortium with the Fundação Bissaya Barreto with a budget of €11 million across 2018 to 2024, financed by Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway. Portugal and Greece are the two western states inside a scheme otherwise aimed at newer member states, which is not something a Portuguese group would guess. WHAT IT FUNDS, BY OUTCOME — and the fourth one is the interesting one: strengthened democratic culture and civic awareness; increased support for human rights; empowerment of vulnerable groups; and enhanced capacity and sustainability of civil society, which has included training, mentoring, coaching and consulting in the cross-cutting areas of advocacy, watchdog work and fundraising, based on an organisational needs assessment. Being taught to do watchdog work and to fundraise is a durable asset for a community group in a way a project grant is not. THE PRACTICAL DETAIL: it publishes a named project manager for each outcome, with contact addresses, plus a promoter's manual and online application forms, and it ran calls annually with access rules and assessment criteria published on the programme site before each call opened. Ask the manager for the outcome your case fits rather than writing to a general address. AND IT CONSULTED FIRST: the programme's rules were negotiated after a wide consultation of Portuguese NGOs in January 2018, with their conclusions taken into account. A funder that asked the sector what it needed is a funder worth telling what is missing. PORTUGAL NOW HAS FOUR ROUTES in this file: a small land-buying foundation, a body holding estates in the Alentejo, the complaints and public-participation association, and this — the money and the capacity building. Note the period: 2018 to 2024. Check what has succeeded it before relying on an open call.

trackers.name: BALADI — the baldíos federation, and it is telling communities not to sign
trackers.desc: WHAT A BALDÍO IS: communal land belonging to the Local Community, restored to the compartes by Decree-Laws 39/76 and 40/76 in February 1976 and written into the Constitution of the Portuguese Republic by the Constituent Assembly that April as property belonging to Local Communities — a common property, neither public nor private. The Assembleia de Compartes holds broad administration and management powers and decides the use and products of the communal property for the development of the local community, electing the assembly board, the conselho diretivo and the supervisory commission for terms of one to four years. Baldíos exist across the national territory but are now concentrated in the north and centre. WHY THIS IS URGENT RATHER THAN HISTORICAL: BALADI has issued a public warning to all local communities about new draft 'delegation of powers' agreements circulating from the state forestry institute, accompanied by model convocation notices and minutes for approval by Assembleias de Compartes. Its assessment is blunt — this is not simple technical support and not a continuation of co-management, and the drafts should be examined with maximum prudence. It asks every conselho diretivo, baldío commission, managing parish council and assembly to: get independent legal and technical analysis before signing anything; weigh alternatives to the institute and to contracts with financial funds; contact BALADI and its affiliated associations before any deliberation; and propose alternatives that keep the decision in the hands of the compartes. WHAT IT OFFERS A COMMUNITY: its affiliated associations provide technical, administrative, legal and forestry and environmental support without substituting for the baldío's own organs and without taking the decision over its territory away from the Assembleia de Compartes. That is the distinction to test any offer of help against, anywhere. IT ALSO KNOWS THE PRESSURE ON GRAZING: it has reported receiving dozens of baldíos, compartes, shepherds and farmers in open conflict, attributing it to national agricultural payment agency criteria reducing the area available for agricultural applications year after year since 2014. AND IT WORKS WITH GALICIA: it has held Iberian and European congresses of community areas jointly with the Galician organisation of montes veciñais.

trackers.name: SPEA — publishes its pareceres on projects, and holds Portugal's IBA inventory
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: the Sociedade Portuguesa para o Estudo das Aves, founded 1993, a scientific association and environmental NGO with around 3,200 members, BirdLife's partner in Portugal, headquarters in Lisbon. It holds national-scope status in the National Register of Environmental Non-Governmental Organisations, which in Portugal is what gives an association standing to be heard. Portugal's bucket held ZERO, LPN, MONTIS and BALADI but nothing running the bird record. THE SECTION TO OPEN FIRST: its site carries a standing Pareceres/cartas section — the formal opinions and letters it has submitted on projects — alongside IBAs, Censos, Projetos, Informação técnica and Atlas. A published archive of opinions on development projects is the second such archive in this file, after Ireland's FIE, and it tells you what arguments a recognised Portuguese NGO has already run and how it phrased them. IT HOLDS THE INVENTORY AND THE CENSUSES: the IBA inventory for Portugal, the Censo de Aves Comuns, the Chegadas project and the RAM counts, a Comité Português de Raridades, and it publishes an Anuário Ornitológico of ratified observations plus a register of observations open to contributors. Its Red List of the Birds of Continental Portugal found one in three Portuguese bird populations threatened with extinction, with the situation particularly serious for farmland birds, long-distance migrants and seabirds. If your site holds any of those, the national assessment already says so. AND IT WANTS VOLUNTEERS WITHOUT EXPERIENCE: its ciência cidadã programme states that it seeks volunteers with prior knowledge of bird identification and also volunteers who simply like nature, with no need for specific knowledge of environmental subjects or birds. The Censo de Aves Comuns, Chegadas and the RAM counts are named as always needing observers. IT ALSO OPERATES BEYOND PORTUGAL — in partnership in Cabo Verde, São Tomé and Príncipe, Malta and Greece — and runs the Priolo Environmental Centre in the Azores, where its work moved that species from Critically Endangered to Endangered.

trackers.name: Fundo Ambiental — ONGA-only nature calls, and the register you must be on to apply
trackers.desc: THE GATE, AND IT IS THE POINT OF THIS ENTRY: the Fundo Ambiental's nature and biodiversity calls name as beneficiaries ONGA registered in the Registo Nacional das Organizações Não Governamentais de Ambiente (RNOE) — the national register of environmental NGOs, governed by its own published regulation. Being on that register is the precondition for the money, and the fund publishes the list of acts registering, modifying, suspending or cancelling entries, so you can check whether an organisation's status is current. Portugal's bucket held Quercus, LPN, MONTIS, ZERO, BALADI and SPEA; this is the state money they compete for. THE RATES, WHICH ARE UNUSUALLY GENEROUS TO NGOs: one biodiversity call carried 1,200,000 EUR with a maximum co-financing rate of up to 85 per cent for ONGA and up to 80 per cent for other beneficiaries, capped at 80,000 EUR per project. Another ran at 500,000 EUR with up to 95 per cent, also capped at 80,000 EUR. A wildlife recovery centre call ran at 440,000 EUR, up to 95 per cent, capped at 40,000 EUR. The NGO rate is explicitly higher than everyone else's. TWO STRUCTURES WORTH KNOWING: calls have been split into Tipologia 3.1 for LIFE projects already approved by the European Commission, where the Fundo Ambiental provides part of the national component, and Tipologia 3.2 for projects that have not had LIFE support — so the fund is the co-financing partner for an EU LIFE bid as well as a standalone funder. And projects may be presented in consortium with other entities, with municipal associations, intermunicipal communities, higher education institutions and scientific societies eligible on some typologies. THE PRACTICAL CATCHES: support is given as reimbursement of eligible costs actually incurred and paid — so you must be able to spend first. Calls are for mainland Portugal, run to a published Diário da República notice with a hard closing time, and each carries FAQs and a final reasoned evaluation report you can read before applying again.

trackers.name: Milvoz — a network of Bio-Reservas for small sites nothing else protects
trackers.desc: WHY THIS ONE: born in 2019 in Coimbra, Milvoz seeks to give active voice to citizenship in favour of preserving native ecosystems, and its principal mission is the creation of a network of BIO-RESERVAS, with the aim of filling the ABSENCE OF MECHANISMS OF EFFECTIVE PROTECTION FOR AREAS OF SMALL SIZE with high conservation value. Small sites are exactly what this file exists for, and Portugal now has a body whose stated purpose is the gap where a parcel is too small to interest the state. Portugal's bucket held Quercus and MONTIS as acquirers; this is a third route and the one aimed lowest. AND TWO MORE BODIES NAMED IN THE SAME FOUNDATION'S CONSERVATION PORTFOLIO: MONTIS, founded 2014 in Vouzela, which manages territories relevant to conservation THROUGH THE PURCHASE OF LAND — already filed here — working the Vouga and Paiva ranges on threatened wolf populations, mountain rivers and agricultural abandonment, and contributing to the creation of the Parque Natural Local Vouga-Caramulo; and Rewilding Portugal, established 2019 in Guarda, working Riba-Côa and Beira Alta, a region where high rates of rural abandonment created opportunities to bring nature back. A local natural park created by an association's work is the outcome a community should ask about by name.

trackers.name: The Lifescape report for Portugal — and the direito de superfície used to secure land for rewilding
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a legal report commissioned by Rewilding Portugal and written by The Lifescape Project, Legal Mechanism for Conservation and Restoration in Europe: Examples and Lessons for Portugal, addressing the absence of a dedicated legal instrument capable of securing long-term commitments on privately owned land REGARDLESS OF FUTURE CHANGES OF OWNERSHIP. THE INSTRUMENT THAT HAS ACTUALLY BEEN USED: the direito de superfície — the surface right — was used, so far as is known FOR THE FIRST TIME, to secure land destined for rewilding, through an earlier joint project between Rewilding Portugal and Lifescape. Portugal's existing tools — property right, surface right, servidões, usufruto and arrendamento — can be used voluntarily, and this is the report that sets out how. THE CONTEXT IT RECORDS, worth citing in any Portuguese case: most land of ecological value in Portugal, as in the rest of Europe, lies OUTSIDE protected areas and in private hands, used for agriculture or forestry; the first version of Portugal's Plano Nacional de Restauro, required under the European nature restoration regulation, is due in September 2026; and the Court of Justice of the European Union recently imposed financial sanctions on Portugal for failures in implementing the Habitats Directive.

trackers.name: Archer & Associados — runs ações populares, and its head is a lawyer AND an environmental engineer
trackers.desc: WHY THIS FIRM: the area is coordinated by the head of the consortium, who has DOUBLE HIGHER EDUCATION IN LAW AND IN ENVIRONMENTAL ENGINEERING — and its lawyers act in civil and administrative court actions including THE IMPUGNMENT OF ACTS LICENSING URBANISTIC OPERATIONS, in proceedings relating to TERRITORIAL PLANNING PLANS, and in AÇÕES POPULARES in matters of environment, urbanism and territorial planning. Portugal's bucket held Quercus and the ação popular route, but no firm that runs one. A lawyer who is also an environmental engineer can read the impact study himself, which is the expense this file has recorded as the bottleneck in eleven countries. AND THE OTHER SIDE OF ITS PRACTICE, RECORDED SO YOU CAN CHECK CONFLICTS: it also defends companies and individuals in environmental contraordenação proceedings for discharge of liquid or gaseous effluents, waste disposal, noise emission or other infractions, at both administrative and judicial stages. TWO MORE PORTUGUESE PRACTICES WORTH THE CALL, from their own service lists: one names ações populares, sanctioning procedures, and administrative, civil and criminal liability alongside environmental impact assessment and licensing; another names expropriation proceedings for public utility, and REVERSIONS, alongside municipal master plans, detail plans, subdivisions and Projects of Potential National Interest.

trackers.name: Habita — the association that fights speculation and stands with people facing eviction
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: a Portuguese non-governmental organisation founded in 2013 by activists from previous social movements, advocating for HOUSING RIGHTS AND URBAN JUSTICE, operating primarily in Lisbon and other major Portuguese cities. WHAT IT DOES THAT MATTERS TO A LAND FIGHT: it advocates for housing as a SOCIAL RIGHT RATHER THAN A MARKET COMMODITY, campaigns against REAL ESTATE SPECULATION, especially in Lisbon and other large Portuguese cities, and provides DIRECT SUPPORT to individuals and communities affected by homelessness or eviction proceedings. Development pressure displaces people as well as habitat, and this is the Portuguese organisation that supports the people — every other Portuguese entry in this file is about ground, species or law. A community facing a scheme that will price out or evict its residents has a different ally from one facing a scheme that will clear a wood, and both fights are usually the same fight. It sits within a wider revival of housing movements recorded in the Portuguese press, and works in the context of the country's housing market crisis.

trackers.name: GEOTA — its river programme SUPPORTS THE FOUNDING of movements defending river basins
trackers.desc: WHAT IT OFFERS A COMMUNITY DIRECTLY, and it is the most specific offer in the Portuguese bucket: its rivers programme SUPPORTS THE CONSTITUTION AND THE ACTIONS OF MOVEMENTS IN DEFENCE OF OUR HYDROGRAPHIC BASINS, alongside defending the NON-CONSTRUCTION OF UNNECESSARY DAMS, promoting the removal of obsolete barriers harmful to ecosystems, and fighting for the improvement and the fulfilment of legislation on water resources. An organisation that will help you FOUND the group, not just advise it once it exists, is what a village with no association needs first. Portugal was the smallest bucket in the file at 22 entries. WHO IT IS: a national environmental NGO with PUBLIC UTILITY STATUS, non-profit, active since 1981, whose object is the defence of the environment and the promotion of sustainable development, through education, information and training, REFLECTION AND POLITICAL INTERVENTION, and the carrying out of actions to resolve SPECIFIC environmental problems. AND THE ACCESS IT HAS, which is why its name on a letter matters: from the start a priority was intervention with the political powers AT THE HIGHEST LEVEL — the President of the Republic, the Assembly of the Republic, the Government, THE PROSECUTOR GENERAL'S OFFICE; and internationally the European Commission — through thematic studies, formal opinions, and proposals for legislation, always rigorously grounded. It runs a nature reserve interpretation centre jointly with a local association, and takes members, volunteers and donations.

trackers.name: ENEA's register of supported organisations — the Portuguese ONGA list, described one by one
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the environment agency's own register of environmental non-governmental organisations, each entry describing what the body is, when it was founded and what it does — the official list rather than a private directory. A state register of recognised environmental organisations is where a community checks whether the body offering help is formally an ONGA, which in Portugal carries standing. WHAT ITS ENTRIES SHOW: the country's oldest such association, founded in 1948 and THE OLDEST ENVIRONMENTAL DEFENCE ASSOCIATION IN THE IBERIAN PENINSULA, non-profit with PUBLIC UTILITY STATUS, aiming at the defence of the environment and contributing to the conservation of the Natural Heritage, of the diversity of species and of ecosystems; and a national forest association founded in 1992 to actively support THE MANAGEMENT, THE DEFENCE AND THE ASSOCIATIVE MOVEMENT IN PRIVATE AND COMMUNITY FOREST, recognised as equivalent to an environmental NGO in 2001. A body whose stated job is supporting private and community forest owners is the one to bring a woodland question to — and this file has repeatedly found that the owner beside you is the person who decides. Six named organisations also act together as a standing coalition on European nature directives.

trackers.name: ATN — it owns about 1,000 hectares, and a PROPERTY ACQUISITION FUND takes 10–30% of every sale
trackers.desc: THE FUNDING MECHANISM, AND IT IS THE MOST COPYABLE IN THE PORTUGUESE BUCKET: the association runs its own brand of products — organic olive oil, artisanal jams and almonds, olive paste — and ecotourism activities, and states plainly that with every visit or product bought you are supporting the expansion of the Reserve: A PERCENTAGE OF BETWEEN 10 AND 30 PER CENT OF ALL SALES GOES TO THE PROPERTY ACQUISITION FUND, WHICH ALLOWS ATN TO CONTINUE BUYING LAND ALONG THE VALLEY. A named fund inside a trading business, taking a fixed share of every sale and spending it on buying ground, is a model a community organisation can set up itself. WHAT IT HAS BOUGHT WITH IT: created in 2000, ATN is the owner of a set of properties along the valley which constitute the Reserve — THE FIRST PRIVATE PROTECTED AREA IN PORTUGAL — today about 1,000 HECTARES of land, managed exclusively for the conservation of biodiversity, forming a continuum of about 5 KILOMETRES ALONG THE RIVER, COVERING BOTH BANKS, precisely where much of the cliff-nesting bird life breeds and where the largest stand of cork oak in the district lies. AND ITS MISSION, in its own words: to conserve, value, know and publicise the natural heritage of the north-east of Portugal, by way of sustainability AND WITH THE PARTICIPATION OF THE COMMUNITY, through the management and protection of natural areas. Its strategic vectors include guaranteeing the economic sustainability of nature conservation projects.

trackers.name: Rewilding Portugal — set up where LAND ABANDONMENT has created the opportunity
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a private non-profit organisation, established in January 2019 in a named city, whose mission is to promote nature conservation through REWILDING MEASURES in Portugal. Portugal's bucket held a land-purchase fund and a commons federation; this is the body working the abandoned ground. AND WHY IT WORKS WHERE IT DOES, which tells a rural community whether the model fits its own area: it works in two named northern regions, a region where HIGH RATES OF LAND ABANDONMENT HAVE CREATED OPPORTUNITIES FOR BRINGING NATURE BACK. Where land is being abandoned rather than developed, a rewilding organisation is the buyer or partner most likely to take it on. AND THE FUNDING LINEAGE BEHIND IT, worth knowing because it shows where this money comes from: the European foundation it belongs to is a private-law foundation based in the Netherlands, supported by a national POSTCODE LOTTERY, which gave rise to a fund created by a group of non-governmental organisations to finance projects in art, culture and environment; its founders applied to that fund in 2012, were selected, and then opened a Europe-wide competition to finance renaturalisation projects in various landscapes of the continent. A Portuguese association and a Spanish foundation applied jointly with a cross-border project and were chosen. Its capital arm has also made loans to local wildlife-tourism businesses in the same area.

trackers.name: Apoio judiciário — NON-PROFIT BODIES qualify, and the fee waiver is the part that matters
trackers.desc: WHAT AN ASSOCIATION CAN ACTUALLY GET, and it answers the cost question for a Portuguese residents' group: ENTITIES, WITH AND WITHOUT PROFIT-MAKING PURPOSES, HAVE THE RIGHT TO LEGAL AID ONLY IN THE FORMS OF EXEMPTION FROM THE COURT FEE AND OTHER PROCEDURAL COSTS, AND THE APPOINTMENT AND PAYMENT OF THE COMPENSATION OF A LAWYER or an enforcement agent. Portugal is the smallest bucket in this file. An association gets its court fees waived and a lawyer appointed and paid — but not a preliminary legal consultation, which is expressly excluded for non-profit entities. Knowing which half is available stops a group applying for the wrong thing and losing time. AND WHAT EVERY APPLICATION MUST CARRY: all requests must be accompanied by PROOF OF THE ECONOMIC DIFFICULTIES that do not allow the costs of the proceedings to be borne. AND THE PRACTICAL TOOL: eligibility can be checked in advance using the SIMULATOR on the social security website, under Simulations > Legal Protection. A public simulator that tells a group whether it qualifies before it applies is worth running first — the answer decides whether a case is affordable at all.

trackers.name: Portuguese urbanismo practices — THREE MONTHS to challenge a licence decision
trackers.desc: THE CLOCK, stated plainly by a practice that takes this work: a refusal of a building licence MAY BE CHALLENGED BY THE ADMINISTRATIVE ROUTE — through a complaint or a HIERARCHICAL APPEAL — OR BY THE JUDICIAL ROUTE, BEFORE THE ADMINISTRATIVE COURTS. THE DEADLINE FOR ACTING IS SHORT, GENERALLY 3 MONTHS FROM THE NOTIFICATION. Three months from notification, with an internal appeal and a court route running in parallel — and the same courts hear a challenge to a licence that was granted, not only one refused. AND WHAT THE FIELD COVERS: urbanism law regulates THE USE OF THE SOIL, THE LICENSING OF WORKS AND THE RELATIONS BETWEEN PRIVATE PARTIES AND THE MUNICIPAL COUNCILS, and a lawyer is needed when the council refuses a licence, EMBARGOES A WORK, applies an urbanistic fine, or when you want to CONTEST AN ADMINISTRATIVE DECISION on construction or the use of buildings. An embargo on works is a named, ordinary outcome of this area of law — which is what a community facing an unlawful build is actually asking for. AND THE COST TRANSPARENCY WORTH LOOKING FOR: this practice publishes a fixed CONSULTATION PRICE of 70 EURO, a reply within 24 working hours, and states YOU KNOW EXACTLY WHAT YOU WILL PAY BEFORE PROCEEDING — NO SURPRISES, NO HIDDEN COSTS.

trackers.name: Fundação Terra Agora — a LAND BANK that buys or accepts land, and can never resell it
trackers.desc: A PORTUGUESE FOUNDATION WHOSE WHOLE PURPOSE IS TAKING LAND OUT OF THE MARKET: RECOGNISED BY THE GOVERNMENT at the start of 2024, it has as its object TO ACQUIRE LAND, WHETHER BY PURCHASE OR BY DONATION, and to promote on it PROJECTS OF CONSERVATION AND REGENERATION OF NATURE, through entities that become its GUARDIANS. AND THE CLAUSE THAT MAKES IT PERMANENT: THE LAND ACQUIRED CANNOT AFTERWARDS BE SOLD AGAIN NOR USED FOR ANY SPECULATIVE PURPOSES WHATSOEVER. A buyer that is legally barred from ever reselling is the safest destination for a threatened parcel — and it takes land by gift as readily as by purchase, so an owner who cannot afford to refuse a developer can hand it over instead. AND WHAT IT LOOKS FOR, which tells a community how to approach it: OUR PRINCIPAL MISSION AFTER THE ACQUISITION OF THE LAND IS TO FIND PEOPLE AND COMMUNITIES DEDICATED TO PRESERVING AND REGENERATING IT OVER THE COMING GENERATIONS. THE FOUNDATION ACTS AS A FOUNDATION-STONE, ENSURING THEY HAVE ALL THE SUPPORT NEEDED to create and implement projects with great ecological and socio-economic impact. It states that IT IS LOOKING FOR NEW LAND AND GUARDIAN PROJECTS, and already has the regeneration of a 1,600-HECTARE property under way. It needs local people as much as a local group needs it.

trackers.name: Florestgal — the state company that buys 500 HECTARES A YEAR from private owners in protected areas
trackers.desc: THE PUBLIC BUYER MOST PORTUGUESE OWNERS DO NOT KNOW EXISTS: the state company created after the great fires of 2017 has as its aim TO BUY AROUND 500 HECTARES FROM PRIVATE OWNERS EVERY YEAR IN AREAS WITH NATURAL PROTECTION STATUS, in its president's words to the national news agency. AND THE DISTINCTION HE DRAWS, which is the part that matters to a community: while many of the company's holdings follow A LOGIC OF COMMERCIAL EXPLOITATION, IN THESE PURCHASES THE OBJECTIVE IS DIFFERENT — WE WANT TO TAKE ON NEW AREAS THAT HAVE VALUE IN TERMS OF NATURE CONSERVATION, AND WE WANT TO RENATURALISE THOSE SPACES. A state company with a standing annual target to buy protected land, expressly not for commercial use, is a buyer a community can name to a wavering owner. AND WHAT IT SEEKS, which suits exactly the parcels nobody else wants: it LOOKS FOR LAND WITHOUT COMMERCIAL INTEREST in order to go ahead with RENATURALISATION PROJECTS and to combat fires. Its work includes the reconversion of some 60 HECTARES of eucalyptus plantation to OAKS AND CORK OAKS, and a similar project replacing ALMOST A THOUSAND HECTARES of eucalyptus in cooperation with the national conservation institute.

trackers.name: A RESIDENTS' ASSOCIATION and a national body, filing to the PUBLIC PROSECUTOR together
trackers.desc: THE PAIRING A PORTUGUESE COMMUNITY SHOULD AIM FOR: a named RESIDENTS' ASSOCIATION filed a COMPLAINT TO THE PUBLIC PROSECUTOR about a large urbanisation, and a national conservation body then sent someone to look, with its national directorate deciding whether to file its own COMPLAINT TO THE PUBLIC PROSECUTOR AND TO THE INSPECTORATE-GENERAL FOR AGRICULTURE, THE SEA, THE ENVIRONMENT AND SPATIAL PLANNING. Two addressees, a prosecutor and an inspectorate, are open to a residents' association without a lawyer — and a national body filing alongside doubles the weight without the residents losing control of their own complaint.
