It unites twelve organisations working in the environmental field. Its stated mission is to unite organisations' knowledge, experience and resources and take part together in forming and implementing environmental protection policy, and its stated ambition is to become the public environmental competence centre that is turned to first when the non-governmental sector's position is sought. AND IT IS OPEN: the coalition states plainly that it is open to new members. After the Bulgarian coalition that admits unincorporated groups by letter, this is the second national platform in this file a community can actually enter. WHERE TO FIND THE WIDER LIST: the Lithuanian environment ministry publishes its environmental NGO social partners, and the list runs far beyond the coalition — the environmental policy centre, the environmental management and audit institute, the environmental information centre, the coalition itself, and named citizens' associations including one formed by Klaipėda residents. A Lithuanian community can see, on a government page, which organisations the ministry itself recognises as partners. IT IS ALSO INSIDE THE NATIONAL NGO STRUCTURE: the coalition is a member of the Nacionalinė NVO koalicija alongside the youth council, the local community organisations union, the human rights coalition and others — and members' annual activity and financial reports are published. You can read a prospective ally's accounts before approaching it. THE CONTEXT IT ITSELF NAMES: on World NGO Day the national coalition wrote publicly that in Lithuania and in Europe there are increasing attempts to diminish the name of non-governmental organisations and spread doubts about their aims and transparency. Eighth jurisdiction in this chat recording pressure on the sector itself.

trackers.name: APVA — and the municipal environmental programme funded by pollution charges next door
trackers.desc: THE NATIONAL AGENCY: the Aplinkos projektų valdymo agentūra, Labdarių g. 3-102, 01120 Vilnius, administers projects financed from the Aplinkos apsaugos rėmimo programa, whose purpose is to finance environmental protection and other measures set out in the Act on that programme. It also administers the Klimato kaitos programa and the Lithuanian Environmental Investment Fund programme, which funds environmental investment projects reducing the negative impact of economic activity and securing a continuing environmental effect. AND THE PART A COMMUNITY SHOULD ASK ABOUT FIRST: there is a separate savivaldybių aplinkos apsaugos rėmimo specialioji programa — a municipal special environmental protection programme — governed by its own Act, whose funding sources are the pollution charges and state natural resources tax paid in that municipality. Money raised from polluting your district is held by your own council under a statute that says what it may be spent on, and the Supreme Administrative Court has published a summary of case law on challenging decisions about how those funds are used. That is the closest fund to a Lithuanian community and the one with a local decision-maker. A WORKED EXAMPLE OF WHAT NGOs GET: a project of the Aplinkosaugos koalicija — already filed here — received 85,856.43 EUR, of which 7,200 EUR to the coalition as partner, financed from the Klimato kaitos programa administered by APVA, to implement its long-term strategy and strengthen members' capacity so they can more effectively represent the environmental public interest. Its planned work included reviewing its advocacy and monitoring strategies against institutions' legislative plans and members' pressing topics. A state climate fund paying an NGO coalition to do advocacy and monitoring is unusual enough to record, and it tells a Lithuanian group which door its national allies already use. PRACTICAL: the ministry publishes the AARP funds usage rules and the list of projects that received AARP financing; ministry at A. Jakšto g. 4, 01105 Vilnius, info@am.lt.

trackers.name: Teisės vartai — Lithuanian law offices listed with Aplinkos apsaugos teisė as a named practice
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a directory of Lithuanian advokatų kontoros — law offices — with each firm's practice areas listed, its address, and the advocates' names, the year each began practice, telephone and email. The practice-area lists include Aplinkos apsaugos teisė (environmental protection law), Administracinė teisė ir procesas, and Nekilnojamojo turto ir statybų teisė (real property and construction law) — the three labels a community needs to filter on. WHY A DIRECTORY: Lithuania's bucket held the Vilnius University Law Clinic, which gives free primary legal aid to NGOs, and the Aarhus-style route — but no way to find a paid specialist when the clinic's help runs out. A named list with practice areas and the year each advocate qualified lets a community pick on experience rather than on advertising. WHAT LITHUANIAN FIRMS SAY THEY DO IN THIS FIELD: representation in dealings with municipalities and with the State Territorial Planning and Construction Inspectorate; advice on the lawfulness of construction and on change of use purpose; pre-trial dispute resolution; and court representation. Others list reconciliation of the interests of neighbouring plot owners — plot boundaries, building at the boundary, planting, insolation and surface water run-off — and restrictions on property rights including special land use conditions.

trackers.name: Lithuanian environmental standing — the suinteresuota visuomenė may demand action and punishment
trackers.desc: WHAT THE LAW GIVES A COMMUNITY, stated on the EU's own access-to-justice pages: one or more natural or legal persons, and the suinteresuota visuomenė — the interested public — have the right to lodge a complaint or application demanding that appropriate action be taken to avoid or reduce damage to the environment or to restore the environment to its original state, and demanding the punishment of persons guilty of harmful effects on the environment and of officials whose decisions, acts OR INACTION infringed the rights or legally protected interests of citizens, the interested public, or other persons. Inaction is expressly covered, and so is restoration to the original state — not merely stopping further harm. Second country in this sweep after Cyprus where an omission is actionable. AND A SEPARATE ROUTE ON INFORMATION: there is a right to apply to court where a request made under the rules on access to environmental information was unlawfully refused, answered partially or improperly, or not properly taken into account. A refused information request is itself a case. THE STATUTE BEHIND IT: the Aplinkos apsaugos įstatymas regulates relations in environmental protection and sets the basic rights and duties of legal and natural persons in preserving biological diversity, ecological systems and landscape features, alongside Articles 53 and 54 of the Constitution.

trackers.name: Municipal aplinkosaugos competitions — schools, kindergartens and bendruomenės can apply
trackers.desc: WHERE THE LOCAL MONEY ACTUALLY IS: Lithuanian municipalities run their own environmental competitions from the funds of the savivaldybių aplinkos apsaugos rėmimo specialioji programa — the municipal special environmental protection programme already recorded in this file, fed by the pollution charges paid in that municipality. This is the application portal where those calls appear. WHO MAY APPLY, and it is broader than any national fund: non-governmental organisations, public institutions, BENDRUOMENĖS — communities — SCHOOLS AND KINDERGARTENS. A neighbourhood community and a village school are named applicants, which no national environmental fund in this file allows. WHAT THE PROGRAMME IS FOR, in its own words: to involve city residents in protecting the environment of their own place of residence, develop ecological thinking and responsibility, increase awareness of environmental problems, and encourage residents' activity and partnership in solving environmental questions. AND A SECOND MUNICIPAL LINE WORTH ASKING FOR: a parallel competition implements the Law on the Development of Community Organisations in culture, sport, social affairs, ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION and youth policy, to widen NGO involvement in meeting local community needs. PRACTICAL: smaller municipalities publish their own budgets — one district allocated 38,000 euro to NGOs and communities, covering three lines including co-financing of up to 5 per cent of the compulsory contribution to EU or national programme projects and operating costs. Ask your own municipality what it has budgeted and whether co-financing is one of the lines.

trackers.name: Aktyvių piliečiụ fondas — 9 million euro, with at least 80 small local organisations targeted
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Active Citizens Fund in Lithuania, financed under the EEA financial mechanism — at least 10 per cent of that mechanism's funds go to strengthening civil society through the fund, by agreement between the EU, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway — allocating 9 million euro across a five-year period in Lithuania. It is administered by a consortium of three named NGOs. THE TARGET THAT MATTERS TO A VILLAGE GROUP: the fund plans to involve more than 250 civil society organisations, INCLUDING AT LEAST 80 SMALL ORGANISATIONS OPERATING AT LOCAL LEVEL, to finance at least 180 projects, and to engage about 10,000 people directly. A published target for small local organisations is a commitment you can hold a funder to. THE TWO PROJECT SIZES: small-scale projects from 5,000 to 15,000 euro, and medium-scale projects above 15,000 and up to 80,000 euro. In one call the fund received 157 concept applications — only 16 per cent for the small tier, so the small window is the less crowded one. AND A DETAIL ABOUT PARTNERSHIP WORTH COPYING: two thirds of applications had partners, 179 partners in total across the round, with one applicant naming eleven. Partnering is the norm here, not a bonus.

trackers.name: Anyone can propose a gamtos paveldo objektas — and the agency lists exactly what to send
trackers.desc: THE INVITATION, IN THE AGENCY'S OWN WORDS: if you have noticed a valuable natural object — for example a rare species, an impressive stone or a unique landscape — assessed it against the criteria and think it should be protected, YOU CAN SUBMIT A PROPOSAL. For a state-protected object or natural heritage object, send it to the protected areas service; for a MUNICIPAL protected object, apply to the relevant municipal administration, whose contacts are published. Two tiers, one form, and a published contact list for both — Lithuania had one land acquirer filed and this is the route by which a resident gets a single feature protected. WHAT TO PUT IN THE PROPOSAL, listed by the agency so nothing is guessed: the exact location — municipality, eldership, COORDINATES; quantitative features where applicable such as height, length, AGE, diameter; and qualitative features such as form, composition, transparency, AESTHETIC VALUE and NATURALNESS. The object must meet at least two of the criteria, one being naturalness — whether the object and its surroundings are unaffected by human activity. AND THE SCALE THAT SHOWS IT IS ROUTINE: Lithuania had 701 state-protected natural heritage objects, 155 of them declared natural monuments, AND 232 MUNICIPALITY-PROTECTED ONES. The agency also publishes a handbook on the general and special principles of managing such objects.

trackers.name: The Lithuanian municipal NGO funds — money for improving public spaces, council by council
trackers.desc: WHAT ONE DISTRICT PUBLISHES, and every Lithuanian council runs something comparable: a call inviting NGOs to submit applications for PART-FINANCING from the municipal budget under a multi-year non-governmental organisations activity funding programme, with 20,000 EURO allocated and a stated application window. Eligible applicants are NGOs registered AND OPERATING IN THE DISTRICT'S TERRITORY. AND WHAT THE MONEY CAN BE SPENT ON, from another municipality's rules, which is the part that matters to a group defending a place: funds may be awarded competitively for INITIATIVES INTENDED TO IMPROVE THE QUALITY OF PUBLIC SPACES AND THE ENVIRONMENT — the fitting out of PARKS, sports and recreation grounds, AND OTHER REST AND RECREATION PLACES IN THE LOCAL COMMUNITY'S TERRITORY; for strengthening NGO cooperation with other public legal persons, developing partnership and SOLVING QUESTIONS RELEVANT TO THE LOCAL COMMUNITY; and for strengthening the organisation's own activity and cohesion. Priority goes to organisations holding formal NGO status — and the exclusions are published too: no funding for organisations that failed to report on earlier municipally-funded projects, for everyday running costs or salaries, or for premises repair and equipment UNRELATED TO THE PROJECT.

trackers.name: Lietuvos ornitologų draugija — the country's largest conservation membership body, and it does the fieldwork
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a non-governmental organisation operating for 40 years, uniting Lithuanian people who care about the protection of living nature, who look after and observe birds and their environment, care for environmental preservation and public ecological education, AND PARTICIPATE AS CITIZENS IN FORMING ENVIRONMENTAL AND BIODIVERSITY PROTECTION POLICY. It is THE MOST NUMEROUS CONSERVATION MEMBERSHIP ORGANISATION IN THE COUNTRY. Lithuania had one land-holding body filed. AND WHO CAN JOIN, which is the resource: any citizen who pays the membership fee can be a member. The society unites people of varied interests — professional researchers, bird watchers, naturalists, FARMERS, FORESTERS, teachers, schoolchildren, students and other citizens not indifferent to Lithuanian nature. A membership body that already contains farmers and foresters is one that can talk to the landowners around your site, rather than only to officials. AND WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES ON THE GROUND: it CARRIES OUT GAMTOTVARKA WORKS — practical habitat management — conducts SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH into bird populations and monitoring, and PUBLICLY CONTROLS THE MAKING AND IMPLEMENTATION OF LAWS regulating environmental and biodiversity protection. Since 1994 it has represented BirdLife International in Lithuania. Its Vilnius street address and email are published.

trackers.name: The Lithuanian park directorates — 36 staff, a street address and a phone, per protected area
trackers.desc: WHO ACTUALLY RUNS A LITHUANIAN PROTECTED AREA, and it is a body with a door: the directorate of a named national park and state nature reserve is A BUDGETARY INSTITUTION EMPLOYING 36 STAFF, with a street address in a named town, a website and a direct telephone number. The park covers 58,519 hectares — one of the largest protected territories in Lithuania. AND ITS DUTIES, which tell a resident exactly what to ask it for: it organises the natural science RESEARCH AND OBSERVATIONS of the park and reserve and ACCUMULATES INFORMATION ABOUT THE STATE AND CHANGE OF THEIR NATURAL ENVIRONMENT COMPONENTS; protects natural and cultural heritage values; creates conditions for recreational activity; carries out ecological education; and fosters the region's cultural traditions, crafts and trades. A directorate that accumulates information on the changing state of its own area is the body holding the baseline data your objection needs — and it is a public institution obliged to answer. AND THE INTERNATIONAL LAYERS ON ITS GROUND, each a separate lever: the reserve is declared a NATURA 2000 territory and entered on the list of the RAMSAR CONVENTION protecting wetlands of international importance, and the wider area is one of thirteen European PAN Parks. It also holds a European Solidarity Corps quality label, so it takes volunteers.

trackers.name: The new Saugomų teritorijų įstatymas — individual notice, and compensation for EVERY owner
trackers.desc: TWO CHANGES A LITHUANIAN LANDOWNER SHOULD KNOW, recorded by the forest owners' association that argued for them. First: it is established that BEFORE ESTABLISHING OR DESIGNATING NATURA 2000 TERRITORIES, LANDOWNERS MUST BE INFORMED INDIVIDUALLY. Until now this was done only in the case of establishing national protected areas. Individual written notice before a Natura designation is what stops an owner learning about it from a neighbour, and this file recorded in Turkey that failure to notify villagers was alone sufficient to annul a decision. SECOND, AND IT REACHES PEOPLE WHO WERE PREVIOUSLY EXCLUDED: from now on, compensation for activity restrictions on a specific land or forest plot can be received by ALL OWNERS WHO HAVE NOT YET RECEIVED COMPENSATION, not only those who recovered or acquired the holding BEFORE the protected area was established. Under the old rule, if the land or forest in an existing protected area was bought by another owner, that owner LOST THE RIGHT to the compensation due for the environmental restrictions. Someone who bought into a protected area after designation may now be owed money they were previously refused — worth checking before assuming nothing is available. The association states it actively participated in the deliberations, submitting comments and proposals so the regulation would reflect forest and land owners' interests.

trackers.name: NŽT — the pre-emption list for farmland, and the fees for getting onto it
trackers.desc: WHAT HAPPENS WHEN FARMLAND IS SOLD, and it is the part a community wanting to buy needs: if a person received information from the land service about an AGRICULTURAL LAND PLOT FOR SALE, it means they are on THE LIST OF PERSONS HOLDING A PRE-EMPTION RIGHT to acquire it, the categories being set out in the land acquisition act. A statutory list of who gets first refusal on farmland is a queue a community body may be able to join before the land ever reaches the open market. AND THE CLOCKS AND FEES, published: having received the notice, a person has 15 WORKING DAYS to submit their consent to buy; the seller's notification-and-certificate service costs 47 EURO, and the land service's consent to acquire agricultural land costs 11 EURO for a private person. Eleven euro and fifteen working days is the whole cost of standing in the queue — which makes it worth registering before a sale is announced rather than after. AND THE RULE FOR EVERYONE ELSE: buying an agricultural plot WITHOUT a pre-emption right is possible only if ALL persons holding that right have refused, and only AT THE PRICE STATED IN THE SELLER'S ORIGINAL NOTICE. A person without the right must apply to the service on their own initiative for consent.

trackers.name: Baltijos aplinkos forumas — 20 staff, and it works on WIN-WIN SOLUTIONS with farmers
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: founded in 2003 as a NON-GOVERNMENTAL, NON-PROFIT ORGANISATION, described as one of the strongest and most efficient environmental NGOs in Lithuania, with 20 EMPLOYEES, among them SOME OF THE LEADING EXPERTS ON AGRI-ENVIRONMENTAL MEASURES MANAGEMENT IN THE COUNTRY. AND WHAT IT DOES THAT A COMMUNITY CAN USE: defining the most valuable priority areas for targeted species conservation; EVALUATION OF CONSERVATION STATUS AND MANAGEMENT NEEDS; INSTITUTIONAL CAPACITY BUILDING OF PROTECTED AREAS ADMINISTRATIONS; and STAKEHOLDER DIALOGUE. An organisation that will evaluate a site's conservation status is the one that turns a village's worry into a document a ministry must answer, and it publishes its team, their expertise and its Vilnius office location. AND THE APPROACH WORTH BORROWING WHERE FARMERS ARE THE OBSTACLE: it raises awareness BY ENSURING ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL MOTIVATION to foster WIN-WIN SOLUTIONS FOR AGRICULTURE AND ENVIRONMENT, by achieving CONCRETE BENEFIT FOR THE FARMERS in a long-term perspective, and works in collaboration with local environmental authorities. One named staff member coordinates communication and NATURE TOURISM, supervises VOLUNTEERS, and runs a named public initiative.

trackers.name: Lithuania's court fee — 30 EURO to file, 15 to appeal, and NOTHING where the authority delays
trackers.desc: THE PRICE OF GOING TO COURT, published by the supreme administrative court itself: the court fee for lodging a complaint with the FIRST-INSTANCE court is currently 30 EURO. For lodging an APPEAL to the Supreme Administrative Court, a fee of 15 EURO is paid. Thirty euro to start an administrative case is the cheapest court access recorded in this file — against a 600-dollar New Zealand appeal and a 200-euro Greek deposit. AND THE EXEMPTION THAT MATTERS MOST, from the same system: the Law on Administrative Proceedings provides several exemptions from the court fee, FOR EXAMPLE COMPLAINTS OR APPLICATIONS CONCERNING THE DELAY BY PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION ENTITIES IN PERFORMING ACTS WITHIN THEIR COMPETENCE. Challenging an authority for sitting on a decision costs nothing at all, which is the cheapest lever a Lithuanian community has when a permit is being allowed to slide through. AND THE COURT'S PRACTICAL DETAIL: its Vilnius street address, telephone, MOBILE NUMBER and email are published with its opening hours, and on Mondays and Wednesdays from 17.00 to 17.30 the court accepts applications and complaints from PERSONS WHO HAVE REGISTERED IN ADVANCE. It also warns that the court has the right to require payment of the fee IF PERSONS ABUSE THE RIGHT TO JUDICIAL DEFENCE.

trackers.name: Free primary legal aid in Lithuania — the municipality must see you WITHIN FIVE DAYS
trackers.desc: THE ENTITLEMENT, and it has no means test: the law gives EVERY PERSON LAWFULLY RESIDENT IN LITHUANIA THE RIGHT TO FREE PRIMARY LEGAL AID — a legal consultation. Free first advice for everyone, regardless of income, is a starting point most communities never use, and it is delivered locally rather than in the capital. WHO GIVES IT: municipal administration officials and employees, AND ALSO ADVOCATES OR SPECIALISTS FROM PUBLIC INSTITUTIONS with whom the municipality has signed a contract. They will personally advise HOW TO RESOLVE THE DISPUTE WITHOUT A COURT, inform you about the legal system, laws and other legal acts, HELP TO PREPARE A SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND TO FILL IN THE APPLICATION FOR SECONDARY LEGAL AID. AND THE TIMING GUARANTEE, which is unusually firm: primary legal aid must be given to you IMMEDIATELY. If that is not possible, you will be told the next reception time, WHICH MUST BE NO LATER THAN 5 DAYS from your approach. A five-day statutory maximum wait for free legal advice is worth quoting when an office tries to put a resident off. Applicants must approach the municipality OF THEIR DECLARED PLACE OF RESIDENCE.

trackers.name: Lithuania's compensation for restrictions — the state pays for the FOREST PLAN too
trackers.desc: WHAT AN OWNER GETS FOR ACCEPTING RESTRICTIONS, and it is the offer that persuades a Lithuanian landowner: compensation may be ONE-OFF OR ANNUAL, calculated INDIVIDUALLY FOR EACH FOREST PLOT, taking into account THE VALUE OF THE TIMBER LEFT UNCUT, with the figures set by the preparer of the forest management project. Lithuania had two land-acquisition entries filed. AND THE DETAIL THAT REMOVES THE LAST OBSTACLE: together with the compensation for the restrictions, the forest owner MAY ASK FOR THE COSTS OF PREPARING THE FOREST MANAGEMENT PROJECT TO BE COMPENSATED. The state pays for the very document needed to calculate the payment, so an owner is not out of pocket for finding out what they are owed. AND WHERE THE MONEY COMES FROM WHEN THE SITE IS EUROPEAN: most Lithuanian protected areas OVERLAP with Natura 2000 sites, and in those cases private forest owners' losses ARE COMPENSATED FROM EUROPEAN UNION FUNDS under a named rural development programme — with payments made TO PRIVATE FOREST OWNERS OR THEIR ASSOCIATIONS where felling is forbidden or restricted. An owners' association can receive the payment collectively, which is the fourth community-landholding route recorded in this region. Protected areas cover about 17.5 PER CENT of the country.

trackers.name: The Suvalkija national park plan — owners are offered compensation OR A BUY-OUT
trackers.desc: WHAT HAPPENS TO PRIVATE LAND WHEN A NEW LITHUANIAN NATIONAL PARK IS PLANNED: during the planning process, land owners will, under the provisions of the law, HAVE THE POSSIBLE COMPENSATION preliminarily calculated FOR LOSSES CAUSED BY RESTRICTIONS ON ECONOMIC ACTIVITY, OR THEY MAY BE OFFERED THE BUY-OUT OF THE PRIVATE LAND. A buy-out is offered as an alternative to compensation when a park is created — so designation is itself a route by which private land inside a threatened area can pass into public hands. AND THE SCALE AND STAGE: the government approved the start of preparation of the planning scheme and the planning objectives for a park that could occupy UP TO 35,000 HECTARES. AND THE POINT THAT SHAPES ANY OBJECTION: national parks are NOT protected areas with a single uniform environmental regime — the boundaries and the internal zones are settled during planning, which is when a community's submission has effect. The protected-areas service also publishes NATURE OBJECTS IN PROTECTED AREAS RECENTLY ADAPTED FOR VISITING, which is what gives a designation local support.

trackers.name: Pelkių fondas — a fund for ONE habitat type, and what a single-habitat body is for
trackers.desc: A SPECIALIST BODY FOR ONE KIND OF GROUND, which matters because a wetland is the habitat most often lost quietly to drainage rather than to a permit: the fund works on THE SEARCH FOR AND APPLICATION OF EFFECTIVE SOLUTIONS, ENSURING THE PROTECTION OF NATURAL PEATLANDS AND THEIR BIOLOGICAL DIVERSITY, THE SUCCESSFUL RESTORATION OF DAMAGED PEATLANDS, AND INCREASING THE RESILIENCE OF NATURAL ECOSYSTEMS TO CHANGE. Lithuania is among the least-worked buckets in this file. A fund devoted to a single habitat will take on a site the general conservation bodies consider too small or too damaged — and it names DAMAGED peatlands as its own subject, not an exception, which puts drained and dug ground squarely within what it wants. That is the Finnish and German finding again from a third direction: harmed land is the work, not a disqualification. AND HOW A COMMUNITY KEEPS TRACK OF IT: EVERY MONTH WE SHARE NEWS OF EVENTS, OF ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AND OF OUR ACTIVITIES. A monthly bulletin from a specialist fund is how a local group hears that a restoration programme has opened before the money is allocated.

trackers.name: The state agency's OWN list of Lithuanian environmental organisations
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY PUBLISHED BY THE REGULATOR ITSELF, which is worth more to a community than a campaigner's list because it is the roster the authorities recognise: the environmental protection agency publishes ENVIRONMENTAL ORGANISATIONS IN LITHUANIA, naming the MINISTRY OF THE ENVIRONMENT, the agency itself as SUBORDINATE TO THE MINISTRY, an INSTITUTE OF ENVIRONMENTAL ENGINEERING, an ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION POLICY CENTRE, the LITHUANIAN FUND FOR NATURE and the national branch of a BALTIC ENVIRONMENTAL FORUM. When the agency that issues permits also publishes the list of bodies working against bad ones, a community can cite that list back to the agency — the same asset as the Serbian funders directory in batch606, where the permitting ministry appeared among the funders. AND WHY THE MIX MATTERS: the roster puts A POLICY CENTRE AND AN ENGINEERING INSTITUTE ALONGSIDE THE CAMPAIGNING FUNDS, so a group needing technical rather than legal help has a named starting point. An engineering institute on the official list is where a community takes a question about hydrology or emissions, which is not the kind of body a campaign directory would carry.

trackers.name: Persónuvernd (Icelandic DPA)
trackers.desc: Persónuvernd (Icelandic DPA) — Iceland’s independent data-protection / information commissioner, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Iceland (Hæstiréttur)
trackers.desc: Official site publishing the judgments of Iceland's Supreme Court. · Find here: the judgments of the Supreme Court of Iceland (Hæstiréttur).

trackers.name: Parliamentary Ombudsman of Althingi
trackers.desc: Iceland’s Parliamentary Ombudsman, elected by the Althingi to investigate complaints against public administration.

trackers.name: Landvernd — landgræðslu- og umhverfisverndarsamtök Íslands
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Iceland's environmental association, which wins at the environment and natural resources appeals committee often enough to publish an archive of the rulings. It got Skútustaðahreppur's construction permit for the Kröflulína 4 power line annulled — a result it calls precedent-setting because the committee recognised nature-protection considerations as bearing on the decision — and obtained an interim ruling halting works on Þeistareykjalína 1 and Kröflulína 4. The committee has also upheld its claims over changes to the Kjalvegur road and a new hotel building in Kerlingarfjöll, and it filed jointly with three other conservation groups to stop the Hvalá hydropower scheme. WHO IT SUITS: communities facing power lines, hydropower, roads and highland tourism development. It appeals in its own name, so you do not need standing of your own to get a decision reviewed — but you do need to reach it inside the one-month appeal window.

trackers.name: Úrskurðarnefnd umhverfis- og auðlindamála (ÚUA) — environmental appeals committee
trackers.desc: The independent administrative committee that rules on appeals against environmental and natural-resource decisions in Iceland — the venue where a construction or operating permit actually gets overturned. WHO TO ENLIST: nobody; you file here yourself. You CAN: appeal as an environmental, outdoor-recreation or interest organisation WITHOUT having to show a legally protected interest of your own, which is how Iceland implements the Aarhus access-to-justice requirement, and the committee can suspend a decision's effect so work stops while it decides. For activists: the deadline is the thing. You generally have ONE MONTH from when you knew or should have known of the decision, running from publication where the decision is publicly notified. Say which decision you are appealing, how it touches your interests and what you want — usually annulment. Every appellant must sign or give written authority, and note that a lawyer's ordinary court mandate does NOT carry here; a separate authorisation is needed.

trackers.name: Icelandic National Audit Office
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Iceland, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Statistics Iceland
trackers.desc: Iceland's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Iceland.

trackers.name: Iceland — National Audit Office (Ríkisendurskoðun)
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution; independent body under the Althingi auditing State finances & institutions and publishing public audit reports, Iceland.

trackers.name: Ríkiskaup (Central Procurement)
trackers.desc: National public-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Iceland, and for how much.

trackers.name: Skatturinn – Company Registry
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Register of Enterprises
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Publicly searchable.

trackers.desc: Reykjavík District Court (Iceland) — first instance court in Iceland (Wikidata record).

trackers.desc: Court of Appeal — appellate court in Iceland (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: Úrskurðarnefnd umhverfis- og auðlindamála — ask for the interim halt
trackers.desc: THE APPEALS COMMITTEE THAT CAN STOP THE MACHINERY WHILE IT THINKS. Constituted under Act No. 130/2011, it rules on appeals against administrative decisions. YOUR ORGANISATION HAS STANDING: in case 68/2008 (Helguvík) it held that a free association of people interested in nature protection satisfied the conditions for party status in appeals about projects falling under environmental impact assessment law, and took the case to substantive consideration — so standing is established, not arguable. AND ASK FOR THE INTERIM SUSPENSION IN THE APPEAL ITSELF: an appellant may demand a ruling halting construction while the case is heard, a provision that exists so the parties' legal position is not substantially altered before the merits are decided. It has been used — works on Þeistareykjalína 1 and Kröflulína 4 were halted within the Þeistareykir planning area pending decision, and the committee later annulled the construction permit for Kröflulína 4. THE LIMIT, PLAN AROUND IT: under Article 44(2) of the Planning Act, grenndarkynning (neighbour notification) is directed at neighbours with individual, legally determined interests — and in case 107/2023 it was argued that appellant associations owning no property on or near the route could not rely on a failure to notify. Pair the association's appeal with an affected landowner who can run that ground.

trackers.name: Náttúruverndarsamtök Íslands — who to join, and an honest record
trackers.desc: A FREE ASSOCIATION OF PEOPLE INTERESTED IN NATURE PROTECTION, over 1,400 registered members, formally founded 29 May 1997, open to anyone who accepts its aims — annual subscription 3,500 kr, joining by email with name, address, phone and kennitala. Protecting the central highlands is among its most important aims. It is the kind of body whose standing the appeals committee has recognised, so joining or working with it is a route into appeals for an individual who could not easily bring one alone. TWO PRACTICAL LEVERS IT HAS USED: the information appeals committee has ordered Landsnet to hand over documents refused to conservation groups — a transmission-line contract and a report on ground cables — and Icelandic groups have complained to the EFTA Surveillance Authority (ESA) over legislation. BE REALISTIC: the organisations' own account of years of appeals, court actions against open-pen aquaculture licences and an ESA complaint records that in most cases the results were limited.

trackers.name: Rekstrarstyrkir — core funding, and only 30 members needed
trackers.desc: MONEY FOR THE ORGANISATION ITSELF, NOT JUST A PROJECT — the rarest kind in this map. The environment ministry has given voluntary environmental associations operating grants plus project and travel grants since 2000, allocated once a year at the start of the year, to promote open and free exchange of views on environmental and resource matters. THE RULES ARE REACHABLE BY A SMALL GROUP: environmental matters must be one of the main objectives in your own statutes; the association must be open to general membership, not for profit, have at least 30 members, keep open and audited accounts and produce annual reports. Thirty members is among the lowest thresholds recorded anywhere in this map — against Norway's 5,000 — so a village association qualifies. ASK FOR MULTIPLE YEARS: in one round a grant ran 2 years and two ran 3 years, rather than annual reapplication.

trackers.name: What the grants actually fund, and your odds
trackers.desc: THE NUMBERS, SO YOU CAN JUDGE THE EFFORT. In one year the ministry allocated about ISK 111 million in total: ISK 49 million in operating grants to 23 associations, and just under ISK 62 million to 40 projects. COMPETITION IS REAL BUT NOT HOPELESS: 75 project applications were received seeking ISK 219.6 million — so roughly half succeeded, for well under half the money sought. WHAT GETS FUNDED, from the ministry's own list: nature conservation, wetlands, land reclamation, bird life, geographic information, hunting management, forestry, plastic pollution, nature maps and digital mapping, conferences and environmental education — so mapping and evidence work is fundable, not only action on the ground. AND FOR BIGGER MONEY: EU LIFE Strategic Nature Projects run a two-stage process — an English-language concept note first, with only shortlisted applicants invited to submit fully — and preparation grants are available for writing the concept note itself.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Landgræðslusjóður and the skógræktarfélög (Iceland)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Iceland has around sixty local forestry societies, federated under Skógræktarfélag Íslands, and between them they built most of the country's public woodland — Heiðmörk, Öskjuhlíð, Kjarnaskógur. Anyone can join one. Behind them sits Landgræðslusjóður, a self-owning foundation established in 1944 at the founding of the republic and operating under law 19/1988, whose remit is clothing the land in forest and which also covers other land reclamation and vegetation protection. Write to Landgræðslusjóður, Þórunnartúni 6, 105 Reykjavík, or skog@skog.is. USE IT: the fund's own rules let it support projects by other associations, companies, institutions and individuals, not only its member societies — calls go out to the societies by March each year, but the door is wider than the call. Past allocations have paid for planning, thinning, planting, path-building and, directly to the point here, the protection and fencing of new land areas. And the programme's own paperwork carries the instrument worth asking for: Landgræðsluskógar requires a secure written agreement over every piece of ground planted under it, there is a template land agreement, and new agreements are made and old ones renewed as more land is needed. Iceland's route is an agreement over the land, not a purchase of it. THE LIMIT, WHICH IT PUBLISHES: the foundation's capital may not be depleted — only the return is distributable. Own capital stood at ISK 367.5 million in the 2016 accounts while the 2022 round distributed a little over ISK 14 million across many projects. This pays for work on a site; it does not buy one. Applications must be written and specific, and the fund reserves the right to withdraw a grant if the work is not carried out as applied for.

trackers.name: Fuglavernd — and the legal fund Icelandic conservation groups set up for each other
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Iceland's main non-governmental bird conservation organisation, established 1963, around 1,300 members, fuglavernd@fuglavernd.is. Its mission is the protection of birds and their habitats, and its record is one of things that actually changed: it is credited with saving the Icelandic white-tailed eagle from extinction in the 1960s, and it argued successfully for bans on hunting rock ptarmigan and Greenland white-fronted goose. IT HELPED CREATE A RESERVE WITH A MUNICIPALITY: the Flói reserve east of the Ölfusá and north of Eyrarbakki — about 5 square kilometres of low-lying wetland, an Important Bird Area — was established from 1997 in cooperation with the Árborg community, with founding money from an environmental fund and continuing support from the RSPB. A community and a bird society together, and a municipality as partner rather than opponent. THE THING TO CHASE, WHICH IS RARER THAN ANYTHING ELSE IN THE ICELANDIC BUCKET: its own pages point to Lögverndarsjóður náttúru og umhverfis — a legal protection fund for nature and the environment, established in 2002 by several Icelandic nature conservation organisations to provide financial support for resolving legal questions concerning nature and environmental protection. Iceland has no named environmental counsel in this file. A standing fund that pays for legal questions, set up by the conservation sector for its own use, is the nearest thing, and a community should ask Fuglavernd how it is accessed. SOURCING CAVEAT ON THAT FUND: I have it from Fuglavernd's own published material rather than from a dedicated page of the fund itself, and I have not confirmed that it is currently active or how it is applied to. Verify before relying on it. IT ALSO RESTORES: it works on re-wetting drained wetland, including projects on the Mýrar in western Iceland, with partners planning the re-wetting of at least several hundred hectares of degraded habitat — coastal lowlands that hold half the world population of European golden plover, 40% of whimbrel and 20% of redshank, and which are threatened by drainage and by afforestation. If the threat to Icelandic ground is tree planting on open wetland, this is the organisation that treats that as damage.

trackers.name: Náttúruverndarsamtök Íslands — open to anyone, 3,500 kr a year
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: a free association of people interested in nature protection with over 1,400 registered members, formally founded 29 May 1997 to be an advocate for those who care about nature protection and environmental matters. Þórunnartún 2, 105 Reykjavík. Iceland's bucket held twenty courts and registries and only four allies; this is a fifth, and the cheapest to join. THE ENTRY TERMS, WHICH ARE THE POINT: the association is open to everyone who supports its aims and wants to work in accordance with its rules, and the annual fee is 3,500 kr. To join or support, you email your name, email, phone number and kennitala. That is the lowest barrier to membership recorded anywhere in this file. THE PRINCIPLE IT SAYS IT WORKS BY: it follows the principles of the 1992 Rio Declaration, including the precautionary rule — that a project which may have serious effects on the environment should not be undertaken unless it is shown that it does not have such effects. That is the burden of proof reversed, stated as the organisation's own standing position. Its most important stated policy aim is protecting Iceland's central highlands. AND THE OTHER HALF OF THE ICELANDIC SECTOR, from the same sources: Landvernd — already in this file — has 40 member associations across the country alongside its roughly 6,000 individual members, and was founded in 1969 as a federation of land reclamation and nature protection societies that most of the larger conservation organisations belonged to. So Iceland does have a federation, and it is a body already recorded here for its legal work. THE REGIONAL SOCIETIES TO ASK FOR BY NAME: SUNN, the society for nature protection in the north, founded 1970 and the first Icelandic body devoted solely to nature protection built on public membership; NAUST in the east; and Náttúruverndarsamtök Suðvesturlands in the south-west, which appears in Icelandic appeal proceedings as a complainant. The rangers' association Landvarðafélagið works with them.

trackers.name: Skipulagsgátt — comment on the scoping plan before the study is even written
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: Skipulagsgátt is Iceland's consultation portal for planning matters, environmental impact assessment and framkvæmdaleyfi — development permits — where you can find matters in progress, make comments during the presentation period, and reach the final documents and decisions. THE TWO WINDOWS, AND THE FIRST IS THE ONE MOST COUNTRIES DO NOT GIVE YOU: the developer first submits a matsáætlun — a scoping plan setting out the project and how it intends to assess it. Skipulagsstofnun publishes that to the public on Skipulagsgátt and seeks comments, and the public and other interested parties are expressly given the chance to comment on it, before the agency issues its opinion instructing the developer on the preparation, content and presentation of the assessment report. You can object to the METHOD before the study exists. Comments at this stage may address the definition of alternatives, data gathering, data processing and how the report is presented. THE SECOND WINDOW: when the umhverfismatsskýrsla is submitted, it is published on Skipulagsgátt and must lie available at an accessible place near the project site and on the agency's website for six weeks from the notice, advertised in the Lögbirtingablað and in a medium likely to reach those living near the site. The agency may also hold an open house or public meeting. AND WHAT HAPPENS TO YOUR COMMENT: everyone may submit an umsogn, and comments received during the presentation periods are part of the material Skipulagsstofnun takes a position on when preparing its opinion. Those who commented are notified when the opinion is issued, and the opinion may specify conditions and mitigation measures the agency considers must be set in the permits. WHO ELSE COMMENTS, worth reading alongside yours: Umhverfisstofnun on pollution matters and Minjastofnun on cultural heritage. Municipalities issue the building and development permits after the assessment is complete. The agency's own note is that local people often have good local knowledge of the environment and conditions, and that knowledge can be used in the design of the project.

trackers.name: The náttúruminjaskrá and the state's forkaupsréttur — get the land listed, and the State gets first refusal
trackers.desc: THE PROVISION THAT ANSWERS ICELAND'S MISSING LAND-BUYER: under the náttúruverndarlög, the State Treasury shall have a right of pre-emption over farms and other landed properties which are wholly or partly on the náttúruminjaskrá — the register of natural monuments — after those parties who are given pre-emption under the land act. Iceland had no organisation that buys ground. Getting a property onto the register means the State gets first refusal when it is sold, which is a different and cheaper campaign than raising a purchase price. WHO CAN PUSH FOR A LISTING OR A FRIDLYSING: the minister may friðlýsa — protect by declaration — land areas, individual natural formations, natural monuments in the sea, catchments and whole water systems. The declaration must state the aim of the protection, the natural monuments it seeks to preserve and their conservation value, and be accompanied by a map showing the boundaries. AND THE DEFINITION THAT DECIDES WHO COUNTS AS A CONSERVATION BODY IN ICELANDIC LAW, which governs standing and consultation throughout: nature and environmental protection organisations are those whose main objective is nature and environmental protection, WHICH MUST BE OPEN TO GENERAL MEMBERSHIP, PUBLISH ANNUAL REPORTS ON THEIR ACTIVITIES AND HAVE AUDITED ACCOUNTS. Three conditions, and all three are administrative rather than expensive. PRACTICAL: before a permit is granted the authority must seek the opinion of Umhverfisstofnun, the Icelandic Institute of Natural History and the relevant local nature protection committee, unless a confirmed aðalskipulag and approved deiliskipulag already carry those opinions — and special care must be shown towards habitat types, ecosystems and species on part C of the register, to prevent their natural range or habitat shrinking and their conservation status worsening.

trackers.name: Umhverfisstofnun's friðlýsingar desk — and the fact that it can hand custody to someone else
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the agency page for friðlýsing — the method used to protect distinctive and important natural features over a defined area, setting aside a site that then enjoys protection in perpetuity for nature and coming generations. Declarations rest on the nature protection act and are worked out IN COOPERATION WITH LANDOWNERS, MUNICIPALITIES AND OTHER STAKEHOLDERS. Iceland has more than 130 protected areas and three national parks. THE PROVISION A COMMUNITY GROUP SHOULD ASK ABOUT: the agency manages and operates a friðland under the nature protection act — AND MAY ENTRUST ITS CUSTODY TO OTHERS under the same act. An association can be handed the running of a protected area without owning it, which is the Icelandic counterpart of Malta's guardianship deed. AND THE TERMS ARE NOT UNIFORM, which cuts both ways: rules for protected areas differ according to the objectives of the declaration, the nature of the site AND THE AGREEMENT WITH STAKEHOLDERS; protection can be stronger or weaker. What your site's declaration says is negotiated, not standard — so the text is worth arguing over. A WORKED EXAMPLE OF ENLARGEMENT: a minister decided, on the proposal of the agency, with the opinion of the natural history institute and WITH THE CONSENT OF THE MUNICIPALITY AND THE LANDOWNER, to ENLARGE an existing friðland and renew its declaration — the original dating from 1975. Grounds cited included nesting by species rare nationally, on the red list, and Icelandic responsibility species.

trackers.name: Landeigendafélag and the Hornstrandir committee — the landowners' association with a seat
trackers.desc: THE STRUCTURE WORTH COPYING: ownership inside one Icelandic friðland is dispersed — land owned by former inhabitants and their descendants, other private parties, ASSOCIATIONS and the state. To speak for them, a LANDEIGENDAFÉLAG — a landowners' association — was founded in 1973 and has been the spokesman for house and land owners inside the protected area ever since the site was declared in 1975. AND IT HAS A SEAT: a standing consultative committee for the friðland exists, composed of representatives nominated by the municipality, by the LANDOWNERS' ASSOCIATION, and by the environment agency, with a role covering advice on the affairs of the protected area, WORKS IN THE AREA, and policy. Forming a landowners' association inside a designated area buys a permanent seat on the body that advises on works — a structure a community can build itself, and one that outlasts any single campaign. ALSO RECORDED: the plan notes the agency informing the municipality to add into the aðalskipulag those roads which are permitted — the protected-area plan feeding directly into the municipal plan.

trackers.name: Náttúruverndarsamtök Austurlands — a regional society that proposed the country's first fólkvangur
trackers.desc: WHY A REGIONAL SOCIETY MATTERS MORE THAN A NATIONAL ONE HERE: NAUST, founded in 1970 and now past fifty years old, covers a working area stretching between two named rivers across the whole east of the country. Its record is the point: it submitted A LARGE NUMBER OF PROPOSALS FOR THE PROTECTION OF AREAS AND OF INDIVIDUAL NATURAL MONUMENTS, and pressed for the protection of land areas NEAR SETTLEMENTS for outdoor recreation and nature observation. A regional society whose stated business is filing protection proposals is the ally a community brings its site to — and milestones on that road included the first fólkvangur in Iceland, the category of protected area established at local initiative. HOW IT WORKED, which is a shape a community can copy: its activity was characterised by well-attended annual meetings, varied issue and COMMITTEE work, participation in nature protection assemblies and in the Náttúruverndarráð, and PUBLICATION OF THE NÁTTÚRUMINJASKRÁ — the register of natural monuments this file recorded in batch 331 as triggering the State's pre-emption right. AND THE PEOPLE, because in a small country they are findable: its founder and first chairman later became a member of parliament and minister; a later chairman and several former chairs contributed to its anniversary volume, as did the serving environment minister.

trackers.name: LEX — it drafts stjórnsýslukærur for individuals in planning cases, and it is 40 lawyers strong
trackers.desc: WHAT IT OFFERS AN INDIVIDUAL: from the outset LEX has provided INDIVIDUALS, companies and public bodies with comprehensive and specialised service in the field of administrative law, PLANNING MATTERS and related areas of law, and its lawyers have experience across advice, assistance with permit applications, REPRESENTATION BEFORE THE PARLIAMENTARY OMBUDSMAN, and conducting disputes before ADJUDICATING BODIES AND THE COURTS. AND THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST TO A RESIDENT: it also protects the interests of INDIVIDUALS and companies in planning matters, such as ASSESSING THEIR LEGAL POSITION AND DRAFTING ADMINISTRATIVE APPEALS. Iceland had thirty-one filed entries and one legal resource. Assessment of legal position plus drafting the appeal is exactly the two-step a community needs, and it names the parliamentary ombudsman route alongside the courts. THE FIRM: one of the largest and oldest law practices in Iceland, about 40 lawyers, 18 owners, at Borgartún 26 in Reykjavík, repeatedly rated by foreign directories among the country's leading firms and a member of an international professional network. A CONFLICT NOTE, RECORDED PLAINLY BECAUSE IT IS UNAVOIDABLE IN A SMALL COUNTRY: the same page states that LEX provides MUNICIPALITIES with varied advice on the handling of planning matters. Ask at the first call whether the firm acts for your council.

trackers.name: Leit.is lögmenn — the Icelandic directory, from sole practitioners to the large firms
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a published overview of lawyers and legal practitioners in Iceland, from SOLE PRACTITIONERS to larger practices offering comprehensive legal services and other specialist advice, browsable by place. In a country of Iceland's size, the sole practitioner is often the affordable option, and a national directory is how a community finds one outside the capital. WHAT THE ENTRIES TELL YOU BEFORE YOU CALL: each describes its own specialisms — the listing names practices specialising in accident and damages compensation, and others with around thirty years' experience of litigation in civil and criminal cases — so a group can filter for someone who actually litigates rather than advises. WHY THIS MATTERS ALONGSIDE THE BIG FIRM: this file recorded in batch 355 that Icelandic law lets the environment agency entrust custody of a protected area to others, and in batch 372 that a national association costs 3,500 króna a year to join. The legal step between those two — someone to draft the appeal when a permit is granted anyway — is what this directory supplies, and Iceland's own adjudicating body publishes its rulings, so a practitioner can be checked against decided cases before instruction.

trackers.name: Umhverfissjóður sjókvíaeldis — the polluter-funded pot INDIVIDUALS can apply to
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a fund whose purpose is minimising the environmental effects caused by SEA-CAGE FISH FARMING, paying the cost of research for carrying-capacity assessment and MONITORING, and other projects the board decides. 170.4 million króna was available in one year. AND WHO MAY APPLY, which is the point: INSTITUTIONS, FISH FARMING COMPANIES, INDIVIDUALS AND LEGAL PERSONS can apply for grants from the fund. An industry-linked fund that individuals can apply to, for monitoring the industry's own effects, is a route a coastal community would never guess at — and the board has said it will look particularly at projects that REDUCE the environmental effects of sea-cage farming and projects that STRENGTHEN MITIGATION MEASURES against them, with emphasis on work that can be done within a year. AND THE TRANSPARENCY CONDITION WORTH KNOWING BEFORE YOU APPLY OR BEFORE YOU GO LOOKING FOR EVIDENCE: final and progress reports of projects the fund supports SHALL GENERALLY BE ACCESSIBLE ON THE FUND'S WEBSITE. Grant holders must send the board information on project status at least every six months, and results of research projects are made accessible. A named member of staff and an email address are published.

trackers.name: Anyone may NOMINATE a site for friðlýsing — and the government answers the questions in public
trackers.desc: THE SENTENCE A COMMUNITY NEEDS: LANDOWNERS, MUNICIPALITIES, INSTITUTIONS AND OTHERS ARE PERMITTED TO NOMINATE AN AREA FOR FRIÐLÝSING. The nomination route is open, published on the ministry's own questions-and-answers page, and costs nothing to use — Iceland's bucket held the agency custody route and the association membership threshold; this is the door a resident walks through first. AND THE DISTINCTION THE PAGE DRAWS, which decides what you should ask for: friðlýsing concerns protecting A PARTICULAR AREA OF LAND, A PARTICULAR WATERFALL, CAVE OR FOREST. Friðun, by contrast, is about protecting nationwide or in a defined land or sea area — for example an animal species, a plant species, or a natural phenomenon such as ALL DRIPSTONES IN CAVES WHEREVER THEY ARE IN THE COUNTRY. Ask for the right one: the place, or the thing found in the place. The page records that Icelandic conservation action has leaned on protection of DEFINED LAND AREAS because the distinctiveness of the nature there is considered great, or because A NATURAL JEWEL IS FOUND THERE, with the designation intended to limit disturbance.

trackers.name: Skógræktarfélag Íslands — the local forestry societies, one of which BOUGHT A 650-HECTARE FARM
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a NATIONAL UMBRELLA ORGANISATION FOR LOCAL AND REGIONAL FORESTRY ASSOCIATIONS throughout Iceland, who together form ONE OF THE LARGEST NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS IN ICELAND, founded in 1930 and so one of the oldest environmental associations in Iceland. It advocates for all the forestry associations, guards their interests and speaks and acts on their behalf as needed. Its street address in the capital, website and telephone number are published. AND WHAT ITS MEMBER SOCIETIES CAN DO, which is the reason this is filed as a land resource: one regional forestry society BOUGHT A FARM of about 650 HECTARES outright. A network of local societies where one member can buy a 650-hectare farm is a land-holding structure a community can join rather than build. AND HOW A PERSON GETS IN: by joining a forestry society you lend support to a good cause — membership is the route. The umbrella guides member societies, companies and the public on the various aspects of forestry, works with named partner projects, publishes the only journal about forestry in Iceland, and its societies run forest walks, courses and lectures, conferences, Christmas tree sales and educational trips. Its stated goal is to advance forest and tree cultivation in the country and to promote environmental improvements of every kind.

trackers.name: The state's PRE-EMPTION RIGHT over land on the náttúruminjaskrá
trackers.desc: THE PROVISION, and it is the strongest single thing a listed site gives a community: THE STATE TREASURY SHALL HAVE A RIGHT OF PRE-EMPTION OVER FARMS AND OTHER LANDED PROPERTIES WHICH ARE IN PART OR IN WHOLE ON THE NATURE REGISTER, after those parties given pre-emption under the land act. The treasury's deadline to answer a pre-emption offer is 60 DAYS from receipt. Where the state can step into any sale of listed land, getting a site onto the register changes who is able to buy it — and Iceland's bucket already holds the route by which anyone may nominate an area. AND THE PROVISION FOR THE OWNER WHO FEELS TRAPPED, which is the other side of the same page: if a landowner or rights-holder considers that a protection notice causes them SUBSTANTIAL DAMAGE OR UNREASONABLE DIFFICULTY in using their land, they may apply to the minister for an exemption — OR REQUEST THAT THE AREA BE PROTECTED AS A FRIÐLAND instead. An owner burdened by a blanket protection can ask to be moved into the designated-reserve system, where compensation and management agreements exist. The ministry must seek the opinion of the environment agency, the natural history institute and the relevant local nature protection committee, and weigh whether a corresponding protected area can be built up elsewhere. The act also provides for ACTION PLANS AND AGREEMENTS ON CARE where work is needed to reach favourable conservation status.

trackers.name: Skapa.is styrkir — the Icelandic directory of grant funds, listed by what they support
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a national gateway listing GRANT FUNDS OPEN IN ICELAND, each with what it supports, who may apply and how often it awards. Iceland's three filed funding entries were all ministry money. A single directory of funds saves the search that otherwise has to be done fund by fund, and it surfaces the corporate and community sources a group would not otherwise know exist. AND WHAT IT SHOWS ABOUT WHO ELSE PAYS IN ICELAND: an energy company's COMMUNITY FUND whose aim is TO SUPPORT SOCIALLY POSITIVE PROJECTS OF INDIVIDUALS OR GROUPS, with grants awarded TWICE A YEAR; a bank's COMMUNITY GRANTS covering, among other fields, RESEARCH AND SCIENCE AND THE FIELD OF ENVIRONMENTAL MATTERS AND NATURE CONSERVATION; and a fund supporting general research projects in the field of environment and energy, whose grants go to students and to research projects of universities, INSTITUTIONS, COMPANIES AND INDIVIDUALS. An energy company's community fund pays individuals and informal groups twice a year — no registration, no annual round to miss, and it is the sort of money a village committee can actually reach.

trackers.name: A bank's environment grants — what 250,000 and 500,000 KRONUR actually bought
trackers.desc: THE SCALE AND THE ODDS: in one round FIVE PROJECTS RECEIVED 500,000 KRONUR EACH AND TEN PROJECTS 250,000 KRONUR EACH, a total of FIVE MILLION KRONUR, from ABOUT 70 APPLICATIONS. The grants are intended to support projects IN THE FIELD OF ENVIRONMENTAL MATTERS AND NATURE CONSERVATION, with a jury seeking ambitious projects THAT HAVE CLEAR SIGNIFICANCE FOR ICELANDIC NATURE AND THE ECOSYSTEM. Fifteen winners from seventy applications is far better odds than the four-from-fifty-eight recorded in North Macedonia — and the sums are small enough that the application is short. AND WHAT THE MONEY WENT ON, which is the most useful part for a group wondering whether its own work qualifies: a LANDOWNERS' ASSOCIATION received a grant for LAND CONSERVATION in a named bay AND THE MANAGEMENT OF WALKING AND DRIVING TOURIST TRAFFIC IN THE AREA; a forestry committee got money to set up toilet facilities, an outdoor table, AND TO RENEW FENCES AND GATES; a travel association funded the making of footpaths and repairs to older paths; a national environmental body funded A COAST-CLEANING DRIVE; and a volunteer group has removed about 1,340 TONNES of rubbish from Iceland's nature across 140 CLEAN-UP PROJECTS. A landowners' association managing tourist traffic is exactly the kind of applicant a community group can be.

trackers.name: Landvernd — a federation of 40 MEMBER ASSOCIATIONS, not just 6,000 individuals
trackers.desc: THE STRUCTURE THAT MATTERS TO A LOCAL ICELANDIC GROUP: LANDVERND IS A FREE ASSOCIATION WHICH STANDS GUARD OVER ICELANDIC NATURE, and while THE MEMBERS OF LANDVERND ARE MORE THAN 6,000, the important number is the second one: 40 ASSOCIATIONS ARE AFFILIATED TO THE ORGANISATION. Iceland is among the least-worked buckets in this file. A body whose members include forty other associations is one a village society joins as an organisation, not one its residents join as individuals — which gives a small local group a national voice without dissolving into it. AND WHERE IT ACTS, which tells a community what it can be asked to do: THE ORGANISATION TAKES PART IN POLICY-MAKING, EDUCATION AND DECISION-MAKING IN MATTERS CONCERNING, FOR EXAMPLE, LAND USE, RESOURCES AND THE ENVIRONMENT IN ICELAND. Land use is named first among its fields, which is the one a development fight sits in. AND THE AIMS AS STATED, including the one most relevant to a damaged site: PROTECTION OF THE NATURE AND ENVIRONMENT OF ICELAND ON LAND, IN WATER AND IN THE AIR, SO THAT THEY ARE SPOILED AS LITTLE AS POSSIBLE, FOR US AND FOR COMING GENERATIONS, and RESTORATION OF SPOILED NATURE, NATURAL QUALITIES AND ENVIRONMENT IN THE MANNER THAT BEST SUITS NATURAL CONDITIONS. Founded in 1969, it has stood guard FOR HALF A CENTURY.

trackers.name: Commission for the Prevention of Corruption – Lobbying
trackers.desc: Slovenia's CPC runs a mandatory lobbying register and publishes lobbying contacts with officials. Notably, its scope extends to lobbying of the judicial branch — one of the few regimes worldwide that does so. — Holds to account: lobbyists & influence-seekers, top officials & cabinet — find who is lobbying whom, and meetings held; their assets, interests and integrity declarations.

trackers.name: Information Commissioner of Slovenia
trackers.desc: Slovenia's independent regulator for access to public information and data protection. — Holds to account: public bodies that hold records — find information-commissioner decisions and appeals.

trackers.name: Sodna praksa
trackers.desc: Official Slovenian case-law database maintained by the Supreme Court. · Find here: the case-law database of Slovenia's higher courts (Sodna praksa).

trackers.name: Information Commissioner of the Republic of Slovenia
trackers.desc: Independent state authority overseeing the right of access to public information (and data protection); acts as the appeals body against refusals and publishes its access-to-information decisions and non-binding opinions.

trackers.name: PIC — Zelena svetovalnica (free green legal advice line)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Slovenia's leading legal-protection-of-the-environment NGO, whose Zelena svetovalnica is an independent advice service that has given over 3,170 hours of free legal counselling on environmental protection, nature conservation, spatial planning and climate to NGOs, civil initiatives and individuals. Runs an environmental law clinic with the Ljubljana law faculty and intervenes in the drafting of environmental and spatial legislation. WHO IT SUITS: anyone actively fighting an environmental or spatial-planning problem in Slovenia — the door is explicitly open to unaffiliated individuals, not only registered organisations.

trackers.name: Justice and Environment — European green-law network
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the European network of environmental-law NGOs, whose national member here is PIC. Its fifteen members act as the environmental-law service point in their own countries, taking cases and intervening in legislative processes, while the network defends communities and nature in court and lodges infringement complaints against member-state governments. Its standing themes are access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, environmental assessment and pollution control. WHO IT SUITS: anyone who does not yet know which lawyer to call — knock on PIC's door first, and use the network only if your problem crosses a border. The network itself does not take individual cases; its members do. YOUR NATIONAL MEMBER IS Legal Center for the Protection of Human Rights and the Environment (PIC) (pic.si) — go to them, not to the network. J&E members serve as environmental law ‘service points’ in their countries, handling cases, participating in legislative processes and sometimes providing legal analyses and consultations for national governments. The network has 11 full and 4 associate members, and can launch infringement proceedings against faulty governments — a route a national body alone does not have. CURRENT SCOPE: access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, climate, environmental assessments, and the Environmental Liability Directive. It previously worked on waste, transport, health and Natura 2000, so an older document may overstate what it covers today.

trackers.name: Pod črto
trackers.desc: Slovenian nonprofit newsroom investigating corruption and systemic abuse of public money.

trackers.name: AJPES
trackers.desc: Slovenia's business register and public beneficial-ownership register (eRTR). — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find who really owns and controls them; their registration, directors and filings.
