WHAT ELSE IS ON THE MONEY MAP HERE: the European Commission has awarded 15 new grants amounting to over 2 million euro to support the actions of civil society organisations throughout Cyprus; and the Active Citizens Fund programme, run under the EEA and Norway Grants by a consortium including the NGO Support Centre — already filed here — gave particular emphasis to bi-communal cooperation and intercultural dialogue and to strengthening bilateral relations between Cypriot NGOs and organisations in Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway. AND THE OFFICE TO KNOW: Cyprus has a Commissioner for Volunteerism and NGOs, with a standing dialogue between the Minister of the Interior and voluntary organisations. Where a state has a commissioner for the sector, that office is the route to ask which scheme fits.

trackers.name: BirdLife Cyprus — it runs a nature reserve, and it got 69 villas refused
trackers.desc: WHAT IT HOLDS, which closes Cyprus's acquirer gap: Thkio Mosfilies, its first nature reserve and outdoor learning space, in the Famagusta district near the villages of Frenaros, Avgorou and Vrysoulles — its first targeted effort to create and maintain a rich and diverse habitat, nestled in a mosaic of pine woodland, carob scrub and open habitats, and an outdoor education space for the local communities. THE WINS IT RECORDS, which tell a community what is achievable: the Department of Environment REJECTED a proposal for a large-scale development of 69 LUXURY VILLAS at the entrance of Akamas, near a named beach; a landmark legal appeal for safeguarding the wild coastline of another named place; the first recorded breeding attempt among released griffon vultures; and completion of Cyprus's Article 12 bird status report. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND BIRDS: it defined 34 Important Bird Areas following BirdLife International's methodology, and IBAs have been recognised by the European Court of Justice as a scientifically sound basis for determining Special Protection Area boundaries — though in one case only 55 per cent of the IBA is covered by the current SPA boundaries. Where the designated boundary is narrower than the scientific one, the gap is itself the argument. Founded 2003 from the merger of two ornithological societies; offices in Kato Deftera, Nicosia.

trackers.name: The Cyprus environmental front — eight organisations on one Bern Convention complaint
trackers.desc: THE ROSTER, which is the free artefact Cyprus offers: a complaint on the Akamas peninsula to the Bern Convention was supported by the Federation of Environmental Organisations of Cyprus, BirdLife Cyprus, the Cyprus Wildlife Society, the Ecological Movement of Cyprus, Enalia Physis Environmental Research Centre, Friends of Akamas, Friends of the Earth Cyprus and the Initiative for the Protection of the Natural Coastline. A separate joint statement to the President was signed by five of them. Eight named organisations including a FEDERATION and a site-specific 'Friends of' group — the model for a community that wants its own name on the list. AND THE INTERNATIONAL LEVER THEY USED: the Bern Convention's Standing Committee recommends that the Government declare the whole of the Akamas peninsula a national park, a biosphere reserve or a protected area with comparable international protected status, managing it as a whole, including terrestrial and marine parts, in a sustainable, integrated way. A Bern Convention recommendation is a standing instruction to a government that a community can cite — this file has recorded the same lever working in Montenegro. AND WHAT THE MOVEMENT ASKS FOR BEYOND DESIGNATION: the setting up of a SPECIAL ENTITY FOR THE INTEGRATED MANAGEMENT of the peninsula, drawing on the experience of other Natura 2000 sites that are being properly managed. Their complaint notes that current laws are frequently disregarded as construction proceeds without the required permits.

trackers.name: Coucounis Law — and the mistake that got a neighbour's whole case thrown out
trackers.desc: THE ERROR IT DOCUMENTS, which would cost a Cypriot community everything: an owner of neighbouring property challenged a municipality's decision to authorise an apartment building — but filed the recourse ONLY against the town planning permit and failed to challenge the building permit. If he files only against the town planning permit, THE BUILDING PERMIT REMAINS VALID AND LEGAL and consequently the recourse is considered incomplete and DISMISSED AS INADMISSIBLE. Every affected person must file against BOTH the town planning and the building permit, and the firm cites a 2022 Administrative Court judgment showing exactly how the affected neighbour must act. The same applicant also failed to specify the existing or certainly upcoming damage from the construction. AND THE DUTY IT NAMES, which is the ground to run: the town planning authority is OBLIGED BY LAW to ensure that the independent operation, the comfortable possession and enjoyment of the development will not substantially affect THE AMENITIES OF THE AREA OR THE NEIGHBOURING PROPERTIES; and the issue of a town planning permit in disregard of the rights of the neighbour entitles him to invoke a LEGITIMATE INTEREST to apply for annulment. The authority must consider the applicable development plan and any other essential factor, BUT NOT EXTERNAL ones.

trackers.name: Cypriot environmental and planning practices — the 75-day clock, and who else to call
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE AND WHAT THEY COVER: a Cyprus-based boutique firm with offices in Nicosia and Paphos, publishing on environmental enforcement — including appeals against a regulator's decision NOT to grant an environmental permit, or against the CONDITIONS contained in one, and the enforcement powers of environmental regulators, where criminal liability and sanctions apply to anyone operating an installation or performing activities contrary to a requirement to obtain an environmental permit. THE CLOCK EVERY CYPRIOT OBJECTOR NEEDS: the right of recourse may be exercised within 75 DAYS from the date the decision is notified to the interested person, and some laws provide for a HIERARCHICAL REVIEW as an intermediary step before filing. AND THE ROUTE WHEN INFORMATION IS REFUSED: any person not content with the response, or lack of response, to a request for disclosure of ENVIRONMENTAL INFORMATION is entitled to apply for hierarchical review and/or lodge an administrative recourse. A refused information request is itself actionable — the same rule this file recorded in Lithuania. ALSO ON THE MAP: a Cypriot practice records a criminal appeal concerning use and alteration of a property's approved purpose without authorisation, where a municipality sought an injunction to suspend a business, and notes that courts can issue interim orders to halt unauthorised construction — a firm of 16 legal professionals. And a national land-use-and-zoning lawyer directory lists practices by city.

trackers.name: The Laona Foundation — it was set up to prove that mass tourism was not the answer
trackers.desc: WHY IT EXISTS, and it is the clearest founding story in this file: by the mid-1980s concern for the fate of the unspoilt western peninsula made Friends of the Earth realise that SPECIFIC ACTION WAS NECESSARY IN ORDER TO DEMONSTRATE TO LOCALS AND GOVERNMENT ALIKE THAT MASS TOURISM DEVELOPMENT WAS NOT A SOLUTION TO THE ECONOMIC PROBLEMS OF THE AREA, BUT RATHER THE PRESERVATION OF ITS NATURAL BEAUTY AND TRADITIONAL CULTURE. A planning consultant was brought in, an EU-funded project set up in 1989, and three years later it became a foundation aiming to support rural communities. Arguing that conservation IS the economic case, rather than a cost, is the argument a village facing a resort needs — and here an organisation was built specifically to prove it. WHAT IT STANDS FOR NOW, in its own list: regenerating the Cypriot countryside sustainably and SUPPORTING ITS COMMUNITIES; preserving the natural and cultural heritage, especially landscape, architecture and traditions; protecting distinctive areas such as the Akamas peninsula and THE TERRACED LANDSCAPES of Cyprus; CONFRONTING DESERTIFICATION and preserving the soil; encouraging sustainable tourism AS AN OPPORTUNITY, NOT AS A PANACEA; and sharing expertise with NGOs in Cyprus and abroad. It participates as an observer in the meetings of the LANDSCAPE CONVENTION at the Council of Europe, and works with Friends of the Earth Cyprus and a named environmental institute.

trackers.name: The Cyprus Environmental Directory — the island's green organisations, one by one
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a compiled directory of Cypriot environmental organisations, each entered with its aims, activities and contact details — the kind of artefact this file has found most useful in every country, because it turns one fight into a list of possible allies. WHAT ITS ENTRIES CARRY, from the ones visible: a research centre described as a non-governmental, non-profit organisation headquartered in the capital which, THROUGH RESEARCH, IN-DEPTH SCIENTIFIC STUDY AND EDUCATION, aims at effective contribution to the protection of the LAND AND MARINE environment, and which takes part in EU programmes for NGOs as well as BI-COMMUNAL PROGRAMMES; and a body whose stated purpose includes contributing to the study, protection and advertisement of the NATURAL BEAUTIES AND HISTORICAL MONUMENTS of Cyprus. An organisation that already does in-depth scientific study is the one to ask for the survey a planning objection needs — and the directory says which those are. AND THE FUNDER NAMED THROUGHOUT IT: a private foundation dedicated to the preservation of the cultural and natural heritage of Greece and Cyprus, which awards every year a number of educational grants and is recorded elsewhere in this file as the annual funder behind the island's conservation foundation.

trackers.name: Friends of the Earth Cyprus — a registered charity since 1993, with its bank details published
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: a non-governmental, non-political, non-profit environmental organisation established in 1993 and based in Limassol, which is A REGISTERED ASSOCIATION AND A RECOGNISED CHARITY IN THE REPUBLIC OF CYPRUS, with roughly 300 to 500 members and a youth section. Registered charity status is what lets a body receive a legacy or a donation of land, and this one publishes its full bank account number, IBAN and SWIFT code on its own site so money can be sent without an intermediary. ITS PLACE IN THE ISLAND'S NETWORK, which is the practical value: it is a member group of Friends of the Earth Europe and Friends of the Earth International, and also of THE FEDERATION OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND ECOLOGICAL ORGANISATIONS OF CYPRUS and the European Environmental Bureau. Where a country has a federation of environmental organisations, one letter reaches all of them. AND ITS STATED GOAL, in its own words: to raise awareness on the importance of preserving the natural environment and to campaign for solutions to environmental and social problems by promoting sustainable policies, envisioning a society built upon peoples' sovereignty and participation. Its address, telephone and fax are published by its international federation.

trackers.name: The Cyprus Department of Forests — it holds TEN national forest parks, with a phone and a PO box
trackers.desc: WHAT IT HOLDS, and this is the answer to Cyprus's thin land bucket: TEN NATIONAL FOREST PARKS, each with a founding year, district and area — running from a 26-hectare park near a coastal resort and a 45-hectare park inside the capital's suburbs, up to a 4,523-hectare mountain park and a 9,147-hectare park in the Troodos range, with a national park proposed for the Akamas peninsula. A state department that has already turned ten separate places into national forest parks, including small urban ones, is the body to bring a neighbourhood site to — the 26- and 45-hectare parks show the floor is low. AND ITS STATED FIELDS OF WORK: afforestation and silviculture; production of timber and non-wood products; PROTECTION AGAINST FIRES AND OTHER HAZARDS; CONSERVATION OF ECOSYSTEMS, FLORA, FAUNA AND HERITAGE; LOCAL PLANS AND VILLAGE DEVELOPMENT; and institutional reform and capacity building — with a mission to serve the Government AND THE PEOPLE, for the benefit of all sections of society. A forest department with a standing programme line for LOCAL PLANS AND VILLAGE DEVELOPMENT is one a village can approach about its own surroundings. Its Nicosia PO box, telephone and fax are published, and it has district offices; it also holds and runs the aerial firefighting contracts.

trackers.name: The Akamas action plan — four named authorities, two million euro, and an open complaint file
trackers.desc: WHAT EXISTS AND WHO RUNS IT: an action plan for the peninsula developed by the Department of Environment as beneficiary, to be implemented ALONG WITH OTHER COMPETENT AUTHORITIES — the DEPARTMENT OF FORESTS, THE DEPARTMENT OF FISHERIES AND MARINE RESEARCH, AND THE GAME AND FAUNA SERVICE — with an estimated budget of 2 MILLION EURO and actions already being implemented, eligible for co-funding from the European Regional Development Fund. Four named authorities on one plan is four doors, and a community should write to the one whose remit its own problem falls under. AND WHAT THE MONEY BUYS, which a community can ask to have extended to its site: MONITORING THE GOOD CONSERVATION STATUS of the habitats and species — populations of important species of PLANTS, AMPHIBIANS, REPTILES, BATS, MAMMALS, SEA TURTLES, FISH, SEALS, BIRDS AND ARTHROPODS — alongside management actions. Consistent and coordinated conservation measures are implemented in ALL NESTING BEACHES of the peninsula and a neighbouring Natura site, through a yearly marine turtle programme. AND THE STANDING FILE THIS SITS IN: a Council of Europe complaint case-file remains OPEN on Cyprus concerning the peninsula, and campaigners' demands recorded there include declaring the whole peninsula a national park, a biosphere reserve or a protected area with comparable international protected status.

trackers.name: Terra Cypria on the Akamas — it names the UNUSED TOOL for landowners inside a protected area
trackers.desc: THE INSTRUMENT IT POINTS AT, which exists on paper and is not being used: the foundation, expressing concern for the future of the peninsula if the proposed Local Plan takes effect, PROPOSES THE PASSAGE OF A 2011 BILL FOR THE TRANSFER OF DEVELOPMENT RIGHTS. Transferring the right to build off a protected parcel and onto another site pays the owner without anything being built where it matters — the answer to the owner who says they cannot afford to leave their land alone. The foundation's headline is that these are TOOLS AVAILABLE FOR LANDOWNERS THAT THE GOVERNMENT HAS LEFT UNUSED. AND THE GROUNDS IT ARGUES ON: the peninsula is one of the most important and most beautiful natural areas of Cyprus. Part of it belongs to the European NATURA 2000 network of protected areas because of the VERY IMPORTANT BIODIVERSITY it hosts. For that reason it requires PARTICULAR LOCAL MANAGEMENT precisely because of the environmental particularities of the area, TAKING INTO ACCOUNT THE NEEDS OF THE INHABITANTS OF THE SURROUNDING COMMUNITIES. Arguing for local management that names residents' needs is what separates a durable designation campaign from one the village will fight. A companion page records the foundation's judgment on the same area after two years: inaction, non-implementation of decisions and a complete absence of accountability.

trackers.name: The Cyprus Lands and Surveys apallotriosi page — A COMMUNITY ASSEMBLY can be the expropriating authority
trackers.desc: WHO CAN EXPROPRIATE IN CYPRUS, published by the Department of Lands and Surveys itself: subject to a named article of the Constitution and the Compulsory Acquisition Law of 1962, ANY PROPERTY MAY BE COMPULSORILY ACQUIRED FOR PURPOSES OF PUBLIC BENEFIT, and the acquiring authority may be (a) THE REPUBLIC, (b) A MUNICIPAL AUTHORITY, (c) A COMMUNITY ASSEMBLY, or (d) A LEGAL PERSON OF PUBLIC LAW OR A PUBLIC-BENEFIT ORGANISATION to which the right is granted. Cyprus had two land-acquisition entries filed. A community assembly is named as an expropriating authority in its own right — so in Cyprus the village body itself, not only the state, can acquire land for public benefit. And a public-benefit organisation can be granted the same right, which is the route for a conservation body that has no purchase money of its own. AND WHY THE PAGE MATTERS BOTH WAYS: the same law and the same authorities govern a taking a community may want to resist, so the statute and its article numbers are the first thing to read whether the acquisition is wanted or fought. The department publishes it as a standing reference alongside its other land procedures.

trackers.name: The five Cypriot environmental organisations that act together — named, and still active
trackers.desc: THE FIVE BODIES A CYPRIOT COMMUNITY CAN APPROACH, named together in a joint action: TERRA CYPRIA, BIRDLIFE CYPRUS, FRIENDS OF THE EARTH CYPRUS, THE CYPRUS WILDLIFE SOCIETY, and CYPRUS NATURAL COASTLINE — the INITIATIVE FOR THE SALVATION OF THE NATURAL COASTS, calling on the President to take immediate action for the substantive protection of nature, and to keep his environmental commitments under the governing programme. Five organisations that already act as a bloc are five doors that open on one knock — and a local group joining an existing coalition inherits its access. AND THE ASSESSMENT ONE OF THEM GAVE ON NATIONAL RADIO, which is the language a community can borrow: speaking for one of the organisations, a named representative stressed that THE ENVIRONMENT IS UNDER ATTACK FROM EVERY SIDE, while THE MINISTRY HAS FAILED IN ITS TASK, and the President must now intervene. AND WHAT THEIR JOINT LETTER RESTS ON, which is the strongest available lever in Cyprus: the need for IMMEDIATE COMPLIANCE WITH THE EUROPEAN ENVIRONMENTAL ACQUIS, since CYPRUS CONTINUES TO FACE SERIOUS INFRINGEMENT PROCEEDINGS, PARTICULARLY IN RELATION TO THE NATURA 2000 NETWORK. A live infringement proceeding against the state is a pressure a local objection can attach itself to. They ask for THE ADEQUATE DESIGNATION, EFFECTIVE PROTECTION AND INTEGRATED MANAGEMENT of Natura 2000 areas, and the IMPROVEMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES.

trackers.name: Cyprus Natural Coastline — a CITIZENS' initiative fighting for the coast, 6,000 strong
trackers.desc: A NAMED CYPRIOT CITIZENS' BODY, and the only one of the five coalition members that is not a professional organisation: it describes itself as A CITIZENS INITIATIVE DEMANDING AND FIGHTING FOR THE PROTECTION OF THE NATURAL COASTLINE IN CYPRUS, with 6,080 followers. A citizens' initiative that sits at the table with the national conservation foundations is proof that an unincorporated group of residents can hold that seat — it is the model a new local campaign should look at before deciding it must first become a registered association. AND WHERE IT HAS REACHED: it is named as a co-signatory, alongside TERRA CYPRIA, BIRDLIFE CYPRUS, FRIENDS OF THE EARTH CYPRUS and the CYPRUS WILDLIFE SOCIETY, of open letters sent TO THE PRESIDENT OF THE REPUBLIC over the protection of a named peninsula and the Natura 2000 network. HONEST LIMIT ON THIS ENTRY: the initiative's public presence found here is a social-media page giving its purpose and its following, not a constitution, an office or a contact procedure. It is filed as A ROUTE INTO AN ACTIVE COASTAL CAMPAIGN, not as an incorporated body a community can instruct.

trackers.name: Selling your building rights instead of your land — the transfer route, and the bill for it
trackers.desc: A ROUTE THAT PAYS AN OWNER WITHOUT ANYONE BUYING THE LAND, which is the missing answer wherever protection strands a landowner: a bill PROVIDES FOR PRIVATE PROPERTY OWNERS WHO HAVE BUILDING RIGHTS BUT CANNOT UTILISE THEM FOR VARIOUS REASONS, TO SELL THEM OR TRANSFER THEM TO GOVERNMENT-OWNED LAND ELSEWHERE, IN AREAS SPECIFIED BY THE INTERIOR MINISTRY. Cyprus has one of the smallest bases in this file. The owner sells the right to build, keeps or gives up the land, and the building happens somewhere the state chooses — which converts an objector's opponent into a compensated party without a purchase fund. AND THE PRECEDENT THAT SHOWS IT WORKS: A SIMILAR PRACTICE ALREADY EXISTS FOR OWNERS OF LISTED BUILDINGS WHERE STRICT DEVELOPMENT CONDITIONS EXIST. UNDER A 2002 ACT, OWNERS CAN SELL THEIR THEORETICAL BUILDING RIGHTS TO BUILD AN EXTRA FLOOR OR ROOM, FOR EXAMPLE, TO PROPERTY OWNERS IN OTHER AREAS NOT BOUND BY SUCH RESTRICTIONS. The heritage sector has run this since 2002, so a community can point at a working domestic precedent rather than a foreign one. AND THE COMPLAINT THAT MAKES IT URGENT, from the foundation's named executive director: they see A BILL LYING DORMANT SINCE 2011 AND CONSTANT GOVERNMENT STATEMENTS ABOUT FINALISING THE LOCAL PLAN WITHIN MONTHS, WITHOUT THE EXISTENCE OF RELEVANT LEGISLATION TO TRANSFER THE DEVELOPMENT RIGHTS.

trackers.name: A foundation that sits on the government's OWN assessment committees
trackers.desc: A CONSERVATION BODY WITH A SEAT INSIDE THE PROCESS, not only outside it: WE ALSO PARTICIPATE IN VARIOUS PARLIAMENTARY COMMITTEES OF THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES, AS WELL AS GOVERNMENTAL TECHNICAL COMMITTEES ASSESSING THE ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT OF PROJECTS AND PROGRAMMES. Cyprus has one of the smallest bases in this file. A body that sits on the technical committee assessing a project's environmental impact is in the room where the assessment is written — earlier than any objection, and the earliest point of entry recorded anywhere in this file. AND HOW IT DESCRIBES ITS FIRST OBJECTIVE, which tells a community what to ask it for: THE FIRST OBJECTIVE OF THE FOUNDATION IS THE APPLICATION OF PRESSURE FOR BETTER ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION. OUR POLICY ACTIONS ARE ACHIEVED THROUGH CONTINUOUS COMMUNICATION AND AWARENESS OF PEOPLE IN KEY POSITIONS WHO CAN INFLUENCE OUR DAILY LIVES, SUCH AS POLITICIANS AND TECHNOCRATS. THIS IS DONE THROUGH LETTERS, MEETINGS, PUBLICATIONS, SEMINARS AND EXHIBITIONS. Naming technocrats alongside politicians as the target is unusual and correct, because the official who drafts the assessment decides more than the minister who signs it. Founded in 1992 AS A CHARITABLE, NON-PROFIT ORGANISATION, it also runs a field studies centre for schools and universities.

trackers.name: Pakistan Information Commission (PIC)
trackers.desc: National right-to-information authority; the Pakistan Information Commission is the independent federal enforcement body under the Right of Access to Information Act 2017 — deciding complaints and directing federal bodies (provinces have separate commissions), Pakistan.

trackers.name: Punjab Information Commission (Pakistan)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (FOI oversight body); Punjab Information Commission (Pakistan) — the national authority overseeing citizens’ right of access to public information (ICIC member).

trackers.name: Punjab Lok Sujag
trackers.desc: Pakistani investigative outlet reporting on governance and public resources.

trackers.name: Pakistan Information Commission
trackers.desc: Federal commission enforcing the Right of Access to Information Act — appeals against denials by executive bodies. — Holds to account: public bodies that hold records — find information-commissioner decisions and appeals.

trackers.name: Election Commission – Asset Declarations
trackers.desc: Legislator / public-official financial interest & asset declarations.

trackers.name: Justice Project Pakistan (JPP)
trackers.desc: Lahore legal-action NGO representing prisoners facing the death penalty and torture; maintains an open death-penalty database and data-driven research on executions, detention and prison conditions in Pakistan.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Pakistan
trackers.desc: Supreme Court of Pakistan — supreme court (Pakistan).

trackers.name: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics
trackers.desc: Pakistan's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Pakistan.

trackers.name: PPRA
trackers.desc: Pakistan's Public Procurement Regulatory Authority tender notices. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Pakistan, and for how much.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Pakistan
trackers.desc: Official Supreme Court judgments and case information. · Find here: judgments and case information of the Supreme Court of Pakistan.

trackers.name: SECP
trackers.desc: Pakistan's Securities and Exchange Commission corporate registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Pakistan
trackers.desc: Supreme Court of Pakistan — supreme court in Pakistan (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: Find your province's act first — there is no national one
trackers.desc: WILDLIFE AND ENVIRONMENT ARE PROVINCIAL SUBJECTS, so no single national statute governs your site. In Khyber Pakhtunkhwa it is the KP Wildlife and Biodiversity Act 2015, replacing the NWFP Wildlife Act 1975 — and it must be read with the KP Province Forest Ordinance 2002, because where the two conflict on ‘acts prohibited’ the Forest Ordinance prevails. WHAT THE ACT GIVES YOU: a Wildlife Board chaired by the Chief Minister with the Environment Secretary as its Secretary, so the escalation point is political and named; provisions on protected areas and expressly on participatory management; power to constitute a Conservancy, which is the community-facing designation to ask about; and power to demarcate a National Park. HOLD THEM TO THE DEADLINE: an application to the Wildlife authority is to be disposed of within 60 days of receipt. A DIRECT PRECEDENT FOR URBAN ENCROACHMENT: Parliament passed the Islamabad Nature Conservation and Wildlife Management Act 2023 specifically to strengthen protection of Margallah National Wildlife Park against unregulated urban expansion.

trackers.name: Two warnings — unresolved ownership, and unstandardised management plans
trackers.desc: 1. A DESIGNATION DOES NOT SETTLE OWNERSHIP. Chitral Gol National Park was declared on 18 October 1984 — yet the case of ownership of the Park and of rights and privileges was recorded as still sub judice, with the technical team supplying the Wildlife Department scenarios for different court outcomes. Establish who owns the land and who holds customary rights before relying on a designation, because protection can sit on top of an unresolved title for decades. 2. THERE IS NO CODE FOR PROTECTED-AREA MANAGEMENT PLANS. Forest working plans follow an approved Forest Working Plan Code nationwide, but protected-area management planning is not yet institutionalised or standardised by provincial wildlife departments — so a designation may arrive with no enforceable management plan behind it, and asking for the plan is a fair and awkward question. AN ALLY FOR FOREST-RIGHTS HOLDERS: forest communities have criticised successive national forest policies as contrary to their rights and interests, and the Forest Ordinance 2002 has been targeted as exploitative by Sarhad Awami Forestry Itehad, representing small forest holders from Dir-Kohistan, Swat and other regions. AND A NEGOTIATED WIN: at Chitral Gol, communities agreed not to graze goats inside the park, with some villages giving up goats entirely — recorded as the cornerstone of community integration in the park's conservation.

trackers.name: WWF-Pakistan Small Grants — an individual can apply
trackers.desc: RUNNING SINCE 1986, and unusually open. It supports grassroots level organisations, research-based institutions, researchers and students — and its stated value is enabling small-scale conservation work and field projects by individual scientists as well as by institutions. Very few funds in this map admit an individual, which matters where no registered organisation exists yet: you can start the evidence work before you have a constitution. Its purpose also includes building the capacity of small grassroots organisations, not just funding outputs. PRIORITIES TO NAME IF THEY FIT YOUR SITE: marine turtles, snow leopards, the Indus River dolphin, sharks and vultures; and the critical ecosystems — mangrove forests, the Indus River Delta and coniferous forests. ALSO IN PAKISTAN: the GEF Small Grants Programme funds CSOs and CBOs directly with special focus on Indigenous Peoples, women and youth, and the share flowing directly to community organisations was raised to 72 percent for GEF-8 core projects, up from 62 in GEF-7.

trackers.name: PPAF Small Grants — funding to build your governance documents
trackers.desc: THE ANSWER TO A BARRIER THAT RECURS ACROSS THIS MAP. Finland, Italy, Poland, Greece and Hungary all gate environmental funding on the wording of your own constitution — and PPAF's Small Grants Project exists precisely to give technical assistance to small or new partner organisations to define their role and develop SOPs, by-laws and internal control systems, enhancing their capability rather than funding a single output. It is money to become fundable. PPAF is Pakistan's leading poverty reduction agency, receiving large annual government allocations alongside corporate and individual contributions. CHECK YOUR DISTRICT IS IN SCOPE — coverage is targeted at vulnerable areas, recorded as Balochistan (Khuzdar, Chagai, Kech, Zhob, Panjgur, Barkhan) and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (Torghar, Kohistan, Buner, Lower Dir, Upper Dir, Bannu, Battagram, Mohmand, Kurram). PPAF works through partner organisations: MGPO, a non-profit working with mountain communities since 2001, has run community management and flood relief with PPAF support in Gilgit-Baltistan and maintains its own flood fund for District Ghanche.

trackers.name: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
trackers.desc: Sub-national government portal (Pakistan) — entry point to this unit's budget, procurement and finance information. Formerly listed as North-West Frontier Province, renamed Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in 2010.

trackers.name: Centre for Environmental Justice (CEJ)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Sri Lanka's most active environmental litigator — files fundamental-rights and writ petitions in the Supreme Court and Court of Appeal against deforestation, sand mining, quarrying, wetland filling, hazardous waste, coastal reclamation and defective land-use decisions, and publishes its ongoing and completed case lists. It forced the return of illegally imported waste containers to the UK and litigates the X-Press Pearl marine pollution disaster. It also files comments on EIAs and runs a scoring tool for reading them. WHO IT SUITS: a Sri Lankan community facing clearing, mining, filling or a project approved on a weak EIA — CEJ takes strategic cases, usually as petitioner or co-petitioner, and is not a general legal-aid service.

trackers.name: Environmental Foundation (Guarantee) Limited (EFL)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Sri Lanka's oldest environmental litigator, founded in 1981 and incorporated under the Companies Act precisely so that it would have standing to sue in its own name — a paired legal and science operation in which researchers build the technical case the lawyers then argue. Its own site records more than 100 cases filed; reported wins include keeping Galle Face Green a public space, the Eppawala phosphate and Kandalama hotel cases, and the air-pollution case that made vehicle emissions testing mandatory. WHO IT SUITS: a community whose fight turns on evidence as much as argument. EFL is known for a deliberately neutral, non-campaigning posture, which serves a technical challenge well and an outright confrontation less well than a movement litigator would.

trackers.name: Friends of the Earth Asia Pacific
trackers.desc: The Asia Pacific regional structure of Friends of the Earth International, formed in 2008, whose member groups work on community-based struggles against destructive projects, particularly mining and other extractive industries, alongside Indigenous peoples, peasant farmers, fisherfolk and trade unions. WHO TO ENLIST: the national member group nearest the project. In this region Friends of the Earth International's own directory names groups in Bangladesh (BELA, the Bangladesh Environmental Lawyers' Association), India, Indonesia (WALHI), Japan, Malaysia (Sahabat Alam Malaysia), Nepal, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines (the Legal Rights and Natural Resources Center), South Korea and Sri Lanka. You CAN: reach an organisation that already works community-side in your own country, and draw regional weight onto a local fight. For activists: in several of these countries the Friends of the Earth affiliate is the most experienced community-side environmental body there is.

trackers.name: Legal Aid Commission — 77 centres, focused on litigation
trackers.desc: SEVENTY-SEVEN CENTRES, AND THEY LITIGATE. The Legal Aid Commission was established by Legal Aid Law No. 27 of 1978 and runs 77 legal aid centres island-wide including the Colombo centre under head office — and the stated main focus of the centres is litigation, not advice alone, which is what separates it from a helpline. Its 9 members are 3 nominated by the justice ministry and 6 by the Bar Council of Sri Lanka, so the profession holds the majority. THRESHOLD, AND WHY TO ASK ANYWAY: legal aid goes to ‘deserving persons’ with monthly income of Rs 15,000 or less — but the Commission states the income level is relaxed in special circumstances, for example representation of women seeking maintenance. Do not self-exclude on income without asking.

trackers.name: Land Acquisition Act — the objection right and the 14-day window
trackers.desc: WHEN THE STATE IS TAKING YOUR LAND, THIS IS THE SEQUENCE. A section 2 notice is exhibited in conspicuous places in Sinhala, Tamil and English saying land in the area is required for a public purpose. The section 4 notice is your objection point: it must state that written objections may be made to the specified Secretary to the Ministry and must allow not less than 14 days. THE HEARING IS A RIGHT, SO ASK FOR IT: under section 4(4) the Secretary must consider objections and must give every person who objects an opportunity to be heard before recommending to the Minister. Later, a section 7 notice is gazetted in all three languages — and in newspapers where the value is thought to exceed 500 rupees — stating that compensation claims may be made to the named Acquiring Officer. WATCH THE URGENCY SECTIONS: sections 38 and 38A allow immediate possession on grounds of urgency at any time after the section 2 notice is first exhibited — so act on the section 2 notice, not the section 4 one, because urgency can overtake the ordinary objection window.

trackers.name: Compensation, inquiries and the gap to raise in your objection
trackers.desc: A HANDBOOK ON THE ACT from the Law & Society Trust, plus the details that decide compensation. KEEP EVERY ENVELOPE: where a compensation inquiry is adjourned and cannot resume on the notified date, notice of the new date must be sent by registered post to reach claimants at least 7 days before — service dates are how procedural challenges get built. VALUATION follows the Land Acquisition Regulations 2008, approved 17 March 2009 and applying where intention to acquire was published on or after that date; where part of a land is taken and the remnant is worth proportionately less on its own, compensation should be proportionate to the value of the main land. TAKE ADVICE BEFORE ACCEPTING ANY PAYMENT — the timing of accepting tendered compensation relative to appealing matters, and a question of law goes to the Court of Appeal by written petition. THE ARGUMENT TO PUT IN YOUR OBJECTION: the Act contains no requirement for impact assessments before section 2 or section 4 notices are issued — the Minister may allow investigation afterwards but has no duty to assess impact before selecting the land, which analysts identify as a principle of the National Involuntary Resettlement Policy never written into the legislation.

trackers.name: GEF Small Grants Programme — direct to CBOs, but only in three landscapes
trackers.desc: MONEY THAT GOES DIRECTLY TO COMMUNITY ORGANISATIONS, not through an intermediary — up to USD 50,000, though in practice the average is USD 20,000–25,000 and SGP usually asks for 50 percent co-funding, so budget for that before planning around the headline. Focus areas include biodiversity, climate adaptation and land degradation and sustainable forest management. THE STEP MOST APPLICANTS MISS: a national CBO or NGO contacts the SGP National Coordinator to receive the guidelines and forms — there is no generic download route, the country team is the entry point, alongside a National Steering Committee. A proposal must show how it meets GEF SGP criteria, how it aligns with the SGP Country Programme Strategy, and that it comes from a national CBO or NGO. SRI LANKA IS GEOGRAPHICALLY TARGETED — CHECK THIS FIRST: Operational Phase 7 supports 3 landscapes only — the Colombo urban wetlands, the Knuckles conservation forest and World Heritage site, and the coastal region from Mannar island to Jaffna. Outside those, a project does not fit the current phase. SCALE OF A ROUND: one signing entered 29 agreements with community organisations — 20 community grants plus 3 capacity development, 3 knowledge management and 3 social enterprise grants. Sri Lanka is an upgraded country programme, and special consideration goes to indigenous peoples, women and youth. Grievances about the programme, including fund management, go to the National Coordinator.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.desc: The Asia Pacific regional structure of Friends of the Earth International, formed in 2008, whose member groups work on community-based struggles against destructive projects, particularly mining and other extractive industries, alongside Indigenous peoples, peasant farmers, fisherfolk and trade unions. WHO TO ENLIST: the national member group nearest the project. In this region Friends of the Earth International's own directory names groups in Bangladesh (BELA, the Bangladesh Environmental Lawyers' Association), India, Indonesia (WALHI), Japan, Malaysia (Sahabat Alam Malaysia), Nepal, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines (the Legal Rights and Natural Resources Center), South Korea and Sri Lanka. trackers.name: Bangladesh Environmental Lawyers Association (BELA)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the organisation whose 1997 case persuaded Bangladesh's Supreme Court to recognise public-interest litigation at all, opening standing to representative civil-society organisations and to individual public-interested litigants. That precedent is the single most important lever in the country for anyone without a personal stake in a project. Founded in 1992, BELA has filed more than 350 PILs on river and industrial pollution, wetland encroachment, hill cutting, ship-breaking and compensation for losses inflicted by development projects, and was joint winner of the Tang Prize in Rule of Law in 2020. WHO IT SUITS: individuals or communities affected by an environmental problem — and unusually, there is a published intake route. Its legal cell takes applications by email, replies within 15 days, then meets the applicant, scrutinises documents and conducts a field verification before deciding whether to file. Screened, but genuinely open.

trackers.name: District and Union Legal Aid — free lawyer down to union level
trackers.desc: THE STRUCTURE REACHES BELOW THE DISTRICT. District Legal Aid Offices sit inside district judge court buildings across Bangladesh, and Union Legal Aid Committees operate at union level — the lowest administrative tier — expressly to reach grassroots communities, which is rare anywhere. There is also a Supreme Court Legal Aid Office (from 2015) and Labour Law Legal Aid Cells at the labour courts in Dhaka and Chattogram. It is run by NLASO, a statutory body under the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs. INCOME THRESHOLDS under clause 2 of the Legal Aid Services Policy: annual income under Tk 1.5 lakh for a Supreme Court case, under Tk 1 lakh for other courts — and those receiving income-related benefits may also qualify. CHECK A 2025 CHANGE FIRST: from 1 July 2025 mandatory mediation was introduced under 9 laws listed in the schedule to the Legal Aid Services (Amendment) Ordinance 2025, so for those matters mediation comes before litigation. NON-STATE OPTIONS if you do not qualify or want a second route: Ain o Salish Kendra, BLAST, the Bangladesh National Women Lawyers' Association, Madaripur Legal Aid Association and BRAC.

trackers.name: Khas land — the award is the easy part, possession is not
trackers.desc: GOVERNMENT LAND THE LANDLESS CAN CLAIM. Khas land covers agricultural, non-agricultural and water bodies, owned by the Ministry of Land with Collectors as custodians. Research puts distributable khas land above 10 million bighas against a landless population of more than 68 percent — district averages of roughly 1.14 acres per landless household, 0.37 acres for agricultural khas alone, with at least 14 of 64 districts above that. NOW THE PART THAT DECIDES OUTCOMES: receiving khas land and holding it are different things. In one documented case a woman was properly enlisted and received 0.34 acres with proper documents but could not take possession — the plot had long been cultivated by a local rich farmer, who on learning of the award sold it without documents to another influential person. Research records a complicated mechanism with high risk of mismanagement, landless people often not involved in the listing process while local influentials were, and a network of influentials as the main threat to proper distribution. PLAN FOR POSSESSION, NOT JUST THE PAPER — the literature's own conclusion is to organise a community movement for access rather than applying individually, and to press for proper identification of khas land, periodic survey and maintained public records of what is available. Note also that under the 1995 non-agricultural policy, religious and charitable organisations settle at 10 percent of determined market price.

trackers.name: Social forestry — planting on state land under a benefit-sharing agreement
trackers.desc: THE OTHER ROUTE ONTO STATE LAND. The Forest Department involves landless people, including women, in planting on forest land, marginal government land and roadside strips under participatory benefit sharing agreements, under which participants have received their share. It grew through tripartite agreements with Zila Parishads and the Roads and Highway Department for roadside plantation — the model to copy for strip land, since it settles in advance who signs and who benefits. THE CONTEXT THAT EXPLAINS THE PRESSURE: forest land managed by the Forest Department, Land Ministry and private owners is about 2,460 thousand hectares, 16.85 percent of the country — but actual forest cover does not exceed 6 percent, and per capita forest land at 0.022 ha is the lowest in the world. BE REALISTIC: benefit-share distribution has been described as small-scale, segmented and at an early stage with little published documentation, so get the sharing terms written into the agreement rather than relying on precedent.

trackers.name: BCCTF NGO window — apply through PKSF, not the Trust
trackers.desc: THE NATIONAL CLIMATE FUND, PAID FROM BANGLADESH'S OWN BUDGET. Established under the Climate Change Trust Act 2010 under the environment ministry, BCCTF was the first national climate fund created by a least developed country and is resourced entirely from national revenue rather than donor pledges. 66 percent is earmarked for resilience-building projects and 34 percent reserved for responding to climate-induced disasters, so two thirds is the realistic project pot. WRITE TO THE BCCSAP: projects must contribute to implementing the Bangladesh Climate Change Strategy and Action Plan 2009 — its priority actions, not general environmental aims. A Technical Committee headed by the ministry reviews proposals, with expert sub-committees for highly technical ones, and the Trustee Board approves. IF YOU ARE AN NGO, THE ENTRY POINT IS PKSF, the government-owned foundation that oversees the NGO window — not the Trust directly. Both governmental and non-governmental institutions working in Bangladesh are eligible.

trackers.name: PKSF — what the NGO window actually pays, and what disqualifies you
trackers.desc: THE RECORD OF AN ACTUAL ROUND, so you can judge the effort. BCCTF provided about BDT 25.06 crore to PKSF for 63 NGOs; PKSF disbursed about BDT 23.85 crore to 61 of them for plantation, sanitation, food security, capacity building and research, with 57 receiving the full sanctioned amount in 3 instalments. BE READY FOR THE REPORTING BURDEN: those 57 submitted a Project Completion Report and Audit Report, and government auditors audited activities at both PKSF and NGO level. A DISQUALIFIER WORTH CHECKING BEFORE YOU APPLY: two NGOs received no disbursement at all because they were defaulters under a Bangladesh Bank housing loan project — an unrelated financial default blocked their climate funding entirely, and undisbursed money from six problematic NGOs was refunded to the Trust. THE OTHER WINDOW: the donor-funded BCCRF put 90 percent into public sector projects and 10 percent through NGOs, again via PKSF, financing community-based adaptation on food security, social protection, health, disaster management and infrastructure. RECORDED HONESTLY: Bangladeshi civil society was strongly critical of the multi-donor model, preferring a state-run board, with concerns about 10–15 percent management fees charged by World Bank consultants and about democratic access to adaptation funding.

trackers.name: Cross Cultural Foundation (CrCF)
trackers.desc: Founded in 2002, The Cross Cultural Foundation (CrCF) is a Thailand-based nonprofit foundation working to ensure equal access to justice for all people in Thailand by monitoring and investigating human rights abuses; advocating for and promoting a vision of justice that empowers people to understand and realize their rights; and the direct protection of human rights through legal strategies. Within this integrated purview, CrCF has focused on initiatives that enhance access to justice for Thai citizens as well as indigenous and minority populations, including migrant workers, refugees or defenders in exile, stateless persons, and victims of conflict; the prevention of torture of human rights defenders; and providing free legal aid and tangible assistance to vulnerable groups in Thailand’s southern border provinces. We work closely with international human rights networks to empower and include indigenous and minority populations.

trackers.name: พ.ร.บ.ป่าชุมชน 2562 — community forests, after a 26-year campaign
trackers.desc: THAILAND'S COMMUNITY FOREST ACT, published in the Royal Gazette on 29 May 2019 — 8 chapters, 104 sections. Its purpose is to promote communities acting together with the state in conserving, restoring, managing, maintaining and taking benefit from natural resources, environment and biodiversity. CHECK WHICH PARTS WERE IN FORCE WHEN: most of the Act applied the day after publication, but chapters 4–8 and sections 97–103 took effect 180 days later — so older commentary may describe a different legal position. The Forest Department publishes the Act and its subordinate instruments with English versions available for download. CIVIL SOCIETY PUSHED FOR THIS LAW FOR MORE THAN 26 YEARS — worth knowing both as the honest timescale of statutory change and because it means the movement infrastructure around community forestry in Thailand is deep and long-established. A national policy committee chaired at Deputy Prime Minister level now drives establishment of community forests, builds the countrywide community forest network as the supporting mechanism, and promotes community forests as carbon dioxide sinks under Thailand's greenhouse gas targets.

trackers.name: Check the subordinate law exists — and the no-permission planting route
trackers.desc: THE ACT ALONE MAY NOT REACH YOUR FOREST. Subordinate legislation is what makes it operable, and some was still incomplete: a ministerial regulation designating valuable trees (ไม้ทรงคุณค่า) was issued in 2564, but the royal decree on establishing community forests in other state areas was still being procured for study and drafting, and the ministerial regulation designating conservation forest areas was still in coordination between the national parks and forestry departments over land being prepared as national parks and wildlife sanctuaries. So if your forest sits in a conservation area or on ‘other state land’, check whether the enabling instrument yet exists before building a plan around the Act. AND A ROUTE THAT AVOIDS PERMISSION ENTIRELY: a Thai forest-law briefing records that where a project is carried out jointly with the Royal Forest Department — planting for the state and sharing carbon, with the private party controlling and maintaining — permission is not required, and the law was being amended so planting inside reserved forests would not require permission either. Check the current position before assuming you need a permit for restoration planting.

trackers.name: กองทุนสิ่งแวดล้อม — a village committee can be the applicant
trackers.desc: THAILAND'S ENVIRONMENTAL FUND, established in the Ministry of Finance under the 1992 National Environmental Quality Act as a financial mechanism on the polluter pays principle. TWO INSTRUMENTS, AND THE SPLIT DECIDES WHICH IS YOURS: loans go to the private sector, state enterprises and local administrative organisations; grants (เงินอุดหนุน) go to government agencies, local administrative organisations, public organisations and environmental NGOs. Civil society is on the grant side. THE ELIGIBLE LIST IS UNUSUALLY BROAD: alongside registered environmental NGOs it names the village volunteer network for protection of natural resources and environment (ทสม.), tambon community organisation councils, village committees (คณะกรรมการหมู่บ้าน), state educational institutions and local natural environment and arts conservation units. A community body that is not a registered NGO can therefore be the applicant — rare in this map, where most funds demand a registered legal person. Support follows 6 framework directions under section 23(4), published for the 2566–2570 budget period, with a guidance manual on developing proposals.

trackers.name: Get into the provincial plan first — the condition on Thai grants
trackers.desc: THE STEP THAT COMES BEFORE THE APPLICATION. A project seeking a grant must be included in the provincial-level action plan for environmental quality management under section 39 of the 1992 Act — and a local administrative organisation applying must already have allocated matching revenue in the proportion set by National Environment Board announcement. So the first move is getting your project into the provincial plan, not drafting a proposal. That is a months-ahead, relationship-based task at provincial level, and a strong proposal outside the plan will not be funded. WHAT HAS BEEN FUNDED: forest fire management, and an organic agriculture network project to protect natural resources in a watershed headwater area in Chiang Mai — so headwater and fire work are both established categories. Separate approval procedures exist for promotion projects, private-sector loans and wastewater or waste facility construction. CONTACT BY SUBJECT: natural resources 02-265-6593, environment and pollution 02-265-6591, climate change 02-265-6598, email envifund@onep.go.th. An English section exists.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: WALHI — Wahana Lingkungan Hidup Indonesia (Friends of the Earth Indonesia)
trackers.desc: Indonesia's largest and oldest environmental advocacy network, founded 1980, uniting several hundred member NGOs and individuals with independent offices in most provinces. WHO TO ENLIST: the provincial WALHI office nearest the project — the organisation works on agrarian conflict over natural resources, indigenous and peasant rights, coastal and marine issues, deforestation, mining and pollution. You CAN: plug into an existing regional campaign, get help arranging legal representation for a community, and draw on WALHI's record of pushing law enforcement in environmental crime cases and forcing the primary-forest, peatland and oil-palm moratoria. For activists: the fastest route to allies who already know the province and the company.

trackers.name: The Samdhana Institute — grants programme
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a Southeast Asian grantmaker giving micro to medium-sized grants, plus urgent-action grants, directly to Indigenous peoples and local communities, community-based and civil-society organisations, informal groups and individual activists — for land and territorial rights, natural-resource governance, and community-led climate and livelihood work. Its own site names offices only in Bogor, Indonesia and in Cagayan de Oro and Quezon City, Philippines, which is where this entry is placed; it describes its remit as Southeast Asia generally, so groups elsewhere in the region should still ask. WHO IT SUITS: groups that cannot get money from conventional donors — Samdhana states its grantmaking principle as funding the "un-fundable", and an unregistered informal group is not disqualified. HOW IT DIFFERS: it supplies environmental conflict mediation and technical support alongside the grant rather than only writing cheques.

trackers.name: Friends of the Earth Asia Pacific
trackers.desc: The Asia Pacific regional structure of Friends of the Earth International, formed in 2008, whose member groups work on community-based struggles against destructive projects, particularly mining and other extractive industries, alongside Indigenous peoples, peasant farmers, fisherfolk and trade unions. WHO TO ENLIST: the national member group nearest the project. In this region Friends of the Earth International's own directory names groups in Bangladesh (BELA, the Bangladesh Environmental Lawyers' Association), India, Indonesia (WALHI), Japan, Malaysia (Sahabat Alam Malaysia), Nepal, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines (the Legal Rights and Natural Resources Center), South Korea and Sri Lanka. You CAN: reach an organisation that already works community-side in your own country, and draw regional weight onto a local fight. For activists: in several of these countries the Friends of the Earth affiliate is the most experienced community-side environmental body there is.

trackers.name: Badan Pemeriksa Keuangan (BPK RI)
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Indonesia, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: AHU Online
trackers.desc: Indonesia's Ministry of Law company registry (AHU). — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.desc: Indonesia's national AMDAL (environmental impact assessment) system, run by the environment ministry (launched Feb 2023). You CAN get: environmental-assessment filings and permit processing routed through the national platform. You CAN'T get: older paper-era files not migrated. For activists: check whether a project has lodged its AMDAL, and follow the documents.

trackers.name: ICEL — Indonesian Center for Environmental Law
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a non-profit foundation established 19 July 1993, working specifically on environmental law through research, advocacy and building the legal capacity of communities. THE PART THAT MATTERS FOR PEOPLE AT RISK: ICEL files amicus curiae briefs supporting environmental defenders who are themselves prosecuted for opposing land control and company operations, working with the Center for Environmental Law and Climate Justice at the University of Indonesia and with ELAW, the Environmental Law Alliance Worldwide — so there is a route here for a defender facing criminal charges, not only for a community challenging a permit. It also publishes Jurnal Hukum Lingkungan Indonesia and a compendium of selected environmental judgments. Offices in Jakarta.

trackers.name: IUPHHK-RE — holding forest through a restoration concession
trackers.desc: HOW LAND GETS HELD HERE, AND IT IS A WORKAROUND. Conservation groups cannot readily buy and own Indonesian forest; instead they take a timber concession licence over production forest and use it to restore rather than log. The first, to PT REKI under SK Menhut SK.293/Menhut-II/2007 of 28 August 2007, covered 52,170 hectares in Musi Banyuasin, South Sumatra; a second in 2010 added 46,385 hectares in Jambi — together Hutan Harapan, about 98,554 hectares. THE TRANSFERABLE LESSON: a production-forest concession must be held by a legally constituted company, so the BirdLife consortium (Burung Indonesia, RSPB, BirdLife International) formed a foundation AND had to incorporate PT REKI as a corporate vehicle to hold the licence. Holders may manage water services, biodiversity protection, nature tourism, carbon, and non-timber products such as rattan, sago, nipah and bamboo. KNOW WHAT YOU ARE TAKING ON. The licence is legally still an HPH, so logging remains permitted on a restoration concession — researchers have called for that rule to be removed. Allocated areas are not clean and clear: tenurial conflict may be unresolved, and sites face encroachment, illegal logging and illegal mining. Fees are charged at the same rate as commercial concessions despite no timber revenue, permitting does not run through a market mechanism, and local government support has been weak. And community work is not optional — one concession protects its ecosystem by working with 900 communities through village forest management, small enterprise and loans, because without alternative income, encroachment and land-clearing fires continue whatever the licence says.

trackers.name: Hutan adat — customary forest is not state forest (MK 35/2012)
trackers.desc: THE RULING THAT CHANGED OWNERSHIP. Before it, customary forest was state forest whose management could merely be handed to the community — leaving the community as, in effect, a proxy of the state with only a right to manage. Constitutional Court decision 35/PUU-X/2012 split forest into three categories — hutan hak, hutan negara and hutan adat — and placed hutan adat within hutan hak, forest encumbered with land rights, not state forest. That now sits in Article 5(1)(b) of Forestry Law 41/1999 as amended by Law 6/2023. In hutan adat the customary community is both owner and manager, the main actor rather than a partner, and the forest keeps its conservation, protection and/or production functions. CRITERIA FOR DESIGNATION: the area lies within the customary territory, is forested with clear boundaries, is managed according to the community's local wisdom, and there is still forest-product gathering nearby for daily needs. Hutan adat is one of 5 social forestry schemes, alongside Hutan Kemasyarakatan, Hutan Desa, Kemitraan Kehutanan and Hutan Tanaman Rakyat.

trackers.name: Applying for hutan adat — the Perda first, and a 180-day clock
trackers.desc: THE SEQUENCE DEFEATS MOST APPLICANTS. Recognition of hutan adat is an accessory act — it must be preceded by recognition of the customary community itself. If the community is inside state forest area, that means a Peraturan Daerah; if outside, a regulation of the regional head. So the first fight is at the kabupaten or provincial legislature, not the ministry. THE APPLICATION goes to the Minister of Environment and Forestry, copied to regional parties including the regional head, and the Dirjen Perhutanan Sosial dan Kemitraan validates and verifies the documents. REQUIREMENTS SPLIT IN TWO: syarat mutlak (absolute) — identity of the community, a map of the customary territory, and a statement letter signed by its head — and syarat toleransi, which is where the Perda or regional head decision sits, so field verification can proceed while that is still outstanding. WATCH THE 180-DAY CLOCK: if requirements are incomplete or incorrect the application is returned, and if not completed within 180 days it is rejected. EXPECT RESISTANCE: roughly 40 million hectares was at stake after the ruling, and a 2013 ministry circular (SE.1/Menhut-II/2013) said release of hutan adat from state forest required regional government agreement — read by commentators as institutional self-preservation — while related rules demand written proof of claims over land held customarily.

trackers.name: Gugatan Warga Negara — the citizen lawsuit route (Jakarta)
trackers.desc: THE MECHANISM RESIDENTS HAVE ACTUALLY USED: a gugatan warga negara (citizen law suit) lets residents sue their own government. An alliance of capital residents brought one in 2019 over Jakarta's air pollution at the Central Jakarta District Court — case 374/Pdt.G/LH/2019/PN.Jkt.Pst. This ICEL compendium of selected environmental judgments sets it out alongside criminal judgments and, more useful for a land fight, hak uji materil (judicial review) rulings that struck at regulations themselves, including Putusan No. 77 P/HUM/2019 and Putusan No. 29 P/HUM/2019 against a provincial governor's regulation. USE THAT: judicial review of a subordinate regulation is the tool when the spatial-planning rule itself was written for the developer. BE REALISTIC ABOUT TIME: LBH Jakarta's advocacy team has publicly criticised how slowly the Jakarta air pollution citizen lawsuit moved through the Central Jakarta District Court compared with similar cases elsewhere. The route exists and has been used — it is not fast.

trackers.desc: Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC) — Singapore’s independent data-protection / information commissioner, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Singapore.

trackers.name: ACRA Register
trackers.desc: Electronic register of legal entities and public accountants.

trackers.name: Parks and Trees Act — and check what the designation covers underground
trackers.desc: READ THIS BEFORE ASSUMING A DESIGNATION SETTLES ANYTHING. Nature reserve protection runs through the Parks and Trees Act 2005, successor to the Nature Reserves Ordinance (1951), the Nature Reserves Act (1985) and the National Parks Act (1990). An NUS Asia-Pacific Centre for Environmental Law working paper examines the PTA's nature reserve provisions specifically so they may be given their intended effect — and frames the problem as relentless pressure and improving capability to develop subterranean space, noting Singapore has ‘left no stone unturned, and now look set to leave no granite undrilled either’. UNDERGROUND DEVELOPMENT BENEATH A PROTECTED SURFACE IS A LIVE QUESTION HERE: establish what your site's designation covers vertically, not just its boundary on a map. BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE ROUTE — Singapore has no community forest mechanism, no land trust tradition, no NGO standing regime and no land-defence grant fund; the decisive channel is evidence plus direct engagement, not litigation.

trackers.name: Chek Jawa, Dover, Kranji — what has actually changed decisions
trackers.desc: THE METHODS WITH A TRACK RECORD. CHEK JAWA IS THE PRECEDENT: in December 2001 individuals campaigning to save it were invited to a closed-door meeting at the National Development Ministry, where the minister announced the site would not be reclaimed; in January 2002 two new nature reserves at Labrador Park and Sungei Buloh were gazetted. That is the shape of a win here — technical evidence and direct engagement, with the decision announced rather than litigated. CITIZEN EVIDENCE THAT WORKED: a secondary school teacher documented older and endangered species in Dover Forest by measuring the girth of tree trunks and examining droppings on the forest floor — girth is a cheap, defensible proxy for tree age that anyone can gather; and Global Forest Watch satellite monitoring let citizens track land-use change and surface unreported developments, which is how the clearing of Kranji woodland came to light. THE STRATEGIC SHIFT: an area once needed endangered species present before conservation could be argued, and authorities could dismiss a society as having a limited following — but they cannot brush aside a sympathetic general public. Broad support is now the lever where species rarity used to be the only one. ALIGN WITH A PUBLISHED PLAN: the Singapore Terrestrial Conservation Plan names sites to elevate to Nature Park status and to restore — a site campaign is stronger inside it than alone — and the Friends of Sungei Buloh model shows a standing volunteer body is the recognised way to stay attached to a site.

trackers.name: URCDP — Unidad Reguladora y de Control de Datos Personales
trackers.desc: URCDP — Unidad Reguladora y de Control de Datos Personales — Uruguay’s national data-protection / information authority, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.desc: Unidad de Acceso a la Informacion Publica (UAIP, Uruguay) — oversight body for the right of access to public information.

trackers.name: Qué Sabés — FOI requests (URY)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (FOI request platform); Qué Sabés — civic Freedom-of-Information request platform (Alaveteli/mySociety network) — lets citizens file public-records requests and publishes the requests and the authorities’ responses in a public archive.

trackers.name: CAinfo (Centro de Archivo y Acceso a la Información Pública)
trackers.desc: Uruguayan civil-society organisation promoting the right of access to public information and transparency. Publishes the Active Transparency Online Index (ITAeL) assessing public bodies' compliance, and monitors press freedom and freedom of expression.

trackers.name: Vida Silvestre Uruguay — Refugios de vida silvestre
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a civil association founded in 1995 running the Refugios de vida silvestre programme since 2011 — a national network of voluntary private reserves, which matters in Uruguay because almost all the natural grassland, native woodland, wetland, sierra and coast sits on private land outside the state protected-area system. Refugios now protect over 500 plant, 300 invertebrate and 362 vertebrate species, many of them in no SNAP area at all. USE IT: if you own or work rural land in Uruguay and want it recognised and mapped as a refugio; the programme has its own sign-up route and works with landowners who keep farming.

trackers.name: REDES — Amigos de la Tierra Uruguay
trackers.desc: Founded in 1988 and the Friends of the Earth member group in Uruguay, working alongside the social movements affected by a project rather than for them. What it supplies is capacity and evidence: participatory research run jointly with faculties of the Universidad de la República, training and institutional strengthening for affected movements, and — through its Programa Uruguay Sustentable with the Comisión Nacional en Defensa del Agua y la Vida — a territorial GIS information system built for water-basin campaigning. It has fought the Neptuno-Arazatí water project, arguing the contract breached the Escazú Agreement on access to information and participation, and offshore hydrocarbon prospecting. WHO IT SUITS: organised groups already in a fight who need research, mapping and national coordination. It campaigns and researches; it does not litigate.

trackers.name: Tribunal de Cuentas de la República
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Uruguay's external audit body (supreme audit institution), created by the 1934 Constitution and governed by Section XIII, the TOCAF and articles 210, 211 and 212. Under article 211 literal B it intervenes preventively in state spending and payments — before the money moves — solely to certify legality, recording observaciones where it finds a problem, so an objection to a public works contract or land purchase lands at the approval stage rather than afterwards. KNOW THE LIMIT: it was given no jurisdictional or sanctioning powers and acts administratively — it observes, reports and denounces, it does not decide or punish. USE THE ESCALATION: where an ordenador reiterates a spend the Tribunal has observed and the Tribunal maintains the observation, it can have the matter flagged de urgente consideración when communicated to the General Assembly or the relevant Junta Departamental — which puts a contested departmental contract in front of the elected body that can act. Its resolutions are published and searchable, naming the contracting authority and the procurement, including intendencias. Contact: Juan Carlos Gómez 1324, 11100 Montevideo, 2916 1032/36, tribunal@tcr.gub.uy.

trackers.name: Base de Jurisprudencia Nacional
trackers.desc: Official free database of Uruguayan court decisions (Supreme Court from 1989; appellate and lower courts more recently), no registration required. · Find here: Uruguay's National Jurisprudence Database of court rulings.
