Ask any Egyptian organisation what its current registration and funding status is before you rely on it for a long case — not because they are unwilling, but because their ability to act can change without notice. WHO IT SUITS: Egyptians facing land loss, housing demolition, coastal or reef damage, or agricultural dispossession. CAVEATS: A CONSTRAINED CIVIC SPACE; several of these records are historical and status should be confirmed. For litigation on land and the housing right, Egypt's ECESR and EIPR entries.

trackers.name: Nature Conservation Egypt and AOYE — an Egyptian conservation NGO founded by the country's leading biodiversity experts with named staff, and a 1978 body whose volunteer programme turned 4,000 young people into paid staff, plus a 100-NGO Arab network
trackers.desc: THE CONSERVATION BODIES AND THE FOUR THOUSAND VOLUNTEERS — this file's Egyptian record has held rights centres and a Red Sea association; these are the national conservation organisations: NATURE CONSERVATION EGYPT (NCE, natureegypt.org), AN EGYPTIAN NGO ESTABLISHED IN 2005 BY A NUMBER OF EGYPT'S LEADING EXPERTS IN THE FIELD OF NATURE AND BIODIVERSITY, working towards CONSERVING EGYPT'S NATURAL HERITAGE AND THE PROMOTION OF ITS SUSTAINABLE USE, FOR THE BENEFIT OF PRESENT AND FUTURE GENERATIONS. IT NAMES ITS INDIVIDUAL STAFF ON ITS OWN SITE WITH THEIR SPECIALISMS — including a SENIOR CONSERVATION OFFICER who is an ENVIRONMENTAL RESEARCHER AND ORNITHOLOGIST with expertise dating to 2000 and A WILDLIFE DOCUMENTARY PHOTOGRAPHER since 2005, PUBLISHED IN INTERNATIONAL MAGAZINES AND NEWSPAPERS, who also teaches photography workshops. A named ornithologist who is also a documentary photographer is two resources in one person: the survey that establishes what lives on your site, and the images that make the case publicly. Write to the officer by name and ask what NCE has recorded on your ground. THE OLDEST AND THE BIGGEST NETWORK: THE ARAB OFFICE FOR YOUTH AND ENVIRONMENT (AOYE, aoye.org), ESTABLISHED DECEMBER 1978 to promote environmental awareness and create active stewardship in Egypt, the Arab nations and beyond, WHICH FOUNDED THE ARAB UNION FOR YOUTH AND ENVIRONMENT IN 1983 to activate youth concerned with environmental issues — AND WHOSE 1993 YOUTH VOLUNTEER PROGRAMME TOOK ABOUT 4,000 YOUTH VOLUNTEERS FROM VARIOUS GOVERNORATES WHO WERE THEN HIRED AS PART-TIME AND FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES. Four thousand volunteers converted into paid staff is the clearest demonstration in this file that environmental work can be an employment programme. That is the argument to put to a governor: protection creates jobs, and an Egyptian organisation has the numbers to prove it. AOYE has TRAINED THOUSANDS OF YOUNG PEOPLE, its chairman is NAMED AND HAS BEEN HONOURED BY THE EGYPTIAN SOCIETY FOR NATURE CONSERVATION, and it convenes work under the patronage of ministers and governors — including a PROJECT IN THE NORTHERN NILE DELTA THAT PRODUCED KEY RECOMMENDATIONS on weather instability, and regional disaster-risk workshops in Cairo. AND THE REGIONAL DOOR: RAED — THE ARAB NETWORK FOR ENVIRONMENT AND DEVELOPMENT — INVOLVES MORE THAN 100 NGOs FROM ARAB COUNTRIES WHO SHARE EXPERIENCES AND EXCHANGE INFORMATION ON ENVIRONMENTAL AND DEVELOPMENTAL ISSUES. A hundred-plus organisation network across the Arab world, hosted from Cairo, is how an Egyptian case reaches organisations in every neighbouring country at once. If your project has a regional dimension — a shared aquifer, a coastline, a migratory route — RAED is the multiplier. ALSO NAMED: the EGYPTIAN SOCIETY FOR NATURE CONSERVATION; and the MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, ESTABLISHED 1997, WHOSE POLICIES ARE EXECUTED BY THE EGYPTIAN ENVIRONMENTAL AFFAIRS AGENCY (eeaa.gov.eg) — the operational body, not the ministry, being where an environmental file is actually handled. WHO IT SUITS: Egyptians needing a species survey, photographic evidence, a youth programme, or a regional network. CAVEATS: CONSERVATION AND AWARENESS ORGANISATIONS with close state relations — pair with counsel for a contested case, and note this file's record of a constrained civic space. For the environmental rights and land centres and the Aswan office, Egypt's Habi Center and Land Center entry; for litigation on land and housing, ECESR and EIPR.

trackers.name: The Egyptian Foundation for Environmental Rights — Egypt's first public interest environmental law firm, founded to replace the centre that closed when its founder died — plus HEPCA's 700 staff and dive-centre origin
trackers.desc: THE CENTRE CLOSED WHEN HE DIED; SOMEBODY OPENED ANOTHER — and that is the most useful thing in this file's Egyptian record: AHMED EL SEIDI HAS LAUNCHED EGYPT'S FIRST PUBLIC INTEREST ENVIRONMENTAL LAW FIRM, THE EGYPTIAN FOUNDATION FOR ENVIRONMENTAL RIGHTS (EFER) — AND HIS OWN ACCOUNT OF WHY IS PLAIN: THIS HAS BEEN MY DREAM SINCE MY MENTOR, THE FOUNDER OF THE HABI CENTER FOR ENVIRONMENTAL RIGHTS, DIED IN 2018 AND HIS CENTER CLOSED. A country's only environmental rights centre closed because one man died. This file has flagged that fragility repeatedly — an institution resting on a single person ends with them. What is new here is the second half: a person he trained rebuilt it under a new name. If the organisation you depend on is one person, the succession question is not morbid, it is the most practical thing you can raise with them. THE ROUTE HE TOOK, WHICH IS REPRODUCIBLE: IN 2023 HE TRAVELLED FOR AN ELAW FELLOWSHIP AND CONSULTED WITH THE ELAW TEAM ABOUT LAUNCHING A NEW ORGANIZATION. A fellowship with an environmental law network, then a new national organisation. That is a named, walkable path for any lawyer in a country whose environmental bar is thin — and this file records the same network elsewhere as one of three organisations advising on legal-action grants of five to fifteen thousand dollars. The training and the money come from the same place. THE PROBLEM HE NAMED, WHICH APPLIES FAR BEYOND EGYPT: MANY ENVIRONMENTAL CHALLENGES, COMPOUNDED BY WEAK ENFORCEMENT OF EXISTING LAWS AND LIMITED PUBLIC AWARENESS OF PERSONAL ENVIRONMENTAL RIGHTS. PERSONAL environmental rights — not the environment's rights, yours. Most of the people in this file do not know they hold any, which is why the laws go unenforced. AND THE PROGRAMME IS THE UNUSUAL PART: EFER AIMS TO PROTECT THE ENVIRONMENT BY EMPOWERING PUBLIC WORKERS, LAW STUDENTS, AND COMMUNITIES — AND THROUGH TARGETED TRAINING PROGRAMS WILL EQUIP PUBLIC SECTOR EMPLOYEES WITH SKILLS TO MONITOR ENVIRONMENTAL VIOLATIONS EFFECTIVELY AND ENFORCE ENVIRONMENTAL LAWS. Training the government's own inspectors, not only suing them. Where enforcement is weak because the officials lack the skill rather than the will, that is the shorter route — and a public interest firm that trains public workers is welcome in rooms a litigator alone is not. Law students are the third group: the next generation of the environmental bar, being built deliberately because the last one rested on one man. THE OTHER ORGANISATION, PROPERLY DESCRIBED: A HURGHADA ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AND CONSERVATION ASSOCIATION WAS ESTABLISHED IN 1992 BY DIVE CENTRES IN TWO NAMED RED SEA TOWNS, IS CONSTITUTED AS AN ASSOCIATION WITH AN ASSEMBLY AS ITS MAIN ORGAN, HAS OVER 700 EMPLOYEES, AND WORKS PRIMARILY WITH MARINE AND LAND CONSERVATION IN THE RED SEA GOVERNORATE. Founded by the dive centres themselves — the businesses whose livelihood depends on the reef staying alive, organising as an association with a general assembly. Seven hundred employees from a start like that. If an industry near you depends on the thing being destroyed, that industry is a constituency, not an opponent: ask the operators to constitute an association before you ask them for money. AND THE CONSERVATION BODY: NATURE CONSERVATION EGYPT WAS ESTABLISHED IN 2005 BY A NUMBER OF EGYPT'S LEADING EXPERTS IN NATURE AND BIODIVERSITY CONSERVATION, WORKS IN SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH, ADVOCACY, EDUCATION AND OUTREACH TO SUPPORT SPECIES, THEIR HABITATS, AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES, AND WORKS IN PARTNERSHIP WITH LOCAL EXPERTS AND GOVERNMENTAL BODIES. THE CASE WORTH READING, BECAUSE IT IS THE SHAPE OF THINGS TO COME: RAPID DEVELOPMENT OF A SITE FOR RENEWABLE ENERGY PROJECTS POSED AN UNPRECEDENTED THREAT TO A LIZARD'S HABITAT — THE CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION OF WIND TURBINES AND ASSOCIATED INFRASTRUCTURE, PARTICULARLY IN AREAS WITHIN 150 METRES OF ACTIVE BURROWS, RAISING SERIOUS CONCERNS ABOUT HABITAT DESTRUCTION, DIRECT HARM FROM MACHINERY, AND LONG-TERM ECOLOGICAL DISRUPTION — met by a proposed TRANSLOCATION STRATEGY MOVING THE ANIMALS TO A CAREFULLY SELECTED LOCATION THAT MIMICS THEIR NATURAL HABITAT. A renewable energy project as the threat, and 150 metres from an active burrow as the measured danger zone. Clean energy projects take land like any other project, and this file's Kenyan and Tanzanian entries record the same. A stated distance from a feature is the kind of specific, checkable number to demand in any assessment — and translocation is a mitigation, not a cancellation, so ask who pays for it and who monitors whether the animals survive. WHO IT SUITS: Egyptian communities with an environmental complaint, Red Sea coastal and dive businesses, and lawyers wanting to build an environmental practice. CAVEATS: EFER IS NEW and Egypt's civic space is constrained. For Habi Center's history and the organisations by name, Egypt's environment and land organisations entry; for litigated expropriation, the Egyptian Center for Economic and Social Rights entry; for a standing right-to-housing file and legal aid, EIPR; for the conservation NGO with named staff and 4,000 volunteers turned paid staff, the Nature Conservation Egypt and AOYE entry.

trackers.name: Research agencies that work on behalf of communities harmed by environmental violence and build evidence for courtrooms — 100+ investigations in 31 countries, plus a completed African partnership whose evidence communities can use in a reparations claim
trackers.desc: THEY TURN THE STATE'S OWN FORENSIC TOOLS AROUND — THE FOUNDING PRINCIPLE, STATED: THE INVERSION OF FORENSIC TECHNIQUES TYPICALLY USED BY STATES, APPLYING THEM INSTEAD TO CHALLENGE OFFICIAL NARRATIVES AND PRODUCE COUNTER-EVIDENCE IN LEGAL, ACTIVIST, AND PUBLIC DOMAINS. Forensics is normally something done to communities by police and prosecutors. Here the same techniques are pointed at the official account of what happened — which is precisely what a community needs when the report says the clearance was peaceful and the spill was small. WHO THEY WORK FOR, AND THIS IS WHY THE ENTRY IS HERE: THEY WORK ON BEHALF OF COMMUNITIES AFFECTED BY POLICE BRUTALITY, BORDER REGIMES, AND ENVIRONMENTAL VIOLENCE, AND DEVELOP EVIDENTIARY MATERIALS THAT CAN BE DEPLOYED IN COURTROOMS AND POLITICAL PROCESSES, AS WELL AS IN GALLERIES, CULTURAL INSTITUTIONS, AND THROUGH MEDIA, IN PURSUIT OF ACCOUNTABILITY FOR VIOLENCE COMMITTED BY STATES AND THEIR AGENTS. ENVIRONMENTAL VIOLENCE named alongside police brutality, and the output deployed in four places from one investigation — a courtroom, a political process, an exhibition and the press. For a community whose case may never reach a friendly court, the other three still land. THE METHODS: SPATIAL AND ARCHITECTURAL ANALYSIS, OPEN-SOURCE INVESTIGATION, DIGITAL MODELLING, IMMERSIVE TECHNOLOGIES, DOCUMENTARY RESEARCH, INTERVIEWS AND ACADEMIC COLLABORATION — CROSS-REFERENCING NEW MEDIA, REMOTE SENSING, MATERIAL ANALYSIS, WITNESS TESTIMONY AND CROWD-SOURCING. REMOTE SENSING and MATERIAL ANALYSIS cross-referenced against WITNESS TESTIMONY. Satellite images and soil samples on one side, what people saw on the other, checked against each other. That combination is what makes an account hard to dismiss as hearsay. SITUATED TESTIMONY, WHICH IS THE MOST TRANSFERABLE IDEA HERE: THE PRACTICE USES IMMERSIVE 3D ENVIRONMENTS TO HELP SURVIVORS RECONSTRUCT THEIR EXPERIENCES, ALLOWING THEM TO REVISIT TRAUMATIC INCIDENTS IN A SAFE AND CONTROLLED ENVIRONMENT — AND AS THE FOUNDER PUT IT, ARCHITECTURE AND MEMORY ARE RELATED; ARCHITECTURE IS ALWAYS A COLLABORATIVE PROCESS, AND IT ALLOWS WITNESSES TO RE-CONSTRUCT MEMORIES THAT ARE FRAGMENTED AND TORN APART BY THE EFFECT OF TRAUMA. Rebuilding the place lets people remember the event. A witness who cannot narrate what happened may still be able to point at where it happened — and this file has recorded again and again that the people with the best evidence are the ones least able to give a courtroom account of it. Even a hand-drawn plan of the compound, made together, works on this principle. THE RECORD: MORE THAN 100 INVESTIGATIONS ACROSS AT LEAST 31 COUNTRIES AND TERRITORIES, PROVIDING CRUCIAL EVIDENCE FOR INTERNATIONAL COURTS AND WORKING WITH A WIDE RANGE OF ACTIVIST GROUPS, NGOs AND THE UN. THE ENVIRONMENTAL CASES: IT HAS INVESTIGATED CRIMES RELATED TO THE ENVIRONMENT, INCLUDING SHEDDING LIGHT ON ILLEGAL GOLD MINING AND VIOLENCE IN INDIGENOUS TERRITORIES OF A RAINFOREST, AND ENVIRONMENTAL VIOLENCE AND CLIMATE CHANGE IN HIGHLAND REGIONS. Illegal gold mining on indigenous land is one of the commonest patterns in this file, from the Congo Basin to the Sahel. It has been investigated to evidentiary standard before, which means there is a method to ask for rather than one to invent. THE AFRICAN CASE ALREADY COMPLETED, AND WHAT IT IS FOR: A MULTIYEAR INVESTIGATION WITH PARTNERS IN A NAMED AFRICAN COUNTRY USED COLLABORATIVE MODELLING, SITUATED TESTIMONIES AND GEOLOCATIONS TO ANALYSE KEY SITES OF A GENOCIDE, AND ALSO EXPLORES THE ONGOING ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT OF A COLONIAL PRESENCE — AND THE EVIDENCE THAT THE ORGANIZATIONS' COLLABORATION PRODUCED CAN BE USED BY LOCAL COMMUNITIES IN THEIR CLAIM FOR REPARATIONS. The evidence belongs to the communities' claim, not to the exhibition. That is the arrangement to insist on: ask, before agreeing to any collaboration, whether the material produced can be used in your own legal claim afterwards, and whether you hold a copy. THE MODEL BEHIND IT: A NEW MODEL FOR COLLABORATIVE TRUTH-PRODUCTION, BRINGING TOGETHER OPEN SOURCE INVESTIGATION, COUNTER-FORENSICS AND STRATEGIC HUMAN RIGHTS LITIGATION — COMBINING THE KNOWLEDGE OF SURVIVORS OF VIOLENCE AND DISPOSSESSION WITH METHODS FROM JOURNALISM, LAW, ACTIVISM AND ARTS. THE KNOWLEDGE OF SURVIVORS listed first among the inputs, before the professional methods. The community is a source of evidence, not merely its subject. AND THE SECOND AGENCY, WHICH IS THE ONE TO KNOW ABOUT FOR PURELY ENVIRONMENTAL CASES: A FORENSIC INVESTIGATION AGENCY WHICH, USING SPATIAL AND VISUAL TECHNIQUES FROM ARCHITECTURE AND MEDIA STUDIES, PRODUCES EVIDENCE FOR LEGAL ACTIONS INCLUDING BRIEFINGS AND PETITIONS TO THE INTERNATIONAL CRIMINAL COURT — AND HAS RELEASED A LEXICON OF ITS APPLIED INVESTIGATIVE PRACTICES, WHOSE CONCEPTS SECTION SETS OUT THE UNIQUE EVIDENTIARY CHALLENGES OF REPRESENTING ENVIRONMENTAL DESTRUCTION. A published lexicon on the specific difficulty of proving environmental harm — slow damage, dispersed victims, no single moment to point at. That is the problem every case in this file runs into, and somebody has written down how to handle it. WHO IT SUITS: African communities facing environmental destruction or state violence who need evidence built to a standard a court or a UN body will accept. CAVEATS: THESE ARE SMALL RESEARCH AGENCIES WITH LONG QUEUES, NOT A SERVICE ON DEMAND — approach through a lawyer or an organisation already working with you. For making your own phone footage court-ready, Niger's video-as-evidence entry; for the scientists who critique impact assessments free, Nigeria's ELAW entry; for the damage valuation study to bring to a negotiation, Ghana's Strategic Response Mechanism entry.

trackers.name: The Equator Prize (UNDP) — the cash award that goes to the village group itself — open to rural community-based organisations three years old or more across almost every African country, with published criteria and a 300-organisation network of past winners
trackers.desc: THE PRIZE THAT GOES TO THE VILLAGE GROUP, NOT THE NGO — adjacency declared first: THE INITIATIVE'S OWN DOMAIN ALREADY APPEARS AS A SOURCE URL UNDER GAMBIA, TOGO AND ETHIOPIA FOR THREE DIFFERENT LOCAL ORGANISATIONS, AND A SEPARATE INDIGENOUS-TERRITORIES CONSORTIUM HAS ITS OWN ENTRY UNDER MOROCCO. NEITHER DESCRIBES THIS PRIZE, ITS ELIGIBILITY OR ITS NOMINATION ROUTE. WHO IT IS FOR, AND THIS IS THE FIND: THE NOMINEE MUST BE EITHER A LOCAL COMMUNITY-BASED GROUP OPERATING IN A RURAL AREA, BASED IN A COUNTRY RECEIVING UN DEVELOPMENT SUPPORT — OR AN INDIGENOUS PEOPLES' COMMUNITY IN ANY COUNTRY, OPERATING IN A RURAL AREA. A rural community-based group, named as the unit. Almost every fund in this file routes money through a registered NGO that then decides what a village gets; this one is addressed to the village group directly. That is rare enough to be worth an application even at long odds. THE OTHER TWO CONDITIONS: THE INITIATIVE MUST HAVE BEEN IN EXISTENCE FOR AT LEAST THREE YEARS, AND/OR THE ACTIONS TAKEN MUST HAVE BEEN IN PLACE FOR AT LEAST THREE YEARS — AND THE ACTIONS MUST BE NATURE-BASED AND DELIVER BENEFITS RELATED TO TWO OR MORE SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT GOALS. AND/OR THE ACTIONS is the clause to read twice. A committee formed last year can still qualify if the practice it protects — a sacred grove, a closed season, a grazing rotation — has been in place for three years or more. Most communities in this file are far older than their committees, and this wording is written for exactly that. THE AFRICAN ELIGIBILITY LIST IS NEARLY THE WHOLE CONTINENT: IT NAMES ALGERIA, EGYPT, LIBYA, MAURITANIA, MOROCCO, SUDAN AND TUNISIA IN THE NORTH, AND ANGOLA, BENIN, BOTSWANA, BURKINA FASO, BURUNDI, CAMEROON, CAPE VERDE, THE CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC, CHAD, COMOROS, THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF THE CONGO, DJIBOUTI, EQUATORIAL GUINEA, ERITREA, ESWATINI, ETHIOPIA, GABON, GAMBIA, GHANA, GUINEA, GUINEA-BISSAU, IVORY COAST, KENYA, LESOTHO, LIBERIA AND MADAGASCAR AMONG OTHERS. The countries this file has recorded as hardest to fund — Djibouti, Eritrea, Equatorial Guinea, Libya, Chad — are all on the published list. The barrier here is not geography. THE MONEY, RECORDED HONESTLY BECAUSE IT MOVES: ONE CYCLE'S ANNOUNCEMENT STATES EACH WINNING INITIATIVE RECEIVES USD 10,000; A LATER STATEMENT PUTS THE AWARD BETWEEN US$15,000 AND $25,000. CHECK THE CURRENT CYCLE RATHER THAN TRUSTING EITHER FIGURE. THE SELECTION CRITERIA, WHICH DOUBLE AS A CHECKLIST FOR ANY FUNDING APPLICATION YOU EVER WRITE: AN INDEPENDENT TECHNICAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE ASSESSES IMPACT — MEASURABLE AND POSITIVE ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL AND ECONOMIC IMPACTS RELATED TO TWO OR MORE GOALS; SOCIAL INCLUSION — THE PROJECT MUST ENGAGE YOUTH, ELDERS, INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES AND OTHER DIVERSE GROUPS IN DECISION-MAKING AND IMPLEMENTATION; AND GENDER EQUALITY — THE INITIATIVE SHOULD FOSTER THE EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN AND GIRLS. MEASURABLE is the word that decides it. A community that has counted something — hectares restored, catch per boat, households supplied — writes a different application from one that has not. Start counting now, whatever else you do; this file's community mapping and monitoring entries are how. AND ELDERS listed beside youth in the inclusion test. A committee of middle-aged men will score badly on a criterion that is published in advance. THE ODDS, STATED PLAINLY SO NOBODY BUILDS A PLAN ON IT: TEN WINNERS SELECTED FROM OVER 700 NOMINATIONS FROM 103 COUNTRIES IN ONE CYCLE, AND ELEVEN FROM MORE THAN 600 NOMINATIONS FROM 102 COUNTRIES IN ANOTHER. Roughly one in sixty. Write the nomination because assembling it forces you to state your impact in measurable terms — a document you will reuse with every funder in this file — not because the prize is likely. THE NETWORK, WHICH MAY BE WORTH MORE THAN THE CASH: WINNERS JOIN A NETWORK OF OVER 300 COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS FROM 84 COUNTRIES HONOURED SINCE 2002. Three hundred community organisations that have already done what you are attempting, findable by name and country. Even without winning, that published list is a directory of peers to write to — and this file has recorded repeatedly that a village which has visited another village learns faster than one that attends a workshop. WHAT WINNERS GET BESIDES MONEY: SUPPORT TO PARTICIPATE IN A SERIES OF POLICY DIALOGUES AND SPECIAL EVENTS, WITH THE OPPORTUNITY TO PARTICIPATE IN GLOBAL EVENTS INCLUDING A UN GENERAL ASSEMBLY AND A UN CLIMATE CHANGE CONFERENCE. A village committee in the room at a UN conference is leverage no amount of local petitioning produces — and a government that ignores you at home behaves differently when its own delegation is standing nearby. THE ONGOING PLATFORM: COMMUNITY DIALOGUES PROVIDE A PLATFORM FOR INDIGENOUS AND LOCAL LEADERS FROM PRIZE-WINNING ORGANIZATIONS TO EXCHANGE KNOWLEDGE, SHARE BEST PRACTICES AND COLLABORATE ON SUSTAINABLE ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT — DESIGNED TO STRENGTHEN LEADERSHIP SKILLS, SHOWCASE THEIR NATURE-BASED SOLUTIONS, AND AMPLIFY THEIR VOICES IN NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL POLICY PROCESSES. AND THE AFRICAN WINNERS ALREADY ON RECORD: RECENT CYCLES NAME WINNERS FROM KENYA AND TANZANIA AMONG THE TEN, AND ONE CYCLE HONOURED ELEVEN COMMUNITIES FROM EIGHT COUNTRIES SPANNING ASIA, AFRICA, AND LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN. WHO IT SUITS: African rural community groups and indigenous communities with three or more years of practice protecting land, water, forest or fisheries. CAVEATS: NOMINATION WINDOWS ARE SHORT AND CLOSE EARLY IN THE YEAR, AMOUNTS VARY BY CYCLE, AND THE ODDS ARE ROUGHLY ONE IN SIXTY — treat the nomination as a document-building exercise first. For the free small grants with no co-financing, Kenya's BIOPAMA entry; for the advisor-nominated grants where 40% of grantees are first-time, Ghana's African Women's Development Fund entry; for the indigenous-territories consortium and its registry, Morocco's entry.

trackers.name: The Access Initiative (TAI) — a 250-organisation network whose African chapters are led by African organisations and are independent of each other — individuals may join, and its toolkit is built for communities demanding pollution data from named companies
trackers.desc: TWELVE AFRICAN COUNTRIES ALREADY HAVE A CHAPTER YOU CAN JOIN — THE SIZE AND THE JOINING RULE: A NETWORK OF MORE THAN 250 CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS IN 60 COUNTRIES — ALWAYS LOOKING TO EXPAND MEMBERSHIP TO INCLUDE LIKE-MINDED ORGANIZATIONS AND INDIVIDUALS, WITH NEW MEMBERSHIP RULES THAT MAKE IT MUCH EASIER FOR PEOPLE TO JOIN. INDIVIDUALS, not only organisations. One person from a village committee can join a continental network on their own name — which this file has recorded as rare, and which matters because membership is usually gated behind registration your group does not have. THE AFRICAN STRUCTURE, AND WHO LEADS IT: MEMBERS IN ANGLOPHONE AND FRANCOPHONE AFRICA INCLUDE NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS AND INDIVIDUAL MEMBERS FROM 12 AFRICAN COUNTRIES, WITH CORE TEAM MEMBERS FROM THE REGION BEING CODELT (DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO) AND THE ZIMBABWE ENVIRONMENTAL LAW ASSOCIATION (ZELA). THE GOVERNANCE, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH COPYING: COUNTRY CHAPTERS ARE INDEPENDENT OF EACH OTHER AND OF THE HOSTING INSTITUTE; EACH CHAPTER IS LED BY A PARTNER ORGANIZATION AND CONSISTS OF INDIVIDUAL EXPERTS AND CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS WHICH DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT THEIR OWN PROGRAMS; AND MEMBERS FROM EACH REGION ELECT A REPRESENTATIVE TO THE CORE TEAM EVERY FOUR YEARS. INDEPENDENT OF THE HOSTING INSTITUTE. The chapter in your country is not a branch office taking instructions from abroad — it sets its own programme and elects its own regional representative. That is the arrangement to look for before joining any international network, and the one this file has repeatedly recorded as missing. WHAT AFRICAN PARTNERS ACTUALLY DO, AS FOUR STATED ACTIVITIES: CONDUCT EVIDENCE-BASED ASSESSMENTS TO EVALUATE THE IMPLEMENTATION OF ACCESS RIGHTS IN THEIR OWN COUNTRIES; CONDUCT ADVOCACY AROUND ACCESS RIGHTS AND LAND, EXTRACTIVES AND FORESTS; USE ACCESS RIGHTS IN THEIR WORK; AND WORK REGIONALLY TO PROMOTE ACCESS RIGHTS IN OTHER COUNTRIES. LAND, EXTRACTIVES AND FORESTS named as the advocacy subjects. This is not a general transparency network that might stretch to cover a mine — that is its African agenda. THE POLLUTION TOOLKIT, WHICH IS THE MOST DIRECTLY USABLE THING HERE: A PROJECT EMPOWERING COMMUNITIES TO IMPROVE THEIR ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH THROUGH DEMANDS FOR INFORMATION ON AIR AND WATER POLLUTION — WITH A TOOLKIT FOR CIVIL SOCIETY TO WORK WITH COMMUNITIES TO ANALYSE THE GAPS IN LAW AND PRACTICE IN THE RELEASE OF POLLUTION INFORMATION AND TO ASSESS PUBLIC PARTICIPATION FORUMS. CIVIL SOCIETY USE THEIR RIGHT TO INFORMATION TO DEMAND INFORMATION ABOUT THE PERFORMANCE OF PRIVATE AND PUBLIC COMPANIES TO MEET NATIONAL STANDARDS ON POLLUTION, AND PARTNERS ARE TRAINED TO MAKE FREEDOM OF INFORMATION REQUESTS AND USE APPEAL MECHANISMS — TO DEMAND RESTORATION, CLEAN UP AND ACCOUNTABILITY BY COMPANIES THAT POLLUTE. Not whether pollution is happening, but whether the company is meeting the standard it was licensed under — and that is a document the state holds and can be asked for. This file's Somalia entry gives the cheap instruments to take your own readings; this gives the paper trail to compare them against, and the appeal route when the request is refused. THE WORKED AFRICAN CASE AND ITS HONEST TIMESCALE: A COALITION IN A NAMED CENTRAL AFRICAN COUNTRY MET ITS GOVERNMENT AND SHARED FINDINGS AND RECOMMENDATIONS FOR HOW GOVERNMENT AND CIVIL SOCIETY CAN WORK TOGETHER TO BRING ABOUT ENVIRONMENTAL GOVERNANCE CHANGES — BASED ON THE COALITION'S 18 MONTHS OF RESEARCH ON ENVIRONMENTAL LAWS PERTAINING TO ACCESS TO INFORMATION, ACCESS TO JUSTICE, PUBLIC PARTICIPATION AND CAPACITY BUILDING. Eighteen months of research before the meeting. A delegation that arrives with a year and a half of evidence is received differently from one that arrives with a grievance — and the government sat down with them. THE IMPACT ASSESSMENT TOOLS: THE NETWORK HAS PRODUCED SOME OF THE MOST HELPFUL TOOLS TO ENABLE THE PUBLIC TO UNDERSTAND HOW TO PARTICIPATE IN THE ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT PROCESS AND IN POLICY DIALOGUES TO SHAPE HOW NATURAL RESOURCES ARE EXPLOITED. The impact assessment is where a project is approved or stopped, and it is the process communities in this file most often discover after it has closed. Free material on how to take part in it is worth more than most legal advice bought later. THE CONTINENTAL LEGAL FOUNDATION IT POINTS TO: THE AFRICAN CHARTER ON HUMAN AND PEOPLES' RIGHTS, THE AFRICAN CHARTER ON DEMOCRACY, ELECTIONS AND GOVERNANCE AND THE AFRICAN UNION CONVENTION AGAINST CORRUPTION ALL RECOGNISE A RIGHT TO INFORMATION — AND THE AFRICAN CHARTER ALSO RECOGNISES THE RIGHT TO PARTICIPATE IN GOVERNMENT, THE RIGHT TO A HEALTHY ENVIRONMENT, AND THE RIGHT TO APPEAR BEFORE THE AFRICAN COMMISSION AND AFRICAN COURT. Three continental instruments your own government has signed, all recognising a right to information. When a ministry refuses a document, those are the citations to put in the appeal — and the last clause is the route this file records under Seychelles. THE AFRICAN POLICY RESULT: IT WORKED WITH THREE NAMED AFRICAN ORGANISATIONS TO REVIEW AND COMMENT ON A MODEL AFRICAN UNION ACCESS TO INFORMATION LAW, AND INFLUENCED ITS DEVELOPMENT. WHAT MEMBERSHIP GIVES, PUBLISHED AS A LIST: INTERNATIONAL ADVOCACY, WITH OPPORTUNITIES TO JOIN GLOBAL PROJECTS AND CAMPAIGNS; LEARNING FROM OTHER ACTIVISTS IN THE NETWORK; AND ASSESSMENT TOOLS, INCLUDING DEVELOPING NEW ONES AND USING EXISTING NETWORK RESOURCES — ALONGSIDE BI-ANNUAL GLOBAL GATHERINGS. WHO IT SUITS: African community organisations and individuals who cannot get the impact assessment, the licence conditions or the pollution monitoring data their government holds. CAVEATS: A NETWORK AND A TOOLKIT, NOT A FUNDER OR A LAWYER, AND ONLY 12 AFRICAN COUNTRIES HAVE CHAPTERS — check whether yours does before assuming a local route exists. For cheap instruments to take your own pollution readings, Somalia's entry; for free legal advice where a document was withheld for a bribe, Mali's entry; for the co-complainant route to the continental court, Seychelles' entry.

trackers.name: They filed a complaint against an international conservation organisation over ranger abuses in an African forest — and a European government agreed to mediate, unprecedented — while supporting legal representation and stating openly they can take only a few cases at a time
trackers.desc: THEY FILED AGAINST A CONSERVATION ORGANISATION, AND A GOVERNMENT AGREED TO MEDIATE — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S MOROCCO ENTRY COVERS AN INDIGENOUS TERRITORIES CONSORTIUM, ITS SEYCHELLES ENTRY THE CO-COMPLAINANT ROUTE TO THE CONTINENTAL COURT, ITS CHAD ENTRY THE NATIONAL CONTACT POINTS USED IN THE CASE BELOW, ITS COMOROS ENTRY THE CARBON GRIEVANCE REVIEW, AND ITS TANZANIA AND DJIBOUTI ENTRIES PASTORALIST COALITIONS. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE CONSERVATION COMPLAINT ON RECORD, WHICH IS THE FIND: IT FILED A COMPLAINT AGAINST AN INTERNATIONAL CONSERVATION ORGANISATION THROUGH A EUROPEAN GOVERNMENT'S CONTACT POINT, OVER CLAIMS THAT THE ORGANISATION FAILED TO DO ENOUGH TO STOP ECOGUARDS IT SUPPORTS IN A CENTRAL AFRICAN COUNTRY FROM ABUSING MEMBERS OF AN INDIGENOUS RAINFOREST PEOPLE — AND THAT GOVERNMENT TOOK THE HIGHLY UNUSUAL STEP OF AGREEING TO MEDIATE, DESCRIBED AS UNPRECEDENTED. A conservation organisation taken to the same complaint body used against mining and oil companies. This file has recorded conservation projects evicting people from the Seychelles judgment onward; here is the established route for treating a conservation body as what it is in that moment — a foreign organisation whose programme is causing harm, answerable in its home country. The contact points are filed under Chad; this is the precedent that shows they accept such a case. THE PROGRAMME AT ISSUE: A MULTI-MILLION-DOLLAR PROGRAMME WITH THAT COUNTRY'S GOVERNMENT SUPPORTING RANGERS WHO PATROL ENVIRONMENTALLY PROTECTED AREAS AND WORK TO PREVENT POACHING — WITH THE CONSERVATION ORGANISATION'S AFRICA DIRECTOR CALLING THE APPROACH TO FOREIGN AUTHORITIES REGRETTABLE AND SAYING THE GROUP HAD NOT TAKEN UP REPEATED OFFERS FOR A MEETING ON THE GROUND. Both sides recorded. The organisation's answer was that talks should have happened locally — which is the response a community should expect, and the reason to document every refused or fruitless local meeting before escalating abroad. WHAT IT ACTUALLY PROVIDES: WE WORK IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THEM. WE GIVE THEM A PLATFORM TO SPEAK TO THE WORLD. WE INVESTIGATE ATROCITIES AND PRESENT EVIDENCE TO THE UNITED NATIONS AND OTHER INTERNATIONAL FORUMS. WE SUPPORT LEGAL REPRESENTATION. WE EDUCATE, RESEARCH, CAMPAIGN, LOBBY AND PROTEST. WE SUPPORT LEGAL REPRESENTATION — paying for or arranging counsel, not providing it. Ask which, and for what stage, before relying on it. THE CAPACITY LIMIT IT STATES OPENLY: SINCE ITS RESOURCES ARE LIMITED, IT CAN BE MOST EFFECTIVE BY FOCUSING ON A SMALL NUMBER OF CASES AT ANY ONE TIME — WHILE HAVING NEARLY ONE HUNDRED ONGOING CASES, AND FOCUSING ON THOSE WHO HAVE THE MOST TO LOSE. A small number at a time, chosen by them. This file records that honesty rarely; it means an approach is a request to be selected, and the case is stronger when a local indigenous organisation brings it with documentation already assembled. THE CAMPAIGN IT RUNS AGAINST FORTRESS CONSERVATION: TELL A WORLD HERITAGE BODY THAT EVICTIONS, ARRESTS AND VIOLENCE AGAINST AN INDIGENOUS PASTORALIST PEOPLE IN THE NAME OF FORTRESS CONSERVATION HAVE TO END — AND HELP US CAMPAIGN AGAINST THE COMPLICITY OF WESTERN CONSERVATIONISTS AND DONORS IN THE EVICTIONS, WHICH WILL ALSO PUT PRESSURE ON THE GOVERNMENT. A WORLD HERITAGE BODY as the target. Heritage listing is what a government invokes to justify clearing people from a landscape, and the listing body has its own reporting and reactive-monitoring procedures — so the designation cuts both ways, and pressure abroad translates into pressure at home. THE FRAMING IT USES: THE PEOPLE NEED THEIR LAND IN ORDER TO SURVIVE AND LIVE WELL — AND THEY HAVE A RIGHT TO IT. FOR THE PEOPLE, FOR NATURE, FOR ALL HUMANITY. Need and right stated together, with nature on the same side. Communities are routinely forced to argue either that they are harmless to wildlife or that their rights outweigh it; this refuses the choice. THE CARBON NOTE ON THE SAME PAGE: A CARBON CERTIFIER HAS RE-CERTIFIED, FOR THE SECOND TIME, A CONTROVERSIAL CARBON CREDITS PROJECT IN AN EAST AFRICAN COUNTRY. Re-certified twice despite the controversy — which is the practical answer to whether certifier review protects anyone, and it matches the grievance-mechanism finding filed under Comoros. THE STATED PURPOSE OF ITS CAMPAIGNS: THEY GENERALLY FOCUS ON TRIBAL PEOPLES' DESIRES TO KEEP THEIR ANCESTRAL LANDS, WHICH THEY RELY ON FOR FOOD, HOUSING, MEDICINES, CLOTHING AND A SENSE OF IDENTITY AND BELONGING — AIMING TO ERADICATE WHAT IT CALLS COLONIAL LAND GRABS, AND TO PUBLICISE HARM CAUSED TO TRIBES BY CORPORATIONS AND GOVERNMENTS. HOW IT WORKS WITH LOCAL BODIES: IT WORKS CLOSELY WITH LOCAL INDIGENOUS ORGANIZATIONS, AND OFFERS TRIBAL PEOPLE THEMSELVES A PLATFORM TO ADDRESS THE WORLD. THE PREJUDICE IT NAMES AND WORKS AGAINST: TRIBAL PEOPLES ARE PORTRAYED AS BACKWARD AND PRIMITIVE SIMPLY BECAUSE THEIR COMMUNAL WAYS ARE DIFFERENT, AND INDUSTRIALIZED SOCIETIES SUBJECT THEM TO VIOLENCE SO THEY CAN TAKE THEIR LANDS, RESOURCES AND LABOR IN THE NAME OF PROGRESS AND CIVILIZATION — WITH ITS EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMMES AIMED AT DEMOLISHING THE MYTH THAT TRIBAL PEOPLE ARE RELICS DESTINED TO PERISH THROUGH PROGRESS. The same framing this file has recorded being used against pastoralists before their grazing is reallocated. Naming it as a myth with a purpose — to justify taking land — is what turns an insult into an argument you can answer. THE POSTURE IT STATES: IF WE WANT TO HELP SOCIETIES OUR FIRST JOB IS TO LISTEN, RATHER THAN TO DICTATE WHAT WE THINK THEY NEED, AND WE MUST BE PREPARED TO BE SURPRISED. AND THE SCALE IT ORGANISES AROUND: MORE THAN 476 MILLION INDIGENOUS PEOPLE IN MORE THAN 90 COUNTRIES, INCLUDING AT LEAST 196 UNCONTACTED PEOPLES IN 10 COUNTRIES, WITH CAMPAIGNS IN THE AMERICAS, AFRICA, THE PACIFIC AND ASIA — AND A FREE MAILING LIST FOR URGENT UPDATES. The free mailing list is the low-cost thing to do today: it is how a community organisation learns that an urgent action is running on a case like its own, and who is already mobilised. WHO IT SUITS: African indigenous and pastoralist peoples facing eviction in the name of conservation, heritage listing or carbon — approaching through a local indigenous organisation. CAVEATS: A CAMPAIGNING ORGANISATION TAKING A SMALL NUMBER OF CASES, NOT A LAW FIRM OR A FUNDER, AND ITS CONFRONTATIONAL METHOD IS CONTESTED BY SOME CONSERVATION BODIES — weigh that against a working relationship you may need locally. For the contact points it used, Chad's entry; for the co-complainant route to the continental court, Seychelles' entry; for the carbon grievance review, Comoros' entry.

trackers.name: La Vía Campesina — an international peasant movement a farmers organisation can join as a member — two African regions, each electing one man, one woman and a youth to the coordinating committee, and a rule barring anyone who is not a genuine grassroots peasant body
trackers.desc: YOUR FARMERS ORGANISATION CAN JOIN IT, AND ELECT WHO SPEAKS FOR AFRICA — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S ALGERIA ENTRY MENTIONS A GLOBAL PEASANT MOVEMENT AS THE GRANTEE OF A FUNDER WITHOUT NAMING IT OR SHIPPING ITS HOST; THIS ENTRY IS THAT MOVEMENT, DESCRIBED ON ITS OWN TERMS. ITS LIBYA, MALI, MAURITANIA, SEYCHELLES AND ESWATINI ENTRIES COVER THE AFRICAN FARMER FEDERATIONS AND THE CONTINENTAL PLATFORM; THOSE ARE SEPARATE BODIES AND ARE NOT RESTATED. NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. THE MEMBERSHIP RULE, WHICH IS THE FIND: IT DOES NOT ACCEPT INTO MEMBERSHIP ORGANISATIONS THAT ARE NOT TRUE, GRASSROOTS-BASED PEASANT ORGANISATIONS — UNLIKE MANY CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, IT ESTABLISHED IMPORTANT CRITERIA FOR BUILDING ITS MEMBERSHIP AND SETTING THE PRINCIPLES FOR FUNDING. The gate is aimed at NGOs, not at communities. An organisation of actual farmers is what qualifies; a professional body speaking on farmers' behalf is what does not. That reverses the sorting this file has recorded across almost every network in it, where the well-staffed intermediary gets the seat and the growers' association does not. HOW EACH REGION IS REPRESENTED, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: THE INTERNATIONAL COORDINATING COMMITTEE IS REPRESENTED BY ONE MAN AND ONE WOMAN PER REGION AND ONE YOUTH PER CONTINENT, EACH ELECTED BY THEIR RESPECTIVE REGION'S MEMBER ORGANISATIONS. Elected by the members, with gender parity built into the seat rather than into a policy. A member organisation votes on who represents its region internationally — which is a form of standing this file has otherwise recorded only as something conferred from outside. THE TWO AFRICAN REGIONS: THE MOVEMENT IS ORGANISED IN NINE REGIONS, TWO OF WHICH ARE AFRICAN — ONE COVERING COUNTRIES IN THE SOUTH OF THE CONTINENT AND ONE COVERING NORTH AND WEST AFRICA. Two regions, so four adult seats plus youth representation for Africa. Worth knowing which region your country sits in before approaching, because the regional secretariat is the practical contact rather than the international office. THE SCALE AND WHO IS IN IT: 182 ORGANISATIONS IN 81 COUNTRIES, WITH EARLIER FIGURES OF MORE THAN 164 IN OVER 73 — A CONSTITUENCY OF OVER 200 MILLION PEASANTS, SMALL AND MEDIUM-SIZED PRODUCERS, LANDLESS PEOPLE, RURAL WORKERS AND INDIGENOUS PEOPLE. LANDLESS PEOPLE are named in the constituency. A community that has already lost its land is inside this movement's definition, not outside it. WHO THE MEMBERS ARE: ORGANIZATIONS OF PEASANTS, SMALL AND MEDIUM-SCALE FARMERS, RURAL WOMEN, FARM WORKERS AND INDIGENOUS AGRARIAN COMMUNITIES — A GRASSROOTS MOVEMENT, WITH ACTIVISM AT THE LOCAL AND NATIONAL LEVEL. WHY AFRICAN MOVEMENTS JOIN, IN THEIR OWN FRAMING: AFRICA, INCLUDING THE MAGHREB REGION, WAS THE LAST CONTINENT TO BE PART OF THE MOVEMENT; SINCE 2004 THE NUMBER OF AFRICAN PEASANT MOVEMENTS JOINING HAS BEEN INCREASING, AND AFRICAN MOVEMENTS CONSIDER THEIR MEMBERSHIP AS A STRATEGIC PROCESS OF AMPLIFYING THEIR STRUGGLES AND REINFORCING INTERNATIONALISM. A STRATEGIC PROCESS OF AMPLIFYING THEIR STRUGGLES — African members' own reason, not the movement's pitch. Joining is described by the people who did it as a tactic, which is the honest way to weigh it. THE HIGHEST DECISION-MAKING SPACE: THE INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE IS THE HIGHEST AND MOST SIGNIFICANT DECISION-MAKING SPACE OF THE MOVEMENT, WHERE AFRICAN PEASANTS HAVE HIGHLIGHTED THEIR STRUGGLES. A member organisation can put its own land conflict on the agenda of a global conference. For a community whose government ignores it, that is a forum that exists and can be reached. WHAT MEMBERSHIP GIVES A LOCAL ORGANISATION: IT PROVIDES OPPORTUNITIES FOR PEASANTS TO ARTICULATE A COHERENT SET OF DEMANDS IN THE INTERNATIONAL ARENA — ACHIEVED BY CONSOLIDATING A COLLECTIVE IDENTITY, PROVIDING SPACES FOR INTERNAL DEBATE, AND BUILDING ALLIANCES WITH OTHER SOCIAL MOVEMENTS AND PROGRESSIVE NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS. THE INTERNAL SUPPORT IT COMMITTED TO: EXTRA EFFORT TO INTERNAL TRAINING FOR MEMBER ORGANISATIONS, STRENGTHENING OPERATIONAL MECHANISMS, AND BUILDING REGIONAL SECRETARIATS TO ENSURE SUSTAINED REGIONAL AND LOCAL ENGAGEMENT — DESCRIBED AS A CRITICAL CHALLENGE, AS SOME ORGANISATIONS ARE MUCH WEAKER THAN OTHERS. The movement says openly that its members differ in strength and that training them is the answer. A weak organisation is a recognised condition here rather than a disqualification — and internal training is one of the concrete things membership brings. THE AUTONOMY IT WAS BUILT FOR: IT EMERGED FROM RURAL ACTIVISM THAT CARVED OUT AN AUTONOMOUS SPACE, INDEPENDENT OF THOSE WHO HAD PATERNALISTICALLY CLAIMED TO REPRESENT THEM — SUCH AS THE CHURCH, CONSERVATIVE POLITICAL PARTIES AND EXISTING CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS. Founded specifically to escape being spoken for. That is the same complaint this file records from communities about the NGOs, ministries and consultants who arrive claiming to represent them — and here it is the movement's founding premise. WHAT IT ADVOCATES: FAMILY FARM-BASED SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE, AGRARIAN REFORM IN SEVERAL COUNTRIES, AND AGROECOLOGICAL AGRICULTURE REJECTING THE USE OF AGROCHEMICALS AND GENETICALLY MODIFIED SEEDS — REGARDING ITS FARMERS AS GUARDIANS OF THE DIVERSITY OF SEEDS ON THE PLANET, AND HAVING COINED THE TERM FOOD SOVEREIGNTY. Recorded plainly because it is a commitment, not a menu: membership means signing up to positions on seeds and agrochemicals. An organisation that works with certified seed programmes should know that before joining. AND THE EVIDENCE THE FRAMING TRAVELS: SINCE 1996 IT HAS DEFENDED THE CONCEPT OF FOOD SOVEREIGNTY, WHICH HAS SPREAD OVER SOCIAL MOVEMENTS AROUND THE GLOBE AND HAS EVEN BEEN INCLUDED IN THE REFORMED CONSTITUTIONS OF NAMED COUNTRIES — WITH THE MOVEMENT FOUNDED IN 1993. A phrase invented by peasant organisations that ended up in national constitutions. When a community is told its position has no standing in law, that is the counter-example: the language of the constitution can come from below. WHO IT SUITS: African farmers' unions, peasant associations, landless movements, rural women's organisations and agrarian communities — as members, not beneficiaries. CAVEATS: MEMBERSHIP IS FOR GENUINE PEASANT AND FARMER ORGANISATIONS, NOT NGOs OR SUPPORT BODIES; IT IS A MOVEMENT RATHER THAN A FUNDER, AND IT CARRIES POSITIONS YOU WOULD BE ADOPTING — approach the regional secretariat for your part of Africa. For the funder that has resourced this movement's national operations, Algeria's entry; for the continental African farmers' platform, Seychelles' entry.

trackers.name: A standing regional court covering fifteen West African states that individuals and NGOs can file with directly — no requirement to exhaust domestic remedies first, a three-year limit that stops running while the harm continues, and binding judgments
trackers.desc: FILE DIRECTLY — YOU DO NOT HAVE TO LOSE AT HOME FIRST — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S ALGERIA ENTRY NAMES THIS COURT'S DECISIONS AS PART OF A FREE LIBRARY WITHOUT DESCRIBING THE COURT; ITS GAMBIA AND LIBERIA BUCKETS MENTION IT IN PASSING; ITS GAMBIA BUCKET ALSO CARRIES THE PAN-AFRICAN PRO BONO LITIGATOR THAT PUBLISHES GUIDANCE ON IT. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS RUN ON THE HOST ACTUALLY BEING SHIPPED. THE EXHAUSTION RULE, WHICH IS THE FIND: THERE IS NO NEED FOR EXHAUSTION OF DOMESTIC REMEDIES IN ORDER TO APPLY — INDIVIDUALS DO NOT NEED TO PURSUE NATIONAL JUDICIAL REMEDIES BEFORE BRINGING A CLAIM, AND THE COURT HAS STATED THAT IT IS NOT AN APPEAL COURT, SO A CASE SHOULD BE FILED DIRECTLY WITH IT. Every other international route in this file requires a community to fight through its own courts first — years of cost, and the case usually dies there. This one does not. A West African community facing a concession, an eviction or a poisoned river can file at the regional court while the domestic system is still ignoring it, which is the single most useful procedural fact recorded in this file. WHO MAY BRING A CASE, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: PERSONS WHO ARE VICTIMS OF HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATION OCCURRING IN ANY MEMBER STATE — WITH BROAD ACCESS AND STANDING RULES THAT PERMIT INDIVIDUALS AND NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS TO BYPASS NATIONAL COURTS AND FILE SUITS DIRECTLY. Individuals and NGOs, by name. No observer status, no accreditation, no state sponsor — the barrier that this file recorded defeating applications at the continental commission does not exist here. THE ADMISSIBILITY CONDITIONS, STATED SHORTLY: THE APPLICATION MUST NOT BE ANONYMOUS, AND THE MATTER MUST NOT BE PENDING BEFORE ANOTHER INTERNATIONAL COURT OR A COURT OF SIMILAR STATUS. Two conditions, both manageable. But NOT ANONYMOUS is a real decision for a community whose organisers are already threatened — weigh it against the protection resources filed elsewhere in this file before naming applicants. THE TIME LIMIT AND THE EXCEPTION THAT MATTERS: CASES MUST BE BROUGHT WITHIN THREE YEARS OF THE CAUSE OF ACTION ARISING — BUT WHERE VIOLATIONS ARE ONGOING, THIS GIVES RISE TO A CAUSE OF ACTION DAY IN AND DAY OUT AND POSTPONES THE RUNNING OF TIME. A continuing harm resets the clock daily. Pollution still flowing, an occupation still in place, an eviction still unremedied — none of these times out, which matters for the long-running disputes this file is full of. THE TWO THINGS IT WILL NOT DO: IT WILL NOT HEAR MATTERS THAT HAVE BEEN DETERMINED ON THE MERITS BY DOMESTIC COURTS, AND IT HOLDS NO APPELLATE JURISDICTION OVER DOMESTIC COURTS — THOUGH ADMISSIBILITY IS NOT AS STRICTLY APPLIED AS AT THE OTHER COURTS. This is the trap on the other side of the open door: fight the case at home to a final judgment and you lose this forum. The choice of where to litigate has to be made early, with advice — not after a domestic defeat. THE LAW IT APPLIES: ITS DECISIONS INTERPRET THE AFRICAN CHARTER ON HUMAN AND PEOPLES' RIGHTS, WHICH A COMMUNITY PROTOCOL TREATS AS CONTAINING CONSTITUTIONAL PRINCIPLES SHARED BY ALL MEMBER STATES AND LEGALLY BINDING ON THEM. The Charter is where peoples' rights to their natural resources and environment sit — collective rights, not only individual ones, which suits a community claim better than most national constitutions do. THE MEMBER STATES IT COVERS: BENIN, BURKINA FASO, CAPE VERDE, CÔTE D'IVOIRE, GAMBIA, GHANA, GUINEA, GUINEA-BISSAU, LIBERIA, MALI, NIGER, NIGERIA, SENEGAL, SIERRA LEONE AND TOGO — HEADQUARTERED IN A NAMED WEST AFRICAN CAPITAL. Fifteen states, and the court sits on the continent rather than in Europe. Travel, translation and lawyers' costs are all regional rather than intercontinental. THE REPRESENTATION REQUIREMENT: REPRESENTATION BY AN AGENT OR LAWYER IS OBLIGATORY WHEN FILING, AND ANY LAWYER REPRESENTING A VICTIM MUST BE AUTHORISED TO PRACTISE BEFORE A COURT OF A MEMBER STATE. You cannot file alone — but the lawyer can be admitted in ANY member state, not necessarily your own. A community whose national bar is hostile or captured can be represented by counsel from a neighbouring country. THE LANGUAGE RULE: THE OFFICIAL LANGUAGES ARE ENGLISH, FRENCH AND PORTUGUESE, BUT A CASE AGAINST A MEMBER STATE MUST BE FILED IN ONE OF THE OFFICIAL LANGUAGES OF THAT STATE. Portuguese included, which covers the lusophone states this file has struggled to serve. WHAT HAPPENS AFTER FILING: THE DEFENDANT HAS A MONTH TO LODGE A DEFENCE; A JUDGE-RAPPORTEUR PREPARES THE CASE AND RECOMMENDS WHAT INQUIRIES MIGHT BE NEEDED — WHICH MIGHT INCLUDE FURTHER DOCUMENTS, ORAL TESTIMONY, EXPERT REPORTS, OR SITE VISITS; PROCEEDINGS ARE WRITTEN AND ORAL, AND JUDGMENT IS HANDED DOWN IN OPEN COURT. SITE VISITS. The court can come and look. For a community whose evidence is the place itself — the cleared forest, the tailings dam, the dry riverbed — that is a remedy no affidavit matches, and it is worth asking the judge-rapporteur for. THE FORCE OF THE JUDGMENT: JUDGMENTS ARE BINDING ON EACH MEMBER STATE, ON INSTITUTIONS OF THE COMMUNITY AND ON INDIVIDUALS — THOUGH THE COMMUNITY INSTRUMENTS DO NOT SPECIFY THE REMEDIES THE COURT CAN PROVIDE, AND IN PAST CASES REMEDIES HAVE INCLUDED AWARDS. Binding, but with no specified remedies and the enforcement problem this file records everywhere. Plan the implementation campaign alongside the case, and read this beside the national commissions filed under Algeria, whose published job is chasing exactly these decisions. AND THE CASES THAT SHOW ITS REACH: PATH-BREAKING JUDGMENTS AGAINST ONE MEMBER STATE FOR CONDONING MODERN FORMS OF SLAVERY AND AGAINST ANOTHER FOR IMPEDING THE RIGHT TO FREE BASIC EDUCATION FOR ALL CHILDREN — WITH THE COURT DESCRIBED AS FOUR COURTS IN ONE, AND IN A RECENT CASE CONFIRMING THAT A MATTER BEING UNDER JUDGEMENT DOMESTICALLY DOES NOT BAR ITS JURISDICTION WHEN ALL JURISDICTIONAL REQUIREMENTS ARE MET. A state condemned for condoning slavery, and another for failing on education — both brought by or for individuals. And the recent ruling that a live domestic case does not block the filing is the point to put to any lawyer who says you must wait. WHO IT SUITS: communities and organisations in the fifteen West African member states with a land, environmental or eviction claim their national courts will not hear or will not decide. CAVEATS: A COURT, NOT A SERVICE — A LAWYER IS OBLIGATORY, PROCEEDINGS TAKE YEARS, APPLICATIONS CANNOT BE ANONYMOUS, AND A DOMESTIC JUDGMENT ON THE MERITS CLOSES THE DOOR; REMEDIES ARE UNSPECIFIED AND ENFORCEMENT DEPENDS ON THE STATE. For the pro bono litigator that publishes guidance on this court, Gambia's entry; for the national commissions that monitor implementation, Algeria's entry.

trackers.name: Chapter Four Uganda, Kampala — first-line legal response when activists are arrested, with the Uganda Law Society pro bono scheme and Justice Centres Uganda as backups; its permit was suspended by the NGO Bureau in January 2026
trackers.desc: SOMEONE TO CALL IN THE FIRST HOUR AFTER AN ARREST — AND THE BACKUPS IF THEY ARE CLOSED — method and adjacency declared first: ELEVENTH NAMED-ATTORNEY ROUND. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN FOUR HOSTS AND SIX DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; THE SUBJECT'S OWN HOST AND FIVE FACTS ABSENT. ONE NAME MATCHED A UGANDA ENTRY ABOUT A STATE LEGAL AID SERVICE ON A GOVERNMENT HOST, READ IN FULL AND A DIFFERENT SUBJECT. THIS FILE'S BOTSWANA ENTRY COVERS THE FREE LEGAL DIRECTORY MODEL FOR A DIFFERENT COUNTRY. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE SERVICE, WHICH IS THE FIND: RAPID, EFFICIENT AND QUICK LEGAL RESPONSE TO VIOLATIONS METED OUT ON HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS AND PRO-DEMOCRACY ACTIVISTS DURING THEIR ACTIVITIES — PARTICULARLY WHEN SUCH ACTIVISTS ARE ILL-TREATED AT THE HANDS OF STATE AGENTS AND ARE SUBJECTED TO ARBITRARY ARRESTS AND DETENTION. An organisation whose entire purpose is the first hour. This file's Burundi entry records that counsel in the initial phase cuts torture by up to 80%; this is what that looks like as a standing service, built for the moment a land defender is taken at a protest or a site. WHAT IT WAS BUILDING TOWARD: A MECHANISM TO INCLUDE INTERNET PHONE APPLICATIONS, A TOLL FREE LEGAL AID HELP LINE FOR CIVIL RIGHTS, AND OTHER MECHANISMS THAT CAN ACTIVATE SWIFT AND IMMEDIATE LEGAL REPRESENTATION AND INTERVENTION IN EMERGENCY SITUATIONS. A TOLL FREE LINE FOR CIVIL RIGHTS, specifically, rather than for general legal advice. Worth asking whether one exists in your country — and if a coalition is building one, this is the design brief. THE FEASIBILITY FINDING BEHIND ITS DESIGN, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: A STUDY CONCLUDED THAT A COORDINATED AND ROBUST LEGAL RESPONSE MECHANISM WOULD BE IMPORTANT TO ENSURE EFFICIENT AND EFFECTIVE USE OF RESOURCES AND CAPACITIES — THE ORGANISATION NOT INTENDED TO REPLACE OR COMPETE WITH EXISTING HUMAN RIGHTS PROTECTION INITIATIVES, BUT TO HOST A ROBUST AND COORDINATED PROCESS. NOT TO REPLACE OR COMPETE, stated in its founding study. This file has recorded coalitions fragmenting because each new body duplicated the last; an organisation created explicitly to coordinate rather than to add is the corrective, and the feasibility study is a document worth reading before founding anything. THE THREE SHARED ASSETS IT SET OUT TO BUILD: EFFICIENT USE OF HUMAN AND OTHER RESOURCES BY WORKING WITH OTHER ORGANISATIONS; CREATION OF CASE AND REFERENCE DATABASES FOR USE BY ALL; AND THE CREATION OF A CIVIL LIBERTIES LAWYERS PLATFORM AND DATABASE. A LAWYERS PLATFORM AND DATABASE is the asset a community actually needs and almost nobody maintains: a list of which advocates in the country will take a civil liberties case. Building one is cheap and it survives any single organisation being closed. WHAT IT DOES ACROSS THE BOARD: WORKING IN THE COURTS, LEGISLATURE AND COMMUNITIES THROUGH STRATEGIC AND PUBLIC INTEREST LITIGATION, FIRST LINE LEGAL REPRESENTATION, RESEARCH AND DOCUMENTATION, LEGISLATIVE AND STRATEGIC ADVOCACY, AND GENERAL COUNSEL SUPPORT — OFTEN PRO BONO TO THOSE UNABLE TO AFFORD LEGAL AID, WITH FOCUS AREAS INCLUDING CRIMINAL JUSTICE, LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT RIGHTS AND ACCESS TO INFORMATION. ACCESS TO INFORMATION is the one that matters for a project fight: the same organisation that answers an arrest can also litigate a refused records request. WHAT IT DID IN PRACTICE AT THE START: FRONTLINE FIRST-LINE LEGAL RESPONSE FOR HUNDREDS OF CIVIL SOCIETY LEADERS WHO WERE ARBITRARILY ARRESTED FOR PARTICIPATING IN THE BLACK MONDAY MOVEMENT AGAINST THEFT OF PUBLIC FUNDS. HOW IT WAS INCORPORATED, WHICH IS A ROUTE IN ITSELF: INCORPORATED IN 2013 AS A NON-PROFIT COMPANY LIMITED BY GUARANTEE AT THE NATIONAL REGISTRATION SERVICES BUREAU, WITH COUNSEL LADISLAUS RWAKAFUUZI PROVIDING LEGAL SUPPORT DURING THE INCORPORATION PROCESS. COMPANY LIMITED BY GUARANTEE rather than an association. Where NGO registration is slow or politically controlled, the companies registry is a different door with different rules — and an advocate helped them through it for nothing. ITS FIRST COURT WIN: THE CONSTITUTIONAL COURT AGREED WITH THE SUBMISSIONS OF ITS NAMED LAWYER ON THE ISSUE OF QUORUM, STRIKING DOWN THE ANTI-HOMOSEXUALITY ACT 2014. An entire statute struck down on QUORUM — whether enough members were present when it passed. Procedural grounds beat substantive ones more often than communities expect, and the parliamentary record that establishes them is public. THE SUSPENSION, RECORDED WITHOUT SOFTENING: IN JANUARY 2026 THE NATIONAL BUREAU FOR NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS SUSPENDED ITS OPERATING PERMIT WITH IMMEDIATE EFFECT, CITING INTELLIGENCE REPORTS ALLEGING INVOLVEMENT IN ACTIVITIES PREJUDICIAL TO THE SECURITY AND THE LAWS OF THE COUNTRY, IN VIOLATION OF SECTION 42(d) OF THE NGO ACT CAP 109 (AS AMENDED). Check current status before relying on it. And note this is the second such closure recorded in this file within thirteen months, after the December 2024 suspension under Djibouti's entry — in both cases a regulator's notice rather than a prosecution. That is the instrument to expect, which is precisely why the backups below matter. THE FIRST ALTERNATIVE LISTED ALONGSIDE IT: THE NATIONAL LAW SOCIETY'S OWN SCHEME — PROFESSIONAL LEGAL AID WORK UNDERTAKEN VOLUNTARILY AND WITHOUT PAYMENT OR AT A LOW COST TO VULNERABLE OR UNDERPRIVILEGED PERSONS, WITH THE UGANDA LAW SOCIETY'S PUBLISHED PRO BONO SCHEME PAGE. The law society cannot be suspended by an NGO regulator. Where civil society organisations are being closed, the professional body is the more durable door — and this file has now recorded law societies inside civil society networks in three countries. THE SECOND ALTERNATIVE: JUSTICE CENTRES UGANDA PROVIDING FREE LEGAL SERVICES TO THE POOR, VULNERABLE AND MARGINALIZED INDIVIDUALS AND COMMUNITIES TO REALIZE THEIR RIGHTS — WITH ALL SERVICES DELIVERED BY THE LISTING AGENCY AND ITS PARTNERS, INCLUDING REGISTRATION, PROVIDED FOR FREE. AND THE THIRD, WITH ITS FULL SERVICE LIST AND ADDRESS: THE LAW SOCIETY'S LEGAL AID PROJECT, TARGETING INDIGENT MEN, WOMEN AND CHILDREN — PROVIDING LEGAL INFORMATION AND ADVICE; MEDIATION, NEGOTIATION AND OTHER ALTERNATIVE DISPUTE RESOLUTION; COURT REPRESENTATION; TRAINING PARALEGALS IN AREAS WHERE THERE IS LIMITED SUPPLY OF ADVOCATES; AWARENESS PROGRAMMES; PUBLICATIONS; LOBBYING FOR PRO-POOR LAWS; AND RESEARCH — WITH A PUBLISHED PLOT NUMBER, AVENUE AND POST BOX IN THE CAPITAL. TRAINING PARALEGALS IN AREAS WHERE THERE IS LIMITED SUPPLY OF ADVOCATES, run by the law society itself. A rural community can ask the professional body to train its own people, which is a request most communities never think to make. WHO IT SUITS: communities whose members are being arrested at project sites or protests, and organisers who want a first-hour contact identified before it is needed rather than after. CAVEATS: ONE COUNTRY, AND THE PRIMARY ORGANISATION'S PERMIT WAS SUSPENDED IN JANUARY 2026 — VERIFY ITS STATUS BEFORE RELYING ON IT AND USE THE LAW SOCIETY AND JUSTICE CENTRE ROUTES MEANWHILE; ITS FRAME IS CIVIL LIBERTIES AND CRIMINAL JUSTICE RATHER THAN LAND OR PLANNING. For the earlier regulator suspension of a comparable body, Djibouti's entry; for counsel in the first hours and its measured effect, Burundi's entry.

trackers.name: Natural Justice: Lawyers for Communities and the Environment
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an African public-interest law organisation — lawyers and paralegals working with communities facing mining, oil and gas, logging and large infrastructure, combining legal empowerment, community protocols, policy work and litigation. Hubs in Cape Town, Nairobi and Dakar, staff in Madagascar, Botswana and Guinea, and country programmes in Burkina Faso, Guinea, Kenya, Madagascar, Namibia, Nigeria, Senegal and South Africa. It also runs the Environmental Lawyers Collective for Africa and an EIA Process Tracker. WHO IT SUITS: an Indigenous or rural community whose land, water or customary rights are threatened by an extractive or infrastructure project. It takes selected cases and works project-to-project outside its programme countries, so expect an approach-and-assess conversation rather than open intake. IS THERE AN OFFICE NEAR YOU? YES — Dakar (hub). Natural Justice keeps 3 hubs: Cape Town, Nairobi and Dakar. A hub means staff on the ground rather than a project relationship. WHAT IT DOES: founded 2007 in Cape Town, it supports communities to know the law, use the law and shape the law — access to land and governance of natural resources, the struggle against harmful extractive and infrastructure developments, traditional knowledge and benefit sharing, community rights within conservation, and climate action. ITS SIGNATURE TOOL IS THE COMMUNITY PROTOCOL — a documented instrument letting a community set out its biological, cultural and spiritual resources, norms and values, and assert existing rights under customary, domestic and international law, aimed squarely at laws and projects developed by government and industry without consultation. Ask for it by name. Contact: 63 Hout Street, Cape Town 8001; +27 21 426 1633; info@naturaljustice.org.

trackers.name: African Environmental Defenders Fund (emergency grants)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the African Environmental Defenders Fund — an emergency grant fund run by Natural Justice with the International Land Coalition Africa, ICCA Consortium, PACJA, Oxfam Novib, FEMNET and others, giving up to US$5,000 to land and environmental defenders anywhere in Africa who are under threat because of their activism. It can cover the cost of legal representation where a defender is arrested, summoned or prosecuted, plus relocation and other short-term transitional costs. WHO IT SUITS: an individual frontline defender who is a citizen or legal resident of an African country, facing an imminent threat, and not already supported by another body — it is not project or core funding, and routine office and administrative costs are excluded. HOW IT DIFFERS: applications are rolling, by email or helpline, not to a grant round. Natural Justice's own site names Burkina Faso, Guinea, Kenya, Madagascar, Namibia, Nigeria, Senegal, South Africa and Botswana as its country programmes, which is where this entry is placed; the fund's stated eligibility is any African country, so apply from elsewhere on the continent too.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a pan-African feminist rapid-response fund with reach across all 54 African countries — small grants released quickly for unanticipated, time-critical situations rather than planned programme work, covering safety and protection needs when defenders are threatened and short windows for advocacy after an unexpected event. WHO IT SUITS: women's rights organisations, feminist collectives and movements in which women or gender-diverse people are the primary decision-makers. It does NOT fund individuals, and the action must be strategic, genuinely unanticipated, and completable in under three months. HOW IT DIFFERS: this is emergency money for a moment, not a budget for a campaign — decisions are fast and grants are modest.

trackers.name: Cour des comptes du Sénégal
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Senegal — audits government accounts and the use of public money.

trackers.name: Senegal EITI Register
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Publicly searchable.

trackers.name: Office National de Lutte contre la Fraude et la Corruption (OFNAC)
trackers.desc: Senegal’s national anti-fraud and anti-corruption office — investigates corruption and manages public-official asset declarations.

trackers.name: OHADA RCCM (regional company registry)
trackers.desc: Federated regional registry of companies and financial statements across all OHADA member states (based at the CCJA, Abidjan). Here you can trace companies, their directors and filings registered in Senegal.

trackers.name: Senegal — Bureau d’Appui à la Création d’Entreprise (APIX)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the APIX one-stop business office registers companies, issues the RCCM & tax ID and publishes legal announcements, Senegal. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Marchés Publics
trackers.desc: National public-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Senegal, and for how much.

trackers.name: Extraordinary African Chambers
trackers.desc: Extraordinary African Chambers — tribunal in Senegal (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: Code forestier 2018 — a commune can create its own bois communal
trackers.desc: THE AUTHORITY MOVED DOWNWARD, SO ADDRESS THE COMMUNE. Loi 2018-25 of 12 November 2018 replaced the 1998 Code and was aligned with the Code général des Collectivités locales, which redistributed environment and natural resource competences formerly held by the region to the department and the commune. WHAT THAT ENABLES: a bois communal is a wooded space created by the commune, outside the classified forest domain, for conservation or recreation — the commune can simply create one. The domaine forestier protégé covers forêts de terroir, réserves communautaires, bois communaux and natural sites of local interest. And conventions locales let territorial collectivities agree conservation and sustainable management of forest resources — subject to the forest service's opinion and approval by the State representative. Transferred competences must be organised in a plan simple de gestion or plan d'aménagement forestier. TWO FUNDS CAME WITH THE REFORM: the FNI for conservation of forest patrimony, and the Fonds local d'Aménagement (FLA), whose object is supporting the participation of concerned actors in implementing management plans — ask your commune about it.

trackers.name: Défrichement thresholds — who signs depends on the hectares
trackers.desc: KNOW THE THRESHOLD, AND WATCH FOR SPLITTING. A municipal council deliberation authorising défrichement is not executory until approved — and who approves depends on area: up to 10 hectares, the Sous-préfet or the Préfet; between 10 and 50 hectares, only the Préfet of the department; above 50 hectares, only the Governor of the region, by registered regulatory act at the Secrétariat général du gouvernement. That tells you whose decision to scrutinise — and whether a clearance has been divided into sub-threshold parcels to avoid a higher approval. THE HONEST CRITIQUE, from Senegalese analysis: requiring management plans for any forest over 20 hectares, drawn up by the local collectivity, was found to limit from the outset the exercise of these councils' power; under participatory management projects, delivery of cutting authorisations passed from rural councils to newly created village committees; private actors leasing community forest for hunting and tourism need the opinion of the regional council as well, giving a level with no territory of its own access to resources and revenue; and forest agents sit on all regional and technical commissions. Decentralisation on paper is not control in practice — check who actually signs.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: Lumière Synergie pour le Développement — files complaints against the banks funding the project, and has had them declared admissible
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Senegalese non-profit, constituted in 2008, that attacks a project through its financiers rather than through its permits — which is the route that exists when a national process is closed or already decided. It has filed, with the affected communities themselves as co-complainants: a complaint to the African Development Bank's accountability mechanism over the Sendou coal plant at Bargny, alongside the women fish processors whose livelihoods it affected; a complaint with the Collectif des Impactés de la Centrale Electrique de Malicounda against the AfDB over a 120 MW thermal plant; a complaint to the Turkish OECD National Contact Point against Tosyali Holding; and, with the artisanal fishers' association at the Langue de Barbarie, a complaint against BP and Kosmos Energy over the Grand Tortue Ahmeyim gas project, which the United Kingdom's OECD contact point ruled admissible in 2026 — the fishers called it historic. A Dutch development bank's independent complaints mechanism has sent repeated monitoring missions to Senegal on the Sendou case. WHY THIS MATTERS TO A COMMUNITY ELSEWHERE: every one of those routes exists because someone abroad lent the money, and none of them requires standing in a national court. The organisation also runs capacity-building workshops across Africa on the transparency, accountability and involuntary-resettlement rules of international financial institutions — including one for Ivorian journalists in Abidjan — so its expertise is deliberately exportable. WHO IT SUITS: communities affected by a project with a development bank, export credit agency or foreign multinational behind it, who can document the harm and are prepared for a process measured in years. CAVEATS: this is complaints work and advocacy, not litigation and not land purchase — the mechanisms produce findings, monitoring and negotiated remedy rather than injunctions, and the Sendou complaint has been running since the plant was built. Contact is by email to the executive director rather than through a published intake form.

trackers.name: Enda Pronat and the CRAFS land coalition — someone is on the ground within a day of a dispossession, and they have won 10,000 hectares back in court
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Enda Pronat, working in Senegal since the 1980s on agroecology and, for the last fifteen years, squarely on land grabbing — and a founding member of CRAFS, the Cadre de Réflexion et d'Action sur le Foncier au Sénégal, an alliance of farmers' organisations, scientists and NGOs. THE RAPID-RESPONSE SYSTEM IS THE PART WORTH COPYING ANYWHERE IN THE WORLD: CRAFS members each hold direct contacts in rural communities, share alerts internally by mailing list, and when farmers are dispossessed, at least one member organisation travels to the site THE SAME DAY OR THE NEXT, investigates, and reports back to the others. What follows is chosen case by case: informing residents of their rights, mediation, help organising marches, instructing lawyers, then press interviews, social media and formal approaches to the authorities. Speed is the scarce commodity in a land grab — boundaries and facts are established in the first week, and almost nothing in this file moves that fast. WHAT IT HAS WON: reported three judicial victories for local land rights, one of them over 10,000 hectares of farmland at Dodel, plus training for producers, elected officials and local authorities on land regularisation procedures in the Niayes, the groundnut basin and eastern Senegal. It works with the community at Ndiaël, dispossessed of more than 20,000 hectares of agro-pastoral land. It also helped rural communities set up local watch platforms (plateformes de veille) to defend their rights and mobilise when a grab starts — a standing structure, built before the threat arrives. Enda Pronat is Senegal's focal point for COPAGEN, the West African coalition on genetic resources, biopiracy and land grabbing across nine countries. WHO IT SUITS: Senegalese farming and pastoral communities losing land to agro-industrial or investor allocations. CAVEATS: a farmer-movement and advocacy organisation — it instructs lawyers rather than being one; CRAFS itself has no verified standalone contact point, so approach through a member such as Enda Pronat; and for pressure on a project's foreign financiers, Senegal's Lumière Synergie entry is the other route.

trackers.name: Océanium de Dakar and the Bamboung community marine protected area — 7,000 ha declared by the villages, guarded by villagers, paid for by its own eco-lodge
trackers.desc: WHAT A VILLAGE CAN DECLARE: Océanium, a Senegalese environmental association founded in 1984, working on mangrove replanting, coastal clean-up, and against overfishing, forest pillage and bush fires. It piloted the creation of the Bamboung community marine protected area (AMPC) in the Sine-Saloum delta — reported as the first functional community MPA in West Africa. THE SEQUENCE, WHICH IS THE PART TO COPY: work began in 2000; the artisanal FISHERS THEMSELVES proposed which bolon to protect, and the precise boundary was agreed jointly between Océanium, the Senegalese authorities and the fishers; the rural council of Toubacouta voted the creation UNANIMOUSLY by deliberation on 10 October 2002; conservation began in 2003; and a presidential decree in November 2004 gave official recognition to something that already existed on the water. The community acted first and the state ratified afterwards — the opposite order to almost every other route in this file. SCALE AND WHO GUARDS IT: 7,000 hectares with the support of 13 surrounding villages, 72 fish species recorded; the eco-guards are residents of the neighbouring villages, taking shifts in a watchtower at the river mouth, and most of the area's 23 employees began as eco-guards. HOW IT PAYS FOR ITSELF: the villagers OWN the Keur Bamboung eco-tourism lodge, and its takings fund the area's running costs and surveillance plus community projects — with visitor numbers deliberately capped. Océanium has since run the same process at Pointe Saint-Georges and in the Petit Kasa in Casamance, and advises on community MPAs elsewhere in the sub-region. WHO IT SUITS: Senegalese coastal and estuarine villages wanting a protected zone they control and finance, and communities elsewhere studying how to make protection pay its own way. CAVEATS: management sits in a partnership with the state marine directorate and the communal council, so it is CO-management, not sole community control; the model depends on tourism revenue and on continued village consensus across 13 villages. For land-grab response and litigation in Senegal, the Enda Pronat entry; for pressure on a project's financiers, Lumière Synergie.

trackers.name: Nébéday — works through the village committees that already exist, and will not plant on land people are using
trackers.desc: WHO WORKS WITH THE COMMITTEE YOU ALREADY HAVE: Nébéday (Wolof for the moringa, the “tree of life”), a Senegalese association for participatory management of natural resources, created in June 2011 by a former coordinator of Océanium projects, with the stated motto that the environment sits at the heart of development. Its work runs across the Sine-Saloum, Petite Côte, Thiès and Saint-Louis regions. THE METHOD, AND IT IS THE PART WORTH INSISTING ON WITH ANY OUTSIDE ORGANISATION: it works with inter-village forest management committees, marine protected area management committees and local artisanal fishing councils (CLPA) to decide WHERE to plant and WHICH species — explicitly so that the work respects existing uses and community dynamics, for example by NOT replanting an area people are already using. An organisation that asks your existing committee which ground is in use, instead of arriving with a map, is the kind to let onto your land. WHAT IT DELIVERS: reported at nearly 3 million trees planted since 2015, with 1,150,000 planted in 2020; in the classified forests of the Sine-Saloum, 56,156 trees planted with community participation — 15,222 in Djilor forest, 10,770 in Néma Bah and 30,164 in Sangako. In Sangako it supported a forest management plan, 55,574 seedlings raised in 15 VILLAGE NURSERIES, firebreaks cleared, 5 villages engaged and 14 village committees established. Since 2016 every planting is recorded by species, zone, date and GEOLOCATION in a public register — which is exactly the evidence a community needs if someone later claims the land was empty. It also supports income activities that make protection pay: mangrove beekeeping, improved cookstoves, straw-based biochar, and women's producer groups. WHO IT SUITS: Senegalese villages with a forest, mangrove or protected-area committee wanting restoration that strengthens rather than overrides local governance. CAVEATS: a restoration and livelihoods organisation — NOT a legal service, and not a route for contesting a concession or an expropriation; its geography is concentrated in the Saloum and the north. For land grabs, Senegal's Enda Pronat entry; for financier complaints, Lumière Synergie; for the community MPA model, Océanium.

trackers.name: AJS Boutiques de Droit — ten free legal-advice shops across Senegal with published addresses and phone numbers, and LAND is among the commonest questions
trackers.desc: WHERE TO WALK IN: the Association des Juristes Sénégalaises (AJS), founded 1974, runs BOUTIQUES DE DROIT — spaces of listening, accompaniment and orientation on legal and judicial matters, staffed by jurists trained in listening and counselling techniques, with consultations FREE whatever the nature of the problem. The name was deliberately not commercial: the point was to put law in a shop people already pass. TEN BOUTIQUES ARE OPERATIONAL ACROSS THE NATIONAL TERRITORY — three in the Dakar region (Médina, Pikine, Gueule Tapée-Fass-Colobane) plus Thiès, Kaolack, Kolda, Kébémer, Sédhiou and Kédougou, and the association publishes the street address, telephone number and e-mail of each one: Pikine at the Maison de la Femme, Icotaf Est, 76 555 65 92 / 33 834 24 30; Thiès at CEDAF on the two-lane road toward the Zac, 76 555 65 95; Kaolack in the old public works building facing the gendarmerie, 33 942 22 67; Kolda at CEDAF-Sare Kemo, 76 555 65 93; Kébémer, Quartier Galla facing the lycée, 33 969 12 07. Published addresses and phone numbers for ten offices is the single most actionable access record in this file — nothing else here lets a person in a regional town simply ring the nearest door. WHY IT BELONGS IN A LAND MAP: staff report that inheritance, LAND (foncier) and civil-status questions are the most recurrent, and the boutiques orient people to the tax and domains service (impôts et domaines) on land matters, conduct mediations, draft requests that go to court and write complaints. Reported volume: 6,367 legal consultations in 2024, 3,807 of them in family law. WHO IT SUITS: Senegalese households — especially women — with an inheritance, land or civil-status problem, in Dakar or in the regions. CAVEATS: ADVICE, MEDIATION AND DRAFTING RATHER THAN COURTROOM REPRESENTATION, with a women-and-children focus; several boutiques run on project funding, so confirm the nearest is open. For land grabs and the 24-hour rapid response, Senegal's Enda Pronat entry; for pressure on a project's financiers, Lumière Synergie; for the community marine protected area model, Océanium.

trackers.name: Senegal's réserves naturelles communautaires — the rural council creates it, the state recognises it, the mayors govern it, and a minister used one to stop a mine
trackers.desc: HOW A COMMUNITY TAKES A TERRITORY UNDER ITS OWN PROTECTION: Senegal's RÉSERVE NATURELLE COMMUNAUTAIRE (RNC) is created on the initiative of local populations and BY DECISION OF THE LOCAL COUNCIL, and is then LEGALLY RECOGNISED BY THE STATE — at DINDÉFELO (Kédougou) the Conseil Rural decided in 2010 to create the reserve after scientific studies, with a management plan and an inventory following. WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE AT SCALE: the RNC DU BOUNDOU, created 2009, covers 120,000 HECTARES of former hunting land across FOUR COMMUNES — Dougué, Sinthiou Fissa, Koussan and Toumboura — and is MANAGED BY THE COMMUNITIES THROUGH A CONSERVATOIRE (CORENA) DIRECTED BY THE MAYORS OF THOSE FOUR COMMUNES, supported by a manager seconded from the national parks directorate and a salaried warden-animator DRAWN FROM THE LOCAL COMMUNITIES.
