Four communes governing 120,000 hectares jointly is the answer to the boundary problem that stopped Eswatini's Sivule project dead — create the reserve across all the communes that share the land, and make the mayors the board. The RNC de Palmarin, created 15 May 2001 on local initiative, covers 10,430 hectares in the Saloum delta. THE DOCUMENTED WIN, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS AN ACQUIRE INSTRUMENT AND NOT A LABEL: on a visit to Dindéfelo the environment minister OPPOSED ANY POSSIBILITY OF DOLOMITE EXTRACTION INSIDE THE RESERVE, undertook to find a solution with local authorities to STOP that mining project, and committed to posting a water-and-forests agent on site and a mobile anti-bushfire unit. A community reserve gave a minister the ground to refuse a mine — that is the whole case for creating one before a project arrives rather than after. WHO IT SUITS: Senegalese rural communities wanting durable protection over a shared territory, especially where several communes share it. CAVEATS: THIS IS COMMUNITY MANAGEMENT UNDER STATE RECOGNITION, NOT PRIVATE OWNERSHIP — it depends on council decision and continuing state acceptance, and reserves have been sustained by external project funding. For land grabs and the 24-hour rapid response, Senegal's Enda Pronat entry; for the community marine protected area at Bamboung, Océanium; for free legal advice with published addresses, the AJS Boutiques de Droit.

trackers.name: Senegal's DAMCP — the state directorate that accompanies communities into marine protected areas, and the two decrees showing a commune's letter can create one
trackers.desc: THE LETTER THAT CREATED A PROTECTED AREA: Senegal created the DIRECTION DES AIRES MARINES COMMUNAUTAIRES PROTÉGÉES (DAMCP) to strengthen protection of fisheries, and its stated mission is SUPPORT TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF COMMUNITY INITIATIVES for better management of marine and coastal ecosystems. A state directorate whose named job is accompanying communities is a door, not an obstacle — and the file shows two worked examples with decree numbers. SANGOMAR: THE AIRE MARINE PROTÉGÉE DE SANGOMAR WAS CREATED BY DÉCRET N°2014-338 OF 25 MARCH 2014 AT THE REQUEST OF THE LOCAL COMMUNITIES OF THE COMMUNES OF PALMARIN AND DIONEWAR. AT 87,437 HECTARES IT IS THE LARGEST MARINE PROTECTED AREA IN SENEGAL, AND IT TAKES IN THE THREE ISLAND VILLAGES OF DIONEWAR COMMUNE — NIODIOR, DIONWAR AND FALIA — AND FIVE VILLAGES OF PALMARIN — NGALOU, SESSÈNE, NGUETH, NGOUNOMANE AND DIAKHANOR, WITH THE HAMLET OF DJIFFER. Eighty-seven thousand hectares protected AT THE REQUEST OF the communities, with every village named in the record. Ask for your village to be named in the decree — being inside the boundary and being named in the instrument are not the same thing. SOKONE, AND THIS IS THE PROCEDURE IN ONE SENTENCE: FOLLOWING A LETTRE DE SAISINE FROM THE COMMUNE OF SOKONE, THE DAMCP ACCOMPANIED THE COMMUNITIES IN PUTTING IN PLACE A MARINE PROTECTED AREA, AND DÉCRET N°2023-337 OF 15 FEBRUARY 2023 CREATED THE AIRE MARINE PROTÉGÉE DE SOKONE COVERING 21,426 HECTARES ACROSS THE FLUVIO-MARITIME PARTS OF THE COMMUNES OF SOKONE, DJILOR, DIOSSONG, TOUBACOUTA AND BASSOUL. A commune wrote a letter and twenty-one thousand hectares became a protected area. That letter is the cheapest instrument in this entire file — have your commune write one, address it to the DAMCP, and ask which neighbouring communes should be joined to it, because Sokone's decree covers five. The earlier network was created by decree covering JOAL-FADIOUTH including the commune's maritime dependencies, the arm of the sea and THE MANGROVE; ABENE including the rural community's maritime dependencies and the mangrove; and BAMBOUNG, with each area's objectives and the principles of access, exploitation and management DEFINED BY JOINT ARRÊTÉS OF THE MINISTERS FOR ENVIRONMENT AND FISHERIES. The decree creates the area; the joint arrêté sets the access rules. Fight for the arrêté as hard as the decree — that is where who may fish and who may build is decided. WHO ELSE WORKS THERE: WETLANDS INTERNATIONAL'S WEST AFRICAN COAST AND GULF OF GUINEA OFFICE, whose named executive director works on a NATIONAL MANGROVE STRATEGY approved by the public authorities and awaiting financing, covering Senegal, Guinea-Bissau, Gambia, Sierra Leone and Liberia; and IDEE CASAMANCE, rue Capitaine Javelier, ZIGUINCHOR (ideecasamance.org), on wetlands protection in southern Senegal. A named project has also equipped the GESTION COMMITTEES of protected areas in Ziguinchor with boats and protective equipment, targeting over 6,000 women and about 86,000 people living beside the mangroves of ten marine protected areas and indigenous and community heritage areas of the Saloum Delta and Casamance. WHO IT SUITS: Senegalese coastal and estuarine communes and villages, and mangrove communities. CAVEATS: A STATE DIRECTORATE — it accompanies, it does not litigate. For the first functional community MPA in West Africa and the village-owned lodge, Senegal's Océanium and Bamboung entry; for the village committees that already exist, Nébéday; for the rural-council route to a réserve naturelle communautaire, the RNC entry; for ten free legal-advice shops, AJS Boutiques de Droit.

trackers.name: CONGAD and the Enda network structure — a national NGO council since 1982, 24 thematic teams and 21 decentralised branches, and the European office whose job is finding southern entities their funding
trackers.desc: TWENTY-ONE BRANCHES, AND THE OFFICE IN EUROPE THAT FINDS THE MONEY — starting with the council this file's Senegalese record did not hold: CONGAD, THE CONSEIL DES ONG D'APPUI AU DÉVELOPPEMENT AU SÉNÉGAL, DAKAR, HAS EXISTED SINCE 1982, and is listed alongside two further national bodies, CNCR AND FONGS. A national NGO council running since 1982 is the register of who is legitimate. Before you accept help from an organisation you have not heard of, ask whether it is a CONGAD member — and if you are forming one, ask what membership requires. THE STRUCTURE THAT EXPLAINS EVERY ENDA A COMMUNITY MEETS: ENDA TIERS MONDE — ENVIRONNEMENT, DÉVELOPPEMENT ET ACTION DANS LE TIERS MONDE — WAS CREATED IN 1972 IN DAKAR BY MEN AND WOMEN WHO BELIEVED IN THE POSSIBILITY OF A DEVELOPMENT THAT RESPECTS THE ENVIRONMENT AND IN THE PERMANENT SEARCH FOR SOCIAL JUSTICE FOR ALL. IT IS TODAY ORGANISED AS A NETWORK OF AUTONOMOUS ENTITIES CARRYING OUT THEIR OWN PROJECTS AND PROGRAMMES, WITH 24 THEMATIC TEAMS AT THE DAKAR HEAD OFFICE AND SOME 21 DECENTRALISED BRANCHES, 14 OF THEM IN AFRICA, CO-ORDINATED BY AN EXECUTIVE SECRETARY. AUTONOMOUS entities is the word that matters. The Enda body working in your area makes its own decisions — you are negotiating with that entity, not with a head office, and its commitments are its own. Ask which entity you are dealing with and what it can decide without referring upward. ITS STATED OBJECTIVE IS TO REINFORCE THE CAPACITIES OF LOCAL COMMUNITIES SO THAT THEY CAN TAKE CHARGE OF THEIR OWN DEVELOPMENT, THROUGH A PARTICIPATORY APPROACH ACTIVELY INVOLVING COMMUNITY MEMBERS IN THE DEFINITION OF THEIR NEEDS, THE PLANNING AND THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROJECTS — born in the South to serve the peoples of the South, and describing itself as having always fought against the marginalisation of the disadvantaged. THE PART WORTH ASKING FOR DIRECTLY: A EUROPEAN ASSOCIATION, CREATED 1977, REPRESENTS THE ORGANISATION IN THE NORTH — AND ITS STATED JOBS INCLUDE PUTTING THE SOUTHERN ENTITIES IN CONTACT WITH POTENTIAL PARTNERS IN EUROPE, AND SUPPORTING THOSE ENTITIES IN THE SEARCH FOR FINANCING AND THE ASSEMBLY OF PROJECTS, AS WELL AS TRANSMITTING RELEVANT INFORMATION FROM NORTH TO SOUTH AND LOBBYING TO INFLUENCE INTERNATIONAL COOPERATION POLICIES. An office in Europe whose written job is to find money and partners for African entities, and to write the applications with them. That is the function most organisations in this file lack entirely. If you are working with an Enda entity, ask whether it has been introduced to that interface — the fundraising capacity is inside the network, not outside it. AND IT RUNS THE ROOMS: a FORUM DES INNOVATIONS ET SOLUTIONS LOCALES VERTES held over three days in a named commune brought together PUBLIC ACTORS, RESEARCHERS AND GREEN ENTREPRENEURS; and a joint mission with a foreign refugee council examined a coastal north-western commune where HUMAN MOBILITY CAN NO LONGER BE ANALYSED INDEPENDENTLY OF CLIMATIC AND SOCIO-ECONOMIC REALITIES. A three-day forum with public actors and researchers in the room is where a community case gets heard by the people who write the studies. Ask when the next edition is and how a village group gets a slot. ALSO NAMED: JEUNESSE ET DÉVELOPPEMENT (JED), 49 AVENUE LAMINE GUEYE, DAKAR, WHICH DESCRIBES ITSELF AS IMPLANTED IN ALL THE REGIONS OF SENEGAL, DRAWING ON SCOUT VALUES, AT THE SERVICE OF YOUNG PEOPLE AND THE COMMUNITY, with environment among its listed cause areas. Implanted in all the regions with a street address in Dakar is exactly the shape a rural community needs: a national body with a local presence and one place to write to. WHO IT SUITS: Senegalese communities seeking a vetted partner, an entity with decision-making power, or help assembling a funded project. CAVEATS: A NETWORK OF AUTONOMOUS ENTITIES — what one commits to does not bind another. For the entity on the ground with farmers and the land coalition, Senegal's Enda Pronat entry; for the community marine protected area, Océanium de Dakar; for working through village committees that already exist, Nébéday; for ten free legal-advice shops, the AJS Boutiques de Droit entry; for the rural council creating a community nature reserve, the réserves naturelles communautaires entry.

trackers.name: The PRCM — a seven-country West African coastal coalition of 78 members from village associations upward, which any marine or coastal organisation can join by returning one signed form and charter
trackers.desc: FILL IN THE FORM, SIGN THE CHARTER, POST IT — placement note first: THIS IS A SEVEN-COUNTRY REGIONAL COALITION, FILED UNDER SENEGAL BECAUSE ITS SECRETARIAT AND FORUMS SIT IN DAKAR AND THE FILE HAS NO REGIONAL KEY. IT COVERS CAPE VERDE, THE GAMBIA, GUINEA CONAKRY, GUINEA-BISSAU, MAURITANIA, SENEGAL AND SIERRA LEONE. THE MEMBERSHIP DOOR IS THE FIND, AND IT IS AS LOW AS ANY IN THIS FILE: ANY ORGANISATION INTERVENING IN THE MARINE AND COASTAL DOMAIN MAY JOIN THE PARTNERSHIP — IT SUFFICES TO FILL IN THE INFORMATION SHEET, TO SIGN THE MEMBERSHIP FORM ACCOMPANYING THE CHARTER, AND TO RETURN IT SCANNED BY EMAIL OR BY POST. One information sheet, one signature, sent by email or in the post. No sponsor, no invitation, no minimum size. If your village association works on the coast in any of those seven countries, it can be a member of a regional coalition this month — and membership is what puts your name on the list that funders, ministries and researchers read. AND THE COMPOSITION PROVES IT IS NOT A CLUB OF BIG BODIES: THE STRENGTH OF THE PARTNERSHIP IS ITS DIVERSITY — ITS SPIRIT AND ITS STRENGTH RESIDE IN ITS NETWORK OF 78 MEMBERS, RANGING FROM SMALL ASSOCIATIONS ACTIVE AT THE LOCAL LEVEL TO VERY LARGE INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATIONS, CONCEIVED AS A GROUPING OF DIVERSIFIED FORCES AND INITIATIVES IN THE SERVICE OF A COMMON OBJECTIVE. Small local associations named in the same sentence as very large international organisations, as the point rather than the exception. A village association sitting in a body alongside the international NGOs that work on its coast is in the room where those organisations plan — which is the difference between being consulted about a project and being present when it is designed. WHAT BINDS THEM: THE PARTNERSHIP IS GOVERNED BY A CHARTER WHICH ENGAGES ITS MEMBERS ON THE PRINCIPLES AND VALUES THAT FOUND IT. Read the charter before signing — it binds the big members as much as the small ones, which means it is also a standard you can hold an international member to when it works on your coast. ITS ORIGIN: A JOINT INITIATIVE OF FOUR INTERNATIONAL NGOs — A CONSERVATION UNION, A WORLD WIDE FUND FOR NATURE, A WETLANDS ORGANISATION AND A BANC D'ARGUIN FOUNDATION — IN PARTNERSHIP WITH A SUB-REGIONAL FISHERIES COMMISSION. A fisheries commission of the states themselves as a founding partner. That is the body that regulates who may fish in these waters, sitting inside the same partnership as the conservation NGOs and the village associations. THE MONEY IT MOVES, WHICH IS WHY MEMBERSHIP IS WORTH HAVING: ONE GOVERNMENT SIGNED AN 8 MILLION EURO CONTRIBUTION FOR FOUR YEARS, ADDED TO 10 MILLION EUROS FROM A NATURE FOUNDATION AND 1 MILLION FROM A NATIONAL COOPERATION AGENCY — FOR A PHASE COVERING BIODIVERSITY CONSERVATION, SUSTAINABLE FISHERIES MANAGEMENT, AND INTEGRATED MANAGEMENT PROCESSES. Nineteen million euros across three funders for one regional programme phase. Money at that scale reaches the coast through member organisations — so the question for a local association is not how to apply to those funders directly, but which member is implementing in your area and what its programme covers. THE FORUM, AND WHO ATTENDS: MORE THAN 400 EXPERTS, DECISION-MAKERS, REPRESENTATIVES OF NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL NGOs, RESEARCH INSTITUTES AND MEMBERS OF CIVIL SOCIETY PARTICIPATE IN THE COASTAL FORUM, WHOSE OPENING HAS BEEN PRESIDED OVER BY A HEAD OF STATE, WITH GOVERNMENT MINISTERS AND THE DIPLOMATIC CORPS PRESENT. A president opening a conservation forum, with four hundred people in the room including the ministries and the funders. For a community organisation, one accepted abstract or one intervention from the floor at that forum reaches more decision-makers than a year of letters. Ask a member how to get on the programme. ITS NAMED PARTNERS INCLUDE DEVELOPMENT BANKS, A COASTAL AREAS MANAGEMENT PROGRAMME, A BLUE ACTION FUND, A GLOBAL ENVIRONMENT FUND, A REGIONAL ECONOMIC UNION, A MARINE PROTECTED AREAS NETWORK SECRETARIAT AND A BIRD CONSERVATION FEDERATION. A regional MARINE PROTECTED AREAS NETWORK secretariat is on that list — if your community manages or wants a protected area on this coast, that network is the peer body, reachable through the same partnership. AND THE FIGURE TO CARRY INTO ANY ARGUMENT ABOUT WASTE: THE LOSS OF NATURAL CAPITAL CAUSED BY PLASTIC POLLUTION, ON FISHING AND TOURISM ALONE, ALREADY AMOUNTS TO 8 BILLION DOLLARS A YEAR. Eight billion a year lost to fishing and tourism, which are the two industries governments in this region most want to grow. That number turns a rubbish problem into an economic one, which is the register decision-makers answer in. WHO IT SUITS: any coastal association, fishers' group or community organisation in the seven named countries. CAVEATS: A COALITION AND A PROGRAMME, not a direct grant window for villages — the money reaches you through member organisations. For the West African coastal training that put NGO leaders, journalists, builders and financiers in one room, Guinea's coastal partnership entry.

trackers.name: Sobanukirwa (Rwanda)
trackers.desc: Sobanukirwa (Rwanda) — Rwanda’s Freedom of Information request portal (in English, Kinyarwanda and French) — helps citizens request information from public bodies and publishes the responses. — Holds to account: Rwanda’s public authorities on disclosure — find public FOI requests, responses and non-responses.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a pan-African feminist rapid-response fund with reach across all 54 African countries — small grants released quickly for unanticipated, time-critical situations rather than planned programme work, covering safety and protection needs when defenders are threatened and short windows for advocacy after an unexpected event. WHO IT SUITS: women's rights organisations, feminist collectives and movements in which women or gender-diverse people are the primary decision-makers. It does NOT fund individuals, and the action must be strategic, genuinely unanticipated, and completable in under three months. HOW IT DIFFERS: this is emergency money for a moment, not a budget for a campaign — decisions are fast and grants are modest.

trackers.name: Beneficial Owners Register
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Access restricted to authorities/obliged entities.

trackers.name: Office of the Registrar General (RDB)
trackers.desc: Rwanda’s official business register within the Rwanda Development Board — company incorporation records.

trackers.name: Judiciary of Rwanda
trackers.desc: Official judiciary portal with case-tracking and published decisions. · Find here: information and judgments of the Judiciary of Rwanda.

trackers.name: Office of the Ombudsman (Rwanda)
trackers.desc: National anti-corruption body of Rwanda — investigates graft, financial crime and abuse of public office.

trackers.name: Transparency International Rwanda (TI-RW)
trackers.desc: Transparency International's Rwanda chapter. Publishes the Rwanda Bribery Index, analyses the Auditor General's reports on public financial management, runs a citizen complaints web portal (with the Supreme Court), and engages Parliament on anti-corruption.

trackers.name: Umucyo e-GP
trackers.desc: Rwanda's national e-procurement system. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Rwanda, and for how much.

trackers.name: Expropriation Law 32/2015 — the deadlines, and no suspension on filing
trackers.desc: THERE IS NO CUSTOMARY LAND OWNERSHIP IN RWANDA — every holder has a title, and after tenure regularization most hold emphyteutic leases (up to 99 years for agriculture, 20 for residential; investors 49). The community-land and customary routes this map records elsewhere do not apply here; the question is always the lease and the expropriation against it. THE DEADLINES UNDER LAW 32/2015: within 15 days of the valuation report being submitted the expropriator must decide and publish it, posting a copy at the Cell office and communicating through at least one wide-audience radio station and one widely read newspaper — if that did not happen it is a documented procedural failure. The window for signing an approved compensation report may not be less than 7 days or more than 21, so a demand to sign immediately is outside the law. THE APPEAL LADDER: 30 days after the project approval decision to appeal; then to the immediate higher Land Commission within 15 working days, which must decide within 30 days; then the competent court. THE RULE THAT SHAPES STRATEGY: under article 26, filing in court does not stop the expropriation from being effected — no automatic suspension, unlike Belgium or Switzerland. So the early rungs and the publication requirements matter far more than they otherwise would.

trackers.name: Attack the valuation method — and check for a development bank behind it
trackers.desc: THREE ROUTES BEYOND THE NUMBER ITSELF. 1. VALUATION IS ITS OWN LEGAL FIELD: Law N° 17/2010 establishes the real property valuation profession and stipulates the valuation methods to be applied — so challenge the method against that law, not merely the figure, which is a legal argument rather than a dispute about opinion. 2. THERE IS A VILLAGE-LEVEL FORUM: the Cell Adjudication Committee comprises all 5 members of the cell land committee plus 5 members of the particular umudugudu where demarcation is taking place, with the cell Executive Secretary as secretary without voting rights — and it can be used to resolve resettlement conflict in a project area before the Land Commissions. 3. CHECK WHO IS FINANCING: where a project is funded by the World Bank or AfDB, the implementing agency must satisfy World Bank ESS5 (formerly OP 4.12) and AfDB OS 2 on involuntary resettlement in addition to Rwandan law — and analysts record that the Bank policy goes further than national law on property rights and human settlement. A development bank behind the project means a second, often stronger, set of obligations and its own grievance route. ALSO WORTH CITING: Law 32/2015 is expressly grounded in the ICCPR, the ICESCR and article 14 of the African Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights — the statute invokes them itself.

trackers.name: Abunzi mediation committees — you cannot choose a court for a small land claim, and the committee that hears it is unpaid and untrained
trackers.desc: RWANDA MAKES COMMUNITY MEDIATION COMPULSORY RATHER THAN OPTIONAL: FOR CLAIMS UNDER THE THRESHOLD THERE IS NO COURT TO GO TO, ONLY THE CELL COMMITTEE. Mediation committees sit at cell level, with an appeal committee at sector level, in every district. Each committee is seven residents of that cell or sector, elected by the cell or sector council for a renewable five-year term, at least thirty per cent of them women, and they serve as volunteers, unremunerated. THE COMPOSITION RULE IS THE ONE TO CHECK, BECAUSE IT IS CHECKABLE AND IT IS BREACHED: members must be elected from among people who are not staff of local administrative entities or of judicial organs. If the person mediating your dispute with a local official also works for that administration, the committee is not properly constituted, and that is an objection you can make in writing before the hearing rather than an argument about bias afterwards. WHAT TO EXPECT: the process is oral, public and participatory, the parties pick three committee members to preside over their session, and the decision binds — a conventional court sees the matter only if a party appeals. CAVEATS, AND THE THRESHOLD IS THE IMPORTANT ONE: secondary sources put mandatory jurisdiction at claims below 3,000,000 Rwandan francs for land and other immovable property and 1,000,000 for movable property, but the ministry's own page does not state a figure and the organic law has been amended more than once — confirm the current threshold at the cell office before assuming your claim is above or below it. The people deciding a binding land dispute are respected neighbours, not lawyers, which is the system's strength for boundary and inheritance quarrels and its weakness where a company or an arm of the state is on the other side; commentators have argued for exactly that reason that disputes against the state should have another route.

trackers.name: ARCOS Network — a Kigali-based conservation network that backs community organisations, including in places nobody else reaches
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Albertine Rift Conservation Society, founded 1995, headquartered in Kigali and registered as an international NGO in Rwanda and Uganda, with over a hundred staff across three countries. It is a network of NGOs, community-based organisations and governments rather than a single field operator, which is what makes it useful to a small local group: its stated priorities are capacity building, information sharing and empowering the organisations already on the ground. THE PART THAT MATTERS FOR AN ISOLATED COMMUNITY: ARCOS has specifically supported community-based organisations in remote areas of eastern DRC and in Burundi, and built a regional information and training centre in Kigali to reach organisations in places that are hard to get to. If your group is too small or too far out to be visible to national NGOs, this is a network that deliberately looks for you. It also launched a revolving fund in 2017 — the terms are not set out on its public pages, so ask — and runs restoration work at scale across mountains, wetlands and farmland, including a thirty-year landscape project around Mukura Forest and the Lake Kivu catchment in Rutsiro and Ngororero districts begun in 2023. It holds the MacArthur award for creative and effective institutions. WHO IT SUITS: community organisations and local NGOs in Rwanda and the wider Albertine Rift — Burundi, eastern DRC, Uganda, Tanzania, northern Zambia — that need technical capacity, data or a regional ally rather than a lawyer. CAVEATS: a conservation and development network, not a legal or advocacy defence organisation — nothing here confronts a state project directly, and Rwandan civic space rewards partnership with government rather than opposition to it. Membership and fund terms are not published; the entry is placed under Rwanda because that is where it is registered and based, not because its work stops at the border.

trackers.name: Legal Aid Forum — walk-in free legal advice in Kigali, and community paralegals in all 30 districts whose commonest civil work is land
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Legal Aid Forum, a membership network of around 38 Rwandan and international NGOs, professional bodies, universities, legal aid clinics, faith-based organisations and trade unions providing legal aid, established 2006 and registered as a national NGO network in 2009. THE THINGS IT OFFERS THAT ARE RARE ENOUGH TO NAME: you can walk in during business hours and speak to its lawyer free of charge at the Kigali office; it has deployed community-based paralegals in all 30 districts of Rwanda, through a National Paralegal Network it helped establish in 2013, with district representatives elected by the paralegals themselves; and it runs mobile legal aid clinics that take paralegals, legal officers and attorneys into neighbourhoods rather than waiting for people to travel. Four university legal aid clinics sit in the network. WHAT THE PARALEGALS ACTUALLY DO, and why this belongs in a land map: their services are legal education, legal advice, mediation, referral and accompaniment, and their civil caseload is mostly land-related issues, alongside succession and family matters. WHY COST IS THE POINT: LAF's director has put the problem plainly — in the suburbs of Kigali there are people who cannot afford an advocate when a case goes to court, where the minimum cost is around RWF 500,000 — and LAF has an arrangement with the Rwanda Bar Association for lawyers to take such cases, with advice, mediation and other routes offered where court can be avoided. Kimihurura, KN 14, KG 668 St, Kigali; info@legalaidrwanda.org. WHO IT SUITS: Rwandans facing land disputes, expropriation or succession problems who cannot pay a lawyer, anywhere in the country. CAVEATS: a legal aid network for individuals and families rather than a campaigning or environmental organisation — it is not a route for opposing a state project, and Rwandan civic space is narrow; its work runs alongside the state Abunzi mediation route already recorded here, and for technical and conservation support Rwanda's ARCOS entry is the other one. THE SCALE, AND IT SHOWS THIS IS NOT A TOKEN SERVICE: over two years LAF served 24,666 individuals, of whom 1,058 received LEGAL REPRESENTATION before the courts, the National Prosecution Authority and the Rwanda Investigation Bureau; 17,019 of those cases were CIVIL and 7,647 criminal, with 16,032 female clients against 8,634 male. It describes itself as Rwanda's largest legal aid and human rights organisation, bringing together 36 MEMBER ORGANISATIONS — national and international NGOs, professional associations, university legal aid clinics and faith-based institutions, and it runs a NATIONAL CALL CENTRE alongside in-court representation. WHAT DECIDES WHETHER YOU QUALIFY: the National Legal Aid Policy of October 2014 provides legal aid — advice, assistance, representation, education and alternative dispute resolution — to indigent persons, women, children, persons with disabilities and victims of gender-based violence, WITHOUT LIMITATION as to civil, criminal, administrative, children or asylum cases; and LAF works through UBUDEHE, Rwanda's government social categorisation system, which is how indigence is assessed in practice. Find out which Ubudehe category your household is in before you apply — that classification, not your account of your circumstances, is what the assessment turns on. Pro bono work in Kigali is delivered with named Rwandan organisations including a women's rights NGO, a human rights association and the Rwandan human rights defence association, in collaboration with the Rwanda Bar Association and university legal aid clinics.

trackers.name: Rwanda's contrat de cession gratuite — land granted to NGOs, churches and nonprofit associations WITH NO LIMIT ON DURATION, and the association that restored Gishwati with it
trackers.desc: THE INSTRUMENT THAT PUTS LAND IN A NONPROFIT BODY'S HANDS: Rwandan land tenure includes the CONTRAT DE CESSION GRATUITE, GRANTED TO NGOs, CHURCHES AND OTHER NONPROFIT ASSOCIATIONS for donated or sanctioned land — and it has NO LIMIT ON ITS DURATION. An unlimited-duration grant to a nonprofit association is the strongest hold available in a country where almost everything else is leasehold; if your community can form a registered association, that is the vehicle to ask about. Compare the other named forms: the ACTE DE NOTORIÉTÉ, an occupancy permit common in urban areas, issued by the district mayor, with no fixed term but ANNUAL RENT plus a 6% TAX ON LAND VALUE ON REGISTRATION, preliminary to a long-term lease and mostly NOT REGISTERED CENTRALLY; and PAYSANNAT LAND, allocated in the 1960s-70s on condition of a use such as tea, with rights continuing SO LONG AS THE CONDITIONS OF USE ARE MET. If you hold paysannat land, the condition is the vulnerability — document that you are meeting it. WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE IN PRACTICE: FOREST OF HOPE ASSOCIATION (fharwanda.org), a Rwandan association working at GISHWATI — a forest that lost 98% OF ITS COVER in the early 2000s — which through the Gishwati Area Conservation Programme from 2008 and then as Forest of Hope significantly restored it through ASSISTED NATURAL REGENERATION and reduction of unsustainable resource use, with LOCAL COMMUNITY SUPPORT, now recorded as a conservation success. Around Gishwati-Mukura and Volcanoes National Park, community agroforestry plots, TEA COOPERATIVES and WOMEN-LED BEEKEEPING GROUPS hold ground outside the park boundaries. WHO IT SUITS: Rwandan associations, cooperatives and community groups seeking a durable hold on land for restoration or conservation. CAVEATS: THE CESSION GRATUITE IS A STATE GRANT TO A REGISTERED BODY, not a purchase — you must be constituted and the land must be donated or sanctioned; land pressure in Rwanda is extreme and most disputes recorded are intra-family inheritance claims. For small land disputes you cannot take to court directly, Rwanda's Abunzi entry; for representation and the Ubudehe category test, the Legal Aid Forum entry.

trackers.name: RISD, Kigali — helped draft Rwanda's Land Policy and Organic Law, works land conflict resolution and women's land rights in 11 districts down to cell level, with a published address
trackers.desc: THE ORGANISATION THAT HELPED WRITE THE LAND LAW: RWANDA INITIATIVE FOR SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT (RISD, risdrwanda.org), ESTABLISHED 1994 AND OPERATING FROM 1997, FOUNDED BY A GROUP OF RWANDAN PROFESSIONALS, which OBTAINED ITS LEGAL PERSONALITY AS A NON-PROFIT BY MINISTERIAL ORDER No. 090/11, GAZETTED 28 AUGUST 2003, at Nyarutarama Kangondo 1, House No. 2014, Remera, PO Box 2669, KIGALI, governed by a board and led by a named chief executive. RISD HAS BEEN INVOLVED IN THE LAND REFORM PROCESS SINCE 1999, WORKING CLOSELY WITH THE MINISTRY IN CHARGE OF LAND DURING THE FORMULATION OF BOTH THE LAND POLICY AND THE ORGANIC LAW, AND CURRENTLY ON THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE LAND REFORM. An organisation that sat in the drafting of the law now being applied to you knows what each clause was meant to do. That is a different kind of help from a lawyer who reads it afterwards — ask RISD what the provision was intended to mean. WHERE IT REACHES, WHICH IS THE PRACTICAL PART: RISD is PRESENT IN 11 OF RWANDA'S DISTRICTS — GASABO, KICUKIRO AND NYARUGENGE in Kigali City; KARONGI AND RUBAVU in the Western Province; KAMONYI, MUHANGA AND NYARUGURU in the Southern Province; MUSANZE AND GAKENKE in the Northern Province; and KIREHE in the Eastern Province — WORKING CLOSELY WITH GRASSROOTS COMMUNITY MEMBERS AND LOCAL LEADERS AT THE CELL, SECTOR AND DISTRICT LEVELS, while maintaining a high-profile relationship with the central government. Cell level is the smallest administrative unit in Rwanda. An organisation that works there is one that can be reached from a village rather than from Kigali — check whether your district is among the eleven. ITS NAMED FIELDS OF WORK: LAND CONFLICT RESOLUTION; LAND POLICY AND MULTI-STAKEHOLDER DIALOGUE; LEGAL ASSISTANCE, LEGAL EMPOWERMENT AND ACCESS TO JUSTICE; WOMEN'S LAND RIGHTS; SECURE TENURE RIGHTS; and constituencies including FARMERS, PEASANTS AND FOREST DWELLERS; it also engages on LAND DISPUTE MANAGEMENT, EXPROPRIATION AND LAND USE. Expropriation is a named part of its practice. If your land is being taken for a declared public purpose, this is the Rwandan organisation whose stated work covers exactly that. ITS OWN FRAMING OF WHY LAND MATTERS THERE: RISD RECOGNISES THAT ISSUES ON LAND ARE A GOVERNANCE ISSUE, and notes that new land issues are emerging as Rwanda experiences RAPID URBANISATION AND INCREASED POPULATION. ALSO NAMED: APEFA, working on environmental degradation, climate-smart agriculture and food security with a stated focus on integrating YOUTH AND WOMEN. WHO IT SUITS: Rwandans facing expropriation, a land dispute, or a women's land rights question. CAVEATS: A POLICY, RESEARCH AND ADVOCACY ORGANISATION with close government relations — pair it with counsel for a contested case. For mediation you cannot opt out of, Rwanda's Abunzi entry; for walk-in free advice, the Legal Aid Forum; for a Kigali conservation network, ARCOS; for land granted to NGOs in perpetuity, the contrat de cession gratuite entry.

trackers.name: ARCOS's 40,000 hectares and 56,000 farmers, the continental NGO alliance it launched that is open to applications, and a Rusizi district NGO that prints its legal personality number and its committee structure
trackers.desc: THE ALLIANCE THAT SAYS IT IS OPEN, AND THE COMMITTEES TO COPY: THE ALBERTINE RIFT CONSERVATION SOCIETY (ARCOS), FOUNDED 1995, IS A REGIONAL NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATION that EMPOWERS GRASSROOT ORGANISATIONS TO PARTICIPATE MORE EFFECTIVELY IN ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT AND BUILDING RESILIENCE, with a named founder and executive director. ITS GROUND NUMBERS: IT PLAYS A LEADING ROLE IN AFRICA IN LANDSCAPE RESTORATION, WITH GRASSROOT INTERVENTIONS WHERE OVER 40,000 HECTARES ARE UNDER RESTORATION AND 56,000 HOUSEHOLD FARMERS ARE ENGAGED TODAY. Fifty-six thousand household farmers is a restoration programme built out of individual farms rather than one fenced block. Ask on what terms a household joins — that is the unit that scales, and it is the unit a single family can enter. WHAT IT CONVENES: ARCOS HOLDS THE SECRETARIAT OF THE AFRICA REGIONAL MOUNTAIN FORUM AND HAS BEEN INSTRUMENTAL IN SECURING RECOGNITION AT THE HIGHEST LEVELS, INCLUDING THE AFRICAN MINISTERIAL CONFERENCE ON THE ENVIRONMENT — AND IT SIGNED A MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING WITH THE EAST AFRICAN COMMUNITY to join efforts on TRANSBOUNDARY ECOSYSTEMS, covering INFORMATION SHARING, CIVIL SOCIETY ENGAGEMENT AND SUPPORTING SUSTAINABLE COMMUNITY LIVELIHOODS. An NGO holding an MOU with a regional intergovernmental body, with civil society engagement written into it, is a route from a village to a ministerial conference. If your problem crosses a border — a river, a forest, a migration route — that MOU is the frame it fits. AND THE DOOR THAT IS EXPLICITLY OPEN: ARCOS LAUNCHED THE AFRICAN NGOs ALLIANCE FOR ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY (ANAES) IN KIGALI IN OCTOBER 2023, TO UNITE AFRICAN NGOs' CONSERVATION EFFORTS, FOSTER LEADERSHIP AND SHARE EXPERIENCES — AND THE ALLIANCE IS OPEN TO ALL AFRICAN NGOs THAT MEET THE NECESSARY SELECTION CRITERIA. Open to all African NGOs is stated, not implied. That is a continental alliance a registered organisation anywhere on this file's African record can apply to — ask for the selection criteria and the application route. THE LOCAL MODEL, AND ITS PAPERWORK: FRIENDS OF ENVIRONMENT AND SOCIAL DEVELOPMENT (FESD), A RWANDAN NON-PROFIT ESTABLISHED 2018 WITH LEGAL PERSONALITY NUMBER 898-RGB/NGO/LP/04/2023 PRINTED ON ITS OWN PROFILE, BASED IN GIHUNDWE SECTOR, RUSIZI DISTRICT, WITH A NAMED MANAGING DIRECTOR, founded to address CLIMATE CHANGE, DEFORESTATION, BIODIVERSITY LOSS, INAPPROPRIATE AGRICULTURAL PRACTICES AND DESERTIFICATION. ITS STRUCTURE IS THE THING TO COPY: 33 ACTIVE MEMBERS, WITH ROLES ACROSS A BOARD OF DIRECTORS, TECHNICAL COMMITTEES FOR TENDER, AUDIT AND CONFLICT RESOLUTION, EXECUTIVE DIRECTION, PROJECT MANAGEMENT, ACCOUNTANCY AND AGRONOMY — ALL WORKING UNDER THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY. A thirty-three member district association with a TENDER committee, an AUDIT committee and a CONFLICT RESOLUTION committee, all under a general assembly. Those three are exactly what fails first in the small organisations throughout this file: who awards the contract, who checks the money, and who settles a dispute between members. Write them into your constitution at the start. THE FIGURE WORTH CARRYING: Rwanda's cooperative approach is credited with the country's forest cover reaching 30 PER CENT, with ARCOS's director stating that WE HUMANS POOL RESOURCES, BENEFITTING FROM NATURE, BUT NOT PAYING BACK OR TAKING CARE OF NATURE — WE NEED TO PARTNER AND WORK TOGETHER TO RESTORE THESE DEGRADED ECOSYSTEMS; WHEN HUMANS ARE POOLING RESOURCES THEY DO IT INDIVIDUALLY, BUT WE CAN'T ACT INDIVIDUALLY. ALSO NAMED: a RWANDA ENVIRONMENTAL NGO FORUM sits within a national civil society platform's membership. WHO IT SUITS: Rwandan district associations, farmers entering restoration, and any African NGO seeking a continental alliance. CAVEATS: A REGIONAL NETWORK AND A SMALL DISTRICT NGO — neither is a litigator. For the organisation that helped draft the Land Policy and works at cell level in 11 districts, Rwanda's RISD entry; for mediation you cannot opt out of, the Abunzi entry; for walk-in free advice, the Legal Aid Forum; for land granted to NGOs in perpetuity, the contrat de cession gratuite entry.

trackers.name: LandNet Rwanda Chapter — a 32-member land network with its membership published, including the Office of the Ombudsman and two human rights leagues — plus the apex platform that ran a public dialogue on land expropriation and followed it up
trackers.desc: THE OMBUDSMAN SITS IN THE LAND NETWORK — and that single fact is why this membership list is worth reading rather than skimming: LANDNET RWANDA CHAPTER IS PART OF LANDNET AFRICA AND IS A NETWORK OF LOCAL RWANDAN ORGANIZATIONS AND INTERNATIONAL NGOs WHICH DEALS WITH LAND ISSUES — ITS IDEA BEING TO BRING TOGETHER ACADEMICIANS, POLICY MAKERS AND THE CIVIL SOCIETY TO DISCUSS TOGETHER ABOUT LAND ISSUES. IT WAS OFFICIALLY LAUNCHED ON 21 SEPTEMBER 2000 AND CONSISTS OF 32 NGO MEMBERS. THE MEMBERSHIP IS PUBLISHED, AND IT INCLUDES: TWO NAMED RWANDAN HUMAN RIGHTS LEAGUES; AN ASSOCIATION OF ECOLOGISTS; A WOMEN'S LEGAL ORGANISATION; AN ASSOCIATION OF PEACE VOLUNTEERS; A HEALTH-ENVIRONMENT PROJECT INITIATIVE; A POLICY ANALYSIS AND RESEARCH INSTITUTE; A NATIONAL UNITY AND RECONCILIATION COMMISSION; A NATIONAL UNIVERSITY; AND THE OFFICE OF THE OMBUDSMAN. An ombudsman's office and a national university as MEMBERS of a land network, alongside two human rights leagues and a women's legal organisation. That combination is rare and it is useful in a precise way: the ombudsman is the office that hears complaints about administration, and it is already sitting in the room where land grievances are discussed. If your land problem is an administrative one — a decision taken wrongly, a file that never moved, compensation not paid — that is the member to reach, and the network is the introduction. And a national university in the membership means the research capacity is inside the network too. A community that needs a study rather than a lawyer has a route that does not begin with a consultancy fee. THE APEX BODY ABOVE IT: THE RWANDA CIVIL SOCIETY PLATFORM IS AN APEX BODY OF RWANDAN CSOs WITH 14 MEMBERS, ESTABLISHED IN JULY 2004, WHICH SERVES AS AN UMBRELLA ORGANIZATION FOR CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS THAT THEMSELVES FUNCTION AS UMBRELLA GROUPS FOR OTHER CSOs WITHIN A SPECIFIC SECTOR. An umbrella of umbrellas, with only fourteen members. That is a small enough body to write to directly, and each of its members carries a whole sector behind it — so one letter reaches further than it looks. AND WHAT IT ACTUALLY DID ON LAND, WHICH IS THE MODEL: IT ORGANISED A PUBLIC POLICY DIALOGUE ON THE ANALYSIS OF LAND EXPROPRIATION AND TRANSFER PROCESS IN RWANDA, HELD AT A NAMED CONVENTION CENTRE — AND THEN HELD A ONE-DAY FOLLOW-UP MEETING SIX MONTHS LATER REGARDING THE PROGRESS IN IMPLEMENTING THE RECOMMENDATIONS, WHOSE OBJECTIVE WAS TO SET UP STRATEGIES WITH THE CONCERNED INSTITUTIONS FOR THE FOLLOW UP AND DRAW AN IMPLEMENTATION PLAN OF THE RECOMMENDATIONS. The follow-up meeting is the part nobody organises. A dialogue produces recommendations; six months later somebody has to ask what happened to them, in a room with the same institutions. Build the follow-up into the first invitation — name the date before anyone goes home. AND THE ROOM IT ASSEMBLED IS THE LIST OF WHO DECIDES ABOUT LAND IN RWANDA: THE INFRASTRUCTURE MINISTRY; THE MINISTRY OF LANDS AND FORESTRY; THE RWANDA LAND MANAGEMENT AND USE AUTHORITY; THE ROADS DEVELOPMENT AGENCY; THE RWANDA HOUSING AUTHORITY; THE ENERGY GROUP; THE WATER AND SANITATION CORPORATION; A PUBLIC PROCUREMENT AUTHORITY; AND ON THE CIVIL SOCIETY SIDE A NATIONAL NGO FORUM, A WOMEN'S UMBRELLA, THE ENVIRONMENTAL NGOs FORUM, A HUMAN RIGHTS COLLECTIVE AND THE LEGAL AID FORUM. Roads, housing, energy and water in the same room as the lands ministry. Those four agencies are the ones that actually trigger expropriations, and this file has recorded elsewhere that communities usually meet them one at a time. A dialogue that puts all of them opposite civil society at once is the format to ask for. THE ENVIRONMENTAL COALITION, WITH AN ADDRESS: THE RWANDA ENVIRONMENTAL NGOs FORUM IS A COALITION OF NGOs AND CBOs WORKING ON ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION, PUBLIC AWARENESS, AND CLIMATE CHANGE, AT A PUBLISHED KIGALI STREET ADDRESS. CBOs are named alongside NGOs in its own description — a community-based organisation is an eligible member, not just a beneficiary. WHO IT SUITS: Rwandan communities facing expropriation for a road, a power line, water works or housing, and groups wanting a research or ombudsman route. CAVEATS: RWANDA'S NGO LEGAL FRAMEWORK IS UNDER REVISION and civic space is constrained — this file records that plainly. For the organisation that helped draft the Land Policy and Organic Law, Rwanda's RISD entry; for walk-in free legal advice in Kigali and community paralegals, the Legal Aid Forum entry; for the mediation committees you cannot bypass for a small land dispute, the Abunzi entry; for 40,000 hectares restored with 56,000 farmers, ARCOS.

trackers.name: The Alternative Mining Indaba — an annual continental gathering held in the same city and week as the industry's own mining investment conference — community representatives from 33 countries, travel commonly paid by larger organisations, and a declaration marched across town and delivered
trackers.desc: THE SAME CITY, THE SAME WEEK, AND THEY MARCH THE DECLARATION OVER — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S ZIMBABWE ENTRY MENTIONS THIS GATHERING IN PASSING WITHOUT NAMING ITS DATES, STRUCTURE, DECLARATION OR FUNDING ROUTE; ITS NIGER ENTRY THE MINING-AFFECTED COMMUNITIES MOVEMENT THAT CONVENES AT IT; ITS MALAWI AND MAURITANIA ENTRIES THE PUBLIC INTEREST LAW CENTRES; ITS SOUTH AFRICA BUCKET A CENTRE FOR ENVIRONMENTAL RIGHTS HOST. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THIS GATHERING WAS CARRIED AS A PENDING CANDIDATE SINCE ROUND 20 ALONGSIDE THE MOVEMENT FILED LAST ROUND; BOTH FLAGS ARE NOW CLOSED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. THE TIMING AND THE PLACE, WHICH IS THE FIND: IT IS A SIMULTANEOUS COUNTERPOINT GATHERING TAKING THE SIDE OF AFFECTED COMMUNITIES, HELD IN THE SAME CITY AND THE SAME WEEK AS THE WORLD'S LARGEST ANNUAL MINING INVESTMENT EVENT — WHICH IN ONE EDITION DREW SOME 6,500 PARTICIPANTS INCLUDING TWO HEADS OF STATE, OVER 40 AFRICAN CABINET MINISTERS, AT LEAST 900 GLOBAL INVESTORS AND ABOUT 1,600 MINING INDUSTRY OPERATORS. Forty cabinet ministers and nine hundred investors are already in one city for three days. A community that cannot get a meeting with its own minister at home can be in the same place at the same time, once a year, on a date published far in advance. That is the whole logic of this gathering, and it is copyable wherever an annual investment conference exists. THE DECLARATION AND WHAT IS DONE WITH IT, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: ON THE LAST DAY WELL OVER 100 PARTICIPANTS BOARDED BUSES AND MARCHED SEVERAL KILOMETRES TO DELIVER THE DECLARATION TO THE CORPORATE MINING CONFERENCE. The document is not published and left online. It is carried, physically, to the door of the people it addresses, with press present because the press is already there for the conference. A declaration adopted by communities from 33 countries and hand-delivered is a different object from a submission emailed to a ministry. WHO ACTUALLY ATTENDS IT: PARTICIPANTS FROM 33 COUNTRIES INCLUDING REPRESENTATIVES FROM MINING-AFFECTED COMMUNITIES, HUMAN RIGHTS AND ENVIRONMENTAL ADVOCATES, NGOs, FAITH-BASED ORGANISATIONS, TRADITIONAL LEADERS, OFFICIAL STAKEHOLDERS AND PRIVATE-SECTOR REPRESENTATIVES — WITH MORE THAN 500 PARTICIPANTS IN ONE EDITION. FAITH-BASED ORGANISATIONS and TRADITIONAL LEADERS in the same room as community representatives and NGOs. For a community whose church or chieftaincy is a real power, that combination is unusual and worth using. HOW COMMUNITY REPRESENTATIVES GET THERE, WHICH MATTERS MOST PRACTICALLY: MANY ATTENDEES ARE FUNDED BY LARGER NON-PROFITS TO UNDERTAKE THE TRIP — WITH ONE INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATION BRINGING PARTICIPANTS FROM NINE NAMED AFRICAN COUNTRIES, DESCRIBING ITSELF AS ACTING AS A BRIDGE THAT PLACES LOCAL LEADERS IN A HIGH-LEVEL SPACE WHERE THEY CAN VOICE THEIR CHALLENGES AND SUCCESSES DIRECTLY TO A GLOBAL AUDIENCE. You do not pay your own way. The route in is to ask an international organisation already going to sponsor a delegate — and this file records several such organisations. That request is far smaller and far more likely to succeed than a grant application, and it should be made months ahead of February. THE PRINCIPLES THE DECLARATION REITERATES: THE LONG-STANDING PRINCIPLES OF NOTHING ABOUT US WITHOUT US AND THE RIGHT TO SAY NO — WITH ONE DECLARATION STATING THAT THE GATHERING WILL NOT BE MUTED, IN THE CONTEXT OF PANDEMIC RESTRICTIONS AND SHRINKING CIVIC SPACE. THE GAP IT EXISTS TO FILL, AS OBSERVERS RECORD IT: AT THE INDUSTRY CONFERENCE THE WORD COMMUNITIES STEADILY FELL FROM THE MOUTHS OF MINING EXECUTIVES AND GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS, MOST SUGGESTING THAT MAXIMIZING BENEFITS AND MINIMIZING HARMS FOR COMMUNITY MEMBERS WAS A SACROSANCT PRIORITY — BUT ABSENT FROM ALMOST ALL OF THE ROOMS WHERE THAT WORD WAS INVOKED WERE MEMBERS OF MINING-AFFECTED COMMUNITIES, WITH THE AGENDA INCLUDING ONLY ONE INVITATION-ONLY ENGAGEMENT SESSION. An independent account of an industry conference talking about communities all week with none present except by invitation. Worth quoting when a company reports that it has engaged extensively with stakeholders. WHERE THE COMMUNITIES WERE INSTEAD: ONE PLACE THAT WAS REPLETE WITH COMMUNITY STAKEHOLDERS WAS THIS GATHERING, WHICH HAS OPERATED IN DISTANT PARALLEL TO THE MAIN ONE FOR 15 YEARS. THE PROPOSAL PUT TO THE INDUSTRY: THE DEEP-POCKETED MINING COMPANIES AND RICH-COUNTRY GOVERNMENTS THAT SPONSOR THE INDUSTRY CONFERENCE COULD CONTRIBUTE TO A POOLED FUND THAT GRANTS ADMISSION AND TRAVEL BURSARIES TO COMMUNITY ACTIVISTS AND REPORTERS FROM AFRICA'S MINERAL-RICH NATIONS — WITH ONE SELF-FUNDED JOURNALIST REPORTING THAT NO MEDIA HOUSES BACK HOME COULD PAY FOR JOURNALISTS TO ATTEND. The absence of African reporters at the conference deciding African mining is a funding problem with a named solution. A community organisation can make the same demand of the companies operating on its own land: pay for our delegate and our local journalist to be in the room. THE FORMAT IT HAS MOVED TO: ONE RECENT EDITION REPLACED TRADITIONAL CONFERENCE STRUCTURES WITH WORKSHOP SPACES, DRAMA AND EXHIBITIONS THAT SPEAK DIRECTLY TO STATE ACTORS AND INVESTORS — UNDER A THEME OF ALTERNATIVE STORIES OF MINING. Drama and exhibition instead of panels. A community delegate who is not a practised conference speaker is not disadvantaged by that format, which is the point of the change. THE THEMES IT HAS RUN UNDER: A JUST ENERGY TRANSITION AND UNLOCKING COMMUNITY POTENTIAL AND PARTICIPATION; A JUST ENERGY TRANSITION FOR SUSTAINABLE MINING COMMUNITIES IN A CLIMATE CRISIS ERA; AND ENVIRONMENTALLY AND ECONOMICALLY SUSTAINABLE MINERAL ECONOMIES IN AN ERA OF CLIMATE CHANGE. WHO ELSE COMES AND WHAT THEY BRING: A CONTINENTAL CORPORATE ACCOUNTABILITY COALITION AND A UNIVERSITY HUMAN RIGHTS CENTRE HAVE ENDORSED ITS DECLARATION, AND A NON-PROFIT LAW CLINIC ATTENDS TO CONTRIBUTE EXPERT LEGAL INSIGHT ON MINE REHABILITATION AND THE ENFORCEMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL LAW. Lawyers are in the room, free, for three days. For a community that cannot afford an initial consultation, that is a realistic place to have its situation looked at by somebody who litigates mining cases — and MINE REHABILITATION is the subject most communities discover too late, when the company has gone and the pit remains. AND ITS STANDING DESCRIPTION: A COMMUNITY-LED AND JUSTICE-FOCUSED PLATFORM AIMING TO CHALLENGE DOMINANT NARRATIVES IN THE EXTRACTIVES INDUSTRY, AND FOR MORE THAN A DECADE A SANCTUARY FOR GRASSROOTS COMMUNITIES, CIVIL SOCIETY AND FAITH-BASED ORGANISATIONS — HELD OVER THREE DAYS IN FEBRUARY. February, annually, in the same city. Put it in the calendar and start looking for a sponsor in the second half of the year. WHO IT SUITS: African mining-affected communities and the organisations supporting them — as delegates, and as a model for counter-convening wherever an investment conference is held. CAVEATS: AN ANNUAL THREE-DAY GATHERING, NOT A SERVICE, A FUND OR A LEGAL BODY; ATTENDANCE USUALLY DEPENDS ON A LARGER ORGANISATION PAYING THE TRAVEL, AND THE DECLARATION HAS NO LEGAL FORCE — its value is access, contacts and visibility. For the movement that convenes there and its community-written charter, Niger's entry; for the law centre defending the right to organise, Malawi's entry.

trackers.name: LAMOSA (Land Access Movement of South Africa) — a federation formed by 48 dispossessed communities that litigated against the national parliament over a restitution law — with a fifth programme area devoted to making government deliver infrastructure to communities after they win their land back
trackers.desc: 48 COMMUNITIES FEDERATED — AND THEY TOOK PARLIAMENT TO COURT — method and adjacency declared first: THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THE SHIPPED HOST, TWO SIBLING HOSTS, AND FIVE SUBJECT SPELLINGS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; THE SHIPPED HOST AND THREE SPELLINGS ABSENT. THIS FILE'S SOUTH AFRICA AND BOTSWANA BUCKETS CARRY A LAW-REPORTS HOST AND ITS SOUTH AFRICA BUCKET A LAND CLAIMS COURT MENTION, NONE ABOUT THIS FEDERATION; ITS NIGER ENTRY THE COMMONAGE ACQUISITIONS AND THE POST-TRANSFER GAP, ITS MALAWI ENTRY THE MEMBERSHIP MOVEMENT. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. WHAT IT IS AND WHO OWNS IT, WHICH IS THE FIND: AN INDEPENDENT FEDERATION OF RURAL COMMUNITY BASED ORGANISATIONS ADVOCATING FOR LAND AND AGRARIAN RIGHTS — FORMED IN 1991 BY 48 DISPOSSESSED COMMUNITIES TO MOBILISE AND EMPOWER ITS AFFILIATES TO COLLECTIVELY FIGHT DISCRIMINATORY FORCED REMOVALS, RACIAL AND GENDER DISCRIMINATION. Forty-eight communities that had each lost land, federating rather than each pursuing its own claim. This file has recorded the sequencing of dispossession — one settlement at a time, each fighting alone — and this is the direct structural answer to it. THE COURT CASE IT BROUGHT AND WHAT WAS AT STAKE, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: A CONSTITUTIONAL COURT MATTER IN WHICH THE SPEAKER OF THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY WAS THE APPLICANT AND THIS FEDERATION THE RESPONDENT — CONCERNING WHETHER NEW RESTITUTION CLAIMS COULD BE PROCESSED ALONGSIDE OLD ONES, WITH THE COURT RECORDING THAT THE OLD CLAIMS WOULD NOT BE FINALISED FOR APPROXIMATELY 43 YEARS, AND THAT AN INTERDICT HAD BEEN PLACED ON THE NEWER CLAIMS. A federation of rural communities litigating against the national legislature, in the highest court, and the case is reported under their name. FORTY-THREE YEARS to finish the existing claims is the figure that matters: a restitution programme that slow is a refusal expressed as a queue, and it took a community federation to get that fact into a judgment. THE REMEDY ARGUED FOR: THAT THE COURT LIFT THE INTERDICT AND ALLOW THE COMMISSIONER TO PROCESS THE INTERDICTED CLAIMS CONCURRENTLY WITH THE OLD ONES, AND THAT IN THE EVENT OF A CONFLICT THE REGIONAL CLAIMS COMMISSIONER MUST REFER THAT CLAIM TO THE LAND CLAIMS COURT FOR A JUST AND EQUITABLE DECISION ON A CASE-BY-CASE BASIS. The remedy is procedural and precise — not compensation, but an order about the ORDER IN WHICH CLAIMS ARE HEARD. Where a community's claim is stuck behind an older queue, that is the shape of the application to make. WHO IT HAS EXPANDED TO INCLUDE: FROM THOSE WHO WERE DISPOSSESSED TO OTHER LANDLESS COMMUNITIES, INCLUDING FARMDWELLERS. FARMDWELLERS — people living on land owned by someone else, with no claim to lodge at all. Widening membership beyond claimants is what keeps a restitution federation relevant after the claim window closes. WHERE IT WORKS: IN PARTNERSHIP WITH GOVERNMENT AND CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS IN FOUR NAMED PROVINCES PLUS THE EASTERN PART OF A FIFTH BECAUSE OF CROSS-BORDERS. HOW IT DECIDES WHAT TO DO: IT TAKES A LEAD IN IMPLEMENTATION, HOWEVER THESE ARE DONE IN CONJUNCTION WITH ITS MEMBER COMMUNITIES — BUILDING REGIONAL AND PROVINCIAL STRUCTURES WITH THE AIM OF COLLECTIVE CAMPAIGNS THAT WOULD CULMINATE IN ONE BIG NATIONAL CAMPAIGN. Regional, then provincial, then national. The sequence is worth copying: the national campaign is assembled from structures that already exist, not announced first and populated afterwards. THE FIFTH RESULT AREA, WHICH IS THE ONE THIS FILE KEEPS FINDING MISSING: ADVOCACY AND LOBBYING USED FOR ENSURING THAT RESETTLED COMMUNITIES ARE PROVIDED WITH THE NECESSARY INFRASTRUCTURE AND BASIC SOCIAL SERVICES BY LOCAL GOVERNMENT AND OTHER GOVERNMENT DEPARTMENTS. A standing programme area for the thing that failed eleven of twelve communities in this file's Niger entry. The gap between winning land and being able to live on it is treated here as a permanent campaign, not an afterthought. WHAT ITS WOMEN'S GROUPS LOBBY FOR SPECIFICALLY: WOMEN'S LAND RIGHTS AND CO-OWNERSHIP OF FAMILY LAND AS WELL AS INHERITANCE RIGHTS. CO-OWNERSHIP OF FAMILY LAND is the precise ask — not land for women separately, but both names on the family holding. That is the change that survives a death, which is where this file records most individual land loss happening. THE HONEST ASSESSMENT IT PUBLISHES OF COMMUNITIES THAT WON: WE HAVE ALSO NOTED SOME SUCCESSES AND FAILURES OF COMMUNITIES WHO HAVE RECEIVED THEIR LAND BACK — THE COMMON CRY IS LACK OF GOVERNMENT SUPPORT OR CONFLICT WITHIN THE COMMUNITIES AND MANY OTHER PROBLEMS INCLUDING ACCOUNTS WHERE THERE ARE ROYALTIES. CONFLICT WITHIN THE COMMUNITIES, named by the federation itself alongside government failure. Royalty accounts are singled out: money arriving into a community body is the point at which a successful claim turns into a dispute, and planning for that before the first payment is the lesson. THE CONSTITUTIONAL POSITION IT TOOK IN A PUBLIC HEARING, IN A MEMBER'S OWN WORDS: THAT WE SHOULD NOT PLAY MARBLES WITH OUR CONSTITUTION — WHILE PROPOSING INDICATIVE TEXT FOR THE AMENDMENTS IT WISHED TO MOTIVATE FOR. INDICATIVE TEXT: they arrived at the hearing with drafted wording rather than objections. That is the difference between being consulted and being answered. THE STANDARD IT SIGNS UP TO THROUGH ITS COALITION: PREVENT AND REMEDY LAND GRABBING, RESPECTING TRADITIONAL LAND USE RIGHTS AND LOCAL LIVELIHOODS, AND ENSURING THAT ALL LARGE-SCALE INITIATIVES INVOLVING LAND, WATER AND OTHER NATURAL RESOURCES ARE BASED ON THE FREE, PRIOR AND INFORMED CONSENT OF EXISTING LAND USERS; A THOROUGH ASSESSMENT OF ECONOMIC, SOCIAL, CULTURAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS WITH RESPECT TO BOTH WOMEN AND MEN; DEMOCRATIC PLANNING AND INDEPENDENT OVERSIGHT; AND TRANSPARENT CONTRACTS THAT ARE SPECIFIC AND BINDING ON THE SHARING OF RESPONSIBILITIES AND BENEFITS. Four tests to apply to any project arriving on your land, in one sentence: consent of existing users, a full impact assessment covering women and men separately, independent oversight, and a contract that binds on benefit-sharing. Ask which of the four the project in front of you meets. AND THE REMEDY CLAUSE IN THAT SAME STANDARD: WHERE ADVERSE IMPACTS HAVE OCCURRED, CONCERNED ACTORS SHOULD PROVIDE FOR, AND COOPERATE IN, IMPARTIAL AND COMPETENT MECHANISMS TO PROVIDE REMEDY, INCLUDING THROUGH LAND RESTITUTION AND COMPENSATION — WITH THE FEDERATION'S NAMED COOPERATING BODIES INCLUDING TWO GOVERNMENT DEPARTMENTS, A GRASSROOTS WOMEN'S COMMISSION, A LAND COALITION, A TRADE UNION CONGRESS, A NATIONAL FARMERS UNION AND A CONGRESS OF TRADITIONAL LEADERS. Traditional leaders and trade unions in the same list of cooperating bodies. A land federation that can talk to both the chiefs and the unions has reach that neither has alone. WHO IT SUITS: rural communities with restitution or dispossession claims, farmdwellers without claims, and organisers looking for a federation model that litigates and campaigns on post-transfer support. CAVEATS: ONE COUNTRY AND FOUR PROVINCES, AND SOME PUBLISHED MATERIAL IS OLDER — CHECK CURRENT ACTIVITY BEFORE RELYING ON IT; IT FEDERATES, LOBBIES AND LITIGATES THROUGH COUNSEL RATHER THAN OPERATING A LAW CLINIC. For the commonage acquisitions and the post-transfer failure rate, Niger's entry; for the accredited free law clinic, Mauritania's entry.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a pan-African feminist rapid-response fund with reach across all 54 African countries — small grants released quickly for unanticipated, time-critical situations rather than planned programme work, covering safety and protection needs when defenders are threatened and short windows for advocacy after an unexpected event. WHO IT SUITS: women's rights organisations, feminist collectives and movements in which women or gender-diverse people are the primary decision-makers. It does NOT fund individuals, and the action must be strategic, genuinely unanticipated, and completable in under three months. HOW IT DIFFERS: this is emergency money for a moment, not a budget for a campaign — decisions are fast and grants are modest.

trackers.desc: Ethiopian Institution of the Ombudsman (EIO) — Ethiopia’s Ombudsman institution — oversees the Freedom of the Mass Media and Access to Information Proclamation, handling access complaints. — Holds to account: Ethiopia’s public bodies on disclosure — find access-to-information complaint handling, compliance monitoring and reports.

trackers.name: African Convention on Nature — check WHICH version binds your state
trackers.desc: THERE ARE TWO AFRICAN CONVENTIONS OF THIS NAME, AND CITING THE WRONG ONE IS THE AVOIDABLE ERROR HERE. The Algiers Convention was signed 15 September 1968, in force 16 June 1969. The revised Maputo Convention was adopted by the Assembly of the Union in Maputo on 11 July 2003 and entered into force 23 July 2016 — thirteen years later. THE OPERATIVE RULE: the 1968 Convention remains in force for those countries that have not ratified the 2003 revisions, so the two coexist and which binds your state depends on its ratification status. Commentary records only about 30 percent of African states had ratified Maputo. This entry does not assert which binds your state — the African Union publishes a Status List alongside the treaty text at au.int. Check it first. WHY THE DELAY IS AN ARGUMENT FOR IT: commentary attributes the thirteen years to the revised text containing strong provisions that could create accountability and also slow down social and economic development — a treaty resisted for creating accountability is one worth invoking where it applies. PROVISIONS TO KNOW: article XXXIX — no reservation may be made to this Convention, so a ratifying state takes all of it; article XL — withdrawal takes effect only one year after written notification; and no instrument of accession to the 1968 Algiers Convention may be deposited any longer, so the older text is closed to new entrants. THE OBJECTIVES ARE BROADER THAN USUAL: conservation, utilisation and development of soil, water, flora and fauna for present and future welfare, from an economic, nutritional, scientific, educational, cultural and aesthetic point of view — so a claim resting on cultural or aesthetic value has a treaty basis. BUT IF THE 1968 TEXT IS WHAT BINDS YOU, EXPECT LITTLE: parties were encouraged to cooperate but were not required to submit regular reports on implementation, and there were no financial mechanisms — no reporting trail, no funding attached. Article XLI also provides for interim secretariat arrangements, so check current institutional capacity. IUCN publishes a commentary on each provision in English and French.

trackers.name: EWNHS — Ethiopia's oldest conservation society, and the national door to a continental taskforce that has stopped damaging developments at 35 sites
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a membership-based Ethiopian conservation society founded in 1966, licensed with the civil society authority under registry number 0720 — the oldest non-governmental conservation organisation in the country, and the one with standing to be heard. It runs the Important Bird Areas programme, which is how a specific place in Ethiopia gets formally identified, surveyed and put on a national conservation inventory: an unlisted site is far harder to defend than a listed one, and getting your area recognised is something you can start before a project is announced. WHY THIS IS THE ENTRY FOR ETHIOPIA RATHER THAN A BIRDWATCHING CLUB: EWNHS is the national partner of an international conservation federation whose African Site Casework on Emerging Threats taskforce has, over fifteen years, safeguarded 35 major sites from damaging developments across the continent. That casework is reachable through the national partner, not directly — which makes EWNHS the door for an Ethiopian site facing a dam, plantation, road or industrial scheme. It also works with local communities on site management and monitoring under a regional flyway programme, and produces the survey data that an objection has to be built on. WHO IT SUITS: communities beside a wetland, lake, forest or flyway site facing a development, and anyone who needs their place formally recognised and surveyed. CAVEATS, AND THEY MATTER IN ETHIOPIA: this is a conservation society that describes its role as supporting government conservation efforts with advice, data and best practice — it is not a litigator, not an opponent of the state, and civil society operating space is tightly regulated under the civil society proclamation. The argument that moves it is biodiversity, not injustice: bring the species, the wetland, the flyway. No intake route, case-selection criteria or fee information was published, and membership carries an annual subscription.

trackers.name: Ethiopia's legal aid providers and the woreda Land Administration Committee — who to ask, and who actually issues the certificate
trackers.desc: WHERE TO GET HELP: three named providers of free legal assistance. The Ethiopian Women Lawyers Association (EWLA) runs a Legal Aid Program giving legal advice and counselling, writing court briefs and affidavits, AND REPRESENTING CLIENTS IN COURT, free of charge, and is credited with legal support to more than 100,000 women and with a central role in changing the Family Law; near Bulgaria Mikael Church, Mexico, Kirkos Subcity, Addis Ababa; +251 11 50 87 83. The Ethiopian Lawyers Association, a non-partisan professional body, provides legal aid to the economically and socially underprivileged. Bahir Dar University Legal Aid Center gives free counselling, prepares pleadings and represents people in court, with an emphasis on women, children, people with disabilities and prison inmates. WHO ISSUES THE PAPER, WHICH IS THE PART MOST PEOPLE GET WRONG: Ethiopian land administration is decentralised — the federal Rural Land Administration and Land Use Proclamation No. 456/2005 frames it, regional states legislate the detail, and the work runs down to woreda (district) and kebele (village) level. Regional councils must form district-level LAND ADMINISTRATION AND USE COMMITTEES (LACs), which oversee land administration, REGISTRATION and DISPUTE RESOLUTION, and are obliged to include elected women members. So the body that registers your holding and hears your boundary dispute is a committee in your own district — find out who sits on it before you need it. The Constitution recognises long-term unchallenged possession of state land and grants usufruct rights to collectives, peasant farmers, semi-pastoralists and pastoralists WITH NO TIME LIMIT. Women in Oromia and Tigray have described certification as giving proof of ownership, protection from boundary encroachment and the confidence to submit claims. WHO IT SUITS: Ethiopian smallholders, pastoralists and women needing certification, a boundary dispute heard, or free representation. CAVEATS: THESE ARE GENERAL LEGAL AID BODIES, NOT LAND OR ENVIRONMENTAL SPECIALISTS, and Ethiopian civic space for advocacy organisations has been constrained; certification programmes are donor-supported and uneven by region, and security conditions have halted work in some zones. For birdlife and site-level conservation casework, Ethiopia's EWNHS entry.

trackers.name: Guassa-Menz Community Conservation Area — the community stopped two commercial sheep ranches BEFORE it had legal status, then won designation in 2008
trackers.desc: HOW A COMMUNITY HELD ITS LAND AND STOPPED AN INVESTMENT: the Guassa area of Menz in the Amhara highlands — over 11,000 hectares of Afro-alpine moorland above 3,200m — was governed for OVER 400 YEARS under a communal system called QERO, in which ELECTED HEADMEN determined when and for how long people could harvest thatch grass and graze livestock, with closure periods enforced by the users themselves. After the 1974 revolution abolished communal tenure the system collapsed and the grassland degraded; from 2003 the initiative revived it, transferring control to a GUASSA CONSERVATION COUNCIL, mapping the area in workshops with local village associations, DRAWING UP BYLAWS governing use of its resources, and training COMMUNITY SCOUTS in local bylaw enforcement. Map it, write the bylaws, appoint your own scouts — that sequence is the reproducible part, and the community did it before any authority recognised them. THE STOPPED INVESTMENTS, WHICH ARE THE POINT: PRIOR TO DESIGNATION as a community conserved area, the initiative SUCCESSFULLY HALTED TWO ATTEMPTS to establish COMMERCIAL SHEEP-FARMING in the Guassa area — applications to the regional investment office proposing a 150-HECTARE ENCLOSURE as a commercial sheep ranch — OPPOSED ON THE BASIS THAT IT WOULD ESTABLISH A LEGAL PRECEDENT FOR PRIVATE LAND ENCLOSURES. That is the argument to borrow: do not fight the single enclosure on its own merits, fight it as the precedent that opens all the others. LEGAL RECOGNITION OF THE GUASSA COMMUNITY CONSERVED AREA FOLLOWED IN 2008. THE LEGAL FOOTING: under the Amhara Regional Rural Land Administration Proclamation No. 46/2000, COMMUNAL LANDS CAN BE MANAGED AND USED BY CUSTOMARY LAWS so long as they do not contradict the law — the provision under which the area continues to be managed by the residents of NINE FARMERS' ASSOCIATIONS. WHO IT SUITS: Ethiopian communities holding communal grazing, grassland or forest, particularly in Amhara and Oromia where joint community-forestry office management exists. CAVEATS: RECOGNITION IS REGIONAL AND CUSTOMARY-BASED, NOT A TITLE — it rests on a regional proclamation and continuing state acceptance; Ethiopia has very few gazetted conservation areas. For free legal advice and the woreda committees, Ethiopia's EWLA entry.

trackers.name: Ethiopia's ESIA regime after Proclamation 1317/2025 — the clearance certificate renews ANNUALLY, plans update every three years, audits every two, and a grievance gets a decision in 30 days
trackers.desc: HOW TO OBJECT BEFORE IT IS BUILT, AND THE DATES THAT LET YOU DO IT AGAIN: Ethiopia's ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT PROCLAMATION NO. 1317/2025 SUPERSEDED the 2002 EIA proclamation, BROADENING THE SCOPE TO EXPLICITLY INCLUDE SOCIAL, ECONOMIC AND CULTURAL CONSIDERATIONS. An ESIA CLEARANCE CERTIFICATE IS NOW A MANDATORY PRECONDITION for implementing specified projects, requiring PRIOR APPROVAL FROM THE ETHIOPIAN ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AUTHORITY OR THE RELEVANT REGIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL AGENCY. THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST TO A COMMUNITY, BECAUSE IT TURNS ONE CHANCE INTO MANY: the new law introduces CONTINUOUS COMPLIANCE OBLIGATIONS — MANDATORY ANNUAL RENEWAL OF THE CLEARANCE CERTIFICATE, TRIENNIAL UPDATES OF THE ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL MANAGEMENT PLAN, AND AUDITS AT LEAST ONCE EVERY TWO YEARS — and ONLY LICENSED PROFESSIONALS ACCREDITED BY THE AUTHORITY MAY CONDUCT ESIA STUDIES. A certificate that must be renewed every year is a project that must justify itself every year. If you missed the original consultation, the renewal, the three-year plan update and the two-year audit are all dated re-openings — mark them in a calendar and ask the authority for the audit report each time. And check that whoever wrote the study is on the accreditation list. THE RIGHT TO COMPLAIN, WITH A CLOCK ON IT: persons dissatisfied with the AUTHORISATION of a project MAY SUBMIT THEIR GRIEVANCES TO THE RELEVANT AUTHORITY AND ARE ENTITLED TO A DECISION WITHIN 30 DAYS of the grievance notice. A thirty-day deadline is a date you can hold them to — file in writing, keep the receipt, and count the days. AND THE WEAKNESSES, STATED PLAINLY SO NOBODY RELIES ON THIS ALONE: where the relevant authority sits inside the ministry that also promotes the sector, that is a CONFLICT OF INTEREST; THERE ARE NO SET STANDARDS OR GUIDELINES ON HOW GRIEVANCES ARE ADDRESSED, nor provisions making the process transparent; and reviewers record that PUBLIC PARTICIPATION IN ETHIOPIAN EIA PROCESSES IS MINIMAL. Most concerns raised by communities during Ethiopian ESIA processes have been about INADEQUATE COMPENSATION, PARTICULARLY LOSS OF LAND OR OTHER RESOURCES — so put the compensation question in writing at the assessment stage, where it is on the record, rather than at the objection stage. The companion instrument, ENVIRONMENTAL POLLUTION CONTROL PROCLAMATION NO. 300/2002, ENSURES THE RIGHT OF CITIZENS TO A HEALTHY ENVIRONMENT and defines pollution broadly as any condition hazardous to human health, safety or welfare or to living things. WHO IT SUITS: Ethiopian communities facing a mine, factory, dam or plantation, at any stage of its life. CAVEATS: A NEW LAW — confirm the implementing directives and which projects are specified. For the community conserved area that stopped two ranches, Ethiopia's Guassa-Menz entry.

trackers.name: MELCA-Ethiopia and the Ethiopian environmental organisations directory — an elders' forum that is winning recognition for sacred natural sites in Bale, plus a named list of the country's environmental bodies
trackers.desc: THE ELDERS' FORUM AND THE DIRECTORY: MELCA-ETHIOPIA — THE MOVEMENT FOR ECOLOGICAL LEARNING AND COMMUNITY ACTION (melca-ethiopia.org) works with local communities, traditional elders and government authorities in the HIGH ALPINE BALE MOUNTAINS, OROMIA REGIONAL STATE, SOUTH-EAST ETHIOPIA — and the record is explicit about the result: LONG-TERM WORK WITH LOCAL COMMUNITIES, TRADITIONAL ELDERS AND GOVERNMENT AUTHORITIES IS NOW RESULTING IN THE RECOGNITION AND PROTECTION OF A GROWING NUMBER OF SACRED NATURAL SITES. Communities, elders and government at the same table, sustained over years, is what produces recognition. Not a campaign against the authorities — the authorities in the room. That is the single method this file has now seen work for sacred sites in Ethiopia, Uganda, Benin and Côte d'Ivoire alike. WHAT MELCA ACTUALLY DID, AND IT IS COPYABLE: WITH ITS SUPPORT THE AREA'S ELDERS' FORUM HAS BEEN STRENGTHENED, CULTURAL HOUSES HAVE BEEN RE-BUILT, AND YOUTH HAVE BEEN RE-INTRODUCED TO ASPECTS OF THEIR CULTURE THAT HAD BEEN IMPERILLED, alongside work to REVIVE TRADITIONAL ECOLOGICAL KNOWLEDGE AND CUSTOMARY LAW AND GOVERNANCE SYSTEMS. Strengthen the forum, rebuild the house, bring the young people back. Those are three concrete, fundable tasks — and none of them is a fence. A custodian institution that has members, a building and a successor generation is the thing that actually holds ground; the legal recognition follows it rather than creating it. AND THE COMPARATIVE POINT THE RECORD MAKES ITSELF: IN BENIN, INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES AND CIVIL SOCIETY GROUPS SUCCESSFULLY LOBBIED FOR A NATIONAL LAW PROTECTING SACRED FORESTS IN 2012 — A LAW WHICH RECOGNISES SACRED FORESTS AS AREAS OF CULTURAL AND SPIRITUAL POTENCY AS WELL AS BIOLOGICAL DIVERSITY, AND EMPOWERS CUSTODIAN COMMUNITIES TO CONTINUE PLAYING THEIR LEADING ROLE IN MANAGING THEM. A national law that names custodian communities as the managers already exists in Africa. Cite it: when a ministry says there is no legal category for what you are asking, Benin's 2012 law is the answer that there is. THE DIRECTORY, WHICH IS THE REST OF WHO EXISTS IN ETHIOPIA: A PUBLISHED DIRECTORY OF ENVIRONMENTAL ORGANISATIONS AND ENVIRONMENTAL GOVERNMENT AGENCIES IN ETHIOPIA lists each with its web address — including the HORN OF AFRICA REGIONAL ENVIRONMENT CENTRE AND NETWORK (HoA-REC), the INSTITUTE FOR SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT (ISD), PASTORALIST FORUM ETHIOPIA (PFE), WILDLIFE FOR SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT (WSD), the ETHIOPIAN WOLF CONSERVATION PROGRAMME and others. Two of those are worth naming for a land case: PASTORALIST FORUM ETHIOPIA, because pastoral land is what most large Ethiopian projects take and pastoralists are the constituency with a national forum of their own; and HoA-REC, a REGIONAL centre and NETWORK, which means a cross-border issue has a body that already spans it. AND ON MEMBERSHIP, RECORDED PLAINLY: Ethiopia's oldest conservation society is MEMBERSHIP-BASED, with members receiving its publications, a QUARTERLY NEWSLETTER and an annual journal, for a published YEARLY SUBSCRIPTION FEE. A named annual subscription is the cheapest formal standing a person can buy in this file — join, and you are a member of the body that speaks on national conservation rather than a petitioner to it. WHO IT SUITS: Ethiopian communities with a sacred site, pastoralists, and anyone seeking the right organisation or a cross-border network. CAVEATS: A DIRECTORY AND SMALL NGOs — confirm current operations, and note Ethiopia's charities law governs what registered bodies may do. For the national conservation society and the site casework route, Ethiopia's EWNHS entry; for legal aid and the woreda Land Administration Committee, the legal aid providers entry; for the annual renewal and 30-day grievance window, the ESIA Proclamation 1317/2025 entry.

trackers.name: ECSOC — Ethiopia's statutory CSO council representing 3,600+ organisations with its own code of conduct and a federal-to-local complaints platform — plus Forum for Environment's 12 local groups and a published NGO directory
trackers.desc: RATHER THAN BEING IN ADDIS AND SHOUTING OUT TO THE COMMUNITIES — that is how a named Ethiopian environmental platform describes what it decided not to do, and it is the sharpest line on organising in this file's Ethiopian record: FORUM FOR ENVIRONMENT, ESTABLISHED IN 1997 AS A NON-GOVERNMENTAL, NON-PROFIT ENVIRONMENTAL COMMUNICATION AND ADVOCACY GROUP SERVING AS A PLATFORM FOR ADVOCACY AND COMMUNICATION AMONG PEOPLE AND INSTITUTIONS CONCERNED WITH THE ETHIOPIAN ENVIRONMENT, HAS HELPED TO ESTABLISH AND CONSOLIDATE 12 LOCAL GROUPS THROUGHOUT ETHIOPIA — ACTIVELY SUPPORTING LOCAL GROUPS THAT FOCUS ON LOCAL ISSUES AND HAVE A DEGREE OF AUTONOMY, TRANSLATING INTO A LOUDER VOICE IN THEIR COMMUNITIES. A degree of autonomy, deliberately given. A national body that builds twelve local groups and then lets them set their own agenda is a different offer from one that opens branch offices. If a capital-city organisation approaches your area, ask which of the two it is proposing — and ask whether one of those twelve groups is already near you. ITS FIVE THEMATIC AREAS ARE NAMED: FORESTS; PROTECTED AREAS; URBAN ENVIRONMENT; ENERGY; AND CLIMATE CHANGE — and its cross-cutting work includes AWARENESS RAISING THROUGH PUBLIC ENGAGEMENTS; RESEARCH AND PUBLICATIONS; MOBILIZING THE PUBLIC THROUGH ESTABLISHING AND STRENGTHENING LOCAL GROUPS; CAPACITY BUILDING; POLICY LEVEL DEBATES AND DISCUSSIONS; AND INCENTIVE AND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT SCHEMES. IT HOSTS THE ETHIOPIAN CIVIL SOCIETY NETWORK ON CLIMATE CHANGE, CONSISTING OF 60 MEMBER ORGANISATIONS, AND PUBLISHES AN ETHIOPIA ENVIRONMENT REVIEW. URBAN ENVIRONMENT is on that list beside forests and protected areas — useful, because most environmental organisations in this file will not take a city case. And a network of 60 organisations hosted inside it is a room your group can be introduced to through one door. THE STATUTORY UMBRELLA, AND IT IS UNUSUAL: THE ETHIOPIAN CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS COUNCIL WAS ESTABLISHED ON 31 DECEMBER 2020 UNDER ARTICLE 85 OF THE ORGANIZATIONS OF CIVIL SOCIETIES PROCLAMATION No. 1113/2019, AND CURRENTLY REPRESENTS OVER 3,600 CSOs INCLUDING CONSORTIUMS AND ASSOCIATIONS. ITS HIGHEST DECISION-MAKING ORGAN IS A 300-MEMBER GENERAL ASSEMBLY, WITH A 21-MEMBER EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE, AND IT GAINS ITS BUDGET FROM MEMBERS' CONTRIBUTIONS AND OTHER LEGAL MEANS. Three thousand six hundred organisations, a three-hundred-member assembly, and funded by member subscriptions rather than a donor. A body that lives on its members' money answers to its members — that is the first thing to check about any umbrella, and here the answer is printed. ITS THREE FUNCTIONS ARE THE REASON TO JOIN: ENACT THE CODE OF CONDUCT FOR THE SECTOR AND DEVISE ENFORCEMENT MECHANISMS; ADVISE THE AUTHORITY FOR CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS ON THE REGISTRATION AND ADMINISTRATION OF CSOs; AND REPRESENT AND COORDINATE THE CIVIL SOCIETY SECTOR. A code of conduct WITH enforcement mechanisms means a complaint about another organisation has somewhere to go — this file has flagged that gap in almost every country. And a council that advises the registering authority is the body to ask BEFORE you file registration papers, because it helps write the rules you will be judged by. THE PLATFORM THAT REACHES DOWN TO YOUR LEVEL: a NEW COORDINATION PLATFORM SPANS FEDERAL, REGIONAL, AND LOCAL LEVELS, MANAGED BY A CENTRAL COMMITTEE AND VARIOUS SUBCOMMITTEES, AND ENABLES CSOs TO RAISE CONCERNS AND COLLABORATIVELY DEVELOP SOLUTIONS. Federal, regional and local, with subcommittees. Ask which subcommittee covers environment or land, and who from your region sits on it — a coordination platform is only useful if you know the name of the person from your zone.
