AND THE COUNCIL'S OWN POSITION, STATED BY ITS EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR: IT REMAINS POLITICALLY NEUTRAL AND REPRESENTS NEITHER THE GOVERNMENT NOR ANY POLITICAL PARTY. Worth reading alongside the fact that it was created by statute and advises a government authority. Declared neutrality and statutory origin can both be true; judge it on your own issue, and note that a published draft CSO law has been criticised elsewhere as threatening hard-won gains on civic freedom — so the sector's own legal footing is contested. THE DIRECTORY: A PUBLISHED DIRECTORY OF ETHIOPIAN NGOs LISTS ORGANISATIONS ALPHABETICALLY WITH THEIR FULL NAMES AND ACRONYMS — INCLUDING AN ASSOCIATION FOR DEVELOPMENT AND BIODIVERSITY CONSERVATION, A REGIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION ASSOCIATION, A REGIONAL FORUM FOR ENVIRONMENT IN A NAMED TOWN, AN ENVIRONMENT AND DEVELOPMENT SOCIETY, A CONSORTIUM OF RELIEF AND DEVELOPMENT ASSOCIATIONS, A POPULATION HEALTH AND ENVIRONMENT CONSORTIUM, A POVERTY ACTION NETWORK, AND A REGIONAL RELIEF SOCIETY — each with a profile page and estimated beneficiary numbers. A regional Forum for Environment in a named town, and a regional environmental protection association, both listed. Ethiopia's environmental civil society is not only in Addis, and the directory is how you find the one in your region. WHO IT SUITS: Ethiopian community groups seeking a local partner, organisations registering or complaining about another body, and anyone with an urban environmental case. CAVEATS: THE CSO LEGAL FRAMEWORK IS UNDER REVISION and the umbrella is statutory rather than independent — judge it on your issue. For elders' forums strengthened and cultural houses rebuilt in the Bale Mountains, Ethiopia's MELCA entry; for the rural land registration and certification programme, the land certification entry; for free legal aid, the legal aid entries under Ethiopia.

trackers.name: AMARC (World Association of Community Radio Broadcasters) — the association of 4,000+ community radio stations with an African section — its published membership categories, the licensing principles to argue a regulator down with, an alert network for threatened broadcasters, and a free guide listing its African members
trackers.desc: THE STATION IS THE ONE PIECE OF INFRASTRUCTURE A VILLAGE CAN OWN — declared adjacency first: THIS FILE ALREADY NAMES FOUR AFRICAN STATIONS OR RADIO PROJECTS, UNDER UGANDA, SOUTH SUDAN AND ZAMBIA. NONE DESCRIBES THE ASSOCIATION, THE MEMBERSHIP ROUTE, THE LICENSING ARGUMENT OR THE MEMBERS LIST — WHICH IS WHAT THIS ENTRY IS FOR. THE SIZE AND THE AFRICAN SECTION: A NETWORK OF MORE THAN 4,000 COMMUNITY RADIOS, FEDERATIONS AND COMMUNITY MEDIA STAKEHOLDERS IN MORE THAN 115 COUNTRIES, FOUNDED IN 1983 — WITH AN AFRICAN REGIONAL SECTION GROUPING TOGETHER RADIOS FROM ALL THE CONTINENT, AND A REGIONAL OFFICE ESTABLISHED WITH A PARTNER CENTRE FOR THE STUDY OF RURAL RADIO IN A NAMED WEST AFRICAN CAPITAL. WHY THIS IS A LAND RESOURCE: a community that owns a transmitter can call a meeting, correct a rumour, announce a hearing date and reach the people who cannot read the notice — in the language they actually speak. This file has recorded consultations held in the wrong language, at the wrong hour, in the wrong town. A station fixes all three, and unlike a lawyer it keeps working after the case ends. THE MEMBERSHIP CATEGORIES, PUBLISHED: REGULAR MEMBERS ARE COMMUNITY RADIO STATIONS, PRODUCTION GROUPS, FEDERATIONS AND ASSOCIATIONS OF COMMUNITY RADIO STATIONS, AND THEIR REPRESENTATIVES HAVE THE RIGHT TO SPEAK AND VOTE AT ALL MEETINGS OF THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY. PRODUCTION GROUPS are members too — so a community that makes programmes for somebody else's station, without a licence of its own, is already eligible. That is the cheapest way in, and it is how most stations start. THE DEFINITION THAT DECIDES WHETHER YOU QUALIFY: COMMUNITY REFERS TO A COLLECTIVE OR A GROUP OF PEOPLE SHARING COMMON CHARACTERS AND/OR INTERESTS — WHICH CAN BE SOCIAL, SECTORAL, SECULAR, POLITICAL, ECONOMIC OR CULTURAL. HOWEVER, SOME COUNTRIES' LEGISLATION RESTRICTS THE RANGE OF COMMUNITIES ELIGIBLE FOR COMMUNITY RADIO LICENCES, AND THE MOST COMMON CASE OF EXCLUSION IS THAT OF ORGANISED POLITICAL PARTIES. A community of interest counts, not only a community of place. So a fishers' association or a pastoralist federation spread across several districts can hold a licence as one community — and the usual exclusion is political parties, not campaigning groups. Check your own broadcasting act for that distinction before anyone tells you a land committee is too political to broadcast. THE LICENSING PRINCIPLES, WHICH ARE THE ARGUMENT TO TAKE TO A REGULATOR: LICENSING SHOULD BE DESIGNED TO SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE STATION AND SHOULD NOT RESTRICT IT IN ANY WAY; THE ENTIRE PROCESS SHOULD BE CLEAR OF GOVERNMENT INTERFERENCE; PROCEDURES SHOULD BE FAIR AND APPARENT AND SET OUT IN LAW, AND THE RESPONSIBILITY OF AN INDEPENDENT LICENSING BODY; THERE SHOULD BE NO UNNECESSARY OBSTACLES THAT WOULD EXCLUDE COMMUNITIES FROM HAVING A RADIO BROADCASTER, AND NO UNREASONABLE TECHNICAL, ECONOMIC OR OTHER BARRIERS TO GAIN ENTRY; AND CRITERIA SHOULD BE PRIMARILY BASED ON DEMONSTRATING SOCIAL PURPOSE AND BENEFIT AND SUFFICIENT REQUIREMENTS FOR COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION IN OWNERSHIP AND FUNCTION. NO UNREASONABLE TECHNICAL OR ECONOMIC BARRIERS. Licence fees and equipment standards set for commercial broadcasters are the usual way a community application dies, and there is an international principle against exactly that to cite in the objection. THE FUNDING ASK IT PUTS TO GOVERNMENTS: COMMUNITY STATIONS SHOULD BE ALLOCATED SUITABLE FREQUENCIES, EQUITABLE ACCESS TO LICENCES, AND PUBLIC FINANCIAL AND TECHNOLOGICAL SUPPORT AND TRAINING — AND GOVERNMENTS SHOULD REINVEST THEIR REVENUES FROM THE SALE OF SPECTRUM, CABLE AND TELECOMMUNICATIONS LICENCES INTO SOCIAL COMMUNICATION OBJECTIVES, AND PROVIDE TAX INCENTIVES, PRODUCTION FUNDS AND LEGISLATIVE SUPPORT. IT NOTES THAT STATE SUBSIDIES FOR COMMUNITY MEDIA ARE THE NORM IN EUROPE AND NORTH AMERICA BUT LARGELY LACKING IN AFRICA. Your government sells spectrum for large sums. The argument that a fraction should return to community broadcasting is already made and already normal elsewhere — which turns a request for a favour into a comparison your ministry has to answer. THE PROTECTION: A SOLIDARITY ACTION NETWORK OF COMMUNITY BROADCASTERS WHOSE MAIN PURPOSE IS TO MOBILIZE THE WORLDWIDE COMMUNITY RADIO MOVEMENT IN SOLIDARITY WITH BROADCASTERS WHOSE RIGHT TO FREEDOM OF SPEECH IS THREATENED — DISTRIBUTING ACTION ALERTS, AND HAVING ACTED IN SOLIDARITY WITH STATIONS IN NAMED COUNTRIES. When a station is shut or a presenter arrested, four thousand stations can be told the same day. This file records land campaigns silenced by closing the one outlet that covered them; membership is what makes that closure expensive. WHAT THE AFRICAN ARM PROVIDES: A REGIONAL NETWORK TO DISTRIBUTE INFORMATION, SHARE EXPERIENCES AND TRANSFER SKILLS — GIVING MEMBERS ACCESS TO NEW TECHNOLOGY, HUMAN RESOURCES AND TRAINING PROGRAMMES ON BROADCASTING, GENDER ISSUES, NEW TECHNOLOGIES AND COMMUNICATION — AND SUPPORTING THE LEGAL, POLITICAL AND CULTURAL FRAMEWORK IN WHICH BOTH MEN AND WOMEN ARE ABLE AND ENCOURAGED TO PARTICIPATE. THE INDIGENOUS DECLARATION, WHICH IS DIRECTLY ON THIS FILE'S GROUND: MEMBERS COMMITTED TO PROMOTING OPPORTUNITIES FOR INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES TO ACCESS COMMUNITY BROADCASTING, DECLARING THAT RESEARCH AND DOCUMENTATION OF TRADITIONAL KNOWLEDGE IS IMPORTANT TO PRESERVING AND CONSERVING INDIGENOUS TRADITIONS, LANGUAGES, CULTURES AND THE MANAGEMENT OF NATURAL RESOURCES. Broadcasting treated as a way of conserving natural resource management knowledge, not just of spreading news. Recording elders on air preserves the boundary knowledge and shares it in one act — and the recordings become the archive this file's oral-history mapping entry can place on a map. AND THE FREE GUIDE: A PUBLISHED RESOURCE GUIDE, WHAT IS COMMUNITY RADIO, WHOSE SIXTH APPENDIX LISTS THE ASSOCIATION'S MEMBERS IN AFRICA. A published list of African community stations. Before founding one, find the nearest — they will take your programme, lend equipment, or tell you how their licence was obtained. WHO IT SUITS: African communities wanting their own station or airtime, and existing stations seeking training, protection or a network. CAVEATS: LICENSING IS NATIONAL AND VARIES SHARPLY — the principles above are advocacy positions, not law in your country. For a station already running alongside a sustainability school, Uganda's Community Green Radio entry; for lawyers and journalists working together on land evictions, Uganda's Witness Radio entry; for legal defence when a broadcaster is sued, South Sudan's media defence entry.

trackers.name: Senior and retired lawyers from the firms that draft the other side's contracts, working free on an attorney-client basis where you direct the strategy — with on-site placements of one to five months and natural resource contract renegotiation among their named specialisms
trackers.desc: RETIRED PARTNERS FROM THE FIRMS THAT WROTE THE OTHER SIDE'S CONTRACTS — note recorded first: THE SWEEP RETURNED A FALSE POSITIVE ON A SIMILARLY-NAMED LEGAL BROKERAGE, WHOSE STRING MATCHED INSIDE MADAGASCAR'S LAND TRUST HOST. HOST-LEVEL COMPARISON CONFIRMED NO COLLISION. THAT BROKERAGE IS ALREADY A NAMED ENTRY UNDER THE CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC AND IS NOT RESTATED HERE. WHO THE LAWYERS ARE, AND IT IS THE FIND: AN INTERNATIONAL VOLUNTEER NETWORK OF SENIOR-LEVEL AND RETIRED ATTORNEYS WITH A DEEP UNDERSTANDING OF THE LEGAL FRAMEWORKS THAT SHAPE ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, RECOGNIZED EXPERTS IN THEIR FIELDS — DRAWN LARGELY FROM LEADING LAW FIRMS AND INDEPENDENT SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTS. Not junior associates donating an afternoon. These are the people who spent careers drafting concession agreements, tax structures and investment treaties for the other side of the table — and who now have time. This file has recorded communities and ministries negotiating against firms whose partners have done a hundred such deals; this is the only entry that puts an equivalent on your bench. THE CONTROL CLAUSE, AND IT IS THE SECOND FIND: THEY ADVISE CLIENTS WITHIN CAREFULLY SELECTED AND STRUCTURED PROJECTS, ON AN ATTORNEY-CLIENT BASIS IN WHICH THE CLIENT IS IN CHARGE — VOLUNTEER LEGAL EXPERTS PROVIDE ADVICE AND GUIDANCE, WHILE CLIENTS DIRECT DEVELOPMENT DECISIONS AND OUTCOMES. ATTORNEY-CLIENT, stated as the model. That is a legal relationship with confidentiality and duty attached, not a partnership or a project — and it means the advice is yours, privileged, and does not go into somebody's report. Ask any organisation offering free legal help whether the relationship is attorney-client; the answer decides what you can safely tell them. WHO THE CLIENTS ARE: LOW-INCOME GOVERNMENTS, CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS AND SOCIAL ENTERPRISES IN THE GLOBAL SOUTH — AND THEY ALSO PARTNER WITH SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTS FROM ACADEMIC INSTITUTIONS AND LEADING LOCAL COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS AND NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS. Governments and civil society, on the same list. A national land commission or a ministry that is being out-lawyered by an investor is as eligible as an NGO — which matters, because this file has recorded that a weak ministry signing a bad contract does as much damage as a hostile one. WHERE THE WORK IS: MOST OF THEIR WORK IS CURRENTLY IN AFRICA, LATIN AMERICA AND ASIA, WITH CURRENT ACTIVE MATTERS IN SUB-SAHARAN AFRICA AND NORTH AFRICA — AND THEY ARE FURTHER EXPANDING THEIR FOOTPRINT IN EAST AFRICA. THE FOCUS AREAS: ACCOUNTABILITY AND TRANSPARENCY, COMMUNITY-INCLUSIVE DEVELOPMENT, INNOVATIVE FINANCE AND SOCIAL ENTERPRISES, INVESTMENT AND TRADE, MEDIA LAW AND FREEDOM OF EXPRESSION, NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, RESPONSIBLE TECHNOLOGY, AND TAX. COMMUNITY-INCLUSIVE DEVELOPMENT and NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT as standing programmes, and TAX beside them. A concession's tax terms decide whether a country sees any money at all from the land it gave away — and almost nobody on the community side can read them. THE FORMS THE HELP TAKES: TRANSACTIONAL AND NEGOTIATION SUPPORT, TRAINING WORKSHOPS, RESEARCH AND PUBLICATIONS, LEGISLATIVE DRAFTING SUPPORT, AND STRATEGIC LEGAL ADVICE — WITH THE CORE TEAM PROVIDING HANDS-ON PROJECT MANAGEMENT FROM SCOPING TO COMPLETION. LEGISLATIVE DRAFTING SUPPORT is the one to notice. If your country's land or mining law is the problem, they will help write the replacement — which this file's Ethiopian environment tribunal case shows is achievable. THE ON-SITE PLACEMENTS, WHICH ALMOST NOTHING ELSE IN THIS FILE OFFERS: LONG TERM ON-SITE ASSIGNMENTS OF 1-5 MONTHS TO MENTOR, ASSIST AND BUILD ORGANIZATIONAL CAPACITY; SHORT TERM OVERSEAS TRAININGS AND WORKSHOPS; EXPERT COUNSEL FROM THEIR DESKS ON CORPORATE TRANSACTIONAL, LITIGATION AND LEGISLATIVE MATTERS; AND CROSS-BORDER RESEARCH AND ANALYSIS ON HUMAN RIGHTS AND OTHER ISSUES. A senior lawyer sitting in your office for up to five months. Remote advice arrives too late and misses the context; somebody present through a negotiation season is a different order of help — and it is a specific thing to request by name. THE LANGUAGES AND EXPERTISE THEY RECRUIT FOR, WHICH TELLS YOU WHAT THEY CAN COVER: VOLUNTEER LAWYERS FROM ALL COUNTRIES AND LEGAL SYSTEMS — FRENCH AND SPANISH SKILLS ESPECIALLY HELPFUL FOR WORK IN COUNTRIES LIKE MALI, ENGLISH PREDOMINANT IN MOST AFRICAN PROJECTS — WITH EXPERIENCE IN CRIMINAL LAW, LITIGATION, HUMAN RIGHTS LAW, COMMERCIAL LAW, NATURAL RESOURCE LAW, ENVIRONMENTAL LAW AND MEDIA LAW ESPECIALLY WELCOMED. THE CONTRACT WORK ON RECORD: A WELL-ESTABLISHED PROGRAM OF ADVICE TO GOVERNMENTS ACROSS SUB-SAHARAN AFRICA, INCLUDING ADVISING ON THE RENEGOTIATION OF NATURAL RESOURCE CONTRACTS AND THE ESTABLISHMENT OF LEGAL AND REGULATORY FRAMEWORKS FOR INVESTMENT, TAX AND TRADE — AND COORDINATING LEGAL ASSISTANCE TO A NATIONAL GOVERNMENT NEGOTIATING A NEW CONCESSION CONTRACT FOR A COPPER MINE. RENEGOTIATION. A signed contract is not necessarily final — and there are lawyers who do this for free, which is worth knowing when your government says the deal cannot be reopened. THE AFRICAN MINING TOOLKIT: IT ASSISTED A DEVELOPMENT BANK AND AN AFRICAN LEGAL SUPPORT FACILITY IN DEVELOPING A TOOLKIT, APPEARING ALONGSIDE THAT FACILITY, AN AFRICAN DEVELOPMENT BANK, A TAX JUSTICE NETWORK AND A NATIONAL REVENUE AUTHORITY AT AN AFRICAN MINING CONFERENCE AND ITS ALTERNATIVE COUNTERPART, FOR THE SOFT LAUNCH OF A MINERAL TAXATION TOOLKIT ATTACHED TO AN AFRICAN MINING LEGISLATION ATLAS. An AFRICAN LEGAL SUPPORT FACILITY and an AFRICAN MINING LEGISLATION ATLAS both exist and are named here — two continental resources worth finding on their own, and both attached to the bank whose review mechanism this file records under Nigeria. THE SELECTION TEST: THEY SEEK TO ENGAGE WHERE THERE IS A GENUINE NEED FOR PRO BONO LEGAL ASSISTANCE AND THE OPPORTUNITY TO MAKE A CONTRIBUTION TO GLOBAL DEVELOPMENT AND THE RULE OF LAW. AND THE CLIMATE FINANCE CASE: IT SUPPORTED A NATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL FUND IN ACHIEVING A LANDMARK CLIMATE FINANCE DEAL UNDER WHICH MULTINATIONAL CORPORATE BUYERS PURCHASED HIGH-INTEGRITY CREDITS. A national environmental fund of the kind filed under Sudan, lawyered properly before signing with corporate buyers. That is the difference between a carbon deal a community benefits from and one it discovers afterwards. WHO IT SUITS: African civil society organisations, community bodies and government agencies facing a concession, contract or law they are being out-lawyered on. CAVEATS: PROJECTS ARE CAREFULLY SELECTED AND SCOPED, AND MUCH OF THE WORK IS WITH GOVERNMENTS AND ESTABLISHED ORGANISATIONS — a village committee will need a national partner. For the brokerage where lawyers have two weeks to volunteer, the Central African Republic's entry; for the finite-project pro bono broker and free legal health check, Eritrea's entry; for the continental lawyers' union, Algeria's entry.

trackers.name: Synchronicity Earth — a conservation funder with no pass-or-fail assessment, simple forms in multiple languages, due diligence done largely by conversation — and core flexible funding to around 80% of its partners, who decide how it is spent
trackers.desc: WE DO NOT HAVE A PASS OR FAIL SYSTEM — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S DR CONGO ENTRY COVERS THE CONGO BASIN ORGANISATIONAL-SUPPORT BODY NAMED IN THIS FUNDER'S OWN MATERIAL, ITS CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC ENTRY THE FUND THAT WAIVES REGISTRATION, ITS SOUTH SUDAN ENTRY THE PRODUCER GRANTS WITH THE 67%-AGAINST-2% COMPARISON, AND ITS SOUTH AFRICA ENTRY A NAMED GRASSROOTS GRANTMAKER. THE AFRICAN ORGANISATIONAL-SUPPORT BODY THAT CO-AUTHORED THE FUNDING STUDY CITED BELOW ALREADY HAS ITS OWN ENTRY UNDER TANZANIA. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE NO-FAIL RULE, WHICH IS THE FIND: IN IDENTIFYING PARTNERS TO WORK WITH, WE DO NOT HAVE A PASS OR FAIL SYSTEM, AND WE UNDERSTAND THAT NO ORGANISATION OR INDIVIDUAL WILL HAVE EVERYTHING RUNNING PERFECTLY AT ALL TIMES — ALSO RECOGNISING THAT THERE ARE DIVERSE APPROACHES TO CONSERVATION, TO RUNNING A SUCCESSFUL PROGRAMME OR ORGANISATION, AND TO UNDERSTANDING IMPACT. An organisation with imperfect books, no audit history and an unusual way of working is not disqualified at the first screen. This file has recorded that gate closing on community organisations again and again — here it is explicitly not applied, and the phrase is worth quoting back to any funder that does apply it. THE DUE DILIGENCE DESIGN: THE PROCESS IS DESIGNED TO REDUCE THE BURDEN ON PARTNERS BY LIMITING EXCESSIVE PAPERWORK AND DOCUMENTATION — MUCH CAN BE DONE THROUGH CONVERSATIONS, WHICH FLAG POTENTIAL RISKS RATHER THAN RULE PARTNERS IN OR OUT. SIMPLE APPLICATION FORMS IN MULTIPLE LANGUAGES HELP PARTNERS TO DEVELOP PROPOSALS. Conversations instead of documents, and forms in more than one language. For a committee whose records are handwritten and whose working language is not English, that is the difference between eligible and excluded — and RISKS FLAGGED RATHER THAN USED TO EXCLUDE is the standard to ask for elsewhere. THE FUNDING TYPE, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: AROUND 80% OF PARTNERS RECEIVE CORE AND FLEXIBLE FUNDING, ALLOWING THEM TO DEFINE HOW GRANTS ARE BEST SPENT — WITH CORE FUNDING AND SUPPORT FOR ORGANISATIONAL DEVELOPMENT OFTEN PROVIDED, AS WELL AS FUNDING FOR START-UP INITIATIVES ADDRESSING KEY GAPS. CORE FUNDING, to four partners in five. That is the salary, the rent, the accountant and the vehicle — precisely what this file's DR Congo entry identifies as the thing no funder pays for, and what collapses community organisations between project grants. START-UP funding is the other rarity: money for something that does not exist yet. WHO IT FUNDS: SMALL, LOCALLY LED ORGANISATIONS ACTING WITH AND FOR THE COMMUNITIES THEY ARE PART OF, INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND INDIGENOUS-LED FUNDS, AND LARGER NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL NGOs WORKING ON POLICY AND ADVOCACY — INCLUDING INDIVIDUALS. INDIGENOUS-LED FUNDS as recipients, and INDIVIDUALS. Money to a fund that indigenous people themselves control is one step further than money to an indigenous organisation, and this file's Chad entry describes what such a fund then does with it. THE RELATIONSHIP MODEL: IT CONSIDERS EVERY ORGANISATION AND INDIVIDUAL IT FUNDS A PARTNER, AIMS TO BUILD LONG-TERM, TWO-WAY, TRUSTING RELATIONSHIPS, AND FOCUSES ON BUILDING PARTNERSHIPS RATHER THAN FUNDING ONE-OFF PROJECTS — WITH LONG-TERM SUPPORT TO A NAMED DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO ORGANISATION GIVEN AS AN EXAMPLE. THE SCALE AND SCOPE: SINCE 2009 IT HAS DISTRIBUTED OVER £27 MILLION TO MORE THAN 180 ORGANISATIONS PROTECTING FOREST, FRESHWATER AND OCEAN BIODIVERSITY IN SUB-SAHARAN AFRICA, SOUTHEAST ASIA, LATIN AMERICA AND MELANESIA — FOCUSING ON REGIONS, SPECIES AND ECOSYSTEMS THAT ARE OVERLOOKED AND UNDERFUNDED. OVERLOOKED AND UNDERFUNDED as the selection criterion. A species or ecosystem nobody has heard of is an advantage here rather than a weakness, which inverts the usual competition against famous landscapes. THE MEASURED RESULTS OVER TEN YEARS: APPROXIMATELY 600,000 MARGINALISED OR UNDER-REPRESENTED PEOPLE SUPPORTED, 690 MILLION HECTARES OF TERRESTRIAL, OCEAN AND FRESHWATER HABITATS PROTECTED, 170 KEY BIODIVERSITY AREAS IDENTIFIED OR LISTED, AND 1,200 SPECIES MONITORED AND RESEARCHED. THE AFRICAN FUNDING FIGURES IT PUBLISHES, WHICH ARE THE ARGUMENT TO CARRY: GLOBALLY, LESS THAN ONE PER CENT OF ALL CLIMATE FUNDING REACHES INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND LOCAL COMMUNITY ORGANISATIONS; ONLY 6.7 PER CENT OF UK FOUNDATIONS' ENVIRONMENTAL GIVING GOES TO AFRICA; AND EVEN AMONG AFRICAN PHILANTHROPIC GIVING TO AFRICAN GRANTEES, ONLY NINE PER CENT OF LARGE-SCALE FUNDING WENT TO LOCAL ORGANISATIONS. Nine per cent, from African philanthropy to African grantees. The problem is not only foreign donors — and that figure is the one to put to a national foundation or a government fund, published by a funder about its own sector. THE STUDY BEHIND THOSE FIGURES: A REPORT PRODUCED WITH A NAMED AFRICAN ORGANISATIONAL-SUPPORT PARTNER, ASKING BOTH RECIPIENTS AND PROVIDERS HOW TO MAKE GRANT-GIVING IN AFRICA MORE EFFECTIVE — CALLING FOR INCREASING DIRECT FUNDING FOR AFRICAN CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, BUILDING TRUST SO RISK CAN BE SHARED, AND BUILDING GRANTEES' ABILITY TO FUNDRAISE AND TAP INTO OTHER SOURCES. ASKING RECIPIENTS as well as providers. An African organisation's account of why the money does not arrive is in a published report co-authored by a funder — which makes it usable in a proposal rather than only in a complaint. THE RECOMMENDATIONS IT MAKES TO OTHER FUNDERS: INVEST MORE IN RE-GRANTERS, POOLED FUNDS, OR FUNDER COLLECTIVES; AND INCLUDE THOSE WITH LOCAL EXPERIENCE IN DECISION-MAKING, FOR EXAMPLE BY UTILISING INDIGENOUS-LED FUNDS. RE-GRANTERS. A national or regional organisation that can receive a large grant and pass it on in small ones is the structure this whole file keeps needing — and here a funder is telling other funders to back exactly that, which is an argument a national body can use to propose becoming one. THE POOLED FUND AND WHAT ONE PARTNER GRANT COVERS: A CONGO BASIN POOLED FUND, WITH A NAMED PHILANTHROPY'S NON-PROGRAMMATIC GRANT WITHIN IT FOCUSED ON INSTITUTIONAL STRENGTHENING AND CAPACITY BUILDING FOR LOCAL ORGANISATIONS — BUILDING ON EXPERTISE IN IDENTIFYING IMPACTFUL COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS, PROVIDING TAILORED CAPACITY-BUILDING SUPPORT, AND CONNECTING ORGANISATIONS WITH DONORS. A NON-PROGRAMMATIC GRANT — money not tied to delivering a project. Congo Basin organisations should know that line exists inside the pooled fund. AND THE CONNECTING ROLE IT NAMES: DEVELOPING STRONG, RESPECTFUL, LONG-TERM RELATIONSHIPS WITH LOCAL PARTNERS AND, WHERE RELEVANT AND APPROPRIATE, HELPING TO CONNECT THEM INTO GLOBAL NETWORKS AND INITIATIVES. WHO IT SUITS: small locally led African conservation organisations — including young or imperfect ones — working on overlooked forest, freshwater or ocean biodiversity. CAVEATS: IT IDENTIFIES PARTNERS RATHER THAN RUNNING OPEN CALLS, SO THE ROUTE IN IS USUALLY A RECOMMENDATION FROM AN EXISTING PARTNER OR ADVISER — and it funds conservation, not litigation or land purchase. For core organisational support in the Congo Basin, DR Congo's entry; for the fund that waives registration, bank account and ID, the Central African Republic's entry; for grants paid straight to producer organisations, South Sudan's entry.

trackers.name: The Early Warning System (International Accountability Project) — a daily-updated database of 27,000+ development-bank projects built so communities learn about them before the financing is approved — search access granted to community organisers and refused to the banks and investors who ask for it
trackers.desc: COMMUNITIES CAN SEARCH IT. BANKS AND INVESTORS ARE TURNED DOWN — adjacency declared first: THIS SYSTEM IS CO-PUBLISHED ON A COALITION HOST ALREADY PRESENT UNDER NIGERIA AND UGANDA; THAT COALITION'S ENTRIES ARE NOT RESTATED AND ITS HOST IS NOT SHIPPED. THIS FILE'S GUINEA ENTRY CARRIES A BANK INFORMATION HOST, ITS BENIN ENTRY AN INCLUSIVE DEVELOPMENT HOST, ITS BURUNDI ENTRY AN ACCOUNTABILITY COUNSEL HOST, AND ITS DR CONGO ENTRY THE ENVIRONMENTAL LAW ORGANISATION THAT CO-LAUNCHED THIS TOOL. NONE IS RESTATED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. THE TIMING, WHICH IS THE FIND: IT ENSURES LOCAL COMMUNITIES, AND THE ORGANIZATIONS THAT SUPPORT THEM, HAVE VERIFIED INFORMATION ABOUT PROPOSED BANK-FUNDED PROJECTS LIKELY TO CAUSE HUMAN AND ENVIRONMENTAL RIGHTS ABUSES, AND PROVIDES CLEAR STRATEGIES FOR ADVOCACY BEFORE THE PROJECT FINANCING IS APPROVED BY THE BANK. Before the money is committed is the only moment a project is genuinely stoppable. Every legal and complaint route in this file operates after approval, when the bank, the government and the company all have money at stake; this one exists to move the fight upstream of that. A community that learns of a project when the machinery arrives has already lost the cheapest year of the campaign. WHO GETS ACCESS AND WHO IS REFUSED, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: ACCESS TO SEARCH THE DATABASE IS AVAILABLE UPON REQUEST FOR CIVIL SOCIETY GROUPS, COMMUNITY ORGANIZERS AND COMMUNITY REPRESENTATIVES — THE TEAM RECEIVES MANY REQUESTS FROM GOVERNMENTS, BANKS AND INVESTORS TO ACCESS THE DATABASE, AND CONTINUES TO FOCUS ON REINFORCING THE WORK OF CIVIL SOCIETY GROUPS, COMMUNITY ORGANIZERS AND COMMUNITY REPRESENTATIVES, DESCRIBED AS A CLEAR EFFORT TO REDISTRIBUTE AND RECENTRALIZE POWER. An information asymmetry deliberately reversed. Banks and governments are the ones being told no, and a community organiser can ask for search access by request — no registration, no institution named as a condition. This file has recorded almost nothing else where the community is on the inside of the gate. THE SIZE AND THE REFRESH RATE: THE FIRST CIVIL SOCIETY-LED DATABASE TO ORGANIZE, SUMMARIZE AND STANDARDIZE PROJECTS AT 15 DEVELOPMENT FINANCE INSTITUTIONS, UPDATED DAILY, HOLDING MORE THAN 27,000 INVESTMENTS VALUED AT USD 2.8 TRILLION PROPOSED SINCE JANUARY 2016 — AND THE ROLES OF MORE THAN 12,000 PRIVATE ACTORS. A LATER FIGURE PUTS IT ABOVE 30,000. UPDATED DAILY. Check it on a schedule for your district rather than once, because the entry you need may not exist yet — that is the whole point of an early warning. WHAT YOU CAN SEARCH BY: LOCATION, SECTOR, OR EVEN SPECIFIC RIGHTS THAT MAY BE THREATENED. Searching by location is the practical move: put in your region and see what is proposed for it that nobody has told you about. THE PRIVATE ACTOR CHAIN: TRACKING DEVELOPMENT ACTORS OPENS UP THE ENTIRE INVESTMENT CHAIN PROCESS, PROVIDING COMMUNITIES WITH ADDITIONAL LEVERAGE POINTS TO HOLD GOVERNMENTS, CORPORATIONS AND DEVELOPMENT ACTORS ACCOUNTABLE — INCLUDING THE ROLES OF ANY PRIVATE ACTORS. Twelve thousand private actors named against the projects they are in. The company operating on your land is usually a local subsidiary with nothing to lose; the chain shows who is behind it and which of them answers to a bank with a complaints office. WHAT THE TEAM ACTUALLY SPENDS ITS TIME ON: THE DATABASE ITSELF IS AN IMPORTANT RESOURCE, HOWEVER THE TEAM FOCUSES MOST OF ITS TIME ON COMMUNITY CAMPAIGN SUPPORT AND OUTREACH — GETTING THIS INFORMATION AND SUPPORT TO THOSE NEAREST THE PROPOSED PROJECT WHO NEED IT MOST. The tool is not the offer; the people are. Ask for campaign support, not only for a login. HOW THE SUMMARIES TRAVEL: ALL OF THE PROJECT SUMMARIES VERIFIED AND PUBLISHED ARE PUBLIC, AND THE TEAM AND OVER 600 CIVIL SOCIETY GROUPS AROUND THE WORLD DISTRIBUTE THESE PROJECT SUMMARIES TO THOSE NEAREST THE IMPACTS. The summaries themselves are public even where search access is granted by request — and 600 groups pass them on, so an African organisation that joins that distribution list becomes the one who warns its own region. THE METHODS OF COMMUNITY RESPONSE IT NAMES: ACCESSING DECISION-MAKERS, COMMUNITY-LED SURVEYS AND RESEARCH, UNDERSTANDING POSSIBLE LEVERAGE POINTS RELATED TO INVESTMENTS MADE BY PRIVATE ACTORS, FILING COMPLAINTS, AND DETERMINING LOCAL DEVELOPMENT PRIORITIES. COMMUNITY-LED SURVEYS sit in the same list as filing complaints. A community's own count of who lives there and what they use is treated as a response method, not as background — and it is the evidence that outlasts the consultation report. THE SEQUENCE IT DESCRIBES: PROJECTS ARE PROPOSED WITHOUT COMMUNITY INPUT; THE SYSTEM COLLECTS, SUMMARIZES AND VERIFIES; PARTNERS AND COMMUNITIES RECEIVE IT IDEALLY BEFORE FUNDING IS DECIDED; COMMUNITIES MAY ORGANIZE MEETINGS AND CONDUCT THEIR OWN RESEARCH; WORKSHOPS AND TRAININGS REINFORCE THEIR EFFORTS; COMMUNITIES DECIDE TO TAKE ACTION AND ADVANCE THEIR OWN PRIORITIES; AND THE TEAM AND PARTNERS CONTINUE SUPPORTING THE CAMPAIGN. THE FINDING IT PUBLISHES ABOUT CONSULTATION: LOCAL COMMUNITIES RARELY LEAD THIS PROCESS, EVEN THOUGH DEVELOPMENT PLANNERS ARE REQUIRED TO INFORM AND CONSULT WITH THE PEOPLE WHO MAY BE AFFECTED — AND EVIDENCE SUGGESTS THAT CONSULTATIONS ARE RARELY COMPLETED ON TIME OR DESIGNED IN AN INCLUSIVE MANNER. A published finding that consultations are routinely late and badly designed. That is a citable statement when contesting a consultation record, rather than one community's word against a signed attendance sheet. THE OTHER DATABASE IT CURATES: A COMPREHENSIVE DATABASE OF COMMUNITY COMPLAINTS FILED WITH INDEPENDENT ACCOUNTABILITY MECHANISMS ABOUT THE IMPACTS OF INTERNATIONALLY FINANCED PROJECTS. Search it for complaints already filed against the same bank or the same company. What worked, what was dismissed and on what ground is the cheapest preparation available before filing your own. AND THE GUIDES AND WORK AREAS: INTERACTIVE COMMUNITY ACTION GUIDES IN ENGLISH, PORTUGUESE, SPANISH, THAI AND VIETNAMESE — WITH WORK DIVIDED INTO CLIMATE JUSTICE, COMMUNITY CAMPAIGN SUPPORT, CORPORATE ACCOUNTABILITY, THE EARLY WARNING SYSTEM, AND POLICY AND ADVOCACY, AND THE STATED RECOGNITION THAT COMMUNITIES MAY HAVE THEIR OWN DEVELOPMENT PRIORITIES OR NOT WANT ANY DEVELOPMENT AT ALL. OR NOT WANT ANY DEVELOPMENT AT ALL, written into how the organisation describes its own work. That is the position most funders and agencies in this file cannot say out loud. Recorded honestly: the action guides are not published in French or Arabic, which limits them across much of the continent even though the database itself is searchable by anyone granted access. WHO IT SUITS: African community organisations and organisers who want to know what is being planned for their area before it is approved, and who is financing it. CAVEATS: DEVELOPMENT-BANK FINANCE ONLY — A PRIVATELY FUNDED PROJECT MAY NOT APPEAR — SEARCH ACCESS IS BY REQUEST, AND THE ACTION GUIDES HAVE NO FRENCH OR ARABIC EDITION. For complaint mechanisms and who files them for you, this file's Cape Verde and Djibouti entries; for the environmental law organisation that co-launched this tool, DR Congo's entry.

trackers.name: Land Rights Now — an open land rights campaign any community can join and act under without registering — with published policy recommendations to put to your own government, dated global weeks of action, and a standing mobilisation against the criminalisation of land defenders
trackers.desc: AN UNREGISTERED COMMUNITY CAN JOIN AND ACT UNDER THE BANNER — adjacency declared first: THE THREE CONVENING ORGANISATIONS ARE ALREADY IN THIS FILE — A LAND COALITION HOST UNDER LIBERIA AND ZIMBABWE AND A NAME UNDER CAMEROON AND SENEGAL, A RIGHTS AND RESOURCES HOST UNDER GHANA, AND AN AID CONFEDERATION NAMED IN THREE DESCRIPTIONS. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS RUN ON THE HOST ACTUALLY BEING SHIPPED. WHO CAN JOIN, WHICH IS THE FIND: THE CAMPAIGN IS OPEN — ANYONE, ACTIVE CITIZENS OR COMMUNITIES OR ORGANIZATIONS, WHO ENDORSES THE GOAL CAN JOIN AND ACT UNDER THE BANNER. No registration, no membership committee, no application. A village committee can act under an international banner from the day it decides to — which changes how a local dispute is reported and how a government reads it, at no cost. This file has recorded registration as the gate on nearly every fund and network in it; here there is none. THE POLICY RECOMMENDATIONS IT HANDS YOU, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: THE CAMPAIGN IS GUIDED BY A SET OF POLICY RECOMMENDATIONS ANCHORED IN HUMAN RIGHTS, AND IT INVITES PEOPLE TO SHARE AND USE THOSE RECOMMENDATIONS WITH THEIR GOVERNMENT OR ANY OTHER ACTOR AT EVERY OPPORTUNITY TO ASSERT THEIR RIGHTS. A drafted set of demands, free to take. A community that knows what it objects to but not what to ask for now has language that 800 organisations already stand behind — which is a stronger thing to table at a consultation than a locally worded complaint. THE MOBILISATION AGAINST CRIMINALISATION: A GLOBAL MOBILISATION CALLING ON GOVERNMENTS AND CORPORATE ACTORS TO END CRIMINALISATION AND FULLY PROTECT THE PEOPLE DEFENDING THE EARTH — ON THE STATED GROUND THAT EVERY SINGLE DAY LAND RIGHTS DEFENDERS ARE INTIMIDATED, BRANDED AS CRIMINALS, LOCKED UP OR TAKEN TO COURT, AND THAT THIS IS A STRATEGY BEING USED BY GOVERNMENTS AND CORPORATIONS TO STOP DEFENDERS DOING THEIR WORK. Prosecution named as a deliberate tactic rather than a coincidence. A community whose organisers are facing charges can attach its own case to a standing international mobilisation instead of arguing alone that the charges are political. HOW THE MOBILISING WORKS: IT MOBILIZES ACTIVE CITIZENS AROUND THE NATIONAL CAMPAIGNS ITS PARTICIPANTS ARE LEADING, AND THROUGH YEARLY GLOBAL WEEKS OF ACTION. AROUND THE NATIONAL CAMPAIGNS ITS PARTICIPANTS ARE LEADING — so the campaign amplifies your fight rather than asking you to join someone else's. The dated weeks of action are the moment to time a local event for maximum outside attention, the same logic as the counter-summit filed under Rwanda. THE SCALE OF WHAT HAS JOINED: SINCE ITS LAUNCH IN MARCH 2016, OVER 800 ORGANISATIONS AND OVER 40,000 INDIVIDUALS HAVE SIGNED UP — CONVENED BY THREE NAMED INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATIONS. THE FIGURE THE WHOLE CAMPAIGN RESTS ON: WHILE INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES CUSTOMARILY CLAIM AND MANAGE OVER 50% OF THE WORLD'S LANDS, THEY LEGALLY OWN JUST 10% — SO AT LEAST 40% OF THE WORLD'S LAND SURFACE IS SUBJECT TO A MASSIVE TENURE CRISIS AND VULNERABLE TO LAND GRABBING BY MORE POWERFUL ACTORS. Fifty per cent managed, ten per cent owned. That gap is the reason a community can be farming ground for generations and still be legally invisible when a concession is granted over it. WHAT THAT LAND IS GRABBED FOR, LISTED: LARGE PLANTATIONS, FOSSIL-FUEL PROJECTS, HYDROELECTRIC DAMS, TOURISM, SPECULATION — OR CONSERVATION. CONSERVATION listed as a cause of land grabbing, in a land rights campaign convened by conservation-adjacent bodies. This file has recorded that repeatedly, including a continental ruling on a park created by eviction; it is useful to have the point made inside the sector rather than only against it. THE ARGUMENT IT ARMS A COMMUNITY WITH: SECURING LAND RIGHTS HELPS COMMUNITIES MANAGE THEIR LAND MORE SUSTAINABLY, ACCESS CREDIT, DIVERSIFY ACTIVITIES AND INVEST — AND CAN BOOST FARMERS' PRODUCTIVITY BY 60 PERCENT AND MORE THAN DOUBLE FAMILY INCOME; 70% OF THE WORLD'S FOOD IS PRODUCED BY SMALL-SCALE PRODUCERS. Productivity up 60 per cent, family income more than doubled. That is the economic case put to a ministry that treats community tenure as a brake on development, and it is sourced rather than asserted. THE AFRICAN RESULTS ON RECORD: THE CAMPAIGN LED TO SIGNIFICANT LAW AND POLICY CHANGES IN A NAMED WEST AFRICAN COUNTRY AMONG OTHERS — AND LAW WAS CHANGED AS A RESULT OF A SUCCESSFUL CAMPAIGN AND CAPACITY BUILDING TO PROTECT THE LAND RIGHTS OF A NAMED INDIGENOUS PEOPLE IN THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO, WHOSE RECOGNITION MEMBERS HAD BEEN PUSHING FOR SINCE 2015 ON BEHALF OF 600,000 PEOPLE. A national law changed for 600,000 people, after seven years of pushing. Both halves matter: it can be done, and it takes that long — which is the honest timescale to plan a campaign around. THE METHOD BEHIND ONE OF THOSE WINS, WHICH TRANSFERS: MEMBERS IN ANOTHER COUNTRY OPPOSED THE CONSTRUCTION OF A FIVE-STAR HOTEL ON LAND BELONGING TO AN INDIGENOUS COMMUNITY THROUGH CAPACITY BUILDING AND PUBLIC DEMONSTRATIONS. A hotel stopped by training and demonstrations, with no litigation named. Worth recording because most of this file's routes are legal ones, and this was neither expensive nor slow. WHAT IT SAYS ABOUT ITS OWN METHODS AND GOVERNANCE: IT BELIEVES IN PEACEFUL ACTION AND THE POWER OF PEOPLE, AND HAS AN ADVISORY BOARD WHICH REVIEWS ITS PLANS AND PROVIDES GUIDANCE. AND THE PLEDGES ITS CONVENING COALITION REQUIRES OF MEMBERS: ALL MEMBERS OF THAT COALITION SIGN ON TO TWO PLEDGES THAT PROTECT AND EMPOWER BOTH WOMEN AND LAND DEFENDERS WITHIN THE NETWORK — A COALITION OF ALMOST 300 MEMBERS IN 81 COUNTRIES. Two binding pledges inside the convening coalition, one on women and one on defenders. Ask any organisation offering to help your community whether it has signed them, and what it does when a member breaches them. WHO IT SUITS: African communities and committees, registered or not, who want an international banner, a drafted set of demands, and a dated moment each year to act. CAVEATS: A CAMPAIGN, NOT A FUNDER, A LAW FIRM OR A PROTECTION SERVICE — JOINING BRINGS VISIBILITY AND MATERIAL, NOT MONEY OR REPRESENTATION, AND VISIBILITY CARRIES ITS OWN RISK WHERE ORGANISERS ARE ALREADY TARGETED. For the emergency protection behind that risk, the Republic of Congo's and Comoros' entries; for the community-written charter demanding the right of consent, Niger's entry.

trackers.name: CODEC Guinée (Collectif des OSC pour la défense des droits des communautés impactées par les projets de développement) — eleven organisations in one consortium for people a mining, energy or agricultural project is about to displace
trackers.desc: ELEVEN ORGANISATIONS IN ONE SEAT, FOR PEOPLE A PROJECT IS ABOUT TO MOVE — method and adjacency declared first: THE WORD-BOUNDARY PROBE RAN FOUR HOSTS AND SIX DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL FOUR HOSTS AND FOUR FACTS ABSENT. TWO MEMBER ORGANISATIONS ARE ALREADY FILED UNDER GUINEA ON THEIR OWN HOSTS AND WERE READ IN FULL — ONE THAT REPRESENTED THIRTEEN VILLAGES AGAINST A BAUXITE LENDER, ONE THAT HELPS COMMUNITIES WRITE THEIR OWN PROTOCOL. THE CONSORTIUM ITSELF, AND THE NATIONAL COMPENSATION STANDARD IT EXISTS TO WIN, ARE ABSENT. NEITHER MEMBER IS RESTATED AND NEITHER HOST IS SHIPPED. WHAT IT IS AND WHO IS IN IT, WHICH IS THE FIND: A COLLECTIVE OF CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS FOR THE DEFENCE OF THE RIGHTS OF COMMUNITIES IMPACTED BY DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS — CREATED IN 2018 AS A CONSORTIUM OF ELEVEN NATIONAL CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, EARLIER RECORDED AS TEN. Eleven organisations behind one name and one door. A village facing a mine does not have to work out which of eleven bodies to approach, and the consortium can put a specialist on a case the others cannot handle. This file already carries two of its members separately; the collective is the way in when you do not know which one you need. THE SECTORS IT COVERS: MINES, LAND, AGRICULTURE, ENERGY, INFRASTRUCTURE AND WATER — ANY PROJECT WITH A DIRECT OR INDIRECT IMPACT ON THE LIFE OF LOCAL COMMUNITIES. Six sectors, and INDIRECT impact included. A community downstream of a dam or beside a haul road is inside the mandate, which is where most resource lists stop. THE MISSING LAW IT IS FIGHTING FOR, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: A NATIONAL REFERENCE STANDARD ON COMPENSATION, INDEMNIFICATION AND RESETTLEMENT OF POPULATIONS AFFECTED BY DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS — WITH THE ABSENCE OF A BINDING NATIONAL NORM NAMED AS A REAL CONCERN THAT RISKS AFFECTING THE RIGHTS OF IMPACTED COMMUNITIES. THERE IS NO BINDING NATIONAL STANDARD. That is the single most useful fact here for anyone being offered compensation: what a company proposes is not measured against a national rule, because none exists. Ask what standard the offer is being calculated against, and expect the answer to be the lender's policy rather than the country's law. WHY THAT MATTERS NOW, IN ITS OWN WORDS: THE COUNTRY IS A BUILDING SITE, WITH MANY PROJECTS IN MINING, ENERGY, INFRASTRUCTURE AND AGRICULTURE; ALL OF THEM NEED LAND ACQUISITION, AND THE STANDARD WOULD LET COMMUNITIES BE PROTECTED IN THEIR LANDS AND THEIR LEGITIMATE RIGHTS RESPECTED. THE MEMORANDUM ROUTE IT USES, WHICH IS THE THIRD FIND: IT ADDRESSED A FIVE-PAGE ADVOCACY MEMORANDUM TO THE NATIONAL AUTHORITIES ON LAND OWNERSHIP AND TENURE SECURITY AND THE URGENCY OF A NATIONAL LAND POLICY, MADE PUBLIC AT A PRESS CONFERENCE IN THE CAPITAL. FIVE PAGES, published, then a press conference. That is a replicable shape for a coalition with no litigation budget: a short written demand on the record, released publicly so it cannot be quietly shelved. THE NAMED MEGA-PROJECT IT PUT ON THE RECORD: A MEMORANDUM ON A MAJOR IRON ORE PROJECT, ALERTING TO HIGH RISKS THAT INTERNATIONAL SOCIAL, ENVIRONMENTAL AND GOVERNANCE STANDARDS WOULD NOT BE FULLY RESPECTED OR IMPLEMENTED BY ALL PARTIES. THE CONTRACT DEFECT IT FOUND, WHICH IS THE FOURTH FIND: ITS ANALYSIS OF THE SIGNED CONVENTIONS REVEALED INSUFFICIENCIES — INCLUDING THE CLASSIFICATION OF THE ENVIRONMENTAL AUDIT UNDER THE HEADING OF CONFIDENTIALITY IN THE BASE CONVENTION WITH ONE OF THE CONSORTIA. THE ENVIRONMENTAL AUDIT FILED AS CONFIDENTIAL. That is a specific, checkable clause and it is the thing to look for in any project convention: not whether an audit exists, but whether the contract lets anyone read it. Read beside this file's Mauritania entry on the contract repositories — the convention is often public even when the audit is not. THE LOCAL DEVELOPMENT FUND PROBLEM IT NAMES: THE WEAK CAPACITY OF IMPACTED LOCAL COMMUNITIES TO MANAGE EFFECTIVELY THE REVENUES DESTINED FOR FINANCING LOCAL DEVELOPMENT, UNDER A NAMED NATIONAL FUND. Money arriving is not the same as money used. A community winning a development fund should budget for the administration of it from the start. THE REGIONAL INSTRUMENT IT CITES: A REGIONAL ECONOMIC COMMUNITY DIRECTIVE OF 27 MAY 2009 ON THE HARMONISATION OF GUIDING PRINCIPLES AND POLICIES IN THE MINING SECTOR. A regional directive binding across the whole bloc, usable where the national law is silent — which, on compensation, it is. WHAT IT DOES FOR THE STATE AS WELL AS AGAINST IT: IT ACCOMPANIES THE LEGAL AND INSTITUTIONAL REFORMS UNDERTAKEN BY GOVERNMENT AND GIVES TECHNICAL AND STRATEGIC SUPPORT TO THE STATE THROUGH TECHNICAL ANALYSES AND RECOMMENDATIONS — WHILE ACCOMPANYING LOCAL COMMUNITIES AND PEASANT FARMERS SO THEIR CONCERNS ARE TAKEN INTO ACCOUNT IN PUBLIC POLICY. Filed plainly because a community should know it: this body advises the government as well as the affected. That gets it into rooms a purely oppositional group cannot enter, and it means it will not always take the most confrontational line. THE RESEARCH IT PUBLISHES AND WITH WHOM: A STUDY ON THE COUNTRY'S LAND COMMISSIONS, THEIR STATE AND REFORM, BY THREE NAMED AUTHORS — WITH AN INTERNATIONAL DEVELOPMENT INSTITUTE THAT SUPPORTS LOCAL CIVIL SOCIETY TO PROMOTE COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION IN POLICY REFORM; PLUS A DRAFT AGRICULTURAL ORIENTATION LAW, A POLICY NOTE ON LAND GOVERNANCE, AND ADVOCACY FOR THE IMPLEMENTING TEXTS OF THE ENVIRONMENT CODE. IMPLEMENTING TEXTS is the detail that decides whether a code works. A country can have an environment code and no regulations under it, in which case nothing in it can be enforced — worth checking before relying on your own. AND HOW IT LEARNS: AN EXPERIENCE-SHARING TRIP TO A NEIGHBOURING COUNTRY AND EXCHANGES WITH PARTNERS IN TWO OTHERS — PLUS WORKSHOPS BRINGING TOGETHER REPRESENTATIVES OF LOCAL COMMUNITIES, PEASANT ORGANISATIONS AND CIVIL SOCIETY ACTORS, OPENING IN A CONTEXT OF GROWING FRUSTRATION AMONG COMMUNITIES IMPACTED BY DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS, NOTABLY MINING. WHO IT SUITS: communities in this country facing displacement by a mine, dam, road or plantation, and coalitions elsewhere looking for the shape of a consortium that can both advise a ministry and stand with the displaced. CAVEATS: ONE COUNTRY, FRANCOPHONE, AND A CONSORTIUM RATHER THAN A LAW FIRM — IT ANALYSES, ADVOCATES AND ACCOMPANIES RATHER THAN LITIGATING; ITS DUAL ROLE ADVISING GOVERNMENT MAY TEMPER ITS POSITIONS; AND THE NATIONAL COMPENSATION STANDARD IT SEEKS WAS STILL NOT ADOPTED AT THE LAST RECORD. For a member that represented thirteen villages against a bauxite lender, and for another that helps communities write their own protocol, Guinea's own entries.

trackers.name: Environmental Defenders Office — Pasifika Program
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the largest environmental legal centre in the Australia-Pacific region, whose Pasifika-led programme works on extractive industries, forestry, marine protection and climate across Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands, Fiji, Vanuatu and Tuvalu. WHO IT SUITS: an in-country organisation rather than an individual — EDO works predominantly through partner organisations (CELCOR in PNG, the Landowners Advocacy and Legal Support Unit and the Solomon Islands Environmental Law Association, the Fiji Environmental Law Association and the Vanuatu Environmental Law Association), supplying strategic legal capacity, co-authored law-reform papers and litigation support. Approach your national environmental law association first; its free advice hotline is for Australia only. YOUR NATIONAL PARTNER IS the Fiji Environmental Law Association. EDO is an Australian organisation based in Sydney, and its Pasifika Program is Pasifika-led — including diaspora Pasifika lawyers with cultural and spiritual links to the region — working predominantly through partner organisations. So the partner is the front door and EDO is the legal capacity behind it. Focus areas: climate change, threats to marine environments, forestry and mining. EDO is an accredited community legal service with a community advice hotline, the largest environmental legal centre in the Australia-Pacific, and records a historic Solomon Islands bauxite mine case. REACH IS LIMITED AND STATED: EDO names PNG, Solomon Islands, Fiji and Vanuatu, plus Tuvalu — it does not cover the other Pacific states, so do not assume regional coverage.

trackers.name: Fiji Environmental Law Association (FELA)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Fiji's only dedicated environmental law body — a membership association of lawyers, conservationists and academics, registered as a company limited by guarantee since 2008, whose members provide legal advice and technical support to community groups and run training on the Environment Management Act, the EIA process, coastal fisheries, qoliqoli rights and gravel extraction. It has co-authored policy and law papers on marine protected areas and Fiji's coastal fisheries. WHO IT SUITS: a Fijian community or landowning unit facing a coastal development, extraction or fisheries decision — advice is given in matters that meet the association's casework guidelines, so it is a screened service rather than open legal aid.

trackers.name: Office of the Auditor-General
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Fiji, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Fiji — Ministry of Finance
trackers.desc: National budget authority; the Budget Division prepares the national budget and publishes budget resources & estimates, Fiji. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Fiji.

trackers.name: Fiji — Registrar of Companies Office
trackers.desc: National company registry; registers business names, companies, credit unions & money lenders and maintains entity records (online platform since 2019), Fiji. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: PacLII
trackers.desc: Pacific Islands Legal Information Institute: free case law for Fiji and other Pacific jurisdictions. · Find here: free legislation and case-law for around twenty Pacific Island jurisdictions (PacLII).

trackers.name: Fiji Bureau of Statistics
trackers.desc: Fiji's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Fiji.

trackers.name: SPREP — three conventions, and 26 members is not 12 parties
trackers.desc: THE REGIONAL BODY FOR PACIFIC ENVIRONMENT, AND IT IS SECRETARIAT TO THREE CONVENTIONS. SPREP is an independent intergovernmental organisation, autonomous since the Agreement Establishing SPREP was signed at Apia on 16 June 1993, with the Article 2 purpose of providing assistance to protect and improve the environment and ensure sustainable development for present and future generations. It has 26 members — 14 Pacific island countries, 7 territories and 5 metropolitan states — and is headquartered in Apia, Samoa. ESTABLISH WHICH CONVENTION FITS YOUR ISSUE: the Noumea Convention (1986, in force 1990), described by UNEP as the only comprehensive multilateral umbrella agreement for protection of natural resources and environment in the region; the Waigani Convention on hazardous and radioactive waste imports; and the Apia Convention on nature conservation. THE NOUMEA CONVENTION IS UNDER ACTIVE REVIEW — WHICH IS AN OPENING: a 2021 Review produced recommendations now being implemented through a Noumea Workplan and Budget whose stated aim is to elevate the work of the Convention and enhance awareness and implementation, with a Communications Plan and a Finance Strategy named as critical. BUT CHECK WHETHER YOUR STATE IS A PARTY: SPREP has 26 members while the Noumea Convention has only 12 contracting parties — membership and party status are different things, and this entry does not assert the latter. GOVERNANCE POINT WORTH KNOWING: the SPREP Meeting is the plenary decision-making body; the Executive Board (established 2015) is subordinate to it and has no power to make decisions requiring input of all Members — so a decision affecting all members must go to the Meeting. IF YOUR ISSUE IS SEABED MINING: UNEP records deep sea mining as an emerging contentious issue the region is dealing with — the regional body has already named it. SPREP is also developing a portal for protected areas managers. THERE IS A SPREP PRESENCE IN YOUR COUNTRY: beyond Apia, host country agreements exist with the Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, the Marshall Islands, Solomon Islands and Vanuatu — so you need not approach Samoa first.

trackers.name: Pacific Development and Conservation Trust — citizens may apply
trackers.desc: AN INDIVIDUAL CAN APPLY, AND THE FIRST DOCUMENT IS SHORT. The Pacific Development and Conservation Trust, administered through the New Zealand government's Community Matters service with requests assessed by Advisory Trustees, states that ‘citizens or organisations’ from eligible Pacific places may request funding — so no incorporated body is required, which removes the commonest barrier recorded across this map. THE PROCESS IS TWO-STAGE: submit an Expression of Interest; only successful applicants are invited to submit a full project application. Do not prepare a full proposal before the EOI is accepted — wasted work, and expensive wasted work where drafting means travelling. Applications must be on the current form with all sections completed, submitted online where connection allows. READ THE PUBLISHED GRANT RECORD BEFORE DRAFTING: the Trust publishes records of grants by round — 2020/21, 2021/22, 2022/23 (two rounds), 2023/24 and 2024/25 — showing what the Trustees have actually funded, at what size and in which countries. That is better evidence of what will succeed than any guidance note. UNDP SUPPORT HERE IS COUNTRY-LEVEL: UNDP's Pacific Office provides country support to this state, so an in-country office is a realistic second route alongside the Trust.

trackers.name: SPREP EIA and SEA guidelines — intervene at scoping, not after
trackers.desc: SCOPING IS WHERE STAKEHOLDER CONCERNS BECOME TERMS OF REFERENCE — and the guidelines say so themselves. Assessments must be individually customised to the aspects most relevant to stakeholders, and ‘customisation usually occurs during the scoping phase and results in the preparation of terms of reference’. Intervene at scoping and the assessment is required to examine your issue; intervene later and you are commenting on an assessment that was never asked to look. SPREP's Strengthening Environmental Impact Assessment: Guidelines for Pacific Island Countries and Territories (60pp, English and French) is the regional practice standard, SPREP having been mandated on EIA capacity since the 1990s. KNOW WHICH INSTRUMENT YOUR FIGHT NEEDS: EIA assesses a project; the companion Strategic Environmental Assessment guidelines (developed 2018–2020) assess a policy, plan or programme and are addressed to environment agencies, national planning offices, development control agencies, municipal authorities and provincial administrations — so if the problem is a tourism plan or a zoning programme rather than one hotel, SEA is the instrument and the municipal or provincial authority is the addressee. There is also a sector guideline for coastal tourism development, made with the South Pacific Tourism Organisation. THE HONEST PART, FROM A REGULATOR'S OWN ACCOUNT: Vanuatu's Principal EIA Officer publicly described her department's challenges as lack of staff, lack of political support, weaknesses in public consultation, and low capacity in monitoring and enforcement. Expect to supply evidence the agency cannot gather itself, and expect post-consent monitoring to be weak unless someone outside government does it — it is also a citable admission when arguing that a condition needs an independent monitoring mechanism attached. CHECK YOUR OWN ENVIRONMENT ACT FIRST: many Pacific countries have EIA mandated under their Environment Acts and EIA Regulations, and these guidelines support the implementation of current legal requirements rather than replacing them — the practice standard, not the obligation. SPREP runs in-country EIA training workshops, and the Pacific Environment Portal carries regional and national data.

trackers.name: Waigani Convention — radioactive waste, and 200 miles not 12
trackers.desc: IT REACHES WHERE BASEL CANNOT — and for island states that is the whole point. The Waigani Convention is modelled on Basel and is the regional implementation of the hazardous waste regime, but differs in two decisive ways: it also covers radioactive wastes, and its territorial coverage includes each Party's Exclusive Economic Zone — 200 nautical miles — rather than stopping at the 12 nautical mile territorial sea as Basel does. That makes it the instrument for dumping, transhipment and seabed disposal cases Basel cannot touch. It is annex-driven: obligations extend to all wastes in Annex I or those possessing the listed characteristics — check Annex I first; if the substance is listed the obligations attach automatically, and if not, the argument runs through the hazard characteristics instead. It is closely tied to the London Convention on dumping at sea. THE BODY TO CONTACT: the Pacific Regional Centre for the Waigani and Basel Conventions, based at SPREP in Samoa, which has developed a model law implementing all four waste conventions (Basel, Rotterdam, Stockholm, Waigani) with a worked Tonga project — so where a national statute is missing or fragmented, the model already exists and a government can be pointed at it. AND A CONSULTATION WINDOW IS OPEN NOW: Cleaner Pacific 2025, the regional waste and pollution strategy built with 21 member countries around four goals and 15 strategic actions, is being replaced — the successor CP2036 was endorsed at the 31st SPREP Meeting (September 2023) with consultation in Suva, 21–22 July 2025. Priorities for the next decade are being set now. Ask whether your country has a national waste and pollution policy written against the regional strategy — it is the document your government is measured against. Delivery vehicles include PacWaste Plus (EUR 16.5 million, 72 months, EU-funded, across eight waste streams). THE HONEST LIMIT, FROM SPREP'S OWN REVIEW: Australia's reporting capability far exceeds that of most Pacific island countries, relying on weighbridge data requiring infrastructure that is not available — so do not assume an absence of data means an absence of a problem, and community-gathered data may be the best evidence there is. Watch the Clean Pacific Roundtable and CIRCLE EXPO, held alternately for an annual meeting of countries, industry and civil society — named as a participant category, not an observer.

trackers.name: Right to information — what your country actually has
trackers.desc: ASK EVEN WHERE THERE IS NO STATUTE — UNESCO's 2022 report on SDG 16.10.2 records that even Pacific states without access-to-information laws have an environment ‘generally favourable to the public's exercising of their right to information’. The absence of a law is not, on the region's own evidence, a reason to expect refusal. AND THERE IS A COMMITMENT TO CITE WHERE NO LAW EXISTS: the Boe Declaration on Regional Security (2018) Action Plan includes the adoption and implementation of constitutional, statutory and/or policy guarantees for public access to information as a measure for success — a government that signed Boe has already agreed that access to information is a measure of its own success. The Pacific Plan 2005 and the UN Pacific Strategy urge the same. The underlying right sits in article 19 of the ICCPR and of the Universal Declaration. REGIONAL POSITION: only four Pacific island countries have adopted RTI laws — Cook Islands (2008), Palau (2014), Vanuatu (2016) and Fiji (2018) — with several others drafting. A SOURCING WARNING FROM VANUATU'S OWN RTI UNIT, which applies region-wide: its site carries the notice ‘beware of fake websites pretending to be official’ — verify the domain before submitting anything containing your identity and your concern. IN FIJI — READ THE LIMITS BEFORE RELYING ON IT: the Information Act 2018 defines information broadly, but only Fijian residents or citizens may apply; requests are limited to cases where the information directly affects a decision regarding the requester; and only if the information came into existence after the law entered into force. Exemptions are broad, the Act does not address conflicts with secrecy provisions in other laws, and the only ground of appeal is where access is refused. Historic documents about a site are outside it entirely.

trackers.name: Fiji EIA Administrator — the public-concern trigger and the cash bond
trackers.desc: TWO PROVISIONS MOST COMMUNITIES NEVER LEARN ABOUT, AND BOTH HAVE TO BE ASKED FOR. FIRST, THE PUBLIC-CONCERN TRIGGER: if the EIA Administrator has reason to believe that there is a public concern relating to a proposal, the Administrator may require the approving authority to submit the EIA report for consideration to take into account the public concern — the threshold is not proof of harm, it is the Administrator having reason to believe concern exists, so documented concern addressed to that office by name is what the provision contemplates. SECOND, THE ENVIRONMENTAL CASH BOND: an approval may be subject to an environmental cash bond deposited into the Fund as security to cover the probable cost of preventing or mitigating environmental damage — the strongest condition available here, and discretionary, so ask for it by name at approval with a figure and a basis. THREE SEPARATE 21-DAY WINDOWS: the public may inspect and view an EIA report within 21 days of submission; a second public meeting must be held within 21 days of submission; and appeal to the Environmental Tribunal is within 21 days of the decision. To read, to be heard, and to appeal — diarise all three. Consultation happens twice and the first shapes the report: the proponent must consult during the EIA study, and hold a public hearing within the vicinity of the proposed development once it is complete — held by the proponent, not the regulator, and it must be near the site. CHECK THE REPORT FOR THE NO-ACTION OPTION: it must state the alternatives considered including the option of taking no action, and the reasons for choosing the proposed action — if it does not, it is incomplete on the face of the regulations. CONTACT: the Environment Impact Assessment Unit, senimili.baleicakau@govnet.gov.fj, +679 3311699, mobile 9905176; Monday–Thursday 8:00–16:30, Friday to 16:00; screening determination in 14 working days; application form EMA/EIAP 1. AND THE FILE CONTAINS THE LEASE OR TITLE among required supporting documents — which establishes who actually holds the land, often the first thing a community needs and cannot easily get elsewhere. Two structural points: a ministry or local authority proposing its own development must refer it to the EIA Administrator — government cannot assess its own project — and an approved EIA is valid only for the specific activity approved and must not be transferred, so if the project has changed, the approval may not cover it.

trackers.name: ELAW — free attorneys and scientists who will critique the developer's EIA
trackers.desc: IT WILL READ THE DEVELOPER'S EIA AND TELL YOU WHAT IS WRONG WITH IT — which is the thing a community cannot produce alone and usually cannot afford. ELAW is a global alliance of attorneys, scientists and other advocates, founded 1989 in Eugene, Oregon by public interest lawyers from ten countries, that provides legal and scientific support to grassroots advocates to challenge destructive projects. FOUR CONCRETE FORMS OF HELP: legal support to local public interest lawyers; scientific support, including critiquing environmental assessments; economic insights on projects; and security expertise — ‘ELAW helps environmental lawyers improve their security so they can work without fear. When our partners are targeted, we act quickly to help defend and protect them.’ That last one is a named function, not an aspiration, and ELAW co-founded the Alliance for Land, Indigenous and Environmental Defenders. HOW TO USE IT — THROUGH A LAWYER, NOT AS A CLIENT: ELAW works through more than 300 public interest advocates in its network, and its stated strategy is ‘locating strong lawyers who are committed to protecting the environment in their home countries’. You can approach ELAW directly, but the leverage is greatest when a local advocate is the conduit — that is how the network is built. It has hosted nearly 300 advocates from more than 65 countries as Fellows and provided support on thousands of cases; several partners have won the Goldman Environmental Prize. Focus areas include biodiversity, fossil fuels — expressly assisting advocates in contesting fossil fuel development projects — plastic pollution, and work with coastal communities. It publishes guidebooks, including one to give communities sufficient understanding to challenge oil and gas projects, and clause-level summaries of national EIA law — so its site is also a route to learning exactly what your own EIA law requires. ASK WHETHER ELAW HAS A PARTNER IN YOUR COUNTRY: the network is described as spanning 70 to 80 countries but the member list is not published country by country, so this entry does not assert a presence in yours.

trackers.name: NatureFiji-MareqetiViti — the NGO that works through customary landowners
trackers.desc: Fiji's first and only local biodiversity conservation NGO, working on habitat conservation, endangered species and sustainable use through collaborative conservation action, research and education. THE REASON TO CALL THEM ABOUT LAND: it expressly recognises the key role to be played by Fiji's indigenous landowners — and in Fiji most land is under customary ownership, so an organisation that works THROUGH landowners rather than around them is the one that can change what happens on a site. It also aims to generate local expertise in wildlife conservation and management — which means it can supply the biodiversity evidence a community needs and cannot produce alone. IF YOU NEED A DIFFERENT ORGANISATION, TWO DIRECTORIES WILL FIND YOU ONE: PIANGO publishes a member directory of national umbrella NGOs across 25 Pacific countries, with named contacts and addresses — an umbrella body is the fastest route to the right local organisation when you do not know who to call. PICAN lists members including the Anglican Church of Melanesia (nine dioceses across Solomon Islands, Vanuatu and New Caledonia) — a community-level network with reach no NGO in the region matches — and Vanuatu's Campaign for Justice, whose stated mission is to actively confront and expose those who obstruct natural justice with impunity. Live & Learn runs Climate Resilient Islands with rural communities in Fiji, Tonga, Vanuatu, Tuvalu, Solomon Islands, PNG and Samoa, with outcome areas including nature-based land management, and publishes filterable case studies and fact sheets. AND A FUNDING MODEL PACIFIC NGOs HAVE STUDIED: at Mida Creek in Kenya, 22 organisations share resources and finances around one protected area, funding guided eco-tours and alternative livelihoods such as beekeeping to relieve harvesting pressure — pooling finances around a single site is a funding model, not just a partnership.

trackers.name: Nakau — income instead of logging, with the land staying with the clans
trackers.desc: WHERE LAND IS UNDER CUSTOMARY OWNERSHIP AND CANNOT BE BOUGHT, THIS IS THE EQUIVALENT OF BUYING IT: an income stream that makes keeping the forest worth more than felling it, with ownership staying with the landholders. Nakau works with Indigenous customary landowners across the Pacific, within local governance systems, expressly to ensure all projects are owned by the customary landholders — which is the difference between this and a concession. Its delivery partner across Fiji, Solomon Islands, Vanuatu and PNG is Live & Learn. It now protects close to 4,000 hectares, is verified under Plan Vivo Climate, and won the International Energy Globe Award. WHERE THE MONEY WENT MATTERS MORE THAN THE HECTARES: credit income funded water and sanitation across five villages and supported women-led enterprises, honey, agroforestry, ecotourism and youth initiatives — the argument to put to neighbours who fear protection means poverty. Others include Yato on Makira (10,000 hectares, with timber concessions still encroaching as recently as early 2025), East Rennell with 11 tribes, and 1,000+ hectares on New Georgia.
