Named backers include the EU, Ekos, MFAT, WWF-Australia and the Solomon Islands Threshold Program; Nakau and Live & Learn publish a toolkit for project coordinators.

trackers.name: Environmental Defenders Office — Pasifika Program
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the largest environmental legal centre in the Australia-Pacific region, whose Pasifika-led programme works on extractive industries, forestry, marine protection and climate across Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands, Fiji, Vanuatu and Tuvalu. WHO IT SUITS: an in-country organisation rather than an individual — EDO works predominantly through partner organisations (CELCOR in PNG, the Landowners Advocacy and Legal Support Unit and the Solomon Islands Environmental Law Association, the Fiji Environmental Law Association and the Vanuatu Environmental Law Association), supplying strategic legal capacity, co-authored law-reform papers and litigation support. Approach your national environmental law association first; its free advice hotline is for Australia only. YOUR NATIONAL PARTNER IS the Centre for Environmental Law and Community Rights (CELCOR). EDO is an Australian organisation based in Sydney, and its Pasifika Program is Pasifika-led — including diaspora Pasifika lawyers with cultural and spiritual links to the region — working predominantly through partner organisations. So the partner is the front door and EDO is the legal capacity behind it. Focus areas: climate change, threats to marine environments, forestry and mining. EDO is an accredited community legal service with a community advice hotline, the largest environmental legal centre in the Australia-Pacific, and records a historic Solomon Islands bauxite mine case. REACH IS LIMITED AND STATED: EDO names PNG, Solomon Islands, Fiji and Vanuatu, plus Tuvalu — it does not cover the other Pacific states, so do not assume regional coverage.

trackers.name: Centre for Environmental Law & Community Rights (CELCOR)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Papua New Guinea's public-interest environmental law NGO, established in 2000 — legal advice and representation for customary landowners, community organisations and NGOs facing logging, mining, oil palm, other extractives and marine development, alongside community legal education, paralegal training and mediation. It has intervened in most of PNG's provinces and supported the Mesulam v Joku ruling on the public's right to project information. WHO IT SUITS: a customary landowning group or CBO facing a resource project on its land — assistance to landowners is the core mandate, but this is a nine-person office working from Port Moresby only, so travel and capacity limit what it can take.

trackers.name: Friends of the Earth Asia Pacific
trackers.desc: The Asia Pacific regional structure of Friends of the Earth International, formed in 2008, whose member groups work on community-based struggles against destructive projects, particularly mining and other extractive industries, alongside Indigenous peoples, peasant farmers, fisherfolk and trade unions. WHO TO ENLIST: the national member group nearest the project. In this region Friends of the Earth International's own directory names groups in Bangladesh (BELA, the Bangladesh Environmental Lawyers' Association), India, Indonesia (WALHI), Japan, Malaysia (Sahabat Alam Malaysia), Nepal, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines (the Legal Rights and Natural Resources Center), South Korea and Sri Lanka. You CAN: reach an organisation that already works community-side in your own country, and draw regional weight onto a local fight. For activists: in several of these countries the Friends of the Earth affiliate is the most experienced community-side environmental body there is.

trackers.name: Office of the Auditor-General
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Papua New Guinea, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: IPA Companies Office
trackers.desc: National — Investment Promotion Authority company register, Papua New Guinea. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: PacLII – Papua New Guinea
trackers.desc: Free case law and legislation for Papua New Guinea via the Pacific Islands Legal Information Institute. · Find here: free Papua New Guinea legislation and court decisions, hosted by PacLII.

trackers.name: Papua New Guinea — Department of Treasury
trackers.desc: National budget authority; prepares the national budget and publishes annual budget volumes & economic updates, Papua New Guinea. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Papua New Guinea.

trackers.name: SPREP — three conventions, and 26 members is not 12 parties
trackers.desc: THE REGIONAL BODY FOR PACIFIC ENVIRONMENT, AND IT IS SECRETARIAT TO THREE CONVENTIONS. SPREP is an independent intergovernmental organisation, autonomous since the Agreement Establishing SPREP was signed at Apia on 16 June 1993, with the Article 2 purpose of providing assistance to protect and improve the environment and ensure sustainable development for present and future generations. It has 26 members — 14 Pacific island countries, 7 territories and 5 metropolitan states — and is headquartered in Apia, Samoa. ESTABLISH WHICH CONVENTION FITS YOUR ISSUE: the Noumea Convention (1986, in force 1990), described by UNEP as the only comprehensive multilateral umbrella agreement for protection of natural resources and environment in the region; the Waigani Convention on hazardous and radioactive waste imports; and the Apia Convention on nature conservation. THE NOUMEA CONVENTION IS UNDER ACTIVE REVIEW — WHICH IS AN OPENING: a 2021 Review produced recommendations now being implemented through a Noumea Workplan and Budget whose stated aim is to elevate the work of the Convention and enhance awareness and implementation, with a Communications Plan and a Finance Strategy named as critical. BUT CHECK WHETHER YOUR STATE IS A PARTY: SPREP has 26 members while the Noumea Convention has only 12 contracting parties — membership and party status are different things, and this entry does not assert the latter. GOVERNANCE POINT WORTH KNOWING: the SPREP Meeting is the plenary decision-making body; the Executive Board (established 2015) is subordinate to it and has no power to make decisions requiring input of all Members — so a decision affecting all members must go to the Meeting. IF YOUR ISSUE IS SEABED MINING: UNEP records deep sea mining as an emerging contentious issue the region is dealing with — the regional body has already named it. SPREP is also developing a portal for protected areas managers.

trackers.name: Pacific Development and Conservation Trust — citizens may apply
trackers.desc: AN INDIVIDUAL CAN APPLY, AND THE FIRST DOCUMENT IS SHORT. The Pacific Development and Conservation Trust, administered through the New Zealand government's Community Matters service with requests assessed by Advisory Trustees, states that ‘citizens or organisations’ from eligible Pacific places may request funding — so no incorporated body is required, which removes the commonest barrier recorded across this map. THE PROCESS IS TWO-STAGE: submit an Expression of Interest; only successful applicants are invited to submit a full project application. Do not prepare a full proposal before the EOI is accepted — wasted work, and expensive wasted work where drafting means travelling. Applications must be on the current form with all sections completed, submitted online where connection allows. READ THE PUBLISHED GRANT RECORD BEFORE DRAFTING: the Trust publishes records of grants by round — 2020/21, 2021/22, 2022/23 (two rounds), 2023/24 and 2024/25 — showing what the Trustees have actually funded, at what size and in which countries. That is better evidence of what will succeed than any guidance note. CHECK BEFORE EXPECTING A UNDP OFFICE: UNDP's Pacific Office provides only regional support to this state — not country-level — so do not assume an in-country presence when planning a second funding route.

trackers.name: SPREP EIA and SEA guidelines — intervene at scoping, not after
trackers.desc: SCOPING IS WHERE STAKEHOLDER CONCERNS BECOME TERMS OF REFERENCE — and the guidelines say so themselves. Assessments must be individually customised to the aspects most relevant to stakeholders, and ‘customisation usually occurs during the scoping phase and results in the preparation of terms of reference’. Intervene at scoping and the assessment is required to examine your issue; intervene later and you are commenting on an assessment that was never asked to look. SPREP's Strengthening Environmental Impact Assessment: Guidelines for Pacific Island Countries and Territories (60pp, English and French) is the regional practice standard, SPREP having been mandated on EIA capacity since the 1990s. KNOW WHICH INSTRUMENT YOUR FIGHT NEEDS: EIA assesses a project; the companion Strategic Environmental Assessment guidelines (developed 2018–2020) assess a policy, plan or programme and are addressed to environment agencies, national planning offices, development control agencies, municipal authorities and provincial administrations — so if the problem is a tourism plan or a zoning programme rather than one hotel, SEA is the instrument and the municipal or provincial authority is the addressee. There is also a sector guideline for coastal tourism development, made with the South Pacific Tourism Organisation. THE HONEST PART, FROM A REGULATOR'S OWN ACCOUNT: Vanuatu's Principal EIA Officer publicly described her department's challenges as lack of staff, lack of political support, weaknesses in public consultation, and low capacity in monitoring and enforcement. Expect to supply evidence the agency cannot gather itself, and expect post-consent monitoring to be weak unless someone outside government does it — it is also a citable admission when arguing that a condition needs an independent monitoring mechanism attached. CHECK YOUR OWN ENVIRONMENT ACT FIRST: many Pacific countries have EIA mandated under their Environment Acts and EIA Regulations, and these guidelines support the implementation of current legal requirements rather than replacing them — the practice standard, not the obligation. SPREP runs in-country EIA training workshops, and the Pacific Environment Portal carries regional and national data.

trackers.name: Waigani Convention — radioactive waste, and 200 miles not 12
trackers.desc: IT REACHES WHERE BASEL CANNOT — and for island states that is the whole point. The Waigani Convention is modelled on Basel and is the regional implementation of the hazardous waste regime, but differs in two decisive ways: it also covers radioactive wastes, and its territorial coverage includes each Party's Exclusive Economic Zone — 200 nautical miles — rather than stopping at the 12 nautical mile territorial sea as Basel does. That makes it the instrument for dumping, transhipment and seabed disposal cases Basel cannot touch. It is annex-driven: obligations extend to all wastes in Annex I or those possessing the listed characteristics — check Annex I first; if the substance is listed the obligations attach automatically, and if not, the argument runs through the hazard characteristics instead. It is closely tied to the London Convention on dumping at sea. THE BODY TO CONTACT: the Pacific Regional Centre for the Waigani and Basel Conventions, based at SPREP in Samoa, which has developed a model law implementing all four waste conventions (Basel, Rotterdam, Stockholm, Waigani) with a worked Tonga project — so where a national statute is missing or fragmented, the model already exists and a government can be pointed at it. AND A CONSULTATION WINDOW IS OPEN NOW: Cleaner Pacific 2025, the regional waste and pollution strategy built with 21 member countries around four goals and 15 strategic actions, is being replaced — the successor CP2036 was endorsed at the 31st SPREP Meeting (September 2023) with consultation in Suva, 21–22 July 2025. Priorities for the next decade are being set now. Ask whether your country has a national waste and pollution policy written against the regional strategy — it is the document your government is measured against. Delivery vehicles include PacWaste Plus (EUR 16.5 million, 72 months, EU-funded, across eight waste streams). THE HONEST LIMIT, FROM SPREP'S OWN REVIEW: Australia's reporting capability far exceeds that of most Pacific island countries, relying on weighbridge data requiring infrastructure that is not available — so do not assume an absence of data means an absence of a problem, and community-gathered data may be the best evidence there is. Watch the Clean Pacific Roundtable and CIRCLE EXPO, held alternately for an annual meeting of countries, industry and civil society — named as a participant category, not an observer.

trackers.name: Right to information — what your country actually has
trackers.desc: ASK EVEN WHERE THERE IS NO STATUTE — UNESCO's 2022 report on SDG 16.10.2 records that even Pacific states without access-to-information laws have an environment ‘generally favourable to the public's exercising of their right to information’. The absence of a law is not, on the region's own evidence, a reason to expect refusal. AND THERE IS A COMMITMENT TO CITE WHERE NO LAW EXISTS: the Boe Declaration on Regional Security (2018) Action Plan includes the adoption and implementation of constitutional, statutory and/or policy guarantees for public access to information as a measure for success — a government that signed Boe has already agreed that access to information is a measure of its own success. The Pacific Plan 2005 and the UN Pacific Strategy urge the same. The underlying right sits in article 19 of the ICCPR and of the Universal Declaration. REGIONAL POSITION: only four Pacific island countries have adopted RTI laws — Cook Islands (2008), Palau (2014), Vanuatu (2016) and Fiji (2018) — with several others drafting. A SOURCING WARNING FROM VANUATU'S OWN RTI UNIT, which applies region-wide: its site carries the notice ‘beware of fake websites pretending to be official’ — verify the domain before submitting anything containing your identity and your concern. IN PAPUA NEW GUINEA: the government committed in 2016 to adopting an RTI law in its national action plan under the Open Government Partnership — an OGP commitment is publicly monitored, which makes it citable.

trackers.name: CEPA and the Director — the permit gate, and a seat on the Council
trackers.desc: FIRST, A DOMAIN WARNING: a site presenting itself as ‘PNG CEPA’ on a .com address carries official-sounding guidance with an injected gambling advert mid-sentence in its advice to proponents. That is SEO spam inside a page pretending to be a regulator. This map does not cite it, and CEPA's own canonical domain was not verified in this round — verify any CEPA address before sending anything. This link goes to SPREP's PNG portal, which hosts CEPA's own EIA guideline. THE STRONGEST PROVISION IN THE ACT IS A GATE ON EVERY OTHER AGENCY: under the Environment Act 2000, other governmental authorities shall be restrained from issuing permits or licences for level 2 or level 3 activities until an environment permit exists — so if a mining, forestry or works authority issued something first, that is a question worth asking in writing. Any other authority receiving an application for a level 2 or 3 activity shall refer it to the Director. The carve-out, stated plainly: this does not apply to approvals under the Investment Promotion Act 1992. THE EARLIEST DOCUMENTARY SIGNAL AVAILABLE: a proponent must register its intention in writing with the Director at least one month before commencing any preparatory work — that registration exists before any site clearance, earlier than an EIA or a permit application. Ask the Director whether an intention has been registered for your area. AND A SEAT ON THE DECIDING BODY, WHICH IS RARE: the Environment Council is appointed from a list of not less than 10 persons prepared after applications have been publicly invited by the Director from among citizens of Papua New Guinea — almost nothing else in this map offers a community member a seat on the body rather than a submission to it. Watch for that invitation. Activities are classified Level 1, Level 2 (2A/2B) and Level 3, but not all activities are listed in the Regulation — which makes a project's level classification itself contestable. For a large project, ask for the environmental and social management plans and the monitoring and reporting conditions, not just the permit — that is where monitoring obligations live, as in the Papua LNG Upstream Level 3 permit granted in September 2025 after more than a decade of assessment. Working without a permit can bring stop-work orders, substantial fines and prosecution of company directors. Provincial environment offices are a named point of consultation alongside CEPA.

trackers.name: ELAW — free attorneys and scientists who will critique the developer's EIA
trackers.desc: IT WILL READ THE DEVELOPER'S EIA AND TELL YOU WHAT IS WRONG WITH IT — which is the thing a community cannot produce alone and usually cannot afford. ELAW is a global alliance of attorneys, scientists and other advocates, founded 1989 in Eugene, Oregon by public interest lawyers from ten countries, that provides legal and scientific support to grassroots advocates to challenge destructive projects. FOUR CONCRETE FORMS OF HELP: legal support to local public interest lawyers; scientific support, including critiquing environmental assessments; economic insights on projects; and security expertise — ‘ELAW helps environmental lawyers improve their security so they can work without fear. Focus areas include biodiversity, fossil fuels — expressly assisting advocates in contesting fossil fuel development projects — plastic pollution, and work with coastal communities. It publishes guidebooks, including one to give communities sufficient understanding to challenge oil and gas projects, and clause-level summaries of national EIA law — so its site is also a route to learning exactly what your own EIA law requires. ASK WHETHER ELAW HAS A PARTNER IN YOUR COUNTRY: the network is described as spanning 70 to 80 countries but the member list is not published country by country, so this entry does not assert a presence in yours.

trackers.name: KVKK — Personal Data Protection Authority
trackers.desc: KVKK — Personal Data Protection Authority — Turkey’s national data-protection / information authority, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Ortak
trackers.desc: Istanbul-based independent investigative-journalism newsroom producing collaborative deep-dive investigations into power, corruption and environmental harm in Turkey. — Holds to account: officials handling public money & power — find investigations into Turkish state and corporate power.

trackers.name: Constitutional Court of Turkey
trackers.desc: Official decisions database, including the individual-application (constitutional complaint) case law. · Find here: information and individual-application decisions of the Constitutional Court of Turkey.

trackers.name: Yargıtay Karar Arama (Court of Cassation)
trackers.desc: Official search of Turkey's Court of Cassation decisions (8M+ rulings). · Find here: the official decision search of Turkey's Court of Cassation (Yargıtay).

trackers.name: Danıştay Karar Arama (Council of State)
trackers.desc: Official decisions database of Turkey's supreme administrative court. · Find here: the official decision search of Turkey's Council of State (Danıştay).

trackers.name: Constitutional Court Decisions Database
trackers.desc: Anayasa Mahkemesi Kararlar Bilgi Bankası — norm-review and individual-application judgments. · Find here: the Turkish Constitutional Court's decisions database.

trackers.name: UYAP Emsal Karar Arama (Ministry of Justice)
trackers.desc: Official precedent search spanning Court of Cassation, Council of State and regional appellate courts. · Find here: the Turkish Ministry of Justice's UYAP precedent search across the higher and regional courts.

trackers.name: TEMA Vakfı — hukuk mücadelesi ve il temsilcilikleri
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Turkish foundation that has been suing the state over land since 1997, when it took the Prime Ministry and the Forestry Ministry to the Council of State to strike down part of a regulation. Its biggest win was legislative — the Pasture Law, stalled for 38 years and lapsed four times, passed unanimously in 1998 after its campaign. It brings annulment actions against environmental plans and ÇED (impact assessment) decisions, including two cases against the 1/100,000 Mersin-Adana environmental plan covering the nuclear site. WHO IT SUITS: any community anywhere in the country, because of the thing that makes it unusual — it publishes a directory of provincial representatives, named individuals with phone numbers and emails, and it operates in all 81 provinces. Start with the temsilci for your province, not the head office. Be realistic about the odds: its 2014 action to annul the positive ÇED decision for the Akkuyu nuclear plant was dismissed and construction proceeded. This is a large mainstream foundation that litigates steadily and does not win everything.

trackers.name: Turkish Council of State
trackers.desc: Turkish Council of State — supreme court (Turkey).

trackers.name: Court of Cassation
trackers.desc: Court of Cassation — supreme court (Turkey).

trackers.name: EKAP
trackers.desc: Turkey's electronic public-procurement platform run by the Public Procurement Authority. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Turkey, and for how much.

trackers.name: MERSIS (Central Trade Registry System)
trackers.desc: Türkiye's central trade registry, run by the Ministry of Trade. Here you can trace companies, their directors and filings registered in Turkey.

trackers.name: Şeffaflık Derneği (Transparency International Türkiye)
trackers.desc: Transparency International's Turkey chapter (since 2008). Works on anti-corruption and political integrity — asset and interest declarations, political finance and public-procurement transparency — and runs the 'Integrity Watch Türkiye' data platform and election-period monitoring.

trackers.name: Sayıştay
trackers.desc: National — Turkish Court of Accounts (supreme audit institution). Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Turkey.

trackers.name: Ticaret Sicil Gazetesi
trackers.desc: Turkey's official Trade Registry Gazette of companies. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Turkish Statistical Institute (TurkStat)
trackers.desc: Türkiye's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Turkey.

trackers.name: WWF-Türkiye (Doğal Hayatı Koruma Vakfı) — protection record
trackers.desc: WHO HAS ACTUALLY GOT LAND PROTECTED HERE. Founded as Doğal Hayatı Koruma Derneği in 1975, became a foundation in 1996 and the WWF network's Turkey office in 2001. Its record is protection rather than campaigning: protection status secured for 20 areas of unique natural value, international status for 8 critically important wetlands, a role in 5 areas being declared national parks, identification of Turkey's important bird areas, and contributing to stopping activities that threatened important natural areas. Landscapes worked in include the Caucasus Ecological Region, Eastern Black Sea Basin, Konya Closed Basin, Küre Mountains, Akyatan, Çıralı, Kaş, İğneada and the Susurluk Basin. As of 2025: over 100,000 supporters and more than 40 staff. THE TAX POINT, IF YOU ARE MOVING MONEY: it is registered with the Vakıflar Genel Müdürlüğü under registry number 3787 and holds vergi muafiyeti (tax exemption) granted by Council of Ministers decision no. 2009/15313 of 10 August 2009 — that Council-of-Ministers grant is the marker to check for any Turkish foundation before routing donations. Note the website takes individual transactions only; corporate requests go via info@wwf.org.tr.

trackers.name: Sivil Düşün — support for groups with no legal personality
trackers.desc: THE ONE THAT WILL TAKE YOU BEFORE YOU INCORPORATE. Alongside associations, foundations and unions, the EU's Sivil Düşün programme explicitly supports civic initiatives with no legal personality, networks, platforms and individual activists — so a residents' group formed last month to fight a development can apply in its own right, without first becoming a dernek or vakıf. That is rare anywhere. Support comes under 5 categories: events and meetings, organising, mobility and network-building, advocacy and campaigning, and communication. It takes applications from all 81 provinces and had supported 794 pieces of work at the time of this record. USE IT for the campaign phase — the advocacy and organising categories fit a land fight far better than a conservation grant would.

trackers.name: STGM — where Turkish grant calls are listed
trackers.desc: THE STANDING PLACE TO WATCH FOR MONEY. Sivil Toplum Geliştirme Merkezi announces open calls and publishes a guide to the grant programmes of 7 Turkish foundations that run them — Açık Toplum Vakfı, Bolu Bağışçılar Vakfı, Hayata Artı Vakfı, GençBank (TOG), Sabancı Vakfı, Türkiye Vodafone Vakfı and WWF-Türkiye, which runs its own grant programme as well as protecting land. STGM is also technical implementer for EU-funded civil society grant programmes, with the Central Finance and Contracts Unit (MFİB) as contracting authority. TWO THINGS TO CHECK BEFORE DRAFTING. EU programmes have run with Çevre ve Doğanın Korunması as a named thematic area — but sitting alongside children's, women's, disability and cultural rights, and requiring projects to cover at least 2 different thematic areas and build cooperation between CSOs from different fields, so a single-issue environmental project may need a partner from another sector to qualify. And Sivil Toplum için Destek Vakfı's programmes, open to associations, foundations and cooperatives established in Türkiye for work up to 12 months (an organisation supportable at most 2 years, reapplying each year), are aimed at social participation and the welfare of disadvantaged groups rather than conservation as such. TEMA Vakfı has separately hosted an environmental participation grant programme under ENV.net for advocacy and lobbying on the EU environmental acquis.

trackers.name: Tescil — apply to have an area registered as protected
trackers.desc: YOU CAN ASK FOR AN AREA TO BE REGISTERED. The Tabiat Varlıklarını Koruma Genel Müdürlüğü sets the procedures for determining, registering (tescil), approving and announcing natural assets, doğal sit alanları and special environmental protection zones, and fixes their boundaries — as it does for nature parks, nature monuments, nature conservation areas and wetlands. APPLICATION IS MADE TO THE GENERAL DIRECTORATE OR THE PROVINCIAL İL MÜDÜRLÜĞÜ, and the Directorate then carries out or commissions the research. The assessment team is specified by regulation: a city planner and landscape architect plus, according to the area, forest, agricultural, environmental, architectural or survey-cadastre engineers, hydrologists, biologists, zoologists and ecologists. THE PART THAT SAVES A COMMUNITY THE DECISIVE COST: for natural site areas the ecologically based scientific research report covering at least 4 seasons is commissioned by the General Directorate, not by the applicant — four seasons of survey is precisely the expense that defeats community groups elsewhere. NOTE THE SPLIT: national park boundaries are set by the forestry ministry and registered by Council of Ministers decision. Where natural, archaeological and urban site designations overlap on one property, a protocol of 01.10.2012 governs which rules apply.

trackers.name: Trampa — swap a building-banned parcel for Treasury land
trackers.desc: WHAT MAKES PROTECTION SURVIVABLE FOR THE OWNER. A regulation allows building-prohibited immovables left inside natural assets, doğal sit alanları and special environmental protection zones to be exchanged for Treasury (Hazine) land. The eligible applicant is defined as the owner of a separately owned property, all co-owners together where ownership is shared, and real or private-law legal persons wishing to transfer their closed or restricted-use property to the public. So an owner whose land has been made unbuildable by protection can seek land in exchange rather than absorb the loss — which is often what decides whether a designation is politically survivable locally. Apply through the provincial Çevre, Şehircilik ve İklim Değişikliği directorate. CHECK THE EXCLUSIONS FIRST: land not registrable in the Treasury's name; land that must be allocated to the forestry ministry because it falls inside a national park, nature park, nature monument or nature conservation area; land in agrarian reform application areas where exchange is not approved; and land under the Cultural and Natural Heritage Law where the ministry has not approved exchange.

trackers.name: Çevre Hukuku AĞı — legal support network for urban and environmental cases (Turkey)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Turkish network whose stated purposes include providing legal support to vulnerable groups in urban, environmental and climate cases, supporting strategic cases that change a law or a practice, and encouraging pro bono mechanisms for public-interest legal help. It is open not only to lawyers but to public administrators, engineers, archaeologists, planners, anthropologists and economists — which matters, because a mining or dam case needs a hydrologist and an archaeologist as much as an advocate, and this network is built to carry both. WHERE IT COMES FROM: it stands in a line running back to the Izmir bar association's environment commission and the Çevre Hareketi Avukatları who fought the Bergama cyanide gold mine for over twenty years, and to the Çevre ve Ekoloji Hareketi Avukatları formed in 2011. Its legal coordinator has published on standing and legal interest in urban and environmental cases for the Union of Turkish Bar Associations, on the ecosystem effects of small hydro schemes and the case types that follow, and on the legal problems of the Akkuyu agreement. THE SOBER PART, FROM THAT SAME HISTORY: at Bergama the Council of State ruled in 1997 that the cyanide mine was contrary to the public interest, and the company accelerated its operations instead of complying. Over twenty-two years of litigation the mine was closed twice, once for less than a day. Lawyers who worked that case have said publicly that the non-implementation of judgments is what exhausted the villagers. Turkish communities should go in knowing that a favourable judgment is a step, not an ending, and plan for enforcement from the start.

trackers.name: Doğa Derneği — can tell you your site is one of Turkey's 305 key areas
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Turkish conservation association based at Seferihisar near İzmir which holds the country's baseline biodiversity record and works to remove threats to specific species and sites. It compiled Turkey's inventory of Önemli Doğa Alanları — Key Nature Areas — completed in 2006, synthesising data on plants, dragonflies, butterflies, freshwater fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals, and identifying 305 such areas across the country. If your site is one of the 305, that is a national-level designation you can put in front of a governor, a court or a newspaper, and it exists already: nobody has to survey anything first. Ask them whether it is, and ask for the underlying record. WHAT ELSE IT OFFERS: it describes advocacy as its method for eliminating threats to a species or a habitat, and it runs volunteer bird monitoring that a local group can join — which is one of the cheapest ways for a community to start generating its own evidence about a site rather than waiting for someone else's. Membership is open, at a stated annual subscription, and it publishes a donor bill of rights setting out that you may ask questions and receive immediate, accurate and open answers about how your money will be used. WHAT IT IS NOT, AND THIS IS A GAP IN TURKEY: it does not buy land, and across this work I found no Turkish organisation that does. For a Turkish community the available allies are the environmental law network, TEMA, and bodies like this one that supply the science. If your case needs the ground taken off the market, that route does not appear to exist domestically and you should plan without it.

trackers.name: Sivil Toplum için Destek Vakfı — grants that reach very small associations (Turkey)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Support Foundation for Civil Society, a Turkish grant-maker to civil society organisations, running among other things a şartlı hibe — conditional grant — programme. Turkey had no funder at all in this file. THE EVIDENCE THAT IT REACHES THE RIGHT KIND OF ORGANISATION: it granted to DOĞÇEV, the Nature and Environment Protection and Preservation Association, which described using the grant to meet the feeding, health and care needs of the animals it looks after, to provide for the care of its forests, and to keep the association's activities running. AND THE SENTENCE THAT SHOWS WHY THIS MATTERS MORE IN TURKEY THAN ELSEWHERE, in that association's own words: organisations like it survive on the small contributions of a few concerned people, those contributions are meaningful but insufficient, and associations with no other income have to stand on donations — and when the subject is nature and animals, it gets harder still. A Turkish community group should expect to be funding itself from donations, and this is one of the few doors that opens onto anything else. WHAT TURKEY STILL DOES NOT HAVE, recorded honestly across four searches now: no conservation land buyer. Its other entries in this file are the organisation holding the 305 Key Nature Areas inventory and the environmental law network. This adds money. AND THE SECTOR IS LARGER THAN THE FILE SUGGESTS: alongside those, publicly listed Turkish environmental organisations include TEMA, which has planted across thousands of hectares and campaigns on erosion, desertification and land protection; ÇEKÜL, working on natural and cultural heritage across Anatolian cities through volunteer representatives and expert staff in the localities themselves; TÜRÇEK, founded in Istanbul in 1972 as one of Turkey's first voluntary environmental bodies; and TURMEPA on the seas and coasts. SOURCING NOTE: the grant and the association's account of it come from the foundation's own published interview; the wider sector names come from third-party Turkish directories and are given as leads to verify, not as filed entries.

trackers.name: ÇEKÜL Vakfı — volunteer representatives in the towns, and the city inventories
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a foundation established in 1990 to protect Turkey's natural, historical and cultural assets, at Ekrem Tur Sok. No 8, Beyoğlu 34435 Istanbul. Its own description is the reason it is here: a civil society organisation that Anatolian cities consult, are guided by and trust, working through its volunteer representatives and expert staff to meet demands for the protection of natural and cultural heritage. Its approach runs deliberately from the smallest settlement outward to the country as a whole. THE MOST USEFUL THING IT PRODUCES: kent envanterleri — city culture inventories — prepared with local authorities as usable databases of what a place actually holds. Inventories have been prepared in Adana, Amasya, Antalya, Battalgazi, Burdur, Gaziantep, Gümüşhane, Gürün, İzmir, Karaman, Kilis, Mardin, Muğla, Ordu, Tekirdağ and Uşak. They are held and continuously updated at the ÇEKÜL Information and Documentation Centre, which it describes as one of Turkey's most comprehensive reference centres for nature and culture, open to researchers. If your site is in one of those cities, the record of what is there may already exist and be public. That is the seventh country in this file where the answer to who already surveyed this is yes. HOW IT WORKS WITH COMMUNITIES AND COUNCILS: its stated method is bringing together experts from local authorities, civil organisations, professional chambers and universities to join a city's conservation process, turning what they find into books, inventories and maps, and helping each city build conservation plans suited to its own fabric and living practices. Its Çarşamba meetings at the ÇEKÜL house exist to give direction to ongoing conservation work in Anatolian cities and to build road maps for it, on a stated principle of public, local, civil and private working together. IT ALSO PLANTS: it continues afforestation work in cooperation with the General Directorate of Forestry to protect natural heritage and prevent deforestation. WHAT IT IS NOT: not a land buyer, not a funder and not a law firm. It is expertise, documentation, convening and local representation — which in a country with no conservation land buyer is what a community can actually get.

trackers.name: DKM — systematic conservation planning, and the coalition list of Turkey's sector
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: Doğa Koruma Merkezi, the Nature Conservation Centre, an IUCN member working for the conservation of nature throughout Türkiye. Formally established as a foundation in 2012, but the same team has been doing conservation work since 2004, first as a cooperative. Ankara-based. Its purpose is effective conservation of biodiversity and sustainable use of natural resources through scientific and integrated approaches, grounded in conservation biology, and it is explicit that conservation can only be achieved with the joint efforts of communities and institutions. WHAT IT CAN DO FOR A SITE: its work falls under five headings — biological diversity, soil and water, climate change, systematic conservation planning, and nature education. Systematic conservation planning is the discipline that answers which areas must be protected and why, in a form a ministry recognises. It has published a guide to biodiversity-focused ecosystem restoration after fire, a report on forest ecosystems and carbon sink management in the climate crisis, and a twenty-year activity report. It has been funded through the Forest Fires Emergency Support Fund run by the Sivil Toplum için Destek Vakfı already filed here — so the Turkish funder and this research body already work together. AND THE LIST THAT IS WORTH AS MUCH AS THE ENTRY: TEMA publishes the supporters of the Tabiat Kanunu İzleme Girişimi — the Nature Law Monitoring Initiative — which demanded a draft law be withdrawn, that nature's rights and international commitments be considered, and that any new law be prepared together with civil society. Its supporting organisations include Boğatepe Çevre ve Yaşam Derneği, Buğday, Doğa Derneği, DKM, Doğa ve Çevre Vakfı, Doğa ve Yaban Hayatı Koruma Derneği, WWF-Türkiye, Doğal ve Tarihi Değerleri Koruma Derneği, Ege Derneği and the Ekosistemi Koruma ve Doğa Sevenler Derneği, among others. That is a vetted directory of Turkey's environmental sector, published by one of its members.

trackers.name: WWF-Türkiye (Doğal Hayatı Koruma Vakfı) — a foundation that argues sites into protection
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: founded in 1975 as the Doğal Hayatı Koruma Derneği by a group of artists and intellectuals, it became a VAKIF — a foundation — in the 2000s and holds the WWF-Türkiye title. Turkey had TEMA, Doğa Derneği and DKM filed but no foundation of this kind; a vakıf is the Turkish legal form that can hold assets in perpetuity, which is the gap the acquirer sweep is chasing. WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES FOR A THREATENED SITE, from its own submission on one mountain: it prepares formal area proposals to the ministry arguing that a named place should become a protected area, resting them on its own completed scientific work — in that case the identification of the mountain as one of Turkey's 122 Important Plant Areas, its status as an Important Bird Area with breeding populations of bearded vulture and golden eagle, and the presence of species listed in Annex I of the Bern Convention. A community with a threatened site can bring it to a body that writes ministry submissions and already holds the national datasets to support one. THE NUMBERS IT ARGUES WITH: its own Korunan Alanlar report, and the global target agreed at the biodiversity convention to raise protected areas — it argues Turkey must rapidly increase its protected areas and secure better protection for them, and that creating new protected areas plus ecological corridors connecting them would be a historic step. HOW TO SUPPORT IT: regular giving, and a species-adoption scheme for special occasions.

trackers.name: Turquoise Coast Environment Fund — a coastal fund with an INCOME CEILING, not a floor
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a recurring grant programme, now in its sixth round, financing civil society organisations working on nature, biodiversity, marine and coastal protection in Turkey's southern and western coastal regions, including islands, coastal zones and wetlands. Turkey's bucket had one funder; this is a fund aimed squarely at coastal ground under development pressure. THE ELIGIBILITY RULE THAT INVERTS THE USUAL ONE: applicants must be associations, foundations, non-profit cooperatives, trade unions or federations established in Turkey, active in the field for at least one year, and — the unusual part — organisations whose income was BELOW 6,000,000 TL. An income CEILING means a small local group is the intended recipient, not a disadvantaged one; a related fund sets a band of 40,000 to 4,000,000 TL, and one earthquake-response fund applied no income limit at all. Read the income criterion before assuming you are too small — here, being small is the qualification. THE MONEY, AND WHAT IT HAS ACTUALLY FUNDED: at least 2,700,000 TL distributed per round, up to 700,000 TL per applicant. In one round seven organisations shared 2,067,830 TL — including a local environmental protection association awarded 290,830 TL for a river and delta environmental vision plan and awareness campaign, and a marine body funding a survey of marine biodiversity, pollution and invasive species along the Aegean coast. A vision plan for a named river is exactly the document a community needs and cannot afford. AND WHAT COMES WITH THE GRANT: the funder's programmes include work with mentors, subject-based expert support, volunteers from the private sector and capacity-building workshops — and its priorities name capacity to access accurate data and information in order to mobilise advocacy, network-building and protection action.

trackers.name: Turkey's environmental organisations, listed with what each one is for
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a published directory of Turkish environmental associations and foundations, each described by what it actually does and how to support it — the free artefact this file has found most useful in eighteen countries, and Turkey did not have one. WHO IS ON IT AND FOR WHAT: if the subject is birds, Doğa Derneği is where you go — Turkey's birds, wetlands and biological diversity are entrusted to them, and they direct conservation work by saying, WITH SCIENTIFIC DATA, 'THIS IS AN IMPORTANT NATURE AREA'. A body that can designate your site an Important Nature Area on published data is the one to bring your records to. Also listed: a marine and coastal organisation working since 1994 on the seas and shores that surround three sides of the country; TEMA, founded 1992, attending to erosion and desertification in a country losing 743 million tonnes of soil to erosion a year; and a heritage foundation and sustainability bodies. HOW TO SUPPORT THEM, in the directory's own terms: becoming a REGULAR DONOR secures the continuity of long-haul projects; buying from their online shops is also a support method; and for the bird body, joining their bird observation events or FIELD STUDIES, becoming a member or donating. Regular giving is what funds the long project; one-off giving funds the campaign.

trackers.name: Av. Orçun Akbulut — ÇED and mining-licence annulment, and the four laws the lawyer must know
trackers.desc: THE STRONGEST GROUNDS IN A ÇED ANNULMENT CASE, listed by a practice that runs them: the public participation process was carried out FORMALLY, without real participation being achieved — THIS ALONE CAN BE A GROUND FOR ANNULMENT; and specifically failure to announce the meeting, FAILURE TO NOTIFY THE VILLAGERS, missing minutes, and participation not being ensured. Also very strong, and frequent in the high court's decisions: the project's environmental effects were not assessed TOGETHER WITH EXISTING ACTIVITIES IN THE REGION — NO CUMULATIVE IMPACT ANALYSIS WAS DONE. Not being told, and not being counted alongside the mine already next door, are the two commonest ways these decisions fall. AND ITS OWN WARNING ABOUT WHO TO INSTRUCT: ÇED cases are not won with a standard petition — the lawyer must know administrative law, ZONING law, ENVIRONMENTAL law AND MINING law, and the work involves plan hierarchy, technical report examination, DIRECTING THE COURT EXPERT, site-visit strategy and use of high court precedent. Its mining practice works with geology, environment, agriculture and urbanism specialists, and in one case near an olive grove the operating permit looked lawful at first inspection — but independent technical reports prepared at the site-visit stage revealed the effects on underground water sources. File fast, it says, and the irreparable harm must be made concrete.

trackers.name: Turkish idare hukuku practices — an environmental dernek can sue on its statute alone
trackers.desc: WHO CAN BRING THE CASE, and it is the clearest statement of standing in the file: an ENVIRONMENTAL ASSOCIATION can bring an action to annul a positive ÇED decision permitting mineral exploration in an area with national park status — BECAUSE THE PURPOSE IN THE ASSOCIATION'S STATUTE IS TO PROTECT THE ENVIRONMENT, and that decision violates the collective interest the association represents. The object clause of your own statute is the standing — but the same practice draws the line: someone living in Antalya suing over a zoning change in Trabzon, with no personal connection at all, will have the case rejected for lack of capacity because there is no interest relationship. The required link is legitimate, personal and current, and it exists not only for direct addressees but for NEIGHBOURS INDIRECTLY AFFECTED by the act, and for rival traders operating in the same area. AND THE PRACTICAL SEQUENCE THESE FIRMS SET OUT: the general time limit is 60 DAYS; request SUSPENSION OF EXECUTION in the case petition itself, so it can be assessed without a separate application, requiring manifest unlawfulness and difficult-to-repair harm together; and after an annulment decision, bring a TAM YARGİ (full remedy) action for the damage suffered. One Istanbul office has worked in administrative law since 1992, covering annulment of building permits issued by municipalities, zoning plan changes, expropriation, and environmental impact assessments.

trackers.name: TEMA in the Danıştay — it sued to annul a law it judged unconstitutional
trackers.desc: THE LITIGATION, which is the part a community can ask for: assessing that a numbered law was contrary to the constitution, the foundation FILED A CASE IN THE COUNCIL OF STATE SEEKING THE ANNULMENT OF THE LAW. A national foundation that has taken a statute to the supreme administrative court is one that can be asked to challenge the instrument behind a local project, not merely to plant trees near it. AND THE ARGUMENT IT MADE, which transfers to any farmland-to-industry conversion: these lands must be used in accordance with their purpose. Otherwise, ESTABLISHING AN INDUSTRIAL FACILITY ON SOIL THAT SHOULD BE FARMED is a use of that soil outside its purpose. Such out-of-purpose land use is VERY WIDESPREAD throughout Turkey. To stop it, a campaign was launched in a named region for agricultural land to be used in accordance with its purpose, and the foundation argued that a numbered article of the Constitution should be reviewed and the law issued under it re-drafted — thereby also preventing the plundering of forests. AND ITS LOCAL STRUCTURE: TEMA volunteer representative offices are established, and TEMA clubs in universities; its volunteers work with the forestry ministry to meet the wishes of local people through the TEMA forests they establish there. It also runs a documentation and information centre whose archive is open to anyone who asks.

trackers.name: Sivil Sayfalar's hibe archive — every open Turkish grant call in one place
trackers.desc: WHAT IT CARRIES: a running archive of GRANT CALLS OPEN TO TURKISH CIVIL SOCIETY, each with its subject, its eligible region and its CLOSING DATE. Turkey had three funding entries filed. One page listing every open call is what stops a small association missing the round it could have won, and it costs nothing to watch. AND THE RANGE VISIBLE ON IT, which shows how much of this money is regional rather than national: a coastal environment fund for the SOUTHERN AND WESTERN COASTAL REGIONS, INCLUDING ISLANDS, COASTAL AREAS AND WETLANDS; a MICRO-GRANT programme for local organisations carrying out earthquake-focused work in FOUR NAMED PROVINCES; a human rights programme from a Norwegian committee aimed specifically at organisations in cities OTHER THAN the three largest; and a digital transformation fund run with a development bank. A fund that deliberately excludes the big cities is one a rural association is competing for against far fewer rivals — and this file has repeatedly found that the geography condition, not the theme, decides who wins. The archive also carries sub-grant programmes, where a larger project redistributes money in SECOND-CYCLE CALLS with extended deadlines.

trackers.name: The regional Doğa Koruma directorate — it EXPROPRIATES and takes usufruct FOR conservation
trackers.desc: WHAT THIS DIRECTORATE IS EMPOWERED TO DO, and it is the state body a Turkish community should be writing to: its published duties include CARRYING OUT THE WORK AND PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO THE ALLOCATION OR EXPROPRIATION of the necessary movable and IMMOVABLE PROPERTY, ITS RENTING, AND THE OBTAINING OF USUFRUCT RIGHTS. Turkey had one land-acquisition entry filed. A conservation directorate that can expropriate, rent or take a usufruct right over land is a public body with the power to acquire ground a community cannot buy — and asking it to use that power costs nothing. AND THE STEP BEFORE THAT, which is what a community can actually trigger: the directorate PREPARES A PROPOSAL REPORT IN ORDER TO BEGIN THE DECLARATION PROCESS, by carrying out or commissioning A SURVEY AND INVENTORY STUDY IN AREAS THAT NEED TO BE TAKEN UNDER PROTECTION. A survey and inventory study is the document that starts a designation, and this office is required to produce it. AND WHAT IT COVERS: NATIONAL PARKS, NATURE PARKS, NATURE CONSERVATION AREAS, NATURE MONUMENTS, WILDLIFE PROTECTION AND DEVELOPMENT AREAS and WETLANDS — planning, survey, inventory, projecting, implementation, maintenance and control. It also runs the permits and EASEMENT RIGHTS granted in protected areas, and the ALLOCATIONS AND TRANSFERS made there.

trackers.name: Kuzey Ormanları Araştırma Derneği — it organises in EVERY VILLAGE of a 2-million-hectare forest
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES FOR LOCAL PEOPLE, and it is the clearest statement of a support role in this file: the association tries to ORGANISE IN EVERY VILLAGE AND LOCALITY of the Northern Forests, and SUPPORTS THE CITIZENS, LOCAL ADMINISTRATORS, CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, PRODUCER COOPERATIVES AND FARMERS who are trying to protect the Northern Forests IN THE REGION WHERE THEY LIVE. An organisation whose stated job is backing whoever is already fighting locally is the first call for a Turkish village — not a body that arrives to run the campaign itself. AND WHAT IT BRINGS: it carries out MONITORING, EDUCATION AND RESEARCH activities and builds COMMON GROUNDS FOR THE MEETING OF KNOWLEDGE WITH ACTION, AND OF THE ACADEMY WITH NATURAL AND RURAL LIFE, as the product and the subject of a natural and rural area defence sustained FOR 10 YEARS. AND THE SCALE OF WHAT IT COVERS: the Northern Forests are a union of ecosystems lying within 12 NAMED PROVINCES, covering an area of close to 2 MILLION HECTARES, containing 30 IMPORTANT NATURE AREAS and bordering three seas and two strait ecosystems. Its monitoring reports are quantified: one quarterly report identified 573 instances of threat, destruction and defence covering drought, wildlife, fires, thermal power stations and mine pits. Regular donations of an amount the donor sets themselves are taken through a named platform.

trackers.name: DHKD — the association that got FOUR COASTLINES declared Special Environmental Protection Areas
trackers.desc: WHAT IT ACHIEVED, and it is the clearest record in this file of a Turkish organisation getting ground protected: the coasts of FOUR NAMED AREAS, of great importance as SEA TURTLE BREEDING GROUNDS, WERE DECLARED 'SPECIAL ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AREAS', and it took the endangered ANATOLIAN LEOPARD under protection. Four coastlines designated after one association's work is the outcome a Turkish community is asking for — and the body that did it is still there. AND THE STATUS IT HOLDS, which matters for what it can do: founded in 1975 and based in Istanbul, fifteen years after its foundation it gained, BY DECISION OF THE COUNCIL OF MINISTERS, THE STATUS OF AN ASSOCIATION WORKING FOR THE PUBLIC BENEFIT. Public-benefit status is a formal designation that changes how an association is treated — worth asking whether a local group can obtain it. AND THE METHOD IT USES, stated plainly: it carries out CONSERVATION PROJECTS; MAINTAINS LOBBYING ACTIVITIES SO THAT THE RELEVANT LAWS CAN BE APPLIED; and cooperates with the public, with LOCAL OR CENTRAL ADMINISTRATORS, AND WITH COMPANIES. Its IMPORTANT BIRD AREAS PROJECT ended with certain areas important for bird species BEING TAKEN UNDER PROTECTION and new such areas identified.

trackers.name: Türkiye Yaban Hayatı — volunteers who record what is happening, and name the top threat
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: a volunteer team who describe themselves as nature lovers who set out with an amateur spirit AND BECAME PROFESSIONAL IN THIS SUBJECT OVER TIME, working to protect our country's nature and wildlife and to equip people with real and correct information about living things. AND WHAT THEY NAME AS THE PRINCIPAL THREAT, which is the sentence that makes this a development-fight resource: thousands of unforgivable crimes are committed against wildlife and nature in our country. THE MOST FREQUENT OF THESE IS THE PLUNDERING OF FOREST LANDS AND THEIR OPENING TO CONSTRUCTION. The second named factor is POACHING, and they judge that these two elements harm nature more than human waste. A wildlife group that names forest land being opened to construction as the single commonest crime is an ally already framing the problem as a community would. AND WHAT THEY PRODUCE: we carry out research for the future, WE PUT THIS RESEARCH ON RECORD, and we strive to leave a treasury of information for our future — and they note that about 465 BIRD SPECIES can be observed within Turkey's borders. Support asked for is simply to share their information and writings, which are solely on education.

trackers.name: The four Turkish protection categories — what each one actually requires
trackers.desc: THE STATUTORY DEFINITIONS, and a community should pick its category from these words rather than asking for the grandest one: a MILLI PARK (national park) means natural pieces that, from a SCIENTIFIC AND AESTHETIC standpoint, hold NATURAL AND CULTURAL RESOURCE VALUES RARE NATIONALLY AND INTERNATIONALLY, together with conservation, rest and tourism areas. AND THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES CAN ACTUALLY WIN: a TABIAT PARKI (nature park) means natural pieces POSSESSING VEGETATION AND WILDLIFE CHARACTER, SUITABLE FOR THE REST AND RECREATION OF THE PUBLIC WITHIN THE INTEGRITY OF THE LANDSCAPE. Turkey had two land-acquisition entries filed. A nature park asks only for vegetation, wildlife, landscape integrity and public use — no claim of national rarity, which is why there are hundreds of them and a village can realistically propose one. AND THE OTHER TWO: a TABIAT ANITI (nature monument) is a piece possessing characteristics and SCIENTIFIC VALUE created by nature and natural events, protected under national-park principles; and a TABIATI KORUMA ALANI (nature conservation area) contains RARE, ENDANGERED OR VANISHING ECOSYSTEMS, SPECIES and outstanding examples, is ABSOLUTELY REQUIRED TO BE PROTECTED, and is set aside ONLY for science and education purposes. A single notable tree or rock formation can qualify as a nature monument, which is the smallest designation in the Turkish system.

trackers.name: A guide to WHICH Turkish body does what — and which one to approach for a site
trackers.desc: A DESCRIBED DIRECTORY RATHER THAN A LIST OF NAMES, which is what lets a Turkish community pick the right body first time. One national foundation, founded by artists and intellectuals in 1975, later became the domestic arm of an international conservation federation and now RUNS PROJECTS DIFFERING FROM ONE ANOTHER IN THE FIELDS OF SEAS, FRESH WATER, FORESTS, WILD LIFE, FOOD, CLIMATE AND ENERGY, working particularly on WETLANDS, FORESTS, SPECIES UNDER THREAT OF EXTINCTION AND SENSITIVE LIVING SPACES. Turkey had two acquisition entries against 34 total. Knowing which body works on wetlands and which on forests decides who will actually take your case — and it also names the one that ESTABLISHES COOPERATION WITH COMPANIES, which a community may want to avoid or to use. AND THE SOIL AND EROSION FOUNDATION, with the figure it argues from: it works SINCE 1992 to draw attention to erosion and desertification IN OUR COUNTRY, WHERE 743 MILLION TONNES OF SOIL A YEAR SUFFERS EROSION, and aims at THE PROTECTION OF ALL NATURAL ASSETS SUCH AS WATER, FOREST AND BIOLOGICAL DIVERSITY THAT MAKE UP THE ECOSYSTEM ALONG WITH THE SOIL, running AFFORESTATION PROJECTS, RURAL DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS AND PROJECTS COMBATING DESERTIFICATION. Rural development sits in the same body as afforestation, so a village can bring an economic case rather than only an ecological one.

trackers.name: Turkish environmental bodies by CAUSE — seas, soil, culture-and-nature together
trackers.desc: A SECOND DESCRIBED DIRECTORY, organised by what each body is for, so a community with a specific threat can find its match. The soil foundation's MAIN TARGET IS TO PROVIDE THE NECESSARY AWARENESS IN COMBATING THE DESERTIFICATION AND EROSION THAT THREATEN TURKEY, TO PROTECT THE SOIL, TO CARRY OUT AFFORESTATION, TO DEVELOP SOLUTION-FOCUSED PROJECTS AND TO PROTECT NATURAL ASSETS, and it LAID IMPORTANT FOUNDATIONS SO THAT ALL THESE EFFORTS WOULD TURN INTO A STATE POLICY. Turkey had two acquisition entries against 34 total. A body that has already turned its cause into state policy is one whose backing changes how an official reads your objection. AND THE ONE THAT REFUSES TO SEPARATE NATURE FROM HERITAGE, which matters where a threatened site is both: founded as a foundation in 1990, it works WITH THE AIM OF PROTECTING TURKEY'S NATURAL, HISTORICAL AND CULTURAL ASSETS, putting THE IMPORTANCE OF THE NATURE-CULTURE-HUMAN INTERACTION IN THE FIRST PLACE, under the slogan WE EXIST WITH NATURE AND CULTURE, and it has A CONSIDERABLE NUMBER OF VOLUNTEER REPRESENTATIVES in Anatolian towns. A site that is both a habitat and a heritage place has a body that will argue both at once. A fourth, founded 1996, works on ecological improvement and public awareness.

trackers.name: Baro adli yardım bürosu — free advocate, and seven days of silence is a refusal
trackers.desc: THE TRAP THAT ENDS CASES: IF THE BARO PRESIDENT DOES NOT DECIDE IN SEVEN DAYS, YOUR REQUEST COUNTS AS REFUSED. Under the Türkiye Barolar Birliği Adli Yardım Yönetmeliği, a rejected applicant may go — orally is enough — to the baro başkanı, who decides within seven days and whose decision is final; where no decision is made in time the request is deemed rejected. Silence is not a pending file. Diarise the seventh day. HOW TO APPLY: to the adli yardım bürosu, with form Ek-1, the signed undertaking at Ek-2 and the documents at Ek-3. WHERE TO APPLY IS NOT WHERE YOU LIVE — the regulation sends the request to the office of the place where the service will be performed, so if the quarry, the dam or the plan is in the next province, you apply to that province's baro, not your own. Assignments are then made from the province's advocates through TBB's electronic system on an equality basis, and in provinces with more than one baro a single combined list is used. SECOND TRAP, AND IT IS EXPENSIVE: adli yardım gets you a lawyer, not a free case. Court costs are a separate application to the court — adli müzaheret — and the regulation expressly contemplates the situation where adli müzaheret has been refused, in which case the applicant must put up the compulsory expense advance before the assigned advocate proceeds. Winning one does not give you the other; make both applications. CONTAMINATION TRAP LOGGED: baro.org.tr is not the Union of Turkish Bar Associations — it states on its own about page that it is an independent guide and not the official organ of TBB or of any provincial baro. The canonical domain is barobirlik.org.tr.

trackers.name: Çevre, Şehircilik ve İklim Değişikliği İl Müdürlükleri — the ÇED meeting is in your village, the decision is in Ankara
trackers.desc: SEND YOUR OBJECTION TO BOTH ADDRESSES, BECAUSE THE OFFICIAL WHO CHAIRS THE MEETING IS OFTEN NOT THE OFFICIAL WHO DECIDES. Under article 9 of the ÇED Yönetmeliği the proponent must hold a Halkın Bilgilendirilmesi ve Sürece Katılımı Toplantısı, at a date and time set by the Ministry, somewhere the public can easily reach; the provincial director chairs it in person, or an official they specifically designate does. Provincial notices state that questions, views and proposals may be sent within the ÇED process either to the Ministry's Çevresel Etki Değerlendirmesi Genel Müdürlüğü or to the Valilik. For ÇED Yönetmeliği Ek-1 projects, for Ek-2 projects where the provincial organisation has issued a “ÇED Gereklidir” decision, and for Ek-2 item 41 — hydroelectric plants of 1 to 10 MWm, which is the size band most Turkish river fights are fought in — the process itself is run centrally. Write to the province because that is where the file and the meeting record sit, and to Ankara because that is where the decision is taken. WHAT THE NOTICES GIVE YOU: the published announcements name the company, the installed megawatts, the hectares, the parcel and district, and the venue and hour of the meeting, which is the earliest hard information most communities get. WHERE TO LOOK: each province publishes its own at a subdomain of csb.gov.tr — verified for izmir.csb.gov.tr and bursa.csb.gov.tr. Use the directory rather than guessing the string for your province; a guessed subdomain that happens to resolve is worse than a click. Note also that this ministry is the developer in some fights, running Kentsel Dönüşüm and Millet Bahçesi programmes on the ground it also regulates.

trackers.name: Doğa Derneği — holds the ÖDA inventory, the one document Turkish nature lawyers actually cite
trackers.desc: FIRST QUESTION FOR ANY TURKISH SITE: IS IT ONE OF THE 305? Between 2004 and 2006 Doğa Derneği coordinated Turkey's Önemli Doğa Alanları inventory with more than forty academics and a range of conservation bodies, synthesising data on eight groups — plants, dragonflies, butterflies, freshwater fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals — and identified 305 Key Nature Areas, published as a book in 2006. THE REASON THIS IS A RESOURCE AND NOT A BOOKSHELF: the association records that the inventory is still used widely by nature conservationists and by nature lawyers, and that it remains Turkey's first and only book of its kind. If your valley is inside a listed ÖDA you are not asserting that the place is important, you are citing a published national inventory built to a standard the IUCN adopted — the ÖDA method, first designed in 2004 by an international team working from BirdLife's Important Bird Area work, was taken up by IUCN at the 2016 World Conservation Congress in Hawaii as the international standard for identifying priority areas. The inventory is being updated against the newer IUCN criteria after seventeen years, so check whether your area's entry has moved. WHAT ELSE IT HOLDS: eKuşBank, the bird observation recording system it established in 2004, which is where the observation record for a site may already exist. Founded in İzmir in 2002. It works through partnership with municipalities and village associations rather than acting alone — its Seferihisar Doğa Okulu was built with Seferihisar Belediyesi and the Orhanlı Köyü Derneği — so bring your muhtar or your council. THE SOBERING CASE TO READ FIRST IS MARMARA GÖLÜ: registered in 2017 as a Wetland of National Importance and dried completely over the following years under water policy and badly planned projects. A designation is evidence, not protection. DOMAIN WARNING: a staging build of this site is live at dev.dogadernegi.org and carries much of the same content. Use dogadernegi.org.

trackers.name: Vakıflar Genel Müdürlüğü — dedicated foundation land cannot be seized, and misuse gets the occupier evicted
trackers.desc: THE ENFORCEMENT ROUTE FIRST, BECAUSE ALMOST NOBODY USES IT: allocated foundation property may not be used for a commercial activity, and where use contrary to the allocation is established, the immovable is evicted by the civil administration of the place on the General Directorate's request. If a development is operating commercially on land allocated to a vakıf purpose, that is not merely a planning complaint — it is a route to eviction with a named actor at the end of it. Report it to your Vakıflar Bölge Müdürlüğü, whose telephone and address are published on vgm.gov.tr. Related protection: hayrat immovables of foundations cannot be attached or pledged, which puts them beyond ordinary creditor enforcement. THE TRAP, AND IT DEMOLISHES THE COMFORTABLE ASSUMPTION THAT VAKIF LAND IS SAFE FOREVER: foundation land can be sold. Where the conditions in article 12 of Law 5737 are met, akar-type foundation immovables are sold following a regional directorate proposal, the General Directorate's concurrence and a final decision of the Vakıflar Meclisi — to public bodies by agreement under article 30 of expropriation law 2942/4650, and to private persons and companies by tender under State Tender Law 2886. Hayrat-type immovables can go the same way under article 15 where they can no longer serve their purpose. THAT SAME RULE IS ALSO YOUR EARLY WARNING SYSTEM: the tender announcements are published in the Official Gazette, in local newspapers, on the notice boards of the Vakıflar Bölge Müdürlükleri and on vgm.gov.tr. Watching them tells you which foundation land is about to change hands before anything is built on it. AND THE ROUTE THAT ACTUALLY TAKES LAND OUT OF THE MARKET: you can establish a vakıf, or give land to one. The General Directorate publishes each year the minimum asset that must be dedicated to a new foundation's purposes, under article 5 of Law 5737 and article 111 of the Foundations Regulation, so the threshold for the coming year is a published figure rather than a guess; where the dedicated asset is immovable it is registered in the foundation's name. The tax position is the part to put to a landowner: immovables donated to a foundation, at establishment or afterwards, are exempt from inheritance and transfer tax, and expenditure, donations and sponsorship for the upkeep, repair, restoration, landscaping and even expropriation of registered foundation cultural assets, carried out under the General Directorate's control, are deducted in full from the income and corporation tax base. ONE THING TO CHECK BEFORE RELYING ON A FOUNDATION'S OWN MANAGERS: a mülhak foundation left without an appointed manager for ten years is taken over by the General Directorate by court decision and becomes mazbut, after which no manager may ever be elected again — beneficiaries' usufruct rights under the foundation deed survive, but control does not. Switchboard +90 312 415 50 00.

trackers.name: Koruma Bölge Kurulları — registration puts a construction ban on the parcel and an annotation on the title deed
trackers.desc: THIS IS THE HARDEST STOP AVAILABLE ON A TURKISH SITE, AND IT TURNS ON A DETERMINATION THAT THE COUNCIL ITSELF MAKES. Findings about immovable cultural and natural assets requiring protection are registered by decision of a regional conservation council, and once that happens, contrary to those decisions and the High Council's principle decisions, no constructional or physical intervention may be made on the asset, its protection area or the site, they may not be reopened to use, and their use may not be changed. That is a prohibition on building, not a consultation. AND IT FOLLOWS THE LAND, NOT THE OWNER: the registration is entered directly in the declarations column of the title register by the land registry directorate, on the letter of the vali where the parcel is in a provincial central district or of the kaymakam elsewhere, or on the council's own notification, recording the parcel as an immovable cultural asset requiring protection, a protection area, or a site, with the conservation group stated. A buyer cannot claim not to have known. THE ARGUMENT MOST WORTH MAKING IS ABOUT THE BUFFER, NOT THE BUILDING. Deciding the protection area, and deciding whether construction and installation may take place inside it, belongs to the councils — and the regulation defines that area as the land considered to affect the registered immovable in silhouette, appearance and similar respects, sufficient to preserve the asset's appearance and its harmony with its surroundings. A tall or bulky scheme beside a registered asset is therefore attackable on visual impact, on the face of the criterion, without needing to touch the asset itself. THE PRACTICAL ROUTE: the ministry publishes the current list of the regional councils on the Directorate General for Cultural Heritage and Museums website, so find the council covering your province from that list rather than guessing; the same site publishes the councils' registration decisions, which is where to read how comparable sites were argued. Registration decisions for sites, natural assets and individually registered immovables whose owners cannot be identified are published in the Resmî Gazete and announced on the ministry's website for one month. Where an owner applies, grouping of a registered asset is done by the council within three months. THE ROUTE NOBODY ASKS ABOUT: public institutions, municipalities, provincial special administrations and local authority unions may expropriate registered immovable cultural assets, provided they are used in the function the conservation council determines — so where a sympathetic municipality exists, buying the owner out for a council-approved function is a real option rather than a theoretical one. CHECK WHICH BODY COVERS YOUR SITE TYPE BEFORE YOU FILE: responsibility for natural sites and natural assets was moved away from the culture ministry to the environment ministry's own conservation commissions, so a purely natural site may belong to a different council from a cultural one, and this entry does not establish the current division. Ask the regional council which one takes your application.

trackers.name: Doğa Koruma Merkezi — the outfit that maps which areas are conservation priorities, and will do it for your area
trackers.desc: WHAT THIS ORGANISATION CAN GIVE A CAMPAIGN IS A PRIORITY MAP THAT SOMEONE ELSE MADE. DKM brought Systematic Conservation Planning to Türkiye and has applied it across the Mediterranean, South-Eastern Anatolia, Black Sea and Aegean regions, the Lower Caucasus and the Anatolian Diagonal — the method exists to identify, from data rather than from argument, which areas must be conserved to hold a region's biodiversity. If your valley falls inside one of those analyses, the case that it matters has already been made by a body with standing, and you are citing rather than asserting. Ask them what their planning outputs say about your area before commissioning anything. WHAT ELSE IT HOLDS THAT IS DIRECTLY CITABLE: the Red Book of Butterflies of Türkiye, practitioner and planner guides for integrating biodiversity into forest management plans, and a post-fire guide to biodiversity-focused ecosystem restoration — the last matters because burnt ground is routinely reclassified and rebuilt, and a published restoration standard is what an objection to that needs. It also completed monitoring of how Mediterranean forest and maquis recovered after the fires, funded through a wildfire emergency fund. WHO: a foundation based in Ankara, operating since 2004 and formally constituted in 2012, IUCN member, part of Butterfly Conservation Europe and Climate Action Network Europe. THE HONEST LIMIT, AND IT IS THE SAME TEST THIS FILE APPLIED WHEN DECLINING A COMPARABLE BODY IN GEORGIA: no community-facing programme was found. DKM's published partners are the General Directorate of Forestry and the General Directorate of Nature Conservation and National Parks, and it describes developing alternatives to classical conservation in coordination with public and private sector partners — which is the language of an institutional adviser, not a campaigner. It is recorded here as a supplier of evidence and planning, on the same footing as ACBK in Kazakhstan and NACRES in Georgia, and not as a body that will oppose a project for you. For that in Türkiye, this file already carries Çevre Hukuku Ağı for lawyers and Doğa Derneği for the Key Nature Areas inventory.

trackers.name: Yeşil Artvin Derneği — took a mining licence to court with the provincial bar association and had it revoked outright
trackers.desc: THE THING TO COPY IS WHO THEY BROUGHT WITH THEM: the association went to court in 2005 TOGETHER WITH THE ARTVIN BAR ASSOCIATION to seek revocation of the Cerattepe mining licence. Operations were suspended in July 2005, the licence was revoked outright in October 2008, the company blockaded its tunnel and left, and the revocation was upheld by the Council of State. A provincial bar association joining as co-claimant is a different proposition from a village hiring a lawyer — it brings standing, institutional weight and counsel at once, and every Turkish province has one. Ask your baro to join, not merely to represent. THE SECOND TACTIC, ALSO DOCUMENTED: mass co-claimants. On 26 September 2013, 281 people filed to annul the environmental impact decision. Earlier, roughly ten thousand signatures were gathered and taken to Ankara by bus to be handed to the environment minister in person. AND THE PART THAT MUST BE READ ALONGSIDE THE WIN, BECAUSE THIS FILE WILL NOT SELL A VICTORY THAT DID NOT HOLD: they lost the second round. After the licence areas were retendered, a ten-thousand-strong demonstration in April 2013, sit-ins from May 2013 and a watch that ran continuously for 245 days were ended by police using tear gas and rubber bullets, with six people detained; mining companies now work the site. A revoked licence can be reissued under a new tender, and the association's own framing is that the fight did not end with the court win. WHAT THEY DO NOW, WHICH IS WHY THEY ARE A RESOURCE RATHER THAN A CASE STUDY: continuous work across Cerattepe, Yukarı Maden Köyü, Cankurtaran, Arhavi, Şavşat, Murgul, Yusufeli and Maçahel against mining, hydro and wind projects and forest clearance — site inspections, scientific reports prepared with academics, and litigation that has produced decisions at the Constitutional Court as well as the administrative courts. They also inspect and publish: after examining the Hod mine site they warned publicly that stream beds were being filled with waste rock, raising landslide and pollution risk. Chaired by Nur Neşe Karahan, with a board that includes the association's own lawyer. Contact info@yesilartvindernegi.org, telephone +90 466 212 70 80, Atatürk Caddesi, Artvin centre. SAFETY CONTEXT, STATED BECAUSE IT CHANGES WHAT IS SAFE TO DO: this association is listed on a human rights defenders platform, describes itself as having spent a year under heavy pressure, and its members have faced prosecution — in one instance for occupying forest land over a wooden watch hut built by the community. Expect the counter-suit as part of the terrain.

trackers.name: Sivil Toplum için Destek Vakfı — its project grant programme takes applications at any time, and the second year is where the match bites
trackers.desc: THE PROJECT GRANT PROGRAMME HAS NO APPLICATION WINDOW — organisations may apply whenever they like, and applications are considered at board meetings held roughly every two months. For a campaign that cannot time its need to a funding round, that is the whole point of this foundation. THE TRAP IS IN YEAR TWO, AND YOU SHOULD BUDGET FOR IT BEFORE YOU APPLY IN YEAR ONE: no co-financing is required on a first application, but where an organisation was supported by one of the foundation's programmes the previous year, a second-year application in the same frame carries an expected in-kind or cash match equal to the grant requested. Plan the match a year ahead or the follow-on will not happen. WHAT THE APPLICATION WANTS, so you can prepare it: the completed project programme form, detailed CVs for the two people who would be first-degree responsible for the work, a one-year budget for the organisational development you are proposing showing what you are asking the foundation for, and a detailed timetable. Downloadable form versions are published so you can draft offline. ONE BUDGET RULE THAT CATCHES COALITIONS: giving grants onward to third parties, cash support and scholarships are not eligible budget lines — you cannot use a grant to fund the smaller groups around you, though you can budget for the staff needed to run such support. Keep invoices for three years; the foundation may require a financial audit. Applications are assessed with independent experts, the advisory board, foundation members and the board. Contact kurumsal@siviltoplumdestek.org. THE HONEST LIMIT, AND IT IS SIGNIFICANT FOR THIS MAP: there is no standing environmental or land-defence fund here.
