trackers.name: Information & Data Protection Commissioner (IDPC)
trackers.desc: Information & Data Protection Commissioner (IDPC) — Malta’s national data-protection / information authority, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Parliamentary Ombudsman of Malta
trackers.desc: Malta’s Parliamentary Ombudsman, investigating complaints against public bodies and monitoring places of detention.

trackers.name: Din l-Art Ħelwa — National Trust of Malta
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the National Trust of Malta, founded 1965, which does two things a community needs. It holds around seventeen sites under Deeds of Guardianship with the government or in trust from the ecclesiastical authorities, restoring and opening them — so it can take on a threatened site. And its Heritage and Environment Protection sub-committee reads the list of planning applications published WEEKLY IN THE GOVERNMENT GAZETTE, which is how you find out at all, and files objections at scale: 1,500 in one year against 9,599 applications. It built DLHAlert so the public can follow objections. WHO IT SUITS: everyone in Malta and Gozo, but understand the ladder before you climb it. Objecting is cheap; appealing is not. By its own account an appeal costs €200 to €1,000, needs a written case citing the policies and legislation, and runs to three or four sittings with photomontages, surveys, drawing analysis and expert affidavits, all rebutted and then defended in person — with a court appeal beyond that. It is volunteer-run with professionals acting pro bono, so it prioritises hard, and it cannot appeal everything it objects to. A GUARDIANSHIP DEED DOES NOT REQUIRE ANYONE TO BUY THE LAND: at Manoel Island a deed was signed between the developer and the Gżira Local Council, establishing a non-profit foundation to ensure heritage buildings, foreshore and significant green park spaces are restored and preserved for the whole community — so a local council can be a party to it, and the developer can be bound by it. AND NGOs CAN HOLD HALF THE BOARD OF A NATIONAL PARK: Il-Majjistral Nature & History Park is run by a federation of Din l-Art Ħelwa, Nature Trust (Malta) and the Gaia Foundation, with three NGO representatives, three public-sector representatives and a chairperson — a precedent to cite wherever a community is told park management must rest with government.

trackers.name: Malta Business Registry
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: National Audit Office
trackers.desc: National — National Audit Office of Malta. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Malta.

trackers.name: Malta Business Registry
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Access restricted to authorities/obliged entities.

trackers.name: Daphne Caruana Galizia Foundation
trackers.desc: Foundation continuing the anti-corruption and money-laundering investigations of assassinated journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia, and pressing for justice and rule of law in Malta.

trackers.name: ePPS eTenders
trackers.desc: National public-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Malta, and for how much.

trackers.name: National Statistics Office
trackers.desc: Malta's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Malta.

trackers.name: Malta Environment Foundation — no deadline, and first-timers are preferred
trackers.desc: A FUND THAT ACTIVELY PREFERS GROUPS THAT HAVE NEVER BEEN FUNDED. Priority is given to grassroots NGOs who have not received funding from MEF before — the same newcomer preference this map records for Seoul and Malaysia, and the opposite of the track-record gates in India and Ireland. If you have never been funded, say so; it counts in your favour. AND THERE IS NO DEADLINE RACE: the call remains open for the foreseeable future, with 3–4 steering committee meetings a year at which applications are reviewed — so submit when ready and expect a decision at the next committee. TWO CONCRETE GATES: you must be a voluntary organisation registered with the Office of the Commissioner for Voluntary Organisations (OCVO) with a strong environmental focus, and hold an active account with a local bank. WHAT THEY SELECT FOR: measurable and sustainable long-term results, capacity building, participation by the local community, and projects sufficiently visible to leverage additional support from other funders — visibility is a stated selection factor, so design for it. Training, equipment and facilitation are fundable, not only activity. OBLIGATIONS: interim and final reports, possible site visits, and participation in evaluation questionnaires and focus group discussions.

trackers.name: VO Funding Portal — including a scheme that pays your EU co-financing
trackers.desc: ONE PLACE LISTING THE SCHEMES OPEN TO MALTESE VOLUNTARY ORGANISATIONS — and it contains the answer to a barrier this map records again and again. Alongside the Sustainable Development Fund (grants to non-profit organisations for environmental, social and economic sustainability aligned to the SDGs, capped at EUR 10,000 per project and covering up to 80 percent of eligible costs — so budget the other 20 percent), the portal lists a scheme intended to support the co-financing obligations of voluntary organisations benefitting from EU institutions funding. If an EU grant requires a match you cannot raise, there is a national scheme aimed precisely at that gap — which is worth checking for in other member states too. Also listed: training and capacity-building schemes, and the Voluntary Organisations Project Scheme run by the Malta Council for the Voluntary Sector. FOR LARGER AMBITION: EU LIFE action grants are open to private non-commercial organisations including NGOs registered in the EU, and NGO Framework Partnership Agreements support operating grants co-financing NGOs' operating costs where they pursue an aim of general Union interest and are primarily active in environment or climate action.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Flimkien għal Ambjent Aħjar (FAA) — joins residents' planning objections (Malta)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Maltese non-profit working since 2006 across Malta and Gozo, whose listed methods include campaigns and planning objections alongside heritage tours and community events. Its pattern is to join residents already objecting to a specific application rather than run separate campaigns — recent examples on its channels include supporting residents of a two-metre-wide Valletta alley against a joinery workshop beneath their homes, and joining objections to a townhouse conversion inside Attard's urban conservation area. It maintains a contact route specifically for environment and planning concerns, separate from general enquiries. THE CASE IT PUBLISHES THAT EVERY MALTESE OBJECTOR SHOULD READ FIRST: application PA 03552/15, a six-storey addition on a house that had been certified unstable, was recommended for refusal by the Planning Authority's own case officer, by the Sanitary Officer and by the Cultural Heritage Officer — and was approved anyway. The refusal grounds turned on sanitary law limiting building height in narrow streets to preserve light and air. A case officer's recommendation to refuse is not the decision. A community that hears its objection has been accepted by the case officer should treat that as the halfway point, not the end. HOW IT PAYS FOR ITSELF, WHICH IS ALSO HOW YOU HELP: it runs heritage tours, gardening workshops and lectures, and states that ticket sales fund the campaigns. Turning up to an event is a concrete way for a community with no money to contribute to the body objecting on its behalf. IT COMPLEMENTS RATHER THAN REPEATS: Malta's other ally in this file holds sites under guardianship deeds. This one contests applications. Different fights, different phone calls.

trackers.name: Nature Trust – FEE Malta — manages the protected sites, and fronts the joint demands
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: a non-profit environmental NGO founded in 1962, one of the oldest in the Maltese Islands, voluntary organisation VO0048, a privileged partner of WWF and the Maltese coordinator for the Foundation for Environmental Education. Its own statement of purpose is conservation, managing areas of natural and scientific interest, and lobbying for effective environmental legislation. WHAT IT ACTUALLY HOLDS, WHICH IS THE POINT FOR A COMMUNITY: it manages or is taking on a list of named sites — Wied Għollieqa Nature Reserve, Xrobb l-Għagħin Nature Park, il-Ballut Natura 2000 at Marsaxlokk, il-Magħluq Natura 2000 at Marsascala, Pembroke garigue Natura 2000, Fiddien and Chadwick Lakes, Ħirkewwa Marine Park, Simar Nature Reserve at Xemxija, Foresta 2000 near Mellieħa, and Majjistral Nature and History Park jointly with others. If a threatened Maltese site adjoins or resembles one of these, there is an organisation with management experience of that exact habitat and a track record the authorities already recognise. Simar is a degraded wetland it restored into a Ramsar site of international importance — useful precedent when a developer argues ground is too far gone to be worth protecting. AND IT ORGANISES THE OTHERS: it has fronted joint environmental demands to the political parties, endorsed by Extinction Rebellion Malta, Għawdix, Moviment Graffitti, Rota, the Grow 10 Trees Project, Wirt Għawdex and Żminijietna. That is the third confirmation in this file that small-island cases move when organisations sign together — the same pattern as the two Cypriot Akamas letters. Ask who else will sign. IT NAMES THE THREATS ITSELF: urban development and land reclamation head its own list, alongside illegal hunting, littering, water scarcity and climate impacts. WHAT IT IS NOT: not a land buyer and not a law firm. Malta's other entries here are the guardianship-deeds body and the objections body; this is the site manager and the convenor.

trackers.name: Moviment Graffitti — publishes the objection template and the deadline (Malta)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Maltese organisation set up in 1994 at 67 Strait Street, Valletta, info@movimentgraffitti.org, active against the exploitation of people, the environment and animals. It states that it is autonomous from any economic power or political party, has no hierarchies, and welcomes new members as activists or supporting members. In a two-party island that independence is the first thing a residents' group should check, and it is stated outright. WHAT IT DOES ON A LIVE APPLICATION, WHICH IS AS PRACTICAL AS THIS FILE GETS: on a proposed lido reclaiming land from the sea it published the objection address, the deadline, and the application number to cite — and put an objection template on its own channels so any resident could send one. Nothing else in this file combines the site, the reference number, the closing date and the ready text in one place. IT ALSO PAYS FOR APPEALS: it launched a crowdfunding campaign to appeal a permit for uprooting 800 trees and heavy construction on the Comino Nature Reserve, publishing its bank account and IBAN, and asked the public to leave contact details through a dedicated form so further action could be organised. A community facing an appeal it cannot fund has a working precedent for raising the money publicly. AND IT WORKS ACROSS THE PARTY LINE: it helped set up Kamp Emergenza Ambjent, took a lead in the campaign for coastal access at Manoel Island in alliance with a Labour-led council, and teamed up with a Nationalist-led St Julian's council and a Labour-led Pembroke council to oppose a project on land granted by government to a developer. Two councils of opposing parties on the same objection is the strongest local configuration available in Malta, and it has assembled it. WHAT IT IS: direct actions, protests, coalitions and awareness work — not a law firm, not a land buyer, not a funder for others. Its own framing is that development should be judged by its effect on people's lives rather than carried out for its own sake.

trackers.name: BirdLife Malta — publishes its objections by application number, and it stopped a road in 1966
trackers.desc: WHY THIS FILLS A HOLE: Malta's bucket held the National Trust, Nature Trust, Moviment Graffitti and FAA. What it lacked was the body that does the species science and publishes its objection texts. THE POLICY PAGE IS THE RESOURCE: it lists BirdLife Malta's objections and submissions with the planning application numbers attached — an objection to a residential block of 18 apartments and 21 garages within the buffer zone of Simar Nature Reserve (PA/05846/24), an objection to works in Wied Għomor (PA/06798/24), recommendations for the EIA terms of reference of a waste management facility, comments on an EIA for a school, feedback on a local plan review, and comments on conservation objectives and measures. A Maltese objector can read a published, professional objection against a comparable application before writing their own. Note the first item: a reserve buffer zone did not stop an application being made. THE PRECEDENT: established 1962, Malta's oldest environmental organisation. Its first success, in 1966, was stopping the building of a proposed road through the heart of the Għadira wetland — now one of its own nature reserves. Its own conclusion from that: birds could not be protected without protecting their habitats. Sixty years of Maltese planning objections start there. WHAT IT HOLDS AND RUNS: four nature reserves — Salina, Simar, Għadira and Foresta 2000, the last created by planting over 20,000 trees. Simar opened in 1995 on a marshy patch of neglected land, is managed by BirdLife Malta volunteers on behalf of the government, and more than 180 bird species have been recorded there. Salina is described as the latest land management project entrusted to it. Land management by delegation, not purchase — the instrument for a country with almost no land to buy. IT ALSO ENFORCES: its conservation team reported an unregistered finch-trapping site to the police, officers confiscated equipment and live finches, and the case concluded with a 1,200 euro fine and a three-year suspension of the trapping licence. It has run night surveillance with the Malta Ranger Unit. And its campaigning produced Malta's first eight marine Special Protection Areas, the strict reserve on Filfla and the bird sanctuary on Comino.

trackers.name: Malta's four funding routes for voluntary organisations — and enrolment is the gate to all of them
trackers.desc: THE GATE FIRST, BECAUSE EVERY ROUTE SHARES IT: applicants must be a voluntary organisation enrolled and fully compliant with the Office of the Commissioner for the Voluntary Sector by the application closing date, with no outstanding projects from previous years. Malta's bucket had Nature Trust, Din l-Art Ħelwa and BirdLife but no money; this is the money, and enrolment is the precondition. THE FOUR ROUTES. (1) The Environment Fund — financial support to voluntary organisations engaged in environmental conservation and its promotion, to incentivise further environmentally-beneficial volunteering project proposals. (2) The Sustainable Development Fund Support Scheme for Voluntary Organisations, run by the environment ministry for non-government not-for-profit organisations to undertake tangible sustainable development projects. (3) VOPS, the Voluntary Organisations Project Scheme, administered by the Malta Council for the Voluntary Sector — total budget 800,000 euro, grants from 4,000 to 20,000 euro depending on the action, 12-month implementation, with proposals required to be innovative and not a repeat of previously approved projects by the same organisation, sustainable for at least three years, and only one application per organisation per call. (4) The LIFE Projects Co-Financing Grant, which provides the national co-financing contribution for projects eligible under the EU LIFE programme — the piece that usually stops a small organisation bidding for LIFE at all. AND A NON-STATE ROUTE WORTH THE SAME ATTENTION: the Malta Environment Foundation offers grants of up to 10,000 euro to grassroots environmental organisations for conservation, sustainability and ecosystem regeneration, with priority given to first-time applicants. PRACTICAL: the MCVS runs three Volunteer Centres — Valletta, Rabat and Xewkija in Gozo — providing space and facilities from which voluntary organisations can operate, and a Small Initiatives Scheme for small community projects. A youth activism scheme names organisations in the field of the environment and animal welfare as eligible.

trackers.name: Vincent Micallef and Associates — files objections against a proposed OR EXISTING development
trackers.desc: WHY THIS FIRM: most Maltese planning practices sell appeals for refused applicants. This one lists the objector's side explicitly. Its stated services include submission of objections against a proposed OR AN EXISTING development; submission of requests for reconsideration, appeals to the Tribunal, and appeals to the Court of Appeal; and submission, representation and procedures before the PA, the Environment and Planning Review Tribunal and the Courts of Justice. An objection against an EXISTING development is the rarer service — most of this file records routes that close once something is built. Malta's bucket had four funders, the voluntary-sector enrolment route and no litigator; this is one.

trackers.name: Malta's EPRT — where juridical interest does not apply to environmental appeals
trackers.desc: THE BODY: the Environment and Planning Review Tribunal, now governed by its own Act (Chapter 551 of the Laws of Malta), reviews decisions of the Planning Authority and the Environment and Resources Authority, examining both the legality and the facts behind them. It was set up to provide more effective and accessible access to justice in cases relating to the environment specifically, and originally sat as three members — one versed in environment or development planning presiding, a lawyer and an architect. THE STANDING POINT, AND IT IS UNUSUAL: on environment matters the Tribunal's jurisdiction has grown to cover any decision taken by the Environment and Resources Authority, and it is specified that THE DOCTRINE OF JURIDICAL INTEREST PERTAINING TO LEGAL STANDING DOES NOT APPLY TO SUCH APPEALS. You do not have to prove a personal legal interest to appeal an environmental decision in Malta — the only country in this file where the standing requirement is expressly switched off. THE DEADLINE, AND THE TRAP IN IT: appeals must be made within 30 days from publication of the decision notification in the press; where a request for reconsideration was made within that limit, the 30 days start when the Authority's reply on the reconsideration is received. AND WHAT THE 2025 PERMITTING RULES CHANGED: decisions are published on the ERA website, a wider range of activities is now subject to public comment and representation, ERA decisions on more significant applications are taken in public sessions with documents online via the ERIS portal, and members of the public and NGOs can follow live applications and in some cases appeal. But transitional authorisations are expressly EXCLUDED FROM THIRD-PARTY APPEAL, a point raised during the public consultation — operators newly regulated may run for up to four years under cover you cannot challenge.

trackers.name: The Maltese deed of guardianship — NGOs given legal care of named sites, including new ones
trackers.desc: THE INSTRUMENT: after a Neolithic temple was damaged in 2001, campaigning produced the Cultural Heritage Act of 2002, which introduced a national heritage regulator AND GRANTED NGOs THE LEGAL RIGHT TO CARE FOR HERITAGE SITES. Seventeen properties are now held in Din l-Art Ħelwa's guardianship, from medieval chapels and coastal fortifications to a lighthouse and burial grounds. Malta had no land-holding body filed; guardianship is how land is held there. AND IT IS STILL BEING USED: new guardianship deeds have been signed with three environmental NGOs for the conservation and protection of three natural areas — two in Malta and one in Comino. Friends of the Earth Malta took a 14,400 square metre plot in Comino and a building; Din l-Art Ħelwa took 670 square metres in the National Park at Ta' Qali; and Fondazzjoni Rurali Manikata took a 4,022 square metre site with several small buildings. A local rural foundation holding a deed alongside two national NGOs is the model a village group should ask about. WHAT THE HOLDER DOES BESIDES HOLD: Din l-Art Ħelwa reviews around 750 development applications each year and challenges proposals that threaten traditional streetscapes, coastal areas and countryside; has saved 40 national sites with funds raised entirely from donations, sponsorship and fundraising; and helped establish Foresta 2000 and Il-Majjistral Nature and History Park. Its work is entirely voluntary.

trackers.name: Nature Trust — FEE Malta — it manages the Natura 2000 sites themselves
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a non-profit environmental NGO founded in 1962 that is active in the managing of ecologically important sites in the Maltese Islands, including Pembroke Natura 2000, Wied Għollieqa Nature Reserve, Il-Magħluq Natura 2000, Il-Ballut Natura 2000 and Xrobb l-Għagħin Nature Park, and runs a wildlife rescue and rehabilitation service through volunteers. It is a privileged partner of WWF and delivers the FEE programmes — EcoSchools, Young Reporters for the Environment, Learning About Forests — plus Blue Flag and Green Key. An NGO managing named Natura 2000 sites is the body to approach when a European-designated site near you is threatened, because it already holds the management relationship with the state. AND THE JOINT FRONT, which is the free membership list Malta offers: environmental demands have been put together by BirdLife Malta, Din l-Art Ħelwa, Flimkien Għal Ambjent Aħjar, Friends of the Earth Malta, Nature Trust Malta and the Ramblers Association of Malta, and endorsed by Extinction Rebellion Malta, Għawdix, Moviment Graffitti, Rota, the Grow 10 Trees Project, Wirt Għawdex and Żminijietna. Thirteen named organisations that have signed together, including a demand that protection of the environment, its custody and its rights for future generations be written into the Maltese Constitution. SEPARATELY: BirdLife Malta manages four nature reserves — Salina, Simar, Għadira and Foresta 2000.

trackers.name: Ambjent Malta — it pays eNGOs ANNUAL FUNDING to manage Natura 2000 sites
trackers.desc: THE ARRANGEMENT A COMMUNITY SHOULD ASK FOR BY NAME: as the implementational arm of the Environment and Resources Authority, Ambjent Malta executes the management plans for terrestrial Natura 2000 sites — and it, the ministry and ERA have a number of MANAGEMENT AGREEMENTS in place with local eNGOs for the management of various Natura 2000 sites. Through these agreements, eNGOs are PROVIDED ANNUAL FUNDING to implement conservation measures in line with the Management Plans. An eNGO can be paid every year by the state to manage a protected site — not a one-off grant but a standing agreement, and this file has recorded guardianship deeds and custody transfers elsewhere but not the funding that comes with them. WHAT THOSE MEASURES ACTUALLY COVER, which is the scope of work on offer: invasive and alien plant eradication programmes, SITE PATROLLING, restoration and expansion of habitats listed in the Habitats Directive, measures to prevent trampling, installation of surveillance systems, and monitoring of fauna. AND A PRECEDENT FOR OUTSIDE MONEY ON A PROTECTED SITE: around a thousand trees and shrubs were planted at one major Natura 2000 site under an agreement between the Maltese environment ministry and the Turkish Ministry for Agriculture and Forestry — a foreign government funding planting on a domestic protected site.

trackers.name: Majjistral Park — three NGOs federated to run Malta's first national park
trackers.desc: THE STRUCTURE, WHICH IS THE MODEL: Malta's first natural national park is managed by a HERITAGE PARKS FEDERATION CONSISTING OF THREE NGOs — a heritage trust, a nature trust and a foundation — under an agreement signed with government, which contributed a starting sum toward the project, while a bank sponsored it at an annual figure for three years. The team engaged a part-time RANGER and organised public walks. Three organisations federating to manage one park, with government seed money and a corporate sponsor on a three-year commitment, is a structure a community can propose — and the park is a member of the EUROPARC Federation. THE SCALE OF WHAT ONE OF THOSE NGOs HOLDS: over 55 years it has saved 42 heritage sites and tracts of land of ecological importance, funded by corporate support, memberships and its own fund-raising, and currently holds 11 PROPERTIES UNDER GUARDIANSHIP AGREEMENTS WITH GOVERNMENT AND 3 IN TRUST WITH THE DIOCESE OF MALTA. The church holds land too, and it can be placed in trust with a conservation body. AND THE TERMS OF THE NEWER DEEDS: the NGOs are obliged to manage the site in a way that respects its ecological value, promotes environmental education, improves biodiversity and encourages sustainable public use, with an action plan drawn up for each agreement illustrating the restoration, use and final product expected at each site by 2035.

trackers.name: Moviment Graffitti — it publishes an OBJECTION TEMPLATE and the address to send it to
trackers.desc: WHAT IT GIVES A RESIDENT DIRECTLY, and it is the most practical single item in the Maltese bucket: for a live application it publishes the deadline, the Planning Authority representations email address, THE APPLICATION NUMBER TO CITE, and AN OBJECTION TEMPLATE on its own pages. A template plus an address turns an angry resident into a filed objection. AND WHAT IT DOES WHEN THE PERMIT IS GRANTED ANYWAY: it organised fifteen ENGOs AND RESIDENTS filing a joint appeal against a road permit taking nearly 50,000 square metres of agricultural land, the uprooting of several hundred trees and demolition — the signatories listed with their voluntary organisation numbers, and INDIVIDUAL RESIDENTS NAMED ALONGSIDE THE ORGANISATIONS. AND IT RAISES THE MONEY: with seven other NGOs, three LOCAL COUNCILS and hundreds of residents it took legal action against a major permit granted despite over 4,500 objections, stating that as there are high costs involved this will only be possible with the public's financial support — LOCAL COUNCILS AND NGOs WILL COVER PART OF THE PROCEDURAL AND PROFESSIONAL FEES, with a public donation link. AND ITS GROUNDS-CHECKLIST FOR A COASTAL CASE, worth copying: the authority cannot ignore its obligations under the local plan, Maltese law, EU ENVIRONMENTAL LAW, THE PUBLIC DOMAIN ACT, the strategic plan, AND INTERNATIONAL CONVENTIONS protecting the coast and marine environment.

trackers.name: Nature Trust — FEE Malta — it holds SEVEN named sites, and membership is FREE
trackers.desc: WHAT IT HOLDS, site by site, which is what makes it a land resource rather than a campaign group: under SITE MANAGEMENT AND HABITAT RESTORATION it lists a nature reserve which is a Special Area of Conservation, a MARINE PARK, a nature park, a Natura 2000 garigue site, a nature and heritage park held JOINTLY WITH A HERITAGE PARKS FEDERATION, and two further Natura 2000 sites. Malta was the smallest bucket in this file at 21 entries. An organisation already managing seven protected sites is one that can be asked to take on an eighth, and it is committed to conserving Maltese nature by promoting environmental awareness, MANAGING AREAS OF NATURAL AND SCIENTIFIC INTEREST, and LOBBYING FOR EFFECTIVE ENVIRONMENTAL LEGISLATION. AND HOW TO GET INVOLVED, all published: BECOME A MEMBER FOR FREE; volunteer; or adopt a turtle against a donation of just 30 EURO A YEAR and receive a photograph and certificate. It is a registered Voluntary Organisation with a published VO number. IT ALSO RUNS AN EMERGENCY SERVICE: a wildlife rescue team of volunteers made up of DIVERS, BIOLOGISTS AND MARINE MAMMAL MEDICS, AVAILABLE 24 HOURS A DAY, rescuing injured marine turtles and stranded dolphins, with a wildlife rehabilitation and education centre funded through the European regional development fund. It works with WWF and is a member of the European Environmental Bureau.

trackers.name: BirdLife Malta — four reserves, 20,000 trees planted, and a Nature Guardian scheme to join
trackers.desc: WHAT IT MANAGES: four nature reserves, of which one is described as THE LATEST LAND MANAGEMENT PROJECT ENTRUSTED TO BIRDLIFE MALTA — so the portfolio is still growing. Another is an afforestation project where OVER 20,000 TREES HAVE BEEN PLANTED, and a third is Malta's only semi-natural woodland. An organisation that is still being entrusted with new land is the one to approach about a site nobody is managing — and it says plainly: we will strive to increase these places for nature while ensuring they are accessible for everyone to enjoy. THE ARGUMENT IT PUBLISHES, which any Maltese objection can quote: Malta is BY FAR THE MOST BUILT-UP COUNTRY IN THE EU. Over 33 per cent of our country is built up, the runner-up being Belgium with only 13 per cent — and with dense population and nearly two million tourists a year, the pressures on biodiversity are severe. In these areas biodiversity is given priority, and our nature reserves have PROVED HOW NATURE FLOURISHES WHEN GIVEN A CHANCE. AND THE WAY IN FOR A RESIDENT: become a NATURE GUARDIAN; founded in 1962, it is the oldest environmental organisation in Malta, was instrumental in the creation of three of the island's most important nature reserves, and grows partly through volunteering programmes via the European Solidarity Corps.

trackers.name: Claire Bonello — the Maltese environmental lawyer NGOs and residents actually instruct
trackers.desc: WHO SHE IS: a long-time ally of environmental NGOs in their court battles to challenge development permits that fly in the face of policy — and the record shows she acts for both organisations and individuals. Malta was among the smallest buckets in this file. WHAT SHE HAS ACTUALLY RUN: a joint appeal to the planning tribunal filed by THREE ENGOs TOGETHER WITH A RESIDENTS' ASSOCIATION, prepared by her WITH AN ARCHITECT, which succeeded in having the plans sent back to the authority for a new assessment; an objection filed on behalf of a named movement AND ON HER OWN BEHALF, arguing an application be unequivocally refused as yet another attempt to urbanise one of the very few remaining stretches of natural coastline; and a three-year fight for one householder in which the Court of Appeal TWICE REVOKED the development permit next door. A lawyer paired with an architect, acting for NGOs and residents together, is the configuration that wins these appeals — and the objections she runs cite the impact assessment's omissions, infrastructure, overshadowing, and the inadequacy of the social impact assessment. AND HER OWN WARNING, worth reading before you start: it is the responsibility of the Planning Authority and the Tribunal to respect and enforce those laws, plans and policies which militate for the safeguarding of our natural and cultural heritage. So why should they be forced to live up to those responsibilities only by NGOs and residents WHO END UP WASTING SO MUCH OF THEIR OWN PRECIOUS TIME AND RESOURCES ON NEVER-ENDING APPEALS?

trackers.name: The Environment and Planning Review Tribunal — a panel of an advocate, a planner and an architect
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS AND WHY IT MATTERS TO AN OBJECTOR: an INDEPENDENT BODY TO REVIEW DECISIONS MADE BY THE PLANNING AUTHORITY AND THE ENVIRONMENT AND RESOURCES AUTHORITY, whose primary role is to examine BOTH THE LEGALITY AND THE FACTS behind these decisions, offering a legal avenue for individuals and businesses to contest outcomes they believe are unjust or incorrect. A tribunal that reviews the FACTS, not only the law, is one where a resident's own evidence counts — unlike the legality-only forums recorded in Denmark and Cyprus. WHO SITS ON IT, which tells you what kind of case to bring: a panel of three members — ONE MUST BE AN ADVOCATE AND THE OTHER TWO WELL-VERSED IN DEVELOPMENT PLANNING AND ENVIRONMENTAL MATTERS RESPECTIVELY. In practice this usually translates into an advocate, A PLANNER AND AN ARCHITECT. And crucially: the tribunal MAY ENGAGE EXPERTS to assist it in its deliberations. Where the panel includes a planner and an architect, planning and design evidence lands directly on people trained to read it. AND THE SEPARATE COURT ROUTE NAMED ALONGSIDE: the civil courts may enquire into the validity of any administrative act or declare it null, invalid or without effect, but only where the act violates the Constitution of Malta or is ULTRA VIRES on specified grounds. A named advocates' practice publishes this explainer and offers representation.

trackers.name: Din l-Art Ħelwa — founded 1965 by a judge, and it TAKES LEGAL ACTION to halt development
trackers.desc: WHO IT IS: a non-governmental, non-profit, VOLUNTARY organisation founded in 1965 BY A MALTESE JUDGE to safeguard Malta's cultural heritage AND NATURAL ENVIRONMENT, with its offices at a named palazzo address in the capital and its executive president named. WHAT IT DOES, in the plainest terms this file has recorded for a heritage body: it promotes the preservation and protection of historic buildings and monuments, THE CHARACTER OF MALTA'S TOWNS AND VILLAGES, AND PLACES OF NATURAL BEAUTY. It is VERY ACTIVE IN CAMPAIGNING AGAINST PROPOSED CONSTRUCTION WHICH INFRINGES PLANNING LAWS OR POLICIES, and REGULARLY OBJECTS TO PLANNING APPLICATIONS, TAKING LEGAL ACTION TO HALT DEVELOPMENT IN SOME CASES. An organisation whose published purpose includes taking legal action to halt development is one a community can approach without having to persuade it that objecting is legitimate. AND THE LONGER GAME IT PLAYS: it STIMULATES THE ENFORCEMENT OF EXISTING LAWS AND THE ENACTMENT OF NEW ONES for the protection of Malta's natural and built heritage — and its sites are open to visitors and for events, thanks to an army of dedicated VOLUNTEERS. A recorded instance of its watchdog role: when a developers' body proposed a scheme allowing developers TO TRANSFER GROSS FLOOR AREA RIGHTS from historic village cores to less sensitive areas, the organisation called it a negation of planning regulation.

trackers.name: The VO Funding Portal — Malta's standing list of funds open to voluntary organisations
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the national funding portal where every scheme open to Maltese VOLUNTARY ORGANISATIONS is published with its allocation, guidelines and call documents. Malta had four funding entries filed. One portal listing every fund a registered voluntary organisation can apply to is where a Maltese group should start rather than searching ministry by ministry. AND THE PRINCIPAL SCHEME ON IT: the Voluntary Organisations Project Scheme, with A TOTAL ALLOCATION OF 800,000 EURO per annual call, managed and administered by the MALTA COUNCIL FOR THE VOLUNTARY SECTOR, designed to fund projects that can make a real difference... for the benefit of the COMMUNITIES THEY WORK IN. Since its start in 2016 it has provided voluntary organisations with MORE THAN 4,500,000 EURO, translating into projects within the community. AND THE OBJECTIVE A LOCAL GROUP CAN USE: among its stated aims is to encourage NON-GOVERNMENTAL BODIES AND PRIVATE ENTITIES OR PERSONS AND LOCAL COUNCILS to contribute, and to provide a platform from which to develop CO-OPERATION BETWEEN VOLUNTARY ORGANISATIONS AND THE GOVERNMENT. Local councils are named as intended participants, so a village council and a residents' organisation can come to this money together — the same council-plus-association pairing recorded as decisive in Luxembourg and Malta's own courts.

trackers.name: VOPS eligibility and terms — 4,000 to 20,000 EURO, 80% covered, and NO REPEATS
trackers.desc: THE TERMS, from the government services listing: the fund allows volunteer organisations ENROLLED WITH THE COMMISSIONER FOR VOLUNTARY ORGANISATIONS to apply for funding to undertake projects, and SUPPORTS UP TO 80% OF THE PROJECT TO A MAXIMUM OF 20,000 EURO. Organisations can apply for grants ranging from 4,000 to 20,000 EURO depending on the action, over a 12-MONTH implementation period. Eighty per cent covered means a Maltese group needs to find only a fifth of the cost, and enrolment with the Commissioner is the single gate — there is no minimum age for the organisation. AND THE FOUR CONDITIONS THAT SINK APPLICATIONS: applicants must be ENROLLED AND FULLY COMPLIANT with the Commissioner by the closing date; must have NO OUTSTANDING PROJECTS FROM PREVIOUS YEARS; must demonstrate SUFFICIENT FINANCIAL CAPACITY TO MEET THE CO-FINANCING REQUIREMENTS; and the proposal MUST BE INNOVATIVE AND NOT A REPEAT OF PREVIOUSLY APPROVED PROJECTS by the same organisation. Only ONE application per organisation per deadline is allowed. A no-repeats rule means the same group cannot fund the same campaign twice, which is worth knowing before a second year is planned around it. One action within the scheme specifically funds RESEARCH, another EVENTS AND ACTIVITIES, with allocations from 4,000 to 10,000 EURO and 20% co-financing.

trackers.name: A Dummy's Guide to petitioning Malta's Planning Authority — registration is the right to appeal
trackers.desc: THE STEP THAT DECIDES WHETHER A MALTESE OBJECTOR HAS ANY RIGHTS LATER: submitting an objection MAKES YOU A REGISTERED THIRD PARTY, AND ONLY REGISTERED THIRD PARTIES HAVE A RIGHT TO APPEAL. Malta is joint-smallest bucket in this file. Objecting at the application stage is what buys the right to appeal the permit — a community that waits for the decision has already lost. AND THE COST, which is unusually favourable and worth knowing before anyone assumes an appeal is beyond them: the appeal must be accompanied by the appeal fee, WHICH IS 5% OF THE FEE ORIGINALLY PAID BY APPLICANT. There is a MINIMUM FEE OF 150 EURO and IT IS CAPPED AT 3,500 EURO together with a 50 EURO ADMINISTRATION FEE. An objector pays a twentieth of what the developer paid, and it stops at a ceiling — so the larger the scheme, the smaller the appeal costs relative to what is at stake. AND THE MECHANICS: the appeal goes before the ENVIRONMENT AND PLANNING REVIEW TRIBUNAL, WHICH IS A THREE-PERSON BOARD responsible for deciding appeals; it HAS TO BE FILED WITHIN 30 DAYS OF PUBLICATION OF THE DECISION IN THE GOVERNMENT GAZETTE; and you PICK UP APPEAL FEE FORMS FROM the Planning Authority AND DEPOSIT MONEY IN THE BANK ACCOUNT SPECIFIED IN THE FORMS.

trackers.name: The EPRT's own scope page — which decisions a registered objector may actually appeal
trackers.desc: WHAT THE TRIBUNAL SAYS IT CAN HEAR, published by the tribunal itself, and it is narrower and more specific than most objectors assume: AN INTERESTED THIRD PARTY WHO HAD SUBMITTED WRITTEN REPRESENTATIONS as established by the Planning Authority in terms of a named article of the Development Planning Act MAY APPEAL IN THE FOLLOWING INSTANCES: A DECISION FOLLOWING AN APPLICATION FOR DEVELOPMENT APPLICATION; A DECISION FOLLOWING A PLANNING CONTROL APPLICATION RELATING TO A CHANGE IN ALIGNMENT; and A DECISION GIVEN IN RELATION TO SCHEDULING AND CONSERVATION ORDERS. Written representations at application stage are the stated precondition, and the tribunal names the article they must be made under — which is the provision to comply with exactly. AND THE HEADS OF APPEAL BEYOND DEVELOPMENT DECISIONS: it also hears appeals against A NOTICE issued under a named Part of the Development Planning Act; A DECISION IN RELATION TO SCHEDULING AND CONSERVATION ORDERS; and A DECISION ON A REQUEST FOR MODIFICATION OR REVOCATION OF PERMISSION. A decision on a request to REVOKE an existing permission is appealable — so a permit already granted is not always the end of the matter. The tribunal is now also competent to determine appeals from SANITARY DECISIONS and planning control decisions relating to MINOR AMENDMENTS TO LOCAL PLANS.

trackers.name: Ęustizzja għal Artna — a NAMED standing coalition of nine Maltese organisations
trackers.desc: A COALITION THAT EXISTS UNDER ITS OWN NAME, so a resident can address one campaign instead of nine organisations: the environmental NGOs FORM PART OF THE GUSTIZZJA GHAL ARTNA (JUSTICE FOR OUR LAND) CAMPAIGN, and the statement is signed by THE RAMBLERS' ASSOCIATION OF MALTA, FLIMKIEN GHAL AMBJENT AHJAR, DIN L-ART HELWA, MOVIMENT GRAFFITTI, BIRDLIFE MALTA, FRIENDS OF THE EARTH MALTA, NATURE TRUST MALTA, WIRT GHAWDEX, and GHAWDIX. Nine named organisations under one campaign banner, including two specific to Gozo, is a single door to the whole Maltese environmental sector. AND WHAT THEY ARE PUSHING FOR, which is the change that would matter most to any objector: they TOOK NOTE OF THE GOVERNMENT'S PLAN TO AMEND THE LAW SO THAT WORKS ARE SUSPENDED WHILE AN APPEAL IS BEING HEARD, and asked that the reform be A SIMPLE AMENDMENT TO THE EXISTING LAW REGULATING APPEALS, with NO OTHER UNRELATED PROVISIONS BUNDLED WITH THIS CHANGE. Whether works stop while an appeal runs is the single question that decides if an appeal is worth bringing — and warning against unrelated provisions being bundled into a favourable reform is a lesson for any campaign that wins a promise. They urged the government to TURN THE PAGE ON THE MISTAKES of an earlier bill and hoped reform would not be tabled AS AN ACCOMPLISHED FACT.

trackers.name: Общественная экологическая экспертиза — a citizens' review with legal standing
trackers.desc: A STATUTORY PROCEDURE, NOT A PROTEST. Federal Law 174-ФЗ of 23 November 1995 gives an entire chapter to the rights of citizens, public associations and other non-state non-commercial organisations in environmental review, and to public environmental review as an institution: article 21 (objects), 22 (conducting), 23 (conditions), 24 (refusal to register the application) and 25 (the conclusion). It is a registered procedure running in parallel with state review and producing a formal заключение. READ ARTICLE 24 FIRST: it sets out the grounds on which registration may be refused, and that is where applications die — the refusal grounds are your drafting checklist. AND THE LEVER MOST PEOPLE MISS: the law provides for organisation of public environmental reviews по требованию населения — at the demand of the population — and for informing federal executive bodies about planned economic activity on the territory of the municipal formation. Residents can demand their municipality organise a review, and the municipality carries an information duty about planned activity on its own territory.

trackers.name: Is your site inside an ООПТ? That decides whether review is compulsory
trackers.desc: THE THRESHOLD QUESTION FOR ANY RUSSIAN SITE. State environmental review is mandatory for capital construction planned within the boundaries of federal-level protected natural territories (ООПТ) — excepting listed social infrastructure objects that are not category I or II and sit in settlements listed under article 3_1 of Federal Law 33-ФЗ. It is also mandatory for especially dangerous, technically complex and unique objects, and defence and security objects, planned within regional and local-level ООПТ where federal law permits building there at all. So establish whether your site sits inside an ООПТ, and at which level, before anything else — it determines whether review is compulsory. NOTE HOW WIDE THE BAIKAL DEFINITION IS: the Baikal natural territory covers the lake, its water protection zone, its catchment within Russia, adjoining protected territories, and the adjoining land up to 200 kilometres west and north-west. PUBLIC REGISTERS TO MINE: Rosprirodnadzor maintains a register of public discussion materials and a register of issued state environmental review conclusions — primary evidence of what was decided and what was consulted on.

trackers.name: Before you organise: designation risk under the foreign-agent laws
trackers.desc: SAID PLAINLY, BECAUSE IT AFFECTS HOW YOU USE EVERYTHING ELSE HERE. Russia's foreign-agent and undesirable-organisations legislation has been applied to environmental organisations, several of which have been designated or liquidated; designation brings labelling obligations, reporting burdens and personal legal exposure for those involved, and status can change faster than any directory is updated. THIS MAP THEREFORE RECORDS STATUTORY MECHANISMS RATHER THAN A LIST OF ORGANISATIONS TO CONTACT FOR RUSSIA — the rights in 174-ФЗ belong to citizens and municipalities and do not depend on joining any organisation. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCES: check the current designation status of any organisation before affiliating with it or accepting funding from it; be aware that foreign funding is the specific trigger the legislation targets, so international grants recorded elsewhere in this map carry a risk in Russia that they do not carry elsewhere; and prefer routes that operate through your own municipality and through registered statutory procedures, which are harder to characterise as foreign-directed activity. Verify the present state of the law before acting — it has changed repeatedly and this entry may lag it.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: Get into the ten-year regional scheme — it plans terminations too
trackers.desc: THE DOCUMENT THAT DECIDES WHETHER YOUR SITE IS EVEN A CANDIDATE. Under Zakon No. 150-Z of 15 November 2018 on specially protected natural territories, региональные схемы рационального размещения ООПТ местного значения are developed by oblast and Minsk city executive committees together with the National Academy of Sciences and other interested bodies, for a ten-year period, and include measures planning the declaration, transformation and termination of заказники and local памятники природы — approved by local councils in agreement with Minprirody. THREE CONSEQUENCES: get into the scheme, as with Thailand's provincial action plan recorded elsewhere here; the same scheme plans TERMINATIONS as well as declarations, so read it for what is being removed; and the Academy of Sciences is a statutory co-author, so a scientific case addressed to НАН Беларуси reaches a body with a drafting role. STATE ADMINISTRATION IS SHARED: the President, Council of Ministers, Minprirody, and local Councils of Deputies and executive bodies — with article 9 setting out the local powers expressly. Minprirody maintains the реестр, the register of specially protected natural territories, which is where to establish existing status. A BROADER CONTAINER TO KNOW: a биосферный резерват includes individual protected territories as well as other territories where rational (sustainable) use of natural resources is purposefully stimulated — a category that expressly takes in ordinary land under economic use.
