trackers.name: Two permissions, not one — the registration and grant regime
trackers.desc: READ THIS BEFORE PLANNING ANY FUNDED WORK. Amendments adopted in February 2013 make it impossible for unregistered groups to legally receive grants and donations, and increased fivefold the fines for receiving funding without concluding a grant agreement and registering it with the Ministry of Justice. Registered organisations must seek Ministry of Justice approval for any grant — so there are two separate permissions: register the organisation once, then register each grant agreement. After the 2014 crackdown, registering independent NGOs is described as nearly impossible, foreign NGOs were expelled, and the reported result is a stark absence of registered independent environmental NGOs, with the space dominated by GONGOs. Groups operating independently often lack registration and cannot legally accept grants. AND THE MONEY IS SCARCE SEPARATELY FROM THE REPRESSION: a review of international grant policies found Azerbaijani civil society receives the least financial support for environmental issues in the South Caucasus, with donors allocating no or minimal funding to ecological work. THIS MAP THEREFORE RECORDS CONSTRAINTS RATHER THAN A DIRECTORY FOR AZERBAIJAN — naming active independent groups would expose people already at risk, and most cannot lawfully receive funding in any case.

trackers.name: Strasbourg case law — including an environmental society's dissolution
trackers.desc: THE DURABLE LEGAL REFERENCE, AND ONE CASE IS DIRECTLY ANALOGOUS. The European Court of Human Rights has ruled repeatedly on Azerbaijani NGO registration and dissolution: Tebieti Mühafize Cemiyyeti and Israfilov v. Azerbaijan, no. 37083/03, 8 October 2009 — arbitrary dissolution of what was an environmental society; Islam-Ittihad Association and Others, no. 5548/05, 13 November 2014; and Rasul Jafarov, no. 69981/14, 17 March 2016, where the Court observed that the legislative environment governing NGO registration, funding and reporting has grown increasingly harsh. ONE PATTERN WORTH KNOWING: several earlier registration cases were struck out after the NGOs concerned were registered — so filing at Strasbourg has sometimes produced registration before judgment. The Council of Europe's Venice Commission has made recommendations on revising the NGO law. WHAT EXISTS BY TREATY RATHER THAN PERMISSION: REC Caucasus, whose charter was signed in September 1999 by the governments of Azerbaijan, Armenia, Georgia and the EU, has a mandate covering free exchange of information in line with the Aarhus Convention, assistance to all environmental NGOs, and increasing public participation in decision-making — a body the government co-founded is a different proposition from an independent NGO. The Caucasus Nature Fund also covers Azerbaijan.

trackers.name: Aarhus Centre Baku — information only; do not expect help with participation or a court case
trackers.desc: READ THE SCOPE BEFORE YOU RELY ON IT: the OSCE records that Azerbaijan's Aarhus Centre in Baku focuses primarily on supporting public access to environmental information. The Aarhus Convention has three pillars — information, participation in decisions, and access to justice — and on the OSCE's own description this centre is built around the first. That is a real limit, not a quibble: it means the centre is the place to obtain the environmental data underlying a project, and not the place to expect help lodging an objection or reaching a court. Plan for it by using the centre to get documents and building the objection elsewhere. WHY THIS ENTRY AND NOT AN AZERBAIJANI ORGANISATION: Azerbaijan is a closed operating environment, and naming small domestic groups in a public map can expose the people in them, so this file records the intergovernmental instrument and stops there. A SECOND THING AZERBAIJANI READERS SHOULD KNOW, BECAUSE IT LOOKS LIKE A ROUTE AND IS NOT: the Caucasus Nature Fund names Azerbaijan in its mandate, but its published list of supported protected areas carries 16 Georgian and 5 Armenian sites and no Azerbaijani site, and its own parks filter offers only Armenia and Georgia. An Azerbaijani community reading about CNF's three-country remit should not assume the funding route exists there. Aarhus Centres across this region vary enormously in what they actually do and several have gone quiet; establish that the Baku centre is currently staffed and answering before building a timetable around it.

trackers.name: OSME Conservation Fund — small grants across this whole region, and about half of applications succeed
trackers.desc: THE FUNDING RATE IS THE FACT THAT SHOULD MAKE YOU APPLY: OSME states on its own how-to-apply page that it receives more applications than it can support but that its current funding rate is in the region of fifty per cent. Very few funders publish that, and against a one-in-two chance a modest application is worth the week it takes to write. AND ONE OF ITS NAMED FUNDING PRIORITIES IS DIRECTLY USEFUL FOR DEFENDING A PLACE: investigating potential new Important Bird Areas, or ornithologically little-known areas. If your valley has never been surveyed, this fund exists to pay for the survey that could put it on a designation map — and designation is what lenders and planners screen against. It also funds ecological studies of little-known species and, notably, studies related to illegal bird killing and unsustainable hunting. WHAT IT IS: the Ornithological Society of the Middle East, the Caucasus and Central Asia, a volunteer-run society established 1978 and extended in 2001 to cover the Caucasus and Central Asia, with members in over forty countries — by its own account the only ornithological body covering this entire region, which includes Azerbaijan. Its Conservation Fund has run since the early 1980s; grants are typically £1,000 to £3,000 with no stated maximum, and in 2022 it passed £50,000 awarded in a single year. A separate Trevor Poyser Species Conservation Fund awards one grant of up to £5,000 a year for research on threatened species, and there is a Youth Development Fund. WHAT WINS: applications initiated and carried out by nationals of the region, or carrying a strong educational element that proactively engages local communities, or building long-term sustainability such as training local counterparts. Applications go by email in English on the downloadable grant application form; enquiries to crf@osme.org. You must state whether you are seeking funding elsewhere. WHAT WILL NOT BE FUNDED: projects collecting specimens, whole organisms or DNA samples, unless fully justified with all local authorisations obtained; and general bird-ringing projects setting up new long-term programmes are unlikely to succeed. OSME has funded work at the Besh Barmag migration bottleneck on the Caspian north of Baku and youth projects in Azerbaijan. THE LIMITS: this funds bird and habitat research, not litigation, land purchase or campaigning, and the sums are small. Its value to a land defence is evidential — it pays for the survey that establishes what is there.

trackers.name: Rufford Small Grants — Azerbaijan is named eligible, and an individual can apply in their own name
trackers.desc: AZERBAIJAN IS NAMED ON THE FOUNDATION'S OWN ELIGIBILITY PAGE, AND APPLICATIONS COME FROM INDIVIDUALS AND SMALL GROUPS RATHER THAN REQUIRING A REGISTERED ORGANISATION. This map records only international instruments for Azerbaijan, and this is the third — a route that needs no Azerbaijani body to be named or exposed. NO DEADLINES: applications may be submitted at any time of year, with the focus on people early in a conservation career, especially current or recent postgraduate students; undergraduates are not funded. THE SPECIES TEST IS PRECISE AND CHECKABLE IN ADVANCE: work on any species not listed as Least Concern globally on the IUCN Red List qualifies, as does work on species not yet assessed but thought to be globally threatened. Habitat, human-wildlife conflict and community education projects qualify without a species focus. FUNDING IS A STAIRCASE: a first grant up to £7,000, then a second, a Booster and a Completion Grant, running to roughly £18,000 — each stage requiring the last to be finished and reported, with updates and the final report published on the applicant's page. For a country where independent environmental work is difficult, a published international funding record is a form of standing. CONSTRAINTS: one application per twelve months; twelve months' wait after a rejection; the foundation expects to fund between half and all of the project and requires evidence of co-funding where there is any; and it does not support pure research without conservation benefit or expeditions requiring the applicant to fundraise to take part. Read this alongside the ornithological society's grants also recorded here for Azerbaijan, which fund survey work toward site designation — the two are complementary rather than alternatives.

trackers.name: Eastern Partnership Civil Society Forum — a national platform with an environment working group, and it funds members
trackers.desc: THERE IS A NATIONAL PLATFORM IN THIS COUNTRY AND MEMBERSHIP IS OPEN. National platforms have operated in all six eastern partnership countries since 2011, membership is stated to be open to all eligible civil society organisations, and each platform runs WORKING GROUPS MIRRORING THE FORUM'S OWN — including one on ENVIRONMENT, CLIMATE CHANGE AND ENERGY SECURITY. In a country where this file records four entries, all of them foreign organisations or state portals, a structure that a domestic organisation can actually join is worth knowing about. AND IT PROVIDES MONEY AND TRAINING, NOT JUST MEETINGS: the forum states plainly that it provides FUNDING AND TRAINING TO REINFORCE CIVIL SOCIETY'S OPERATIONAL CAPACITIES, and members elsewhere in the region are described as gaining access to a regranting scheme, to advocacy training, and to consultations organised by the Council of Europe, the World Bank and the European Investment Bank. That last is the practical one where an international lender finances a scheme. A separate European-funded civil society facility also runs capacity courses open to organisations in this country. IT IS LARGE AND CURRENT: working since 2009 with around eleven hundred civil society organisations, carrying the recommendations of some twelve hundred to policy makers, with national platform facilitators and working group coordinators named for a 2026 to 2028 cycle, an elected steering committee, a general assembly and an independent compliance committee. NOW THE CAVEAT, AND IT IS NOT SMALL: an academic assessment of the forum records that the criteria for selecting which organisations participate ARE NOT TRANSPARENT, and that the steering committee effectively chooses the members who then elect the following steering committee. A structure that selects its own electorate can be difficult for an outsider to enter, and a group in this country should establish how its national platform actually admits members before assuming the stated openness is the whole picture. THE OTHER LIMITS: this is a European integration and civil society platform, not an environmental body. It will not object to a scheme, assess one or litigate, and its national platform's independence in any given country depends on conditions in that country. Use it as a route to membership, to training, to funding, and to the environment working group's members.

trackers.name: Global Forest Watch — a monitoring tool one person can use alone, with no organisation involved
trackers.desc: IT REQUIRES NO ORGANISATION, NO REGISTRATION WITH ANYONE LOCAL, AND NO MONEY. Anyone can define an area of interest by drawing it on a map, uploading a boundary file or selecting a region, and subscribe to AUTOMATED EMAIL ALERTS when tree cover loss or fire is detected there — the whole platform is free, with no subscription or licence fee. Every other entry recorded for this country is a foreign institution or a state portal, because naming domestic organisations here can expose people. A TOOL AN INDIVIDUAL OPERATES ALONE IS WORTH MORE IN THAT SITUATION THAN AN ORGANISATION NOBODY CAN SAFELY JOIN. WHAT IT GIVES YOU: the annual tree cover loss record from 2001 onwards, comparable year by year for any patch of ground anywhere in the world, alongside DAILY FIRE ALERTS and more than sixty other datasets covering land use, protected areas and concessions. Two decades of loss data for a specific slope, produced independently of any national institution, is evidence that exists whether or not anyone local will confirm it. BE CLEAR ABOUT WHAT DOES NOT APPLY HERE: the weekly near-real-time deforestation alerts are described as covering the tropics, and this country lies outside them. The annual record and the fire feed do apply. ITS FIELD APP WORKS OFFLINE, WHICH MATTERS WHERE CONNECTIVITY OR ATTENTION IS A RISK: store the change data on the device beforehand, navigate to a point WITHOUT ANY SIGNAL, photograph what is there and complete a structured form, then upload later. TREAT AN ALERT AS A QUESTION RATHER THAN A FINDING — the platform itself says an alert indicates where loss MAY be occurring and needs verification against recent imagery, concession and protected area boundaries, and ideally a site visit. THE LIMITS: the main platform needs internet, several datasets refresh only annually, and it takes time to learn. AND IT APPEARS TO BE REBRANDING UNDER A NEW NAME COVERING NATURE RATHER THAN FORESTS — verify the current address rather than trusting a saved link.

trackers.name: OCCRP Aleph — a company-ownership search one person can run alone, in Russian
trackers.desc: IT NEEDS NO LOCAL ORGANISATION, NO INTRODUCTION AND NO MONEY. An investigative data platform indexing over a billion records from more than three hundred datasets across more than a hundred and eighty countries — CORPORATE REGISTRIES, COURT RECORDS, LAND REGISTRIES, sanctions lists, air and maritime registries and leaked archives — with an interface available in RUSSIAN. Every other entry recorded for this country is a foreign institution or a state portal, because naming domestic organisations here can expose people. A SEARCH ONE PERSON RUNS FROM A BROWSER IS THE KIND OF RESOURCE THAT FITS THAT SITUATION, and this file recorded the same reasoning for a satellite imagery service and a forest monitoring platform. ITS COVERAGE IS DESCRIBED AS STRONGEST IN EASTERN EUROPE AND THE FORMER SOVIET STATES, so this region is where its records are deepest rather than thinnest. WHAT IT LETS YOU ESTABLISH: who owns the company named on a permit, what other companies those people own, whether a firm appears on sanctions lists, what court records exist, and — where the data reaches — what the land registry says. This file has recorded across the region that the decisive facts in a land dispute are usually the price, the contract and the beneficiary rather than the ecology. AND YOU CAN BRING YOUR OWN PAPERS: upload documents you already hold and the platform cross-references the names and companies in them against its whole corpus. ACCESS: anyone may search the publicly available data; journalists, researchers AND ACTIVISTS working in the public interest may apply for broader access AT NO CHARGE, with restricted datasets granted case by case. THE WARNINGS ARE SERIOUS HERE. FINDINGS MUST BE INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED — the platform says so itself, and leaked datasets are incomplete by nature. Consider carefully what an application for broader access discloses about you and from where, given what this file has recorded about the treatment of investigative work in this country. And the platform was rebuilt in December 2025, so older tutorials describe a system that has been retired.

trackers.name: Digital Security Helpline — free, 24 hours, answers within two hours, in Russian
trackers.desc: THIS FILE TOLD YOU TO THINK ABOUT WHAT AN APPLICATION FOR DATABASE ACCESS DISCLOSES ABOUT YOU. THIS IS WHO ANSWERS THAT QUESTION. A free helpline operating twenty-four hours a day for civil society — activists, community groups, journalists and human rights defenders — which RESPONDS TO EVERY REQUEST WITHIN TWO HOURS, with support available in RUSSIAN among ten languages. IT WORKS IN TWO MODES AND YOU SHOULD KNOW WHICH ONE YOU NEED. If you are at risk but nothing has happened yet, it walks you or your group through ASSESSING THE RISKS YOU ACTUALLY FACE and prioritising what to fix first. If you are already under attack, it provides RAPID-RESPONSE EMERGENCY ASSISTANCE. IT SECURES THE THINGS A SMALL GROUP ACTUALLY HAS: technical infrastructure, WEBSITES AND SOCIAL MEDIA ACCOUNTS against attack. That matters more here than it sounds — this map records bodies across the region that exist only as a social account, and for them losing the account is losing the organisation. AND IT DOES SOMETHING THAT CONVERTS AN ATTACK INTO EVIDENCE: it helps people ANALYSE, DOCUMENT AND EXPOSE advanced attacks such as SPYWARE and targeted phishing. A documented, technically verified intrusion is a fact an international body or a court can be shown; a suspicion is not. It also provides guidance materials, training, capacity building and referrals to others who can help. HOW TO REACH IT: by email to a published address, from anywhere. It is an accredited member of a computer emergency response body for civil society, and it publishes a data usage policy and terms of service — read both before sending anything sensitive, and consider from which device and connection you write. THE LIMITS: it handles DIGITAL SECURITY ONLY. It will not advise on your land case, fund anything, or represent you — use it alongside the international protection routes for defenders and the investigative and satellite tools recorded elsewhere in this file, which are precisely the activities that attract the attacks it defends against.

trackers.name: Eco-Corridor Fund for the Caucasus — a community can be paid, under contract, to keep its land
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY HAS NO ENTRY IN THIS MAP FOR HOLDING OR ACQUIRING LAND. THIS IS ONE, AND IT WORKS WITHOUT ANYONE BUYING ANYTHING. A regional funding instrument supports community-based biodiversity conservation across this country and its two neighbours, USING CONTRACTUAL NATURE CONSERVATION AGREEMENTS to fund ecologically sustainable land use in selected regions and communities. IN PLAIN TERMS: A COMMUNITY ENTERS AN AGREEMENT AND IS PAID TO KEEP ITS LAND IN SUSTAINABLE USE. That is an alternative to the offer a village usually gets — lease it to a company, or to a hunting concession — and it requires no purchase, no designation and no new law. This file has recorded seven ways land is held for protection in this region; THIS IS THE EIGHTH AND THE ONLY ONE THAT PAYS THE COMMUNITY AN INCOME FOR HOLDING IT. WHAT IT IS BUILDING IS BIGGER THAN ONE VILLAGE: eco-corridors that connect parks and protected areas across all three countries, producing an interconnected mosaic of managed and unmanaged habitat under various land categories — with the stated aim of preserving LARGE, SUSTAINABLY USED LANDSCAPES while ensuring the socio-economic position of local communities. A community whose land sits between two protected areas is therefore worth more to this fund than the same land in isolation, which is an argument to make when approaching it. IT IS A LONG-TERM INSTRUMENT rather than a project, capitalised through a European development bank alongside a separate regional fund that finances protected areas themselves — so it is not dependent on a single grant cycle, which this file has recorded as the weakness of most funding here. THE PRECEDENT ACROSS THE BORDER IS WORTH KNOWING BEFORE YOU NEGOTIATE. In the neighbouring country, communities offered money by a company to lease their land, and pressed to lease community land as a HUNTING GROUND, decided instead to place it under conservation — and the body that holds it LEASES FROM THE COMMUNITIES, giving them an income for village improvements, and employs RANGERS DRAWN FROM THE COMMUNITY to patrol it. That is the shape of the deal to ask for: payment, local employment, and the land still yours. THE LIMITS, AND ONE OF THEM CUTS BOTH WAYS. It funds SELECTED regions and communities rather than accepting open applications — eligibility depends on where your land sits. It is a fund, not an advocate: it will not oppose a project. AND CONTRACTUAL CONSERVATION BINDS YOU TOO: an agreement to keep land in ecologically sustainable use restricts what your own people may do with it, so read what is prohibited, for how long, and what happens if the community changes its mind. NOTE ON THE ADDRESS: this entry points at a published case study of the fund's work in this country rather than the fund's own site, which was not established here.

trackers.name: ICCA Consortium — it names this country's own customary system, and takes unregistered members
trackers.desc: THE INTERNATIONAL FRAMEWORK ALREADY HAS A PLACE FOR THIS COUNTRY'S OWN TRADITION. The territories and areas conserved by Indigenous peoples and local communities that this association upholds expressly include systems called YERLI QORUKH, alongside himas, qoroq and others. A community defending land it has always looked after is not proposing something imported; it is claiming a category that already exists internationally under its own name. AND MEMBERSHIP DOES NOT REQUIRE STATE RECOGNITION. Member organisations DO NOT NEED TO BE FORMALLY RECOGNISED BY STATE GOVERNMENTS, and eligible members expressly include traditional communities and THEIR CUSTOMARY NETWORKS, ASSOCIATIONS AND FEDERATIONS, and SELF-INITIATED GROUPINGS. That matters especially here, where this file has recorded that domestic organisations cannot safely be named and where almost every other entry is a foreign institution or a tool used alone — this one can be joined by people who have registered nothing. WHAT IT IS: an international membership association of Indigenous peoples, local communities and supporting organisations documenting, sustaining and DEFENDING territories of life, with over a hundred and sixty member organisations, around four hundred honorary members across eighty countries, and regional coordinators and national focal points who can be contacted directly. IT PUBLISHES A SEQUENCE TO FOLLOW: understand and strengthen your territory; communicate it; CREATE A CRITICAL MASS OF SUPPORT; REGISTER IT; SECURE LEGAL OR POLICY RECOGNITION. Registration runs through a registry managed by a United Nations conservation monitoring centre, is made VOLUNTARILY BY THE CUSTODIANS, and can lead to a territory being counted among the world's recognised protected and conserved areas — which is a designation that outside institutions understand. THE CAUTION IS THE SAME ONE THIS FILE HAS GIVEN ABOUT EVERY MAPPING AND REGISTRATION TOOL: REGISTERING A TERRITORY PUBLISHES ITS LOCATION AND ITS CUSTODIANS. Read it alongside the digital security helpline recorded separately for this country, and note that the consortium's own steps place registration late, after support has been built, rather than at the start. THE OTHER LIMITS: it does not fund, litigate or represent; members must be not-for-profit; and any legal recognition is granted by the state rather than by the consortium.

trackers.name: The Commissioner for Human Rights — it can go to court against a state body on your behalf
trackers.desc: ITS MANDATE DESCRIBES THE OTHER SIDE OF A LAND DISPUTE ALMOST EXACTLY. It exists to restore rights violated by STATE BODIES, MUNICIPALITIES, and LEGAL ENTITIES IN STATE OR MUNICIPAL OWNERSHIP OR WHOSE CONTROLLING STAKE BELONGS TO THE STATE OR A MUNICIPALITY — including public legal entities and budget organisations — and their officials. The permitting authority, the municipality and a state-controlled developer all fall inside that. AND IT HAS A POWER ALMOST NOTHING ELSE IN THIS MAP HAS: IT MAY APPLY TO THE COURT FOR THE RESTORATION OF RIGHTS VIOLATED BY A DECISION, AN ACTION OR AN INACTION of a state body, a municipality, another institution or an official. Inaction is included — which covers a request ignored, a hearing never held, an inspection never carried out. SOMEBODY ELSE CAN COMPLAIN FOR YOU. A complaint may be lodged by a THIRD PERSON OR A NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATION with the consent of the person whose rights were violated, and WITHOUT that consent where it cannot be obtained. In a country where this file has declined throughout to name domestic organisations because doing so can expose people, a channel that accepts a complaint filed on someone's behalf is worth knowing about. Complaints are accepted from citizens, foreigners, stateless persons AND LEGAL ENTITIES. ITS OTHER POWERS WHEN IGNORED: escalating to the higher instance of the body concerned or to other state bodies; REFERRING THE MATTER FOR A CRIMINAL CASE where signs of a crime appear; appealing through cassation; PUBLISHING THE RESULTS OF ITS INSPECTIONS IN THE MASS MEDIA; and, where a violation is of SPECIAL PUBLIC IMPORTANCE and its own means are insufficient, applying to the President and speaking with a report before parliament. Publication and escalation are what make an ignored complaint costly. IT IS NOT ONLY IN THE CAPITAL: it operates regional centres in several named cities. Established at the end of 2001 under a constitutional law, with a published telephone number. THE LIMITS, AND THEY ARE REAL. It is a state institution, and it CANNOT EXAMINE the President, members of parliament or judges. Its independence in practice is a judgement this file does not make for you — and this payload records a digital security helpline for this country precisely because of documented risk. Weigh what a written complaint discloses, and consider having an organisation file it rather than a household.

trackers.name: Environmental Defender Law Center — pro bono lawyers, a funded expert, and money for litigation expenses
trackers.desc: IT DOES THREE THINGS, ALL WITHOUT CHARGE, AND THE SECOND CLOSES THE GAP THIS FILE HAS FOUND IN ALMOST EVERY COUNTRY. It FINDS LAWYERS — enlisting private firms to act pro bono for communities facing harm from projects affecting their health, land and way of life, for people CHARGED OR IMPRISONED IN POLITICALLY MOTIVATED PROSECUTIONS, and for land claims. IT PROVIDES RESOURCES — advising LOCAL lawyers running domestic cases, preparing and submitting legal briefs, and giving ACCESS TO EXPERT NETWORKS where experts frequently work pro bono or at reduced fee AND IT IS OFTEN ABLE TO FUND THEIR EXPENSES. A community here can describe what a scheme is doing to its water, its air or its ground; what it cannot do is pay a qualified person to prove it. THIS IS THE BODY THAT FINDS THAT PERSON AND PAYS FOR THEM. AND IT GIVES GRANTS FOR THE EXPENSES OF LITIGATION — a programme running since 2010, roughly a hundred grants made, aimed at the costs of public interest cases against those responsible for resource development projects. Expenses rather than fees are what kill cases: filing costs, translation, travel, expert reports. ITS METHOD IS WORTH ADOPTING EVEN IF IT NEVER TAKES YOUR CASE: it INTERNATIONALISES the issue, showing decision-makers that the acts complained of breach international human rights norms AND THE GOVERNMENT'S OWN TREATY OBLIGATIONS. This file has recorded that this country is party to conventions on environmental information and participation; an argument framed against commitments the state has itself accepted travels further than one framed as objection. WHY IT SUITS THIS COUNTRY PARTICULARLY: this chat has declined throughout to name domestic organisations here because doing so can expose people, and it records a digital security helpline and an ombudsman with power to go to court. AN OUTSIDE BODY THAT RECRUITS LAWYERS AND FUNDS EXPERTS WITHOUT REQUIRING A LOCAL ORGANISATION TO EXIST IS THE KIND OF SUPPORT THAT FITS THAT SITUATION. THE LIMITS. It works in developing countries and specialises in cases of INTERNATIONAL SIGNIFICANCE where a strategy can later be replicated — a purely local dispute with no wider bearing may not qualify. It is funded by foundation grants and donations and based abroad, so approaching it is a foreign contact, which in this country is a decision to weigh alongside the security guidance recorded here. Contact is by email, and eligibility and how to apply must be asked directly.

trackers.name: BankTrack — find out which banks finance the project, then use their own complaint channels
trackers.desc: THIS MAP TELLS COMMUNITIES HOW TO COMPLAIN TO A PROJECT'S FINANCIERS AND HAS NEVER TOLD THEM HOW TO FIND OUT WHO THE FINANCIERS ARE. This organisation does that, and says so plainly: it offers RESEARCH SUPPORT, ASSISTING IN RESEARCHING THE FINANCIAL ARCHITECTURE OF SPECIFIC DEALS AND SECTORS, and states it is ready to assist COMMUNITIES AND THE ORGANISATIONS REPRESENTING THEM in dealing with banks financing activities that directly affect their rights and interests. IT ALSO KEEPS A PUBLIC DATABASE LINKING NAMED BANKS TO NAMED PROJECTS AND COMPANIES, so the financing behind a scheme near you may already be mapped before you ask. This country's listing holds two corporate accountability organisations that help communities bring complaints; what none of them supplies is THE NAME OF THE LENDER, and that name is what makes those channels usable. ONCE YOU HAVE IT, THEIR GUIDE TELLS YOU WHERE TO TAKE IT: banks' OWN GRIEVANCE MECHANISMS, their WHISTLEBLOWING CHANNELS, OECD NATIONAL CONTACT POINTS, UN SPECIAL PROCEDURES, the independent accountability mechanisms of development banks, industry-level mechanisms, and a dedicated complaints channel for projects financed under the Equator Principles — with guidance on the extent and LIMITS OF BANKS' DUTIES OF CONFIDENTIALITY. Confidentiality is the standard refusal, and knowing its limits is the difference between accepting it and answering it. THEY ALSO RECORD WHAT BANKS ACTUALLY SAY: a response-tracking database scores how banks replied to specific allegations, including one that answered by citing client confidentiality and declining to comment on data linked to its clients. Read those before writing, so the reply does not surprise you. AND THEY WILL MAKE THE SCHEME VISIBLE: they offer space to profile a company or project alongside its financiers, and a community can ask to be listed in the RESISTANCE section of a given deal. THE LIMITS, AND THE FIRST IS A DECISION ONLY YOU CAN MAKE. BEING PROFILED IS PUBLIC. In a country where this file has declined throughout to name domestic organisations because visibility endangers people, asking to appear in a public campaign listing is a serious step — read this with the digital security helpline recorded separately here, and note that RESEARCH SUPPORT AND A PRIVATE ENQUIRY REQUIRE NO PUBLIC PROFILE AT ALL. They target COMMERCIAL banks rather than the state, and they campaign rather than litigate.

trackers.name: Caucasus Nature Fund — it pays the running costs, which is what nobody funds
trackers.desc: THIS FILE CAN NOW TELL A COMMUNITY IN EVERY COUNTRY OF THIS REGION HOW TO GET LAND PROTECTED. IT HAS ALMOST NOTHING ON WHO PAYS FOR IT AFTERWARDS — the wardens, the fences, the fuel, the plans. THIS FUND EXISTS FOR EXACTLY THAT: its mission is LONG-TERM FUNDING FOR OPERATING COSTS, improved management and the sustainable development of the region's protected areas. It supports EIGHTEEN PROTECTED AREAS across this country and its two neighbours, from an endowment of around twenty-four million euro, and it was founded in 2007 by an international conservation organisation, a European development ministry and a global wildlife fund. ITS DESIGN IS THE PART TO UNDERSTAND BEFORE APPROACHING IT, BECAUSE IT IS BOTH A LEVER AND A VULNERABILITY. THE FUND WORKS THROUGH PUBLIC-PRIVATE PARTNERSHIPS WITH THE THREE GOVERNMENTS BY MATCHING, BUT NOT EXCEEDING, THE STATE BUDGETS — so each side commits long-term support and neither can quietly withdraw. The lever is that a government cutting its protected-area budget also loses the matching money, which is an argument to put in public. The vulnerability is that the fund follows official priorities: IT WILL NOT PAY FOR A SITE THE STATE DOES NOT FUND, so it cannot be used to protect ground the authorities have decided to develop. WHAT THAT MEANS PRACTICALLY FOR A COMMUNITY HERE. If the ground you are defending lies inside or beside an existing protected area, this is where the money for managing it comes from, and a case for strengthening that area's management is a case this fund is built to hear. If your ground is outside the protected area system, the contractual conservation fund recorded separately for this country — which pays communities to hold land under agreement — is the nearer instrument. THE LIMITS, PLAINLY. IT FUNDS PROTECTED AREAS RATHER THAN LAND PURCHASE, and mostly state ones. It is headquartered in Germany with programme offices in the two neighbouring capitals AND HAS NO OFFICE IN THIS COUNTRY, so an approach goes through the region rather than locally. And a fund whose method is matching government budgets is a partner of the government, not an opponent of it — read that alongside everything else this file records about naming yourself in this country.

trackers.name: National hydrological committee chair — a named hydrometeorologist at the state university
trackers.desc: THIS FILE HAS REFUSED THROUGHOUT TO NAME DOMESTIC ORGANISATIONS IN THIS COUNTRY, BECAUSE NAMING THEM CAN EXPOSE PEOPLE. AN ACADEMIC POST IS DIFFERENT: THE CHAIRPERSON OF THE NATIONAL HYDROLOGICAL COMMITTEE HOLDS THE CHAIR OF HYDROMETEOROLOGY AT THE STATE UNIVERSITY, and is published as this country's contact for the international water science programme. That is an institution and a professional post, not an activist — the same boundary this file drew when recording a bar's assistance office and a constitutional complaints commission in another restricted country. WHAT HYDROMETEOROLOGY ACTUALLY HOLDS IS THE POINT. Rainfall series, river flow records, flood frequency, drought history — THE DATA UNDERNEATH ANY CLAIM ABOUT A WATERCOURSE. A scheme proposed on a floodplain, a diversion that will change a flow, an abstraction that will lower a water table: each of those is an argument about numbers that already exist in a university department. This file has said in almost every country that communities cannot afford to prove harm. A UNIVERSITY CHAIR HOLDS THE MEASUREMENTS ALREADY, and a request for published records costs nothing. ASK FOR WHAT IS ALREADY PUBLISHED, AS THIS FILE LEARNED A ROUND EARLIER: an existing record cannot be dismissed as evidence commissioned by objectors, and a flood series held by a state university is the state's own science. AND ASK WHO ELSE SITS ON THE COMMITTEE. The programme's council recommends that these national committees be MULTI-STAKEHOLDER IN MEMBERSHIP, including not only scientists and water managers but government bodies, professional associations AND CIVIL SOCIETY — so asking which civil society bodies are members, or asking to be included, is asking for what the programme itself says should exist. In a country where independent organisations are hard to identify at all, THE COMMITTEE'S MEMBERSHIP LIST IS A MAP OF WHO WORKS ON WATER HERE. THE LIMITS. The committee is constituted and runs under the authority of the national government, so it is not independent; the chairperson is an academic who will not advocate for anyone; and no direct telephone number was published in what was reached, so an approach goes through the university's hydrometeorology department. Frame the request as a technical question about records for a named place, and read this alongside the digital security helpline recorded separately for this country before making contact.

trackers.name: Bar legal aid centre — an address, a telephone, an email and opening hours
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING HELD A STATE COMMISSIONER AND AN INTERNATIONAL PRO BONO NETWORK AND NO DOMESTIC WAY TO REACH A LAWYER. THE BAR'S PRESIDIUM CREATED A LEGAL AID AND TRAINING CENTRE THAT HAS OPERATED SINCE 26 DECEMBER 2019, AND IT PUBLISHES A STREET ADDRESS IN THE CAPITAL, A TELEPHONE NUMBER, AN EMAIL ADDRESS ON THE BAR'S OWN DOMAIN, AND OPENING HOURS OF HALF PAST NINE TO FOUR ON WEEKDAYS. Very few entries in this entire payload carry all four. THERE IS A SECOND DOOR AT THE SAME HOURS: THE JUSTICE ACADEMY'S LAW CLINIC. Two separate places to ask, in a country where this file has been able to name almost nothing domestic. WHAT TO TAKE WITH YOU, BECAUSE ARRIVING WITHOUT IT WASTES THE VISIT: AN APPLICATION REQUESTING FREE LEGAL AID, AND A DOCUMENT PROVING THAT YOU FALL WITHIN A CONCESSION CATEGORY — an income certificate, a disability certificate, a veteran's document or the equivalent. THE CONCESSION CATEGORY IS THE GATE, so establish which category you might fall into before you go, and take the paper that proves it. THE ENTITLEMENT IS CONSTITUTIONAL, WHICH IS WORTH SAYING IN THE APPLICATION ITSELF: ARTICLE 61 OF THE CONSTITUTION GUARANTEES EVERYONE THE RIGHT TO HIGH-QUALITY LEGAL AID AND, IN THE CASES PROVIDED BY LAW, LEGAL AID FREE OF CHARGE AT STATE EXPENSE. Note the words HIGH-QUALITY: the guarantee is not merely of a lawyer but of a competent one. AND THE STATE HAS PUT MONEY BEHIND IT. A PRESIDENTIAL ORDER PROVIDED FOR PREMISES FOR THE COLLEGIUM'S STRUCTURES IN THE CAPITAL AND IN THE REGIONS, AND FOR TRIPLING THE SUM PAID FOR STATE-FUNDED LEGAL AID. That matters more than it sounds: this file found next door that assigned counsel underperform largely because assignment pays badly, so a threefold increase is the single most likely thing to improve the service a person actually receives. NOW THE SCALE PROBLEM, AND IT IS SEVERE. REPORTING CITES ONE LAWYER PER TEN THOUSAND PEOPLE IN CRIMINAL MATTERS, and a dedicated free legal aid law remains AT CONCEPT STAGE, discussed as covering FOUR REGIONS INITIALLY. Expect scarcity, apply early, and ask at both doors rather than one. THE OTHER LIMITS: this is the bar's own centre and a state-funded scheme, so it is not independent; the contact details published for the centre should be confirmed by telephone before travelling; and a concession-category gate means an ordinary landowner in a property dispute may not qualify — ASK WHICH CATEGORIES AND WHICH CASE TYPES ARE COVERED BEFORE BUILDING ANY PLAN ON IT.

trackers.name: State support agency for NGOs — an annual grant cycle with published ceilings, and a round that only coalitions could enter
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING HELD ONLY FOREIGN GRANT WINDOWS. THERE IS A DOMESTIC ONE, IT RUNS ON A FIXED ANNUAL CYCLE, AND THE DATES ARE PUBLISHED: SMALL, MEDIUM AND LARGE COMPETITIONS FOR 2026 OPENED FOR DOCUMENTS ON 22 SEPTEMBER 2025, CLOSED ON 22 OCTOBER 2025, and results were to be announced IN THE FIRST QUARTER OF 2026 after expert review. An organisation that misses the autumn window waits a year, so the date matters more than the wording of any proposal. THE CEILINGS ARE PUBLISHED TOO. In a joint competition with the ecology ministry the MEDIUM COMPETITION CARRIED UP TO 30,000 MANAT AND THE LARGE UP TO 50,000, each with an implementation period of UP TO SIX MONTHS. SIX MONTHS IS THE PLANNING CONSTRAINT: this funds a season of work — a survey, a planting, a monitoring round, a training programme — not a multi-year defence of a site. Design the project to finish. AND THE CONDITION WORTH KNOWING BEFORE YOU START IS THE MOST UNUSUAL THING IN THIS ENTRY: IN THAT ENVIRONMENTAL ROUND, ORGANISATIONS COULD TAKE PART ONLY AS A COALITION. The funder required them to combine before it would consider them at all. Where a funder demands coalitions, THE RELATIONSHIPS ARE THE ELIGIBILITY — and they cannot be built in the month before a deadline. If your group is alone, the useful work between now and the next window is finding the two or three other bodies you could apply with. ENVIRONMENTAL THEMES REACH THIS FUNDER MAINLY THROUGH JOINT COMPETITIONS WITH THE ECOLOGY MINISTRY rather than as a standing window, so watch both bodies' announcements rather than only the agency's. THE AGENCY DOES THREE OTHER THINGS WORTH KNOWING: it CONDUCTS EXPERT REVIEW of the projects submitted to it, which means a rejected proposal has been assessed and the assessment can be asked about; it ALLOCATES FUNDS FOR NGOs TO TAKE PART IN INTERNATIONAL EVENTS, which is a separate and much smaller ask than a project grant and a way to put a local problem in front of an outside audience; and it MONITORS THAT STATE-BUDGET GRANTS ARE USED FOR THEIR STATED PURPOSE, so reporting obligations are real. THE LIMITS, AND THEY ARE THE SAME ONES THIS FILE ATTACHES TO EVERYTHING IN THIS COUNTRY. IT IS A STATE AGENCY DISBURSING STATE-BUDGET MONEY ON THEMES THE GOVERNMENT SETS; nothing found shows it funding work that opposes a development. Applying identifies your organisation and its members. And grants go to registered non-governmental organisations, so an unregistered group must first constitute itself or join a coalition with a body that already has. Read this with the digital security helpline recorded separately here.

trackers.name: State nurseries that give saplings to citizens, and the planting campaign to join
trackers.desc: THIS FILE ASKED TWO ROUNDS AGO WHERE RESTORATION PLANTS COME FROM. HERE IS THE PLAINEST ANSWER IT HAS FOUND: IN A SINGLE SPRING SEASON, MORE THAN 121,000 TREE SAPLINGS GROWN IN THE ENVIRONMENT MINISTRY'S OWN NURSERIES WERE DISTRIBUTED TO CITIZENS, TO EXECUTIVE AUTHORITIES, AND TO STATE AND PRIVATE ORGANISATIONS. CITIZENS ARE NAMED AS RECIPIENTS — the trees exist, they are grown at public expense, and they are handed out. ASK THE FORESTRY SERVICE WHICH NURSERY SERVES YOUR DISTRICT, WHAT SPECIES IT HOLDS, WHEN DISTRIBUTION OPENS, AND WHAT A COMMUNITY GROUP MUST DO TO RECEIVE A CONSIGNMENT. That is a request for something already budgeted, not a favour. THE CAMPAIGN AROUND IT IS THE WAY IN. A JOINT PLANTING CAMPAIGN RUN BY THE ENVIRONMENT MINISTRY WITH A PUBLIC UNION PUT MORE THAN 400,000 FOREST TREES INTO OPEN AREAS OF THE STATE FOREST FUND IN ONE SPRING AND SOWED MORE THAN FOUR TONNES OF SEED to assist forest restoration — with state bodies, private companies, media, VOLUNTEERS AND CIVIL SOCIETY REPRESENTATIVES all named as taking part. A community that wants its own degraded hillside or riverbank planted is asking to be included in something that already exists and already counts its results. THE CIVIL VEHICLE IS A PUBLIC UNION FOUNDED IN JULY 2011 for environmental awareness, work with young people and education. Two of its projects are worth copying anywhere. IT PLANTS FRUIT ORCHARDS IN THE REGIONS AND HANDS THEM OVER FREE OF CHARGE FOR THE USE OF LOW-INCOME FAMILIES — restoration that produces food and income for named households, which is the form hardest for any authority to refuse. AND IT PLANTS TREES CHOSEN TO SUIT THE SOIL AND CLIMATE of the area rather than whatever is available, which is the difference between a plantation that survives and one that dies in its second summer. It also works on restoring green cover in residential courtyards, and holds observer membership of the United Nations climate convention process. AND THE ROUTES IN THIS MAP NOW JOIN UP. This file recorded at R363 the state agency that runs grant competitions for organisations here. A LOCAL ECOLOGICAL UNION HAS USED EXACTLY THAT AGENCY'S FINANCIAL SUPPORT TO RUN A TREE-PLANTING ACTION ON A RIVER. SO THE FULL SEQUENCE IS AVAILABLE: A GRANT FROM THE AGENCY, SAPLINGS FROM THE MINISTRY'S NURSERIES, AND A NATIONAL CAMPAIGN TO PLANT UNDER — none of which requires a community to buy anything. THE LIMITS, AND THEY ARE THE SAME ONES THIS FILE ATTACHES TO EVERYTHING IN THIS COUNTRY. These are state and state-linked bodies; planting happens where the authorities agree, and nothing here will be turned against a development the government supports. Participation is public and identifies those who take part. AND PLANTING IS NOT PROTECTION — trees on ground without status can be cleared, so ask what status the planted area will have before choosing where to put them.

trackers.name: The environment ministry's public council — a seat civil society elects, and who may stand for it
trackers.desc: IN THE MOST RESTRICTED COUNTRIES THIS FILE HAS RECORDED WHAT THE STATE OFFERS AND LITTLE THAT COMMUNITIES CONTROL. HERE IS A STATUTORY BODY ATTACHED TO THE ENVIRONMENT MINISTRY WHOSE MEMBERS ARE ELECTED BY CIVIL SOCIETY INSTITUTIONS, UNDER A 2013 LAW ON PUBLIC PARTICIPATION AND A 2014 REGULATION SETTING OUT HOW THE ELECTION RUNS. AND THE COMPOSITION OF THE ELECTION COMMISSION IS THE PART THAT MATTERS: IT HAS NINE MEMBERS — FOUR FROM THE AUTHORITY AND FIVE FROM CIVIL SOCIETY INSTITUTIONS, and for a ministry those five come from bodies SPECIALISED IN THAT FIELD. CIVIL SOCIETY HOLDS THE MAJORITY ON THE COMMISSION THAT RUNS THE ELECTION. That is a real, written allocation of control, and it is worth knowing before assuming the process is decorative. WHO MAY STAND IS WIDER THAN ANYONE EXPECTS: ANY CAPABLE CITIZEN AGED SIXTEEN OR OVER with knowledge or experience in ecology and natural resources — expressly regardless of race, nationality, language, religion, sex, origin, PROPERTY STATUS, position, belief, or membership of any party, union or association. A SIXTEEN-YEAR-OLD FROM A VILLAGE WITH REAL KNOWLEDGE OF ITS RIVER OR PASTURE IS ELIGIBLE, and so is someone with no property and no institutional position. THE NOMINATION RULES REWARD ORGANISATION. EACH CIVIL SOCIETY INSTITUTION — NGOs, public associations, trade unions, committees, FOUNDATIONS — MAY NOMINATE ONLY ONE CANDIDATE, so a coalition must agree on a single name rather than splitting its vote. AND THIS IS THE PROVISION MOST GROUPS MISS: INSTITUTIONS THAT NOMINATE NOBODY MAY STILL TAKE PART IN THE ELECTION, by registering their representatives with the commission TEN DAYS BEFORE THE VOTE. A SMALL LOCAL BODY WITH NO CANDIDATE OF ITS OWN STILL HAS A VOTE — which means a network of village associations can decide who sits on the council. WHAT THE COUNCIL CAN THEN DO: MAKE PROPOSALS ON DRAFT LEGAL ACTS concerning state policy in its field, and COLLECT, GENERALISE AND SUBMIT CIVIL SOCIETY PROPOSALS ON SOCIALLY SIGNIFICANT ISSUES to central and local executive and self-government bodies. It may form COMMITTEES, COMMISSIONS, EXPERT GROUPS AND WORKING GROUPS, AND DRAW IN EXPERTS, SCIENTIFIC ORGANISATIONS AND INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATIONS. A COUNCIL WORKING GROUP IS A LAWFUL WAY TO PUT OUTSIDE EXPERTISE IN FRONT OF A MINISTRY. NOTE ALSO THAT THESE COUNCILS EXIST AT LOCAL EXECUTIVE AND SELF-GOVERNMENT LEVEL TOO, not only at ministries — which is the level most land disputes are decided at, and the level where a village body's five-member share of a commission is most achievable. THE LIMITS, STATED PLAINLY AND PARTLY BY THE COUNCILS THEMSELVES: THIS IS A CONSULTATIVE BODY. It advises, proposes and submits; it does not decide, and it cannot stop a project. A council chair has been quoted saying the country has good laws and that the gap is the absence of mechanisms. Elections are organised by the authority the council will advise, and membership is public. USE IT AS A ROUTE FOR EVIDENCE AND PROPOSALS, ALONGSIDE THE ENVIRONMENTAL INFORMATION CENTRE AND THE GRANT AGENCY RECORDED SEPARATELY HERE — not as a substitute for them.

trackers.name: Rivers without Boundaries (RwB)
trackers.desc: An international coalition of NGOs and experts working to save transnational rivers across north-east Asia, with its own named Mongolia coordinator. WHO TO ENLIST: the place to start when the threat is a dam, a reservoir or placer gold mining in a river basin. It runs independent hydropower assessments, maps threatened basins including the Selenga, Kherlen, Onon and the Mongolian Great Lakes, and tracks where mining licences sit relative to water-protection zones. You CAN: draw on its river-by-river document files and on its record of backing Mongolian herder movements pressing for enforcement of the 2009 law restricting mining near rivers, headwaters and forests. For activists: its work extends into Russia and China too, but Mongolia is the country for which it names a coordinator on its own site, so that is where this entry sits — ask about elsewhere.

trackers.name: General Authority for State Registration
trackers.desc: National — state register of legal entities (companies), Mongolia. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Mongolian National Audit Office
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Mongolia, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: IAAC
trackers.desc: Mongolia's Independent Authority Against Corruption, which also publishes officials' asset declarations.

trackers.name: General Authority for State Registration

trackers.desc: Supreme Court of Mongolia — supreme court (Mongolia).

trackers.name: Government e-Procurement
trackers.desc: National public-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Mongolia, and for how much.

trackers.name: Nukhurlul — herder communities named themselves into the civil code
trackers.desc: AN ORIGIN WORTH KNOWING. Nukhurlul is the name the early herder communities in the Gobi gave themselves — and during the 2000–2004 legislative period, South Gobi members of parliament introduced community organisations into Mongolia's civil law under that chosen name, as rural civil society organisations. Communities self-organised, named themselves, and the legislature adopted both the institution and the name; elsewhere in this map communities apply into categories drawn up for them. WHAT RECOGNITION UNLOCKED: it allowed contracts on communal land management to be made between local government and the communities, giving them legal standing to contract with the soum — not a designation, but the capacity to hold an agreement. Community organisations now protect wetlands, local protected areas and prehistoric sites. THE ASSESSED OUTCOME, in respondents' words: through the process they learned to express opinions and talk to the governor, and learned to have a stronger voice — many active communities made the soum governor listen and influenced pasture management plans. EXPECT THIS QUESTION IN THE ROOM: the assessment literature asks whether donor support has built a parallel structure to the territorial administrative structure, and whether local government sees community organisations as a threat. WHERE TO ENGAGE: soum and bag levels, aimag and soum khurals, and buffer zone councils, whose head sits within the Soum Khural.

trackers.name: Eternal Mongolia and GEF — a third of the money is outside protected areas
trackers.desc: TWO ROUTES, AND THE LARGER ONE TARGETS COMMUNITIES DIRECTLY. Eternal Mongolia is a Project Finance for Permanence partnership between The Nature Conservancy and the Government of Mongolia toward the country's 30x30 goals, mobilising about USD 198 million over 15 years. Its three targets: safeguard an additional 14.4 million hectares; strengthen management of the protected area network; and extend sustainable community-managed practices to 34 million hectares OUTSIDE protected areas, with a 2040 goal of secure community-based natural resource management involving up to 24,000 herder households. So a herder community is a target participant, not a bystander — the largest single component is community-managed land beyond the park boundaries. WATCH THE LAW REVISION: the Mongolia Nature's Legacy Foundation supports revisions to the Protected Areas Law so the 30x30 goal has clear legal frameworks and stable financing, and Mongolia approved its first Climate Change Law in the State Great Khural. FOR SMALLER, FASTER MONEY: the GEF Small Projects Programme, implemented by UNDP, gives up to USD 50,000 over up to 18 months for biodiversity conservation and sustainable agriculture — open to NGOs, CSOs and local community groups.

trackers.name: Put 'environmental protection' in your charter — a court said so
trackers.desc: THE STANDING TRAP THAT LOST A CASE BEFORE IT WAS HEARD. CHRD challenged extraction licences in Khuvsgul aimag and the court rejected its standing to sue, emphasising the absence of the words ‘environmental protection’ in its charter. Across this map the wording of an organisation's own constitution decides funding eligibility in six European countries — in Mongolia it decides access to the court itself. If your organisation might ever litigate, put environmental protection in the charter before you need it; Mongolian civil society's own recommendation was to create a legal environment allowing NGOs to sue. THE SECOND OBSTACLE IS MONEY FOR EXPERTS: expert evidence is unavoidable in environmental cases, and although the court is authorised to pay for it, it is often reluctant — in an administrative case on cancelling a uranium licence the court appointed an expert on its own initiative and the expert refused to work because the court did not pay. Budget for your own expert rather than relying on the court. WHO LITIGATES: CHRD has run public interest litigation on mining since 2005, around 40 cases on illegal licences, inadequate environmental impact assessment, water law breaches, mines left without rehabilitation and toxic contamination — and won cancellation of two illegally issued licences on the Burenkhaan phosphate deposit in 2014.

trackers.name: The Munkhbayar precedent — and what the petition actually asked for
trackers.desc: A SUPREME COURT ORDER TO ENFORCE. On 20 October 2011 the Supreme Court ruled that the government must enforce its 2009 resolution restricting mining, in a case filed by the United Movement of Mongolian Rivers & Lakes. The statute behind it prohibits mining at headwaters of rivers, protected zones of water reservoirs and forested areas, and was designed to protect up to 25 percent of Mongolia's natural ecosystems. THE PETITION IS A TEMPLATE WORTH STUDYING: it asked for assessment of damage to named river basins within 2 months, public notification of that assessment, recovery of damages from the respondent, restoration carried out by the petitioner organisation itself under contract to the respondent, enforcement of the Law, and revocation of the licences of entities operating there. Asking to be contracted to do the restoration is an unusual and powerful ask. AFTERWARDS the government began real implementation — the first batch of licences was revoked, protection zones approved, damage evaluated — and UMMRL then helped delineate the protection zones and negotiate them with local populations. BUT WINNING DID NOT END IT: after Munkhbayar's Goldman Prize for pressuring 35 of 37 operations in the Onggi basin, new companies received new licences for the same protected areas. TWO DOCUMENTS TO OBTAIN: the EIA report, and the annual environmental management plan that licence holders must file with the ministry by 1 November each year, covering subcontractor activities — a dated, ministry-held document is the most checkable obligation in the regime.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: Auditor General's Office
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Maldives, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Information Commissioner’s Office (Maldives)
trackers.desc: Information Commissioner’s Office (Maldives) — the Maldives’ independent Information Commissioner’s Office overseeing the Right to Information Act and adjudicating access-to-information appeals. — Holds to account: the Maldives’ public bodies on disclosure — find RTI appeal decisions, guidance and annual reports.

trackers.name: Information Commissioner’s Office (ICOM, Maldives)
trackers.desc: National right-to-information authority; the Maldives’ Information Commissioner’s Office is the independent oversight & appeal body under the Right to Information Act (2014) — ruling on access complaints (its decisions appealable to the courts), Maldives.

trackers.name: Maldives — Ministry of Finance
trackers.desc: National budget authority; prepares & publishes the national budget (and a dedicated budget portal) under the Fiscal Responsibility Act, Maldives. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in the Maldives.

trackers.desc: Official site of the Maldivian Supreme Court with judgments. · Find here: information and judgments of the Supreme Court of the Maldives.

trackers.name: Maldives — Ministry of Economic Development & Trade (Business Registration)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the trade regulator provides company & business-name registration services and maintains the business register, Maldives. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Protected Areas Regulation 2018/R-78 — consultation is a stated objective
trackers.desc: QUOTE THE REGULATION'S OWN OBJECTIVES BACK. Regulation No. 2018/R-78 lists six objectives, and two are about community involvement in designation: to ensure the process of protected area declaration is consultative and transparent, and to enhance awareness and participation of community in protected area designation and management. Where a designation process has excluded a community, that departs from the regulation's own stated purpose — cite those two limbs. It also aims to enlist environmentally significant areas, and it covers areas already declared and areas protected before or after it came into force, so it applies to existing sites too. THE ACT BEHIND IT, Law 4/93 (ratified 19 April 1993): the ministry identifies protected areas and reserves (s.4); an impact assessment must be submitted before any development project that may have a potential impact on the environment (s.5) — note that low threshold, not ‘significant’ impact; and the ministry has authority to TERMINATE any project that has an undesirable impact. Termination, not conditions or fines — and the test is ‘undesirable’, not ‘unlawful’. The Act declares the natural environment a national heritage.

trackers.name: Farukolhu — designation used instead of an airport, and the paper-parks answer
trackers.desc: A PRECEDENT AND A REBUTTAL. Sh. Farukolhu was designated a protected area under Act 4/93 in 2018 — recorded as a major victory because the island had previously been considered for development of an airport to boost tourism infrastructure. Its reefs are nurseries for endangered hawksbill turtles and vulnerable sicklefin lemon sharks; its mangroves and wetlands are bird nesting grounds. Designation is a demonstrated alternative to an airport in this jurisdiction. AND THE ANSWER TO ‘IT WILL NEVER BE MANAGED ANYWAY’: 93 sites have been designated in recent years while management has not kept pace — but as a conservationist puts it, paper parks are not always a bad thing, because declaring them helps earmark and preserve them rather than allocating them for industrial or tourism development. A designated site is one not allocated to something else. WHERE MONEY IS COMING FROM: the CATENATE project, US$2 million from the GEF plus US$7.5 million co-funding from the ministry, Sh. Funadhoo Council and the earlier USAID-funded REGENERATE, to manage Farukolhu and 14 other protected areas in the same atoll. An island council is a named co-funder — local councils can put money into protected area management. A CANDID NOTE: a legal handbook records that the Maldivian judiciary ‘has not yet taken an activist role in environmental management’, so administrative and designation routes are likely to outperform litigation here.

trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. trackers.name: EcoPeace Middle East
trackers.desc: Founded in 1994 as Friends of the Earth Middle East and still a member of Friends of the Earth International, EcoPeace is staffed and directed jointly by Jordanians, Palestinians and Israelis, with its own offices in Amman, Ramallah and Tel Aviv and a national director in each. WHO TO ENLIST: the office in your own country. Its Good Water Neighbors programme works with communities on either side of a shared water problem, pairing them across the border rather than treating each in isolation. You CAN get community-level organising support and technical and advocacy weight on water, sewage and Jordan Valley development. You CAN'T get a litigator — EcoPeace works by cross-border cooperation, research and advocacy, not by suing proponents, so a community that needs a permit or an approval challenged in court should look elsewhere. For activists: in Jordan and Palestine this was the only substantial environmental organisation with an office and a named national director that could be verified on its own domain.

trackers.name: Palestine — Ministry of National Economy (Companies Registry)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the MNE Companies Registry (Companies Controller) registers & regulates companies and business entities in the State of Palestine. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: State Audit & Administrative Control Bureau
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Palestine, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Palestine — Ministry of Finance & Planning
trackers.desc: National budget authority; controls public expenditure, prepares the budget, and publishes fiscal & financial reports, State of Palestine. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Palestine.

trackers.name: Supreme Constitutional Court of the State of Palestine
trackers.desc: Supreme Constitutional Court of the State of Palestine — supreme court (Palestine).

trackers.name: Establish your area classification first — it decides who has authority
trackers.desc: THE QUESTION THAT COMES BEFORE EVERY OTHER ONE. Of the 18 protected areas transferred to the Palestinian Authority under the Oslo agreements, only 8 are under actual Palestinian control, totalling less than 15 km²; the remaining 10 lie within Area C or overlapped areas. So establish your site's area classification before approaching any authority — the answer differs site by site, not governorate by governorate, and approaching the wrong body costs months. THE BODY THAT MANAGES RESERVES: the Directorate of Forests, Rangelands and Wildlife in the Ministry of Agriculture, with 4 divisions — forestry, nature reserves, rangelands and nurseries — and offices in all governorates of the West Bank, plus 40 rangers patrolling protected areas and natural forests. A governorate office with a rangelands division is the practical door, and rangelands matters where grazing land rather than forest is at issue. The Environment Quality Authority is the separate regulator, established 10 December 1996. NOTE THE LAYERED LEGAL HISTORY: Jordanian environmental laws applied in the West Bank and Egyptian in Gaza until 1967, so statutes of Jordanian origin may still be relevant — this map records Jordan's environment law separately.

trackers.name: Inspect your land physically — the appeal window is 10 days
trackers.desc: A PROCEDURAL RULE TO DIARISE. Demolition orders in the relevant administrative system are, under the rules, to be issued 10 days prior to action and are subject to appeal — and reporting records that orders are not always effectively communicated to those affected. The practical consequence is the same either way: inspect your land regularly and physically, because an order you do not find is an appeal window lost, and the window is short. THE ENFORCEMENT CHAIN THAT DOES WORK, for wildlife cases: EQA inspectors alongside the Environmental Police handed 29 illegally captured or nest-poached mammals and birds to the Nature Palestine Society in a single year — including 5 Palestine mountain gazelles, critically endangered globally — with rehabilitation at Tamoun Nature Reserve and a named EQA governorate office (Jenin) in the chain. If your issue is capture or poaching, that is a working route with named participants. TRAINING EXISTS: Nature Palestine Society has run environmental law training for young environmentalists covering national law, international conventions and the challenges that impede their enforcement. Since 2009 a sectoral working group on environment has brought together donors and national stakeholders, monitoring projects and giving environmental approvals.

trackers.name: CEPF Mediterranean Basin — Palestine is named eligible in current calls, and this is the first funding route recorded here
trackers.desc: PALESTINE IS NAMED AS AN ELIGIBLE COUNTRY IN CEPF'S OWN CURRENT CALLS FOR PROPOSALS, IN BOTH THE SMALL AND LARGE GRANT WINDOWS. The small-grants call ran from 9 February to 15 March 2026, offering twenty to fifty thousand US dollars from a total of five hundred and forty thousand, restricted to conservation of threatened freshwater biodiversity, with projects starting 1 August 2026 and completing by 30 September 2027; the regional implementation team scheduled its English-language webinar with a session time given specifically for Palestine. The large-grants window opened 1 July 2026 and closes 18 September 2026, offering fifty thousand to a hundred and eighty thousand dollars under two directions: traditional land use practices, and preservation of threatened plant species. LOCAL AND NATIONAL NGOS ARE EXPLICITLY PRIORITISED in the small-grants call. ELIGIBILITY: applicants must be legally registered entities holding their own bank accounts with authorisation under national law to receive charitable funding; individuals cannot apply directly but may work with a qualifying organisation. Letters of inquiry are submitted through the ConservationGrants portal in English or French; the regional implementation team is BirdLife International together with DOPPS. WHY THIS ENTRY NAMES NO PALESTINIAN ORGANISATION: this map treats Palestine as a context where recording local bodies can expose the people in them, so it records international instruments only. That is a deliberate limit rather than a finding that no Palestinian organisations exist, and a reader should understand it as such. CEPF'S OWN 2024 ECOSYSTEM PROFILE STATES THAT THE SECURITY AND GEOPOLITICAL SITUATION, PARTICULARLY IN PALESTINE AND LEBANON, HAS IMPACTED INHABITANTS AND ORGANISATIONS — the fund is operating with that on the record, and anyone weighing an application should read the current call document rather than this entry for what is presently possible.

trackers.name: GEF Small Grants Programme — UNDP's Palestinian programme runs its own calls, inviting NGOs and community organisations directly
trackers.desc: UNDP'S PROGRAMME OF ASSISTANCE TO THE PALESTINIAN PEOPLE PUBLISHES ITS OWN SMALL GRANTS CALLS, INVITING NON-GOVERNMENTAL AND COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS TO SUBMIT PROPOSALS ADDRESSING LOCAL ENVIRONMENTAL PRIORITIES, with a stated emphasis on youth and women. This is the second funding route recorded for Palestine and it is structurally different from the first: where the Mediterranean hotspot fund runs on periodic regional calls decided abroad, this one is administered through a country programme with its own coordinator. THE ACCESS SEQUENCE IS WHAT TO LEARN, BECAUSE IT IS NOT A SINGLE APPLICATION: you approach the National Coordinator first, who provides the guidelines and forms; you submit a short concept paper; the coordinator pre-screens it against the programme's criteria and the Country Programme Strategy; if it passes you prepare the full proposal, in some cases supported by a planning grant; and the National Steering Committee then accepts it, rejects it, or returns it for more work. A concept paper is a far smaller investment than a full proposal, so the screening step is a genuine protection against wasted effort. MONEY COMES IN THREE INSTALMENTS — up front, mid-term against a satisfactory progress report, and a final payment on the completion report — which a community with no reserves must plan around. Grants under the core programme run up to seventy-five thousand US dollars, with up to a hundred and fifty thousand for strategic projects; older material widely quotes a fifty thousand ceiling. Focal areas are biodiversity, climate change mitigation and adaptation, land degradation and sustainable forest management, international waters and chemicals. THIS ENTRY NAMES NO PALESTINIAN ORGANISATION, DELIBERATELY: this map records only international instruments for Palestine, because naming local bodies can expose the people in them. That is a limit on what is written here, not a statement about what exists. Confirm the current call status and the coordinator before preparing anything, and read the country strategy first.

trackers.name: Prince Albert II of Monaco Foundation — Mediterranean basin funding, with a short pre-application
trackers.desc: THE MEDITERRANEAN BASIN IS ITS FIRST STATED PRIORITY AREA, and its domains cover BIODIVERSITY PROTECTION and WATER RESOURCES AND DESERTIFICATION alongside climate and renewable energy — water being the frame that fits most land disputes here. ENTRY IS CHEAP: an annual call open for one month in June, starting with a SHORT ONLINE PRE-APPLICATION rather than a full proposal, so testing whether an idea interests them costs little. IT SETS NO CEILING ON THE GRANT BUT WILL NOT EXCEED HALF THE PROJECT BUDGET — the other half must come from elsewhere. This file recorded a neighbouring case where this foundation provided additional support for a plan that another fund had already initiated; sequencing funders that way is how the fifty per cent condition is normally met, and the hotspot fund recorded separately for this country is the obvious first step in that sequence. ITS PRE-APPLICATION FORM ACCEPTS ASSOCIATIONS, COMPANIES, PUBLIC ORGANISATIONS AND INDIVIDUALS, and it makes grants to civil society organisations, foundations, public and international bodies and enterprises alike — an unusually wide range of eligible applicants. THE LIMITS: no project here was found among those it publishes, and it funds environmental work rather than objection, litigation or advocacy. It advises grant seekers to study its funded projects as the guide to its interests, which is the first thing to do before writing anything.

trackers.name: MedPAN — the network of Mediterranean protected-area managers, and you can join before you have an area
trackers.desc: MEMBERSHIP IS OPEN TO ORGANISATIONS CONTRIBUTING TO THE CREATION OF A MARINE PROTECTED AREA, NOT ONLY TO THOSE ALREADY MANAGING ONE — its own invitation asks whether your organisation manages a protected area OR is contributing to the management or creation of one. A community trying to get a stretch of coast designated therefore qualifies before it has won anything, which is unusual and is the single most useful fact here. IT GATHERS AROUND EIGHTY TO A HUNDRED MEMBER ORGANISATIONS — institutions and NGOs across the Mediterranean that either run protected areas or are creating them — which makes its membership A DIRECTORY OF PEOPLE WHO HAVE ALREADY DONE WHAT YOU ARE TRYING TO DO. This file has found repeatedly that the hardest thing to find is someone who has already succeeded at the same task nearby; a network of practitioners is that. IT ALSO GIVES MONEY, AND THIS TERRITORY IS ON ITS PUBLISHED ELIGIBLE LIST: calls for small projects of up to around twenty-five thousand euros for a single area, or up to around forty-five thousand where three or more areas cooperate on one project. Applications go by a grant application form to a published secretariat email, with a rules document setting eligibility and an online question session before the deadline. CRUCIALLY, THE CALLS ARE OPEN NOT ONLY TO THE BODY MANAGING THE AREA BUT TO OTHER ORGANISATIONS — NGOs, scientific institutions, private companies — WORKING WITH THE AUTHORITIES RESPONSIBLE FOR IT. A community organisation partnering with the relevant authority can apply. AND IT TRAINS: it runs courses to build the operational capacity of protected-area managers and holds regional workshops drawing hundreds of participants. It manages a Mediterranean protected-areas database and publishes a status report on them every four years, which is where to check what already exists along this coast. THE LIMITS: marine and coastal areas only; earlier calls required the applicant to match around a quarter of the cost; and it funds and trains management rather than opposition or litigation. Created in 2008 to coordinate a managers' network that had existed since the 1990s, non-profit, with a permanent secretariat.

trackers.name: Palestinian Hydrology Group — it monitors the water, and it builds the alternative
trackers.desc: IT HAS RUN A WATER, SANITATION AND HYGIENE MONITORING PROGRAMME SINCE 2002, AND IT MONITORS, ANALYSES AND REPORTS ON WATER QUALITY, WATER ACCESS, POLLUTION AND INFRASTRUCTURE, developing information systems including GEOGRAPHIC INFORMATION SYSTEMS. Every other entry recorded for this territory is a foreign fund, a foreign network or a state portal. THIS IS THE EVIDENCE LAYER, AND IT IS DOMESTIC — more than two decades of systematic monitoring by an organisation with offices in Ramallah, Gaza, Hebron, Jerusalem and Nablus, working across SIXTEEN GOVERNORATES. IT ALSO BUILDS THE ALTERNATIVE RATHER THAN ONLY DOCUMENTING THE PROBLEM: rainwater harvesting cisterns, SPRING DEVELOPMENT AND REHABILITATION, groundwater well rehabilitation, rain-fed catchment systems, biogas units for wastewater, and school sanitation — over eight hundred projects reaching more than three hundred thousand people. This file has recorded across the region that a worked alternative plan beats objection alone; here is a body that has built eight hundred of them. NOTE HOW IT COUNTS PEOPLE, BECAUSE IT IS THE MOST COPYABLE THING HERE: in one named village it describes 140 RIGHT HOLDERS — 69 women and girls, 71 men and boys — facing daily problems of water access. Not beneficiaries, RIGHT HOLDERS, counted and disaggregated by sex. A community that can state how many right holders a scheme affects, with the breakdown, has produced the one number an authority has to answer; an unquantified complaint has not. IT CAN BE JOINED AND STEERED: its GENERAL ASSEMBLY IS COMPOSED OF PROFESSIONALS REPRESENTING LOCAL COMMUNITIES, and that assembly ELECTS A BOARD OF DIRECTORS EVERY THREE YEARS — founded, in its own account, on citizens' right to associate for the development of resources. Very few bodies in this payload are membership organisations with elected leadership, and those that are can be influenced from below rather than merely petitioned. ITS FRAMING IS RIGHTS-BASED AND WORTH BORROWING: it works to promote the right of individual access to clean water, EQUAL AND JUST ALLOCATION of water, the involvement of marginalised groups and especially women in decision-making, and good governance in the water sector. THE LIMITS: its subject is water, sanitation and environmental resources — a land dispute unconnected to water fits it poorly. It is a development and monitoring organisation, not a litigator, and it works alongside the water authority rather than against it. Use it for the monitoring record, the mapping, the count of affected right holders and the technical alternative; take an objection to the accountability and legal routes recorded separately here.

trackers.name: ARIJ — village profiles for every locality, and the mapping that shows what official figures miss
trackers.desc: YOUR VILLAGE MAY ALREADY HAVE A PROFILE, FREE AND ONLINE, IN ARABIC AND ENGLISH. This institute publishes detailed profiles for the localities of named governorates — fact sheets, maps and aerial photographs, location and physical characteristics, history, religious and archaeological sites, population, education, health, economic activities, THE LOCAL INSTITUTIONS AND ASSOCIATIONS THAT EXIST THERE, and LOCALITY DEVELOPMENT PRIORITIES AND NEEDS — alongside fact sheets for every governorate. A community facing a scheme usually has no baseline document about itself. Check whether one already exists before commissioning anything. AND ONE THING IN THOSE PROFILES IS WORTH MORE THAN THE REST.
