Its own mapping survey found MORE AGRICULTURAL LAND THAN THE OFFICIAL STATISTICS DID — because the official survey defined agricultural area BY LAND OWNERSHIP and counted only actual holdings, EXCLUDING FRAGMENTED SMALL SEASONAL PLOTS AND HOME GARDENS, which its own survey found in high proportion. If your land is dismissed as not agricultural, the official figure may be measuring something different from what you grow. That is a checkable, documented discrepancy, and it is the kind of argument that changes what a plan is allowed to do with land. ITS GEO-INFORMATICS DEPARTMENT IS A FULL MAPPING CAPABILITY: it acquires and analyses SATELLITE IMAGES, MONITORS LAND USE CHANGE, maintains and updates a geographical database, runs tracking systems using satellite positioning, and produces atlases, interactive maps and the GIS-based village profiles themselves. CRUCIALLY IT WILL WORK FOR OTHERS RATHER THAN ONLY FOR ITSELF: it states that it supports national organisations with reports, geographical records and maps, and that it TRAINS MUNICIPALITIES AND LOCAL COUNCILS ON THE JOB in geo-informatics to improve their performance in natural resource management. A council that can produce its own maps argues differently with a developer than one that cannot, and this file has recorded across the region that councils are often the decisive actor. ITS WIDER WORK COVERS LAND USE, WATER RESOURCES, WASTEWATER AND SOLID WASTE, BIODIVERSITY AND DESERTIFICATION, ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING INCLUDING POLLUTION AND MODELLING, and the empowerment of local communities including capacity building in good governance, transparency and accountability. It monitors land use change, land expropriation and demolitions, and runs a long-standing joint monitoring project with another Palestinian land research body, funded externally, which publishes its findings publicly. THE LIMITS: it is a research and mapping institute, not a law practice or an objector — it produces the evidence and the maps, and somebody else must use them. Its village profiles vary in age, so check the date on any profile before relying on its figures. Use it with the water and sanitation organisation recorded separately here: between them they cover the mapping and the monitoring that this territory's foreign entries cannot supply.

trackers.name: Land Research Center — documents land and housing rights violations, and sits inside a pro bono legal consortium
trackers.desc: ITS ENTIRE SUBJECT IS LAND. It exists to DOCUMENT VIOLATIONS OF LAND AND HOUSING RIGHTS AND DESTRUCTIVE ACTS DIRECTED AT AGRICULTURE AND THE ENVIRONMENT, and to develop the land and the capacities of the people affected by them. Founded in 1986 and registered as an independent non-governmental body in 1999 under a numbered licence, it is a member of the international conservation union. THE MOST USEFUL THING ABOUT IT IS WHAT IT BELONGS TO: a FOUR-ORGANISATION HUMAN RIGHTS CONSORTIUM formed in 2019 with a three-year European Union grant, whose three stated components are PRO BONO LEGAL AID, COUNSELLING AND REPRESENTATION; local and international ADVOCACY TARGETING EUROPEAN UNION INSTITUTIONS AND MEMBER STATES; and capacity building — aimed at protecting marginalised communities. The other three members are legal aid and counselling organisations, including a long-established legal aid and human rights centre. This territory previously had no route to a lawyer recorded in this map at all; a documentation body that sits at the same table as three legal aid organisations is the way in. IT CAN BE JOINED AND ITS LEADERSHIP CHANGED: a GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF TWENTY-FOUR MEMBERS drawn from different professional fields, which elects a SEVEN-MEMBER BOARD EVERY THREE YEARS. That is the second Palestinian membership body recorded here in three rounds, and membership bodies can be influenced from below rather than only petitioned. KNOW WHERE IT ACTUALLY IS BEFORE YOU TRAVEL: its main Jerusalem headquarters HAS BEEN CLOSED SINCE FEBRUARY 2002 BY A MILITARY ORDER THAT IS AUTOMATICALLY RENEWED EVERY SIX MONTHS. Its working branches are in Hebron, Bethlehem and Nablus, with a published telephone number and email. IT ALSO CO-RUNS THE LONG-STANDING MONITORING PROJECT DESCRIBED IN THE ENTRY FOR THE MAPPING INSTITUTE RECORDED SEPARATELY HERE — the two work together, and a community needing both maps and documented violations should approach them as a pair. ONE THING TO WEIGH BEFORE APPROACHING IT: this organisation and its funding partners are the subject of contested characterisations by groups that monitor non-governmental bodies, including allegations about a partner organisation's political affiliations. This file records what a body does and publishes; it does not adjudicate such disputes. Read the competing accounts yourself, and understand that association with a contested organisation can itself become an argument used against a community — which this payload has recorded happening in Georgia and Kyrgyzstan in different forms.

trackers.name: JLAC — free lawyers for demolition, displacement and land confiscation cases, with mobile clinics
trackers.desc: IT TAKES PRO BONO CASES ON HOUSE DEMOLITION, FORCED DISPLACEMENT AND LAND CONFISCATION, and has done so for more than forty years. That is this map's subject stated as an organisation's core practice, and until this round the territory had no route to a lawyer recorded here at all. IT REACHES BEYOND ITS OFFICES: branches in Ramallah, Jerusalem and Salfit, PLUS MOBILE LEGAL CLINICS IN THE NORTHERN WEST BANK. This file has now recorded travelling legal services in three countries — the pattern is that where communities cannot reach a lawyer, the lawyer who matters is the one who comes to the district. AND IT WILL ACT AGAINST WHOEVER IS RESPONSIBLE, INCLUDING ITS OWN AUTHORITY. Its own pages state that the cases it adopts are NOT LIMITED to violations by the occupying power but ALSO INCLUDE VIOLATIONS BY THE PALESTINIAN NATIONAL AUTHORITY in areas under its jurisdiction, naming arbitrary dismissal from public service and political detention. A community whose own government has granted the permit, sold the land or ignored the objection needs a lawyer who will sue that government; very few bodies in this payload will, and fewer still say so in writing. IT HAS WON THE KIND OF CASE A COMMUNITY ACTUALLY FACES: its legal department overturned a DEMOLITION AND REMOVAL ORDER FOR A 1,200-METRE PRIMARY WATER PIPELINE serving a residential community of more than ten housing units. Infrastructure saved by litigation is a rarer outcome than a scheme delayed, and it shows the work reaches beyond individual homes to the services a community depends on. IT COMBINES INDIVIDUAL CASES WITH PUBLIC INTEREST LITIGATION, LEGAL REFORM, COMMUNITY AWARENESS AND ADVOCACY, and it targets poor and marginalised groups and communities specifically. Through the consortium it anchors, it and three partner organisations describe themselves as the largest providers of pro bono legal assistance in East Jerusalem, together serving around thirteen hundred people a year and having taken on 125 HOUSE DEMOLITION CASES, 370 residency cases and 525 social and economic rights cases; the consortium publishes its own telephone number and email. ITS RECORD IS CHECKABLE: it publishes factsheets, legal interventions, legal papers, and annual and financial reports. ONE THING TO WEIGH: this organisation is the subject of contested characterisations by groups that monitor non-governmental bodies, including about its funding origins and its advocacy positions. This file records what a body does and publishes and does not adjudicate such disputes — read the competing accounts, and note that association with a contested organisation can itself be used against a community, as this payload has recorded happening elsewhere in the region.

trackers.name: PARC — it builds and trains the cooperatives, which are how land gets held
trackers.desc: IT WORKS WITH FORTY-ONE COOPERATIVES, EACH OF TWENTY TO EIGHTY MEMBERS — a farmer network of something like one to three thousand households — and it TRAINS THEM AND HELPS BUILD THEM. This file established in the Jordanian case that a cooperative is the vehicle a village uses to keep its land: members agree to sell only inward, and the body holds what would otherwise be sold away. AN ORGANISATION THAT BUILDS COOPERATIVES IS THEREFORE BUILDING THE THING THAT HOLDS LAND, and it has been doing it since 1983. IT BUILDS THEM ON STATED PRINCIPLES OF DEMOCRATIC PARTICIPATION, TRANSPARENCY AND ACCOUNTABILITY, which is the difference between a cooperative that can safely hold an asset and one that cannot. THE TRAINING IS PRACTICAL RATHER THAN RHETORICAL: WATER TREATMENT SYSTEMS, STORAGE FACILITIES, quality control testing of produce, fertilisation and harvesting, FINANCING, marketing, packaging, shipping and export — delivered with its own trading arm. A cooperative that can store, test and sell its crop has an income, and this file has recorded repeatedly that a community body with its own revenue outlasts one that depends on grant cycles. ITS FOUNDING PURPOSE WAS THE LAND ITSELF: it was formed in 1983 by agronomists, agricultural engineers, pioneer farmers and veterinary doctors out of the voluntary movement, who held that specialised agricultural groups would serve farmers and THE NATIONAL GOAL OF PROTECTING THE LAND. Its work spans LAND DEVELOPMENT, WATER RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENT, poverty reduction, women's empowerment and olive oil marketing, and it reaches the West Bank including the Jordan Valley, and Gaza. TWO OF ITS PUBLISHED STRATEGIC OBJECTIVES ARE DIRECTLY USABLE: CREATING AN ENABLING LEGAL ENVIRONMENT AND GOVERNMENT POLICIES for agricultural and rural development, and ENHANCING THE ROLE OF AGRICULTURAL COOPERATIVES AND GRASSROOTS INSTITUTIONS. A community that wants its cooperative recognised, or a rule changed, is asking for something this body already works on. ITS OWN STATEMENT OF PURPOSE IS TO MOBILISE RURAL PEOPLE SO AS TO ENABLE THEM TO CONTROL THEIR RESOURCES — which is the whole of what this map is for. THE LIMITS AND THE CAUTION. It is a development organisation, not a law practice: it will not litigate, and its legal work is policy rather than casework. Its self-description is politically framed, and it is the subject of published criticism by organisations that monitor non-governmental bodies, including scrutiny of its donors. This file records what a body does and publishes and does not adjudicate such disputes — read the competing accounts, and understand, as this payload has recorded elsewhere, that association with a contested organisation can itself become an argument used against a community.

trackers.name: ACAD — agricultural micro-credit, and it lends to cooperatives as well as to farmers
trackers.desc: NOTHING ELSE IN THIS MAP LENDS FARMERS MONEY. This body is specialised in MICRO-CREDIT and business support for poor and low-income producers, and between 1988 and the end of 2013 it financed 14,773 PROJECTS WITH THIRTY-FOUR MILLION DOLLARS — AND THIRTY COOPERATIVE SOCIETIES WITH A FURTHER HALF A MILLION. THAT SECOND FIGURE IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS HERE. This file has established that a cooperative is the vehicle through which a community holds land — a village keeps its fields by having members sell only inward. A COOPERATIVE THAT CAN BORROW CAN BUY, BUILD, STORE AND SURVIVE A BAD SEASON; and a farmer who can borrow is a farmer who does not have to sell. IT WAS FOUNDED FOR EXACTLY THAT PURPOSE: established in 1988 to build the economic capacity of small farmers who were at risk of collapse, through IN-KIND FINANCING, starting in the Jordan Valley and extending to the central and northern West Bank, with a Gaza branch from 1996 and branches now in all West Bank governorates. Its support services reach beyond loans to INFRASTRUCTURE, WATER, and the strengthening of baseline organisations and COOPERATIVE SOCIETIES in marginalised rural areas. ITS STATED OBJECTIVES INCLUDE ENCOURAGING AND SUPPORTING THE DEFENCE OF THE RIGHTS OF INDIVIDUAL FARMERS AND FARMING GROUPS, and it is recorded by the land coalition it belongs to under LEGAL ASSISTANCE, LEGAL EMPOWERMENT AND ACCESS TO JUSTICE and under EFFECTIVE ACTIONS AGAINST LAND GRABBING. AND IT CARRIES THE NATIONAL LAND COALITION'S PROGRAMME, WHICH IS THE MOST CONCRETE LIST OF LAND DEFENCE MEASURES IN THIS ENTIRE MAP: awareness sessions on land governance, youth and women's empowerment, THE FENCING OF AGRICULTURAL LANDS TO RESIST EXPANSION, and THE CREATION OF COOPERATIVES. Fencing and forming a cooperative are cheap, physical and available to any village — this file recorded fencing once before, as the first protective act taken at sacred sites in Kyrgyzstan. NOW THE CAUTION, AND IT IS THE WHOLE OF THE RISK: CREDIT IS DEBT. A loan secured against land is one of the commonest ways land is finally lost, and a borrower who cannot repay in a bad year can end up handing over the very field the loan was meant to save. Ask what security is required, whether land can be taken, what happens in a season of drought or closure, and whether the cooperative rather than the household can carry the obligation. THE OTHER LIMITS: it is a lender and development organisation, not a law practice — its legal work is empowerment and advocacy rather than casework; and it operates in a contested environment where donors and organisations are subject to public scrutiny. Use it for finance, for cooperative formation, and for the fencing programme; take a case to the legal routes recorded separately for this territory.

trackers.name: Hebron University legal clinics — including one on housing rights and eviction
trackers.desc: THERE IS A CLINIC HERE SPECIFICALLY ON HOUSING RIGHTS, GIVING LEGAL ADVICE TO OWNERS AND TENANTS ON RENT INCREASES, REPAIRS AND EVICTION. In a payload of nearly three hundred entries, that is the closest thing to a property clinic anywhere in this region — every other legal body recorded in this file handles land questions incidentally, as part of a general practice, or not at all. IT IS NOT ONE CLINIC BUT A SET, EACH ORGANISED BY SUBJECT: family law, covering divorce, custody, ill-treatment and INHERITANCE; anti-violence; HOUSING RIGHTS; human rights; labour law, on workers' and employers' rights and conditions; criminal law, run in partnership with an international legal institution; women's rights, covering discrimination, education and violence; ACADEMIC FREEDOM; and juvenile and children's rights. A community can therefore approach the clinic whose subject actually fits, rather than a general enquiry desk. THE COLLEGE STATES ITS OWN AIM PLAINLY: PROVIDING FREE LEGAL AID SERVICES TO THE MARGINALISED CLASSES OF SOCIETY THROUGH THE LEGAL CLINICS — alongside moot trials, FIELD VISITS, workshops and training courses, and comparative research and international conferences on the law here and elsewhere. Field visits matter: a clinic that goes out is one that can see a site. ITS TRAINING PURPOSE IS ALSO THE COMMUNITY'S GAIN: the clinics exist to give students practice before graduation, which means supervised people with time — the resource a community usually cannot buy. AND IT SITS AT THE CENTRE OF SOMETHING LARGER: this clinic anchors a union of SIX PALESTINIAN UNIVERSITY LEGAL CLINICS formed in 2012 across the West Bank and Gaza, and has been described as a model for clinics in this territory and across the region. If this one cannot help, five others exist. The university itself is the first Palestinian university, founded in 1971, and its college of law was the first of its kind here. THE LIMITS. It is a teaching clinic, so its rhythm is academic and its capacity finite; several of its specialised clinics are advisory rather than representative. Land and planning disputes against public authorities are not among the named subjects — the housing clinic's stated scope is landlord and tenant. And the university's own record includes closures by military order lasting months and, at one point, years, so continuity cannot be assumed. Put the question to the housing clinic first, and ask whether the human rights clinic will take a land matter.

trackers.name: Independent Commission for Human Rights — an ombudsman office that handles thousands of complaints a year
trackers.desc: IT HANDLES BETWEEN TWO AND A HALF AND THREE THOUSAND COMPLAINTS EVERY YEAR — by conducting investigations, collecting the necessary data and information, following up with the concerned authorities, and settling them as quickly as possible. Almost nothing else recorded in this map states what it actually processes. A published caseload tells you the door is open, that complaints are handled rather than filed, and roughly how long a queue you are joining. IT IS THE NATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS INSTITUTION HERE AND IT OPERATES AS AN OMBUDSMAN OFFICE — the state-facing complaints body this territory's listing in this file did not have, despite twelve other entries. Established by presidential decree in 1993 under an article of the Basic Law providing for exactly such a commission, published in the official gazette in 1995, and working since 1994. ITS FUNCTIONS ARE FOUR, AND TWO ARE DIRECTLY USABLE IN A LAND DISPUTE: receiving and following up COMPLAINTS; LEGISLATIVE OVERSIGHT; PROVIDING LEGAL ADVICE; and monitoring places of deprivation of liberty. Legislative oversight means a rule or a draft law can be put to it, not only an individual grievance. AND THE MANDATE MOST WORTH ASKING IT TO USE IS ITS REPORTING POWER: it may REPORT WITHOUT RESTRICTION on the human rights situation — on SPECIFIC MATTERS or through THEMATIC REPORTS — and make recommendations to the government, to parliament and to other competent bodies. A community facing a pattern rather than a single decision can ask for a thematic report; this file has recorded repeatedly that a pattern documented in an official publication moves institutions that ignore individual letters. ON INDEPENDENCE THERE IS AN EXTERNAL VERDICT RATHER THAN THIS FILE'S OPINION: IT HOLDS FULL ACCREDITATION WITHIN THE GLOBAL ALLIANCE OF NATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS INSTITUTIONS, and it belongs to Arab, Asia-Pacific and Mediterranean networks of such institutions. It has maintained that standing while operating across a territorial and political division that has produced two administrations since 2007, and it works on both sides of it. NOW THE LIMIT THAT DECIDES WHETHER IT IS THE RIGHT DOOR AT ALL: ITS COMPLAINTS RUN AGAINST PALESTINIAN OFFICIAL BODIES. A demolition order, a land seizure or a permit refusal issued by the occupying authority is a different target, and the international accountability routes, the land documentation bodies and the legal aid organisations recorded elsewhere in this file are the ones for that. Use this commission where the decision-maker is a Palestinian ministry, municipality or authority — and note that it advises and recommends rather than representing you in court.

trackers.name: Legal Empowerment Fund — core funding for the kind of legal work this territory already does
trackers.desc: IT GIVES THE RAREST KIND OF MONEY: FLEXIBLE, RENEWABLE, LONG-TERM CORE FUNDING. The emergency fund recorded elsewhere in this file states plainly that core costs and programme costs are NOT covered; this one provides them. Core funding pays the salary of the person who answers the telephone, keeps a clinic open between cases and lets an organisation say no to work that does not fit. This payload has recorded body after body whose real weakness is that it exists only between grants. IT IS THE FIRST GRANTMAKING INITIATIVE CREATED SOLELY TO SUPPORT GRASSROOTS LEGAL EMPOWERMENT, established in 2021 and hosted by an international human rights fund, and it backs strategies of ADVOCACY, EDUCATION AND LITIGATION — describing legal empowerment as combining law with organising to build power among people affected by injustice. THAT DESCRIPTION FITS WHAT ALREADY EXISTS HERE. This map records for this territory university legal clinics organised by subject including one on HOUSING RIGHTS AND EVICTION, a union of six such clinics, a pro bono legal aid organisation working on demolition and land confiscation, a land research body and an agricultural association whose objectives include creating an enabling legal environment. Those are grantee-shaped organisations, and this is the fund built for them. KNOW THE ODDS BEFORE YOU SPEND WEEKS ON AN APPLICATION, BECAUSE THE FUND PUBLISHES THEM: a recent round gave FORTY-TWO GROUPS IN TWENTY-FOUR COUNTRIES a total of one and a half million dollars in two-year grants — AND IT RECEIVED APPLICATIONS FROM ONE HUNDRED AND FIFTY-THREE COUNTRIES REQUESTING OVER TWO HUNDRED AND THIRTY-THREE MILLION. Demand outruns supply by something like a hundred and fifty to one. Apply, but do not plan around it. TWO PRACTICAL POINTS. IT RUNS THEMATIC CALLS, including one for groups working at the intersection of legal empowerment and LAND AND ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE — watch for one covering this region rather than only the open rounds. AND ANONYMITY IS POSSIBLE: two grantees were omitted from a published list because of the sensitive nature of their work. THE LIMITS: it funds ORGANISATIONS rather than individuals or unregistered committees; grants are modest, averaging some tens of thousands of dollars over two years; and it is a foreign fund, which in a contested environment is a fact that can be used against a recipient — this file has recorded that pattern here already.

trackers.name: Palestinian Bar — a searchable lawyer directory, and a duty the bar president can invoke for someone who cannot pay
trackers.desc: TWO INSTRUMENTS, AND THE SECOND IS THE ONE PEOPLE DO NOT KNOW ABOUT. THE FIRST IS A SEARCHABLE DIRECTORY OF PALESTINIAN LAWYERS on the bar's unified portal — so a community can verify that the person it is dealing with is admitted, and find lawyers by name before instructing anyone. THE SECOND IS A DUTY WRITTEN INTO THE BAR'S OWN INTERNAL REGULATION. THE HEAD OF THE BAR MAY ASSIGN ANY LAWYER TO PROVIDE ONE FREE PROFESSIONAL SERVICE EACH YEAR, AND A LAWYER WHO REFUSES WITHOUT ACCEPTABLE REASON, OR WHO NEGLECTS THE DUTY OF DEFENDING FAITHFULLY, IS EXPOSED TO DISCIPLINARY PENALTIES. AND ONE OF THE PERMITTED FORMS OF THAT SERVICE IS DEFENDING A PERSON WHOM THE HEAD OF THE BAR HAS ESTABLISHED TO BE POOR AND UNABLE TO PAY ANY LAWYER'S FEES. So the route is not to ask a lawyer for charity but TO ASK THE HEAD OF THE BAR TO ESTABLISH POVERTY AND ASSIGN COUNSEL. That is the fourth country in this file where the bar, rather than the courts, holds a power to put a lawyer on a case. NOW THE CATCH, AND IT DECIDES WHETHER THE REQUEST WORKS. THE DUTY IS ONCE PER LAWYER PER YEAR, AND THE LIST OF QUALIFYING SERVICES ALSO INCLUDES GIVING A LECTURE TO TRAINEES, ADVISING TRAINEES, PREPARING LESSONS, ORGANISING CONFERENCES AND WRITING LEGAL ARTICLES. A lawyer can therefore discharge the entire obligation by delivering one lecture. ASK EXPLICITLY FOR THE SERVICE TO BE PROVIDED IN THE FORM OF REPRESENTATION, cite the clause on defending a person of established poverty, and put the request in writing to the head of the bar rather than to an individual advocate. KNOW WHAT IT WILL AND WILL NOT REACH: the person's poverty must be ESTABLISHED TO THE HEAD OF THE BAR, so prepare that evidence first; and one assigned service is one service, not an ongoing retainer for a long land dispute. PRACTICAL NOTE ON REACHING THEM: the bar's main website is currently under maintenance while technical and operational updates are carried out, but the unified portal and a separate lawyer services gateway operate alongside it, and the association publishes a telephone, a fax and an email address. The bar was established in 1973 and states its aim as promoting the rule of law and defending the legal rights of Palestinians. THE LIMITS: a directory confirms admission and not competence, and shows no specialism; the assignment duty is discretionary in the head of the bar and thin in volume; and the bar regulates lawyers rather than advocating for clients. Use it with the university housing rights clinic, the union of six legal clinics and the pro bono legal aid organisation recorded separately for this territory — those hold the subject expertise this route does not guarantee.

trackers.name: Engineers Association — the licence application, compulsory supervision, and how to check an engineer
trackers.desc: START WITH THE RULE IT STATES PLAINLY: UNDER THE BUILDINGS REGULATION, ANYONE INTENDING TO CARRY OUT ANY CONSTRUCTION PROJECT MUST SUBMIT AN APPLICATION TO THE COMPETENT COMMITTEE, ON THE PRESCRIBED FORM, TO OBTAIN A LICENCE. That gives a community two things at once: A NAMED BODY THAT HOLDS THE FILE for any scheme near it, and a test — if no application was made on that form, the works are unlicensed, and that is a different and simpler argument than disputing the merits of a permit. SECOND, ENGINEERING SUPERVISION OF CONSTRUCTION PROJECTS IS COMPULSORY, AND THE INSTRUMENTS ARE NAMED. A cabinet decision of 2020 amended the BUILDINGS AND PLANNING REGULATION FOR LOCAL AUTHORITIES of 2011 and brought its supervision requirement into force; supervision protocols were then signed with the municipalities of a governorate; and engineering offices are bound by the supervision instructions set out in the association's CONSULTANCY WORK MANUAL. CITE THE REGULATION BY NUMBER AND YEAR. This file has found across four countries that a named, licensed supervising engineer is the most consistent accountability handle available — that person is identifiable, their standing is checkable, and their professional body can receive a complaint about their conduct EVEN WHERE THE PERMIT ITSELF CANNOT BE TOUCHED. THIRD, YOU CAN CHECK THE ENGINEER. The association operates a lookup against its practice-of-engineering department: enter a name and verify standing before engaging anyone — or before accepting that the person supervising the site next door is entitled to be doing it. FOURTH, AND THIS IS THE SPECIALISM TO ASK FOR BY NAME: THE EVALUATION AND REHABILITATION OF EXISTING BUILDINGS AND STRUCTURES IS A LISTED FIELD WITHIN STRUCTURAL ENGINEERING. When excavation, piling or heavy vehicles crack a neighbouring house, that is the engineer who assesses it — not a general contractor, and not a lawyer. Other listed fields cover roads, traffic systems, ports, airports, railways, bridges and tall buildings, so the specialism can be matched to the project being resisted. THE ASSOCIATION IS ONE OF THE OLDEST AND LARGEST PROFESSIONAL BODIES IN THE TERRITORY, licensed in 1958 with two centres and operating from this one since 1963, grown from dozens of members to thousands, with its headquarters address published. THE LIMITS: it regulates engineers and will not object to a project on your behalf; engaging an office costs money; registration categories differ between local and Jordanian membership, which affects which funds a member belongs to but not the services above. And supervision protocols were signed with the municipalities of one governorate — ASK WHETHER THEY APPLY WHERE YOU ARE. Use it with the university housing rights clinic, the union of legal clinics and the bar's poverty-assignment route recorded separately here: the engineer establishes what is happening physically, and those carry it.

trackers.name: Registry of historic buildings — look up your own village, and the organisation that documented 50,320 buildings before anyone threatened them
trackers.desc: THE SINGLE MOST USEFUL THING IN THIS ENTRY IS THAT YOUR VILLAGE MAY ALREADY BE DOCUMENTED. THIS ORGANISATION'S REGISTRY OF HISTORIC BUILDINGS RECORDED 50,320 HISTORIC BUILDINGS IN 422 VILLAGES AND TOWNS, compiled between 1994 and 2007 and published as three volumes of detailed histories, maps and photographs covering some 420 villages across sixteen districts — AND IT IS BROWSABLE BY DISTRICT AND TOWN ON THE ORGANISATION'S OWN SITE, down to individual houses, their vaults, their courtyards and what they are used for now. DOCUMENTATION MADE BEFORE A THREAT EXISTS IS WORTH MORE THAN ANY SURVEY COMMISSIONED AFTER ONE. A record compiled years ago by architects, archaeologists and historians cannot be dismissed as got up for the dispute — GO AND SEE WHETHER YOUR OWN BUILDINGS ARE IN IT BEFORE YOU COMMISSION ANYTHING, and if they are, that entry is your starting evidence and it costs nothing. THE ORGANISATION IS A NON-PROFIT FOUNDED IN JUNE 1991 WHOSE STATED AIM IS PROTECTING AND DEVELOPING ARCHITECTURAL HERITAGE, AND IT IS DISTINGUISHED BY ITS FOCUS ON RURAL AREAS — which is where this map's work almost always is, and where heritage bodies almost never are. In thirty years it has completed MORE THAN ONE HUNDRED RESTORATION PROJECTS, including monuments in the old city of Jerusalem and the renovation of historic streets in Bethlehem, and it has been recognised internationally, including a 2006 award for best practices in improving the living environment. THE STRATEGIC INSIGHT IN ITS OWN WORK IS WORTH COPYING ANYWHERE: ITS DATA SHOWED THAT REHABILITATING FIFTY VILLAGES WOULD SAVE ROUGHLY HALF THE ARCHITECTURAL HERITAGE OF THE WHOLE COUNTRY, so it built a fifty-village programme around that finding. WHEN YOU HAVE A REGISTRY, YOU CAN WORK OUT WHERE EFFORT BUYS THE MOST — and argue for your village on that basis rather than on sentiment. AND SINCE 2001 IT HAS RUN RESTORATION AS JOB CREATION, which answers the argument every community faces: that protection costs jobs while development brings them. RESTORATION WORK EMPLOYS PEOPLE LOCALLY, AND THIS ORGANISATION HAS TWO DECADES OF EVIDENCE FOR IT. Its work also aims at community and cultural centres for marginalised groups, so a building saved becomes a building used. THE LIMITS: it is a heritage organisation and will speak to the architectural and cultural value of a place, not to its ecology or to planning law — pair it with the land research and legal bodies recorded separately here. The registry closed in 2007, so a building put up or lost since then will not appear, and buildings in it have been threatened by demolition and conflict in the years since. IT DOES NOT HOLD LAND OR PROVIDE LAWYERS.

trackers.name: Heritage award now open here — a regional fund for tangible and intangible heritage projects
trackers.desc: IN FEBRUARY 2026 A HERITAGE AWARD RUN FROM A NEIGHBOURING COUNTRY WAS EXPANDED TO INCLUDE THIS ONE. That matters because it is money and recognition for heritage work, from a source that was previously closed to organisations here. WHAT IT FUNDS: INNOVATIVE PROJECTS THAT CONTRIBUTE TO SAFEGUARDING TANGIBLE AND INTANGIBLE CULTURAL HERITAGE, aiming to promote best practice in that work. It is run by the region's oldest national heritage organisation — a non-governmental non-profit founded in 1989 — in partnership with the European Union's delegation, two banks including one operating here, and a private donor. PREVIOUS EDITIONS RAN IN 2024 AND 2025 AND HONOURED COMPLETED HERITAGE WORK, and the 2025 round had a published application deadline extended into late July — SO EXPECT AN ANNUAL CYCLE WITH A FIXED CLOSING DATE AND WATCH FOR IT, because the expansion to this country is new and the first local round is the least contested one you will ever enter. THIS FITS EXACTLY WHAT THIS COUNTRY ALREADY HAS. This file records here a registry documenting more than fifty thousand historic buildings across four hundred and twenty-two villages, compiled before any present dispute. A REGISTRY ENTRY IS THE EVIDENCE BASE; THIS AWARD IS A WAY TO FUND DOING SOMETHING WITH IT — surveying, stabilising, restoring or recording the practices attached to a place. AND INTANGIBLE HERITAGE IS EXPRESSLY WITHIN SCOPE, which is the opening for communities whose claim rests on crafts, seasonal land use, terracing, water practices or oral knowledge rather than on a listed building. THE LIMITS: it is an award decided competitively by an organisation based in another country, oriented to heritage rather than to land tenure or planning disputes, and it will not fund opposition to a scheme as such — frame the work as safeguarding, documentation or restoration. Confirm the current cycle, the eligibility rules for applicants here and the deadline before building a plan around it.

trackers.name: Documentation organisation — it takes affidavits about land loss, publishes them with legal analysis, and its law library is open to the community
trackers.desc: THE MOST USEFUL THING HERE IS THE METHOD, NOT THE REPUTATION. THIS ORGANISATION'S DOCUMENTATION OF LAND LOSS RUNS ON AFFIDAVITS TAKEN FROM THE PEOPLE IT HAPPENED TO. A published case on the confiscation of TWENTY-NINE DUNUMS of village land rests on AN AFFIDAVIT GIVEN TO IT BY THE HEAD OF THE VILLAGE COUNCIL, recording that the land was fertile and under cultivation and setting out his own account of the circumstances — published alongside analysis against the property provisions of international instruments. THAT IS A ROUTE THIS FILE HAS NOT RECORDED ANYWHERE ELSE IN TWENTY-THREE COUNTRIES: A VILLAGE COUNCIL HEAD OR AN AFFECTED LANDOWNER CAN GIVE A SWORN STATEMENT TO AN ESTABLISHED ORGANISATION AND HAVE IT PUBLISHED, DATED AND ANALYSED. The affidavit is evidence that exists outside your own files, held by a body that will still have it in ten years. THE ORGANISATION IS AN INDEPENDENT PALESTINIAN NON-GOVERNMENTAL HUMAN RIGHTS BODY BASED IN RAMALLAH, ESTABLISHED IN 1979 — among the oldest in the region — AND IN SPECIAL CONSULTATIVE STATUS WITH THE UNITED NATIONS ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL COUNCIL SINCE 2000. That status is what allows it to appear before international bodies, which is the second half of what it offers: documentation that goes somewhere. ITS STATED METHOD IS WORTH QUOTING WHEN APPROACHING IT: IT DOCUMENTS VIOLATIONS OF THE INDIVIDUAL AND COLLECTIVE RIGHTS OF PALESTINIANS IRRESPECTIVE OF THE IDENTITY OF THE PERPETRATOR, and seeks to end them through advocacy before national and international mechanisms. COLLECTIVE RIGHTS ARE NAMED ALONGSIDE INDIVIDUAL ONES — which matters for a village whose loss is communal grazing, water or access rather than one family's title. AND THERE IS A PHYSICAL RESOURCE MOST PEOPLE DO NOT KNOW ABOUT: IT KEEPS A SPECIALISED INTERNATIONAL LAW LIBRARY FOR THE USE OF ITS STAFF AND THE LOCAL COMMUNITY. A LAWYER OR A STUDENT WORKING ON A LAND CASE CAN USE IT. This file has told communities across the region to find legal materials without ever naming a library open to them. IT ALSO WORKS WITH PALESTINIAN CIVIL SOCIETY AND GOVERNMENTAL INSTITUTIONS to bring international standards into local law and policy, and prepares research, studies and interventions. THE LIMITS: it is a documentation and advocacy organisation — IT DOES NOT BUY LAND, FUND COMMUNITIES OR PROVIDE ROUTINE LEGAL REPRESENTATION, and this country's listing records separate bodies for legal aid, land research and village profiles that do those things. International advocacy produces findings and pressure over long periods, not orders that return land. AND IT OPERATES UNDER SUSTAINED PRESSURE ITSELF, INCLUDING LITIGATION AND MEASURES AGAINST IT ABROAD — which is worth knowing before relying on it as a permanent fixture.

trackers.name: Land settlement and registration — be there on survey day, and what counts as proof
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING HELD A BUILDING REGISTRY, VILLAGE PROFILES, FREE LAWYERS FOR DEMOLITION CASES AND AN ORGANISATION THAT DOCUMENTS LAND VIOLATIONS — AND NOTHING ON HOW TO GET LAND REGISTERED IN THE FIRST PLACE, WHICH IS THE STRONGEST PROTECTION THERE IS. Settlement is run by a LAND AND WATER SETTLEMENT AUTHORITY established in 2016 to SECURE AND CONFIRM PRIVATE AND PUBLIC OWNERSHIP and to RESOLVE DISPUTES OVER BOUNDARIES, OWNERSHIP, DISPOSAL AND USUFRUCT. AND THE AUTHORITY'S OWN GUIDANCE CONTAINS THE SINGLE MOST ACTIONABLE SENTENCE IN THIS ENTRY: YOUR PRESENCE ON YOUR LAND AND AT YOUR HOUSE ON THE DAY IT IS SURVEYED AND ITS BOUNDARIES ARE DEMARCATED IS A FUNDAMENTAL FACTOR IN PRESERVING YOUR RIGHTS. BE THERE ON SURVEY DAY. Boundaries are fixed by what the surveyor is shown and told on the ground; an absent owner is a boundary decided by whoever did turn up. THIS FILE RECORDED FOR ANOTHER COUNTRY THAT NEIGHBOURS' PLOTS ARE NOT MEASURED AT THE SAME TIME AND THAT OVERLAPS FOLLOW — the same risk applies here, so agree lines with neighbours BEFORE the survey and stand on the ground during it. WHAT TO BRING IS SPECIFIED: EVERY DOCUMENT YOU HOLD, INCLUDING AN EXTRACT FROM THE PROPERTY TAX REGISTER, AND ANY OTHER PAPERS SUPPORTING THE CLAIM. NOTE WHAT THAT MEANS — A TAX RECORD IS TREATED AS EVIDENCE OF OWNERSHIP. Households without a deed are not without proof, and this payload has now found tax receipts named as evidence in two separate countries. SETTLEMENT ORDERS ARE PUBLISHED AS PUBLIC ANNOUNCEMENTS, so the start of settlement in an area is knowable in advance rather than a surprise. WATCH FOR THE ORDER COVERING YOUR VILLAGE AND TELL EVERY HOUSEHOLD IN IT — a settlement round is the one moment when unregistered land can be brought onto the register cheaply and lawfully, and it does not come round often. THE PROGRAMME IS ACTIVE: THIRTY-FIVE THOUSAND DUNUMS WERE REGISTERED IN THE NORTHERN GOVERNORATES USING MODERN TECHNIQUES, a SECOND REGISTRATION PROJECT is under discussion with an international bank mission, and the authority has run training on applying ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL MANAGEMENT PROCEDURES WITHIN SETTLEMENT WORK — which is a hook for anyone whose land has environmental or social sensitivities. AND ONE FACT MATTERS ENORMOUSLY FOR THE DISPLACED: THE AUTHORITY STATES THAT IT RETAINS OFFICIAL COPIES OF THE REGISTERS OF THE SOUTHERN TERRITORY, AND WARNS AGAINST ANY DISPOSAL OF OR TAMPERING WITH PRIVATE AND PUBLIC PROPERTY. IF LOCAL RECORDS ARE DESTROYED OR INACCESSIBLE, COPIES EXIST ELSEWHERE — which is the answer to the assumption that a lost registry means a lost claim. THE LIMITS: settlement proceeds where the authority is able to operate, and registration under this system does not resolve claims arising under another authority's control — the documentation and legal bodies recorded separately here handle those. Fees, timetables and the governorates currently under settlement were not verified in this round; confirm before travelling. And a settlement round is also when weak claims are tested, so prepare documents before the surveyor arrives rather than after.

trackers.name: Federal Board of Supreme Audit
trackers.desc: National — supreme audit institution of Iraq. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Iraq.

trackers.name: Iraq — Companies Registration Directorate (Ministry of Trade)
trackers.desc: National corporate registry; the General Directorate of Company Registration at the Ministry of Trade is Iraq’s Companies’ Registrar, registering LLCs, joint-stock & foreign companies and branches under the Companies Law No. 21 of 1997 (as amended), Iraq. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Iraq
trackers.desc: Supreme Court of Iraq — supreme court in Iraq (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: Kuwait Regional Convention (ROPME) — and its Judicial Commission
trackers.desc: THE ONE BINDING ENVIRONMENTAL INSTRUMENT COVERING ALL EIGHT GULF STATES. The Kuwait Regional Convention for Cooperation on the Protection of the Marine Environment from Pollution was signed 24 April 1978 and entered into force 1 July 1979 — 30 articles, described as the basic legal instrument binding the eight States of the Region. ALL EIGHT ARE FULL PARTIES: ROPME records ‘no signatories without ratification, acceptance, approval or accession’, so unlike some regional instruments there is no signed-but-unratified state to argue about. ARTICLE II fixes the Sea Area by coordinates, from Ras Dharbat Ali (16°39'N, 53°3'30"E) to Ras Al Fasteh (25°04'N, 61°25'E) — a treaty boundary you can check a project location against. Use the term ‘ROPME Sea Area’: it was coined by the Plenipotentiaries to achieve unanimity, cooperating in spite of existing geopolitical boundaries, and it is the name all eight accepted. THE ORGAN MOST PEOPLE DO NOT KNOW EXISTS: alongside the Council and Secretariat, ROPME has a Judicial Commission, established March 1989, of 6 nationals of Member States highly qualified in international law. In a region with almost no environmental litigation route, a standing judicial commission under a ratified convention is the most significant legal fact available — though this entry does not assert that individuals may petition it; establish who may seise it first. AN EVIDENCE SOURCE THAT NEEDS NO SITE ACCESS: ROPME's scientific bodies include a Remote Sensing Unit, alongside RIIS and MEMAC. WHICH PROTOCOL FITS YOUR ISSUE: oil-spill emergency response; land-based sources of pollution — the limb for a coastal development, discharge or reclamation; and transboundary movement of hazardous wastes. Development is named as a stressor in ROPME's own statement of purpose. At stake: over 20 species of dolphin and whale, all five subtropical turtle species, and more than 1,000 fish species, most endemic.

trackers.name: Nature Iraq — it mapped 82 Key Biodiversity Areas with the environment ministry, and it is the region's only Waterkeeper member
trackers.desc: THE FIRST QUESTION FOR ANY IRAQI SITE IS WHETHER IT IS ONE OF THE 82. Nature Iraq ran the Key Biodiversity Areas programme with the Iraqi Ministry of Environment and BirdLife International, surveying the country in the field from 2004 to 2010, and identified eighty-two sites as globally important for biological diversity. If your land is one of them, the case that it matters has been made jointly with the ministry itself rather than by you, which is a fundamentally stronger position than an unsupported objection. Ask what the survey recorded at your location. ON RIVERS IT IS BLUNTER THAN ALMOST ANY ORGANISATION IN THIS FILE, AND ITS OWN WORDS ARE THE REASON TO CALL IT: it states that government decision-makers view the rivers as abstract resources they can pollute, divert, drain and trade away without regard to the communities and ecosystems destroyed in their wake, and that its water resources projects exist to inform local communities what is happening and what they can do to influence those decisions. That is an organisation that says out loud what a dam or diversion actually is. It is also the only Middle Eastern member of the Waterkeeper Alliance, a network built specifically around defending particular rivers and waterways, which gives an Iraqi river dispute an international channel that does not otherwise exist in this region. WHO AND WHERE: an Iraqi non-governmental organisation registered in Iraq and the Kurdistan Region, accredited to the United Nations Environment Programme, an IUCN member and Iraq's first and only BirdLife International affiliate, created in the early 2000s. Offices in Sulaimani, Baghdad and Chubayish in the marshes, and it runs two field camps — one on Peramagroon Mountain, one at Chibayish near the proposed Mesopotamian Marshlands National Park. Contact info@natureiraq.org and the published Iraqi telephone numbers; it states that volunteers are welcome. Its stated goals include building the capacity of Iraqi institutions, developing a scientific database of environmental conditions through monitoring and research, and promoting community-based environmental centres and clubs. TWO THINGS TO WEIGH: much of the KBA fieldwork dates from 2004 to 2010, and a separate body, the Iraqi Organization for Conservation of Nature, has conducted later surveys — so ask which organisation holds the current data for your area. And this is a research, monitoring and advocacy organisation rather than a litigator or a landholder; it will document your site and speak publicly, not take a case.

trackers.name: Rufford Small Grants — Iraq is named eligible, and an individual can apply without an organisation behind them
trackers.desc: IRAQ IS NAMED ON THE FOUNDATION'S OWN ELIGIBILITY PAGE, AND THE APPLICANT CAN BE A PERSON. That matters in a country this map records under a restriction against listing local organisations: a researcher or community member can seek funding in their own name without a registered body, and this file names no Iraqi organisation in doing so. NO DEADLINES — applications go in at any time of year, which suits work that has to fit around conditions rather than a funding calendar. The focus is people early in a conservation career, particularly current or recent MSc and PhD students, though others may apply against the published criteria; undergraduates are excluded. CHECK THE SPECIES TEST BEFORE YOU WRITE: the foundation considers work on any species not listed as Least Concern globally on the IUCN Red List, and also species not yet assessed but believed globally threatened. Projects on threatened habitats, human-wildlife conflict or community education qualify without a species focus at all — relevant where the issue is a marsh, a river or a landscape rather than an animal. STAGED FUNDING: up to £7,000 first, then a second grant, a Booster and a Completion Grant, reaching around £18,000, each stage conditional on finishing the last and filing updates and a final report which are then published on the applicant's own page. PLAN AROUND THE RULES: one application per twelve months, twelve months' wait after a rejection, the foundation covering between half and all of the cost, and evidence of co-funding required if others are contributing. Pure research without conservation benefit and self-funded expeditions are excluded. Pair with the Key Biodiversity Areas record held by the Iraqi organisation recorded elsewhere in this file: a project inside one of the eighty-two identified sites has a far stronger case than one that is not.

trackers.name: Humat Dijlah — a national river movement whose stated purpose is protecting water bodies from dams
trackers.desc: ITS OWN STATED AIM IS STRENGTHENING THE PROTECTION OF IRAQI RIVERS, MARSHES AND WATER BODIES FROM THE DANGERS OF DAMS — which makes it one of the few bodies in this entire payload that exists to oppose infrastructure rather than to manage land around it. It describes itself as a social environmental movement operating at NATIONAL SCALE, run by a river protectors association, working through monitoring, advocacy AND THE IMPLEMENTATION OF TECHNICAL PROJECTS. THE TECHNICAL SIDE IS WHAT DISTINGUISHES IT FROM A CAMPAIGN. Its published public policy work sets out concrete methods — ENGINEERING SURVEYS to assess technologies for Iraqi agricultural land, ECONOMIC FEASIBILITY STUDIES, surveys of current irrigation practice, farmer training, and seeking partnerships with financiers to fund the alternative. This file has recorded across several countries that a worked alternative plan beats objection alone; this organisation builds them. IT ALSO NAMES THE DOMESTIC BODIES IT COORDINATES WITH, WHICH IS A MAP OF WHO ELSE MATTERS HERE: agricultural associations, the ENGINEERS SYNDICATE, and the WATER CONSUMERS ASSOCIATION. A syndicate of engineers and an association of water users are precisely the kinds of body that can carry technical objections and represent affected users, and this file has recorded professional chambers doing exactly that in Turkiye. IT ORGANISES PUBLIC ACTION AS WELL AS PAPERS — street events in Baghdad with artists to raise awareness of threats to the Tigris and Euphrates — and its leadership sits on the steering committee of a regional campaign to protect the water resources and heritage of the wider river basin, which is the route to allies in neighbouring countries facing the same dams from the other side of the border. THE LIMITS: it is an advocacy and technical organisation, not a law practice, and nothing found shows it litigating. Its central subject is water — rivers, marshes and dams — so a land dispute unconnected to water fits it poorly. For a community whose river, marsh or irrigation supply is threatened by a dam or diversion, it is the strongest domestic body recorded here.

trackers.name: Waterkeepers Iraq — a named river keeper in the north, working on dam prevention and removal
trackers.desc: ITS PROGRAMME INCLUDES THE PREVENTION AND REMOVAL OF DAMS THAT DAMAGE RIVERS AND THEIR COMMUNITIES, stated as an explicit area of work alongside water allocation, transboundary water issues, long-range planning and WATER-RELATED LEGISLATION. Very few bodies in this payload name dam prevention as a function; this one does. IT IS BASED IN THE NORTH, IN SULAIMANI, AND STAFFS A NAMED RIVER KEEPER FOR THE UPPER TIGRIS — a single person with responsibility for a defined stretch of river, which is a different and more reachable thing than a national organisation. That matters in a country where this file's other entries operate nationally or from the capital: if your water is in the Kurdistan region or the upper basin, there is a named post whose job is that water. IT MONITORS CONTAMINANTS THAT POLLUTE WATERWAYS and seeks solutions to protect water quality for both the natural environment and the communities depending on it — which is evidence work, and this file has recorded repeatedly that contamination measured and documented is what changes a case. ITS STATED PURPOSE INCLUDES SUPPORTING LOCAL COMMUNITIES IN THE SUSTAINABLE USE of rivers and streams, and its outreach is aimed at community, scientific and government audiences alike. KNOW ITS SCALE BEFORE YOU APPROACH: its own description says it currently has ONE WATERKEEPER ON STAFF, with jurisdiction intended to expand to further waterways and basins as the organisation develops. That is a small body with a wide mandate, so expect to bring your own capacity rather than to hand a problem over. THE OTHER LIMITS: water and rivers only; it is an advocacy and monitoring organisation rather than a legal one; and nothing found shows it litigating or representing anyone. Use it alongside the national river movement recorded above and, where a lender or foreign company is involved, the international accountability routes recorded for this country.

trackers.name: The farmers' cooperative federations — statutory bodies whose job includes defending farmers' rights
trackers.desc: THERE IS A STATUTORY FEDERATION WHOSE PUBLISHED FUNCTIONS INCLUDE DEFENDING FARMERS' RIGHTS, AND IT HAS LOCAL FEDERATIONS IN THE GOVERNORATES. The law establishes a general federation of agricultural cooperative societies representing the cooperative farming movement across all its branches, with among its listed responsibilities caring for farmers' interests and DEFENDING THEIR RIGHTS, and with local federations operating at province level. If your land is farmland or orchard, you are not starting from nothing: there is a body that already exists to speak for you, and it is organised where you live rather than only in the capital. ITS STANDING IS DEMONSTRATED, NOT ASSUMED. Its president was received by parliament's agriculture committee, together with water ministry officials, TO DISCUSS AN AMENDMENT TO THE LAW ON IMPLEMENTING IRRIGATION PROJECTS — the law that governs how land is taken for water schemes. A federation that is invited to help redraft the expropriation law is a federation whose letter carries weight. THE ARGUMENT ITS DELEGATES MADE IS THE ONE TO REUSE ANYWHERE SUBSTITUTE LAND IS OFFERED: they said that compensating a farmer with alternative land that is UNFIT FOR AGRICULTURE would make the statute A DISPLACEMENT LAW RATHER THAN A LAW GUARANTEEING THE FARMER'S RIGHTS. The test is not whether land was given but whether it can be farmed — demand a soil and water assessment of any replacement plot before accepting it. AND KNOW THAT COMPENSATION MONEY HAS BEEN APPROPRIATED: the committee recorded securing 1.3 TRILLION DINARS for farmer compensation within the internal loan law and including it in a budget year, while complaining that the finance ministry was delaying payment. Ask which allocation covers your case and whether it has been released — a delayed payment is a different fight from an unfunded one. ONE MEMBER OF THE COMMITTEE ARGUED FOR INVOLVING THE AGRICULTURE MINISTRY AND THE FARMERS' SOCIETIES ALONGSIDE THE WATER MINISTRY IN IMPLEMENTING PROJECTS, to stop powers overlapping. That is an opening to ask your local federation to be formally included in a scheme's implementation. THE LIMITS, AND THEY ARE SERIOUS. Farming societies and federations publicly complain of HAVING NO COMMUNICATION CHANNELS WITH GOVERNMENT and of demands going unanswered, so weight is not the same as access. The founding statute dates from an earlier political era and its language reflects that. AND NO WEBSITE FOR THE FEDERATION COULD BE FOUND — this entry points at the official parliamentary record of its appearance; reach it through the local federation in your governorate or through the agriculture directorate. THE THREAT IT NAMES IS THE ONE THIS MAP EXISTS FOR: orchards being bulldozed and converted into housing projects.

trackers.name: International Center for Community Land Trusts — how a community comes to own its land permanently
trackers.desc: A COMMUNITY LAND TRUST IS A NONPROFIT THAT HOLDS THE LAND PERMANENTLY WHILE THE PEOPLE ON IT OWN ONLY WHAT STANDS THERE. Its board is made up of resident members, wider community members and public representatives, so no single owner and no future council can sell the ground out from under it. Such trusts run RURAL AND URBAN AGRICULTURE PROJECTS AND CONSERVE LAND AND GREEN SPACES as well as housing. This file recorded that orchards in this country are being bulldozed and converted into housing projects; a trust is the vehicle built precisely to stop land passing from the people who use it to whoever can pay most for it. THIS CENTRE EXISTS TO HELP PEOPLE BUILD ONE. It was established to promote and support such trusts and similar strategies of community-led development on community-owned land IN COUNTRIES THROUGHOUT THE WORLD, and it provides TRAINING, REFERRAL AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE to organisers and practitioners, alongside case studies, directories and guides. START WITH WHAT IS FREE ON ITS OWN SITE: a start-up manual setting out the organisational and operational choices in founding a trust — including WHO SPONSORS IT, which is the first decision and the one that shapes everything after. It also runs a global summit of free online events over several weeks each year, bringing together practitioners, residents, organisers and researchers, and keeps the recordings; and it has published jointly with a national bar association on the part LAWYERS play in establishing trusts, which is the document to hand a lawyer who has never set one up. BEFORE ANY OF THAT, ESTABLISH TWO THINGS. Whether the land can lawfully be sold at all — this file has recorded a Basic Law in one country of this region forbidding the sale of state land outright, and a rule in another confining sale of valley farmland to a single public buyer. And whether you can form the nonprofit that would hold it: a trust needs a registered legal entity, which this file has identified as the commonest barrier between communities and land or money across the whole region. THE LIMITS: it is a support and knowledge organisation, not a funder — IT WILL NOT BUY YOUR LAND, and someone still has to pay for the ground. Its materials and case studies come overwhelmingly from North America and Europe, and no activity in this region was established; ask it directly what it can offer here, since referral is one of its stated services.

trackers.name: ELAW — scientific and legal backing for whichever lawyer takes a river or contamination case here
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY HAS BODIES THAT PRODUCE TECHNICAL WORK AND NO LAWYER TO USE IT. This file recorded a national river movement here that runs ENGINEERING SURVEYS AND ECONOMIC FEASIBILITY STUDIES and builds alternative irrigation proposals, and a northern waterkeeper that MONITORS CONTAMINANTS AND WORKS ON WATER LEGISLATION. Neither is a law practice, and no environmental legal route exists in this map for this country. This alliance is what fills that gap from the other side. IT IS A GLOBAL NETWORK OF ATTORNEYS AND SCIENTISTS SUPPLYING LEGAL, SCIENTIFIC, SECURITY AND ORGANISATIONAL EXPERTISE TO PUBLIC INTEREST LAWYERS — more than three hundred advocates in over eighty countries, handling upwards of four hundred requests a year. ITS SCIENCE TEAM DOES FOUR THINGS THAT MATTER PRECISELY HERE: it CRITIQUES ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT ASSESSMENTS, SUBMITS EXPERT TESTIMONY TO COURTS, builds systems to MONITOR ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS, and RECOMMENDS CLEANER ALTERNATIVES TO PROPOSED PROJECTS. A community facing a dam, a diversion or an oilfield discharge needs an independent critique of the assessment and an expert who will stand behind it; a movement that has already surveyed the ground needs someone to turn that into evidence a court accepts. AND IT DOES THE INTRODUCTION THAT NOBODY ELSE MAKES: it FACILITATES ENGAGEMENT BETWEEN LOCAL SCIENTISTS AND LOCAL LAWYERS. This file recorded that a university science faculty here holds unpublished internal reports and contradicted international figures in print, and separately that a farmers' federation argued the compensation law in parliament. THE SCIENTISTS, THE AFFECTED USERS AND THE ADVOCATES IN THIS COUNTRY ARE ALL RECORDED AND NONE OF THEM IS CONNECTED TO THE OTHERS. ITS LAW TEAM HELPS PARTNERS BRING ENFORCEMENT ACTIONS, critique draft legislation and REPLICATE MODEL LAWS FROM OTHER JURISDICTIONS — directly usable where a river body is already working on water legislation. It also works explicitly on DEFENDING DEFENDERS and the safety of advocates under attack. HOW TO USE IT: IT WORKS THROUGH PARTNERS — PUBLIC INTEREST LAWYERS IN THEIR OWN COUNTRIES — NOT DIRECTLY WITH COMMUNITIES. Find or instruct a local advocate first, then have them request support, which is provided at no cost to the partner. THE LIMITS: it will not represent you, fund litigation or campaign, and whether it has partners in this country was not established — ask before relying on it. It is also a DIFFERENT ORGANISATION from the similarly named environmental defender law centre recorded elsewhere in this file, which places pro bono lawyers rather than supplying expertise to lawyers who already have the case.

trackers.name: Grassroots Justice Network — find the legal empowerment people here, or train your own
trackers.desc: IT HAS A MEMBER DIRECTORY, AND THIS COUNTRY HAS NO LAWYER RECORDED ANYWHERE IN THIS MAP. The network gathers more than seventeen thousand six hundred members across a hundred and eighty-nine countries — community paralegals and the organisations that deploy them — and its directory can be reached by joining or as a guest by giving an email address. This file searched a whole legal sector in this country and could not name one reachable organisation; a directory of justice defenders is the shortest remaining route to whoever is actually working here. ITS LAND WORK IS DESCRIBED IN THE EXACT TERMS OF THIS MAP: increasing LAND TENURE SECURITY, gaining RECOGNITION FOR COMMUNITY LAND RIGHTS, and SIGNIFICANTLY REDUCING ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL HARM IN MINING, AGRICULTURAL OR DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS. BUT THE MODEL IS WORTH MORE HERE THAN THE DIRECTORY, BECAUSE IT IS WHAT A COMMUNITY CAN BUILD WHEN THERE ARE NO LAWYERS. COMMUNITY PARALEGALS are ordinary people trained in basic law AND in mediation, organising, education and advocacy — a frontline that can, in the network's own words, squeeze justice out of even broken systems. ITS STATED POSTURE IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE EXPERT SERVICE: rather than treating affected people as victims who need someone to solve the problem for them, paralegals BUILD POWER AMONG THE PEOPLE THEY WORK WITH. For a district where the technical bodies recorded elsewhere in this file hold surveys and contaminant data but nobody can take a case, training two or three local people in the relevant law is a more realistic step than waiting for a lawyer who does not exist. AND ONE PRACTICE IN THAT MODEL IS DIRECTLY COPYABLE WHATEVER ELSE YOU DO: PARALEGALS TRACK DATA ON THE PROCESS AND RESULT OF EVERY CASE. A single refused permit application is an anecdote; forty of them, recorded with dates, officials and outcomes, is evidence of a pattern — and this file has recorded across the region that patterns move institutions where individual complaints do not. THE CONVENOR ALSO RUNS A COMMUNITY LAND PROTECTION PROGRAMME supporting organisations to help rural communities PROTECT, DOCUMENT AND STEWARD their collectively managed lands, and maintains a library of practical resources and online spaces where members meet. THE LIMITS, PLAINLY: the convening organisation trains and deploys paralegals in six countries and NONE OF THEM IS IN THIS REGION — expect a network, a method and a library, not a team arriving. Reaching the directory means giving an email address to a foreign organisation, which is a decision to weigh in some places. And it is a network, not a law firm: it will not take your case.

trackers.name: Global Fund for Community Foundations — it pays to build the local fund, not just the project
trackers.desc: EVERY OTHER FUNDER IN THIS MAP PAYS FOR A PROJECT. THIS ONE PAYS TO BUILD THE BODY THAT WILL FUND YOUR PROJECTS AFTERWARDS. It gives small grants and technical support to community philanthropy organisations — community foundations, WOMEN'S FUNDS, ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS, grassroots grantmakers and national public foundations — to strengthen their GRANTMAKING SYSTEMS, GOVERNANCE AND MANAGEMENT STRUCTURES, FUND DEVELOPMENT AND SUSTAINABILITY and communications. AND ITS PRIORITY RULE POINTS STRAIGHT AT THIS COUNTRY: PRIORITY IS GIVEN TO THOSE COUNTRIES WHERE ACCESS TO OTHER FUNDING OPPORTUNITIES IS LIMITED. This file has recorded here a farmers' federation with parliamentary standing, river movements running their own engineering surveys, agricultural cooperatives, and a compensation scheme with committees — and no local fund of any kind. The pieces of a community foundation exist; what is missing is the vehicle. ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES ARE NAMED IN WHAT IT WILL SUPPORT: strengthening these bodies to respond to complex, sensitive or apparently intractable issues at community level, expressly including environmental issues, alongside social cohesion and community divisions, women's, youth and minority rights, and marginalised communities. In a country where this file recorded orchards being converted to housing and rivers dammed upstream, a local fund that can grant money to the affected village without waiting for a foreign call is a different kind of asset. ITS OWN RATIONALE IS THE BEST ARGUMENT FOR LOCAL MONEY THIS FILE HAS FOUND: community philanthropy BUILDS ON ASSETS THAT ALREADY EXIST WITHIN COMMUNITIES rather than depending only on what comes from outside — and when local resources are brought to the table, A FLATTER POWER DYNAMIC IS CREATED and traditional donor-beneficiary imbalances are challenged. That is the reason to raise money locally even when foreign money is available: it changes who decides. HOW TO APPROACH IT: it works through concept notes and publishes its eligibility guidelines; grants are small and normally run for an initial year with follow-on possible. CHECK THE PUBLISHED GUIDELINES FOR CURRENT AMOUNTS AND TERMS — the only sources stating a figure were aggregators this file does not use. THE LIMITS: applicants must be organisations that make grants or mobilise local resources, not a village committee with a single dispute; it does not fund land purchases, litigation or campaigns directly; and it works in developing and emerging economies, so eligibility depends on the country as well as the applicant.

trackers.name: High Commission for Human Rights — complaints kept confidential, and violations from before 2008 still count
trackers.desc: ITS FOUNDING LAW REQUIRES IT TO RECEIVE COMPLAINTS WHILE MAINTAINING COMPLETE CONFIDENTIALITY OF THE NAMES OF THOSE WHO SUBMIT THEM. Almost no other channel recorded anywhere in this map carries that protection in its constituting text. For a household in a district where the counterparty is a ministry, a governor or a state-linked company, confidentiality is the difference between complaining and not. AND THE SECOND CLAUSE MATTERS AS MUCH: ITS SCOPE COVERS VIOLATIONS THAT OCCURRED BEFORE THE LAW CAME INTO FORCE AS WELL AS AFTER IT. Land taken years ago, an orchard cleared before 2008, a displacement never compensated — none of that is automatically out of time here, which is unusual and worth testing. COMPLAINTS MAY COME FROM INDIVIDUALS, FROM GROUPS, AND FROM CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS. A village association, a farmers' body or a river movement can file on behalf of the people affected, which is the same feature that makes these institutions usable where households fear exposure. IT DOES MORE THAN RECEIVE: it CONDUCTS PRELIMINARY INVESTIGATIONS into violations on the basis of information, and VERIFIES THE ACCURACY of the complaints it receives. An institution that investigates is one that can be asked to go and look. IT IS REQUIRED TO OPEN OFFICES AND BRANCHES IN THE REGIONS AND IN THE GOVERNORATES, so this is not only a Baghdad body — ask where your governorate office is. AND IT REPORTS PUBLICLY: an ANNUAL REPORT TO PARLIAMENT giving a general assessment of the human rights situation, PUBLISHED IN THE VARIOUS MEDIA. A pattern of complaints from one district can surface in a document parliament receives, which is a route this file has recorded working elsewhere — forty recorded refusals are evidence where one is an anecdote. WHAT IT IS: an independent commission formed under a 2008 law, aiming to guarantee the protection of human rights and the rights and freedoms set out in the constitution, in law, and in the international treaties Iraq has ratified. THE LIMITS, PLAINLY. It investigates, verifies and reports; NO POWER TO BRING PROCEEDINGS IN COURT WAS FOUND, unlike the equivalent institution in another country recorded in this file. It is established by statute and funded accordingly, and its effectiveness is contested. It is not a substitute for a lawyer — and this country still has none recorded here. Use it for the confidential complaint, the investigation and the public record; use the farmers' federation, the legal empowerment network and the scientific support alliance recorded separately for the rest.

trackers.name: Save the Tigris — it got the Marshes onto the World Heritage list, and it researches the dams
trackers.desc: IT CAN POINT TO A RESULT, WHICH ALMOST NOTHING ELSE IN THIS MAP CAN. After several years of campaigning, THE IRAQI MARSHES WERE INSCRIBED ON THE UNESCO WORLD HERITAGE LIST IN 2016. The campaign began in March 2012 as a coalition of Mesopotamian and international activists formed to protect the Tigris from dams and other megaprojects, focused first on a large dam in a neighbouring country that would drown an ancient town, and on the marshes themselves. IT PRODUCES THE TECHNICAL ARGUMENTS A COMMUNITY COULD NEVER FUND. It conducts ITS OWN ORIGINAL RESEARCH on dams, pollution and water harvesting — including RESEARCH ON EVAPORATION IN DAM RESERVOIRS, which is the argument that a reservoir in this climate loses more water than it secures. It publishes project-specific DAM WATCH REPORTS, one in March 2025 investigating the risks posed by a named dam, and in May 2026 a report on the ECONOMIC LIFE OF THE INHABITANTS of the central and western Hammar marshes — on how recurring drought and declining water threaten traditional livelihoods, cultural heritage and the resilience of the marsh communities. THAT LAST KIND OF REPORT IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES MOST OFTEN LACK: evidence that a water change costs people their living, written down and published by someone other than themselves. AND IT SUPPLIES A LEGAL FRAME ANY COMMUNITY IN A SHARED-RIVER DISPUTE CAN BORROW. It argues that dams built without consultation and without assessment of their impacts breach the established international norms on the use of international watercourses — EQUITABLE AND REASONABLE UTILISATION, PARTICIPATION, AND THE OBLIGATION NOT TO CAUSE SIGNIFICANT HARM to those who depend on the water. Three named principles are a stronger objection than an appeal about damage. ITS COALITION CONTAINS A LEGAL ROUTE: alongside ecology movements and heritage initiatives in a neighbouring country, its international partners include AN ENVIRONMENTAL DEFENDERS LAW CENTRE and European organisations specialising in rivers and dams. It also convenes a Mesopotamian water forum and facilitates cross-border information sharing, which matters where the decision harming your district is taken in another country. KNOW TWO THINGS BEFORE YOU APPROACH IT. It now operates as a FOUNDATION BASED IN EUROPE rather than as an Iraqi organisation, though it grew from and works with Iraqi groups — including the river association recorded separately in this file, whose director served as its coordinator in this country. And in July 2025 IT WAS EXPELLED FROM A UNESCO WORLD HERITAGE COMMITTEE SESSION, which tells you both how far its reach extends and what it meets there. THE LIMITS: it is research and advocacy, not legal representation, and its scale is the basin rather than the single village — bring it a problem that connects to the river system, and take a purely local dispute to the bodies recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Lifeline — emergency money for legal representation when your organisation is prosecuted
trackers.desc: THE QUALIFYING TEST NAMES THE THING THAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS TO COMMUNITY GROUPS. An emergency is assessed on need, urgency, and whether the organisation faces significant security risks, loss of property or equipment, injury or imprisonment of staff, AND OR PROSECUTION OR OTHER LEGAL PROCEEDINGS. A lawsuit brought against a river association, a farmers' body or a village committee because of what it said or documented is itself a qualifying emergency — and this file has recorded that pattern across five countries. WHAT THE EMERGENCY GRANT PAYS FOR IS LISTED PLAINLY: security, medical expenses, LEGAL REPRESENTATION, PRISON VISITS, TRIAL MONITORING, temporary relocation, equipment replacement and other urgently needed expenses. This payload holds more than eighty funding entries and almost none of them will pay a lawyer or send someone to sit in a courtroom. THIS ONE WILL. TWO FURTHER WINDOWS ARE WORTH KNOWING. ADVOCACY GRANTS are highly flexible and can fund STRATEGIC LITIGATION, policy and legal advocacy, coalition building, awareness campaigns and security and protection training. RESILIENCY GRANTS pay for PREVENTION — including MAPPING AND COORDINATING CIVIL SOCIETY ACCESS TO PRO BONO SERVICES, joint protection strategies, contingency plans, organisational risk assessments and legal technical assistance. That second one is the round of funding to seek BEFORE anything happens: building the list of lawyers who will act, while nobody is yet in trouble. IT IS A CONSORTIUM OF SEVEN INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATIONS LED BY A FREEDOM ORGANISATION, WITH EMERGENCY REQUESTS HANDLED THROUGH IT AND THROUGH A DEFENDERS' ORGANISATION; a third consortium member also receives requests and forwards them. It is supported by around twenty government and foundation donors. THE LIMITS, AND THE FIRST ONE MATTERS MOST HERE. IT FUNDS CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS — human rights groups, journalist associations, student groups, unions and similar — SO AN UNREGISTERED VILLAGE COMMITTEE MAY NOT QUALIFY AS AN APPLICANT. This file established that lacking a registered entity is the commonest barrier in this region; here it bites again, and the answer is to apply through an existing organisation that supports you. IT ALSO DOES NOT FUND CORE COSTS, PROGRAMMES, LONG-TERM SUPPORT OR FINANCIAL HARDSHIP — only the emergency — and it is funded by donor governments, so association with it is a political fact in some places.

trackers.name: OECD Watch — complain about a foreign company in the country where it is headquartered
trackers.desc: THE RULE THAT MAKES THIS USABLE HERE: A COMPLAINT CAN BE FILED AGAINST A MULTINATIONAL HEADQUARTERED IN A COUNTRY THAT FOLLOWS THE OECD GUIDELINES, EVEN WHERE THE HARM HAPPENS IN A COUNTRY THAT DOES NOT. Those governments must each maintain a non-judicial complaints office, and that office is obliged to handle complaints about the conduct of companies based there. A community facing a foreign oil, engineering or construction company therefore has a forum outside this country, reached without a lawyer and usually without cost. THIS NETWORK EXISTS TO HELP CIVIL SOCIETY USE IT, AND WHAT IT SUPPLIES IS PRACTICAL: guidance broken into SEVEN STAGES of the process, A MODEL COMPLAINT LETTER written for these offices, and a COMPLAINTS DATABASE you can filter by issue, sector and region to read what happened in cases like yours before you write a word. They invite contact for advice on drafting and strategy. THEIR GUIDANCE ON EVIDENCE IS THE MOST TRANSFERABLE PART: collect WITNESS STATEMENTS, COMPANY POLICIES, SCIENTIFIC TESTS and published articles or reports showing the harm and its connection to the company — and collect information about the company itself, INCLUDING WHERE IT IS HEADQUARTERED, because that determines which office hears you. This file records for this country a farmers' federation, a river campaign that produces its own dam research, and a legal empowerment network; all of them generate exactly the material this process runs on. CHECK THE OFFICE BEFORE YOU FILE. The network evaluates these offices against THIRTY-EIGHT PERFORMANCE INDICATORS, and one official report found that THIRTY-ONE PER CENT OF THEM HAD NOT RECEIVED A SINGLE CASE IN OVER FIVE YEARS. Some are serious; some are dormant. Read the evaluation of the specific office before investing months. AND WEIGH THE CONFIDENTIALITY TRADE-OFF IN ADVANCE: confidentiality can protect complainants and encourage dialogue, but it MAY RESTRICT YOUR ABILITY TO SPEAK PUBLICLY about the case. Campaigning is permitted so long as confidential documents and mediation details are not disclosed — check that office's transparency rules before filing rather than after. THE LIMITS, IN THEIR OWN WORDS: THE STANDARDS ARE VOLUNTARY, THE OFFICES CANNOT REQUIRE A COMPANY TO TAKE PART OR TO REMEDY ANYTHING, and complaints SOMETIMES THOUGH NOT OFTEN result in remedy — more often they raise awareness and shift future conduct. Their own advice is that complaints succeed when embedded in a wider strategy with media, allies and investors, which is how this should be used: as one instrument among several, not as the remedy.

trackers.name: Bar register — verify the lawyer, check which courts they may enter, and know the fee floor
trackers.desc: THE BAR'S OFFICIAL SITE CARRIES A REGISTER OF LAWYERS, SO ADMISSION CAN BE VERIFIED BEFORE A CASE AND A FEE ARE HANDED OVER. Everything else this map records for this country — a foreign environmental law alliance, a legal empowerment network, a national complaints commission, an international complaints route — tells a reader where to seek help. NONE OF THEM LETS YOU CHECK THE PERSON IN FRONT OF YOU. BUT THE MORE USEFUL THING ON THIS SITE IS THE QUESTION IT TEACHES YOU TO ASK. LAWYERS HERE HOLD GRADES OF AUTHORITY THAT GOVERN WHICH COURTS THEY MAY APPEAR BEFORE, and the bar council has recently CHANGED THE MECHANISMS FOR GRANTING THAT AUTHORITY AND ADDED TWO DISTINCT AUTHORITIES under the law. ASK WHICH AUTHORITY YOUR LAWYER HOLDS BEFORE INSTRUCTING THEM. A land or administrative case may end up before a court their grade does not admit them to, and discovering that late means starting again with someone else, after limitation periods have run. This file has recorded the same structure in another country's profession law, where a claim above a stated value could not be brought except through a lawyer; here the constraint is not the claim's value but THE LAWYER'S RANK. AND THE BAR PUBLISHES A FEE FLOOR, WHICH ALMOST NO PROFESSIONAL BODY IN THIS REGION DOES: MINIMUM MONTHLY RETAINERS OF THREE HUNDRED THOUSAND DINARS FOR IRAQI COMPANIES AND SIX HUNDRED THOUSAND FOR FOREIGN COMPANIES. Two things follow. You can tell whether a quoted fee is inside professional norms rather than guessing. And you can estimate what the company on the other side is paying its own counsel each month — which is a useful figure when deciding whether to fight, to seek the free routes recorded separately here, or to apply to the litigation-expenses funders this file records for other countries. THE BAR IS REACHABLE: its official public page carries a following of more than three hundred thousand, and it publishes its rules of admission and practice alongside the register. THE LIMITS. A REGISTER CONFIRMS ADMISSION, NOT COMPETENCE, INDEPENDENCE OR WILLINGNESS — it will not tell you who has run an environmental or land case, and no specialism field was found. The published fees are minimums for company retainers, not a guide to what an individual should pay. And the bar is a professional body that regulates lawyers rather than an advocate for anyone. Use it to check the person, ask about their authority, and sense-check the money — and use the legal empowerment network and the complaints commission recorded separately for the case itself.

trackers.name: Engineers Union — licensed testing offices, engineer ranks, and a disciplinary route that ends in court
trackers.desc: THE MOST USEFUL THING HERE IS A LICENSED CATEGORY MOST PEOPLE DO NOT KNOW EXISTS: OFFICES FOR TESTING AND INSPECTION ARE A RECOGNISED ENGINEERING SPECIALISM, licensed and classified by the union. A community that needs a structure examined, a material tested or works inspected does not need a favour from a university — IT NEEDS A LICENSED TESTING AND INSPECTION OFFICE, and the union is where the licensed ones are listed. PETROLEUM ENGINEERING IS ANOTHER LICENSED SPECIALISM, covering the identification, evaluation, development and drilling of oil and gas fields, which matters where the project in dispute is a field or a pipeline. SECOND, AND THIS IS A REAL REMEDY: A DISCIPLINARY COMMITTEE INSIDE THE UNION DECIDES COMPLAINTS AGAINST ENGINEERING OFFICES — brought by the union's own offices committee OR BY THOSE CONTRACTING WITH THE OFFICE — where the office has breached the law, the instructions, or THE RULES OF PROFESSIONAL CONDUCT, or has departed from its stated objectives. THE COMMITTEE IMPOSES PENALTIES, AND ITS DECISION IS APPEALABLE TO THE COURT OF CASSATION WITHIN THIRTY DAYS OF NOTIFICATION. A professional complaint with a defined forum, defined grounds and an appeal to the highest court is a stronger instrument than most of the complaint channels recorded anywhere in this file. AND THE UNION CAN STRIKE AN OFFICE OFF THE REGISTER ALTOGETHER if it does work conflicting with the union's law, regulations or instructions. THIRD, ASK THE RANK BEFORE YOU ENGAGE ANYONE. A LICENSED-RANK ENGINEER MAY DO ANY WORK WITHIN HIS SPECIALISM WITHOUT LIMIT, INCLUDING CHAIRING ARBITRATION AND PLANNING COMMITTEES; ONLY A CONSULTANT-RANK OFFICE MAY REGISTER IN MORE THAN ONE SPECIALISM, and must employ engineers in each. This file recorded that advocates in this country hold GRADES OF AUTHORITY deciding which courts they may enter; THE SAME STRUCTURE RUNS THROUGH ENGINEERING, so in this country rank is the first question for both professions.
