Promotion to consultant requires five years plus a higher degree, or three specialism courses, OR DOCUMENTED SUPERVISION OF NAMED PROJECTS — so a senior engineer's record of supervised projects is itself checkable. THE OFFICES COMMITTEE THAT LICENSES ALL THIS IS REQUIRED TO INCLUDE PRIVATE SECTOR REPRESENTATION, with members of consultant rank drawn from different specialisms. THE LIMITS, AND THE FIRST ONE DECIDES WHO CAN USE THE COMPLAINT. THE DISCIPLINARY ROUTE IS DESCRIBED FOR THE OFFICES COMMITTEE AND FOR THOSE CONTRACTING WITH THE OFFICE — A NEIGHBOUR WHO HAS NO CONTRACT MAY NOT HAVE STANDING, and would need to bring the matter to the offices committee to refer. The union regulates engineers and will not oppose a project; engaging an office costs money; and this is a professional route to evidence and accountability, not to stopping a scheme.

trackers.name: The waqf diwans — an endowment that can buy land, and the trap of which diwan you fall under
trackers.desc: THIS FILE HAS RECORDED ENDOWMENTS IN SIX COUNTRIES AS A WAY TO HOLD LAND. HERE, FOR THE FIRST TIME, AN ENDOWMENT CAN ALSO BUY IT: the diwan's board decides on REQUESTS BY TRUSTEES TO PURCHASE PROPERTY FOR THE WAQF, TO REPAIR IT, OR TO CONSTRUCT NEW BUILDINGS FOR IT. An existing endowment with income can therefore acquire ground, on its trustee's application — which turns endowment from a way of freezing what you already own into a way of getting more. THE MONEY IS GUARDED IN A WAY WORTH KNOWING: endowed funds may be put into investment projects ONLY AFTER ECONOMIC FEASIBILITY IS ESTABLISHED AND WITH REGARD TO THE CONDITION OF THE ENDOWER. The endower's condition binds the investment decision, so a condition written into the endowment deed is not decoration. THE BOARD ALSO DECIDES ON RECEIVING AND ADMINISTERING CHARITABLE INSTITUTIONS ESTABLISHED BY BENEFACTORS, and on approving the establishment of such institutions — so a benefactor who builds something can have it taken into the endowment system rather than left to heirs. The parallel diwan operates a directorate whose stated task is DEVELOPING AND INVESTING WAQF FUNDS AND PROPERTIES AND FOLLOWING UP THE AFFAIRS OF TRUSTEES AND ENDOWERS — a department that exists to deal with endowers. NOW THE STRUCTURAL FACT THAT DECIDES EVERYTHING ELSE, AND NOBODY SHOULD ENDOW ANYTHING HERE WITHOUT UNDERSTANDING IT. AFTER 2003 THE MINISTRY OF ENDOWMENTS WAS DISSOLVED AND ITS FUNCTIONS SPLIT AMONG SEPARATE DIWANS BY CONFESSION, each with its own founding law. WHICH DIWAN YOUR ENDOWMENT FALLS UNDER CHANGES WHAT YOU MAY CREATE. AND THE DIFFERENCE IS NOT SMALL. LEGISLATION PERMITTED THE LIQUIDATION OF FAMILY AND MIXED ENDOWMENTS UNDER ONE DIWAN AND BARRED APPROVING NEW ONES THERE. UNDER THE OTHER, A FAMILY ENDOWMENT CONVERTS INTO A CHARITABLE ONE — ACCORDING TO ANALYSIS IN THE COUNTRY, EVEN WITHOUT THE ENDOWER'S KNOWLEDGE. A family that endows land expecting to keep control of its use may find the endowment has become charitable and passed into the diwan's administration. ASK, BEFORE SIGNING, WHICH DIWAN APPLIES, WHETHER THE FORM YOU WANT MAY LAWFULLY BE CREATED THERE, AND WHAT HAPPENS TO IT IF THE LAW CHANGES AGAIN. THE OTHER LIMITS ARE SERIOUS TOO: the same analysis describes a substantial political contest over endowment revenues since 2003, with the institutions politicised. These are state diwans, not community bodies. AND THE PROTECTION THIS FILE VALUES IN ENDOWMENT — THAT LAND CANNOT BE TAKEN BY LONG OCCUPATION OR SOLD ON — SHOULD BE VERIFIED HERE SPECIFICALLY rather than assumed from the neighbouring country where this file recorded it.

trackers.name: Tree-planting foundations and the nurseries that supply them — restoration a community can actually start
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING HELD SEVENTEEN ENTRIES AND NOTHING ABOUT PUTTING LAND BACK. THE MOST USEFUL FACT HERE IS THE SMALLEST ONE: AGRICULTURAL NURSERIES SUPPLY SEEDLINGS AT REDUCED PRICES, and they are the reason ordinary planting campaigns here are affordable at all. FIND YOUR NEAREST NURSERY AND ASK ITS PRICE FOR QUANTITY BEFORE YOU ASK ANYONE FOR MONEY — a costed planting proposal built on real nursery prices is a fundable document; an aspiration is not. AND THERE IS A CIVIL FOUNDATION SHOWING WHAT THAT BUILDS TO. It began a planting campaign in a war-damaged northern city in 2017 and has since put in MORE THAN FIFTY THOUSAND TREES across that province, under named campaigns for a green city and a green road. That is not a state programme — it is an organisation that started in a ruined place with nothing and now plants at scale, which is the most transferable example in this entry. THE STATE SIDE IS WORTH KNOWING BECAUSE IT IS WHERE THE MONEY AND SEEDLINGS SIT: a national initiative launched in 2023 to plant five million trees had reached three million by that summer according to the agriculture minister, following an earlier initiative for a million fruit trees. CIVIL AND ENVIRONMENTAL ORGANISATIONS RUN THE PUBLIC EDUCATION AROUND THESE CAMPAIGNS, so a local group asking to join an existing national initiative is asking for something already funded and already counted. THE SCALE OF WHAT IS BEING FOUGHT: 6,694,641 HECTARES ARE CLASSIFIED AS DESERTIFIED — FIFTEEN PER CENT OF THE COUNTRY — and official estimates put the first phase of restoration at AT LEAST THREE HUNDRED MILLION TREES, with WATER AVAILABILITY THE MAIN OBSTACLE. That last point is the one to design around: planting without a secured water source fails, and a proposal that answers the water question before the tree question is the one that survives. THE TECHNIQUE WORTH COPYING COMES FROM THE SOUTHERN MARSHES, WHERE A PILOT CONSTRUCTED WETLAND USES REEDS TO TREAT SEWAGE, restoring ecosystems while solving a sanitation problem. THIS FILE RECORDED AT R350 THAT REMOVING THE PRETEXT IS STRONGER THAN OPPOSING THE ACT — a reed bed that treats a village's wastewater removes the argument that a wetland is a health hazard to be filled, and creates habitat while doing it. AND THE PRECEDENT BEHIND ALL OF IT: the southern marshes covered around twenty thousand square kilometres until the 1970s and were then almost entirely drained — AND CAME BACK IN PART BECAUSE OF INITIATIVES LAUNCHED BY RESIDENTS THEMSELVES TO REOPEN THE WATERWAYS. By May 2026 rising water had brought herders and fishers back to areas they had abandoned. WHAT COMMUNITIES DID THERE IS THE ANSWER TO ANYONE WHO SAYS A PLACE IS TOO FAR GONE. THE LIMITS: this entry rests on national press reporting rather than the foundation's own account, so CONFIRM THE ORGANISATION IS STILL ACTIVE AND WHERE IT WORKS before approaching it. Planting is not protection — trees can be cleared unless the ground has status, so pair this with the endowment route and the biodiversity mapping recorded separately for this country. And nothing here addresses who owns the land you plant on.

trackers.name: NGO directorate — where organisations are registered, and where grant calls are published
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING HELD RIVER MOVEMENTS, BIODIVERSITY MAPPING, COOPERATIVE FEDERATIONS, ENDOWMENT DIWANS AND A BAR REGISTER — AND NO ANSWER TO THE FIRST QUESTION A NEW GROUP ASKS: HOW DO WE BECOME AN ORGANISATION? THIS IS THE GOVERNMENT DEPARTMENT THAT REGISTERS NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS, and registration is the precondition for almost everything else this file records for this country. BUT THE REASON TO WATCH IT IS THE SECOND FUNCTION: IT PUBLISHES GRANT OPPORTUNITIES. One notice invited non-governmental organisations, civil society organisations, LAW FACULTIES AND BAR ASSOCIATIONS — already registered with the government — to apply to a SMALL GRANTS PROGRAMME AIMED AT CAPACITY BUILDING, funded by an international development agency under an access-to-justice programme. READ WHO WAS ELIGIBLE THERE: LAW FACULTIES AND BAR ASSOCIATIONS. This file has recorded a bar register and university legal clinics for this country as places to find a lawyer; THAT NOTICE SHOWS THEY ARE ALSO FUNDABLE APPLICANTS. A community that wants legal capacity in its province can propose a project TO a law faculty or a bar association rather than only asking one for help — the money exists to build exactly that capacity, and the institution applies for it. THE REGISTRAR ALSO ANNOUNCES COOPERATION WITH FOREIGN ORGANISATIONS OPERATING IN THE COUNTRY, framed around building civil society capacity and delivering services to citizens — so its announcements are the public record of which international bodies are working here and under what arrangements. FOR ANYONE TRYING TO FIND A PARTNER WITH MONEY, THAT LIST IS THE STARTING POINT. WHAT TO DO: CHECK THE REGISTRATION REQUIREMENTS BEFORE PLANNING ANYTHING THAT NEEDS A LEGAL PERSON, and then watch the announcements page as a funding source rather than a bureaucratic one. Where a call names your kind of body — an association, a faculty, a union — that is an invitation, and this file has found repeatedly that communities never see these notices because they look for grants on funders' sites rather than on their own government's registrar. THE LIMITS: it is a state registration authority, so it approves, monitors and can refuse; registration brings supervision as well as standing. Its grant notices are third-party programmes with their own deadlines and eligibility, and calls close. AND REGISTRATION REQUIREMENTS AND PROCESSING TIMES WERE NOT VERIFIED IN THIS ROUND — confirm them directly. Use it with the bar register, the engineers union and the cooperative federations recorded separately here.

trackers.name: Proving who owns a parcel — the route for unregistered land and for registers that burned
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING HELD ENDOWMENT DIWANS, COOPERATIVE FEDERATIONS, RIVER MOVEMENTS AND A REGISTRAR OF ORGANISATIONS — AND NO WAY TO ANSWER THE FIRST QUESTION IN ANY LAND DISPUTE: WHO OWNS THIS GROUND, AND HOW DO I PROVE IT IS MINE. THERE IS A NAMED GOVERNMENT SERVICE FOR EXACTLY THAT, AND IT IS BUILT FOR THE HARDEST CASES — PROPERTIES NEVER ENTERED IN THE REGISTERS, AND PROPERTIES WHOSE REGISTERS AND FILES WERE BURNED IN THE EVENTS OF 2003 AND 2001. THE PROCEDURE IS THREE STEPS AND WORTH KNOWING EXACTLY. FIRST, GO TO THE REGISTRATION DIRECTORATE COVERING YOUR AREA WITH THE TITLE DEED IF YOU HAVE ONE — OR, IF YOU DO NOT, WITH ANY PRELIMINARY EVIDENCE FOR THE PROPERTY SUCH AS A BUILDING PERMIT OR ELECTRICITY RECEIPTS. SECOND, THE DIRECTORATE WRITES TO THE COMPETENT COURT OF FIRST INSTANCE FOR A JUDICIAL DECISION. THIRD, ONCE THAT DECISION IS FINAL, YOU RETURN TO THE DIRECTORATE AND THE PROPERTY IS REGISTERED. READ WHAT COUNTS AS EVIDENCE THERE, BECAUSE IT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE: ELECTRICITY RECEIPTS. A HOUSEHOLD THAT HAS PAID ITS POWER BILL FOR TWENTY YEARS HOLDS PROOF OF OCCUPATION IT PROBABLY THINKS IS WORTHLESS. This payload has now found utility or tax records named as ownership evidence in three separate countries — KEEP THE BILLS, AND GET COPIES FROM THE UTILITY IF YOURS ARE GONE, because the supplier holds the other half of the record. THE LAW ADDS SOMETHING A CLAIMANT SHOULD PREPARE FOR: AN OWNERSHIP-CONFIRMATION COMMITTEE INSPECTS THE PROPERTY ON SITE, applies the descriptions in the deed or register copy TO THE ACTUAL GROUND, AND VERIFIES WHO IS IN POSSESSION where that is needed, recording rights for and against the property in a report. THE DECISION IS MADE ON THAT REPORT — SO THE SITE VISIT IS THE MOMENT THE CASE IS DECIDED, and, as this file found in two other countries, BEING PRESENT WHEN THE COMMITTEE COMES IS NOT OPTIONAL. AND IF THE DECISION GOES AGAINST YOU, OBJECTION IS BY FILING A CASE IN THE COMPETENT COURT — not by appealing inside the department, which matters for timing and for what kind of help you need. The bar register and the free legal routes recorded separately here are the ones to use at that point. THE SYSTEM IS ALSO MOVING ONLINE: AN ELECTRONIC DEED, A PROPERTY MAP, AND SERVICES FOR OPENING A PROPERTY STATEMENT, ORGANISING TRANSACTIONS AND MAKING OWNER REQUESTS have been launched, starting in six named registration directorates. A PROPERTY MAP AND A PROPERTY STATEMENT ARE EXACTLY WHAT A COMMUNITY NEEDS WHEN A DEVELOPER CLAIMS GROUND — ask whether your directorate is among those already live. THE LIMITS: this route ends in a court decision, so it takes time and costs money, and it establishes title rather than stopping a project. Coverage of the electronic services is partial and expanding. And in areas where registers were destroyed, competing claims over the same parcel are common — gather your evidence before anyone else does, because the committee decides on what it is shown.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Kazakhstan
trackers.desc: Official judicial portal of Kazakhstan with case search and court information. · Find here: the portal of Kazakhstan's Supreme Court, including its bank of judicial acts.

trackers.name: Ecological Society 'Green Salvation' (Экологическое общество «Зеленое спасение»)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Kazakhstan's veteran environmental-rights organisation, which litigates and publishes an annual review of its own court practice so you can see exactly what it runs and how it fares. It files in the Specialised Inter-district Administrative Court in Almaty both for itself and — the lever worth knowing — in defence of an indeterminate circle of persons, which is how an association carries a claim for a community that could not bring one alone. Its grounds are usually article 4 of the Aarhus Convention on access to timely, complete and reliable environmental information, read with articles 13 and 17 of the Environmental Code and the access-to-information law; it also ran the long campaign over Kok-Zhailau and the national park. WHO IT SUITS: anyone refused environmental information or facing a project pushed through without disclosure. It is Almaty-based and small, so expect reach to be strongest there.

trackers.name: State Revenue Committee – Legal Entity Search
trackers.desc: National — official legal-entity / company search, Kazakhstan. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: EITI Kazakhstan
trackers.desc: National Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative body — discloses oil, gas and mining revenues, contracts and licences in Kazakhstan.

trackers.name: Goszakup
trackers.desc: Kazakhstan's public-procurement web portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Kazakhstan, and for how much.

trackers.name: Bureau of National Statistics
trackers.desc: Kazakhstan's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Kazakhstan.

trackers.name: Supreme Audit Chamber
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Kazakhstan, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Constitutional Court of the Republic of Kazakhstan
trackers.desc: Constitutional Court of the Republic of Kazakhstan — supreme court (Kazakhstan).

trackers.name: ООПТ местного значения — aim at the oblast akimat, not the ministry
trackers.desc: THERE ARE TWO TIERS AND THE NEARER ONE IS LOCAL. Alongside the republican list of ООПТ approved by government decree, the law provides for protected areas of local significance, with местные исполнительные органы of oblasts, cities of republican significance and the capital acting within their competence. For a site of regional rather than national importance, the oblast akimat is the route — as in Albania, Montenegro and Luxembourg, and unlike Tunisia where the municipal route is closed. THE DEFINITION THAT ANSWERS ‘PROTECTION WILL END OUR FARMING’: the law defines традиционное землепользование as historically established types of agricultural activity in the region which do not have a harmful effect on natural complexes and the state nature reserve fund, are adapted to the given ecological system, and are carried out by owners of land plots or land users. Frame your existing use in exactly those four terms — historically established, non-harmful, adapted, and by an owner or land user — because they are the statute's own words. CATEGORIES WORTH KNOWING: государственный памятник природы covers individual unique, irreplaceable objects, the category for a single feature rather than a landscape; and биосферный резерват expressly includes охранные зоны, buffer zones.

trackers.name: Reserved zones, and the mining article to ask about
trackers.desc: TWO PROVISIONS THAT DECIDE HOW YOU ARGUE. 1. LAND CAN BE HELD BEFORE DESIGNATION: a государственная заповедная зона is a protected area with differentiated protection regimes, established to conserve and restore the nature reserve fund and biodiversity on land and waters reserved for future zapovedniks, national parks and reserves — a mechanism in place since 1976. So reservation can protect a site while full designation is still incomplete. 2. DO NOT ASSERT A BAN THE CODE DOES NOT CONTAIN: the Экологический кодекс sets ecological requirements for siting within ООПТ of settlements, industrial, agricultural, energy, transport and defence objects not connected with the purposes and functioning of the ООПТ, and article 255 sets special ecological requirements for subsoil use operations on the territory of state reserved zones. Mining inside a заповедная зона is therefore subject to special requirements rather than simply prohibited — so ask which requirements were applied and how compliance was assessed, which is a question with a documentary answer, instead of claiming a blanket prohibition that can be rebutted in one line.

trackers.name: CAREC — two organisations share the name, neither is a grant fund
trackers.desc: ‘CAREC’ IS TWO DIFFERENT ORGANISATIONS AND YOU WILL PROBABLY APPROACH THE WRONG ONE. The Regional Environmental Centre for Central Asia (carecnet.org / carececo.org) was established following the 4th Pan-European Conference in Aarhus, 1998, operating since 2001 as an independent, non-commercial and non-partisan organisation of international character. Its founders are Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan plus UNDP and the European Commission; headquarters in Almaty, with country offices in all five member states (the Kyrgyz office is at 142 Gorky str., office 410, Bishkek 720005). The unrelated Central Asia Regional Economic Cooperation (CAREC) Program is an Asian Development Bank programme founded 1997, based in Manila, with 11 members including Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, China and Pakistan. NEITHER IS A COMMUNITY GRANT FUND. The Environmental Centre offers a dialogue platform for environmental NGOs and representation at international forums and thematic networks, and collaborates with NGOs, government and business — a route to partnership, visibility and project consortia, not an application window. The ADB programme's Climate and Sustainability Project Preparatory Fund (US$3m from Korea, US$2m from China) supports preparation of bankable regional projects and its eligible recipients are developing member countries — states, not community groups. Approach the Environmental Centre's country office for partnership; do not send it a grant application expecting an award.

trackers.name: GEF Small Grants Programme — up to US$50,000 direct to communities
trackers.desc: WHERE THE COMMUNITY MONEY ACTUALLY IS. The GEF Small Grants Programme, running since 1992 and implemented by UNDP, reached 135 countries of 144 eligible in GEF-8, which secured US$135 million for the core programme with nearly US$1 million allocated to each participating country — a per-country floor, so the money is not competed for across borders. Grants of up to US$50,000 go directly to local communities, community-based organisations and other non-governmental groups. Focal areas: biodiversity, climate change, land degradation and sustainable forest management, international waters and chemicals. KAZAKHSTAN HAS ONE OF THE MOST MATURE SGP PROGRAMMES — recorded among those upgraded to full-sized projects and managed by UNDP's Communities, Livelihoods and Markets cluster, alongside Brazil, India, Mexico and Pakistan. An upgraded programme is larger and better established, but also more formal — expect fuller documentation than a standard country programme.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: ACBK — leases land out of hunting use, and writes the expert review of a developer's OVOS
trackers.desc: TWO THINGS IT DOES THAT NO COMMUNITY CAN DO FOR ITSELF. First, it takes ground off the market by holding the lease: ACBK has leased two hunting areas totalling some 340,000 hectares that mattered for saiga calving and migration, which is the same tactic as buying land — acquire the use-right so nobody else can exercise it. Second, and more immediately useful to a campaign, it produces the written expert critique of the developer's own impact assessment. ACBK publishes formal correspondence and specialist reviews on its own site under a Problems and Solutions section, including its objection concerning the Kokzhailau mountain resort planned on former and current lands of the Ile-Alatau State National Nature Park, and a named specialist's review of that project's preliminary OVOS on biodiversity components. That written assessment by a named scientist, addressed to the body deciding, is the thing communities most often cannot produce and most often lose without. WHO TO CONTACT: office 406, Beybitshilik 18, Astana 010000; acbk@acbk.kz; telephone and fax (7172) 91 00 44. Executive Director Vera Voronova. WHAT IT IS NOT: a litigator. ACBK is a research and conservation association, so pair it with counsel rather than expecting it to run your case — this file already carries Ecological Society Green Salvation for Kazakhstan, and the sensible division is that one supplies the evidence and the other files. SOURCING CAVEAT: the 340,000-hectare lease figure comes from Frankfurt Zoological Society, ACBK's partner in the Altyn Dala Conservation Initiative, not from ACBK's own domain, and a widely repeated claim that the 127 Important Bird Areas ACBK inventoried with RSPB all now hold national legal protection could not be confirmed on acbk.kz either — treat both as questions to put to the Astana office rather than facts to quote.

trackers.name: State-guaranteed legal aid — the list of participating advocates is published every 25 December, so get it before you need it
trackers.desc: THE ONE DATE TO DIARISE: BY 25 DECEMBER EACH YEAR THE TERRITORIAL JUSTICE BODY PUBLISHES ON ITS WEBSITE THE LIST OF ADVOCATES PARTICIPATING IN THE STATE-GUARANTEED LEGAL AID SYSTEM, AND THE REPUBLICAN BAR ASSOCIATION PUBLISHES THE SAME LIST IN THE UNIFIED LEGAL AID INFORMATION SYSTEM. That means you can find out in advance exactly which advocates in your oblast take state-funded work, rather than ringing round after a project is announced. Get the list while nothing is happening. THE TIER MOST PEOPLE MISS: free legal INFORMATION is available to all natural AND legal persons, with no means test at all — so a registered community association qualifies in its own right, not merely its individual members. Consultation goes further and is delivered in the advocate's own office at the moment the applicant turns up, rather than through an appointment queue. WHO ASSIGNS THE LAWYER: under the Law on Advocacy and Legal Assistance the participation of advocates in state-guaranteed aid is arranged by the bar association of your oblast or city of republican significance or the capital, and for rural settlements by the oblast bar association, with the selection criteria for participating advocates approved by the Republican Bar Association. ADMINISTRATIVE MATTERS ARE INSIDE THE SYSTEM: representation is available to a person brought to administrative responsibility, as well as to a claimant or respondent in proceedings. THE EXCLUSION THAT WILL CATCH LAND CASES: the low-income route — for people or families with per-capita monthly income below the poverty line set for their oblast or city — applies only to matters NOT connected with entrepreneurial activity. If the threatened land is a farm, a cooperative holding or anything with a commercial character, expect that argument from the other side and settle the classification early. CAPACITY, IN THE BAR'S OWN WORDS: the Republican Bar Association publishes its own account of the problems in the system, describing travel to institutions located far from any public transport, waiting for a room to become free, a single police officer expected to escort detainees and obtain permissions from other buildings at the same time, and visit certificates handed over at best the following day. Expect an appointed advocate who is stretched. Pair this with Ecological Society Green Salvation and ACBK, both already in this file, for litigation experience and expert evidence respectively.

trackers.name: Committee of Forestry and Wildlife — the 2035 expansion list names the oblasts, so check whether yours is on it
trackers.desc: THE PIPELINE IS PUBLISHED AND IT NAMES REGIONS, WHICH TURNS A VAGUE ASPIRATION INTO SOMETHING YOU CAN ATTACH A SITE TO. A committee directorate head has set out the concept running to 2035: the area of specially protected natural territories is to be increased in the Atyrau, Almaty, Kostanay and Turkestan oblasts, with new natural objects appearing in West Kazakhstan, Akmola and the Zhetysu region. If your land sits in one of those, you are arguing for inclusion in a programme the state has already committed to rather than asking it to start one — a completely different conversation. The same concept carries a named, concrete item worth citing as precedent: an ecological corridor between the Kolsai and Altyn-Emel national parks to allow snow leopard migration, which establishes that connective corridors between existing parks, not just blocks of land, are within what this committee will create. CURRENT SCALE, for arguing proportion: specially protected natural territories stand at 31.1 million hectares, close to 11.5 per cent of the country. THE ROUTE MOST PEOPLE OVERLOOK IS EXPANSION RATHER THAN CREATION: the governing law of 7 July 2006 regulates the creation and the expansion of specially protected natural territories alike, and extending the boundary of a park that already exists, already has an administration and already has a management regime is a far shorter path than constituting a new one. If your site adjoins an existing protected area, argue extension. WHO: the Committee of Forestry and Wildlife of the Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources, whose own pages sit on the GOV.KZ state platform. THE LIMIT, AND IT IS THE SAME ONE THIS FILE HAS RECORDED FOR RSCN, GEORGIA'S PROTECTED AREAS AGENCY AND OTHERS: this committee also administers forestry and hunting use. It is the body that grants what it also restricts, so approach it about designation rather than expecting it to oppose a licence it issued. Note the related tactic already recorded in this file for Kazakhstan: ACBK took two hunting concessions totalling some 340,000 hectares out of hunting use by holding the leases itself. SOURCING CAVEAT: the 2035 regional list and the hectare figures come from a state broadcaster's report quoting the committee official by name, not from the committee's own published concept — ask the committee for the concept document itself before building a submission on those regions.

trackers.name: EcoMuseum Karaganda — it takes its own samples at contaminated sites and publishes the results
trackers.desc: THIS ORGANISATION DOES THE ONE THING A POLLUTION FIGHT ALWAYS NEEDS AND ALMOST NOBODY WILL DO: it collects information on contaminated territories and on places where toxic and hazardous substances may be buried — naming abandoned military ranges and industrial sites specifically — and it shares the results of its own sampling and analysis at those sites through its information platforms and the media. Independent sampling, published, is worth more than any amount of objection letters, and if a scheme is proposed on or beside ground with an industrial or military past this is where to ask what is already known about it before anyone commissions a survey with the developer's money. Its own stated aims include studying acute environmental problems by gathering information and conducting its own environmental research. THERE IS ALSO A STANDING ADVICE CENTRE: an Information and Consultation Centre on Chemical Safety of Kazakhstan operates at the museum, accumulating information on the state of the environment, and its training programme covers how the public can influence state decision-making, how to initiate legislative change, and how to find sources of finance for regional projects — which is unusually practical for a body of this kind. AND IT PASSES MONEY DOWN: it runs local and national awareness campaigns through an established network of non-governmental organisations using sub-grants, so a small group elsewhere in Kazakhstan may be able to reach it through that network rather than approaching alone. WHAT ELSE IT HOLDS: an exhibition hall with an information centre and library, mobile exhibitions, and distance online courses. Its historical work includes the mercury contamination of the Nura river and documentation of the consequences of nuclear testing at Semipalatinsk, publishing maps, photographs and scientific reports that had previously been inaccessible; it posted on a mercury-bearing river in Karaganda oblast as recently as 2023. It publishes annual activity reports on its own site, which is a better accountability record than most organisations in this file offer. Based in Karaganda; a public association, membership-based, working with volunteers. THE LIMITS: it is an information, research and education body, not a litigator, a funder of your case, or a landholder. It works in cooperation with the state rather than against it — one of its stated aims is developing cooperation between government and the public — so pair it with Ecological Society Green Salvation, already in this file for Kazakhstan, which litigates, and with ACBK for biodiversity evidence. Its regional focus is Karaganda and industrial contamination; for a case elsewhere, ask whether its NGO network reaches your oblast.

trackers.name: Eco Mangystau — official air testing arrives too late to catch the exceedance, so they put up twelve of their own sensors
trackers.desc: THE REASON THIS ORGANISATION EXISTS IS A PROBLEM EVERY RURAL COMMUNITY FACING AN INDUSTRIAL NEIGHBOUR WILL RECOGNISE, AND ITS DIRECTOR STATES IT PLAINLY: after residents complain about air quality, state specialists do come out and take laboratory measurements — but because the districts are remote the work is carried out with delay, and by then it is no longer possible to establish whether the maximum permissible concentration was exceeded. The official system is not refusing to measure; it is arriving after the evidence has dispersed. That is why the answer is a sensor on the ground before the next episode, not a complaint after it. THEY HAVE BUILT EXACTLY THAT: twelve citizen-monitoring sensors installed across Mangystau oblast — in Bautino, Kuryk, the Munaily district including Mangyshlak station and Baskuduk, and in Zhanaozen and Aktau among others. Their public environmental inspection also runs gas analysers reading nitrogen dioxide, carbon monoxide, hydrogen sulphide, ammonia, methane and carbon dioxide, so they can characterise a release rather than merely record that one happened. AND THERE IS A PUBLIC MAP YOU CAN ADD TO: with partners in Karaganda and the Czech Republic they built an online map of environmental hot spots covering more than twenty cases, on which citizens can comment or submit new ones. Getting your site onto a public register that already has standing is faster than establishing your own. The problems it documents across the region are accumulating solid waste and unauthorised dumps in the steppe, abandoned industrial sites, oil spills and poaching of rare animals. IT ALSO ENGAGES ON NAMED DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS, WHICH MOST MONITORING BODIES DO NOT: its representatives visited Bozzhyra and its director published a public assessment of the condition of the site and of a proposed safari hotel there, in a case that drew attention well beyond Kazakhstan. WHO AND WHERE: a non-governmental institution describing itself as non-party, non-commercial and non-state; director named; office in Aktau, microdistrict 4, and contactable on info@ecomangystau.kz and the Aktau number. ONE THING TO WEIGH ON INDEPENDENCE: the gas-analyser equipment was reported as bought with support from a state-linked presidential foundation, for the stated purpose of strengthening independent civic control over environmental protection. Funding from that quarter is worth knowing about even where the work is genuinely independent — ask before assuming. SCOPE: this is Mangystau. For Karaganda and industrial contamination this file carries EcoMuseum, for litigation Green Salvation, for biodiversity evidence ACBK.

trackers.name: AEOK — publishes a current register of member environmental organisations with the leader, region, email and telephone for each
trackers.desc: THIS IS HOW YOU FIND THE ORGANISATION NEAREST YOU IN A COUNTRY THE SIZE OF WESTERN EUROPE: the association publishes a member register giving, for each organisation, its name, the name of its head, a short description of what it does, the region it works in with its business identification number, an email address and a telephone number. Most Kazakh environmental organisations have no website at all; this register is the practical substitute, and it was current as of May 2026. If a scheme is proposed in your oblast, look up who is already constituted and working there before starting anything of your own — an existing organisation with a registration number and a track record can act where an unincorporated group of neighbours cannot. WHAT IT IS: an association of legal entities, describing itself as non-commercial, independent and non-governmental, whose stated purpose is consolidating Kazakhstan's environmental community to generate and advance systemic environmental initiatives. Based in Astana. IT IS ALSO CONNECTED TO A PUBLIC MONITORING MAP: an interactive map of public environmental monitoring lists the association among its contacts, which is worth following up if your dispute turns on measured pollution — read it alongside the twelve citizen sensors run by the Mangystau organisation recorded elsewhere in this file, and the independent sampling done by the Karaganda ecological museum. THE LIMITS, AND THEY MATTER FOR HOW YOU USE IT: an association consolidates a sector, it does not litigate, fund a case or hold land, and a body whose purpose is coordination is unlikely to lead opposition to a specific project. Its value is the register and the introductions. For litigation Kazakhstan has Ecological Society Green Salvation already in this file; for independent sampling the Karaganda museum; for air monitoring the Mangystau organisation; for biodiversity evidence ACBK; for an appointed advocate the state-guaranteed legal aid route. TWO NOTES: directory listings give two different Astana addresses for this association, so take the address from aeok.kz itself; and a second national body, an association of practising ecologists, separately publishes its own list of environmental NGO contacts dated October 2025 — between them the two registers are the closest thing Kazakhstan has to a national directory of who is active where.

trackers.name: Ecoforum Kazakhstan — it incorporated after 23 years as a network because public environmental expertise requires a legal entity
trackers.desc: IF YOUR GROUP IS DECIDING WHETHER TO REGISTER, THIS IS THE ANSWER, AND IT COMES FROM A NETWORK THAT SPENT TWENTY-THREE YEARS NOT REGISTERING: Ecoforum existed from 1997 as an informal network of public organisations and independent experts, and in 2020 registered as an association of legal entities because — in its own words — in order to carry out public environmental expertise, public oversight and other important functions, it is necessary to be a legal person. An unincorporated group of neighbours can protest, gather signatures and give evidence; it generally cannot lodge the formal public environmental review that carries weight against a developer's own assessment. Registering is not bureaucracy for its own sake, it is what unlocks the instrument. AND YOU CAN JOIN WITHOUT MONEY: its charter provides two tiers — full membership, which pays dues and votes in the general assembly, and associate membership, which pays no dues and takes no part in governance. For a small local group that wants the network's cover and contacts without a subscription it cannot afford, the associate tier is the door. IT ALSO USES THE INTERNATIONAL COMPLIANCE ROUTE, WHICH ALMOST NO LOCAL BODY DOES: its public participation working group made a submission to the Aarhus Convention Compliance Committee arguing that hearings held by video conference had widened access for environmental organisations and should continue after the state of emergency ended. A network that has already corresponded with a treaty compliance body knows how to put a Kazakh participation failure in front of one. It describes itself as a national network of environmental non-governmental organisations, is a co-organiser of the Central Asian civil society climate network, works with the international chemical safety network and the European ECO Forum, and states that it supports no political party though its members may. ONE OF ITS CO-FOUNDERS ALSO HEADS THE MANGYSTAU MONITORING ORGANISATION RECORDED ELSEWHERE IN THIS FILE, which is worth knowing: the Kazakh environmental sector is small and interlocking, and an approach through one body reaches several. THE LIMITS: a network coordinates, trains and makes submissions; it does not litigate your case, fund it or hold land. Kazakhstan's other entries here cover litigation, independent sampling, air monitoring, biodiversity evidence, an appointed advocate and a member register. Use this one for the expertise route and the Aarhus channel.

trackers.name: CEPF Mountains of Central Asia — Kazakhstan is a named eligible country, and a new grant portfolio opened in 2026
trackers.desc: KAZAKHSTAN IS NAMED IN CEPF'S OWN CALLS AS AN ELIGIBLE COUNTRY, ALONGSIDE KYRGYZSTAN, TAJIKISTAN, TURKMENISTAN AND UZBEKISTAN — and the fund is entering a new phase, with nearly a hundred projects completed in the first and a new portfolio starting in 2026. Only the southern part of the country falls inside the hotspot, which follows the Tien Shan rather than administrative borders, so the first question is whether your site is inside it. WHAT IT FUNDS AND WHO CAN APPLY: letters of inquiry are accepted from non-governmental organisations, community groups, Indigenous peoples' organisations, women's groups, private companies and other civil society organisations. Large grants in recent calls ran from fifty thousand to a hundred and fifty thousand US dollars; small grants average around fifteen thousand and are handled by the regional implementation team rather than the secretariat. THE GATE IS THE ECOSYSTEM PROFILE, AND IT IS SPECIFIC: applications must align with the strategic directions, investment priorities, priority species, priority Key Biodiversity Areas or priority corridors named in that document, with the priority lists set out in its own numbered chapters and per-country tables. The 2025 update identified 126 globally threatened species in the hotspot, close to double the 2017 figure, and around 170 Key Biodiversity Areas covering some 200,000 square kilometres. ONE OPERATIONAL DETAIL THAT DECIDES WHERE TO APPLY, AND ALMOST NOBODY EXPECTS IT: CEPF has previously stated a preference NOT to fund additional projects in Key Biodiversity Areas that already carry three or more CEPF-funded projects. Crowding counts against you. Check which sites are already saturated before choosing yours. THE INDIVIDUAL BAR APPLIES: individuals cannot apply directly and must work through a civil society organisation. CEPF is funded jointly by the French Development Agency, Conservation International, the European Union, the Global Environment Facility, the Government of Japan and the World Bank; the global fund belongs elsewhere in this map, this entry records the Central Asian window. Confirm the current regional implementation team and the open call before drafting — the team for earlier phases may not be the team for the 2026 portfolio.

trackers.name: ProtectDefenders.eu — an individual can ask without an organisation, in Russian, at any hour
trackers.desc: THERE ARE TWO SEPARATE REQUEST CHANNELS, ONE FOR INDIVIDUALS AND ONE FOR ORGANISATIONS — so a person facing retaliation does not need a registered body behind them to ask. That matters in a region where this file has repeatedly found registration to be the gate. AND YOU CAN CORRESPOND OFFICIALLY IN RUSSIAN, alongside English, French, Spanish and Arabic, through a 24/7 emergency helpline and an encrypted secure contact form. WHAT THE MONEY COVERS AND WHAT IT IS WORTH: emergency grants for urgent protection measures, capped at €10,000 with an AVERAGE GRANT OF ABOUT €3,000, assessed case by case with no deadline and applications on a rolling basis. For organisations the grants cover capacity building, psychosocial support, security, advocacy training and emergency relocation, and it states that list is not exhaustive and an organisation may propose other measures. Delivered through partner organisations, one of which is recorded separately in this file. THE THREE CRITERIA ARE SHORT AND WORTH CHECKING YOURSELF: that you are a defender working for human rights consistent with the United Nations declaration; that you face risk BECAUSE OF that work; and that the need is urgent — with lack of access to other sources of support expressly taken into account. The third point rewards saying plainly that nobody else will help. NOW THE WARNING NO OTHER FUNDER IN THIS FILE GIVES: its own guidance states that payment may be made by bank transfer or Western Union, that the transfer WILL SHOW IT COMES FROM ProtectDefenders.eu, and that a recipient should understand the security implications of receiving such a transfer and tell the secretariat. Receiving the money can itself expose you. Raise it before the grant is made, not after. IT ALSO RUNS TEMPORARY RELOCATION, and the design point is worth knowing: preference is given to relocating a defender WITHIN THEIR OWN COUNTRY OR SUB-REGION where possible, so that they can keep working — funding goes to a host organisation that implements it, for up to twelve months, and it cannot cover the whole cost. THE LIMITS, STATED BY THE MECHANISM ITSELF: it cannot support all defenders in need, and it directs those it cannot help to other organisations. Its central secretariat no longer assesses grant application forms directly; it assesses your request and routes you to the partner running the relevant programme. No case of its own in Kazakhstan could be established.

trackers.name: Save Kok-Zhailau — the land was moved out of protected status before the project came, and they proved it
trackers.desc: CHECK THE LAND'S CATEGORY HISTORY, NOT JUST ITS CURRENT STATUS. This group documented that the tract in question had been TRANSFERRED OUT OF THE CATEGORY OF SPECIALLY PROTECTED NATURAL TERRITORIES AND INTO RESERVE LANDS, and argued that the transfer was unjustified and had itself already caused substantial ecological deterioration. A developer does not need to defeat a protected area if the protection can be lifted administratively first. Ask when your site's legal category last changed, on whose decision, and what justification was given — that document is often older and less guarded than the project file. THE CAMPAIGN RAN MORE THAN EIGHT YEARS AND THE PROJECT WAS ABANDONED after the head of state said publicly that it was not needed. IT HAS SINCE RETURNED UNDER A NEW NAME and this group is contesting it again, which is why the entry is written for a reader starting today rather than as a history. ITS SITE IS A MODEL WORTH COPYING EXACTLY, BECAUSE IT IS BUILT AS A WORKING TOOL RATHER THAN A BLOG: sections for information about the construction, a standing reference briefing, a petition to sign, and a journalistic investigation. Facts, briefing, action and investigation in four places a newcomer can find in seconds. Its 2018 petition drew 28,960 signatures; a 2025 online appeal to the president, demanding transparency and early discussion of projects, drew more than 8,000. EXPECT TWO SPECIFIC OBSTRUCTIONS THAT THIS CAMPAIGN HAS MET REPEATEDLY. Authorities restrict access to project documents by classifying them as being for OFFICIAL USE — a refusal ground to prepare for, and one the access-to-information routes recorded elsewhere in this file exist to contest. And a project that is paused is not a project that is stopped: at one point the city administration offered to postpone the scheme for three to five years for more thorough study, and the group refused to treat a delay as a solution. Earlier still, the same scheme was rebranded from a ski resort into an all-season mountain park of supposedly reduced scale; this file records the same rebranding pattern in Turkiye, where annulled plans returned in new forms. IT ARGUES WITH THE DEVELOPER'S OWN NUMBERS, WHICH IS THE HABIT TO COPY: from the project's own assessment it drew that atmospheric emissions during operation could rise from 19 to 104.9 tonnes a year. It works alongside the Almaty ecological society recorded in this map, whose members photographed excavators and trucks leaving fresh tracks on the mountain paths in October 2025 — documenting machinery on the ground is what turns an argument about permits into a record of what is actually happening. An initiative group rather than a registered body, with named participants, based in Almaty.

trackers.name: KIBHR — ten regional branches, free legal consultations, and receptions that travel to district towns
trackers.desc: TEN REGIONAL BRANCHES ACROSS THE COUNTRY, WHICH IS THE POINT IN A STATE THIS SIZE. Every other Kazakh entry in this file works out of Almaty, Karaganda or Mangystau; this one has offices in cities across the regions, with published street addresses and telephone numbers. Founded in 1993 by a group of human rights defenders and civil society activists, it is described as one of the largest human rights organisations in the country. IT RUNS TWO THINGS A COMMUNITY CAN USE DIRECTLY: a human rights centre staffed by its own lawyers, and a volunteer centre that provides FREE LEGAL CONSULTATIONS TO CITIZENS. AND ITS RECEPTIONS TRAVEL. Its own notices advertise field legal receptions in district towns — one scheduled in a town in the Almaty region — and free legal consultations run by its regional branches. This file has now recorded the same arrangement in Tajikistan: where state legal aid is narrow, the practical free lawyer is a rights organisation with branches that comes to you. Check its announcements page for the next reception in your region rather than assuming you must travel to the head office. IT ALSO PUBLISHED SOMETHING WORTH HAVING BEFORE YOU NEED IT: A LIST OF THE HUMAN RIGHTS COMMISSIONER'S REPRESENTATIVES IN EACH REGION OF KAZAKHSTAN, WITH THEIR CONTACTS. Knowing which official in your own region receives complaints, by name and number, removes the first obstacle in most disputes — and this file has recorded across several countries that finding the right desk is most of the difficulty. It runs an education centre giving training, lectures and seminars, and annual human rights schools. It remains active, having held director elections and moved its head office in 2024, with notices published into 2026. THE LIMIT: this is a civil and political rights organisation, not an environmental or planning one. Nothing found shows it litigating a development scheme or a land use decision. Approach it for the consultation, for the branch nearest you, and for matters where a land dispute has become a rights dispute — obstruction of a public hearing, pressure on objectors, detention at a protest, or refusal of information. For the scheme itself, use the ecological society and the association of environmental organisations recorded separately here, and the international complaint routes where a lender is involved.

trackers.name: Tabigat Association — a rural association running hotspot-fund conservation work in named villages
trackers.desc: THE MOST USEFUL THING ABOUT THIS ENTRY MAY BE HOW IT WAS FOUND. It is a local association implementing the mountain Central Asia programme of an international hotspot conservation fund — a fund this file records for eight countries as a source of money. IT DID NOT SURFACE BY SEARCHING FOR ORGANISATIONS; IT SURFACED AS SOMEBODY'S GRANTEE. THAT MAKES A FUNDER'S GRANTEE LIST A DIRECTORY OF ACTIVE LOCAL BODIES, WHICH IS PRECISELY WHAT THIS MAP HAS FAILED TO ASSEMBLE BY OTHER MEANS. Thirteen organisations in this payload are documented as real, active and unrecordable because no address could be found. Asking a fund which organisations currently hold its grants in your country is a route to the same layer, and it works in the countries where searching does not. WHAT IT DOES: conservation of key biodiversity areas in the mountains, working at village level and naming the settlements it works in rather than describing a region. Its own account of the area is unusually candid about how conservation there actually functions — that the local population historically hunted game, especially the hoofed animals once abundant there; that PROTECTED AREA STATUS AND THE OPENING OF HUNTING CONCESSIONS TOGETHER SLOWED THE UNCONTROLLED DESTRUCTION OF ANIMAL RESOURCES AND REDUCED POACHING; and that neither has stopped it completely. THAT IS THE SAME MECHANISM THIS FILE RECORDED IN KAZAKHSTAN AND TAJIKISTAN FROM THE OTHER DIRECTION — that a concession which gives someone a stake in the animals surviving does more than a designation alone — and here it is stated by a village-level body about its own district, including the part most organisations leave out, which is that it only partly worked. THE LIMITS: it is a conservation association, not an objector, and nothing found shows it opposing a development scheme. Its work is grant-funded, so its presence in any particular district depends on a grant cycle continuing. Ask what it currently holds and where, and treat it as a route into the villages it names rather than as a national body. DO NOT CONFUSE IT WITH THE KAZAKH ASSOCIATION OF ENVIRONMENTAL ORGANISATIONS RECORDED SEPARATELY HERE, which publishes a member register and is a different body with a different function.

trackers.name: ELAW — expert critiques of impact assessments, and help building the alternative plan
trackers.desc: IT SUPPLIES WHAT A LOCAL CASE USUALLY LACKS: SCIENCE. A global alliance of attorneys and scientists whose science team CRITIQUES ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT ASSESSMENTS, SUBMITS EXPERT TESTIMONY TO COURTS, develops systems to MONITOR environmental conditions, and RECOMMENDS CLEANER ALTERNATIVES TO PROPOSED PROJECTS. That last one matters here more than anywhere: this file recorded a Kazakh case where a WORKED ALTERNATIVE PLAN, not objection alone, is what moved the outcome, and another where a developer split a project into pieces to escape cumulative assessment. Both are arguments that need technical authorship, and this is where a local advocate gets it. IT ALSO CONNECTS LOCAL SCIENTISTS TO LOCAL LAWYERS — the gap this payload has documented repeatedly, where a museum or institute holds the contamination data and the litigator never reaches them. ITS LAW TEAM HELPS PARTNERS BRING ENFORCEMENT ACTIONS, critique draft legislation and REPLICATE MODEL LAWS FROM OTHER JURISDICTIONS, which is directly usable where this file has recorded a foreign court ruling being cited across borders against project fragmentation. It works on DEFENDING DEFENDERS as well, improving the safety of advocates under pressure. HOW TO USE IT, AND THIS IS THE KEY POINT: IT WORKS THROUGH PARTNERS — PUBLIC INTEREST LAWYERS IN THEIR OWN COUNTRIES — NOT DIRECTLY WITH COMMUNITIES. Instruct or find a local advocate first, then have them request support. Founded in 1989 by public interest lawyers from ten countries, now numbering over three hundred advocates in more than eighty countries, handling upwards of four hundred requests a year, and bringing advocates abroad as fellows. THE LIMITS: it does not represent clients, fund cases or campaign; its partners must be lawyers; and whether it has partners in this country was not established here — ask first. It is also a different organisation from the similarly named centre recorded elsewhere in this file that places pro bono lawyers.

trackers.name: International Center for Community Land Trusts — a vehicle for holding land that cannot be sold off later
trackers.desc: THE POINT OF A COMMUNITY LAND TRUST IS THAT THE LAND STOPS BEING SELLABLE. A nonprofit holds the ground permanently, residents own only what stands on it, and the board combines resident members, wider community members and public representatives — so the land cannot be quietly transferred by one owner or one administration. This file recorded a provision in this country by which land left unworked can attract a tenfold tax and then pass into a state fund for sale at auction; a trust that holds land collectively, with a constitution and a board, is a different proposition from a family plot that lapses. TRUSTS ARE NOT ONLY FOR HOUSING: they develop RURAL AND URBAN AGRICULTURE PROJECTS AND CONSERVE LAND AND GREEN SPACES, which is the use most relevant where pasture, orchard or steppe is at issue. THIS CENTRE PROVIDES THE HOW: established to support such trusts and similar community-owned-land strategies IN COUNTRIES THROUGHOUT THE WORLD, offering TRAINING, REFERRAL AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE to organisers, plus case studies, directories and guides. A FREE START-UP MANUAL SITS ON ITS OWN SITE, covering the organisational and operational choices in founding a trust and the alternative sponsors who can carry a start-up — an existing organisation, a municipality, a group of residents, or a combination. That question of sponsorship matters here, because this file has recorded that community land holding in this region runs through associations and committees that already exist rather than through new bodies. Its annual global summit of free online sessions, with recordings kept, is the cheapest way to see how others did it. THE LIMITS, PLAINLY: it is a knowledge and support body, NOT A FUNDER — it will not buy the land, and this file records a separate international fund that pays for acquisition and long-term leases, which is the other half of this. Its case material is overwhelmingly North American and European, and no activity in this region was established. It also requires you to be able to form a registered nonprofit, which is the barrier this payload has found decisive again and again.

trackers.name: OCCRP Aleph — search corporate registries, court records and land registries to find who is really behind a project
trackers.desc: THIS IS WHERE YOU FIND OUT WHO OWNS THE COMPANY THAT IS TAKING YOUR LAND. It indexes over a billion records from more than three hundred datasets across more than a hundred and eighty countries — CORPORATE REGISTRIES, COURT RECORDS, LAND REGISTRIES, sanctions lists, procurement databases, air and maritime registries and leaked archives — all searchable and cross-referenceable in one place, WITH A RUSSIAN-LANGUAGE INTERFACE. ITS COVERAGE IS DESCRIBED AS STRONGEST IN EASTERN EUROPE AND THE FORMER SOVIET STATES, which includes this country. IT ANSWERS THE SPECIFIC PROBLEM THIS FILE RECORDED HERE. A resort scheme defeated after an eight-year campaign CAME BACK UNDER A NEW NAME, and another project was split into separate objects so that no single one required a full assessment. A renamed company and a fragmented project are both visible in a registry: same directors, same address, same beneficial owner, different name. Search the developer, then search the people behind it, then search their other companies. THE FEATURE THAT MATTERS MOST IS CROSS-REFERENCING: you can UPLOAD YOUR OWN DOCUMENTS — information requests you have obtained, permits, contracts, correspondence — and the platform will match the names and companies in them against its entire corpus. A permit naming a company you have never heard of becomes a chain of ownership in an afternoon. ACCESS AND COST: anyone may search the publicly available data, and JOURNALISTS, RESEARCHERS AND ACTIVISTS WORKING IN THE PUBLIC INTEREST CAN APPLY FOR BROADER ACCESS AT NO CHARGE. Some datasets are restricted and access is decided case by case on application. TWO WARNINGS THAT MATTER. FINDINGS MUST BE INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED before you use them — the platform itself says so, leaked datasets are by nature incomplete, and a claim built on an unverified record hands the other side its rebuttal. And the platform was rebuilt in December 2025 after the original open-source version was retired, so guides written earlier describe a system that no longer exists. IT WILL NOT TELL YOU WHAT TO DO WITH WHAT YOU FIND. Pair it with the ownership and procurement routes recorded separately for this country, and with the litigating organisations — this file has recorded that following the money reaches places an environmental objection cannot.

trackers.name: Aarhus Centres — regional offices that advise the public on access to justice in environmental matters
trackers.desc: THERE ARE CENTRES IN CITIES AND REGIONS ACROSS THE COUNTRY, NOT ONLY IN THE CAPITAL — among them Almaty, Astana, Karaganda, Kokshetau, Kyzylorda, Burabay and the eastern region. Their published purpose is to organise the conditions for PUBLIC ACCESS TO INFORMATION, PARTICIPATION IN DECISION-MAKING and ACCESS TO JUSTICE. This file has recorded for this country a project that returned under a new name, a scheme split into pieces to escape cumulative assessment, and land recategorised before approval — all of which are questions of who knew what, and when. ONE REGIONAL CENTRE'S PUBLISHED ACTIVITIES INCLUDE ADVISING THE PUBLIC ON ACCESS TO JUSTICE IN ENVIRONMENTAL MATTERS, alongside organising PUBLIC HEARINGS and running lectures, seminars, forums and round tables for executive bodies, public associations, and individuals and legal entities. A body that convenes public hearings is a body that can be asked to convene one. THEY ARE CONSTITUTED UNDER BOTH THE INTERNATIONAL CONVENTION AND THE NATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL CODE, which means their function rests on this country's own law rather than on a donor's programme — a durability this payload's funded projects mostly lack. AND THEIR STATED ROLE IS TO SERVE AS A LINK BETWEEN CENTRAL AND LOCAL STATE AUTHORITIES AND NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS on environmental policy and its implementation in the region. For a community whose objection dies between a district office and a ministry, an institution whose declared job is to connect those two is worth approaching early. THE NETWORK IS LARGE: sixty centres across fourteen countries, seven of them in this chat's region, working as a network with each other. THE LIMITS: these centres are supported by an intergovernmental security organisation and work in close co-operation with host authorities — THEY ARE NOT INDEPENDENT, and several sit alongside the very bodies a community may be contesting. They facilitate access rather than represent anyone: expect information, hearings and advice on how to reach a court, not a lawyer. Pair them with the free legal consultations, the litigating organisations and the corporate ownership search recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Commissioner for Human Rights — it can demand the documents, and put the officials in the room
trackers.desc: TWO OF ITS STATUTORY POWERS ARE THINGS A COMMUNITY CANNOT DO FOR ITSELF. FIRST, WHEN CONSIDERING A COMPLAINT IT MAY REQUEST AND OBTAIN FROM STATE BODIES, LOCAL GOVERNMENT AND SELF-GOVERNMENT BODIES, OTHER ORGANISATIONS AND OFFICIALS THE DOCUMENTS, MATERIALS AND INFORMATION NEEDED TO CONSIDER IT. That reaches beyond the state to other organisations, and it is a disclosure power — this file has recorded across the region that the decisive documents are the ones a community is never shown. SECOND, IT MAY ORGANISE PROMPT RECEPTION OF COMPLAINANTS INCLUDING WITH THE INVITATION OF REPRESENTATIVES OF STATE BODIES, LOCAL GOVERNMENT AND OTHER ORGANISATIONS — JOINT RECEPTIONS. Getting the authority and the operator into the same room, at a third party's invitation, is the thing almost no community can arrange for itself. AND IT DOES NOT NEED A COMPLAINT AT ALL: it may consider matters ON ITS OWN INITIATIVE where there is information of a MASS VIOLATION of rights, or where a violation HAS PUBLIC SIGNIFICANCE. A village-wide displacement, a contaminated water supply or a scheme affecting a whole district is both — which means the route can begin with published information rather than with a signed complaint from an exposed household. IT ALSO HAS ACCESS, IN THE ESTABLISHED PROCEDURE, TO DOCUMENTS OF STATE ORGANISATIONS AND OF PUBLIC ASSOCIATIONS on questions of human rights and freedoms. IT IS NOT ONLY IN THE CAPITAL, WHICH THE OTHER INSTITUTIONS OF THIS KIND RECORDED IN THIS FILE COULD NOT DEMONSTRATE: regional representatives have taken up work across nine named regions and the three cities, with representations planned in SEVENTEEN REGIONS, and at least one city representative publishes a mobile telephone number and an office address. Ask for the representative in your own region rather than writing to the capital. NOW THE RULE THAT DECIDES YOUR ORDER OF OPERATIONS, AND IT IS EASY TO GET WRONG: THE DOCUMENT POWER DOES NOT EXTEND TO CASES AND MATERIALS ALREADY IN COURT PROCEEDINGS. If you file suit first, this office can no longer obtain the file. CONSULT IT BEFORE LITIGATING, not after — use it to get the documents and the joint meeting, and go to court with what it produces. THE OTHER LIMITS: its primary task is stated as assisting the restoration of violated rights and improving legal acts, not representing anyone; no power to bring proceedings in court was established; and it is a state office, so a complaint is a disclosure.

trackers.name: Public hearings register — see which hearings are open right now, not after they close
trackers.desc: IT PUBLISHES THE LIST OF PUBLIC HEARINGS AVAILABLE AT THE PRESENT MOMENT. That is the difference between finding out about a hearing and finding out about it afterwards — and in this country this file has recorded three separate ways a scheme gets past people who were not watching. A PROJECT DEFEATED ONCE CAME BACK UNDER A NEW NAME. A SCHEME WAS SPLIT INTO PIECES so that no single part triggered cumulative assessment. LAND WAS RECATEGORISED BEFORE APPROVAL so that the approval became routine. All three are visible, if they are visible at all, at the hearing stage — and only to somebody who knew the hearing was being held. A national list of open hearings is how a village checks that without waiting for a notice pinned to a wall. IT IS RUN THROUGH THE ENVIRONMENT MINISTRY'S INFORMATION AND ANALYTICAL CENTRE, as part of the national database on the state of the environment and natural resources — so it sits inside the state's own environmental information system rather than being a project website that lapses. CHECK IT FOR THE DISTRICT NEXT TO YOURS AS WELL AS YOUR OWN. This file has recorded across the region that upstream and adjacent works decide what happens on your ground — a dam above a valley, a quarry over a ridge, a road corridor two districts away. USE IT WITH TWO OTHER ENTRIES ALREADY RECORDED FOR THIS COUNTRY, AND IN THIS ORDER. The Aarhus centres here advise on ACCESS TO JUSTICE IN ENVIRONMENTAL MATTERS and themselves organise public hearings, so they can tell you what the hearing must contain. The human rights commissioner can DEMAND DOCUMENTS from state bodies and other organisations — but that power stops once a matter is in court, so use it before litigating, not after. THE LIMITS: this is a state portal and it shows what has been NOTIFIED — a hearing that was never posted is invisible here, which is itself worth recording if you later discover one took place. Registration and participation procedures vary by hearing, and the environmental code sets the periods, so confirm the closing date rather than assuming it. And a hearing held is not a hearing heeded: attendance creates a record, not a veto.

trackers.name: Environmental Defender Law Center — it funds the expert and the litigation expenses
trackers.desc: THE SERVICE TO ASK FOR FIRST IS THE EXPERT. It has ACCESS TO EXPERT NETWORKS, experts frequently work for it pro bono or at reduced fee, AND IT IS OFTEN ABLE TO FUND THEIR EXPENSES — and this file has recorded across this region that the decisive gap is not willingness but the cost of proving harm. This country's listing already holds satellite imagery, species databases, an environmental hearings register and a commissioner who can demand documents. WHAT IT HAS NOT HELD IS ANYONE WHO WILL PAY FOR THE ANALYSIS THAT TURNS THOSE INTO EVIDENCE. IT ALSO ASSISTS LOCAL LAWYERS DIRECTLY: it is frequently asked to help lawyers in cases before domestic courts, and prepares and submits legal briefs in those cases. A local advocate running an environmental case here can therefore obtain outside legal drafting and argument without surrendering the case. AND IT GIVES GRANTS FOR THE EXPENSES OF PUBLIC INTEREST LITIGATION against those responsible for resource development projects — a programme running since 2010 with about a hundred grants made. ITS THIRD SERVICE IS FINDING LAWYERS: enlisting private firms to act pro bono for communities harmed by projects, for people CHARGED OR IMPRISONED IN POLITICALLY MOTIVATED PROSECUTIONS, and for land claims. This payload has documented in this country a project that returned under a new name, a scheme split to escape cumulative assessment, and land recategorised before approval — the kind of pattern that needs a lawyer able to look at the whole sequence rather than one permit. ITS STRATEGY IS TO INTERNATIONALISE: demonstrating to decision-makers that what has been done breaches international human rights norms AND THE STATE'S OWN TREATY OBLIGATIONS. Where this country has ratified conventions on environmental information and public participation, that is the frame to use. THE LIMITS: it works in developing countries and prefers cases of international significance whose legal strategy can be replicated, so it screens hard; it is a foreign non-profit funded by foundations and donations; and contact is by email, with eligibility and application details to be requested directly. Use it alongside the Aarhus centres and the free legal consultations recorded separately for this country, which are where a case starts.

trackers.name: Privately protected areas country profile — which land-holding tools exist here, and what holding land requires
trackers.desc: THERE IS A COUNTRY PROFILE FOR THIS COUNTRY, AND IT SETS OUT THE LEGAL, POLICY AND INSTITUTIONAL MECHANISMS USED TO ESTABLISH AND INCENTIVISE PRIVATELY PROTECTED AREAS — which is the question a community asks first and this map has usually answered with an example rather than a rule. The profiles were produced with a United Nations agency for thirty understudied countries. THEY NAME THE TOOLS THAT ACTUALLY EXIST, WHICH DIFFER BY COUNTRY: private nature reserves, formal and informal; LAND PURCHASES BY ORGANISATIONS FOR CONSERVATION; CONSERVATION AND ECOLOGICAL EASEMENTS — legal limitations on the rights of use and exploitation imposed on a property for the conservation of renewable natural resources; and AGREEMENTS BETWEEN ADJACENT LANDOWNERS in which an organisation holds one parcel and restricts what may be done on the neighbouring one, a device that has been UPHELD BY THE COURTS where it was used. That last one is worth dwelling on: it means an organisation can restrain use of land it does not own, by holding the plot next to it. AND THE PROFILES SET THE STANDARD A HOLDING MUST MEET, WHICH IS THE QUESTION THIS FILE HAS SPENT THREE HUNDRED ROUNDS NOT ASKING. A protected area counts if its protection is RECOGNISED AND DURABLE with long-term conservation intent, if it is GOVERNED BY A PRIVATE OR NON-GOVERNMENTAL ENTITY, and if it is GOVERNED AND MANAGED TO MEET CONSERVATION OBJECTIVES. Securing ground is the beginning; that sentence is the rest of it. THE CONDITIONS THAT CATCH PEOPLE OUT ARE ALSO THERE: REGISTERED TITLE in the owner's name, MINIMUM DURATIONS of five, ten or twenty years with renewal, MAXIMUM AREAS, and A MANAGEMENT PLAN stating how activities will be applied to protect the resources named. A community that secures land without a management plan and a named holder has not finished. AND THERE IS AN OPTION FOR THOSE WHO CANNOT REGISTER ANYTHING: in one country owners AFFILIATE TO A NATIONAL NETWORK OF PRIVATE RESERVES, gaining the benefit of association with a larger regulatory organisation WITHOUT LEGALLY REGISTERING THEIR PROPERTY. This payload's most repeated finding is that communities are blocked by registration; that is a route around it, and worth asking whether an equivalent network exists here. WHY IT MATTERS IN THIS COUNTRY PARTICULARLY: this file records a conservation initiative here working toward a corridor linking two reserves THROUGH NEW STATE PROTECTED AREAS, COMMERCIALLY MANAGED HUNTING AREAS AND PRIVATELY MANAGED LANDS. The profile is where the legal basis for that third category is set out. THE LIMITS: THE PROFILES WERE COMPLETED IN 2018 AND PUBLISHED IN 2019, so what is permitted may have changed and the current law must be checked before relying on any mechanism named. It is a research network rather than a body that acts — nobody there will buy land, fund anything or advise on a case. And the framework is written around landowners, so a community without title reads it to learn what an ALLY WITH TITLE could do on its behalf.

trackers.name: UNESCO Chair on Water Resources Management — a water chair held by a lawyer
trackers.desc: IT IS A WATER CHAIR HELD BY SOMEONE LEGALLY TRAINED, AND THAT COMBINATION IS WHAT A WATER DISPUTE ACTUALLY REQUIRES. Established in 2016 at a German-Kazakh university, the chair covers WATER RESOURCES MANAGEMENT ACROSS CENTRAL ASIA, and its holder is a doctor of laws — so the same person can address what the hydrology shows AND what the legal framework requires. This payload records hydrologists and it records lawyers; it has never before recorded one person who is both. THE CHAIR PUBLISHES A NAMED HOLDER AND A STREET ADDRESS, which is more than most academic institutions in this file offer. A letter can be addressed to a person rather than to an institution. WHY THIS MATTERS IN THIS COUNTRY SPECIFICALLY: the disputes recorded here run to irrigation allocation, pasture water, industrial abstraction and transboundary flows arriving from upstream neighbours. A chair whose subject is regional water management is positioned to say whether a proposed abstraction or diversion is consistent with the arrangements between states — an argument no local objection can make on its own. AND THE APPROACH IS SANCTIONED BY THE PROGRAMME ITSELF: UNESCO chairs are described as THINK TANKS AND BRIDGEBUILDERS BETWEEN ACADEMIA, CIVIL SOCIETY, LOCAL COMMUNITIES, RESEARCH AND POLICY-MAKING. Quote that when you write; it makes the request a function rather than a favour. WHAT TO ASK FOR: a written opinion on whether a scheme's water assumptions hold, an assessment of the instruments that bind this country on shared waters, and an introduction to researchers who hold the field data. NOT representation — a chair cannot act for anyone. THE LIMITS. It is an academic post inside a university with an international partnership, and its work is research, teaching and cooperation rather than advocacy. A chair engaged in regional water diplomacy is also close to the governments doing the diplomacy, so a question framed technically will travel much further than one framed as a complaint. And the listing reached is on a UNESCO water information platform rather than the university's own page — confirm the current holder and address before writing.

trackers.name: National hydrological committee chair — geospatial economics inside an institute of water security
trackers.desc: THIS PAYLOAD HAS RECORDED SATELLITE IMAGERY AND MAPPING TOOLS FOR THIS COUNTRY AND HAS NEVER NAMED ANYONE WHO CAN INTERPRET THEM. The chairperson of the national hydrological committee HEADS A LABORATORY OF GEOSPATIAL ECONOMICS AT AN INSTITUTE OF GEOGRAPHY AND WATER SECURITY, and serves there as chief project and digitalisation manager. GEOSPATIAL CAPABILITY AND WATER SECURITY INSIDE ONE INSTITUTE IS THE PAIRING A COMMUNITY ACTUALLY NEEDS: imagery shows what has changed on the ground, and water science shows what that change does to the water. Separately each is half an argument. AND THE CHAIRPERSON IS AN ECONOMIST, WHICH IS THE UNUSUAL PART. A laboratory of geospatial ECONOMICS measures the VALUE of land and water change — what a converted pasture, a drained wetland or a lowered water table costs. This file recorded in another country that a carbon sequestration figure converts standing habitat into a quantified public value a development case must answer; AN ECONOMIC VALUATION OF LANDSCAPE CHANGE IS THE SAME INSTRUMENT, and a development proposal that counts only its own benefits has to answer it. WHAT TO ASK FOR: whether the institute holds geospatial analysis covering your area, what published work exists on water security in your basin, and what an assessment of land-use change would involve. ASK FOR EXISTING WORK FIRST — published institute research is free, citable, and cannot be dismissed as commissioned by objectors. AND ASK WHO SITS ON THE COMMITTEE. The programme recommends these national committees be MULTI-STAKEHOLDER, including government bodies, professional associations and CIVIL SOCIETY — so the membership list names the country's water institutions in one document, which is a map this file could not otherwise draw. THE LIMITS: the institute operates within state structures and the committee runs under government authority, so neither is independent of the administration; the chairperson is a researcher and will not advocate; and no direct number was published in what was reached, so approach through the institute. Use it with the environmental hearings register, the commissioner who can demand documents, and the litigation-expenses funders recorded separately for this country — this supplies the analysis, those supply the forum and the money.

trackers.name: Treaty compliance committee — file against the state yourself, and check first whether your issue is already under monitoring
trackers.desc: ONE OR MORE MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC MAY BRING A COMMUNICATION TO THIS COMMITTEE ABOUT ANY STATE PARTY'S COMPLIANCE WITH THE TREATY ON ENVIRONMENTAL INFORMATION, PUBLIC PARTICIPATION AND ACCESS TO JUSTICE. No organisation and no lawyer is required to file. THIS COUNTRY HAS A LONG RECORD BEFORE IT, AND TWO OF ITS CASES TEACH OPPOSITE LESSONS. IN ONE, THE COMMITTEE DETERMINED THAT FEASIBILITY STUDIES RELATING TO DRAFT LEGISLATION WERE ENVIRONMENTAL INFORMATION — useful whenever you are told a study is internal. IN ANOTHER, A COMMUNICATION WAS DECLARED INADMISSIBLE BECAUSE IT RAISED ISSUES ALREADY COVERED BY EARLIER FINDINGS THAT WERE UNDER IMPLEMENTATION MONITORING. SO THE FIRST STEP HERE IS NOT TO WRITE BUT TO CHECK: FIND OUT WHETHER YOUR ISSUE IS ALREADY THE SUBJECT OF FINDINGS AGAINST THIS STATE. If it is, THAT IS BETTER NEWS THAN A NEW CASE — you can feed evidence into the existing monitoring rather than starting a process that takes years. THE CURRENT CYCLE: SUBMISSIONS REACHING THE SECRETARIAT BY 28 SEPTEMBER 2026 ARE CONSIDERED FOR PRELIMINARY ADMISSIBILITY IN THE WEEK OF 9 TO 13 NOVEMBER 2026, if complete, in the REQUIRED FORMAT and needing no translation. RUSSIAN IS AN ACCEPTED LANGUAGE and the secretariat arranges translation — but translation costs the deadline, so an English filing is faster. WHAT ITS FINDINGS TREAT AS ENVIRONMENTAL INFORMATION, WHICH IS WORTH KNOWING BEFORE YOU EVEN ASK A MINISTRY: government decrees on LAND USE AND PLANNING, feasibility studies, financial agreements, RENTAL CONTRACTS FOR LAND ADMINISTERED BY A STATE FORESTRY FUND, and RAW UNCALIBRATED DATA on the state of air and atmosphere. A refusal to hand any of these over is itself the material for a communication.
