WHAT GETS REJECTED: anonymity, abuse of the right, manifest unreasonableness, re-running lost domestic litigation, duplication, submissions by state organs, AND INSUFFICIENT CORROBORATING INFORMATION. THE LIMIT: it is a compliance mechanism, NOT A REDRESS PROCEDURE FOR INDIVIDUAL RIGHTS — it cannot quash a decision or award compensation. Use it with the national information centres, the human rights commissioner and the environmental law bodies recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Central Agency for Public Tenders (CAPT)
trackers.desc: National public-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Kuwait, and for how much.

trackers.name: Kuwait — Ministry of Commerce & Industry (MOCI)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the Corporate Affairs & Business Licenses agency registers & licenses companies and regulates commercial activity, State of Kuwait. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Ministry of Justice (Kuwait)
trackers.desc: Official ministry portal with court case inquiry and judicial services. · Find here: Kuwait's Ministry of Justice — court services and legal information.

trackers.name: State Audit Bureau
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Kuwait, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Kuwait Regional Convention (ROPME) — and its Judicial Commission
trackers.desc: THE ONE BINDING ENVIRONMENTAL INSTRUMENT COVERING ALL EIGHT GULF STATES. The Kuwait Regional Convention for Cooperation on the Protection of the Marine Environment from Pollution was signed 24 April 1978 and entered into force 1 July 1979 — 30 articles, described as the basic legal instrument binding the eight States of the Region. ALL EIGHT ARE FULL PARTIES: ROPME records ‘no signatories without ratification, acceptance, approval or accession’, so unlike some regional instruments there is no signed-but-unratified state to argue about. ARTICLE II fixes the Sea Area by coordinates, from Ras Dharbat Ali (16°39'N, 53°3'30"E) to Ras Al Fasteh (25°04'N, 61°25'E) — a treaty boundary you can check a project location against. Use the term ‘ROPME Sea Area’: it was coined by the Plenipotentiaries to achieve unanimity, cooperating in spite of existing geopolitical boundaries, and it is the name all eight accepted. THE ORGAN MOST PEOPLE DO NOT KNOW EXISTS: alongside the Council and Secretariat, ROPME has a Judicial Commission, established March 1989, of 6 nationals of Member States highly qualified in international law. In a region with almost no environmental litigation route, a standing judicial commission under a ratified convention is the most significant legal fact available — though this entry does not assert that individuals may petition it; establish who may seise it first. AN EVIDENCE SOURCE THAT NEEDS NO SITE ACCESS: ROPME's scientific bodies include a Remote Sensing Unit, alongside RIIS and MEMAC. WHICH PROTOCOL FITS YOUR ISSUE: oil-spill emergency response; land-based sources of pollution — the limb for a coastal development, discharge or reclamation; and transboundary movement of hazardous wastes. Development is named as a stressor in ROPME's own statement of purpose. At stake: over 20 species of dolphin and whale, all five subtropical turtle species, and more than 1,000 fish species, most endemic.

trackers.name: MBZ Species Conservation Fund — frame it as species work, not climate
trackers.desc: DO NOT DRESS A SPECIES PROJECT UP AS A CLIMATE PROJECT HERE — which is the opposite of the advice that fits almost every other fund in this map. The MBZ Fund was established on the basis that direct species conservation has lost out to wider concerns such as climate change, sustainability and poverty alleviation, and is now seen as a by-product of larger issues, leaving underfunded field biologists and wardens. It exists to correct that displacement, so frame the work as direct, field-based species conservation. A philanthropic endowment announced at the World Conservation Congress in Barcelona, October 2008, taking applications since March 2009; managing director Razan Khalifa Al Mubarak, also President of IUCN. By end-2010 it had disbursed just over US$5 million to about 380 projects in almost 100 countries; awards run up to US$25,000. TWO UNUSUAL ELIGIBILITY POINTS: it covers all animal, plant AND FUNGI species — fungi are named, which almost no other fund in this map does — and its focus includes data-deficient species, so you need not prove the species is threatened; where the problem is that nobody knows, that is itself a qualifying category. Individual conservationists may apply, and priority goes to projects supporting young conservationists. Funding is for direct conservation impact rather than administrative costs. HOW IT RUNS: three rounds a year, March, June and October; the Fund forwards recommendations to an independent body, so its staff are not the final decision-makers; and late submissions are automatically moved to the next round — missing a deadline costs a cycle, not the application. Apply online in English; the form requires a budget, references and permits, so have your permissions in order before applying. READ THE PROJECTS DATABASE FIRST — searchable by species, IUCN classification, continent and year, it shows what has been funded for comparable species in comparable places. NOTE: THIS FUND IS GLOBAL, NOT REGIONAL — it is recorded here because this country holds no other funding entry, not because Gulf applicants receive any preference.

trackers.name: Kuwait Environment Protection Society — founded 1974, and its charter objectives name resource depletion by irresponsible actors
trackers.desc: READ ITS FOURTH CHARTER OBJECTIVE BEFORE YOU WRITE TO ANYONE ELSE IN KUWAIT: PROTECTING THE COUNTRY'S NATURAL WEALTH FROM DEPLETION CAUSED BY IRRESPONSIBLE PRACTICES BY SOME PARTIES. That is unusually direct language for a Gulf environmental charter — it names actors rather than abstract pollution — and it is the hook a resident should quote when asking KEPS to take an interest in a specific development. Its other stated objectives are protecting the Kuwaiti environment and combating causes of pollution across all fields while gathering and coordinating the efforts of those concerned; working to bring about scientific thinking, legal legislation and administrative regulation that secure environmental safety in Kuwait; and taking all possible preventive and remedial measures against pollution in its various forms. WHO TO CONTACT: info@keps.org.kw, telephone +965 24848256. Founded on 31 March 1974 in the wake of the 1972 Stockholm conference, which makes it one of the oldest environmental societies in the Gulf, and it is the BirdLife International partner for Kuwait — so it can route a bird or habitat question into an international partnership rather than handling it alone. WHAT IT IS NOT, AND THE LIST IS LONG: it does not litigate, does not buy or hold land, and runs no community grant window. Its coordinating and legislative objectives describe influence on rule-making rather than intervention in a particular permit. Kuwait's regulator is the separate, governmental Environment Public Authority, which houses the environmental impact assessment function and works alongside the environmental police — so the realistic sequence is to build the case with KEPS and file it at the Authority yourself. KEPS is nonetheless the only non-governmental body this search found in Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar or Saudi Arabia that a resident can simply join and approach.

trackers.name: Kuwait Dive Team — thirty years of seabed and reef condition data, and it is funded by the oil corporation
trackers.desc: WHAT THIS TEAM HOLDS IS THE BASELINE, AND FOR A COASTAL OR MARINE SCHEME THE BASELINE IS THE ARGUMENT. It monitors reef health in partnership with an Australian university, collecting data on coral colour, water temperature and reef condition, and shares it with international environmental research databases. If a marina, a landfill or a coastal development is proposed near Kuwaiti reefs, the record of what was there before already exists and is held outside the country as well as inside it — ask for it before commissioning a survey, and before the developer's own assessment sets the terms. IT ALSO HAS A PHYSICAL CAPABILITY ALMOST NO CAMPAIGN CAN CALL ON: it salvages sunken vessels and removes abandoned fishing gear, reporting more than nine hundred marine objects recovered across three decades, and in a single year sixteen boats and ships totalling 177 tonnes plus a hundred tonnes of discarded nets and debris, at a rate of roughly one operation every three days. Thirty to fifty active members, working from the Environmental Voluntary Foundation, with a named team leader and vice president; it also runs national beach cleanups with the ministries of social affairs and education drawing in Kuwaiti and expatriate volunteers alike. NOW THE PART THAT DECIDES HOW YOU USE THEM: this is not an oppositional body, and its funders make that plain. Its reported activities have been carried out with the cooperation of the Environment Public Authority and the Environmental Protection Fund and with support from Kuwait International Bank and the Kuwait International Petroleum Corporation. An organisation part-financed by the national petroleum corporation will not front a campaign against a coastal development, and expecting it to would waste everyone's time. Approach it for data, for documented condition of a specific site, and for the physical work of clearing what is already there — and take the objection to Kuwait Environment Protection Society, already in this file as the only joinable non-state body found across four Gulf states. TWO VERIFICATION NOTES: sources give two different founding dates, 1991 in the aftermath of the Iraqi invasion when volunteers began raising sunken vessels, and 1986 in one international listing — the 1991 account is the more widely and consistently reported. And the team's web presence sits on a domain whose name does not match the organisation, so confirm you have the right site before sending anything.

trackers.name: Rufford Small Grants — Kuwait is named eligible, which is unusual for a high-income Gulf state
trackers.desc: KUWAIT APPEARS BY NAME ON THE FOUNDATION'S OWN ELIGIBILITY PAGE, WHICH IS WORTH NOTING BECAUSE MOST CONSERVATION FUNDS EXCLUDE HIGH-INCOME GULF STATES ENTIRELY — this file has repeatedly found Gulf communities shut out of funding on income grounds. Applications come from individuals and small groups rather than requiring a registered organisation, and there are no deadlines: you may apply at any time of year. The focus is on people early in a conservation career, particularly current or recent MSc and PhD students, with others considered against the published criteria; undergraduates are not funded. THE ELIGIBILITY TEST FOR SPECIES WORK IS EXACT: any species not listed as Least Concern globally on the IUCN Red List qualifies, as do species not yet assessed but thought to be globally threatened. Look yours up before drafting. Habitat work, human-wildlife conflict and community education projects qualify without a species focus — which suits coastal, reef and desert habitat questions. THE STAGED STAIRCASE: up to £7,000 for a first grant, then a second, a Booster and a Completion Grant, reaching about £18,000, each conditional on completing and reporting the previous stage, with updates and final reports published on the applicant's own page. CONSTRAINTS: one application in any twelve months, twelve months' wait after rejection, the foundation covering half to all of the cost with evidence of co-funding required where others contribute, and no support for pure research without conservation benefit or for expeditions requiring self-fundraising. Pair with the marine baseline held by the dive team recorded here and with the country's environmental society — an application resting on thirty years of existing reef condition data is a stronger one.

trackers.name: Accountability Counsel — Kuwait is a named dark spot, and the complaint route runs through the lender not the courts
trackers.desc: KUWAIT IS NAMED AS AN ACCOUNTABILITY DARK SPOT IN THIS ORGANISATION'S RESEARCH — a country from which no community complaint has ever reached a development bank's accountability office. That matters most where domestic routes are closed: an accountability office sits inside the lending institution, operates independently of it and reports to its highest leadership, and can investigate compliance or convene dispute resolution without any national court being involved. THIS BODY REPRESENTS COMMUNITIES IN THAT PROCESS ON REQUEST, with support scaling from multi-year accompaniment down to a limited review of key documents, and it is expert in the mechanisms of the World Bank Group, regional development banks, export credit agencies and OECD National Contact Points. It partners with local lawyers so the international complaint and a domestic strategy run together. IT PUBLISHES A FREE DATABASE OF EVERY COMPLAINT EVER FILED TO EVERY ACCOUNTABILITY OFFICE — useful for finding how a comparable coastal, industrial or infrastructure project was challenged elsewhere. Founded 2009, working with communities in fifty countries. CHECK THE FINANCING BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE: whether an office exists depends on which institution is lending, and a wholly domestically financed project has no such route. Pair with the marine baseline held by the dive team recorded elsewhere in this file — a complaint supported by thirty years of independent reef condition data is a materially stronger one.

trackers.name: Inclusive Development International — it finds the lender behind a coastal or industrial scheme, which decides what routes exist
trackers.desc: WHETHER YOU HAVE A CASE AT ALL OFTEN DEPENDS ON WHO LENT THE MONEY, AND THIS IS THE BODY THAT FINDS OUT. It takes requests from community advocates to map the investment and supply chain behind a project, identifying banks, investors, insurers, development finance institutions and brands, working from financial databases, company reports, import data and shipping manifests. Shipping manifests and import data matter particularly for coastal and industrial projects, where equipment and materials arrive by sea and leave a documentary trail the developer does not control. IT RETURNS A SUMMARY WITH AN ANALYSIS OF PRESSURE POINTS AND ADVOCACY STRATEGIES, supports execution in high-potential cases, and refers others onward. Its free shareholder and development bank investment trackers allow the first stage to be done without cost or contact. READ IT WITH THE OTHER TWO KUWAITI ENTRIES IT COMPLETES: the accountability route recorded here has never once been used from this country, and the dive team's thirty-year reef dataset is the evidence such a complaint would rest on. Financier, forum, evidence — this supplies the first. THE LIMIT: its documented casework and requests come from Southeast Asia, Africa and the Americas; no work in Kuwait or this region could be established. Its service is described as open to community requests with no geographic bar stated, which makes this untested rather than unavailable.

trackers.name: KISR — it evidenced environmental damage to a standard that won a multi-billion compensation award
trackers.desc: THE MOST USEFUL FACT HERE IS ABOUT STANDARD OF PROOF. A scientist at this institute headed a national rehabilitation programme that resulted in an environmental compensation award to the state of nearly three billion dollars — which means environmental damage has been documented in this country to a standard that survived adjudication. What such a claim requires is a baseline, a damage assessment and a costed rehabilitation plan, and this institute has produced all three at national scale. A community arguing that harm is real and quantifiable is arguing something its own national institute has already proved. ITS DEPARTMENTS MAP ONTO WHAT LAND DISPUTES ACTUALLY TURN ON: coastal and air pollution; environmental pollution and climate; an air quality programme; biodiversity of terrestrial ecosystems; ecosystem-based management of marine resources; oceanography, mariculture and fisheries; a water research centre; and a national seismic network. Its published work includes a decade of atmospheric radiological monitoring assessed for risk, and studies of hydrocarbon-degrading bacteria isolated from contaminated Kuwaiti oil — contamination science with a decade-long series behind it. ITS WIDER RECORD COVERS INVENTORIES OF NATURAL RESOURCES, RESTORATION OF ARID ECOSYSTEMS, WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT AND SUSTAINABLE LAND-USE PLANNING, which is the desert equivalent of the coastal baselines recorded for other Gulf states in this file. It is building a national oceanography and marine resources unit with thirty-four laboratories, whose stated objects include monitoring environmental and coastal parameters and forecasting impacts and remedies. Its research output is browsable through a national science foundation portal, so a named researcher can be identified before writing to anyone. NOW THE WARNING, AND IT IS SHARPER HERE THAN FOR THE OTHER RESEARCH BODIES IN THIS FILE: ITS PUBLISHED SERVICE LIST INCLUDES ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT AND SOCIAL ASSESSMENT. This institute may have written the assessment for the very scheme being contested. Establish that before approaching it, and treat its published data as the asset rather than its advice. ITS OWN DIRECTOR HAS DESCRIBED IT AS A PARTIALLY INDEPENDENT GOVERNMENT RESEARCH INSTITUTE with over a thousand staff — an honest description a reader should take at face value in both directions: not a ministry, and not independent either.

trackers.name: Kuwait Bar Association Legal Aid Centre — free representation, with an office in every court
trackers.desc: THERE IS AN OFFICE FOR LEGAL AID IN EACH COURT. That is the sentence that matters, and this file has found nothing like it anywhere else in the Gulf — every other legal route recorded for the six Gulf states is a foreign organisation reached by email. The association operates a legal aid centre established under the law governing the legal profession and running SINCE 1963, providing pro bono services, legal consultations and REPRESENTATION to people who cannot afford to pay privately, with the stated aim of ensuring equal access to justice. IT IS NOT A SMALL BODY AND ITS REACH IS TOTAL: registration as a lawyer in Kuwait is compulsory, so the association covers the entire profession — some five to six thousand active members — and it describes itself as providing services directly to the community rather than only to its own members. SET YOUR EXPECTATIONS HONESTLY, THOUGH: an international survey of pro bono practice records that pro bono work in Kuwait is NOT AS WIDESPREAD OR INSTITUTIONALISED as in many western jurisdictions, while noting that practices are in place so that those without means can access legal services. Treat the court offices as the point of first contact rather than assuming a case will be taken. AND FRAME THE MATTER CORRECTLY WHEN YOU ARRIVE. This is a general legal aid service, not an environmental or planning one, and nothing found shows it acting on a development scheme. A land dispute presented as an environmental complaint is unlikely to fit; the same dispute presented as a property, compensation, permit or administrative matter is an ordinary piece of legal work. This file has recorded the same reframing succeeding in Georgia, where the free lawyers available take private property cases rather than environmental ones. USE IT WITH THE OTHER KUWAITI ENTRIES: the national research institute for the evidence, the volunteer dive team and the environment protection society for the subject, and the international accountability and investment-chain organisations where a foreign lender or company is involved. ADDRESS WARNING: no website could be reached for the association despite repeated searching, although its own posts refer to a website and an app through which services including certificates and registrations are provided electronically. This entry points at its own public account; confirm the current address and the location of the legal aid office in your court before relying on it.

trackers.name: Kuwaiti Union of Fishermen — an elected public benefit association that ministries answer
trackers.desc: IT IS ELECTED, WHICH MEANS IT CAN BE JOINED AND ITS LEADERSHIP CHANGED. Its president and NINE BOARD MEMBERS ARE CHOSEN BY ITS GENERAL ASSEMBLY EVERY THREE YEARS under ministry supervision, and a recent election was genuinely contested — one list took all nine seats, with observers present. No state agency, university centre or foreign fund recorded for this country can be joined or redirected by the people affected. This one can. IT IS A CONSTITUTED BODY, NOT AN INFORMAL GROUP: a PUBLIC BENEFIT ASSOCIATION declared by the social affairs ministry under a numbered licence in 1980, operating under a BASIC STATUTE that its own president cited publicly when accused of acting arbitrarily — saying decisions are taken according to that statute. Obtain the statute: it defines who may be a member, how the general assembly is convened, and how a member forces an item onto the agenda. That is the mechanism by which a fishing community turns a local grievance into a decision of a body ministries deal with. AND MINISTRIES DO DEAL WITH IT. Representatives of its board met the LEADERSHIP OF THE PUBLIC AUTHORITY FOR AGRICULTURE to press the union's demands on opening a fishing season, and after it issued a statement on the division of quotas following the fish auction, AN ASSISTANT UNDERSECRETARY OF THE COMMERCE MINISTRY WAS NAMED IN THE PUBLIC RESPONSE. A body whose statements draw named replies from ministry officials is a body worth having on your side. KNOW ITS POSTURE FROM ITS OWN WORDS: its president has said the union does not work alone but as an integrated system working with the relevant authorities, and it frames its purpose around contributing to the country's FOOD SECURITY. That is a cooperative posture, not an adversarial one — so an argument that a coastal scheme threatens the national fish supply and the livelihoods behind it will travel further through this body than an argument about habitat. THE LIMITS: it works within fisheries and food policy, is supervised by a ministry, and nothing found shows it opposing a development project. Its address here is its own public account rather than a website. Use it to organise the affected fishermen, to reach ministries with a collective voice, and to put a number of livelihoods behind an objection; take the objection itself to the legal aid centre and the international accountability routes recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: The waqf funds — this country once ran one for the environment, and the endower sets the terms
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY HAD NO ROUTE IN THIS MAP FOR HOLDING OR DEDICATING LAND. AN ENDOWMENT IS ONE, AND HERE IT IS NOT A THEORY: a general system for WAQF FUNDS was approved by the waqf affairs council on 11 October 1994, creating TEN SELF-MANAGED FUNDS financed from the revenue of endowments assigned to each — AND ONE OF THEM WAS THE WAQF FUND FOR THE CONSERVATION OF THE ENVIRONMENT. The funds were merged and reduced to four by ministerial decision in 2001, so the environmental fund no longer stands alone. But the precedent is domestic and documented: this state has already constituted an endowment fund for the environment once. THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST TO ANYONE CONSIDERING IT: THE ADMINISTRATION MUST DISBURSE ENDOWMENT REVENUE WITHIN THE CONDITIONS SET BY THE ENDOWER. That is what separates an endowment from a donation — the endower writes the purpose, and it binds afterwards. A family, a business or a landowner who wants a stretch of coast, a stand of trees or a water source kept for a stated purpose can write that purpose into the endowment deed, and it outlives them. AND THE PROCEDURE IS NOT ARCHAIC: the national portal carries an ONLINE WAQF SERVICE through which an endowment can be created over the internet. THE INSTITUTION BEHIND IT: a public foundation established in 1993 whose remit is CALLING FOR ENDOWMENT and doing everything relating to its affairs — managing and investing endowment assets and spending their revenue within the endower's conditions, to serve the purposes of the endowment and develop society. Endowment here is old and continuous: the first documented endowment in this country dates from 1695, a dedicated ministry was created in 1962, and this foundation in 1993. HOW A COMMUNITY WOULD USE IT, GIVEN ITS LIMITS: it cannot endow land it does not own, so this is a route for a landowner sympathetic to the community, or for endowing MONEY whose revenue funds a stated environmental purpose rather than endowing the land itself. The second is often the achievable version: a modest permanent fund, its purpose written by the donor, producing income for a specific place — which is the standing local fund this file recorded elsewhere as the most durable answer to paying for land defence. THE LIMITS, PLAINLY: this is a state foundation, not an independent body, and the asset passes into its administration; the dedicated environmental fund was merged away in 2001 and no successor fund devoted solely to the environment was found; and nothing establishes that a community here has used an endowment for conservation. Ask the foundation what conditions it will accept, and cite the 1994 environmental fund when you do.

trackers.name: The area cooperatives — your neighbourhood already has an elected body with money and premises
trackers.desc: THE HARDEST THING FOR A COMMUNITY IN THIS REGION IS BECOMING A LEGAL BODY. IN THIS COUNTRY EVERY RESIDENTIAL AREA ALREADY HAS ONE. Around sixty cooperative societies exist, one established in EACH AREA to provide services to its residents, and THE RESIDENTS OF THAT AREA ELECT ITS BOARD EVERY YEAR. This file has recorded across twenty-three countries that the absence of a registered entity is what stops communities from holding land, receiving money or being heard — and separately that a cooperative is the vehicle through which a community does hold land. HERE THE VEHICLE IS ALREADY CONSTITUTED, ALREADY FUNDED AND ALREADY ELECTED, IN EVERY NEIGHBOURHOOD. WHAT THAT GIVES YOU IS UNUSUAL: LEGAL PERSONALITY, PREMISES, A MEMBERSHIP ROLL OF LOCAL RESIDENTS, ANNUAL ELECTIONS, AND REAL REVENUE — the societies run stores and rent space to private operators, and together account for something like sixty to seventy per cent of retail trade in the country. An organisation with its own income is one this payload has repeatedly found outlasts those living grant to grant. AND THE ELECTION IS THE LEVER. A board chosen annually by the residents of the very area a scheme would affect is answerable to those residents in a way no ministry or foreign body is. A community facing a project can put the question to its own cooperative's general assembly, stand candidates, or ask the board to write, to fund a study, or to host a meeting — none of which requires forming anything new or registering anything. THERE IS ALSO AN APEX BODY: a union of the consumer cooperative societies, which is the route to raising a matter beyond one area and to reaching societies in neighbouring districts affected by the same scheme. THE LIMITS, AND THEY ARE REAL. THEIR PURPOSE IS CONSUMER SERVICES AND RETAIL, NOT LAND DEFENCE — nothing found shows a cooperative here opposing a development, and a board will reasonably ask why this is its business. They are supervised by the ministry responsible for social affairs, and their elections are contested on local and political lines, so a board may be unwilling to take a contentious position. And a cooperative that trades with contractors and landlords has commercial relationships of its own. Approach it as a membership organisation you already belong to rather than as an ally: the argument has to be won inside it, which is a different and often easier task than building a body from nothing.

trackers.name: Water Resources Division at the national research institute — a named director, a telephone and an email
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY HAS THE FEWEST RECORDED RESOURCES OF ANY NON-RESTRICTED STATE IN THIS FILE, AND ITS ENTRIES ARE MOSTLY BODIES YOU CANNOT REACH. HERE IS A NAMED DIRECTOR OF THE WATER RESOURCES DIVISION AT THE NATIONAL SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH INSTITUTE, PUBLISHED WITH A POSTAL ADDRESS, A DIRECT TELEPHONE NUMBER AND TWO EMAIL ADDRESSES — his own and the national commission's. He is listed as this country's focal point for the international hydrological programme. AND THE INSTITUTE ITSELF CARRIES INTERNATIONAL STANDING: ITS WATER RESEARCH CENTRE WAS APPROVED AS A WATER CENTRE UNDER UNESCO AUSPICES, one of a small network of such centres worldwide. That matters for two reasons. It means the institute's water work is recognised beyond the country, so its findings travel. And it means the centre has obligations to an international programme as well as to domestic clients. WHAT THIS IS USEFUL FOR. Disputes in this country turn on GROUNDWATER, on coastal reclamation, and on industrial discharge — and the national research institute is where the country's water data and analytical capacity actually sit. A community that needs to know what an aquifer is doing, what a discharge contains, or whether a project's water assumptions are sound is asking a question this division exists to answer. ASK FOR PUBLISHED WORK FIRST. A research institute will send you what it has already published far more readily than it will undertake new analysis, and a published national study is more useful in an objection than a private opinion — it is already citable, already reviewed, and already the state's own science. THE LIMITS, PLAINLY. IT IS A NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE SERVING GOVERNMENT AND INDUSTRY, not a public advice service and not independent of the administration; the contact is a programme focal point rather than an enquiries desk. A technical question about a place will be received; a request to oppose a project will not. Use it with the environment society's monitoring and complaints team and the elected area cooperatives recorded separately for this country — the institute supplies the science, the society carries the complaint, and the cooperative is the body that already represents your neighbourhood.

trackers.name: University centre for Gulf studies — the named archaeologist, and the missions already in the field
trackers.desc: ARCHAEOLOGICAL SIGNIFICANCE IS ONE OF THE VERY FEW GROUNDS THAT HALTS CONSTRUCTION, AND THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING IN THIS MAP CONTAINED NOTHING ON HERITAGE AT ALL. The national university's CENTRE FOR GULF AND ARABIAN PENINSULA STUDIES runs scientific lectures, and in October 2025 it hosted one on RECENT ARCHAEOLOGICAL DISCOVERIES IN THIS COUNTRY. IT WAS GIVEN BY A NAMED ACADEMIC — AN ASSISTANT PROFESSOR SPECIALISING IN ARCHAEOLOGY AND ANTHROPOLOGY, WHOSE RESEARCH INTERESTS INCLUDE CULTURAL HERITAGE AND THE ARCHAEOLOGY OF THE ARABIAN GULF — who set out the latest findings of the archaeological missions working here, with material evidence of the depth of the land's history. Two things follow, and both are practical. FIRST, ARCHAEOLOGICAL MISSIONS ARE ACTIVELY IN THE FIELD IN THIS COUNTRY. That means SURVEY DATA EXISTS — excavation reports, site records, find distributions — and the first question about any threatened ground is whether a mission has already recorded it. That question is free to ask and answers a great deal. SECOND, THERE IS A NAMED SPECIALIST WHO CAN SAY WHETHER A PARTICULAR PIECE OF GROUND IS LIKELY TO HOLD ANYTHING. This file established a round earlier that identifying the right department and the right author is the step that must precede any request for analysis; here the department is a university sociology department and the specialism is archaeology and anthropology. HOW TO APPROACH: write to the centre or the department about a specific place, not about a project. Ask whether the area has been surveyed, whether any mission has worked nearby, what period the surrounding finds belong to, and what would be visible on the surface if something were there. An academic answers a question about a landscape; they will not answer a request to oppose a development. AND ATTEND THE LECTURES. A centre that runs a public scientific programme is a place where the people who know the ground can be met in person, which is worth more than correspondence in a country where this file has found very few reachable bodies of any kind. THE LIMITS: it is a research centre inside a state university, not a protection body — designation and antiquities decisions rest elsewhere, and academics identify and publish rather than object. Access may need an appointment, and a single named specialist is a thin thread — ask the department who else works on the subject. Use it with the environment society's monitoring and complaints team and the elected area cooperatives recorded separately for this country: the archaeology establishes what is there, and those two carry it.

trackers.name: Municipality practice-of-profession committee — who may practise, and the conflict declaration they sign
trackers.desc: THE MOST USEFUL THING HERE IS A DECLARATION EVERY REGISTERED OFFICE ENGINEER MUST SIGN: THAT THEY ARE FULL-TIME AT THE ENGINEERING OFFICE AND THAT THEY DO NOT TRADE IN CONSTRUCTION MATERIALS OR PARTICIPATE IN ANY CONSTRUCTION CONTRACTING COMPANY. A community facing a scheme can ask a single question with that in hand: DOES THE ENGINEER ON THIS PROJECT HAVE CONTRACTING OR MATERIALS INTERESTS? If they do, the declaration on which their registration rests is breached, and the body that registered them is the body to tell. AND THAT BODY IS NOT THE ENGINEERS' SOCIETY — IT IS THE MUNICIPALITY. A PRACTICE OF THE PROFESSION COMMITTEE examines the application and THE MUNICIPAL COUNCIL ISSUES THE DECISION approving an engineer's registration to an engineering office. This file established elsewhere that municipal councils in this region are ELECTED BODIES; here an elected council decides who may practise engineering in the country. That makes the register a matter an elected member can be asked about. THE SOCIETY IS STILL A GATEKEEPER: proof of WORKING OR AFFILIATE MEMBERSHIP OF THE ENGINEERS' SOCIETY is among the required documents, alongside a certified degree and WORK CERTIFICATES SHOWING AT LEAST FIVE YEARS OF PRACTICE SINCE GRADUATION, a civil identity card, and an undertaking to comply with a numbered article of the profession-practice system for engineering offices. Ask which of these an engineer actually holds. THERE IS A SECOND REGISTER TOO. Other authorities, when approving an engineer for their own works, require BOTH the municipality's practice-of-profession letter AND a certificate of registration with the UNION OF KUWAITI ENGINEERING OFFICES AND CONSULTANCY HOUSES, plus a social-insurance letter confirming the engineer is full-time at that office. AN ENGINEER APPEARING ON A PROJECT SHOULD THEREFORE BE TRACEABLE THROUGH THREE SEPARATE RECORDS — municipality, society, union — and inconsistency between them is itself a finding. THE MUNICIPALITY PUBLISHES ITS REQUIREMENTS AND ITS ADDRESS: a named building, street and floor. THE LIMITS: this is a licensing counter, not a service for residents — it registers engineers, it does not investigate projects on request, and the R26 audit generally bars state bodies from this file. It will confirm whether a person is registered and will receive information bearing on that registration; it will not take a position on a development. Use it with the environment society's monitoring and complaints team and the elected area cooperatives recorded separately here.

trackers.name: Law school legal studies centre — where a society or cooperative can commission a written opinion
trackers.desc: START WITH WHAT WAS LOOKED FOR AND NOT FOUND: THIS COUNTRY APPEARS TO HAVE NO FREE PUBLIC LEGAL CLINIC. Both law faculties name community service among their aims, and neither publishes a walk-in advice service — unlike three neighbouring states where university law clinics are recorded in this file. Do not spend weeks looking for one. WHAT EXISTS INSTEAD IS A LEGAL STUDIES AND RESEARCH CENTRE ATTACHED TO A LAW SCHOOL, DESCRIBED AS AN ACADEMIC, TRAINING AND CONSULTATIVE INSTITUTION, WHICH PROVIDES STUDIES, RESEARCH, WRITTEN LEGAL OPINIONS AND CONSULTATIONS TO BODIES AND COMPANIES. THAT PHRASE — TO BODIES — IS THE OPENING, BECAUSE A CONSTITUTED COMMUNITY BODY IS A BODY. The elected area cooperatives recorded separately for this country, a licensed society, a professional association: each is an entity that can commission work in its own name, where an individual resident cannot. This file has said in country after country that the thing communities cannot obtain is A WRITTEN EXPERT OPINION on whether a scheme is lawful, and this is the nearest thing this country offers. THE CENTRE ALSO STATES A RESPONSIBILITY TOWARDS SOCIETY AND A COMMITMENT TO SERVING ITS INTERESTS AND ITS PEOPLE through professional partnership — which is the sentence to quote when a cooperative asks whether a study can be done for a neighbourhood rather than for a company. It draws on the school's faculty of MORE THAN EIGHTY-SIX MEMBERS OF VARIOUS NATIONALITIES, so specialist coverage is wide. WHAT TO ASK FOR, PRECISELY: not advice, but A WRITTEN STUDY OR LEGAL OPINION on a defined question — whether a permit complied with the applicable law, what the procedure required, what an authority was obliged to publish. A defined question is answerable and quotable; a request to help oppose a project is neither. THE LIMITS. IT IS A CONSULTANCY, SO EXPECT TO PAY, and its stated clients are institutions and companies rather than households. It is attached to a private law school. It produces opinions and studies, NOT REPRESENTATION — for a lawyer, this file records the bar's legal aid centre separately for this country. And nothing found shows it acting for a community against a development, so approach it as a client commissioning research, which is what it is.

trackers.name: Species conservation grants — an individual can apply, and unlisted species count
trackers.desc: TWO FEATURES MAKE THIS USABLE IN A COUNTRY WHERE ALMOST NO FUNDING IS. FIRST, AN INDIVIDUAL MAY APPLY — you do not need a registered organisation, which this file has identified as the single commonest barrier across twenty-three countries. SECOND, ELIGIBILITY EXTENDS TO ALL PLANT, ANIMAL AND FUNGI CONSERVATION WITHOUT DISCRIMINATION BASED ON REGION OR SPECIES, so a high-income Gulf state is not excluded. AND HERE IS THE OPENING MOST PEOPLE MISS. The fund is aimed at critically endangered and endangered species — BUT ALSO AT DATA DEFICIENT ONES, AND AT SPECIES NOT LISTED AT ALL BUT SUSPECTED OF BEING HIGHLY THREATENED. A creature nobody has assessed on ground nobody has surveyed is not outside this fund; it is close to the centre of it. That matters on a coastline or a patch of desert facing development, where the honest position is that nobody knows what is there. THE HARD LIMIT ON MONEY: THE MAXIMUM GRANT IS TWENTY-FIVE THOUSAND DOLLARS, AND AN APPLICATION ASKING FOR MORE WILL BE REJECTED. The project's total budget may be larger if others are contributing — so ask this fund for its share and show the rest. WHAT IT WILL NOT PAY FOR: WORK THAT IS PRIMARILY LABORATORY-BASED. It wants field conservation. It may, however, cover salary or travel costs for a specific project, usually for support staff. THE MECHANICS, WHICH DECIDE WHETHER AN APPLICATION SURVIVES AT ALL: apply for ONE SPECIES — multi-species proposals are considered but you must name a PRIMARY SPECIES; submit ONLY through the online system, IN ENGLISH, WITH BUDGETS IN US DOLLARS; and note that CONTINUATION FUNDING REQUIRES A FRESH APPLICATION and your reporting on the first project will be weighed. THE DEADLINES ARE INFLEXIBLE AND TIMED TO GMT. In 2026 one round ran through 31 May; the next opened 15 September and closes 15 OCTOBER 2026, with decisions expected late December. A LATE APPLICATION IS NOT REFUSED — IT AUTOMATICALLY ROLLS INTO THE FOLLOWING ROUND, which costs months. BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE ODDS AND APPLY ANYWAY: the fund distributes roughly five hundred thousand dollars per round across eight taxonomic groups against fifteen hundred to eighteen hundred applications a year. Since 2009 it has put over twenty-seven million dollars into 2,894 projects covering 1,789 species in more than 150 countries. Use it with the university archaeology specialist and the environment society's documentation and flora teams recorded separately for this country — a species record made with them is the evidence an application needs.

trackers.name: Kuwait Foundation for the Advancement of Sciences — a domestic funder whose money comes from company profits, not the budget
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING CONTAINED ONLY FOREIGN GRANT WINDOWS. HERE IS A DOMESTIC FUNDER, AND ITS FUNDING MODEL IS THE REASON IT LASTS: it is a PRIVATE NON-PROFIT FOUNDATION, established by decree in 1976, FINANCED BY PRIVATE-SECTOR SHAREHOLDING COMPANIES WHICH PLEDGE A SET PERCENTAGE OF THEIR ANNUAL PROFITS — CURRENTLY ONE PER CENT. Its money therefore does not rise and fall with a ministry's budget, and it has been running for more than forty-five years. AND IT NAMES CIVIL SOCIETY AS AN AUDIENCE. Its offerings are organised by who you are, and one of those groups is THE PUBLIC SECTOR OR CIVIL SOCIETY WORKER, with a sponsorship and funding section and a published introduction to its grants. That is not a research-only door: a licensed society or association is being addressed directly. WHAT IT SUPPORTS AND HOW TO FRAME A REQUEST: its stated purpose is harnessing science, technology and innovation to address NATIONAL CHALLENGES, and its current strategy rests on a research ecosystem, applicable innovation and human creativity. A COMMUNITY PROPOSAL THAT IS FRAMED AS MEASUREMENT, MONITORING OR APPLIED PROBLEM-SOLVING FITS THAT LANGUAGE; ONE FRAMED AS A CAMPAIGN DOES NOT. Coastal survey work, water or soil monitoring, species recording, a study of what a scheme will do — these are the shapes to propose. IT ALSO RUNS PRIZES AND RESEARCH GRANTS, so a group working with a university department already recorded in this listing can enter through the researcher rather than through the society — and this file has recorded a law school research centre and a university archaeology specialist for this country who could be that partner. THE LIMITS: it is a science and technology funder, not an environmental or legal one, and nothing found shows it funding advocacy or opposition to a project. Its published pages describe programmes rather than open calls with deadlines, so THE FIRST STEP IS TO ASK WHAT IS CURRENTLY OPEN AND ON WHAT TIMETABLE. And a proposal will need a credible technical partner.

trackers.name: State agricultural nurseries — two open seasons a year, a million seedlings, and volunteer campaigns are a named recipient
trackers.desc: THE AGRICULTURE AUTHORITY'S OWN NURSERIES DISTRIBUTE AND SELL TREE, SHRUB AND PLANT SEEDLINGS TO THE PUBLIC — AND THE NURSERY STATES THAT IT DELIBERATELY RESERVES STOCK FOR NATIONAL OCCASIONS, SCHOOL OPENINGS AND VOLUNTEER CAMPAIGNS, in order to distribute the largest possible number. A VOLUNTEER CAMPAIGN IS A NAMED CATEGORY OF RECIPIENT HERE, which means a community planting effort is not asking for an exception. THE TIMING DECIDES EVERYTHING AND ALMOST NOBODY KNOWS IT: DISTRIBUTION RUNS FOR THREE MONTHS FROM OCTOBER TO DECEMBER; THE NURSERY THEN CLOSES TO RAISE THE SUMMER STOCK UNTIL MARCH; AND OPENS AGAIN FROM THE FIRST OF MARCH TO THE END OF MAY. There are two windows a year and no more. Ask in September for the winter window and in February for the spring one — arriving in July means waiting. THE SCALE IS REAL: 650,000 SEEDLINGS OF EIGHTY VARIETIES PREPARED AT THE START OF ONE SEASON, BEING RAISED TOWARD A MILLION BEFORE IT ENDED. And the quality point matters more than the quantity: SEVENTY-FIVE PER CENT OF WHAT IS DISTRIBUTED IS LOCALLY PRODUCED, and staff have succeeded in growing EIGHTY-THREE PLANT TYPES ADAPTED TO THIS COUNTRY'S ENVIRONMENT — with the species people actually ask for being those suited to extreme heat, including sidr, willow and eucalyptus. THE DETAIL THAT PREVENTS THE COMMONEST FAILURE: PLANTS ARE FULLY ACCLIMATISED AND PREPARED FOR PLANTING BEFORE THEY LEAVE, AND INSTRUCTIONS ON HOW TO PLANT THEM ARE GIVEN TO EVERY RECIPIENT. This file has recorded planting schemes across the region that died because stock went straight from a shaded nursery into open ground in summer. ASK FOR THE INSTRUCTIONS AND FOLLOW THEM; they are free and they are the difference between a wood and a row of dead sticks. THE NURSERY ALSO SUPPLIES THE NATIONAL AFFORESTATION CAMPAIGN WITH THE SEEDLINGS IT NEEDS, so a group can either take stock directly or ask to be planted under that campaign — the second route brings the authority's own labour and publicity with it. Further nurseries under the same sector operate in two agricultural areas, with more under study in the south, so ask which is nearest before travelling to the main one. THE LIMITS: THIS IS DISTRIBUTION AND SALE, NOT A FREE GIVEAWAY — the nursery records daily sales revenue, so budget for stock even if it is cheap. It is a government authority and will not plant against a scheme the state supports. And the same authority is currently WITHDRAWING AND CANCELLING AGRICULTURAL HOLDINGS FOUND IN BREACH under a 2026 ministerial decision, so anyone using agricultural land here should confirm their own holding is in order before drawing attention to it. This entry rests on national press reporting; confirm current seasons and prices with the nursery directly.

trackers.name: Regional defenders' centre — the body to have contacted before anyone is detained, covering this country by name
trackers.desc: THIS FILE RECORDS FOR THIS COUNTRY A BAR LEGAL AID CENTRE, A UNIVERSITY LAW CENTRE AND A COMPLAINTS ROUTE — AND NOTHING ABOUT PROTECTION FOR THE PEOPLE WHO SPEAK. THIS ORGANISATION NAMES THIS COUNTRY AMONG THE ELEVEN IT COVERS, AND ITS EMERGENCY ASSISTANCE RUNS TO MEDICAL SUPPORT, TRAINING, SECURITY, TRIAL OBSERVATION AND EVACUATION. THE ORDER IN WHICH TO USE IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE LIST. THE TIME TO MAKE CONTACT IS BEFORE ANYTHING HAPPENS — when a group is forming, when it first publishes something, when the first summons or warning arrives. An organisation that already knows who you are can act in hours; one hearing of you for the first time after an arrest is starting from nothing. IT SUPPORTS INDEPENDENT LAWYERS ALONGSIDE JOURNALISTS, ACADEMICS AND ONLINE ACTIVISTS. In a country where this file has struggled to find any public-interest legal capacity, that is worth knowing in both directions: the lawyer taking your case can themselves be supported, and a lawyer who knows that may be readier to act. IT PROVIDES CAPACITY-BUILDING GRANTS TO CIVIL SOCIETY PARTNERS AND EMERGENCY GRANTS TO DEFENDERS AT RISK, and works with United Nations and European protection mechanisms including a defenders' protection consortium and A TEMPORARY RELOCATION PROGRAMME. It also trains people to MANAGE THEIR OWN SECURITY, which is the part that is useful even when nothing has gone wrong. AND IT PUBLISHES IN ENGLISH AND ARABIC, carries out advocacy at the United Nations, and links people to international media and organisations — the bridge out, for a case that would otherwise stay local and unheard. THE LIMITS: ITS FRAME IS HUMAN RIGHTS, NOT LAND. A dispute reaches it through detention, prosecution, threats or silencing, not through planning. It is based outside the country and works publicly, so approaching it is a deliberate step with consequences both ways; ask what it can do quietly first. Read it with the digital and legal entries recorded separately here.

trackers.name: Volunteer dive team — it answers environmental reports, patrols the sea, and pulls wildlife out of industrial intakes
trackers.desc: AFTER SEVERAL ROUNDS OF FUNDS, REGISTRIES AND REGULATORS, THIS IS A BODY THAT TURNS UP AND DOES SOMETHING — AND THE MOST USEFUL FACT ABOUT IT IS THAT IT RESPONDS TO ENVIRONMENTAL REPORTS FROM THE PUBLIC. In June 2026 it acted immediately on a report at a named coast, clearing the beach of large quantities of dead small fish BEFORE decomposition set in, which protected both beach users and the shoreline's ecology. A COMMUNITY THAT SEES SOMETHING WRONG ON THE COAST HAS SOMEONE TO CALL WHO WILL COME. WHAT ITS DIVERS ACTUALLY DO IS PHYSICAL AND SPECIFIC: THEY REMOVE ENTANGLED FISHING NETS, HEAVY PLASTIC WASTE, TIMBER AND ABANDONED ROPES that obstruct boats and threaten marine life; THEY RAISE SUNKEN BOATS AND WRECKAGE; THEY CLEAR WASTE AND DESTRUCTIVE NETS FROM CORAL REEFS; and they run FIELD SEA PATROLS MONITORING THE GENERAL STATE OF MARINE LIFE. THAT LAST ONE IS THE UNDERRATED SERVICE. A VOLUNTEER TEAM THAT PATROLS AND RECORDS THE STATE OF THE SEA IS PRODUCING EXACTLY THE BASELINE THIS FILE KEEPS TELLING COMMUNITIES THEY NEED — evidence of what a coast held BEFORE a project was proposed. Ask them what they have recorded about your stretch of water; the record may already exist. THEIR WILDLIFE WORK POINTS STRAIGHT AT INDUSTRY. They free turtles trapped in ABANDONED GHOST NETS, and they EXTRACT TURTLES THAT STRAY INTO THE WATER-INTAKE CHANNELS OF FACTORIES, POWER STATIONS AND DESALINATION PLANTS, returning them to the sea. A TEAM THAT ROUTINELY PULLS PROTECTED ANIMALS OUT OF INDUSTRIAL INTAKES KNOWS WHICH INSTALLATIONS KILL WILDLIFE AND HOW OFTEN — that is operational knowledge no assessment report will contain. THEY ALSO WORK INSIDE PROTECTED AREAS ALONGSIDE THE STATE: in January 2026 they ran a campaign to clean and REHABILITATE THE BAY with the administration of a nature reserve under the environment authority, lifting abandoned nets and plastics from the reserve's shores and tonnes of waste from named coasts — and they clean two islands that are turtle nesting sites. THE ORGANISATION ITSELF IS INSTRUCTIVE: it began after the occupation with TWENTY-FIVE VOLUNTEERS clearing war debris from the sea, and grew as qualified divers holding INTERNATIONAL LICENCES joined. Its work is now funded partly through a bank partnership renewed for a FOURTH CONSECUTIVE YEAR — evidence that corporate sponsorship of practical environmental work is obtainable and renewable in this country, which is worth knowing for any group seeking money. THE LIMITS: it is a volunteer environmental team, NOT A CAMPAIGNING OR LEGAL BODY — it cleans, rescues, monitors and educates, and works cooperatively with government agencies rather than against them; nothing found shows it opposing a development. Its remit is marine and coastal only. AND FOUNDING ACCOUNTS DIFFER BETWEEN 1986 AND 1991 IN PUBLISHED SOURCES, which is noted rather than resolved. This entry rests on national press reporting; confirm current contacts before relying on it.

trackers.name: Constitutional Chamber (Kyrgyzstan)
trackers.desc: Official site of the Constitutional Chamber of the Supreme Court, publishing constitutional-review decisions. · Find here: the decisions of the Constitutional Chamber of the Supreme Court of Kyrgyzstan.

trackers.name: Accounts Chamber
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Kyrgyzstan, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Kloop
trackers.desc: Kyrgyz investigative outlet exposing corruption and official wrongdoing.

trackers.name: Kyrgyzstan — Ministry of Economy & Finance
trackers.desc: National budget authority; oversees public finances and prepares & executes the State budget, Kyrgyz Republic. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Kyrgyzstan.

trackers.name: Kyrgyzstan — State Registration Service (Ministry of Justice)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the SRS under the Ministry of Justice maintains the Unified State Register of Legal Entities with a free public online company search (by name or INN), Kyrgyz Republic. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Local self-government can withdraw land from economic use — since 2018
trackers.desc: THE SHORTEST DESIGNATION ROUTE IN CENTRAL ASIA, AND IT IS RECENT. Law No. 58 of 2 June 2018 added a definition of protected natural territories of local significance: plots of land, water surface and airspace above them holding natural complexes of special conservation, scientific, cultural, recreational or health value, withdrawn wholly or partly from economic use by decision of local self-government bodies. So the ayil okmotu or municipal council can withdraw land from economic use — not the Cabinet, not the ministry. It dates only from 2018, so older guidance will not mention it. The same amendment defined wetlands to include shallows and excessively moistened areas where the water table is usually at or near the surface — a seasonal wet meadow can qualify; it need not be open water. FOR A VERY SMALL SITE ASK FOR A МИКРОЗАПОВЕДНИК (micro-reserve), a named category alongside local-significance territories, biosphere reserves and transboundary areas — the right frame for a single spring, grove or nesting area. The power to establish is expressly shared between the Government, executive bodies and local self-government. Governing statute: the Law on Specially Protected Natural Territories of 3 May 2011 No. 18, succeeding that of 28 May 1994.

trackers.name: There is no operative cadastre — keep the establishing decision yourself
trackers.desc: DO NOT ASSUME AN OFFICIAL REGISTER WILL PROVE YOUR SITE'S STATUS. An Aarhus Centre legal review records that in March 2021 a draft resolution approving the procedure for maintaining the state cadastre of protected natural territories was put out for public discussion — but has not been approved, and is not in the country's normative legal base. So there is no operative procedure for the state cadastre of protected areas: obtain and keep the establishing decision itself, because it may be the only durable proof. The same review examined 110 active normative legal acts making up Kyrgyz environmental law, and was produced under a project aimed at expanding public participation in decision-making and building civil society capacity — the Aarhus Centre Kyrgyzstan is the body to approach on participation rights. A DEFINITIONAL POINT WORTH USING: protected territories may be natural or artificially created complexes, so a restored or planted site is not excluded by definition — useful where the argument is rehabilitation rather than pristineness.

trackers.name: CAREC — two organisations share the name, neither is a grant fund
trackers.desc: ‘CAREC’ IS TWO DIFFERENT ORGANISATIONS AND YOU WILL PROBABLY APPROACH THE WRONG ONE. The Regional Environmental Centre for Central Asia (carecnet.org / carececo.org) was established following the 4th Pan-European Conference in Aarhus, 1998, operating since 2001 as an independent, non-commercial and non-partisan organisation of international character. Its founders are Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan plus UNDP and the European Commission; headquarters in Almaty, with country offices in all five member states (the Kyrgyz office is at 142 Gorky str., office 410, Bishkek 720005). The unrelated Central Asia Regional Economic Cooperation (CAREC) Program is an Asian Development Bank programme founded 1997, based in Manila, with 11 members including Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, China and Pakistan. NEITHER IS A COMMUNITY GRANT FUND. The Environmental Centre offers a dialogue platform for environmental NGOs and representation at international forums and thematic networks, and collaborates with NGOs, government and business — a route to partnership, visibility and project consortia, not an application window. The ADB programme's Climate and Sustainability Project Preparatory Fund (US$3m from Korea, US$2m from China) supports preparation of bankable regional projects and its eligible recipients are developing member countries — states, not community groups. Approach the Environmental Centre's country office for partnership; do not send it a grant application expecting an award.

trackers.name: GEF Small Grants Programme — up to US$50,000 direct to communities
trackers.desc: WHERE THE COMMUNITY MONEY ACTUALLY IS. The GEF Small Grants Programme, running since 1992 and implemented by UNDP, reached 135 countries of 144 eligible in GEF-8, which secured US$135 million for the core programme with nearly US$1 million allocated to each participating country — a per-country floor, so the money is not competed for across borders. Grants of up to US$50,000 go directly to local communities, community-based organisations and other non-governmental groups. Focal areas: biodiversity, climate change, land degradation and sustainable forest management, international waters and chemicals. KYRGYZSTAN'S OP8 PRIORITIES WERE SET THROUGH A NATIONAL CONSULTATION, in which the Regional Environmental Centre for Central Asia participated. The Country Programme Strategy that resulted determines which themes and geographies are eligible — read it before drafting, because global eligibility does not mean your region or theme is in scope.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: Kyrgyz Jayity — the national association of the pasture committees that actually hold the land-use right
trackers.desc: IN KYRGYZSTAN THE BODY WITH THE LEGAL INTEREST IN A THREATENED PASTURE IS NOT THE VILLAGE, IT IS THE VILLAGE'S JAYIT COMMITTEE — FIND YOURS BEFORE YOU DO ANYTHING ELSE. Pasture is used through pasture-user unions and their jayit committees, and Kyrgyz Jayity is their national association: a voluntary union of legal entities and a non-governmental organisation, whose stated purpose is to improve the capacity of pasture users, pasture-user unions and their jayit committees to manage and use pasture resources, working under Kyrgyz Republic legislation and its own Charter. The point for a land defence is that a mine, a road or a resort on pasture land does not merely upset residents — it collides with an existing, held use-right belonging to a constituted body that can act in its own name. The association also lists among its purposes the protection of the rights and lawful interests of its members, and reports work on self-governance of pasture-user unions, restoration of pastures and pasture infrastructure. It operates alongside the Ministry of Agriculture, the ARIS agency and the Research Institute of Livestock and Pastures, which means a jayit committee raising an objection is inside an existing state-facing structure rather than outside it. TWO CAVEATS THAT WEAKEN THIS AND SHOULD BE READ ANYWAY. Capacity is thin: reporting on Kyrgyz pasture degradation records that committee members received only basic donor-funded training and that the shortage of knowledge and experience in sustainable pasture management remains acute — expect to bring your own expertise. And this entry could not confirm recent activity: the newest association material reached during verification dates from 2018 and 2019, so establish that the association is currently functioning before relying on it, and in any case deal with your own jayit committee first.

trackers.name: Ecological Movement BIOM — the scientists who do the public expert review and run an environmental-rights portal
trackers.desc: THIS IS THE KYRGYZ BODY THAT PRODUCES THE THING A COMMUNITY OBJECTION USUALLY LACKS: A WRITTEN EXPERT REVIEW BY PEOPLE WITH SCIENTIFIC STANDING. BIOM is a non-commercial public organisation founded in 1993 bringing together specialists, scientists and leaders on environmental problems in the Kyrgyz Republic and Central Asia; its described activities include expert support to decision-making, expert review and monitoring, research, and work with local communities to strengthen the role of the public in environmentally significant decisions, including the protection of vulnerable groups. GO TO THE ENVIRONMENTAL-RIGHTS PORTAL FIRST: BIOM runs justice.biom.kg, which carries analytical work on the mechanisms for securing environmental rights in the Kyrgyz Republic, produced with the Konrad Adenauer Foundation, the public foundation ALGA and the Max Planck Foundation with European Union funding, and including a toolkit for public participation in significant decisions. BIOM has also published sample documents usable in public-participation campaigns, a genetic-fund cadastre of Kyrgyz biodiversity, and a manual for local self-government bodies on regional and local sustainable-development strategy — the last matters because in Kyrgyzstan the local council is often the decision point. CONTACT DETAILS ARE IN CONFLICT ACROSS DIRECTORIES AND THIS ENTRY WILL NOT PICK ONE: one business directory gives Chuy Prospekt 164a room 408/1 in Bishkek with a landline, another maps the organisation to Turusbekova 109/1 in the Leninsky district. Take the address and telephone from biom.kg itself. Note also that a newer build of the site appears at next.biom.kg alongside the main domain; both carry the same identity text, but prefer biom.kg. WHAT BIOM IS NOT: a litigator or a land-holder. Pair it with counsel, and with your jayit committee where the land is pasture.

trackers.name: Nezavisimaya Ekologicheskaya Ekspertiza — the body that runs community environmental review, and that wrote the government's own transboundary assessment procedure
trackers.desc: ITS STANDING IS THE POINT: this Bishkek public association prepared the procedure for conducting assessment under the Espoo Convention on environmental impact assessment in a transboundary context — commissioned by the Kyrgyz state environmental protection and forestry agency itself, with the UNECE convention secretariat, the government of Norway and OSCE offices behind it. An organisation that wrote the state's own assessment procedure is not easily dismissed when it later reviews a project against it, and that is the reason to bring it in early rather than after a decision. WHAT IT DOES THAT A COMMUNITY CANNOT: obshchestvennaya ekologicheskaya ekspertiza — community environmental review, which it runs as a standing function. In the post-Soviet legal tradition this sits alongside the state's own expert review as a recognised counterweight, and this is the body in Kyrgyzstan that performs it. Its stated purpose is the protection of the rights of present and future generations to an environment favourable to life and health. Registered as a public association on 8 April 1998, Bishkek, with a long-serving director who is also Kyrgyzstan's representative on the public council of the interstate sustainable development commission under the Aral Sea fund — so it carries a regional seat as well as a national one. IT WILL ALSO GO PUBLIC, WHICH MATTERS WHEN A DECISION IS BEING TAKEN QUIETLY: on the Bishkek landfill it stated in national press that waste is merely stockpiled rather than sorted or processed, that the site now holds many times what it was designed for, and that a river five hundred metres away feeds reservoirs in the irrigation system, so the contamination reaches farmers' fields and then the market. WHAT IT IS NOT: a litigator, a fund or a landholder. Pair it with BIOM and with your jayit committee, both already in this file for Kyrgyzstan — BIOM for the environmental-rights portal and public-participation toolkit, the jayit committee because on pasture it is the body holding the use-right. NAME COLLISION, AND IT IS AN EASY ONE TO FALL INTO: a Russian commercial laboratory trades under the identical Russian name, selling environmental project development and instrumental measurement services. That is a business in another country, not this association. Verify on the Kyrgyz domain.

trackers.name: Bir Duino Kyrgyzstan — free legal aid hotline, an office in Osh as well as Bishkek, and it took a statement to COP30
trackers.desc: IT HAS AN OFFICE IN THE SOUTH, WHICH FOR KYRGYZSTAN IS THE POINT. Almost every national organisation in this file operates from the capital; this human rights movement runs a staffed regional office in Osh with its own head and its own advocates, alongside Bishkek. If your land is in the south, that is the difference between a body you can reach and one you can only write to. IT PUBLISHES A FREE LEGAL AID HOTLINE and states that the line continues to operate, and it tells people directly that if they or those close to them have encountered torture or ill-treatment they should come to its offices for legal help. THE ENVIRONMENTAL CONNECTION IS REAL BUT INDIRECT, AND WORTH UNDERSTANDING BEFORE YOU APPROACH: this is a human rights movement, not an environmental organisation. It is the legal successor of a human rights centre previously named Citizens Against Corruption, so its lineage is corruption and rights rather than land. But it made an official statement to the thirtieth Conference of the Parties to the UN climate convention in 2025, and it built one edition of the international documentary human rights festival it runs around the question of how to stop risks becoming disasters. So the framing that reaches it is the same one that works for its counterparts elsewhere in this region: present the persecution, the corruption or the disaster risk, not the landscape. It also trains people to take local office — by its own account thirteen women who went through its training became deputies of local keneshes across four provinces — which matters because in Kyrgyzstan the local council is where land decisions are taken, and because it develops young advocates in-house, with a named senior lawyer bringing them through real cases. THE LIMITS AND THE GAPS: nothing found this round establishes that it has acted for communities in a mining or land dispute, so treat the environmental route as available on framing rather than proven; and the hotline number was published in the pandemic period, so confirm it is current before relying on it. Pair with BIOM and the independent expertise association, both already in this file for Kyrgyzstan, for the environmental evidence — and remember that on pasture the body with the legal interest is your jayit committee.

trackers.name: CEPF Mountains of Central Asia — small grants averaging about $15,000 direct to community groups, but your project must map to a strategic direction
trackers.desc: THIS IS ONE OF THE FEW FUNDS ANYWHERE IN THIS REGION THAT GIVES MONEY DIRECTLY TO COMMUNITY GROUPS RATHER THAN THROUGH A NATIONAL PARTNER. Eligible applicants are civil society organisations of all sizes — farmers' cooperatives, community groups, indigenous peoples' groups, universities, small businesses and non-governmental organisations alike. Small grants average around fifteen thousand US dollars and are handled by a regional implementation team based in or near the hotspot; larger grants average around a hundred and fifty thousand and are handled by the secretariat, with roughly twenty thousand dollars the dividing line. THE CONDITION THAT DECIDES ELIGIBILITY, AND IT IS NOT NEGOTIABLE: every project must link to one of the strategic directions set out in the hotspot's ecosystem profile. Read the profile before writing anything — a good project that does not map onto a strategic direction is not a fundable project here, and CEPF works to Key Biodiversity Areas and corridors rather than to political boundaries, so what matters is whether your site sits in a priority area. TWO PRACTICAL POINTS THAT CATCH APPLICANTS: individuals cannot apply directly and must work through a civil society organisation — which is the second time this file has found that registering matters, after the Kazakh network that incorporated specifically in order to be able to act — and calls are open only intermittently, typically for six to eight weeks at a time, so subscribe to the newsletter and watch the open calls page rather than checking occasionally. Small-grant applications start with a short letter of inquiry by email, which may be accepted in a local language specified in the call rather than only in English. CEPF is a joint initiative of the French Development Agency, Conservation International, the European Union, the Global Environment Facility, the Government of Japan and the World Bank. VERIFY THE COUNTRY LIST BEFORE YOU PLAN: this entry records the Mountains of Central Asia hotspot, which is among those currently open, but the precise list of countries and the current call status were not confirmed on cepf.net during verification. Check the ecosystem profile and the open calls page first. AND KNOW WHAT IS CLOSED: CEPF's Caucasus investment ran from 2004, committed 8.5 million dollars and awarded 42 grants, and that window has ended — Armenian and Georgian groups will find extensive Caucasus material online that no longer corresponds to an open fund.

trackers.name: ICCA Global Support Initiative — funding aimed specifically at territories and areas that communities already conserve themselves
trackers.desc: THIS IS THE STREAM TO ASK FOR WHEN THE LAND YOU ARE DEFENDING IS ALREADY CONSERVED BY YOUR OWN COMMUNITY RATHER THAN BY THE STATE. Within the Small Grants Programme there is a dedicated Global Support Initiative for territories and areas conserved by Indigenous Peoples and local communities — land held and looked after under customary arrangements, without formal protected-area status. Most conservation funding assumes either a state reserve or a private owner; this one is built around the third case, which is the common one across Central Asian pasture, forest and mountain territory. KYRGYZSTAN HAS SEEN A CALL UNDER IT: the United Nations country team published a Small Grants Programme call for proposals on strategic support to Indigenous Peoples and Community Conserved Areas, with applications accepted in Russian on a national template and submitted to a named programme address. Applications in Russian rather than English removes a barrier that quietly excludes most village-level applicants. WHY THIS MATTERS PARTICULARLY HERE: on pasture in Kyrgyzstan the body holding the use-right is the jayit committee, recorded elsewhere in this file, and pasture managed by such a committee is close to the definition this initiative was written for. A jayit committee approaching this stream is not stretching to fit a category; it is the category. The wider programme's rules apply — approach the National Coordinator first with a short concept paper, expect the money in three instalments, and remember that community groups which are not formally registered can be funded through a Memorandum of Agreement without an intermediary organisation, which for an unregistered pasture users' group is the decisive point. TWO CAVEATS. The Kyrgyz call reached dates from 2020, so establish whether the stream is currently open before planning around it — this file has repeatedly found Central Asian programmes that ran, did good work and lapsed. And the initiative is a global one; only its application in this country is recorded here, and a related response initiative appears in the same programme's material, so ask which vehicle is live rather than naming one.

trackers.name: Adilet Legal Clinic — it will register your organisation as a legal entity, which is the step that unlocks everything else
trackers.desc: START HERE IF YOUR GROUP IS NOT REGISTERED, BECAUSE REGISTRATION IS THE BLOCKER AND THIS CLINIC REMOVES IT. Among its listed services are the state registration, re-registration and closure of legal entities. Elsewhere in this file two findings meet at exactly this point: a Kazakh network that spent twenty-three years as an informal group registered in 2020 specifically because conducting public environmental expertise requires legal personality; and the Central Asian hotspot fund requires a registered entity with its own bank account while the small grants programme can reach an unregistered group only through a special memorandum. Registration is what turns a group of neighbours into a body that can commission expertise, hold a grant and appear in a case. THE OTHER SERVICES ARE THE ONES A LAND DISPUTE NEEDS: analysis of documents of legal significance, and disputes arising under contracts — which covers a lease, a concession or a construction agreement. ITS RECORD AGAINST THE STATE IS THE REASON TO TRUST IT WITH SOMETHING DIFFICULT: since 2002 its lawyers are credited with around thirty-three thousand legal consultations, and it won a case with no precedent in the country on behalf of parents of children infected with HIV in hospital, against state bodies. It also obtained citizenship documents for thirty-three residents of a state institution, offered free legal help to medical workers facing persecution over their statements, and publishes legal analyses of draft legislation — the last matters because a body that comments on bills before they pass knows the drafters. Based at Umetaliev Street 39 in Bishkek; it has run more than forty projects funded by United Nations agencies including the refugee and human rights offices, the development programme and the population fund, alongside European and Central Asian foundations. THE NAME IS A SERIOUS HAZARD AND YOU MUST CHECK YOU HAVE THE RIGHT BODY. At least five things answer to Adilet: this clinic; a SEPARATE Kyrgyz foundation with a nearly identical name whose registry entry records the termination of its activity in 2015 and whose company profile still appears in search looking current; a consumer protection society in Astana in another country; a law academy; and a political party in Kazakhstan. Match on this domain and on the Bishkek address, never on the name alone. WHAT IT IS NOT: not an environmental specialist. Its published record is civil rights, health, statelessness and legislative analysis, so frame a land matter as registration, contract or administrative process rather than as ecology — the same framing point this file has made for the Armenian and Georgian rights bodies.

trackers.name: Global Greengrants — you cannot apply to it; an advisor who lives in the region has to find you
trackers.desc: THE FIRST THING TO UNDERSTAND IS THAT THERE IS NO APPLICATION FORM. This fund does not accept unsolicited proposals. Groups are identified and invited by volunteer advisors who live in the region, are part of the movements they fund, and find potential grantees through their own networks; the regional board then decides who is funded. So the work is not writing a proposal — it is becoming known to the people on the Central Asia board, which means being visible in the regional movement, at gatherings, in the federations and networks recorded elsewhere in this file. WHY IT IS WORTH THE TROUBLE: its own account is that this model reaches critical groups most other funders cannot, and it launched a CENTRAL ASIA ADVISORY BOARD IN 2023 expressly to reach areas off the funding radar. Its stated focus areas include resource rights, ecosystem protection and environmental defenders. THE MONEY IS SMALL, FAST AND SUITED TO A VILLAGE RATHER THAN AN INSTITUTION: grants average around five thousand dollars, with many in the five hundred to five thousand range — which is the scale that pays for a survey, a lawyer's expenses, a bus to a hearing or a translation, and it is deliberate: the fund describes small grantmaking as a strategic approach overlooked by larger environmental funders. Across 2023 it made over fourteen hundred grants in more than a hundred and twenty countries. THIS SUITS THE KYRGYZ SITUATION BECAUSE THE BODIES THAT HOLD LAND HERE ARE PASTURE COMMITTEES AND VILLAGE GROUPS, not institutions with grant departments — and a fund that finds its grantees rather than waiting for forms is one of the few that can reach them. THE LIMITS: it names Central Asia as a region it works in but no country individually; it is based in the United States; and being unable to apply means there is no way to be sure of a hearing. Treat it as a reason to be present in the regional movement rather than as a window to watch.

trackers.name: CAMP Alatoo — it got a community micro-reserve into official decisions, and it builds the pasture committees' case with data
trackers.desc: IT PUT A PROTECTION CATEGORY AT VILLAGE SCALE INTO OFFICIAL DECISIONS. Its proposals for district pasture management commissions, a COMMUNITY MICRO-RESERVE, resource conflict resolution and support to forest enterprises were taken up by the relevant state bodies and fixed in their decisions.
