Every other designation route in this file runs at national or provincial level; this one is small enough for a single community to hold, and there is a precedent for creating it. Ask about the micro-reserve first. IT WORKS DIRECTLY WITH THE BODIES THAT HOLD KYRGYZ PASTURE: its work centres on preventing and settling CONFLICTS OVER PASTURE and building the capacity of the jayit committees — recorded separately in this file as the holders of the pasture use-right — across Jalal-Abad, Batken, Osh and Naryn provinces, with the aim of embedding the model in national pasture policy. AND IT SUPPLIES THE THING A COMMITTEE NEEDS TO WIN AN ARGUMENT: numbers. Its specialists, working with forest enterprise staff and committee members, calculated a grazing norm from THREE YEARS OF PASTURE MONITORING DATA, and it has been completing a unified method for monitoring pastures at local level. This file has now recorded the same approach in Georgia and Jordan: a stocking rate derived from measurement is what turns a dispute about grazing into a decision. IT ALSO HELPS COMMITTEES TURN A MANAGEMENT PLAN INTO MONEY: after assessment and specialist consultation, committees drew up project proposals for CO-FINANCING to improve pasture infrastructure as part of their Pasture Management Plan — so the plan is not only a compliance document but the basis of a funding application. KNOW THE FORUM: pasture questions are decided at a District Pasture Commission chaired by a deputy district head, whose membership includes forest enterprise directors, the pasture committees, district administration, agrarian development and the committees' own national association. It handles distribution of State Forest Fund pastures, grazing permits, payment for use and conditions for shepherds moving stock to summer pasture. That is where a pasture dispute is actually resolved. It also works on a national electronic jayit committee system administered by the agriculture ministry's pasture department and intended to cover all 454 committees, which gives a committee an auditable record of stock numbers and pasture condition over time. THE LIMITS: it is a technical and development foundation working with ministries, not a campaigner, and nothing found shows it opposing a project. It also works in Tajikistan.

trackers.name: ProtectDefenders.eu — for when the organisation you would have turned to is itself facing shutdown
trackers.desc: RECORD WHY THIS IS HERE, BECAUSE IT CHANGES HOW YOU SHOULD READ THE OTHER KYRGYZ ENTRIES IN THIS FILE. A law in force since April 2024 requires non-governmental organisations that receive foreign funding and engage in broadly defined political activity to register as foreign representatives, to LABEL ALL THEIR MATERIALS as such, and to submit to reporting and auditing — with non-compliance punishable by suspension of activities for up to six months or COMPLETE SHUTDOWN. Independent monitoring records that some organisations have chosen to self-liquidate or curtail their work rather than be targeted, and that the law may deter international funders from supporting Kyrgyz organisations at all. THAT IS WHY AN EXTERNAL ROUTE MATTERS HERE NOW: the domestic body this file records as the country's free legal aid route for defenders is itself litigating against the law rather than sheltering anyone from it. WHAT THIS MECHANISM OFFERS: separate request channels for INDIVIDUALS and for organisations, so a person needs no registered body behind them — which matters acutely where registration is the thing being weaponised; correspondence accepted officially in RUSSIAN; a 24/7 helpline and an encrypted contact form; and emergency grants capped at €10,000 with an average of about €3,000, rolling and without deadlines, covering urgent protection measures including security, legal costs and relocation. Its three criteria are that you are a defender working consistently with the United Nations declaration, that you face risk because of that work, and that the need is urgent, with LACK OF ACCESS TO OTHER SOURCES OF SUPPORT EXPRESSLY TAKEN INTO ACCOUNT — a Kyrgyz applicant can point directly to the law for that. ITS RELOCATION PROGRAMME PREFERS MOVING A DEFENDER WITHIN THEIR OWN COUNTRY OR SUB-REGION where possible, so they can keep working. HEED ITS OWN WARNING ABOUT ITS OWN MONEY, WHICH IS SHARPER HERE THAN ANYWHERE: payment may come by bank transfer or Western Union and WILL SHOW THE MECHANISM AS THE SOURCE, and it asks recipients to consider the security implications and raise them with the secretariat. In a country where receiving foreign funds is the trigger for the labelling regime, that is not a formality — discuss it before any grant is made. THE LIMITS: it states it cannot support every defender in need and routes requests to partner organisations rather than assessing grant forms centrally; and no casework of its own in Kyrgyzstan could be established.

trackers.name: Whitley Fund for Nature — the step above small grants, awarded to an individual conservation leader
trackers.desc: EVERY OTHER FUND RECORDED FOR THIS COUNTRY IS A SMALL GRANT. This one is £50,000 over a year to a named individual, with CONTINUATION FUNDING OF UP TO £100,000 available afterwards to winners who completed their grant, and a further £60,000 award for outstanding past recipients. Roughly fifty-five per cent of previous winners have gone on to win continuation funding, so it is better understood as an entry point to multi-year support than as a prize. IT IS BUILT FOR THE SITUATION THIS FILE HAS DOCUMENTED IN KYRGYZSTAN: pasture committees, community bodies and conservancies whose work depends on a particular person. Applications must NAME THE TEAM LEADER who would receive the award, and the fund's stated purpose is to raise that person's profile as much as to fund the project — international recognition, communications and media support, and entry to a network of more than two hundred conservation leaders across eighty countries. For someone whose obstacle is being unknown outside their district, that is the substance of the offer rather than a garnish. ELIGIBILITY IS SPECIFIC: nationals of the country where they work, leading grassroots projects, working for or leading a LOCALLY INCORPORATED organisation rather than as in-country staff of a foreign-headquartered body; and the country must not be classified as a high-income economy, which this one is not. WHAT THE APPLICATION MUST SHOW: practical action FOUNDED ON SCIENCE with community involvement at grassroots level; work that is replicable or scalable and already on the cusp of significant impact; clear measurable outcomes with the INDICATORS thought through; and sustainability beyond the award. The fund also expects to provide a significant share of the project cost — in the region of thirty per cent or more — so it is not a top-up. Applications run annually and close in the autumn, are screened by an expert academic panel with international reference checks, and finalists are interviewed. THE LIMIT: this is conservation funding, not campaign funding. It will not pay for objections, litigation or advocacy against a project — for those, use the litigation and defender funds recorded elsewhere in this file.

trackers.name: IUCN NL Land Acquisition Fund — grants for securing land through lease or agreement
trackers.desc: IT WILL FUND LONG-TERM MANAGEMENT RIGHTS OVER AN AREA WITHOUT ANY TRANSFER OF OWNERSHIP — leases and conservation agreements — as well as purchase, in grants of up to around a hundred thousand euros to locally registered non-profit organisations. This country's community land holding runs through statutory use-rights rather than ownership: pasture committees hold and allocate grazing rights under law, and this file recorded a community micro-reserve taken into official decisions and grazing norms set from years of data. A FUND THAT PAYS FOR RIGHTS RATHER THAN TITLE FITS THAT SYSTEM DIRECTLY. WHAT IT LOOKS FOR: land holding critically endangered, endangered or vulnerable red list species; recognised biodiversity sites; ecosystems underrepresented in the protected area network; and land that maintains CONNECTIVITY between fragmented habitats as a corridor or stepping stone. Mountain and pasture ecosystems fragmented by roads, mines or fencing fit the connectivity priority squarely. THE REGISTERED LOCAL ORGANISATION HOLDS WHAT IS ACQUIRED AND CARRIES THE RESPONSIBILITY FOR IT, which is the fund's stated model rather than an exception. ELIGIBILITY TURNS ON THREE CHECKABLE THINGS: local registration as a non-profit, non-governmental or civil society organisation; direct responsibility for preparing and running the project; and A BANK ACCOUNT IN THE ORGANISATION'S OWN NAME in the country of establishment or where the project runs. A pasture committee or informal group without registration should apply through a registered partner. Annual call, spring deadline, running since 2001 with more than a hundred and fifty projects in over forty countries. THE LIMITS: nothing in its published record shows a project in this country or the wider region, and its examples are heavily tropical — so this is a route that is open on its written criteria, not a proven one here. It funds acquisition, not campaigning or litigation. Ask the fund whether it will consider this region before committing effort to a proposal.

trackers.name: Aigine — it has inventoried 1,202 sacred sites, and helped communities recover the right to govern them
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR LAND IS ALREADY IN ITS INVENTORY. It has compiled a record of 1,202 SACRED SITES and 36 pilgrimage practices across this country — springs, caves, mountains, lakes, trees, tombs and mausoleums that people visit as pilgrims. A spring or a tree that a developer's assessment treats as unremarkable may already be documented as a sacred site with recorded custodians and rituals, and that is a materially different thing to defend. WHAT IT ACTUALLY DID THAT MATTERS MOST: IT WAS INSTRUMENTAL IN RECOVERING THE LOCAL GOVERNANCE SYSTEMS FOR THESE SITES — the customary arrangements by which particular families and communities look after particular places. This file has recorded five ways land is held for protection in this region, all requiring title, lease, agreement or statutory right. THIS IS A SIXTH THAT REQUIRES NONE OF THEM: recognised custodianship of a site held as a commons. Scholarship on this country describes such sites as the CORE OF COMMUNITY-CONSERVED AREAS, and states the conditions plainly — a sacred natural site CANNOT BE HELD BY ONE EXCLUSIVE OWNER, and needs some form of PUBLIC PROPERTY STATUS so that it stays open to everyone who would come. ITS PRACTICAL CONSERVATION TOOLS AT ONE SITE COMPLEX ARE COPYABLE AND CHEAP: it FENCED several sacred sites, HUNG SIGNS AT THE ENTRANCES SETTING OUT RULES OF APPROPRIATE BEHAVIOUR, published a book recording the site's description, history and visitors' accounts, built basic facilities for pilgrims, and brought local custodians into workshops and conferences — so that today local people themselves guide visitors and explain the rules. A fence, a sign, a published record and a named custodian together assert a claim that no title deed is needed to make. IT WORKS BY PARTICIPATORY ACTION RESEARCH RATHER THAN BY STUDYING PEOPLE, and it BRIDGES TRADITIONAL PRACTITIONERS AND STATE AGENCIES, which is the connection a community usually cannot make alone. Founded in 2004 in the capital, accredited to the United Nations cultural body for intangible heritage, publishing its field research openly in the national language and in English, and working with a provincial state university's students alongside custodians. THE LIMITS: it is a research and cultural organisation, not an objector or a law practice — nothing found shows it opposing a mine, a road or a dam. Its subject is sacred and cultural sites, so land with no such site is outside it. And its own scholarship warns that the status of these sites is contested domestically, including on religious grounds. Use it to establish what your place is and who has always looked after it; take the objection to the bodies recorded elsewhere in this file.

trackers.name: Mapeo — a free offline app for a community to map its own land and keep the record
trackers.desc: IT WORKS WITH NO INTERNET AND NO SPECIAL EQUIPMENT, AND THE COMMUNITY OWNS THE DATA. With one button a person records a GPS POINT, A PHOTOGRAPH AND A NOTE; storage is decentralised on the devices themselves; and records move between collaborators by DIRECT PHONE-TO-PHONE SYNCHRONISATION rather than through any server. A community that maps its land on somebody else's platform has handed over the record. This one does not. IT WAS BUILT FOR EXACTLY WHAT THIS MAP EXISTS FOR: its own documentation says it exists so that frontline groups can document what is happening in order to take community action, REPORT INFORMATION TO AUTHORITIES, FILE LAWSUITS, launch media campaigns, or CREATE MAPS FOR LAND CLAIMS. THAT MATTERS PARTICULARLY HERE, WHERE THIS FILE RECORDED AN INVENTORY OF MORE THAN TWELVE HUNDRED SACRED SITES AND THE RECOVERY OF THE LOCAL GOVERNANCE SYSTEMS THAT LOOK AFTER THEM — protection through recognised custodianship rather than title. A custodian community with no deed needs its own record of what it holds: where the spring is, which trees, who tends them, what was there before. A dated, photographed, georeferenced record made by the people who hold the place is a different kind of evidence from an assertion. ANYONE CAN LEARN IT: its own materials say a person who has never used a smartphone can learn to collect points and photographs in a few hours. The desktop version needs some computer skill and produces PRINTED OR PDF REPORTS, and exports to the standard mapping formats — so what the community gathers can be handed to a lawyer, an official or a court in a form they accept, and can be imported into the satellite tools recorded elsewhere in this file. IT HAS WORKED WHERE IT MATTERED: an indigenous nation in South America used it for over four years to build territorial data and maps that were used as evidence against their government in opposition to oil development, and they won. A version developed with a United Nations conservation centre and a forest peoples' organisation is aimed specifically at communities documenting territories they conserve, with data staying on the device and any submission to global registries made only voluntarily and after the community's own consent process. THE LIMITS: it is software, not an organisation — nobody will do the work for you, and customising it with your own categories and offline maps takes technical help. Its listed interface translations do not currently include Russian, Kyrgyz or the other languages of this region, though it can be translated into any language. Note also that the organisation behind it now appears under a changed name, so verify the current source before downloading.

trackers.name: Rural Development Fund — survey capacity in every province, and the pasture law explained
trackers.desc: IT HAS FIELD ENUMERATORS AND SUPERVISORS IN EVERY PROVINCE OF THE COUNTRY, AND IT REPORTS IN KYRGYZ AS WELL AS RUSSIAN AND ENGLISH. It designs survey tools, trains and supervises interviewers, runs data entry and analysis, and conducts LEGAL AND ECONOMIC REVIEWS. This file has recorded across the region that what decides a land dispute is documented evidence, and that communities cannot produce it alone. HERE IS A DOMESTIC BODY WITH THE FIELD CAPACITY TO GATHER IT, working in the language people actually speak. IT HAS ALREADY PUBLISHED THE DOCUMENT MOST USEFUL IN A GRAZING DISPUTE: a comprehensive study of past and current land management including AN OVERVIEW OF THE LEGISLATION ON PASTURE ACCESS AND MANAGEMENT, with practical examples of how pasture management works in practice, alongside a national livestock study. Read that before arguing with anyone about grazing rights — it sets out what the law actually provides. AND IT HAS SIGNED COMMITMENTS YOU CAN QUOTE BACK TO IT. Through the global land coalition it belongs to, it is committed to respecting and strengthening the land rights of women and men living in poverty, and to ensuring that NO ONE IS DEPRIVED OF THE USE AND CONTROL OF THE LAND on which their well-being and human dignity depend — INCLUDING THROUGH EVICTION, EXPULSION OR EXCLUSION — with compulsory changes to tenure undertaken ONLY IN LINE WITH INTERNATIONAL LAW AND HUMAN RIGHTS STANDARDS. A signed commitment is a lever: it is a great deal harder for an organisation to decline a request that falls squarely inside a principle it has publicly endorsed. IT ALSO DOES SOMETHING NOTHING ELSE IN THIS PAYLOAD DOES: since 2010 it has run conflict prevention and mitigation work, including peer learning between local governments on managing conflict and strengthening BORDER VILLAGES to handle disputes arising from the use of WATER, PASTURES, LAND AND TIMBER. Where a land dispute is between communities rather than against a company — which this file has recorded as common in the pasture systems here — that mediation experience is the relevant capability. IT IS NETWORKED WITH BODIES ALREADY IN THIS MAP: the national association of pasture committees, and an association of forest and land users. Approach it through them if a direct approach is difficult. Established in 2003, non-profit and non-governmental, with expertise in natural resource management, local governance, social mobilisation and agricultural economics. THE LIMITS: it is a policy and research organisation, not a litigator or an objector — it produces studies, surveys and recommendations, and somebody else must use them. Its work is largely donor-funded and project-based, so its presence in any district depends on a project. AND NO WEBSITE OF ITS OWN COULD BE CONFIRMED: this entry points at its membership record in the global land coalition, which also carries the commitments quoted above.

trackers.name: KAFLU — the association of forest and land users, existing to secure its members' access
trackers.desc: IT IS THE AFFECTED-USER BODY FOR FORESTS, AND ITS STATED PURPOSE IS ACCESS. A professional organisation PROMOTING ITS MEMBERS' INTERESTS in sustainable ecosystem and natural resource management, working to ensure FAIR ACCESS, responsible use and effective conservation for resilient livelihoods and poverty alleviation IN THE COMMUNES — across both the forest and agriculture sectors. This file has proved in eight countries that where no environmental organisation can be found, the union or association of the people whose livelihood the project takes is the body that exists, is legally recognised and is invisible to searches for the wrong noun. THIS IS THAT BODY FOR FOREST AND LAND USERS HERE. IT COMPLETES A SET. This map already records the national association of pasture committees and a rural research organisation with field capacity in every province; all three belong to the same global land-rights coalition, which means they know each other and can be approached through one another. Grazing goes to the pasture committees, forest and farmland use goes here, and the survey and legal-review work goes to the research body. AND IT HAS SIGNED SOMETHING WORTH KNOWING ABOUT: every member of that coalition signs pledges to PROTECT AND EMPOWER BOTH WOMEN AND LAND DEFENDERS within the network. This payload has documented defenders prosecuted, sued, smeared and detained across five countries, with almost no organisation formally committed to protecting them. A member organisation that has signed such a pledge can be asked what it commits them to when one of your people is targeted. THE WIDER COALITION'S COMMITMENTS ARE QUOTABLE TOO: that no one be deprived of the use and control of the land on which their well-being and dignity depend, INCLUDING THROUGH EVICTION, EXPULSION OR EXCLUSION, and that compulsory changes to tenure be made only in line with international law and human rights standards. THE LIMITS: it is a professional and membership association promoting sustainable management and enterprise, not an objector or a litigator, and nothing found shows it opposing a project. Its emphasis on entrepreneurship development in the forest and agriculture sectors means it may see a commercial proposal as an opportunity rather than a threat — establish its position before assuming alignment. AND NOTE THE ADDRESS: no site of its own was confirmed, so this entry points at its membership record in the global coalition, which carries its description and the pledges. A reviewer should look for its own domain.

trackers.name: Unified public discussion portal — draft rules, their progress, and someone who already analyses them
trackers.desc: IT CARRIES DRAFT SUBORDINATE ACTS AS WELL AS DRAFT LAWS, AND THAT IS THE PART THAT MATTERS FOR LAND. Statutes rarely allocate a pasture or licence a quarry; SUBORDINATE ACTS DO — allocation rules, licensing procedures, permitting requirements, category changes. The portal is the single national place where those drafts are put for public discussion, created by a government decree in 2020 and run under the justice ministry. IT ALSO PUBLISHES INFORMATION ON THE PROGRESS OF DRAFTS, NOT ONLY THEIR TEXT — so you can see where an instrument has reached rather than discovering it once adopted, and it offers an advanced search across several thousand instruments. THE STRONGEST REASON TO USE IT IS SOMETHING THIS FILE ALREADY HOLDS: THE LEGAL CLINIC RECORDED SEPARATELY FOR THIS COUNTRY PUBLISHES WRITTEN ANALYSES OF DRAFTS POSTED HERE, citing the portal item by its number and date. So before writing your own comment, look for an existing analysis of the draft that affects you — and if none exists, that clinic is the obvious body to ask for one. A community comment supported by a lawyer's published analysis is a different document from a letter of objection. AND THE RULES OF THE CONSULTATION ARE THEMSELVES PUBLISHED: the procedure for placing a draft on the portal and running the public discussion sits in the centralised legal database. That matters because it converts a complaint that a consultation was unfair into a measurable claim that a written procedure was not followed — which this file has recorded as the difference between an objection that is dismissed and one that must be answered. THE LIMITS. Comments feed rule-making; they do not bind anyone. The portal shows what was posted, so an instrument that never appeared is invisible here — though the published procedure is what tells you whether it should have appeared. IT REQUIRES JAVASCRIPT AND SEVERAL PAGES SIMPLY REFUSE TO LOAD WITHOUT IT, which is a real barrier on an old phone or a slow connection — use a library or a district office computer if needed. And the portal was built with foreign donor support, so its continuity depends on the ministry maintaining it.

trackers.name: Accountability Console — compare the complaint offices before choosing one
trackers.desc: THE FEATURE THAT MATTERS MOST IS THE COMPARISON. This database lets you COMPARE AND ANALYSE THE POLICIES OF THE DIFFERENT ACCOUNTABILITY OFFICES OF INTERNATIONAL FINANCE and produce comparison reports — so a community facing a financed project can see, before committing, which office has rules it can actually satisfy. That matters because of what the same database shows about outcomes: TOO FEW COMPLAINTS GET THROUGH THE SYSTEM AND ACHIEVE A RESULT, AND A HIGH NUMBER ARE CLOSED WITHOUT OUTCOME HAVING BEEN RULED INELIGIBLE. MOST CASES ARE LOST AT THE DOOR, NOT ON THE ARGUMENT. IT ALSO HOLDS EVERY COMPLAINT EVER FILED TO THOSE OFFICES, searchable by institution, sector and region — so you can find complaints about projects like yours, read the documents from those that produced results, and identify which organisations advised them. This file has recorded for this country a legal clinic that analyses draft laws, pasture committees, a forest and land users' association and a defenders' protection mechanism; what none of them supplies is a record of what complaining to a financier has ever actually produced. A COMPLAINT PATHFINDER WALKS THROUGH THE OPTIONS FIRST, which is the right order: choose the forum, check its eligibility rules, then write. ON COST: viewing the complaints list and the mechanisms' policies is open to any member of the public, and premium access runs on a sliding scale with THE FEE WAIVED FOR USERS ON A LIMITED BUDGET — ask for it rather than assuming. THE LIMITS: it covers projects financed INTERNATIONALLY, so a purely domestic scheme is outside its scope; and it is a database and strategy tool, not a representative — it will not file anything for you, though it names the organisations that might.

trackers.name: National planting programme and its public monitoring platform — free saplings from forest nurseries, and a way to check the claims
trackers.desc: THE FOUR RESTORATION ENTRIES BEFORE THIS ONE ALL TOLD A COMMUNITY WHERE TO GET PLANTS. THIS ONE ALSO TELLS IT HOW TO CHECK WHAT THE STATE SAYS IT PLANTED. A DIGITAL PLATFORM IS BEING LAUNCHED FOR REAL-TIME MONITORING OF TREE PLANTING ACROSS THE COUNTRY — ANYONE CAN SELECT A REGION AND SEE HOW THE PROGRAMME IS BEING IMPLEMENTED THERE, and the monitoring is expressly open NOT ONLY TO STATE BODIES BUT TO ALL CITIZENS. IF TREES ARE REPORTED AS PLANTED WHERE YOU LIVE, THAT IS NOW A CHECKABLE CLAIM — and a discrepancy between the platform and the ground is the kind of documented fact this file has spent hundreds of entries teaching communities to gather. THE PROGRAMME ITSELF IS A NATIONAL CAMPAIGN RUNNING SINCE MARCH 2022, ANNUAL, WITH NINE MILLION SAPLINGS PLANNED FOR 2026. Its stated aims include increasing forest land and building environmental responsibility among citizens, which is language a community can quote when asking to be included. THE PLANTS COME FROM THE FOREST ENTERPRISES AND THEIR NURSERIES, AND THE RECORDED ACTIONS SHOW THE SCALE A LOCAL EFFORT ACTUALLY WORKS AT: 555 rosehip saplings on a single hectare at one forest enterprise; A THOUSAND JUNIPER SAPLINGS RAISED IN A FORESTRY NURSERY; 1,500 elm and apricot saplings across three hectares PLANTED BY SIXTY-NINE PEOPLE; two hundred deciduous trees for the international day of forests. THESE ARE VILLAGE-SIZED NUMBERS — ask your district forest enterprise which nursery it runs, what it holds, and whether it will supply a community planting. TWO OPERATIONAL DETAILS WORTH MORE THAN THE HEADLINE FIGURES. FIRST, FULL FENCING WAS ORGANISED AROUND A PLANTING AREA TO PROTECT THE YOUNG PLANTS FROM ANIMALS AND OTHER HARMFUL FACTORS — in a country of grazing livestock, unfenced planting is feeding, not forestry, and the fence should be in the budget before the trees. SECOND, SURVIVAL IS BEING MEASURED: seventy-five per cent of trees planted in one province in 2025 were reported to have taken root. ASK FOR THE SURVIVAL RATE IN YOUR OWN DISTRICT, because it is the number that shows whether planting there is done properly. NOW THE PART A READER DESERVES AND WHICH THE PROGRAMME'S OWN PUBLICITY WILL NOT SUPPLY. CRITICAL REPORTING ON THE SAME CAMPAIGN STATES THAT FOUR YEARS IN THERE ARE NO PRECISE FIGURES FOR HOW MANY TREES HAVE ACTUALLY BEEN PLANTED OR HOW MUCH HAS BEEN SPENT, and that the programme lives largely in ministry reports while the capital keeps losing green space and its air quality worsens. BOTH THINGS CAN BE TRUE: the nurseries and the saplings are real and reachable, and the national totals may be unreliable. THAT IS PRECISELY WHY THE MONITORING PLATFORM MATTERS — use it to check your own area rather than trusting a national figure, and if what it claims is not on the ground, that is a finding worth recording and raising. THE LIMITS: this is a state programme driven from the top, it plants where authorities decide, and it will not be turned against a development the government supports. Municipal headquarters have been created for it in the capital, so in cities the route runs through the mayor's office. Use it with the pasture committees and the forest and land users' association recorded separately here — both of which hold ground where planting could go.

trackers.name: Land and cadastre agency — four property certificates by phone, including the full history of rights and restrictions
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING HAS PASTURE COMMITTEES AND A FOREST USERS' ASSOCIATION THAT HOLD GROUND, AND NO WAY TO FIND OUT WHAT IS ACTUALLY REGISTERED OVER A PARCEL. FOUR CERTIFICATES ARE AVAILABLE WITHOUT VISITING ANY OFFICE, THROUGH THE STATE E-SERVICES PORTAL AND A MOBILE APPLICATION: AN EXTRACT OF RIGHTS AND RESTRICTIONS; THE TECHNICAL PARAMETERS OF THE PROPERTY; THE HISTORY OF RIGHTS AND RESTRICTIONS; AND A CERTIFICATE OF HAVING OR NOT HAVING RIGHTS TO A PROPERTY. THE THIRD ONE IS THE PRIZE, AND NOTHING ELSE IN THIS PAYLOAD OFFERS IT SO PLAINLY: THE HISTORY OF RIGHTS AND RESTRICTIONS GIVES THE CHAIN — WHO HELD THE PARCEL, WHEN IT CHANGED HANDS, AND WHAT ENCUMBRANCES SAT ON IT OVER TIME. A COMMUNITY THAT SUSPECTS LAND WAS QUIETLY TRANSFERRED BEFORE A SCHEME APPEARED CAN ESTABLISH THAT FROM A PHONE, and a dated official history is evidence no meeting minute can match. THE FOURTH IS QUIETLY USEFUL TOO: A CERTIFICATE OF HAVING OR NOT HAVING RIGHTS. That is how you prove a person or company does NOT hold what they claim to hold — the negative is as provable as the positive. REGISTRATION ITSELF IS FASTER AND CHEAPER THAN ALMOST ANYWHERE ELSE RECORDED HERE: AN APPLICATION IS CONSIDERED WITHIN FIVE WORKING HOURS OF BEING REGISTERED AT THE LOCAL BRANCH, at a published fee of roughly a thousand soms, AND THERE IS A PUBLISHED TELEPHONE NUMBER TO CALL IF AN APPLICATION IS SUSPENDED FOR MISSING DOCUMENTS. A HOUSEHOLD THAT HAS NEVER REGISTERED ITS RIGHTS HAS NO GOOD REASON NOT TO. AND THE LEGAL DEFINITION REACHES FURTHER THAN PEOPLE EXPECT, WHICH MATTERS ENORMOUSLY FOR THIS MAP: IMMOVABLE PROPERTY INCLUDES LAND PLOTS, SUBSOIL PLOTS, ISOLATED WATER BODIES, AND EVERYTHING FIRMLY CONNECTED WITH THE LAND — EXPRESSLY INCLUDING FORESTS AND PERENNIAL PLANTINGS. ORCHARDS AND WOODLAND ARE PART OF THE REGISTERED UNIT, NOT SCENERY SITTING ON TOP OF IT. This file has spent rounds on trees that belong to no forest and enjoy no protection; here, established plantings are inside the property itself, and damage to them is damage to registered property. KNOW THE SYSTEM'S OWN DOCUMENTS WHEN ASKING: THE CADASTRAL PLAN, THE REGISTRATION MAPS, THE REGISTRATION CARD, THE REGISTRATION FILE, AND THE JOURNAL OF APPLICATIONS FOR STATE REGISTRATION. THAT LAST ONE IS WORTH ASKING ABOUT SEPARATELY — A JOURNAL OF APPLICATIONS SHOWS WHAT IS BEING APPLIED FOR NOW, not only what has already been decided. THE LIMITS: this is a records and registration agency, not an advocate — it reports what is registered and will not say whether it is right, and challenging an entry is a separate matter for the courts and the legal aid routes recorded separately here. Electronic access requires a personal account on the state portal. Fees and processing times change; the figures here were current when recorded.

trackers.name: Friends of the Earth Asia Pacific
trackers.desc: The Asia Pacific regional structure of Friends of the Earth International, formed in 2008, whose member groups work on community-based struggles against destructive projects, particularly mining and other extractive industries, alongside Indigenous peoples, peasant farmers, fisherfolk and trade unions. WHO TO ENLIST: the national member group nearest the project. In this region Friends of the Earth International's own directory names groups in Bangladesh (BELA, the Bangladesh Environmental Lawyers' Association), India, Indonesia (WALHI), Japan, Malaysia (Sahabat Alam Malaysia), Nepal, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines (the Legal Rights and Natural Resources Center), South Korea and Sri Lanka. You CAN: reach an organisation that already works community-side in your own country, and draw regional weight onto a local fight. For activists: in several of these countries the Friends of the Earth affiliate is the most experienced community-side environmental body there is.

trackers.name: Center for Investigative Journalism, Nepal
trackers.desc: Nepal's investigative-journalism center reporting on corruption, kleptocracy and public accountability.

trackers.name: Bolpatra (PPMO e-GP)
trackers.desc: Nepal's electronic government-procurement system. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Nepal, and for how much.

trackers.name: PPMO e-GP (Bolpatra)
trackers.desc: National public-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Nepal, and for how much.

trackers.name: Commission for the Investigation of Abuse of Authority (CIAA)
trackers.desc: Nepal’s constitutional anti-corruption body — investigates and prosecutes abuse of public office and corruption.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Nepal
trackers.desc: Official Supreme Court site with judgments and the Nepal Kanoon Patrika law reports. · Find here: judgments and case information of the Supreme Court of Nepal.

trackers.name: National Information Commission (Nepal)
trackers.desc: Nepal's National Information Commission oversees the Right to Information Act 2007: it hears RTI appeals and complaints, penalises non-compliance and promotes proactive disclosure, publishing decisions, guidance and annual reports. USE IT: it can penalise a body that ignores a request, not merely order release.

trackers.name: Office of Company Registrar (OCR)
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings. Official company and business register of Nepal — incorporation records.

trackers.name: CFUG handover — the operational plan is a contract, so write it carefully
trackers.desc: HOW A NEPALI COMMUNITY GETS FOREST HANDED OVER TO IT. Under the Forest Act 1993 and Forest Regulations 1995, a Community Forest User Group forms democratically from individuals representing households and registers at the forest office; writes a CFUG constitution defining the rights of users to a particular forest; elects an executive committee that by law must include 33 percent female members; and prepares an operational plan — a forest working plan based partly on a forest resource inventory, typically covering 5 years — for approval by the District Forest Officer. The forest is handed over once that plan is approved. THE PLAN IS THE INSTRUMENT THAT MATTERS: it forms part of the contract between the CFUG and the government, covering growing stock, block division, silvicultural operations, conservation measures and provisions for harvesting, utilisation and sale. A community wanting to prevent a use should get that use excluded in the plan — because the plan is contractual, not advisory. SCALE: about 1.23 million of Nepal's 5.5 million forest hectares is community forest, held by more than 14,000 CFUGs, with several thousand groups awaiting certification.

trackers.name: Read your own constitution — and budget for up to 90 percent tax
trackers.desc: THREE THINGS A NEPALI CFUG MEMBER SHOULD KNOW. 1. THE TAX STRESS IS SEVERE. The Local Government Operation Act 2017 requires community forests to contribute 10 percent of product sales to the local Reserved Fund, and with other enforced and proposed taxes across all three tiers of government the total is estimated at up to 90 percent of a CFUG's annual transactions — FECOFUN, the national federation of community forestry users, has been protesting it. Build any plan against that, not against gross revenue. 2. CHECK WHICH OFFICE IS YOURS. Under the 2015 constitution forest is in the concurrent list, with community forestry the responsibility of local and provincial government; the Divisional Forest Office under the province approves operational plans and transfers forest rights, across 528 forest sub-divisions and 753 local bodies — and who approves is politically live, with CFUGs and local governments favouring local control and forest officers resisting. 3. GET AND READ YOUR CONSTITUTION AND OPERATIONAL PLAN. Research finds elites exercising power because they are more aware of legislation and better able to access information, while many members are hardly aware of their own constitutions and operational plans and do not know their rights. NOTE ALSO a recognised structural flaw: the Department of Forest is both regulator and provider of technical services, which analysts identify as creating conditions for rent seeking — so delays or charges from the same body that approves your plan are a known problem, not bad luck.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: Mother Nature Cambodia
trackers.desc: A youth-led Cambodian environmental rights movement, active since 2012, which stopped a Chinese-led hydroelectric dam threatening an Indigenous community in the Areng Valley and helped end the sand-export trade that was destroying the Koh Kong estuaries. Right Livelihood Award, 2023. It was deregistered as an NGO by the Ministry of Interior in 2017 and has continued without legal registration. CHECK YOU HAVE THE RIGHT ONE: a separate, government-aligned organisation using the same name was launched in 2025 — this entry is the original movement, at mothernaturecambodia.org. For activists: association carries real risk. Five members have been imprisoned since July 2024 on plotting and lese-majeste charges, bail refused by both the Appeal and Supreme Courts, and dozens more have been arrested since 2015.

trackers.name: National Audit Authority
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Cambodia, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: MoC Business Registration
trackers.desc: National — Ministry of Commerce business / company register of Cambodia. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Constitutional Council (Cambodia)
trackers.desc: Constitutional Council (Cambodia) — supreme court (Cambodia).

trackers.name: Cambodia — Ministry of Economy & Finance (MEF)
trackers.desc: National budget authority; administers financial & economic policy and the distribution & allocation of the national budget, Kingdom of Cambodia. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Cambodia.

trackers.name: Community Forest agreement — a written request starts it, 15 years runs it
trackers.desc: ESTABLISH WHICH MINISTRY HOLDS YOUR FOREST FIRST — Cambodian forest is state owned and split between the Forestry Administration under MAFF and the Ministry of Environment for protected areas, and a March 2016 reshuffle moved protected areas and nature preserves to the Environment ministry, so older guidance may name the wrong body. ON FA LAND: Sub-decree 79 (2003) under the 2002 Forestry Law gives any Cambodian community the right to establish a Community Forest on state public property. IT STARTS WITH A WRITTEN REQUEST from the local communities to the Forestry Administration, which then assesses their requirements and problems with the involvement of local authorities. The management committee is formed with help from the Commune Council and elected by secret ballot with at least two-thirds of members present at a public meeting. TWO DOCUMENTS GIVE YOU HARVESTING RIGHTS: a Community Forestry Agreement and a Community Forest Management Plan, both approved by the FA Cantonment. TERM: not more than 15 years from approval, extendable on monitoring and evaluation reports. KNOW YOUR secondary users — non-members who may still access the forest consistent with the plan — and note that royalties and premiums should be set after consultation with the community.

trackers.name: Community Protected Areas — you get management rights but not exclusion rights
trackers.desc: THE GAP THAT DECIDES WHETHER THIS ROUTE SOLVES YOUR PROBLEM. Inside Ministry of Environment protected areas, communities may agree to manage part of the area — but legal analysis finds CPA communities hold only partial land tenure: they can generally exercise access, use, withdrawal and management rights, but lack exclusion rights, the ability to keep outsiders from entering or using CPA land. So a CPA can manage a forest but cannot keep others out of it — if your threat is incursion by outsiders rather than your own community's use, this route does not by itself solve it. WATCH THE DROP-OFF: of 182 CPAs established across 31 protected areas, 141 hold a Prakas of recognition, only 39 have a signed management agreement and just 48 a completed management plan — recognition is common, real management authority is not. AND A 15-DAY DEADLINE: within 15 days of being elected the CPA committee must obtain a warrant of recognition from the Commune/Sangkat Chief to legitimise its leadership. OTHER VARIANTS EXIST: Community-Based Production Forest, Partnership Forestry where the commune council is the management body rather than a community committee, and Community Conservation Forestry with more limited use rights.

trackers.name: GEF Small Grants — a concept paper, and only shortlists get a reply
trackers.desc: MONEY THAT GOES DIRECTLY TO COMMUNITY ORGANISATIONS. GEF SGP has financed projects in Cambodia since 2005 through the UNDP country office, supporting nearly 218 grant projects, with grants up to USD 50,000 awarded competitively to local NGOs and community-based organisations. WHAT YOU SUBMIT FIRST IS A CONCEPT PAPER, not a full proposal — and only shortlisted proposals are contacted, so the concept paper is your entire first impression and silence is the normal outcome otherwise. THE ENTRY POINT IS A PERSON: contact the GEF SGP National Coordinator at UNDP Cambodia, Corner Sothearos & Sihanouk Blvd, Tonle Bassac, Phnom Penh, for guidelines — verify the current post-holder on UNDP's page rather than relying on a name recorded here, since individual officials move. BUDGET FOR A MATCH: SGP expects applicants to match funding with equivalent contributions, so this is not full cost recovery. WHAT SATISFIES THE MATCH — AND IT IS NOT ONLY CASH: UNDP's own wording is that the remaining funding may come from the organisation, community contribution and/or other donors, either monetary or in kind and services. Labour and in-kind contribution count, so budget them deliberately rather than assuming the match must be found in money — for a community group with no cash this is the difference between eligible and not. AND THE CEILING MOVES BY PHASE: recorded calls show USD 20,000 in an earlier round and up to USD 75,000 under Operational Phase 8, so verify the live call rather than relying on a fixed figure. Note too that Indigenous Peoples' community groups are named as eligible applicants in their own right alongside NGOs and CBOs — which matters given that the Community Protected Area route leaves communities without exclusion rights.

trackers.name: Check which landscape the call names — and the sub-grant route
trackers.desc: GEOGRAPHY IS THE FILTER THAT DECIDES ELIGIBILITY. Cambodian SGP calls target specific landscapes rather than the whole country — recorded examples include villages and districts inside and nearby the Central Cardamom Mountain National Park and biodiversity hotspots; the Stung Siem Reap Watershed in Siem Reap province; and Mekong River, Tonle Sap and coastal provinces under a blue economy stream running since July 2019 on community-based use of ocean and coastal resources. A strong project outside the named landscape does not qualify, so check the live call before investing time — the same trap this map records for Sri Lanka. A DEDICATED INDIGENOUS PEOPLES STREAM EXISTS: since June 2023, under the UNDP Climate Promise initiative, IPOs, local NGOs and CBOs working directly with indigenous communities in the forest and land use sector may apply — including for indigenous community-based ecotourism as an option that does not rely heavily on forest and land resources. AND IF YOU CANNOT WIN A DIRECT GRANT: REDD+ programmes in Cambodia support organisations which in turn sub-contract grants and further funds to local NGOs and small local initiatives — so being a sub-grantee of a larger programme holder is a real route for a group too small to apply directly.

trackers.name: Timor-Leste — SERVE, I.P. (Serviço de Registo e Verificação Empresarial)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the one-stop SERVE maintains the Companies Register, issues unique company numbers & commercial-registration certificates and licenses business activity, Timor-Leste. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Timor-Leste — Ministry of Finance
trackers.desc: National budget authority; prepares the state budget and publishes budget transparency & execution data, Timor-Leste. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Timor-Leste.

trackers.name: Ombudsman for Human Rights and Justice (Provedor) of Timor-Leste
trackers.desc: National institution of Timor-Leste that provides free legal representation and defends access to justice, fair-trial and due-process rights for people who cannot afford counsel.

trackers.name: Tara bandu — a customary law named in the statute's own definitions
trackers.desc: A CUSTOMARY PRACTICE DEFINED BY NAME IN NATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL LEGISLATION IS RARE. The Environmental Basic Law (Decree-Law No. 26/2012 of 4 July) defines tara bandu in Article 1 as ‘a custom that is part of the culture of Timor-Leste that regulates the relationship between humans and the environment’, recognising it as applicable under rituals-based local common law, intended to conserve and promote the environment. So a tara bandu is not an informal arrangement the state may choose to respect — it is an instrument the environmental law itself names. It is a ceremony enshrining customary law with state recognition, generally at the scale of the suco, the smallest administrative division, over several years, focused on forests and on relations among people — and it anchors participatory land use plans, including agreements on property boundaries, rules of engagement, and interdictions and sanctions. One ceremony can settle a boundary, set a rule and attach a sanction — three things most jurisdictions need three separate processes for. AND IT NOW REACHES THE SEA: coastal communities have applied tara bandu, traditionally terrestrial, to marine resource management, creating MPAs that often give seagrass and dugongs special protection.

trackers.name: Vila Maumeta — temporary closure by ceremony, and the statute that backs it
trackers.desc: A WORKED, DATED TEMPLATE. At Vila Maumeta on Ataúro Island, the community with the NGO Roman Luan and the government demarcated a Marine Protected Area by applying tara bandu rules for closures; the MPA was launched in September 2017. Communities set temporary closures of a marine or terrestrial area through a tara bandu ceremony — a periodic instrument renewed by ceremony, which is a different and often easier proposition than permanent designation. The same Ataúro communities went on to water conservation and permaculture. THE STATUTE THAT BACKS IT: Decree-Law No. 5/2016 establishing the National System of Protected Areas provides that classification of a protected area should take into account the uses and customs of Timor-Leste which do not contravene the Constitution — naming lisuk, ofatin lulik, lisane and tarabandu — with community leaders, traditional leaders and local communities in the involved and adjacent area engaged. Named customs, named participants. It also provides for communities participating actively in environmental impact evaluation carried out in or near the area and for programmes offering alternative income. Decree-Law No. 6/2020 adds the biodiversity framework, covering protection, rehabilitation and ex situ restoration and requiring active participation of all sectors of society. Regulation 2000/19 focuses on forests, coral reefs and mangroves.

trackers.name: GEF Small Grants Programme — up to US$50,000 direct to communities
trackers.desc: THE COMMUNITY-SCALE ROUTE. The GEF Small Grants Programme, running since 1992 and implemented by UNDP, reached 135 countries of 144 eligible in GEF-8, which secured US$135 million for the core programme with nearly US$1 million allocated to each participating country — a per-country floor, so the money is not competed for across borders. Grants of up to US$50,000 go directly to local communities, community-based organisations and other non-governmental groups. Focal areas: biodiversity, climate change, land degradation and sustainable forest management, international waters and chemicals. READ THE COUNTRY PROGRAMME STRATEGY FIRST — each country writes its own, emphasising particular themes and geographies, so global eligibility does not mean your region or theme is in scope. Under SGP 2.0 the implementing agency may be FAO or Conservation International rather than UNDP, and the host may be a national host institution rather than the UNDP country office — confirm which applies before addressing an application.

trackers.name: Transparency International Zimbabwe (TI Z)
trackers.desc: Transparency International's Zimbabwe chapter (accredited since 1996). Knowledge-driven anti-corruption CSO — legal aid, community journalism and trial observation, and monitoring of policy and legislation, with focus areas including land and mining corruption.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a pan-African feminist rapid-response fund with reach across all 54 African countries — small grants released quickly for unanticipated, time-critical situations rather than planned programme work, covering safety and protection needs when defenders are threatened and short windows for advocacy after an unexpected event. WHO IT SUITS: women's rights organisations, feminist collectives and movements in which women or gender-diverse people are the primary decision-makers. It does NOT fund individuals, and the action must be strategic, genuinely unanticipated, and completable in under three months. HOW IT DIFFERS: this is emergency money for a moment, not a budget for a campaign — decisions are fast and grants are modest.

trackers.name: PRAZ
trackers.desc: National public-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Zimbabwe, and for how much.

trackers.name: Southern Africa Litigation Centre (SALC)
trackers.desc: Johannesburg-based regional NGO that advances human rights, the rule of law and access to justice in Zimbabwe through strategic litigation, criminal-justice reform and capacity-strengthening of local lawyers and courts. SALC RESOURCES A LAWYER — IT DOES NOT REPLACE ONE. It provides technical and monetary support to local and regional lawyers and organisations litigating human rights and rule of law cases, working primarily through strategic litigation and capacity-strengthening support to lawyers and grassroots organisations. So the ask is not ‘please take my case’ but ‘please back my lawyer’ — come with a local lawyer or local organisation. It also trains human rights lawyers and facilitates networks across the region, so it is a route to finding counsel too. THE SECOND FORUM MOST PEOPLE MISS: SALC supports litigation in South African courts that advances human rights in the southern African region — so where your own courts are slow, captured or hostile, there may be another venue, and SALC is the body that supports using it. NAME THE RIGHT CLUSTER WHEN YOU APPROACH: its themes are criminal justice, civil and political rights, socio-economic rights, international criminal justice, business and human rights and equality rights — ‘environment’ is not one of them, so frame a land-defence case as business and human rights or socio-economic rights. Established 2005 in Johannesburg out of the International Bar Association and OSISA. It has also run open calls for small organisational development grants to emerging CBOs in Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia, Malawi, Zambia and Zimbabwe — periodic, so watch for them.

trackers.name: Zimbabwe Lawyers for Human Rights (ZLHR)
trackers.desc: Harare-based membership organisation of lawyers upholding the rule of law, separation of powers and the unimpeded administration of justice in Zimbabwe through strategic and anti-impunity litigation, monitoring of judicial intimidation and public-interest advocacy.

trackers.name: Zimbabwe Anti-Corruption Commission (ZACC)
trackers.desc: National anti-corruption body of Zimbabwe — investigates graft, financial crime and abuse of public office.

trackers.name: Zimbabwe — Registrar of Companies (DCIP / ZimConnect e-Services)
trackers.desc: National corporate registry; the Registrar of Companies under the Deeds, Companies & Intellectual Property (DCIP) office registers PLCs, PBCs & other entities under the Companies and Other Business Entities Act [24:31], via the official ZimConnect government e-services portal, Zimbabwe. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: ZimLII
trackers.desc: Zimbabwe Legal Information Institute: free judgments and legislation. · Find here: free Zimbabwean judgments and legislation (ZimLII / Laws.Africa).

trackers.name: SADC Protocol on Wildlife Conservation and Law Enforcement
trackers.desc: A REGIONAL TREATY WHOSE DEFINITIONS DO REAL WORK. The SADC Protocol on Wildlife Conservation and Law Enforcement (1999, in force 2003) defines ‘taking’ as hunting, killing, injuring, capturing, harassing, collecting, picking, uprooting, digging up, cutting, destruction and removal of any wildlife species. So clearing vegetation for a development is ‘taking’ under this definition, not merely site preparation — that reframing is the most useful thing here. It defines community based wildlife management as management by a community which has the right to manage the wildlife AND to receive the benefits from that management, giving a benefit-sharing argument a treaty source; and ‘conservation’ to include rehabilitation and restoration, so restoration sits inside the defined term. THE CROSS-BORDER HOOK: States Parties must cooperate to manage shared wildlife resources as well as any transfrontier effects of activities within their jurisdiction or control — a mine, dam or plantation whose effects cross a border engages a treaty duty on the state that authorised it. Article 4 objectives include enforcing wildlife laws within, between and among States Parties and facilitating community-based natural resources management. CHECK YOUR STATE HAS RATIFIED — the Protocol is legally binding only for countries that have signed and ratified it, and this entry does not assert that your state has. ON TFCAs: they encompass protected areas as well as multiple resource use areas, so they are not exclusion zones; a TFCA practitioners network founded September 2013 has membership open to all stakeholder groups. And SADC's own 2023–2033 TFCA programme names the marginalisation of communities living in and around protected areas as a problem it exists to address — quotable against the body that wrote it.

trackers.name: Zimbabwe Environmental Law Association — public interest lawyers who litigate for communities against mining, with a rights-violation hotline
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a public interest environmental law organisation that publishes a hotline for people whose environmental, economic, social or cultural rights have been violated or are about to be — +263 777 195 006 and +263 719 556 893. Formed in 2000 and constituted as a trust in 2001, it does impact litigation, not only advocacy — it puts its own lawyers on cases for communities rather than referring them elsewhere. Its programmes are organised around mining and extractives, land and natural resources, responsible investment and business, and local service delivery, which is the right shape for a community facing a concession rather than a factory. It also does conflict resolution and civic education, and it convenes and trains — so a community that is not yet in a dispute can get its people trained before one starts. WHO IT SUITS: its published strength is extractives — mining, lithium, minerals, and access to information about investment contracts, including Chinese investment contracts, and it has run work on community development agreements and on mediation mechanisms for the mining industry. If your fight is a mine, a quarry or a concession, this is the strongest single door in Zimbabwe. It is a smaller organisation than the national scale of the problem, so treat the hotline as a triage line rather than a guarantee of representation. Offices at 26B Seke Road, Hatfield, Harare; info@zela.org; +263 8677 010060. CAVEAT: no published intake criteria, means test or case-selection policy was found — unlike South Africa's law clinic, ZELA does not say in advance who qualifies, so make the first call short and factual: what is proposed, where, who is behind it, what stage it has reached. WHICH DESK TO ASK FOR: ZELA was formed in 2000 and legally constituted as a Trust in November 2001, and runs five programmes — Extractive Industries and Mining; Climate Change and Energy; Local Service Delivery; Land and Natural Resources; and Responsible Investments. Naming the programme when you approach an organisation this size gets you to a lawyer who already knows your sector. Its stated methods are public interest environmental litigation, investigative and evidence-based research, advocacy, legal education, COMMUNITY ORGANISING AND MOBILISING, institutional strengthening and CONFLICT RESOLUTION — so it will mediate as well as litigate, which matters where a case would take years. THE INSTRUMENT TO ASK ABOUT IF A MINE IS NEAR YOU: ZELA has analysed COMMUNITY SHARE OWNERSHIP TRUSTS (CSOTs) — the Zimbabwean vehicle through which a mining company is expected to place a shareholding or payment in trust for the host community — alongside the indigenisation legislation and the minerals revenue transparency initiative. Ask whether a CSOT exists for your district, who its trustees are, what the company actually paid in, and where that money went; a trust that exists on paper and pays nothing is a common outcome. ZELA holds observer status with the African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights, so a case that exhausts domestic remedies has a route onward, and it is based in Harare.

trackers.name: CAMPFIRE Association — the route by which a Zimbabwean district holds legal authority over its own wildlife, and the money that comes with it
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY, AND WHY IT IS ALSO A WAY OF HOLDING LAND: under the Communal Areas Management Programme for Indigenous Resources, rural district councils are granted Appropriate Authority — legal devolution of the rights to manage, use and benefit from wildlife — and, acting for the communities on communal land, sell safari operators access to that wildlife. Land that earns is land that is defended. The association reports the programme operating in 58 districts, with 23 rural district councils contributing to it, covering about 50,000 km² or roughly 12.7 per cent of the country, and touching 2.4 million people in an estimated 800,000 households; income comes principally from levies on 33 hunting safari operators and eight photographic operators. The first two councils received Appropriate Authority status in 1988. WHAT TO DO WITH THIS IF YOUR AREA IS UNDER PRESSURE: find out whether your district council holds Appropriate Authority, and if it does not, whether it has applied — a district with devolved authority over its wildlife has a revenue interest in refusing a land use that destroys habitat, and that converts a conservation argument into a council budget argument. The association works with the parks and wildlife authority and the local government ministry. THE ARGUMENT AGAINST IT, WHICH YOU SHOULD KNOW BEFORE RELYING ON IT: authority was devolved only to district councils, not to wards or villages, and independent studies of southern lowveld districts found the direct household benefits small — with councils criticised for excessive retention of the revenue generated — though households valued the infrastructure built with it. WHO IT SUITS: communal-area communities in wildlife districts, and ward councillors who want the district's own money argument on their side. CAVEATS: this is a national programme association working with government, not an advocacy or legal body — for litigation Zimbabwe's entry for the Zimbabwe Environmental Law Association is the one to use. Revenue depends on safari hunting, which is exposed to import bans and market shifts, and no intake route for a community approach was published.

trackers.name: Zimbabwe Homeless People's Federation and Dialogue on Shelter — savings collectives that turned into a fund, then into land and 5,000 built houses
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Zimbabwe Homeless People's Federation (ZHPF), constituted in December 1998 as a national network of women-based savings and credit collectives of the urban poor (men are not excluded), with Dialogue on Shelter for the Homeless in Zimbabwe Trust, registered April 1998, as its support NGO. It began among families in the holding camps people were dumped in after mass evictions from informal settlements. THE SEQUENCE IS WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT FROM THE OTHER FEDERATION ENTRIES IN THIS FILE: savings first, then a collectively held Urban Poor Fund (Gungano), then negotiation with councils, then land allocated to the federation itself and houses built on it. Reported delivery is roughly 5,000 housing units — including 512 at Victoria Falls, 233 at Crowborough in Harare and 150 at Kariba — with reach reported at more than 12,000 families across 73 of Zimbabwe's 92 councils. The Harare Slum Upgrading Programme, 2010–2016, was co-led by the federation, Dialogue on Shelter and Harare City Council, piloted at Dzivarasekwa Extension, where the council contributed exemption of approval fees, equipment and technical supervision alongside community contributions. Enumerations and settlement profiles were produced by residents — Dzivarasekwa, Mbare, Chinotimba — and used to show how long people had actually lived where they lived. Money you saved collectively is the only money in this file that buys land on your own terms. WHO IT SUITS: Zimbabwean urban households facing eviction, living in holding camps or unserviced settlements, or wanting a route to serviced land and title through a savings collective. CAVEATS: this is a slow route — progress has been minimal against the scale of need, regularisation is politically sensitive, and settlements have been tolerated or evicted according to shifting political allegiances; large projects here depended on foreign foundation grants. It builds housing; it does not litigate — for that, Zimbabwe's ZELA entry.

trackers.name: Legal Resources Foundation — free lawyers and paralegals in 25 offices across 9 of Zimbabwe's 10 provinces, and legal pamphlets in Shona and Ndebele
trackers.desc: WHERE TO GET FREE LEGAL HELP: the Legal Resources Foundation (LRF), which provides legal education and legal services so that disadvantaged people, particularly women, can assert their rights. THE COVERAGE IS THE POINT, and it is the widest recorded anywhere in this file: underprivileged people get FREE ADVICE AND HELP FROM LAWYERS AND PARALEGALS IN 25 OFFICES ACROSS 9 OF ZIMBABWE'S 10 PROVINCES, organised as provincial centres with district offices under them — a provincial centre manager coordinating four district offices is the documented pattern. Its practitioners list COMMUNITY AND CUSTOMARY LAND RIGHTS and ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE among their working areas, alongside inheritance, marriage and gender-based violence. THE PUBLICATIONS UNIT IS THE SECOND REASON IT IS HERE: LRF produces practical information on around 28 legal topics — including wills, the Declaration of Rights and birth certificates — in ENGLISH, SHONA AND NDEBELE, distributed through workshops, offices, partner networks and places people already go, such as HOSPITALS AND POLICE STATIONS; it also publishes law reports and textbooks for the profession. Putting plain-language rights pamphlets in the hospital waiting room reaches people who will never enter a law office — the same logic as Malawi siting its legal aid desks inside the agriculture building. Offices in Harare at 5th Floor Blue Ridge, Eastgate, Sam Nujoma Street/Robert Mugabe Road, and 16 Oxford Road, Avondale. It also trains community leaders, teachers and prison officers as multipliers. Alongside it, Zimbabwe's justice ministry runs a Legal Aid Directorate providing advice and representation to indigents in civil and criminal litigation, and the Midlands State University Legal Aid Clinic offers free civil litigation and consultations subject to a means test. WHO IT SUITS: Zimbabweans anywhere outside the capital who need free legal advice, including on customary land and inheritance. CAVEATS: LRF'S OWN SITE DID NOT RESOLVE TO A VERIFIED PAGE — this entry points at a directory record documenting it; it is a generalist legal aid and education body, not an environmental litigator. For mining and environmental cases, Zimbabwe's ZELA entry; for wildlife devolution, CAMPFIRE.

trackers.name: AZTREC, Masvingo — a grassroots conservation body made up of chiefs, spirit mediums, war veterans and villagers, which elects ordinary members as chairperson, plus the Zimbabwe environmental NGO directory
trackers.desc: THE ORGANISATION MADE OF CHIEFS AND SPIRIT MEDIUMS — which matters because in Zimbabwe traditional authority holds real standing over land, and this file had no route through it: the ASSOCIATION OF ZIMBABWE TRADITIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL CONSERVATIONISTS (AZTREC), BASED IN MASVINGO PROVINCE in southern Zimbabwe, A POWERFUL GRASSROOTS ENVIRONMENTAL FORCE COMPOSED OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLE, TRIBAL CHIEFS, SPIRIT MEDIUMS AND CONSERVATIONISTS, whose founding came out of the liberation struggle and a second struggle described as THE LIBERATION OF CREATION. ITS PHILOSOPHY IS GROUNDED IN THE REVITALISATION OF INDIGENOUS KNOWLEDGE AND CULTURAL TRADITIONS, AND ITS ACTIVITIES RANGE FROM IMPROVING THE SITUATION OF WOMEN IN RURAL SOCIETY TO ADVOCATING SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT OF NATURAL RESOURCES; its main objective is recorded as REVIVING CULTURAL NORMS AND VALUES, PARTICULARLY TRADITIONAL FARMING PRACTICES, WHILE PROMOTING ENVIRONMENTAL CONSERVATION AND RESPECT FOR MOTHER EARTH. An organisation whose members include the chiefs and the spirit mediums is one that can convene the people whose word settles a land question in a Zimbabwean village. Bring your case to the traditional authority THROUGH a body they already belong to, rather than approaching them cold. AND ITS MEMBERSHIP IS OPEN IN A WAY THAT MATTERS: AZTREC INCLUDED SPIRIT MEDIUMS, CHIEFS, WAR VETERANS AND ORDINARY PEOPLE — one member records that she was approached at her WOMEN'S CLUB, chosen to represent it in the organisation, attended the meetings and workshops, AND WAS EVENTUALLY ELECTED AS CHAIRPERSON OF THE ORGANISATION. A rural women's club member became chairperson of the whole association. That is what an open membership structure actually produces — ask whether your women's club or village group can be represented, because representation is the route to the chair. WHERE TO FIND THE REST: A PUBLISHED DIRECTORY OF ENVIRONMENTAL NGOs OPERATING ACROSS ZIMBABWE (ecohubmap.com) lists organisations by country, naming among others AN ALL-FEMALE ANTI-POACHING UNIT working through community-based conservation strategies, and the GO GREEN ASSOCIATION OF ZIMBABWE, which empowers communities to engage in environmental stewardship. A country directory is the cheapest first step — search it for your province before writing to anyone in Harare. AND ON THE LEGAL SIDE, WORTH KNOWING WHAT IS COMING: ZELA'S EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR SAT ON A PANEL ON THE ESTABLISHMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL COURTS, at a regional dialogue attended by Zimbabwe, Kenya, South Africa and Senegal, on strengthening environmental law for thriving communities — with SPECIALISED ENVIRONMENTAL COURTS OR TRIBUNALS named as one of the ways of doing it. ZELA also COORDINATES THE PUBLISH WHAT YOU PAY COALITION and has chaired the ALTERNATIVE MINING INDABA and the KIMBERLEY PROCESS CIVIL SOCIETY COALITION, and trains media practitioners on profiling environmental human rights defenders. An organisation that chairs the Alternative Mining Indaba can put a community's case in front of the whole regional mining sector once a year. WHO IT SUITS: Zimbabwean rural communities, women's clubs, and anyone whose land question runs through a chief. CAVEATS: PARTS OF THIS RECORD ARE HISTORICAL — confirm AZTREC's current activity. For public interest environmental litigation, Zimbabwe's ZELA entry; for the CAMPFIRE route to a share of wildlife revenue, the CAMPFIRE Association entry; for land through savings schemes, the Homeless People's Federation entry; for free lawyers and paralegals, the Legal Resources Foundation entry.

trackers.name: ZERO Regional Environment Organisation, Harare — a 1987 land organisation naming the landless and resettled among its constituencies, plus ZELA's trust deed number, street address and research arm
trackers.desc: THE ORGANISATION FOR PEOPLE WHO WERE MOVED: ZERO REGIONAL ENVIRONMENT ORGANIZATION IS A NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATION ESTABLISHED IN 1987, AT 158 FIFE AVENUE, GREENWOOD PARK, PO BOX 5338, HARARE, aimed at MAKING STRATEGIC CONTRIBUTIONS TOWARDS EQUITABLE DISTRIBUTION AND EFFECTIVE MANAGEMENT OF LAND AND LAND-BASED RESOURCES WITHIN SOUTHERN AFRICA — with the more specific goal TO INFORM THE PROCESS OF FORMULATING AND IMPLEMENTING LAND POLICIES THAT ARE SENSITIVE TO THE NEEDS OF DISADVANTAGED RURAL COMMUNITIES, PAYING PARTICULAR ATTENTION TO WOMEN. ITS NAMED CONSTITUENCIES ARE THE POINT: RURAL COMMUNITIES, RURAL WOMEN, AGRICULTURE WORKERS, FARMERS, FISHERS, FOREST USERS AND DWELLERS, INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND ETHNIC MINORITIES, THE LANDLESS, PEASANTS AND RESETTLED PEOPLE. The LANDLESS and the RESETTLED are named as constituencies in their own right. Almost nothing else in this file speaks to people who have ALREADY lost land rather than people trying to keep it — if your community was moved and is still without secure tenure where it was put, that is the organisation whose stated constituency you are. HOW IT WORKS, AND THE FIRST TWO ARE WHAT A COMMUNITY CAN USE: APPLIED RESEARCH; PARTICIPATORY POLICY ADVOCACY; CAPACITY BUILDING; INFORMATION SHARING AND NETWORKING; AND BUILDING COLLABORATION AND PARTNERSHIPS AMONG VARIOUS STAKEHOLDERS. Participatory policy advocacy means the community is in the advocacy, not represented by it. Ask ZERO what participation means in practice before you agree to be researched. THE STANDARD IT WORKS TO, WORTH QUOTING BACK AT ANY EVICTION: RESPECT, PROTECT AND STRENGTHEN THE LAND RIGHTS OF WOMEN AND MEN LIVING IN POVERTY, ENSURING THAT NO ONE IS DEPRIVED OF THE USE AND CONTROL OF THE LAND ON WHICH THEIR WELL-BEING AND HUMAN DIGNITY DEPEND, INCLUDING THROUGH EVICTION, EXPULSION OR EXCLUSION, AND WITH COMPULSORY CHANGES TO TENURE UNDERTAKEN ONLY IN LINE WITH INTERNATIONAL LAW AND STANDARDS ON HUMAN RIGHTS — AND ENABLE THE ROLE OF LOCAL LAND USERS IN TERRITORIAL AND ECOSYSTEM MANAGEMENT, RECOGNISING THAT STEWARDSHIP IS BEST ACHIEVED THROUGH PARTICIPATORY DECISION-MAKING AND MANAGEMENT AT THE TERRITORIAL LEVEL. Eviction, expulsion AND exclusion are named as three separate ways of being deprived. Exclusion is the quiet one — you keep the title and lose the access — and it is the form most projects in this file actually take. AND THE INCORPORATION DETAIL FOR THE COUNTRY'S ENVIRONMENTAL LAW GROUP, WHICH IS THE TEMPLATE FOR HOLDING ASSETS: ZELA WAS FORMED IN 2000 AND LEGALLY CONSTITUTED AS A TRUST IN NOVEMBER 2001 UNDER NOTARIAL DEED OF TRUST MA1669/2001, at 26B SEKE ROAD, HATFIELD, HARARE, telephone (+263) 08677010060, email published. A notarial deed of trust with its number printed is the Zimbabwean vehicle for an organisation that must outlive its founders and hold property. If your association needs to own anything, that is the form to ask a lawyer about — and ZELA's own deed number is the worked example. ZELA UNDERTAKES RESEARCH THROUGH ITS OWN ARM, THE AFRICA INSTITUTE OF ENVIRONMENTAL LAW, WHOSE MANDATE IS TO GENERATE CREDIBLE, ANALYTICAL AND EVIDENCE-BASED INFORMATION, and its methods include CONFLICT RESOLUTION alongside impact litigation and civic education; it has published guidance under a project on STRENGTHENING COMMUNITY LAND RIGHTS AND RESPONSES TO INVOLUNTARY DISPLACEMENTS CAUSED BY DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS IN ZIMBABWE, HIGHLIGHTING CRITICAL AREAS TO BE ACCOUNTED FOR BEFORE INTRODUCING LARGE SCALE DEVELOPMENTAL PROJECTS, and has analysed COMMUNITY SHARE OWNERSHIP SCHEMES. A published guide on what to account for BEFORE a large project arrives is the document to get hold of while you still have time. Ask ZELA for it by name, and ask the Institute what its research shows about the company approaching you. WHO IT SUITS: Zimbabwean resettled and landless communities, rural women, and any association that needs to hold property. CAVEATS: A RESEARCH AND ADVOCACY BODY AND A PUBLIC INTEREST LAW GROUP. For chiefs and spirit mediums in one association, Zimbabwe's AZTREC entry; for the CAMPFIRE route to wildlife revenue, the CAMPFIRE Association entry; for land through savings schemes, the Homeless People's Federation entry; for free lawyers and paralegals, the Legal Resources Foundation entry.

trackers.name: The Urban Poor Fund International — capital for national community funds in nine African countries, held so communities negotiate with government and banks from a position of liquidity — and the Gungano loan fund still running after two decades
trackers.desc: MONEY THE COMMUNITY CONTROLS BEFORE IT NEGOTIATES — and the fund states the reasoning itself: THE URBAN POOR FUND INTERNATIONAL IS THE FINANCE FACILITY OF THE SLUM DWELLERS NETWORK AND PROVIDES CAPITAL TO NATIONAL URBAN POOR FUNDS AFFILIATED TO IT — FOUNDED ON THE PROPOSITION THAT THE POOR ARE CENTRAL ACTORS IN URBAN DEVELOPMENT AND ARE BEST ABLE TO DECIDE AND CO-MANAGE THEIR OWN IMPROVEMENT PROGRAMMES, BECAUSE GIVING THE POOR DIRECT CONTROL OF CAPITAL ENABLES THEM TO NEGOTIATE WITH FORMAL BODIES SUCH AS GOVERNMENT AND BANKS. DIRECT CONTROL OF CAPITAL as the point of the fund, not the outcome of it. A community that already holds money is negotiating; a community waiting for money is petitioning. That is the whole argument, and this file has watched it play out from the other side in every entry where a project arrived with financing and a village arrived with none. THE BRIDGING FUNCTION, STATED PLAINLY AND WORTH KNOWING BEFORE YOU SIGN ANY GOVERNMENT DEAL: WHEN FEDERATIONS STRIKE DEALS AT THE NATIONAL LEVEL, IT CAN TAKE TIME TO RECEIVE FUNDS FROM GOVERNMENT, OR CERTAIN REGULATIONS MAY HOLD UP PROJECT IMPLEMENTATION — THE FUND CAN HELP BRIDGE THIS GAP, STRENGTHENING THE HAND OF THE FEDERATIONS IN THESE NEGOTIATIONS, AND THE AUTONOMY OF AFFILIATES IS ENHANCED BY ITS LIQUIDITY. The government agrees, and then the money takes a year. Every community that has won something in this file has met that delay, and it is where agreements quietly die. A bridging fund is the specific answer: it lets you start while the state catches up, which also means the state cannot use the delay against you. WHERE IT REACHES IN AFRICA: SINCE ITS INCEPTION IN 2007 IT HAS PROVIDED GRANTS AND LOANS TO NAMIBIA, SOUTH AFRICA, ZIMBABWE, MALAWI AND ZAMBIA IN SOUTHERN AFRICA; KENYA, UGANDA AND TANZANIA IN EAST AFRICA; AND GHANA IN WEST AFRICA. Nine African countries with a national community fund already capitalised. Before founding anything, ask whether your country has one — and if it does, ask what it lends for and at what rate. THE ZIMBABWEAN EXAMPLE, STILL RUNNING: A GUNGANO URBAN POOR LOAN FUND WAS CREATED IN 1999 BY THE NATIONAL HOMELESS PEOPLE'S FEDERATION AND IS STILL HELPING TO UPGRADE INFORMAL SETTLEMENTS OVER TWO DECADES ON — SUPPORTED BY A NAMED LOCAL SHELTER TRUST, BY HARARE CITY FUNDS, AND BY A LIST OF INTERNATIONAL FUNDERS. HARARE CITY FUNDS is the detail to notice: the municipality itself put money into a fund the residents run. That is a further step beyond an MOU — not the city building for you, the city lending to the fund you control. Twenty-five years and still lending is the durability test, and this one passed it. THE SOUTH AFRICAN FUND'S OWN DESCRIPTION IS THE MODEL TO COPY: IT IS NOT A HOUSING DELIVERY AGENCY — IT SUPPORTS SUSTAINABLE USES OF BROADER ASSET MOBILISATION, BLENDING LOANS, SAVINGS, AND SOCIAL CAPITAL, AND LINKING ALL THIS TO THE STATE HOUSING SUBSIDY SYSTEM — AND IT IS DESCRIBED AS A PIONEER IN TENURE SECURITY, INCREMENTAL HOUSING DEVELOPMENT, HOUSING FINANCE INNOVATION AND THE CREATIVE UTILISATION OF POLICY AND SUBSIDY INSTRUMENTS BY BUILDING PRAGMATIC PARTNERSHIPS WITH GOVERNMENT.
