trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Publicly searchable.

trackers.name: Guyana — Ministry of Finance
trackers.desc: National budget authority; the Office of the Budget prepares & monitors the national budget and publishes budget speeches & estimates, Guyana. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Guyana.

trackers.name: Audit Office
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Guyana, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Caribbean Court of Justice (CCJ)
trackers.desc: YOUR FINAL COURT OF APPEAL — this is one of only 5 states that have acceded to the CCJ's Appellate Jurisdiction, replacing the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council for civil and criminal appeals: Barbados, Belize, Dominica, Guyana and Saint Lucia. Everywhere else in the Eastern Caribbean the final court remains the Privy Council, so do not assume the CCJ is your appeal route from a neighbouring jurisdiction's practice. BE CLEAR WHAT THE OTHER JURISDICTION DOES NOT COVER: in its Original Jurisdiction the CCJ interprets the Revised Treaty of Chaguaramas on freedom of movement of people, goods, services, capital and the right of establishment — it does not extend to human rights generally, and it is not an environmental forum. A land-defence claim does not fit there unless it has a cross-border economic dimension, such as a project licensed to a company from another CARICOM state. WHERE IT DOES FIT, INDIVIDUALS CAN GET IN: under Article 222 a natural or juridical person may seek special leave, granted where the Treaty intended the right to enure to the benefit of individuals, the applicant has been prejudiced, and the member state entitled to espouse the claim omitted or declined to. 35 such cases have been brought, so the route is used rather than theoretical — Trinidad Cement Ltd v Republic of Guyana [2009] CCJ 1 (OJ) established that individuals and companies can use the Treaty to make their own state comply. The Court sits as a court of first instance there, its rulings immediately binding in international law, and hearings are broadcast live.

trackers.name: Protected Areas Commission — Kanashen kept title AND management authority
trackers.desc: THE SEQUENCE IS THE MODEL. The Kanashen Village Council received absolute title to its lands in 2004; in 2007 the Wai Wai designated that land a Community Owned Conservation Area under the Amerindian Act 2006, a decision they took themselves against threats including gold mining and language loss; in 2013 the Village applied to the Protected Areas Commission for recognition as a National Protected Area, and PAC worked with them on a management plan and a joint application to Government; it was gazetted in 2017 as Guyana's first and so far only Amerindian Protected Area, about 648,567 hectares — roughly 3 percent of the country. THE KANASHEN VILLAGE COUNCIL IS THE MANAGEMENT AUTHORITY; PAC provides technical support, not control. Title first, self-designation second, state recognition third — and the council keeps management authority. The Protected Areas Act also allows the system to include approved privately managed protected areas. ASK WHO IS DRAFTING YOUR REQUEST: Cultural Survival reported in 2010 that southern Guyana projects met resistance from the Makushi and Wapishana because land rights were unaddressed and consultation was ‘deficient to non-existent’, and that the origin of a Wai Wai letter requesting protected status had been suspect — reporting that predates the 2017 gazettal under which the Council holds title. Both belong in the record.

trackers.name: Protected Areas Trust — and it funds a community-owned area
trackers.desc: A NATIONAL ENDOWMENT THAT FUNDS COMMUNITY-OWNED LAND — which is the point: community ownership does not put you outside the national financing system. Established as a corporate body under the Protected Areas Act 2011 to co-finance management of the National Protected Areas System, it is a true endowment: capital is preserved and invested globally to earn annual returns of approximately 5 percent, with revenues funding conservation projects. It co-finances Kaieteur National Park, the Kanuku Mountains and coastal Shell Beach — and expressly supports the Kanashen community-owned protected area. FUNDING HISTORY: EUR 4 million (US$5m) from the German government through KfW under the ‘Conservation of Tropical Forests’ agreement of 10 September 2009. ONE SMALL ITEM WORTH COPYING: a US$15,000 donation in 2016 financed logistics for final consultations between Kanashen Village and the Commission on integrating the Wai Wai territory into the system. Consultation logistics are a fundable line item — useful when costing a community process, where travel to remote villages is often the real barrier. Conservation International Guyana separately funded the Trust's own institutional strengthening and fundraising under a grant of 23 March 2017.

trackers.name: Environmental Defenders Office — Pasifika Program
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the largest environmental legal centre in the Australia-Pacific region, whose Pasifika-led programme works on extractive industries, forestry, marine protection and climate across Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands, Fiji, Vanuatu and Tuvalu. WHO IT SUITS: an in-country organisation rather than an individual — EDO works predominantly through partner organisations (CELCOR in PNG, the Landowners Advocacy and Legal Support Unit and the Solomon Islands Environmental Law Association, the Fiji Environmental Law Association and the Vanuatu Environmental Law Association), supplying strategic legal capacity, co-authored law-reform papers and litigation support. Approach your national environmental law association first; its free advice hotline is for Australia only. YOUR NATIONAL PARTNER IS the Vanuatu Environmental Law Association. EDO is an Australian organisation based in Sydney, and its Pasifika Program is Pasifika-led — including diaspora Pasifika lawyers with cultural and spiritual links to the region — working predominantly through partner organisations. So the partner is the front door and EDO is the legal capacity behind it. Focus areas: climate change, threats to marine environments, forestry and mining. EDO is an accredited community legal service with a community advice hotline, the largest environmental legal centre in the Australia-Pacific, and records a historic Solomon Islands bauxite mine case. REACH IS LIMITED AND STATED: EDO names PNG, Solomon Islands, Fiji and Vanuatu, plus Tuvalu — it does not cover the other Pacific states, so do not assume regional coverage.

trackers.name: Vanuatu Environmental Law Association (VELA)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an association of ni-Vanuatu lawyers formed to protect Vanuatu's environment through the legal system, and one of the Environmental Defenders Office's named Pacific partners — the EDO channels strategic legal capacity and law-reform work through it rather than acting directly in Vanuatu. It has been a Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund grantee for organisational strengthening and has run community legal-awareness work alongside the Fiji and Solomon Islands associations. WHO IT SUITS: a Vanuatu community or custom landowning group facing a development, logging or coastal decision — this is a small association of practising professionals, not a staffed legal-aid office, so expect referral to a member lawyer rather than intake. Domain unverified: reachable through the partner list on the Environmental Defenders Office's own site (edo.org.au/our-work), and named by Vanuatu's Department of Environmental Protection and Conservation at environment.gov.vu. VELA has no website of its own; the link is the Pacific Islands Climate Action Network member directory, which lists it as a non-government, not-for-profit public interest environmental law organisation. It is also a named Pacific partner of the Australian Environmental Defenders Office, which delivers joint legal work with its partners — so an approach through EDO is a second route in.

trackers.name: Vanuatu Environmental Advocacy Network (VEAN)
trackers.desc: The Vanuatu Environmental Advocacy Network — a national network of environmental civil-society organisations, named by Vanuatu's Department of Environmental Protection and Conservation as a Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund grantee receiving support to strengthen its capacity for biodiversity work. For activists: the non-legal counterpart to the Vanuatu Environmental Law Association, and the likelier first call for finding out who else is already working on a site. Domain unverified: named on the Vanuatu government's own environment department site, environment.gov.vu. No website or directory listing could be verified for VEAN, so none is given rather than guessing one. It is active: the Vanuatu Department of Environmental Protection and Conservation records VEAN and VELA as recipients of CEPF small grants administered by IUCN Oceania, to strengthen their organisations for biodiversity work. USE IT: reach VEAN through the Department, through IUCN Oceania's CEPF programme, or through VELA.
trackers.noWebsite: no website or directory listing found; verified as active through the Vanuatu Department of Environmental Protection and Conservation and IUCN Oceania

trackers.name: Vanuatu — Department of Finance & Treasury (MFEM)
trackers.desc: National budget authority; the Treasury Division’s Budget Section prepares the Budget Policy Statement and national budget, Vanuatu. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Vanuatu.

trackers.name: PacLII – Vanuatu
trackers.desc: Free case law and legislation for Vanuatu via the Pacific Islands Legal Information Institute. · Find here: free Vanuatu legislation and court decisions, hosted by PacLII.

trackers.name: VFSC Company Registry
trackers.desc: National — Vanuatu Financial Services Commission online company registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: SPREP — three conventions, and 26 members is not 12 parties
trackers.desc: THE REGIONAL BODY FOR PACIFIC ENVIRONMENT, AND IT IS SECRETARIAT TO THREE CONVENTIONS. SPREP is an independent intergovernmental organisation, autonomous since the Agreement Establishing SPREP was signed at Apia on 16 June 1993, with the Article 2 purpose of providing assistance to protect and improve the environment and ensure sustainable development for present and future generations. It has 26 members — 14 Pacific island countries, 7 territories and 5 metropolitan states — and is headquartered in Apia, Samoa. ESTABLISH WHICH CONVENTION FITS YOUR ISSUE: the Noumea Convention (1986, in force 1990), described by UNEP as the only comprehensive multilateral umbrella agreement for protection of natural resources and environment in the region; the Waigani Convention on hazardous and radioactive waste imports; and the Apia Convention on nature conservation. THE NOUMEA CONVENTION IS UNDER ACTIVE REVIEW — WHICH IS AN OPENING: a 2021 Review produced recommendations now being implemented through a Noumea Workplan and Budget whose stated aim is to elevate the work of the Convention and enhance awareness and implementation, with a Communications Plan and a Finance Strategy named as critical. BUT CHECK WHETHER YOUR STATE IS A PARTY: SPREP has 26 members while the Noumea Convention has only 12 contracting parties — membership and party status are different things, and this entry does not assert the latter. GOVERNANCE POINT WORTH KNOWING: the SPREP Meeting is the plenary decision-making body; the Executive Board (established 2015) is subordinate to it and has no power to make decisions requiring input of all Members — so a decision affecting all members must go to the Meeting. IF YOUR ISSUE IS SEABED MINING: UNEP records deep sea mining as an emerging contentious issue the region is dealing with — the regional body has already named it. SPREP is also developing a portal for protected areas managers. THERE IS A SPREP PRESENCE IN YOUR COUNTRY: beyond Apia, host country agreements exist with the Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, the Marshall Islands, Solomon Islands and Vanuatu — so you need not approach Samoa first.

trackers.name: Pacific Development and Conservation Trust — citizens may apply
trackers.desc: AN INDIVIDUAL CAN APPLY, AND THE FIRST DOCUMENT IS SHORT. The Pacific Development and Conservation Trust, administered through the New Zealand government's Community Matters service with requests assessed by Advisory Trustees, states that ‘citizens or organisations’ from eligible Pacific places may request funding — so no incorporated body is required, which removes the commonest barrier recorded across this map. THE PROCESS IS TWO-STAGE: submit an Expression of Interest; only successful applicants are invited to submit a full project application. Do not prepare a full proposal before the EOI is accepted — wasted work, and expensive wasted work where drafting means travelling. Applications must be on the current form with all sections completed, submitted online where connection allows. READ THE PUBLISHED GRANT RECORD BEFORE DRAFTING: the Trust publishes records of grants by round — 2020/21, 2021/22, 2022/23 (two rounds), 2023/24 and 2024/25 — showing what the Trustees have actually funded, at what size and in which countries. That is better evidence of what will succeed than any guidance note. UNDP SUPPORT HERE IS COUNTRY-LEVEL: UNDP's Pacific Office provides country support to this state, so an in-country office is a realistic second route alongside the Trust.

trackers.name: SPREP EIA and SEA guidelines — intervene at scoping, not after
trackers.desc: SCOPING IS WHERE STAKEHOLDER CONCERNS BECOME TERMS OF REFERENCE — and the guidelines say so themselves. Assessments must be individually customised to the aspects most relevant to stakeholders, and ‘customisation usually occurs during the scoping phase and results in the preparation of terms of reference’. Intervene at scoping and the assessment is required to examine your issue; intervene later and you are commenting on an assessment that was never asked to look. trackers.desc: KNOW WHICH OF THE FOUR DIVISIONS YOU NEED — it saves a week. Contact: Ministry compound, Nambatu, PMB 9063, Port Vila, (678) 25302 or 33430 — and there is a provincial presence at the Sanma Provincial Government Council, Luganville, which matters in an archipelago of about 80 islands: if you are on Santo, Sanma is closer than Port Vila. AND A WARNING FROM THE DEPARTMENT ITSELF: ‘beware of fake websites pretending to be official — official Vanuatu Government sites end with .gov.vu’.

trackers.name: In-depth Solomons
trackers.desc: In-depth Solomons — Non-profit investigative newsroom in the Solomon Islands (OCCRP member centre) exposing corruption, unexplained wealth of leaders, and abuses in logging and mining. — Independent watchdog of officials and public power.

trackers.name: Environmental Defenders Office — Pasifika Program

Approach your national environmental law association first; its free advice hotline is for Australia only. trackers.name: Public Solicitor's Office — Landowners Advocacy and Legal Support Unit (LALSU)

WHO IT SUITS: any Solomon Islander in need — eligibility is means-tested and weighs the nature of the problem, age and disability. PSO lawyers never charge; if one asks you for money, report it to the Public Solicitor.

trackers.name: Solomon Islands Environmental Law Association (SIELA)

WHO IT SUITS: customary landowners and community groups facing logging or mining licensing — SIELA is a professional network rather than a firm, so it is the route to a lawyer and to plain-language explanation of the law, not a service that will take your case itself. Domain unverified: reachable through the partner list on the Environmental Defenders Office's own site, edo.org.au/our-work. trackers.name: Solomon Islands — Ministry of Finance & Treasury (MoFT)
trackers.desc: National budget authority; prepares & manages the annual recurrent budget and advises on monetary, budget & fiscal policy, Solomon Islands. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in the Solomon Islands.

trackers.name: PacLII – Solomon Islands
trackers.desc: Free case law and legislation for Solomon Islands via the Pacific Islands Legal Information Institute. · Find here: free Solomon Islands legislation and court decisions, hosted by PacLII.

trackers.name: Solomon Islands Business Registry (Company Haus)

trackers.name: Environment & Conservation Division — three Acts, one desk, consultation open
trackers.desc: ONE SMALL DIVISION HOLDS DEVELOPMENT CONTROL, WILDLIFE AND PROTECTED AREAS TOGETHER — so a single approach can raise a species point, a protected-area point and a permit point at the same desk. The Environment and Conservation Division, established 1985 by Cabinet directive and given legal status under section 5 of the Environment Act 1998, administers three Acts — the Environment Act 1998 (development control, EIA and pollution control), the Wildlife Protection and Management Act 1998 with its 2008 Regulations (birds, reptiles, amphibians, mammals, insects, plants and marine organisms, and CITES compliance), and the Protected Areas Act 2010 — ‘despite its relatively small size’, in its own words, which also means it is stretched. A CONSULTATION IS OPEN ON THE STATUTE ITSELF: the Division records that it is reviewing the Environment (Amendment) Act 1998 and is now inviting submissions on the proposed amendments as part of a public consultation. trackers.name: Contraloría General de la República

HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Cuba — Ministerio de Finanzas y Precios (MFP)

trackers.name: Caribbean Biodiversity Fund (CBF)
trackers.desc: THE REGIONAL CARIBBEAN CONSERVATION FUND, established September 2012, managing roughly USD 70 million through two instruments — an Endowment Fund of about USD 43 million that is a permanent funding source to National Conservation Trust Funds, and the EbA Facility. APPLY TO YOUR NATIONAL FUND, NOT TO CBF, for the endowment stream: at national level the NCTFs lead the grantmaking process, with proceeds held in country-based subaccounts. The EbA Facility is the direct route, awarding through competitive calls for proposals — medium grants USD 250,000–1 million, large grants up to USD 2 million — scoped to the marine and coastal zone, so an inland project must show its connection there. Eligible recipients expressly include community-based organisations and non-registered citizen groups, alongside NGOs, government agencies and universities. CBF has supported the establishment of conservation trust funds in 8 countries, contributed to management of over 500 protected areas, and worked with over 50 local implementing partners. IF YOU ARE TOO SMALL FOR EbA: CBF partners with GEF SGP across 12 shared countries — the community-scale sibling route, recorded separately in this map. CUBA-SPECIFIC ROUTE: CBF partners with UNDP Cuba to channel funding through GEF SGP Cuba, so the practical door here is the GEF Small Grants Programme country office rather than a national conservation trust fund.

trackers.name: Ley 150/2022 — environmental damage now carries civil and criminal liability
trackers.desc: IF YOU ARE WORKING FROM LEY 81 MATERIAL, YOU ARE WORKING FROM THE OLD LIABILITY REGIME. Ley 150/2022 ‘Del Sistema de los Recursos Naturales y el Medio Ambiente’, approved 14 May 2022 and published in Gaceta Oficial No. 87 of 13 September 2023, defines the concept of environmental damage and establishes civil and criminal responsibility for those who cause it — a precision absent from Ley 81, which is described as having lacked clear mechanisms to hold infringers effectively responsible. It regulates the actions of the State, of citizens and of society in general. ACCOMPANYING MEASURES: restructuring of CITMA as governing body of environmental policy; Evaluación Ambiental Estratégica; and monitoring and continuous reporting on compliance. Strategic assessment applies to plans and programmes, not only projects — so a sectoral plan or investment programme is assessable in its own right. CITE THE CONSTITUTION TOGETHER WITH IT: Article 75 gives all persons the right to a healthy and balanced environment, tied to the survival, wellbeing and security of present and future generations; and Article 90(j) makes it a duty of citizens to protect natural resources and velar por la conservación of a healthy environment. That is a duty, not only a right — where individual standing is narrow, making a report discharges a constitutional obligation rather than asserting an interest.

trackers.name: Ley 81 art. 16 — local bodies can propose stricter local standards
trackers.desc: THE ROUTE THROUGH THE BODY YOU CAN ACTUALLY REACH. Article 16 of Ley 81 (11 July 1997) provides that los Órganos Locales del Poder Popular may propose to the competent bodies the establishment, in their respective territories and in attention to their particular situation, of environmental norms and parameters more rigorous or specific than the general ones. A local assembly can propose stricter standards than the national baseline, framed as responsive to local circumstances. The law also allows dirimir discrepancias between organs of government and whatever other declarations relating to specific areas, ecosystems or resources are needed to fulfil its objectives — a catch-all declaratory power. ASK WHICH OF THE ELEVEN INSTRUMENTS APPLIES: Title III lists environmental planning, ordenamiento ambiental, licencia ambiental, evaluación de impacto ambiental, the environmental information system, the sistema de inspección ambiental, education, research, economic regulation, the Fondo Nacional del Medio Ambiente, and the regimes of administrative, civil and criminal responsibility. Licence and inspection are separate instruments — an inspection is not a licensing act, and both generate documents. ADDRESS WILDLIFE TO THE RIGHT MINISTRY: protection of wild flora and fauna belongs to the Ministry of Agriculture and the Ministry of Fishing Industry, not CITMA. Article 8(h) covers preservation of cultural heritage associated with the natural setting.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: Ley 217 art. 20 — the money to pay owners must exist before the declaration
trackers.desc: THE STRONGEST ADVANCE-COMPENSATION PROVISION IN THIS MAP. Protected areas are declared by law, and article 20 of Ley 217 lists six things that must be taken into account before the declaratoria — including (5) the budget line to pay, in cash and in advance, the owners who would be affected, (2) a technical study covering biophysical, social and cultural conditions, and (6) the indigenous communities where the area is established on their lands. The appropriation must exist before the area is declared — so if a declaration is proposed over your land, ask which budget line covers point 5. Compare Lesotho, where late payment was a breach; here the money must be voted beforehand. ARTICLE 21: all activities in a protected area must conform to the plan de manejo approved by MARENA — and where an area has no management plan, activities run under the default regime, so the absence of a plan is itself worth checking. Article 18 objectives include protecting watersheds, hydrological cycles and aquifers and the surroundings of historical, archaeological and artistic monuments — a route where your site has heritage value. The law declares the environment patrimonio común de la nación, makes it the duty of the State and of all inhabitants to protect and restore, and requires the State to support indigenous communities of the Autonomous Regions, the Pacific or the Centre — not only the Caribbean coast.

trackers.name: Ley 445 — communal land, with or without title, and a fund to demarcate it
trackers.desc: ‘WITH OR WITHOUT REAL TITLE OF DOMAIN’ IS THE OPERATIVE PHRASE. Ley 445 defines communal land as a geographic area in possession of an indigenous or ethnic community with or without title — comprising inhabited land and the traditional scope of its social, economic and cultural activities, sacred places, forested areas for reproduction and multiplication of flora and fauna, boat construction, and subsistence hunting, fishing and agriculture. Possession founds the claim, and sacred sites and forest reproduction areas are named categories. THE CONSTITUTIONAL PROTECTION TO QUOTE: communal lands cannot be encumbered and are inembargables, inalienables e imprescriptibles — not attachable for debt, not alienable, not lost by lapse of time. THE PROCEDURE: article 41 creates CONADETI, which directs demarcation and rules on applications; you begin by filing with the corresponding CIDT. AND THERE IS A DEDICATED FUND FOR THE COST: a Fondo Nacional de Demarcación y Legalización de Tierras Comunales, administered by CONADETI under Finance Ministry supervision, for which CONADETI must render accounts. GOVERNANCE ON YOUR OWN TERMS: elections and removals of communal and territorial authorities follow the customs and traditional procedures of the communities (art. 6). AND THE COUNCILS OWE YOU A TRANSLATION: art. 67 requires the law to be translated and widely disseminated in the languages of the indigenous peoples. It covers the Atlantic Coast and the Coco, Bocay, Indio and Maíz river basins, and traces to the Harrison-Altamirano treaty of 1905.

trackers.name: 环境民事公益诉讼 — who may sue, and on what evidence
trackers.desc: THE STANDING TEST, FROM THE SUPREME PEOPLE'S COURT'S OWN INTERPRETATION (adopted 8 December 2014, in force 7 January 2015). Under Article 58 of the Environmental Protection Law a social organisation may sue over pollution or ecological destruction harming the public interest if it is registered with the civil affairs department of a government at or above the level of a city divided into districts, and has engaged specifically in environmental protection public interest activities continuously for more than 5 years with no record of violation. If those are met the court shall accept the case; the organisation must not seek economic benefit from the suit. WHAT THE TERMS MEAN: social groups, private non-enterprise units and foundations all count. YOUR CHARTER DECIDES WHAT YOU CAN SUE ABOUT — the test is met where the charter states that the purpose and main business scope is protecting the social public interest, and the public interest at stake in the suit must be related to that stated scope. ‘No violation record’ means no administrative or criminal penalty in the course of business in the 5 years before filing. HAVE THIS READY WHEN YOU FILE: registration certificate, charter, the annual work reports or annual inspection reports for the 5 consecutive years before suit, and a signed and stamped declaration of no violation record. Article 9 lets the court invite you to add claims such as ceasing the infringement and restoring the original state if what you asked for is too narrow to protect the public interest. THE LIMIT: this is the CIVIL route. Environmental administrative public interest litigation — challenging a government decision — can be brought only by the procuratorate, so a challenge to an approval must go through persuading it to act.

trackers.name: CEPF — Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund grants
trackers.desc: MONEY THAT REACHES SMALL GROUPS. CEPF funds civil society organisations of all sizes — farmers' cooperatives and community groups as much as universities and international NGOs. Small grants average about USD 15,000 and large grants about USD 150,000; in the Indo-Burma Phase IV call, which listed China among its eligible countries, small grants ran to USD 50,000 and large grants USD 50,000–250,000. ITS STATED PREFERENCES FAVOUR YOU: priority goes to projects showing a leading role for local organisations or building local civil society capacity, and to projects supporting Indigenous and local communities in community-based or co-management conservation — explicitly including actions that enhance local communities' tenure and resource use rights. Small grant applications in that call were accepted in Chinese and other regional languages, not only English. HARD CONDITIONS: your organisation needs its own bank account and must be able to receive charitable contributions under national law; the project must sit inside a biodiversity hotspot where CEPF currently works and support at least one strategic direction in that hotspot's ecosystem profile — read the profile before writing anything. Excluded: anything that could adversely affect critical habitat, introduce invasive non-indigenous species, or remove or alter tangible cultural heritage. CHECK THE CURRENT CALL: eligible countries are listed per call and windows are fixed — Indo-Burma Phase IV ran 2 February to 16 March 2026. Since 2000 CEPF has given over USD 300 million to more than 2,700 organisations across more than 112 countries.

trackers.name: 社会公益型保护地 — a 50-year management agreement instead of a purchase
trackers.desc: YOU CANNOT BUY THE LAND, SO YOU CONTRACT FOR IT. In 2011, with Sichuan provincial support, China's first civil nature reserve was created at Laohegou, Pingwu County — core giant panda habitat and a migration corridor that sat in no legally protected area system, with management limited to basic patrol and fire prevention while poaching, snaring and poison-fishing were common. THE MECHANISM: a 50-year entrusted management agreement (委托管理协议) with the county gave the Taohuayuan Foundation long-term management rights over three forest parcels within 110 km², with the foundation raising social funds and taking full responsibility for establishment, management and financing. YOU NEED A REGISTRABLE LOCAL ENTITY: a 民办非企业 private non-enterprise unit, the Pingwu Laohegou Nature Conservation Centre, was registered to run it. The model is described as more flexible than government reserves, able to work where government cannot, and able to bring collective and individual land into protection at relatively low cost — made possible by collective forest tenure reform. Recognised by the State Forestry Administration, it has been replicated at Bayuelin (Leshan, Sichuan) and Xicaohai (Heqing, Yunnan).

trackers.name: 保护地役权 and 社区协议保护 — easements and community agreements
trackers.desc: TWO CONTRACT ROUTES, WITH THEIR LIMITS STATED. Conservation easements (保护地役权): Qianjiangyuan National Park and others have piloted collective forest and moso bamboo easements, and Article 22 of the Hainan Tropical Rainforest National Park Regulations (Trial) expressly lets the park authority manage collectively owned natural resources through easement contracts. BUT LEGAL SCHOLARSHIP RECORDS REAL WEAKNESSES: subjects, rights, creation procedures and registration requirements differ widely between localities and lack internal consistency; practice is usually led by the protected-area authority or local government, emphasising public objectives with little attention to protecting private property rights; and some localities hold back over doubts about the legal basis under the Civil Code. Community conservation agreements (社区协议保护) follow a clear sequence: first establish who owns the resource and who can authorise — reserve authority for state reserves, the village for collective land; then mobilise, choosing communities with genuine willingness and organisational capacity; then negotiate and sign, drafting a conservation plan and a development plan together. At Longge village in Sanjiangyuan this took about 5 months of discussion and produced a cooperative joined by all 53 herding households. AND THE APPROACH THAT MADE IT WORK NEAR LAOHEGOU: the foundation did not start by policing hunters — it asked what the community's own grievance was, found it was outsiders digging medicinal herbs, and villagers amended their own 村规民约 to bar them. Only then did protection extend to wildlife, and the community accepted it.

trackers.name: Kuwait Regional Convention (ROPME) — and its Judicial Commission
trackers.desc: THE ONE BINDING ENVIRONMENTAL INSTRUMENT COVERING ALL EIGHT GULF STATES. The Kuwait Regional Convention for Cooperation on the Protection of the Marine Environment from Pollution was signed 24 April 1978 and entered into force 1 July 1979 — 30 articles, described as the basic legal instrument binding the eight States of the Region. ALL EIGHT ARE FULL PARTIES: ROPME records ‘no signatories without ratification, acceptance, approval or accession’, so unlike some regional instruments there is no signed-but-unratified state to argue about. ARTICLE II fixes the Sea Area by coordinates, from Ras Dharbat Ali (16°39'N, 53°3'30"E) to Ras Al Fasteh (25°04'N, 61°25'E) — a treaty boundary you can check a project location against. Use the term ‘ROPME Sea Area’: it was coined by the Plenipotentiaries to achieve unanimity, cooperating in spite of existing geopolitical boundaries, and it is the name all eight accepted. THE ORGAN MOST PEOPLE DO NOT KNOW EXISTS: alongside the Council and Secretariat, ROPME has a Judicial Commission, established March 1989, of 6 nationals of Member States highly qualified in international law. In a region with almost no environmental litigation route, a standing judicial commission under a ratified convention is the most significant legal fact available — though this entry does not assert that individuals may petition it; establish who may seise it first. AN EVIDENCE SOURCE THAT NEEDS NO SITE ACCESS: ROPME's scientific bodies include a Remote Sensing Unit, alongside RIIS and MEMAC. WHICH PROTOCOL FITS YOUR ISSUE: oil-spill emergency response; land-based sources of pollution — the limb for a coastal development, discharge or reclamation; and transboundary movement of hazardous wastes. Development is named as a stressor in ROPME's own statement of purpose. At stake: over 20 species of dolphin and whale, all five subtropical turtle species, and more than 1,000 fish species, most endemic.

trackers.name: GEF Small Grants Programme Iran — a Tehran office, a twelve-member steering committee, and grants that go straight to community organisations
trackers.desc: THIS IS THE FIRST RESOURCE IN THIS MAP FOR IRAN THAT GIVES SOMETHING RATHER THAN MERELY RECORDS SOMETHING — every other Iranian entry here is a court or a registry. The programme maintains an office in Tehran, hosted with UNDP at Shahrzad Boulevard in Darrous, Pasdaran, and awards grants directly to community-based and non-governmental organisations rather than through government. DECISIONS ARE MADE BY A TWELVE-MEMBER NATIONAL STEERING COMMITTEE DRAWN FROM IRANIAN CIVIL SOCIETY, ACADEMIA AND GOVERNMENT AGENCIES, SERVING VOLUNTARILY, with the programme's guidelines requiring a majority of such committees to come from the non-governmental sector. That composition is the reason a community proposal can succeed here: the people assessing it are not solely officials. THE ROUTE MOST RELEVANT TO DEFENDING LAND IS THE ONE FOR COMMUNITY CONSERVED AREAS: the Iran programme has run work under the global support initiative for territories and areas conserved by Indigenous Peoples and local communities — a designation route for land that a community already manages by custom, which is precisely the situation of many Iranian pastoral and village territories. Ask about that stream specifically rather than about general environmental grants. HOW TO APPROACH IT: contact the National Coordinator first, obtain the guidelines, submit a short concept paper, and only prepare a full proposal if it passes pre-screening against the programme's criteria and the Iran Country Programme Strategy; the steering committee then accepts, rejects or returns it. Grants are paid in three instalments — on signature, on a satisfactory mid-term report, and on completion — so a group with no working capital must plan for the gap. Focal areas are biodiversity, climate change, land degradation and sustainable forest management, international waters and chemicals. THE SAFETY POINT, AND IT IS NOT A FORMALITY IN THIS COUNTRY: this map records only international instruments for Iran and names no Iranian organisation or individual, because naming them can expose them. Anyone considering an application should weigh what association with foreign-funded environmental work may mean for the people whose names appear on it, and should take current guidance from the programme office rather than from this entry. Confirm the office, the coordinator and the current call before acting; the country page reached carries material of uncertain currency.

trackers.name: Copernicus Browser — free satellite imagery you can compare across dates, from any browser
trackers.desc: PICK YOUR AREA, PICK TWO DATES, AND SEE WHAT CHANGED. This free service lets anyone browse and download FULL-RESOLUTION imagery from the European Copernicus satellite missions, COMPARE IMAGES SIDE BY SIDE, and CREATE TIMELAPSES DIRECTLY IN THE BROWSER — which is how change over months or years becomes something you can show rather than assert. Imagery refreshes every five to ten days. THIS COUNTRY HAS TWO ENTRIES IN THIS ENTIRE MAP, AND THIS IS THE ONLY ONE THAT REQUIRES NO ORGANISATION, NO INTRODUCTION AND NO PERMISSION — a browser and a free account. Where naming a domestic body could put people at risk, a tool one person uses alone is not a convenience but the whole of what is available. WHAT IT IS ACTUALLY USED FOR, ACCORDING TO AN INVESTIGATIVE RESEARCH TOOLKIT: TRACKING CONSTRUCTION PROJECTS, MINING OPERATIONS AND LAND DEVELOPMENT, and documenting environmental degradation — with the timelapse function singled out as particularly valuable for creating visual evidence of change. A dam wall rising, a wetland shrinking, a quarry spreading, a road cut through a slope: all of them are visible from orbit on dates you choose. BEYOND PLAIN PHOTOGRAPHS IT OFFERS PROCESSED VIEWS THAT ANSWER SPECIFIC QUESTIONS: false-colour composites, a VEGETATION index for plant health and a WATER index for surface water, plus atmospheric and air quality data from a dedicated mission. A lake or marsh contracting year on year shows in the water index even when a photograph looks ambiguous. THE PRACTICAL LIMITS: a free account is currently required; resolution is moderate rather than the sub-metre imagery people expect from commercial services, so small structures may not be legible; cloud cover blocks optical images, though radar imagery from another mission in the same collection sees through it; and the interface takes some learning. AND A WARNING ABOUT OLD GUIDES: THE PREDECESSOR VIEWER WAS SHUT DOWN IN FEBRUARY 2025 and its functions moved here. Any tutorial, bookmark or training material naming the older tool is pointing at a dead service.

trackers.name: Digital Security Helpline — emergency help when devices or accounts are compromised
trackers.desc: IT IS FREE, IT RUNS AROUND THE CLOCK, AND IT ANSWERS EVERY REQUEST WITHIN TWO HOURS. A helpline for civil society worldwide — activists, community groups, journalists and human rights defenders — with support in ten languages including RUSSIAN and ARABIC. This country has three other entries in the whole of this map, all of them tools or instruments requiring no local organisation; THIS IS THE FIRST THAT PUTS A PERSON ON THE OTHER END. IT DOES TWO DIFFERENT JOBS. Before anything happens, it walks you through ASSESSING THE RISKS YOUR WORK ACTUALLY CREATES and deciding what to secure first. Once you are under attack, it provides RAPID-RESPONSE EMERGENCY ASSISTANCE — and it helps ANALYSE, DOCUMENT AND EXPOSE advanced attacks including SPYWARE and targeted phishing. That last part is the one to remember: a technically documented intrusion becomes evidence that an international body can act on, where an unverified suspicion cannot. IT SECURES INFRASTRUCTURE, WEBSITES AND SOCIAL MEDIA ACCOUNTS, and provides guidance materials, training and referrals onward to others who can help. REACH IT BY EMAIL AT A PUBLISHED ADDRESS. It is an accredited member of a civil society computer emergency response body, and it publishes both a data usage policy and terms of service for the helpline — read them first, and think about which device and connection you use to make contact. THE LIMITS ARE IMPORTANT HERE: it handles digital security and nothing else. It will not take up an environmental case, fund anything or represent anyone, and it cannot change the conditions that make the work dangerous. Use it alongside the satellite imagery and corporate ownership tools recorded separately in this file — those are exactly the activities that draw the attention this helpline exists to defend against, and the two belong together.

trackers.name: iNaturalist — photograph what lives on the ground, and it becomes a scientific record
trackers.desc: THIS IS HOW A COMMUNITY CREATES THE SPECIES RECORD IT CANNOT FIND. Photograph a plant, animal or fungus with a free app, or record a sound; an automated system suggests what it is; a global community of naturalists then reviews it; and WHEN THEY AGREE THE OBSERVATION BECOMES RESEARCH GRADE AND IS AUTOMATICALLY SHARED WITH THE GLOBAL BIODIVERSITY DATABASE. This file recorded that database separately and warned that an under-surveyed district looks empty in it — and that a developer can cite that emptiness. THIS IS THE ANSWER TO THAT PROBLEM, and it costs nothing. OLD PHOTOGRAPHS COUNT. If you know roughly when and where a picture was taken, it is welcome — so photographs a family already has of a valley, a spring or an orchard can become dated, located species records without anyone going back into the field. AND THE PRIVACY SETTING IS THE ONE TO UNDERSTAND BEFORE YOU START: observations can be public, private, or OBSCURED — obscured randomises the location to protect sensitive species or habitats, and you can grant exact coordinates only to users you specifically trust. In a country where this file records no domestic organisation that can safely be named, publishing precise coordinates of what you are documenting, and of where you were, is a decision to take deliberately rather than by default. Use it with the digital security helpline recorded separately here. IT WORKS OFFLINE FOR CAPTURE: photographs and location are stored on the phone without a connection and uploaded when you have one. PRACTICAL POINTS THAT DECIDE WHETHER A RECORD IS USABLE: turn on location so coordinates are logged; take SEVERAL PHOTOGRAPHS FROM DIFFERENT ANGLES of a single individual, because that is what lets the community identify it to species; and add sounds where the animal is easier heard than seen. THE LIMITS. Identification depends on other people, so a rare or difficult organism may sit unidentified. Uploading needs a connection. And research-grade records are HARVESTED PERIODICALLY rather than fixed — if an identification is later contested and changed, the record can drop out of the global database. Once your observations reach research grade, download and cite them from that database, where a download carries a permanent identifier that cannot be revised away.

trackers.name: OSME Conservation Fund — small grants to nationals, three times a year, about half funded
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY HAS FIVE ENTRIES IN THIS ENTIRE MAP AND NO FUNDING ROUTE. THIS IS ONE, AND ITS CRITERIA ARE WRITTEN IN FAVOUR OF PEOPLE WHO LIVE HERE: projects should be INITIATED AND CARRIED OUT BY NATIONALS of the region, and/or engage local communities, and/or include TRAINING OF LOCAL COUNTERPARTS — while applications carrying significant international airfare costs are unlikely to be approved. A fund that discourages flying in outside experts is one that expects local people to do the work and be paid for it. THE TERMS: THREE DECISION ROUNDS A YEAR, with deadlines of 31 January, 31 May and 30 September; typical awards of one to three thousand pounds and NO STATED MAXIMUM; and a published funding rate of AROUND FIFTY PER CENT. Few funders in this payload disclose their success rate at all. WHAT IT WILL PAY FOR MATTERS MORE THAN THE SUM, BECAUSE IT INCLUDES GETTING A PLACE RECOGNISED: INVESTIGATING POTENTIAL NEW IMPORTANT BIRD AREAS or ornithologically little-known areas; strengthening the record of EXISTING important bird areas through breeding censuses and systematic counts; investigating the status of threatened species; and STUDIES OF ILLEGAL BIRD KILLING AND UNSUSTAINABLE HUNTING. This file has recorded repeatedly that a place with an internationally recognised designation is defended on different terms from a place without one, and that a community's central problem is proving its ground is not ordinary. This fund pays for exactly that proof. TWO OTHER GRANTS RUN ALONGSIDE IT: a threatened species research award of up to five thousand pounds annually, with a deadline around 1 December, and a youth fund of one to two thousand pounds for bird camps and education projects for sixteen to twenty-five year olds, LED FROM WITHIN THE REGION. The society publishes a country profile for this country, and a major international bird reference platform is now freely accessible throughout its region. THE LIMITS, AND ONE IS SPECIFIC TO HERE: it funds ornithological conservation and research only; the sums are modest; specimen collection needs justification and all necessary local authorisations; and it is a scientific society that will not oppose a project. Consider also what an international grant application discloses about you and your work — read it alongside the digital security helpline recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: ICCA Consortium — you do not need to be a registered organisation to join it
trackers.desc: ITS MEMBER ORGANISATIONS DO NOT NEED TO BE FORMALLY RECOGNISED BY STATE GOVERNMENTS. Eligible members expressly include traditional tribes, nations and peoples AND THEIR CUSTOMARY NETWORKS, ASSOCIATIONS AND FEDERATIONS, traditional local communities and their customary networks, and SELF-INITIATED GROUPINGS. This file has established across the region that the commonest barrier between a community and land, money or standing is not merit but the absence of a registered legal entity. THIS IS THE FIRST BODY RECORDED IN THIS ENTIRE MAP THAT SETS THAT BARRIER ASIDE — a village that has never registered anything can be a member in full standing. AND IT ALREADY HAS A NAME FOR WHAT YOU HAVE. The concept it works with — territories and areas conserved by Indigenous peoples and local communities, or territories of life — expressly covers systems called QOROQ and QOROQ-E BUMI, alongside himas and a dozen others from around the world. A community here is not asking to import a foreign model; the international framework already has a place for the one that exists. IT IS AN ASSOCIATION RATHER THAN AN AGENCY: an international membership organisation of Indigenous peoples, local communities and supporting organisations DOCUMENTING, SUSTAINING AND DEFENDING those territories, with over a hundred and sixty member organisations and some four hundred honorary members from eighty countries, plus regional coordinators and national focal points to approach. IT SETS OUT A ROUTE, IN ORDER: understand and strengthen your territory; communicate it; CREATE A CRITICAL MASS OF SUPPORT; REGISTER IT; and SECURE LEGAL OR POLICY RECOGNITION. That sequence is the closest thing in this payload to a plan for a community that holds land by custom and wants that holding acknowledged. THE REGISTRY IS RUN BY A UNITED NATIONS CONSERVATION MONITORING CENTRE AND SUBMISSION IS VOLUNTARY BY THE CUSTODIANS THEMSELVES, and a registered territory can be listed among the world's recognised protected and conserved areas. NOW THE CAUTION, AND IN THIS COUNTRY IT IS THE WHOLE OF THE DECISION: REGISTERING A TERRITORY MEANS PUBLISHING WHERE IT IS AND WHO LOOKS AFTER IT. This file has recorded for this country a digital security helpline and a mapping tool whose locations can be deliberately obscured; read those first, decide what to disclose and to whom, and note that the consortium's own steps put registration late in the sequence rather than first. THE OTHER LIMITS: it is not a funder and not a law practice; members must be not-for-profit and for-profit bodies are excluded; and recognition it helps pursue is granted by states, not by it.

trackers.name: Judicial Assistance Office — a free lawyer, and refusing the case is a disciplinary offence
trackers.desc: IT PROVIDES FREE REPRESENTATION AND LEGAL ADVICE TO PEOPLE WHO CANNOT PAY A LAWYER'S FEE, AND THE OBLIGATION ON LAWYERS IS NUMBERED. Every advocate must accept AT LEAST THREE ASSISTANCE CASES A YEAR referred by the bar's judicial assistance institution — A LEGAL DUTY, not a request — and a lawyer who refuses or neglects one HAS A DISCIPLINARY OFFENCE RECORDED AGAINST HIM. This country had no route to a lawyer anywhere in this map. This is one, it is old, and it has teeth. AND YOU WILL NOT BE GIVEN A TRAINEE: referral of assistance cases to trainee lawyers is PROHIBITED by the regulation. IT REACHES CIVIL MATTERS, WHICH IS THE QUESTION THAT DECIDES WHETHER IT IS ANY USE FOR LAND. Officials have said publicly that CLAIMANTS AND DEFENDANTS — not only the accused — should be able to have a lawyer, and that because judges may not gather evidence for the parties, the assistance unit exists to fill exactly that gap. A dispute over a plot, a permit or compensation is a civil matter, so ask for assistance on that basis rather than assuming the office is only for criminal defence. IT IS RUN BY THE PROFESSION, NOT BY THE STATE: the office receives NO GOVERNMENT BUDGET and is carried at the lawyers' own expense, and providing this service has been a statutory duty of the bar since 1936. In a country where this file records no domestic organisation it can safely name, a service funded by the profession rather than the treasury is a meaningful distinction. THE STRUCTURE AND WHAT TO EXPECT: the institution has a secretariat, a petitions branch and a judicial branch; it MAY INVESTIGATE YOUR APPLICATION and summon you by letter for further explanation or documents; and free legal consultation is given to callers at the office — at one recent event SEVEN HUNDRED LAWYERS provided free consultations in a single day. THE COST FALLS ONLY IF YOU WIN: where the assisted client succeeds, the lawyer collects ONE FIFTH OF THE FEE and pays it into the bar's fund, unless he proves collection is legally impossible. Nothing is due from a case that fails. THE LIMITS. It is means-tested and you must show you cannot pay. Capacity is finite — three cases per lawyer is a floor for the profession, not a promise to every applicant. The independent provincial bars run their own assistance rather than routing everything through the centre, so apply to the bar for YOUR province. And an application is a disclosure of your dispute to an institution — read this alongside the digital security helpline recorded separately for this country before you write.

trackers.name: The Article 90 Commission — a written complaint parliament is obliged to answer
trackers.desc: THE CONSTITUTION GIVES EVERY PERSON A WRITTEN COMPLAINT ROUTE, AND MAKES ANSWERING IT COMPULSORY. Anyone with a complaint about THE MANNER OF WORK of the assembly, the executive or the judiciary may submit it IN WRITING to the assembly, which is OBLIGED to examine it and give a SUFFICIENT ANSWER — and where the complaint concerns the executive or the judiciary, to require examination and a sufficient answer FROM THEM and to announce the result within an appropriate period. This country's listing in this map has held no domestic complaints channel at all. AND THE ENFORCEMENT CLAUSE IS UNLIKE ANYTHING ELSE RECORDED ANYWHERE IN THIS FILE. The commission may summon officials of the three branches or correspond with them directly AND THEY ARE OBLIGED TO COMPLY — and where an offence is proven for failing to answer or failing to give a convincing answer, THE OFFENDER FACES IMPRISONMENT OF THREE MONTHS TO ONE YEAR AND DISMISSAL FROM STATE SERVICE FOR SIX MONTHS TO ONE YEAR. Elsewhere in this payload an ignored complaint is simply ignored. Here silence by an official is itself an offence. AND THERE IS A SECOND DUTY WORTH FRAMING YOUR COMPLAINT AROUND: IN INDIVIDUAL MATTERS THE COMMISSION'S DUTY IS TO GIVE A SUFFICIENT ANSWER, BUT IN MATTERS OF PUBLIC CONCERN ITS DUTY IS TO INFORM THE GENERAL PUBLIC. A scheme affecting a whole district, a water source or a shared pasture is a matter of public concern, and saying so in the complaint invokes a duty of publication rather than merely of reply. WHAT IT COVERS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. Its subject is THE MANNER OF WORK of the three branches and their officials — how a decision was taken, whether procedure was followed, whether an authority answered — rather than the merits of the decision itself. An interpretation of the constitutional council confirms it examines the manner of work of CURRENT officials. Complaints about bodies affiliated to the executive or judiciary must first go through the channels the law provides for them, so this is the LAST avenue rather than the first. The commission has a unit dedicated to examining manners of work and received complaints, staffed by member deputies, advisers and experts, and it may summon both the complainant and the party complained of to explain. THE LIMITS, PLAINLY. It is not a court: courts must rule on every complaint, whereas this commission's obligation is a sufficient answer or public information, not a judgment or a remedy. It cannot reverse a permit or stop a project. It sits inside the legislature, and A WRITTEN COMPLAINT IS A DISCLOSURE OF YOUR NAME AND YOUR DISPUTE TO A STATE INSTITUTION — read this alongside the digital security helpline recorded separately for this country before writing. Use it where an authority has failed to follow its own procedure or has refused to answer, and use the bar's judicial assistance office recorded separately here for the case itself.

trackers.name: Free seedlings from the natural resources offices — and the coordinates that make it a record
trackers.desc: THE SEEDLINGS ARE FREE AND THE REQUEST IS A TELEPHONE CALL. Provincial natural resources departments supply the seedlings applicants need at no charge under the national tree-planting programme, with requests taken through a national telephone number and a national system; in the capital a separate city system operates alongside NINETY-THREE FLOWER AND PLANT TRAINING CENTRES distributing both fruit and non-fruit trees, and under one scheme staff attend homes, plant the seedling and leave written care instructions. BUT THE PART THAT MATTERS FOR LAND IS THE CONDITION ATTACHED. REGISTRATION OF THE PLANTING AREA IN THE STATE SYSTEM IS MANDATORY, AND AN APPLICANT MUST GO TO THE DISTRICT NATURAL RESOURCES AND WATERSHED OFFICE CARRYING THE COORDINATES OF THE PLANTING SITE IN ORDER TO RECEIVE THE TREES. This file has established across three countries that a state service can find land UNUSED and reallocate it, and that dated, witnessed evidence of use is the cheapest answer to that finding. HERE THE STATE ITSELF RECORDS, DATES AND GEO-REFERENCES YOUR PLANTING AS A CONDITION OF GIVING YOU THE TREES — the proof is created by the authority that would otherwise make the finding, and it costs nothing. AND A COMMUNITY BODY CAN APPLY AS AN INSTITUTION RATHER THAN AS INDIVIDUALS. The scheme names as participants not only nature-lovers and volunteers but COMPANIES, INDUSTRIES AND MINES, CITY AND VILLAGE COUNCILS AND VILLAGE ADMINISTRATORS, AND ASSOCIATIONS AND NATURAL-RESOURCE COOPERATIVES. A village council or a cooperative requesting seedlings for a named area, with coordinates, is doing something the scheme expressly invites. THE SUPPLY IS REAL AND SUITED TO DRY GROUND: production runs through 126 STATE NURSERIES COVERING NEARLY THREE THOUSAND HECTARES, plus around thirteen DESERT NURSERIES producing desert species, alongside private nurseries; hundreds of millions of seedlings are prepared for the planting week, and desert species such as haloxylon and atriplex are planted on natural-resource land. Ask for species suited to your ground rather than accepting whatever is offered. THE LIMITS, AND THE FIRST IS A DECISION. GIVING COORDINATES REGISTERS YOUR SITE AND YOUR NAME IN A STATE SYSTEM — that is what makes the record valuable and also what makes it a disclosure; read this with the digital security helpline recorded separately for this country. The distribution is SEASONAL, concentrated around the natural resources week in late winter, so the window is short. And officials themselves note that seedlings taken in previous years were often badly planted, unattended and died — A DEAD SEEDLING PROVES NOTHING, so plan the watering before you collect the trees.

trackers.name: UNESCO Chair on Water Reuse — a named professor with a telephone number
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY HAS THE FEWEST RECORDED RESOURCES OF ALL TWENTY-THREE IN THIS FILE, AND ALMOST NONE OF THEM CAN BE TELEPHONED. THIS ONE CAN: a UNESCO chair established in 2014 at the principal national university, WITH A NAMED CHAIRHOLDER AND TWO WORK TELEPHONE NUMBERS PUBLISHED. ITS SUBJECT IS WATER REUSE — the science of treated wastewater and recycled water — AND THAT IS MORE USEFUL THAN IT SOUNDS. Schemes across this region justify their water demand by promising to recycle, to treat and reuse effluent, or to return water to the system. A chair whose entire field is water reuse is the person who can say whether a particular claim of that kind is technically credible, at what quality, and with what residue. This file has found in nearly every country that the decisive gap is the cost of expert analysis; here is a named academic in the field, reachable directly. THE PROGRAMME THAT ESTABLISHED IT DESCRIBES ITS CHAIRS AS THINK TANKS AND BRIDGEBUILDERS BETWEEN ACADEMIA, CIVIL SOCIETY, LOCAL COMMUNITIES, RESEARCH AND POLICY-MAKING, so an approach from residents is within the post's stated purpose rather than an imposition on it. ASK A TECHNICAL QUESTION ABOUT A SPECIFIC SITE: what happens to the treated water, what it contains, where it goes, and whether the volumes stated in a proposal are achievable. Do not ask for support against a project — a chair cannot represent anyone and will not take sides. THE LIMITS, AND THE SECOND ONE IS A DECISION FOR YOU. It is an academic post inside a state university, so it is not independent of the administration; its output is research and teaching. AND IN THIS COUNTRY ANY APPROACH IDENTIFIES YOU AND YOUR INTEREST — an enquiry framed as a technical question about water quality is a quieter thing than a complaint, but it is still a disclosure, and this file's guidance on that for this country applies here too. The listing reached sits on a UNESCO water information platform rather than the university's own page, so confirm the current holder and the numbers before calling.

trackers.name: Provincial engineering organisation — the supervisor's duty to report violations, and where the report goes
trackers.desc: EVERY BUILDING HERE HAS SUPERVISING ENGINEERS UNDER A STATUTORY DUTY, AND THE DUTY IS THE OPENING A COMMUNITY NEEDS. They are obliged to supervise the works CONTINUOUSLY for conformity with the specifications in THE PERMIT AND THE APPROVED DRAWINGS, and at completion to CERTIFY that the building conforms to the permit, the drawings and the technical calculations. AND WHERE THE WORKS DEPART FROM THE APPROVED DRAWINGS, THE SUPERVISOR MUST PREPARE A REPORT OF THE VIOLATIONS AND DELIVER IT TO THE PROVINCIAL ORGANISATION AND TO THE PERMIT-ISSUING AUTHORITY — AND IF THE VIOLATIONS ARE NOT REMEDIED, THE MATTER IS REFERRED TO THE MUNICIPALITY'S ARTICLE 100 COMMISSION. That is a complete chain with a body at every step, and it changes the question entirely. A COMMUNITY DOES NOT HAVE TO PROVE THE WORK IS UNLAWFUL. IT HAS TO ASK WHETHER THE SUPERVISOR HAS FILED A REPORT — and if a departure from the drawings is visible and no report exists, the failure lies with a named licensed professional. THE DOCUMENTS ALSO ALREADY EXIST. A COORDINATING SUPERVISOR — an architect or civil engineer holding a supervision licence — is responsible for coordinating all the supervisors on a building or complex AND SUBMITTING STAGE REPORTS TO THE MUNICIPALITY, THE PROVINCIAL ORGANISATION AND OTHER RELEVANT AUTHORITIES. Stage reports are not something a community must commission; they are produced for every project, and they are held by two bodies. ASK WHICH LICENCE AND WHICH GRADE. Licences are split three ways: by DISCIPLINE — seven building disciplines including SURVEYING, URBAN PLANNING and TRAFFIC; by COMPETENCY — supervision, execution, and design or calculation, WITH A SEPARATE LICENCE ISSUED FOR EACH; and by GRADE, which limits the scale of work a person may take. Someone may hold a supervision licence and no design licence, or a grade too low for the project they are signing. TWO INTEGRITY RULES ARE WORTH KNOWING: A SUPERVISOR MAY NOT BE THE CLIENT OR THE CLIENT'S LEGAL REPRESENTATIVE ON THE SAME PROJECT, and a final disciplinary conviction of degree three or above disqualifies a professional from receiving referred supervision work. The provincial organisation checks competence and capacity before referring work, and its board sets the geographic area within the province in which a supervisor may operate. THE STRUCTURE IS PROVINCIAL: EACH PROVINCE HAS ITS OWN ORGANISATION WITH ITS OWN SITE, established under the building engineering and control law and described as non-governmental. FIND YOUR OWN PROVINCE'S ORGANISATION — the one linked here is a single provincial example. THE LIMITS. It regulates engineers rather than assisting residents, and in the statutory chain the complainant is the SUPERVISOR, not the neighbour — a community's route is to ask the provincial organisation whether reports were filed and to raise a supervisor's failure with it. Engaging services costs money. And any approach identifies you; read this with the digital security guidance recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Endowments organisation — a single tree can be endowed, and several people can endow together
trackers.desc: THE SMALLEST UNIT OF PERMANENT PROTECTION THIS FILE HAS FOUND IN THREE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-THREE ROUNDS IS HERE: ENDOWED TREES. In one province alone there are more than FIVE HUNDRED ENDOWED ORCHARDS, together with agricultural land, residential, administrative and industrial endowments — AND INDIVIDUAL ENDOWED TREES. A community that cannot conceivably buy a valley can still place a grove, a spring-side plot or a single old tree permanently outside the market. AND SEVERAL PEOPLE MAY ENDOW TOGETHER. A province has launched its first PARTICIPATORY ENDOWMENT, expressly using COLLECTIVE FINANCING to build a permanent financial base — which confirms in a second country the joint form this file recorded a round earlier. Many small contributions can become one endowment. THE SCALE MEANS THIS IS ORDINARY, NOT EXOTIC: there are MORE THAN TWO HUNDRED THOUSAND ENDOWMENTS in the country, and the organisation is establishing ENDOWMENT ADVISORY OFFICES. THE ENDOWER'S INTENTION IS ENFORCED, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE INSTRUMENT. All intentions and endowment deeds are registered and categorised in a comprehensive system SO THAT THE INCOME OF EACH ENDOWMENT IS SPENT IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE INTENTION OF ITS ENDOWER. AND YOU CAN NAME YOUR OWN WATCHDOG. A SUPERVISOR APPOINTED BY THE ENDOWER OVERSEES THE TRUSTEE'S WORK AND THE PRECISE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE DEED. This payload assembled across four endowment entries that the endower's conditions are the entire protection; HERE THE ENDOWER MAY ALSO APPOINT THE PERSON WHO POLICES THEM. Draft the deed to describe the land, the permitted uses and what may never be done — then name a supervisor who will outlive the argument. THERE IS ALSO A NEW ROUTE FOR DISPUTED ENDOWED LAND: a legal framework and integrated system now allows OWNERSHIP CLAIMS OVER ENDOWMENTS TO BE REGISTERED AND PURSUED, and the organisation has publicly invited anyone with such a claim to bring it — the facility being open to the public as well as to the organisation itself. Endowed ground that was taken or transferred is therefore contestable through a named channel. THE LIMITS, AND TWO ARE SERIOUS. THE ORGANISATION IS MOVING DELIBERATELY FROM TRADITIONAL ADMINISTRATION AND LEASING TOWARDS INVESTMENT, so endowed land may be developed rather than left alone — the deed's conditions are the only brake. ITS TAKING OF A SUPERVISION FEE FROM ENDOWMENT INCOME HAS BEEN QUESTIONED IN LEGAL SCHOLARSHIP AND BEFORE THE ADMINISTRATIVE JUSTICE COURT, so the cost of state administration is contested rather than settled. It is a state organisation with broad powers over endowments lacking a trustee. And in this country any dealing with an institution identifies you — read this with the digital security guidance recorded separately here.

trackers.name: Village administration and elected council — who holds the plan, who issues the permit, who must prosecute
trackers.desc: IF A SCHEME IS GOING UP ON RURAL LAND HERE, FOUR BODIES STAND BETWEEN IT AND LAWFULNESS, AND A RESIDENT CAN CHECK EVERY ONE OF THEM. FIRST, THE PLAN. EVERY VILLAGE'S DEVELOPMENT IS GOVERNED BY A RURAL GUIDE PLAN PREPARED BY A NATIONAL HOUSING FOUNDATION, AND YOU OBTAIN IT FROM THE VILLAGE ADMINISTRATION — WHOSE OFFICIALS ARE OBLIGED TO PROVIDE YOU WITH ITS DETAILS. That is a duty owed to an ordinary resident, and the plan shows whether a given plot lies inside or outside the built fabric. Ask neighbours who know the village too; the plan's boundary is the fact everything else turns on. SECOND, THE PERMIT. THE VILLAGE ADMINISTRATOR FORMS THE FILE AND ISSUES THE BUILDING PERMIT FOR STRUCTURES WITHIN THE VILLAGE'S LEGAL BOUNDARY — BUT ONLY AFTER COORDINATING WITH THE HOUSING FOUNDATION AND OBTAINING ITS TECHNICAL OPINION, AND ONLY WITHIN THE FRAMEWORK OF THE APPROVED GUIDE PLAN. A separate duty covers files for buildings, installations AND THE SUBDIVISION OF LAND, which are referred onward for the permit to issue. So the questions are simple and answerable: is there a permit, was the housing foundation's technical opinion taken, and does the work match the guide plan. THIRD, AND THIS IS THE STRONGEST LINK: BEFORE ANY ACTION, THE PERMIT-ISSUING AUTHORITY MUST OBTAIN THE OPINION OF THE COMMISSION UNDER THE LAW ON PRESERVING THE USE OF AGRICULTURAL LAND AND ORCHARDS. A permit granted without that opinion is defective on its face — and even where a village has NO approved guide plan, construction still needs a permit from the village administration and the land REMAINS SUBJECT TO THE AGRICULTURAL LAND PRESERVATION LAW. FOURTH, CHANGING WHAT LAND MAY BE USED FOR IS NOT A LOCAL DECISION: ANY LAND-USE CHANGE INSIDE A GUIDE PLAN REQUIRES THE AGREEMENT OF THE NATIONAL LAND AFFAIRS ORGANISATION. A developer promising that farmland will be reclassified is describing a decision that a national body must make. NOW THE LEVER, AND IT IS THE MOST USEFUL SENTENCE IN THIS ENTRY: THE AGRICULTURAL AUTHORITY IS OBLIGED, AS SOON AS IT LEARNS OF THE OFFENCE — EVEN THROUGH A REPORT BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC — TO PURSUE IT AND FILE A COMPLAINT. A resident's report is not a request for a favour; it starts a duty. AND THE ELECTED COUNCIL HOLDS THE PURSE: revenue from the fees charged under these provisions is spent on the village's public affairs UNDER THE SUPERVISION OF THE VILLAGE COUNCIL — so the council can be asked what was collected on a development and what became of it. THE LIMITS: these are state and quasi-state bodies, not allies; the source reached is a ministry guidance text for village administrators hosted on a third-party site, so confirm current wording; and in this country any approach identifies you — a question about whether a permit exists is far safer than a stated objection to a project.

trackers.name: Heritage-friends associations and the harim — the perimeter that stops building
trackers.desc: THE MOST POWERFUL THING IN THIS COUNTRY'S LAND LAW FOR SOMEONE TRYING TO STOP CONSTRUCTION IS THE HARIM — THE PROTECTIVE PERIMETER AROUND A HISTORIC WORK. ANY CONSTRUCTION WITHIN IT REQUIRES A PERMIT FROM THE CULTURAL HERITAGE AUTHORITY, and permits for projects inside the harim of nationally registered works must issue through official systems that cover construction, exploitation AND PHYSICAL CHANGES to the site. AND THE DECISIVE ADMINISTRATIVE ACT IS THE ONE MOST PEOPLE NEVER THINK TO ASK ABOUT: DETERMINING THE SITE'S EXTENT AND ITS HARIM. Campaigners fighting for a five-thousand-year-old mound on the western edge of the capital put it exactly right — that determination is NOT MERELY AN ADMINISTRATIVE STEP BUT THE LAST CHANCE TO PROTECT THE SITE. Until the perimeter is fixed, there is nothing to enforce. THE BODIES THAT DO THIS WORK ARE HERITAGE-FRIENDS ASSOCIATIONS, AND THEY ARE REGISTERED NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS — NON-PROFIT, NON-COMMERCIAL AND NON-POLITICAL. One has operated officially since 2000 in an ancient southern city, working to safeguard historic works, make them known, and research them. That legal form matters here: an association constituted on those three terms is doing something the state recognises, which is a different position from an informal group. FIND WHETHER ONE EXISTS FOR YOUR CITY, AND IF NONE DOES, THE MODEL FOR FOUNDING ONE IS ESTABLISHED. THEIR ASKS ARE THE TEMPLATE TO COPY, AND THE SECOND IS CLEVERER THAN THE FIRST: STOP NEW CONSTRUCTION IN THE HARIM; AND INSTALL PROPER SEWAGE NETWORKS IN AREAS ALREADY BUILT UP, SO THAT DESTRUCTIVE UNAUTHORISED DIGGING CANNOT BE CARRIED OUT UNDER THE PRETEXT OF LAYING SEWERS. That second demand converts a protection argument into an infrastructure request an authority can actually deliver — and removes the excuse under which damage happens. THE PRECEDENT IS WORTH CARRYING TO ANY MEETING. A MUNICIPALITY DIGGING TO INSTALL A FUEL TANK STRUCK GRAVES FROM THE ACHAEMENID PERIOD AND THE WORK WAS STOPPED; a provincial heritage director then stated that no permit would thereafter issue without heritage review, and that excavation and construction permits already granted would be halted. WHAT IS UNDER THE GROUND CAN STOP WHAT IS PLANNED ABOVE IT. AND THE ROLE IS OFFICIALLY ACKNOWLEDGED: a police official has said publicly that protecting cultural heritage requires the cooperation of all agencies, HERITAGE ASSOCIATIONS AND POPULAR GROUPS. THE LIMITS. The anchor is news coverage of a live campaign rather than an association's own page, so a local association must be found locally. Association capacity varies hugely by city. Registration and heritage decisions rest with state bodies. AND IN THIS COUNTRY ANY PUBLIC CAMPAIGN IDENTIFIES ITS PARTICIPANTS — a request to determine a site's perimeter is an administrative ask and a far safer one than a protest.

trackers.name: Registering a people's organisation — the provincial door, the statute that binds you, and the field that lets you in
trackers.desc: THIS FILE RECORDS FUNDING AND LEGAL ROUTES ACROSS TWENTY-THREE COUNTRIES THAT ALL REQUIRE ONE THING FIRST: THAT YOU ARE A LEGAL PERSON. HERE IS HOW TO BECOME ONE IN THIS COUNTRY, AND THE FIRST FACT SAVES A WASTED JOURNEY — THESE ORGANISATIONS ARE LOCAL OR AT MOST PROVINCIAL, SO THE APPLICATION IS PURSUED AT THE COUNTY OR PROVINCIAL GOVERNOR'S OFFICE, NOT IN THE CAPITAL. Permits are issued as either provincial or national, and a group whose concern is one valley should be asking for the provincial one. ENVIRONMENT AND NATURAL RESOURCES IS ONE OF THE LISTED FIELDS OF ACTIVITY — as are development and construction, citizens' rights, women, children, youth and the prevention of social harm. A body formed to look after a stretch of land is applying within a recognised category rather than asking for an exception, and CHOOSING THE FIELD IS THE FIRST STRATEGIC DECISION: it defines what you may lawfully do afterwards. THE STEPS ARE PUBLISHED. Complete the application form on the ministry's portal and take the TRACKING CODE. Assemble identity and education documents for the founders, their photographs, the minutes of the general assembly and of the board — AND THE STATUTE. The request is examined by the SUPERVISORY BOARD ON NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS within a few working days AND MUST ALSO BE CONFIRMED BY THE COMPETENT AUTHORITIES. A permit then issues, with an introduction letter to the documents and property registration organisation, and is delivered after publication in the official gazette. NOW THE PART THAT MATTERS FOR YEARS AFTERWARDS AND THAT ALMOST EVERYONE TREATS AS A FORMALITY: THE ORGANISATION MUST OPERATE IN ACCORDANCE WITH ITS STATUTE, OR IT IS IN VIOLATION. Every activity you may later want — receiving donations, holding property, commissioning studies, appearing in proceedings, working with a university — MUST BE INSIDE THE OBJECTS YOU WRITE NOW. This payload has recorded funders in several countries that require a programme to fall within the applicant's own stated objects; a narrow statute closes those doors permanently, and amending one is far harder than drafting it. THE LIMITS, AND THE SECOND IS SERIOUS. THE PERMIT DEPENDS NOT ONLY ON THE SUPERVISORY BOARD BUT ON CONFIRMATION BY THE COMPETENT AUTHORITIES, WHICH IS A VETTING STEP AND NOT A FORMALITY. AND REGISTERING NAMES YOUR FOUNDERS, THEIR ADDRESSES AND THEIR DOCUMENTS TO THE STATE — in this country that is a decision to take deliberately, not by default. Read it with the digital security guidance recorded separately here, and with the heritage associations entry, which shows the legal form already being used for site protection.

trackers.name: Rural cooperative organisation — the member-owned structure villages already hold assets through, and the union that grows saplings
trackers.desc: THIS FILE HAS RECORDED THE COOPERATIVE AS A LAND AND ASSET VEHICLE IN FOUR OTHER COUNTRIES. HERE IS THE STRUCTURE BEHIND IT IN THIS ONE, AND ITS OWNERSHIP IS THE FIRST THING WORTH KNOWING: the national rural cooperative organisation, founded in 1963 under the agriculture ministry, is a joint-stock body that is 78.2 PER CENT STATE-OWNED AND 21.8 PER CENT OWNED BY THE RURAL AND AGRICULTURAL COOPERATIVES THEMSELVES. THE COOPERATIVES OWN A FIFTH OF THE BODY THAT EXISTS TO SERVE THEM — which is a shareholding, and shareholders may ask questions that petitioners may not. ITS STATUTORY TASK IS RURAL AND AGRICULTURAL DEVELOPMENT THROUGH COOPERATIVES AND MEMBER ORGANISATIONS. That is the phrase to quote: development here is legally supposed to run THROUGH village bodies, not around them. THE CONDITIONS OF MEMBERSHIP ARE FEW AND WORTH KNOWING BEFORE ANYONE IS TURNED AWAY: be a national of the country; not be legally incapacitated; be under no legal prohibition; AND NOT ALREADY BELONG TO A SIMILAR COOPERATIVE. That last one matters — check what your household is already enrolled in before founding anything, because duplicate membership will block it. AND THE RANGE OF PEOPLE WHO MAY FORM AN AGRICULTURAL COOPERATIVE IS WIDER THAN MOST VILLAGES REALISE: farmers, ORCHARDISTS, livestock keepers, silkworm and BEE keepers, FISH FARMERS, villagers working in local and rural industries, AND AGRICULTURAL WORKERS — so people with no land of their own are inside the category. A community whose members are mostly labourers or herders can still constitute itself here. THE PIECE THAT JOINS THIS TO THE PLANTING WORK RECORDED ACROSS THIS REGION: among the national unions under this organisation is A UNION OF AGRICULTURAL COOPERATIVES PRODUCING FLOWERS, PLANTS, SEEDS AND SAPLINGS. THAT IS A MEMBER-OWNED NURSERY SUPPLY CHAIN — the answer to the question this file has asked in five countries about where restoration plants come from, and here it is owned by cooperatives rather than by a ministry. There is also a RURAL COOPERATIVE FUND COMPANY and a national medicinal plants association. KNOW WHERE THE SUPPORT GOES BEFORE CHOOSING YOUR FORM: IN ALL COOPERATIVE SUPPORT, PRIORITY GOES TO PRODUCTION COOPERATIVES. Distribution cooperatives supplying villagers' and nomads' needs get priority in commodity quotas and in government and banking support — and the stated reason is that rural cooperatives REDUCE MIGRATION FROM VILLAGES TO CITIES. A COMMUNITY THAT FRAMES ITS PROPOSAL AS KEEPING PEOPLE ON THE LAND IS SPEAKING TO THE STATE'S OWN STATED PRIORITY. THE LIMITS: this is a state-majority organisation under a ministry, and cooperatives here operate within an administrative system rather than against it — nothing in it will oppose a project. Its history includes compulsory membership after land reform, so older villagers may distrust the form. And this entry describes the national structure; the useful counterpart is the provincial office and the specific union for your activity.
