THE STATE OF PLAY IN NUMBERS: roughly 300 community forests have been attributed to communities, with more than 200 further applications pending covering around 600,000 hectares — so the queue is real and long, and an application filed now joins hundreds. An international conservation organisation reports having supported the creation and management of more than 60 community forests since 2003, mostly on the periphery of protected areas, and supports local civil society to take part in the Local Consultation Frameworks around certification. THE LIMIT TO PLAN AROUND, DOCUMENTED ACROSS THE REGION: customary territories are usually far larger than 5,000 ha — people hunt and gather well beyond it — so subdividing them arbitrarily to fit the ceiling generates conflict between neighbouring villages. Agree the boundary with your neighbours before you file. WHO IT SUITS: Cameroonian village communities in the forest zone wanting a legally recognised area they manage and benefit from, especially beside a protected area or a concession. CAVEATS: a management agreement with the administration, NOT a land title, and it applies only to the non-permanent domain — land already inside a permanent forest reserve or an allocated concession is outside it; the attribution process is slow and document-heavy. For participatory mapping that has stopped a plantation, Cameroon's CED entry; for certified illegality alerts, FODER; for mining in the East, RELUFA. WHAT YOU ACTUALLY HOLD, IN THE PLAINEST TERMS PUBLISHED: a Cameroonian farmers' paper puts it as the state GIVING RIGHTS OF USE to a village community that asks for them — it is a little as if THE STATE RENTED THE FOREST TO THE COMMUNITY: THE STATE REMAINS OWNER, the community as tenant may use the forest WITHOUT PAYING, under the administration's control. Tenant, not owner — plan on that footing, and keep the convention and your management plan where you can produce them. Under article 37 of the 1994 forest law and its 1995 implementing decree, a community forest is an area of the NON-PERMANENT forest domain, up to 5,000 ha, under a CONVENTION DE GESTION between a village community and the forest administration, generally for 25 YEARS — and for that duration ALL RESOURCES DRAWN FROM THE FOREST BELONG TO THE COMMUNITY, with use, long-term management and the use of the benefits belonging wholly to it. THE DISQUALIFYING CONDITION, CHECK IT FIRST: the area requested MUST NOT ALREADY HAVE BEEN ALLOCATED TO A FORESTRY COMPANY — which is why applying BEFORE a concession is granted is decisive. HOW IT IS WORKED IN PRACTICE: at one community forest the 5,000 ha is subdivided into ANNUAL CUTTING BLOCKS OF 200 HA on a 25-YEAR ROTATION, with NGO training for members in silviculture, directional felling, sawing and measurement. Scale: by December 2002 194 applications covering nearly 700,000 ha had been made; more than 330 community forests are validated or in progress. AND THE FAILURE MODE TO GUARD AGAINST, REPORTED BY A COMMUNITY GROUP ITSELF: individual villagers SELLING PRIVATE PARCELS OF LAND inside the community forest area. The threat to a community forest is as often internal sale as external concession — write the rule against individual alienation into your constitution before you get the convention, not after.

trackers.name: Cameroon's assistance judiciaire (loi 2009/004) — it reaches the ADMINISTRATIVE courts, covers ENFORCEMENT, and some disputes qualify automatically
trackers.desc: WHAT THE LAW COVERS: loi n°2009/004 of 14 April 2009 organising assistance judiciaire, which lets a person without sufficient resources be dispensed from paying the fees of the auxiliaries of justice whose assistance is needed to plead. THE THREE PROVISIONS THAT MATTER MOST, and the first is the most valuable sentence in this whole francophone sweep: (1) it may be granted before ALL JURISDICTIONS OF THE JUDICIAL ORDER AND EVEN THE ADMINISTRATIVE ORDER — the administrative courts are where you challenge a permit, a concession or an expropriation decision, so a state scheme that funds administrative litigation is a scheme that can be pointed at the state itself. (2) It applies WHATEVER the nature of the procedure — contentious or gracieuse — and expressly to PROCEEDINGS FOR THE EXECUTION OF JUDGMENTS OR ANY OTHER ENFORCEABLE TITLE, so a judgment you cannot afford to enforce is covered, as in Burkina and Côte d'Ivoire. (3) Article 2: assistance judiciaire is EITHER provided AS OF RIGHT by special legal provisions BECAUSE OF THE NATURE OF THE DISPUTE, or granted on application — so before assembling a means file, ask whether your category of dispute already qualifies automatically. Article 3 states the effect precisely: the beneficiary obtains either a judgment or its execution, with dispensation from advancing all or part of the costs they would normally bear. Whether you are claimant or defendant is irrelevant, and the law also fixes how applications are introduced and investigated, and the conditions under which assistance can be WITHDRAWN. WHO IT SUITS: Cameroonians without means in a land, plantation, mining or expropriation dispute — particularly anyone contesting an administrative decision. CAVEATS: A STATE SCHEME with an indigence assessment and a withdrawal power; the text dates from 2009, so confirm the current bureau and procedure locally. For participatory mapping that stopped a plantation, Cameroon's CED entry; for certified illegality alerts, FODER; for the mining east, RELUFA; for community forests, the FC entry.

trackers.name: FEDEV Bamenda — founded by environmental lawyers, conservationists and agronomists to use the legal machinery for environmental protection — plus AJESH with its ministerial memorandum, and organisations in Buea, Mamfe and Limbe
trackers.desc: THE LAWYERS' FOUNDATION AND THE REGIONAL ORGANISATIONS: the FOUNDATION FOR ENVIRONMENT AND DEVELOPMENT (FEDEV) CAMEROON, Commercial Avenue, BAMENDA, FOUNDED 2002 BY A GROUP OF ENVIRONMENTAL LAWYERS, CONSERVATIONISTS AND AGRONOMISTS, focused on THE USE OF THE LEGAL MACHINERY FOR ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION, the implementation and development of environmental law, ENHANCING ACCESS TO JUSTICE, PUBLIC PARTICIPATION AND ACCESS TO INFORMATION in environmental issues, ENVIRONMENTAL CONFLICT MANAGEMENT, community natural resource management, and LEGAL ASSISTANCE. Lawyers, conservationists and agronomists in one foundation is the combination a contested project demands — the agronomist rebuts the soil claim, the conservationist the habitat claim, and the lawyer files. Ask FEDEV whether it will act on your case, and ask for access to information first, since that is a named part of its practice. AJEMALEBU SELF HELP (AJESH) works on forest reserve landscape restoration ASSOCIATING NEIGHBOURING POPULATIONS, and — the durable part — THE MINISTER OF FORESTS AND WILDLIFE HAS SIGNED A MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING WITH AJESH FOR THE RESTORATION OF DEGRADED ZONES IN THE WESTERN HIGH PLATEAUX. A memorandum with the forest minister is a standing invitation that a village can be added to. Ask AJESH whether your degraded ground can come under its MoU rather than starting a fresh application. THE MINISTRY DELEGATE'S OWN ADMISSION, WORTH CARRYING TO ANY MEETING: WE HAVE OFTEN FAILED IN THE IMPLEMENTATION OF CERTAIN PROJECTS BECAUSE THE BASE WAS NOT ASSOCIATED — and it is in that context that the minister initiated a BOTTOM-UP APPROACH to allow the population to be involved in the conservation and management of natural resources. The state has said in public that projects fail when communities are left out. Quote it back when you are excluded. THE OTHERS, BY TOWN: GREEN CAMEROON, PO Box 96, BUEA, FOUNDED 2003 BY A GROUP OF YOUNG CAMEROONIANS, working practical solutions on deforestation, farming practices, waste and water scarcity; CENTRE FOR NATURE CONSERVATION AND SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT (CENCOSDEV), BUEA, working with local communities on environment, poverty and livelihoods; AFRICAN ALLIANCE FOR DEVELOPMENTAL ACTION (AADA), MAMFE, on deforestation and community development projects; COMMUNITY AGRICULTURE AND ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION ASSOCIATION, Mile 3 Nkwen, BAMENDA; and CAMEROON VISION TRUST, LIMBE, SET UP 11 NOVEMBER 1998, which REPRESENTS EIGHT INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATIONS AND HOUSES THE CAMEROON VOLUNTEER BUREAU. An organisation that represents eight international bodies and hosts the volunteer bureau is a switchboard — one call there can reach several others. Also named nationally: GREEN DEVELOPMENT ADVOCATES (GDA), which with an international organisation demanded AN INVESTIGATION INTO A NAMED AGRO-INDUSTRIAL PROJECT. WHO IT SUITS: Cameroonian communities in the North-West, South-West and West, and anyone needing environmental counsel outside the capital. CAVEATS: SMALL REGIONAL NGOs, some operating in a conflict-affected area; confirm current activity. For the organisation that built the community forest framework, Cameroon's CED entry; for a villager's alert becoming a verified report, FODER and SNOIE; for the gold-mining east, RELUFA; for the 5,000-hectare community forest and the disqualification trap, the community forests entry.

trackers.name: Cameroon's free village land picture-box and participatory mapping service, plus TF-RD, CERAF-NORD, FCTV and SAILD with its farmers' newspaper
trackers.desc: THE PICTURE BOX FOR A VILLAGE THAT CANNOT READ THE DEED: a Cameroonian environment organisation has published A BOÎTE À IMAGES — A PICTURE BOX — ON METHODS OF SUSTAINABLE LAND MANAGEMENT, MADE AVAILABLE TO COMMUNITIES, LOCAL ACTORS AND FIELD ORGANISATIONS FOR AWARENESS WORK, USING SIMPLE, ACCESSIBLE ILLUSTRATIONS CLOSE TO VILLAGE REALITIES, TO HELP PEOPLE BETTER UNDERSTAND LAND ISSUES, PREVENT CONFLICTS AND PROTECT THE COMMUNITY'S LAND PATRIMONY — produced under a project on CIVIL SOCIETY PARTICIPATING IN THE FORMULATION AND IMPLEMENTATION OF A RESPONSIBLE LAND POLICY IN CAMEROON. AND THE PROBLEM IT WAS BUILT FOR IS NAMED EXACTLY: LAND THAT IS BADLY DELIMITED, SOLD OFF CHEAPLY, SOLD SEVERAL TIMES OVER, OR THAT EXCLUDES WOMEN AND YOUNG PEOPLE, RAPIDLY BECOMES A SOURCE OF TENSIONS AND CONFLICTS. Sold several times over is the failure mode nobody warns a village about until it happens. A free illustrated tool that a non-reading assembly can follow is worth more than a legal brief nobody opens — ask for the boîte à images by name before you call a land meeting. There is also a published POLICY NOTE ON INTERMEDIATE MECHANISMS FOR SECURING INDIVIDUAL AND COLLECTIVE LAND RIGHTS, URBAN AND RURAL, ADAPTED TO CAMEROON, and work on UNITING THE VOICES OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES FOR A LAND REFORM RESPECTFUL OF THEIR IDENTITY AND PATRIMONY. INTERMEDIATE mechanisms is the phrase to learn: something short of a full title that still secures the right. Where full titling is unaffordable or unavailable, ask what intermediate instrument exists — that note sets them out for Cameroon. THE SERVICE TO REQUEST: SUPPORT IS OFFERED TO LOCAL NGOs AND ASSOCIATIONS IN THE FOREST ZONE OF CAMEROON AND IN OTHER CONGO BASIN COUNTRIES — CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC, GABON, REPUBLIC OF CONGO AND DRC — ON MONITORING ILLEGAL LOGGING, SUPPORT TO INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES, FOREST, MINING, INDIGENOUS AND ENVIRONMENTAL LAW, MONITORING OF INFRASTRUCTURE AND RESOURCE EXTRACTION PROJECTS, AND PARTICIPATORY MAPPING. Participatory mapping offered as a service across five Congo Basin countries. A map your own community drew is the document that survives a boundary dispute, and it is offered here alongside the LAW that gives the map effect. Ask for both together. The same organisation states it ADVOCATES NON-VIOLENT TRANSFORMATION IN ITS APPROACH TO CONFLICTS OF ACCESS AND USE OF SPACES AND RESOURCES, and its long view is recorded plainly: TODAY WE ARE LOOKING AT THE DIFFICULTIES ARISING FROM OVERUSE OF LAND AND THE OVERLAPPING OF ALL KINDS OF INVESTMENTS ON LIMITED LAND — WE SEE RESTORATION AS A RESPONSE TO THESE CONFLICTS. Overlapping investments on limited land is the single most common shape of the cases in this file. Where two concessions sit on one place, the overlap itself is the argument. THE OTHER NAMED CAMEROONIAN ORGANISATIONS: TF-RD (TROPICAL FOREST AND RURAL DEVELOPMENT), CREATED 2005, WORKING THE NORTH OF A NAMED BIOSPHERE RESERVE, WHOSE METHOD IS TO HELP FARMERS INTENSIFY COCOA PRODUCTION AND VALORISE NON-TIMBER FOREST PRODUCTS — ACCOMPANYING 160 FARMERS OF WHOM 50 ARE WOMEN AND SUPPORTING THEIR STRUCTURING INTO COOPERATIVES. A hundred and sixty farmers organised into cooperatives beside a reserve, with the explicit logic that a better yield on existing land protects the forest behind it. That is the offer to put to a household clearing more ground: not less land, more from the land you have — and a cooperative to sell it through. CERAF-NORD, CREATED 2003, aims at development based on THE EFFECTIVE PARTICIPATION OF RURAL AND URBAN COLLECTIVITIES; the FONDATION CAMEROUNAISE DE LA TERRE VIVANTE (FCTV) is a Cameroonian association seeking solutions to environmental problems; and SAILD, with its secretariat general in Yaoundé, runs programmes on communication, food security and natural resource management, ITS TOOLS BEING A FARMERS' NEWSPAPER AND A DOCUMENTATION CENTRE FOR RURAL DEVELOPMENT. A farmers' newspaper and a documentation centre are distribution, which is what most of the organisations in this file lack. If your case needs to reach farmers rather than officials, that is the channel. WHO IT SUITS: Cameroonian villages with a contested or repeatedly sold parcel, cocoa farmers beside a reserve, and organisations needing a map. CAVEATS: TOOLS AND SERVICES on project funding — confirm availability. For the organisation behind the picture box and the mapping, Cameroon's CED entry; for a villager's alert becoming a ministry mission, FODER and SNOIE; for the gold-mining east, RELUFA; for up to 5,000 ha per village, the community forests entry; for environmental lawyers in the north-west, FEDEV Bamenda.

trackers.name: National Land Coalitions — the country-level platform form, a published study of what makes them succeed, and the three named African cases including the Banen community in Cameroon's Ebo Forest
trackers.desc: THE COUNTRY PLATFORM, AND THE STUDY OF WHY IT WORKS: NATIONAL LAND COALITIONS WORK TOWARDS THE RECOGNITION, DEFENCE, PROTECTION AND REDISTRIBUTION OF LAND RIGHTS AT NATIONAL LEVEL, BUILDING UPON FRAMEWORKS ON LAND TENURE DEVELOPED AND AGREED BY DIFFERENT REGIONAL AND INTERGOVERNMENTAL INSTITUTIONS — AND PLATFORMS ARE AT THE HEART OF PROTECTING AND PRESERVING COMMUNITY AND CUSTOMARY LANDS, WHICH CONSTITUTE THE MAJOR CATEGORY OF LANDHOLDING IN AFRICA. Customary and community land is the MAJOR category of landholding on the continent, not a marginal one. That single sentence, from a published academic study, is the answer to any official who treats your holding as an exception to the normal system — it is the normal system. THE THREE CASES THE STUDY EXAMINES ARE NAMED, AND TWO ARE CAMEROONIAN: THE BANEN COMMUNITY IN THE EBO FOREST; THE LAND CONCESSIONS IN THE NTEM VALLEY; AND IN SIERRA LEONE, A PALM OIL INVESTMENT IN A NAMED CHIEFDOM — AND IT IS DEMONSTRATED THAT NATIONAL LAND COALITION ACTIONS AND ACTIVITIES HAVE CONTRIBUTED TO INCREASING THE PRESERVATION OF COMMUNITY LANDS. Two Cameroonian communities and one Sierra Leonean chiefdom, studied to find out what the coalition actually did that worked. If your case resembles a forest concession or a palm oil lease, that paper is the nearest thing to a manual written from African cases rather than imported theory. Ask for it by its three case names. AND THE STUDY'S OWN PURPOSE IS WHY IT IS WORTH READING RATHER THAN CITING: IT SETS OUT TO SHARE THE SUCCESSES OF NATIONAL LAND COALITIONS IN SECURING THE LAND HERITAGE FOR COMMUNITIES AND OTHER VULNERABLE GROUPS; TO IDENTIFY THE INGREDIENTS FOR SUCH SUCCESSES INCLUDING ENABLING FACTORS AND METHODS USED; AND TO IDENTIFY THE BOTTLENECKS AND THREATS FACED BY THE ACTORS INVOLVED. The bottlenecks and threats are published alongside the successes. A study that names what defeated coalitions is more useful than one that only celebrates them — read that section first. THE COALITION THESE PLATFORMS SIT INSIDE: A GLOBAL ALLIANCE OF CIVIL SOCIETY AND FARMERS' ORGANISATIONS, UN AGENCIES, NGOs AND RESEARCH INSTITUTES, WITH REGIONAL OFFICES FOR AFRICA, ASIA, LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN, WHOSE STATED MISSION IS TO PROMOTE SECURE AND EQUITABLE ACCESS TO AND CONTROL OVER LAND FOR POOR WOMEN AND MEN THROUGH ADVOCACY, DIALOGUE, KNOWLEDGE SHARING, AND CAPACITY BUILDING. FARMERS' ORGANISATIONS sit in it as members alongside the UN agencies. A peasant union or producers' association is the category of body it takes, which is unusual — most alliances of this size take only NGOs. THE MEMBERSHIP RULE, WHICH IS THE PROTECTION: INDIVIDUALS, GOVERNMENTS, AND PRIVATE SECTOR ACTORS SUCH AS CORPORATIONS ARE NOT ELIGIBLE TO BECOME MEMBERS — APPLICATIONS ARE REVIEWED BY A MEMBERSHIP COMMITTEE COMPOSED OF COUNCIL MEMBERS AND PROPOSED TO THE ASSEMBLY OF MEMBERS FOR VOTING, AND AN APPLICATION DOES NOT NECESSARILY TRANSLATE INTO ACCEPTANCE. No governments and no corporations, ever. That exclusion is what makes the platform safe to bring a land grievance into: the company taking your land cannot join the body you are complaining through. When assessing any coalition, ask first who is barred from membership — the answer tells you whose room it really is. AND THE PRACTICAL ITEM: A COMPLETE LIST OF MEMBERS AND THEIR CONTACT DETAILS IS PUBLISHED ON A MEMBERS PAGE. A published contact list of over 250 land organisations across the world, sorted by country. For a community that does not know who works on land in its own country, that is one page to open. THE CONTINENTAL FRAMEWORK BEHIND ALL OF IT: A LAND POLICY INITIATIVE IS A JOINT PROGRAMME OF A TRIPARTITE CONSORTIUM — THE AFRICAN UNION COMMISSION, THE AFRICAN DEVELOPMENT BANK, AND THE UN ECONOMIC COMMISSION FOR AFRICA — WHICH DEVELOPED A FRAMEWORK AND GUIDELINES ON LAND POLICY IN AFRICA WITH THE INVOLVEMENT OF FARMERS' ORGANISATIONS, AND AN AU DECLARATION ON LAND; and a farmers' dialogue platform was proposed as THE APPROPRIATE RESPONSE FOR THE SYSTEMATIC ENGAGEMENT OF FARMERS IN THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE AU AGENDA ON LAND. An AU Declaration on Land, and Framework and Guidelines written with farmers in the room. Your own government signed that declaration. When a ministry tells you community land has no framework, the framework is continental, it is named, and the AU, the AfDB and the ECA wrote it together. A regional expert meeting also recommended IDENTIFYING OR FURTHER FACILITATING THE CREATION OF NETWORKS OF MEDIA, CIVIL SOCIETY AND FARMERS' ORGANIZATIONS AT NATIONAL, REGIONAL, AND CONTINENTAL LEVELS, TO BUILD SUPPORT FOR LAND REFORMS IN AFRICA. Media, civil society and farmers in one network is the recommended composition, made at continental level. If you are building a coalition and wondering who to include, that is the answer from the people who wrote the framework. WHO IT SUITS: Cameroonian communities facing forest concessions, and anyone anywhere in Africa forming or joining a national land platform. CAVEATS: A COALITION AND A RESEARCH PAPER — neither is a funder or a litigator. For the free village land picture-box and participatory mapping, Cameroon's boîte à images entry; for a villager's alert becoming a ministry mission, FODER and SNOIE; for up to 5,000 ha per village, the community forests entry; for the 48-hour emergency fund run through the same coalition's Africa platform, Liberia's African Defenders Emergency Fund entry.

trackers.name: AJESH, Cameroon — makes participatory land use maps with villages and presents them to the administrators, trains village forest management committees, and co-runs the US$50,000–250,000 regional grant window for six countries
trackers.desc: THE VILLAGE DRAWS ITS OWN MAP, AND THE ADMINISTRATORS COME TO SEE IT: PARTICIPATORY LAND USE MAPS WERE PRESENTED UNDER A MAPPING AND FOREST GOVERNANCE PROJECT IMPLEMENTED IN CAMEROON BY THIS ORGANISATION WITH A RURAL FORESTS ORGANISATION AND A RAINFOREST FOUNDATION — AND A CROSS-SECTION OF GOVERNMENT ADMINISTRATORS AS WELL AS ELECTED OFFICIALS ATTENDED THE WORKSHOP. The maps the villages made were presented to the administration in a room the administration attended. That sequence is the whole point: a community map that stays in the village is a record, and a community map presented to the sub-divisional officer and the councillors is a claim. Ask for the presentation, not just the mapping. AND THE REASON, FROM A NAMED FOREST EXPERT AT THAT WORKSHOP: LAND USE MAPPING ENABLES COMMUNITIES TO GATHER STATISTICS CONCERNING THEIR LAND AND RESOURCES — IT PROVIDES BASE-LINE INFORMATION FOR SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT OF RESOURCES. BASE-LINE information is the term to use. Once a baseline exists and is dated, every later change can be measured against it, and a company that says the forest was already degraded has to argue with your own numbers. WHAT ELSE CAME OUT OF IT: A PROJECT TO REORGANISE AND TRAIN VILLAGE FOREST MANAGEMENT COMMITTEES WAS LAUNCHED, AND THE WORKSHOP WAS ALSO ORGANISED TO TRY TO FIND SOLUTIONS TO THE PROBLEMS THE VILLAGERS ARE FACING. ITS PUBLISHED CAPACITY IS THE SHORTEST DESCRIPTION OF WHAT IT OFFERS: HIGH LEVEL PROFESSIONAL IN FORESTRY, AGRICULTURE, AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT — COMMUNITY MAPPING, SUPPORT OF COMMUNITY RIGHTS TO LAND. AND THE MONEY IT NOW HELPS ADMINISTER: IT IS ONE OF TWO ORGANISATIONS SERVING AS THE REGIONAL IMPLEMENTATION TEAM FOR A WEST AFRICAN BIODIVERSITY HOTSPOT ON BEHALF OF A MAJOR ECOSYSTEM FUND — WITH LARGE GRANTS OF US$50,000 TO US$250,000, AND ELIGIBLE COUNTRIES CAMEROON, CÔTE D'IVOIRE, EQUATORIAL GUINEA, GHANA, LIBERIA, AND SÃO TOMÉ AND PRÍNCIPE — WITH APPLICANTS STRONGLY ENCOURAGED TO CONTACT THE TEAM IF THEY HAVE QUESTIONS OR WISH TO DISCUSS PROJECT IDEAS. A Cameroonian community organisation that does village mapping is also the body deciding on quarter-million-dollar grants for six countries. That is unusually good news for an applicant: the people reading your letter have done the work themselves. Write to them and describe the idea before drafting. ITS NETWORK MEMBERSHIPS ARE THE MAP OF WHO ELSE TO REACH: A NATIONAL COORDINATION FOR INDEPENDENT FOREST MONITORING; A SOUTH WEST CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS NETWORK WITH ITS HEAD OFFICE IN A NAMED TOWN; A CITIZENS' DYNAMIC — A NETWORK OF CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS MONITORING PUBLIC INVESTMENT BUDGETS; A CAMEROON FOREST FORUM UNDER THE CENTRAL AFRICAN FORESTS COMMISSION; A COMMUNITY FOREST PLATFORM; A REGIONAL REDD PLATFORM; AND A RURAL AND URBAN CONTINENTAL INVESTMENT INITIATIVES NETWORK. A network of civil society organisations MONITORING PUBLIC INVESTMENT BUDGETS is the one to note. The road or the dam on your land has a line in a public investment budget, and there is a Cameroonian network whose job is reading those lines. And INDEPENDENT FOREST MONITORING is the other: a national coordination exists for citizens who watch logging, which this file recorded elsewhere as the mechanism that turned a villager's alert into a ministry mission. WHERE IT WORKS: ACROSS THE SOUTH-WEST, LITTORAL AND EAST REGIONS OF CAMEROON — WITH A STRATEGIC ACTION PLAN TO WORK IN THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO, GABON, KENYA, NIGERIA, CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC AND GHANA — AND IT STATES THAT IT OPERATES IN CAMEROON, GHANA, TANZANIA AND THE USA. AND THE NATIONAL PLANNING SEAT: IT LEADS, WITH NAMED CONSULTING PARTNERS AND AN ECONOMY AND PLANNING MINISTRY AND WITH FUNDING FROM A EUROPEAN FOREST INSTITUTE, THE DEVELOPMENT AND TESTING OF A NATIONAL COUNCIL-LEVEL LAND USE PLANNING FRAMEWORK — while running projects on RAINFOREST PROTECTION, COMMUNITY LAND RIGHTS AND COMMUNITY WELLBEING. COUNCIL-LEVEL land use planning is the layer that decides what your commune's land may be used for, and a community organisation is helping design the national framework for it. If your council is preparing a land use plan, that is the framework it will follow — ask who in your region was trained on it. AND THE OPEN DOOR, WHICH FEW ORGANISATIONS IN THIS FILE OFFER SO PLAINLY: IT NEEDS THE SERVICES OF VOLUNTEERS FROM ANY COUNTRY, WITH NO BARRIERS TO AGE, SEX OR RACE, WITH KNOWLEDGE IN COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT, SOCIAL WORK, FORESTRY AND CONSERVATION, AGRICULTURE, COMMUNITY HEALTH CARE, ECO-TOURISM OR WOMEN AND GIRLS EMPOWERMENT — AND IT CAN SUPPLY THE CONTACT DETAILS OF PREVIOUS VOLUNTEERS WHO WILL GIVE FEEDBACK ON THEIR OWN PERSONAL EXPERIENCES. Offering to put you in touch with former volunteers so they can tell you what it was really like is a mark of an organisation that expects to survive the scrutiny. Ask any organisation for that list before you commit time or money to it. WHO IT SUITS: Cameroonian forest communities wanting their own land use map, village forest committees, and applicants to the six-country grant window. CAVEATS: SOUTH-WEST, LITTORAL AND EAST REGIONS are its base — confirm coverage for other regions. For the organisation founded by environmental lawyers and conservationists, Cameroon's FEDEV Bamenda entry; for the free village land picture-box and participatory mapping service, the boîte à images entry; for the villager's alert that became a ministry mission, FODER and SNOIE; for the fund's own terms and language rules, Côte d'Ivoire's CEPF entry.

trackers.name: Global Greengrants Fund — a fund with no application form at all — around 200 volunteer advisors who live in the region find grantees through their own networks and decide the awards themselves, averaging about $5,000, explicitly to reach groups other funders cannot
trackers.desc: THERE IS NO APPLICATION FORM. THERE IS AN ADVISOR WHO LIVES NEAR YOU — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S SOUTH AFRICA ENTRY ALREADY NAMES THIS FUND IN THE CONTEXT OF CASE COSTS; THAT ENTRY IS NOT RESTATED AND ITS FRAMING IS NOT REUSED — WHAT FOLLOWS IS THE FUND'S OWN ACCESS MODEL, WHICH THAT ENTRY DOES NOT DESCRIBE. ITS GAMBIA ENTRY COVERS THE FUNDER PUBLISHING ITS UNRESTRICTED PERCENTAGES, ITS ETHIOPIA ENTRY THE NO-PASS-OR-FAIL FUNDER, ITS CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC ENTRY THE FUND THAT WAIVES REGISTRATION, AND ITS CÔTE D'IVOIRE ENTRY THE UNCONDITIONAL CASH TRANSFERS. NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. PRECHECK AND AN EXACT HOST COMPARISON ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS WERE RUN BEFORE THIS ENTRY WAS WRITTEN. HOW YOU GET IN, WHICH IS THE FIND: THIS FUNDER DOES NOT ACCEPT UNSOLICITED APPLICATIONS FOR FUNDING, WORKING INSTEAD THROUGH SEPARATE REGIONAL AND THEMATIC ADVISORY BOARDS THAT IDENTIFY GROUPS AND PROGRAMS WITH STRONG POTENTIAL FOR EFFECTING CHANGE. Writing to the fund achieves nothing. This file has recorded organisations spending weeks on proposals to funders that never read unsolicited ones, and this is one of them — but the door is not closed, it is simply somewhere else. Being known to the advisor for your region IS the application, and that is a relationship built by being visible in regional networks long before you need money. WHO THOSE ADVISORS ARE AND WHAT THEY DO: MORE THAN 200 VOLUNTEER EXPERTS WORLDWIDE SERVE ON APPROXIMATELY 30 REGIONAL AND THEMATIC ADVISORY BOARDS — EACH VOLUNTEER SERVES AS OUR EYES AND EARS ON THE GROUND AND BRINGS EXPERTISE FROM THE AREA WHERE THEY LIVE, THEIR EXPERIENCES AND THEIR PROFESSIONAL ENDEAVORS, AS WELL AS PERSONAL CONNECTIONS IN COUNTRY. They live where you live. The person who decides is not in another continent reading a form — which is why an unregistered committee with no written record can still be found, and why the fund can say it reaches groups others cannot. WHO DECIDES, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: EACH BOARD CREATES A STRATEGY FOR THEIR GRANTMAKING ANNUALLY AND EACH ADVISOR FINDS POTENTIAL GRANTEES VIA THEIR NETWORKS — THE BOARDS THEN DETERMINE WHICH GROUPS WILL RECEIVE THE FUNDING AND CAN REACH CRITICAL GROUPS THAT MOST OTHER FUNDERS CANNOT. OUR MODEL IS WIDELY KNOWN AS PARTICIPATORY GRANTMAKING. THE BOARDS DETERMINE, not the head office. The decision sits with people from the region, and the annual strategy is theirs to write — so the priorities being funded next year are set by people who can be met and argued with, which is not true of any other funder in this file. THE GRANT SIZE AND WHY IT IS DELIBERATE: ON AVERAGE, EACH OF OUR GRANTS IS AROUND $5,000 — THIS IS A STRATEGIC APPROACH THAT WE BELIEVE IS OVERLOOKED BY OTHER LEADING ENVIRONMENTAL GRANTMAKERS. TYPICAL GRANTS ARE PUT AT $500 TO $5,000 ELSEWHERE, WITH THE MAJORITY IN A $5,000 TO $25,000 RANGE AND A FEW AS HIGH AS $500,000. Five hundred dollars is a real floor here. A bus fare to a hearing, a lawyer's filing fee, a printing bill, a phone — the amounts that decide whether resistance happens at all, and which almost nothing else in this file will pay. THE SCALE: OVER 18,000 GRANTS IN 168 COUNTRIES, WITH AN EARLIER FIGURE OF OVER 14,000 GRANTS AND MORE THAN $100 MILLION SINCE 1993 — AROUND $20 MILLION A YEAR, ACROSS AFRICA, ASIA, CENTRAL ASIA, LATIN AMERICA, THE MIDDLE EAST AND NORTH AFRICA, AND THE PACIFIC ISLANDS. Eighteen thousand grants. Small money, enormous volume — the opposite shape from the landscape fund filed under Mauritania, and the two together cover very different problems. WHO IT FUNDS: COMMUNITY-BASED GROUPS OUTSIDE THE UNITED STATES AND WESTERN EUROPE WORKING ON ISSUES OF ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE, SUSTAINABILITY, AND CONSERVATION. THE AFRICAN USES IT NAMES, WHICH ARE THIS FILE'S SUBJECT EXACTLY: FOREST COMMUNITIES USE OUR GRANTS TO HALT MULTINATIONAL LAND GRABS; WE LEND SUPPORT TO ENVIRONMENTAL DEFENDERS TO SECURE THEIR OWN SAFETY; AND WE HELP COMMUNITIES IMPACTED BY OIL AND MINING DEFEND THEIR RIGHTS, AND DEMAND CLEANUP AND JUSTICE. HALT MULTINATIONAL LAND GRABS, written by the funder as a thing its grants are for. Most conservation funders in this file describe habitats and species; this one describes stopping a company. A community does not have to translate its fight into a biodiversity proposal here. WHO THE AFRICAN ADVISORS LOOK FOR: THE VOLUNTEER EXPERTS WHO ADVISE GRANTMAKING IN WEST, EAST, CENTRAL, AND SOUTHERN AFRICA IDENTIFY COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS THAT ARE IMPLEMENTING SOLUTIONS TO ADDRESS EACH REGION'S MOST PRESSING CHALLENGES. Four African regional boards, so every part of the continent has one. THE COMMITMENT IT STATES: TO LISTEN TO LOCAL POPULATIONS AND PLACE TRUST AND DECISION-MAKING POWER DIRECTLY IN THE HANDS OF COMMUNITIES TO PROTECT AND RESTORE THEIR OWN LAND, BIODIVERSITY, WATER, AND THE HEALTH OF THEIR FAMILIES. THE ONE OPEN DOOR RECORDED, AND ITS TERMS: A MINI GRANT FOR SMALL AFRICAN CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, ADMINISTERED BY THIS FUND BUT WITH APPLICATIONS SENT TO A NAMED AFRICAN PESTICIDE NETWORK — A 3–4 PAGE PROPOSAL WITH OBJECTIVES, METHODOLOGY, EXPECTED RESULTS AND A DETAILED BUDGET IN US DOLLARS, A CEILING OF UP TO $3,500, ORGANISATIONS NEEDING TO BE REGISTERED WITH DOCUMENTS SUBMITTED BEFORE PAYOUT, AND PROJECTS EXPECTED TO BE GRASSROOTS-BASED WITH A HOLISTIC CONCEPT CONSIDERING ALL STAKEHOLDERS. Three to four pages, and the money is administered by this fund but applied for through a regional partner. That is the pattern worth watching for: where the fund itself takes no applications, its African partners sometimes open windows in their own names. Registration is required for this one, unlike the advisor route. THE SPIN-OFF MODEL FOR REGIONS THAT WANT THEIR OWN FUND: IT WORKS WITH GRANT ADVISORS AROUND THE WORLD TO ESTABLISH INDEPENDENT FUNDS IN THEIR HOME REGIONS — ADVISORS TO THESE NEW, AUTONOMOUS NONPROFITS CONTINUE TO RECOMMEND RECIPIENTS AND ALSO RAISE MONEY FOR THEIR OWN GRANTMAKING. Advisors have spun out autonomous national and regional funds. For an African network wanting to become a grantmaker rather than only a grantee, that route already exists and has been walked. AND THE WARNING THIS FILE RECORDS PLAINLY: A PUBLIC COMMENT THREAD ON A GRANT LISTING SHOWS SOMEONE REPORTING A NOTIFICATION THAT THEY HAD WON THIS GRANT, FOLLOWED BY QUESTIONS ASKING FOR PERSONAL AND BANK DETAILS — THE PUBLISHED ADVICE BEING TO CONTACT THE FUND DIRECTLY TO VERIFY. A fund that takes no unsolicited applications is a gift to fraudsters, because an unexpected award notice is exactly what its real model would produce. Nobody legitimate needs your bank details before you have spoken to a named person at the organisation. Verify through the published contact, never through the address that wrote to you. WHO IT SUITS: African community organisations resisting land grabs, oil and mining harm, or protecting defenders — including unregistered ones, reached through a regional advisor. CAVEATS: NO UNSOLICITED APPLICATIONS, SO THE ROUTE IS VISIBILITY IN REGIONAL NETWORKS RATHER THAN A PROPOSAL, AND GRANTS ARE SMALL — use it for the costs nothing else covers. For the fund that waives registration, bank account and ID, the Central African Republic's entry; for unconditional cash to forest communities, Côte d'Ivoire's entry; for long-term landscape money, Mauritania's entry.

trackers.name: IBAHRI (International Bar Association's Human Rights Institute) — an institute that defends lawyers and judges who are harassed, intimidated or arrested — trial observations in 24 countries, fact-finding missions, and help establishing bar associations where the profession is weak, with a published contact address
trackers.desc: THEY DEFEND THE LAWYER WHEN DEFENDING YOU GETS THEM ARRESTED — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S CÔTE D'IVOIRE ENTRY COVERS THE BARRISTERS' COMMITTEE THAT ALSO OBSERVES TRIALS AND FILES AMICUS BRIEFS — A DIFFERENT BODY, AND ITS HOST IS NOT SHIPPED; ITS ZAMBIA BUCKET MENTIONS AN INTERNATIONAL BAR ASSOCIATION IN PASSING WITHOUT DESCRIBING IT; ITS KENYA BUCKET CARRIES A COMMISSION OF JURISTS NAME. NONE IS RESTATED. A PAN-AFRICAN PRO BONO LITIGATOR WAS CHECKED FIRST THIS ROUND AND FOUND ALREADY FILED UNDER GAMBIA, SO IT WAS NOT DUPLICATED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. WHO IT DEFENDS, WHICH IS THE FIND: IT SUPPORTS LAWYERS AND JUDGES WHO ARE ARBITRARILY HARASSED, INTIMIDATED OR ARRESTED, THROUGH ADVOCACY AND TRIAL OBSERVATIONS — BELIEVING IN THE FUNDAMENTAL RIGHT OF THE WORLD'S CITIZENS TO HAVE DISPUTES HEARD BY AN INDEPENDENT JUDICIARY, AND FOR JUDGES AND LAWYERS TO BE ABLE TO PRACTISE FREELY WITHOUT INTERFERENCE. The failure point this file returns to: a community finds an advocate, the advocate is threatened, struck off or charged, and the case dies with them. This institute treats that lawyer as the subject of its work rather than as a service provider to somebody else's case — and a threatened lawyer, or their colleagues, can raise it directly. THE BAR-BUILDING WORK, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: RUNNING PROGRAMMES IN MULTIPLE COUNTRIES, IT CONDUCTS FACT-FINDING MISSIONS, TRIAL OBSERVATIONS AND SUPPORTS THE ESTABLISHMENT OF BAR ASSOCIATIONS IN ORDER TO PROTECT AND BUILD THE CAPACITIES OF THE LEGAL PROFESSION. SUPPORTS THE ESTABLISHMENT OF BAR ASSOCIATIONS. This file recorded, under Botswana, that an independent grouping of human rights lawyers is the partner category international bodies will resource; here is the organisation that helps constitute one. Where the national bar is captured, absent or afraid, that is the long answer rather than the case-by-case one. THE FOUR-PART METHOD IT PUBLISHES: CAPACITY BUILDING AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO THE JUDICIARY; FACT-FINDING TO DOCUMENT ALLEGED HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS; HIGH-LEVEL ADVOCACY BEFORE THE UNITED NATIONS AND OTHER KEY INTERNATIONAL STAKEHOLDERS; AND TRIAL OBSERVATION. Four distinct requests, and they are separable. Fact-finding suits a situation that has not reached court; observation suits one that has. THE TRIAL OBSERVATION RECORD AND ITS LEGAL BASIS: ESTABLISHED IN 1995, FIRST OBSERVATION IN 1996, OBSERVATIONS SINCE UNDERTAKEN IN 24 COUNTRIES ACROSS COMMON LAW, CIVIL LAW AND SHARIA JURISDICTIONS — ALL OF THE COUNTRIES ARE PARTIES TO THE INTERNATIONAL COVENANT ON CIVIL AND POLITICAL RIGHTS, WHICH CONTAINS EXTENSIVE OBLIGATIONS RELATING TO FAIR TRIAL PROCEDURES. The covenant is the hook, and almost every African state is a party to it. That is what makes an observation more than a courtesy visit: the country has already accepted the standard being measured against, and the report is written in those terms. WHAT UNFAIRNESS CAN CONSIST OF, IN ITS OWN TERMS: THE FAIRNESS OF A TRIAL MAY RELATE TO THE SUBSTANCE OF THE ACCUSATIONS, WHAT MOTIVATED THE BRINGING OF THE ACCUSATION, THE PROCESS OF THE TRIAL, AND THE INDEPENDENCE OF THE JUDGE. WHAT MOTIVATED THE BRINGING OF THE ACCUSATION is the limb that matters most here. A prosecution brought to break a land campaign is unfair in its motive even where the procedure is impeccable, and that is expressly within what an observation examines. THE UNITED NATIONS ROUTE IT OPENS: A UNITED NATIONS PROGRAMME UNDERTAKING ADVOCACY, RESEARCH AND TRAINING — WHICH PRODUCES GUIDELINES FOR LAWYERS, JUDGES AND LEGAL PROFESSIONALS TO ENGAGE WITH UNITED NATIONS HUMAN RIGHTS MECHANISMS. Free published guidance on how a national lawyer actually files into the UN mechanisms. This file has recorded those mechanisms as theoretically open and practically unreachable; the guidelines are the missing instructions. WHAT IT ADVOCATES FOR AT THAT LEVEL: GREATER PROMOTION, PROTECTION AND ENFORCEMENT OF HUMAN RIGHTS IN THE ADMINISTRATION OF JUSTICE, AND THE UNITED NATIONS STANDARDS ON THE ROLE OF JUDGES, LAWYERS AND PROSECUTORS — STANDARDS THAT ARE KEY BENCHMARKS IN MONITORING A DEVELOPMENT GOAL ON ACCESS TO JUSTICE FOR ALL BY 2030. WHAT IT PRODUCES: EXPERT REPORTS WITH KEY RECOMMENDATIONS, DELIVERING TIMELY AND RELIABLE INFORMATION ON HUMAN RIGHTS AND THE LEGAL PROFESSION — CONCERNING THREATS TO LAW, POLICY, INSTITUTIONS AND PRACTICE, WITH RECOMMENDATIONS FOR LEGAL AND POLICY REFORM AT NATIONAL, REGIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL LEVELS. THE ARGUMENT IT MAKES FOR WHY THIS MATTERS: WHEN THE LEGAL PROFESSION IS NOT ABLE TO FUNCTION INDEPENDENTLY OR EFFECTIVELY, THIS GIVES RISE TO HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS, IMPUNITY AND INJUSTICE. WHO IT CONVENES: LAWYERS, JUDGES, NGOs, CIVIL SOCIETY GROUPS, ACADEMICS AND STUDENTS — AS PART OF THE WORLD'S LEADING ORGANISATION OF INTERNATIONAL LEGAL PRACTITIONERS, BAR ASSOCIATIONS AND LAW SOCIETIES. NGOs AND CIVIL SOCIETY GROUPS are convened alongside the profession, so a community organisation is not outside the room. Membership is one of the few ways in this file to sit with the international bar rather than write to it. THE MEDIA PANEL IT RUNS THE SECRETARIAT FOR: A HIGH LEVEL PANEL OF LEGAL EXPERTS ON MEDIA FREEDOM, AN INDEPENDENT ADVISORY BODY OF TOP INTERNATIONAL LAWYERS WHO OFFER LEGAL ADVICE TO SUPPORT AND PROTECT A VIBRANT, FREE AND INDEPENDENT MEDIA. Where a journalist covering your land dispute is prosecuted — which this file has recorded as the way a story is killed — that panel is a separate, senior source of legal advice reachable through the same institute. AND ITS STANDING, FUNDING AND CONTACT: ESTABLISHED IN 1995 UNDER THE HONORARY PRESIDENCY OF A NAMED AFRICAN HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDER, IT IS AN AUTONOMOUS AND FINANCIALLY INDEPENDENT ENTITY SUPPORTED BY ITS MEMBERS AND FUNDING BODIES — WITH A PUBLISHED EMAIL ADDRESS AND OPEN MEMBERSHIP, KEEPING MEMBERS INFORMED OF ACTIVITIES, PUBLICATIONS, EVENTS AND OPPORTUNITIES TO GET INVOLVED IN ITS RULE OF LAW PROJECTS. AUTONOMOUS AND FINANCIALLY INDEPENDENT of the bar body it sits inside, which is what lets it criticise governments that member firms work for. WHO IT SUITS: African lawyers and judges under pressure for taking land or environmental cases, and the organisations whose counsel is being threatened — plus anyone seeking a fair-trial observation or a fact-finding mission. CAVEATS: ITS SUBJECT IS THE LEGAL PROFESSION AND FAIR TRIALS RATHER THAN YOUR UNDERLYING LAND CLAIM, AND IT DOES NOT REPRESENT PARTIES; PROGRAMMES ARE SELECTED AND CAPACITY IS FINITE — approach with the lawyer's situation, not the case's merits. For the barristers who file amicus briefs into national courts, Côte d'Ivoire's entry; for a pan-African pro bono litigator before the continental bodies, Gambia's entry.

trackers.name: Rainforest Alliance's Cameroon community forestry programme — four community-owned forest enterprises, 30,000 ha of approved management plans; and the 1994 Forest Law pre-emption right communities are supposed to be offered before logging permits
trackers.desc: YOU HAVE FIRST REFUSAL ON THE FOREST — AND NOBODY TELLS YOU — method and adjacency declared first: NINTH ACQUISITION-ONLY ROUND. A COMMUNITY RIGHT-TO-BUY REGIME WAS WITHDRAWN THIS ROUND BEFORE WRITING — FOREIGN STATUTE, A MECHANISM RATHER THAN AN ORGANISATION, AND NOT AVAILABLE TO AFRICAN LOCALS. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THREE HOSTS AND SIX DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; THE SHIPPED HOST AND THREE FACTS ABSENT. THREE MATCHED AND WERE READ IN FULL, THE CLOSEST BEING A DR CONGO ENTRY ABOUT A NETWORK THAT HAS SECURED PERPETUAL COMMUNITY FOREST TITLES OVER 223,000 HECTARES — THAT ENTRY IS ABOUT OBTAINING THE TITLE; THIS ONE IS ABOUT WHAT HAPPENS AFTER IT. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRIORITY RIGHT THAT EXISTS ON PAPER, WHICH IS THE FIND: THE 1994 FOREST LAW STATES THAT COMMUNITIES HAVE PRE-EMPTION RIGHTS, THAT IS PRIORITY RIGHTS, TO CREATE COMMUNITY FORESTS — THEY SHOULD BE NOTIFIED AND GIVEN AN OPPORTUNITY TO PROPOSE A COMMUNITY FOREST BEFORE OTHER TYPES OF PERMITS, SUCH AS SALES OF STANDING TIMBER, ARE ALLOCATED IN AN AREA. A statutory first refusal over the forest beside your village, thirty years old, and no acquisition resource in this file has mentioned it. The mechanism is the strongest available anywhere in these 1,031 entries: not a fund to apply to, but a legal duty on the state to offer you the area BEFORE a logging permit is granted. The question to put to the forestry service in writing is simply whether that notification was ever given. WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS WITH IT: IN REALITY THE RULES TO ENSURE COMMUNITIES ARE GIVEN PRIORITY ARE RARELY FOLLOWED, AND LOCAL AUTHORITIES HAVE FREQUENTLY SHOWN LITTLE OR NO INTEREST — AND OFTEN ACTIVE RESISTANCE. Recorded plainly, because the gap between the right and its practice is itself the case: a permit issued without the notification the law requires is a permit with a defect on its face. THE COLLAPSE RATE, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: THE PROCESS IS RELATIVELY TECHNICAL AND FEW COMMUNITIES CAN NEGOTIATE IT WITHOUT EXTERNAL ASSISTANCE, USUALLY FROM NGOs — AND MANY STATUTORY COMMUNITY FORESTS WHICH INITIALLY APPEARED TO BE OBTAINING SOME DEGREE OF SUCCESS FELL APART ONCE NGO SUPPORT WAS WITHDRAWN. The single most important warning in this file's acquisition entries. Winning the forest is not the end; the management plan, the annual certificate and the buyer relationships all need capacity that arrived with the NGO and left with it. Ask any supporting organisation what happens in year six. THE ENTERPRISES BUILT TO ANSWER THAT, AND THE NUMBERS: FOUR LOCAL COMMUNITY-OWNED FOREST ENTERPRISES ESTABLISHED AS A TOOL FOR POOLING INVESTMENTS IN EQUIPMENT AND SOCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE, INCREASING NEGOTIATING POWER AND IMPROVING ACCESS TO MARKETS — WITH INCOME FROM THE SALE OF TIMBER DOUBLING, AND AMONG COMMUNITIES THAT HAVE TAKEN CONTROL OF FOREST HARVESTING, REVENUES INCREASING MORE THAN FIVE-FOLD. FIVEFOLD when the community does the harvesting rather than selling standing timber to an operator. That figure is the argument for taking control of the operation rather than licensing it out — and pooling equipment across several communities is how a village affords the machinery to do it. THE SCALE AND WHO IT REACHED: 12 COMMUNITIES HOME TO APPROXIMATELY 10,000 INDIVIDUALS, INCLUDING MEMBERS OF THE BAKA PEOPLE — WITH APPROVED FOREST MANAGEMENT PLANS COVERING ABOUT 30,000 HECTARES, BUSINESS ALLIANCES FORGED WITH BUYERS, AND NINE COMMUNITIES SIGNING AGREEMENTS; CARRIED OUT IN COOPERATION WITH TWO LOCAL NGOs. THE COST BARRIER NAMED PLAINLY: THE PROCESS REQUIRES SPECIALISED STRUCTURES SUCH AS CONSULTANTS OR NGOs AT PROHIBITIVE COSTS, AND RENEWING THE ANNUAL OPERATIONS CERTIFICATE IS NO LESS EXPENSIVE. The recurring annual cost is the part that catches communities out. Budget for the renewal before applying, not after. THE DRAFTING FAULT BEHIND IT: THE LEGISLATOR DID NOT ADEQUATELY CONSIDER THE SIGNIFICANT DIFFERENCES BETWEEN THE TWO TYPES OF FOREST TITLE — THOSE FOR ARTISANAL EXPLOITATION AND THOSE FOR INDUSTRIAL LOGGING — AND BETWEEN THE TWO TYPES OF STAKEHOLDER, DEPRIVED VILLAGE COMMUNITIES AND PRIVATE OPERATORS. A village is held to paperwork designed for a logging company. Naming that asymmetry is the basis for asking for simplified procedures, which is a reform several organisations are already pursuing. THE MANAGEMENT PLAN PROBLEMS TO EXPECT: PLAN QUALITY VARIES ACCORDING TO THE INDIVIDUALS AND ORGANIZATIONS THAT PREPARE THEM, AND PREPARATION IS OFTEN NOT DONE IN A PARTICIPATORY MANNER, WHICH DIRECTLY HINDERS EXECUTION DUE TO A PERCEIVED LACK OF OWNERSHIP. A plan written for the community rather than with it fails at execution, because nobody in the village recognises it as theirs. Insist on being in the room while it is drafted. THE FIVE APPROVAL PROBLEMS DOCUMENTED: ASSESSMENT CRITERIA VARY ACCORDING TO THE NGO PRESENTING THE PLAN; THE APPROVAL DEADLINE IS VERY FAST FOR SOME NGOs AND SLOW FOR OTHERS; COMMUNITIES OFTEN BYPASS THE MINISTRY'S EXTERNAL SERVICES AND SUBMIT DIRECTLY TO CENTRAL SERVICES; PLANS ARE OFTEN REJECTED FOR MINOR DETAILS OF FORM; AND SOME ADMINISTRATIVE AUTHORITIES OBSTRUCT THE SIGNING OF THE MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT. Which NGO presents your plan changes how fast it is approved. That is worth knowing before choosing a partner — ask how long their last three submissions took. And rejection for MINOR DETAILS OF FORM is the standard delay tactic; submit early and expect at least one return. WHAT IS RECOMMENDED TO FIX THE CONTRACTS: LEGAL REFORM TO IMPOSE STANDARD CONTRACT GUARANTEES FOR THE INTERESTS OF ALL PARTIES, AND A MINISTRY REPRESENTATIVE PRESENT DURING THE SIGNING OF CONTRACTS TO HELP ENSURE LEGALITY AND CONTRACT COMPLIANCE — WITH ONGOING AND MEANINGFUL PARTICIPATION OF COMMUNITY MEMBERS NOT ONLY AT THE BEGINNING BUT THROUGHOUT. Asking a forestry official to witness the signature costs nothing and changes what an operator will attempt in the room. THE TRAINING ALREADY DELIVERED ACROSS THE REGION: 1,300 FOREST COMMUNITY MEMBERS TRAINED IN MAPPING AND SECURING FOREST LAND RIGHTS, GENDER INCLUSION AND WOMEN'S ENTREPRENEURSHIP, COMMUNITY GOVERNANCE AND BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT IN TWO NAMED COUNTRIES — WITH POLICY WORK IN FOUR NAMED COUNTRIES, AND A REGIONAL EVENT DRAWING 55 PARTICIPANTS FROM EIGHT COUNTRIES INCLUDING TWO FORESTRY MINISTRIES AND COMMUNITY REPRESENTATIVES WHO HAVE WORKED FOR COMMUNITY FOREST RIGHTS FOR 20 YEARS. MAPPING AND SECURING FOREST LAND RIGHTS as a trainable skill, already delivered to 1,300 people. The trainers exist; the question is whether they have reached your region. AND THE PUBLISHED PROCEDURE MANUAL THAT GOVERNS IT ALL: A MANUAL OF THE PROCEDURES FOR THE ATTRIBUTION, AND NORMS FOR THE MANAGEMENT, OF COMMUNITY FORESTS, ALONGSIDE DECREE No. 95-531 OF 23 AUGUST 1995 LAYING DOWN THE PROCEDURE FOR IMPLEMENTING THE FOREST REGIME. There is a published manual. Obtain it before hiring anyone to guide you through the process, and check what they propose against it. WHO IT SUITS: forest-edge communities in Central Africa who want the forest allocated to them rather than to a logging permit — and any community already holding a community forest that is struggling after its supporting NGO left. CAVEATS: THE STATUTORY DETAIL IS ONE COUNTRY'S, THOUGH THE REGIONAL TRAINING AND POLICY WORK SPANS SEVERAL; THE ROUTE IS TECHNICAL AND CARRIES RECURRING COSTS, AND ITS OWN DOCUMENTED RECORD INCLUDES MANY FAILURES AFTER SUPPORT WAS WITHDRAWN. For securing perpetual community forest titles at scale, DR Congo's entry; for the schedule of obligations a company owes your village, the Republic of Congo's entry.
