trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Benin — audits government accounts and the use of public money.

trackers.name: Benin — Ministère de l’Économie et des Finances
trackers.desc: National budget authority; governs & manages the economy and public finances and publishes the State budget, Benin. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Benin.

trackers.name: Benin — MonEntreprise.bj (APIEx)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the APIEx electronic one-stop window for company creation, registration & management, Benin. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: ECOWAS Court of Justice — file directly, but sue the State
trackers.desc: A COURT YOU CAN REACH WITHOUT EXHAUSTING DOMESTIC REMEDIES. The ECOWAS Community Court of Justice has held human rights jurisdiction since 2005 and has broad access and standing rules permitting individuals and NGOs to bypass national courts and file directly. THE PRECEDENT: in SERAP v Federal Republic of Nigeria (ECW/CCJ/APP/08/09) the Court dismissed all three preliminary objections — no locus standi, no jurisdiction, statute-barred — and rejected the government's attempt to exclude an Amnesty International report from the evidence. NGO research was admitted as evidence, which matters when no state data exists. It found violations of articles 1 and 24 of the African Charter — article 24: ‘all peoples shall have the right to a general satisfactory environment favourable to their development’ — and of article 21, the right to natural wealth and resources. THE FAULT WAS AN OMISSION: the state ‘defaulted in its duties in terms of vigilance and diligence’, and ‘the omission to act and to prevent damage to the environment characterises the violation’. It ordered restoration within the shortest possible time and measures to prevent further damage, citing the ICJ that the environment ‘is not an abstraction but represents the living space, the quality of life and the very health of human beings, including generations unborn’. THE LIMIT THAT DECIDES WHO YOU SUE: the Court held it had no jurisdiction over the private oil corporations, which were struck from the suit. You sue the State for failing to regulate; you cannot sue the company here — naming one as respondent loses that part of the case. AND PLAN FOR ENFORCEMENT: commentary records the Court did not identify a means for Nigeria to implement the ruling, and the ICJ later wrote to the President pressing for enforcement — judgment is the start of an enforcement campaign, not a self-executing remedy. Proposals to require exhaustion of domestic remedies were rejected by ECOWAS experts and Heads of Government, so the direct-access rule has been tested and held.

trackers.name: ORFAO — comparative land-law tables, and a directive in draft
trackers.desc: COMPARATIVE LEGAL TABLES FOR YOUR COUNTRY AND ITS NEIGHBOURS, IN ONE DOCUMENT. The Observatoire Régional du Foncier Rural en Afrique de l'Ouest (ORFAO), hosted by UEMOA, publishes a regional study on rural land markets containing side-by-side ‘cadre légal comparé’ tables — one covering Bénin, Burkina Faso, Côte d'Ivoire and Sénégal, another Guinée-Bissau, Mali, Niger and Togo — plus typologies of direct and indirect interventions in land markets and a table of regulatory issues and families of instruments. If you need to know what instrument exists in your country and whether a neighbour has a stronger one, that is the document — comparative tables let a campaign point to a neighbour's provision as an achievable ask rather than a novelty. A WINDOW IS OPENING: on 26 June 2026 in Ouagadougou the UEMOA ministers for urbanisme, habitat, domaines et cadastre approved a draft directive to harmonise rules on immatriculation foncière, accès au titre de propriété and a système d'information foncière, aiming at a common framework of land governance. BE PRECISE ABOUT STATUS: that was a DRAFT directive approved by ministers, not an adopted and transposed instrument — check adoption and transposition before relying on it. But transposition is the moment domestic land law is reopened in each state, and that is when community provisions can be argued for. FOR A GRAZING OR TRANSHUMANCE DISPUTE: a regional pastoral situation bulletin covers 11 West African countries with the support of decentralised technical services — an evidence source drawing on the same services you would otherwise approach one by one. RECORDED PLAINLY: cattle theft is documented as a driver of conflict and instability in the Sahel, so a land dispute here may sit inside a security context that changes what is safe to do. And confirm your state's current ECOWAS standing — several members are recorded as suspended.

trackers.name: Eco-Bénin — it sets up community conservation areas that the villages themselves manage, and it sacralised 500 hectares of mangrove
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Beninese NGO founded in 1999 that helps communities create Aires Communautaires de Conservation de la Biodiversité (ACCB) — community conservation areas — and then leaves the villages managing them. Its established areas include the Bouche du Roy and Lac Ahémé in the Mono transboundary biosphere reserve. THE PROTECTION IT USES THAT NO LAW PROVIDES, AND WHICH IS WORTH THINKING ABOUT ANYWHERE CUSTOM STILL BINDS: alongside ecological restoration, Eco-Bénin has placed 500 hectares of mangrove under the protection of the Zangbéto divinity — the “night watchman” — sacralising the forest so that local custom, not only the state, forbids cutting it. Around 500 hectares of degraded mangrove have been restored across the two community areas, 475,000 mangrove seedlings produced in a single year, and more than 1,500 community members trained in mangrove management. WHY THE MONEY SIDE IS THE POINT: the organisation runs community ecotourism as the economic pillar, projects are managed by the host communities themselves with the stated aim that they become autonomous, and between 10 and 25 per cent of takings goes to community projects — a school repair, latrines — or to the poorest households. Conservation that pays is conservation that survives a bad harvest. It also distributes improved cookstoves to cut pressure on forest, and works with allies including a dam-affected persons' committee at Adjarala and the Lac Ahémé fishers' association. WHO IT SUITS: coastal, wetland and forest-edge communities in southern and northern Benin that want an area recognised and managed locally rather than allocated away. Zogbadjè, Calavi; +229 95 28 52 20; contact@ecobenin.org. CAVEATS: this is conservation and ecotourism development, not legal defence — there is no litigation capacity here, and no purchase of land; a successor entity, ECOBENIN INTERNATIONAL, now also uses the name, so confirm which body you are dealing with.

trackers.name: Synergie Paysanne — Benin's peasant union, which funded legal support for 200 farmers dispossessed by a member of parliament
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Synergie Paysanne (Synpa), founded in 2002 by young farmers and Benin's first peasant union, with around 2,000 members, campaigning on family farming, against GMOs and agrofuels, and squarely on land grabbing. WHAT IT HAS ACTUALLY DONE FOR DISPOSSESSED FARMERS: in 2008 it funded legal support for an association of 200 farmers dispossessed of their land by a member of parliament, in a village in the Plateau department in the south-east. It also promoted a practical tool most smallholders never hear about — the formalisation of oral customary contracts for the loan, gift and leasing of farmland, which it pushed with landowners and mayors to open up land that urban elites were hoarding, and which was written into the 2007 rural land law on its proposals. If you farm land you do not own under an oral arrangement, getting that arrangement written down is the cheapest protection available to you. THE DEFEAT IT IS HONEST TO RECORD: between 2010 and 2013 the union mobilised hard against the draft land code, which it regarded as an instrument for agribusiness and land grabbing. Researchers who studied that campaign concluded it was a political failure — technical advocacy plus media denunciation won the union institutional recognition and a seat in the drafting arenas, but not the changes it sought, and the technical investment weakened its collective dynamic. Advocacy alone did not stop the code. WHO IT SUITS: Beninese smallholders and farming associations facing dispossession, large-scale land acquisitions, or insecure customary access. CAVEATS: NO CURRENT CANONICAL WEBSITE WAS VERIFIED — this entry points at the union's own blog, which is dated; approach through Beninese farmer networks. It is a union, not a law firm: it has financed legal support rather than provided it, and Benin's Eco-Bénin entry covers community conservation areas.

trackers.name: Benin's aide juridique decree of October 2024 — and the three French words that decide which help you are actually asking for
trackers.desc: WHAT THE NEW LAW GIVES YOU: Benin adopted in Council of Ministers the Décret N°2024-1275 of 23 OCTOBER 2024 regulating AIDE JURIDIQUE in the Republic of Benin — the newest legal-aid instrument recorded in this file. Its stated purpose is to secure equal access to law and justice and to prevent discrimination in access to justice whose origin might be ILLITERACY, IGNORANCE OF ONE’S RIGHTS, ethnicity, gender, religion, social or economic status, disability or any other cause. Illiteracy and not knowing your rights are named in the decree itself as forms of discrimination to be remedied — that is unusually direct, and it is worth quoting when someone tells you the problem is that you do not understand the procedure. THE VOCABULARY THAT DECIDES YOUR REQUEST, and it applies across every francophone country in this file: AIDE JURIDIQUE is the whole set of free assistance mechanisms — awareness-raising, advice, analysis AND representation before a court or any conciliation or arbitration body; AIDE JUDICIAIRE is assistance to a litigant before the court itself; AIDE JURIDICTIONNELLE is the FINANCIAL aid the state grants to litigants whose income is insufficient. Ask for the wrong one and you will be sent away: if you need money for costs say aide juridictionnelle, if you need someone beside you in court say aide judiciaire, if you do not yet know what you need say aide juridique. A published national brochure explains the Benin scheme in question-and-answer form. WHO IT SUITS: Beninese households — including farmers facing dispossession — who cannot pay for legal help, and anyone in francophone Africa who needs to name the right service. CAVEATS: A DECREE ADOPTED IN OCTOBER 2024 IS A NEW MACHINE — confirm locally which office receives applications and whether it is operating in your commune before relying on it; seven countries in this file have statutes whose implementing machinery never arrived. For the peasant union that funded legal support for 200 dispossessed farmers, Benin's Synergie Paysanne entry; for community conservation areas, Eco-Bénin.

trackers.name: Benin's sacred forests and arrêté 021/MEHU — a national framework for COMMUNITY MANAGEMENT of sacred forests, with recognition through the mairie and the forest inspectorate
trackers.desc: THE FOREST NOBODY DARED CUT: Benin lost roughly 44,000 HECTARES of forest between 2001 and 2022 — 26% of its cover — yet certain spaces resisted, NOT through a law or a public policy but through CENTURIES OF COMMUNITY MANAGEMENT AND CULTURAL PROTECTION. THE INSTRUMENT THAT PUT LAW BEHIND THAT: the INTERMINISTERIAL ARRÊTÉ N°021/MEHU/MDGLAT/DC/SGM/DGFRN/SA OF 16 NOVEMBER 2012, ESTABLISHING A FRAMEWORK FOR THE COMMUNITY MANAGEMENT OF SACRED FORESTS IN BENIN, which ALLOWS LOCAL FOREST MANAGEMENT BY THE LOCAL POPULATIONS THEMSELVES and confers RECOGNITION THROUGH STRUCTURES INCLUDING THE MAIRIE AND THE FOREST INSPECTORATE, WHICH THEN ACCOMPANY the enrichment and conservation actions undertaken. Your commune hall and the forest inspectorate become partners rather than obstacles — that is the whole point of the 2012 arrêté, and it is the cheapest recognition route recorded in West Africa. HOW IT REACHED THE VILLAGES: the PROJET D'INTÉGRATION DES FORÊTS SACRÉES DANS LE SYSTÈME D'AIRES PROTÉGÉES (PIFSAP) integrated sacred forests into the formal protected-area system, strengthened the legal and institutional framework and promoted COMMUNITY CO-MANAGEMENT; named forests recognised through it include WIANSO, SINATABÉ and WÊWÊRÉ at Bembèrèkè (Borgou), each managed by a named community — Gandé and Sinadouwirou among them — and each proposed as a protected area before 2000 but only made effective locally by the 2012 arrêté. If your forest was proposed for protection decades ago and nothing happened, the 2012 framework is the instrument that finished the job for three named forests. Cite them. WHAT COUNTS AS ONE: Beninese sacred forests fall in four categories — fetish forests (nearly 60%), secret-society forests (21%), COMMUNITY FORESTS PROTECTED COLLECTIVELY BY VILLAGERS (10%), and CEMETERY FORESTS where graves are integrated into the woodland (8%) — supplying medicinal plants, fruits and animal products, and protecting soils against erosion. A burial ground is a recognised category here, which matters everywhere in this file where a community's strongest claim is its ancestors rather than a title. A forestry engineer's stated priority is equipping these forests with FUNCTIONING MANAGEMENT ORGANS AND TOOLS, arguing communes can mobilise resources through them; a Beninese NGO won a UNESCO-Japan prize in 2025 for restoring the OOKPO sacred forest at Pobè, in existence since the 17th century. WHO IT SUITS: Beninese villages holding a sacred grove, burial forest or collectively protected woodland. CAVEATS: RECOGNITION UNDER AN ARRÊTÉ, NOT TITLE — the registry records continuing pressure for a full legal declaration. For Benin's three-word aide juridique vocabulary and the 2024 décret, the legal aid entry.

trackers.name: Benin's FNEC — the national environment and climate fund, with a published annual call for projects, downloadable eligibility guide and budget template, and 25 communes funded
trackers.desc: WHERE THE ENVIRONMENT MONEY IS AND HOW TO APPLY: the FONDS NATIONAL POUR L'ENVIRONNEMENT ET LE CLIMAT (FNEC), a financing mechanism for programmes and projects protecting and rationally managing the environment, combating climate change and promoting sustainable development, created by décret n°2017-128 of 27 February 2017 and re-founded by décret n°2021-191 of 5 May 2021, under the ministry for the living environment and sustainable development, with its seat in Cotonou next to the maison des médias. THE PART A VILLAGE CAN USE: FNEC RUNS A PUBLISHED ANNUAL APPEL À PROJETS, and publishes for download the GUIDE DE FORMULATION, D'ÉLIGIBILITÉ ET DE SÉLECTION, an EXCEL BUDGET TEMPLATE, the monitoring-evaluation manual, and its GUIDELINES FOR IDENTIFYING ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL RISKS, along with the procès-verbal of the admissibility review for each round. A downloadable eligibility guide and budget template is the rarest thing in African environmental finance — most funds publish an announcement and nothing else. Download both before you write a word, and read the admissibility procès-verbal from the last round to see why applications were rejected. WHY IT REACHES FURTHER THAN A NATIONAL FUND USUALLY DOES: FNEC is ACCREDITED TO THE GREEN CLIMATE FUND (2019), RE-ACCREDITED TO THE ADAPTATION FUND, and ELIGIBLE to a German ministry's small-grants initiative; it collaborates with public, private AND NON-GOVERNMENTAL structures whose activities serve national environment and natural-resource strategies. THE RESULT WORTH CITING: BENIN WAS THE FIRST AFRICAN COUNTRY to join the LoCAL mechanism and obtain Green Climate Fund financing to scale it — the SAP032 LoCAL project, launched 8 October 2024, worth 5.473 BILLION FCFA from the GCF plus about 288.79 MILLION FCFA from FNEC, DELIVERING CLIMATE FINANCE TO 25 COMMUNES to strengthen local climate governance and raise adaptation investment in agriculture and food security, health, water and the built environment. Money routed to communes rather than to ministries is the shape to ask for: if your commune is among the 25, the adaptation budget is already in your mairie's planning process, and that is a meeting you can attend. WHO IT SUITS: Beninese communes, associations and community groups with an environment, climate-adaptation or natural-resource project. CAVEATS: A COMPETITIVE STATE FUND ON AN ANNUAL CYCLE — read the current call before assuming eligibility. For sacred forests and the community-management framework, Benin's arrêté 021/MEHU entry; for community conservation areas villages hold, Eco-Bénin; for the peasant union that funded legal support, Synergie Paysanne.

trackers.name: Nature Tropicale ONG, Cotonou — holds the presidency of Benin's national IUCN committee and a signed government agreement against environmental crimes, with a published address and four phone lines
trackers.desc: THE NGO WITH A GOVERNMENT AGREEMENT, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT KIND OF ALLY: NATURE TROPICALE ONG, CREATED 1995, a legally recognised Beninese non-profit whose mission is to promote the conservation and rational use of biological diversity through information, education and awareness of the different actors and above all of young people. SINCE 2004 IT HAS BEEN THE FIRST BENINESE NGO ADMITTED AS A MEMBER OF THE WORLD CONSERVATION UNION, and IT HOLDS THE PRESIDENCY OF THE NATIONAL IUCN COMMITTEE FOR BENIN. THE TWO INSTRUMENTS THAT MATTER: IT SIGNED A PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT WITH THE GOVERNMENT OF BENIN IN DECEMBER 2016 FOR THE FIGHT AGAINST ENVIRONMENTAL CRIMES, AND AN ACCORD-CADRE WITH THE GOVERNMENT IN MAY 2019. An NGO holding a signed agreement with the state on environmental crime is one whose report to a ministry arrives as a partner's report rather than a complaint. If what is happening near you is an offence rather than a permitted project, that is the door — and the national IUCN committee presidency means it also carries your case into the international conservation system. WHERE TO FIND IT AND WHAT IT RUNS: Lot 4477 R Yagbé, 06 BP 1015, Akpakpa PK 3, Cotonou, with FOUR PUBLISHED PHONE LINES and several email addresses including info@naturetropicale.org. Since May 1996 it has run in Cotonou the FIRST MUSEUM OF NATURAL SCIENCES in Benin — a centre for animation, education, training and leisure with collections in five specialised departments: aquariology, zoology, entomology, a library and video library, and the promotion of mini-livestock farming; and from 2017 it began installing at GRAND-POPO the GBENAWA centre for environmental education and sustainable development, the FIRST PUBLIC TROPICAL AQUARIUM IN BENIN. Its marine turtle and manatee protection work has been extended NATIONALLY along the coast and into the WETLANDS OF SOUTHERN BENIN through education of all stakeholders via the media. A permanent public centre in the capital plus a second on the coast means this is an organisation with places you can physically go and people who are there tomorrow — rarer than it sounds. TWO MORE NAMED BENINESE ORGANISATIONS working on biodiversity conservation through their own programmes: the ASSOCIATION VIVE LE PAYSAN NOUVEAU (AVPN) and CREDI ONG. WHO IT SUITS: Beninese communities on the coast or in the southern wetlands, and anyone whose problem is an environmental offence. CAVEATS: A CONSERVATION AND EDUCATION NGO, NOT A LAW FIRM OR A FUNDER. For community conservation areas villages hold, Benin's Eco-Bénin entry; for the peasant union that funded legal support, Synergie Paysanne; for the sacred-forest framework, the arrêté 021/MEHU entry; for the annual call with a downloadable budget template, the FNEC entry.

trackers.name: GRABE-Bénin, Avrankou — works through kings and traditional chiefs to save sacred forests, trained sixty religious dignitaries across two communes, and is drafting the legal framework for Benin's community conserved areas
trackers.desc: THE ORGANISATION THAT WORKS THROUGH THE KINGS: GROUPE DE RECHERCHE ET D'ACTION POUR LE BIEN-ÊTRE AU BÉNIN (GRABE-BENIN), A NON-PROFIT ASSOCIATION BORN IN OCTOBER 1996 from a group of young professionals, OFFICIALLY DECLARED TO THE MINISTRY OF THE INTERIOR, SECURITY AND DECENTRALISATION UNDER N°2001/463/MISD/DC/SAAP-Assoc OF 27 SEPTEMBER 2001, at Rue de la Mairie d'Avrankou, Ouémé, with a published email, working since 2001 on ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION AND SUPPORT TO INDIGENOUS AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES FOR SUSTAINABLE NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT AND THE VALORISATION OF ENDOGENOUS KNOWLEDGE, across environmental protection, cultural biodiversity, local development and action research, SOCIAL INTERMEDIATION, CITIZEN WATCH, sustainable agriculture, ecotourism and advisory support. Its declared registration number is printed on its own site — the document this file tells you to demand from every organisation. ITS METHOD IS THE POINT: WE WORK WITH THE KINGS AND THE TRADITIONAL CHIEFS TO IDENTIFY AND SAVE WHAT CAN STILL BE SAVED — THEIR ROLE HAVING BEEN STRONGLY DEVALUED IN BENINESE SOCIETY, SO THAT THEY PROGRESSIVELY NEGLECTED THEIR NATURAL AND CULTURAL HERITAGE. It ran a workshop bringing together SOME SIXTY ACTORS OF TRADITIONAL RELIGION — DIGNITARIES OF ENDOGENOUS CULTS AND THOSE RESPONSIBLE FOR SACRED SITES — IN THE COMMUNES OF AVRANKOU AND ADJARRA, to bring them to safeguard the natural resources of the sacred forests. Sixty custodians of sacred sites in one room is a convening no outside organisation can arrange for itself. If your grove is failing because its keepers have lost standing, the repair is to restore the keepers, not to fence the trees. AND THE FOUNDER'S OWN ACCOUNT IS THE CLEAREST ECOLOGICAL ARGUMENT IN THIS FILE FOR RESTORING A TABOO: IN THE 1980s THE PYTHONS — HARMLESS HERE AND VENERATED — WERE ACCUSED OF WITCHCRAFT, KILLED AND EATEN. THE PREDICTABLE RESULT: THE ECOLOGICAL BALANCE WAS BROKEN, THE RATS THE PYTHONS HAD FRIGHTENED OFF MULTIPLIED, THE MAIZE WAS RAVAGED AND AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION FELL. WITH GRABE-BENIN WE REINTRODUCED PYTHONS INTO THE FORESTS, AND ALSO TORTOISES AND MONITOR LIZARDS. A broken taboo cost the harvest, and reintroducing the animal restored it. That is an argument a farmer will accept when a conservation argument alone will not. WHAT IT IS BUILDING NOW: having accompanied a sacred forests and sites project, GRABE-BENIN IS CONDUCTING A STUDY TO ESTABLISH THE LEGAL FRAMEWORK FOR APACs — COMMUNITY CONSERVED AREAS — IN BENIN, and proposes BOTANICAL GARDENS AND MICRO-CREDIT AS BOTH A TOOL FOR REDUCING PRESSURE ON APACs AND A MEANS OF ECONOMIC VALORISATION OF TRADITIONAL KNOWLEDGE, together with A NATIONAL INSTITUTION TO DEFEND THEIR INTERESTS. Somebody is drafting the legal framework for Benin's community conserved areas right now. Get your grove into that study while it is being written. HOW IT SURVIVES, STATED HONESTLY BY ITS FOUNDER: ON MEANS IT IS DIFFICULT, BUT WE FIGHT ON — I AM NOT PAID BY THE NGO, I AM SECRETARY GENERAL OF A TOWN HALL IN ORDER TO HELP IT; MEMBERS' SUBSCRIPTIONS LET US DO SMALL ACTIVITIES, AND FRIENDS GAVE US A BUS FOR THE MOBILE LIBRARY WITH WHICH WE GO INTO THE VILLAGES. An unpaid founder with a bus and a members' subscription is what most of this file's best organisations actually look like. Judge by the villages reached, not the budget. It belongs to a continental biodiversity network and several national coalitions. WHO IT SUITS: Beninese communities with a sacred forest, traditional authorities, and anyone wanting an APAC recognised. CAVEATS: A SMALL, LARGELY VOLUNTEER ASSOCIATION. For community conservation areas villages hold, Benin's Eco-Bénin entry; for the sacred-forest management framework, the arrêté 021/MEHU entry; for the government agreement on environmental crime, Nature Tropicale; for the annual call with a downloadable budget template, FNEC.

trackers.name: The Maison de la Société Civile in Cotonou and the human rights commission's chambre de concertation — where a Beninese association registers itself as civil society, and the rule that a chieftaincy must take associative form
trackers.desc: THE CHIEFTAINCY MUST FORM AN ASSOCIATION — and that single rule decides whether the traditional authority behind your land can speak in its own name: at Beninese civil society's états généraux, attended by numerous CSOs from ALL THE DEPARTMENTS, a position document was adopted called the CONSENSUS NATIONAL DES OSC BÉNINOISES, which settled that TRADITIONAL CHIEFTAINCIES, RELIGIOUS CONFESSIONS AND THE MEDIA CAN ONLY BE MEMBERS OF CIVIL SOCIETY IN THEIR ASSOCIATIVE FORM — with ASSOCIATIONS (OF YOUTH, OF DEVELOPMENT, OF WOMEN, OF TRADITIONAL CHIEFTAINCIES, OF RELIGIOUS CONFESSIONS, MEDIA AND OTHERS) NAMED AS ONE OF FOUR RETAINED COMPONENTS. An association OF traditional chieftaincies is an explicitly recognised category in Benin. If the custodians of your sacred forest or your land want standing in national civil society, they do not have to stop being chiefs — they have to constitute themselves as an association. That is the one step, and it is cheap. WHERE TO GO: THE MAISON DE LA SOCIÉTÉ CIVILE (MdSC) PUBLISHES A FULL WALKING ADDRESS — QUARTIER SIKÈCODJI, RUE N°216, CARRÉ 00350 U, BOULEVARD DES ARMÉES, DIRECTION ÉTOILE ROUGE, SECOND STREET ON THE RIGHT AFTER THE CARREFOUR COSSI, 01 BP 414 COTONOU — WITH A TELEPHONE AND AN EMAIL. Directions rather than a postal box. An organisation that tells you which turning to take after which junction expects people to arrive in person, which is what a delegation from a village needs. AND THE SECOND DOOR, WHICH IS A SEAT RATHER THAN A SERVICE: THE COMMISSION BÉNINOISE DES DROITS DE L'HOMME ESTABLISHED A CHAMBRE DE CONCERTATION WITH CIVIL SOCIETY AND LAUNCHED AN APPEL À CANDIDATURE TO NGO NETWORKS, PLATFORMS, NGOs AND CSOs — the purpose being TO POOL AND HARMONISE THE POTENTIAL OF THOSE ACTORS AND REINFORCE THEIR CAPACITY TO PROMOTE AND PROTECT HUMAN RIGHTS IN ALLIANCE AND SYNERGY WITH THE COMMISSION. HOW YOU APPLY: ANY NGO NETWORK, PLATFORM, NGO OR CSO WISHING TO REQUEST MEMBER STATUS DEPOSITS A REQUÊTE DOCUMENTÉE AT THE COMMISSION'S CENTRAL SECRETARIAT, WHICH LETS THE COMMISSION ASSESS THE WILL AND CAPACITY OF THE ORGANISATION TO WORK TOWARDS ITS OBJECTIVES. AND THE ELIGIBLE THEMES ARE THE POINT: THEY EXPLICITLY INCLUDE DROIT À LA VIE, SANTÉ ET ENVIRONNEMENT; ACCÈS À LA JUSTICE, DROIT À LA RÉPARATION, DROITS ÉCONOMIQUES SOCIAUX ET CULTURELS; AND DÉFENSEURS DES DROITS DE L'HOMME, LIBERTÉ D'ASSOCIATION ET LIBERTÉ DE LA PRESSE. Environment sits inside the right to life on the national human rights commission's own list of themes, and a documented request is all it takes to apply for a seat. A community association whose case is a poisoned river or a lost forest is eligible on the commission's own terms — and the reparation theme is there too, which is the word to use if your loss has already happened. THE FORMS THAT EXIST, WORTH KNOWING BEFORE YOU CHOOSE ONE: Beninese practice distinguishes the ORGANISATION DES COMMUNAUTÉS DE BASE (OCB), the ORGANISATION PAYSANNE (OP), the ONG, the ONG INTERNATIONALE and the OSC — and above them sit a COLLECTIF DES FÉDÉRATIONS ET RÉSEAUX D'ONG DU BÉNIN (CFRONG), a PLATEFORME DES ACTEURS DE LA SOCIÉTÉ CIVILE AU BÉNIN (PASCiB) and a CENTRE DE PROMOTION DE LA SOCIÉTÉ CIVILE. Organisation des communautés de base is a named legal category for exactly what a village group is. Ask which form fits before registering — an OCB and an ONG are not treated the same by ministries or by funders. A civil society strengthening programme for Benin was launched at 12 MILLION EUROS, with the Maison de la Société Civile named at its launch. Where a programme of that size exists, the umbrella named at its launch is where the sub-grants pass through. Ask what is currently open. WHO IT SUITS: Beninese village associations, traditional custodians seeking standing, and groups wanting a seat on the human rights commission's chamber. CAVEATS: SOME OF THIS RECORD IS FROM PUBLISHED PROGRAMME DOCUMENTS — confirm current calls and criteria. For community conservation areas the villages themselves set up, Benin's Eco-Bénin entry; for the peasant union that funded legal support, Synergie Paysanne; for the national framework for community management of sacred forests, the arrêté 021/MEHU entry; for the national environment and climate fund, FNEC; for kings and traditional chiefs, GRABE-Bénin.

trackers.name: The UN Special Rapporteur on Human Rights Defenders' emergency line — a 24-hour emergency helpline for threatened defenders in five languages, protection grants that pay legal fees, medical bills and family support for the imprisoned, an African relocation programme, and two directories of who else gives this money
trackers.desc: A PHONE LINE THAT ANSWERS AT NIGHT, IN FIVE LANGUAGES — placement note first: THESE ARE GLOBAL AND PAN-AFRICAN MECHANISMS, FILED UNDER BENIN BECAUSE THIS BUCKET CARRIED NO DEFENDER-PROTECTION RESOURCE. THE AFRICA-RUN PROGRAMME IS NAMED BELOW. THE HELPLINE: AN EMERGENCY 24-HOUR PHONE LINE FOR HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS, OPERATING IN ARABIC, ENGLISH, FRENCH, RUSSIAN AND SPANISH — AND THE EU MECHANISM PROVIDES 24/7 URGENT SUPPORT FOR DEFENDERS FACING IMMINENT DANGER OR THREATS, CONTACTABLE THROUGH A PERMANENT EMERGENCY HELPLINE AND A SECURE CONTACT FORM. Arabic and French cover most of the countries in this file that have no reachable domestic protection at all. Write the number down now and give it to three people, because the person who needs it may not be the one who can look it up. WHAT THE PROTECTION GRANTS ACTUALLY PAY FOR, LISTED ITEM BY ITEM: FUNDING TO IMPROVE DIGITAL SECURITY; COMMUNICATION SECURITY; LEGAL FEES FOR DEFENDERS WHO ARE BEING JUDICIALLY HARASSED; MEDICAL FEES FOR DEFENDERS WHO HAVE BEEN ATTACKED OR WHO HAVE SUFFERED A MEDICAL CONDITION AS A RESULT OF THEIR PEACEFUL HUMAN RIGHTS ACTIVITIES; AND FAMILY ASSISTANCE FOR IMPRISONED DEFENDERS — STATED EXPLICITLY AS NOT AN EXHAUSTIVE LIST. LEGAL FEES FOR JUDICIAL HARASSMENT is the line that matters most to this file. The commonest thing that happens to a land defender is a charge, and defending a nuisance prosecution costs money nobody budgeted. FAMILY ASSISTANCE FOR IMPRISONED DEFENDERS is the second: when the person who earns is inside, the family is the pressure point, and it is fundable. WHO CAN APPLY, AND THIS IS THE UNUSUAL PART: SUPPORT IS AVAILABLE TO INDIVIDUALS, INFORMAL GROUPS, UNREGISTERED COLLECTIVES AND REGISTERED ORGANISATIONS, WORKING ACROSS A WIDE RANGE OF HUMAN RIGHTS THEMES. Individuals AND unregistered collectives. Almost nothing else in this file funds a person directly, and a village committee with no papers is eligible here. THE OTHER THINGS THE MECHANISM DOES BESIDES PAYING: THROUGH ITS PARTNERS IT UNDERTAKES URGENT ACTIONS, WHICH CAN INCLUDE FAXED OR PHONED APPEALS TO THE RELEVANT AUTHORITIES, RAISING THE CASE THROUGH THE EU OR INDIVIDUAL GOVERNMENT REPRESENTATIVES, PRACTICAL HELP WITH TEMPORARY RELOCATION, OR ASSISTANCE WITH MEDICAL OR LEGAL EXPENSES — AIMING TO REACH EVERY CORNER OF THE WORLD, INCLUDING THE MOST DIFFICULT COUNTRIES AND REMOTE LOCATIONS. An appeal phoned to the police commander, or the case raised by a foreign embassy, sometimes changes what happens that night more than any grant does. Ask for the urgent action, not only the money — they are separate requests. THE AFRICAN PROGRAMME, RUN FROM AFRICA: UBUNTU HUB CITIES — RELOCATION AND SUPPORT FOR HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS AT RISK IN AFRICA, OPERATED BY A PAN-AFRICAN HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS NETWORK. Relocation within Africa, arranged by Africans, to African cities. That is a fundamentally different offer from evacuation abroad: you stay in your region, your language and your legal system, and returning is possible. For a farmer or a village leader, leaving the continent is usually not survivable as a plan; moving to another African city for six months may be. THE TWO DIRECTORIES THAT SAVE YOU WEEKS OF SEARCHING: A PUBLISHED LIST OF ORGANISATIONS PROVIDING GRANTS FOR HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS, AND A SEPARATE PUBLISHED LIST OF ORGANISATIONS PROVIDING RELOCATION OR RESPITE — PLUS A RAPID RESPONSE DIRECTORY. Somebody has already compiled who gives this money and who provides refuge. Two lists, kept current, free. That is the first thing to open rather than the last. OTHER NAMED FUNDS IN THE SAME FIELD: A FUND GIVING SMALL, SHORT-TERM EMERGENCY GRANTS TO CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS THREATENED BECAUSE OF THEIR HUMAN RIGHTS WORK; A GERMAN INITIATIVE PROVIDING THREATENED DEFENDERS WITH A SAFE PLACE TO RECUPERATE, COPE WITH TRAUMA AND, WHERE POSSIBLE, NETWORK AND FURTHER DEVELOP THEIR PROFESSIONAL SKILLS; AN EMERGENCY FUND RUN BY A CIVIL RIGHTS ORGANISATION; AND A PRESS ORGANISATION'S ASSISTANCE DESK WHICH DISBURSES AROUND 100 INDIVIDUAL SUPPORT GRANTS EACH YEAR, ENABLING JOURNALISTS WHO HAVE BEEN VICTIMS OF REPRISALS TO COVER IMMEDIATE NEEDS, PAY MEDICAL OR LEGAL BILLS, OR FIND A SAFE REFUGE. A hundred grants a year for journalists specifically. This file has recorded reporters being targeted alongside communities in Uganda, Mozambique and Burundi — the journalist covering your case has their own fund, and telling them so is a real form of support. AND THE PROVISION ALMOST NOBODY OFFERS: REST, RESPITE AND OTHER OPPORTUNITIES FOR HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS DEALING WITH EXTREME STRESS. Money to stop for a while. Campaigns in this file end more often through exhaustion than through defeat, and rest is a funded category. THE STRUCTURE BEHIND IT: A CONSORTIUM OF 12 INTERNATIONAL AND REGIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS ORGANISATIONS DELIVERING EMERGENCY SUPPORT THROUGH THE ESTABLISHED EMERGENCY GRANTS PROGRAMMES OF ITS NAMED PARTNERS, WHICH ALSO DRAW ON NON-EU FUNDING — WITH A RENEWAL FOR FOUR AND A HALF YEARS AND A BUDGET INCREASE OF 30 MILLION EUROS. Twelve organisations behind one door, so one contact reaches the whole set. If the first partner cannot help, ask which of the other eleven can. WHO IT SUITS: any African land or environmental defender under threat, prosecuted, injured or imprisoned — including individuals and unregistered groups. CAVEATS: PROTECTION FUNDS MOVE FAST BUT ARE NOT UNLIMITED, and relocation is temporary. For the 48-hour decision on relocation, urgent legal help and family support after a death or imprisonment, Liberia's African Defenders Emergency Fund entry; for the three application windows including a protection grant, Mauritania's rapid-response fund entry; for the centre giving rapid legal support when defenders are criminalized, Kenya's Strategic Legal Response Centre entry.

trackers.name: Fellowships that pay a person's living costs for up to three years so they can run their organisation full-time — self-nomination accepted, no age or education bars, and pro bono legal and management services attached
trackers.desc: SOMEBODY PAYS YOUR RENT SO YOU CAN DO THIS FULL-TIME — THE THING ALMOST NO FUNDER IN THIS FILE PAYS FOR: A NEEDS-BASED LIVING STIPEND, TYPICALLY FOR UP TO THREE YEARS, ALLOWING FOUNDERS TO FOCUS FULL-TIME ON GROWING THEIR VENTURE — A MONTHLY STIPEND MEANT TO ALLOW THE ENTREPRENEUR TO FOCUS 100% ON THEIR WORK. Every grant in this file pays for activities and forbids paying the person. That is why community campaigns are run in the evenings by people with jobs, and why they collapse when the founder has to go back to farming. A stipend that covers a household for three years is the difference between a movement and a hobby — and it is the single scarcest form of support there is. THE SELF-NOMINATION ROUTE, WHICH IS THE PART PEOPLE DO NOT KNOW: NOMINATIONS COME FROM STAFF, VOLUNTEERS, PARTNERS, FELLOWS AND NOMINATORS — AND WHILE THE PRIMARY SOURCE IS A NETWORK OF VOLUNTEER NOMINATORS, THEY ALSO WELCOME SELF-NOMINATIONS FROM SOCIAL ENTREPRENEURS WHO BELIEVE THEY MEET THE CRITERIA. ALL THESE WAYS OF SUGGESTING A POTENTIAL FELLOW ARE EQUAL. ALL THESE WAYS ARE EQUAL. You do not need to be discovered. Someone leading a community land defence can put themselves forward, and it is not counted as a lesser route — and equally, you can nominate the person in your own area who is carrying the work. THE BARS THAT DO NOT EXIST: THERE ARE NO AGE, EDUCATION, CLASS, RACE, OR OTHER SUCH BARS TO ELECTION. No education requirement. A farmer who organised twelve villages qualifies on the same terms as a graduate with a proposal — which is rarer than it should be among the funders in this file. WHAT COMES WITH IT BEYOND MONEY, AND THIS IS WHY IT BELONGS IN A LAND FILE: ACCESS TO INSTITUTIONAL FUNDERS AND GRANT MAKERS; ACCESS TO PRO-BONO MANAGEMENT CONSULTANCY SERVICES; ACCESS TO PRO-BONO LEGAL SERVICES; KNOWLEDGE SHARING AND LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES; WORLDWIDE ONLINE AND OFF-LINE MARKETING; AND POSSIBLE RECOGNITION BY VARIOUS AWARD COMMITTEES. PRO BONO LEGAL SERVICES arrive attached to the fellowship rather than as a separate hunt. And ACCESS TO INSTITUTIONAL FUNDERS is the compounding part: this file records over and over that the barrier is not the absence of funds but not being known to the people holding them. THE NETWORK: LIFETIME MEMBERSHIP IN A GLOBAL NETWORK OF MORE THAN 3,800 FELLOWS ACROSS OVER 90 COUNTRIES, OFFERING PEER SUPPORT, STRATEGY COLLABORATION AND VISIBILITY — A LIFELONG, NON-RESIDENTIAL FELLOWSHIP, WITH EACH FELLOW EMBARKING ON A TAILORED TIMELINE OF INVESTMENTS AND SUPPORT OVER THEIR LIFETIME. NON-RESIDENTIAL means you stay where you are. Several routes in this file require leaving — this one funds you to remain in the place you are defending. THE CONDITIONS, STATED SO YOU CAN JUDGE YOUR OWN CASE: DEMONSTRATE ENTREPRENEURIAL LEADERSHIP AND A CLEAR COMMITMENT TO LONG-TERM IMPACT; SHOW EVIDENCE THAT THE SOLUTION HAS THE POTENTIAL TO CREATE CHANGE BEYOND A SINGLE COMMUNITY OR ORGANISATION; BE WORKING FULL-TIME, OR PREPARED TO WORK FULL-TIME; AND LEAD A REGISTERED ORGANISATION, WHICH MAY BE A NONPROFIT, FOR-PROFIT OR HYBRID ENTERPRISE, WITH EARLY EVIDENCE OF IMPACT OR TRACTION. BEYOND A SINGLE COMMUNITY is the bar to write to. Defending one valley will not qualify on its own; a method other valleys are already copying will. So describe the replication, not just the campaign — and note that a registered organisation is required, which the pro bono brokerage entry in this file can help you obtain. THE PROCESS, SO NOBODY IS SURPRISED: FROM NOMINATION TO ELECTION, CANDIDATES UNDERGO AN EXTENSIVE SERIES OF IN-DEPTH INTERVIEWS, A JUDGING PANEL, AND A FINAL VOTE BY THE EXECUTIVE BOARD — THE LOCAL VENTURE TEAM REVIEWS NOMINATIONS, CONDUCTS SITE VISITS AND MEETS THE CANDIDATE, AND REVIEWS THEIR WORK WITH OTHER EXPERTS; THEN A SENIOR REPRESENTATIVE GIVES A SECOND OPINION. Site visits mean they come to you. That is months of process, not weeks — apply while things are stable rather than during the crisis. THE TIMING: THE APPLICATION PROCESS IS OPEN ALL-YEAR ROUND IN OVER 90 COUNTRIES. THE SECOND FELLOWSHIP, WITH FIGURES: A TWO-YEAR FELLOWSHIP PROVIDING MORE THAN $2 MILLION IN SEED FUNDING — FELLOWS RECEIVE UP TO $90,000 TO LAUNCH NEW ORGANIZATIONS, HEALTH INSURANCE AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT STIPENDS, ACCESS TO A NETWORK OF 500+ ALUMNI, LEADERSHIP DEVELOPMENT, AND ONE-TO-ONE SUPPORT AND COUNSELING. HEALTH INSURANCE. For a defender in the countries this file covers, cover for an injury or an illness removes one of the real reasons people step back from exposed work. AND A THIRD PROGRAMME: FELLOWS ARE SUPPORTED IN THEIR NATURAL WORK ENVIRONMENTS, PAIRED WITH PERSONALIZED EXECUTIVE COACHES, WITH UP TO $10,000 IN FUNDING, LEADERSHIP ASSESSMENT RESOURCES, A NETWORK OF PEER LEADERS AND SECTOR EXPERTISE. Three different sizes of the same idea — $10,000 with a coach, $90,000 to launch, or three years of living costs. Match the one to where you actually are, because applying to the largest first is the commonest way people waste a year. WHO IT SUITS: African individuals leading a registered community, land or environmental organisation whose method could spread beyond their own area. CAVEATS: A REGISTERED ORGANISATION AND A REPLICABLE IDEA ARE BOTH REQUIRED, AND SELECTION TAKES MONTHS — this is not emergency money. For free legal help getting registered, the Central African Republic's pro bono brokerage entry; for the advisor-nominated small grants where 40% of grantees are first-time, Ghana's African Women's Development Fund entry; for money that moves in 72 hours, Mauritania's rapid-response fund entry.

trackers.name: They will do the Wall Street research for you on request — mapping the banks, insurers, brands and buyers behind a project, building free replacements for subscription-only financial databases, and training African advocates to do it themselves
trackers.desc: THEY WILL DO THE WALL STREET RESEARCH FOR YOU, ON REQUEST — adjacency declared first: THEIR CAMPAIGN SITE IS ALREADY A HOST UNDER CHAD, A DEVELOPMENT-RIGHTS COALITION UNDER NIGERIA AND UGANDA, AND THIS FILE'S GUINEA ENTRY ALREADY NAMES THE TWO TRACKER TOOLS. NONE OF THOSE CARRIES THE REQUEST SERVICE, THE TRAINING OR THE AGRICULTURAL GUIDE BELOW. THE REQUEST SERVICE, AND IT IS THE FIND: SINCE 2016 THEY HAVE BEEN TAKING REQUESTS FROM COMMUNITY ADVOCATES TO RESEARCH AND MAP THE INVESTMENT AND SUPPLY CHAINS BEHIND HARMFUL PROJECTS — IDENTIFYING THE BANKS, INVESTORS, INSURANCE COMPANIES, DEVELOPMENT FINANCE INSTITUTIONS, MAJOR BRANDS AND OTHER STAKEHOLDERS ENABLING THEM, THEN WORKING WITH THOSE ADVOCATES TO USE THE INFORMATION IN THEIR OWN STRATEGY. You can ask them to find out who is behind the company on your land, and they will do the work. INSURANCE COMPANIES and MAJOR BRANDS are in that list for a reason: a plantation may be indifferent to a village and highly sensitive to the European supermarket that buys its crop or the insurer that underwrites it. THE PRINCIPLE, STATED: THE MORE THAT ADVOCATES AND AFFECTED COMMUNITIES KNOW ABOUT A HARMFUL PROJECT — WHO OWNS IT, AND WHO ELSE MAKES IT POSSIBLE AND PROFITABLE — THE MORE AVENUES THEY HAVE TO SECURE ACCOUNTABILITY. WHY THE FREE TOOLS EXIST, IN THEIR OWN WORDS: SOME OF THE MOST POWERFUL TOOLS IN OUR ARSENAL ARE SUBSCRIPTION-ONLY WALL STREET DATABASES THAT HELP US DIG UP CRITICAL INFORMATION ON THE WEB OF ACTORS BEHIND IRRESPONSIBLE INVESTMENT PROJECTS. BUT THESE DATABASES ARE EXPENSIVE TO ACCESS, ESPECIALLY FOR THE ADVOCATES AND COMMUNITIES THAT NEED THEM MOST. SO WE ARE DEVELOPING A SUITE OF OUR OWN DATA TOOLS THAT AUTOMATE INVESTMENT AND SUPPLY CHAIN RESEARCH — AND WE ARE MAKING THEM FREE TO USE, FORMING AN OPEN-ACCESS FINANCIAL TERMINAL FOR ADVOCATES. The information asymmetry is a subscription fee. The company knows who owns it and you do not, because the answer sits behind a paywall no village can afford — and somebody is dismantling that specific barrier rather than complaining about it. THE LEVERAGE SORT, WHICH IS THE MOST DIRECTLY USEFUL FEATURE: ADVOCATES CAN ACCESS A SEARCHABLE LIST OF THE CURRENT EQUITY HOLDINGS OF SPECIFIC INVESTORS, ASSESS HOW WELL THOSE INVESTORS ARE UPHOLDING COMMITMENTS TO DIVEST FROM SPECIFIC COMPANIES OR SECTORS, AND SORT INVESTORS BY THE MARKET VALUE OF THEIR SHAREHOLDINGS IN SPECIFIC COMPANIES — MEANING THEY CAN EASILY IDENTIFY THOSE ACTORS WITH THE MOST POTENTIAL LEVERAGE. RESULTS CAN BE FILTERED BY INVESTOR TYPE AND DOWNLOADED. Sorted by who has the most to lose. A pension fund holding a large stake, with a public divestment promise it is breaking, is a different target from a shareholder with a token holding — and the tool tells you which is which before you spend a year writing to the wrong one. THE COMPLAINT-LINKED SEARCH: ONE TOOL LETS USERS SEARCH INVESTMENTS MADE BY 16 DEVELOPMENT FINANCE INSTITUTIONS THAT HAVE INDEPENDENT COMPLAINT MECHANISMS ACCESSIBLE TO AFFECTED COMMUNITIES. Search for financiers that can actually be complained to. If the project on your land is backed by one of those sixteen, a route exists that would not otherwise — and this file's Burundi entry holds the database of what such complaints have achieved. THE AGRICULTURAL GUIDE, CO-PRODUCED: DEVELOPED WITH AN INTERNATIONAL ENVIRONMENT AND DEVELOPMENT INSTITUTE FOR LOCAL ADVOCATES SUPPORTING COMMUNITIES WHOSE LAND RIGHTS AND LIVELIHOODS HAVE BEEN NEGATIVELY IMPACTED BY AGRICULTURAL INVESTMENTS — SHOWING HOW TO IDENTIFY AND ANALYZE THE COMPANIES, INVESTORS, BUYERS AND OTHER INFLUENTIAL ACTORS LINKED TO THESE PROJECTS. BUYERS. Tracing who purchases the crop is the step communities skip, and it is often the shortest route to someone who will answer a letter. THE AFRICAN TRAINING, WITH ITS CADENCE SO YOU CAN CATCH IT: SINCE 2022 THEY HAVE RUN INTENSIVE COURSES COVERING THE FULL SEQUENCE, FROM INVESTMENT AND SUPPLY CHAIN RESEARCH THROUGH DESIGNING MULTI-PRONGED ADVOCACY STRATEGIES — TRAINING DOZENS OF ADVOCATES FROM AFRICA, LATIN AMERICA AND ASIA PACIFIC, AND MORE THAN 1,500 OTHERS ON SELECT SKILLS. THEY GENERALLY RUN ONE OR TWO COURSES PER YEAR, EACH TAILORED TO A SPECIFIC REGION, WITH A CALL FOR APPLICATIONS PUT OUT APPROXIMATELY THREE MONTHS IN ADVANCE. One or two a year, regionally tailored, announced three months ahead. So the African course is a specific window to watch for rather than an open door — and the number to aim at is the intensive course, not the 1,500. THE SELECTION PRIORITY, RECORDED HONESTLY BECAUSE IT WILL DECIDE SOME APPLICATIONS: THEY PRIORITIZE GROUPS WHOSE GOALS ALIGN WITH THEIR STRATEGIC FOCUS ON ADVANCING A RAPID AND RIGHTS-BASED TRANSITION AWAY FROM FOSSIL FUELS. A community facing an oil, gas, coal or pipeline project is squarely inside that priority; one facing a plantation or a dam is not, and should say why the case still fits. THE SPREAD AND THE AFTERCARE: SEVERAL PARTICIPATING ORGANISATIONS HAVE GONE ON TO OFFER THEIR OWN VERSIONS OF THE TRAINING TO CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS IN THEIR OWN NETWORKS — AND AFTER TRAINING THEY PROVIDE ONGOING COUNSEL AND STRATEGIC SUPPORT AS PARTICIPANTS EXECUTE THEIR STRATEGIES, INCLUDING ONE-ON-ONE MEETINGS, JOINT WEBINARS AND RESOURCE-SHARING VIA GROUP MESSAGING PLATFORMS. Graduates re-teach it locally. So the nearest trained person may be in your own country rather than abroad — ask the coalition you already belong to who has been through it. AND THE RECORDED RESULTS: MULTI-MILLION-DOLLAR COMPENSATION PACKAGES FOR FAMILIES DISPLACED BY INTERNATIONALLY-FINANCED DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS; FORCED EVICTIONS STOPPED IN THEIR TRACKS; LAND TITLES SECURED FOR THREATENED COMMUNITIES; AND THOUSANDS OF ACRES OF OLD-GROWTH FORESTS PREVENTED FROM BEING CLEARED FOR INDUSTRIAL MONO-CROP PLANTATIONS — WITH 255 OPPORTUNITIES TO ACCESS INTERNATIONAL ACCOUNTABILITY MECHANISMS IDENTIFIED AMONG THE ADVOCACY TARGETS. SECURING LAND TITLES is on that list beside compensation. Following the money is usually framed as a way to punish; here it produced title, which is the outcome most communities in this file actually want. WHO IT SUITS: African community advocates who know which company is on their land but not who finances, insures or buys from it. CAVEATS: RESEARCH IS BY REQUEST AND CAPACITY IS FINITE, TRAINING RUNS ONCE OR TWICE A YEAR WITH A FOSSIL-FUEL PRIORITY — approach with a specific project named. For the two tracker tools themselves, Guinea's entry; for the database of what complaints to financiers have achieved, Burundi's entry; for the request-only legal non-profit, Burundi's entry.

trackers.name: IPIS (International Peace Information Service), Antwerp — free open data and open-source webmap code on mining sites, roadblocks and armed interference — filterable by child labour, mercury use and armed presence, exportable as a spreadsheet, with a tutorial written for people using Excel
trackers.desc: THE MAP CODE IS OPEN SOURCE, SO YOU CAN BUILD YOUR OWN — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S BURUNDI ENTRY COVERS THE FOREST FINANCE DATABASE AND ITS AFRICAN COVERAGE GAP; ITS ANGOLA ENTRY THE COMMERCIAL BANK CAMPAIGNING ORGANISATION; ITS GUINEA-BISSAU ENTRY THE COMPARATIVE MINING LAW ATLAS; AND ITS DR CONGO ENTRIES COVER COMMUNITY FOREST MAPPING AND CORE ORGANISATIONAL SUPPORT. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE OPEN-SOURCE CODE, WHICH IS THE FIND: IT USES A PUBLIC CODE REPOSITORY TO OPEN SOURCE THE CODE OF SOME OF ITS WEBMAPS — INCLUDING A WEBMAP OF ARTISANAL MINING SITES IN ONE COUNTRY'S RIVER VALLEY BUILT WITH A NAMED NATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL LAW ASSOCIATION, A WEBMAP OF MINING SITES IN A NAMED EAST AFRICAN COUNTRY, WEBMAPS OF MINING SITES AND ROADBLOCKS IN THE EAST OF A CENTRAL AFRICAN COUNTRY, AND A WEBMAP OF INCIDENTS AND ROADBLOCKS IN ANOTHER. The working code for a professional mapping platform, free to copy. A national organisation with one technical person can stand up its own map of its own country's sites rather than waiting to be included in somebody's programme — and one of the published maps was built WITH a national environmental law association, which is the partnership model rather than the service model. WHAT IS PUBLISHED AS OPEN DATA: DATASETS FROM ITS OWN COLLECTION CAMPAIGNS AND RESEARCH, INTERNALLY REVIEWED AND PROCESSED, LINKED TO THE INTERNAL DATABASE SO THAT A DOWNLOAD INCLUDES THE MOST UP TO DATE DATA-POINTS — WITH DIRECT DOWNLOADS PUBLISHED FOR TWO NAMED AFRICAN COUNTRIES. THE TUTORIALS, AND THE MIDDLE ONE MATTERS MOST: AN OPEN DATA FAQ AND DICTIONARY PAGE HELPING USERS UNDERSTAND THE DIFFERENT COLUMNS AND VALUES; AN OPEN DATA GETTING STARTED USING EXCEL GUIDE EXPLAINING HOW TO USE THE DATA IN A COMMON SPREADSHEET PROGRAMME; AND A FULLER TUTORIAL FOR MORE ADVANCED DATA RESEARCHERS. A guide written for somebody with a spreadsheet and no training. This file has recorded open data repeatedly as a resource in principle and unusable in practice; a dictionary explaining what each column means is the difference. THE FILTERS, WHICH ARE THE SUBSTANCE: THE DATA CAN BE SUBSET BY DATE OF VISIT, SOURCE OF DATA, PROVINCE, MINERAL, NUMBER OF WORKERS PER MINING SITE, ACCESS TO THE MINING SITE, MINERAL TRACEABILITY, OFFICIAL QUALIFICATION STATUS, PRESENCE OF STATE SERVICES, ARMED GROUPS, AS WELL AS REPORTED ARMED INTERFERENCE, PRESENCE OF CHILD LABOUR AND MERCURY USE. OFFICIAL QUALIFICATION STATUS is the filter to reach for: it separates sites the state has formally cleared from those it has not. A community can check whether the operation beside it is qualified at all — and MERCURY USE and CHILD LABOUR are recorded per site, which turns a general complaint into a located one. THE EXPORT FUNCTION: THE LIST OF MINING SITES ON THE MAP IS AVAILABLE AS AN INTERACTIVE DATA TABLE WHICH CAN BE DOWNLOADED AS A CSV FILE — ALLOWING USERS TO EXPORT THEIR OWN DATASET AFTER CHOOSING THEIR PREFERRED FILTER COMBINATION. A GLOSSARY DEFINES THE TERMINOLOGY. Filter to your province and export. That is a document you can print and table at a district meeting, produced in an afternoon. WHAT THE MAP SHOWS AT SITE LEVEL: CLICK ON MINES TO LEARN THE KIND OF MINERALS PRODUCED, THE PRESENCE OF STATE AND NON-STATE ARMED ACTORS — POSSIBLY ENGAGING IN SPECIFIC ILLEGAL ACTIVITIES — OR STATE SERVICES OPERATING AT THE SITE. PICTURES ARE AVAILABLE FOR THE MAJORITY OF THE MINES, NAVIGABLE WITH A SLIDER, AND A POP-UP ENABLES FURTHER EXPLORATION OF MINERAL SALES LOCATIONS AND CHECKPOINTS. PHOTOGRAPHS OF MOST SITES, and the checkpoints mapped. Roadblocks are where the money is taken from miners and traders, and mapping them names a practice everyone knows and nobody records. THE SCALE AND SOURCES: SINCE 2009 IT HAS MAPPED MORE THAN 2,800 AND LATER MORE THAN 3,400 ARTISANAL AND SMALL-SCALE MINING SITES — DRAWING BOTH ON SITES VISITED BY ITS OWN TEAMS AND ON THIRD-PARTY SOURCES INCLUDING THE NATIONAL MINING CADASTRE AND MINISTERIAL QUALIFICATION TEAMS. THE PRIMARY DATA IT COLLECTS: THE INTERFERENCE OF ARMED GROUPS, TYPES OF MINERALS, MINERAL PRICING AND WORKER DEMOGRAPHICS — WITH ONE SURVEY OF 829 ACTIVE MINING SITES REPRESENTING OVER 132,320 ARTISANAL MINERS. MINERAL PRICING collected at the site. A miners' association that knows the price recorded at comparable sites bargains differently with the buyer at the pit. THE LARGE-FORMAT PAPER MAPS: A0 MAPS OF KNOWN PAST AND PRESENT MINING SITES COVERING FIVE NAMED PROVINCES, EACH DETAILING THE TYPE OF MINERALS, THE QUALIFICATION STATUS BY OFFICIAL AUTHORITIES, THE MINING TITLES AND AN OVERVIEW OF ARMED PRESENCE. A0 PAPER, showing the mining titles. A wall map in a community meeting hall showing whose title covers which ground does work no website does — and titles printed beside armed presence is a combination few official maps will ever show. THE FRAMING IT PUBLISHES ABOUT THE SECTOR, WHICH IS WORTH BORROWING: WHILE ARTISANAL AND SMALL-SCALE MINING IS A VITAL SOURCE OF INCOME FOR MANY RURAL COMMUNITIES, IT HAS ACQUIRED A NEGATIVE REPUTATION OVER THE PAST TWENTY YEARS — IN PART BECAUSE THE GOVERNMENT HAS DIFFICULTIES TACKLING CORRUPTION, CRIMINAL ACTIVITY, CONFLICT FINANCING, FRAUD AND SMUGGLING IN THE SECTOR. The reputation problem is laid at the state's failure to police the sector, not at the miners. Communities whose livelihood is artisanal mining are routinely treated as the problem to be cleared — often to make room for an industrial concession — and this is a research institute's published counter. WHAT THE INSTITUTE IS: AN INDEPENDENT RESEARCH INSTITUTE PROVIDING TAILORED INFORMATION, ANALYSIS, CAPACITY ENHANCEMENT AND POLICY ADVICE. AND THE UNDER-OBSERVED AREA IT NAMES: THE WESTERN PART OF ONE NAMED TERRITORY HAS BEEN OVERLOOKED BY NATIONAL AUTHORITIES AND INTERNATIONAL PARTNERS, DESPITE MAJOR EXPANSIONS OF ARTISANAL GOLD MINING INCLUDING INSIDE A NAMED WILDLIFE RESERVE. Naming where nobody is looking is itself a service. If your area is in that gap, the absence of data is the finding to lead with. WHO IT SUITS: African mining-affected communities and miners' associations, and national organisations that want their own map — the code is published. CAVEATS: COVERAGE IS CONCENTRATED IN EASTERN DR CONGO WITH SMALLER DATASETS ELSEWHERE, AND THE GEOSERVER HAS BEEN OFFLINE DURING A MIGRATION — use the direct downloads if the map fails. For the comparative mining law atlas, Guinea-Bissau's entry; for the free instruments to take your own readings, Somalia's entry; for community-owned offline mapping tools, Equatorial Guinea's entry.

trackers.name: Month-long field courses where half the places are reserved for African and Malagasy participants, with scholarships that can cover international travel — and a stated willingness to write a letter of support for your other funding applications
trackers.desc: HALF THE PLACES ARE RESERVED FOR AFRICANS, AND THE SCHOLARSHIP PAYS THE AIRFARE — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S ANGOLA ENTRY NAMES THIS ASSOCIATION AMONG THE FOUR BODIES THAT BUILT THE FREE ORGANISATIONAL SELF-ASSESSMENT PLATFORM, WITHOUT DESCRIBING IT; ITS BURUNDI ENTRY THE FREE EVIDENCE DATABASE AND JOURNAL; ITS ESWATINI ENTRY THE TEAM-BASED CONSERVATION LADDER. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE HALF-THE-PLACES RULE, WHICH IS THE FIND: A KEY FEATURE OF EACH ONE-MONTH COURSE IS THAT HALF THE PARTICIPANTS ARE SELECTED FROM COUNTRIES IN AFRICA AND FROM MADAGASCAR; THE OTHER HALF FROM THE REST OF THE WORLD — BECAUSE IT BUILDS THE CAPACITY OF SCIENTISTS COMMITTED TO THE AFRICAN REGION, AND ESTABLISHES A STRONG INTERNATIONAL NETWORK. A fixed quota rather than an aspiration. African applicants are not competing against the whole world for the same seats — they are competing for half of them, and that changes the odds arithmetic completely. MADAGASCAR is named separately, which is worth noting given how often it is left out of both African and Asian programmes. THE SCHOLARSHIPS AND EXACTLY WHAT THEY COVER: A LIMITED NUMBER OF FULL OR PARTIAL SCHOLARSHIPS ARE AVAILABLE TO SUCCESSFUL AFRICAN APPLICANTS FOR COURSES IN AFRICA — COVERING THE COSTS OF INTERNATIONAL TRAVEL TO AND FROM THE RENDEZVOUS LOCATION, AS WELL AS TUITION, NATIONAL TRAVEL, ACCOMMODATION AND SUBSISTENCE. The airfare is inside the scholarship. This file has recorded training after training that waives the fee and leaves the flight, which is the cost that actually excludes people — and NATIONAL TRAVEL is covered too, meaning the bus from a rural district to the airport is not the thing that stops you. THE LETTER OF SUPPORT THEY WILL WRITE, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: PRIORITY GOES TO OUTSTANDING APPLICANTS BUT WE WILL ALSO TAKE INTO CONSIDERATION THOSE WHO CAN RAISE FULL OR PART OF THEIR PARTICIPATION COSTS — WE WOULD STRONGLY ENCOURAGE YOU TO LOOK FOR FUNDING FROM GRANTS, FOUNDATIONS OR YOUR ORGANISATION, AND WE WILL BE WILLING TO PROVIDE A LETTER OF SUPPORT TOWARDS YOUR APPLICATIONS. Ask for the letter. A conditional acceptance in writing is what turns a vague request to a foundation or an employer into a fundable one — and this file has recorded that document being the missing piece in dozens of failed approaches. Note the trade-off recorded honestly alongside it: bringing your own money improves your chances, which means the scholarship route and the self-funded route are not equally weighted. THE REAPPLICATION RULE: YOU CAN ONLY ATTEND ONE COURSE, BUT YOU MAY APPLY IN SUCCESSIVE YEARS IF NOT SELECTED — WITH APPLICATIONS TYPICALLY OPENING BETWEEN OCTOBER AND MARCH. Rejection is not final, and the window is published. Diarise October. THE ENTRY REQUIREMENT: COMPLETED 3 YEARS OF A BIOLOGICAL DEGREE, AS WELL AS PROFICIENCY IN SPOKEN AND WRITTEN ENGLISH — FOR STUDENTS AT ADVANCED UNDERGRADUATE OR EARLY POSTGRADUATE LEVEL WHO HAVE A KEEN INTEREST, BUT LITTLE EXPERIENCE, IN TROPICAL BIOLOGY. Three years of a degree and English are hard gates, and they exclude most community members outright. Recorded plainly: this is a route for the young graduate from an affected area, not for the committee itself — and it is a francophone and lusophone barrier too, despite a course having run in Guinea-Bissau. THE FEES AND THE MEMBERSHIP DISCOUNT: THE FEE IS £1,400, COVERING INTERNAL TRANSPORT, ACCOMMODATION, SUBSISTENCE AND TUITION, BUT NOT AIRFARES, INSURANCE AND VISA COSTS — PARTICIPANTS FROM MEMBER ORGANISATIONS PAY £1,000, AND APPLICANTS FROM MEMBER ORGANISATIONS ALSO RECEIVE PRIORITY FOR COURSE PLACES. MEMBER ORGANISATIONS GET PRIORITY, and members pay less. If an African university or research institution joins, its students gain both a discount and a better chance — which makes institutional membership a concrete thing to lobby a department for, rather than an abstraction. THE ALUMNI NETWORK AND WHERE THEY END UP: GRADUATES JOIN AN ACTIVE NETWORK OF OVER 2,500 ALUMNI IN 86 COUNTRIES, AND A REMARKABLE 95% OF ALUMNI ARE WORKING IN CONSERVATION — FROM RESEARCH INSTITUTIONS TO GOVERNMENT DEPARTMENTS AND NGOs. GOVERNMENT DEPARTMENTS is the one that matters for this file's readers. The alumni network includes people now inside the ministries that issue permits and write forest codes — and a community organisation whose member is in that network has a different quality of access. WHAT THE COURSES TEACH: PRACTICAL TRAINING AND EXPERIENCE IN THE TROPICS WITH AN EMPHASIS ON BUILDING SKILLS — HANDS-ON FIELD RESEARCH, PROJECT DESIGN, AND CONSERVATION CASE STUDIES, TAUGHT OUTSIDE THE CLASSROOM. PROJECT DESIGN is the transferable skill. A community organisation that can design a defensible survey is the one whose evidence survives challenge — and it connects directly to the evidence database filed under Burundi, which only accepts work that quantifies its results. THE SOCIAL CONTENT, UNUSUAL FOR A BIOLOGY COURSE: WE EXPOSE PARTICIPANTS TO THE CHALLENGES OF MEETING THE NEEDS OF LOCAL PEOPLE WHILE SAFEGUARDING THE NATURAL RESOURCES THEY RELY ON. Taught as a real tension rather than assumed away. Graduates who have been made to think about it are the ones who later design projects communities can live with. WHO TEACHES AND WHERE: COURSES RUN IN COLLABORATION WITH CONSERVATION AND RESEARCH INSTITUTIONS IN AFRICA AND SOUTH EAST ASIA, COVERING PRIORITY TOPICS THAT ARE RELEVANT — DRAWING ON SPECIALIST TEACHERS FROM THE HOST REGION AND THE GLOBAL CONSERVATION SCIENCE COMMUNITY, AT NAMED AFRICAN UNIVERSITY AND RESEARCH FIELD STATIONS, WITH AN ONLINE ELEMENT USING A VIRTUAL LEARNING ENVIRONMENT. THE OTHER AFRICAN COURSES ON RECORD: AN ECOLOGY MASTERCLASS WITH A NAMED ECOLOGICAL SOCIETY THAT GAVE 24 YOUNG AFRICAN SCIENTISTS THE SKILLS TO DESIGN SCIENTIFICALLY ROBUST PROJECTS IN THE FIELD; A FIRST FIELD COURSE IN GUINEA-BISSAU WITH A NAMED PORTUGUESE UNIVERSITY RESEARCH CENTRE; AND A CALL FOR AFRICAN CONSERVATION SCIENTISTS FOR A FIVE-DAY IN-PERSON COURSE IN NAIROBI. A five-day course is a different proposition from a month away. Watch for the short African-only calls — they carry no airfare problem for someone already in the region and no degree-length absence. AND WHAT IT SAYS IT IS: A SKILLS TRAINING NGO THAT PUTS YOUNG PEOPLE AT THE HEART OF CONSERVATION — RUNNING FIELD COURSES SINCE 1994. WHO IT SUITS: young African graduates from communities facing land and forest pressure, and African universities that could join as member institutions. CAVEATS: THREE YEARS OF A BIOLOGICAL DEGREE AND ENGLISH ARE REQUIRED, SCHOLARSHIPS ARE LIMITED, AND SELF-FUNDING IMPROVES YOUR CHANCES — this is not a route for a committee without a graduate member. For the free self-assessment platform this association co-built, Angola's entry; for the free journal that will publish the resulting work, Burundi's entry.

trackers.name: The vehicle that lets an African organisation take tax-deductible donations from American donors without incorporating in the United States — $1,000 to open against $15,000 to set up a US charity, with the annual fees and the percentage cut published
trackers.desc: $1,000 TO OPEN, INSTEAD OF $15,000 TO INCORPORATE — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S SOMALIA ENTRY RECORDS A FUNDER RECEIVING AMERICAN DONATIONS ON AN AFRICAN ORGANISATION'S BEHALF; ITS BURUNDI ENTRY RECORDS A CHARITY USING A NAMED INTERMEDIARY FOR THE SAME PURPOSE WITHOUT NAMING OR DESCRIBING IT; ITS LIBYA ENTRY THE FISCAL SPONSOR REQUIREMENT. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. WHAT IT LETS A FOREIGN ORGANISATION DO, WHICH IS THE FIND: WITH A FRIENDS FUND, FOREIGN ORGANIZATIONS CAN LAUNCH AND MAINTAIN A UNITED STATES FUNDRAISING APPEAL AND SOLICIT TAX-DEDUCTIBLE DONATIONS OF ANY SIZE FROM UNITED STATES DONORS — AND ANY FOREIGN CHARITABLE ORGANIZATION THAT IS ELIGIBLE IS WELCOME TO OPEN ONE. This file has now hit the same wall three times: an African organisation with willing American supporters cannot give them a tax receipt, so the gift does not happen. The obstacle is administrative rather than financial, and this is the instrument that removes it — DONATIONS OF ANY SIZE, so it works for a hundred small givers as well as one large one. THE PUBLISHED COST, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: OPENING A FRIENDS FUND REQUIRES A $1,000 SETUP FEE, FOLLOWED BY AN ANNUAL FEE OF $2,500 — WITH NO MINIMUM BALANCE REQUIREMENT, ALLOWING THE ORGANIZATION TO BEGIN RECEIVING TAX DEDUCTIBLE GIFTS AS SOON AS MEMBERSHIP IS APPROVED. Real numbers, so the decision can be made with arithmetic rather than hope. $2,500 a year is the break-even test: below roughly that in expected American giving, this costs more than it raises. NO MINIMUM BALANCE matters for a small organisation — the fund can sit empty between appeals. THE COST OF THE ALTERNATIVE, PUBLISHED BESIDE IT: ESTABLISHING A UNITED STATES CHARITY REQUIRES A TAX-EXEMPT STATUS APPLICATION WITH A COMPREHENSIVE NARRATIVE AND LEGAL GUIDANCE, ADDRESSING THE CONDUIT ISSUE WHICH ENSURES THE UNITED STATES ENTITY IS INDEPENDENT OF ITS FOREIGN COUNTERPART, PLUS STATE REGISTRATION AND MONTHS OF WAITING — A PROCESS THAT CAN COST UPWARDS OF $15,000 PLUS LEGAL FEES, WITH STATE REGISTRATION ADDING $2,700 TO $3,000 ANNUALLY. THE CONDUIT ISSUE is the trap worth understanding before anyone advises setting up an American arm: the United States entity must be genuinely independent of the African organisation, which means the body raising money in your name would not be under your control. The cheaper route is also the one that leaves the African organisation in charge. THE STEPS: COMPLETE A GRANT ELIGIBILITY APPLICATION, WHICH ALLOWS THE ORGANISATION TO BE VETTED FOR COMPLIANCE WITH UNITED STATES TAX LAWS; PAY THE INITIAL SETUP COSTS; AND ONCE THE VALIDATION PROCESS IS PASSED, DONORS CAN CONTRIBUTE WITH THE BENEFIT OF TAX DEDUCTIONS. WHAT THE APPLICATION INVOLVES: A COMPLETE, SIGNED ELIGIBILITY APPLICATION FORM, AND THE ORGANISATION WILL ALSO BE ASKED TO SIGN A GRANT AGREEMENT. One form and one agreement. Getting through the eligibility vetting once also produces a compliance record that other international funders recognise — which is worth more than the fund itself to an organisation that has never been vetted before. WHY IT EXISTS: FOR MANY FOREIGN NONPROFIT ORGANIZATIONS, ACCESSING DONORS FROM THE UNITED STATES IS AN IMPORTANT GOAL FOR FINANCIAL SUCCESS — HOWEVER, APPLYING FOR AND MAINTAINING A CHARITY THERE CAN BE A COSTLY AND CHALLENGING REALITY. THE MISCONCEPTION IT CORRECTS: IT IS WIDELY BELIEVED THAT THE ONLY WAY TO SUCCESSFULLY ENGAGE UNITED STATES DONORS IS TO ESTABLISH A FRIENDS-OF ORGANIZATION, A FULLY FLEDGED PUBLIC CHARITY — IN REALITY THERE IS AN EASIER AND LESS EXPENSIVE WAY. WHAT IT IS, DEFINED: A FORM OF FISCAL SPONSORSHIP THAT ALLOWS FOREIGN CHARITABLE ORGANIZATIONS TO RECEIVE DONATIONS FROM UNITED STATES DONORS AND OFFER THOSE DONORS A WAY TO RECEIVE A TAX DEDUCTION — WITH THE UNITED STATES PUBLIC CHARITY SERVING AS THE FISCAL SPONSOR. FISCAL SPONSORSHIP is the same term this file's Libya entry records as an alternative to holding your own bank account for a grant. One arrangement can therefore answer two separate requirements. THE FEE STRUCTURE STATED GENERALLY, INCLUDING THE PART THAT IS EASY TO MISS: IN GENERAL THE FOREIGN CHARITY PAYS A SETUP FEE AND AN ANNUAL FEE, AND THE UNITED STATES PUBLIC CHARITY ALSO TAKES PERCENTAGE BASED FEES ON GIFTS THE FUND RECEIVES. Recorded plainly because it is the number not on the headline: a percentage of every gift, on top of the annual fee. Ask for that percentage in writing before signing, and set it against the zero-overhead funder recorded in this file's Somalia entry. THE WORKED EXAMPLE ON RECORD: A CHARITY WORKING IN AFRICA CLOSED ITS OWN UNITED STATES PUBLIC CHARITY AND INSTEAD ESTABLISHED A FRIENDS FUND, AS A CHEAPER AND MORE EFFICIENT VEHICLE FOR RECEIVING TAX-EFFECTIVE DONATIONS. An organisation that had already done it the expensive way, and reversed. That is stronger evidence than any comparison table. THE OTHER ROUTE, AND ITS LIMIT: DONORS MAY ESTABLISH A DONOR ADVISED FUND, BUT WHERE A DONOR IS LOOKING TO TAX-EFFECTIVELY SUPPORT GRASSROOTS ORGANISATIONS LOCATED IN A FOREIGN COUNTRY, THE FRIENDS-OF AVENUE DOES NOT PERMIT SUCH ACTIVITY — WITH VETTING FOR DIRECT FOREIGN GRANTS INVOLVING EXPENDITURE RESPONSIBILITY AND EQUIVALENCY DETERMINATION. EQUIVALENCY DETERMINATION is the finding that your organisation is the equivalent of an American public charity. Once obtained it is reusable, and it is the document that lets foundations grant to you directly — worth asking whether the vetting you are already paying for produces it. AND THE PRACTICAL ADVICE PUBLISHED FOR DONORS, WHICH IS USEFUL IN REVERSE: DUE TO THE FEES INVOLVED, DONORS USUALLY RECOMMEND DIRECT FOREIGN GRANTS FAR IN EXCESS OF A NORMAL MINIMUM, AND IF A DONOR INTENDS TO SEND GRANTS MULTIPLE TIMES IN A YEAR THEY SHOULD REDUCE THE FREQUENCY, SINCE THIS INCREASES EFFICIENCY AND MAY REDUCE COSTS — AND DONORS SHOULD INFORM THE CHARITY THAT THEY HAVE RECOMMENDED A GRANT AND THAT IT SHOULD EXPECT COMMUNICATION ABOUT THE VETTING PROCESS. Read from the receiving end: ask a supporter for one annual gift rather than quarterly ones, because each transfer carries cost. And if a message arrives asking you to complete vetting, somebody has already recommended a grant to you — answer it quickly. WHO IT SUITS: African organisations with American supporters, diaspora networks or a public appeal in mind, that cannot afford or do not want a United States entity. CAVEATS: A PAID SERVICE WITH A SETUP FEE, AN ANNUAL FEE AND AN UNSTATED PERCENTAGE ON GIFTS — IT IS ONLY WORTH IT ABOVE A CERTAIN LEVEL OF AMERICAN GIVING, AND ELIGIBILITY DEPENDS ON PASSING A COMPLIANCE VETTING. It solves a tax problem, not a fundraising one: you still have to find the donors. For the funder that receives American donations for partners at no cost, Somalia's entry; for the fund requiring a fiscal sponsor, Libya's entry.

trackers.name: Legal Resources Foundation Zambia and its own law firm, Legal Resources Chambers — salaried advocates appearing free in court for about 35,000 people a year, with paralegal desks inside police stations (NOT the same-named Zimbabwean LRF, filed separately)
trackers.desc: A CHARITY THAT OWNS A LAW FIRM, SO ITS LAWYERS CAN STAND UP IN COURT — method and adjacency declared first: NAME COLLISION FOUND AND HANDLED. THIS FILE ALREADY CARRIES A ZIMBABWEAN FOUNDATION OF THE SAME NAME UNDER ZIMBABWE, ON A DIFFERENT HOST, WITH 25 OFFICES ACROSS 9 PROVINCES. THIS IS A DIFFERENT ORGANISATION IN A DIFFERENT COUNTRY — ZAMBIA — AND BOTH ARE NAMED HERE SO NO FUTURE ROUND CONFUSES THEM. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN FOUR HOSTS AND SIX DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; THE SUBJECT'S OWN HOST AND FOUR FACTS ABSENT, WITH ONE GENERIC PHRASE MATCHING THE ZAMBIAN STATUTORY LEGAL AID BOARD ON ITS OWN HOST, WHOSE ENTRY RECORDS LAND DISPUTES AS ITS FIRST LISTED CASE TYPE. NEITHER IS RESTATED. THE STRUCTURE, WHICH IS THE FIND: THE FOUNDATION HAS A REGISTERED LAW FIRM OF ITS OWN — A CHAMBERS THAT EMPLOYS LAWYERS UNDER THE FOUNDATION WHO PROVIDE FREE LEGAL REPRESENTATION TO LITIGANTS IN COURT, HEADED BY A PRINCIPAL ADVOCATE. A charity that owns a law firm. Most organisations in this file must find and pay outside counsel, or refer and hope; this one employs its advocates directly, which is why it can take a matter all the way into court without a fee arriving from anywhere. Worth asking any prospective helper: do you instruct lawyers, or employ them. THE DIVISION OF LABOUR INSIDE IT, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: PROFESSIONAL SERVICES ARE PROVIDED BY LAWYERS UNDER THE CHAMBERS, WHILE PARALEGALS AND SUPPORT STAFF CARRY OUT THE ACTUAL IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PROGRAMME ACTIVITIES — WITH A BOARD AS THE POLICY-MAKING ORGAN. Paralegals do the volume, advocates do the court work, and the two sit in one organisation. That structure is the reason 35,000 people a year can be reached by a body with a small number of lawyers. THE CASELOAD AND WHAT IS ON OFFER: ESTABLISHED IN 1993, PROVIDING LEGAL AID, PROMOTING HUMAN RIGHTS AND CONDUCTING LITIGATION IN THE PUBLIC INTEREST, DESCRIBED AS THE LEADING PROVIDER OF LEGAL SERVICES TO FINANCIALLY DISADVANTAGED PERSONS IN THE COUNTRY — HELPING ABOUT 35,000 PEOPLE EACH YEAR THROUGH LEGAL ADVICE AND IMPACT LITIGATION. WHERE ITS DOORS ARE AND HOW TO REACH THEM: FREE LEGAL ADVICE TO THE PUBLIC WITH OFFICES THROUGHOUT THE COUNTRY — A PUBLISHED HEAD OFFICE FLOOR, BUILDING, STREET, POST BOX, TELEPHONE AND EMAIL IN THE CAPITAL, A SECOND PUBLISHED OFFICE AND TELEPHONE IN LIVINGSTONE, AND NAMED CONTACT PERSONS INCLUDING A CHAIRMAN, VICE CHAIRMAN AND PROJECTS OFFICER. Named individuals with roles, not a general enquiries form. A community can ask for the projects officer by name. THE PARALEGAL DESK AT THE POLICE STATION: A PARALEGAL TEAM CONDUCTING A ROUTINE SCREENING AT KABWATA POLICE STATION PARALEGAL DESK IDENTIFIED THREE BOYS AGED 13, 16 AND 17 WHO HAD BEEN ARRESTED, AND THE PARALEGAL OFFICERS, TRAINED TO SEE BEYOND THE CRIME AND INTO THE CIRCUMSTANCES, DECIDED TO TAKE ACTION. A ROUTINE SCREENING at a police station desk. This file's Burundi entry records that counsel in the first hours cuts torture by up to 80%; a standing paralegal desk inside the station is how someone is actually found in those hours, and it is a cheap thing for a coalition to negotiate with a station commander. THE OBJECTS IT PUBLISHES: TO WORK ALONGSIDE OTHER NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL GROUPS, ORGANISATIONS AND ACTIVISTS WHO SHARE A SIMILAR CONCERN; TO LOBBY GOVERNMENT TO ADOPT INTERNATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS STANDARDS; TO WORK TOWARDS THE EVOLUTION OF A JURISPRUDENCE OF HUMAN RIGHTS CASE LAW THROUGH PROVIDING FREE LEGAL REPRESENTATION TO PERSONS WHOSE RIGHTS ARE VIOLATED; AND TO CAMPAIGN FOR LAW REFORM AND TRANSFORMATION OF INSTITUTIONS. THE EVOLUTION OF A JURISPRUDENCE is the giveaway that this organisation wants precedent, not just outcomes. A community whose case would settle a point of law is the kind it is looking for. WHAT IT SAYS IT IS AIMING AT: A COUNTRY WHERE SOCIAL JUSTICE AND A SUSTAINABLE HUMAN RIGHTS CULTURE ARE ATTAINABLE THROUGH LITIGATION IN THE PUBLIC INTEREST. THE SCARCITY FIGURE THAT EXPLAINS WHY ANY OF THIS EXISTS: ONLY AROUND 2,050 REGISTERED LAWYERS ARE AVAILABLE TO A POPULATION OF OVER 18 MILLION, HIGH-QUALITY LEGAL SUPPORT BEING RARE AND THEREFORE VERY EXPENSIVE. One lawyer for roughly every 8,800 people, and most of them in the cities. That ratio is why the paralegal layer exists at all, and it is worth checking for your own country before assuming an advocate can be found. THE PARALEGAL SYSTEM AROUND IT AND ITS SCALE: PARALEGALS HAVE BASIC TRAINING IN LAW AND HUMAN RIGHTS, ARE NOW OFFICIALLY RECOGNISED WITH THEIR TRAINING FORMALISED, AND WORK IN COURTS, AT POLICE STATIONS OR IN PRISONS; SINCE 2017, 104,000 PEOPLE HAVE RECEIVED FREE LEGAL COUNSEL THIS WAY, WITH 317 PARALEGALS TRAINED UNDER ONE PROGRAMME AND A NATIONAL LEGAL AID POLICY ADOPTED BY THE MINISTRY OF JUSTICE. OFFICIALLY RECOGNISED, with the training formalised and a national policy behind it. Where a country has taken that step, a community organisation can have its own members trained into a recognised role rather than depending entirely on outside lawyers. THE LIMIT ON WHAT A PARALEGAL MAY DO, PUBLISHED PLAINLY: PARALEGALS PROVIDE LEGAL INFORMATION AND STRUCTURED, PRACTICAL SUPPORT BUT DO NOT OFFER FORMAL LEGAL ADVICE — AND WHERE A MATTER BECOMES COMPLEX OR FALLS OUTSIDE THEIR REMIT, INCLUDING DISPUTES OVER LAND TITLES REQUIRING HIGH COURT ACTION, URGENT COURT DEADLINES OR CONSTITUTIONAL CLAIMS, THE PARALEGAL MUST ESCALATE PROMPTLY TO A QUALIFIED ADVOCATE. DISPUTES OVER LAND TITLES REQUIRING HIGH COURT ACTION is named as beyond the paralegal remit. That is the honest boundary this file has needed: paralegals are excellent at the first mile and cannot take a title fight to the High Court — so a community facing one needs an advocate identified before the deadline, not after. THE FREE TRAINING AND REFERENCE MATERIAL THAT EXISTS FOR THEM: A NATIONAL LEGAL INFORMATION INSTITUTE PUBLISHING PRACTICAL TOOLS, TRAINING MATERIALS AND SIMPLIFIED LEGAL INFORMATION — INCLUDING TRAINING MANUALS, STEP-BY-STEP GUIDES ON COMMON LEGAL ISSUES SUCH AS LAND RIGHTS, AND CURATED SUMMARIES OF LAWS AND COURT DECISIONS, ALL FREE, REGULARLY UPDATED, WITH AN OPTION TO ENABLE OFFLINE ACCESS SO THEY CAN BE USED WITHOUT AN INTERNET CONNECTION. OFFLINE ACCESS on a national law database, with a land rights guide inside it. Downloadable law is what makes a paralegal useful in a village with no signal. AND THE REGIONAL PATTERN VISIBLE ALONGSIDE IT: THE SAME-NAMED FOUNDATION IN THE NEIGHBOURING COUNTRY COORDINATES A HELP DESK INITIATIVE AT MAGISTRATES' COURTS LEADING A CONSORTIUM OF SEVEN PARTNERS, RUNS MOBILE LEGAL AID CLINICS IN RURAL AREAS AND A TOLL-FREE HELPLINE STAFFED BY ITS OWN LAWYERS, ASSISTS AN AVERAGE OF 16,200 CLIENTS A YEAR, AND HELPS SELF-ACTORS PRESENT THEIR OWN CASES — INCLUDING PROPERTY RIGHTS DISPUTES. A HELP DESK AT THE COURTHOUSE, run by a consortium rather than one organisation, assisting people to present their own cases. Where no lawyer is available, that is the fallback that keeps a matter from being thrown out on a technicality — and seven organisations sharing one desk is cheaper than seven offices. WHO IT SUITS: people who cannot pay for a lawyer and need one to actually appear for them, and coalitions considering a paralegal desk or a courthouse help desk of their own. CAVEATS: ONE COUNTRY, AND ITS CASELOAD IS DOMINATED BY CRIMINAL AND FAMILY MATTERS RATHER THAN LAND OR PLANNING; ITS OWN PUBLISHED RULES PUT HIGH COURT LAND TITLE DISPUTES BEYOND THE PARALEGAL LAYER, SO EXPECT TO NEED AN ADVOCATE. NOT TO BE CONFUSED WITH THE SAME-NAMED ZIMBABWEAN FOUNDATION ALREADY FILED UNDER ZIMBABWE. For the statutory board that lists land disputes first and processes applications in 48 hours, Zambia's own entry; for counsel in the first hours after arrest, Burundi's entry.
