trackers.desc: Vietnam's official national business registration portal. Here you can trace companies, their directors and filings registered in Vietnam.

trackers.name: National e-GP (muasamcong)
trackers.desc: Vietnam's national e-procurement system. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Vietnam, and for how much.

trackers.name: General Statistics Office
trackers.desc: Vietnam's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Vietnam.

trackers.name: Cộng đồng dân cư is a forest owner — and the district decides
trackers.desc: A COMMUNITY IS A FOREST OWNER IN ITS OWN RIGHT. Under the Forestry Law 16/2017/QH14, chủ rừng means an organisation, household, individual or cộng đồng dân cư to whom the State allocates or leases forest, or who receives it by transfer, gift or inheritance — so a community sits in the same category as an organisation, and forest can be inherited and gifted, which most community-forest regimes in this map leave unaddressed. THE DEFINITION IS BROAD AND NAMES THE WORDS DIFFERENT PEOPLES USE: Vietnamese people living in the same thôn, làng, ấp, bản, buôn, bon, phum, sóc or similar residential point and having the same customs and practices — shared customs are part of the test, so document them. GO TO THE DISTRICT, NOT THE PROVINCE: under article 23 the district People's Committee allocates, converts and revokes forest for residential communities, while the province handles organisations and leases to foreign-invested enterprises. Note the asymmetry — for communities the district may allocate, convert and revoke, but the leasing power listed for households is not listed for communities. Where a revocation area contains both organisations and communities, the province decides or delegates down.

trackers.name: The state pays for your forest inventory — use it
trackers.desc: AN OBLIGATION THAT IS ALSO FUNDING. Forest owners must carry out kiểm kê rừng (forest inventory) and submit to inspection — by the district forestry agency for households, individuals and communities — declaring data on prescribed forms. BUT THE SPECIALIST FORESTRY AGENCY MUST GUIDE AND SUPPORT TECHNICALLY AND MUST PROVIDE FUNDING FOR THE INVENTORY to owners who are households, individuals or communities. The state pays to document what you hold — elsewhere in this map communities must fund that themselves, and it is usually the step that stops them. WHAT OWNERSHIP GIVES YOU: quyền sử dụng rừng, the right to exploit the forest's uses and enjoy its fruits and income; and for planted production forest, possession, use and disposal of trees, livestock and other assets you invested — planted assets are owned outright even where the land is not. Note also giá trị rừng, defined as the total value of the ecosystem's components and its forest environmental values — a statutory basis for valuing environmental services, not just timber. TWO POLICY COMMITMENTS TO QUOTE BACK (article 4): the State ensures resources for special-use and protection forest, and protects the lawful rights and interests of communities engaged in forestry. And where an international treaty Vietnam has joined differs from this Law, or Vietnamese law is silent, the treaty applies.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: Royal Audit Authority
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Bhutan, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Bhutan — Ministry of Finance
trackers.desc: National budget authority; prepares & publishes the national budget and budget reports, Royal Government of Bhutan. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Bhutan.

trackers.name: Anti-Corruption Commission of Bhutan (ACC)
trackers.desc: Bhutan’s lead anti-corruption body — investigates and prosecutes graft, runs asset declaration and corruption prevention.

trackers.name: Bhutan — Corporate Regulatory Authority (CRA)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the CRA (formerly Office of the Registrar of Companies, upgraded 2024) incorporates companies and runs the online single-window company registry & compliance system, Bhutan. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Every Bhutanese is a trustee — the clause an individual can cite
trackers.desc: THE STRONGEST CONSTITUTIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL PROVISION IN THIS MAP. Article 5 of the 2008 Constitution requires that a minimum of 60 percent of Bhutan's total land be maintained under forest cover for all time — a permanent safeguard, not a policy target. AND IT VESTS A DUTY PERSONALLY: Article 5 states that every Bhutanese is a trustee of the Kingdom's natural resources and environment. That trusteeship clause is what an individual cites — stronger than the diffuse-interest provisions this map records for Paraguay and the Dominican Republic, because it is framed as a duty held personally rather than an interest shared collectively. HEADROOM: actual forest cover is around 71–72 percent and more than 51 percent of the country is protected across 10 national parks and sanctuaries — the largest protected share of any Asian country — so the 60 percent floor is not currently the binding constraint. BUT DO NOT MISUSE THE MANDATE: the World Bank's Bhutan Forest Note records that public debate is ‘prone to the misconception that sustainably managed forests do not count toward forest cover’. Arguing that management per se breaches the 60 percent mandate will fail — argue degradation, conversion or biodiversity impact instead. Only about 3.5 percent of land is managed for commercial production.

trackers.name: Community forests run on a certificate — and rule 63 can cancel it
trackers.desc: TWO THINGS TO READ BEFORE YOU NEED THEM. The Forest and Nature Conservation Rules and Regulations 2017 govern Community Forests with named provisions on sale of surplus forest produce (r.61), royalty (r.62), cancellation of the Community Forest Certificate (r.63), formation of CF network and association (r.64) and monitoring and evaluation (r.65). Your community forest exists by certificate, and rule 63 provides for cancelling it — read the grounds now, not later. And rule 64 gives community forest groups a statutory basis for forming a network and association, so groups can organise together rather than each negotiating alone. The 2017 Rules supersede all earlier government notifications, circulars, orders and rules. THE TENURE RULE: under rule 12, private registered land acquired by the Government for national interest becomes State Reserved Forest Land from the date of acquisition — conversion is automatic on that date. CHECK WHICH ACT YOU ARE READING: the Forest and Nature Conservation Act 2023 replaces the 1995 Act and both circulate; its 11 chapters cover State Reserved Forest Land, nature conservation, soil, water and waste, forest-based industry and offence and penalty, with powers in the Ministry of Energy and Natural Resources and the Department of Forests and Park Services. Your local contact is the Divisional Forest Office in the dzongkhag.

trackers.name: Bhutan Trust Fund — individuals and unregistered groups can apply
trackers.desc: NO LEGAL PERSONALITY REQUIRED — which removes the commonest barrier in this map. The Bhutan Trust Fund for Environmental Conservation, established 1991 as the world's first environmental trust fund by the Royal Government with UNDP and WWF and a US$20 million endowment, incorporated under Royal Charter in 1996 and renewed in 2021, is autonomous of government, with a Management Board fully Bhutanised in May 2001. ANY AGENCY, INSTITUTION, COMMUNITY OR INDIVIDUAL THAT IS BHUTANESE IS ELIGIBLE — recorded applicant types include communities and non-registered citizen groups, individuals, NGOs, subnational government and towns and municipalities. THE PAPERWORK IS WHERE GOOD PROPOSALS FAIL: small grant proposals may be submitted at any time of year in the prescribed template (with a separate annual call for larger grants); proposals from an agency must be approved by their head and carry an official forwarding letter; and an individual working in any agency, public or private, needs a No Objection Letter from it. Get the forwarding letter or NOL before drafting, not after. Fundable sectors include land management, sustainable rural livelihoods, community development and eco-tourism; thematic windows have included managing development impacts — expressly reducing environmental harm caused by development activities. It is also accredited to the Adaptation Fund (since 2018, valid to 6 February 2029) and the Green Climate Fund (2020), so it is a route to international climate finance too. Contact: Post Box 520, Genyen Lam, Thimphu; 975-2-33981.

trackers.name: Associação Projecto Vitó
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a Cape Verdean environmental association that began on Fogo as a volunteer effort after a sea-turtle rescue and now works on Fogo, Brava, Santo Antão, São Nicolau and Santiago, and in the Reserva Natural Integral dos Ilhéus do Rombo. It supports management of the Parque Natural do Fogo and the operationalisation of the Fogo Biosphere Reserve, working through citizen science and transferring technical knowledge to civil society. The first environmental NGO awarded Cape Verde's Medal of Merit, First Class. USE IT: as the organisation with standing and field presence inside Cape Verde's protected-area network — the route to getting a site monitored, documented and argued for. It is a conservation and education body, not a campaigning or legal one.

trackers.name: Biosfera
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a Cape Verdean NGO working on coastal and marine species and their habitats from São Vicente, with long-running field operations on the uninhabited island of Santa Luzia. It states a dual mission — conservation, and mobilising Cape Verdean civil society for the protection of the environment — and its strategic objectives include protecting coastal and marine habitats, promoting responsible artisanal fishing and reducing pollution that disturbs species and habitats. USE IT: as the coastal counterpart to the protected-area bodies. It is the organisation to approach about a shoreline, a fishery or a marine habitat under pressure, and the one in Cape Verde that most explicitly treats mobilising the public as part of its job.

trackers.name: Cabo Verde. Supremo Tribunal de Justiça
trackers.desc: Cabo Verde. Supremo Tribunal de Justiça — supreme court (Cabo Verde).

trackers.name: Tribunal de Contas
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Cabo Verde, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Cabo Verde — Ministério das Finanças
trackers.desc: National budget authority; the DGPOG prepares & publishes the State Budget (Orçamento do Estado) and provisional accounts, Cabo Verde. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Cabo Verde.

trackers.name: Cabo Verde — Casa do Cidadão (Porton di nos Ilha / Empresa no Dia)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the Casa do Cidadão portal handles company name reservation (Certificado de Admissibilidade de Firma) & the “Empresa no Dia” incorporation regime (IRN), with beneficial-ownership disclosure via CENTIF, Cabo Verde. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: Conselho Assessor — a statutory council per island, or per protected area
trackers.desc: A NAMED BODY WHOSE STATED PURPOSE IS POPULATION PARTICIPATION. Article 22(1) of Decreto-Lei n.º 3/2003 of 24 February provides that the government department responsible for the environment may create a Conselho Assessor for each island or, exceptionally, for a single protected area, with the object of facilitating management through the participation of the population and cooperation. TWO QUESTIONS FOLLOW: does a Conselho Assessor exist for your island or your area — and if not, can one be requested? The composition is set out in the Boletim Oficial, I Série n.º 44 of 23 July 2014, with certain representatives designated by the respective members of Government, so the balance between state and community seats is checkable in the gazette rather than a matter of practice. This is the route into management decisions short of litigation, and in a small-island jurisdiction it is likely to be the more productive one.

trackers.name: Six categories — and two of them have never been used
trackers.desc: PICK YOUR CATEGORY KNOWING WHICH ARE EMPTY. Decreto-Lei n.º 3/2003 creates the typology of protected areas and gives them juridical content, configures the Rede Nacional das Áreas Protegidas as an open system into which declared areas are progressively integrated, and articulates the public participation guaranteed in the Lei de Bases da Política do Ambiente. ‘An open system’ is the phrase to use — the network is designed to keep admitting areas, so a proposal works with the statute's logic; and the participation guarantee lives in the Lei de Bases, so cite both. THE SIX: Reserva Natural (15 sites, in integral, parcial and temporal subcategories — a ‘temporal’ reserve is protection for a defined period); Parque Nacional — no sites have been decreed; Parque Natural; Monumento Natural; Paisagem Protegida — zones where the integrated action of man and nature has created aesthetic or cultural value, protection centred on maintenance and restoration, so this is the category for a worked, inhabited landscape; and Sítio de Interesse Científico — places generally of reduced dimension holding populations threatened with extinction, of which none have yet been designated. For a small site with a threatened population that category is unused rather than unavailable — being first is harder, but it exists and is designed for small sites. Coverage exceeds 10 percent of the country, about 632.09 km²; Parques and Reservas Naturais are at least 75 percent of the network. Responsible body: Direção Nacional do Ambiente.

Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: ADAD, Praia — Cape Verde's oldest environmental association, and the 2020 decree that gives you an EIA to comment on
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Associação para a Defesa do Ambiente e Desenvolvimento (ADAD), a legally constituted NGO created in 1991 in Praia, Santiago, and published in the official gazette — the country's long-standing national environmental association, working on sustainable practice, biodiversity protection and environmental justice, alongside education and engagement with decision-makers. It is a member of the international conservation union and of regional marine and coastal networks, so a small island community has a route through it to outside technical and legal attention. Address: Avenida Cidade Lisboa, Fazenda, Praia, Santiago. THE LEGAL HOOK TO NAME, and it is recent enough that many people do not know it exists: Decreto-Lei n.º 27/2020 approves the legal regime for environmental impact assessment of PUBLIC AND PRIVATE projects likely to produce significant effects on the environment, published in the official bulletin of 19 March 2020, with requirements for impact studies and assessment processes aligned to established good practice. If a hotel, quarry, marina or road is proposed near you in Cape Verde, ask which EIA was done under the 2020 regime, and ask to see it — that document is the only formal opening most residents will get. WHO IT SUITS: Cape Verdean residents and community associations facing coastal development, quarrying or infrastructure, and island groups needing a national body with international network reach. CAVEATS: NO VERIFIED LIVE SITE OF ITS OWN WAS FOUND — this entry points at the conservation union's member record, and the association's public presence is largely through social media; it is an environmental association, not a law firm or a fund. For Sao Vicente and marine reporting, Cape Verde's Biosfera entry.

trackers.name: Cape Verde — free legal assistance is a state-assured right delivered by STATE-APPOINTED ADVOCATES, with an access-to-law institute alongside
trackers.desc: WHAT YOU ARE ENTITLED TO: in Cape Verde access to free legal assistance is a right ASSURED BY THE STATE, so that every citizen regardless of economic condition can have adequate legal representation — and the service is delivered by ADVOCATES APPOINTED BY THE STATE who act in judicial proceedings AT NO COST to the beneficiary. The mechanism is appointment, not application to a fund: what you are asking for is the nomination of an advocate, and the phrase to use is apoio jurídico / assistência jurídica gratuita. THE INSTITUTION NAMED ALONGSIDE IT: the Instituto de Acesso ao Direito e à Justiça (IADJ), described as a principal instrument of legal support, offering ORIENTATION and LEGAL REPRESENTATION to citizens; the Ordem dos Advogados de Cabo Verde sits beside it, running continuing training for advocates. The barriers the same account names are the familiar pair — lack of financial resources and the COMPLEXITY OF LEGAL PROCEDURES — with government and NGOs running free or reduced-cost assistance programmes to mitigate them. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ISLAND LAND DISPUTE: Cape Verde's development pressure is coastal and touristic, and the country's environmental impact regime — recorded separately in this file — gives a resident a document to contest; a state-appointed advocate is how an ordinary household actually contests it, because the EIA route is worthless if nobody can file. WHO IT SUITS: Cape Verdeans without means facing an expropriation, coastal development, inheritance or property dispute on any island. CAVEATS: THIS ENTRY IS SOURCED FROM A CAPE VERDEAN LEGAL-SECTOR PUBLICATION RATHER THAN A GOVERNMENT PORTAL — confirm the current procedure and the IADJ's contact details with the Ordem dos Advogados de Cabo Verde before relying on specifics; appointment depends on advocate availability across a nine-island archipelago. For the EIA regime and the national environmental association, Cape Verde's ADAD entry; for Sao Vicente marine reporting, Biosfera.

trackers.name: Fundo do Ambiente, Cape Verde — a public institute that finances environmental preservation projects, and it funds MUNICIPALITIES directly
trackers.desc: WHERE TO APPLY FOR MONEY: the FUNDO DO AMBIENTE, a Cape Verdean PUBLIC INSTITUTE whose current statute was approved by Decreto-lei nº59/2020 of 5 August, developing the regulatory norms foreseen in the Lei de Bases da Política do Ambiente and establishing the fundamental principles for managing and protecting the environment against all forms of degradation. The financing regime for projects relating to environmental preservation activity sits in Decreto-Lei nº40/2013. A dedicated financing decree plus a public institute means the money is not discretionary charity — cite the decree number when you ask what the current window is. WHO IT ACTUALLY PAYS, WHICH IS THE USEFUL PART: documented disbursements go to MUNICIPAL COUNCILS — the Câmara Municipal de São Miguel received a rotating excavator to give effect to its projects, and a new urban solid waste collection truck, and a memorandum of understanding was signed between the Fund, that municipal council and the island water utility. Equipment and works through your own câmara municipal is how island environmental money actually lands — so the lever, as in Mali, is the municipal council rather than a direct community application. Ask your câmara what it has requested from the Fundo do Ambiente and what it received; both sides of that are public. WHO IT SUITS: Cape Verdean municipalities, associations and communities with an environmental preservation, waste or water project on any island. CAVEATS: A STATE FINANCING INSTITUTE — it funds environmental preservation, NOT litigation, land purchase or opposition to a licensed development, and the documented flow is to municipal councils rather than to villages directly; confirm the current window and eligibility before relying on it. For the 2020 EIA regime and the national environmental association, Cape Verde's ADAD entry; for a state-appointed advocate, the legal assistance entry; for Sao Vicente marine reporting, Biosfera.

trackers.name: Cape Verde's protected areas and their Conselho Assessor — article 22 lets a council be created FOR A SINGLE PROTECTED AREA, to secure local community participation
trackers.desc: THE SEAT AT THE TABLE AND HOW TO GET IT: Cape Verde's protected areas sit in the REDE NACIONAL DE ÁREAS PROTEGIDAS under DECRETO-LEI Nº3/2003 of 24 February, with categories including Parque Natural, Reserva Natural and Reserva Natural Integral, each delimited by its own decreto-regulamentar. ARTICLE 22 IS THE PROVISION TO QUOTE: the government department responsible for the environment MAY CREATE A CONSELHO ASSESSOR FOR EACH ISLAND OR, EXCEPTIONALLY, FOR A SINGLE PROTECTED AREA, to facilitate management THROUGH THE PARTICIPATION OF THE POPULATION and cooperation between administrative bodies — and where such a council has been created its stated objects are TO SUPPORT AND ENSURE THE PARTICIPATION OF LOCAL COMMUNITIES AND PARTNER ENTITIES, and TO PROPOSE DIRECTIVES AND ACTIONS. A council can be created for ONE protected area, and its job is your participation — that is the cheapest formal standing available in Cape Verde: ask the environment department to constitute a Conselho Assessor for the area you live beside. WHAT THE DECLARATIONS ARE BUILT ON, which tells you what argument works: the Boa Vista Parque Natural do Norte was declared to conserve natural values AND THEIR INTERACTION WITH THE SOCIOECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT OF LOCAL POPULATIONS, THROUGH THE STRENGTHENING OF TRADITIONAL ACTIVITIES. Traditional activity is written into the ground of declaration — so a fishing or salt-working practice is an argument FOR protection, not an obstacle to it. WHAT THESE AREAS FACE, DOCUMENTED ON SAL: the Ponta do Sinó reserve is ALMOST ENTIRELY SURROUNDED BY RESORTS, its size reduced not only by government decrees but by the loss of sand migration, with dunes that have disappeared; threats listed are vehicle traffic across the dunes, coastal development, light and noise pollution, and disturbance of nesting and feeding sites. The Baía da Murdeira reserve, created 2003, is the ONLY officially designated MARINE reserve in Cape Verde — about 2,067 hectares; Costa da Fragata covers 2,693 hectares, 346 on land and 2,347 marine. Local conservation work is run as COOPERATIVE MANAGEMENT of the protected areas — training, trail delimitation, codes of conduct, dune restoration, and community outreach including GUIDE TRAINING AND SUSTAINABLE LIVELIHOODS FOR FISHERS AND RESIDENTS. WHO IT SUITS: Cape Verdean island communities beside a protected area or facing resort expansion. CAVEATS: STATE-DECLARED AREAS WITH ADVISORY COMMUNITY BODIES, NOT COMMUNITY TENURE — the council is assessor, and decrees have themselves reduced reserve areas. For the EIA regime, Cape Verde's ADAD entry; for money, the Fundo do Ambiente entry; for a state-appointed advocate, the legal assistance entry.

trackers.name: Cape Verde's island-by-island conservation organisations — FMB on Maio, BIOS.CV on Boa Vista, Projeto Biodiversidade on Sal, Lantuna nationally, and the honest gap in community management
trackers.desc: WHICH ORGANISATION IS ON YOUR ISLAND — the only question that matters in a ten-island archipelago: FUNDAÇÃO MAIO BIODIVERSIDADE (FMB, fmb-maio.org), A CABO VERDEAN NON-PROFIT FOUNDED 2010 ON MAIO ISLAND, running four programmes — TURTLE PROTECTION, MARINE CONSERVATION, TERRESTRIAL CONSERVATION, and SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT AND ECOTOURISM — with projects characterised by COMMUNITY-BASED STRATEGIES, strong scientific foundations and extensive outreach. WHAT IT ACHIEVED, WHICH IS WHY IT LEADS THIS ENTRY: work with FMB AS LOCAL PARTNER DELIVERED THE DESIGNATION OF A UNESCO BIOSPHERE RESERVE AND THE APPROVAL OF CABO VERDE'S FIRST PROTECTED AREAS MANAGEMENT PLAN, plus a GUARDIANS OF THE SEA initiative. A single-island foundation that produced the country's first protected-areas management plan is proof the instrument can start locally and end nationally — and FMB records that RANGERS deliver more than half the objectives of the biodiversity plan, so ask about ranger posts, which are jobs as well as protection. THE OTHERS, BY ISLAND: BIOS.CV, a Cabo Verdean NGO BASED ON BOA VISTA, TWENTY YEARS in environmental conservation — habitat protection for threatened turtles and birds, HUMPBACK WHALE MONITORING, environmental education for local people AND VISITORS, and TRAINING YOUNG PEOPLE in conservation of protected species and habitats; PROJETO BIODIVERSIDADE, a Cabo Verdean non-profit ON SAL ISLAND, protecting wildlife THROUGH COMMUNITY-LED ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION PROGRAMMES; and LANTUNA (lantuna.org), A CABO VERDEAN NGO CONSTITUTED 2013, for study, conservation and protection of the archipelago's environment, contributing to the sustainable development of RURAL AND URBAN COMMUNITIES and to ecotourism, working on the PARQUE NATURAL DA BAÍA DO INFERNO E DO MONTE ANGRA, and stating that it ACTS WITH AUTONOMY, guided by impartiality and merit, FREE OF EXTERNAL INFLUENCES, with a commitment to the collective interest and to making all essential information about its projects accessible. An organisation that publishes an independence clause is telling you it can act against an interest. Ask for that clause in writing from whoever offers to help you. AND THE STRUCTURAL GAP, RECORDED HONESTLY: UNLIKE OTHER WEST AFRICAN COUNTRIES, THERE IS NO PRACTICE OF COMMUNITY MANAGEMENT IN CABO VERDE — THOUGH A VARIETY OF COMMUNITY ASSOCIATIONS ACROSS THE ISLANDS REPRESENT FISHERS' INTERESTS, and partners are supporting those groups toward CO-MANAGEMENT OF MARINE RESOURCES AND COMMUNITY-LED PROTECTED AREAS. There is no established community-management route here yet — which means the fishers' associations that already exist are the vehicle, and the first community-led protected area is still unclaimed. WHO IT SUITS: Cabo Verdeans on any island, especially fishing communities and those near a natural park. CAVEATS: SMALL ISLAND NGOs, donor-dependent. For the oldest environmental association and the EIA route, Cape Verde's ADAD entry; for public financing, the Fundo do Ambiente entry; for the advisory council a protected area may create, the Conselho Assessor entry; also Projecto Vitó and Biosfera.

trackers.name: Plataforma das ONG de Cabo Verde — 724 registered organisations, a published roster of associations by island and concelho with phone numbers, and the 1987 law associations are formed under
trackers.desc: THE ROSTER BY ISLAND AND CONCELHO — which is what a Cape Verdean on one island actually needs: the PLATAFORMA DAS ONG DE CABO VERDE (platongs.org.cv) IS AN INDEPENDENT NON-PROFIT NGO WITH FINANCIAL, ADMINISTRATIVE AND PATRIMONIAL AUTONOMY, with a NAMED PRESIDENT, TWO PUBLISHED TELEPHONE NUMBERS AND AN EMAIL, whose mission is TO CONTRIBUTE TO STRENGTHENING AND IMPROVING THE LEVEL OF INTERVENTION OF ITS MEMBER ORGANISATIONS, and whose stated purpose has always been CREATING CONDITIONS THAT FAVOUR DIALOGUE, PARTICIPATION AND THE EMPOWERMENT OF CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, IN STRICT RESPECT FOR THEIR AUTONOMY. Patrimonial autonomy means it can hold property in its own right, and strict respect for members' autonomy is written into its purpose — an umbrella that says so is one your association can join without being absorbed. WHAT IT HOLDS: A BASE OF 724 ORGANISATIONS REGISTERED, and it has sought to take on FROM THE JUSTICE MINISTRY THE FUNCTION OF REGISTERING LEGAL PERSONS — arguing that because it is on the ground it could record each successive change within every association and so say AT ANY MOMENT HOW MANY ASSOCIATIONS EXIST IN CABO VERDE WITH EFFECTIVE FUNCTIONING, HOW MANY DO NOT FUNCTION, AND HOW MANY FUNCTION ILLEGALLY. Seven hundred and twenty-four organisations on one register, and the umbrella itself says the hard part is knowing which are actually working. Ask the Plataforma whether the association offering to help you is functioning — that is precisely the question it built the base to answer. AND IT PUBLISHES THE LIST: A GUIA DAS ONG AND A MAPEAMENTO DA SOCIEDADE CIVIL CABO-VERDIANA, PLUS A ROSTER OF CABO VERDEAN NGOs AND ASSOCIATIONS ARRANGED BY ISLAND AND BY CONCELHO WITH POSTAL ADDRESSES AND MOBILE AND LANDLINE NUMBERS — including, on Santiago, NAMED ASSOCIATIONS OF FISHERS AND FISHWIVES AND OF FARMERS AND LIVESTOCK KEEPERS at concelho level. An association of fishers and fishwives with a phone number in your own concelho is the ally a coastal project affects directly. Producer associations are already organised, already local, and already have a reason to object. THE NUMBERS THAT TELL YOU WHAT TO EXPECT: in one named concelho the survey records 18 CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, OF WHICH 14 ARE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT ASSOCIATIONS, WITH AN ASSOCIATIONAL PENETRATION RATE OF 16% AND FEMALE PARTICIPATION AROUND 47% — AND ONLY TWO OF THE SEVENTEEN AFFILIATED TO THE PLATAFORMA. Community development association is the dominant form in Cabo Verde, and most are NOT affiliated to the national platform. So the roster is where you find them, and affiliation is a step you can help a local association take. THE LAW THEY ARE FORMED UNDER IS NAMED: the associations law published in 1987, LEI Nº 78/III/87, is recorded alongside independence in 1975 and the political opening as one of the main references of Cape Verdean civil society's development. The Plataforma also records the sector's honest weakness: ONGs AND OTHER CSOs FACE NUMEROUS DIFFICULTIES, BEGINNING WITH THEIR LIMITED INSTITUTIONAL CONDITIONS AND INTERNAL CAPACITY TO PROPERLY MANAGE THE RESOURCES THEY OBTAIN FROM NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL PARTNERS. Capacity to manage money, not lack of money, is named as the first constraint. If you are raising funds for a local association, budget for its administration too. WHO IT SUITS: Cape Verdeans on any island seeking the association nearest them, and groups wanting to form or verify one. CAVEATS: A PLATFORM AND A DIRECTORY — not a funder or a law firm. For the local partner that delivered a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and the country's first protected areas plan, Cabo Verde's FMB entry; for the organisations on Boa Vista and Sal, BIOS.CV and Projeto Biodiversidade; for the independence clause, Lantuna.

trackers.name: AfricanDefenders (Pan-African Human Rights Defenders Network) — five sub-regional members with their own country lists, seven named Ubuntu Hub host cities from Kampala to Accra, and national coalitions it will help you build
trackers.desc: SEVEN CITIES WHERE YOU CAN GO AND STILL SPEAK THE LANGUAGE — placement note first: THIS IS A PAN-AFRICAN NETWORK, FILED UNDER CAPE VERDE BECAUSE THIS BUCKET CARRIED NO DEFENDER-NETWORK RESOURCE. ITS FIVE SUB-REGIONS COVER THE WHOLE CONTINENT. THE SEVEN HOST CITIES, NAMED: KAMPALA IN UGANDA; ABIDJAN IN CÔTE D'IVOIRE; TUNIS IN TUNISIA; JOHANNESBURG, PRETORIA AND CAPE TOWN IN SOUTH AFRICA; AND ACCRA IN GHANA — THE SEVENTH ADDED TO HOST ADDITIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS FROM WEST AFRICA. Seven actual cities with actual housing. This file's round on protection funds named the relocation programme in one line; here are the places it goes. Anglophone, francophone and arabophone options, which means for almost any African defender there is a destination where the language and the paperwork are familiar. AND WHAT THE RELOCATION IS FOR, IN ITS OWN TERMS: TEMPORARILY RELOCATING ARTISTS, BLOGGERS, JOURNALISTS OR OTHER HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS FACING VIOLENCE OR THREATS IN THEIR HOME COUNTRY — MOVING THESE ACTIVISTS TO A SAFE HOST CITY WHERE THEY SPEAK THE LANGUAGE AND REMAIN CONNECTED TO LOCAL ORGANIZATIONS, HELPING THEM CONTINUE THEIR IMPORTANT WORK — AND IN ADDITION TO PROVIDING HOUSING, THE NETWORK WORKS WITH LOCAL PARTNERS TO PROVIDE MEDICAL SUPPORT AND SERVICES. CONTINUE THEIR WORK, not stop it. That is the difference between relocation and exile: the point is to keep organising from somewhere safer, which is why the language and the connection to local organisations are stated as design features rather than conveniences. THE STRUCTURE, WHICH TELLS YOU HOW TO REACH IT: A NETWORK OF FIVE AFRICAN SUB-REGIONAL ORGANISATIONS, NATIONAL COALITIONS FOR HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS, AND INDIVIDUAL DEFENDERS — SO AN INDIVIDUAL IS A CATEGORY OF MEMBER, NOT ONLY AN ORGANISATION. THE EAST AND HORN MEMBER, WITH ITS COUNTRY LIST: IT ESTABLISHES AND SUPPORTS NATIONAL COALITIONS OF HRDs IN VARIOUS COUNTRIES THROUGH WHICH HRDs CAN COME TOGETHER AND CLAIM THEIR RIGHTS AT THE NATIONAL LEVEL — AND SERVES AS SECRETARIAT OF A SUB-REGIONAL NETWORK DRAWING MEMBERSHIP FROM BURUNDI, DJIBOUTI, ERITREA, ETHIOPIA, KENYA, RWANDA, SOMALIA TOGETHER WITH SOMALILAND, SOUTH SUDAN, SUDAN, TANZANIA AND UGANDA, REPRESENTING MORE THAN 100 HRDs, BOTH INDIVIDUALS AND ORGANISATIONS. ESTABLISHES AND SUPPORTS NATIONAL COALITIONS is a service, not a description. If your country has no defenders' coalition, this is the body whose stated job is helping you build one — and note the country list: Djibouti, Eritrea, Somalia, Sudan and South Sudan are all in it, which are among the thinnest buckets in this entire file. THE CENTRAL AFRICA MEMBER: BASED IN DOUALA, CAMEROON, IT ACCOMPANIES AND REINFORCES THE WORK OF HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS WITH THE AIM TO MITIGATE THEIR VULNERABILITIES AND RISKS, AND TO RAISE AWARENESS OF THE HUMAN RIGHTS SITUATION IN THE SUB-REGION — ITS VISION BEING TO PROMOTE, TRAIN AND SUPPORT DEFENDERS, FOSTER SOLIDARITY AMONG THEM, AND DEFEND THEIR RIGHTS WHENEVER THESE ARE UNDER PRESSURE. THE WEST AFRICA MEMBER: CREATED IN MAY 2005, COMPOSED OF NATIONAL COALITIONS FOR HUMAN RIGHTS AND INDIVIDUALS. AND THE SOUTHERN AFRICA MEMBER, WITH ITS OWN NINE-COUNTRY ASSEMBLY: DELEGATES FROM ANGOLA, BOTSWANA, THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO, ESWATINI, LESOTHO, MALAWI, SOUTH AFRICA, ZAMBIA AND ZIMBABWE. Four sub-regional bodies with published country lists between them. Find which one covers you, then ask it which national coalition exists in your country — that is a two-step route to the nearest organised protection, and it works from anywhere on the continent. THE PRACTICE WORTH REQUESTING BY NAME: THE NETWORK AND ITS MEMBERS ISSUE UNDERSIGNED REGIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL CALLS — INCLUDING ONE DEMANDING THE IMMEDIATE AND UNCONDITIONAL RELEASE OF A NAMED DEFENDER AND THE WITHDRAWAL OF HIS PROSECUTION, AND ONE OVER A RESTRICTION IMPOSED ON A MEMBER NETWORK'S ABILITY TO OPERATE THROUGHOUT A COUNTRY. A joint statement signed by regional and international organisations, naming a prosecution and demanding its withdrawal. That costs the network nothing and can cost a government a great deal. It is one of the fastest things to ask for when somebody is arrested — ask for the statement before you ask for money. THE RECOGNITION: A SHIELD AWARDS RECOGNISING OUTSTANDING DEFENDERS FOR THEIR IMPACT ON THE PROTECTION AND PROMOTION OF HUMAN RIGHTS. An award is protection. A named, publicly honoured defender is measurably harder to disappear quietly, and nominations are usually open. AND THE NOTE ON WHY ONE HOST CITY WORKS: THE HOST COUNTRY HAS LONG BEEN HOSTING REFUGEES COMING FROM ACROSS THE REGION, AND ITS REFUGEE POLICY HAS BEEN PRAISED AS ONE OF THE MOST OPEN IN THE WORLD. The relocation programme sits where the immigration rules already permit it. When considering where to move someone, the legal question is as important as the distance — and that is why these seven cities and not others. WHO IT SUITS: African land and environmental defenders under threat, and anyone in a country with no national defenders' coalition. CAVEATS: RELOCATION IS TEMPORARY and demand exceeds places. For the 24-hour helpline, the protection grants and the two directories, Benin's defender protection entry; for the 48-hour emergency fund, Liberia's African Defenders Emergency Fund entry; for the three application windows including a protection grant, Mauritania's rapid-response fund entry.

trackers.name: Farm Radio International — free radio scripts, dramas and interview questions already translated into local African languages, for the 1,300+ stations in 38 countries that have signed up — plus a published method that lets the community choose the topic and measured uptake of up to 48%
trackers.desc: THE SCRIPTS ARE FREE, AND OFTEN ALREADY IN YOUR LANGUAGE — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S ETHIOPIA ENTRY COVERS THE COMMUNITY RADIO ASSOCIATION, MEMBERSHIP AND THE LICENSING ARGUMENT; ITS CHAD ENTRY COVERS A FUND THAT PAYS FOR TRANSMITTERS AND EQUIPMENT. NEITHER CARRIES THE FREE PROGRAMME RESOURCES, THE LOCAL-LANGUAGE SCRIPTS OR THE PARTICIPATORY METHOD BELOW. WHAT THEY GIVE, AND THE LANGUAGE CLAUSE IS THE FIND: RADIO RESOURCES LIKE BACKGROUNDERS, DRAMA SCRIPTS AND SUGGESTED INTERVIEW QUESTIONS — OFTEN AVAILABLE IN LOCAL AFRICAN LANGUAGES — PLUS INFORMATION PACKAGES WITH SCRIPTS, INTERVIEWS AND DRAMAS, A WEEKLY NEWS SERVICE ABOUT RURAL COMMUNITIES IN AFRICA, AND ONLINE DISCUSSIONS BETWEEN BROADCASTERS AND SUBJECT EXPERTS IN ENGLISH AND FRENCH. A station with a transmitter and nothing to broadcast is the commonest failure this file could record. Here is a library of finished programmes — dramas, interviews, background briefings — already written and often already in the language your listeners speak, free, and the site lets you save and edit a resource as a Word document so it can be rewritten for your own valley. SUGGESTED INTERVIEW QUESTIONS is the item to notice. A volunteer presenter facing a district officer or a company representative for the first time does not need courage so much as a page of the right questions. THE NETWORK, AND WHAT IT DELIBERATELY IS NOT: MORE THAN 1,300 RADIO STATIONS IN 38 AFRICAN COUNTRIES HAVE SIGNED UP AS BROADCASTING PARTNERS — AND, IN THEIR OWN WORDS: WE DON'T OWN RADIO STATIONS, WE DON'T EQUIP, OPERATE OR FINANCE THEM. WE WORK WITH AFRICAN RADIO STATIONS TO PROVIDE THE COMMUNICATION SERVICES THAT AFRICAN FARMERS, ENTREPRENEURS AND RURAL COMMUNITIES NEED. They do not own or run anything, which means the station stays yours. Read that beside this file's warnings about outside organisations arriving with their own agenda — an organisation that supplies content and refuses ownership is a different kind of partner. THE MEASURED SCALE: IN ONE YEAR, 154 RESOURCES PROVIDED TO 3,420 BROADCASTERS; 33 PROJECTS WITH 259 PARTNERS; 256 STATIONS HELPED TO INTERACT WITH MORE THAN 401,470 OF THEIR LISTENERS — REACHING AN ESTIMATED 24.5 MILLION PEOPLE ACROSS RURAL AFRICA. THE EVIDENCE THEY PUBLISH ABOUT THEIR OWN METHOD: PARTICIPATORY FARM RADIO PROGRAMMING, WHEN IT MEETS STANDARDS OF QUALITY AND CONSISTENCY, LEADS TO REMARKABLE GAINS IN KNOWLEDGE — AND SPECIALIZED, CAREFULLY DESIGNED PROGRAMS CAN LEAD TO UPTAKE OF MORE EFFECTIVE PRACTICES BY UP TO 48%, ON AVERAGE 21%, OF FARMING FAMILIES IN LISTENING AREAS, AT A COST OF PENNIES PER PERSON. A fifth of families in the listening area actually changing what they do, measured. If you are trying to get a whole district to adopt a boundary rule, a closed season or a testing routine, that is the benchmark to hold your own communications to — and the qualifier QUALITY AND CONSISTENCY is doing the work: one broadcast changes nothing. AND THE HONEST ORIGIN OF THAT EVIDENCE, WHICH IS RARER STILL: PRIOR TO THE RESEARCH INITIATIVE, INVESTMENTS IN RADIO PROGRAMS FOR FARMERS HAD ASSUMED THAT, BECAUSE RADIO IS THE MOST ACCESSIBLE AND RELEVANT MEDIUM FOR FARMERS IN SUB-SAHARAN AFRICA, AGRICULTURAL INFORMATION PROVIDED ON THE RADIO WAS MEANINGFUL AND HELPFUL — BUT THERE WAS VERY LITTLE HARD EVIDENCE TO BACK UP THIS CLAIM. They went and tested an assumption their whole sector was built on. Ask the same of anything offered to your community: who measured it, and against what. THE PARTICIPATORY PRINCIPLE, WHICH IS THE TRANSFERABLE PART: THE APPROACH ACKNOWLEDGES THAT FARMERS UNDERSTAND AND CAN EXPRESS THEIR OWN NEEDS, CAN EVALUATE OPTIONS IF THEY HAVE THE RIGHT INFORMATION, AND CAN MAKE DECISIONS TO ADOPT — OR NOT TO ADOPT — A PARTICULAR PRACTICE. IT ACTIVELY ENGAGES FARMERS IN IDENTIFYING AND CHOOSING THE THEME OF THE CAMPAIGN, AND FEATURES THEIR VOICES, PERSPECTIVES, CONCERNS AND QUESTIONS. OR NOT TO ADOPT. A method that treats refusal as a legitimate outcome is the opposite of the consultations this file records, where the decision was made before the meeting and the meeting existed to record consent. THE FIRST TWO STEPS, SO A STATION CAN RUN IT WITHOUT THEM: COMMUNITY RAPID APPRAISALS IN 100 COMMUNITIES, FOUR PER PARTICIPATING STATION, EACH TYPICAL OF THE AREA SERVED — GATHERING WHAT FARMERS NEED AND HOW FARMERS USE RADIO; THEN IMPROVEMENT SELECTION, ENGAGING KNOWLEDGE PARTNERS SUCH AS AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH INSTITUTIONS AND UNIVERSITY EXTENSION SERVICES. HOW FARMERS USE RADIO, asked before anything is broadcast — what hour, on whose set, with whom listening. A campaign aimed at a time when the women who do the work are in the fields reaches nobody. THE SPILLOVER FINDING: WHEN EVEN A SMALL NUMBER OF FARMERS ARE ENGAGED BY A RADIO STATION ON A CONTINUOUS, INTERACTIVE BASIS, LISTENERS IN OTHER COMMUNITIES BENEFIT BY LEARNING ABOUT AND INTRODUCING PRACTICES THEMSELVES. Engage a few properly and the rest overhear. That is the argument for depth in one village rather than a thin campaign across twenty. THE OFFICES: OPERATIONS BEGAN IN ONE EAST AFRICAN COUNTRY, WITH OFFICES IN MALAWI, UGANDA, GHANA, MALI, BURKINA FASO AND MOZAMBIQUE. AND THE LIMIT THEY STATE THEMSELVES: NOT ALL OF THE RADIO STATIONS WHO RECEIVE OUR RESOURCES PARTICIPATE IN OUR RADIO PROJECTS. Two different things: the free resources, open to any partner station, and the funded projects, which are selected. Sign up for the first without expecting the second. WHO IT SUITS: African community and rural radio stations, and the farming or fishing communities who want their issue on air in their own language. CAVEATS: RESOURCES ARE AIMED AT BROADCASTERS AND SKEW AGRICULTURAL — a station or a partner organisation is the route in, and funded projects are selective. For the association a station joins and the licensing argument, Ethiopia's entry; for grants that pay for transmitters and equipment, Chad's entry; for legal defence when a broadcaster is sued, South Sudan's entry.

trackers.name: SOMO (Centre for Research on Multinational Corporations) — a research centre running since 1973 that files complaints to accountability mechanisms on behalf of people harmed by financed projects — with a complaint-tools website covering the African development bank, and the published finding that fear of reprisal is what stops communities using these routes
trackers.desc: THEY FILE THE COMPLAINT THEMSELVES, ON YOUR BEHALF — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S CHAD ENTRY COVERS THE NATIONAL CONTACT POINTS, ITS BURUNDI ENTRY THE DATABASE OF COMPLAINTS TO ACCOUNTABILITY MECHANISMS AND THE REQUEST-ONLY LEGAL NON-PROFIT, ITS NIGERIA ENTRY THE AFRICAN DEVELOPMENT BANK'S OWN REVIEW MECHANISM, AND ITS COMOROS ENTRY THE CARBON GRIEVANCE REVIEW WHICH CITES THIS CENTRE'S RESEARCH. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. WHAT IT DOES FOR AFFECTED PEOPLE, AND IT IS THE FIND: IT SUPPORTS THOSE PEOPLE ADVERSELY AFFECTED BY DEVELOPMENT-FINANCE-INSTITUTION-FINANCED ACTIVITIES BY FILING COMPLAINTS TO THE INDEPENDENT ACCOUNTABILITY MECHANISMS. Not a guide to filing — the filing itself. This file holds several entries explaining how these mechanisms work; this is an organisation that will draft and lodge the complaint, which is the step where most communities stop. THE COMPLAINT-TOOLS WEBSITE IT PROVIDES: A WEBSITE PROVIDING INFORMATION AND TOOLS TO FILE COMPLAINTS AGAINST A COMPANY, BUSINESS OR MULTINATIONAL CORPORATION IN ORDER TO PREVENT, STOP AND SEEK JUSTICE FOR NEGATIVE IMPACTS CAUSED BY THEIR BUSINESS ACTIVITIES — WITH THE MECHANISMS COVERED INCLUDING THOSE OF AN AFRICAN DEVELOPMENT BANK. PREVENT and STOP, not only seek justice afterwards. The African bank's mechanism is covered on the same site as the corporate routes, so one page compares the option against your government's financier with the option against the company itself. THE HONEST FINDING ABOUT WHY THESE ROUTES GO UNUSED, WHICH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT THING HERE: RESEARCH CARRIED OUT WITH PARTNERS SHOWS THAT VICTIMS OF HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS ARE AFRAID TO SPEAK OUT AGAINST THOSE VIOLATIONS, AND EXPRESSED THAT THIS FEAR PREVENTED THEM FROM RAISING A COMPLAINT WITH INTERNATIONAL NON-JUDICIAL GRIEVANCE MECHANISMS. Every complaint route in this file assumes somebody is willing to be named. Researchers asked why they were not being used and the answer was fear, not ignorance — which means the first question before any filing is who will be exposed, and whether the mechanism accepts a complaint lodged by an organisation on the community's behalf. That is exactly what this centre does. THE AFRICAN CASE IT RECORDS: ALSO IN LIBERIA, IT WAS OBSERVED THAT THE COMMUNITIES THAT EXPRESSED COMPLAINTS OR GRIEVANCES TO A NAMED STEEL MULTINATIONAL RECEIVED THREATS FROM BOTH THE COMPANY AND FROM LOCAL OFFICIALS. FROM BOTH THE COMPANY AND FROM LOCAL OFFICIALS. The district administration and the concession holder responded together — which is why this file's defender-protection entries under Benin and Morocco belong in the plan before the complaint is lodged, not after. THE SERVICES IT OFFERS: CUSTOM-MADE SERVICES — RESEARCH, CONSULTING AND TRAINING — TO NON-PROFIT ORGANISATIONS AND THE PUBLIC SECTOR, AND STRENGTHENING COLLABORATION BETWEEN CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS THROUGH ITS WORLDWIDE NETWORK. CUSTOM-MADE RESEARCH for non-profits. A national organisation can commission the corporate investigation it cannot do itself — and this file's Benin entry covers a second organisation doing the same on request. HOW IT DESCRIBES ITS OWN PLACEMENT: COOPERATING WITH HUNDREDS OF ORGANISATIONS AROUND THE WORLD, IT ENSURES THAT ITS RESEARCH LANDS WHERE IT HAS THE MOST IMPACT — FROM COMMUNITIES AND COURTROOMS TO THE DESKS OF CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, MEDIA, AND POLITICIANS. COURTROOMS listed second. Research produced to evidentiary standard is a different product from a campaign report, and worth specifying when commissioning. THE NETWORKS IT HOSTS: DOZENS OF THEMATIC GLOBAL NETWORKS, AND IT HOSTS SEVERAL — INCLUDING A GOOD ELECTRONICS NETWORK, A RESPONSIBLE BUSINESS PLATFORM, AN OECD WATCH, AND A TAX JUSTICE NETWORK. AN OECD WATCH hosted here. That is the network monitoring the national contact points filed under Chad — so the same address reaches both the route and its watchdog. THE SECTORS IT RESEARCHES: ELECTRONICS, ENERGY AND WATER, MINERALS, AGRICULTURE AND FOOD, CLOTHING, PHARMACEUTICALS AND FINANCIAL SECTORS — AND ON CORPORATE ACCOUNTABILITY IT TRACKS SUPPLY CHAINS, TAX AVOIDANCE, LEGAL LOOPHOLES AND ABUSES OF CORPORATE POWER. ENERGY AND WATER as a named sector. Water concessions and utility privatisations rarely get corporate-research attention, and a community fighting one has few places to ask. THE ADVOCACY SUPPORT IT NAMES: SUPPORTING COMMUNITIES, UNIONS AND NGOs IN STRATEGIC CAMPAIGNS FOR JUSTICE AND REGULATION. THE LETTERBOX PRECEDENT ON RECORD, WHICH IS THE TACTICAL FIND: A NATIONAL CONTACT POINT ACCEPTED A COMPLAINT FILED BY INDIGENOUS GROUPS AGAINST AN OIL MULTINATIONAL — THE FIRST TIME A COMPLAINT AGAINST A LETTERBOX COMPANY HAD BEEN DECLARED ADMISSIBLE. A LETTERBOX COMPANY — a shell with an address and no operations, used to hold a concession at one remove from the parent. Communities are told repeatedly that the entity on their land has no reachable owner. That defence has now failed once, on the record, in a case brought by indigenous groups. THE REGULATORY STRATEGY IT PUBLISHES: PROMOTING BINDING LEGISLATION AND SELECTIVELY SUPPORTING POWERFUL SOFT LAW STANDARDS THAT CAN PAVE THE WAY FOR HARD RULES; ALIGNING CLOSELY WITH PARTNERS TO ADVANCE MORE ROBUST REGULATIONS OR ENFORCEMENT; SUPPORTING STRONG MANDATORY HUMAN RIGHTS AND ENVIRONMENTAL DUE DILIGENCE AT NATIONAL AND EUROPEAN LEVELS; AND STRENGTHENING AND STRATEGICALLY USING THE OECD GUIDELINES. MANDATORY DUE DILIGENCE laws in Europe require companies to check their supply chains for harm. When those laws bite, the evidence they need is exactly what an African community already holds — and knowing which organisations feed that machine is how your case gets into it. AND THE CRITIQUE IT RECORDS OF THE FINANCE SIDE: NGOs CRITICIZED A FINANCE CORPORATION'S POOR RECORD IN SANCTIONING COMPANIES IT FINANCES FOR NON-COMPLIANCE WITH ITS STANDARDS IN CONFLICT-AFFECTED AND FRAGILE ENVIRONMENTS. Standards that are not enforced against the financed company. Filed honestly: expect the mechanism to find in your favour and the money to keep flowing, and plan the campaign accordingly. WHO IT SUITS: African communities and national organisations facing a multinational or a financed project, particularly where naming individual complainants would be dangerous. CAVEATS: AMSTERDAM-BASED AND WORKING THROUGH PARTNERS RATHER THAN INTAKE, AND ITS OWN RESEARCH SHOWS THESE MECHANISMS OFTEN FAIL — pair with legal and protection support. For the national contact points, Chad's entry; for what such complaints have actually achieved, Burundi's entry; for research done on request, Benin's entry.

trackers.name: An African conservation NGO that incubates emerging non-profit organisations, publishes a named officer's direct email, and asks anyone with a specific project to write in — plus community training that has ended in paid internships
trackers.desc: THEY INCUBATE NEW NON-PROFITS, AND THEY PUBLISH AN EMAIL ADDRESS — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S TOGO ENTRY COVERS THE 12-COUNTRY CONSERVATION IMPLEMENTER, ITS SEYCHELLES ENTRY THE TAX DEDUCTION, ITS SÃO TOMÉ ENTRY THE SERVITUDE TRUST, ITS SOUTH SUDAN ENTRY THE LAND BUYER, ITS CHAD ENTRY THE TRUST-FUND LIBRARY. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. THE INCUBATION LINE, WHICH IS THE FIND: AMONG THE THINGS IT DOES — ALONGSIDE LANDSCAPE WILDERNESS MANAGEMENT, DEVELOPING YOUNG LEADERS FROM DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES, DIRECT ACTION ANTI-POACHING AND ADVOCACY AT A GOVERNMENT LEVEL — IS THE INCUBATION OF EMERGING NON-PROFIT ORGANISATIONS. Incubating new organisations, stated as ordinary work. This file has recorded registration, governance and a bank account as the gate that keeps community groups out of every fund in it — and has repeatedly had to advise finding a fiscal sponsor. An established body that will host and grow a new organisation is the direct answer, and almost nothing else here offers it. THE OPEN DOOR, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: IF THERE IS A SPECIFIC PROJECT THAT YOU WOULD LIKE TO GET INVOLVED IN, PLEASE SEND US A MESSAGE AND WE WILL GET IN TOUCH WITH YOU TO DISCUSS ALL THE OPTIONS. An invitation to write in about a specific project, published on their own site. Write with the project, not with a request for support in general — that is the shape they asked for. THE NAMED CONTACT: A CHIEF OPERATIONS OFFICER FOR CONSERVATION IS NAMED WITH A DIRECT EMAIL ADDRESS AGAINST THE SPECIES PROGRAMME. A named senior officer with a working email, not a contact form. That is the difference between a message that reaches a person and one that reaches an inbox nobody owns. THE TRAINING THAT ENDED IN PAID WORK, WITH ITS NUMBERS: AN EMPLOYABILITY, WELLNESS AND LEADERSHIP TRAINING COURSE, FUNDED BY A NAMED COMMUNITY CONSERVATION FUND, INCLUDED YOUTH FROM COMMUNITIES AROUND A NAMED WILDLIFE RESERVE — 20 GRADUATES COMPLETED THE TRAINING, AND TWO NAMED GRADUATES EARNED PAID INTERNSHIPS AT THAT RESERVE THANKS TO A NAMED CONSERVATION FUND. Twenty trained, two into paid work, reported honestly with the names of the funders who paid for each part. That ratio is worth knowing before a community invests its young people's time — and the funders named are themselves two more doors, since a course like this is arranged between an NGO and a fund rather than applied for. WHAT THE SOCIAL PROGRAMMES ARE FOR: IT IS ONE OF THE FEW CONSERVATION NGOs IN ITS COUNTRY CURRENTLY INVOLVED IN ACTIVE, SUSTAINABLE SOCIAL INTERVENTION PROGRAMMES — THROUGH WHICH YOUNG PEOPLE ARE EMPOWERED TO BECOME FINANCIALLY INDEPENDENT ENTREPRENEURS AND BREADWINNERS FOR THEIR FAMILIES. THE FLAGSHIP-SPECIES METHOD IT PUBLISHES: A PROGRAMME USES ICONIC WILDLIFE SPECIES AS FLAGSHIPS TO DRAW ATTENTION TO CHALLENGES FACING CONSERVATION AND WILDERNESS AREAS — INTERVENTIONS DIRECTED TOWARDS THESE SPECIES RESULT IN THE PROTECTION OF LANDSCAPES AND THE ASSOCIATED WILDLIFE, AND THE PROMOTION OF BENEFICIATION TO LOCAL COMMUNITIES. The method stated plainly: pick the animal that attracts money and attention, and the landscape is protected behind it. A community whose land holds a well-known species has a lever that a community with only rare plants does not — which is worth knowing when deciding how to frame an appeal, and worth naming as the reason obscure ecosystems go unfunded. WHAT A SPECIES INITIATIVE CONTAINS IN PRACTICE: THE ESTABLISHMENT OF NEW POPULATIONS IN SUITABLE HABITAT, LAW ENFORCEMENT SUPPORT, AND DEMAND REDUCTION WORK IN THE CONSUMER COUNTRY — WITH A CAMPAIGN USING LOCALLY GENERATED INFORMATIVE MATERIAL, SOCIAL MEDIA, EVENTS, SEMINARS, PRESENTATIONS, COMPETITIONS AND FIRST-HAND WILDLIFE EXPERIENCES TO WORK ALONGSIDE YOUTH IN THAT COUNTRY. DEMAND REDUCTION IN THE CONSUMER COUNTRY. Work aimed at the buyers thousands of kilometres away, run alongside the field work — the same logic as the investment-chain entries elsewhere in this file. WHAT IT SAYS IT DOES OVERALL: IT PROTECTS AND SUSTAINS LANDSCAPES THROUGH AN AGILE AND INNOVATIVE APPROACH, INTEGRATING SPECIES, SPACES AND PEOPLE — INCLUDING BUILDING CLIMATE RESILIENCE. THE RECURRING-DONATION AND BANKING DETAIL IT PUBLISHES: FULL BANK ACCOUNT DETAILS INCLUDING BRANCH CODE, ACCOUNT NUMBER AND SWIFT CODE, AN INSTANT MOBILE DONATION APP OPTION WITH INSTALLATION GUIDANCE, AND MONTHLY, QUARTERLY OR ANNUAL RECURRING CONTRIBUTIONS. Recorded because it is a template rather than a service: publishing full banking details, a mobile app route and a recurring option is how a small African organisation makes itself payable from anywhere. Most community organisations in this file cannot receive money even when someone wants to send it. ITS AGE AND STANDING: OVER 45 YEARS OF RESULTS AND A FIFTY-YEAR EXPERIENCE, WITH THE WORK RECEIVING A NAMED INTERNATIONAL AWARD FOR ENTERPRISE IN 2008, AND A LEADERSHIP HANDOVER IN 2000 FROM ITS FOUNDING FIGURE. THE ALLIANCE IT CO-FOUNDED: IN 2015 IT CO-FOUNDED AN INTERNATIONAL ALLIANCE OF ACTION-ORIENTED ORGANISATIONS WHO UNDERSTAND THAT WILDERNESS AREAS HAVE LOCAL MEANING AND GLOBAL SIGNIFICANCE — WHOSE FOUNDING MEMBERS ARE THIS FOUNDATION AND TWO NAMED NORTHERN ORGANISATIONS, WITH A LEADERSHIP SCHOOL FOUNDED IN 1957 AS A PATRON PARTNER. An African organisation as a founding member of a northern alliance rather than a grantee of one. Worth noting as the structure to ask for when an international body proposes a partnership. AND THE POLICY BODY IN THAT ALLIANCE: A WILDERNESS SPECIALIST GROUP OF A WORLD COMMISSION ON PROTECTED AREAS WHICH ASSURES GLOBAL WILDERNESS POLICY AND LEGISLATION THAT SAFEGUARDS THE IRREPLACEABLE LIFE SUPPORT SERVICES OF WILD NATURE AND PROVIDES DIRECT CULTURAL AND SOCIAL BENEFITS TO HUMAN COMMUNITIES. A specialist group inside the body that sets protected-area standards internationally. Where a designation is being drafted over your land, that is where the definitions are argued. WHO IT SUITS: African community groups that need to become an organisation, and southern African communities near reserves seeking training, work or a landscape partner. CAVEATS: SOUTH AFRICA-BASED WITH ITS FIELD WORK CONCENTRATED THERE; IT IS A CONSERVATION IMPLEMENTER RATHER THAN A FUNDER OR A LAW FIRM, AND ITS SPECIES PROGRAMMES INCLUDE ANTI-POACHING LAW ENFORCEMENT SUPPORT, WHICH SOME COMMUNITIES WILL WEIGH CAREFULLY. For the 12-country implementer with free assessment tools, Togo's entry; for the fund that has bought land, Eswatini's entry.

trackers.name: An encrypted reporting app with automatic GPS, built with communities facing illegal logging — plus an investigation dashboard and a storytelling tool, designed around low literacy, weak networks and surveillance, with credentials issued on request by email
trackers.desc: AN ENCRYPTED APP THAT STAMPS THE GPS ON YOUR EVIDENCE — method and adjacency declared first: A NATIONAL CIVIL SOCIETY LAND COALITION WAS CHECKED FIRST THIS ROUND AND FOUND ALREADY FILED UNDER GHANA BY NAME AND BY FACT, SO IT WAS NOT DUPLICATED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THREE HOSTS AND SIX DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS THE FULL NAME AND DESCRIPTION TEXT OF ALL 53 BUCKETS; THE SHIPPED HOST AND FIVE FACTS ARE ABSENT, AND ONE GENERIC PHRASE MATCHED ONE ENTRY, READ IN FULL AND A DIFFERENT SUBJECT. THIS FILE'S GAMBIA ENTRY COVERS THE FREE GUIDES ON FILMING SO FOOTAGE STANDS AS EVIDENCE AND ITS SIERRA LEONE ENTRY THE SCHOOL THAT TRAINS RESIDENTS TO DOCUMENT A MINE. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. WHAT THE APP RECORDS AND HOW IT PROTECTS IT, WHICH IS THE FIND: GPS AUTOMATICALLY RECORDS LOCATION; RECORD VIDEO, AUDIO OR TAKE PHOTOS; END-TO-END ENCRYPTION; AUTOMATIC LOGOUT AFTER 5 MINUTES; COMPATIBILITY WITH A TOR PROJECT PROXY; A RECORD OF ALL REPORTS KEPT IN THE APP; AND EXPORT OF AN ENCRYPTED ZIP FILE TO SD CARD — WITH BUILT-IN VIDEO TUTORIALS. Every funder, court, complaints desk and petition in this file assumes the community arrives with a dated, located, credible record. This is the instrument that makes one. AUTOMATIC LOGOUT AFTER 5 MINUTES and TOR COMPATIBILITY are the details that matter where phones get taken at roadblocks — and EXPORT TO SD CARD means the evidence survives the phone being confiscated. THE THREE TOOLS AND WHAT EACH IS FOR, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: A REPORTING APP FOR SIMPLE, SECURE AND SYSTEMATIC REPORTING FROM THE FRONTLINE; AN INVESTIGATION DASHBOARD TO FIND CONNECTIONS BETWEEN EVENTS AND INDIVIDUALS OVER SPACE AND TIME; AND A STORYTELLING TOOL TO SHARE EMBEDDABLE MULTIMEDIA NARRATIVES. The dashboard is the part communities rarely have: fifty separate incidents become one pattern across space and time, which is what turns a list of complaints into an argument a regulator or a court can act on. This file's Sierra Leone entry records monitors concluding that reporting alone changed nothing — the dashboard is the answer to that. HOW TO GET IT: IT IS A CLOSED APPLICATION — TO GET CREDENTIALS THAT ALLOW YOU TO USE THE APP, GET IN TOUCH VIA A PUBLISHED EMAIL ADDRESS. Closed by design rather than by gatekeeping: an open reporting app is an open target. One email gets an organisation credentialed, and that is the whole application process. WHERE IT CAME FROM AND WHO BUILT IT: FIRST DEVELOPED TO TARGET ILLEGAL LOGGING IN ONE WEST AFRICAN COUNTRY, FOUNDED BY A FILMMAKER AS A RESULT OF WORK WITH A TEAM OF ACTIVISTS FROM A NAMED NATIONAL INSTITUTE — APPLYING THE KNOWLEDGE OF JOURNALISTS, SCIENTISTS, TECHNOLOGISTS, DESIGNERS AND SECURITY EXPERTS. WHAT IT WAS DESIGNED AROUND, WHICH IS UNUSUAL: THE TEAM STARTED FROM SQUARE ONE, BUILDING THE SYSTEM TO WITHSTAND THE DIFFICULTIES OF RUNNING A TECHNOLOGY PROJECT IN THE REGION — TAKING INTO ACCOUNT INFRASTRUCTURE AND NETWORK CHALLENGES, AS WELL AS LIMITATIONS IN LITERACY AND SECURITY CONCERNS; THE SYSTEM WAS DESIGNED TO FIT THE NEEDS OF A GIVEN COMMUNITY. LITERACY named as a design constraint alongside network and security. Most reporting tools in this file assume a user who can read a form in English; this one was rebuilt from nothing because that assumption failed. THE TIMING ARGUMENT: REAL-TIME REPORTING MEANS USERS CAN PREVENT ILLEGAL LOGGING BEFORE THE FIRST TREE IS FELLED — WITH THE AIM OF DELIVERING ACTIONABLE REPORTS THAT TRIGGER ACTION FROM GOVERNMENT AND POLICYMAKERS. BEFORE THE FIRST TREE IS FELLED. Read beside the development bank's complaint desk filed under Morocco, which accepts complaints while a project is still under preparation: the two together are a route to stopping something rather than documenting its aftermath. WHAT IT WAS FUNDED TO ACHIEVE: A SECURE AND EFFECTIVE MECHANISM FOR EVIDENCE-BASED REPORTING OF ENVIRONMENTAL CRIMES — ENABLING CITIZENS TO HOLD BUSINESSES AND GOVERNMENT TO ACCOUNT AND ENSURE COMMUNITIES' VOICES ARE CENTRAL TO DIALOGUES ON WHAT HAPPENS TO THE COUNTRY'S LAND AND RESOURCES. THE SECURITY BENEFIT ITS USERS REPORTED, IN THEIR OWN WORDS: IT HAS HELPED WITH OUR SECURITY. Users found the tool made them safer, not more exposed — which is the opposite of what documenting a powerful operation usually costs, and worth weighing against the risks this file records elsewhere. WHAT THE TEAM SAID IT STILL WANTED: TO FIGURE OUT HOW TO MAKE THESE TECHNOLOGIES SAFER, MORE ACCESSIBLE, SCALABLE AND FREE — INTENT ON INTEGRATING REPORTING SYSTEMS INTO MAINSTREAM MEDIA, LOCAL AND NATIONAL GOVERNANCE AND JUSTICE SYSTEMS, AND ENSURING THERE ARE FEEDBACK MECHANISMS TO COMMUNITIES THAT LACK EVEN BASIC PHONE NETWORK. FEEDBACK TO COMMUNITIES THAT LACK EVEN BASIC PHONE NETWORK is the honest limit stated by the builders themselves: a village with no signal can still be reported ABOUT but struggles to be told what happened next. Plan a physical route back — a printed summary carried to the meeting. WHO USES IT AND WHERE: USED EXTENSIVELY IN AFRICA AND SOUTHEAST ASIA, PARTICULARLY BY CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS BUT ALSO SOME INDIGENOUS GROUPS — AND CUSTOMISED FOR ISSUES BEYOND FORESTS, INCLUDING ENVIRONMENTAL CONSERVATION IN ONE SOUTH AMERICAN COUNTRY AND WOMEN'S HEALTH IN ONE EAST AFRICAN COUNTRY. Not a forestry tool. The same suite has been reconfigured for health reporting, which means a community can use it for evictions, pollution, water levels or violence without waiting for a purpose-built version. THE PROJECT THAT SCALED IT AND THE TRAINING BEHIND IT: A PRIZE-WINNING NATIONAL ACTIVIST USING IT TO MONITOR ILLEGAL LOGGING AND DESTRUCTIVE OIL PALM PLANTATION EXPANSION, WITH HIS WORK TO TRAIN LOCAL COMMUNITIES TO USE THE APP SUPPORTED BY A PRIZE GRANT PROGRAMME AND A NAMED FOUNDATION — THE PROJECT STILL EXPANDING TWO YEARS AFTER ITS ORIGINAL FUNDING ENDED. Still growing two years after the grant stopped, which this file has recorded as the rare exception rather than the rule. The training was the thing that lasted, not the funding. AND THE SEPARATE NATIONAL TOOL PUBLISHED ALONGSIDE IT: A FREE MOBILE APP IN ANOTHER WEST AFRICAN COUNTRY DESIGNED TO COMBAT ILLEGAL MINING, LETTING ANYONE REPORT INCIDENTS BY PROVIDING LOCATION COORDINATES, UPLOADING PHOTOS AND ADDING COMMENTS — WITH INCIDENTS STORED ON A SERVER AND VIEWABLE ON A MAP, AND AN OPTION TO REPORT ANONYMOUSLY; ITS PUBLISHED PRIVACY NOTICE STATES THAT CONTACT INFO AND IDENTIFIERS MAY BE COLLECTED AND LINKED TO YOUR IDENTITY. Recorded together deliberately, because the contrast is the lesson: a free open app that offers anonymous reporting while its own privacy notice says identifiers may be linked to you. Read the privacy notice of any reporting app before a community uses it — the promise on the download page and the disclosure in the store listing can say different things. WHO IT SUITS: community organisations documenting logging, mining, eviction or pollution who need evidence that is located, dated, encrypted and defensible — and anyone weighing which reporting app is safe to use. CAVEATS: A TOOL AND ITS MAKERS, NOT A FUNDER, A LAWYER OR AN ORGANISER; ACCESS IS BY CREDENTIAL ON REQUEST RATHER THAN OPEN DOWNLOAD, IT NEEDS SMARTPHONES AND SOME NETWORK, AND ITS BUILDERS NAME FEEDBACK TO OFF-NETWORK COMMUNITIES AS AN UNSOLVED PROBLEM. For the free guides on filming so footage stands as evidence, Gambia's entry; for training residents to monitor a mine, Sierra Leone's entry.

trackers.name: The Kitengela Wildlife Conservation Lease, Kenya — run by FoNNaP then The Wildlife Foundation, paying landowners about US$4 per acre a year to keep land unfenced and unsold; with IFAW's US$1.2m/year Kitenden lease alongside it
trackers.desc: FOUR DOLLARS AN ACRE TO KEEP IT OPEN — AND WHAT THAT BOUGHT — method and adjacency declared first: FOURTH ACQUISITION-ONLY ROUND, AND THE FIRST COVERING THE ROUTE WHERE NO LAND CHANGES HANDS. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THREE HOSTS AND SIX DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL HOSTS AND FOUR FACTS ABSENT. TWO GENERIC PHRASES MATCHED TWO ENTRIES, BOTH READ IN FULL: A SIERRA LEONEAN STATUTE PAGE, AND A KENYAN UMBRELLA MEMBERSHIP BODY WHICH MENTIONS A LEASING INCOME MODEL IN A SINGLE LINE WITHOUT ITS PRICE, CONTRACT TERMS OR OUTCOME. THIS ENTRY IS THE LEASE PROGRAMME ITSELF; NEITHER IS RESTATED AND NEITHER HOST IS SHIPPED. THIS FILE'S TANZANIA BUCKET CARRIES A VOLUNTARY LAND EASEMENT ENTRY AND ITS LESOTHO ENTRY THE CARBON ROUTE WHERE COMMUNITY LAND STAYS IN TITLE. THE PRICE AND WHAT IT BUYS, WHICH IS THE FIND: LANDOWNERS WERE PAID KSh 300 PER ACRE PER YEAR, ROUGHLY US$4, IN RETURN FOR AGREEING TO LEAVE THEIR LAND OPEN AND NOT ENGAGE IN QUARRYING, FENCING, LAND SUBDIVISION AND SALE OR POACHING — WITH THE AVERAGE ANNUAL PAYMENT AROUND US$400 TO US$800 PER HOUSEHOLD. The three acquisition rounds before this one were about getting land into community hands. This is the opposite arrangement and often the only one available: the household keeps its title and is paid not to develop. Four dollars an acre is the number to start any such negotiation from — it is what was actually paid, not what was asked. THE FOUR RESTRICTIONS, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: QUARRYING, FENCING, SUBDIVISION AND SALE, AND POACHING — THE CONTRACT NAMING SUBDIVISION AND SALE ALONGSIDE THE PHYSICAL USES. SUBDIVISION AND SALE inside the same clause as quarrying is the operative part. A payment that only stops fencing leaves the owner free to sell to a developer next year; this one buys the parcel's continuity, which is what a community trying to hold a corridor together actually needs. Copy those four words into any such agreement. THE PAYMENT TIMING: PAYMENTS ARE SCHEDULED SEVERAL TIMES PER YEAR TO COINCIDE WITH SCHOOL PAYMENT TIME — WITH PARTICIPANTS REPORTED AS SENDING THEIR CHILDREN TO SCHOOL, INCLUDING SECONDARY SCHOOL. Paid when school fees fall due. A small design choice that decides whether a household stays enrolled, because the alternative to the lease payment is selling an acre in the same week. HOW SMALL IT STARTED AND HOW FAR IT GOT: BEGUN AS A PILOT IN 2000 LEASING SEVERAL HUNDRED ACRES FROM 11 PARTICIPANTS, WITH ONE IMPLEMENTER STATING IT STARTED WITH 214 ACRES AND 2 FAMILIES — EXPANDING TO 8,545 ACRES FROM 117 FAMILIES BY LATE 2003, THEN 417 FAMILIES AND 60,000 ACRES, WITH AN EVALUATION TABLE REPORTING 61,067 ACRES BY 2012; 115 HOUSEHOLDS WERE ON A WAITING LIST. Two families to sixty thousand acres. And a waiting list is the detail worth carrying to a funder: demand from landowners outran the money, which is the opposite of the usual problem. WHO RAN IT AND WHO PAID: INITIATED BY A LOCAL CONSERVATION NGO OF PARK SUPPORTERS WITH SUPPORT FROM A US WILDLIFE TRUST, THE FIRST PHASE FUNDED BY A DEVELOPMENT BANK'S GLOBAL ENVIRONMENT FACILITY, THE SECOND IMPLEMENTED BY A NATIONAL WILDLIFE FOUNDATION — WITH THE STATE WILDLIFE SERVICE PAYING AN ANNUAL KSh 900,000, ABOUT US$13,235, AND US$64,000 OVER FIVE YEARS. A local volunteer association started it and the state and the development bank followed. The sequence matters: nobody funded the idea until a small group had proved it on 214 acres. WHO ACTUALLY HELD THE POWER, STATED PLAINLY: THE MOST IMPORTANT ACTORS ON THE GROUND WERE THE PASTORALIST LANDOWNERS, BECAUSE THEY CONTROLLED THE ACTUAL DISPERSAL LAND — THE ENTIRE PROGRAMME DEPENDED ON THEIR WILLINGNESS TO ACCEPT PAYMENTS AND MAINTAIN OPEN RANGELAND USE ON PRIVATE LAND. Worth quoting back at any conservation body arriving with a plan: the people with the title are the ones who decide, and the scheme exists at their discretion. THE MAPPING THAT MADE IT WORK, DONE WITH THE LANDOWNERS' OWN ASSOCIATION: SUCCESS DEPENDED ON SPATIAL INFORMATION ABOUT WHERE FENCES HAD BEEN PUT UP AND WHERE LAND REMAINED UNFENCED — THE MAPS DEVELOPED TOGETHER BY MEMBERS OF THE KITENGELA ILPARAKUO LANDOWNERS ASSOCIATION (KILA) AND SCIENTISTS AT ILRI, SHOWING PARCELS ALREADY ENROLLED AND THOSE ON THE WAITING LIST, AND USED TO TARGET PRIORITY AREAS AND ATTRACT MORE FUNDING. A fence map, made by the landowners with researchers, that then attracted the money. Read beside the resident drone-mapping filed under Somalia: in both cases the community's own map was the asset that unlocked everything after it. THE GAP BETWEEN WHAT WAS PAID AND WHAT WAS ASKED: A SURVEY FOUND THE AVERAGE ANNUAL COMPENSATION DEMANDED PER HOUSEHOLD WAS KSh 60,022, ROUGHLY US$920, PER ACRE — AGAINST THE KSh 300 PER ACRE ACTUALLY PAID, WITH THE RANGE OF RESPONSES SO LARGE THAT THE VALUATION METHODOLOGY WAS DEEMED QUESTIONABLE. Landowners named a figure roughly two hundred times what they were eventually paid. Recorded because it is the honest measure of what these payments are: not compensation for the land's value, but a small annual sum against the temptation to sell. A community should go in knowing that. WHAT THE PROGRAMME WAS RACING: THE FIRST GROUP RANCH WAS SUBDIVIDED IN 1986 INTO PRIVATE PARCELS AVERAGING 255 ACRES, DECLINING TO 154 ACRES MAINLY AS A RESULT OF LAND SALES. Average holdings fell by 40% through sales. Subdivision converts collective land into parcels that leave one by one, and this file has recorded the same sequence in several countries. THE OUTCOME, RECORDED WITHOUT SOFTENING: THE CORE PERIOD RAN FROM 2002 AND EXPANDED AFTER 2008 — AND OVER THE SAME DECADES WILDEBEEST IN THE ECOSYSTEM DECLINED FROM 38,000 IN 1978 TO ABOUT 10,000 BY 2012, WITH ANOTHER ACCOUNT RECORDING A FALL FROM 30,000 TO 8,000 IN TWENTY YEARS. Sixty thousand acres enrolled and the population still collapsed. Filed unsoftened because a community weighing this route deserves it: the lease held some land open, and it did not on its own reverse what was happening around it. THE LARGER LEASE ON RECORD ALONGSIDE IT: A FIVE-YEAR AGREEMENT PRESENTED TO ROUGHLY 9,000 LANDOWNERS AT AN ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING, WITH AROUND 1,600 SIGNING UP AND ANOTHER THOUSAND ON RENEWAL, SECURING 26,000 ACRES AND LATER OVER 55,000 — A US$1.2 MILLION PER YEAR AGREEMENT INCLUDING SCHOLARSHIPS, A MANAGEMENT PLAN, LIVELIHOOD PROJECTS FOR WOMEN, AND EMPLOYMENT FOR COMMUNITY GAME SCOUTS INCLUDING ONE OF THE FIRST ALL-WOMEN COMMUNITY RANGER UNITS, WITH A BANK DRIVEN INTO THE VILLAGES TO OPEN ACCOUNTS. The contrast is the lesson: the same instrument at $1.2 million a year carried scholarships, jobs and a management plan. Ask for the package, not the per-acre rate alone — and note that only 1,600 of 9,000 landowners signed initially, so a lease presented at a general meeting does not need unanimity to start. AND THE PUBLISHED WARNING ABOUT WHO BENEFITS: THE SUBDIVISION OF THESE RANGELANDS HAS TENDED TO BENEFIT ELITES, AND THIS TREND IS REINFORCED IN LAND-BASED SCHEMES SUCH AS THESE — LAND LEASES DO HOWEVER KEEP THE LANDS THEY COVER TOGETHER; BUT CONSIDERATION MUST BE GIVEN TO ADJACENT COMMUNITIES THAT MAY FACE NEGATIVE KNOCK-ON EFFECTS, AND LEASES MAY NOT OFFER AS MUCH TO LANDOWNERS IN OTHER AREAS OR BE FINANCIALLY SUSTAINABLE ACROSS VAST AREAS. Payments flow to whoever holds title, so where subdivision already favoured the well-connected, the lease pays them again. And the displaced pressure lands on the neighbouring community. Both belong in the discussion before a village signs. WHO IT SUITS: landowning communities asked to keep land open rather than sell it, and anyone negotiating a payment-for-conservation agreement who needs real prices, real contract terms and a real failure on record. CAVEATS: ONE COUNTRY AND ONE ECOSYSTEM, WITH FIGURES SPANNING 2000–2012 AND VARYING BETWEEN SOURCES — THESE ARE PRECEDENTS AND NUMBERS TO NEGOTIATE FROM, NOT AN OPEN PROGRAMME TO JOIN; PAYMENT DEPENDS ON DONOR FUNDING THAT WAS NEVER PERMANENT. For a body a village organisation can actually join, Kenya's entry; for a voluntary easement with the village keeping the land, Tanzania's entry.

trackers.name: Judiciary of The Republic of The Gambia
trackers.desc: Judiciary of The Republic of The Gambia — supreme court (Gambia).

trackers.name: The Gambia — Companies Department (Registrar of Companies, MoJ)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the Registrar of Companies (Attorney General’s Chambers & Ministry of Justice) administers the Companies Registry under the Companies Act 2013 & Single Window Business Registry Act, The Gambia. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: National Audit Office
trackers.desc: National — supreme audit institution of The Gambia. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in the Gambia.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: ECOWAS Court of Justice — file directly, but sue the State
trackers.desc: A COURT YOU CAN REACH WITHOUT EXHAUSTING DOMESTIC REMEDIES. The ECOWAS Community Court of Justice has held human rights jurisdiction since 2005 and has broad access and standing rules permitting individuals and NGOs to bypass national courts and file directly. THE PRECEDENT: in SERAP v Federal Republic of Nigeria (ECW/CCJ/APP/08/09) the Court dismissed all three preliminary objections — no locus standi, no jurisdiction, statute-barred — and rejected the government's attempt to exclude an Amnesty International report from the evidence. NGO research was admitted as evidence, which matters when no state data exists.
