THE MEASURED RESULT, WHICH IS THE NUMBER TO CARRY: A STUDY SHOWING 77% YIELD GAINS AND STRONG FINANCIAL RETURNS DESPITE EXTREMELY DRY CONDITIONS IN ONE NAMED COUNTRY — AND AN IMPACT ASSESSMENT SHOWING A CLEAR TREND: THE FURTHER A FARMER ADVANCES IN THEIR TRANSITION TO AGROECOLOGY, THE GREATER THEIR YIELDS AND INCOME. Seventy-seven percent more, in a drought year. When a ministry or a company argues that only industrial inputs can feed the district, that is a measured African figure to put against it — and the second finding matters as much: the gains rise the further the transition goes, which answers the objection that a half-converted farm underperforms. THE TREE PRACTICE AT ITS CENTRE: FOSTERING THE SPREAD OF FARMER-MANAGED NATURAL REGENERATION OF TREES AND OTHER LOCALLY ADAPTED ECOLOGICAL FARMING PRACTICES — A PROGRAMME THAT BENEFITED MORE THAN 176,000 RURAL PEOPLE IN ONE REPORTED YEAR. FARMER-MANAGED NATURAL REGENERATION is the cheapest land restoration method in this file: protecting and pruning the tree stumps already in the field rather than buying and planting seedlings. It costs labour and a rule, not money — and it is directly relevant to the tree tenure problem recorded under Somalia, because a farmer who may not own the trees has little reason to nurse them. THE METHOD IT SPREADS: FARMER EXPERIMENTATION WITH ECOLOGICAL FARMING APPROACHES, FARMER-TO-FARMER SHARING OF LOCALLY GENERATED SOLUTIONS, AND STRENGTHENING OF COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS TO LEAD — WITH FARMER FIELD SCHOOLS THAT BUILD ON EXISTING AGROECOLOGICAL EFFORTS, LETTING FARMERS EXPERIMENT AND ADAPT, WITH EFFECTIVE PRACTICES THEN SPREAD THROUGH FARMER-TO-FARMER NETWORKS. BUILD ON EXISTING EFFORTS. The school starts from what the best farmers in the village already do, which is why the results travel — and it is the opposite of a demonstration plot run by an outside agronomist. THE RADIO AND RIGHTS WORK OF ONE PARTNER: A RADIO PROGRAM PROVIDING EDUCATION ON THE DANGER OF CHEMICAL PESTICIDES, WHILE SUPPORTING STUDIES ON PEASANT RIGHTS, FARMER-MANAGED NATURAL RESOURCES, AND FOOD SECURITY AND NUTRITION — PLUS RAINWATER MANAGEMENT PROJECTS HELPING FARMERS ADAPT TO LOW AND ERRATIC RAINFALL. A national partner already running a radio programme. This file's Cape Verde entry supplies free scripts in local languages and its Chad entry the money for equipment — an existing programme is where both land. THE YOUTH PROGRAMME AND ITS CARAVAN: A YOUTH STORYTELLER PROGRAM ELEVATING THE VOICES OF WOMEN AND YOUTH FARMERS AND DEVELOPING LEADERSHIP AND MEDIA SKILLS — AND AN AGROECOLOGY YOUTH CARAVAN FOR 18 YOUTH FROM 6 WEST AFRICAN PARTNER ORGANIZATIONS IN BURKINA FASO, GHANA, MALI AND SENEGAL, TRAVELLING OVER 12 DAYS THROUGH FOUR NAMED REGIONS TO DOCUMENT REAL RURAL SUCCESS STORIES. Young people from farming villages trained to film and write, then sent across four countries to record what works. A community that can produce its own material stops depending on a journalist arriving — and this file's video-as-evidence entry under Niger is what turns that footage into something usable in a dispute. THE YOUTH BARRIER IT NAMES HONESTLY RATHER THAN GLOSSES: YOUTH STILL SEE CONVENTIONAL FARMING AS LABOR-INTENSIVE, POORLY PAID, AND LACKING DIGNITY, AND THE LACK OF JOBS IN RURAL AREAS PUSHES MANY TO LEAVE HOME — WHILE THE CAPITAL REQUIRED IS FAR ABOVE THE REACH OF MANY YOUNG MEN AND WOMEN JUST STARTING LIFE, AND OFTEN STANDS AS THE MAJOR GAP BETWEEN YOUTH AND THEIR AGRICULTURAL ENTERPRISE. A community defending its land needs young people who intend to stay on it. Naming capital as the barrier points at a specific fix — the savings groups and cooperative lending filed under Djibouti and São Tomé — rather than at exhortation. THE MARKET WORK: STRENGTHENING LOCAL MARKETS BY SUPPORTING DIRECT FARMER-TO-CONSUMER RELATIONSHIPS AND DIVERSE COMMUNITY-LED INITIATIVES SUCH AS GRAIN RESERVES, SEED BANKS, YOUTH GROUPS AND FARMER COOPERATIVE ENTERPRISES. GRAIN RESERVES AND SEED BANKS. A village that holds its own seed and its own reserve is far harder to pressure at harvest, and both are buildable without outside capital. THE POLICY POSITION IT SHARES WITH AFRICAN FARMER ORGANISATIONS: AFRICAN FARMERS' ORGANIZATIONS ARE CONCERNED THAT NEW GREEN REVOLUTION PROPOSALS WILL HAVE NEGATIVE EFFECTS IN AFRICA AND IGNORE PROVEN, VIABLE ALTERNATIVES TO ADDRESSING POVERTY — AND THESE ORGANIZATIONS ARE COMING TOGETHER TO PROMOTE MORE APPROPRIATE STRATEGIES BASED ON SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE AND STRENGTHENING OF LOCAL FOOD SYSTEMS. THE STATED ACCESSIBILITY TEST, WORTH APPLYING TO ANY PROJECT OFFERED TO YOUR VILLAGE: THESE METHODS ARE FINANCIALLY ACCESSIBLE TO SMALL SCALE FARMERS, DEPEND ON LOCAL INITIATIVE AND INNOVATION, AND ARE APPROPRIATELY ADAPTED TO LOCAL ECOSYSTEMS. Three questions to ask of any agricultural scheme arriving with a company or a ministry: can the poorest farmer here afford it, does it need us to run it, and was it designed for this soil. AND THE CONVENING CADENCE: A GLOBAL CONFERENCE GATHERING PARTNERS EVERY TWO YEARS, WITH OVER 30 PEOPLE FROM WEST AFRICA, SOUTH ASIA, THE AMERICAS AND EUROPE AT ONE NAMED EDITION. WHO IT SUITS: West African farming communities looking for the national organisation already doing this work near them, and groups wanting a measured case for agroecology to put to a ministry. CAVEATS: WEST AFRICA ONLY WITHIN AFRICA, AND IT WORKS THROUGH NATIONAL NGO PARTNERS RATHER THAN FUNDING VILLAGES DIRECTLY — the partner page is the route. For the pan-African alliance with an open WhatsApp community, Libya's entry; for the West African peasant federation, Mauritania's entry; for free radio scripts in local languages, Cape Verde's entry.

trackers.name: Fauna & Flora International — a conservation organisation whose published rule is that the local partner defines the terms of the relationship — demand-led rather than one-size-fits-all, with community and Indigenous organisations among 400+ partners and a free online capacity resource
trackers.desc: IT IS OUR PARTNERS WHO DEFINE THE TERMS OF THE RELATIONSHIP — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S ESWATINI ENTRY COVERS THE TEAM-BASED CONSERVATION LEADERSHIP LADDER THIS ORGANISATION IS ASSOCIATED WITH, ITS SEYCHELLES ENTRY THE ENVIRONMENTAL LAW CHARITY WORKING THROUGH PARTNERS, AND ITS ETHIOPIA ENTRY THE NO-PASS-OR-FAIL FUNDER. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. WHO SETS THE TERMS, WHICH IS THE FIND: WE CHOOSE OUR IN-COUNTRY PARTNERS CAREFULLY, NOT LEAST BECAUSE WE ARE COMMITTED TO WORKING WITH THEM FOR AS LONG AS IT TAKES — BUT IT IS OUR PARTNERS WHO DEFINE THE TERMS OF THE RELATIONSHIP. THIS ENSURES THAT WE GIVE THEM THE KIND OF SUPPORT THEY NEED, RATHER THAN OFFERING A STANDARD SOLUTION THAT MAY NOT FIT THE LOCAL CONTEXT. Written down, on a public page, and therefore quotable back. This file has recorded partnership after partnership in which the international organisation arrived with the workplan, the indicators and the reporting format already fixed. A community organisation entering this relationship can open by asking what it wants the terms to be — and point at the sentence if the answer drifts. THE DEMAND-LED RULE STATED SEPARATELY: WE ARE DEMAND-LED, RESPONDING TO REQUESTS FOR SUPPORT AND TAILORING OUR APPROACH ACCORDINGLY, RATHER THAN IMPOSING A ONE-SIZE-FITS-ALL SOLUTION. DEMAND-LED means you ask for what you need rather than choosing from a menu. Know what to ask for before the first meeting; that is the whole leverage the rule gives you. WHO THE PARTNERS ARE: LOCAL NGOs, COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS, INDIGENOUS PEOPLE'S ORGANISATIONS, GOVERNMENT BODIES AND SOCIAL ENTERPRISES — MORE THAN 400 PARTNERS ACROSS NEARLY 50 COUNTRIES. COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS and INDIGENOUS PEOPLE'S ORGANISATIONS named as partner types, not beneficiary types. That is the distinction this file keeps returning to. THE FORMS THE SUPPORT TAKES: STRATEGIC ADVICE; PRACTICAL TRAINING; ORGANISATIONAL DEVELOPMENT; HELP WITH FUNDRAISING OR NETWORKING — AND AT INSTITUTIONAL LEVEL, SUPPORT IN STRATEGIC PLANNING, BUILDING STRONG GOVERNANCE, FINANCE AND ADMINISTRATION STRUCTURES AND IMPROVING ACCESS TO FUNDING, WITH INTERVENTIONS FROM MENTORING AND COACHING TO TRAINING, INFORMATION SHARING AND EXCHANGES. HELP WITH FUNDRAISING is the one to request. Every funder entry in this file assumes an organisation that can write a proposal, hold an account and report on time; being taught to do that is upstream of all of them, and it is on the published list of what can be asked for. THE TWO MODES OF WORKING: FOR SOME PROJECTS OUR OWN STAFF WORK HANDS-ON, SIDE-BY-SIDE WITH OUR PARTNERS EVERY DAY; FOR OTHERS WE PROVIDE ONGOING CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT AND SUPPORT FROM AFAR — WHETHER THROUGH FUNDING, TECHNICAL EXPERTISE OR HELP WITH OPERATIONS. Ask which mode is proposed for you, and why. Staff on the ground every day is a different relationship from a quarterly call, and it changes who is really running the work. THE STATED END GOAL: OUR END GOAL IS FOR PARTNERS TO BE ENTIRELY SELF-SUFFICIENT IN TACKLING THE THREATS TO NATURE THAT THEY FACE LOCALLY — AND WE ARE COMMITTED TO DOING WHATEVER WE CAN, FOR AS LONG AS IS NEEDED. An exit written as the objective rather than a risk. Ask what self-sufficiency would look like in this partnership and how it would be measured; an organisation that cannot answer has not really adopted its own goal. THE OBJECTIVE OF THE CAPACITY WORK: WHETHER FORMAL OR INFORMAL, OUR OVERALL OBJECTIVE IS TO STRENGTHEN ORGANISATIONS TO MAKE THEM BETTER ABLE TO SUSTAIN THEIR CONSERVATION ACTIVITIES INDEPENDENTLY AND TO MEET THEIR OWN CONTINUED DEVELOPMENT AND RESOURCE NEEDS. THE PEER NETWORK SHIFT: TRADITIONALLY EVERY LOCAL PARTNER HAS BENEFITED FROM ONE-TO-ONE SUPPORT GEARED TO ITS OWN NEEDS, BUT MANY OF THESE ORGANISATIONS OFTEN ENCOUNTER THE SAME GENERIC PROBLEMS — THEREFORE WE ARE INCREASINGLY ENCOURAGING OUR PARTNERS AROUND THE WORLD TO DEVELOP THEIR OWN PEER SUPPORT NETWORKS. Partners talking to each other instead of only to the funder. That is how a partner learns what terms others negotiated — and it is being actively encouraged rather than discouraged, which is not always the case in this file. THE FREE ONLINE RESOURCE IT CO-BUILT: ONE OBVIOUS WAY TO ACHIEVE MAXIMUM REACH FOR MINIMUM COST IS TO PROVIDE ACCESS TO ONLINE SUPPORT RESOURCES — SO IT JOINED FORCES WITH OTHER MEMBERS OF A NAMED CAMBRIDGE INITIATIVE TO DEVELOP AND LAUNCH A CAPACITY-FOR-CONSERVATION SITE, ALONGSIDE A ONE-STOP COLLECTION OF DOCUMENTS AND RESOURCES FOR CONSERVATION PARTNERS. Free organisational-development material for conservation organisations, usable without any partnership at all. That is the part of this entry a group can act on today. THE PROBLEM IT NAMES: THE ABILITY OF LOCAL INSTITUTIONS AND INDIVIDUALS TO ADDRESS CONSERVATION CHALLENGES — PARTICULARLY IN SOME OF THE WORLD'S MOST BIOLOGICALLY RICH AREAS — IS OFTEN CONSTRAINED BY A LACK OF EXPERIENCE OR LIMITED ACCESS TO THE NECESSARY RESOURCES, FINANCIAL OR OTHERWISE. THE BELIEF UNDERLYING IT: THOSE LIVING CLOSEST TO NATURE HAVE THE BEST KNOWLEDGE AND EXPERIENCE OF THEIR LOCAL ENVIRONMENT AND SHOULD BE AT THE HEART OF ALL CONSERVATION STRATEGIES AND ACTIONS — AND IT PIONEERED THE CAPACITY-BUILDING CONCEPT, IN ESSENCE PUTTING CONSERVATION IN LOCAL HANDS. PARTNERSHIP IS A TWO-WAY STREET: BOTH SIDES BRING COMPLEMENTARY SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE, AND LEARN FROM EACH OTHER. AND THE FUNDING CHANNEL, WITH THE CAUTION RECORDED ALONGSIDE IT: ITS LONG HISTORY WITH ON-THE-GROUND PARTNERS MAKES IT WELL PLACED TO CHANNEL FUNDING DIRECTLY TO PROJECTS AND PARTNERS IN PRIORITY CONSERVATION AREAS, WITH TRUST AND FOUNDATION COMMITMENTS RANGING FROM £100 TO £5 MILLION A YEAR — WHILE COMMENTARY NOTES THAT CLIMATE FINANCE, CARBON MARKETS, NATURE-BASED SOLUTIONS AND BIODIVERSITY CREDITS BRING NEW MONEY AND NEW ACTORS INTO CONSERVATION, WHICH CAN ALSO CREATE NEW RISKS IF LAND RIGHTS ARE UNCLEAR OR BENEFITS ARE NOT FAIRLY SHARED. An intermediary channelling foundation money to local partners is useful and is also the arrangement the fund filed under Sudan disqualifies outright. Both positions are defensible; what matters is knowing which one you are in, and asking what share arrives and on what terms. And the caution about carbon and biodiversity credits is the same warning this file records under Comoros — unclear land rights are what turn new money into new dispossession. WHO IT SUITS: African community, Indigenous and national conservation organisations wanting organisational strengthening on their own terms — and anyone who can use the free capacity site without a partnership. CAVEATS: A PARTNERSHIP ORGANISATION THAT CHOOSES ITS PARTNERS RATHER THAN RUNNING OPEN CALLS, AND IT IS NOT A GRANT PROGRAMME YOU APPLY TO — the free online resources are the open door. For unrestricted money with no pass-or-fail screen, Ethiopia's entry; for the team-based conservation ladder, Eswatini's entry; for the carbon-project cautions in full, Comoros' entry.

trackers.name: EWT (Endangered Wildlife Trust) — a 12-country African conservation organisation that works with landowners and communities on protected area expansion and catchment protection — with free public tools for environmental impact assessments and a published position on poorly-planned infrastructure
trackers.desc: FREE EIA TOOLS, AND A PUBLISHED LINE ON BADLY PLANNED INFRASTRUCTURE — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S SEYCHELLES ENTRY COVERS THE TAX DEDUCTION, ITS SÃO TOMÉ ENTRY THE SERVITUDE TRUST, ITS ESWATINI ENTRY THE CAPITAL FUND, ITS CHAD ENTRY THE TRUST-FUND LIBRARY, ITS SOUTH SUDAN ENTRY THE LAND BUYER; ITS SOUTH AFRICA BUCKET MENTIONS THIS TRUST IN PASSING WITHOUT DESCRIBING IT. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. THE INFRASTRUCTURE POSITION, WHICH IS THE FIND: WHILE AFRICA IS UNDERGOING A NECESSARY DEVELOPMENT TRAJECTORY, POORLY-PLANNED INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS CAN HAVE DISASTROUS IMPACTS ON BIODIVERSITY, THE ECOSYSTEM SERVICES ON WHICH MANY PEOPLE RELY, AND THE ECONOMIC SUSTAINABILITY OF THE PROJECTS THEMSELVES. THE ECONOMIC SUSTAINABILITY OF THE PROJECTS THEMSELVES is the phrase to borrow. A community arguing that a road, dam or line is bad for nature is easily dismissed as anti-development; the same community arguing that the project will not pay for itself is speaking the language the finance ministry uses, and here is a mainstream conservation organisation making that argument in public. THE FREE TOOLS, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: A COLLECTION OF WILDLIFE AND HABITAT CONSERVATION TOOLS AND RESOURCES FOR ANYTHING FROM SCHOOL PROJECTS TO ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT ASSESSMENTS — WITH THE ORGANISATION GIVING THE PUBLIC ACCESS TO ITS PERSPECTIVE ON TOPICAL CONSERVATION SUBJECTS. Tools pitched at people doing an EIA, published for anyone. The assessment is the document that decides most projects in this file, and communities almost never have the technical material to contest one — which is what makes a free, public toolset for that specific document worth more than another campaign guide. THE ASSESSMENT DATA IT PUBLISHES: A MAMMAL RED LIST PROVIDING AN UP-TO-DATE ASSESSMENT OF THE CONSERVATION STATUS OF THE MAMMALS OF THREE NAMED SOUTHERN AFRICAN COUNTRIES, OF WHICH 57 — 17% — ARE DEEMED THREATENED WITH EXTINCTION AND 34 — 10% — NEAR THREATENED. A national red list is citable evidence that a particular animal on your land is threatened. That is the fact an impact assessment must address and the one a community can check for itself before the consultants arrive. HOW IT PICKS WHERE TO WORK, AND THE DATA LAYERS IT USES: NINE PRIORITY LANDSCAPES ACROSS EAST AND SOUTHERN AFRICA IDENTIFIED THROUGH DATASETS COVERING THREATENED SPECIES, AT-RISK ECOSYSTEMS AND LANDSCAPE-LEVEL FEATURES — INCLUDING KEY BIODIVERSITY AREAS, STRATEGIC WATER SOURCE AREAS, A NATIONAL PROTECTED AREA EXPANSION STRATEGY, PROVINCIAL CRITICAL BIODIVERSITY AREAS, PROTECTED AREAS AND TRANSFRONTIER CONSERVATION AREAS. Those layers are public datasets, and each is a status your land might already hold without anyone telling you. Land inside a Key Biodiversity Area, a Strategic Water Source Area or a provincial Critical Biodiversity Area carries planning weight — check your parcel against them before the objection is written. WHAT IT COMMITS TO DO IN THEM: CREATE AND SECURE SAFE SPACES FOR THREATENED SPECIES, FACILITATE CLIMATE CHANGE ADAPTATION, EXPAND PROTECTED AREA CORRIDORS, REDUCE HUMAN-WILDLIFE CONFLICT AND IMPROVE THE WELL-BEING AND ECOLOGICAL RESILIENCE OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES. WHO IT SAYS IT WORKS WITH: GOVERNMENTS, LANDOWNERS, AND INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES — ENABLING THOSE COMMUNITIES TO THRIVE THROUGH NATURE-BASED SOLUTIONS THAT CONNECT CONSERVATION WITH HUMAN WELL-BEING, EQUITY, AND SUSTAINABLE LIVELIHOODS. THE FRESHWATER PRIORITY: IT PRIORITISES THE SAFEGUARDING OF CRITICAL FRESHWATER SYSTEMS AND CATCHMENTS ACROSS AFRICA'S THREATENED LANDSCAPES. Catchments rather than reserves. A community whose spring or river is the thing at risk has a named priority to point at. THE SECTORS IT DELIBERATELY WORKS INSIDE: IT EMBEDS CONSERVATION PRINCIPLES ACROSS SECTORS, FROM AGRICULTURE AND MINING TO URBAN PLANNING AND EDUCATION — ADDRESSING THE ROOT CAUSES OF BIODIVERSITY LOSS INCLUDING HABITAT DESTRUCTION AND UNSUSTAINABLE LAND USE. THE CORPORATE NETWORK IT RUNS: A NATIONAL BIODIVERSITY AND BUSINESS NETWORK THAT BUILDS CORPORATE CAPACITY TO MAINSTREAM BIODIVERSITY INTO BUSINESS OPERATIONS BY MEASURING BIODIVERSITY FOOTPRINT AND PROACTIVELY MITIGATING IMPACTS — ALONGSIDE A BIODIVERSITY DISCLOSURE PROJECT, A BIODIVERSITY MEASUREMENT PROTOCOL AND A MAINSTREAMING BIODIVERSITY INTO BUSINESS TOOLKIT. A DISCLOSURE PROJECT and a MEASUREMENT PROTOCOL cut two ways: the company on your land may already be a member and may already have published a biodiversity footprint. Its own disclosure is the cheapest evidence available against it, and this is where to look for it. THE SPECIFIC LAND ACTIONS IT LISTS: PROTECTED AREA EXPANSION, CATCHMENT MANAGEMENT, SPRING SOURCE PROTECTION, FODDER PRODUCTION, IMPROVED LAND MANAGEMENT PRACTICES, BETTER LIVESTOCK MANAGEMENT AND THE CONSERVATION OF STRATEGIC WATER SOURCE AREAS — AND, IN ONE DRYLAND PROGRAMME, WORKING WITH LANDOWNERS TO CHAMPION THE CONSERVATION AND IMPROVED MANAGEMENT OF THAT LANDSCAPE. SPRING SOURCE PROTECTION and FODDER PRODUCTION are the practical, small things a pastoralist or farming community actually needs, sitting in the same list as protected area expansion. THE SIZE AND REACH: FOUNDED IN 1973, OVER 80 PROJECTS ACROSS 12 CONSERVATION PROGRAMMES, MORE THAN 100 STAFF, SERVING 12 COUNTRIES IN SOUTHERN AND EAST AFRICA — WITH FIELD STAFF DEPLOYED THROUGHOUT THE REGION, AND A NICHE DESCRIBED AS CONSERVATION ACTION THROUGH APPLIED FIELD-WORK, RESEARCH AND DIRECT ENGAGEMENT WITH STAKEHOLDERS. Field staff already in twelve countries. Unlike most organisations in this file, there may be someone from it working near you already. AND THE COMMUNITY WORK ON RECORD, WITH ITS NUMBERS: IN ONE NAMED MOUNTAIN LANDSCAPE WHERE COMMUNAL FARMS FACE UNSUSTAINABLE HIGH-INPUT FARMING METHODS ERODING SOILS, LOWERING YIELDS AND FRAGMENTING HABITAT — WITH WEAK ACCESS TO RELIABLE MARKETS KEEPING PROFITS MARGINAL AND LEAVING LANDHOLDERS LITTLE INCENTIVE TO FAVOUR CONSERVATION OVER SHORT-TERM SURVIVAL — MORE THAN 200 INDIVIDUALS ARE DIRECTLY INVOLVED, FROM COMMUNITY-LED FARMING COOPERATIVES TO TRAINING PROGRAMMES FOR UNEMPLOYED GRADUATES. LITTLE INCENTIVE TO FAVOUR CONSERVATION OVER SHORT-TERM SURVIVAL, named plainly by a conservation organisation. The answer offered is market access and skills rather than a lecture, which is the only version of this that has ever held. WHO IT SUITS: communal farms, landowners and community organisations in southern and East Africa wanting protected area expansion, catchment or spring protection — and anyone contesting an impact assessment. CAVEATS: RECORDED SO YOU KNOW BEFORE PARTNERING — THIS ORGANISATION HAS A PUBLISHED POSITION SUPPORTING TROPHY HUNTING OF ELEPHANTS, BIG CATS AND OTHER WILDLIFE, WHICH SOME COMMUNITIES AND ALLIES WILL NOT ACCEPT; IT ALSO WORKS CLOSELY WITH BUSINESS, INCLUDING MINING. IT IS A CONSERVATION IMPLEMENTER, NOT A FUNDER OR A LAW FIRM. For the tax deduction that pays landowners annually, Seychelles' entry; for binding protection to the title deed, São Tomé's entry.

trackers.name: The Gaia Foundation's Earth Jurisprudence training — a three-year course that trains African practitioners to go home and revive customary ecological governance — graduates now working with communities in seven named countries, using eco-cultural maps and calendars communities draw themselves
trackers.desc: THEY TRAIN AFRICANS FOR THREE YEARS TO GO HOME AND REVIVE CUSTOMARY LAW — method and adjacency declared first: AFTER A WITHDRAWN DUPLICATE LAST ROUND, THE PRE-WRITE CHECK NOW RUNS THE SHIPPED HOST, THE SUBJECT NAME AND SIX DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS THE FULL NAME AND DESCRIPTION TEXT OF ALL 53 BUCKETS. THE HOST AND FOUR FACTS ARE ABSENT; TWO FACTS MATCHED FOUR ENTRIES, ALL READ IN FULL BEFORE WRITING AND ALL DIFFERENT SUBJECTS — A NATURAL HISTORY SOCIETY AND A COMMUNITY RADIO STATION UNDER UGANDA, AN ELDERS' FORUM UNDER ETHIOPIA, AND A GLOBAL COMMUNITY-TERRITORY REGISTRY UNDER MOROCCO. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. WHO THE PRACTITIONERS ARE AND WHERE THEY WORK, WHICH IS THE FIND: A NETWORK OF EARTH JURISPRUDENCE PRACTITIONERS ACCOMPANYING TRADITIONAL AND INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES IN THE REVIVAL AND ENHANCEMENT OF THEIR EARTH-CENTRED CUSTOMARY GOVERNANCE SYSTEMS — IN KENYA, UGANDA, BENIN, SOUTH AFRICA, ZIMBABWE, ETHIOPIA AND CAMEROON, WITH GRADUATES EACH WORKING WITH COMMUNITIES IN THEIR OWN HOME COUNTRIES. Africans trained and then working at home, rather than foreign staff placed in country. This file has recorded the difference that makes to what has to be explained and what is believed; here it is the design of the programme rather than a happy accident. THE TRAINING ITSELF: A THREE-YEAR COURSE, THE FIRST OF ITS KIND, BLENDING WILDERNESS EXPERIENCE AND WRITTEN ASSIGNMENTS, AFRICAN AND WESTERN PHILOSOPHICAL AND LEGAL TRADITIONS, ANALYSIS OF THE IMPACTS OF THE INDUSTRIAL GROWTH ECONOMY, ADVOCACY STRATEGIES AND PRACTICES FOR REVIVING INDIGENOUS KNOWLEDGE SYSTEMS — INCLUDING A DEEP-DIVE INTO PRE-COLONIAL CUSTOMARY GOVERNANCE SYSTEMS IN WHICH THE RIGHTS OF NATURE ARE EMBEDDED. Three years is a serious commitment and the honest thing to weigh: this is not a workshop. What comes out the other end is a person who can argue customary governance in both African and Western legal registers, which is exactly the gap this file has recorded when a community's own law meets a state court. THE TALKING TOOLS, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: THROUGH SIMPLE YET POWERFUL TALKING TOOLS SUCH AS ECO-CULTURAL MAPS AND CALENDARS, COMMUNITIES CAN REBUILD CONFIDENCE AND COHESION, AND DETERMINE THEIR OWN PATHS INTO THE FUTURE — WITH AN ECO-CULTURAL MAPPING WORKSHOP ORGANISED BY COMMUNITIES IN A NAMED SOUTH AFRICAN AREA FACILITATING THE REVIVAL OF TRADITIONAL KNOWLEDGE, PRACTICES AND CUSTOMARY LAWS. A map and a calendar drawn by the community itself, requiring no equipment and no outside surveyor. The map records what is where and who is responsible for it; the calendar records when things happen. Together they are the documentary record a community needs and the process that rebuilds agreement about it — and the workshop was ORGANISED BY COMMUNITIES, not for them. WHERE THE KNOWLEDGE COMES FROM: DIALOGUES WITH KNOWLEDGEABLE ELDERS — BOTH MEN AND WOMEN — AND SACRED SITES CUSTODIANS; DIALOGUES ARE TRANSFORMATIVE, RE-OPENING INTER-GENERATIONAL EXCHANGES WHERE RELATIONSHIPS WERE FRACTURING, AND ENABLING THE REVIVAL OF INDIGENOUS SEED VARIETIES THOUGHT TO BE LOST. BOTH MEN AND WOMEN, stated deliberately. This file has recorded custom being invoked to exclude women from land decisions; a method that treats women elders as knowledge holders cuts against that from inside the tradition rather than against it. THE LEGAL OBJECTIVE IT PURSUES: HELPING TO SECURE LEGAL RECOGNITION OF CUSTOMARY LAWS WHICH ARE DERIVED FROM THE LAWS OF THE EARTH AND PROTECT CRITICAL THREATENED ECOSYSTEMS AND SACRED NATURAL SITES AND TERRITORIES. LEGAL RECOGNITION is the destination, not just cultural revival. A customary law a court will apply is a defence against a concession; one that exists only in memory is not. THE POSITION IT TAKES AGAINST TOP-DOWN CONSERVATION: RATHER THAN RELYING ON TOP-DOWN, CONSERVATIONIST INTERVENTIONS TO PROTECT AFRICAN ECOSYSTEMS, THIS WORK ENABLES COMMUNITIES TO TAKE THE LEAD IN REVIVING AND ENHANCING THEIR DEEP ECOLOGICAL KNOWLEDGE, PRACTICES AND GOVERNANCE SYSTEMS. THE ARGUMENT ITS AFRICAN DIRECTOR MAKES: THE CONTINENT HAS A RICH CULTURAL HERITAGE OF ECOLOGICALLY ROOTED TRADITIONS THAT IT NEEDS TO DRAW ON TO FORGE A VIABLE FUTURE AND DEAL WITH CLIMATE CHANGE AND THE SCRAMBLE FOR LAND — TRADITIONAL AFRICAN CUSTOMARY LAWS AND GOVERNANCE SYSTEMS ARE FOUNDED IN EARTH JURISPRUDENCE, AND AFRICA'S HERITAGE IS HER FUTURE. THE SCRAMBLE FOR LAND named as the thing this answers. The claim is that the governance system already exists and needs reviving rather than inventing, which is a cheaper and faster proposition than building an institution from nothing. WHAT PRACTITIONERS DO ON RETURNING: BRINGING BACK INDIGENOUS SEED DIVERSITY, PROTECTING SACRED NATURAL SITES, RESTORING ASSOCIATED RITUALS, RE-ESTABLISHING FOOD SOVEREIGNTY, AND STRENGTHENING ECOLOGICAL GOVERNANCE SYSTEMS — INCLUDING AGROECOLOGICAL FARMING PRACTICES. Read beside the seed banks filed under Chad: the same recovery of lost varieties, approached through custodians and ritual rather than through a store and a register. Two routes to the same result, and a community can run both. THE EXCHANGE THAT STARTED IT: EXCHANGE VISITS TO THE COLOMBIAN AMAZON ENABLED AFRICAN CIVIL SOCIETY LEADERS TO LEARN HOW INDIGENOUS PEOPLE HAD REVIVED THEIR TRADITIONAL ECOLOGICAL KNOWLEDGE AND SECURED LEGAL RECOGNITION OF THEIR CUSTOMARY GOVERNANCE SYSTEMS OF SACRED TERRITORIES — WHICH INSPIRED THE FORMATION OF LOCAL AND COMMUNITY-LED ORGANISATIONS ACROSS AFRICA. The whole African movement began with African leaders travelling to see something already working elsewhere. That is the travel-grant argument recorded in this file's Burundi entry, with a measurable result attached. THE DOCUMENTS THAT CAME OUT OF IT: A SET OF NAMED PRINCIPLES OF EARTH JURISPRUDENCE AGREED IN ONE SOUTHERN AFRICAN COUNTRY AND A FILM; A CUSTODIAN MEETING IN ANOTHER COUNTRY LEADING TO A CUSTODIAN STATEMENT WITH RECOMMENDATIONS — WITH TRAININGS IN THREE NAMED AFRICAN COUNTRIES ON APPLYING THE HOLISTIC METHODOLOGY FOR REVIVING INDIGENOUS KNOWLEDGE SYSTEMS, SACRED NATURAL SITES AND CUSTOMARY GOVERNANCE. A custodians' statement is a document produced by the people who hold the sites, in their own terms. Worth having before any negotiation, because it fixes what the community says its own law is before anyone else characterises it. THE RECOGNITION IT HAS ATTRACTED: FROM UNITED NATIONS HARMONY WITH NATURE DIALOGUES TO A GLOBAL CONSERVATION UNION AND THE AFRICAN COMMISSION FOR HUMAN AND PEOPLES' RIGHTS, AS WELL AS A GROWING NUMBER OF PRECEDENTS RECOGNISING EARTH-CENTRED CUSTOMARY GOVERNANCE SYSTEMS AND THE RIGHTS OF NATURE — WITH ONE COUNTRY BECOMING THE FIRST IN THE WORLD TO RECOGNIZE LEGALLY ENFORCEABLE RIGHTS OF NATURE IN ITS CONSTITUTION. The African Commission is on that list, which matters: it is the body this file's Eritrea entry records taking communications from communities without lawyers or accreditation, and it has engaged with this framework. AND THE COLLECTIVE THAT NOW CARRIES IT: AN AFRICAN EARTH JURISPRUDENCE COLLECTIVE MADE UP OF DEDICATED PRACTITIONERS FROM ACROSS EAST, WEST, CENTRAL AND SOUTHERN AFRICA, WHO TOGETHER ACCOMPANY LOCAL AND INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES TO PUT INTO PRACTICE AFRICAN ALTERNATIVES TO THE DESTRUCTIVE INDUSTRIAL DEVELOPMENT MODEL. The graduates now form their own continental collective. Ask for the practitioner in your region rather than writing to the founding organisation — that is the person who will arrive speaking the language. WHO IT SUITS: communities with sacred sites, customary governance or lost seed varieties they want revived and legally recognised — and African civil society leaders willing to commit to a long training. CAVEATS: A TRAINING AND ACCOMPANIMENT ORGANISATION, NOT A FUNDER, A LAW FIRM OR A LAND-PURCHASE BODY; THE COURSE RUNS THREE YEARS AND PRACTITIONERS ARE CONCENTRATED IN SEVEN NAMED COUNTRIES; AND ITS FRAME IS CUSTOMARY AND SPIRITUAL GOVERNANCE, WHICH WILL NOT FIT EVERY COMMUNITY. For community seed banks built without any of this, Chad's entry; for the continental complaints body that takes communications without a lawyer, Eritrea's entry.

trackers.name: The Zambia Homeless and Poor People's Federation with PPHPZ (People's Process on Housing and Poverty in Zambia) — active in 44 towns, bought the land and built 55 houses from members' own daily savings and labour; join by being poor and resident
trackers.desc: THEY BOUGHT THE LAND WITH THEIR OWN SAVINGS AND BUILT IT THEMSELVES — method and adjacency declared first: SIXTH ACQUISITION-ONLY ROUND. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THREE HOSTS AND SIX DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL HOSTS AND FIVE FACTS ABSENT, WITH ONE GENERIC PHRASE MATCHING A DIFFERENT NATIONAL FEDERATION UNDER NAMIBIA ON ITS OWN HOST. THIS FILE'S SOMALIA ENTRY COVERS THE FRANCOPHONE RESIDENTS' FUND, ITS TUNISIA ENTRY THE BORROWER-OWNED CO-OPERATIVE UNION, ITS SOUTH AFRICA BUCKET THE GLOBAL SLUM DWELLERS' NETWORK. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. WHO BOUGHT THE LAND, WHICH IS THE FIND: THE ACQUIRING OF LAND AND CONSTRUCTION WAS SPEARHEADED BY THE NATIONAL HOMELESS AND POOR PEOPLE'S FEDERATION, WHO PROVIDED SWEAT EQUITY AND CONTRIBUTED THEIR SAVINGS TOWARDS THE CONSTRUCTION OF THE HOUSES — WITH 55 HOUSES COMPLETED IN 2022 AND DELIVERED TO THE INTENDED BENEFICIARIES. Five acquisition rounds so far have found funds that grant, lenders that lend, and schemes that pay communities to hold land they cannot own. This is the version where the members bought it. Land acquired from daily savings by people living in slums, and built with their own labour — no funder in the transaction at all. THE MEMBERSHIP RULE, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: PEOPLE SAVE SMALL AMOUNTS ON A DAILY BASIS, MEMBERSHIP TO THE SAVING SCHEMES IS VOLUNTARY, AND THE ONLY QUALIFYING CRITERIA IS THAT ONE MUST BE POOR AND RESIDENT. Poor and resident. No registration, no collateral, no minimum deposit, no vetting — the shortest eligibility test recorded anywhere in this file, and the reason the model spreads. Daily saving rather than monthly is the other half: it matches how income actually arrives for a trader or a casual labourer. THE REACH: THE FEDERATION IS ACTIVE IN 44 CITIES AND TOWNS ACROSS THE COUNTRY — THE SUPPORT NGO WORKING WITH PARTNER ORGANIZATIONS, GRASSROOTS-LED MOVEMENTS AND INFORMAL SETTLEMENT NETWORKS IN RURAL AND URBAN POOR COMMUNITIES IN ALL TEN PROVINCES. HOW IT STARTED, WHICH IS WORTH COPYING: WITH SUPPORT FROM THE FEDERATION OF A NEIGHBOURING COUNTRY, THE NATIONAL FEDERATION WAS FIRST STARTED IN A RESORT TOWN — THE SUPPORT NGO ITSELF ESTABLISHED IN 2005 THROUGH THE SUPPORT OF AN INTERNATIONAL SLUM DWELLERS BODY. A federation in one country started the federation in the next, beginning in a single town. That is the propagation route: not a programme launched nationally, but organisers from across the border showing one settlement how it works. WHAT THE SUPPORT NGO SAYS ITS OWN ROLE IS: TO CAPACITATE GRASSROOTS THROUGH THE FEDERATION WITH SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE AND TECHNICAL SUPPORT, AND TO MOBILIZE RESOURCES AND LINK THE FEDERATION TO GOVERNMENT AND OTHER ORGANIZATIONS SO THAT POOR PEOPLE ARE PLACED AT THE CENTRE OF DEVELOPMENT. The NGO raises the money and makes the introductions; the federation decides and builds. That division is the thing to insist on when a support organisation offers to help — ask which of the two roles it intends to occupy. WHAT THE FEDERATION IS FOR, IN ITS OWN TERMS: A GRASSROOTS MOVEMENT OF PEOPLE LIVING IN SLUMS AGGLOMERATED IN HOUSING SAVINGS SCHEMES IN ORDER TO COLLECTIVELY ADDRESS ACCESS TO LAND, HOUSING, SECURITY OF TENURE, WATER, SANITATION AND LIVELIHOODS THROUGH SELF-HELP MECHANISMS. SECURITY OF TENURE listed alongside water and sanitation as a thing savings can buy. Most savings groups in this file fund livelihoods; this one is explicitly aimed at the land. THE RESULT OF THE PARTNERSHIP WITH THE STATE: THE FEDERATION HAS CREATED COLLABORATIVE PARTNERSHIPS WITH THE GOVERNMENT RESULTING IN THE RECEIPT OF TECHNICAL SUPPORT ON HOUSING AND INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT. Technical support rather than cash, which is what a government that will not fund you can still be asked for — the same shape as the municipal land contribution recorded in this file's Tunisia entry. THE ACCOUNTABILITY AIM: TO CAPACITATE MARGINALIZED RURAL AND URBAN SLUM DWELLERS TO WORK TOGETHER IN NETWORKS AND MOVEMENTS TO ENSURE THAT THE POOR ARE ABLE TO HOLD TO ACCOUNT THEIR CIVIC LEADERS BOTH AT LOCAL AND NATIONAL LEVEL. THE TEACHING METHOD AND THE CLAIM BEHIND IT: LEARNING IS ROOTED AT THE COMMUNITY, IN PARTICULAR THROUGH COMMUNITY-TO-COMMUNITY EXCHANGE — EXCHANGES LEADING TO A NEW SET OF PEOPLE LEARNING NEW SKILLS, BECAUSE IN OTHER ORGANISATIONS SUCH KNOWLEDGE IS OFTEN RESTRICTED TO EDUCATED PROFESSIONALS, IT BEING WRONGLY ASSUMED THAT THE QUALITIES OF GOOD TEACHING ARE LINKED TO FORMAL EDUCATION. Stated bluntly, and it is the operating principle behind the whole model: the people who did it teach the people who have not. A settlement wanting to start should ask for an exchange visit rather than a training. THE HOUSING FINDING IT ARGUES FROM: THE HOUSING POLICY INDICATES THAT AROUND 40% OF CONSTRUCTED HOUSES ARE SUBSTANDARD, FURTHER WORSENING THE VULNERABILITY OF THE URBAN POOR AS POVERTY FORCES THEM TO BUILD STRUCTURES THAT REDUCE THEIR ADAPTIVE CAPACITIES. The government's own policy document supplies the figure. Quoting the state back to itself is cheaper than commissioning research. THE POSITION IT TAKES ON EXTERNAL SCHEMES: THERE IS A CONCERNING TREND OF FALSE CLIMATE SOLUTIONS THAT DO NOT EFFECTIVELY ADDRESS GRASSROOTS ADAPTIVE CAPACITIES — AND CLIMATE ACTION SHOULD BE LOCALLY SHAPED AND LOCALLY OWNED, TAILORED TO THEIR REAL NEEDS AT THE COMMUNITY LEVEL. Worth reading beside the carbon revenue figures filed under Morocco and the criticism under Lesotho: a federation of the intended beneficiaries saying plainly that much of what arrives labelled as climate finance does not reach them. AND THE PRIORITY GAP IT NAMES, PLUS ITS PUBLISHED CONTACT: URBAN POVERTY IS ON THE INCREASE HOWEVER VERY LITTLE HAS BEEN DONE TO ALLEVIATE IT, GOVERNMENT'S DEVELOPMENT PRIORITIES HAVING BEEN TO ADDRESS RURAL POVERTY AND LANDLESSNESS — WITH A PUBLISHED CONTACT EMAIL AND MEMBERSHIP OF AN INTERNATIONAL NETWORK THAT ENABLES THE ALLIANCE TO SHARE AND LEARN FROM OTHER LIKE-MINDED INSTITUTIONS. WHO IT SUITS: settlement residents who want to acquire land collectively without waiting for a funder, and organisers looking for the shortest membership rule and the exchange-visit method that spread this model across borders. CAVEATS: ONE COUNTRY'S FEDERATION, THOUGH THE MODEL IS DELIBERATELY PROPAGATED BETWEEN COUNTRIES; SAVINGS-BASED ACQUISITION IS SLOW AND THE DOCUMENTED BUILD IS 55 HOUSES, SO THIS IS A ROUTE FOR A SETTLEMENT PREPARED TO WORK OVER YEARS RATHER THAN AN ANSWER TO AN IMMINENT EVICTION; THE SUPPORT NGO ORGANISES AND FUNDRAISES RATHER THAN LITIGATING. For a fund whose borrowers set its terms, Somalia's entry; for a lender owned by its borrowers, Tunisia's entry.

trackers.name: ADN — Associació per a la Defensa de la Natura (Andorra)
trackers.desc: Andorra's nature-defence association, founded in 1986, working on conservation, research and public information across the whole country. WHO TO ENLIST when a development touches a valley, a river or a protected area — its record is the reason to: it made the first proposal to protect the Madriu valley in 1997, a valley now inscribed as World Heritage, and it still publishes the documents from that campaign. You CAN: use its Denúncies channel to report an environmental breach, and draw on its practice of naming areas that ought to be protected and pressing for their designation, which is the lever in a country with little formal land-protection machinery. It also runs river monitoring through Projecte Rius, so it can supply baseline water data. For activists: this is a volunteer scientific association, not a law firm — expect evidence, designation proposals and a public voice rather than representation.

trackers.name: Andorra business registry (company register)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (official company register); Andorra business registry (company register) — the official register of companies and legal entities in Andorra — the primary public record of corporate existence, ownership, directors and filings. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM A BENEFICIAL-OWNERSHIP REGISTER: this shows the registered entity, its directors and filings; where a separate beneficial-ownership register exists, use that to reach the real humans behind a shell company.

trackers.name: Andorra — Ministeri de Finances
trackers.desc: National budget authority; the Department of Budget & Patrimony prepares the State budget and manages budget execution, Andorra. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Andorra.

trackers.name: Andorra — Registre de Societats
trackers.desc: National company registry; the official corporate register recording all legal entities (name, legal form, registration number, directors, share capital & status) in the Principality of Andorra. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Tribunal de Comptes
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Andorra, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Biodiversity subsidy — individuals may apply, and it is undersubscribed
trackers.desc: A GRANT WITH ALMOST NO COMPETITION — the opposite of the position almost everywhere else in this map. The Subvenció a favor de la biodiversitat i del paisatge is an annual call run by Medi Ambient, and the Government extended the 2026 deadline to 31 July 2026 after finding that as at 16 June only one application had been formalised in each of the two calls, despite several expressions of interest — the extension's stated purpose being to favour greater participation. WHO MAY APPLY: any natural person with capacity to act and an administrative identification number (NIA), and any entity with its own legal personality and a NIA acting through a representative holding the electronic certificate for representatives of legal persons. Recorded beneficiaries include public and private entities, particulars, non-profit associations and holders of agricultural, livestock and beekeeping operations. ASSEMBLE THE PAPERWORK BEFORE DRAFTING: the bases de la convocatòria duly signed; a declaration (annex 1) that you are not a debtor of the Administration; a responsible declaration (annex 2) on capacity to contract with the public sector; and a bank domiciliation authorisation (form H1T003). A SECOND CALL RUNS IN PARALLEL: subsidies to prevent damage caused by protected fauna in agricultural, livestock and beekeeping operations — where protected species are the source of local opposition, that is the fund which answers it. What has been funded shows the range accepted: educational fishing courses, and the Federació Andorrana de Caça i Pesca's perdiu xerra breeding centre using radiotelemetry to track survival of released birds — so a hunting and fishing federation and a commercial guide are both among the funded; this is not restricted to conservation NGOs. Apply via the seu electrònica at e-tramits.ad.

trackers.name: Recurs administratiu — but planning is expressly excluded, and nothing stops
trackers.desc: READ THE EXCLUSION FIRST, BECAUSE IT COVERS MOST LAND DISPUTES. Any person who considers themselves harmed by an act of the Administració General may lodge a recurs administratiu before the Govern — against definitive acts and against procedural acts that make continuation impossible or produce indefensió — but ‘queden exceptuats els recursos en matèria de construcció i urbanisme’. Construction and urban planning are expressly outside the ordinary administrative appeal, along with fiscal matters and anything with a special statutory procedure. So do not file a general recurs against a planning decision assuming it is the right route — establish which special procedure applies, and note that planning powers in Andorra sit substantially with the comuns rather than the Govern. WHERE IT DOES LIE: one month from notification, under article 129 of Llei 14/2023 of 3 July, the consolidated Codi de l'Administració. Eligible to file: any natural person with capacity to act and a NIA, and any entity with legal personality and a NIA. The resolution ends the administrative route. THE TRAP TO PLAN AROUND: under articles 52 and 135, ‘la interposició de recurs no suspèn l'execució de l'acte impugnat’ — lodging an appeal does not suspend execution. Works may proceed while you appeal; any suspension must be sought separately, and nothing stops by itself.

trackers.name: Batllia and the Raonador — name the co-defendants; the Ombudsman is free
trackers.desc: TWO ROUTES ABOVE THE ADMINISTRATION, AND ONE COSTS NOTHING. THE SECCIÓ ADMINISTRATIVA DE LA BATLLIA: the recurs contenciós administratiu is governed by Llei 9/2022 of 7 April, replacing the 1989 law that had originally created an administrative jurisdiction which did not previously exist in Andorra. Proceedings start with a demanda addressed to that Section (article 16), which must identify the party and justify its legitimacy; identify the act, actuació or reglamentary norm challenged and which administration authored it; and identify the parties to be treated as co-defendants. TWO CONSEQUENCES: a reglamentary norm is directly challengeable, not only an individual act — the regulation itself can be the target; and you must name the co-defendants yourself, which in a development dispute means identifying the promoter, not only the administration. Administrations are defended by lletrats of their own legal cabinets. THE RAONADOR DEL CIUTADÀ IS THE FREE ROUTE, taking complaints against Andorran institutions on rights and freedoms set out in the Constitution as they touch the Administration, and reporting annually to the Consell General. Its own reports record why it matters: people entitled to go to the Batllia ‘desisteixen d'acudir-hi per manca de recursos’ — give up going for lack of means. It keeps a dedicated urbanisme sector, so planning complaints are a recognised category even though excluded from the ordinary recurs. LIMIT: in the justice sector it is limited to transmitting the complaint to the Consell Superior de la Justícia. LEVERAGE: its reports record files closed without reply from the administration despite reminders of the obligation to answer — a documented non-response, published to Parliament, is itself a usable outcome.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: The comuns — seven parish authorities holding the communal land (Andorra)
trackers.desc: THE FACT THAT CHANGES WHO YOU WRITE TO: under the Constitution of the Principality of Andorra the seven comuns — the local public bodies of the parishes — manage and administer the goods of parish property, among them the communal public domain, which accounts for a high percentage of Andorran forest area. Each parish has its own Comú and manages directly the cadastre, public services, the communal patrimony and urban development, with its own legal personality and wide competences including planning, territorial planning and regulation of land. SO IN ANDORRA THE LANDOWNER AND THE PLANNING AUTHORITY ARE OFTEN THE SAME BODY. A community with a threatened site on communal ground is not looking for someone to buy it — it is asking its own parish authority, which already owns it and also decides what may be built on it. Write to the Comú, and ask which of the two hats it is wearing. THE PRECEDENT THAT SHOWS THIS WORKING: the Madriu-Perafita-Claror valley — 4,247 hectares, about 9% of the country, inscribed as World Heritage in 2004, with a periphery of roughly 4,000 further hectares — was protected through a Carta signed in January 2003 by government ministers and by the cònsols of Encamp, Andorra la Vella, Sant Julià de Lòria and Escaldes-Engordany on behalf of the comuns of the four parishes. Four parish authorities acting together protected a tenth of Andorra. THE TENSION TO EXPECT, and it is public: the Associació de Propietaris de Terres Andorranes — the association of Andorran landowners — publicly blames the comuns for urban planning disorder and legal insecurity, complaining that after the pandemic they went too far one way and now too far the other, and citing a boundary where building is permitted in one parish and not at all across the line in the next. Planning powers really do differ sharply between parishes, and landowners are organised and vocal about it. WHAT THIS IS NOT: not an NGO and not a funder. It is the level of government that holds the land, and in a country of seven parishes it is reachable.

trackers.name: Col·legi d'Advocats d'Andorra — the torn d'ofici, and the Batllia decides
trackers.desc: WHO TO CONTACT: the Col·legi Oficial d'Advocats d'Andorra — caa@cada.ad, +376 80 69 30 and +376 86 96 69 — which under Llei 48/2014 must designate a lawyer through the corresponding torn d'ofici when the competent jurisdictional body decides that a person must be defended and assisted by a lawyer, and that defence is free to those granted the benefit. Its site also carries a searchable directory of its col·legiats, which is how you find an Andorran lawyer at all. Andorra had no legal ally in this file. THE ROUTE, WHICH IS SHORT AND WORTH KNOWING EXACTLY: the application is made to the Batllia, and the Batllia decides whether the requirements are met — not the Col·legi. The free-assistance right rests on article 10.3 of the Andorran Constitution: the law shall regulate the cases in which, to guarantee the principle of equality, justice must be free. AND THE HONEST WARNING, from the Andorran lawyers themselves: participation in the torn d'ofici is voluntary, and lawyers providing it have publicly complained that the payment from Government was frozen for a decade, called a recent 6 per cent increase entirely insufficient, and said that if the situation continues they will stop doing it. Expect a thin duty roster and a reluctant one — which is a reason for an Andorran community to approach a lawyer directly through the directory rather than relying on the duty system. WHAT THIS DOES NOT COVER: the scheme is aimed at people without resources to pay a lawyer's fees. As in Kosovo, and unlike Cyprus, the route runs through an individual resident rather than through an association. Andorra's other doors remain the comuns, already filed here as the bodies that own the communal land and grant the planning permission, and ADN as the association with the record of pressing for designation.

trackers.name: Subvenció a favor de la biodiversitat i del paisatge — and only one applicant came forward
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: an annual call for subsidies for actions in favour of biodiversity and the landscape of Andorra, applied for through the government's electronic procedures desk. Andorra had no funder filed at all; this is the state's own environmental line. WHO MAY APPLY: any natural person with capacity to act holding an administrative identification number (NIA), and any entity or organisation with its own legal personality holding an NIA, acting through a legal representative with an electronic certificate. A sister call names the intended beneficiaries as public and private entities, individuals, NON-PROFIT ASSOCIATIONS, and holders of agricultural, livestock and beekeeping operations. AND THE FACT THAT SHOULD SEND A COMMUNITY STRAIGHT THERE: the government extended the deadline for both this call and a parallel one on preventing damage by protected fauna because, three days before closing, only ONE application had been formalised in each competition — while several potential beneficiaries had made enquiries. The extension was granted expressly to encourage greater participation. In a country this size an environmental call can close with a single applicant; the competition is not the obstacle. PRACTICAL: you must file the signed bases, a declaration that you are not a debtor of the Administration, a responsible declaration on capacity to contract with public sector entities, and bank domiciliation. Where a project is organised jointly by several parties, the bases address that case.

trackers.name: Observatori de subvencions — who got Andorran public money, ranked
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: an independent observatory of the Principality's subsidies and grants, searchable by body, by beneficiary or by call, with filters for purpose, type of aid, year and amount. It covers the Government, the Comuns and other public entities, showing amount awarded and number of calls per body, and a ranking of beneficiaries by amount received with the detail of each award. WHAT IT SHOWS ABOUT WHERE THE MONEY SITS: the Ministeri de Medi Ambient, Sostenibilitat i Agricultura ranks fourth among awarding bodies at about 6.79 million euro, with the Oficina de l'Energia i del Canvi Climàtic and the Ministeri de Territori i Urbanisme also in the top ten — and two of the seven comuns rank above most ministries. The comuns are already filed here as the parish authorities holding the common land; this shows they are also among the largest grant-givers. WHY THIS IS A RESOURCE AND NOT A CURIOSITY: a searchable record of who received what tells you which organisations are funded, which calls actually pay out, and who to approach as a partner — the same use this file made of grantee lists in North Macedonia and Turkey.

trackers.name: Caribbean Biodiversity Fund (CBF)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a regional environmental endowment established in 2012, managing an endowment plus a sinking fund for Ecosystem-based Adaptation, which it disburses mainly through partner National Conservation Trust Funds rather than directly — it helped establish several of them, including the Dominica, Grenada, Jamaica, St Kitts & Nevis, St Lucia and St Vincent funds. Its EbA window runs open calls for proposals. WHO IT SUITS: organisations doing on-the-ground ecosystem work that reduces climate vulnerability. Check whether your country has a national trust fund first — that is usually the door, and the CBF itself is the wholesaler behind it. HOW IT DIFFERS: endowment income committed for the long term, so it funds sustained protected-area management rather than a campaign. APPLY TO YOUR NATIONAL FUND, NOT TO CBF — for most of the money. CBF is a regional umbrella: at national level the partner National Conservation Trust Funds (NCTFs) lead the grantmaking process, with endowment proceeds held in country-based subaccounts and channelled through them. So for the Conservation Finance stream, the regional body is the wrong door — find your NCTF. THE EXCEPTION IS THE EbA FACILITY, which awards through competitive calls for proposals and is a direct route. THE NUMBERS: EbA medium grants USD 250,000–1 million, large grants up to USD 2 million — large by the standards of most funds here, and not aimed at a small unincorporated group acting alone. Eligible recipients expressly include NCTFs, NGOs, community-based organisations, government agencies, universities and the private sector. SCOPE CHECK: the EbA Facility covers the marine and coastal zone of the insular Caribbean, so an inland project must show its connection to marine and coastal ecosystems. IF YOU ARE TOO SMALL FOR EbA: CBF partners with GEF SGP across 12 shared countries — that is the sibling route for community-scale grants, and it is recorded separately in this map. Endowment disbursements go to NCTFs that have signed agreements with CBF, the first in 2016 with Fondo MARENA in the Dominican Republic.

trackers.name: CANARI — Caribbean Natural Resources Institute
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a regional technical non-profit founded in 1989 and headquartered in Trinidad, working with grassroots and community-based organisations across the Caribbean on participatory natural resource governance. It supplies capacity rather than representation: coaching, mentoring, training of trainers, facilitated dialogues for planning and policymaking, and practical evidence tools including participatory GIS mapping, three-dimensional modelling and participatory video. WHO IT SUITS: community organisations that need to be equipped for a planning or policy fight. COVERAGE NOTE: CANARI is not registered as a non-profit in this country, but has delivered sub-grants to communities here under its Caribbean ecosystem-restoration work, so it does operate here — ask what is currently running. It is not a litigator and its re-granting is tied to donor projects. IS YOUR SITE A KBA? CHECK BEFORE YOU WRITE ANYTHING. CANARI publishes the CEPF Caribbean Islands Biodiversity Hotspot Ecosystem Profile, which identifies 45 Key Biodiversity Areas and 6 conservation corridors covering 28 KBAs as priorities for funding support, with maps — formulated through a process engaging over 200 stakeholders from more than 160 organisations. A campaign whose site is a KBA, or sits in one of the six corridors, has a materially stronger funding case and should say so explicitly. CORRECTED — AND THIS STREAM IS CLOSING. CEPF returned for a Phase II running August 2021 to July 2027, and CANARI is once again the Regional Implementation Team, managing US$11.8 million. THE ELEVENTH AND FINAL SMALL-GRANT CALL offers USD 5,000–50,000 for projects of up to 12 months between April 2026 and March 2027, and the tenth call was the final open call for large grants in the region — so treat the current call as the last scheduled opportunity, not one of many, though targeted solicitations may still fill portfolio gaps. ELIGIBILITY NARROWED IN PHASE II: the Phase I list of 11 countries no longer applies; Phase II calls name Antigua and Barbuda, The Bahamas, the Dominican Republic, Jamaica, Saint Lucia, and St Vincent and the Grenadines, with CEPF stating 7 countries initially eligible. BUT THE SITE TEST CAN OUTRANK THE COUNTRY TEST: applicants based outside the eligible countries may submit provided activities focus on a conservation need within a priority corridor or site. THREE RULES: applicants must not be a government agency (government-owned bodies qualify only with independent legal personality and authority to receive private funds); joint projects are eligible with one lead organisation; and NGOs, community groups, universities and private enterprises may all apply. ASK BEFORE YOU DRAFT: RIT Manager Nicole Brown, caribbeanrit@canari.org — applicants uncertain about eligibility are expressly encouraged to make contact first. A Grievance Redress Mechanism exists for concerns about a funded project. WHAT CANARI ITSELF IS: a non-profit technical institute of thirty years' standing that acts as a conduit, channelling funding, information and technical support to CSOs — not a standing grant fund. Its project pattern is small grants plus technical coaching for partner CSOs to run participatory community vulnerability assessments and then design a project from the results.

trackers.name: Antigua & Barbuda — Ministry of Finance
trackers.desc: National budget authority; responsible for public finances, economic planning, revenue & budgeting, Antigua and Barbuda. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Antigua and Barbuda.

trackers.name: Antigua & Barbuda — Intellectual Property & Commerce Office (ABIPCO)
trackers.desc: National company registry; ABIPCO handles company & business-name registration alongside intellectual-property administration, Antigua & Barbuda. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: National Audit Office
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Antigua and Barbuda, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court (ECSC)
trackers.desc: A SUPERIOR COURT OF RECORD SERVING NINE EASTERN CARIBBEAN JURISDICTIONS, and the practical point is that you file at home. Established 27 February 1967 under the West Indies Associated States Supreme Court Order, the ECSC serves 6 independent states — Antigua and Barbuda, Dominica, Grenada, St Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, St Vincent and the Grenadines — and 3 British Overseas Territories — Anguilla, the Virgin Islands and Montserrat. It has unlimited jurisdiction in each member state and territory, and High Court operations are decentralised through registries in each participating territory, headed by trained registrars, allowing local filing, case management and initial hearings by resident or assigned judges. It exists so that very small jurisdictions can reach specialised judicial expertise without funding a standalone supreme court. THE BENCH HAS BEEN BRIEFED ON ESCAZÚ: ECLAC and the Government of Saint Lucia ran a consultation with ECSC judicial officers on the Regional Agreement on access to information, public participation and justice in environmental matters — so an environmental access-to-justice argument goes to judges who have had that agreement formally explained. Headquarters: Heraldine Rock Building, Castries, Saint Lucia; tel 758-457-3600; an e-Litigation Portal is available. CHECK YOUR FINAL COURT BEFORE PLANNING AN APPEAL — appeals from the ECSC go to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council or the Caribbean Court of Justice depending on the territory, and this is not uniform across the nine. For St Kitts and Nevis the final court is recorded as the Privy Council.

trackers.name: Bahamas National Trust
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: an independent statutory body created by the Bahamas National Trust Act 1959, modelled on the British National Trust and given the job of ACQUIRING LAND and managing protected areas nationwide; it now holds and runs 32 national parks covering over two million acres, and its governing council seats government, private-sector and scientific representatives. Park rules are made under section 24 of the Act, so its bylaws carry legal force on trust property. USE IT: to propose a threatened Bahamian site for national-park status or trust acquisition, and to check whether land a developer wants already sits inside a park boundary.

trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a regional environmental endowment established in 2012, managing an endowment plus a sinking fund for Ecosystem-based Adaptation, which it disburses mainly through partner National Conservation Trust Funds rather than directly — it helped establish several of them, including the Dominica, Grenada, Jamaica, St Kitts & Nevis, St Lucia and St Vincent funds. Its EbA window runs open calls for proposals. WHO IT SUITS: organisations doing on-the-ground ecosystem work that reduces climate vulnerability. HOW IT DIFFERS: endowment income committed for the long term, so it funds sustained protected-area management rather than a campaign. APPLY TO YOUR NATIONAL FUND, NOT TO CBF — for most of the money. CBF is a regional umbrella: at national level the partner National Conservation Trust Funds (NCTFs) lead the grantmaking process, with endowment proceeds held in country-based subaccounts and channelled through them. So for the Conservation Finance stream, the regional body is the wrong door — find your NCTF. THE EXCEPTION IS THE EbA FACILITY, which awards through competitive calls for proposals and is a direct route. THE NUMBERS: EbA medium grants USD 250,000–1 million, large grants up to USD 2 million — large by the standards of most funds here, and not aimed at a small unincorporated group acting alone. Eligible recipients expressly include NCTFs, NGOs, community-based organisations, government agencies, universities and the private sector. SCOPE CHECK: the EbA Facility covers the marine and coastal zone of the insular Caribbean, so an inland project must show its connection to marine and coastal ecosystems. IF YOU ARE TOO SMALL FOR EbA: CBF partners with GEF SGP across 12 shared countries — that is the sibling route for community-scale grants, and it is recorded separately in this map. Endowment disbursements go to NCTFs that have signed agreements with CBF, the first in 2016 with Fondo MARENA in the Dominican Republic.

trackers.name: Judiciary of The Bahamas
trackers.desc: Official judgments archive of the Supreme Court and the Court of Appeal of the Commonwealth of The Bahamas. · Find here: the Bahamian Judiciary's official judgments archive.

trackers.name: Office of the Auditor General
trackers.desc: National — supreme audit institution of The Bahamas. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in the Bahamas.

trackers.name: Bahamas — Registrar General’s Department
trackers.desc: National company registry; registers companies & IBCs, provides online company search and document filing via CARS, The Bahamas. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of the Bahamas
trackers.desc: Supreme Court of the Bahamas — supreme court in Bahamas (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund (CEPF)
trackers.desc: A FUND WHOSE SMALL-GRANT APPLICATION IS A SINGLE LETTER. CEPF (founded 2000; a joint initiative of the French Development Agency, Conservation International, the EU, the GEF, the Government of Japan, the MacArthur Foundation and the World Bank) has funded more than 2,500 grantees. FOR SMALL GRANTS THE LETTER OF INQUIRY IS THE ENTIRE APPLICATION — no longer project proposal is required — reviewed by the hotspot's Regional Implementation Team, with an offline template provided in the call's languages. Large grants go through the ConservationGrants portal and only then invite a full proposal. Reported averages: small grants around US$15,000, large around US$150,000; the small/large threshold varies by call (US$20,000 and US$50,000 both recorded), so read it. TIMING: calls run 6–8 weeks and notification comes several months after closing — but CEPF stops accepting letters once the designated funds are committed, so an open call can close early. WHO IS DISQUALIFIED: individuals cannot apply — you need a legally registered organisation with its own bank account — and government cannot apply. Community groups, farmers' cooperatives, Indigenous Peoples' organisations and women's groups all can, and CEPF welcomes first-time applicants. TWO RULES THAT SINK GOOD APPLICATIONS: your letter must aim at one single strategic direction; and site-based directions are geographically bound — community management work must be in a listed priority KBA, corridor work in a named corridor, while civil-society strengthening can be anywhere in the hotspot. THE STEP MOST PEOPLE SKIP: CEPF encourages you to contact RIT staff to discuss the idea before submitting — free, and the cheapest way to learn whether it fits.

trackers.name: BPAF is Registrar of 123 protected areas — start with the register
trackers.desc: THE FIRST PLACE TO ESTABLISH WHETHER YOUR SITE IS PROTECTED, AND UNDER WHICH LAW. The Bahamas Protected Areas Fund Act 2014 (No. 28) requires the Board to establish and maintain a Register of Protected Areas, and BPAF is the Registrar of 123 protected areas. That matters because the system draws on four different statutes: forest reserves, protected forests and conservation forests under the Forestry Act; and areas declared under the Fisheries Resources (Jurisdiction and Conservation) Act, the Bahamas National Trust Act, and the Wild Birds Protection Act. Identify which of the four applies before arguing — the powers, decision-maker and appeal route differ by statute, and the Wild Birds Protection Act is an unexpected route to area protection. THE MANDATE IS BROADER THAN PARKS: carbon sinks, water resources, wetlands, blue holes, degraded ecosystems and climate adaptation areas are all named. GOVERNANCE IS PUBLISHED AND CHECKABLE: a board of at most 11 — 5 appointed by Government, one each by the Bahamas National Trust and The Nature Conservancy, four co-opted — with 4-year maximum terms, members including expertise in law, and a stated position that only two directors are employed by, affiliated with or controlled by Government. Check that statement against the current board. Grantees include Waterkeepers Bahamas, the Bahamas National Trust and the University of The Bahamas.

trackers.name: Bahamas Protected — a coalition proposal became a gazetted expansion
trackers.desc: A DOCUMENTED PATH FROM CIVIL SOCIETY PROPOSAL TO GOVERNMENT INSTRUMENT, WITH A REALISTIC TIMESCALE. The coalition Bahamas Protected — The Nature Conservancy, the Bahamas National Trust and BREEF with national stakeholders, funded by Oceans 5 — made a written proposal to expand marine protected areas in September 2018. In July 2021 the Government gazetted an expansion adding 5,254,179 acres to the 13.9 million already protected, bringing the country to 20 percent of its marine and coastal habitat. Roughly three years from proposal to gazettal — that is the interval to plan for. THE METHOD IS COPYABLE: a marine gap analysis engaging about 40 scientists and practitioners from more than 26 organisations across three consultations, identifying priority areas of interest for further vetting — evidence assembled collectively, then a specific written ask. It also worked with the BEST Commission and the Department of Marine Resources. CONTEXT: the first Bahamian protected area dates from 1892 and the Exuma Cays Land & Sea Park (1958) was the first of its kind — a managed no-take zone. Bahamas National Trust: P.O. Box N-4105, Nassau.

trackers.name: Caribbean Biodiversity Fund (CBF)

trackers.name: Maya Leaders Alliance [2015] CCJ 15 — the abstention undertaking to quote
trackers.desc: THE JUDGMENT, AND THE SENTENCE THAT DOES THE WORK. The Caribbean Court of Justice — Belize's highest appellate court — affirmed that Maya customary land tenure in the Toledo District gives rise to collective and individual rights under sections 3(d) and 17 of the Constitution, constituting property equal in legitimacy to any other form of property. THE UNDERTAKING TO QUOTE: the Court accepted the Government's undertaking that until the recognition measures are achieved it shall cease and abstain from any acts — whether by government agents or by third parties acting with its leave, acquiescence or tolerance — that might adversely affect the value, use or enjoyment of lands used and occupied by Maya villages, unless preceded by consultation to obtain their informed consent. Note the breadth: it reaches acts merely acquiesced in or tolerated, not only permitted — a concession granted or an incursion ignored falls inside it. In the immediate term the Solicitor General directed heads of departments to immediately cease all activities and operations on the affected lands. WHAT PROMPTED IT: authorisations for oil drilling, logging, grazing and surveying, including the Golden Stream incursion where the Lands Department issued an agricultural lease over Maya village lands.

trackers.name: A judgment is not implementation — watch the policy that implements it
trackers.desc: TWO LESSONS FROM WHAT HAPPENED AFTER THE WIN. 1. PERSISTENCE THROUGH APPEALS WAS THE STRATEGY. Favourable judgments in the Belize Supreme Court in 2007 and 2010, upheld by the Court of Appeal in 2013, then the CCJ in 2015 — roughly two decades, with the government appealing at every stage and the courts ruling for the Maya at every level. Note also the tactical value of the Consent Order of 22 April 2015: both parties conceded that customary tenure exists, which the CCJ said rendered moot the contest over whether the rights existed at all — removing the foundational question and leaving only remedy. 2. THE ORDER HAS YET TO BE FULFILLED. The CCJ heard arguments on 29 November 2022 specifically on Belize's compliance with its own 2015 decision, and compensation for the constitutional breaches remained outstanding. AND WATCH THE IMPLEMENTING INSTRUMENT AS CLOSELY AS THE JUDGMENT: a draft Maya Customary Land Policy dated 8 December 2023 was reported to contain last-minute inserted language under which companies would no longer need free, prior and informed consent for industrial activity outside determined circular areas. A policy written to implement a ruling can narrow it. Context: in 2010 Belize granted oil concessions in the Sarstoon-Temash National Park. The CCJ treated IACHR findings as persuasive though not binding, alongside Saramaka People v Suriname.

trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. trackers.desc: THE RIGHT BODY EVEN IF YOUR SITE IS NOT IN A NATIONAL PARK. The Division — whose Forest Service dates to 1949 — has jurisdiction over sites within the National Parks System (Morne Diablotin, Morne Trois Pitons, Cabrits) and over several other nature sites which are not within the established national parks, expressly including Soufriere Sulphur Springs, Indian River and Trafalgar Falls. Its National Park Unit is the largest section in the Division. A FUNDING MODEL WORTH COPYING: the Eco-tourist Site User Fee programme, running since June 1997, collects entry fees from non-residents only at 12 eco-tourism sites, including the Morne Trois Pitons World Heritage sites — Emerald Pool, Boiling Lake, Freshwater Lake, Boeri Lake and Middleham Falls. A non-resident fee at named sites, sustained for nearly three decades, is durable domestic revenue for park management that does not tax local users — a directly transferable design. CONTEXT: Morne Diablotin was established January 2000 at 3,335.3 ha, 4.4 percent of the nation; Morne Trois Pitons became a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1998; each of the three parks has a management plan and continuous monitoring; and EIAs are recorded as mandatory for all developments.

trackers.name: DNCTF — it only adopted its governing policies in 2024
trackers.desc: TIME YOUR APPROACH. The Dominica National Conservation Trust Fund exists to provide a sustainable source of funding for effective management, conservation and restoration of Dominica's biodiversity — but it approved its foundational governance documents and internal policies only in 2024, aligning with the international Standards of Practice for Conservation Trust Funds. A fund that has just adopted its governing policies is at the start of its grantmaking life: expect procedures to be new and expect them to be applied strictly. IT IS ALSO A REGIONAL HUB — it hosted a USAID Sustainable Financing workshop building capacity among peer national funds from St Vincent and the Grenadines, St Kitts and Nevis and Suriname, engaged volunteers through the CORE project with CBF and CUSO International, and joined a regional capital-raising strategy led by the Bahamas Protected Areas Fund. MIRROR ITS OWN THREAT LIST IN AN APPLICATION: deforestation, overexploitation of wildlife, encroachment, land degradation, unregulated development, invasive species, loss of agrobiodiversity, climate impacts, pollution, hurricanes and seismic activity, land mining, gradual loss of traditional knowledge — and inappropriate legal and institutional frameworks. A national conservation fund naming the legal framework itself as a threat is quotable. ALSO ON THE ISLAND: Wild Dominica Conservancy, which invites people to join as member, trustee or sponsor — note it is a US 501(c)(3), so a US-registered charity operating on Dominica rather than a Dominican body.

trackers.name: Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund (CEPF)
trackers.desc: A FUND WHOSE SMALL-GRANT APPLICATION IS A SINGLE LETTER.
