trackers.name: Caribbean Court of Justice (CCJ)
trackers.desc: YOUR FINAL COURT OF APPEAL — this is one of only 5 states that have acceded to the CCJ's Appellate Jurisdiction, replacing the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council for civil and criminal appeals: Barbados, Belize, Dominica, Guyana and Saint Lucia. Everywhere else in the Eastern Caribbean the final court remains the Privy Council, so do not assume the CCJ is your appeal route from a neighbouring jurisdiction's practice. BE CLEAR WHAT THE OTHER JURISDICTION DOES NOT COVER: in its Original Jurisdiction the CCJ interprets the Revised Treaty of Chaguaramas on freedom of movement of people, goods, services, capital and the right of establishment — it does not extend to human rights generally, and it is not an environmental forum. A land-defence claim does not fit there unless it has a cross-border economic dimension, such as a project licensed to a company from another CARICOM state. WHERE IT DOES FIT, INDIVIDUALS CAN GET IN: under Article 222 a natural or juridical person may seek special leave, granted where the Treaty intended the right to enure to the benefit of individuals, the applicant has been prejudiced, and the member state entitled to espouse the claim omitted or declined to. 35 such cases have been brought, so the route is used rather than theoretical — Trinidad Cement Ltd v Republic of Guyana [2009] CCJ 1 (OJ) established that individuals and companies can use the Treaty to make their own state comply. The Court sits as a court of first instance there, its rulings immediately binding in international law, and hearings are broadcast live.

trackers.name: Saint Lucia National Trust — can acquire land, and you can stand for its Council
trackers.desc: A STATUTORY BODY WHOSE OBJECTS INCLUDE ACQUIRING LAND. Established 1975 under the Saint Lucia National Trust Act, Chapter 6.02, as a body corporate, with objects that include to acquire property for the benefit of the State and to conserve areas of beauty including submarine and subterranean areas — so a cave system or reef is within its express statutory remit. Under section 16 it may make by-laws to protect and maintain property it holds: a body that can make its own rules over land it holds is stronger than one that merely owns it. YOU CAN JOIN AND YOU CAN STAND: it is a membership organisation with an 11-member Council, 7 elected annually by the membership at the AGM, the other four representing the Archaeological and Historical Society and the Government. HOW LAND REACHES IT: properties have been vested in, or donated and bequeathed by individuals for conservation — bequest is an established route here, not a theory. It manages national landmarks, historical sites, environmental protection areas and nature reserves whether owned or vested in it, including Pigeon Island, Maria Islands Nature Reserve (declared 1982), Anse La Liberte and the Pointe Sable Environmental Protection Area. ASK WHICH LEVEL APPLIES TO YOUR SITE: in the Trust's own words, some sites are protected areas by law and others are deemed for protection by nature of their biological components — two very different levels of security.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court (ECSC)
trackers.desc: A SUPERIOR COURT OF RECORD SERVING NINE EASTERN CARIBBEAN JURISDICTIONS, and the practical point is that you file at home. Established 27 February 1967 under the West Indies Associated States Supreme Court Order, the ECSC serves 6 independent states — Antigua and Barbuda, Dominica, Grenada, St Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, St Vincent and the Grenadines — and 3 British Overseas Territories — Anguilla, the Virgin Islands and Montserrat. It has unlimited jurisdiction in each member state and territory, and High Court operations are decentralised through registries in each participating territory, headed by trained registrars, allowing local filing, case management and initial hearings by resident or assigned judges. It exists so that very small jurisdictions can reach specialised judicial expertise without funding a standalone supreme court. THE BENCH HAS BEEN BRIEFED ON ESCAZÚ: ECLAC and the Government of Saint Lucia ran a consultation with ECSC judicial officers on the Regional Agreement on access to information, public participation and justice in environmental matters — so an environmental access-to-justice argument goes to judges who have had that agreement formally explained. Headquarters: Heraldine Rock Building, Castries, Saint Lucia; tel 758-457-3600; an e-Litigation Portal is available. CHECK YOUR FINAL COURT BEFORE PLANNING AN APPEAL — appeals from the ECSC go to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council or the Caribbean Court of Justice depending on the territory, and this is not uniform across the nine. For St Kitts and Nevis the final court is recorded as the Privy Council.

trackers.name: NPRBA — its own mission commits it to full community involvement
trackers.desc: A STATUTORY BODY THAT HAS WRITTEN YOUR STANDARD FOR YOU. The National Parks, Rivers and Beaches Authority was established by Act No. 33 of 2002 for the preservation, protection, management and development of natural, physical and ecological resources and historical and cultural heritage — and its mission is to protect those resources ‘by fully involving all relevant community groups and stakeholders in promoting and managing their use’. Quote that back. ITS DEFINITION OF A PROTECTED AREA IS BROAD: an area of land or water managed for ecological systems, biological diversity and/or specific natural, cultural and aesthetic resources — aesthetic resources are named, so a site can qualify on landscape value alone. AND ONE SYSTEM OBJECTIVE IS UNUSUALLY CONCRETE: protection of ecosystem function, expressly water, electricity and soil conservation. Where a development threatens a watershed feeding hydro generation or water supply, that is already a stated objective of the managing authority, not an argument you must construct. Other objectives include wilderness protection and landscape maintenance, maintenance of environmental services, maintenance of cultural and traditional attributes, and meeting obligations under international conventions. Contact: Jaycee's Building, corner Leeward Highway and Stoney Ground Road, Kingstown. Resource context: about 12,700 ha of tropical forest including palm brakes and elfin woodland, habitat of the St Vincent parrot.

trackers.name: SVG National Trust — it went dormant, and Cabinet revived it
trackers.desc: A LESSON ABOUT ANY BODY YOU FIND IN LEGISLATION. The Trust was established in 1969 to assist with the preservation and management of historical monuments and sites and to safeguard cultural patrimony — but the official history records that ‘interest waned and the Trust remained dormant for some time’. Cabinet then appointed a Board of Trustees to spearhead its revitalisation, with the Ministry of Tourism and Culture as parent ministry, and it now holds meetings of both the Board and the general membership — so it can be joined. TWO PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCES: first, do not assume a body named in legislation is currently active — check for recent meetings before building a plan around it; second, where a useful statutory body has lapsed, revival by Cabinet appointment is a documented route in this jurisdiction rather than a novel request. FOR SCALE ON WHAT IS AT STAKE: the Tobago Cays marine park is a 1,400-acre lagoon encompassing five cays, the inhabited island of Mayreau and the 4 km Horseshoe Reef, listed as a regionally significant ecosystem under the SPAW Protocol in December 2014 — with an estimated 3,000 yachts anchoring in the lagoon each year and 10,000 cruise visitors reaching the cays.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a pan-African feminist rapid-response fund with reach across all 54 African countries — small grants released quickly for unanticipated, time-critical situations rather than planned programme work, covering safety and protection needs when defenders are threatened and short windows for advocacy after an unexpected event. WHO IT SUITS: women's rights organisations, feminist collectives and movements in which women or gender-diverse people are the primary decision-makers. It does NOT fund individuals, and the action must be strategic, genuinely unanticipated, and completable in under three months. HOW IT DIFFERS: this is emergency money for a moment, not a budget for a campaign — decisions are fast and grants are modest.

trackers.name: African Convention on Nature — check WHICH version binds your state
trackers.desc: THERE ARE TWO AFRICAN CONVENTIONS OF THIS NAME, AND CITING THE WRONG ONE IS THE AVOIDABLE ERROR HERE. The Algiers Convention was signed 15 September 1968, in force 16 June 1969. The revised Maputo Convention was adopted by the Assembly of the Union in Maputo on 11 July 2003 and entered into force 23 July 2016 — thirteen years later. THE OPERATIVE RULE: the 1968 Convention remains in force for those countries that have not ratified the 2003 revisions, so the two coexist and which binds your state depends on its ratification status. Commentary records only about 30 percent of African states had ratified Maputo. This entry does not assert which binds your state — the African Union publishes a Status List alongside the treaty text at au.int. Check it first. WHY THE DELAY IS AN ARGUMENT FOR IT: commentary attributes the thirteen years to the revised text containing strong provisions that could create accountability and also slow down social and economic development — a treaty resisted for creating accountability is one worth invoking where it applies. PROVISIONS TO KNOW: article XXXIX — no reservation may be made to this Convention, so a ratifying state takes all of it; article XL — withdrawal takes effect only one year after written notification; and no instrument of accession to the 1968 Algiers Convention may be deposited any longer, so the older text is closed to new entrants. THE OBJECTIVES ARE BROADER THAN USUAL: conservation, utilisation and development of soil, water, flora and fauna for present and future welfare, from an economic, nutritional, scientific, educational, cultural and aesthetic point of view — so a claim resting on cultural or aesthetic value has a treaty basis. BUT IF THE 1968 TEXT IS WHAT BINDS YOU, EXPECT LITTLE: parties were encouraged to cooperate but were not required to submit regular reports on implementation, and there were no financial mechanisms — no reporting trail, no funding attached. Article XLI also provides for interim secretariat arrangements, so check current institutional capacity. IUCN publishes a commentary on each provision in English and French.

trackers.name: Algeria's public inquiry register — the one opening a resident has, and it closes in fifteen days
trackers.desc: WHERE TO FILE, AND WHY THIS ENTRY IS WRITTEN AS AN ABSENCE: no Algerian civil society organisation providing land defence, environmental litigation or community legal support could be verified for this file. What a resident does have is the enquête publique attached to environmental impact assessment, run by the environment ministry's procedure. THE MECHANICS, WHICH ARE THE WHOLE POINT: the order opening the public inquiry must be made known by posting at the wilaya headquarters, at the communes concerned and at the project site, and by insertion in two national daily newspapers AT THE PROMOTER'S EXPENSE; it must state the detailed object of the inquiry, its duration, and the hours and place where the public may record observations in a numbered and initialled register opened for that purpose. THE DURATION MUST NOT EXCEED FIFTEEN DAYS FROM THE DATE OF POSTING — so the window can open and close inside a fortnight, and a village that hears about it late has lost it. Requests to consult the impact study or notice are addressed to the wali, who must invite the person to read it at a place he designates and give them fifteen days to formulate their views and observations. For the inquiry the wali appoints a commissaire enquêteur responsible for ensuring the posting and publication rules are respected. The governing texts are the executive decree of 19 May 2007 on the scope, content and approval of impact studies and notices, with the lists of installations subject to a full study or a lighter notice set out in annexes. WATCH THE NOTICEBOARD AT THE COMMUNE, AND WRITE IN THE REGISTER — an entry in a numbered, initialled register is a dated record that the project file must carry. WHO IT SUITS: Algerian residents near a proposed installation who want a formal, dated objection on the record. CAVEATS: THIS IS A STATE PROCEDURE, NOT AN ALLY, and no independent Algerian organisation is recorded here to help you use it — Algeria was researched twice for this file without a qualifying civil society body being found. The publicity requirement depends on the promoter paying for it and on the wali's administration; fifteen days is the maximum, not a guarantee.

trackers.name: Algeria — under loi 13-07 an advocate designated by the bâtonnier MUST act for you, and when commis d'office must defend you before ALL jurisdictions, free
trackers.desc: WHO OWES YOU A LAWYER, AND THIS CORRECTS THIS FILE'S OWN EARLIER RECORD FOR ALGERIA: under loi n°13-07 organising the profession of advocate, Article 11 — THE ADVOCATE DESIGNATED BY THE BÂTONNIER OR HIS DELEGATE IN THE FRAMEWORK OF ASSISTANCE JUDICIAIRE MUST LEND HIS CONCOURS TO ANY LITIGANT WHO BENEFITS FROM IT; and when COMMIS D'OFFICE by the bâtonnier or his delegate, he is BOUND TO ENSURE THE DEFENCE OF THE INTERESTS OF ANY LITIGANT, BEFORE ALL JURISDICTIONS, gratuitously. So the person to approach in Algeria is THE BÂTONNIER OF THE TERRITORIALLY COMPETENT BAR — designation is his to make, and once made the advocate has no discretion to refuse. WHAT AN ADVOCATE'S ROLE COVERS, per the same law: representation, assistance and defence of the parties, and the provision of advice and LEGAL CONSULTATIONS (Art. 5), with power to take any measure and intervene in any act of procedure (Art. 6). Advocates must open a cabinet within the jurisdiction of a court and may have only one. WHERE THE BARS ARE: the BARREAU D'ALGER, seated at the Palais de Justice, Algiers, is described as the largest bar in Algeria and on the continent, with close to 7,000 registered advocates, appearing before the Cour d'Alger and the tribunals of Sidi M'Hamed, Bab El Oued, El Harrach, Hussein Dey, Bir Mourad Raïs, Dar El Beïda and Rouiba; other bars sit at each cour, including Blida. Seven thousand advocates in one bar means the constraint in Algeria is not supply but designation — get the bâtonnier to designate, and use the environment and immovable-property categories when asking for one who practises in your matter. WHO IT SUITS: Algerians without means facing expropriation, an immovable-property dispute or an environmental harm, anywhere a cour sits. CAVEATS: DESIGNATION RUNS THROUGH THE BÂTONNIER and the conditions of assistance judiciaire are set by separate legislation and regulations — confirm them; no independent Algerian civil society organisation providing land or environmental support could be verified for this file, across three searches. For the fifteen-day public inquiry window and the register to write in, Algeria's enquête publique entry.

trackers.name: Algeria's loi 11-02 — a protected area can be created by decision of the WALI or of your COMMUNAL POPULAR ASSEMBLY PRESIDENT, with a wilaya commission giving the opinion
trackers.desc: WHO CAN CREATE A PROTECTED AREA, AND THE ANSWER IS CLOSER TO HOME THAN MOST PEOPLE ASSUME: under LOI N°11-02 OF 17 FEBRUARY 2011 on protected areas, AN AIRE PROTÉGÉE MAY BE CREATED BY VIRTUE OF A DECISION OF THE WALI OR OF THE PRESIDENT OF THE COMMUNAL POPULAR ASSEMBLY, with A COMMISSION DE WILAYA comprising the sectors concerned charged with giving an OPINION ON THE PROPOSAL AND OBJECTIVE OF CLASSIFICATION and approving the classification studies (décret exécutif 16-259 of 10 October 2016 fixes the composition and functioning of the national and wilaya commissions). Your own APC president can create one. That makes classification a local political question you can actually reach — take the proposal to the commune first, and the wilaya commission is who must then be persuaded. WHAT THE PAPERWORK CONSISTS OF, so you know what you are asking a commune to commission: a SCHÉMA DIRECTEUR setting long-term objectives for biodiversity conservation, sustainable use of natural AND CULTURAL heritage, ecotourism and ecosystem restoration — drawn up IN CONCERTATION WITH THE SECTORS CONCERNED AND LOCAL ACTORS, and revised every FIFTEEN YEARS — and a PLAN DE GESTION (décret of 13 August 2019, under article 37 of loi 11-02) described as A TECHNICAL AND DYNAMIC DOCUMENT containing the heritage evaluation, strategic and operational objectives, protection means, short and medium-term intervention programme, research programme, an exhaustive state of the area highlighting PROBLEMS, STAKES AND OPPORTUNITIES, a YEAR-BY-YEAR, ZONE-BY-ZONE WORK PLAN with localisation AND FINANCIAL EVALUATION of operations, and mapping. Ask to see the plan de gestion for any Algerian protected area near you: the annual work plan carries costed, located operations, which is the most checkable document in this entire national system. The plan is approved by the managing establishment's orientation council after the scientific council's opinion. Practitioners writing on Algeria's parks have named the standing agenda as settling disputes arising after park creation — aggregate quarry concessions, public dumps, polluting industrial units, uncontrolled urbanisation — and associating neighbouring populations with rural development through local projects. WHO IT SUITS: Algerian communes, associations and residents seeking classification of ground, or scrutiny of an existing park's plan. CAVEATS: CLASSIFICATION AND MANAGEMENT SIT WITH PUBLIC ESTABLISHMENTS, not communities; no independent Algerian land or environmental civil-society organisation could be verified for this file. For the fifteen-day inquiry register, Algeria's enquête publique entry; for a designated advocate, the loi 13-07 entry.

trackers.name: Algeria's environmental associations by wilaya — a published directory with postal addresses, naming AREA-ED in Tipaza, the APE of Tizi-Ouzou, Le Flambeau Vert in Constantine and others
trackers.desc: THE WILAYA-BY-WILAYA DIRECTORY — and this is the first Algerian civil society in this file, which previously held only registers, the bar and the protected-areas law: a published ANNUAIRE OF ALGERIAN ENVIRONMENTAL ASSOCIATIONS GIVING EACH ONE'S POSTAL ADDRESS AND FIELD OF ACTIVITY, ORGANISED BY WILAYA. Algeria's environmental sector is local and scattered rather than national — so the question is never who is the big organisation, it is who is in my wilaya. A directory with street addresses answers exactly that. NAMED ENTRIES: ASSOCIATION DE RÉFLEXION, D'ÉCHANGE ET D'ACTION POUR L'ENVIRONNEMENT ET LE DÉVELOPPEMENT (AREA-ED), Route de Cherchell, Nador, 42240 TIPAZA, BP 61 — a MULTIDISCIPLINARY association for environment and sustainable development contributing to THE PRESERVATION AND VALORISATION OF NATURAL RESOURCES, beginning with WATER; the ASSOCIATION POUR LA PROTECTION DE L'ENVIRONNEMENT DE TIZI-OUZOU (APE), Centre Commercial Mehlal, Azazga 15300, CREATED 2006, whose mandate is environmental protection notably through awareness work with children; ASSOCIATION LE FLAMBEAU VERT DE L'ENVIRONNEMENT (AFVE), 01 rue Hamida Bentlis, Sidi Mabrouk, CONSTANTINE — which SINCE 2004 HAS BROUGHT TOGETHER YOUNG GRADUATES AND SPECIALISTS IN ENVIRONMENT; ECOLOGIATURE, BP 288, TLEMCEN 13000, with a named director; AEEV in TIARET, with a named president, working on AWARENESS AT NEIGHBOURHOOD LEVEL, information and communication; ESSAADA at Dar Echabab Tayeb Lokbi, Boussaada, M'SILA, working on environmental education and ÉCOCITOYENNETÉ; the ASSOCIATION POUR LA PROTECTION DE L'ENVIRONNEMENT DE BÉNI SAF (apeb-dz.org); a MARINE ECOLOGICAL ASSOCIATION WHOSE FOUNDING MEMBERS ARE DIVERS concerned at the degradation of the marine ecosystem; and locality nature projects covering the wilaya of NAÂMA and the fauna and flora of SAÏDA. A group of young environment graduates in Constantine and a diving club on the coast are the two shapes that recur here — professional competence without a budget, and people who see the damage first-hand. Both are worth having: the graduates can read an impact study, the divers can photograph what is on the seabed. Reported association activity includes a 500-METRE GHOST FISHING NET REFLOATED from the port basin at ORAN with the local fisheries directorate, coastal mobilisation by GREEN BIKE at ANNABA, and beach clean-ups by a national volunteering association at MOSTAGANEM. WHO IT SUITS: Algerians in any of the named wilayas, and coastal or urban communities needing a local association. CAVEATS: A THIRD-PARTY DIRECTORY of small volunteer associations — several entries lack a named president and some records are dated; confirm before relying on one. For the enquête publique register that opens a comment route, Algeria's public inquiry entry; for an advocate the bâtonnier MUST designate, the loi 13-07 entry; for a protected area created on the initiative of an APC president or wali, the loi 11-02 entry.

trackers.name: APEB at Béni-Isguen and the RADDO oasis network — an Algerian oasis-town association inside a Maghreb-and-Sahel network this file already holds the Moroccan end of, plus the national environmental training centre
trackers.desc: THE OASIS NETWORK THAT CROSSES THE BORDER: THE ASSOCIATION POUR LA PROTECTION DE L'ENVIRONNEMENT DE BÉNI-ISGUEN (APEB) IS PART OF THE RADDO NETWORK — AN INTERNATIONAL NETWORK OF ASSOCIATIONS ACTIVE IN THE MAGHREB AND THE SAHEL, FOR THE SAFEGUARD OF OASES AND THE PROMOTION OF SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT. This file already holds the Moroccan end of that same network at Tinjdad. So RADDO is not a listing — it is a working corridor between oasis associations in at least two countries, and a Saharan Algerian community facing the same water table, the same palm grove economy and the same pressure on collective land can reach people who have already argued the case next door. Ask APEB or the network for the association nearest your oasis, and ask what the Moroccan members did. Béni-Isguen sits in the M'Zab valley, so this is a town association in a historic oasis settlement rather than a capital-city NGO. Where a whole settlement is the heritage, the association that protects the environment and the association that protects the built fabric are often the same conversation — which is worth knowing before you decide which one to approach. THE TRAINING CENTRE, FILED AS BOTH RESOURCE AND CAUTION: ALGERIA HAS A CENTRE NATIONAL DE FORMATION ENVIRONNEMENTALE (CNFE), A NATIONAL CENTRE FOR ENVIRONMENTAL TRAINING WITH ITS OWN PUBLIC SITE — AND THE SAME RECORD NOTES PLAINLY THAT IT IS SPONSORED BY BIG INDUSTRY. A national training centre is where an Algerian association gets its people trained without paying a consultancy, and that is genuinely useful. But industrial sponsorship of the body that trains environmental practitioners is a fact to know before you sit in the room. Both things are true; take the training and keep your own counsel on the curriculum. ALSO RECORDED: a designated biosphere reserve in the Kabylie region near a named coastal town, and Algeria's responsibilities for climate and environment are described as split ACROSS VARIOUS ADMINISTRATIVE LEVELS. Responsibilities split across levels is the standing difficulty in Algeria: a wilaya answer and a national answer can differ. Get both in writing, and note this file's separate finding that a protected area can be created by decision of the wali — the level that decides is the level to lobby. AND A NOTE ON WHAT THIS ROUND FOUND: most of what a search returns for Algerian environmental associations is already in this file — the wilaya-by-wilaya directory, the Tipaza multidisciplinary association, the Tizi-Ouzou association created 2006, the Constantine association of young environmental graduates and specialists founded 2004, the Tiaret association and the divers' marine association. The two things NOT already held were the oasis network and the training centre, and this entry is those two rather than a repetition. If you are working in Algeria, the directory entry is the one to open first — it carries the president's name, postal address and stated activities for each association by wilaya, which is more contact detail than almost anything else in this file's North African record. WHO IT SUITS: Algerian oasis communities in the M'Zab and the south, associations needing training, and anyone wanting a cross-border counterpart. CAVEATS: A SMALL TOWN ASSOCIATION AND A STATE TRAINING CENTRE with industrial sponsorship — neither is a litigator. For the wilaya-by-wilaya directory with addresses and named presidents, Algeria's environmental associations by wilaya entry; for the advocate the bâtonnier MUST designate, the loi 13-07 entry; for a protected area created by decision of the wali, the loi 11-02 entry; for the public inquiry register a resident can open, the enquête publique entry; and for the Moroccan end of the oasis network, Morocco's AOFEP and RADDO entry.

trackers.name: The Environmental Justice Atlas — 2,100 community struggles searchable across 100 fields including commodity, company and outcome, with published inclusion criteria and an open invitation to submit your own case
trackers.desc: SEARCH BY COMMODITY, AND ADD YOUR OWN CASE — placement note first: THIS IS A GLOBAL REGISTER, FILED UNDER ALGERIA ONLY BECAUSE THIS FILE HAS NO GLOBAL KEY AND THIS BUCKET CARRIED NO CROSS-COUNTRY RESEARCH RESOURCE. IT IS REACHABLE FROM ANYWHERE. WHAT IT IS: AN ONLINE INTERACTIVE MAP THAT CATALOGUES LOCALIZED STORIES OF RESISTANCE AGAINST DAMAGING PROJECTS, FROM MINING TO OIL EXTRACTION TO PLANTATION FORESTRY — AND IT ALLOWS SEARCHING AND FILTERING ACROSS 100 FIELDS, INCLUDING INFORMATION ON COMMODITIES AND ACTORS, FORMS OF MOBILIZATION, OUTCOMES AND SOURCES. FILTER BY COMMODITY, ACTOR AND OUTCOME. That is the single most useful search a community can run: find every recorded case involving the same company, or the same mineral, and see what the people there did and whether it worked. This file has repeatedly noted that communities meet a company for the first time while that company has met a hundred communities. This is how you close some of that gap in an afternoon. THE SCALE: 2,100 CASES OF ECOLOGICAL DISTRIBUTION CONFLICTS, CAREFULLY CRAFTED BY A TEAM OF OVER 100 SCIENTISTS AND ACTIVISTS ALL OVER THE WORLD, AND DESCRIBED AS A REFERENCE FOR SCIENTISTS, JOURNALISTS, TEACHERS AND ACTIVISTS AND A VIRTUAL SPACE FOR INFORMATION, NETWORKING AND KNOWLEDGE SHARING. THE INCLUSION CRITERIA ARE PUBLISHED, SO YOU CAN TELL BEFORE YOU WRITE WHETHER YOUR CASE QUALIFIES: AN ECONOMIC ACTIVITY OR LEGISLATION WITH ACTUAL OR POTENTIAL NEGATIVE ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL OUTCOMES; A CLAIM AND MOBILISATION BY ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE ORGANISATION(S) THAT SUCH HARM OCCURRED OR IS LIKELY TO OCCUR AS A RESULT; AND REPORTING OF THAT PARTICULAR CONFLICT IN ONE OR MORE MEDIA STORIES. Three conditions, and the third is the one to act on first: at least one media story. If your struggle has never been reported anywhere, getting one article published is both the entry ticket here and a record that exists independently of you. And note POTENTIAL negative outcomes and harm that IS LIKELY TO OCCUR — a project that has not started yet still qualifies. THE OPEN DOOR: THE EDITORS INVITE ORGANIZATIONS AND ACADEMICS WITH EXPERTISE ON SPECIFIC ISSUES TO CONTRIBUTE TO THE FURTHER DEVELOPMENT OF THIS CONSTANTLY EXPANDING DATABASE — AND ALSO INVITE COLLABORATION IN THE CREATION OF FEATURED MAPS ON SPECIFIC ISSUES OF CONCERN. You can submit your own case, and you can propose a themed map. A featured map of every conflict over one commodity or one river basin is a campaign asset somebody else builds and hosts for you. AND AFRICA IS UNDER-REPRESENTED, WHICH IS AN OPENING: THE ATLAS IS INCREASING ITS REGISTERED CONFLICTS IN NAMED COUNTRIES WHICH UNTIL RECENTLY HAD NO LOCAL COLLABORATORS, INCLUDING EGYPT, ETHIOPIA AND THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF THE CONGO. NO LOCAL COLLABORATORS in large African countries. If you are in one of them, becoming the local collaborator is a real position — it puts your country's conflicts on a map that researchers, journalists and funders already read. THE LICENCE, WHICH MATTERS FOR ANYONE BUILDING THEIR OWN MATERIAL: THE DATA SET IS MADE AVAILABLE UNDER A CREATIVE COMMONS ATTRIBUTION-NONCOMMERCIAL-SHAREALIKE LICENCE — YOU ARE FREE TO USE THE WORK FOR NONCOMMERCIAL PURPOSES WITH ATTRIBUTION AND A LINK, AND RESULTING WORK MUST BE DISTRIBUTED UNDER THE SAME OR A SIMILAR LICENCE. Free to reuse for a community handbook, a school lesson or a submission, provided you credit it and share alike. That is rare among databases of this size and it removes the permission step entirely. ITS STATED PURPOSE INCLUDES THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST HERE: TO SERVE AS A VIRTUAL SPACE FOR THOSE WORKING ON THESE ISSUES TO GET INFORMATION, FIND OTHER GROUPS WORKING ON RELATED ISSUES, AND INCREASE THE VISIBILITY OF ENVIRONMENTAL CONFLICTS — AND TO MAKE THE CASE FOR TRUE CORPORATE AND STATE ACCOUNTABILITY. FIND OTHER GROUPS WORKING ON RELATED ISSUES. Every case entry names the organisations involved, which makes the atlas a directory of the people who have already fought your fight. THE FRAMING TO CARRY INTO ANY ARGUMENT: A MINE, A DAM, A ROAD IN THE FOREST ARE NOT ISOLATED OBJECTS BUT CONNECTED SITES ALONG WHICH VALUE FLOWS, ACCUMULATION OCCURS AND COSTS ARE EXTERNALIZED — AND AT EACH STAGE OF THE COMMODITY CHAIN, ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS ARE EXTERNALIZED ONTO THE MOST MARGINALIZED POPULATIONS, OFTEN FAR FROM THE EYES OF CONCERNED CITIZENS OR CONSUMERS OF THE END-PRODUCTS. The road is not a road; it is a link in a chain that ends in somebody's purchase. Naming the end consumer and the end market is how a local objection reaches people with leverage the local authority does not have. AND IT STANDS UP FOR PEOPLE PUBLICLY: the project has issued a public statement of support for activists receiving anonymous death threats, and has published research on women environmental defenders in a named African country. IT IS DIRECTED AT A NAMED UNIVERSITY ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCE INSTITUTE BY TWO NAMED CO-DIRECTORS AND COORDINATED BY A NAMED PERSON — people you can write to, not an anonymous portal. WHO IT SUITS: any African community facing a mine, dam, plantation, road or waste site, and anyone wanting to find who else fought the same company. CAVEATS: A RESEARCH DATABASE, NOT A FUNDER OR A LITIGATOR — and coverage is uneven, so absence from the map means nobody has filed it yet, not that nothing happened. For rapid response grants, Algeria's Urgent Action Fund–Africa entry; for the published directory of Algerian environmental associations by wilaya, that entry; for the advocate the bâtonnier must designate, the loi 13-07 entry.

trackers.name: PALU (Pan African Lawyers Union), Arusha — the continental lawyers' union whose Council is the presidents of 54 national bar associations — based in the same town as the African Court, training civil society alongside lawyers on extractives and infrastructure cases, with published fees and a postal address
trackers.desc: THE PRESIDENTS OF FIFTY-FOUR NATIONAL BARS SIT ON ONE COUNCIL — THE COUNCIL IS MADE UP OF THE PRESIDENTS OF THE FIVE REGIONAL AND FIFTY-FOUR NATIONAL LAWYERS' ASSOCIATIONS — BAR ASSOCIATIONS AND LAW SOCIETIES — AND IT MEETS AT LEAST ONCE EVERY YEAR. Every national bar on the continent, in one room, annually. This file has recorded over and over that the hard part is finding an advocate who will take a land case; the head of the body that licenses every advocate in your country sits on this council, and the council has a published address in Arusha. That is a route to the profession itself rather than to one lawyer. WHERE IT SITS, AND IT IS NOT AN ACCIDENT: A SECRETARIAT STRATEGICALLY LOCATED IN ARUSHA, TANZANIA, WHICH IS ALSO THE SEAT OF THE AFRICAN COURT ON HUMAN AND PEOPLES' RIGHTS AND THE AFRICAN UNION ADVISORY BOARD ON CORRUPTION, AMONGST OTHERS — WITH A FULL POSTAL ADDRESS PUBLISHED. The same town as the continental court whose land judgments this file records under Seychelles. A community pursuing that route has the court, a lawyers' union and a regional bar within walking distance of each other. THE TRAINING, AND THE SECOND HALF OF THE SENTENCE IS THE FIND: A SERIES OF REGIONAL SEMINARS AND COLLOQUIA ON THE AFRICAN LEGAL AND HUMAN RIGHTS SYSTEM, TO CAPACITATE LAWYERS AND CIVIL SOCIETY REPRESENTATIVES ON ENGAGING THE EMERGING HUMAN RIGHTS, GOVERNANCE AND PEACE AND SECURITY ARCHITECTURES — WITH A FURTHER SPECIAL FOCUS ON LITIGATION AT THE AFRICAN COURT ON HUMAN AND PEOPLES' RIGHTS AND THE EAST AFRICAN COURT OF JUSTICE. CIVIL SOCIETY REPRESENTATIVES sit in that training beside the lawyers. So somebody from a community organisation can learn how continental litigation actually works rather than being told about it afterwards — and this file's Togo entry records the same conversion happening to generalist lawyers. THE SUBJECT MATTER THEY TRAIN ON, WHICH IS THIS FILE'S SUBJECT: A SPECIAL FOCUS ON THE EXTRACTIVE INDUSTRY — MINERALS, OIL AND GAS — AND LARGE-SCALE INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS, ALONGSIDE COMPLEX INTERNATIONAL COMMERCIAL TRANSACTIONS AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION, BOTH LITIGATION AND ARBITRATION, AND VULTURE FUNDS. ARBITRATION is the word to notice. When a state is sued by an investor over a cancelled concession, the case is decided in arbitration, not in your courts, and communities are almost never represented there. African lawyers are being trained in it — ask whether anyone in your country has been. THE MEMBERSHIP AND ITS PRICE, PUBLISHED: A DUAL MEMBERSHIP FORUM FOR INDIVIDUAL AFRICAN LAWYERS AND FOR LAWYERS' ASSOCIATIONS — WITH INSTITUTIONAL MEMBERSHIP FOR BAR ASSOCIATIONS AND LAW SOCIETIES FROM ACROSS AFRICA AND ITS DIASPORA AT AN ANNUAL FEE OF $1,000 TO $2,000, DETERMINED BY THE SIZE OF THE ASSOCIATION. IT BRINGS TOGETHER THE CONTINENT'S REGIONAL AND NATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS AND OVER 1,000 INDIVIDUAL LAWYERS. AND THE DECISION BEHIND THE FEE, WHICH SHOWS INTENT: WE HAVE LOWERED OUR INSTITUTIONAL MEMBERSHIP FEES, TO BE MORE RESPONSIVE TO THE DIFFERENCES IN SIZE AND FINANCIAL SITUATION OF AFRICAN LAWYERS' ASSOCIATIONS — WHILE THIS LOWERS OUR INCOME IN THE SHORT TERM, IT ATTRACTS MORE INSTITUTIONAL MEMBERS TO BE ACTIVE. A body that cut its own income to let poorer bars participate. That is worth knowing when your national association claims it cannot afford to engage continentally. THE LANGUAGE OUTREACH, WHICH MATTERS FOR HALF THIS FILE: SPECIAL CAMPAIGNS TO ARAB-, FRENCH- AND PORTUGUESE-SPEAKING CONSTITUENCIES, WHICH ULTIMATELY LED MORE BAR ASSOCIATIONS TO BE ACTIVE, INCLUDING NOMINATING AND VOTING FOR CANDIDATES FOR ELECTION INTO THE BOARD. Francophone, lusophone and Arabic-speaking bars were deliberately brought in and now vote. If your country's bar is not active, that is a gap somebody is already trying to close. IT LITIGATES IN ITS OWN NAME: IT HAS BROUGHT A CASE AS NAMED APPLICANT AGAINST AN ATTORNEY GENERAL AND MINISTER OF JUSTICE BEFORE THE EAST AFRICAN COURT OF JUSTICE, AND ENGAGES WITH REGIONAL AND CONTINENTAL COURTS THROUGH STRATEGIC LITIGATION. A lawyers' union willing to be the applicant itself. This file's Seychelles entry records the same arrangement from a different angle: an organisation putting its own name on the claim beside the community's, so the community is not the only one exposed. THE POLICY OUTPUT: IT REGULARLY DEVELOPS POLICY MEMORANDA, STATEMENTS AND LEGAL ANALYSES THAT INFORM AFRICAN UNION ORGANS, REGIONAL COURTS AND OTHER STAKEHOLDERS — AND HAS NEGOTIATED A MODEL LAW ON UNIVERSAL JURISDICTION AND WORKED ON AN AFRICAN TRANSITIONAL JUSTICE POLICY FRAMEWORK. AND THE REGIONAL BAR ALONGSIDE IT: A REGIONAL BAR ASSOCIATION OF EAST AFRICA, FORMED IN 1995, WITH OVER 42,000 MEMBERS AND A PUBLISHED ARUSHA ADDRESS. Forty-two thousand lawyers in one regional association. Somewhere in that number is an advocate who will take your case — and a regional body is easier to write to than a national one that has already refused you. WHO IT SUITS: African community organisations that cannot find counsel, and national coalitions wanting their own bar association engaged on land, extractives and infrastructure. CAVEATS: A PROFESSIONAL MEMBERSHIP BODY, NOT A LEGAL AID SERVICE — it will not represent a village directly; the route is your national bar or a member lawyer. For pro bono counsel already carrying a hundred community cases a year, Togo's entry; for a co-complainant before the continental court, Seychelles' entry; for university law clinics as free representation, Comoros' entry.

trackers.name: They put a community's allegation directly to company headquarters and publish the reply — or the silence — then invite the community to answer back, with researchers based in Kenya, Senegal and South Africa and a site in Arabic, French and Portuguese
trackers.desc: THEY PUT YOUR ALLEGATION TO HEAD OFFICE AND PUBLISH THE SILENCE — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S ANGOLA ENTRY COVERS THE BANK CAMPAIGNING ORGANISATION THAT FEATURES PROJECTS BEFORE FINANCIERS, ITS CAPE VERDE ENTRY THE CENTRE THAT FILES ACCOUNTABILITY COMPLAINTS, ITS DJIBOUTI ENTRY THE COMPLAINT-OFFICE SCORING NETWORK, ITS BENIN ENTRY THE FOLLOW-THE-MONEY RESEARCH SERVICE, AND ITS KENYA ENTRY A GRASSROOTS JUSTICE NETWORK OF WHICH THIS ORGANISATION IS A MEMBER. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE MECHANISM, AND IT IS THE FIND: SINCE 2005 IT HAS APPROACHED COMPANY HEADQUARTERS OVER 2,800 TIMES SEEKING A PUBLIC RESPONSE TO ALLEGATIONS RAISED BY COMMUNITIES, CIVIL SOCIETY AND THE MEDIA — TAKING UP ALLEGED ABUSE QUICKLY AND DIRECTLY WITH COMPANIES, AT OVER 1,500 INVITATIONS TO RESPOND PER YEAR. A letter from a village reaches a subsidiary's local manager. A letter from this organisation reaches head office, and the company knows the answer will be published. That is the cheapest escalation in this file — no lawyer, no filing fee, no forum — and QUICKLY is the word that distinguishes it from every complaint route here that takes years. THE PUBLICATION RULE: IT WILL ALWAYS PUBLISH ANY RESPONSE RECEIVED FROM THE COMPANY IN FULL — AND IT RECORDS BOTH RESPONSES AND NON-RESPONSES, WITH THE RECORD PUBLISHED. NON-RESPONSES RECORDED. A company that ignores the question has created a permanent public entry saying so, which is often worth more than an answer — and it is citable to a financier, a buyer or a national contact point later. THE REJOINDER RIGHT, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: IT UPDATES COMPLAINANTS ON DEVELOPMENTS AND INVITES THEM TO ISSUE REJOINDERS TO COMPANY RESPONSES — THE ALLEGATIONS AND RESPONSES POSTED ARE MEANT TO BE SCRUTINISED NOT JUST BY THE PARTIES INVOLVED BUT BY THE WIDER BUSINESS AND HUMAN RIGHTS COMMUNITY. The community gets the last word, in public, beside the company's statement. This file has recorded consultation records in which the company's account is the only one that survives; here both are posted and the rebuttal is invited. WHY IT MATTERS: COMMUNITIES AND WORKERS AFFECTED BY CORPORATE HUMAN RIGHTS ABUSE FACE HUGE BARRIERS IN ACCESSING JUSTICE AND REMEDY — AND THIS CAN BE AN IMPORTANT FIRST STEP TO INCREASE TRANSPARENCY, DIALOGUE AND PUBLIC ACCOUNTABILITY, AND AN OPPORTUNITY TO RAISE HUMAN RIGHTS ISSUES WITH COMPANIES, OFTEN BEYOND THE WELL-RECOGNISED BRANDS. BEYOND THE WELL-RECOGNISED BRANDS. The obscure holding company operating the concession is reachable here even though no consumer campaign would ever touch it. THE FOLLOW-UP COMMITMENT: IT SYSTEMATICALLY FOLLOWS UP ON COMPANY RESPONSES, PURSUING COMPANIES THAT FAIL TO RESPOND ADEQUATELY TO ALLEGATIONS OF EGREGIOUS ABUSE. THE ESCALATION IT WILL SOMETIMES DO, AND THE CASE IS WORTH READING: OCCASIONALLY IT TAKES AN ACTIVE ROLE IN SUPPORTING COMMUNITIES AND NGOs — IN ONE CASE SUPPORTING GROUPS WORKING TO FREE AN INDIGENOUS COMMUNITY LEADER AND ENVIRONMENTAL RIGHTS DEFENDER SENTENCED TO FIVE YEARS IN PRISON AND A LARGE FINE AFTER LEADING OPPOSITION TO A PROPOSED MINE IN HIS COMMUNITY'S TERRITORY: IT POSTED THE ALLEGATIONS, SOUGHT RESPONSES FROM TWO COMPANIES WHO DID NOT RESPOND, AND ASSISTED THE LOCAL VILLAGERS IN SUBMITTING THE CASE TO A UN SPECIAL REPRESENTATIVE ON HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS. A leader jailed on fraud and bribery charges after opposing a mine — the pattern this file has recorded from Uganda to Tanzania. Note the sequence: allegations posted, companies asked and silent, then help filing to a UN special procedure. That is a three-step ladder a community can follow, and the second step costs nothing but the request. THE AFRICAN RESEARCHERS, NAMED BY LOCATION: REGIONAL RESEARCHERS BASED IN KENYA, SENEGAL AND SOUTH AFRICA, AMONG OTHER COUNTRIES — WORKING WITH LOCAL COMMUNITIES TO UNDERSTAND THE IMPACTS OF BUSINESSES ON THE GROUND, AND REGULARLY TALKING WITH BUSINESSPEOPLE AND GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS. Three African bases, one francophone. A researcher in Dakar is a nearer and more reachable contact for West African communities than a London office, and reaching them is how an allegation gets taken up. THE LANGUAGES: FULL NAVIGATION AND HOMEPAGES IN SEVERAL LANGUAGES INCLUDING ARABIC, ENGLISH, FRENCH AND PORTUGUESE — REPORTED VARIOUSLY AS SEVEN, EIGHT AND TEN LANGUAGES ACROSS SOURCES. Arabic, French and Portuguese all covered. North, West and lusophone African communities can read and submit without translation, which this file has repeatedly recorded as the barrier that stops everything else. THE COMPANY COVERAGE: TRACKING THE HUMAN RIGHTS POLICY AND PERFORMANCE OF COMPANIES IN OVER 180 COUNTRIES — REPORTED AS OVER 6,000, OVER 9,000, MORE THAN 10,000 AND OVER 20,000 ACROSS SOURCES OF DIFFERENT DATES — WITH COMPANY PAGES AND DASHBOARDS HIGHLIGHTING ALLEGATIONS, FINANCIAL INFORMATION, KEY DATA POINTS BASED ON CORPORATE POLICIES, AND SCORES FROM PROMINENT CIVIL SOCIETY BENCHMARKS. Look up the company on your land before the first meeting. A page listing what it has been accused of elsewhere, with its own responses, changes what a community knows walking into a negotiation. THE STANDING IT HAS BEEN GIVEN: A UN SPECIAL REPRESENTATIVE OBSERVED THAT, IN THE ABSENCE OF A UNIVERSAL DATABASE THAT STORES ALLEGATIONS OF ABUSE, ITS ONLINE LIBRARY IS THE MOST COMPREHENSIVE, OBJECTIVE SOURCE AVAILABLE — AND USED ITS CORPORATE RESPONSE DATABASE TO OBTAIN AN OVERVIEW OF PATTERNS OF CORPORATE IMPACT ON HUMAN RIGHTS. An entry here is read by the UN machinery. That is why getting your case posted matters beyond the company's reply. THE FREE SUBSCRIPTION AND ITS AUDIENCE: A FREE WEEKLY UPDATE E-NEWSLETTER WITH OVER 16,000 SUBSCRIBERS INCLUDING ADVOCATES, ACTIVISTS, BUSINESSPEOPLE, GOVERNMENTS, INVESTORS AND THE UN — WITH THE WEBSITE VISITED BY OVER 177,000 PEOPLE EVERY MONTH. AND THE PRIORITY PROGRAMMES: LABOUR RIGHTS; JUST ENERGY TRANSITION; ACCOUNTABLE DIGITAL TECHNOLOGIES; CORPORATE LEGAL ACCOUNTABILITY; AND CIVIC FREEDOMS AND HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS. JUST ENERGY TRANSITION as a standing programme. Transition-mineral mines and renewable projects on community land fall inside a named priority, not a stretch — which matters given how many such projects this file records arriving now. WHO IT SUITS: African communities with a documented allegation against a company, especially where the operator is obscure and no lawyer or forum is yet available. CAVEATS: IT SEEKS A RESPONSE AND PUBLISHES IT — IT CANNOT COMPEL, AWARD REMEDY OR REPRESENT YOU — and taking an active role beyond that is occasional. For the organisation that files complaints on communities' behalf, Cape Verde's entry; for scoring which complaint office to use, Djibouti's entry; for featuring your project before bankers, Angola's entry.

trackers.name: Grassroots International — a grantmaker with a dedicated West Africa resource-rights fund, whose three published grant categories are seeds and tools, movement building, and legal aid for the inevitable clashes with power
trackers.desc: ONE OF THREE GRANT CATEGORIES IS LEGAL AID FOR WHEN YOU CLASH WITH POWER — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S SENEGAL ENTRY NAMES A LAND COALITION; ITS LIBERIA ENTRY A TENURE FACILITY AND A LAND COALITION HOST; ITS DJIBOUTI, CAMEROON, REPUBLIC OF CONGO, COMOROS AND CÔTE D'IVOIRE ENTRIES THE OTHER FUNDERS ADDED IN THIS RUN; AND THIS BUCKET ALREADY CARRIES A RAPID-RESPONSE WOMEN'S FUND NAME AND AN ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE ATLAS HOST. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. THE THIRD GRANT CATEGORY, WHICH IS THE FIND: GRANTS FOR DEFENDING HUMAN RIGHTS, TO PROTECT THE CIVIL AND POLITICAL RIGHTS OF ACTIVISTS, AND TO PROVIDE LEGAL AID DURING THE INEVITABLE CLASHES WITH POWER THAT ACTIVISTS EVERYWHERE MUST ENDURE. THE INEVITABLE CLASHES. A funder that budgets for the arrest, the injunction and the fabricated charge as a normal cost of the work rather than as a project failure. This file has recorded organisation after organisation discovering that its grant cannot pay a lawyer; here that is one of three standing categories, written in advance. THE WEST AFRICAN FUND, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: THE FUND TO ADVANCE RESOURCE RIGHTS IN WEST AFRICA SUPPORTS GRASSROOTS ORGANIZATIONS AND SOCIAL MOVEMENTS IN WEST AFRICA THAT ADVANCE RESOURCE RIGHTS. A named regional fund for one part of Africa, on exactly this file's subject. West African organisations should ask about it by name rather than approaching the global programme. THE OTHER TWO CATEGORIES: SUSTAINABLE LIVELIHOOD GRANTS, WHICH PROVIDE SEEDS AND TOOLS AND OTHER BASICS NECESSARY FOR DIGNIFIED LIVELIHOODS AND COMMUNITY-LED DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS; AND MOVEMENT BUILDING GRANTS, WHICH NURTURE LEADERSHIP — ESPECIALLY AMONG WOMEN AND YOUTH — AND HELP PARTNERS ORGANIZE, ADVOCATE, AND COMMUNICATE WITH THEIR CONSTITUENTS, THEIR GOVERNMENTS, AND THE WORLD AT LARGE. SEEDS AND TOOLS is unusually concrete for a rights funder. A community holding its land also has to eat off it, and the two grants can run together — which is the combination the unconditional cash entry filed under Côte d'Ivoire argues for on different reasoning. WHAT IT SAYS IT FUNDS: LAND, WATER AND FOOD AS HUMAN RIGHTS, AND NOURISHING THE POLITICAL STRUGGLE NECESSARY TO ACHIEVE THESE RIGHTS — CONNECTING WITH GLOBAL MOVEMENTS THAT DEFEND LAND, TERRITORY, WATER, FOOD, SEEDS, AND THE EARTH. THE POLITICAL STRUGGLE, named as the thing being funded. Most funders in this file describe outcomes and avoid the word; an organisation whose work is plainly political does not have to disguise it here. WHO IT FUNDS: SOCIAL MOVEMENTS, MADE UP OF PEOPLE ORGANIZED COLLECTIVELY WITH LEADERSHIP FROM IMPACTED COMMUNITIES — WHICH IT DESCRIBES AS THE DRIVING FORCE BEHIND TRANSFORMATION — ACCOMPANYING, FUNDING AND WORKING IN SOLIDARITY WITH MOVEMENTS PREDOMINANTLY IN THE GLOBAL SOUTH. LEADERSHIP FROM IMPACTED COMMUNITIES is the test. An organisation run from a capital city on behalf of a district is the weaker candidate here; the committee from the affected village is the stronger one. THE NAME IT GIVES ITS MODEL: WE PARTNER WITH MOVEMENTS THROUGH AN APPROACH WE CALL SOLIDARITY PHILANTHROPY — AN EVOLVING FRAMEWORK BUILT ON PRINCIPLES AND PRACTICES INFORMED BY THE SOCIAL MOVEMENTS WE ACCOMPANY. WHAT IT DOES BESIDES GRANTING: STANDING UP WITH MOVEMENTS TO WIN DEMANDS, SHIFT POLICY, AND DEFEND COMMUNITIES; AND PROMOTING A BOLDER POLITIC IN PHILANTHROPY TO MOBILIZE MORE RESOURCES FOR SOCIAL MOVEMENTS. It lobbies other funders on your behalf. An organisation it backs gains an advocate inside philanthropy, which is worth as much over time as the grant. THE AFRICAN ORGANISING IT POINTS TO: A WEST AFRICAN CARAVAN FOR THE RIGHT TO LAND AND WATER — WITH THE LINE THAT LAND IS NEVER JUST LAND; IT IS FOOD, LIVELIHOOD AND MORE. A regional caravan is a tactic as well as an event: organisations along a route meet, and the travelling itself is the organising. Worth knowing it exists and has been funded. ITS EAST AFRICAN AND LIBERATION ROOTS: EARLY WORK ON FAMINE RESPONSE IN EAST AFRICA INVOLVED GETTING SEEDS, LIVESTOCK, AND TOOLS DIRECTLY INTO PEOPLE'S HANDS, AND IT SUPPORTED NATIONAL LIBERATION MOVEMENTS IN WHICH STRUGGLES OVER LAND AND TERRITORY WERE CENTRAL — INCLUDING MOVEMENTS IN SOUTH AFRICA IN ITS EARLY YEARS. THE PEASANT NETWORK IT HAS FUNDED SINCE 1996: ITS FIRST GRANT TO A GLOBAL PEASANT MOVEMENT WAS MADE THE SAME YEAR THAT MOVEMENT LAUNCHED FOOD SOVEREIGNTY ON THE WORLD STAGE — AN INTERNATIONAL ADVOCACY NETWORK OF SMALL-PRODUCER ORGANISATIONS REPRESENTING OVER 150 MILLION FARMERS, FISHERS, FORESTERS AND AGRICULTURAL WORKERS ON FIVE CONTINENTS, COMPOSED OF SMALL FARMERS, FISHERS, CONSUMERS, ENVIRONMENTALISTS AND INDIGENOUS PEOPLES ALL SEEKING TO DEFINE THEIR OWN AGRICULTURAL, LABOUR, FISHING, FOOD AND LAND POLICIES. A hundred and fifty million members across five continents, and an African farmers' organisation can affiliate to it directly. That is a route to standing and to allies that costs nothing but the application — and this funder has resourced its operations at national level, so membership and funding travel together. WHAT ITS SUPPORT OF THAT NETWORK CONSISTED OF: SUPPORT OF ITS OPERATIONS AT THE GLOBAL, REGIONAL AND NATIONAL LEVELS; PARTNERSHIP WITH MANY OF ITS MEMBER ORGANISATIONS; AND ACCOMPANIMENT IN COMMUNICATIONS, ADVOCACY, AND THE EXPANSION OF ITS DONOR BASE. EXPANSION OF ITS DONOR BASE — helping a partner find other funders. Ask for that explicitly; it is the thing that outlasts any single grant. AND THE DEFINITION IT WORKS FROM: FOOD SOVEREIGNTY IS THE RIGHT OF PEOPLES TO HEALTHY AND CULTURALLY APPROPRIATE FOOD PRODUCED THROUGH ECOLOGICALLY SOUND AND SUSTAINABLE METHODS, AND THEIR RIGHT TO DEFINE THEIR OWN FOOD AND AGRICULTURE SYSTEMS — WITH ITS PARTNERSHIP MODEL GROUNDED IN GRANTMAKING AND ACCOMPANYING MOVEMENTS SINCE 1983. WHO IT SUITS: West and East African farmers' movements, community organisations and land committees — especially those facing prosecution alongside the land fight. CAVEATS: IT ACCOMPANIES A SELECTED SET OF MOVEMENT PARTNERS RATHER THAN RUNNING OPEN CALLS, AND ITS DEEPEST PROGRAMMES ARE OUTSIDE AFRICA — the named West Africa fund is the door to ask about. For a funder with a phone number and no form, Djibouti's entry; for the advisor-nominated route, Cameroon's entry; for legal costs specifically, this file's South Africa entry.

trackers.name: NANHRI (Network of African National Human Rights Institutions), Nairobi — the continental network of the 47 state human rights commissions that must handle complaints and conduct investigations — with published work on access to remedy, on small-scale fishers in coastal governance, and a warning about one member's independence
trackers.desc: THERE IS A STATE BODY IN YOUR OWN CAPITAL THAT MUST TAKE COMPLAINTS — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S DJIBOUTI ENTRY NAMES NATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS INSTITUTIONS AS BODIES THE WEST AFRICAN DEFENDERS NETWORK WORKS THROUGH, WITHOUT IDENTIFYING THIS NETWORK OR SHIPPING ITS HOST; ITS CAPE VERDE AND DJIBOUTI BUCKETS CARRY A CONTINENTAL DEFENDERS HOST. NONE IS RESTATED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS RUN ON THE HOST ACTUALLY BEING SHIPPED, NOT MERELY ON A SEARCH TERM — THE CORRECTION RECORDED LAST ROUND. WHAT THESE BODIES CAN ACTUALLY DO, WHICH IS THE FIND: NATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS INSTITUTIONS ARE BODIES ESTABLISHED BY GOVERNMENTS TO AID IN PROMOTION AND PROTECTION OF HUMAN RIGHTS WITHIN THEIR RESPECTIVE JURISDICTIONS THROUGH HANDLING COMPLAINTS AND CONDUCTING INVESTIGATIONS, CONDUCTING RESEARCH, ADVOCACY AND EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMMES. HANDLING COMPLAINTS AND CONDUCTING INVESTIGATIONS, as a statutory duty, in your own capital, in your own language, at no cost. Almost every resource in this file is foreign, distant and selective; this one is domestic and obliged. A community that has never considered filing with its national commission is overlooking the nearest body with investigative powers. HOW MANY THERE ARE: IN OPERATION SINCE 2007, WITH 47 MEMBERS DRAWN FROM NATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS INSTITUTIONS ACROSS AFRICA — ONE OF FOUR REGIONAL GROUPINGS WITHIN A GLOBAL ALLIANCE OF SUCH INSTITUTIONS. Forty-seven, so the presumption is that your country has one. The network's member list is where to find its name. THE ACCREDITATION CLASSES, WHICH DECIDE HOW MUCH WEIGHT YOURS CARRIES: FULL MEMBERS AT CLASS A, ASSOCIATE MEMBERS AT CLASS B, MEMBERS AT CLASS C, AND SUSPENDED MEMBERS — WITH CLASS A INSTITUTIONS DEEMED FULLY COMPLIANT WITH THE INTERNATIONAL PRINCIPLES. Check your own commission's class before relying on it. Class A means independently accredited; a lower class or a suspension is a published signal that the body may not be independent of the government you are complaining about — and that is knowable in advance rather than discovered after filing. THE LITIGATION POWER IT DOCUMENTS, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: AMONG THE FUNCTIONS THESE INSTITUTIONS HAVE IS THE POTENTIAL TO TAKE ACTION AT THE NATIONAL LEVEL INCLUDING THROUGH LITIGATION — WITH A PUBLISHED BASELINE STUDY CONSIDERING THE NATIONAL-LEVEL LITIGATION ACTIVITIES THEY CAN UNDERTAKE. A national commission can litigate. For a community that cannot afford counsel and cannot meet a legal aid means test, persuading the state's own human rights body to bring or join the case is a route this file has not recorded elsewhere — and there is a published study of which commissions have the capacity. THE MONITORING ROLE AND THE GUIDELINES FOR IT: AFRICAN TREATY BODIES ISSUE CONCLUDING OBSERVATIONS SETTING OUT ACTION THE STATE SHOULD TAKE, AND NATIONAL ACTORS PLAY AN IMPORTANT ROLE IN MONITORING WHAT ACTION STATES HAVE TAKEN — SO IN 2016 THE NETWORK ADOPTED GUIDELINES FOR THESE INSTITUTIONS IN MONITORING SUCH DECISIONS. This is the implementation half that this file has repeatedly recorded missing: continental judgments won and then ignored. The domestic commission is the body formally tasked with chasing them, and there are guidelines telling it how. THE PUBLISHED WORK CLOSEST TO THIS FILE'S SUBJECT: A PROJECT BRIEF ON ACCESS TO REMEDY IN A NAMED COUNTRY'S JUST TRANSITION, UNDER A CORPORATE ACCOUNTABILITY, RESILIENCE AND PARTICIPATION PROJECT — AND PUBLISHED WORK ON THE ROLE OF THESE INSTITUTIONS IN PROMOTING THE MEANINGFUL PARTICIPATION OF SMALL-SCALE FISHERS IN MARINE AND COASTAL RESOURCE GOVERNANCE AND CONSERVATION. Small-scale fishers and coastal resource governance, addressed directly to what a national commission can do about it. Read beside the fishers' co-operative litigation filed under Mali: the same fight, approached through the state's own rights body. THE BUSINESS AND HUMAN RIGHTS STRAND: A PEER EXCHANGE ON THE EFFECTIVE DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF NATIONAL ACTION PLANS ON BUSINESS AND HUMAN RIGHTS IN AFRICA. A national action plan on business and human rights is a government document that commits the state on how companies must behave. Where one exists or is being drafted, the commission is the body shaping it — and community input goes in there. THE FREE DOCUMENT LIBRARY IT RUNS: AN ONLINE CENTRE COMPILING DOCUMENTATION FROM REGIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS MECHANISMS — ACTIVITY REPORTS PLUS SELECT REPORTS, DECISIONS AND COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE AFRICAN COMMISSION, THE AFRICAN CHILDREN'S RIGHTS COMMITTEE, THE AFRICAN COURT, AND A WEST AFRICAN ECONOMIC COMMUNITY. Decisions and communications from four continental mechanisms in one searchable place, free. That is where a national lawyer finds the precedent, and it includes the West African economic community's court — a forum this file has otherwise barely touched. THE ROUTE IT BUILT INTO THE CONTINENTAL COMMISSION: GUIDELINES FOR REPORTING BY THESE INSTITUTIONS TO THE AFRICAN COMMISSION HAVE BEEN DEVELOPED, FINALISED AND CIRCULATED FOR ONWARD USE — WITH CONSULTATIVE MEETINGS AT THE MARGINS OF ORDINARY SESSIONS. Your national commission has a standing channel into the African Commission. A community that persuades it to report on their situation reaches the continental body without holding observer status itself. THE TRAINING IT HAS ORGANISED: A TRAINING WORKSHOP FOR AFRICAN INSTITUTIONS RUN WITH A NAMED FOUNDATION'S JUSTICE INITIATIVE AND A UNIVERSITY HUMAN RIGHTS IMPLEMENTATION CENTRE. WHAT IT SAYS ABOUT ITS OWN MEMBERS' WEAKNESS: INDEPENDENT, WELL CAPACITATED AND RESOURCED INSTITUTIONS ARE KEY TO A STRONG AND EFFECTIVE NATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS SYSTEM — AND IT CALLS ON THE CONTINENTAL COMMISSION AND LIKE-MINDED STAKEHOLDERS TO STRENGTHEN THEIR SUPPORT FOR AFRICAN INSTITUTIONS IN EVERY WAY POSSIBLE. AND THE INDEPENDENCE WARNING IT PUBLISHES ABOUT A NAMED MEMBER: A PRESS STATEMENT RECORDING CONCERNS OVER THE INDEPENDENCE OF A NAMED NATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS COMMISSION FOLLOWING THE RE-ASSIGNMENT OF ITS CHAIRPERSON. The network publicly criticises its own members when a government interferes with them. That is both a reason to trust the accreditation classes above and a warning: a commission can be captured between the time you file and the time it reports. WHO IT SUITS: African communities and organisations who have not yet used their own national human rights commission — for complaints, investigations, and a domestic route into the continental bodies. CAVEATS: THIS IS THE COORDINATING NETWORK, NOT A COMPLAINTS BODY — YOU FILE WITH YOUR OWN COUNTRY'S INSTITUTION, WHOSE INDEPENDENCE AND CAPACITY VARY AND ARE PUBLISHED AS ACCREDITATION CLASSES; SOME MEMBERS ARE SUSPENDED. For the West African defenders network that works through these institutions, Djibouti's entry; for the fishers' co-operative litigation route, Mali's entry.

trackers.name: Alkarama, Geneva — files pro bono before the UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention, the only non-treaty UN body that decides individual complaints from anyone anywhere, on a published questionnaire in English, French and Spanish
trackers.desc: ONE UN BODY DECIDES INDIVIDUAL CASES FROM ANYWHERE — AND A FOUNDATION FILES FOR FREE — method and adjacency declared first: SEVENTH NAMED-ATTORNEY ROUND. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THREE HOSTS AND SIX DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL HOSTS AND FOUR FACTS ABSENT, WITH TWO GENERIC PHRASES IN OTHER ENTRIES ON OTHER HOSTS. THIS FILE'S REPUBLIC OF CONGO ENTRY COVERS THE 24/7 DEFENDER HELPLINE, ITS CAMEROON ENTRY THE BODY DEFENDING HARASSED LAWYERS, AND ITS BURUNDI ENTRY COUNSEL IN THE FIRST HOURS. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE MECHANISM AND WHY IT IS DIFFERENT, WHICH IS THE FIND: THE WORKING GROUP ON ARBITRARY DETENTION IS UNIQUE IN THAT ITS MANDATE EXPRESSLY PROVIDES FOR THE CONSIDERATION OF INDIVIDUAL COMPLAINTS, AND IS THE ONLY NON-TREATY-BASED UN HUMAN RIGHTS MECHANISM TO INVESTIGATE AND DECIDE INDIVIDUAL COMPLAINTS — INDIVIDUALS ANYWHERE IN THE WORLD ARE THEREFORE ABLE TO PETITION IT. NON-TREATY-BASED is the whole point. Every other route recorded in this file depends on which conventions your government has signed and whether it accepted individual complaints; this one does not. A defender detained in a state that has ratified nothing can still be petitioned for. That makes it the widest-open door in these 1,038 entries. WHO MAY FILE, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: COMMUNICATIONS MAY BE SUBMITTED BY THE INDIVIDUALS CONCERNED, THEIR FAMILIES, THEIR REPRESENTATIVES OR NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS — WITH A PUBLISHED MODEL QUESTIONNAIRE IN ENGLISH, FRENCH AND SPANISH, TO BE FILLED IN AND SUBMITTED PREFERABLY BY EMAIL, AND A PUBLISHED POSTAL ADDRESS AT THE UN OFFICE AT GENEVA. THE FAMILY may file, on a form, by email. No lawyer, no accreditation, no fee. A wife with the questionnaire and an internet cafe can begin the process herself — which is the answer where this file has recorded detained defenders whose organisations could not reach them. THE TWO PROCEDURES IT RUNS: URGENT APPEALS, AND COMMUNICATIONS UNDER ITS REGULAR PROCEDURE, SENT TO CONCERNED GOVERNMENTS TO CLARIFY OR BRING THEIR ATTENTION TO THESE CASES. The urgent track exists separately. Where someone has just been taken and the risk is immediate, that is the one to name in the submission. THE TEST IT APPLIES: IT MUST DISTINGUISH BETWEEN LAWFUL EXERCISE OF POLICE POWER, AND DETENTION SO LACKING IN LAWFUL BASIS OR OTHERWISE UNREASONABLE THAT IT MUST BE CONSIDERED ARBITRARY. Knowing the test tells you what to put in the form: not that the arrest was unjust, but that it lacked lawful basis or was unreasonable. This file's Seychelles entry records that 99% of one country's evictions never saw a court — the same absence of lawful basis is what this body is looking for. THE ORGANISATION THAT FILES FOR PEOPLE, AND WHAT IT COSTS: A FOUNDATION THAT BRINGS PRO BONO LEGAL ASSISTANCE TO VICTIMS OF THE MOST SERIOUS HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS, WITHOUT ANY DISCRIMINATION — FOCUSING ON EXTRAJUDICIAL EXECUTIONS, ENFORCED DISAPPEARANCES, TORTURE AND ARBITRARY DETENTION. PRO BONO, WITHOUT ANY DISCRIMINATION. Four violation types only, which is a narrow door but an open one, and a land defender who has been disappeared or tortured is squarely inside it. HOW IT WORKS A CASE: IT DOCUMENTS INDIVIDUAL CASES THROUGH DIRECT CONTACT WITH THE VICTIMS, THEIR FAMILIES OR LAWYERS, AND SUBMITS COMPLAINTS ON THEIR BEHALF TO THE UN SPECIAL PROCEDURES AND TREATY BODIES — WORKING CLOSELY WITH THE OFFICE OF THE UN HIGH COMMISSIONER FOR HUMAN RIGHTS. WHO MANDATES IT: IN ONE NORTH AFRICAN CASE IT ACTED MANDATED BY THE DETAINED ACTIVIST'S FAMILY, DEMONSTRATING THAT THE DETENTION CONSTITUTED AN ARBITRARY DEPRIVATION OF LIBERTY SOLELY MOTIVATED BY HER PEACEFUL EXERCISE OF THE RIGHT TO FREEDOM OF EXPRESSION AND HER CIVIC ENGAGEMENT. MANDATED BY THE FAMILY is the practical route in: the detainee cannot instruct anyone, so the family does. Worth knowing before a detention happens, because afterwards nobody is thinking clearly. THE FACTS THAT CASE TURNED ON: SHE WAS ABDUCTED IN THE STREET BY PLAINCLOTHES POLICE OFFICERS WITHOUT A WARRANT OR EXPLANATION, AND HER DETENTION WAS ONLY ACKNOWLEDGED 24 HOURS LATER. No warrant, and 24 hours before the state admitted holding her. Both facts are the kind a family can record contemporaneously — note the hour, the place, the absence of a warrant, the time acknowledgement came. That contemporaneous note is the submission's spine. WHAT IT PUBLISHES AFTERWARDS, AND WHY: IT SHARES THE VICTIMS' STORIES AND THE RECOMMENDATIONS ISSUED BY THE UN MECHANISMS ON THEIR CASES — AND ALL OF THESE MECHANISMS ISSUE RECOMMENDATIONS WHICH CAN IN TURN BE USED BY LOCAL CIVIL SOCIETY TO LOBBY FOR THEIR IMPLEMENTATION. The output is a document a local coalition can then campaign on. A UN finding does not free anyone by itself; it gives the people at home something with a stamp on it. THE VOLUME ONE PERSON ACHIEVED: BETWEEN 2004 AND 2007 ITS THEN SOLE EMPLOYEE SUBMITTED AROUND 400 INDIVIDUAL CASES TO THE UN SPECIAL PROCEDURES, PROMPTING THEM TO ENGAGE WITH A NUMBER OF STATES, WHICH LED TO A NOTICEABLE IMPROVEMENT OF THE SITUATION FOR MANY OF THE VICTIMS. Four hundred cases, one employee, three years. That is the clearest evidence in this file that the barrier to these mechanisms is knowledge rather than capacity — the filing itself is not expensive. THE STRONGER PROCEDURE IT REACHES FOR WHERE IT EXISTS: BY FILING WITH THE COMMITTEE ON THE RIGHTS OF PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES IT REFERRED A CASE TO THE STRONGEST PROCEDURE AVAILABLE AT UN LEVEL, BECAUSE THAT STATE HAD ACCEPTED THE RELEVANT CONVENTION AND INDIVIDUAL COMPLAINTS COULD THEREFORE BE HEARD — THAT COMMITTEE REQUESTING IMMEDIATE RELEASE AS AN URGENT MEASURE ON REPEATED OCCASIONS. Check which conventions your state has accepted individual complaints under before choosing where to file. Where a stronger treaty route is open, use it; where none is, the Working Group is always available. AND WHAT IT COSTS THE ORGANISATION, RECORDED PLAINLY: IT CONSIDERS A RESOLUTION AGAINST IT TO BE POLITICAL IN NATURE, CONSTITUTING A FORM OF REPRISALS AGAINST ITS ENGAGEMENT WITH THE UN HUMAN RIGHTS MECHANISMS, IN PARTICULAR THE SUBMISSION OF COMPLAINTS ON BEHALF OF VICTIMS. Filing at the UN draws retaliation against the filer, not only the family. Recorded so that a community understands what it is asking an ally to absorb. WHO IT SUITS: families of detained or disappeared land and environmental defenders anywhere — including in states that have signed no relevant convention — and organisations that want to file on their behalf. CAVEATS: THE FOUNDATION'S CASELOAD IS CONCENTRATED IN THE ARAB REGION, SO NORTH AFRICAN COMMUNITIES ARE ITS NATURAL CONSTITUENCY AND OTHERS SHOULD CHECK BEFORE RELYING ON IT; IT COVERS FOUR VIOLATION TYPES ONLY AND NOT LAND, PLANNING OR EVICTION AS SUCH; AND A UN OPINION IS A FINDING, NOT AN ENFORCEABLE ORDER. For the 24/7 defender helpline and evacuation grants, the Republic of Congo's entry; for counsel in the first hours after arrest, Burundi's entry.

trackers.name: Southern Africa Litigation Centre (SALC)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a regional litigation centre supporting and co-counselling cases across Angola, Botswana, DR Congo, Eswatini, Lesotho, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, South Africa, Tanzania, Zambia and Zimbabwe. Its socio-economic rights work challenges large-scale agricultural and extractive land use that dispossesses customary landholders without adequate consent, consultation or compensation, and covers mining, pollution and climate justice — live matters include a Zambian community's pollution claim against copper processors and San and Bayei claims to ancestral land in Botswana. WHO IT SUITS: in-country lawyers and community organisations who need a partner with regional capacity and resources; SALC generally works through local counsel and partners rather than taking clients directly. SALC RESOURCES A LAWYER — IT DOES NOT REPLACE ONE. It provides technical and monetary support to local and regional lawyers and organisations litigating human rights and rule of law cases, working primarily through strategic litigation and capacity-strengthening support to lawyers and grassroots organisations. So the ask is not ‘please take my case’ but ‘please back my lawyer’ — come with a local lawyer or local organisation. It also trains human rights lawyers and facilitates networks across the region, so it is a route to finding counsel too. THE SECOND FORUM MOST PEOPLE MISS: SALC supports litigation in South African courts that advances human rights in the southern African region — so where your own courts are slow, captured or hostile, there may be another venue, and SALC is the body that supports using it. NAME THE RIGHT CLUSTER WHEN YOU APPROACH: its themes are criminal justice, civil and political rights, socio-economic rights, international criminal justice, business and human rights and equality rights — ‘environment’ is not one of them, so frame a land-defence case as business and human rights or socio-economic rights. Established 2005 in Johannesburg out of the International Bar Association and OSISA. It has also run open calls for small organisational development grants to emerging CBOs in Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia, Malawi, Zambia and Zimbabwe — periodic, so watch for them.

trackers.name: Angola — Guiché Único da Empresa (GUE)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the GUE one-stop public office handles company constitution, modification & dissolution and publishes registered companies online, Angola. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Portal da Transparência Pública (Angola)
trackers.desc: Angola civil-society transparency portal (Pro Bono Angola): state budgets, expense authorisations, public works and extractive-industry data. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Angola.

trackers.name: Constitutional Court of Angola
trackers.desc: Constitutional Court of Angola — supreme court (Angola).

trackers.name: Tribunal de Contas
trackers.desc: National — supreme audit institution of Angola. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Angola.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: SADC Protocol on Wildlife Conservation and Law Enforcement
trackers.desc: A REGIONAL TREATY WHOSE DEFINITIONS DO REAL WORK. The SADC Protocol on Wildlife Conservation and Law Enforcement (1999, in force 2003) defines ‘taking’ as hunting, killing, injuring, capturing, harassing, collecting, picking, uprooting, digging up, cutting, destruction and removal of any wildlife species. So clearing vegetation for a development is ‘taking’ under this definition, not merely site preparation — that reframing is the most useful thing here. It defines community based wildlife management as management by a community which has the right to manage the wildlife AND to receive the benefits from that management, giving a benefit-sharing argument a treaty source; and ‘conservation’ to include rehabilitation and restoration, so restoration sits inside the defined term. THE CROSS-BORDER HOOK: States Parties must cooperate to manage shared wildlife resources as well as any transfrontier effects of activities within their jurisdiction or control — a mine, dam or plantation whose effects cross a border engages a treaty duty on the state that authorised it. Article 4 objectives include enforcing wildlife laws within, between and among States Parties and facilitating community-based natural resources management. CHECK YOUR STATE HAS RATIFIED — the Protocol is legally binding only for countries that have signed and ratified it, and this entry does not assert that your state has. ON TFCAs: they encompass protected areas as well as multiple resource use areas, so they are not exclusion zones; a TFCA practitioners network founded September 2013 has membership open to all stakeholder groups. And SADC's own 2023–2033 TFCA programme names the marginalisation of communities living in and around protected areas as a problem it exists to address — quotable against the body that wrote it.

trackers.name: SOS Habitat — the Angolan association that documents demolitions, and the sequence a lawful eviction is supposed to follow
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an Angolan civic association working on the right to housing, which has spent two decades documenting forced evictions and demolitions in Luanda and beyond — its research with an international human rights organisation established that at least 18 mass evictions involving violence and excessive force took place in a four-year period, and it has continued through the demolitions at Zango, Areia Branca, Quiçama and Vida Pacífica, and the 2023 destruction of more than 300 houses at Zango 3. THE MOST USEFUL THING IT PUBLISHES IS A SEQUENCE, because in Angola the demolition usually comes first: its coordinator sets out that demolition should be the last step, after notification of the families, registration of the affected households, and provision of a housing alternative — and that what happens instead is demolition for the benefit of a private party with no legal procedure and no follow-up. Quote that order back at whoever arrives, and ask which step has been completed. THE OTHER GAP IT DOCUMENTS IS THE ONE TO ATTACK FIRST: investigations found the state did not tell residents which body issued the eviction order, on what legal basis, or which authority to appeal to. Those three questions, in writing, are where a defence starts. WHAT IT DOES BESIDES DOCUMENT: it supports affected residents' marches and negotiations — in one Luanda case the threat of a march it backed produced a government commitment to house more than 460 people demolished years earlier — and it has convened affected communities from Luanda, Benguela, Kwanza Sul, Huíla and Lunda Sul in a national gathering, the first of its kind. WHO IT SUITS: households in informal settlements without formal title — which is most of Luanda — facing demolition for a state or private project. CAVEATS: NO CANONICAL WEBSITE FOR SOS HABITAT WAS FOUND, so this entry carries no URL rather than pointing at a third party; contact is through Angolan civil society networks. It is a documentation and advocacy association, not a law firm. And the risk is real: its activists have themselves been subjected to state force, and residents who refused to leave or protested peacefully have been beaten and detained.

trackers.name: ADRA Angola — assembles the paperwork rural communities need to legalise their land, including the free perpetual community title
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Acção para o Desenvolvimento Rural e Ambiente, an Angolan NGO working on democratic and sustainable rural development, with provincial presence including Huambo. What it does that matters here: it works with the provincial government to assemble the documentation required to legalise the land of agricultural cooperatives and rural communities, because those communities cannot complete the paperwork alone — and it convenes provincial land security conferences bringing together family farmers, traditional authorities, civil society and government. THE INSTRUMENT TO ASK FOR BY NAME: under the Angolan land law, rural community land is defined as land used by a rural community according to custom — including the complementary areas for shifting cultivation, the corridors giving cattle access to water, pastures and the customary rights of way — and the state issues a Título de Reconhecimento, a title recognising the community's right of use and enjoyment of defined land, of PERPETUAL duration, and ISSUED FREE OF CHARGE.
