WHAT THE NEW CYCLE ADDED, AND IT IS THE PART THAT MATTERS FOR LAND: selection was described as particularly competitive, the retained projects now integrate REINFORCED COMMUNITY RESILIENCE CRITERIA, and the cycle carries unprecedented co-financing under the second phase of the GLOBAL INITIATIVE ON INDIGENOUS AND COMMUNITY CONSERVED TERRITORIES AND AREAS (ICCA-GSI). An ICCA window is money specifically for territories communities already conserve — the same instrument recorded in Burkina Faso's APAC entry, and it is open in Burundi now. THE THREE FINANCING STREAMS BEHIND IT, so you ask for the right one: the global environment facility itself, funding climate, biodiversity, land restoration, international waters and waste; STAR funds mobilised through the environment, agriculture and livestock ministry, promoting sustainable agriculture and HILLSIDE COLLECTIVE IRRIGATION; and the ICCA co-financing. Note also the constraint the national environment office states openly: it lacked the expertise and data to fill in climate-fund application dossiers, and needed training to write concept notes — if the state office found the forms hard, budget for help with yours. WHO IT SUITS: Burundian community organisations and associations with a conservation, restoration, agriculture or climate project — especially one on land the community already protects. CAVEATS: A DONOR-CYCLE PROGRAMME with competitive selection and fixed calls — confirm whether the current phase is open; it funds environmental projects, NOT litigation or land purchase. For park-edge site support groups, Burundi's ABO entry; for the first environmental civil society organisation, ODEB; for free legal advice and representation, the legal clinics entry.

trackers.name: Burundi's forest code — a planted woodlot belongs to whoever made it, if you hold real rights over the land; plus the state woodlots handed to communities to co-manage
trackers.desc: PLANT IT AND IT IS YOURS — WITH ONE CONDITION THAT DECIDES EVERYTHING: Burundi's forest code provides that BOISEMENTS BELONG TO THE NATURAL OR LEGAL PERSONS WHO MADE THEM OR HAD THEM MADE, SUBJECT TO THOSE PERSONS HOLDING REAL RIGHTS OVER THE LAND SO REFORESTED. Establish your right to the ground FIRST, then plant — in that order. Trees planted on land you cannot show a real right to belong to whoever can, and Burundi's forest domain is otherwise included in the PUBLIC DOMAIN of the state and the collectivities. The forest code was REVISED BY LOI N°1/07 OF 15 JANUARY 2016, whose objects include ending the reduction of forest cover, sustainable management, and significantly increasing the area of PROTECTED forest and of sustainably managed forest; protected areas are governed separately by loi n°1/10 of 30 May 2011 on the creation and management of protected areas. WHAT CATEGORY YOUR TREES FALL IN: Burundian forest formations are classed as NATURAL FORMATIONS, and BOISEMENTS that are DOMANIAL (state), COMMUNAL, or PRIVATE — the last including MICRO-BOISEMENTS; agroforestry covers roughly 60,000 ha, and most forest products people actually use come from plantations, wooded islets and agroforestry systems rather than natural forest, of which only about 6.6% of the territory remains. A micro-boisement or a family woodlot is a recognised legal category in Burundi, not an informality — which makes tree-planting one of the cheapest tenure acts available to a household. THE COMMUNITY ROUTE, DOCUMENTED AS A PILOT: the forests minister launched an experimental COMMUNITY MANAGEMENT approach over TWO PILOT STATE WOODLOTS in the north — 65 HA in Gashikanwa commune, Ngozi province, and 30 HA on Ntamba hill — under an instrument establishing PARTICIPATORY MANAGEMENT (AMÉNAGEMENT PARTICIPATIF) OF STATE WOODLOTS to reconcile poverty reduction with sustainable management, requiring the forest administration to RESPONSABILISER local populations in managing forest resources. Ask whether a state boisement near you has been placed under participatory management — the pilots are small and named, so the precedent is concrete. Note that exploitation of state AND COMMUNAL forests requires MANAGEMENT PLANS APPROVED by the forest administration. WHO IT SUITS: Burundian households, hills and communes planting or holding woodlots. CAVEATS: OWNERSHIP OF TREES FOLLOWS RIGHTS IN LAND, and land pressure and inheritance disputes are Burundi's dominant land problem; the code was under revision alongside the land code. For free advice and representation, Burundi's legal clinics entry; for 21 civil-society grants and the ICCA window, the GEF Small Grants entry; for park-edge groups, ABO.

trackers.name: Burundi's land watchdogs — the OAG, which published the land commission's members and their political affiliations, FOCODE, OLUCOME, and the commune land office
trackers.desc: WHO WATCHES THE LAND COMMISSION, in a country whose defining dispute is who gets their hill back: the OBSERVATOIRE DE L'ACTION GOUVERNEMENTALE (OAG), Bujumbura, published an ANALYSIS OF THE ORGANISATION AND FUNCTIONING OF THE COMMISSION NATIONALE TERRES ET AUTRES BIENS (CNTB) — the body that decides restitution claims — subtitled as a thorn in the process of peace consolidation and national reconciliation, and THE OAG PUBLISHED THE LIST OF THE CNTB'S PERMANENT MEMBERS TOGETHER WITH THEIR POLITICAL AFFILIATIONS. An organisation that will publish who sits on the commission deciding your land claim, and which party each of them belongs to, is the most useful kind of ally there is. Ask the OAG for the current membership before your file is heard — knowing who will decide is half of preparing. WHO ELSE SPEAKS ON LAND: the FORUM POUR LA CONSCIENCE ET LE DÉVELOPPEMENT (FOCODE), Bujumbura, issued a public declaration that THE GOVERNMENT MUST GUARANTEE THE CNTB DOES NOT DEVIATE FROM ITS MISSION OF RECONCILING BURUNDIANS; and the OBSERVATOIRE DE LUTTE CONTRE LA CORRUPTION ET LES MALVERSATIONS ÉCONOMIQUES (OLUCOME), an INDEPENDENT NON-GOVERNMENTAL ANTI-CORRUPTION WATCHDOG that INVESTIGATES ALLEGATIONS OF CORRUPTION WITHIN THE BURUNDIAN GOVERNMENT AND BUSINESS SECTORS and is known to be critical of the government. If a land allocation near you smells of money rather than of law, OLUCOME is the body whose stated business is exactly that — and it is independent, which in this file's Burundi record is a short list. THE OFFICE NEAREST YOUR HILL: Burundi has established, by decree, a SERVICE FONCIER COMMUNAL — A LAND SERVICE AT COMMUNE LEVEL — alongside a COMMISSION FONCIÈRE NATIONALE with a permanent secretariat, and an INTERMINISTERIAL STEERING COMMITTEE FOR LAND REFORM chaired by the Second Vice-President. The commune land service is the closest registration desk to a rural family in this file's Burundi record. Ask what it can register and what it charges before assuming a title is out of reach — and note the law defines a SINISTRÉ broadly, covering the returnee, the displaced, the regrouped or dispersed, and THE WIDOW. The widow is named in the statute as a category of claimant. That is worth knowing before anyone tells a widow she has no standing. WHO IT SUITS: Burundians with a restitution or land claim, and communities facing an allocation that looks irregular. CAVEATS: WATCHDOGS AND ANALYSTS, NOT LAW FIRMS — and several records here predate recent political change; confirm current status and whether an organisation is still operating. For free advice AND representation, Burundi's legal clinics entry; for the first environmental organisation, ODEB; for site support groups at Kibira, ABO; for project money through 21 organisations, the GEF small grants entry.

trackers.name: Burundi's protected-area memoranda — four local groupings signed collaboration agreements with the OBPE at Bururi, the three-NGO consortium behind them, and the published register of approved local NGOs
trackers.desc: THE MEMORANDUM FOUR VILLAGE GROUPINGS SIGNED, WHICH IS THE INSTRUMENT TO ASK FOR BY NAME: management of protected areas in Burundi is carried out by the OFFICE BURUNDAIS POUR LA PROTECTION DE L'ENVIRONNEMENT (OBPE), a national institution under the environment ministry, WHICH IS SUPPORTED BY OTHER PARTNERS — NOTABLY LOCAL ASSOCIATIONS AND GROUPINGS, AND NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL NGOs. MÉMORANDUMS DE COLLABORATION BETWEEN THE OBPE AND FOUR LOCAL GROUPINGS WERE SIGNED AT THE RÉSERVE NATURELLE FORESTIÈRE DE BURURI, WITH THE SUPPORT OF A PROJECT IMPLEMENTED BY A CONSORTIUM OF THREE BURUNDIAN ORGANISATIONS — ABN, APRN/BEPB AND FCBN — ON FOREIGN ECOSYSTEM-FUND FINANCING. Four village groupings holding signed memoranda with the state agency that manages the reserve is the closest thing to co-management in this file's Burundian record. Ask the OBPE for a mémorandum de collaboration, and cite Bururi: the precedent is Burundian, recent, and involved four groupings at once rather than one. AND THE STRUCTURE UNDERNEATH IT: COMITÉS D'APPUI À LA PROTECTION HAVE BEEN PUT IN PLACE AT COMMUNITY LEVEL ACROSS THREE PROTECTED AREAS — with the official record itself stating that THESE COMMITTEES DESERVE REDYNAMISATION AND CAPACITY STRENGTHENING TO BETTER FULFIL THEIR MISSION. The state has written down that the community committees are under-supported. That is an admission you can quote when asking for the training and the running costs — you are not requesting a favour, you are asking for what the government's own document says is needed. WHO THE LEAD ORGANISATION IS: the ASSOCIATION BURUNDAISE POUR LA PROTECTION DE LA NATURE (ABN), A NON-PROFIT NGO GOVERNED BY THE DÉCRET-LOI N°1/011 OF 8 FEBRUARY 2000 ON ASSOCIATIONS SANS BUT LUCRATIF AND AGRÉÉE BY ORDONNANCE MINISTÉRIELLE N°530/231 OF 8 APRIL 2000, intervening in PROTECTED AREAS, WATERSHEDS (BASSINS VERSANTS), WETLANDS AND LANDSCAPES, whose aims include GATHERING THE FRIENDS OF NATURE AROUND THE OBJECTIVE OF ITS PRESERVATION, REHABILITATION AND SUSTAINABLE USE, working through local media and ENVIRONMENT CLUBS, WHICH IT CALLS THE SOUNDING BOARD FOR THE MESSAGE. ITS METHOD, WITH THE NUMBERS: a participatory approach in which COMMUNITY ASSOCIATIONS ARE INVOLVED IN IDENTIFYING RESOURCES AND MAJOR THREATS; WORKSHOPS INVOLVING 53 COMMUNITY MEMBERS TO IDENTIFY CHALLENGES AND DEVELOP ADAPTATION PLANS — which named HEAVY RAINS LEADING TO SOIL EROSION, LANDSLIDES, SEDIMENTATION AND WIND DAMAGE TO HOUSES as the most pressing; AND AT LEAST 267 COMMUNITY MEMBERS ENGAGED IN SETTING UP TREE NURSERIES AND GROWING TREES ON THEIR OWN CROPLANDS, with a named executive director stating that ABN supports communities AND the government TO INCREASE LAND PROTECTION THROUGH AGROFORESTRY. Trees grown on people's own croplands rather than on a project plot is why the planting survives — the owner of the land is the owner of the tree. Insist the nurseries go onto members' own ground. ALSO NAMED: ORGANISATION DE DÉFENSE DE L'ENVIRONNEMENT ET DE DÉVELOPPEMENT DURABLE (ODEB), A LOCAL NGO CREATED IN 1992, BUJUMBURA. AND THE REGISTER: BURUNDI'S APPROVED LOCAL NGOs ARE PUBLISHED AS AN OPEN-DATA FILE GIVING EACH ONE'S DATE OF APPROVAL, ORDINANCE NUMBER AND POSTAL ADDRESS — including named commune development associations such as ADECOB for Bururi and ADECOMA for Mabanda. A downloadable list of every approved NGO with its ordinance number lets you verify an organisation in one search, and shows that COMMUNE-level development associations are a registered category in Burundi — that is a form your own commune can take. WHO IT SUITS: Burundian communities beside a reserve, commune associations, and farmers wanting nurseries on their own land. CAVEATS: A DONOR-FUNDED CONSORTIUM PROJECT — confirm which memoranda are current. For the body that published the political affiliations of a land commission's members, Burundi's OAG entry; for the communal land service, the Service Foncier Communal entry.

trackers.name: FORSC — Burundi's principal civil society platform of 146 organisations still publishing on land crises and a forced title reform — and the de-registration of five organisations, with the bar council that refused to strike off their lawyer
trackers.desc: THE BAR COUNCIL REFUSED — hold on to that, because the rest of this entry is about how much pressure Burundian civil society has been under: A NAMED LAWYER FACED NUMEROUS MEASURES OF INTIMIDATION AND REPRESSION INCLUDING AN INTERNATIONAL ARREST WARRANT AND A DEMANDED STRIKING-OFF FROM THE BUJUMBURA BAR — AND THAT DEMANDED STRIKING-OFF WAS REJECTED BY A DECISION OF THE COUNCIL OF THE ORDER OF ADVOCATES OF BUJUMBURA. A bar council refusing a government demand to disbar a lawyer is a real and citable act of professional independence. If your advocate is threatened with removal from the roll, the bar's own council is the body that decides — and there is a Burundian precedent of it saying no. THE PLATFORM: FORSC IS THE PRINCIPAL PLATFORM OF BURUNDIAN CIVIL SOCIETY, BRINGING TOGETHER 146 ORGANISATIONS. SET UP IN 2002, IT AROUSED THE INTEREST OF BURUNDIAN CIVIL SOCIETY MEMBERS IN CONCERTED WORK, AND WORKED TO CARRY OUT A DIAGNOSIS OF THE SOCIAL, ECONOMIC, POLITICAL AND SECURITY CONTEXT IN ORDER TO ARRIVE AT A SHARED VISION AND IDENTIFY COMMON ACTIONS TO CARRY OUT. A diagnosis first, then a shared vision, then common actions. That order is the method — and it is why a platform holds together: the members agreed what the situation was before they agreed what to do about it. ITS COMPOSITION IS THE USEFUL PART: ORGANISATIONS OF WOMEN, OF YOUTH, HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS, ACTIVISTS WORKING ON GOOD GOVERNANCE, GRASSROOTS COMMUNITY GROUPINGS, JURISTS, TRADE UNIONS, MEDIA, JOURNALISTS AND OTHER ACTORS — AND IT HAS FREQUENTLY LED ADVOCACY ACTIONS TARGETING NATIONAL DECISION-MAKING BODIES. GRASSROOTS COMMUNITY GROUPINGS are a named member category alongside the unions and the jurists. A village grouping is eligible for the same platform as the lawyers — which is the point of a platform rather than a federation of professionals. AND IT STILL PUBLISHES ON LAND, WHICH IS WHY IT IS IN THIS FILE: recent items include A LAND CRISIS AND SUSPICIONS OF ILLEGAL MINING EXPLOITATION UNDER HEAVY MILITARY GUARD IN A NAMED LOCALITY, and A FORCED REFORM OF LAND TITLES IN BURUNDI DESCRIBED AS BETWEEN PRECIPITATION, LEGAL OPACITY AND RISKS OF MASSIVE DISPOSSESSION. A forced title reform carrying risks of massive dispossession is the kind of national change that reaches every rural household at once and is usually noticed too late. If a titling reform is underway where you are, find out who is publishing about it — in Burundi, this platform is. THE RISK THIS FILE OWES YOU, RECORDED PLAINLY: A MINISTERIAL ORDINANCE OF 19 OCTOBER 2016 DEFINITIVELY STRUCK FIVE NAMED BURUNDIAN ORGANISATIONS FROM THE LIST OF NON-PROFIT ASSOCIATIONS — A CIVIL SOCIETY REINFORCEMENT FORUM, A CONSCIENCE AND DEVELOPMENT FORUM, AN ANTI-TORTURE ASSOCIATION, A HUMAN RIGHTS AND DETAINEES ASSOCIATION AND A CITIZENS' NETWORK — AFTER THEIR ACTIVITIES HAD BEEN PROVISIONALLY SUSPENDED ON 23 NOVEMBER 2015. THREE GROUNDS WERE STATED: DEPARTING FROM THE OBJECTIVES SET OUT IN THEIR STATUTES; TARNISHING THE IMAGE OF BURUNDI; AND SOWING HATRED AND DIVISION AMONG THE POPULATION. A FURTHER ORDINANCE FIVE DAYS LATER PROVISIONALLY SUSPENDED OTHERS, INCLUDING AN ELECTORAL MONITORING COALITION, A JOURNALISTS' UNION AND A HUMAN RIGHTS LEAGUE. DEPARTING FROM THE OBJECTIVES SET OUT IN THEIR STATUTES is the ground to notice, because it is the one that turns your own founding document into the weapon. Write your statutes broadly enough to cover what you will actually do, and keep a record showing your activities match them. That is not legalism — it is the specific defence against the specific charge used here. AND THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST: SOME OF THESE ORGANISATIONS CONTINUE TO PRODUCE REGULAR REPORTS ON HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS. Struck from the register and still publishing. De-registration ends the legal person, not the work — and the platform whose site carries current land reporting is one of the five. Where the register is closed to you, documentation is what remains, and it still reaches people. THE ENVIRONMENTAL BODY, FOR THE OTHER HALF OF THE WORK: A BURUNDIAN NATURE PROTECTION ASSOCIATION IS A NON-PROFIT NGO APPROVED BY A NAMED MINISTERIAL ORDINANCE, INTERVENING IN THE PROTECTION OF THE NATURAL ENVIRONMENT — NOTABLY PROTECTED AREAS, WATERSHEDS, WETLANDS AND LANDSCAPES — AND IT BASES ITS ACTIVITIES ON REINFORCED AWARENESS-RAISING OF THE POPULATION AND OF THE POLITICAL AUTHORITIES, THROUGH LOCAL MEDIA AND THROUGH SUPPORT TO ENVIRONMENT CLUBS, WHICH CONSTITUTE THE SOUNDING BOARD FOR THE MESSAGE. Environment clubs as the sounding board, plus local media, plus the political authorities addressed alongside the population. In a constrained space that is a survivable model: clubs are small, local and hard to characterise as political, and they carry a message further than a press release. WHO IT SUITS: Burundian communities facing a title reform, a mine or a land dispute, and any group deciding how to write its statutes. CAVEATS: CIVIC SPACE IN BURUNDI IS SEVERELY CONSTRAINED and several bodies named here have been de-registered — this file records that rather than pretending otherwise; take local advice before contacting anyone. For the four local groupings that signed collaboration agreements at a forest reserve and the association with 267 community members in nurseries, Burundi's ABN and protected-area memoranda entry; for the country's first environmental civil society organisation, ODEB; for 21 civil society organisations funded through small grants, the GEF small grants entry; for the human rights league, Ligue Iteka.

trackers.name: Up to $5,000 to map your own area, from a network with two African regional hubs — funds usable for devices, events and training, no prior affiliation required, and a named person in the region to help before you apply
trackers.desc: ONE BILLION PEOPLE ARE MISSING FROM THE MAP — that is the organisation's own framing, and this file has met the consequence everywhere: WHEN A PLACE IS NOT ON THE MAP, THE MAP AN INVESTOR OR A MINISTRY LOOKS AT SHOWS EMPTY GROUND. THIS FILE'S LANDMARK ENTRY RECORDS THE SAME MECHANISM — UNMAPPED READS AS VACANT. THE MONEY AND WHAT IT BUYS: UP TO $5,000 IS AVAILABLE FOR COMMUNITY MAPPING PROJECTS THAT RESPOND TO A LOCAL CHALLENGE — AND THE FUNDS CAN BE USED TO PURCHASE DEVICES, HOST EVENTS, AND FACILITATE TRAINING TO PROVIDE THE TOOLS AND RESOURCES NEEDED TO COMPLETE THEIR OWN MAPPING PROJECTS. DEVICES is the item that unlocks the rest. Everything else in this file that a community can do with a phone — offline mapping, evidence video, boundary recording, deforestation alerts — assumes somebody owns the phone. This grant buys the handsets, and it is one of very few that will. THE ELIGIBILITY LINE THAT REMOVES THE USUAL OBSTACLE: APPLICANTS DO NOT NEED TO BE CURRENTLY AFFILIATED WITH THE ORGANISATION, BUT PROJECTS MUST CONTRIBUTE BROADLY TO ITS MISSION OF CREATING COMMUNITY-LED OPEN MAP DATA FOR HUMANITARIAN RESPONSE AND SOCIO-ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT. No prior relationship needed. That is rare enough among the funders in this file to be worth stating twice — you are not applying to a club you have to join first. THE TWO AFRICAN HUBS AND THE PERSON IN THEM: FOUR REGIONAL OPEN MAPPING HUBS EXIST, TWO OF THEM EASTERN & SOUTHERN AFRICA AND WEST & NORTHERN AFRICA — AND MICROGRANT RECIPIENTS ARE SUPPORTED THROUGHOUT THEIR PROJECTS BY REGIONAL COMMUNITY MANAGERS BASED IN THESE HUBS, WHO OFFER LOCALISED SUPPORT. THE HUB ENGAGES WITH OPEN MAPPING ORGANIZATIONS AND COMMUNITIES TO FACILITATE THE EXCHANGE OF IDEAS AND EXPERTISE ACROSS THE REGION. A regional community manager whose job is supporting grantees, based on the continent rather than in a distant office. Whether the grant is won or not, that is a person to introduce yourself to. THE OFFER MOST APPLICANTS NEVER TAKE UP: IF THERE IS ANYTHING YOU WOULD LIKE THEM TO SUPPORT YOU WITH IN ORDER TO STRENGTHEN YOUR PROJECT, LET THEM KNOW — FOR EXAMPLE BUILDING RELATIONSHIPS WITH OTHER MAPPING COMMUNITIES, SOURCING UPDATED IMAGERY FOR MAPPING PROJECTS, OR GUIDANCE ON HOW TO USE SOME OF THE TOOLS THEY HAVE CREATED. WRITE NO MORE THAN 150 WORDS. SOURCING UPDATED IMAGERY is buried in that list and is worth the whole application. Current satellite imagery of your area, obtained for you, is what shows the clearing that was not there last year — and communities routinely pay for it or go without. Ask for it in the 150 words. THE COLLABORATION PREFERENCE, WITH AN EMAIL TO HELP YOU MEET IT: PRIORITY WILL BE GIVEN TO APPLICATIONS THAT COLLABORATE WITH OTHER MAPPING COMMUNITIES IN THE REGION — COUNTRY SPECIFIC OR REGIONAL, INCLUDING ESTABLISHED COMMUNITIES, YOUTH MAPPER CHAPTERS, OR OTHER MEMBERS TO HELP WITH TRAINING AND VALIDATION — AND FOR SUPPORT IN SOURCING COLLABORATORS THERE IS A PUBLISHED EMAIL ADDRESS. They will find you the collaborator that their own scoring rewards. Write to that address before writing the application, not after — and note YOUTH MAPPER CHAPTERS: university mapping societies exist in many African countries and will map for a cause without charging. THE FIRST PROJECT PRINCIPLE, WHICH IS ALSO THE TEST OF ANY MAPPING OFFER: COMMUNITY-DEFINED PROJECT GOALS — GOALS WILL BE COMMUNITY-LED AND WILL ALIGN WITH THE COMMUNITY'S LONG TERM VISION, AND THE APPLICANT WILL CLEARLY EXPLAIN HOW THE ACTIVITIES LISTED REFLECT THE PROJECT GOALS. The funder is asking whether the community set the goal. So write the application from the community's decision outward, not from the technology inward — and if an outside organisation is drafting it for you, that is the sentence to check they got right. THE CONDITIONS, STATED PLAINLY: YOU WILL PROVIDE WRITTEN DOCUMENTATION AND RECEIPTS FOR ALL OF YOUR EXPENSES; AND YOU UNDERSTAND THAT THE DECISIONS MADE BY THE MICROGRANTS COMMITTEE ARE FINAL. Receipts for everything. Small grants are lost more often through missing paperwork than misspent money — appoint the person who keeps the receipts on the day the grant lands. THE EMERGENCY WINDOW: RAPID RESPONSE EMERGENCY MICROGRANTS FUND LOCAL MAPPING GROUPS IN PLACES MOST AT-RISK — AND GRANTS HAVE BEEN PROVIDED TO 27 COMMUNITIES ACROSS SEVERAL PROGRAMMES. THE FREE TOOLS AND THE FREE SCHOOL: A COMBINATION OF OPEN MAPPING TOOLS DEVELOPED BY THE OPEN-SOURCE COMMUNITY TO CREATE, ACCESS, MANAGE, ANALYZE AND SHARE OPEN MAP DATA — ALL OF THESE TOOLS AND RESOURCES ARE FREELY AVAILABLE FOR YOU TO USE — ALONGSIDE AN EDUCATIONAL WEBSITE FOR LEARNING THE MAPPING ITSELF. Free tools and a free school. The grant buys the devices and the training; the software costs nothing either way, so a community with two phones and an internet cafe can begin before any money arrives. THE INCLUSION COMMITMENT: BY INVOLVING WOMEN AND GENDER NON-CONFORMING PEOPLE IN MAPPING INITIATIVES, THEY ENSURE THEIR NEEDS ARE PRIORITIZED, ENABLING TARGETED AND EFFECTIVE INTERVENTIONS. Who holds the phone decides what gets mapped. If only men walk the boundary, the water points, gathering grounds and paths that women use will not appear on it — and this file has recorded that omission deciding compensation. WHO IT SUITS: African community groups and mapping societies that need devices, imagery and training to put their own area on the map. CAVEATS: ROUNDS OPEN AND CLOSE, AND ELIGIBLE COUNTRY LISTS VARY BY ROUND — check which is open before planning. For the platform where a boundary becomes a public record, Mali's LandMark entry; for the free offline tools where the community owns the data, Equatorial Guinea's entry; for the free system for rights neither registered nor registerable, Comoros' entry.

trackers.name: Accountability Counsel — the legal non-profit that takes cases only when a community asks first, publishes the criteria it screens by, refers on what it cannot take — and runs a free database of every community complaint ever filed against an internationally financed project
trackers.desc: THEY WILL NOT COME TO YOU. YOU HAVE TO ASK — adjacency declared first: THIS ORGANISATION'S NAME APPEARS INSIDE NIGERIA'S ENTRY ON AN AFRICAN DEVELOPMENT BANK REVIEW MECHANISM, A BANK INFORMATION CENTRE IS A HOST UNDER GUINEA, AND A SMALL-GRANTS CONNECTOR UNDER BURKINA FASO. NONE OF THOSE CARRIES THE REQUEST-ONLY RULE, THE SELECTION CRITERIA, THE REFERRAL PRACTICE OR THE COMPLAINTS DATABASE. THE REQUEST-ONLY RULE, AND IT IS THE FIND: ASSISTANCE BEGINS WITH A REQUEST FOR SUPPORT FROM THE COMMUNITY ITSELF OR A LOCAL CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATION — WE DO NOT SOLICIT COMMUNITIES FOR CASES; COMMUNITIES MUST DEMONSTRATE THAT WE ARE A WANTED AND TRUSTED PARTNER BY REACHING OUT TO US. An organisation that refuses to arrive uninvited. This file has recorded the opposite pattern repeatedly — outside bodies selecting a community as a case, running it their way, and leaving. Here the initiative must be yours, which means nothing happens unless somebody writes. Waiting to be found is the commonest way a community never gets help at all. HOW COMMUNITIES ACTUALLY REACH THEM: NEARLY ALL CASES COME THROUGH REFERRALS THROUGH CIVIL SOCIETY NETWORKS, OFTEN WITH ONLY ONE OR TWO DEGREES OF SEPARATION BETWEEN LOCAL COMMUNITIES AND THE ORGANISATION. One or two degrees. The national coalition, the paralegal group or the law clinic already working with you almost certainly knows somebody who knows them — so the practical step is asking your existing partner to make the introduction rather than writing cold. THE PUBLISHED SELECTION CRITERIA, SO YOU CAN JUDGE YOUR OWN CASE BEFORE ASKING: REQUESTS ARE SCREENED ON WHETHER THERE CAN BE A POSITIVE OUTCOME FOR THE COMMUNITIES AND WHETHER LESSONS FROM THE CASE CAN BE TRANSLATED INTO SYSTEMIC CHANGE; CASES MUST INVOLVE A TRUSTWORTHY LOCAL PARTNER WITH WHOM THEY CAN CLOSELY COLLABORATE; AND A CODE OF ETHICS IS PUBLISHED ALONGSIDE. A TRUSTWORTHY LOCAL PARTNER is a condition, not a nicety. Building that relationship first is therefore the preparation — and the code of ethics is published, which means you can read in advance what they will and will not do in your name. WHAT HAPPENS WHEN THEY CANNOT TAKE THE CASE, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: WE DO NOT HAVE THE CAPACITY TO TAKE ON EVERY REQUEST, SO WE ALSO SERVE AS A RESOURCE HUB — TRAINING COMMUNITIES AND ADVOCATES ON WHAT ACCOUNTABILITY OFFICES ARE AND HOW TO USE THEM, SHARING LESSONS FROM OUR CASES PUBLICLY, AND CONNECTING PEOPLE WITH ORGANIZATIONS WHO MAY BE BETTER ABLE TO SUPPORT THEM. A refusal comes with a referral. So the downside of asking is close to nothing: the worst outcome is being pointed at somebody better suited, which is itself the thing most communities in this file are missing. THE RANGE OF SUPPORT: FROM DEEP, MULTI-YEAR ACCOMPANIMENT THROUGH A COMPLAINT PROCESS AND ITS FOLLOW UP, TO A MORE LIMITED REVIEW OF KEY DOCUMENTS. A REVIEW OF KEY DOCUMENTS is the small ask worth making. Having someone experienced read the agreement, the resettlement plan or the impact assessment before you sign or object is a few hours of their time and can change everything — and it is far likelier to be granted than years of representation. THE WORKED OUTCOME, AND ITS CONTENTS ARE THE MODEL FOR WHAT TO DEMAND: HUNDREDS OF FARMERS AND THEIR FAMILIES, REPRESENTING NEARLY 4,000 PEOPLE, REACHED AN HISTORIC NEGOTIATED AGREEMENT WITH THEIR GOVERNMENT AND A DEVELOPMENT BANK CONCERNING THE TAKING OF THEIR FARMLAND FOR AN INDUSTRIAL PARK — PROVIDING REMEDIAL SUPPORT WITH A COMBINATION OF LAND, EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES, AGRICULTURAL EQUIPMENT AND TRAINING, AND SUPPORT FOR MICRO-ENTERPRISE FOCUSED ON WOMEN AND THE MOST VULNERABLE MEMBERS OF THE COMMUNITY. LAND, not only cash. That is the distinction this file has recorded communities losing again and again: compensation is spent and gone, replacement land is not. Ask for the settlement in the shape above — land first, then equipment and training, with a share ring-fenced for women and the poorest. OTHER RECORDED RESULTS: SUPPORTING COMMUNITIES TO PREVENT ABUSES IN TWO NAMED COUNTRIES, TO COMPEL REDESIGN OF A PROJECT IN A THIRD, AND TO REACH HISTORIC AGREEMENTS IN TWO OTHERS. COMPEL REDESIGN is worth noting as an outcome distinct from stopping or accepting. A project moved, re-routed or rescoped is a win, and it is the one most often available. THE FREE DATABASE: AN INTERACTIVE DATABASE OF EVERY COMMUNITY COMPLAINT EVER FILED TO EVERY ACCOUNTABILITY OFFICE — WITH TOOLS TO UNDERSTAND HOW AND WHY COMMUNITIES ARE HARMED AND TO IDENTIFY THE MAIN ROADBLOCKS AND BOTTLENECKS IN REACHING EFFECTIVE REMEDY, PLUS BENCHMARKING TOOLS TO COMPARE POLICIES AND PRACTICES ACROSS FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS. AND WHAT IT IS EXPLICITLY FOR: IF YOU ARE SEEKING JUSTICE FOR HARM CAUSED BY INTERNATIONALLY FINANCED PROJECTS, IT PROVIDES UNPARALLELED INSIGHT INTO WHAT OUTCOMES A COMPLAINT PROCESS CAN ACHIEVE, THE LIMITATIONS, AND HOW A PROCESS CAN DIFFER ACROSS MECHANISMS — SUPPORTING COMMUNITIES IN FILING MORE EFFECTIVE COMPLAINTS. Every complaint ever filed, searchable, with outcomes. Before spending years on one route, look up what communities like yours actually got from it — and which financier's office produced results. That is a decision this file has repeatedly recorded being made blind. THE TRAINING: THEY TRAIN LOCAL, REGIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL ORGANIZATIONS ON HOW TO EFFECTIVELY USE THESE OFFICES, AND THE GROUPS THEY TRAIN GO ON TO CONTINUE ADVOCACY IN THEIR COMMUNITIES, REGIONS AND COUNTRIES. AND THE AFRICAN STATUS, RECORDED HONESTLY: A GLOBAL TEAM WORKING FROM FOUR REGIONS DIVIDED EQUALLY BETWEEN THE GLOBAL SOUTH AND NORTH, WITH A REGIONAL PRESENCE IN ASIA AND BUILDING A PRESENCE IN AFRICA. BUILDING, not built. African coverage is the thinnest part of their footprint — so expect referral and training more often than representation, and treat the database and the training as the reliable offer. WHO IT SUITS: African communities harmed by a project financed by a development bank or international investor, working with a local organisation that can partner on the case. CAVEATS: REQUEST-ONLY, CAPACITY-LIMITED, AND THE AFRICAN PRESENCE IS STILL BEING BUILT — approach through your existing partner. For the review mechanism one person can now trigger, Nigeria's entry; for the trackers naming the financier behind a project, Guinea's entry; for the home-country complaint route against a foreign firm, Chad's entry.

trackers.name: An open database of bank credit flows and policy scores covering Central and West Africa — which publishes exactly why its African coverage is weak, names the gap in the company registers, and tells you what to do instead
trackers.desc: IT PUBLISHES WHY IT CANNOT SEE YOUR REGION, WHICH IS THE MOST USEFUL THING IN IT — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S ANGOLA ENTRY COVERS THE COMMERCIAL BANK CAMPAIGNING ORGANISATION THAT LISTS THIS COALITION AMONG ITS PROJECTS; ITS BENIN ENTRY THE FOLLOW-THE-MONEY RESEARCH SERVICE; ITS GUINEA ENTRY THE INVESTOR TRACKERS; AND A NAMED INVESTIGATIVE ORGANISATION IS A HOST UNDER LIBYA. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PUBLISHED ADMISSION, AND IT IS THE FIND: MANY OF THE ACTORS THAT DRIVE DEFORESTATION IN CENTRAL AND WEST AFRICA DO NOT REQUIRE LARGE SYNDICATED FINANCING THAT IS USUALLY RECORDED IN THE FINANCIAL DATABASES. MOREOVER, THEY HAVE NOT LISTED COMPANIES AND THE COMPANY REGISTERS IN THE RELEVANT JURISDICTION DO NOT MAKE SUFFICIENTLY DETAILED COMPANY-LEVEL DATA AVAILABLE. THIS MAKES ACCESS TO INFORMATION ON FINANCIAL RELATIONSHIPS MORE DIFFICULT TO OBTAIN COMPARED TO COMPANIES THAT ARE LISTED OR REGISTERED IN COUNTRIES WHERE COMPANY REGISTERS PROVIDE DETAILED INFORMATION. A financial watchdog stating in public that it cannot see your region properly, and why. That is worth more to an African community than the database itself: it explains why every investor-tracing tool in this file comes back empty on the logging company next door — the company is unlisted, the loan is small, and the national register holds nothing. The failure is structural, not your research. AND IT NAMES THE OTHER HALF: MANY COMPANIES ACTIVE IN CENTRAL AND WEST AFRICA ALSO OBTAIN FINANCE FROM SOURCES THAT ARE NOT COVERED BY THIS DATASET, SUCH AS FROM INDIVIDUAL FINANCIERS. INDIVIDUAL FINANCIERS — a person, not an institution. No campaign against a bank reaches them, and no benchmark scores them. Where that is the case, the leverage is the buyer of the timber or the permit-issuing ministry instead, which this file's supply-chain and register entries address. WHAT IT TELLS YOU TO DO INSTEAD, PLAINLY: IF YOUR BANK IS NOT INCLUDED IN THIS EVALUATION, YOU COULD CHECK YOUR BANK'S WEBSITE OR ASK THEM DIRECTLY. Ask them directly. Unsatisfying, and it is the honest answer — and a written question creates a record of refusal that is itself usable. WHAT THE ASSESSMENT COVERS: 50 FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS SELECTED WITH THE MOST SIGNIFICANT EXPOSURE TO THE FOREST-RISK SECTOR IN SOUTHEAST ASIA, CENTRAL AND WEST AFRICA AND PARTS OF SOUTH AMERICA — WITH A LATER ASSESSMENT COVERING 200 INSTITUTIONS EXPOSED TO COMPANIES IN AREAS AT RISK OF DEFORESTATION. THE SCORING RESULT, STATED BLUNTLY: THAT ASSESSMENT SCORED 59% OF THEM UNDER ONE OUT OF TEN — DESCRIBED AS A SIGN OF AN ABJECT FAILURE TO MITIGATE ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL AND GOVERNANCE RISKS. Nearly six in ten scoring below one out of ten. When a bank tells your ministry it applies rigorous environmental standards, that figure is the sector-wide answer — and the scores are per-institution, so the specific claim is checkable. WHAT THE POLICY CRITERIA INCLUDE, WHICH DOUBLE AS QUESTIONS TO PUT TO A LENDER: WHETHER OPERATIONS IN PRIMARY FORESTS ARE PROHIBITED, AND WHETHER THE BANKS ARE SIGNATORIES TO THE MAIN INTERNATIONAL COVENANTS RELATED TO FOREST AND LAND ISSUES. Two questions any community can put in a letter. A bank that has not prohibited primary forest operations has said so by omission, and the omission is on the record. THE DATASET AND ITS SECTORS: UPDATED CREDIT FLOWS AND INVESTMENT HOLDINGS, ANALYZING 300 COMPANIES ACROSS SIX TROPICAL FOREST-RISK COMMODITY SECTORS — BEEF, PALM OIL, PULP AND PAPER, RUBBER, SOY AND TIMBER — OPERATING IN SOUTHEAST ASIA, SOUTH AMERICA, AND CENTRAL AND WEST AFRICA. RUBBER AND PULP beside palm oil and timber. Plantation crops this file has recorded arriving on African community land are all inside the definition, so search by sector when the company name yields nothing. THE HEADLINE FIGURE: OVER $395 BILLION DIRECTED TO THESE SECTORS SINCE A NAMED CLIMATE AGREEMENT, WITH $77 BILLION IN A SINGLE YEAR AND A HALF — AND FINANCING TO SECTORS LINKED TO DEFORESTATION CONTINUES TO RISE DESPITE INTERNATIONAL COMMITMENTS AIMING TO HALT AND REVERSE BIODIVERSITY LOSS BY 2030. The money went up after the agreements were signed. That is the counter to any assurance that global commitments have changed the lending — and it is measured rather than asserted. HOW THE DATA IS BUILT, WHICH TELLS YOU ITS LIMITS: FINANCIAL DATA FROM TWO NAMED COMMERCIAL TERMINALS AS WELL AS PUBLICLY AVAILABLE COMPANY REPORTS, TO IDENTIFY CORPORATE LOANS, CREDIT AND UNDERWRITING FACILITIES — RUN BY A COALITION OF CAMPAIGN AND RESEARCH ORGANIZATIONS INCLUDING A RAINFOREST ACTION NETWORK AND A DUTCH NOT-FOR-PROFIT FINANCIAL ANALYST ORGANISATION. Built from the same paid terminals a community cannot afford, then published free. That is the same barrier and the same answer as the open financial tools filed under Benin. ITS STATED PURPOSE: ESSENTIALLY AN EFFORT TO BRING MORE TRANSPARENCY AND ACCOUNTABILITY TO FOREST-RISK SECTOR FUNDING. THE REGULATION ASSESSMENT ADDED LATER: EXAMINING WHETHER CURRENT FINANCIAL SECTOR REGULATIONS ARE ADEQUATE TO STOP THE TIDE OF FINANCING FROM THE BANKS AND INVESTORS MOST RESPONSIBLE FOR TROPICAL DEFORESTATION, COVERING INSTITUTIONS IN FIVE NAMED JURISDICTIONS. AND THE POSITION IT ARGUES FROM: VOLUNTARY SOCIAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL POLICIES ARE NOT ENOUGH TO STOP BANKS PROVIDING FINANCIAL SERVICES TO LAND-GRABBING COMPANIES OR FOREST-RISK COMPANIES. Said by the people who spent a decade scoring voluntary policies. Treat a bank's published commitment as a document to hold it to, not as protection — and put the regulatory demand to your own government alongside the campaign against the lender. WHO IT SUITS: Central and West African forest communities trying to identify who finances a plantation, logging or agribusiness operation — and those needing to understand why that search keeps failing. CAVEATS: ITS OWN CONTACT PAGE SAYS AFRICAN COVERAGE IS THE WEAKEST PART, MANY LOCAL FINANCIERS ARE OUTSIDE THE DATASET, AND IT IS A DATABASE RATHER THAN A SERVICE — pair it with research done on request. For that research service, Benin's entry; for the organisation that will feature your project in front of bankers, Angola's entry; for company directors and registries, Côte d'Ivoire's entry.

trackers.name: Conservation Evidence — a free database of which conservation actions actually work, each study summarised in one jargon-free paragraph — with a companion journal that is free to publish in, open access, and accepts papers as short as a page from practitioners
trackers.desc: FREE TO PUBLISH IN, AND A PAPER CAN BE ONE PAGE LONG — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S ANGOLA ENTRY COVERS THE FREE ORGANISATIONAL SELF-ASSESSMENT PLATFORM, AND ITS SÃO TOMÉ ENTRY THE AWARD WHOSE USEFUL-LINKS PAGE RECOMMENDS BOTH. NEITHER IS RESTATED AND NEITHER HOST IS SHIPPED. THE JOURNAL THAT COSTS NOTHING TO PUBLISH IN, WHICH IS THE FIND: IT RUNS A PRACTITIONER-FOCUSED JOURNAL PUBLISHING THE RESULTS OF TESTING INTERVENTIONS; IT IS FREE TO PUBLISH IN THE JOURNAL, AND ALL PAPERS ARE OPEN ACCESS SO THAT OTHER CONSERVATIONISTS CAN READ THEM. Publication fees are what keep African practitioners out of the scientific record — hundreds or thousands of dollars per paper, which is why work done on this continent is so often written up by somebody else, elsewhere. Free to publish and free to read removes both halves of that. WHO IT IS FOR AND HOW SHORT A PAPER MAY BE: PAPERS CAN BE AS SHORT AS A PAGE AND THE EMPHASIS IS ON TESTING INTERVENTIONS, NOT ON SCIENTIFIC NOVELTY — HELPING CONSERVATION PRACTITIONERS WHO MIGHT NOT PUBLISH IN TRADITIONAL SCIENTIFIC JOURNALS TO SHARE THEIR WORK WITH OTHERS. One page, and novelty is not required. A community group that tried a fence design, a fire break, a grazing rotation or a nursery method and measured what happened has a publishable paper. That matters twice over: the knowledge travels, and the organisation acquires a citable publication — which every funder entry in this file treats as evidence of capacity. WHAT THE DATABASE IS: A FREE, AUTHORITATIVE INFORMATION RESOURCE DESIGNED TO SUPPORT DECISIONS ABOUT HOW TO MAINTAIN AND RESTORE GLOBAL BIODIVERSITY — SUMMARISING EVIDENCE FROM THE SCIENTIFIC LITERATURE ABOUT THE EFFECTS OF ACTIONS TO CONSERVE WILDLIFE AND ECOSYSTEMS. THE SCALE OF WHAT HAS BEEN READ FOR YOU: OVER 600 EXPERTS HAVE SUMMARISED THE EVIDENCE FOR THE EFFECTIVENESS OF OVER 4,000 CONSERVATION INTERVENTIONS ACROSS 29 SPECIES GROUPS, HABITATS OR OTHER ISSUES — SCANNING OVER 1.2 MILLION PAPERS IN MORE THAN 670 JOURNALS. Before designing anything, look up whether it has been tested. This file has recorded communities and funders repeating methods that were shown not to work years ago, because the literature sits behind paywalls nobody local can pass. THE NON-ENGLISH SEARCH, WHICH DETERMINES WHAT IS IN THERE: 53 MEMBERS OF A NAMED TRANSLATION PROJECT SEARCHED JOURNALS IN 16 NON-ENGLISH LANGUAGES, AND OVER 330 NON-ENGLISH-LANGUAGE JOURNALS HAVE BEEN SEARCHED, SO ADDITIONAL STUDIES WILL BE ADDED TO SYNOPSIS UPDATES. Deliberately looking beyond English. Worth checking whether francophone and lusophone African journals are among them — and if the work from your region is absent, that is an argument for publishing it in the free journal rather than assuming it does not count. HOW EACH STUDY IS PRESENTED: FOR EACH INTERVENTION, EACH SCIENTIFIC PAPER IS SUMMARIZED IN A SINGLE, JARGON-FREE PARAGRAPH, AND THE KEY MESSAGES ARE EXTRACTED FROM ALL PAPERS TO PROVIDE A QUICK OVERVIEW. JARGON-FREE, one paragraph per study. That is what makes this usable by a committee member rather than only by a scientist — and quotable in a submission to a ministry without a translator. THE EFFECTIVENESS RATING: A COMPANION ASSESSMENT PROVIDES EXPERT ASSESSMENTS OF THE EFFECTIVENESS OF ACTIONS, WITH 231 ADDITIONAL EXPERTS GENERATING A GENERALIZED, OVERALL EFFECTIVENESS CATEGORY FOR EACH ACTION. A category per action means you can say, on record, that a proposed mitigation measure is rated as having no evidence of benefit. When a developer's impact assessment promises to offset the harm by planting or relocating, that rating is the check — and this file has recorded such promises going unexamined for want of exactly this. WHAT A SYNOPSIS COVERS: THE EFFECTIVENESS OF ALL ACTIONS YOU COULD TAKE TO CONSERVE A SPECIES GROUP OR HABITAT OR TO TACKLE A SPECIFIC CONSERVATION ISSUE — SUBJECTS SO FAR INCLUDING AMPHIBIANS, BIRDS, MAMMALS, FORESTS, PEATLAND AND CONTROL OF FRESHWATER INVASIVE SPECIES. FORESTS and PEATLAND are both covered, which is directly relevant where a plantation, a drainage scheme or a restoration project is proposed on community land. THE FORMATS IT COMES IN: SYNOPSES ARE AVAILABLE INDIVIDUALLY, ONLINE — BOTH AS A DOWNLOADABLE PDF AND AS A SEARCHABLE DATABASE — AND SOME IN PRINT, AND ARE COMBINED AS A SEARCHABLE DATABASE COVERING ANY HABITAT AND TAXON, ANYWHERE IN THE WORLD. DOWNLOADABLE PDF, so it can be taken offline and read where there is no connection. Download the synopsis for your habitat once and keep it. HOW TO SEARCH IT, IN ITS OWN WORKED EXAMPLE: SEARCH A SPECIES NAME TO SEE WHAT ACTIONS HAVE BEEN TESTED FOR IT; SEARCH THE WIDER GROUP TO SEE WHAT HAS BEEN LEARNED THAT YOU MAY WANT TO APPLY; OR SEARCH AN ACTION PHRASE TO SEE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF DIFFERENT METHODS. The middle one is the trick for African species with little literature: search the genus or family rather than the species, and apply what was learned elsewhere. THE CORRECTION ROUTE: IF YOU THINK EVIDENCE HAS BEEN MISSED, EMAIL THE PROJECT WITH THE DETAILS AND ATTACH IT — BUT IT HAS TO BE WORK THAT SCIENTIFICALLY QUANTIFIES THE CONSEQUENCES OF INTERVENTIONS, AND INTERVENTIONS ARE PERIODICALLY REVIEWED AND UPDATED USING SUGGESTIONS AND FURTHER LITERATURE REVIEWS. SCIENTIFICALLY QUANTIFIES is the bar, and it excludes an unmeasured account however true. Which is the argument for measuring: a community that counts before and after has something the database will take. AND HOW IT WAS BUILT: 290 ADVISORY BOARD MEMBERS — PRACTITIONERS, ACADEMICS AND POLICY MAKERS REPRESENTING THE GEOGRAPHIC RANGE AND EXPERTISE COVERED — REFINED THE SCOPE AND STRUCTURE OF EACH SYNOPSIS, ADDED ACTIONS AND SOURCES, AND REVIEWED THE PROTOCOL AND NEAR-FINAL SYNTHESIS, WITH COLLABORATORS LARGELY PROVIDING THEIR TIME FOR FREE. PRACTITIONERS on the boards alongside academics, giving their time free. That is why the actions listed are things somebody could actually do, rather than only things somebody could study. WHO IT SUITS: African community organisations, conservancies and practitioners deciding what to do — and any group with a measured result worth publishing free. CAVEATS: SCIENTIFIC EVIDENCE ON CONSERVATION ACTIONS, NOT LAW, FUNDING OR LAND RIGHTS, AND COVERAGE IS UNEVEN BY REGION AND TAXON — absence of evidence is not evidence of failure. For the free organisational self-assessment platform, Angola's entry; for the species funds that pay for the work itself, Niger's and Sudan's entries.

trackers.name: Tusk Trust — a grant-maker that says plainly it runs no open application process and works only through vetted partnerships — prioritising African-led organisations, paying travel grants for partners to visit each other, and awarding £225,000 by nomination to winners' own organisations
trackers.desc: NO OPEN APPLICATION — SO GET VETTED, AND GET NOMINATED — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S ANGOLA ENTRY COVERS THE NO-DEADLINE SMALL-GRANTS FUNDER, ITS SOMALIA ENTRY THE ZERO-OVERHEAD FUNDER, ITS CAPE VERDE ENTRY THE INCUBATING FOUNDATION, ITS ZIMBABWE ENTRY THE CO-MANAGEMENT FOUNDATION. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. THE SELECTION ROUTE, STATED HONESTLY, WHICH IS THE FIND: IT DOES NOT OPERATE AN OPEN GRANT APPLICATION PROCESS; RATHER, IT IDENTIFIES AND DEVELOPS STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIPS WITH VETTED ORGANISATIONS. Filed precisely because it saves the wasted month. An organisation that reads the size of this fund and drafts a proposal is drafting into nothing — there is no form. Being found is the only route, which makes the visibility work below the actual application: symposia, awards, partner referrals and published results are how a small organisation becomes findable. WHAT IT SAYS IT PRIORITISES: LOCAL LEADERSHIP AND EXPERTISE — AFRICAN-LED ORGANISATIONS WITH IN-DEPTH KNOWLEDGE OF LOCAL CONTEXTS; COMMUNITY INTEGRATION — PROJECTS THAT SUCCESSFULLY ENGAGE COMMUNITIES AND USE CONSERVATION TO ALLEVIATE POVERTY; AND HIGH IMPACT. AFRICAN-LED as the first stated criterion, and poverty alleviation named as a conservation purpose rather than a side benefit. A community organisation is the target here, not the subcontractor. THE COLLABORATION FUND, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: IT HAS FUNDED 35 COLLABORATION VISITS AND TRAVEL GRANTS BETWEEN ITS PROJECT PARTNERS OVER SIX YEARS — WITH ONE FULLY FLEDGED COLLABORATION PROJECT BETWEEN TWO NAMED PARTNERS ARISING FROM A SYMPOSIUM, AND FOUR MORE HOPED FOR. Money to go and see how another organisation does it. This file has recorded again and again that the most useful thing available to a community organisation is another community organisation that has already been through the same fight — and travel is what makes that real rather than an email. Thirty-five funded visits is a working precedent to point at when asking any funder for the same line item. THE AWARDS AND WHERE THE MONEY GOES: AWARDS TOTALLING £225,000 — A £100,000 AWARD FOR LIFETIME ACHIEVEMENT, A £75,000 AWARD FOR CONSIDERABLE COMMITMENT AND SIGNIFICANT IMPACT, AND A £30,000 WILDLIFE RANGER AWARD FOR FIELD-BASED INDIVIDUALS — WITH GRANTS PAID TO THE WINNERS' REGISTERED ORGANISATIONS OVER THREE YEARS. The money goes to the organisation, not the individual, and it is spread over three years. That makes an award a funding stream rather than a prize — and the ranger award reaches the people this file has recorded as least likely to be funded directly. THE NOMINATION RULE: SELF-NOMINATIONS ARE EXCLUDED ACROSS ALL AWARD CATEGORIES, AND RANGERS ARE ELIGIBLE IF ACTIVELY ENGAGED IN CONSERVATION OR ENFORCEMENT WITHIN PROTECTED AREAS — WITH RANGER JUDGING CRITERIA OF LEADERSHIP, INTEGRITY, COURAGE, RESILIENCE, COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT AND SUSTAINED TEAMWORK. You cannot nominate yourself, so somebody else must. That is a specific, small favour to ask of a partner organisation, a university contact or a national NGO — and it is the same relationship-building the reference requirement in this file's Angola entry demands. THE FOUNDING PREMISE: ITS FOUNDER ENVISIONED AN ORGANISATION THAT WOULD SUPPORT AND AMPLIFY PROGRESSIVE, LOCALLY-DRIVEN CONSERVATION INITIATIVES RATHER THAN IMPOSING TOP-DOWN SOLUTIONS. THE PROBLEM IT NAMES: IN-COUNTRY, COMMUNITY-DRIVEN ORGANISATIONS OFTEN REMAIN UNDER-RECOGNISED AND LACK THE RESOURCES NEEDED TO GROW — SO ITS WORK BOLSTERS LOCAL AFRICAN LEADERSHIP AND INCREASES THE PROFILE OF ORGANISATIONS AND THEIR TEAMS. PROFILE treated as a deliverable. Being unknown is diagnosed here as a funding problem in itself, which is worth naming when asking any supporter for help with communications rather than only with fieldwork. WHAT PARTNERS ACTUALLY RECEIVE: DIRECT GRANTS TO PARTNER NGOs AND RANGER TEAMS SUPPORTING HABITAT PROTECTION, ANTI-POACHING OPERATIONS AND COMMUNITY-BASED CONSERVATION, ALONGSIDE ADVOCACY AND CAPACITY BUILDING — AND, THROUGH ONE NAMED PARTNERSHIP, EQUIPMENT, TRAINING, MENTORING AND COLLABORATIVE DATA EXCHANGE TO PLAN, TRAIN, INITIATE OR ENHANCE FIELD DATA COLLECTION, ANALYTICS, INFORMATION MANAGEMENT AND REPORTING CAPABILITIES. Funding aimed specifically at an organisation's ability to collect and manage its own data. That capability is what turns a community's observations into the evidence every other entry in this file assumes it already has. THE CRISIS FUNDING ON RECORD: COLLABORATIVE FUNDRAISING INCLUDING A RANGER CHALLENGE CAMPAIGN PROVIDING CRISIS FUNDING — WITH RELIEF GRANTS RAISED THROUGH A CRISIS APPEAL SUPPORTING ONE NAMED CONSERVANCY WHEN TOURISM REVENUE COLLAPSED, ENSURING RANGERS COULD CONTINUE WORK WITHOUT FEAR OF BEING LAID OFF. Read beside the collapse recorded in this file's South Sudan entry, where a conservancy's rangers went unpaid when its donor went. Somebody runs a standing appeal for exactly that emergency. THE SCALE: FOUNDED IN 1990, MORE THAN £130 MILLION GENERATED, OVER 250 LOCAL PARTNER ORGANISATIONS AND RANGER TEAMS ACROSS MORE THAN 25 AFRICAN COUNTRIES — CURRENTLY SUPPORTING APPROXIMATELY 80 COMMUNITY-BASED PROJECTS ACROSS 24 COUNTRIES, PROTECTING OVER 50 MILLION HECTARES AND SUPPORTING OVER 9,000 RANGER LIVELIHOODS. THE BREADTH OF WHAT IT WILL BACK: THE FULL SPECTRUM OF AFRICA'S LANDSCAPES AND THREATENED SPECIES, FROM ICONIC MAMMALS TO A SEAGRASS-EATING MARINE MAMMAL OF THE INDIAN OCEAN AND AN ELUSIVE PRIMATE OF WESTERN AFRICA'S TROPICAL RAINFOREST — WITH PARTNERS RESOLVING THOUSANDS OF HUMAN-WILDLIFE CONFLICTS EACH YEAR. Marine and rainforest work alongside savanna, so coastal and forest communities are not outside the frame. AND THE US DONATION ROUTE IT USES: THROUGH A NAMED INTERMEDIARY, FOREIGN CHARITABLE ORGANISATIONS CAN RAISE FUNDS FROM UNITED STATES DONORS WHILE AVOIDING THE COMPLEXITIES OF ESTABLISHING A UNITED STATES CHARITY, SOLICITING TAX-DEDUCTIBLE DONATIONS WITH DEDICATED SUPPORT. The same problem solved a second way. This file's Somalia entry records a funder receiving American donations on an African organisation's behalf; here is a dedicated intermediary that exists to do only that. An African organisation with willing American supporters has two routes rather than none. WHO IT SUITS: established African-led conservation organisations and ranger teams seeking long-term partnership, travel money to learn from peers, or nomination for a funded award. CAVEATS: NO OPEN APPLICATION PROCESS AND NO FORM — PARTNERSHIP IS BY VETTING AND AWARDS BY THIRD-PARTY NOMINATION; ITS FRAME IS WILDLIFE AND SPECIES CONSERVATION, INCLUDING ANTI-POACHING ENFORCEMENT, SO A PURE LAND-RIGHTS OR POLLUTION FIGHT WILL NOT FIT. For a funder with no deadlines and an open form, Angola's entry; for the one that pays the bank fees, Somalia's entry.

trackers.name: IBJ (International Bridges to Justice), Geneva — country programmes in Burundi and DR Congo providing free defence counsel and monitoring police cells, and JusticeMakers fellowships of US$2,000–5,000 awarded to individual lawyers and defenders
trackers.desc: A LAWYER IN THE FIRST HOURS CUTS TORTURE BY UP TO 80% — method and adjacency declared first: TWO CANDIDATES WERE WITHDRAWN THIS ROUND BEFORE DRAFTING, BOTH ALREADY FILED — A TANZANIAN COLLECTIVE-TITLE ORGANISATION UNDER TANZANIA AND A CONGOLESE FREE LEGAL CLINIC UNDER THE REPUBLIC OF CONGO, THE SECOND WITH THE SAME FINDS ALREADY WRITTEN OUT. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THREE HOSTS AND SIX DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL ABSENT. THIS FILE'S REPUBLIC OF CONGO ENTRY COVERS THE 24/7 DEFENDER HELPLINE AND EVACUATION GRANTS, ITS COMOROS ENTRY THE AFRICA-BASED DEFENDERS NETWORK, ITS CAMEROON ENTRY THE BODY DEFENDING LAWYERS AND JUDGES WHO ARE THEMSELVES HARASSED. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE TIMING FINDING, WHICH IS THE FIND: ITS EXPERIENCE HAS DEMONSTRATED THAT LEGAL ADVICE DURING THE INITIAL PHASES OF CRIMINAL DEFENCE REDUCES CASES OF TORTURE BY UP TO 80% — SO IT WORKS JOINTLY WITH DUTY COUNSEL AND COURT-APPOINTED LAWYERS. This file has recorded land defenders arrested again and again, and has answered with protection funds, helplines and relocation. None of them addresses the first night in a cell, which is when the damage is done. A lawyer present in the initial phase is the intervention, and the figure is the argument for spending money on duty counsel rather than on a campaign after the fact. WHAT IT PROVIDES AND WHERE: THROUGH ITS 8 COUNTRY PROGRAMMES IT OFFERS DIRECT LEGAL ASSISTANCE, TRAINS LAWYERS, ORGANISES ROUND TABLES FOR JUSTICE SECTOR OFFICIALS AND RUNS INFORMATION CAMPAIGNS ON LEGAL RIGHTS — WITH OFFICES INCLUDING FOUR NAMED COUNTRIES, TWO OF THEM AFRICAN. THE FREE ASSISTANCE IN ONE NAMED AFRICAN COUNTRY: SINCE 2016 IT HAS GRANTED FREE LEGAL ASSISTANCE TO ORDINARY ACCUSED AND CHARGED PERSONS WHO ARE INDIGENT OR VULNERABLE, AND/OR VICTIMS OF TORTURE — ACCOMPANIED BY MONITORING OF CELLS AND LOCK-UPS, PARTICIPATION IN PEACEKEEPING TASKFORCE MEETINGS, AND SUPPORT TO MILITARY JUSTICE; CARRIED OUT BY A LOCAL AFFILIATED ENTITY. MONITORING OF CELLS AND LOCK-UPS is the part worth knowing about: an organisation that already visits the places detainees are held has a route to a person the family cannot reach. And MILITARY JUSTICE matters where defenders are arrested by soldiers rather than police. THE SEED GRANTS AND WHO CAN APPLY: AN ACCESS TO JUSTICE COMPETITION AWARDING FELLOWSHIPS TO LAWYERS AND HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS FOR THE MOST INNOVATIVE AND SUSTAINABLE PROJECTS — US$2,000 IN ONE ROUND AND US$5,000 IN OTHERS, WITH A DETAILED PROPOSAL REQUIRED AND WINNERS CONNECTED TO A GLOBAL NETWORK OF SUPPORT; ONE ROUND WAS OPEN TO ANY FEMALE COMMUNITY ACTIVISTS, LAWYERS AND HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS. Money to an individual lawyer rather than to an organisation. Most funds in this file require a registered body with audited accounts; this one is a competition an individual defence advocate can enter alone, which is the shape that fits a country where the lawyer willing to take these cases is one person. THE AFRICAN ROUND ON RECORD: A COMPETITION FOR PREVENTION OF TORTURE IN FRANCOPHONE AFRICA AWARDED 10 DEDICATED LAWYERS, HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS AND LEGAL ACTIVISTS WITH FELLOWSHIPS — AND FELLOWS TO DATE HAVE INCLUDED INDIVIDUALS FROM 37 COUNTRIES. A francophone Africa round, run in French. This file has recorded francophone Central Africa as its thinnest region for legal help; this is a route that has already been opened there once. THE SIX JUDGING CRITERIA, PUBLISHED: INNOVATION; RELEVANCE; URGENCY; PRACTICABILITY; EFFICACY, MEANING THE PROJECT IS DESIGNED TO PRODUCE THE DESIRED IMPACT WITHIN A ONE-YEAR TIME FRAME; AND COLLABORATION, MEANING THE PROJECT WORKS JOINTLY WITH DOMESTIC GROUPS, INSTITUTIONS, LEGAL WORKERS, JUDGES, PROSECUTORS, POLICE, PRISON OFFICIALS AND PRISON GUARDS. The criteria are published, so a proposal can be written against them directly. Note that COLLABORATION explicitly includes police and prison guards — an application framed purely as opposition will score badly, which is worth knowing before writing one. THE WORKED EXAMPLES IT PUBLISHES FOR APPLICANTS: PLACE LEGAL AID LAWYERS AT POLICE STATIONS TO ENSURE ACCUSED PERSONS HAVE ACCESS TO COUNSEL; ESTABLISH CHILDCARE AT THE COURTHOUSE SO WOMEN DEFENDANTS CAN ATTEND PROCEEDINGS; DEVELOP A MOBILE ARRAIGNMENT COURT; CREATE ALTERNATIVES TO CUSTODIAL SENTENCING; AND ESTABLISH A MICROFINANCE LEGAL INSURANCE PRODUCT SO PEOPLE HAVE FUNDING TO SECURE COUNSEL. Five funded project shapes, published as examples. A LAWYER STATIONED AT THE POLICE STATION is the one that maps directly onto a community where arrests at a project site are routine, and LEGAL INSURANCE is a genuinely unusual idea: a village paying small sums in advance against the day someone is detained. THE FREE REFERENCE LIBRARY: A CRIMINAL DEFENSE WIKI BRINGING CASE LAW, CODES, TREATIES AND OTHER RESOURCES TO LAWYERS IN DEVELOPING COUNTRIES — WITH ITS ELEARNING PROGRAMME AND THE WIKI RECORDING 15,276,212 INTERACTIONS BY THE END OF 2019, REACHING 106 COUNTRIES. Free codes and case law for a lawyer who cannot afford a subscription. Where a defender's advocate is working from an outdated printed code, this is the fix. THE PRO BONO PARTNERSHIP FOR LAW FIRMS: A LAWYER-TO-LAWYER PROGRAMME WHOSE BASELINE COMMITMENT IS TO CREATE AT LEAST ONE COUNTRY-SPECIFIC ELEARNING COURSE AND DEFENDERS MANUAL FOR PUBLIC DEFENDERS — THE ORGANISATION PROVIDING A TEMPLATE AND RESOURCES, THE PARTNER DEVELOPING THE COURSE WITH INPUT FROM LOCAL AFFILIATES, THEN WORKING WITH THE LOCAL BAR ASSOCIATION TO OBTAIN CERTIFICATION. BAR ASSOCIATION CERTIFICATION is the detail that makes it stick: a course that counts toward a lawyer's professional requirements gets taken, and one that does not gets ignored. Any organisation building legal training should seek that accreditation from the start. WHAT IT SAYS THE PARTNERSHIP GIVES THE FIRM: WORK ALLOWING LAWYERS IN THE POOREST AND MOST REMOTE REGIONS TO BUILD THE SKILLS TO PROTECT THEIR CLIENTS FROM CRUEL AND UNUSUAL PUNISHMENT; AND HIGH-LEVEL NETWORKING, SINCE EACH PROGRAMME REQUIRES THE FIRM TO BUILD CONTACTS WITH GOVERNMENTS, BAR ASSOCIATIONS AND LAWYERS. The pitch to the firm is stated openly, including what the firm gets out of it. Useful for any group approaching a commercial firm for pro bono help: name the benefit rather than only the need. THE THREE RIGHTS IT NAMES: THE RIGHT TO COMPETENT LEGAL REPRESENTATION, THE RIGHT TO BE PROTECTED FROM CRUEL AND UNUSUAL PUNISHMENT, AND THE RIGHT TO A FAIR TRIAL FOR EVERY MAN, WOMAN AND CHILD — IN FRAGILE OR CONFLICT-AFFECTED COUNTRIES. AND THE PUBLISHED ROUTES IN: AN APPLICATIONS PAGE FOR THE FELLOWSHIP AND A DEDICATED PUBLISHED EMAIL FOR SPECIFIC QUESTIONS — PLUS A ROLLING INTERNATIONAL INTERNSHIP TAKING LAW STUDENTS AND GRADUATES YEAR-ROUND, WHOSE PAST TASKS INCLUDED RESEARCHING CRIMINAL PROCEDURE AND PENAL CODES, SUPPORTING LOCAL PUBLIC DEFENDERS AND ASSISTING IN GRANT WRITING. The internship is a way for a national organisation to get research capacity it cannot pay for — including help writing the grant applications this file records communities failing at for want of a drafter. WHO IT SUITS: land and environmental defenders who have been detained or charged, the lawyers who represent them, and anyone wanting a seed grant an individual advocate can win alone. CAVEATS: ITS FRAME IS CRIMINAL DEFENCE AND TORTURE PREVENTION RATHER THAN LAND, PLANNING OR LAND PURCHASE — IT HELPS WITH THE ARREST, NOT THE PROJECT; ITS DIRECT PROGRAMMES COVER EIGHT COUNTRIES ONLY, THE COMPETITION ROUNDS ARE PERIODIC AND REGION-SPECIFIC, AND SOME FIGURES CITED ARE FROM EARLIER YEARS. For the 24/7 defender helpline and evacuation grants, the Republic of Congo's entry; for trial observation and support to harassed lawyers, Cameroon's entry.

trackers.name: Chad — Agence Nationale des Investissements et des Exportations (ANIE)
trackers.desc: National corporate registry; the ANIE (public agency, Loi 004/PR/07) runs Chad’s Guichet Unique for company creation — the single window registering businesses & handling investment & export formalities, Chad. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Chad — Ministère des Finances et du Budget
trackers.desc: National budget authority; the Ministry of Finance & Budget manages public finances, prepares & executes the state budget, treasury & taxation and publishes budgetary information, Chad. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Chad.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: COMIFAC Treaty and Plan de Convergence — and its community protocol
trackers.desc: A TREATY BODY WITH A TEMPLATE YOU CAN COPY. The Traité relatif à la conservation et à la gestion durable des écosystèmes forestiers d'Afrique Centrale, signed by heads of state at their second summit on 5 February 2005 in Brazzaville, instituted the Commission des Forêts d'Afrique Centrale — described as the unique instance d'orientation, de décision et de coordination for subregional forest action, and the cadre politique et juridique global for cooperation in the field. A transboundary forest question belongs in that forum. The Plan de Convergence is the reference framework for all such interventions — first edition 2005–2014, revised in 2014 for 2015–2025 and restructured into 10 strategic axes, executed by a Secrétariat exécutif. CIVIL SOCIETY IS A NAMED STAKEHOLDER in implementing it, alongside state administrations, CEEAC and the private sector — so participation is built into the framework, not conceded case by case. Axis 7 covers capacity and participation des acteurs, expressly contemplating micro-projets générateurs de revenus pour les populations locales; axis 9 covers innovative financing mechanisms. THE DOCUMENT LIBRARY IS THE MOST USEFUL PART: COMIFAC publishes a worked Protocole Bioculturel Communautaire for a named village, a guide to inventorying genetic resources and traditional knowledge, a paper on les droits d'usage des peuples autochtones et communautés locales et les obligations qui en découlent, a subregional APA (access and benefit-sharing) strategy, and directives on forests and the SDGs built with FAO as 5 principles and 12 directives across 31 prioritised targets. A community biocultural protocol published by a treaty body is a template, not a theory. AND ITS OWN DIAGNOSIS IS QUOTABLE: the Plan records that participatory natural resource management and mediation of use conflicts, though already mapped out, are insufficiently developed.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: GRAMPTC — took a complaint against the World Bank's lender on behalf of 25,220 farmers in the Doba oil zone, and got it declared admissible
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Groupe de Recherches Alternatives et de Monitoring du Projet Pétrole Tchad-Cameroun, a non-profit founded in 2001 and registered in December 2001 under folio 1226, working on the environmental, social and economic impacts of oil production. WHAT IT DID, WHICH IS THE LARGEST COMMUNITY COMPLAINT IN THIS FILE: with six other organisations it filed a complaint in October 2011 on behalf of 25,220 farmers from 25 villages of the Doba oil zone against the World Bank Group's private-sector lender, over the land take of the oil installations, pollution damage to crops and livestock, inadequate compensation, restricted movement between villages under a de facto night curfew, and the absence of monitoring. The complaints office found it eligible in January 2012 and held 115 individual and 25 community complaints admissible, then sent a mission to meet the affected people. WHY YOU SHOULD READ ITS RESEARCH BEFORE ACCEPTING ANY COMPENSATION OFFER: GRAMPTC's field studies found that compensation for crops was still being paid at the prices used in the 1995 environmental impact study while market prices had risen sharply, that goods to be destroyed were miscounted or misidentified, and that on the sites it surveyed the restored topsoil was a fraction of the required depth, with some 76 hectares of farmland effectively lost. Compensation frozen at the price list in the original impact study is a pattern worth checking anywhere. It publishes a monthly bulletin, La Lettre de Transparence, and has continued to press on newer operators. B.P. 4021, N'Djaména Moursal. WHO IT SUITS: farming communities in Chad's oil zone facing land take, pollution or a compensation offer. CAVEATS: NO LIVE ORGANISATIONAL WEBSITE WAS VERIFIED, so this entry carries no URL rather than pointing at a third party — its bulletins are mirrored on Chadian research-centre sites. It is a research and monitoring body, not a law firm; the complaint route produced assessment and negotiation, not an order; and much of the published record dates from the 2011-2013 period.

trackers.name: Chad's three legal assistance services — APLFT, the women lawyers' association and the public interest law centre
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: three Chadian organisations that offer legal advice and judicial assistance, from providing information through to assistance BEFORE THE COURTS — the Association pour la Promotion des Libertés Fondamentales au Tchad (APLFT), the Association des Femmes Juristes du Tchad (AFJT), and the Public Interest Law Center (PILC). They were supported together under a two-year access-to-justice programme for people in vulnerable situations, funded by the European Union and run with an international lawyers' organisation. APLFT was founded on 9 June 1991 and recognised in June 1992; it works through standing commissions including “assistance et conseil juridiques” and one on women's and children's rights, publishes a monthly bulletin on fundamental freedoms, and has hundreds of active members in Chadian towns beyond the capital. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR LAND IN CHAD SPECIFICALLY: pressure on land in the far south is severe — farmland expanding onto traditional grazing areas, herders migrating in from neighbouring countries, and agropastoral conflicts that reached unprecedented levels between 2021 and 2024, with more than a thousand people killed and over two thousand injured, in provinces where a majority live below the poverty line. Most Chadian land disputes are not company-versus-village but neighbour-versus-neighbour under demographic pressure, and the resource that fits is a legal advice service, not a campaign. WHO IT SUITS: Chadians facing land disputes, farmer-herder conflict, expropriation or any matter needing advice or representation, especially women. CAVEATS: NO VERIFIED LIVE SITE WAS FOUND FOR ANY OF THE THREE — this entry points at the international lawyers' organisation's published record of the joint programme; some details date from the programme period and should be confirmed locally. These are general legal-aid and human rights services, not land specialists. For the oil zone and the complaint route to a project's financier, Chad's GRAMPTC entry.

trackers.name: Chad's Fonds Spécial en faveur de l'Environnement — calls for proposals open to associations, with training workshops held in the provinces, at a published N'Djamena address
trackers.desc: WHERE TO APPLY FOR MONEY: the Fonds Spécial en faveur de l'Environnement (FSE), created by loi n°014/PR/98 of 17 August 1998 setting the general principles of environmental protection, and made operational in 2012 by décret n°168/PR/PM/MERH/2012, under the environment ministry. Its mission is to mobilise, manage and allocate finance for concrete projects of protection, restoration and valorisation of the environment across the whole national territory, and it expressly supports initiatives carried by LOCAL AUTHORITIES, CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, public services and technical partners. Address: Avenue Ngarta Tombalbaye, Klemat, rue de 40m, opposite the two water towers, N'Djamena. HOW THE MONEY IS ACTUALLY OFFERED, AND IT IS THE PART TO WATCH FOR: the FSE runs APPELS À PROPOSITIONS — numbered calls — and holds INFORMATION AND TRAINING WORKSHOPS IN THE PROVINCES before the deadline, explaining the guidelines and the application form to local organisations and associations; a third call was worked through in Moyen-Chari, and it has run workshops in Batha and Ouaddaï to help local actors capture climate financing. If a call is open, the FSE will come and teach you how to fill in the form — attend that workshop; it is the cheapest application training a Chadian association will ever get. WHERE ITS MONEY COMES FROM: state and local-authority subsidies, ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION TAXES, AND FINES COLLECTED FOR DAMAGE CAUSED TO THE ENVIRONMENT — so polluter penalties are meant to fund community projects. THE FUND'S OWN ADMISSION, RECORDED BECAUSE IT SETS EXPECTATIONS: its director general has publicly identified the NON-DISBURSEMENT of FSE money held at the public treasury in recent years as delaying both its activities and its international accreditation. A fund that cannot draw its own money will be slow; ask what has actually been disbursed in the last cycle, not what was allocated. WHO IT SUITS: Chadian associations, local authorities and community organisations with an environmental restoration, desertification or climate project. CAVEATS: A STATE FUND under the environment ministry — it finances environmental action, NOT litigation or land purchase, and its own disbursement record is the constraint. For legal advice and court assistance, Chad's APLFT/AFJT/PILC entry.

trackers.name: Chad's loi 14/PR/2008 — community forests are CLASSED on the Conseil Rural's advice, and a classed forest is inalienable, imprescriptible and unseizable
trackers.desc: THE LAW THAT MAKES YOUR FOREST UNSEIZABLE: loi n°14/PR/2008 of 10 June 2008 on the regime of forests, wildlife and fisheries resources — 336 ARTICLES, and THE FIRST LAW OF ITS KIND IN CHAD SINCE INDEPENDENCE IN 1960. THE TWO PROVISIONS THAT MATTER: COMMUNITY FORESTS ARE CLASSED BY DECISION OF THE MINISTER IN CHARGE OF FORESTS, AFTER THE OPINION OF THE CONSEIL RURAL CONCERNED or the groupement d'intérêt — so the route runs through your rural council, not around it; and CLASSED FORESTS ARE INALIENABLE, IMPRESCRIPTIBLE AND UNSEIZABLE, AND THEY KEEP THEIR NATURE AS CLASSED FOREST EVEN WHEN THEY NO LONGER CARRY FOREST. Cannot be sold, cannot be lost by lapse of time, cannot be seized — and clearing it does not release it. That last clause defeats the commonest tactic in this file: destroy the trees, then argue there is nothing left to protect. Classing does not block buildings, tracks and infrastructure needed for the forest's own management, nor associated forestry activities consistent with the forest's vocation. THE SECOND INSTRUMENT, FOR WILDLIFE COUNTRY: the law introduces many notions of natural-resource management BY COMMUNITIES and expressly provides for RECLASSIFYING CERTAIN CATEGORIES OF PROTECTED AREA — particularly THOSE CURRENTLY PERFORMING BADLY — INTO A ZONE DE GESTION CONCERTÉE DE LA FAUNE, MANAGED BY LOCAL COMMUNITIES in partnership with state services and the private sector; it also allows a protected area to be organised as A CENTRAL CORE surrounded by PERIPHERAL ZONES MANAGED BY THE COMMUNITIES. A failing protected area next to you is an opportunity, not only a burden — the statute names underperformance as a ground for handing management to communities. Ask for reclassification by name. The law's stated policy options include the effective participation and responsabilisation of the population and poverty reduction through local employment and revenue. WHO IT SUITS: Chadian villages and rural councils near forest or a weak protected area. CAVEATS: CLASSING IS A MINISTERIAL DECISION and the recorded field pressures are severe — chronic insecurity, pastoral pressure, organised poaching; note also that Chad banned wood-cutting and charcoal production outright in 2008, which criminalises common village activity. For environmental project money and the provincial training workshops, Chad's Fonds Spécial en faveur de l'Environnement entry; for legal advice, the APLFT entry.

trackers.name: AFPAT, N'Djamena — Mbororo women's organisation working land-conflict resolution and 3D participatory mapping, with parity governance and a published address
trackers.desc: WHO MAPS AND WHO SETTLES LAND CONFLICTS: the ASSOCIATION DES FEMMES PEULES ET PEUPLES AUTOCHTONES DU TCHAD (AFPAT), a Chadian COMMUNITY ORGANISATION OF INDIGENOUS FULANI (MBORORO) WOMEN, CREATED 1999 WITH OFFICIAL AUTHORISATION TO OPERATE FROM 2005, based at Rue de Bouta, N'Djamena (afpat.net). ITS STATED WORKING METHODS ARE THE REASON IT IS IN THIS FILE: AFPAT works on THE DEFENCE OF FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS, the creation of economic activities, and THE PROTECTION AND MANAGEMENT OF THE NATURAL RESOURCES ON WHICH NOMADIC HERDING COMMUNITIES DEPEND, using innovative methods for THE RESOLUTION OF LAND CONFLICTS, THREE-DIMENSIONAL PARTICIPATORY MAPPING OF NATURAL RESOURCES, and work against climate change, desertification and biodiversity loss. Land-conflict resolution and 3D participatory mapping in one Chadian organisation is the exact pairing that has won cases elsewhere in this file — Brainforest in Gabon, Action Mines in Guinea. In Chad it is held by a herders' women's association, which means it is reachable by pastoralists rather than only by villages with fixed fields. HOW IT IS GOVERNED, AND THIS IS WORTH COPYING: AFPAT is A STRUCTURE OF PARITY GOVERNANCE — the bureau and the team respect STRICT PARITY — with governance and all projects resting on the participation of women. Parity written into the statutes rather than promised in a proposal is what makes a women's mandate survive a change of leadership. WHERE ITS REACH EXTENDS: AFPAT is a member of the Congo Basin indigenous peoples' network (REPALEAC) and took part in a REGIONAL WORKSHOP ON LAND RIGHTS under a Community of Practice on land tenure in the Congo Basin (October 2025); it is registered in the UN civil-society database; and its coordinator sits as president of an international forest-certification body's Indigenous Peoples council. Its field campaigns run across Logone Occidental, Mayo Kebbi-Ouest and Mayo Kebbi-Est, with a green-entrepreneurship and climate-adaptation training workshop for women trainers held in N'Djamena with the environment ministry. WHO IT SUITS: Chadian pastoralist and Mbororo communities facing land conflict, and anyone needing a terroir mapped or a regional land-rights channel. CAVEATS: AN ADVOCACY AND MAPPING ORGANISATION, NOT A FUNDER OR A LAW FIRM. For the law that makes a classed forest inalienable and unseizable, Chad's loi 14/PR/2008 entry; for environment project money and the provincial calls, the Fonds Spécial en faveur de l'Environnement entry; for legal advice, APLFT.

trackers.name: Chad's community hunting reserve at Binder-Léré — 40,000 ha managed by a local decision body, and the three-year term that was never renewed
trackers.desc: THE COMMUNITY RESERVE THAT EXISTS, AND THE CLAUSE THAT KILLED IT: east of the RÉSERVE DE FAUNE DE BINDER-LÉRÉ (created 1974, 135,000 ha, Mayo-Kebbi Ouest) lies an experimental RÉSERVE DE CHASSE COMMUNAUTAIRE OF 40,000 HECTARES, part of the ZONE AGRO-PASTORALE COMMUNAUTAIRE D'INTÉRÊT CYNÉGÉTIQUE (ZAPIC). It was CLASSIFIED IN 2004 BY ARRÊTÉ N°020/MEE/SG/DCFAP/04, amended by ARRÊTÉ N°071/MEE/SG/DCFAP/05, AND ITS MANAGEMENT WAS ENTRUSTED TO AN INSTANCE LOCALE D'ORIENTATION ET DE DÉCISION (ILOD) FOR A PERIOD OF THREE YEARS — and the record states plainly that it has been NEITHER MODIFIED NOR RENEWED SINCE. THIS IS THE MOST TRANSFERABLE WARNING IN THIS FILE: a community management mandate with a fixed term and no renewal clause simply expires, and nobody tells you. If you are offered a three-year delegation, put the renewal mechanism in the same arrêté — name who renews it, by when, and what happens on silence. Chad's own community reserve has been running on a lapsed mandate for two decades. An ILOD — a LOCAL BODY OF ORIENTATION AND DECISION — is nonetheless the named Chadian vehicle for community management of a classified area: ask for one by name, and ask for the arrêté number. WHY THE RESERVE MATTERS NOW: the ministry delegated management of Binder-Léré to a conservation NGO on the express condition that the reserve's BIODIVERSITY CORE BE UPGRADED TO A NATIONAL PARK, after heavy elephant poaching (89 animals killed in March 2013, 19 in February 2018, 7 in August 2019); the PARC NATIONAL DE ZAH SOO, 815 km2, was created in 2022 as Chad's FOURTH national park, holding the country's third savanna elephant population, Kordofan giraffe and its only manatee population, with the stated aim that RIVERSIDE COMMUNITIES OF BINDER-LÉRÉ BENEFIT FROM INCLUSIVE DEVELOPMENT, making the complex an ISLAND OF INTEGRITY AND GOOD GOVERNANCE. Poaching numbers were what forced the state to act — count and record what is being taken from your area, because that is the evidence that moves a ministry. Chad has around 10.1% of its territory in protected areas, and the assessment notes that state budget for the parks directorate is very limited, with most field action funded by external partners. WHO IT SUITS: Chadian riverside communities near a classified reserve, and anyone negotiating a fixed-term community management delegation.
