CAVEATS: SMALL ASSOCIATIONS AND DONOR-FUNDED PROGRAMMES — several of these records are dated; confirm current activity. For Anjouan village agreements, Comoros' Dahari entry; for Grande Comore and the park-conservator convention, Ulanga-Ngazidja; for the one-agreement-per-village design and the Mohéli financing failure, the accords de cogestion entry; for eight communal plans and a participatory monitoring system, the ecosystem-adaptation entry; for community works money, FADC.

trackers.name: What a Comorian association is and why they fail — the 1901-law model, the three required officers, the audit of assemblies and accounts, and the customary power that outranks the state
trackers.desc: THREE OFFICERS, AND THE THREE THINGS THAT GO WRONG: THE COMORIAN ASSOCIATIVE MODEL DERIVES FROM THE FRENCH LAW OF 1 JULY 1901, AND THE VERY GREAT MAJORITY OF THE ASSOCIATIVE FABRIC IS MADE UP OF VILLAGE ASSOCIATIONS WITH VERY TARGETED PURPOSES — WOMEN'S, SPORTING, CULTURAL OR LOCAL DEVELOPMENT — alongside thematic CSOs, MILITANT ORGANISATIONS, TRADE UNIONS, AND PROFESSIONAL AND ECONOMIC ASSOCIATIONS. THE FIELD OF INTERVENTION OF A CSO DEPENDS ON ITS STATUTES AND MAY BE NATIONAL, INSULAR, REGIONAL OR VILLAGE-LEVEL. Your statutes decide your reach. If you write village-level statutes you cannot later act at island level without amending them — write the scope you will eventually need, not the one you start with. THEY ARE STRUCTURED INTERNALLY BY STATUTES AND A BUREAU, WITH AT MINIMUM A PRESIDENT, A TREASURER AND A SECRETARY-GENERAL. Three officers is the floor. That is the whole formal requirement — a Comorian village can constitute a legal association with three named people and a set of statutes. AND THE AUDIT, WHICH IS THE MOST USEFUL SENTENCE HERE BECAUSE IT NAMES EXACTLY WHAT KILLS THESE BODIES: THE FUNCTIONING OF ASSOCIATIVE INSTANCES RARELY RESPECTS WHAT THEIR OWN INTERNALLY ADOPTED TEXTS PROVIDE — IN PARTICULAR, THE ASSEMBLIES ARE NOT HELD AT THE ADEQUATE INTERVALS OR ACCORDING TO THE ADEQUATE MODALITIES, THE LIST OF MEMBERS AND THE FINANCIAL ACCOUNTS ARE NOT UP TO DATE. Hold the assembly on time, keep the membership list current, keep the accounts current. Those three failures are what a ministry, a court or a funder will point to when it wants to say your association does not really represent anyone — and they are the three cheapest things in this entry to fix. Do them before you need them. THE PARALLEL STRUCTURE, AND ITS WEIGHT: BESIDES THE OFFICIAL AND MODERN STRUCTURES THERE EXIST SEVERAL HUNDRED CUSTOMARY, TRADITIONAL, RELIGIOUS AND COMMUNITY STRUCTURES WHICH PARTICIPATE IN SOCIAL LIFE AND CONCORD BUT WHICH HAVE NO LEGAL STATUS — AND ON GRANDE COMORE, CUSTOMARY POWER IS VERY INFLUENTIAL, AT THE CENTRE OF DECISIONS AT NATIONAL, REGIONAL AND VILLAGE SCALE, WITH DECISIONS TAKEN AT THAT LEVEL MORE RESPECTED THAN THOSE OF THE STATE. More respected than the state, and holding no legal status at all. That is the pairing to work with: take the decision through the customary body, and register an association to give that decision a legal face. Neither alone is enough — the custom carries the village, the statutes carry the paperwork. The same record notes that THE VITALITY OF THE ASSOCIATIVE MOVEMENT AMONG YOUNG PEOPLE AND THE STRICT DISTINCTION OF GENDER BETWEEN ASSOCIATIONS PROBABLY REFLECTS TRADITIONAL STRUCTURES LINKED TO AGE CLASSES AND GENDER. Age-class and gender associations already exist in every village. You do not need to invent a body — ask which ones are already meeting. WHAT THE STATE HAS BEEN BUILDING TOWARDS: a named capacity and volunteering project FOLLOWED STEPS TOWARDS THE CREATION OF THREE NATIONAL PROTECTED AREAS AND THREE COMMUNITY RESERVES, alongside a community engagement project on Anjouan, within a national protected-area expansion strategy whose priorities include A STRATEGY KNOWN AND SHARED BY ALL, A PRAGMATIC STRUCTURE ADAPTED TO NEEDS AND FINANCING, EFFICIENT AND SIMPLE PROCESSES AND PROCEDURES, AND GOOD COOPERATION BETWEEN THE MULTIPLE ACTORS. Three community reserves were an explicit national objective. Ask the protected areas service where that count now stands and whether a slot remains — a state target with an unfilled number is the easiest thing in government to volunteer for. ALSO NAMED: CEDAC, an association for childhood and community development, ran a project on REINFORCING LOCAL GOVERNANCE OF THE COMMUNES, touring Anjouan, Mohéli and Ngazidja to build collaboration between COMMUNES AND BASE ASSOCIATIONS, HANDING POSTERS TO THE MAYORS reading that COLLABORATION AND DIALOGUE BETWEEN THE COMMUNE AND THE ASSOCIATIONS ARE THE KEY TO LOCAL DEVELOPMENT. Somebody has already toured all three islands persuading mayors to work with village associations. If your commune is unresponsive, that campaign and its posters are the precedent to invoke. WHO IT SUITS: Comorian villages constituting or repairing an association, and anyone weighing the customary route against the legal one. CAVEATS: THIS IS A CIVIL SOCIETY ASSESSMENT, not a legal opinion — confirm current registration practice. For one agreement PER VILLAGE under article 60, Comoros' accords de cogestion entry; for the NGO that helped create a national park, Ulanga-Ngazidja; for reef monitoring at 20 sites, ONG AIDE; for the community development fund, FADC; for attorneys with street addresses, the published attorney list entry.

trackers.name: The village Ulanga movement — associations called Nature founded in most Comorian villages on two islands — plus Malezi Mema's first permanent community marine reserve, the Mrémani seedling nursery and 950 metres of anti-erosion lines
trackers.desc: AN ASSOCIATION CALLED NATURE, IN MOST OF THE VILLAGES — and this is the Comorian precedent worth carrying anywhere: ASSOCIATIONS NAMED ULANGA — WHICH MEANS NATURE IN COMORIAN — WERE CREATED ON NDZOUANI AND ON NGAZIDJA, IN MOST OF THE VILLAGES. ALMOST EVERYWHERE, ACTIONS OF REFORESTATION, CLEANING AND AWARENESS-RAISING OF THE POPULATION WERE ORGANISED WITHIN THE COMMUNITIES THANKS TO THE INITIATIVE OF THESE ASSOCIATIONS — AND THIS MOVEMENT SIGNIFICANTLY CONTRIBUTED TO THE COLLECTIVE AWARENESS OF ENVIRONMENTAL STAKES. Village by village, under one name, in the local language, on their own initiative. Not a national NGO opening branches — separate village associations that took the same name because the idea travelled. That is the cheapest form of national movement there is, and the Comorian record says it worked: the environment framework law and the government's sustainable development declaration came AFTER the villages had already organised, not before. WHAT ONE OF THEM ACTUALLY DOES, WITH THE NUMBERS: A NAMED ULANGA ASSOCIATION AT MRÉMANI IS DESCRIBED AS A LOCAL ASSOCIATION SPECIALISING IN THE PRODUCTION OF FOREST AND FRUIT SEEDLINGS, AND WAS ENGAGED TO DELIVER THE TRAINING — WITH 4,098 SEEDLINGS RAISED IN NURSERY IN TOTAL, 80% FOREST SPECIES AND 20% FRUIT SPECIES INCLUDING JACKFRUIT, ORANGE, AVOCADO, MANGO AND BREADFRUIT. A village association that is the SPECIALIST, hired by a bigger organisation to train others. That is the position to aim for: the skill stays in the village and the village gets paid for it. And the 80/20 split is the practical lesson — four fifths forest species for the watershed, one fifth fruit trees so households get something to eat and sell. AND THE EARTHWORKS, MEASURED: 950 LINEAR METRES OF ANTI-EROSION LINES WERE BUILT IN A NAMED WATERSHED, WITH THE STATED PURPOSE OF PROTECTING THE LAND — done with a water management committee and the farmers of the zone. Nine hundred and fifty metres, built with the water committee and the farmers together. If erosion is taking your soil, that is the scale one season's work reaches — and this file has recorded the same technique with published dimensions in Somaliland. THE MARINE FIRST: THANKS TO THE COMMITMENT OF THE MALEZI MEMA ASSOCIATION, THE CREATION OF A PERMANENT MARINE RESERVE AT A NAMED SITE BECAME THE FIRST PERMANENT COMMUNITY MARINE RESERVE IN THE COMOROS — described as an innovative conservation model. The FIRST permanent one, and a village association is named as the reason it exists. If your coast has no protection, somebody has to be first; here is the association that was, and its name is on the record for anyone who wants to ask how. AND THE FISHERS' FORUM THAT FOLLOWED: AROUND FIFTY FISHERMEN FROM 11 COASTAL VILLAGES MET AT A FORUM IN A NAMED TOWN TO STRENGTHEN THEIR COOPERATION ON MARINE RESOURCES. Fifty fishers from eleven villages in one room — the same shape this file recorded in Madagascar, where fifty-five people from eighteen areas founded a national network. The first forum is always small and always the turning point. MORE NAMED BODIES: ADIC, AN NGO SPECIALISED FOR MORE THAN 25 YEARS IN THE IMPROVEMENT OF THE LIVING CONDITIONS OF THE COMORIAN POPULATION, WORKING ANJOUAN AND MOHÉLI; AND A UJAMAA ASSOCIATION IN GRANDE COMORE. THE SCALE OF THE PROBLEM, AND ITS STATED CAUSE: THE COMOROS HAS LOST 28 PERCENT OF ITS FOREST COVER IN THE PAST 20 YEARS AND EROSION HAS CAUSED COASTAL AREAS TO RECEDE BY 30 METRES; POPULATION DENSITY ON ANJOUAN IS AROUND 900 PEOPLE PER SQUARE KILOMETRE — AND THE CAUSE IS NAMED PLAINLY AS INEQUALITIES IN HOW LAND AND RESOURCES WERE ALLOCATED AT INDEPENDENCE, FORCING POORER PEOPLE INTO LIVELIHOODS BASED ON UNSUSTAINABLE RESOURCE EXTRACTION. Deforestation traced to how land was allocated at independence, said by a conservation organisation about its own country. That sentence is the one to reuse wherever a community is blamed for cutting the forest it was pushed onto — the extraction is downstream of the allocation, and somebody credible has written it down. AND THE ARTISTS: an album was released by SOME OF THE BEST KNOWN COMORIAN ARTISTS TO ENCOURAGE THE REFORESTATION OF ANJOUAN, FOLLOWED BY A SERIES OF CONCERTS. Musicians recording an album for a reforestation campaign, then touring it. Where a leaflet reaches nobody, a song reaches everybody — and the artists in your country are approachable in a way a ministry is not. WHO IT SUITS: Comorian villages on any island, coastal communities wanting a reserve, and anyone whose soil is eroding. CAVEATS: SMALL VILLAGE ASSOCIATIONS with limited capacity — this file's separate entry on why Comorian associations fail is worth reading alongside. For the organisation supporting rural communities with individual conservation agreements, Comoros' Dahari entry; for the Grande Comore NGO that helped create a national park, Ulanga-Ngazidja; for coral reef monitoring at 20 sites, ONG AIDE; for article 60 co-management agreements, the accords de cogestion entry; for the national community development fund, FADC.

trackers.name: STDM (Social Tenure Domain Model), GLTN / UN-Habitat — the free open-source system for recording land rights that are neither registered nor registerable — communities draw boundaries on printed satellite images, and it stores photographs, videos and sketches as supporting proof
trackers.desc: PRINT THE SATELLITE IMAGE AND LET PEOPLE DRAW THEIR OWN BOUNDARIES — declared overlap first: THE NETWORK BEHIND THIS TOOL ALREADY APPEARS AS A SOURCE URL IN TWO ENTRIES IN THIS FILE, UNDER LIBYA AND SUDAN. NEITHER DESCRIBES THE TOOL, WHICH IS WHAT THIS ENTRY IS FOR. THE SCALE OF THE PROBLEM, IN ONE FIGURE: UP TO 70% OF LAND USES IN MANY DEVELOPING COUNTRIES IS NOT RECORDED IN NATIONAL LAND REGISTRIES. Seven tenths of land use unrecorded. Your community is not an oversight, it is the norm — and the fix is not waiting for the registry to reach you. WHAT THE TOOL IS FOR, AND IT IS THE EXACT SITUATION MOST COMMUNITIES IN THIS FILE ARE IN: IT FOCUSES ON LAND AND PROPERTY RIGHTS WHICH ARE NEITHER REGISTERED NOR REGISTERABLE, AS WELL AS OVERLAPPING CLAIMS THAT MAY HAVE TO BE ADJUDICATED IN TERMS OF WHO, WHERE AND WHAT RIGHT — SUPPORTING THE DEVELOPMENT AND MAINTENANCE OF RECORDS IN AREAS WHERE REGULAR OR FORMAL REGISTRATION OF LAND RIGHTS IS NOT THE RULE, AND TACKLING THE NEEDS OF NEGLECTED COMMUNITIES SUCH AS PEOPLE IN INFORMAL SETTLEMENTS AND CUSTOMARY AREAS. NEITHER REGISTERED NOR REGISTERABLE. Most tools assume a title exists or could exist; this one is built for the case where neither is true, and it handles OVERLAPPING claims rather than forcing one answer — which is what customary and grazing land actually looks like. AND THE PRINCIPLE: IT ENABLES YOU TO SHOW WHAT CAN BE OBSERVED ON THE GROUND IN TERMS OF TENURE, AS AGREED WITHIN LOCAL COMMUNITIES — REPRESENTING PEOPLE-LAND RELATIONSHIPS INDEPENDENT OF THE LEVEL OF FORMALITY, LEGALITY AND TECHNICAL ACCURACY. AS AGREED WITHIN LOCAL COMMUNITIES is the standard of proof, not a surveyor's certificate. So the record can be built by the people who know the boundaries. IT COSTS NOTHING: A FREE AND OPEN SOURCE PRO-POOR LAND RECORDATION SYSTEM — IT IS OPEN SOURCE, THUS AVAILABLE FREE, HENCE ITS SUSTAINABILITY — A PLUGIN FOR FREE MAPPING SOFTWARE, USABLE ON WINDOWS, LINUX AND MAC, WITH ITS SOURCE CODE PUBLIC AND TWO PUBLIC MAILING LISTS FOR USERS AND ANNOUNCEMENTS. Free forever, with the code public — so no organisation can take the system away when a project ends, and the mailing lists mean you can ask other users when you get stuck. THE METHOD, WHICH IS THE MOST TRANSFERABLE THING HERE AND NEEDS NO SOFTWARE AT ALL: SATELLITE IMAGERY IS USED AS THE BASIS FOR DATA COLLECTION — PEOPLE RECOGNISE IMMEDIATELY THE ROADS AND SPATIAL UNITS ON THE IMAGES; HIGH RESOLUTION IMAGES CAN BE ENLARGED AND PRINTED WITH OVERLAPS WITH NEIGHBOUR PRINTS; AND BASED ON THE IDENTIFICATION OF BOUNDARIES ON THE IMAGES, THE BOUNDARIES CAN BE DRAWN ON THE IMAGE. PEOPLE REALLY UNDERSTAND WHAT THEY SEE ON THE IMAGE — THEY CAN IDENTIFY THE PLACE WHERE THEY LIVE, AND WHERE THEIR NEIGHBOURS LIVE. Print the image large, overlap the sheets, and let people draw. An elder who cannot read a cadastral plan can find their own compound on a photograph in seconds. This file has recorded participatory mapping across the Congo Basin and Cameroon; this is the cheapest version of it, and the printing is most of the cost. WHAT ELSE IT HOLDS AS PROOF: DOCUMENTS THAT SUPPORT SOCIAL TENURES — PHOTOGRAPHS, VIDEOS, SKETCHES, MAPS, OR OTHER DOCUMENTS — ALONGSIDE TITLE DEEDS, NAMES, GENDER AND PROPERTIES. A photograph of the old boundary tree and a video of an elder describing it are storable evidence here. Nothing else in this file treats that material as part of a land record. THE RANGELAND APPLICATION, FOR PASTORALISTS: AS PILOTED BY A NAMED REGIONAL INSTITUTE AND PARTNERS, IT ADDRESSED SECURITY OF TENURE THROUGH PARTICIPATORY COMMON RESOURCE IDENTIFICATION, MAPPING AND DOCUMENTATION — KEY RESOURCES INCLUDING CATTLE DIPS, SALT LICK AREAS AND WATER POINTS — AND MANAGEMENT IMPROVED DUE TO THE RECOGNITION OF BOUNDARIES ANTICIPATORILY DEFINED, LEADING TO THE REVIVAL AND ESTABLISHMENT OF COMMUNITY RESOURCE MANAGEMENT COMMITTEES ESPECIALLY AROUND WATER AND GRAZING LANDS. Mapping the water points and salt licks rather than the plots. For grazing land the resource is the thing to record, not the perimeter — and the mapping itself revived the committees that manage them. THE RECORD: FROM A FIRST PROTOTYPE IN ONE AFRICAN COUNTRY IT SPREAD TO OVER 100 SETTLEMENTS IN DIFFERENT MUNICIPALITIES, MOBILISING COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT, AWARENESS BUILDING, TECHNICAL TRAINING AND DATA GENERATION USING PARTICIPATORY APPROACHES — AND THE SUCCESSES CAUGHT THE ATTENTION OF LOCAL AUTHORITIES, WHO FOUND THE DATA GENERATED VALUABLE INSIGHTS. The authorities came to want the data. A community record that is accurate enough for the municipality to use becomes the municipality's record too, which is a far stronger position than being outside the system. THE EVIDENCE ACROSS THREE CASE STUDIES: A REMARKABLE IMPROVEMENT IN INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS AND COLLABORATION AMONG DIFFERENT INSTITUTIONS, AS WELL AS A NOTABLE REDUCTION IN LAND CONFLICTS OR DISPUTES. AND THE NETWORK'S STATED VALUES, WHICH ARE THE TERMS TO HOLD ANY PARTNER TO: PRO-POOR, EQUITY, AFFORDABILITY, GOOD GOVERNANCE, SUBSIDIARITY, GENDER SENSITIVENESS, SYSTEMATIC LARGE SCALE APPROACH AND SUSTAINABILITY — WITH A PUBLISHED LIST OF IMPLEMENTING ORGANIZATIONS. A published list of implementing organisations is the route in: find the one nearest you rather than starting alone, because the software is free but the first training is not something to improvise. WHO IT SUITS: African communities on customary, grazing or informal land with no registrable title, and organisations helping them record it. CAVEATS: IT NEEDS SOMEONE COMFORTABLE WITH A COMPUTER AND A FIRST TRAINING — the tool is free, the capacity is not. For the participatory mapping that put seven million hectares on the map, DR Congo's MappingForRights entry; for the global platform where a boundary becomes a public record, Mali's LandMark entry; for the free land library and country pages, Guinea-Bissau's entry.

trackers.name: University law clinics as free representation — the network that opened 14 of them, what its clinics actually do for communities, the curriculum other faculties copy, and the continental associations to ask in a country with no clinic yet
trackers.desc: THE LAW FACULTY DOWN THE ROAD HAS A CLINIC — declared adjacency first: THIS FILE ALREADY CARRIES FIVE NATIONAL FREE-LEGAL-CLINIC ENTRIES, UNDER MOROCCO, BURKINA FASO, CÔTE D'IVOIRE, THE REPUBLIC OF CONGO AND MADAGASCAR. NONE DESCRIBES THE CONTINENTAL NETWORKS, THE CURRICULUM, OR HOW A COMMUNITY REACHES A CLINIC IN A COUNTRY WITH NO ENTRY OF ITS OWN. THAT IS WHAT THIS ONE IS FOR. WHAT A LAW CLINIC IS: CLINICAL LEGAL EDUCATION, BY WAY OF LAW CLINICS, TRAINS LAW STUDENTS IN THE SPIRIT OF SOCIAL JUSTICE AND PUBLIC SERVICE, AND PROVIDES DESPERATELY-NEEDED LEGAL SERVICES TO POOR COMMUNITIES AND UNDERPRIVILEGED PERSONS — LAW CLINICS SERVE TO FILL A GAP NOT ADEQUATELY ADDRESSED BY GOVERNMENTAL LEGAL AID PROGRAMMES. A law faculty is a standing pool of supervised legal labour that costs a community nothing and exists in almost every African capital and many provincial cities. It is the nearest free legal help most people have and the one they least often think of — and unlike a busy advocate, a clinic wants the case because the case is the teaching. THE NETWORK: ESTABLISHED IN 2003, A NON-GOVERNMENTAL, NON-PROFIT AND NON-POLITICAL ORGANIZATION COMMITTED TO PROMOTING CLINICAL LEGAL EDUCATION, LEGAL EDUCATION REFORM, LEGAL AID AND ACCESS TO JUSTICE, AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF FUTURE PUBLIC INTEREST LAWYERS — BUILDING A NETWORK OF COHESIVE UNIVERSITY-BASED LAW CLINICS PROVIDING PRO-BONO LEGAL SERVICES TO THE UNDER-SERVED. SINCE 2004, 14 UNIVERSITY-BASED LAW CLINICS HAVE OPENED, INCLUDING AT THE NATIONAL LAW SCHOOL — WITH A NAMED STREET LOCATION IN THE CAPITAL AND PUBLISHED OPENING HOURS, WEEKDAYS 9AM TO 5PM. Fourteen clinics from one organisation in twenty years, and it keeps office hours anyone can walk into. WHAT ITS CLINICS DO, WITH NAMED EXAMPLES WORTH ASKING YOUR OWN FACULTY TO COPY: ONE CLINIC PROVIDES PRO BONO LEGAL AND ADVISORY SERVICES TO THE POOR AND UNDERSERVED MEMBERS OF THE COMMUNITY WITHIN AND OUTSIDE THE UNIVERSITY, AND ENGAGES IN PUBLIC ENLIGHTENMENT AND SENSITIZATION ON THE HUMAN RIGHTS OF THE PEOPLE. ANOTHER ORGANISED A COMMUNITY JUSTICE SPEAK OUT FORUM FOR MEMBERS OF TWO NAMED COMMUNITIES TO INTERACT WITH THE POLICE, THE LEGAL AID COUNCIL AND THE DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC PROSECUTION. ANOTHER CONDUCTED A TWO-DAY PRISON CLINIC AT TWO NAMED PRISONS, INTERVIEWING PRISONERS OF WHOM 36 WERE ON PRE-TRIAL DETENTION. A COMMUNITY JUSTICE SPEAK OUT FORUM is the copyable one: the clinic convened the villagers, the police and the prosecutors in one room, and hosting it as a university event rather than a protest is what made all three come. If your committee cannot get officials to a meeting, ask a law faculty to convene it instead. AND THE PRISON CLINIC matters where land defenders are held: students went in, interviewed, and found thirty-six people on pre-trial detention. Somebody has to count them before anyone can be released. ITS CURRENT WORK NAMES THIS FILE'S SUBJECTS DIRECTLY: IT FOSTERS LEGAL REFORMS, SUPPORTS CIVIC SPACE DEFENDERS, AND PROMOTES ENVIRONMENTAL AND CLIMATE JUSTICE. THE CURRICULUM, WHICH IS THE PART THAT TRAVELS: IT DEVELOPED A CLINICAL LEGAL EDUCATION CURRICULUM FOR UNIVERSITY LAW FACULTIES AND CLINICS, INTRODUCED AS PART OF THE UNDERGRADUATE LAW PROGRAMME, WITH TRAINING WORKSHOPS AND MANUALS FOR TEACHERS — AND IT HOSTED THE FIRST NATIONAL COLLOQUIUM IN PARTNERSHIP WITH A JUSTICE INITIATIVE, WHERE PARTICIPATING LAW FACULTIES SUPPORTED THE INTRODUCTION OF CLINICAL LEGAL EDUCATION. The curriculum and the teachers' manuals already exist. A dean who says a clinic would take years to design can be told the design is written, tested and free — which turns a long argument into a short one. THE OTHER NETWORKS, WHICH ARE THE ROUTE IF YOUR COUNTRY HAS NO CLINIC: AN ASSOCIATION OF UNIVERSITY LEGAL AID INSTITUTIONS, A EUROPEAN NETWORK OF CLINICAL LEGAL EDUCATION, AND A GLOBAL ALLIANCE FOR JUSTICE EDUCATION — THESE NETWORKS PROMOTE TRANSNATIONAL STUDY VISITS AND EXCHANGE PROGRAMS, ENJOY COLLABORATION BETWEEN CLINICAL PROGRAMS AND LEGAL PROFESSIONALS, AND PROMOTE INITIATIVES THAT MIGHT IMPROVE THE COMMUNITY UNDERSTANDING OF THE BENEFITS OF CLINICAL LEGAL EDUCATION. STUDY VISITS AND EXCHANGE PROGRAMS mean a faculty with no clinic can send someone to watch one working. That is the cheapest way a new clinic gets started, and these networks pay for it. THE PUBLISHED JOURNALS: AN AFRICAN JOURNAL OF CLINICAL LEGAL EDUCATION AND ACCESS TO JUSTICE, AND AN INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF CLINICAL LEGAL EDUCATION, WITH AN EDITORIAL BOARD NAMING LAW ACADEMICS AND SENIOR ADVOCATES FROM SEVERAL AFRICAN COUNTRIES. An editorial board is a published list of senior lawyers who have already committed themselves to access to justice in print. This file has repeatedly noted that finding the right advocate is the hard part; that list is a starting point, and writing to a named professor gets answered more often than writing to a firm. AND THE EFFECT RECORDED: THE INTERVENTION BY LEGAL CLINICS IN PROVIDING LEGAL AID, ADVICE AND ACCESS TO JUSTICE HAS BROUGHT RELIEF TO PEOPLE WHO OTHERWISE WOULD NOT HAVE HAD ACCESS TO JUSTICE, DUE TO THE INSUFFICIENCY OF FUNDS AND THE INADEQUACY OF LEGAL AID FACILITIES PROVIDED BY GOVERNMENT. WHO IT SUITS: African communities near any university with a law faculty, and organisations wanting a clinic started in a country that has none. CAVEATS: CLINICS ARE STAFFED BY SUPERVISED STUDENTS AND RUN ON THE ACADEMIC YEAR — they are strong on advice, documentation and convening, weaker on long litigation, and quiet in vacation. For the national clinics already filed, Morocco's, Burkina Faso's, Côte d'Ivoire's, the Republic of Congo's and Madagascar's entries; for the free brokerage that finds a law firm, the Central African Republic's entry; for the community paralegal method where there is no lawyer at all, Sierra Leone's Timap entry.

trackers.name: The Amplio Talking Book — a battery audio device that plays hours of local-language content off-grid and records the community's spoken replies back — no cost to the user, one device serving 100 listeners, with a Ghanaian arm that sets it up and a phone platform for basic handsets
trackers.desc: IT PLAYS THE LAW ALOUD, AND RECORDS WHAT THE VILLAGE SAYS BACK — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S REPUBLIC OF THE CONGO ENTRY NAMES TALKING BOOKS IN ONE LINE AS A TOOL USED BY A LAND-RIGHTS ORGANISATION, AND THE ETHIOPIA AND CAPE VERDE ENTRIES COVER COMMUNITY RADIO. NONE DESCRIBES THE DEVICE, THE FEEDBACK LOOP, THE VOICE PLATFORM OR THE GHANAIAN ARM. WHAT IT IS: A BATTERY-POWERED AUDIO DEVICE DESIGNED WITH AND FOR LOW-LITERATE PEOPLE IN RURAL, REMOTE AND OFF-GRID COMMUNITIES — USING AUDIO PROMPTS AND VISUAL ICONS, EACH ICON EMBOSSED WITH A DOT FOR THE VISUALLY IMPAIRED — DELIVERING HOURS OF CONTENT IN ANY LANGUAGE, WITH MULTIPLE TOPICS AND PLAYLISTS, PLAYED ON DEMAND. THE TWO-WAY CLAUSE, WHICH IS THE FIND AND WHICH ALMOST NOTHING ELSE IN THIS FILE OFFERS: WITH THE BUILT-IN MICROPHONE, USERS CAN RECORD THEIR FEEDBACK DIRECTLY ONTO THE DEVICE — AND EACH DEVICE CAN COLLECT HUNDREDS, OR EVEN THOUSANDS, OF USER FEEDBACK MESSAGES, TYPICALLY RECORDED IN A COMMUNITY'S LOCAL LANGUAGE. Every other information tool here pushes outward. This one comes back with the community's own voice on it, in their own language, unmediated by a form or a translator. For a consultation that was never really held, that is a way of producing the record the developer never took — hundreds of recorded statements from people who cannot write a submission. WHY THAT MATTERS, IN THEIR OWN FRAMING: WHILE IT IS A BEST PRACTICE TO INCLUDE STAKEHOLDERS IN THE EVALUATION PROCESS, IT IS NOT ALWAYS EASY, ESPECIALLY IN RURAL COMMUNITIES — PROJECT TEAMS OFTEN FACE BARRIERS DUE TO GEOGRAPHIC REMOTENESS, ILLITERACY AND LANGUAGE ABILITIES, AND POWER DYNAMICS. POWER DYNAMICS named alongside distance and literacy. People say different things into a device at home than in a meeting with the chief and the company sitting there — which is exactly why a recording made privately is worth more than a show of hands. WHAT PEOPLE ACTUALLY SAID WHEN GIVEN THE CHANCE: ONE PILOT COLLECTED 1,200 USER FEEDBACK MESSAGES IN ABOUT SIX MONTHS — PEOPLE ASKED A WIDE RANGE OF QUESTIONS ABOUT HEALTH SERVICES, THE COST OF HEALTH CARE, CORPORAL PUNISHMENT, CHILD PROTECTION ISSUES AND MORE. Twelve hundred messages in six months, on subjects nobody had put on the agenda. Give a community a way to speak and it raises what it actually cares about, not what the programme was designed around. THE HONEST PROCESSING PROBLEM, RECORDED BECAUSE IT WILL BE YOURS TOO: THE FEEDBACK WAS IN LOCAL LANGUAGES, SO THEY HAD TO WORK WITH LOCAL LANGUAGE SPEAKERS TO SORT AND PROCESS THE RECORDINGS AND FEED THE DATA INTO THE IMPACT ASSESSMENT AND, MORE IMPORTANTLY, INTO THE PROGRAM DESIGN — AND EXISTING SOFTWARE WAS TOO CUMBERSOME FOR AUDIO AND TOO COMPLEX FOR THE LOCAL LANGUAGE SPEAKERS TO NAVIGATE, SO THEY BUILT NEW WEB-BASED SOFTWARE FOR IT. Collecting the voices is the easy half. Budget for the people who will listen to a thousand recordings in the local language and sort them — and note that the tool for doing it was built because the professional software defeated the local speakers, which is a warning about every system handed to a community. WHO MAKES THE CONTENT: LOCAL PARTNERS ABLE TO CUSTOMIZE MESSAGES DEPENDING ON THE CULTURAL CONTEXT — USUALLY SONGS, DRAMAS, INTERVIEWS AND ENDORSEMENTS — PRODUCED WITH SUBJECT EXPERTS, MUSICIANS AND THEATER GROUPS, IN MORE THAN A DOZEN LANGUAGES. SONGS AND DRAMAS, made with musicians and theatre groups from the area. A land law explained as a drama by people the village knows is listened to; the same law read out as a notice is not. THE SHARING RATIO AND THE PRICE: A BUILT-IN SPEAKER ALLOWS FAMILIES AND GROUPS TO LISTEN AND LEARN TOGETHER, AND DEPENDING ON PROGRAM DESIGN A SINGLE DEVICE CAN SERVE 100 LISTENERS OR MORE — AND THERE IS NO COST TO THE END USER. One device, a hundred people. That changes the arithmetic of a funding request from a device per household to a handful per village. THE PHONE PLATFORM FOR EVERYONE WITHOUT A DEVICE: A VOICE PLATFORM LETS TEAMS REACH ENTIRE COMMUNITIES INSTANTLY — TEXT MESSAGES OR AUTOMATED VOICE CALLS TO THOUSANDS OF NUMBERS AT ONCE, INCLUDING BASIC FEATURE PHONES WITH NO INTERNET REQUIRED, DELIVERING CONTENT AND COLLECTING FEEDBACK OVER A REGULAR PHONE CALL. Automated voice calls to thousands of basic handsets. When a hearing date moves or an eviction notice appears, that is how a whole district is told in an hour — and the reply comes back by voice, not by form. THE AFRICAN ARM AND WHAT IT SELLS: A NON-PROFIT GHANAIAN ORGANISATION PARTNERS WITH GOVERNMENT AGENCIES, LOCAL NGOs AND INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATIONS TO PLAN AND DELIVER PROGRAMS IN THE HARDEST-TO-REACH RURAL COMMUNITIES, OFFERING SERVICES FROM TECHNOLOGY SETUP AND TRAINING TO PROGRAM DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION. An African organisation you can contract for the setup rather than importing a team. LOCAL NGOs are named among its partners, so a national organisation supporting your community is an eligible customer. THE MULTI-TOPIC POINT, FROM A GOVERNMENT HEALTH DIRECTOR RATHER THAN THE VENDOR: MOST OF OUR PARTNERS ARE WORKING ON MULTISECTORAL PROJECTS — WITH THE DEVICE WE CAN SHARE KNOWLEDGE ABOUT MANY TOPICS AND ADDRESS CRITICAL, INTERCONNECTED ISSUES, SUCH AS CLIMATE CHANGE AND GENDER EQUITY. THE REACH AND THE AFRICAN DEPLOYMENTS: OVER TWO MILLION PEOPLE IN 14 COUNTRIES SINCE 2007 — INCLUDING A LAND-RIGHTS PROGRAMME IN LIBERIA, AN ADOLESCENT RIGHTS PROJECT IN ZAMBIA, A SMART VILLAGES PROJECT IN NIGER, A 73-COMMUNITY FARMER PROGRAMME IN NORTHERN GHANA, AND A PROJECT THAT ECONOMICALLY EMPOWERED 23,000+ WOMEN FARMERS. A LAND-RIGHTS PROGRAMME IN LIBERIA is the precedent to cite: this exact device has already been used to explain a land law to rural people, which means the use case is proven rather than proposed. AND THE SCALE OF THE GAP: NEARLY 800 MILLION PEOPLE WORLDWIDE CANNOT READ OR WRITE. WHO IT SUITS: African communities where the law, the notice or the contract exists only in writing and only in a foreign language — and organisations that need the community's own answer on record. CAVEATS: SUPPLIED THROUGH PARTNER ORGANISATIONS AND GOVERNMENTS RATHER THAN SOLD TO VILLAGES, AND THE CONTENT AND FEEDBACK PROCESSING MUST BE BUDGETED — the Ghanaian arm is the route for setup. For talking books used in a land-rights programme, the Republic of the Congo's entry; for free radio scripts in local languages, Cape Verde's entry; for the association a station joins, Ethiopia's entry.

trackers.name: They reviewed every carbon standard's complaint system and named the only one that works — with a table of recommendations per standard, a benefit-sharing audit of 47 projects, and complaints filed in their own name on communities' behalf
trackers.desc: THEY REVIEWED EVERY CARBON STANDARD'S COMPLAINT SYSTEM AND NAMED THE ONE THAT WORKS — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S TOGO ENTRY COVERS THE TRAINING THAT PREPARES COMMUNITIES BEFORE A CARBON DEVELOPER ARRIVES, ITS SOUTH SUDAN ENTRY THE CARBON-VIOLENCE PLANTATION REPORT, ITS CHAD ENTRY THE INDIGENOUS-LED FUND, AND ITS TANZANIA AND DJIBOUTI ENTRIES PASTORALIST COALITIONS. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE REVIEW AND ITS SINGLE-NAME FINDING, WHICH IS THE FIND: A REVIEW CONDUCTED ON ITS BEHALF FOUND THAT ONLY ONE STANDARD BODY PROVIDES APPROPRIATE RECOURSE TO FILE GRIEVANCES TO COMMUNITIES AFFECTED BY CLIMATE PROJECTS — THE REMAINING ASSESSED STANDARDS HAVE INADEQUATE OR NON-EXISTENT GRIEVANCE MECHANISMS, LEAVING LOCAL COMMUNITIES AND INDIGENOUS PEOPLES VULNERABLE AND INFRINGING ON THEIR ACCESS TO JUSTICE. One out of all of them. Before a community spends a year filing under whichever standard certified the project on its land, this tells it whether that route exists at all — and the briefing names each standard with specific recommendations, so the answer for yours is a table lookup rather than a year of discovery. THE SUBMISSION CHANNELS IT DOCUMENTS, WHICH ARE WHAT TO DEMAND: REQUIREMENTS FOR GRIEVANCE SUBMISSIONS INCLUDE AN ONLINE COMPLAINTS FORM, MAIL, WHATSAPP, EMAIL, VOICE OR VIDEO RECORDING, CALLING A TOLL-FREE HOTLINE, OR AN IN-PERSON MEETING AT THE PLACE WHERE THE COMPLAINANT IS. WHATSAPP, VOICE RECORDING, AND A MEETING WHERE THE COMPLAINANT IS. A grievance system that only accepts a written English form has excluded the people it exists for — and here is a documented list of what an accessible one looks like, usable as the demand when yours does not. THE OVERALL VERDICT: MOST ARE OPAQUE AND DO NOT PROPERLY DESCRIBE THEIR PROCEDURES, WITH ONE STANDARD HAVING NO MECHANISM AT ALL — AND THE DOCUMENT PROVIDES DETAILED RECOMMENDATIONS OF GENERAL AND SPECIFIC ACTION FOR EACH STANDARD, SUMMARISED IN A TABLE. THE ACCESS PROBLEM NAMED BLUNTLY, WITH A CASE THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT: THE GRIEVANCE MECHANISMS FOR SUCH PROJECTS ARE TOO COMPLEX AND REMOTE FOR THE AFFECTED COMMUNITIES TO ACCESS EFFECTIVELY — ONE VILLAGE VISITED WISHED TO WITHDRAW ITS CONSENT FOR THE CARBON MARKET PROJECT BUT HAD NO IDEA HOW TO GO ABOUT THIS. A village that had decided to withdraw consent and could not find out how. Consent that cannot be withdrawn is not consent — and asking, before signing, exactly how a community exits and who to write to is a question this file has recorded almost nobody putting. THE BENEFIT-SHARING AUDIT AND ITS NUMBERS: A COMMISSIONED INVESTIGATION REVIEWED PROJECT DESIGN DOCUMENTS FROM 47 PROJECTS — ONLY 15 CONTAINED A REFERENCE TO BENEFIT SHARING; OF THOSE 15, ONLY FOUR CONTAINED EVIDENCE OF BENEFIT SHARING WITH LOCAL COMMUNITIES AND/OR INDIGENOUS PEOPLES; FIVE SHOWED BENEFIT SHARING ONLY WITH THE PROJECT IMPLEMENTERS OR COULD NOT BE ASCERTAINED; AND SIX CONTAINED NO EVIDENCE WHATSOEVER BEYOND A CURSORY REFERENCE. Four out of forty-seven. That is the honest base rate for a carbon project sharing anything with the community, measured from the projects' own design documents — and the design document is public, so yours can be checked the same way before anyone signs. THE COMPLAINTS IT FILES IN ITS OWN NAME: A LETTER FROM ITS EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR TO A CERTIFIER'S PRESIDENT DETAILING A FORMAL COMPLAINT ABOUT THE REGISTRATION OF AND ISSUANCE TO FOREST-CARBON PROJECTS, CALLING ON IT TO EXECUTE ITS GRIEVANCE MECHANISM — AND A SEPARATE COMPLAINT TO AN INTEGRITY COUNCIL FLAGGING THAT THE CERTIFIER'S REVIEW OF ANOTHER ORGANISATION'S GRIEVANCE WAS NOT IMPARTIAL. They complain about the complaint process itself, one level up. When a certifier reviews an accusation against a project it certified and clears it, the body that accredits the certifier is the next address — and somebody has already established that route works. THE STANDARD-ABOVE-THE-STANDARD THEY USED: AN ASSESSMENT FRAMEWORK CRITERION TITLED PUBLIC ENGAGEMENT, CONSULTATION AND GRIEVANCES REQUIRES THAT CARBON-CREDITING PROGRAMMES SHALL HAVE A PROCESS FOR ADDRESSING GRIEVANCES, WHICH SHALL BE CLEAR AND TRANSPARENT, ENSURE IMPARTIALITY AND WHERE APPROPRIATE CONFIDENTIALITY, IN THE FILING AND RESOLUTION OF GRIEVANCES. IMPARTIALITY, written into the framework the certifiers signed up to. If the people reviewing your complaint are the people who approved the project, that clause is the lever. THE AFRICAN EVENT AND CO-HOST: AN EVENT CO-ORGANISED WITH A NAMED MAASAI INTERNATIONAL SOLIDARITY ALLIANCE, AT WHICH COMMUNITY SPEAKERS DESCRIBED CARBON COLONIALISM — THE THREAT TO THEIR TRADITIONAL PASTORALIST WAY OF LIFE, THE RISK OF RENEWED WIDESCALE LAND GRABBING, FORCED CHANGES TO THEIR GRAZING PATTERNS, THE SPECTRE OF TENSION AND CONFLICT BETWEEN ADJACENT COMMUNITIES, CORRUPTION, AND THE DELAYING OF TRUE CLIMATE ACTION. An African pastoralist alliance as co-host, with its own people speaking. That alliance is a contact in its own right for communities facing the same projects. THE DIVISION IT WARNS ABOUT, WHICH IS THE HARM NOBODY BUDGETS FOR: THE POTENTIAL OF THESE PROJECTS TO SPARK CONFLICT BETWEEN COMMUNITIES WHO HAVE SIGNED UP AND THOSE WHO REFUSED TO SIGN. Neighbours set against each other by a signing bonus. Agreeing a common position with adjacent communities BEFORE the developer arrives is the cheapest protection available, and this file's coalition entries are where that gets organised. THE OTHER AFRICAN CASES ON RECORD: A NAMED ZIMBABWEAN FOREST-CARBON PROJECT FREQUENTLY CITED AS AN EXAMPLE; AND, IN KENYA, A REPORT BY TWO ORGANISATIONS ON WIDESPREAD SEXUAL HARASSMENT AND ABUSE BY SENIOR MALE STAFF MEMBERS AND RANGERS AT A 200,000-HECTARE FOREST-CARBON PROJECT AFFECTING 360,000 PEOPLE, WITH COMPLAINTS DATING BACK AT LEAST A DECADE. Rangers employed by a carbon project, and a decade of complaints. This file has recorded the same pattern under conservation enforcement; a carbon project that hires guards has created a policing force answerable to a company. AND THE PRICING FINDING: OPAQUE PRICING AND COMPLEX CHAINS OF INTERMEDIARIES MEAN COMMUNITIES RECEIVE ONLY A FRACTION OF WHAT BUYERS PAY. Ask what the credits sell for, not only what your share is. Without the buyer's price, a percentage means nothing — and the intermediary chain is where the rest goes. WHO IT SUITS: African communities inside or beside a carbon or REDD+ project, and organisations advising them before consent is given. CAVEATS: A RESEARCH AND ADVOCACY WATCHDOG, NOT A LEGAL SERVICE OR A FUNDER, AND EUROPE-BASED — pair the briefing with local counsel. For the training that prepares a community before a carbon developer arrives, Togo's entry; for the indigenous-led fund that pays communities directly, Chad's entry; for the pastoralist alliances, Tanzania's and Djibouti's entries.

trackers.name: Core flexible grants to unregistered grassroots collectives, applied for in any one of seven languages including French, Arabic and Portuguese — and decided by the applicants themselves, who vote on each other's proposals
trackers.desc: NO REGISTRATION, SEVEN LANGUAGES, AND THE APPLICANTS PICK THE WINNERS — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC ENTRY CARRIES A WOMEN'S FUND HOST; ITS CAMEROON ENTRY THE ADVISOR-NOMINATED GRASSROOTS FUND; ITS REPUBLIC OF CONGO ENTRY THE CATALYST-GRANT LADDER; ITS DR CONGO ENTRY THE INDIVIDUAL NOMINATION GRANT. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. PRECHECK AND AN EXACT HOST COMPARISON ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS WERE RUN BEFORE THIS ENTRY WAS WRITTEN. THE REGISTRATION RULE, WHICH IS THE FIND: YOU DO NOT NEED TO BE A LEGALLY REGISTERED ORGANIZATION TO APPLY — GRANTEES DO NOT NEED TO BE OFFICIALLY REGISTERED AS AN ASSOCIATION, AND INFORMAL AND FORMAL GROUPS, NETWORKS OR COLLECTIVES ARE BOTH ELIGIBLE. Registration is the gate this file has recorded closing more doors than any other single requirement. A collective of young women organising against a concession, a mine or an eviction does not need a constitution, an audit or a certificate to apply here. THE LANGUAGES, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: ALL APPLICATIONS ARE SENT ONLINE, AND YOU CAN APPLY IN ANY ONE OF SEVEN LANGUAGES — ARABIC, ENGLISH, FRENCH, RUSSIAN, SPANISH, PORTUGUESE OR MANDARIN. French, Arabic and Portuguese all accepted, and the application is written in whichever one you use. Francophone West and Central Africa, North Africa and the lusophone countries can apply without a translator — which this file has recorded as the quiet disqualifier across most of the funders in it. WHO DECIDES: YOU WANT THE FUNDING, SO YOU GET TO DECIDE WHO WE SHOULD FUND. ONCE YOUR GROUP IS SCREENED BY ADVISERS AND THE ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA ARE MET, YOU WILL BE INVITED TO VOTE FOR THE TOP GROUPS FROM YOUR REGION WHO YOU THINK SHOULD GET THE FUNDING; VOTES ARE TALLIED AND THE HIGHEST SCORING GROUPS GET THE GRANTS AFTER A DUE DILIGENCE PROCESS. The applicants are the panel. That means the document is written for peers in your own region rather than for a foreign officer — plain description of a real situation beats development jargon, because the readers live in the same conditions and can tell the difference. THE VOTING RULES: APPLICANTS WHO MEET THE CRITERIA ARE EXPECTED TO VOTE FOR THEIR TOP PROPOSAL CHOICES AND GIVE COMMENTS ON THEIR SELECTIONS, AND GROUPS MAY NOT VOTE FOR THEIR OWN PROPOSALS — WITH VOTERS ASKED TO KEEP IN MIND WHAT THEY THINK IS IMPORTANT FOR THE PROMOTION AND DEFENCE OF RIGHTS IN THEIR REGION. Voting is an expectation, not an option. Applying commits you to reading other groups' proposals — which is itself the most direct way this file has recorded of finding out who else in your region is organising, and on what. WHAT STAFF DO INSTEAD OF CHOOSING: RATHER THAN CHOOSING RECIPIENTS, STAFF ARE CHARGED WITH HELPING APPLICANTS THROUGH THE PROCESS, ASSISTING WITH SCREENING TO ASSURE APPLICANTS MEET THE CRITERIA, AND CHECKING APPLICANTS' REFERENCES — WITH APPLICATIONS REVIEWED AND VOTED ON BY BOTH CURRENT GRANTEES FROM PAST CYCLES AND THE APPLICANTS THEMSELVES. Staff exist to get you through the form. Ask them for help; that is the job as they have defined it. THE AMOUNT AND WHAT KIND OF MONEY IT IS: GRANTS OF UP TO USD 5,000 IN EARLIER CYCLES AND USD 6,000 TO ALL GROUPS AWARDED GRANTS IN A LATER ONE — DESCRIBED AS CORE, FLEXIBLE FUNDING AND AS GENERAL SUPPORT FUNDING. CORE and FLEXIBLE at that size is unusual. It pays for the things a project grant refuses: transport to a hearing, phone credit, food at a meeting, somebody's time. WHO IS ELIGIBLE, STATED EXACTLY: GROUPS LED BY YOUNG WOMEN, GIRLS, TRANS AND/OR INTERSEX YOUTH AGED 30 AND UNDER — AT LEAST 70% OF THE MEMBERSHIP MUST BE WOMEN, GIRLS, TRANS AND/OR INTERSEX YOUTH UNDER 30, AND THE LEADERSHIP OR THE INDIVIDUALS WITH DECISION-MAKING POWER MUST BE THE SAME. A hard threshold, and worth checking against your actual membership before writing anything. Where a wider community organisation does not qualify, a young women's committee within it may — constituted in its own name, with its own leadership. THE AFRICAN REGIONS COVERED: GROUPS, NETWORKS OR COLLECTIVES BASED IN WEST, EAST, SOUTH AND CENTRAL AFRICA, AND IN SOUTH WEST ASIA AND NORTH AFRICA. Every part of the continent, North Africa included. WHO IT IS FOR: SMALL AND EMERGING GRASSROOTS GROUPS, NETWORKS OR COLLECTIVES WITH LITTLE OR NO ACCESS TO MAJOR FUNDING — COMMITTED TO INCLUSIVE ORGANIZING, COLLECTIVE ACTION AND MOVEMENT BUILDING. LITTLE OR NO ACCESS TO MAJOR FUNDING is the qualifying condition. Having never been funded is an advantage here, not the disadvantage it is almost everywhere else in this file. THE TWO GROUPS IT SAYS IT LOOKS FOR: GROUPS USING CREATIVE AND INNOVATIVE STRATEGIES TO FURTHER THEIR ACTIVISM — INCLUDING ART, MUSIC, CULTURE, POETRY, SOCIAL MEDIA AND ACTIVIST-DRIVEN RESEARCH — AND GROUPS LOCATED IN REMOTE, UNDERSERVED AREAS. REMOTE, UNDERSERVED AREAS named as a priority rather than a logistical problem. The village far from the capital is what they are looking for. WHAT COMES WITH THE MONEY, AND THE CYCLE: THE FUNDS ARE MORE THAN JUST MONEY — SELECTED GROUPS PARTICIPATE IN CAPACITY BUILDING AND NETWORKING ACTIVITIES; OPEN CALLS ARE ISSUED PERIODICALLY, ONE RAN FOR SIX WEEKS, AND BETWEEN ROUNDS THE ORGANISATION SOLICITS FEEDBACK FROM ALL STAKEHOLDERS TO REFINE ITS PROCESSES. IF YOU HAVE APPLIED IN PREVIOUS YEARS, YOU ARE WELCOME TO APPLY AGAIN. Six weeks is a short window and the calls are periodic rather than annual. Watch for the opening rather than checking once a year — and a previous rejection is explicitly no bar. AND THE LIMIT IT STATES PLAINLY: IT WILL NOT PROVIDE FUNDING TO GROUPS LED BY YOUNG CIS MEN EVEN IF THEY SELF-DEFINE AS FEMINISTS, BECAUSE OF LIMITED RESOURCES DEDICATED TO ADDRESSING THE FUNDAMENTAL INEQUALITY AND DISCRIMINATION FACED BY GIRLS, YOUNG WOMEN, TRANS AND INTERSEX YOUTH — AND ITS REGIONAL COMMITTEES ARE THEMSELVES SELECTED EVERY TWO YEARS THROUGH AN OPEN APPLICATION PROCESS. The exclusion is stated rather than left for applicants to discover after the work of applying. And the regional committees are themselves openly recruited — so a young African activist can sit on the body that shapes the round, not only apply to it. WHO IT SUITS: unregistered collectives of young women and girls in African communities facing land, mining or infrastructure pressure — including in remote areas, applying in their own language. CAVEATS: A HARD ELIGIBILITY THRESHOLD ON AGE, LEADERSHIP AND 70% MEMBERSHIP; CALLS ARE PERIODIC AND SHORT; AND APPLYING COMMITS YOU TO VOTING — a community organisation that does not meet the threshold should look to the funds filed under Cameroon and the Central African Republic instead.

trackers.name: An Africa-based defenders organisation staffed partly by exiled defenders themselves, covering eleven East and Horn of Africa countries — with a 24/7 emergency phone number, a street address, a secure protection-grant form, and a regional network you can join
trackers.desc: AN AFRICAN ORGANISATION, STAFFED BY EXILED DEFENDERS, WITH THE PHONE NUMBER PUBLISHED — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S REPUBLIC OF CONGO ENTRY NAMES AN EAST AND HORN OF AFRICA DEFENDERS PROJECT AS A CONSORTIUM DELIVERY PARTNER WITHOUT IDENTIFYING OR DESCRIBING IT; ITS DR CONGO ENTRY THE VOLUNTEER LAWYERS' COMMITTEE; ITS EQUATORIAL GUINEA BUCKET A PROTECTION GRANTS HOST. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. WHO RUNS IT, WHICH IS THE FIND: WE ARE AN AFRICA-BASED ORGANISATION, RUN BY PEOPLE FROM THE SUB-REGION — AND IN IT, MANY ARE EXILED HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS THEMSELVES, WHICH ENABLES THE ORGANISATION TO FILL THE GAP USING THE RELEVANT TOOLS, METHODS AND STRATEGIES. The people assessing your emergency have been through one. Every other protection resource in this file is answered from Europe or North America by staff who have read about the situation; here the person on the line may have fled the same country. That changes what has to be explained and what is believed without evidence. THE PUBLISHED CONTACT DETAILS, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: A 24/7 EMERGENCY PHONE LINE AND A SEPARATE GENERAL PHONE LINE, BOTH WITH FULL INTERNATIONAL NUMBERS PUBLISHED; A SECURE EMAIL FORM; A SECURE FORM TO APPLY FOR A PROTECTION GRANT; AND A FULL STREET ADDRESS AND POST BOX IN A NAMED CAPITAL CITY. A telephone number you can dial at three in the morning and an address you can walk into. This file has recorded almost nothing else offering both — and the separate general line matters, because not every question is an emergency and using the emergency line for routine matters is how it gets blocked. WHAT IT PROVIDES: IT PROTECTS DEFENDERS THROUGH EMERGENCY SUPPORT, PROTECTION GRANTS, RELOCATION PROGRAMMES AND LEGAL SUPPORT. LEGAL SUPPORT sits alongside the protection work, so an arrested organiser's defence and their safety are handled by the same body rather than assembled from two. THE COUNTRIES IT COVERS: BURUNDI, DJIBOUTI, ERITREA, ETHIOPIA, KENYA, RWANDA, SOMALIA TOGETHER WITH SOMALILAND, SOUTH SUDAN, SUDAN, TANZANIA AND UGANDA. Eleven named countries, including several this file has struggled to find any responsive resource for. Somaliland is named alongside Somalia, which resolves a coverage question that defeats many international bodies. WHERE IT ADVOCATES ON THEIR BEHALF: AT THE UNITED NATIONS HUMAN RIGHTS COUNCIL AND THE AFRICAN COMMISSION ON HUMAN AND PEOPLES' RIGHTS. Both the global and the continental forum, from one organisation. A community's case can be raised at the African Commission by a body that is itself African and regional, rather than through an intermediary in another hemisphere. WHAT IT TRAINS PEOPLE IN: PHYSICAL AND DIGITAL SECURITY, ADVOCACY, MONITORING AND REPORTING, AND MENTAL HEALTH — ALONGSIDE PROTECTION AND SECURITY MANAGEMENT, TECHNOLOGY DEVELOPMENT, RESEARCH AND COMMUNICATIONS. MONITORING AND REPORTING training is the practical bridge: it teaches a community organisation to produce the documented record that the funders, courts and UN mechanisms elsewhere in this file all assume it already has. THE NETWORK IT IS THE SECRETARIAT OF, AND HOW TO JOIN: IT SERVES AS THE SECRETARIAT OF A REGIONAL DEFENDERS NETWORK REPRESENTING HUNDREDS OF MEMBERS — INDIVIDUAL DEFENDERS, HUMAN RIGHTS ORGANISATIONS AND NATIONAL DEFENDER COALITIONS — WITH THREE MEMBERSHIP CATEGORIES PUBLISHED TOGETHER WITH THE CRITERIA FOR ADMISSION AND THE OBLIGATIONS OF EACH MEMBER. Criteria and obligations both published, so an organisation can decide before applying whether it qualifies and what it would be taking on. Individual defenders are a membership category, so a person without an organisation is not excluded. THE NATIONAL COALITIONS IT BUILDS: IT ESTABLISHES AND SUPPORTS NATIONAL COALITIONS OF DEFENDERS IN VARIOUS COUNTRIES, THROUGH WHICH DEFENDERS CAN COME TOGETHER AND CLAIM THEIR RIGHTS AT THE NATIONAL LEVEL. Where no national coalition exists in your country, this is the body that helps constitute one — the same answer the bar-association work in this file's Cameroon entry gives for lawyers, applied to defenders generally. WHAT THE NETWORK ASKS ITS MEMBERS TO PASS ON: INFORMATION ABOUT HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS FORCED TO LEAVE THEIR COUNTRIES OF ORIGIN AND OTHERS WHO ARE UNDER THREAT SHOULD ALSO BE SHARED. Reporting other people's cases is a stated membership obligation. That is how a defender who cannot reach anyone gets reached — through somebody else's report — and it means a third party can raise a case on their behalf. THE GAP IT WAS BUILT TO FILL: BEFORE IT EXISTED, THERE WERE NO REGIONAL ORGANISATIONS PROMOTING AND COORDINATING THE WORK OF HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS IN THE EAST AND HORN OF AFRICA. ITS MANDATE AND STANDING: ESTABLISHED IN 2005 AND REGISTERED AS A FOREIGN NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATION IN A NAMED COUNTRY, ITS CORE MANDATE IS TO PROMOTE THE SAFETY, SECURITY AND WELLBEING OF DEFENDERS — REDUCING THEIR VULNERABILITY TO THE RISK OF PERSECUTION. AND THE WIDER CONTINENTAL FAMILY IT SITS IN, WITH A WARNING FROM IT: IT IS ONE OF SEVERAL REGIONAL MEMBER NETWORKS OF A CONTINENTAL DEFENDERS BODY — WHOSE MEMBERS PUBLICLY RECORDED DEEP CONCERN AT THE IMPOSITION OF A RESTRICTION ON THE NETWORK OF HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS IN CENTRAL AFRICA, BARRING IT FROM OPERATING THROUGHOUT A NAMED COUNTRY. Two things follow. There are sister networks for West, Southern and Central Africa, so a defender outside these eleven countries has a regional equivalent to find. And one of those networks was banned from operating in a country — recorded plainly, because it means the regional body you rely on can itself be shut out, and a second contact outside the region is worth holding. WHO IT SUITS: land and environmental defenders and community organisations in the eleven named countries — for emergency help, protection grants, legal support, training or network membership. CAVEATS: BOUND TO THE EAST AND HORN OF AFRICA; DEFENDERS ELSEWHERE ON THE CONTINENT NEED THE SISTER NETWORK FOR THEIR REGION, AND THE REGIONAL NETWORKS THEMSELVES CAN BE RESTRICTED BY GOVERNMENTS. It protects defenders rather than litigating your land claim. For the EU mechanism it delivers for, the Republic of Congo's entry; for the volunteer lawyers' committee that campaigns for threatened lawyers, DR Congo's entry.

trackers.name: SELAVIP — grants up to USD 72,000 per project for land title regularization, new housing and water, free to the families with no reimbursement, open annually to any legally incorporated non-profit in Africa, Asia or Latin America
trackers.desc: A GRANT, NOT A LOAN, AND IT PAYS FOR THE TITLE — method and adjacency declared first: THIRD ACQUISITION-ONLY ROUND; THIS BUCKET WAS THE THINNEST MEASURED PAIR REMAINING. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THREE HOSTS AND FIVE DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL HOSTS AND FOUR FACTS ABSENT. THE FOUNDATION'S NAME APPEARS ONCE, INSIDE A FIVE-FUNDER LIST IN A ZAMBIA ENTRY ON A GOVERNMENT-ASSETS HOST — A PASSING MENTION WITH NO DESCRIPTION AND A DIFFERENT HOST, NOT RESTATED HERE. THIS FILE'S TUNISIA AND SOMALIA ENTRIES COVER THE CO-OPERATIVE UNION AND THE RESIDENTS' REVOLVING FUND, BOTH CREDIT RATHER THAN GRANT; ITS EQUATORIAL GUINEA AND LIBYA ENTRIES THE CONSERVATION LAND-PURCHASE FUNDS. NONE IS RESTATED. WHAT IT FUNDS, WHICH IS THE FIND: A PRIVATE FOUNDATION THAT SUPPORTS HOUSING PROJECTS — NEW HOUSING, LAND TITLE REGULARIZATION AND WATER SYSTEMS — FOR VERY POOR URBAN FAMILIES IN THE CITIES OF AFRICA, ASIA AND LATIN AMERICA, WITH PRIORITY GIVEN TO INITIATIVES THAT HELP THE POOR ACCESS LAND AND SECURE BASIC SHELTER. LAND TITLE REGULARIZATION as a funded category in its own right. The last two acquisition rounds filed credit — money a household repays. This is a grant, and it pays for the part communities almost never find funding for: the survey, the fees and the paperwork that turn occupation into a title. WHO IT IS FOR, IN ITS OWN WORDS, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: ITS FOCUS IS ON EXTREME SOCIAL EMERGENCY FACED BY URBAN GROUPS DWELLING IN PRECARIOUS AND UNSAFE CONDITIONS AND PLACES, OR EXPOSED TO EVICTIONS — OPENING REALISTIC ALTERNATIVES FOR THOSE WHO DO NOT FIT INTO ANY EXISTING HOUSING PROGRAMS, PUBLIC OR PRIVATE. EXPOSED TO EVICTIONS, written into the eligibility. A community under threat of clearance is not an awkward fit for this fund; it is the stated target. THE MONEY, WITH ITS CEILINGS AND ITS FLOOR: THE MAXIMUM AMOUNT GRANTED PER PROJECT IS USD 72,000, WITH THE MAXIMUM CONTRIBUTION PER NEW DWELLING AT USD 1,400 — AND IT WILL NOT CONSIDER PROJECTS WHOSE TOTAL COST IS LESS THAN USD 20,000, EXCEPT LAND REGULARIZATION RELATED PROJECTS. The exception is the important half: the $20,000 floor does NOT apply to land regularization. A small community wanting titles, and only titles, can apply for a modest sum — which is the one door in this file open to a group too small for a development grant. And $1,400 per dwelling matches, almost exactly, the per-home construction cost recorded in this file's Tunisia entry. THE RULE THAT MATTERS MOST TO A FAMILY: THE CONTRIBUTION IS FREE FOR THE BENEFICIARIES AND MUST BE USED SOLELY FOR THE SELECTED PROJECT — AND IT REQUIRES A DOCUMENT SIGNED BY EACH BENEFICIARY FAMILY CONFIRMING ITS ACTIVE PARTICIPATION AND ACKNOWLEDGING THAT THE CONTRIBUTION IS FREE FOR THEM, MEANING THEY MAY NOT BE ASKED ANY REIMBURSEMENT OR REFUND. Each family signs a paper saying nobody may charge them for this. That clause exists because intermediaries do charge, and it hands every household a document to produce if an organisation later asks for repayment. Worth copying into any grant a community accepts on its members' behalf. HOW THE MONEY MUST BE SPENT: AT LEAST 95% OF THE FINANCIAL RESOURCES SHOULD BE USED FOR THE PURCHASE OF MATERIALS — AND IN THE CASE OF LAND TITLE REGULARIZATION, THE RESOURCES ARE USED FOR THAT PROCESS. Ninety-five per cent to materials means almost nothing for staff time. An applicant organisation must have its own overheads covered from elsewhere, which is the practical constraint to plan for before applying. WHO MAY APPLY: ALL NON-PROFIT AND LEGALLY INCORPORATED PRIVATE AND PUBLIC INSTITUTIONS, NGOs, FOUNDATIONS AND RELIGIOUS ORGANIZATIONS MAY ANSWER THE CALL — PROVIDED THEY ARE DULY REGISTERED AND APPROVED IN ITS REGISTRY OF ORGANIZATIONS, WITH PUBLISHED STEPS TO CREATE AN ACCOUNT, REGISTER THE NGO AND APPLY THROUGH ITS MANAGEMENT SYSTEM. RELIGIOUS ORGANIZATIONS are explicitly eligible, which matters where the parish or mosque committee is the only incorporated body a settlement has. But note the registration requirement: an unregistered community group needs a constituted partner to apply through, the same barrier this file records at almost every funder. THE WOMEN'S OWNERSHIP PREFERENCE, STATED AS A SELECTION FACTOR: TO CONSIDER WOMEN AS ASSIGNEES AND OWNERS IN LAND REGULARIZATION RELATED PROJECTS. Putting women's names on the title scores better in the assessment. Read beside this file's Sudan entry on tenure held through a husband ending with him: here the funder pays for the correction. THE SIX OBJECTIVES IT PUBLISHES: TO ENCOURAGE LOCAL DONORS TO JOIN IT; TO SECURE LAND TITLE FOR THE POOREST OF POOR IN URBAN SLUMS; TO PROMOTE FRESH WATER, BASIC SANITARY AND SEWAGE EQUIPMENT; TO FACILITATE THE EXCHANGE OF KNOW-HOW BETWEEN NGOs; TO ENCOURAGE HOUSING MECHANISMS THAT CAN GROW INTRINSICALLY OVER TIME; AND TO ENCOURAGE MECHANISMS THAT WILL SERVE AS REFERENCE AND EXAMPLE FOR REPLICATION. GROW INTRINSICALLY OVER TIME and SERVE AS REFERENCE FOR REPLICATION are the two that shape a winning application: a proposal that ends when the money does will score worse than one that seeds something continuing. WHAT IT ASKS PROPOSALS TO DO: MEET HOUSING AND SANITATION NEEDS FROM URBAN FAMILIES, FROM HOUSING PRODUCTION OR SLUM IMPROVEMENT TO PROMOTION OF COMMUNITY BASED PROCESSES TO SECURE SHELTER. WHO IT WANTS TO BRING IN: MORE COMMUNITIES, LEADERS, VOLUNTEERS, PROFESSIONALS AND INSTITUTIONS FROM THE DEVELOPING WORLD, HOPING TO RECEIVE INNOVATIVE PROPOSALS AND TO SUPPORT THE MOST DARING PROJECTS. HOW IT DECIDES AND FROM WHERE: FOUNDED FOUR DECADES AGO BY FATHER JOSSE VAN REST S.J., ITS BOARD MEETS EVERY YEAR IN NOVEMBER IN ONE EUROPEAN CITY AND PROVIDES GUIDELINES THAT ORIENT THE WORK OF ITS OPERATIONAL UNIT BASED IN A SOUTH AMERICAN CAPITAL — AND IT RESERVES THE RIGHT TO DECREASE THE REQUESTED AMOUNT AND THE NUMBER OF SOLUTIONS ACCORDING TO BUDGET AVAILABILITY. A November board meeting setting the following year's guidelines is a calendar an applicant can work to, and the right to cut the requested amount means a proposal should be able to survive being funded at less than it asked for. AND WHAT IT OFFERS BESIDES MONEY: SUPPORT FOR NEW BASIC, INCREMENTAL OR EMERGENCY HOUSING AS WELL AS RENOVATION OR REPAIR, WITH FUNDING, TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, STRATEGIC ALLIANCES AND TRAINING MATERIAL — ITS FOCUS INCLUDING ACCESS TO WATER AND SANITATION. INCREMENTAL housing is worth noting: it will fund a house built in stages rather than requiring a finished unit, which is how households actually build. WHO IT SUITS: urban communities facing eviction who need titles rather than buildings, and any incorporated non-profit — including a church body — applying on their behalf. CAVEATS: URBAN ONLY, SO RURAL AND CUSTOMARY LAND FALLS OUTSIDE IT; THE APPLICANT MUST BE A REGISTERED LEGAL ENTITY, 95% OF FUNDS MUST GO TO MATERIALS, AND FIGURES CITED COME FROM PUBLISHED CALLS OF PARTICULAR YEARS — CHECK THE CURRENT CALL. For credit rather than grant, Tunisia's and Somalia's entries; for funds that buy rural land outright, Equatorial Guinea's and Libya's entries.

trackers.name: Observatoire Congolais des Droits de l’Homme (OCDH)
trackers.desc: Leading independent human-rights organization in the Republic of Congo (Congo-Brazzaville), founded in 1994 — it monitors and documents the country’s catastrophic prison conditions and deaths in custody from starvation and neglect, torture and arbitrary detention, and the treatment of political prisoners, runs projects to prevent torture and arbitrary detention, and supports victims of human-rights violations in seeking justice; an ACHPR-observer NGO and member of FIDH and the World Organisation Against Torture, twice awarded the French Republic’s Human Rights Prize.

trackers.name: Association pour les Droits de l'Homme et l'Univers Carcéral (ADHUC)
trackers.desc: L’association pour les Droits de L’Homme et de L’Univers (ADHU) is concerned with the protection and promotion of human rights, in particular the rights of indigenous peoples such as the Pygmies. It is also concerned with respecting the rights of prisoners and improving conditions in Congolese detention facilities.

trackers.name: Cour des comptes et de discipline budgétaire
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Congo (Rep.), auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: ITIE Congo
trackers.desc: National Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative body — discloses oil, gas and mining revenues, contracts and licences in Republic of the Congo.

trackers.name: Republic of the Congo — Agence Congolaise pour la Création des Entreprises (ACPCE)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the ACPCE one-stop window centralises company-creation formalities, legal announcements & the business register, Republic of the Congo. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Republic of the Congo — Ministère des Finances, du Budget et du Portefeuille public
trackers.desc: National budget authority; prepares & executes the State budget and manages public finances & the public portfolio, Republic of the Congo (Brazzaville). Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in the Republic of the Congo.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: COMIFAC Treaty and Plan de Convergence — and its community protocol
trackers.desc: A TREATY BODY WITH A TEMPLATE YOU CAN COPY. The Traité relatif à la conservation et à la gestion durable des écosystèmes forestiers d'Afrique Centrale, signed by heads of state at their second summit on 5 February 2005 in Brazzaville, instituted the Commission des Forêts d'Afrique Centrale — described as the unique instance d'orientation, de décision et de coordination for subregional forest action, and the cadre politique et juridique global for cooperation in the field. A transboundary forest question belongs in that forum. The Plan de Convergence is the reference framework for all such interventions — first edition 2005–2014, revised in 2014 for 2015–2025 and restructured into 10 strategic axes, executed by a Secrétariat exécutif. CIVIL SOCIETY IS A NAMED STAKEHOLDER in implementing it, alongside state administrations, CEEAC and the private sector — so participation is built into the framework, not conceded case by case. Axis 7 covers capacity and participation des acteurs, expressly contemplating micro-projets générateurs de revenus pour les populations locales; axis 9 covers innovative financing mechanisms. THE DOCUMENT LIBRARY IS THE MOST USEFUL PART: COMIFAC publishes a worked Protocole Bioculturel Communautaire for a named village, a guide to inventorying genetic resources and traditional knowledge, a paper on les droits d'usage des peuples autochtones et communautés locales et les obligations qui en découlent, a subregional APA (access and benefit-sharing) strategy, and directives on forests and the SDGs built with FAO as 5 principles and 12 directives across 31 prioritised targets. A community biocultural protocol published by a treaty body is a template, not a theory. AND ITS OWN DIAGNOSIS IS QUOTABLE: the Plan records that participatory natural resource management and mediation of use conflicts, though already mapped out, are insufficiently developed.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: Comptoir Juridique Junior — free legal clinics in Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire, staffed by young lawyers and supervised by magistrates
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Congolese association founded in 2000 by young jurists, which runs free legal clinics in neighbourhoods of Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire — open since 2002, staffed by young and unemployed lawyers, supervised by professional magistrates. The premise is the one that matters where courts feel unreachable: people have no money for an advocate and no confidence in the system, so the clinic is the relay that gets them into it. Its services are free legal advice, judicial accompaniment, and alternative dispute resolution — mediation and non-violent communication — alongside information campaigns and training. WHY IT BELONGS IN THIS MAP RATHER THAN A GENERAL LEGAL AID LIST: CJJ states that it fights continuously for the rights of indigenous peoples in the Republic of Congo through projects across the country, and it hosts the Congolese arm of the standardised external independent forest monitoring system, SNOIE-Congo — a certified process for documenting forest infractions and getting them to the authorities, run out of its Brazzaville office with a technical and ethics evaluation committee. A community with a logging or land problem therefore gets both the documentation route and the lawyers in one place. It also does citizen monitoring of public spending. B.P. 13700 Brazzaville. WHO IT SUITS: indigenous and rural communities and poor urban households in the Republic of Congo; the clinics take general civil matters too, which is how most people first walk in. CAVEATS: a small, lightly structured association run substantially on volunteers, and the reported caseload is heavy across many subjects, so expect queues; published email addresses are personal or generic, and older material sits on a legacy Google Sites page as well as the current domain.

trackers.name: RPDH, Pointe-Noire — works the cahier des charges, the schedule of obligations a company owes your village, and why it goes unrespected
trackers.desc: WHO ENFORCES WHAT THE COMPANY OWES YOU: Rencontre pour la Paix et les Droits de l'Homme (RPDH), a Congolese organisation working on natural resource governance, which publishes on what prevents respect of the CAHIER DES CHARGES in the Kouilou department — the schedule of social obligations a forestry or mining company signs up to for the communities around its permit. If a company promised your village a school, a road or a water point, that promise lives in the cahier des charges; the document exists whether or not anyone has shown it to you, and the first move is to obtain it and read what was actually signed. RPDH also anchors the national chapter of the extractives transparency coalition, whose published monitoring has covered 179 public investment projects in health, energy and water across a budget year, and it convenes national multi-actor forums on climate initiatives and sustainable forest management jointly with the Congolese human rights observatory. THE LAW THAT CHANGED IN 2020, AND THE GAP INSIDE IT: law n°33-2020 of 8 July 2020, the forest code, for the first time in Congo authorises forest management directly by LOCAL COMMUNITIES AND INDIGENOUS POPULATIONS (CLPA) — community forestry. Communities affected by logging also hold a right to benefit-sharing under a specific cahier des charges, and management plans must be adopted by a commission including civil society, local authorities and the communities and indigenous peoples concerned. BUT the code does NOT set out the attribution procedure: it defers to a ministerial order for how a community forest is allocated and delimited, how the monitoring body works, and what the simple management plan must contain — so ask whether that order has been issued before relying on the right. Community representatives have separately demanded that government and extractive companies guarantee their involvement in drawing up those particular cahiers de charges. WHO IT SUITS: Congolese villages beside a logging or mining permit, especially in Kouilou and the south-west, and communities pursuing benefit-sharing or the new community forestry route. CAVEATS: a governance, monitoring and advocacy organisation — not a law firm and not a fund; the community forestry route depends on implementing texts that may not yet exist. For free legal clinics in Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire, Congo's Comptoir Juridique Junior entry; for indigenous rights monitoring, OCDH.

trackers.name: Congo's Fonds de Développement Local — each forest unit's fund has its own published arrêté fixing the project/running-cost SPLIT and the payment dates
trackers.desc: THE MONEY OWED TO YOUR VILLAGE: in Congo-Brazzaville each unité forestière d'aménagement (UFA) has a SÉRIE DE DÉVELOPPEMENT COMMUNAUTAIRE with its own FONDS DE DÉVELOPPEMENT LOCAL, fed by a redevance paid by the logging company, and each fund is governed by its OWN ARRÊTÉ PUBLISHED IN THE JOURNAL OFFICIEL — Ngombé, Missa, Ipendja, Loundoungou-Toukoulaka, Djua-Ikié among them. Find the arrêté for the UFA next to your village: it is a public document and it states the rules of your fund by name. WHAT THOSE ARRÊTÉS ACTUALLY FIX, and this is the number to check first: the SPLIT between projects and administration — at Ngombé and Missa, 85% to the activities in the annual programme and 15% to running costs; at Djua-Ikié, 70% to activities and 30% to running costs INCLUDING PAYING A TECHNICAL ASSISTANT. Compare that with Gabon, where monitors found a company charging committee running costs against the fund with no ceiling at all — a published percentage is the defence. Djua-Ikié further splits the investment share 60% to microprojects of the communities DIRECTLY IMPACTED in or near the annual cutting block, 40% to the others. WHEN THE MONEY MUST ARRIVE: the arrêtés set the instalments — 50% of the annual redevance on delivery of the annual cutting authorisation, 25% in the first half of June, and 25% on completion of the annual cut AFTER the exploited volume has been readjusted. That last clause matters: the final instalment is recalculated on the volume actually cut, so ask for the readjustment figure. TWO PROTECTIONS WORTH KNOWING: cheques for disbursement must be countersigned by the president, the second vice-president of the conseil de concertation and the fund's accountant; and unused funds at year-end are automatically returned IN FULL to the local development fund rather than lapsing. WHO IT SUITS: Congolese villages inside or beside a forest management unit. CAVEATS: A CONTRACTUAL AND REGULATORY ENTITLEMENT, NOT A GRANT — it exists only where a UFA operates, and reporting from Louvakou records expropriation without compensation where land was sold to companies without the village committee's agreement. For the cahier des charges and mining, Congo's RPDH entry; for free legal clinics, Comptoir Juridique Junior; for indigenous rights, OCDH.

trackers.name: Réserve Communautaire du Lac Télé — 438,960 hectares and the ONLY community protected area in Congo; the precedent to cite when asking for a second
trackers.desc: THE ONE COMMUNITY-HELD AREA IN THE COUNTRY: the RÉSERVE COMMUNAUTAIRE DU LAC TÉLÉ-LIKOUALA-AUX-HERBES (RCLT), 438,960 HECTARES in the Likouala department, is recorded as THE ONLY CONGOLESE PROTECTED AREA DESCRIBED AS COMMUNAUTAIRE, and THE FIRST OF ITS TYPE TO BE INSCRIBED ON THE RAMSAR LIST as a wetland of international importance — swamp forest, seasonally flooded forest, savanna and marsh. One precedent is enough to argue from: a community reserve of that size already exists in Congolese law and practice, so the answer to a request for a second one cannot be that the category does not exist. WHAT THE LAW PROVIDES AND WHAT IT STILL LACKS, STATED TOGETHER: Congo's protected-areas law lists COMMUNITY RESERVES alongside special reserves, wildlife sanctuaries and zones of interest and is the central legal instrument for protected-area management — BUT its implementing texts were recorded as STILL BEING VALIDATED, so it is NOT YET EQUIPPED WITH THE DECREES that would let it operate fully. Ask which implementing decree governs the category you are applying under, and whether it has been published — this is the fifth Congolese instrument in this file where the statute exists and the machinery lags. A SECOND ROUTE IN THE SAME LEGAL FAMILY: the forest code does not mention protected areas explicitly but defines FORÊTS DE CONSERVATION NATURELLE (article 10), part of the state domain, whose mission is to secure the permanence of forest species, protect wildlife and flora habitats and preserve landscapes — and it sets the management rules for their peripheral zones, which is where villages sit. WHO IT SUITS: Congolese communities seeking recognised protection over a large shared territory, especially wetland or swamp-forest, and anyone needing a domestic precedent. CAVEATS: A STATE-RECOGNISED COMMUNITY RESERVE, NOT COMMUNITY OWNERSHIP — management is co-run and the enabling decrees were incomplete at the time recorded; verify the current position. For the logging fund your villages are owed and its published percentages, Congo's Fonds de Développement Local entry; for the cahier des charges and mining, RPDH; for free consultation, the bureaux de consultations gratuites.

trackers.name: Renatura Congo, Pointe-Noire — a Congolese association backing the country's first marine protected area, with a citizen observation tool anyone can file into, plus the unmandated forest-observation route
trackers.desc: THE COASTAL ORGANISATION AND THE UNMANDATED OBSERVATION ROUTE: RENATURA CONGO (renatura.org), AN ASSOCIATION OF CONGOLESE LAW FOUNDED IN 2005 AT POINTE-NOIRE, promotes sustainable development through preserving biodiversity by ACTION — studies and activities to safeguard THREATENED NATURAL ENVIRONMENTS — INFORMATION of the public, and SUPPORT TO PROJECTS relating to the protection of threatened species and environments, working for over twenty years ALONG THE WHOLE CONGOLESE COASTLINE, combining scientific research, field conservation, environmental education and SUPPORT TO PUBLIC POLICY. THE PART THAT MAKES IT A RESOURCE RATHER THAN A CHARITY: ITS WORK INCLUDES SUPPORT TO THE CREATION OF THE FIRST MARINE PROTECTED AREA IN CONGO. An organisation that is actively building the country's first marine protected area is the one to approach if your coast needs a designation — there is a first, it is unfinished, and the people doing it are named and based in Pointe-Noire. Renatura became an IUCN MEMBER at the union's 117th council session, and its programme includes daily monitoring of nesting beaches, release of accidental captures from artisanal fishing nets, and weekly sea outings from JULY TO SEPTEMBER to study humpback whales. HOW AN ORDINARY PERSON CONTRIBUTES: with a Cameroonian NGO's CITIZEN AND PARTICIPATORY DATA-COLLECTION TOOL, originally built to work with ARTISANAL FISHERS on manatee sightings and adapted for wider ocean users, ANYONE — FISHER, SAILOR, RESEARCHER, SURFER, TOURIST, SEA WORKER OR RESIDENT OF KOUILOU OR POINTE-NOIRE — CAN RECORD THEIR OBSERVATIONS OF THE MARINE ENVIRONMENT. A tool that lets a fisherman file a dated observation is how a coastline gets a record before a project arrives. Renatura's own instruction for a stranded or nesting turtle is: do not disturb it, photograph from a distance, and contact Eaux et Forêts, the gendarmerie or Renatura immediately — every report counts. That is the discipline to copy for anything you find. AND THE FOREST ROUTE WORTH KNOWING: CONGO RECOGNISES TWO TYPES OF INDEPENDENT FOREST OBSERVATION — MANDATED (OIM), CONDUCTED WITH THE FOREST ADMINISTRATION UNDER A SIGNED PROTOCOLE D'ACCORD AUTHORISING FIELD AND DOCUMENTARY MISSIONS IN ALL THE COUNTRY'S FORESTS; AND EXTERNAL OR NON-MANDATED (OIE), CARRIED OUT BY CITIZENS OR CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, WHICH REQUIRES NO PRIOR AGREEMENT FROM THE ADMINISTRATION; international NGOs progressively trained Congolese civil society members and handed the activity over to them. Citizens may observe forest operations without asking permission. That is the single most enabling sentence in this file's Congolese record. ALSO NAMED: a CADRE DE CONCERTATION of Congolese civil society GROUPING ABOUT SIXTY environment, human rights and development NGOs, working alongside the state and private sector against illegal forest exploitation and for the living conditions of LOCAL COMMUNITIES AND INDIGENOUS POPULATIONS, at 59 rue Franceville, Moungali, BRAZZAVILLE, with four published telephone numbers. WHO IT SUITS: Congolese coastal communities, fishers, and forest villages wanting operations observed. CAVEATS: CONSERVATION AND OBSERVATION BODIES, not funders or law firms; Renatura ceased community tourism activities in 2020. For the only communal protected area in Congo, the Réserve Communautaire du Lac Télé entry; for the cahier des charges, RPDH; for free legal clinics, Comptoir Juridique Junior; for the forest unit's development fund, the Fonds de Développement Local entry.

trackers.name: Congo's USLAB units and article 93 of loi 37-2008 — the anti-poaching unit every protected area must have, and the law naming logging, mining and oil operators as recruiters of commissioned agents
trackers.desc: THE LAW THAT MAKES THE COMPANY HIRE THE GUARDS — and it answers the question this file keeps meeting, which is who watches the ground and who pays them: EACH PROTECTED AREA PUTS IN PLACE AN UNITÉ DE SURVEILLANCE ET DE LUTTE ANTI-BRACONNAGE (USLAB), MADE UP MAJORITARILY OF AGENTS COMMISSIONNÉS DES EAUX ET FORÊTS. A standing surveillance unit is a structure, not a project. If your area has protected status, ask whether its USLAB exists, who is in it and where it is based — an absent unit is a specific, nameable failure rather than a general complaint.
