AND THE RECRUITMENT CLAUSE IS THE PART TO USE: ARTICLE 93 OF LOI N°37-2008 OF 28 NOVEMBER 2008 ON WILDLIFE AND PROTECTED AREAS PROVIDES THAT THE AGENTS COMMISSIONNÉS DES EAUX ET FORÊTS ARE RECRUITED BY CONTRACT — BY THE FOREST OPERATORS, THE CONSERVATION PROJECTS, THE PROTECTED AREAS, AND THE EXPLOITATION AND RE-EXPLOITATION SITES FOR MINING AND PETROLEUM — IN THE MANAGEMENT AND CONSERVATION ZONES AND IN THE ZONES PERIPHERAL TO PROTECTED AREAS. The logging company, the mining site and the oil site are each named in the law as recruiters. That means the operator arriving on your land is a body the statute expects to be paying commissioned agents in the surrounding zone — so the question to put to it is not whether it will fund conservation, but how many agents it has contracted and from which villages. And note the phrase ZONES PERIPHERAL TO PROTECTED AREAS: your village does not have to be inside the park to be inside the clause. WHAT THE CATEGORY COVERS, WHICH IS BROADER THAN GUARDING: THE CONCEPT OF AGENTS COMMISSIONNÉS DES EAUX ET FORÊTS COVERS ÉCO-GARDES, ÉCO-GUIDES, PISTEURS, SOIGNEURS, AMÉNAGISTES AND PAYSAGISTES. Guides, trackers, animal carers, planners and landscape workers are all inside the same legal category as the guards. A community negotiating jobs should ask for the whole list, not only the ranger posts — tracker and guide are the roles where local knowledge is the qualification, and they are the ones outsiders cannot fill. ARTICLE 94 GOES TO THE CONTRACT ITSELF, and the published analysis works through how the agents are recruited, trained and managed. If the contract terms are in the statute, they are not the operator's to invent. Get article 94 read to you before anyone signs. AND A CAUTION ABOUT DEBT SWAPS, RECORDED HONESTLY BECAUSE THIS FILE HAS ELSEWHERE POINTED COMMUNITIES TOWARDS THEM: a fisheries coalition published a correction to its own reporting on a neighbouring country's debt-for-nature swap, noting that a previous version had said the swap DESIGNATED NEARLY 30% OF THE COASTLINE AS MARINE PROTECTED AREAS, BUT THAT THOSE AMPs HAD IN REALITY BEEN DESIGNATED BEFORE THE AGREEMENT — AND THAT NO INFORMATION IS AVAILABLE AS TO THE USE OF THE FUNDS GENERATED BY THE DEBT SWAP. A debt-for-nature swap can be credited with protection that already existed, and the money it raised can be untraceable. Both things happened next door. Where one is proposed, ask two questions in writing: which areas were designated BEFORE the deal, and where do the funds go and who reports on them. The same coalition records that THE GOVERNMENT INSTALLED BEACONS ON ARTISANAL PIROGUES WITH TWO STATED OBJECTIVES — PREVENTING ILLEGAL ENTRY INTO MARINE PROTECTED AREAS AND IMPROVING SAFETY AT SEA — while noting that for the beacons to be useful they must be functional and there must be a fully operational sea rescue system. Tracking devices justified partly by safety are only a safety measure if the rescue service exists. Ask what rescue capacity was funded alongside the beacons before accepting the framing. WHO IT SUITS: Congolese villages beside a protected area or facing a logging, mining or oil operator, and coastal fishing communities. CAVEATS: THIS IS A LAW AND A PUBLISHED ANALYSIS OF IT — verify the current text and get local advice. For the schedule of obligations a company owes, Republic of the Congo's RPDH entry; for each forest unit's fund with its own published account, the Fonds de Développement Local entry; for 438,960 hectares and the only community reserve, Lac Télé; for the first marine protected area and unmandated forest observation, Renatura Congo; for free legal clinics in two cities, Comptoir Juridique Junior.

trackers.name: Global Forest Watch — free weekly deforestation alerts for your own forest, an offline phone app to verify them on the ground, and a US$10,000–40,000 fund that pays for the response — with the published examples of loggers fined and a mining site shut down
trackers.desc: SUBSCRIBE TO ALERTS FOR YOUR OWN FOREST, FREE — placement note first: THE PLATFORM AND FUND ARE GLOBAL, FILED UNDER THE REPUBLIC OF CONGO BECAUSE THE CONGO BASIN IS THE AFRICAN FOREST REGION THIS FILE COVERS MOST AND THIS BUCKET CARRIED NO MONITORING OR GRANT RESOURCE. THE TOOL, AND IT COSTS NOTHING: FREE, REAL-TIME DATA, TECHNOLOGY AND TOOLS FOR MONITORING THE WORLD'S FORESTS — VIEW, ANALYZE, AND SUBSCRIBE TO GET WEEKLY DEFORESTATION ALERTS THAT SHOW WHERE TREE COVER LOSS IS HAPPENING RIGHT NOW IN THE TROPICS, WITH OVER 65 GLOBAL AND LOCAL DATA SETS TO EXPLORE. SUBSCRIBE is the operative word. You draw your forest once and the alerts arrive every week thereafter, without anyone visiting. For a community that cannot patrol its whole boundary, that is a watchman who works for free — and it means you learn about a clearing in days rather than after the trucks have gone. AND THE PART THAT MAKES IT USABLE WHERE THERE IS NO SIGNAL: A MOBILE APP BRINGS THE ONLINE MONITORING AND ALERT SYSTEMS OFFLINE AND INTO THE FIELD. Download the alerts in town, walk to the coordinates without a network, record what you find. That closes the gap between a satellite pixel and a fact somebody witnessed. THE MONEY TO ACT ON IT: A SMALL GRANTS FUND PROVIDES FINANCIAL AND TECHNICAL SUPPORT TO NON-PROFIT NGOs THAT WANT TO USE THE PLATFORM IN THEIR RESEARCH, ADVOCACY AND FIELDWORK, WITH GRANTS RANGING BETWEEN US$10 THOUSAND AND US$40 THOUSAND — AND THE FUND FOCUSES ON RAPID RESPONSE TO DEFORESTATION THROUGH EARLY WARNING SYSTEMS TO IDENTIFY, VERIFY, INVESTIGATE, AND ACT UPON SATELLITE-BASED ALERTS. IDENTIFY, VERIFY, INVESTIGATE, ACT — four stages, and the fund pays for the last three. The alert is free; the fuel, the phones and the person who walks out there are what the grant covers. WHAT PAST PROJECTS ACTUALLY DID, PUBLISHED AS EXAMPLES: A CONSERVATION ORGANISATION COLLABORATES WITH PARK RANGERS TO PATROL A PROTECTED AREA AND COLLECT DATA USING ALERTS THROUGH THE MOBILE APP, IDENTIFIES AN ILLEGAL LOGGING CAMP WITHIN THE RESERVE, DOCUMENTS ITS FINDINGS, AND THE PERPETRATORS ARE FINED. AN INDIGENOUS COMMUNITY USES ALERTS TO IDENTIFY THE LOCATION OF AN ILLEGAL MINING SITE, DOCUMENTS FURTHER EVIDENCE BY TAKING AERIAL PHOTOS WITH A DRONE, COMPILES THE DATA, MAPS AND PHOTOS AND SUBMITS A FORMAL COMPLAINT TO LOCAL AUTHORITIES — WHO THEN SHUT DOWN THE SITE. A mining site closed because a community assembled satellite alerts, drone photographs and a written complaint. That is the whole method in one sentence, and none of the three pieces requires a lawyer. The complaint is what turns the evidence into an act. THE FUNDABLE ACTIVITIES ARE LISTED, AND TWO ARE UNUSUAL: CROWDSOURCING, COMPILING AND PUBLISHING DATA ON CONCESSIONS THAT OVERLAP WITH ANCESTRAL COMMUNITY LANDS, AND SUPPORTING COMMUNITIES IN APPLYING PUBLIC PRESSURE TO GET THESE CONCESSIONS REVOKED; AND TRAINING POLICE, PROSECUTORS AND/OR JUDGES TO RAISE AWARENESS AS TO HOW SATELLITE IMAGERY AND DATA CAN BE USED TO PROVIDE ACCURATE, TIMELY AND COST-EFFECTIVE EVIDENCE OF DEFORESTATION. Getting concessions REVOKED is named as a fundable aim, not just documented. And training the judges is the quiet one: a prosecutor who does not accept satellite evidence will drop your case, so somebody has to teach the court before the case arrives. Very little else in this file funds that. THE OTHER TWO: DEVELOPING THE CAPACITY OF FOREST MONITORING BRIGADES TO CONDUCT FIELD VERIFICATIONS OF NEAR-REAL-TIME ALERTS AND WORK WITH ENFORCEMENT OFFICIALS; AND SUPPORTING COMMUNITIES IN DEVELOPING RESPONSE PROTOCOLS, FORMULATING LEGAL STRATEGIES AND COMPILING EVIDENCE OF ILLEGAL DEFORESTATION INCLUDING SATELLITE IMAGERY, DATA AND ANALYSES, AND SUBMITTING IT TO LAW ENFORCEMENT THROUGH FORMAL COMPLAINTS OR OTHER LEGAL PROCESSES. A RESPONSE PROTOCOL is the document to write before the first alert: who goes, who photographs, who files, and to whom. Communities that improvise this lose days, and the loggers only need days. THE AFRICAN GRANTEE TO NOTE: an organisation will REPLICATE AND SCALE COMMUNITY-LED FOREST MONITORING EFFORTS IN A NEW LANDSCAPE — A NAMED CAMEROONIAN NATIONAL PARK OF OVER 230,000 HECTARES FACING AN ALARMING INCREASE IN DEFORESTATION. AND THE FUND'S OWN FRAMING OF THE CONTINENT: ACROSS AFRICA, COMMUNITIES ARE STEPPING UP AS THE FIRST LINE OF DEFENSE AGAINST DEFORESTATION — WITH PROJECTS EQUIPPING LOCAL RESIDENTS, YOUTH AND COMMUNITY LEADERS WITH THE SKILLS, TECHNOLOGY AND NETWORKS NEEDED TO MONITOR THREATS AND COLLABORATE WITH AUTHORITIES, STRENGTHENING BOTH FOREST PROTECTION AND LOCAL GOVERNANCE FROM THE GROUND UP. AND THE TRAINING ROUTE FOR AN INDIVIDUAL: A TECHNOLOGY FELLOWSHIP RECRUITS AND TRAINS FOREST MANAGERS, PROTECTORS AND ADVOCATES IN USING THESE TOOLS AND SUPPORTS THEM TO TRAIN OTHERS IN THEIR NETWORKS. A fellowship for one person who then trains their own network. If your organisation cannot win a grant yet, sending one person through a fellowship is the cheaper first step — and this file has recorded the same route working for an Egyptian lawyer who came home and founded a firm. WHO IT SUITS: any African forest community, community forest association or monitoring brigade, and organisations wanting to fund a response system. CAVEATS: THE GRANT GOES TO NON-PROFIT ORGANISATIONS, so a village group applies through or as a registered body — and alerts are tree-cover loss, which needs field verification before it is a claim. For the alert system that reaches law enforcement and pays for verified reports, DR Congo's MappingForRights entry; for the villager's alert that became a ministry mission, Cameroon's FODER and SNOIE entry; for the commissioned-agent recruitment clause naming forest and mining operators, the Republic of Congo's loi 37-2008 entry.

trackers.name: They walk a community through the multi-step process of turning customary land into an actual statutory deed — 41,000 people over 54,000 hectares in one year — with talking books in 13 languages, a 25-organisation coalition and mobile paralegals
trackers.desc: THEY WALK A COMMUNITY THROUGH GETTING AN ACTUAL DEED — adjacency declared first: A TENURE FACILITY HAS ITS OWN NAMED ENTRY UNDER LIBERIA, A RIGHTS-AND-RESOURCES BODY IS A HOST UNDER GHANA, AND A LIBERIAN LAND AUTHORITY HAS ITS OWN ENTRY. NONE CARRIES THE FORMALIZATION PROCESS, THE COALITION, THE MOBILE PARALEGALS OR THE TALKING BOOKS. THE SERVICE, AND IT IS THE FIND: THEY GUIDE COMMUNITIES THROUGH COMMUNITY LAND FORMALIZATION, THE MULTI-STEP PROCESS REQUIRED TO OBTAIN AN OFFICIAL DEED FOR CUSTOMARY LAND — AND WITH LEGAL OWNERSHIP, COMMUNITIES ENJOY PROTECTION FROM EXPLOITATIVE LAND GRABS AND CAN BETTER MANAGE THE RESOURCES THEY DEPEND ON. A deed, not a map. This file holds many entries on recording, mapping and documenting community land; this one is about completing the legal process that ends in a title the state itself issued. That is the difference between evidence you can show and ownership you can enforce — and the multi-step process is exactly where communities get lost without a guide. THE MEASURED RESULT: IN ONE YEAR, FOLLOWING THEIR SUPPORT, FIVE CLANS — MORE THAN 41,000 PEOPLE INHABITING MORE THAN 54,000 HECTARES — RECEIVED A STATUTORY COMMUNITY DEED. Fifty-four thousand hectares titled to the people living on it, in twelve months. Set against the announced land-deal figures elsewhere in this file, that is the same order of magnitude moving in the opposite direction. WHAT THE DEED MEANS, IN A COMMUNITY MEMBER'S OWN TERMS: PROTECTION FROM EXPLOITATION, SECURITY FOR THE FUTURE, AND THE PEACE OF MIND THAT COMES FROM HAVING LEGALLY RECOGNIZED AND DOCUMENTED LAND RIGHTS. THE LOW-LITERACY TOOL, WHICH IS THE MOST COPYABLE THING HERE: THEY RAISE AWARENESS OF THE LAND RIGHTS LAW IN LOW-LITERACY AREAS USING TALKING BOOKS — DURABLE HANDHELD AUDIO DEVICES OFFERING EDUCATIONAL MESSAGING IN 13 OF THE COUNTRY'S LANGUAGES. ONLY ONE THIRD OF WOMEN NATIONWIDE ARE LITERATE, AND MUCH OF THE COUNTRY PRIMARILY SPEAKS ONE OF 16 LOCAL LANGUAGES. A law that exists in a language two thirds of the women cannot read is not available to them. A durable audio device that needs no network, no charge cycle to speak of and no reading is how the law actually arrives — and it is a specific, purchasable item to ask a funder for rather than another leaflet. THE RESIDENTIAL-PLOT TRAP THEY NAME, AND IT IS WORTH WATCHING FOR IN ANY FORMALIZATION: AS COMMUNITIES FORMALIZE THEIR CUSTOMARY LAND, MEMBERS RECEIVE FORMAL DEEDS TO THEIR RESIDENTIAL PLOTS — BUT DESPITE A CLEAR PROVISION STATING ALL CITIZENS REGARDLESS OF GENDER ARE ENTITLED TO RESIDENTIAL LAND, LOOSE INTERPRETATIONS HOLD POTENTIAL TO EXCLUDE WOMEN AND OTHER GROUPS. The law says one thing and the local interpretation does another, at the exact moment the paperwork is issued. Titling is not automatically fair — who is named on each residential deed has to be watched during the process, not corrected afterwards, because a deed once issued is far harder to change than a draft. WHAT CHANGED INSIDE ONE COMMUNITY: THROUGHOUT THE PROCESS, WOMEN STOOD NEXT TO MEN — IN YEARS PRIOR, WOMEN, AND PARTICULARLY WIDOWS, DID NOT SPEAK AT COMMUNITY MEETINGS; NOW THEY PARTICIPATE FULLY IN THE DECISION-MAKING. THE COALITION MODEL: A GLOBAL INITIATIVE WORKING VIA A NATIONAL COALITION MODEL, FACILITATED BY A GLOBAL STEERING COMMITTEE AND LED BY GRASSROOTS AND NATIONAL PARTNERS — WITH ONE AFRICAN NATIONAL COALITION COMPOSED OF 25 GRASSROOTS ORGANIZATIONS WORKING TO ENABLE WOMEN TO REALIZE THEIR RIGHTS TO LAND. Twenty-five grassroots organisations in one country under a single national coalition, led by the national partners rather than the international one. If a coalition exists in your country, joining it is faster than founding anything — and this file's Mauritius entry describes the same logic for extractives. THE MOBILE PARALEGAL PARTNERSHIP: THAT COALITION PARTNERED WITH A MOBILE LEGAL SERVICE PROVIDER — WHOSE NAME MEANS LAW ON YOUR PALM — TO ENABLE COMMUNITY PARALEGALS TO OFFER LAND-RELATED LEGAL ASSISTANCE TO HUNDREDS OF WOMEN IN HARD-TO-REACH AREAS. THE SIMPLIFIED GUIDES FINDING: THE USE OF SIMPLIFIED LEGAL GUIDES IS HELPING TO EMPOWER COMMUNITIES TO ENGAGE IN DIALOGUE AND NEGOTIATIONS WITH GOVERNMENT AUTHORITIES AND INVESTORS. THE PUBLISHED SERVICE LIST, WHICH IS WHAT YOU CAN ACTUALLY ASK FOR: FIELD ASSESSMENTS, INSTITUTIONAL ASSESSMENTS, LEGISLATIVE DRAFTING AND POLICY ADVICE, DEVELOPMENT OF FOLLOW-ON REGULATIONS AND PROCEDURES, TECHNICAL SUPPORT FOR LEGAL ASSISTANCE, SOCIAL IMPACT STUDIES, IMPLEMENTATION PLANNING, IMPLEMENTATION MONITORING, TRAINING, PUBLIC EDUCATION PROGRAMS, AND PROGRAM DESIGN AND MANAGEMENT. IMPLEMENTATION MONITORING is the item to notice. A good land law that nobody enforces is the pattern this file has recorded from Burundi to Kenya — and there is an organisation that treats watching the implementation as a service in itself. THE TRAINING ROUTES: A GLOBAL FELLOWSHIP PROGRAM FOR PROFESSIONALS PURSUING A CAREER IN SECURING LAND AND PROPERTY RIGHTS; A VISITING PROFESSIONALS PROGRAMME; AND CONVENINGS WHERE PRACTITIONERS FROM ASIA AND SUB-SAHARAN AFRICA SHARE COMPARATIVE EXPERTISE AND LAUNCH JOINT ADVOCACY. AND THE WARNING THEIR OWN AFRICAN STAFF RAISE ABOUT EVIDENCE: GENDER-DISAGGREGATED DATA IN RURAL COMMUNITIES EFFECTIVELY MEASURES THE PLIGHT OF WOMEN IN RELATION TO LAND RIGHTS, AND EVIDENCE-BASED PROGRAMMING IS LESS COSTLY AND MAKES MONITORING SIMPLER — BUT PARTNERS FACE PRESSURE TO USE UNVERIFIED STATISTICS THAT CREATE A HEIGHTENED SENSE OF NEED AND URGENCY. An African researcher naming the temptation to inflate figures for funders, and arguing that real counting is cheaper. A number you can defend survives a hostile question; one you borrowed does not. WHO IT SUITS: African communities whose land is customary and untitled, and the national coalitions and paralegals working with them. CAVEATS: THEY WORK THROUGH GOVERNMENTS AND NATIONAL PARTNERS IN SELECTED COUNTRIES, NOT ON OPEN REQUEST — approach the national coalition. For the tenure facility funding community titling, Liberia's entry; for the free system recording rights neither registered nor registerable, Comoros' entry; for the community paralegal method, Sierra Leone's Timap entry.

trackers.name: Global Energy Monitor's Africa energy trackers — a dedicated Africa energy tracker updated monthly — every power plant, mine, pipeline and terminal with its own editable wiki page carrying ownership and human rights impacts, 25 downloadable datasets, and a named project manager for each
trackers.desc: EVERY PROJECT HAS A PAGE, AND YOU CAN EDIT IT — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S CÔTE D'IVOIRE ENTRY COVERS THE DEVELOPMENT FINANCE CAMPAIGNING ON AFRICAN ENERGY, ITS BENIN ENTRY THE OPEN MINING SITE DATA AND OPEN-SOURCE WEBMAP CODE, ITS BURUNDI ENTRY THE FOREST FINANCE DATABASE, AND ITS LIBYA ENTRY THE OPEN LAND-DEAL DATABASE. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE AFRICA TRACKER, WHICH IS THE FIND: A COMPREHENSIVE DATASET OF ENERGY INFRASTRUCTURE ACROSS AFRICA COVERING OIL AND GAS, COAL, RENEWABLES AND OTHER POWER INFRASTRUCTURE — POWER GENERATION (SOLAR, WIND, GEOTHERMAL, HYDROPOWER, BIOENERGY, OIL AND GAS-FIRED, COAL-FIRED AND NUCLEAR-FIRED PLANTS), EXTRACTION (COAL MINES AND OIL AND GAS EXTRACTION SITES), AND THE MOVEMENT OF FUELS (LNG TERMINALS, COAL TERMINALS, AND OIL AND GAS PIPELINES). A dedicated African dataset, not a global one you must filter. And RENEWABLES sit in it beside coal and oil — a solar field or hydropower scheme taking your land is tracked as infrastructure the same way, which this file has recorded communities discovering only after the fact. THE EDITABLE WIKI, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: EACH PROJECT HAS A DEDICATED WIKI PAGE — BASED ON THE SOFTWARE PLATFORM DEVELOPED BY THE WIKIPEDIA FOUNDATION THAT ALLOWS ANYONE TO EDIT EXISTING ARTICLES AND CREATE NEW ONES. EACH SUCCESSIVE VERSION IS SAVED ALONG WITH A TIME STAMP AND A BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE CHANGE. Anyone can edit, and every change is timestamped and attributed. A community that knows the pipeline route was moved, the plant was commissioned early, or the compensation was never paid can put that on the project's own public page — and the version history means it cannot be quietly deleted. That is the rarest thing in this file: a public record about a project that a village can write into. WHAT THOSE PAGES CARRY BESIDES THE TECHNICAL DATA: THE PROJECT'S HISTORY, STATUS, CAPACITY AND OWNERSHIP, ALONG WITH BACKGROUND INFO SUCH AS ENVIRONMENTAL, HEALTH, SAFETY AND HUMAN RIGHTS IMPACTS — TOGETHER WITH LINKS TO SOURCES, ADDITIONAL NARRATIVE INFORMATION, AND A MAP OF THE PROJECT SITE. HUMAN RIGHTS IMPACTS as a standing field on an energy infrastructure database. Most such registers stop at megawatts and ownership; this one has a place for what the project did to people, and it is the field to fill. THE UPDATE CYCLE: THE INTERACTIVE MAP ALLOWS USERS TO VISUALIZE PIPELINE ROUTES AND INFRASTRUCTURE LOCATIONS, AND THE MAP AND UNDERLYING DATA ARE UPDATED ON A MONTHLY BASIS. THE SCALE OF THE OPEN DATA: 25 OPEN-SOURCE DATASETS AVAILABLE FOR DIRECT DOWNLOAD — OPEN-ACCESS DATA ON GLOBAL ENERGY INFRASTRUCTURE, RESOURCES AND USES, DELIVERED AS A SPREADSHEET FILE WITH A RECOMMENDED CITATION AND A DATED RELEASE. A DATED RELEASE AND A RECOMMENDED CITATION. That is what makes a downloaded figure usable in a submission or a court filing rather than merely interesting — you can say exactly which version you relied on. THE NAMED TRACKERS: INTEGRATED POWER; GAS INFRASTRUCTURE; OIL INFRASTRUCTURE; OIL AND GAS EXTRACTION, COVERING FIELDS FROM DISCOVERY TO DECOMMISSIONING WITH LOCATION, OWNERSHIP, PRODUCTION AND RESERVES; COAL PLANTS; COAL MINES; COAL TERMINALS; SOLAR, WIND, BIOENERGY, GEOTHERMAL, NUCLEAR AND HYDROPOWER; METHANE EMITTERS; AND AN ENERGY TRANSITION TRACKER. FROM DISCOVERY TO DECOMMISSIONING. A field that is only a discovery today is already in the dataset, which is years before the trucks arrive — the earliest warning available to a community, and free. THE TRANSITION TRACKER'S STATED PURPOSE: AN OPEN PLATFORM OF ENERGY DATA AND INFORMATION ON SPECIFIC REGIONS, OR ICONIC ZONES, THAT HAVE THE POTENTIAL TO ENGAGE CIVIL SOCIETY IN TRANSITIONING AWAY FROM FOSSIL FUELS. THE OWNERSHIP CHAIN SUPPLEMENT: A SUPPLEMENTAL FILE WITH DETAILED INFORMATION ON CRUDE OIL AND NATURAL GAS LIQUID TRANSMISSION PIPELINE OWNERSHIP CHAINS. OWNERSHIP CHAINS, supplied as a file on request. This file's Côte d'Ivoire entry records that intermediary structures are where the trail goes cold; for pipelines, somebody has already done that work. THE PUBLISHED CONTACT ROUTE: EACH TRACKER PUBLISHES A NAMED PROJECT MANAGER WITH A GET IN TOUCH CONTACT, AND MAILING LISTS FOR ANNOUNCEMENTS. A named person per dataset. If the project on your land is missing, wrong or misdated, there is somebody to write to who is responsible for that specific tracker. THE AFRICAN FINDING IT PUBLISHES: EMERGING PRODUCERS IN SUB-SAHARAN AFRICA AIM TO MONETIZE LOCAL RESERVES AND ENTER GLOBAL MARKETS, WITH PROJECTS PRIMARILY LED BY STATE-OWNED ENTERPRISES AS WELL AS NAMED OIL MAJORS — AND WHILE CONSTRUCTION HAS SLOWED SINCE 2019, DEVELOPMENT CONTINUES LARGELY UNCHECKED. STATE-OWNED ENTERPRISES leading. When the developer is your own government's company, the complaint routes in this file that target foreign lenders and buyers matter more, not less — because the domestic regulator and the developer answer to the same ministry. THE ASSET-LIFETIME POINT, WHICH IS THE ARGUMENT TO CARRY: GLOBAL OIL DEMAND IS PROJECTED TO PEAK BY 2030, BUT PIPELINES ARE BUILT TO OPERATE FOR 30–50 YEARS. A community is being asked to give up land for half a century to serve a demand curve that turns in a few years. That mismatch is the strongest economic objection available, and it comes from an energy dataset rather than an advocacy claim. AND THE TRANSITION-FUEL CAVEAT IT RECORDS: IMPORTING COUNTRIES CITE GROWING ENERGY DEMAND, ENERGY SECURITY CONCERNS, AND PERCEPTIONS OF GAS AS A TRANSITION FUEL — DESPITE LNG HAVING EMISSIONS ON THE SAME ORDER AS COAL. Gas sold locally as the clean option. Recorded here, with the comparison, by the organisation that counts the infrastructure. WHO IT SUITS: African communities facing a pipeline, power plant, LNG terminal, coal mine or large renewable project — and anyone who needs the project named, dated and owned in a citable record. CAVEATS: ENERGY INFRASTRUCTURE ONLY, WITH SIZE THRESHOLDS THAT EXCLUDE SMALLER FACILITIES, AND THE WIKI IS ONLY AS COMPLETE AS ITS CONTRIBUTORS — which is also the invitation. For open mining site data and webmap code, Benin's entry; for the campaigning on African energy finance, Côte d'Ivoire's entry; for the open land-deal database you may correct, Libya's entry.

trackers.name: Long-term unrestricted general operating support to grassroots groups including informal ones, entered through a US$5,000 catalyst grant rather than an application — from a funder that published an African partner's decision to vet funders before accepting money
trackers.desc: THEIR AFRICAN PARTNER RAN DUE DILIGENCE ON THEM, AND THEY PUBLISHED IT — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S CAMEROON ENTRY COVERS THE FUND WITH NO APPLICATION FORM REACHED THROUGH REGIONAL ADVISORS; ITS CÔTE D'IVOIRE ENTRY THE UNCONDITIONAL CASH TRANSFERS; ITS GAMBIA ENTRY THE FUNDER PUBLISHING ITS UNRESTRICTED PERCENTAGES; ITS ETHIOPIA ENTRY THE NO-PASS-OR-FAIL FUNDER; AND THIS BUCKET ALREADY CARRIES A LAND-RIGHTS HOST AND A FOREST MONITORING HOST. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. PRECHECK AND AN EXACT HOST COMPARISON ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS WERE RUN BEFORE THIS ENTRY WAS WRITTEN. THE DUE-DILIGENCE REVERSAL, WHICH IS THE FIND: A PARTNER ORGANISATION DREW A CLEAR LINE WHEN IT COMES TO FUNDERS, WORKING ONLY WITH FUNDERS THAT VALUE AND SUPPORT AFRICAN SOVEREIGNTY AND COMMUNITY-LED ADVOCACY — SAYING WE CANNOT COMPROMISE THE WORK OF OUR COMMUNITY PARTNERS JUST SO WE CAN SUSTAIN OUR ORGANIZATION. THE QUESTION POSED AFTERWARDS: WHAT IF IT WAS THE NORM FOR GRANTEE PARTNERS TO CONDUCT DUE DILIGENCE ON FUNDERS BEFORE ENTERING INTO A RELATIONSHIP? THE FOUNDATION RECORDS THIS AS A HUMBLING YET INSTRUCTIVE MOMENT THAT SHINED A LIGHT ON SYSTEMIC POWER IMBALANCES. An African organisation refused money on its own terms, and the funder published the story against itself. That is the practical lesson of this whole file turned around: every entry here assesses whether a community qualifies for a resource, and almost none asks whether the resource qualifies for the community. The questions to put to any funder in this list — what do you require of us, whose name goes on the work, what happens to us when your priorities change — are legitimate, and at least one funder has said so in print. WHAT IS ACTUALLY GIVEN: WE APPROACH OUR GRANTMAKING IN TERMS OF A PARTNERSHIP MODEL — PROVIDING LONG-TERM GENERAL OPERATING SUPPORT, AND TRUSTING IN THE VISION, BRILLIANCE, AND LEADERSHIP OF OUR PARTNERS. GENERAL OPERATING SUPPORT, long-term. Salaries, rent, the accountant, the vehicle — the costs this file has repeatedly identified as the ones nobody funds and the absence of which collapses organisations between project grants. WHY IT STOPPED FUNDING PROJECTS: AT FIRST IT MADE SMALL, SPORADIC, PROJECT-BASED GRANTS, BUT AFTER SEVERAL YEARS IT REALIZED THAT PROJECT-BASED SUPPORT ADDRESSED ONLY SYMPTOMS OF SOCIAL PROBLEMS, NOT ROOT CAUSES — SO IT SWITCHED TO SUSTAINED, UNRESTRICTED GRANTS SUPPORTING THE LONG-TERM STRATEGIES AND VISION OF ITS PARTNERS, NOT JUST THEIR SHORT-TERM FINANCIAL NEEDS. A funder describing its own earlier model as having treated symptoms. Useful to quote when arguing with a donor still offering twelve-month project money for a thirty-year land struggle. THE SELF-DETERMINATION POINT MADE BY ITS OWN DIRECTOR: THIS PRACTICE DELIBERATELY TILTS THE POWER IMBALANCE THAT EXISTS BETWEEN GRANTMAKERS AND GRANT RECIPIENTS — IT ENSURES THE PARTNER SELF-DETERMINES THE USE OF RESOURCES. HOW YOU GET IN, AND THE ONE PUBLISHED ROUTE: IT DOES NOT ACCEPT UNSOLICITED GRANT REQUESTS — HOWEVER, INTERESTED ORGANISATIONS IN ITS PARTNER COUNTRIES CAN CONTACT IT REGARDING THE SELECTION CRITERIA FOR CATALYST GRANTS OF US$5,000 — AND IT INVITES THE MOST SUCCESSFUL OF THESE SMALL GRANTEES TO BECOME ITS PARTNERS, AND TO BENEFIT FROM CONTINUED AND EXPANDED FUNDING. This is the ladder, and it is the most useful line in the entry: a small first grant that can be asked about directly, which is the entry point to long-term unrestricted funding. Check first whether your country is on the partner list — the route only exists inside it. WHO THE PARTNERS ARE: INDIGENOUS PEOPLES ORGANISATIONS; WOMEN-, YOUTH- AND LGBTQ+-LED ORGANISATIONS; COOPERATIVES; RESEARCH AND POLICY THINK TANKS; REGIONAL AND GLOBAL COALITIONS; AND OTHERS — MOVEMENT ACTORS OF MANY TYPES, SIZES, AND STRATEGIES, INCLUDING FORMAL AND INFORMAL FORMATIONS. INFORMAL FORMATIONS and COOPERATIVES both named. An unregistered movement and a farmers' cooperative are inside the category, which most of the funders in this file exclude by requiring a constitution and an audit. THE LEADERSHIP IT FUNDS: PARTNERS ARE PRIMARILY LED BY WOMEN, YOUNG PEOPLE, AND INDIGENOUS PEOPLE WHO ARE OFTEN IN THE BEST POSITION TO OFFER SOLUTIONS RELEVANT TO THEIR COMMUNITIES. THE FOUR THINGS ITS THEORY OF CHANGE FOCUSES ON, AFTER AN EVALUATION OF ITS PARTNERS: SUPPORTING SELF-DETERMINATION OF COMMUNITIES; BUILDING ORGANIZATIONAL RESILIENCE; FACILITATING ALLIANCE BUILDING AMONG PARTNERS; AND INFORMING THE PRACTICE OF SOCIAL JUSTICE GRANTMAKING. ALLIANCE BUILDING AMONG PARTNERS is a funded activity, not an afterthought. Money to meet other organisations facing the same company or the same law is rarely available anywhere in this file. THE SUBJECTS IT FUNDS: FOOD SOVEREIGNTY; ALTERNATIVE ECONOMIES; AND CLIMATE JUSTICE — WITH ATTENTION TO SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE, EROSION CONTROL, WATER SECURITY, CLIMATE CHANGE, ENVIRONMENTAL CONSERVATION AND RELATED NATURAL RESOURCE ISSUES AT COMMUNITY LEVEL, INTEGRATED WITH EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN AND GIRLS, HEALTH AND NUTRITION, AND TRAINING AND EDUCATION. FOOD SOVEREIGNTY as a headline theme. A community defending farmland from acquisition is describing food sovereignty, which is a stronger frame here than conservation. THE SCALE AND THE PERIOD: OVER $60 MILLION MOVED TO MORE THAN 650 GRASSROOTS GROUPS AND MOVEMENTS ACROSS 85 COUNTRIES OVER FORTY YEARS, COLLECTIVELY REACHING AND MOBILIZING MORE THAN 200 MILLION PEOPLE. THE NAMING CHOICE, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS DELIBERATE: IT IS DELIBERATE IN REFERRING TO ITS GRANTEES AS PARTNERS, INDICATING AN ATTEMPT TO DIMINISH THE INHERENT POWER DIFFERENTIAL IN A DONOR-GRANTEE RELATIONSHIP — AND IT WAS FORMERLY KNOWN BY A DIFFERENT NAME BEFORE 2016, WHICH MATTERS WHEN SEARCHING OLDER RECORDS. The name changed in 2016, so grant records, evaluations and references from before then sit under the old one. Search both when checking their history in your country. AND WHAT IT TEACHES OTHER FUNDERS: IT RUNS AN ACADEMY WHERE OTHER INSTITUTIONAL FUNDERS AND WEALTHY INDIVIDUAL DONORS ARE INVITED TO LEARN ABOUT TRUST AND SOLIDARITY-BASED MODELS OF GRANTMAKING — AND ITS ENGAGEMENT AND LEARNING PROGRAMMES, THOUGH GEARED TOWARD GRANTMAKERS AND DONORS, COLLABORATE WITH INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES, LOCAL LEADERS AND MOVEMENT BUILDERS, WHICH ARE THE OPPORTUNITIES THAT EXIST TO GET TO KNOW IT. Since there is no application, the learning programmes are the published way to become known. And an organisation invited to speak to a room of funders is being paid attention by more than one of them at once. WHO IT SUITS: African grassroots groups, cooperatives and informal movements led by women, youth or Indigenous people — in its partner countries. CAVEATS: NO UNSOLICITED REQUESTS, A PARTNER-COUNTRY LIST THAT BOUNDS EVERYTHING, AND THE CATALYST GRANT IS THE ONLY PUBLISHED DOOR — check the country list first. For the fund reached through regional advisors, Cameroon's entry; for unconditional cash to forest communities, Côte d'Ivoire's entry; for the funder that publishes its unrestricted percentage, Gambia's entry.

trackers.name: A 24/7 emergency helpline for threatened defenders in Arabic, French, English, Russian and Spanish — with evacuation, medical, legal and relocation grants up to a published ceiling, a fast-track decision route, and a stated preference for moving within your own region
trackers.desc: A 24/7 HELPLINE IN FRENCH AND ARABIC, AND MOVE WITHIN YOUR OWN REGION FIRST — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S DR CONGO ENTRY NAMES THIS MECHANISM AS AN ONWARD REFERRAL WITHOUT DESCRIBING IT OR SHIPPING ITS HOST; ITS EQUATORIAL GUINEA BUCKET CARRIES A PROTECTION GRANTS HOST THAT IS ONE OF THIS MECHANISM'S DELIVERY PARTNERS, AND ITS LIBYA AND MALI ENTRIES THE DIGITAL HELPLINE AND SECURITY TOOLKIT. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. THE HELPLINE AND ITS LANGUAGES, WHICH IS THE FIND: 24/7 URGENT SUPPORT FOR DEFENDERS FACING IMMINENT DANGER OR THREATS — IN THE EVENT OF A CRISIS, DEFENDERS CAN MAKE CONTACT THROUGH A PERMANENT EMERGENCY HELPLINE AVAILABLE IN ARABIC, ENGLISH, FRENCH, RUSSIAN AND SPANISH, AND THROUGH A SECURE CHANNEL. Arabic and French on a line that answers at any hour. Almost every emergency resource in this file operates in English on office hours, which is useless at two in the morning in a francophone or North African country — which is precisely when the arrest happens. WHAT AN EMERGENCY INTERVENTION CAN COVER: AID FOR AN EVACUATION, SOCIAL AND RELOCATION ASSISTANCE, LEGAL ASSISTANCE, AID FOR MEDICAL CARE IN CASES OF VIOLENCE OR TORTURE, AND/OR AN INTERVENTION WITH THE RELEVANT AUTHORITIES. AN INTERVENTION WITH THE RELEVANT AUTHORITIES is the item easiest to overlook and often the fastest: a call or letter from a European mechanism to the ministry or the police commander, made the same day, is sometimes what ends a detention. HOW TO APPLY, STATED SIMPLY: THE DEFENDER SHOULD FILL OUT A CONTACT FORM ON THE WEBSITE; EMAILS ARE CHECKED DAILY SO REQUESTS CAN BE PROCESSED QUICKLY, AND STAFF MAY ASK FOR FURTHER INFORMATION OR START PROCESSING THE CASE. THE TEST APPLIED: THAT THE PERSON IS AT RISK BECAUSE OF HIS OR HER WORK PROTECTING HUMAN RIGHTS, AND THE SITUATION PRESENTS ITSELF AS AN EMERGENCY. Two conditions only. A land defender is a human rights defender for this purpose, which is the framing to use in the form. WHERE IT REACHES: THE EMERGENCY GRANTS PROGRAMME AIMS TO REACH EVERY CORNER OF THE WORLD, INCLUDING MOST DIFFICULT COUNTRIES AND REMOTE LOCATIONS. WHO ACTUALLY DELIVERS IT: THROUGH THE ESTABLISHED EMERGENCY GRANTS PROGRAMMES OF SEVERAL NAMED PARTNER ORGANISATIONS, INCLUDING ONE EAST AND HORN OF AFRICA DEFENDERS PROJECT, WHICH ALSO DRAW ON NON-EU FUNDING TO PROVIDE RAPID PRACTICAL SUPPORT. An East and Horn of Africa body is inside the delivery consortium, so a defender in that region may be dealing with a regional organisation rather than Brussels. Approaching any one consortium partner reaches the whole mechanism. THE RELOCATION PROGRAMME AND ITS LIMITS, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: IT FUNDS RELOCATION OF DEFENDERS WHO INTEND TO RETURN TO THEIR HOME COUNTRY OR REGION IF CIRCUMSTANCES ALLOW AND WHO PLAN TO CONTINUE THEIR WORK AFTERWARDS — FOR UP TO 1 YEAR, AND IT DOES NOT FACILITATE PERMANENT RELOCATION OR ASYLUM PROCEDURES. Filed plainly so nobody applies for the wrong thing: this is a year away and back, not a route out. A defender seeking asylum needs the refugee-agency chain recorded in this file's DR Congo entry instead. THE PREFERENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: IF RELOCATION IS JUDGED THE MOST EFFECTIVE OPTION, PRIORITY SHOULD BE GIVEN TO RELOCATION IN THE DEFENDER'S OWN COUNTRY OR IN THEIR SUB-REGION IF POSSIBLE, THUS ALLOWING THEM TO CONTINUE THEIR WORK. Moving to a safer town or a neighbouring country is preferred over Europe, and is funded on that basis. That is cheaper, faster, keeps the person near the campaign, and is far more likely to be approved — propose it that way. THE MONEY, THE CEILING AND THE CO-FUNDING RULE: BUDGETS BASED ON REAL COSTS, A MAXIMUM OF 60,000 EURO PER DEFENDER FOR A CONTRACT PERIOD AND A MAXIMUM DURATION OF 12 MONTHS IF DULY JUSTIFIED — THOUGH GRANT AMOUNT AVERAGES ARE MUCH LOWER; IT CANNOT SUPPORT 100% OF RELOCATION COSTS UNDER ITS CO-FUNDING RULES, AND A GRANT CAN BE EXTENDED BY UP TO 6 MONTHS IF DULY JUSTIFIED. The ceiling is high and the averages are not — they say so themselves. And because it will not cover the whole cost, line up a second contributor before applying; the small unrestricted funds recorded elsewhere in this file are the realistic match. HOW A DECISION IS MADE, AND THE FAST TRACK: ONCE THE SECRETARIAT ESTABLISHES THAT THE APPLICATION MEETS THE PROGRAMME CRITERIA, IT IS PRESENTED TO THE BOARD AND EVALUATED AT MONTHLY MEETINGS — BUT IF THE REQUEST IS LINKED TO AN EMERGENCY, AN EMERGENCY DECISION PROCEDURE CAN BE APPLIED TO GIVE A RESPONSE IN A SHORTER TIME. Monthly board meetings are the default speed. Say explicitly in the request that it is an emergency and why, or the file waits for the next meeting. THE PAYMENT WARNING IT PUBLISHES: PAYMENT CAN BE MADE BY BANK TRANSFER OR WESTERN UNION — BUT THE TRANSFER WILL STATE THAT IT IS COMING FROM THE MECHANISM, AND A RECIPIENT SHOULD UNDERSTAND ANY SECURITY IMPLICATIONS OF SUCH A TRANSFER AND COMMUNICATE THIS TO THE SECRETARIAT. The money arrives with a European human rights label attached to it, in a country where that name on a bank record can itself be evidence against you. Raise it before the transfer, not after — this is the kind of operational detail this file has recorded almost no funder disclosing. AND THE ORGANISATIONAL SIDE, WITH THE ROUTING CHANGE: FINANCIAL AND TECHNICAL SUPPORT FOR LOCAL HUMAN RIGHTS ORGANISATIONS FACING PRESSURE, AND TRAINING IN SECURITY, ADVOCACY AND PSYCHOSOCIAL WELL-BEING — AN ORGANISATION OR COMMUNITY IN NEED CAN REACH OUT AND BE GUIDED THROUGH THE AVAILABLE CHANNELS, THOUGH THE SECRETARIAT NO LONGER ASSESSES GRANT APPLICATION FORMS VIA THAT CENTRALISED CHANNEL; A SHELTER INITIATIVES PROGRAMME PROVIDES DIRECT MATERIAL AND FINANCIAL SUPPORT TO NEW AND EMERGING SHELTER PROGRAMMES THROUGH A CALL FOR PROPOSALS. SINCE 2015 IT REPORTS SUPPORTING MORE THAN 85,000 INDIVIDUALS, INCLUDING OVER 10,000 PEOPLE FROM 113 COUNTRIES IN A SINGLE RECENT YEAR. Two things there: the central grants channel has closed, so go to a consortium partner rather than the secretariat — and an African organisation running a safe house can apply to have that shelter funded, which is a role a community organisation can actually take on. WHO IT SUITS: African land and environmental defenders under immediate threat, and the organisations sheltering them — including francophone and Arabic-speaking defenders needing help outside office hours. CAVEATS: EMERGENCY AND TEMPORARY BY DESIGN — NO ASYLUM, NO PERMANENT RELOCATION, AND NOT 100% OF COSTS; THE CENTRAL SECRETARIAT NO LONGER ASSESSES GRANT FORMS, SO APPROACH A CONSORTIUM PARTNER, AND WEIGH THE SECURITY IMPLICATIONS OF THE TRANSFER LABEL. For the referral chain into a national refugee programme, DR Congo's entry; for protection grants up to €7,500, Equatorial Guinea's entry.

trackers.name: ASADHO (Association Africaine de Défense des Droits de l'Homme), Kinshasa, and ASADHO/Katanga in the mining belt — monitors army conduct at mine sites, accompanies whistleblowers through the courts, campaigns to revise mining contracts
trackers.desc: A SECTION IN THE MINING PROVINCE, AND LAWYERS FOR THE PERSON WHO TALKS — method and adjacency declared first: SECOND NAMED-ATTORNEY ROUND, AIMED AT FRANCOPHONE CENTRAL AFRICA, THE REGION THIS FILE HAS REPEATEDLY MEASURED AS THINNEST FOR LEGAL HELP. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN FOUR HOSTS AND SIX DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; THE SUBJECT'S NAME AND FIVE FACTS ABSENT, WITH TWO UNRELATED HOSTS IN THREE BUCKETS AND TWO GENERIC TERMS ELSEWHERE. THIS BUCKET'S OWN ENTRIES COVER THE OBLIGATIONS SCHEDULE A COMPANY OWES A VILLAGE, THE LOCAL DEVELOPMENT FUND, THE ANTI-POACHING UNIT AND THE COASTAL ASSOCIATION — NONE OF THEM COUNSEL. NONE IS RESTATED. THE PROVINCIAL SECTION IN THE MINING BELT, WHICH IS THE FIND: A SEPARATELY IDENTIFIED PROVINCIAL SECTION WHOSE STATED INVOLVEMENT IS MONITORING OF HUMAN RIGHTS LINKED TO MINING RESOURCE EXPLOITATION, ADVOCACY TO BRING MINING COMPANIES TO APPLY THE INTERNATIONAL PRINCIPLES ON CORPORATE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY AND HUMAN RIGHTS, AND MONITORING OF THE IMPACT OF MINING EXPLOITATION ON THE ENVIRONMENT. A section of the national body located in the province where the mines are, rather than only an office in the capital. For a village on a concession, that is the difference between writing to a city four days away and reaching someone who already knows the site. THE CONTRACT DEMAND IT CAMPAIGNS ON, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: COMMITMENT TO A PUBLISH-WHAT-YOU-PAY COALITION AND THE EXTRACTIVE INDUSTRIES TRANSPARENCY INITIATIVE, FIGHTING FOR THE REVISION OR REHABILITATION OF MINING CONTRACTS. REVISION OF THE CONTRACT ITSELF, not compensation after the fact. This file has recorded communities negotiating with a company whose terms were fixed years earlier in a capital; an organisation campaigning to reopen those contracts is working the layer above the negotiation. WHAT IT DOCUMENTS ABOUT THE ARMY: A PUBLICATION FOCUSING ON HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS CARRIED OUT BY MEMBERS OF THE NATIONAL ARMED FORCES IN THE MINING SECTOR IN SOUTH KIVU PROVINCE — SEVERAL VIOLATIONS BEING REGULARLY COMMITTED BY THOSE FORCES, EITHER IN OPERATION OR WHEN DEPLOYED. Soldiers at mine sites are the actor this file's protection entries handle worst, because a defender arrested by the army is outside the police system entirely. An organisation that already publishes on military conduct in the mining sector is the one to approach when that happens. THE WHISTLEBLOWER SERVICE, WHICH IS THE THIRD FIND: LEGAL AND JUDICIAL ACCOMPANIMENT OF WHISTLEBLOWERS — ALONGSIDE IMPROVEMENT OF THE LEGAL FRAMEWORK AND ADVOCACY. ACCOMPANIMENT means through the proceedings, not advice at the door. The person inside a company or a ministry who reports what a project is really doing is the single most useful witness a community can have, and is also the most exposed — this is ASADHO will stand beside them in court. HOW IT INVESTIGATES CORRUPTION AND WHERE: INVESTIGATION AND MONITORING OF ACTS OF CORRUPTION IN THE DIFFERENT SECTORS OF NATIONAL LIFE — THE ADMINISTRATION OF JUSTICE, THE PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION, ACCESS TO PUBLIC SERVICES, THE POLICE AND ELECTIONS. THE ADMINISTRATION OF JUSTICE is first on its own list. An organisation that investigates corruption inside the courts is unusually placed to advise whether a case is worth bringing in a given jurisdiction. WHAT IT PRODUCES FROM THAT WORK: THE RESULTS ARE IN MOST CASES SANCTIONED BY LETTERS TO THE AUTHORITIES, PRESS RELEASES OR REPORTS — PLUS PUBLIC AWARENESS CAMPAIGNS. Stated honestly: most of the output is letters and reports rather than judgments. Worth knowing before expecting litigation as the default. THE TREATY MONITORING IT DOES: FOLLOW-UP OF THE REPUBLIC'S INTERNATIONAL COMMITMENTS. WHAT IT IS, LEGALLY: A NON-PROFIT ORGANISATION UNDER CONGOLESE LAW AND A MEMBER OF CONGOLESE CIVIL SOCIETY, BASED IN KINSHASA/GOMBE — ITS VISION BEING TO CONTRIBUTE TO THE ADVENT OF A STATE OF LAW, AND ITS MISSION THE PROMOTION AND PROTECTION OF HUMAN RIGHTS. A domestic association under national law, not a foreign branch. It can be sued and it can sue, in its own courts, in French. THE NETWORKS THROUGH WHICH IT CAN BE REACHED: LISTED AS A CONTACT ORGANISATION BY A CORPORATE-CONDUCT COMPLAINTS WATCHDOG; LISTED AMONG HUMAN RIGHTS ORGANISATIONS WORLDWIDE BY AN INTERNATIONAL FEDERATION; A MEMBER OF AN ANTI-CORRUPTION COALITION'S AFRICA NETWORK; AND A MEMBER OF A NETWORK OF AFRICAN CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS ON OVERSIGHT OF THE PRIVATE SECURITY INDUSTRY. Four separate routes to reach it, which matters where a national organisation's own site is intermittent. And its private-security membership is the relevant one where a project is guarded by a contracted force rather than by police. THE SISTER ORGANISATION IT ACTS WITH: ACAJ (ASSOCIATION CONGOLAISE POUR L'ACCÈS À LA JUSTICE), WITH WHICH IT ISSUES JOINT POSITIONS. THE LEVERAGE ITS PRESIDENT NAMES, IN HIS OWN WORDS: THAT THE COUNTRY'S ELECTION TO THE INTERNATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS COUNCIL IS BOTH A RESPONSIBILITY AND A CHALLENGE TO THE AUTHORITIES FOR MORE CONCRETE ACTS — AND THAT IT IS ALSO A RESPONSIBILITY FOR THE PEOPLE, BECAUSE NOW WE HAVE A ROPE BY WHICH WE HOLD THE REGIME TO REMIND IT OF ITS NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL OBLIGATIONS. A ROPE BY WHICH WE HOLD THE REGIME. Membership of an international human rights body is a commitment a government has made in public, and it is usable by anyone: check whether your own state currently sits on such a body before deciding it has no reason to answer you. AND WHAT IT ASKS THAT LEVERAGE BE USED FOR, PLUS THE COUNTER-VIEW PUBLISHED BESIDE IT: RELEASING PEOPLE UNJUSTLY DETAINED OR CONVICTED, NOTABLY JOURNALISTS, HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS AND POLITICIANS — WHILE ANOTHER NAMED FOUNDATION ARGUED THE ELECTION IS NOT REASSURING GIVEN CLANDESTINE CELLS, JUDICIAL SLOWNESS AND ABDUCTIONS. Filed with the disagreement intact. One organisation treats the seat as leverage; another says it launders a record that includes secret detention. Both views are on the record, and a community deciding whether international pressure will help should read both. WHO IT SUITS: francophone communities on or near mining concessions, defenders detained by soldiers rather than police, and insiders who intend to report what a project is doing. CAVEATS: ONE COUNTRY, WITH A CORRUPTION AND CIVIL-LIBERTIES FRAME RATHER THAN LAND OR PLANNING; BY ITS OWN ACCOUNT MOST OUTPUT IS LETTERS, PRESS RELEASES AND REPORTS RATHER THAN LITIGATION, AND SOME MATERIAL CITED IS OLDER. For the schedule of obligations a company owes your village, this bucket's own entry; for the free legal clinics staffed by young lawyers, this bucket's clinic entry.

trackers.name: Cour des comptes
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Djibouti, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Djibouti — Ministère de l’Économie et des Finances (MEFIP)
trackers.desc: National budget authority; manages public finances & the economy and prepares the State budget, Djibouti. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Djibouti.

trackers.name: Djibouti — Guichet Unique (ANPI)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the ANPI’s Guichet Unique registers company constitution acts and (with the ODPIC) handles RCCM immatriculation & fiscal/social registration, Djibouti. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: African Convention on Nature — check WHICH version binds your state
trackers.desc: THERE ARE TWO AFRICAN CONVENTIONS OF THIS NAME, AND CITING THE WRONG ONE IS THE AVOIDABLE ERROR HERE. The Algiers Convention was signed 15 September 1968, in force 16 June 1969. The revised Maputo Convention was adopted by the Assembly of the Union in Maputo on 11 July 2003 and entered into force 23 July 2016 — thirteen years later. THE OPERATIVE RULE: the 1968 Convention remains in force for those countries that have not ratified the 2003 revisions, so the two coexist and which binds your state depends on its ratification status. Commentary records only about 30 percent of African states had ratified Maputo. This entry does not assert which binds your state — the African Union publishes a Status List alongside the treaty text at au.int. Check it first. WHY THE DELAY IS AN ARGUMENT FOR IT: commentary attributes the thirteen years to the revised text containing strong provisions that could create accountability and also slow down social and economic development — a treaty resisted for creating accountability is one worth invoking where it applies. PROVISIONS TO KNOW: article XXXIX — no reservation may be made to this Convention, so a ratifying state takes all of it; article XL — withdrawal takes effect only one year after written notification; and no instrument of accession to the 1968 Algiers Convention may be deposited any longer, so the older text is closed to new entrants. THE OBJECTIVES ARE BROADER THAN USUAL: conservation, utilisation and development of soil, water, flora and fauna for present and future welfare, from an economic, nutritional, scientific, educational, cultural and aesthetic point of view — so a claim resting on cultural or aesthetic value has a treaty basis. BUT IF THE 1968 TEXT IS WHAT BINDS YOU, EXPECT LITTLE: parties were encouraged to cooperate but were not required to submit regular reports on implementation, and there were no financial mechanisms — no reporting trail, no funding attached. Article XLI also provides for interim secretariat arrangements, so check current institutional capacity. IUCN publishes a commentary on each provision in English and French.

trackers.name: Djibouti Nature — the country's oldest conservation association, and the civil society relay on the marine protected areas
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an independent, membership-based, non-profit grassroots association established in December 1999 (formerly the Wildlife Protection Organization) — the oldest and most experienced civil society organisation working on nature conservation in Djibouti. It is small, and it is effectively the only such body with a public record. WHY IT MATTERS WHERE YOU LIVE: Djibouti's marine protected areas are drawn around inhabited places — Khor Angar, Godoria, Ras Siyan, the Seven Brothers islands, Douda-Haramous, the Musha and Maskali islands and Arta — and the national programme has involved those communities in marine biodiversity protection, with training delivered locally in tourism and coastguard work. The government's own stated aim has been to expand the protected marine area substantially. That means the designation is the lever: a community inside or beside a protected area has a standing that a community on unprotected coast does not, and Djibouti Nature is named in national biodiversity reporting as one of the associations that acts as the relay between those programmes and the public. Note the honest complication, because it cuts both ways: analysts have observed that the siting of Djibouti's marine areas serves territorial control as well as ecology — the designations are not purely environmental, and a community should understand which interest it is aligning with. Its own published work is species and site documentation across the Goda mountains, Day forest, Bankouale, Assamo, the mangroves at Godoria and Douda, and the islands. WHO IT SUITS: coastal, island and mountain communities needing baseline documentation, membership of a recognised association, or a national counterpart. CAVEATS: a small scientific and conservation association — no legal capacity, no intake route, no fee information; civic space in Djibouti is narrow and the organisation works with rather than against the state.

trackers.name: GEF Small Grants in Djibouti — an open call to community groups, 24 months maximum, and a 50% CO-FINANCING requirement half of which may be in kind
trackers.desc: WHERE TO APPLY FOR MONEY: the GEF Small Grants Programme (SGP), eighth operational phase, in DJIBOUTI, implemented with the UN development programme, inviting proposals FROM CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS AND GRASSROOTS COMMUNITY GROUPS for community-led projects on biodiversity conservation, climate mitigation and adaptation, SUSTAINABLE LAND MANAGEMENT, international waters, and reduction of harmful chemicals and waste. THE TWO TERMS THAT DECIDE WHETHER YOU CAN APPLY, and they are published: projects may run a MAXIMUM OF 24 MONTHS, and are required to provide AT LEAST 50% CO-FINANCING, DIVIDED EQUALLY BETWEEN CASH CONTRIBUTIONS AND IN-KIND SUPPORT. That means half the co-financing can be labour, land, materials or premises rather than money — count what your community already contributes before deciding you cannot meet the match, because in-kind is where a village's real contribution lives. Eligible proposals must align with national frameworks including the National Action Plan for Sustainable Environment (NAPE), show strategic relevance and clear environmental and social impact, and be DESIGNED COLLABORATIVELY WITH THE LOCAL COMMUNITY. Priorities include local climate resilience, affordable sustainable energy for household and economic use, and environmentally responsible livelihoods including agricultural production, processing and marketing. WHY THIS ENTRY EXISTS: Djibouti was searched THREE TIMES in this file for a local land or legal organisation and nothing verifiable was found beyond its conservation association. As in the Comoros, the realistic route in a small state with a thin associative sector is not an NGO to enlist but a CALL TO ANSWER — and this one is addressed to grassroots community groups by name. WHO IT SUITS: Djiboutian community groups and associations with a land management, water, energy or livelihoods project. CAVEATS: A DONOR CYCLE WITH FIXED DEADLINES and a real co-financing requirement — confirm the current call before counting on it; it funds environmental action, NOT litigation, land purchase or opposition to a project. For the country's conservation association, Djibouti's Djibouti Nature entry.

trackers.name: Djibouti's audiences foraines — the court travels to your commune and the calendar MUST be posted on the mairie door; there are only about 12 advocates, all in the capital
trackers.desc: WHERE JUSTICE PHYSICALLY HAPPENS, AND WHY THAT IS THE WHOLE QUESTION HERE: under Djibouti's Code de procédure civile (loi n°004/AN/18/8), Article L.111-12, the seat of the TRIBUNAL DE PREMIÈRE INSTANCE is in Djibouti city and its jurisdiction covers the ENTIRE territory — BUT AUDIENCES FORAINES (travelling hearings) MAY BE HELD at the seat of the communes of Djibouti city and Balbala AND AT THE SEAT OF EACH REGIONAL COUNCIL. AND THE PUBLICITY RULE IS THE PART TO USE: the CALENDAR OF THE AUDIENCES FORAINES IS MADE PUBLIC BY POSTING ON THE DOOR OF THE MAIRIES OR REGIONAL COUNCILS CONCERNED, and by any other appropriate means. Watch the door of your mairie — that posted calendar is how a person outside the capital learns when a court will physically be within reach, and it is required, not discretionary. A second provision: a DETACHED JUDGE of the personal status tribunal sits in each commune and region of the interior and must RESIDE at the regional or communal chief town, with the number and days of hearings fixed at the start of the judicial year. THE CONSTRAINT THAT SHAPES EVERYTHING, STATED PLAINLY: an official account records about TWELVE ADVOCATES registered at the Djiboutian bar, ALL PRACTISING IN THE CAPITAL — for the simple reason that there are no tribunals in the other districts; fees are agreed freely between advocate and client under the profession's governing law. Twelve advocates for a whole country means the binding constraint is availability, not eligibility — secure counsel before you time anything else. New civil and civil procedure codes were adopted to replace the inherited colonial codes, with the second book of the civil code covering PROPERTY and patrimony. WHO IT SUITS: Djiboutians outside the capital needing to reach a court, and anyone timing a land or property claim. CAVEATS: NO LEGAL AID ORGANISATION OR CLINIC COULD BE VERIFIED for Djibouti — this entry records a procedural right and a bar of about twelve practitioners, not a service; foreign missions publish attorney lists that should be checked as current. For community environmental funding, Djibouti's GEF Small Grants entry; for the conservation association, Djibouti Nature.

trackers.name: Djibouti's loi 16/AN/23 on protected areas — the LOCAL COMMUNITY is named as a possible gestionnaire, and DECAN got two areas classified on its own initiative
trackers.desc: THE LAW THAT NAMES YOUR COMMUNITY AS MANAGER: LOI N°16/AN/23/9ème L on protected areas defines a GESTIONNAIRE D'UNE AIRE PROTÉGÉE as ANY PUBLIC OR PRIVATE PERSON, MIXED GROUPING, LEGALLY CONSTITUTED GROUPING OR THE LOCAL COMMUNITY assuring the management of the protected area in collaboration with the stakeholders concerned. The local community is written into the statute as a category of manager, not as a consultee — that single definition is what a Djiboutian community should quote when asking to manage the ground it lives on. The law also defines ÉCOTOURISME as responsible and sustainable tourism based on conserving Djibouti's natural heritage, RESPECTING THE ENVIRONMENT AND THE POPULATIONS WHILE ENSURING AN EQUITABLE REDISTRIBUTION OF THE ECONOMIC BENEFITS, and requires a PLAN D'AMÉNAGEMENT ET DE GESTION for each area, with areas linked in a RÉSEAU. Equitable redistribution is in the definition of the activity itself — so a tourism operation inside a protected area that returns nothing locally is failing the statutory definition, not merely being ungenerous. Behind it, the CODE DE L'ENVIRONNEMENT (loi 51/AN/09) guarantees EVERY PERSON RESIDING IN DJIBOUTI THE RIGHT TO A HEALTHY ENVIRONMENT, and places environmental policy on the state IN CLOSE COLLABORATION WITH LOCAL AUTHORITIES, CITIZENS AND CIVIL SOCIETY ACTORS. WHO HAS ACTUALLY DONE IT: DECAN, a Djiboutian association for the protection of the country's fauna and flora, IDENTIFIED AND DEFINED TWO PROTECTED AREAS — the DJALÉLO valley (45 km2, Arta region, 40 km from the capital) and the ASSAMO massif (15 km2, Ali-Sabieh region) — and it was ON THAT ASSOCIATION'S INITIATIVE, with ministry support, THAT THE GOVERNMENT CLASSIFIED BOTH SITES, creating a particular legal status of aire naturelle protégée for them; DECAN built an eco-camp on each area, and THE TOTALITY OF THE FUNDS RECEIVED IS REUSED DIRECTLY FOR PROTECTING THE SITES IT MANAGES. A local association identified the land, defined the boundary and the state then classified it — in Djibouti the initiative can come from below, and there are two named precedents. The context is stark: the Day forest, Djibouti's only forest and one of the continent's last primary forests, has fallen from about 7,500 ha two centuries ago to 1,500 ha in 1984 and under 900 ha today, with a law voted to give it protected-area status. WHO IT SUITS: Djiboutian communities and associations seeking to have ground classified and to manage it. CAVEATS: CLASSIFICATION IS A STATE ACT AND MANAGEMENT IS BY DESIGNATION — not tenure; the Day forest case shows protection status arriving without secured finance. For the posted travelling-court calendar and the twelve-advocate bar, Djibouti's audiences foraines entry; for community project money, the GEF Small Grants entry; for the conservation association, Djibouti Nature.

trackers.name: Djibouti's association networks — the FAONG/DD forum, the climate and development network, and eight named associations doing reforestation and land restoration
trackers.desc: THE NETWORKS THAT FEDERATE SMALL ASSOCIATIONS, WHICH IS HOW A DJIBOUTIAN VILLAGE GROUP GETS HEARD: the FORUM DES ASSOCIATIONS ET ONGs DJIBOUTIENNES POUR LE DÉVELOPPEMENT DURABLE (FAONG/DD) analysed EIGHT named associations and NGOs — the ASSOCIATION DES FEMMES DE TADJOURAH (AFT), A.P.S.E.R.A.S, AJCD, Association Autisme Sport et Loisir, NADIF, ONG EVA, SOUNA AL HAYA and BENDER DJEDID — finding that Djiboutian civil society is not a spectator on water access, climate change and the energy transition: IT ACTS, as indispensable acteurs de proximité delivering concrete responses. Named associations with a forum that publishes an analysis of them is the fastest route into Djibouti's small associative sector — ask FAONG/DD which of its members works in your region rather than starting from nothing. WHAT THEY ACTUALLY DO ON THE GROUND: beyond water and sanitation these organisations engage against climate change through REFORESTATION, LAND RESTORATION and community awareness — and even bodies working in education or social support take part in those environmental initiatives, which the forum reads as a cross-cutting mobilisation. In a country this small, an education or disability association may be the one with people in your district — do not filter by an organisation's headline theme. THE HONEST FINDING, PUBLISHED BY THE FORUM ITSELF: these organisations rest on a SIMILAR INSTITUTIONAL ARCHITECTURE — general assembly, executive bureau, operational teams — BUT THEIR CAPACITIES REMAIN UNEVENLY DISTRIBUTED, and the sector is a development actor in its own right ON CONDITION THAT IT IS GIVEN THE MEANS. Copy the architecture — assembly, bureau, operational team — because it is what the forum recognises as an organisation; then be honest about which capacities you lack when you ask for support. TWO MORE NAMED BODIES: the RÉSEAU CLIMAT ET DÉVELOPPEMENT DE DJIBOUTI, which brings together NGOs and associations working on local or national development under climate pressure; and ÉCOLO À DJIBOUTI (ecoloadjibouti.com), a Djiboutian association working on environmental education, LOCAL SUSTAINABLE PROJECTS and scientific outreach, which states it has spent over four years cultivating trust and collaboration within local communities. WHO IT SUITS: Djiboutian community groups seeking allies, recognition or a route into national processes. CAVEATS: NETWORKS AND SMALL ASSOCIATIONS, NOT FUNDERS OR LAW FIRMS — the capacity gap is stated by the sector itself. For the oldest conservation association and the Day forest species, Djibouti's Djibouti Nature entry; for project money with the 50% co-financing rule, the GEF Small Grants entry; for the posted travelling-court calendar, the audiences foraines entry.

trackers.name: Association Amis Juristes de Djibouti — magistrates, jurists and legal advisers in one association, with a named secretary general and two published phone numbers, in a country with about a dozen advocates
trackers.desc: THE JURISTS WHO PUBLISH A PHONE NUMBER — and this file records that Djibouti has only about twelve advocates in the whole country, all in the capital, so a reachable legal body matters more here than almost anywhere: the ASSOCIATION AMIS JURISTES DE DJIBOUTI (AJD), whose stated mission is TO INFORM, TRAIN AND POPULARISE NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL LEGAL INSTRUMENTS AMONG PRIVATE-SECTOR ACTORS AND ALL COMPONENTS OF CIVIL SOCIETY, SO AS TO RAISE THEIR AWARENESS AND, CONSTRUCTIVELY, TO ADVOCATE WITH PUBLIC INSTITUTIONS FOR STRONGER MEASURES AND MEANS. ITS COMPOSITION IS THE POINT: THE ORGANISATION IS MADE UP OF JURISTS FROM DIFFERENT LEGAL HORIZONS — MAGISTRATES, JURISTS AND LEGAL ADVISERS — and it SENSITISES AND TRAINS DIFFERENT CATEGORIES OF CITIZENS ON THE IMPLEMENTATION AND APPLICATION OF LEGAL INSTRUMENTS, through its own projects and activities. An association containing sitting magistrates alongside advocates and advisers is a different instrument from a law firm: it will not take your case, but it will tell you which instrument applies and train your people to use it. In a country of a dozen advocates, that is the difference between a claim you can argue and one you cannot. AND IT IS CONTACTABLE, WHICH IS RARE IN THIS FILE'S DJIBOUTIAN RECORD: A NAMED SECRETARY GENERAL, AN EMAIL BEGINNING WITH THE WORD AVOCAT, AND TWO PUBLISHED MOBILE NUMBERS. Two numbers and a named person is a door. Ring it and ask which national or international instrument covers your situation before you approach anyone in the administration — that is exactly the service the association says it provides. ITS DECLARED SUBJECTS are the implementation of legal instruments against corruption, drugs and the trafficking of human beings, and it is listed on an international anti-corruption civil society network. An anti-corruption membership means the association is already positioned to receive an allegation about how a permit or an allocation was obtained — which is often the real story behind a project on your land. ALSO NAMED, FOR THE SOCIAL SIDE: the ASSOCIATION DJIBOUTIENNE POUR L'ÉQUILIBRE ET LA PROMOTION DE LA FAMILLE (ADEPF), ESTABLISHED 1994, which WORKS CLOSELY WITH THE MINISTRY FOR THE PROMOTION OF WOMEN, THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND THE STATE SECRETARIAT OF YOUTH, whose method is AWARENESS CREATION, ADVOCACY AND COUNSELLING using TV AND RADIO PROGRAMMES AND EDUCATIONAL LEAFLETS AND BROCHURES, and which has LED ADVOCACY EFFORTS WITH PARLIAMENTARIANS; a founding member of it also helped draft Djibouti's family code. An association with a working relationship to three ministries and a record of moving parliamentarians is a channel, whatever its subject. In a country this small the same people sit on everything — ask ADEPF who to speak to, not just what it does. WHO IT SUITS: Djiboutians needing to know which law applies, communities suspecting an irregular allocation, and anyone needing a route to a ministry or a parliamentarian. CAVEATS: TRAINING AND ADVOCACY BODIES, NOT LITIGATORS — and this file records only about a dozen advocates nationally. For the country's oldest conservation association and the Day forest, Djibouti's Djibouti Nature entry; for the eight named associations and the forum that analysed them, the association networks entry; for the travelling-court calendar posted at the mairie door, the audiences foraines entry; for project money with the 50% co-financing rule, the GEF Small Grants entry.

trackers.name: UNFD — Djibouti's national women's union, founded weeks before independence, which certifies community associations at its own headquarters and holds direct implementation contracts
trackers.desc: THE ORGANISATION THAT CERTIFIES THE COMMUNITY ASSOCIATIONS: THE UNION NATIONALE DES FEMMES DJIBOUTIENNES (UNFD) IS A NON-GOVERNMENTAL, NON-PROFIT ORGANISATION CREATED ON THE BASIS OF THE 1901 LAW ON ASSOCIATIONS, WHICH CAME INTO BEING ON 30 APRIL 1977 — JUST UNDER TWO MONTHS BEFORE THE REPUBLIC OF DJIBOUTI'S ACCESSION TO NATIONAL SOVEREIGNTY — BORN OUT OF THE DJIBOUTIAN WOMEN'S INDEPENDENCE MOVEMENT. An organisation older than the state itself, formed under the association law rather than by decree. In a country this file records as having very few reachable bodies, that is the one with the deepest roots — and it is a membership organisation, not an agency. ITS OWN CLAIM ABOUT REACH IS THE POINT: EVERY DJIBOUTIAN IS NATURALLY LINKED TO THE UNFD, DESCRIBED AS A MAJOR ASSET FOR THE ORGANISATION THAT ENHANCES ITS CREDIBILITY AND POSITION AS A KEY PLAYER IN THE COUNTRY'S SOCIO-ECONOMIC AND POLITICAL DEVELOPMENT. Read that as capacity rather than as a boast: it means a message routed through the UNFD reaches households in quartiers and rural districts that a new association cannot. If your community needs to be heard nationally and has no standing of its own, this is the body with the distribution. AND HERE IS THE FUNCTION THAT MATTERS MOST FOR A NEW GROUP: THE UNFD HOLDS CERTIFICATE CEREMONIES FOR COMMUNITY ASSOCIATIONS OF A NAMED LOCALITY AT ITS OWN HEADQUARTERS IN DJIBOUTI. A national body that trains community associations and then certifies them at its own headquarters is a route to recognition that does not go through a ministry. If your association needs credibility in front of a funder or an authority, ask the UNFD what its certification involves and whether your locality is covered. IT ALSO WORKS QUARTIER BY QUARTIER: it hosted a LAUNCH WORKSHOP FOR THE ACTIVITIES OF A NAMED NUMBERED QUARTIER under a national project for the EXTENSION AND REHABILITATION OF DJIBOUTI'S SANITATION NETWORK. Sanitation, quartier by quartier, with the workshop held at the women's union rather than at a ministry. If drainage, sewerage or wastewater is your problem, that is where the project meetings actually happen — and neighbourhood-level launch workshops are the moment to put your street on the list. WHAT IT IS TRUSTED TO EXECUTE: the UNFD has held A DIRECT AGREEMENT CONTRACT FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF LITERACY ACTIVITIES FOR OUT-OF-SCHOOL GIRLS AND WOMEN, and has been sought under a CRISIS RESPONSE SOCIAL SAFETY NET PROJECT AS A SENIOR NGO FOR THE EXECUTION OF ACTIVITIES. Direct agreement contract means a funder engaged it without a competitive tender, which is what happens when an organisation is the only one that can reach the population. That is worth knowing when you are deciding who to partner with. AND IT CONVENES ON THE SUBJECT THAT MATTERS TO ANYONE FACING A COMPANY: THE UNFD HOSTED A REGIONAL TRAINING DEVOTED TO BUSINESS AND HUMAN RIGHTS AT ITS HEADQUARTERS, WITH A VISITING REGIONAL INTERGOVERNMENTAL DELEGATION, ON FOREIGN COOPERATION FUNDING. Business and human rights training, held in Djibouti, at a body a community can walk into. If a port, a logistics zone or an energy project is affecting your area, ask who attended that training and what framework they were taught — the vocabulary a company responds to is taught in rooms like that one. ALSO NAMED: the ASSOCIATION DJIBOUTIENNE POUR L'ÉQUILIBRE ET LA PROMOTION DE LA FAMILLE (ADEPF), ESTABLISHED 1994, working with three ministries and focusing on AWARENESS CREATION, ADVOCACY AND COUNSELLING rather than clinics; and the ASSOCIATION AL BIRI and ASSOCIATION BENDER DJEDID, which support widows and orphans, and ASSOCIATION IRIS, which provides assistance. Associations that support widows and orphans are the ones already trusted in a quarter. Where a displacement or a demolition has already happened, they are who the affected households are talking to. WHO IT SUITS: Djiboutian community associations seeking certification, neighbourhoods facing sanitation or infrastructure works, and anyone needing national reach. CAVEATS: A LARGE NATIONAL ORGANISATION WORKING CLOSELY WITH GOVERNMENT — judge its independence for yourself on your issue. For the country's oldest conservation association, Djibouti's Djibouti Nature entry; for an open call to community groups with a 24-month maximum, the GEF Small Grants entry; for the court that travels to your commune, the audiences foraines entry; for the FAONG/DD forum and the climate and development network, the association networks entry; for magistrates and legal advisers with two published numbers, the Amis Juristes entry.

trackers.name: Protection experts who will build your community a written security plan even where they have no office — free training in three languages, a manual in five African languages, and an honest note that they do not do evacuations, with the number that does
trackers.desc: TEN PEOPLE TRAINED, WHO THEN TRAINED A HUNDRED AND FIFTY — that is the method, and it is the reason this belongs in a thin bucket: IT TRAINED 10 DEFENDERS IN ONE AFRICAN COUNTRY — FOCAL POINTS FOR HUMAN RIGHTS IN THEIR PROVINCE — WHO LEARNED RISK MANAGEMENT, THREAT ASSESSMENT, HOW TO IMPROVE THEIR SAFETY AT WORK AND AT HOME, AND HOW TO WORK IN CONFLICT ZONES. AFTERWARDS, THE FOCAL POINTS TRANSFERRED THEIR KNOWLEDGE TO 150 OTHER HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS. One training reached a hundred and sixty people. If your area has no organisation with security expertise, the ask is not to send trainers to every village — it is to get two or three of your own people onto one course and have them come back and teach. Name them focal points, as this programme did, so the role survives the individual. AND IT WORKS WHERE IT HAS NO OFFICE, WHICH IS THE POINT FOR COUNTRIES LIKE THIS ONE: IN COUNTRIES WHERE IT HAS NO PERMANENT PRESENCE, IT OFFERS TAILORED ONSITE AND ONLINE CAPACITY BUILDING SUPPORT ON SECURITY MANAGEMENT AND PROTECTION — ITS PROTECTION EXPERTS SUPPORT COMMUNITIES, ORGANISATIONS AND INDIVIDUAL DEFENDERS IN ASSESSING THEIR RISKS IN THEIR SPECIFIC CONTEXTS, AND WORK TOWARDS DEVELOPING AND IMPLEMENTING COMPREHENSIVE SECURITY PLANS AND PROTOCOLS THAT ADDRESS THEIR PHYSICAL AND DIGITAL SECURITY. A written security plan for your committee, built with you rather than handed to you. Most groups in this file have never made one and improvise during the first crisis; this is who helps you write it beforehand. THE STANCE, AND IT IS WORTH HOLDING ANY HELPER TO IT: IT UNDERSTANDS THAT HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS ARE SUBJECTS OF RIGHTS, INSTEAD OF OBJECTS FOR PROTECTION — TAKING A PREVENTIVE AND COLLECTIVE PERSPECTIVE OF PROTECTION INSTEAD OF THE MOST OFTEN REACTIVE PERSPECTIVES. PREVENTIVE AND COLLECTIVE. The plan is for the group, not just for the leader — which matters because the person attacked is often not the one everybody expected. THE HONEST BOUNDARY, PUBLISHED ON ITS OWN CONTACT PAGE, AND MORE USEFUL THAN MOST ORGANISATIONS' PROMISES: IT DOES NOT PROVIDE EMERGENCY EVACUATION SUPPORT OR EMERGENCY GRANTS FOR DEFENDERS IN IMMINENT DANGER — AND IT NAMES THE URGENT HELPDESK TO CONTACT INSTEAD, PUBLISHING A 24-HOUR EMERGENCY HOT LINE NUMBER, A CALL HANDLE, AND EMAIL THROUGH A SECURE AND ENCRYPTED CHANNEL. They tell you plainly what they cannot do and give you the number of who can. Put both in your phone: this one for the plan, that one for the night it goes wrong. THE DESKS AND THE RECORD: IT PROVIDES ADVICE ON A DAILY BASIS TO 600 DEFENDERS AND THEIR ORGANISATIONS THROUGH ITS PERMANENT PROTECTION DESKS, AND DELIVERED TRAININGS ON SECURITY AND PROTECTION MEASURES FOR NEARLY 1,500 DEFENDERS IN A SIXTEEN-MONTH PERIOD — AND IT LIAISES WITH THE AFRICAN COMMISSION ON HUMAN AND PEOPLES' RIGHTS AND WITH THE UN SPECIAL RAPPORTEUR IN ORDER TO DESIGN AND IMPLEMENT NEW PROTECTION MECHANISMS. THE TRAINING ITSELF: AN E-LEARNING PROGRAMME ON SECURITY AND PROTECTION MANAGEMENT, OFFERED THREE TIMES PER YEAR IN ENGLISH, SPANISH AND FRENCH, INCORPORATING THE PHYSICAL, DIGITAL AND EMOTIONAL DIMENSIONS OF SECURITY, WITH INSTRUCTORS WALKING THROUGH CONCRETE SITUATIONS OF RISK AND THE VARIOUS WAYS TO INTERPRET RISK DEPENDING ON THE DIFFERENT IDENTITIES OF DEFENDERS — DESIGNED FOR NGOs, DEFENDERS AND THEIR COMMUNITIES, AND PRIORITISING THE ENROLMENT OF PEOPLE COMMISSIONED BY AN ORGANISATION, ASSOCIATION OR COMMUNITY WHO WILL BE ABLE TO APPLY WHAT THEY LEARNED TO A BROADER GROUP OR COLLECTIVE. Enrolment is prioritised for someone SENT BY a community rather than applying alone — so write a short letter from your association naming your candidate, because that letter is what moves them up the list. FILED HONESTLY: THE COURSE WAS MARKED SUSPENDED UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, so ask whether it has resumed before planning around it. THE EMOTIONAL DIMENSION is named alongside physical and digital. Fear and exhaustion are treated as security factors, not weakness — which is the framing that lets people admit them in a meeting.
