trackers.desc: NO OUTSIDE CAPITAL, ON PURPOSE — THE PRINCIPLE, HELD AGAINST ADVICE: IT REQUIRED NO OUTSIDE CAPITAL, A PRINCIPLE HELD TO EVEN WHEN AN EARLY EVALUATION RECOMMENDED ADDING AN EXTERNAL CREDIT LINE. THE WOMEN WERE SO CLEAR — THIS IS OUR MONEY, THIS IS OUR PROJECT — AND THAT SENSE OF OWNERSHIP IS WHY THESE GROUPS OUTLAST THE INDIVIDUAL PROGRAMS BUILT AROUND THEM. Every other funding entry in this file is somebody else's money arriving with somebody else's conditions and ending on somebody else's timetable. This one is the community's own, and it does not end. For a group facing a project that will take years, having any money at all that nobody can withdraw is worth more than a larger grant that expires. WHAT IT IS: A GROUP OF PEOPLE WHO MEET REGULARLY TO SAVE TOGETHER AND TAKE SMALL LOANS FROM THOSE SAVINGS — ACTIVITIES RUN IN CYCLES OF ONE YEAR, AFTER WHICH THE ACCUMULATED SAVINGS AND THE LOAN PROFITS ARE DISTRIBUTED BACK TO THE MEMBERS. IT IS A TRANSPARENT, DEMOCRATIC AND STRUCTURED VERSION OF THE INFORMAL SAVINGS GROUPS FOUND IN MANY PARTS OF THE DEVELOPING WORLD, FOR COMMUNITIES WITHOUT EASY ACCESS TO FORMAL FINANCIAL SERVICES. A STRUCTURED VERSION OF WHAT ALREADY EXISTS. Most villages in this file already run some form of rotating savings; this is that practice with written rules, which is what turns it into something a bank, a court or a funder will recognise. THE MECHANICS, PUBLISHED SO YOU CAN COPY THEM WITHOUT ANYONE'S PERMISSION: CYCLES USUALLY LAST BETWEEN 9 AND 12 MONTHS; MEMBERS MEET AT REGULAR INTERVALS, USUALLY ONCE A WEEK; EACH MEMBER DEPOSITS A FIXED MINIMUM AMOUNT REFERRED TO AS ONE SHARE, DEFINED BY THE GROUP AT THE BEGINNING OF THE CYCLE, AND MEMBERS CAN CONTRIBUTE MORE THAN ONE SHARE PER MEETING UP TO A MAXIMUM AGREED BY THE GROUP; ONCE THE FUND GROWS, MEMBERS TAKE LOANS REPAID WITH A SMALL INTEREST OR SERVICE CHARGE. The share is set by the group, and the maximum too. So the poorest member and the richest can both belong without one dominating — which is the design detail that decides whether a village fund unites people or divides them. THE FREE MANUAL: A PRACTICAL, STEP-BY-STEP GUIDE FOR FORMING, TRAINING, AND MENTORING A GROUP, WITH A TRAINING CALENDAR — AND AN ONLINE LIBRARY OF RESOURCES IS MAINTAINED ALONGSIDE IT. THE THREE PHASES AND THE HANDOVER: A NEWLY FORMED GROUP BEGINS IN AN INTENSIVE PHASE OF LEARNING AND LEARNING-BY-DOING; MOVES TO A DEVELOPMENT PHASE, INCREASINGLY SELF-MANAGING AS MEMBERS SAVE, BORROW AND REPAY; THEN ADVANCES TO A MATURITY PHASE, CONFIDENT AND AUTONOMOUS — AND IF IT CONTINUES AFTER ITS FIRST YEAR IT DOES SO AS AN INDEPENDENT, SELF-MANAGING GROUP. THE FACILITATOR ATTENDS EVERY SESSION IN THE INTENSIVE PHASE, BI-WEEKLY IN THE DEVELOPMENT PHASE, AND MONTHLY IN THE MATURITY PHASE. The helper's attendance is designed to fall away on a schedule. Ask any organisation offering to support your group to show you their withdrawal timetable; if they do not have one, they are building a dependency. THE PERMISSION STEP, WHICH IS THE PART GROUPS SKIP AND REGRET: BUILD TRUST WITH LOCAL LEADERS, GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS AND THEIR REPRESENTATIVES; OBTAIN PERMISSION TO OPERATE IN THE AREA; UNDERSTAND POTENTIAL SOCIAL AND ECONOMIC BARRIERS IN THE COMMUNITY THAT EXCLUDE SOME PEOPLE FROM PARTICIPATING; AND ORGANISE THE FIRST MEETING IN A SAFE SPACE — AN AREA WHERE PARTICIPANTS NORMALLY MEET OR FEEL COMFORTABLE AND FREE. Go to the chief and the district officer first. A savings group that appears without warning looks like a political organisation to a nervous administration — and this file has recorded groups de-registered on thinner grounds than that. THE TWO RULES THAT KEEP IT ALIVE: STRONG ADHERENCE TO ZERO TOLERANCE TO ARREARS IS CRITICAL — AND NO OUTSIDE ENTITY SHOULD BE IN THE GROUP'S CONSTITUTION. Write your constitution with no outsider named in it. An NGO, a project or a donor written into the founding document becomes a claim on the fund and a reason for the group to dissolve when they leave. HOW IT SPREADS, AND THE ORIGIN STORY IS THE INSTRUCTION: TOLD THAT THE ORGANISATION HAD HELPED START THE PROCESS, A TEACHER WENT TO ITS OFFICE, ASKED FOR A TRAINING GUIDE, AND DISAPPEARED FOR SEVERAL MONTHS — WHEN SHE CAME BACK SHE HAD ALREADY STARTED SIX SAVINGS GROUPS ON HER OWN. AGAIN AND AGAIN, THE MODEL SPREAD THIS WAY BECAUSE COMMUNITIES MADE IT THEIR OWN. One person, one downloaded guide, six groups. Nobody needs to be invited into this and no project has to be funded first — which is why it is the single most transferable thing in this file. WHAT THE GROUPS DO BEYOND MONEY, AND THIS IS WHY IT BELONGS HERE: OFTEN INDEPENDENTLY OF THE ORGANISATION, THEY ROUTINELY SUPPORT EACH OTHER TO SET UP SMALL BUSINESSES, NEGOTIATE FAIR PRICES IN THE MARKETPLACE, ADVOCATE FOR GENDER EQUALITY IN THEIR COMMUNITIES, AND PURSUE PUBLIC OFFICE — AND THE MODEL CAN BE ADAPTED FOR EMERGENCIES. NEGOTIATE FAIR PRICES and PURSUE PUBLIC OFFICE. A savings group becomes a standing organisation with money, records, weekly meetings and trust — which is exactly what a community needs when a project arrives, and it is far harder to dismiss than a committee formed the week of the crisis. THE TRAINER ROUTE: APPOINTED AND TRAINED COMMUNITY BASED TRAINERS OR VILLAGE AGENTS GUIDE THE FORMATION OF GROUPS AND OFFER TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE FOR ONE CYCLE, TYPICALLY 12 MONTHS — AND VILLAGE AGENTS ARE TRAINED TO ESTABLISH AND TRAIN NEW GROUPS THEMSELVES. AND A MEASURED FIGURE: A GROUP IN WEST AFRICAN COCOA-GROWING COMMUNITIES MOBILISES AN AVERAGE OF AROUND USD 2,000 IN SAVINGS PER YEAR AND REDISTRIBUTES A LARGE PORTION IN INTERNAL LOANS. SOME TRY TO RESTRICT WHAT YOU MAY SAY PUBLICLY. Given that publicity is what the same network says makes complaints work, agree your communications position before entering any mediation, and be wary of confidentiality terms that trade your only leverage. THE PRACTICAL FILING DETAILS: COMPLAINTS CAN USUALLY BE SUBMITTED BY LETTER, EMAIL OR ONLINE FORM, THOUGH SOME BODIES REQUIRE A SPECIFIC FORMAT OR TEMPLATE; COMPLAINTS AND SUPPORTING DOCUMENTS CAN TYPICALLY BE WRITTEN IN YOUR OWN LANGUAGE, BUT NOT ALL ACCEPT EVERY LANGUAGE OR OFFER TRANSLATION; AND A COMPLAINT SHOULD INCLUDE THE NAME OF EACH PERSON OR ORGANIZATION FILING, CONTACT DETAILS FOR KEY COMMUNITY REPRESENTATIVES, AND, IF APPLICABLE, WRITTEN AUTHORIZATION FOR REPRESENTATIVES ACTING ON BEHALF OF AFFECTED INDIVIDUALS OR COMMUNITIES. WRITTEN AUTHORIZATION is the document to prepare early: a signed mandate from the affected households letting an organisation act for them. Without it a representative filing is refused; with it, individuals need not be exposed. THE DRAFTING HELP OFFERED: IF YOU ARE CONSIDERING FILING, YOU CAN CONTACT A NAMED LEGAL NON-PROFIT OR THIS NETWORK FOR HELP WITH DRAFTING AND STRATEGIZING YOUR COMPLAINT. AND THE PROCESS SHAPE: WHERE MULTIPLE BODIES ARE INVOLVED THEY COORDINATE TO DECIDE A LEAD AND SUPPORTING BODIES, WITH AN INDICATIVE TIMELINE OF TWO MONTHS FOR THAT STEP; THE LEAD BODY THEN CONDUCTS AN INITIAL ASSESSMENT, ATTEMPTS MEDIATION IF IT ACCEPTS, MAY INVESTIGATE AND ISSUE RECOMMENDATIONS IF MEDIATION FAILS, AND SHOULD PUBLISH A FINAL STATEMENT. MULTIPLE BODIES can take one case — the company's home country and the country where it operates. Filing in both is a choice, and the coordination step is where you can argue for the stronger-scoring office to lead. WHO IT SUITS: African communities and organisations facing a multinational, deciding whether this route is worth the years — and needing help drafting if it is. CAVEATS: MULTINATIONALS ONLY, NO ENFORCEMENT POWER, AND THE NETWORK'S OWN RECORD SHOWS REMEDY IS UNCOMMON — use it as one prong of a campaign. For the contact points themselves, Chad's entry; for the centre that files complaints on communities' behalf, Cape Verde's entry; for the request-only legal non-profit, Burundi's entry.

trackers.name: AJWS (American Jewish World Service) — a funder whose land and water programme exists to defend communities from irresponsible development projects — it paid for a Kenyan community's case at the African Court of Human and Peoples' Rights, and has no application form, only an email address and phone number
trackers.desc: THEY PAID FOR A COMMUNITY TO TAKE ITS LAND CLAIM TO THE AFRICAN COURT — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S KENYA ENTRY CARRIES A WILDLIFE FOUNDATION AND A FOREST PEOPLES HOST; ITS SENEGAL ENTRY A LAND COALITION NAME; ITS LIBERIA ENTRY A TENURE FACILITY AND A LAND COALITION HOST; ITS CAMEROON, REPUBLIC OF CONGO, COMOROS AND CÔTE D'IVOIRE ENTRIES THE OTHER FUNDERS ADDED IN THIS RUN. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS — THE CORRECTION MADE AFTER A DUPLICATE WAS CAUGHT ON A SIBLING HOST. THE COURT CASE IT PAID FOR, WHICH IS THE FIND: A CLIMATE JUSTICE GRANTEE IN KENYA, A NAMED INDIGENOUS PEOPLES' DEVELOPMENT PROJECT, RECEIVED SUPPORT FOR A LEGAL BATTLE IN THE AFRICAN COURT OF HUMAN AND PEOPLES' RIGHTS THAT SECURED THE COMMUNITY'S LEGAL CLAIM TO THE LAND — AND GRANTEES HAVE SECURED STATE RECOGNITION OF INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES' ANCESTRAL LANDS IN KENYA. A community organisation, funded by a grantmaker, winning land recognition at the continental court. This file has recorded the African Court as a route communities cannot reach for want of money; here is the funder that paid, and the result. When arguing that a continental case is worth funding, that precedent is the argument. WHAT THE PROGRAMME IS FOR, IN ITS OWN WORDS: IN KENYA, IT DEFENDS COMMUNITIES' ACCESS TO LAND, WATER AND OTHER NATURAL RESOURCES THAT ARE BEING EXPLOITED BY IRRESPONSIBLE DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS. IRRESPONSIBLE DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS, named as the thing being defended against. Not habitat loss, not climate in the abstract — the project itself. A community does not have to reframe its opposition as conservation to be on-brief here. HOW YOU APPROACH IT: THOUGH THEY DO NOT HAVE A FORMAL GRANT APPLICATION PROCESS, THEY DO PROVIDE AN EMAIL ADDRESS AND PHONE NUMBER ON THEIR WEBSITE — AND A GRASSROOTS ORGANISATION WORKING ON ADVOCACY FOR LAND RIGHTS, ENVIRONMENTAL OR CLIMATE JUSTICE IN AFRICA IS DESCRIBED AS MORE LIKELY TO GET FUNDED BY THIS ORGANISATION. No form, but a phone number. That is a different proposition from the funds in this file that take no unsolicited approaches and give no contact at all — a short, specific email describing the project threatening your land is a real first move, and there is a voice at the end of a line. THE THREAT IT NAMES: THE AGGRESSIVE DRIVE TO DEVELOP LAND, BUILD MEGA-DAMS, MINE FOR MINERALS, HARVEST RIVERS AND OCEANS AND LOG THE EARTH'S REMAINING FORESTS IS UNJUSTLY PUSHING MILLIONS OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLE AND SMALL FARMERS OUT OF THE HOMES WHERE THEY'VE LIVED FOR GENERATIONS — LANDS AND WATERS THAT OFTEN HOLD SPIRITUAL AND CULTURAL SIGNIFICANCE CENTRAL TO THEIR IDENTITIES. AND THE GOVERNMENTS' PART, STATED PLAINLY: MANY GOVERNMENTS BLATANTLY DISREGARD LAWS AND TREATIES PROTECTING THE RIGHTS OF THESE COMMUNITIES, PUTTING PROFIT OVER THE NEEDS OF PEOPLE AND OUR PLANET. A funder willing to say in public that governments break their own laws. That matters practically: an organisation whose case is against the state does not have to soften it to fit this funder's language. WHO IS ELIGIBLE: NON-GOVERNMENTAL, COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS IN AFRICA, LATIN AMERICA, THE CARIBBEAN AND ASIA — WITH ONE ISSUE AREA BEING NATURAL RESOURCE RIGHTS AND ECONOMIC JUSTICE, SUPPORTING GRASSROOTS ORGANISATIONS TO DEFEND THEIR RIGHTS TO THEIR NATURAL RESOURCES, FOSTER MORE JUST ECONOMIES BASED ON THEIR SUSTAINABLE USE, AND BUILD MORE INCLUSIVE SOCIAL MOVEMENTS. COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS as the named recipient type, not a partner category beneath an international lead. THE OTHER ISSUE AREA THAT BEARS ON THIS FILE: CIVIL AND POLITICAL RIGHTS — LAYING THE GROUNDWORK FOR A JUST AND INCLUSIVE SOCIETY IN CONFLICT, POST-CONFLICT, AND REPRESSIVE REGIME SETTINGS. REPRESSIVE REGIME SETTINGS named as a place it works rather than a risk it avoids. Where a community's problem is that organising is dangerous, that is inside the remit. THE STATED BELIEF BEHIND THE GRANTMAKING: GRASSROOTS ORGANIZATIONS ARE BEST PLACED TO ENVISION, ARTICULATE AND IMPLEMENT THEIR OWN SOLUTIONS, AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT CANNOT TAKE PLACE WHEN HUMAN RIGHTS ARE DENIED. THE SCALE: SOME 500 GRASSROOTS ORGANIZATIONS SUPPORTED EVERY YEAR ACROSS 17 COUNTRIES, WITH MORE THAN 100 ORGANISATIONS DEVOTED TO CLIMATE JUSTICE. Seventeen countries, so the first question is whether yours is one of them — the named African ones below are the place to start. THE AFRICAN COUNTRIES AND WORK NAMED: KENYA, DEFENDING ACCESS TO LAND AND WATER AGAINST IRRESPONSIBLE DEVELOPMENT; UGANDA, WHERE ACROSS THE WEST AND NORTH IT SUPPORTS FEMINIST COLLECTIVES AND GRASSROOTS MOVEMENTS FIGHTING TO PROTECT THEIR COMMUNITIES' LAND, FORESTS AND NATURAL RESOURCES, WITH A NAMED NORTHERN UGANDAN FOREST RESERVE AMONG ITS STORIES; AND SENEGAL, SUPPORTING GRASSROOTS ORGANISATIONS HELPING PEOPLE ACCESS JUSTICE AND HOLD ELECTED OFFICIALS ACCOUNTABLE, AND PARTNERING ON PEACE IN A NAMED REGION AFTER OVER 35 YEARS OF CONFLICT. FEMINIST COLLECTIVES DEFENDING FOREST is a specific and unusual combination to fund. A women's group organising against logging in Uganda has a funder that already backs exactly that shape of organisation. THE MOVEMENT REQUIREMENT IT DESCRIBES: THE ACTIVISTS IT SUPPORTS KNOW THEY CANNOT DO THIS WORK ALONE — THEY BUILD GRASSROOTS SOCIAL MOVEMENTS TO CREATE CHANGE, FIGHTING AT THE LOCAL, NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL LEVEL. Read that as a selection signal: an organisation that can show it works with others is a better fit than one working alone, which is an argument for joining the coalitions filed throughout this list before approaching. AND THE FIGURE IT PUBLISHES: INDIGENOUS PEOPLE REPRESENT JUST 5% OF THE WORLD'S POPULATION, BUT THEY PROTECT OVER 80% OF THE EARTH'S BIODIVERSITY — WITH THE ORGANISATION ACKNOWLEDGING THAT THE ACTIVISTS IT SUPPORTS AND THE COMMUNITIES THEY FIGHT FOR ARE THE TRUE STEWARDS OF THE PLANET'S FUTURE. Five per cent of people, eighty per cent of biodiversity. That pairing is the standard counter to any proposal that a place would be better protected without the people in it. WHO IT SUITS: African community-based organisations in its focus countries fighting a dam, mine, logging concession or land acquisition — including those whose case is against their own government. CAVEATS: SEVENTEEN FOCUS COUNTRIES BOUND EVERYTHING, THERE IS NO APPLICATION FORM, AND IT FUNDS ORGANISATIONS AND MOVEMENTS RATHER THAN INDIVIDUALS — check the country list, then use the published contact. For the fund reached through regional advisors, Cameroon's entry; for the catalyst-grant ladder into long-term unrestricted money, the Republic of Congo's entry; for unregistered collectives applying in their own language, Comoros' entry.

trackers.name: WAHRDN / ROADDH (West African Human Rights Defenders Network) — the West African defenders network — national coalitions and individual focal points across sixteen named countries, a secretariat address, a published email, observer status at the African Commission and a seat on the NGO Forum steering committee
trackers.desc: SIXTEEN COUNTRIES, A FOCAL POINT IN EACH, AND A SEAT AT THE CONTINENTAL COMMISSION — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S COMOROS ENTRY COVERS THE EAST AND HORN OF AFRICA NETWORK AND NOTES THAT SISTER NETWORKS EXIST WITHOUT NAMING THEM; ITS CAPE VERDE AND LIBERIA BUCKETS CARRY A CONTINENTAL DEFENDERS HOST AND NAME; ITS REPUBLIC OF CONGO ENTRY THE EU MECHANISM. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. THE SIXTEEN COUNTRIES IT COVERS, WHICH IS THE FIND: MALI, MAURITANIA, GUINEA, SENEGAL, GAMBIA, NIGER, BURKINA FASO, IVORY COAST, CAPE VERDE, SIERRA LEONE, LIBERIA, TOGO, BENIN, GHANA, NIGERIA AND GUINEA BISSAU — WITH A SECRETARIAT BASED IN A NAMED WEST AFRICAN CAPITAL. West Africa is where this file's land conflicts concentrate and where its resources thin out fastest, because almost everything else here operates in English from the east or south. A regional defenders body with a secretariat inside the sub-region closes that gap. WHAT IT IS MADE OF, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: IT COMPRISES NATIONAL COALITIONS OF HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS AND INDIVIDUAL FOCAL POINTS FROM THOSE 16 COUNTRIES. INDIVIDUAL FOCAL POINTS. There is a named person for your country, not a regional inbox — which is the difference between a message that is read by someone who knows the district and one that is filed. Ask for the focal point by country first. THE CONTINENTAL STANDING IT HOLDS: OBSERVER STATUS WITH THE AFRICAN COMMISSION ON HUMAN AND PEOPLES' RIGHTS, AND MEMBERSHIP OF THE STEERING COMMITTEE FOR THE NGO FORUM WHICH PRECEDES THE COMMISSION'S ORDINARY SESSIONS — ALSO SITTING ON THAT FORUM'S EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE. Observer status is the credential this file recorded, under Sudan, defeating an application that lacked it. A body that holds it can carry a community's material into the Commission, and sitting on the NGO Forum steering committee means it helps set what that pre-session discusses. THE GLOBAL COALITION IT BELONGS TO: A HUMAN RIGHTS COUNCIL NETWORK, A GLOBAL COALITION OF CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS ENGAGED IN ADVOCACY AND LOBBYING WITH THE UNITED NATIONS HUMAN RIGHTS COUNCIL. THE COURT COALITION IT IS A MEMBER OF: A COALITION FOR AN EFFECTIVE AFRICAN COURT ON HUMAN AND PEOPLES' RIGHTS. A standing coalition on the continental court itself. For a community weighing a continental filing — which this file has recorded as expensive and procedurally treacherous — that coalition is where the practitioners who have tried it are gathered. WHOM ITS STRATEGY WORKS THROUGH: CLOSE COOPERATION WITH DIPLOMATIC REPRESENTATIONS, FOREIGN MINISTRIES, NATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS INSTITUTIONS, AND REGIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS MECHANISMS. NATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS INSTITUTIONS are the domestic body most communities never think to use — a statutory commission in your own capital with powers to investigate. This network works through them, which is a route in. WHAT IT AIMS AT: TO SHAPE THE DOMESTIC AND FOREIGN POLICY OF WEST AFRICAN COUNTRIES IN LINE WITH HUMAN RIGHTS STANDARDS, TO STRENGTHEN THE RULE OF LAW, AND TO DEFEND AND PROTECT THE RIGHTS OF HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS IN THE SUB-REGION. THE PUBLISHED CONTACT: A GENERAL EMAIL ADDRESS PUBLISHED IN AN INTERNATIONAL DEFENDER RESOURCE LIST FOR THE NETWORK. WHERE IT SITS IN THE CONTINENTAL STRUCTURE: A SUB-REGIONAL MEMBER OF A PAN-AFRICAN HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS NETWORK, CREATED IN MAY 2005. THE SOUTHERN AFRICAN SISTER NETWORK, NAMED WITH ITS COUNTRIES: ESTABLISHED IN FEBRUARY 2013, COMPRISING REPRESENTATIVES FROM HUMAN RIGHTS ORGANISATIONS IN TEN COUNTRIES — WITH DELEGATES FROM ANGOLA, BOTSWANA, THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO, ESWATINI, LESOTHO, MALAWI, SOUTH AFRICA, ZAMBIA AND ZIMBABWE PARTICIPATING IN ITS GENERAL ASSEMBLY. Recorded so the map is complete: with the East and Horn network filed under Comoros, the sixteen countries above, and these ten, most of the continent now has a named regional defenders body — and a defender can identify theirs without searching. THE SPECIAL RAPPORTEUR THE WHOLE STRUCTURE FEEDS: A COMMISSIONER OF THE AFRICAN COMMISSION SERVING AS SPECIAL RAPPORTEUR ON HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS IN AFRICA AND AS FOCAL POINT ON REPRISALS AGAINST HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS IN AFRICA, PRESENTING INTERSESSION REPORTS TO ORDINARY SESSIONS — WITH THE COMMISSION'S POSTAL ADDRESS, TELEPHONE, FAX AND EMAIL PUBLISHED. There is a named continental office for reprisals against defenders, with a published address and telephone number. Where an organiser is punished for testifying or for engaging an international body, that is the specific mandate to write to — and this file has recorded reprisal as the standard consequence of raising a case. AND THE RESTRICTION THAT SHOWS WHY THE STRUCTURE MATTERS: THE CONTINENTAL BODY AND ITS MEMBER NETWORKS PUBLICLY RECORDED DEEP CONCERN AT THE UNJUSTIFIABLE IMPOSITION OF A RESTRICTION ON THE NETWORK OF HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS IN CENTRAL AFRICA, BARRING IT FROM OPERATING THROUGHOUT A NAMED COUNTRY — AND THE SAME BODIES ISSUED A JOINT REGIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL CALL FOR THE IMMEDIATE AND UNCONDITIONAL RELEASE OF A NAMED DETAINED DEFENDER AND THE WITHDRAWAL OF HIS PROSECUTION. Both halves are the point: the regional networks can be banned, and when a defender is detained the whole structure issues one joint statement rather than five separate ones. A joint call carries further than any single organisation's letter, and it is what membership buys. WHO IT SUITS: West African community organisations and land defenders — for a national focal point, a route into the African Commission, and a joint regional response when someone is detained. CAVEATS: AN ADVOCACY AND COORDINATION NETWORK RATHER THAN A FUNDER, A LAW FIRM OR AN EMERGENCY SERVICE; IT WORKS THROUGH NATIONAL COALITIONS AND FOCAL POINTS, SO THE ROUTE IN IS YOUR OWN COUNTRY'S — and regional networks themselves can be restricted by governments. For the 24/7 emergency line and protection grants, Comoros' entry; for the EU mechanism behind much of the funding, the Republic of Congo's entry.

trackers.name: Ethiopia's eight university free legal aid centres — Addis Ababa, Arba Minch, Assosa, Debark, Gambella, Jigjiga, Mekelle and Samara — convened by the Ethiopian Human Rights Commission, plus EHRCO, suspended by the regulator in December 2024
trackers.desc: EIGHT UNIVERSITIES RUN FREE LEGAL AID CENTRES — AND THEY ARE NAMED — method and adjacency declared first: EIGHTH NAMED-ATTORNEY ROUND. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN FOUR HOSTS AND SIX DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; BOTH SUBJECT HOSTS, THE ACRONYM AND FOUR FACTS ABSENT. ONE CITY NAME MATCHED A SOMALIA ENTRY ON TOWN ENVIRONMENTAL ASSOCIATIONS AND ONE REGULATOR NAME AN ETHIOPIA ENTRY ON A STATUTORY CSO COUNCIL, BOTH READ IN FULL AND DIFFERENT SUBJECTS. THIS FILE'S BENIN AND CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC ENTRIES COVER PARALEGAL CLINICS IN OTHER COUNTRIES. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE EIGHT NAMED CENTRES, WHICH IS THE FIND: FREE LEGAL AID CENTRES AT ADDIS ABABA, ARBA MINCH, ASSOSA, DEBARK, GAMBELLA, JIGJIGA, MEKELLE AND SAMARA UNIVERSITIES — THEIR REPRESENTATIVES BROUGHT TOGETHER BY THE NATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS COMMISSION WITH A GOVERNMENT MINISTRY, THE UN REFUGEE AGENCY AND OTHER NGOs. Eight universities, named, spread from the far north to the eastern and western peripheries rather than clustered in the capital. This file has recorded again and again that lawyers concentrate in cities; a law faculty in a regional town is a permanent institution that is already there, already free, and asked for by name. Look up the nearest law faculty before assuming there is no lawyer within reach. WHAT THE FORUM WAS FOR, AND WHAT IT MEASURED: TO ASSESS THE OPERATIONAL STATUS OF THE UNIVERSITY-BASED FREE LEGAL AID CENTRES, IDENTIFY CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES AND FACILITATE CONDITIONS FOR FUTURE COLLABORATION — WITH A DISCUSSION OF THE COMMISSION'S OWN MONITORING FINDINGS ON THE RIGHT OF REFUGEES AND ASYLUM SEEKERS TO ACCESS JUSTICE. The national commission convened them and checked whether they were actually operating. That is a body a community can write to asking which centres are currently open, which is a different and better question than whether they exist on paper. THE THREE BARRIERS IT NAMED, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: LANGUAGE BARRIERS, INFORMATION AND AWARENESS GAPS, AND REMOTENESS OF SHELTERS FROM COURTS AND FREE LEGAL AID CENTRES — WITH BUDGET CUTS FOR FREE LEGAL AID ALSO RAISED. Not capacity: LANGUAGE, AWARENESS AND DISTANCE. All three are fixable by the community side — bring your own interpreter, tell people the centre exists, and organise the transport. A coalition that solves those three has doubled the value of a service that already exists. THE NATIONAL ORGANISATION AND WHAT IT PROVIDES: A REGISTERED NON-PROFIT, INDEPENDENT, NON-PARTISAN AND LOCAL HUMAN RIGHTS ORGANISATION, THE OLDEST INDEPENDENT ONE IN THE COUNTRY — PROVIDING FREE LEGAL AID TO HUMAN RIGHTS VICTIMS, MONITORING THE FAIRNESS AND LEGALITY OF TRIAL PROCEEDINGS, AND INVESTIGATING THE CONTENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF NATIONAL LAWS AND POLICIES. WHO FOUNDED IT AND WHEN: ESTABLISHED IN OCTOBER 1991 BY 32 MEMBERS FROM ACADEMIA, BUSINESSES AND PROFESSIONS — MEMBERSHIP-BASED, WITH A MANDATE COVERING MONITORING, INVESTIGATION AND REPORTING, ELECTION OBSERVATION, EDUCATION, ADVOCACY, LEGAL AID AND RESEARCH. Thirty-two people from academia and the professions, exactly as this file's Côte d'Ivoire entry records a francophone association being founded by university researchers. The pattern repeats: where no rights organisation exists, the professions are where one gets built. HOW IT INVESTIGATES, IN ITS OWN PUBLISHED METHOD: FIELD INVESTIGATIONS IN THE RELEVANT REGIONS, GATHERING FROM FAMILIES OF VICTIMS, EYE WITNESSES AND RESIDENTS OF THE PLACES OF VIOLATION AS WELL AS GOVERNMENT AUTHORITIES — METHODS INCLUDING COLLECTING AND ANALYSING DOCUMENTS, ON-SITE COLLECTION OF FIELD DATA USING AUDIO-VISUAL EQUIPMENT FROM PLACES OF VIOLATION, INTERVIEW OF VICTIMS AND WITNESSES, AND GROUP DISCUSSIONS WITH RELEVANT CITIZENS AND BODIES. A published investigation method, which is a document a community can read before deciding what to preserve. Note that it interviews government authorities too — a report that recorded the official account is much harder to dismiss than one that did not. WHERE IT GOES IN PERSON: ITS MONITORING INCLUDES VISITING DETAINEES, INTERNALLY DISPLACED PERSONS AND INDIVIDUALS IN POLICE CUSTODY — WITH TARGETED MONITORING OF PRISONS AND OF THE TRIAL PROCESS. People in police custody, visited. Read beside this file's Burundi entry on counsel in the first hours: an organisation that already enters custody suites is one that can find a detained defender before anyone else can. WHAT IT PUSHES FOR THROUGH ITS REPORTS: JUSTICE AND COMPENSATION FOR VICTIMS, LEGAL ACCOUNTABILITY FOR PERPETRATORS, THE ABOLITION OF THE CULTURE OF IMPUNITY, AND THE ADOPTION OF POLICY AND ENFORCEMENT CHANGES. THE FIRST TIME IT WAS ATTACKED, AND WHAT IT DID: IN 1993 IT FILED A LAWSUIT AGAINST THE GOVERNMENT FOR REFUSING ITS REGISTRATION AS A CITIZENS' ASSOCIATION, THE GOVERNMENT CLAIMING IT WAS A POLITICAL ORGANISATION THAT SIDED WITH THE OPPOSITION AND MADE INACCURATE REPORTS — WHICH IT DISPUTED; ITS FOUNDING HEAD WAS DETAINED THAT YEAR AND LATER RELEASED ON BAIL WITHOUT CHARGE OR TRIAL. It sued over its own registration refusal. Where a community organisation is refused registration — the barrier this file records at nearly every funder — that refusal is itself challengeable, and there is a precedent of an organisation doing it. THE FUNDING LAW THAT NEARLY ENDED IT: ITS FUNDS AND STAFF WERE GREATLY REDUCED IN 2009 BY A LAW LIMITING THE ROLE OF FOREIGN FUNDS IN CITIZENS' ASSOCIATIONS, AND RESTORED BY 2020 UNDER A NEW GOVERNMENT — WITH A VERY NEGLIGIBLE AMOUNT OF ITS BUDGET, UNDER TWO THOUSAND DOLLARS, RAISED LOCALLY FROM MEMBERSHIP FEES. Under two thousand dollars raised from members, against a budget otherwise foreign. That is the vulnerability a foreign-funding law exploits, and it is the argument for the member-funded models recorded elsewhere in this file — the Malawi movement's annual card, the Togo federation's daily savings. THE SUSPENSION, RECORDED WITHOUT SOFTENING: IN DECEMBER 2024 THE NATIONAL REGULATOR SUSPENDED BOTH THIS ORGANISATION AND THE ETHIOPIAN HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS CENTER (EHRDC), CITING DEVIATION FROM THEIR FOUNDING OBJECTIVES BY NOT REMAINING INDEPENDENT — CRITICISED BY THE NATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS COMMISSION, A DEMOCRACY MOVEMENT, AN ANTI-TORTURE ORGANISATION, THE UN SPECIAL RAPPORTEUR ON HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS AND AN INTERNATIONAL RIGHTS ORGANISATION. Filed unsoftened: check current status before relying on it. And note the shape of the attack — not a prosecution but a regulator's suspension on a founding-objectives technicality, which is the cheapest way to close an organisation and the one to expect. AND THE DEFENDERS CENTRE ALONGSIDE IT: A NON-PARTISAN NONPROFIT FOUNDED IN 2019 IN THE CAPITAL TO SUPPORT AND PROTECT HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS FROM ATTACKS — ESTABLISHED AFTER 60 DEFENDERS AND ORGANISATIONS MET AT THE CLAIMING SPACE FORUM ORGANISED BY DEFENDDEFENDERS. Sixty people in one room founded a national defenders network. That is a convening any coalition can attempt, and the regional network that organised it is the one filed under Comoros in this file. WHO IT SUITS: communities in this country needing a free lawyer within reach of a regional town, and organisers looking for a university-clinic model or for what a regulator's suspension looks like before it happens. CAVEATS: ONE COUNTRY; THE UNIVERSITY CENTRES' PRIMARY DOCUMENTED CASELOAD IS REFUGEES, ASYLUM SEEKERS AND DISPLACED PEOPLE RATHER THAN LAND OR PLANNING, AND THEIR OPERATIONAL STATUS AND BUDGETS WERE UNDER REVIEW; THE NATIONAL ORGANISATION WAS SUSPENDED IN DECEMBER 2024, SO ITS CURRENT STANDING MUST BE CHECKED BEFORE APPROACHING IT. For paralegal clinics in other countries, Central African Republic's entry; for the regional defenders network with a published phone line, Comoros' entry.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: COMIFAC Treaty and Plan de Convergence — and its community protocol
trackers.desc: A TREATY BODY WITH A TEMPLATE YOU CAN COPY. The Traité relatif à la conservation et à la gestion durable des écosystèmes forestiers d'Afrique Centrale, signed by heads of state at their second summit on 5 February 2005 in Brazzaville, instituted the Commission des Forêts d'Afrique Centrale — described as the unique instance d'orientation, de décision et de coordination for subregional forest action, and the cadre politique et juridique global for cooperation in the field. A transboundary forest question belongs in that forum. The Plan de Convergence is the reference framework for all such interventions — first edition 2005–2014, revised in 2014 for 2015–2025 and restructured into 10 strategic axes, executed by a Secrétariat exécutif. CIVIL SOCIETY IS A NAMED STAKEHOLDER in implementing it, alongside state administrations, CEEAC and the private sector — so participation is built into the framework, not conceded case by case. Axis 7 covers capacity and participation des acteurs, expressly contemplating micro-projets générateurs de revenus pour les populations locales; axis 9 covers innovative financing mechanisms. THE DOCUMENT LIBRARY IS THE MOST USEFUL PART: COMIFAC publishes a worked Protocole Bioculturel Communautaire for a named village, a guide to inventorying genetic resources and traditional knowledge, a paper on les droits d'usage des peuples autochtones et communautés locales et les obligations qui en découlent, a subregional APA (access and benefit-sharing) strategy, and directives on forests and the SDGs built with FAO as 5 principles and 12 directives across 31 prioritised targets. A community biocultural protocol published by a treaty body is a template, not a theory. AND ITS OWN DIAGNOSIS IS QUOTABLE: the Plan records that participatory natural resource management and mediation of use conflicts, though already mapped out, are insufficiently developed.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: Brainforest — mapped Gabonese communities' forests with them, and documented seventeen communities standing up to logging companies
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Gabonese NGO of more than twenty years, working on forests and the environment with a deliberate double footing — support on the ground and monitoring of policy — and with the protection and promotion of the rights of forest communities and in particular of indigenous peoples as a stated purpose. It works across Haut-Ogooué, Ogooué-Ivindo, Nyanga, la Ngounié, Woleu-Ntem and the Estuaire. WHAT IT PUTS IN A COMMUNITY'S HANDS: participatory mapping of community forest resources, supported by satellite imagery — the same combination that won the Guinean bauxite mediation — plus independent external observation of forests and of non-forest investments, for which it publishes a simplified field guide, and work on getting the contractual obligations in logging concession specifications (cahiers de charges) actually implemented in a named concession. Those specifications are where a company's promises to a village are written down, and Brainforest's work is checking whether they were kept. IT ALSO PUBLISHES THE PRECEDENT ITSELF: its report titled, in translation, impunity is not what it was — seventeen communities stand up to logging companies, which is the document to put in front of a village that thinks nobody has ever won here. It runs analyses of forest conversion by large investments, and a programme on protecting environmental defenders in Gabon. Boulevard Rue Ndoukouet, Ambowé, Libreville; B.P. 23749; +241 011 73 08 86. WHO IT SUITS: forest villages and indigenous communities facing logging concessions, land conversion or non-forest investment. CAVEATS: this is advocacy, mapping and monitoring, not litigation — no legal service or intake route was found, and some published project material is old; a second domain, brainforestgabon.org, also carries its material.

trackers.name: Muyissi Environnement, Mouila — based inside the plantation belt, investigates for villages that cannot pay for a laboratory
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Muyissi Environnement, a Gabonese NGO founded in 2008 with its seat at Mouila in Ngounié province — inside the palm-oil belt rather than in the capital — working with villages that since 2012 have contested land-taking by an industrial oil palm company. WHAT IT DOES THAT NOBODY ELSE THERE WILL: its members carry out investigations in the affected villages, and the reason that matters is stated by a young farmer with skin irritation from the river water: communities have no means to contact laboratories and verify the degree of pollution. Villagers report dead fish in the watercourses, destruction of areas where they gathered fruit and medicinal plants, habitat fragmentation increasing conflict with elephants, and contamination of water sources by plantation agrochemicals. It has toured Ngounié villages to record the impact of the plantations on women specifically, and paired that with income-generating activities and a sale-exhibition of women's products, in villages where hunger had set in. THE ORGANISING ADVICE GIVEN AT ITS WORKSHOPS is worth carrying: communities were urged to invoke the Gabonese code against the company's violations, and to constitute themselves as COOPERATIVES OR ASSOCIATIONS so they speak with one voice — and were brought together with community delegations from Cameroon and Congo-Brazzaville facing the same company model, so that experience crossed borders. THE RISK IS DOCUMENTED: after one such workshop bringing affected communities together, a local NGO director and community leaders were intimidated by local authorities and told to stop organising such events. WHO IT SUITS: Gabonese villages inside or beside industrial plantations, especially in Ngounié, and women's groups losing gathering grounds and clean water. CAVEATS: no verified site of its own was found — this entry points at a land-grab archive record of its village work; it investigates and organises rather than litigating, and the certification label the plantations carry has not prevented the impacts communities report. For participatory mapping and national-level forest work, Gabon's Brainforest entry.

trackers.name: Gabon's environment charter for civil society — the protocol that makes a local association a recognised counterpart, and ACOSAH in Ogooué-Ivindo
trackers.desc: WHAT TO SIGN TO BE RECOGNISED: Gabon operates a CHARTE POUR LA PROTECTION DE L'ENVIRONNEMENT ET LA PRÉSERVATION DE LA NATURE — a protocol of understanding governing relations between the Direction Générale de l'Environnement et de la Protection de la Nature and the civil society organisations working in that field. An organisation signs it at the Directorate General's office, within the Ministry of Water and Forests. WHY A SMALL ASSOCIATION SHOULD CARE, in the words of one signatory's president: the signature “legitimises our actions as a CSO and auxiliary of the public authorities”, and from the Directorate's side the charter is intended to give the sector visibility through regular reporting of CSO activities, making that engagement visible to government and creating institutional synergies for MOBILISING RESOURCES. A signed protocol with the ministry converts a village association from a nuisance into a counterpart, and puts it on the list when money is allocated — ask whether your country has an equivalent instrument, because it is cheap and almost never mentioned. THE SIGNATORY THIS ENTRY RECORDS: ACOSAH (Association des Communicateurs Ogivins pour la Santé et l'Action Humanitaire), which signed on 25 October 2024 and states it has been active since 2019 in the protection of the environment in OGOOUÉ-IVINDO, alongside local communities, and against transnational environmental crime in the Congo Basin forests — which puts a community-facing organisation in Gabon's north-eastern forest province, away from the coastal and Ngounié work already recorded here. WHO IT SUITS: Gabonese local associations wanting formal standing with the environment administration, and communities in Ogooué-Ivindo facing logging, poaching networks or environmental crime. CAVEATS: THE CHARTER IS RECOGNITION, NOT FUNDING OR PROTECTION — it comes with a reporting expectation to the administration, which cuts both ways for an organisation that may later need to criticise that administration; ACOSAH is a communicators' and humanitarian association rather than a legal or land specialist. For participatory mapping, Gabon's Brainforest entry; for the plantation belt, Muyissi Environnement.

trackers.name: Gabon's Fonds de Développement Local — the concessionaire owes your villages 800 FCFA per cubic metre logged, and you can compute what you are owed
trackers.desc: THE MONEY OWED TO YOUR VILLAGE: under Gabon's forest framework, the CAHIER DES CHARGES CONTRACTUELLES is a contract signed between the FOREST CONCESSIONAIRE, the village communities, the local authorities and the forest administration, fixing how benefits from logging are shared and what each side commits to. It establishes a COMITÉ DE GESTION ET DE SUIVI DES PROJETS (CGSP), which must negotiate between villages to draw the map of their finage (customary land envelope), then set how the FONDS DE DÉVELOPPEMENT LOCAL (FDL) is divided, and meets regularly to choose which projects the money funds. THE RATE IS PUBLISHED AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT: the concessionaire feeds the FDL at 800 FCFA PER CUBIC METRE logged during the previous year. Volume times 800 is what your villages are owed — the only funding stream in this entire file a community can calculate for itself rather than apply for. Ask the administration for the declared annual production, do the arithmetic, and compare it with what reached the fund. THE DOCUMENTED ABUSE, RECORDED SO YOU KNOW WHAT TO LOOK FOR: monitoring in the Ngounié province (Douya-Onoye, Ndolou, Tsamba-Magotsi) found companies not respecting their social obligations; the Mokabo village grouping, which signed a cahier des charges in May 2017, denounced the lack of transparency in FDL management; communities did not even know the amount of the FDL; and one company's contract stipulated that the CGSP's OPERATING COSTS would be taken OUT OF the local development fund — 500,000 FCFA in the first year — while the annual production was not known, which the monitors called a clear breach. Watch for running costs being charged against your fund, and for production figures being withheld: without the volume, the rate is unenforceable. Nationally, the committee's own legal basis has been recognised as poorly defined, with reform proposed. WHO IT SUITS: Gabonese village groupings inside or beside a logging concession. CAVEATS: THIS IS A CONTRACTUAL ENTITLEMENT, NOT A GRANT YOU APPLY FOR — it exists only where a concession operates near you; the committee framework is legally weak and the administration under-resourced. For participatory mapping, Gabon's Brainforest entry; for the plantation belt, Muyissi; for formal standing with the environment administration, the charter entry.

trackers.name: RIAG and the Barreau du Gabon — a searchable directory of Gabonese lawyers, and free consultation days documented in Port-Gentil
trackers.desc: WHERE TO FIND A LAWYER: the Réseau International des Avocats Gabonais (RIAG), which runs RIAGCONNECT — a searchable directory for people looking for an advocate — and, with Gabonese diplomatic missions, organises FREE LEGAL CONSULTATIONS (consultations juridiques gratuites) aimed at the Gabonese community, to promote access to justice. A searchable public directory of practising advocates is the first thing to reach for in a country with no legal aid organisation; the second is a free consultation day. AND THE BAR ITSELF RUNS THEM DOMESTICALLY: the BARREAU DU GABON organised free legal consultations in PORT-GENTIL — the oil city, and the closest thing in this file to a scheduled walk-in service for Gabonese outside the capital. Ask the Barreau when the next consultation day is and which town it covers, and ask RIAG for a named advocate in your field — land, mining and environment are practised in Libreville. THE INSTABILITY TO PLAN AROUND, RECORDED BECAUSE IT DETERMINES WHAT YOU WILL FIND WHEN YOU CALL: Gabon's legal sector has passed through open turbulence — a crisis in the ordre des avocats following the ANNULMENT BY THE CONSEIL D'ÉTAT of a bar election, and an unlimited strike by magistrates over their working conditions — alongside a National Assembly-adopted judicial reform. A bar in crisis and striking magistrates mean delays that are institutional rather than personal; build your timetable around that rather than assuming your file has been forgotten. WHO IT SUITS: Gabonese needing to identify and instruct an advocate on a land, forest, plantation or mining matter, in Libreville, Port-Gentil or the provinces. CAVEATS: THIS IS A PROFESSIONAL DIRECTORY AND EPISODIC FREE CONSULTATIONS, NOT A LEGAL AID SCHEME — no Gabonese legal aid organisation could be verified for this file, and private practice in Libreville is oriented to business clients. For participatory mapping that stopped a plantation, Gabon's Brainforest entry; for the Ngounié plantation belt, Muyissi; for the logging fund your villages are owed, the FDL entry.

trackers.name: Gabon's forêts communautaires — the village forms an Entité Juridique de Gestion, cuts its own boundary layons, and signs a convention; 85 definitive conventions and 750,000 ha so far
trackers.desc: HOW A GABONESE VILLAGE GETS A FOREST: under articles 156-162 of loi n°016/01 of 31 December 2001 (code forestier) a forêt communautaire is a portion of the RURAL forest domain affected to a village community for sustainable natural-resource management on the basis of a CONVENTION DE GESTION between the water and forests administration and a village community ORGANISED AS AN ENTITÉ JURIDIQUE DE GESTION (EJG) — in practice a village association. Article 157 lets the request come from A VILLAGE, A GROUPING OF VILLAGES OR A CANTON, and the process is expressly volontariste — it happens only on the community's own demand. THE STEPS, IN ORDER: the village creates the legal entity, files the creation request with the LOCAL FOREST AUTHORITIES, holds information meetings INCLUDING PARTICIPATORY MAPPING of the territory concerned — with the WHOLE population, expressly INCLUDING WOMEN, YOUNG PEOPLE AND MINORITY ETHNIC GROUPS, required to understand the process — then a CONVENTION PROVISOIRE is signed, a PLAN SIMPLE DE GESTION prepared, and the definitive convention follows. TWO RULES WORTH KNOWING BEFORE ANYONE TELLS YOU OTHERWISE: (1) the 2022 arrêté states that the AREA OF A FC VARIES ACCORDING TO THE SIZE OF THE VILLAGE ASSOCIATION AND THE FOREST AVAILABLE — while sector guidance records a 5,000 ha working limit, the arrêté itself sets no fixed national ceiling; and (2) CREATION CANNOT BE THE ACT OF AN INDIVIDUAL, A FAMILY OR A CLAN. That second rule is protection, not obstruction — it is what stops one powerful family converting the village forest into a private holding, the exact failure recorded in Cameroon. AND THE BOUNDARY IS YOURS TO CUT: delimitation of the FC perimeter is carried out BY THE VILLAGE COMMUNITIES THEMSELVES, with support from the administration or a competent provider, by OPENING AND MAINTAINING TWO-METRE LAYONS around the whole perimeter WITH THE BOUNDARY TREES MARKED IN PAINT. A physically cut and painted boundary is worth more than a line on a map when a concession arrives — and it is work your own people can do. SCALE: launched 2013 in Ogooué-Ivindo, interrupted for TEN YEARS and relaunched in 2022; the country now counts 85 forests under definitive convention, 39 provisional and 45 reservation decisions — over 750,000 HECTARES. WHO IT SUITS: Gabonese villages, village groupings and cantons in the rural forest domain. CAVEATS: A MANAGEMENT CONVENTION WITH THE STATE, NOT OWNERSHIP, requiring a simple management plan and supply contracts to exploit; the ten-year interruption shows the queue can stop entirely. For participatory mapping to prepare the file, Gabon's Brainforest entry; for the logging fund your villages are owed, the FDL entry; for finding an advocate, RIAG.

trackers.name: Conservation Justice — has followed 271 community contracts since 2014, supports about a hundred villages a year, and has a legal department that takes community claims to the national courts
trackers.desc: THE ORGANISATION WITH A LEGAL DEPARTMENT AND 271 CONTRACTS: CONSERVATION JUSTICE, CREATED 2010 and working in Gabon on strengthening the application of wildlife and forest law and on informing and raising awareness of local communities across the country, also WORKS TO STRENGTHEN LOCAL COMMUNITIES BY FOLLOWING QUESTIONS SUCH AS THE CAHIERS DE CHARGES CONTRACTUELLES AND THE ESTABLISHMENT OF COMMUNITY FORESTS. THE NUMBERS: ABOUT A HUNDRED VILLAGES ARE SUPPORTED EACH YEAR, AND SINCE 2014 THE ORGANISATION HAS FOLLOWED 271 CAHIERS DE CHARGES CONTRACTUELLES on behalf of local communities. Two hundred and seventy-one contracts followed is institutional memory of what these agreements actually deliver. Before you sign one, ask what the last ten in your province produced. AND ITS LEGAL DEPARTMENT HEAD SAYS THE PART THAT MATTERS, BY NAME: WHEN POPULATIONS COMPLAIN, FEELING SOMETIMES CHEATED BY CERTAIN ECONOMIC OPERATORS, WE ARE CONTACTED TO ACCOMPANY THEM IN THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE DIFFERENT CONTRACTS THEY HAVE WITH THE OPERATORS, AND WE DO OUR BEST TO ASSERT THEIR RIGHTS BEFORE THE AUTHORITIES — AND WE SOMETIMES HELP THEM CARRY THOSE RIGHTS BEFORE THE NATIONAL JURISDICTIONS. A named chef du département juridique who will take a village's contract dispute into court is the closest thing to a community lawyer in this file's Gabonese record. Contact the legal department, not the general address. ITS OTHER WORK: with the provincial water and forests directorate it ran social forestry workshops at LAMBARÉNÉ AND NDJOLÉ in the MOYEN-OGOOUÉ on the contractual charge books and community forests; it has sensitised 1,856 community members and 9,347 pupils in the LASTOURSVILLE-OKONDJA-FRANCEVILLE zone around forest concessions, and over 7,350 pupils in the MVOUNG, MULUNDU AND LOPÉ departments; and with a partner organisation operating FOUR PROVINCIAL BASES it works on MOBILE ELECTRIC FENCES for human-wildlife conflict, with its executive director stating that one cannot work durably without the participation of local communities. THE STATE'S OWN ADMISSION, WORTH QUOTING BACK: although mechanisms exist to let communities lead their own development through the CCC and community forests, THE UNDERSTANDING AND MANAGEMENT OF THESE TOOLS STILL POSES A PROBLEM IN GABON, AND THE BENEFITS ARE LITTLE VISIBLE IN THE VILLAGES. If your village has a CCC and sees nothing from it, that is a documented national pattern, not your failure — and there is an organisation that has followed 271 of them. ALSO NAMED: CROISSANCE SAINE ENVIRONNEMENT (CSE), whose purpose is promoting sustainable development and good governance through awareness and advocacy, and which intervened publicly over the JUNE 2025 DEMOLITIONS in greater LIBREVILLE, deploring the absence of a judicial resolution and noting residents awaiting court decisions on persons of good faith who received no compensation for the loss of their property. WHO IT SUITS: Gabonese villages with a contractual charge book or a community forest, and Libreville residents facing demolition. CAVEATS: A FOREIGN-REGISTERED NGO working as a ministry partner — its enforcement work is with the state. For community forest mapping and the two-metre layons, Gabon's Brainforest entry; for work inside the plantation zone, Muyissi Environnement; for the searchable advocates' directory, RIAG and the Barreau du Gabon entry.

trackers.name: Named Gabonese environmental associations with contacts — Gabon Ecologie's 497 members and four phone lines, Gabon Environnement's eco-guide school, PROGRAM at Moukalaba-Doudou, and two association directories
trackers.desc: FOUR PHONE NUMBERS AND FOUR HUNDRED AND NINETY-SEVEN MEMBERS: GABON ECOLOGIE PUBLISHES ITS MEMBERSHIP COUNT — 497 ADHÉRENTS — ALONGSIDE A POSTAL ADDRESS AT BATAVEA 2933, LIBREVILLE, FOUR TELEPHONE NUMBERS AND AN EMAIL, under the slogan UN ENVIRONNEMENT PROPRE ET SAIN. ITS ORGANS ARE PUBLISHED TOO: AN ASSEMBLÉE GÉNÉRALE, A CONSEIL D'ADMINISTRATION, A DIRECTION EXÉCUTIVE, AND COMMISSIONS SCIENTIFIQUES ET TECHNIQUES. Four hundred and ninety-seven members with a general assembly above the executive is a body that can be held to account by its own membership — and a scientific and technical commission inside an association is where a community gets an opinion written for it without paying a consultant. Ask what the commission can be asked to look at. AND ITS STATED METHOD IS THE LINE TO NOTE: TO INTEGRATE THE LEGAL WEAPON FOR THE DEFENCE OF THE ENVIRONMENT ALONGSIDE THE TRADITIONAL METHODS OF COMBAT FOR THE DEFENCE OF THE PLANET, WHICH ARE CONSCIENTISATION AND SENSITISATION — and it supports a PLATEFORME NATIONALE D'APPUI AU DÉVELOPPEMENT DURABLE DU GABON (PNADD), a platform of concertation, coordination, communication and action. An awareness organisation that says out loud it intends to add law to its methods is one to ask about litigation before assuming you need a firm. THE FIELD ORGANISATION: ONG GABON ENVIRONNEMENT (gabon-environnement.org) HAS WORKED SINCE 2004 AND RUN MORE THAN FIFTEEN YEARS OF CONCRETE FIELD PROJECTS IN CLOSE COLLABORATION WITH LOCAL COMMUNITIES AND WITH THE NATIONAL PARKS AGENCY AND THE NATIONAL BIODIVERSITY FUND — covering MARINE TURTLE MONITORING AND BIODIVERSITY INVENTORIES, from the leatherback turtles of one named site to the forests of another, and running AN ÉCOLE DES ÉCO-GUIDES AND LOCAL CAPACITY BUILDING. A school for eco-guides is a training pipeline into exactly the paid roles the region's conservation laws create. If your young people want the guide and tracker jobs rather than watching outsiders take them, that is where the qualification comes from. MORE NAMED BODIES: LES AMIS DU PANGOLIN, A NON-PROFIT ASSOCIATION OF GABONESE LAW working on communication and environmental education to contribute to the preservation of the environment and the conservation of natural resources FOR THE WELL-BEING OF POPULATIONS CONSIDERED IN ITS TRIPLE ECOLOGICAL, ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL DIMENSION; the RÉSEAU GABONAIS POUR L'ENVIRONNEMENT ET LE DÉVELOPPEMENT DURABLE (RGEDD), CREATED IN 2018 BY YOUNG GABONESE GRADUATES IN PROJECT ANALYSIS AND SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT; and PROGRAM, A GABONESE ASSOCIATION CREATED IN 2004 AND OFFICIALLY RECOGNISED IN 2007, WORKING ON THE PROTECTION OF GREAT APES AND OF BIODIVERSITY AS A WHOLE AND ON THE POVERTY OF LOCAL POPULATIONS IN THE MOUKALABA-DOUDOU NATIONAL PARK. An association whose stated object joins great ape protection to LOCAL POVERTY in one named park is the shape to look for: if the organisation working your park does not name the people in its object, ask why not. AND TWO DIRECTORIES TO FIND THE REST: ASSO-GABON DESCRIBES ITSELF AS THE PLATEFORME DES ASSOCIATIONS DU GABON AND RUNS AN ANNUAIRE OF ASSOCIATIONS ARRANGED BY THEME AND BY PROVINCE AND ARRONDISSEMENT; and a separate business directory lists Gabonese associations, foundations and NGOs WITH THEIR LIBREVILLE NEIGHBOURHOOD GIVEN FOR EACH — including a central African protected areas network based at Bas de Gué-Gué. A directory that gives the NEIGHBOURHOOD rather than a postcode is what you need in a city where addresses are described by quarter. Two directories, one thematic and one geographic — use both. AND THE MONEY NOW ARRIVING: A PROJECT FINANCE FOR PERMANENCE NAMED GABON INFINI WAS OFFICIALLY LAUNCHED TO MOBILISE UP TO 200 MILLION DOLLARS OVER TEN YEARS FOR CONSERVATION AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF LOCAL COMMUNITIES, SUPPORTING A PLAN DE DÉVELOPPEMENT COMMUNAUTAIRE ET DE CONSERVATION, tied to a commitment to protect 30% of terrestrial, freshwater and marine ecosystems by 2030. Community development is written into the name of the plan, not appended to it. Ask who is drafting that plan and how a village gets its needs into it — a ten-year fund is being allocated now, and the allocation is the moment. WHO IT SUITS: Gabonese communities near a park, young people seeking guide training, and anyone looking for the association nearest them. CAVEATS: MEMBERSHIP AND PROJECT ASSOCIATIONS — confirm current contacts. For mapping communities' forests with them, Gabon's Brainforest entry; for work inside the plantation belt, Muyissi Environnement; for 271 community contracts and a legal department head who goes to court, Conservation Justice; for the Entité Juridique de Gestion, the forêts communautaires entry; for a searchable lawyer directory, RIAG and the Barreau du Gabon.

trackers.name: Habitat for Humanity — an operational housing organisation whose Africa work includes secure land tenure and housing microfinance — with savings groups that train women to obtain land occupancy licences giving them ownership of the ground their home stands on
trackers.desc: SAVINGS GROUPS THAT END IN A LICENCE OVER THE GROUND YOU LIVE ON — disambiguation and adjacency declared first: THIS IS NOT THE 450-MEMBER HABITAT COALITION FILED UNDER GUINEA-BISSAU, WHICH IS A MEMBERSHIP NETWORK ON FORCED EVICTION; THIS IS A SEPARATE OPERATIONAL HOUSING ORGANISATION. DO NOT CONFUSE THEM. THIS FILE'S GHANA AND UGANDA BUCKETS CARRY A SHACK DWELLERS HOST AND ITS NAMIBIA BUCKET THE NAME; ITS MALAWI ENTRY THE SOCIO-ECONOMIC RIGHTS INSTITUTE. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS RUN ON THE HOST ACTUALLY BEING SHIPPED. THE LICENCE ROUTE, WHICH IS THE FIND: IN A NAMED ZAMBIAN SETTLEMENT, WOMEN ARE TRAINED AND SUPPORTED THROUGH SAVINGS GROUPS WHICH TEACH THEM HOW TO MANAGE THEIR FINANCES, HOW TO SAVE AND INVEST, AND HOW TO OBTAIN LAND OCCUPANCY LICENCES THAT WILL GIVE THEM OWNERSHIP OF THEIR OWN HOME AND THE LAND IT IS BUILT ON. The standing brief asks how ordinary people get title to the ground they are on. This is the household-scale answer, and it is unglamorous: a savings group, a training course, and an occupancy licence at the end of it. No purchase fund, no international litigation — the same instrument the district office issues anyway, obtained by people who were never told how. A settlement whose residents hold licences is far harder to clear than one whose residents hold nothing. WHAT THE SAVINGS GROUP DOES BESIDES SAVE: TRAINING IN ENTREPRENEURSHIP AND BUSINESS SKILLS SO THAT MEMBERS BECOME INNOVATIVE, SELF-RELIANT, AND NOT DEPENDENT ON ANY CHARITY OR GOVERNMENT — ADVANCING LAND RIGHTS, SECURITY OF TENURE AND SOCIO-ECONOMIC CHANGE. NOT DEPENDENT ON ANY CHARITY OR GOVERNMENT is the design goal, stated by the charity itself. Read it beside the collapse recorded in this file's South Sudan entry, where a community project failed the year its donor left. WHAT IT HELPS FAMILIES GET IN AFRICA, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: ACCESS TO DECENT AND AFFORDABLE HOUSING, HOUSING MICROFINANCE SERVICES, CLEAN WATER AND SAFE SANITATION, AND SECURE LAND TENURE — IN RURAL AREAS AS WELL AS CITIES. SECURE LAND TENURE listed as a service alongside water and sanitation, and rural areas named explicitly. Most housing organisations stop at the city edge. THE CREDIT BARRIER IT WORKS ON: BY FACILITATING ACCESS TO CREDIT IN A NAMED COUNTRY IT IS HELPING ADDRESS HISTORICAL BARRIERS TO HOUSING FINANCE FOR LOW-INCOME HOUSEHOLDS AND MARGINALIZED GROUPS. WHAT ITS FINANCE CENTRE ACTUALLY DOES FOR LENDERS: PROVIDING INSTITUTIONAL TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS TO DEVELOP OR REFINE HOUSING MICROFINANCE PRODUCTS — THROUGH MARKET MAPPINGS, MARKET RESEARCH, PRODUCT DESIGN, PILOT PLANNING AND SUPPORT TO TAKE THOSE PRODUCTS TO SCALE. It works on the lenders, not only the borrowers. A community whose local bank will not lend against untitled land is describing a product design problem this organisation exists to solve — and the bank, not the community, is the party it approaches. THE RESEARCH IT PUBLISHES THAT BEARS DIRECTLY ON TENURE: WORK ON UNDERSTANDING THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN HOUSING MICROFINANCE AND LAND TENURE IN A NAMED COUNTRY, ALONGSIDE MATERIAL ON ARTISAN TRAINING AND ON MAINTAINING A HEALTHY LOAN PORTFOLIO. THE CAMPAIGN AND WHAT IT ASKS FOR: POLICIES THAT PRIORITIZE LAND AND HOUSING RIGHTS FOR HISTORICALLY MARGINALIZED COMMUNITIES, PROMOTE INCLUSIVE URBAN DEVELOPMENT THAT PREVENTS FORCED EVICTIONS AND DISPLACEMENT, AND ENCOURAGE INVESTMENT IN AFFORDABLE HOUSING. PREVENTS FORCED EVICTIONS AND DISPLACEMENT written into a mainstream housing charity's policy asks. That is a large, well-funded organisation available to say the same thing your community is saying, in rooms it cannot enter. WHAT IT URGES THE CONTINENTAL BODY TO DO: SECURE LAND AND HOUSING RIGHTS FOR MARGINALIZED COMMUNITIES THROUGH INCLUSIVE POLICY FRAMEWORKS; INTEGRATE SUSTAINABLE HOUSING INTO URBAN PLANNING TO PROTECT VULNERABLE POPULATIONS; AND MOBILIZE PUBLIC AND PRIVATE FINANCING. THE NUMBERS IT PUBLISHES ABOUT THE CONTINENT: ABOUT 238 MILLION PEOPLE LIVE IN INFORMAL SETTLEMENTS; THE AFFORDABILITY GAP IS LARGER THAN ANY OTHER CONTINENT; AND LAND TENURE SECURITY AND GOVERNANCE CHALLENGES CONTINUE TO LIMIT EQUITABLE ACCESS TO HOUSING. 238 million people without secure tenure where they live. That is the scale figure to put in a submission arguing that a community's insecurity is a national condition rather than a local failure. THE COUNTRIES ITS LAND RIGHTS CAMPAIGN RUNS IN: NATIONAL ORGANISATIONS INCLUDING CÔTE D'IVOIRE, LESOTHO, KENYA, SOUTH AFRICA AND ZAMBIA IN AFRICA, ALONGSIDE MANY OUTSIDE IT. Five named African countries with a national organisation on the ground. Approach the national office rather than the international one. THE WOMEN'S LAND PLATFORMS IT WORKS THROUGH: A NAMED WOMEN'S LAND LINK AFRICA ADVOCACY PLATFORM FOR GRASSROOTS WOMEN'S LAND RIGHTS, AND A NAMED STAND FOR HER LAND CAMPAIGN — WITH EVENTS BRINGING GRASSROOTS WOMEN LEADERS AND CIVIL SOCIETY PRACTITIONERS TOGETHER TO SHARE HOW SECURE LAND TENURE TRANSFORMS LIVES. Two further platforms to trace by name. This file has recorded women excluded from community land negotiation as the standard outcome; a continental platform built specifically for grassroots women's land rights is the counter-structure. AND ITS REACH AND ONE MEASURED FIGURE: BEGUN IN 1976 AS A GRASSROOTS EFFORT ON A COMMUNITY FARM AND NOW WORKING IN MORE THAN 70 COUNTRIES, WITH A REGIONAL HOUSING FORUM CONVENED FOR THE CONTINENT — AND IN ONE COUNTRY OVER 6,000 CITIZENS ENGAGED IN BUILDING AND ADVOCATING FOR DECENT SHELTER. WHO IT SUITS: African settlements and rural households without title to the ground they occupy — particularly women's groups — and communities whose banks will not lend against untitled land. CAVEATS: A HOUSING AND FINANCE ORGANISATION, NOT A LAND-PURCHASE FUND, A LAW FIRM OR A CAMPAIGN AGAINST A SPECIFIC PROJECT; ITS WORK RUNS THROUGH NATIONAL OFFICES IN A LIMITED SET OF COUNTRIES, AND MICROFINANCE IS DEBT — WEIGH THE TERMS. For the coalition on forced eviction, Guinea-Bissau's entry; for the servitude registered against a title deed, São Tomé's entry.

trackers.name: REDHAC (Réseau des Défenseurs des Droits Humains en Afrique Centrale), Douala — eight country focal points across Central Africa; with Toges Noires, Kinshasa, practising since 1988, and the SAJ legal clinic at the University of Goma
trackers.desc: EIGHT COUNTRY FOCAL POINTS, AND A CLINIC RUN OUT OF A LAW FACULTY — method and adjacency declared first: TWELFTH NAMED-ATTORNEY ROUND, AIMED AT FRANCOPHONE CENTRAL AFRICA, THE REGION THIS FILE HAS REPEATEDLY MEASURED AS THINNEST FOR LEGAL HELP. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THREE HOSTS AND SIX DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; BOTH SUBJECT HOSTS, BOTH ORGANISATION NAMES AND TWO FACTS ABSENT, WITH ONE REFERENCE HOST UNDER THE REPUBLIC OF CONGO AND TWO GENERIC TERMS IN FIVE OTHER BUCKETS. THIS FILE'S COMOROS ENTRY COVERS AN EAST AFRICAN DEFENDERS NETWORK AND ITS REPUBLIC OF CONGO ENTRY THE 24/7 HELPLINE. NONE IS THIS NETWORK, NONE IS RESTATED. THE EIGHT COUNTRY FOCAL POINTS, WHICH IS THE FIND: THE NETWORK CONSISTS OF THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY, THE BOARD OF ADMINISTRATION, THE EIGHT FOCAL POINTS IN THE DIFFERENT COUNTRIES WHICH DRIVE THE NETWORK, AND THE PERMANENT SECRETARIAT WHOSE SEAT IS IN DOUALA, CAMEROON. A focal point in each country, and the focal points DRIVE the network rather than report to it. This file's Comoros and Djibouti entries record the equivalent structures for East and West Africa; this is the Central African one, and it closes the last regional gap in defender protection coverage. A defender in Gabon, Cameroon, Chad, the Congos or Equatorial Guinea has a national contact rather than a foreign office. WHAT IT EXISTS TO DO, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: TO ENSURE THE RECOGNITION OF THE STATUS AND PROTECTION OF HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS — STRENGTHENING THE CAPACITIES OF DEFENDERS FOR THEIR SAFETY AND PROTECTION IN THEIR WORK, CONDUCTING EFFECTIVE ADVOCACY ON THEIR BEHALF, INVESTIGATING AND ANALYSING THEIR SITUATION, AND FINDING NECESSARY RESOURCES FOR ITS ACTIVITIES. RECOGNITION OF THE STATUS of defenders is the first aim, and it is the one that matters legally: where a country has no defender protection law, a land activist is simply a private person with no special standing. Establishing the category is what makes everything else claimable. WHO HAS LED IT AND SINCE WHEN: MAXIMILIENNE NGO MBE HAS LED THE NETWORK SINCE 2010. THE NATIONAL NGO THAT PRACTISES IN THE COURTS: A NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATION UNDER CONGOLESE LAW BASED IN THE CAPITAL, HANDLING THE DEFENCE AND PROMOTION OF HUMAN RIGHTS IN SEVERAL PROVINCES SINCE 1988. Practising since 1988, through everything that has happened in that country since. Longevity is a real credential where organisations are routinely closed — this file has now recorded two regulator suspensions of newer bodies within thirteen months. THE DEMAND IT MADE OF THE PROSECUTOR, WHICH IS THE THIRD FIND: IT ASKED THE PROSECUTOR GENERAL OF THE REPUBLIC TO OPEN JUDICIAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST MEMBERS OF THE PREVIOUS GOVERNMENT WHO HAD NOT DECLARED THEIR ASSETS AT THE BEGINNING AND AT THE END OF THEIR MANDATE. ASSET DECLARATIONS, and the failure to file them, used as the hook. Most countries require ministers to declare assets on entering and leaving office, almost nobody checks, and non-declaration is an offence that needs no proof of corruption — only proof of the missing form. Where a minister has signed off a concession, that is a checkable public record. THE FREE CLINIC IN THE EAST AND WHO IT SERVES: A LEGAL CLINIC NAMED AS A SYNERGY FOR JUDICIAL ASSISTANCE TO VICTIMS OF HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS, OPERATING IN NORTH KIVU AND ATTACHED TO THE UNIVERSITY OF GOMA THAT PLACES LAW STUDENTS WITH IT FOR PRACTICAL TRAINING. A law faculty in a conflict-affected eastern province running a clinic and staffing it with its own students. Read beside this file's Djibouti entry on eight named university legal aid centres: the regional university is the most reliable free-legal institution in places where NGOs are closed and advocates will not travel. THE BODIES IT WORKS AMONG, FROM ITS OWN ABBREVIATION LIST: A UNITED NATIONS HUMAN RIGHTS OFFICE, A HIGH COMMISSIONER FOR HUMAN RIGHTS, A NORWEGIAN REFUGEE COUNCIL, A SPECIAL POLICE FOR CHILD PROTECTION AND A UNITED NATIONS CHILDREN'S FUND — ITS CASELOAD RECORDED AS CONCERNING SEXUAL VIOLENCE AND THE FLOUTING OF HUMAN RIGHTS. A SPECIAL POLICE FOR CHILD PROTECTION exists as a separate force. Where a settlement is cleared with children in it, that is a distinct body to report to, and most communities do not know it exists. WHAT THE STATE ITSELF ASKED THE NGOs TO DO: A DEPUTY MINISTER OF JUSTICE ENCOURAGED NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS NGOs TO DENOUNCE ALL ABUSES SO THAT THE AUTHORS ANSWER FOR THEIR ACTS BEFORE THE JUDICIAL INSTANCES — ASKING THEM TO HELP VICTIMS GET THE EVIDENCE TO THE COURTS BEFORE WHICH ACTIONS ARE OPEN, AND NOT TO NEGLECT DENUNCIATION. A minister publicly inviting NGOs to bring evidence to court. That invitation is quotable: an organisation later obstructed can point to the government's own request that it do exactly this. THE HISTORICAL ARGUMENT HE USED FOR IT: THAT BETWEEN 1885 AND 1908 THE ATROCITIES THAT CAUSED 13,000 DEATHS WERE ENDED THANKS TO DENUNCIATION. THE WOMEN'S LAW PRACTICE ORGANISING PUBLICLY: WOMEN ADVOCATES OF CABINET NGUANGU, KINSHASA, SPEAKING OUT AT A CONFERENCE-DEBATE AGAINST THE INJUSTICES WOMEN SUFFER, RAISING AWARENESS TO BREAK THE SILENCE, AND RECALLING THE RESPONSIBILITY OF THE STATE IN THE FIGHT AGAINST DEGRADING CUSTOMARY PRACTICES — ME MIRIAM MATA STRESSING THAT WOMEN VICTIMS FACE SEVERAL OBSTACLES WHEN THEY SEEK TO MAKE THEIR VOICES HEARD. A private chambers organising publicly rather than waiting for instructions. Where no NGO exists, a firm of women advocates convening a public meeting is itself the resource — and it is a door a community can knock on. THE CRITICISM PUBLISHED AGAINST THE SECTOR, RECORDED WITHOUT SOFTENING: THAT WHILE THE FUNDERS OF THESE ORGANISATIONS OPERATE IN COUNTRIES WHERE THE RULE OF LAW IS STRICTLY APPLIED, THEIR CRITICISMS OF THE NATIONAL JUDICIAL SYSTEM APPEAR TO MANY CITIZENS DISCONNECTED FROM LOCAL REALITIES, FEEDING A GROWING MISTRUST OF THESE NGOs AS ENTITIES DISTANT FROM THE DAILY SUFFERING OF THE POPULATION — AND THAT VICTIMS' RIGHTS ARE OFTEN LEFT OUT OF THE DOMINANT HUMAN RIGHTS DISCOURSE. Filed because a community should know how its allies are perceived locally before appearing beside them. Foreign-funded rights organisations carry a legitimacy cost in some places, and a campaign that leads with them rather than with residents can inherit it. AND WHAT THAT CRITICISM ASKS FOR: A CONSTRUCTIVE DIALOGUE BETWEEN DEFENDERS AND THE AUTHORITIES, AND A REVISION OF ADVOCACY STRATEGIES TO AVOID IDEOLOGICAL EXCESSES — SO THAT THE DEFENCE OF HUMAN RIGHTS DOES NOT BECOME A TOOL OF DIVISION BUT A MOTOR OF RECONCILIATION AND TRUE JUSTICE. WHO IT SUITS: land and environmental defenders in francophone Central Africa who need a national focal point rather than a foreign office, and communities in the eastern provinces who can reach a university law clinic. CAVEATS: THE NETWORK IS A PROTECTION AND ADVOCACY BODY RATHER THAN COUNSEL, AND THE NATIONAL ORGANISATIONS NAMED HAVE CIVIL AND POLITICAL RIGHTS FRAMES RATHER THAN LAND OR PLANNING; SOME MATERIAL CITED IS OLDER AND THE CLINIC'S DOCUMENTED CASELOAD IS SEXUAL VIOLENCE, SO CHECK CURRENT SCOPE AND CONTACTS. For the East African defenders network with a published phone line, Comoros' entry; for the 24/7 helpline and evacuation grants, the Republic of Congo's entry.

trackers.name: Les Mêmes Droits Pour Tous (MDT)
trackers.desc: Guinea’s leading prisoner legal-aid organisation (“Same Rights For All”), founded in 2005 and specialising in criminal justice. Under a standing agreement with the Ministry of Justice it has unrestricted access to all of Guinea’s prisons — where the great majority of detainees are held in prolonged pretrial detention — and provides free legal and judicial assistance to people deprived of liberty, having won the release of hundreds who were illegally or unlawfully detained. It documents prison conditions, assists victims of torture and gender-based violence and communities affected by mining projects, and works from its Conakry headquarters and regional offices in N’Zérékoré and Kankan; it holds ECOSOC observer status.

trackers.name: Natural Justice: Lawyers for Communities and the Environment
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an African public-interest law organisation — lawyers and paralegals working with communities facing mining, oil and gas, logging and large infrastructure, combining legal empowerment, community protocols, policy work and litigation. Hubs in Cape Town, Nairobi and Dakar, staff in Madagascar, Botswana and Guinea, and country programmes in Burkina Faso, Guinea, Kenya, Madagascar, Namibia, Nigeria, Senegal and South Africa. It also runs the Environmental Lawyers Collective for Africa and an EIA Process Tracker. WHO IT SUITS: an Indigenous or rural community whose land, water or customary rights are threatened by an extractive or infrastructure project. It takes selected cases and works project-to-project outside its programme countries, so expect an approach-and-assess conversation rather than open intake. IS THERE AN OFFICE NEAR YOU? STAFF, NOT A HUB — Guinea. The 3 hubs are Cape Town, Nairobi and Dakar; here there are additional staff, so expect a smaller presence and a longer route into casework. WHAT IT DOES: founded 2007 in Cape Town, it supports communities to know the law, use the law and shape the law — access to land and governance of natural resources, the struggle against harmful extractive and infrastructure developments, traditional knowledge and benefit sharing, community rights within conservation, and climate action. ITS SIGNATURE TOOL IS THE COMMUNITY PROTOCOL — a documented instrument letting a community set out its biological, cultural and spiritual resources, norms and values, and assert existing rights under customary, domestic and international law, aimed squarely at laws and projects developed by government and industry without consultation. Ask for it by name. Contact: 63 Hout Street, Cape Town 8001; +27 21 426 1633; info@naturaljustice.org.

trackers.name: African Environmental Defenders Fund (emergency grants)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the African Environmental Defenders Fund — an emergency grant fund run by Natural Justice with the International Land Coalition Africa, ICCA Consortium, PACJA, Oxfam Novib, FEMNET and others, giving up to US$5,000 to land and environmental defenders anywhere in Africa who are under threat because of their activism. It can cover the cost of legal representation where a defender is arrested, summoned or prosecuted, plus relocation and other short-term transitional costs. WHO IT SUITS: an individual frontline defender who is a citizen or legal resident of an African country, facing an imminent threat, and not already supported by another body — it is not project or core funding, and routine office and administrative costs are excluded. HOW IT DIFFERS: applications are rolling, by email or helpline, not to a grant round. Natural Justice's own site names Burkina Faso, Guinea, Kenya, Madagascar, Namibia, Nigeria, Senegal, South Africa and Botswana as its country programmes, which is where this entry is placed; the fund's stated eligibility is any African country, so apply from elsewhere on the continent too.

trackers.name: Cour des comptes
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Guinea, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Guinea — Ministère du Budget
trackers.desc: National budget authority; optimises budget policy, prepares the finance law (loi de finances), and oversees fiscal & customs administration, Republic of Guinea. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Guinea.

trackers.name: Guinea — APIP-Guinée (Guichet Unique de Création d’Entreprise)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the APIP one-stop window handles company creation, online name reservation & RCCM formalities and promotes private investment, Republic of Guinea. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Association Guinéenne pour la Transparence (AGT)
trackers.desc: Transparency International's national contact in Guinea (since 2000). Anti-corruption advocacy that monitors public procurement and asset declarations and pushes UNCAC implementation. Its primary online presence is its Facebook page.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: Commission de classement — ask at the prefecture, and use the right words
trackers.desc: DO NOT ASK FOR A ‘FORÊT COMMUNAUTAIRE’ IN GUINEA. IUCN's review records that the forest code does not speak of community forests — but it does provide for classing the forest domain to the benefit of local collectivities. Ask for classement au bénéfice de la collectivité; the wrong term gets a request refused as unknown to the law. WHO CAN HOLD ONE: the Code names a commune urbaine, a Communauté Rurale de Développement, a district, A VILLAGE, or a groupement forestier — a village is named in its own right, so it need not federate first. NOTE THE INSTRUMENT: the State's forest domain is classed by décret; a collectivity's by arrêté — the lower and faster instrument. Land not yet subject to either is simply non-classé, so classement is the act that changes its status. WHERE IT IS DECIDED: a Commission de classement des forêts is instituted in each prefecture — this is decided locally, not in Conakry, so direct the request there and ask who sits on it. A DOCUMENT YOU CAN REQUEST: for each Plan Forestier Préfectoral the Préfet must produce an annual report on execution, submitted to the Ministry. Article 1: Guinean forests are a good of national interest. Codes in force: forest 1999, environment 1989, wildlife 1998.

trackers.name: The 1959 Dalaba status — sacred woods and spring heads, named
