THE CARD FOR GRANTMAKERS is the one to send upward: it tells your funder what it should do when you are attacked, which is a conversation few grantees can start from nothing. WHO IT SUITS: African community groups, collectives and organisations facing threats — including unregistered ones, and including those who need the wellbeing side rather than the security side. CAVEATS: GLOBAL SOUTH GROUPS THAT CANNOT OTHERWISE FUND THE SUPPORT, DEMAND IS RISING, AND DIGITAL SECURITY IS NOT DELIVERED IN FRENCH OR ARABIC — pair it accordingly. For the two-hour digital helpline in French and Arabic, Libya's entry; for grants that buy the equipment, Equatorial Guinea's entry; for the 24-hour defender helpline, Benin's entry.

trackers.name: The Transnational Institute (TNI) — free primers and reports on land and water grabbing written with agrarian movements — including North African extractivism, a pan-African water justice network, and the question of what to do about deals that break no law at all
trackers.desc: THE HARD CASE IS THE DEAL THAT BREAKS NO LAW — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S EGYPT ENTRY COVERS THE PEASANT MOVEMENT; ITS ALGERIA ENTRY THE MOVEMENT FUNDER; ITS ERITREA ENTRY THE FOREST NETWORK WITH AFRICAN-LANGUAGE BOOKLETS; ITS BURKINA FASO AND MADAGASCAR ENTRIES A FOOD RIGHTS ORGANISATION; ITS DJIBOUTI BUCKET CARRIES A SEEDS AND LAND RESEARCH HOST. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. THE DISTINCTION THAT DECIDES MOST AFRICAN CASES, WHICH IS THE FIND: ACQUISITIONS WHERE FORMAL STATE LAWS ARE SKIRTED ARE CLEARLY GRABS — BUT THEN WHAT ABOUT CASES WHERE THE DEALS DO NOT BREAK FORMAL RULES AND LAWS? THIS IS THE CASE IN MANY AFRICAN COUNTRIES. Most of this file's legal entries assume an illegality to expose. The harder and commoner situation is the concession granted entirely lawfully, because the law already vests the land in the state and treats customary occupation as absence. A community whose lawyer reports that everything was done correctly has not lost the argument — it has discovered that the argument is about the law itself, and this is where that case is set out. THE NORTH AFRICA REPORT: EXTRACTIVISM AND RESISTANCE IN NORTH AFRICA, EXAMINING THE COMMODIFICATION OF NATURE AND PRIVATISATION OF RESOURCES ASSOCIATED WITH OIL AND GAS EXTRACTION IN ALGERIA AND TUNISIA, PHOSPHATE MINING IN TUNISIA AND MOROCCO, AND WATER-INTENSIVE AGRIBUSINESS ALONG WITH TOURISM IN MOROCCO AND TUNISIA — DOCUMENTING CASES THAT TAKE THE FORM OF ACCUMULATION BY DISPOSSESSION. Named countries, named sectors. North Africa is thinly covered by almost everything else in this file, and phosphate, gas and water-intensive agribusiness are precisely the industries taking land there. THE PAN-AFRICAN WATER NETWORK IT REPORTS, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: FROM SILOS TO A PAN-AFRICAN FRONT — THE AFRICA WATER JUSTICE NETWORK, UNITING WATER COMMONING STRUGGLES AGAINST CAPITAL — ALONGSIDE A REPORT ON A DEVELOPMENT BANK'S WATER AND SANITATION POLICIES IN TUNISIA AND PRIVATISATION AT THE EXPENSE OF FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS. A continental network on water specifically, reported by name. Communities losing a river, a borehole or an irrigation system to a private operator have very few allies in this file; that network is the one to trace and join. THE WATER POINT IT MAKES ABOUT AFRICA: AS LAND IS GRABBED AND EARMARKED IN AFRICA FOR SUPPOSED DEVELOPMENT, THERE ARE NEARLY ALWAYS IMPLICATIONS FOR THE WATER NEARBY, FOR LOCAL PEOPLE'S LAND AND WATER RIGHTS AND ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY. The land deal is also a water deal, and it is rarely written that way in the contract. A community negotiating over hectares should be asking how much water the operation will take and from where — that is the loss that arrives later and is hardest to reverse. WHAT THE PROGRAMME IS: RESEARCH AND ANALYSIS ON THE COLLECTIVE STRUGGLES OF RURAL WORKING PEOPLE TO DEMOCRATISE ACCESS, OWNERSHIP, AND CONTROL OF LAND, WATER AND OTHER NATURAL RESOURCES. WHO THE MATERIAL IS WRITTEN WITH: MANY OF THESE HAVE BEEN PRODUCED WITH TRANSNATIONAL AGRARIAN MOVEMENTS AND PARTNERS ON THE GROUND. Written with movements rather than about them, which is why the primers read as arguments a community can use rather than as findings about it. THE STATED AIM: TO CONTRIBUTE TO STRENGTHENING THE CAMPAIGNS BY AGRARIAN SOCIAL MOVEMENTS IN ORDER TO MAKE THEM MORE EFFECTIVE IN RESISTING LAND AND WATER GRABBING, AND IN DEVELOPING AND ADVANCING ALTERNATIVES SUCH AS LAND, FOOD AND WATER SOVEREIGNTY AND AGRO-ECOLOGICAL FARMING SYSTEMS. THE DEFINITION IT WORKS FROM: A GLOBAL PHENOMENON WHEREBY THE ACCESS, USE AND RIGHT TO LAND AND OTHER CLOSELY ASSOCIATED NATURAL RESOURCES IS BEING TAKEN OVER, RESULTING IN A CASCADE OF NEGATIVE IMPACTS ON RURAL LIVELIHOODS AND ECOLOGIES, HUMAN RIGHTS, AND LOCAL FOOD SECURITY — OFTEN PACKAGED AS LARGE-SCALE INVESTMENT FOR RURAL DEVELOPMENT. PACKAGED AS INVESTMENT FOR RURAL DEVELOPMENT is the phrasing a community will meet in the consultation. Having the counter-framing written down and sourced is what stops a public meeting turning into a discussion of jobs. THE CLIMATE WARNING IT CARRIES: DOMINANT APPROACHES TO CLIMATE CHANGE MITIGATION ARE PUTTING NEW PRESSURES ON SMALL FARMERS AND VILLAGE DWELLERS, JUSTIFYING DISPOSSESSION BY POWERFUL ACTORS — WITH MAINSTREAM NARRATIVES OFTEN INTENSIFYING PRESSURE TO REPLACE SO-CALLED INEFFICIENT USERS OF LAND, INCLUDING SMALL FARMERS AND PASTORALISTS, WITH MARKET-BASED ACTORS. INEFFICIENT USERS OF LAND is the exact language used against pastoralists and shifting cultivators across this file, and it now arrives wrapped in climate justification. Naming that move in advance is half of answering it. THE FRONTLINE VOICES REPORT: COOLING THE PLANET — FRONTLINE COMMUNITIES LEAD THE STRUGGLE, AMPLIFYING THE VOICES OF FRONTLINE COMMUNITIES AND SHARING THE POLITICAL MESSAGES OF 16 SOCIAL MOVEMENT LEADERS CONNECTED TO A GLOBAL CONVERGENCE OF LAND AND WATER STRUGGLES. A GLOBAL CONVERGENCE OF LAND AND WATER STRUGGLES is itself a body worth tracing — sixteen named movement leaders are sixteen possible contacts. THE PRIMERS AND THE PRINT OPTION: A GLOBAL LAND GRAB PRIMER AND A GLOBAL WATER GRAB PRIMER, ALONGSIDE A WATER JUSTICE REPORT INTENDED TO STRENGTHEN STRUGGLES FOR PUBLIC AND COMMUNITY WATER SYSTEMS — WITH PRINT COPIES ORDERABLE AND A MONTHLY NEWSLETTER. PRINT COPIES ORDERABLE. Everything else here is a download; a printed primer can be read at a village meeting by people without devices, which this file has repeatedly identified as the difference between a resource existing and being used. AND THE AFRICAN CASES ITS OWN CITATIONS POINT TO: WORK ON NEW INVESTMENT AND OLD CHALLENGES IN LAND DEALS AND THE WATER CONSTRAINT IN AFRICAN AGRICULTURE, AND ON THE POLITICS OF BIOFUELS AND LAND-WATER GRABBING IN A NAMED MOZAMBICAN CASE — WITH THE INSTITUTE FOUNDED IN 1974. WHO IT SUITS: African farmers' organisations, pastoralist associations and community committees who need the argument and the evidence, especially where the deal against them is lawful. CAVEATS: RESEARCH AND ANALYSIS, NOT FUNDING, LEGAL REPRESENTATION OR ORGANISING SUPPORT; MUCH OF THE MATERIAL IS IN ENGLISH AND ACADEMIC IN REGISTER — the primers are the accessible entry point. For the peasant movement you can join, Egypt's entry; for community booklets in African languages, Eritrea's entry; for the funder whose categories include legal aid, Algeria's entry.

trackers.name: Wildlife Works — a community forest-carbon project where 13 blocks of land stay in the communities' own legal title and locational committees decide the spending — filed with the fieldwork finding that ranch owners hold 30-year contracts while communities have no binding agreement
trackers.desc: INCOME FROM THE LAND WITHOUT SELLING IT — AND GET YOUR AGREEMENT IN WRITING — method and adjacency declared first: A BIRD CONSERVANCY WITH A LARGE LAND-PURCHASE RECORD WAS CHECKED FIRST THIS ROUND AND FOUND TO OPERATE ONLY IN LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN — NOT A RESOURCE AVAILABLE TO AFRICAN LOCALS, SO IT WAS NOT FILED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THE SHIPPED HOST AND THREE SUBJECT SPELLINGS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL ABSENT. THIS FILE'S CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC, DR CONGO, COMOROS AND GAMBIA BUCKETS MENTION FOREST-CARBON SCHEMES AND ITS CÔTE D'IVOIRE, EGYPT, KENYA AND TANZANIA BUCKETS CARBON CREDITS, IN PASSING; NONE IS THIS PROJECT AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. ITS EQUATORIAL GUINEA AND LIBYA ENTRIES COVER THE LAND-PURCHASE FUNDERS. WHO HOLDS THE TITLE, WHICH IS THE FIND: 13 BLOCKS OF LAND OWNED BY INDIGENOUS COMMUNITY OWNERSHIP GROUPS, EACH OWNED BY DIFFERENT LEGAL ENTITIES FORMED YEARS AGO BY THE COMMUNITIES AND THE GOVERNMENT TO HOLD LEGAL TITLE TO THE LAND — 12 LEASEHOLD AND 1 FREEHOLD — WITH CARBON RIGHTS HELD BY THE INDIGENOUS COMMUNITY GROUP OF LANDOWNERS. The land is not bought and not leased away: it stays in community title, and the community holds the carbon rights over it. For a community that cannot afford to buy its ground and does not want to sell it, this is the third option — income from the land while keeping it. CARBON RIGHTS as a separate thing from land rights is the point to settle before signing anything. THE GOVERNANCE STRUCTURE THAT DECIDES THE SPENDING, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: LOCATIONAL CARBON COMMITTEES ARE THE GOVERNANCE STRUCTURE THROUGH WHICH THE COMMUNITIES DIRECTLY ALLOCATE FUNDS — SET UP WITHIN EACH COMMUNITY, DETERMINING HOW THEY WOULD LIKE TO SPEND THEIR CARBON REVENUES, RESULTING IN SCHOLARSHIPS, SCHOOL INFRASTRUCTURE AND WATER INFRASTRUCTURE. A committee per location, not one committee for the whole scheme. That is the structure to insist on: money decided where it lands, by people the neighbours can hold to account. THE PUBLISHED REVENUE TARGET: OUR TARGET IS FOR 50% OR MORE OF PROJECT REVENUE TO GO DIRECTLY TO COMMUNITY PARTNERS — WITH THE MODEL CHANGING BETWEEN PROJECTS DEPENDING ON LOCALISED FACTORS SUCH AS LAND TENURE RIGHTS AND THE HOST GOVERNMENT'S POLICIES. A TARGET, not a guarantee, and it varies by project. Ask what the actual percentage is in the contract in front of you. THE THIRDS AS DESCRIBED: ONE THIRD OF REVENUE GOES TO THE LANDOWNERS, THE IMPLEMENTER RUNS THE PROJECT'S OPERATING COSTS, AND THE PROFIT IS THEN SPLIT 50/50 BETWEEN THE COMMUNITIES AND THE PROJECT INVESTORS. THE PUBLISHED CRITICISM, RECORDED IN FULL BECAUSE IT IS THE WARNING: FIELD RESEARCH CARRIED OUT OVER A YEAR FOUND THAT IN PRACTICE, RANCH OWNERS ARE PAID FIRST, THEN PROJECT COSTS ARE DEDUCTED, AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES RECEIVE THE REMAINDER — THAT RANCH OWNERS SIGNED 30-YEAR CONTRACTUAL AGREEMENTS ENTITLING THEM TO ONE-THIRD, WHILE LOCAL COMMUNITIES DO NOT HAVE LEGALLY BINDING AGREEMENTS WITH THE PROJECT. This is why the entry exists in this form. The landowners' third is contractual and the community's share is a residue — whatever is left after the two prior claims. A community entering any carbon arrangement should read that sentence twice and then ask for its own 30-year written agreement, on the same footing as the landowners', before the first credit is sold. Everything else here is secondary to that. WHO ACTUALLY OWNED THE RANCHES IN THAT PHASE: OF 13 RANCHES COVERING 169,731 HECTARES, FIVE WERE INDIVIDUALLY OWNED, FOUR WERE OWNED BY PRIVATE COMPANIES, AND FOUR WERE COMMUNAL RANCHES OWNED MAINLY BY ONE ETHNIC GROUP BASED ON KINSHIP TIES AND TRADITIONAL LAND RIGHTS, UNDER THE DIRECTORSHIP OF A MINISTRY REPRESENTATIVE. Nine of thirteen were private or company-owned. The phrase COMMUNITY PROJECT can cover an arrangement where most of the land and most of the landowner payments sit with individuals and firms — establish the ownership breakdown before believing the label. THE SCALE AND THE MARKET: UP TO 1,800,000 VERIFIED CARBON UNITS A YEAR, SOLD ON THE VOLUNTARY MARKET TO INDIVIDUALS OR CORPORATIONS INCLUDING TWO NAMED FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS — WITH AN ESTIMATE OF OVER 48 MILLION TONNES AVOIDED OVER 30 YEARS. THE VERIFICATION IT CARRIES: IN 2011 IT BECAME THE FIRST SUCH PROJECT IN THE WORLD VALIDATED AND VERIFIED BY TWO STANDARDISING BODIES, WHICH TOGETHER EVALUATE EVERY ASPECT INCLUDING HOW EMISSION REDUCTIONS ARE CALCULATED AND WHETHER THE BENEFIT-SHARING TO COMMUNITIES IS FAIR AND EQUITABLE — WITH A GOLD-LEVEL DISTINCTION FROM ONE. The standards audit the benefit-sharing, not only the carbon. That makes the standard-setters a place to complain to when the split is not honoured — a route that exists independently of the project developer. THE JOBS IT COUNTS: APPROXIMATELY 400 PEOPLE EMPLOYED, MAINLY LOCAL, INCLUDING AN EXPORT-PROCESSING FACTORY FOR CLOTHING — AND EIGHT PERMANENT STAFF MANUALLY PROCESSING 850–1,274 HALF-KILOGRAM BRIQUETTES A WEEK OF ECO-CHARCOAL PRODUCED WITHOUT CUTTING DOWN A SINGLE TREE. Charcoal made without felling trees, at a documented weekly output with eight staff. That is a copyable enterprise on its own, independent of any carbon scheme, for communities where charcoal burning is the pressure on the forest. THE MODEL IT SAYS IT REPLACED: IT BROKE THE MOLD OF THE TRADITIONAL AND FAILING FORTRESS MODEL OF CONSERVATION — ALLEVIATING PRESSURE ON THE ECOSYSTEM THROUGH JOB CREATION, CO-CREATING LONG-TERM JOBS THAT REPLACE POACHING, SUBSISTENCE FARMING AND ILLEGAL TREE HARVESTING. Recorded as their claim. Note that SUBSISTENCE FARMING sits on their list of things to be replaced — which a farming community should weigh carefully before agreeing that its own food growing is the problem. THE ENABLING LAW A COMMENTARY IDENTIFIES, AND ITS DOUBLE EDGE: BEFORE 2016 MILLIONS OCCUPIED LAND FOR GENERATIONS BUT DID NOT LEGALLY OWN IT, CLASSIFIED AS GOVERNMENT TRUST LAND AND VULNERABLE TO EXPROPRIATION — A COMMUNITY LAND ACT CHANGED THIS, SO COMMUNITIES CAN NOW REGISTER LAND COLLECTIVELY, OBTAIN TITLE CERTIFICATES, ESTABLISH GOVERNANCE STRUCTURES AND ENTER LEGALLY BINDING CONSERVANCY AGREEMENTS, WITH WOMEN AND YOUTH REQUIRED TO HAVE REPRESENTATION IN MANAGEMENT COMMITTEES; BUT SUBDIVISION INTO PRIVATE PARCELS CAN FRAGMENT WILDLIFE CORRIDORS UNLESS COMMUNITIES CHOOSE COLLECTIVE REGISTRATION. COLLECTIVE REGISTRATION IS THE CHOICE THAT MATTERS. Individual parcels feel safer to each family and destroy the block's value together — and once subdivided it is close to irreversible. Whether such an act exists in your own country is the first thing to establish. AND WHAT THE IMPLEMENTER OFFERS BEYOND ITS OWN PROJECTS: OVER 25 YEARS OF DIRECT FIELD MANAGEMENT, AND IT HAS BECOME A TRUSTED CONSULTANT TO GOVERNMENTS DEVELOPING JURISDICTIONAL PROGRAMMES AND NATIONAL FRAMEWORKS. WHO IT SUITS: African communities holding or able to register collective title who want income from keeping land intact — and any community being approached by a carbon developer, who should read the criticism first. CAVEATS: A COMMERCIAL CARBON DEVELOPER, NOT A GRANT-MAKER; INDEPENDENT FIELDWORK FOUND COMMUNITIES RECEIVING A RESIDUE WITHOUT BINDING AGREEMENTS WHILE LANDOWNERS HELD 30-YEAR CONTRACTS; MOST OF THE LAND IN THE PHASE STUDIED WAS PRIVATE OR COMPANY-OWNED; AND CARBON PRICES ARE A VOLATILE MARKET, NOT AN INCOME GUARANTEE. Get a written agreement of your own, and get it checked by counsel. For the funds that pay for land purchase instead, Equatorial Guinea's and Libya's entries.

trackers.name: Audit Bureau
trackers.desc: National — supreme audit institution of Libya. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Libya.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: African Convention on Nature — check WHICH version binds your state
trackers.desc: THERE ARE TWO AFRICAN CONVENTIONS OF THIS NAME, AND CITING THE WRONG ONE IS THE AVOIDABLE ERROR HERE. The Algiers Convention was signed 15 September 1968, in force 16 June 1969. The revised Maputo Convention was adopted by the Assembly of the Union in Maputo on 11 July 2003 and entered into force 23 July 2016 — thirteen years later. THE OPERATIVE RULE: the 1968 Convention remains in force for those countries that have not ratified the 2003 revisions, so the two coexist and which binds your state depends on its ratification status. Commentary records only about 30 percent of African states had ratified Maputo. This entry does not assert which binds your state — the African Union publishes a Status List alongside the treaty text at au.int. Check it first. WHY THE DELAY IS AN ARGUMENT FOR IT: commentary attributes the thirteen years to the revised text containing strong provisions that could create accountability and also slow down social and economic development — a treaty resisted for creating accountability is one worth invoking where it applies. PROVISIONS TO KNOW: article XXXIX — no reservation may be made to this Convention, so a ratifying state takes all of it; article XL — withdrawal takes effect only one year after written notification; and no instrument of accession to the 1968 Algiers Convention may be deposited any longer, so the older text is closed to new entrants. THE OBJECTIVES ARE BROADER THAN USUAL: conservation, utilisation and development of soil, water, flora and fauna for present and future welfare, from an economic, nutritional, scientific, educational, cultural and aesthetic point of view — so a claim resting on cultural or aesthetic value has a treaty basis. BUT IF THE 1968 TEXT IS WHAT BINDS YOU, EXPECT LITTLE: parties were encouraged to cooperate but were not required to submit regular reports on implementation, and there were no financial mechanisms — no reporting trail, no funding attached. Article XLI also provides for interim secretariat arrangements, so check current institutional capacity. IUCN publishes a commentary on each provision in English and French.

trackers.name: Environment General Authority — the only environmental body a Libyan community can address, and an honest account of what does not exist
trackers.desc: WHO TO APPROACH, AND WHY THIS ENTRY IS WRITTEN AS AN ABSENCE: no verified Libyan civil society organisation providing land defence, environmental litigation or community legal support could be found. What exists is the Environment General Authority (EGA), established in 2000, a scientific, regulatory and advisory body responsible for conservation of biological resources, environmental pollution and integrated planning. The single legal hook worth knowing: the Environment Law of 2003 gives the environment ministry and the EGA under it the right to monitor pollution levels and to require emission permits for facilities covered by the regulation. If a facility near you is emitting, the permit and the monitoring duty are what to ask about, in writing, naming the law. WHAT YOU SHOULD EXPECT, STATED PLAINLY: the EGA long operated as an independent autonomous institution but now reports directly to the environment ministry; Libya has had no national development plan since 2011, its institutions were deeply divided and fragmented, and the authority itself is described as still needing international partnership to articulate environmental management measures and mobilise resources. Libya has ratified the main environmental conventions and the Paris Agreement but had not submitted a nationally determined contribution. There are branch offices in regional cities, including at Tobruk. WHO IT SUITS: Libyan residents facing industrial pollution or a facility operating without permits — as the only formal address available. CAVEATS: THIS IS A STATE REGULATOR, NOT AN ALLY: it is part of the government that licenses the projects, there is no independent civil society counterpart recorded here, and no intake or complaints procedure was found. NO VERIFIED LIVE SITE FOR THE EGA EXISTS — this entry points at an intergovernmental network's record of the organisation. In a fragmented state, confirm which authority is actually functioning in your region before relying on any of this.

trackers.name: GEF Small Grants in Libya — added by name in the eighth cycle, and the first thing in this file a Libyan community can actually apply to
trackers.desc: WHERE TO APPLY FOR MONEY: the GEF SMALL GRANTS PROGRAMME expanded country coverage in its eighth replenishment from 124 to 135 countries, ADDING LIBYA BY NAME — alongside Somalia, South Sudan, Equatorial Guinea and São Tomé and Príncipe. This file's Libya entry has until now recorded only a state regulator and the ABSENCE of civil society support; this is the first thing here a Libyan community group can actually apply to. THE ALLOCATION RULE: the eighth cycle secured USD 135 million for the core programme and ensures EQUAL ALLOCATION OF NEARLY USD 1 MILLION IN CORE FINANCING TO EACH of the 135 participating countries — regardless of size or previous participation, with STAR allocations raised over 30 per cent. A newly added country is not competing against large established programmes for the core money, which is the argument for applying in the FIRST cycle rather than waiting to see how it goes. The programme's stated objective is to catalyse and mobilise CIVIL SOCIETY actors and LOCAL ACTIONS addressing the major drivers of environmental degradation, and it has funded community-level environmental projects since 1992. WHO IT SUITS: Libyan community groups and associations with an environmental, water, waste or land degradation project. CAVEATS: A DONOR CYCLE WITH FIXED CALLS, AND A COUNTRY WHERE CIVIL SOCIETY OPERATES UNDER SEVERE CONSTRAINT — confirm the country programme is actually operational and what registration it requires before counting on it; it funds environmental action, NOT litigation or land purchase. For the state environmental regulator and the honest record of what does not exist, Libya's EGA entry.

trackers.name: Libya — the Bar Association does referrals, a Libyan legal aid organisation exists, and LFJL runs strategic litigation from the diaspora
trackers.desc: WHO TO ASK FOR A LAWYER, IN A COUNTRY THIS FILE HAS UNTIL NOW RECORDED ONLY AS AN ABSENCE: LAWYERS FOR JUSTICE IN LIBYA (LFJL), established in response to the February 2011 uprising BY A NETWORK OF LIBYAN LAWYERS, works through transitional justice, LEGAL REFORM, human rights education, STRATEGIC LITIGATION and advocacy, and is a member of the international legal-empowerment network. A strategic litigation organisation founded by Libyan lawyers is the closest thing to public interest counsel recorded for Libya — approach it for a case of wider significance, not an individual dispute. TWO OTHER NAMED BODIES: the LIBYAN BAR ASSOCIATION, which maintains A DIRECTORY OF PRACTISING LAWYERS and provides REFERRALS to law firms and lawyers — and which is also where you report a lawyer's misconduct — with a Tripoli bar named separately; and the LIBYAN ORGANIZATION FOR LEGAL AID. Legal-directory material also names the Libyan Center for Civil Liberties and Human Rights (lcclhr.org.ly). Start with the Bar Association referral: in a country where no walk-in legal aid desk could be verified, a referral from the professional body is how you reach a named practitioner rather than guessing. The justice ministry is cited as the second point for information on legal services and procedures. WHO IT SUITS: Libyans needing to identify counsel for a property, expropriation or rights matter, and anyone with a case of wider public significance. CAVEATS: SOURCING IS INDIRECT AND THE ENTRY SAYS SO — LFJL is verified through a legal-empowerment network profile; the bar association and the legal aid organisation are named in legal-directory material rather than through their own verified sites, so confirm contacts before relying on them. Libya is divided and insecure, civil society operates under severe constraint, and none of these bodies is a walk-in service. For the state environmental regulator and the record of what does not exist, Libya's EGA entry; for community environmental funding newly opened to Libya, the GEF Small Grants entry.

trackers.name: The Libyan Nature Platform's reserve register — named reserves with hectares, dates and candid failure notes, plus the laws that already protect pastures and forests
trackers.desc: WHAT IS ALREADY PROTECTED AND WHO KEEPS THE LIST: a Libyan platform publishes a REGISTER OF THE COUNTRY'S NATURE RESERVES AND NATIONAL PARKS with names, areas, dates and honest condition notes — for example BIR AYAD NATURE RESERVE, 12,000 HECTARES in the Nafusa Mountains, 120 km southwest of Tripoli, INITIALLY AN AGRICULTURAL PROJECT AND DECLARED A RESERVE IN 1992, holding around 300 species of trees, shrubs and herbs; and KOUF, established 1975, one of seven national parks. An existing register with named areas and dates is what you cite when a project is proposed near you — and Bir Ayad shows the most useful precedent in Libya: an AGRICULTURAL PROJECT WAS CONVERTED INTO A DECLARED RESERVE, so the conversion runs in the direction you want. THE FAILURE NOTE WORTH MORE THAN THE SUCCESSES, PUBLISHED BY LIBYANS ABOUT LIBYA: ELNAGGAZA NATIONAL PARK, established 1992, 4,000 HECTARES with 600 STRICTLY PROTECTED, whose PINE FORESTS WERE CREATED BY SEASONAL REFORESTATION CARRIED OUT BY STUDENTS AND SCOUTS — but LACK OF MANAGEMENT HAS LED TO WILDFIRES AND LOCAL ENCROACHMENT, ESPECIALLY IN COASTAL AREAS. Volunteers can create a forest; only a funded management body keeps it. If you plant, negotiate who patrols and who pays before the first season ends — the same gap that emptied Mohéli's park of finance for fourteen years. THE LAWS THAT ALREADY EXIST TO CITE: LAW NO. 15 OF 2003 on the Protection and Improvement of the Environment covering pollution, natural resource management and wildlife conservation; LAW NO. 5 OF 1982 ON THE PROTECTION OF PASTURES AND FORESTS; LAW NO. 3 OF 1982 on the exploitation of water resources; the 1970 Law for the Protection of Agricultural Land; and Council of Ministers Decree No. 6 of 1997 PROHIBITING HUNTING IN ALL REGIONS, with Decree No. 183 of 2006 establishing the NATIONAL PARKS PROJECT to create new parks and upgrade existing ones. A pasture-and-forest protection law from 1982 and a national hunting ban are old, broad and still on the books — in a country with a weak central state, an existing statute you can name is worth more than a new one you must lobby for. Protected areas fall under national parks, protected reserves, protected areas and wetlands, managed through a technical committee for wildlife and national parks; an international conservation union report has called for improvements to the legal and institutional framework and identified 24 NEW MARINE AND COASTAL AREAS for protection. WHO IT SUITS: Libyan communities near an existing or proposed reserve, and anyone needing to name the statute that already covers their ground. CAVEATS: STATE-MANAGED AREAS IN A DIVIDED COUNTRY — management capacity is the documented weak point, not the legal categories. For the regulator and what does not exist, Libya's EGA entry; for a lawyer, the Bar Association and LFJL entry; for community funding newly opened to Libya, the GEF Small Grants entry.

trackers.name: Libyan Wildlife Trust and five other named Libyan conservation organisations — founded 2011, restoring named forests with hectare targets, and funded through a North African small-grants programme
trackers.desc: WHO TO CALL IN LIBYA — AND THIS CORRECTS THE THIN PICTURE THIS FILE HELD: the LIBYAN WILDLIFE TRUST (LWT), FOUNDED 9 NOVEMBER 2011 by a group of nature lovers and wildlife defenders, is a Libyan environmental NGO and a member of the international conservation union, described as the most active civil society association in the protection of wildlife in Libya, working year by year under unstable national conditions. A Libyan-founded organisation that has kept working through fourteen years of instability is a more reliable contact than any ministry in this file's Libya record — and it is reachable. WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES, WITH THE NUMBERS: restoration of the JODAYEM FOREST, a coastal ecosystem east of AL-ZAWIYA and west of Tripoli, 110 HECTARES including 11 hectares of rocky terrain between the forest and the sea, degraded by plastic waste accumulation, erosion and LACK OF MANAGEMENT PLANS — with LWT introducing a comprehensive system of PLANNING, MONITORING AND COMMUNITY MANAGEMENT, working with local institutions and civil society, publishing scientific evaluations of the restoration, and restoring 45 HECTARES through planting. It also rehabilitated the NASSER FOREST, whose biodiversity had deteriorated from excessive water salinity, by RESTORING THE WATER INFRASTRUCTURE. Naming the hectares, publishing the evaluation and fixing the water before planting is the sequence — Libya's own record shows volunteer planting without management ends in wildfire and encroachment. IT ALSO SPEAKS PUBLICLY: LWT has warned that Libyan tortoise species are heading toward extinction through smuggling out of the country, and green activists have raised the increasing axing of acacia in the southwestern Al-Widyan region. WHERE ITS MONEY COMES FROM, WHICH IS THE REPLICABLE PART: LWT is supported by a SMALL INITIATIVES PROGRAMME FOR NORTH AFRICAN CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, coordinated in Libya by a regional conservation union office and co-funded by three foundations. A small-grants programme with a named in-country coordinator is how a Libyan association gets funded at all — ask the coordinator, not the donors. FIVE MORE NAMED LIBYAN BODIES active in conservation: the LIBYAN SOCIETY FOR BIRDS, the LIBYAN ORGANISATION FOR CONSERVATION OF NATURE, ALHAYA ORGANIZATION FOR THE PROTECTION OF WILDLIFE AND MARINE ORGANISMS, and THE NEW LIBYA. LWT's own stated message: Libya is an open protected area for everyone. WHO IT SUITS: Libyan communities facing coastal degradation, forest loss or wildlife trafficking, and anyone needing a named domestic partner. CAVEATS: A VOLUNTEER-ROOTED NGO IN A DIVIDED COUNTRY, dependent on external small grants; contacts should be confirmed. For the reserve register with hectares and failure notes, Libya's Nature Platform entry; for the regulator, EGA; for a lawyer, the Bar Association and LFJL entry.

trackers.name: Named Libyan law firms with offices in BOTH Tripoli and Benghazi — and the Benghazi Bar Association's Rights and Freedoms Committee
trackers.desc: NAMED LIBYAN FIRMS AND WHERE THEY SIT, WHICH IN A DIVIDED COUNTRY IS THE FIRST QUESTION: ASHAFAH & PARTNERS LAW FIRM publishes specialised advice on COMMERCIAL, REAL-ESTATE (عقارية) AND INVESTMENT MATTERS as well as CUSTOMS DISPUTES, and names its own advocates with their qualifications — including practitioners who are FACULTY MEMBERS AT THE FACULTY OF LAW, UNIVERSITY OF TRIPOLI and one who PRACTISES BEFORE THE LIBYAN SUPREME COURT in civil, commercial and labour disputes and has worked with major companies including an oil refining company. MIRAS LAW FIRM advertises services in TRIPOLI AND BENGHAZI; an older Libyan directory lists a firm with a TRIPOLI OFFICE at 129, 1st September Street and a BENGHAZI OFFICE at 36, Nasser Street, offering advice, consultation and legal representation before Libyan courts, and another Tripoli practice covering civil, banking, commercial, transport, contract, insurance, petroleum and foreign investment law. Firms with offices in BOTH Tripoli and Benghazi can act on either side of the country's division — ask that question before anything else, because a firm that cannot appear in the court where your land lies is of no use to you. A BODY THAT EXISTS AND IS WORTH KNOWING: the BENGHAZI BAR ASSOCIATION has a RIGHTS AND FREEDOMS COMMITTEE, whose head has been a Benghazi practitioner and law teacher; Libyan lawyers are recorded as participating in legal committees focused on rights, freedoms and legal reform under that association. A rights and freedoms committee inside a bar is where a public-interest question is heard when the commercial side of the profession will not take it — ask for that committee by name. THE HONEST FRAME: the firms reachable this way practise COMMERCIAL, OIL AND GAS, BANKING AND INVESTMENT law — they are equipped for a property or expropriation file but are not public-interest lawyers, and Libya has a documented tradition of human-rights advocates who are something else again. Ask what a firm has done against a state entity before you retain it. WHO IT SUITS: Libyans with a property, land-registry, expropriation or contract matter, in either half of the country. CAVEATS: PRIVATE COMMERCIAL FIRMS — fees apply and contacts should be confirmed in a country whose institutions are divided. For the bar's referral function and the Libyan legal aid organisation, Libya's Bar Association and LFJL entry; for the Libyan NGO restoring named forests, the Libyan Wildlife Trust entry.

trackers.name: Libya's municipalities as the reachable door — decentralisation under Law 59 of 2012, the 100-metre coastal building ban, and the 2011 land registration freeze
trackers.desc: THE MUNICIPALITY IS THE REACHABLE DOOR IN A COUNTRY WHOSE NATIONAL INSTITUTIONS ARE DIVIDED: Libya launched a decentralisation process with the adoption of LAW 59 IN 2012, and MUNICIPALITIES WERE GIVEN WIDER POWERS OVER TAX COLLECTION, PUBLIC UTILITIES AND INFRASTRUCTURE, with TAXES ON VACANT LAND allocated and distributed to municipalities ACCORDING TO THEIR URBAN DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS' NEEDS (Law 116/1972). Vacant-land tax flows to your municipality according to its development plans — which means the municipal plan is where a project near you is enabled or refused, and it is a local body you can physically reach. THE PLANNING LAW TO CITE: LAW 3 OF 2011 is comprehensive and detailed on urban planning functions — giving definitions and objectives, DEFINING THE COMPETENT AUTHORITIES, and describing the planning TYPES AND LEVELS: NATIONAL, REGIONAL, LOCAL AND URBAN PLANS; the 1965 planning law (Law 5) established the URBAN PLANNING AUTHORITY, overseeing planning and certification, roads, LAND SUBDIVISIONS, building and land use classification, and the regularisation of informal settlements. Ask which LEVEL of plan covers your ground — national, regional, local or urban — because that determines which authority must certify a subdivision, and a subdivision is how land is taken piece by piece. TWO RULES WORTH KNOWING VERBATIM: BUILDING LESS THAN ONE HUNDRED METRES FROM THE SEASHORE IS FORBIDDEN, EXCEPT FOR APPROVED TOURISTIC FACILITIES (Law 32 of 1977 amending the earlier law); and LAW 7 OF 1982 PROTECTS THE ENVIRONMENT FROM URBAN EXPANSION AND OTHER ENCROACHMENTS, naming prohibited pollutants and the enforcement authorities. A hundred-metre coastal setback with a tourism exception is exactly the clause a resort application must argue around — make them prove the exception applies. THE FACT THAT DECIDES WHETHER YOU CAN REGISTER ANYTHING: a LAND REGISTRATION FREEZE INTRODUCED IN 2011 PRACTICALLY STOPPED NEW PROPERTIES FROM BECOMING TAXABLE, hindering the tax base and raising questions about equality; tax collection rates are very low. If you cannot register, you are not alone and it is not your failure — gather every other form of evidence instead: municipal records, utility connections, tax receipts where they exist. LARGE DONOR PROGRAMMES FUND MUNICIPALITIES DIRECTLY, one covering 24 LIBYAN MUNICIPALITIES with balanced coverage across the country on health, education, water and sanitation, and others building local-authority capacity and promoting collaborative governance and participation. Ask whether your municipality is one of the 24: a funded municipality has staff, meetings and reporting obligations you can attend and read. WHO IT SUITS: Libyans facing coastal or urban development, subdivision, or unregisterable property. CAVEATS: A DIVIDED STATE and a frozen registry; municipal capacity varies. For the reserve register, Libya's Nature Platform entry; for named firms in both cities, the law-firms entry; for the NGO restoring named forests, the Libyan Wildlife Trust entry.

trackers.name: BADO Environmental Society, the PPI-OSCAN grant window with its Libyan national coordinator, and the Mediterranean MPA managers' network that trains and lists Libyan organisations
trackers.desc: THE SECOND SOCIETY, THE GRANT WINDOW AND THE DIRECTORIES: alongside the Libyan Wildlife Trust already in this file, BADO ENVIRONMENTAL SOCIETY FOR THE PROTECTION OF MARINE AND WILDLIFE is a named Libyan organisation whose representative has spoken publicly on THE NEED TO BUILD THE CAPACITY OF LOCAL ENVIRONMENTAL ORGANISATIONS, WHICH CAN CONTRIBUTE TO SECURING A BETTER FUTURE FOR LIBYA AND FOR THE MEDITERRANEAN ENVIRONMENT IN GENERAL. A second named Libyan society, with marine protection in its own title, means the country's environmental sector is not one organisation — and a marine body matters on a coast where this file records a hundred-metre building setback that somebody has to enforce. Libyan conservationists have been taken on capacity-building visits to a biosphere reserve abroad, where a Libyan Wildlife Trust member recorded learning THE IMPORTANCE OF THE TREES WE PLANT AND OUR NEED FOR SOME SPECIFIC SPECIES AND NOT OTHERS, noting that LIBYA'S FLORA INCLUDES A MIX OF PLANTS USED BY THE LOCAL COMMUNITY, PROVIDING MEDICINE AND FOOD. Choosing the right species, not just planting, is the lesson a Libyan restoration project has already paid to learn — ask which species before you accept a donation of seedlings. THE MONEY, NAMED AND WITH A LIBYAN COORDINATOR: LWT WORKS IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND WITH THE NATIONAL COORDINATOR OF PPI-OSCAN — the small initiatives programme for North African civil society organisations — AND ITS FOREST REHABILITATION WORK WAS DELIVERED WITH PPI-OSCAN SUPPORT, COUNTED AS A CONTRIBUTION TO THE UN DECADE ON ECOSYSTEM RESTORATION. A grant window with a named in-country coordinator and a ministry sitting alongside it is the fundable route for a Libyan association. Ask the national coordinator when the next PPI-OSCAN call opens — that is a person, not a portal. THE NETWORK THAT TRAINS AND LISTS: A MEDITERRANEAN NETWORK OF MARINE PROTECTED AREA MANAGERS CARRIES LWT IN A PUBLIC DIRECTORY OF ORGANISATIONS AND OFFERS TRAINING COURSES DESIGNED TO DEVELOP THE OPERATIONAL CAPACITIES OF MPA MANAGERS, describing MPAs as slices of sea and coast placed under protection and managed for their ecological importance, ENSURING THE LIVELIHOODS OF FISHERMEN AND STIMULATING THE LOCAL ECONOMY. Training for MPA managers is available to Libyans through a Mediterranean network — which means a Libyan coastal community can send someone to be trained to run the thing it wants created. ITS OWN GOVERNANCE AND ITS OWN LESSON: LWT names A CHAIRMAN OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS AND A PRESIDENT publicly, and the chairman states that CONTINUITY, LEADERSHIP AND SUPPORTING FUTURE GENERATIONS ARE KEY TO MAINTAINING THE SUCCESS OF NGOs AND BUILDING STRONG COLLABORATIONS IN LIBYA AND BEYOND; the association contributes to environmental policy THROUGH PLATFORMS SUCH AS THE MULTILATERAL ENVIRONMENTAL AGREEMENTS. An organisation with a named board that has survived since 2011 in Libya is planning for succession, not just for the next project. Ask who takes over — the lapsed mandates elsewhere in this file all failed on exactly that. AND TO FIND THE REST: TWO PUBLIC NGO DIRECTORIES COVER LIBYA — an Arab-region NGO portal listing civil society organisations across the region, and a Libyan NGO listing site. WHO IT SUITS: Libyan coastal communities, restoration groups, and associations seeking funding or training. CAVEATS: A SMALL, DONOR-DEPENDENT SECTOR IN A DIVIDED COUNTRY; confirm contacts. For the Jodayem and Nasser forest hectares and five more named bodies, Libya's Libyan Wildlife Trust entry; for named firms in both Tripoli and Benghazi, the law-firms entry; for the municipality route and the coastal setback, the decentralisation entry; for the reserve register, the Nature Platform entry.

trackers.name: Two searchable Libyan NGO directories — 84 organisations listed for Tripoli with what each does, plus named Libyan agriculture and wildlife organisations and the resource centres in Sebha and Derna
trackers.desc: EIGHTY-FOUR IN TRIPOLI, AND A GRANT DESK IN SEBHA — because this file records Libya as one of the hardest places in Africa to find anybody, and the answer is two searchable lists: A CITY-LEVEL DIRECTORY OF NGOs, CHARITIES AND NON-PROFITS WORKING IN TRIPOLI RETURNS 84 RESULTS, EACH WITH A ONE-LINE DESCRIPTION OF WHAT THE ORGANISATION ACTUALLY DOES AND A CATEGORY PATH — for example EDUCATION AND TRAINING then CAPACITY BUILDING AND TRAINING. Eighty-four organisations in one city, each with its work described rather than just named. That is the difference between a list and a directory: you can tell before you write whether the body does capacity building, health, agriculture or media. Search the city, then the category. THE SECOND DIRECTORY IS FILTERABLE BY COUNTRY AND BY CATEGORY and carries Libyan civil society organisations describing themselves — including THE LIBYAN ORGANIZATION FOR AGRICULTURE, DEDICATED TO PROMOTING SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURAL PRACTICES, IMPROVING FOOD SECURITY AND SUPPORTING RURAL COMMUNITIES; TAFARROD, WHICH FOCUSES ON EMPOWERING AND STRENGTHENING WOMEN AND YOUTH BY TRAINING THEM ON ECONOMIC AND POLITICAL LEVELS TO CREATE MORE OPPORTUNITIES FOR THEM; a LIBYAN CSO THAT BUILDS THE CAPACITIES OF YOUNG PEOPLE IN SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT AND SUPPORTS OFFICIAL AUTHORITIES; a body working to EMPOWER WOMEN, INTEGRATE MIGRANTS AND YOUTH AND ENHANCE LIVELIHOODS THROUGH LEADERSHIP AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMMES; and a group introducing itself simply as A GROUP WORKING TO PROTECT WILDLIFE AND MARINE LIFE. An organisation for AGRICULTURE that names rural communities in its own object is the one to call about farmland, water and grazing — subjects the conservation bodies in this file's Libyan record do not cover. And a CSO whose stated work includes SUPPORTING OFFICIAL AUTHORITIES is useful in a divided country: it can carry a question into an administration that will not take it from a complainant. THE PART THAT PUTS A DESK NEAR YOU: AN INTERNATIONAL NGO PRESENT IN LIBYA SINCE 2011 HAS FOUR OFFICES — TRIPOLI, BENGHAZI, SEBHA AND DERNA — PLUS A SUPPORTING OFFICE IN TUNIS, AND PROVIDES SERVICES INCLUDING CAPACITY BUILDING, GRANTING, MENTORING, COORDINATION AND NETWORKING THROUGH ITS RESOURCE CENTRES, RELYING ON MORE THAN A DECADE OF EMPOWERING CIVIL SOCIETY ACROSS LIBYA. GRANTING is the word to notice, and the four cities are the point: Sebha is in the south and Derna in the east, so this is money and mentoring reachable outside Tripoli. If your community is nowhere near the capital, ask the nearest resource centre what it grants and what it requires — a resource centre with a mentoring function will help you write the application rather than just receive it. Its sectors span WATER, SANITATION AND HYGIENE, PROTECTION, SHELTER, CASH, EDUCATION AND INFRASTRUCTURE REHABILITATION, STRENGTHENING CIVIL SOCIETY AND SMALL BUSINESSES, AND PROMOTING CIRCULAR ECONOMY INITIATIVES. The honest context is recorded alongside: FOLLOWING THE 2011 REVOLUTION LIBYA EXPERIENCED A CIVIL WAR FROM 2014 TO 2020, RESULTING IN A DIVISION BETWEEN EAST AND WEST LIBYA, AND THE FRAGMENTATION AND INSTABILITY HAVE HINDERED INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT, LIMITED SOCIAL SUPPORT FOR VULNERABLE COMMUNITIES AND CREATED BARRIERS FOR CIVIL SOCIETY. An east-west division means an organisation registered in one half may not function in the other. Before you rely on a body from a directory, check which city its office is in and whether it operates on your side — that is the first question in Libya and almost nowhere else in this file. WHO IT SUITS: Libyan communities anywhere outside Tripoli, farming and rural groups, and anyone who needs to find an organisation from scratch. CAVEATS: DIRECTORIES GO STALE AND MANY LISTED BODIES ARE INTERNATIONAL AGENCIES RATHER THAN LIBYAN ASSOCIATIONS — read the descriptions before writing. For the Libyan conservation organisations and the forest rehabilitation, Libya's Libyan Wildlife Trust entry; for the small grants window with its Libyan national coordinator, the BADO and PPI-OSCAN entry; for named reserves with hectares, the Libyan Nature Platform register; for firms with offices in both Tripoli and Benghazi, the named law firms entry; for the reachable administrative door, the municipalities entry.

trackers.name: Global Witness, London — the investigative organisation that works through 30+ local partner organisations and takes evidence communities gathered themselves — 2,200 attacks documented since 2012, and a report that reached 1,600 news articles in 48 hours
trackers.desc: THEY TAKE EVIDENCE COMMUNITIES GATHERED THEMSELVES — and that sentence is the reason this entry exists, because most international documentation projects only read newspapers: DESK-BASED RESEARCH HAS ITS LIMITATIONS. MANY ATTACKS ON LAND AND ENVIRONMENTAL DEFENDERS RECEIVE LITTLE OR NO MEDIA ATTENTION, DUE TO THE REMOTE LOCATION OF ATTACKS, STIGMATISATION BY INVESTIGATING AUTHORITIES, OR WIDESPREAD GOVERNMENT REPRESSION OF THE MEDIA. IN MOST INSTANCES THEY SUPPLEMENT IDENTIFIED CASES WITH ADDITIONAL RESEARCH — INCLUDING WORKING CLOSELY TO SHARE INFORMATION WITH TRUSTED CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS AND COMMUNITIES WHO HAVE GATHERED EVIDENCE THROUGH THEIR OWN INVESTIGATIONS. If it happened where no journalist goes, it can still be recorded — by you. A community that keeps its own account of what was done to it has something an international organisation will use. That is a reason to write things down on the day they happen, with dates and names, even when nobody appears to be listening. THE ROUTE IN IS THROUGH PARTNERS: IN PARTNERSHIP WITH OVER 30 LOCAL, NATIONAL AND REGIONAL ORGANISATIONS IN MORE THAN 20 COUNTRIES, IT PRODUCES AN ANNUAL REPORT, AND HAS DONE SO SINCE 2012. Thirty-odd local organisations feed it. Find which one covers your country — the annual report lists its contributors — and take your documentation to them rather than writing to London. WHAT THEY ACTUALLY VERIFY, SO YOU KNOW WHAT TO DOCUMENT: THEY WORK CLOSELY WITH IN-COUNTRY PARTNERS TO VERIFY WHETHER THERE IS A REASONABLE AND SUSPECTED LINK BETWEEN THE KILLING OR DISAPPEARANCE AND THE PERSON'S ACTIVISM — AND TESTIMONY FROM FAMILIES, COMMUNITIES AND ORGANISATIONS WORKING WITH TARGETED DEFENDERS OFTEN PROVIDES KEY INFORMATION. The test is the LINK between the harm and the activism, not proof of who did it. So the record to keep is what the person was doing, who they had opposed, and what threats came before — which is exactly the part a police report leaves out. Family testimony is named as key information, so the family's own account counts. THE DATABASE: OVER 2,200 KILLINGS OR LONG-TERM DISAPPEARANCES OF DEFENDERS SINCE 2012, WITH 146 CASES DOCUMENTED IN 2024 — BUILT THROUGH A YEAR-LONG PROCESS OF CROSS-REFERENCING DATA FROM DIFFERENT SOURCES TO ENSURE ITS CREDIBILITY. AND THE HONESTY THAT MAKES IT USABLE: IT STATES PLAINLY THAT ITS DATA DOES NOT INCLUDE EVERY PERSON KILLED FOR PROTECTING THE ENVIRONMENT, AND THAT UNDOCUMENTED CASES POSE CHALLENGES. A count that admits it is an undercount. Cite it as a floor rather than a total — and note the implication for your own area: absence from the list means nobody filed, not that nobody died. WHAT PUBLICATION ACHIEVED, WITH NUMBERS: WITHIN 48 HOURS, ONE REPORT HAD BEEN COVERED IN 1,600 NEWS ARTICLES, TAKING THE MESSAGE AROUND THE WORLD — AND A NATIONAL ENVIRONMENT MINISTER RESPONDED IN A VIDEO STATEMENT CALLING FOR THE RATIFICATION OF A LANDMARK REGIONAL AGREEMENT GIVING DEFENDERS GREATER PROTECTION. Two days, sixteen hundred articles, and a minister publicly calling for a protection treaty to be ratified. A case that enters this annual report enters that wave — which is worth far more than a single local story, and costs your community only the documentation. THE TIMING LESSON, WHICH IS COPYABLE: AS A PARLIAMENT DEBATED NEW LEGISLATION TO MAKE COMPANIES ACCOUNTABLE FOR HARM TO PEOPLE IN THEIR SUPPLY CHAINS, IT RELEASED TWO INVESTIGATIONS SHOWING THE URGENT NEED FOR CONSULTATION AND SAFETY MEASURES — REVEALING HOW PEOPLE AFFECTED BY A $15 BILLION AIRPORT DEVELOPMENT AND BY A LANDFILL HAD BEEN SUBJECTED TO THREATS AND COERCION. They published while the law was being voted on, not after. If a supply-chain or accountability law is moving in a country that buys from your region, that is the week your evidence is worth most — ask the partner organisation when those windows are. THE AFRICAN CASE IT CARRIES, RECORDED IN THE COMMUNITIES' OWN TERMS: COMMUNITIES AFFECTED BY AN EAST AFRICAN OIL PIPELINE REPORT RECEIVING THREATS AFTER REFUSING TO LEAVE THEIR HOMES WITHOUT ADEQUATE COMPENSATION. Threatened for refusing an inadequate offer — not for protesting, simply for declining. This file has recorded the same sequence from Mozambique to Uganda: the pressure arrives when you say the price is too low. AND THE MODEL, STATED: INVESTIGATE, EXPOSE, ADVOCATE — WITH THIRTY YEARS OF HOLDING COMPANIES AND OFFICIALS TO ACCOUNT AND FOCUSING ATTENTION ON THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN ENVIRONMENTAL HARMS AND HUMAN RIGHTS ABUSES. Three steps in order. A community that has only exposed, without investigating first, gets contradicted; one that investigates and exposes but never advocates gets sympathy and no change. WHO IT SUITS: African communities and organisations documenting attacks, threats or criminalisation of land and environmental defenders. CAVEATS: THIS IS AN INVESTIGATIVE AND CAMPAIGNING ORGANISATION — IT DOES NOT FUND, LITIGATE OR PROTECT; documentation is what it offers and what it needs. For the 24-hour helpline and protection grants, Benin's defender protection entry; for the confidential complaint with no need to exhaust domestic courts, Equatorial Guinea's environmental defenders entry; for security plans and cascade training, Djibouti's protection experts entry.

trackers.name: 100,000+ volunteer linguists who translate for non-profit partners free, in 200+ languages including Arabic, French, Hausa and Swahili — with a free glossary app, free translator training, and a way for your own speakers to join
trackers.desc: THE DOCUMENT THAT DECIDES YOUR LAND IS IN A LANGUAGE NOBODY IN THE VILLAGE READS — that is the gap this fills, and this file has hit it in almost every country: A GLOBAL COMMUNITY OF OVER 100,000 LANGUAGE VOLUNTEERS OFFERING LANGUAGE SERVICES TO HUMANITARIAN AND DEVELOPMENT ORGANIZATIONS WORLDWIDE, FOUNDED IN 1993 TO LINK THE WORLD'S TRANSLATORS WITH VETTED NONPROFIT ORGANIZATIONS — WORKING IN 200+ LANGUAGES. The impact assessment, the concession contract, the compensation schedule, the funder's application form: all arrive in English, French, Arabic or Portuguese, and the people whose land it is often read none of them. A hundred thousand volunteers exist to close exactly that gap, and they work for non-profit partners at no charge. THE PURPOSE, IN THEIR WORDS: HELPING PEOPLE GET VITAL INFORMATION AND BE HEARD, WHATEVER LANGUAGE THEY SPEAK — AND CLOSING THE LANGUAGE GAPS THAT HINDER CRITICAL HUMANITARIAN AND INTERNATIONAL DEVELOPMENT EFFORTS. AND BE HEARD is the half that matters most here. Translation is usually framed as getting information to a community; this names the other direction — your submission, your complaint, your testimony reaching the body that decides. THE AFRICAN LANGUAGES NAMED AS PRIORITIES: ARABIC, FRENCH, HAUSA AND SWAHILI AMONG OTHERS — WITH A STATED SPECIAL FOCUS ON LOW-RESOURCE LANGUAGES. LOW-RESOURCE LANGUAGES is the term for the ones commercial translators will not touch because there is no market. If your community's language has never had a document translated into it, that is precisely the case they exist for rather than a reason to be turned away. THE GLOSSARY WORK, WHICH IS THE FIND FOR ANY CAMPAIGN: MULTILINGUAL GLOSSARIES ARE CREATED AND PUBLISHED, DESIGNED TO SUPPORT INTERPRETERS, TRANSLATORS, FIELD STAFF, COMMUNITY OUTREACH WORKERS, AND ENUMERATORS IN USING THE MOST APPROPRIATE TERMS — WITH A NAMED COUNTRY GLOSSARY PUBLISHED AND VIEWABLE ON MOBILE PHONES. Agreeing the words before the meeting is half the negotiation. CONSULTATION, COMPENSATION, EASEMENT, FREE PRIOR AND INFORMED CONSENT — if each translator renders those differently, a community can agree to something nobody understood. A fixed glossary in your language, on everyone's phone, means the same word means the same thing in the village hall and in the ministry. THE FREE APP: A GLOSSARY APP AVAILABLE FOR ANDROID AND IOS THAT ALLOWS ANY FIELD WORKER TO ACCESS THE LANGUAGE GLOSSARIES, WITH A FACTSHEET GIVING INSTRUCTIONS TO START USING IT. THE FREE TRAINING: A LEARNING CENTER WITH FREE, SELF-PACED ONLINE TRANSLATION COURSES — A GREAT WAY FOR NEWCOMERS AND LANGUAGE PROFESSIONALS ALIKE TO DEVELOP THEIR SKILLS — INCLUDING A BASIC TRANSLATOR TRAINING COURSE BEING TRANSLATED INTO AT LEAST TEN LANGUAGES, A COURSE ON TRANSLATION TOOLS, AND COURSES ON LANGUAGE QUALITY AND DEVELOPING GLOSSARIES. FOR NEWCOMERS. A bilingual young person in your community can take a free course and become the person who reads the contract. That is a skill acquired inside the village rather than hired from outside it — and a course on DEVELOPING GLOSSARIES means they can build the terms list for your own language. HOW A SPEAKER JOINS: REGISTER AS A TRANSLATOR WITH NAME AND EMAIL, COMPLETE A PROFILE LISTING LANGUAGE PAIRS, OPTIONALLY SUBMIT CREDENTIALS OR PASS A TEST TO BECOME VERIFIED, AND ACCEPT TRANSLATION TASKS WHEN AVAILABLE — THE WORK IS FULLY REMOTE, ASYNCHRONOUS AND AT YOUR OWN PACE, WITH NO HOURS MINIMUM, AND A PUBLISHED CONTACT EMAIL FOR QUESTIONS. No minimum hours and no credentials required to start. Someone who speaks a minority language and some English can register this week; and being inside that community is how a small language gets an advocate who can be called on when a document matters. WHAT VOLUNTEERS ACTUALLY TRANSLATE: NEEDS ASSESSMENTS, HEALTH MESSAGES AND INFORMATION MATERIALS FOR HUMANITARIAN ORGANIZATIONS — COMMUNITY MEMBERS WORK TO HELP NONPROFIT PARTNERS PROVIDE MULTILINGUAL MESSAGES, ENSURING EVERYONE CAN UNDERSTAND. The route runs through non-profit partners, so a village committee usually reaches it via an organisation already working with them. Ask whichever NGO supports you to make the request — that is the doorway, and it costs them nothing either. THE STRUCTURE: IT IS THE LARGEST DIVISION AND CORE OF A PARENT ORGANISATION CREATED IN 2021, WHICH ALSO COMPRISES A TECHNOLOGY ARM AND AN INSIGHTS ARM — AND THE PARENT STRENGTHENS LANGUAGE CAPACITY BY TRAINING TRANSLATORS AND INTERPRETERS, CREATING MULTILINGUAL GLOSSARIES, AND COLLABORATING ON RESEARCH AND TECHNOLOGY. AND THE LINE FROM A SPEAKER OF A SMALL LANGUAGE, WHICH IS WHY THIS BELONGS IN A FILE ABOUT LAND: I NEVER THOUGHT MY LANGUAGE MIGHT BE CONSIDERED SO IMPORTANT TO BE PUT ON A DEVICE. A community that cannot read the papers about its own land is negotiating blind, and everyone in the room knows it. Getting the key documents into the language people actually speak is among the cheapest things that changes a negotiation — and it is available for nothing. WHO IT SUITS: African communities facing documents, contracts or consultations in a language they do not read, and organisations supporting them. CAVEATS: SERVICES GO TO VETTED NONPROFIT PARTNERS RATHER THAN DIRECTLY TO INDIVIDUALS — route the request through an organisation working with you. For the field guide in French and Arabic on making footage court-ready, Niger's entry; for the toolkit with a community website builder, Mauritius' entry; for the free brokerage that finds a law firm, the Central African Republic's entry.

trackers.name: The Land Matrix — the open land-deal database anyone may correct — intended, concluded and failed acquisitions in almost 100 countries, including carbon trading and conservation, with an African focal point hosted by an African institute and everything under an open licence
trackers.desc: THE DATABASE YOU ARE ALLOWED TO CORRECT — adjacency declared first: A LAND PORTAL IS ALREADY A HOST UNDER GUINEA-BISSAU, MOZAMBIQUE AND ESWATINI, A RIGHTS-AND-RESOURCES BODY UNDER GHANA, AND THIS FILE CARRIES A CONTRACTS REPOSITORY UNDER SUDAN — WHICH THIS INITIATIVE HAS PARTNERED WITH. NONE OF THEM CARRIES THE DEAL DATABASE, THE FOCAL POINTS OR THE OPEN LICENCE BELOW. THE PARTICIPATION CLAUSE, WHICH IS THE FIND: AS AN OPEN-ACCESS TOOL, THE DATABASE IS DESIGNED TO ENABLE BROAD PUBLIC PARTICIPATION IN CONTINUALLY UPGRADING, CORRECTING, AND IMPROVING INFORMATION ON LARGE-SCALE LAND ACQUISITIONS. You are invited to correct it. Almost every register in this file is something done to a community; this one is a public record a community can amend when the entry about its own valley is wrong, incomplete, or missing entirely. If the deal over your land is not listed, that absence is fixable by you. AND HOW LOCAL KNOWLEDGE ACTUALLY GETS IN: RELIABLE AND UP-TO-DATE INFORMATION IS FOUND IN RESEARCH PAPERS AND POLICY REPORTS OFTEN BASED ON ON-THE-GROUND EXPERIENCE, AND AUTHORS OF THESE REPORTS REGULARLY PROVIDE ADDITIONAL INFORMATION WHEN CONTACTED BY THE REGIONAL FOCAL POINTS — FORMING PART OF AN EVER-GROWING LOCAL NETWORK. So the practical route is to write to the African focal point rather than to a form. A community organisation that documents a deal becomes a source they come back to, which is a standing relationship rather than a single submission. THE AFRICAN FOCAL POINT: HOSTED BY A NAMED AFRICAN RESOURCE CONFLICT INSTITUTE, COVERING THE WHOLE CONTINENT — WHICH IS THE MOST TARGETED REGION FOR LARGE-SCALE LAND ACQUISITIONS IN THE GLOBAL SOUTH. IT ENGAGES WITH ORGANISATIONS ACROSS THE CONTINENT TO DISSEMINATE INFORMATION, SUPPORT ADVOCACY AND STIMULATE LAND DEBATE, AND WORKS WITH A NAMED SENEGALESE AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE THAT SUPPORTS WEST AFRICA, WITH A NAMED NATIONAL FOCAL POINT. The African desk sits in an African institute this file has already recorded elsewhere for its work with a national land commission. So the person to write to is on the continent, in an organisation that also does land advocacy — not a data clerk abroad. WHAT THE DATABASE HOLDS, AND THE SECOND WORD IS THE ONE TO NOTICE: DETAILED INFORMATION ABOUT DEALS IN ALMOST 100 COUNTRIES — INCLUDING INTENDED, CONCLUDED, AND FAILED ATTEMPTS TO ACQUIRE LAND THROUGH PURCHASE, LEASE OR CONCESSION. INTENDED and FAILED deals are recorded, not only completed ones. A deal still being negotiated over your land may already be listed — which is the only stage at which objecting is cheap. And the failed column is a catalogue of acquisitions that were stopped, with the investors named: read the failures in your own country before deciding yours cannot be stopped. THE INTENDED USES IT TRACKS: AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION, TIMBER EXTRACTION, RENEWABLE ENERGY PRODUCTION, CARBON TRADING, INDUSTRY, CONSERVATION AND TOURISM. CARBON TRADING and CONSERVATION are logged as land acquisitions alongside timber and industry. A carbon project or a new protected area is counted here as what it is — a deal over land — which is the framing this file's Togo and Kenya entries both record communities discovering too late. THE SCALE: SINCE 2012 IT HAS CAPTURED 1,785 CONCLUDED DEALS COVERING OVER 50 MILLION HECTARES, AND IS REGARDED AS ONE OF THE MOST COMPREHENSIVE DATA COLLECTIONS OF ITS KIND. ITS STATED PURPOSE, WORTH QUOTING IN A SUBMISSION: TO SUPPORT GREATER PUBLIC INVOLVEMENT IN CRITICAL DECISIONS THAT AFFECT THE LIVES OF LAND USERS; TO ADDRESS MAJOR IMBALANCES IN ACCESS TO INFORMATION, WHICH CURRENTLY DISADVANTAGE WEAKER STAKEHOLDERS LIKE SMALLHOLDERS, PASTORALISTS, AND OTHER VULNERABLE LAND USERS; AND TO CONTRIBUTE TO MORE TRANSPARENT, EQUITABLE AND DEMOCRATIC DECISION-MAKING. PASTORALISTS named among those disadvantaged by information imbalance. This file has recorded pastoralist land as the least documented and the most easily reallocated; the omission is now itself on the record. THE OPEN LICENCE, STATED EXACTLY: AN OPEN DATA POLICY AIMING TO PROVIDE INFORMATION FREE FROM CONSTRAINTS AND RESTRICTIONS ON USE — DATA, INFOGRAPHICS, CHARTS AND MAPS CARRY A CREATIVE COMMONS ATTRIBUTION LICENCE, SO USERS MAY DOWNLOAD, SHARE AND ADAPT THE MATERIAL FOR ANY USE, INCLUDING COMMERCIAL USE, PROVIDED MODIFICATIONS ARE INDICATED AND ATTRIBUTION GIVEN. PHOTOGRAPHS AND CERTAIN SOURCE DOCUMENTS MAY COME FROM THIRD PARTIES AND CARRY OTHER LICENCES. Maps and charts you may reprint in your own leaflet, in your own language, without asking. Check the licence on any photograph separately. WHAT THE NATIONAL OBSERVATORIES DO: MONITORING LAND DEALS, SCRUTINISING GOVERNMENT CONTRACTING PRACTICES, AND FOSTERING PUBLIC PARTICIPATION IN LAND CONTRACT NEGOTIATIONS THROUGH ADVOCACY — INVESTIGATING THE SOCIAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL EFFECTS OF ACQUISITIONS AND FEEDING THAT DATA INTO ADVOCACY STRATEGIES. THE HONEST LIMITATIONS IT PUBLISHES ABOUT ITSELF: WHILE PARTNER CONTRACTS CONTAIN DETAILED INFORMATION, THEY OFTEN FAIL TO INCORPORATE CRUCIAL INFORMATION SUCH AS SPECIFIC LOCATIONAL DATA — AND WHERE INFORMATION IS TOO SCARCE TO DISTINGUISH SINGLE PROJECTS, SEVERAL PROJECTS OF ONE INVESTOR IN THE SAME REGION MAY BE SUBSUMED UNDER ONE PARENT DEAL. NO LOCATIONAL DATA is the gap that matters most to a village: a contract can name hectares without naming where. That is exactly the hole your own boundary mapping fills — and supplying the coordinates is the single most valuable correction a community can make to this record. AND THE TWO GOVERNMENTS THAT PUBLISHED THEIR OWN DEALS: SOME STATES HAVE INCREASED THE TRANSPARENCY OF THE ACQUISITIONS THEY ARE INVOLVED IN AND PUBLISHED CONTRACTS AND OTHER INFORMATION ONLINE — TWO AFRICAN COUNTRIES ARE NAMED AS EXAMPLES. Two African governments already do it. That removes the argument that publication is impossible, and gives a named precedent to put to your own ministry. WHO IT SUITS: African communities and organisations checking whether a deal over their land is recorded, and those able to supply the location data nobody else has. CAVEATS: A MONITORING DATABASE, NOT A LEGAL OR FUNDING SERVICE, AND ENTRIES CAN BE INCOMPLETE OR MERGED — verify before relying on a figure. For the contracts archive with business plans and maps, South Sudan's entry; for the repository this initiative partnered with, Sudan's entry; for the platform mapping community land against concessions, Mali's LandMark entry.

trackers.name: AFSA (Alliance for Food Sovereignty in Africa) — Africa's largest civil society food platform — 48 member networks across 50 countries, three published membership categories, an open invitation to join, a pan-African WhatsApp community, and a members page that doubles as a directory of who to call in your country
trackers.desc: FORTY-EIGHT NETWORKS, FIFTY COUNTRIES, AND AN OPEN INVITATION — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S SOUTH AFRICA ENTRY COVERS AN INDIGENOUS PEOPLES' COORDINATING COMMITTEE OF 135 ORGANISATIONS, WHICH IS A NAMED CORE MEMBER OF THIS ALLIANCE. THAT ENTRY IS NOT RESTATED AND ITS HOST IS NOT SHIPPED HERE. THE INVITATION, WHICH IS THE FIND: IT INVITES NETWORKS, MOVEMENTS AND ORGANISATIONS ACROSS AFRICA TO JOIN THE ALLIANCE, SHARE THEIR EXPERIENCES AND STRENGTHEN THE MOVEMENT — WITH THREE PUBLISHED MEMBERSHIP CATEGORIES: CORE MEMBERS, ASSOCIATE MEMBERS AND FRIENDS. Three tiers, published, with an open call. A small organisation that could not qualify as a core member can still enter as an associate or a friend — and this file has recorded repeatedly that being inside a continental network is what turns a local committee into something a ministry answers. THE SIZE: THE CONTINENT'S LARGEST CIVIL SOCIETY PLATFORM ADVOCATING FOR FOOD SOVEREIGNTY AND AGROECOLOGY — A TRUE NETWORK OF NETWORKS COMPRISING 48 MEMBER ALLIANCES ACTIVE IN 50 AFRICAN COUNTRIES AND REACHING OVER 200 MILLION PEOPLE. WHO ITS MEMBERSHIP SPANS, AND THE BREADTH IS THE POINT: FARMERS' ORGANISATIONS, PASTORALIST AND FISHERFOLK ASSOCIATIONS, INDIGENOUS PEOPLES' GROUPS, WOMEN AND YOUTH MOVEMENTS, CONSUMER ORGANISATIONS, CIVIL SOCIETY NETWORKS, FAITH-BASED INSTITUTIONS AND ENVIRONMENTAL ADVOCATES — REPRESENTING SMALLHOLDER FARMERS, PASTORALISTS, HUNTER-GATHERERS AND INDIGENOUS PEOPLES. PASTORALISTS, FISHERFOLK AND HUNTER-GATHERERS are named alongside farmers. The groups whose land claims this file records as hardest to document are inside the membership definition, not an afterthought to it. THE OPEN CHANNEL, WHICH COSTS NOTHING: JOIN OUR BIG PAN-AFRICAN COMMUNITY ON WHATSAPP TO SHARE YOUR STORIES, ACCESS UPDATES, CAMPAIGN OPPORTUNITIES AND RESOURCES TO ORGANISE, MOBILISE AND ACT. A WhatsApp group is the lowest-friction thing in this entire file. No registration, no application, no English proposal — one number, and a village organiser is connected to campaigns across fifty countries. Where data is scarce and a smartphone is shared, that is the channel that actually works. THE MEMBERS PAGE AS A DIRECTORY, WITH WHAT EACH ONE DOES: A WEST AFRICAN ORGANISATION DIRECTLY ENGAGING OVER 25,000 SMALLHOLDERS TO IMPROVE THEIR FARMS AGROECOLOGICALLY; AN INTERNATIONAL PEASANT MOVEMENT BRINGING TOGETHER MILLIONS OF PEASANTS, SMALL AND MEDIUM-SIZE FARMERS, LANDLESS PEOPLE, WOMEN FARMERS, INDIGENOUS PEOPLE, MIGRANTS AND AGRICULTURAL WORKERS; A REGIONAL SMALL-SCALE FARMERS FORUM FOR EASTERN AND SOUTHERN AFRICA; A REGIONAL PARTICIPATORY ECOLOGICAL LAND USE MANAGEMENT ASSOCIATION; A NATIONAL UMBRELLA ORGANISATION IN ETHIOPIA HELPING WOMEN FARMERS SECURE LAND; AND A COUNTRYWIDE ALLIANCE IN ZAMBIA UNITING CIVIL SOCIETY, FAITH-BASED AND RESEARCH INSTITUTIONS. LANDLESS PEOPLE named as a constituency. Almost every land resource in this file assumes you have land to defend; a movement that organises people who have none is a different door, and it is the one for evicted and displaced households. THE FOUNDING AND THE VISION IT STATES: FOUNDED IN 2011 AT A CLIMATE CONFERENCE IN DURBAN, IT STANDS AS A UNIFYING VOICE FOR AFRICAN MOVEMENTS WORKING TO TRANSFORM FOOD SYSTEMS, CHALLENGE INDUSTRIAL AGRICULTURE AND DEFEND COMMUNITY RIGHTS — WITH A VISION OF AFRICAN PEOPLES CONTROLLING THEIR TERRITORIES, LIVELIHOODS AND GOVERNANCE SYSTEMS AND RELATED DECISION-MAKING PROCESSES, AND HOLDING THEIR GOVERNMENTS AND CORPORATE POWERS TO ACCOUNT FOR THEIR LEGACY TO FUTURE GENERATIONS. THE CHALLENGES IT NAMES, WHICH ARE THIS FILE'S SUBJECTS: COMMUNITY STRUGGLES FOR LAND AND SEED, NATURAL RESOURCE DEGRADATION, CLIMATE CHANGE, FOOD INSECURITY, AND POPULATION HEALTH IMPACTS FROM MALNUTRITION. LAND AND SEED together. A community can win its land and still lose control of what it may plant on it — seed law is the quieter half of the same fight, and this is the continental body that treats them as one subject. THE CASE-STUDY COLLECTION AND WHAT IT MEASURES: CASE STUDIES SHOWING HOW AGROECOLOGY BENEFITS AFRICA IN TERMS OF FOOD SECURITY, NUTRITION, POVERTY REDUCTION, CLIMATE CHANGE ADAPTATION AND MITIGATION, BIODIVERSITY CONSERVATION, CULTURAL SENSITIVITY, DEMOCRACY, AND VALUE FOR MONEY. VALUE FOR MONEY is the column that wins arguments with a finance ministry. When a government defends a plantation as the economically serious option, the answer is a costed comparison rather than a moral one — and somebody has already assembled the studies. THE PASTORALIST WORK: PUBLICATIONS DEMONSTRATING PASTORALISTS' ESSENTIAL ROLE IN LAND GOVERNANCE AND THEIR CONTRIBUTION TO AFRICA'S SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT. Pastoralist land is the most easily reallocated in this file precisely because it looks unused. Published evidence that grazing is land governance rather than absence is the counter-argument, and it is free. AND THE FIGURE IT ORGANISES AROUND: IN A CONTINENT WHERE 70% OF THE POPULATION DEPENDS ON AGRICULTURE, SECURE ACCESS TO LAND AND SEED IS THE FOUNDATION. WHO IT SUITS: African farmer, pastoralist, fisherfolk and indigenous organisations — and any community group wanting into a continental network without a registration or a proposal. CAVEATS: AN ADVOCACY ALLIANCE, NOT A FUNDER OR A LEGAL SERVICE, AND MEMBERSHIP IS FOR ORGANISATIONS RATHER THAN INDIVIDUALS — the WhatsApp community is the route for a person. For the indigenous coordinating committee that is a core member here, South Africa's entry; for the pastoralist coalition and its regional focal points, Tanzania's PINGO's Forum entry; for the network whose African chapters are independent and admit individuals, Egypt's entry.

trackers.name: A free 24/7 digital security helpline for civil society that answers every request within two hours, in French, Arabic and Portuguese among ten languages — for groups already under attack as well as those preparing
trackers.desc: TWO HOURS, ANY HOUR, IN FRENCH OR ARABIC, FREE — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S MOROCCO ENTRY CARRIES A DIGITAL EMERGENCY FUND HOST, ITS EQUATORIAL GUINEA ENTRY THE PROTECTION GRANTS THAT PAY FOR DIGITAL SECURITY, AND ITS BENIN ENTRY THE 24-HOUR DEFENDER HELPLINE. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PUBLISHED RESPONSE TIME, WHICH IS THE FIND: WE RESPOND TO ALL REQUESTS WITHIN TWO HOURS. WE ARE A FREE-OF-CHARGE RESOURCE FOR CIVIL SOCIETY AROUND THE WORLD. A stated maximum, not a promise to be in touch. This file records emergency routes whose real answer is a fortnight; two hours is the number to hold them to, and it is the reason to save the contact before anything happens rather than searching for it while your accounts are being taken. THE HOURS AND THE LANGUAGES: 24/7 SERVICES WITH SUPPORT IN TEN LANGUAGES — ENGLISH, SPANISH, FRENCH, GERMAN, PORTUGUESE, RUSSIAN, TAGALOG, ARABIC, ITALIAN AND UKRAINIAN (EARLIER SOURCES LIST NINE, WITHOUT THE LAST). FRENCH, ARABIC AND PORTUGUESE all covered, at any hour. Francophone West and Central Africa, North Africa and the lusophone countries can all call in their working language — which this file has recorded again and again as the difference between a resource existing and a resource being usable. THE TWO STATES IT COVERS: IF YOU'RE AT RISK, WE CAN HELP YOU IMPROVE YOUR DIGITAL SECURITY PRACTICES TO KEEP OUT OF HARM'S WAY; IF YOU'RE ALREADY UNDER ATTACK, WE PROVIDE RAPID-RESPONSE EMERGENCY ASSISTANCE. Both doors, one number. Most groups only look for this after the phone is compromised; the same line handles the quiet preparation, and that call is free too. THE PUBLISHED TRIAGE PROCESS, WHICH TELLS YOU WHAT TO HAVE READY: EVERY REQUEST GOES THROUGH TRIAGE — AN INITIAL TWO-HOUR RESPONSE TO GATHER MORE DETAILS, VERIFICATION THAT THE REQUESTER BELONGS TO CIVIL SOCIETY, AND CONFIRMATION THAT THE HELPLINE CAN PROVIDE THE NEEDED SUPPORT — AFTER WHICH THE TEAM DESIGNS AND IMPLEMENTS A CUSTOMIZED SOLUTION. VERIFICATION THAT THE REQUESTER BELONGS TO CIVIL SOCIETY is the step that will slow an unknown village committee down. Being able to point to a network membership, a partner organisation or a published report shortens it — another reason the coalition entries in this file matter before a crisis rather than during one. HOW THE HELP IS PITCHED TO THE PERSON: SECURITY INCIDENT HANDLERS ARE THE FIRST LINE OF RESPONSE, ASSESSING EACH REQUEST AND DESIGNING TAILORED SOLUTIONS SUITED TO THE BENEFICIARY'S NEEDS, CAPACITIES, AND LEVEL OF DIGITAL KNOWLEDGE. LEVEL OF DIGITAL KNOWLEDGE, written into the method. Nobody is turned away for not understanding the question, which is the barrier that keeps rural organisers off technical helplines. THE JOINT ASSESSMENT IT OFFERS: THE HELPLINE WILL WALK YOU OR YOUR ORGANIZATION THROUGH ASSESSING THE RISKS YOU FACE IN YOUR WORK, AND TOGETHER WE'LL PRIORITIZE YOUR DIGITAL SECURITY NEEDS — RESOLVING EXISTING PROBLEMS, TEACHING SOME OF THE MOST IMPORTANT BEST PRACTICES, AND HELPING YOU GET INTO A SECURE MINDSET FOR THE FUTURE. A risk assessment done with you, free. Land and forest organisations rarely have one, and the mapping, membership lists and witness statements this file records them holding are exactly what an opponent wants. THE THREATS IT NAMES: TARGETED CYBER ATTACKS SUCH AS HACKING, PHISHING AND MALWARE DESIGNED TO STEAL SENSITIVE INFORMATION OR DISRUPT ACTIVITIES; SURVEILLANCE AND INTERCEPTION OF COMMUNICATIONS BY HOSTILE ACTORS SEEKING TO SUPPRESS DISSENT; AND ONLINE GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE. ONLINE GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE named as its own category. This file has recorded women organisers driven out of leadership by campaigns that were never physical, and there is a specialist route for it. THE SERVICES BEYOND THE EMERGENCY: EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES ON SECURITY PRACTICES; ASSISTANCE SECURING TECHNICAL INFRASTRUCTURE AND SOCIAL MEDIA; REFERRALS, CAPACITY-BUILDING, CONSULTATIONS AND TRAINING; TRAININGS AND WORKSHOPS; AND IN-PERSON ADVICE DURING CONFERENCES AND OTHER EVENTS. SECURING SOCIAL MEDIA is the practical one: a hijacked page is how a campaign's own supporters get fed false statements, and recovering an account is a specific thing to ask for. THE ACCREDITATION AND THE NETWORK BEHIND IT: THE HELPLINE IS A MEMBER OF A CIVIL SOCIETY COMPUTER EMERGENCY RESPONSE TEAM, AN ACCREDITED BODY FOCUSED ON IMPROVING THE INCIDENT RESPONSE CAPABILITIES OF CIVIL SOCIETY GROUPS — ITSELF AN INITIATIVE OF A RAPID RESPONSE NETWORK OF NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS, INTERNET CONTENT AND SERVICE PROVIDERS, AND INDIVIDUALS WHO CONTRIBUTE THEIR TIME AND RESOURCES. An accredited emergency response team for civil society, with service providers inside it. That is what lets a helpline get a platform or a host to act on your case rather than sending you to a support form. THE WIDER ORGANISATION'S OTHER ARM: IT DEFENDS THE DIGITAL RIGHTS OF AT-RISK COMMUNITIES BY PROVIDING LEGAL SUPPORT AND ADVOCATING FOR PUBLIC POLICIES THAT PROTECT ONLINE FREEDOMS. LEGAL SUPPORT on digital rights, alongside the technical line. For an organiser prosecuted over a post or an internet shutdown during a protest, those are the same organisation. AND THE ARGUMENT IT MAKES ABOUT COST: MAKING SERVICES AND SECURITY TOOLS AVAILABLE FREE OF CHARGE IS A KEY WAY TO SUPPORT CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS, WHICH ARE OFTEN CASH-STRAPPED AND CURRENTLY FACING A MORE COMPLEX FINANCIAL ENVIRONMENT. WHO IT SUITS: any African community organisation, land defender or journalist whose phones, accounts, documents or membership lists are at risk — before an incident as much as during one. CAVEATS: DIGITAL SECURITY ONLY, WITH A CIVIL-SOCIETY VERIFICATION STEP, AND IT ADVISES AND ASSISTS RATHER THAN FUNDING — for the money to buy equipment, use the protection grants. For those grants and their encrypted application, Equatorial Guinea's entry; for the 24-hour defender helpline and the protection cluster, Benin's and Morocco's entries.

trackers.name: An Indigenous-led fund whose approval committee is itself Indigenous, funding groups with or without state registration, accepting the project concept as written text, video or audio, and offering a ladder from a first grant to larger ones
trackers.desc: SEND THE PROPOSAL AS A VIDEO IF WRITING IS THE BARRIER — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC ENTRY COVERS THE FUND THAT WAIVES REGISTRATION, BANK ACCOUNT AND ID; ITS CHAD ENTRY THE INDIGENOUS-LED FUND ACCEPTING VIDEO APPLICATIONS; ITS GAMBIA ENTRY THE FUNDER PUBLISHING ITS INDIGENOUS-LED PERCENTAGES; ITS COMOROS ENTRY THE UNREGISTERED-COLLECTIVE FUND WITH SEVEN LANGUAGES; ITS SEYCHELLES BUCKET CARRIES A MINORITY RIGHTS HOST. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. THE REGISTRATION RULE, WHICH IS THE FIND: IT FUNDS PROJECTS IMPLEMENTED BY GRASSROOTS AND EMERGING GROUPS, WITH OR WITHOUT OFFICIAL REGISTRATION FROM THEIR STATE GOVERNMENT, AND IS THE FIRST SOURCE OF FUNDING THAT SOME ORGANIZATIONS AND COMMUNITIES HAVE EVER RECEIVED. WITH OR WITHOUT OFFICIAL REGISTRATION FROM THEIR STATE GOVERNMENT. Where the state refuses to register an Indigenous organisation — which this file has recorded as a deliberate tactic, not an oversight — that refusal does not reach this fund. WHO DECIDES, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: OUR FUND IS LED BY INDIGENOUS PEOPLES, AND THE PROJECTS ARE COLLECTIVELY APPROVED BY AN INTERNAL COMMITTEE ALSO MADE UP OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES — MANAGED BY INDIGENOUS STAFF. The people assessing the proposal are Indigenous themselves. That changes what needs explaining: a project premised on ritual practice, ancestral governance or a relationship to a place does not have to be translated into development language for a reviewer who has never encountered it. THE APPLICATION FORMAT: YOU MUST FILL OUT A QUESTIONNAIRE AND AT THE END ATTACH THE PROJECT CONCEPT WRITTEN, IN VIDEO, OR IN AUDIO FORMAT — WITH A SEVEN-QUESTION NOTE SUBMITTED TO A PUBLISHED EMAIL ADDRESS, AND VIDEO SUBMISSIONS UPLOADED TO A VIDEO PLATFORM AND SENT AS A LINK. Seven questions, and the concept itself can be spoken rather than written. An elder who holds the knowledge but does not write proposals can record the case in their own language and voice — which removes the literacy and drafting barrier that this file has recorded deciding who gets funded far more often than merit does. THE LANGUAGES: DETAILED PROPOSAL FORMS CAN BE SUBMITTED IN ENGLISH, AFRIKAANS, SETSWANA AND KHOEKHOEGOWAB FOR A SOUTHERN AFRICAN CALL — WITH AN EARLIER ROUND ACCEPTING ENGLISH, SPANISH, PORTUGUESE, AFRIKAANS, NEPALI, FRENCH OR RUSSIAN AMONG SEVERAL INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. SETSWANA AND KHOEKHOEGOWAB. Not colonial languages with a translation offer, but the languages the applicants actually speak, named on the form. That is rarer in this file than any funding amount. THE AMOUNTS AND THE LADDER: UP TO $12,000 USD TO GRASSROOTS INDIGENOUS-LED ORGANIZATIONS, COLLECTIVES AND TRADITIONAL GOVERNMENTS — WITH ONE AFRICAN CALL AWARDING UP TO $8,000, AND, UPON SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF AN INITIAL GRANT AND REPORTING, APPLICANTS MAY APPLY FOR SUBSEQUENT GRANTS OF UP TO $10,000. The ladder is conditional on reporting, which is the cheapest thing a small organisation can get right and the thing this file has recorded neglected most often. THE AFRICAN CALL ON RECORD AND ITS SUBJECTS: A CALL IN BOTSWANA, NAMIBIA AND SOUTH AFRICA PRIORITISING CLIMATE CHANGE SUCH AS REFORESTATION AND FLOOD PREVENTION; FOOD SOVEREIGNTY SUCH AS SEED BANKS, TRADITIONAL FOOD SYSTEMS AND FISHING AND HUNTING RIGHTS; INDIGENOUS ECONOMIES; GOVERNANCE BASED ON ANCESTRAL SYSTEMS; KNOWLEDGE TRANSFER FROM KNOWLEDGE KEEPERS TO YOUTH; AND INDIGENOUS SPIRITUALITIES INCLUDING THE PRACTICE OF RITUALS.
