GOVERNANCE BASED ON ANCESTRAL SYSTEMS and FISHING AND HUNTING RIGHTS are fundable subjects in their own right. A community strengthening the authority that actually decides about its land is doing the thing this file keeps identifying as decisive, and here it can be paid for directly rather than smuggled into a project budget. THE OPENING LEFT IN THAT LIST: NEVERTHELESS, APPLICANTS ARE ENCOURAGED TO SUBMIT PROPOSALS IN TOPICS OR THEMES IMPORTANT TO THEIR COMMUNITY — ANY PRIORITY OR SOLUTION IMPORTANT TO THEIR COMMUNITY. The priority list is not a fence. Say what the community actually needs, even if it is not on it. THE GEOGRAPHIC RULE: OPEN TO ANY COUNTRY WHERE THERE IS A PRESENCE OF INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES, WITH A SLIGHT PREFERENCE FOR NAMED COUNTRIES IN A GIVEN ROUND — AND A STATED PREFERENCE FOR PROPOSALS IN COUNTRIES WITHIN GEOGRAPHIC PROXIMITY TO STAFF, BECAUSE IT AIMS TO PERSONALLY VISIT THE MAJORITY OF PROJECTS IT FUNDS. Recorded plainly because it shapes the odds: any African country with Indigenous communities may apply, but rounds name particular countries and staff proximity is weighed. Watch for the call that names your region rather than applying cold. THE ADMINISTRATIVE CONDITION AND ITS ALTERNATIVE: APPLICANTS MUST BE AN INDIGENOUS NON-PROFIT GRASSROOTS COMMUNITY, ORGANIZATION OR GOVERNMENT WITH COLLECTIVE DECISION MAKING, AND MUST HAVE A BANK ACCOUNT IN THE NAME OF THE APPLICANT ORGANIZATION OR HAVE AN EXISTING WRITTEN AGREEMENT WITH A FISCAL SPONSOR. A bank account OR a fiscal sponsor. Registration is waived but money still has to land somewhere — so an unregistered community's practical first step is a written agreement with an organisation that will hold the funds, and that agreement is worth making before a call opens. WHO IS EXCLUDED: GOVERNMENT AGENCIES AND FOR-PROFIT ENTITIES ARE NOT ELIGIBLE — AND ALL APPLICANTS MUST BE INDIGENOUS-LED OR REPRESENT AN INDIGENOUS-LED PROJECT. THE QUESTION IT ASKS ABOUT DISTANCE: WHERE IS YOUR ORGANIZATION BASED IN RELATION TO THE COMMUNITY WHERE THE PROJECT WILL TAKE PLACE — WITH AN OPTION STATING THAT THE ORGANISATION IS BASED IN THE COMMUNITY WHERE THE PROJECT WILL TAKE PLACE. The form asks how far you are from the people you say you serve. A capital-city organisation cannot present itself as the community, and the village association is advantaged by answering honestly. AND THE RECORD AND THE RELATIONSHIP IT SEEKS: SINCE 2017, 392 PROJECTS IN 40 COUNTRIES THROUGH SMALL GRANTS AND A WRAP-AROUND APPROACH TOTALLING $2,219,369 DIRECTLY TO INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES, COLLECTIVES, ORGANIZATIONS AND TRADITIONAL GOVERNMENTS — SEEKING LONG-TERM RELATIONSHIPS AND PROGRESSIVE GROWTH TOWARDS SELF-SUFFICIENCY, PREDICATED ON A UN DECLARATION ON THE RIGHTS OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES. TRADITIONAL GOVERNMENTS receive money directly. A chieftaincy, council of elders or customary authority is a grantee category here, not a stakeholder to be consulted. WHO IT SUITS: African Indigenous communities, collectives and traditional authorities — including unregistered ones, and including those who would rather record their proposal than write it. CAVEATS: INDIGENOUS-LED APPLICANTS ONLY, A BANK ACCOUNT OR FISCAL SPONSOR IS REQUIRED, CALLS NAME PARTICULAR COUNTRIES, AND STAFF PROXIMITY IS WEIGHED — southern Africa is the named African focus on record. For the fund that waives the bank account too, the Central African Republic's entry; for unregistered collectives applying in seven languages, Comoros' entry.

trackers.name: ICFC (International Conservation Fund of Canada) — a conservation funder that has participated in land acquisitions for more than a dozen private reserves and aims for those reserves to be managed by local field partners — and which publishes the case for when buying the land is not necessary at all
trackers.desc: A DOZEN PRIVATE RESERVES BOUGHT — AND THEY SAY WHEN NOT TO BUY — name note, method and adjacency declared first: IN 2025 THIS ORGANISATION ADOPTED A SECOND OPERATING NAME; BOTH NAMES REFER TO THE SAME ORGANIZATION — SEARCH UNDER EITHER. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THREE HOSTS, INCLUDING THE NEW OPERATING NAME, AND FOUR SUBJECT SPELLINGS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL ABSENT. THIS FILE'S EQUATORIAL GUINEA ENTRY COVERS THE FUND THAT GRANTS PURCHASE MONEY, ITS SOUTH SUDAN ENTRY THE ORGANISATION THAT BUYS FARMS OUTRIGHT, ITS SÃO TOMÉ ENTRY THE CONSERVATION SERVITUDE. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE ACQUISITIONS ON RECORD, WHICH IS THE FIND: IT HAS PARTICIPATED IN LAND ACQUISITIONS FOR MORE THAN A DOZEN PRIVATE RESERVES OF HIGH CONSERVATION VALUE — UNDERTAKING LAND ACQUISITIONS OF SITES AT RISK AND RICH IN BIODIVERSITY, WITH THE GOAL OF HAVING PRIVATE RESERVES MANAGED BY LOCAL FIELD PARTNERS. PARTICIPATED IN is the word to notice: it goes in alongside others rather than funding a purchase alone. For a community whose parcel costs more than any single grant in this file, that is the model that reaches the price — several funders in one transaction, with a local organisation holding the result. WHEN BUYING IS NOT THE ANSWER, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: IN SOME AREAS, THE ACQUISITION OF LAND IS NOT REQUIRED SINCE LEGAL PROTECTION IS PRESENT — ONLY LOCAL SUPPORT TO NGOs FOR THEIR CONTINUITY WAS NEEDED. A land-buying organisation saying plainly that buying is often unnecessary. Where the ground already carries a protective designation, the money is better spent keeping the local organisation alive to enforce it — and CONTINUITY funding, the unglamorous cost of staying in existence between projects, is the hardest money to raise anywhere in this file. Check what protection your ground already has before costing a purchase. WHAT MAKES A SITE A TARGET: LANDS WITH THE PRESENCE OF THREATENED AND RARE SPECIES ARE POTENTIAL TARGETS — THOUGH IT FOCUSES ON THE TROPICAL SYSTEM IN GENERAL RATHER THAN PARTICULAR SPECIES, WITH ALL PROJECTS PROTECTING HABITAT FOR SPECIES UNDER SIGNIFICANT THREATS SUCH AS RAMPANT EGG HARVESTING AND ILLEGAL HUNTING. THE SYSTEM RATHER THAN THE SPECIES is a softer test than the Red List requirement recorded in this file's Equatorial Guinea entry. A site with no flagship animal has a route here that it does not have there. THE FOUR PROGRAMME AREAS IT SORTS PROJECTS INTO: LAND CONSERVATION, THREATENED SPECIES, A SHOREBIRD INITIATIVE, AND MARINE CONSERVATION. Marine and shorebird programmes as separate streams, so coastal and estuary ground — which this file has struggled to place with land-focused funders — has its own category. WHY IT WORKS THROUGH LOCAL BODIES, IN ITS OWN WORDS: KEY TO OUR SUCCESS IS OUR MODEL OF WORKING IN PARTNERSHIP WITH LOCALLY BASED CONSERVATION ORGANISATIONS — THEY KNOW BEST WHAT NEEDS DOING AND HOW TO GO ABOUT IT, AND THEY EXCEL AT ENGAGING LOCAL COMMUNITIES AND GOVERNMENT RELATIONS. GOVERNMENT RELATIONS named as a thing the local partner is better at. Where an international body would have to negotiate a concession or a designation from outside, the African organisation's existing relationships are treated as the asset — which is worth saying explicitly in an approach. WHERE IT WORKS: PROJECTS IN MORE THAN 30 COUNTRIES IN LATIN AMERICA, AFRICA AND ASIA, FOUNDED IN 2007 — WITH LARGE PROTECTED AREAS OF HUNDREDS OR THOUSANDS OF SQUARE KILOMETRES CONSERVED IN A NAMED EAST AFRICAN COUNTRY AND ELSEWHERE. THE SPEED IT CLAIMS: IT HAS THE CAPACITY TO QUICKLY EXPAND ITS WORK TO TAKE ADVANTAGE OF EXCELLENT OPPORTUNITIES, AND ITS SMALL STAFF WORKS WITH A SENSE OF URGENCY. Worth testing when a parcel comes to market with a short window. Most funders in this file cannot move at the speed of a land sale; this one says it can. HOW IT CHOOSES, PUBLISHED: IT MAINTAINS PROJECT SELECTION CRITERIA ON ITS OWN SITE, WITH DIRECT CONSERVATION ACTION AND LOCAL POPULATION ENGAGEMENT AMONG THE NAMED TOPICS — AND AFTER APPLYING THEM IT ASSESSES WHICH OPPORTUNITIES OFFER THE BEST VALUE FOR MONEY IN TERMS OF LASTING CONSERVATION GAINS, WHILE FACTORING IN RISK. VALUE FOR MONEY AND RISK, stated as the deciding test. That tells an applicant what to lead with: hectares secured per euro, and a credible answer to what could go wrong. THE CO-BENEFITS IT NAMES: STRIKING CO-BENEFITS IN CLIMATE MITIGATION AND ADAPTATION, AND BENEFITS FOR LOCAL AND INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES — LIVELIHOODS, ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL BENEFITS. THE RECORD IT PUBLISHES: 18 MILLION HECTARES CONSERVED, BENEFITING 2.7 MILLION PEOPLE AND 531 THREATENED SPECIES, WITH AN EARLIER FIGURE OF OVER 15 MILLION HECTARES — AND $8.2 MILLION SPENT ON CONSERVATION PROJECTS IN 2024. THE HONEST GEOGRAPHY, RECORDED PLAINLY: LATIN AMERICA REPRESENTED 61% OF PROGRAM COSTS IN 2024, WITH 12 NAMED LATIN AMERICAN COUNTRIES LISTED — SO AFRICA AND ASIA SHARE THE REMAINDER. Six pounds in ten go to Latin America. An African applicant is competing for a minority of the budget, and should say so to itself before investing weeks in a proposal — this file records that kind of arithmetic rarely being published at all. AND THE SISTER FUND AND ITS ADMISSION: A SEPARATE UNITED STATES BODY RAISES FUNDS FOR THE SAME LOCAL FIELD PARTNERS AND RELIES ON THIS ORGANISATION FOR MUCH OF THE PROJECT MANAGEMENT, KEEPING ADMINISTRATIVE COSTS EXTREMELY LOW BECAUSE IT IS CURRENTLY A VOLUNTEER RUN ORGANIZATION — STATING THAT THE ACTUAL CONSERVATION WORK IS BEING DONE BY OUR INTERNATIONAL FIELD PARTNERS ON THE GROUND, AND THAT IT SEEKS TO FUND LOCAL ORGANISATIONS. Two doors to the same partners, one Canadian and one American, and the American one is volunteer-run with near-zero overhead. Read beside this file's Benin entry on taking American donations: an African organisation with supporters in both countries has two established routes rather than a paperwork problem. WHO IT SUITS: locally based African conservation organisations with a site at risk — whether the answer is buying it, leasing it, or simply being funded to keep existing and enforce protection that already applies. CAVEATS: IT FUNDS AND PARTNERS WITH ESTABLISHED LOCAL ORGANISATIONS RATHER THAN COMMUNITIES DIRECTLY; ITS FRAME IS TROPICAL BIODIVERSITY, NOT COMMUNITY LAND CLAIMS; AND 61% OF ITS 2024 SPENDING WENT TO LATIN AMERICA. For the fund that grants purchase money and hands over the title, Equatorial Guinea's entry; for the organisation that buys farms itself, South Sudan's entry.

trackers.name: #MineAlert and #GreenAlert (Oxpeckers) — free map-and-alert tools that tell a resident which mining applications, water use licences and environmental impact assessments are live over their own area, with the subscribe-by-area steps published
trackers.desc: FIND OUT WHAT IS BEING APPLIED FOR OVER YOUR OWN GROUND, BEFORE IT IS DECIDED — method and adjacency declared first: FOUND WHILE VERIFYING A PLACEHOLDER IN THIS FILE'S ACCESS INITIATIVE ENTRY. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THREE HOSTS AND SIX DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL HOSTS AND ALL SIX FACTS ABSENT. THE PARENT NAME APPEARS IN TWO BUCKETS: THE SOUTH AFRICA ENTRY, READ IN FULL AND FOUND TO BE A ONE-LINE STUB NAMING NO TOOLS, AND THE GUINEA-BISSAU CODE FOR AFRICA ENTRY, WHICH IS A FUNDER OF THESE TOOLS AND A DIFFERENT SUBJECT. NEITHER IS RESTATED AND NEITHER HOST IS SHIPPED. THE ALERT, WHICH IS THE FIND: A CITIZEN-FOCUSED WEBSITE AND MOBILE APP THAT ALERTS RESIDENTS AND ORGANISATIONS TO MINING APPLICATIONS AND LICENCES IN THEIR REGIONS — AND A SISTER TOOL THAT LETS YOU TRACK AND SHARE ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT ASSESSMENTS THE SAME WAY. Almost every entry in this file helps a community AFTER it has learned about a project. This one is how it learns. An application is a public document that sits in a register nobody reads; an alert keyed to your own coordinates turns that into a letter arriving before the comment window closes. HOW A PERSON ACTUALLY USES IT, PUBLISHED STEP BY STEP: OPEN THE SITE; USE MY LOCATION TO FIND PROJECTS IN YOUR AREA, OR REGISTER WITHOUT LOCATION SERVICES; OPEN THE MAP; CREATE ALERT; THEN SUBSCRIBE BY AREA, MINE, COMPANY, COMMODITY OR TYPE OF MINE — AND ALERTS ARRIVE AUTOMATICALLY. Five steps, published. SUBSCRIBE BY COMPANY is the one organisers miss: if a company has already taken land in the next district, an alert on its name tells you when it files near you. WHAT ELSE IS ON THE MAP: A MINING LICENCES LAYER FROM SEVERAL COLLATED DATASETS; A WATER LICENCES LAYER SHOWING WATER USE LICENCES AND APPLICATIONS FOR MINING DEVELOPMENTS AGAINST THE COUNTRY'S FRESHWATER PRIORITY AREAS; AND WATER THREATS LAYERS SHOWING THE VULNERABILITY OF FRESHWATER RESOURCES TO MINING, BUILT FROM THE NATIONAL MINE WATER ATLAS COMPILED BY THE WATER RESEARCH COMMISSION. THE WATER LICENCE IS THE SEPARATE PERMISSION, and it is often the weaker one. A mine may hold its mineral right and still need water it has not been granted; a community that can see both applications on one map can object to the one that is actually vulnerable. WHAT IT IS FOR, IN ITS OWN WORDS: TO EQUIP MINING-AFFECTED COMMUNITIES WITH THE RIGHT AMOUNT OF INFORMATION TO MAKE THEIR VOICES HEARD — FREE, FAST AND EASY TO USE, BRIDGING THE TRANSPARENCY GAP BETWEEN GOVERNMENT, ORGANISATIONS RALLYING FOR CHANGE, AND ORDINARY CITIZENS. WHAT A REGISTERED USER GETS: ALERTS ON ALL THE MINING COMPANIES OR GEOGRAPHIES THEY ARE INTERESTED IN, TO USE TO PETITION FOR CHANGE — WITH ACCESS TO MINING LICENCES, WATER USE LICENCES AND SOCIAL AND LABOUR PLANS. SOCIAL AND LABOUR PLANS are the commitments a company made to the community to get its licence — housing, jobs, local procurement. Read beside this file's Republic of Congo entry on the schedule of obligations: the plan is the promise, and almost nobody checks it against what was built. WHY IT WAS BUILT, AND THE GAP IT NAMES: A DRAFT NATIONAL MINING CHARTER WAS SILENT ABOUT THE POLLUTER PAYS PRINCIPLE, SET NO GOALS FOR WATER CONSUMPTION AND DESTRUCTION BY MINES, AND MADE NO PROVISION FOR MINE CLOSURE — WITH GRIEVANCE MECHANISMS FOR LOCAL COMMUNITIES, THEIR RIGHT TO SAY NO TO MINING, AND EASY ACCESS TO RELEVANT EXPERTISE ALSO ABSENT. Four omissions named in a national charter, and the tool was built because of them. That list is a template for reading your own country's mining policy: closure, water, polluter-pays, grievance. If those four are missing, the same gap exists. THE OTHER TOOLS ON THE SAME SHELF: A TRACKER FOR BIODIVERSITY THREATS CAUSED BY MINING LICENCES ACROSS AFRICA; A POWER TRACKER FOR RENEWABLE AND COAL-BASED ENERGY SOURCES; A GLOBAL AND REGIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL-CRIME TRACKER WITH EUROPE AND ASIA EDITIONS; A CLIMATE TRACKER; AND TRACKERS FOR POACHING COURT CASES AND INCIDENTS SINCE 2010. The biodiversity layer is continental, not national — so a community outside the home country still has something to search. WHO BUILDS AND PAYS FOR IT: A PROJECT OF AN INVESTIGATIVE ENVIRONMENTAL JOURNALISM CENTRE, SUPPORTED BY A CONTINENTAL CIVIC-TECH NETWORK AND A NATIONAL OPEN SOCIETY FOUNDATION, DEVELOPED BY A NAMED TECHNICAL PARTNER. WHAT THE PARENT NEWSROOM IS: A CORE NEWSROOM COMBINING TRADITIONAL INVESTIGATIVE REPORTING WITH DATA-DRIVEN JOURNALISM, GEO-NARRATIVE TECHNIQUES AND DIGITAL ENGAGEMENT TOOLS, BOLSTERED BY FELLOWS, WITH SPECIAL DIGITAL PROJECTS DESIGNED TO CREATE PUBLIC RESOURCES TO IMPROVE CITIZEN ACCESS TO ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE. A newsroom that builds public tools rather than only publishing stories. Worth approaching with a documented local problem: they run a fellowship and take investigations. WHAT THE MAPPING IS MEANT TO ENABLE: CITIZENS AND COMMUNITIES PARTICIPATING MEANINGFULLY IN DECISION-MAKING, TRACKING THE PROGRESS OF PROJECTS, NOTIFYING STAKEHOLDERS AND AUTHORITIES IF SOMETHING SEEMS AMISS, AND TAKING PREVENTATIVE MEASURES TO AVOID EXPOSURE TO POSSIBLE RISKS. THE DATA IT WAS BUILT FROM: THE MOST RECENT MINING APPLICATIONS AND LICENCES IN ONE PROVINCE, THE LATEST DATASETS FROM THE MINERALS DEPARTMENT, AND A DATASET FROM AN AFRICAN MINES SOURCE. AND THE HONEST LIMIT: THE ALERTING IS BUILT ON WHATEVER DATASETS THE GOVERNMENT HAS RELEASED, SO COVERAGE FOLLOWS DISCLOSURE — THE MINING AND EIA TOOLS ARE STRONGEST IN ONE COUNTRY, WITH THE BIODIVERSITY LAYER EXTENDING ACROSS AFRICA. Filed with that limit attached: an empty map is not proof that nothing is being applied for near you, only that nothing has been disclosed in a machine-readable form. Where the map is blank, the records request is still the route. WHO IT SUITS: anyone who wants to know what is being applied for over their own ground before it is granted, and organisers who want an alert on a company that is moving through a region. CAVEATS: THE UNDERLYING LICENCE DATA IS STRONGEST IN ONE SOUTHERN AFRICAN COUNTRY; IT ALERTS AND MAPS BUT DOES NOT OBJECT, LITIGATE OR FUND; AND ITS COVERAGE DEPENDS ENTIRELY ON GOVERNMENT DISCLOSURE. For the schedule of obligations a company owes your village, the Republic of Congo entry; for the civic-tech network that co-funds these tools, the Guinea-Bissau entry.

trackers.name: Guamina (Friends of the Earth Mali)
trackers.desc: The Malian member of Friends of the Earth International, based in Bamako. Its work covers desertification, mining, sustainable agriculture, food security and ecological debt, alongside training and literacy courses delivered in local languages and a particular focus on the status of women. WHO TO ENLIST: one of very few points of contact in Mali for a community facing a mining or land-use problem, and a route into the wider Friends of the Earth Africa network. Domain unverified: Guamina appears in Friends of the Earth International's own member directory at foei.org with a Bamako postal address and telephone number but no website listed, so reach it through that entry. Guamina has no website of its own, so the link is Friends of the Earth International's member-group page for Mali, which publishes its address and telephone numbers: Hamdallaye près du pont Diafarana, Rue 42 porte 232, 2744 Bamako, on +223 20 80 01 16 or +223 76 11 83 38. It takes part in FoEI's campaigns on desertification and mining as well as sustainable agriculture, food security and ecological debt, and separately runs training and literacy courses in local languages — which is why it can reach communities a capital-city organisation cannot.

trackers.name: Section des comptes de la Cour suprême du Mali
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Mali — audits government accounts and the use of public money.

trackers.name: ITIE Mali
trackers.desc: National Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative body — discloses oil, gas and mining revenues, contracts and licences in Mali.

trackers.name: Mali — Guichet Unique API-Mali
trackers.desc: National company registry; the API-Mali one-stop window centralises company formalisation & RCCM immatriculation (within 72h) and investment-code approvals, Mali. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Mali — Budget de l’État (budget.gouv.ml)
trackers.desc: National budget-transparency portal of the Ministry of Finance; lets citizens explore the State budget, expenditure & revenue data, Mali. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Mali.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: ECOWAS Court of Justice — file directly, but sue the State
trackers.desc: A COURT YOU CAN REACH WITHOUT EXHAUSTING DOMESTIC REMEDIES. The ECOWAS Community Court of Justice has held human rights jurisdiction since 2005 and has broad access and standing rules permitting individuals and NGOs to bypass national courts and file directly. THE PRECEDENT: in SERAP v Federal Republic of Nigeria (ECW/CCJ/APP/08/09) the Court dismissed all three preliminary objections — no locus standi, no jurisdiction, statute-barred — and rejected the government's attempt to exclude an Amnesty International report from the evidence. NGO research was admitted as evidence, which matters when no state data exists. It found violations of articles 1 and 24 of the African Charter — article 24: ‘all peoples shall have the right to a general satisfactory environment favourable to their development’ — and of article 21, the right to natural wealth and resources. THE FAULT WAS AN OMISSION: the state ‘defaulted in its duties in terms of vigilance and diligence’, and ‘the omission to act and to prevent damage to the environment characterises the violation’. It ordered restoration within the shortest possible time and measures to prevent further damage, citing the ICJ that the environment ‘is not an abstraction but represents the living space, the quality of life and the very health of human beings, including generations unborn’. THE LIMIT THAT DECIDES WHO YOU SUE: the Court held it had no jurisdiction over the private oil corporations, which were struck from the suit. You sue the State for failing to regulate; you cannot sue the company here — naming one as respondent loses that part of the case. AND PLAN FOR ENFORCEMENT: commentary records the Court did not identify a means for Nigeria to implement the ruling, and the ICJ later wrote to the President pressing for enforcement — judgment is the start of an enforcement campaign, not a self-executing remedy. Proposals to require exhaustion of domestic remedies were rejected by ECOWAS experts and Heads of Government, so the direct-access rule has been tested and held. VERIFY MEMBERSHIP BEFORE FILING: this state has been reported as withdrawing from ECOWAS. This entry does not resolve that question — confirm current membership and the Court's jurisdiction over your state before relying on this route, because withdrawal, if effective, would remove it.

trackers.name: ORFAO — comparative land-law tables, and a directive in draft
trackers.desc: COMPARATIVE LEGAL TABLES FOR YOUR COUNTRY AND ITS NEIGHBOURS, IN ONE DOCUMENT. The Observatoire Régional du Foncier Rural en Afrique de l'Ouest (ORFAO), hosted by UEMOA, publishes a regional study on rural land markets containing side-by-side ‘cadre légal comparé’ tables — one covering Bénin, Burkina Faso, Côte d'Ivoire and Sénégal, another Guinée-Bissau, Mali, Niger and Togo — plus typologies of direct and indirect interventions in land markets and a table of regulatory issues and families of instruments. If you need to know what instrument exists in your country and whether a neighbour has a stronger one, that is the document — comparative tables let a campaign point to a neighbour's provision as an achievable ask rather than a novelty. A WINDOW IS OPENING: on 26 June 2026 in Ouagadougou the UEMOA ministers for urbanisme, habitat, domaines et cadastre approved a draft directive to harmonise rules on immatriculation foncière, accès au titre de propriété and a système d'information foncière, aiming at a common framework of land governance. BE PRECISE ABOUT STATUS: that was a DRAFT directive approved by ministers, not an adopted and transposed instrument — check adoption and transposition before relying on it. But transposition is the moment domestic land law is reopened in each state, and that is when community provisions can be argued for. FOR A GRAZING OR TRANSHUMANCE DISPUTE: a regional pastoral situation bulletin covers 11 West African countries with the support of decentralised technical services — an evidence source drawing on the same services you would otherwise approach one by one. RECORDED PLAINLY: cattle theft is documented as a driver of conflict and instability in the Sahel, so a land dispute here may sit inside a security context that changes what is safe to do. And confirm your state's current ECOWAS standing — several members are recorded as suspended.

trackers.name: CMAT — five farmer and jurist organisations in one convergence against land grabbing, running a legal clinic for the dispossessed
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Convergence Malienne contre les Accaparements de Terres, formed in 2012 and formalised in 2013, which joins five umbrella organisations — the farmers' professional associations (AOPP), the Coalition des Alternatives Africaines (CAD-Mali), the national peasant coordination (CNOP), the association of the dispossessed (UACDDDD), and the Ligue des Jeunes Juristes pour le Développement Humain. That last member is the point: the convergence has lawyers inside it, and one of its stated objectives is to run a legal clinic for victims of expropriation, eviction and land grabbing. ITS STATED AIMS ARE UNUSUALLY OPERATIONAL: enable victims of expropriation and eviction to know and assert their rights; stop evictions and expropriations legally and legitimately; and demand reparation for both material and immaterial damage. It supports named village communities through their disputes, and its own estimate is that more than a million hectares have been grabbed in a country where the agricultural land law it pressed for was finally passed in 2017. It has also run training for communities on the UN declaration on peasants' rights, and published a comparative analysis of Mali's various natural resource codes — useful because, as its own briefing puts it, Mali has no single legal instrument covering agricultural land: the provisions are scattered across many texts, and that vagueness is what makes customary holders easy to dispossess. WHO IT SUITS: villages and urban neighbourhoods facing expropriation, eviction or an investor allocation. CAVEATS: a coalition rather than a service provider — approach is through a member organisation, and no intake route, fee or clinic timetable was published; its own account records severe repression of protesting communities, including arrests and long arbitrary detention, which is context a community should weigh.

trackers.name: CNOP-Mali — supports the village land commissions that let a village delimit its own terroir under the 2017 agricultural land law
trackers.desc: WHO GETS YOUR VILLAGE COMMISSION WORKING: the Coordination Nationale des Organisations Paysannes du Mali (CNOP), created in May 2002 as a framework for exchange and joint action between Malian farmers' organisations, active in policy dialogue with the state and in denouncing land-grab cases, notably in the Office du Niger zone; it hosted the international peasant conference against land grabbing at Nyéléni in November 2011. WHAT IT IS DOING NOW THAT A VILLAGE CAN USE: in February 2025 it convened the first steering committee of a project on SUPPORTING THE LAND AND FOREST SECURITY OF COMMUNITIES THROUGH THE LAND COMMISSIONS (COFO), bringing civil society, ministries and technical services together on the commissions' role in preventing and resolving land conflicts and protecting community land and natural resources. THE INSTRUMENT BEHIND IT: the agricultural land law of April 2017 recognises the land rights of rural communities and puts VILLAGE LAND COMMISSIONS at the centre — for the first time letting villages DELIMIT THEIR OWN TERROIR; a CNOP staffer's diagnosis of why this was needed is exact — the state had never put in place any mechanism for getting customary rights recognised. Implementing decrees were adopted in late March. ASK WHETHER YOUR VILLAGE HAS A COMMISSION FONCIÈRE VILLAGEOISE AND WHETHER IT HAS DELIMITED THE TERROIR — that delimitation is the document that answers an investor's map. THE HONEST WARNING FROM THE MOVEMENT ITSELF: campaigners record that the bill went from 180 articles to 49 during adoption, losing coherence and clarity precisely on the application of customary rights and the roles of the village land commissions — so expect the text to be thinner than the promise, and press for the implementing detail. WHO IT SUITS: Malian villages and farmers' organisations wanting their terroir delimited and their customary rights recognised, especially in the Office du Niger zone. CAVEATS: a farmers' movement and policy organisation, not a law firm — for legal advice and aid it works alongside the jurists' league inside the CMAT convergence, whose entry is also in this file; Mali's security situation constrains fieldwork in much of the country. WHY THIS IS A LAND-HOLDING INSTRUMENT AND NOT ONLY AN ADVISORY ONE: THE DELIMITED TERROIR IS THE ASSET. Once a village has delimited its terroir through the commission, it holds a bounded, officially acknowledged area attached to the village rather than to individuals — which is what an investor, a neighbouring village or a state service must then negotiate against. Delimit before you are approached, not after: every instrument in this file that works — Senegal's reserves, Cameroon's convention, the Congolese CFCL, Ethiopia's Guassa — was in place BEFORE the project arrived, and the ones that failed were attempted after.

trackers.name: ANICT and the FNACT — Mali's national fund for local-authority investment, five windows, 37.9 billion FCFA in one year, and your commune is the applicant
trackers.desc: WHERE THE MONEY FOR LOCAL PROJECTS SITS: the Agence Nationale d'Investissement des Collectivités Territoriales (ANICT), a public administrative establishment created by loi n°0042 of 7 July 2000 to manage the subsidies allocated to local investments carried out UNDER THE PROJECT OWNERSHIP OF THE TERRITORIAL COLLECTIVITIES, and to guarantee certain loans they contract. It runs the FONDS NATIONAL D'APPUI AUX COLLECTIVITÉS TERRITORIALES (FNACT), which has FIVE WINDOWS covering investment, training and support to the collectivities' functioning. THE APPLICANT IS YOUR COMMUNE, NOT YOU — which is exactly why a village should know this exists: the money for a borehole, a road or a market is already allocated to your local authority, and the lever is the mayor and the communal council, not a donor. One window worth naming: the Dotation d'Investissement affectée au Financement du Développement Économique Régional (DIN-DER), placed at the disposal of Regional Councils expressly for projects of economic interest that valorise THE PROTECTION AND VALORISATION OF NATURAL RESOURCES and improve access to goods and services. THE SCALE, PUBLISHED IN ITS OWN ANNUAL REPORT: in 2024 the FNACT was funded to 37,905,274,755 FCFA — the Malian state providing the largest share (22.6 billion for the regions' FNACT budget plus 6.6 billion via the special investment budget), with KfW, Denmark, the World Bank and UNCDF completing it — financing 140 PROJECTS across all regions, with emphasis on Koulikoro, Ménaka and Nioro. Performance-linked grants of 230 to 256 million FCFA per commune have been awarded under a conditional performance programme, and ANICT publishes which dossiers were judged compliant — in one regional round, 32 of 40 submitted. Ask your commune what it submitted, and whether it was judged compliant; the list is public. WHO IT SUITS: Malian villages and communal councillors seeking financing for local infrastructure or natural-resource projects. CAVEATS: THE COLLECTIVITY IS THE BENEFICIARY, NOT THE COMMUNITY DIRECTLY, so this is a lever over your mayor rather than a grant you can win; security conditions restrict verification visits in several regions. For village land commissions and terroir delimitation, Mali's CNOP entry; for the land-grab convergence and its lawyers, CMAT.

trackers.name: Mali's named organisations — AMEDD which brokers between communities and banks, AMRED which holds a government accord-cadre, AMEPANE which counts wildlife with the forestry service, and the women jurists' association
trackers.desc: FOUR MALIAN ORGANISATIONS, EACH DOING SOMETHING DIFFERENT A COMMUNITY NEEDS: ASSOCIATION MALIENNE D'EVEIL AU DÉVELOPPEMENT DURABLE (AMEDD, ameddmali.org), based at KOUTIALA, working SINCE 1998 on ecology, economy and the social, WORKING CLOSELY WITH THE COLLECTIVITÉS TERRITORIALES AND RURAL ORGANISATIONS, ESPECIALLY THEIR UNIONS AT LOCAL AND REGIONAL LEVEL. ITS STATED ROLE IS TO FACILITATE COLLABORATIVE RELATIONS BETWEEN CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, LOCAL ENTREPRENEURS — BANKS, ECONOMIC OPERATORS AND OTHERS — RESEARCH INSTITUTIONS, LOCAL AUTHORITIES AND STATE PUBLIC SERVICES, with four governing principles including THE PARTICIPATION OF LOCAL POPULATIONS and THE PERPETUATION OF PROJECTS AND RESULTS, and a stated objective to CREATE APTITUDES AND KNOW-HOW IN GRASSROOTS ORGANISATIONS AND THEIR UNIONS FOR AUTONOMOUS AND QUALIFIED DEVELOPMENT OF THEIR OWN POTENTIAL. An organisation whose declared job is to introduce a village union to a BANK is rare in this file — most brokers connect communities to donors. If your group needs credit rather than a grant, that is the door, and AMEDD works through the unions rather than around them. ASSOCIATION MALIENNE DE RECHERCHE SUR L'ENVIRONNEMENT ET LE DÉVELOPPEMENT (AMRED), Rue Nelson Mandela, Immeuble Nyogondeme So, Hippodrome, BAMAKO — which HAS AN ACCORD-CADRE D'ONG WITH THE GOVERNMENT OF MALI, working on environmental problems, drinking water and energy for disadvantaged areas, and socio-economic development including microfinance, through studies and research, support and advice, and training and awareness. A framework agreement with the state is what lets an NGO be received rather than merely heard. ASSOCIATION MALIENNE POUR LA PROTECTION DE LA NATURE (AMEPANE), which with a partner association and IN CLOSE COOPERATION WITH THE DIRECTION NATIONALE DES EAUX ET FORÊTS RAN A PROGRAMME OF FAUNAL INVENTORIES IN THE PROTECTED AREAS OF THE BAFING-FALÉMÉ ZONE, tied to the creation of a transboundary protected area there. Counting the animals alongside the forestry service is how a boundary case gets built — the inventory is the evidence, and doing it WITH the state means the state cannot dispute its own numbers. AND FOR COUNSEL: the ASSOCIATION DES JURISTES MALIENNES (AJM), OFFICIALLY ESTABLISHED 1988, AN APOLITICAL ORGANISATION whose membership is AROUND FIFTY WOMEN LAWYERS, SOLICITORS, MAGISTRATES AND JUDGES, promoting and protecting women's rights in Malian law, and a member of a national women's rights group. Fifty women jurists including sitting magistrates is a professional network, not a charity — for a widow's or a woman's land claim in Mali, this is the first call. WHO IT SUITS: Malian village unions, communities near Bafing-Falémé, and women with a land or inheritance claim. CAVEATS: SMALL NATIONAL NGOs; confirm current operations given the security situation. For the village land commissions and delimiting your terroir before you are approached, Mali's CNOP entry; for five farmer and jurist organisations in one convergence, CMAT; for local-authority money, ANICT.

trackers.name: Sahel Eco, Bamako — a foreign NGO's Mali programme handed over to Malians in 2004, holding a national water-initiative secretariat, plus the CAFO and regional NGO coordinations
trackers.desc: THE NGO THAT WAS HANDED OVER TO MALIANS, WHICH IS A MODEL AS MUCH AS AN ADDRESS: SAHEL ECO IS A MALIAN NGO CREATED IN 2004 BY THE ORGANISATIONAL TRANSFORMATION OF A BRITISH NGO'S MALI PROGRAMME — WHICH HAD WORKED IN THE COUNTRY SINCE 1989 — INTO A NATIONAL AND AUTONOMOUS STRUCTURE, at HAMDALLAYE ACI 2000, RUE 402, BP 259, BAMAKO, with TWO PUBLISHED TELEPHONE NUMBERS and an email. Its stated VISION IS TO BE A REFERENCE AFRICAN NGO IN ENVIRONMENTAL GOVERNANCE, its MISSION TO WORK WITH THE POPULATIONS OF MALI AND OF NEIGHBOURING WEST AFRICAN COUNTRIES TO IMPROVE THEIR STANDARD OF LIVING THROUGH BETTER MANAGEMENT OF THE ENVIRONMENT, its domain ENVIRONMENT AND RURAL ECONOMY, and its slogan simply REVERDIR LE SAHEL. An international programme converted into a Malian-owned organisation is the succession this file keeps finding missing elsewhere. If a foreign body is working on your land, ask what its handover plan is — Sahel Eco is the precedent that it can be done, with the staff and the address kept. WHAT IT HOLDS: SAHEL ECO PROVIDES THE SECRETARIAT OF A WATER INITIATIVE WHOSE PROJECTS ARE IMPLEMENTED BY A CONSORTIUM OF NGOs, working on integrated water management in selected zones, strengthening actor movements at national and regional level, and developing an area of influence beyond the initiative itself to secure impact at larger scale. A Malian NGO holding the secretariat of a multi-NGO consortium is who convenes the others. If you need several organisations behind one question, ask the secretariat, not each member. WHAT IT DOES ON THE GROUND: it runs a TREES FOR LIVELIHOODS PROJECT with a named project chief, supporting NON-TIMBER FOREST PRODUCT ENTREPRENEURS and reporting publicly on THE CONSTRAINTS AND CHALLENGES THOSE ENTREPRENEURS FACE; and it has handed over completed works on HARIMA — PASTORAL HALTING-PLACES (GÎTES D'ÉTAPES) AND WAITING ZONES — IN THE COMMUNE OF SIO. Halting-places and waiting zones are physical infrastructure for herders, built and formally received. In a country whose land conflicts are largely pastoral, a built and handed-over gîte d'étape is a claim on a route that a map alone is not. AND THE STANDING FORUMS, WHICH ARE WHERE A REGIONAL QUESTION IS RAISED: THE COORDINATION RÉGIONALE DES ONGs AND THE COORDINATION RÉGIONALE DE LA CAFO — the coordination of women's associations and NGOs — PROVIDE THE FRAMEWORKS FOR EXCHANGE FOR CIVIL SOCIETY ACTORS IN THE REGIONS, alongside cultural events that carry discussions on integrated water resource management. It is recorded that the first such event was where TRADITIONAL MODES OF WATER RESOURCE MANAGEMENT AND THEIR LINKS WITH MALI'S CURRENT WATER CODE WERE DISCUSSED — A DIALOGUE BETWEEN LOCAL KNOWLEDGE AND MODERN LEGISLATION DESCRIBED AS A MAJOR ELEMENT FOR ACTORS' OWNERSHIP. Regional exchange spaces are few, and cultural festivals double as them. If there is a festival in your region, that is where the water and land conversation actually happens — go to it with your question prepared. ALSO NAMED: MALI FOLKECENTER NYETAA, and SOLIDARITÉ INTERNATIONALE POUR L'AFRIQUE (SIA-Mali), A MALIAN NATIONAL NGO CREATED 2005 UNDER ACCORD-CADRE N°02127, apolitical and non-profit, whose mission is PROMOTING THE ACTIVE AND RESPONSIBLE PARTICIPATION OF RURAL COMMUNITIES IN THEIR OWN DEVELOPMENT, targeting young farmers' organisations and women's groupings. WHO IT SUITS: Malian pastoralists, forest-product producers, women's groupings, and communities needing several NGOs behind one question. CAVEATS: CONFIRM CURRENT OPERATIONS given the security situation. For the broker that introduces a village union to a bank, Mali's AMEDD entry; for fifty women jurists including magistrates, the AJM; for delimiting your terroir before you are approached, CNOP; for local-authority money, ANICT.

trackers.name: CAFO — 2,500+ member associations represented in every region and cercle of Mali, with its Bamako door number, and the interface it runs between members and the public authorities
trackers.desc: TWO THOUSAND FIVE HUNDRED MEMBERS, IN EVERY CERCLE — on the numbers this is the largest membership body recorded anywhere in this file's African record: CAFO, THE COORDINATION DES ASSOCIATIONS ET ONG FÉMININES DU MALI, WAS CREATED ON 20 OCTOBER 1991 BY FOUR WOMEN'S ASSOCIATIONS AND OBTAINED ITS RÉCÉPISSÉ ON 24 MARCH 1992 UNDER N° 0244/MAT-DNAT. IT IS EFFECTIVELY REPRESENTED IN ALL THE REGIONS AND IN ALL THE CERCLES OF THE NATIONAL TERRITORY, AND COUNTED MORE THAN 2,500 MEMBER ASSOCIATIONS AND NGOs, OF WHICH MORE THAN 500 IN BAMAKO. Every cercle. That is the administrative unit below the region, which means CAFO has a presence in the district your village belongs to — not in the capital, in your district. Four founding associations became two and a half thousand in twenty years, and the récépissé number is printed, which is the document this file tells you to demand from anyone. THE ADDRESS IS PUBLISHED TO THE DOOR NUMBER: COURA BOLIBANA, RUE 376, PORTE 63, BP E 194, BAMAKO, WITH A TELEPHONE, A FAX AND AN EMAIL. AND THE TWO FUNCTIONS ARE THE REASON TO WRITE: IT BRINGS TECHNICAL SUPPORT TO ITS MEMBERS THROUGH APPUI-CONSEIL AND ORIENTATION IN THE MATTER OF THE SEARCH FOR FINANCING — AND IT ASSURES THE INTERFACE BETWEEN ITS MEMBERS AND THE PUBLIC AUTHORITIES. Help finding money, and a standing interface with the state. Those are the two things a village women's association cannot build for itself, and CAFO's own description says it supplies both. Join first, then ask — membership is what turns the interface into yours. ITS MISSION IS TO CONTRIBUTE TO VALORISING THE STATUS OF WOMEN BY THE REGROUPING AND COORDINATION OF MEMBERS' ACTIONS AND THE INFLUENCE OF POLICIES, and its first stated objective is TO BRING THE WOMEN OF MEMBER ASSOCIATIONS AND NGOs TO COLLABORATE WITHIN AN ORGANISED, CREDIBLE STRUCTURE SERVING THEM AS A FRAMEWORK OF MOBILISATION, CONCERTATION, TRAINING AND ACTION. It TAKES POSITIONS CLEARLY ON THE GREAT NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL QUESTIONS AND EXERTS PRESSURE ON THE PUBLIC POWERS TO SERVE WOMEN'S INTERESTS. A body that says openly it pressures the public authorities, and has members in every cercle, is a national campaign infrastructure that already exists. If land is being taken and the women of your area are affected, this is the structure that can carry it beyond your commune. AND IT IS HONEST ABOUT ITS OWN MONEY, WHICH IS WORTH READING BEFORE YOU DEPEND ON IT: ITS FINANCING IS CONSTITUTED THROUGH PROJECTS OR ACTION PROGRAMMES AND FOR THE MOST PART CAME FROM A FOREIGN EMBASSY AND A UN AGENCY, WITH MINISTRIES HELPING IMPLEMENT TRAINING SESSIONS — AND A PROGRAMME WAS PUT IN PLACE TO DIVERSIFY THE SOURCES OF FINANCING. Project-based funding from two main donors is a fragility the organisation itself named and acted on. Ask what is currently funded before you plan around it. THE FORMS THAT ALREADY EXIST IN MALI, WHICH IS WHAT A VILLAGE NEEDS BEFORE INVENTING ONE: the national civil society record names, among others, the ASSOCIATION VILLAGEOISE (AV); the ASSOCIATION DE SANTÉ COMMUNAUTAIRE (ASACO); the ASSOCIATION DES ORGANISATIONS PROFESSIONNELLES PAYSANNES (AOPP); the ASSEMBLÉE PERMANENTE DES CHAMBRES D'AGRICULTURE (APECAM); ACTION POUR LA RECHERCHE ET LE DÉVELOPPEMENT DES INITIATIVES LOCALES (ARDIL); the CELLULE D'APPUI AU DÉVELOPPEMENT À LA BASE (CADB); and the COMITÉ DE CONCERTATION ET D'APPUI AUX ORGANISATIONS NON GOUVERNEMENTALES (CCA-ONG). ASSOCIATION VILLAGEOISE is a recognised category with its own acronym in the national record. A Malian village does not need to invent a legal form — the AV already is one, and AOPP is the peasant professional organisation that speaks for farmers nationally. A national directory also lists Malian organisations with STREET ADDRESS TO THE DOOR NUMBER, TELEPHONE, FAX AND EMAIL, sorted by category including CSO and TRAINING AND RESEARCH. WHO IT SUITS: Malian women's associations anywhere in the country, village associations choosing a form, and anyone needing help finding financing. CAVEATS: SOME FIGURES AND CONTACTS DATE FROM PUBLISHED RECORDS OF EARLIER YEARS, AND MALI'S SECURITY SITUATION AFFECTS OPERATIONS — confirm before travelling. For the NGO handed over to Malians in 2004 and the regional coordinations, Mali's Sahel Eco entry; for the broker that introduces a village union to a bank, AMEDD; for fifty women jurists including magistrates, the AJM; for delimiting your terroir before you are approached, CNOP; for local-authority money, ANICT.

trackers.name: LandMark — the global platform that maps community land to prove it is not empty, showing 78.9% of Africa held under customary tenure and only 21% formally recognised, with impact analysis needing no mapping expertise and an open route to submit your boundary
trackers.desc: SEVENTY-EIGHT PER CENT OF AFRICA, AND MOST OF IT UNRECOGNISED — placement note first: THIS IS A GLOBAL PLATFORM, FILED UNDER MALI ONLY BECAUSE THIS FILE HAS NO GLOBAL KEY AND THIS BUCKET CARRIED NO LAND-DATA RESOURCE. IT COVERS EVERY AFRICAN COUNTRY. THE NUMBER: 78.9 PERCENT OF AFRICA'S LAND MASS IS HELD BY INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND COMMUNITIES UNDER CUSTOMARY TENURE — ABOUT 21 PERCENT IS FORMALLY RECOGNIZED, WHILE THE REMAINING 57.9 PERCENT IS NOT. Four fifths of the continent is community land, and more than half of it has no legal recognition at all. That single pair of figures reframes almost every case in this file: your situation is not an exception, it is the majority condition of African land. AND WHY THAT MATTERS, STATED PLAINLY: WHEN INFORMATION ON CUSTOMARY BOUNDARIES IS NOT EASILY ACCESSIBLE OR AVAILABLE, GOVERNMENTS AND PRIVATE DEVELOPERS SEE THOSE PLACES AS VACANT EMPTY LOTS AVAILABLE FOR INVESTMENT — SO THE PLATFORM PROVIDES EVIDENCE THAT THESE LANDS ARE NOT VACANT, IDLE OR NECESSARILY AVAILABLE FOR OUTSIDERS. VACANT EMPTY LOTS. That is how your land appears on the map an investor is shown, and the fix is not an argument but a boundary on a map somebody can look up. This file has recorded that same logic from the Congo Basin to the Comoros; here is the global register where the boundary can sit. THE THREE LAYERS IT CARRIES: THE PHYSICAL BOUNDARIES OF THE LAND; NATURAL ASSETS LOCATED ON THAT LAND, SUCH AS FORESTS, CARBON, AND ECOSYSTEM SERVICES; AND CRITICAL THREATS TO COMMUNITY LANDS, SUCH AS CONCESSIONS MADE TO PRIVATE DEVELOPERS. The third layer is the one to open first: concessions granted over community land, drawn against the community boundary. An overlap you can point at ends the argument about whether anyone lives there. THE OFFER THAT REMOVES THE USUAL BARRIER: IT ENABLES INDIGENOUS PEOPLES, LOCAL COMMUNITIES AND THEIR SUPPORTERS TO CONDUCT IMPACT ANALYSES OF THEIR LANDS WITH LITTLE TO NO MAPPING EXPERTISE NEEDED, GENERATING THE EVIDENCE THEY NEED TO MAKE A STRONG CASE FOR LAND RIGHTS — AND CONNECTS THEM TO RESOURCES AND GUIDANCE TO HELP THEM MAP AND PROTECT THEIR LANDS. NO MAPPING EXPERTISE NEEDED, written by the platform itself. Every other mapping route in this file needs a technician or a project; this one is a website a literate person can run an analysis on. If you cannot yet afford participatory mapping, start here. THE SUBMISSION ROUTE: HELP US CLOSE THE MAP GAP BY CONTRIBUTING DATA — AND GEOGRAPHERS AND EXPERTS WORKING WITH THESE COMMUNITIES ARE ENCOURAGED TO SUBMIT MAPS SO THE PROJECT CAN SHARE THEM WITH ITS USERS. If your community has already been mapped by an NGO or a university, that map can go onto the global platform — which is where a boundary stops being one organisation's file and becomes a public record. Ask whoever mapped you whether they submitted it, because often nobody did. THE DISCLAIMER, WHICH IS ITSELF A USEFUL SENTENCE: THE ABSENCE OF DATA DOES NOT INDICATE THE ABSENCE OF INDIGENOUS OR COMMUNITY LAND. Printed on the map itself. Quote it when anyone argues from a blank space that nobody is there — the platform's own operators say the blank means unmapped, not empty. THE COVERAGE, HONESTLY STATED: IT HAS MAPPED 36.8% OF THE WORLD'S LAND AS HELD OR USED BY INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES, OUT OF AN ESTIMATED 50% OR MORE THAT EXPERTS PROJECT IS ACTUALLY HELD OR USED — with coverage weakest in Africa, the Middle East and much of Asia, where it is currently focusing its attention. Africa is named as a weak-coverage region being prioritised. That is an opening rather than a gap: submissions from African communities are actively wanted now. THE LEGAL FINDING TO CARRY INTO ANY MEETING: MANY DEVELOPING COUNTRIES — TANZANIA, SOUTH SUDAN AND BURKINA FASO ARE NAMED — ACTUALLY HAVE STRONGER LAND RIGHTS LAWS THAN DEVELOPED ONES; BUT NO COUNTRY WITH INDICATOR SCORES ON THE PLATFORM PROVIDES FULL PROTECTION, AND WEAK LEGAL PROTECTION IS A CENTRAL REASON WHY INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND COMMUNITIES ARE LOSING THEIR LAND AND SOMETIMES THEIR LIVES. Your country's law may be stronger than you were told and stronger than a rich country's. Look up its indicator score before accepting that the law offers nothing — and note the finding that the usual problem is implementation, not absence. WHO RUNS IT: A CONSORTIUM OF LOCAL, REGIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATIONS WITH A 13-MEMBER STEERING GROUP, LAUNCHED IN 2015, WHOSE MISSION IS TO SUPPORT INDIGENOUS PEOPLES' AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES' LAND AND RESOURCE RIGHTS GLOBALLY. AND THE WORKED CASE: NEW PLATFORM DATA REVEALED ILLEGAL LOGGING DEVASTATING A NAMED COUNTRY'S FORESTS, PUBLISHED ALONGSIDE A NAMED PEOPLE'S FIGHT AGAINST DEFORESTATION. The map produced the evidence of the crime. Change detection over your own boundary is the cheapest monitoring there is once the boundary exists. WHO IT SUITS: any African community wanting its boundary on a public record, and anyone needing the customary-tenure figures for an argument. CAVEATS: A DATA PLATFORM, NOT A TITLING SERVICE — appearing on it is visibility, not legal recognition; pair it with a domestic instrument. For the participatory mapping that puts seven million hectares on the map, DR Congo's MappingForRights entry; for a registry a community documents itself into on its own terms, Morocco's ICCA Registry entry; for the searchable register of community struggles, Algeria's Environmental Justice Atlas entry.

trackers.name: Transparency International's Advocacy and Legal Advice Centres (ALACs) — free confidential legal advice centres in 60 countries — reachable online, by phone or in person, with a mobile version that travels to rural areas, and whose own record says land problems are the commonest complaint they hear
trackers.desc: THE COMMONEST COMPLAINT THEY HEAR IS ABOUT LAND — declared adjacency first: THREE NATIONAL CHAPTERS ARE ALREADY FILED IN THIS FILE UNDER KENYA, RWANDA AND ZIMBABWE AS BARE ORGANISATION NAMES. NONE DESCRIBES THE ADVICE CENTRES, THE MOBILE VERSION, THE REPORTING ROUTES OR THE LAND FINDING. AND THAT FINDING IS THE REASON THIS ENTRY EXISTS: THE MOST FREQUENT CORRUPTION PROBLEMS THAT MOBILE CENTRES ENCOUNTER ARE LAND PROBLEMS, PROBLEMS ASSOCIATED WITH LIVESTOCK THEFT, AND TRADITIONAL JUDGEMENTS THAT ARE FRAUDULENT OR ABUSIVE. Land first, livestock second, corrupt customary rulings third. An anti-corruption service that goes to rural Africa discovers it is mostly a land service — which means a community whose plot was reallocated, whose title vanished, or whose chief ruled for money is not off-topic here. It is the main topic. TRADITIONAL JUDGEMENTS THAT ARE FRAUDULENT OR ABUSIVE names something this file has circled repeatedly without a route attached: the customary decision that cannot be appealed. Here is a body that treats a bought verdict as corruption rather than as custom. THE SERVICE: OPERATING IN MORE THAN 50 COUNTRIES — 90+ CENTRES ACROSS 60 — THEY EMPOWER INDIVIDUALS, FAMILIES AND COMMUNITIES TO SAFELY REPORT CORRUPTION WHEN THEY SEE IT HAPPEN, PROVIDING FREE AND CONFIDENTIAL ADVICE AND SUPPORT TO VICTIMS AND WITNESSES, ENABLING THEM TO ASSERT THEIR RIGHTS, SEEK REDRESS AND STAND UP FOR JUSTICE. WITNESSES, not only victims. Somebody who saw the payment but did not lose land is inside the definition — and is often the person who can actually prove it. THREE WAYS TO REACH THEM: ONLINE, BY PHONE OR IN-PERSON — AND RECEIVE SUPPORT FROM A TRAINED ADVISOR. HOW FAR THE HELP GOES, WHICH IS FURTHER THAN ADVICE: OFTEN STARTING WITH AN INITIAL CONSULTATION, CENTRES ASSIST CLIENTS IN PURSUING CORRUPTION-RELATED COMPLAINTS — RANGING FROM NAVIGATING BUREAUCRATIC RED TAPE AND SUBMITTING THE RIGHT GOVERNMENT FORM TO CONDUCTING FORMAL INVESTIGATIONS AND PREPARING JUDICIAL CASES. SUBMITTING THE RIGHT GOVERNMENT FORM at one end and PREPARING JUDICIAL CASES at the other. Most land losses in this file begin with a form filed wrongly or not at all; this is free help with the small clerical thing as well as the big legal one. THE MOBILE VERSION, BUILT FOR EXACTLY THIS FILE'S READERS: MOBILE CENTRES BRING FREE LEGAL ADVICE TO RURAL POPULATIONS — BECAUSE OFTEN THE VICTIMS OR WITNESSES ARE ILLITERATE, MARGINALISED AND EXTREMELY VULNERABLE, OR SIMPLY PEOPLE LIVING IN RURAL AREAS VERY FAR FROM LEGAL INFRASTRUCTURE, WHO DO NOT HAVE REAL ACCESS TO LEGAL ADMINISTRATIONS. The lawyer travels to the village. That inverts the arrangement every other legal entry in this file depends on, and it is the only version that reaches people who cannot afford the bus to the district town. THE MOBILE METHOD, STEP BY STEP AND WORTH REQUESTING BY NAME: THE ACTION STARTS WITH A TRAINING SESSION INCLUDING A PUBLIC MEETING ON THEMES THAT MATTER TO THE LOCAL POPULATION — FOR EXAMPLE, CORRUPT PRACTICES IN LAND MANAGEMENT. THE TEAM INFORMS CITIZENS OF LEGISLATION AT THEIR DISPOSAL, INCLUDING THE PENAL CODE, THE CIVIL CODE, OTHER LAWS RELEVANT TO PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION, AND INTERNATIONAL INSTRUMENTS SUCH AS A UN CONVENTION AGAINST CORRUPTION. AFTER THE TRAINING SESSION, THE LEGAL COUNSELLOR AND ASSISTANTS COLLECT THE COMPLAINTS OF CITIZENS WHO ARE WILLING TO SHARE THEM. Public meeting first, then complaints collected. The order matters: people will not name what happened to them until they have heard, in public and from a lawyer, that it was unlawful. If you are organising the visit, insist on that sequence rather than a private clinic — and ask for LAND MANAGEMENT as the session theme, since it is one they already run. THE RECORD: IN ONE YEAR THE CENTRES WORKED WITH 7,480 VICTIMS AND WITNESSES ACROSS 65 COUNTRIES, MAKING 264 CORRUPTION-RELATED LEGAL SUBMISSIONS TO HOLD WRONGDOERS ACCOUNTABLE. THE WORKED AFRICAN CASE: AFTER COMPLAINTS OF BRIBERY AND EXTORTION AT A HOSPITAL, A CENTRE'S INVESTIGATION UNCOVERED LARGE-SCALE ADMINISTRATIVE CORRUPTION AND PROMPTED A NATIONAL DEBATE AND OFFICIAL ENQUIRIES — DETERRING STAFF FROM DEMANDING BRIBES IN THAT HOSPITAL AND MANY OTHERS ACROSS THE COUNTRY. Individual complaints, aggregated, became a national scandal. That is the same arithmetic as the paralegal casebook filed under Sierra Leone: one story is an anecdote, a hundred logged ones are a finding. THE CASE-TO-POLICY LOOP, STATED: NATIONAL CHAPTERS GAIN INVALUABLE INSIGHT FROM ANALYSING CENTRE CASES, WHICH HELPS THEM ADVOCATE FOR LEGISLATIVE, INSTITUTIONAL, ADMINISTRATIVE AND PROCEDURAL CHANGE — THE CENTRES ARE THE CANARIES IN THE COAL MINE, IDENTIFYING CORRUPTION HOTSPOTS THAT DEMAND REFORM OR OFFICIAL ACTION. So reporting is not only about your own case. If enough people from one district report the same land office, that office becomes a named hotspot in a national report — which is a form of pressure no individual complaint achieves. THE STRUCTURE AND THE LOCAL RULE: MORE THAN 100 CHAPTERS — LOCALLY ESTABLISHED, INDEPENDENT ORGANISATIONS — STAFFED WITH LOCAL EXPERTS AND IDEALLY PLACED TO DETERMINE THE PRIORITIES AND APPROACHES BEST SUITED TO THEIR COUNTRIES, WITH WORK RANGING FROM VISITING RURAL COMMUNITIES TO PROVIDE FREE LEGAL SUPPORT TO ADVISING THEIR GOVERNMENT ON POLICY REFORM. AND THE FINDING ROUTE: PER-COUNTRY REPORTING PAGES NAME HOW MANY CENTRES EXIST AND WHICH TO CONTACT — YOUR NEAREST IS NORMALLY THE MOST SUITABLE, BUT IF IN DOUBT, CONTACT ANY OF THE CENTRES LISTED AND THEY WILL MAKE SURE YOU SPEAK TO THE RIGHT PEOPLE. Contact any of them and they route you. That removes the commonest reason people give up on a directory — not knowing which of the listed offices is theirs. WHO IT SUITS: African communities whose land was taken through a bribe, a bought ruling or a falsified record, and the witnesses who saw it. CAVEATS: THE FRAME IS CORRUPTION — a land dispute with no improper payment or abuse of office may not fit, and mobile visits depend on the national chapter's programme. For the three chapters already listed, Kenya's, Rwanda's and Zimbabwe's entries; for the paralegal method where no lawyer exists, Sierra Leone's Timap entry; for university law clinics as free representation, Comoros' entry.

trackers.name: A farmer-owned regional forum in 16 countries with a published Tanzanian registration number and a district-forum structure a village group joins — one national chapter alone holds 1,359 farmer groups and 48,210 farmers, 64% of them women
trackers.desc: FARMER INITIATED, FARMER LED AND FARMER OWNED — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S LIBYA ENTRY COVERS THE PAN-AFRICAN FOOD SOVEREIGNTY ALLIANCE OF WHICH THIS FORUM IS A NAMED CORE MEMBER; THAT ENTRY IS NOT RESTATED. THE SWEEP ALSO MATCHED A SIMILARLY-ABBREVIATED ORGANISATION ALREADY NAMED IN LESOTHO'S BUCKET — A DIFFERENT BODY, WHOSE HOST IS NOT SHIPPED HERE. WHO OWNS IT, AND IT IS THE FIND: A NETWORK OF GRASSROOTS SMALL-SCALE FARMERS' ORGANIZATIONS WORKING IN 16 COUNTRIES OF THE EASTERN AND SOUTHERN AFRICA REGION — A MOVEMENT WHICH IS SMALL SCALE FARMER INITIATED, FARMER LED AND FARMER OWNED. Not an NGO that works with farmers. Farmers started it, run it and own it — which is the distinction this file has recorded mattering most when a government or a company asks who exactly a delegation speaks for. A farmer-owned forum answers that question in its own constitution. THE FORMAL FACTS, PUBLISHED IN FULL: STARTED IN 2002 AT A WORLD SUMMIT IN JOHANNESBURG, FULLY OPERATIONAL SINCE APRIL 2009, REGISTERED IN TANZANIA UNDER A NAMED NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS ACT SINCE 27 AUGUST 2007 WITH A PUBLISHED REGISTRATION NUMBER — WITH THE SECRETARIAT IN MOROGORO, TANZANIA, LED BY A COORDINATOR WHO REPORTS TO A REGIONAL BOARD. A registration number published on the record. This file has repeatedly recorded registration as the gate that shuts groups out and the pretext used to deregister them; a regional body that publishes its own number, act and date is showing the paperwork every member chapter can point to. THE STRUCTURE A VILLAGE GROUP ACTUALLY JOINS, WITH ITS NUMBERS: ONE NATIONAL CHAPTER OPERATIONALISED IN 2008 HAS BECOME THE LARGEST SMALL-SCALE FARMER-LED ADVOCACY MOVEMENT IN THAT COUNTRY — WITH 1,359 FARMER GROUPS COMPRISING 48,210 INDIVIDUAL SMALL-SCALE FARMERS, OF WHICH 64 PER CENT ARE WOMEN, ACROSS 54 DISTRICTS, UNDER THE ADMINISTRATION OF 30 HISTORICAL DISTRICTS' FORUMS. ANOTHER PUBLISHED FIGURE PUTS THE SAME CHAPTER AT 12,588 SMALL-SCALE FARMER COMMUNITY ORGANISATIONS IN 54 DISTRICTS. DISTRICTS' FORUMS is the level to look for. You do not apply to a continental body — a farmer group joins a district forum, the district forums make the national chapter, and the chapters make the region. That is a ladder a village committee can actually climb, and the two differing membership figures are recorded as found rather than reconciled. AND 64 PER CENT WOMEN, counted and published. Most farmer organisations in this file cannot say what their gender composition is. THE STATED PURPOSE: TO ENABLE SMALL FARMERS TO SPEAK AS A UNITED VOICE SO THAT ISSUES, CONCERNS AND RECOMMENDATIONS BECOME AN INTEGRAL PART OF POLICIES AND PRACTICES AT GRASSROOTS LEVELS, NATIONAL LEVELS AS WELL AS AT REGIONAL AND GLOBAL LEVELS — FACILITATING PROCESSES THROUGH WHICH SMALL SCALE FARMERS' DEVELOPMENT CONCERNS CAN BE SOLICITED, ARTICULATED AND ULTIMATELY ADDRESSED. SOLICITED, ARTICULATED AND ADDRESSED, in that order. The first step is asking members what the problem is — which sounds obvious and is the step most coalitions in this file skip before speaking on somebody's behalf. THE MISSION AND ITS THREE METHODS: TO EMPOWER SMALL-SCALE FARMERS TO INFLUENCE DEVELOPMENT POLICIES AND PROMOTE ECOLOGICAL AGRICULTURE THROUGH CAPACITY STRENGTHENING, RESEARCH, AND NETWORKING. THE GLOBAL CONNECTION: THE NETWORK REGULARLY PARTICIPATES IN GLOBAL POLICY FORUMS, SEVERAL MEMBERS ARE REPRESENTED IN AN INFLUENTIAL AGRARIAN MOVEMENT ORGANIZATION, AND ONE NATIONAL CHAPTER IS PART OF THAT MOVEMENT — DESCRIBED AS THE LARGEST PEASANT ORGANISATION IN THE WORLD. A farmer group in a district can, through two steps, be inside the largest peasant movement on earth. That is the shortest route in this file from a village to a global platform, and it costs nothing but organising. THE RESEARCH SHIFT, IN A FARMER'S OWN WORDS: FOR THE FIRST TIME, WE ARE NOT JUST BEING CONSULTED; WE ARE HELPING TO DESIGN THE RESEARCH QUESTIONS THAT WILL SHAPE AGROECOLOGY IN OUR OWN COMMUNITIES. Designing the questions, not answering them. Every study done about a community in this file was scoped by somebody else — and the demand to help set the research question is small, specific and refusable only with difficulty. THE PAID OPPORTUNITIES IT PUBLISHES: THE FORUM INVITES QUALIFIED CONSULTANTS TO SUBMIT EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST TO UNDERTAKE WORK. Watch that page. Paid research and facilitation work commissioned by a farmer-owned body is money staying inside the movement, and an African researcher or organiser can bid. THE ACCOUNTABILITY CONSORTIUM IT SITS IN: A CONSORTIUM LED BY AN INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATION AND INCLUDING A UNIVERSITY-BASED PUBLIC SERVICE ACCOUNTABILITY MONITOR AND A REGIONAL HEALTH ORGANISATION, IMPLEMENTING A PROJECT ON STRENGTHENING SOCIAL ACCOUNTABILITY AND OVERSIGHT IN HEALTH AND AGRICULTURE IN SOUTHERN AFRICA. AND THE BUDGET FINDING IT PRESSES ON: DESPITE PROGRESS IN REALISING A CONTINENTAL COMMITMENT TO END HUNGER AND HALVE POVERTY, EAST AFRICAN COUNTRIES STILL SPEND LESS FROM THEIR NATIONAL BUDGETS ON THE AGRICULTURE SECTOR WHICH EMPLOYS MANY CITIZENS. A continental commitment your government signed, and a budget line that shows whether it meant it. That comparison is public, annual and checkable — and it is a stronger question at a district meeting than any general complaint. WHO IT SUITS: farmer groups in eastern and southern Africa looking for a structure to join, and organisers who want a farmer-owned rather than NGO-led route to national and global platforms. CAVEATS: 16 COUNTRIES IN EASTERN AND SOUTHERN AFRICA ONLY, AND IT IS AN ADVOCACY FORUM RATHER THAN A FUNDER OR LEGAL SERVICE — west and central African groups should look to the continental alliance instead. For that alliance and its open WhatsApp community, Libya's entry; for the pastoralist and hunter-gatherer coalition, Tanzania's PINGO's Forum entry; for the free community fund built with no outside capital, Djibouti's savings-group entry.

trackers.name: A printable digital-safety toolkit in 40+ languages they will email you as a PDF in the language you name — plus a free trainers' manual whose first rule is that a badly chosen training can deepen the conflicts inside a community
trackers.desc: ASK FOR IT ON PAPER, IN YOUR LANGUAGE, AND THEY SEND IT — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S LESOTHO ENTRY COVERS A DIFFERENT ORGANISATION'S HOLISTIC SECURITY PROTOCOL AND HANDBOOK, ITS LIBYA ENTRY THE TWO-HOUR DIGITAL HELPLINE, AND ITS EQUATORIAL GUINEA ENTRY THE PROTECTION GRANTS. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRINT-AND-POST OFFER, WHICH IS THE FIND: WE'VE LOCALIZED THE PRINT VERSION OF THE KIT INTO MANY GLOBAL LANGUAGES. IF YOU'D LIKE TO REQUEST A PDF COPY, WRITE TO A NAMED PERSON AT A PUBLISHED STUDIO ADDRESS, INDICATING THE LANGUAGE YOU NEED, AS WELL AS YOUR IDEA OF HOW AND WHERE YOU'D LIKE TO USE IT. A person's name, a language request, and a printable file. Almost every security resource in this file assumes a working connection and a device per person; this one is designed to be printed once and handed round a meeting where two people have phones. For a village committee, that is the difference between a resource and a rumour of one. THE TRANSLATION INVITATION: WE'RE ALSO LOOKING FOR PEOPLE TO TRANSLATE AND LOCALIZE THE KIT FOR ADDITIONAL LANGUAGES AND GEOGRAPHICAL CONTEXTS — AND IF YOU'D BE INTERESTED IN TRANSLATING, ADAPTING, PROOFREADING, OR CONTRIBUTING NEW CONTENT OR IDEAS, GET IN TOUCH. If your language is missing, they are asking. A national organisation that translates it once has the material permanently, in the language its members actually use — and this file has recorded language as the barrier that quietly disqualifies more communities than any eligibility rule. THE SCALE AND THE FORM: A SIMPLE, ACCESSIBLE TOOLKIT IN PHYSICAL AND DIGITAL VERSIONS, AVAILABLE IN OVER 40 LANGUAGES, USED BY ORGANISATIONS AND INDIVIDUALS AROUND THE WORLD TO PROMOTE CONVERSATIONS AROUND DIGITAL PRIVACY, SECURITY, WELLBEING, THE IMPACT OF TECHNOLOGY ON THE ENVIRONMENT AND HOW TO TACKLE MISINFORMATION. WHAT THE SECTIONS COVER: A PRIVACY SECTION ON WHICH PERSONAL DATA IS COLLECTED AND BY WHOM, WITH SPECIAL GUIDES TO USE WHEN YOU'RE VOTING OR PROTESTING; A SECURITY SECTION ON STRENGTHENING PASSWORDS, CHOOSING THE RIGHT SCREEN LOCK, CLEANING UP YOUR VIRTUAL VALUABLES, AND HOW TO RESPOND TO DATA BREACHES; AND A WELLBEING SECTION ON BUILDING POSITIVE HABITS, BURSTING YOUR FILTER BUBBLE, AND SPOTTING DESIGN NUDGES AND MISINFORMATION. A GUIDE FOR WHEN YOU'RE PROTESTING, specifically. What to carry, what to leave, what a phone reveals about who was present — the practical questions before a demonstration that this file's legal entries cannot answer. THE FACILITATOR MATERIALS: THE DIGITAL VERSION INCLUDES A RESOURCES DOWNLOAD CENTER, MULTIMEDIA RESOURCES AND A WORKSHOPS SECTION, INCLUDING TIPS AND ACTIVITIES FOR EDUCATORS AND FACILITATORS INTERESTED IN ENGAGING THEIR AUDIENCES IN CONVERSATION AND ACTIONS. THE TRAINERS' MANUAL AND ITS CENTRAL WARNING, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: CONSIDER THE DO-NO-HARM PRINCIPLE WHEN SELECTING PARTICIPANTS. OFTEN, TRAININGS CONSTITUTE AN INTERVENTION IN A SITUATION OF MULTIPLE CONFLICTS — BETWEEN DEFENDERS AND THEIR ADVERSARIES, BUT ALSO AMONG DEFENDERS ALONG GENDER AND OTHER LINES OF POTENTIAL DISCRIMINATION. ENSURE THAT THE TRAINING DOESN'T AGGRAVATE SUCH CONFLICTS. A training is an intervention in the community's own divisions, not a neutral event. Who is invited, who is left out, and who speaks in front of whom all shift power inside a village — and this file has recorded outside programmes doing exactly that damage without noticing. The warning is free, and it applies to any workshop anyone offers you. THE JUDGEMENT IT ASKS TRAINERS TO MAKE: IN SOME CASES THIS MAY MEAN LIMITING PARTICIPANTS TO ONE GROUP, WHEREAS IN OTHER CASES IT IS BEST FOR ALL GROUPS TO BE REPRESENTED, WITH TIME DEDICATED TO RAISING AWARENESS OF AND COUNTERING THE DYNAMICS OF PRIVILEGE THAT MAY EXIST — AND CONSIDER WHETHER YOU EVEN NEED TO SHARE THE EXACT NATURE OF THE TRAINING. WHETHER YOU EVEN NEED TO SHARE THE EXACT NATURE OF THE TRAINING. Announcing a security workshop tells your opponents that you expect to be targeted, and tells them who attended. THE STARTING POINT THE MANUAL TAKES: IN PREPARE, WE BEGIN BY RECOGNISING THAT EACH OF US ALREADY HAS AND TAKES SECURITY MEASURES — OUR STRATEGIES FOR HEALTH AND WELL-BEING, OUR PERSONAL BELIEFS AND SOURCES OF RESILIENCE AND OUR INSTINCTIVE RESPONSES TO THREAT AND DANGER. It starts from what people already do rather than from what they lack. Communities that have survived decades of pressure have practices worth naming, and a training that begins by cataloguing them is the opposite of the deficit approach this file keeps recording. THE GROUP FOCUS: GROUPS AND ORGANISATIONS HAVE COMPLEX INTERNAL DYNAMICS AND CULTURES WHICH INFLUENCE THE WAYS WE INTERACT AND PLAN — WITH A SECTION ON BUILDING SECURITY STRATEGIES AND PLANS IN GROUPS, AND AN EXPLORE STAGE THAT FOLLOWS A SERIES OF STEPS TO GET A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF CONTEXT AND REACH CONCLUSIONS ABOUT CONCRETE THREATS. THE ORGANISATION AND ITS TWO AUDIENCES: AN INTERNATIONAL NON-PROFIT WORKING AT THE INTERSECTION OF TECHNOLOGY, HUMAN RIGHTS AND CIVIL LIBERTIES — SERVING A BROAD PUBLIC AUDIENCE, AND CIVIL SOCIETY ACTORS SUCH AS JOURNALISTS, OTHER NGOs AND HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS, WITH WHOM IT WORKS TO CREATE SAFER, MORE ROBUST AND MORE INFORMED PRACTICES. THE INVESTIGATIONS PROJECT: A PROJECT HELPING EMPOWER PEOPLE TO USE DIGITAL INVESTIGATIONS TO UNCOVER TRUTH OR CORRUPTION — ALONGSIDE A NOTE THAT WHETHER YOU ARE TRYING TO CLEAN YOUR DATA, SPOT PATTERNS, OR CREATE A DATA VISUALISATION, THERE ARE MANY FREE TOOLS AVAILABLE ONLINE. Investigation training for people who are not journalists. A community tracing who owns the company on its land is doing exactly this work, and this file's registry and ownership entries are what those methods are applied to. AND THE LOW-COST EXHIBITION FORMAT: A PUBLIC INTERVENTION AND INTERACTIVE EXPERIENCE INVITING VISITORS TO REFLECT ON HOW TECHNOLOGY IMPACTS THEIR LIVES AND SOCIETY — AVAILABLE FROM LARGE-SCALE EXHIBITIONS TO LOW-COST SELF-PRINT FORMATS, EASILY USED AND ADAPTED, WITH POSTER EXHIBITIONS, ANIMATIONS, APPS, WORKSHOP CURRICULA AND OTHER ASSETS IN AROUND 30 LANGUAGES. SELF-PRINT POSTERS AND A WORKSHOP CURRICULUM, free to adapt. A community organisation can run a public event in its own town with materials it printed itself — no venue fee, no visiting facilitator, no permission. WHO IT SUITS: African community organisations, unions and committees wanting printed, translatable security material and a method for running their own workshops. CAVEATS: MATERIALS AND METHOD, NOT A HELPLINE, A FUNDER OR AN INCIDENT RESPONSE SERVICE — for an attack in progress, use the helpline. For the two-hour digital helpline in French and Arabic, Libya's entry; for fully funded support with no registration requirement, Lesotho's entry; for grants to buy equipment, Equatorial Guinea's entry.

trackers.name: The Green Connection, Cape Town — an African organisation that files offshore oil and gas judicial reviews with a fishers co-operative as named co-applicant, publishes the law firm acting for it, and won a court order halting a seismic survey on the ground that nobody consulted the fishing communities
trackers.desc: THE FISHERS CO-OPERATIVE IS A CO-APPLICANT ON THE PAPERS, NOT A WITNESS — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S MADAGASCAR ENTRY COVERS THE INTERNATIONAL PROGRAMME THAT PARTNERED ON THESE CASES, AND THE AFRICAN LEGAL EMPOWERMENT ORGANISATION THAT IS THE OTHER CO-APPLICANT, NATURAL JUSTICE, ALREADY HAS ENTRIES IN NINE AFRICA BUCKETS. NEITHER IS RESTATED AND NEITHER HOST IS SHIPPED. THIS FILE'S MAURITIUS ENTRY COVERS THE MARINE FUND AND ITS CÔTE D'IVOIRE ENTRY THE UNCONDITIONAL CASH TRANSFERS. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. WHO IS ON THE PAPERS, WHICH IS THE FIND: AUKOTOWA FISHERIES PRIMARY CO-OPERATIVE OF PORT NOLLOTH, THIS ORGANISATION, AND NATURAL JUSTICE ARE THE APPLICANTS — WITH THE CO-OPERATIVE'S CHAIRPERSON, HIMSELF A SMALL-SCALE FISHER, SPEAKING FOR THE CASE IN PUBLIC. A fishers' co-operative as a party to the case, not an affected group mentioned in it. That is the difference between a community whose interests are argued and one that can instruct, settle or refuse — and it is achievable because a registered co-operative already exists for the fishing itself. This file has repeatedly found that the vehicle a community already has is the one that gives it standing. THE LEGAL GROUND THEY RAN AND WON ON: FISHERS TOLD THE COURT THAT A SEISMIC SURVEY WAS UNLAWFUL SINCE THE COMPANY DID NOT SEEK AN ENVIRONMENTAL AUTHORISATION AS REQUIRED, NOR DID IT CONSULT WITH ANY SMALL-SCALE FISHING COMMUNITIES ALONG THE WEST COAST — AND A JUDGE DIRECTED THE COMPANY TO DISCONTINUE ANY ACTIVITIES RELATED TO THE SEISMIC SURVEY. Two grounds, both procedural, both winnable: no authorisation, and no consultation. Neither required proving ecological harm, which is the expensive part. An operation already under way was stopped on them. WHAT THE ADVOCATE ARGUED, IN THE ORGANISATION'S OWN ACCOUNT: OUR ADVOCATE ARGUED OUR CASE STRONGLY, SHOWING THAT COMMUNITIES WERE NOT MEANINGFULLY CONSULTED — WITH THE HOPE THAT IT SERVES AS A LESSON FOR OIL, GAS, AND ANY OTHER COMPANIES WANTING TO DO BUSINESS IN THE COUNTRY. MEANINGFULLY is the operative word. A company that held a meeting has not necessarily consulted, and this file has recorded attendance registers produced as proof of consent. The finding that consultation was not meaningful is the one worth aiming at. THE RECORD OF DECISION, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: THEY OBTAINED THE RECORD OF DECISION IN ORDER TO PROGRESS THE LEGAL CHALLENGE — REVIEWING IT IS DESCRIBED AS CRUCIAL BECAUSE IT PROVIDES TRANSPARENCY AND ACCOUNTABILITY IN THE GOVERNMENT'S DECISION TO GRANT AN ENVIRONMENTAL AUTHORISATION. The record of decision is the file the official actually relied on. Getting it is a discrete, achievable step that precedes any argument about the merits, and it is where the gap between what was assessed and what was approved becomes visible. Ask for it early; this case shows the challenge could not proceed without it. THE CURRENT CASE AND ITS SHAPE: APPLICANTS SEEK A JUDICIAL REVIEW OF AN ENVIRONMENTAL AUTHORISATION GRANTED IN 2023 TO TOTALENERGIES EP SOUTH AFRICA, AFTER AN APPEAL TO THE RELEVANT MINISTER — AND THEY OPPOSED A SECOND OIL MAJOR'S BID TO JOIN THE PROCEEDINGS. Appeal to the minister first, then judicial review. That sequence matters: the internal appeal is usually a precondition, and skipping it can end a case before it starts. WHO IS OPPOSING THEM, NAMED: THE MINISTER AND DIRECTOR-GENERAL OF THE MINERAL RESOURCES AND ENERGY DEPARTMENT, THE MINISTER OF THE FORESTRY, FISHERIES AND ENVIRONMENT DEPARTMENT, AND THE OIL COMPANY ITSELF ALL OPPOSE THE LEGAL CHALLENGE. Two ministries and the company on the other side. Recorded plainly because it is the realistic picture: the environment ministry did not become an ally when the case was filed. THE LAW FIRM NAMED PUBLICLY: THE ORGANISATIONS ARE REPRESENTED BY CULLINAN & ASSOCIATES. Naming the firm in the press release is itself useful to other communities — it is a working answer to the standing question of which attorneys actually run these cases in the country. THE CAMPAIGN THAT SURROUNDS THE LITIGATION: A NAMED OCEANS CAMPAIGN WORKING WITH COASTAL COMMUNITIES WHOSE LIVELIHOODS ARE THREATENED — AIMING TO EMPOWER LOCAL OCEAN-DEPENDENT COMMUNITIES, ENSURING FISHER LIVELIHOODS AND THEIR TOOLS AND KNOWLEDGE ARE SUSTAINED, AND THAT COMMUNITIES ARE ABLE TO ENGAGE WITH DECISION-MAKERS. HOW IT BUILDS THAT: THE CAMPAIGN BUILDS ON EXISTING NETWORKS OF SMALL-SCALE FISHERS AND OTHER COASTAL COMMUNITIES, AS WELL AS ENGAGING CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS WORKING ON CLIMATE AND ENERGY — WITH A COMMUNITY OUTREACH COORDINATOR AND A NAMED LEGACY PROJECT SUPPORTING FISHERS IN A DISTANT COASTAL TOWN. A paid community outreach coordinator, and fishers hundreds of kilometres away brought into the same campaign. The litigation did not create the network; it used one that already existed. THE TRIBUNAL AND THE FINANCE ANGLE: AN OCEANS TRIBUNAL DESCRIBED AS EXPOSING THE DEVASTATING IMPACT OF THE GOVERNMENT'S SECRET DECISIONS, AND COASTAL COMMUNITY MEMBERS FROM THREE NAMED TOWNS CALLING ON THE BANKS NOT TO FUND A POWERSHIP PROJECT — ALONGSIDE CHALLENGES TO ELECTRICITY GENERATION APPLICATION PROCESSES AND TARIFF PLANS. A people's tribunal and a direct appeal to the banks, run alongside the court case rather than instead of it. Where the courts are slow, the financing is the other pressure point — and community members from named towns made that appeal themselves. THE CONTINENTAL FRAMING IT USES: BY EXTENDING THE FIGHT FOR CLIMATE JUSTICE TO OPPOSING DEEP-SEA OIL AND GAS EXPLOITATION, WE WILL SERVE THE COUNTRY AND THE AFRICAN CONTINENT AS A WHOLE, WHILST ACKNOWLEDGING THE COURAGEOUS FIGHT OF A NAMED NIGERIAN PEOPLE AND BUILDING ON A NAMED ACTIVIST'S LEGACY. AND WHAT THE FISHERS THEMSELVES PUT ON RECORD: FOR TRADITIONAL FISHERS, WHO HAVE BEEN LIVING FROM THE OCEAN FOR HUNDREDS OF YEARS, THE OCEAN IS MORE THAN JUST A RESOURCE THAT SUSTAINS OUR LIVELIHOODS — FOR US, WHO HAVE LOST FAMILY MEMBERS AND ANCESTORS AT SEA, THE OCEAN IS PART OF OUR HERITAGE, WHICH WE BELIEVE IS WORTH PROTECTING. Heritage and burial, put into the court record by the fishers rather than by a lawyer. That is the evidence a compensation calculation cannot absorb, and it is the reason to have the community speak in its own words in the papers. WHO IT SUITS: African coastal and fishing communities facing seismic surveys, offshore drilling or port and power projects — and any community organisation looking for a workable litigation structure to copy. CAVEATS: A SOUTH AFRICAN ORGANISATION LITIGATING UNDER SOUTH AFRICAN LAW; THE CASES AND REMEDIES ARE NATIONAL, THOUGH THE STRUCTURE AND GROUNDS TRANSFER — and it is a campaigning body, not a service you apply to. For the international programme that partnered on these cases, Madagascar's entry; for marine funding with community conservation measures, Mauritius' entry.

trackers.name: Spaces for Change, Lagos — an organisation whose legal experts run sessions teaching communities the laws that justify their own eviction — plus field visits after demolitions that publish what compensation was actually offered, and the constitutional argument built from how the demolition was carried out
trackers.desc: THEY TEACH YOU THE LAWS THAT WILL BE USED TO EVICT YOU — method and adjacency declared first: THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THE SHIPPED HOST AND FOUR SUBJECT SPELLINGS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL ABSENT. THIS FILE'S NIGERIA BUCKET CARRIES A COMMUNITY-PARALEGAL ORGANISATION ON A DIFFERENT HOST, READ BEFORE WRITING AND NOT RESTATED; ITS GUINEA-BISSAU ENTRY THE 450-MEMBER EVICTION COALITION AND ITS MALAWI ENTRY THE SOCIO-ECONOMIC RIGHTS INSTITUTE WITH ITS EVICTION GUIDE. NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. WHAT ITS LAWYERS ACTUALLY TEACH, WHICH IS THE FIND: LEGAL EXPERTS FACILITATED LEARNING SESSIONS THAT EXPLAINED THE LAWS THAT JUSTIFY FORCED EVICTIONS IN THE COUNTRY. Not the laws that protect you — the ones that will be used against you. This file is full of guidance on rights; this is the inverse and rarer service: knowing in advance which statute the notice will cite, what it requires the state to do first, and therefore where the state will fail to do it. That is what turns a demolition into a case. WHY THAT MATTERS TO THE PEOPLE IN THE ROOM: BECAUSE MOST RESIDENTS LACK TITLED LAND DOCUMENTATION, THEY ARE PRONE TO URBAN-INDUCED GENTRIFICATION AND FORCED DISPLACEMENT, IN CONSTANT DANGER OF FORCEFUL EVICTION WITHOUT PROPER COMPENSATION OR RESETTLEMENT. WHAT PARTICIPANTS SAID THEY GOT: THAT THE PARTNERSHIP WAS A SAFE PLACE TO INTERACT WITH STATE AND LOCAL AUTHORITIES AND ALSO MAINSTREAMING THE NEEDS OF INFORMAL COMMUNITIES INTO THE STATE'S HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT AGENDA — WITH LEADERS COMMITTING TO STEP DOWN THE KNOWLEDGE AND TRAINING TO THEIR OWN MEMBERS. A SAFE PLACE TO INTERACT WITH AUTHORITIES is a distinct thing to ask an organisation for: not representation, but a room in which the meeting can happen without the community negotiating alone. And STEP DOWN THE TRAINING is how twenty people become a thousand. THE FIELD DOCUMENTATION IT DOES AFTER A DEMOLITION, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: ON A FIELD VISIT, COMMUNITY MEMBERS DISCLOSED THAT A FORM WAS CIRCULATED BY A LOCAL DEVELOPMENT COMMITTEE PROPOSING A TOKEN PAYMENT OF THREE HUNDRED THOUSAND NAIRA FOR STRUCTURES MADE OF PLANK AND FIVE HUNDRED THOUSAND FOR A PERMANENT STRUCTURE, TO BE DISTRIBUTED AT THE TRADITIONAL RULER'S PALACE — AND, CONTRARY TO NARRATIVES CIRCULATING ON SOCIAL MEDIA, AFFECTED RESIDENTS HAD NOT RECEIVED ANY FORM OF COMPENSATION.
