trackers.name: Niger's PMF/FEM small-grants machinery — civil society sits on the deciding committee, grants cover up to 75% of cost, volunteer labour counts as co-financing, and a preparatory grant pays for the baseline study
trackers.desc: THE FRANCOPHONE SMALL-GRANTS MACHINE, SET OUT IN FULL BECAUSE EVERY STEP IS A PLACE A VILLAGE FILE CAN BE HELPED OR LOST — and this closes the last funding gap in this file's Nigerien record: THE PROGRAMME DE MICROFINANCEMENT DU FONDS POUR L'ENVIRONNEMENT MONDIAL (PMF/FEM/NIGER) LAUNCHES APPELS À PROPOSITION DE PROJETS under STAR and CORE fund allocations, awarding small grants to CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, NATIONAL ORGANISATIONS COMMUNAUTAIRES DE BASE AND RESEARCH INSTITUTIONS, to support innovative and inclusive community initiatives that improve socioeconomic conditions and produce positive global environmental impacts, with selected projects required to PROMOTE AND VALORISE THE KNOWLEDGE AND KNOW-HOW OF LOCAL COMMUNITIES in addressing biodiversity loss, land degradation, climate impacts and pollutants. Your own knowledge is a stated selection criterion, not a decoration — write what your community already knows how to do into the proposal. WHO DECIDES, AND WHO SITS THERE: THE NATIONAL COORDINATOR ACTS AS THE PRINCIPAL FOCAL POINT FOR NGOs, ASSOCIATIONS AND ORGANISATIONS COMMUNAUTAIRES DE BASE; the COMITÉ NATIONAL DE PILOTAGE (CNP) IS THE NATIONAL DECISION BODY for both strategy and the award of grants — AND REPRESENTATIVES OF CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS SIT ON IT alongside state structures and technical and financial partners. Civil society sits on the committee that awards the money. Find out who your sector's representative is and speak to them before the call closes — that is a seat, not a suggestion box. FOUR TERMS WORTH KNOWING BEFORE YOU APPLY: grants represent UP TO 75% OF THE TOTAL COST of the initiative; a separate PREPARATORY GRANT SUPPORTS NECESSARY PRIOR STUDIES — SUCH AS ESTABLISHING THE BASELINE SITUATION or other technical analysis — whose results then ENRICH AND FINALISE the project proposal; the CNP MAY MANDATE ITS OWN MEMBERS OR IDENTIFY RESOURCE PERSONS TO ACCOMPANY organisations in finalising their proposal, AND PRESELECTED PROPONENTS MAY BE INVITED TO PRESENT THEIR INITIATIVE BEFORE THE COMMITTEE; and CO-FINANCING MAY BE IN KIND, INCLUDING VOLUNTEER LABOUR (BÉNÉVOLAT), with project duration not exceeding 24 MONTHS and ONE PROPOSAL PER ORGANISATION. Ask for the preparatory grant first and let it pay for the baseline study — that study is also the evidence you will need later if a project disputes what your land was like before. And eligibility is landscape-bound: projects must sit in the PAYSAGES PRIORITAIRES, so check the country strategy document for whether yours is one. THE WORKED NIGERIEN EXAMPLE: ONG ACTION POUR LE DÉVELOPPEMENT DU NIGER restores degraded land through CASH FOR WORK with conditional transfers to WOMEN AND YOUNG HEADS OF HOUSEHOLD to create productive assets, implemented PARTICIPATIVELY WITH BENEFICIARIES BEFORE restoration activities begin. WHO IT SUITS: Nigerien village committees, women's and youth groups, and community organisations restoring land. CAVEATS: A CYCLE-BASED WINDOW with a landscape restriction — read the current call and the country strategy. For the rural code land commissions, Niger's COFO entries.

trackers.name: ANSEN and Niger's named organisations — regional antennas in three regions, school nurseries owned by the schools that built them, the giraffe association, and the national NGO directory
trackers.desc: THE OWNERSHIP CLAUSE AND THE ANTENNAS: the ASSOCIATION NIGÉRIENNE DES SCOUTS DE L'ENVIRONNEMENT (ANSEN), at PALAIS DES SPORTS PORTE 402, BP 2013, NIAMEY, WITH REGIONAL ANTENNAS IN THE REGIONS OF ZINDER, DOSSO AND AGADEZ, has run AN ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION PROGRAMME SPREAD OVER THE WHOLE SCHOOL YEAR IN CERTAIN NIAMEY SCHOOLS SINCE 1994, with NURSERIES AND SCHOOL GARDENS CREATED INSIDE THE ESTABLISHMENTS CONCERNED. AND ITS OWN STATEMENT OF WHO OWNS THE RESULT IS THE MOST TRANSFERABLE SENTENCE IN THIS ENTRY: THE PROPERTY RIGHTS BELONG EXCLUSIVELY TO ANSEN AND THE SCHOOLS THAT IMPLEMENTED IT; AS FOR THE FINANCIAL PARTNER, IT SIGNED A CONVENTION WITH US, WHICH MEANS THAT THOSE RESPONSIBLE FOR IMPLEMENTATION ARE THE OWNERS. The funder signs a convention; the implementers own the nursery. Write that clause into any agreement you sign — who owns the trees, the fence and the well when the project ends is the question most communities in this file discovered too late. WHAT ELSE ANSEN DOES: tree planting in areas affected by desertification with young people; land recuperation with young people in the national services and young scouts; an ANNUAL YOUTH CAMP FOR THE REHABILITATION OF THE LAND; a project to combat desertification THROUGH THE PRODUCTION OF GUM ARABIC; AND COLLABORATION WITH NIGER'S UNCCD FOCAL POINT ON IMPLEMENTING THE NATIONAL ACTION PROGRAMME TO COMBAT DESERTIFICATION AND MANAGE NATURAL RESOURCES, working with two education ministries and a named foreign NGO. Gum arabic turns anti-desertification planting into a crop with a buyer, and an annual camp is recurring labour that costs nothing. Both are answers to the question of who maintains a restoration after the grant ends. THE OTHERS, NAMED: L'ASSOCIATION DE SAUVEGARDE DES GIRAFES DU NIGER (ASGN), FORMED 1996 WITH THE OBJECTIVE OF SAVING THE LAST POPULATION OF WEST AFRICAN GIRAFFES — WHEN IT WAS FORMED ONLY 50 INDIVIDUALS SURVIVED IN THE COUNTRY — EXPLICITLY INCLUDING PRESERVATION OF THEIR HABITAT IN THE FACE OF AGRICULTURAL EXPANSION, with a named leader. An association founded when fifty animals were left is proof that a last population is still worth organising around. And note the framing: the threat named is agricultural expansion, not poaching — habitat loss is stated as the enemy, which is the framing a community losing land can use. ONG ACTION POUR LE DÉVELOPPEMENT DU NIGER, ESTABLISHED 2018 AS A LEGALLY RECOGNISED NON-PROFIT, INTERVENING IN THE REGIONS OF TILLABÉRY, DIFFA, TAHOUA, ZINDER, MARADI AND DOSSO, WITH A NATIONAL OFFICE IN NIAMEY AND THREE SUB-OFFICES AT TAHOUA/ILLELA, TILLABÉRY/OUALLAM AND DOSSO. Sub-offices in named towns is what distinguishes an organisation that can reach a village from one that can only receive letters in Niamey. A national forum has also convened ONG ADESSA, ONG ADKOUL, ONG AGIR PLUS, ONG KARKARA and others alongside the hydraulics ministry and a research institute. AND TO FIND THE REST: A RÉPERTOIRE DES ONG NATIONALES AU NIGER IS PUBLISHED AS A CURATED HUMANITARIAN RESPONSE RESOURCE. A national NGO directory maintained for emergency coordination is also the most current list of who is actually operating — in a country with a difficult security situation, currency matters more than completeness. WHO IT SUITS: Nigerien communities in Zinder, Dosso, Agadez, Tillabéry, Tahoua, Diffa or Maradi, and schools wanting a nursery they will own. CAVEATS: CONFIRM CURRENT OPERATIONS given the security situation. For the 75% grant, the preparatory grant and the civil-society seat on the national steering committee, Niger's PMF/FEM entry.

trackers.name: Niger's peasant platform, herders' federation and milk cooperatives inside a six-country 55-organisation campaign — plus the Maisons du Paysan with a published management plan for each named village, and DIMOL's Niamey contacts
trackers.desc: THE FARMERS' PLATFORM, AND THE HOUSE IN THE VILLAGE: NIGER'S NAMED MEMBERS OF A SIX-COUNTRY REGIONAL CAMPAIGN INCLUDE THE PLATEFORME PAYSANNE DU NIGER (PFPN); THE FÉDÉRATION NATIONALE DES ÉLEVEURS DU NIGER (FNEN DADO); KARKARA; GAJEL; A NAMED REGIONAL CHAMBER OF AGRICULTURE; A MILK COOPERATIVE AT A NAMED TOWN; TWO NAMED DAIRIES; AND A HYGIENE ENTERPRISE — PART OF A CAMPAIGN INVOLVING 55 MEMBER ORGANISATIONS ACROSS SIX WEST AND CENTRAL AFRICAN COUNTRIES. A national peasant platform and a national herders' federation, both named, both already inside a regional campaign. If you are a Nigerien farmer or herder, you do not need to found anything — those two bodies exist and are already federated across six countries. AND THE CAMPAIGN'S OWN FIGURES ARE THE ARGUMENT, WHICH IS WHY THEY ARE WORTH CARRYING: 2,000 PRODUCERS AFFECTED; 15 MINI-DAIRIES IN THE SIX COUNTRIES UNDER THREAT; 54 DISTRIBUTORS UNDER THREAT; 48 MILLION PASTORALISTS AND AGROPASTORALISTS IN THE SIX COUNTRIES WHOSE SURVIVAL IS AT STAKE; AND 276,892 TONNES OF SKIMMED-MILK-AND-VEGETABLE-FAT POWDER IMPORTED FROM EUROPE INTO WEST AFRICA IN A SINGLE YEAR. Forty-eight million pastoralists against a named tonnage of imported milk powder. That is how a livelihood campaign is built: count your own people, count the imports, and put the two numbers side by side. The campaign's own framing is the model — IF LOCAL MILK IS NOT PROTECTED, IT IS A WHOLE ECOSYSTEM AND ALL ITS ACTORS THAT ARE THREATENED. Substitute your own product and the sentence still works. THE PHYSICAL INSTITUTION THIS FILE HAD NOT RECORDED: MAISONS DU PAYSAN — FARMERS' HOUSES — EXIST AT NAMED NIGERIEN VILLAGES, AND EACH HAS ITS OWN UPDATED PLAN DE GESTION ENVIRONNEMENTALE ET SOCIALE PUBLISHED UNDER A COMMUNITY ACTION PROJECT FOR CLIMATE RESILIENCE, IN SEVEN VOLUMES, ONE PER NAMED LOCALITY, PUBLICLY DISCLOSED. A Maison du Paysan is a building in a village that belongs to the farmers who use it — stores, inputs, a meeting room. And each one has a published environmental and social management plan naming that specific village. Two uses: if your village has one, the plan is a public document you can demand and read; and if it does not, the seven published plans are the template for asking for one. THE ORGANISATIONS WITH CONTACTS: DIMOL, AT BP 13 874, NIAMEY, WITH TWO TELEPHONE NUMBERS, A FAX AND A PUBLISHED EMAIL, WORKING ON THE PROMOTION AND FLOURISHING OF NIGERIEN WOMEN AND ACCREDITED TO A CONTINENTAL HUMAN RIGHTS BODY; ONG-VIE KANDE NI BAYRA, WHOSE COORDINATOR ALSO CHAIRS A CADRE DE CONCERTATION AND WHICH IS DESCRIBED AS THE SAHEL PARTNER NOW GROUPING BENIN, NIGER, CHAD, TOGO AND MALI; AND ONG FAILATOUL HAIRAN, A YOUNG NIGERIEN NON-PROFIT CREATED BY ARRÊTÉ NUMBER 00445 OF THE MINISTRY OF THE INTERIOR ON 16 JULY 2016, WORKING ON ACCESS TO DRINKING WATER, HEALTH, EDUCATION, ENVIRONMENT AND HUMANITARIAN ACTION. An arrêté number and a date is what a Nigerien association's existence rests on — note the form: a numbered ministerial order from the interior ministry. Ask any organisation for its arrêté number, and know that is what yours will look like. AN ACCREDITATION TO A CONTINENTAL HUMAN RIGHTS BODY, as DIMOL holds, means the organisation can appear at that body's sessions. If your case needs to be raised continentally, an accredited national organisation is the vehicle — and there is one in Niamey with a published phone number. THE WOMEN AND LAND QUESTION IS DOCUMENTED: a published Sahel network paper addresses LA FEMME RURALE ET LE PROBLÈME FONCIER AGRICOLE AU NIGER, recording that 80% OF THE POPULATION IS RURAL, that AGRICULTURE IS THE PRINCIPAL ECONOMIC ACTIVITY, and that food insecurity structurally affects more than 30% of households. A paper specifically on rural women and the agricultural land problem in Niger, written through a Sahel network rather than about it from outside. If your dispute involves a woman's claim to farmland, that is the document to have in hand. AND THE STATE INTERLOCUTOR, NAMED: A CONSEIL NATIONAL DE L'ENVIRONNEMENT POUR UN DÉVELOPPEMENT DURABLE HAS AN EXECUTIVE SECRETARIAT IN NIAMEY WITH A NAMED FOCAL POINT. A national environment council with an executive secretariat is the body that receives national environmental questions. One named person, one office. WHO IT SUITS: Nigerien farmers, herders and women's groups, villages with or wanting a Maison du Paysan, and anyone needing a continentally accredited national organisation. CAVEATS: SOME FIGURES AND CONTACTS COME FROM PUBLISHED PROGRAMME AND CAMPAIGN DOCUMENTS — confirm before relying, and note Niger's security situation. For regional antennas in three regions, school nurseries since 1994 and the clause that implementers own the result, Niger's ANSEN entry; for 50 giraffes in 1996 and habitat loss named, ASGN; for the NGO directory, the Niger NGO directory entry.

trackers.name: The free field guide, in French and Arabic, for making phone footage stand up as court evidence — filming plans, camera reports, a collection plan agreed with your lawyer, and a 250-item library on archiving and verification
trackers.desc: THE PHONE FOOTAGE IS ALREADY THERE; THE PROBLEM IS IT WILL NOT STAND UP — anchor note first: THE FILE-WIDE SWEEP FLAGGED THIS ORGANISATION'S DOMAIN AS A SUBSTRING INSIDE LIBYA'S ENTRY, WHICH CITES A DIFFERENT ORGANISATION WITH A SIMILAR NAME. THEY ARE UNRELATED. THE GAP IT EXISTS TO CLOSE, STATED PLAINLY: CITIZENS AND ON-THE-GROUND HUMAN RIGHTS ACTIVISTS ARE BETTER POSITIONED TO COLLECT EVIDENCE OF HUMAN RIGHTS ABUSE THAN PROFESSIONAL INVESTIGATORS, BECAUSE INVESTIGATORS ALMOST ALWAYS ARRIVE AFTER-THE-FACT WHEN EVIDENCE HAS DETERIORATED OR IS GONE — HOWEVER, THE QUALITY OF CITIZEN VIDEO RARELY PASSES THE HIGHER BAR NEEDED TO FUNCTION AS EVIDENCE IN A COURT OF LAW. You were there and the investigator was not. That is an advantage nobody can buy — and it is routinely wasted, because the footage was filmed in a way a court cannot use. This file has recorded evictions, clearances and spills that hundreds of people filmed and nobody could prove. AND THE FIX IS SMALL: WITH SLIGHT MODIFICATIONS, THE FOOTAGE CITIZENS AND ACTIVISTS OFTEN RISK THEIR LIVES TO CAPTURE CAN SERVE AS EVIDENCE IN CRIMINAL AND CIVIL JUSTICE PROCESSES. SLIGHT MODIFICATIONS. Not better cameras, not training courses — a handful of habits. That is the cheapest evidentiary upgrade available to any community in this file. THE GUIDE'S FOUR SECTIONS: THE LAW, COVERING BASIC LEGAL PRINCIPLES AND PROCESSES; BASIC PRACTICES, WITH TIPS FOR CAPTURING VIDEO WITH ENHANCED EVIDENTIARY VALUE; FILMING FOR EVIDENCE, ON FILMING, ORGANIZING AND MANAGING YOUR VIDEOS FOR EVIDENTIARY PURPOSES; AND SHARING AND USING EYEWITNESS VIDEO IN HUMAN RIGHTS REPORTING AND ADVOCACY, WITH TECHNIQUES FOR VERIFYING VIDEO CONTENT AND GUIDELINES FOR USING EYEWITNESS VIDEO ETHICALLY. AND IT IS DOWNLOADABLE IN ENGLISH, ARABIC, FRENCH, SPANISH, UKRAINIAN AND RUSSIAN. French and Arabic cover most of the countries in this file that have no equivalent resource in their own language. Download it before anything happens and give it to whoever holds the camera. THE PIECE ALMOST NOBODY KNOWS ABOUT: HOW A COLLECTION PLAN CAN HELP INVESTIGATORS AND LAWYERS COMMUNICATE THEIR NEEDS TO FRONTLINE ACTIVISTS, SO THE FOOTAGE ACTIVISTS COLLECT CAN BETTER SUPPORT A LEGAL CASE. Ask your lawyer what they will need to prove, before you film it. A collection plan is that conversation written down — and it turns filming from an instinct into an assignment. Communities that do this bring back what the case requires; those that do not bring back an hour of shouting. THE FIELD METHOD, WHICH IS CONCRETE: GUIDANCE ON SAFELY AND EFFECTIVELY GATHERING VIDEO DOCUMENTATION AT THE SCENE OF AN ALLEGED HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATION — INCLUDING DEVELOPING A FILMING PLAN, CAPTURING DETAILS AND VARIOUS ANGLES, AND FILLING OUT A CAMERA REPORT. A CAMERA REPORT is a written note of who filmed, where, when and what — a page in a notebook. Without it, months later nobody can say which valley the clip shows, which is the commonest way good footage becomes useless. THE SAFETY WARNING, PUBLISHED BY THEM RATHER THAN BURIED: FILMING FOR HUMAN RIGHTS CAN BE DANGEROUS. IT CAN PUT YOU, THE PEOPLE YOU ARE FILMING AND THE COMMUNITIES YOU ARE FILMING IN AT RISK. CAREFULLY ASSESS THE RISKS BEFORE YOU PRESS RECORD — NOTHING STATED IN THIS GUIDE IS ABSOLUTE, YOU SHOULD MODIFY THE PRACTICES TO FIT YOUR NEEDS, AND WHEN POSSIBLE, SEEK SUPPORT FROM LOCAL EXPERTS. THE PEOPLE YOU ARE FILMING are put at risk too. A face in your footage is a name for somebody else's file — decide as a community who may be shown before the day arrives, not afterwards. THE LIBRARY: OVER 250 LEARNING MATERIALS TO SUPPORT ACTIVISTS IN USING VIDEO AND TECHNOLOGY FOR HUMAN RIGHTS, INCLUDING AN ACTIVIST'S GUIDE TO ARCHIVING VIDEO AND RESOURCES ON ARCHIVING AND PRESERVATION. ARCHIVING is the half everyone skips. Footage on one phone that gets seized, broken or sold is gone — and the guide on preserving it is free. THE VERIFICATION TIP SHEET: FOUR BASIC STEPS THAT CAN BE TAKEN TO DETERMINE WHETHER OR NOT THE CONTENT OF AN ONLINE VIDEO IS AUTHENTIC, INTENDED TO SUPPORT NEWS MEDIA, HUMAN RIGHTS ADVOCATES, INVESTIGATORS AND ACTIVISTS — ALSO AVAILABLE IN ARABIC. Use it on the other side's material as well as your own. A developer's promotional video of a consultation meeting can be checked for when and where it was actually taken. AND THE FAILURE MODES NAMED FROM PRACTICE, WORTH READING AS A CHECKLIST: STRICT AUTHENTICATION STANDARDS MUST BE MET; FILMMAKERS MAY FACE RISKS WHEN PROVIDING TESTIMONY; IMPROPERLY COLLECTED FOOTAGE CAN CONFLICT WITH WITNESS STATEMENTS; AND WITHOUT PROPER MANAGEMENT, CONFUSION CAN ARISE REGARDING WHERE THE FOOTAGE WAS FILMED AND WHAT IT DEPICTS. FOOTAGE CAN CONFLICT WITH WITNESS STATEMENTS is the danger nobody expects: a video that contradicts your own witness on a small detail damages the case rather than helping it. Take the statements and the film together, and check them against each other before either goes anywhere. WHO IT SUITS: any African community filming an eviction, a clearance, a spill or a police action, and the lawyers working with them. CAVEATS: A GUIDE AND A LIBRARY, NOT LEGAL REPRESENTATION — and their own warning about risk should be read first. For the offline tools where the community owns the footage, Equatorial Guinea's entry; for the free digital security helpline if a device is seized, Morocco's entry; for the organisation that takes evidence communities gathered themselves, Libya's entry.

trackers.name: NRGI (Natural Resource Governance Institute) — two African summer schools that teach civil society to analyse real oil, gas and mining contracts — full scholarships covering travel and tuition, evening one-on-one clinics, a post-course mentorship, and a free index scoring your own country
trackers.desc: THEY TEACH PEOPLE TO READ THE CONTRACT, AND THEY PAY THE FARE — THE FRANCOPHONE AFRICA SCHOOL, WHICH NAMES THIS COUNTRY AMONG ITS OWN: A REGIONAL KNOWLEDGE HUB RUN WITH A CENTRAL AFRICAN UNIVERSITY, WHOSE ANNUAL SUMMER SCHOOL HAS RUN SINCE 2011, USUALLY AROUND AUGUST — ATTRACTING UP TO 40 MEMBERS OF THE MEDIA AND CIVIL SOCIETY FROM 12 DIFFERENT COUNTRIES INCLUDING BURKINA FASO, CAMEROON, THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO, GUINEA AND NIGER — TAUGHT BY A DIVERSE TEAM OF EXPERTS WITH PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SECTOR BACKGROUNDS, MOSTLY FROM ACROSS FRANCOPHONE WESTERN AND CENTRAL AFRICA. Taught in French by francophone Africans, for francophone Africans. Most training in this file arrives in English through an interpreter; this one does not, and it has run every August for over a decade. WHAT IS ACTUALLY PRACTISED THERE, AND IT IS THE FIND: THE SCHOOL PLACES STRONG EMPHASIS ON PRACTICAL ANALYTICAL SKILLS — EACH LESSON PROVIDES PARTICIPANTS WITH THE OPPORTUNITY TO ANALYZE REAL-LIFE CONTRACTS, LEGISLATION AND FISCAL POLICIES, AND ENCOURAGES COMPARISONS BETWEEN COUNTRIES TO DETERMINE BEST PRACTICES. Real contracts, taken apart in a classroom. This file's Mauritania entry records where those contracts can be found; this is where somebody from your organisation learns what the clauses mean. A community that can read its own concession agreement negotiates differently from one that cannot, and the skill stays with the person afterwards. AND THE TWO TRACKS IN ONE ROOM: ATTENDING JOURNALISTS PRACTISE THEIR REPORTING AND WRITING SKILLS UNDER THE SUPERVISION OF A SKILLED EXTRACTIVE SECTOR REPORTER; CIVIL SOCIETY DELEGATES LEARN HOW TO ENGAGE IN CONSTRUCTIVE AND EVIDENCE-BASED POLICY ADVOCACY AROUND EXTRACTIVE SECTOR GOVERNANCE. Reporters and campaigners trained together for two weeks. The relationships formed there are why a journalist later takes your call — and this file's Gambia entry has the money that pays such a reporter to travel to your area. THE MENTORSHIP THAT CONTINUES: ALL PARTICIPANTS CAN SIGN UP FOR A MENTORSHIP PROGRAM THAT MOBILIZES EXPERTS IN SUPPORT OF STUDENTS' RESEARCH AND PROJECTS AFTER THE COURSE. Support that outlasts the fortnight. This file's Guinea-Bissau entry names the opposite pattern — consultants who parachute in and disappear — and a post-course mentorship is the answer to it. THE EVENING CLINICS, WHICH ARE THE MOST DIRECTLY USEFUL HOUR OF THE WHOLE COURSE: PARTICIPANTS CAN SIGN UP FOR ONE-ON-ONE CLINICS IN THE EVENING WITH COURSE EXPERTS TO DISCUSS THE CHALLENGES THEY FACE IN THEIR COUNTRIES AND REQUEST ADVICE. Bring your actual case. Somebody sent by a community can put the real concession, the real compensation offer and the real refusal in front of an expert who has seen fifty of them — free, and without hiring anyone. THE ANGLOPHONE SCHOOL AND ITS PRICE, STATED PLAINLY: A COMPREHENSIVE, INTERMEDIATE-LEVEL TWO-WEEK RESIDENTIAL COURSE COVERING GOVERNANCE ISSUES IN THE DECISION CHAIN OF NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, DEEPENING ANALYTICAL SKILLS IN FISCAL AND REVENUE MANAGEMENT POLICIES, TRANSPARENCY REPORTS, CONTRACTS AND KEY LEGISLATION — OPEN TO GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS, CIVIL SOCIETY ACTORS, JOURNALISTS, PARLIAMENTARIANS AND PRIVATE SECTOR ACTORS, AT APPROXIMATELY $2,500 INCLUSIVE OF ACCOMMODATION, FOOD AND TUITION, WITH A NAMED CONTACT PERSON. THE SCHOLARSHIPS, WHICH ARE WHAT MAKE IT REACHABLE: WITH DONOR SUPPORT, A NUMBER OF SCHOLARSHIPS ARE AVAILABLE TO ELIGIBLE PARTICIPANTS FROM SELECT COUNTRIES — AND FOR THE ADVANCED COURSE, A LIMITED NUMBER OF FULL SCHOLARSHIPS COVERING TRAVEL, ACCOMMODATION AND TUITION ARE AVAILABLE ON A COMPETITIVE BASIS FOR MEMBERS OF GOVERNMENT, CIVIL SOCIETY, PARLIAMENTS AND THE MEDIA FROM SELECTED RESOURCE-RICH COUNTRIES, WITH A RESTRICTED NUMBER OF EXCEPTIONS FOR OUTSTANDING APPLICANTS FROM OTHER COUNTRIES. WOMEN ARE PARTICULARLY ENCOURAGED TO APPLY. TRAVEL INCLUDED, and exceptions made for outstanding applicants from countries not on the list. So a community organisation in a country that is not named should still apply rather than assume exclusion — the exception clause is published for a reason. THE APPLICATION ITSELF IS SHORT: A SHORT ESSAY ON THE GOVERNANCE CHALLENGES ASSOCIATED WITH EXTRACTIVE INDUSTRIES IN THE APPLICANT'S COUNTRY, AND THE APPLICANT'S EXPECTATIONS OF HOW THE COURSE WILL BENEFIT THEM AND THEIR ORGANIZATION. One essay. Somebody who has lived the problem writes that more convincingly than any consultant. THE FREE INDEX ANYONE CAN OPEN TODAY: IT MEASURES THE QUALITY OF GOVERNANCE IN THE OIL, GAS AND MINING SECTORS — A ROBUST, EVIDENCE-BASED TOOL LETTING GOVERNMENTS, CIVIL SOCIETY ACTORS, PRIVATE COMPANIES AND CITIZENS UNDERSTAND HOW THEIR COUNTRIES PERFORM — A FREELY AVAILABLE PUBLIC DATA PRODUCT SERVING AS A GLOBAL BENCHMARK, COUNTRY AND SECTOR DIAGNOSTIC TOOL, AND A ROADMAP FOR POLICY AND PRACTICE REFORM, WITH COUNTRY PROFILES. Your country has a score and a profile setting out exactly which parts of its own system are weak. That is an official-looking document arguing your case before you say a word — and it costs nothing to print. THE TEACHING METHOD: LEARNING THROUGH PARTICIPANTS' OWN EXPERIENCES, USING SUSTAINED DEBATES AND POLICY LABS TO APPLY NEW KNOWLEDGE TO THEIR PROFESSIONAL ROLES, EXAMINING AND DEBATING THE PROS AND CONS OF POLICY DECISIONS FROM VARIOUS ANGLES. AND THE AFRICAN FINDING FROM THE INDEX, WHICH IS THE ARGUMENT TO CARRY: A REPORT ON SUB-SAHARAN AFRICA CONCLUDES THAT POLICYMAKERS, PARLIAMENTARIANS, CIVIL SOCIETY, MEDIA AND REGIONAL INSTITUTIONS SHOULD FOCUS MORE ON NARROWING THE IMPLEMENTATION GAP, WHICH WILL HELP RESTORE TRUST BETWEEN GOVERNMENT, COMMUNITIES AND INVESTORS — AND THAT CONSULTING STAKEHOLDERS HELPS GOVERNMENTS DESIGN LAWS ADEQUATE FOR THEIR INSTITUTIONAL CAPACITY, AND ASSESS WHAT IS NEEDED FOR EFFECTIVE IMPLEMENTATION BEFORE LAWS ARE PASSED. THE IMPLEMENTATION GAP, named by the sector's own diagnostic. This file has recorded the same thing from Burundi's unissued decrees to Kenya's unenforced judgment: the law usually exists and is not applied. Arguing for implementation of what is already law is a narrower and far more winnable demand than arguing for new law. WHO IT SUITS: African community organisations, coalitions and journalists facing an oil, gas or mining project who need somebody trained to read the documents. CAVEATS: COURSES RUN ANNUALLY WITH COMPETITIVE SCHOLARSHIPS AND ELIGIBLE-COUNTRY LISTS THAT VARY BY YEAR — and the paid fee is beyond most community budgets without one. For the repository where contracts are published, Mauritania's entry; for the coalition a national body joins with one form, Mauritius' entry; for story grants paying a reporter's travel, Gambia's entry.

trackers.name: The Huairou Commission's Community Resilience Funds — a fund applied for on a form and decided by an independent committee of grassroots women — paying in cash, tools or other resources, monitored locally by the leaders themselves, with named African member organisations and a farmer on the governing council
trackers.desc: A COMMITTEE OF GRASSROOTS WOMEN DECIDES WHO GETS THE MONEY — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE CARRIES A SHACK AND SLUM DWELLERS FEDERATION UNDER SOUTH AFRICA AND GHANA, A NAMED PARTNER OF THE FUND DESCRIBED HERE, AND THE REPUBLIC OF THE CONGO ENTRY NAMES A GLOBAL WOMEN'S LAND CAMPAIGN THIS NETWORK CO-DESIGNS. NEITHER IS RESTATED AND NEITHER HOST IS SHIPPED. WHO DECIDES, AND IT IS THE FIND: TO ACCESS THE FUNDS, MEMBERS COMPLETE A FORM DETAILING THEIR NEEDS AND HOW THEY PLAN TO MAKE USE OF THE RESOURCES — AND AN INDEPENDENT COMMITTEE OF GRASSROOTS WOMEN REVIEWS ALL APPLICATIONS AND DECIDES WHICH GO FORWARD, AND WHETHER SUPPORT WILL BE IN THE FORM OF CASH, TOOLS OR OTHER RESOURCES. Village women reviewing village women's applications. Every other fund in this file is decided by programme officers abroad, however participatory the language on the website — here the panel is the constituency. And the support can arrive as TOOLS rather than money, which sidesteps the bank account, the transfer fee and the argument about who holds the cash. WHAT THE FUND IS: A FLEXIBLE FINANCING MECHANISM THAT HAS OVER TEN YEARS CHANNELED FUNDS TO COMMUNITY RESILIENCE BUILDING INITIATIVES LED BY ORGANIZED GRASSROOTS WOMEN'S GROUPS — DESIGNED WITH GRASSROOTS WOMEN LEADERS AND THEIR TECHNICAL ALLIES. WHAT IT ALSO PAYS FOR, WHICH FEW FUNDS COVER: GRASSROOTS WOMEN'S ABILITIES TO TRANSFER AND AGGREGATE THEIR WORK THROUGH EXCHANGES, BUILD COALITIONS WITH OTHER CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS AND NETWORKS, AND LEVERAGE THEIR WORK TO ADVOCATE WITH GOVERNMENT INSTITUTIONS TO FORMALLY RECOGNIZE AND RESOURCE GRASSROOTS WOMEN'S RESILIENCE PRACTICES. Exchanges and coalition-building as fundable line items. This file has recorded over and over that a village which visits another village learns faster than one that attends a workshop — and that the travel is what nobody will pay for. THE MONITORING ARRANGEMENT: THE FUND IS MONITORED AT LOCAL LEVEL BY LEADERS THEMSELVES, AND AT GLOBAL LEVEL AT ANNUAL REVIEW MEETINGS WHERE IT IS EVALUATED IN TERMS OF SUCCESSES AND RISKS AND OPPORTUNITIES TO FURTHER SCALE. WHAT A MEMBER GROUP ACTUALLY DID WITH IT: ONE KENYAN MEMBER ORGANIZED GRASSROOTS WOMEN IN 5 COMMUNITIES TO MAP RISKS AND COLLECTIVELY PLAN AND DELIVER RESILIENCE BUILDING ACTIONS, ADDING MORE COMMUNITIES IN LATER YEARS — USING THE FUND TO IMPROVE SOIL pH, ACCESS TO CLEAN WATER AND SECURE LAND RIGHTS, AND TO ENHANCE FOOD AND NUTRITION SECURITY, ACCESS TO CLEAN ENERGY AND PARTICIPATION IN FOREST MANAGEMENT. SECURE LAND RIGHTS listed beside soil pH and clean water. A fund that treats tenure as a resilience expense will pay for the survey, the meeting and the paperwork that a conservation or emergency funder would refuse. THE ALTERNATIVE TO MONEYLENDERS: THAT MEMBER OFFERED GRASSROOTS WOMEN ALTERNATIVES TO MICROFINANCE INSTITUTIONS BY HELPING GROUPS SET UP THEIR OWN SAVINGS AND CREDIT SCHEMES — AND IS PLANNING TO ORGANIZE 500 GRASSROOTS WOMEN FARMERS INTO A COOPERATIVE TO LEND LARGER SUMS TO MEMBERS, EXPAND MARKETS FOR FARM PRODUCE, AND ACT AS A BRIDGE BETWEEN GRASSROOTS WOMEN AND MICROFINANCE INSTITUTIONS. A cooperative that can lend more than a savings group and negotiate with lenders as a block. That is the next rung above the no-outside-capital savings model filed under Djibouti, and it is reachable from it. THE AFRICAN MEMBER PROFILE, WITH ITS STRUCTURE PUBLISHED: ONE UGANDAN MEMBER WORKS WITH 53 CONSOLIDATED MEMBERS, 8 AFFILIATED ORGANIZATIONS IN RURAL AREAS, AND 2 MAIN PARTNERS — ENGAGED IN WOMEN'S RIGHTS, GOVERNANCE, HEALTH, LAND AND HOUSING, RESILIENCE AND GIRLS' EDUCATION, PRIORITIZING WOMEN'S LAND RIGHTS, FOOD SECURITY AND COMMUNITY RESILIENCE, AND HOSTING PEER LEARNING AND DISTRICT GENDER NETWORK SESSIONS. THE THEMATIC NETWORKS IT BUILT, WHICH ARE FOUR SEPARATE DOORS: GRASSROOTS WOMEN NETWORKING AROUND LAND AND HOUSING THROUGH A NAMED AFRICAN LAND LINK; CARE-GIVING THROUGH A HOME-BASED CARE ALLIANCE; RESILIENCE THROUGH A COMMUNITY PRACTITIONERS PLATFORM; AND SAFETY THROUGH A SAFER CITIES NETWORK. THE LAND ANALYSIS IT WORKS FROM: INSECURITY OF TENURE CHALLENGES GRASSROOTS WOMEN THE MOST, BECAUSE ACCESS TO AND CONTROL OVER LAND IS LINKED TO THEIR SOCIAL AND ECONOMIC STATUS IN THE COMMUNITY — AND SECURITY OF TENURE BECOMES KEY TO THEIR ECONOMIC, SOCIAL AND CONSEQUENTLY POLITICAL EMPOWERMENT. ITS THREE LAND OBJECTIVES, AND THE FIRST IS THE ONE TO DEMAND LOCALLY: PROMOTE GRASSROOTS WOMEN'S REPRESENTATION WITHIN LAND GOVERNANCE STRUCTURES; ENSURE THEIR ACCESS TO AND CONTROL OVER LAND; AND SUPPORT THEIR GROUPS' INNOVATION IN LAND MANAGEMENT, NUTRITION AND FOOD SECURITY. Representation within the land governance structures themselves — the committee, the board, the allocation panel — not merely consultation by it. That is a specific, checkable ask at a district land office. THE ARGUMENT ONE MEMBER MADE TO OFFICIALS, WHICH IS WORTH BORROWING WHOLE: THE WOMEN SHOWCASED TO LOCAL OFFICIALS HOW SECURE TENURE AND LAND RIGHTS BUILD SELF-SUFFICIENCY AND COMMUNITY RESILIENCE, REDUCING RELIANCE ON RELIEF AND SOCIAL SECURITY FROM GOVERNMENT, MEANWHILE POSITIONING THE GROUP AS A VIABLE PARTNER. Secure our tenure and we will need less from you. That reframes a rights claim as a saving to the district budget, and it is the argument most likely to move an official who is unmoved by everything else. AND THE TOOL NAMED AT A CONTINENTAL LAND CONFERENCE: WOMEN'S GROUPS IN RURAL WESTERN KENYA HAVE ORGANIZED THEMSELVES INTO GROUPS CALLED COLLECTIVE WOMEN FARMERS, WHICH THEY USE AS A TOOL TO FIGHT FOR LAND ACCESS FOR FOOD PRODUCTION — AND ONE MEMBER SECURED A FORMAL AGREEMENT WITH A MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE ENSURING AGRICULTURAL SUBSIDIES REACH IMPOVERISHED HOUSEHOLDS IN DROUGHT-AFFECTED REGIONS. A written agreement with a ministry, obtained by a grassroots women's group. Not a promise at a meeting — a formal agreement, which is the form to insist on. WHO IT SUITS: organised African women's groups needing small flexible money for land, water or food security work, and those wanting a route onto land governance bodies. CAVEATS: THE FUND IS FOR MEMBER GROUPS OF THE NETWORK, SO JOINING OR AFFILIATING COMES FIRST — the African member organisations named on its pages are the way in. For the savings model that needs no outside capital at all, Djibouti's entry; for the federation partner named here, South Africa's entry; for the deed-formalization service and its talking books, the Republic of the Congo's entry.

trackers.name: Up to $25,000 for species work, open to anyone directly involved with no organisation required — three rounds a year, a published 12% success rate, a searchable archive of every grant since 2009, and support-staff salaries in developing countries considered
trackers.desc: ANYONE DIRECTLY INVOLVED CAN APPLY. NO ORGANISATION REQUIRED — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S ESWATINI ENTRY COVERS THE TEAM-BASED CONSERVATION LADDER, ITS SÃO TOMÉ ENTRY THE MID-CAREER NATIONAL AWARD, ITS SOMALIA ENTRY THE ROLLING INDIVIDUAL SMALL GRANTS, AND ITS MOROCCO AND CAPE VERDE ENTRIES A CONSERVATION UNION HOST. THIS IS A DIFFERENT FUND WITH DIFFERENT RULES; NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. WHO MAY APPLY, WHICH IS THE FIND: ANYONE DIRECTLY INVOLVED IN SPECIES CONSERVATION CAN APPLY — WHETHER YOU ARE A FIELD RESEARCHER, A CONSERVATIONIST, A SCIENTIST, OR PART OF AN NGO. ELIGIBILITY EXTENDS TO ALL PLANT, ANIMAL AND FUNGI SPECIES CONSERVATION EFFORTS, WITHOUT DISCRIMINATION ON THE BASIS OF REGION OR SELECTED SPECIES. No registration, no institution, no host organisation named as a condition. A person who knows the animal or plant on their own land, and is doing something about it, is inside the definition. This file has recorded that most conservation money is unreachable without an organisation behind you; here the applicant can be a person. THE CEILING AND THE HARD RULE ABOUT IT: THE FUND MAXIMUM GRANT SIZE IS $25,000, AND ANY APPLICATION ASKING FOR MORE THAN THIS WILL BE REJECTED — THE TOTAL BUDGET OF A PROJECT CAN BE HIGHER IF THERE ARE OTHER SOURCES OF FUNDING, BUT THE FUND WILL NOT AWARD MORE THAN $25,000. Rejected, not reduced. Ask for $25,000 or less and let other funders cover the rest — and note that a larger total project budget is explicitly allowed, so this can be the first piece of a bigger package. THE STATED INTENTION: IT IS THE INTENTION OF THE FUND TO PROVIDE SMALL, TARGETED GRANTS TO LOCAL AND GRASSROOTS PROJECTS, BUT APPLICATIONS FOR LARGER GRANTS WILL OCCASIONALLY BE CONSIDERED AT THE INVITATION OF THE BOARD. THE SALARY AND TRAVEL RULE, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: THE FUND WILL CONSIDER COVERING SALARY EXPENSES OR TRAVEL COSTS FOR A SPECIFIC PROJECT — THIS WOULD USUALLY BE FOR SUPPORT STAFF IN DEVELOPING COUNTRIES — HOWEVER THIS CAN ONLY BE AS PART OF THE OVERALL GRANT AS OFFICIALLY APPLIED FOR, AND THE FUND WILL NOT CONSIDER APPLICATIONS WHICH ONLY COVER SALARY OR TRAVEL EXPENSES. Paying local field staff is explicitly allowed, and explicitly aimed at developing countries. Community members doing the patrols, the counts and the guiding can be paid from this grant — which is what turns volunteering into work people can afford to keep doing. But the salaries must sit inside a real project, so build the budget that way from the start. THE SPECIES CONDITION, STATED BLUNTLY: IF YOUR PROJECT IS NOT ABOUT AN ENDANGERED SPECIES IT IS PROBABLY NOT WORTH YOUR WHILE SUBMITTING AN APPLICATION — WITH A FOCUS ON CRITICALLY ENDANGERED, ENDANGERED, AND DATA-DEFICIENT SPECIES. DATA-DEFICIENT is the opening most communities miss. A species nobody has studied qualifies on the grounds that nobody knows — and a community that can name what lives on the land a project would clear has the beginning of an application. THE PREFERENCE FOR THE OVERLOOKED: IT IS POTENTIALLY INTERESTED IN APPLICATIONS FROM ANY COUNTRY AND FOR ANY SPECIES TYPE — AMPHIBIAN, BIRD, INVERTEBRATE, FISH, FUNGUS, MAMMAL, PLANT, REPTILE — PARTICULARLY THOSE THAT ARE THREATENED BUT DO NOT NORMALLY RECEIVE CONSERVATION ATTENTION. Invertebrates, fungi and plants on the same footing as mammals, and being unfashionable is an advantage. A frog, a snail or a tree in a valley due to be flooded is exactly the subject. THE ROUNDS AND THE LATE RULE: APPLICATIONS ARE REVIEWED IN THREE ANNUAL CYCLES WITH PUBLISHED SUBMISSION WINDOWS — AND APPLICATIONS RECEIVED LATE WILL AUTOMATICALLY BE REVIEWED IN THE FOLLOWING ROUND. A missed deadline is a delay, not a rejection. Three chances a year, and nothing is thrown away. THE COMPETITION, PUBLISHED HONESTLY: ONLY AROUND 12% OF APPLICANTS IN ONE YEAR RECEIVED A GRANT, WITH APPROXIMATELY 1,500–1,800 APPLICATIONS ANNUALLY ACROSS THE THREE ROUNDS. Roughly one in eight. Worth knowing before the effort — and worth reapplying in the next round rather than treating one refusal as the answer. THE RECORD SO FAR: OVER $27 MILLION ALLOCATED, 2,894 PROJECTS, 1,789 SPECIES ACROSS MORE THAN 150 COUNTRIES, AVERAGING AROUND $1.5 MILLION EACH YEAR TO AS MANY AS 200 PROJECTS — OPERATIONAL SINCE JANUARY 2009. Two hundred grants a year. Small money, but a great many of them, which is a different shape from the funds in this file that make four to six awards. THE SEARCHABLE ARCHIVE: A GRANTS EXPLORER PAGE WITH A DETAILED BREAKDOWN OF GRANTS AWARDED SINCE 2009, TOTALS BY SPECIES TYPE, AND PUBLISHED CASE STUDIES FROM SOME RECIPIENTS. Search it for your country and your species group before writing anything. It shows what was funded, at what size, and who did it — and the recipients in your country are people you can write to. THE CONTINUATION AND REVIEW RULES: IT IS HAPPY TO PROVIDE CONTINUATION SUPPORT FOR A PROJECT PREVIOUSLY SUPPORTED, NOW COMPLETED, AND FOR WHICH ALL REQUIRED REPORTING HAS BEEN RECEIVED BY THE DEADLINE; AND THE BOARD MAY ASK FOR AN APPLICATION TO BE PASSED ON FOR ADDITIONAL REVIEW, WHICH MAY ADD TO THE RESPONSE TIME. Reporting on time is what makes the next grant possible. That is the cheapest thing a small organisation can do to build a funding record, and this file has recorded it being neglected more often than any other step. AND THE SUBMISSION METHOD AND A SPECIAL CATEGORY: ONLY APPLICATIONS SUBMITTED THROUGH THE ONLINE SYSTEM WILL BE CONSIDERED, THOUGH SUPPORTING DOCUMENTS CAN BE SENT AS EMAIL ATTACHMENTS — AND A PILOT CATEGORY FOR THREATENED SOIL SPECIES IS SELECTED UNDER A NAMED SPECIAL FOCUS OPTION ON THE FORM. Online only, which is the real barrier for a rural applicant — plan for a trip to a connection, or ask a partner organisation to submit while the work and the money stay yours. WHO IT SUITS: individual African conservationists, community members and small groups working on a threatened or unstudied species — including one on land under threat from a project. CAVEATS: MUST BE ABOUT A SPECIES AND ITS CONSERVATION STATUS, $25,000 CEILING ENFORCED BY REJECTION, ONLINE SUBMISSION ONLY, AND ROUGHLY ONE IN EIGHT SUCCEED — it will not fund a land dispute as such. For the team-based ladder with no education requirement, Eswatini's entry; for rolling applications with no deadline, Somalia's entry; for the mid-career national award, São Tomé's entry.

trackers.name: MACUA (Mining Affected Communities United in Action) — a movement of mining-affected communities with 80+ branches, a women's structure inside each one, and a charter they wrote themselves demanding the right of consent — plus a won high court ruling that communities must be engaged in the laws affecting them
trackers.desc: THEY WROTE THEIR OWN MINING CHARTER, AND ITS FIRST DEMAND IS THE RIGHT TO SAY NO — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S ZIMBABWE BUCKET MENTIONS AN ALTERNATIVE MINING GATHERING; ITS SOUTH AFRICA BUCKET CARRIES A CENTRE FOR ENVIRONMENTAL RIGHTS HOST AND AN APPLIED LEGAL STUDIES NAME; ITS MADAGASCAR ENTRY THE INTERNATIONAL LEGAL PROGRAMME THAT CO-SIGNED A UN SUBMISSION ON THIS SECTOR; ITS MALAWI ENTRY THE SOCIO-ECONOMIC RIGHTS INSTITUTE. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THIS ORGANISATION HAS BEEN CARRIED AS A PENDING CANDIDATE SINCE ROUND 20 AND IS FILED HERE. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. THE DEMAND AT THE CENTRE OF THE CHARTER, WHICH IS THE FIND: COMMUNITY VOICE IN DECISION MAKING THROUGH NEGOTIATION BASED ON RIGHT OF CONSENT TO DETERMINE WHAT ACTIVITIES OCCUR ON ONE'S LAND — AND DEMOCRATIC COMMUNITY REPRESENTATION AND CUSTOMARY DECISION MAKING PROCESSES THAT ARE COMMUNITY BASED AND NOT BASED ON UNDEMOCRATIC TRADITIONAL AUTHORITY. The second half of that demand is the one almost nothing else in this file will say out loud. Companies and governments prefer to negotiate with a chief because a chief can sign for everybody; this charter, written by the affected communities themselves, refuses that shortcut. A community deciding who speaks for it should read that clause before its first meeting with a company. THE RIGHT IT CAMPAIGNS FOR IN PLAIN TERMS: IT CAMPAIGNS FOR THE RIGHT OF PEOPLE HARMED BY DESTRUCTIVE EXTRACTIVE INDUSTRIES TO HAVE THE RIGHT TO SAY NO TO DEVELOPMENTS ON THEIR LAND. THE RIGHT TO SAY NO, stated as the object of the campaign rather than as a negotiating position. Consultation without that right is what this file has recorded again and again as a formality performed on the way to approval. THE COURT WIN, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: THE MOVEMENT AND ITS WOMEN'S STRUCTURE JOINED A HIGH COURT CHALLENGE IN 2017 DEMANDING MODIFICATIONS TO A MINING CHARTER, AND WON A LANDMARK VICTORY IN FEBRUARY 2018 WHEN THE HIGH COURT RULED THAT COMMUNITIES ARE SIGNIFICANT PARTNERS IN MINING AND MUST BE ENGAGED IN LAWS AND POLICIES THAT AFFECT THEM. A ruling that communities must be engaged in the making of the law itself, not merely consulted about a project under it. That is the precedent to cite when a community is told the policy was settled before it arrived — and it was won by a community movement as a party, not by an NGO on its behalf. THE STRUCTURE A COMMUNITY WOULD JOIN: MORE THAN 80 BRANCHES ACROSS THE COUNTRY, AND EACH BRANCH INCLUDES A WOMEN AFFECTED BY MINING GROUP — WITH SOME BRANCHES ALSO INCLUDING YOUTH GROUPS UNDER A YOUTH AFFECTED BY MINING BANNER. A women's structure inside EVERY branch, by design rather than as an add-on. This file has recorded women's exclusion from community negotiation as the standard outcome; building the women's group into the branch constitution is the practical answer, and it is copyable by any community organisation. WHAT THOSE BRANCHES DO: THE STRUCTURES ARE SUPPORTED TO UNDERTAKE SOCIAL AUDITS AND COMMUNITY HEALTH SURVEYS TO UNDERSTAND THE EFFECT THAT CHANGES HAVE ON THEIR DAILY LIVES. SOCIAL AUDITS and COMMUNITY HEALTH SURVEYS done by the branch itself. That is community-generated evidence, produced before anyone needs it in court — and it is the kind of measured record the evidence database filed under Burundi will accept and the funders filed elsewhere will recognise. WHY IT EXISTS: A NON-GOVERNMENTAL, COMMUNITY BASED, UNITED FRONT FORMED TO PROTECT THE INTEGRITY AND INTERESTS OF PEOPLE IMPACTED BY MINING — A RADICAL MOVEMENT RAISING THE VOICE OF COMMUNITIES WHO HAVE NOT BEEN CONSULTED IN THE PROCESSES OF ALLOCATING MINING LICENCES, DEVELOPING COMMUNITIES AND DISTRIBUTING MINING RENTS AND WEALTH, BUT WHO BEAR THE BRUNT OF THE SOCIAL, ECONOMIC AND ENVIRONMENTAL DEGRADATION. THE REPRESENTATION GAP IT NAMES: IT STRENGTHENS THE AGENCY OF MINING-AFFECTED COMMUNITIES SO THEY CAN HOLD THOSE IN POWER TO ACCOUNT AND AMPLIFY THEIR VOICES NATIONALLY, GIVEN THAT THEY ARE NOT REPRESENTED IN STATUTORY AND REGULATORY BODIES THAT MAKE DECISIONS ON THEIR BEHALF. Not represented in the bodies that decide. That is the structural fact behind most of this file, named precisely — and the movement's answer is to build the counterweight rather than to petition for a seat. HOW THE CHARTER WAS MADE: THE COMMUNITIES COMMITTED TO A DEMOCRATIC PROCESS OF COLLECTING DEMANDS FROM MINING AFFECTED COMMUNITIES ACROSS THE COUNTRY AND BRINGING THEM TOGETHER IN A PEOPLES MINING CHARTER THAT SHOULD BE INCLUDED IN THE GOVERNING MINERALS ACT — AFTER A DIALOGUE HOSTED BY THREE NAMED ORGANISATIONS REPRESENTING COMMUNITIES IN 8 PROVINCES, AT WHICH A COORDINATING COMMITTEE WAS ELECTED. The method is the transferable part: collect the demands from every affected community, consolidate them into one document, and demand its inclusion in the statute. A single community's objection is answerable; a charter assembled from dozens is not. THE PRINCIPLE IT ASSERTS: AFFECTED PEOPLE MUST DETERMINE THEIR OWN DESTINIES — CHOOSING FOR OURSELVES BOTH OUR OWN DEVELOPMENTAL PATHS, AND TO PARTICIPATE IN ALL DECISION MAKING AND MANAGE OR CO-MANAGE THE UTILISATION OF OUR RESOURCES IF WE SO CHOOSE — WITH THE STATEMENT THAT THERE CAN BE NOTHING ABOUT US, WITHOUT US. WHAT THE ORGANISING PRODUCED: THE CAMPAIGN REACHED THOUSANDS OF PEOPLE AFFECTED BY MINING AND HELPED LOCAL ACTIVISTS TO FOCUS ON ASSISTING COMMUNITIES TO ORGANISE THEMSELVES INTO COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS AND ESTABLISHING ACTIVIST NETWORKS ACROSS THE COUNTRY. Helping communities constitute themselves as organisations was an output of the campaign, not a precondition for joining it. For a village with no registered body, that is the order of operations that actually works. THE SCALE AND THE COUNTER-SUMMIT: A NATIONAL ORGANISATION OF OVER SEVENTY AFFILIATES AND TWENTY CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, FORMED IN 2012 — WHICH HOSTED ITS OWN SUMMIT OF ABOUT 200 PEOPLE DELIBERATELY TIMED TO COINCIDE WITH THE INDUSTRY'S OWN CONFERENCE, ON THE STATED GROUND THAT GOVERNMENT WAS ENGAGING ONLY WITH BUSINESS PEOPLE ABOUT MINING WHILE THE AFFECTED COMMUNITIES WERE LEFT OUT. A counter-summit held in the same week as the industry conference. The press, the ministers and the investors are already assembled and already talking about mining; holding the community meeting then is the cheapest way to be heard, and the tactic transfers to any country with an annual investment conference. AND WHO CARRIES THE BURDEN, AS THE MOVEMENT PUTS IT: IT HAS AN EXTENSIVE FOOTPRINT IN RURAL AREAS AND UNDERSTANDS THAT IT IS MOSTLY WOMEN WHO CARRY THE BURDEN OF THE IMMEDIATE AND LONG-TERM EFFECTS OF BOTH FOSSIL FUEL EXTRACTION AND ENERGY PRODUCTION — WITH A NATIONAL SCHOOL DEBATE PROGRAMME INVOLVING LEARNERS FROM MARGINALISED COMMUNITIES. WHO IT SUITS: African mining-affected communities — as a structure to join or to copy, and as the clearest available model for a community-written charter and a women's branch. CAVEATS: A SOUTH AFRICAN NATIONAL MOVEMENT; ITS CHARTER AND ITS COURT WIN ARE TIED TO SOUTH AFRICAN MINING LAW, THOUGH THE METHOD AND THE STRUCTURE TRANSFER — and it is a movement to join, not a service to apply to. For the socio-economic rights litigation that defends organisers, Malawi's entry; for the international legal programme working on transition minerals, Madagascar's entry.

trackers.name: An NGO that helped more than 12 communities acquire over 400,000 hectares of commonage land — and then published the finding that only one of them ever received an infrastructure grant, with the list of what post-transfer support must actually include
trackers.desc: 400,000 HECTARES WON — AND ONE COMMUNITY OUT OF TWELVE GOT A GRANT — method and adjacency declared first: THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THE SHIPPED HOST, A SIBLING DIRECTORY HOST, AND FIVE SUBJECT SPELLINGS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; BOTH HOSTS AND THREE SPELLINGS ABSENT. THIS FILE'S LESOTHO BUCKET USES THE WORD COMMONAGE IN A DIFFERENT ENTRY, ITS TOGO BUCKET AGRO-ECOLOGY, AND FIVE BUCKETS FOOD SOVEREIGNTY, ALL ON OTHER HOSTS AND NONE ABOUT THIS ORGANISATION; ITS EQUATORIAL GUINEA AND LIBYA ENTRIES THE LAND-PURCHASE FUNDERS AND ITS MALAWI ENTRY THE MEMBERSHIP MOVEMENT. NONE IS RESTATED. THE HECTARES ACTUALLY ACQUIRED, WHICH IS THE FIND: IN ONE NAMED REGION IT ASSISTED MORE THAN 12 COMMUNITIES IN ACQUIRING MORE THAN 400,000 HECTARES OF COMMONAGE LAND. Four hundred thousand hectares into community hands, by an NGO whose job was facilitating the transfer rather than owning anything. That is the largest acquisition figure in this file achieved for communities rather than for a conservation body — and COMMONAGE is the mechanism: land held by the municipality and made available to the poor of that town, which exists in law in many countries and is almost never claimed. THE FINDING IT PUBLISHED ABOUT ITS OWN SUCCESS, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: OF THOSE COMMUNITIES, ONLY ONE HAS TO DATE RECEIVED AN INFRASTRUCTURE GRANT, AND MOST OF THE FARMS HAVE INFRASTRUCTURAL PROBLEMS — OUR EXPERIENCE HAS SHOWN WHERE COMMUNITIES OR INDIVIDUALS RECEIVED LAND, THERE IS A LACK OF COMPREHENSIVE POST SETTLEMENT SUPPORT. One in twelve, published by the organisation that ran the programme. This is the warning that belongs beside every land-acquisition entry in this file: winning the land is not the end of the process but the start of a second one, and the second one is where communities are abandoned. A campaign that plans only as far as transfer has planned half of it. WHAT IT SAYS SUPPORT MUST ACTUALLY INCLUDE: NOT ONLY EXTENSION SERVICES BUT INPUTS SUCH AS WATER, DEVELOPMENT RESOURCES, ACCESS TO CREDIT, ACCESS TO MARKETS, TRAINING AND CAPACITY BUILDING — WITH A SHIFT FROM JUST LAND REFORM TO A MORE COMPREHENSIVE LAND AND AGRARIAN REFORM AGENDA. Six items, and they are the checklist to put in writing before signing any transfer agreement. WATER first: land without water is a liability, and this file has recorded transfers where that was discovered afterwards. WHAT IT DOES: ITS CORE BUSINESS IS THE FACILITATION OF LAND REFORM AND CAPACITY BUILDING FOR ENGAGEMENT WITH LAND AND AGRARIAN REFORM, WORKING WITH THE POOR AND LANDLESS IN TWO NAMED PROVINCES — AND DURING THE PERIOD OF FORCED REMOVALS IT FOUGHT FOR THE RESTORATION OF PEOPLE TO THE LAND. CAPACITY BUILDING FOR ENGAGEMENT is the precise service: not representing the community, but making it able to negotiate the transfer itself. THE MINING LAW GAP IT IDENTIFIED TO A NATIONAL RIGHTS COMMISSION: LAND GRABBING, IN VIOLATION OF PEOPLE'S CIVIL AND POLITICAL RIGHTS AND THE PRINCIPLE OF FREE, PRIOR, AND INFORMED CONSENT, IS A SERIOUS ISSUE IN RURAL AREAS — AND THE NAMED MINERALS ACT DOES NOT FULLY RECOGNISE THE RIGHTS OF MINING-AFFECTED COMMUNITIES OR GIVE THEM AN ADEQUATE VOICE IN MINING DECISIONS. Filed as a route as much as a finding: the national human rights commission held hearings on rural land and took written submissions from organisations like this one. That is the domestic body recorded in this file's Algeria entry, being used exactly as intended. WHAT IT ORGANISES: PUBLIC FORUMS AND LOCAL SEMINARS IN COMMUNITIES TO RAISE AWARENESS, AND POPULAR AND POLITICAL EDUCATION SESSIONS — FACILITATED TOWARDS A GREATER UNDERSTANDING OF LOCAL CONTEXT AND DEEPER ANALYSIS OF THE ROOT CAUSES OF LANDLESSNESS, STRENGTHENING ORGANISATIONAL CAPACITY AND BUILDING SOLIDARITY AND NETWORKS WITHIN AND OUTSIDE THE PROVINCES. WHOSE VOICE IT DEFERS TO, STATED AS A CHOICE: WE HAVE MADE A CHOICE TO WORK WITH THE RURAL POOR AND TO FACILITATE THE VOICE, CHOICES, STRATEGIES AND APPROACHES OF STRUGGLE AS DETERMINED BY THE PEOPLE THEMSELVES. Worth holding an organisation to when it offers help: whose strategy is it, and who decides when to settle. WHOM IT PRIORITISES: IT BELIEVES IN THE PARTICULAR POWER AND POSSIBILITY OF YOUNG PEOPLE AND WOMEN AND ACTIVELY FACILITATES OPPORTUNITIES FOR THEIR GROWTH IN ITS STRATEGY. WHAT IT IS AIMING AT: SECURE ACCESS AND TENURE, OWNERSHIP AND CONTROL OVER PRODUCTIVE LAND, WATER AND NATURAL RESOURCES FOR LAND BASED AGRARIAN LIVELIHOODS. ACCESS, TENURE, OWNERSHIP AND CONTROL listed as four separate things. A community can hold one without the others — access without tenure, or ownership without control — and naming which one is missing is the first step in any negotiation. THE DEMAND IT DOCUMENTED: AN INCREASING DEMAND FOR LAND BY RURAL POOR PEOPLE IN THE TWO PROVINCES, AND LAND IS A PRODUCTIVE ASSET, SO LAND AND AGRARIAN REFORM ARE CRITICAL IN THE QUEST FOR JOB CREATION, POVERTY ERADICATION, FOOD SOVEREIGNTY AND ECONOMIC GROWTH. THE INDEPENDENT RESEARCH THAT CONFIRMS THE SAME GAP: TWO STUDIES POINTED TO A GAP BETWEEN LAND REDISTRIBUTION AND AGRARIAN DEVELOPMENT, WITH A RESEARCHER STATING THAT POST-TRANSFER SUPPORT IS SUCH A CENTRAL ISSUE THAT IT COULD EITHER MAKE OR BREAK LAND REFORM — BENEFICIARIES IDENTIFYING A CRITICAL NEED FOR AGRICULTURAL TRAINING, FINANCE AND FUNDING FOR PRODUCTION, FARMING EQUIPMENT AND GREATER ACCESS TO PROJECT-RELATED INFORMATION. Two independent studies reaching the organisation's own conclusion. When arguing for post-transfer money, that convergence is the evidence — and ACCESS TO PROJECT-RELATED INFORMATION being on the beneficiaries' own list is telling: people were given land and not told what had been planned for it. AND THE MISMATCH THAT RESEARCH FOUND BETWEEN WHAT PEOPLE DO AND WHAT THEY ARE OFFERED: DESPITE THE FACT THAT MOST BENEFICIARIES AND RURAL HOUSEHOLDS ARE INVOLVED IN GRAZING AND DRY-LAND CROPPING, THE KEY FOCUS OF MOST RURAL DEVELOPMENT NGOs AND STATE AGENCIES IS ON CRAFT PRODUCTION, ORGANIC FARMING AND THE MARKETING OF HIGH-VALUE CROPS — AND WHERE SMALL-SCALE FARMING UNITS WERE SUCCESSFUL, IT IS OFTEN BECAUSE THEY HAD EITHER ABANDONED OR AMENDED PROJECT PLANS RECOMMENDED BY THE STATE DEPARTMENT. The most useful sentence here for a community that has just won land: the ones that succeeded ignored or rewrote the official plan. Grazing and dry-land cropping is what people actually do; craft and high-value export crops is what they are funded for. Negotiate the plan, do not accept it. WHO IT SUITS: rural communities pursuing municipal commonage or restitution claims, and any community that has already won land and been left without water, credit or markets. CAVEATS: ONE COUNTRY AND TWO PROVINCES, AND SOME FIGURES DATE FROM AN EARLIER SUBMISSION — CHECK CURRENT PROGRAMMES BEFORE RELYING ON THEM; IT FACILITATES AND BUILDS CAPACITY RATHER THAN LITIGATING OR FUNDING PURCHASES. For funds that pay the purchase price, Equatorial Guinea's and Libya's entries; for the national commissions that take rural land submissions, Algeria's entry.

trackers.name: Fundação Príncipe
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: an NGO working to conserve Príncipe Island with and for its people, with a team of nearly fifty, more than 90 per cent of them local, running marine conservation, terrestrial conservation and community-engagement programmes in partnership with the regional authorities and local communities. The whole island has been a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve since 2012. Its terrestrial work documents species and the threats to them, builds protection initiatives with communities, and trains technicians in local government institutions and guide associations. USE IT: for Príncipe specifically. This is an island-scale organisation in an autonomous region, not a national body, so it is the wrong contact for a problem on São Tomé island.

trackers.name: São Tomé & Príncipe — Guiché Único para Empresas (GUE)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the GUE (Ministry of Justice) one-stop handles company constitution, alteration & extinction with online registration in 1–5 days, São Tomé & Príncipe. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: São Tomé & Príncipe — Ministério do Planeamento, Finanças e Economia Azul
trackers.desc: National budget authority; formulates & executes financial policy and prepares the State budget, São Tomé and Príncipe. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in São Tomé and Príncipe.

trackers.name: São Tomé & Príncipe — Tribunal de Contas
trackers.desc: National public-finance watchdog; the constitutional Court of Auditors (Art. 126) supervises the legality of public finances and audits the public accounts submitted annually by state institutions, São Tomé & Príncipe.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: Article 31 park fund, and the plans you can demand by date
trackers.desc: THREE INSTRUMENTS WITH NUMBERS ATTACHED. The Lei de Base do Ambiente (10/1999) and the Lei da Conservação da Fauna, Flora e das Áreas Protegidas (11/1999) were given effect by Lei n.º 6/2006 of 13 June creating the Parque Natural Obô de São Tomé (19,500 ha) and Lei n.º 7/2006 creating the Parque Natural Obô do Príncipe (8,500 ha). ‘Obô’ means virgin forest in forro. ARTICLE 31 OF LEI 11/1999 CREATES A FUNDO ESPECIAL DO PARQUE, funded by fines (coimas and multas) and fees — enforcement generates the management money, so ask whether the fund has been constituted and what has been paid in; documentation refers to the need to ‘create and consolidate’ it, so it may exist on paper first. DOCUMENTS YOU CAN DEMAND: the Plano de Manejo is the statutory management instrument on a 5-year cycle covering the park and its buffer zone — PNOST has had three (2009–2014, 2015–2020, 2021–2025); and the Plano de Gestão is annual, must coincide with the economic year, and is presented at the latest 30 days after approval. CHECK CONFFAP IS ACTUALLY CONVENING before addressing it: the coordinating Conselho was to function only from the first completed year of park services operating. NOTE THE BUFFER: on Príncipe the zona tampão is extensible to the entire remainder of the island. And delegated management is established practice — MARAPA and the Jalé Ecolodge have held management of part of PNOST under state supervision.

trackers.name: 21 Reservas Especiais — a live category, and HCV is the accepted method
trackers.desc: A DESIGNATION ROUTE THAT HAS JUST BEEN USED AT SCALE. With funding from the Rainforest Trust and the European Union, BirdLife International with academic institutions and national and international NGOs supported the Government in identifying and designating 21 new areas with the status of Reservas Especiais, totalling more than 12,300 hectares on São Tomé island, selected using High Conservation Value (HCV) criteria. THREE THINGS FOLLOW: Reserva Especial is a live, recently used category; HCV criteria are the accepted selection method, so frame a proposal in those terms; and the official rationale is directly quotable — the buffer zones, the lowland forests and the coastal and marine zones, also rich in biodiversity, have limited or non-existent protection. That is the state acknowledging the gaps lie outside the two parks, which is exactly where most sites are. THREATS NAMED IN THE PARKS' OWN DOCUMENTATION: disordered hunting, disordered and illegal felling, extraction of sand from beaches and palm planting for palm wine. Both parks are uninhabited, attributed to relief, high rainfall, difficult access and soils unsuited to agriculture — so a proposal covering inhabited land is a different and less-tested proposition here.

trackers.name: MARAPA — the São Toméan fishing NGO that co-manages the resource with fishers, and helped designate the country's marine protected areas
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a São Toméan non-governmental organisation founded in 1999 out of a French-funded artisanal fisheries programme, staffed by fisheries technicians, marine biologists and development workers, and treated as one of the country's leading NGOs. Its stated work is protecting marine and coastal habitats, co-managing fisheries resources, and supporting the people in the fishing chain — production, processing and marketing — including the palaiês, the women fish traders who are usually left out of any consultation. WHY IT IS THE ENTRY FOR THIS COUNTRY: on a small island state, the development that takes a community's livelihood is usually coastal or marine — a port, a resort, an industrial fishing licence, a mangrove cleared — and MARAPA is the organisation with the technical standing to contest it. It is one of three consortium members that delivered the national network of marine protected areas, alongside Fundação Príncipe and a development NGO, with international technical support; those designations were made with local communities and local conservation teams rather than over them, and the stated next problem is whether the protected areas are actually managed — which is where a community can insist on a role. Its longer-running programmes cover sea turtles and cetaceans, ecotourism around the Malanza mangrove and the Jalé beach camp near the Obô national park, and improving safety at sea for fishers. WHO IT SUITS: fishing communities and coastal villages in São Tomé and Príncipe facing a coastal project, a mangrove clearance or exclusion from a fishery. CAVEATS: a technical conservation and fisheries organisation, not a legal service — no litigation capacity, intake route or fee information was found; much of its work runs inside donor-funded projects, so what it can do in your area depends on which project is live. THE CONFLICT IT EXISTS TO HANDLE, AND WHY A COMMUNITY SHOULD CALL IT EARLY: the coastal zone of Caué district, the southern littoral from Angra Toldo to the bay of São Miguel, is described as having become a battleground of the artisanal fishing sector — it is where fish still remain, because the north of the island no longer has them — with coastal species still abundant near Ilhéu das Rolas, Sete Pedras, São Miguel and Porto Alegre. A MARAPA study found that 60 per cent of those fishing in the south come from the north of the country, and the resulting disputes, sometimes violent, have reached the port captaincy, the coast guard and the fisheries directorate. Resource exhaustion in one part of a country arrives in the next as a conflict between neighbours, not as a conservation problem — which is why the response MARAPA works on is SHARED MANAGEMENT of fishery resources: research on the species and the pressures on them first, then negotiated dialogue between the fishing groups. It was created in 1999 by fisheries technicians, marine biologists and development workers out of a French-funded artisanal fisheries project, and published in the Diário da República that December. It also supports the palaê women fish traders with training in handling and conservation of fish and with drying ovens supplied to a fishers' and palaê association, works alongside the national federation of fishers' and palaê associations, and developed an improved cookstove cutting fuelwood use by around 60 per cent.

trackers.name: São Tomé's legal assistance — provided for in law but NOT formally organised; the working route is the Ministério Público and the bar, district by district
trackers.desc: WHAT EXISTS AND WHAT DOES NOT, STATED FIRST BECAUSE IT SAVES A WASTED JOURNEY: in São Tomé and Príncipe judicial assistance and legal assistance ARE PROVIDED FOR BY LAW BUT ARE NOT FORMALLY ORGANISED. There is no legal aid institute to walk into here — do not spend a day looking for one. WHAT IS BEING BUILT INSTEAD, AND WHAT TO ASK FOR: a judicial modernisation programme working IN COLLABORATION WITH THE ORDEM DOS ADVOGADOS undertook to work immediately on DECENTRALISING LEGAL CONSULTATION AND PUBLIC ATTENDANCE BY THE MINISTÉRIO PÚBLICO IN EVERY DISTRICT OF THE COUNTRY, expressly so that citizens are not obliged to travel to the CAPITAL to bring a matter forward. So the two doors in São Tomé are the public prosecutor's public-attendance service in your own district and the bar association — ask for consulta jurídica by name. The same programme covers digitalisation of judicial procedures, aimed at removing the existing GEOGRAPHIC AND ECONOMIC BARRIERS to the justice system — the programme's own words, and the two barriers this whole file keeps recording. WHO IT SUITS: São Toméans with a land, inheritance or fishing-rights dispute who cannot travel to São Tomé city and cannot pay an advocate. CAVEATS: THIS IS A REFORM IN PROGRESS, NOT A STANDING SERVICE — confirm locally whether district attendance has actually begun before relying on it, and treat published dates as intentions; there is no organised legal aid scheme behind it. For the fishing sector and the Caué coastal conflict, São Tomé's MARAPA entry; for Príncipe, the Fundação Príncipe entry.

trackers.name: Obô natural parks — the Conselho de Gestão MUST include the communities resident in the buffer zones, and the buffer boundary is where the argument happens
trackers.desc: THE SEAT THE LAW RESERVES FOR YOU: São Tomé and Príncipe's protected-area system rests on the LEI DE BASES DO AMBIENTE (LEI Nº10/1999) and the LEI DE CONSERVAÇÃO DA FAUNA, FLORA E ÁREAS PROTEGIDAS (LEI Nº11/1999), under which LEI Nº6/2006 created the PARQUE NATURAL OBÔ DE SÃO TOMÉ and LEI Nº7/2006 the PARQUE NATURAL OBÔ DO PRÍNCIPE — together covering about 30% OF THE COUNTRY'S LAND AREA, with the Príncipe park incorporating ALL REMAINING NATIVE FOREST and occupying 45% of that island. THE PROVISION TO QUOTE IS ARTICLE 29 OF LEI 11/1999: the park's CONSELHO DE GESTÃO, a minimum of FIVE people, INTEGRATES REPRESENTATION OF THE LOCAL AUTHORITIES AND OF THE COMMUNITIES RESIDENT IN THE BUFFER ZONES. A statutory minimum of five with your community named among them is a seat, not a consultation — ask who currently sits for the buffer-zone communities and when the council next meets. The management plan is the park's principal tool, and the annual plan must be presented within 30 DAYS of the plano de manejo's approval, revised EVERY 12 MONTHS, and APPROVED BY THE CONSELHO DE GESTÃO. Twelve-month revision means a live document you can move each year rather than a settlement fixed once. WHY THE BUFFER ZONE IS WHERE THE ARGUMENT HAPPENS: the law provides a ZONA TAMPÃO surrounding the park limits WHERE HUMAN ACTIVITY IS MOST NOTABLE, serving simultaneously as A MODEL FOR SUSTAINABLE USE and as a BARRIER protecting the park's forests; the São Tomé park is uninhabited, with no permanent settlements, so the residents the law names are buffer-zone residents. AND THE RECORDED WEAKNESS, WHICH CUTS BOTH WAYS: park limits are well defined in the respective law WITH THE EXCEPTION OF THE ZONA TAMPÃO, WHOSE INTERPRETATION HAS REMAINED ARBITRARY. The one boundary the law left vague is the one your houses and fields sit inside — press for the buffer zone to be mapped, because an arbitrary boundary can be read against you as easily as for you. Documented pressures include unregulated hunting, sand extraction from beaches and palm planting for wine. WHO IT SUITS: São Toméan and Principense communities living beside or inside a buffer zone. CAVEATS: A STATE PARK WITH A STATUTORY COMMUNITY SEAT, NOT COMMUNITY TENURE. For fisheries co-management, São Tomé's MARAPA entry; for the concept-note test and HCV survey contracts, the Príncipe Foundation entry.

trackers.name: FONG STP and the Santomean environmental NGOs — a federation of 72 affiliated organisations, and Monte Pico, which runs park sectors under protocol
trackers.desc: THE FEDERATION AND WHO IS IN IT: the FEDERAÇÃO DAS ONGS DE SÃO TOMÉ E PRÍNCIPE (FONG STP) is the national platform, with 72 AFFILIATED NGOs recorded, of which TWENTY-TWO have or have had environmental education in their activities. One federation holding 72 members is the whole map of organised Santomean civil society — ask FONG STP which affiliate works in your district rather than searching organisation by organisation. NAMED ENVIRONMENTAL NGOs: ASSOCIAÇÃO MONTE PICO, created JULY 2006, whose objects are protection of the environment of São Tomé and Príncipe, support to ecotourism development and promotion; MARAPA, described as a very popular association whose target public is FISHERMEN, FISH-SELLERS AND THEIR CHILDREN; ADAPA; and ZATONA ADIL, which works with rural communities and farmers on QUALITY OF WATER SUPPLY and REFORESTATION. THE ARRANGEMENT WORTH COPYING, FROM THE OBÔ PARK'S OWN MANAGEMENT PLAN: it proposes that BY PROTOCOL the Associação Monte Pico ASSUME THE PARK'S SECTORS OF CONSERVATION, GUIDES AND ECOGUARDS, ECOTOURISM AND ENVIRONMENTAL INFORMATION — contractualising that PART OF THE PARK'S SERVICES ARE PROVIDED BY MEMBERS OF THE ASSOCIATION, working within the park directorate's hierarchy, WITHOUT OVERLAP OR SUBSTITUTION OF ENTITIES. A written protocol under which a local association staffs named sectors of a national park is the most concrete community-into-park arrangement in this file — it turns goodwill into jobs and a defined role. Ask for a protocol, name the sectors, and accept the hierarchy; that is what made this one work. THE FUNDING REALITY, PUBLISHED BY THE FEDERATION ITSELF: Santomean NGOs have A LARGE DEPENDENCE ON INTERNATIONAL AGENCIES AND COOPERATION AS THEIR MAIN FUNDING SOURCE, WITHOUT MEANS OR MECHANISMS OF THEIR OWN SUSTAINABILITY AND WITHOUT STATE FINANCIAL SUPPORT. FONG STP has nonetheless built an ADVOCACY AND POLITICAL-INFLUENCE dimension over several years, running a REDE DA SOCIEDADE CIVIL PARA A BOA GOVERNAÇÃO on public-policy monitoring with a partner organisation. An organisation with no state funding cannot be defunded by the state — that independence is worth naming when you choose who to work with. WHO IT SUITS: Santomean communities seeking an affiliate, a park role, or a route into policy monitoring. CAVEATS: A FEDERATION AND SMALL MEMBER ASSOCIATIONS, DONOR-DEPENDENT. For fisheries co-management, São Tomé's MARAPA entry; for the statutory buffer-zone seat on the park council, the Obô entry; for the concept-note test, the Príncipe Foundation entry.

trackers.name: The São Tomé bar association, its own verdict on the courts, and the seven district councils that hold autonomous decision-making powers
trackers.desc: THE BAR, ITS OWN VERDICT ON THE COURTS, AND THE DISTRICT COUNCILS — this file's São Toméan record had conservation bodies and no route to a lawyer: the ORDEM DOS ADVOGADOS DE SÃO TOMÉ E PRÍNCIPE (OASTP) WAS CREATED IN 2006, with its BASTONÁRIOS NAMED ON THE PUBLIC RECORD — including a jurist sworn in as bastonária in 2017 and a later holder who spoke publicly on the state of the courts. A bar association with a named bastonário is the one office that can point a São Toméan at counsel. Write to the bastonário, not to a firm — in a bar this small the head knows who takes what. AND THE BAR'S OWN ASSESSMENT IS WORTH CARRYING INTO ANY CASE: the bastonário stated that the functioning of the judicial system, WHICH WAS ALREADY IN ITSELF SLOW, EXCESSIVELY BUREAUCRATIC AND CARRYING AN ENORMOUS PROCEDURAL BACKLOG, became still slower and does not meet citizens' expectations — adding that much could have been done under the much-talked-of justice reform IF THERE HAD BEEN MORE POLITICAL WILL, and that COURAGE AND POLITICAL WILL ARE NEEDED TO REFORM THE SYSTEM PROFOUNDLY. A later bastonário raised concern at DELAY IN THE SUPREME COURT OF JUSTICE. The head of the bar says on the record that the courts are slow and backlogged. Plan for that: an injunction you cannot get in time is worth less than a decision stopped before it is made — which is why the council seat and the protocol in this file's other São Toméan entries matter more here than litigation. WHERE THAT DECISION IS MADE, AND IT IS CLOSER THAN THE COURTS: THE COUNTRY IS DIVIDED INTO SEVEN MUNICIPAL DISTRICTS — SIX ON SÃO TOMÉ AND ONE COMPRISING PRÍNCIPE — AND THE GOVERNING COUNCILS IN EACH DISTRICT MAINTAIN A LIMITED NUMBER OF AUTONOMOUS DECISION-MAKING POWERS AND ARE RE-ELECTED EVERY FIVE YEARS; PRÍNCIPE HAS HAD SELF-GOVERNMENT SINCE 29 APRIL 1995. Seven councils, elected every five years, holding autonomous powers. In a country of this size that is the most reachable decision-making body there is — and Príncipe's self-government means an island matter does not have to travel to São Tomé at all. ON THE COMMERCIAL SIDE, FOR COMPLETENESS AND WITH THE OBVIOUS CAVEAT: STP COUNSEL, headquartered in the capital, provides services to a clientele PREDOMINANTLY MADE UP OF INTERNATIONAL COMPANIES, as the local member of a regional alliance whose teams cover project financing, corporate and regulatory work, labour and REAL ESTATE, and are active in various judicial proceedings under the OHADA framework. The firm that advises the investors is also the firm that knows how the transaction is structured. Ask what it will and will not act on before you disclose anything — and ask the bastonário for an alternative first. ALSO NAMED: the UNIÃO GERAL DOS TRABALHADORES DE SÃO TOMÉ E PRÍNCIPE, the national trade union centre, affiliated internationally. A national union centre is a membership body with legal standing that most environmental campaigns never think to approach — plantation and port workers are affected people too. WHO IT SUITS: São Toméans needing counsel, a district-council decision, or an organised membership ally. CAVEATS: A SMALL BAR AND A SLOW COURT SYSTEM, stated by the bar itself. For the federation of 72 affiliated NGOs and the park protocol, São Tomé's FONG STP entry; for fisheries co-management, MARAPA; for the statutory buffer-zone seat, the Obô entry; for the concept-note test, the Príncipe Foundation entry.

trackers.name: Rede.Bio, the seven-NGO Santomean environmental network, and the co-management assembly in which fishing communities approved six marine protected areas the regional government then enacted
trackers.desc: THE ASSEMBLY THAT VOTED SIX PROTECTED AREAS INTO BEING: on Príncipe, SIX MARINE PROTECTED AREAS TOTALLING 29.82 SQUARE KILOMETRES WERE APPROVED IN AN ASSEMBLEIA DE COGESTÃO WITH ALL INTERESTED PARTIES — GOVERNMENT ENTITIES, FISHING COMMUNITIES AND CIVIL SOCIETY ENTITIES — AND THE REGIONAL ASSEMBLY AND THE REGIONAL GOVERNMENT THEN PROMULGATED THE DECREE-LAW FOR THEIR LEGAL ESTABLISHMENT. A co-management assembly in which the fishing communities sat as parties, voting areas into existence, and the elected regional body converting that vote into law. That is the sequence: the assembly decides, the government enacts. Ask whether the body being convened about your waters is an ASSEMBLY that approves, or a consultation that advises — the two words carry entirely different weight, and Príncipe shows which one produces a decree. The work sits under a project running SINCE 2018 BY A CONSORTIUM OF FOUR NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL NGOs, TITLED THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A NETWORK OF MARINE PROTECTED AREAS IN SÃO TOMÉ AND PRÍNCIPE THROUGH A CO-MANAGEMENT APPROACH, on dedicated ocean-fund financing; the island's biosphere reserve includes a MARINE CORE ZONE OF 11,199 HECTARES. THE NETWORK TO JOIN: SINCE 2017, REDE.BIO BRINGS TOGETHER SEVEN SÃO TOMEAN ENVIRONMENTAL NGOs TO PROMOTE INTEGRATED AND SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT FOUNDED ON THE PROTECTION AND VALORISATION OF THE COUNTRY'S NATURAL PATRIMONY — NAMELY BY REINFORCING THE PARTICIPATION OF CIVIL SOCIETY IN ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT. Seven organisations in a country of two islands is most of the sector in one room. Reinforcing civil society participation in environmental management is its stated purpose, not a side activity — which makes it the address for a community that wants a seat rather than a service. AND THE CONTRACTING ROUTE WRITTEN INTO THE OBÔ PARK'S OWN MANAGEMENT PLAN, WHICH IS THE MOST DIRECTLY COPYABLE THING HERE: THE PLAN PROVIDES THAT MANAGEMENT OF PART OF THE PARK'S TERRITORY AND ACTIVITIES MAY BE COMMITTED BY CONTRACT OR PROTOCOL TO A NAMED NGO AND/OR TO A NAMED ECOLODGE — WITH THE STATE PARK SERVICE REMAINING ALWAYS THE OFFICIAL AND FORMAL ENTITY, ITS SUPERVISION GUARANTEED BY THE MANAGEMENT AND HANDLING PLANS, AND EXPLICITLY WITH NO OVERLAP OR SUBSTITUTION OF ENTITIES. Part of a national park handed to an NGO by contract or protocol, with the state keeping formal ownership and supervision. That is the arrangement to ask for where a full transfer is refused: you are not asking to replace the park service, you are asking for a protocol over a defined part — and the plan itself says the two do not overlap. It also names the guarantee that makes it acceptable to the state, which is that the supervision lives in the management plan. The same plan records that the park's own field presence IS ASSURED BY ELEMENTS OF A NAMED SANTOMEAN ASSOCIATION, and that ecolodge arrangements in a named zone COULD BE RAPIDLY CONTRACTUALISED. Rapidly contractualised is the state's own phrase for how fast this can move when the community body already exists. Have the association registered before the conversation starts. ALSO RECORDED: the four organisations most often named in Santomean conservation are A FISHING AND MARINE NGO PUBLISHED IN THE DIÁRIO DA REPÚBLICA N°14 IN DECEMBER 1999 AND CREATED BY FISHERIES TECHNICIANS, MARINE BIOLOGISTS AND DEVELOPMENT AGENTS; AN ASSOCIATION CREATED IN JULY 2006 BY A GROUP OF SÃO TOMÉANS TRAINED UNDER A REGIONAL FOREST PROGRAMME, WORKING ON ECOTOURISM AND SUSTAINABLE RURALITY AND SUPPORTING PROTECTED-AREA MANAGEMENT; A FOUNDATION ESTABLISHED 2015 WORKING IN CLOSE PARTNERSHIP WITH REGIONAL AUTHORITIES AND COMMUNITIES; and a coastal-development association. Note the founding pattern twice over: both the 1999 and the 2006 organisation were created by people already trained and working on a project who chose to constitute themselves as an association when the project ended. If a programme is winding up in your area, that is the moment its trained staff can become a permanent local body. WHO IT SUITS: Santomean fishing communities, villages beside the Obô parks, and associations seeking a network or a management protocol. CAVEATS: A SMALL SECTOR ON DONOR PROJECT CYCLES — confirm which consortium projects are current. For the fishing NGO that co-manages the resource, São Tomé's MARAPA entry; for a federation of 72 affiliates, FONG STP; for the Conselho de Gestão that MUST include the communities, the Obô natural parks entry; for the bar's own verdict on the courts, the São Tomé bar entry.

trackers.name: São Tomé's four-organisation marine division of labour with its own public network site, the Fundação Fluta Non and Associação Roça Mundo, and the Fogobô stove that cuts fuelwood by about 60%
trackers.desc: WHEN THE PROJECT ENDED, THE STAFF FOUNDED AN ASSOCIATION — and that is the origin story worth carrying out of São Tomé: an artisanal fisheries support project financed by a foreign development agency came to an end, and THE STAFF ATTACHED TO THE PROJECT DECIDED TO CREATE AN ASSOCIATION, PUBLISHED IN THE DIÁRIO DA REPÚBLICA N°14 IN DECEMBER 1999 — CREATED BY FISHERIES TECHNICIANS, MARINE BIOLOGISTS AND DEVELOPMENT AGENTS, AND KEEPING THAT PLURIDISCIPLINARITY IN ITS TEAM SO AS TO HAVE A GLOBAL VIEW OF THE ARCHIPELAGO'S PROBLEMS. A project ends, the funder leaves, and the national staff constitute themselves as an association instead of dispersing. That is the single most reproducible act in this file: when a programme closes in your area, the people it trained are still there, and a founding notice in the official gazette is what turns them into an institution that outlasts it.
