THE DIVISION OF LABOUR, STATED EXPLICITLY BY THE PARTNERS THEMSELVES: FOUR ORGANISATIONS JOINED THEIR COMPETENCES — AN INTERNATIONAL CONSERVATION BODY FOR NATURE CONSERVATION; A PRÍNCIPE FOUNDATION FOR COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT ON THAT ISLAND; MARAPA FOR THE REPRESENTATION OF THE FISHERS; AND A FOURTH ORGANISATION FOR COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION AND SUSTAINABLE LIVELIHOODS — TO ACHIEVE, WITH SEVERAL INTERNATIONAL FUNDERS, SOMETHING NONE OF THE ORGANISATIONS COULD HAVE ACHIEVED ALONE. Four organisations, four named competences, one of them explicitly REPRESENTATION OF THE FISHERS. That is the seat to check for in any coalition offered to your community: is somebody in the room whose stated job is representing you, as distinct from conserving the resource or delivering the project? If not, the coalition is incomplete however good its funding. AND THE COALITION HAS ITS OWN PUBLIC SITE FOR THE MARINE PROTECTED AREA NETWORK, WHICH INTRODUCES THE TEAMS BY NAME, AND WHOSE WORK INCLUDES COLLECTING HOLISTIC DATA ON FISHING ACTIVITY — while ALTERNATIVE SOURCES OF INCOME TO SUPPORT FISHING COMMUNITIES ARE IMPLEMENTED UNDER THE NAME COMMUNITY IDEAS. COMMUNITY IDEAS as the name of the livelihoods component. The naming matters: it says the ideas come from the community and the project pays for them, rather than the reverse. Ask, of any alternative-livelihoods offer, whose idea it was — and ask for the community ideas process by name. TWO SANTOMEAN BODIES THIS FILE DID NOT HOLD: THE FUNDAÇÃO FLUTA NON, WITH A NAMED ADMINISTRATOR, AND THE ASSOCIAÇÃO ROÇA MUNDO, WITH A NAMED PRESIDENT — both partners, alongside the Príncipe foundation, in an EU-funded project on TOURISM AND COMMUNITIES IN THE PROTECTION OF BIODIVERSITY, coordinated with the environment ministry and articulated with the agriculture, fisheries and rural development ministry. A foundation and an association with named officers, working tourism and communities together with two ministries. On a small archipelago the number of organisations is small enough to learn by heart — these two complete the list this file holds, and the roça is the São Toméan plantation estate, so an association named for it is working the estates where people actually live. THE MEASURED TECHNOLOGY, WITH THE SAVING STATED: MARAPA DEVELOPED THE FOGOBÔ — AN IMPROVED STOVE BASED ON THE PRINCIPLES OF THE ROCKET STOVE MODEL, ALLOWING MORE EFFECTIVE COMBUSTION AND RESULTING IN AN OPTIMISATION OF FUELWOOD CONSUMPTION OF ABOUT 60% LESS WOOD, DESCRIBED AS AN IMPORTANT MEASURE TO COMBAT DEFORESTATION — DEVELOPED UNDER A LANDSCAPE RESTORATION PROJECT IMPLEMENTED BY A UN FOOD AGENCY AND EXECUTED BY THE NATIONAL FORESTS AND BIODIVERSITY DIRECTORATE. Sixty per cent less firewood, from a stove designed by a national NGO and named in the local language. That is a deforestation intervention a household adopts because it saves them work, not because they were asked to. If your forest is being cut for fuel, the stove is the lever — and here is one already designed, tested and named in a country with the same problem. THE PROBLEMS THE SAME ORGANISATION NAMED IN PRINT: INSUFFICIENT AWARENESS AND TRAINING OF THE COMMUNITY ON THE DISASTROUS CONSEQUENCES OF HUMAN ACTIONS; WEAK ACCESS TO INFORMATION AND ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION BY THE COMMUNITY IN GENERAL; LACK OF CONTROL OF COASTAL PROTECTION AND OF INSPECTION IN FISH CAPTURE; AND CONSERVATION AND SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH THAT IS LITTLE EFFECTIVE, DUE TO SCARCE FINANCIAL AND HUMAN RESOURCES. An organisation naming the weakness of inspection and of its own sector's research in a published book is being straight with its readers. Scarce human resources is the constraint behind most of what this file records — and it is why the four-way division of labour above exists. WHO IT SUITS: São Toméan fishing and roça communities, and anyone whose programme is closing or whose forest is being cut for fuel. CAVEATS: A SMALL ARCHIPELAGO WITH FEW ORGANISATIONS — the same names recur, so approach the coalition rather than one body. For the fishing NGO that co-manages the resource, São Tomé's MARAPA entry; for the Príncipe foundation, its own entry; for the seven-NGO network and the co-management assembly that voted six marine protected areas, Rede.Bio; for the Conselho de Gestão that must include the communities, the Obô parks entry; for a federation of 72 affiliates, FONG STP.

trackers.name: Blue Ventures — the organisation behind community-run marine areas — a 30-day closure that raised village income 136% in a peer-reviewed study, a free guide in Kiswahili and English, and 32 partner organisations supported across 10 countries
trackers.desc: THIRTY DAYS CLOSED, AND VILLAGE INCOME ROSE 136 PER CENT — declared adjacency first: THIS FILE'S MADAGASCAR ENTRY COVERS THE FISHERS' OWN NATIONAL NETWORK OF 175+ ASSOCIATIONS. THIS ENTRY IS THE SUPPORTING ORGANISATION, THE FREE GUIDE, THE MEASURED RESULTS AND THE PARTNER COUNTRIES — NONE OF WHICH IS IN IT. THE NUMBER THAT WINS THE ARGUMENT AT A VILLAGE MEETING: IN A SEVEN-YEAR PEER-REVIEWED STUDY, THE 30-DAY TEMPORARY CLOSURE MODEL YIELDED SIGNIFICANT AND RECURRING ECONOMIC BENEFITS FOR LOCAL COMMUNITIES — INCLUDING A 136 PERCENT AVERAGE INCREASE IN VILLAGE INCOME IN THE MONTH AFTER A CLOSURE, AND AN 87 PERCENT INCREASE IN FISH CAUGHT PER DAY. Close one area for a month and earn more afterwards, measured over seven years and peer-reviewed. Conservation is almost always presented to fishing families as a sacrifice; here is the study showing the opposite, with figures. If you are asking your own people to accept a closure, this is the evidence to bring — and thirty days is short enough that a household can survive the wait. WHAT AN LMMA ACTUALLY IS: AREAS OF OCEAN MANAGED BY COASTAL COMMUNITIES TO HELP PROTECT FISHERIES AND SAFEGUARD MARINE LIFE, PLACING LOCAL COMMUNITIES AT THE HEART OF MANAGEMENT — A HUMAN RIGHTS-BASED, COST-EFFECTIVE AND SCALABLE SOLUTION — WITH RESOURCES MANAGED ALMOST ENTIRELY BY LOCAL COMMUNITIES AND FISHERY STAKEHOLDERS THAT LIVE IN THE REGION, AND GOALS TYPICALLY INCLUDING MAINTAINING THE LIVELIHOOD AND ECONOMIC AND CULTURAL GOALS OF THE LOCAL COMMUNITY ALONGSIDE ENVIRONMENTAL GOALS. ECONOMIC AND CULTURAL GOALS written into the definition beside the environmental ones. That is the distinction from a marine park declared over your heads, and it is the wording to insist on when a protected area is proposed near you. THE TOOLS CO-MANAGEMENT PUTS IN COMMUNITY HANDS: COMMUNITIES, IN COLLABORATION WITH LOCAL GOVERNMENT, DEVELOP MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES FOR THEIR LOCAL MARINE ENVIRONMENT WHICH RESPOND TO THEIR NEEDS AND ADDRESS LOCAL THREATS — INCLUDING GEAR RESTRICTIONS, NO-TAKE ZONES AND TEMPORARY FISHERY CLOSURES — AND GROUPS HAVE ALSO FOCUSED ON REDUCING DEPENDENCY ON FISHING BY DIVERSIFYING INTO ECOTOURISM AND AQUACULTURE. THE FREE GUIDE, IN A LANGUAGE PEOPLE READ: A GUIDE TO LOCAL MANAGEMENT OF MARINE RESOURCES, AVAILABLE IN BOTH KISWAHILI AND ENGLISH — GIVING AN OVERVIEW OF THE APPROACH, INTRODUCING THE IDEAS AND PROCESSES INVOLVED IN ESTABLISHING CO-MANAGEMENT, AND SETTING OUT THE LEGAL FRAMEWORKS IN TWO NAMED COUNTRIES WHICH SUPPORT ITS IMPLEMENTATION. It names the laws that already permit this. Most communities are told co-management would need a new law; the guide shows where the legal basis already exists — which turns the conversation with a fisheries officer from a request into a citation. WHAT THEY GIVE PARTNERS: 32 PARTNERS ACROSS 10 COUNTRIES SUPPORTED WITH TOOLKITS, TRAINING, TECHNICAL ADVICE, MENTORING, AND LEARNING EXCHANGES — AND AS OF 2023, 750,000 PEOPLE IN 13 COUNTRIES SUPPORTED TO DEVELOP PERIODIC FISHERY CLOSURES. They work through community-based organisations rather than replacing them. LEARNING EXCHANGES is the item to ask for: sending your committee to a village where a closure already works does more than any workshop, and this file has recorded that same method succeeding from the Karamoja cluster to the Comoros. THE AFRICAN SPREAD, SO YOU CAN FIND YOUR NEAREST EXAMPLE: THE CORE MODEL HAS BEEN ADOPTED BY PARTNERS IN TANZANIA, MOZAMBIQUE, COMOROS, MAURITIUS AND MAYOTTE AMONG OTHERS, WITH REPLICATION UNDERWAY IN KENYA — AND GUINEA-BISSAU IS A NEW VENTURE, FOCUSED ON DATA-DRIVEN COMMUNITY-LED MANAGEMENT OF FISHERIES WHICH ARE OF ENORMOUS IMPORTANCE TO COASTAL COMMUNITIES, IN PARTICULAR WOMEN. IN PARTICULAR WOMEN. Gleaning and near-shore collection are usually women's work and usually left out of fisheries policy; naming that is what makes a management plan fair rather than merely agreed. THE POLICY RESULT THE FISHERS THEMSELVES WON: ADVOCACY BY THE NATIONAL NETWORK RESULTED IN AMBITIOUS NATIONAL COMMITMENTS FROM A MINISTER OF FISHERIES TO TRIPLE THE AREA OF MARINE PROTECTED AREAS AND REFORM THE MARINE LEGISLATION TO SUPPORT COMMUNITY FISHING RIGHTS. THE HONEST LIMITS, PUBLISHED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: OTHERS HAVE STRUGGLED TO ENFORCE THEIR PROPOSED MANAGEMENT MEASURES, SUCH AS TEMPORARY CLOSURES AND NO-TAKE ZONES, OR TO MAINTAIN GOVERNANCE ACTIVITIES SUCH AS REGULAR COMMITTEE MEETINGS — AND A STUDY DOCUMENTS LIMITS TO ENFORCEMENT, PARTICIPATION AND INSTITUTIONAL CAPACITY. REGULAR COMMITTEE MEETINGS is the unglamorous failure point. The closure works; the committee stops meeting. Budget for the meetings, not just the launch. AND THE DISTRIBUTIONAL QUESTION, NAMED PLAINLY: RULES FOR TEMPORARY CLOSURES DETERMINE WHO AGREES THE RESTRICTIONS, WHO CAN COMPLY, WHO BEARS LOST INCOME AND WHO GAINS WHEN CATCHES RECOVER. Four separate questions, and they can have four different answers. A closure agreed by boat owners and borne by shore gleaners is not a community decision. Ask all four out loud before the rules are set. THE PRESSURE BEHIND IT ALL: THERE IS EVIDENCE THAT UP TO 75% OF ALL FISH CAUGHT IN SELECT VILLAGES IS NOW SOLD TO OUTSIDE ENTITIES FOR INTERNATIONAL EXPORT. Three quarters of the catch leaving for export markets. The pressure on the reef is not local appetite — which means local restraint alone cannot fix it, and the buyers belong in the conversation. WHO IT SUITS: African coastal and island fishing communities, and community-based organisations wanting to establish a managed area or a closure. CAVEATS: IT WORKS THROUGH PARTNER ORGANISATIONS RATHER THAN TAKING DIRECT REQUESTS FROM EVERY VILLAGE — approach the nearest partner. For the fishers' own national network and the 700% octopus landing increase, Madagascar's MIHARI entry; for the marine areas fishers establish without legal designation, Mauritius' voluntary conservation areas entry; for the fishing community councils, Mozambique's entry.

trackers.name: The Whitley Award (Whitley Fund for Nature) — £50,000 for a grassroots leader who is a national of their own country — with published rules that exclude in-country staff of Global North NGOs, a continuation ladder 55% of winners climb, and an African island exception written into the criteria
trackers.desc: THE MONEY GOES TO THE LOCAL ORGANISATION, NOT THE FOREIGN ONE'S FIELD OFFICE — THE ELIGIBILITY LINE THAT IS THE FIND, PUBLISHED IN THEIR OWN CRITERIA: APPLICANTS SHOULD WORK FOR OR LEAD LOCALLY INCORPORATED NGOs IN THE GLOBAL SOUTH, RATHER THAN BE IN-COUNTRY STAFF EMPLOYED BY NGOs HEADQUARTERED IN THE GLOBAL NORTH. A funder that explicitly declines to fund the country office of a foreign organisation. This file has recorded again and again that money labelled for African communities lands with international NGOs who then employ Africans to spend it; here that route is closed by rule. If your organisation is small and locally registered, that exclusion is working in your favour. THE NATIONALITY RULE: THE AWARDS SUPPORT NATIONALS OF THE COUNTRY IN WHICH THEY ARE WORKING — YOU WERE BORN THERE, OR HAVE LIVED THERE A LONG TIME AND ACHIEVED NATIONAL STATUS. IF YOU ARE NOT A NATIONAL BUT BELIEVE YOU HAVE AN EXCEPTIONAL CASE BASED ON LONG TERM RESIDENCY OF 15+ YEARS AND A DEMONSTRABLE COMMITMENT TO THAT COUNTRY OR REGION, CONTACT THEM. AND THE COUNTRY RULE, WITH AN AFRICAN EXCEPTION WRITTEN IN: PROJECTS LED BY LOCAL LEADERS BASED IN COUNTRIES NOT DEFINED AS A HIGH INCOME ECONOMY — WITH EXCEPTIONS TO THIS CRITERION INCLUDING EQUATORIAL GUINEA AND CERTAIN ISLAND NATIONS. Read that exception carefully before assuming your country qualifies or does not: income classification excludes some places and the published exception list adds others back. When in doubt their own page says to write and ask, which costs an email. THE MONEY, RECORDED HONESTLY BECAUSE THE FIGURE HAS MOVED: EACH AWARD IS WORTH £50,000 IN PROJECT FUNDING OVER ONE YEAR IN CURRENT CALLS; EARLIER MATERIAL GIVES £40,000. A GOLD AWARD FOR A PREVIOUS WINNER IS WORTH £60,000 OVER UP TO TWO YEARS. THE LADDER, AND ITS SUCCESS RATE IS THE NUMBER TO NOTICE: WINNERS BECOME ELIGIBLE FOR FUTURE CONTINUATION FUNDING — OPEN ONLY TO PREVIOUS AWARD WINNERS, WHO CAN APPLY COMPETITIVELY EACH YEAR — AND 55% OF ALL PREVIOUS AWARD WINNERS HAVE GONE ON TO WIN CONTINUATION FUNDING. More than half come back for more. That changes what winning once is worth: it is entry to a fund you can return to for years, which is the closest thing in this file to durable core support for a small local organisation. WHAT ELSE WINNERS RECEIVE: INTERNATIONAL RECOGNITION AND PROFILE-RAISING; PROFESSIONAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEDIA SUPPORT; PEER LEARNING, TRAINING AND COLLABORATION; AND MEMBERSHIP OF A COMMUNITY OF MORE THAN 230 CONSERVATION LEADERS ACROSS OVER 80 COUNTRIES. PROFESSIONAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEDIA SUPPORT is worth naming separately. A local leader with a press office behind them is far harder for a company or a ministry to sideline quietly — and this file has recorded that visibility functions as protection. WHAT THEY LOOK FOR, WHICH DOUBLES AS A CHECKLIST FOR ANY APPLICATION YOU EVER WRITE: GRASSROOTS, PRAGMATIC WORK THAT IS REALISTIC BUT AMBITIOUS; APPLICANTS ON THE CUSP OF ACHIEVING SIGNIFICANT IMPACT, WITH PROJECTS THAT ARE REPLICABLE OR SCALABLE; ACTIONS WITH CLEAR, MEASURABLE OUTCOMES, WITH CAREFUL CONSIDERATION OF THE INDICATORS THAT WILL BE USED TO EVIDENCE IMPACT; SUSTAINABLE PROJECTS THAT WILL CONTINUE WELL BEYOND THE AWARD; PROJECTS THAT DEMONSTRATE VALUE FOR MONEY AND ABILITY TO MANAGE FUNDING AT THAT LEVEL; AND PROJECTS FOR WHICH AN AWARD WILL MAKE A SIGNIFICANT DIFFERENCE. PRIORITY IS GIVEN TO APPLICANTS THAT CAN CLEARLY DEMONSTRATE NEED. THE INDICATORS THAT WILL BE USED TO EVIDENCE IMPACT — they ask you to name them in advance, before the work. Deciding what you will count, and starting to count it, is the single cheapest thing a community organisation can do this year, and it is what separates a fundable application from an earnest one. THE TWO PRACTICAL GATES, STATED SO NOBODY WASTES A CYCLE: ORGANISATIONS WITH AUDITED ACCOUNTS ARE PREFERRED, AND APPLICANTS MUST BE ABLE TO COMMUNICATE IN ENGLISH. AUDITED ACCOUNTS. If your organisation has never had an audit, that is a concrete task with a known cost, and it unlocks more than this one funder — this file has recorded two years of accounts as a gate at almost every serious source. THE PROFILE THEY SEEK: DYNAMIC, MID-CAREER CONSERVATIONISTS LEADING VITAL PROJECTS — EMBEDDED IN AND/OR FROM THE COMMUNITIES WHERE THEY WORK, SEEKING TO SCALE UP PROVEN WORK. PROJECTS MUST INVOLVE COMMUNITIES AT THE GRASSROOTS LEVEL AND DELIVER PRACTICAL ACTION FOUNDED ON SCIENCE — AND THEY SEEK GOOD COMMUNICATORS AND PASSIONATE PEOPLE WHO WILL INSPIRE OTHERS AND WHO WILL COLLABORATE AND SHARE RESULTS. SCALE UP PROVEN WORK, not start something new. This is the wrong funder for an idea and the right one for a practice your community has already run for years — the same distinction the prize entry filed under Egypt draws. THE DEADLINE PATTERN: APPLICATIONS CLOSE AT THE END OF OCTOBER FOR THE FOLLOWING YEAR'S AWARDS. THE SCALE: ESTABLISHED IN 1993, IT HAS CHANNELLED OVER £23–24 MILLION TO BETWEEN 200 AND 220 CONSERVATION LEADERS IN MORE THAN 80 COUNTRIES ACROSS THE GLOBAL SOUTH. AND THE TOOLKIT: A PUBLISHED APPLICANT TOOLKIT EXISTS TO BE SHARED WITH SOMEONE WHO WOULD BENEFIT, ALONGSIDE PUBLISHED FAQs AND A CONTACT ROUTE. They ask you to pass it on. If you are not the right applicant, somebody in your district is — and forwarding the toolkit costs nothing. WHO IT SUITS: African leaders of locally registered conservation organisations with several years of proven, community-based work and accounts to show for it. CAVEATS: ENGLISH, AUDITED ACCOUNTS PREFERRED, NATIONALS ONLY, AND AIMED AT MID-CAREER LEADERS SCALING PROVEN WORK — not a first grant. For grants an individual can hold with no organisation, Somalia's entry; for the cash award addressed to the village group itself, Egypt's entry; for the fund that waives registration, bank account and ID entirely, the Central African Republic's entry.

trackers.name: An African-founded and African-led pastoralist organisation running since 1989, with named country offices and national partner organisations across the Horn — and which issues and manages lending capital to women's groups itself
trackers.desc: AFRICAN INSPIRED AND AFRICAN LED, SINCE 1989 — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S SOMALIA ENTRY NAMES THIS ORGANISATION ONLY AS AN UNNAMED IMPLEMENTING PARTNER IN ONE CLAUSE, AND ITS TANZANIA ENTRY COVERS A PASTORALIST AND HUNTER-GATHERER COALITION. NEITHER DESCRIBES WHAT IS BELOW AND NEITHER HOST IS SHIPPED. WHO FOUNDED IT, AND IT IS THE FIND: AN AFRICAN INSPIRED AND AFRICAN LED INTERNATIONAL NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATION AND RESEARCH INSTITUTE, FOUNDED IN 1989 BY A GROUP OF DEVELOPMENT PRACTITIONERS AND PROFESSIONALS FROM THE HORN OF AFRICA CONCERNED ABOUT THE FUTURE OF PASTORALISM — ADDRESSING PASTORAL DEVELOPMENT FROM A REGIONAL PERSPECTIVE. An INGO founded by Africans about their own region, thirty-five years ago, still running. This file has recorded the ordinary shape repeatedly: a European or American organisation decides to work on African pastoralism and hires Africans to do it. This is the reverse, and it is the model to point at when a funder claims local leadership is aspirational. THE LENDING, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: IT ISSUES AND MANAGES LENDING CAPITAL TO WOMEN'S GROUPS IN ONE NAMED TERRITORY. Not a grant programme and not a referral to a bank — the organisation holds the capital and lends it. For pastoralist women with no collateral, no title and no branch within a day's travel, that is the only credit that exists. And it sits directly above the savings-group model filed under Djibouti: a group that has built its own fund is exactly who such a lender can serve. THE ENTERPRISE PROGRAMME BEHIND IT: ONE OF ITS PRIMARY PROGRAMS IS THE PROMOTION OF MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES AND JOB CREATION FOR WOMEN, INVOLVING SUPPORTING HONEY VALUE CHAINS — AIMING TO DIVERSIFY PASTORALISTS' LIVELIHOODS IN ORDER TO GENERATE AN ALTERNATIVE INCOME STREAM. DIVERSIFY, not replace. Alternative income is what allows a household to refuse a bad offer for its herd or its grazing — and this file has recorded that a community with one income stream negotiates from desperation. THE OFFICES AND PARTNERS, NAMED SO YOU KNOW WHO TO WRITE TO: A REGIONAL OFFICE IN SOMALILAND, AN OFFICE IN ETHIOPIA — A NEW ADDIS ABABA OFFICE OPENED IN 2020, HAVING HAD A REGIONAL OFFICE AT A NAMED UNIVERSITY FROM 1994 TO 1998 — AND COUNTRY OFFICES OR CLOSE INSTITUTIONAL PARTNERS IN ERITREA, SUDAN AND UGANDA. NAMED PARTNERS INCLUDE AN ETHIOPIAN UNIVERSITY, A PASTORALIST ENVIRONMENT ASSOCIATION IN A NAMED SUDANESE STATE, A UGANDAN GENDER RESOURCE CENTRE AND A UGANDAN DEVELOPMENT AGENCY. A partner list that is itself a directory: for a pastoralist community in Sudan or Uganda, the nearer contact is the national partner, not the London address. Eritrea appearing at all is worth noting — very few organisations in this file have any presence there. THE MISSION AND ITS UNUSUAL WORD: TO REDUCE POVERTY AMONG PASTORALISTS THROUGH THE EMPOWERMENT OF COMMUNITIES AND TO FOSTER SUSTAINABLE AND DIGNIFIED LIVESTOCK-BASED AND NON-LIVESTOCK-BASED LIVELIHOODS — PROMOTING PASTORALISM AS A DIGNIFIED WAY OF LIFE AND AS AN IMPORTANT CONTRIBUTION TO THE ECONOMY, LINKING PRACTICE WITH POLICY. DIGNIFIED, twice. Pastoralists are described across this file's land records as backward, wasteful or absent — which is the argument that precedes taking their grazing. An organisation that puts dignity in its mission statement is fighting that framing directly. THE MISCONCEPTION PROBLEM IT NAMES AS ITS LONG-TERM STRATEGY: AWARENESS RAISING AT COMMUNITY, POLICY AND PUBLIC SECTOR LEVELS TO CHANGE MISCONCEPTIONS AND NEGATIVE ATTITUDES TOWARDS PASTORALISM BY PROVIDING UP TO DATE, CONCRETE, STRONG AND HOLISTIC INFORMATION AND DATA — WITH ACTION-ORIENTED RESEARCH AS ITS MAIN TOOL FOR INFLUENCING POLICY. DATA against prejudice. When a ministry treats rangeland as idle, the counter is measured stocking rates, herd movements and contribution to national meat and milk supply — and there is a research institute that produces exactly that, free to cite. WHAT IT DELIVERS: TRAINING, ORGANISATIONAL DEVELOPMENT AND EMPOWERMENT OF PASTORALIST COMMUNITIES AT COUNTRY AND REGIONAL LEVELS, AND CAPACITY BUILDING FOR COMMUNITIES, CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS AND LOCAL MINISTRIES. LOCAL MINISTRIES on the same list as communities. Training the district officer who decides grazing allocations is slow work that changes more than any single case. THE TWO STATED GOALS: TO EMPOWER PASTORALIST COMMUNITIES AND THEIR INSTITUTIONS TO PLAY A FULL ROLE IN THEIR OWN DEVELOPMENT; AND TO INFLUENCE DEVELOPMENT POLICY AND PROGRAMME DESIGN TO FOSTER SUSTAINABLE LIVELIHOODS AMONG PASTORALISTS. THEIR INSTITUTIONS — the customary councils that already allocate grazing and water. Strengthening those rather than replacing them with a project committee is the distinction this file has recorded mattering most after the funding ends. THE FIVE-YEAR STRATEGY AND ITS FOUR AREAS: POLICY AND ADVOCACY; PROGRAM CREATION; RESEARCH; AND CONSULTANCY AND NETWORKING, OPERATING AT LOCAL, NATIONAL, REGIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL LEVELS. THE WOMEN'S PROGRAMME ON RECORD: ACCORDING TO A DONOR'S APPRAISAL OF A REGIONAL WOMEN'S ASSISTANCE EFFORT, IT HAS SUPPORTED WOMEN'S ORGANISATIONS IN UGANDA, SUDAN AND SOMALILAND THROUGH ITS WOMEN ECONOMIC EMPOWERMENT PROGRAMME — AND ONE COUNTRY PROGRAMME HAS PUT GENDER EQUALITY AT THE CENTRE OF ITS WORK SINCE ITS FORMATION IN 2001. THE ADVOCACY WORKSHOP MODEL, WORTH COPYING: IT HOSTED A REGIONAL PASTORAL ADVOCACY WORKSHOP WITH A WORLD INITIATIVE FOR SUSTAINABLE PASTORALISM AND A CONSERVATION UNION — SO THAT LOCAL AND INTERNATIONAL DEVELOPMENT ORGANISATIONS COULD SHARE KNOWLEDGE ON IMPLEMENTING PASTORALIST ADVOCACY STRATEGIES IN A MUCH MORE VISIBLE AND RESULTS-ORIENTED WAY, AND CONSOLIDATE AND DISSEMINATE STRATEGIES THAT HAVE HAD A POSITIVE IMPACT ON CHANGING PERCEPTIONS. A workshop whose purpose was to collect what has actually worked, rather than to plan more. Convening the organisations already in your region to compare tactics is cheap, and somebody has done it before at continental scale. AND THE NETWORKS IT BELONGS TO: A COALITION OF EUROPEAN LOBBIES ON EASTERN AFRICAN PASTORALISM, AND A NAMED LIVESTOCK GENETIC DIVERSITY NETWORK. A European lobbying coalition specifically for Eastern African pastoralism. That is a route to donor and parliamentary pressure abroad that most pastoralist communities do not know exists. WHO IT SUITS: pastoralist and agro-pastoralist communities across the Horn — Ethiopia, Somaliland, Eritrea, Sudan, Uganda — and women's groups in those areas needing credit rather than grants. CAVEATS: THE HORN OF AFRICA ONLY, AND IT WORKS THROUGH NATIONAL PARTNERS AND RESEARCH RATHER THAN AS AN EMERGENCY OR LEGAL SERVICE — approach the country office or named partner. For the pastoralist and hunter-gatherer coalition and its focal points, Tanzania's PINGO's Forum entry; for the savings model needing no outside capital, Djibouti's entry; for the network with independent African chapters, Egypt's entry.

trackers.name: PILnet (The Global Network for Public Interest Law) — a free pro bono clearinghouse that names community-led organisations as clients, circulates your matter to 800+ lawyers, runs no contracts between the parties, and lets you opt out of having your request shared locally
trackers.desc: THEY PUBLISH EXACTLY HOW YOUR REQUEST TRAVELS TO 800 LAWYERS — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S ERITREA ENTRY COVERS A LEGAL BROKER WITH A FINITE-PROJECT TEST, ITS ETHIOPIA ENTRY SENIOR LAWYERS ON ATTORNEY-CLIENT TERMS, ITS TOGO ENTRY A PRO BONO SERVICE CARRYING 100+ COMMUNITY CASES A YEAR, AND ITS DR CONGO ENTRY THE ENVIRONMENTAL LAW ORGANISATION THAT IS NOT A LAW FIRM. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE SWEEP'S TRUSTLAW HOST QUERY RETURNED FALSE POSITIVES AGAIN — TRUST.ORG MATCHES INSIDE WORLDLANDTRUST.ORG AND RAINFORESTTRUST.ORG, THE SAME SUBSTRING FAULT RECORDED IN ROUND 19W. NO REAL COLLISION. WHO IT WORKS WITH, WHICH IS THE FIND: IT COLLABORATES WITH NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS AND COMMUNITY-LED ORGANIZATIONS AROUND THE WORLD TO OBTAIN FREE LEGAL ASSISTANCE FROM VOLUNTEER LAWYERS WITH THE RELEVANT SKILLS AND EXPERTISE, CONNECTING THEM WITH A QUALIFIED PRO BONO LAWYER AT NO COST. COMMUNITY-LED ORGANIZATIONS named alongside NGOs. Most pro bono brokers in this file describe their clients as NGOs and leave a village committee guessing whether it counts; here the category is written in. THE PLACEMENT MECHANISM, PUBLISHED STEP BY STEP, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: ONCE CONFIRMATION OF THE MATTER DESCRIPTION IS RECEIVED, IT IS UPLOADED TO A PERIODIC CLEARINGHOUSE LIST — A REGULAR LIST OF PRO BONO OPPORTUNITIES SENT TO LEGAL PARTNERS, A GLOBAL NETWORK OF MORE THAN 800 LAWYERS REACHED RIGHT AWAY WITH YOUR REQUEST; THE CLEARINGHOUSE THEN WAITS FOR LAWYERS TO VOLUNTEER OR REACHES OUT DIRECTLY TO SELECTED PARTNERS. Your request becomes a line on a list that hundreds of lawyers read. That means the MATTER DESCRIPTION is the whole application — short, specific, and interesting enough that a volunteer picks it up. A vague plea about a land dispute will sit unclaimed; a defined question with a defined end will not. THE CONFLICT CHECK, WHICH IS THE STEP TO ANTICIPATE: AFTER A VOLUNTEER IS FOUND, THE ORGANIZATION IS INFORMED AND THE LAW FIRM IS ASKED TO RUN A CONFLICT CHECK — A STANDARD PROCESS LAW FIRMS USE BEFORE TAKING ON NEW CLIENTS OR CASES. The firm checks whether it already acts for your opponent. In a case against a mining, oil or agribusiness company, the largest firms often do — so name the company early rather than late, and expect some volunteers to withdraw at this stage. THE OPT-OUT ON SHARING YOUR REQUEST: IT WORKS CLOSELY WITH NATIONAL PRO BONO SERVICE PROVIDERS OPERATING REGIONALLY AND, IF GIVEN PERMISSION IN THE INTAKE FORM, MAY SHARE YOUR REQUEST WITH THESE LOCAL PROVIDERS TO REACH MORE LAWYERS — AND IF YOU ARE NOT COMFORTABLE WITH THAT SHARING, YOU CAN OPT OUT IN THE INTAKE FORM. You decide whether your matter circulates inside your own country. Where the opponent is well connected locally, that is a real choice with real consequences, and it is offered on the form rather than assumed. THE PRICE, STATED TWICE, WITH ITS LIMIT: THERE IS NO FEE FOR USING THE CLEARINGHOUSE, AND THE LAWYERS WORK FREE OF CHARGE — HOWEVER, THE PRO BONO SERVICE COVERS ONLY THE LEGAL SERVICES PROVIDED. Advice is free; court fees, travel, expert reports and filing costs are not. Budget those separately — this file's litigation-cost entries under South Africa are where that money comes from. THE QUALITY ASSURANCE IT STATES: BEFORE CONNECTING YOU WITH A LAWYER, IT ENSURES THAT THEY HAVE THE SPECIFIC KNOWLEDGE REQUIRED FOR YOUR PROJECT. THE ABSENCE OF PAPERWORK BETWEEN THE PARTIES: THE GLOBAL CLEARINGHOUSE DOES NOT REQUIRE PARTIES TO SIGN CONTRACTS OR AGREEMENTS, THOUGH ONE REGIONAL CLEARINGHOUSE ASKS LAWYERS TO COMPLETE A ONE-PAGE REGISTRATION FORM. No contract to sign is a low barrier — and also means the scope is only as clear as what you both wrote down. Agree in writing with the lawyer what is and is not included, even though the clearinghouse does not require it. WHAT THE LAWYERS CAN DO: ADVICE AND ADVOCACY, RESEARCH, ANALYSIS AND DRAFTING, AND TRAINING — AND A WIDE RANGE OF SERVICES REGARDING YOUR ORGANISATION'S OPERATIONS, INCLUDING SETTING IT UP AND REVIEWING LEGAL DOCUMENTS, CONTRACTS OR REQUIREMENTS SUCH AS EMPLOYMENT CONTRACTS, AN ANTI-MONEY LAUNDERING POLICY, OR A DATA PROTECTION POLICY. SETTING UP YOUR ORGANISATION is the one to notice. Registration is the gate this file has recorded shutting community groups out of nearly every fund; a lawyer to do it properly, free, is upstream of all of that. And a DATA PROTECTION POLICY matters more than it sounds when you hold membership lists and witness statements. THE STRUCTURE AND WHAT THE GLOBAL DESK COVERS: THREE REGIONAL CLEARINGHOUSES SERVE ASIA, EURASIA AND HUNGARY, WHILE THE GLOBAL CLEARINGHOUSE FOCUSES ON CROSS-JURISDICTIONAL MATTERS AS WELL AS ALL LOCATIONS NOT COVERED BY THE REGIONAL ONES. There is no African regional clearinghouse, so African requests go to the global desk — which is the desk built for cross-border work anyway. THE CROSS-BORDER REACH DEMONSTRATED: ASSISTANCE IS NOT LIMITED BY JURISDICTION OR REGION AND MULTI-JURISDICTIONAL SUPPORT IS AVAILABLE — IN ONE CASE IT LOCATED LAW FIRMS ACROSS THREE CONTINENTS TO PROVIDE LEGAL ANALYSIS ON THE RULES IN SIX OTHER NAMED JURISDICTIONS. Analysis of how six other countries handle the same question. For a community arguing that its government's rules fall below what neighbours require, that comparison is exactly the evidence — and it is the kind of desk research a volunteer firm does well. THE LANGUAGES AND THE REQUEST ROUTE: ASSISTANCE IS OFFERED IN ENGLISH, RUSSIAN, HUNGARIAN, SPANISH AND CHINESE, WITH THE REQUEST SUBMITTED BY CHOOSING A LANGUAGE — THE PUBLISHED CHOICES INCLUDING PORTUGUESE. Recorded as found: the language list and the form's own options differ, and neither includes French or Arabic. Lusophone African organisations have a route; francophone and North African ones should ask before assuming they do not. AND THE SCALE AND THE AFRICAN PRECEDENT: IN ONE YEAR IT ASSISTED OVER 200 NGOs BY ENGAGING 50 LAW FIRMS, PROVIDING DIRECT LEGAL SERVICES VALUED AT APPROXIMATELY $3,705,000 — AND A FOUNDATION GRANT EXPANDED ITS LAW FIRM NETWORK TO REACH NGOs IN NAMED PRIORITY COUNTRIES INCLUDING NIGERIA, WITH ASSISTANCE RANGING FROM ADMINISTRATIVE PAPERWORK SUCH AS TAX OR EMPLOYMENT ADVICE TO LITIGATION SUPPORT AND RESEARCH ON COMPLEX INTERNATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS ISSUES. LITIGATION SUPPORT is named. Not the court appearance itself — the research, the drafting and the analysis behind it, which is what a small local advocate most often lacks. WHO IT SUITS: African community-led organisations and NGOs needing free legal work on registration, contracts, policies, comparative research or litigation support. CAVEATS: LEGAL SERVICES ONLY — NOT COSTS OR DISBURSEMENTS — NO AFRICAN REGIONAL DESK, NO PUBLISHED FRENCH OR ARABIC ROUTE, AND PLACEMENT DEPENDS ON A VOLUNTEER STEPPING FORWARD. For a broker with a published finite-project test, Eritrea's entry; for senior lawyers on attorney-client terms, Ethiopia's entry; for a service already carrying 100+ community cases, Togo's entry.

trackers.name: The Overberg Renosterveld Conservation Trust — an African trust that registers a conservation servitude on the farm's title deed, binding on every future owner — with a management plan attached, incentive funding paid to the landowner, the whole method published as a toolkit, and 1,300+ hectares protected in perpetuity
trackers.desc: IT GOES ON THE TITLE DEED AND BINDS EVERY OWNER AFTER YOU — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S SOUTH SUDAN ENTRY COVERS THE INTERNATIONAL BODY THAT BOUGHT A FARM ALONGSIDE THIS TRUST, WITHOUT NAMING OR DESCRIBING THE TRUST; ITS SOUTH AFRICA BUCKET CARRIES A GREEN TRUST HOST AND A CONSERVATION OUTCOMES HOST AND NAME; ITS MADAGASCAR AND SOUTH AFRICA BUCKETS A WORLD LAND TRUST HOST. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRIOR SCAN FOUND CONSERVATION EASEMENT ABSENT FROM ALL 53 BUCKETS; THIS ENTRY FILLS THAT GAP. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. THE INSTRUMENT ITSELF, WHICH IS THE FIND: A FARMER REGISTERS A SERVITUDE OVER HIS OR HER PROPERTY IN FAVOUR OF A PARTICULAR NGO — THE CONSERVATION SERVITUDE IS THEN WRITTEN INTO THE TITLE DEEDS OF THE FARM, AND A SERVITUDE ATTACHED TO THE TITLE DEED IS BINDING ON THE SUCCESSOR IN TITLE. Registered against the land itself rather than agreed with the person. Every protection in this file that depends on a promise, a policy or a sympathetic official expires when that person leaves; this one survives the sale, the inheritance and the change of government, because it sits in the deeds registry. For a community or a friendly landowner holding ground that a developer will eventually want, it is the strongest instrument recorded here. WHAT IS ATTACHED TO IT: A MANAGEMENT PLAN IS ATTACHED TO THE SERVITUDE, PROVIDING SUPPORT TO LANDOWNERS AND IDENTIFYING PRIORITY MANAGEMENT INTERVENTIONS — DRAWN UP BY THE TRUST IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE LANDOWNER BEFORE THE LEGAL DOCUMENTATION IS DRAWN UP, WITH THE TRUST THEN ASSISTING IN IMPLEMENTING THOSE INTERVENTIONS. The plan is negotiated before the deed is signed, and the NGO is bound to help carry it out. That is what stops a servitude becoming an unfunded obligation the owner resents. THE MONEY THAT COMES WITH IT, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: THE TEAM PROVIDES SUPPORT INCLUDING INCENTIVE FUNDING TO PROTECT REMAINING PATCHES — INCENTIVISING LANDOWNERS WITH ADVICE AND ASSISTANCE WITH KEY MANAGEMENT INTERVENTIONS. The landowner is paid to protect it, not merely asked. That is the difference between a scheme farmers sign and one they decline, and it is the answer to the question this file keeps running into: why would the owner agree? THE METHOD, PUBLISHED STEP BY STEP: KEY AREAS ARE INITIALLY IDENTIFIED BASED ON DESK-TOP STUDIES AND EXTENSIVE MAPPING; THE LANDOWNERS ARE THEN APPROACHED AND ASKED IF THEIR LAND MAY BE SURVEYED, WITH A THOROUGH SURVEY USUALLY REQUIRING MULTIPLE VISITS AT DIFFERENT TIMES OF THE YEAR. Map first, then ask permission to survey, then negotiate. A local organisation can follow that sequence exactly — and the multiple-visit point matters, because a single dry-season survey misses most of what makes a case. THE LEGAL SIDE-BENEFITS IT NAMES TO LANDOWNERS: SIGNING THE EASEMENT AND THE ASSOCIATED MANAGEMENT PLAN BRINGS YOU IN LINE WITH ALL ENVIRONMENTAL LEGISLATION, PARTICULARLY REGARDING THE LAWS WHICH STATE THAT YOU MAY NOT SELL A PROPERTY CONTAINING INVASIVE ALIEN PLANTS — AND IT FORCES THE NEXT LANDOWNER TO ACKNOWLEDGE WHERE THE VIRGIN LAND IS. Compliance sold as a benefit rather than conservation sold as a duty. An approach that solves a legal problem the owner already has is the one that gets signed. THE ARGUMENT IT PUTS TO THE OWNER: THE IDEA IS THAT YOU YOURSELF WOULD WANT TO PREVENT FUTURE OWNERS FROM DESTROYING OR DEGRADING THE VEGETATION ON YOUR FARM — IT IS THE ONLY WAY TO LEAVE THIS LEGACY. THE RESULTS ON RECORD: FIVE FARMS WITH SIGNED EASEMENTS, BRINGING OVER 1,300 HECTARES INTO CONSERVATION IN PERPETUITY — INCLUDING ONE NAMED FARM WITH 360 HECTARES, AND 370 HECTARES OF THE LARGEST REMAINING AREA OF A NAMED VEGETATION TYPE UNDER THE FIRST SUCH EASEMENT. Five farms, thirteen hundred hectares. Small numbers, permanent effect — which is the honest scale at which this instrument works, one owner at a time. THE PURCHASE PROGRAMME ALONGSIDE IT: A 270-HECTARE STRETCH WAS SECURED THROUGH AN INTERNATIONAL BUY AN ACRE PROGRAMME WHICH ENABLES PEOPLE WORLDWIDE TO FUND LAND PURCHASES FOR THREATENED HABITATS — BUT LAND ACQUISITION IS JUST ONE TOOL. A public buy-an-acre appeal is a real route to the purchase price, and it is run by international partners on behalf of local trusts. That is the fundraising mechanism the standing brief asks about, working, on African ground. THE CORRIDOR STRATEGY: THE TRUST IS BUILDING CONSERVATION CORRIDORS WITH FARMING NEIGHBOURS, INCLUDING A NAMED NEIGHBOURING EASEMENT SITE — SO THAT WILDLIFE, ESPECIALLY POLLINATORS AND INVERTEBRATES, CAN MOVE FREELY AND SAFELY ACROSS NATURAL REMNANT PATCHES IN A HIGHLY TRANSFORMED LANDSCAPE. Neighbouring farms signed one after another add up to a corridor. Each easement makes the next one easier to ask for, because the neighbour has already seen the terms. WHY IT EXISTS AND WHY PRIVATE LAND IS THE WHOLE PROBLEM: THE REMAINING REMNANTS ARE ESSENTIALLY ALL FOUND ON PRIVATELY-OWNED LAND, SO WORKING WITH COMMERCIAL FARMERS IS CRUCIAL TO THE SURVIVAL OF THE ECOSYSTEM — WITH OVER 95% OF THE HABITAT ALREADY CONVERTED FOR AGRICULTURE, AND MOST OF THE COUNTRY'S BIODIVERSITY RESTING IN THE HANDS OF PRIVATE LANDOWNERS. MOST BIODIVERSITY IS ON PRIVATE LAND. State protected areas cannot reach it, which is why an instrument aimed at the title deed matters more than another park. THE THREAT IT IDENTIFIED, WHICH IS NOT THE OBVIOUS ONE: THE GREATEST THREAT TO WHAT REMAINS IS MISMANAGEMENT — NOT NECESSARILY MALICIOUS MISMANAGEMENT, BUT MORE A CASE OF LANDOWNERS NOT APPRECIATING THE UNIQUENESS AND RARITY OF THESE HABITATS. Worth carrying into any approach: the owner is often not an opponent, and a survey showing them what is on their land is the first move rather than a confrontation. AND THE OTHER MECHANISMS IT SITS AMONG, WITH THE CONSTRAINT NAMED: FROM BIODIVERSITY STEWARDSHIP, TO PROTECTED ENVIRONMENTS, TO PRIVATE NATURE RESERVES, THERE ARE MANY MECHANISMS AVAILABLE FOR LANDOWNERS TO FORMALLY PROTECT THEIR LAND — BUT A CHALLENGE IS LIMITED CAPACITY AND RESOURCES, RESULTING IN CIRCUMSTANCES WHERE THE NEED TO PROTECT BIODIVERSITY OUTWEIGHS THE SUPPLY TO DO SO. Three named alternatives to ask your own country's conservation authority about, and an honest statement that the bottleneck is people to do the paperwork rather than willing owners. WHO IT SUITS: African trusts, community organisations and sympathetic landowners wanting permanent protection registered against land, and anyone looking for a working easement model to copy. CAVEATS: A SMALL REGIONAL TRUST WORKING IN ONE SOUTH AFRICAN ECOSYSTEM WITH COMMERCIAL FARMERS — IT IS A MODEL AND A TOOLKIT FOR ELSEWHERE, NOT A SERVICE THAT OPERATES IN OTHER COUNTRIES, AND WHETHER A SERVITUDE CAN BE REGISTERED THIS WAY DEPENDS ON YOUR OWN PROPERTY LAW. For the body that buys farms outright, South Sudan's entry; for the self-declared community territory registry, Morocco's entry.

trackers.name: The Rural Women's Assembly — a 170,000-member movement of rural women across 11 countries that publishes its membership country by country — with its own charter, a demand worded as land with water rights, and a counter-summit timed against the regional heads of state meeting
trackers.desc: 170,000 WOMEN, COUNTED COUNTRY BY COUNTRY, DEMANDING LAND WITH WATER — method and adjacency declared first: THIS MOVEMENT WAS FOUNDED BY THREE ORGANISATIONS ALREADY IN THIS FILE — THE 48-COMMUNITY FEDERATION UNDER RWANDA, THE SIX-NGO RURAL COLLECTIVE UNDER SOMALIA, AND A FARM WOMEN'S PROJECT. THEIR ENTRIES NAME A RURAL WOMEN'S ASSEMBLY IN PASSING WITHOUT DESCRIBING IT OR SHIPPING THIS HOST, AND NONE IS RESTATED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THE SHIPPED HOST AND FIVE SUBJECT SPELLINGS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL ABSENT. THE PER-COUNTRY MEMBERSHIP, PUBLISHED, WHICH IS THE FIND: 23,000 IN ESWATINI, 2,050 IN MALAWI, 5,000 IN LESOTHO, 9,000 IN ZAMBIA, 9,017 IN SOUTH AFRICA, 65,000 IN ZIMBABWE AND 10,000 IN MOZAMBIQUE — WITH A CLAIMED TOTAL OF NEARLY 170,000 WOMEN IN 11 COUNTRIES. Almost no movement in this file publishes its membership broken down by country, and the breakdown is what makes it usable: a woman in Malawi can see that 2,050 others are already in, and a Zimbabwean chapter of 65,000 is a body a ministry has to answer. The uneven figures are also honest — this is not a movement pretending to be equally strong everywhere. THE DEMAND AS IT IS WORDED, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: TO ADVANCE LAND WITH WATER RIGHTS, FOOD SOVEREIGNTY, CLIMATE JUSTICE, AND WOMEN'S LEADERSHIP. LAND WITH WATER RIGHTS as the phrase, matching the rural collective recorded in this file's Somalia entry — the same correction reached twice, independently. Land granted without water is the failure this file recorded under Niger, and these movements now write the water into the demand itself. THE OWNERSHIP PROBLEM IT NAMES: RELATIVELY FEW WOMEN OWN THE LAND THEY CULTIVATE, LIMITING THEIR DECISION-MAKING POWER — IN A MEMBER'S WORDS, WE HAVE PART-CONTROL OVER SYSTEMS OF PRODUCTION, BUT IF YOU DON'T OWN THE LAND THEN THE INCOME, WHAT YOU PLANT AND HOW YOU PLANT IS OFTEN DECIDED ELSEWHERE. Working the land and controlling it are different things, and the gap between them is where a woman's labour turns into someone else's decision. HOW IT WAS FOUNDED AND BY WHOM: BORN IN 2009 WHEN OVER 250 WOMEN FROM NINE COUNTRIES — PEASANT PRODUCERS, SMALL-SCALE FARMERS, LAND RIGHTS ACTIVISTS AND LABOUR UNIONISTS — MET AT A THREE-DAY GATHERING ORGANISED BY THREE NAMED ORGANISATIONS, WHICH BECAME THE CATALYST FOR A UNIFIED FEMINIST GRASSROOTS MOVEMENT AND PRODUCED ITS CHARTER AND PLATFORM FOR ACTION. One three-day meeting of 250 people produced a charter and a movement now numbering six figures. That is a costable, repeatable act: convene the existing organisations, write the charter in the room, and leave with a platform rather than a communiqué. HOW IT IS STRUCTURED: A SELF-ORGANISED NETWORK OF RURAL WOMEN MOVEMENTS, ASSEMBLIES AND ORGANISATIONS IN DIFFERENT COUNTRIES, WHOSE MISSION IS TO MAKE SURE WOMEN IN THEIR OWN COUNTRIES' CHAPTERS ARE ABLE TO MOBILISE OTHER WOMEN AND ARTICULATE THE ISSUES. THE LEGAL FRAMEWORK IT HAS ADOPTED: A UNITED NATIONS DECLARATION ON THE RIGHTS OF PEASANTS, TAKEN UP AS AN ADVOCACY AND LEGAL FRAMEWORK THAT CAN PUT AUTHORITIES TO TASK AND CREATE ASSESSMENT CRITERIA. A declaration specifically for peasants, adopted deliberately as a measuring stick. This file has recorded communities searching for a standard to hold a government to; this is one written for exactly this constituency, and adopting it formally is a decision any assembly can take. WHAT IT ORGANISES THROUGH: TEACH-INS, WORKSHOPS, RESEARCH AND DOCUMENTATION, AND POLICY ADVOCACY — PROMOTING SEED SAVING, SEED SHARING AND SEED BANKS, SMALL-SCALE FARMING, NATURAL COMPOST AND THE REINTRODUCTION OF INDIGENOUS AND NUTRITIOUS FOODS; IT ALSO ENGAGES IN URGENT ACTION, PROVIDING RESOURCES AND COMFORT FOR SISTERS IN DIFFICULTY. URGENT ACTION for members in difficulty, run by the membership itself rather than by a foreign protection fund. Slower and smaller than the mechanisms filed elsewhere here, but it answers to the women it serves. THE SEED ARGUMENT IT MAKES: WHEN WOMEN LOSE THEIR SEEDS THEY LOSE MORE THAN CROPS — THEY LOSE INDEPENDENCE, NUTRITION, CULTURAL KNOWLEDGE, AND THE POWER TO DECIDE WHAT GROWS IN THEIR FIELDS; ACROSS THE REGION RURAL WOMEN FACE GROWING PRESSURE FROM AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS THAT ENCOURAGE THEM TO BUY COMMERCIAL SEED, FERTILISER AND PESTICIDES EVERY SEASON. Seed dependency as a form of dispossession that takes no land at all. A household buying seed every season has lost something even while holding title. THE CROSS-BORDER SEED PRACTICE, AND THE DEMAND BEHIND IT: WHEN THERE WAS TROUBLE IN ONE COUNTRY, WOMEN FROM OTHER SOUTHERN AFRICAN COUNTRIES CAME BRINGING INDIGENOUS SEEDS TO THE WOMEN OF THE ASSEMBLY THERE — AND IT HAS CALLED FOR THE OPENING OF BORDERS FOR SEED SHARING AND THE PROTECTION OF TRADITIONAL AND INDIGENOUS SEEDS FROM MULTINATIONAL CORPORATIONS. Members carried seed across borders to replant after a disaster. That is a mutual-aid system a network can run itself, and it is worth building the seed banks before the drought rather than after. THE COUNTER-SUMMIT IT HOLDS: A PEOPLE'S SUMMIT TIMED TO COINCIDE WITH THE ANNUAL REGIONAL HEADS OF STATE SUMMIT, WITH CLOSE TO 200 WOMEN GATHERING FROM NINE NAMED COUNTRIES, TRAVELLING AS AN ACT OF SOLIDARITY WITH THEIR SISTERS IN THE HOST COUNTRY. The same timing tactic as the mining counter-gathering recorded in this file's Rwanda entry: hold your assembly in the same city, the same week, while the press and the ministers are already there. THE COLLECTIVE WORK PRACTICE IT HAS REVIVED, AND THE CAMPAIGN NAME: A REVIVED AFRICAN TRADITION OF COLLECTIVE COMMUNITY WORK, IN ONE INSTANCE BRINGING MORE THAN 70 COMMUNITY MEMBERS INCLUDING WOMEN, MEN AND YOUNG PEOPLE TOGETHER TO PREPARE LAND FOR PLANTING — AND A ONE WOMAN, ONE HECTARE CAMPAIGN, ALONGSIDE SEED MULTIPLICATION SITES AND PRACTICAL AGRO-PROCESSING TRAINING SUCH AS MAKING JAM AND CANNING FRUIT. ONE WOMAN, ONE HECTARE is a demand small enough to be granted and specific enough to be counted. And the collective work tradition brings men and young people into a women's movement's activity without diluting who leads it. AND THE CONSULTATION PRINCIPLE IT ASSERTS: WHEN THE GOVERNMENT WANTS TO MAKE CHANGES IT HAS TO GO TO THE GROUND AND CONSULT US, WOMEN — BECAUSE OFTEN, WOMEN ARE NOT CONSULTED WHEN IT COMES TO CLIMATE JUSTICE; IT IS A BOTTOM-UP APPROACH. WHO IT SUITS: rural women farmers anywhere in southern Africa wanting a chapter to join or start, and organisations looking for a charter-plus-platform founding model or a seed-sharing mutual aid system. CAVEATS: A MEMBERSHIP MOVEMENT, NOT A FUNDER, A LAW CENTRE OR A LAND-PURCHASE BODY; ITS STRENGTH IS VERY UNEVEN BETWEEN COUNTRIES ON ITS OWN PUBLISHED FIGURES, AND CHAPTERS ARE SELF-ORGANISED, SO WHAT EXISTS NEAR YOU VARIES. For the federation that litigated against parliament, Rwanda's entry; for the collective that builds rural organisations before the land claim, Somalia's entry.

trackers.name: Nature Seychelles
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the oldest and largest environmental NGO in Seychelles, a registered association since 1998 with a board of trustees and around fifteen full-time staff including protected-area specialists. It manages Cousin Island Special Reserve and the Sanctuary at Roche Caiman, and through its Locally Empowered Area Protection project it has pioneered CO-MANAGEMENT under the country's nature reserve and conservancy legislation — the route by which local people take on protection and management of an area rather than leaving it to government. USE IT: start with LEAP if you want an area near you protected and locally run; use its protected-area staff if you need the technical case for why a site matters. It sits on government committees and taskforces and in the Citizen Engagement Platform Seychelles, so it has standing in consultations — but it works with government rather than against it, and will not fight a project for you.

trackers.name: Seychelles — Financial Services Authority (FSA)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the FSA registers & regulates companies, IBCs, foundations, trusts & securities and maintains the corporate register, Seychelles. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: SeyLII
trackers.desc: Seychelles Legal Information Institute: free judgments and legislation. · Find here: free Seychelles judgments and legislation (SeyLII / Laws.Africa).

trackers.name: Anti-Corruption Commission Seychelles (ACCS)
trackers.desc: National anti-corruption body of Seychelles — investigates graft, financial crime and abuse of public office.

trackers.name: Seychelles — Ministry of Finance, National Planning & Trade
trackers.desc: National budget authority; the Finance Department plans & manages the Government budget and runs programme performance-based budgeting, Seychelles. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in the Seychelles.

trackers.name: Seychelles — Office of the Auditor General (OAG)
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution; conducts financial, compliance, performance & special investigative audits per ISSAI and reports to the National Assembly, Seychelles.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: Court of Appeal — the state must clean up, and may owe damages
trackers.desc: A CONSTITUTIONAL DUTY TO ACT AGAINST POLLUTION BY PRIVATE PARTIES. Seychelles' highest court held that Article 38 of the Constitution means the state must act to ensure ‘that private citizens do not pollute the environment’; that it is obliged to take steps to clean up pollution caused to public places like rivers and beaches; and that failure to act could lead to claims for damages. The case was brought by a landowner at Fairview estate against the Minister of Environment, the Minister of Health and the Attorney General over serious E. coli pollution of a river, with the state arguing it was not constitutionally obliged to act. THREE THINGS MAKE THIS UNUSUALLY USEFUL: the duty runs against state passivity, so where a regulator does nothing the inaction is itself the breach; it attaches to public places, rivers and beaches named; and it carries a damages remedy, not merely a declaration. The judgment was unanimous, written by Janak de Silva, a non-resident judge from Sri Lanka — the appellate bench includes non-resident judges, which is why its environmental reasoning draws on wider common-law authority and why the decision is described as potentially influential beyond Seychelles.

trackers.name: EPA 2016 Appeals Board — written procedure, but budget for the fee
trackers.desc: THE ROUTE BELOW THE COURTS. The Environment Protection Act 2016 (No. 18 of 2016), gazetted 5 September 2016, expressly establishes an Appeals Board, and dedicated Appeals Rules of Procedure Regulations exist — so the procedure is written down and obtainable. BUDGET FOR THE FEE: the statutory Memorandum of Appeal requires you to state the grounds of appeal and to certify that a fee in Seychelles Rupees has been paid, with receipt number and date — appeals are not free, so establish the current fee before the deadline, not after. WHAT ELSE THE ACT PROVIDES: the Minister may declare protected coastal zones and prepare an Integrated Coastal Zone Management Plan; may regulate petroleum and mineral exploration in territorial waters and the EEZ; EIA runs by prescribed classes, with an Environmental Appraisal Committee and registered EIA consultants — so a consultant's registration is checkable. THE ADMINISTRATOR MAY SERVE AN ENFORCEMENT NOTICE OR A PROHIBITION NOTICE — ask whether either has been served, because they are documents. Obstructing an inspection is punishable. The Act is live: plastic bag rules 2017, a tourism environmental sustainability levy, effluent standards and laboratory rules all 2023. WHO OPERATES: Nature Seychelles (BirdLife partner) manages the Cousin Special Island Reserve — 27 ha plus waters to 400 m from the high-water mark; Island Conservation Society staffs centres on 6 outer islands under a 2007 agreement with the parastatal Islands Development Company. DO NOT APPROACH the Nature Protection Trust of Seychelles — the first environmental NGO registered here (1992) — it ceased operating in 2011.

trackers.name: SeyCCAT Blue Grants Fund — grant money created by converting national debt, with the application form translated into Creole so locals could actually apply
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the Seychelles Conservation and Climate Adaptation Trust, created in 2015 as an independent, nationally based public-private trust fund to manage the proceeds of the world's first debt-for-nature swap for ocean conservation — US$21.6 million of national debt bought back at a discount, with the redirected debt service capitalising the trust — later joined by proceeds of a sovereign blue bond that raised US$15 million from investors. It runs the Blue Grants Fund. WHAT IT PAYS AND ON WHAT TERMS: reported disbursement rose from about US$286,500 in the first call to roughly US$889,000 across twenty-one projects in the third year, with US$700,000 a year available at that point and more than US$5.3 million distributed in total by 2025. Two windows are described: small-to-medium grants up to SCR 100,000, awarded on an approved concept note, maximum 12 months; and large grants between SCR 100,000 and SCR 1,000,000, shortlisted on a concept note then awarded on a full proposal, maximum 24 months. A concept note first, not a full proposal, is a low-cost way in for a small association. THE PART TO STEAL, BECAUSE IT IS AN ACCESS PROBLEM EVERY FUND IN THIS FILE HAS: the application form was originally in a standard European format that experienced NGOs could handle but local stakeholders could not, so in 2019 SeyCCAT translated the application form into Creole so people could apply in their own language, held public meetings across three islands, and did one-to-one visits with fishing communities, students and young women entrepreneurs. Ask any fund whether its form exists in the language its intended applicants speak. WHO IT SUITS: Seychellois NGOs, fishers' associations and community groups working on marine protection, sustainable fisheries and climate adaptation. CAVEATS: it funds ocean, fisheries and climate work — not litigation, not land purchase, and not opposition to a project; grants run to fixed short terms; and the model depends on debt-conversion and bond proceeds rather than open-ended income.

trackers.name: Seychelles legal aid — EVERY licensed lawyer must take legal aid cases as a condition of their licence, and you apply to the Judiciary
trackers.desc: WHO OWES YOU A LAWYER, AND IT IS THE STRONGEST RULE FOUND ANYWHERE IN THIS FILE: in Seychelles ALL LICENSED LEGAL PRACTITIONERS — UNLESS EXEMPT — MUST, AS A CONDITION OF THEIR LEGAL PRACTITIONER'S LICENCE, TAKE LEGAL AID CASES. Not a voluntary scheme, not a pro bono appeal to conscience: the obligation is attached to the licence itself, so the entire practising profession is the pool. Compare Mozambique and Angola, where the bar's statutes impose a duty, and every other country in this file where legal aid depends on who volunteers. HOW TO APPLY, AND WHERE: applications are filed WITH THE JUDICIARY, which reviews them, notifies the outcome, and ALLOCATES A LAWYER to your case if approved. THE MEANS TEST IS PUBLISHED AS A NUMBER: you must earn LESS THAN SCR 8,000 PER MONTH, and proof of your financial position is required. A published income threshold means you can determine your own eligibility before you go — rarer in this file than it should be. Scale: 784 legal aid applications were filed with the Judiciary in a single year in a country of under 100,000 people. The Registrar of the Supreme Court licenses practitioners under the Legal Practitioners Act, and publishes the roll of licensed lawyers — including suspensions, so you can check who is currently entitled to practise before instructing anyone. WHO IT SUITS: Seychellois who cannot afford a lawyer in a land, property, planning or environmental matter, on any island. CAVEATS: A MEANS-TESTED STATE SCHEME administered by the Judiciary — allocation is to an available practitioner rather than a specialist of your choosing, and the scheme does not fund campaigning; the threshold figure should be confirmed as current. For the coastal and marine conservation route and the Blue Grants Fund, Seychelles' SeyCCAT entry; for standing to litigate environmental matters, the Eco-Sud precedent recorded under Mauritius.

trackers.name: CEPS and the Seychelles NGO directory — the civil society umbrella that publishes every member's address, phone and named focal person, plus TRASS on Praslin and the Islands Foundation
trackers.desc: THE DIRECTORY AND THE ISLAND GROUPS: the CITIZENS ENGAGEMENT PLATFORM SEYCHELLES (CEPS, ceps.sc) is THE UMBRELLA ORGANISATION OF CIVIL SOCIETY IN SEYCHELLES, whose members include this file's Nature Seychelles, and which is recorded as able to take A MONITORING AND WATCHDOG ROLE to ensure CITIZEN CONCERNS ARE NOT BEING NEGLECTED on national engagement platforms; it belongs to the Southern African council of NGOs. THE PART THAT MAKES IT USABLE TODAY: CEPS PUBLISHES A DIRECTORY OF NGOs GIVING EACH MEMBER'S FOUNDING DATE, POSTAL ADDRESS, TELEPHONE NUMBER, EMAIL AND NAMED FOCAL PERSON — including entries for the TERRESTRIAL RESTORATION ACTION SOCIETY OF SEYCHELLES at Baie Ste Anne, Praslin (tel +248 513370, focal person named), SUSTAINABILITY FOR SEYCHELLES (tel +248 422 4072, focal person named, category Environment and Natural Resources), and the SEYCHELLES ISLANDS FOUNDATION at La Ciotat Building, Mont Fleuri, PO Box 853, Victoria. A published directory with a named focal person per organisation removes the hardest step in a small country — you are not writing to an institution, you are writing to a person whose name and number are printed. Start there. THE ISLAND ORGANISATION AND WHAT IT DOES WITH PRIVATE LAND: TRASS is a not-for-profit based on PRASLIN committed to restoring degraded ecosystems, mobilising interested parties for the restoration, enhancement, maintenance and SAFEGUARDING of areas AFFECTED BY FOREST FIRES, and WORKING IN PARTNERSHIP WITH PRIVATE LANDOWNERS, government, the private sector and other NGOs so that degraded land can be fully restored. Fourteen years on it holds a solid group of volunteers — one member records having MOBILISED OVER 200 OTHER VOLUNTEERS — and has opened a second nursery with capacity for TWELVE THOUSAND LOCAL AND RARE FRUIT PLANTS, integrating agroforestry with endemic, native and medicinal planting under a USD 31 MILLION ridge-to-reef project CO-FINANCED BY GOVERNMENT, A UN AGENCY AND CIVIL SOCIETIES. An organisation that partners with PRIVATE LANDOWNERS is the one to bring to a landowner who is wavering — restoration is an alternative to selling, and here it comes with a nursery and two hundred volunteers attached. AND THE TRUST THAT HOLDS WORLD HERITAGE: the SEYCHELLES ISLANDS FOUNDATION (SIF, sif.sc), a NON-PROFIT CHARITABLE ORGANISATION ESTABLISHED AS A PUBLIC TRUST BY THE GOVERNMENT IN 1979, manages ALDABRA ATOLL AND THE VALLÉE DE MAI, governed by a BOARD OF FIFTEEN TRUSTEES, with the local population encouraged to engage through public awareness and outreach. WHO IT SUITS: Seychellois on any island seeking an organisation, a landowner considering restoration, or a community wanting its concern monitored nationally. CAVEATS: A SMALL VOLUNTEER SECTOR; confirm listings. For the island bought in 1968 and the co-management act, Seychelles' Nature Seychelles entry; for grant money from a debt conversion, SeyCCAT; for the duty on every licensed lawyer, the legal aid entry.

trackers.name: Island Conservation Society — signed a 2007 agreement to be conservation manager on a state company's islands and now staffs six of them, plus the island bought outright by a single donor in 1973
trackers.desc: THE ISLAND SOMEBODY BOUGHT, AND THE CONTRACT TO STAFF THE REST: the ISLAND CONSERVATION SOCIETY (ICS) WAS REGISTERED AS AN NGO IN SEYCHELLES ON 25 MARCH 2001, with its head office — THE ISLAND CONSERVATION CENTRE — AT POINTE LARUE, MAHÉ, focusing on THE PROTECTION AND REHABILITATION OF THE SMALL ISLANDS OF SEYCHELLES, PARTICULARLY THE OUTER ISLANDS. THE ARRANGEMENT IS THE RESOURCE: MOST OF THE OUTER ISLANDS ARE GOVERNMENT-OWNED AND MANAGED BY A PARASTATAL COMPANY, AND IN 2007 ICS SIGNED AN AGREEMENT WITH THAT COMPANY TO ACT AS CONSERVATION MANAGERS AND ADVISERS ON ALL ITS ISLANDS — AND ICS NOW EMPLOYS FULL-TIME SCIENTISTS AND RANGERS AT CONSERVATION CENTRES ON SIX OF THEM. A single agreement with the state company that holds the land put paid conservation staff onto six islands. Where a parastatal holds the ground you want protected, the route is a management-and-advice agreement with the company — not a campaign against it. Ask what it would take to be named conservation adviser. ICS records OVER 20 YEARS OF SCIENTIFIC DATA ON THE MARINE AND TERRESTRIAL BIODIVERSITY OF SIX ISLANDS AND ATOLLS, with a presence across ARIDE, ALPHONSE, DESROCHES, PLATE ISLAND, SILHOUETTE and the outer atolls of FARQUHAR, ASTOVE and COSMOLEDO, working seabird monitoring, marine protection, invasive species removal and habitat restoration, with fewer than 50 staff. Twenty years of biodiversity data held by an NGO rather than a ministry is a body of evidence that does not disappear when a government changes. Ask ICS what its series shows for your island. AND THE PURCHASE, WHICH IS THE PLAINEST PRECEDENT IN THIS FILE'S SEYCHELLOIS RECORD: A UK-INCORPORATED WILDLIFE CHARITY PURCHASED ARIDE ISLAND NATURE RESERVE IN SEYCHELLES WITH FUNDS DONATED BY A NAMED INDIVIDUAL IN 1973. An entire island bought outright with one person's donation, and still a nature reserve half a century later. When somebody asks whether buying the land is realistic, Aride is the answer — and the vehicle was a charity incorporated by charter that could hold it in perpetuity. HOW ICS FUNDS ITSELF, WORTH COPYING AND WORTH WATCHING: PARTNERSHIPS HAVE BEEN DEVELOPED FOR THE CONSTRUCTION OF HOTELS ON SEVERAL ISLANDS, and a named cosmetics company agreed a TWO-YEAR SPONSORSHIP focused on enhancing the protection of one island's marine environment. Hotel partnerships fund the rangers and also put buildings on the island. Read that arrangement carefully before you copy it: ask what the developer got, and what the NGO can veto. ITS NAMED PARTNERS INCLUDE: the PLANT CONSERVATION ACTION GROUP (PCA), whose mission is to serve as THE PRINCIPAL SOURCE OF ADVICE AND INFORMATION ON THE TECHNICAL ASPECT OF PLANT CONSERVATION IN SEYCHELLES and to mobilise action for species threatened with extinction AND THOSE OF IMPORTANCE FOR HUMAN WELFARE, publishing a newsletter available online; and the MARINE CONSERVATION SOCIETY SEYCHELLES, incorporating a shark research institute. A group that names itself the principal source of technical plant advice is who to ask for the species list before a clearance — and note it counts plants important for HUMAN welfare, not only rare ones. WHO IT SUITS: Seychellois island communities, anyone facing a parastatal landholder, and groups considering outright purchase. CAVEATS: HOTEL AND CORPORATE SPONSORSHIP UNDERPINS SOME OF THIS WORK — check the terms. For the co-management pioneered under the nature reserve and conservancy act, Seychelles' Nature Seychelles entry; for grant money from converted national debt, SeyCCAT; for named focal persons per organisation, the CEPS directory; for a 12,000-plant nursery run by volunteers, TRASS.

trackers.name: The Seychelles Islands Foundation — a public trust whose 14-member board reserves at least five seats for conservation organisations — plus the farmers' and wildlife club members with phone numbers and the schools training programme
trackers.desc: FIVE OF THE FOURTEEN SEATS ARE RESERVED — and that clause is the reason this entry exists: THE SEYCHELLES ISLANDS FOUNDATION IS A PUBLIC TRUST ESTABLISHED IN 1979 BY THE GOVERNMENT, WITH THE PRESIDENT AS PATRON, TO MANAGE AND PROTECT THE COUNTRY'S TWO UNESCO WORLD HERITAGE SITES — AND ITS BOARD OF TRUSTEES, APPOINTED BY THE PRESIDENT, HAS 14 MEMBERS, INCLUDING AT LEAST FIVE REPRESENTATIVES FROM ORGANIZATIONS CONCERNED WITH THE CONSERVATION OF WILDLIFE AND NATURAL HISTORY, OR NATIONAL ACADEMIES OF SCIENCE. At least five of fourteen, written into the trust's own constitution, held by conservation organisations rather than by ministries. That is a minority with a guaranteed floor — and it is the clause to ask for whenever a body is being created to manage land near you: not consultation, not observer status, a stated minimum number of seats for organisations of your kind. Seychelles wrote it in 1979. AND WHY: ITS FORMATION WAS DRIVEN BY THE NEED FOR AN INDEPENDENT, SCIENCE-BASED INSTITUTION TO OVERSEE THE CONSERVATION OF THESE SITES, PARTICULARLY THOSE AT RISK DUE TO THEIR ISOLATION AND SENSITIVITY — and it is described as THE LONGEST ESTABLISHED LOCAL ORGANISATION WORKING IN NATURE CONSERVATION IN SEYCHELLES, having taken a PIONEERING MANAGEMENT APPROACH BY TWINNING THE TWO SITES, and being MANDATED TO ENSURE THEY ARE WELL-MANAGED PROTECTED AREAS WHERE CONSERVATION, RESEARCH, EDUCATION AND TOURISM ARE SUSTAINABLY BALANCED. A public trust rather than a government department, deliberately, so that the science would be independent of the ministry of the day. This file has flagged the trust form repeatedly as the vehicle able to hold land in perpetuity — here it is holding two World Heritage Sites and a nature reserve. THE MONITORING RECORD, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES A CLAIM STICK: SINCE 2014 THE FOUNDATION HAS ANNUALLY MONITORED THE CORAL REEFS OF ONE ATOLL, DOCUMENTING CHANGES THROUGH MAJOR BLEACHING EVENTS IN 2016 AND 2024 AND PROVIDING KEY INSIGHTS INTO THEIR RESILIENCE AND RECOVERY. Ten years of annual monitoring across two bleaching events. A ten-year series is the difference between saying the reef is dying and proving when and how fast — and it only exists because somebody started counting in a year when nothing was happening. THE ENERGY FIGURE WORTH KNOWING FOR ANY REMOTE STATION: A RENEWABLE ENERGY SYSTEM TODAY SUPPLIES 98% OF THE ATOLL'S ELECTRICITY DEMAND WITH SOLAR POWER — IMPLEMENTED OVER FOUR YEARS BY A STAFF MEMBER, AS PART OF HER MSc THESIS. Ninety-eight per cent solar on a remote atoll, and it was somebody's masters project. If your community facility runs on generators and diesel, a student needing a thesis subject is a free engineer — approach the nearest university department, not a contractor. THE TRAINING THAT MEMBER ORGANISATIONS CAN GET: with financial support from a critical ecosystem partnership fund, the national civil society platform ran a FOUR-DAY TRAINING PROGRAMME FOR MEMBERS REPRESENTING A WIDE RANGE OF THEMATIC AREAS, EMPHASISING TECHNICAL CAPACITY-BUILDING WITH A PARTICULAR FOCUS ON CLIMATE RESILIENCE AND ECOSYSTEM-BASED ADAPTATION; A THREE-DAY SESSION FOR SEVEN OF ITS CORE TEAM; AND A THREE-DAY PROGRAMME BRINGING TOGETHER OVER 40 STUDENTS FROM FIVE SECONDARY SCHOOLS — concluding with a site visit to a named bay. Members, staff and schoolchildren trained in the same programme, and the platform trained its own core team too. That last part is the one organisations skip: the umbrella that trains everyone else and never itself becomes the bottleneck. Ask your national platform when it last trained its own staff. TWO MORE MEMBER BODIES WITH CONTACTS, BOTH FILED UNDER AN ENVIRONMENT AND NATURAL RESOURCES COMMISSION: WILD LIFE CLUBS OF SEYCHELLES, C/O A NAMED PO BOX IN VICTORIA, MAHÉ, WITH TWO TELEPHONE NUMBERS AND A FOCAL PERSON; AND A VAL D'ANDORRE FARMERS ASSOCIATION, WITH A TELEPHONE NUMBER AND AN EMAIL. A FARMERS ASSOCIATION sitting in the environment and natural resources commission of the national civil society platform. On a small island the farmers and the conservationists are in the same commission by design — which is how a land-use disagreement gets settled between neighbours rather than in a ministry. Also named in the same platform: AN ECOTOURISM SOCIETY OF SEYCHELLES with a named focal person and address, and a SUSTAINABILITY ORGANISATION with a named doctor as focal person and a published telephone, which states it COLLABORATES WITH CITIZENS, THE GOVERNMENT, NGOs AND THE PRIVATE SECTOR and invites people to CONTACT US TO BECOME A VOLUNTEER OR MEMBER. An open invitation to become a member or volunteer, with a phone number. That is the lowest possible barrier to entry, and it is worth taking literally. WHO IT SUITS: Seychellois community groups, farmers' associations and anyone arguing for reserved seats on a management body. CAVEATS: A PRESIDENTIALLY-PATRONED PUBLIC TRUST — independent by design but appointed from the top. For the umbrella and the full NGO directory, Seychelles' CEPS entry; for the organisation that signed a 2007 agreement to manage six outer islands and staffs full-time scientists and rangers, the Island Conservation Society entry.

trackers.name: Wetlands International — the mangrove organisation with African regional offices, small grants for community groups and an eleven-country exchange network — whose whole method is that planting is the part that fails and the water flow is what to fix
trackers.desc: PLANTING IS THE PART THAT FAILS; FIX THE WATER INSTEAD — an off-brief note first, recorded honestly: THIS ROUND FIRST EXAMINED A WETLAND CONVENTION'S ADVISORY-MISSION ROUTE AND DID NOT FILE IT. A SITE CAN BE ADDED TO THAT REGISTER ONLY WITH THE APPROVAL OF THE PARTY IN WHOSE TERRITORY IT LIES, AND THE MISSION COMES ONLY UPON RECEIVING A REQUEST FROM A CONTRACTING PARTY — SO A COMMUNITY CANNOT TRIGGER IT. IT IS A STATE MECHANISM, NOT A RESOURCE AVAILABLE TO LOCALS. THE METHOD, WHICH IS THE FIND: INSTEAD OF FOCUSING SOLELY ON MANGROVE PLANTING, IT WORKS TO RESTORE UNDERLYING HYDROLOGY LIKE THE MIXING OF SALTWATER AND FRESHWATER SO THAT THE MANGROVES REGENERATE NATURALLY — CONSIDERING ADJUSTMENTS TO A DISTURBED AREA'S TOPOGRAPHY, RESULTING IN TRUE ECOSYSTEM RESTORATION WITH A RICHER BIODIVERSITY. Restore the water flow and the mangroves come back on their own. Planting seedlings is what every project does and what most projects lose — the seedlings die because the reason the mangroves went is still there. If somebody offers your community a planting day, ask first what blocked the tidal channel. THE FAILURE DIAGNOSED BY A COMMUNITY MEMBER RATHER THAN THE ORGANISATION: MANY MANGROVE RESTORATION INITIATIVES HAVE BEEN FAILING TO BEAR FRUIT DUE TO A LACK OF KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS ON ECOLOGICAL MANGROVE RESTORATION — IN ONE NAMED PLACE, MOST RESTORATION INITIATIVES HAVE FOCUSED ON PLANTING AND IGNORED THE CRUCIAL ASPECTS OF THE RESTORATION PROCESS: MAINLY BIOLOGICAL, SOCIAL, HISTORICAL AND POLITICAL. SOCIAL, HISTORICAL AND POLITICAL listed as parts of a restoration process. Who used to hold that shoreline, who cut it and why, and who benefits now are restoration questions, not distractions from it. THE TRAINING, AND WHO SITS IN THE ROOM: SINCE 2019 IT HAS PARTNERED WITH A NAMED MANGROVE ORGANISATION TO TRAIN LOCAL COMMUNITIES, FOREST MANAGERS, NATIONAL AND SUB-NATIONAL GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS, ACADEMIA AND RESEARCH INSTITUTIONS, CIVIL SOCIETY AND PRIVATE SECTOR ON THE COMMUNITY-BASED ECOLOGICAL MANGROVE RESTORATION APPROACH — AND IMPORTANTLY, LOCAL MANGROVE COMMUNITIES LEARN TO PERFORM THIS WORK, AND IN THE PROCESS LEARN TO RESTORE, VALUE, AND RESPONSIBLY STEWARD THEIR MANGROVES. Communities and the forest officers who police them, trained together on the same method. That is worth more than the technique itself: after it, both sides are arguing from the same manual. THE MONEY THAT REACHES GROUPS DIRECTLY: SMALL GRANTS FOR COMMUNITY GROUPS HAVE BEEN USED TO SUPPORT MANGROVE ACTIVITIES — AND THE EXCHANGE VISITS SHOWED PRACTICAL EXAMPLES OF COMMUNITY INVOLVEMENT THROUGH THE PROVISION OF FUNDING FOR LIVELIHOOD DIVERSIFICATION AND COASTAL PROTECTION. THE STRUCTURE THAT KEEPS IT ALIVE AFTER THE PROJECT: A GROUP OF VOLUNTEERS HAS BEEN RECRUITED AND TRAINED AS FOCAL POINTS TO MAINTAIN RESTORATION ACTIVITIES AS FAR AS POSSIBLE. Named volunteer focal points, as this file has recorded working for pastoralist security training and for park-edge site support groups. The same cheap device keeps appearing because it works: give two or three people a title and the work survives the funding. THE ELEVEN-COUNTRY EXCHANGE NETWORK, WHICH IS THE THING TO ASK TO JOIN: MANGROVE EXCHANGE VISITS BROUGHT TOGETHER PRACTITIONERS REPRESENTING COMMUNITIES, POLICYMAKERS, CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS AND RESEARCHERS FROM KENYA, MADAGASCAR, MOZAMBIQUE AND TANZANIA ON THE WESTERN INDIAN OCEAN SIDE, AND SENEGAL, GUINEA-BISSAU, GUINEA, SIERRA LEONE, LIBERIA, NIGERIA AND GAMBIA ON THE ATLANTIC COAST — WHERE THEY SAW BEST PRACTICES IN SITE SELECTION, COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT AND RESTORATION METHODS. A REGIONAL PLATFORM FOR AFRICA'S MANGROVE CONSERVATION WAS ESTABLISHED OUT OF IT. Eleven countries and both coasts, with community representatives travelling alongside the officials. A platform that already exists is far easier to join than one you have to build — ask the regional office when the next exchange is and who nominates. THE PROGRAMME'S SIZE: A TEN-YEAR PROGRAMME LAUNCHED IN 2017 AIMS TO SAFEGUARD 1 MILLION HECTARES OF AFRICAN MANGROVES BENEFITTING 2 MILLION PEOPLE, WITH A NEWER PROJECT AIMING AT 65,000 HECTARES IN ONE NAMED REGION AND AN OFFICE OPENED IN A NAMED REGIONAL TOWN, PLUS TRAINING FOR LOCAL STAKEHOLDERS AROUND A GLOBAL MANGROVE WATCH TOOL. An office in a regional town rather than only the capital, and a free monitoring tool taught to local stakeholders. Both are reachability, which is what decides whether a resource is real for a village. WHAT IS ACTUALLY AT STAKE, IN NUMBERS: MORE THAN 100,000 INHABITANTS IN ONE NAMED DELTA DEPEND ON THE AREA'S MANGROVES FOR HONEY PRODUCTION, AGRICULTURE, SALT EXTRACTION AND ECO-TOURISM — AND COASTAL COMMUNITIES CONTRIBUTE TO RESTORATION AND IN RETURN ARE EMPOWERED TO DEVELOP ALTERNATIVE LIVELIHOODS AND SUSTAINABLY USE MANGROVE PRODUCTS LIKE OYSTERS. Honey, salt, oysters and tourism from a mangrove nobody was paying for. Listing what your wetland already produces, with numbers, is the argument against the development that would replace it — and one this file has recorded winning where a bare conservation appeal lost. AND THE OFFICES: A NAMED REGIONAL AFRICA ARM AND A NAMED EAST AFRICA ARM, EACH WITH ITS OWN SITE AND CONTACTS. WHO IT SUITS: African coastal and island communities whose mangroves, deltas or wetlands are degraded or under development pressure. CAVEATS: IT WORKS THROUGH PROGRAMMES AND PARTNERSHIPS, NOT OPEN APPLICATIONS — approach the regional arm nearest you. For the 30-day closure that raised village income 136%, São Tomé's community marine management entry; for the fishers' own national network, Madagascar's MIHARI entry; for the free grants with no co-financing, Kenya's BIOPAMA entry.

trackers.name: The organisation that becomes a co-complainant beside your own community body before the African Commission and Court — with two won land judgments, a published legal-cases site, and an independent 15-year evaluation of whether the approach works
trackers.desc: THEY PUT THEIR OWN NAME ON THE CASE BESIDE YOURS — adjacency declared first: A BANJUL-BASED PRO BONO COUNSEL THAT TAKES COMMUNITY CASES TO THE SAME BODIES ALREADY HAS ITS OWN ENTRY UNDER GAMBIA. THIS IS A DIFFERENT ORGANISATION WITH A DIFFERENT ROLE, CROSS-REFERENCED BELOW. THE STRUCTURAL FIND, AND IT IS ABOUT WHO IS NAMED ON THE PAPERS: IN ONE CASE THE COMPLAINANTS WERE A NATIONAL MINORITY RIGHTS CENTRE AND THIS ORGANISATION, ACTING ON BEHALF OF A COMMUNITY WELFARE COUNCIL. IN THE SECOND, THE THREE ORIGINAL COMPLAINANTS WERE THIS ORGANISATION, THE COMMUNITY'S OWN DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME, AND THE SAME NATIONAL CENTRE. The community's own organisation is a named complainant, not a beneficiary. That is the arrangement to insist on: this file has recorded case after case brought FOR communities in which the community had no standing, no say in settlement and no copy of the file. Here a village-level body sits on the claim alongside a national NGO and an international one — three names, one case. THE ROUTE THOSE CASES TOOK, STATED PLAINLY: AFTER FAILED ATTEMPTS AT NATIONAL LEVEL, INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES RESORTED TO THE AFRICAN COMMISSION AND COURT ON HUMAN AND PEOPLES' RIGHTS, WHICH BOTH RULED IN FAVOUR OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES' LAND RIGHTS, ORDERED THAT MEASURES BE TAKEN FOR LAND RESTITUTION AND COMPENSATION, AND DECLARED THAT THE STATE HAD VIOLATED THEIR HUMAN RIGHTS. AFTER FAILED ATTEMPTS AT NATIONAL LEVEL. Losing at home is a precondition of these routes rather than the end of the road — and communities routinely stop at the point where this actually begins. WHAT THE FIRST DECISION ESTABLISHED, AND IT IS DIRECTLY THIS FILE'S SUBJECT: THE COMMISSION EXAMINED A GOVERNMENT'S EVICTION OF AN INDIGENOUS COMMUNITY FROM ANCESTRAL LAND AROUND A LAKE TO ESTABLISH A GAME RESERVE — FINDING VIOLATIONS OF THE RIGHTS TO RELIGION, CULTURE, PROPERTY, NATURAL RESOURCES AND DEVELOPMENT, AND CALLING FOR RECOGNITION OF THE COMMUNITY'S OWNERSHIP OF ITS ANCESTRAL LAND AND ITS RESTITUTION — AN IMPORTANT PRECEDENT FOR ENSURING EQUITY AND PARTICIPATION IN NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT AND DEVELOPMENT ON INDIGENOUS LANDS. Evicted to make a game reserve, and the eviction was held unlawful. Conservation displacement is not an exception to rights law on this continent — there is a continental decision saying so, and it is citable by any community facing the same. WHAT THE SECOND DID: THE FIRST INDIGENOUS PEOPLES' RIGHTS CASE CONSIDERED BY THE COURT, AND BY FAR THE LARGEST EVER CASE IT HAD TO CONSIDER, FINDING VIOLATIONS OF SEVEN ARTICLES OF THE AFRICAN CHARTER AND CREATING A MAJOR LEGAL PRECEDENT — WITH A REPARATIONS JUDGMENT FOLLOWING THAT CLARIFIED THE SCOPE AND CONTENT OF STATE OBLIGATIONS TO UPHOLD INDIGENOUS PEOPLES' LAND RIGHTS. THE PARTICIPATION MODEL, WHICH IS THE MOST COPYABLE PART: THE LITIGATION ITSELF AND THE COMMUNITY'S PARTICIPATION IN THE VARIOUS STAGES OF THE LEGAL PROCESS PROVIDED A MODEL FOR COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT, THROUGH WHICH THE COMMUNITY WERE EMPOWERED TO BETTER UNDERSTAND AND ADVOCATE FOR THEIR RIGHTS — AND AT THE HEARING, 25 COMMUNITY MEMBERS ATTENDED IN PERSON AND A FURTHER 40 VIEWED IT AT HOME BY LIVESTREAM. Twenty-five people in the courtroom and forty watching at home. Somebody budgeted for that, and it is why the case built a movement rather than only a judgment. If your lawyers are not planning for community attendance, ask them to — it is a line in a grant application, not an impossibility. THE INDEPENDENT EVALUATION OF WHETHER ANY OF THIS WORKS: A COMMISSIONED EVALUATION OF 15 YEARS OF LITIGATION AND LEGAL EMPOWERMENT PROGRAMMES WITH MINORITIES AND INDIGENOUS PEOPLES IN EAST AFRICA FOUND THESE ACTIVITIES TO BE POWERFUL TOOLS THAT CREATE SPACES AND OPPORTUNITIES FOR COMMUNITIES TO UNITE AROUND SHARED STRUGGLES AND MAKE DECISIONS THAT CAN IMPACT POSITIVELY ON THEIR COLLECTIVE RIGHTS — CONSIDERING THREE NAMED EAST AFRICAN COMMUNITIES, FINDING THE PROGRAMMES SUCCESSFUL OVERALL, AND DRAWING LESSONS FOR FUTURE ACTIVITIES. THE FINDINGS ARE STRONGLY BASED ON FEEDBACK DIRECT FROM THE RELEVANT COMMUNITIES, AND THE FULL REPORT IS PUBLISHED. An organisation that paid for an outside review of its own method and published it, with the communities' own verdict in it. Read that before agreeing to be somebody's test case.
