THE HONEST RECORD ON ENFORCEMENT, WHICH THIS FILE HAS FLAGGED BEFORE: THERE WERE CONTINUING VIOLATIONS OF THE PROVISIONAL MEASURES ORDER, INCLUDING A VIOLENT EVICTION OF APPROXIMATELY 1,000 PEOPLE AND POLICE INTIMIDATION WHILE JUDGMENT WAS AWAITED — AND THE ORGANISATION ITSELF NOTED A HISTORY OF LAX IMPLEMENTATION OF THE EARLIER JUDGMENT. An order in your favour did not stop the evictions. Budget the enforcement fight as a separate campaign with its own years and its own money, as this file's Kenyan strategic-legal entry also records. THE SUPPORTING PRESSURE THAT CAME WITH IT: A UN ANTI-RACISM BODY URGED THE GOVERNMENT TO ENSURE LEGAL ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF THE COLLECTIVE RIGHTS OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND TO PREVENT, PUNISH AND SANCTION ACTS THREATENING THEIR SECURITY AND PROPERTY. Two international bodies saying the same thing in the same year. Cases are won in parallel, not in a single forum — and a second body's statement costs far less to obtain than a judgment. THE STAKES AS ITS LEGAL DIRECTOR PUT THEM: THE CASE IS OF FUNDAMENTAL IMPORTANCE FOR INDIGENOUS PEOPLES IN AFRICA, PARTICULARLY GIVEN THE CONTINENT-WIDE CONFLICTS BETWEEN COMMUNITIES SPARKED BY PRESSURES OVER LAND AND RESOURCES — AND ULTIMATELY THE COURT WOULD BE RULING ON THE CRUCIAL ROLE OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES IN THE CONSERVATION OF LAND AND NATURAL RESOURCES. AND THE PUBLISHED RESOURCES: A LEGAL CASES WEBSITE, ACADEMIC ARTICLES ON LITIGATING INDIGENOUS PEOPLES' RIGHTS IN AFRICA INCLUDING ITS POTENTIALS, CHALLENGES AND LIMITATIONS, AND A NAMED WORK ON LITIGATION AS A TOOL FOR COMMUNITY EMPOWERMENT. POTENTIALS, CHALLENGES AND LIMITATIONS — published by the people who won the cases. That is the honest reading list before a community commits years to a case. WHO IT SUITS: African indigenous and minority communities who have exhausted national courts over eviction, land or resource rights, and the national organisations working with them. CAVEATS: A SMALL ORGANISATION TAKING STRATEGIC CASES OVER MANY YEARS, NOT A GENERAL LEGAL SERVICE — approach through a national partner, and expect a decade. For pro bono counsel before the same bodies, Gambia's IHRDA entry; for rapid legal support when defenders are criminalized, Kenya's Strategic Legal Response Centre entry; for university law clinics as free representation, Comoros' entry.

trackers.name: PAFO (Pan-African Farmers Organisation) — the continental platform recognised as the representative body of African farmers' organisations at the highest level — five regional member networks, founded under African Union sponsorship, with signed memoranda giving farmers a named door at a development bank
trackers.desc: THE HIGHEST CONTINENTAL SEAT AFRICAN FARMERS HOLD — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S MAURITANIA ENTRY COVERS THE WEST AFRICAN MEMBER NETWORK IN DETAIL, ITS ESWATINI ENTRY THE ALLIANCE THAT PARTNERS WITH THESE NETWORKS, AND ITS MALI ENTRY THE EASTERN AND SOUTHERN FARMERS' FORUM. THE SAME DEVELOPMENT BANK NAMED BELOW HAS ITS REVIEW MECHANISM UNDER NIGERIA AND ITS LEGAL FACILITY UNDER GAMBIA. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THEIR HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE RECOGNITION, AND IT IS THE FIND: IT IS RECOGNIZED AS THE REPRESENTATIVE BODY OF AFRICAN FARMERS' ORGANIZATIONS AT THE HIGHEST CONTINENTAL LEVEL — A CONTINENTAL ORGANIZATION WHOSE MEMBERSHIP BASE IS REGIONAL FARMERS NETWORKS. There is a recognised continental seat, and farmers hold it. That matters practically rather than symbolically: when a community's issue is bigger than its country — a transboundary concession, a regional trade rule, a continental agriculture policy — there is an existing body with standing to raise it, reachable through your own national organisation. This file has recorded communities trying to build that reach from scratch. THE LADDER, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES IT USABLE: MORE THAN 80 MILLION FARMERS INTEGRATED INTO NEARLY 70 TO 73 NATIONAL ORGANIZATIONS, UNIONS, FEDERATIONS, COOPERATIVES AND ASSOCIATIONS, PRESENT IN MORE THAN 45 TO 48 COUNTRIES, UNITED IN FIVE REGIONAL NETWORKS — GROUPED WITHIN THE NATIONAL PLATFORMS OF MORE THAN 30 COUNTRIES. Village group to national platform to regional network to continental seat. Four steps, all of them existing, none requiring anybody's permission to begin — and the figures are recorded as found, ranging because different sources count differently. THE FIVE NAMED REGIONAL MEMBER NETWORKS: AN EASTERN AFRICA FARMERS FEDERATION; A REGIONAL PLATFORM OF FARMERS' ORGANIZATIONS OF CENTRAL AFRICA; A NETWORK OF PEASANT AND PRODUCER ORGANISATIONS OF WEST AFRICA; A SOUTHERN AFRICAN CONFEDERATION OF AGRICULTURAL UNIONS; AND A MAGHREB AND NORTH AFRICAN UNION OF FARMERS. A MAGHREB AND NORTH AFRICAN UNION is worth naming separately: North African farmers are inside this structure, which is rare in a file where most continental networks stop at the Sahara. HOW IT WAS FOUNDED, AND BY WHOM, WHICH IS THE MODEL: THE FIVE SUB-REGIONAL NETWORKS HAD BEEN WORKING TOGETHER SINCE 2003 ON ISSUES OF CONTINENTAL INTEREST; THEY MET IN ADDIS ABABA IN MAY 2008 TO DISCUSS THE CONDITIONS FOR CREATING A PLATFORM THAT WOULD UNITE THEIR EFFORTS AND HARMONIZE THEIR CONCERNS; THOSE CONSULTATIONS PRODUCED A DECLARATION; AND THE CONSTITUTIVE ASSEMBLY WAS HELD UNDER AFRICAN UNION SPONSORSHIP IN LILONGWE FROM 27 TO 29 OCTOBER 2010, ON THE SIDELINES OF A CONFERENCE OF AFRICAN MINISTERS IN CHARGE OF AGRICULTURE. Seven years of working together before founding anything, and the constitutive assembly deliberately timed to sit beside the ministers' own conference. Both are tactics: existing collaboration first, and holding your founding meeting where the decision-makers are already gathered costs them nothing to attend. THE FIRST MANDATE GIVEN TO ITS OFFICE: TO SET UP THE EXECUTIVE SECRETARIAT, TO MAKE THE ORGANISATION FUNCTIONAL AND OPERATIONAL, AND TO NEGOTIATE THE PARTNERSHIPS NECESSARY FOR THE LIFE OF THE ORGANIZATION. ITS STATED FUNCTION: A FUNDAMENTAL COORDINATING FUNCTION BOTH WITH ITS MEMBER NETWORKS AND WITH CONTINENTAL AND INTERNATIONAL ORGANIZATIONS — ABLE TO FACILITATE DIALOGUE AND COOPERATION WITH CONTINENTAL AND INTERNATIONAL INSTITUTIONS, AND WITH FINANCIAL AND TECHNICAL PARTNERS. WHAT ITS OWN CHIEF EXECUTIVE SAYS IT IS FOR: THE ONLY FARMERS PLATFORM ON A CONTINENTAL SCALE IN THE WORLD — IMPORTANT FOR ADVOCACY AND FOR MAKING THE VOICES OF FARMERS HEARD AT CONTINENTAL AND INTERNATIONAL LEVELS, AND FOR KNOWLEDGE MANAGEMENT, THE EXCHANGE OF EXPERIENCE AND THE PROMOTION OF THE ACHIEVEMENTS OF FARMERS AND THEIR ORGANIZATIONS. FROM THE BEGINNING, IT HAS TRIED TO UNITE THE FARMERS OF THE CONTINENT AROUND COMMON NEEDS, THEMES AND CHALLENGES THAT BRING THEM ALL TOGETHER. THE HEADQUARTERS AND CONTACTS: HEADQUARTERS IN KIGALI, RWANDA, WITH PUBLISHED MEDIA AND TECHNICAL CONTACT ROUTES. THE DEVELOPMENT BANK RELATIONSHIP AND ITS PAPER TRAIL, WHICH IS THE USABLE PART: A MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING SIGNED WITH AN AFRICAN DEVELOPMENT BANK IN OCTOBER 2023, WITH A DELEGATION LED BY ITS PRESIDENT VISITING THE BANK'S HEADQUARTERS ON 13 DECEMBER 2024 TO ADVANCE ITS IMPLEMENTATION — THE BANK'S DIRECTOR OF AGRICULTURE AND AGRO-INDUSTRY REAFFIRMING COMMITMENT AND HIGHLIGHTING INVESTMENTS THAT HAVE BENEFITED OVER 14 MILLION PRODUCERS. A signed memorandum with the bank that finances the projects arriving on your land, held by the body your farmers' union belongs to. When a bank-funded project harms a member community, that memorandum is a named relationship to invoke — and this file's Nigeria entry holds the same bank's complaint mechanism. THE SECOND SIGNED AGREEMENT AND WHAT IT COVERS: A COOPERATION AGREEMENT WITH A CONTINENTAL AGRICULTURE ALLIANCE TO STRENGTHEN THE CAPACITIES OF AFRICAN FARMERS' ORGANIZATIONS — SUPPORTING THEM TO CONDUCT POLITICAL ADVOCACY AROUND AREAS OF COMMON INTEREST AT CONTINENTAL, REGIONAL AND NATIONAL LEVELS, AND SUPPORTING PROGRAMS ENSURING WOMEN AND YOUNG FARMERS HAVE ACCESS TO RESOURCES THAT ALLOW THEM TO BE MORE PRODUCTIVE, UNHINDERED BY GENDER AND SOCIOCULTURAL NORMS, BARRIERS TO MARKET ENTRY AND OTHER INSTITUTIONAL OBSTACLES. POLITICAL ADVOCACY, named in a signed agreement as fundable. Compare the indigenous-led fund under Chad, which excludes political campaigns outright — knowing which doors treat advocacy as legitimate decides where the same work should be sent. AND THE GLOBAL SEAT: DELEGATIONS ATTEND A FARMERS' FORUM HELD IN ROME ALONGSIDE AN INTERNATIONAL AGRICULTURAL DEVELOPMENT FUND, WITH 80-PLUS FARMERS' LEADERS REPRESENTING MILLIONS OF SMALLHOLDERS AND RURAL PRODUCERS. A standing forum where farmer leaders sit with the fund that lends to their governments. The route there begins at a district meeting. WHO IT SUITS: African farmers' unions, cooperatives and national platforms — and community groups wanting their issue carried above national level through a structure that already exists. CAVEATS: MEMBERSHIP IS REGIONAL NETWORKS, NOT INDIVIDUAL GROUPS, AND IT COORDINATES AND ADVOCATES RATHER THAN FUNDING OR LITIGATING — join your national platform, which joins the regional network. For the West African member network from the inside, Mauritania's entry; for the farmer-governed development agencies, Eswatini's entry; for the same bank's complaint mechanism, Nigeria's entry.

trackers.name: ClientEarth — an environmental law charity that has no African offices and works through named strategic partners instead — with a published rule that it only brings cases it expects to win, and a forest-community result already on record
trackers.desc: IN AFRICA THEY WORK THROUGH PARTNERS. FIND THE PARTNER — adjacency declared first: A COMMUNITY-AND-ENVIRONMENT LAW NON-PROFIT WITH OFFICES IN CAPE TOWN, NAIROBI AND DAKAR IS ALREADY A NAMED ENTRY IN NINE AFRICA BUCKETS, AND AN ENVIRONMENTAL DEFENDER LAW CENTRE IS A HOST UNDER SOUTH AFRICA; NEITHER IS RESTATED AND NEITHER HOST IS SHIPPED. THIS FILE'S DR CONGO ENTRY COVERS THE INTERNATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL LAW ORGANISATION THAT IS EXPLICITLY NOT A LAW FIRM. HOW IT OPERATES IN AFRICA, WHICH IS THE FIND AND ALSO THE LIMIT: ITS ENTITIES SIT ACROSS THREE REGIONS — NORTH AMERICA, ASIA AND THE PACIFIC, AND EUROPE — AND IT ADDITIONALLY OPERATES IN LATIN AMERICA AND AFRICA VIA STRATEGIC PARTNERS. There is no African office to write to. Approaching the London headquarters about a case in your district is the wrong door; the right one is the partner organisation in your country, which is a national body with its own staff and its own mandate. Establish who that is before spending effort — and note that the relationship runs the other way too: a national organisation that becomes a strategic partner gains access to a large litigation team. THE NAMED AFRICAN PARTNER, WHICH IS THE CONCRETE ADDRESS: A FOUNDATION FOR COMMUNITY INITIATIVES IN LIBERIA, ONE OF ITS PARTNER ORGANISATIONS, WHOSE EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR HAS SPENT A DECADE WORKING TO IMPROVE WOMEN'S LIVES IN RURAL AREAS BY ADVOCATING FOR THEIR RIGHTS TO LAND OWNERSHIP AND EQUAL PARTICIPATION IN FOREST GOVERNANCE. A named Liberian organisation led by a named woman working on rural land ownership and forest governance. For West African forest communities that is a contact in the region, and it is the kind of partner this charity chooses — which tells you what a candidate partner looks like. THE AFRICAN AIM AS IT STATES IT: WE SUPPORT FOREST COMMUNITIES TO HAVE A SAY IN THE LAWS AFFECTING THEIR LAND BECAUSE WE BELIEVE IT'S THE BEST LONG-TERM APPROACH TO PROTECTING FORESTS. A SAY IN THE LAWS, not only in the project. This file has recorded communities consulted about a concession after the forest code was already written; the work here is upstream of that, at the drafting stage. THE AFRICAN RESULT ON RECORD: IT HAS HELPED COMMUNITIES IN AFRICA'S LAST GREAT RAINFOREST CUT ILLEGAL LOGGING. THE CASE-SELECTION RULE, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND AND SAVES A WASTED APPROACH: WE ONLY BRING CASES WHEN WE STRONGLY BELIEVE WE HAVE A REASONABLE CHANCE OF WINNING, AND THE OUTCOME WILL HAVE POSITIVE ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS ON A LARGE SCALE. Two conditions, both hard. A strong claim about one village will not qualify if the ruling changes nothing beyond it. Communities should read that honestly: this is a route for cases that set a precedent, and the file's local legal aid and paralegal entries are the route for cases that matter to one place. THE ACCESS-TO-JUSTICE WORK IT DESCRIBES: IT SUPPORTS THE PEOPLE AND COMMUNITIES MOST AFFECTED BY ENVIRONMENTAL DEGRADATION TO DEFEND THEIR RIGHTS, AND MAKES SURE PEOPLE, PROSECUTORS AND CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS CAN PARTICIPATE IN ENVIRONMENTAL DECISION-MAKING, AND GO TO COURT WHEN LAWS ARE BROKEN. PROSECUTORS named alongside communities. Where a state prosecutor could act on environmental crime but does not know how, training them is a route that removes the burden from the community entirely — and it is a thing to ask a partner organisation to pursue. THE INFORMATION RIGHT IT WORKS ON: IT MAKES SURE PEOPLE CAN FIND INFORMATION ABOUT THE ENVIRONMENT WHERE THEY LIVE AND WORK, SO THEY CAN TAKE THAT INFORMATION TO COURT WHEN THINGS GO WRONG — PROMOTING THE RIGHT TO INFORMATION AND ACCESS TO JUSTICE. The right to the document comes before the case. This file has recorded again and again that the impact assessment, the permit and the concession map are what a community cannot get; establishing the right to them is the work that makes everything else possible. THE FULL RANGE: INFORMING, IMPLEMENTING AND ENFORCING THE LAW; ADVISING DECISION-MAKERS ON POLICY; AND TRAINING LEGAL AND JUDICIAL PROFESSIONALS — STRENGTHENING THE ENTIRE SYSTEM, FROM HOW LAWS ARE WRITTEN TO HOW THEY ARE APPLIED, INTERPRETED AND ENFORCED BY COURTS AND REGULATORS. TRAINING JUDGES. A court that has never heard an environmental case decides badly through unfamiliarity as often as through bias, and judicial training is a slow intervention that changes every case afterwards. THE OTHER THINGS IT DOES FOR COMMUNITIES: IT DRAFTS LEGISLATION, TRAINS JUDGES, SUPPORTS COMMUNITIES FACING ENVIRONMENTAL HARM AND SHAPES GLOBAL POLICY FRAMEWORKS — WHETHER DEFENDING FORESTS FROM ILLEGAL LOGGING, PROTECTING RIVERS FROM POLLUTION OR CHALLENGING FOSSIL FUEL EXPANSION. ITS STATED THEORY, RECORDED BECAUSE IT SHAPES WHAT IT WILL TAKE ON: THE ENVIRONMENTAL CRISIS IS TOO BIG TO BE ADDRESSED BOTTOM-UP; TO DELIVER CHANGE AT THE RATE NEEDED THERE NEEDS TO BE SYSTEMIC CHANGE, AND TO DO THIS YOU NEED THE LAW — AND IT CHANGES THE SYSTEM FROM WITHIN, WORKING WITH, INSTEAD OF AGAINST, ITS MOST POWERFUL PLAYERS. Recorded plainly because it will not suit everyone: an organisation that says the crisis cannot be addressed bottom-up, and that works with powerful players rather than against them, is a different proposition from the confrontational routes elsewhere in this file. Where a community's whole case is that the powerful player is the problem, weigh that before approaching — and compare the organisation under Egypt, which states the opposite posture. THE TOOLS COMMITMENT: IT GIVES PEOPLE, PARTNERS AND ORGANISATIONS THE TOOLS THEY NEED TO DO THE SAME. AND THE SCALE AND THE CASES IT NAMES: FOUNDED IN 2007, ACTIVE IN OVER 60 COUNTRIES, WITH CASES INCLUDING TAKING A GOVERNMENT TO COURT FOR BREAKING AIR QUALITY LAWS, CONFRONTING A STATE FOR BREACHING THE HUMAN RIGHTS OF ISLANDERS WHOSE HOMES ARE BEING WASHED AWAY BY RISING SEAS, SUING A FOOD MULTINATIONAL OVER PLASTIC WASTE, AND A GREENWASHING CASE AGAINST AN AIRLINE THAT SET A PRECEDENT. ISLANDERS WHOSE HOMES ARE BEING WASHED AWAY, taken as a human rights case against a state. For African coastal and island communities losing land to the sea, that is the closest precedent in this entry — and it was won on rights, not on environmental law. WHO IT SUITS: African national environmental organisations that could become strategic partners, and forest communities whose case would change the law rather than one permit. CAVEATS: NO AFRICAN OFFICES, WORKS THROUGH PARTNERS, TAKES ONLY CASES IT EXPECTS TO WIN WITH LARGE-SCALE IMPACT, AND WORKS WITH POWERFUL ACTORS BY DESIGN — for a single community's dispute, use the national and regional legal entries. For the environmental law organisation that builds tools for others to use, DR Congo's entry; for the confrontational posture, Egypt's entry.

trackers.name: BirdLife South Africa — the organisation that got a biodiversity tax deduction written into national law — communities and communal landowners can deduct the value of land they protect, with the rules, the fact sheets and a named tax specialist published
trackers.desc: PROTECT IT FOR 99 YEARS AND DEDUCT THE VALUE OF THE LAND FROM YOUR TAX — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S SÃO TOMÉ ENTRY COVERS THE SERVITUDE TRUST, ITS ESWATINI ENTRY THE CAPITAL FUND, ITS SOUTH SUDAN ENTRY THE BODY THAT BUYS FARMS; ITS SOUTH AFRICA BUCKET CARRIES A BIODIVERSITY INSTITUTE HOST AND NAME. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. WHAT THE PROJECT PUT INTO LAW, WHICH IS THE FIND: IT INTRODUCED A NEW TAX INCENTIVE, SECTION 37D, INTO THE NATIONAL INCOME TAX ACT — ALLOWING LANDOWNERS AND COMMUNITIES DECLARING NATURE RESERVES AND NATIONAL PARKS TO DEDUCT THE FULL VALUE OF THE LAND DECLARED FROM THEIR TAXABLE INCOME. An NGO wrote a clause into the tax code. Most of this file records organisations arguing against laws; this one added one, and the result pays the people who protect land every year rather than once. When a community asks what it gains by declaring its land protected, this is a number on a tax return. THE COMMUNAL LAND POINT, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: THE INCENTIVE APPLIES TO PROTECTED AREAS DECLARED ON PRIVATE OR COMMUNALLY OWNED LAND, AND PROVIDES A REDUCTION IN TAX LIABILITY FOR COMMUNAL AND PRIVATE LANDOWNERS — WITH DECLARATIONS MADE BY PRIVATE LANDOWNERS, COMMUNAL PROPERTY ASSOCIATIONS OR OCCUPIERS OF COMMUNAL LAND. COMMUNAL PROPERTY ASSOCIATIONS AND OCCUPIERS OF COMMUNAL LAND named as eligible. Community-held land is inside the scheme, not an exception to it — which is rare in tax law and is the detail worth checking against your own country's code. THE MECHANICS, PUBLISHED: ELIGIBILITY APPLIES TO LAND DECLARED AS A NATURE RESERVE OR NATIONAL PARK UNDER TWO NAMED SECTIONS OF THE PROTECTED AREAS ACT; THE LAND MUST BE SUBJECT TO A TITLE DEED ENDORSEMENT FOR A MINIMUM OF 99 YEARS; THE DEDUCTION IS A 4% STRAIGHT-LINE DEDUCTION ON THE VALUE OF THE LAND DECLARED; IT BECOMES EFFECTIVE IN THE YEAR THE LAND IS DECLARED AND THE ENDORSEMENT IS EFFECTED; AND IT CAN BE SET OFF AGAINST TAXABLE INCOME OR USED TO INCREASE AN ASSESSED LOSS. Ninety-nine years, endorsed on the title deed. Read that beside the servitude filed under São Tomé: both put the protection into the deeds registry, but this one comes with an annual payment attached. 4% straight-line means the full value is recovered over 25 years, which is a serious sum against a farm. THE PENALTY IF IT IS UNDONE: IF THE PROTECTED AREA STATUS IS TERMINATED UNDER THE PROTECTED AREAS ACT, THE TAXPAYER MAY BE LIABLE FOR CERTAIN TAX PENALTIES. A financial cost to reversing the protection, which is the teeth. A future owner who wants to develop the land inherits a tax bill for doing so. WHY THIS IS UNUSUAL AT ALL: GENERALLY, THE VALUE OF LAND IS NOT DEDUCTIBLE FOR TAX PURPOSES — THIS DEDUCTION OFFERS A UNIQUE OPPORTUNITY TO DEDUCT THE VALUE OF LAND. THE PROOF IT WORKS: TESTED AT PILOT SITES ACROSS THE COUNTRY, RESULTING IN THE SUCCESSFUL INCLUSION OF THIS TAX BREAK IN A TAX RETURN IN 2016 — AND ONE NAMED PRIVATE RESERVE RECEIVED THE DEDUCTION, WITH THE TANGIBLE FINANCIAL BENEFIT BOLSTERING ITS CASH FLOW SO THAT ADDITIONAL RESOURCES COULD BE MOBILISED. Claimed, accepted, and on record. That precedent is what a landowner's accountant will want to see before advising them to sign. THE FREE MATERIAL AND THE NAMED CONTACT: THE PROJECT PROVIDES HIGH-LEVEL SUMMARIES AND TECHNICAL TAX OVERVIEWS, WITH UPDATED FACT SHEETS PUBLISHED FOR IMPLEMENTERS, LANDOWNERS AND OTHER VESTED STAKEHOLDERS — WITH A NAMED PROJECT MANAGER AND TAX SPECIALIST GIVEN AS THE CONTACT. A named tax specialist inside a conservation organisation, reachable, with the technical sheets free. That combination does not exist anywhere else in this file, and it is exactly what a community negotiating with a landowner cannot otherwise obtain. THE STATED LIMIT ON THAT MATERIAL: THESE TAX RESOURCES DO NOT CONSTITUTE TAX ADVICE AND MAY NOT BE USED AS SUCH. Recorded plainly — the fact sheets prepare the conversation with an accountant, they do not replace it. THE SCALE OF THE OPPORTUNITY: APPROXIMATELY 75% OF THE COUNTRY IS HELD IN PRIVATE OWNERSHIP; LANDOWNERS BEAR THE RESPONSIBILITY OF MANAGING PROTECTED AREAS AND FACE FINANCIAL COMMITMENTS AS A RESULT — AND THE COST TO THE STATE OF BIODIVERSITY STEWARDSHIP IS A FRACTION OF THE COST OF ACQUIRING AND MANAGING STATE-OWNED PROTECTED AREAS. CHEAPER THAN BUYING IT is the argument that persuades a treasury. Where a government says it cannot afford to protect an area, the counter is that a stewardship declaration costs it a fraction of an acquisition — and this is the sourced version of that claim. HOW THE DECLARATION HAPPENS: THROUGH A GOVERNMENT-LED REGIME OF BILATERAL AGREEMENTS WITH PRIVATE AND COMMUNAL LANDOWNERS TO FORMALLY CONSERVE AND MAINTAIN A PARTICULAR AREA OF LAND — ESTABLISHED THROUGH A NATIONAL BIODIVERSITY STEWARDSHIP INITIATIVE, WHOSE KEY PRINCIPLES INCLUDE FOCUSING ON PRIORITY AREAS, VOLUNTARY COMMITMENT FROM LANDOWNERS, AND WORKING IN PARTNERSHIPS. VOLUNTARY COMMITMENT is the safeguard to check: a community entering such an agreement is contracting with the state, and the terms of that agreement decide whether it keeps its use of the land. THE NATIONAL GUIDELINE THAT EXISTS FOR IT: A BIODIVERSITY STEWARDSHIP GUIDELINE DETAILING EVERY ASPECT OF SECURING HIGH BIODIVERSITY LAND UNDER LONG TERM PROTECTION AND MANAGEMENT, WITH EXPERT INPUT FROM LEADING PRACTITIONERS, PRACTICAL TOOLKITS PER CHAPTER, AND AN EXAMPLE DECLARATION DIAGRAM DEFINING A GEOGRAPHIC AREA OVER A CADASTRE. Toolkits per chapter and a worked declaration diagram over a cadastre. That is the document to hand a lawyer or a provincial official rather than describing what you want. AND THE LESSON THE PROJECT PUBLISHES ABOUT ITS OWN METHOD: ATTEMPTING TO INTRODUCE THE COUNTRY'S FIRST BIODIVERSITY TAX INCENTIVE IN ISOLATION WOULD HAVE BEEN AN ERROR — IT HAD TO BE INTRODUCED INTO THE CONTEXT OF AN EXISTING COMMUNITY OF PRACTICE OF IMPLEMENTERS RANGING FROM NATIONAL AND PROVINCIAL GOVERNMENT TO NGOs AND SPECIALISTS. The tax change succeeded because it was carried by people already running the stewardship programme. Anyone attempting the same in another country should find that existing community of practice first rather than drafting alone. WHO IT SUITS: African communities, communal property associations and sympathetic landowners weighing formal protection — and organisations elsewhere seeking a working model for a biodiversity tax incentive. CAVEATS: THE INCENTIVE IS SOUTH AFRICAN LAW AND DEPENDS ON A DECLARED PROTECTED AREA AND A 99-YEAR TITLE DEED ENDORSEMENT, WHICH IS A PERMANENT COMMITMENT; THE PUBLISHED MATERIAL IS EXPRESSLY NOT TAX ADVICE — take it to an accountant. For binding land through a servitude instead, São Tomé's entry; for the fund that has bought land, Eswatini's entry.

trackers.name: Nkuzi Development Association — the association whose own national survey found 4.18 million people displaced from farms in twenty years with only 1% involving any legal process — and which runs the paralegal service, claim-form help and legal facility that came out of it
trackers.desc: 1.7 MILLION EVICTED, AND ONLY 1% WENT THROUGH A COURT — method and adjacency declared first: THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THE SHIPPED HOST AND FIVE SUBJECT SPELLINGS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL ABSENT. THIS FILE'S SOUTH AFRICA BUCKET CARRIES A RURAL ADVANCEMENT ASSOCIATION WORKING WITH FARM DWELLERS ON A DIFFERENT HOST, ITS ESWATINI ENTRY THE FARM WOMEN'S NGO AND THE TENURE GRANT, ITS RWANDA ENTRY THE 48-COMMUNITY RESTITUTION FEDERATION. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE SURVEY FIGURES, WHICH IS THE FIND: BETWEEN 1984 AND 2004, ABOUT 4.18 MILLION PEOPLE HAD BEEN DISPLACED FROM FARMS, AND ABOUT 1.7 MILLION OF THESE HAD BEEN EVICTED — AND ONLY 1% OF THESE DISPLACEMENTS HAD INVOLVED A LEGAL PROCESS. ONE PER CENT. This file has recorded eviction after eviction described as lawful; here is the measured proportion that ever saw a court, produced by a community organisation's own national survey and presented to a parliamentary committee. Ninety-nine times in a hundred there was no order, which means the first question a farm dweller should ask — where are the papers — is almost always the winning one. WHEN THE EVICTIONS HAPPEN, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: MOST OCCURRED DURING TIMES OF POLITICAL UNCERTAINTY AND TRADE LIBERALISATION, AND TIMES OF DROUGHT — WITH CHILDREN AND WOMEN THE MOST VULNERABLE; A LACK OF INFORMATION AND ACCESS TO LEGAL HELP WAS A GREAT PROBLEM. Evictions cluster around elections, trade shocks and drought. A community can therefore anticipate rather than react: the season to have paralegals trained and contacts in place is the season before the water fails or the political calendar turns. THE PRACTICE THE SURVEY EXPOSED: ONCE IT BECAME CLEAR THAT LAWS RESTRICTING MOVEMENT WOULD BE PHASED OUT, SOME LANDOWNERS STARTED THE PRACTICE OF SHACK FARMING, AND WERE GUILTY OF INFRINGING UPON THE RIGHTS OF WORKERS — WITH SOME WORKERS RECLASSIFIED AS RETRENCHED RATHER THAN EVICTED. RETRENCHED RATHER THAN EVICTED is the relabelling to watch for: end the job and the housing claim is presented as ending with it. Two separate rights, deliberately collapsed into one. WHAT IT DOES ON A CLAIM: ESTABLISHED IN 1997 TO ASSIST COMMUNITIES TO LODGE LAND CLAIMS AFTER A RESTITUTION ACT, WHEN THE CLAIMS COMMISSION'S OFFICES WERE ONLY IN THE CAPITAL — ASSISTING IN THE COMPLETION OF CLAIMS FORMS, FACILITATION OF LAND CLAIMS COMMITTEES, AND DOCUMENTATION OF SUPPORTING EVIDENCE, SO CLAIMANT COMMUNITIES WOULD NOT MISS THE CUT-OFF DATE. The organisation exists because the state put its only claims office in the capital and set a deadline. Filling in forms and gathering evidence is unglamorous work, and it is the difference between a claim lodged and a claim lost to a date — the same barrier this file records under every registration requirement. THE LEGAL FACILITY IT INITIATED: A LAND RIGHTS MANAGEMENT FACILITY ESTABLISHED TO PROVIDE SPECIALISED LEGAL SKILLS AND TO ASSIST LAND DWELLERS AND EVICTEES WITH LEGAL ADVICE — AN INITIATIVE OF THIS ASSOCIATION, WHICH SOUGHT LEGAL ASSISTANCE FOR BENEFICIARIES OF LAND REFORM AFTER THE COURTS RULED THAT INDIGENT FARM DWELLERS ARE ENTITLED TO IT. A court ruled that poor farm dwellers are ENTITLED to legal assistance, and a community organisation then built the facility to deliver it. That is the sequence worth copying: win the entitlement, then construct the thing that supplies it, rather than waiting for the state to. ITS FOUR PROGRAMMES: LAND REFORM IMPLEMENTATION, FARM DWELLER, RESEARCH AND POLICY, AND LEGAL SERVICES — WITH THE FIRST CONTAINING COMMUNITY ORGANIZING AND TRAINING AND SUSTAINABLE LIVELIHOODS SUPPORT. THE FOURTH OBJECTIVE, STATED PLAINLY: FOR QUALITY LEGAL AND PARALEGAL SUPPORT TO BE AVAILABLE TO ENABLE THE POOR AND LANDLESS PEOPLE TO EXERCISE THEIR LAND RIGHTS AND OTHER HUMAN RIGHTS. THE DEPENDENCY IT DOCUMENTS: WHERE FARM DWELLERS RECEIVE SERVICES SUCH AS HOUSING, ELECTRICITY AND SCHOOLING, IT IS OFTEN AT THE MERCY OF LANDOWNERS — IF LANDOWNERS DO NOT WANT THEM TO HAVE A MOBILE CLINIC OR SCHOOLS, THEY WILL NOT GET THEM, WHICH EXPLAINS WHY MOST OF THE CHILDREN OR PEOPLE ON FARMS ARE NOT EVEN DOCUMENTED AND DO NOT EVEN GET SOCIAL GRANTS. Undocumented people cannot claim a grant, register a birth, or prove they lived somewhere for thirty years. The landowner's veto over a clinic becomes, a generation later, the reason a family cannot prove its own occupation — which is why getting documents is land work. THE SCHOOL CLOSURE FINDING: NATIONALLY, MOST OF THE SCHOOLS EARMARKED FOR CLOSURE ARE MOSTLY FARM SCHOOLS, WHICH WILL OBVIOUSLY AFFECT FARM DWELLER CHILDREN'S RIGHT TO EDUCATION. Closing the school is a quieter way of clearing a farm than any eviction notice. ITS ASSESSMENT OF THE OFFICIAL COMMITTEES: DESPITE BEING SIDE-LINED, IT AND OTHER ORGANISATIONS WERE MOBILISING LOCAL COMMUNITIES TO ATTEND THE MEETINGS AND PARTICIPATE — BUT DISTRICT LAND REFORM COMMITTEES DO NOT SEEM TO HAVE POLICIES OR STRATEGIES AIMED AT THE BETTERMENT OF PEOPLE IN RURAL AREAS, AND ONE CANNOT HELP BUT CONCLUDE THAT THE COMMITTEES ARE A SCHEME AIMED AT JUSTIFYING THE EXPENDITURE OF FUNDS BY THE DEPARTMENT. An honest verdict on a participation structure, from an organisation that keeps sending people to it anyway. Both halves are the lesson: attend, and do not mistake attendance for influence. ITS POSITION ON A MORATORIUM: A MORATORIUM ON EVICTIONS, WITHOUT PUTTING MEASURES IN PLACE THAT ENSURE IT IS PROPERLY IMPLEMENTED AND MONITORED, WOULD NOT ACHIEVE WHAT IS INTENDED. A land organisation arguing against the headline demand unless monitoring comes with it. Worth remembering when a government offers a freeze instead of a remedy. AND WHAT IT SAYS IT IS AIMING AT, PLUS HOW IT LEARNS: DISADVANTAGED WOMEN AND MEN ORGANISED AND EMPOWERED TO ASSERT THEIR RIGHTS, BASED ON ACCESS TO SUFFICIENT LAND, SECURE TENURE, BASIC SERVICES AND INTEGRATED LOCAL ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT — WITH LANDLESS PEOPLE EMPOWERED TO DRIVE A LAND REFORM PROCESS WHICH SHIFTS POWER RELATIONS; ITS DIRECTOR, DEPUTY DIRECTOR, FARM DWELLER PROGRAMME MANAGER AND A VOLUNTEER RESEARCHER ATTENDED A WEEK-LONG WORKSHOP ON PARTICIPATORY ACTION RESEARCH, AND IT WAS ASKED TO JOIN A TASK TEAM DRAFTING AN ALTERNATIVE FARM DWELLER POLICY. The senior staff went on a research training course together, and the survey above is what came of it. A community organisation that can produce its own national numbers gets asked to help draft the policy. WHO IT SUITS: farm dwellers and landless communities lodging restitution claims or facing eviction — and organisations anywhere wanting the survey-then-parliament model, or the argument that most evictions never see a court. CAVEATS: ONE COUNTRY, AND THE HEADLINE SURVEY COVERS 1984–2004, SO THE FIGURES ARE HISTORICAL EVEN THOUGH THE PATTERN PERSISTS; IT ORGANISES, RESEARCHES AND ARRANGES PARALEGAL AND LEGAL SUPPORT RATHER THAN LITIGATING AS A LAW CENTRE. For the statutory grant that buys land for farm dwellers, Eswatini's entry; for the federation that litigated restitution delays, Rwanda's entry.

trackers.name: Somalia — Registrar of Companies (Ministry of Commerce & Industry)
trackers.desc: National corporate registry; the Registrar of Companies at the Ministry of Commerce & Industry registers local & foreign-owned companies & business licences (renewable annually), Somalia. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Somalia — Ministry of Finance
trackers.desc: National budget authority; the Federal Ministry of Finance develops economic policy, prepares & executes the federal budget (presented to Parliament each October) and publishes fiscal & revenue reports, Somalia. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Somalia.

trackers.name: Somalia — Office of the Auditor General (OAG)
trackers.desc: National public-finance watchdog; the federal Supreme Audit Institution (strengthened by the 2023 Federal Audit Law) conducts financial, compliance & performance audits of government institutions and reports to Parliament, Somalia.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: East African Court of Justice — it stopped a road across the Serengeti
trackers.desc: THIS COURT STOPPED A GOVERNMENT FROM BUILDING A ROAD. In African Network for Animal Welfare v Attorney General of the United Republic of Tanzania (Reference No. 9 of 2010, judgment 20 June 2014), the East African Court of Justice held Tanzania's proposed highway across the Serengeti National Park unlawful and issued an injunction restraining Tanzania from operationalising it. THE TREATY ARTICLES THAT DID THE WORK: article 5(3)(c) of the EAC Treaty — promotion of sustainable utilisation of natural resources and measures that would effectively protect the natural environment of the Partner States — and article 114(1)(a), which enjoins partner states to conserve, protect and manage the environment. THE HARMS PLEADED ARE A REUSABLE CHECKLIST: disrupted animal migration, fragmentation of habitats, loss of scenic and visual quality, deterioration of air quality, increased poaching, and surface water and soil pollution. NOTE THE SHAPE OF THE RELIEF: at para 78 the Court said its orders must be preventative, and that roads in the Serengeti should be used by wildlife, tourists and Park administrators and not the general public — a restriction on who may use a road is a narrower and more grantable order than an outright ban. The government's own report had conceded grave negative impacts. THREE THINGS MAKE THIS ROUTE UNUSUAL: (1) standing survived a full challenge — the objection on jurisdiction, limitation and form was overruled on 26 August 2011 and the appeal dismissed on 15 March 2012; (2) the applicant was not from the respondent state — ANAW is a pan-African charity that sued Tanzania without being Tanzanian, so an NGO based in one partner state can challenge another's project; and (3) this is a trade-and-integration court, not a specialist environmental one — the claim runs through treaty obligations between states. CONFIRM PARTNER-STATE STATUS BEFORE FILING: this state's EAC accession is relatively recent, and the Court's jurisdiction follows partner-state status. This entry does not assert current standing to file — verify it first.

trackers.name: Candlelight — a Somaliland organisation with eighty staff and four offices that restores communal grazing land with the communities that hold it
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Candlelight for Environment, Education and Health, founded in 1995 in the wreckage of the civil war, now working across all six regions of Somaliland with more than eighty staff, a head office in Hargeisa and sub-offices in Sheikh, Burao and Erigavo, and stated work in Somalia, Ethiopia and Kenya as well. Environmental restoration and protection is its first stated priority. WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES ON LAND, which is the part that transfers: it works on the restoration of communal grazing areas — its documented case being the Dulcad plain — using crescent-shaped soil bunds built to a standard section, roughly 80 centimetres high on a one-metre base, in runs of thirty metres and up, which is a technique a village can be trained in and can build itself. In a pastoral economy where the land is held in common and the threat is degradation, enclosure and charcoal cutting rather than a permit, rehabilitating and re-establishing the commons is how you hold it. It runs community environmental awareness in named villages, trains community animal health workers, and researches the invasive mesquite that is taking over degraded land — including testing whether it can be turned into charcoal so the pressure comes off the native Acacia. It sits in the Resource Management Somali Network, which brings together thirteen organisations and teams from Somalia and Somaliland working on environment, and works with the pastoral development and environment ministry. WHO IT SUITS: pastoral and rural communities in Somaliland facing loss of communal grazing, enclosure or deforestation. Sha'ab Road, Hargeisa. CAVEATS: THIS IS A SOMALILAND ORGANISATION and its reach into south-central Somalia should not be assumed — it is filed under Somalia because this map has no separate key. It is a development and environment NGO, not a legal or advocacy defence body: no litigation, no intake route, no fee information, and published contact addresses vary between its own pages.

trackers.name: SOLLA and Somalia's land-dispute routes — the bar association whose members must give free legal aid, and the collective land purchase that worked
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: SOLLA, Somaliland's bar association, whose members are OBLIGED to provide free legal aid — with lawyers representing female clients at all stages of proceedings and paralegals working in the Hargeisa region; a legal aid clinic operates at the University of Hargeisa. That obligation is the single most useful fact for anyone in Somaliland who cannot pay. THE TWO COMMUNITY ROUTES THAT RESEARCH RECORDS AS HAVING WORKED, and both are things a group can organise itself: MINORITY GROUPS COLLECTIVELY PURCHASING LAND to improve their negotiating power, which has secured tenure; and grassroots MEDIATION COMMITTEES, in regions such as Kismayo, resolving disputes outside the formal courts. In Puntland, community elders are reported to resolve between 90 and 95 per cent of land disputes — so the forum that decides your case is probably not a court, and the elders' process is the one to prepare for. WHAT THE DISPUTES ACTUALLY ARE: most people buy and sell land outside the formal system; very few hold registered ownership and most are squatters or tenants. Disputes involve land grabbing and illegal occupation by clan leaders, businessmen, corporations, returnees and members of the diaspora, abuses by IDP camp gatekeepers, conflicts between international NGOs and private landowners, and returning refugees claiming the same plot. Officials have been reported abusing their positions for land grabbing and forced eviction, particularly against displaced returnees. Women are structurally exposed — excluded from inheritance and holding unequal negotiating power in customary dispute resolution — which is why the free representation of female clients matters. Somalia has National Eviction Guidelines (2019) and an IDP policy; campaigners note the guidelines still need enabling legislation to sue under. WHO IT SUITS: Somalis and Somalilanders facing eviction, occupation of their plot, or a land dispute headed to elders rather than a court — especially women and displaced returnees. CAVEATS: NO VERIFIED LIVE SITE FOR SOLLA WAS FOUND — this entry points at the housing, land and property mapping that records it, and some details date from that research; provision is concentrated in Somaliland and Hargeisa. For environment and communal grazing restoration, Somalia's Candlelight entry.

trackers.name: GEF Small Grants in Somalia — the eighth cycle added Somalia by name, with nearly USD 1 million allocated equally to every participating country
trackers.desc: WHERE TO APPLY FOR MONEY: the GEF SMALL GRANTS PROGRAMME, running since 1992 to fund CIVIL SOCIETY and LOCAL ACTION on environmental degradation. THE FACT THAT MATTERS HERE, AND IT IS RECENT: the eighth replenishment EXPANDED COUNTRY COVERAGE FROM 124 TO 135 COUNTRIES, ADDING SOMALIA BY NAME — alongside SOUTH SUDAN, LIBYA, EQUATORIAL GUINEA, SÃO TOMÉ AND PRÍNCIPE and Angola. Somalia was outside this window and now is inside it; if you were told years ago that no environmental small grants existed here, that answer is out of date. THE ALLOCATION RULE IS THE UNUSUAL PART: the cycle secured USD 135 million for the core programme and ensures EQUAL ALLOCATION OF NEARLY USD 1 MILLION IN CORE FINANCING TO EACH OF THE 135 COUNTRIES — regardless of size or previous participation levels, with STAR allocations to the programme raised over 30 per cent. Equal allocation regardless of size means a small or newly-added country is not competing against large established programmes for the core money — that is the argument for applying early in a first cycle. Its stated objective is to catalyse and mobilise civil society actors and LOCAL ACTIONS addressing the major drivers of environmental degradation. ALSO OPEN TO SOMALI ORGANISATIONS, recorded together because the search is the same: UN-administered LOW-VALUE GRANTS of USD 30,000 to USD 80,000 per project for Somali civil society organisations, and larger community-resilience grants of up to USD 1,000,000 over 24 to 36 months requiring legal registration BOTH in the target federal member state AND with the federal government. Registration in both places is the gate on the large grants — check yours before drafting. WHO IT SUITS: Somali and Somaliland community organisations with an environmental, rangeland, water or resilience project. CAVEATS: DONOR CYCLES WITH FIXED DEADLINES — confirm the country programme is operational before counting on it, and note it funds environmental and resilience action, NOT litigation or land purchase. For land disputes, free legal aid and the collective-purchase route, Somalia's SOLLA entry; for environment and communal grazing, Candlelight.

trackers.name: Community rangeland enclosures and grazing reserves — the Balaanbal sequence that worked, and the difference between a community reserve and a private land grab
trackers.desc: HOW A COMMUNITY HOLDS GRAZING GROUND: the working instrument in Somaliland and Puntland is the COMMUNITY RANGELAND ENCLOSURE or GRAZING RESERVE — land fenced and closed by a village so pasture regenerates and is held in reserve for drought. THE DOCUMENTED SEQUENCE, WHICH IS THE PART TO COPY, from BALAANBAL in the TOGDHEER region: residents were asked to LIST THEIR NATURAL RESOURCES and then IDENTIFY THE AREA to be fenced; a NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT COMMITTEE was set up; the committee DEVELOPED A NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT PLAN, STOPPED ALL ONGOING CHARCOAL PRODUCTION on community land, SET UP A COMMUNITY PATROL, and then RAISED EXTENSIVE COMMUNITY AWARENESS about the reserve. List, choose, commit a plan, stop the extraction already happening, patrol, then tell everyone — in that order. Stopping your own charcoal cutting before you ask anyone else to respect the boundary is what makes the claim defensible. WHAT IT PRODUCED: the project was HANDED OVER TO THE GOVERNMENT on completion, and during the 2025 drought the government OPENED THE ENCLOSED AREAS for livestock — officials reported 20,000 ANIMALS GRAZING in the enclosure when there was no pasture in the open rangelands. Research on the AROORI GRAZING RESERVE, re-established 2016, records reserves as fodder refuges in prolonged drought and as tools to maintain indigenous grass biodiversity, and identifies the emerging form as VILLAGE GRAZING LOTS established through JOINT LAND-USE PLANNING. THE DISTINCTION THAT DECIDES WHETHER YOURS IS LEGITIMATE, RECORDED HONESTLY: conflict research finds unregulated enclosures PREDOMINANT in rural Somaliland, often built to produce CHARCOAL FOR CASH from the trees inside, with the state too weak to regulate land — and attempts to dismantle them in Balligubadle FAILED because people simply re-established them when no alternative livelihood was offered. A private enclosure that harvests what is inside it is a land grab; a community reserve that closes an area, bans charcoal and opens in drought is the opposite — the paperwork looks identical, so make the ban, the patrol and the drought rule explicit and public from the start. WHO IT SUITS: Somali and Somaliland pastoral communities and village committees. CAVEATS: CUSTOMARY AND PROJECT-BASED, NOT TITLE — the Balaanbal reserve was handed to government and opened by government decision; land regulation is weak and enclosure is itself a live source of conflict. For land disputes and collective purchase, Somalia's SOLLA entry; for environment and communal grazing work, Candlelight; for community funding, the GEF Small Grants entry.

trackers.name: Somali Greenpeace Association, Mogadishu — 40+ members across Somalia, and the named NGO roster that sat with traditional elders in the national land-degradation consultations
trackers.desc: WHO WORKS IN THE SOUTH, AND WHO SAT AT THE TABLE — because this file's Somalia record has been Somaliland-weighted and a Mogadishu-based route was missing: the SOMALI GREENPEACE ASSOCIATION (SOGPA), a civil-society non-profit FORMED IN 2019 IN MOGADISHU with MORE THAN 40 MEMBERS LOCATED AROUND SOMALIA, committed to climate and environmental justice, with a mission to build community resilience adaptable to climatic shocks. ITS DOCUMENTED WORK IS THE USEFUL PART: SOGPA ran a TWO-DAY POLICY DIALOGUE AND TRAINING on the BLUE ECONOMY AND THE IMPACTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE ON SOMALIA'S COASTAL COMMUNITIES in Mogadishu (28-29 October 2025), JOINTLY WITH AN ENVIRONMENTAL-LAW ORGANISATION, bringing together government, civil society, private sector, academics, youth, WOMEN LEADERS AND MEMBERS OF COASTAL COMMUNITIES. A national organisation that puts coastal community members in the same room as ministries and lawyers is the convening a village cannot arrange for itself — ask when the next dialogue is and whether your community can send someone. ITS CO-FOUNDER NAMES THE THREATS PLAINLY: deforestation affecting 80 PER CENT OF SOMALIA'S LANDS, the DUMPING OF WASTE AND POISONOUS CHEMICALS ALONG SOMALIA'S COASTLINE, and ILLEGAL FISHING AND POACHING. THE WIDER ROSTER, FROM THE NATIONAL LAND-DEGRADATION CONSULTATIONS: civil-society participants named alongside government ministries, the PARLIAMENTARY COMMITTEE ON ENVIRONMENT AND NATURAL RESOURCES, and TRADITIONAL ELDERS AND RELIGIOUS LEADERS, included CANDLELIGHT, ADO, PENHA, HYDA, HIRDA, HAVOYOCO, IRADA, PARTNER AID, SONYO, SONSAD, the University of Hargeisa, Golis University and the women's group NAGAAD. Traditional elders sitting in the same consultation as ministries and universities is how Somali land questions are actually settled — bring your elders to the table rather than sending a letter without them; the precedent for their presence is already established at national level. WHO IT SUITS: south-central Somali and coastal communities, women's groups, and anyone needing a national organisation outside Somaliland. CAVEATS: ADVOCACY AND CONVENING ORGANISATIONS, NOT FUNDERS OR LAW FIRMS; several of the roster bodies are Somaliland-based. For eighty staff and four offices in Somaliland, Somalia's Candlelight entry; for the bar association and land-dispute routes, SOLLA; for the Balaanbal closure sequence, the community rangeland enclosures entry; for community money, the GEF Small Grants entry.

trackers.name: Somalia's community-level environmental associations by town — MADO in Baidoa, SOCDO in Abudwak, Save the Environment in Garowe, Female Farah in Galdogob, plus Tadamun, Barwaaqo and HAVOYOCO with their registrations
trackers.desc: THE ASSOCIATIONS IN YOUR OWN TOWN — this file's Somali record has named the national bodies; these are the ones below them, with the place each one sits in: SOGPA SERVES AS AN UMBRELLA GROUPING FOR COMMUNITY-LEVEL ASSOCIATIONS WORKING ON ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES, NAMELY THE MA'IB AID AND DEVELOPMENT ORGANIZATION (MADO) IN BAIDOA, SOUTH WEST STATE; THE SOMALI COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT ORGANIZATION (SOCDO) IN ABUDWAK, GALMUDUG; SAVE THE ENVIRONMENT IN GAROWE, PUNTLAND; AND THE FEMALE FARAH FOUNDATION IN GALDOGOB, PUNTLAND. Four named associations in four named towns across three federal member states is the map a Somali villager needs — write to the one in your state, and if none is listed, ask the umbrella to name one nearer you. AND THE COORDINATOR SAYS PLAINLY WHAT THEY NEED, WHICH IS ALSO WHAT TO ASK A FUNDER FOR ON THEIR BEHALF: THESE ORGANISATIONS NEED SUPPORT IN ORGANISATIONAL CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT, HELP WITH OPERATIONAL COST, AND FUNDING FOR CLIMATE CHANGE AND ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION PROGRAMMES, AS WELL AS ENVIRONMENTAL SCHEMES THAT HELP CREATE JOB OPPORTUNITIES FOR SOMALI YOUTH. Operational cost is the honest ask most grant applications are not allowed to make. When a funder asks what a Somali community organisation needs, that sentence is the answer. THREE MORE WITH THEIR REGISTRATIONS, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THEM VERIFIABLE: TADAMUN SOCIAL SOCIETY (TASS, tadamun.so), BASED IN BOSASO, BARI REGION, ESTABLISHED 1992, REGISTERED IN PUNTLAND AND CLOSELY COLLABORATING WITH LINE MINISTRIES to provide inclusive services to communities; BARWAAQO VOLUNTARY ORGANIZATION, HARGEISA, FOUNDED 1996 BY A COMMITTED GENDER-BALANCED GROUP AND REGISTERED AT THE MINISTRY OF NATIONAL PLANNING OF SOMALILAND, whose mission is to work closely with local communities, particularly women and children, TO ENSURE POSITIVE SOCIO-ECONOMIC CHANGE AND SUSTAINABLE NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, active in HARGEISA, BURAO, BERBERA AND BORAMA; and HORN OF AFRICA VOLUNTARY YOUTH COMMITTEE (HAVOYOCO, havoyoco.org), FOUNDED 23 AUGUST 1992 IN HARGEISA, with country programmes in SOMALILAND AND THE SOMALI REGION OF ETHIOPIA and a published address and phone at Badda Cas, Jigjiga Yar, Hargeisa — whose recorded works include CONSTRUCTED ANIMAL TROUGHS IN DROUGHT-AFFECTED AREAS and STRATEGIC WATER POINTS WITH SOLAR SYSTEMS IN THE SANAAG REGION. Ask which ministry an organisation is registered with before you rely on it — Somaliland's is the Ministry of National Planning, Puntland registers separately. And an organisation that has built water points in your region has plant, staff and a route in that a paper partner does not. ALSO NAMED: SOMRAR, Hargeisa, REGISTERED AT THE MINISTRY OF NATIONAL PLANNING AND DEVELOPMENT IN SOMALILAND, FOUNDED 15 APRIL 2018, whose listed programme areas include ENVIRONMENT PROTECTION alongside livestock improvement and IDP protection; and CANDLELIGHT, Shacab Street, Hargeisa. Environment listed alongside livestock and displacement is the honest shape of Somali organisations — do not discount a body because environment is fourth on its list; in a drought economy those are the same problem. WHO IT SUITS: Somali communities in Baidoa, Abudwak, Garowe, Galdogob, Bosaso, Burao, Berbera, Borama or Sanaag. CAVEATS: SMALL ASSOCIATIONS, donor-dependent, several with capacity gaps they state themselves. For the Mogadishu umbrella and the national roster, Somalia's SOGPA entry; for eighty staff and four offices, Candlelight; for the bar association and land-dispute routes, SOLLA; for the Balaanbal enclosure sequence, the rangeland enclosures entry.

trackers.name: What it costs to register an NGO in each Somali administration, the Somalia NGO Consortium's monthly meetings, and two Somali environmental organisations with their own sites
trackers.desc: WHAT IT COSTS TO REGISTER, AND WHO ELSE IS IN THE ROOM — the prices first, because nothing in this file's Somali record has stated them: SOMALILAND CHARGES $110 FOR INITIAL REGISTRATION AND $60 ANNUALLY FOR RENEWAL; PUNTLAND CHARGES $200 INITIAL AND $100 ANNUAL; FEES IN GALMUDUG AND SOUTH-WEST STATE ARE NOT PUBLICLY SPECIFIED. Registration is an annual bill, not a one-off. Budget the renewal from year one — an association that lapses because nobody paid sixty dollars loses the standing it spent years building. And where the fee is not published, ask in writing what it is before you pay anything. AND THE TAX POSITION, WHICH DECIDES WHETHER FUNDERS CAN REACH YOU: SOMALILAND'S INLAND REVENUE LAW NO. 72/2016 DOES NOT PROVIDE A GENERAL EXEMPTION FOR NGOs — EXEMPTIONS MUST BE REQUESTED ON A CASE-BY-CASE BASIS — AND PUNTLAND'S INCOME TAX LEGISLATION SIMILARLY LACKS A STANDING CHARITABLE EXEMPTION. A PENDING FEDERAL INCOME TAX BILL WOULD CREATE A FRAMEWORK FOR EXEMPTING CHARITABLE AND NOT-FOR-PROFIT ORGANISATIONS BUT HAS NOT BEEN ENACTED. THE ABSENCE OF A STANDARDISED PUBLIC BENEFIT STATUS ALSO AFFECTS DONOR CONFIDENCE, AS INTERNATIONAL FUNDERS OFTEN REQUIRE PROOF OF TAX-EXEMPT STATUS FOR COMPLIANCE WITH THEIR OWN REGULATIONS. This is the practical reason a Somali community group gets turned down by a foreign funder, and it has nothing to do with the merits of the case. Apply for the case-by-case exemption early and keep the paper — it is the document the funder's compliance officer will ask for. THE UMBRELLA, AND ITS CALENDAR: THE SOMALIA NGO CONSORTIUM CONTINUES TO FACILITATE COORDINATION BETWEEN CSOs, GOVERNMENT ACTORS AND INTERNATIONAL DONORS, AND RUNS MONTHLY CONSORTIUM MEETINGS — INCLUDING A PUNTLAND MEETING — ALONGSIDE AN ANNUAL POST-BUDGET BRIEFING CONFERENCE AND A ROUND TABLE FORUM FOR NGO CHIEF EXECUTIVES, BOARD MEMBERS AND DIRECTORS. A monthly meeting with a published calendar is the cheapest access in this entry. Government actors and donors are in the same room; a community organisation that attends is in front of both without arranging a single appointment. Note also that the round table is for BOARD members — send a trustee, not only staff. TWO SOMALI ENVIRONMENTAL ORGANISATIONS WITH THEIR OWN SITES: NATURE SOMALIA (naturesomalia.org) PROTECTS AND RESTORES BIRD HABITATS BY PLANTING NATIVE TREES, RESTORES DEGRADED LANDS AND COMBATS DESERTIFICATION IN PUNTLAND, JUBALAND AND SOUTH CENTRAL SOMALIA, AND SUPPORTS WATER CONSERVATION THROUGH RAINWATER HARVESTING SYSTEMS, TRADITIONAL WELL RESTORATION AND SMART WATER USE, running school and community eco-clubs and hands-on workshops. Traditional well restoration sits in the same programme as habitat work. In a rangeland dispute the well is the asset everyone agrees matters — an organisation that restores wells can enter a community on that footing and stay for the land question. SEDO (sedosomalia.org) WAS FOUNDED IN 2010 BY A GROUP OF SOMALIS WHO HAD ALREADY BEEN INVOLVED IN ENVIRONMENTAL CONSERVATION AND COMMUNITY SERVICE AT VARIOUS LEVELS PRIOR TO OFFICIAL REGISTRATION, WHO UNIFIED THEIR HUMAN RESOURCES TO FORM AN ENVIRONMENT-FOCUSED ORGANISATION, and has hosted AN AGRICULTURAL MARKET DEMONSTRATION EVENT IN GAROWE FOR FARMER COOPERATIVES IN THE NUGAL REGION, PUNTLAND, works anti-plastic campaigns, and TRAINS AND EMPOWERS WOMEN AND ENSURES THEIR INVOLVEMENT IN THE SOCIAL, ECONOMIC AND POLITICAL LIFE OF THE COMMUNITY. Registration followed the work, not the other way round. That is the pattern this file keeps recording: people already doing it constitute themselves once there is something to protect. AND THE NUMBERS A RANGELAND COMMUNITY CAN CITE: published assessments cover A COMMUNITY-LED GRAZING LAND MANAGEMENT MODEL FOR THE DHAROOR VALLEY IN PUNTLAND, AND THE ECONOMIC IMPACT OF LAND DEGRADATION IN THE BALIGUBADLE AND BOOKH RANGELANDS IN SOMALILAND — with the stated aim of strengthening research and government institutions SO LOCAL DECISION MAKERS CAN DRAW UPON RECOMMENDATIONS BASED ON SOUND ECONOMIC EVIDENCE. An economic valuation of what degradation costs, done for your own named rangeland, converts a grazing argument into a money argument. Ask whether one exists for your valley before you go to the authority. WHO IT SUITS: Somali and Somaliland groups registering or renewing, rangeland communities, and anyone needing donor-facing paperwork. CAVEATS: FEES AND TAX RULES CHANGE AND DIFFER BY ADMINISTRATION — confirm locally before paying. For eighty staff and four offices, Somalia's Candlelight entry; for the bar association and land-dispute routes, SOLLA; for the enclosure sequence, the community rangeland enclosures entry; for member organisations by town, the community-level environmental associations entry.

trackers.name: Somaliland's climate justice training numbers with the University of Hargeisa, the Somaliland Biodiversity Foundation, and the mobile schools, camel library and 6,300 metres of soil bands that reach pastoralists
trackers.desc: A CAMEL LIBRARY AND SIX THOUSAND METRES OF SOIL BANDS — because in a pastoral landscape the question is always how anything reaches people who move: PRIMARY EDUCATION IS PROVIDED FOR PASTORALIST CHILDREN THROUGH MOBILE SCHOOLS, A CAMEL LIBRARY AND AN AUDIO RADIO TEACHING PROGRAM. A library carried by camel and lessons by radio. If your community is mobile, the delivery method is the whole problem, and these three are the tested answers — ask which organisation runs them in your region before designing anything new. THE TRAINING NUMBERS, FROM A COLLABORATION BETWEEN AN AFRICAN CLIMATE JUSTICE PROGRAMME, A LOCAL ENVIRONMENTAL ORGANISATION AND THE UNIVERSITY OF HARGEISA: OVER 1,088 INDIVIDUALS — 67% OF THEM WOMEN — WERE EMPOWERED THROUGH TRAINING AND WORKSHOPS FOCUSING ON CLIMATE ACTION, WITH GENDER-TRANSFORMATIVE INTERVENTIONS A KEY PRIORITY; A CLIMATE JUSTICE INCUBATOR GRADUATED OVER 120 STUDENTS; AN AMBASSADOR PROGRAMME MOBILISED OVER 250 YOUTH CLIMATE ACTIVISTS WITH 135 TRAINED AMBASSADORS AND A TARGET OF 500; AND 20 STUDENTS FROM THE UNIVERSITY RECEIVED CLIMATE JUSTICE TRAINING AND SUBSEQUENTLY LED INITIATIVES IN FOUR DISTRICTS. Sixty-seven per cent women, in a programme reported by its own partners. And note the last figure: twenty trained students went out and led initiatives in four districts. Twenty people is a number any community can imagine reaching — the university is the place they came from, so ask the nearest one whether it runs anything similar and whether your district is covered. THE UNIVERSITY IS THE PARTNER, WHICH IS THE STRUCTURAL POINT: a local environmental organisation and a national university running a climate justice programme together, with a children's book launched in Somali. A book in the language the children actually speak. This file records repeatedly that materials arrive in a language the community does not read — here somebody wrote one that they do. THE FOUNDATION AND THE PERSON TO WRITE TO: A SOMALILAND BIODIVERSITY FOUNDATION HAS A NAMED PRESIDENT WHO IS ALSO CHAIR OF A SOMALILAND ENVIRONMENT, EDUCATION AND HEALTH ORGANISATION, LECTURES ON ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCE AT THE UNIVERSITY OF HARGEISA, AND IS THE AUTHOR OF SEVERAL BOOKS INCLUDING ONE OF SELECTED ESSAYS ON THE SOMALI ENVIRONMENT. One person holding a foundation, a chairmanship and a university lectureship is how expertise concentrates in a small system. That is a strength and a fragility at once — useful because a single letter reaches all three, risky because the institutions depend on the individual. Ask the foundation who else can answer. THE FIELD WORK, WITH THE MEASUREMENTS PUBLISHED — AND THIS IS THE MOST DIRECTLY COPYABLE THING IN THE ENTRY: 6,300 LINEAR METRES OF SOIL BANDS WERE CONSTRUCTED IN DEGRADED RANGELAND AT A NAMED PASTORAL VILLAGE, CRESCENT SHAPED, WITH A STANDARD MEASUREMENT OF 80 CENTIMETRES IN HEIGHT BY 1 METRE AT THE BASE, IN VARIABLE LENGTHS FROM 30 METRES UPWARDS. Crescent-shaped, 80cm high, 1m at the base, 30m and up. Those are build instructions, not a description. A community with hand tools and labour can construct soil bands to that specification on its own degraded ground without waiting for a project — and 6,300 metres is what one programme achieved, so the scale is achievable. AND THE MONITORING THAT FOLLOWED: 100 FARMERS TRAINED ON BEST FARMING PRACTICES AND GIVEN TILLAGE HOURS, HAND TOOLS AND SEEDS ACROSS THREE NAMED VILLAGES WERE THEN MONITORED TO ASSESS PRODUCTION STATUS. TILLAGE HOURS as an input alongside tools and seed — paid tractor time, counted in hours. That is a specific ask a farming community can make of a programme, and it is easier to account for than equipment. ONE MORE ORGANISATION: A GREEN SOMALI INITIATIVE, FOUNDED IN 2015, WORKS ON REFORESTATION, WASTE MANAGEMENT, CLEAN WATER ACCESS AND SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE ACROSS MULTIPLE REGIONS — INCLUDING TRAINING FARMERS IN CLIMATE-RESILIENT TECHNIQUES AND ESTABLISHING COMMUNITY SEED BANKS. Community seed banks are the quiet insurance: a community that holds its own seed does not have to buy it back after a drought, and it is the cheapest thing on this list to start. WHO IT SUITS: Somali and Somaliland pastoral and farming communities, and anyone needing to reach mobile populations or restore rangeland. CAVEATS: MOST OF THIS IS SOMALILAND-FOCUSED and programme figures come from the implementers — confirm current activity. For the organisation with eighty staff and four offices, Somalia's Candlelight entry; for the bar association whose members take land disputes, SOLLA; for community rangeland enclosures and grazing reserves, the Balaanbal entry; for 40+ members across Somalia, the Somali Greenpeace Association entry; for what registration costs in each administration, the registration entry.

trackers.name: Public Lab — free open-source designs for the equipment that proves contamination — water sensors buildable for under $100, a heavy-metals tester, smartphone spectrometers, and balloon-and-kite aerial mapping instead of a drone
trackers.desc: A WATER SENSOR YOU CAN BUILD FOR UNDER A HUNDRED DOLLARS — THE PROBLEM IT EXISTS TO SOLVE, STATED PLAINLY: MOST WATER QUALITY MONITORING USES EXPENSIVE, PROPRIETARY TECHNOLOGY, LIMITING THE ACCESSIBILITY OF WATER QUALITY DATA — SO INEXPENSIVE, OPEN-SOURCE APPROACHES COULD ENABLE GROUPS RANGING FROM WATERSHED MANAGERS TO HOMEOWNERS TO MORE EASILY COLLECT AND SHARE IT. The reason your community has no evidence of what the mine is putting in the river is usually that testing costs more than anyone has. This file has recorded that gap from the Niger Delta to the Copperbelt: the pollution is visible, the proof is unaffordable. THE PRICE, WHICH IS THE FIND: OPEN SOURCE WATER QUALITY SENSORS DEVELOPED FOR LESS THAN $100 AND TESTED — OPEN HARDWARE ALTERNATIVES, SENSORS THAT YOU CAN BUILD AT HOME AND USE TO MEASURE TRENDS AND DEVIATIONS FROM THEM IN TEMPERATURE, CONDUCTIVITY AND WATER DEPTH, TO ASSESS INDUSTRIAL POLLUTION, COLIFORM BACTERIA, ROAD SALT AND AGRICULTURAL RUNOFF IN WATERWAYS. MEASURE TRENDS AND DEVIATIONS FROM THEM is the useful framing. You do not need a laboratory-grade absolute number to make an argument — you need a year of your own readings showing the river changed when the plant opened. That is achievable with equipment your own people build. THE HEAVIER TESTS: INEXPENSIVE, SMARTPHONE-COMPATIBLE MINISPECTROMETERS TO DETECT WATER POLLUTION; A DIY SPECTROMETRY KIT; AND A DIY POTENTIOSTAT TO TEST FOR HEAVY METALS IN WATER. HEAVY METALS is the test that matters where there is mining, and it is normally the most expensive thing a community can be asked to pay for. An open design for the instrument changes what a village can prove about its own water. THE AERIAL MAPPING, WHICH NEEDS NO DRONE AND NO PERMIT: LOW-ALTITUDE AERIAL MAPPING WITH BALLOONS AND KITES, ALONG WITH SOFTWARE TO KNIT TOGETHER THE IMAGES — PLUS DIY INFRARED CAMERAS. A kite and a camera. Where drones are restricted, seized or unaffordable — which is most of the countries in this file — a kite gets you an overhead photograph of the clearing, the spill or the encroachment, dated and yours. And an infrared camera shows stressed vegetation that looks normal to the eye. WHAT THE ORGANISATION IS: A COMMUNITY OF THOUSANDS OF RESEARCHERS, SCIENTISTS, EDUCATORS AND MAKERS FOCUSED ON CIVIC SCIENCE, CREATING OPEN SOURCE HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE, RUNNING WORKSHOPS AND FOSTERING DIY SCIENTIFIC ENGAGEMENT IN ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE ISSUES — DEVOTED TO EMPOWERING COMMUNITIES AND CITIZEN SCIENTISTS TO MONITOR THEIR OWN ENVIRONMENTS THROUGH THE USE OF INEXPENSIVE DIY TECHNIQUES. IT WAS FORMED IN THE AFTERMATH OF A MAJOR OIL DISASTER TO PROMOTE OPEN SOURCE SCIENCE AND COLLABORATION. Founded after an oil disaster by people who could not get the official data. That origin is the same as most of the organisations worth knowing in this file. THE CATALOGUE IS PUBLISHED: AN OPEN SOURCE TOOLKIT CATALOG RANGING FROM WATER QUALITY SENSORS TO INDOOR AIR QUALITY AND KITE MAPPING KITS, WITH A FULL TOOL ARCHIVE ONLINE — PLUS A BROAD RANGE OF OPEN SOURCE WATER QUALITY DEVICES AND INSTRUCTIONS, RESEARCH NOTES AND WIKIS. RESEARCH NOTES means other people's attempts, including the failures. Read what went wrong for someone else before building. THE SOFTWARE, AND IT WORKS WITHOUT A CONNECTION: FREE, OPEN-SOURCE SOFTWARE ACCESSIBLE OFFLINE FOR DOWNLOADING THE SENSOR DATA TO A LAPTOP, PLUS AN OPEN ONLINE PLATFORM ONTO WHICH CITIZEN SCIENTISTS CAN UPLOAD AND SHARE THE DATA. THE OFFER TO COMMUNITIES, WHICH IS UNUSUAL: THEY OFFER TO HELP COMMUNITY MEMBERS DEVELOP DIY KITS THAT CAN ULTIMATELY BE SOLD AND DISTRIBUTED — AND THEY HOLD WORKSHOPS AROUND THE WORLD SO THAT OTHER PEOPLE CAN CONNECT WITH WHAT A BIG, OPEN COMMUNITY HAS TO OFFER, WITH A NAMED OPEN HARDWARE COMMUNITY MANAGER WHOSE JOB IS REACHING OUT TO PEOPLE WHO MIGHT BE INTERESTED IN BUILDING, LEARNING OR EXPLORING WITH DIY ENVIRONMENTAL TOOLS. They will help you turn a kit into something your group can sell. That makes the monitoring pay for itself rather than depending on the next grant — and there is a named person whose job is answering people who write in. THE ORGANISING IDEA WORTH COPYING: STRATEGIES FOR DEVELOPING COMMUNITY SUPPORT INCLUDING TOOL LIBRARIES THAT INCLUDE WATER QUALITY MONITORING TOOLS. One set of instruments shared across a district by a lending library, rather than every village buying its own. That is how a small budget covers a whole valley. AND THE DIFFICULTIES THEY NAME THEMSELVES, WHICH ARE WORTH PLANNING FOR: MAP LITERACY, ACCESS TO DIGITAL TOOLS, TIME AVAILABLE FOR THE MAPMAKING EXPERIENCE, AND STORYTELLING WITH THE MAP. TIME AVAILABLE is the one that kills these projects. People with fields to work cannot monitor daily — so design the schedule around what your members can actually sustain, weekly rather than daily, and decide who is responsible before the equipment arrives. WHO IT SUITS: African communities near a mine, refinery, plantation or waste site who need their own measurements and cannot pay a laboratory. CAVEATS: DIY READINGS SUPPORT AN ARGUMENT BUT MAY NOT ALONE SATISFY A COURT — pair them with an expert who can vouch for the method. For scientists who critique impact assessments free, Nigeria's ELAW entry; for the free system storing photographs and sketches as land evidence, Comoros' entry; for making phone footage court-ready, Niger's video-as-evidence entry.

trackers.name: Conservation grants an individual can hold with no organisation behind them — a four-stage ladder from roughly £7,000 upward, applications accepted at any time, field and living costs covered, and a published three-referee rule
trackers.desc: A GRANT AN INDIVIDUAL CAN HOLD, WITH NO ORGANISATION BEHIND THEM — note recorded first: A DIFFERENT SMALL-GRANTS PROGRAMME IS ALREADY FILED IN THIS BUCKET WITH DIFFERENT RULES. THIS IS A SEPARATE FUNDER, CROSS-REFERENCED BELOW RATHER THAN RESTATED. WHO CAN RECEIVE IT, AND THIS IS THE FIND: THE GRANT CAN BE GIVEN TO INDIVIDUALS OR SMALL ORGANISATIONS — AND THERE ARE NO RESTRICTIONS BY NATIONALITY OR COUNTRY OF RESIDENCE, PROVIDED THE PROJECT ITSELF IS IN AN ELIGIBLE COUNTRY. An individual. No registration, no bank account in an organisation's name, no board. This file has recorded registration as the gate that shuts most funders to a village committee; here one person with a project can hold the money. For a community whose association is unregistered or was refused, that is a route that does not depend on fixing the legal status first. THE LADDER AND THE AMOUNTS, RECORDED HONESTLY BECAUSE THE PUBLISHED FIGURES DISAGREE: FOUR STAGES — A FIRST GRANT, A SECOND GRANT, A BOOSTER GRANT AND A COMPLETION GRANT. ONE PAGE GIVES UP TO £7,000 AT STAGE 1 AND UP TO £8,000 AT STAGE 2; ANOTHER GIVES A RANGE OF £7,000 TO £18,000 ACROSS THE FOUR; AN EARLIER GUIDELINE GIVES £5,000, £5,000, £10,000 AND £15,000. THE AMOUNTS HAVE RISEN OVER TIME — CHECK THE CURRENT PAGE RATHER THAN ANY OF THESE. The shape matters more than the figure: a small first grant that becomes a larger one if you deliver. Most funders in this file give once; this is a relationship that grows, and the first application is the cheapest one to win. THE TIMING RULES, WHICH ARE UNUSUALLY FORGIVING: APPLICATIONS CAN BE SUBMITTED AT ANY TIME — NO WINDOW, NO DEADLINE. YOU CAN ONLY MAKE ONE FUNDING APPLICATION IN ANY 12-MONTH PERIOD; THE REVIEW CAN TAKE UP TO 6 MONTHS; AND EACH FOLLOW-UP MUST BE AT LEAST 12 MONTHS AFTER THE PREVIOUS PAYMENT. NO DEADLINE is rare across this whole file. But SIX MONTHS to decide means this is not emergency money — apply while things are calm, not when the bulldozers arrive. THE CONDITION FOR MOVING UP THE LADDER: YOU MUST HAVE SUBMITTED INTERIM REPORTS AND A FINAL REPORT ON THE PREVIOUS GRANT BEFORE APPLYING FOR THE NEXT — AND COPIES OF YOUR UPDATES AND FINAL REPORT WILL BE POSTED ON YOUR OWN WEBPAGE. They publish your reports on a page in your name. That page becomes a public record of work done, with a funder's name attached — which is a credential a community organiser can point every later funder at, and it costs nothing extra to acquire. THE REFERENCE RULE, SPELLED OUT SO YOU CAN LINE PEOPLE UP IN ADVANCE: THREE REFERENCES, AT LEAST ONE NOT USED FOR THE PREVIOUS GRANT. IDEALLY CHOOSE PEOPLE YOU HAVE MET IN PERSON. ONE MUST BE BASED AT A WELL-ESTABLISHED INSTITUTION SUCH AS A MAJOR CONSERVATION NGO, UNIVERSITY OR GOVERNMENT BODY; ONE MUST BE FROM THE COUNTRY WHERE YOU WILL BE WORKING AND ONE FROM OUTSIDE THAT COUNTRY; AND NOT MORE THAN ONE PERSON FROM THE SAME INSTITUTION. One referee from outside your country is the hard one, and it is the reason to build the relationships in this file before you need them — a coalition you joined, a school you attended, a mapping network you contributed to. Any of those produces the foreign referee this form requires. WHAT THE MONEY MAY COVER, WHICH IS THE PART THAT SUITS FIELD WORK: THEY GENERALLY DO NOT FUND SALARIES, BUT WILL CONSIDER SUBSISTENCE, TRAVEL AND ACCOMMODATION AS YOU DELIVER THE PROJECT, INCLUDING FIELD AND LIVING COSTS — AND ESSENTIAL PAYMENTS TO INDIVIDUALS SUCH AS DRIVERS, PORTERS OR GUIDES WHO MIGHT ASSIST. PUBLICATION COSTS ARE NOT GENERALLY COVERED. DRIVERS, PORTERS OR GUIDES paid as project costs. That is money reaching people in the community rather than only the person holding the grant — and living costs while you do the work is the closest thing to a stipend most conservation funders offer. THE PROPORTION: IDEALLY THEY PROVIDE BETWEEN 50 AND 100% OF THE COSTS; WHERE THEY ARE NOT THE ONLY FUNDER, EVIDENCE OF CO-FUNDING IS REQUIRED, AND APPLICANTS ARE ENCOURAGED TO SEEK OTHER SOURCES. Up to 100%. No co-financing requirement unless you already have another funder — which this file has recorded as the condition that disqualifies poor applicants elsewhere. WHAT THEY WILL NOT FUND: ACTIVITIES IN DEVELOPED NATIONS, OR PURE RESEARCH WITHOUT CONSERVATION BENEFITS — PROJECTS MUST FOCUS ON BIODIVERSITY CONSERVATION AND HAVE MEASURABLE LONG-TERM IMPACTS, AND THE FOUNDATION PREFERS PROJECTS THAT ARE PRAGMATIC AND THAT HAVE A SIGNIFICANT HUMAN ELEMENT. A SIGNIFICANT HUMAN ELEMENT, stated as a preference. A community protecting a forest it depends on fits better here than a pure species survey. THE CAREER GATE, STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE IT IS REAL: APPLICANTS SHOULD BE IN THE EARLY STAGES OF THEIR CONSERVATION CAREERS, WITH PRIORITY TO THOSE UNDERTAKING A POSTGRADUATE DEGREE OR WHO GRADUATED IN THE PAST 3 YEARS; APPLICATIONS FROM OTHERS ARE CONSIDERED IF THEY FIT THE GENERAL CRITERIA, BUT UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS ARE NOT FUNDED — AND FOR FOLLOW-UP GRANTS THESE CRITERIA MATTER LESS. The postgraduate priority is the real limit, and it is worth naming: this suits the young graduate from your district more than the elders' committee. Pair them — the graduate holds the grant, the community directs the work — and read the criteria as a reason to find that person rather than to give up. THE LANGUAGE AND THE ACCOUNT: APPLICATIONS ARE ONLY ACCEPTED ONLINE, THE APPLICATION AND REFERENCES MUST BE IN ENGLISH, AND YOU MUST FIRST CREATE A USER ACCOUNT WITH A VALID EMAIL ADDRESS. AND THE SCALE: OVER £30 MILLION AWARDED THROUGH MORE THAN 5,100 GRANTS IN OVER 150 COUNTRIES, FUNDING PILOT PROJECTS THAT OFTEN FORM THE CORNERSTONE OF FUTURE LARGE-SCALE INITIATIVES. WHO IT SUITS: individual African conservationists and small groups — especially a recent graduate working with a community that has no registered organisation. CAVEATS: ENGLISH-ONLY, ONLINE-ONLY, A SIX-MONTH REVIEW AND A POSTGRADUATE PRIORITY — not an option for an unlettered committee acting alone. For the other small-grants window already filed here, Somalia's GEF entry; for the fund that waives registration, bank account and ID, the Central African Republic's entry; for the cash award addressed to the village group itself, Egypt's entry.

trackers.name: Tropenbos International — a forest network whose African country members are their own legal national entities rather than branch offices — with the international office acting as secretariat that fundraises for them, and a named programme lobbying for tree tenure reform
trackers.desc: THE COUNTRY MEMBER IS ITS OWN LEGAL ENTITY, NOT A BRANCH OFFICE — adjacency declared first: A EUROPEAN FOREST-POLICY ORGANISATION IS ALREADY A HOST UNDER THE CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC; THAT HOST IS NOT SHIPPED HERE AND ITS ENTRY IS NOT RESTATED. THE STRUCTURE, AND IT IS THE FIND: A GLOBAL NETWORK OF LOCAL ORGANIZATIONS — AND ONE NAMED AFRICAN MEMBER, ESTABLISHED IN 2001, BECAME A LEGAL NATIONAL ENTITY AND A MEMBER OF THE NETWORK IN 2017. An African country programme that converted itself into a nationally registered organisation and then joined the network as a member. This file has recorded the opposite arrangement everywhere: a foreign organisation opens a country office, employs nationals, and closes it when the grant ends. Here the national body owns itself and can outlive the network — which is the model to ask for when any international organisation proposes working in your country. WHAT THE INTERNATIONAL OFFICE DOES FOR THEM, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: IT IMPLEMENTS ACTIVITIES AT THE INTERNATIONAL LEVEL THAT COMPLEMENT AND SUPPORT THE WORK IN THE NETWORK COUNTRIES, AND IS DESIGNATED AS THE SECRETARIAT PROVIDING SUPPORT SERVICES INCLUDING QUALITY CONTROL, ADMINISTRATIVE PROCESSES, COMMUNICATION, CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT AND FUNDRAISING AT THE INTERNATIONAL LEVEL. FUNDRAISING AT THE INTERNATIONAL LEVEL, on behalf of the national members. That inverts the usual flow this file records, where the international body raises money for itself and subcontracts the work. Ask any prospective partner which way round theirs runs. THE AFRICAN IMPLEMENTING PARTNERS, NAMED BY TYPE: IN BOLIVIA, ETHIOPIA AND UGANDA THE PROGRAMME IS IMPLEMENTED BY A BOLIVIAN FOREST RESEARCH INSTITUTE, A PASTORAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL NETWORK IN THE HORN OF AFRICA, AND AN ECOLOGICAL TRENDS ALLIANCE RESPECTIVELY. A PASTORAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL NETWORK IN THE HORN OF AFRICA runs the programme in its region. For Horn communities, that is a regional organisation of their own kind holding the contract, not a forestry institute flown in. THE COUNTRY PROGRAMMES AND THE WIDER PROJECT COUNTRIES: PROGRAMMES IN COLOMBIA, THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO, GHANA, INDONESIA, SURINAME AND VIET NAM — AND UNDER A GREEN LIVELIHOODS ALLIANCE IT PARTICIPATES IN PROJECTS IN BOLIVIA, LIBERIA, NIGERIA, UGANDA AND THE PHILIPPINES. THE AFRICAN MEMBER'S FOUR OBJECTIVES, WHICH ARE THIS FILE'S SUBJECTS ALMOST WORD FOR WORD: ACTIVELY ENGAGE LOCAL COMMUNITIES WITH THE GOVERNMENT AND THE PRIVATE SECTOR ON NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT; IMPROVE ENFORCEMENT AND MONITORING OF FORESTRY, MINING AND LOGGING LAWS AND REDUCTION OF ILLEGAL PRACTICES; STRENGTHEN NON-STATE ACTORS TO IMPROVE FOREST GOVERNANCE AND FOREST-CARBON PROCESSES; AND, TOGETHER WITH CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, LOBBY GOVERNMENT AND DEVELOP MULTI-STAKEHOLDER DIALOGUES ON TREE TENURE REFORMS. TREE TENURE, named as its own reform target. In much of West Africa a farmer owns the land but the state owns the timber on it — which is why a community watches a logging company fell trees it planted and can do nothing. Separating land tenure from tree tenure in your own demands is the difference between a claim that half-works and one that does. ITS MISSION AND METHOD: TO GENERATE, COMMUNICATE AND ADVOCATE THE APPLICATION OF INFORMATION THAT OPTIMIZES FOREST BENEFITS THROUGH PARTICIPATORY AND COLLABORATIVE APPROACHES — THROUGH RESEARCH, CAPACITY BUILDING FOR INDIVIDUALS, COMMUNITIES, INSTITUTIONS AND RELEVANT STAKEHOLDERS, AND THE PROVISION OF PLATFORMS FOR INFORMED DIALOGUES. ITS GOAL, STATED IN TERMS THAT INCLUDE CONFLICT: TO ENSURE FOREST SECTOR ACTORS APPLY SOUND INFORMATION FOR POVERTY REDUCTION POLICIES, IMPLEMENT ACTIVITIES THAT INCREASE FOREST COVER, PROMOTE CLIMATE-RESILIENT PRACTICES, AND REDUCE CONFLICTS ASSOCIATED WITH FOREST MANAGEMENT AND ECOSYSTEM SERVICES. THE NETWORK'S FOCUS AREAS: INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES SUSTAINABLY MANAGING FORESTS BASED ON THEIR OWN EXPERIENCES, NEEDS AND PRIORITIES; LOCALLY-LED RESTORATION OF DEGRADED LANDS PROVIDING ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES; SMALLHOLDERS GROWING A VARIETY OF TREES AND CROPS; COMMUNITIES WORKING WITH OTHER LANDSCAPE ACTORS TO REDUCE WILDFIRE RISK; SMALLHOLDERS AND COMMUNITY-BASED ENTERPRISES HAVING ACCESS TO FINANCE AND MARKETS; AND WOMEN AND YOUNG PEOPLE PLAYING A LEADING ROLE. LOCALLY-LED RESTORATION PROVIDING ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES is the answer to a restoration project that arrives as unpaid labour on somebody else's carbon scheme. THE FINANCE PROGRAMME AND EXACTLY WHO IT IS FOR: A GREEN FINANCE PROGRAMME BRIDGING THE GAP BETWEEN INTERNATIONAL FINANCE AND LOCAL ENTREPRENEURS WITH IDEAS FOR SUSTAINABLE BUSINESSES — ITS LOCAL STAKEHOLDERS BEING SMALL AND MEDIUM-SIZED ENTERPRISES, COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS, COOPERATIVES, SMALLHOLDER FOREST AND FARM PRODUCERS AND THEIR ORGANISATIONS, AND INDIGENOUS PEOPLE AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES. WHAT IT DOES, IN THREE PARTS: STRENGTHENING CAPABILITIES, INCLUDING FINANCIAL LITERACY AND THE CAPACITY TO CONSTRUCT BANKABLE BUSINESS CASE PROPOSALS; FINANCIAL PRODUCTS DEVELOPMENT WITH LOCAL, NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL PROVIDERS TO DEVELOP LOCALLY APPROPRIATE PRODUCTS THAT REDUCE THE PERCEIVED RISKS ASSOCIATED WITH LOANS IN THIS SECTOR; AND KNOWLEDGE MANAGEMENT, DOCUMENTING SUCCESSFUL CASES. THE PERCEIVED RISKS is the honest phrasing: banks refuse forest and farm lending because they think it is risky, not because it is. Work that changes the lender's product rather than lecturing the borrower is rare, and this file's savings-group and cooperative entries are what it connects to. THE EXCHANGE ON RECORD: A LEARNING EXCHANGE ON COCOA BETWEEN TWO AFRICAN COUNTRY MEMBERS. African members teaching each other directly, rather than both reporting to a European office.
