AND THE LANDSCAPE PROBLEM IT NAMES: IN TWO NAMED ADJOINING COCOA LANDSCAPES WITH SOME OF THE COUNTRY'S HIGHEST BIODIVERSITY AND RELATIVELY INTACT HIGH FORESTS ADJACENT TO A NATIONAL PARK AND FOREST RESERVE, EXPANSION OF COCOA FARMS INTO FORESTED LANDS — BOTH WITHIN AND OUTSIDE FOREST RESERVES — HAS BEEN INCREASING IN THE PAST THREE DECADES. BOTH WITHIN AND OUTSIDE FOREST RESERVES. Reserve status alone stopped nothing over thirty years, which is worth knowing before a campaign rests its whole case on getting an area gazetted. WHO IT SUITS: African forest and farming communities and national organisations — especially those wanting a partnership model where the national body is the legal owner of the work. CAVEATS: COUNTRY PROGRAMMES COVER A SHORT LIST OF AFRICAN COUNTRIES AND IT IS A KNOWLEDGE AND DIALOGUE ORGANISATION RATHER THAN A FUNDER OR LAWYER — the structure is as useful to copy as the programmes are to join. For core organisational support in the Congo Basin, DR Congo's entry; for the pan-African food sovereignty alliance, Libya's entry; for participatory mapping of community forest land, DR Congo's MappingForRights entry.

trackers.name: A foundation funding on-the-ground work on threatened trees for up to 3 years, with overheads capped at 10%, regional calls including one for Eastern Africa, and an unpublished threat assessment accepted if you can justify it
trackers.desc: OVERHEADS CAPPED AT TEN PERCENT, AND THEY SAY SO IN ADVANCE — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S SUDAN ENTRY COVERS THE ANIMALS-ONLY FUND THAT EXCLUDES PLANTS, ITS NIGER ENTRY THE SPECIES FUND THAT ACCEPTS PLANTS AND FUNGI FROM INDIVIDUALS, AND ITS CÔTE D'IVOIRE ENTRY THE HOTSPOT FUND WHOSE RECOMMENDATIONS THIS FOUNDATION ASKS PROJECTS TO ALIGN WITH. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE OVERHEAD CAP, WHICH IS THE FIND: INDIRECT COSTS AND OVERHEADS MUST NOT EXCEED 10 PERCENT OF THE TOTAL PROJECT BUDGET. Ninety cents in the dollar has to reach the work. That is a published, checkable limit — and it is the number to put beside any partner's proposed budget, because this file has recorded overheads of a third and more disappearing before anything happens on the ground. A local organisation with low overheads is structurally advantaged here. THE POSTURE IT STATES: THE FOUNDATION PROVIDES FINANCIAL SUPPORT BUT IS NOT INTERESTED IN REMAINING JUST DONORS. Expect involvement, not just money. Whether that is welcome depends on your organisation — ask early what it means in practice. WHAT IT FUNDS AND FOR HOW LONG: PRIMARILY IN SITU CONSERVATION ACTIONS OF GLOBALLY THREATENED TREE SPECIES; PROJECTS MUST IMPLEMENT CONCRETE ON-THE-GROUND CONSERVATION ACTIONS AND CAN SPAN A PERIOD OF UP TO 3 YEARS. IN SITU means the tree where it stands, not a seedling in a nursery. For a community whose forest is due to be cleared, that is the right shape — and three years is longer than most grants in this file. THE SPECIES TEST AND THE OPENING INSIDE IT: ONLY PROJECTS IMPROVING THE CONSERVATION STATUS OF GLOBALLY THREATENED TREE SPECIES LISTED AS VULNERABLE, ENDANGERED OR CRITICALLY ENDANGERED ARE ELIGIBLE, AND APPLICANTS MUST CHECK THE STATUS OF THEIR TARGET SPECIES — BUT IF A SPECIES IS CONSIDERED THREATENED AND THE ASSESSMENT IS NOT YET PUBLISHED, DETAILED ADDITIONAL INFORMATION JUSTIFYING THAT STATUS MUST BE PROVIDED. The unlisted tree is not automatically excluded. A community that knows a tree is down to a handful of stands can make the case with its own evidence — which is the opening for exactly the species nobody has got round to assessing, and this file has recorded that being most of them. THE PREFERENCE FOR GLOBAL OVER LOCAL, WHICH IS THE LIMIT TO READ FIRST: THE FOUNDATION WILL FAVOUR PROJECTS OF GLOBAL RELEVANCE VERSUS PROJECTS PROTECTING SPECIES LOCALLY OR REGIONALLY THREATENED — AND THREATENED TREE SPECIES MUST BE THE MAIN TARGET, THOUGH POSITIVE IMPACT ON OTHER THREATENED SPECIES AND ASSOCIATED HABITATS WILL BE FAVOURED AS COLLATERAL BENEFITS. A tree that is common elsewhere but nearly gone in your district does not qualify. The forest, the water and the community come in as COLLATERAL BENEFITS — real, but written around the species, which is how the proposal has to be built. THE CO-FUNDING RULE: A MINIMUM OF 20 TO 50% CO-FUNDING WILL BE REQUIRED, DEPENDING ON PROJECT SIZE AND REGION — A DIVERSIFIED FUNDING BASIS ENSURES BETTER SUSTAINABILITY, SO CO-FUNDING IS AN IMPORTANT CRITERION, BUT IT IS IMPORTANT TO DOCUMENT THE SPECIFIC IMPACT OF THE FOUNDATION'S OWN CONTRIBUTION. Between a fifth and half from elsewhere. Line up the second funder first — and note that the small species grants filed under Niger and Sudan can be that co-funding, since their ceilings are compatible with a modest tree project. WHO MAY APPLY, AND WHO MAY NOT: ANY ORGANIZATION WITH WELL-ESTABLISHED EXPERTISE AND EFFICIENCY IN PLANT CONSERVATION; INDIVIDUALS ARE NOT ELIGIBLE; AND EACH ORGANIZATION MAY SUBMIT ONLY ONE PROPOSAL UNDER A GIVEN CALL. No individuals, unlike the fund under Niger. A person with the knowledge needs an organisation to apply through — and only one proposal per organisation per call, so choose the strongest site rather than spreading. THE REGIONAL CALLS, INCLUDING AN AFRICAN ONE: CALLS ARE ISSUED BY REGION — ONE FOR EASTERN AFRICA WITH A PUBLISHED MIDNIGHT DEADLINE, AND ANOTHER FOR THE MEDITERRANEAN BASIN — SO THE OPEN CALL DETERMINES WHICH PART OF AFRICA IS ELIGIBLE AT ANY TIME. Eastern Africa and the Mediterranean basin have both had their own calls, which between them cover North Africa and the Horn. Watch the call page rather than assuming your region is out. THE ALIGNMENT IT ASKS FOR: WHERE POSSIBLE, PROJECTS SHOULD SUPPORT EXISTING THREATENED TREE SPECIES CONSERVATION ACTION PLANS, FOREST LANDSCAPE CONSERVATION AND RESTORATION STRATEGIES, RELEVANT RECOMMENDATIONS OF A NAMED HOTSPOT FUND, AND/OR CONSERVATION ACTIONS IN KEY BIODIVERSITY AREAS WHERE TREE SPECIES ARE TRIGGER SPECIES. Aligning with a plan somebody else already wrote makes an application stronger and shorter. Find out whether your area sits in a Key Biodiversity Area and which tree triggered it — that single fact can carry a proposal. THE SELECTION CRITERIA: THE PROJECT IS SCIENTIFICALLY SOUND AND JUSTIFIED, AND IT TACKLES THE DIRECT THREATS TO THE TREE SPECIES — WITH REASONABLE BUDGETS IN RELATION TO PROPOSED ACTIVITIES. DIRECT THREATS. Logging, clearance for a plantation, charcoal, a road — naming the actual threat and acting on it is the criterion, which suits a community that can say precisely what is happening and when. THE REVIEW ROUTE: PROJECTS ARE REVIEWED FIRST BY THE SECRETARIAT AND THEN BY AN EXPERT COMMITTEE, WHICH PROVIDES RECOMMENDATIONS TO THE BOARD. AND THE APPROACH IT ADOPTED, PLUS THE ASSESSMENT IT PAYS FOR: A SPECIES APPROACH RECOGNIZING THAT SPECIES CONSERVATION IS INEVITABLY LINKED TO HABITAT CONSERVATION AND THE PROTECTION OF THE INTERESTS OF HUMAN POPULATIONS DEPENDING ON THEM — AND, TO ENSURE ALL TREE SPECIES ARE ASSIGNED A THREAT CATEGORY, IT SUPPORTS A GLOBAL ASSESSMENT OF ALL 60,000+ TREE SPECIES LED BY A BOTANIC GARDENS BODY AND A GLOBAL TREE SPECIALIST GROUP. EARLIER SUPPORT ALSO COVERED BOTANICAL COLLECTIONS, TAXONOMIC STUDIES, PRODUCTION OF FLORAS, COMPILATION OF LISTS OF THREATENED SPECIES, AND REINTRODUCTION PROGRAMMES. THE INTERESTS OF HUMAN POPULATIONS DEPENDING ON THEM, written into the foundation's own approach. Communities whose food, medicine or building timber comes from a threatened tree are inside the framing, not an add-on to it. And the global assessment is why an unlisted tree may already have been evaluated — check before assuming it has not. WHO IT SUITS: African organisations working where a globally threatened tree still stands — particularly in Eastern Africa, the Horn and the Mediterranean rim. CAVEATS: ORGANISATIONS ONLY, TREES ONLY, GLOBAL RATHER THAN LOCAL THREAT STATUS, 20–50% CO-FUNDING, ONE PROPOSAL PER CALL, AND REGIONAL CALLS THAT OPEN AND CLOSE — for plants and fungi from an individual, Niger's entry; for animal species with no plant eligibility, Sudan's entry.

trackers.name: Wildlife Conservation Network (WCN) — a funder that removes no overhead at all and pays the bank transfer fees itself so partners receive the whole donation — low-bureaucracy grants reaching 80% of African countries, scholarships to US$45,000 for community-based conservationists, and free exhibition space at its donor expo
trackers.desc: NO OVERHEAD, AND THEY PAY THE BANK FEES SO YOU GET ALL OF IT — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S KENYA BUCKET CARRIES A WILDLIFE FOUNDATION HOST AND A RANGELANDS TRUST HOST AND NAME; ITS TANZANIA BUCKET A RAINFOREST TRUST AND A NATURE CONSERVANCY HOST; ITS NIGER ENTRY THE MINING COMMUNITIES MOVEMENT; ITS RWANDA ENTRY THE ANNUAL GATHERING. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. THE OVERHEAD RULE, WHICH IS THE FIND: 100% OF DESIGNATED DONATIONS TO CONSERVATION PARTNERS GO DIRECTLY TO THE FIELD WITH NO OVERHEAD REMOVED, AND 100% OF DONATIONS TO THE FUNDS GO DIRECTLY TO THE FIELD WITH ZERO OVERHEAD REMOVED — THE ORGANISATION NEVER TAKES A FEE OR PERCENTAGE. Set that against the 10% overhead cap this file records one European foundation imposing on its grantees, and against the intermediaries elsewhere in the file that keep a share before the money moves. Zero is the number to hold every other funder against, and it is published rather than claimed in conversation. THE DETAIL UNDERNEATH IT, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: BANK TRANSFER FEES ARE PAID BY THE ORGANISATION ITSELF SO THAT PARTNERS CAN SIMPLY RECEIVE 100% OF THEIR DESIGNATED DONATIONS — AND ON AVERAGE 92% OF ALL MONEY THAT COMES IN GOES STRAIGHT TO THE FIELD, WITH ONLY 8% USED FOR OPERATING EXPENSES, WHICH IT ASKS SUPPORTERS TO COVER SEPARATELY. The transfer fee is the detail nobody warns a small African organisation about. An international wire can lose a meaningful slice of a small grant to correspondent bank charges before it lands, and this funder absorbs that itself. Ask any prospective funder who pays the transfer fee — it is a short question with a revealing answer. THE AFRICAN REACH OF THE FUNDS: COLLECTIVELY THEY HAVE SUPPORTED PROJECTS IN OVER 53 COUNTRIES, INCLUDING 80% OF THE COUNTRIES IN AFRICA — WITH PARTNERS AND PROJECTS IN 69 COUNTRIES AND OVER $475 MILLION RAISED SINCE INCEPTION. 80% of African countries already reached. Whichever country you are in, the probability is that something here has been funded there already, and a previously funded organisation nearby is the introduction worth seeking. HOW THE GRANTS ARE RUN: FLEXIBLE, LOW-BUREAUCRACY GRANTS THAT GET FUNDING TO THE FIELD QUICKLY AND EFFICIENTLY — FROM PILOT PROJECTS TO TIME-TESTED PROGRAMS, TARGETING THE NEEDS ON THE GROUND WITH MINIMAL RED TAPE, AND INVESTING IN EFFECTIVE PROJECTS FROM A WIDE RANGE OF ORGANIZATIONS. PILOT PROJECTS named alongside established programmes. An organisation with an idea and no track record is inside the stated range. THE SCHOLARSHIP, WITH ITS AMOUNTS AND ITS AUDIENCE: IT FUNDS GRADUATE EDUCATION AND APPLIED TRAINING FOR COMMUNITY-BASED CONSERVATIONISTS, PROVIDING TUITION AND LIVING EXPENSES, WITH AWARDS FROM US$5,000 TO US$45,000 — MADE THROUGH A CALL FOR PROPOSALS, WITH STUDENTS FROM AFRICA WELCOME TO APPLY. TUITION AND LIVING EXPENSES, up to forty-five thousand dollars, for a COMMUNITY-BASED conservationist rather than an academic. This file has recorded communities depending permanently on outside technical expertise; funding one of your own people through a degree is how that dependency ends, and this is the largest such award recorded here. THE FREE EXHIBITION SPACE: EXHIBITORS RECEIVE A FREE SPACE TO EXHIBIT AT THE ORGANISATION'S EXPO, WITH EXHIBITOR STATUS GIVEN TO QUALIFIED NONPROFIT ORGANIZATIONS ACTIVE IN WILDLIFE CONSERVATION AND/OR ANIMAL WELFARE — APPLICANTS SUBMIT APPLICATIONS TO REQUEST THAT FREE SPACE. A free stand in front of the donors who fund this whole network. That is direct access to individual givers, which is a different and more durable money supply than institutional grants — and it is applied for, not invited. WHAT PARTNERS RECEIVE BESIDES MONEY: NETWORKING, MEDIA PROMOTION, COACHING IN FUNDRAISING AND DONOR DEVELOPMENT, AND TECHNICAL AND COMPUTER ASSISTANCE — WITH IN-KIND CONTRIBUTIONS FOR NETWORKING AND CAPACITY BUILDING. COACHING IN FUNDRAISING AND DONOR DEVELOPMENT is the part that outlasts the grant, and this file has recorded very few funders offering it by name. WHO IT LOOKS FOR: INDEPENDENT CONSERVATIONISTS WHO LIVE AND WORK IN DEVELOPING COUNTRIES, AND WHO ARE EXPLORING NEW WAYS TO RESOLVE THE CONFLICTS BETWEEN PEOPLE AND WILDLIFE. LIVE AND WORK IN is the qualifying condition, and an individual conservationist rather than an institution is the unit it backs. THE FISCAL-HOST FUNCTION ON RECORD: A NAMED SOUTH AFRICAN ORGANISATION RECORDS THAT THE NETWORK CONTINUES TO SUPPORT ITS WORK BY ACCEPTING DONATIONS ON ITS BEHALF IN THE UNITED STATES FROM THE NETWORK'S SUPPORTERS, AND BY PASSING ON 100% OF THOSE DONATIONS TO IT. It will receive money in the United States on your behalf and forward all of it. For an African organisation that cannot offer American donors a tax receipt — the quiet reason many will not give — that function solves the problem without setting up a foreign entity, and it complements the fiscal sponsor requirement recorded in this file's Libya entry. THE EMERGENCY FUND: AN EMERGENCY RELIEF FUND SUPPORTS CONSERVATIONISTS, WILDLIFE AND COMMUNITIES IN TIMES OF CRISIS — FOR WHEN CRISES GENERATE HEALTH, SOCIAL, ECONOMIC AND POLITICAL CHALLENGES THAT ALSO LEAD TO INCREASED PRESSURE ON WILDLIFE AND NATURAL RESOURCES AND DISRUPTIONS IN FUNDRAISING. DISRUPTIONS IN FUNDRAISING named as a fundable emergency in itself. An organisation whose donor collapsed mid-crisis is describing a situation this fund exists for. THE LOCAL LEADERSHIP PROGRAMME: CREATING A HEALTHY FUTURE FOR WILDLIFE RELIES ON THE LEADERSHIP OF LOCAL PEOPLE WHO ARE SHAPING CONSERVATION IN THEIR HOME COUNTRIES — WITH THE FUNDS ALSO CONNECTING GRANTEES TO EACH OTHER. AND THE ACCOUNTABILITY IT PUBLISHES: IT MAINTAINS THE HIGHEST POSSIBLE RATINGS ON TWO NAMED CHARITY RATING SERVICES AND IS AN ACCREDITED CHARITY WITH A NAMED GIVING ALLIANCE, DESCRIBING ITS MODEL AS A 100% DONATION MODEL WITH A DEEP VETTING PROCESS. DEEP VETTING cuts both ways — recorded plainly: an organisation approaching this network should expect its finances and governance to be examined closely, which is the price of the zero-overhead promise. WHO IT SUITS: African conservationists and community organisations working on wildlife and habitat — including individuals seeking a degree, organisations needing a US donation route, and groups with a pilot idea. CAVEATS: WILDLIFE AND ENDANGERED SPECIES ARE THE FRAME, SO A PURE LAND-RIGHTS OR POLLUTION FIGHT MAY NOT FIT; PARTNERSHIP IS BY VETTING AND INVITATION RATHER THAN OPEN APPLICATION, THOUGH THE SCHOLARSHIP AND EXHIBITOR SPACE ARE APPLIED FOR DIRECTLY. For the fund that waives registration and takes video applications, Libya's entry; for legal aid as a standing grant category, Algeria's entry.

trackers.name: A national collective of six NGOs that builds rural people's own organisations and then helps them access land with water — eight named movements it helped establish, farmers' associations in 200+ villages, and a mobile-phone system built from an audit of how communities actually get news
trackers.desc: THEY BUILD THE ORGANISATION FIRST, THEN GO AFTER LAND WITH WATER — method and adjacency declared first: THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THE SHIPPED HOST, TWO SIBLING HOSTS AND FIVE SUBJECT SPELLINGS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL HOSTS AND FOUR SPELLINGS ABSENT, WITH ONE GENERIC PHRASE APPEARING IN FOUR ENTRIES ON OTHER HOSTS. THIS FILE'S NIGER ENTRY COVERS THE COMMONAGE ACQUISITIONS, ITS RWANDA ENTRY THE 48-COMMUNITY FEDERATION, ITS MALI ENTRY THE FISHERS' CO-OPERATIVE LITIGATION. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES, WHICH IS THE FIND: TO STIMULATE THE BUILDING OF LOCAL ORGANISATIONS AND LOCAL LEADERSHIP AND ASSIST THESE ASSOCIATIONS TO ACCESS LAND AND PRODUCTIVE ASSETS — AND, IN A LATER STATEMENT, TO ACCESS LAND WITH WATER. LAND WITH WATER. Two words that answer the failure recorded in this file's Niger entry, where communities won hectares and then found the farms unusable. An organisation that writes water into the objective is negotiating for something that can actually be lived on. And the sequence matters: the local organisation is built FIRST, and the land claim comes from it. Every fund, court and complaints desk in this file requires a constituted body on the other end; this is the work of creating one before it is needed. THE EIGHT MOVEMENTS IT HAS HELPED ESTABLISH, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: IT HELPS ESTABLISH AND SUPPORT MOVEMENTS AND ASSOCIATIONS OF SMALL-SCALE FARMERS, FISHERS AND LANDLESS PEOPLE — NAMING A LAND RIGHTS MOVEMENT, A FARMERS ASSOCIATION, A FARMERS' ORGANISATION, A RURAL WOMEN'S ASSEMBLY, A COASTAL LINKS ORGANISATION, A SECOND LAND RIGHTS MOVEMENT AND TWO UNEMPLOYED PEOPLE'S MOVEMENTS. Eight named organisations that now exist and did not before. That is the measurable output to ask any capacity-building organisation for: not workshops delivered, but bodies still standing afterwards. THE SCALE OF THE VILLAGE WORK: FARMERS ASSOCIATIONS AND WOMEN'S GROUPS IN MORE THAN 200 VILLAGES, TO ENABLE ACCESS, UTILIZATION AND MANAGEMENT OF LAND FOR FOOD SECURITY AND SUSTAINABLE LIVELIHOODS. HOW IT IS STRUCTURED AND FUNDED: A NATIONAL COLLECTIVE OF SIX NGOs ESTABLISHED IN 1983, WHOSE REGIONAL OPERATIONS HAVE THEIR OWN GOVERNANCE STRUCTURES AND REGIONAL SUPPORT STAFF — WITH FUNDRAISING DONE BOTH BY THE NATIONAL OFFICE AND AT THE REGIONAL LEVEL. Regional affiliates that raise their own money and govern themselves. A national body whose regions can fundraise independently does not collapse when the head office's grant ends — the failure this file has recorded repeatedly. THE PRINCIPLE IT WORKS FROM: ONLY THE CONSCIOUS, ORGANISED ACTIONS OF THE POOR THEMSELVES CAN DRIVE LASTING CHANGE — SUPPORTING A NATIONAL, INDEPENDENT MOVEMENT OF RURAL AND PERI-URBAN COMMUNITIES THAT CAN ARTICULATE THEIR OWN NEEDS, DEFEND THEIR INTERESTS, AND CHALLENGE STRUCTURAL INJUSTICE. HOW IT DECIDES WHAT TO WORK ON: ITS APPROACH SHIFTED TO ORGANISE PEOPLE AROUND ISSUES IDENTIFIED BY THEM AS CRITICAL, HENCE ITS SHIFT TO LAND RIGHTS AND RURAL POVERTY — AFTER RETRAINING AND RE-ORIENTATING ITS STAFF TO WORK IN A WAY THAT EMPHASISED COMMUNITY EMPOWERMENT THROUGH PARTICIPATORY DEVELOPMENT METHODOLOGIES. The organisation changed its own programme because the communities named a different priority, and retrained its staff to do it. Worth asking any NGO offering help: what did you last change because a community told you to. WHO IT COMMITS TO ORGANISING: ALL SECTORS OF THE RURAL AND COASTAL POOR — WOMEN, SMALL SCALE FARMERS, COMMODITY GROUPS, FISHERS, FARM WORKERS AND YOUTH — FOR CONTROL AND OWNERSHIP OF NATURAL RESOURCES, BUILDING A MASS BASED NATIONAL FORMATION WITH STRONG, DEMOCRATIC AND ACCOUNTABLE LEADERSHIP. FISHERS AND FARMERS IN ONE FORMATION. Coastal and inland communities are usually organised separately and lose separately; a named coastal links organisation sitting alongside farmers' associations is the structure that prevents that. WHAT IT SAYS IT IS UP AGAINST: SYSTEMIC DISPOSSESSION, THE SKEWED LAND HOLDING PATTERNS IN THE COUNTRY AND THE DISCONNECTION OF COMMUNITIES FROM THE NATURAL RESOURCES AND COMMONS — AND PATRIARCHY, POLITICAL POWER AND CORPORATE CAPTURE OF THE COMMONS. THE COMMUNICATION AUDIT, WHICH IS UNUSUAL AND PRACTICAL: IT CONDUCTED AN EXTENSIVE COMMUNICATION AUDIT TO UNDERSTAND THE BEST WAY TO COMMUNICATE AND DISTRIBUTE NEWS TO THE COMMUNITIES, AND ESTABLISHED AN ELECTRONIC COMMUNICATION SYSTEM THAT UTILISES THE MOBILE PHONE TO COMMUNICATE CRITICAL INFORMATION. They researched how people actually receive information before building the channel. Most organisations in this file publish a website and assume it reaches the village. An audit first, then a mobile system — that ordering is the transferable part. THE TRANSLATION WORK IT COUNTS AS AN ACHIEVEMENT: DISSEMINATION OF USEFUL INFORMATION THROUGH POPULAR COMMUNITY NEWSLETTERS AS WELL AS SIMPLIFYING GOVERNMENT POLICIES IN A WAY THAT ORDINARY WOMEN AND MEN CAN ENGAGE WITH. SIMPLIFYING GOVERNMENT POLICIES listed as an achievement in its own right. A community cannot object to a policy it cannot read, and this file has recorded consultation periods passing unused for exactly that reason. THE OTHER ACHIEVEMENTS IT LISTS: WELL-INFORMED LEADERS WHO CAN LEAD LOCAL INITIATIVES AND CAMPAIGNS; STRENGTHENED RURAL WOMEN'S VOICE THROUGH A NAMED ASSEMBLY; FACILITATION OF POPULAR RURAL ORGANISATIONS, FARM WORKER UNIONS AND SMALL SCALE FARMERS ASSOCIATIONS; STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIPS WITH ORGANISATIONS WORKING ON LAND AND AGRARIAN REFORM; AND DEVELOPING ALTERNATIVES FOR FOOD PRODUCTION AND LIVELIHOOD. FARM WORKER UNIONS among the things it helped found. Workers living on the land they work are the group with the least security in this file, and a union is a different instrument from a land claim. AND ITS ORIGIN, WHICH EXPLAINS THE METHOD: INFLUENCED BY AN EDUCATION FOUNDATION FOUNDED BY A NAMED YOUNG ACTIVIST IN THE LATE 1970s, ITS INITIAL MANDATE WAS TO SOURCE FUNDS TO GIVE BURSARIES TO MARGINALISED STUDENTS — BROADENING FROM THE EARLY 1990s TO COMBAT ILLITERACY AND INITIATE PROJECTS THAT COULD ASSIST WOMEN TO BECOME MORE SELF RELIANT, ENTERPRISING AND SKILLED, WITH EMPHASIS ON THE HOMELANDS AND COASTAL VILLAGES. Forty years from bursaries to land rights, by following what communities asked for at each stage. The through-line is education, and it shows in the newsletters, the policy translation and the leadership training. WHO IT SUITS: rural and coastal communities that have no organisation yet — farmers, fishers, farm workers, landless people and rural women — and anyone needing land that comes with water. CAVEATS: ONE COUNTRY, ORGANISED THROUGH SIX REGIONAL AFFILIATES, AND IT BUILDS ORGANISATIONS RATHER THAN LITIGATING, FUNDING PURCHASES OR REPRESENTING YOU; SOME PUBLISHED MATERIAL IS OLDER, SO CHECK CURRENT REGIONAL COVERAGE. For the commonage acquisitions and what happened afterwards, Niger's entry; for the federation that litigated against parliament, Rwanda's entry.

trackers.name: FSH (Fédération Sénégalaise des Habitants) with urbaSEN and urbaMonde, Dakar — 20,000 members in 700+ savings groups, 96% women, a revolving fund governed by the borrowers at 5% over 20 months, and the Cité FSH co-operative separating land from housing ownership
trackers.desc: THE BORROWERS WRITE THE LOAN TERMS, AND THE LAND CANNOT BE SOLD — method and adjacency declared first: SECOND ACQUISITION-ONLY ROUND; THIS BUCKET WAS THE THINNEST MEASURED PAIR IN AFRICA. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THREE HOSTS AND SIX DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL HOSTS AND FOUR FACTS ABSENT, WITH ONE ACRONYM MATCHING AS SUBSTRING NOISE AND ONE GENERIC PHRASE MATCHING THREE ENTRIES, ALL READ AND ALL DIFFERENT FEDERATIONS ON OTHER HOSTS IN OTHER COUNTRIES. THIS FILE'S NAMIBIA BUCKET CARRIES A DIFFERENT NATIONAL FEDERATION'S REVOLVING FUND, ITS SOUTH AFRICA BUCKET THE GLOBAL SLUM DWELLERS' NETWORK, ITS TUNISIA ENTRY THE BORROWER-OWNED HOUSING CO-OPERATIVE UNION. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. WHO SETS THE TERMS, WHICH IS THE FIND: UNLIKE TRADITIONAL MICROFINANCE MECHANISMS, IN THIS CASE THE RESIDENTS DEFINE THE TERMS OF ACCESS TO FUNDING AND PRIORITISE THEIR NEEDS — THE FUND RELYING ON SOLIDARITY FROM THE SAVINGS GROUP ITSELF, WHICH IS COLLECTIVELY RESPONSIBLE FOR THE LOAN GRANTED TO ITS MEMBERS. This file has recorded microfinance arriving in settlements on terms set elsewhere. Here the people repaying wrote the rules, and the group carries the risk together rather than each household alone — which is what makes lending to people with no collateral possible at all. THE PUBLISHED LOAN TERMS, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: LOANS REPAID OVER 20 MONTHS AT AN EFFECTIVE INTEREST RATE OF 5%, OF WHICH 2% IS PAID BACK INTO THE FUND, 1% TO THE TECHNICAL NGO, 1% TO THE SAVINGS GROUP THE HOUSEHOLD BELONGS TO, AND 1% TO THE FEDERATION — WITH LOANS OF UP TO 984,000 XOF, ABOUT $1,600 USD. Five per cent, split four ways, every share published. That is a complete, copyable financial design: a group anywhere can adopt the same split, and the fact that 1% returns to the borrower's own savings group is what keeps the group interested in whether its member repays. HOW THE FUND RENEWS ITSELF: ONE MEMBER'S REIMBURSEMENT IN TURN ENABLES ANOTHER MEMBER TO FINANCE A HOUSING IMPROVEMENT PROJECT; IT IS FED WITH SAVINGS AND INTERNATIONAL DONATIONS FROM TWO NAMED EUROPEAN COOPERATION AGENCIES. Savings first, donations second. A fund seeded by its members' own money survives the donor leaving, which this file has recorded ending most externally funded schemes. THE SIZE AND COMPOSITION OF THE FEDERATION: NEARLY 20,000 MEMBERS IN MORE THAN 700 SAVINGS GROUPS, THE VAST MAJORITY MADE UP OF WOMEN AT 96% — PRESENT IN AROUND FIFTEEN MUNICIPALITIES IN THE SUBURBS OF THE CAPITAL AND IN THREE NAMED REGIONS, AND A MEMBER OF A SLUM DWELLERS NETWORK PRESENT IN 32 COUNTRIES. Ninety-six per cent women, and this file's Sudan entry records why that matters for land: tenure held through a husband ends with him. A federation where women are the members and the borrowers puts the asset in their own names. WHAT HAS BEEN BUILT WITH IT: 800 HOUSING IMPROVEMENT OR RECONSTRUCTION PROJECTS, AND THROUGH COLLECTIVE LOANS 100 PUBLIC SPACE AND SANITATION PROJECTS INCLUDING PLAYGROUNDS, STORMWATER BASINS, SANITARY FACILITIES, RAINWATER MANAGEMENT STRUCTURES, DRAINAGE PAVEMENTS AND SEEPAGE PITS — WITH 213 HOUSEHOLDS SECURING FUNDING TO REBUILD THEIR HOMES IN ONE NAMED PROJECT. COLLECTIVE LOANS for drainage and public space. A settlement that finances its own stormwater basin removes the flooding that is so often the stated justification for clearing it. WHO APPROVES A PROJECT: PROJECTS ARE DRAWN UP BY MEMBERS OF THE SAVINGS GROUPS AND APPROVED BY BOTH THE MEMBERS AND THE FEDERATION'S CREDIT COMMITTEE — WITH THE TECHNICAL TEAM SUPPORTING EACH PROJECT THROUGH COSTING, MONITORING AND HANDOVER. THE ANTI-SPECULATION ARRANGEMENT, WHICH IS THE THIRD FIND: A RESIDENTS' COOPERATIVE HAS BEEN SET UP TO ENABLE MEMBERS TO BENEFIT FROM A 150-HOUSE ECO-NEIGHBOURHOOD PROJECT, WITH A LEGAL AND FINANCIAL ARRANGEMENT ENSURING THERE IS NO SPECULATION IN THE LAND — COLLECTIVE OWNERSHIP OF IT BY THE COOPERATIVE AND OWNERSHIP OF THE HOUSING BY THE MEMBERS, WITH A RESTRICTIVE CLAUSE ON RESALE, A SEPARATION OF OWNERSHIP OF LAND AND BUILDINGS INSPIRED BY COMMUNITY LAND TRUSTS. This is the structure that answers the failure recorded throughout this file: land won, then sold within a decade by the households who won it. The co-operative holds the ground permanently, members own their houses, and the resale clause blocks the flip. Being built now in francophone West Africa, which means the legal drafting exists in French. THE STATE SUPPORT IT IS ARTICULATED WITH: LINKED TO THE GOVERNMENT'S 100,000 HOUSING PROGRAMME, ALLOWING STATE SUPPORT VIA A BANK GUARANTEE THROUGH THE FONDS DE L'HABITAT SOCIAL (FHS) AND PRIMARY SERVICING WORKS VIA SAFRU — WITH APPROVAL SOUGHT FROM THE MINISTRY IN CHARGE OF SOCIAL HOUSING. A BANK GUARANTEE from the state rather than cash. That is the cheapest thing a government can give and the thing that unlocks a loan for people with no collateral — worth asking for by name where a housing programme already exists. THE MAPPING RESIDENTS DO THEMSELVES: RESIDENTS CARRY OUT DRONE-MAPPING AND SUPPLY DATA TO MUNICIPAL AUTHORITIES — THIS DATA ALSO HELPING GENERATE CERTIFICATES OF OCCUPANCY AS A FIRST STEP TOWARDS LAND TENURE REGULARISATION. Residents mapping their own settlement and the map producing occupancy certificates. The municipality lacks the data and the residents supply it, which converts an informal settlement into something the register can recognise. WHY THE FEDERATION EXISTS BEYOND THE MONEY: IT MOBILISES AND FEDERATES ITS MEMBERS TO MAKE THEIR VOICES HEARD WITH PUBLIC AUTHORITIES AND DEFEND THEIR INTERESTS REGARDING ACCESS TO DECENT AND SUSTAINABLE HOUSING, AND HANDLES INFORMATION SHARING, ADMISSION OF NEW GROUPS AND BENEFICIARY SELECTION. BENEFICIARY SELECTION done by the federation, not the funder. Who gets the loan is the decision that determines whether a scheme is trusted, and here it stays inside the membership. THE PROBLEM IT NAMES: THE EXPECTATIONS AND NEEDS OF PEOPLE LIVING IN INFORMAL SETTLEMENTS ARE ONLY VERY PARTIALLY TAKEN INTO ACCOUNT, AND RESIDENTS ARE RARELY LISTENED TO — WITH AROUND 1.8 MILLION PEOPLE IN INFORMAL SETTLEMENTS ON THE CAPITAL'S OUTSKIRTS FACING RECURRENT FLOODING. AND THE SUPPORTING STRUCTURE BEHIND IT: SINCE 2011 THE NATIONAL TECHNICAL NGO HAS BEEN SUPPORTED BY A FRENCH-SWISS ASSOCIATION WHICH HELPS WITH STRATEGIC DEVELOPMENT, INTERNATIONAL FUNDRAISING, REPORTING AND NETWORKING — AND WHICH CO-AUTHORED A STUDY ON AFFORDABLE AND COOPERATIVE HOUSING COMMISSIONED BY A CONTINENTAL AFFORDABLE HOUSING FINANCE CENTRE. Three tiers, each doing one job: residents' federation, national technical NGO, international partner raising money abroad. Worth copying as a division of labour — the fundraising is done by the body best placed to do it, and the decisions are not. WHO IT SUITS: settlement residents who want a fund they control rather than microfinance on someone else's terms, and groups needing a legal structure that stops land being sold on. CAVEATS: THE FEDERATION IS ONE COUNTRY'S, AND THE FUND LENDS MAINLY FOR HOUSING IMPROVEMENT AND SANITATION, WITH THE LAND-HOLDING CO-OPERATIVE STILL BEING BUILT — SO THE ANTI-SPECULATION ARRANGEMENT IS A DESIGN TO COPY RATHER THAN A FINISHED PRECEDENT; THESE ARE LOANS REPAID BY MEMBERS, NOT GRANTS. For the borrower-owned co-operative union that lends for land purchase, Tunisia's entry; for a community land trust already established, Kenya's entry.

trackers.name: Sudan — Commercial Registration Department (Registrar General)
trackers.desc: National corporate registry; the Commercial Registration Department (Registrar General) under the Ministry of Justice maintains the commercial register under the Companies Act 1925 & Registration Law 1971, with an online registered-company-name search, Sudan. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Sudan — Ministry of Finance & Economic Planning (MoFEP)
trackers.desc: National budget authority; the MoFEP oversees Sudan’s public finances — budgeting, fiscal policy & economic planning — and publishes the national budget, Sudan. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Sudan.

trackers.name: National Audit Chamber (Sudan)
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Sudan — audits government accounts and the use of public money.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: African Convention on Nature — check WHICH version binds your state
trackers.desc: THERE ARE TWO AFRICAN CONVENTIONS OF THIS NAME, AND CITING THE WRONG ONE IS THE AVOIDABLE ERROR HERE. The Algiers Convention was signed 15 September 1968, in force 16 June 1969. The revised Maputo Convention was adopted by the Assembly of the Union in Maputo on 11 July 2003 and entered into force 23 July 2016 — thirteen years later. THE OPERATIVE RULE: the 1968 Convention remains in force for those countries that have not ratified the 2003 revisions, so the two coexist and which binds your state depends on its ratification status. Commentary records only about 30 percent of African states had ratified Maputo. This entry does not assert which binds your state — the African Union publishes a Status List alongside the treaty text at au.int. Check it first. WHY THE DELAY IS AN ARGUMENT FOR IT: commentary attributes the thirteen years to the revised text containing strong provisions that could create accountability and also slow down social and economic development — a treaty resisted for creating accountability is one worth invoking where it applies. PROVISIONS TO KNOW: article XXXIX — no reservation may be made to this Convention, so a ratifying state takes all of it; article XL — withdrawal takes effect only one year after written notification; and no instrument of accession to the 1968 Algiers Convention may be deposited any longer, so the older text is closed to new entrants. THE OBJECTIVES ARE BROADER THAN USUAL: conservation, utilisation and development of soil, water, flora and fauna for present and future welfare, from an economic, nutritional, scientific, educational, cultural and aesthetic point of view — so a claim resting on cultural or aesthetic value has a treaty basis. BUT IF THE 1968 TEXT IS WHAT BINDS YOU, EXPECT LITTLE: parties were encouraged to cooperate but were not required to submit regular reports on implementation, and there were no financial mechanisms — no reporting trail, no funding attached. Article XLI also provides for interim secretariat arrangements, so check current institutional capacity. IUCN publishes a commentary on each provision in English and French.

trackers.name: SECS — Sudan's pioneer environmental society, registered in 1975, with a branch network reaching far past Khartoum
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Sudanese Environment Conservation Society, officially registered in 1975 as the country's pioneer national environmental NGO — national, voluntary and independent, and by its own account grown into a network of more than 113 branches across Sudan, run largely by volunteers. In a country where almost every organisation is Khartoum-bound, a branch network of that reach is the point: the nearest branch, not the capital office, is the realistic contact. WHAT IT DOES FOR PEOPLE ON THE LAND: environmental rehabilitation and conservation work at community level; water, sanitation and health work with farmers and pastoralists specifically; lobbying and advocacy for environmental rights; and capacity building for grassroots communities. It campaigned for the creation of the higher council for environment and natural resources at national and state level, and has pressed for environmental provisions in Sudan's constitution and for enforcement of environmental law — which is unusual: this is an organisation that has argued about the shape of the law, not only about trees. Deforestation is its long-running specific focus. It runs a centre for environmental research and studies. Str. 57 Extension, PO Box 44266, Khartoum. WHO IT SUITS: farming and pastoral communities facing land degradation, deforestation, or loss of water access. CAVEATS, AND THEY ARE OVERRIDING: SUDAN IS IN A FULL-SCALE WAR. Institutional capacity, staffing and reachability cannot be assumed, published contact details predate the current conflict, and much of the descriptive record is several years old. SECS is a voluntary conservation and advocacy society, not a law firm: no litigation capacity, no intake route, no fee information.

trackers.name: Darfur Bar Association — 535 volunteer lawyers who represent people the state is prosecuting, and the reason land records now matter more than ever
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Darfur Bar Association, a Sudanese lawyers' organisation created in 1995 to protect and defend victims of violence, with a reported membership of 535 lawyers across Sudan volunteering as human rights defenders and providing legal aid to citizens, with an emphasis on activists. It participates in consultations at the African Commission and UN bodies, and received an international democracy award in 2020 for supporting marginalised people to advocate for their rights. A client's account of what it is worth is blunt: if the DBA has not supported you, you will be hurt and you will be in court. During the 2019 revolution it represented hundreds of arbitrarily detained people. THE LAND FACT THAT MAKES THIS URGENT, and it is the reason a bar association appears in a land map: reporting on Sudan's judicial system records that across Khartoum, the Darfur states, Kordofan and Gezira the civilian judicial infrastructure has collapsed, courts have been bombed or looted, and there has been DELIBERATE BURNING OF JUDICIAL RECORDS AND LAND REGISTRIES. If the registry that held proof of your family's land has been destroyed, the copy in your own hands — and any dated statement a lawyer takes from you now — becomes the record. Separately, an Emergency Lawyers group provides legal assistance and documents war-related abuses including attacks on civilian areas. WHO IT SUITS: Sudanese households and displaced families needing representation, documentation of what happened to their property, or help reconstructing lost land proof. CAVEATS: SUDAN IS AT WAR AND THIS IS DANGEROUS WORK — lawyers have been forced into exile, arrested and tortured, Darfuri rights monitors have been killed, and legal representation itself has been criminalised; the elected national bar council was dissolved by decree in 2023. Contact details and capacity may have changed. For the environmental branch network, Sudan's SECS entry.

trackers.name: Sudan's mutual aid funding route — money going DIRECTLY to Emergency Response Rooms and local coordination councils, not through international intermediaries
trackers.desc: WHERE MONEY REACHES COMMUNITIES: with Sudan at war and formal institutions collapsed, the funding route that works is DIRECT AND FLEXIBLE EMERGENCY GRANTS TO VETTED MUTUAL AID GROUPS. A funder coalition expanded its commitment to AT LEAST USD 16 MILLION in such grants by the end of 2026, having exceeded an earlier commitment to channel at least USD 2 million by end-2024. THE STRUCTURES THAT RECEIVE IT ARE THE POINT, because they are things communities already are rather than organisations to approach: EMERGENCY RESPONSE ROOMS, LOCAL COORDINATION COUNCILS and other community groups — the coalition works with partners on the ground to MAP them, conduct due diligence and determine transfer options, delivering through transfer services, HAWALA, digital cash and other pathways. If your neighbourhood runs an emergency response room, it is already the kind of body this money is designed for — the task is being mapped and vetted, not being founded. A separate route: a migration agency Rapid Response Fund makes SMALL GRANTS to local partners, and identifies MENTOR ORGANISATIONS so funds can be channelled in support of informal networks including the Emergency Response Rooms — explicitly recognising that front-line response runs through informal structures. Ask which registered organisation is acting as mentor for your area; that is how an unregistered neighbourhood group gets funded without registering. Funders state the case plainly: mutual aid networks and local leadership are the most viable and cost-effective mechanism to reach at-risk communities. WHO IT SUITS: Sudanese neighbourhood committees, emergency response rooms and community groups — including those trying to hold ground, keep records and support displaced families. CAVEATS: THIS IS HUMANITARIAN MUTUAL AID FUNDING, NOT LAND OR ENVIRONMENTAL GRANT-MAKING — it will not buy land or fund litigation, and vetting and transfer mechanics are the practical obstacles; nothing here is safe to publicise carelessly in a war. For representation, documentation of what happened to your property, and the burned land registries, Sudan's Darfur Bar Association entry; for the environmental branch network, SECS.

trackers.name: Forests National Corporation — the body that has registered and coordinated Sudanese forests since 1989, and the extension route that reaches village women directly
trackers.desc: WHO REGISTERS A FOREST IN SUDAN: the FORESTS NATIONAL CORPORATION (FNC) has coordinated forestry development in Sudan SINCE 1989, standing at the end of a statutory line that runs back to the WOODS AND FORESTS ORDINANCE OF 1901, the FIRST FOREST ACT OF 1908 which replaced it, and a century of successive legislation. An institution with a continuous mandate since 1989 and a legal lineage since 1901 is the body that holds the forest register — in a country where most other records have been destroyed or displaced, ask the FNC what is recorded for your area and get a copy of it. THE ROUTE THAT REACHES ORDINARY PEOPLE, DOCUMENTED: the FNC has run FORESTRY EXTENSION ACTIVITIES built on explicit recognition of the role of WOMEN in natural resource management AS PRODUCERS, USERS AND CONSUMERS OF TREES AND FORESTS, with extension work concentrated in the EASTERN AND CENTRAL REGIONS and reviews specifically examining women's participation. Extension officers are the cheapest formal contact with the forest authority a village has — and where the programme is already built around women's use of trees, a women's group is a recognised interlocutor rather than a petitioner. The record notes what any claim must account for: Sudan is large and diverse, with significant REGIONAL AND CULTURAL VARIATION in agricultural production systems, LAND TENURE, and the exploitation of forest products — so the tenure position in Kassala is not the tenure position in Darfur, and a national rule will not settle a local claim. WHO IT SUITS: Sudanese villages, women's producer groups and displaced communities seeking to establish or recover a record of forest rights. CAVEATS: STATED PLAINLY — this is a state forestry institution, not a community-tenure grant, and the sources verified for this file predate the current war; FNC capacity, records and field presence in an active conflict cannot be assumed. Confirm before relying on it. For USD 16M in mutual-aid funding, the mentor-organisation route for unregistered groups and hawala transfer, Sudan's Emergency Response Rooms entry; for 535 volunteer lawyers, the Darfur Bar Association entry.

trackers.name: Sudan's land claim routes — the hakura system, the Darfur Land Commission, the Native Administration as mediator, and the restitution entitlement for displaced people
trackers.desc: WHO HEARS A LAND CLAIM IN SUDAN: land is governed by PLURAL LEGAL SYSTEMS — statutory law alongside customary law, with little coordination between them. The customary unit is the HAKURA: a piece of land ASSIGNED BY A TRIBAL CHIEF TO A GROUP OF PEOPLE FOR A SPECIFIC LAND USE, and capable of being assigned to a small family or an individual, FOR A SPECIFIC PERIOD OR AGAINST A SET OF AGREEMENTS; the plural HAWAKEER denotes the lands of a clan or tribal group. A hakura can be held for a fixed period or on agreed conditions — so ask what period and what conditions yours carries, because that is the ground on which it is defended or lost. THE TWO NUMBERS THAT SHOW WHY PAPER MATTERS: among non-displaced residents 91% OWN THEIR HOUSING PLOT BUT ONLY 30% HOLD A REGISTRATION CERTIFICATE PROVING IT; among returnees, 79% OWN THEIR PLOT AND ONLY 9% CARRY THE OFFICIAL DOCUMENT, while in a city like El Fasher 94-97% of residents hold a registered area certificate. Ownership without a certificate is the normal condition in rural Darfur and the ordinary condition of return — get whatever document exists, and note that returnees report the cost of official GPS demarcation as high. THE BODIES: the DARFUR LAND COMMISSION, established 13 July 2007 under Article 20 of the Darfur Peace Agreement, to address traditional and historical land tenure and review natural-resource management; a NATIONAL LAND COMMISSION set out in the later peace agreement; and, on the ground, the NATIVE ADMINISTRATION — described as A CRUCIAL LOCAL INSTITUTION FOR RESOLVING LAND CONFLICTS whose MEDIATION ROLE SHOULD BE SCALED UP. The Native Administration is the body that actually mediates — go to it first; the commissions are where a historical or tribal-level claim belongs. THE ENTITLEMENT TO CITE: the DOHA DOCUMENT FOR PEACE IN DARFUR states that ANY CITIZEN OF SUDAN IS ENTITLED TO OWN LAND, AND THAT INTERNALLY DISPLACED PERSONS WHOSE LANDS ARE OCCUPIED ARE ENTITLED TO RESTITUTION; the 2020 Juba Peace Agreement EXPLICITLY RECOGNISES TRADITIONAL OWNERSHIP OF TRIBAL LANDS (HAWAKEER) and historic rights. Say the word restitution: occupation of your land does not extinguish your claim, and both agreements say so in terms. One land-tenure programme secured tenure for returning displaced people across 51 VILLAGES. WHO IT SUITS: displaced and returning Sudanese families, and communities defending a hakura. CAVEATS: STATED PLAINLY — commissions have faced enormous challenges, individual titling has had minimal reach, the rights of SECONDARY OCCUPANTS complicate every return, and this record largely predates the conflict that erupted in April 2023. For 535 volunteer lawyers, Sudan's Darfur Bar Association entry; for the forest register, the Forests National Corporation entry; for mutual-aid money, the Emergency Response Rooms entry.

trackers.name: The Sudanese Women's Union and the registration desk every Sudanese NGO goes through — a membership body founded 1952 that predates every government since, plus a named environmental research centre
trackers.desc: THE UNION THAT OUTLASTED EVERY GOVERNMENT: the SUDANESE WOMEN'S UNION (SWU, الاتحاد النسائي السوداني), CREATED IN 1952, WITH ITS FOUNDING MEETING HELD ON 17 JANUARY 1952 — ONE OF THE BIGGEST POST-INDEPENDENCE WOMEN'S RIGHTS ORGANISATIONS IN AFRICA, with its founding president, secretary and named members on the public record. An organisation founded before independence and still named is one that has survived every Sudanese government since. In a country whose courts and ministries this file records as broken by war, a membership body with that much continuity is a more durable address than a state office — and a woman with a land or inheritance claim has somewhere that predates the dispute. WHERE THE ENVIRONMENTAL RESEARCH SITS: SECS runs the NADIR AWAD CENTRE FOR ENVIRONMENTAL RESEARCH AND STUDIES, and the society's stated method is that SECS DEPENDS FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF ITS ACTIVITIES ON VOLUNTEERS WITH EMPHASIS ON YOUTH MEMBERS, AND ALL INTERVENTIONS ARE DESIGNED TO ENSURE THE ACTIVE CONTRIBUTION OF VOLUNTEERS SO THAT ITS ENDEAVOURS HAVE A POPULAR DIMENSION. A named research centre inside a volunteer society is where a Sudanese community gets a study written without paying a consultancy — ask the centre, not the head office. THE REGISTRATION DESK, WHICH IS THE PRACTICAL FACT FOR ANYONE FORMING A BODY: SECS WAS OFFICIALLY REGISTERED IN 1975 AT THE HUMANITARIAN AID COMMISSION, MINISTRY OF HUMANITARIAN AFFAIRS, AS A PIONEER NATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL NGO. The Humanitarian Aid Commission is the door a Sudanese association goes through to exist in law. Ask what it currently requires before you draft anything — and note that an environmental society was registered there, so the environmental purpose is an accepted one. WHAT SECS HAS ACTUALLY WON AT NATIONAL LEVEL, worth citing when you are told nothing can change: THE SOCIETY MILITATED FOR THE ESTABLISHMENT OF THE HIGHER COUNCIL OF ENVIRONMENT AND NATURAL RESOURCES AT BOTH NATIONAL AND STATE LEVELS, AND ADVOCATES FOR ENVIRONMENTAL ARTICLES AND LAWS IN SUDAN'S CONSTITUTION, lobbying specifically on DEFORESTATION. A civil society organisation campaigned a national environmental council into existence, and state-level councils with it. If your state has one, that is a body you can address; if it does not, the precedent for demanding one is Sudanese. Its published contact is Street 57 Extension, PO Box 44266, KHARTOUM, and it holds consultative status at the UN. WHO IT SUITS: Sudanese women with a land or inheritance claim, groups seeking to register an association, and communities needing a study or a state-level council to petition. CAVEATS: SEVERAL OF THESE RECORDS PREDATE THE CONFLICT THAT ERUPTED IN APRIL 2023 — confirm which branches and offices are functioning. For 113 branches and the society itself, Sudan's SECS entry; for 535 volunteer lawyers, the Darfur Bar Association entry; for money going directly to Emergency Response Rooms, the mutual aid entry; for the hakura and the restitution entitlement, the land claim routes entry.

trackers.name: A categorised directory of Sudanese organisations with post boxes, phone and fax for each — SCOVA the voluntary agencies council, SEDO, the industries chamber and the Catholic secretariat
trackers.desc: THE DIRECTORY WITH POST BOXES AND PHONE NUMBERS — which in a country where this file records almost no working contacts is the thing that matters: A PUBLISHED RESOURCE GUIDE LISTS SUDANESE ORGANISATIONS BY CATEGORY, GIVING FOR EACH A MAILING ADDRESS, TELEPHONE, FAX AND WHERE AVAILABLE AN EMAIL AND WEB PAGE — AND IT SORTS THEM INTO GOVERNMENT, PRIVATE SECTOR, CSO AND INFORMATION. A directory that tells you whether a body is government, private sector or civil society before you write is how you avoid sending a community's case to the wrong kind of institution. Work the category first, then the address. THE UMBRELLA IT NAMES: SCOVA — THE SUDAN COUNCIL OF VOLUNTARY AGENCIES, P.O. BOX 11925 KHARTOUM, WITH TWO TELEPHONE NUMBERS, A FAX AND A PUBLISHED EMAIL, CATEGORISED AS CSO. A national council of voluntary agencies is the body that knows which Sudanese organisations still function. In a country whose civic landscape has been repeatedly disrupted, that is the first call — not to ask for help, but to ask who is operating in your state. THE ENVIRONMENTAL ONE THIS FILE DID NOT HOLD: SEDO — THE SUDANESE ENVIRONMENT AND DEVELOPMENT ORGANIZATION, PO BOX 399 KHARTOUM, WITH A PUBLISHED TELEPHONE. Environment AND development in one organisation's name is the combination a farming or pastoral community needs, because the argument that a place should be protected and the argument that people should live from it are the same argument. AND TWO BODIES WORTH KNOWING FOR DIFFERENT REASONS: THE SUDANESE CHAMBER OF INDUSTRIES ASSOCIATION, AT A NAMED BUILDING ON AFRICA ROAD, KHARTOUM, WITH TELEPHONE AND FAX, CATEGORISED AS PRIVATE SECTOR; AND THE SUDAN CATHOLIC SECRETARIAT, P.O. BOX 6011 KHARTOUM, WITH TELEPHONE AND FAX. An industries chamber is the address at which a whole sector can be asked to respond — useful when the operator on your land is a member of it and you want the industry association, not just the company, to hear the complaint. And a church secretariat is a national structure with parish-level reach; this file has recorded across the region that where lay associations are thin, the congregation is the room that already fills. THE MEMBERSHIP MODEL WORTH COPYING, FROM SUDAN'S OLDEST ENVIRONMENTAL SOCIETY: IT IS A MEMBERSHIP BASED ORGANIZATION WITH BRANCHES ALL OVER SUDAN AND MEMBERS FROM DIFFERENT CULTURES AND QUALIFICATIONS, AND IS A FOUNDING MEMBER OF MANY NATIONAL, SUB-REGIONAL AND REGIONAL NETWORKS AND COALITIONS, AND AN ACCREDITED MEMBER OF THE UN COPs. Members from different cultures and qualifications is a deliberate design in a country whose conflicts run along those lines — an organisation built that way can convene people a single-community body cannot. And accreditation to the UN conferences of the parties is a standing that lets a Sudanese case be raised internationally through a Sudanese body rather than a foreign one. ITS COMMUNITY-LEVEL WORK NAMES WHO IT IS FOR: ENVIRONMENTAL REHABILITATION AND CONSERVATION; ADDRESSING CLIMATE CHANGE IMPACTS; WATER, SANITATION, HEALTH AND HYGIENE FOR MARGINALIZED PEOPLE — FARMERS AND PASTORALISTS; LOBBYING AND ADVOCATING FOR ENVIRONMENTAL RIGHTS; AWARENESS CAMPAIGNS FOR FARMERS, PASTORALISTS, GRASSROOTS COMMUNITIES, YOUTH AND CHILDREN; AND CAPACITY BUILDING FOR THE SAME. Farmers and pastoralists named twice, as the marginalised people the lobbying is for. Where a scheme takes grazing land or blocks a stock route, that is the organisation whose stated constituency you already are — and lobbying for environmental RIGHTS, not just conservation, is the wording that covers a community's loss. WHO IT SUITS: Sudanese farming and pastoral communities, and anyone who needs a working address for a Sudanese organisation. CAVEATS: THIS DIRECTORY IS OLDER AND SUDAN'S CIVIC LANDSCAPE HAS BEEN SEVERELY DISRUPTED SINCE — treat every number as needing confirmation, and expect some bodies to have moved or stopped. For the society itself with its 113 branches and its Khartoum street address, Sudan's SECS entry; for 535 volunteer lawyers who represent people the state will not, the Darfur Bar Association entry; for money going directly to Emergency Response Rooms, the mutual aid entry; for the body that has registered and coordinated community forests, the Forests National Corporation entry; for the hakura system and the Darfur Land Commission, the land claim routes entry; for the registration desk every Sudanese NGO goes through, the Sudanese Women's Union entry.

trackers.name: Business & Human Rights Resource Centre — the non-profit that will put your allegation to the company and publish its answer — a 70% response rate across 9,000 tracked firms — plus a foreign government ombudsperson for mining and oil, with a plain-language procedure and a written retaliation section
trackers.desc: SEVENTY PER CENT OF COMPANIES ANSWER WHEN THEY ASK — that is the find, because a community writing to a company directly is usually ignored: THE CENTRE SERVES AS A LINK BETWEEN LOCAL COMMUNITIES AND ACTIVISTS AND COMPANIES, SEEKING RESPONSES FROM BUSINESSES TO ALLEGATIONS OF MISCONDUCT — AND IT GIVES COMPANIES AN OPPORTUNITY TO RESPOND TO ALLEGATIONS BEFORE POSTING THEM. GLOBALLY, IT HAS ACHIEVED A 70 PERCENT RESPONSE RATE FROM COMPANIES. You send them the allegation; they put it to the company under their own name; seven times in ten the company answers, and the answer is published beside your account. That is a reply on the record from a firm that has never replied to you — and it costs nothing. WHY THE COMPANY BOTHERS: refusing is also published. A blank where the response should be is itself the record, which is why the rate is what it is. THE SCALE: IT TRACKS THE HUMAN RIGHTS POLICY AND PERFORMANCE OF OVER 9,000 COMPANIES IN OVER 180 COUNTRIES, MAKING INFORMATION PUBLICLY AVAILABLE, WITH THE WEBSITE UPDATED HOURLY — AND INFORMATION IS AVAILABLE BY REGION OR COUNTRY, SECTOR, INDIVIDUAL COMPANY, OR BUSINESS ORGANIZATION. Search the company on your land by name before you do anything else. If it has been accused elsewhere, the account and the company's own answer are already there — which tells you what defence it will run on you. WHAT IT SAYS IT DOES: WE HELP COMMUNITIES AND NGOs GET COMPANIES TO ADDRESS HUMAN RIGHTS CONCERNS, AND PROVIDE COMPANIES AN OPPORTUNITY TO PRESENT THEIR RESPONSE — AND WE AMPLIFY THE VOICES OF THE VULNERABLE. HOW THE RECORD IS BUILT, WHICH IS WHY IT CARRIES WEIGHT: EVERY STORY HAS AT LEAST ONE COMPONENT SUCH AS AN NGO REPORT, A MEDIA ARTICLE, A LAWSUIT SUMMARY, OR A COMPANY RESPONSE, SO THAT ALLEGATIONS ARE DESCRIBED FROM MULTIPLE SOURCES AND VIEWPOINTS — AND AN API LETS USERS QUERY THE ENTIRE DATABASE. Multiple sources per allegation, including the company's own words. A journalist or a court treats that differently from a single community statement, which is exactly why getting your case in is worth the effort. THE SECOND ROUTE, AND IT IS A GOVERNMENT OFFICE: A HUMAN RIGHTS OMBUDSPERSON REVIEWS COMPLAINTS ABOUT HARMFUL EFFECTS WHEN HUMAN RIGHTS ARE ABUSED BY THAT COUNTRY'S COMPANIES DOING BUSINESS IN OTHER COUNTRIES — IN THE GARMENT, MINING, AND OIL AND GAS SECTORS — THROUGH A FLEXIBLE PROCESS THAT CAN INCLUDE MEDIATION AND REVIEWS, WITH A PUBLISHED FLOW CHART AND PLAIN LANGUAGE OPERATING PROCEDURES. MINING and OIL AND GAS are two of the three sectors it covers, which is most of what this file records. And PLAIN LANGUAGE OPERATING PROCEDURES published as a separate document means somebody has already translated the process out of legal English — read that version, not the formal one. AND ITS RETALIATION SECTION IS WRITTEN TO YOU, NOT ABOUT YOU: YOU MAY WORRY THAT FILING A COMPLAINT WILL PUT YOU OR OTHERS IN DANGER. YOU MAY WORRY ABOUT YOUR JOB, YOUR HOME, OR YOUR PROPERTY. YOU MAY BE AFRAID THAT THOSE YOU NAME IN YOUR COMPLAINT WILL RETALIATE AGAINST YOU — AND RETALIATION IS DEFINED AS ACTING IN A WAY THAT HAS A NEGATIVE EFFECT ON A PERSON BECAUSE THEY CONTACTED THE OFFICE, FILED A COMPLAINT, WORKED TO RESOLVE ONE, OR PROVIDED INFORMATION SUCH AS BY ACTING AS A WITNESS. WITNESSES ARE COVERED, not only the person who signs. That matters when the people who saw what happened are the ones with jobs to lose — tell them the protection extends to them, in those words. AND THE THIRD ROUTE, INSIDE THE COMPANY ITSELF, NOW REQUIRED OF FIRMS UNDER SOME SUPPLY-CHAIN LAWS: A COMPLAINTS PROCEDURE ACCESSIBLE TO ALL EMPLOYEES, BUSINESS PARTNERS AND THIRD PARTIES WHO HAVE LEGITIMATE REASONS TO BELIEVE HUMAN RIGHTS AND/OR ENVIRONMENTAL OBLIGATIONS HAVE BEEN VIOLATED WITHIN THE COMPANY'S OWN BUSINESS AREA OR WITHIN ITS SUPPLY CHAINS — A WEB-BASED SYSTEM ACCESSIBLE WORLDWIDE, FREE OF CHARGE AND AVAILABLE AROUND THE CLOCK, WITH 15 LANGUAGES TO CHOOSE FROM, WHERE THE COMPLAINANT MAY CHOOSE WHETHER TO PROVIDE CONTACT DETAILS AND RECEIVES A RANDOM CASE ID AND PASSWORD FOR A SECURE MAILBOX. THIRD PARTIES, which means neighbours and not only workers. Anonymous submission with a case ID and a secure mailbox to follow up. Large European buyers increasingly must run one of these — so if the operator on your land supplies a big foreign firm, look for that firm's whistleblowing portal and file there too. It is a different desk from anything local, and it is answerable to a law in the buyer's country. WHO IT SUITS: African communities facing a company that will not answer them, especially in mining, oil and gas, or an export supply chain. CAVEATS: THE CENTRE PUBLISHES AND SEEKS RESPONSES — IT DOES NOT LITIGATE OR COMPENSATE; and the ombudsperson covers only its own country's companies in three sectors. For the trackers naming which foreign company and financier stands behind a project, Guinea's investment chain entry; for the home-country mediation offices covering all adhering states, Chad's entry; for the 24-hour helpline and protection grants, Benin's defender protection entry.

trackers.name: CAFÉ (Consortium of African Funds for the Environment) — the network of 19 African national environmental funds holding US$400 million in endowments — already financing 125 communal conservancies and community forests, with a published members directory and a membership route
trackers.desc: FOUR HUNDRED MILLION DOLLARS, HELD BY AFRICAN FUNDS — WHAT IT IS: A MEMBERSHIP-BASED NETWORK OF ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS, ALSO KNOWN AS CONSERVATION TRUST FUNDS, IN AFRICA, IN OPERATION SINCE 2011 — WITH 19 MEMBER FUNDS THAT SUPPORT OVER 90 PARKS AND RESERVES AND 125 COMMUNAL CONSERVANCIES AND COMMUNITY FORESTS, COVERING OVER 270,000 SQUARE KILOMETRES ACROSS 20 COUNTRIES. COLLECTIVELY, MEMBERS MANAGE OVER US$400 MILLION IN ENDOWMENTS AND ABOUT US$100 MILLION IN SINKING FUNDS. 125 COMMUNAL CONSERVANCIES AND COMMUNITY FORESTS is the number that matters here, not the parks. These funds already pay for community-held land, which means a community conservancy is a recognised thing they finance rather than an exception you would have to argue for. AND THE MONEY IS AFRICAN-HELD. An endowment sits in a national trust in Kampala or Lilongwe rather than a foreign foundation — so the decision about your area is taken on your continent, by people who can be met, and it does not end when a donor's country changes government. This file has recorded repeatedly that where a fund sits determines who can reach it. THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE TWO KINDS OF MONEY, WORTH UNDERSTANDING BEFORE ASKING: AN ENDOWMENT IS INVESTED AND ONLY ITS RETURNS ARE SPENT, SO IT PAYS OUT INDEFINITELY; A SINKING FUND IS SPENT DOWN TO NOTHING OVER A FIXED PERIOD. Ask which kind you are being offered. Endowment income is small but permanent, and it will still be there in ten years when the project that threatens you is still being pushed; sinking-fund money is larger and finite. A community guarding a forest needs the first. THE MEMBER FUNDS NAMED IN THE RECORD, SO YOU CAN FIND YOURS: A MOZAMBICAN FUND, A BENINESE TRUST FUND, A MALAWIAN MOUNTAIN FUND, A UGANDAN BIODIVERSITY FUND, A MALAWI ENVIRONMENTAL ENDOWMENT TRUST WHICH HAS HOSTED THE SECRETARIAT, AND A SANGHA TRI-NATIONAL TRUST FUND IN CAMEROON CURRENTLY HOLDING THE PRESIDENCY. A TRI-NATIONAL trust fund covering one forest across three countries. Where your landscape crosses a border — as this file has recorded from the Karamoja cluster to the Congo Basin — there may already be a single fund for the whole of it rather than three national ones to petition separately. WHAT ONE MEMBER LOOKS LIKE IN PRACTICE: A NATIONAL BIODIVERSITY FUND REGISTERED IN 2016 AND OFFICIALLY LAUNCHED IN 2018 AS A TRUST ESTABLISHED TO PROVIDE SUSTAINABLE FINANCING FOR THE CONSERVATION OF THAT COUNTRY'S BIODIVERSITY. Two years from registration to launch. If your country has no such fund, that is the timescale for building one — and the network below is who would help. WHAT MEMBERSHIP GIVES, PUBLISHED AS A LIST: CONNECT WITH ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS ACROSS AFRICA TO SHARE RESOURCES AND EXPERTISE; ACCESS TRAINING PROGRAMS, WORKSHOPS AND KNOWLEDGE SHARING; GAIN ACCESS TO FUNDING MECHANISMS AND FINANCIAL SUPPORT FOR CONSERVATION PROJECTS; LEARN FROM SUCCESSFUL CONSERVATION MODELS AND PROVEN STRATEGIES ACROSS AFRICA; RECEIVE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE AND EXPERT GUIDANCE FOR YOUR CONSERVATION INITIATIVES; AND JOIN UPCOMING CONFERENCES, WORKSHOPS AND MEMBER GATHERINGS. THE ROUTE AND ITS GATE, STATED PLAINLY: BECOME PART OF THE NETWORK, HERE IS HOW TO GET STARTED — ENSURE YOUR ORGANIZATION MEETS THE REQUIREMENTS FOR ENVIRONMENTAL FUND MEMBERSHIP IN AFRICA. Membership is for funds, not for villages. So the practical use for a community organisation is the members directory: find the fund covering your country and approach it directly, because that is the body actually disbursing to conservancies near you. THE WINDOW WITH PUBLISHED AMOUNTS: FINANCIAL SUPPORT RANGES FROM 50,000 EUROS TO 150,000 EUROS, WITH 6 MEMBERS RECEIVING FUNDING UNDER A NAMED PROJECT FOR INITIATIVES THAT ENGAGE THE PRIVATE SECTOR IN CONSERVATION FINANCE. WHAT THE FUNDS TEACH EACH OTHER, WHICH TELLS YOU WHAT THEY WILL ASK YOU ABOUT: TOPICS HAVE RANGED FROM FUNDRAISING, GOVERNANCE, PRIVATE SECTOR ENGAGEMENT AND INVESTMENT MANAGEMENT TO COMMUNICATIONS — FULL OF VALUABLE LESSONS FOR MORE INFORMED DECISIONS AND BETTER MANAGEMENT. GOVERNANCE and INVESTMENT MANAGEMENT are what these bodies worry about, so an application that shows how your committee is elected and how money is accounted for speaks their language. This file's savings-group entry is the cheapest way to acquire both. THE GOVERNANCE, WORTH COPYING FOR ANY NETWORK YOU BUILD: THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY IS THE HIGHEST DECISION MAKING ORGAN; THE PRESIDENT IS ELECTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY FROM AMONGST THE EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE; MEMBERS CREATE SUBCOMMITTEES AND WORKING GROUPS AROUND AREAS OF COMMON INTEREST, COMPRISED OF MEMBERS AND/OR RESOURCE PERSONS OUTSIDE THE NETWORK; AND THE EXECUTIVE SECRETARIAT IS AN INDEPENDENT BODY HOSTED BY THE FUND HOLDING THE PRESIDENCY. The secretariat moves with the presidency rather than sitting permanently in one country. That rotation is what stops a continental network becoming one nation's project — and it is a clause worth writing into any alliance your community joins or founds. AND THE PUBLIC OUTPUTS: A LIBRARY OF RESEARCH PAPERS, REPORTS, GUIDELINES AND EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS ON CONSERVATION; A DECLARATION ADOPTED BY MEMBER FUNDS AT A GENERAL ASSEMBLY; A NEWSLETTER; AND A PUBLISHED CONTACT ROUTE FOR PARTNERSHIPS, MEDIA INQUIRIES OR SUPPORT. A declaration adopted by nineteen funds is a document your own fund has signed. If it commits members to community participation, quote it back to them when applying. WHO IT SUITS: African communities and organisations looking for the national conservation fund that finances community conservancies in their country. CAVEATS: MEMBERSHIP IS FOR FUNDS, NOT COMMUNITY GROUPS — use the directory to find your national fund and apply there. For the money and technical help to hold land as a conservancy, Kenya's Conservancies Fund entry; for the endowment funding 48 of 123 marine protected areas, Madagascar's FAPBM entry; for the grant windows with no co-financing requirement, Kenya's BIOPAMA entry.

trackers.name: CCSI (Columbia Center on Sustainable Investment) — two free guides written for the community side of the table — one for before the investor arrives, one for negotiating the contract — plus a repository of agreements other communities actually signed, in French as well as English
trackers.desc: TWO GUIDES WRITTEN FOR THE COMMUNITY SIDE OF THE TABLE — declared adjacency first: THIS FILE'S MAURITANIA ENTRY COVERS A REPOSITORY OF EXTRACTIVES CONTRACTS. THIS ONE COVERS THE AGRICULTURE, FORESTRY AND RENEWABLE ENERGY REPOSITORY, A SEPARATE REPOSITORY OF COMMUNITY-INVESTOR AGREEMENTS, AND TWO GUIDES WRITTEN FOR COMMUNITIES THEMSELVES. THE TWO GUIDES: WRITTEN FOR COMMUNITIES AND THEIR ADVISORS ON INTERACTING WITH INVESTORS, HELPING COMMUNITIES TO PROTECT THEIR RIGHTS AND INTERESTS WHEN INVESTORS WANT TO USE THEIR LAND — GUIDE 1 SETS OUT PRACTICAL GUIDANCE TO PREPARE BEFORE POTENTIAL INVESTORS ARRIVE, AND AFTER AN INVESTOR HAS APPROACHED A COMMUNITY; GUIDE 2 PROVIDES PRACTICAL GUIDANCE ON THE ISSUES TO CONSIDER WHEN NEGOTIATING AND DRAFTING COMMUNITY-INVESTOR CONTRACTS. BEFORE POTENTIAL INVESTORS ARRIVE. Almost everything in this file is a response to something already happening. A guide for the years when nothing is happening yet is rarer and worth more — the community that has already decided what it would and would not accept negotiates from a position; the one starting on the day of the first meeting negotiates from surprise. THE SCOPE, STATED HONESTLY BY THE AUTHORS: DESIGNED TO APPLY TO AGRICULTURE AND FORESTRY PROJECTS, ALTHOUGH THEY MAY HAVE SOME APPLICABILITY TO AGREEMENTS REACHED IN OTHER CONTEXTS, SUCH AS AROUND MINING OR RENEWABLE ENERGY — AND THEY ARE PUBLISHED IN FRENCH AS WELL AS ENGLISH. WHO WROTE THEM: A LEADING APPLIED RESEARCH CENTER DEDICATED TO SUSTAINABLE INTERNATIONAL INVESTMENT, PARTNERED WITH AN INTERNATIONAL ORGANIZATION DEDICATED TO ADVANCING LEGAL EMPOWERMENT AND STRENGTHENING PEOPLE'S CAPACITY TO EXERCISE AND DEFEND THEIR RIGHTS. An investment research centre and a legal empowerment organisation, together. The first knows how the contracts are actually drafted; the second knows how a village committee will actually use a guide. That pairing is why this is usable rather than academic. THE AFRICAN PILOT: MEMBERS OF A NATIONAL ENGAGEMENT STRATEGY PILOTED THE GUIDES IN A NAMED DISTRICT OF AN EAST AFRICAN COUNTRY, WITH A PUBLISHED ACCOUNT OF HOW SIMPLIFIED LEGAL GUIDES ARE EMPOWERING COMMUNITIES. Already tested in an African district rather than only drafted. Ask for the pilot account before running your own workshop — somebody has recorded what did and did not translate. THE SECOND REPOSITORY, WHICH IS THE FIND AND HAS NO EQUIVALENT ELSEWHERE IN THIS FILE: A COLLECTION OF PUBLICLY AVAILABLE AGREEMENTS BETWEEN LOCAL COMMUNITIES AND INVESTORS — IN SOME INSTANCES ALSO FEATURING AGREEMENTS THAT INCLUDE HOST GOVERNMENT PARTIES. THE AGREEMENTS INCLUDE BENEFIT SHARING AGREEMENTS, LEASES, MEMORANDA OF UNDERSTANDING AND REVENUE SHARING AGREEMENTS CONCLUDED IN THE CONTEXT OF AGRICULTURE, FORESTRY, MINING, OIL AND GAS EXTRACTION, RENEWABLE ENERGY AND OTHER NATURAL RESOURCE PROJECTS. Agreements other communities signed, published in full. Before agreeing terms, read what a comparable community got — what the royalty was, what the employment clause said, what happened about water. A company negotiating with you has seen a hundred such agreements and you have seen none; this closes that gap for the price of an internet connection. THE FIRST REPOSITORY: THE FIRST GLOBAL REPOSITORY OF PUBLICLY AVAILABLE INVESTOR-STATE CONTRACTS FOR COMMERCIAL AGRICULTURE OR FORESTRY PROJECTS — SEARCHABLE BY COUNTRY, BY NATURAL RESOURCE, OR BY TYPE OF CONTRACT, WITH SUMMARIES OF KEY SOCIAL, HUMAN RIGHTS, ENVIRONMENTAL, FISCAL AND OPERATIONAL PROVISIONS, THE ABILITY TO COMPARE PROVISIONS ACROSS CONTRACTS, AND FULL PDF DOWNLOADS. SUMMARIES OF KEY PROVISIONS means somebody has already read the hundred-page contract and pulled out what it says about your water, your resettlement and your jobs. You do not need a lawyer to start. WHY THEY EXIST: LARGE-SCALE INVESTMENTS IN AGRICULTURE AND FORESTRY CAN HAVE FAR-REACHING IMPLICATIONS, YET ARE OFTEN NEGOTIATED AND APPROVED BEHIND CLOSED DOORS, AND GOVERNED BY CONTRACTS THAT ARE DIFFICULT TO ACCESS AND UNDERSTAND. THE OTHER NAMED TOOLS: A GUIDE TO NEGOTIATING INVESTMENT CONTRACTS FOR FARMLAND AND WATER — A TOOL FOR PARLIAMENTARIANS, GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS, LANDHOLDERS AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES, FOCUSED ON LONG-TERM LEASES OF FARMLAND, GIVING A STEP-BY-STEP FRAMEWORK INCLUDING ASSESSING FOOD SECURITY, LAND AND WATER RIGHTS, COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT AND PROJECT IMPACTS BEFORE SIGNING A DEAL; AND A MODEL MINING DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT, A 200+ PAGE BALANCED DRAFT CONTRACT WITH SAMPLE CLAUSES DRAWN FROM REAL AGREEMENTS, AVAILABLE IN SIX LANGUAGES INCLUDING FRENCH AND PORTUGUESE. ASSESSING FOOD SECURITY BEFORE SIGNING is the item to insist on. A lease that leaves a district unable to feed itself is a bad deal at any royalty, and there is a published framework for working that out in advance. THE DIRECTORY: A DIRECTORY OF COMMUNITY GUIDANCE ON AGREEMENTS RELATING TO AGRICULTURE OR FORESTRY INVESTMENTS, GATHERING THE EXISTING RESOURCES THAT CAN ASSIST COMMUNITIES AND THEIR ADVOCATES IN THEIR INTERACTIONS WITH INVESTORS OVER LAND. AND THE QUESTION IT PUTS TO THE JOBS PROMISE, WHICH IS THE PROMISE EVERY PROJECT IN THIS FILE MAKES: THE EMPLOYMENT POTENTIAL OF EXTRACTIVE PROJECTS AND LAND ACQUISITIONS IS OFTEN TOUTED BY BOTH GOVERNMENTS AND COMPANIES — SO RESEARCH EXAMINES HOW JOB NUMBERS ARE CALCULATED, WHICH FACTORS INFLUENCE JOB CREATION, THE QUALITY AND SUSTAINABILITY OF THOSE JOBS, AND WHETHER JOB CREATION IS NET POSITIVE. WHETHER IT IS NET POSITIVE. Jobs promised are counted; livelihoods destroyed are not. Asking for the net figure, and citing research that the gross one is unreliable, is the single most useful question at a consultation meeting — and this file's marine and mangrove entries show what the uncounted side is worth in honey, fish and salt. WHO IT SUITS: African communities approached by an agricultural, forestry, mining or renewable energy investor, and the advisors preparing them. CAVEATS: GUIDES AND DATABASES, NOT LEGAL REPRESENTATION OR NEGOTIATORS — pair them with a lawyer or paralegal. For the extractives contract repository, Mauritania's entry; for the school that teaches contract analysis with scholarships, Niger's entry; for the paralegal method where no lawyer exists, Sierra Leone's Timap entry.

trackers.name: Resource Equity's Landesk — a free help desk that answers the specific women's land rights question you send it, plus a searchable archive of past answers, a law library covering national, state and local levels, and online courses linking the few practitioners in each country
trackers.desc: THERE IS A DESK THAT ANSWERS THE QUESTION YOU SEND IT — adjacency declared first: A RIGHTS-AND-RESOURCES BODY IS ALREADY A HOST UNDER GHANA AND HAS SINCE ACQUIRED THE LAW LIBRARY NAMED BELOW; THE REPUBLIC OF THE CONGO ENTRY COVERS THE LAND-TITLING ORGANISATION THAT ORIGINALLY LAUNCHED IT. NEITHER IS RESTATED AND NEITHER HOST IS SHIPPED. THE HELP DESK, AND IT IS THE FIND: IT IS NOT ALWAYS EASY TO FIND THE INFORMATION AND ANSWERS YOU ARE LOOKING FOR, AND WE ARE HERE TO SUPPORT PEOPLE WHO WORK WITH AND CARE ABOUT WOMEN GAINING RIGHTS TO LAND — SUBMIT THE SPECIFIC QUESTION YOU ARE LOOKING FOR ANSWERS TO, AND WE WILL SHARE THE INFORMATION AND KNOWLEDGE WE HAVE COLLECTED OVER THE YEARS. Almost every resource in this file is a library you must search. This is a person who answers. For a paralegal or a committee secretary facing one specific question — can a widow inherit here, does registration require a husband's signature, what does the local by-law actually say — that is the difference between a week of reading and an answer. AND THE ARCHIVE BEFORE YOU ASK: SEARCH OUR DATABASE OF PREVIOUS HELP DESK QUESTIONS TO SEE IF YOURS HAS ALREADY BEEN ANSWERED; IF NOT, SUBMIT IT. A GLOSSARY OF IMPORTANT TERMS IS ALSO PUBLISHED. Somebody else has probably asked. The archive is a record of what practitioners actually get stuck on, which is more useful than a curriculum — and the glossary is what lets a committee member follow a lawyer's letter. THE FREE LEGAL LIBRARY: A DATABASE CONTAINING LAWS AND LEGAL MATERIALS ABOUT WOMEN'S LAND RIGHTS — CONNECTING USERS TO LEGAL MATERIALS, INFORMATION ABOUT RELEVANT CUSTOMARY PRACTICES, AND EXPLANATORY MATERIALS. CUSTOMARY PRACTICES documented alongside the statutes. Most women in this file lose land under custom rather than under law, and a library that records both is the only kind that helps. WHAT IT COLLECTS, AND THE LAST LEVEL IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS: LAND LAWS AND FAMILY LAWS AND RELATED MATERIAL FROM AS MANY COUNTRIES AS POSSIBLE — FROM ALL LEVELS OF GOVERNMENT: NATIONAL, STATE AND LOCAL. FAMILY LAW sits beside land law here, which is correct and rare: inheritance, marriage and divorce decide who holds land far more often than the land code does. And LOCAL by-laws are what a district actually applies. THE OPEN CONTRIBUTION ROUTE: IF YOU HAVE ANY MATERIALS YOU WOULD LIKE TO RECOMMEND FOR INCLUSION, CONTACT US — AND CONTACT US IF YOU HAVE UPDATED INFORMATION. Your country's new land act, the district by-law nobody has digitised, the customary code your elders wrote down: all can be sent in. Contributing puts your jurisdiction on a map other advocates search. THE WARNINGS THEY PUBLISH ABOUT THEIR OWN MATERIAL, WHICH IS WHY IT CAN BE TRUSTED: WE CANNOT GUARANTEE THAT ALL LAWS ARE THE MOST RECENT VERSIONS; MANY MATERIALS ARE ENGLISH TRANSLATIONS AND, UNLESS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED, TRANSLATIONS ARE NOT OFFICIAL VERSIONS, SO USERS SHOULD BE CAREFUL; AND THIS IS GENERAL LEGAL INFORMATION THAT CANNOT REPLACE THE ADVICE OF COMPETENT LEGAL COUNSEL LICENSED IN YOUR JURISDICTION. TRANSLATIONS ARE NOT OFFICIAL VERSIONS. Never quote a translated statute to a court or a ministry without checking the gazetted original — an opponent who finds the discrepancy will use it to discredit everything else you brought. THE COURSES AND WHAT THEY ARE REALLY FOR: THROUGH CROSS-CULTURAL ONLINE COURSES THEY TRAIN PRACTITIONERS IN TECHNIQUES, APPROACHES AND BEST PRACTICES IN WOMEN'S LAND AND NATURAL RESOURCE RIGHTS — AND AS MANY STUDENTS ARE OFTEN ONE OF THE FEW PRACTITIONERS IN THEIR COUNTRY, THE INSTITUTE IS BUILDING A DEEP NETWORK OF IN-COUNTRY EXPERTS WHO COLLABORATE ACROSS CONTINENTS. ONE OF THE FEW PRACTITIONERS IN THEIR COUNTRY. That is the isolation this file has recorded repeatedly — the single person in a district who knows this subject, with nobody to ask. The course is worth taking as much for the other students as for the syllabus. THE AFRICAN COUNTRIES OF OPERATION, NAMED: BURKINA FASO, CABO VERDE, ETHIOPIA, GHANA, KENYA, LIBERIA, MADAGASCAR, MOROCCO, RWANDA, TANZANIA AND UGANDA. THE ORGANISATION: A NON-PROFIT FOUNDED IN DECEMBER 2014, DESCRIBED BY ITS OWN EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR — A GENDER AND LAND TENURE LAWYER — AS A SMALL BUT MIGHTY NON-PROFIT. Small, and it says so. Expect a considered answer rather than a fast one, and ask early rather than in the week of a hearing. THE LIBRARY'S HISTORY AND ITS NEW HOME: LAUNCHED IN JULY 2013 BY A CENTRE FOR WOMEN'S LAND RIGHTS, TRANSFERRED IN OCTOBER 2015, AND IN SEPTEMBER 2023 ACQUIRED BY A RIGHTS AND RESOURCES GROUP — WHOSE COORDINATOR SAID IT HAS CAPTURED LAWS AND RESEARCH ON WOMEN'S LAND RIGHTS FOR OVER A DECADE AND BOOSTS THEIR EXISTING RESOURCES ON COMMUNITY LAND TENURE AND A GROWING GENDER JUSTICE PROGRAM. Recorded because it changes where to look: the library has moved twice in a decade. If a link fails, search the new owner rather than assuming the resource is gone. THE COMPANION TOOL AT THAT NEW HOME: A TOOL SHOWCASING NATIONAL, REGIONAL AND GLOBAL DATA ON THE STRENGTH AND EXTENT OF COMMUNITIES' AND COMMUNITY WOMEN'S TENURE RIGHTS OVER TIME — WITH FRESHWATER TENURE DATA NOW INCLUDED. OVER TIME is the useful axis: it shows whether your country's community tenure protections have strengthened or weakened since the last law was passed, which is the question a reform campaign needs answered first. AND THE RESEARCH FINDING THEY PUBLISH, WHICH IS A SURVEY DESIGN IN ITSELF: TO PROMOTE THE SOCIAL CHANGES NEEDED FOR WOMEN TO HAVE SECURE AND EQUITABLE LAND RIGHTS, IT IS ESSENTIAL TO BUILD ON EXISTING CUSTOMARY PRACTICES AND SOCIAL NORMS THAT POSITIVELY AFFECT WOMEN — AND CRUCIAL TO COLLECT INFORMATION ABOUT HOW WOMEN AND MEN USE AND CONTROL LAND, HOW COMMUNITY DECISIONS ARE MADE AND WHAT ROLE WOMEN PLAY IN COMMUNITY GOVERNANCE, HOW WEALTH IS DISTRIBUTED WITHIN THE HOUSEHOLD THROUGH INHERITANCE AND DOWRY OR BRIDE PRICE, AND WHAT CUSTOMS EXIST FOR CARING FOR THE ELDERLY OR WIDOWED. BUILD ON THE CUSTOMS THAT ALREADY HELP WOMEN, rather than arriving to overturn custom wholesale. That is the approach least likely to unite a village against you — and the four questions listed are a ready-made agenda for a community meeting that costs nothing to hold. WHO IT SUITS: African paralegals, committee members, lawyers and women's organisations with a specific question about land, inheritance or marriage law they cannot get answered locally. CAVEATS: GENERAL LEGAL INFORMATION, NOT ADVICE, WITH TRANSLATIONS THAT ARE UNOFFICIAL AND LAWS THAT MAY NOT BE CURRENT — verify against the gazette before relying on anything. For the deed-formalization service and its talking books, the Republic of the Congo's entry; for the fund decided by a grassroots women's committee, Niger's entry; for university law clinics as free representation, Comoros' entry.
