trackers.name: Up to €50,000 where local non-profits are the stated target beneficiaries, an intermediary applying on somebody else's behalf is barred outright, and international applicants must minimise the share spent overseas
trackers.desc: AN INTERMEDIARY APPLYING FOR SOMEBODY ELSE IS NOT ELIGIBLE — adjacency declared first: A CONSERVATION UNION IS A HOST UNDER MOROCCO AND CAPE VERDE; THIS FUND IS CO-MANAGED BY THAT UNION'S SPECIES PROGRAMME BUT IS A SEPARATE INITIATIVE WITH ITS OWN RULES, AND NEITHER ENTRY IS RESTATED NOR THAT HOST SHIPPED. THIS FILE'S NIGER ENTRY COVERS THE $25,000 SPECIES FUND OPEN TO INDIVIDUALS, ITS ESWATINI ENTRY THE TEAM LADDER, AND ITS SÃO TOMÉ ENTRY THE NATIONAL AWARD. WHO THE FUND IS FOR, WHICH IS THE FIND: IN LINE WITH THE FUND'S OBJECTIVE, TARGET BENEFICIARIES ARE PRIMARILY LOCAL NON-PROFIT ORGANISATIONS — AND IT BACKS LOCAL CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANISATIONS, INDIGENOUS AND COMMUNITY GROUPS, AND EARLY-CAREER RESEARCHERS, THOSE CLOSEST TO THE SPECIES AND ECOSYSTEMS MOST AT RISK. THE INTERMEDIARY BAR, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: APPLICATIONS SUBMITTED BY A BODY ACTING AS AN INTERMEDIARY FOR A THIRD PARTY ARE NOT ELIGIBLE — THE APPLICANT MUST BE DIRECTLY RESPONSIBLE FOR THE PREPARATION AND IMPLEMENTATION OF THE GRANT PROJECT. Read those two together and the design is clear: the money is meant to arrive at the organisation doing the work, and an international body cannot apply on a local group's behalf and pass a share down. This file has recorded that chain repeatedly — the grant lands abroad, the local organisation becomes a sub-contractor. Here that arrangement is disqualifying, which makes a local applicant advantaged rather than merely permitted. AND THE OVERSEAS-COST LIMIT ON THE INTERNATIONALS WHO DO APPLY: INTERNATIONAL NGOs MUST MINIMIZE OVERSEAS COSTS — INDIRECT COSTS, SALARIES, INTERNATIONAL TRAVEL — WITH CLEAR JUSTIFICATION. Foreign salaries and flights must be justified line by line. If an international partner is leading, ask to see that justification: it is where a budget quietly stops being about your species and starts being about their staff. THE ADMINISTRATIVE CONDITIONS, WHICH ARE THE REAL GATE: THE APPLICANT MUST HAVE A BANK ACCOUNT IN THE NAME OF THE ORGANISATION, AND BE AUTHORIZED UNDER RELEVANT NATIONAL LAWS TO RECEIVE CHARITABLE CONTRIBUTIONS, INCLUDING FROM SOURCES OUTSIDE THEIR RESPECTIVE COUNTRIES. A bank account in the organisation's own name and legal permission to receive foreign donations. Many African countries restrict the second, and this file has recorded that restriction being used deliberately against community organisations. Check your own status before writing anything — it is the condition most likely to end an application that would otherwise have succeeded. THE LEAD PARTNER ARRANGEMENT: THE LEAD PARTNER MAY ACT INDIVIDUALLY OR WITH CO-APPLICANTS; IF AWARDED, IT BECOMES THE GRANTEE, IS THE MAIN INTERLOCUTOR OF THE SECRETARIAT, REPRESENTS AND ACTS ON BEHALF OF ANY CO-APPLICANTS, AND COORDINATES DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION — AND AN ORGANISATION CAN ONLY BE AWARDED ONE GRANT AS LEAD PARTNER. Being lead partner means holding the contract and speaking for the others. Decide that before drafting, and put the division of money and decisions in writing between the partners — the funder recognises only the lead. THE TWO GRANT TYPES AND THEIR CEILINGS: CONSERVATION ACTION GRANTS UP TO EUR 50,000 FOR A MAXIMUM OF 12 MONTHS, TO CARRY OUT SUSTAINABLE CONSERVATION MEASURES AT LOCAL LEVEL TO PROTECT THE SPECIES, THEIR HABITATS AND TO IMPROVE THE LIVELIHOODS OF THE PEOPLE WHO DEPEND ON THEM; AND RESEARCH SUPPORT GRANTS UP TO EUR 7,000 FOR YOUNG AND EARLY SCIENTISTS ENROLLED IN A CURRICULUM AT AN ACADEMIC INSTITUTION. LIVELIHOODS OF THE PEOPLE WHO DEPEND ON THEM is written into the objective, so a proposal that is about the community as well as the animal is on-brief rather than a stretch. And the €7,000 research grant is a route for a student from the affected area — the enrolment condition makes it reachable for a local university student in a way the action grant is not. THE SPECIES RULE AND ITS PRECISION: PROJECTS MUST FOCUS ON IMPROVING THE STATUS OF THREATENED ANIMAL SPECIES — TERRESTRIAL, FRESHWATER AND MARINE — LISTED AS VULNERABLE, ENDANGERED OR CRITICALLY ENDANGERED; PLANT AND FUNGUS SPECIES ARE NOT ELIGIBLE; ONLY GLOBAL RED LIST STATUS COUNTS, WITH SUB-SPECIES AND SUB-POPULATIONS OF DIFFERENT STATUS NOT CONSIDERED; AND FOR ENDEMIC SPECIES LACKING A GLOBAL ASSESSMENT, A NATIONAL RED LIST ASSESSMENT CAN BE CONSIDERED WITH PUBLICLY AVAILABLE REFERENCES. ANIMALS ONLY here — for a threatened tree or plant, the fund filed under Niger accepts plants and fungi and this one does not. And the national-assessment opening matters: an endemic species with no global listing is not automatically excluded if your country has assessed it and the reference is public. THE RESEARCH RULE THAT DECIDES MANY APPLICATIONS: PROJECTS MUST IMPLEMENT CONCRETE CONSERVATION ACTIVITIES ON THE GROUND; RESEARCH IS ELIGIBLE ONLY IF THE PROPOSAL SUPPORTS TANGIBLE CONSERVATION ACTIONS USING THE RESULTS WITHIN THE TIMEFRAME OF THE PROJECT, AND PURE RESEARCH PROJECTS ARE NOT ELIGIBLE. THE EXAMPLES IT GIVES OF ELIGIBLE RESEARCH-INTO-ACTION, AND ONE IS DIRECTLY USEFUL HERE: A PRACTICAL MANAGEMENT PLAN OR NEW POLICY, A NEW PROTECTED AREA DESIGN, OR A NEW NATURAL RESOURCES MANAGEMENT PLAN; GATHERING EVIDENCE NEEDED TO UNDERTAKE NECESSARY MITIGATION WORK; USING SCIENTIFIC EVIDENCE TO GET CHANGES MADE TO LOCAL, NATIONAL OR INTERNATIONAL POLICY; AND DEVISING AND TESTING A NEW METHODOLOGY FOR MONITORING. USING SCIENTIFIC EVIDENCE TO GET CHANGES MADE TO LOCAL, NATIONAL OR INTERNATIONAL POLICY is an eligible activity, named by the funder. A community that surveys what lives on land facing a concession, and uses the result to argue for a different decision, is describing exactly this — and A NEW PROTECTED AREA DESIGN is the other listed activity that a community can propose on its own terms. THE HUMAN-WILDLIFE CONFLICT CONDITION: APPLICATIONS INVOLVING HUMAN-WILDLIFE CONFLICT SHOULD DEMONSTRATE A THOROUGH UNDERSTANDING OF THE UNDERLYING SOCIAL AND POLITICAL CONTEXTS AND HOW THE WORK WILL ADDRESS SOME OF THESE — OR EXPLAIN HOW SUCH UNDERSTANDING WILL BE GAINED BEFORE A MITIGATION STRATEGY IS DEVELOPED. Social and political context demanded, not just fences and compensation. A community that can describe why the conflict exists — whose grazing was taken, which corridor was cut — is better placed here than an outside applicant. THE CONFLICT-OF-INTEREST AND REPEAT RULES: NO CONFLICT OF INTEREST, WHICH MAY ARISE FROM ECONOMIC INTERESTS, POLITICAL OR NATIONAL AFFINITIES, FAMILY OR EMOTIONAL TIES, OR ANY OTHER RELEVANT CONNECTION; APPLICANTS CANNOT BE EMPLOYEES OF THE TWO MANAGING BODIES OR CLOSE RELATIVES; AND AN APPLICANT WITH AN ONGOING GRANT CANNOT APPLY FOR THE SAME PROJECT LOCATION, THOUGH THEY MAY APPLY FOR ANOTHER. AND THE SCOPE, SCALE AND CURRENT STATUS: A FIVE-YEAR INITIATIVE COVERING AFRICA AMONG FOUR OTHER REGIONS, FOCUSING ON UNDERFUNDED SPECIES AND CONSERVATION LEADERS, WITH ROUGHLY EUR 500,000 A YEAR AND ABOUT 90% OF THAT GOING TO THE ACTION GRANTS — AND THE FOUNDATION NOT CURRENTLY ACCEPTING UNSOLICITED CONCEPT NOTES, SO THE PUBLISHED CALLS ARE THE ROUTE. Half a million a year across five regions is thin, so the calls are competitive and the timing matters more than the polish. WHO IT SUITS: local and national African conservation organisations and community groups working on a threatened animal species — as the lead applicant, which is what the rules favour. CAVEATS: ANIMALS ONLY, ONE GRANT AS LEAD PARTNER, 12 MONTHS MAXIMUM, A BANK ACCOUNT AND LEGAL PERMISSION TO RECEIVE FOREIGN FUNDS REQUIRED, AND CALLS RATHER THAN OPEN APPLICATION — for plants and fungi, and for applicants with no organisation at all, Niger's entry.

trackers.name: A university centre that is also an NGO, taking cases to the African Court and Commission with national organisations as co-applicants — and publishing the exact standing rule on which two of its own applications were rejected
trackers.desc: THEY PUBLISH WHY THEIR OWN CASES WERE THROWN OUT ON STANDING — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S BOTSWANA ENTRY MENTIONS THIS CENTRE IN PASSING WITHOUT DESCRIBING IT; ITS NIGERIA ENTRY NAMES A CONTINENTAL CORPORATE ACCOUNTABILITY COALITION; ITS RWANDA ENTRY THE GATHERING WHOSE DECLARATION BOTH ENDORSED; ITS DJIBOUTI ENTRY THE FUNDER THAT PAID FOR A CONTINENTAL COURT CASE. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. THE PROCEDURAL TRAP IT PUBLISHES AGAINST ITSELF, WHICH IS THE FIND: IT PREPARED AND SUBMITTED TWO REQUESTS FOR ADVISORY OPINIONS TO THE AFRICAN COURT, AND BOTH APPLICATIONS WERE REJECTED ON THE BASIS THAT THE APPLICANTS' OBSERVER STATUS BEFORE THE AFRICAN COMMISSION DOES NOT QUALIFY THEM AS AFRICAN ORGANISATIONS RECOGNIZED BY THE AFRICAN UNION — WHICH CAN ONLY BE OBTAINED THROUGH OBSERVER STATUS OR A MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING WITH THE AFRICAN UNION COMMISSION. Two years of work rejected before anyone read the argument, and the centre published exactly why. Observer status at the Commission is not recognition by the Union — they are separate accreditations, and an organisation planning to use the continental system needs the right one before it drafts anything. This file has recorded communities losing on standing repeatedly; here is the specific rule, published by an organisation that lost on it. THE CO-APPLICANT MODEL, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: THE CENTRE AND TWO NAMED AFRICAN PARTNER ORGANISATIONS SUBMITTED A CASE TO THE AFRICAN COURT ON HUMAN AND PEOPLES' RIGHTS AGAINST A GOVERNMENT, SEEKING REDRESS FOR PERSONS SUBJECTED TO KILLINGS, MUTILATIONS AND VARIOUS FORMS OF DISCRIMINATION — AND IT WAS PART OF THE LEGAL TEAM OF AN INDIVIDUAL APPLICANT IN A CASE BEFORE THE AFRICAN COMMISSION. Three organisations on one continental application, and elsewhere the centre joins the legal team of an individual. A national organisation with the facts and no continental standing pairs with bodies that have it — which is the structure that gets an African community's case in front of the continental court at all. WHAT SUCH AN APPLICATION ASKS FOR: FINANCIAL COMPENSATION AND REHABILITATION FOR VICTIMS AND THEIR DEPENDANTS, SYMBOLIC REMEDIES, AS WELL AS STRUCTURAL REFORMS SUCH AS LEGISLATIVE CHANGES. STRUCTURAL REFORMS SUCH AS LEGISLATIVE CHANGES are askable at this level. A national court usually cannot rewrite the statute that permitted the harm; the continental bodies can order the state to. THE CHILDREN'S COMMITTEE ROUTE AND ITS PRECEDENT: THE CENTRE AND A NAMED SENEGALESE ORGANISATION BROUGHT A CASE DECIDED BY THE AFRICAN COMMITTEE OF EXPERTS ON THE RIGHTS AND WELFARE OF THE CHILD, AND A NORTHERN UGANDA CASE WAS THE FIRST CASE EVER SUBMITTED TO THAT COMMITTEE. A third continental forum, less crowded than the other two. Where a project displaces a school, contaminates water children drink or puts children to work, that committee is a route almost nobody uses. WHAT THE LITIGATION UNIT DOES: IT STRATEGICALLY USES THE LAW THROUGH THE INSTRUMENTALITY OF JUDICIAL AND QUASI-JUDICIAL INSTITUTIONS TO ENFORCE HUMAN RIGHTS, PREVENT HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS AND SEEK REDRESS. THE IMPLEMENTATION HALF, WHICH IS WHAT MOST WINS NEED: THE UNIT IS A LITIGATION AND IMPLEMENTATION UNIT, AND ITS CLINIC HAS BEEN MANDATED TO DEVELOP A STRATEGY TO IMPLEMENT DECISIONS OF THE AFRICAN COMMISSION AGAINST A NAMED STATE, INCLUDING A CONCEPT NOTE AND ENGAGEMENT WITH CIVIL SOCIETY. Implementation treated as its own discipline. This file has recorded continental judgments won and then ignored for years — including one on ancestral land that remains unimplemented. A unit whose stated work is making decisions actually happen is the missing half of every such victory. THE FREE STUDENT CLINIC AND THE WORK IT ACTUALLY CARRIES: STUDENTS ON A CONTINENTAL MASTERS PROGRAMME ARE ASSIGNED TO HUMAN RIGHTS CLINICS THAT CONTRIBUTE TO THE CENTRE'S WORK — WITH PAST MANDATES INCLUDING FINALISING SUBMISSIONS TO THE AFRICAN CHILDREN'S RIGHTS COMMITTEE, FINALISING A SUBMISSION TO THE AFRICAN COMMISSION, PREPARING AN AMICUS BRIEF FOR FILING AT THE EAST AFRICAN COURT OF JUSTICE, PREPARING A LEGAL BRIEF ON THE FEASIBILITY OF A LAWSUIT AGAINST A REGIONAL BODY BEFORE A NATIONAL HIGH COURT, AND DEVELOPING AN ADVISORY OPINION ON THE STATUS OF COMPANIES AS RIGHTS HOLDERS. Postgraduate lawyers from across the continent, supervised, drafting real submissions at no cost to the community. A FEASIBILITY BRIEF on whether a lawsuit is possible is exactly what an organisation cannot afford to commission and cannot proceed without — and asking the clinic to take that question as a mandate is a realistic request. THE OTHER UNITS THAT EXIST INSIDE IT: A WOMEN'S RIGHTS UNIT WORKING ON THE IMPLEMENTATION AND POPULARISATION OF A PROTOCOL ON THE RIGHTS OF WOMEN IN AFRICA THROUGH RESEARCH, TRAINING AND ADVOCACY; A MIGRATION UNIT; AND A UNIT ON SEXUAL ORIENTATION AND GENDER IDENTITY. WHAT IT IS, INSTITUTIONALLY: BOTH AN ACADEMIC DEPARTMENT AND A NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATION, BASED AT A UNIVERSITY LAW FACULTY. Being both matters practically: university funding keeps it running between grant cycles, and NGO status lets it litigate and take positions a department could not. WHO IT WORKS FOR: HUMAN RIGHTS EDUCATION IN AFRICA, GREATER AWARENESS, WIDE DISSEMINATION OF PUBLICATIONS, AND THE IMPROVEMENT OF THE RIGHTS OF WOMEN, PEOPLE LIVING WITH HIV, INDIGENOUS PEOPLES, SEXUAL MINORITIES AND OTHER DISADVANTAGED OR MARGINALISED PERSONS OR GROUPS ACROSS THE CONTINENT. INDIGENOUS PEOPLES named in the mandate, which is the opening for a land or territory case. THE NETWORK IT SITS IN: AN UNMATCHED NETWORK OF PRACTISING AND ACADEMIC LAWYERS, NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL CIVIL SERVANTS AND HUMAN RIGHTS PRACTITIONERS ACROSS THE ENTIRE CONTINENT. Its alumni are now in ministries, commissions and national organisations across Africa. For a community organisation, the useful request is a referral into that network in its own country. AND ITS ORIGIN AND OUTPUT: ESTABLISHED IN 1986 AS PART OF DOMESTIC EFFORTS AGAINST THE APARTHEID SYSTEM, WITH MEMBERS PARTICIPATING IN MEETINGS WITH THE LIBERATION MOVEMENTS AND LATER SERVING AS TECHNICAL ADVISORS TO BOTH THE INTERIM AND FINAL CONSTITUTION WRITING PROCESSES — PUBLISHING AN AFRICAN HUMAN RIGHTS LAW JOURNAL AND AFRICAN HUMAN RIGHTS LAW REPORTS. The law reports are the practical output: African human rights decisions collected and published, which is where a national lawyer finds the continental precedent to cite. WHO IT SUITS: African organisations planning a case before the continental bodies, and communities needing a feasibility opinion, a co-applicant with standing, or help implementing a judgment already won. CAVEATS: A UNIVERSITY CENTRE DOING SELECTED STRATEGIC LITIGATION AND ACADEMIC WORK, NOT A WALK-IN LEGAL SERVICE, AND ITS CLINIC MANDATES ARE SET ANNUALLY — approach with a defined question, not a general request. For the fund that paid a community's continental court costs, Djibouti's entry; for the law centre defending the right to organise, Malawi's entry.

trackers.name: Women's Legal Centre, Cape Town — a free feminist law centre that litigates to extend land tenure to women in their own right and to prevent loss of tenure when a relationship ends — and gives free legal advice to other women's organisations nationally and across Africa
trackers.desc: THEY LITIGATE THE MOMENT MOST WOMEN LOSE THE LAND — A SEPARATION — method and adjacency declared first: THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THE SHIPPED HOST AND FIVE SUBJECT SPELLINGS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL ABSENT. THIS FILE'S GAMBIA ENTRY COVERS THE WOMEN LAWYERS ASSOCIATION WITH A LITIGATION FUND, ITS GUINEA-BISSAU ENTRY THE SEVEN-COUNTRY NETWORK WHOSE OBJECTS INCLUDE DEED REGISTRATION, ITS MAURITANIA ENTRY THE ACCREDITED HOUSING LAW CLINIC IN THE SAME COUNTRY ON A DIFFERENT HOST. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE TENURE WORK, WHICH IS THE FIND: WE ATTEND TO CASES THAT EXTEND TENURE AND OWNERSHIP OF LAND TO WOMEN IN THEIR OWN RIGHT, AND PREVENT LOSS OF TENURE ON THE DISSOLUTION OF RELATIONSHIPS, SUCH AS DIVORCE OR SEPARATION. This file has spent hundreds of entries on concessions, bulldozers and courts. But the commonest way an individual African woman loses her land is none of those: it is a separation or a death, and the ground turns out to be in someone else's name. A law centre that litigates that specific moment, for free, is addressing the single largest cause of land loss recorded here — and one almost no land organisation covers. THE PROBLEM IT NAMES, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: WOMEN, IN MOST CASES, ARE NOT GIVEN LEGAL OWNERSHIP TO LAND, HOUSING AND PROPERTY, AND ALSO ENCOUNTER ISSUES IN ATTEMPTING TO OBTAIN LEGAL OWNERSHIP — WITH WOMEN LEFT IMPOVERISHED AND VULNERABLE ON THE DISSOLUTION OF THEIR RELATIONSHIPS, LOSING ACCESS TO ASSETS ACQUIRED DURING THE RELATIONSHIP. ASSETS ACQUIRED DURING THE RELATIONSHIP is the legal handle: not what she brought, but what was built together while she farmed it. That framing is what turns an eviction by a family into a property claim. WHAT IT COSTS AND WHY: THE HIGH COST OF TAKING CASES TO COURTS OFTEN PUTS LEGAL ACTION OUT OF REACH FROM THE WOMEN IN THE MOST NEED OF LEGAL PROTECTION — SO THE CENTRE PROVIDES LEGAL ADVICE AND TAKES ON CASES FOR WOMEN FREE OF CHARGE TO CHALLENGE ESTABLISHED PRINCIPLES AND OVERTURN DISCRIMINATORY LAWS. TAKES ON CASES, free, and specifically the ones meant to overturn a rule rather than settle one dispute. A woman whose situation is typical rather than unusual is the strongest candidate here, which is the opposite of how most legal aid triage works. THE OFFER TO OTHER ORGANISATIONS, INCLUDING BEYOND ITS OWN COUNTRY: IT ALSO PROVIDES LEGAL ADVICE TO OTHER NON-GOVERNMENTAL WOMEN'S ORGANIZATIONS NATIONALLY AND IN AFRICA. Continental reach for organisations, not only individuals in one city. A women's group anywhere on the continent can write for legal advice — which is a rare offer in this file, where almost every national law centre stops at its own border. WHERE ITS DOORS ARE: BASED IN ONE NAMED CITY WITH SATELLITE OFFICES IN A NAMED TOWNSHIP AND A SECOND NAMED CITY. A satellite office inside a township rather than only in the city centre. That is a deliberate decision about who can physically reach the lawyers. THE FIVE FOCUS AREAS: THE RIGHT TO FAVOURABLE AND JUST WORKING CONDITIONS; THE RIGHT TO LAND, HOUSING AND PROPERTY; EQUALITY IN RELATIONSHIPS; SEXUAL AND REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH AND RIGHTS; AND THE RIGHT TO BE FREE FROM VIOLENCE. THE WORKERS IT NAMES: FARM WORKERS, DOMESTIC WORKERS, MIGRANT WORKERS AND SEX WORKERS. FARM WORKERS in the same centre as the land work. A woman living on a farm where she also works loses her home and her job in one act — and here both limbs can be argued by the same lawyers. THE EMERGENCY HOUSING DUTY IT IS TRYING TO ESTABLISH: TO SEEK TO DEVELOP THE DUTY OF THE STATE TO PROVIDE EMERGENCY HOUSING FOR VICTIMS OF DOMESTIC VIOLENCE. An attempt to create a state obligation that does not yet exist. Worth watching in any country: if it succeeds anywhere, it is arguable everywhere with a comparable constitution. THE PARTNERSHIP OFFER ON LAND: TO COLLABORATE AND PARTNER WITH STRATEGIC AND RELEVANT ORGANISATIONS TO PROMOTE THE INTERESTS OF WOMEN'S RIGHTS TO LAND AND TENURE SECURITY. THE CUSTOMARY MARRIAGE POINT IT PUBLISHES: A CUSTOMARY MARRIAGE CAN BE LEGALLY VALID EVEN IF IT HAS NOT BEEN REGISTERED. One sentence that decides many land cases. A woman told her marriage does not count because there is no certificate is being told something that may simply be wrong — and if the marriage is valid, so are the property consequences that follow from it. WHAT IT DOES BESIDES CASES: STRATEGIC IMPACT LITIGATION, LEGAL ADVOCACY, FREE LEGAL ADVICE, AND TRAINING TO COMMUNITIES, PARTNERS AND STATE OFFICIALS — INCLUDING TRAINING THAT ENSURES PEOPLE KNOW AND UNDERSTAND THE IMPACT OF THE JUDGMENTS OF THE COURTS AROUND WOMEN'S RIGHTS, WITH A DEDICATED LEGAL ADVICE UNIT. TRAINING STATE OFFICIALS, alongside communities. The clerk at the deeds office and the magistrate are often where a valid claim dies, and training them is cheaper than appealing them. AND THE OTHER FREE ROUTES PUBLISHED ALONGSIDE IT IN THE SAME COUNTRY: A NATIONAL LAW CENTRE EMPLOYING OVER 65 LAWYERS AND STAFF FROM FOUR NAMED OFFICES, SERVING POOR, HOMELESS AND LANDLESS PEOPLE; UNIVERSITY LAW CLINICS AT MOST LAW FACULTIES; A STATE LEGAL AID SCHEME WHOSE APPLICANTS MUST STATE MONTHLY WAGES AND WHAT THEY OWN; AND A NATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS COMMISSION THAT INVESTIGATES ABUSES, CAN ARRANGE FOR SOMEONE TO HAVE A LAWYER AND CAN TAKE CASES TO COURT — WHICH ANYONE CAN COMPLAIN TO WITHOUT AN ATTORNEY. A CAUTION IS PUBLISHED WITH THEM: JUST BECAUSE YOUR NGO APPLIES DOES NOT AUTOMATICALLY MEAN YOU WILL BE ASSISTED, AND IT WILL DEPEND ON WHETHER THE NGO IS FORMALLY CONSTITUTED AND HAS AUDITED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS. Four parallel free routes and one honest warning. ANYONE CAN COMPLAIN WITHOUT AN ATTORNEY, and the commission can then arrange the lawyer — that is the cheapest first move recorded in this file. And the audited-accounts caution tells any community organisation what to have ready before asking the profession for help. WHO IT SUITS: women losing land or a home through separation, death or an unregistered customary marriage; farm-dwelling women workers; and women's organisations anywhere in Africa needing legal advice. CAVEATS: ONE COUNTRY, WITH THREE OFFICES, AND ITS CASE SELECTION FAVOURS MATTERS THAT WILL CHANGE THE LAW RATHER THAN EVERY INDIVIDUAL DISPUTE; ITS FRAME IS WOMEN'S RIGHTS RATHER THAN COMMUNITY OPPOSITION TO A PROJECT. For the association with a fund that pays court filing fees, Gambia's entry; for the network whose published objects include registering deeds, Guinea-Bissau's entry.

trackers.name: ODAC (Open Democracy Advice Centre), Cape Town — a toll-free whistleblowing hotline on 0800 525 352 giving direct legal support to about 200 whistleblowers a year, plus strategic litigation to force records out under the access-to-information act
trackers.desc: A FREE NUMBER FOR THE PERSON INSIDE WHO DECIDES TO TALK — method and adjacency declared first: THE PRE-WRITE CHECK RAN THREE HOSTS AND FIVE DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; ALL HOSTS AND FOUR FACTS ABSENT. ONE STATUTE ACRONYM MATCHED A SOUTH AFRICA ENTRY, READ IN FULL AND FOUND TO BE A 211-CHARACTER STUB NAMING ONLY THE INFORMATION REGULATOR AND NO SERVICES. DIFFERENT SUBJECT, NOT RESTATED, HOST NOT SHIPPED. THE LINE AND WHO ANSWERS IT, WHICH IS THE FIND: A TOLL-FREE WHISTLEBLOWING HOTLINE ON 0800 525 352 THAT OFFERS DIRECT LEGAL SUPPORT TO WHISTLEBLOWERS — AROUND 200 EVERY YEAR — WITH AN EMAIL HELPLINE ALONGSIDE IT, FOCUSED ON USING THE PROTECTED DISCLOSURES ACT TO SHIELD THEM FROM EMPLOYMENT-BASED DISCRIMINATION. A published number, and 200 people a year actually using it. This file's Republic of Congo entry records legal accompaniment for whistleblowers as a service; here is the same thing with a phone number on it. The person inside the company or the ministry who knows what the project will really do is the best witness a community can have, and the thing they need first is to know whether talking will cost them their job. THE THREE LAWS IT ADVISES ON: THE PROMOTION OF ACCESS TO INFORMATION ACT 2 OF 2000 (PAIA), THE PROTECTED DISCLOSURES ACT (PDA), AND THE PROTECTION OF PERSONAL INFORMATION ACT (POPIA). Two of those cut opposite ways and it is worth knowing which is which: one gets records out, one protects the person who leaks them, and the third governs what may be published about individuals. A community that files under the first should know the third exists before it publishes what comes back. WHAT IT DOES IN COURT, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: IT HAS DRIVEN STRATEGIC LITIGATION ON BOTH THE ACCESS-TO-INFORMATION ACT AND THE WHISTLEBLOWER ACT, AND HAS INITIATED OR SUPPORTED MANY STRATEGIC LITIGATION CASES. A refused records request is not the end of the road. An organisation that has litigated the act itself is the one to approach when a department simply does not answer. WHAT IT IS AND WHO BUILT IT: ESTABLISHED IN 2001 AS A JOINT INITIATIVE BETWEEN A DEMOCRACY INSTITUTE, A RIGHTS TRUST AND A UNIVERSITY LAW DEPARTMENT. THE FAILURE FIGURE THAT EXPLAINS WHY IT EXISTS: THE ACT CREATED TO REALISE THE CONSTITUTIONAL RIGHT IS POORLY IMPLEMENTED AND UNDER-UTILISED, WITH THE NATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS COMMISSION REPORTING THAT FEWER THAN 15% OF AUDITED INSTITUTIONS HAD SPECIFICALLY BUDGETED FOR ITS IMPLEMENTATION AND COMPLIANCE. FEWER THAN 15% BUDGETED FOR IT. That is the practical reason records requests go unanswered — not refusal but the absence of anyone tasked to answer. Knowing that changes the follow-up: ask who the designated information officer is, by name. THE ONLINE REQUESTING TOOL IT BUILT: FROM 2012 IT EXPLORED AN AUTOMATED ONLINE REQUESTING PROCESS FOR THE ACCESS ACT, ADAPTING AN OPEN-SOURCE FREEDOM-OF-INFORMATION PLATFORM — THEN, FINDING NO COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW OF USER EXPERIENCE, CONDUCTED ITS OWN REVIEW OF USERS AND NON-USERS. An open-source request platform is transplantable. A coalition in another country can stand up the same software against its own act rather than commissioning one. THE CONTINENTAL STUDY IT PUBLISHES: A STATE OF ACCESS TO INFORMATION IN AFRICA REPORT COVERING TWELVE COUNTRIES — CÔTE D'IVOIRE, KENYA, MADAGASCAR, MALAWI, MOZAMBIQUE, NAMIBIA, NIGER, NIGERIA, SOUTH AFRICA, TANZANIA, UGANDA AND ZIMBABWE. Twelve countries compared on whether their information laws actually work. Before spending months on a records request, it is worth knowing how your own country scored. THE LAW CHANGES ITS ADVOCACY PRODUCED: POSITIVE AMENDMENTS TO THE PROTECTED DISCLOSURES ACT, A CYBERSECURITY AND CYBERCRIMES BILL, THE PROTECTION OF PERSONAL INFORMATION ACT AND A PROTECTION OF STATE INFORMATION BILL. WHAT IT SELLS TO ORGANISATIONS: CONSULTING TO THE PUBLIC AND NON-PROFIT SECTORS TO IMPROVE WHISTLEBLOWING AND TRANSPARENCY PRACTICES THROUGH POLICY DEVELOPMENT, STAFF AND MANAGEMENT TRAINING, AND LEGAL COMPLIANCE WITH THE THREE ACTS. Worth noting because it means the organisation is partly self-funding — which this file has repeatedly recorded as the difference between a body that survives a funding shift and one that does not. THE TRAINING IT RUNS: TRAINING ON THESE LAWS FOR HUNDREDS OF PEOPLE, INCLUDING ONLINE COURSES DESIGNED FOR THE MEDIA UNDER AN OPEN JOURNALISM WORKSHOP. THE COMMUNITY WORK IT RECORDS: FACILITATING SUCCESSFUL COMMUNITY INTERVENTIONS ON ACCESS TO INFORMATION IN NAMED COMMUNITIES. AND THE WARNING ITS OWN SECTOR PUBLISHES: WHISTLEBLOWERS IN THE COUNTRY ARE UNDER THREAT AS NEVER BEFORE, A DEEPENING CULTURE OF IMPUNITY AND LACK OF ACCOUNTABILITY MAKING IT HARDER FOR THEM — AND FOR EMPLOYEES TO BE COMFORTABLE BLOWING THE WHISTLE THERE MUST BE AN ENCOURAGING AND SUPPORTIVE ENVIRONMENT IN THE WORKPLACE AS WELL AS AN ESTABLISHED CULTURE OF WHISTLE-BLOWING. Filed unsoftened. A statute protecting a whistleblower is not the same as a workplace where using it is survivable, and anyone encouraging an insider to come forward should say so plainly to them first. WHO IT SUITS: anyone deciding whether to report what an employer is doing to land, water or a community — and organisers whose records requests are being ignored. CAVEATS: ONE COUNTRY'S STATUTES AND ONE COUNTRY'S HOTLINE, THOUGH ITS CONTINENTAL STUDY COVERS TWELVE; THE PROTECTED DISCLOSURES ACT SHIELDS EMPLOYMENT-BASED DISCRIMINATION RATHER THAN PHYSICAL RISK; AND SOME MATERIAL CITED IS OLDER, SO CONFIRM THE HOTLINE IS RUNNING BEFORE RELYING ON IT. For legal accompaniment of whistleblowers in francophone Central Africa, the Republic of Congo entry.

trackers.name: Southern Africa Litigation Centre (SALC)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a regional litigation centre supporting and co-counselling cases across Angola, Botswana, DR Congo, Eswatini, Lesotho, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, South Africa, Tanzania, Zambia and Zimbabwe. Its socio-economic rights work challenges large-scale agricultural and extractive land use that dispossesses customary landholders without adequate consent, consultation or compensation, and covers mining, pollution and climate justice — live matters include a Zambian community's pollution claim against copper processors and San and Bayei claims to ancestral land in Botswana. WHO IT SUITS: in-country lawyers and community organisations who need a partner with regional capacity and resources; SALC generally works through local counsel and partners rather than taking clients directly. SALC RESOURCES A LAWYER — IT DOES NOT REPLACE ONE. It provides technical and monetary support to local and regional lawyers and organisations litigating human rights and rule of law cases, working primarily through strategic litigation and capacity-strengthening support to lawyers and grassroots organisations. So the ask is not ‘please take my case’ but ‘please back my lawyer’ — come with a local lawyer or local organisation. It also trains human rights lawyers and facilitates networks across the region, so it is a route to finding counsel too. THE SECOND FORUM MOST PEOPLE MISS: SALC supports litigation in South African courts that advances human rights in the southern African region — so where your own courts are slow, captured or hostile, there may be another venue, and SALC is the body that supports using it. NAME THE RIGHT CLUSTER WHEN YOU APPROACH: its themes are criminal justice, civil and political rights, socio-economic rights, international criminal justice, business and human rights and equality rights — ‘environment’ is not one of them, so frame a land-defence case as business and human rights or socio-economic rights. Established 2005 in Johannesburg out of the International Bar Association and OSISA. It has also run open calls for small organisational development grants to emerging CBOs in Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia, Malawi, Zambia and Zimbabwe — periodic, so watch for them.

trackers.name: Office of the Auditor General
trackers.desc: National — supreme audit institution of Eswatini. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Eswatini.

trackers.name: Anti-Corruption Commission (Eswatini)
trackers.desc: National anti-corruption body of Eswatini — investigates graft, financial crime and abuse of public office.

trackers.name: EswatiniLII
trackers.desc: Eswatini Legal Information Institute: free case law and legislation. · Find here: free Eswatini judgments and legislation (EswatiniLII / Laws.Africa).

trackers.name: Registrar of Companies (online.gov.sz)
trackers.desc: National — online company name search & registration, Registrar of Companies, Eswatini. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: SADC Protocol on Wildlife Conservation and Law Enforcement
trackers.desc: A REGIONAL TREATY WHOSE DEFINITIONS DO REAL WORK. The SADC Protocol on Wildlife Conservation and Law Enforcement (1999, in force 2003) defines ‘taking’ as hunting, killing, injuring, capturing, harassing, collecting, picking, uprooting, digging up, cutting, destruction and removal of any wildlife species. So clearing vegetation for a development is ‘taking’ under this definition, not merely site preparation — that reframing is the most useful thing here. It defines community based wildlife management as management by a community which has the right to manage the wildlife AND to receive the benefits from that management, giving a benefit-sharing argument a treaty source; and ‘conservation’ to include rehabilitation and restoration, so restoration sits inside the defined term. THE CROSS-BORDER HOOK: States Parties must cooperate to manage shared wildlife resources as well as any transfrontier effects of activities within their jurisdiction or control — a mine, dam or plantation whose effects cross a border engages a treaty duty on the state that authorised it. Article 4 objectives include enforcing wildlife laws within, between and among States Parties and facilitating community-based natural resources management. CHECK YOUR STATE HAS RATIFIED — the Protocol is legally binding only for countries that have signed and ratified it, and this entry does not assert that your state has. ON TFCAs: they encompass protected areas as well as multiple resource use areas, so they are not exclusion zones; a TFCA practitioners network founded September 2013 has membership open to all stakeholder groups. And SADC's own 2023–2033 TFCA programme names the marginalisation of communities living in and around protected areas as a problem it exists to address — quotable against the body that wrote it.

trackers.name: Yonge Nawe — the Eswatini environmental justice group that sued a minister to the highest court and won civil society a seat on the environment regulator
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an environmental action group founded in 1987, the Friends of the Earth member in Eswatini, working on environmental justice and getting local voices into environmental decisions. THE PRECEDENT IT SET IS THE REASON TO KNOW IT EXISTS: when the environment law was amended in 2002 it required a representative of an environmental NGO to sit on the management board of the national environment authority. The responsible minister ignored that provision and excluded NGOs. Yonge Nawe, then led by the environmental attorney Thuli Brilliance Makama, pressed the point and, when the minister refused to comply, took the minister to the country's highest court rather than let the disobedience become the precedent for every future minister — work for which Makama received the Goldman Environmental Prize in 2010. WHAT THAT MEANS FOR YOU: in Eswatini a civil society seat on the regulator exists in law and had to be litigated into existence, so ask who currently occupies the NGO seat on the authority's board, and take your project to that person. The authority itself has the statutory power to halt developments that have not been properly assessed for environmental impact. Yonge Nawe also works on industrial pollution of rivers and on land rehabilitation projects in communities, and shares a national radio slot with the environment authority and the national trust commission. WHO IT SUITS: Swazi communities facing pollution, land degradation or a development approved without proper assessment. CAVEATS: LEADERSHIP AND CONTACT DETAILS HAVE CHANGED OVER TIME — Makama has long since moved to international work, published email addresses in directories are old, and the website was not verified as live; confirm before relying on it. Eswatini is an absolute monarchy with narrow civic space, and most rural land is held under the King in trust, which shapes what any organisation there can do.

trackers.name: Swaziland Justice Forum — documents Eswatini's evictions, and the communities it works with took their case to the African Commission
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Swazi civil society organisation that documents forced evictions and names those responsible — it alleged that the royal sugar corporation was complicit in the illegal eviction of 33 farmers and their dependents from Vuvulane, following plans to take over the land, vest it in the royal wealth fund and lease it on to the corporation, and argues that the sugar industry has benefited the King and multinationals while displacing Swazi people from plantation land. WHY DOCUMENTATION IS THE ONLY FOUNDATION HERE: most land is Swazi Nation Land held in trust by the King and allocated through chiefs, with no formal legal security of tenure and no uniform official written record of allocations — so a household has nothing to produce when the bulldozers arrive. Recorded evictions include 61 people, more than 30 of them children, made homeless when armed police and bulldozers demolished homes at Embetseni in 2018; over 100 people from at least 20 homesteads cleared at Nokwane, where a 159-hectare science and technology park now stands; and about 106 people served notice by the national provident fund at Madonsa. THE ROUTE THAT WAS ACTUALLY USED WHEN DOMESTIC REMEDIES CLOSED: Swazi participants submitted a report documenting forced evictions to the African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights and engaged it at its 63rd Ordinary Session in Banjul in October 2018 — and then invited an ACHPR Commissioner to attend their own community meeting in Manzini in 2019. Bringing a regional Commissioner into the affected village is a move worth copying. The legal standard they invoke is that forced evictions may happen only as a last resort, under a court order, once all feasible alternatives are exhausted and procedural protections are in place. WHO IT SUITS: Swazi households and communities facing eviction from Swazi Nation Land, title-deed farms or plantation land. CAVEATS: NO VERIFIED WEBSITE FOR SJF WAS FOUND, so this entry carries no URL rather than pointing at a third party — approach through Swazi civil society networks or Eswatini's Yonge Nawe entry. For pro bono counsel before the African Commission, the IHRDA entry filed under The Gambia is the counsel; Eswatini is an absolute monarchy and the risks of publicity should be weighed.

trackers.name: Eswatini Legal Aid — opened 2023 at RHUS Office, Mbabane; advice, referrals and mediation now, representation NOT yet
trackers.desc: WHAT EXISTS NOW: Eswatini Legal Aid, the country's FIRST legal aid office, set up following the National Legal Aid Policy adopted by Cabinet in September 2022 and established at the RHUS Office in Mbabane, with technical support from the UN development programme to the justice ministry. THE ONE THING TO KNOW BEFORE YOU GO, STATED BY THE MINISTER HERSELF: services are being rolled out across four thematic areas — legal information and awareness; advice and referrals; mediation; and legal assistance including REPRESENTATION — but because legal aid is at the inception stage, services are provided INCREMENTALLY STARTING WITH THE FIRST THREE, WHICH DO NOT INCLUDE LEGAL REPRESENTATION. So this office will inform you, advise you, refer you and mediate for you; it will not yet stand up in court for you. Ask whether representation has since been added before relying on it for a hearing. THE EVIDENCE BEHIND IT, which is also the argument for using it: a 2022 legal aid needs survey found that 58 per cent of emaSwati cannot afford the services of a lawyer, and 90 per cent said they would use legal support if it were made accessible. The ministry identifies the barriers precisely — lack of money, inadequate awareness of how to access services, insufficient command of legal language, and LONG DISTANCES to service providers. The Legal Aid Bill process began in 2012 and stalled; the policy route was taken instead, and the country has faced a case backlog in the absence of legal aid except where capital punishment was in play. A FREE SOURCE OF THE LAW ITSELF: EswatiniLII, operated by the Judiciary, publishes the country's judgments and legislation free online — which matters where government printers charge per page. WHO IT SUITS: emaSwati who need to understand a land, eviction or inheritance problem, get a referral, or attempt mediation. CAVEATS: NO VERIFIED STANDALONE SITE — this entry points at the UN account of the launch; NO COURT REPRESENTATION at inception; and Eswatini is an absolute monarchy where most land is held by the King in trust, so a state office will not challenge an allocation. For forced evictions and the African Commission route, Eswatini's Swaziland Justice Forum entry; for environmental precedent, Yonge Nawe.

trackers.name: Eswatini Environment Fund — grants up to E300,000, open to COMMUNITY GROUPS AND INDIVIDUALS, with 80% required to go to direct environmental action
trackers.desc: WHERE TO APPLY FOR MONEY: the Eswatini Environment Fund (EEF), established under the ENVIRONMENT MANAGEMENT ACT 2002, administered by the Eswatini Environment Authority and approved by a Board of Trustees on the recommendation of a technical proposal selection committee, through an OPEN NATIONAL CALL FOR PROPOSALS covering all four administrative regions. THE TERMS, WHICH ARE UNUSUALLY OPEN: grants of UP TO E300,000; eligibility runs to community groups, non-governmental organisations, environmental organisations, INDIVIDUALS, and educational or research institutions based in Eswatini; and AT LEAST 80% OF THE FUNDING MUST GO TO DIRECT ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIONS. An 80% floor on direct action is the exact protection missing from the Gabonese and Congolese forest funds recorded in this file, where running costs were charged against the community's share — if your country's fund has no such rule, this is the clause to ask for. Priority areas: climate change adaptation, sustainable water and land management, waste management, and biodiversity conservation, with weight given to community participation and long-term impact. WHAT IT HAS ACTUALLY FUNDED, AND THE FAILURE THE AUTHORITY PUBLISHES ITSELF: the Luve wetland and donga rehabilitation project, run through a local NGO under a signed contract, with a corporate partner completing the fencing and adding E30,000; a waste project at Lobamba Inkhundla; and the first-ever grant in 2009 to the Langa project, where the earth dam was successfully protected but the spring later dried up. And the Sivule wetland protection project — 12 ha spanning the boundaries of THREE CHIEFDOMS — could not start despite several meetings, because of conflicts between the chiefdoms. Money does not resolve a boundary dispute between traditional authorities; settle who speaks for the land before you apply, or the grant will sit unspent. WHO IT SUITS: Eswatini community groups, individuals and NGOs with a wetland, land-degradation, water or biodiversity project. CAVEATS: A STATE-ADMINISTERED FUND under the environment authority — it funds environmental action, NOT litigation against a development or land purchase; calls are periodic with fixed deadlines, so confirm the current cycle. For litigation that stopped a mine, Eswatini's Yonge Nawe entry; for forced evictions and the African Commission route, the Swaziland Justice Forum; for advice and mediation, Eswatini Legal Aid.

trackers.name: Khonta on Swazi Nation Land and the Lubombo Conservancy — heritable family tenure through the chiefdom, and a community nature reserve sitting inside a 60,000 ha conservancy
trackers.desc: WHAT YOU HOLD ON SWAZI NATION LAND: access runs through KHONTA — individuals seeking Swazi Nation Land must obtain the approval of the structures associated with the LOCAL CHIEFTAINCY, and obtain USE RIGHTS to build on and cultivate; in exchange the household is expected to KUHLEHLA, render services to the chief's house and in his fields. THE TWO FACTS THAT MATTER MOST, AND THE SECOND IS BETTER NEWS THAN MOST OF THIS FILE: the land MAY PASS TO DESCENDANTS under Swazi customary law; and although chiefs retain powers to evict or re-allocate on evidence of crime or witchcraft, customary landholding rights and family tenure are described as STRONG AND SECURE, and IT IS RARE THAT A FAMILY IS EVICTED from a chiefdom. Heritable and rarely disturbed is a real tenure position — the risk in Eswatini is not usually the chief removing your family, it is a project arriving with authority above the chiefdom. WHAT THE CONTEST IS ACTUALLY ABOUT: research records the tension between chiefs and councils as NOT ONLY over allocation powers but over the REVENUE STREAMS attached — chiefs seeking KHONTA FEES, councils seeking plot and rates payments. Know which body is charging you for what; a demand for money is often a claim of jurisdiction in disguise. THE COLLECTIVE INSTRUMENT: the LUBOMBO CONSERVANCY joins FIVE areas totalling about 60,000 HECTARES — and it deliberately mixes tenure, comprising STATUTORILY PROCLAIMED PROTECTED AREAS, PRIVATE PROPERTY AND SWAZI NATION LAND together, including the SHEWULA COMMUNITY NATURE RESERVE alongside a royal national park, a private game reserve, a national trust reserve and a ranch. A conservancy that admits community land, private land and state reserves as equal members is the model to ask for: it lets a chiefdom sit at the same table as a private reserve without surrendering its land. Note also, as the neighbouring benchmark, that Eswatini's private reserves are PROCLAIMED AND GAZETTED IN LAW FOR PERPETUITY, carrying the highest levels of legal protection available, with land use PREDETERMINED BY LAW so it may not be used for anything but nature conservation. That perpetual gazettement is what a community should ask for over its own reserve — the instrument exists in Eswatini law and has been used for privately owned land. WHO IT SUITS: Swazi households on Nation Land, and chiefdoms considering a community reserve or conservancy membership. CAVEATS: USE RIGHTS UNDER A CHIEFDOM, NOT TITLE, in an absolute monarchy where most land is held by the King in trust; conservancy membership does not itself change tenure. For forced evictions and the African Commission route, Eswatini's Swaziland Justice Forum entry; for project grants up to E300,000, the Environment Fund entry; for litigation that stopped a mine, Yonge Nawe.

trackers.name: Eswatini National Trust Commission — the body that PROCLAIMS sites, with further sites already under investigation for proclamation, plus the authority that can halt an unscrutinised development
trackers.desc: THE BODY THAT CAN PROCLAIM YOUR SITE: the ESWATINI NATIONAL TRUST COMMISSION (ENTC, sntc.org.sz) is responsible for conservation of the Kingdom's natural AND CULTURAL heritage under the NATIONAL TRUST COMMISSION ACT NO. 9 OF 1972, amended by the King's Order in Council of 1973, and CARRIES OUT ITS MANDATE THROUGH PROCLAMATION AND MANAGEMENT of national parks and reserves, museums and MONUMENTS. It is an INDEPENDENT STATUTORY BODY and government parastatal under the tourism and environment ministry, with a BOARD OF COMMISSIONERS APPOINTED BY THE MINISTER, a Chief Executive and FOUR DIRECTORS — including one for NATURE CONSERVATION and one for CULTURAL HERITAGE; it is reachable on (+268) 2416 1489 / 1179, info@sntc.org.sz. THE OPENING, STATED IN ITS OWN RECORD: THREE SITES HAVE BEEN PROCLAIMED NATIONAL MONUMENTS AND A NUMBER OF FURTHER SITES ARE BEING INVESTIGATED WITH A VIEW TO FUTURE PROCLAMATION. Proclamation is an open, live process with sites currently under investigation — so a Swazi community with a grave site, a ruin, a sacred place or a rare habitat has a named body to petition, and CULTURAL heritage counts as much as natural. Write to the Director of Cultural Heritage as well as the Director of Nature Conservation; a cultural claim can protect ground that a biodiversity claim cannot. WHAT IT ALREADY HOLDS AND RUNS, which is what a community would be joining: MALOLOTJA NATURE RESERVE with the adjacent HAWANE DAM RESERVE, MLAWULA NATURE RESERVE with Magadzavane Lodge, MANTENGA NATURE RESERVE AND SWAZI CULTURAL VILLAGE, KING SOBHUZA II PARK and the NATIONAL MUSEUM, alongside environmental education and COMMUNITY OUTREACH PROGRAMMES; its funding is AN ANNUAL GOVERNMENT SUBVENTION AUGMENTED BY REVENUE FROM ITS OWN TOURISM AND HOSPITALITY OPERATIONS, and it has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Forestry Department. A conservation body that earns part of its own income is one that can act without waiting for a budget line. THE ENFORCER TO NAME ALONGSIDE IT: the ESWATINI ENVIRONMENT AUTHORITY (EEA), created by the Environment Act 1992 and made a corporate body by the ENVIRONMENT MANAGEMENT ACT 2002 — WHICH GIVES IT THE POWER TO HALT DEVELOPMENTS THAT HAVE NOT BEEN ADEQUATELY SCRUTINISED FOR THEIR ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT. Halting an unscrutinised development is a power somebody must be asked to use. Put the request in writing to the Authority, and copy the Commission if the site has heritage value. WHO IT SUITS: Swazi communities with a heritage, burial, sacred or high-biodiversity site, and anyone facing an unassessed development. CAVEATS: STATE AND PARASTATAL BODIES under a ministry — the independent route is separate. For the group that sued a minister, Eswatini's Yonge Nawe entry; for grants up to E300,000 open to communities, the Environment Fund entry; for heritable khonta tenure and the Lubombo Conservancy, the Swazi Nation Land entry; for advice since 2023, Eswatini Legal Aid.

trackers.name: CANGO and the briefcase-NGO test — Eswatini's NGO umbrella with named officers, the registration confusion it documents, and HUMARAS with a Mbabane address
trackers.desc: THE BRIEFCASE-NGO TEST, WHICH IS THE MOST USEFUL THING ANY COMMUNITY IN THIS FILE CAN CARRY: the COORDINATING ASSEMBLY OF NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS (CANGO) IS ESWATINI'S NGO UMBRELLA, WITH A NAMED DIRECTOR, A NAMED BOARD CHAIRPERSON AND A NAMED PROGRAMME OFFICER on the public record, AND IT HOLDS AN ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING THAT ITS MEMBER NGOs ATTEND. ITS DIRECTOR COINED THE TEST: THE ABSENCE OF A NATIONAL GOVERNING POLICY LEFT THE DOOR OPEN FOR WHAT WE CALL BRIEFCASE NGOs — THESE ARE NGOs IN NAME ONLY, WITH NO FIXED ADDRESSES, NO BOARDS AND NO STAFFS; THEY EXIST ONLY TO SQUEEZE MONEY OUT OF DONORS. Fixed address, a board, staff. Three questions, asked of anyone who offers to help your community or to raise money on its behalf. If the answer to any of them is no, you are dealing with what Eswatini's own NGO umbrella named a briefcase NGO — and that test works in every country in this file. WHAT CANGO WON, AFTER DECADES: THE GOVERNMENT PASSED GUIDELINES ON THE CREATION, REGISTRATION AND RUNNING OF NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS — with CANGO stating that IT VIEWS THIS STEP AS AN INDICATION THAT GOVERNMENT REGARDS NGOs AS EQUAL PARTNERS IN DEVELOPMENT, and its board chairperson saying the policy WILL ENSURE THAT THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN GOVERNMENT AND NGOs IS FORMALISED. CANGO had been working for a national NGO policy SINCE THE 1980s. Forty years of one umbrella body pushing for a registration policy, and it landed. When you are told a national framework is impossible, that is the counter-example — and note the argument that worked was formalising the relationship, not demanding independence. THE REGISTRATION PROBLEM IT DOCUMENTED, WHICH TELLS YOU WHAT TO ASK: TO BE AN NGO IN ESWATINI YOU MUST LEGALLY REGISTER, BUT SOME GROUPS ARE REGISTERING AS ASSOCIATIONS, SOME AS NONPROFIT ORGANISATIONS, AND SOME AS INDIVIDUALS — with CANGO warning that there had to be overall control SO NGOs CANNOT BE CLOSED AT THE WHIM OF THE HOME AFFAIRS MINISTER OF THE DAY. Ask under which form your association is registered, not merely whether it is. An organisation registered as an individual dies with that individual, and one registered without a governing framework can be closed by a minister. Get the form right at the start. CANGO also records the practical obstacle inside parliament: PARLIAMENTARIANS TOLD US PLAINLY THAT THEIR HANDS ARE TIED, AS THEY ARE ONLY MANDATED TO DISCUSS ISSUES THAT HAVE REACHED POLICY LEVEL, and that a new NGO Act developed with UN technical assistance WAS THROWN OUT BY THE ATTORNEY-GENERAL'S OFFICE — WE WERE TOLD IT WAS NOT OUR DUTY TO DEVELOP POLICIES. An MP who cannot act until something reaches policy level is not refusing you — they are telling you where the blockage is. Aim at the stage that unlocks them. ALSO NAMED, WITH CONTACTS: the SWAZILAND ASSOCIATION OF HUMAN RIGHTS (HUMARAS), P.O. Box 1546, MBABANE, telephone (268) 404 5610, with a published email, holding standing before the African human rights commission; and the TRADE UNION CONGRESS OF ESWATINI (TUCOSWA), the national trade union centre formed in 2012 from a federation founded in the 1970s that had around 40,000 members, based at Manzini. A national union congress is a membership body with legal standing and tens of thousands of members. In a small country where this file records civic space as constrained, a union that already has the right to meet is a room your question can be raised in. WHO IT SUITS: Eswatini community groups registering or checking a partner, and anyone needing a rights body or an organised membership. CAVEATS: SOME OF THIS RECORD IS HISTORICAL — confirm the current registration framework before you file. For the body that PROCLAIMS sites and holds three named reserves, Eswatini's ENTC entry, which also carries the authority's power to halt unscrutinised developments.

trackers.name: Team grants of US$15,000 rising to US$50,000 with no minimum education level required — three nationals of the project country, five years' experience or less, plus leadership training and an alumni network
trackers.desc: NO MINIMUM EDUCATION LEVEL REQUIRED — THAT PHRASE IS PUBLISHED IN THEIR OWN ELIGIBILITY, AND IT IS THE FIND. TEAMS FROM UNDERREPRESENTED GROUPS ARE STRONGLY ENCOURAGED TO APPLY. This file has just recorded two conservation funders that in practice require a postgraduate degree or audited accounts. Here neither applies. A ranger, a fisher, a herder or a village committee member with five years of work behind them is eligible on the same terms as a graduate — and almost no other conservation money in this file can be reached without a diploma or an institution. THE TEAM RULE: TEAMS MUST HAVE AT LEAST THREE MEMBERS, AND ALL TEAM MEMBERS MUST BE NATIONALS OF THE COUNTRY IN WHICH THE PROJECT WILL TAKE PLACE — ALTHOUGH ONE TEAM MEMBER CAN BE A NON-NATIONAL IF THIS IS CLEARLY JUSTIFIED. Three people, not one. That suits a community committee better than an individual fellowship does, and the money arrives to a group that already meets — which this file has repeatedly recorded as the difference between a project that survives and one that leaves with its founder. THE CAREER RULE, AND THE DEFINITION IS UNUSUALLY CAREFUL: ALL TEAM MEMBERS MUST BE EARLY IN THEIR CAREERS — NO MORE THAN FIVE YEARS OF PAID CONSERVATION EXPERIENCE EACH, EVIDENCED BY A DETAILED EMPLOYMENT HISTORY ON THE FORM. ACADEMIC PURSUITS SUCH AS A PhD DO NOT COUNT AS PAID EXPERIENCE. PAID experience. Years spent guarding a forest without a salary do not count against you, and study does not either. Read that carefully before assuming your people are too experienced. THE LADDER: UP TO US$15,000 FOR ONE YEAR AT ENTRY; UP TO US$25,000 IN A FOLLOW-UP AWARD FOR EXCEPTIONAL TEAMS ADDRESSING CONTINUING OBJECTIVES; AND UP TO US$50,000 IN A LEADERSHIP AWARD TO CONSOLIDATE THE WORK — GRANTS MADE IN A PROGRESSIVE ORDER SO SUCCESSFUL APPLICANTS AT ENTRY LEVEL CAN APPLY FOR CONTINUED FUNDING AT THE NEXT STAGE. Fifteen thousand to fifty thousand over three stages, for a team that need not hold a single degree between them. The entry step is the one to aim at; the rest follows delivery. WHAT THE PROJECT MUST BE ABOUT: PROTECTING SPECIES CATEGORISED AS GLOBALLY THREATENED OR DATA DEFICIENT, OR WHERE THERE IS INFORMATION INDICATING THE NEED FOR URGENT CONSERVATION ACTION — AND IT MAY ADDRESS THEMES SUCH AS CLIMATE IMPACT AND ADAPTATION, HABITAT RESTORATION AND/OR MANAGEMENT, SOCIAL DEVELOPMENT AND WELLBEING, INDIGENOUS COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION, AND/OR ENVIRONMENTAL POLICY. DATA DEFICIENT is the opening most communities miss. A species nobody has surveyed qualifies as readily as a famous endangered one — and the animals and plants around a village are very often in that category precisely because no one has looked. INDIGENOUS COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION and ENVIRONMENTAL POLICY are named themes, so the project need not be a pure wildlife count. THE PROJECT SHAPE: PROJECTS MUST BE NEWLY DEVELOPED AND RUN FOR 3 TO 12 MONTHS. NEWLY DEVELOPED — the opposite of the awards filed under São Tomé and Egypt, which fund proven work only. If your community has an idea rather than a track record, this is the door that fits. THE EXCLUSION TO CHECK BEFORE ASSEMBLING A TEAM: TEAM MEMBERS CANNOT BE EMPLOYEES OR CONTRACTORS OF THE THREE PARTNER ORGANISATIONS THAT RUN THE PROGRAMME. WHAT COMES WITH THE MONEY: LEADERSHIP TRAINING AND ONGOING PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT SUPPORT THROUGH A GLOBAL ALUMNI NETWORK, INCLUDING FUNDING, TRAINING AND MENTORSHIP — COMPREHENSIVE TRAINING IN THE BEST AND MOST EFFECTIVE TOOLS, TECHNIQUES AND STRATEGIES TO LEAD AND IMPLEMENT CONSERVATION ACTION IN THEIR RESPECTIVE SITES. THE ALUMNI NETWORK ITSELF DISBURSES FUNDING, not just contacts. So the first award is entry to a standing source rather than a single payment. THE STATED GOAL FOR THE PEOPLE FUNDED, WHICH IS WORTH QUOTING BACK IN AN APPLICATION: ALL TEAM MEMBERS SHOULD HAVE A DESIRE TO BE IMPACT MULTIPLIERS ACROSS THE CONSERVATION SECTOR, WITH THE ULTIMATE GOAL OF MITIGATING THREATS TO BIOLOGICAL DIVERSITY AND TRANSFERRING CAPACITIES TO LOCAL PEOPLE IN THE FIELD. TRANSFERRING CAPACITIES TO LOCAL PEOPLE is written into what they are funding you to do. A plan that trains twenty villagers scores better here than one that produces a report. WHAT THE WORK ITSELF INVOLVES: TEAMS CONDUCT SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH, ENCOURAGE AND PROMOTE PRO-CONSERVATION ATTITUDES AND DELIVER TANGIBLE RESULTS — COMBINING RESEARCH, ACTION, AND EDUCATION AND AWARENESS OF LOCAL STAKEHOLDERS. THE ADMINISTRATIVE FACTS: GRANTS ARE MADE IN ANNUAL CYCLES, APPLICATIONS ARE SUBMITTED ONLINE IN ENGLISH, AND GRANT GUIDELINES, AN APPLICATION FORM AND THE CALENDAR DEADLINE ARE ALL PUBLISHED. AND WHAT PAST WINNERS SAY IT DID BESIDES PAY: THE AWARDS NOT ONLY GAVE IMPORTANT PROJECT FUNDING, BUT ALSO RATIFIED THE CONSERVATION WORK BEING DONE, INFUSED THE TEAM WITH NEW ENTHUSIASM AND RENEWED SELF-BELIEF. RATIFIED is the word to notice. An outside body naming your work as conservation changes how a district officer, a chief and a ministry treat the same committee — and this file has recorded that recognition functioning as a form of protection. WHO IT SUITS: three or more young Africans from the same country, with or without formal education, wanting to start something on a threatened or unsurveyed species or habitat. CAVEATS: ENGLISH, ONLINE, ANNUAL CYCLE, AND THE PROJECT MUST BE NEW AND SPECIES-FOCUSED — not a fit for a long-running land campaign. For grants an individual can hold alone, Somalia's entry; for the award to a national leading a registered organisation, São Tomé's entry; for the cash award to the village group itself, Egypt's entry.

trackers.name: AgriCord — an alliance whose development agencies are governed by farmers' organisations rather than boards of donors — with published membership rules that a Senegalese farmers' body has already used to join as a full member, and 500+ partner organisations
trackers.desc: THE DEVELOPMENT AGENCIES ARE GOVERNED BY FARMERS — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S MAURITANIA ENTRY COVERS THE WEST AFRICAN PEASANT FEDERATION NAMED BELOW AS A PROGRAMME PARTNER, ITS MALI ENTRY THE EASTERN AND SOUTHERN FARMERS' FORUM, AND ITS SOUTH SUDAN ENTRY THE PRODUCER GRANTS FACILITY THIS ALLIANCE CO-MANAGES. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THEIR HOSTS IS SHIPPED. WHAT AN AGRI-AGENCY IS, AND IT IS THE FIND: AGRI-AGENCIES ARE GOVERNED BY FARMERS' AND OTHER RURAL PEOPLE'S ORGANISATIONS AND COOPERATIVES, AND FOCUS THEIR DEVELOPMENT WORK ON STRENGTHENING SIMILAR FARMERS' ORGANISATIONS AND COOPERATIVES ELSEWHERE — NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS FOR INTERNATIONAL DEVELOPMENT COOPERATION WITH STRUCTURAL LINKS TO THE FARMERS' ORGANISATIONS IN THEIR HOME COUNTRIES. The development agency is owned by farmers, and it exists to strengthen farmers' organisations. That is a different animal from an NGO with a rural programme: the people deciding its priorities hold land themselves, and the counterpart it deals with is your union rather than your ministry. This file has recorded again and again that whoever governs a funder determines what it will pay for. THE MEMBERSHIP OPENING, AND IT IS THE SECOND FIND: SINCE 2011, ORGANISATIONS FROM NON-OECD COUNTRIES HAVE ALSO JOINED THE ALLIANCE — ONE FROM THE ASIAN REGION, AND ONE FROM SENEGAL, THE AGRI-AGENCY FOR A LARGE GROUP OF SENEGALESE FARMERS' ORGANISATIONS. An African farmers' body sits as a full member of the alliance, not as a grantee of it. So the position of member is reachable — and a national federation that wants to stop receiving and start deciding has a precedent and a published route. THE MEMBERSHIP TEST, PUBLISHED: APPLYING ASSOCIATED ORGANISATIONS MUST HAVE THE LEGAL STATUTE OF A NON-PROFIT ORGANISATION, AND MUST HAVE A PROVEN RECORD OF CONCRETE INVOLVEMENT IN DEVELOPMENT COOPERATION ISSUES. Two conditions, both achievable over a few years. Compare the funder entries elsewhere here, where the ceiling for an African organisation is a grant. THE SCALE: SEVEN PROGRAMMES BRINGING TOGETHER 13 AGRI-AGENCY MEMBERS AND OVER 500 PARTNER ORGANISATIONS IN 31 COUNTRIES — OPERATING AS A NETWORK MANAGING A MULTI-DONOR ENVELOPE OF PROGRAMMES IMPLEMENTED BY AGRI-AGENCIES, FARMERS' ORGANISATIONS AND FARMER-LED COOPERATIVES. WHAT THE AGENCIES PROVIDE, WHICH IS THE THING NOBODY ELSE FUNDS: ORGANISATIONAL DEVELOPMENT FOR FARMERS' ORGANISATIONS — TO IMPROVE THEIR SERVICES TO FARMERS, TO RUN THEIR ECONOMIC BUSINESSES IN A MORE RESILIENT, EFFICIENT, SUSTAINABLE AND TRANSPARENT WAY, AND TO REPRESENT FARMERS' VOICES IN VALUE CHAINS AND WITH POLICY MAKERS — THROUGH ADVISORY SERVICES AND PROJECT MANAGEMENT RELATED BACKSTOPPING. BACKSTOPPING is the word to notice: somebody experienced standing behind your project manager when the reporting, the audit or the procurement goes wrong. That is what this file's DR Congo entry identifies as the gap that collapses community organisations between grants. THE EXCHANGE MECHANISM: THE AGRI-AGENCIES FACILITATE SOUTH-SOUTH AND NORTH-SOUTH FARMER TO FARMER AND FARMER ORGANISATION TO FARMER ORGANISATION EXCHANGES AND TWINNING ARRANGEMENTS. TWINNING — a standing relationship between your organisation and a comparable one abroad, rather than a single visit. Ask for that specifically; it survives staff changes on both sides. THE AFRICAN PROGRAMME AND ITS RESULT: A FARMERS' ORGANIZATIONS PROGRAMME RUN 2019 TO 2025 SUPPORTED 28 PROJECTS IN 12 AFRICAN COUNTRIES, REACHING TENS OF THOUSANDS OF PRODUCERS EACH YEAR AND STRENGTHENING FARMERS' ORGANIZATIONS INSTITUTIONALLY AND ECONOMICALLY — WITH A SUB-PROGRAMME OF 23 PROJECTS ACROSS SUB-SAHARAN AFRICA. THE NAMED AFRICAN REGIONAL PARTNERS, WHICH ARE A DIRECTORY IN THEMSELVES: AN EASTERN AFRICA FARMERS FEDERATION IN KENYA, A PAN-AFRICAN FARMERS ORGANISATION IN RWANDA, A CENTRAL AFRICAN PLATFORM IN CAMEROON, A WEST AFRICAN PEASANT NETWORK IN BURKINA FASO, A SOUTHERN AFRICAN CONFEDERATION OF AGRICULTURAL UNIONS IN SOUTH AFRICA, AND A TUNISIAN AGRICULTURAL UNION. Six regional farmer bodies covering the whole continent, each with an address. Whatever region you are in, one of those is the body your national organisation should already belong to — and this file's Mauritania entry describes the West African one from the inside. THE RESEARCH PROGRAMME AND ITS AFRICAN COUNTRIES: A FARMER-LED RESEARCH AND INNOVATION PROGRAMME COVERING BURKINA FASO, MALI, SENEGAL, CAMEROON, BURUNDI, THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO, MADAGASCAR AND TANZANIA — 13 PROJECTS IN 17 COUNTRIES, IMPLEMENTED BY 7 MEMBER AGENCIES WITH PARTNER FARMER ORGANISATIONS AT NATIONAL, SUBNATIONAL AND LOCAL LEVEL, WITH A LIST OF ACTION-RESEARCH PROJECTS AND DOWNLOADABLE FACTSHEETS. DOWNLOADABLE FACTSHEETS per project. Before designing your own trial, read what a farmers' organisation two countries away already tested and what it cost. THAT PROGRAMME'S THIRD AIM IS THE ONE TO QUOTE: INCREASE LOCAL FARMER KNOW-HOW TO APPLY AGROECOLOGICAL APPROACHES AND TO INNOVATE FOR SUSTAINABLE AND RESILIENT AGROECOLOGICAL AGRI-FOOD SYSTEMS — ALONGSIDE IMPROVING INFLUENCE OVER OTHER STAKEHOLDERS ON FARMER-LED ACTION RESEARCH. HOW RESULTS TRAVEL, WHICH IS THE DESIGN WORTH COPYING: THE RESULTS OF THESE PROJECTS WILL BE CAPITALISED THROUGH THE ADVOCACY WORK OF THE PARTNER REGIONAL FARMERS ORGANISATIONS. The research is fed to the regional farmer bodies to argue with, rather than to a journal. A finding that ends in a regional federation's policy submission has a route to a ministry; one that ends in a report does not. AND THE PUBLISHED REPOSITORY: A RESOURCE SPACE OF ARTICLES, BOOKS AND VIDEOS, MEANT AS A REPOSITORY FOR KNOW-HOW AND EXPERTISE IN SUPPORT OF FARMERS AND FARMER ORGANISATIONS EVERYWHERE. WHO IT SUITS: African farmers' organisations and cooperatives wanting organisational strengthening, twinning with a peer abroad, or eventually a seat as a member rather than a grantee. CAVEATS: PARTNERSHIPS RUN THROUGH MEMBER AGENCIES AND REGIONAL FARMER BODIES, NOT BY OPEN APPLICATION — join your regional federation first. For the West African peasant federation, Mauritania's entry; for the eastern and southern farmers' forum and its district structure, Mali's entry; for the grants paid straight to producer organisations, South Sudan's entry.

trackers.name: TrustLaw's legal marketplace (Thomson Reuters Foundation) — a free legal marketplace where law firms submit offers to take your matter — free membership on continuous intake, eligibility confirmed in 1–2 weeks, about a month to placement, and a regional hub in Nairobi
trackers.desc: LAWYERS BID FOR YOUR MATTER. ABOUT A MONTH, START TO FINISH — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S SÃO TOMÉ ENTRY COVERS THE CLEARINGHOUSE THAT CIRCULATES MATTERS TO 800 LAWYERS, ITS ERITREA ENTRY A BROKER WITH A FINITE-PROJECT TEST, ITS ETHIOPIA ENTRY SENIOR LAWYERS ON ATTORNEY-CLIENT TERMS, AND ITS TOGO ENTRY A SERVICE CARRYING 100+ COMMUNITY CASES. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. EARLIER ROUNDS LOGGED TRUST.ORG AS A SUBSTRING FALSE POSITIVE INSIDE WORLDLANDTRUST.ORG AND RAINFORESTTRUST.ORG; THE BUCKET CHECK HERE IS HOST-LEVEL AND EXACT, AND THE HOST IS GENUINELY FREE. THE PUBLISHED TIMELINE, WHICH IS THE FIND: ONCE YOU SUBMIT THE MEMBERSHIP APPLICATION, THE TEAM WILL CONTACT YOU IN THE FOLLOWING 1–2 WEEKS TO CONFIRM ELIGIBILITY; ONCE ACCEPTED, YOU SUBMIT YOUR LEGAL REQUEST ON THE PORTAL AND SCHEDULE A CALL WITH A LAWYER TO DISCUSS IT; FOLLOWING THE CALL, LEGAL MEMBERS SUBMIT OFFERS TO ASSIST YOU PRO BONO — AND ON AVERAGE IT TAKES AROUND 1 MONTH TO CONNECT YOU WITH A LEGAL TEAM. Four named steps and a stated duration. Almost every free legal route in this file ends at an email address with no indication of what happens next or how long to wait; a community can plan around a month, and can tell when something has gone wrong. THE BIDDING MODEL, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: ORGANIZATIONS APPLY FOR FREE MEMBERSHIP, EXPLAIN THEIR PROJECT AND SPECIFIC NEEDS, AND LAWYERS CAN VOLUNTEER TO WORK ON PROJECTS THAT INTEREST THEM — WITH LEGAL MEMBERS SUBMITTING OFFERS TO ASSIST. Firms compete to take the work, and more than one may offer. That means you may be choosing between lawyers rather than accepting whoever is available — ask each what they have done on land, extractives or environmental matters before picking. THE SCHEDULED CALL BEFORE PLACEMENT is worth preparing for: it is where the matter gets defined, and a vague description is what leaves a request unclaimed. THE SIZE OF THE NETWORK: A FREE SERVICE FOR BOTH LAW FIRMS AND NGOs, CONNECTING LAWYERS IN MORE THAN 175 COUNTRIES — MORE THAN 4,000 MEMBERS, INCLUDING OVER 800 LAW FIRMS AND IN-HOUSE LEGAL TEAMS BRINGING THE EXPERTISE OF AROUND 120,000 LAWYERS TO OVER 3,800 NGOs AND SOCIAL ENTERPRISES — WITH ANOTHER SOURCE PUTTING IT AT MORE THAN 900 FIRMS. IN-HOUSE LEGAL TEAMS as well as firms. A company's own lawyers volunteering is a different pool from private practice, and often carries commercial and contract expertise a community negotiating with a developer does not otherwise reach. THE STATED MISSION AND WHY IT MATTERS WHERE PRO BONO IS RARE: TO CONNECT PEOPLE AND SPREAD THE PRACTICE OF PRO BONO AROUND THE WORLD — PARTICULARLY TO COUNTRIES WHERE PRO BONO IS NOT TRADITIONALLY PRACTICED — AIMING TO IMPROVE THE OPERATIONAL EFFICIENCY OF NGOs AND GIVE THEM ACCESS TO THE POWER OF THE LAW WHICH CAN BE USED TO TACKLE SOCIAL PROBLEMS AT A FUNDAMENTAL LEVEL. COUNTRIES WHERE PRO BONO IS NOT TRADITIONALLY PRACTICED. In much of Africa there is no expectation that a firm gives free work; this network exists partly to build that habit, so an approach in a country with no pro bono culture is on-mission rather than hopeless. WHO IT SERVES: BOTH INTERNATIONAL AND LOCAL NGOs AND SOCIAL ENTERPRISES WITH THEIR DAY-TO-DAY LEGAL NEEDS. LOCAL is named, and SOCIAL ENTERPRISES too — so a community cooperative or producer company qualifies alongside a non-profit, which this file has recorded as a gap in most legal services. THE MATTERS IT HANDLES: LEGAL ISSUES RELATED TO DAILY OPERATIONS — USE OF IMAGES ON THE INTERNET, TRADEMARK REGISTRATION, EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENTS, COMPLIANCE WITH DATA PROTECTION REGULATIONS, TAX EXEMPTIONS, COLLABORATION AGREEMENTS AND LEGAL STRUCTURES — AND ALSO RESEARCH PROJECTS THAT CAN BE USEFUL TO FULFIL A SOCIAL MISSION AND BE USED AS A TOOL FOR ADVOCACY. RESEARCH USED AS A TOOL FOR ADVOCACY, named by the service itself. That is the opening for a comparative study of how other countries regulate the industry on your land — the sort of document that changes a ministry's position and that no community can pay for. COLLABORATION AGREEMENTS is the other one to use: the memorandum between your committee and an outside NGO is exactly what should be lawyered before it is signed. THE RESEARCH ARM STATED SEPARATELY: IT FACILITATES GROUND-BREAKING PRO BONO LEGAL RESEARCH AND DEVELOPS LEGAL BEST PRACTICE GUIDES FOR THE SOCIAL SECTOR. THE COUNTRY-LEVEL CONNECTION IT OFFERS: IT CAN HELP YOU BETTER UNDERSTAND YOUR SITUATION AND OPTIONS, AND POTENTIALLY CONNECT YOU WITH A SPECIALIZED ATTORNEY OR LEGAL FIRM IN YOUR COUNTRY, FOR FREE. A lawyer in your own country, not only an analysis from abroad. That is what the standing brief keeps asking for, and it is the specific thing to request at the call. THE AFRICAN PRESENCE: HEADQUARTERED IN LONDON WITH REGIONAL HUBS IN NEW YORK AND NAIROBI, KENYA. A Nairobi hub is a nearer contact and an African timezone. Write there first. THE PARTNERSHIP THAT WIDENS THE POOL: A PARTNERSHIP WITH A GLOBAL REFERRAL NETWORK OF 700+ MEMBER FIRMS ACROSS 205 COUNTRIES, EXTENDING REACH TO MORE THAN 1,500 OF THE WORLD'S LEADING LAW FIRMS — INTENDED TO ADDRESS THE GROWING GAP BETWEEN THE NEED FOR PRO BONO LEGAL ADVICE AND THE NUMBER OF FIRMS AVAILABLE TO PROVIDE IT. The gap is acknowledged by the people running the largest network. Demand exceeds supply, so a well-framed request that is easy to say yes to beats a sprawling one. AND THE SEPARATE MEDIA SERVICE: A LEGAL SERVICE FOR INDEPENDENT MEDIA OFFERING TAILORED SUPPORT TO EQUIP JOURNALISTS, NEWSROOMS AND MEDIA FREEDOM FOCUSED NON-PROFITS TO COUNTER LEGAL THREATS AND STRENGTHEN THEIR RESILIENCE. For the local reporter sued for covering a project — which this file has recorded as a standard tactic — there is a separate named service rather than the general queue. WHO IT SUITS: African community organisations, cooperatives and NGOs needing registration, contracts, tax status, agreements with partners, or comparative legal research — free. CAVEATS: OPERATIONAL AND RESEARCH WORK RATHER THAN COURT REPRESENTATION, MEMBERSHIP AND ELIGIBILITY MUST BE CONFIRMED FIRST, AND PLACEMENT DEPENDS ON A FIRM OFFERING — for representation, use the local routes. For the clearinghouse with a published opt-out on sharing your request, São Tomé's entry; for senior lawyers on attorney-client terms, Ethiopia's entry.

trackers.name: The Table Mountain Fund — an endowed African conservation trust fund whose published record includes purchasing conservation land outright — with grant ceilings and durations stated, micro-grants that are often an organisation's first ever funding, and unregistered bodies considered where well motivated
trackers.desc: AN ENDOWED FUND THAT HAS ALREADY SPENT ITS MONEY BUYING LAND — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S SÃO TOMÉ ENTRY COVERS THE EASEMENT TRUST THAT THIS FUND FINANCED, WITHOUT NAMING THIS FUND; ITS SOUTH SUDAN ENTRY THE BODY THAT BUYS FARMS; ITS SOUTH AFRICA BUCKET CARRIES A GREEN TRUST HOST AND A BIODIVERSITY INSTITUTE HOST AND NAME; ITS MAURITIUS ENTRY THE MARINE FUND NAMING OTHER EFFECTIVE AREA-BASED CONSERVATION MEASURES. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. WHAT THE MONEY HAS ACTUALLY BOUGHT, WHICH IS THE FIND: TO DATE THE FUND HAS INVESTED R116 MILLION IN OVER 380 PROJECTS, RANGING FROM PURCHASING IMPORTANT CONSERVATION LAND AND ENGAGING LANDOWNERS IN SUSTAINABLE LAND MANAGEMENT, TO FUNDING APPLIED RESEARCH, AND SUPPORTING CIVIL SOCIETY TO CARRY OUT INNOVATIVE CONSERVATION PROJECTS. PURCHASING IMPORTANT CONSERVATION LAND, listed first among the things the money has done. The standing question in this file is who pays for the parcel; here is an African fund whose own record says it has, 380 times over and on a published balance. WHAT KIND OF FUND IT IS: A CAPITAL CONSERVATION TRUST FUND ESTABLISHED IN 1998 WITH FUNDS FROM LOCAL AND INTERNATIONAL SOURCES — WHICH INITIATES, DEVELOPS AND PROVIDES SEED AND CATALYTIC FUNDING TO PROJECTS. A CAPITAL fund lives off its endowment rather than off annual donations, which is why it was still funding land purchases decades after it was set up. That is the structure to point at when arguing that a national conservation trust fund should exist in your own country — the money outlives the donor. THE MICRO-GRANT AND WHAT IT MEANS, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: IT SUPPORTS SMALL AND MICRO GRANT FACILITIES FOR CONSERVATION PROJECTS BEING IMPLEMENTED BY FLEDGLING COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS — AT TIMES THESE MICRO GRANTS REPRESENT THE FIRST FINANCIAL SUPPORT THESE ORGANISATIONS HAVE EVER RECEIVED, AND ALLOW THEM A WELL FACILITATED AND MENTORED INDUCTION EXPERIENCE. A first grant with mentoring attached. This file has recorded the first grant as the hardest one to get and the one that unlocks every subsequent application; a fund that treats being unfunded as the qualifying condition rather than a warning sign is rare. THE REGISTRATION DOOR IT LEAVES OPEN: REGISTERED ORGANISATIONS IN GOOD STANDING WITH A PROVEN TRACK RECORD ARE ENCOURAGED TO APPLY — BUT UNDER EXCEPTIONAL CIRCUMSTANCES AND WHERE WELL MOTIVATED FOR, ORGANISATIONS NOT YET REGISTERED AS NON-PROFITS MAY BE CONSIDERED. Not a waiver, but a written exception. An unregistered community organisation should apply and motivate rather than assume it is barred — and should say plainly why registration has not happened, which is usually cost or a stalled state process. THE PUBLISHED CEILINGS AND DURATIONS: A MAXIMUM GRANT OF R300,000 PER ANNUM FOR A MAXIMUM OF FOUR YEARS, THAT IS R1,200,000 IN TOTAL PER PROJECT, AGAINST A TOTAL PROGRAMME POOL OF R6,700,000 — AND FOR A RESEARCH CALL, A MAXIMUM OF R250,000 PER ANNUM FOR UP TO THREE YEARS. Four years is unusually long, and the pool size tells you the real odds: R6.7 million against a R1.2 million ceiling means a handful of projects, not dozens. THE PROGRAMME THE LAND WORK SITS IN: A PROGRAMME ENSURING PRIORITY NATURAL ECOSYSTEMS ARE HEALTHY AND RESILIENT, INCLUDING PROTECTION OF LAND AND THE APPROPRIATE MANAGEMENT THEREOF — WITH APPLICANTS ASKED FOR A TRACK RECORD IN BIODIVERSITY STEWARDSHIP AND/OR PROTECTED AREA EXPANSION. THE ELIGIBLE FUNDING CRITERIA IT PUBLISHES: THE ESTABLISHMENT OF PROTECTED AREAS OR OTHER EFFECTIVE AREA BASED CONSERVATION MEASURES — WITH GRANT SIZES IN BANDS UNDER US$5,000, US$5,001 TO 20,000 AND US$20,001 TO 50,000, COVERING FOREST AND WOODLANDS, FRESHWATER, MARINE AND COAST, WETLAND, AND WILDLIFE ECOSYSTEMS. OTHER EFFECTIVE AREA BASED CONSERVATION MEASURES is the category that lets community-governed land count without becoming a state park. Land held and run by the people on it can be funded under that heading. THE DELEGATED SMALL-GRANT MODEL, WITH ITS NUMBERS: ONE FACILITY WAS DESIGNED TO FINANCE UP TO 21 PROJECTS, EACH OF APPROXIMATELY R30,000, AVAILABLE TO COMMUNITIES AND LANDOWNERS OR LAND MANAGERS INCLUDING FIVE NAMED COMMUNITIES — ADMINISTERED BY A PROVINCIAL CONSERVATION AUTHORITY WITH SUPPORT FROM A CITY OVER THREE YEARS. The fund pays; the provincial authority runs the facility. Worth knowing because the application goes to the authority, not the fund — and a community's own conservation department may already be holding money like this without advertising it widely. HOW THAT FACILITY IS ACCESSED: ADVERTISED VIA A CALL FOR PROPOSALS ANNUALLY, WITH BENEFICIARIES APPLYING BY SUBMITTING A PROJECT PROPOSAL REVIEWED BY A COMMITTEE; ONCE APPROVED, THE AUTHORITY AND THE BENEFICIARY ENTER INTO A CONTRACTUAL AGREEMENT. Annual, so missing it costs a year. Ask the administering authority to put you on the notification list rather than watching for the advertisement. THE ENTRY IT IS TRYING TO CREATE: IT IS COMMITTED TO GROWING THE CONSERVATION COMMUNITY BY FACILITATING THE INCLUSION AND INVOLVEMENT OF NEW ENTRANTS — WITH A CAPACITY PROGRAMME TO ENABLE PREVIOUSLY DISADVANTAGED PERSONS TO BECOME CONSERVATION PROJECT MANAGERS AND LEADERS, INCLUDING ACADEMIC BURSARIES AND TWO-YEAR WORKPLACE PLACEMENTS. Bursaries plus a two-year placement, which is a route into paid conservation work rather than a training certificate. Read it beside the scholarship recorded in this file's Somalia entry. THE MIXED-TENURE LANDSCAPE IT WORKS IN: ONE PARTNERSHIP AREA COMPRISES PUBLIC, PRIVATE AND COMMUNAL LAND IN HIGHLY THREATENED, POORLY CONSERVED HABITAT — WITH AN AQUIFER SUPPLYING POTABLE WATER TO A MAJOR CITY, AND THE PRESERVATION OF CULTURAL IDENTITY, WATER SECURITY, NATURE-BASED LIVELIHOODS AND ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES NAMED AS PARTICULARLY IMPORTANT. An aquifer supplying a city's drinking water is the argument that moves a municipality. Where the land you are defending feeds a water supply, that connection is worth establishing early and in writing. AND THE THREATS IT NAMES: URBAN AND AGRICULTURAL EXPANSION, COMMERCIAL AFFORESTATION, THE AGGRESSIVE SPREAD OF INVASIVE PLANT SPECIES AND THE CONTINUAL THREAT OF TOO FREQUENT, UNCONTROLLED FIRES. WHO IT SUITS: organisations and communities in its region needing money to buy, protect or manage land — including first-time applicants and, on motivation, unregistered ones.
