In a region with almost no environmental litigation route, a standing judicial commission under a ratified convention is the most significant legal fact available — though this entry does not assert that individuals may petition it; establish who may seise it first. AN EVIDENCE SOURCE THAT NEEDS NO SITE ACCESS: ROPME's scientific bodies include a Remote Sensing Unit, alongside RIIS and MEMAC. WHICH PROTOCOL FITS YOUR ISSUE: oil-spill emergency response; land-based sources of pollution — the limb for a coastal development, discharge or reclamation; and transboundary movement of hazardous wastes. Development is named as a stressor in ROPME's own statement of purpose. At stake: over 20 species of dolphin and whale, all five subtropical turtle species, and more than 1,000 fish species, most endemic.

trackers.name: MBZ Species Conservation Fund — frame it as species work, not climate
trackers.desc: DO NOT DRESS A SPECIES PROJECT UP AS A CLIMATE PROJECT HERE — which is the opposite of the advice that fits almost every other fund in this map. The MBZ Fund was established on the basis that direct species conservation has lost out to wider concerns such as climate change, sustainability and poverty alleviation, and is now seen as a by-product of larger issues, leaving underfunded field biologists and wardens. It exists to correct that displacement, so frame the work as direct, field-based species conservation. A philanthropic endowment announced at the World Conservation Congress in Barcelona, October 2008, taking applications since March 2009; managing director Razan Khalifa Al Mubarak, also President of IUCN. By end-2010 it had disbursed just over US$5 million to about 380 projects in almost 100 countries; awards run up to US$25,000. TWO UNUSUAL ELIGIBILITY POINTS: it covers all animal, plant AND FUNGI species — fungi are named, which almost no other fund in this map does — and its focus includes data-deficient species, so you need not prove the species is threatened; where the problem is that nobody knows, that is itself a qualifying category. Individual conservationists may apply, and priority goes to projects supporting young conservationists. Funding is for direct conservation impact rather than administrative costs. HOW IT RUNS: three rounds a year, March, June and October; the Fund forwards recommendations to an independent body, so its staff are not the final decision-makers; and late submissions are automatically moved to the next round — missing a deadline costs a cycle, not the application. Apply online in English; the form requires a budget, references and permits, so have your permissions in order before applying. READ THE PROJECTS DATABASE FIRST — searchable by species, IUCN classification, continent and year, it shows what has been funded for comparable species in comparable places. NOTE: THIS FUND IS GLOBAL, NOT REGIONAL — it is recorded here because this country holds no other funding entry, not because Gulf applicants receive any preference.

trackers.name: Rufford Small Grants — Bahrain is named eligible, individuals can apply, and there is no deadline
trackers.desc: THIS IS THE FIRST RESOURCE RECORDED FOR BAHRAIN IN THIS MAP, AND IT IS OPEN TO A PERSON RATHER THAN AN ORGANISATION — which matters here more than anywhere, because searching this country produced no environmental organisation with a verifiable presence at all. Bahrain appears by name on the foundation's own eligibility page. THREE FEATURES SET IT APART FROM EVERY OTHER FUND IN THIS FILE. There are no deadlines — applications can be submitted at any time of year. Applicants are individuals and small groups, not necessarily registered bodies, with the focus on people early in a conservation career, current or recent MSc and PhD students in particular, though others may apply against the published criteria; undergraduates are not funded. And the eligibility test for species work is exact enough to check yourself before writing a word: the foundation considers work on any species NOT listed as Least Concern globally on the IUCN Red List, and also species not yet assessed but thought to be globally threatened. Look your species up first. Projects may equally focus on threatened habitats, human-wildlife conflict or community education rather than on a species at all. THE MONEY IS STAGED AND THE STAIRCASE IS THE POINT: a first grant up to £7,000, then a second, then a Booster and finally a Completion Grant, with the range running to about £18,000. Each stage requires the previous project to have been completed with updates and a final report, which are published on your own page on the foundation's site. That public record is itself an asset for a community group with no track record. THE CONSTRAINTS TO PLAN AROUND: one application in any twelve-month period, a twelve-month wait after a rejection before reapplying, and the foundation expects to provide between half and all of a project's cost — where it is not the only funder it requires evidence of the co-funding. It will not fund pure research with no obvious conservation benefit, nor expeditions the applicant must fundraise to join. The foundation is UK-registered; its global operation belongs elsewhere in this map and only its application to this country is recorded here.

trackers.name: Accountability Counsel — Bahrain is a named dark spot, and this is the body that files the complaint for you
trackers.desc: BAHRAIN IS NAMED IN THIS ORGANISATION'S RESEARCH AS AN ACCOUNTABILITY DARK SPOT — no community complaint has ever been submitted from the country to any development bank's accountability office. The organisation's own view is that this reflects inability or unwillingness to use the mechanism rather than an absence of harm. WHAT IT DOES: at the request of communities it assists people in using accountability offices to defend their rights and remedy harm caused by internationally financed projects, with support ranging from multi-year accompaniment through a complaint to a limited review of key documents. It is expert in the mechanisms of the World Bank Group, regional development banks, export credit agencies and OECD National Contact Points, and it trains communities on the options available while partnering with local lawyers so that the international complaint runs alongside a domestic strategy. ITS FREE PUBLIC DATABASE HOLDS EVERY COMMUNITY COMPLAINT EVER FILED TO EVERY ACCOUNTABILITY OFFICE, which lets you see how similar projects and the same lenders have been challenged elsewhere before you commit to anything. ESTABLISH THE FINANCING FIRST: whether an accountability office is available depends entirely on which institution is providing the money. Founded 2009 and having worked with communities in fifty countries. THIS MATTERS PARTICULARLY HERE BECAUSE BAHRAIN HAS BEEN ESTABLISHED ACROSS THREE ROUNDS OF THIS WORK AS HAVING NO INDEPENDENT ENVIRONMENTAL ORGANISATION AT ALL. Its other two entries in this map are a foreign grant portal and an intergovernmental heritage centre that serves states rather than communities. This is the first entry for Bahrain of a body that will act for a community on request.

trackers.name: Inclusive Development International — free tools to trace a project's financiers, and researchers who will do it on request
trackers.desc: THE FREE TOOLS ARE THE PLACE TO START BECAUSE THEY COST NOTHING AND NEED NOBODY'S PERMISSION: a shareholder tracker and a development bank investment tracker that map the investment chain behind a project and identify its investors and financiers. This organisation built them because the subscription financial databases its own researchers use are unaffordable for the communities that need them most. BEYOND THE TOOLS, IT TAKES REQUESTS FROM COMMUNITY ADVOCATES to research and map who is behind a project — banks, investors, insurers, development finance institutions, brands — using company reports, import data and shipping manifests, and returns a summary together with an analysis of pressure points and advocacy options. In high-potential cases it will help execute strategies; otherwise it refers to partners. THIS COMPLETES THE SEQUENCE FOR BAHRAIN. This file records that no community complaint has ever reached a lender's accountability office from this country, and that Bahrain has no independent environmental organisation. Identifying the financier is the step that turns those facts into a possible case. THE LIMIT: no work by this organisation in Bahrain or anywhere in this region could be established — its documented casework is in Southeast Asia, Africa and the Americas. The service is open to requests without a stated geographic restriction, so it is untested here. The tools, however, are usable by anyone immediately.

trackers.name: University of Bahrain, College of Science — published critiques of the country's own impact assessments
trackers.desc: ACADEMICS HERE HAVE PUBLISHED AN EVALUATION OF BAHRAIN'S ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT SYSTEM, AND A SEPARATE EVALUATION OF THE QUALITY OF THE ECOLOGICAL INPUT IN ITS EIA REPORTS. If scholars have documented in print that the assessments are weak, that is a citable objection to the assessment in front of you — far stronger than asserting it yourself, and this file has recorded across several countries that attacking the assessment is what actually works. THEY HAVE ALSO PUBLISHED THE CUMULATIVE IMPACTS OF RECLAMATION AND DREDGING ON MARINE ECOLOGY AND LAND USE, ASSESSED BY READING THE RECENT ASSESSMENT REPORTS TOGETHER and mapped with geographic information covering 1963 to 2008 — finding reclamation running at around 21 square kilometres a year over one decade, and adding some 118 square kilometres, about 17.7 per cent, to the national land area since the 1960s. Cumulative analysis is exactly what a project split into separate applications is designed to avoid, as this file recorded in Kazakhstan and Turkiye; here the cumulative work already exists for a whole country. AND THERE IS DIRECT EXPERIMENTAL EVIDENCE OF WHAT RECLAMATION DOES: organisms taken from a PROPOSED reclamation site were buried in the laboratory under sediment from the designated borrow area, and 41.8 per cent survived. An experiment using the actual site and the actual fill is the most specific harm evidence in this payload. THE HISTORICAL BASELINE EXISTS TOO: a satellite study mapped 312 sites and produced seventeen maps of marine habitats and coastal ecology INCLUDING AREAS RECOMMENDED FOR PROTECTION, with an accompanying volume, and a repeat survey was planned a decade later to measure change. Ask for both surveys; two dates make an argument that one cannot. Published work also covers seagrass beds and the fauna depending on them, and names the pressures precisely — reclamation, dredging, industrial effluents, domestic discharges and brine from desalination plants. Heavy metals have been measured in fish, oysters, snails and sediments, and a state marine monitoring programme has tracked priority metal contaminants since 2007. IT IS CURRENTLY RUNNING A MANGROVE ECOSYSTEM STUDY IN PARTNERSHIP WITH A UNITED NATIONS AGENCY, covering vegetation cover, biomass and carbon stock, water quality, soil and sediment properties, AND A SOCIO-ECONOMIC STUDY — with students placed in the fieldwork teams. THE LIMITS: a state university, working here alongside the national environment council, which is the regulator, and a bank. It will not campaign, and the route in is a named researcher and the published record rather than a request for help. Contact details for individual academics appear on the university domain in their published papers, which is the practical way to reach the person who wrote the study you need.

trackers.name: MBZ Species Conservation Fund — up to $25,000 to a person, for survey work and data gathering
trackers.desc: IT PAYS INDIVIDUALS AND COMMUNITIES, NOT ONLY ORGANISATIONS — which is what makes it usable here, since this file could verify no independent Bahraini environmental organisation and the country's other entries are foreign bodies, state portals and a university. THE MOST USEFUL THING IT FUNDS IS SURVEY WORK AND DATA GATHERING IN THE FIELD, alongside direct action, recovery management and training. That matters in a country where this payload has recorded reclamation adding roughly a sixth of the national land area and academics publishing on the weakness of the impact assessments — what is missing in such a dispute is usually current, site-specific evidence of what lives there, and this fund pays for exactly that. A grant of up to twenty-five thousand dollars to one person to survey a threatened species on a threatened site is a proportionate and achievable ask. IT WILL COVER STIPENDS, PER DIEMS AND PROJECT LIVING COSTS as part of the fieldwork, but not an organisation's overheads — the reverse of most funders, and suited to someone working without an institution. IT PREFERS SPECIES THAT ARE THREATENED BUT DO NOT NORMALLY RECEIVE ATTENTION, including plants, fungi and invertebrates — so intertidal and coastal invertebrates, the very organisms this country's published reclamation research concerns, are squarely within its interest. Maximum twenty-five thousand dollars, applications above that rejected; three review rounds a year through its own online system; continuation grants for completed and properly reported projects; grantee case studies published on its site, which are worth reading for this country before applying. THE LIMIT: it funds species conservation, not objection — and no casework of its own here could be established.

trackers.name: Professional Fishermen's Society — the people who lose the ground when the sea is filled in
trackers.desc: ITS OWN PRESIDENT DESCRIBES WHAT THESE SOCIETIES DO, AND IT IS EXACTLY WHAT A COMMUNITY LOSING GROUND NEEDS: CONVEYING THE FISHERMEN'S VOICE TO OFFICIAL BODIES, DEMANDING THEIR RIGHTS, AND PARTICIPATING IN FORMULATING POLICIES relating to fish wealth. In a country where this file could previously record no independent domestic organisation at all, a vocational society that speaks to ministries on behalf of its members is the closest thing to a body that represents people against a scheme. AND IT SPEAKS TO THE RIGHT HARM. Its secretary appeared on a national newspaper's programme on THE FISHING PROFESSION COLLAPSING BECAUSE OF SAND SUCTION IN THE COUNTRY'S SEA, describing environmental protection policies as neither serious nor strict and the marine and fish wealth of the country and the wider Gulf as deteriorating. This file recorded the science of that separately — published research on the cumulative impacts of reclamation and dredging, reclamation adding roughly a sixth of the national land area, and a burial experiment using sediment from a real borrow area in which fewer than half the organisms survived. The fishermen are the human side of that evidence, and a case that joins the two is far stronger than either alone. ITS POLICY ASKS SHOW WHERE IT WILL ENGAGE: stocking government artificial reef sites with juvenile fish, siting those reefs near the coastal areas where ARTIFICIAL ISLANDS HAVE BEEN CREATED, deterrent laws protecting juveniles, and shifting the closed season from the spawning period to the nursery period so that breeding females remain. A community objecting to reclamation can attach itself to demands a recognised body is already making. NOW THE WARNING, AND IT COMES FROM THE SAME PRESIDENT: SEVERAL SUCH SOCIETIES EXIST, AND HE SAYS THEIR STRENGTH IS MEASURED NOT BY THEIR NUMBER BUT BY CLOSENESS TO FISHERMEN, SINCERITY OF REPRESENTATION AND EFFECTIVENESS IN DEFENDING THEM — adding that what matters is which are accredited and trusted BY THE FISHING COMMUNITY ITSELF. Ask fishermen at the landing site which society actually represents them before relying on any of them. THE REGIONAL POINT IS WORTH CARRYING: the same collapse is described across the Gulf, and the society was asked publicly whether it would raise the matter REGIONALLY with neighbouring states where the profession still operates more freely. THE LIMITS: it is a vocational society working within fisheries policy, not an objector or a law practice, and nothing found shows it opposing a specific development. Its address here is its own public account rather than a website, though a domain under the same name appears to exist — verify it.

trackers.name: Bahrain Women's Association — its environmental programme is accredited to the UN environment programme
trackers.desc: IT IS A DOMESTIC MEMBERSHIP ASSOCIATION, AND ITS ENVIRONMENTAL PROGRAMME HOLDS ACCREDITATION STATUS FROM THE UNITED NATIONS ENVIRONMENT PROGRAMME. That accreditation is unusual for a national association of this size, and it matters practically: a body with standing at a United Nations programme can carry a concern into forums a community cannot reach, and its statements are harder to dismiss at home. THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING IN THIS MAP HAS BEEN A FISHERMEN'S SOCIETY, A UNIVERSITY AND STATE PORTALS. This is the second independent domestic organisation recorded here, and the first that a resident might join on the basis of who they are rather than what they do for a living. ITS ENVIRONMENTAL CITIZENSHIP PROGRAMME IS FRAMED AS RAISING AWARENESS OF HUMAN IMPACT AND OF THE CONSEQUENCES OF OUR ACTIONS, and it argues environmental protection as an individual and shared responsibility arising from self-motivation rather than instruction — the language of a body building a constituency, which is what a community needs alongside it. IT IS PRESENT INTERNATIONALLY: a member and environmental activist of the association took part in the global climate summit at the twenty-ninth session of the climate convention's conference of parties. A named person who has been in that room is a route out of a purely local argument. WHY THIS PARTICULAR BODY IS WORTH APPROACHING ON LAND QUESTIONS: this file has documented across the region that women are excluded from land decisions and stripped of claims by customary inheritance practice — recorded in Iraq, Palestine, Israel and Kyrgyzstan, and named in the land-rights pledges signed by bodies in Yemen and Kyrgyzstan. A women's association with an environmental mandate sits exactly at that intersection, and no other entry for this country does. THE LIMITS ARE PLAIN. Environment is one programme among several for this association, not its core purpose. Its stated method is awareness and citizenship rather than objection, and nothing found shows it opposing a development scheme, challenging a permit or taking a case. Use it to reach women in affected communities, to have a documented environmental concern raised by an accredited body, and for a route into international climate forums; take an objection to the free legal aid routes and the international accountability bodies recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: University of Bahrain Legal Clinic Centre — and it teaches administrative claims
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY HAD NO ROUTE TO A LAWYER IN THIS MAP. There is a LEGAL CLINIC CENTRE inside the national university's college of law, and it has run a clinical legal skills programme since October 2022 with around thirty-five students under the college's dean. ONE OF ITS WORKSHOP SUBJECTS IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST FOR A LAND DISPUTE: ADMINISTRATIVE CLAIMS — the category into which a challenge to a permit, a licence or an official decision falls. The programme also covers LEGAL CONSULTATIONS, legislative drafting, legal interpretation, drafting memoranda and judicial reports, practical court pleadings, labour claims, the new enforcement law, personal status, legal translation, and ARBITRATION AND MEDIATION. A law faculty teaching administrative litigation is a faculty that can explain how an official decision is contested here, which is the first thing a community needs and the hardest to find in this sub-region. BE CLEAR ABOUT WHAT IS AND IS NOT ESTABLISHED. The programme is documented as CLINICAL TRAINING FOR STUDENTS rather than as a public legal aid service; whether the centre accepts cases or enquiries from members of the public was not established. Ask that question first. The sister clinics recorded in this file for two neighbouring countries do take public cases, referring them to licensed lawyers with students working under supervision, so the model exists in the sub-region — but it should not be assumed here. WHY IT IS STILL WORTH THE APPROACH: this country's bar association was examined in this file and its objects found entirely member-facing, and no other legal route has been found in nine rounds of work on this country. A law college is also where an academic opinion on a contested administrative decision can be sought, which in a jurisdiction with few independent lawyers is sometimes the only written expert view available. NOTE FOR ANYONE APPLYING THIS MAP: the same university's college of law is separately recorded here for its published critique of this country's environmental impact assessment system and its cumulative analysis of reclamation — a DIFFERENT body at the SAME institution. Between them, one faculty holds the environmental critique and the administrative law teaching, which for a reclamation dispute is an unusually useful combination.

trackers.name: The waqf directorates — over three thousand endowed properties, and the founder's terms bind
trackers.desc: FIRST, CHECK WHETHER THE LAND YOU ARE DEFENDING IS ENDOWED, BECAUSE A GREAT DEAL OF THIS COUNTRY IS. On a minister's published figures the Sunni directorate holds 1,348 properties of which 783 ARE WAQF PROPERTIES rather than places of worship, and the Jaafari directorate holds 4,167 of which 2,651 ARE WAQF PROPERTIES — MORE THAN THREE THOUSAND FOUR HUNDRED ENDOWED PROPERTIES THAT ARE NOT MOSQUES, in a country of around 780 square kilometres. If a plot is waqf, the decision-maker is the endowment directorate and the terms of the original endowment, not a developer's offer. AND THE GOVERNING RULE FAVOURS WHOEVER WROTE THOSE TERMS: the guardian of a waqf must safeguard its assets AND FULFIL THE STIPULATIONS SET BY ITS FOUNDER, an obligation on which jurists agree unanimously. That is the lever. If an endowment was made for a garden, a well, a burial ground or the benefit of a particular quarter, that purpose is not a sentiment — it is a condition the administration is bound to honour, and departing from it can be challenged on the endowment's own terms rather than on planning grounds. A QUARTER OF ONE DIRECTORATE'S HOLDINGS SIT UNUSED, WHICH IS AN OPENING: of 783 Sunni properties offered for investment, 511 are in the directorate's hands — 290 invested or leased and 221 NOT INVESTED — with a 2021 study covering fifteen investment endowments totalling 34,675 square metres and seeking suitable investors. A directorate looking for uses for two hundred idle properties is a directorate that can be approached with a proposal, and this file has recorded in a neighbouring state that an endowment fund for environmental conservation was actually constituted there in 1994. THE REGISTER ITSELF EXISTS BECAUSE ENDOWMENTS WERE BEING LOST: a proclamation of 1927 required every waqf trustee to come forward and declare the palm groves and property in their hands, precisely because endowments were exposed to loss and dissipation. That history is worth citing: the registration system was created to stop endowed land disappearing, which is the same argument a community makes today. THE LIMITS. These are state directorates under the justice and Islamic affairs ministry, divided by sect, and the asset is administered rather than held by any community. Their stated purpose for idle property is INVESTMENT, so a conservation proposal must be framed to answer that. A community cannot endow land it does not own — the practical route is a sympathetic owner, or endowing money whose revenue serves a stated purpose. Ask the relevant directorate whether a specific plot is registered as waqf and on what conditions; that single question can change what a scheme is permitted to do with it.

trackers.name: e-Participation — it says the government integrates public opinion when planning projects
trackers.desc: THE SENTENCE TO QUOTE BACK IS PUBLISHED ON THE STATE'S OWN PORTAL: THE GOVERNMENT INTEGRATES PUBLIC OPINIONS WHEN PLANNING PROJECTS, AND TAKES CORRECTIVE ACTIONS IF NECESSARY. That is a commitment about PROJECTS, not merely about services, made by the government about itself — and this file has recorded throughout the region that an objection framed against a body's own published undertaking travels further than one framed as disagreement. THE POLLS PAGE INVITES OPINION ON PROJECTS AND INITIATIVES RELATED TO ECONOMIC, DEVELOPMENTAL AND SOCIAL AFFAIRS, and notes that many government entities run periodic consultations through their own websites — so the central page is an index, and the entity that would actually decide your matter is where to look next. AND OUTCOMES ARE PUBLISHED: the e-government authority posts the ACTIONS TAKEN after a consultation, thanking participants and stating what was done. Only two other systems in this entire survey publish what happened after a consultation, and being able to read them tells a community whether this process has ever changed anything. WHY IT MATTERS HERE PARTICULARLY: this country's listing in this map is a fishermen's society, a women's association, a university legal clinic, an endowment administration and foreign bodies. NONE OF THEM IS A CHANNEL INTO A DECISION BEFORE IT IS TAKEN. This is that channel, such as it is. THE LIMITS, PLAINLY. The consultations are largely about services and digital initiatives rather than land, the scope is whatever the entity chooses to ask about, and A DECISION ON A SPECIFIC RECLAMATION OR DEVELOPMENT WILL NOT APPEAR AS A POLL. Use it for the published commitment, for the index of which entities consult, and for the record that a view was submitted — and use the university law faculty's own critique of this country's impact assessment system, recorded separately here, for the substance.

trackers.name: Municipal councils — they must be asked in advance about the use of a public facility
trackers.desc: ONE OF THEIR LISTED COMPETENCES IS A PRE-DECISION RIGHT, AND IT IS THE MOST USEFUL LINE HERE: GIVING AN OPINION IN ADVANCE ON THE EXPLOITATION OF ANY PUBLIC FACILITY FALLING WITHIN THE MUNICIPALITY'S JURISDICTION. That turns a vague grievance into a checkable question — WAS THE COUNCIL ASKED, AND WHAT DID IT SAY? — and a scheme that took a public asset without the council's prior opinion has skipped a step that is written down. AND THE REST OF THE LIST NAMES THE COAST, WHICH IN THIS COUNTRY IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT. The councils work TO PROTECT THE ENVIRONMENT FROM POLLUTION in coordination with the environmental authorities; they DECIDE THE ESTABLISHMENT AND DEVELOPMENT OF PARKS AND PUBLIC RECREATION AREAS AND THE PROTECTION OF BEACHES FROM EROSION AND POLLUTION; they MONITOR THE IMPLEMENTATION of regulations on water, sewerage, lighting and other public utilities; and they propose roads, the rules governing their occupation, and the cleaning of streets, squares, public places and beaches. This file records for this country a university faculty's published critique of the environmental assessment of reclamation. BEACH EROSION AND COASTAL PROTECTION ARE NOT A CAMPAIGN THEME HERE — THEY ARE EXPRESSLY THE ELECTED COUNCIL'S BUSINESS. THEY ALSO PROPOSE MUNICIPAL FEES AND THEIR AMENDMENT, EXEMPTION, CANCELLATION AND METHOD OF COLLECTION, which matters where a charge is being used to price people out of a use they have always had. HOW TO USE THEM: identify the council covering your area and its elected members, put the matter to your member in writing with dates and the specific competence you say is engaged, and ask formally whether the council's prior opinion was sought on any public facility involved. Municipal councils here are old — the first dates from 1920 — and elected membership is part of the reform framework. THE LIMITS: they act within the state's general policy and development plans; most of their powers are to PROPOSE, MONITOR AND GIVE OPINIONS rather than to decide; and they sit inside the municipal structure rather than outside it. Pair them with the university law clinic and the appraisers recorded separately here — the council raises it, the others prove it.

trackers.name: Friends of the Environment Society — a youth website that became a registered society
trackers.desc: THE WAY IT CAME INTO EXISTENCE IS WORTH MORE TO A COMMUNITY THAN ANYTHING IT DOES. THREE YOUNG BAHRAINIS BUILT THE COUNTRY'S FIRST BILINGUAL ARABIC AND ENGLISH ENVIRONMENTAL AWARENESS WEBSITE, AND THAT INITIATIVE DEVELOPED INTO A DECLARED, REGISTERED SOCIETY. This payload's single most repeated finding across twenty-three countries is that people are blocked because they are not a legal person. HERE IS A DOCUMENTED CASE OF THE OPPOSITE: an informal project by three individuals, built in public, which turned into a registered body with an elected board. That is the route, and it happened in a Gulf state where this file has otherwise recorded only a women's association, a fishermen's society and a university faculty. IT IS MEMBER-RUN AND UNUSUALLY YOUNG: strong youth presence among its members, among its COMMITTEE CHAIRS and on its ELECTED BOARD — and it was THE FIRST NON-WOMEN'S SOCIETY IN THE COUNTRY TO BE CHAIRED BY A WOMAN. A body with elected committee chairs is one where, as this file recorded a round earlier, you write to the COMMITTEE that handles your subject rather than to the society in general — ask which committees exist before writing. ITS DECLARED OBJECTS ARE CONTRIBUTING TO THE COUNTRY'S ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION EFFORTS AND WORKING FOR POSITIVE CHANGE TOWARD PROTECTION OF THE ENVIRONMENT, with fixed core programmes in ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION AND AWARENESS. WHAT THAT MEANS PRACTICALLY: this is a body to bring evidence and a story to, and one whose bilingual habit means material it publishes is readable outside the country — which matters where the international accountability routes recorded separately in this file are the realistic ones. THE LIMITS, PLAINLY. ITS STATED CORE IS EDUCATION AND AWARENESS, NOT LEGAL DEFENCE, LAND HOLDING OR FUNDING, and nothing found shows it opposing a development scheme — the reclamation disputes this country is known for do not appear in what was reachable. AND THE ANCHOR IS A NATURE PORTAL'S PAGE ABOUT THE SOCIETY RATHER THAN A CONFIRMED SITE OF ITS OWN, so verify the current contact and whether it is still active before relying on it. Use it with the university law college's published critique of this country's impact assessment system, the elected municipal councils with their coastal competences, and the endowment directorates — all recorded separately here.

trackers.name: History and Archaeology Society — the record of what is buried where, and a journal that will publish it
trackers.desc: ARCHAEOLOGY IS ONE OF THE FEW GROUNDS THAT ACTUALLY STOPS CONSTRUCTION, AND ON THIS ISLAND THE COMPETITION IS DIRECT. The country's burial mounds are inscribed as WORLD HERITAGE — twenty-one archaeological sites, six cemeteries holding ELEVEN THOUSAND SEVEN HUNDRED AND SEVENTY-FOUR MOUNDS between them, and fifteen further sites with seventeen royal mounds, built between 2200 and 1750 BC. THE STATE'S OWN CULTURE AUTHORITY RECORDS THAT A LARGE ANCIENT SETTLEMENT EXISTED BEFORE THE RAPID URBAN DEVELOPMENT MOVEMENT FROM THE 1980s. THIS SOCIETY WAS FOUNDED IN 1953 AND IS ONE OF THE OLDEST SPECIALIST HISTORY AND ARCHAEOLOGY SOCIETIES IN THE REGION. It is independent and member-based, it runs lectures and research events, FIELD TRIPS TO HISTORICAL SITES and an annual cultural season, and it maintains A RESEARCH LIBRARY OPEN TO STUDENTS AND RESEARCHERS. That library is where the existing record of a particular locality is found — and the first question in any heritage argument is what has already been recorded on the ground in question. AND IT PUBLISHES A JOURNAL, ISSUED SINCE THE 1970s, CARRYING PEER-REVIEWED RESEARCH, FIELD STUDIES AND ARTICLES BY RESEARCHERS FROM INSIDE AND OUTSIDE THE COUNTRY. THAT IS THE PART TO USE. A community that finds mounds, foundations, sherds or a well on ground threatened by a scheme is not confined to complaining: THERE IS A PEER-REVIEWED VENUE IN WHICH A FIELD STUDY OF THAT GROUND CAN BE PUBLISHED, and a published, refereed record is a far harder thing for a developer or an authority to set aside than a residents' letter. THE SOCIETY ALSO STATES THAT IT CONTRIBUTES TO NATIONAL INITIATIVES TO PROTECT HERITAGE, so heritage protection is inside its declared work rather than outside it. WHAT TO ASK FOR, IN ORDER: whether the library or the journal already holds a record of your area; whether a field trip or a specialist visit could take in the site; and what would be required for a field study of it to be written up. Do not open by asking the society to oppose a project. THE LIMITS. IT IS A LEARNED SOCIETY, NOT A CAMPAIGNING BODY — it documents, publishes and educates, and nothing found shows it objecting to a development. Designation and protection decisions rest with the state culture authority, which is a separate body. Publication takes time, so a field study is a slow instrument, not an emergency one — begin it before the machines arrive rather than after. Use it with the elected municipal councils and their coastal competences, and with the university law faculty's published critique of impact assessment, both recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Judicial aid under the new advocacy law — the committee's decision IS the power of attorney, free of fees
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING HELD A UNIVERSITY LAW CLINIC AND AN INTERNATIONAL COMPLAINT BODY AND NO WAY TO OBTAIN A LAWYER. AN ADVOCACY LAW ISSUED IN 2026 CREATES A JUDICIAL AID COMMITTEE, AND ONE CLAUSE IN IT REMOVES A BARRIER THAT STOPS PEOPLE EVERYWHERE ELSE IN THIS FILE. THAT CLAUSE: THE COMMITTEE'S DECISION, ONCE APPROVED BY THE MINISTER, IS DEEMED TO BE THE POWER OF ATTORNEY GRANTED BY THE CLIENT TO THE PRACTISING LAWYER — AND IT IS NOT SUBJECT TO ANY FEES. In most countries in this payload a person granted a free lawyer must still produce, and pay for, a notarised authority before that lawyer can act; here the grant of aid IS the authority, and it costs nothing. For a household that cannot raise a notary's fee, that is the difference between having a lawyer and having a letter saying they qualify for one. WHAT THE LAW LEAVES TO A MINISTERIAL DECISION IS EXACTLY WHAT AN APPLICANT NEEDS, SO OBTAIN THAT DECISION BEFORE APPLYING: it fixes THE COMMITTEE'S WORKING SYSTEM, THE CASES IN WHICH JUDICIAL AID IS AVAILABLE, THE DOCUMENTS REQUIRED FOR AN APPLICATION, and THE MECHANISM FOR SELECTING THE LAWYERS WHO ARE ASSIGNED, their responsibility, how they carry out their work AND HOW THEY ARE FOLLOWED UP. ASK WHETHER PROPERTY, PLANNING AND ADMINISTRATIVE CASES ARE AMONG THE QUALIFYING CATEGORIES — that single question decides whether this route is open to a land dispute at all, and the answer sits in the decision rather than in the law. THE FOLLOW-UP PROVISION IS WORTH NOTING AGAINST WHAT THIS FILE FOUND NEXT DOOR. A neighbouring bar's aid scheme is delivered by trainees whose files the committee follows in form rather than substance; HERE THE SUPERVISION OF ASSIGNED LAWYERS IS EXPRESSLY PART OF WHAT THE MINISTER MUST REGULATE. That is a better design on paper, and paper is all that can be judged yet. AND THE PROFESSION IS DISCIPLINED UNDER THE SAME LAW: without prejudice to civil or criminal liability, a lawyer who breaches the law or the decisions issued under it, or the duties of the profession, or who does anything detracting from its honour, traditions or standing, faces disciplinary penalties. A lawyer assigned to you and neglecting your file is therefore answerable, and the complaint route is a disciplinary one. THE LIMITS, AND THE FIRST IS ABOUT AGE. THE LAW IS NEW, SO THE IMPLEMENTING DECISIONS MAY NOT YET BE ISSUED OR MAY BE UNTESTED — confirm what exists before relying on any of it. Registration of those qualified to practise is handled through the justice ministry's own service, which is where a lawyer's standing can be checked. A bar society exists but could not be verified beyond a social media presence, so it is not recorded here. And this is a state scheme; use it with the university law clinic already recorded for this country.

trackers.name: Palm protection and the farm register — the consent nobody asks for, and the record that proves your land is agricultural
trackers.desc: THERE IS A LAW FROM 1983 THAT PLACED THE PALM UNDER PROTECTION AND PRESERVATION IN THIS COUNTRY, AND THE PRACTICAL POINT ABOUT IT WAS MADE PLAINLY IN 2026: THE PROBLEM IS NOT THE RULE BUT THE CASES WHERE PALMS ARE REMOVED WITHOUT ANYONE REFERRING TO THE COMPETENT AUTHORITIES — which is how sites holding orchards and distinctive palm groves are lost. THAT MAKES A SINGLE QUESTION WORTH ASKING THE MOMENT MACHINERY ARRIVES NEAR PALMS: HAS THE COMPETENT AUTHORITY BEEN CONSULTED, AND WHAT DID IT SAY? Removal without that reference is the failure, and it is a documentary question rather than an argument about the merits of a project. Photograph the palms, dated, before anything happens; a grove that is gone cannot be assessed. SECOND, AND THIS IS THE RECORD MOST PEOPLE DO NOT KNOW EXISTS: THE PLANT WEALTH DIRECTORATE MAINTAINS A DATABASE OF FARMS, RECORDING 720 ACTIVE PRODUCING PRIVATE FARMS ON ARABLE LAND, THE MAJORITY CONCENTRATED IN THE NORTHERN GOVERNORATE, alongside six government farms used for research and trials. WHETHER A PLOT APPEARS IN THAT DATABASE AS AN ACTIVE PRODUCING FARM IS A FACT ON THE STATE'S OWN RECORD — and it is the kind of fact that answers a developer's claim that ground is idle. Ask whether your land is on it, and if it is not and should be, ask what registering it requires. THE CONTEXT EXPLAINS WHY THIS MATTERS MORE EVERY YEAR. THE NUMBER OF BAHRAINI FARMERS HAS BEEN REPORTED TO HAVE FALLEN FROM FIFTEEN THOUSAND TO ABOUT ONE THOUSAND, with groundwater depletion and urban encroachment among the named pressures, and public argument records land distributed to traders rather than farmers and left uncultivated for years. A country that has lost that share of its farmers has very little agricultural land left to lose, which is an argument to make in public. THERE IS ALSO STATE CAPACITY YOU CAN USE RATHER THAN FIGHT: an agricultural training centre has run courses for Bahraini farmers, for technical staff of ministries concerned with palms, and for citizens, with a programme of a dozen courses in a year. TRAINING IS THE CHEAPEST THING AN AUTHORITY CAN GIVE, and a community that has been trained in palm husbandry is a community with standing to speak about a grove. THE LIMITS, PLAINLY. THIS ENTRY RESTS ON NATIONAL PRESS REPORTING RATHER THAN THE AUTHORITY'S OWN PAGES, WHICH COULD NOT BE REACHED — verify the current law, the competent authority's name and the database before relying on any of it. The bodies concerned are government directorates, not allies. And a protection law for trees is not a protection for land: it constrains how a site is cleared, not whether it is developed.

trackers.name: Cooperative societies — the form that already invests in property here, and the farmer and fisher cooperatives that exist
trackers.desc: THE MINISTRY'S OWN ACCOUNT CONTAINS THE SENTENCE THAT MAKES THIS A LAND ROUTE: COOPERATIVE SOCIETIES HERE HAVE ACTIVITIES VARYING BETWEEN THE CONSUMER MARKET, THE MANAGEMENT OF FUEL STATIONS, AND REAL ESTATE INVESTMENT. Cooperatives in this country are not only shops — THEY ALREADY HOLD AND INVEST IN PROPERTY, which makes the cooperative the second vehicle available to a community that wants to hold ground, alongside the endowment recorded separately here. AND THE SECTOR IS OLD AND ORDINARY RATHER THAN EXOTIC. Cooperative work began in the 1970s with consumer societies that became A BASIC SOURCE OF FOOD SUPPLY FOR BAHRAINI FAMILIES — so established that the word for society came to mean any consumer market. A community proposing to form one is proposing something the country has done for fifty years. THE TYPES HAVE MULTIPLIED, AND TWO OF THEM MATTER DIRECTLY: THERE ARE COOPERATIVES SPECIFIC TO FARMERS, TO POULTRY BREEDERS AND TO FISHERMEN, alongside savings and lending societies operating inside a number of ministries. IF YOUR LAND PROBLEM IS AGRICULTURAL OR COASTAL, THERE IS ALREADY A COOPERATIVE FORM FOR PEOPLE LIKE YOU, and probably an existing society — ask which one covers your area before founding anything, because joining an established society with property and a bank account is faster than building one. WHAT THIS COMBINES WITH IS THE POINT. This file records for this country a farm register that shows whether a plot is an ACTIVE PRODUCING FARM, a palm protection rule requiring the authorities to be consulted before palms are removed, and endowment directorates holding thousands of endowed properties. A FARMERS' COOPERATIVE THAT CAN INVEST IN PROPERTY IS THE BODY THAT CAN ACT ON ALL THREE — it can hold the land, it appears on the register, and it can endow what it buys. WHAT TO ASK THE MINISTRY: which cooperatives exist in your governorate and of what type; what registration requires; whether an existing society's objects already permit property investment; and what supervision and reporting follow. The cooperatives section sits with the ministry responsible for social development, which is also where the register of societies is kept. THE LIMITS: cooperatives here are registered and supervised by a ministry, and the page reached is descriptive rather than a service guide — confirm the current law, the minimum membership and the registration steps before relying on any of it. Nothing found shows a Bahraini cooperative used to protect land from development; the property investment recorded is commercial. THE FORM IS AVAILABLE, THE PRECEDENT IS NOT.

trackers.name: National mangrove planting programme — put a protected habitat on the shore you are trying to keep
trackers.desc: FOUR GULF COUNTRIES IN THIS MAP HOLD SIXTY-NINE ENTRIES BETWEEN THEM AND NOT ONE OF THEM TELLS A COMMUNITY HOW TO PUT A HABITAT BACK. THIS IS THE LARGEST RESTORATION PROGRAMME IN THE REGION: launched in December 2024, IT HAD PLANTED MORE THAN 2.2 MILLION MANGROVE SEEDLINGS BY MID-2026, reported at 138 PER CENT OF ITS TARGET, with 1,622,844 planted by 2025 across five named coastal sites — a bay, two headlands, an offshore shoal and a second bay. It sits inside a national plan to plant 3.6 million trees. THE OPENING IS IN THE MINISTRY'S OWN LANGUAGE: IT SAYS IT WORKS THROUGH EFFECTIVE ENVIRONMENTAL POLICIES AND COMPREHENSIVE COMMUNITY INITIATIVES TO MULTIPLY THE NUMBERS OF MANGROVE TREES. Commentary on the programme goes further — that its success DEPENDS HEAVILY ON COMMUNITY AWARENESS AND ACTIVE PARTICIPATION and requires A GENUINE PARTNERSHIP BETWEEN THE STATE AND SOCIETY. A COMMUNITY ASKING TO HAVE ITS OWN SHORELINE PLANTED IS THEREFORE OFFERING THE STATE SOMETHING IT HAS PUBLICLY SAID IT NEEDS, not asking for a favour. AND THIS IS WHY IT BELONGS IN A MAP ABOUT STOPPING PROJECTS. MANGROVES PROTECT COASTS FROM EROSION, PURIFY WATER AND PROVIDE BREEDING HABITAT FOR FISH AND BIRDS. A stretch of shore that has been planted is no longer vacant coastal land awaiting a use — IT IS A FISH NURSERY AND A BIRD HABITAT, with a national programme's name attached to it and a count of seedlings recorded against it. That changes what the ground is before anyone proposes to fill it. THE PRECEDENT FROM NEXT DOOR SHOWS BOTH THE STAKES AND THE METHOD. In a neighbouring Gulf state the environment authority planted four thousand seedlings in a nature reserve, FROM SEED BROUGHT FROM SEVERAL GULF COUNTRIES AND PROPAGATED IN ITS OWN LABORATORIES — because the tree had existed there and WENT EXTINCT THROUGH URBAN EXPANSION. It has worked since 2018 with government and private bodies to rehabilitate the coastal environment. WHAT WAS LOST TO BUILDING WAS PUT BACK FROM A LABORATORY, WHICH MEANS THE ARGUMENT THAT A COAST IS ALREADY TOO DEGRADED TO MATTER IS ANSWERABLE. WHAT MAKES PLANTING FAIL, FROM PRACTITIONERS WHO HAVE WATCHED IT FAIL: choose a site that actually has the conditions for germination; STUDY THE TIDES BEFORE PLANTING SO THE CURRENTS DO NOT UPROOT THE SAPLINGS; watch for seagrass breaking young trees on the tide; and USE THE EXPERIENCE OF THE GOVERNMENT BODIES THAT HAVE ALREADY DONE THIS — the environment authority, the wildlife body and the fisheries side of the agriculture ministry. In the nursery, bright indirect light and warmth around twenty-five to thirty degrees, transplanting at ten to fifteen centimetres once a few true leaves have formed, into muddy saline intertidal ground. THE LIMITS: this is a state programme under royal patronage, so it plants where the state chooses and will not plant to block a scheme it supports. PLANTING DOES NOT BY ITSELF CONFER LEGAL PROTECTION — ask separately whether mangrove stands are protected in law here and what removing them requires, in the same way this file records that palms may not be removed without reference to the authorities. And badly sited planting fails and discredits the next attempt.

trackers.name: Regional defenders' centre — trial observation and emergency support, and this country is named in its remit
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING HOLDS A JUDICIAL AID COMMITTEE, A UNIVERSITY LEGAL CLINIC AND A COMPLAINTS ROUTE — AND NOTHING ABOUT WHAT HAPPENS TO PEOPLE WHO SPEAK PUBLICLY. THIS ORGANISATION NAMES THIS COUNTRY AMONG THE ELEVEN IT COVERS, AND IT FACILITATES EMERGENCY REQUESTS COVERING MEDICAL SUPPORT, TRAINING, SECURITY, TRIAL OBSERVATION AND EVACUATION. TRIAL OBSERVATION IS THE SERVICE TO ASK FOR BY NAME HERE. This file recorded separately that a new advocacy law creates a judicial aid committee whose decision itself serves as the power of attorney, with no fee — a good design. AN OBSERVER IN THE ROOM IS THE COMPLEMENT TO A FREE LAWYER: the lawyer argues the case, and the observer records how the hearing was actually conducted. IT SUPPORTS INDEPENDENT LAWYERS ALONGSIDE JOURNALISTS AND ONLINE ACTIVISTS, so the advocate who takes a land or environmental case is within its remit too — which is worth saying to a lawyer weighing whether to act. IT ALSO GIVES EMERGENCY GRANTS TO DEFENDERS AT RISK and capacity-building grants to civil society partners, works with United Nations and European protection mechanisms including A TEMPORARY RELOCATION PROGRAMME, and trains people to MANAGE THEIR OWN SECURITY — the part worth doing before anything has gone wrong. It publishes cases in English and Arabic and links people to international media and UN mechanisms. MAKE CONTACT EARLY. An organisation that already knows who you are can move in hours; one hearing your name for the first time after an arrest starts from nothing. THE LIMITS: its frame is freedom of expression, association and assembly — A PLANNING OR LAND DISPUTE REACHES IT ONLY WHEN SOMEONE IS DETAINED, PROSECUTED, THREATENED OR SILENCED OVER IT. It is based outside the country and publishes internationally, which is a consequential choice here; ask what it can do quietly before anything is published.

trackers.name: The licensed lawyers list — names and contacts published by the ministry, and how to check which court yours may enter
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING OFFERED A JUDICIAL AID COMMITTEE AND A UNIVERSITY LEGAL CLINIC AND NO WAY TO FIND OR CHECK A LAWYER. THE JUSTICE MINISTRY PUBLISHES A LIST OF LICENSED LAWYERS TOGETHER WITH THEIR CONTACT DETAILS, UPDATED IN JULY 2026, alongside a separate downloadable list of LAWYERS UNDER TRAINING. USE IT FOR VERIFICATION AS WELL AS FOR FINDING SOMEONE. If a person offering to act for you is not on the current list, that is the end of the conversation — and the list is republished, so check the date on the version you are reading. THE STRUCTURE OF THE PROFESSION DECIDES WHICH COURT YOUR CASE CAN REACH, AND THE FEES REVEAL IT: REGISTRATION COSTS 500 DINARS FOR THE TABLE OF LAWYERS LICENSED BEFORE THE COURT OF CASSATION, 300 FOR PRACTISING LAWYERS, AND 250 FOR LAWYERS UNDER TRAINING. A SEPARATE AND MORE EXPENSIVE LICENCE IS REQUIRED TO APPEAR BEFORE THE HIGHEST COURT. THIS FILE HAS NOW RECORDED THAT PATTERN IN THREE COUNTRIES: THE ROLL OR TABLE A LAWYER SITS ON DETERMINES WHICH COURTS THEY MAY ENTER. ASK BEFORE INSTRUCTING ANYONE, because a land case that ends up on final appeal cannot be carried there by an advocate who is not licensed for it, and discovering that at the appeal stage is a disaster. A NEW ADVOCACY LAW ISSUED IN 2026 ADDS TWO THINGS A CLIENT SHOULD KNOW. FIRST, A PRACTISING LAWYER MUST PRODUCE PROOF OF PRACTICE FOR THE TWO PRECEDING CONTINUOUS YEARS WHEN REQUIRED, AND IF HE CANNOT HE IS TREATED AS HAVING CEASED PRACTISING and may be transferred to the non-practising table. THAT IS A CONTINUOUS-ACTIVITY TEST — so a lawyer who has not worked recently may not be on the table you think, and the current list is the check. SECOND, AND THIS ANSWERS A COMMON EXPERIENCE: A LAWYER MAY EMPLOY BAHRAINI OR NON-BAHRAINI LEGAL PROFESSIONALS, BUT THEIR WORK IS LIMITED TO GIVING LEGAL ADVICE WITHOUT DIRECT CONTACT WITH CLIENTS EXCEPT IN THE PRESENCE OF A BAHRAINI LAWYER FROM THE OFFICE, and they must be registered in a ministry register. IF THE PERSON HANDLING YOUR CASE IS NOT THE LAWYER, THAT ARRANGEMENT IS REGULATED AND YOU ARE ENTITLED TO THE LAWYER BEING PRESENT — ask for it. ONE MORE PRACTICAL DETAIL: REGISTRATION PAPERS GO BY EMAIL TO THE REGISTRAR-GENERAL'S OFFICE AND A LAWYERS' REGISTRATION COMMITTEE MAY REQUIRE FURTHER DOCUMENTS — useful if you are querying someone's standing, because there is a named office that holds the record. THE LIMITS: this is a list and a licensing framework, NOT A REFERRAL SERVICE — it will not tell you who handles planning, land or environmental work, and this file has found no environmental legal practice in this country. Pair it with the judicial aid committee and the university clinic recorded separately here, and ask any candidate the four questions this file uses everywhere: which table, may I see the entry, where is the registered office, and is this consultation or representation.

trackers.name: Jabatan Audit (Audit Department)
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Brunei, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Brunei — Ministry of Finance & Economy (MoFE)
trackers.desc: National budget authority; MoFE (and its Treasury Department) prepares & executes the national budget, manages public finances & state stores and publishes the annual budget, Brunei Darussalam. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Brunei.

trackers.name: One Common Portal
trackers.desc: National — Registry of Companies and Business Names (ROCBN), Brunei. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Forest Act Cap. 46 — the inquiry stage is where you intervene
trackers.desc: THE RESERVATION PROCEDURE HAS A HEARING BUILT INTO IT. Chapter 46 runs: power to constitute reserved forests → notification of proposal → proclamation by the Director → inquiry by the Director → order by the Minister → notification declaring the reserved forest, published before it operates. The inquiry stage, between proclamation and the Minister's order, is where claims and objections are heard — that is the point at which an affected person intervenes. ‘Abandonment of proposal to reserve’ is a named outcome, so a proposal can lawfully be dropped. AND THE PROCESS ITSELF FREEZES ACTIVITY: new buildings and cultivation are prohibited after proclamation, before the designation is final — which cuts both ways depending on who wants to build. ONCE RESERVED: forests are classified restricted or non-restricted, entry into restricted forest is prohibited, and rights of entry may be suspended. PRIVILEGES ARE A DEFINED THING that can be granted, regulated, rescinded and modified — establish what privileges attach to your area and whether they have been altered — and they cannot be transferred. Subsidiary legislation provides privileges to natives of Brunei Darussalam, and requires no cutting without permission of the person having control of the land, use permits, licences for removing forest produce, and royalty. THE REVERSE POWER HAS A CATCH: forest may be declared no longer reserved — but the Minister must replace land that ceases to be reserved forest, so de-gazetting is not simply a subtraction.

trackers.name: Two different ‘protected’ Acts — and the six priority sites
trackers.desc: CHECK WHICH ACT SOMEONE MEANS. The Protected Areas and Protected Places Act (Cap. 147) is a security statute, not a conservation one: contravention carries 2 years' imprisonment and a $2,000 fine, and a person who fails to stop after being challenged 3 times by an authorised officer may be arrested by force. The 2004 Protected Places Order lists locations in a Schedule with plans deposited in the office of the Surveyor-General — which is where the plans are held either way. The conservation instrument is the Forest Act, Cap. 46. THE NUMBERS FOR AN ARGUMENT: forest reserves cover 235,519 ha, about 41 percent of land area, but only 17 percent of the country is officially protected — and marine protected areas remained at 0.2 percent in 2022, which is the stark gap. SIX SITES ARE IDENTIFIED AS MERITING PRIORITY ATTENTION AND CONTINUED PROTECTION: the inland forests of Ulu Temburong (Batu Apoi); the peat swamp forests of the Belait system (Ulu Mendaram); the mangroves of Brunei Bay; Tasek Merimbun; Bukit Batu-Sungei Ingei, contiguous with Gunung Mulu National Park in Sarawak; and the coastal kerangas forests. If your site is one of those six, that is a government-sourced argument. Existing protection: Ulu Temburong National Park, the first, since 1991, inside the 50,000 ha Batu Apoi reserve; three protected areas overall; and a proposed Bukit Teraja extension of 2,500 ha valued for connectivity, under the Heart of Borneo initiative.

trackers.name: No community grant window — the route is the national programme
trackers.desc: RECORDED HONESTLY: TWO ROUNDS OF SEARCHING FOUND NO DOMESTIC COMMUNITY GRANT SCHEME IN BRUNEI. Brunei is a high-income state rather than an aid recipient, GEF SGP does not cover it, and the funding architecture runs to governments and programmes, not to community applicants. So do not spend effort looking for an application window — frame a proposal as a contribution to a national programme. WHAT EXISTS: the Heart of Borneo Initiative, a voluntary transboundary cooperation with Indonesia and Malaysia, launched 27 March 2006 and declared in Bali on 12 February 2007 — signed for Brunei by the Minister of Industry and Primary Resources, not an environment ministry, which tells you where the file sits. It covers roughly 220,000 km² and provides ecological services for at least 11 million Borneans. THE ASIAN DEVELOPMENT BANK IS LEAD AGENCY FOR MOBILISING FINANCE, and the HoB project includes ‘pilot schemes for local communities to be paid for ecosystem services’ — the single community-facing element in the whole architecture. If you seek payment for conserving land, ask whether a PES pilot exists under HoB and who administers it; the answer routes through government agencies. DOMESTICALLY, the National Forestry Policy expressly recognises the role of local communities in forest management, and the Forestry Department — which also chairs the National CITES Scientific Authority — delivered 11 forest recreation parks by 1998 under the 6th National Development Plan. WATCH THE SOURCE: Heart of Borneo searches return Sarawak (Malaysian) government pages first, and Brunei's own HoB page has been archived since 2012.

trackers.name: Tender Board e-Tendering
trackers.desc: National public-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Oman, and for how much.

trackers.name: Invest Easy – Commercial Registrations
trackers.desc: National — public search of Oman’s commercial register (Oman Business Platform). — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Oman Data Portal
trackers.desc: National — official government open data / budget portal. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this is the broad budget/open-data hub for how money is allocated overall — for the specific firms winning tenders use the procurement portal, and for findings of misspending use the supreme audit institution. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Oman.

trackers.name: State Audit Institution
trackers.desc: National — supreme audit institution of Oman. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Oman.

trackers.name: Supreme Judicial Council (Oman)
trackers.desc: Body overseeing Oman's courts and Supreme Court (the apex cassation-level court), with judicial information. · Find here: Oman's Supreme Judicial Council — administration and oversight of the courts.

trackers.name: Kuwait Regional Convention (ROPME) — and its Judicial Commission
trackers.desc: THE ONE BINDING ENVIRONMENTAL INSTRUMENT COVERING ALL EIGHT GULF STATES. The Kuwait Regional Convention for Cooperation on the Protection of the Marine Environment from Pollution was signed 24 April 1978 and entered into force 1 July 1979 — 30 articles, described as the basic legal instrument binding the eight States of the Region. ALL EIGHT ARE FULL PARTIES: ROPME records ‘no signatories without ratification, acceptance, approval or accession’, so unlike some regional instruments there is no signed-but-unratified state to argue about. ARTICLE II fixes the Sea Area by coordinates, from Ras Dharbat Ali (16°39'N, 53°3'30"E) to Ras Al Fasteh (25°04'N, 61°25'E) — a treaty boundary you can check a project location against. Use the term ‘ROPME Sea Area’: it was coined by the Plenipotentiaries to achieve unanimity, cooperating in spite of existing geopolitical boundaries, and it is the name all eight accepted. THE ORGAN MOST PEOPLE DO NOT KNOW EXISTS: alongside the Council and Secretariat, ROPME has a Judicial Commission, established March 1989, of 6 nationals of Member States highly qualified in international law. In a region with almost no environmental litigation route, a standing judicial commission under a ratified convention is the most significant legal fact available — though this entry does not assert that individuals may petition it; establish who may seise it first. AN EVIDENCE SOURCE THAT NEEDS NO SITE ACCESS: ROPME's scientific bodies include a Remote Sensing Unit, alongside RIIS and MEMAC. WHICH PROTOCOL FITS YOUR ISSUE: oil-spill emergency response; land-based sources of pollution — the limb for a coastal development, discharge or reclamation; and transboundary movement of hazardous wastes. Development is named as a stressor in ROPME's own statement of purpose. At stake: over 20 species of dolphin and whale, all five subtropical turtle species, and more than 1,000 fish species, most endemic.

trackers.name: MBZ Species Conservation Fund — frame it as species work, not climate
trackers.desc: DO NOT DRESS A SPECIES PROJECT UP AS A CLIMATE PROJECT HERE — which is the opposite of the advice that fits almost every other fund in this map. The MBZ Fund was established on the basis that direct species conservation has lost out to wider concerns such as climate change, sustainability and poverty alleviation, and is now seen as a by-product of larger issues, leaving underfunded field biologists and wardens. It exists to correct that displacement, so frame the work as direct, field-based species conservation. A philanthropic endowment announced at the World Conservation Congress in Barcelona, October 2008, taking applications since March 2009; managing director Razan Khalifa Al Mubarak, also President of IUCN. By end-2010 it had disbursed just over US$5 million to about 380 projects in almost 100 countries; awards run up to US$25,000. TWO UNUSUAL ELIGIBILITY POINTS: it covers all animal, plant AND FUNGI species — fungi are named, which almost no other fund in this map does — and its focus includes data-deficient species, so you need not prove the species is threatened; where the problem is that nobody knows, that is itself a qualifying category. Individual conservationists may apply, and priority goes to projects supporting young conservationists. Funding is for direct conservation impact rather than administrative costs. HOW IT RUNS: three rounds a year, March, June and October; the Fund forwards recommendations to an independent body, so its staff are not the final decision-makers; and late submissions are automatically moved to the next round — missing a deadline costs a cycle, not the application. Apply online in English; the form requires a budget, references and permits, so have your permissions in order before applying. READ THE PROJECTS DATABASE FIRST — searchable by species, IUCN classification, continent and year, it shows what has been funded for comparable species in comparable places. NOTE: THIS FUND IS GLOBAL, NOT REGIONAL — it is recorded here because this country holds no other funding entry, not because Gulf applicants receive any preference.

trackers.name: Environment Society of Oman — by its own account the only environmental non-profit in the country, and listed in the regulator's own directory
trackers.desc: ESO DESCRIBES ITSELF AS THE ONLY NON-PROFIT ORGANISATION IN OMAN THAT FOCUSES ON CONSERVING THE ENVIRONMENT. For a resident facing a development, that sentence is the whole strategic picture: there is no second organisation to fall back on, and no Omani land trust or public-interest environmental firm was found. WHY IT STILL HAS WEIGHT: ESO appears in the Environment Authority's own online directory of environment-interested groups, and it has been an IUCN member since February 2009 — so a submission carrying ESO's name is not an outsider's letter. MEMBERSHIP IS THE ACCESS ROUTE AND IT IS GENUINELY OPEN: anyone over 18 with an interest may join, and the base has passed 500 individual members alongside corporate members, with an elected board serving two-year terms drawn from Oman's scientific, conservation and business communities and from different regions. Contact admin@eso.org.om, +968 9985 5108, based in Ruwi. Founded March 2004. WHAT YOU CANNOT GET HERE, AND IT IS MOST OF WHAT A LAND DEFENCE NEEDS: ESO does not litigate, does not buy or hold land, and runs no community grant window. Its published strengths are research on threatened and endangered species, education, awareness and advocacy, with a long-running marine emphasis — cetacean and turtle work, and a national strandings database. The realistic use is therefore evidentiary and reputational: commission or obtain species and habitat evidence for the site, and get a recognised conservation body's name attached to it, then take that to the Environment Authority yourself. Treat the absence of any litigating or land-holding body in Oman as a finding to plan around rather than a gap in this file.

trackers.name: BirdLife Hima Fund — Oman is one of four named grant recipients, and this is the country's only funding route found
trackers.desc: THIS IS THE ONLY GRANT WINDOW THIS FILE HAS FOUND FOR OMAN, AND OMAN IS ONE OF ONLY FOUR COUNTRIES BIRDLIFE NAMES AS HAVING RECEIVED ONE. BirdLife records that the Hima Fund launched in 2011 with four approved grants to Partners in Jordan, Lebanon, Qatar and Oman, to reinforce or revitalise Himas at four sites. The fund was established in Qatar in 2008 with a one million dollar donation from Sheikha Jawaher Bint Hamad Bin Suhaim Al-Thani, aimed at conserving Important Bird Areas and their threatened species in the Middle East. That matters here because the Oman entry already in this file records a country with no land trust, no public-interest environmental law practice and no community grant window — this is the single documented exception, and it is bird-habitat specific. THE ROUTE: grants go to BirdLife Partners rather than direct to communities, so the application is carried by the national partner organisation; this entry does not name Oman's BirdLife Partner because that was not verified during this round, and the Environment Society of Oman recorded in this file is the obvious body to ask. FRAME THE SITE AS A HIMA: the Hima is a traditional designation under which a defined community controls access and use and may forbid hunting, wood cutting and the destruction of trees and shrubs — which is a far better fit for Omani rangeland than a purchase model. CAVEAT, AND IT IS A SERIOUS ONE: no evidence of grant-making after the early 2010s was found. Treat the fund as documented in its founding and unverified in its current operation. ANTI-FANOUT NOTE: press reporting names twelve countries in the fund's remit; BirdLife's own page names four grant recipients, and this entry exists in those four only.

trackers.name: Oman's electronic waqf system — the auction page tells you which endowment land is going to a developer, and the register tells you if its boundaries just moved
trackers.desc: THIS IS THE BEST EARLY-WARNING SOURCE FOUND ANYWHERE IN THIS REGION, AND IT IS OPEN TO ANYONE: the Ministry of Awqaf and Religious Affairs runs a searchable page of endowment properties put up for auction, and bidding is registered through this same system. Watch it. In June 2026 the ministry offered a set of endowment assets for investment under its Tathmeer project for multi-use plots, land and assets spread across a number of wilayats, with the Wilayat of Sohar alone carrying several separate investment opportunities and independent auctions. The practice is long-standing rather than new — as far back as 2017 the ministry, through its department for the development of endowment funds, advertised open competitive tendering for well-located land plots across the governorates. ENDOWMENT STATUS IS NOT PROTECTION FROM DEVELOPMENT IN OMAN; IT IS A DIFFERENT ROUTE INTO IT. THE SECOND THING TO DO IS READ THE REGISTER ENTRY FOR THE PARCEL. The system holds per-parcel records carrying the property description, its classification as waqf or bayt al-mal, the supervising administrative body, the endower's details, the named agents with civil numbers — and a dated change history recording entries such as the waqf boundaries having been amended, with the name of the person who made the change and the timestamp. A boundary moved shortly before a scheme appears is impossible to prove later and trivial to spot now. Records go down to individual holdings, one covering four commercial shops belonging to a mosque's endowments within a named plan in the Wilayat of Izki. HOW THE DEVELOPMENT ITSELF IS STRUCTURED, WHICH TELLS YOU WHAT TO ARGUE ABOUT: on a summary published by an Omani law firm rather than by the ministry, and so to be checked before it is relied on, investment on vacant endowment land not attached to a mosque may take the form of an investor constructing apartments and shops, assigning the yield of one or more of them to the endowment or paying a monthly ground rent, keeping the use of the rest for the contract term — with ownership of the buildings passing to the endowment when the term ends. The endowment's interest is therefore in the building being built, which is worth knowing before assuming the ministry shares your objection. Investment is stated to follow feasibility studies by a specialised expert body. THE ROUTE THAT RUNS THE OTHER WAY, AND IT IS THE MOST ACCESSIBLE IN THE REGION: the endowment-share scheme accepts in-kind participation expressly including commercial, residential, industrial and agricultural buildings and land, alongside cash, at whatever scale a person can manage, through the same electronic system; the ministry states that what reaches a project's accounts becomes an endowment asset that is not spent but invested, with only its proceeds disbursed. That endowment property sits in the path of infrastructure is visible on the system's own front page, which has carried an appeal for a mosque affected by the Batinah Coastal Line project. A separate mosques system on the same ministry domain publishes a mosques map. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: no enforcement route against misuse of endowment land was found, unlike Türkiye where the civil administration evicts on the directorate's request, and no consent gate on expropriation of the kind Jordan's Awqaf Council provides. Use this as an auction watch, a register and a dedication route, and ask the ministry directly what happens when endowment land is taken or misused.

trackers.name: Rufford Small Grants — Oman is named eligible, and an individual can apply where the country has almost no organisations
trackers.desc: OMAN APPEARS BY NAME ON THE FOUNDATION'S OWN ELIGIBILITY LIST, AND THE APPLICANT CAN BE A PERSON RATHER THAN AN ORGANISATION — which matters here because this file has established that Oman has essentially one independent environmental non-profit, which describes itself as the only one in the country. Where there is no organisation to join, a fund that takes applications from individuals is the difference between doing the work and not. NO DEADLINES: applications are accepted at any time of year. The focus is people early in a conservation career, particularly current or recent MSc and PhD students, with others considered against the published criteria; undergraduates are not funded. THE SPECIES TEST IS EXACT AND CHECKABLE BEFORE YOU WRITE: any species not listed as Least Concern globally on the IUCN Red List qualifies, as do species not yet assessed but thought to be globally threatened. Habitat, human-wildlife conflict and community education projects qualify without a species focus — which suits wadi, coastal and mountain habitat questions. FUNDING IS STAGED: up to £7,000 for a first grant, then a second, a Booster and a Completion Grant, running to roughly £18,000, each conditional on completing and reporting the last, with reports published on the applicant's own page. One application in any twelve months; twelve months' wait after a rejection; the foundation expects to fund between half and all of a project and requires evidence of co-funding where others contribute; it will not support pure research without conservation benefit or expeditions requiring the applicant to fundraise to take part. Pair with the environment society already recorded here, and note that Oman's electronic waqf system lets you check whether the land in question is endowment land before designing any project on it.

trackers.name: Accountability Counsel — Oman is a named dark spot, and it partners with local lawyers rather than replacing them
trackers.desc: OMAN IS NAMED AS AN ACCOUNTABILITY DARK SPOT IN THIS ORGANISATION'S OWN RESEARCH — a country from which no community complaint has ever reached any development bank's accountability office. ITS METHOD SUITS A COUNTRY WITH ALMOST NO INDEPENDENT CIVIL SOCIETY: it partners with local lawyers or organisations to discuss domestic legal strategies alongside its own in-depth work on international complaint procedures, so a single sympathetic local lawyer plus this body is a workable combination where a campaigning organisation does not exist. It assists communities on request in using accountability offices to defend their rights and remedy harm from internationally financed projects, with support ranging from multi-year accompaniment to a limited document review, and it is expert in the mechanisms of the World Bank Group, regional development banks, export credit agencies and OECD National Contact Points. IT PUBLISHES A FREE DATABASE OF EVERY COMPLAINT EVER FILED TO EVERY ACCOUNTABILITY OFFICE. Founded 2009, having worked with communities in fifty countries. ESTABLISH THE FINANCING FIRST — the route exists only where an international institution is lending. Use it with the two Omani resources already in this file: the country's single environmental society, and the electronic endowment register that lets you establish whether the land in question is waqf before a dispute begins.

trackers.name: Inclusive Development International — it identifies the financier, which is what decides whether the complaint route is open
trackers.desc: EVERY INTERNATIONAL ROUTE IN THIS FILE DEPENDS ON KNOWING WHO IS PAYING, AND THIS ORGANISATION ESTABLISHES THAT ON REQUEST. Since 2016 it has researched and mapped the investment and supply chains behind harmful projects for community advocates, identifying banks, investors, insurers, development finance institutions and brands, from financial databases, company reports, import data and shipping manifests. It returns a summary with an analysis of pressure points and advocacy options; in high-potential cases it supports execution, and otherwise refers the case onward to partners. ITS FREE SHAREHOLDER AND DEVELOPMENT BANK INVESTMENT TRACKERS MAKE THE FIRST STAGE SELF-SERVICE, and it has trained more than fifteen hundred advocates in selected methods, teaching around the projects they are actually fighting. IT FITS THE OMANI SET PRECISELY: this file records that Oman has one independent environmental society, an endowment register that reveals whether land is waqf, and an accountability route that has never been used from the country. Establishing the financier is what turns that route from theory into a filing. THE LIMIT: its documented casework is in Southeast Asia, Africa and the Americas, and no work in Oman or this region could be established. Its service is described as open to community requests with no geographic restriction stated — untested here, not closed.

trackers.name: CESAR at Sultan Qaboos University — a published national review of Oman's coastal pollution
trackers.desc: THERE IS A PUBLISHED REVIEW OF THE ENVIRONMENTAL STATUS OF OMAN'S COASTAL AREAS, AND IT IS THE BASELINE A COASTAL OBJECTION NEEDS. It assesses pollution and impacts across the country's coast — SALINITY, HEAVY METALS AND PETROLEUM HYDROCARBONS — covering groundwater, soil, and marine and coastal water, and their effects on biological systems and marine organisms. A community told a scheme will have no significant effect can start from a national review that already documents what is in the water and the soil. AND ITS MONITORING IS MEASURED AGAINST OMANI STANDARDS — its published work compares results for conductivity, nitrite and nitrate, chloride, sulfate and phosphate against the national standards, which means the data arrives already framed in the terms a regulator has to answer, rather than in terms a regulator can dismiss as academic. THE MOST PRACTICAL THING HERE IS THE SEARCHABLE RESEARCH PORTAL: the university publishes its research output in a public expertise database, browsable by organisation and by collaborating country, so you can find WHICH NAMED RESEARCHER WORKS ON YOUR PROBLEM before you write to anyone. Naming the right person is most of the difficulty in getting expert help, and this removes it. ITS SUBJECT RANGE MATCHES OMAN'S ACTUAL LAND PRESSURES: climate change, biodiversity, desertification, wastewater and environmental management, with published work on water quality, groundwater pollution and clean-up, soil and water conservation, salt-affected soils, and the vulnerability and adaptation of FARMERS in a named wilayat — the last of which shows it works at community scale, not only at national scale. Its director combines that technical range with water resources management AND LEGISLATION, which is an unusual pairing and the right one for a permit dispute. THE LIMITS, AND THEY ARE THE SAME AS FOR ANY UNIVERSITY CENTRE IN THE REGION: this is a state university, its funding sources expressly include EXTERNAL CONTRACTS AND CONSULTANCY, and it has research partnerships with public and private sector organisations. It may have worked for the developer, and it will not campaign. Take the published data first; approach a named researcher second; expect a research collaboration rather than a service. Oman's only independent environmental organisation is recorded separately in this file and describes itself as the country's only one — this is not a second, it is the place the evidence lives.

trackers.name: iNaturalist — free identification, and every confirmed observation enters the scientific record
trackers.desc: IT IDENTIFIES WHAT YOU FOUND AND THEN MAKES IT COUNT. Photograph a plant, animal or fungus with a free app, or record a sound; an automated system offers an identification; a global community reviews it; and once they agree the observation becomes RESEARCH GRADE AND IS AUTOMATICALLY SHARED WITH THE GLOBAL BIODIVERSITY DATABASE. This country has an environmental society and a university research centre, but no route by which a resident's own observation becomes part of the record. This is that route, and it is free. IT SOLVES THE PROBLEM THIS FILE KEEPS FINDING: a community can rarely name what lives on the ground it is defending, and an assessment that lists nothing of interest is hard to contradict without species evidence. Point a phone at it; the community will tell you what it is. Invertebrates and plants — the groups most often absent from assessments — are exactly where crowd identification helps most. OLD PHOTOGRAPHS ARE ACCEPTED provided you know roughly when and where they were taken, so existing pictures of a wadi, a coast or a grove can be turned into dated records now. IT CAPTURES OFFLINE — photographs and coordinates are saved on the phone without a connection and uploaded later — which matters for remote coast and interior. AND LOCATIONS CAN BE OBSCURED: randomised to protect a sensitive species or habitat, with precise coordinates visible only to users you trust. Use that where publishing an exact location could attract collectors or hunters rather than protection. TO MAKE RECORDS USABLE: enable location so coordinates are logged, take SEVERAL PHOTOGRAPHS FROM DIFFERENT ANGLES of one individual, and record sounds where relevant. THE LIMITS: identification depends on volunteers and difficult organisms may go unresolved; uploading requires a connection; the platform is for observations you make yourself, not a place to deposit existing datasets. AND RESEARCH-GRADE RECORDS ARE HARVESTED PERIODICALLY — a contested identification can be changed and the record can drop out of the global database at the next harvest. Once observations reach research grade, download and cite them from that database, where the download carries a permanent identifier.

trackers.name: Hima revival and its fund — community-held protected land, revived at a site in this country
trackers.desc: A HIMA IS A PROTECTED PLACE DECLARED BY A COMMUNITY AND CUSTOMARILY HELD AND MANAGED BY IT, regulating the use of pasture, rangeland and water rather than transferring ownership — and a fund supported the revival of one AT A SITE IN THIS COUNTRY, alongside three others in the region. This map records for this country a conservation society, a university centre and foreign instruments; a community-held protected area is a different kind of thing, and it is native here rather than imported.
