AND THERE IS A ROUTE TO SPECIALISED EXPERTISE THAT DOES NOT EXIST IN MOST COUNTRIES HERE: THE LAW ALLOWS THE MINISTER TO LICENSE INTERNATIONAL LAW OFFICES WITH SPECIALISED EXPERTISE, for five renewable years, entered in their own table, with their lawyers registered on the practising table. WHERE A CASE NEEDS EXPERTISE THE DOMESTIC PROFESSION LACKS — environmental assessment, planning, complex construction — THOSE OFFICES ARE PRESENT AND REGISTERED, and some undertake pro bono work; asking costs nothing. THE LIMITS: this is a register and a licensing structure, NOT A REFERRAL SERVICE OR A LEGAL AID SCHEME. It will not say who handles land or environmental matters, and this file has found no environmental legal practice in this country. Pair it with the university law clinic recorded separately here, and put the four standard questions to any candidate: which grade, may I see the entry, where is the registered office, and is this consultation or representation.

trackers.name: Ministry of Commerce
trackers.desc: Saudi Arabia's commercial registry of companies. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Saudi Open Data
trackers.desc: National — official government open data / budget portal. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this is the broad budget/open-data hub for how money is allocated overall — for the specific firms winning tenders use the procurement portal, and for findings of misspending use the supreme audit institution. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Saudi Arabia.

trackers.name: Etimad
trackers.desc: Saudi Arabia's unified government-procurement and contracting platform. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Saudi Arabia, and for how much.

trackers.name: General Court of Audit
trackers.desc: General Court of Audit -KSA

trackers.name: Ministry of Justice (Saudi Arabia)
trackers.desc: Official ministry portal that publishes a compilation of selected judicial judgments (Mudawanat al-Ahkam). · Find here: Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Justice — court services, e-litigation and the publication of selected judgments.

trackers.name: General Authority for Statistics
trackers.desc: Saudi Arabia's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Saudi Arabia.

trackers.name: Kuwait Regional Convention (ROPME) — and its Judicial Commission
trackers.desc: THE ONE BINDING ENVIRONMENTAL INSTRUMENT COVERING ALL EIGHT GULF STATES. The Kuwait Regional Convention for Cooperation on the Protection of the Marine Environment from Pollution was signed 24 April 1978 and entered into force 1 July 1979 — 30 articles, described as the basic legal instrument binding the eight States of the Region. ALL EIGHT ARE FULL PARTIES: ROPME records ‘no signatories without ratification, acceptance, approval or accession’, so unlike some regional instruments there is no signed-but-unratified state to argue about. ARTICLE II fixes the Sea Area by coordinates, from Ras Dharbat Ali (16°39'N, 53°3'30"E) to Ras Al Fasteh (25°04'N, 61°25'E) — a treaty boundary you can check a project location against. Use the term ‘ROPME Sea Area’: it was coined by the Plenipotentiaries to achieve unanimity, cooperating in spite of existing geopolitical boundaries, and it is the name all eight accepted. THE ORGAN MOST PEOPLE DO NOT KNOW EXISTS: alongside the Council and Secretariat, ROPME has a Judicial Commission, established March 1989, of 6 nationals of Member States highly qualified in international law. In a region with almost no environmental litigation route, a standing judicial commission under a ratified convention is the most significant legal fact available — though this entry does not assert that individuals may petition it; establish who may seise it first. AN EVIDENCE SOURCE THAT NEEDS NO SITE ACCESS: ROPME's scientific bodies include a Remote Sensing Unit, alongside RIIS and MEMAC. WHICH PROTOCOL FITS YOUR ISSUE: oil-spill emergency response; land-based sources of pollution — the limb for a coastal development, discharge or reclamation; and transboundary movement of hazardous wastes. Development is named as a stressor in ROPME's own statement of purpose. At stake: over 20 species of dolphin and whale, all five subtropical turtle species, and more than 1,000 fish species, most endemic.

trackers.name: MBZ Species Conservation Fund — frame it as species work, not climate
trackers.desc: DO NOT DRESS A SPECIES PROJECT UP AS A CLIMATE PROJECT HERE — which is the opposite of the advice that fits almost every other fund in this map. The MBZ Fund was established on the basis that direct species conservation has lost out to wider concerns such as climate change, sustainability and poverty alleviation, and is now seen as a by-product of larger issues, leaving underfunded field biologists and wardens. It exists to correct that displacement, so frame the work as direct, field-based species conservation. A philanthropic endowment announced at the World Conservation Congress in Barcelona, October 2008, taking applications since March 2009; managing director Razan Khalifa Al Mubarak, also President of IUCN. By end-2010 it had disbursed just over US$5 million to about 380 projects in almost 100 countries; awards run up to US$25,000. TWO UNUSUAL ELIGIBILITY POINTS: it covers all animal, plant AND FUNGI species — fungi are named, which almost no other fund in this map does — and its focus includes data-deficient species, so you need not prove the species is threatened; where the problem is that nobody knows, that is itself a qualifying category. Individual conservationists may apply, and priority goes to projects supporting young conservationists. Funding is for direct conservation impact rather than administrative costs. HOW IT RUNS: three rounds a year, March, June and October; the Fund forwards recommendations to an independent body, so its staff are not the final decision-makers; and late submissions are automatically moved to the next round — missing a deadline costs a cycle, not the application. Apply online in English; the form requires a budget, references and permits, so have your permissions in order before applying. READ THE PROJECTS DATABASE FIRST — searchable by species, IUCN classification, continent and year, it shows what has been funded for comparable species in comparable places. NOTE: THIS FUND IS GLOBAL, NOT REGIONAL — it is recorded here because this country holds no other funding entry, not because Gulf applicants receive any preference.

trackers.name: Rufford Small Grants — Saudi Arabia is named eligible, and the applicant can be a person with no institution behind them
trackers.desc: SAUDI ARABIA APPEARS BY NAME ON THIS FOUNDATION'S OWN ELIGIBILITY LIST, WHICH MATTERS BECAUSE THIS FILE PREVIOUSLY RECORDED THE COUNTRY AS HAVING NOTHING. Searching Saudi Arabia found every environmental society to be chartered by a university or registered under a ministry, several stating participation in government policy among their objectives, and no independent body a community could enlist. That remains true of organisations — but this is a foreign funder that requires no Saudi institution at all. APPLICATIONS COME FROM INDIVIDUALS AND SMALL GROUPS, AND THERE ARE NO DEADLINES: you can apply at any time of year. The focus is people early in a conservation career, particularly current or recent MSc and PhD students, with others considered against the published criteria; undergraduates are not funded. THE SPECIES TEST IS EXACT AND YOU CAN CHECK IT BEFORE WRITING: work on any species not listed as Least Concern globally on the IUCN Red List qualifies, as does work on species not yet assessed but thought to be globally threatened. Projects on threatened habitats, human-wildlife conflict or community education qualify with no species focus at all. THE FUNDING IS A STAIRCASE: up to £7,000 for a first grant, then a second, a Booster and a Completion Grant, reaching roughly £18,000, each stage conditional on completing the last and filing updates and a final report, which are published on the applicant's own page on the foundation's site. CONSTRAINTS: one application in any twelve-month period, a twelve-month wait after rejection, the foundation expecting to cover between half and all of a project's cost with evidence of co-funding required where there is any, and no support for pure research without conservation benefit or for expeditions the applicant must fundraise to join. The foundation is UK-registered and its global operation belongs elsewhere in this map.

trackers.name: Accountability Counsel — Saudi Arabia is named as a country where no community has ever filed a complaint against a development bank
trackers.desc: THIS ORGANISATION'S OWN RESEARCH NAMES SAUDI ARABIA AS AN ACCOUNTABILITY DARK SPOT: a country from which no community complaint has ever reached any development bank's accountability office. Across the whole Middle East and North Africa it counts 68 complaints from 22 countries, and notes that such regional absence occurs almost nowhere else in the world. It does not accept that this means the projects are safer — it states there is little reason to believe the same banks behave differently in one region. THE ROUTE IS OPEN AND UNUSED, AND THIS IS THE BODY THAT WALKS YOU THROUGH IT. It is a legal nonprofit that, at the request of communities, assists people in using accountability offices to defend their rights and remedy harm from internationally financed projects. THE SUPPORT SCALES TO WHAT YOU NEED: from multi-year accompaniment through an entire complaint process down to a limited review of your key documents — so a community that only needs someone to read the loan agreement can ask for that. It trains communities in the options available, is expert in the accountability mechanisms of the World Bank Group, regional development banks, export credit agencies and OECD National Contact Points, and partners with local lawyers to combine the international complaint with a domestic legal strategy rather than treating them as alternatives. It also publishes a free public database of every community complaint ever filed to every accountability office, so you can check what has been filed against your project's lender before you begin. FIRST ESTABLISH WHO IS FINANCING THE PROJECT, because that determines whether an accountability office exists at all — the route runs through the lender, not the developer. Founded 2009, having worked with communities in fifty countries; headquartered in the United States with a regional presence in Asia. THE LIMIT: no international finance, no accountability office, no case here. Saudi Arabia otherwise carries one entry in this map, a foreign grant window, and this file has established that the country has no independent environmental organisation — which makes an external legal partner that answers community requests directly more significant here than it would be elsewhere.

trackers.name: Inclusive Development International — it maps the investment chain behind a project when nothing is disclosed locally
trackers.desc: WHERE NOTHING ABOUT A PROJECT IS PUBLISHED LOCALLY, THE MONEY BEHIND IT IS STILL TRACEABLE FROM OUTSIDE. This organisation takes requests from community advocates and maps the investment and supply chain behind a project — the banks, investors, insurers, development finance institutions and brands enabling it — working from financial databases, company reports, import data and shipping manifests rather than from anything the developer chooses to release. That matters most in a country where this file has established there is no independent environmental organisation and no domestic body that will investigate on a community's behalf. IT RETURNS A SUMMARY WITH AN ANALYSIS OF PRESSURE POINTS AND ADVOCACY OPTIONS, will on request help execute legal, advocacy and negotiation strategies in cases with high potential, and refers cases it cannot take to partners who can. ITS FREE SHAREHOLDER AND DEVELOPMENT BANK INVESTMENT TRACKERS LET YOU BEGIN THE WORK YOURSELF AT NO COST, built because the financial databases behind them are priced beyond the communities that need them. PAIR IT WITH THE ACCOUNTABILITY ENTRY ALSO RECORDED FOR SAUDI ARABIA: that one shows this country has never once had a community complaint reach a lender's accountability office, and this one identifies whether such a lender exists behind your project at all. Neither works without the other. THE LIMIT, STATED PLAINLY: its documented work is in Southeast Asia, Africa and the Americas and no case anywhere in this region could be established. Its service is described as open to community requests with no stated geographic bar, so treat this as untested rather than available.

trackers.name: KAUST Red Sea Research Center — the coral and oceanographic baseline for the coast being built on
trackers.desc: IT HOLDS THE BASELINE FOR THE STRETCH OF COAST UNDER THE MOST DEVELOPMENT PRESSURE IN THE COUNTRY. Its work covers coral reef ecosystems and the surrounding oceanographic conditions along the Red Sea coast, with the stated aim of maintaining conditions suitable for coral reef growth and ensuring the reefs' preservation. A community or objector facing a coastal scheme needs to know what was there before, and this is where that record is kept. IT ALSO RUNS A RED SEA BIOGEOGRAPHIC INFORMATION SYSTEM — a structured record of what lives where, alongside programmes in coral reef ecosystem studies, marine microbial ecology, fisheries and the marine environment, Red Sea hydrography and oceanography, and plankton distribution and biodiversity. Ask for the biogeographic data for your stretch of coast; a species distribution record is harder for an assessment to contradict than an opinion. It has laboratories for analysis, microbiology, ecology and microscopy, and was established in 2009. IT IS DESCRIBED IN INTERNATIONAL MARINE DIRECTORIES AS PRIVATE NON-PROFIT RATHER THAN A STATE INSTITUTION, which distinguishes it from the university centres recorded for two other Gulf states in this file — those are state universities, and this file recorded them against its own rule about state bodies. NOW THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST AND IS SHARPER HERE THAN IN ANY OTHER ENTRY OF THIS KIND: its declared mission is to PROVIDE SCIENTIFIC GUIDANCE TO KEY SAUDI STAKEHOLDERS, and the coast it studies is the coast on which the country's largest development programme is building. Assume its researchers may be advising those developers. That is a reason to take the published record and the data rather than to seek advocacy or share a strategy — the same caution this file has attached to a Qatari centre that sells consultancy, to a Jordanian body with a ministry agreement, and to three environmental organisations found to sit on the developer's side of a project. WHAT THIS ENTRY IS: Saudi Arabia's first domestic entry in this map, and an evidence route rather than an ally. The country's other three entries are a foreign small-grants window and two foreign accountability bodies; this file searched repeatedly and could verify no independent Saudi environmental organisation, finding that such societies there are university-chartered or ministry-registered. That finding stands — what changes is that the DATA is now locatable.

trackers.name: MBZ Species Conservation Fund — it gives grants to individuals, which matters where there is no organisation to join
trackers.desc: ANYONE DIRECTLY ENGAGED IN SPECIES CONSERVATION CAN APPLY — INDIVIDUALS, COMMUNITIES AND ORGANISATIONS. That single sentence is why this entry exists: this file searched repeatedly and could verify no independent Saudi environmental organisation, finding that such societies are university-chartered or ministry-registered. Where there is nothing to join, a fund that pays a person with a plan is the only door of its kind. WHAT IT PAYS FOR IS FIELDWORK, NOT PAPERWORK: it funds in situ conservation — SURVEY WORK AND DATA GATHERING, direct action, recovery management and training, focused on a species in its natural habitat. Survey work and data gathering is precisely what a community needs before a scheme is approved, and this file has recorded across the region that the absence of a baseline is what loses cases. THE CEILING IS 25,000 DOLLARS PER PROJECT and an application asking for more is rejected, though a larger total budget is acceptable if other funders cover the rest. It states its intention is small, targeted grants to LOCAL AND GRASSROOTS PROJECTS. It will consider salaries, stipends, per diems and project living costs where these are part of the conservation work — but not an organisation's core running costs or overheads, which is the reverse of most funders and suits someone working alone. IT IS PARTICULARLY INTERESTED IN SPECIES THAT ARE THREATENED BUT DO NOT NORMALLY RECEIVE CONSERVATION ATTENTION, and covers plants, fungi and invertebrates as well as the familiar groups. An unglamorous local species is an advantage here rather than a weakness. AND ITS GRANTEES PUBLISH CASE STUDIES ON THE FUND'S OWN SITE — read them for this country to find who is already doing this work here. Applications go through its own online system, are reviewed three times a year by an independent advisory board, and continuation grants are available for a completed project that reported properly. It is headquartered in the region, has supported around two thousand projects across more than a hundred and fifty countries, and states that eligibility extends worldwide without discrimination by region. THE LIMITS: it funds species conservation, not opposition. It will not pay for a campaign, a lawyer or an objection — but a funded survey establishing that a threatened species uses the ground in question is evidence, and evidence is what this file has recorded winning. No casework of its own in this country could be established.

trackers.name: Thuwal Fishermen's Cooperative Society — the Kingdom's first fishing cooperative, on the coast under most pressure
trackers.desc: IT IS THE FIRST FISHERMEN'S COOPERATIVE SOCIETY IN THE KINGDOM ON THE RED SEA, IT HAS ITS OWN WEBSITE, AND IT SITS ON THE STRETCH OF COAST THIS FILE HAS ALREADY RECORDED AS THE MOST DEVELOPED. R140 recorded a research centre holding the coral reef and species-distribution baselines for that same water; this is the body of the people whose living comes out of it. A case that joins published reef data to a constituted body of affected fishermen is far stronger than either alone. IT WAS ESTABLISHED UNDER A NUMBERED LICENCE IN 1403 OF THE HIJRI CALENDAR, UNDER MINISTERIAL SUPERVISION, AND THE STUDIES BEHIND IT WERE DONE BY THE AGRICULTURE MINISTRY'S FISHERIES ARM TOGETHER WITH THE UNITED NATIONS FOOD AND AGRICULTURE ORGANISATION. An international agency helped create it, which is worth knowing: bodies founded that way tend to have documented purposes and records. ITS OWN ACCOUNT OF HOW IT WAS FORMED IS A TEMPLATE ANY COASTAL COMMUNITY CAN FOLLOW: a study, then a public announcement, then subscription by members, then the formation of a founding council, then the licence. AND HERE IS THE THRESHOLD, WHICH THIS FILE HAS BEEN UNABLE TO STATE FOR ANY COUNTRY UNTIL NOW: the national council of cooperative societies states that founding a cooperative requires AT LEAST TWELVE PEOPLE to submit the application, through the human resources and social development ministry's service. This payload has established repeatedly that the barrier between a community and land, money or standing is not merit but the absence of a registered body. Twelve people is the number. THERE IS A SECOND SUCH COOPERATIVE WITH ITS OWN SITE IN THE SOUTHERN REGION OF THE RED SEA COAST, so this is a form with more than one instance rather than a single survivor — and the southern one covers a different fishing ground. THE LIMITS: these are cooperatives under ministry supervision, constituted for the welfare of their members and the fishing economy, not objectors. Nothing found shows either opposing a development scheme, and in a country where this file could verify no independent environmental organisation at all, that limit should be assumed rather than tested carelessly. Use them to establish who fishes which ground, how many households depend on it, and what the catch was before — a membership roll and a landing record are evidence no assessment can dismiss.

trackers.name: Hima recognition as a community conserved area — the country's own route to community-held land
trackers.desc: THERE WERE AN ESTIMATED THREE THOUSAND HIMAS IN THIS COUNTRY IN THE 1960s, AND BY 2003 ONLY A FEW DOZEN REMAINED. Nearly every village in the south-western mountains had one or more; they ranged from ten hectares to well over a thousand; and they were lost after public lands were nationalised in the 1950s. The national wildlife commission itself recorded that this loss had MARKEDLY REDUCED THE DIVERSITY OF HABITATS — which means the case for restoring them is made in the state's own documents, not by outsiders. AND THERE IS NOW A RECOGNITION PATHWAY. The revised national protected area system plan proposes SIX TO SEVEN TRADITIONAL HIMAS FOR RECOGNITION AS COMMUNITY CONSERVED AREAS — one of the named examples is just 1.5 SQUARE KILOMETRES, so small size is not a bar. Separately, SEVENTY-FIVE SITES were identified for designation as protected areas, MANY OF THEM HISTORICALLY HOME TO HIMAS. The first question for any village here is whether its own former hima is among them. KNOW WHAT A HIMA ACTUALLY REGULATED, BECAUSE THAT IS THE RULE-SET TO PROPOSE: PROTECTED WOODLANDS in which cutting trees or branches is prohibited or regulated except in acute need; MANAGED RANGELANDS in which grazing and grass-cutting are seasonal to allow regeneration after plants have flowered and seeded, or are limited to specified kinds and numbers of livestock, or permitted only for a set period in drought; and RESERVES FOR BEE-KEEPING. These are precise, workable rules a community can put forward rather than a vague request to be left alone. THE TIMING FAVOURS A COMMUNITY THAT ASKS NOW: the national plan is built around protecting thirty per cent of the country's land and sea by 2030, and states that implementation REQUIRES REINFORCED COOPERATION BETWEEN GOVERNMENTAL ENTITIES AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES. A state committed to that figure needs areas that are already conserved and already governed — which is exactly what a functioning hima is. THERE IS ALSO A DOOR: the national wildlife body has been the lead authority for protected areas since 2019, a royal decree required the registration and designation of all protected areas, and an annual national forum named HIMA is held whose attendees include protected area representatives, educational institutions and THE NON-PROFIT SECTOR. THE LIMITS ARE SERIOUS AND SHOULD DECIDE YOUR EXPECTATIONS. Recognition is granted by the state, and it was the state's nationalisation of public land that destroyed the himas in the first place. A hima regulates use rather than conferring title. This file has verified across five separate rounds that this country has no independent environmental organisation to advocate for you, so a community must approach the authorities directly or through the regional hima network recorded elsewhere in this map.

trackers.name: National Society for Human Rights — it receives complaints and answers within 24 hours
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY HAD NO DOMESTIC ROUTE OF ANY KIND FOR A GRIEVANCE. Six earlier attempts across this file found a bar association with no public function, law faculties with no clinic, and no independent environmental organisation. THIS BODY RECEIVES COMPLAINTS AND FOLLOWS THEM UP WITH THE COMPETENT AUTHORITIES, and verifies allegations of violations and abuses. ITS PUBLISHED SERVICE TERMS ARE UNUSUALLY CONCRETE: complaints and SPECIALISED CONSULTATIONS handled IN COMPLETE CONFIDENTIALITY, WITH A RESPONSE WITHIN TWENTY-FOUR HOURS, submitted through its own platform. Almost nothing else in this payload commits to a turnaround time. AND IT PUBLISHES ON PRECISELY THE QUESTION AN EXPROPRIATION RAISES: explanatory material on COMPENSATION FOR DAMAGE AND THE MECHANISM FOR DETERMINING IT under the civil transactions law — alongside a KNOW YOUR RIGHTS series of booklets that can be requested from it free. A household facing the taking of land needs to know how compensation is calculated before it negotiates, and this is the only domestic source of that explanation found here. WHAT IT IS: founded in March 2004, based in the capital, with a general assembly of founding and admitted members and a nine-member executive council, working for citizens, residents and visitors alike, and cooperating with governmental and non-governmental bodies inside and outside the country. NOW THE DISPUTE ABOUT IT, WHICH YOU SHOULD WEIGH BEFORE DECIDING WHAT TO SEND. IT DESCRIBES ITSELF AS FINANCIALLY AND ADMINISTRATIVELY INDEPENDENT, WITH NO CONNECTION TO ANY GOVERNMENT APPARATUS. EXTERNAL REFERENCE WORKS DESCRIBE IT AS CLOSELY ASSOCIATED WITH AND FUNDED BY THE GOVERNMENT, and its president has publicly defended the state's position in an international diplomatic dispute. This file records what a body does and publishes and does not adjudicate such questions. TREAT IT AS A COMPLAINTS CHANNEL INTO THE ADMINISTRATION RATHER THAN AS AN ADVOCATE AGAINST IT — which is how this payload has treated state-linked legal aid in four other countries. IT IS ALSO DISTINCT FROM THE GOVERNMENT'S OWN HUMAN RIGHTS COMMISSION, established the following year, which runs a separate electronic service for submitting complaints and reports. Two channels exist; neither is independent of the state, and a person choosing between them should assume both are visible to it.

trackers.name: Taqeem — the valuation regulator, and the standard every offer on your land must meet
trackers.desc: THIS FILE ALREADY RECORDS A BODY HERE THAT PUBLISHES HOW COMPENSATION FOR DAMAGE IS DETERMINED. THIS IS THE AUTHORITY THAT LICENSES WHOEVER CALCULATES IT — the regulator of the valuation profession in this country, covering REAL ESTATE, business, MACHINERY AND EQUIPMENT, damage to vehicles, and precious metals. Between the two, a household facing the taking of land has the rule and the qualified person. ITS OWN DEFINITION OF VALUATION IS THE MOST USEFUL SENTENCE IN THIS ENTRY, BECAUSE IT IS A STANDARD YOU CAN HOLD AN OFFER TO. Valuation is estimating the value of property rights for a specific asset, purpose, time and users — TAKING INTO ACCOUNT ALL THE CHARACTERISTICS AND FEATURES OF THE PROPERTY and all fundamental economic factors of the market, INCLUDING ALL INTERESTS, RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS relating to its ownership, WITH ALL IMPROVEMENTS PERMANENTLY AFFIXED TO IT AND THE APPURTENANCES ATTACHED TO IT. IF THE FIGURE PUT TO YOU IGNORED YOUR WELL, YOUR TERRACING, YOUR TREES, YOUR WALLS OR YOUR ACCESS RIGHTS, IT DID NOT MEET THE REGULATOR'S OWN DEFINITION — and saying so, in those words, is an argument that does not require a lawyer. AND IT DISCIPLINES ITS OWN PROFESSION: it referred SIX VIOLATORS TO THE PUBLIC PROSECUTION in the first half of 2026. A valuation you believe is defective can be complained about to the body that licensed the valuer who produced it — a route this payload can offer for almost no other profession in this region. THERE IS ALSO A DIRECT SERVICE: an individual may SUBMIT A REQUEST FOR A REAL ESTATE VALUATION OF ASSETS THEY OWN through the national services platform. That is how you obtain your own number rather than arguing about someone else's. ASK WHICH BRANCH YOUR VALUER IS ACCREDITED IN, because accreditation is by branch: real estate, machinery and equipment, or business are separate, and practical experience of at least two years in the relevant branch is required after membership, documented in the authority's own electronic systems. A valuer accredited for machinery is the right person if what you are losing is a workshop, a pump or a production line rather than only ground — which this file has recorded as a real gap where livelihoods rather than plots are taken. THE LIMITS: this is a state regulator, not an advocate. It sets rules, licenses and disciplines; it will not take your side against a public authority, and its purpose is stated as contributing to an investment-friendly environment. Valuations cost money. And a regulator that trains valuers also trains the ones the acquiring authority will use.

trackers.name: Istitlaa — comment on a regulation before it is approved, and read what happened to the comments
trackers.desc: IT SURVEYS THE VIEWS OF THE GENERAL PUBLIC — NOT ONLY COMPANIES — ON REGULATIONS AND SIMILAR INSTRUMENTS ISSUED BY GOVERNMENT BODIES, BEFORE THEY ARE APPROVED. It was established by a Council of Ministers resolution and is run as a single unified platform, so drafts from many ministries appear in one place. This file needed seven rounds to find any domestic channel in this country at all, and the one it found was a complaints body whose independence is disputed. THIS IS A SECOND CHANNEL, AND IT OPERATES BEFORE A DECISION RATHER THAN AFTER IT. THE SCALE IS REAL: in a single year it carried around FIVE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-SEVEN PROJECTS FROM ONE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-FOUR GOVERNMENT BODIES — AND PUBLISHED FOUR HUNDRED AND SIXTEEN RESULTS AND DECISIONS. That second figure is the unusual one. This payload has recorded consultation windows in a dozen countries and VERY FEW OF THEM PUBLISH WHAT HAPPENED TO THE COMMENTS. Being able to read the outcome of past consultations tells you what kind of argument this system actually absorbs. EACH CONSULTATION CARRIES A STATED CLOSING DATE — one published batch of ninety projects with twenty-one government bodies each named its own deadline. Find the closing date first and work backwards; a comment filed late is a comment not filed. NOW THE LIMIT THAT DECIDES WHETHER THIS IS YOUR DOOR AT ALL. IT IS THE RULES LAYER, NOT THE PROJECT LAYER. A zoning rule, a licensing procedure, a permitting requirement or a compensation regulation is economic and developmental and belongs here. A DECISION ABOUT ONE SPECIFIC SITE IS NOT A REGULATION AND WILL NOT APPEAR. Use it to shape the rule that will govern the next hundred decisions, and use the complaints body and the valuation regulator recorded separately here for the decision in front of you. TWO PRACTICAL WARNINGS. The platform's own list of common questions asks whether ALL draft regulations are published on it, which is a strong hint that not all of them are — so absence from the platform does not mean a rule is not being made. And one attempt to reach the site's front page during this round was REJECTED OUTRIGHT, so access may be restricted from some connections; approach through the projects listing rather than the root, and expect the machine translation offered for other languages to be disclaimed by the operator itself.

trackers.name: Beekeepers' cooperative — protecting the bee pastures is written into its objects
trackers.desc: TWO OF ITS PUBLISHED OBJECTS ARE WHAT THIS MAP EXISTS FOR. It works to CONTRIBUTE TO THE PROTECTION OF THE BEE PASTURES, TO CARE FOR THEM AND TO DEVELOP THEM — and to REPRESENT ITS MEMBERS BEFORE THE RELEVANT AUTHORITIES AND SPEAK FOR THEM. Habitat protection written into a cooperative's constitution, and a standing mandate to speak to government on members' behalf, is the affected-user pattern this file has proved in nine countries — the union or cooperative of the people whose livelihood a scheme takes. AND BEEKEEPERS ARE AFFECTED USERS WHO CAN PRICE THE HARM. Bees depend on wild flowering plants; clearing scrub, quarrying a hillside, flooding a valley or spraying changes the forage, AND THE LOSS APPEARS IN THE YIELD — which is weighed, sold and recorded. Most affected users in this payload can describe damage; a beekeeper can produce figures for it, year against year. IT ALSO CONNECTS TO SOMETHING THIS FILE ALREADY RECORDED ABOUT THIS COUNTRY: ITS TRADITIONAL PROTECTED-AREA CATEGORIES INCLUDED RESERVES FOR BEE-KEEPING, and six to seven traditional himas are proposed for recognition as community conserved areas. A beekeepers' cooperative asking for its forage ground to be recognised is therefore asking for a category THE NATIONAL PROTECTED AREA PLAN ALREADY CONTAINS, under a name the authorities use. That is a far shorter argument than proposing something new. WHAT ELSE IT DOES FOR MEMBERS: it is a registered cooperative under the ministry responsible for social development, providing A SCIENTIFIC AND ORGANISATIONAL REFERENCE FOR BEEKEEPERS IN ITS REGION, training and guidance, production inputs at suitable prices, better packaging for marketing, awareness of the value of bees and their products, and support for needy families to develop their apiaries. This file recorded elsewhere that forming a cooperative in this country requires a minimum of twelve people — so a district without one has a route to founding it. THE LIMITS. IT SERVES ONE REGION and this entry is anchored to a third-party business directory rather than the cooperative's own site, so contact details and current activity must be confirmed. It is a cooperative for its members' economic interests, not a campaigning body — nothing found shows it opposing a project. And its representation mandate is exercised before authorities, which means it is a channel into government rather than a challenge to it. Approach it for the forage argument, the yield evidence and the standing to be heard.

trackers.name: Saudi Bar Association — check the licence, find the rules, complain about a lawyer
trackers.desc: THREE THINGS A COMMUNITY NEEDS FROM A PROFESSIONAL BODY, AND THIS COUNTRY HAD NONE OF THEM RECORDED. It is the national body for the legal profession, and it publishes THE PROFESSION'S LEGISLATION IN ONE PLACE — the code of law practice issued in 1422 and amended twice since, together with its implementing regulation. Reading the rules your lawyer works under is the cheapest form of protection there is, and this file has recorded across the region that people lose cases to procedure rather than to argument. USE IT FIRST TO VERIFY THAT THE PERSON YOU ARE TALKING TO IS ACTUALLY A LICENSED PRACTITIONER. The profession here is defined by statute as pleading before the courts, before the grievances board and before committees formed under regulations to hear matters within their jurisdiction, and practising legal and sharia consultancy — and a register of practising and non-practising lawyers is maintained. Anyone offering to handle a land or compensation matter should be checkable against it. AND NOTE ONE RIGHT THE STATUTE ITSELF PRESERVES: EVERY PERSON HAS THE RIGHT TO PLEAD ON THEIR OWN BEHALF. Representation is a choice here rather than a requirement, which matters for a household that cannot pay — and it differs from the neighbouring country recorded in this file, where claims above a stated value MUST go through a lawyer. THE THIRD USE IS THE ONE PEOPLE DISCOVER TOO LATE: A PROFESSIONAL BODY IS WHERE A COMPLAINT ABOUT A LAWYER GOES — fees taken and work not done, a file abandoned mid-case, a conflict of interest. This payload has recorded a valuation regulator in this country that referred violators to the public prosecution; a profession that regulates itself is worth approaching on the same basis. THE LIMITS, PLAINLY. It regulates lawyers; it does not provide them. NO ASSIGNMENT OR JUDICIAL-AID ARTICLE OF THE KIND FOUND IN THREE OTHER COUNTRIES IN THIS FILE COULD BE ESTABLISHED HERE, so this is not a route to a free lawyer — ask the association directly whether one exists before assuming it does not. It will not take a position on a scheme, and it exists to serve the profession as much as the public. Use it with the complaints body and the valuation regulator recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Sudair Evergreen Society — a licensed local society that plants, and the service for requesting trees
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY HAS ALMOST NO INDEPENDENT CIVIL SOCIETY IN THIS MAP, AND THIS IS A LICENSED LOCAL ENVIRONMENTAL SOCIETY WITH A PUBLISHED LICENCE NUMBER, A WHATSAPP CONTACT AND AN EMAIL ADDRESS. It was founded in 1441 of the Hijri calendar, sits in a named governorate of the central region, and is supervised by the local social development centre. ITS OBJECTIVES INCLUDE SOMETHING MORE THAN AWARENESS: DEVELOPING AND IMPLEMENTING LANDSCAPE MANAGEMENT PLANS TO CONSERVE BIODIVERSITY AND IMPROVE THE NATURAL ENVIRONMENT, and cooperating with government bodies, authorities, COMPANIES and the third sector to carry out projects serving those aims. A body whose constitution includes landscape management planning is one that can be asked to make a plan for a particular place — which is a different offer from a planting day. AND IT HAS BEEN COMMISSIONED BY THE NATIONAL BODY: it afforested a named park UNDER COMMISSIONING FROM THE NATIONAL CENTRE FOR VEGETATION COVER DEVELOPMENT AND COMBATING DESERTIFICATION. A small local society being engaged by the national centre to do the work is the precedent that matters — it means the route from a community initiative to a funded, official planting exists and has been used. NOW THE MECHANISM, WHICH IS WORTH MORE THAN ANY SINGLE SOCIETY. IT PARTNERS WITH THE ENVIRONMENT MINISTRY AND A GROUP OF GREEN LEAGUES AND NON-PROFIT SOCIETIES TO DELIVER THE MINISTRY'S PERIODIC AFFORESTATION PLANS, THROUGH AN ELECTRONIC SERVICE BY WHICH TREES CAN BE REQUESTED to support the vegetation cover, planting campaigns can be joined, AND FINANCIAL SUPPORT CAN BE GIVEN TO THE VEGETATION COVER FUND. THAT IS A LAND-DEFENCE INSTRUMENT, NOT ONLY A GREENING ONE. This file recorded that a state land service in another country identifies UNUSED LAND as a ground for reallocating it, and that a dated, witnessed planting programme is the cheapest proof that ground is in use. A NATIONAL SERVICE THROUGH WHICH A COMMUNITY CAN REQUEST TREES, AND A LICENSED SOCIETY THAT WILL COME AND PLANT THEM, IS HOW THAT PROOF GETS MADE. AND THERE ARE OTHERS LIKE IT: the ministry's partnership runs with a GROUP of green leagues and societies, so an equivalent body may exist in your own governorate — ask the ministry which society covers your area before approaching this one, which works in the central region. THE LIMITS, PLAINLY: it is licensed, supervised by a state centre and partnered with the ministry, so it is not an opponent of official schemes and nothing found shows it objecting to a development. Its work is planting, awareness and landscape planning, not legal defence or land purchase. And its own donations facility appeared to be in test mode, so confirm before sending money.

trackers.name: Accredited environmental associations — find the society for your region, or apply to found one
trackers.desc: THIS FILE RECORDED A LICENSED ENVIRONMENTAL SOCIETY IN ONE GOVERNORATE OF THIS COUNTRY AND COULD NOT THEN ESTABLISH WHICH SOCIETY COVERED ANYWHERE ELSE. THE MINISTRY MAINTAINS THE LIST: accredited civil associations working in environment and agriculture, named individually. AND REGIONAL SOCIETIES EXIST BY REGION — an environment society for one of the southern regions is separately registered with the national non-profit sector centre. ASK FOR THE SOCIETY OF YOUR OWN REGION BY NAME; do not assume the one you have heard of is the one that covers you. SECOND, AND MORE USEFUL THAN THE LIST: THESE SOCIETIES ARE CREATED DELIBERATELY, REGION BY REGION, ACCORDING TO MAPPED NEED. The environment agency and the social development agency agreed to study A HEAT MAP OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND AGRICULTURAL NEEDS ACROSS THE COUNTRY IN ORDER TO ESTABLISH SOCIETIES WHERE THEY ARE NEEDED, with targets covering both the number of societies and their spread across regions. A place with a real environmental problem and no society is, on that policy, a gap the state has undertaken to fill. THIRD, THE ROUTE TO FOUNDING ONE IS DEFINED AND THIS IS THE PART TO ACT ON. The two agencies are LINKED ELECTRONICALLY IN THE SERVICE FOR FOUNDING CIVIL ASSOCIATIONS, and applications to establish an environmental association are APPROVED OR REJECTED SUBJECT TO TECHNICAL SUPERVISION BY THE ENVIRONMENT AGENCY. This payload's most repeated finding across twenty-three countries is that communities are blocked because they are not a constituted legal person. HERE THE FOUNDING ROUTE IS NAMED, THE APPROVING BODY IS NAMED, AND THE STATE HAS SAID IT WANTS MORE OF THESE SOCIETIES IN MORE REGIONS. FOURTH, THERE IS A SECOND NETWORK ALREADY IN PLACE: FIVE HUNDRED SOCIAL DEVELOPMENT COMMITTEES were targeted for activation in afforestation and environmental volunteering. A committee already exists in many localities where no environmental society does, and it is a faster door than founding anything. HOW TO USE ALL THIS: identify the accredited society for your region from the ministry's list; check it against the national non-profit register for its licence number, which this file has recorded as the proof that a body is a legal person; ask your local social development committee what environmental work it is mandated to do; and if no society covers your area, apply to found one through the linked service. THE LIMITS. These are licensed associations under technical supervision by the environment agency — they are partners of the ministry, not opponents of its projects, and nothing found shows any of them objecting to a development. The list is state-maintained, so it shows recognised bodies and not others. And founding an association means accepting that supervision.

trackers.name: University soil and water laboratories — they analyse samples for citizens
trackers.desc: A UNIVERSITY SOIL SCIENCE DEPARTMENT HAS ESTABLISHED A LABORATORY SPECIFICALLY FOR COMMUNITY SERVICE, AND IT WORKS WITH CITIZENS, NON-GOVERNMENTAL BODIES AND COMPANIES TO ANALYSE SAMPLES OF SOIL, WATER, PLANTS AND CHEMICAL AND ORGANIC FERTILISERS — and it provides technical consultancy and recommendations to CITIZENS AND NON-GOVERNMENTAL BODIES who want samples analysed. This file has spent scores of rounds on the fact that communities can describe harm and cannot prove it, and has answered with funders, research chairs and international complaint bodies. THE ORDINARY ANSWER IS A UNIVERSITY LABORATORY THAT ADVERTISES SERVICE TO THE PUBLIC, and it costs a sample and a fee rather than a grant application. AND HERE IS WHAT GIVES THE RESULT ITS WEIGHT. THE SAME DEPARTMENT CARRIES OUT THE ANALYSES REQUIRED BY GOVERNMENT BODIES — the agriculture and water ministry, the national standards authority, the health ministry, the capital's development authority and its municipality. A result from a laboratory that the ministries themselves use is not something those ministries can wave away as partisan. That is a different quality of evidence from a photograph or a petition. THERE IS MORE THAN ONE. A second university operates a WATER ANALYSIS LABORATORY alongside materials and corrosion laboratories and desalination facilities, and a centre whose stated work includes research on AIR AND WATER POLLUTION AND SOLID WASTE TREATMENT, the provision of HIGH-QUALITY LABORATORY SERVICES TO INTERNATIONAL STANDARDS, CONSULTANCY STUDIES FOR GOVERNMENTAL AND NON-GOVERNMENTAL SECTORS, and supplying scientific information on climate change TO THE PUBLIC and to authorities. A third university hosts an environmental research and sustainability centre whose mission is excellence in studies, research and COMMUNITY SERVICE across environment, agriculture and natural resources. HOW TO USE THEM PROPERLY, BECAUSE A BADLY TAKEN SAMPLE IS WORSE THAN NONE. Ask the laboratory FIRST how it wants the sample taken — container, volume, depth, preservation, timing — and record where and when each sample was collected, by whom, and in whose presence. Photograph the collection. Keep the laboratory's own submission form. A RESULT WITHOUT A RECORD OF HOW THE SAMPLE WAS OBTAINED CAN BE DISMISSED, AND THAT RECORD COSTS NOTHING TO CREATE. THE LIMITS: these are university laboratories serving ministries, companies and the public alike — they analyse, they do not advocate, and they will not comment on who is responsible. They charge. A laboratory that works for government bodies may be cautious about a contested project, so frame the request as a sample analysis rather than as evidence for a dispute. And confirm current services and fees before travelling. Use the result with the accredited regional environmental association and the elected municipal representatives recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Desert, water and environment research institute — it researches the environmental impact of projects
trackers.desc: AMONG ITS DECLARED RESEARCH INTERESTS IS THE ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT OF PROJECTS. That phrase, published by a national research institute as a field it works in, is the rarest thing this file looks for and it has found it in almost no country. The institute's other stated interests run to DESERT ENVIRONMENT SYSTEMS, ARIDITY AND ARIDITY CONTROL MEASURES, ENVIRONMENTAL POLLUTION, CLIMATE CHANGE AND EARLY WARNING OF CLIMATIC DISASTERS, maintaining environmental balance, ecotourism, and LAND DETERIORATION. ITS PROJECT LIST IS EQUALLY DIRECT. It has worked on developing and increasing the use of DAM WATER AND WADI TRIBUTARIES together with sustainable agriculture in WADI BASINS, OASES AND MEADOWS; on a project to REDUCE FLOOD RISK TO THE CAPITAL; and on a programme to REHABILITATE VILLAGES BY CONSTRUCTING SMALL DAMS. THOSE THREE ARE ARGUMENTS AS WELL AS PROJECTS. A scheme proposed on a wadi floor faces an institute that has studied flood risk in this country; a village losing water has an institute that has built small dams for exactly that purpose; and ground dismissed as empty desert has an institute whose subject is what deserts actually do. ITS CONSTITUTION MATTERS TOO: it was established in 1986 by administrative decree as a centre for desert studies and remains AN INDEPENDENT ADMINISTRATIVE UNIT ATTACHED DIRECTLY TO THE UNIVERSITY'S RECTOR — not a section of a teaching department. It conducts research on the arid zones of the peninsula, supports research carried out elsewhere in the university, cooperates with research bodies at home and abroad, runs conferences and workshops on desertification and environment, and issues its own publications. It also hosts the secretariat of an international water prize and supplies its scientific support through an advisory panel of the university's water specialists — WHICH MEANS IT CONVENES THE COUNTRY'S WATER EXPERTISE IN ONE PLACE. WHAT TO ASK FOR: published work on your wadi, your aquifer or your stretch of desert; whether the institute has studied flood risk where a scheme is proposed; and which of its researchers works on the specific question. ASK FOR PUBLISHED WORK FIRST — it is free, refereed, and cannot be dismissed as commissioned by objectors. THE LIMITS: it is a research institute inside a state university — it publishes and advises rather than advocating, and nothing found shows it opposing a scheme. IT IS ALSO NOT THE SAME AS THE UNIVERSITY SOIL AND WATER LABORATORY RECORDED SEPARATELY FOR THIS COUNTRY, which explicitly analyses samples for citizens; no equivalent public analysis service was confirmed here. Approach it as a research question about a place.

trackers.name: Regional green societies — licensed local bodies doing the physical work, and what each has actually built
trackers.desc: THIS FILE COULD NAME ONE LICENSED LOCAL ENVIRONMENTAL SOCIETY IN THIS COUNTRY AND THEN COULD ONLY POINT AT A MINISTRY LIST AND SAY FIND YOURS. HERE ARE SEVERAL, WITH WHAT THEY HAVE ACTUALLY DONE — which is the difference between a directory and a resource. IN ONE EASTERN GOVERNORATE THE SOCIETY IS BUILDING A SAND-ENCROACHMENT BARRIER OUT OF DRY PALM FRONDS ALONG SIX KILOMETRES, in cooperation with a United Nations food body, and has run a training workshop on environmental volunteering with the environment ministry. THAT IS THE MOST TRANSFERABLE THING IN THIS ENTRY: a barrier against moving sand, built from an agricultural waste product that every date-growing community already has, at a length that is measurable. A village losing ground to sand does not need a budget for imported engineering; it needs fronds, labour and a society that has done it before. IN A NORTHERN REGION ANOTHER SOCIETY WORKS IN THE VALLEYS AND FLOOD CHANNELS, planting local species with volunteers alongside government bodies, running periodic clean-up campaigns of wild and recreation sites, and planting around mosques. WORK IN WADIS AND FLOOD CHANNELS IS EXACTLY WHERE LAND IS LOST AND WHERE DEVELOPMENT PRESSURE IS HEAVIEST, and a society already operating there is a partner with standing to be consulted. A THIRD USES THE MIYAWAKI METHOD — DENSE PLANTING OF LOCAL SPECIES TO GROW A SMALL FOREST FAST ON A SMALL PLOT, raising biodiversity and cutting urban heat — alongside workshops, exhibitions, sorting and reuse programmes, and hosting university and school students to teach them their own local environment. A method that turns a small urban plot into woodland quickly is a direct answer to the argument that a patch of ground is too small to be worth keeping. A FOURTH CONCENTRATES ON VEGETATION COVER, AFFORESTATION AND OPEN VOLUNTEERING. HOW TO USE THEM: FIND THE SOCIETY FOR YOUR OWN REGION FIRST — these bodies are regional, and one will not act outside its area. Then ask for the three things they can give that cost them least: a site visit, TRAINING FOR YOUR OWN PEOPLE, and joint work with the government bodies they already partner with. Ask also to see how a project of theirs was structured, because a licensed society's completed project is a template your own group can copy. THE LIMITS: these are licensed societies working WITH ministries and government agencies, not against them — nothing found shows any of them opposing a development, and asking one to do so will fail. Each covers its own region only. And the fourth society's activity was confirmed less fully than the others. Read this with the ministry's accredited-associations list recorded separately here, which is how you find the one for your area and check it is licensed.

trackers.name: Associations Support Fund — it pays the cost of setting an association up, and rescues one that is failing
trackers.desc: THE BARRIER THIS FILE NAMES MORE OFTEN THAN ANY OTHER IS THAT A COMMUNITY IS NOT A CONSTITUTED ORGANISATION AND THEREFORE CANNOT RECEIVE MONEY, HOLD LAND OR COMMISSION WORK. THIS FUND PAYS FOR THE STEP ITSELF: A FOUNDING EXPENSES GRANT OF UP TO ONE HUNDRED THOUSAND RIYALS, covering an association's establishment and first-year operating needs. The conditions are published: an approved estimated budget for founding and first-year operation, a copy of the LICENCE and the decision approving the board, and the association MUST NOT HAVE HAD PREVIOUS SUPPORT from the fund. It is for parent associations, not for branches, and taking it bars another grant in the same financial year. THERE IS ALSO A PROGRAMMES AND PROJECTS GRANT, AND ITS CONDITIONS TELL YOU WHAT A FUNDABLE PROPOSAL LOOKS LIKE ANYWHERE. The programme must fall WITHIN THE ASSOCIATION'S OWN STATED OBJECTIVES; the technically supervising body must approve it; and you must submit AN IMPACT MEASUREMENT PLAN SPECIFYING THE NUMBER OF BENEFICIARIES, THE SUCCESS INDICATORS, AND THE MECHANISMS OF FOLLOW-UP AND EVALUATION. TWO NUMBERS DECIDE WHETHER YOU QUALIFY: THE ASSOCIATION'S OWN CONTRIBUTION MUST BE AT LEAST TWENTY PER CENT OF THE PROGRAMME COST AND MUST BE EVIDENCED, AND OPERATING COSTS MAY NOT EXCEED THIRTY-FIVE PER CENT OF IT. Budget backwards from those two limits before writing anything else. Where support has been received before, a detailed report is required INCLUDING AUDITED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS for the previous year — so an association that wants a second grant must keep proper accounts from the first day of the first. AND THERE ARE TWO GRANTS FOR WHEN THINGS GO WRONG, WHICH ALMOST NO FUNDER IN THIS PAYLOAD OFFERS: AN EMERGENCY GRANT FOR RAPID ORGANISED RESPONSE TO CRISES AND NATURAL DISASTERS, AND A GRANT FOR ASSOCIATIONS PASSING THROUGH FINANCIAL OR ADMINISTRATIVE CIRCUMSTANCES THAT THREATEN THEIR CONTINUITY. A community body that has taken on a long fight and run short is not automatically finished. There is also a grant for FUNDRAISING AND MARKETING itself, covering operational, technical and media costs of raising money. THE LIMITS: this funds LICENSED associations, so it rewards the constituted and does nothing for an informal group until it registers; approval by the technically supervising authority is a condition, which means the supervising ministry has a say; and nothing here funds opposition to a development. Use it with the ministry's accredited-associations list and the regional green societies recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Regional defenders' centre — external protection and emergency grants, covering this country by name
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING RECORDS A BAR ASSOCIATION, A HUMAN RIGHTS SOCIETY, AN ASSOCIATIONS SUPPORT FUND AND REGIONAL GREEN SOCIETIES — ALL OF THEM DOMESTIC AND ALL OF THEM WORKING WITHIN THE STATE. THIS ORGANISATION IS OUTSIDE IT, AND NAMES THIS COUNTRY AMONG THE ELEVEN IN ITS REMIT. WHAT IT PROVIDES: EMERGENCY REQUESTS COVERING MEDICAL SUPPORT, TRAINING, SECURITY, TRIAL OBSERVATION AND EVACUATION; EMERGENCY GRANTS TO PEOPLE AT RISK; and work with United Nations and European protection mechanisms including A TEMPORARY RELOCATION PROGRAMME. THE MOST USEFUL SERVICE FOR SOMEONE NOT IN TROUBLE IS THE LEAST DRAMATIC ONE: TRAINING IN MANAGING YOUR OWN SECURITY. Everything else on the list is for after something has happened; that one reduces the chance it does. Ask for it first. IT SUPPORTS INDEPENDENT LAWYERS ALONGSIDE JOURNALISTS, ACADEMICS AND ONLINE ACTIVISTS. This file has recorded here a bar association and a licence check for choosing an advocate; THE PROTECTION QUESTION RUNS THE OTHER WAY — an advocate deciding whether to take a case is weighing their own exposure, and knowing that external support exists for lawyers is part of that calculation. IT DOCUMENTS AND PUBLISHES IN ENGLISH AND ARABIC AND CARRIES CASES TO UNITED NATIONS BODIES. For a matter that would otherwise remain entirely internal, that is the only route out recorded for this country in this map. THE LIMITS, AND THEY ARE SHARP HERE. IT IS A FOREIGN-BASED HUMAN RIGHTS ORGANISATION THAT PUBLISHES INTERNATIONALLY AND ISSUES PUBLIC APPEALS. Contact is a serious decision with real consequences, and its engagement begins where expression, association or assembly are restricted — not where a permit is granted. ASK EXPLICITLY WHAT CAN BE DONE WITHOUT PUBLICATION, and read this alongside the domestic bodies recorded separately here, which are the appropriate first approach for ordinary matters.

trackers.name: Heritage preservation society — UNESCO advisory standing, and the national register of 36,000 sites created to stop encroachment
trackers.desc: START WITH THE REGISTER, BECAUSE IT IS THE THING THAT PROTECTS GROUND: A NATIONAL REGISTER OF URBAN HERITAGE HAS BEEN BUILT WITH MORE THAN THIRTY-SIX THOUSAND ARCHITECTURAL HERITAGE SITES ENTERED, AND ITS STATED PURPOSE IS TO PROTECT THOSE SITES FROM ENCROACHMENTS OR NEGLECT. FIND OUT WHETHER THE BUILDINGS OR QUARTER YOU ARE DEFENDING ARE ON IT — and if they are not, that is the question to put to the heritage authority before anything else. AND THERE IS MONEY ATTACHED TO OWNERSHIP RATHER THAN TO CAMPAIGNING: THE CULTURE MINISTRY, THROUGH THE HERITAGE AUTHORITY, STATES THAT IT ATTACHES GREAT IMPORTANCE TO SUPPORTING OWNERS OF URBAN HERITAGE SITES TO RESTORE, REHABILITATE AND INVEST IN THEIR PROPERTIES. A FAMILY THAT OWNS A CRUMBLING OLD HOUSE IS NOT A NUISANCE IN THAT FRAMEWORK — IT IS THE INTENDED RECIPIENT OF SUPPORT, which is a far stronger position than objecting to a scheme. THE SOCIETY ITSELF IS THE BODY TO WORK THROUGH, AND ITS STANDING IS UNUSUAL FOR A NATIONAL NON-PROFIT ANYWHERE IN THIS MAP: FOUNDED IN 2010, IT IS ACCREDITED AS AN ADVISORY BODY TO UNESCO IN THE FIELD OF INTANGIBLE CULTURAL HERITAGE, HOLDS AN OFFICIAL PARTNERSHIP WITH UNESCO, AND BECAME THE FIRST NATIONAL MEMBER OF THE UNESCO INTANGIBLE CULTURAL HERITAGE EVALUATION COMMITTEE FOR 2025 TO 2029 — the committee that assesses nominations. It was the second national organisation registered with UNESCO and the first in the region in the heritage field. THAT MATTERS PRACTICALLY, NOT JUST AS PRESTIGE: A BODY THAT SITS ON THE EVALUATION COMMITTEE KNOWS EXACTLY WHAT A NOMINATION MUST CONTAIN. If a community's claim rests on living practices — crafts, building techniques, seasonal use, water management — this is the organisation that can say whether it would survive scrutiny and what evidence it needs. ITS OWN OBJECTS INCLUDE COORDINATING WITH THE COMPETENT AUTHORITIES TO ADOPT PROJECTS FOR RESTORING AND REHABILITATING HERITAGE AND HISTORIC ARCHITECTURAL LANDMARKS AND PRESERVING THEM — so approaching it about a specific building is asking it to do a stated part of its job. It also cooperates with similar associations at home and abroad, publishes research, and RUNS TRAINING COURSES, which this file has repeatedly found is the cheapest thing any organisation can give. A SECOND ASSOCIATION IS WORTH KNOWING ABOUT TOO: it runs OPEN MEMBERSHIPS WITH COURSES RESERVED FOR MEMBERS, and has delivered a course PREPARING SPECIALISTS IN COMMUNITY AWARENESS OF HERITAGE — which is training aimed precisely at people who want to organise their neighbours around a place. THE LIMITS: these are heritage bodies working with ministries and under royal patronage — they restore, document, train and advise, and NOTHING FOUND SHOWS EITHER OPPOSING A DEVELOPMENT. Their remit is buildings and cultural practice, not ecology or planning law. And registration of a site does not by itself stop a project; it changes what may lawfully be done to it, which is why the register entry is the first thing to establish. Read this with the regional green societies and the associations support fund recorded separately here.

trackers.name: Federal Competitiveness & Statistics Centre
trackers.desc: United Arab Emirates's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in the United Arab Emirates.

trackers.name: State Audit Institution (SAI)
trackers.desc: National — supreme audit institution of the United Arab Emirates. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in the United Arab Emirates.

trackers.name: National Economic Register (NER)
trackers.desc: National — UAE National Economic Register; verify any licensed company nationwide. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: UAE Accountability Authority
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of United Arab Emirates — audits government accounts and the use of public money.

trackers.name: UAE Ministry of Justice
trackers.desc: Federal Ministry of Justice portal with judicial services and a published judgments collection. · Find here: the UAE Ministry of Justice — federal court services and legal information.

trackers.name: Kuwait Regional Convention (ROPME) — and its Judicial Commission
trackers.desc: THE ONE BINDING ENVIRONMENTAL INSTRUMENT COVERING ALL EIGHT GULF STATES. The Kuwait Regional Convention for Cooperation on the Protection of the Marine Environment from Pollution was signed 24 April 1978 and entered into force 1 July 1979 — 30 articles, described as the basic legal instrument binding the eight States of the Region. ALL EIGHT ARE FULL PARTIES: ROPME records ‘no signatories without ratification, acceptance, approval or accession’, so unlike some regional instruments there is no signed-but-unratified state to argue about. ARTICLE II fixes the Sea Area by coordinates, from Ras Dharbat Ali (16°39'N, 53°3'30"E) to Ras Al Fasteh (25°04'N, 61°25'E) — a treaty boundary you can check a project location against. Use the term ‘ROPME Sea Area’: it was coined by the Plenipotentiaries to achieve unanimity, cooperating in spite of existing geopolitical boundaries, and it is the name all eight accepted. THE ORGAN MOST PEOPLE DO NOT KNOW EXISTS: alongside the Council and Secretariat, ROPME has a Judicial Commission, established March 1989, of 6 nationals of Member States highly qualified in international law. In a region with almost no environmental litigation route, a standing judicial commission under a ratified convention is the most significant legal fact available — though this entry does not assert that individuals may petition it; establish who may seise it first. AN EVIDENCE SOURCE THAT NEEDS NO SITE ACCESS: ROPME's scientific bodies include a Remote Sensing Unit, alongside RIIS and MEMAC. WHICH PROTOCOL FITS YOUR ISSUE: oil-spill emergency response; land-based sources of pollution — the limb for a coastal development, discharge or reclamation; and transboundary movement of hazardous wastes. Development is named as a stressor in ROPME's own statement of purpose. At stake: over 20 species of dolphin and whale, all five subtropical turtle species, and more than 1,000 fish species, most endemic.

trackers.name: MBZ Species Conservation Fund — frame it as species work, not climate
trackers.desc: DO NOT DRESS A SPECIES PROJECT UP AS A CLIMATE PROJECT HERE — which is the opposite of the advice that fits almost every other fund in this map. The MBZ Fund was established on the basis that direct species conservation has lost out to wider concerns such as climate change, sustainability and poverty alleviation, and is now seen as a by-product of larger issues, leaving underfunded field biologists and wardens. It exists to correct that displacement, so frame the work as direct, field-based species conservation. A philanthropic endowment announced at the World Conservation Congress in Barcelona, October 2008, taking applications since March 2009; managing director Razan Khalifa Al Mubarak, also President of IUCN. By end-2010 it had disbursed just over US$5 million to about 380 projects in almost 100 countries; awards run up to US$25,000. TWO UNUSUAL ELIGIBILITY POINTS: it covers all animal, plant AND FUNGI species — fungi are named, which almost no other fund in this map does — and its focus includes data-deficient species, so you need not prove the species is threatened; where the problem is that nobody knows, that is itself a qualifying category. Individual conservationists may apply, and priority goes to projects supporting young conservationists. Funding is for direct conservation impact rather than administrative costs. HOW IT RUNS: three rounds a year, March, June and October; the Fund forwards recommendations to an independent body, so its staff are not the final decision-makers; and late submissions are automatically moved to the next round — missing a deadline costs a cycle, not the application. Apply online in English; the form requires a budget, references and permits, so have your permissions in order before applying. READ THE PROJECTS DATABASE FIRST — searchable by species, IUCN classification, continent and year, it shows what has been funded for comparable species in comparable places. NOTE: THIS FUND IS GLOBAL, NOT REGIONAL — it is recorded here because this country holds no other funding entry, not because Gulf applicants receive any preference.

trackers.name: Emirates Nature-WWF — read the board list before you approach it: the regulators and economic authorities sit on it
trackers.desc: THIS IS THE UAE'S PRINCIPAL ENVIRONMENTAL CHARITY AND IT IS NOT AN ADVERSARIAL BODY — CHECK WHO SITS ON THE BOARD BEFORE YOU PLAN AROUND IT. Its published board includes the Vice Chairman of the Environment Agency – Abu Dhabi, the Chairwoman of the Environment and Protected Areas Authority, the Minister of Economy, a Minister of State, the Director General of Fujairah Municipality and the Director General of Dubai's Department of Economy and Tourism. The regulator you would be objecting to and the authority promoting the development are represented in the same room. That is not a criticism of its conservation work; it is the fact that determines what you can realistically ask it for. WHAT IT CAN GIVE YOU: data and volunteer capacity. Its Leaders of Change programme reports more than 10,000 participants, 40,000 volunteer hours and 100,000 data points collected for science, and the organisation works on Hajar mountain range conservation and on building a network of protected areas and ecological corridors across the emirates. Founded 2001; contact via the Contact Us page on its own site. WHAT NO ONE IN THE UAE APPEARS TO OFFER: this search found no independent public-interest environmental law practice, no land trust, and no community objection fund in the country. Land protection runs through the state — the Zayed Protected Areas Network is managed by the Environment Agency – Abu Dhabi, and reserve designations are made by leadership direction rather than by petition. A resident's realistic route is therefore evidentiary and administrative: assemble species and habitat evidence for the site, use the citizen-science channels above to generate a record, and address the relevant emirate-level environment authority directly. Record this as an established absence rather than an unfinished search.

trackers.name: Emirates Natural History Group — its volunteers found a mammal two official government surveys had missed
trackers.desc: THE SINGLE MOST USEFUL FACT ABOUT THIS GROUP IS WHAT IT FOUND: in March 1997 ENHG members on a birdwatching outing rediscovered the Arabian tahr on Jebel Hafit, a mammal considered extinct in the UAE, unseen for over fifteen years and NOT RECORDED BY TWO EXTENSIVE OFFICIAL SURVEYS IN 1986 AND 1990. If a developer's assessment reports that nothing of note lives on your site, that precedent is the answer — absence from an official survey is not evidence of absence, and it has been demonstrated here in the clearest possible way. Ask this group what its members have recorded at your location before accepting anyone's baseline. IT HOLDS THE RECORD ITSELF: Tribulus, established 1991 and still published, is the journal of record for UAE natural history and the only peer-reviewed English-language scientific journal of its kind in the country, carrying species occurrence records and species new to science; back issues sit on the group's own site. Members also get access to its natural history and archaeology library by arrangement, and the group runs expert-led field trips including survey work and mangrove visits. AND IT GIVES MONEY, WHICH ALMOST NOTHING ELSE IN THIS COUNTRY DOES: it has funded field research, including a grant that let the UAE Dolphin Project buy equipment for a survey around Saadiyat Island, and in 2014 it funded production of a shark and ray identification guide. The sums are small and the purpose is research rather than campaigning, but in a country where this file has found no community objection fund at all, a body that pays for a survey is worth knowing. WHAT IT IS: described on its own chapter pages as the oldest non-governmental organisation dealing with environmental topics in the United Arab Emirates, and identified in its own journal as a non-governmental member of IUCN. Founded in Abu Dhabi in the mid-1970s, with chapters since established in Al Ain, Dubai, Fujairah and Ras Al Khaimah, so there is a chapter near most of the country. Membership is inexpensive and open to individuals and families; the group does not meet in July and August. THE LIMITS, PLAINLY: this is a natural history society, not a campaign. It will not object to a scheme, litigate or hold land, its membership is largely amateur naturalists and long-term expatriate residents, and it operates comfortably within UAE establishment structures. Use it for records, for the journal, for the library and for a small research grant — and read it alongside the Emirates Nature-WWF entry in this file, whose board includes the regulators and economic authorities a project would be argued in front of. Two small notes: founding is given as both 1976 and 1977 across sources, and the Abu Dhabi chapter runs its membership through a separate hosted platform rather than the main domain.

trackers.name: Rufford Small Grants — the UAE is named eligible, and it funds a person rather than an institution
trackers.desc: THE UNITED ARAB EMIRATES APPEARS ON THIS FOUNDATION'S ELIGIBLE COUNTRY LIST, WHICH IS THE FIRST OPEN FUNDING ROUTE THIS FILE HAS FOUND FOR THE COUNTRY. Searching the UAE previously established that no independent public-interest environmental law practice, land trust or community objection fund could be found, and that its principal environmental charity has the regulators and economic authorities on its own board. A foreign funder taking applications from individuals sidesteps all of that. NO DEADLINES — apply at any time of year. Applicants are individuals and small groups, with the focus on people early in a conservation career, particularly current or recent MSc and PhD students; undergraduates are not funded. CHECK THE SPECIES TEST FIRST: work on any species not listed as Least Concern globally on the IUCN Red List qualifies, as does work on species not yet assessed but thought to be globally threatened. Habitat work, human-wildlife conflict and community education qualify without a species focus. STAGED FUNDING from up to £7,000 to about £18,000 across four grants, each requiring the last to be completed and reported, with those reports published on the applicant's own page — a public, independent record of work done, which is worth something in itself where documentation is otherwise controlled. One application per twelve months; twelve months after a rejection before reapplying; the foundation covers half to all of a project and wants evidence of any co-funding; no pure research without conservation benefit, no self-fundraised expeditions. Pair with the natural history society recorded here, whose members' records established that an official survey had missed a mammal thought extinct — an application resting on that kind of prior record is stronger than one starting from nothing.

trackers.name: Accountability Counsel — the UAE is not among the Gulf states from which nobody has ever complained
trackers.desc: THIS ORGANISATION'S OWN RESEARCH NAMES EIGHT MIDDLE EASTERN COUNTRIES AS PLACES FROM WHICH NO COMMUNITY COMPLAINT HAS EVER REACHED A DEVELOPMENT BANK'S ACCOUNTABILITY OFFICE — INCLUDING BAHRAIN, KUWAIT, OMAN, QATAR AND SAUDI ARABIA. THE UAE IS NOT AMONG THEM. Of fourteen Middle Eastern countries counted, thirty complaints had been submitted from six. That does not tell you a complaint from the UAE will succeed, but it does mean this route is not untried here in the way it is next door — and it is worth asking this organisation what has been filed before you start. WHAT IT DOES: at the request of communities it assists people in using accountability offices to defend their rights and remedy harm caused by internationally financed projects. An accountability office sits inside the lending institution, operates independently of it, reports to its highest leadership, and can conduct compliance investigations or convene dispute resolution — entirely outside the national courts, which matters in a country where this file could find no independent public-interest environmental law practice at all. THE SUPPORT SCALES TO WHAT YOU CAN USE: from multi-year accompaniment through a whole complaint down to a limited review of your key documents — so a community that needs someone qualified to read a financing agreement and say whether an accountability office applies can ask for exactly that and nothing more. It is expert in the mechanisms of the World Bank Group, regional development banks, export credit agencies and OECD National Contact Points, and it partners with local lawyers to run the international complaint alongside a domestic strategy rather than instead of one. ITS DATABASE OF EVERY COMPLAINT EVER FILED TO EVERY ACCOUNTABILITY OFFICE IS FREE AND PUBLIC, so checking what has been filed against your project's lender, or from this country, costs nothing. THE DECIDING QUESTION IS WHO IS FINANCING THE PROJECT: no international public or development finance means no accountability office and no route here. Founded 2009, having worked with communities in fifty countries, headquartered in the United States with a regional presence in Asia; no casework of its own in the UAE could be established. This is the first entry for this country offering legal representation of any kind.

trackers.name: United Arab Emirates University — decade-by-decade coastline change, and conservation scenarios modelled with and without dredging
trackers.desc: ITS RESEARCHERS PUBLISHED WORK IDENTIFYING COASTAL AND MARINE PRIORITY AREAS FOR CONSERVATION IN THE COUNTRY, AND MODELLED IT AS EIGHT PLANNING SCENARIOS — varying the conservation targets, whether existing marine protected areas were counted, and WHETHER DREDGING WAS TAKEN INTO ACCOUNT, dredging being identified in that work as an activity linked with coastal development. A community objecting to a coastal scheme is almost always told there is no alternative. This is published, peer-reviewed work that models several, produced with the national environment agency and an overseas university — which makes it hard to dismiss as advocacy. AND ITS GEOGRAPHY DEPARTMENT PUBLISHED THE SPATIOTEMPORAL VARIATION OF THE COUNTRY'S COASTLINE FOR EACH DECADE FROM 1991 TO 2021. A decade-by-decade record of where the shoreline actually was is the single most useful document for anyone contesting reclamation or arguing that a coast has already absorbed enough — this file has repeatedly found that communities lack a before-record, and here one exists for an entire national coast. THE WIDER LITERATURE IS OPEN ACCESS AND SAYS WHAT A DEVELOPER'S ASSESSMENT WILL NOT: a systematic review of fifty years of Gulf coastal urbanisation, by researchers at another university in the country, records that development accelerated in the early 2000s with large-scale coastal MEGA-PROJECTS and produced significant habitat modification and land-cover change. It also notes that remote sensing research has concentrated on the southern and western Gulf coasts and that the northern Gulf is far less studied — so a reader in Kuwait or Iraq should expect thinner published evidence than one in the Emirates. HOW TO USE A UNIVERSITY RATHER THAN AN ORGANISATION: find the published work first, then the named department. The relevant work here sits in biology and in a department of geography and urban sustainability, and the country's universities are described in the literature as a principal source of environmental data for researchers and government departments alike. THE LIMITS: this is a state university and it will not campaign; there is no community request route, only research collaboration; and the priority-areas work was produced WITH the national environment agency, which is also the regulator — useful for credibility, but it means the analysis was not designed to oppose anything. Take the data and the scenarios; take the objection elsewhere.

trackers.name: Dubai's voluntary legal services portal — free lawyers, chosen by the area of law they volunteer in
trackers.desc: THE PORTAL IS OPEN TO ALL MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC SEEKING FREE LEGAL SERVICES, and it works by connecting them to volunteering advocates and legal consultancy firms in the emirate. An individual registers with a few basic personal details; participating firms register their own details and SPECIFY THE AREAS OF LAW IN WHICH THEY ARE QUALIFIED TO VOLUNTEER, and those firm details are then made available to the public. THAT LAST POINT IS THE USABLE ONE: YOU CAN SEE WHICH FIRMS VOLUNTEER IN WHICH FIELD AND APPROACH ONE WHOSE PRACTICE MATCHES A PROPERTY, PLANNING OR ADMINISTRATIVE DISPUTE, rather than taking whoever is assigned. This file has recorded across the region that framing a land dispute as a property or administrative matter, not an environmental one, is what gets it taken seriously; here you can choose a lawyer on exactly that basis. It is reachable through the department's website and through an application on the main mobile stores. THE SAME DEPARTMENT PUBLISHES A DIRECTORY OF ALL ADVOCATES AND LEGAL CONSULTANTS REGISTERED WITH IT, including the licensed firms they work in, with a published address, telephone number and separate email addresses for advocates and for legal consultants. Use it to confirm that anyone you are about to instruct is licensed — the Saudi bar publishes an equivalent register, and this file recorded in R158 that verifying a lawyer is real is the first practical step. NOW THE CONFLICT, AND IT IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN INCIDENTAL: THE DEPARTMENT RUNNING THIS PORTAL IS THE GOVERNMENT'S OWN LAWYER. Its functions include representing the government and government entities in proceedings brought by or against them, and receiving complaints and claims against government entities with a view to settling them amicably. If your dispute is with a government entity or a state-linked developer, the body operating the free legal channel is the body that would defend the other side. That does not make the volunteering firms unusable — they are private firms — but establish early who your opponent is, and do not route sensitive information through the department itself. THE OTHER LIMIT: reported practice is that free legal help in the emirate concentrates on labour, family and social welfare matters, so a land or planning case may be harder to place. Ask which firms volunteer in property and administrative law before assuming none does. The department was established in 2008 and also licenses and supervises the advocacy and legal consultancy professions in the emirate, which is why it can convene the profession at all.

trackers.name: Abu Dhabi Judicial Department Legal Aid Section — it pays for the lawyer, the expert and the notices
trackers.desc: IT PAYS THE EXPERT'S FEE IN FULL, AND THAT IS THE PART THAT MATTERS FOR LAND. Its published legal aid package covers guidance on litigation procedure, PAYMENT OF THE LAWYER'S FEES for those who are not well off, PAYMENT OF THE EXPERT'S FEE where a court orders an expert to study a case filed by or against a financially distressed person, and payment of the cost of serving notices by publication in newspapers. This file has recorded in four countries that the court-appointed expert is what decides a land case, and that communities lose because they cannot pay for evidence. A scheme that covers the expert removes that obstacle directly.
