trackers.desc: IN A COUNTRY WHOSE COURTS AND ADMINISTRATION ARE DIVIDED BY CONFLICT, THE QUESTION IS OFTEN NOT WHICH DOMESTIC REMEDY TO USE BUT WHETHER ANY EXISTS. THIS ORGANISATION REPRESENTS INDIVIDUALS SUBJECTED TO SEVERE HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS BEFORE INTERNATIONAL PROTECTION MECHANISMS — UNITED NATIONS SPECIAL PROCEDURES AND TREATY BODIES — which are reachable regardless of which authority controls the ground you live on. IT IS A GENEVA-BASED LEGAL ADVOCACY ORGANISATION founded in 2018, and it works directly with VICTIMS, THEIR FAMILIES AND THEIR LAWYERS: documenting cases, PROVIDING LEGAL ASSISTANCE, and analysing the patterns behind violations rather than treating each as isolated. THE PRACTICAL POINT FOR THIS COUNTRY: THE APPROACH CAN COME FROM A LAWYER OR A LOCAL ORGANISATION RATHER THAN FROM THE PERSON AT RISK. This file records here a women's union legal department with neighbourhood lawyers, free legal offices and the bar's duty to assign counsel; ANY OF THOSE COULD CARRY A CASE OUTWARD, which matters where the person concerned may be detained, displaced or unreachable. IT ALSO DOCUMENTS TRANSNATIONAL REPRESSION AND POLITICALLY MOTIVATED EXTRADITION arising from warrants circulated through regional channels — relevant in a country from which very many people have left, because leaving is not always the end of the risk. THE LIMITS, AND THEY ARE REAL HERE. IT ADDRESSES SEVERE VIOLATIONS AGAINST PEOPLE, NOT LAND OR PLANNING DECISIONS. International mechanisms are slow and produce findings and pressure rather than remedies on the ground. Communications about a divided country face contested facts and multiple de facto authorities. AND SUBMITTING A CASE PUBLICLY NAMES PEOPLE — ask first what can be done without publication. Use it with the legal and humanitarian routes recorded separately here.

trackers.name: Conservation action fund — up to fifty thousand euros for habitat work, and it deliberately looks for underfunded places
trackers.desc: THE SELECTION CRITERION IS THE REASON THIS BELONGS IN THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING RATHER THAN A RICHER ONE: THE FUND FOCUSES ON UNDERFUNDED SPECIES AND CONSERVATION LEADERS. Being in a place where almost no conservation money reaches is not a weakness in this application — IT IS WHAT THE FUND SAYS IT IS LOOKING FOR. WHAT IT PAYS FOR: LOCALLY LED, SCIENCE-BASED ACTION AND RESEARCH TO PROTECT THREATENED ANIMAL SPECIES AND THE HABITATS THEY DEPEND ON, across a list of regions that expressly includes the Middle East. TWO GRANT SIZES: CONSERVATION ACTION GRANTS OF UP TO FIFTY THOUSAND EUROS for on-the-ground work improving the status of threatened species and their habitats, AND RESEARCH SUPPORT GRANTS OF UP TO SEVEN THOUSAND EUROS for young scientists. THE SMALLER GRANT IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES SHOULD LOOK AT FIRST. Seven thousand euros for a young researcher to establish what lives on a threatened area is a modest, winnable sum — and this file has argued repeatedly that documentation is the missing step and that nobody funds it. HERE IS A GRANT WHOSE WHOLE PURPOSE IS TO PAY A YOUNG SCIENTIST TO PRODUCE IT. Pair the application with a university department: the researcher applies, the community provides the site, the access and the local knowledge. THE FOUNDATION'S OWN PRIORITIES REACH BEYOND SINGLE SPECIES AND ARE WORTH QUOTING IN AN APPLICATION: CRITICAL HABITAT PROTECTION — maintaining, restoring and protecting critical habitats and functional ecosystems — and SUSTAINABLE RESOURCE USE COVERING FORESTS, WATER AND RANGELANDS. RANGELANDS AND WATER ARE NAMED, which is precisely what this country's land disputes are about. TWO WARNINGS ABOUT TIMING, AND BOTH MATTER BEFORE ANYONE PLANS AROUND THIS. THE FUND IS A FIVE-YEAR INITIATIVE RUNNING TO 2026, SO ITS CONTINUATION BEYOND THAT IS UNKNOWN AND MUST BE CHECKED. AND DIRECT APPLICATIONS TO THE FOUNDATION ARE REPORTED AS PAUSED UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE — the working route is the FIXED-DEADLINE CALLS run by the species programme that co-manages the fund, so watch that programme's calls rather than writing to the foundation. THE OTHER LIMITS: IT FUNDS THREATENED ANIMAL SPECIES AND THEIR HABITATS — a site with no qualifying species does not qualify, however valuable, and plant-only work belongs to the tree fund recorded elsewhere in this map. Applicants must be civil society organisations rather than individuals or government bodies. And in a country divided by conflict, a grant agreement requires a body that can receive and account for funds; the social fund and the cooperative union recorded separately here are the kind of partner that can.

trackers.name: The lands, survey and planning authority — the register, the maps, and a published complaints line
trackers.desc: LAND DISPUTES ARE AMONG THE COMMONEST CAUSES OF VIOLENCE IN THIS COUNTRY, AND THIS FILE HAD RECORDED COOPERATIVES, A SOCIAL FUND AND LEGAL ROUTES WITHOUT EVER NAMING THE BODY THAT REGISTERS LAND. ONE OF THIS AUTHORITY'S FOUR MAIN SECTORS IS LAND ADMINISTRATION AND THE REAL ESTATE REGISTER — REGISTERING LAND, ISSUING OWNERSHIP DOCUMENTS, AND SUPERVISING SALES, PURCHASES AND LEASES. IT ALSO HOLDS THE MAPS, AND THAT IS THE PART COMMUNITIES OVERLOOK: IT CONDUCTS TOPOGRAPHIC AND CADASTRAL SURVEYS, PREPARES MAPS, AND DRAWS UP THE STRUCTURAL AND DETAILED PLANS FOR CITIES AND AREAS. THE PLAN THAT DECIDES WHETHER YOUR LAND IS MARKED FOR BUILDING, ROAD OR OPEN SPACE IS MADE HERE — ask to see the structural and detailed plan covering your area before you argue about anything else, because everything downstream follows from it. IT IS ALSO THE BODY THAT DEFINES WHICH LAND IS STATE LAND AND WHICH IS PRIVATE, and it is charged with RESOLVING REAL ESTATE DISPUTES and contributing to STABILITY IN LAND OWNERSHIP. WHERE A COMMUNITY IS TOLD ITS GROUND IS STATE LAND, THIS IS THE AUTHORITY WHOSE RECORD SUPPORTS OR CONTRADICTS THAT CLAIM. AND IT PUBLISHES A COMPLAINTS LINE — TWO NUMBERS FOR COMPLAINTS OPERATIONS — alongside its website and official channels, and it maintains a team for DEVELOPING SERVICES AND SIMPLIFYING PROCEDURES for citizens. A PUBLISHED COMPLAINTS NUMBER IS A SMALL THING THAT MATTERS: it gives a villager a route that is not a personal favour, and a call that can be repeated and referred to. THE PRACTICAL SEQUENCE: ASK WHAT IS REGISTERED FOR YOUR PARCEL; ASK FOR THE PLAN COVERING YOUR AREA; ASK WHETHER ANY PART OF IT IS RECORDED AS STATE LAND; AND GATHER YOUR OWN EVIDENCE BEFORE ANY OF THOSE CONVERSATIONS. This file recorded in two neighbouring countries that TAX RECEIPTS, UTILITY BILLS, BUILDING PERMITS AND WITNESS STATEMENTS are treated as proof where no deed exists — assemble those first. THE LIMITS, AND THEY ARE SERIOUS AND MUST BE UNDERSTOOD BEFORE ANYONE ACTS. AUTHORITY OVER LAND IN THIS COUNTRY IS DIVIDED, AND PARALLEL INSTITUTIONS OPERATE IN DIFFERENT AREAS: A DOCUMENT ISSUED BY ONE IS NOT NECESSARILY HONOURED BY ANOTHER, AND REGISTERING WITH THE WRONG BODY CAN CREATE A RECORD THAT IS USELESS OR WORSE WHERE YOU LIVE. Establish which institution actually administers land in your district before submitting anything, and take local legal advice — the bar's duty to assign counsel, the women's union legal department and the free legal offices recorded separately here are where to get it. Its current operational reach was not verified in this round.

trackers.desc: National public-finance watchdog; the State Audit Organization of Lao PDR (ASEANSAI/ASOSAI member) audits state institutions, budget use, SOEs & public projects (financial, compliance & performance audit). The SAO has no standalone website; this is its official social-media presence, Laos.

trackers.desc: National budget authority; the Ministry of Finance manages public finances, prepares & executes the state budget, public debt & revenue and publishes fiscal data, Lao PDR. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Laos.

trackers.name: Laos — Department of Enterprise Registration & Management (MOIC)
trackers.desc: National corporate registry; the Enterprise Registration Office / Department of Enterprise Registration & Management under the Ministry of Industry & Commerce registers enterprises & issues the Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC), with a National Enterprise Database, Laos. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Articles 47–49 — be at the demarcation, and put customary use in writing
trackers.desc: THE MOMENT WITH A STATUTORY HOOK. Under the Forestry Law No. 64/NA of 13 June 2019, natural forest is the property of the Lao Nation and the State manages it centrally — but expressly ‘with the participation of all organisations and the people’. Articles 47–49 give local people formal opportunities to participate in forest boundary demarcation at village level. DEMARCATION IS WHERE CUSTOMARY ACCESS IS WON OR LOST: legal analysis records that past demarcation limited customary access, and that the provisions do not account for customary access, resource use, management, exclusion and governance — so the right to attend exists but the categories are narrower than customary practice. Attend, and record customary use in writing on the day. Across Laos, Cambodia, Myanmar and Vietnam the power to set community forest boundaries sits with state agencies, which analysis says often restricts the size of customary land. AND CUSTOMARY USE IS BOUNDED: it is granted for all forest land excluding protection forests and conservation forests — the two categories most likely to cover a high-biodiversity site.

trackers.name: Carbon income, guardian villages, and timber for your own school
trackers.desc: THREE RIGHTS WORTH KNOWING BY NAME. 1. CARBON IS IN THE STATUTE: participating villagers have the right to benefits from sale of planted trees and NTFPs and income generated from trade in forest carbon credits, as defined in the Forestry Law 2019, with forest carbon separately defined as CO2 absorbed by forests measured in tonnes per hectare. That places Laos with Liberia here as a country where community carbon rights are stated in law rather than left to contract. 2. GUARDIAN VILLAGES: Conservation Forest is the official Lao term for Protected Area, and the revised Protected Area Decree (No. 219) was written to clearly describe the rights and obligations of guardian villages — a defined status for villages attached to a protected area. Establish which zone you are in: the regime names a Total Protection Zone, a Controlled Use Zone and a Corridor Zone, and permitted use differs by zone. Co-management models are being built in three areas including Nam Et-Phou Louey National Park under an EU/AFD/WCS partnership. 3. TIMBER FOR VILLAGE PUBLIC USE: timber for schools, health centres, meeting halls, temples and bridges may be taken from the allocated village use forest only, with logging approved by the Provincial Agriculture and Forestry Office under the annual provincial plan — a lawful village route that does not need a commercial operator. NOTE: no PSFM logging quotas have been issued since 2013 under the logging ban, so village forest management is the main route in practice.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: MyCO – Myanmar Companies Online
trackers.desc: National — DICA electronic company register, searchable free (Myanmar). — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Office of the Auditor General of the Union
trackers.desc: National — supreme audit institution of Myanmar. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Myanmar.

trackers.name: PERAC Principles — protected zones when domestic machinery has stopped
trackers.desc: AN INSTRUMENT WRITTEN FOR EXACTLY THIS SITUATION, AND IT NAMES NO ONE. The Principles on Protection of the Environment in Relation to Armed Conflicts — 28 principles adopted by the International Law Commission on second reading on 27 May 2022 and welcomed by the UN General Assembly in A/RES/77/104 of 7 December 2022, adopted without vote — cover the whole arc: before, during and after armed conflict, and situations of occupation. BE HONEST ABOUT THEIR STATUS: they are nonbinding — but ILC documents are recorded as increasingly interpreted by tribunals, courts and governments as ‘reflections of customary international law’. Cite them as that, not as treaty obligations. PRINCIPLE 4 IS THE DESIGNATION ROUTE WHEN DOMESTIC MACHINERY HAS STOPPED: States should designate, by agreement or otherwise, areas of environmental importance as protected zones in the event of an armed conflict, including where those areas are of cultural importance — cultural importance is an express qualifying ground. PRINCIPLE 5 requires States, international organisations AND other relevant actors to protect the environment of the lands and territories that indigenous peoples inhabit or traditionally use, and where conflict has harmed it, to consult and cooperate with indigenous peoples on remedial measures — note that the addressees are not only States, which reaches bodies operating where a government cannot or will not act. PRINCIPLE 3 requires effective legislative, administrative, judicial and other measures. AND THE STRUCTURAL POINT: the ILC chose not to differentiate between international and non-international armed conflicts, so the environment-related conduct of non-state armed groups also comes within their purview — which matters where harm is done by armed groups rather than a state army. The distinctions sit in the commentaries, which should be read together with the principles. CITE ALONGSIDE: the 2020 ICRC Guidelines on protection of the natural environment in armed conflict, UNEA resolution 2/15 (27 May 2016), the 2019 Geneva List of Principles on the Protection of Water Infrastructure, and victim-assistance provisions in the Mine Ban Treaty and the Convention on Cluster Munitions.

trackers.desc: Afghanistan’s court judgments, where published online, can be searched via the WorldLII free-access-to-law network (coverage varies by country). · Directory pointer (one extra hop)

trackers.name: PERAC Principles — protected zones when domestic machinery has stopped
trackers.desc: AN INSTRUMENT WRITTEN FOR EXACTLY THIS SITUATION, AND IT NAMES NO ONE. The Principles on Protection of the Environment in Relation to Armed Conflicts — 28 principles adopted by the International Law Commission on second reading on 27 May 2022 and welcomed by the UN General Assembly in A/RES/77/104 of 7 December 2022, adopted without vote — cover the whole arc: before, during and after armed conflict, and situations of occupation. BE HONEST ABOUT THEIR STATUS: they are nonbinding — but ILC documents are recorded as increasingly interpreted by tribunals, courts and governments as ‘reflections of customary international law’. Cite them as that, not as treaty obligations. PRINCIPLE 4 IS THE DESIGNATION ROUTE WHEN DOMESTIC MACHINERY HAS STOPPED: States should designate, by agreement or otherwise, areas of environmental importance as protected zones in the event of an armed conflict, including where those areas are of cultural importance — cultural importance is an express qualifying ground. PRINCIPLE 5 requires States, international organisations AND other relevant actors to protect the environment of the lands and territories that indigenous peoples inhabit or traditionally use, and where conflict has harmed it, to consult and cooperate with indigenous peoples on remedial measures — note that the addressees are not only States, which reaches bodies operating where a government cannot or will not act. PRINCIPLE 3 requires effective legislative, administrative, judicial and other measures. AND THE STRUCTURAL POINT: the ILC chose not to differentiate between international and non-international armed conflicts, so the environment-related conduct of non-state armed groups also comes within their purview — which matters where harm is done by armed groups rather than a state army. The distinctions sit in the commentaries, which should be read together with the principles. CITE ALONGSIDE: the 2020 ICRC Guidelines on protection of the natural environment in armed conflict, UNEA resolution 2/15 (27 May 2016), the 2019 Geneva List of Principles on the Protection of Water Infrastructure, and victim-assistance provisions in the Mine Ban Treaty and the Convention on Cluster Munitions.

trackers.name: GEF Small Grants Programme — the grant committee has a non-governmental majority
trackers.desc: A GRANT COMMITTEE WITH A NON-GOVERNMENTAL MAJORITY, WHICH IS WHY THIS PROGRAMME REACHES COMMUNITIES WHERE GOVERNMENT-ROUTED FUNDING DOES NOT. SGP operates decentralised and country-driven through a National Coordinator and a National Steering Committee drawn from NGOs, academic and scientific institutions, the private sector, government and UNDP — with a majority of members from the non-governmental sector. Afghanistan has a country programme: the GEF's own SGP manual carries a photograph credited to SGP Afghanistan, from Band-e Amir National Park. GRANTS UP TO US$50,000 go direct to local communities, CBOs and other non-governmental groups across biodiversity, climate change, land degradation and sustainable forest management, international waters and chemicals, with special consideration for Indigenous Peoples, women and youth; over 20,000 community projects have been supported since 1992. ESTABLISH WHICH AGENCY HOLDS YOUR COUNTRY PROGRAMME BEFORE YOU WRITE: under SGP 2.0 the core programme is implemented by UNDP, FAO and Conservation International — no longer UNDP alone — and participation rose to 135 of 144 eligible countries under GEF-8. READ THE COUNTRY PROGRAMME STRATEGY FIRST: an application must show how it responds to or aligns with the targets and objectives of the SGP Country Programme Strategy, and that it is proposed by national CBOs and NGOs — alignment is an express criterion, not an implicit one. SGP applies UNDP's Social and Environmental Standards and the Social and Environmental Screening Procedure to project design — a standard you can hold others to. A complementary SGP CSO Challenge Program, led by IUCN, launched in June 2026.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Uzbekistan
trackers.desc: Official Supreme Court portal (built with USAID/UNDP support) offering case information, reports of decisions and hearing broadcasts. · Find here: the portal and judgments of the Supreme Court of Uzbekistan.

trackers.name: Open Judgment Data (data.egov.uz)
trackers.desc: Uzbekistan's official open-data portal dataset of court judgments (de-identified), separate from the Supreme Court site. · Find here: Uzbekistan's official open-data dataset of de-identified court judgments.

trackers.name: Open Data Uzbekistan
trackers.desc: National — official government open data / budget portal. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this is the broad budget/open-data hub for how money is allocated overall — for the specific firms winning tenders use the procurement portal, and for findings of misspending use the supreme audit institution. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in UZB.

trackers.name: Uzbekistan — Unified Interactive Government Services Portal (State Registration)
trackers.desc: National company registry; legal entities register via the Unified Portal (State Registration Center, Ministry of Justice) with online name reservation & status records, Uzbekistan. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Statistics Agency of Uzbekistan
trackers.desc: Uzbekistan's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in UZB.

trackers.name: Xarid e-Procurement
trackers.desc: National public-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in UZB, and for how much.

trackers.name: Economic-use zone — existing land users keep their land
trackers.desc: READ THIS BEFORE OPPOSING A DESIGNATION. The 2022 decision creating the Markaziy Qizilqum national nature park (1,200,000 ha) and the Oqtogʻ-Tomdi state reserve (40,000 ha) shows the zoning model: a national nature park splits into a strictly protected zone, a recreation zone and an economic-use zone — and lands in the economic-use zone remain at the disposal of the land users and tenants located there. So a national nature park does not automatically dispossess existing users; that is written into the establishing decision, not left to practice, and it answers the commonest local objection to designation. FUNDING IS NAMED IN THE SAME DECISION, which is unusual: from 2023, the local budget of Navoi region, the State Ecology Committee's Fund for Ecology, Environmental Protection and Waste Management, and other lawful sources. A regional (viloyat) budget is a named funding source for protected-area operation — so the regional administration is a legitimate target for funding arguments, not only the centre. The State Ecology Committee is the founder of both areas.

trackers.name: The state programme says its own reserves are too small — quote it
trackers.desc: AN ARGUMENT FOR ENLARGEMENT YOU DO NOT HAVE TO MAKE YOURSELF. The state programme for developing and expanding protected natural territories, running 2021–2028 with a road map for reorganising and expanding existing areas and establishing new ones, states in its own analysis that some zapovedniks have very small areas and cannot fully perform the tasks set by law — that is, they cannot fully protect ecosystems. A government programme admitting its protected areas are too small to work is a citable argument for enlarging one. THE BASELINE IT GIVES: 7 zapovedniks (186,335 ha), 1 complex landscape sanctuary (628,300 ha), 2 biosphere reserves (111,670 ha), 4 national nature parks (555,154.5 ha), 11 nature monuments (3,803.1 ha) and 12 sanctuaries (572,404 ha). Nature monuments average under 350 ha each — the realistic category for a single small site. WHO DECIDES: the Cabinet of Ministers approves both the boundaries and the regimes of nature protection and economic activity — one instrument, so the permitted-activity regime is as much a Cabinet decision as the boundary. THE PLANNING HOOK MOST CAMPAIGNS MISS: under the Urban Planning Code the boundaries of protection zones of protected natural territories are established by urban planning documents — so if a development is proposed nearby, the planning document is where the buffer is defined and can be checked.

trackers.name: Ministry of Ecology complaints route — read the criminal-liability warning attached to it before you file
trackers.desc: THE COMPLAINT CHANNEL CARRIES A CRIMINAL WARNING ON ITS FACE, AND ANYONE FILING IN UZBEKISTAN SHOULD READ IT FIRST. The ministry's own notice states that breach of the legislation on appeals, and the submission of appeals of a slanderous or insulting character, entail liability in the established manner, and that article 237 of the Criminal Code provides liability for knowingly supplying false information about a crime. That is not a reason to stay silent, but it is a reason to file narrowly: document what you observed, attach evidence, give dates and coordinates, and do not characterise anyone's motives or name wrongdoing you cannot evidence. Write the complaint as a report of facts, not as an accusation. THE MOST USEFUL THING ON THE SITE IS NOT THE COMPLAINT FORM BUT THE REGISTER: the ministry publishes a register of state environmental expertise conclusions, so you can establish whether a project has an expertise conclusion at all and what it says, before arguing about anything else. Pair that with the published procedure for handling appeals and information requests, which sets out how a request must be dealt with. HOW TO REACH IT: applications, proposals and complaints go through the citizens' appeals page; the ministry also runs trust lines on 1205 and 1275 and a call centre for waste matters, and states that proposals and complaints made on those numbers will not be left unattended. THE MINISTRY HAS DOCUMENTED ITS OWN FAILURE HERE, WHICH IS WORTH QUOTING BACK: it ran a study of the handling of public complaints about illegal tree felling, refuse accumulating in unauthorised places, illegal dumps and emissions from large industrial enterprises, and expressly included complaints that the hotline numbers of its regional subdivisions and inspectorates were frequently unreachable. Expect to need a written, traceable submission rather than a phone call. ONE STRUCTURAL POINT THAT EXPLAINS A GREAT DEAL: heads of the regional ecology and environmental protection departments are appointed on the nomination of the regional hokims — the same regional governors who preside over development — according to the founding decree as reproduced in the FAO legal database rather than on the ministry's own pages, so treat it as something to confirm. Note also a canonical-domain trap: this ministry appears under gov.uz/ru/eco and eco.gov.uz, and at least one government information site names uznature.uz as the official address; verify which is current before citing.

trackers.name: Uzbekistan Society for the Protection of Birds — it brought the KBA standard into the country, and KBA status is what lenders screen against
trackers.desc: THE REASON THIS MATTERS BEYOND BIRDS: this society introduced the IUCN Global Standard for Key Biodiversity Areas to Uzbekistan, convening the Tashkent workshop on it in November 2018 with UNDP and GEF support, and framing it explicitly around how KBA status is used in environmental planning AND in investment. That second use is the one a community should care about — international lenders and investors screen projects against biodiversity designations, so establishing that your site is a Key Biodiversity Area or an Important Bird Area can reach a financier when it cannot reach a ministry. This is the body in Uzbekistan that identifies and documents such sites; its stated purposes include the identification, study and protection of important bird habitats, alongside conserving the gene pool of birds resident or migratory in Uzbekistan and training young specialists. ASK IT WHETHER YOUR AREA IS ALREADY ON A LIST before commissioning any survey of your own. WHAT IT IS: a republican non-governmental non-commercial organisation of ornithological profile, bringing together professional ornithologists and amateur birdwatchers, registered with the Ministry of Justice of Uzbekistan on 14 November 2007 under certificate number 664, with regional branches. It carries out field work with local communities — its Sociable Lapwing programme in Kashkadarya was built around raising awareness among local residents as well as governmental and non-governmental conservation bodies — and it represents Uzbekistan in international counts including the waterbird census and the white stork census run with the German nature conservation union. THE LIMITS, AND THEY ARE REAL. This is a scientific society, not an adversarial one: it does not litigate, fund, hold land or oppose projects, and it works alongside state conservation bodies and UN programmes rather than against them. In a country where independent environmental expertise is effectively a state monopoly, it is nonetheless the one independent registered conservation organisation this file has verified — approach it for evidence and designation, and take the objection itself elsewhere. Note two live domains, uzspb.org and uzspb.uz; the former carried the fuller content when checked. Much of the published activity dates from 2016 to 2020, so confirm current capacity before relying on it.

trackers.name: CEPF Mountains of Central Asia — Uzbekistan is a named eligible country, and most of its population lives inside the hotspot
trackers.desc: THIS MATTERS MORE IN UZBEKISTAN THAN ALMOST ANYWHERE ELSE IN THE HOTSPOT, BECAUSE OF HOW MANY PEOPLE LIVE IN IT: CEPF's 2026 profile summary records that of Uzbekistan's roughly 37 million people, at least 27 million live within the hotspot, including the Ferghana Valley. Eastern Uzbekistan is inside it, and Uzbekistan is named in CEPF's own calls as an eligible country alongside Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Turkmenistan. IT IS ALSO ONE OF VERY FEW ROUTES TO MONEY FOR UZBEK CIVIL SOCIETY: this file has established that the country's principal environmental organisation was converted into a parliamentary party and that environmental expertise is effectively a state monopoly. An external fund that accepts letters of inquiry from community groups, women's groups, Indigenous peoples' organisations and small NGOs is a genuinely different channel. Large grants in recent calls ran from fifty thousand to a hundred and fifty thousand US dollars, small grants average around fifteen thousand, and a new portfolio began in 2026 after nearly a hundred projects in the first phase. THE ELIGIBILITY GATE: applications must align with the strategic directions, investment priorities, priority species, priority Key Biodiversity Areas or priority corridors named in the ecosystem profile, which lists them by country in its own tables. Around 170 Key Biodiversity Areas covering some 200,000 square kilometres have been identified across the hotspot, and the 2025 profile update named 126 globally threatened species, nearly twice the 2017 count. TWO TRAPS: individuals cannot apply directly and must go through a civil society organisation — which in Uzbekistan means the registration question is the first one to solve — and CEPF has stated a preference against funding further projects in Key Biodiversity Areas that already hold three or more of its grants. Confirm the current regional implementation team and whether a call is open before drafting.

trackers.name: Rufford Small Grants — Uzbekistan is named eligible, and it funds a person rather than an institution
trackers.desc: UZBEKISTAN APPEARS BY NAME ON THE FOUNDATION'S ELIGIBILITY LIST, AND THE APPLICANT CAN BE AN INDIVIDUAL. Three separate rounds of searching established that Uzbekistan has one verifiable independent conservation organisation, that its principal environmental movement was converted into a parliamentary party, and that environmental expertise is effectively a state monopoly. A foreign fund that will pay a named person to do fieldwork bypasses all of that. NO DEADLINES — applications may be submitted at any time of year. The focus is early-career conservationists, particularly current or recent MSc and PhD students, with others considered against the published criteria; undergraduates are not funded. THE ELIGIBILITY TEST IS PUBLISHED AND PRECISE: any species not listed as Least Concern globally on the IUCN Red List, or not yet assessed but thought to be globally threatened. Habitat, human-wildlife conflict and community education projects qualify without a species focus. STAGED GRANTS from up to £7,000 to roughly £18,000 across four levels, each conditional on completing and reporting the previous, with reports published on the applicant's own page — which in a country where independent environmental documentation is scarce is a durable public record in itself. One application per twelve months; twelve months after a rejection before reapplying; the foundation funds half to all of a project and requires evidence of co-funding where there is any. Pair with the bird society recorded here, which holds the Key Biodiversity Area work: an application resting on an existing designation is stronger than one starting from nothing.

trackers.name: Environmental Defender Law Center — it finds pro bono lawyers, pays the case expenses, and defends people prosecuted for objecting
trackers.desc: IT DOES THE THREE THINGS A COMMUNITY WITHOUT A LAWYER ACTUALLY NEEDS, AND CHARGES FOR NONE OF THEM: it finds lawyers, it provides resources, and it gives grants. On the first, it enlists law firms around the world to act pro bono, screens cases from a lawyer's point of view before taking them on, and then helps decide strategy — scores of lawyers have donated thousands of hours and travelled to distant countries for its cases. ON THE SECOND, IT PAYS FOR THE CASE ITSELF. It created a fund in 2010 for expenses in public interest litigation against those responsible for resource development projects that harm communities, on the reasoning that the sums needed are small but nearly impossible to raise from foundations on a one-time, one-case basis — and it describes this as the only fund of its type spanning the developing world. Roughly a hundred such grants have been made. In one recent year it worked on over fifty matters in twenty-four countries and funded litigation expenses through agreements with lawyers and organisations in fourteen. THIRD, IT SUPPLIES WHAT THIS FILE HAS REPEATEDLY FOUND COMMUNITIES CANNOT GET: expert help. It has access to expert networks and has obtained scientific and technical assistance on numerous occasions, and it writes and files legal briefs on the international human rights dimension, expressly designed to dovetail with local lawyers arguing domestic law rather than replace them. AND IT DEFENDS PEOPLE PROSECUTED FOR OBJECTING — it acts for individuals charged or imprisoned in politically motivated criminal prosecutions. That matters here specifically: this file records that Uzbekistan's own complaints route carries a warning about criminal liability for the complainant, and that the country has one verifiable independent environmental organisation. THE LIMITS: its remit is developing countries, and no case of its own in Uzbekistan or anywhere in this region could be established — its named work is elsewhere. It also selects cases of international significance where a strategy can be replicated, so it will not take everything. Its service is open to approach; treat this as untested here rather than unavailable. Founded 2003, funded by foundation grants and individual donations.

trackers.name: Global Greengrants — it funds groups other funders cannot reach, and it finds them rather than being applied to
trackers.desc: ITS OWN CLAIM IS THAT ITS BOARDS REACH CRITICAL GROUPS THAT MOST OTHER FUNDERS CANNOT, AND THAT IS THE REASON TO RECORD IT FOR A COUNTRY WHERE THIS FILE COULD VERIFY ONLY ONE INDEPENDENT ENVIRONMENTAL ORGANISATION. It launched a Central Asia Advisory Board in 2023, describing the move as extending its reach to areas often off the funding radar. BUT THERE IS NO APPLICATION FORM AND YOU CANNOT SUBMIT ONE. The fund does not accept unsolicited proposals: volunteer advisors who live in the region and belong to the movements they fund identify groups through their own networks and invite them, and the regional board decides. Where forming and registering an organisation is difficult, that is an advantage rather than an obstacle — a group that could never satisfy a registration requirement can still be found and funded — but it changes the task entirely, from writing well to being known. THE SUMS FIT A COMMUNITY RATHER THAN AN INSTITUTION: an average grant of about five thousand dollars, many between five hundred and five thousand, which the fund describes as a deliberate strategy overlooked by larger environmental grantmakers. Over eighteen thousand grants have been made in a hundred and sixty-eight countries, with focus areas including resource rights, ecosystem protection and environmental defenders. READ IT AGAINST THE OTHER UZBEK FUNDING ENTRIES, WHICH ALL REQUIRE YOU TO APPLY: the small grants programme can fund an unregistered group through a memorandum, the hotspot fund needs a registered entity, and the small grants foundation takes an individual's application at any time. This one requires none of those things and offers no way to ask. THE LIMITS: Central Asia is named as a region of work but no country individually; the fund is United States based; and there is no route by which a group can put itself forward.

trackers.name: Front Line Defenders — an encrypted channel and a 24-hour line, where complaining itself carries a criminal warning
trackers.desc: THIS MATTERS HERE BECAUSE OF SOMETHING THIS FILE RECORDED ABOUT UZBEKISTAN ITSELF: the state's own environmental complaints route carries a warning about criminal liability for the person complaining. Where objecting is framed as a potential offence, the first resource a person needs is not a grant but a way to reach help safely. THIS ORGANISATION OPERATES A 24-HOUR EMERGENCY LINE WITH A RUSSIAN-SPEAKING OPTION AND A SECURE, ENCRYPTED EMAIL CHANNEL for defenders in urgent need, staffed by people who can mobilise rapid international support. Its own guidance asks applicants to confirm that the method of contact they give is secure and safe to use — an organisation that thinks about how contacting it might itself endanger you. ITS PROTECTION GRANTS, UP TO €7,500, COVER WHAT A PERSON IN THAT POSITION ACTUALLY NEEDS: digital and communications security, physical security for an individual or organisation, legal fees where a defender is being judicially harassed, medical costs following an attack, and FAMILY ASSISTANCE WHERE A DEFENDER IS IMPRISONED OR THEIR FAMILY IS AT RISK. It also runs temporary relocation and training in holistic and digital security. THE EXCLUSIONS: not for broader human rights programming, not for defenders already in exile, not for salaries or rent. THE LIMITS: no case of its own in Uzbekistan could be established, and it publishes no country eligibility list. Based in Dublin; the service is described as open to defenders at risk without a stated geographic bar. In a country where this file could verify one independent environmental organisation, an external body reachable at any hour on an encrypted channel is a materially different kind of resource from the funds recorded elsewhere here.

trackers.name: GEF Small Grants Programme Uzbekistan — a national grant door, and its news names the organisations it funds
trackers.desc: IT HAS ITS OWN NATIONAL SITE, IT HAS RUN SINCE 2008, AND IT HAS SUPPORTED MORE THAN A HUNDRED PROJECTS — which makes it the most substantial funding door recorded for this country, where this file could verify only one independent environmental organisation across six separate lines of enquiry. It gives grants to non-governmental non-profit organisations and to COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS for locally driven initiatives on biodiversity conservation, ecosystem restoration, climate adaptation, waste and low-carbon solutions, and a call for proposals was open when this entry was written. READ ITS NEWS PAGES AS A DIRECTORY, NOT JUST AS NEWS. They name the Uzbek organisations it is funding and what those organisations are doing — one is preparing a project to bring foreign farmers to deliver practical training to Uzbek farmers through a volunteer expert association. In a country where searching for organisations six different ways produced almost nothing, the list of who a funder pays is the directory that does not exist anywhere else. Every grantee named is a body that was assessed, funded and judged capable of delivering. ITS STATED APPROACH TELLS YOU HOW TO WRITE THE APPLICATION: it looks for technologies and practices that conserve natural resources WHILE creating better living conditions for local people, on the explicit principle that nature can only be conserved when doing so is profitable for the people living with it. An application framed purely as protection will read as a poor fit; one that shows a livelihood alongside the conservation reads as its core business. AND IT FUNDS PEOPLE, NOT ONLY INSTITUTIONS: it describes itself as helping INITIATORS — it calls them champions — who have an idea and a goal, to demonstrate a technology, by providing grant support. That is an unusually open door for someone with a plan and no organisation behind them. IT ALSO COMES TO THE REGIONS: it has held meetings on grant opportunities in Tashkent, Samarkand and Namangan rather than only in the capital. ONE THING THIS FILE ESTABLISHED EARLIER THAT MATTERS HERE: a correction recorded in R60 found that this programme can contract with UNREGISTERED groups through a memorandum of agreement, so an absence of registration is not automatically the barrier it appears to be. Ask directly. THE LIMITS: it is a grant programme, not an advocate — it will not object to a scheme, and it is delivered in partnership with a United Nations agency and alongside government, so it works within the state's priorities rather than against them.

trackers.name: Ferghana Valley community adaptation grants — eight local organisations selected, applications in Uzbek
trackers.desc: IT SELECTS LOCAL ORGANISATIONS TO WORK WITH COMMUNITIES, AND IT NAMES THE PROVINCES. A regional water body's scientific centre has published terms of reference to select EIGHT LOCAL NON-GOVERNMENTAL NON-PROFIT ORGANISATIONS to plan and deliver sub-projects on LOCAL ADAPTATION TO CLIMATE CHANGE with local communities in the Ferghana Valley — open to organisations registered in the ANDIJAN, NAMANGAN OR FERGANA provinces of this country, alongside named provinces of two neighbours. Almost every funding route recorded for this country is national or international; this one is addressed to a specific valley, which is where a quarter of Central Asia's population lives. APPLICATIONS ARE ACCEPTED IN UZBEK, RUSSIAN, KYRGYZ OR TAJIK — NOT ENGLISH. This file has recorded funder after funder whose forms are in English, which quietly excludes exactly the local bodies they claim to seek; this one does not. THE ELIGIBILITY BAR IS HIGHER THAN REGISTRATION AND YOU SHOULD KNOW IT BEFORE APPLYING: at least THREE COMPLETED environment or climate projects at local or community level within the last ten years, plus experience developing training programmes, materials or guides. A newly formed association cannot meet that. BUT A CONSORTIUM OF TWO ORGANISATIONS IS PERMITTED, WITH THE LEAD REGISTERED IN ONE OF THE NAMED PROVINCES — WHICH IS HOW A NEW GROUP GETS IN: pair with an established body that has the record, and be the local partner that has the community. WHAT IT ASKS YOU TO PRODUCE IS ALSO WORTH KNOWING, BECAUSE IT IS WHAT SERIOUS FUNDERS WANT EVERYWHERE: a design and methodology including how target groups and beneficiaries are chosen and how BASELINE AND FINAL ASSESSMENTS will be done, and a monitoring and evaluation plan, both submitted for approval. A group that can write those can apply to almost anything. THE LIMITS, AND THEY ARE REAL: this is a coordinating scientific body under an interstate water commission, not an advocate — it will not object to a project, and its subject is water and climate adaptation rather than opposition to development. THE PARTICULAR CALL'S CURRENT STATUS IS NOT ESTABLISHED HERE, so treat the mechanism rather than the deadline as the finding: this body publishes tender and grant documents on its own releases pages, and that is where to look for the next round.

trackers.name: Madad — free legal advice through 73 regional bureaux and the state service centres
trackers.desc: IT REACHES THE DISTRICTS, WHICH NOTHING ELSE RECORDED FOR THIS COUNTRY DOES. It created legal consultative bureaux in 28 districts and cities from 2019 and had grown them to SEVENTY-THREE REGIONAL BUREAUX by 2022, giving free legal help to local people; and since July 2024 it has organised consultations for citizens INSIDE PUBLIC SERVICE CENTRES ACROSS THE REPUBLIC, alongside an online portal that handles requests in real time. Every other legal route this file records for this country is a foreign organisation reached by email. KNOW THE TWO-TIER STRUCTURE BEFORE YOU ASK, BECAUSE IT DECIDES WHERE TO GO: PRIMARY free legal aid — advice, explanation, help with documents — may be provided by legal clinics and non-governmental non-profit organisations set up for the purpose, and that is what this body does. SECONDARY free legal aid is different: it is the participation of an ADVOCATE IN COURT AT STATE EXPENSE in civil, administrative and criminal matters, assigned after a justice ministry decision or a court or investigator's order, with an information system automatically selecting one of the advocates who work at state expense. If your land dispute is heading to court, ask about the second tier, not the first. ONE RESTRICTION WILL CATCH A COMMUNITY GROUP OUT: THE PORTAL DOES NOT ADVISE LEGAL ENTITIES, and expressly not on the business activity of legal persons. Your association cannot ask — INDIVIDUAL RESIDENTS MUST, which is the reverse of how most entries in this file work, and is worth planning around: send several affected residents with the same question rather than one letter from a committee. WHAT IT IS, PLAINLY: a non-governmental non-profit institution created by a 2019 government resolution on improving the legal aid system and registered by the justice ministry, working in cooperation with that ministry and now delivering inside state service centres. IT IS NOT AN INDEPENDENT ORGANISATION, and this file has recorded the same character in the Gulf — a state-created legal aid service is a real service, and it is not an ally against the state. Use it to learn what the law is, what documents are needed and what the procedure is; take an objection to a government decision elsewhere. ITS OWN PORTAL STATES THAT ITS INFORMATION IS ADVISORY IN NATURE. Its establishment was supported by a foreign embassy in its first phase, and it publishes its cooperation memoranda and its record of work.

trackers.name: Central Asia Pastoralist Alliance — the bloc that changed pasture law and secured 39 million hectares
trackers.desc: IT HAS ALREADY DONE THE BIGGEST THING IN THIS MAP. Members of this alliance were HIGHLY INVOLVED IN DRAFTING AND IMPLEMENTING SIX LAND-RELATED POLICIES, INCLUDING AMENDMENTS TO PASTURE LAWS in three countries of the region — changes that prompted the RECOGNITION OF PASTORALIST AND HERDER COMMUNITY LAND RIGHTS, SECURED MORE THAN THIRTY-NINE MILLION HECTARES OF PASTURELAND, and affected the livelihoods of OVER EIGHTY THOUSAND HOUSEHOLDS. No other entry in this file records an outcome of that size. It shows what the affected users of common land can achieve when they organise across borders rather than village by village. IT COVERS THIS COUNTRY. The alliance spans Afghanistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Mongolia, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan, and it sits inside a global land-rights coalition of nearly three hundred organisations — whose members all sign pledges to uphold gender justice and TO DEFEND LAND AND ENVIRONMENTAL DEFENDERS who are criminalised, intimidated or marginalised for advocating change. THE PROBLEM IT EXISTS FOR IS THE ONE ON THE GROUND HERE: an estimated SIXTY TO EIGHTY-EIGHT PER CENT OF ALL PASTURELANDS IN CENTRAL ASIA HAVE DEGRADED, under mounting pressure on common resources, rising livestock numbers and the WIDE-SCALE EXPANSION OF INDUSTRIES. A community losing grazing to a mine, a plantation or an enclosure is not facing a local anomaly but the regional pattern this alliance was formed to fight. HOW TO REACH IT: through its member organisations rather than directly. Three of them are already recorded in this file — a national association of pasture committees, a rural policy and research fund with field staff in every province, and an association of forest and land users, all in the neighbouring country whose pasture law was among those amended. They have done this before and can say how it was done. WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES: leads advocacy and lobbying at national, regional and global level — including the campaign for an international year of rangelands and pastoralists — and promotes sustainable rangeland use and climate adaptation across the region. THE LIMITS: it is an alliance of organisations, not a body an individual herder joins, and it will not take up one community's dispute. Its work is legislative and regional; the wins recorded are changes to law, not cases won. AND WHETHER IT HAS A MEMBER ORGANISATION BASED IN THIS COUNTRY WAS NOT ESTABLISHED — the alliance names the country, which is not the same thing. Ask before assuming there is someone here.

trackers.name: Ecoforum of NGOs of Uzbekistan — the environmental network this file said did not exist
trackers.desc: THIS FILE CONCLUDED SEVEN TIMES THAT THIS COUNTRY HAS NO REACHABLE INDEPENDENT CIVIL SOCIETY. IT WAS WRONG. An ecoforum of non-governmental non-commercial organisations was founded in September 2004 at a conference of the leaders of FORTY-EIGHT NGOs AND INITIATIVE GROUPS, and it exists to integrate their efforts. ITS STATED PURPOSES ARE THIS MAP'S SUBJECT: RAISING THE EFFECTIVENESS OF PUBLIC PARTICIPATION in preparing and implementing the national nature conservation strategy, and CONTRIBUTING TO THE INTEGRATED MANAGEMENT OF WATER AND LAND RESOURCES — alongside building civil society on environmental values, projects on mountain environmental tourism, public awareness work, and SUPPORTING THE DEVELOPMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL JOURNALIST NETWORKS. A community here has, in other words, a national body whose declared job is getting the public into environmental decisions. AND THE WIDER LANDSCAPE IS FAR LARGER THAN THIS FILE BELIEVED: the national ecological movement publishes that it maintains working contacts with MORE THAN 250 SPECIALISED NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS ACROSS EVERY REGION, and names many of them — among them a COUNCIL OF FARMERS, a public association for the sustainable use of WATER RESOURCES, a union of hunters' and fishermen's societies, a women's public fund, regional local associations, and the bird protection society recorded separately here. A farmers' council and a water-users' association are precisely the affected-user bodies this file has found decisive in eight other countries. THE PARTICIPATION ROUTE IS ALSO CURRENT RATHER THAN HISTORICAL. In late August 2026, days before this entry was written, a training seminar was held in the capital for representatives of non-governmental organisations on PREPARING ALTERNATIVE REPORTS under international human rights treaties and on the three pillars of the Aarhus Convention — the RIGHT OF ACCESS TO ENVIRONMENTAL INFORMATION, the RIGHT OF THE PUBLIC TO PARTICIPATE IN DECISIONS AFFECTING THE ENVIRONMENT, and RECOURSE TO THE COURTS TO DEFEND ENVIRONMENTAL RIGHTS. Those are the three things a community facing a scheme needs, being taught to Uzbek organisations now. THE LIMITS, AND THE FIRST IS SERIOUS. THE FORUM'S OWN WEBSITE APPEARS STALE — its published results run to 2011 and a security check in 2023 reported an invalid certificate — so this entry points instead at its listing in an international convention's civil society register. ESTABLISH THAT IT IS STILL OPERATING BEFORE RELYING ON IT. Second, the national ecological movement whose partner list is quoted above holds fifteen permanent seats in the legislative chamber and founded a political party; it is not independent, and its partner list should be read as a directory rather than an endorsement. Third, this is a network and a coordinating forum, not a law practice, a funder or an objector.

trackers.name: The farmers', dehkan and household-land councils — you are already a member, and they can also take your land
trackers.desc: IF YOU FARM OR HOLD A HOUSEHOLD PLOT HERE, YOU ARE ALREADY A MEMBER — MEMBERSHIP HAS BEEN COMPULSORY FOR ALL FARMING AND DEHKAN HOUSEHOLDS SINCE 1 JULY 2018. The councils were established to PROTECT THE RIGHTS AND LEGITIMATE INTERESTS of farming and dehkan households and owners of household land, and they operate at district level as well as nationally. Household plots produce around 87.5 per cent of this country's agricultural output, so this is the body for by far the largest group of land users here. THE PART A HOUSEHOLD CAN ACTUALLY USE: the councils MONITOR AND EXERCISE PUBLIC CONTROL OVER THE FULFILMENT OF CONTRACTUAL OBLIGATIONS IN AGRICULTURE. If a procurement organisation, processor, exporter, agro-firm or trading enterprise breaks its contract with you, this is the body constituted to monitor that — and the justice ministry has separately been directed to maintain systemic control over how such contracts are drawn up and performed, and to hold parties responsible for breaching contract discipline. That is a real lever against a buyer. NOW THE PART YOU MUST KNOW BEFORE YOU APPROACH IT, BECAUSE IT CUTS THE OTHER WAY. The councils were given the right to conduct REGULAR MONITORING BY HOUSE-TO-HOUSE VISITS of whether land is being used for its purpose and effectively — the state of cultivation, sowing, planting of seedlings and trees, greenhouses, livestock and poultry; to ISSUE BINDING INSTRUCTIONS to members about the use of their own land; and to PUT PROPOSALS TO THE DISTRICT GOVERNOR, WHICH HE IS OBLIGED TO CONSIDER, THAT A HOUSEHOLD'S LAND RIGHTS BE TERMINATED. AND THE SHARPEST FACT OF ALL: LOSING MEMBERSHIP OF THE COUNCIL IS ITSELF A GROUND FOR TERMINATING THE RIGHT OF POSSESSION, PERMANENT OR FIXED-TERM USE, OR LEASE OF YOUR LAND — and membership is ended by decision of the presidium of the district council. A body you cannot leave, which can inspect your fields, instruct you, and recommend that you lose them, is not an ally in the ordinary sense. Keep records of your cultivation, sowing and livestock, because “ineffective use” is the finding that starts the process. THE GOVERNMENT'S OWN LATER DECREE RECORDS THAT THIS COUNCIL FAILED TO PERFORM AT THE PROPER LEVEL THE TASKS ASSIGNED TO IT in protecting the rights and lawful interests of farming and dehkan households. Expect to have to press it, and to put requests in writing. THE LIMITS: it is a quasi-official body with compulsory membership and enforcement powers, funded by members' dues; it is not independent, will not oppose a state decision, and its district presidiums decide who remains a member. Compare it with the chambers of agriculture recorded for another country in this file, where compulsory membership carries a duty to represent rather than a power to expel.

trackers.name: Suvchi — a voluntary water association working in six provinces, including the Aral region
trackers.desc: IT IS VOLUNTARY, WHICH IS THE WHOLE DIFFERENCE FROM THE OTHER BODY RECORDED FOR THIS COUNTRY. A non-governmental non-profit public association for the sustainable use of water resources, with a named director — and, unlike the compulsory farmers' council recorded separately here, it has NO POWER TO INSPECT YOUR LAND, INSTRUCT YOU, OR RECOMMEND THAT YOUR LAND RIGHTS BE TERMINATED. For a household with an irrigation or water problem, that difference decides which door to knock on. IT WORKS IN SIX NAMED PROVINCES, AND THE LIST MATTERS: Fergana, Samarkand, Surkhandarya, Syrdarya, Khorezm, and the Republic of Karakalpakstan. That covers the Aral region, where water loss is the defining land question, and the Fergana valley, which this file recorded as holding around a quarter of Central Asia's population and as the target of a cross-border community adaptation grant scheme. ITS STANDING IS THE USEFUL PART. It was a co-implementer of a European Union funded national programme on water awareness in which THE WATER MINISTRY ITSELF WAS THE NATIONAL PARTNER, alongside the European Union delegation and a regional environmental centre — so it is an organisation the ministry works with rather than one it ignores. AND ITS REPRESENTATIVE CO-AUTHORED THE NATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL REPORT ISSUED BY THE STATE NATURE PROTECTION COMMITTEE. That is a documented route into the official record: a body that helps write the national report is a body that can put a problem where officials must read it. This file has recorded across the region that getting a fact into an official document is often what forces a response. ITS PROGRAMME WORK INCLUDED BUILDING COOPERATION BETWEEN THE WATER MINISTRY'S PRESS SERVICE, THE MEDIA AND NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS — which is the introduction a community usually cannot arrange for itself. THE WEAKNESSES, PLAINLY. NO WEBSITE OF ITS OWN COULD BE FOUND, so this entry points at a regional centre's report of the programme it co-implemented; the programme concerned ran to around 2020, so establish that the organisation is still active before relying on it; and it works alongside the ministry rather than against it — nothing found shows it opposing a scheme. Use it for water expertise in those six provinces, for an introduction to the ministry and to journalists, and as a possible route into national reporting; take an objection to the state-paid advocate route and the international accountability bodies recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: The Ombudsman of the Oliy Majlis — parliamentary control over state bodies, reachable on a short-code number
trackers.desc: THE OTHER TWO LEGAL ROUTES RECORDED FOR THIS COUNTRY ADVISE CITIZENS. THIS ONE SUPERVISES STATE BODIES. Its function is PARLIAMENTARY CONTROL OVER COMPLIANCE WITH HUMAN RIGHTS LEGISLATION BY STATE ORGANS, and it exercises its powers INDEPENDENTLY OF STATE BODIES AND OFFICIALS while being accountable to parliament. A community contesting a decision of a district administration or a state enterprise needs a body constituted to look at that administration, not one constituted to explain the law to them. IT IS ELECTED BY BOTH CHAMBERS OF PARLIAMENT FOR A FIVE-YEAR TERM, and a NEW LAW ADOPTED IN NOVEMBER 2024 restates it as a NATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS INSTITUTION that SUPPLEMENTS the existing forms and means of protecting rights and freedoms — which means it is meant to be used alongside the courts and the prosecutor, not instead of them. IT ACTS ON PUBLIC INFORMATION AND NOT ONLY ON FORMAL COMPLAINTS: it has examined, in a supervisory capacity, a video appeal circulated on social media about a named individual's situation. That matters for a community that has published something and been ignored — a documented public appeal can itself trigger examination. IT IS EASY TO REACH, WHICH IS RARER THAN IT SOUNDS: it publishes a SHORT-CODE TELEPHONE NUMBER, a street address in the capital, an email address and its working hours. Almost every other entry in this country's listing requires a letter or a form. NOW WHAT COULD NOT BE ESTABLISHED, AND YOU SHOULD ASK BEFORE RELYING ON IT. Whether it can GO TO COURT on a complainant's behalf, whether an ORGANISATION may complain for an affected household, whether the COMPLAINANT'S NAME IS PROTECTED, whether its scope reaches violations that PREDATE it, and whether it maintains OFFICES OUTSIDE THE CAPITAL — none of these was confirmed. Those five questions decide whether an institution of this kind is a complaints desk or a route, and this file recorded a neighbouring country's commissioner that can litigate against a state body and accept a complaint filed by an organisation. Put the five questions to it directly; the answers change what you should send. THE OTHER LIMITS: it is a parliamentary office rather than an independent organisation, it supplements rather than replaces other remedies, and a complaint to it is a disclosure to a state institution.

trackers.name: Draft acts discussion portal — the hokim's decision appears here before it binds you
trackers.desc: THE INSTRUMENT THAT TAKES LAND IN THIS COUNTRY IS A DECISION, NOT A PLANNING PERMISSION — AND DECISIONS APPEAR HERE BEFORE THEY TAKE EFFECT. Around three hundred and fifty items are under discussion at any one time, INCLUDING DECISIONS OF HOKIMS, presidential decrees, ministry orders and cabinet resolutions. This file recorded that the farmers' council every household must belong to may put proposals to the district governor THAT A HOUSEHOLD'S LAND RIGHTS BE TERMINATED, and that losing council membership is itself a ground for losing the land. THE GOVERNOR'S DECISIONS ARE PUBLISHED HERE IN DRAFT. POSTING IS NOT OPTIONAL FOR THE DRAFTER: all draft normative-legal acts must be placed on the portal by the organisation developing them, under a presidential decree of 2019 and the article of the law on normative-legal acts governing public discussion. If a draft affecting your district never appeared, that is a departure from the rule and worth recording. AND COMMENTS HAVE A STATED ROUTE INTO THE TEXT: after the discussion closes, ALL COMMENTS ARE ANALYSED by the body responsible for preparing the draft, AND THE MOST SUBSTANTIVE PROPOSALS ARE TAKEN INTO ACCOUNT IN THE NEW VERSION. That is weaker than a veto and stronger than nothing — it means a well-argued comment is read by the drafter rather than filed. ONE FEATURE IS WORTH ORGANISING AROUND: USERS CAN SUPPORT THE COMMENT THEY MOST AGREE WITH. A village is better served by one carefully drafted objection with fifty supporters behind it than by fifty separate weak ones — agree the text first, then post once and support it. AND THE PORTAL SUPPLIES THE LANGUAGE TO WRITE IT IN. It also carries REGULATORY IMPACT ASSESSMENT and ANTI-CORRUPTION EXPERTISE of drafts, aimed at identifying provisions that CREATE CONDITIONS FOR CORRUPTION OR OTHER OFFENCES, that introduce EXCESSIVE ADMINISTRATIVE RESTRICTIONS on business, or that cause UNJUSTIFIED COSTS. An objection saying a draft creates conditions for abuse, imposes excessive restriction or imposes unjustified cost is answering the state's own test — which travels further than saying the community disagrees. THE LIMITS: comments are analysed rather than binding; the portal only shows what the drafter posted, so a decision already taken will not be there; it operates in Uzbek and Russian; and it is a state system, so a comment is a public statement made under your own registration. Read it with the ombudsman entry recorded separately for this country, which supervises state bodies rather than advising citizens.

trackers.name: Beekeepers' Association — it publishes the rule that governs access to forage
trackers.desc: IT PUBLISHES THE REGULATION ON THE PROCEDURE FOR THE MIGRATION AND TRANSPORT OF HONEY BEES, AND THAT IS WHY IT BELONGS IN A MAP ABOUT LAND. Migratory beekeeping is how hives reach flowering ground — so a rule about moving hives is a rule about ACCESS TO LAND. A beekeeper turned away from a forage area, or blocked from moving hives to a valley, has a written procedure to point at rather than a grievance to express, and this file has recorded across the region that the difference between those two decides whether an objection is answered. AND IT HAS BEEN SEEN SPEAKING FOR ITS MEMBERS RATHER THAN MERELY PROMISING TO. When movement restrictions stopped beekeepers from reaching apiaries outside the capital, the regional association PUBLICLY ASKED THE GOVERNMENT FOR HELP, warning that at the season when the whole year's harvest is determined the bees could die of hunger or simply fly away — with a named member quoted in the national press. The previous entry in this file recorded a cooperative whose constitution promises representation; this one has demonstrated it. IT IS A NATIONAL ASSOCIATION WITH REGIONAL BODIES BENEATH IT, including separate associations for the capital and its province, so there is a local branch to approach rather than only a head office. IT ALSO PUBLISHES THE STATE'S OWN LIVESTOCK DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME DECREES, which means members can read what the government has committed to for the sector and hold it to that — the same technique this file has recommended in a dozen countries, made easy here because the association hosts the texts. AND IT PROVIDES PRACTICAL TOOLS: mobile applications carrying a beekeeping encyclopaedia and an information-exchange system for members. It also engages outside the country — receiving an agriculture ministry delegation from a neighbouring state, and taking part in an international agency's competition on coverage of the beekeeping sector. WHY BEEKEEPERS MATTER FOR A LAND DISPUTE HERE: bees depend on wild and cultivated flowering plants, so clearing, flooding, quarrying or spraying changes the forage — AND THE LOSS APPEARS IN THE HARVEST, which is weighed and sold. That is quantified harm, from an organised constituency, in a country where this file has documented that land rights can be terminated on an administrative decision. THE LIMITS: it is an industry association concerned with production, marketing and disease, not a campaigning body; it works alongside ministries rather than against them; and nothing found shows it opposing a development scheme. Approach it for the migration rules, for forage evidence, and for a constituency that can put a figure on what a project costs.

trackers.name: OECD Watch — a forum outside the country for complaints about a foreign company
trackers.desc: START WITH THE DATABASE RATHER THAN THE COMPLAINT. It holds the complaints civil society has already brought against companies under the OECD Guidelines, filterable by ISSUE, SECTOR AND REGION — so before writing anything you can read what was argued, what the office decided, and whether anything changed, in cases resembling yours. This payload has told readers repeatedly to find out what worked before; here that is a search box. THE MECHANISM ITSELF: governments following the Guidelines must maintain a non-judicial complaints office, and A COMPLAINT MAY BE BROUGHT AGAINST A MULTINATIONAL HEADQUARTERED IN ONE OF THOSE COUNTRIES EVEN WHERE THE HARM OCCURS ELSEWHERE. For a community here facing a foreign investor in cotton, textiles, mining or energy, that is a forum outside the domestic system, reached in writing and usually without cost. WHAT TO GATHER, ON THEIR GUIDANCE: witness statements, company policies, SCIENTIFIC TESTS, published articles and reports connecting the harm to the company — and the company's own details INCLUDING WHERE IT IS HEADQUARTERED, since that decides which office hears the case. They publish a MODEL COMPLAINT LETTER and seven-stage guidance, and invite contact for help with drafting and strategy. CHECK WHICH OFFICE YOU WOULD BE FILING WITH, BECAUSE THEY DIFFER ENORMOUSLY: the network evaluates them against THIRTY-EIGHT PERFORMANCE INDICATORS, and an official report found THIRTY-ONE PER CENT HAD NOT RECEIVED A SINGLE CASE IN OVER FIVE YEARS. AND DECIDE THE CONFIDENTIALITY QUESTION BEFORE FILING: confidentiality may protect you but can also RESTRICT YOUR ABILITY TO SPEAK PUBLICLY about the case, though campaigning remains permitted where confidential documents and mediation details are not disclosed. In a country where this file has recorded that a public comment is made under your own registration, that trade-off deserves thought in advance. THE LIMITS, STATED BY THEM: the standards are VOLUNTARY, the offices CANNOT COMPEL A COMPANY TO PARTICIPATE OR TO REMEDIATE, and complaints SOMETIMES THOUGH NOT OFTEN produce remedy. Use it alongside the draft-acts portal and the ombudsman recorded separately here — domestic channels for the decision, this one for the company behind it.

trackers.name: UNESCO Chair on Water Diplomacy and Environmental Protection — a named professor, with a telephone number
trackers.desc: IT PUBLISHES A NAMED PROFESSOR, A FACULTY, A FULL POSTAL ADDRESS, TWO TELEPHONE NUMBERS AND TWO EMAIL ADDRESSES — which makes it one of the few academic resources in this entire payload that a person can simply telephone. The chair was established in 2018 at the national irrigation and agricultural mechanisation institute, covers WATER DIPLOMACY, WATER RESOURCES MANAGEMENT AND ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION, and its holder heads the DEPARTMENT OF ECOLOGY AND WATER MANAGEMENT within the hydro-melioration faculty. THAT DEPARTMENT COMBINATION IS THE USEFUL PART: ecology and water management under one head means a single approach can cover what a scheme does to the water AND what it does to what lives in it. WHAT TO ASK FOR IS ANALYSIS, AND THIS FILE HAS FOUND IN EVERY COUNTRY THAT ANALYSIS IS THE THING COMMUNITIES CANNOT BUY: whether a project's water balance is credible, what an abstraction will do downstream, whether a discharge meets the standards, and which department holds the monitoring data. A university department can answer those in writing. THE PROGRAMME'S OWN DESCRIPTION OF WHAT CHAIRS ARE FOR IS THE OPENING LINE OF YOUR LETTER: they act as THINK TANKS AND BRIDGEBUILDERS BETWEEN ACADEMIA, CIVIL SOCIETY, LOCAL COMMUNITIES, RESEARCH AND POLICY-MAKING. NOW THE CAVEAT, AND IT IS SUBSTANTIAL. THE HOST INSTITUTE IS THE NATIONAL SCHOOL OF IRRIGATION ENGINEERING — THE BODY THAT TRAINS THE STATE'S WATER PROFESSION. Its staff and the water administration are the same professional community, and a request that reads as opposition to state water policy will not travel. Ask a technical question about a specific site, seek data and method rather than conclusions, and expect the answer to be framed in engineering terms. THE OTHER LIMITS: it is academic and cannot represent anyone; the listing reached sits on a UNESCO water information platform rather than the institute's own page, so confirm the holder and the numbers before relying on them; and this country's public participation is recorded elsewhere in this file as requiring registration under your own name — an academic enquiry is a quieter route than a portal comment.

trackers.name: Privatising a land plot — turning a use right into ownership, and the coordinates of land that cannot be sold for development
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY WAS THE ONLY ONE IN THIS ENTIRE MAP WITH NO RECORDED ROUTE TO ACQUIRING OR HOLDING LAND. HERE IS ONE: A 2022 LAW, WITH IMPLEMENTING RULES AMENDED IN SEPTEMBER 2025, ALLOWS NON-AGRICULTURAL LAND PLOTS TO BE PRIVATISED — TRANSFERRED FROM STATE OWNERSHIP INTO THE OWNERSHIP OF CITIZENS AND LEGAL PERSONS. THE PEOPLE WHO CAN APPLY ARE THOSE WHO ALREADY HOLD THE GROUND: applicants are citizens or legal persons holding the plot on LIFETIME INHERITABLE POSSESSION, ON PERMANENT USE, OR ON LEASE. If you or your association already use a plot on any of those bases, THE STEP FROM USING IT TO OWNING IT IS A DEFINED ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEDURE, not a negotiation. That matters more here than almost anywhere in this file, because a use right can be withdrawn and ownership cannot be taken as easily. THE PRICE IS FORMULAIC RATHER THAN NEGOTIATED: the purchase value is A MULTIPLE OF THE BASE LAND TAX RATE fixed at the time of privatisation, and the rules set out how it is calculated. A community body can therefore estimate the cost before applying instead of guessing. ONE PROTECTION IS BUILT INTO THE PROCEDURE: where buildings on the plot belong to other people in private ownership, THEIR RIGHTS OF PERMANENT USE, LEASE OR LIFETIME INHERITABLE POSSESSION ARE CHECKED before the plot is privatised. If somebody else's structure stands on ground being privatised, that person's rights are supposed to be examined — so make sure yours are on the record. NOW THE PART THAT MATTERS FOR STOPPING THINGS RATHER THAN BUYING THEM. LAND FOR ENTREPRENEURIAL AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITY IS SOLD THROUGH ELECTRONIC ONLINE AUCTION on a state system — AND THERE IS A PUBLISHED PROCEDURE FOR PROVIDING AND UPDATING THE COORDINATES OF AREAS THAT ARE NOT OFFERED FOR SUCH ACTIVITY. A LIST OF EXCLUDED COORDINATES EXISTS AND IS UPDATED. Find out whether your pasture, grove or lakeshore is on it; if it is not, the question becomes who submits coordinates for inclusion and on what grounds. THE LIMITS: this is legislation on a state legal database, not an organisation — nobody here will advise you, and the rules have already been amended once, so check the current text. AGRICULTURAL LAND IS EXCLUDED FROM THIS ROUTE ENTIRELY. And privatisation costs money at a rate the state sets. Use it with the farmers' and dehkan councils and the free legal advice service recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: The Waqf foundation — an endowment vehicle being rebuilt, and the law it still lacks
trackers.desc: ENDOWMENT IS THE OLDEST WAY IN THIS REGION TO PUT LAND PERMANENTLY BEYOND SALE, AND IN THIS COUNTRY IT WAS DESTROYED A CENTURY AGO. IT IS BEING REBUILT: a charitable public foundation established under the Muslim Board by presidential decree states that its purpose includes THE CREATION OF WAQF PROPERTIES, alongside restoring religious and cultural heritage. It already holds 189 shrine and pilgrimage sites and spends substantial sums on their repair, improvement and upkeep, and it publicly invites traders and businesses in its districts to engage with it. WHY A COMMUNITY SHOULD CARE: an endowment is the one form this file has found across six countries that holds ground OUTSIDE THE MARKET AND OUTSIDE INHERITANCE, and a functioning national vehicle is the thing that makes it usable by ordinary people rather than only by the wealthy. NOW THE HONEST PART, AND IT DECIDES HOW MUCH WEIGHT TO PUT ON THIS. BECAUSE THE FOUNDATION IS A PUBLIC ORGANISATION, ITS ACTIVITY IS GOVERNED BY THE GENERAL LAWS ON NON-GOVERNMENTAL NON-COMMERCIAL ORGANISATIONS AND ON PUBLIC FOUNDATIONS — THERE IS NO DEDICATED LAW ON WAQF PROPERTY. Commentary in the country argues that such a law is needed precisely to set out HOW WAQF PROPERTY IS FORMED, HOW IT IS RECEIVED FROM NATURAL AND LEGAL PERSONS, HOW IT IS ADMINISTERED AND HOW IT IS PROTECTED. Until that exists, an endowment here rests on general foundation law rather than on the inalienability rules that make endowment powerful in neighbouring countries. SO THE QUESTIONS TO ASK BEFORE COMMITTING ANY LAND ARE EXACT: can the foundation receive immovable property from a private person; what document records the donor's conditions; who may later sell, lease or develop it; and what happens if the foundation is wound up. IN COUNTRIES WITH A PROPER WAQF LAW THIS FILE HAS RECORDED THAT THE ENDOWER'S CONDITIONS BIND THE ADMINISTRATION — ESTABLISH WHETHER THAT IS TRUE HERE BEFORE RELYING ON IT. THE LIMITS: it sits under a religious administration established by decree, its recorded activity is heritage sites rather than land conservation, and nothing found shows it holding land for community or environmental purposes. IT IS A VEHICLE WORTH ASKING ABOUT, NOT A PROVEN ROUTE — and this entry says so rather than implying otherwise.

trackers.name: Intangible heritage register — check whether your own practices and cultural space are already inscribed
trackers.desc: THIS PAYLOAD ESTABLISHED TWO ROUNDS AGO THAT INTANGIBLE HERITAGE IS THE OPENING FOR COMMUNITIES WITH NO MONUMENT TO POINT AT — crafts, seasonal land use, water practices, music, festivals. HERE IS THE NATIONAL REGISTER OF IT, WITH THE RESPONSIBLE ORGANISATIONS LISTED ALONGSIDE THE INSCRIBED ELEMENTS. GO AND SEE WHETHER WHAT YOUR COMMUNITY DOES IS ALREADY ON IT. AND ONE OF THE INSCRIBED ELEMENTS SHOWS HOW FAR THIS CAN REACH: A CULTURAL SPACE OF AN ENTIRE DISTRICT IS INSCRIBED, ALONGSIDE A CLASSICAL MUSIC TRADITION, A SONG GENRE BELONGING TO ONE PARTICULAR VALLEY, AND THE SPRING FESTIVAL.
