A CULTURAL SPACE IS TIED TO A PLACE, NOT ONLY TO A PRACTICE — which is the strongest form this kind of recognition takes, because it attaches heritage status to an area rather than to an activity that could be performed anywhere. If your valley, oasis or district already carries such a designation, that is a fact about your ground and not merely about your customs. WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT DOOR HERE RATHER THAN THE ONE THIS FILE USUALLY RECOMMENDS: THIS COUNTRY HAS NO NATIONAL COMMITTEE OF THE INTERNATIONAL COUNCIL THAT ADVISES ON MONUMENTS AND SITES. That is not an assumption — a state construction directorate states on its own pages that the council has more than nine thousand five hundred members across a hundred and ten countries, that professionals participate through national committees, and that IN ITS VIEW THIS COUNTRY ALSO NEEDS TO JOIN so that conservation work can be carried out professionally. THE EXPERT ROUTE THIS FILE RECOMMENDS ELSEWHERE IS SIMPLY NOT AVAILABLE HERE YET. WHAT PARTLY FILLS THE GAP IS AN INTERNATIONAL NON-COMMERCIAL CULTURAL ORGANISATION CREATED IN 2018 ON THE INITIATIVE OF MORE THAN THREE HUNDRED ORIENTALIST SCHOLARS FROM AROUND THE WORLD, devoted to studying, preserving and popularising this country's cultural heritage, and facilitating international exchange of specialists, publications and documentation. FOR A COMMUNITY THAT NEEDS AN EXPERT OPINION ABOUT THE SIGNIFICANCE OF A PLACE, A BODY OF THREE HUNDRED SPECIALISTS IN THE FIELD IS THE NEAREST THING AVAILABLE — and its purpose is exchange of documentation, which is precisely what an outside expert can give. THE LIMITS, PLAINLY. THE REGISTER IS A LIST, NOT AN ORGANISATION: IT WILL NOT ACT FOR YOU, and inscription of a practice does not by itself stop construction. The national commission behind it is a state body under the cabinet, and heritage protection here runs through government rather than through independent societies. The scholars' organisation was verified from a reference record rather than from its own current account of its work — confirm that it is active and who to approach before relying on it.

trackers.name: Environmental legal centre — free consultations and court defence, and the new public power to block land takings where trees stand
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING HAD LAND ROUTES, HERITAGE REGISTERS, WATER BODIES AND FUNDING — AND NOBODY WHO WOULD ARGUE A CASE. THIS CENTRE PROVIDES FREE LEGAL CONSULTATIONS TO THE PUBLIC AND DEFENDS CITIZENS' ENVIRONMENTAL RIGHTS BEFORE JUDICIAL AND LAW-ENFORCEMENT BODIES. AND ITS TRAINING IS AIMED AT EXACTLY THE READER OF THIS MAP: it runs seminars, trainings and round tables on environmental law for state structures, business, non-governmental organisations AND INITIATIVE GROUPS — the last of those meaning unregistered groups of neighbours, which this file has repeatedly found are excluded from everything else. It also writes and publishes METHODOLOGICAL LITERATURE ON ENVIRONMENTAL LAW AND ON HOW TO DEFEND THE RIGHT TO A FAVOURABLE ENVIRONMENT, which is the manual a community needs before it needs a lawyer. NOW THE THING TO ACT ON, BECAUSE IT IS NEW AND IT IS ABOUT LAND. UNDER A PRESIDENTIAL DECREE OF NOVEMBER 2025, FROM 1 APRIL 2026 THE PUBLIC MAY INITIATE A BAN ON THE SEIZURE OF LAND IN SETTLEMENTS — OR ITS ALLOCATION FOR OTHER PURPOSES — WHERE TREES GROW THAT ARE NOT PART OF THE FOREST FUND. READ THAT AGAIN, BECAUSE OF WHAT IT COVERS. NOT FORESTS: TREES IN TOWNS, SETTLEMENTS AND VILLAGES, OUTSIDE THE FOREST ESTATE — THE EXACT CATEGORY THAT NORMALLY HAS NO PROTECTION ANYWHERE IN THIS MAP. AND THE INITIATIVE COMES FROM THE PUBLIC, not from an official. A stand of old trees on ground somebody wants to reallocate is, from that date, a reason the public can put forward for stopping the reallocation. WHAT TO DO WITH IT: ESTABLISH THE PROCEDURE BEFORE YOU NEED IT — who receives the initiative, in what form, with how many signatures, and within what period a decision follows. Then document the trees now: species, girth, age, photographs and location, which is the same evidence this file has recommended for palms and heritage elsewhere. THE CENTRE ABOVE IS WHO TO ASK ABOUT THE PROCEDURE, AND THIS IS EXACTLY WHAT ITS FREE CONSULTATIONS ARE FOR. THE SAME DECREE CREATES TWO OTHER THINGS WORTH KNOWING: A STATE TARGETED FUND FOR RESOLVING NATIONWIDE ECOLOGICAL PROBLEMS, with its own management council — a fund with a named governing body can be asked what it finances — AND AN ECOLOGICAL CONTROL INSPECTION, with environmental prosecutors in three named regions, which is a complaint destination with enforcement powers rather than an advisory one. THE LIMITS: the centre was verified from an international organisation's published study rather than from its own current site, SO CONFIRM IT IS STILL OPERATING AND WHERE, before relying on it. The tree provision was announced in a 2025 decree to take effect in April 2026 — CHECK THAT THE IMPLEMENTING PROCEDURE ACTUALLY EXISTS, because this file has recorded rights elsewhere that were announced and never operationalised. And civil society here works within tight registration rules; the initiative-group route is the realistic one for most communities.

trackers.name: Tajikistan — Tax Committee (Single State Register)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the Tax Committee is the primary single-window business-registration body, maintaining the Single State Register of legal entities & individual entrepreneurs, Tajikistan. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Constitutional Court of Tajikistan
trackers.desc: Constitutional Court of Tajikistan — supreme court (Tajikistan).

trackers.name: Tajikistan — Ministry of Finance
trackers.desc: National budget authority; oversees public finances and prepares the State budget, Republic of Tajikistan. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in TJK.

trackers.name: Extractive Industry Beneficial Owners Web Portal
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Publicly searchable.

trackers.name: Article 8 — local government powers, in a state that owns everything
trackers.desc: THERE IS NO PRIVATE OR COMMUNITY LAND-ACQUISITION ROUTE IN TAJIKISTAN. Article 13 of the Constitution vests land, water, flora and fauna in the state, and the protected areas law makes specially protected natural areas the exclusive property of the state (article 4). The land trust, easement and community-title mechanisms recorded elsewhere in this map do not exist here — do not spend effort looking for a purchase or covenant route; everything runs through designation and management. BUT LOCAL GOVERNMENT HAS ENUMERATED POWERS: the law names the Government, the authorized state body, local government bodies and ministries as the managers of protected areas — and article 8 is headed ‘Powers of local government bodies concerning specially protected natural areas’. In a system where the state owns everything, a statute that separately enumerates local powers is the opening for a locally driven proposal — read and cite article 8. THE LOCAL BODY IS THE JAMOAT, the constitutional self-government authority of settlements and villages, managing several villages, under the Law on Self-Government Bodies in Towns and Villages (1994, amended 2009 and 2017). Article 79: the representative authority and chairman adopt legal documents whose implementation is compulsory in that territory — so a jamoat decision binds within its area.

trackers.name: The Forest Code does not say what you expect — ask which permit law applies
trackers.desc: GAPS RECORDED BY THE UNECE ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE REVIEW, AND THEY ARE USABLE. The Forest Code (2011 Law No. 761) has not been updated; the regimes in the different categories of protected forests are not described in it, and nor are restrictions on economic activities in forests within specially protected natural areas. The Forestry Agency issues temporary seasonal permits that are outside the scope of the Law on the Permit System, and a 2019 official overview noted an ‘unclear legal framework regarding responsibilities and jurisdiction’. So where logging or forest use is the threat, the restriction you expect to find in the Forest Code may simply not be written there — ask which instrument the permit was issued under, because the answer may itself be the argument. THE STRUCTURE TO ORGANISE THROUGH: Jamoat Resource Centres and District Development Councils are established civil-society structures at jamoat and district level, recorded as crucial for cost-sharing, community mobilisation and awareness building. If your issue is a watershed, the Jamoat Watershed Action Plan is an existing instrument with precedent — 8 were run in the northern Kofirnighan river basin. Note too that proposals pass through jamoats and their approval to the Government.

trackers.name: CAREC — two organisations share the name, neither is a grant fund
trackers.desc: ‘CAREC’ IS TWO DIFFERENT ORGANISATIONS AND YOU WILL PROBABLY APPROACH THE WRONG ONE. The Regional Environmental Centre for Central Asia (carecnet.org / carececo.org) was established following the 4th Pan-European Conference in Aarhus, 1998, operating since 2001 as an independent, non-commercial and non-partisan organisation of international character. Its founders are Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan plus UNDP and the European Commission; headquarters in Almaty, with country offices in all five member states (the Kyrgyz office is at 142 Gorky str., office 410, Bishkek 720005). The unrelated Central Asia Regional Economic Cooperation (CAREC) Program is an Asian Development Bank programme founded 1997, based in Manila, with 11 members including Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, China and Pakistan. NEITHER IS A COMMUNITY GRANT FUND. The Environmental Centre offers a dialogue platform for environmental NGOs and representation at international forums and thematic networks, and collaborates with NGOs, government and business — a route to partnership, visibility and project consortia, not an application window. The ADB programme's Climate and Sustainability Project Preparatory Fund (US$3m from Korea, US$2m from China) supports preparation of bankable regional projects and its eligible recipients are developing member countries — states, not community groups. Approach the Environmental Centre's country office for partnership; do not send it a grant application expecting an award.

trackers.name: GEF Small Grants Programme — up to US$50,000 direct to communities
trackers.desc: WHERE THE COMMUNITY MONEY ACTUALLY IS. The GEF Small Grants Programme, running since 1992 and implemented by UNDP, reached 135 countries of 144 eligible in GEF-8, which secured US$135 million for the core programme with nearly US$1 million allocated to each participating country — a per-country floor, so the money is not competed for across borders. Grants of up to US$50,000 go directly to local communities, community-based organisations and other non-governmental groups. Focal areas: biodiversity, climate change, land degradation and sustainable forest management, international waters and chemicals. READ THE COUNTRY PROGRAMME STRATEGY FIRST. Each participating country writes its own CPS emphasising particular themes and geographies, so global eligibility does not mean your region or theme qualifies. Note also that under SGP 2.0 the implementing agency may be FAO or Conservation International rather than UNDP, and the host may be a national host institution rather than the UNDP country office — confirm which applies before addressing an application.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: Aarhus Centres of Tajikistan — seven of them, and the environment committee takes reports over WhatsApp
trackers.desc: SEVEN CENTRES, WHICH MAKES THIS THE STRONGEST PUBLIC-PARTICIPATION NETWORK THIS CHAT HAS FOUND IN CENTRAL ASIA OR THE CAUCASUS. The Committee for Environmental Protection under the Government of Tajikistan states in its own environmental reporting that seven Aarhus Centres have been created and are operating in various parts of the country, and the network's site carries recent field activity, including a joint visit to the Romit biosphere reserve run by the Dushanbe Aarhus Centre with the committee's Tabiat state enterprise, the protected areas institution and the OSCE Programme Office in Dushanbe. Compare Azerbaijan, recorded elsewhere in this file, where the OSCE describes a single Baku centre focused primarily on access to information — two countries usually grouped together, with very different provision. THE REPORTING ROUTE IS UNUSUALLY LOW-FRICTION AND WORTH KNOWING: the committee activated an electronic number for reporting breaches of environmental protection law through WhatsApp, Viber and IMO on 777-16-22-75, stated to operate around the clock. A photograph with a location, sent from the site, is a far lower barrier than a written submission — though the announcement dates from 2019, so confirm the number is live before relying on it, and keep your own copy of anything you send. WHERE THE DECISIONS ACTUALLY SIT: the committee is the central executive body for environmental protection, specially protected natural areas and natural resource use, and exercises state environmental control. Its structure includes a Directorate of State Environmental Expertise, which is the unit that reviews a project's environmental case and therefore the one to address on a specific scheme, a State Institution for Specially Protected Natural Areas established by decree in July 1992, and a separate general directorate for environmental protection of the city of Dushanbe. Committee address: Shamsi street 5/1, Dushanbe 734034, telephone +992 37 2364059. THE STRUCTURAL LIMIT, STATED PLAINLY: these centres are not independent of the state. They operate with the environment committee and with OSCE support, and the Dushanbe centre's published work is educational and field-based rather than adversarial. Use them to obtain information, to find out how and when a decision is being taken, and to reach the expertise directorate — not in the expectation that they will oppose a project on your behalf. Tajikistan has no verified independent environmental organisation in this file: R4 examined the best-known candidate and could not verify a canonical domain for it.

trackers.name: Zan va Zamin — works on land access for the landless, in a country where land cannot be bought at all
trackers.desc: START FROM WHAT TAJIK LAW ACTUALLY ALLOWS, BECAUSE IT DETERMINES EVERYTHING ELSE: land in the Republic of Tajikistan is the exclusive property of the state. There is no private land ownership to buy, so no land trust can acquire a threatened parcel and no community can purchase its way to safety. What people hold are use rights, land shares and dehkan farm certificates — and the whole contest is over who obtains and keeps those. Tajikistan is also among the most land-poor countries in the world, with arable land in the order of 720,000 hectares of which roughly 500,000 are irrigated, so pressure on every usable hectare is severe. THIS ORGANISATION WORKS ON EXACTLY THAT CONTEST: its stated purpose is achieving access to land for landless dehkans, alongside supporting diversified farming methods and conserving agrobiodiversity, with particular attention to the rights of women. Founded in 1999 by a group of women activists responding to the social and economic wreckage left by the collapse of the Soviet Union and the civil war, in which many women were left without husbands and many children without fathers. WHAT THAT MEANS PRACTICALLY: if a scheme is taking land in Tajikistan, the question is whose use right is being extinguished and whether it was lawfully obtained in the first place, and this is the body with two and a half decades of experience in exactly that question at village level. IT ALSO HAS A ROUTE INTO INTERNATIONAL SCRUTINY THAT MOST LOCAL ORGANISATIONS NEVER USE: it was among the Tajik organisations contributing to an NGO alternative report to the UN committee on discrimination against women. Shadow reporting to a treaty body is a forum outside the domestic system, and an organisation that has done it before knows the cycle and the deadlines. WHAT IT IS NOT: a litigator, a funder, or an environmental campaign group. Its frame is agricultural livelihoods and women's land rights rather than opposition to development projects, so approach it about tenure and evidence of use, not about stopping a permit. Pair it with the Aarhus centre network already recorded for Tajikistan, which is where the environmental documents sit. CURRENCY CAVEAT: the material reached on this organisation's own site is undated and the alternative report dates from 2006, so confirm that it is currently operating before relying on it — a caution this file has had to apply repeatedly in Central Asia.

trackers.name: CEPF Mountains of Central Asia — money that reaches community groups directly, in a country where almost nothing else does
trackers.desc: TAJIKISTAN HAS NO DOMESTIC ENVIRONMENTAL FUND IN THIS FILE AND NO INDEPENDENT ENVIRONMENTAL ORGANISATION THAT THIS CHAT COULD VERIFY, WHICH MAKES AN EXTERNAL FUND THAT GRANTS DIRECTLY TO COMMUNITY GROUPS UNUSUALLY IMPORTANT HERE. CEPF's eligible applicants are civil society organisations of every size — community groups, farmers' cooperatives, indigenous peoples' groups, universities, small businesses and non-governmental organisations. Small grants average about fifteen thousand US dollars and are administered by a regional implementation team based in or near the hotspot; grants above roughly twenty thousand are handled by the secretariat and average around a hundred and fifty thousand. THE ELIGIBILITY GATE IS THE ECOSYSTEM PROFILE: every project must link to one of the strategic directions it sets out, and CEPF targets Key Biodiversity Areas and corridors rather than administrative units, so the question is whether your valley falls inside a priority area, not which district it is in. INDIVIDUALS CANNOT APPLY DIRECTLY — they must work through a civil society organisation. In a country where land is the exclusive property of the state and community groups are often unregistered, that is the practical barrier to clear first; the Tajik organisation already recorded in this file works on exactly the tenure questions such a group will face. Calls open intermittently, usually for six to eight weeks, and small-grant applications begin with a short letter of inquiry by email which may be accepted in a specified local language. Funded jointly by the French Development Agency, Conservation International, the European Union, the Global Environment Facility, the Government of Japan and the World Bank. VERIFICATION CAVEAT, AND IT MATTERS BEFORE ANYONE SPENDS TIME: the Mountains of Central Asia hotspot is listed among those currently open, but neither its exact country composition nor the current call status was confirmed on cepf.net this round. Establish both from the ecosystem profile and the open calls page before building a plan on it.

trackers.name: Rufford Small Grants — Tajikistan is named eligible, and no registration is needed to apply
trackers.desc: TAJIKISTAN APPEARS ON THE FOUNDATION'S OWN ELIGIBILITY LIST, AND APPLICATIONS COME FROM INDIVIDUALS AND SMALL GROUPS. That matters in a country where land is the exclusive property of the state, where community groups are frequently unregistered, and where this file could verify only one independent organisation. THERE ARE NO DEADLINES — apply at any time of year. The focus is people early in a conservation career, especially current or recent MSc and PhD students; undergraduates are excluded. CHECK THE SPECIES TEST FIRST: work on any species not listed as Least Concern globally on the IUCN Red List qualifies, as does work on species not yet assessed but believed globally threatened. Threatened habitat, human-wildlife conflict and community education projects qualify with no species focus — relevant for pasture, juniper woodland and mountain water questions. STAGED FUNDING from up to £7,000 to about £18,000 across four grants, each requiring the previous to be finished and reported, with reports published on the applicant's page. One application per twelve months; a twelve-month wait after rejection; the foundation covers half to all of a project and wants evidence of any co-funding; no pure research without conservation benefit and no self-fundraised expeditions. READ IT ALONGSIDE THE TWO OTHER FUNDING ROUTES RECORDED HERE FOR TAJIKISTAN AND NOTE THE DIFFERENCE: the Central Asian hotspot fund and the small grants programme both work through organisations, and the small grants programme can fund an unregistered community group through a memorandum of agreement. This one funds a named individual. Between them, almost any configuration of applicant is covered.

trackers.name: Bureau on Human Rights and Rule of Law — free legal receptions in regional towns, in a country with no state legal aid system
trackers.desc: THE REASON THIS MATTERS MORE IN TAJIKISTAN THAN THE SAME KIND OF BODY WOULD ELSEWHERE IS STATED ON THE ORGANISATION'S OWN PAGES: there is at present no clearly established state system for providing free legal aid to those without means in Tajikistan. Elsewhere in this region a community can be pointed at a state scheme — Kazakhstan publishes its list of participating advocates annually, Armenia's public defender assigns one — and in Tajikistan there is no such list to be on. Non-governmental legal receptions are the route, not a supplement to one. AND IT RUNS THEM OUTSIDE THE CAPITAL, WHICH IS THE PRACTICAL POINT: it operates legal reception offices providing free legal assistance in regional towns, with receptions documented at Khujand and at Kanibadam in the north — the second of these reached by a woman with nowhere else to go on a neighbour's advice, which is how such an office is actually found. If your land is in Sughd rather than Dushanbe, there is somewhere to walk into. IT ALSO PRODUCED SOMETHING THIS FILE HAS FOUND ONLY TWICE ELSEWHERE IN CENTRAL ASIA: a mapping of the country's civil society organisations working on access to justice, women's empowerment and the rights of people with disabilities. In a country where this file could verify only one independent environmental organisation, a published map of who else exists and what they do is the fastest way to find a partner. Its wider record covers access to justice for journalists, the rights of prisoners and former prisoners, monitoring of closed institutions, and documented work on people at risk of statelessness and without papers in named districts of Sughd province — which is relevant to land because a person who cannot prove who they are cannot prove what they hold. Work has been supported through a United Nations development programme project on strengthening the rule of law. TWO LIMITS, BOTH STATED BY THE ORGANISATION ITSELF. Its resources will not stretch to everyone who needs them, because its work is funded by donor grants — approach early rather than late. And it is a human rights body, not an environmental one: nothing found shows it acting on a land or development case, so frame the matter as access to justice, documentation or administrative process rather than as ecology, which is the same framing this file has recorded for its counterparts in Armenia and Kyrgyzstan. For environmental documents in Tajikistan the Aarhus centre network recorded here is the companion, and on tenure the land-rights organisation already in this file.

trackers.name: Environmental Defender Law Center — it pays the expenses of a case, which matters most where no state legal aid exists
trackers.desc: THIS FILE RECORDS THAT TAJIKISTAN HAS NO CLEARLY ESTABLISHED STATE SYSTEM OF FREE LEGAL AID, AND THAT THE NON-GOVERNMENTAL LEGAL RECEPTIONS FILLING THAT GAP RUN ON DONOR GRANTS THAT WILL NOT STRETCH TO EVERYONE. THIS IS THE BODY THAT FUNDS THE CASE ITSELF. It created a grant programme in 2010 for expenses in public interest litigation against those responsible for resource development projects that harm the rights, health and environment of communities — on the explicit reasoning that such cases are relatively cheap to run in developing countries, that the small amounts needed are nonetheless decisive, and that money for a single case is extremely difficult or impossible to obtain from foundations. It calls its fund the only one of its type spanning the developing world, and has made around a hundred grants. ITS SUPPORT ALSO MAKES THE CASE POSSIBLE IN OTHER WAYS: it enlists law firms internationally to act without charge, screening cases from a lawyer's perspective first; it has access to expert networks and has obtained scientific assistance repeatedly; and it prepares briefs on the international human rights dimension designed to work alongside local lawyers arguing domestic law. Its stated objective is to help defenders influence or stop development projects that threaten a community's health, way of life and environment. USE IT WITH THE TAJIK BODIES ALREADY RECORDED HERE: the human rights bureau runs the legal receptions in the regions, and this can pay for what a case then costs. THE LIMITS: its remit is developing countries; it selects cases of international significance where a legal strategy can be replicated; and no work of its own in Tajikistan or this region could be established. Approach it as an untested route rather than an established one.

trackers.name: ANCOT — community conservancies that hold the land themselves, pay their own rangers from it, and federated when outsiders came for it
trackers.desc: THIS IS THE CLOSEST THING IN CENTRAL ASIA TO COMMUNITIES SIMPLY HOLDING THEIR OWN LAND. Since 2008, wildlife management areas have been established that are held and protected by LOCAL FAMILIES OR ASSOCIATIONS OF LOCAL HUNTERS themselves, and this association is the umbrella those conservancies formed. Its stated work is supporting conservancy managers in the conservation and sustainable use of their wildlife, PASTURES, FORESTS, MOUNTAINS and other natural resources — not a wildlife project bolted onto a village but the village holding the ground. THE MONEY MODEL IS THE PART THAT MAKES IT LAST, AND IT REQUIRES NO DONOR: revenue from guided hiking, wildlife watching, photography and strictly regulated hunting PAYS THE LOCAL RANGERS AND GUIDES, and surpluses go into local development projects. A conservancy funds its own enforcement out of its own ground. AND IT USES THE SAME CONVERSION THIS FILE RECORDED ON THE TURKISH COAST: local EX-HUNTERS are the ones who stop poaching, by community members and outsiders alike. The people best placed to take the wildlife are the people paid to protect it. NOW THE WARNING, AND IT IS WHY THE UMBRELLA EXISTS AT ALL: these conservancies were not threatened by a government or a developer but BY THEIR OWN SUCCESS. Economically powerful holders of hunting concessions elsewhere in the country, together with international marketing agents, moved in on community conservation as a lucrative business — diverting the economic benefit away from the rural families who had built it, and putting the traditional management system at risk. Small family businesses could not resist that alone, so the conservancies grouped to create a stronger front. If your community arrangement starts working, expect people with more money to arrive wanting to run it, and federate before they do. WHY IT EXISTS RATHER THAN THE STATE DOING THIS: research on the region records that protected areas, national parks and the forestry committee lack the resources for adequate wildlife management, so communities carry it. Management combines traditional hunters with scientific experts, with yearly surveys of mountain ungulates. It also advises non-governmental organisations, small family businesses and communities on GOVERNANCE AND INSTITUTIONAL QUESTIONS, including how to invest proceeds — which is precisely the skill a community that suddenly has income needs. THE LIMITS, INCLUDING ONE FROM INSIDE: it is built around regulated hunting and tourism revenue, which some readers will reject outright; it works in the Pamirs and mountain districts rather than nationally; and independent research on these conservancies records real internal governance problems, including a leader who gave unclear direction and favoured a few rangers over others. A community joining this model should ask how each conservancy is governed, not assume the model guarantees fairness. Renamed from an earlier acronym in January 2019.

trackers.name: ProtectDefenders.eu — urgent protection money where there is no state legal aid to fall back on
trackers.desc: ONE OF ITS THREE CRITERIA IS THAT LACK OF ACCESS TO ALTERNATIVE SOURCES OF SUPPORT IS EXPRESSLY TAKEN INTO ACCOUNT — which is the strongest thing a Tajik applicant has to say, because this file records that Tajikistan has no clearly established state system of free legal aid at all, and that the non-governmental legal receptions filling that gap run on donor grants that will not stretch to everyone. Say that plainly in the request. The other two criteria are that you are a defender working for human rights consistent with the United Nations declaration, and that you face risk because of that work. A PERSON CAN ASK ALONE: there are separate request channels for individuals and for organisations, so no registered body is needed behind an individual applicant — and correspondence is accepted officially in Russian as well as English, French, Spanish and Arabic, through a 24/7 helpline and an encrypted contact form. THE SUMS ARE MODEST AND FAST RATHER THAN LARGE: emergency grants up to €10,000, averaging around €3,000, rolling with no deadline, covering urgent protection measures — for organisations, capacity building, psychosocial support, security, advocacy training and emergency relocation, with scope to propose other measures. BEFORE ACCEPTING ANYTHING, NOTE ITS OWN WARNING: payment may come by bank transfer or Western Union and WILL SHOW ProtectDefenders.eu AS THE SOURCE, and the mechanism asks recipients to consider the security implications of that and raise them with the secretariat. In a country where independent legal help is scarce and donor funding is visible, that is not a formality. ITS RELOCATION PROGRAMME PREFERS MOVING A DEFENDER WITHIN THEIR OWN COUNTRY OR SUB-REGION where possible, so they can continue working, paying a host organisation to implement it for up to a year and never the full cost. THE LIMITS: the mechanism states it cannot support every defender in need and points elsewhere for those it cannot; its secretariat routes requests to partner organisations rather than assessing grant forms itself; and no case of its own in Tajikistan could be established. Use it with the human rights bureau recorded here, which runs the regional legal receptions and would be the local body able to corroborate a request.

trackers.name: Little Earth — it works with unregistered initiative groups, not only with registered organisations
trackers.desc: THE PHRASE THAT MATTERS IS INITIATIVE GROUPS. It states that it cooperates with public organisations AND INITIATIVE GROUPS and supplies environmental information to the wider public, with the declared aim of increasing the role and degree of public participation in environmental questions. In a country where this file has established that there is no clearly established state system of free legal aid, that land is the exclusive property of the state, and that only one independent conservation organisation could be verified, a body that will work with a group of villagers who have registered nothing is a scarce thing. IT GOES TO THE PLACES THAT ARE HARDEST TO REACH: more than twenty-five years of work on education, energy and climate with the most remote and vulnerable communities, including villages inside the buffer zone of a nature reserve, where it has demonstrated resource-saving equipment to residents. Buffer-zone villages are exactly the population this file has recorded elsewhere as deciding whether a protected area holds. AND IT SPREADS METHOD RATHER THAN HOLDING IT: by its own account dozens of organisations have taken up not only its publications, consultations and assistance but its ideas, running similar projects and adopting the equipment it distributes and the practices it introduces — so a community that cannot get its direct involvement can still ask for the publications and the approach. VOLUNTEERING IS OPEN TO ANYONE regardless of sex, age, nationality or religious belief, which is the practical way in for a person with time rather than money. Founded by a group of young activists, based in Dushanbe, a member of an international socio-ecological union, with a named senior adviser. Its work with women in a remote valley was recognised by an international climate award in 2024, and it took a national civil society prize the same year in an education category. THE LIMIT, STATED PLAINLY: THIS IS NOT AN OBJECTOR. Nothing found shows it opposing a project, bringing a case or representing a community against a scheme. Approach it for environmental information, for participation support, for practical equipment and methods, and because it will engage with an unregistered group — and use the Aarhus centres recorded here for formal environmental information requests, the land-rights organisation for tenure, and the human rights bureau for a lawyer.

trackers.name: Youth Ecological Centre — it builds rural communities' capacity on land, water and energy use
trackers.desc: ITS SUBJECT IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST HERE: it works with RURAL COMMUNITIES, NATURAL RESOURCE USERS, FARMERS, young people and teachers, and promotes building the capacity of rural communities in the SUSTAINABLE USE OF LAND, WATER AND ENERGY RESOURCES. This file has established that all land in Tajikistan is the exclusive property of the state and that the contest is therefore over use rights rather than ownership — which makes a body whose stated work is the capacity of resource users to manage land and water the most directly relevant Tajik organisation recorded so far. IT IS ALSO OLD AND CONSTITUTED, WHICH MATTERS IN A COUNTRY WITH ALMOST NO INDEPENDENT ORGANISATIONS: founded in 1997 by teachers, scientists and students as a republican public socio-ecological organisation, with a published address and a working news feed. IT RUNS A YOUTH ARM PRODUCING MATERIAL FOR SCHOOLCHILDREN whose stated purpose is to strengthen the position and influence of the environmental movement — a body thinking in terms of movement-building rather than projects is one worth a long relationship. USE IT WITH THE OTHER TAJIK ENTRIES RATHER THAN INSTEAD OF THEM: the Aarhus centres for formal environmental information, the land rights organisation for tenure and dehkan certificates, the community conservancy federation for land actually held by families, the human rights bureau for a lawyer, and the environmental organisation recorded alongside this one for work with unregistered initiative groups. Between them those five cover information, tenure, holding, legal help and organising. THE LIMIT: nothing found shows it opposing a project, bringing a case or representing a community against a scheme. It is a capacity and education body; approach it for the practical management questions that decide whether a use right is defensible, not for a fight. DOMAIN NOTE: an older site on a free hosting service still describes itself as this organisation's official site. Use the address given here; the older one appears to be a legacy.

trackers.name: Whitley Fund for Nature — £50,000 to a named leader, then up to £100,000 more if it works
trackers.desc: IT FUNDS A PERSON, NOT AN ORGANISATION, AND IT IS THE LARGEST SUCH ROUTE IN THIS FILE. An award is worth £50,000 in project funding over one year, and the application must SPECIFY A LEADER OF THE TEAM who would receive it. That matters here because this payload has recorded that Tajik community conservancies are held by families and hunters' associations and turn on named individuals — and because the other funds recorded for this country are small grants, typically under twenty thousand dollars. This is the tier above them. AND IT IS LADDERED RATHER THAN ONE-OFF: previous winners who completed their grant may apply for CONTINUATION FUNDING OF UP TO £100,000 over one or two years, and a further award worth £60,000 exists for outstanding past winners. Around fifty-five per cent of previous award winners have gone on to win continuation funding. A single successful application can therefore be the start of several years of support, which is what a conservancy needs and almost nothing else offers. WHO QUALIFIES: mid-career conservationists who are NATIONALS OF THE COUNTRY WHERE THEY WORK, leading grassroots projects, working for or leading a LOCALLY INCORPORATED ORGANISATION — expressly not in-country staff of a body headquartered in a developed country. Eligible countries are those not classified as high-income economies, which includes this one. TWO REQUIREMENTS DECIDE MOST APPLICATIONS AND ARE WORTH PREPARING FOR EARLY. The project must involve communities at grassroots level and deliver practical action FOUNDED ON SCIENCE — so the survey and monitoring work this file records elsewhere is not a separate task but part of the application. And the fund expects to supply a SIGNIFICANT SHARE OF THE PROJECT COST, around thirty per cent or more, so a realistic total budget matters as much as the request. It also asks applicants to have thought carefully about the INDICATORS that will evidence impact. THE PROCESS IS SLOW AND SERIOUS: annual competitive rounds closing in the autumn, screening by an expert academic panel, international reference checks, and interviews with finalists before selection. Since 1993 it has given around £23 million to some two hundred leaders across eighty countries. THE LIMITS: it funds wildlife and ecosystem conservation, not opposition — it will not pay for a campaign, a lawyer or an objection, and a project framed as stopping a development will not fit. Frame the conservation work; the protection follows from it.

trackers.name: Ferghana Valley community adaptation grants — Sughd organisations eligible, applications in Tajik
trackers.desc: ORGANISATIONS REGISTERED IN SUGHD PROVINCE ARE NAMED AS ELIGIBLE. A regional water body's scientific centre has published terms of reference to select EIGHT LOCAL NON-GOVERNMENTAL NON-PROFIT ORGANISATIONS to plan and deliver sub-projects on LOCAL ADAPTATION TO CLIMATE CHANGE WITH LOCAL COMMUNITIES in the Ferghana Valley, open to bodies registered in Sughd alongside named provinces of two neighbouring countries. This file has recorded that this country's community land holding runs through conservancies and family-held rights in the mountains; this is a funding route addressed to the northern valley instead, and it is province-specific rather than national. APPLICATIONS ARE ACCEPTED IN TAJIK, RUSSIAN, UZBEK OR KYRGYZ — NOT ENGLISH, which removes the barrier that quietly excludes local bodies from most international funding. THE BAR IS HIGHER THAN REGISTRATION: at least THREE COMPLETED environment or climate projects at local or community level in the past ten years, and experience developing training programmes, materials or guides. A CONSORTIUM OF TWO ORGANISATIONS IS ALLOWED PROVIDED THE LEAD IS REGISTERED IN AN ELIGIBLE PROVINCE — so a community group without a track record should partner with an established organisation rather than apply alone. IT ALSO TELLS YOU WHAT A FUNDED PROPOSAL CONTAINS: a design and methodology covering how target groups and beneficiaries are selected and how BASELINE AND FINAL ASSESSMENTS are conducted, plus a monitoring and evaluation plan submitted for approval. That is the standard most serious funders apply without stating it. THE LIMITS: an interstate water coordination body's scientific centre is not an advocate and will not oppose a scheme; its subject is water and adaptation. THE CURRENT STATUS OF THIS PARTICULAR CALL WAS NOT ESTABLISHED, so treat the mechanism as the finding — the body publishes its tender and grant documents on its own releases pages, which is where the next round will appear.

trackers.name: Mapeo — offline mapping that turns community rangers into a monitoring system
trackers.desc: THIS FILE RECORDED THAT COMMUNITY CONSERVANCIES HERE HOLD THE LAND THEMSELVES AND FUND THEIR OWN RANGERS. THIS IS WHAT PUTS A RECORD IN THOSE RANGERS' HANDS. A free offline app on which one button captures a GPS POINT, A PHOTOGRAPH AND A NOTE — no internet, no special hardware, and data synchronised DIRECTLY BETWEEN PHONES rather than through any server. A ranger who walks a boundary anyway becomes, with a phone, a monitoring system producing dated georeferenced evidence of incursion, cutting, grazing or construction. THE COMMUNITY OWNS EVERYTHING IT COLLECTS. Storage is decentralised on the devices, and a version built with a United Nations conservation centre and a forest peoples' organisation lets custodian communities submit records to global conservation registries ONLY VOLUNTARILY AND ONLY AFTER THEIR OWN FREE, PRIOR AND INFORMED CONSENT PROCESS. For a body that holds land without a title deed, a self-owned record is the asset. ITS STATED PURPOSES ARE THIS MAP'S PURPOSES: documenting so that a community can act, REPORT INFORMATION TO AUTHORITIES, FILE LAWSUITS, run media campaigns, or MAKE MAPS FOR LAND CLAIMS. An indigenous nation in South America used it over four years to build the territorial evidence with which they defeated an oil development in court. IT IS LEARNABLE IN HOURS by someone who has never used a smartphone; the desktop version produces PRINTED AND PDF REPORTS and exports to standard mapping formats, so the record can go to a lawyer, a ministry or a court in a form they accept. THE LIMITS: it is software rather than an organisation, customisation with your own categories and offline maps requires technical support, and its listed interface languages do not currently include Russian, Tajik or others of this region — although it can be translated into any language. The organisation behind it now appears under a changed name; verify the current source before downloading. Pair it with the satellite tools recorded elsewhere in this file: those show what changed from above, this records what is there on the ground.

trackers.name: Commissioner for Human Rights — an online reception and an address, and little else established
trackers.desc: THIS IS THE THINNEST ENTRY IN THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING AND YOU SHOULD KNOW THAT BEFORE RELYING ON IT. Three separate searches established two things: the office exists with A STREET ADDRESS IN THE CAPITAL, and it operates an INTERNET RECEPTION — an online channel for submitting an appeal — both published through a regional alliance of ombudsman institutions. WHAT AN ONLINE RECEPTION IS WORTH: it removes the journey to the capital, which for a mountain district is the practical barrier rather than the law. This file has recorded for this country conservancies, a women's land organisation, a rights bureau offering free receptions and an environmental network; none of them is a state institution able to look at an administrative decision. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, AND IT IS ALMOST EVERYTHING: whether it can go to court, whether an organisation may complain for an affected household, whether the complainant's name is protected, whether it reaches violations that predate it, whether it has representatives outside the capital, and what it may demand from a state body. Those six questions were answered for the equivalent institutions in three neighbouring countries recorded in this file, and the answers differed sharply — one can obtain documents from state bodies and other organisations and convene joint meetings with officials present; another can propose disciplinary or criminal proceedings against an official. ASK THIS OFFICE THE SAME QUESTIONS BEFORE DECIDING WHAT TO SEND IT, and note that the regional alliance page is a directory of state institutions rather than an endorsement of any of them. THE HONEST SUMMARY: an address and an online form, in a country where this map otherwise offers no domestic institution that examines administrative decisions. That is worth something and it is not worth much. Pair it with the rights bureau and the free legal reception recorded separately here, which are the bodies that can help draft what you send.

trackers.name: Lifeline — the grant to seek before trouble starts, and the one for when it has
trackers.desc: ASK FOR THE PREVENTIVE GRANT FIRST. Its RESILIENCY grants exist to help organisations at high risk avoid or reduce the threats they face, and the eligible activities include MAPPING AND COORDINATING CIVIL SOCIETY ACCESS TO PRO BONO SERVICES, developing protection networks and local support mechanisms, joint protection strategies and contingency plans, organisational risk assessments, protection training and LEGAL TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE. This file has recorded for this country conservancies, a women's land organisation, a rights bureau and an ombudsman reachable only through an online form. WHAT IT HAS NEVER RECORDED IS MONEY TO BUILD THE LIST OF LAWYERS WHO WOULD ACT, BEFORE ANYONE NEEDS ONE. That is exactly what this window pays for. AND IF SOMETHING HAS ALREADY HAPPENED, THE EMERGENCY GRANT COVERS LEGAL REPRESENTATION, TRIAL MONITORING, PRISON VISITS, medical expenses, security, temporary relocation and equipment replacement. THE QUALIFYING TEST IS BROAD ENOUGH TO REACH LAND DISPUTES: need, urgency, and whether the organisation faces significant security risks, loss of property or equipment, injury or imprisonment of staff, OR PROSECUTION OR OTHER LEGAL PROCEEDINGS. A THIRD WINDOW, RAPID RESPONSE ADVOCACY, CAN FUND STRATEGIC LITIGATION, coalition building and campaigns — which is a different and rarer thing from a project grant. Requests are handled through a consortium of seven international organisations, with two of them receiving emergency applications directly and a third forwarding them on. THE LIMITS. IT FUNDS ORGANISATIONS RATHER THAN INDIVIDUALS OR INFORMAL GROUPS, so a village committee without registration will usually need an established organisation to apply alongside it — the pasture committees, the women's land organisation and the environmental network recorded separately for this country are the obvious candidates. It excludes core costs, programme costs, long-term support and financial hardship. And it is financed by donor governments, which in some settings makes the association itself a consideration — weigh that before applying.

trackers.name: Accountability Console — every complaint ever filed about internationally financed projects, and what came of them
trackers.desc: BEFORE COMPLAINING ABOUT A FINANCED PROJECT, READ WHAT HAPPENED TO EVERYONE WHO ALREADY DID. This database holds EVERY COMPLAINT EVER FILED to the accountability offices of bilateral and multilateral development finance institutions, searchable and comparable ACROSS INSTITUTIONS, SECTORS AND REGIONS. Large infrastructure here is financed internationally, and every one of those financiers maintains an office that receives complaints from affected people. IT ANSWERS THE QUESTION THIS MAP KEEPS RAISING WITHOUT SETTLING: WHAT CAN A COMPLAINT ACTUALLY ACHIEVE? It sets out achievable outcomes, the limitations, and how the process differs between mechanisms — and it gives access to DOCUMENTS FROM COMPLAINTS THAT LED TO RESULTS, and to WHICH GROUPS TO CONSULT FOR ADVICE. AND THE WARNING SITS IN ITS OWN DATA, WHICH IS WHY IT IS WORTH READING FIRST: TOO FEW COMPLAINTS GET THROUGH THE SYSTEM AND ACHIEVE A RESULT, AND A HIGH NUMBER ARE CLOSED WITHOUT ANY OUTCOME BECAUSE THEY WERE RULED INELIGIBLE. Its creators call that the eligibility bottleneck. MOST CASES DIE AT THE DOOR RATHER THAN ON THE MERITS — so the effort goes into meeting the eligibility rules of the specific mechanism, and the database lets you compare those rules side by side and produce a comparison. START WITH ITS COMPLAINT PATHFINDER, which walks through the options and helps build a strategy before committing to a route. THE COST IS ARRANGED SO THAT MONEY IS NOT THE BARRIER: any member of the public may view the complaints list and the mechanisms' policies, and premium access is charged ON A SLIDING SCALE WITH THE FEE WAIVED FOR USERS ON A LIMITED BUDGET — but you have to ask for the waiver. THE LIMITS: it covers INTERNATIONALLY FINANCED projects, so a scheme funded wholly from domestic or state sources falls outside it; and it is a research and strategy tool rather than representation — nobody there files for you. Its own creators put it best: it is a tool for filing complaints, and possibly a tool for avoiding the need to file one. Use it with the emergency and legal empowerment funds recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: Land Acquisition Fund — it pays local organisations to buy or lease land, and to get community rights recognised
trackers.desc: IT PAYS FOR LAND TO BE SECURED, WHICH IS THE FIRST THING THIS MAP IS ASKED FOR AND THE THING IT CAN OFFER LEAST OFTEN. The fund enables local nature organisations to secure important habitat BY PURCHASE OR LONG-TERM LEASE, it has safeguarded more than SIXTY-FOUR THOUSAND HECTARES since 2001, and it CALLS ON LOCAL CONSERVATION ORGANISATIONS WORLDWIDE TO SUBMIT PROPOSALS. AND ITS RECENT WORK INCLUDES EXACTLY THE SITUATION THIS COUNTRY IS IN. It supported a snow leopard conservation organisation to help TWO HERDING COMMUNITIES RECOGNISE AND MANAGE OVER THIRTY THOUSAND HECTARES — giving those communities THE RIGHTS THEY NEED to protect the biodiversity and natural resources of those areas. That is not a purchase; it is a fund for acquiring land paying instead for COMMUNITY RIGHTS TO BE RECOGNISED over pasture. This file has recorded here pasture users, conservancies, a women's land organisation and mountain communities whose problem is precisely that their use of high ground is not secured in law. THIS IS A FUNDER THAT HAS PAID FOR THAT ELSEWHERE. ITS ARGUMENT FOR SMALL SITES IS WORTH BORROWING WHEN YOU WRITE: the strategic acquisition of SMALL PATCHES of land is targeted and cost-effective, because A FEW HECTARES CAN CREATE A CORRIDOR between two isolated areas. Almost every other conservation funder recorded in this payload is oriented to large landscapes and thirty-per-cent targets; this one says explicitly that smaller projects at crucial locations are not to be overlooked, and that they sit on the frontline. HOW IT WORKS: proposals are invited from local NGOs and civil society organisations, new land purchase and long-term lease projects are selected each year through a stated selection procedure, and the fund is supported by private donors. It has entered new countries recently, so absence of a previous project here is not a bar. It has also produced, with a bird conservation partner, practical guidelines for people MANAGING privately protected reserves — which is the part communities usually discover too late, after the land is secured and nobody has planned who maintains it. THE LIMITS. IT FUNDS ORGANISATIONS, NOT INDIVIDUALS OR UNREGISTERED COMMITTEES — the applicant must be a local conservation NGO or CSO, so a community here would apply through the conservancies association or an environmental organisation recorded separately in this file. Selection is annual and competitive. Its purpose is BIODIVERSITY HABITAT, so a case must be made in terms of species and ecosystems rather than livelihood alone — though the herding-communities project shows the two can be argued together.

trackers.name: Small Grants Programme — money paid straight to a community organisation, decided in your own country
trackers.desc: THIS PAYLOAD HOLDS MORE THAN NINETY FUNDING ENTRIES AND ALMOST ALL OF THEM PAY AN ESTABLISHED ORGANISATION TO WORK WITH A COMMUNITY. THIS ONE MAKES GRANTS DIRECTLY TO COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANISATIONS AND NGOs — the money goes to the group itself. Regular grants run UP TO SEVENTY-FIVE THOUSAND DOLLARS, strategic projects UP TO ONE HUNDRED AND FIFTY THOUSAND, and the usual range is twenty-five to fifty thousand. ITS FOCAL AREAS PUT LAND AND WATER AT THE CENTRE: biodiversity; climate change mitigation and adaptation; LAND DEGRADATION AND SUSTAINABLE FOREST MANAGEMENT; INTERNATIONAL WATERS; and chemicals. A proposal about pasture degradation, a threatened forest, a shared river or a contaminated site is squarely inside the programme rather than a stretch. AND IT IS DECIDED WHERE YOU LIVE. The programme runs through a NATIONAL COORDINATOR and a multistakeholder NATIONAL STEERING COMMITTEE: applications are screened for eligibility, reviewed technically, shortlisted, and then considered by that committee, which recommends; selected applicants are invited to submit full proposals. The people deciding are in the country, they can be met, and the committee's composition is worth knowing before you write. THE TRACK RECORD IS THE ANSWER TO ANYONE WHO SAYS THIS IS UNREALISTIC: over eight hundred and thirty-eight million dollars to MORE THAN THIRTY THOUSAND COMMUNITY-LED INITIATIVES ACROSS 127 COUNTRIES, with a further nine hundred and ninety million mobilised as co-finance. IT ALSO GIVES SPECIAL CONSIDERATION TO INDIGENOUS PEOPLES, WOMEN, YOUTH AND PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES, and delivers a dedicated initiative supporting INDIGENOUS AND COMMUNITY-CONSERVED TERRITORIES — which is the funding counterpart to the community-conserved area route recorded separately in this file. TIMING MATTERS RIGHT NOW: in this region the programme is being executed for 2026 to 2028 by a regional conservation fund already recorded in this country's listing, with AT LEAST ONE CALL FOR PROPOSALS PER COUNTRY IN 2026 AND IN 2027. Find the country programme and the coordinator before the call opens, not after. THE LIMITS. THE APPLICANT MUST BE AN ORGANISATION — a community-based organisation counts, which is broader than most funders allow, but an unconstituted group of neighbours does not. CO-FINANCING IS NORMALLY EXPECTED, often around half, THOUGH IT MAY BE IN KIND — labour, land access, materials and volunteer time can count, and that is the difference between impossible and possible. The framing must be environmental: a proposal that reads as opposition to one project will not fit, while one that reads as protecting a pasture, forest or watershed will.

trackers.name: Regional directory of conservation organisations — find the domestic body that already works on your landscape
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING IN THIS MAP HELD EIGHTEEN ENTRIES — FUNDING WINDOWS, LEGAL AID, MAPPING TOOLS, HUMAN RIGHTS OFFICES, COMMUNITY CONSERVANCIES — AND NOT ONE NAMED DOMESTIC CONSERVATION ORGANISATION. This directory lists them BY COUNTRY across five Central Asian states, all five of which appear in this map and all five of which are thinly covered in it. THE BODY IT LEADS TO HERE IS A NATURE FOUNDATION WHOSE STATED MISSION IS THE ONE A COMMUNITY WANTS TO HEAR: to advance conservation BY STRENGTHENING THE LINK BETWEEN NATURE AND LOCAL LIVELIHOODS, AND BY EXPANDING COMMUNITIES' CAPACITY TO USE THEIR OWN NATURAL RESOURCES RATIONALLY — conserving wildlife and WILD LANDSCAPES for future generations. That is conservation defined through the people who live there rather than against them, which is the difference between an organisation that will work with a village and one that will fence it out. WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES: WILDLIFE PROTECTION, RESEARCH, MONITORING, WORK WITH PROTECTED AREAS, AND ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION, focused on named mountain sheep. AND IT RAN A PROGRAMME ON SUPPORTING PRIVATE SECTOR AND COMMUNITY CONSERVATION FROM 2020 TO 2024, funded through a major ecosystem partnership fund — so it has experience of putting money and management into community hands rather than only studying animals. WHY THE DIRECTORY MATTERS MORE THAN ANY SINGLE ENTRY IN IT: THE FIRST PROBLEM A COMMUNITY IN THIS REGION FACES IS NOT ARGUMENT OR MONEY BUT KNOWING WHO EXISTS. A list of domestic organisations, arranged by country and describing what each works on, answers the question this file has struggled to answer for five countries at once. WORK THROUGH IT FOR THE ONE THAT ALREADY WORKS ON YOUR SPECIES, YOUR VALLEY OR YOUR PROTECTED AREA, because an organisation with an existing programme where you live is worth more than a larger one elsewhere. AND THERE IS EVIDENCE THAT THIS APPROACH WORKS AT SCALE: a regional review records conservation work at named key biodiversity sites across three countries which STRENGTHENED THE CAPACITY OF SIX LOCAL ORGANISATIONS, produced management plans and improved local knowledge of valuable species. The same review states that the role of civil organisations IN ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENTS, IMPACT ASSESSMENT AND PUBLIC HEARINGS ON INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS is important and is underpinned by the Aarhus treaty — which this map records as being in force across the region. THE LIMITS: a directory is only as current as its last update, and entries here describe missions rather than confirming activity this year — verify before relying on any listing. The organisations are conservation bodies, not lawyers or land buyers; they will survey, monitor, train and sometimes co-manage, but they will not litigate. And civil society in this country operates under tight registration requirements, so approach through an existing programme rather than proposing something new.

trackers.name: Farmer household land rights — lifetime inheritable use, obtainable without forming a company
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING HELD CONSERVATION GROUPS, FUNDS, LEGAL AID AND A MAPPING TOOL AND NEVER EXPLAINED HOW A FAMILY ACTUALLY HOLDS LAND. THE ANSWER IS THE FARMER HOUSEHOLD, AND THE RIGHT IT CARRIES IS STRONGER THAN MOST PEOPLE REALISE: LAND IS GRANTED FOR IT IN LIFETIME INHERITABLE USE, BY DECISION OF THE DISTRICT EXECUTIVE BODY, ON THE CITIZENS' OWN APPLICATION. IT PASSES TO THE CHILDREN. AND IT REQUIRES NO COMPANY. CITIZENS MAY CREATE A FARMER HOUSEHOLD WITHOUT FORMING A LEGAL PERSON AT ALL — by one person, by one family, or by a group of persons — and any legally capable citizen may create one. THIS FILE HAS SPENT HUNDREDS OF ENTRIES ON THE PROBLEM THAT COMMUNITIES CANNOT HOLD ANYTHING WITHOUT INCORPORATING. HERE THEY CAN. THE APPLICATION IS SPECIFIC AND SHOULD BE PREPARED CAREFULLY, BECAUSE WHAT YOU WRITE FIXES WHAT YOU GET: IT MUST STATE THE PURPOSE OF USE, THE INTENDED SIZE AND LOCATION OF THE PLOT, THE TOTAL NUMBER OF FAMILY MEMBERS, AND, WHERE THE LAND IS LEASED, THE TERM. It goes to the district or city executive body where the plot lies. AND THE LAW EXPRESSLY COVERS PEOPLE MOVING IN FROM OTHER DISTRICTS FOR PERMANENT RESIDENCE — so a returning or relocating family is inside the scheme, not outside it. WHO COUNTS AS A MEMBER MATTERS FOR WHAT EACH PERSON ENDS UP HOLDING: parents, spouses, children and other able-bodied people working jointly are members, BUT SOMEONE WORKING AS A HIRED EMPLOYEE UNDER AN EMPLOYMENT CONTRACT IS NOT. And where the household has no legal personality, THE REGISTRATION DOCUMENTS MUST SHOW EACH MEMBER'S LAND SHARE IN THE COMMON PLOT, with a joint-activity contract setting out rights and duties. GET THE SHARES WRITTEN DOWN AT THE START — that document is what protects a daughter, a widow or a departing brother years later. AND HERE IS THE PROTECTION PEOPLE LOSE SIMPLY BY NOT KNOWING IT EXISTS: CITIZENS WHO RECEIVE A PLOT FOR A FARMER HOUSEHOLD AND WHO HAVE A DWELLING IN A RURAL SETTLEMENT RETAIN THEIR HOMESTEAD PLOT AT THE HOUSE. Taking farm land does not cost you the garden plot by the house — if anyone tells a family otherwise, that is the provision to point at. THERE IS ALSO A PUBLISHED CITIZEN POCKET BOOK ON RIGHTS TO LAND AND LAND USE, WRITTEN AS NUMBERED QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS — including how plots are granted to farmer households. ITS PUBLISHER IS ALREADY RECORDED SEPARATELY IN THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING; ask that organisation for the handbook by name, because a plain-language answer key is worth more to a village than the statute. THE LIMITS: this is a USE right, not ownership — land here remains state property, and use rights can be reallocated or withdrawn under conditions set by law, which is precisely why the paperwork matters. Allocation is decided by the district executive body, so it is an administrative decision with all that implies. And this entry rests on the law and a legal database; CONFIRM CURRENT PROCEDURE LOCALLY, since land legislation here has been amended repeatedly.

trackers.name: Répertoire du Commerce et de l’Industrie
trackers.desc: National — Monaco business / trade and industry register. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Monaco — Direction du Budget et du Trésor (Département des Finances)
trackers.desc: National budget authority; the Budget & Treasury Directorate prepares & executes the State budget, Principality of Monaco. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in MCO.

trackers.name: Monaco — Commission Supérieure des Comptes
trackers.desc: National public-finance watchdog; the Commission Supérieure des Comptes (Art. 42 of the Constitution) is Monaco’s Supreme Audit Institution (INTOSAI/EUROSAI member), auditing the accounts & financial management of the State, commune & public bodies and publishing an annual public report, Monaco.

trackers.name: Volunteers created the reserve in 1976 — and still manage it
trackers.desc: THE SEQUENCE IS THE LESSON: VOLUNTEERS FIRST, INSTRUMENT SECOND, MANAGEMENT CONTRACT THIRD. In 1976 the volunteers of the Association Monégasque pour la Protection de la Nature, chaired by Eugène Debernardi, created the Larvotto underwater reserve to preserve the only Posidonia meadow in Monaco, established by ordonnance souveraine of Prince Rainier III. Faced with the success of that approach a second reserve followed in 1986 — the Tombant des Spélugues, protecting the only coralligenous drop-off in the Principality. Nearly 50 years on the same association is still the manager. Larvotto is described as the world's first urban marine protected area. A small association identified a single irreplaceable habitat, obtained an instrument for it, then kept the job. THE GOVERNANCE IS WORTH COPYING TOO — THREE TIERS: a national monitoring committee setting guidelines, whose members include the Government, the Prince Albert II Foundation, the Institute of Oceanography, the Monaco Scientific Centre and the Departments of Environment and Maritime Affairs; a Marine Protected Areas Coordination Group implementing them; and a manager, AMPN, doing the daily work. The scientific institutions sit on the committee alongside government, so the science is not something the association must fight to have heard.

trackers.name: Inventories are decision support for planning — and the honest tension
trackers.desc: THE GOVERNMENT SAYS ITS OWN INVENTORIES FEED PLANNING DECISIONS. Species and habitat inventories are described as tools of knowledge and awareness but also of decision support for the State in implementing its territorial planning policy and its marine biodiversity surveillance and protection strategy, with time-series monitoring and indicators of species and environments tracking ecosystem health. So the monitoring record is relevant evidence in a planning argument, not merely scientific interest. THE FACTS: Larvotto covers 33.6 ha on the official figure, running from the shore to about 600 m offshore from the eastern frontier with France — note that secondary sources say ‘approximately 50 hectares’; this entry uses the figure published by gouv.mc. Fishing, anchoring and sailing are strictly prohibited, and the reserve is actively patrolled, scientifically monitored and legally enforced. It holds artificial reefs, the last placed in 2004, sheltering large sponges, gorgonians and red coral; it is a Ramsar wetland of international importance; and it sits above the Pelagos Sanctuary for marine mammals. Monaco has only 7.5 km of coastline. THE HONEST TENSION: Monaco is the world's most densely built principality and has expanded its territory by building out into the sea. A rigorously protected marine reserve here has not prevented major coastal construction, and the terrestrial Larvotto area has itself seen significant works — worth knowing before citing Monaco as a model outcome rather than a model mechanism.

trackers.name: Fondation Prince Albert II — 50 percent maximum, and it funds far beyond Monaco
trackers.desc: A MONACO-BASED FUNDER WHOSE REACH COVERS MUCH OF THIS MAP. Established 2006, the Fondation Prince Albert II de Monaco works in three fields — climate change and renewable energies, biodiversity protection, and water resources and desertification — across three priority geographies: the Mediterranean Basin, the Polar Regions, and countries on the UN list of Least Developed Countries. That puts the entire Mediterranean rim and every LDC in scope — so a reader in Lebanon, Morocco, Tunisia, Albania, Malawi, Nepal, Liberia or Kiribati can apply to it, which is why this entry matters well beyond Monaco. It funds civil society organisations, foundations, public and international organisations, private enterprises and government bodies. THE CONSTRAINT TO PLAN FOR: no maximum grant is specified, but requested funding cannot exceed 50 percent of the total project budget — you must have the other half identified before applying; this is a co-financing funder, not a sole funder. AND DO NOT START EARLY: recorded grounds for refusal include projects outside the three domains, projects outside the priority geographies, and activities starting before the designated funding year — retrospective work is excluded. Applications are made online against an annual call for projects.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Fondation Prince Albert II de Monaco — funds projects, but read the rules first
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a Monaco-based environmental foundation created in 2006, funding work on climate change and renewable energy, biodiversity, and water resources and desertification. More than 750 projects funded since 2006, roughly 40 to 50 a year, with representative offices in France, the UK, Switzerland, the United States, Canada, Germany, Italy, Singapore and Spain. Monaco itself had no ally of any kind in this file before this. THE FOUR RULES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT IS WORTH APPLYING, and each one has ended applications: the project must sit in one of its priority areas — the Mediterranean Basin, the polar regions, or countries on the UN list of Least Developed Countries. Requested funding cannot exceed 50% of the project budget, so you need the other half already. Applications run in an annual window, typically through June, and fund activities starting roughly two years later — a 2025 application is for a 2027 start, with decisions notified by the following March. And no project can be submitted directly: only files entered through a call for projects are considered. ONE MECHANICAL DETAIL THAT REJECTS APPLICATIONS OUTRIGHT: files must be sent in the original editable format. Anything scanned or saved as a non-editable PDF is automatically rejected. WHO CAN APPLY: civil society organisations, foundations, public regional and international organisations, private enterprises and government bodies; its pre-application form has also allowed individuals. It runs themed calls alongside the general one, including forests and communities — with an explicit strand on forest conservation through the action of indigenous peoples and local communities — polar work, and coastal resilience. BE REALISTIC: this is a two-year-lead research and programme funder, not emergency money. It cannot help a community facing a decision this season. Use it to build the long work that follows a win, and use the funders in this file with open rounds for the fight itself.

trackers.name: AMPN — volunteers created Monaco's marine reserves, and still manage them
trackers.desc: WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND MONACO: Monaco had one ally in this file, a funder. This is the association — and its history is the most compressed demonstration in 198 candidates that a group of volunteers can create a protected area and end up as its statutory manager. WHAT HAPPENED: founded 22 October 1975 by a team of Monegasque volunteers, statutes approved by ministerial order the following month. By April 1976 the volunteers had created Monaco's first underwater reserve at Larvotto — 33 hectares protecting the Principality's only Posidonia meadow. The results led them to create a second in 1986: the 2-hectare Tombant des Spélugues, protecting the Principality's only coralligenous drop-off. Eleven months from founding an association to designating a reserve. AMPN has managed both since their creation and has been their official manager since 2018. WHAT IT DOES NOW: scientific monitoring of marine ecosystems, particularly Posidonia meadows and coralligenous reefs; ecological restoration projects including artificial reefs and the reintroduction of threatened species — a programme of concrete-block reefs begun in the early 1980s, ancestors of the 3D-printed reefs sunk in Monegasque waters since 2017; research on marine biodiversity and human impacts; and the Aire Marine Éducative launched in 2018 for schools. THE HONEST SCALE: it worked entirely on volunteers until the board authorised employing staff in 2016; there are now three, all scientists. Expect a small, expert, largely voluntary body — and note that in a jurisdiction this small, three resident scientists monitoring the coastline is the national capability. IT WORKS WITH THE STATE RATHER THAN AGAINST IT: in collaboration with the princely government, state services, institutions and socio-economic actors, with the support of the Prince and his foundation — the funder already filed for Monaco. Read that as it is: this is a conservation manager, not a body that will litigate against a Monegasque development.

trackers.name: Monaco's assistance judiciaire — the State pays the lawyer, and they cannot refuse the case
trackers.desc: THE HARD REQUIREMENT FIRST: a recourse to the Tribunal Suprême must be presented by an avocat-défenseur registered with the Ordre des avocats of the Principality, or it cannot be examined at all. A foreign lawyer may draft the requête, but it must be signed by the Monegasque avocat-défenseur, who carries all the procedural formalities. The recourse must be in French, reasoned, and accompanied by all useful documents. So in Monaco the first and unavoidable step is finding a local avocat-défenseur; the Ordre publishes the annuaire. AND THE STATE WILL PAY FOR ONE: for a natural person without the resources to obtain the assistance of an avocat-défenseur, where assistance judiciaire is granted by the bureau de l'assistance judiciaire, all the costs required by the proceedings, notably the avocat-défenseur's remuneration, are borne by the State. It opens the right to an avocat-défenseur, an avocat or avocat stagiaire, and to all officiers ministériels, designated in turn by the bureau. THE DETAIL THAT DISTINGUISHES MONACO FROM ANDORRA, filed last round: avocats-défenseurs, avocats and avocats-stagiaires are designated in turn under the codes of civil and criminal procedure to represent parties benefiting from assistance judiciaire, and THEY CANNOT REFUSE THEIR MINISTRY. Andorra's duty roster is voluntary and its lawyers say they may stop; Monaco's is compulsory. Lawyers who serve receive an indemnity from the State on a published scale of unit values and coefficients. TWO PRACTICAL LIMITS: avocats-stagiaires may plead before all jurisdictions except the Tribunal Suprême and the Cour de Révision, so at the top court you need a full avocat-défenseur. And the bureau is presided by a sitting magistrate, with the avocat-défenseur designated by the bâtonnier. Where the opposing party is ordered to pay costs, the State recovers what it advanced. WHO TO CONTACT: the Ordre des Avocats-Défenseurs, Avocats et Avocats-Stagiaires de la Principauté, ordredesavocats@monaco.mc, +377 97 77 23 32 — which has civil legal personality and exists to defend the collective interest of lawyers and of justiciables.

trackers.name: MC2D — the federation that pulls Monaco's environmental associations together
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: created in July 2004 to bring together the various Monegasque associations dedicated to protecting and improving environmental quality in different fields, so as to collaborate and coordinate their efforts, improving the overall effectiveness of their actions. Its work focuses on raising the awareness of the population AND OF THE PUBLIC AUTHORITIES on environmental questions. Monaco's bucket held a princely foundation, a marine volunteer association and the legal aid route — but nothing that federates. WHY A FEDERATION IS THE RIGHT RESOURCE IN A STATE THIS SIZE: this file has recorded across eighteen countries that the most useful free artefact is a membership list. In Monaco, where the whole environmental sector is a handful of associations, the federation IS the list — and its named members include an association working since 1998 to support sustainable development of the Principality and promote social, cultural and economic behaviours in its favour. IT ALSO RUNS A PUBLIC EVENT: since 2006 MC2D has organised an annual environmental exhibition in Monaco. A recurring public forum is where a community meets the authorities without asking for a meeting.

trackers.name: Tribunal Suprême decisions — the Monegasque record of who challenged a building permit and on what
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Tribunal Suprême publishes its decisions, and its urbanisme docket is a worked record of the grounds on which Monegasque building permits and planning ordinances have been challenged. Monaco had one legal entry — the state-paid assistance judiciaire — and nothing showing what a case looks like. THE GROUNDS THAT HAVE BEEN RUN, taken from its published decisions: that the real nature and intended use of a projected building remained undefined or equivocal; that the technical commission on hygiene, safety and environmental protection had not been consulted as the environment code required; that the permit application lacked a technical study of sub-surface works required by the urbanism regulation where parking and garage access were involved; and, from the other side, that an urbanism ordinance was adopted without sufficient procedural guarantees such as a prior public inquiry allowing any interested person to give an opinion.
