Failure to consult the environmental commission, and a missing technical study, are the two recurring defects — check both in your own file. AND THE PRACTICAL POINTS: associations do litigate here — the reports name an association seeking withdrawal of a Sovereign Ordinance on urbanism after a recours gracieux was rejected, and multiple residents jointly challenging a modified planning authorisation. The sequence is recours gracieux or hiérarchique first, then the Tribunal Suprême, and parties appear through an avocat-défenseur.

trackers.name: LGU — Liechtensteinische Gesellschaft für Umweltschutz
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Liechtenstein's environmental association, founded in 1973 out of the fight against an oil refinery and a nuclear plant across the Rhine, and the holder of what it calls its statutory right of participation and objection in the enforcement of the environmental laws. It uses it: it lodged a Beschwerde against a zoning-plan change at Steg, files Stellungnahmen on impact assessments for road schemes, and with the Verkehrs-Club took a complaint to the Staatsgerichtshof after a court ruling gutted the association right of appeal in EIA cases — arguing, pointedly, that the government was both promoter and decision-maker on the road in question. WHO IT SUITS: anyone in Liechtenstein facing a zoning change or a road. Be realistic about the register it works in: it says plainly that these rights are exercised mainly through consultation rather than formal objection, and it is a small office of a few staff with around 400 members. SINCE 1991 THE LGU OFFICE HAS ALSO RUN CIPRA LIECHTENSTEIN, A NETWORK OF TEN ASSOCIATIONS working in nature, nature conservation and environmental protection, in which member organisations find an opportunity for cooperation, information and joint appearances. So one approach reaches ten organisations, and a joint appearance is an express function of the network — which matters in a country of 41,000 people and eleven communes, covering 160 km², two thirds of it mountains, where a single association's voice would carry little. CIPRA is the Alpine Convention's civil-society counterpart, so a Liechtenstein issue can be raised in an Alpine-wide forum through this route. It is among the largest Liechtenstein associations — 561 members in 1973, 690 in 2009 — financed by membership contributions, donations and state subsidies. Contact: Kirchstrasse 5, FL-9494 Schaan; tel 00423 232 52 62. Stated aims: a careful use of natural resources and a participatory environmental policy. RECORDED HONESTLY: no domestic environmental grant window was found for Liechtenstein. That LGU receives state subsidies indicates such support exists for associations, but the scheme was not located on a canonical source and is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Liechtenstein — National Audit Office (Finanzkontrolle)
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution; supreme financial supervisory body operating under the Finanzkontrollgesetz, supporting Parliament’s Audit Commission, Liechtenstein.

trackers.name: Liechtenstein — Commercial Register (Handelsregister, Amt für Justiz)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the Office of Justice’s public Commercial Register records all legal entities & trusts (40,000+ entries) with an online company-index search, Liechtenstein. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Liechtenstein — Ministry of General Government Affairs & Finance
trackers.desc: National budget authority; prepares the national budget and publishes national financial statements & accounts, Principality of Liechtenstein. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in LIE.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: KVU — your cantonal environment office, and the regional conference above it
trackers.desc: THE REGIONAL CONFERENCE IS A LEVER A SINGLE CANTONAL OFFICE IS NOT. KVU (Konferenz der Vorsteher der Umweltschutzämter, Haus der Kantone, Speichergasse 6, 3001 Bern) publishes a per-canton address directory — this link — and coordinates three regional conferences: CREPE for French-speaking Switzerland, USK Nordwestschweiz, and the Zentralschweizerische Konferenz, whose stated purpose includes harmonising enforcement across the region, producing joint position statements (gemeinsame Stellungnahmen), and carrying out joint actions, monitoring and controls. Where a development crosses cantonal boundaries, or one canton is more willing than its neighbours, that is the level to address. KVU also runs a named contact point for basic water-protection controls outside agriculture. WHAT THE CANTONAL OFFICE IS: cantonal ordinances implementing the federal USG define the Amt für Umwelt as the kantonale Umweltschutzfachstelle im Sinne des Bundesrechts, tasked with controlling the environmental measures of the canton, the municipalities, private parties and other obliged persons — it controls private parties, not only public bodies. THE ACCESS PROVISION IS WORTH CITING BY NAME: Nidwalden's ordinance states ‘alle Umweltdaten sind öffentlich, sofern nicht überwiegende Interessen entgegenstehen’ — all environmental data are public unless overriding interests oppose — with results held in Kataster, Inventare, Kartenwerke oder Berichte. Ask for the Kataster by name; a presumption of publicity with named document types beats a general information request. BUT THAT WORDING IS NIDWALDEN'S — each canton has its own implementing law and the wording differs, so check your own canton's kUSV. NAME THE RIGHT FEDERAL ORDINANCE: noise (LSV), air (LRV), soil (VBBo), contaminated sites (AltlV), major accidents (StFV), waste (TVA, VeVA), non-ionising radiation (NISV) and impact assessment (UVPV) each have their own instrument — naming the right one beats a general environmental objection. WHY THIS IS IN THE LIECHTENSTEIN ENTRY: KVU states that its members are the heads of the environmental offices of the Swiss cantons and of the Principality of Liechtenstein. Liechtenstein's environment office sits inside the Swiss cantonal network — a materially larger technical and enforcement community than a state of 41,000 people and eleven communes has domestically, and a route this map previously recorded only through civil society.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: BZG — the society that holds the record, and the LGU's land-buying since 1973 (Liechtenstein)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Botanisch-Zoologische Gesellschaft Liechtenstein-Sarganserland-Werdenberg, founded in 1970 in the first European Conservation Year. Its stated aims include researching the region botanically and zoologically, preventing damage to natural assets, promoting biotope and landscape protection, and creating and maintaining habitats and protected areas for animals and plants. It publishes the BZG-Bericht, runs excursions and lectures, supports and supervises research projects, and maintains working groups on bats and crayfish and a botanical information service, with a named committee including a water ecologist and a geologist. WHY IT MATTERS FOR A LIECHTENSTEIN CASE: this is the country's naturalist record. On the Ruggeller Riet it commissioned an expert opinion on the site's worthiness of protection from a vegetation scientist at ETH Zurich, producing the first vegetation map in 1972, which confirmed the object's international significance; regular floristic and zoological observation followed, and by 1990 some 1,631 animal and 448 vascular plant species had been described and recorded in a natural history monograph, making it the best-studied area in the country. If your ground needs its value demonstrated, this is who has done that before, and the sequence — independent expert opinion, then vegetation map, then designation — is the model. AND THE LAND-BUYING, which is the fact this file lacked: since 1973 the Liechtensteinische Gesellschaft für Umweltschutz has been acquiring and leasing ground for exchange purposes, and the greater part of the area it acquired was transferred to the State of Liechtenstein, which owns around a third of the Ruggeller Riet. Liechtenstein does have a body that buys land — it buys to swap and hand on rather than to hold. WHAT THE TWO DO TOGETHER: BZG and LGU were jointly decisive in establishing the Ruggeller Riet as a protected area in 1978, and when drainage and a falling water table degraded it they pressed until partial re-wetting projects were carried out. They still name what is missing: buffer strips protecting the parts of the reserve that adjoin intensively farmed land from fertiliser and pesticide input, and better connection of valuable habitats to others. LGU also holds the Verbandsbeschwerderecht — the association right of appeal — since 1996, which is the standing that matters here.

trackers.name: CIPRA Liechtenstein — ten societies that file objections together, coordinated by the LGU
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a network of ten associations working in the fields of nature, nature protection and environmental protection, in which the member organisations find an opportunity for cooperation, information and joint appearances. The care of the network lies in the hands of the LGU, already in this file, based in Schaan. Liechtenstein had five entries and two allies; this is the country's federation, and it is small enough to be complete. WHAT JOINT APPEARANCES MEAN IN PRACTICE: when the municipality of Eschen planned the 'Verfüllung Täli' as an extension of the Rheinau landfill, the LGU and five further organisations of CIPRA Liechtenstein stated that realising the project would have far-reaching consequences for nature and landscape and for the development possibilities of the Alpine Rhine. Six organisations, one position, on a single municipal landfill extension. In a country this size that is most of the sector. AND THE LGU'S OWN RECORD, which tells you what the network can do: it campaigned for the protection of the Ruggeller Riet from 1974 to 1978 and against the Rhine power stations from 1981 to 1992; it holds a seat on the government's Naturschutzkommission; it obtained the Verbandsklagerecht in 1996 under its own pressure; and it takes part in Vernehmlassungen — the formal consultation rounds — to influence executive and legislature. Its four work areas are environmental policy, Umweltanwaltschaft, environmental education and practical measures. TWO MORE THINGS A LIECHTENSTEIN COMMUNITY CAN USE: the LGU argues, in its own words, that the effects of a project must be shown transparently and comprehensively, and that this knowledge must exist before decisions are taken — the position it took publicly on a planned suspension bridge, opposing steering more visitors into a wildlife corridor. And there are Naturwächterinnen und Naturwächter — nature wardens who watch that rules of conduct are observed in their own districts.

trackers.name: Kommission für Natur- und Landschaftsschutz — three seats reserved for private conservation bodies
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the standing commission that advises the government on fundamental questions of nature and landscape protection, in particular in drafting implementing ordinances and developing concepts. Liechtenstein is small enough that this one body is where the sector meets the state. ITS COMPOSITION, WHICH IS THE RESOURCE: a representative of the Office for the Environment as chair, one representative each of the GEMEINDE and of the BÜRGERGENOSSENSCHAFTEN, THREE REPRESENTATIVES OF PRIVATE NATURE PROTECTION ORGANISATIONS, one of agriculture, and a landscape planner. Three of roughly seven seats belong to private conservation organisations — the LGU, BZG and CIPRA Liechtenstein already filed here are the bodies that hold them. A community reaching one of those three is reaching a seat at the table where ordinances are drafted. AND THE SEAT NOBODY OUTSIDE THE ALPS EXPECTS: the Bürgergenossenschaften — the citizens' cooperatives — have their own representative. These are the historic communal landholding bodies of the Alpine states, and this file has already recorded the same shape in Italy's domini collettivi and Andorra's comuns. Where common land exists, its holders sit on the conservation commission.

trackers.name: Liechtenstein's state payments for ecological and landscape services
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: Liechtenstein pays compensation for ecological and animal-friendly services to reward farmers for services that are not remunerated by the market and are demanded by society. The stated purposes include that new habitats are to be created for plants and animals in agricultural areas and that the networking of habitats should be achieved in the long term. Liechtenstein had no funder filed at all; this is the state money that actually reaches land. WHY IT MATTERS TO A COMMUNITY RATHER THAN A FARMER: the recipient is the landholder, so this is what you offer an owner who is being courted by a developer — a standing public payment for keeping and improving habitat, rather than a one-off purchase price. The same logic runs through France's bail rural environnemental and Ukraine's protection obligation, already in this file. WHAT ELSE THE STATE FUNDS: management of alpine pastures, paid as an alpine pasture cost contribution to THE OWNER of the alp; and Alpine infrastructures, promoted expressly taking into account the interests of environmental, nature and landscape protection. AN HONEST NOTE: I searched for a dedicated Liechtenstein nature or landscape fund and did not find one; what exists is the agricultural payment system above and the commission route. For cross-border projects, Swiss foundation directories list funds whose reach includes the neighbouring cantons.

trackers.name: San Marino — Trade Register (Chamber of Commerce)
trackers.desc: National corporate registry; the Chamber of Commerce Trade Register (Registro delle Imprese, Art.5 Law 71/2004) automatically records all licensed economic operators, with downloadable company certificates & balance sheets via an online desk, San Marino. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: San Marino — Segreteria di Stato per le Finanze e il Bilancio
trackers.desc: National budget authority; prepares the State budget (leggi di bilancio) & economic programme and manages public debt, Republic of San Marino. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in SMR.

trackers.name: Legge 126/1995 — fragility and spectacularity are statutory criteria
trackers.desc: CHOOSE THE CATEGORY DELIBERATELY, BECAUSE THE PROTECTION FOLLOWS IT. The Legge quadro per la tutela dell'ambiente e la salvaguardia del paesaggio, della vegetazione e della flora (16 November 1995 n.126) governs the conservation, il recupero and safeguarding of landscape and natural environment — recovery is a statutory purpose, so restoring a degraded site is within the law's object. Article 2 classifies protected areas as: (a) aree naturalistiche tutelate — parts of the territory of landscape and/or environmental significance with characteristics of naturalness and/or conservation integration, where the ‘and/or’ does real work: landscape significance alone qualifies; (b) aree a parco — zones of general public interest for the community, organised with preeminent regard to protecting nature, for cultural, recreational and agroforestry uses fostering the cultural, social and economic growth of the community, so a working landscape can be a park and community economic benefit is a stated purpose, not a concession; (c) riserve naturali — which beyond (a) must show diversità, rappresentatività, fragilità e spettacolarità; and (d) riserve naturali integrali, of particular naturalistic and scientific interest. FRAGILITY AND SPECTACULARITY ARE NAMED STATUTORY CRITERIA — an argument resting on how easily a site is damaged, or how striking it is, stands on the text rather than on sentiment.

trackers.name: AccessInfo.hk — FOI requests (HKG)
trackers.desc: You CAN get: information held by Hong Kong government bureaux and departments, and by the public agencies listed at Annex A of the Code on Access to Information — requested through this volunteer-run platform, which files on your behalf and publishes every request and reply openly, so past answers are searchable before you ask. Anyone may request, resident or not, and requests can be oral or written. Land-relevant precedent exists: the Lands Department has answered requests about specific land grants here. You CAN'T get: a legal right. HONG KONG HAS NO FREEDOM-OF-INFORMATION STATUTE — the Code is an administrative instrument only, with no legal protection of the right, and the Ombudsman has criticised departments for refusing on grounds the Code does not contain. It does not reach the many statutory and advisory bodies that decide policy. Refusal grounds are broad — security, external affairs, administration of justice — subject to a public-interest test the department applies itself. For activists: if refused, ask for internal review, then complain to the Ombudsman. But note the limit that bites hardest on a development fight — the Ombudsman is statutorily barred from investigating the imposition or variation of LAND GRANT CONDITIONS, and will not take a complaint more than two years old.

trackers.name: Hong Kong — The Budget (Financial Services & the Treasury Bureau)
trackers.desc: National budget-transparency portal; the official HKSAR Budget site publishes the annual Financial Secretary’s Budget, detailed revenue & expenditure estimates by head, and supporting fiscal data, Hong Kong. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Hong Kong.

trackers.name: Companies Registry
trackers.desc: National company registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Hong Kong Companies Registry
trackers.desc: Hong Kong's official company registry. Here you can trace companies, their directors and filings registered in Hong Kong.

trackers.name: HKLII
trackers.desc: Hong Kong Legal Information Institute: free judgments and legislation. · Find here: free Hong Kong legislation and the judgments of its courts (HKLII).

trackers.name: Hong Kong Judiciary
trackers.desc: Official judgments and legal-reference system of the HK courts. · Find here: the judgments of the Hong Kong Judiciary across all court levels.

trackers.name: Cap. 208 s.11 — 60 days to object, with a guaranteed hearing
trackers.desc: A FULLY SPECIFIED OBJECTION ROUTE. Under the Country Parks Ordinance (Cap. 208), the Authority publishes a draft map in the Gazette for a new country park (s.8) and makes it available for inspection (s.9(1)) — and under section 11 any person aggrieved may, within the 60-day inspection period from gazettal, send a written statement of objection to both the Authority and the Secretary of the Board. The Board SHALL arrange a hearing, and submits the draft map with a schedule of objections and representations to the Chief Executive in Council. 60 days, in writing, to two addressees, with a guaranteed hearing and a schedule that goes up to the decision-maker — so an objection cannot simply be lost. The Board may reject it or direct the Authority to amend the draft map. BUT READ WHAT CAN STILL HAPPEN INSIDE A PARK: the Director of AFCD may approve overhead power cables proposed by utilities and recreational facilities by the private sector, and small house development may be considered subject to Lands Department approval. A USEFUL PRINCIPLE: the 2011 review confirmed that the mere existence of private land will not be automatically taken as a determining factor for exclusion from a country park boundary. SCALE: 24 country parks and 22 special areas, 44,300 ha or 40 percent of land area, holding over 98 percent of all flora and fauna species. Judicial review is available — see Chan Ka Lam v Country and Marine Parks Authority (CACV 150/2017).

trackers.name: If your site is an enclave, Cap. 208 is the wrong instrument
trackers.desc: THE DISTINCTION THAT DECIDES WHICH LAW APPLIES. Country park enclaves are sites surrounded by or adjacent to country parks but NOT part of them, mostly a mix of private and government land — and control on development there relies on the land lease terms, the Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) and, if available, Development Permission Area plans or Outline Zoning Plans under the Town Planning Ordinance. So if your site is an enclave, the Country Parks Ordinance is not your instrument. Section 16(1)(d) of the Buildings Ordinance may be invoked to reject plans. WHY THIS EXISTS: the Sai Wan incident of June 2010 — unauthorised excavation on private and government land in an enclave — led the Government to undertake to either bring enclaves into country parks or determine their uses through statutory planning. THE FUNDING ROUTE IS THE MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT SCHEME: funding is granted to enable competent non-profit making organisations to enter into management agreements with landowners, giving landowners financial incentives in exchange for management rights over their land or cooperation in conservation — covering private land in enclaves and within country parks. That is a funded, voluntary, contractual route over private land — the closest thing here to the conservation-easement model recorded elsewhere in this map. OTHER INSTRUMENTS: the Town Planning Ordinance (Cap. 131) designates coastal protection areas, SSSIs, Conservation Areas and Green Belt through the Town Planning Board — a separate route with a different decision-maker; Cap. 96 prohibits felling and cutting on Government land; and EIA reports must undergo statutory public inspection and consideration by the Advisory Council on the Environment.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: Macau — Commercial & Movable Property Registry (DSAJ / CRCBM)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the DSAJ’s Commercial & Movable Property Registry runs an online commercial-register information platform (company number, firm, seat, capital, directors), Macau SAR. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Macau — Commission of Audit (Comissariado da Auditoria)
trackers.desc: National public-finance watchdog; the Commission of Audit is Macau’s government auditor, conducting independent financial & performance audits of public operations and publishing audit reports, Macau SAR. — Holds to account: officials handling public money & power — find audit findings and how public money was spent or lost.

trackers.name: Macau — Financial Services Bureau (DSF)
trackers.desc: National budget authority; the Direcção dos Serviços de Finanças prepares & executes the Macau SAR budget, manages public revenue, expenditure & accounts and publishes budget & financial reports, Macau. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Macau.

trackers.name: The heritage law is the instrument with teeth — and it binds the planners
trackers.desc: IN MACAU THE PROTECTIVE INSTRUMENT OVER LAND IS THE CULTURAL HERITAGE LAW, NOT A NATURE LAW — worth knowing before you search for one. Decree-Law No. 11/2013 of 22 August protects immovable property classified OR in the process of being classified, and property in protection zones or provisional protection zones — the third preliminary-protection instrument in this map, after Bosnia's privremena zaštita and Kosovo's mbrojtja paraprake. THE STATUS GOES ON THE LAND REGISTER: it must be noted (averbada) against the property description, and the noting is made ex officio and free of charge — so protection is discoverable by any buyer or developer from the predial description, and securing it costs the applicant nothing. THE STRONGEST PROVISION IS THE BINDING PRIOR OPINION: issuing plantas de alinhamento oficial or plantas de condições urbanísticas for the Historic Centre, classified property or protection zones requires the parecer vinculativo prévio of the IC — a binding, not advisory, opinion over the planning documents that precede any building permission. Ask whether it was obtained. Urban plans of any nature must contain specific protective measures and are elaborated with the participation of the IC. AND THE TRIGGER THRESHOLD IS LOW: obras de grande impacte are public or private works — expressly including hydraulic works, infrastructure and communication routes — which may imply risk of deterioration, destruction OR DIMINUTION OF THE VALUE of classified property or its protection zones. Risk of diminution suffices; certain harm is not required. The Historic Centre's safeguard plan must also guarantee sustainable use in urban, cultural AND environmental terms.

trackers.name: DSPA — hotline, and the plan vocabulary to write your proposal in
trackers.desc: A REACHABLE BODY AND A FRAME TO USE. The Environmental Protection Bureau (DSPA): Estrada de D. Maria II, 32-36, Edifício CEM, 1.º andar, Macau; main line (853) 2872 5134; Environmental Protection Hotline (853) 2876 2626 — a dedicated hotline is the faster route for a complaint. It produced Macao's first environmental planning (2010–2020), whose stated aim includes establishing an urban ecosystem network composed of green points (greening nodes), lines (linear greening and corridors), areas (parks and leisure zones) and spaces (vertical greening). USE THAT VOCABULARY: points, lines, areas and spaces are the plan's own categories, so a corridor or a single node already has a named place in it — a proposal framed in those terms fits the instrument rather than arguing against it. LANGUAGE CAUTION FROM THE GOVERNMENT'S OWN PORTAL: all information is based on the official language of the Macao SAR, and the English version is a translation from the Chinese originals, provided for reference only. Work from the Chinese or Portuguese text wherever anything turns on wording — and note that this map's heritage-law entry for Macau cites the Portuguese text for that reason.

trackers.name: Parliamentary Ombudsman of Greenland
trackers.desc: Greenland’s Parliamentary Ombudsman, investigating complaints against public administration.

trackers.name: Greenland — Business Registration (Akileraartarnermut Aqutsisoqarfik / CVR)
trackers.desc: National corporate registry; since 1 Jan 2018 Greenlandic companies register in the Central Business Register (CVR) under the Danish Companies Act — registration managed locally by Greenland’s Tax Agency (Akileraartarnermut Aqutsisoqarfik), which maintains company data, Greenland. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Greenland — Revisionsudvalget (Inatsisartut Audit Committee)
trackers.desc: National public-finance watchdog; the Inatsisartut Audit Committee (§§18–19) oversees the financial, legal-critical & performance audit of the Landskasse (Treasury) accounts — audit work performed by the appointed Landskasserevisor — and reports to Parliament on their approval, Greenland.

trackers.name: Greenland — Ministry of Finance (Naalakkersuisut)
trackers.desc: National budget authority; the Government of Greenland’s Ministry of Finance is responsible for the budget, tax policy, the Danish block grant, structural policy & Statistics Greenland, Greenland. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Greenland.

trackers.name: Court of Greenland
trackers.desc: Court of Greenland — tribunal in Greenland (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: Two publication regimes — Greenlandic law is on lovgivning.gl
trackers.desc: IDENTIFY WHICH SYSTEM YOUR RULE BELONGS TO BEFORE CITING IT. Under the Act on Greenland Self-Government (Act no. 473 of 12 June 2009), legislative power lies with Inatsisartut, executive power with Naalakkersuisut and judicial power with the courts. The Self-Government authorities' own legal precepts enter into force at the beginning of the day following the day they are made public on www.lovgivning.gl, and each entry must state the day of entry — so that is where you check whether a Greenlandic rule is in force. Realm legislation applying to Greenland is promulgated separately in the Danish Law Gazette, and that promulgation is a precondition for entry into force of administrative orders for Greenland. Two publication regimes run in parallel, and a rule from one will not be found in the other. THE MINERAL POSITION SHAPES MOST LAND DISPUTES HERE: in November 2009 the Self-Government authorities decided to take over the mineral resource area from 1 January 2010, assuming the right to utilise the mineral resources found in the subsoil, with revenues accruing to the Self-Government. So minerals are a Greenlandic competence, not a Danish one — address Naalakkersuisut, and note that the revenue interest sits with the same authority that regulates. The Act records the people of Greenland as a people pursuant to international law with the right of self-determination, Denmark and Greenland being equal partners.

trackers.name: Fredning — read the specific order, because they differ enormously
trackers.desc: TWO ORDERS, TWO COMPLETELY DIFFERENT REGIMES — which is why the general law tells you little. At Lyngmarken, Greenland's oldest natural-history fredning (protected 1954, extended 1979 and 1986) around Arktisk Station, the designation was made for the benefit of scientific investigation and expressly does not restrict the population's right to use the area — the model to cite where a community fears exclusion. At Paradisdalen (Arnangarnuup Qoorua), fredet 1984, all animal and plant life is protected year-round and movement is permitted on foot only. Read the specific bekendtgørelse. Protection rests on Landstingslov nr. 29 af 18. december 2003 om Naturbeskyttelse, with management divided between several departments covering fredning, living resources, råstoffer and genetic resources — establish which holds your issue. A SINGLE COLONY OR HAULING-OUT SITE IS A RECOGNISED UNIT: fredning covers specific localities important for particular species, including bird protection areas, seabird colonies and walrus hauling-out sites — a smaller and more attainable ask than an area designation. SCALE: 12 areas fredet under the Act, 13 bird protection areas regulated in the breeding period, 6 larger area protections, and 11 Ramsar sites; the National Park in North and East Greenland is about 43 percent of Greenland's total area — the world's largest protected area — a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve since 1977. ONE CATEGORY IS NOT PROTECTION: the ‘vigtige områder for dyrelivet’ in the mineral field rules exist to make companies exercise particular regard, and are expressly not protected areas in the proper sense — if a company cites field-rule status, that is not a designation.

trackers.name: Nordic Council of Ministers — Greenland counts toward the three
trackers.desc: YOU COUNT AS A FULL ENTITY, NOT A JUNIOR PARTNER — that is the whole point of this entry. The Nordic Council of Ministers requires that at least three of the following must be involved: Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Iceland, Finland, the Faroe Islands, Greenland, or Åland. The Faroe Islands, Greenland and Åland count toward the three alongside the five states, so a project involving only those three autonomous territories satisfies the requirement without any larger country. The central criterion is that projects provide added value to the Nordic countries, the Faroe Islands, Greenland, and Åland — the three are named again in the added-value test, so the benefit need not accrue to the states. ASK WHICH ROUTE APPLIES BEFORE PREPARING ANYTHING: the Council issues direct calls on particular topics from time to time, but the majority of projects are run by an ‘administrative body’, usually a national agency in the Nordic Region, commissioned by the Council — so most of the money is not distributed by the Council itself. The environment and climate working groups fund Nordic projects as a second layer within the same structure. A GREENLANDIC PRECEDENT WORTH KNOWING FOR ITS OWN SAKE: PISUNA-net, a local observations database built to record, archive and share community observations, won the Nordic Council Environment Prize in 2018 for participatory monitoring protecting marine life. Where a community has observers rather than scientists and needs an evidence base, that is a precedent with a prize attached.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Faroese Parliamentary Ombudsman
trackers.desc: The Faroe Islands’ Parliamentary Ombudsman, investigating complaints against public administration.

trackers.name: Faroe Islands — Landsgrann­ skoðanin (National Audit)
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution; Landsgrannskoðanin is the independent audit body under the Løgting (per Audit Act no. 25 of 21 April 1999) that audits the national accounts and publishes annual reports & appropriation-oversight findings, Faroe Islands.

trackers.name: Faroe Islands — Ministry of Finance (Fíggjarmálaráðið)
trackers.desc: National budget authority; the Ministry of Finance coordinates the Faroese government’s budgetary, financial & economic matters, underpins taxation & fees legislation and oversees public-sector finances, Faroe Islands. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Faroe Islands.

trackers.name: Faroe Islands — Skráseting Føroya (Company Registration Authority)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the Faroese Company Registration Authority registers & maintains records of companies & associations (and the national ship register), Faroe Islands. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Faroe Islands District Court
trackers.desc: Faroe Islands District Court — first instance court in Faroe Islands (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: Jurisdiction is Faroese — and the conservation act dates from 1970
trackers.desc: DO NOT ADDRESS A DANISH MINISTRY. Under the Home Rule Act, environment and nature management are Faroese jurisdictions — the islands are responsible for the legislation protecting nature and regulating harmful activities, and the Løgting legislates on environmental matters. THE THREE INSTRUMENTS: the Act on Nature Conservation, 1970, which protects areas of natural beauty, wildlife and habitats and regulates the creation and management of protected areas such as national parks and nature reserves; the Act on Environmental Protection, 1988, on pollution of air, water and soil and vibrations; and the Act on the Protection of the Marine Environment, 2005. NOTE THE 1970 DATE: the conservation act predates the rapid development the islands have seen since the 1960s in infrastructure, energy consumption and tourism — a half-century-old designation statute is worth reading closely for what it does not anticipate. WHAT IS ALREADY PROTECTED: important bird areas as Ramsar sites, including Skúvoy, Nólsoy and Mykines. Over 300 bird species recorded, 50 breeding regularly, with endemic subspecies including the Faroe eider — and the Faroe charr, an endemic fish known only from Lake Leynavatn. A single-lake endemic is the strongest possible site-specific argument. PRESSURES IN THE BAYS: transportation, sand extraction and aquaculture, alongside 70,000 sheep on semi-natural pasture.

trackers.name: The tourism law puts environment first — in those words
trackers.desc: A STATUTORY PRIORITY ORDERING, STATED IN TERMS. The Løgting's law on sustainable tourism is explained by the Ministry's senior adviser as follows: ‘The aim is to achieve environmental, social, and economic sustainability, in that order.’ A government stating the priority sequence explicitly is unusual and directly quotable against any proposal that inverts it. AND COMMUNITIES CAN CAP VISITOR NUMBERS: the law makes it possible for local communities to restrict the number of tourists, to ensure these communities remain good places to live in — a community power exercised on liveability grounds, which is rare. The law is also to protect the natural environment, existing agricultural activities, and local ownership and participation; access may be restricted when collecting sheep, in lambing season, or in poor weather. Fee income is earmarked for hiking paths and tourism planning. WHY IT WAS NEEDED: the previous rule on walking traditional paths was the agriculture law from 1937, long before tourism was contemplated, and as tourism surged farmers and operators met it with various private unauthorised systems. RECORDED HONESTLY: reporting notes the hiking fee has in places been driven by private landowners rather than government, and that it is not yet clear who exactly benefits — treat the fee regime as unsettled rather than as a model.

trackers.name: Granskingarráðið — ‘significant in a Faroese context’ is an alternative limb
trackers.desc: RECORDED HONESTLY: THREE ROUNDS OF SEARCHING, IN ENGLISH AND FAROESE, FOUND NO COMMUNITY ENVIRONMENTAL GRANT SCHEME IN THE FAROE ISLANDS. What exists is research funding plus Horizon Europe access. The Research Council Faroe Islands is a public research funding body which also administers the islands' association agreement on participation in Horizon Europe. Funding opens once a year — the next deadline published as 15 February 2027, 12:00 noon local time — so missing the single date costs a year. ELIGIBILITY HAS THREE ALTERNATIVE LIMBS: research carried out by a Faroese researcher, OR in cooperation with a Faroese research institute, OR considered significant in a Faroese context. That third limb is an alternative, not an additional requirement — so a project need not be led by a Faroese researcher if its significance to the Faroes can be established. That is the limb to argue if you are a community or outside partner rather than an academic body. It funds PhD projects, postdoc or other projects of at least 6 months, and industrial R&D; criteria are scientific excellence, impact and implementation, with advantage to projects producing data and lasting knowledge and skills. THE PRACTICAL ROUTE: pair with a Faroese research institute and frame the work as producing data — baseline surveys, monitoring and inventories fit this funder in a way campaigning does not.

trackers.name: Umhvørvisstovan — conservation, the cadastre and land registration in one agency
trackers.desc: ONE ENQUIRY ESTABLISHES BOTH OWNERSHIP AND STATUS. The Faroese Environment Agency, under the Ministry of Environment and based at Argir, covers environmental protection, environmental research, nature conservation, energy and electricity supply supervision, woodlands and recreational areas, land and sea maps, the cadastre (matrikul), land registration (tinglýsing) and the national population register. Nature conservation, the cadastre and land registration sit in the same agency — so establishing who is registered against a parcel and its conservation status is a single-agency enquiry, which is unusual and makes early fact-finding far cheaper than in most jurisdictions in this map. IT ALSO CO-FUNDS APPLIED RESEARCH: it is recorded as a named financier of Faroese fjord benthic macrofauna classification work alongside the aquaculture association, and the environment and industry ministry has directly financed environmental monitoring in Faroese fjords — by arrangement rather than through an open call. SO THE THREE REALISTIC ROUTES HERE ARE: partnering with a research institute into the Research Council's annual call; a direct arrangement with Umhvørvisstovan; or Horizon Europe via the association agreement. None is an application form a village association can complete alone — plan for a partner.

trackers.name: GEF Small Grants Programme (SGP) — Turkmenistan
trackers.desc: TURKMENISTAN WAS ADDED TO SGP PARTICIPATION IN GEF-8, and is named among the 11 new countries on the GEF's own page — so this is a newly available route, and older guidance will not list it. SGP is a GEF corporate programme running since 1992, implemented by UNDP and executed by UNOPS; GEF-8 raised participation from 124 countries to 135, out of 144 eligible. THE MONEY IS NOT COMPETED FOR ACROSS COUNTRIES: GEF-8 secured $135 million for the core programme with equal allocation of nearly $1 million in core financing to each of the 135 countries — a per-country floor, which is unusual. Grants of up to $50,000 go directly to local communities, including community-based organisations and other non-governmental groups. FOCAL AREAS: biodiversity, climate change, land degradation and sustainable forest management, international waters and chemicals. READ YOUR COUNTRY PROGRAMME STRATEGY BEFORE APPLYING: each country writes its own CPS which puts emphasis on certain thematic and geographic areas, so it may exclude your region or theme regardless of global eligibility. WHO DECIDES LOCALLY: a locally recruited National Coordinator and a voluntary National Steering Committee, described as the central element of SGP and the body providing substantive oversight. Note that under SGP 2.0 the implementing agency may be FAO or Conservation International rather than UNDP, and the host may be a national host institution rather than the UNDP country office — confirm which applies before addressing an application.

trackers.name: Law on Nature Protection — public associations' rights, and the emergency chapter
trackers.desc: CITE THE RIGHT INSTRUMENT — the statutes are dated and distinct. «Об охране природы» dates from 12 November 1991; «О государственных особо охраняемых природных территориях» from 19 May 1992; «О государственной экологической экспертизе» from 15 June 1995; «Об углеводородных ресурсах» from 1996. WHAT THE NATURE PROTECTION LAW GIVES YOU: it enshrines the rights and obligations of citizens and of public associations (общественных объединений) in nature protection, and establishes financing — a statutory recognition of public associations' rights in the founding law, not a subordinate act. Chapter IX (articles 42–45) covers forests, flora, fauna and specially protected territories, with article 45 on objects subject to special protection. Article 38 sets ecological requirements for activity in the Turkmen sector of the Caspian Sea. AND WHERE DEGRADATION IS ALREADY SEVERE: Chapter XI covers чрезвычайные экологические ситуации and зоны экологического бедствия — emergency ecological situations and ecological disaster zones — with article 49 on the emergency situation. That is a named statutory category with its own chapter, distinct from ordinary protection. Violating the regime of a protected territory carries administrative, civil or criminal responsibility. ASK WHETHER A STATE ECOLOGICAL EXPERTIZA WAS CONDUCTED — it has its own 1995 statute and is a separate act from any permit.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — it takes communications from the public
trackers.desc: A ROUTE THAT DOES NOT DEPEND ON DOMESTIC STANDING. Turkmenistan is a Party to the Aarhus Convention, and UNECE hosts Turkmen environmental legislation within its compliance section under decisions of the Meeting of the Parties, including a country-specific MoP4 decision folder — so the mechanism has been engaged with Turkmenistan before. The Compliance Committee receives communications from members of the public concerning a Party's compliance with obligations on access to information, public participation in decision-making and access to justice. Where domestic routes are closed, this one does not turn on national standing rules — which is why it matters more here than in most jurisdictions in this map. BE REALISTIC ABOUT WHAT IT DELIVERS: the Committee's outputs are findings and recommendations adopted by the Meeting of the Parties, not orders enforceable in a national court. It is a compliance and publicity mechanism, not a remedy — useful for creating a documented international record and for pressure, and it should be planned as that rather than as litigation.

trackers.name: CEPF Mountains of Central Asia — Turkmenistan is a named eligible country, and this is the only resource recorded for it
trackers.desc: TURKMENISTAN IS NAMED AS AN ELIGIBLE COUNTRY IN CEPF'S OWN CALLS FOR PROPOSALS, ALONGSIDE KAZAKHSTAN, KYRGYZSTAN, TAJIKISTAN AND UZBEKISTAN — and the eligible territory is small and specific: a mountainous part of the country's south-east, identified in the ecosystem profile as the Koytendag mountains and Talimerjen. If your site is not in that area it is outside the hotspot, and this route does not apply. WHY THIS IS THE ONLY ENTRY THIS MAP CARRIES FOR TURKMENISTAN, AND WHY IT IS AN EXTERNAL FUND RATHER THAN A LOCAL BODY: Turkmenistan is a closed operating environment, and naming domestic organisations or individuals in a public map can expose the people in them. An international fund names nobody. That is a deliberate limit on what is recorded here, not an omission — and a reader should understand that the absence of Turkmen organisations from this file reflects a decision about safety rather than a finding that none exist. WHAT THE FUND DOES: letters of inquiry are accepted from non-governmental organisations, community groups, Indigenous peoples' organisations, women's groups, private companies and other civil society organisations; large grants in recent calls ran from fifty thousand to a hundred and fifty thousand US dollars and small grants average around fifteen thousand, with a new portfolio beginning in 2026 after nearly a hundred projects in the first phase. Applications must align with the strategic directions, priority species, priority Key Biodiversity Areas or corridors set out in the ecosystem profile, which carries a table of Turkmen priorities of its own. Individuals cannot apply directly and must work through a civil society organisation. CEPF is a joint initiative of the French Development Agency, Conservation International, the European Union, the Global Environment Facility, the Government of Japan and the World Bank. Confirm the current regional implementation team and the open-call status before acting; and consider carefully, in this operating environment, what applying publicly for foreign conservation funding may mean for those named on the application.

trackers.name: Rufford Small Grants — Turkmenistan is named eligible, and no organisation or registration is required
trackers.desc: TURKMENISTAN IS ON THE FOUNDATION'S ELIGIBLE COUNTRY LIST AND NOT ON ITS LIST OF COUNTRIES IT CANNOT CURRENTLY CONSIDER. This is the third international funding route recorded for a country where this map deliberately records no local organisation, and it is the one that asks least of an applicant: individuals and small groups may apply, no registered body is needed, and there are no deadlines at any time of year. The focus is people early in a conservation career, especially current or recent MSc and PhD students, with others considered against the published criteria. THE SPECIES TEST IS PUBLISHED AND CHECKABLE BEFORE YOU START: any species not listed as Least Concern globally on the IUCN Red List, or not yet assessed but thought to be globally threatened. Threatened habitats, human-wildlife conflict and community education projects qualify with no species focus. GRANTS RUN AS A STAIRCASE from up to £7,000 to roughly £18,000 across four stages, each conditional on finishing and reporting the last, with updates and final reports published on the applicant's page. One application per twelve months; a twelve-month wait after rejection; the foundation expects to provide half to all of the cost and requires evidence of co-funding where there is any. THE CAUTION GIVEN FOR THE OTHER TURKMEN ENTRIES APPLIES HERE TOO AND IS REPEATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED TO CARRY: in a closed operating environment, weigh what a public application for foreign conservation funding, and a published project page carrying your name, may mean for you. The reporting that makes this fund attractive elsewhere is a public record, and that cuts both ways.

trackers.name: Copernicus Browser — free imagery, water and vegetation indices, and atmospheric data
trackers.desc: IT NEEDS NOTHING LOCAL. A free service for browsing and downloading FULL-RESOLUTION imagery from the European Copernicus satellite missions, where anyone can select an area and a date range, COMPARE IMAGES SIDE BY SIDE, and BUILD A TIMELAPSE showing how a place has changed — all from a web browser with a free account. Every other entry recorded for this country is a foreign institution or a state portal, because domestic organisations cannot safely be named. A TOOL ONE PERSON OPERATES ALONE IS THEREFORE THE MOST DIRECTLY USABLE RESOURCE IN THIS COUNTRY'S ENTIRE LISTING. IT CARRIES MORE THAN PICTURES: a VEGETATION index for plant health, a WATER index for surface water, radar imagery that sees through cloud, and ATMOSPHERIC AND AIR QUALITY DATA from a dedicated mission. For land drying, canals and irrigation, pasture loss or industrial emissions, those are the layers that turn an impression into a measurement — and this file has recorded across the region that measurement is what an authority or a court will engage with. AN INVESTIGATIVE RESEARCH TOOLKIT LISTS ITS USES AS TRACKING CONSTRUCTION PROJECTS, MINING OPERATIONS AND LAND DEVELOPMENT, and documenting environmental degradation over time. WHAT IT WILL NOT DO: it is imagery and data, not analysis, and nobody interprets it for you. Resolution is moderate, so individual buildings and small clearings may be hard to read; optical images are blocked by cloud; and a free account is currently needed. Pair it with the forest monitoring platform recorded elsewhere in this file, which supplies annual tree cover loss and daily fire alerts for anywhere on earth. AND CHECK THE ADDRESS BEFORE FOLLOWING ANY GUIDE: THE PREDECESSOR VIEWER WAS SHUT DOWN IN FEBRUARY 2025 and its functions were moved here, so older tutorials name a service that no longer exists.

trackers.name: Digital Security Helpline — free, round the clock, answered within two hours, in Russian
trackers.desc: IT COSTS NOTHING, IT RUNS TWENTY-FOUR HOURS A DAY, AND IT ANSWERS EVERY REQUEST WITHIN TWO HOURS — with support available in RUSSIAN among ten languages. Every other entry recorded for this country is a foreign institution, a state portal or a satellite tool used alone, because domestic organisations cannot safely be named here. A HELPLINE IS THE FIRST ENTRY IN THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING THAT PUTS A PERSON ON THE OTHER END OF A MESSAGE. IT DOES TWO DIFFERENT JOBS AND YOU SHOULD KNOW WHICH YOU NEED. Before anything happens, it walks you or your group through ASSESSING THE RISKS YOUR WORK ACTUALLY CREATES and deciding what to secure first. If you are already under attack, it provides RAPID-RESPONSE EMERGENCY ASSISTANCE. AND IT TURNS AN ATTACK INTO EVIDENCE: it helps people ANALYSE, DOCUMENT AND EXPOSE advanced attacks including SPYWARE and targeted phishing. A technically documented intrusion is something an international body can act on; an unverified suspicion is not. IT SECURES WHAT A SMALL GROUP ACTUALLY HAS — devices, accounts, websites and social media — and provides guidance materials, training and onward referrals. REACH IT BY EMAIL AT A PUBLISHED ADDRESS. It is an accredited member of a computer emergency response body for civil society and publishes a data usage policy and helpline terms of service. READ BOTH BEFORE SENDING ANYTHING, AND THINK HARD ABOUT WHICH DEVICE AND CONNECTION YOU USE TO MAKE CONTACT — in this country that decision matters more than the message. THE LIMITS: it handles digital security and nothing else. It will not advise on a land case, fund anything, represent anyone, or change the conditions that make the work dangerous. Use it alongside the satellite imagery browser recorded separately for this country, which is the kind of activity that draws the attention this helpline exists to defend against.

trackers.name: GBIF — free species occurrence records for any location, downloadable and citable
trackers.desc: IT NEEDS NO LOCAL ORGANISATION AND NO PERMISSION. More than three billion species occurrence records — from museums, HERBARIA, government inventories, surveys and citizen science across more than a hundred countries — searchable by place and by species, free to consult, with each record showing the scientific name, coordinates, DATE, source and flags describing its provenance and locational accuracy. Every other entry recorded for this country is a foreign institution, a state portal or a tool used alone, because domestic organisations cannot safely be named here. THIS IS THE FOURTH SUCH TOOL, AND IT ANSWERS THE QUESTION THE OTHERS CANNOT: NOT WHAT CHANGED, BUT WHAT LIVES THERE. AND WHEN YOU DOWNLOAD RECORDS IT ISSUES A PERMANENT IDENTIFIER, so your exact extraction is CITABLE AND REPRODUCIBLE by anyone who wants to check it. That converts a species record from something you assert into something documented, which is the difference this file has repeatedly found between an objection that is dismissed and one that must be answered. THE SPECIMENS AND SURVEYS BEHIND THOSE RECORDS INCLUDE MATERIAL COLLECTED IN THIS REGION OVER MORE THAN A CENTURY AND HELD IN INSTITUTIONS ABROAD — which is precisely the material a person here cannot otherwise reach. DOWNLOADS ARRIVE AS COORDINATES IN A SPREADSHEET AND IMPORT DIRECTLY INTO MAPPING SOFTWARE, including the free satellite imagery browser recorded separately for this country. Species records plus dated imagery is a before-and-after argument built entirely from open sources and made by one person. Access is free under open licences; a free account is required to download, and the programming interface requires no registration at all. THE LIMIT, AND IT CUTS BOTH WAYS: IT SHOWS WHAT HAS BEEN OBSERVED AND PUBLISHED, NOT WHAT EXISTS. Sparsely surveyed country looks empty, and an operator can cite that emptiness exactly as a community would cite a record. Treat a blank map as a gap in the record rather than a fact about the ground.

trackers.name: Central Asia Pastoralist Alliance — regional bloc for rangeland rights, covering this country
trackers.desc: THIS COUNTRY IS NAMED IN A REGIONAL ALLIANCE THAT HAS ALREADY CHANGED PASTURE LAW ELSEWHERE. Its members were HIGHLY INVOLVED IN DRAFTING AND IMPLEMENTING SIX LAND-RELATED POLICIES, INCLUDING AMENDMENTS TO PASTURE LAWS in three countries of the region, prompting RECOGNITION OF PASTORALIST AND HERDER COMMUNITY LAND RIGHTS, SECURING MORE THAN THIRTY-NINE MILLION HECTARES OF PASTURELAND and affecting OVER EIGHTY THOUSAND HOUSEHOLDS. Everything else recorded for this country is a foreign institution, a state portal or a tool used alone. THIS IS THE FIRST ENTRY THAT CONNECTS IT TO A REGIONAL BLOC WITH A RECORD OF WINNING. THE ALLIANCE SPANS Afghanistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Mongolia, Tajikistan, this country and Uzbekistan, and sits within a global land-rights coalition of nearly three hundred organisations across more than eighty countries. EVERY MEMBER OF THAT COALITION SIGNS A PLEDGE TO UPHOLD GENDER JUSTICE AND TO DEFEND LAND AND ENVIRONMENTAL DEFENDERS WHO ARE CRIMINALISED, INTIMIDATED AND MARGINALISED FOR ADVOCATING CHANGE. In a country where this file records no domestic organisation that can safely be named, a regional body whose members have signed that commitment is a channel that exists outside the country. THE CONDITION IT ADDRESSES IS DOCUMENTED AND REGIONAL: an estimated SIXTY TO EIGHTY-EIGHT PER CENT OF ALL CENTRAL ASIAN PASTURELANDS HAVE DEGRADED, under pressure from common-resource decline, livestock numbers and the WIDE-SCALE EXPANSION OF INDUSTRIES. THE ROUTE IN IS THROUGH MEMBER ORGANISATIONS IN NEIGHBOURING COUNTRIES, three of which are recorded in this file — a pasture committee association, a rural research fund and a forest and land users association — and through the coalition's Asia office. THE LIMITS, AND THEY MATTER HERE: it is an alliance of organisations rather than a body an individual joins; its work is legislative advocacy rather than casework; and THE ALLIANCE NAMING THIS COUNTRY IS NOT EVIDENCE THAT A MEMBER ORGANISATION IS BASED IN IT. Establish that before relying on it, and consider what contacting a foreign network discloses — the digital security helpline recorded separately here is the place to ask first.

trackers.name: Aarhus Centre — the one body here whose stated job is giving the public environmental information
trackers.desc: ITS STATED PURPOSE IS THE THING THIS COUNTRY'S LISTING HAS NEVER CONTAINED: to facilitate FREE ACCESS TO ENVIRONMENTAL INFORMATION, PUBLIC PARTICIPATION IN ENVIRONMENTAL DECISION-MAKING, and ACCESS TO JUSTICE ON ENVIRONMENTAL MATTERS. Everything else recorded for this country is a foreign institution or a tool used alone, because domestic organisations cannot safely be named. This is a body inside the country whose published mandate is to give people environmental information — and asking a body to do the thing it exists to do is a different proposition from asking a favour. IT HAS OPERATED SINCE 2012 and its published work includes PRODUCING COMPREHENSIVE ENVIRONMENTAL MATERIALS FOR PUBLICATION IN THE NATIONAL MASS MEDIA, developing partnerships with state and civil society representatives and with the network of equivalent centres in other countries, and supporting the projects of international bodies including development, environment and regional development banks. THE NETWORK BEHIND IT MATTERS AS MUCH AS THE CENTRE: sixty such centres operate across fourteen countries, seven of them in this chat's region, and they work as a network. A question that cannot be pressed locally can sometimes be raised through a counterpart centre in a neighbouring country, or through the network's own reporting on how the convention is being implemented. WHAT THE MODEL CAN INCLUDE, THOUGH IT WAS NOT CONFIRMED HERE: centres elsewhere in the network employ LEGAL STAFF — a legal assistant and a legal associate — alongside a standing network of experts and volunteers brought in as needed. Ask what legal capacity this centre has before assuming it has none. THE LIMIT, STATED PLAINLY AND IT IS THE WHOLE CAUTION: the centre is supported by an intergovernmental security organisation and works IN CLOSE CO-OPERATION WITH THE HOST COUNTRY, in particular the ministry responsible for the environment. IT IS NOT INDEPENDENT. Where a dispute is with a state body or a state-owned project, weigh what you disclose and to whom. Use it to obtain information, to find out when and how a decision is open to comment, and to learn what the law requires; take anything adversarial to the international routes and the self-service tools recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: OSME Conservation Fund — it has asked for applications from this country by name
trackers.desc: THE FUND HAS SAID IT IS ESPECIALLY KEEN TO RECEIVE APPLICATIONS FROM THIS COUNTRY. No other funder recorded anywhere in this map names it. The society behind it covers the whole Middle East, Caucasus and Central Asia, and its small grants support conservation and research across that region. THE TERMS ARE BETTER THAN ALMOST ANY OTHER FUND IN THIS FILE: THREE DECISION ROUNDS EACH YEAR with deadlines of 31 January, 31 May and 30 September; typical awards of one to three thousand pounds WITH NO STATED MAXIMUM; and a published funding rate of AROUND FIFTY PER CENT. Most funds in this payload do not say what proportion they fund. One in two is a real chance rather than a lottery. AND THE ELIGIBLE WORK IS THE WORK THAT PROTECTS GROUND, NOT JUST BIRDS: INVESTIGATING POTENTIAL NEW IMPORTANT BIRD AREAS or ornithologically little-known areas; furthering knowledge of EXISTING important bird areas through breeding censuses and systematic counts; investigating the status of threatened species; STUDIES RELATED TO ILLEGAL BIRD KILLING AND UNSUSTAINABLE HUNTING; and educational programmes. Getting a stretch of steppe, wetland or desert recognised as an internationally important bird area is one of the few ways a place in this country can acquire a designation that outsiders recognise — and this fund pays for the survey that does it. ITS CRITERIA ARE WRITTEN IN FAVOUR OF LOCAL PEOPLE: projects should be INITIATED AND CARRIED OUT BY NATIONALS of the region, and/or engage local communities, and/or build long-term sustainability such as TRAINING LOCAL COUNTERPARTS — and applications carrying significant international airfare costs are unlikely to be approved. A fund that discourages flying in foreign experts is a fund that expects the work to be done by people who live there. TWO FURTHER GRANTS EXIST: one focused on threatened species research, a single award of up to five thousand pounds a year with a deadline around 1 December; and a youth fund for bird camps and education projects for people aged sixteen to twenty-five, LED FROM WITHIN THE REGION, typically one to two thousand pounds. The society also publishes a country profile for this country and has made a major international bird reference platform freely accessible across the region. THE LIMITS: it funds birds and their habitats, not land disputes; the sums are small; specimen collection requires justification and local authorisations; and it is a scientific society, not an advocate — it will not object to a project. Use it to fund the survey; use the survey with the species databases and satellite tools recorded separately for this country.

trackers.name: The Ombudsman — the only domestic institution in this country's listing that receives complaints
trackers.desc: EVERY OTHER ENTRY RECORDED FOR THIS COUNTRY IS A FOREIGN INSTITUTION OR A TOOL USED ALONE. THIS IS A DOMESTIC OFFICE THAT RECEIVES COMPLAINTS. The post was established to secure state protection of the rights and freedoms of people and citizens and their observance by government authorities, local governments and their officials. ITS KEY FUNCTION IS TO EXERCISE CONTROL OVER THE ACTIVITY OF STATE AUTHORITIES BY CONSIDERING CITIZENS' COMPLAINTS AGAINST THE ACTIONS OF BODIES OR OFFICIALS WHO BREACH RIGHTS — conducting INVESTIGATIONS, providing RECOMMENDATIONS, HAVING VIOLATED RIGHTS RESTORED, and submitting proposals to amend legislation. A local government decision on land is the action of a body, and it falls within that description. THE PROCEDURE IS DOCUMENTED AND OBTAINABLE, WHICH IS RARE HERE: a booklet published in TURKMEN, ENGLISH AND RUSSIAN sets out the procedure for making ORAL AND WRITTEN APPEALS to the office, produced with a United Nations agency. Get that booklet before writing — a complaint that follows the published procedure is harder to set aside on form. ORAL APPEALS ARE PROVIDED FOR AS WELL AS WRITTEN ONES, which matters where committing something to paper is itself a decision. THE LIMITS, AND THEY SHOULD SHAPE EXPECTATIONS COMPLETELY. This is a state office created by the state to consider complaints against the state; it makes RECOMMENDATIONS rather than binding orders; and no independent assessment of its effectiveness was found. This file has recorded nothing domestic for this country precisely because naming local organisations can expose people, AND A COMPLAINT IS A DISCLOSURE. Read this alongside the digital security helpline recorded separately here, decide what to put in writing, and remember that the office is described as a link between the state and civil society rather than as an adversary of the state.

trackers.name: Land ownership and the three offices that decide what a plot is
trackers.desc: FAMILIES OF CITIZENS CAN OWN LAND HERE, WHICH THIS MAP HAD NOWHERE RECORDED. District and city governors take decisions on GRANTING LAND PLOTS INTO OWNERSHIP TO FAMILIES OF CITIZENS for personal subsidiary farming — the homestead plot — and separately on privatising state-fund dwelling houses together with use of the land beneath and beside them. Foreign persons and companies cannot own land at all and are confined to long-term lease, so ownership here is a citizen's right rather than a market open to anyone. GRAZING IS ALSO GRANTABLE: governors decide on giving citizens, legal persons and individual holders PASTURES FOR LIVESTOCK in use and in lease, on proposals agreed with the state land management body. A household or a group seeking secure grazing has a named decision-maker and a named process. AND HERE IS SOMETHING THIS FILE HAS NEVER SUPPLIED FOR THIS COUNTRY — WHERE TO GO TO FIND OUT WHAT A PLOT ACTUALLY IS. Boundaries and legal status are fixed in the STATE LAND CADASTRE, maintained by the land resources service of the agriculture ministry. Encumbrances, easements and pledges are checked at the service for the STATE REGISTRATION OF RIGHTS TO IMMOVABLE PROPERTY under the justice ministry. Conformity with the designated purpose and with environmental and planning requirements is controlled by the state committee for environmental protection and land resources. Three offices, three different questions — who holds it, what is charged against it, and what it may lawfully be used for. A community that can answer those three about the plot next door knows more than it did. NOW THE HAZARD, AND IT IS IN THE SAME CODE: THE LAND SERVICE CARRIES OUT WORK TO IDENTIFY UNUSED LANDS AND LANDS USED IN VIOLATION OF THE LAND LEGISLATION. This file recorded the same trigger in a neighbouring country, where irrational use is a ground for ending a holding. KEEP EVIDENCE THAT YOUR LAND IS IN USE — cultivation, grazing, planting, repair — dated and photographed, because the finding that land is unused is made about you rather than by you. THE LIMITS. This is a statute, not an organisation: there is no body here to join, and every office named is a state office in a country where this file records no domestic organisation that can safely be named. Long-term lease of irrigated land of the farmers' associations is governed by a separate procedure tied to the state order for wheat and cotton, so agricultural land is not freely allocated.
