WHAT PUBLICATION DOES FOR THE COMMUNITY ITSELF: THE REPORT IS READ BY OFFICIALS, EXPERTS, SCHOLARS AND JOURNALISTS WORLDWIDE, CAN BE DOWNLOADED FREE OF CHARGE, AND IS ALSO READ BY PEOPLE AT THE SITES, WHICH HELPS TO GIVE LOCAL COMMUNITIES ENCOURAGEMENT AND STRENGTH. AND THE MEMBERSHIP DISTINCTION, RECORDED HONESTLY: FORMAL MEMBERSHIP EXISTS ONLY FOR THE GERMAN ASSOCIATION AND REQUIRES A RECOMMENDATION FROM AN EXISTING MEMBER, THE ABILITY TO READ OFFICIAL DOCUMENTS IN GERMAN AND TO ATTEND ANNUAL MEETINGS IN BERLIN — SO FORMAL MEMBERSHIP IS KEPT TO A SMALL GROUP, WHILE THE NETWORK IS THE WIDER BODY THE ASSOCIATION MANAGES. You cannot join the association, and you do not need to. Contributing a report puts you in the network, which is the part that matters — and knowing the distinction saves an application that would only be refused. WHO IT SUITS: African communities at or near a World Heritage site facing infrastructure, extraction, tourism or eviction — including where the site designation is being used against them. CAVEATS: WORLD HERITAGE SITES ONLY, ANNUAL PUBLICATION CYCLE, AND IT LOBBIES RATHER THAN LITIGATES OR FUNDS — nothing here compels a state. For the campaign against evictions in the name of conservation, Egypt's entry; for the indigenous territories consortium, Morocco's entry; for the co-complainant route to the continental court, Seychelles' entry.

trackers.name: Community booklets in Swahili, Lingala and Malagasy, and meetings that put communities fighting the same plantation company in a room together — plus a West and Central African alliance spanning 10 countries and a booklet naming the tactics companies use to take land
trackers.desc: BOOKLETS IN SWAHILI, LINGALA AND MALAGASY, AND MEETINGS BETWEEN COMMUNITIES FIGHTING THE SAME COMPANY — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S BURKINA FASO AND MADAGASCAR ENTRIES NAME A FOOD RIGHTS ORGANISATION; ITS EGYPT ENTRY THE INTERNATIONAL PEASANT MOVEMENT; ITS ALGERIA ENTRY THE MOVEMENT FUNDER; AND ITS GABON, CAMEROON AND DR CONGO BUCKETS CARRY PLANTATION AND FOREST HOSTS OF THEIR OWN. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS HOST, ENTRY-NAME AND DESCRIPTION ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS. THE AFRICAN LANGUAGES, WHICH IS THE FIND: SOME BOOKLETS AND VIDEOS OF PARTICULAR RELEVANCE FOR LOCAL COMMUNITY GROUPS ARE ALSO AVAILABLE IN LANGUAGES SPOKEN IN THESE LOCATIONS, LIKE SWAHILI, LINGALA AND MALAGASY — WITH AN ONLINE LIBRARY MAINTAINED SINCE 1996 IN SPANISH, FRENCH, ENGLISH AND PORTUGUESE. Swahili, Lingala and Malagasy. Not French and English with a promise of more — the actual working languages of Congo Basin, East African and Malagasy villages, in booklets and videos meant to be used at a meeting. This file has recorded language as the barrier that silently excludes more communities than any eligibility rule; this is one of the few resources in it that crossed that line properly. THE CONVENING WORK, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: NETWORKING AND FACILITATING THE GETTING-TOGETHER OF PEOPLE ACTIVE IN RESISTANCE PROCESSES FROM DIFFERENT PLACES WHERE COMMUNITIES FACE SIMILAR THREATS — FOR EXAMPLE, BRINGING TOGETHER COMMUNITY MEMBERS CONFRONTED WITH THE EXPANSION OF INDUSTRIAL OIL PALM OR TIMBER PLANTATIONS OR FOREST-CARBON PROJECTS. IN THESE MEETINGS OR FIELD VISITS, PEOPLE EXCHANGE EXPERIENCES, STRATEGIZE AND SHARE BOTH THE DIFFICULTIES AND INSPIRATIONS. Two villages facing the same company, in the same room. A company negotiates with each community separately and tells each one that the others have already agreed; the single most effective counter is the two communities comparing what they were told. FOREST-CARBON PROJECTS are named alongside plantations as a threat to be organised against. WHY THAT MATTERS, IN ITS OWN WORDS: EXCHANGES WITH COMMUNITY ACTIVISTS INVOLVED IN SIMILAR STRUGGLES HELPS TO BREAK THE ISOLATION AND MAKE VISIBLE THE EXTENT OF VIOLENCE THAT COMMUNITIES OFTEN FACE. THE AFRICAN ALLIANCE IT CARRIES: AN INFORMAL ALLIANCE AGAINST THE EXPANSION OF INDUSTRIAL MONOCULTURES IN WEST AND CENTRAL AFRICA HAS, FOR ALMOST 10 YEARS, CONNECTED GRASSROOTS ORGANISATIONS AND ACTIVISTS AND STRENGTHENED RESISTANCE AGAINST LAND GRABBING AND OTHER ATTACKS BY OIL PALM AND OTHER PLANTATION COMPANIES — WITH ACTIVISTS FROM 10 COUNTRIES GATHERING AT A GENERAL ASSEMBLY AND ISSUING A NAMED DECLARATION. INFORMAL is the point: no registration, no constitution, no membership fee. Ten years of an alliance that a community organisation can simply be part of, which is the opposite of the registered-body requirement that gates most of this file. THE COUNTRIES IN THAT ALLIANCE: GABON, NIGERIA, CAMEROON, SIERRA LEONE, CÔTE D'IVOIRE, REPUBLIC OF CONGO, DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO, LIBERIA, GHANA AND UGANDA. Ten named countries. If yours is on that list, there are already organisations near you inside the alliance — and the fastest route in is through them rather than through the secretariat. THE BOOKLET THAT NAMES THE TACTICS: THE ALLIANCE LAUNCHED A NEW SUMMARY EDITION OF A BOOKLET ON THE TACTICS PALM OIL COMPANIES USE TO GRAB COMMUNITY LANDS — PROMISE, DIVIDE, INTIMIDATE, AND COERCE. Four words that describe the sequence a community is about to experience, written by the people who already have. Read it before the first meeting with the company, not after — and note DIVIDE, because the split it describes runs through the community itself. WHAT THE BULLETIN IS AND WHO WRITES IT: AN E-NEWSLETTER SINCE 1997 EXPOSING STRUGGLES, THREATS AND RESISTANCE IN FORESTS, AS WELL AS FALSE POLICY SOLUTIONS — ARTICLES ARE WRITTEN BY ACTIVISTS AND ORGANIZATIONS FROM ALL OVER THE WORLD, AND IT IS DISTRIBUTED TO MORE THAN 10,000 INDIVIDUALS AND ORGANIZATIONS IN 131 COUNTRIES. WHAT COUNTRY ORGANISATIONS USE IT FOR: THE BULLETIN IS INSTRUMENTAL IN THE ESTABLISHMENT OF PERMANENT LINKS WITH COUNTRY-BASED ORGANISATIONS, WHICH USE IT TO PUBLICISE THEIR STRUGGLES INTERNATIONALLY. You can write in it. Articles come from activists and organisations, and it reaches ten thousand readers in 131 countries — which is a publication route a community organisation can actually use, unlike the press this file records ignoring rural land disputes. WHO IT WAS SET UP AGAINST: IT HAS SUPPORTED FOREST PEOPLES RESISTING THE ENCLOSURE OF THEIR TERRITORIES BY DIFFERENT ECONOMIC INTERESTS AND EXTRACTIVE INDUSTRIES BEYOND TIMBER — PULP, OIL PALM, MINERALS, DAMS, OIL — IN MANY CASES ENDORSED BY BIG CONSERVATION NGOs. ENDORSED BY BIG CONSERVATION NGOs, said plainly. A community whose opponent is a conservation organisation rather than a company has very few places to turn in this file; this is one that names the problem rather than avoiding it. THE BASIS OF ITS ALLIANCES: INFORMAL ALLIANCES WITH COMMUNITY GROUPS AND SOCIAL MOVEMENTS BASED ON TRUST AND SHARED POLITICAL ANALYSIS, AND A COMMITMENT TO PRIORITIZE THE STRENGTHENING OF COMMUNITY STRUGGLES — WITH THE SECRETARIAT BASING ITS WORK ON WHAT IT HAS LEARNED FROM COMMUNITIES WHO LIVE WITH AND FROM THE FOREST IN AFRICA, ASIA AND LATIN AMERICA. THE MATERIALS IT PRODUCES: MATERIALS DESCRIBING COMMUNITY STRUGGLES IN AN ACCESSIBLE FORM AND RELEVANT LANGUAGES, FOCUSING ON INFORMATION PARTICULARLY RELEVANT FOR COMMUNITY ORGANISATIONS — PLUS CRITICAL ANALYSIS OF INTERNATIONAL INITIATIVES AND POLICIES PRESENTED AT GLOBAL CONFERENCES, AND BOOKS AND BRIEFINGS ON THE IMPACTS OF TREE PLANTATIONS. AND THE CARBON WARNING IT CARRIES, PLUS AN AFRICAN RULING IT REPORTS: A BULLETIN HIGHLIGHTING SEVERAL CASES WHERE THE EXPANSION OF CARBON PROJECTS HAS BECOME AN INTEGRAL PART OF THE EXTRACTIVIST MODEL — AND A REPORT THAT THE AFRICAN COMMISSION ON HUMAN AND PEOPLES' RIGHTS MADE PUBLIC ITS HISTORIC RULING ON AN INDIGENOUS PEOPLE'S RIGHT TO RETURN TO THE ANCESTRAL HOME FROM WHICH THEY WERE VIOLENTLY EVICTED WHEN A NATIONAL PARK WAS CREATED IN EASTERN DR CONGO. A continental commission ruling that people evicted for a national park have a right to return. That is a precedent worth knowing wherever a protected area was created over a community — and it is reported here rather than in any conservation publication. WHO IT SUITS: African forest and farming communities facing plantations, logging, mining, dams or carbon projects — particularly Swahili-, Lingala- and Malagasy-speaking ones. CAVEATS: A SECRETARIAT, A PUBLISHER AND A NETWORK RATHER THAN A FUNDER OR A LAW FIRM; ITS ALLIANCES ARE INFORMAL AND BUILT ON SHARED ANALYSIS, SO IT IS NOT A SERVICE YOU APPLY TO — approach through an alliance member in your country. For the peasant movement you can formally join, Egypt's entry; for the funder whose grant categories include legal aid, Algeria's entry.

trackers.name: The African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights — the continental complaints body a community can file with itself — no lawyer required, no observer status needed, a published form in French, English, Arabic and Portuguese, confidentiality on request, and a stated escape from the exhaustion rule
trackers.desc: NO LAWYER, NO ACCREDITATION, AND THEY TAKE IT IN FOUR LANGUAGES — adjacency declared first: THIS FILE'S EGYPT ENTRY COVERS THE WEST AFRICAN REGIONAL COURT AND CONTRASTS IT WITH THIS BODY'S EXHAUSTION RULE; ITS ALGERIA ENTRY THE NATIONAL COMMISSIONS THAT REPORT INTO THIS ONE; ITS GAMBIA BUCKET THE PAN-AFRICAN PRO BONO LITIGATOR THAT FILES COMMUNICATIONS HERE; ITS BOTSWANA, REPUBLIC OF CONGO, COMOROS AND DJIBOUTI BUCKETS MENTION THIS COMMISSION IN PASSING. NONE IS RESTATED AND NONE OF THOSE HOSTS IS SHIPPED. THE PRE-WRITE CHECK WAS RUN ON THE HOST ACTUALLY BEING SHIPPED. NO LAWYER REQUIRED, WHICH IS THE FIND: THE COMMUNICATION PROCEDURE IS STRAIGHTFORWARD, AND DOES NOT REQUIRE LEGAL REPRESENTATION — A COMPLAINT CAN BE BROUGHT BY THE VICTIM, BY ANOTHER PERSON ACTING ON THEIR BEHALF, OR BY ANY GROUP OF PEOPLE, INCLUDING NGOs. Read that beside the West African court filed under Egypt, where a lawyer is obligatory. Here a community committee can write the complaint itself. This file has recorded the cost of counsel ending more cases than any legal argument; this is the continental forum that does not require it. NO OBSERVER STATUS REQUIRED, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: THERE IS NO REQUIREMENT FOR OBSERVER STATUS FOR NGOs TO FILE A COMMUNICATION — AND INDIVIDUALS MAY ALWAYS MAKE SUBMISSIONS. Filed precisely because this file recorded, under Sudan, an application to the continental COURT rejected for want of the right accreditation. The two bodies differ: accreditation gates the Court, not the Commission. An unregistered village committee can lodge a communication. THE LANGUAGES AND THE FORM: A PUBLISHED COMPLAINT FORM, TO BE FILLED OUT AS CLEARLY AND CONCISELY AS POSSIBLE IN ONE OF THE WORKING LANGUAGES — FRENCH, ENGLISH, ARABIC AND PORTUGUESE — WITH SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION IN THE SAME LANGUAGE WHERE POSSIBLE, OR A TRANSLATION CERTIFIED BY A SWORN TRANSLATOR. Four languages covering almost the whole continent, including Arabic and Portuguese. The sworn-translator requirement for other documents is the cost to budget for — gather evidence in a working language from the start where you can. AND THE ALTERNATIVE TO THE FORM: ALL COMMUNICATIONS MUST BE IN WRITING AND ADDRESSED TO THE SECRETARY OR CHAIRMAN; THERE IS NO FORM OR SPECIAL FORMAT THAT MUST BE FOLLOWED, BUT A COMMUNICATION SHOULD CONTAIN ALL THE RELEVANT INFORMATION. A letter will do. That is the lowest filing threshold recorded anywhere in this file for a body that can condemn a state. WHAT MUST BE IN IT: NAME, NATIONALITY, OCCUPATION, ADDRESS AND SIGNATURE OF THE COMPLAINANT, OR FOR AN NGO ITS ADDRESS AND THE NAMES AND SIGNATURES OF ITS LEGAL REPRESENTATIVES; WHETHER THE COMPLAINANT WISHES THEIR IDENTITY WITHHELD FROM THE STATE; AN ADDRESS FOR CORRESPONDENCE; A DETAILED DESCRIPTION SPECIFYING DATE, TIME IF POSSIBLE, PLACE AND NATURE; THE NAME OF THE STATE; AND ANY STEPS TAKEN TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. DATE, TIME, PLACE AND NATURE for each incident. That is the record a community should be keeping from the first day of a project, and it is the same record the filming and mapping resources elsewhere in this file exist to produce. THE ANONYMITY RULE, EXACTLY: A COMPLAINT CANNOT BE SUBMITTED ANONYMOUSLY — IT NEEDS THE NAME AND ADDRESS OF THE COMPLAINANT AND MUST BE SIGNED; HOWEVER, A COMPLAINANT CAN REQUEST TO REMAIN ANONYMOUS, AND INDIVIDUALS MAY REQUEST CONFIDENTIALITY. The distinction that matters for anyone at risk: the Commission must know who you are, but the STATE need not. Tick that request explicitly — it is a box on the form, not an assumption. THE EXHAUSTION RULE AND ITS ESCAPE: A COMPLAINANT MUST FIRST EXHAUST ANY DOMESTIC REMEDIES WHICH EXIST, UNLESS IT IS OBVIOUS TO THE COMMISSION THAT THE PROCEDURE OF ACHIEVING THESE REMEDIES WOULD BE UNDULY PROLONGED — WITH SUBMISSION WITHIN A REASONABLE TIME AFTERWARDS, AND IT IS ALWAYS ADVISABLE TO SUBMIT AS EARLY AS POSSIBLE. UNDULY PROLONGED is the argument to make where a case has sat in a national court for years. Set out the delay with dates in the communication itself rather than waiting to be asked. THE TWO OTHER ADMISSIBILITY TRAPS: IT MUST NOT BE BASED EXCLUSIVELY ON NEWS FROM THE MASS MEDIA, AND MUST NOT BE WRITTEN IN A WAY THAT INSULTS OR DISPARAGES THE STATE — WITH ONE COMMUNICATION HELD INADMISSIBLE FOR PHRASES SUCH AS REGIME OF TORTURERS AND GOVERNMENT BARBARISMS; THE AUTHOR MUST INVESTIGATE AND ASCERTAIN THE TRUTH OF THE FACTS, AND ALL SEVEN CRITERIA IN ARTICLE 56 MUST BE MET. A real case was thrown out over its adjectives. Write it flat and factual, however justified the anger — and never build it only on newspaper clippings, which is the other common way a community's own submission dies. HOW A CASE STARTS AND THE TIMETABLE: APPLICANTS INITIATE THROUGH A LETTER OF INTRODUCTION; THE COMMISSION MAY DECIDE TO SEIZE ITSELF OF THE CASE, AFTER WHICH THE APPLICANT IS INVITED TO MAKE SUBMISSIONS ON ADMISSIBILITY — STATES GET 60 DAYS TO RESPOND AND THE APPLICANT 30 DAYS TO COUNTER-RESPOND. A LETTER OF INTRODUCTION first, then the argument. You do not need the full legal case ready to start the clock. THE TWO OUTCOMES ONCE ADMISSIBLE: IT WILL EITHER SEEK A FRIENDLY SETTLEMENT OR DECIDE ON THE MERITS — AND IF A FRIENDLY SETTLEMENT IS REACHED, A REPORT CONTAINING ITS TERMS IS PRESENTED AT SESSION, WHICH AUTOMATICALLY BRINGS CONSIDERATION OF THE CASE TO AN END. A settlement ends the case for good. Weigh what is being offered against what a decision on the merits would establish for every other community facing the same thing. WHAT HAPPENS TO THE DECISION: RECOMMENDATIONS ARE SUBMITTED TO THE ASSEMBLY OF HEADS OF STATE AND GOVERNMENT FOR ADOPTION; ALL MEASURES REMAIN CONFIDENTIAL UNLESS THE ASSEMBLY DECIDES OTHERWISE, AND A REPORT IS PUBLISHED FOLLOWING ADOPTION. Recorded plainly: the finding is not public until heads of state adopt it, which is where the delay and the political filtering sit. This is a slow forum with a weak enforcement tail — the national commissions filed under Algeria are the bodies formally tasked with chasing what it decides. AND ITS REACH AND OTHER FUNCTIONS: JURISDICTION IS COMPULSORY AND AUTOMATIC FOR STATES THAT HAVE RATIFIED THE CHARTER, AND A COMPLAINT CAN BE BROUGHT AGAINST ANY STATE THAT HAD JURISDICTION OVER THE VICTIM AT THE TIME — WITH DUTIES ALSO INCLUDING EXAMINING NATIONAL REPORTS EACH STATE SUBMITS EVERY OTHER YEAR, ADOPTING RESOLUTIONS, AND COUNTRY VISITS. IT CAME INTO EXISTENCE ON 21 OCTOBER 1986. COMPULSORY AND AUTOMATIC — no separate declaration is needed from the state, unlike the continental Court. And the biennial state reports are a second, quieter entry: a community organisation can submit a shadow report on what its government has left out. WHO IT SUITS: African communities and organisations, including unregistered ones, wanting to bring a state's conduct before a continental body without counsel or accreditation. CAVEATS: SLOW, WITH FINDINGS CONFIDENTIAL UNTIL ADOPTED BY HEADS OF STATE AND WEAK ENFORCEMENT; DOMESTIC REMEDIES MUST NORMALLY BE EXHAUSTED FIRST, THE SUBMISSION CANNOT BE ANONYMOUS TO THE COMMISSION, AND CARELESS WORDING OR MEDIA-ONLY EVIDENCE WILL SINK IT. For the West African court with no exhaustion requirement, Egypt's entry; for the pro bono litigator that files here for victims, Gambia's entry.

trackers.name: WiLDAF/FeDDAF West Africa (Women in Law and Development in Africa), Lomé — legal aid centres across eleven West African countries plus four focal points, with open membership and a digitalised legal aid centre serving four of them
trackers.desc: LEGAL AID CENTRES IN ELEVEN COUNTRIES, AND YOU CAN JOIN — method declared first: PROBE REBUILT THIS ROUND WITH WORD-BOUNDARY MATCHING, AFTER A FAULT LAST ROUND WHERE A FOUR-LETTER ACRONYM MATCHED INSIDE THE WORD PARTICIPATION AND REPORTED THREE FALSE HITS. THE REBUILT PROBE RAN THREE HOSTS AND FIVE DISTINGUISHING FACTS ACROSS ALL 53 BUCKETS; BOTH SUBJECT HOSTS AND FOUR FACTS ABSENT, WITH TWO GENERIC PHRASES IN OTHER ENTRIES ON OTHER HOSTS. THE ELEVEN COUNTRIES, WHICH IS THE FIND: THE NETWORK IS PRESENT IN BENIN, BURKINA FASO, GHANA, GUINEA-CONAKRY, LIBERIA, MALI, NIGERIA, NIGER, SENEGAL, TOGO AND CÔTE D'IVOIRE — AND IS EXTENDING INTO CAPE VERDE, THE GAMBIA, MAURITANIA AND SIERRA LEONE, WHERE IT WORKS THROUGH FOUR FOCAL POINTS. Eleven countries named, four more with a focal point. This file has recorded francophone West Africa as its thinnest region for legal help in round after round; this is a single network that already has a national chapter in almost all of it, and the chapters are separately registered bodies with their own addresses rather than branch offices. THE LEGAL AID CENTRES AND THEIR DIGITAL VERSION, WHICH IS THE SECOND FIND: A NATIONAL CHAPTER LAUNCHED A DIGITALISED LEGAL AID CENTRE COVERING BENIN, CÔTE D'IVOIRE, GHANA AND TOGO — TO IMPROVE THE OFFER OF LEGAL SERVICES, DENUNCIATION, AND THE COLLECTION AND PUBLICATION OF INFORMATION, BUILT BECAUSE RESTRICTIONS HAD LIMITED PEOPLE'S ACCESS TO THE IN-PERSON CENTRES. A legal aid centre that works when you cannot travel to it. Read beside this file's Djibouti entry, where the three barriers to university legal aid centres were language, awareness and DISTANCE — a digitalised centre is one organisation's answer to the third, and it was built under pressure rather than planned. THE SERVICE A NATIONAL CHAPTER STATES: LEGAL ASSISTANCE AND SUPPORT TO WOMEN AND CHILDREN WHO ARE VICTIMS OF VIOLATION — WITH A PUBLISHED AVENUE, BUILDING AND APARTMENT NUMBER IN ITS CAPITAL. A street address, not a post box. Chapters can be walked into. HOW BIG THE NETWORK IS: A PAN-AFRICAN NETWORK BRINGING TOGETHER 500 ORGANISATIONS AND 1,200 INDIVIDUALS ACROSS 27 COUNTRIES, FOUNDED IN 1990. WHO MAY JOIN, WHICH IS THE THIRD FIND: MEMBERSHIP IS FLEXIBLE AND OPEN — TO NATURAL PERSONS OF ANY PROFESSION INVOLVED IN OR INTERESTED IN THE PROMOTION OF WOMEN'S RIGHTS, AND TO NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANISATIONS AND INSTITUTIONS WORKING IN THE FIELD. ANY PROFESSION, and unregistered individuals as well as organisations. The registration barrier this file records at almost every funder does not apply to joining: a village women's committee with no legal status can affiliate, and affiliation is what puts a lawyer's number in its hands. WHERE THE REGIONAL OFFICE SITS AND SINCE WHEN: THE SUB-REGIONAL OFFICE FOR WEST AFRICA WAS ESTABLISHED IN APRIL 1997 AND IS BASED IN LOMÉ, TOGO, HOLDING THE REGIONAL SECRETARIAT — THE WIDER NETWORK'S SEAT HAVING MOVED THERE FROM HARARE. THE TRAINING PROGRAMME IT HAS RUN SINCE 1997: A TRAINING-OF-TRAINERS PROGRAMME IN LEGAL EDUCATION AND LEGAL ASSISTANCE. TRAINING OF TRAINERS is the multiplier. A community that sends one member gets someone who can then teach the rest, which is how this file's Zambian and Malawian paralegal entries reached the volumes they did. THE LAND WORK IT IS LISTED UNDER: A CONTINENTAL LAND COALITION LISTS IT UNDER WOMEN'S LAND RIGHTS, LEGAL ASSISTANCE AND EMPOWERMENT AND ACCESS TO JUSTICE, SECURING LAND RIGHTS, EQUITABLE LAND RIGHTS BETWEEN MEN AND WOMEN, LAND POLICY AND DIALOGUE, AND THE ROBUSTNESS OF SMALL-SCALE FARMING SYSTEMS — ALONGSIDE NAMED PARTNERS IN SEVEN COUNTRIES. SECURING LAND RIGHTS is on that list, which matters: this is a women's rights network whose formal work programme includes land tenure, so a land case is inside its mandate rather than a favour. WHAT A NATIONAL CHAPTER LOOKS LIKE INSIDE: ONE CREATED IN MARCH 1995 GROUPS ABOUT TWENTY ASSOCIATIONS AND SOME FIFTY INDIVIDUAL MEMBERS, WITH A BOARD AND A COORDINATION BUREAU. Twenty associations and fifty individuals is a reachable size. A community organisation joining is not disappearing into a bureaucracy. WHAT THE NETWORK IS FOR, IN ITS OWN WORDS: PROMOTING AND STRENGTHENING STRATEGIES THAT LINK LAW TO DEVELOPMENT, IN ORDER TO INCREASE WOMEN'S PARTICIPATION AND INFLUENCE AT ALL LEVELS. HOW IT WORKS AS A NETWORK: REGULAR EXCHANGE OF INFORMATION WITH MEMBERS ON EVENTS IN AFRICA AND ACROSS THE WORLD, WITH A BOARD OF SEVEN MEMBERS THAT THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY MAY ENLARGE. AND WHERE IT CAME FROM: ITS ORIGINS TRACE TO THE NGO FORUM IN NAIROBI IN 1985 MARKING THE END OF THE UNITED NATIONS DECADE FOR WOMEN. WHO IT SUITS: women and communities in West Africa needing legal assistance where few lawyers practise, and local groups that want to affiliate rather than apply for funding. CAVEATS: THE MANDATE IS WOMEN'S AND CHILDREN'S RIGHTS, SO A LAND CASE IS TAKEN THROUGH THAT FRAME AND A CASE WITH NO SUCH DIMENSION MAY NOT FIT; CHAPTER CAPACITY VARIES ENORMOUSLY BY COUNTRY AND SOME PUBLISHED MATERIAL IS OLDER — CONFIRM YOUR NEAREST CENTRE IS OPEN BEFORE TRAVELLING. For the eight university legal aid centres and the three barriers they measured, Djibouti's entry; for francophone Central Africa's defenders network, Gabon's entry.

trackers.name: U.S. Treasury OFAC — North Korea Sanctions
trackers.desc: U.S. sanctions program targeting DPRK illicit finance and evasion — among the few public windows onto North Korean money flows. Here you can trace how suspicious transactions are reported and money-laundering intelligence is produced in North Korea.

trackers.name: PERAC Principles — protected zones when domestic machinery has stopped
trackers.desc: AN INSTRUMENT WRITTEN FOR EXACTLY THIS SITUATION, AND IT NAMES NO ONE. The Principles on Protection of the Environment in Relation to Armed Conflicts — 28 principles adopted by the International Law Commission on second reading on 27 May 2022 and welcomed by the UN General Assembly in A/RES/77/104 of 7 December 2022, adopted without vote — cover the whole arc: before, during and after armed conflict, and situations of occupation. BE HONEST ABOUT THEIR STATUS: they are nonbinding — but ILC documents are recorded as increasingly interpreted by tribunals, courts and governments as ‘reflections of customary international law’. Cite them as that, not as treaty obligations. PRINCIPLE 4 IS THE DESIGNATION ROUTE WHEN DOMESTIC MACHINERY HAS STOPPED: States should designate, by agreement or otherwise, areas of environmental importance as protected zones in the event of an armed conflict, including where those areas are of cultural importance — cultural importance is an express qualifying ground. PRINCIPLE 5 requires States, international organisations AND other relevant actors to protect the environment of the lands and territories that indigenous peoples inhabit or traditionally use, and where conflict has harmed it, to consult and cooperate with indigenous peoples on remedial measures — note that the addressees are not only States, which reaches bodies operating where a government cannot or will not act. PRINCIPLE 3 requires effective legislative, administrative, judicial and other measures. AND THE STRUCTURAL POINT: the ILC chose not to differentiate between international and non-international armed conflicts, so the environment-related conduct of non-state armed groups also comes within their purview — which matters where harm is done by armed groups rather than a state army. The distinctions sit in the commentaries, which should be read together with the principles. CITE ALONGSIDE: the 2020 ICRC Guidelines on protection of the natural environment in armed conflict, UNEA resolution 2/15 (27 May 2016), the 2019 Geneva List of Principles on the Protection of Water Infrastructure, and victim-assistance provisions in the Mine Ban Treaty and the Convention on Cluster Munitions.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: COMIFAC Treaty and Plan de Convergence — and its community protocol
trackers.desc: A TREATY BODY WITH A TEMPLATE YOU CAN COPY. The Traité relatif à la conservation et à la gestion durable des écosystèmes forestiers d'Afrique Centrale, signed by heads of state at their second summit on 5 February 2005 in Brazzaville, instituted the Commission des Forêts d'Afrique Centrale — described as the unique instance d'orientation, de décision et de coordination for subregional forest action, and the cadre politique et juridique global for cooperation in the field. A transboundary forest question belongs in that forum. The Plan de Convergence is the reference framework for all such interventions — first edition 2005–2014, revised in 2014 for 2015–2025 and restructured into 10 strategic axes, executed by a Secrétariat exécutif. CIVIL SOCIETY IS A NAMED STAKEHOLDER in implementing it, alongside state administrations, CEEAC and the private sector — so participation is built into the framework, not conceded case by case. Axis 7 covers capacity and participation des acteurs, expressly contemplating micro-projets générateurs de revenus pour les populations locales; axis 9 covers innovative financing mechanisms. THE DOCUMENT LIBRARY IS THE MOST USEFUL PART: COMIFAC publishes a worked Protocole Bioculturel Communautaire for a named village, a guide to inventorying genetic resources and traditional knowledge, a paper on les droits d'usage des peuples autochtones et communautés locales et les obligations qui en découlent, a subregional APA (access and benefit-sharing) strategy, and directives on forests and the SDGs built with FAO as 5 principles and 12 directives across 31 prioritised targets. A community biocultural protocol published by a treaty body is a template, not a theory. AND ITS OWN DIAGNOSIS IS QUOTABLE: the Plan records that participatory natural resource management and mediation of use conflicts, though already mapped out, are insufficiently developed.

trackers.name: Equatorial Guinea — published attorney lists and named firms with Malabo AND Bata offices, for a country where the bar cannot be used as a referral route
trackers.desc: WHERE TO FIND A NAMED LAWYER WHEN THE BAR IS NOT AN OPTION: this file records that the Equatoguinean Colegio de Abogados was dissolved by decree in 2002, its replacement's members reportedly appointed by and under the control of the justice minister, and that it SUSPENDS ADVOCATES FOR REPRESENTING CLIENTS — so the ordinary route used everywhere else in Africa, a bar referral, is closed here. What exists instead are PUBLISHED LISTS. A FOREIGN MISSION IN MALABO PUBLISHES AN ALPHABETICAL LIST OF LAWYERS AND FIRMS WILLING TO PROVIDE LEGAL SERVICES, stating plainly that it assumes no responsibility for their professional ability or integrity and cannot vouch for information the providers supplied themselves. An embassy attorney list is a starting point, not a recommendation — use it to get names, then ask each firm directly what it has actually done in your field. NAMED FIRMS WITH DOMESTIC REACH: NGOMO ASOCIADOS, operating NATIONALLY THROUGH OFFICES IN BOTH MALABO AND BATA, advising companies AND PARTICULARES — private individuals — across all branches of law, with professionals of more than 30 years' experience and a network of collaborating firms abroad (tel +240 551-109-500); CLARENCE ABOGADOS & ASOCIADOS, whose practice areas include ENERGY AND NATURAL RESOURCES and REAL ESTATE; ALOGO LAW FIRM, covering employment, energy and natural resources; and HELPEN ABOGADOS & CONSULTORES at Banapa, Malabo. A national business directory lists firms under a juridical category with addresses in Malabo and Bata. Offices in both Malabo AND Bata is the filter that matters — the mainland is where the forest, the plantations and the concessions are, and a Bioko-only firm cannot reach them. AND THE HONEST WARNING, REPEATED FROM THIS FILE'S OWN RECORD: the firms reachable this way are oriented to corporate and investor clients — the same firms that advise the companies. Ask directly whether a firm will act AGAINST a concession holder before you disclose your case, and remember that Equatoguinean advocates who represent activists have been detained and suspended. WHO IT SUITS: Equatoguineans needing to instruct counsel on land, expropriation, employment or a natural-resource matter. CAVEATS: COMMERCIAL FIRMS AND A FOREIGN-MISSION LIST, NOT LEGAL AID. For lawyers who defend lawyers and represented over 40 activists, Equatorial Guinea's Comisión Ecuatoguineana de Juristas entry; for constituting your own association first, the NGO registration entry.

trackers.name: INDEFOR-AP, Bata — the only reachable environmental body in the country, and the way in is a telephone number
trackers.desc: THIS IS THE FIRST ENTRY IN THE FILE FOR EQUATORIAL GUINEA, AND THE HONEST SUMMARY IS THAT ONE INSTITUTION PUBLISHES A CONTACT AND NOTHING PUBLISHES A COMPLAINT ROUTE. The National Institute for Forestry Development and Management of the Protected Areas System is a public body with administrative and financial autonomy, headquartered in Bata, responsible for sustainable use of the forests and for running the national protected areas system. It is organised in departments for protected-area management, the national herbarium, sustainable forestry, training and outreach, cartography and topography, and administration. The contact page names the Director General, Fidel Esono Mba Eyono, and gives one telephone number, +240 222 250 465; that name is corroborated by independent Equatoguinean press reporting of the institute's ecoguard training, which is why this entry exists at all. WHAT TO KNOW BEFORE YOU RELY ON IT: the published institutional email address is a personal Yahoo account, and the mail link on the same page resolves to an unrelated address left in by the site's developer — the contact form and the email cannot be relied on, so use the telephone or go to Bata. The site is on a .com domain; no government-domain page for the institute was located, and no ministry page listing it was found, so this is recorded as the institute's own site on the strength of its content and the corroborated director rather than because a state domain confirms it. THE ABSENCES, WHICH ARE THE FINDING: no environmental complaint route, no impact-assessment register, no published objection period, no legal aid scheme and no ombudsman were located for this country. Reporting on the protected areas — thirteen of them, with ecoguards deployed in five — comes from conservation NGOs working alongside the institute rather than from the state.

trackers.name: GEF Small Grants in Equatorial Guinea — added by name in the eighth cycle; the only community-accessible money recorded for this country
trackers.desc: WHERE TO APPLY FOR MONEY: the GEF SMALL GRANTS PROGRAMME expanded country coverage in its eighth replenishment from 124 to 135 countries, ADDING EQUATORIAL GUINEA BY NAME — alongside Somalia, South Sudan, Libya and São Tomé and Príncipe. THE ALLOCATION RULE: the eighth cycle secured USD 135 million for the core programme and ensures EQUAL ALLOCATION OF NEARLY USD 1 MILLION IN CORE FINANCING TO EACH of the 135 participating countries — regardless of size or previous participation, with STAR allocations raised over 30 per cent. A newly added country is not competing against large established programmes for the core money, which is the argument for applying in the FIRST cycle rather than waiting to see how it goes. The programme's stated objective is to catalyse and mobilise CIVIL SOCIETY actors and LOCAL ACTIONS addressing the major drivers of environmental degradation, and it has funded community-level environmental projects since 1992. WHY THIS ENTRY EXISTS: Equatorial Guinea has been the thinnest bucket in this entire file, carrying a single honest-absence entry recording that the state forestry and protected-areas institute is all that exists and no independent civil society counterpart could be verified. A funding window is not a substitute for that — but it is the first recorded route by which money could reach a local group, and it costs nothing to ask whether the country programme has opened. WHO IT SUITS: Equatoguinean community groups and associations with an environmental project, and anyone testing whether the window is live. CAVEATS: STATE THIS PLAINLY — civic space in Equatorial Guinea is severely restricted, independent organising carries real risk, and a grant programme does not change that; registration requirements may be the binding obstacle. It funds environmental action, NOT litigation or land purchase. For what does and does not exist institutionally, Equatorial Guinea's INDEFOR-AP entry.

trackers.name: Comisión Ecuatoguineana de Juristas and EG Justice — they defend the lawyers, because in Equatorial Guinea representing a client is what gets an advocate suspended
trackers.desc: WHO DEFENDS THE DEFENDERS, AND THE RISK COMES FIRST BECAUSE IT IS THE POINT: in Equatorial Guinea taking a client can cost an advocate the right to practise. Advocate Ángel Obama Obiang Eseng was ILLEGALLY DETAINED for 48 hours on 4 August and TEMPORARILY SUSPENDED FROM THE PROFESSION on 14 August 2024 by the Colegio de Abogados — the suspension arising BECAUSE HE REPRESENTED a detained activist; the wife and nephew of Doctor Ponciano Mbomio Nvo were arbitrarily detained; and Mbomio himself was earlier suspended for expressing opinions and criticisms of the government in his closing arguments, having already been suspended for a year in similar circumstances. Before you instruct anyone here, understand that you are asking them to accept professional and personal risk — that is the honest frame for this entire entry. WHY THE BAR IS NOT THE ANSWER HERE, UNLIKE EVERY OTHER COUNTRY IN THIS FILE: the original Colegio de Abogados was DISSOLVED BY GOVERNMENT DECREE in May 2002; the justice minister created a High Council of Lawyers chaired by himself and required all lawyers to seek ministry recognition; a new bar was formed in 2003 whose members were reportedly appointed by, and under the control of, the Minister of Justice. So a referral from the bar is not an independent route in Equatorial Guinea — it is the body that suspends advocates for defending clients. WHO TO GO TO INSTEAD: the COMISIÓN ECUATOGUINEANA DE JURISTAS (juristasge.org), working with EG JUSTICE — described as the only human rights organisation devoted solely to Equatorial Guinea, founded by an Equatoguinean exile — which together defend human rights advocates, represent prisoners of conscience, and have secured LEGAL REPRESENTATION FOR OVER 40 ACTIVISTS with humanitarian support for their families, brought legal action against the government in December 2022, and raised the persecution of lawyers at the UN Universal Periodic Review with the Paris bar. WHO IT SUITS: Equatoguineans facing detention, land seizure or reprisal who need counsel that will not be deterred, and families of detained people. CAVEATS: THESE ARE DIASPORA-BASED AND NETWORKED BODIES, not a walk-in service inside the country; contact carries risk for you and for them. For what does and does not exist institutionally, Equatorial Guinea's INDEFOR-AP entry; for the newly opened community funding window, the GEF Small Grants entry.

trackers.name: Ley 6/2025 on protected areas and ANDEGE — the law that finally replaced a statute repealed in 2003, and the national NGO that visits communities bordering Monte Alén
trackers.desc: THE NEW LAW, AND WHY THE GAP IT FILLS MATTERS MORE THAN THE LAW ITSELF: Equatorial Guinea has promulgated LEY 6/2025 ON PROTECTED AREAS, which the state's own account says responds to LEGAL NEEDS OUTSTANDING SINCE THE 2003 REPEAL OF THE EARLIER LEY 4/2000 — A REPEAL THAT LEFT NORMATIVE VOIDS ON THE DECLARATION, PROTECTION, MANAGEMENT AND FINANCING of the country's protected natural areas. For roughly two decades there was no operative rule on how an area gets declared or funded. If you were told in that period that nothing could be done for your forest, that was true and it is no longer — the new law is the reason to ask again. Its stated objects include conserving priority ecosystems AND FOREST CARBON RESERVES, protecting biodiversity, promoting ecotourism, and PROMOTING CARBON AND BIODIVERSITY CREDITS AS A SUSTAINABLE ECONOMIC ALTERNATIVE, aligned with the global biodiversity framework target of protecting at least 30% of terrestrial, marine and coastal areas by 2030; more than 80% of the country's surface is vegetation-covered. Carbon and biodiversity credits are named in the statute as an economic alternative — which means a community forest proposal can be argued in the government's own revenue terms rather than only conservation ones. WHAT ALREADY EXISTS TO ATTACH TO: the SISTEMA NACIONAL DE ÁREAS PROTEGIDAS (SNAP) comprises THIRTEEN protected areas, EXPRESSLY WITHOUT PREJUDICE TO FUTURE EXPANSION — including Monte Alén (2,000 km2), Los Altos de Nsork (700 km2), the Caldera de Luba scientific reserve and Annobón island — built under LEY 1/1997 on the use and management of forests and administered from Bata. Thirteen areas with expansion written into the founding purpose is an open door: the list was never meant to be closed. WHO GOES TO THE VILLAGES: ANDEGE (Amigos de la Naturaleza y del Medio Ambiente de Guinea Ecuatorial), a national NGO, has run awareness missions in the local communities of SENDJE, MISERGUE, TEGUETE and MIDJOBO — districts of Mbini, Evinayong and Kogo, all bordering MONTE ALÉN NATIONAL PARK, working with an international conservation partner. A named national NGO that has physically visited named villages is the most concrete civil-society contact recorded for Equatorial Guinea in this file. WHO IT SUITS: Equatoguinean communities bordering a park or holding forest, and anyone seeking declaration of new ground. CAVEATS: A NEW STATUTE NOT YET TESTED, in a country where the earlier one was repealed and left unreplaced for twenty years, and where an earlier national biodiversity strategy WENT UNIMPLEMENTED FOR LACK OF FINANCING. For the institute that manages the system and what does not exist around it, Equatorial Guinea's INDEFOR-AP entry; for lawyers who defend lawyers, the Comisión Ecuatoguineana de Juristas entry; for community money, the GEF Small Grants entry.

trackers.name: Bioko Biodiversity Protection Program — contracts about 50 LOCAL WORKERS as forest and beach patrol teams in the Gran Caldera protected area, and is building a centre at Moka
trackers.desc: WHO EMPLOYS LOCAL PEOPLE TO PATROL: the BIOKO BIODIVERSITY PROTECTION PROGRAM (BBPP), working across Bioko island in partnership with the NATIONAL UNIVERSITY OF EQUATORIAL GUINEA (UNGE), CONTRACTS APPROXIMATELY 50 LOCAL WORKERS in the GRAN CALDERA AND SOUTHERN HIGHLANDS PROTECTED AREA to serve in FOREST AND BEACH PATROL TEAMS, to deter hunting and collect data on wildlife. Fifty paid local patrol jobs is the most substantial community employment recorded for Equatorial Guinea in this file — in a country where the acquire and legal routes are thin, a conservation operation that pays wages is a real presence on the ground, and worth approaching for work as much as for protection. WHAT ELSE IT RUNS: an annual JANUARY CENSUS of primates in the remote Gran Caldera Volcánica de Luba, conducted by trained students and volunteers; an ONGOING SURVEY OF THE MALABO BUSHMEAT MARKET; a study-abroad programme based at UNGE involving both Equatoguinean and American students; and a wildlife research centre under development in the town of MOKA to host ecotourists and visiting scientists, with a GUEST HOUSE, WILDLIFE SANCTUARY AND A SYSTEM OF TRAILS. A market survey is documentation you can cite, and a named town with a guest house is a place you can physically go — both rarer in this country's record than they sound. THE GROUND IT COVERS AND WHY IT MATTERS: the RESERVA CIENTÍFICA DE LA GRAN CALDERA DE LUBA, created 2000, covers 51,000 HECTARES of dense rainforest on Bioko, much of it PRISTINE FOREST, with a high primate population including species endemic to the reserve, and it is one of the most important nesting areas in the Atlantic for FOUR SEA TURTLE SPECIES. THE THREAT NAMED PLAINLY IN THE RECORD: the primate population is endangered by growing bushmeat demand COUPLED WITH LACK OF ENFORCEMENT OF THE HUNTING BAN INSIDE THE RESERVE — a Spanish NGO had run conservation and ecotourism work there from 1995 focused on green turtles. An unenforced ban is the standing condition here; patrol teams paid to walk the forest are what substitutes for enforcement, which is why the employment matters more than the designation. WHO IT SUITS: Bioko communities, and Equatoguineans seeking conservation work, training or a named institution to approach. CAVEATS: A RESEARCH AND PATROL PROGRAMME WITH FOREIGN UNIVERSITY BACKING, NOT A COMMUNITY-OWNED BODY, and it operates in the severely restricted civic space this file records elsewhere. For the new protected-areas law and the NGO that visits villages, Equatorial Guinea's Ley 6/2025 and ANDEGE entry; for the institute that manages the system, INDEFOR-AP; for lawyers who defend lawyers, the Comisión Ecuatoguineana de Juristas entry.

trackers.name: Registering an NGO in Equatorial Guinea — the published requirements: notarised statutes, a favourable report from the provincial Governor AND from every ministry regulating your activity
trackers.desc: HOW TO BECOME A LEGAL PERSON, WHICH EVERY OTHER INSTRUMENT IN THIS FILE ASSUMES YOU ALREADY ARE: in Equatorial Guinea NGOs ARE DEFINED BY LAW AS ASSOCIATIONS OF AN APOLITICAL, NON-PROFIT AND SOCIAL-UTILITY NATURE WITH THEIR OWN LEGAL PERSONALITY; they HAVE THEIR OWN ASSETS AND MAY ENGAGE IN LUCRATIVE ACTIVITIES that enrich that patrimony for the better fulfilment of their purpose, provided financial contributions received ARE NOT DISTRIBUTED AMONG MEMBERS and are used solely for the purpose. An NGO here may hold assets and trade to fund itself — that is the vehicle a community needs to hold land, receive grant money and sign anything, and it is the step Cameroon, Gabon, Nigeria and Togo all require before their community-forest instruments will look at you. THE DOCUMENTS: a MEMORANDUM OF INCORPORATION AND ARTICLES OF ASSOCIATION reflecting the minimum requirements provided by law, LEGALISED BEFORE A PUBLIC NOTARY; the association must HAVE A SOCIAL PURPOSE AIMED AT BENEFITING A GENERIC GROUP AND NOT ADVOCATE THE PRIVATE INTERESTS OF ITS MEMBERS. Write the purpose as the benefit to the whole community, not to the founding families — the law makes that a condition of existence, and it is also the rule that protects your body from capture. THE GATE, STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE IT IS THE HARD PART: A FAVOURABLE REPORT IS REQUIRED FROM THE GOVERNOR OF THE PROVINCE where the NGO intends to operate, applied for by formal letter to the Governor's office with the legalised statutes and an affidavit attached; AND, to submit the registration application to the MINISTRY OF INTERIOR AND LOCAL CORPORATIONS, A FAVOURABLE REPORT IS ALSO REQUIRED FROM ALL MINISTERIAL DEPARTMENTS REGULATING THE ACTIVITIES OF THE NGO. Every ministry that touches your subject holds a veto. Count them before you start, approach the Governor first, and expect the environment ministry to be one of them — which is why the INDEFOR-AP and ANDEGE contacts in this file matter before you file, not after. The interior ministry has also publicly invited existing associations and NGOs to REGULARISE THEIR SITUATION. WHO IT SUITS: Equatoguinean communities and groups needing a body that can hold assets, receive funds and sign agreements. CAVEATS: SOURCED FROM A LAW-FIRM PRACTICE NOTE, not the statute text — confirm current requirements; and the apolitical condition is enforced in a state this file records as suspending advocates for defending clients. For the protected-areas law and the NGO that visits villages, Equatorial Guinea's Ley 6/2025 and ANDEGE entry; for 50 paid patrol jobs on Bioko, the BBPP entry; for counsel, the Comisión Ecuatoguineana de Juristas entry.

trackers.name: Equatorial Guinea's BOSQUES COMUNALES — communal forest is a named legal category, applications run through the Bata regional delegation, and the boundary must be cut before the plan is signed
trackers.desc: THE COMMUNAL FOREST CATEGORY AND HOW A FILE MOVES: under LEY NÚM. 1/1997 OF 18 FEBRUARY ON THE USE AND MANAGEMENT OF FORESTS, Equatoguinean forests fall into THREE NAMED TYPES: PARCELAS FORESTALES, BOSQUES COMUNALES — COMMUNAL FORESTS — AND BOSQUES NACIONALES. Communal forest is a category in the statute, not a favour. Name it in your application, because asking for a bosque comunal is asking for something the law already recognises. THE PROCEDURE, IN ORDER: applications for forest-resource use are PROMOTED AT THE INITIATIVE OF THE INTERESTED PARTIES, before the ministry OR ITS REGIONAL DELEGATION IN THE CITY OF BATA, requesting the designation of TOPOGRAPHY AND CARTOGRAPHY TECHNICIANS to carry out the PRIOR OFFICIAL DELIMITATION of the type of forest sought. AND THE STEP THAT CANNOT BE SKIPPED: the MEASUREMENT CERTIFICATES AND SITUATION PLANS ISSUED BY THE REGIONAL DELEGATE IN BATA SHALL NOT BE SIGNED WITHOUT THE BOUNDARY TROCHAS OF THE FORESTS APPLIED FOR HAVING FIRST BEEN OPENED by the forest management section. The boundary must be physically cut before the paperwork is valid — the same rule Gabon states for its two-metre layons. Cutting and maintaining your own perimeter is the one part of the process your people control, and no certificate exists without it. A RULE THAT CUTS BOTH WAYS: for natural or replanted forests inside the boundaries of silvo-agricultural or rustic estates up to a maximum of 500 HECTARES, THE FOREST PRODUCTS ON THOSE FORESTS ARE THE EXCLUSIVE PROPERTY OF THEIR TITLE HOLDERS, who must meet their fiscal obligations — with GOVERNMENT DELEGATES AND THE AUTHORITIES OF ENTES LOCALES MENORES of the area empowered to issue the INFORME TESTIFICAL and the ACTA FAMILIAR. A witness statement and a family deed issued by your own local authority are the documents that establish a holding here — that is a route that runs through people who live near you rather than through Malabo. AND THE PROHIBITION TO CITE: DECRETO Nº7/2017 OF 31 JANUARY PROHIBITS THE FELLING OF TREES FOR COMMERCIAL PURPOSES BY CHAINSAW OPERATORS AND SOME FORESTRY COMPANIES THROUGHOUT THE NATIONAL TERRITORY, with implementing rules in a 2017 ministerial order. A national ban on commercial chainsaw felling is a live instrument — if operators are cutting near you, they are arguing against a decree, not merely a policy. Context: national forest cover has fallen sharply, and protected areas cover about 5,228 km2, 19% of the country. WHO IT SUITS: Equatoguinean villages seeking a communal forest or defending one against felling. CAVEATS: A MINISTERIAL PROCEDURE requiring official delimitation and fiscal compliance. For the new protected-areas law and ANDEGE, Equatorial Guinea's Ley 6/2025 entry; for constituting your association first, the NGO registration entry; for 50 paid patrol jobs, BBPP.

trackers.name: What ANDEGE actually does — runs seminars on how to run an association and write projects, wrote the Pico Basilé park plan, and amended plan chapters after touring the communities
trackers.desc: THE SEMINAR THAT TEACHES YOU TO BE AN ASSOCIATION, WHICH IS THE EXACT GAP THIS FILE IDENTIFIES IN EQUATORIAL GUINEA: ANDEGE (AMIGOS DE LA NATURALEZA Y DEL DESARROLLO DE GUINEA ECUATORIAL), IN COLLABORATION WITH ITS PARTNERS, ORGANISED A FOUR-DAY SEMINAR ON THE ADMINISTRATIVE ORGANISATION AND FUNCTIONING OF AN ASSOCIATION, AND ON THE CONCEPTION, PREPARATION AND MANAGEMENT OF PROJECTS, alongside training aimed at civil society organisations. Registering an association in Equatorial Guinea requires notarised statutes and a favourable report from the Governor and every relevant ministry — and here is a Equatoguinean NGO that teaches, in four days, how to run the body you are trying to create and how to write the projects that will fund it. Ask ANDEGE when the next seminar runs before you file anything. ITS STATED PURPOSE is SUPPORTING ACTIONS TO STRENGTHEN COMMUNITY CAPACITIES IN AGROECOLOGY AND BIODIVERSITY CONSERVATION, and its PRESIDENT IS NAMED ON THE PUBLIC RECORD. WHAT IT HAS WRITTEN AND CONVENED: ANDEGE PREPARED A PLAN TO SAFEGUARD THREATENED ECOSYSTEMS AND THE SERVICES THEY PROVIDE TO COMMUNITIES FOR PICO BASILÉ NATIONAL PARK — CREATED IN 2000, 32,256 HECTARES ON NORTHERN BIOKO, HOLDING FOUR GLOBALLY THREATENED PRIMATES, AND THE MAIN SOURCE OF DRINKING WATER FOR THE CAPITAL, THREATENED BY ILLEGAL HUNTING AND INDISCRIMINATE AND UNCONTROLLED LOGGING. The park is the capital's drinking water. That is the single most powerful argument available in Equatorial Guinea for protecting a forest — if your ground feeds a town's water, say so first and say it loudest. It also convened A SYNTHESIS AND DISCUSSION MEETING ON THE MANAGEMENT PLANS OF TWO IMPORTANT NATURAL SITES, ATTENDED BY SOME THIRTY EXPERTS AND REPRESENTATIVES OF DIFFERENT SECTORS, ASSOCIATIONS AND ADMINISTRATIONS, and a two-day technical validation meeting in Bata with experts from the agriculture, forests, fisheries and environment departments, the forestry institute, the national university and the science council. AND THE DETAIL THAT PROVES CONSULTATION CAN CHANGE A DOCUMENT: THE COMMUNITY WORK WAS DONE THROUGH A TOUR OF THE COMMUNITIES DURING AUGUST, AND IN THOSE MEETINGS AND WORKSHOPS THE INTERESTS OF THE POPULATION AND OF CONSERVATION WERE RECONCILED — AND TO THAT EFFECT THE CONTENTS OF CERTAIN CHAPTERS WERE AMENDED. Chapters of a management plan were amended because communities were toured and asked. Demand the tour, attend it, and afterwards ask which chapters changed — that is the test of whether consultation was real. ITS OTHER WORK: it was the ENTITY CONTRACTED to run awareness sessions on urban solid waste management in FOUR COMMUNITIES OF THE CITY OF BATA under a UN development programme project with government ministries and the Bata city council; and it has an agreement with an international conservation foundation covering THE PREPARATION OF A PROPOSAL FOR A FOREST RESERVE. ANDEGE gets contracted by UN agencies and writes reserve proposals — which means a community can ask it to write the proposal rather than trying to draft one alone. ALSO NAMED: ECOGUINEA, working on conservation projects in collaboration with the national university and the forestry institute. WHO IT SUITS: Equatoguinean groups forming an association, communities near a park or a water catchment, and anyone needing a proposal written. CAVEATS: A DONOR-FUNDED NGO working closely with ministries. For the law that replaced the 2003 repeal, Equatorial Guinea's Ley 6/2025 entry; for the three forest categories and the boundary trochas, the bosques comunales entry; for how to register your own body, the NGO registration entry; for named firms in Malabo and Bata, the attorney lists entry; for 50 paid patrol jobs, BBPP.

trackers.name: Equatorial Guinea's cooperatives and secular NGOs — a women's savings and credit cooperative in Bata, a salted-fish cooperative grouping, CEID and four other named bodies, and the hundred base groupings with no legal cover
trackers.desc: THE WOMEN'S SAVINGS COOPERATIVE IN BATA — because this file's Equatoguinean record has almost no domestic money in it, and the cooperatives are where it sits: THE MOST IMPORTANT NAMED COOPERATIVES INCLUDE THE COOPERATIVA PARA LA CONSERVACIÓN DE FRUTAS TROPICALES (COFRUT); THE COOPERATIVA DE AHORRO Y CRÉDITOS DE LAS MUJERES DE BATA (COACREMBA); THE COOPERATIVA MUENDJE; AN AGRUPACIÓN COOPERATIVA DE PESCADO SALADO; AND COVA. A savings and credit cooperative run by the women of Bata is a lending institution your community can approach without a bank, a donor or a ministry. Where this file elsewhere sends people to foreign grant windows, a cooperative is money that is already local and already theirs. Ask COACREMBA what it lends for and who may join. And a COOPERATIVE GROUPING for salted fish and one for tropical fruit conservation are the two forms a coastal or farming community can copy directly: the cooperative is how producers hold a price together, and holding a price is what makes staying on the land pay. THE SECULAR NGOs, NAMED — AND THE NOTE THAT THEY ARE NEW: THE RECORD STATES THAT SECULAR NGOs HAVE, BY CONTRAST WITH THE CHURCHES, A FAIRLY RECENT APPEARANCE, AND NAMES AMONG THE MOST NOTABLE: SENSACIÓN DEL JOVEN FUTURO (SEJOF); THE CENTRO DE ESTUDIOS E INICIATIVAS PARA EL DESARROLLO (CEID); THE ASOCIACIÓN DE MUJERES PARA LA LUCHA CONTRA EL SIDA (AMUSIDA); THE COMITÉ DEL NIÑO GUINEOECUATORIANO (CANIGE); AND A CHILDREN'S VILLAGES ORGANISATION. Secular NGOs being recent is the other half of a fact this file has recorded across the region: where lay organisations are new and few, the church structures are the ones with reach. Use both — the NGO for the paperwork, the congregation for the room full of people. AND CEID IS NOT JUST A NAME ON A LIST: IT SUPPLIED NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL EXPERTS, ALONGSIDE AN INTERNATIONAL CONSERVATION ORGANISATION AND ANDEGE, TO A TEN-DAY TRAINING SEMINAR COORDINATED BY ANDEGE MEMBERS, OPENED IN THE PRESENCE OF NATIONAL AUTHORITIES AND A FOREIGN AMBASSADOR. A development studies centre that can put trainers in a room for ten days is the body to ask when your association needs teaching rather than representing. And note who opens these events: ambassadors attend. An embassy present at a training is an embassy that can be written to afterwards. THE CONSTRAINT, STATED PLAINLY IN THE SAME STUDY AND WORTH KNOWING BEFORE YOU START: THERE ALSO EXIST ABOUT A HUNDRED AGRUPACIONES DE BASE WHICH, GIVEN THE LEGAL CONTEXT, LACK LEGAL COVER IN THE ABSENCE OF A REGULATORY ORDER GOVERNING THEM. A hundred base groupings already exist and none of them is legally covered. So the question for a new Equatoguinean group is not whether to organise — people already have — but whether to seek the notarised registration this file records elsewhere, or to work as one of the hundred. Both are real choices; the second is what most people are actually doing. WHO CONVENES THE ENVIRONMENTAL ROOM, FOR REFERENCE: national biodiversity meetings have brought together the fisheries and environment ministry, the agriculture and forests ministry through INDEFOR-AP, the Bioko biodiversity programme, ANDEGE, an international zoological society, an international conservation foundation, the national university, a botanical garden, a named Spanish conservation association and the Spanish cultural centres of Malabo and Bata — with the Spanish, US and German ambassadors present at the opening. The Spanish cultural centres in both Malabo and Bata host these sessions. A cultural centre is a venue a community group can ask to use, and it is one of the few neutral rooms in the country. WHO IT SUITS: Equatoguinean producers and women's groups needing credit, associations needing training, and anyone weighing registration against working informally. CAVEATS: PARTS OF THIS RECORD COME FROM A CIVIL SOCIETY STUDY AND MAY HAVE MOVED ON — confirm which cooperatives are active. For what ANDEGE actually does, including the seminar on how to run an association and the reserve proposal writing service, Equatorial Guinea's ANDEGE entries; for the notarised registration requirements, the registering an NGO entry; for communal forest as a named legal category, the bosques comunales entry; for about 50 local workers contracted as conservation staff, the Bioko Biodiversity Protection Program entry; for the lawyers who defend lawyers, the Comisión Ecuatoguineana de Juristas entry.

trackers.name: The Aarhus Convention Special Rapporteur on Environmental Defenders (UNECE) — the world's first office dedicated to protecting environmental defenders — confidential complaints by email, no need to go to court first, a 60-day answer demanded of the government, and reach over foreign state and private companies operating in Africa
trackers.desc: NO LAWYER, NO COURT FIRST, AND AN EMAIL ADDRESS — THIS IS THE FIRST MECHANISM SPECIFICALLY SAFEGUARDING ENVIRONMENTAL DEFENDERS TO BE ESTABLISHED WITHIN A LEGALLY BINDING FRAMEWORK, EITHER UNDER THE UN SYSTEM OR ANY OTHER INTERGOVERNMENTAL STRUCTURE. WHO MAY COMPLAIN: ANY MEMBER OF THE PUBLIC CAN SUBMIT A COMPLAINT, EITHER ON THEIR OWN BEHALF OR ON BEHALF OF ANOTHER MEMBER OF THE PUBLIC — PROVIDED THE CONSENT OF THAT OTHER PERSON IS OBTAINED AND SUBMITTED TOGETHER WITH THE COMPLAINT FORM. Any member of the public, and you may file for someone else with their written consent. So a literate neighbour, a teacher or a relative abroad can file for a farmer who cannot — get the consent in writing at the same time, because it must go with the form. THE TWO BARRIERS REMOVED, AND THEY ARE THE TWO THAT STOP EVERYONE: THE SUBMISSION OF A COMPLAINT IS CONFIDENTIAL, AND COMPLAINANTS ARE NOT REQUIRED TO HAVE EXHAUSTED DOMESTIC REMEDIES BEFORE SUBMITTING — BECAUSE TIME IS OF THE ESSENCE WHEN IT COMES TO THE SAFETY OF ENVIRONMENTAL DEFENDERS, AND ACTIONS TO PREVENT THREATS CANNOT BE DELAYED. You do not have to lose in your own courts first. Almost every other international route in this file makes you exhaust domestic remedies, which takes years a threatened person does not have. And the submission is confidential, so filing does not itself expose you. HOW TO SUBMIT: COMPLETE THE COMPLAINT FORM AND SEND IT TO A PUBLISHED UN EMAIL ADDRESS. A form and an email address. That is the whole entry cost — no lawyer, no fee, no travel. THE AFRICAN REACH, WHICH IS THE PART TO READ CAREFULLY BECAUSE IT IS BOTH THE LIMIT AND THE OPENING: WITHIN THE TERRITORY OF PARTIES, THE RAPPORTEUR CAN DEAL WITH CASES OF PENALIZATION, PERSECUTION OR HARASSMENT BY ANY PUBLIC OR PRIVATE ACTOR. OUTSIDE THAT TERRITORY — FOR INSTANCE IN LATIN AMERICA, ASIA-PACIFIC, OR AFRICA — THE RAPPORTEUR CAN DEAL WITH CASES OF PENALIZATION, PERSECUTION OR HARASSMENT BY A STATE ENTITY OR A STATE-OWNED COMPANY OF A PARTY, OR BY PRIVATE COMPANIES BASED IN A PARTY COUNTRY. So for an African defender the question is not where you are but who is doing it to you. If the company harassing you is European, or is a state-owned firm of a European state, you are inside this mandate — and this file's Guinea entry has the free trackers that tell you where a company is based. Run that lookup first; it decides whether this door is open. WHAT THE OFFICE CAN ACTUALLY DO: ISSUE IMMEDIATE AND ONGOING PROTECTION MEASURES; RELEASE PUBLIC STATEMENTS; USE DIPLOMATIC CHANNELS; ATTEND TRIALS IN DOMESTIC COURTS TO MONITOR LEGAL PROCEEDINGS; AND BRING THE MATTER TO THE ATTENTION OF OTHER RELEVANT HUMAN RIGHTS BODIES, ORGANIZATIONS AND GOVERNMENT INSTITUTIONS, AND OF THE CONCERNED GOVERNMENTS AND HEADS OF STATE — WITH MEASURES TAILORED TO EACH SITUATION. ATTEND TRIALS IN DOMESTIC COURTS TO MONITOR PROCEEDINGS. An international monitor in the public gallery changes how a prosecution of a land defender is conducted, and this file has recorded elsewhere that a watched trial goes differently from an unwatched one. Ask for trial observation specifically. THE PROCEDURE AND ITS CLOCK: IF THE COMPLAINT IS ADMISSIBLE AND WITHIN SCOPE, THE RAPPORTEUR SENDS A LETTER OF ALLEGATION TO THE PARTY CONCERNED, SETTING OUT THE ALLEGATIONS AND REQUESTING A RESPONSE WITHIN 60 DAYS OF RECEIPT — AND ONCE THE 60-DAY DEADLINE HAS PASSED, POSTS THE LETTER TOGETHER WITH ANY RESPONSE RECEIVED ON THE WEBSITE. Sixty days, then publication whether or not they answered. That is a fixed, short clock with a public consequence attached, which is rarer than it sounds. THE VOLUME, SO YOU KNOW THE QUEUE: 55 COMPLAINTS RECEIVED IN A SINGLE CALENDAR YEAR, AND 16 OF THE 75 RECEIVED SINCE THE OFFICE BEGAN WERE PUBLICLY ACCESSIBLE. Fifty-five a year is a small enough caseload that a well-documented complaint gets read properly. WHAT THE PUBLISHED COMPLAINTS SHOW OTHERS FACING: VERBAL AND PHYSICAL THREATS AND ATTACKS, ONLINE AND OFFLINE INTIMIDATION AND OTHER FORMS OF HARASSMENT BY PRIVATE INDIVIDUALS, COMPANIES, OR THE AUTHORITIES — INCLUDING DISMISSAL FROM EMPLOYMENT. DISMISSAL FROM EMPLOYMENT counts as persecution here. Losing your job for objecting is a complaint, not just a misfortune. AND THE WIDER UN ROUTE WHERE THIS ONE DOES NOT REACH: URGENT APPEALS FOR TIME-SENSITIVE, LIFE-THREATENING MATTERS, OR ALLEGATION LETTERS TO UN SPECIAL PROCEDURES MANDATE-HOLDERS — THESE APPLY TO ALL UN MEMBER STATES AND ARE NOT TIED TO A COUNTRY'S ACCEPTANCE OF PARTICULAR TREATY OBLIGATIONS, DO NOT REQUIRE EXHAUSTION OF DOMESTIC REMEDIES, AND ANYONE MAY SUBMIT CREDIBLE AND RELIABLE INFORMATION. ALL UN MEMBER STATES, with no treaty ratification needed. So even where your government has signed nothing, this second route exists — and note the warning that SOME MECHANISMS HAVE A NON-DUPLICATION REQUIREMENT, so check before filing the same facts in two places, though special procedures often address complaints jointly. WHO IT SUITS: African environmental and land defenders facing threats, prosecution, intimidation or dismissal — especially where a foreign or state-owned company is involved. CAVEATS: OUTSIDE PARTY TERRITORY THE MANDATE REACHES ONLY PARTY STATE ENTITIES, THEIR STATE-OWNED COMPANIES, AND PRIVATE COMPANIES BASED IN PARTY COUNTRIES — check the company's base first. For a country-specific rapporteur route, Eritrea's Human Rights Concern entry; for the trackers naming a company's home country, Guinea's investment chain entry; for the home-country mediation offices, Chad's entry.

trackers.name: Digital Democracy's Mapeo — free offline mapping and evidence tools built for land defenders, where the community owns the data and phones sync to each other without internet — available in French and Swahili, already used by the Ogiek in Kenya
trackers.desc: THE DATA STAYS ON YOUR OWN PHONES — THIS IS A FREE DIGITAL TOOLSET FOR DOCUMENTING, MONITORING AND MAPPING MANY TYPES OF DATA: OFFLINE-FIRST OPEN-SOURCE TECHNOLOGY WHICH MAKES IT EASY FOR MANY TO USE, WITH NO INTERNET OR SPECIAL HARDWARE REQUIRED TO COLLECT, VIEW, OR SHARE DATA. THE CLAUSE THAT MATTERS MOST, AND ALMOST NOTHING ELSE IN THIS FILE OFFERS IT: ALL DATA IS COMPLETELY OWNED BY THE COMMUNITIES THEMSELVES — BUILT ON A DECENTRALIZED PEER-TO-PEER DATABASE THAT ALLOWS COMMUNITIES TO OWN THEIR OWN DATA AND CONTROL HOW INFORMATION IS SHARED. No server belonging to an NGO, a ministry or a foreign university. This file has recorded communities mapped by outsiders whose maps then lived on somebody else's computer; here the record is on your own devices from the start, and you decide what leaves. Before agreeing to any mapping project, ask that one question: where will the data sit afterwards, and who can delete it. HOW IT WORKS IN PRACTICE: WITH THE PUSH OF A BUTTON, CONTRIBUTORS CAN GATHER MAP DATA BY LINKING GPS POINTS, PHOTOS, AND NOTES — AND DATA CAN BE SHARED BETWEEN PROJECT COLLABORATORS WITH A MOBILE-TO-MOBILE SYNC FEATURE, A PEER-TO-PEER DATABASE ALLOWING GROUPS TO SECURELY EXCHANGE DATA WITHOUT THE INTERNET, IN REGIONS WHERE ACCESS IS CENSORED OR UNRELIABLE. Phones sync to each other directly. So a network shutdown does not stop the documentation, and there is no upload that can be intercepted — which is the exact problem this file recorded in Libya, Sudan and Cameroon when connections were cut during evictions. WHY IT WAS BUILT, AND FOR WHOM: CO-DESIGNED AND DEVELOPED WITH COMMUNITIES WHO FACE THREATS TO THEIR LAND SUCH AS ILLEGAL GOLD MINING, OIL CONTAMINATION AND POACHING — BUILT TO SUPPORT THEM TO DOCUMENT THESE ACTIVITIES IN ORDER TO TAKE COMMUNITY ACTION AGAINST THEM, TO REPORT THEM TO AUTHORITIES, FILE LAWSUITS, LAUNCH MEDIA CAMPAIGNS, OR CREATE MAPS FOR LAND CLAIMS. Four named uses for the same evidence: report it, sue on it, publish it, or claim land with it. Collect once, use four ways — which is why the export formats below matter. THE STATED REASON IT EXISTS: THERE ARE MANY TOOLS THAT COULD BE USED FOR MAKING MAPS OR DOCUMENTING INFORMATION, HOWEVER AFTER WORKING WITH EARTH DEFENDERS FOR MANY YEARS THEY NEVER FOUND A TOOL BUILT WITH THE NEEDS AND PRIORITIES OF EARTH DEFENDERS AT THE FOREFRONT, SO THEY DECIDED TO BUILD ONE. THE LANGUAGES, AND TWO OF THEM ARE THE POINT FOR THIS CONTINENT: IT CAN BE TRANSLATED INTO ANY LANGUAGE, AND IS CURRENTLY AVAILABLE IN FRENCH AND SWAHILI AMONG THIRTEEN OTHERS. French and Swahili already done, and any other language possible. Between them those two cover a large share of the countries in this file — and if yours is not there, translation is a task your own people can do. THE FORMATS, WHICH DECIDE WHETHER THE EVIDENCE TRAVELS: IT IS POSSIBLE TO ADD PHOTOGRAPHS, TO IMPORT GPS TRACKS AND SHAPEFILES, AND TO EXPORT AS A PDF OR PRINT REPORT, GEOJSON, CSV OR SHAPEFILE — WITH SINGLE-POINT EXPORT TO EMAIL AND MOBILE SHARING APPS. THE NEWER VERSION CAPTURES DATA POINTS ENRICHED WITH PHOTOS, AUDIO, GPS COORDINATES, DATES AND CATEGORIZED DETAILS, AND TRACKS ALLOW USERS TO MAP ROUTES. A PDF print report is what you hand to a district officer; a shapefile is what a lawyer's expert needs. The same afternoon's walking produces both. And AUDIO means an elder's account of a boundary is attached to the point itself. THE ACCESSIBILITY TEST, FROM A COMMUNITY LEADER RATHER THAN THE DEVELOPERS: THE INDIGENOUS GUARD RESPONSIBLE FOR MONITORING AND RECORDING HARMFUL ACTIVITIES HAVE BEEN USING IT FOR YEARS — IT IS SO EASY TO USE THAT EVEN OUR ELDERS, WHO DO NOT SPEAK THE NATIONAL LANGUAGE, USE IT. TECHNOLOGY IS AN EXTENSION OF OUR KNOWLEDGE. Elders who do not speak the national language using it themselves. That is the standard to demand of any tool offered to your community, and the reason to ask for a demonstration before agreeing to a training. THE WORKED CASE: OVER TWENTY COMMUNITIES DEFENDED THEIR TERRITORY AGAINST OIL EXPLORATION PROPOSED BY THE GOVERNMENT — THEY USED THE TOOL FOR OVER FOUR YEARS TO RECORD TERRITORIAL DATA AND MAPS, WHICH THEY USED AS EVIDENCE AGAINST THE GOVERNMENT; AND ANOTHER NATION MAPPED 800,000 HECTARES OF RAINFOREST. Four years of recording before it was needed in the case. The evidence that wins is gathered long before the hearing — start now, not when the notice arrives. AND THE AFRICAN USE ALREADY ON RECORD: THE TOOLS HAVE ALSO BEEN USED BY THE OGIEK IN KENYA. The same people whose continental court judgment this file records as still unimplemented. Ask them how it went. THE OTHER FREE THINGS ON OFFER: AN EARTH DEFENDERS TOOLKIT — A COLLABORATIVE SPACE PROVIDING A GROWING COLLECTION OF RESOURCES AND TRAINING MATERIALS FOR COMMUNITIES ON THE FRONTLINES, PLUS COMMUNITY NETWORKS FOR USERS TO CONNECT AND SHARE THEIR EXPERIENCES; AND AN APPLICATION FOR COMMUNITIES TO MAP, PROTECT AND SHARE STORIES ABOUT THEIR LAND, CONNECTING AUDIO OR VIDEO CONTENT TO PLACES ON A MAP. A place where communities using these tools talk to each other, and a separate application for putting oral history onto a map. For a community whose claim rests on what people remember rather than on paper, that second one is the tool that turns memory into a record. WHO IT SUITS: African communities documenting mining, logging, contamination or eviction — especially where the network is unreliable and the record must not leave your hands. CAVEATS: A FREE TOOL, NOT A FUNDER OR A LITIGATOR — and a first training still costs something. For the free system for rights neither registered nor registerable, Comoros' land recording entry; for the participatory mapping of seven million hectares, DR Congo's MappingForRights entry; for the alerts you can subscribe to for your own forest, the Republic of Congo's entry.

trackers.name: Protective accompaniment — international volunteers who physically stay with threatened communities, or simply phone to check on them, on a record of nobody killed under protection in twenty years, with an African field project and a published needs report
trackers.desc: SOMEBODY FOREIGN STANDS NEXT TO YOU, AND THAT IS THE PROTECTION — PROTECTIVE ACCOMPANIMENT IS A STRATEGY FOR PROTECTING HUMAN RIGHTS DEFENDERS AND COMMUNITIES WHOSE LIVES AND WORK ARE THREATENED BY POLITICAL VIOLENCE: TEAMS OF VOLUNTEERS, BACKED UP BY AN INTERNATIONAL SUPPORT NETWORK, ACCOMPANY DEFENDERS AND COMMUNITIES IN AREAS OF CONFLICT. WHY IT WORKS, STATED PLAINLY: THE PREMISE OF ACCOMPANIMENT IS THAT THERE WILL BE AN INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE TO WHATEVER VIOLENCE OR POTENTIAL VIOLENCE THE VOLUNTEER WITNESSES — BEHIND SUCH A RESPONSE LIES THE IMPLIED THREAT OF DIPLOMATIC AND ECONOMIC PRESSURE, PRESSURE THAT THE SPONSORS OF SUCH VIOLENCE PREFER TO AVOID. The volunteer carries no weapon and no authority. What they carry is a phone line to embassies and an audience — and the calculation that whoever ordered the violence would rather it went unwitnessed. Everything else in this file's protection entries responds after the harm; this is designed to make the harm not worth doing. THE FOUR FORMS IT TAKES, AND THE LAST ONE COSTS ALMOST NOTHING: WHEN THE LEVEL OF THREAT IS HIGH, ACCOMPANIMENT IS SOMETIMES ROUND THE CLOCK; IN OTHER SITUATIONS VOLUNTEERS STAY WITH THREATENED COMMUNITIES OR REMAIN IN THE OFFICES OF ORGANISATIONS; THEY ACCOMPANY THREATENED ACTIVISTS WHEN THEY TRAVEL; AND ANOTHER FORM OF ACCOMPANIMENT IS REGULAR PHONE CALLS TO ORGANISATIONS TO CHECK ON THEIR SAFETY. REGULAR PHONE CALLS COUNT AS ACCOMPANIMENT. That is the version any allied organisation anywhere can offer your committee today, at no cost — a fixed call at a fixed hour, with an agreed plan for what happens if nobody answers. Set that up with a partner abroad before you need international volunteers, because it works on the same principle and it is available now. ACCOMPANY THEM WHEN THEY TRAVEL is the second cheap one. This file records that the dangerous moment is usually the journey to the district office or the court, not the meeting itself. WHO IT ACCOMPANIES: INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES, ENVIRONMENTAL ORGANISATIONS, LAWYERS, WOMEN'S ORGANISATIONS, TRADES UNIONS, AND RELATIVES OF THE DISAPPEARED — BECAUSE VICTIMS OF HUMAN RIGHTS ABUSES ARE FREQUENTLY THOSE ATTEMPTING TO ORGANISE FOR SOCIAL JUSTICE, NONVIOLENCE AND RESPECT FOR HUMAN RIGHTS, THUS CHALLENGING THE INTERESTS OF POWERFUL ELITES. Indigenous communities and environmental organisations are the first two named. This is not a general human rights service that might stretch to cover a land case — land and environment defenders are its core constituency. THE RECORD, AND IT IS THE REASON TO TAKE IT SERIOUSLY: SINCE 1981 IT HAS PROTECTED THE LIVES OF HUNDREDS OF ORGANISATIONS AND COMMUNITIES IN 11 COUNTRIES, WITH VOLUNTEERS FROM MORE THAN 30 COUNTRIES — AND IN MORE THAN TWENTY YEARS OF WORK IN SOME OF THE WORLD'S MOST VIOLENT CONFLICTS, NO ONE UNDER ITS PROTECTION WAS KILLED WHILE THEY WERE BEING PROTECTED, NOR HAVE ANY OF ITS VOLUNTEERS BEEN KILLED. THE REQUEST RULE: AT THE REQUEST OF LOCAL ORGANISATIONS, TEAMS PROVIDE ACCOMPANIMENT TO DEFENDERS THREATENED WITH VIOLENCE. You ask; they do not arrive uninvited. So the relationship has to be built before the threat, which is the same lesson this file's small-grants entry records: the connection is the asset. THE AFRICAN PROJECT, AND HOW CAREFULLY IT WAS DECIDED: IT LAUNCHED ITS FIRST EVER FIELD PROGRAMME IN AFRICA IN 2012, HAVING ASSESSED THE PROTECTION NEEDS OF DEFENDERS ACROSS AFRICA IN 2009/10 TO IDENTIFY COUNTRIES WHERE THE METHODOLOGY MAY BE APPROPRIATE, THEN UNDERTAKEN AN IN-DEPTH ASSESSMENT TALKING TO DEFENDERS ABOUT THEIR PROTECTION NEEDS AND WHETHER ACCOMPANIMENT WOULD BE EFFECTIVE — AND ITS REPORT ON THE PROTECTION NEEDS OF DEFENDERS IN AFRICA IS PUBLISHED FOR DOWNLOAD. ONE field project on the whole continent. That is the honest limit: accompaniment is expensive and slow to establish, so most African defenders cannot get the physical version. What they can get is the published Africa needs report, the phone-call form, and the advocacy below. WHAT THE AFRICAN OFFICE ALSO DOES, WHICH IS AVAILABLE MORE WIDELY: ADVOCACY INVOLVING RAISING THE PROFILES OF DEFENDERS AT RISK, ADVOCATING FOR PROTECTION MECHANISMS, AND BRIDGING THE GAP BETWEEN GRASSROOTS DEFENDERS AND THE INTERNATIONAL COMMUNITY, NATIONAL ORGANISATIONS AND STATE AUTHORITIES — PLUS CAPACITY BUILDING CONSISTING OF WORKSHOPS, PERSONALISED RISK ASSESSMENTS, AND SECURITY PLANS FOR DEFENDERS. PERSONALISED RISK ASSESSMENTS for individuals, not just organisational plans. This file's Djibouti entry has the organisational version; this is the one for the named person who is being followed. THE NON-INTERFERENCE POLICY, WORTH HOLDING EVERY OUTSIDE ALLY TO: A STRICT POLICY OF NON-INTERFERENCE IN THE WORK OF PARTNERS, IN THE BELIEF THAT LASTING TRANSFORMATION CANNOT BE IMPOSED FROM OUTSIDE BUT MUST BE BASED ON THE CAPACITY OF LOCAL PEOPLE TO CONSTRUCT GENUINE PEACE. They protect the work without directing it. Ask any international organisation offering your community support whether they have that policy in writing. THE REGISTRATION WARNING IT RAISED AT THE UN: GRASSROOTS HUMAN RIGHTS GROUPS REPORT A COMMUNITY GROUPS REGISTRATION ACT BEING USED TO PRESSURE THEM TO REFRAIN FROM CRUCIAL HUMAN RIGHTS ACTIVITIES, LIKE ADVOCACY AND VIOLATION MONITORING. A registration law used as a leash rather than a formality. This file has recorded the same pattern from Burundi to Eswatini — and here it is on the record at a UN dialogue, which is the kind of citation a national coalition can use. AND THE WIDER PRACTICE, WITH THREE OTHER ORGANISATIONS NAMED: UNARMED CIVILIAN PROTECTION IS THE PRACTICE OF CIVILIANS PROTECTING OTHER CIVILIANS IN SITUATIONS OF IMMINENT, ONGOING OR RECENT VIOLENT CONFLICT — INVOLVING TRAINED INTERNATIONAL CIVILIANS PROTECTING LOCAL CIVILIANS, LOCAL CIVILIANS PROTECTING EACH OTHER, AND EVEN LOCAL CIVILIANS PROTECTING INTERNATIONAL OR NON-LOCAL CIVILIANS. LOCAL CIVILIANS PROTECTING EACH OTHER is a recognised form of the same discipline, with training and doctrine behind it. Where no international team will come, that is the version a community can build itself — and there are three other organisations named who teach it. WHO IT SUITS: African land, indigenous and environmental defenders under threat of violence, and organisations abroad willing to be their standing phone call. CAVEATS: ONLY ONE AFRICAN FIELD PROJECT EXISTS AND ACCOMPANIMENT IS PROVIDED ONLY ON REQUEST FROM LOCAL ORGANISATIONS — the phone-call and risk-assessment forms are far more widely available than the physical presence. A directory of national organisations already doing this work, with what each one does written beside it. PLANTATIONS and MEGA-ENERGY PROJECTS inside the definition. THE PARTICIPATORY RESEARCH OUTPUT: A PAPER SHOWCASING SEVEN COMMUNITY-BASED STUDIES BY ALLIANCE MEMBERS IN SUB-SAHARAN AFRICA, WHICH BEGINS TO FILL THE GAP OF THE VOICES MISSING IN A CONTINENTAL MINING VISION. Communities researching their own case and publishing it against a continental policy document. That is the same move this file records under the mining atlas — answering a framework in its own terms rather than from outside it. THEY ARRIVED AND BLOCKED OUR RIVERS, SO NOW WE CAN'T FETCH WATER; RIGHT NOW WE DON'T HAVE WATER ANYWHERE, WE BUY WATER. WE BUY WATER. A community that drew water free now pays for it, and that cost appears in no impact assessment. Private security as well as soldiers. ALLIES SELECTED BY THE INDIGENOUS PARTNERS. Here the community picks who holds its money. If your group is unregistered or has no bank account, that is the clause to ask about, because it decides whether the money is yours or somebody else's to administer on your behalf.
